100113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
100113.value: Tropical cyclones (TCs), generally known as typhoons, affect many parts of Asia every year, causing loss of lives and property. With the advent of technologies, forecasts of the tracks of individual TCs have improved significantly during the past few decades and have led to reduction of such losses. However, government planners, insurance industries and other related businesses need to know well in advance whether a season is likely to have more or fewer TCs for the sake of disaster preparedness and reduction of financial loss. In addition, with the trend of global warming continuing, knowledge of future changes in the frequency of TC landfall in a particular region is important for long-term planning and adaptation purposes. Many studies on the variability of TC activity on various time scales have been made. However, they focused mainly on such activity over the entire ocean basin and very few have examined the variability of landfalling TCs and even fewer addressed the intensity of the TC at landfall, which is significant because of the greater damage from the stronger winds and the higher storm surge associated with these winds. The objectives of this study are therefore 1. to investigate the variability of TC intensity at landfall along the East Asian coast on time scales from interannual to interdecadal 2. to identify the possible causes of the variability of TC intensity at landfall along the East Asian coast 3. to estimate the potential of predicting the seasonal frequency of TC landfall and its intensity, and 4. to make possible projections of future frequency of TC landfall and its intensity. The results of this study will lead to improved understanding of the physical processes that are responsible for the variability of TCs and their intensity at landfall. In addition, the development of a tool for predicting seasonal, and for projecting future, TC activity at landfall would be extremely useful for society for planning and adaptation purposes.

100113.label: Realisation of objectives
100113.value: The three project objectives have been achieved. Three papers have been published and two other papers are currently under second review, both with conditional acceptance. In fact, we have also achieved the fourth objective in the original proposal (please see section of research outcome). In other words, we have accomplished much more than expected of the project.

100113.label: Major findings and research outcome
100113.value: The variations of tropical cyclone (TC) intensity at landfall along the East Asia coast have been identified. A major finding is that the annual power dissipation index (PDI), which is used as the metric to represent the annual severity of TCs hitting a particular section of the coast, has a northward migration during the last 60 years. Such variations are explained in terms of the concomitant changes in the atmospheric circulation, which brings more TCs northward. The results have been published in Liu and Chan (2016). To estimate the potential for predicting seasonal TC landfall intensity, two different tasks have been performed. The first is to nest the mesoscale WRF model into a regional climate model (RegCM3) to predict the intensity of TCs making landfall over South China. The results (Lok and Chan 2017) show that indeed such an approach can give reasonable predictions of the annual PDI. The second task is to develop a fully 3-dimensional air-sea coupled model so that the TC intensity can be more accurately simulated. The coupled model has been constructed for idealised situations (Zhao and Chan 2017). A second paper is currently under second review (Zhao and Chan 2018) with conditional acceptance. The original proposal contains an objective of making future projections of TC intensity under global warming. This has also been accomplished for estimating TC intensities in three periods: 2030s, 2060s and 2090s for the South China coast. The results have been submitted for publication (Lok and Chan 2018) with conditional acceptance. The research outcome has therefore exceeded what was proposed.

100113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
100113.value: This project has shown that indeed TC intensities at landfall have interannual and interdecadal variations. The question is whether such variations are due to global warming or natural variability. Future research to ascertain this question should be pursued. In addition, one problem with the prediction of TC intensity is a general over-estimation of intensity because the WRF model has no ocean coupling. In order to be more realistic, the coupled model developed under idealised conditions need to be incorporated into the model system.

100113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
100113.value: Annual variations of tropical cyclone intensity at landfall along the East Asia coast have been found to have interannual, and more importantly, interdecadal time scales, as well as possessing a northward migration during the last 60 years. Predictions of such annual variations have been successfully simulated using a nested climate/mesoscale model. Such a model has also been used to project future annual variations of TC intensity for South China.

100313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
100313.value: Considerable advances have been achieved for post-metallocene catalysts with respect to improved performance and new applications in olefin polymerization. Non-covalent interactions such as C–H•••F–C between a functionalized non-innocent ligand and the growing polymer chain (or ‘weak attractive ligand–polymer interactions’) can potentially allow control of the reactivity at the polymer chain, but there is little precedent for their exploration. The nature and relevance of C–H•••F–C interactions is a topical yet controversial issue. Due to the emerging importance and applicability of fluorine substituents, it is desirable to employ spectroscopic methods to probe and elucidate their surrounding environment and connectivity. In this project, the design and preparation of ligand frameworks and the corresponding post-metallocene complexes bearing suitably appended fluorinated (or related hydrogen-bonding acceptor) substituents will be pursued, and strategies to improve catalyst performance will be implemented. Detailed NMR spectroscopic characterization and investigation of intramolecular non-covalent interactions will be undertaken. The underlying objectives are to probe the existence of weak attractive ligand-polymer interactions in the proposed catalysts, examine the consequences of these interactions upon catalytic behavior and polymer properties, and develop novel catalyst systems with attractive characteristics. 茂後金屬催化劑的性能改進及其在烯烴聚合的新應用方面取得了較大的進展。非共價鍵相互作用（或配體與聚合物之間微弱的吸引性相互作用），例如C-H•••F-C，存在於官能化的配體和聚合物的增長鏈之間，它可潛在地控制聚合物鏈的反應活性，但是相關的研究報導非常少。C-H•••F-C的相互作用及性質是一個頗具爭議的課題。由於氟取代基的應用及其新興的重要性，最理想的是採用光譜學方法來探測和闡明其周圍環境和連接性。在這個課題中，設計和製備配體骨架與相應的含氟取代基（或其他相關氫鍵受體）的茂後金屬配合物來改進催化劑性能，並將進行詳細的核磁共振光譜表徵和分子內的非共價鍵相互作用的研究。最終目的是在設計的催化劑體系中檢測配體與聚合物之間微弱的吸引性相互作用的存在，並研究這些相互作用對催化性能和聚合物性質的影響，從而開發更有吸引力的新型催化劑體系。

100313.label: Realisation of objectives
100313.value: The project has been completed and all objectives have been achieved, resulting in several publications. In addition, two research students have been trained under this project and invited talks have been given. Objective 1: In this project, several new classes of group 4 post-metallocene complexes supported by chelating C-based ancillary ligands, including (sigma-aryl)-2-phenolate-6-pyridyl [O,C,N], pyridine-2-phenolate-6-(sigma-aryl) [O,N,C] and pyridine-2-phenolate-6-arylmethine [O,N,CH(Ar)], have been developed, which contain a fluorinated moiety (or potentially hydrogen-bond acceptor substituent) in the vicinity of the metal. The intramolecular C−H∙∙∙F−C contacts in these complexes can be considered as synthetic models for weak attractive ligand–polymer interactions in olefin polymerization processes. Diverse families of complexes bearing four-, five-, six and seven-membered chelate rings have been designed to display different structural symmetry, flexibility and bite angles, all of which would influence catalytic behavior in olefin polymerization as well as olefin insertion reactivity and pathways. Objective 2: Multinuclear NMR spectroscopy and X-ray crystallography have bene employed to characterize and probe the nature of these complexes and catalysts, and especially the intramolecular interactions. The observation of 1H-19F and 13C-19F coupling in derivatives bearing fluorine-containing substituents indicate the presence of intramolecular C−H∙∙∙F−C interactions. Further examination by [1H-19F]-HMQC and especially [1H-19F]-HMBC (J) experiments (which specifically separate contributions from scalar (J) coupling and cross-correlation (CR) interference) reveal a significant scalar component for this coupling, thus confirming that the C−H∙∙∙F−C interactions occur with chemical connectivity. Evidence from NMR spectroscopy also imply the possible existence of C−H∙∙∙Cl−C interactions. The verified spectroscopic detection of such weak and elusive interactions remains sparse in the literature. These conclusions are important because the concept of weak attractive ligand–polymer interactions is only viable if the observed coupling and hence the non-covalent interaction is authentic. The contrasting NMR spectral patterns with regards to 1H-19F coupling for fluorinated Ti (across C−H∙∙∙F−C interactions), Zr and Hf (via M∙∙∙F interactions) analogues have been rationalized. Objective 3: Multinuclear NMR experiments have been performed to study the insertion of unsaturated substrates into the M–C bond of (C-based)-chelating group 4 post-metallocene complexes. In particular, the reactivity of olefin monomers, and their insertion into the M–C(sp2 or sp3)] moieties of [O,C,N], [O,N,C] and [O,N,CH(Ar)] complexes and the corresponding cationic benzyl species, have been investigated. The corresponding cationic benzyl species have been generated cleanly upon treatment with trityl borate and characterized by NMR spectroscopy. DFT calculations have been performed which suggest that olefin insertion into the M–C(sp2) bond of five-membered metallacycles is favorable, particularly for catalysts where steric repulsion would be alleviated. However, the M–C(sp3) bond of four-membered chelates was found to be surprisingly stable against olefin insertion and expansion to six-membered metallacycles, and a kinetic preference for the conventional chain propagation process was indicated (see Objective 4). Objective 4: Investigations into the olefin polymerization behavior of the newly developed catalysts have been undertaken. For catalysts that display intramolecular C−H∙∙∙F−C interactions and may be considered as models for ‘weak attractive ligand–polymer interactions’, polymerization studies were performed with special focus on the possible impact of WALPI-type catalysis. Improved catalytic reactivity was also targeted because first-generation Ti-[O,N,C] catalysts habitually displayed multisite behavior. Importantly, exceptionally high catalytic efficiencies have been observed in conjunction with the trityl borate cocatalyst, and the polymers produced display very high molecular weight values as well as narrow molecular weight distributions, implying single-site character. Furthermore, the existence of intramolecular C−H∙∙∙F−C interactions in cationic active species has been invoked to rationalize the enhanced activity of fluorinated catalysts.

100313.label: Major findings and research outcome
100313.value: A new series of group 4 bis(benzyl) complexes supported by (sigma-aryl)-2-phenolate-6-pyridyl [O,C,N] ligands have been prepared. Fluorinated derivatives have been characterized by multinuclear NMR spectroscopy, which indicate the presence of intramolecular C−H∙∙∙F−C interactions. [1H-19F]-HMBC experiments have been performed which reveal a significant scalar component for this coupling, thus confirming that the C−H∙∙∙F−C interactions occur with chemical connectivity. This result is important because the applicability of weak attractive ligand–polymer interactions in catalysis is feasible only if the observed coupling and hence the non-covalent interaction is genuine. The contrasting NMR spectral patterns for the fluorinated Ti, Zr and Hf analogues have been rationalized. The ethylene polymerization activities for the isoquinolinyl-based Ti-[O,C,N] catalysts are superior to those of pyridyl-based congeners. [Publications 1 and 2] A new class of pyridine-2-phenolate-6-arylmethine [O,N,CH(Ar)] Group 4 catalysts bearing a four-membered C(sp3)-donor chelate ring have been developed. The C(1) symmetry of the complexes was confirmed by NMR spectroscopy and X-ray crystal structures. Investigations by multinuclear NMR spectroscopy (including [1H-19F]-HMBC and -HMQC experiments) indicated the existence of C(methine)−H∙∙∙F−C interactions for fluorinated derivatives. Exceptionally high polymerization efficiencies have been observed with the trityl borate cocatalyst, and the polymers produced display narrow molecular weight distributions, implying single-site character. DFT calculations have been performed which surprisingly revealed a clear preference for the conventional propagation pathway (rather than olefin insertion into the four-membered metallacycle), while C−H∙∙∙F−C interactions are invoked to rationalize the reactivity of fluorinated catalysts. [Publication 3] A new generation of pyridine-2-phenolate-6-(sigma-aryl) [O,N,C] group 4 complexes bearing a seven-membered O,N-donor chelate have been synthesized and characterized by multinuclear NMR spectroscopy. The flexible seven-membered metallacyle is envisaged to facilitate formation of optimal structures and minimize activation energies. Molecular structures have been determined by X-ray crystallography. Ethylene polymerization studies have been undertaken in conjunction with MAO and trityl borate. High catalytic efficiencies, very high molecular weight values and single-site character have been observed. [Publication 4] A family of Group 4 bis(benzyl) complexes supported by pyridine-2-phenolate-6-(sigma-aryl) [O,N,C] ligands, featuring fluoro, chloro, bromo or methyl substituents on the sigma-aryl group, and an anthracenyl moiety ortho to the phenolate oxygen, have been prepared. DFT calculations have been performed on the corresponding active species, which suggest that ethylene insertion into the M–C(sigma-aryl) bond is favorable. Interesting substituent effects upon olefin polymerization behavior, plus well-defined catalytic reactivity and high-MW polymers, are observed. [Publications 5 and 6]

100313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
100313.value: Several classes of post-metallocene complexes supported by chelating C-based ancillary ligands, bearing substituents capable of undergoing weak attractive ligand-polymer interactions, have been developed during this project. Further work to design and synthesize new and modified ligand systems containing fluorinated or alternative hydrogen-bond acceptor substituents can be undertaken. The continued development of new C(sp3)-based (including four- and high-membered) chelates, from cyclometalation of alkyl substituents, is suggested. In this context, further work is proposed with regards to olefin insertion into the M–C(sp3 or sp2) bond of C-based metallacyles, as well as its possible beneficial or detrimental impact on catalytic behavior (including efficiency and well-defined reactivity). Multinuclear NMR experiments and DFT calculations to probe and characterize the intramolecular C−H∙∙∙F−C and related non-covalent interactions in these complexes can provide further insights. Further studies are proposed to utilize C−H∙∙∙F−C and related interactions in catalysis, in particular to derive beneficial consequences during olefin polymerization reactions, which can pave the way towards the development of more efficient and well-defined (e.g. single-site, living) catalyst systems.

100313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
100313.value: This project concerns the preparation, characterization and catalytic applications of group 4 organometallic complexes supported by chelating C-based ancillary ligands. Several families of catalysts bearing four- to seven-membered chelate rings have been developed. Advanced multinuclear NMR experiments have been developed and conducted to probe the observed 1H-19F coupling for derivatives bearing suitably positioned fluorine substituents, which confirmed the existence of C−H∙∙∙F−C interactions occurring with chemical connectivity. This is a critical conclusion because the potential applicability of weak attractive ligand–polymer interactions in catalysis is only viable if the non-covalent interactions are genuine. The authenticated intramolecular C−H∙∙∙F−C contacts in these complexes can therefore be considered as synthetic models of weak attractive ligand–polymer interactions, a novel strategy that offers the capability to manipulate the reactivity of the polymer chain during catalysis. New catalyst systems displaying desirable characteristics have been developed. Exceptionally high catalytic efficiencies have been observed, and the polymers produced exhibit very high molecular weight values as well as narrow molecular weight distributions, indicative of single-site character. This project highlights the usefulness of the ‘weak attractive polymer-ligand interactions’ concept for controlling and modulating olefin polymerization reactions.

100813.label: Project Objectives
100813.value: The main objective of this project is to provide a smoothed analysis of the componentwise condition number for the solution of triangular systems of linear equations. From such analysis, a smoothed analysis of the loss of precision in the solution of these systems follows. A related, but secondary, goal is to provide a similar smoothed analysis for systems of linear equations whose matrices possess a sparsity pattern other than triangularity.

From such analysis, a smoothed analysis of the loss of precision in the solution of these systems follows. A related, but secondary, goal is to provide a similar smoothed analysis for systems of linear equations whose matrices possess a sparsity pattern other than triangularity.

100813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
100813.value: The most commonly used solver of linear systems of equations, Gaussian elimination, reduces the input system Ax = c to a system Lx = b with L lower triangular (and same solution x). Then, it solves the latter by back substitution. As a consequence, triangular systems of equations are routinely solved by computer. Almost on every occasion, the accuracy of the computed solution is very high. Yet, the reasons for this accuracy have been dodging researchers for quite a while and as early as in the 1960s J.H. Wilkinson noted that the accuracy obtained when solving linear systems was better than what common error analyses predicted. In 1998, D. Viswanath and N. Trefethen added a surprising result to this picture. They showed that the condition number ---a key ingredient in the analyses mentioned above--- of random triangular matrices is, almost invariably, very large. This result added strength to the idea that one cannot solve triangular systems with high accuracy and was puzzling since one actually does so in practice. In summary, triangular systems of equations are generally solved to high accuracy in spite of being, in general, ill-conditioned. In a recent paper, the author of this proposal gave a possible explanation of the fact above relying on the fact that the backward error given by Wilkinson for back substitution yields(small) componentwise bounds. One can therefore deduce small error bounds for these solutions if the componentwise condition number of the data (instead of the normwise previously considered) was used. This paper showed small expected value for this componentwise condition number. Recently, however, the suitability of this average analysis to reflect performance of algorithmic practice was questioned. The objection raised is that the probability distribution underlying these analyses -usually, a centered isotropic Gaussian- is chosen because of technical reasons and not because it models "the real world." Consequently, it may well happen that the resulting estimates are too optimistic, just as worst-case analysis is often claimed to be too pessimistic. The proposed alternative, smoothed analysis, interpolates between worst-case and average analyses. The goal of this project is to provide a smoothed analysis of the componentwise condition number of triangular systems which would yield, as a consequence, a smoothed analysis of the loss of precision (the difference between the number of correct digits in the data and in the computed solution) for the solution of triangular systems of equations. 摘要：儘管三角方程系統是病態系統，但一般能得到高精度解。在最近的一篇論文中，本計劃書的作者通過給出線性方程系統分量式條件數的期望值來解釋這種情況。 這種平均分析的適用性最近遭到了質疑。反對意見是這些分析背後的概率分佈﹙通常是一個居中的同向性高斯分佈﹚的選擇是出於技術上的原因而並非對“真實世界”的建模。這裡提議的另一種選擇，平滑分析，介於最壞情形分析和平均分析之間。 這個項目的目標是提供三角線性系統分量式條件數的平滑分析。

101113.label: Project Objectives
101113.value: Construction of a smooth path that leads to a perfect equilibrium: Every Nash equilibrium of a perturbed game with the perturbing probability ε is an ε-perfect equilibrium. This property together with the multilinear form of the payoff function will be fully exploited in the construction of the path. We will first introduce an extra variable in between zero and one to obtain a barrier payoff function from an appropriate convex combination of a barrier term with the payoff function. Then, we will define a barrier game that deforms from a trivial game to the original game when the extra variable varies from one to zero. Corresponding to each positive value of the extra variable, we will form a perturbed game of the original game. The barrier term will force Nash equilibrium of the barrier game to stay in the interior of the perturbed strategy space. For any given sufficiently small positive value of the extra variable, the corresponding coefficient of the barrier term satisfies that each Nash equilibrium of the barrier game closely approximates some Nash equilibrium of the perturbed game. To ensure the existence of a smooth path that leads to a perfect equilibrium, a perturbation term will be subtracted and Sard’s and implicit function theorems will be applied. The key technical issues to tackle are the convergence of the path to a perfect equilibrium and finiteness of the path length. Development of an efficient predictor-corrector method to numerically follow the smooth path: To numerically follow the smooth path to a perfect equilibrium, we will first parameterize each point on the path with the corresponding path length. A system of differential equations will then be formulated to characterize the path. To solve the system, an efficient predictor-corrector method will be proposed by taking advantage of the special structures of the problem. The emphasis will be on numerical stability and efficiency. The sparsity of the problem will be exploited in the Cholesky factorization. When the value of the extra variable is sufficiently close to zero, the numerical instability may happen. To deal with this problem, we will utilize the preconditioning techniques as in interior-point methods. The key technical issue to tackle is the estimation of the step length in the predictor step. Adaption of a simplicial path-following method for computing a perfect equilibrium: Nash equilibrium can be formulated as a stationary point problem. Based on the stationary point formulation of a perturbed game, a continuous mapping can be defined on the perturbed strategy space such that a strategy profile is a Nash equilibrium of the perturbed game if and only if it is a fixed point of the mapping. By introducing a homotopy parameter in between zero and one, a homotopy function can be defined to deform from a trivial game to the original game as the parameter varies from one to zero. When zero is a regular value of the homotopy function, a connected component of zero points of the homotopy function forms a piecewise smooth path that starts from a totally mixed strategy profile and leads to a perfect equilibrium at the limit. To numerically follow this path, a triangulation of continuous refinement of grid size will be constructed to define a piecewise linear path and a simplicial method will be adapted for numerically following the path. The key technical issue to address is how to refine the grid size so that the piecewise linear path can lead to a perfect equilibrium. Implementation of the interior-point path-following method and numerical comparisons: When the method is successfully developed in the proposed research, we will code it in both MATLAB and C++. To numerically compare the method with the existing generic approach to perfect equilibrium, we will also code the state-of-the-art methods for computing Nash equilibria of a sequence of the perturbed games. Extensive numerical tests will be carried out in a systematic way. A software package of the method will be made available in both MATLAB and C++ for the applications. The key technical issue to address is how to reduce the amount of computation of the expected payoff for a game with many players and many pure strategies for each player.

101113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
101113.value: As a powerful mechanism for conflict modeling and decision analysis, game theory has been successfully applied in a variety of fields including biology, economics, engineering, and political science. The concept of Nash equilibrium is one of the most important and elegant ideas in game theory. Nevertheless, as pointed out in the literature, a game can have many Nash equilibria, and some of these equilibria may be inconsistent with intuitive notions about what should be the outcome of a game. To reduce this ambiguity and eliminate some of these counterintuitive equilibria, the concept of perfect equilibrium was introduced in game theory. With this refinement of Nash equilibrium, game theory has significantly advanced. The computation of perfect equilibrium plays an important role in the applications. The existing generic approach to perfect equilibrium is to compute Nash equilibria for a sequence of perturbed games and obtain a perfect equilibrium from a limit of these equilibria. However, such an approach can be very time-consuming. To compute Nash equilibrium, path-following methods have been proposed and numerical performance shows that these methods are very efficient. Unfortunately, no such method exists for perfect equilibrium in general. This deficiency naturally leads to the question: Can a path-following method be found for computing perfect equilibrium? The search for an answer to this challenging question is the motive for the proposed research. This project aims to develop an interior-point path-following approach to computing perfect equilibrium of a finite n-person game in normal form. The basic idea of the approach is to closely approximate a perturbed game by incorporating a barrier term into each player’s payoff function with an appropriate convex combination. The emphasis will be on fully exploiting the multilinear form of the payoff function and differentiability of the problem in the development. As in interior-point methods, we will construct a smooth path that starts from a totally mixed strategy profile and leads to a perfect equilibrium. The existence of the path will be ensured with the subtraction of a perturbation term and an application of Sard’s and implicit function theorems. To numerically follow the path, an efficient predictor-corrector method will be proposed by taking advantage of the special structures and sparsity of the problem. Numerical comparisons with the existing generic approach will be carried out in a systematic way. The ultimately expected outcome of the project is an effective and efficient interior-point path-following method for computing perfect equilibrium.

101113.label: Realisation of objectives
101113.value: By introducing an extra variable ranging between zero and one, we formulate a perturbed game such that every Nash equilibrium of the perturbed game is an epsilon-perfect equilibrium of the original game. To make use of this perturbed game and fully exploit differentiability of the problem, we define a barrier payoff function for each player from a convex combination of a logarithmic barrier term and the player’s payoff function. An application of the barrier payoff function leads to a barrier game that deforms from a trivial game to the original game as the extra variable descends from one to zero. The logarithmic barrier term forces every Nash equilibrium of the barrier game to stay in the interior of the strategy space of the perturbed game. Since the equilibrium system of the barrier game is completely characterized by a finite number of polynomials, an error bound theorem in the literature guarantees that, when the extra variable is sufficiently small, the corresponding coefficient of the barrier term is so small that every Nash equilibrium of the barrier game closely approximate to some epsilon-perfect equilibrium of the original game, provided that the power of the extra variable is large enough. An application of the well-known Sard’s theorem and implicit function theorem shows that there exists a smooth path to a perfect equilibrium. A predictor-corrector method is adapted for numerically following the smooth path. To enhance the performance of the method, sparsity of the problem has been fully explored in the implementation. Numerical experiments further demonstrate that the path indeed leads to a perfect equilibrium. As an extension of a structure theorem in the literature, we attain an equivalent reformulation of Nash equilibrium to a perturbed game, which continuously deforms from a trivial game to the original game as an extra variable varies from one to zero. An application of this reformulation leads to a homotopy mapping on the Euclidean space instead of the product of simplices. With this mapping, we construct a path that starts from an arbitrary point in the space and ends at a perfect equilibrium. To numerically follow this path, we develop a simplicial path-following method for approximating perfect equilibria. The method is derived from an application of a triangulation of arbitrary refinement of grid sizes and a piecewise-linear approximation of the homotopy mapping. It is shown with an error bound theorem in the literature that every limit point of the simplicial path yields a perfect equilibrium. Numerical results further confirm the effectiveness of the simplicial method.

101113.label: Major findings and research outcome
101113.value: To determine a perfect equilibrium, the logistic version of quantal response equilibrium has been extended to a perturbed game. As a result of this extension, a smooth path has been constructed for computing perfect equilibria. The path starts from an arbitrary totally mixed strategy profile and leads to a perfect equilibrium. A predictor-corrector method has been adapted for numerically trace the path and an interior-point path-following method has been successfully developed for computing perfect equilibria in [6]. The computation of perfect equilibrium plays an important role in the applications of game theory. A perfect equilibrium of a finite n-person game in normal form is a limit of a sequence of epsilon_k-perfect equilibria of the game with epsilon_k>0 as epsilon_k approaches zero. For any given epsilon_k>0, to find all epsilon_k-perfect equilibria of a bimatrix game, a mixed-integer linear program is formulated in the project. To solve this mixed-integer program, a fixed-point iterative method for integer programming has been developed in [1]. The method is able to find all integer solutions of an integer program. Furthermore, the method can naturally be implemented in a distributed way, which significantly reduces the amount of computation. Risk-neutral density (RND) is a fundamental concept in asset pricing. Inspired by the idea developed in this project, a more effective nonparametric method has been proposed in [2] for estimating the RND from a set of European option bid-ask quotes based on a linear programming support vector machine regression. The method allows us to fit beyond the range of data and to incorporate all the shape constraints and thus always gives an arbitrage-free density with full tails. The newsvendor model has many applications in practices. Stimulated from the results attained in this project, the conditional value-at-risk measure is incorporated into the decision framework of the newsvendor who aims to minimize opportunity loss in [3]. Switched systems are an important class of hybrid systems that can be efficiently used to model a number of systems. Motivated by the basic scheme of this project, the perturbed equilibrium systems have been formulated to tackle the problems in [4] and [5]. The studies on these switched systems will yield important applications of the methods proposed in this project. The research on augmented Lagrangian objective penalty function, compacted decision tables based attribute reduction, fuzzy-rough feature selection accelerator and fuzzy granular structure distance has been carried out in [7], [8], [9], [10].

101113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
101113.value: The idea formulated in this project can be extended to variational inequality problems to compute refinements of stationary points. One can first formulate a perturbed variational inequality problem and define a barrier variational inequality problem such that there exists a path of stationary points, which starts a unique solution and leads to a perfect stationary point. Then a predictor-corrector method can be adapted for numerically tracing the path to a perfect stationary point.

101113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
101113.value: Game theory has been widely applied in economic analysis. In these applications, the computation of Nash equilibrium plays an essential role. As a refinement of Nash equilibrium, perfect equilibrium is a more rational Nash equilibrium. This project has developed an effective and efficient interior-point path-following method for computing a perfect equilibrium. The method has fully exploited differentiability of the problem. By introducing an extra variable for deforming from a trivial game to the original one, a smooth interior-point path has been constructed, which leads to a perfect equilibrium. Sard’s theorem and perturbations have been applied to derive the existence of the path. An efficient predictor-corrector method has been adapted for numerically tracing the smooth path to a perfect equilibrium. Comprehensive numerical experiments have been carried out to show the effectiveness and efficiency of the method. The research of the project will further promote the applications of game theory.

101713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
101713.value: This project is concerned with the development of efficient catalysts that can activate nitrate, nitrite and nitrous oxide to selectively oxidize a variety of organic functional groups under mild conditions. These nitrogen species are reasonably strong oxidants that form part of the biological nitrogen cycle that is important to life on earth: NO3– → NO2– → NO → N2O → N2; these processes are utilized by some anaerobic bacteria for energy generation. Each redox step in this cycle is catalyzed by a metalloenzyme that contains Mo, Fe or Cu. Inspired by the action of these enzymes; we are interested to make use of these redox steps to carry out efficient catalytic oxidation of various organic substrates under mild conditions using various transition metal complexes as catalysts. Nitrate and nitrite are reasonably cheap, and N2O is also readily available as a byproduct of the industrial manufacture of nylon. Moreover, in principle it is possible to design catalytic processes based on NO3–, NO2– and N2O that ultimately generate N2 as the product, so these are potentially green processes. However, so far there are few efficient catalytic systems based on these nitrogen species. In addition, because of the intensive use of nitrogen fertilizers, NO3– and NO2– have become serious pollutants in water and understanding how they can be reduced efficiently is also of environmental interest. In this project we will also investigate metal-catalyzed oxidation of organic substrates by perchlorate, because ClO4– have similar properties as the nitrogen oxyanions and the strategies that so we will use to activate the nitrogen oxyanions should also be applicable to perchlorate. Although perchlorate is also a relatively strong oxidant, it is very inert in aqueous solutions under ambient conditions, and at room temperature it reacts with reasonable rates only with a few reducing agents. Moreover, because of the extensive use of perchlorate as an oxidant in rockets and explosives, there is widespread occurrence of harmful perchlorate in the environment, hence understanding how perchlorate can be efficiently reduced is also of environmental interest. Our project should contribute to fundamental understanding of the activation of nitrate, nitrite, nitrous oxide, perchlorate and related closed-shell oxyanions by transition metal complexes. It should also lead to the development of new and green catalytic methods for the selective oxidation of organic substrates. 本項目旨在開發能在溫和條件下通過活化硝酸鹽、亞硝酸鹽以及一氧化二氮來選擇氧化各種有機官能團的催化劑。這些氮化物具有比較強的氧化性，是生物界中氮循環：NO3– → NO2– → NO → N2O → N2的重要組成部分，一些厭氧細菌就是利用這一循環過程獲取能量。氮循環中，每一步都由含Mo、Fe 或 Cu的金屬酶催化完成。受這些金屬酶催化的啓發，我們對這些氧化還原過程非常感興趣，希望開發出有效的過渡金屬催化劑，在溫和條件下能夠催化氧化各種有機底物。硝酸鹽和亞硝酸鹽相當便宜，N2O是工業上生成尼龍的副産品，也很容易獲得。設計催化劑，用于催化以NO3–、NO2– 以及 N2O爲氧化劑的反應，並將這些含氮氧化物最終轉化爲N2，理論上是可行的。但是，目前能有效催化這些含氧氮化物進行反應的催化體系很少。此外，由于氮肥的大量使用，NO3–和NO2–已對水造成了很嚴重的汙染。因此，探索還原消除NO3–和NO2–的有效方法對保護環境也具有重要意義。 高氯酸根（ClO4–）與含氮氧化物（NO3– 、 NO2– ）具有類似的化學性質，可用于催化含氮氧化物（NO3– 、 NO2– ）反應的催化劑，也有可能適用于高氯酸根。因此，本項目也將開展金屬催化高氯酸鹽氧化有機底物的研究。雖然高氯酸鹽是很強的氧化劑，但是在室溫下，其水溶液相當惰性，很少有還原劑能將其還原。除此之外，由于高氯酸鹽廣泛用于火箭燃料以及爆炸物中，環境中已經存在大量有害的ClO4–，因此，探索還原消除ClO4–的有效方法對環境保護也具有重要意義。 本項目的研究成果，不僅有助于闡明過渡金屬配合物活化硝酸鹽、亞硝酸鹽、一氧化二氮、高氯酸鹽以及相應的含氧酸根的機理，而且有利于開發氧化有機物的新型綠色催化反應。

101713.label: Major findings and research outcome
101713.value: We have investigated the use of various oxoanions, including perochlorate (ClO4-), periodate (IO4-), nitrate (NO3-) and (NO2-) as oxidants for various organic substrates. Various transition metal complexes have been employed as catalysts for these reactions, including [RuL2(OH2)2]2+ (L = 6,6’-dichloro-2,2’-bipyridine or 2,9-dimethyl-1,10-phenanthroline), [OsVI(N)(L)(CH3OH)]+ (L = N,N’-bis(salicylidene)-o-cyclohexyldiamine dianion) and [Mn(N)(CN)4]2-. The results are summarized below. 1. The oxidation of various alkanes and alcohols catalyzed by [Mn(N)(CN)4]2- using periodate as terminal oxidant at room temperature has been investigated. In catalytic alkane oxidation excellent yields of alcohols and ketones (>95%) are obtained with a maximum turnover of 3000, while in catalytic alcohol >90% conversions and yields can be achieved (Chem. Asian J. 2016, 11, 2846-2848). 2. The osmium(VI) nitrido complex, [OsVI(N)(L)(CH3OH)]+ (1, L = N,N’-bis(salicylidene)-o-cyclohexyldiamine dianion) was tested as a catalyst for the oxidation of alkanes by various oxoanions, but it was not very active. However, it was found to be an efficient catalyst for the oxidation of alkanes at ambient conditions using H2O2 as the oxidant. Alkanes are oxidized to the corresponding alcohols and ketones, with yields up to 75% and turnover number up to 2230. Experimental and computational studies are consistent with a mechanism that involves O-atom transfer from H2O2 to [OsVI(N)(L)]+ to generate an [OsVIII(N)(O)(L)]+ active intermediate (Chem. Commun., 2015, 51, 13686-13689). 3. In an attempt to understand the mechanism of O-atom transfer from oxoanion to various substrates, the kinetics and mechanism of the reaction of a ruthenium(VI) nitrido Complex with HSO3- and SO32- in aqueous solution have been investigated (Chem. Eur. J. 2016, 22, 10754-10758). 4. The use of [RuL2(H2O)2]2+ as catalyst for the oxidation of hydrocarbons using various oxoanions has been studied. When ClO4- was used as oxidant, >30% of the oxidized products can be obtained. On the other hand, these catalysts are less active using when NO3- and NO2- as oxidants.

101713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
101713.value: In future, more efficient catalysts based on earth-abundant metal complexes such as those of iron, cobalt and nickel should be developed. Also, more organic substrates such as alkenes, alcohols and amines should be studied. The use of various Lewis acids, such as Zn2+, Al3+, Sc3+, to activate inorganic oxoanions should also be investigated

101713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
101713.value: Perchlorate, nitrate and nitrite and various other oxoanions are widespread contaminants in ground and surface waters. All these oxoanions are reasonably strong oxidants thermodynamically. In nature, there are enzymes such as perchlorate reductase, nitrate reductase and nitrite reductase that can efficiently reduce perchlorate, nitrate and nitrite to chlorate, nitrite and nitrous oxide, respectively. In chemistry, there are few examples of catalysts that can make use of these these inorganic oxyanions to do organic oxidation. In this project, we have developed some efficient catalysts for the oxidation of a number of organic substrates using various inorganic oxoanions. Our work should provide insights into the development of efficient catalysts for removing oxoanion contaminants from water by converting them into useful products.

102013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
102013.value: Metallic glasses (MGs), as a new emerging class of metallic materials, have attracted extensive scientific and technological interests because of their unique mechanical and physical properties, including extremely high strength, large elastic strain limit, superior magnetic properties, etc. In spite of these promising properties, their widespread applications are limited primarily due to the inhomogeneous deformation localized in extremely thin shear band (~10 nm), displaying catastrophic failure with little plasticity. Over the past years, remarkable efforts have been devoted to revealing the shear banding (SB) mechanism of MGs; however, most of them are based on macroscopic approaches with low instrument resolutions plus with the cast defects in macro-specimens, making the intrinsic behavior of SB blurred, thus the mechanism of SB is still far from fully understood, while, nanoindentation, with nanoscale resolution, offers us an excellent opportunity to tackle this nano-localized process. This proposed research is aiming at elucidating the physical origin of the dynamics and stability of SB. We intend to develop a scientific scheme to bridge the gap between the SB dynamic process and the atomic structure of MGs through a combination of the state-of-the-art experimental techniques and theoretical calculations. Based on the experimental and simulation outcomes from MGs, we plan to extend the research to SB of borosilicate glasses, with the ultimate goal to establish a unified SB theory for glass materials with amorphous structures. Relatively soft/ductile Zr50Cu40Al10 and strong/brittle Fe71Nb6B23 MGs will be chosen to investigate the fundamentals of the SB dynamics and stability through a systematical adjustment of loading stress, strain rate and test temperature during microcompression tests. Using high-resolution TEM and AFM rearrangement of atomic clusters in shear band will be scrutinized. Also, surface coating will be used to monitor SB dynamics and stability, and to enhance the plasticity of MGs. Furthermore, by extending the research to include borosilicate glasses, we will attempt to establish a unified SB theory for metallic and oxide glasses. Besides the systematic experimental studies, we will perform molecular dynamics simulations to probe the atomic-scale structural evolution during SB. These comprehensive investigations coupled with our core-shell structural model will allow us to approach the physical origin of SB dynamics and stability. The implementation of this proposal will expect to lead to an in-depth understanding the SB dynamics and stability of glass materials with amorphous structures. Furthermore, it will provide a scientific guidance for the design of ductile MGs for engineering use. 金属玻璃作为一种高新金属材料，具有独特的力学与物理特性，例如极高的强度和弹性极限，优异的磁特性等等，在各个领域中都有广泛应用，因而引起人们极大的研究兴趣。然而，限制这种材料进一步应用的是其不均匀的塑性变形。塑性变形局域化在非常薄的剪切带（~10nm）中進行，宏观表现为脆性断裂。为了揭露其剪切带变形机理，在过去的几十年里，人们开展了很多工作， 然而由于宏观手段分辨率低，试样中的铸造缺陷等等因素掩盖了真实的剪切带信息，因此还是没有完全理解其变形机理。我们这项研究的目标是探究剪切带变形动力学与稳定性的物理本源。通过结合最先进的微观实验手段和理论计算，试图发展一个科学方案以架起剪切带变形动态过程与内部原子结构演变之间的联系；进一步延伸到硼硅酸盐玻璃的剪切带变形，以最终为所有的玻璃材料建立一个统一的剪切带变形机理。 实验选取相对软/韧的 Zr50Cu40Al10同硬/脆的Fe71Nb6B23金属玻璃，通过改变微压缩过程中加载应力，应变速率，试验温度来系统研究剪切带变形动力学与稳定性的基本原理，通过动态原子力显微镜同高分辨透射电镜来观察剪切带中原子结构信息。进一步，研究延伸到硼硅酸盐玻璃剪切带变形，试图为金属与氧化物玻璃建立一个统一的剪切变形理论。除了系统的实验，我们还会开展分子动力学计算来探究剪切带中原子尺度结构演化。以上综合全面的研究工作加上我们原先提出的结构模型会让我们更加清楚认识剪切带变形动力学与稳定性的物理本质。

102013.label: Realisation of objectives
102013.value: The three objectives of the project have been successfully achieved. Through the research funding, we have published 6 journal papers including the top journals such as Scientific Reports, Applied Physics Letters and International Journal of Plasticity. On the experimental side, the effects of various intrinsic(composition, atomic structure, et al) and extrinsic factors (sample size, strain rate and testing machine stiffness) on dynamics and stability of shear banding in MGs are elucidated(Hu et al Intermetallics, 2015). The key parameter controlling the intermittent shear banding process or serrated flow of metallic glasses (MGs) are found. The critical velocity criterion on the stability of shear banding of various MGs was also determined and reported(Sun et al, Sci. Rep. 2016). We also found a delayed shear banding behavior at the micro-scale deformation of MGs, which is closely related with the spatial evolution of plastic flow units in MGs below the yield stress (Sun et al, App. Phys. Lett, 2014). On the theoretical side, a unified theoretical model describing the stick-slip shear band dynamics is established and successfully explain the experimental results. The instability of shear banding process is also rationalized with the continuum theory of liquid instability. In addition, a theoretical model on the spatial evolution of plastic flow units and the initiation of shear banding is also constructed based on the results of micro-scale deformation results of MGs(Sun et al, App. Phys. Lett, 2014). The insights extracted from shear banding process in MGs are further extended to the deformation behavior of MG-based structures (such as Cu-coating and their composites) and other glasses(Sun et al, Sci. Rep. 2016; Sun et al, Inter. J. Plasticity, 2016). Combined these findings, one can have a physical picture on the dynamics and stability of shear banding process in MGs and other glassy materials and structures. More importantly, These results are helpful to control and design the plasticity of MG and other glassy materials and provide important insights on physical nature of shear banding process which may encounter in many amorphous materials.

102013.label: Major findings and research outcome
102013.value: Through the research fund, there are several major findings, which have been published in international journals: 1. we experimentally studied the variation of serrated flow with different MG compositions, sample size and deformation strain rates and testing machine stiffness. It was found that the serrated flow depends highly on these factors, suggesting a strong dependence of shear band dynamics on various intrinsic and extrinsic factors. Based on these results, We also proposed a theoretical model on the stick-slip shear band dynamics proposed a unified theoretical parameter. Further, based on the stick-slip dynamics of a single shear band, we also first measured the maximum velocity that a shear band could reach during the plastic deformation until the final fracture for BMGs under various conditions (90 samples in total), and found the velocity values of shear banding approach a constant value (~1.5±0.4 ×10-4 m.s-1). The critical shear banding velocity also indicates that shear banding is liquid-type instability process. In addition, the correlation between initiation of shear banding and the evolution of flow units with the microcompress tests of a Zr-based MG is also studied. 2. We studied the mechanical behavior of the commonly used oxide glasses-Pyrex with room-temperature and elevated-temperature compression tests. It was found that the strength and ductility of the glass is increased at temperatures as high as 837 K, However, the deformation behavior is essentially controlled by microcrack propagation, instead of nucleation of shear bands. It can be concluded that the macroscaopic deformation and fracture of Pyrex is crack controlled rather than shear-band controlled at a quite wide temperature range from room temperature to elevated temperatures, the behavior of which is actually different from that in metallic glasses. 3. We studied that the origin of shear stability enhancement of MGs by Cu-coating. We found that the shear instability enhancement by coating mainly comes from the interaction between the coating layer and serrated flow events. The thin soft metal coating layer plays a key role in stopping the final catastrophic fracture of MGs by slowing down shear band dynamics, thus enhance the shear stability and plasticity of MGs. The quantitative stress analysis showed that the enhanced shear stability mainly comes from the lateral tension of coating layer induced by the surface shear step. The interface bonding between the coating layer and MGs rather than the layer thickness, is found to play a key role in the shear stability enhancement.

102013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
102013.value: Further development of the research can be directed to use shear banding dynamics and stability extracted from the research of the project to design the ductility and mechanical behavior of MGs and their composites. This involves a clear understanding of the correlation between shear banding and the atomic structure of MGs. Mechanical tests at micro/nano-scales are still needed to see whether the oxide glass could intrinsically exhibit plastic flow or shear banding behavior similar to metallic glasses. Some of the research is now being undertaken in my laboratories and some of the preliminary results obtained to date are very interesting and promising.

102013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
102013.value: Shear banding plays a central role in the mechanical behavior of MGs and thus the understanding of origin of shear banding dynamics and stability is important for designing and controlling the ductility of new MGs and their composites. However, due to the highly localization of shear banding, characterizing the shear banding process during the deformation is blurred. By advanced structural and mechanical techniques and utilizing the intermittent serrated flow process, we successfully studied the physical origin of shear banding dynamics and stability as well as their dependence on the atomic structure and extrinsic factors. A unified theoretical model for shear band dynamics is proposed and the critical parameter controlling the shear banding stability is found. The insights extracted from shear banding process in MGs are further extended to the deformation behavior of MG-based structures (such as Cu-coating and their composites) and other glasses. These results are helpful to control and design the plasticity of MG and other glassy materials and provide important insights on physical nature of shear banding process.

102613.label: Project Title(Chinese)
102613.value: 關於非綫性抛物數值解的一個新的分析方法

102613.label: Project Objectives
102613.value: With the new approach, we first study two popular physical equations, the thermistor system from electrical conduction and the incompressible miscible flow in porous media. We will introduce an elliptic time-discrete system for each linearized scheme and analyze the error and regularity of the solution of the elliptic system. The key issue is the unconditionally optimal error analysis of several linearized Galerkin type FEMs, including linearized backward Euler scheme and linearized Crank-Nicolson scheme, while previous analysis always requires certain restrictions on the time stepsize. The time stepsize restriction becomes more serious when a problem in a three-dimensional space is studied and/or numerical methods with a non-uniform mesh is used. A systematic numerical simulation for several practical models, different time intergations and different spatial appromations will be presented to confirm our theoretical analysis. Finally we intend to introduce a framework to handle a large class of nonlinear parabolic PDEs, several popular spatial approximations (FEM, FV or FD) and time integrations. Under the framework, unconditionally (or almost unconditionally) optimal error estimates will be investigated for a general form of nonlinear parabolic systems.

102613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
102613.value: Many physical phenomena can be described by time-dependent parabolic partial differential equations. Due to the nature of the evolution, a stable numerical approximation to the time integration in nonlinear time-dependent PDEs is always a key issue in developing efficient numerical methods and their theoretical analysis. However, a time stepsize condition was often required in previous analysis for many numerical methods. The time-step restriction may result in extremely time-consuming in solving various physical problems. The aim of this project is to develop a new approach to analyze several popular numerical methods for a large class of nonlinear parabolic PDEs and establish unconditionally optimal error estimates. Our approach may provide a new understanding on the commonly-used schemes and clear up the misgivings for the time stepsize restriction in practical computations.

102613.label: Major findings and research outcome
102613.value: During this period, we focused on the time-step condition of commonly-used linearized semi-implicit schemes for nonlinear parabolic PDEs with Galerkin finite element approximations. In particular, we studied the following three nonlinear physical equations. 1. We studied the time-dependent nonlinear Joule heating equations (thermistor equations). We present optimal error estimates of the semi-implicit Euler scheme in both the $L^2$ norm and the $H^1$ norm without any time-step restriction. Theoretical analysis is based on a new splitting of error function and precise analysis of a corresponding time-discrete system. The method used here is applicable for more general nonlinear parabolic systems and many other linearized (semi)-implicit time discretizations for which previous works often require certain restriction on the time-step size $tau$. 2. We studied a class of linearized Crank-Nicolson Galerkin finite element methods for the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau (TDGL) equations under the Lorentz gauge. We present an optimal error estimate for the linearized scheme (almost) unconditionally ($i.e.$, when the spatial mesh size $h$ and the temporal step $tau$ are smaller than a given constant), while previous analyses were given only for some schemes with strong restrictions on the time step-size. The key to our analysis is the boundedness of the numerical solution in certain strong norm. We prove the boundedness for the cases $tau > h$ and $tau < h$, respectively. The former is obtained by a simple inequality, with which the error functions at a given time level are bounded in terms of their average at two consecutive time levels, and the latter follows a traditional way with the induction/inverse inequality. Numerical examples were investigated to confirm our theoretical analysis and to show clearly that no time-step condition is needed. 3. We also studied a class of fully discrete Galerkin-Galerkin FEMs for incompressible miscible flow in porous media, which has wide applications in oil and ground water industries. During the project, we presented a systematic numerical simulations for both two and three-dimensional flow models. Numerical results show the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed methods and the unconditional convergence.

102613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
102613.value: In this project, we mainly focused on unconditional stability and convergence of commonly-used linearized Galerkin FEMs for nonlinear parabolic equations. The time stepsize restriction also arises in numerical hyperbolic equations and parabolic-hyperbollic system. Extension to a system of parabolic-hyperbollic equations is of high interest.

102613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
102613.value: Due to the nature of the evolution, a stable numerical approximation to the time integration in nonlinear time-dependent PDEs is always a key issue in developing efficient numerical methods and their theoretical analysis. A fully discrete method consists of an approximation in time direction and an approximation in spatial direction, which are measured by the stepsizes in these two directions. However, a time stepsize condition $ tau < h^{alpha}$ for some $alpha>0$ was often required in previous analysis for fully discrete numerical methods. The time-step restriction may result in extremely time-consuming in solving various physical problems. A new temporal-spatial error splitting has been proposed to analyze several popular numerical methods for a large class of nonlinear parabolic PDEs and to establish unconditionally optimal error estimates. Our approach may provide a new understanding on the commonly-used schemes and clear up the misgivings for the time stepsize restriction in practical computations.

103313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
103313.value: We will investigate the problem of a highly viscous material experiencing external heating. We will consider materials whose surface tension coefficient and viscosity depend strongly on the temperature. Problems of this type present a number of theoretical and numerical challenges. This is because of complicated nonlinear interactions between the temperature, the surface tension, viscous and inertial forces and the rate of heat absorption. These can lead to a number of challenges including singularities, extremely long thin filaments and large temperature gradients. For cylindrical geometries, we will develop a set of long-wavelength partial differential equations based on the small Biot number approximation (which ensures that the radial temperature variations across the cylinder are small). We will use these equations to theoretically study the way in which uniform heating and cooling affect the linear growth of perturbations of uniform threads. We will then apply numerical methods to investigate the nonlinear evolution of the resulting instabilities. We will also consider the effects of non-uniform heating that will give rise to axial variations in the surface tension forces and hence drive fluid flow. In the limit of small inertia, we will use a Lagrangian formulation of the equations to derive some special analytical solutions. When inertia is non-negligible and/or for general types of heating we will obtain results using numerical techniques. We will then examine how all of the forces interact with externally imposed forces. For larger values of the Biot number we will numerically solve the full axisymmetric Navier-Stokes equations in order to understand the differences with the small Biot number dynamics. We will also generalize our results to other geometries and constitutive laws. 我們將研究高粘性材料在外加熱源的情況下的問題，我們將考慮的材料是粘性和表面張力都很強的依賴於溫度的情況。這類問題在數值和理論上帶來了極大的挑戰。這是由於溫度、表面張力、粘性力、慣性力以及熱吸收率之間復雜的非線性相互作用。這會給問題帶來一系列的挑戰，包括：奇異性、液柱局部變得極細以及很大的溫度梯度等。對於圓柱形幾何結構的液柱來說，我們從基於小Biot數的逼近出發得到了一組長波的偏微分方程組（這保證了徑向溫度的變化在整個圓柱面上都很小）。我們用這些方程組去研究一致加熱和一致冷卻給高度一致的長條液柱在小的線性擾動下帶來的影響。然後我們利用數值計算的方法去研究結果不穩定性的非線性發展過程。我們也考慮了非一致加熱的情況，這將會帶來表面張力在軸向的變化，因而驅動流動。在小雷諾數的極限下，我們利用原方程組的拉格朗日形式得到了一些特殊的解析解。而當雷諾數不可忽略或者在一般的熱源情況下，我們利用數值計算的技術來求解。我們將檢驗所有的力是如何與外界給定的力之間相互作用的。而對於大Biot數，為了了解清楚它與小Biot數情況的區別，我們將在數值上計算整個軸對稱的Navier-Stokes方程組。我們也將我們的結果推廣到其他的幾何結構和本構關系上。

103313.label: Major findings and research outcome
103313.value: We have considered the evolution of a long and thin vertically aligned axisymmetric viscous thread that is attached to a solid wall at its upper end, experiences gravity and is pulled at its lower end by a fixed force. As the thread evolves, it experiences either heating or cooling by its environment. We developed a framework that can deal with threads that have arbitrary initial shape, are non-uniformly preheated and experience spatially non-uniform heating or cooling from the environment during the pulling process. When inertia is completely neglected and the temperature of the environment is spatially uniform, we obtained analytic solutions for an arbitrary initial shape and temperature profile and determined the criteria for whether the cross-section of a given fluid element will ever become zero. We further show that the dynamics can be quite subtle and leads to surprising behaviour, such as non-monotonic behaviour in time and space. We also considered the effects of non-zero Reynolds number and showed that there is a subtle competition between three distinct mechanisms. In particular, for a thread with initially uniform radius and a spatially uniform environment but with a non-uniform initial temperature profile, pinching can occur either at the hottest point, at the points near large thermal gradients or at the pulled end, depending on the Reynolds number. Finally, we show that similar results can be obtained for a thread with initially uniform radius and uniform temperature profile but exposed to a spatially non-uniform environment. We also examined the extension of an axisymmetric viscous thread that is pulled at both ends with a prescribed speed such that the effects of inertia are initially small, but may or may not become larger when the thread becomes long and extended. We isolated two generic classes of initial thread shape and determined explicit asymptotic solutions while the effects of inertia remain small. We further showed that inertia will ultimately become important only if the long-time asymptotic form of the pulling speed is faster than a power law with a critical exponent. The critical exponent can take two possible values depending on the initial shape of the thread. We obtained expressions for the solution at large times in the case in which the critical exponent is exceeded. Despite the apparent simplicity of the problem, the solutions exhibit a surprisingly rich structure. Both the small-inertia solutions and the large-time asymptotic expressions compare well with numerical solutions.

103313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
103313.value: The two papers arising from this proposal derive two different frameworks that allow for the analysis of extending threads when thermal effects may become important. These are challenging problems because after sufficient extension the threads can develop extremely long and thin regions that are extremely difficult to deal with from a numerical point of view. We believe that this work will be extremely valuable to experimentalists who are using extensional techniques to create very narrow glass micro-electrode tips, optical microscopes and other glass devices. We are also extremely motivated to pursue research following up on the viscoelastic mechanics of such flows that is extremely important for polymer processing.

103313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
103313.value: We have developed a mathematical framework that can deal with the challenging problem of viscous threads that experience extensional forces. Such flows are challenging because long and thin regions can develop that are extremely difficult to deal both theoretically and numerically. Our framework allows us to consider the effects of heating and how temperature-dependent viscosity and surface tension can lead to extremely surprising behaviour. In particular, we showed that pinching of thread can occur under the competition of three very different mechanics that can lead to surprising behaviour as the inertia is varied. Moreover, we showed that the apparently very simple problem of a thread that is pulled by imposing a prescribed velocity at its end points can have extremely subtle behaviour. In particular, we showed that there are two different generic categories of initial shape that experience very different behaviour when they become sufficiently heavily stretched.

103413.label: Project Objectives
103413.value: To design and synthesize a class of multifunctional, fluorescent organic molecules featuring the desired geometric feature for building porous framework materials, as well as the chemical functions (e.g., pendant alkene groups) for the absorption and sensing of noble metal species. To assemble the synthesized multifunctional molecules into porous framework materials [e.g., using the chemically hard metal zirconium, Zr(IV) ion], and to achieve the desired properties of well-defined porosity and tailored-made chemical functions for noble metal uptake. For better stability and sensing capabilities of the prospective networks, we will also strive to install alkyne units within the pores for polymerization to form a polyacetylene subsidiary grid within the coordination host net. To examine and screen the assembled framework materials for fluorescent sensing of noble metal species from solution samples. We aim to systematically quantify and optimize the sensitivity and selectivity in noble metal detection: e.g., Pd, at ppm and sub-ppm levels and under broad solvent and pH range conditions.

103413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
103413.value: This project aims for highly efficient detection and retrieval of noble metal species— sprinkle a pinch of solid into the solution, look at the color change of the solid, and you know the type and concentration of the noble metal present—as simple as that. We will synergize the forefront technologies in the design and synthesis of porous solid state materials, and develop a class of robust and versatile organic-inorganic hybrid frameworks for the targeted applications. Compared with currently available techniques, the proposed materials and methodologies provide the practical advantages of being low-cost, environmentally friendly and highly reusable. The key idea is to install, within a robust porous solid state framework, the set of chemical functions that will specifically bind and respond to noble metal species. For this, we will synthesize molecular building blocks equipped with two distinct sets of organic functions: one is the chemically hard and hydrophilic carboxyls that favor chemically hard metal ions (e.g., Zr4+) and NOT the softer noble metal species; the other is the chemically soft alkene function that does prefer noble metal species. Thus, the hard carboxyl groups can be first engaged with a hard metal ion to form a well-ordered porous network based on the reversible metal-carboxylate coordination bonds, while the soft alkene groups remain free standing inside the pores. Because of the highly porous and large-surface-area characters of the solid state network, metal species from the solution will be able to quickly diffuse into the pores and access the chemical groups to trigger the color/emission changes for detection purposes. Moreover, the noble metal species thus trapped and concentrated can be immersion the loaded network solid in a solution containing stronger binders such as phosphine or chelating alkene molecules, in order to retrieve the noble metal species, and to recycle the original host network material. 本項目旨在研發一種高效能的檢測和回收貴金屬的技術。我們計劃整合多孔固體材料設計合成方面的前沿技術，開發一種機構穩定，性能優越的有機-無機雜化骨架材料，從而達到高效檢測的目標。和現有的檢測技術相比，我們計劃研發的材料和方法具有成本低，環保以及可循環使用的優點。 本技術的要點是在一種堅固的多孔骨架材料中引入專一有效的鍵合貴金屬的化學功能組合。為此，我們借助於有機分子和無機物之間的協同作用，這是一種近年來合成含可修飾集合構型和化學功能多孔功能材料的有效方法。更具體說來，就是採用軟-硬化學方法設計組裝了目標多孔材料，並在孔道內達到了理想的化學應用。本小組已經在這個新興領域進行了大量紮實有效的研究，為實現所提出的針對貴金屬的檢測技術提供了十分有利的條件。

103413.label: Realisation of objectives
103413.value: The key object “to optimize the sensitivity and selectivity in noble metal detection: e.g., Pd, at ppm and sub-ppm levels and under broad solvent and pH range conditions” was suc-cessfully accomplished in a Zr(IV)-based MOF single crystal platform based on a bis(allythio)terphenyl dicarboxylic linker (i.e., a UiO-68 derivative). The strong Zr(IV)-carboxylate bonds offer greater stability to water and acids, as compared with our previously reported Zn(II)-based systems. The readily accessible, large-sized single crystals also offers convenience in colorimetric detection of the targeted heavy metal species, which is a great advantage over the polycrystalline powder samples (i.e., the allylthio-tagged UiO-66 solid in paper No 1 attached) accomplished in the initial stage of this project. Also, the larger pore size of this MOF solid also allows better access to the allythio functions in the MOF matrix, further enhancing the sensitivity of the presence of Pd(II) and other noble metal analytes. The realization of objects 1 and 2 was highlighted by the improvement of ligand synthesis and crystallization. Previously, the thiol group had to be prepared from the phenol group using the Newman–Kwart arrangement of the O-aryl thiocarbamate precursor. Presently, in pursuing the research objectives of this GRF project, we have developed a much more efficient synthetic method for accessing the thiol function. Namely, we can now use the bromo substrate and subject it to nucleophilic substitution by thiomethoxide, followed by demethylation to give the thiol function. Moreover, we have also successfully obtained large single crystals of the MOF materials based on the linker molecules synthesized in this highly efficient protocol. Such single crystal platform, besides the aesthetic appeal (they look like gems), offers great operational advantages in colorimetric sensing applications under a variety of experimental conditions. With the improvement in linker synthesis and crystallization, we have therefore accomplished the proposed objects in an unexpectedly efficient manner. In other words, the proposed alkyne polymerization was not even needed for effecting the sensing performance, even though such polymerization remains of great scientific interest, and continues to be part of our ongoing pursuit (under auspices of ensuing research projects).

103413.label: Major findings and research outcome
103413.value: As stated above, one major discovery from this GRF project lies in the Zr(IV)-based MOF single crystal platform based on a bis(allythio)terphenyl dicarboxylic linker (i.e., a UiO-68 derivative), which offers a combination of advantages that are crucial for accomplishing the original objectives in noble metal sensing and detection applications. The following is a summary of these technologically advantageous properties of this newly discovered MOF material (these results have not be publicly disclosed, but will be submitted for publication in the near future). First, the strong Zr(IV)-carboxylate bonds offer greater stability to water and acids, as compared with our previously reported Zn(II)-based systems (these Zn-based MOFs are overly sensitive to moisture to be widely applicable for real-world sensing applications). The readily accessible, large-sized single crystals also offers convenience in colorimetric detection of the targeted heavy metal species, which is a great advantage over the polycrystalline powder samples (i.e., the allylthio-tagged UiO-66 solid in paper No 2 attached) accomplished in the initial stage of this project. Also, the larger pore size of this MOF solid also allows better access to the allythio functions in the MOF matrix, further enhancing the sensitivity of the presence of Pd(II) and other noble metal analytes. The development of this highly stable functional MOF material is culminated from our consistent effort in pursuing fundamental studies to improve stability and functionality of porous frameworks. Aside from the publication (paper 1 in attached) in the Midterm report to RGC, the fundamental exploration of this GRF project also led to a MOF system that is stable in boiling water, and features tunable white-emission that is valuable for various sensing applications (see paper 3). In addition, we have also explored the more stable covalent framework, and demonstrate the usefulness in reacting with metal ions, which is not only relevant for sensing applications but for catalytic properties as well (paper 4). The other findings in this modest-sized GRF project are related to the improvement of ligand synthesis and crystallization. Previously, the thiol group had to be prepared from the phenol group using the Newman–Kwart arrangement of the O-aryl thiocarbamate precursor. Presently, in pursuing the research objectives of this GRF project, we have developed a much more efficient synthetic method for accessing the thiol function. Namely, we can now use the bromo substrate and subject it to nucleophilic substitution by thiomethoxide, followed by demethylation to give the thiol function.

103413.value: With the improvement in linker synthesis and crystallization, we foresee a broad horizon for exploring the unique functionality of sulfur groups in the context of the technological applications of the porous solids of MOF materials. Specifically, for wider-ranging applications regarding catalysis and sensing, more robust systems based on harder metal ions such as the Zr(IV)-based MOFs demonstrated in this project should offer the crucial advantages in stability and functionality. Indeed, the improvement in linker synthesis and crystallization have led to the accomplishment of the proposed objects in an unexpectedly efficient manner. In other words, the proposed alkyne polymerization was not even needed for effecting the sensing performance, even though such polymerization remains of great scientific interest, and continues to be part of our ongoing pursuit (under auspices of ensuing research projects).
