103713.label: Realisation of objectives
103713.value: The objectives of the project have been fully addressed, the well-posedness of the Prandtl boundary layer equations have been studied in Sobolev space in both 3D and 2D settings, together with some instability results and generalization to compressible fluid. Precisely, as shown in the Section 6.2, the research outcome has been writing in six papers and among them, five papers have been published or accepted by international refereed journals that include the Archive for Rational Mechanics, Advances in Mathematics, etc. More precisely, to overcome the main difficulty in analysis caused by the secondary flow, we found a new structure constraint on the flow for well-posedness and also show that in the setting of perturbation of shear flow, such structure constraint is necessary for existence of solutions in the framework of Sobolev function spaces. In detail, the well-posedness of the three space dimensional Prandtl equations is studied under some constraint on its flow structure. Together with the instability result, it gives an almost necessary and sufficient structural condition for the stability of the three dimensional Prandtl equations.It reveals that the classical Burgers equation plays an important role in determining this type of flow with special structure, that avoids the appearance of the secondary flow, an unstabilizing factor n the three-dimensional Prandtl boundary layers. And the sufficiency of the monotonicity condition on the tangential velocity field for the existence of solutions to the Prandtl boundary layer equations is illustrated in the three dimensional setting. Moreover, it is shown that this structured flow is linearly stable for any three-dimensional perturbation. To see whether the structure constraint is too strong for proving solutions in the Sobolev space, we give an instability criterion for the Prandtl equations in three-dimensional space, which shows that the monotonicity condition of tangential velocity fields is not sufficient for the well-posedness of the three-dimensional Prandtl equations, in contrast to the classical well- posedness theory of the two-dimensional Prandtl equations under the Oleinik monotonicity assumption of the tangential velocity. Both of linear stability and nonlinear stability are considered. This criterion shows that the monotonic shear flow is linearly stable for the three-dimensional Prandtl equations if and only if the tangential velocity field direction is invariant with respect to the normal variable, and this result is an exact complement to the well-posedness theory for the three-dimensional Prandtl equations with a special structure. Furthermore, the global existence of weak solutions to the three space dimensional Prandtl equations is studied under some constraint on its structure. This is a continuation of our recent study on the local existence of classical solutions with the same structure condition. It reveals the sufficiency of the monotonicity condition on one component of the tangential velocity field and the favorable condition on pressure in the same direction that leads to global existence of weak solutions. This generalizes the result obtained by Xin-Zhang on the two-dimensional Prandtl equations to the three-dimensional setting. For further investigate the well-posedness theories in the framework of Sobolev spaces, we study the instability theories with general decay in the normal direction that shows that the decay in the normal direction does not help the existence theory in principle. Precisely, Motivated by the paper by Gerard-Varet and Dormy about the linear ill-posedness for the Prandtl equations around a shear flow with exponential decay in normal variable, and the recent study of well-posedness on the Prandtl equations in Sobolev spaces, we extend this result to the case when the shear flow has general decay. The key observation is to construct an approximate solution that captures the initial layer to the linearized problem motivated by the precise formulation of solutions to the inviscid Prandtl equations. Finally, some of these well-posedness theories have been generalized to compressible flow. For example, we study viscous layers and thermal layers for the two-dimensional non-isentropic compressible viscous flow with non-slip boundary condition in the small viscosity and heat conductivity limit. First, by multi-scale analysis, we derive the problems of viscous layer profiles and thermal layer profiles for different scales of viscosity and heat conductivity, from which we obtain the interaction mechanism of viscous layers and thermal layers. When the viscosity and heat conductivity go to zero at the same rate, the viscous layers and thermal layers are described by the Prandtl type equations for velocity fields coupled with a degenerate parabolic equation for the temperature. When the heat conductivity goes to zero faster than the viscosity, the viscous layer profiles satisfy the Prandtl type equations for velocity fields coupled with a transport equation for the temperature profile, and the thermal layer is much weaker, the temperature profile satisfies a nonlinear parabolic equation, and the velocity profiles are given explicitly in term of the temperature. When the viscosity goes to zero faster than the heat conductivity, the profiles of the thermal layer satisfy an inviscid Prandtl type equations coupled with a degenerate parabolic equation, and in the viscous layer, the velocity profiles satisfy the same boundary layer equations as in the isentropic flow. In addition, we also study the existence and stability of solutions to the problems of viscous layer profiles and thermal layer profiles, in the class of tangential velocity being strictly monotonic in the normal variable, for which we shall first introduce a generalized Crocco transformation to transform the above mentioned coupled and mixed type equations into degenerate parabolic systems, then to apply the Picard iteration. As a complimentary, we shall also introduce another direct energy approach to study these coupled and mixed type equations of viscous layers and thermal layers by taking the Nash-Moser-Hormander iteration scheme for nonlinear problems.

103713.label: Major findings and research outcome
103713.value: The research output was written in six papers with detail given as follows. In the first paper, under the strictly monotonic assumption on the tangential velocity in the normal variable, we apply the Nash-Moser-Hormander iteration scheme and further develop the approach introduced in our previous work to obtain the well-posedness of the equations locally in time for compressible Prandtl boundary layer equations. In the second paper, the global existence of weak solutions to the three space dimensional Prandtl equations is studied under some constraint on its structure. It reveals the sufficiency of the monotonicity condition on one component of the tangential velocity field and the favorable condition on pressure in the same direction that leads to global existence of weak solutions. In the third paper, we give an instability criterion for the Prandtl equations in three-dimensional space, which shows that the monotonicity condition of tangential velocity fields is not sufficient for the well-posedness of the three-dimensional Prandtl equations, in contrast to the classical well-posedness theory of the two-dimensional Prandtl equations under the Oleinik monotonicity assumption of the tangential velocity. This criterion is an exact complement to the fourth paper. In the fourth paper, the well-posedness of the three space dimensional Prandtl equations is studied under some constraint on its flow structure. Together with the instability result given in third paper, it gives an almost necessary and sufficient structural condition for the stability of the three dimensional Prandtl equations. Moreover, it is shown that this structured flow is linearly stable for three-dimensional perturbation. Motivated by the paper by Gerard-Varet and Dormy about the linear ill-posedness for the Prandtl equations around a shear flow with exponential decay in normal variable, and a recent study of well-posedness on the Prandtl equations in Sobolev spaces, this paper aims to extend the instability result to the case when the shear flow has general decay. The sixth paper is to study viscous layers and thermal layers for the two-dimensional non-isentropic compressible viscous flow with non-slip boundary condition in the small viscosity and heat conductivity limit. First, we derive the problems of viscous layer profiles and thermal layer profiles for different scales of viscosity and heat conductivity, from which we obtain the interaction mechanism of viscous layers and thermal layers. Then we study the existence and stability of solutions to the problems of viscous layer profiles and thermal layer profiles with monotonicity condition on the velocity field.

103713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
103713.value: The mathematical theories for Prandtl equations have been rapidly developed in recent years. The analytic techniques and approaches developed in this project can be applied to other related Prandtl-type systems, such as, the boundary layer equations for plasma governed by the MHD system, the coupled macroscopic and microscopic model, etc. Furthermore, we believe the well-posedness theories for these systems can be used for the study of high Reynolds numbers limit. Moreover, most of the mathematical theories for the Prandtl system are limited locally in time. Therefore, it is interesting to find out the optimal life span of solutions in different function spaces and the possibility of global existence of regular solutions.

103713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
103713.value: The study on fluid around a rigid body with high Reynolds number is an important problem both in physics and mathematics. The seminal work can be traced back to Prandtl in 1904 when he derived the Prandtl equations for boundary layer from the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with no-slip boundary condition. About sixty years after its derivation, a mathematical theory was developed by Oleinik that shows under the monotonicity condition on the velocity field, local in time well-posedness can be justified. This project aims to investigate whether classical solutions can persist for a long time so that we can study their large time behavior, or some kind of singularity will form so that the solutions will blowup in finite time in the setting of Sobolev spaces. Moreover, we will investigate the three space dimensional system. Here, notice that so far the global existence of weak solution in two space dimension was obtained under a favorable condition on the pressure in addition to the monotonicity condition on velocity. Moreover, almost all the existing mathematical theories are for two space dimensional problems. Hence, we believe that the progress made in the project enriches the mathematical theories of the Prandtl system.

103913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
103913.value: The development of highly active and energy efficient novel nanostructured photocatalysts is important in the field of photocatalysis science. Recently, some layered semiconductor materials such as graphite-like C3N4 and graphite oxides demonstrated tremendous potential in this regard due to their novel electronic structures. Their photocatalytic reaction dynamics and mechanisms as well as performance improvements require further extensive studies. Our present proposal will focus on electronic properties of layered semiconductor materials including graphite-like C3N4 and graphite oxides and effects of their structure modulations on photocatalytic reactivity by performing molecular level theoretical studies. By selective doping and/or surface functionalization, we modify and design the materials’ geometric and electronic structures at the molecular level. Their structure-determined physicochemical properties along with the factors governing them will be analyzed so as to identify approaches to improve their photocatalytic performance. Time-dependent density-functional theory calculations incorporating weak interlayer interactions will be applied to investigate the interaction of ionic adsorption on the surface as well as processes of charge transfer and catalytic reaction dynamics. In addition, to reveal the photocatalysis mechanism, we will examine the absorption spectra of the layered semiconductor materials whose excitation corresponds to the π-π* transition involving C-C bonds; we will also inspect fluorescence spectra resulted from the recombination of photo-generated electrons and holes. Based on their microstructures and the factors dictating their photocatalytic performance, we will unveil the physicochemical nature of this class of photocatalysis and improve the design of new photocatalytic materials with high reactivity and improved energy efficiency. 发展高活性和高效节能的新型纳米光催化剂在光催化领域至关重要。最近，一些诸如类石墨氮化碳和石墨氧化物的层状半导体材料由于其新颖的电子结构在这方面表现出巨大应用潜能。其光催化反应动力学和机制及性能改进尚需进一步研究。本项目重点对包括类石墨相C3N4和石墨氧化物的层状半导体材料的电子特性和其结构改性对光催化反应性的调制进行分子水平的理论研究。通过选择性掺杂及表面功能化，我们在分子水平上修改和设计材料的几何结构和电子结构。通过分析它们的结构相关的物理化学性质及其相关原理，找出改善其光催化性能的方法。将使用含时密度泛函理论并计及弱相互作用计算离子在表面的吸附以及电荷转移和催化反应动力学过程。此外，为了揭示光催化机制，我们将研究其涉及C-C键的π-π*跃迁激发对应的层状半导体材料的吸收光谱；我们亦将考查光生电子和空穴复合产生的荧光光谱。基于它们的微观结构和支配其光催化性能的因素，我们将揭示这类光催化的物理化学本质并设计具有高反应活性和高能量转换效率的新型光催化材料。

103913.label: Realisation of objectives
103913.value: In this project, we focus on electronic properties of layered semiconductor materials including graphite-like C3N4 and effects of their structure modulations on photocatalytic reactivity by performing molecular level theoretical and experimental studies. We modified and design the materials’ geometric and electronic structures at the molecular level and analized their structure-determined physicochemical properties along with the factors governing them so as to identify approaches to improve their photocatalytic performance. Based on first-principles calculations, we reveal that the interactions between extended-line-defects (ELDs) of type “585” (formed by five and eight membered rings) ELDs embedded in graphene can induce ordered magnetism and self-doping of graphene. By reducing the distance between 585 ELDs, a distinct charge transfer is predicted from the center of 585 ELDs to their edges, which induces a Dirac point shift below the fermi level, resulting in distance- or density-dependent n-type doping in the graphene. Relevant to the above finding, we found a distance-dependent spin polarization at the edges of 585 ELDs, attributable to the rigidity of the π electronic structure. Our finding suggests a promising approach for achieving n-type graphene for spintronic devices by creating 585 ELDs. We also investigated the thermal expansion behaviors of monolayer graphene and three configurations of graphene with point defects based on calculations using first-principles density functional theory. It was found that the thermal contraction of monolayer graphene is significantly decreased by point defects. Moreover, the corresponding temperature for negative linear thermal expansion coefficient with the maximum absolute value is reduced. The cause is determined to be point defects that enhance the mechanical strength of graphene and then reduce the amplitude and phonon frequency of the out-of-plane acoustic vibration mode. Such defect weakening of graphene thermal contraction will be useful in nanotechnology to diminish the mismatching or strain between the graphene and its substrate. Opening the band gap in graphene can significantly broaden its applications in electronic devices. By introducing four types of graphene-like carbon nitride (g-C3N4) as the substrate of graphene, we revealed, with first principles calculations, symmetry and size dependent band gap opening in graphene. On the one hand, for a substrate with a 3-fold rotational symmetry, a small C3N4 unit can cause a large value of the band gap in the graphene layer. On the other hand, the band gap also depends on the symmetry of the substrate. Our theoretical findings can pave the way for the use of graphene-based semiconductor devices. We have further obtained the new insight into pi-pi stacking involving remarkable orbital interactions in stacked layered structures. For more than half a century, despite intense theoretical and experimental exploration, no unified description of the factors contributing to π-π stacking interactions and its weak bonding process has been proposed. In this work, we showed that π-π stacking interactions involve considerable hybridizations of some of the orbitals. We proposed a unified model for the often nebulous π-π stacking process and its analogs: Firstly when the two monomers are too far apart, the dispersion effect will play the dominant role in bringing them together, but when they are too close, Pauli repulsion will force them apart. Secondly, at the equilibrium distance, electrostatic interaction, Pauli repulsion, dispersion and intermolecular orbital interaction are all pronounced, with part of the molecular orbitals of the two monomers interacting with each other to form a weak intermolecular bond. To understand the optical properties of carbon nitride quantum dots (CNQDs) which are emerging fluorescent material that promise numerous novel applications, we performed time-dependent density functional tight binding (TD-DFTB) calculations and showed that, due to the frontier molecular orbitals (FMOs) localization, CNQDs have superior carrier charge separation, sensitive to the size of the QD. Strong localization of the FMOs was observed in the first excited state due to the alteration of the structure where exciton sticks to the stretched C-N bonds regardless of the size of the QDs. The optical properties of CNQDs are sensitive to size and do not show strong variations with the shape of the QD. Our approach provides an explanation for the enhanced photocatalytic performance of CNQDs over graphene quantum dots (GQDs) and their characteristic exciton localization. Graphitic carbon nitride (g-CN) films are important components of optoelectronic devices, while the present techniques to produce them, such as drop casting and spin coating, fail to deliver uniform and pinhole–free g-CN films on solid substrates. Guided by computational studies, we have successfully achieved versatile, cost–effective and large-area growth of uniform and pinhole–free g–CN films by a thermal vapor condensation method under atmospheric pressure. G–CN films possess multiple active energy states including π*, π and lone pair states, which facilitate their efficient (6% quantum yield in the solid state) photoluminescence, as confirmed by both the experimental measurements and theoretical calculations. Surface morphology and film thickness of the g-CN film can be effectively tuned by changing the substrate and precursor mass, respectively. The g-CN film shows photocurrent density as high as 0.12 mA cm-2, the highest to date for g–CN based photoanode, at the bias of 1.35 V vs reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) with Na2S as the sacrificial reagent. The improved photoresponse of the g–CN film results from intimate contact between the film and the substrate, enhanced light absorption, decreased charge transport and charge transfer resistance with the increase of the process temperature. The success enables the g–CN films being effectively applied in multiple electronic and photoelectronic devices. We showed that the facile TVC method can deliver highly photoactive modified CN films by applying 26D and melamine. The 26D strongly improves the growth of CN films due to the creation of gaseous sp2 C groups at high temperature. The resulting films exhibit strong optical density properties as well as extended absorption in the visible region. The introduction of sp2 C within the g-CN structure enhance the PEC performance of the modified films due to the lowered charge transport and transfer resistance, resulting in a four-fold increase of the photocurrent density with external quantum efficiency of 16% at 400 nm. We further developed a general method to alter the electronic and photoelectrochemical properties of g-CN films by annealing. We found that N atoms can be removed from the g-CN networks after annealing treatment. Assisted by theoretical calculations, we confirm that upon appropriate N removal, the adjacent C atoms will form new C=C π bonds. The highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) and the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) are located at the structure unit with C=C π bonds and the electrons are more delocalized. Valence band X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy spectra together with optical absorption spectra unveil that the structure changes result in the alteration of the g-CN energy levels and position of band edges. The photocurrent density of the annealed g-CN film is doubled compared with the pristine one, thanks to the better charge separation and transport within the film induced by the new C=C π bonds. This work enables the applications of g-CN films in many electronic and optoelectronic devices. Based on their microstructures and the factors dictating their photocatalytic performance, we have unveiled the physicochemical nature of this class of photocatalysis and improved the design of new photocatalytic materials with high reactivity and improved energy efficiency.

Supported by computational studies, we have successfully developed a thermal vapor condensation (TVC) method for depositing uniform graphitic carbon nitride (g-CN) films on FTO substrates and actively applied the films in photoelectrochemical (PEC) cells for hydrogen generation by water splitting. The method allows easy controls of the size, shape, thickness, and the structure of g-CN films. We have modified the optical and electronic properties in order to improve the performance of the films by mixing melamine with co-monomers, such as 2,6-Diaminopyridine (26D) and further demonstrated a general method to alter the electronic and photoelectrochemical properties of g-CN films by annealing which allows removal of N atoms from the g-CN networks. The photocurrent density of the annealed g-CN film is doubled compared with the pristine one, due to the improved charge separation and transport within the film induced by the new C=C π bonds. Our computational studies with spectroscopic (vibrational and absorption) calculations have confirmed our experimentally determined structures of g-CN films and carbon rich g-CN films obtained by annealing deposited using our TVC approach.

103913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
103913.value: Surface catalytic reactions of photocatalytic materials have long been an important subject in photocatalysis. Aiming to elucidate the relevant scientific issues with our theoretical approach for excited states, this project has studied the electronic structures and optical properties in the excited state of a few representative layered semiconductor materials, with focus on the inherent principles governing the interplay among the microscopic structure, photocatalytic reaction dynamics and photocatalytic reaction mechanism. Our important results include the new insight into pi-pi stacking involving remarkable orbital interactions, the transmission lineshape spectrum of zigzag graphene nanoribbon, self-doping and magnetic ordering induced by extended line defects in graphene, point defect weakened thermal contraction in monolayer graphene, symmetry-dependent band gap opening in graphene induced by g-C3N4 substrates, efficient emission facilitated by multiple energy level transitions in uniform graphitic carbon nitride films, uniform graphitic carbon nitride films by thermal vapor condensation with remarkable photocurrent density for photoelectrochemical applications, enhanced efficiency of carbon nitride photoelectrochemical cells via tailored monomers design, and mechanism of charge separation and tunable photoluminescence in carbon nitride quantum dots. The results can help develop highly active and energy efficient novel nanostructured photocatalysts in the field of photocatalysis science.

104113.label: Project Title(Chinese)
104113.value: Kaczmarz型在线学习算法的逼近分析及一些相关样本对损失函数学习算法的富立叶分析

104113.label: Project Objectives
104113.value: Approximation analysis of randomized Kaczmarz algorithms and kernel-based online schemes. An online learning approach will be developed for randomized Kaczmarz algorithms, which will produce confidence-based error bounds leading to the almost sure convergence of the algorithms with general probability distributions controlling the sampling processes. We shall study a unified gradient descent framework for online learning and explore its connections to the orthogonal matching pursuit algorithm in compressed sensing. For kernel-based online learning algorithms for classification and regression, confidence-based error bounds will be derived, and accelerated algorithms will be considered. Fourier analysis of some learning algorithms involving sample pair-based loss functions. Error bounds for minimum error entropy regularization schemes will be obtained by means of the Fourier transform and error decomposition techniques under the assumption of independent noise. We shall investigate minimizers of Renyi's entropy of order 2 and the consistency of minimum error entropy algorithms by bracket products and other methods from wavelet analysis in the case when the conditional density functions are piecewise independent. Characterizations for minimizers of the generalization error associated with some ranking loss functions will be given by Fourier analysis. Some bioinformatics problems concerning peptides, binding affinity and 3D structures of proteins will be considered from learning theory viewpoints. Some theoretical problems on approximation in variable Lp spaces and hypothesis spaces will also be discussed.

104113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
104113.value: Learning theory provides mathematical foundations of many algorithms for analyzing and processing big data which is an important task in various fields of science and engineering. Kernel-based online schemes can be used for learning function features or data structures from samples in efficient ways. This project aims at approximation analysis of kernel-based online schemes and Fourier analysis of some learning algorithms involving sample pair-based loss functions. We shall first conduct error analysis for randomized Kaczmarz algorithms by developing an online learning approach. A unified gradient descent framework will be analyzed and confidence-based error bounds will be derived for kernel-based online learning algorithms. Then we shall study minimum error entropy regularization schemes by Fourier transform and error decomposition techniques. Minimizers of Renyi's entropy with piecewise independent distributions will be analyzed by techniques from wavelet analysis. Finally characterizations of minimizers of the generalization error associated with some ranking loss functions involving sample pairs will be given by means of methods from multivariate approximation theory and reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces generated by radial basis functions. 分析处理大数据是科学技术不同领域中的一个重要课题,学习理论为很多的相应算法提供数学基础.基于核的在线学习方法能有效地用来从样本中学习函数特征及数据结构.本项目旨在基于核在线学习算法的逼近分析及一些相关样本对损失函数学习算法的富立叶分析.我们首先会对随机Kaczmarz算法发展一个在线学习的处理手法,并作误差分析.对一个统一的梯度下降框架进行分析,并为基于核的在线学习算法给出置信度误差阶.然后我们将利用富立叶变换及误差分解技巧研究最小误差熵正则化方法.对带有分片独立分布Renyi熵的极小化子我们将利用小波分析技巧进行分析.最后将利用来自多元逼近论及由径向基函数所产生的再生核希尔伯特空间中的方法刻画由一些相关样本对排序损失函数引导的推广误差的极小化子.

104113.label: Major findings and research outcome
104113.value: In [1] we have studied a relaxed randomized Kaczmarz algorithm by a learning theory approach. The algorithm is investigated in a least squares regression setting. When the sampling values are accurate and the regression function (conditional means) is linear, such an algorithm has been well studied in the community of non-uniform sampling. In our work we mainly deal with the different case of either noisy random measurements or a nonlinear regression function. In this case, we show that relaxation is needed. A necessary and sufficient condition on the sequence of relaxation parameters or step sizes for the convergence of the algorithm in expectation is presented. This is different from the existing literature which often requires another square summable condition. Moreover, polynomial rates of convergence, both in expectation and in probability, are provided explicitly. As a result, the almost sure convergence of the algorithm is proved by applying the Borel-Cantelli Lemma. In [2] kernel-based online pairwise learning algorithms associated with sample pair-based convex loss functions are investigated. These algorithms are closely related to the minimum error entropy principle and Renyi's entropy of order 2. Error bounds for the excess generalization error are derived in terms of the approximation error by an error decomposition technique and some ideas from Fourier analysis. In [3] the problem of learning the kernel function is considered and generalization analysis is carried out. We establish for a wide variety of classes of kernels, such as the set of all multivariate Gaussian kernels, that this learning method generalizes well and, when the regularization parameter is appropriately chosen, it is consistent. In [4] we consider spectral algorithms which form a general framework unifying many regularization schemes. We propose and analyze a class of thresholded spectral algorithms that are designed based on empirical features and achieve sparse approximations by soft thresholding. Our analysis shows that without sparsity assumption of the regression function, the output functions are represented by empirical features with sparsity, and the algorithms achieve satisfactory convergence rates. In [5] we study kernel-based online learning algorithms associated with general convex loss functions. We show that these algorithms can converge comparably fast as corresponding kernel-based batch learning algorithms. Fast learning rates and finite sample upper bounds are established. Our novelty of this work lies in a sharp estimate for the expected values of norms of the learning sequence and a refined error decomposition for online learning algorithms.

104113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
104113.value: Research results produced and methods developed in this project lead to some ideas for studying further learning algorithms with pairwise loss functions and Kaczmarz type algorithms in other settings. We shall investigate these issues in our future work.

104113.value: Learning theory provides mathematical foundations of many algorithms for analyzing and processing big data which is an important task in various fields of science and engineering. Kernel-based online schemes can be used for learning function features or data structures from samples in efficient ways. This project aims at approximation analysis of kernel-based online schemes and Fourier analysis of some learning algorithms involving sample pair-based loss functions. We have conducted error analysis for randomized Kaczmarz algorithms by developing an online learning approach. We have also investigated kernel-based online pairwise learning algorithms associated with sample pair-based convex loss functions which are closely related to the minimum error entropy principle and Renyi's entropy. The related problem of learning the kernel function is then considered and generalization analysis is carried out. 108913.label: Project Title(Chinese)
108913.value: 定向多尺度表示系統的理論研究及設計與應用

108913.label: Project Objectives
108913.value: Characterization and Construction of Directional Multiscale Representation Systems: The main objective of this project is the construction of novel directional multiscale representation systems for anisotropic feature detection and extraction in high-dimensional data analysis. We shall provide a unified framework for analysis, characterizations, and construction of directional multiscale representation systems. We shall focus mainly on the construction of directional multiscale representation systems with many desirable properties such as smooth generators, affine-like structures, directionality selectivity, etc.. We shall investigate the refinability and MRA (multiresolution analyses) structures of the constructed directional multiscale representation systems. Moreover, we shall study the connections and differences among many directional multiscale representation systems based on our characterization. Sparse approximation of new constructed directional multiscale representation systems for a large class of functions such as the cartoon-like images shall also be considered. Digitization and Applications of Directional Multiscale Representation Systems: Another objective of this project is to provide efficient decomposition and reconstruction algorithms for directional multiscale representation systems. We shall study the digitization theory associated with the directional multiscale representation systems for discrete data. We shall design fast algorithm for forward and backward transforms with respect to the digital version of the directional multiscale representation systems based on (directional) filter banks in the spatial domain or FFTs (and its variants) in the frequency domain. Applications of our digital directional multiscale representation systems equipped with fast digital algorithm in high-dimensional data analysis such as image/vedio denoising shall be considered. In the spirit of reproducible research, we shall provide a publicly available software package of the implemented fast algorithms of our directional multiscale representation systems with testing experimental results for many suitable applications.

108913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
108913.value: In the era of information, everyday and everywhere, huge amount of information are acquired, processed, stored, and transmitted in the form of high-dimensional digital data through the Internet, TV, cell phones, and various other modern communication technologies. Efficient and sparse representation of high-dimensional digital data and fast extraction of valuable information from data becomes one of the main goals in nowadays' scientific research. It is well-known that high-dimensional data usually exhibit anisotropic phenomena due to data clustering of various types of structures. For example, a single-channel audio signal consisting of tonal and transient layers in musical audio analysis, two different structures, namely 'dendrites' (curve-like) and 'spines' (point-like), from neuron image in neurobiological imaging, many morphologically distinct objects concentrated near lower-dimensional structures such as points (stars), filaments, and sheets (nebulae) in cosmological data analysis, and so on. The anisotropic features thus encode a large portion of significant information of the data. The design of representation systems that are capable of capturing such anisotropic features is therefore undoubtedly the key for efficient and sparse representation of high-dimensional data. In this project, our main objective is the construction of novel representation systems with directionality selectivity--directional multiscale representaiton system--that are capable of capturing various anistropic information from high-dimensional data, e.g., signals, images, videos, etc.. Our goal is also to provide a unified framework for analysis, characterization and construction of directional multiscale representation systems with many desirable properties. Since efficient decomposition and reconstruction algorithms are crucial for the success of directional multiscale representation systems in many practical applications, we shall study the digitization theory associated with the directional multiscale representation systems for discrete data. Then, we shall design fast algorithms for forward and backward transforms with respect to the digital version of the directional multiscale representation systems based on (directional) filter banks in the spatial domain or FFTs (and its variants) in the frequency domain. Applications to image/signal processing such as image denoising shall be considered. 在當今信息時代，大量的信息無時無刻以高維數字數據的形式通過互聯網，電視，手機，和其他各種現代通信技術被獲取，處理，存儲和傳輸。對高維數字數據的高效和稀疏表示以及從數據中快速提取有價值的信息是時下科研的主要目標之一。眾所周知，由於各種數據類型結構的不同聚類，高維數據通常表現出各向異性的現象。例如，音樂中一個單聲道的音頻信號通常由音調層與過度層組成；神經生物學中的圖像則通常由兩種不同的結構，即“枝晶”（曲線狀）和“刺” （點狀）結構；宇宙學中的數據由許多形態不同的低維聚類構成，如點（星星） ，細絲（星塵），片狀（星雲），等等。可見數據的信息大部分由數據本身的各向異性表現出來。因此，無疑地，設計能夠捕捉這樣各向異性特點的表示系統是高維數據的高效和稀疏表示的關鍵。 在這個項目中，我們的主要目標是構建新型的具有方向性選擇的多尺度表示系統，定向多尺度表示系統，即能夠從高維數據捕獲各種各向異性的表示系統，例如，信號，圖像，視頻等信息。我們的目標是提供一個統一的理論框架以便對具有許多理想性能的定向多尺度表示系統進行分析，刻畫和構造。由於有效的分解和重構算法對定向多尺度表示系統在許多實際應用中至關重要，我們將對定向多尺度表示系統的離散數字化理論進行研究。然後，我們將在空間域中考慮濾波器組，或者在頻域中考慮使用FFT（及其變體）對定向多尺度表示系統的快速分解與重構算法進行設計與實現。這些算法將會考慮應用於圖像/信號處理，如圖像去噪中。

108913.label: Realisation of objectives
108913.value: Objective 5.1: The PI has been working on Objective 5.1 about the characterization and construction of directional multiscale representation systems. To achieve this objective, the PI tackled the problem from many aspects. First, the PI considered the general definition and characterizations of directional multiscale representation system. Based on the so-called “Affine systems”, the PI and his collaborators proposed a general framework for directional multiscale representation systems generated by dilations, shears, and translations. Based on the general framework, the PI gave complete characterizations of such directional systems to be tight frames. Such characterization conditions greatly facilitate and simplify the construction of directional multiscale representation systems. Second, in an even more abstract setting, the PI and his collaborators also consider the directionality and anisotropic properties with connections to the function spaces such as Hardy and BMO spaces for singular integral operators. Third, the PI and his collaborators considered the construction of directional multiscale representation systems in the tensor product setting. The PI showed that directional multiscale representation systems, called tensor product complex tight framelets (TPCTF) can be built using simple one-dimensional complex tight framelets together with tensor product approach. Directionality can be easily achieved, and tightness can be preserved. Such TPCTFs enjoy low redundancy rate but with limited numbers of directions. Fourth, to have flexible numbers of directions, the PI and his collaborators also considered the construction of directional multiscale representation systems in the non-separable setting. One type of such systems is called affine shear tight frames, which can have arbitrary numbers of directions. Using a unitary transform, the PI also considered the construction of Gabor shearlets and proved their optimal approximation rate for cartoon-like functions. Last but not least, by exploring the structures of both the tensor product complex tight frames (TPCTF6) as well as the affine shear tight frames, the PI proposed a new type of directional multiscale representation systems, called affine shear tight frames with 2-layer structure, which can enjoy many nice properties of both the two systems. In summary, the Objective 5.1 has been achieved completely. For major findings and research outcome, we refer to 6.1 of this report. Objective 5.2: The PI has been working on Objective 5.2 about digitization and applications of directional multiscale representation systems. To achieve this objective, the PI has done several works. First, the PI and his collaborators developed theoretical results on the filter bank associations of the directional multiscale representation systems. Based on the filter bank associations, we can further develop fast digital transform algorithms for both the decomposition and reconstruction of data. More importantly, low-redundancy rate of the developed algorithms are emphasized for efficiency in real-world applications. Second, several fast directional filter bank transforms are realized as MATLAB packages for real-world applications in 2D or 3D. These include DAS-1 for the affine shear tight frames, TPCTF6 for tensor product complex tight framelets, and DAS-2 for affine shear tight frames with 2-layer structure. Finally, applications in denoising and inpainting are considered and numerical experiments are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of different approaches considered in Objective 5.1 using the MATLAB packages. We have shown the advantages of using our directional filter banks comparing to many other frame-based directional systems In image/video processing. In summary, the Objective 5.2 has been achieved completely. For major findings and research outcome, we refer to 6.1 of this report.

108913.label: Major findings and research outcome
108913.value: A general framework for directional multiscale representation systems generated by dilations, shears, and translations, systems. Complete characterizations are given. Two types of construction of directional shear systems are proposed: quasi-stationary and non-stationary. Connection between the directional shear systems to the directional tight framelet systems is built. Fast digital affine shear transforms based on the directional filter bank are implemented and the advantages of such directional filter banks over many other state-of-the-art directional systems are shown. Results are published as journal papers, see Part C Sec. 8 Nos. 4 and 5. Using one-dimensional complex tight framelets and a simple tensor product approach, directional tight framelets can be easily built and shown to perform quite well in image/video processing. For TPCTF6, a 2-layer structure were discovered and further development of the affine shear tight frames results in a more flexible systems: affine shear tight frames with 2-layer structure. Results are published as journal papers, see Part C Sec. 8 Nos. 6 and 7. Under a unitary transform, a chirp modulation system can be built to be orthonormal for a wedge-shape domain, based on which directional shear systems are constructed and showed to be an A-tight unit norm frames with redundancy coefficient A arbitrarily close to one. Such directional systems are named Gabor shearlets and they provide almost optimal approximation rate for cartoon-like functions. Results are published as a journal paper, see Part C Sec. 8 No. 3. For the singular integral operators associated with isotropic and anisotropic homogeneity, a common Hardy space or BMO space from anisotropic construction can be built on which the singular integral operators or their compositions are bounded. Such a result is published as a journal paper, see Part C Sec. 8 No. 2. An l-1 inpainting framework to characterize the performance of missing data recovery using cluster coherence and sparsity is proposed. Based on the framework, the advantage of shearlet seismic inpainting over wavelet seismic inpainting is proved in the sense that shearlets can recover larger gap than wavelets do in an asymptotic regime. Experimental results using ShearLab also confirm the performance improvement. Such results are published as a journal paper, see Part C Sec. 8 No. 1.

108913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
108913.value: Potential for further development of the research would be the consideration of directional multiscale representation systems in more general domains. For examples, manifolds, graphs or networks. One can first consider multiscale representation systems on some simple domains such as spheres or torus, and then further generalize to more complex domains.

108913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
108913.value: In this project, we focus on the construction and applications of novel multiscale representation systems with directionality selectivity: directional multiscale representation system. In the era of information, huge amount of information are acquired, processed, stored, and transmitted in the form of digital data (songs, images, videos, etc.) through the Internet, TV, cell phones, and various other modern communication technologies. Directional multiscale representation systems can be used to capture the sparsity of data and fast decomposition and reconstruction algorithms can be developed associated with such directional multiscale representation systems for real-world applications such as image/video processing.

109113.label: Project Title(Chinese)
109113.value: 随机偏微分方程的小概率事件研究

109113.label: Project Objectives
109113.value: Asymptotic analysis: We will develop asymptotic results at exponential or non-exponential level for high excursion regime of the solution. Numerical methods: We will develop fast simulation schemes based on the importance sampling Monte Carlo method and discuss their efficiency. We identify the "most probable" realizations of the random input (conditioned on occurrence of rare events) and use this information to guide the selection of the change of measure for efficient importance sampling in various settings.

Numerical methods: We will develop fast simulation schemes based on the importance sampling Monte Carlo method and discuss their efficiency. We identify the "most probable" realizations of the random input (conditioned on occurrence of rare events) and use this information to guide the selection of the change of measure for efficient importance sampling in various settings.

109113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
109113.value: Rare events are those outcomes in a stochastic system that rarely happen but once they happen, they may have drastic consequences, such as material failure or pollution breakout. They are closely related to the stability or risk measure of the system under extreme conditions. Stochastic partial differential equations (SPDE) are partial differential equations (PDE) that contain random forcing or coefficients and they are extensively used in various fields of science and engineering to incorporate random effects in physical systems. In this proposal, we focus on a special type of SPDE — elliptic PDEs with random coefficients. There is a considerable amount of literature about SPDE in mathematics analysis and numerical techniques. However, traditional stochastic theories and algorithms mainly concern the averaged effect of the random- ness. Rare events occur only at certain locations in the random space which are far away from where the typical behaviors occur. This project aims at the challenges arising from the analysis and computation of the rare events for elliptic partial differential equations with random coefficients which are of great interests in applications, such as material failure, spreading of pollutants in ground water, etc. The random coefficients are modeled as random fields related to Gaussian random field. The solution of the equation is a complicated functional of the input Gaussian field. The rare events of interests correspond to the behaviors of the solution which significantly deviate from the typical states. We will discuss three scenarios of rare events. Different ideas and techniques will be developed for these different scenarios. The common objective is to derive asymptotic results and to design the importance sampling Monte Carlo method to calculate the small probabilities of the rare events. The theory of large deviation principle and Gaussian random function as well as some analysis techniques for elliptic partial differential equation and heuristic arguments will be exploited and unified for our purpose. The numerical method will combine the PDE-related numerical techniques with the rare event simulation schemes, such as the importance sampling method guided by the asymptotic analysis and other types of heuristics. 稀有事件（小概率事件）是以极小的概率发生于随件系统中但是影响巨大的随机事件，比如材料断裂和污染爆发。它们跟极端条件下的风险分析密切相关。在本研究计划，我们考虑一类带随机系数的椭圆偏微分方程中的稀有事件。此类模型是弹性力学的基本方程。由于复杂材料的参数不可避免带有随机分布，本研究考虑跟高斯随机场相关的随机系数。传统的随机模拟理论和方法往往考虑系统的平均性态，并不适合研究极端的小概率事件。 本研究考虑不同渐进条件假设下的方程解的极值行为，特别是跟形变场或者应力场的最大值相关的量的尾分布。基于重要性抽样的渐进分析和蒙特卡洛模拟是本研究的重点。本研究关于小概率事件的发展对“不确定性量化”的深入研究和材料断裂的统计行为有重要意义。

109113.label: Realisation of objectives
109113.value: For the Objective 1, I and my co-authors worked on the asymptotic analysis on the maximum value of the solutions related to the elliptic equation with random coefficients. For the Objective 2, we solved the underlying optimization problem by a Newton type iteration and designed the importance sampling scheme which works very well for the maximum value problem in consideration. This is published in a SIAM journal.

109113.label: Major findings and research outcome
109113.value: Our major finding is the efficient simulation scheme for the maximum value of the solution to the elliptic equation with random coefficients. In addition, we explored many related problems for the elliptic problem arising from transition problems, chemical reactions, etc.

109113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
109113.value: During this project, we are also motivated to consider the moderate-deviation, rather than the large-deviation regime. This has lead to another work which has been subject to the Annals of Applied Probability in 2017.

109113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
109113.value: The elliptic equation with random coefficient is a useful model to study some failure behavior of the elastic material. However, the direct simulation of the failure probability is too expensive for the computer. Our new simulation method can easily speed up over one million when computing 0.001% failure rate. Furthermore, the smaller the failure probability, the more accurate our methods.

109213.label: Project Title(Chinese)
109213.value: 通過氮化硼納米結構的協同作用實現超高熱導率絕緣聚合物複合材料

109213.label: Project Objectives
109213.value: To realize mass production (grams level) synthesis of ultra-thin BN nanosheets. Emphasis will be also placed on direct synthesis of unique BN nanotube/nanosheet hybrid nanostructures. To develop chemical functionalization approaches for fabricating unique covalently bonded BN nanotube/nanosheet hybrid nanostructures. Emphasis will be also placed on surface modification to BN nanostructures for low interfacial thermal resistance. To maximize synergetic effects of BN nanotubes and nanosheets for highly effective thermal conductivity improvement of polymer composites. Polymer composites with thermal conductivity up to 7-20 W/mK are expected. To optimize the over-all performance of the fabricated composite materials. Emphasis will be placed on their dielectric properties, mechanical properties, coefficient of thermal expansion and break-over voltage etc.

109213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
109213.value: [散熱材料的重要性] 最近一些年，作為散熱用電子封裝材料或者熱介面材料的導熱絕緣聚合物複合材料變得非常重要。它們被廣泛的使用在LED封裝，印刷電路板製造，芯片，太陽能電池，發電機，馬達和電源模塊中。 [高熱導率的納米氮化硼材料] 氮化硼納米結構（氮化硼納米管或者氮化硼納米片）是最好的高導熱絕緣聚合物複合材料的填料。它們具有著穩定的寬帶隙， 非常好的機械性能和結構穩定性，超強的抗氧化能力和一個理論值高達大約3000W/mK的熱導率。（實驗上，直徑50nm左右的電絕緣多層氮化硼納米管熱導率可達200-300W/mK，這個數字接近金屬材料鋁的熱導率238W/mK, 和導熱非常好的銅材料的熱導率390W/mK也是可以比較的。 [我們的方法] 我們提出利用氮化硼納米管和納米片的協同作用在絕緣聚合物體系中獲得有效地熱導率改進。我們將會發展多種適合大量製備氮化硼納米結構，特別是氮化硼納米片的合成方法。此外，我們將開發一種氮化硼納米片附著在氮化硼納米管上的複合結構，這種結構可以產生有效的協同作用並且有效降低介面熱阻。氮化硼納米管和納米片之間將採用共價鍵結合，這將最大化協同作用，促進聚合物複合材料中導熱通道的有效大量形成。另外，我們還將對合成的納米複合結構進行有效的表面改性，包括共價鍵改性和弱相互作用改性等，這種改性可以有效改善填充物和聚合物之間的相互作用。我們還將評估製備的複合材料的綜合材料性能。 [目標] 本項目的完成，將會基於氮化硼納米結構之間的有效的協同作用，製備一系列高導熱絕緣的聚合物複合材料，預期熱導率可達10-30W/mK。此外，製備的複合材料也會具有良好的綜合性能，包括低的介電常數和介電損耗，良好的機械性能，低的熱膨脹係數和良好保持的擊穿電壓以及可加工性等。

109213.label: Realisation of objectives
109213.value: To realize large scale fabrication of boron nitride nanosheets, we have tested a variety of solvents, including organic, inorganic and polarized solvents for liquid exfoliation. We figured out polarized solvents are more effective for exfoliating boron nitride platelets into boron nitride nanosheets. However, since most organic polarized solvents are toxic and non-environmentally friendly, we found water is also useful for exfoliation of boron nitride platelets. The typical procedure including long-term sonication of boron nitride platelets in water, centrifugation to remove big sized boron nitride particles and water evaporation. With this method, grams to tens of grams boron nitride nanosheets can be obtained in one day. In addition, we also developed another exfoliation method by molten salts. We found pure NaCl and KCl are not effective when they are mixed with boron nitride platelets at their molten temperature. The boron nitride phase is separated with the salts after it is cooled down. However, when NaCl and KCl is mixed at a certain ratio, their affinity with boron nitride platelets can be effectively improved. In this case, with the high temperature up to over 800 centigrade degree, the Na and K ions may achieved a high mobility, which can be inserted into the layers of boron nitride and eventually exfoliate the boron nitride. After long term high temperature exfoliation, the mixture was dissolved in water. The salts will be dissolved in water and boron nitride nanosheets can be separated out. The advantage of this method is that without strong mechanical exfoliation, the obtained boron nitride sheets can keep large lateral size, which can benefit thermal transfer when being used as fillers. With this method, the production of boron nitride nanosheets can be scale up. Tens of grams boron nitride nanosheets can be produced in one day. We also developed various method to modify the fabricated boron nitride nanosheets and nanotubes. Following a traditional method, we firstly oxide the boron nitride nanosheets to chemically activate their surface. After oxidation, a variety of silane coupling agents were used interact with the boron nitride nanostructures to attached them various organic chains. After modification, the boron nitride nanostructures can be well dispersed in many organic solvents and even water. In addition, the modification effectively improve the affinity between boron nitride nanosheets and polymer matrixes. Furthermore, after attaching ammonia functional groups on boron nitride nanostructures, through the esterification chemical reactions, we graft polystyrene chains of surface of boron nitride nanostructures. The polystyrene coated boron nitride nanostructures can be hot pressed and reshaped to form composite structure. With the modified boron nitride nanosheets, nanotubes and nanospheres, we fabricated highly thermally conductive composite materials. We applied both pure boron nitride nanosheets and the combination of various boron nitride nanostructures to fabricate the polymer composites. We mix epoxy resin with the boron nitride nanostructures with proper design and a thinky mixer was used to disperse the boron nitride nanostructures in the viscose liquid. At high filler fraction, solvents was used to dilute the mixture to achieve uniform dispersion of nanostructures in the composites. The mixture was then be cured through a preset temperature and finally a high quality specimen was obtained by high temperature curing. With proper design, we achieved a thermal conductivity more than 7 W/mK with epoxy as matrix. The fabricated polymer composites possess decent mechanical performance (slightly decreased hardness), great dielectric and insulting performances (almost identical break-over voltage). In addition, we found the boron nitride nanosheets can partially isolate epoxy from oxygen, which enable the polymer composites with fire resistant performance. Moreover, a stretchable and self-healable thermal interface material was successfully fabricated by incorporating boron nitride nanosheets into dual cross-linked polyacrylic acid (PAA) hydrogel through in situ polymerization. The thermal conductivity of composites increase with increasing filler loading fractions. An maximum value of 3.5 W/(m•K) was achieved at proper boron nitride nanosheets loading fraction and water fraction, which is nearly 4-fold of the thermal conductivity of pure hydrogel with only water incorporated. Water fraction is demonstrated to be one of the controlling factors that affect the thermal conductivity of the nanocomposites. In addition, by virtue of the combination of the properties of PAA hydrogel and boron nitride nanosheets, the hydrogel nanocomposites show excellent stretchability, up to 400% elongation, and self-healability for 3 cycles. Additionally, the as-fabricated thermal interface material shows excellent adhesion/delicate structure replicating ability to various kinds of surfaces and gaps, offering an airless environment for efficient thermal conduction with the integral boron nitride nanosheets network. Meanwhile, it can be softened and reused for several times for rough surfaces with different textures. This kind of soft gel thermal interface material has sum up the advantages of hard thermal interface material and the liquid thermal interface materials, which is stable, non-perishable, non-flowable, but meanwhile, tight stick to the devices for a better thermal conduction. To evaluate the effect of the boron nitride nanosheets/PAA gels as thermal interface materials, a simple demonstration showing the heat dissipation ability was performed. A heater and a large alumina ceramic plate were used for the demonstration. Gel Sample 1 contains boron nitride nanosheets, while sample 2 has no boron nitride nanosheets embedded. We put the two samples between the plate and the sheets respectively and test the temperatures of the plate (T1), the sheet on the sample 1 (T2), and the sheet on the sample 2 (T3). The plate has a stable temperature at ~65 ℃, and the two sheets with thermal interface materials on them have an initial temperature of the room temperature (23.6 ℃). After putting the sheets on the plate, we found that the increasing speed of T2 is obviously faster than T3. After 30 seconds, the sheet with the boron nitride nanosheets is 53.9℃ already, while the other was 47.1℃ only and proved the excellent thermal conductive property of the developed boron nitride nanosheets/PAA gel. Our study of soft gel thermal interface materials with facile fabrication and acceptable cost creates considerable potential for the multifunctional and recyclable material for the further research and production in the field of thermal conduction. As a result, it is believed that the hydrogel nanocomposites developed in this study will be one of the promising candidates as high performance and multifunctional thermal interface materials in the future.

109213.label: Major findings and research outcome
109213.value: Utilizing the boron nitride nanostructure fabricated, we fabricated a self-healable highly flexible thermal interface material with boron nitride nanofillers. A dual-cross-linked hydrogel was used as matrix of the nanocomposite. The thermal conductivity of the composites can be tuned by adjusting both fraction of boron nitride nanosheets and water content. The highest thermal conductivity achieved is >3.5 W/mK. Although it is a solid, the highly flexible characteristic of the developed thermal interface materials enables a perfect ability to replicate the texture of a rough surface, which may greatly enhance thermal transfer between adjacent surfaces. By increasing the water content to soften the material, it can be recycled and reused for different kinds of rough surface. In addition, benefiting from the dual-cross-linked structure, the composites are capable of recovering both mechanical strength and thermal conductivity even from severe structural breakdowns, for example, three consecutive cutting and healing cycles. To achieve higher thermal conductivity, we choose epoxy as matrix and boron nitride nanosheets/nanotubes as filler and made a series of composites materials. Pristine boron nitride nanosheets and nanotubes were treated by hydrogen peroxide and silane coupling agents. A series of epoxy resin-BN platelets composites were fabricated with optimized filler loading fractions. A mixer was used to generate homogenous and uniform mixture. After curing, the composites were obtained. Through tuning the filler surface, filler fraction and filler dimensions, a thermal conductivity of 7.2 W/mK was obtained. In addition, polyacrylic resin based boron nitride composites were also fabricated. A highest thermal conductivity of 6.5 W/mK was obtained when optimized filler fraction and filler dimensions were adopted. In addition, we also develop a new class of epoxy composites comprising very long (up to tens of micrometers) single-crystalline copper nanowires (a diameter of ∼20 nm and a length of up to ∼40 μm) as filler. A high thermal conductivity of 2.59 W/mK was obtained at a very low loading fraction of Cu nanowires at 0.12 vol%, corresponding to an 8-fold enhancement in thermal conductivity of plain epoxy resins. We also demonstrate that ytterbium and erbium codoped sodium yttrium tetra-fluoride (NaYF4:Yb/Er) upconversion nanoparticles can be concomitantly incorporated into the epoxy composite, providing an accurate temperature of the composite. The dual functionality should render the epoxy composite an attractive candidate in electronic device.

109213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
109213.value: 1. We will try to achieve polymer composites with higher thermal conductivity. Instead of boron nitride nanosheets and nanotubes, we also plan to use more nano and microsized materials, such as silicon nitride and silicon carbide. In addition, since metals usually possess very high thermal conductivity, we plan to fabricate boron nitride coating copper nanowires as fillers. The fillers will combine thermal insulating property of boron nitride and high thermal conductivity of copper together. These novel fillers may help us to achieve higher thermal conductivity in polymer composites. 2. Another plan for further development is to look for more applications for the fabricated boron nitride nanosheets/nanotubes. As a two-dimensional materials, boron nitride nanosheets can be doped with carbon or other elements. The doping can effectively tune their electrical and optical properties. Thus, the doped boron nitride nanosheets may be applied for energy storage devices and optoelectronic devices. 3. In addition, we plan to apply the developed thermally conductive polymer composites for various applications, such as heat-dissipation for electronic devices, mobile phones or battery modules in electric cars.

109213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
109213.value: Polymers possess very good processibility. They are widely used to package stuff, including many electronic devices. These electronic devices may generate a lot of heat. Therefore, as packaging materials, polymers are supposed to help with heat dissipation of the devices or systems. Unfortunately, polymers usually possess a very low thermal conductivity, which is in the range of 0.05 to 0.4 W/mK (thermal conductivity of air is 0.025 W/mK). Therefore, adding highly thermally conductive powders (fillers) into polymers to improve their thermal conductivity is one of the obvious solutions. One of the best thermal conductive fillers are boron nitride materials, especially the two dimensional boron nitride nanosheets or one dimensional boron nitride nanotubes. In this project, we use both boron nitride nanosheets and nanotubes together to improve thermal conductive polymers. Composites with a high thermal conductivity up to 7W/mK was obtained. The polymer composites are insulating but thermally conductive. The polymer composites can be used to package electronic devices and chips. In addition, we also fabricated a self-healable highly flexible thermal interface material with the boron nitride nanofillers, which possess very good stretchability and flexibility. It can be widely used to assist heat-dissipation in CPU devices.

109413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
109413.value: Lanthanide-doped inorganic crystals represent an important class of luminescent materials that have excelled in lighting, display, and lasering in the 20th century. These materials have a number of advantages including very high stability, low cost, and tunable emission colors. For example, conventional cathode ray tube (CRT) screens comprising Eu-doped YVO4 phosphors can perform for more than ten years without significant loss of brightness. However, lanthanide-based phosphors typically do not exhibit luminescence without intense excitations such as laser irradiation and electron bombardment. These phosphors are therefore unsuitable for most of today's applications in integrated devices including LEDs and photovoltaic cells. Herein, we proposed to develop a new generation of composite luminescent nanomaterials comprising lanthanide-doped nanocrystals conjugated with semiconductor quantum dots. We intend to use the quantum dots as antennae for collecting the excitations by electrical fields or solar light and for subsequently sensitizing the luminescence of lanthanide-doped nanocrystals through non-radiative energy transfer. Importantly, we have previously demonstrated that lanthanide-doped nanophosphors can exhibit tunable lights by doping different lanthanide ions at low dopant concentrations (< 5 mol %). Therefore, different-colored nanocomposites can be readily synthesized following a standard procedure. Once refined, we envision that these nanocomposites will open up the opportunity to constructing novel optoelectronic devices for a broad range of applications such as compact white LEDs and tunable lasers. 镧系掺杂无机晶体是一类非常重要的光学材料，它们曾于20世纪在照明、显示、以及激光等应用领域占据主导地位。这类材料具有一系列突出的优点，如高稳定性、低成本、发光性质可调等。一个典型的例子是阴极射线显示屏的红色荧光粉YVO4:Eu，它可以在保证显示亮度的前提下连续使用10年以上。然而镧系掺杂发光材料通常需要在极高的激发强度如激光辐照和电子轰炸下才能产生明亮的发光，这极大地限制了它们在当代便携设备及小尺寸集成器件中的应用。在本项目中，我们拟开发一类新型复合发光材料，基于在镧系掺杂发光纳米晶表面修饰一层半导体量子点来获得新的发光性质。我们计划利用量子点作为敏化剂来捕获低功率激发光或激发电场，并基于量子点到镧系掺杂纳米晶的无辐射能量传递来实现镧系离子在不同激发条件下的明亮发光。我们之前积累了大量方法来控制镧系掺杂离子内部的能量传递和发光属性，其中包括用微调（<5 mol %）掺杂离子的方式实现发光光谱在紫外至近红外范围的精细调控。由于这一微小成份的变化不会对材料的合成过程产生明显影响，我们有望建立一个通用的工艺来构造具有不同发光性能的复合材料体系。项目的成功实施将为新型光电器件的设计和建造提供新的契机，促进白光LED及可调激光器等领域的应用型研究。

109413.label: Realisation of objectives
109413.value: 1. We have synthesized a series of core-shell-shell nanoparticles. Systematically characterizations of these nanoparticles along with theoretical simulation reveal a spatial confinement effect in the nanostructured materials. Importantly, the spatial confinement effect can be tuned by controlling shell thickness of the nanoparticles, which allows us to create unprecedented optical properties through core-shell nanostructural engineering. In addition, we also developed method to prepare multishell and heterogeneous core-shell nanostructures, which integrate different materials into a single nanoparticle and allow highly flexible energy transfer processes. By controlling the combination and topological arrangement of constituent layers, new luminescent materials can be rationally designed. For example, we can realize full spectrum emission by single wavelength excitation. 2. The core-shell structure engineering not only eliminates surface quenching, but also suppresses concentration quenching of the dopant ions. Accordingly, we can protect the dopant ions in spate shells for highly efficient luminescence with quantum yields up to 90%. By doping a high concentration of Yb ions into a thin layer of a core-shell-shell nanoparticle, we also realize highly efficient 5-photon upconversion in the deep ultraviolet spectra range. The emission has enabled a deep UV lasing by NIR excitation for the first time. 3. By doping a high concentration of lanthanide ions in the nanoparticles, we realize a high extinction coefficient of the nanoparticles that is critical for capturing the energy of quantum dots donors. Specifically, heavily Nd-doped nanoparticles are synthesized to accept the energy of visible emitting quantum dots and generate NIR emissions. 4. By coating the nanoparticles comprising high levels of lanthanide dopants on a LED chip, we have realized optical emission from the lanthanide ions after pumping the LED by electricity.

109413.label: Major findings and research outcome
109413.value: Previously, the design of new lanthanide materials is mainly based on control of materials composition. Our findings suggest that nanostructural engineering can be a powerful compliment to compositional design for creating new luminescent materials. Notably, some abandoned materials compositions can be redesigned to show efficient luminescence through the use of core-shell nanostructures. In this way, the scope of designing lanthanide-doped luminescent nanomaterials can be largely expanded. In addition, we also developed a series of new materials based on the core-shell structural engineering, and demonstrate several new applications that are enabled by unique properties provided by these nanoparticles. Some representative applications include deep tissue imaging, anti-counterfeiting printing, and UV lasing.

109413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
109413.value: The results achieved in the current project have inspired a lot of interests of my collaborators. For example, my study largely promoted the applied research in the field of biology and information technology within my institute by providing better materials for downstream cancer detection and therapy. The creation of unprecedented optical properties also provides exciting opportunities for some new applications. Preliminary exploration indicates that the nanoparticles are promising candidate for constructing compact waveguides and lasers. These materials also provide new platforms for fundamental research, for example, for understanding energy transfer dynamics in solid matters.

109413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
109413.value: A new design philosophy is established for constructing luminescent materials. The design philosophy is substantiated by preparing a series of new materials displaying unprecedented optical properties. By using these new materials, we also demonstrate some unique applications such as biological detection and therapy, anti-counterfeiting printing, and ultraviolet lasing.

109613.label: Project Title(Chinese)
109613.value: 路径相关的混合型控制系统中的马氏链逼近

109613.label: Project Objectives
109613.value: We will investigate numerical methods on a class of stochastic control problems, in which Markov chain approximation is applicable, whereas the conventional numerical PDE method may not work. In particular, we will study the hybrid dynamic system and path-dependent functionals where dynamic programming principle fails or partially fails. A new proof of convergence of Markov chain approximation will be developed based on computations under a suitable topology, which may not depend on dynamic programming principle. We will investigate the relation between regularities of the diffusion on a class of rough boundaries, which leads to a class of sufficient conditions for the convergence of the multidimensional tangency problems. The result is expected to remove hypothesis imposed on the convergence proof; see A2.2 of [Kushner and Dupuis(2001)]. Based on the above theoretical basis, we will also investigate some practical issues arising from numerical implementations: advantages and disadvantages of the various constructions of Markov chain approximations. This leads us to investigate new MC approximation combined by multilevel Monte-carlo method, which may be expected to reduce the computational cost significantly.

109613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
109613.value: Since the extensive development of the stochastic control theory in the 1960s, establishing practically and environmentally reasonable mathematical models is definitely one of the most important and complicated issues in the modern decision making. As one of the developments in this vein, the hybrid system modeling has drawn considerable attentions from both researchers and practitioners in recent decades due to its distinct capability to capture the features of random environments. Such examples can be found in mathematical finance, ecosystem modeling, manufacturing systems, and risk theory, to name just a few. In particular, the systems often display qualitative structural changes by Markov chain, and it turns out to be quite versatile in capturing these inherent randomness. Owing to the complex nature of control problems, the solutions are highly nonlinear and closed-form solutions are not obtainable. Thus, the numerical methods become a viable alternative. Two major types of numerical methods include probabilistic method (e.g., Markov chain approximation initiated by Kushner [see Kushner(1990)] and numerical PDE method (e.g., Finite different/element method). Both developments are highly dependent on the dynamic programming principle. However, dynamic programming principle may not be true for a class of path-dependent stochastic hybrid control problems. In this project, we will take up the challenges of numerical method on a class of path-dependent stochastic hybrid control systems. We aim to design and analyze a feasible Markov chain approximation to the path-dependent stochastic control problem in a mathematically rigorous manner. The main difficulty is that, due to the lack of dynamic programming principle, one cannot expect the conventional Markov chain approximation method or finite difference method to be worked out. Different from the existing theory of the Markov chain approximations, we develop an alternative approach via weak convergence for this purpose, which requires the actual computations on an appropriate topology equivalent to conventional Skorohod topology. Not only does this proof enable us to establish the convergence of the path-dependent control problems, but also it leads to sufficient conditions for the non-occurrence of tangency problem. One advantage of Markov chain approximation over numerical PDE is the flexibility of the construction of various types of good Markov chains. The aforementioned theoretical study of convergence makes it possible to open up a round of new investigations on the comparison of various Markov chain approximations on path-dependent control problems. In this direction, a multilevel approach on Markov chain approximation will be investigated to multidimensional problems to reduce computational cost. 自上世纪60年代控制论的迅速发展，实用并严谨的控制系统的建立方法吸引了大批复杂系统上的决策论研究，其中包括了混合型控制系统的研究。混合型控制系统有广泛的应用基础，比如金融数学，生态系统，风险管理等等。 由于随机控制论的非线性特质，显式解往往不存在，与之代替的事数值逼近解。常用的数值解大体分为两种：概率方法逼近（KUSHNER 1990）和偏微分方程数值解逼近(有限元方法/差分方法)。两种方法都必须依赖控制系统的动态规划原理。但是路径相关的控制系统不满足动态规划原理。 这个项目中我们研究的对象时路径相关的随机混合型控制系统。我们的目标是利用马氏链逼近论去设计这一类问题的概率方法数值解，并提供数学上的收敛分析结果。主要困难来自传统的动态规划原理不能用。相比传统的马氏链逼近论的弱收敛方法，我们要采取完全不同的方法：我们要通过确切的概率分布间的距离计算得到更明确地SKOROHOD TOPOLOGY的几何结构。这种方法的优点在于，这种方法不单单提供收敛性的理论结果，还可以得到TANGENCY PROBLEM的必要条件。

109613.label: Major findings and research outcome
109613.value: During the research investigation of this project, we had fruitful achievements and new discoveries in realizing our earlier proposed ideas, and we are summarising as follows. In the article [1] Weak Convergence Methods for Approximation of Path-dependent Functionals, SIAM J. Control Optim., 51(5), 2013, we are able to successfully prove the convergence of Markov chain approximation method to a class of path-dependent functionals. Particularly, due to the path-dependent feature, the conventional numerical solutions for PDEs do not work in this framework. This work leads to a series of findings in the following areas: (1) Regime switching exotic option pricing in financial market; (2) Regime switching credit risk pricing under systematic risk modeling; (3) Solvability of Integro-Differential equations of HJB types. Based on the aforementioned findings, the methodology using continuous mapping in Skorohod topology is getting matured and can be successfully utilized not only the convergence issues of computational aspects but theoretical weak regularity issues arising from Integro-Differential Equations.

109713.label: Project Objectives
109713.value: To study mathematical foundation of discontinuous Petrov-Galerkin (DPG) methods. To develop robust, competitive DPG methods for solving incompressible Navier-Stokes equation with low viscosity, and some other singular perturbation problems.
