109713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
109713.value: In practice, some partial differential equations allow singular perturbation - their parameters can be very close to zero or infinite. For example, in Naiver-Stokes equations, the viscosity parameter can be very close to zero. Usually, the exact solution may blow up in some sense when parameters approach to zero or infinite. It is difficult to design robust numerical methods which can solve these partial differential equations uniformly efficient, when there is singular perturbation. The long-term goal of the P.I. is to develop and study, theoretically as well as computationally, efficient and robust numerical methods for solving partial differential equations with singular perturbation. In this proposal, the P.I. will concentrate on the study and development of a new, emerging numerical scheme - discontinuous Petrov-Galerkin (DPG) methods. DPG methods are characterized by having enhanced stability, convergence properties and robustness, and by displaying an improved flexibility for handling meshes with hanging nodes. Unlike other discontinuous Galerkin methods obtaining stability by devising various numerical fluxes, DPG methods achieve this objective via computing optimal test function spaces. This feature makes DPG methods suitable for solving partial differential equations with singular perturbation. A good application of DPG methods is to solve high wave number Helmholtz equation. According to recent numerical experiments, there is no phase error (detailed description will be given in background of research). The P.I. is interested in studying mathematical foundation of this new numerical method and developing robust DPG methods for a variety of equations arising in fluid dynamics with low viscosity parameter. 在实践中，一些偏微分方程允许奇异摄动 - 它们的参数可以很 接近零或无穷大。例如，在Naiver -Stokes方程，粘性参数 可以在非常接近零。通常情况下，在某种意义上参数接近零或无穷时, 真实解可能会趋向于无穷大。有奇异摄动时, 难以设计 强大的数值方法可以均匀高效求解这些偏微分方程。 P.I.的长远目标，是开发和研究，在理论上和计算上， 高效和稳健的数值方法求解含奇异摄动的偏微分方程。 在此， P.I.将集中在一个新兴的数值方法的研究和开发 - 间断彼得罗夫辽金方法 (DPG)。 DPG方法，其特征在于，具有增强的稳定性，收敛性和鲁棒性， 并通过悬挂节点处理网格显示一个更高的灵活性。 不像其他的间断有限元方法(DG)通过制定各种数值通量来取得稳定性， DPG方法达到这一目标，是通过计算最佳的测试函数空间。此功能使得 DPG方法适合于求解含奇异摄动的偏微分方程。 DPG是一个很好的方法，来解决高波数Helmholtz方程。 根据最近的数值实验，不存在相位误差 (在研究背景将给予详细的说明)。 P.I.有兴趣在研究这个新的数值计算方法的数学基础和发展 鲁棒DPG方法适用于各种的方程中出现的，具有低粘度流体动力学参数 。

109713.label: Realisation of objectives
109713.value: The first object (studying mathematical foundation of discontinuous Galerkin (DPG) methods) is accomplished. For the second object, a robust first order least squares method, which can be considered as a special kind of discontinuous Galerkin method, is developed and analysed for the convection-dominated diffusion equation. The convection dominated diffusion equation is a starting point to work on incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. The work on the convection dominated diffusion equation inspire the PI to develop some other numerical methods to solve the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, which is supported by PI's another UGC project (CityU 11302014). The third object is finished. The PI didn't develop DPG method for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, because another numerical method supported by UGC project (CityU 11302014) is much easier to implement.

109713.label: Major findings and research outcome
109713.value: The PI developed two first order least squares methods, which can be considered as special examples of discontinuous Galerkin (DPG) methods. The first one is for the convection dominated diffusion equation. Before the PI's work, first order least squares methods were not thought to be suitable for solving convection dominated diffusion equation. The PI's work changes this wrong impression among the community of numerical analysis for convection dominated diffusion problems. The work is mentioned as number 2 of item 8 of Part C. The second one is for the Helmholtz equation with high wave number. The PI gave explicit dependency on mesh size h, polynomial degree p, and the wave number k. The work is mentioned as number 7 of item 8 of Part C. In addition, inspired by techniques developed in this project, the PI developed another numerical method (hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin method) for solving the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. The PI found it is more efficient to use hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin method to solve the Navier-Stokes equations than DPG methods proposed in this project. Actually, the PI proposed hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin method in another GRF project (CityU 11302014). The work of hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin method for solving the Navier-Stokes equations is published in a paper "Analysis of a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin method for the steady-state incompressible Navier-Stokes equations", by Aycil Cesmelioglu, Bernardo Cockburn, and Weifeng Qiu, published in Mathematics of Computation, Volume 86, number 306, July 2017, pages 1643-1670.

109713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
109713.value: The works supported by this project may help the PI to develop a robust DPG method for the time-harmonic Maxwell equations with high wave number, such that its linear system is unconditionally Hermitian positive definite.

109713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
109713.value: Before the PI's work, people don't think the first order least squares method is suitable for solving the convection dominated diffusion problems. ThePI's work shows that a carefully designed (but not complicated to implement) first order least squares method can solve the convection dominated diffusion problems well, and its linear system is always symmetric and positive definite.

110513.value: 一种新的用于简化混合模型的层次化期望值最大化算法

110513.label: Project Objectives
110513.value: Derive a new version of the HEM algorithm that learns a reduced mixture model that best represents the probability density of the base mixture model. Derive HEM for general probabilistic graphical models with hidden variables, using a local message-passing framework similar to belief propagation. Also derive approximations to HEM, such as variational HEM, when inference is intractable. Apply the new density-preserving HEM to a variety of applications, including efficient large-scale density estimation, Bayesian filtering, and belief propagation. Applications of HEM trees include fast nearest-neighbors search, and approximate partial matching between sets of distributions via the pyramid match kernel. Develop a software library for HEM that is extendable, allowing HEM to be easily used, and release the it to the machine learning community.

110513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
110513.value: 随着社交网络和云计算的发展，分析持续增长的大数据集（“大数据”）变得越来越重要。标准的机器学习工具，例如概率生成模型和相关的期望值最大化（EM）学习算法，在建模和分析现实世界数据方面取得了巨大的成功。但是EM方法在可扩展性和效率方面都面临着计算瓶颈。这使得使用生成式模型来处理大规模数据变得十分困难，即使这类模型十分适合处理这些数据中的各种情况，例如有歧义的数据和有噪音的标注。 层次化EM (HEM)算法可以通过把学习问题划分为两个部分，从而在原理上解决这些计算瓶颈：1) 把数据分解成多个较小的部分（例如一幅图像），并对每个部分使用EM方法来估计一个中间模型； 2）使用HEM将多个中间模型合并成最终模型。 HEM是EM的一种拓展, 它使用一个基混合模型（例如高斯混合模型）并把基混合组件（即高斯函数）聚类成多个组，同时学习一个新的聚类中心（即另一个高斯函数）来表示每个组。这些聚类中心是一个基于较少组件的简化混合模型的混合组件。这种方法和使用K-means算法聚类实值向量相似，但HEM使用概率分布来表示数据点。目前HEM在大数据上的应用包括对图像和音乐标注的效层次化密度估计和为快速索引建立索引树。 虽然HEM在这些应用中取得了成功，一些问题仍然需要被解决以便它能有更广泛的应用。首先，HEM的原始形式是一种多实例学习问题（MIL），鼓励常见的混合组件并抑制噪音，因此会扭曲简化混合模型，导致其偏离基密度。当从弱监督的数据中估计标注模型时，目的是在有噪音的训练数据中找出常见的特证。对于这种情况，HEM的这种特性十分有用。但是基于MIL的密度估计方法不适合用来估计用于有效表示基混合模型密度的简化混合模型。其次，对生成模型使用HEM需要推导特定的推论方法，其过程十分冗长而繁复。该项目的目的是为层次化估计开发一种新的“密度保持”的层次化EM算法。具体来说，该项目想要开发一种可以用来估计能够较好表示基混合密度的简化混合模型和一个相应的针对概率图模型的HEM通用推理过程。项目的最终成果是一个新的HEM框架。该框架可以被方便地应用到各种机器学习问题中，包括大规模密度估计，贝叶斯滤波，置信度传播和针对密度的快速最邻近点搜索。

110513.label: Realisation of objectives
110513.value: 1. A "density-preserving" (DP) version of HEM is derived, based on variational approximations to the expected log-likelihood. As a specific case, the DP-HEM for Gaussian mixture models is derived. 2. A variational HEM is derived for hidden Markov models with Gaussian mixture emissions. It is shown how successive variational lower-bounds can be constructed to perform approximate inference. A version for general probabilistic graphical models and local message-passing was not derived yet, and this is future work. 3. DP-HEM was tested on the following applications: as an inference method for belief propagation with GMM messages; recursive Bayesian filtering for vehicle self-localization and visual object tracking; mixture KDE reduction for check-in location modeling. HEM was also applied to eye gaze analysis using hidden Markov models. Ongoing work is applying DP-HEM for approximate inference in Gaussian process models with GMM likelihood functions. 4. The EMHMM toolbox for analyzing eye gaze is released -- the core part of the toolbox uses VHEM-HMM to cluster HMMs to discover common eye gaze strategies. Ongoing work is to release the DP-HEM toolbox in Python.

110513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
110513.value: The project studies how to efficiently model uncertainty for prediction. As more measurements are taken, the complexity of the prediction model increases, and the project derives an algorithm to reduce the complexity while preserving the fidelity of the model. The algorithm is applied to a variety of domains, including computer vision (visual tracking, self-localization), social media (check-in location analysis), and psychology (analyzing eye gaze patterns).

110713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
110713.value: 在微波以及红外波段之间的0.1 到10 THz常常被称为“太赫兹空隙（terahertz gap)”。就目前而言，市场上在该领域产业化可用的信号源及探测器並不多。这个新兴的领域被人们认为将会在未来高速率无线传播相关应用中扮演极其重要的角色，例如安全检查，生化光谱检测，生产质量控制等。而这些应用都必须建立在如太赫兹信号源，滤波器，等元件的研发之上，这正是香港城市大学国家毫米波实验室的重要的研究方向之一 。 香港城市大学现已和华盛顿大学的王伟志（Dr. Wei-Chih Wang）教授展开了试点研究合作。该研究将封装在聚酰亚胺薄层中的聚合物分散液晶（PDLC）用来制作魚网状的频率选择表面（FSS）。香港城市大学加工并且测试了这种可由电压控制的频率选择表面（FSS）。实验显示该选择表面（FSS）以0.87THz为中心频率，可调范围是10GHz，同时也成功的证实了这种用以聚合物分散液晶（PDLC）制作的频率选择表面（FSS）具有负折射率。但是，得到的结果也暴露出一些亟待解决的根本性的问题，例如较窄的可调范围，在魚网状结构的某些地方PDLC会被击穿等。因此在这个项目中，我们将会从不同的选择表面（FSS）单元结构特性入手，尝试使用多种聚合物及液晶的比重，同时优化材料厚度和生产工艺来提升可调范围并降低调控电压。

110713.label: Realisation of objectives
110713.value: This project requires modeling, design, fabrication and testing of tunable frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) in terahertz (THz) frequency range. The project can be divided into two parts, namely, passive FSSs and tunable FSSs. Successful design of tunable FSSs is built upon thorough investigations of the passive FSSs. Knowledge acquired from designing FSSs at microwave and millimeter-wave frequencies can also inform the designs at THz. For the tunable FSSs, device performances can be altered by either changing the operating frequency or replacing the dielectric substrate of the FSS with voltage controllable polymer disperse liquid crystal (PDLC). Tunability of the former depends on the choice of the pixel elements that have the required phase response while that of the latter depends on the amount of liquid crystal in the PDLC substrate as well as the substrate thickness. The objectives of the project include (i) enhancing the FSS performance through FSS unit-cell design, (ii) encapsulation of PDLC and mixing of liquid crystal and polymer matrix, (iii) optimizing thickness of each layer of FSS, PDLC and supporting structure, and (iv) fabrication and testing of the tunable FSS. We have achieved all these objectives initially through designing, fabricating and testing passive FSSs and later replacing the dielectric material with different ratios of liquid crystal and polymer matrix. At microwave and millimeter-wave frequencies, the devices were fabricated with the conventional printed-circuit-board technology. At millimeter-wave and THz frequencies, both 3D printing and micro-fabrication technologies were employed. We also conducted time-domain and frequency-domain techniques for THz measurements. For the investigation of unit-cell geometry, we have demonstrated that unit cells that have multiresonance can have phase response spanning several hundred degrees from which a frequency scanning reflectarray can be designed with a scanning range of 30 degrees from 0.2 to 0.3 THz. Lens antenna and frequency scanning lens antenna at 60 GHz and 0.3 THz have also been demonstrated using the same design principle, assuming that each of the pixels is a periodic structure similar to the FSS. The lens designs were realized by 3D printing. The scanning capability of the lens antenna at 0.3 THz is not as good as that at 60 GHz due to the resolution of our 3D printer. We have developed an equivalent circuit for a 3-layer, aperture coupled FSS from which 1 or 2 transmission zeros can be introduced to enhance the roll-off of the FSS filter at the edge(s) of the passband. Through the introduction of two transmission zeros, one on each side of the passband, high-selectivity FSS bandpass filters have been realized at 60 GHz and 0.85 THz. Through the THz bandpass filter realizations, we acquired the experience in micro-fabrication using Benzocyclobutene (BCB) polymer as a substrate layer for the FSS and as an encapsulation layer of PDLC or nematic liquid crystal. We also employed aluminum for the FSS metallization. The FSS was first fabricated on an aluminum back plane separated by a BCB protection layer. An aperture on the back plane was etched away after the completion of the micro-fabrication, exposing the FSS and forming a supporting structure. The thickness of each layer of the FSS structure has been optimized such that the insertion loss of the filter was minimized. For the 3-layer THz FSS bandpass filter, the measured center frequencies and 3-dB bandwidths are, respectively, 0.851 THz and 53 GHz (time-domain measurement), and 0.843 THz and 48.6 GHz (frequency-domain measurement), which are in agreement with the simulated 0.853 THz and 44 GHz. The measured insertion losses of 3.82 (time domain) and 3.77 dB (frequency domain) are larger than the simulated one (2.5 dB). We have also come up with an equivalent circuit for an FSS with the unit cell consisting of double square loops. This equivalent circuit has been exploited to design a THz FSS absorber at 0.9 THz with 0.102 THz bandwidth and less than -10 dB reflectivity. It has also been employed to realize a reflectarray at 0.875 THz with a 22 dBi gain. We have developed a novel sub-wavelength multiresonance unit-cell element with a Jerusalem cross and an open loop for a broadband single layer, dual circularly polarized (CP) reflectarray with linearly polarized feed. The x- and y-axis dimensions of the proposed element could be individually tuned and an optimization technique was used to minimize the phase errors on both orthogonal components. A single-layer offset fed 20 x 20-element dual-CP reflectarray with measured 1-dB gain and 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidths of 12.5% and 50%, respectively, has been realized at 12 GHz using PCB technology. The same design can be extended to THz using the micro-fabrication processes that we have developed for the THz FSSs. As presented in the last progress report, we had performed simulation study of an aperture-coupled FSS that exhibited a narrow bandpass frequency response with two transmission zeros. Using equivalent dielectric constants for a PDLC substrate under different bias voltages, an FSS having a tuning range of 11.5% (95 GHz) and narrow passband of 60 GHz had been simulated at 0.9 THz. The simulated insertion loss is 4.3 dB. Unfortunately, due to the alignment problem of the 3-layer FSS, we were not able to achieve frequency tuning of the FSS. Instead, we have designed and fabricated a 2-layer FSS with 1 transmission zero. The PDLC was UV-curable acrylate based pre-polymer mixed with 50 wt.%LC. When the bias voltage was increased from 0 to 200V, the transmission resonance frequency varied from 0.815 to 0.810 THz. The tuning range is only 5 GHz and the insertion loss is 5.7 dB due to the large absorption loss of the PDLC. This small tuning range is consistent with our earlier finding (C.-L. Chang, et al. “Tunable terahertz fishnet metamaterial,” Applied Physics Letters, 102(15):151903, 2013). Instead of using PDLC, we replaced the PDLC substrate with nematic liquid crystal. The measured results reveal a 3% tunability from 0.795 to 0.771 THz when the applied voltage between the two slotted FSS screens is tuned from 0 to 30V. Sharp corners of the cross-slots were rounded for avoiding breakdown of the LC under a large biasing voltage, which appeared in our work published in APL in 2013. The measured insertion losses of 2.37 (0 V) and 2.69 dB (30 V) are larger than the simulated one (1.33 dB) but are still small considering that the center frequency of the bandpass FSS filter is 0.795 THz. These insertion losses are smaller than the 3-layer aperture-coupled THz passive FSS (3.77dB) reported above.

110713.label: Major findings and research outcome
110713.value: The goals of this project are to advance frequency selective surface (FSS) technology and to demonstrate tunability with PDLC. Many planar devices have been designed by controlling the amplitude and phase responses of each of their pixel elements when they were illuminated by an electromagnetic source. These responses of the pixel element of concern were obtained by assuming that it is not standalone but periodic in the two orthogonal directions in the plane the planar device resides. Amplitude and phase libraries were generated for different pixel geometries and depending on the amplitude and phase requirements of the intended design, pixel elements meeting them would be assembled to form the device. Research Output 8.1-8.3, 8.6, 8.7, 9.1, and 9.2 investigated the frequency responses of various FSS unit-cell geometries and exploited their characteristics for designing (i) a planar prism with frequency tuning (8.1, 9.1), (ii) planar reflectors in the form of reflectarrays mimicking offset parabolic reflectors (8.2, 8.7), (iii) lens antennas with and without frequency tuning (8.2, 8.3), and (iv) linear to circular polarization converter (8.6). These works addressed Objective 1. In designing, fabricating and testing these devices at THz frequency, they also partly addressed Objectives 2, 3 and 4. For FSS bandpass filters, we have systematically developed an approach to introduce transmission zeros to enhance the selectivity of the filters (8.2, 8.4, 8.5, 9.2, 9.3). We have demonstrated even at THz frequency, the insertion loss of the filter is less than 4 dB for a 3-layer FSS. Again, the design, fabrication and measurement of these bandpass filters addressed Objective 1 and partly addressed Objectives 2-4. We have designed 3-layer FSS bandpass filters with 2 transmission zeros using PDLC substrates but contrary to our design using BCB substrate, we were not able to fabricate the PDLC FSS due to alignment problem. For a 2-layer FSS using 50% weight of LC, the measured tuning frequency is only 5 GHz with an applied voltage of 200V. We finally used nematic LC and successfully achieved a tuning range of 24 GHz (3%) at 0.795 THz with a tuning voltage of 30V. The insertion loss of the bandpass filter is only less than 3 dB. The finding is far better than the 6 GHz tuning range at 280V we have reported in our APL paper in 2013 which formed the basis of this project. The findings of this work address all the 4 objectives of this project.

110713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
110713.value: We have successfully designed a number of THz devices based on FSS technologies. The BCB substrate material is passive and not tunable. Replacing BCB with encapsulated liquid crystal as we have demonstrated in this project could substantially broaden the applications of these devices. Because of the alignment problem, we were not able to realize 3-layer tunable FSS bandpass filters with 2 transmission zeros. However, a new aligner is now available and we should be able to realize high-selectivity tunable THz FSS bandpass filters. In the present tunable THz FSS we have demonstrated, the FSS elements are cross-slots and they are connected for a single bias voltage. If we can design a biasing network that is similar to TV and mobile phone display panels, we can individually tune the effective dielectric constant of the pixel element such that THz beam steering devices can be realized. Of course, other tunable substrate materials can be used if their material loss at THz frequency is not serious. In our project, aluminum was used as it has a better adhesion to BCB substrate. Another research direction is to replace aluminum by graphene, which has plasmonic effects at THz.

110713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
110713.value: Frequency-selective surface (FSS) is composed of a periodic array of pixel elements and it has different frequency responses for different applications. The most commonly seen FSS is the screen, with periodic circular slots, appears on the door of every microwave oven. It allows light (very high frequency) to pass through but blocks the harmful microwave (low frequency) radiation from leaking out of the oven. This FSS screen is a highpass filter. The frequency response of this filter, however, cannot be altered. In this project, we have demonstrated many THz devices based on FSS technology including a planar prism, planar reflectors that mimic off-set parabolic reflectors, THz absorbers, linear to circular polarization converters and last but not least, tunable bandpass filters. The tunability of the bandpass filters is achieved by encapsulating liquid crystal (LC) as a substrate layer for the FSS with different voltages applied across the top and bottom surface of the LC substrate. A 3% tunability from 0.795 to 0.771 THz (24 GHz) is achieved with a tuning voltage of 30V. The measured transmission loss is 2.37 dB at 0V and 2.69 dB at 30V. Controlling the element tunability, we can realize beam steering devices at THz.

110813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
110813.value: Humans use their fingers to mediate the majority of mechanical interactions between themselves and the world. They are complex mechanical systems, both in terms of system dynamics and corresponding control. The sophistication of their coordination is beyond what the most advanced robot is capable of. Decades of experimental studies have already identified and described individual components of fingers, laying the ground for full understanding of how they operate. However, the signal transmission from the central neural commands to the muscular system is a highly nonlinear dynamic multi-input, multi-output (MIMO) system. This hinders an integrative understanding of the control mechanism at the system level. The proposed study aims to develop a hierarchical model to elucidate the interaction between neural and muscular bases of finger kinematics. These bases, in the context of functional networks in electroencephalography (EEG) and spinal modules in electromyography (EMG), have been postulated as an intelligent approach employed by the brain to facilitate control of a redundant system. Yet, how these bases interact across different system levels is largely unclear. A hierarchical modeling approach, describing the general information transformation from EEG signals, spinal modules, to muscle activities related to finger movements in healthy subjects, may offer a more reliable model structure for the prediction of finger kinematics from EEG recordings, something potentially beneficial to mobile motor prosthetic applications. Another important objective of this proposed study is to investigate the changes in neural modules, muscle synergies, and nonlinear dynamics of neuromuscular system associated with motor learning. By applying state-of-art estimation techniques, we will identify these changes in a mathematical and systematic manner. Furthermore, we postulate that such learning is consistent with an optimization principle of the neural and muscular modules. We will develop an objective function based on these neural and muscular modules to provide a mechanistic understanding of such optimal motor learning. The success of our work will provide a generalized framework for designing control algorithm in future neural prostheses. The physiologically plausible models developed may likewise contribute to novel biologically inspired control method to enhance the dexterity of robots. 人類與外界的互動大部分是通過手指協調完成的。無論從系統動力學還是控制學角度，手指都可被看作是非常尖端的機械系統。過去幾十年實驗和研究已經識別和描繪出了人類手指的各個組成部分，這些實驗結果為我們全面的了解手指的控制方式打下了基礎。但是，從中樞神經指令到肌肉系統的信號傳輸是一個高度非線性，多輸入，多輸出的系統。目前在系統層面上仍然缺乏對這種控制機制的綜合理解。 本研究課題旨在制定出一個層次模型，以此來闡明手指運動中神經模組和肌肉模組之間的相互作用。一個能夠描繪出健康人體中的信息從EEG（腦電圖）信號，脊髓模組，到手指運動引起的肌肉活動的轉變的層次建模方法可以为我們提供一個更加可靠的模型結構，由此我們可以從EEG的讀數中預測出手指的運動學數據。這項研究將會對運動神經修復一類的應用有幫助。 本課題的另外一個重要的目的是研究運動學習中神經模組，肌肉的協同作用和神經肌肉系統的非線性動力學特征的變化。我們將會利用目前最新的數學建模技術識別出這些變化。為了從數學的角度理解這種最優運動學習方法，我們將會在這些神經和肌肉模組的基礎上提出一個目標函數。我們的研究成果將會對未來神經修復技術中提出更加有效的控制算法提供一個基本的框架。在增加機器人的靈巧度上，這種生理學模型將有助於啟發新颖的控制方法。

110813.label: Realisation of objectives
110813.value: To elucidate the neural and muscular bases of finger kinematics (Objective 1) and to study neural correlates of multi-finger coordination (Objective 2), we developed mathematical models to elucidate the relationships between the brain, muscles and hand gestures, from electroencephalograph (EEG), electromyograph (EMG) and finger movements measured in a series of experiments. We investigated into the corticomuscular relationship during a grasping task by evaluating the information transfer between EEG and EMG signals (So et al., 2016). Information transfer was computed via a non-linear model-free measure, transfer entropy (TE). To examine the cross-frequency interaction, TEs were computed after the times series were decomposed into various frequency ranges via wavelet transform. Our results demonstrate the capability of TE to capture the direct interaction between EEG and EMG. In addition, the cross-frequency analysis revealed instantaneous decrease in information transfer from EEG to the high frequency component of EMG (100-200Hz) during the onset of movement. On investigating neural connectivity, directionality indices can be used as an indicator of the asymmetry in coupling between systems and have found particular application in relation to neurological systems. The directionality index between two systems is a function of measures of information transfer in both directions. In this project, we illustrated that before inferring the directionality of coupling it is first necessary to consider the use of appropriate tests of significance (Jelfs & Chan, 2017). We proposed a surrogate corrected directionality index which incorporates such testing. We also highlighted the differences between testing the significance of the directionality index itself versus testing the individual measures of information transfer in each direction. To validate the approach, we compared two different methods of estimating coupling, both of which have previously been used to estimate directionality indices. These were the modeling-based evolution map approach and a conditional mutual information (CMI) method for calculating dynamic information rates. For both Objectives 1 and 2, we also investigated how muscle activities drive different hand gestures, which can be applied to human-computer interface development. Hand movement classification based on surface electromyography (sEMG) pattern recognition is a promising approach for upper limb neuroprosthetic control. However, maintaining day-to-day performance is challenged by the non-stationary nature of sEMG in real-life operation. In this study, we developed a self-recalibrating classifier that can be automatically updated to maintain a stable performance over time without the need for user retraining (Zhai et al., 2017). Our classifier is based on convolutional neural network (CNN) using short latency dimension-reduced sEMG spectrograms as inputs. The pretrained classifier was recalibrated routinely using a corrected version of the prediction results from recent testing sessions. Our proposed system was evaluated with the NinaPro database comprising of hand movement data of 40 intact and 11 amputee subjects. Our system was able to achieve ∼10.18% (intact, 50 movement types) and ∼2.99% (amputee, 10 movement types) increase in classification accuracy averaged over five testing sessions with respect to the unrecalibrated classifier. When compared with a support vector machine (SVM) classifier, our CNN-based system consistently showed higher absolute performance and larger improvement as well as more efficient training. These results suggest that the proposed system can be a useful tool to facilitate long-term adoption of prosthetics for amputees in real-life applications. Fingertip force coordination is another crucial factor to the success of multi-finger coordination tasks. In the development of motor prosthesis for daily applications, the ability to accurately classify the desired grasp-and-lift from multi-channel sEMG is essential. In order to extract reliable indicators for fingertip force coordination, we searched an extensive set of sEMG features for the optimal subset of relevant features (Wei, Chow & Chan, 2015; Li, Jelfs & Chan, 2017). Using mutual information based feature selection we found that a subset of not more than 10 sEMG features selected from over seven thousand, could effectively classify object weights in grasp-and-lift tasks. Average classification accuracies of 82.53% in the acceleration phase and 88.61% in the isometric contraction phase were achieved. Furthermore, sEMG features associated with object weights and common across individuals were identified. These time-domain features (entropy, mean/median absolute deviation, pNNx) can be calculated efficiently, providing possible new indicators. To further study the neural correlates of multi-finger coordination (Objective 2) and to identify neural changes during the learning of new gestures (Objective 3), we developed new techniques for high-resolution time-frequency analysis (Li et al., 2016), and we investigated finger coordination through a series of experiments at different motor skill levels. Using a wireless single channel EEG device, we investigated the feasibility of using short-term frontal EEG as a means to evaluate the dynamic changes of mental workload (So et al., 2017). Frontal EEG signals were recorded from twenty healthy subjects performing four cognitive and motor tasks, including arithmetic operation, finger tapping, mental rotation and lexical decision task. Our findings revealed that theta activity is the common EEG feature that increases with difficulty across four tasks. Meanwhile, with a short-time analysis window, the level of mental workload could be classified from EEG features with 65%±75% accuracy across subjects using a SVM model. These findings suggest that frontal EEG could be used for evaluating the dynamic changes of mental workload. For Objective 3, another study assessed the differences in the joint kinematics when playing the piano between highly experienced individuals and those with no experience (Jelfs et al., 2015). The purpose of the study was to highlight differences in the movement of the fingers between the two groups with the aim of using the findings when assessing the neural and muscular systems involved in producing finger movement. Piano playing is skill which requires coordination of both the movement of fingers in sequence and simultaneously making it ideally suited to assess coordination. The study indicated that differences in the level of coordination did not cause large changes in the way subjects move. In fact, the differences which produce more coordinated movements lie in small changes to the patterns of finger kinematics. We have also looked into possible objective function of motor modules for the optimization of coordination (Objective 4). The concept of muscle synergies has proven to be an effective method for representing patterns of muscle activation. The number of degrees of freedom to be controlled are reduced while also providing a flexible platform for producing detailed movements using synergies as building blocks. It has been shown in this project that small components of movement are crucial to producing precise and coordinated movement (Jelfs et al., 2015). Methods which focus on the variance of the data make it possible to overlook these small components in the synergy extraction process. However, algorithms which address the inherent complexity in the neuromuscular system are lacking. To that end we developed a new nonnegative matrix factorization algorithm which employed a cross fuzzy entropy similarity measure, thus, extracting muscle synergies which preserve the complexity of the recorded muscular data (Jelfs et al., 2016). The performance of the proposed algorithm was illustrated on representative EMG data.

110813.label: Major findings and research outcome
110813.value: In this research project, we developed mathematical models to elucidate the relationships between the brain, muscles and hand gestures, from electroencephalograph (EEG), electromyograph (EMG) and finger movements measured in experiments. We first investigated the feasibility of using EEG as a means to evaluate mental workload in a finger tapping task (So et al., 2017). Our findings revealed that theta activity is the common EEG feature that increases with difficulty when more fingers are involved. On the neural level, we have developed a series of computational methods for selecting features (Wei, Chow & Chan, 2015), investigating neural connectivity (She, Chen & Chan, 2016; Jelfs & Chan, 2017) and modelling time-varying systems (Li et al., 2016; Xu et al., 2017). We then investigated the corticomuscular relationship during a grasping task (So et al., 2016). The cross-frequency analysis revealed instantaneous decrease in information transfer from EEG to the high frequency component of EMG during the onset of movement. On the muscular level, we showed that we could predict a wide range of hand gestures (Zhai et al., 2017) and also object weights (Li, Jelfs & Chan, 2017) involved in grasping with high accuracy from surface EMG measured at the arm, which will be crucial to the development of hand prosthetics. Along the way, we have identified the differences in the recruitment of synergies between both novice and experienced pianists (Jelfs et al., 2015). It has been shown in this project that small components of movement are crucial to producing precise and coordinated movement. We developed a new nonnegative matrix factorization algorithm which employed a cross fuzzy entropy similarity measure, thus, extracting muscle synergies which preserve the complexity of the recorded muscular data (Jelfs et al., 2016). The performance of the proposed algorithm was illustrated on representative EMG data. Through these studies, our team observed that motion at wrist actually capture some movements related to hand gesture. Therefore, we investigated hand gesture recognition from acoustic measurements at wrist for the development of a low-cost wearable human-computer interaction (HCI) device (Siddiqui & Chan, 2017). A prototype with microphone sensors on human wrist was benchmarked in hand gesture recognition performance by identifying 36 gestures in American Sign Language (ASL). Ten features were extracted from the signal recorded by each sensor. The average classification accuracy was above 80%. Based on these preliminary results, our proposed technique exhibited a promising means for developing a low-cost HCI.

110813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
110813.value: On the further development of the research, we propose to significantly improve the control mechanism of assistive robotic devices by fusing electrophysiological signals with visual information from video cameras using state-of-the-art artificial intelligence technologies, in particular deep learning. This fusion of technology will allow for better classification of electrophysiological signals and a clearer understanding of the physical environment, which together will create more effective control in the execution of robotic tasks. We will focus on developing practical neural interface using surface electromyography (sEMG) and electroencephalogram (EEG) as separate examples to help patients with different levels of musculoskeletal damages or neurodegenerative diseases. A novel signal fusion technique will be developed to control robotic reach-to-grasp movements using EEG or sEMG, together with visual clues. The proposed approach will encompass different electrophysiological signals, sensor data of different modalities, and various target tasks. This proposal was submitted to UGC GRF last year. In the meantime, we will further develop the hand gesture recognition device, and transfer the technology to the industry.

In this research project, we developed mathematical models to elucidate the relationships between the brain, muscles and hand gestures, from electroencephalograph (EEG), electromyograph (EMG) and finger movements measured in a series of experiments. We first investigated the feasibility of using EEG as a means to evaluate mental workload in a finger tapping task. Our findings revealed that theta activity is the common EEG feature that increases with difficulty when more fingers are involved. Then, we investigated the corticomuscular relationship during a grasping task. 111013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
111013.value: 在诸如生物电子植入技术、干细胞治疗这些视网膜水平上的视觉修复方法中，大脑的动态特性扮演着重要的角色。发展这些技术旨在治疗主要的致盲疾病，比如由于感光细胞退化而导致的视网膜色素变性，该疾病会使中枢神经系统回路丧失对视觉信息输入和重塑的能力。中国的研究者最近发现，视网膜色素变性的发病率大约是1/1000，全国大约有130万人受到该疾病的影响。而治疗方法能否成功在很大程度上依赖于整个视觉通路中存活细胞的机能。因此，为了使视网膜疾病患者能够感知到视觉影象的细节，不光是视网膜，视皮层也发挥着重要作用。然而，感知信息的变化会随着时间改变视神经的感受域和皮层映射图。 有关成人视皮层的研究表明，皮层重组作为视网膜黄斑退化的结果会导致中枢视觉系统的衰退。由于视网膜色素变性而产生的皮层重映射会引起外周视觉系统的缺失，对此人们知之甚少。最近，仅有的一项研究（Gias et.al. 2011）指出在视网膜退化的动物模型中会出现皮层功能的退化。然而，在视网膜退化过程中，视皮层神经元感受域的强度和尺寸以及视网膜映射图的改变都不得而知。 本实验室提出了一种新的方法，即利用视紫红质突变的动物模拟人类的视网膜色素变性（S334ter），然后通过记录视皮层中的视觉诱发及自发放电活动，从而研究视网膜退化过程中的视皮层重组。在研究的第一阶段，需要确定S334ter大鼠在失去光感细胞后皮层功能退化的进程。每个被记录细胞的皮层反应都会用电生理方法进行测量。在第二阶段，我们将会研究S334ter大鼠视皮层的视网膜映射活动。本研究不仅会提供长时程视觉缺失后的视皮层状况信息，还将揭示内层视网膜和视皮层的功能连接。此外，动物模型中的生理学指标将有助于指导视网膜治疗活动，以及测定视皮层中的退化或改变是否会限制这些治疗方法的效用。

111013.label: Realisation of objectives
111013.value: Objectives 1 & 2: Summary - We have successfully examined the basic response properties of visual cortex in normal sighted animal and animal with retinal degeneration (S334ter rat) by measuring the spontaneous firing, the orientation selectivity, the spatial tuning, and the temporal tuning. We also examined the extent of degeneration to the retinotopic organization of the visual cortex in animal with retinal degeneration (S334ter rat) by measuring the receptive field size of visual cortical neurons. Methodology: Animal preparation - Acute experimental recordings were made from 11 S334ter-line-3 and 10 Long-Evans immature rats that were 55-85 days of age. S334ter-line-3 (S334ter-3) rat litters were obtained by breeding transgenic homozygotes (with two copies of the mutant transgene) with Long-Evans rats. Hence, the experimental rats (S334ter-3) carried one copy of the mutant transgene. LE and S334ter-3 rats (3-4 months of age) were used as the WT and retinal degeneration model, respectively. The animal was anesthetized with an intraperitoneal injection of Ketamine-Xylazine combination (Ketamine: 70 mg/kg and Xylazine: 7 mg/kg) initially; then, 2% isoflurane (RWD Life Science, Shenzhen, China) was applied during the recording. After the craniotomy, a bone screw was fixed in the skull and a tungsten electrode was placed on the surface of the primary visual cortex as the ground and recording electrodes, respectively. The exposed cortical surface was covered with 2% agar to prevent drying and reduce the body oscillation caused by breathing; then, a shield was used to attenuate environmental interference. The animal was maintained at 38°C using a warm pad, and ocular solution was regularly applied to keep the eyes moist throughout the procedures, including the recording session. Visual stimulation and recording - The A-M Systems 3600 (A-M Systems, US) and CED Micro 1401-3 (Cambridge Electronic Design, UK) were used as the amplifier and data acquisition system, respectively. Tungsten-in-glass microelectrodes were used to record single units extracellularly. As the microelectrode was advanced slowly by the oil hydraulic micromanipulator (MO-10, Narishige, Japan), various stimuli were displayed across the animal’s visual field to activate the cells. Single-unit activity was filtered from 0.5-5 kHz and then sampled at 40 kHz using an acquisition card (National Instrument, USA). Stimuli were presented in black and white mode on a Dell monitor (screen size 35x26 cm, frame rate 60 Hz, and resolution 800x600 pixels) positioned 23 cm from the rat’s eye (the screen occupied 75x58° in the visual field). Each experiment consisted of several blocks of trials in which stimuli with particular parameter values were presented in a random order to minimize the possible effects of response variability. The results of several repeated blocks (typically 5 but not less than 3) were averaged. Responses to a uniform field of averaged luminance were also recorded to measure the neuron’s spontaneous firing rate. Peri-stimulus time histograms (PSTHs) of unit responses were generated and analysed on-line using custom-made software. Then, the rat was euthanized with an overdose of dorminal (300 mg/kg). Result 1 – Orientation selectivity alteration in the degenerated group: The orientation selectivity index was defined to be (OSI)= (Ropt-Rver)/(Ropt-Rspon), where Ropt and Rver were responses to optimal and orthogonal to optimal orientation, respectively, and Rspon was the spontaneous activity. The OSI indicated the variation in the response between the orthogonal to the optimal orientation. The larger the OSI, the better the orientation selectivity. The average OSI was 0.67±0.23 for the S334ter-3 rats (n=58) and 0.82±0.19 for the LE rats (n=69). There was a significant difference in the OSI between the degenerated group and the control group (P=0.0004, Mann-Whitney U test). Result 2 – Alterations in spatial and temporal tunings in the degenerated group: We used six different spatial frequencies to measure the cell’s responses. We classified the optimal spatial frequencies as the low spatial frequency (≤0.04 cpd) and high spatial frequency (≥0.08 cpd). Twenty cells (38.5%) from the S334ter-3 rats and 17 (28.8%) from the LE rats had an optimal response at the low frequency (≤0.04 cpd). The other cells had an optimal spatial response at the high spatial frequency (≥0.08 cpd). Although more S334ter-3 neurons had optimal responses at the low spatial frequency, there was no significant difference in the distribution of the optimal spatial frequencies in the high and low spatial frequencies in the degenerated group and the control group (P=0.282, Chi-square test). We used eight different temporary frequencies to measure the responses of rat V1 neurons. The results showed that 27 cells (65.9%) in the S334ter-3 rats and 32 (46.4%) cells in the LE rats had optimal responses at ≤1.72 Hz. The other cells had optimal responses at the high temporary frequency. More cells in the S334ter-3 rats had their optimal temporary frequencies at the low temporary frequency compared to the control group. There was a significant difference in the optimal temporary frequencies distributed in the high and low temporary frequencies between the S334ter-3 and LE rats (P=0.048, Chi-square test). Result 3 – Decrease in the receptive field in the degenerated group: We measured how the response amplitude depended on the stimulus diameter. The average RFs were 8.1±2.1 degrees for the cells in the S334TER-3 rats and 12.9±4.4 degrees for the cells in the LE rats. There was a significant difference in the RFs between the S334ter-3 and LE rats (P<0.001, Mann-Whitney U test). No significant difference was found in the RFs between the different layers (P>0.05 for all comparisons, Mann-Whitney U test). Objective 3: Summary – We have successfully studied the brain response to retinal electrical stimulation in normal sighted animal and animal with retinal degeneration (S334ter rat) by examining the effect of spatial extent on various stimulus parameters including stimulus frequency, interpulse interval and pulse duration, using single channel stimulation on retina. Result - Effect of stimulus parameters on visual cortex responses to single channel electrical stimulation of the retina: The spatial correspondence of EEP responses to single retinal stimulation was examined in this study. Electric stimulation single channel stimulation was used to induce the responses in the contralateral visual cortex. A 16-channel recording array (length of electrode: 3 mm, arrangement: 4×4, size of array: 1.2mm × 1.2mm; Spacing: 0.4 mm; Clunburry Scientific LLC, Minnesota, USA) was inserted 1 mm depth in the exposed visual cortex for in vivo electrophysiological recording to single channel retinal electrical stimulation. A total of 10 amplitudes (20 µA – 200 µA) were used, each lasting 500-ms to 10-s with 4 stimulus frequencies ranged from 1 to 20 Hz. For each amplitude, 10 identical stimuli were delivered. For each stimulus frequency, 4 pulse durations were used (200-µs, 500-µs, 1000-µs, 1500-µs) Spatial activation maps were generated according to their location relative to the stimulating electrode. Each grid bin represents the summation of responses for 20 amplitudes in one recording electrode. Long pulse duration (~1-s and 1.5-s) could better activate the neurons in the primary visual cortex than short pulse duration (0.2-s and 0.5-s) in 3 of the representative experiments, as shown. Neurons in the primary visual cortex were better activated in low stimulus frequencies (1 Hz and 5 Hz) than in high frequencies (10 Hz and 20 Hz). These results may suggest that visual cortical neurons tend to prefer low stimulus frequencies.

111013.label: Major findings and research outcome
111013.value: The present study focused on the comparison between receptive field properties in V1 cells from S334ter-3 and LE rats. The dynamic nature of the brain is critical for the success of treatments aimed at restoring vision at the retinal level. The success of these treatments relies highly on the functionality of the surviving neurons along the entire visual pathway. Electrophysiological properties at the retina level have been investigated during the progression of retinal degeneration; however, little is known about the changes in electrophysiological properties that occur in the primary visual cortex (V1) during the course of retinal degeneration. By conducting extracellular recording, we examined the electrophysiological properties of V1 in S334ter-line-3 rats. We measured the orientation tuning, spatial and temporal frequency tunings and the receptive field (RF) size for 127 V1 neurons from 11 S334ter-3 rats and 10 Long-Evans (LE) rats. V1 neurons in the S334ter-3 rats showed weaker orientation selectivity, lower optimal spatial and temporal frequency values and a smaller receptive field size compared to the LE rats. These results suggest that the visual cognitive ability significantly changes during retinal degeneration. We have completed this work and published in two international recognized journals, Scientific Reports and Neuroscience Letters. We have also systematically investigated how a range of stimulating parameters (current level, stimulus pulse duration, and stimulus frequency) influences the spatial interactions in the neural network of the primary visual cortex. Previous studies have revealed that short pulses (for example, 0.1 ms) excite retinal ganglion cells preferentially, whereas longer pulses (for example, 1 ms) excite both retinal ganglion cells and bipolar cells. However, there is little information about how stimulus pulse duration and stimulus frequency affect the spatial extent of primary visual cortical neurons activation. In the present study, we mapped the activation patterns of primary visual cortical responses to a range of stimulus pulse durations, from 0.2-ms to 1.5- ms. Long pulse duration (~1-s and 1.5-s) could better activate the neurons in the primary visual cortex than short pulse duration (0.2-s and 0.5-s) in 3 of the representative experiments. Neurons in the primary visual cortex were better activated in low stimulus frequencies (1 Hz and 5 Hz) than in high frequencies (10 Hz and 20 Hz). These results may suggest that visual cortical neurons tend to prefer low stimulus frequencies. This work has been completed and the manuscript is on-going.

111013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
111013.value: There are two suggested future developments of the present study. First, local field potentials, containing low-frequency fluctuations in the electrical potential generatd by local and more remote neurons, could be recorded and analyzed in the visual cortex of mice with retinal degeneration. Second, signals from the interneurons and pyramidal neurons could be recorded. Their response properties such as orientating tuning, spatial and temporal tunings, as well as the contrast response, repective field size for each type of neuron could be measured and analyzed.

111013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
111013.value: Several different treatments using gene-specific, stem-cell therapy and bioelectronic implant approaches have been proposed to restore vision to the blind. Inherited retinal degeneration disease such as retinitis pigmentosa (RP) has led hundreds of thousand people around the world with poor vision or no vision. Under circumstances in which the retinas of individuals undergo degeneration, reorganization along the visual pathway occurs, including the neural retina and the visual cortex. The study of the condition of visual organization after deprivation of sensory input is paramount because many of the most promising treatments aimed at restoring visions at the retinal level, such as retinal prosthetics, stem-cell therapy and gene-specific approach, reply on the assumption that cortical circuitry remains largely intact. The present study has systematically investigated the response properties of visual cortical neurons in both normal sighted and retinal degenerated rats. The results showed that the visual cortical cells in the retinal generate rats exhibited weaker orientation selectivity, lower optimal spatial and temporal frequency values, and smaller receptive fields compared to the cells in normal sighted rats. These results suggest that the visual cognitive ability significantly changes during retinal degeneration.

111213.value: To demonstrate parallel detection of optical chaos for parallel random bit generation. By optical heterodyning, different slices of the chaotic optical spectrum will be down-converted to different parallel channels. Reduction in the requirements on the high-speed electronics will be examined. 111213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
111213.value: Semiconductor lasers in chaotic dynamics are unique light sources with random-like intensity oscillations. Emissions from these chaotic lasers with their intrinsic noise are excellent for generating broadband electrical signals, which can be sampled, digitized, and sent through proper electronic signal processing to yield sequences of random bits. Such approach of random bit generation using laser chaos excels in its extraordinarily high bit rate compared to the conventional methods. The output bit sequences are of perfect or high randomness as indicated by some practical statistical tests. Our research group and many other groups around the globe have spent continual efforts on improving the techniques of random bit generation using chaotic lasers. However, most of the investigations have relied heavily on high-speed electronics. The chaotic emission from a laser needs to go through an optical-to-electronic (O/E) conversion using a photodetector and enter an analogue-to-digital converter (ADC). High-speed post-processing electronics are also needed to eliminate any residual orders of the digitized waveforms for maintaining sufficiently high randomness at the output. An operation of discarding the most significant bits (MSBs) is commonly used by adopting high-resolution ADCs. The disadvantages of relying on these electronics include the relatively high cost for the high-speed components and the restrictions on only partially using the chaotic emission bandwidths. In this proposal, all-optical parallel chaos-based random bit generation without using high-speed electronics is considered. A parallel detection scheme is proposed by optical heterodyning the chaotic emission into different channels, where different slices of the chaotic optical spectrum is down-converted into the baseband for detection using photodetectors of moderate bandwidths. Then, an all-optical post-processing scheme is considered by injecting the chaotic emission into a laser in period-one (P1) oscillation. Because the P1 frequency is dependent on the injection, the resultant emission can exhibit strong chaotic frequency modulation. A delayed interferometer can then introduce a wrapping of the chaotic waveforms, which is equivalent to an operation of discarding MSBs. Such all-optical post-processing replaces the electrical one, thereby alleviating the ADC resolution requirements. Additionally, with the above schemes, the output optical signal is slow enough for feeding into commercial field-programmable gate arrays, which offer great computation power in allowing transformation of the bit statistics. Random bits of not only uniform distribution but also other important statistical distributions can be generated. Success of the proposed all-optical parallel schemes will improve the practicality of applying chaotic lasers for random bit generation. 混沌態中的半導體激光器的是一種有類隨機強度震蕩的獨特光源。混沌激光因為其內部噪聲能產生寬帶電信號。經過採樣，量化，以及適當的電信號處理，最終用來產生隨機數序列。關於混沌激光產生的隨機數，其速率遠遠高於傳統方法產生的隨機數。同時，經實踐性統計驗證，混沌激光產生的隨機數具有較高的隨機性。近年來, 利用混沌激光產生隨機數在全世界得到深入研究。然而，目前大多數的實現方案都需要藉助高速電子器件。例如，混沌激光信號需要先經過高速光電探測器實現光電信號轉換。 然後經過模數轉換器（ADC）產生數字信號。而且採用多位模數轉換以及去掉最高有效位（MSBs）等後期高速電信號處理，以消除數字信號中殘留的相關信息，進一步提高信號的隨機性。上述方案需要依賴於昂貴的高速電子器件，同時由於電子器件帶寬的限制，激光器產生的寬帶混沌信號在頻域上也不能得到充分利用。本項目提出混沌激光產生平行隨機數的全光實現方案，而且不須採用高速電子器件。通過光外差探測混沌激光信號實現多通道平行輸出，每個通道將寬帶混沌激光信號的一部分頻譜搬移至基帶，以便應用低速光電探測器進行光電轉換。此外，將混沌激光注入處於單週期震蕩（P1）狀態的另一個激光器，可進一步實現全光後期處理。由於P1的震蕩頻率與外部注入有關，進而可以實現顯著的混沌頻率調製。通過延遲干涉儀的混沌信號實現的波形混疊，可以達到與去掉MSBs的相同效果。基於以上方案的全光後期處理突破了現有技術因電子器件帶寬導致的瓶頸，因而減緩了對高精度ADC的需求。同時，所產生的低頻光信號足以兼容現有的場式可程式閘陣列 (FPGA), 其卓越的計算能力可以實現隨機數分佈的轉換輸出。最終產生的隨機數不僅可以服從均勻分佈，還可以服從其他重要的統計學分佈。以上全光平行輸出方案的實現將會進一步提高混沌激光信號產生隨機數的實用性及可行性。

111213.label: Realisation of objectives
111213.value: The project aims to harness the chaotic dynamics of semiconductor lasers for random bit generation (RBG). It intends to investigate and demonstrate high-speed, physically random, and optical RBG that is useful in applications such as encryption and computation. The proposal successfully considered a number of schemes for optical chaotic RBG to facilitate these applications. Optical chaos was first invoked through utilizing optical feedback, grating feedback, as well as optical injection, where the chaotic waveforms were manipulated for approaching a featureless random signal. The chaotic oscillations allowed the demonstration of RBG with improved randomness properties and tunable bit rates. The objectives have been addressed over the duration of the project. Objective 1 was about demonstrating optical chaos-based RBG through the techniques of down-conversion to the baseband. The objective was achieved by developing different methods. These include the use of heterodyne detection that shifts the fast chaotic oscillations to the baseband for electronic detection with an alleviated bandwidth requirement. The heterodyning enabled the use of different parts of the chaotic spectrum for an output channel. As the grating-feedback heterodynes with the signal in the laser, continuous tuning of the output bit rate, reduction of the minimum sampling period, and increment of the number of bits selected per sample were realized. Objective 2 was to investigate the processing of the signal through the optically controlled oscillation through injection. Such an objective was studied by driving the laser in the nonlinear dynamical period-one oscillation. A demonstration of the so-called frequency-modulated continuous-wave signal generation was reported. An alternative method for the generation of fluctuating signals in the baseband was realized via modulation instability (MI) for RBG. Correlated RBG became possible from the MI output pulses in the anti-Stokes and Stoke sidebands. Objective 3 was about implementing bit statistics transformation using field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) with optical inputs. The randomness of the optical inputs was verified by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) test suite. By again utilizing heterodyne detection, the chaotic oscillation frequencies were down-shifted to the baseband, which suited the post-processing by the FPGAs. A high-speed discrete Gaussian sampler based on optical chaos was then implemented. As an important outcome of the project, an approach was developed for fundamentally measuring the randomness in optical chaos. It was achieved through both experimentally and numerically measuring the Shannon entropy. The approach was based on state-space reconstruction from the high-speed measurements of the intensity of optical chaos. The results verified the fast generation of randomness as manifested through the rapid growth of the fundamental physical entropy. The chaotic dynamics was found to amplify the effect of laser noise in yielding a nearly maximal entropy on a subnanosecond time scale.

111213.label: Major findings and research outcome
111213.value: The research contributed to 6 journal publications and 6 conference papers. It directly supported the training of 1 Ph.D. student on the topic of optical chaotic RBG. The project enabled collaborations with different local and non-local groups. The major findings of this project are summarized as follows. The project was enabled by the improved chaotic waveforms generated in the laser through grating-feedback for time-delay concealment. While the suppression of the time-delay signature has been mainly studied in another project, the usage of the waveform for RBG was further investigated in this project. The results on the waveform generation were documented in journal publication [1] and conference publications [2-3] in Part C. Experimentally, by a simple postprocessing of self-differencing, RBG was obtained even when the sampling period was commensurate with the feedback delay time. The sampling period was continuously tunable down to 50 ps with no unwanted residual correlation. RBG at a tunable rate of up to 100 GHz was verified by the NIST tests. The results were documented in journal publication [3] and conference publications [5-6] in Part C. Moreover, a variation of RBG through manipulating the MI dynamics in fibers was demonstrated. By sending a pump pulse through a highly nonlinear fiber, MI generate pulses with baseband amplitude fluctuations for RBG at 50 Gbps. Another variation was demonstrated for intensity-to-frequency conversion of modulation through the period-one dynamics of a laser for tuning the oscillation frequency with a fast sweep rate of 0.42 GHz/ns. The results were documented in journal publications [2, 5] and conference publication [1] in Part C. Furthermore, a high-speed discrete Gaussian sampler was recently realized on a FPGA that was fed with laser chaos after heterodyne detection at the baseband. Instead of the conventional uniform distribution profile in optical chaos-based RBG, the FPGA allowed for the implementation of a real discrete Gaussian sampler at a throughput of up to 40 MSPS. The results were documented in journal publication [6] in Part C. Additionally, the project enabled a more fundamental study of the randomness generated by the laser dynamics. By chaotic attractor reconstruction, both experimental and numerical data revealed a fast generation of Shannon entropy as quantified by the time-dependent exponents (TDEs). The estimated entropy supports the generation of physical randomness a rate reaching 200 Gbps. The results were documented in journal publication [4] and conference publication [4] in Part C.

111213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
111213.value: This project contributed to RBG with a demonstration of bit rate tunability reaching the order of 100 Gbps, an implementation of generating non-uniformly distributed random numbers, as well as the first experimental verification of randomness through a fundamental entropy measurement. The following questions emerged as interesting topics for further investigations. 1. Can the entropy measurements be adopted for setting a limit of the bit rate? Rather than simply relying on the statistical tests, such as those from NIST, the use of attractor reconstruction more fundamentally quantifies the physical entropy. This can potentially be developed as a more reliable verification of randomness for security and computational applications. 2. Can synchronization of the chaotic signal from grating-feedback be utilized for key distribution? With the ability of generating physically random bits at a high-speed, the research is being extended for applications in key distribution. This goal is being pursued in another project at the moment. 3. Can the approach of using MI for RBG be extended to other nonlinear optical processes? By developing approaches for maintaining the possibility of chaos synchronization, these nonlinear processes can be utilized for chaotic RBG at significantly increased rates.

111213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
111213.value: Random bits generated at high-speed is of central importance for computational, security, and encryption applications. Semiconductor lasers offer solutions for RBG based on their inherently fast dynamics that alleviates the need of costly electronic components through the extraction of physical randomness. Building on the results supported by the earlier research projects, this project developed and improved the performances of optical chaos-based RBG. The project successfully contributed to the advancements in high-speed RBG in various aspects. RBG was realized with a tunable bit rate by invoking chaos through injection and grating-feedback. RBG with non-uniform distribution was realized by feeding a baseband chaos signal to FPGA through heterodyning. RBG using the fluctuating signals in MI through optical fibers was realized. Moreover, frequency-modulated continuous-wave signal generation was demonstrated for amplitude-to-frequency waveform conversion. Furthermore, different from the practical approaches based on statistical randomness tests, the project developed a reconstruction-based approach for measuring the physical entropy. The rapid growth of entropy was verified both numerically and experimentally as a more fundamental quantification of randomness, thereby providing support to the area of optical chaos-based RBG in general. Based on these advancements, RBG for secret key distribution for security applications can continually be pursued in the future.

111313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
111313.value: Program testing is the most widely-practiced approach to exposing real failures from software applications and assuring their quality during software development. With the advent of the mulitcore architecture, multithreaded software applications are increasingly integrated to our living environments. Nonetheless, critical concurrent bugs such as deadlocks are from time to time reported by end users of many large-scale multithreaded software applications, indicating that the testing methods applied to them are still far from being adequate to cope with the challenges in real-world software development. Deadlocks stop programs from making progress. When users are performing critical activities that rely on multithreaded programs, deadlocks will be a nightmare. Static analysis or model checking techniques are well known to be imprecise. These techniques could not firmly and consistently expose real failures from multithreaded programs. Dynamic approach to testing is essential and demonstrates the ability to expose real failures instead of simply reporting that such a program has the potential to form deadlocks in some program runs. Nonetheless, our recent work has shown that existing state-of-the-art dynamic techniques are not consistently effective in exposing deadlocks that they target to detect. We have further found that sometimes they may systematically fail to expose certain deadlock bugs. If this is the case, then testers should manually confirm whether the scenarios are really the threats of the programs that they are developing and clear the threats if needed. Such manual inspection and judgment could be tedious and error-prone. New, precise and automated techniques that effectively expose deadlock failures should be developed to facilitate companies to implement high quality multithreaded software applications with pleasant user experience. This project aims at developing a novel C-AGENDA framework to support a Constraint-sensitive Approach to GENeration of Deadlock test schedules for multithreaded Applications that addresses all the above challenges. We propose to investigate the essential constraints and swappable constraints in a deadlock-free concurrent execution of a multithreaded program. We then use these constraints to model how a potential deadlock scenario could become a real nightmare (deadlock) in some other executions and divert the testing effort to confirm whether such a scenario is really a nightmare. The success of this project provides a highly effective framework to the industry to expose real deadlocks. We will also use this project to educate research students. 在软件开发过程中，软件测试技术被广泛用于发掘软件失效和保证软件质量上。近年来随着计算机多核架构的迅速发展，多线程软件逐渐应用到社会的各个领域。然而，在用户使用过程中，许多大型的多线程软件仍时常出现诸如死锁等严重的并发错误。这些事实说明当前的测试技术远未充分解决实际软件开发过程中所遇到的种种挑战。死锁会导致程序停止运行。所以当用户的关键工作依赖于多线程程序进行时，死锁的发生无疑是一场噩梦。 研究人员所熟悉的静态分析技术或者模型检测技术被公认为是不精确的。这些技术无法准确且持续有效地发现真实的软件失效。相比之下，动态测试方法则在程序失效的检测中是必需的，它能够证实程序中存在的真实失效而非简单地分析程序中存在死锁的可能性。然而，我们最近的研究表明，现有的动态检测技术并不能持续有效地检测出它们期望检测到的死锁。我们还进一步发现，这些技术常常系统性地遗失对特定死锁缺陷的检测。在这种情况下，测试人员必须人工地确认这些不确定的情况是否会严重影响到他们的程序的执行。对于可能存在的的严重威胁，测试人员必须清除。这种人工检查和判断的过程是单调乏味的，且极易出错。因此，工业界需要新型的、准确的、自动化的技术来高效地检测死锁失效，从而提高多线程程序（软件）的质量来进而提供良好的用户体验。 为解决上述各项挑战，本项目提出一种基于约束的测试多线程死锁的程序调度生成方法，以及开发了一个新的C-AGENDA框架来应用该方法到多线程程序上。我们提出首先在一个多线程程序的无死锁的运行中研究关键且可交换的约束。然后我们用这些约束建立模型，来描述一个潜在死锁如何在另外的一些运行中真正发生，并生成相应的程序调度。最后使用生成的程序调度来验证这些潜在的死锁场景是否会真实发生。该项目最终可以为工业界提供一个非常高效的真实死锁检测框架，同时可以让研究生得到历练。

111313.label: Realisation of objectives
111313.value: We have investigated the inherent properties of and challenges in confirmation of real deadlocks in multithreaded software applications through case collection and experimentations on representative benchmarks used in top-tier literature and real-world applications whose codebase, bug reports and test cases were publicly available to the research and industry communities. To enable replications and validation across different settings, we developed an automated experimentation program to execute the program subjects and profile execution traces, and developed program scripts to compile statistics. Within the framework, for each selected configuration, each program subject on each test case had been executed for one hundred to one thousand times to enumerate possible thread interleaving scenarios. The experimentation program applied a popular and generic test oracle to check whether an execution trace reached a deadlocking state. Through such repetitive executions, the experimentation program indexed some traces that each formed at least one deadlock while some other traces did not when executing the same program subject over the same specific test case. We inspected the codebase of these programs against such pairs of scenarios and compiled the statistics on each particular lock acquisition sequence and each of its subsequences appearing in such pairs of scenarios on condition that the sequence/sub-sequence resulted in a deadlock in the corresponding traces or did not form any deadlock, respectively. Based on the collected cases and statistics, we have formulated a constraint-sensitive framework for thread schedule selection for deadlock confirmation through the investigation on how to alter one lock acquisition sequence with low probability in deadlocking into another lock acquisition sequence with high probability in deadlocking. Deadlock had a well-defined condition where multiple threads circularly waited for one another to release locks to be held by them. In our investigation, whenever the tail part of an execution trace had a particular lock acquisition order fulfilling this well-defined condition, the trace reached a deadlocking state. Our investigation focus has thus been placed in the part of the traces before this tail part so as to create the deadlock triggering conditions if possible. We split each selected lock acquisition sequence in a trace into multiple subsequences and examined whether there were common lock acquisition subsequences among such split subsequences of the selected traces and whether there were any distinct subsequences having strong evidences in relating the occurrences of deadlocks in the corresponding traces. For these related subsequences of lock acquisition, we iteratively and backwardly located those lock acquisition subsequences that had strong evidences in relating to the former subsequences. We distinguished each located lock acquisition subsequence on whether it was a sufficient condition of the appearance of the deadlock captured in the trace or was a coincidental condition. We then examined the constraints among lock acquisitions to reversely generate such subsequences marking as sufficient conditions, starting from the given predictive deadlock pattern on a given trace to see how to produce feasible traces. To support this generation of thread selection, the framework developed a profiling module to identify deadlock patterns and lock acquisition subsequences, a constraint extraction module to generate the required lock acquisition subsequences and thread suspension hotspots to pause the execution of particular thread in generating target thread schedules and lock acquisition subsequences. We then conducted an experimentation to collect the statistics on successful generation of a chain of such lock acquisition subsequences with respect to the generation of the same target deadlock pattern. This investigation required localization of code patterns statistically, and thus we have also developed some statistical debugging aids to ease the process. We also examined why some chain of lock acquisition subsequences had experienced wrong thread scheduling. We also experimented to replace the generation of a specific lock acquisition subsequence by an application-default thread-guided strategy. We compared the differences in probability in resulting in deadlocking states between the former constraint-based strategy and the later thread-guided strategy. We paid particular attentions to the scenarios where the differences were non-observable and found the common conditions in such pairs of scenarios to be enforced so as to confirm a deadlock pattern. We then further relaxed these found common conditions through experimentations so that the final condition candidates were independent to the lock acquisition subsequences appearing before the appearance of these condition candidates in the same traces and yet the use of such condition candidates can still result in a high probability in reaching a deadlocking state. We have studied both random and adaptive random test case allocation schemes in targeted thread schedule generation. More specifically, whenever an execution point was about to prioritize the set of suspended or current threads and picks one among them to execute, we applied the random test case allocation scheme to randomize the thread schedule generation providing that the selected thread schedule was not in conflict with the enforcing lock acquisition constraints. We systematically examined whether such a setting was an effective allocation scheme by comparing it against a few adaptive versions of this randomized test case allocation scheme by measuring the performance and the chances in leading to a program failure. There were many adaptive random variants in the literature. We have studied the most representative ones including the partition testing strategy, the adaptive random testing strategy and other diversity-based strategies in our experimentations. Each adaptive test case allocation scheme incurred additional performance overheads and had to keep certain historic data to achieve even-ness or diversity. Through experimentations, we examined whether these schemes can improve the confirmation probability on top of the constraint-based plus randomized test case allocation approach as well as whether these schemes each can result in higher or faster rate of program failure. We applied each such scheme to each program over each test case with repeated executions. To avoid biases, we expanded the scope from confirmation of deadlocks to confirmation of different fundamental kinds of concurrency and semantics bugs so that we can cross-check the results. We have implemented a prototype of our framework in C++ with the pintool to profile and manipulate thread executions. To further validate our framework, we have also implemented the prior state-of-the-art techniques and symmetrically compared with our framework in terms of effectiveness and efficiency on the collected C/C++ benchmarks and real-world applications. Owing to resource limitation, we have not implemented the framework to support other languages such as Java. To ensure genericity of our framework, we have ensured our framework being generic across C/C++ and Java. For some dated techniques, owing to lacking in resources in implementing them, we compared our framework against those techniques published in the original papers through literature review and arguments on the technical particulars.
