111313.label: Major findings and research outcome
111313.value: Our investigation showed that dynamically confirming a predictive deadlock with high probability was achievable through enforcing selected few sufficient conditions in lock acquisition subsequences [J1, C2]. Such enforcements require collaboration between different thread executions. This idea further leads to the exploration of the test execution space through various adaptive randomized approaches where different executions of test cases can be more productive by collaboration so that the execution of the prioritized test set can result in higher/faster rate of program failure than pure randomized test case allocation [J3, C5, C9]. The need to repetitively examine many long traces and compile statistics on them led to the development on new and efficient thread representation [J5, C10], new test platform [J6, C6, C7, C11], new insights on statistical debugging [J7, C3, C8], and new empirical findings on regression testing [J2, J4, C1, C4, C12, C13]. More specifically, the project has developed novel constraint-based deadlock confirmation algorithms. In the experiment, almost all deadlock case studies were confirmed with high probability with low performance overhead. The key lesson learnt was that profiling excessive data and excessive thread controls may lower the bug detection rates due to the fact that in some cases, program thread interleaving were time-based rather than lock-based. We believe that the ability of a technique to overcome the challenge in precise and minimal monitoring and altering thread schedule was a major contributing factor behind the techniques developed in this project. We have found that the execution constraints appearing much earlier than the bug locations has little relevancy to the exposure of the bugs. This discovery indicates decoupling the test case generation problem into two independent sub-problems are possible: efficient execution of the whole or reduced test set and the efficient execution of each trace so that the solutions to address individual sub-problems have a wider applicability. We have formulated a generic condition to purge backwardly related lock acquisition order starting from the predictive deadlocking locations in traces. We have also identified that the constraints in between the thread positions of such a generic condition and the thread positions to acquire the locks forming a target deadlocks can be purged without significantly reducing the deadlock confirmation probabilities on the deadlock cases used in the experimentation, and further removing the enforcement of the generic condition will significantly affect these confirmation probabilities.

111313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
111313.value: We have identified certain conditions that meeting them will result in deadlocking in high probability. The negation forms of these conditions can be further developed to avoid re-occurrences of the same deadlocking state in runtime, making the research outcomes of this project to be applicable beyond deadlock confirmation. This project identified the locations of the sufficient yet generic conditions appearing well before the deadlocking locations where enforcing these conditions will likely trigger the deadlocks and ignoring them will significantly less likely trigger the same deadlocks. Research on deadlock avoidance techniques may consider the use of static analysis to identify predictive deadlocks and enumerate such sufficient yet generic conditions to be monitored and altered so that even the first occurrence of a particular deadlock can be avoided. Deadlock confirmations require a high quality input of traces with predictive deadlocks. New fuzz testing or test case synthesis techniques that are aware of the conditions needed in deadlock confirmations have potentials to address this issue.

111313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
111313.value: Many software are written as multithreaded programs to harvest the performance speedup due to the advent of multicore processors. When a deadlock in the course of executing such a program occurs, users may experience critical damages such as data loss, file corruption, or inability to complete critical functions in emergency. Testing these programs against deadlocks is necessary in ensuring their correctness. However, a vast majority of executions of these programs will not experience deadlocking. Dynamic deadlock confirmation aims to predict deadlock potentials in a non-deadlocking execution and trigger the predicted deadlocks in a follow-up execution. Without controlling the interleaving among threads in the follow-up execution until the locations of the predicted deadlock are reached or controlling too much such interleavings is difficult to trigger the predicted deadlock. Each thread has certain orders in acquiring lock objects before reaching its deadlocking location at the predicted deadlock, and lock objects are shared among threads. This project makes use of these two observations to infer the essential locking dependences among threads along the non-deadlocking execution and identify the conditions to be enforced in the follow-up execution so that the follow-up execution is able to reach the predicted deadlocks with high probability at low runtime overhead.

111613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
111613.value: Model reduction is an area of systems and control theory which in recent years has seen increasingly more important applications in the simulation and design of large-scale interconnect circuits. This area of research emphasizes the reduction of model complexity while preserving to the possible extent the essential characteristics of a system's input-output behavior, of which stability and passivity are notable features of passive interconnect circuits. There are mainly two sets of methods which are prevalent currently in passive circuit model reduction: SVD based methods and moment matching based methods, each of which has its advantages and disadvantages. This project amounts to a significant application and outgrowth of control theory and techniques to the field of design automation of VLSI circuits, with the goal to develop computationally efficient model order reduction algorithms that are capable of preserving stability and passivity, the two defining features of passive interconnect circuits. The project seeks the joint development of Caratheodory-Toeplitz interpolation methods and moment matching methods, together with a relative gain array measure for the reduction of multi-port circuits, which promises to fill an important gap in the existing model reduction methods and consequently meet the need for simulation and design of large-scale passive interconnect circuits. The project has the potential to lend tangible tools to IC (integrated circuit) industry. 系統與控制理論中模型降階這一研究領域近年來在大規模電路仿真及其設計中有日益重要的應用。模型降階著重於降低模型複雜性，與此同時儘量保證其輸入輸出的主要特徵。對於無源電路，最突出的特徵是穩定性和無源性。目前針對於無源電路模型降階主要有兩種方法，各有優缺點：基於奇異值解耦方法，和基於矩匹配方法。本項目嘗試利用控制理論中的方法和工具研究大規模集成電路設計中的重要問題，旨在發展能確保穩定性和無源性且能快速計算的模型降階算法。項目嘗試有機地結合並發展Caratheodory-Toeplitz插值方法和矩匹配方法；對於多端口電路，進一步提出相對增益陣列作為降階準則並依此發展有效的多端電路降階方法。擬發展方法面向大規模無源電路仿真與設計中的需要，彌補目前模型降階方法的不足，從而對集成電路工業提供有用的工具。

111613.label: Realisation of objectives
111613.value: This PI tends to believe that the project has been highly successful and very well completed. The outcomes have in fact far exceeded the intended objectives, in both the scope and the depth of the project. The project has resulted in a total of 1 book, 15 journal papers (with 10 published and 5 under review), 1 book, and 10 conference papers, with the majority of the papers published in top archive journals and leading professional conferences. Under the support of this project, a high quality Ph.D. student, Dr. Song Fang, completed his Ph.D. study. Based on Dr. Fang’s Ph.D. thesis, we co-authored a research monograph published by Springer in 2017. In addition, a postdoctoral fellow and an exchange Ph.D. student were trained. The Ph.D. student received his Ph.D. in 2017 from University of Victoria, Canada. The project has not only accomplished successfully the objectives, but in joint effort with other projects, also led to the developments of new problem areas and solution techniques, as summarized in Section 6.1, Major Findings and Research Outcome.

111613.label: Major findings and research outcome
111613.value: The technical objectives set forth in the proposal have been achieved to satisfaction. Regarding Objective 1, we have developed an algorithm (Research Output [5]) which integrates two classical analytic function interpolation methods with the moment matching method. This algorithm integrates judiciously the moments of a system with the methods of Caratheodory-Toeplitz and Nevanlinna-Pick interpolation, which unlike the prevailing, traditional Arnoldi projection method, guarantees the stability and passivity properties of the system. The proposed method is suitable for reduction of passive circuit models such as on-chip power grids. The advantage of the method is validated by computational complexity analysis. Extensive numerical experiments also show that the algorithm enjoys superior numerical accuracy with a very moderate increase of computation. Toward Objective 2, we have developed a balanced truncation method with the waveform relaxation technique (Research Output [4]), which is intended to simulate a large interconnected system composed of several sub-systems. The approach first allows all coupled subsystems to be decomposed by waveform relaxation, whereas the decoupled systems can then be coped with using the balanced truncation. A tool inherently useful for multiport circuits, this approach guarantees the system’s asymptotic stability, controllability, and observability. Finally, we also addressed the important issue of Electromigration (EM) in Research Output 3. EM is a major concern for VLSI interconnect reliability, particularly for interconnect trees with multibranch metal wires. For EM modeling and assessment, one important problem is to perform fast EM time to failure analysis for practical VLSI chips. For this purpose, we developed an analytic model for the stress evolution of interconnect trees under different current density and varying segment length based on the first principles. The stress evolution is modeled by two Korhonen’s equations coupled through boundary conditions which are solved with the Laplace transformation technique. Our method is compared with the finite-element method (FEM) tool COMSOL, and the EM simulator XSim. The comparison shows that our analytical solution agrees well with the results from the FEM numerical analysis and is more compact than the eigenfunction method for the same accuracy. The project has led to the investigation and successes into other related research areas including (1) integration of information and control theories for performance analysis of networked control systems (Research Output [2], [6], [7], [10], [16]), (2) development of consensus protocols for multi-agent systems (Research Output [8], [9], [11]), (3) development of methods and algorithms for studying social networks (Research Output [13], [14], [15]).

111613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
111613.value: Model reduction plays an important role in the simulation and design of large-scale interconnect circuits. An essential challenge facing the reduction of VLSI system models is to reduce the model order and complexity so that the simulation and design can be efficiently conducted and iterated, while preserving the physical characteristics of the system's input-output behavior, of which stability, passivity, controllability and observability are notable features of passive interconnect circuits. This project aims to apply control system analysis and design techniques to develop efficient algorithms for modeling, simulation, and design of VLSI passive systems, with the goal to leverage on the computational efficiency of the prevailing algorithms while bestowing them with the aforementioned physical characteristics. We developed a number of algorithms that achieve these goals, by, e.g., integrating classical analytic function interpolation methods with the moment matching method. The algorithms have the promise to fill an important gap in the existing model reduction methods oriented toward VLSI systems and to meet the need for simulation and design of large-scale passive interconnect circuits.

111913.label: Project Objectives

111913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
111913.value: In 2012, the US President Barack Obama has urged the US congress to pass the Cybersecurity act of 2012 to him in order to sign it into law. Clearly, the importance of Cyber-space security has tightly connected to one National and Economical security, nowadays we have transparently and unintentionally using Cloud services on a daily basis. For example, we use Dropbox to share files among colleagues and friends, we use Google doc to modify and create files on machines and hard-drives miles away passing through interconnection networks shared by potentially adversaries and unknown hackers. One very important question is how can a user ensure the opened file is the same file that he stored previously, and he / she is the sole owner of this file, not even the system administrator. Obviously, with the increasing trend of using mobile devices connecting to the Cloud, the importance of Chip-to-Cloud security will be continued to bloom. Chip-to-Cloud (C2C) security refers to ensuring the security of devices connecting to the Cloud computing platforms. Thus, the designs of secure processor architecture for C2C pose new security challenges for the research communities and governments to enable a safe global community. Trustworthy computing has been gaining increasing importance as computing devices become pervasive and information becomes widely distributed on the Cloud. The Root-of-Trust of a security system comes from the methodology and the quality of random key. The key is a genuine intrinsic true random number generator. By providing hardware-level protection, a secure processor ensures a safe computing environment where confidential data can be protected against both hardware and software attacks. This proposal aims to carry architectural and entropy analysis for the root-of-trust core, True Random Number Generator (TRNG) for the Field-Programmable Gate Array and ASIC platform. The created TRNG core will be placed into a rapid prototyping FPGA platform for building the secure processor architecture. The uses of our novel techniques on Montgomery multiplier using residue number systems and spectral arithmetic will be explored for the processor. Next, we will develop secure protocol for this secure platform such as the boot sequence and mechanism for the content switching of Virtual Machines (VM) on the processor. The corresponding attack model for the processor in the Cloud environment will be introduced with the techniques described in this project. By achieving the objectives described in this proposal, it is expected that a secure processor will become more favorable to everyone. 在2012年，美國總統奧巴馬敦促美國國會通過的網絡安全，讓他可以簽署成為法律。網絡空間安全的重要性已經緊密相連一個國家經濟的安全，現在我們已經透明和無意每天使用雲端服務。例如，我們使用Dropbox的同事和朋友之間的共享文件，我們使用谷歌文檔的修改和創建文件共享的潛在對手和未知的黑客通過互聯網絡傳遞英里遠的機器和硬盤驅動器。其中一個很重要的問題是，用戶如何才能確保打開的文件是一樣的。使用移動設備連接到雲端的增長趨勢，芯片到雲端安全的重要性，將繼續綻放。芯片雲端的安全性是指確保設備連接到雲計算平台的安全性。芯片雲端安全處理器架構設計的研究社區和政府構成新的安全挑戰。可信計算已經得到越來越多的重視，為計算設備的普及和信息廣泛分佈於雲。根信任的安全系統自帶的隨機密鑰的方法和質量。最關鍵的是一個真正的內在的真隨機數發生器。安全處理器提供硬件級保護，確保安全的計算環境，可以保護機密數據，對硬件和軟件的攻擊。該提案旨在根信任的核心，真正的隨機數發生器，現場可編程門陣列和特定應用集成電路平台進行建築和分析。創建隨機數發生器核心建立安全處理器架構，將被放入一個快速原型現場可編程門陣列平台。蒙哥馬利乘法器我們的新技術利用餘數系統和光譜運算的用途將探討的處理器。我們將開發這個安全平台，如處理器上的虛擬機的內容切換啟動順序，以及機制的安全協議。處理器在雲端計算環境中，在這個項目中所描述的技術將出台相應的攻擊模型。通過實現在本方案中所描述的目標，預計一個安全處理器將讓大家更有利。

111913.label: Realisation of objectives
111913.value: The project has been completed with successful research outputs targeting primitive components for building secure true random number generation core, ultra-high speed using optical components for secure cloud environment. We have developed a number of primitive cryptographic components, including a complementary architecture for high-speed True Random Number Generator (TRNG) achieving a double data rate core. The prototype design has been implemented and verified on a Xilinx Virtex-6 ML605 evaluation board. As a result, the generated random number stream is able to pass the statistical NIST and DIEHARD test suites showing a reliable performance. We have also proposed a novel, Bias-Bounded Digital True Random Number Generator Architecture, for embedding to secure processor targeting the open-source RISC-V architecture. Bias phenomenon has been a ubiquitous problem in the designs of digital True Random Number Generator (TRNG). Circuit performance can be improved with some auxiliary modules such as analog circuits and post-processing components, which usually involve the compromising of cost, compatibility, throughput, and security as well. In some cases only sub-optimal designs can be achieved. By utilizing the diverse timing characteristics of different initial states, a staged-running Self-timed Ring (STR) architecture, which is able to suppress the degree of bias is proposed. The proposed architecture is compared with conventional free-running architectures using Xilinx Zynq-7000 FPGA for a throughput of 100 Mbps. With the increase of the ring size, the bias degree of the newly proposed structure is within a negligible level of less than 1%; whereas those of the conventional architectures can exceed 10%. We have further extended the research on TRNG by targeting ultra high speed using optical laser for collecting primitive randomness, targeting cloud computing environment. The proposed laser-FPGA system is able to generate discrete Gaussian numbers with a time-invariant throughput of 35.7 MSPS and 7.8 MSPS on Zedboard for two RLWE schemes. Applying the proposed compressed CDT method, the throughput of the proposed architectures reaches up to 40 MSPS and 8.3 MSPS, which is the fastest amongst the existing architectures based on TRNG inputs. This primitive component has been also integrated into the RISC-V secure processor architecture.

112113.label: Project Title(Chinese)
112113.value: 聚合物光波導模分復用器之設計與製造

112113.label: Project Objectives
112113.value: The first objective is to demonstrate an MD (de)multiplexer that consists of three identical, parallel square waveguide cores with each core supporting the LP01 and LP11 modes, where the two degenerate LP11 modes in the input core are made to couple completely to the corresponding LP11 modes in the two other cores placed alongside with the input core in the horizontal and vertical directions, respectively, and the LP01 mode stays in the input core. This device maintains the mode patterns in each core and can be connected to identical few-mode fiber leads for further signal processing. The second objective is to demonstrate an MD (de)multiplexer that consists of an input square core that supports the LP01 and LP11 modes, where the two degenerate LP11 modes are made to couple completely to the LP01 modes in two smaller, identical single-mode cores placed alongside with the input core in the horizontal and vertical directions, respectively. The device can be connected to single-mode fiber leads to facilitate further signal processing with conventional single-mode components. The third objective is to demonstrate an MD (de)multiplexer that consists of an input rectangular core that supports the LP01 and LP11 modes, where the two LP11 modes are made to couple completely to the LP01 modes of two smaller, non-identical single-mode cores placed alongside with the input core in the horizontal and vertical directions, respectively. The design allows the two non-degenerate LP11 modes in the rectangular core to be separated and is suitable for applications that employ few-mode elliptical-core fibers for more stable system operation.

112113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
112113.value: It is foreseen that the transmission capacity of the global optical fiber networks will need to increase by 1000 times in the next 30 years to meet the growing demand in the communication market, which is mainly due to the expansion in the internet usage and fiber-to-the-home networks. The existing dense wavelength-division multiplexing technology alone, which allows a single-mode fiber to carry many wavelength channels, will not sustain the growth. New technologies to further increase the transmission capacities of fiber cables are being pursued actively. Space-division multiplexing that relies on the use of multicore fibers or multimode fibers, or a combination of both, is a particularly promising technology. A multimode fiber can support many characteristic light waves, known as modes. The technology of using different modes to carry different channels in a multimode fiber is called mode-division (MD) multiplexing. Recently, carefully designed fibers that support a few modes have been found suitable for MD multiplexing and the feasibility of MD multiplexing for long-distance transmission has been demonstrated experimentally. For the development of practical MD multiplexing systems, it is necessary to develop a range of mode-selective components, among which a MD multiplexer (demultiplexer) that can combine (separate) different mode channels at the input (output) end of the system is the key component. The MD (de)multiplexers demonstrated so far are mainly based on free-space optics or fiber couplers, which are bulky or have limited multiplexing capability. The objective of the project is to develop new MD (de)multiplexers with polymer optical waveguides. The polymer waveguide technology offers many advantages: low cost, simple fabrication process, feasibility of forming multilayers, flexibility in structure design, and thermo-optic tuning capability. The project will investigate several new designs of MD (de)multiplexers that combine coplanar and vertical waveguide couplers. The capability of fabricating vertical couplers is a distinct advantage of the polymer waveguide technology. The PI has more than 10 year experience in polymer waveguide research (and much longer experience in waveguide design) and CityU is equipped with the facility necessary for the fabrication of various types of polymer waveguide devices. The project will lead to experimental demonstrations of new waveguide-based MD (de)multiplexers, which can be used as stand-alone components or integrated into planar lightwave circuit (PLC) chips to provide more sophisticated mode-processing functions. So far PLC chips have been primarily designed for single-mode transmission. There is a huge scope in the development of PLC chips for multimode transmission. 可以預見，在未來30年，全球光纖網絡的傳輸容量需要增加1000倍才能滿足不斷增長的通信市場；這主要是互聯網使用與光纖到戶網絡的擴張所致。現在的高密度波分復用技術，僅依賴單模光纖傳送多個波長通道，將不能維持市場的增長，大家都在積極探求能進一步提高光纜傳輸容量的新技術。其中空分復用技術，即使用多芯光纖或者多模光纖甚至是兩者結合作爲傳輸媒體，前景特別樂觀。 多模光纖可以支持多個各具特性的光波，即模式。利用多模光纖中的不同模式傳送不同的通訊頻道，是為模分復用技術。最近幾年，已證實經過精心設計的少模光纖（即支持少數幾個模式的光纖）可適用於模分復用，也有多個實驗演示了模分復用作爲長距離傳輸技術的可行性。爲了發展實用的模分復用系統，必須要開發多種模式選擇器件。其中模復用器（解模復用器），用於系統的輸入（輸出）端以合併（分離）不同的模式， 是尤其關鍵的器件。目前已演示的（解）模復用器主要是建基於自由空間光學或光纖耦合器，缺點是比較笨重或復用功能局限。本項目的目標是研發新穎的聚合物光波導（解）模復用器， 利用聚合物波導技術成本低、製作工藝簡單、可以形成多層薄膜、結構設計靈活、熱光調制能力強等許多優點。本項目將會結合平面和垂直光波導耦合器，設計並製造幾款新穎的（解）模復用器。其中垂直耦合器的研製，能充分體現聚合物波導技術的優勢。 申請人在聚合物波導領域已有十多年的研究經驗（在波導設計方面的經驗更爲久遠）， 且香港城市大學已配備必要的設施，用於製造各種類型的聚合物波導器件。本項目將通過理論與實驗研究，實現幾款新穎的光波導（解）模復用器。這些器件可以獨立使用，也可以集成到平面光波綫路（PLC）的芯片，以提供更複雜的模式處理功能。目前的PLC芯片的設計，主要是針對單模傳輸系統，用於多模傳輸的PLC芯片的研發有十分廣闊的空間。

112113.label: Realisation of objectives
112113.value: (1) Mode (de)multiplexers based on identical waveguides We successfully designed and fabricated a high-performance polymer-waveguide mode (de)multiplexer based on the structure of cascading a horizontal directional coupler and a vertical directional coupler, where the three waveguides had identical cores. A typical fabricated (de)multiplexer, which was 18.5 mm long, showed a coupling ratio higher than ∼96% in the wavelength range of 1530–1570 nm for both couplers. The device showed negligible crosstalk to the LP01-mode channel, while the crosstalks to the two LP11-mode channels were lower than −15.6 and −13.4 dB for the TE and TM polarizations, respectively. This device could find applications in mode-division-multiplexing (MDM) systems, where mode patterns need to be preserved. The first objective of the project has been completely achieved. (2) Mode (de)multiplexers based on non-identical waveguides We carried out a detailed theoretical analysis of a mode (de)multiplexer that consists of an input square core that supports the LP01 and LP11 modes, where the two degenerate LP11 modes are made to couple completely to the LP01 modes in two smaller, identical single-mode cores placed alongside with the input core in the horizontal and vertical directions, respectively. We found, however, that the two small identical single-mode cores in such a structure can cause significant modal crosstalk and thus affect the performance of the device. We solved this problem by using a rectangular core as the input core, so that the two side cores become non-identical. Because of this improvement, the horizontal and vertical directional couplers can be collocated, which leads to a more compact device. We successfully designed and fabricated such a mode (de)multiplexer with polymer material. A typical fabricated device, which had a total length of only 9.0 mm, showed coupling ratios varying from 91% to 99% for the two LP11 modes and crosstalks among the modes in the side cores varying from 23.2 to 14.6 dB in the wavelength range 1530 – 1570 nm (the C-band). The crosstalks in the central core were negligible. This device could be readily used in broadband MDM transmission systems where the few-mode fiber used can be a circular-core fiber or an elliptical-core fiber. In addition, we proposed a new waveguide structure for realizing mode (de)multiplexing. This structure is based on partitioning a few-mode rectangular core into several single-mode cores, which branch out into separate cores in two layers. Mode multiplexing is achieved by adiabatic transition of modes along the waveguide branches. We successfully fabricated a three-mode and a four-mode (de)multiplexer using this new structure with polymer material and demonstrated ultra-broadband operation with these devices. The second and the third objective of the project have been completed achieved. (3) Other relevant studies To measure the performance of a mode (de)multiplexer, it is necessary to selectively launch a higher-order mode (the LP11 mode) into the device, which is difficult to achieve in practice. To solve this problem, we developed three devices: (i) a fiber laser that can generate the LP11 mode; (ii) an electro-optic mode switch with lithium-niobate waveguide that can switch between the LP01 mode and the LP11 mode; and (iii) a CO2-laser written long-period fiber grating that can convert the LP01 mode into the LP11 mode. These devices were used for the excitation of the LP11 mode in the characterization of our fabricated mode (de)multiplexers. In addition, we proposed a new multicore fiber design suitable for broadband MDM systems and analyzed in detail the problem of connecting a square-core/rectangular-core waveguide to a circular-core/elliptical-core fiber to achieve mode-selective coupling for high-order modes. We obtained very good results from these studies. These studies could be considered as supporting studies for the original objectives or extensions of the original objectives.

112113.label: Major findings and research outcome
112113.value: This project has generated very fruitful results. The major findings and research outcome are listed below: (1) We have designed and fabricated a polymer-waveguide mode (de)multiplexer based on the structure of cascading a horizontal coupler and a vertical coupler, where the three waveguides have identical cores [C1],[C5],[J4]. This device shows excellent performance and can be used in mode-division-multiplexing (MDM) systems where the mode patterns need to be kept for further processing, such as mode routing. (2) We have designed and fabricated a compact polymer-waveguide mode (de)multiplexer based on the structure of collocating a horizontal coupler and a vertical coupler, where the three waveguides have non-identical cores [C5],[J6]. The device shows excellent performance and can be used at the input and output ends of an MDM system for direct connection to single-mode fibers. (3) We have experimentally demonstrated a three-mode and a four-mode polymer-waveguide (de)multiplexer based on the mechanism of adiabatic mode transition along waveguide branches in two layers [C6],[C7]. These devices can be used in ultra-broadband MDM systems. (4) We have experimentally demonstrated a mode-locked fiber laser, which can generate stable picosecond pulses for both the LP01 and LP11 modes [C2],[J1]. This laser could be used for the characterization of MDM devices. (5) We have designed and fabricated a mode switch with an electro-optic grating formed along a lithium-niobate waveguide [J2]. This mode switch could find applications in reconfigurable MDM systems. (6) We have experimentally demonstrated CO2-laser written long-period fiber gratings in a two-mode fiber for achieving conversion between the fundamental mode and the higher-order modes [C3],[J3]. The performance of these gratings is insensitive to temperature and polarization variations. These robust mode converters can be used in MDM systems and other areas that require cylindrical vector modes. (7) We have proposed a three-core fiber with a central refractive-index dip in each core for achieving ultra-low group-delay differences (DGDs) among the modes [J5]. Our optimal fiber design offers the lowest DGD over the C-band ever reported and could be developed into fibers for broadband MDM applications. (8) We have analyzed in detail butt-coupling between few-mode fibers and rectangular-core waveguides for the first six spatial modes [J7]. The results are useful for the design of mode-selective waveguide devices, such as mode (de)multiplexers, mode converters, and mode switches, for fiber-based MDM applications. (9) The results of the project have been reported as invited review papers at two international conferences [C4],[C8].

112113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
112113.value: The project has generated a good amount of high-quality results. There is a great potential for some of the research to be further developed into new projects. In fact, the PI has secured a GRF in 2016 to support the development of a new class of thermo-optic mode switches based on the polymer-waveguide technology developed in this project. The PI has also established strong research collaboration with the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China (UESTC) to further explore some of the ideas generated from this project. Such collaboration has already led to a number of joint publications (which are not listed as research outputs of this project) and a joint NSFC proposal submitted early this year.

112113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
112113.value: Mode-division multiplexing (MDM), which allows different spatial modes in a few-mode fiber to carry independent channels, is a promising technology for enhancing the transmission capacity of a fiber and a focus of research in the field of optical communications worldwide. A key component in an MDM system is a mode (de)multiplexer that serves to spatially combine (separate) different mode channels. The objective of the project is to develop high-performance mode (de)multiplexers with the polymer waveguide technology. Polymer waveguide offers many advantages: low cost, simple fabrication process, feasibility of forming multilayers, flexibility in structure design, and thermal-tuning capability. On the completion of the project, several novel mode (de)multiplexers that combine coplanar and vertical waveguide couplers have been successfully designed and fabricated with polymer material. These devices show excellent performance and can be readily used in MDM systems. For the characterization of these mode (de)multiplexers, a range of new devices have also been developed, which include a mode-locked fiber laser for the higher-order mode, an electro-optic mode switch, and a fiber grating mode converter. Many of the ideas generated from this project can be further explored to realize more advanced functional devices for the construction of future fiber-based MDM networks.

112613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
112613.value: 無線感應鏈路是利用同一組耦合線圈與終端設備來轉送電力及數據。在近期材料科學，電力半導體技術，以及微型和納米製造設施的推動下，令無線感應鏈路在許多應用中普及起來，例如，生物醫學電子學，物流運輸等。這個研究領域吸引了許多學術界和工業界各種研究，課題由提高系統的電源管理以至增強數據傳輸。 無線感應鏈路是由一個發射器，一個接收器，和鬆散的耦合線圈所組成。發送線圈和接收線圈之間的能量轉移是通過交變磁場所實現。系統之優化是在於實現最大的功率傳輸效率和提供高數據傳輸率。雖然有不少發射器和接收器的新發明，鏈路效率仍是受制於一個基本的“瓶頸” - 耦合線圈的位置錯位會令電力傳輸和鏈路效率波動。當耦合線圈是置於同軸上，鏈路效率是最大的。若然兩個線圈錯位，其鏈路效率將大大地減少。在過去的幾十年中，雖然感應鏈路已被廣泛研究，包括鏈路效率和線圈結構之優化設計，但在於線圈的結構、耦合的方法、激法和控制方面，今天的感應鏈路與傳統的方法相比，沒有重大的進展。 該項目旨在探索利用高維，二維和三維立體感應線圈，能給予繞組間的磁耦合線圈真正的全方位控制，具有更大的機動性和靈活性，突破傳統的線圈耦合技術。這樣的理念使得線圈即使在錯位的情況下，仍能保持一個較高水平的耦合，帶來一個嶄新的線圈結構技術。

112613.label: Major findings and research outcome
112613.value: A daisy-chained transformer (DCT) structure is proposed to share equally the current delivered from a half-bridge switching circuit and supply the shared currents to multiple string networks and then using a capacitor network in each string network to derive the string current and separate the grounds of the input source and the strings. The capacitor networks give further advantage of balancing the string currents [8.1, 9.1]. Such current-balancing mechanism propagates over a ring capacitor network [8.2, 9.5]. A winding structure that comprises two orthogonally placed windings for lessening the variation of the coupling coefficient due to the coil misalignment is proposed [8.3, 9.2, 9.8]. An output current summing technique that keeps the windings concurrently energized and combines the output currents of the windings has been studied. An inductive power transfer system for driving multiple organic light-emitting diode light panels is presented. Each light panel is driven by an output in a DCT structure through a detachable transformer. The DCT structure allows using a single switching network to drive multiple light panels with good current balancing. Apart from easy and safe operation, the proposed system also offers a modular, scalable, maintenance-free, and hot-swappable platform for large-area illumination [8.4, 9.3]. The power transfer efficiency and power transfer characteristics of wireless inductive links are determined by several intrinsic and extrinsic factors, such as coupling coefficient, quality factors, matching conditions of the transmitting and receiving coils, and operating frequency. A new perspective by processing transmitter-side electrical information with an evolutionary computation technique to estimate several system parameters, including mutual inductance, coil inductances and quality factors, resonant frequencies of the transmitting and receiving networks, and coupling coefficient, for the transmitter to manage power transfer has been proposed [8.5, 8.6, 9.4]. Techniques of long-term in-vivo electrophysiological recording play important roles in brain research and neural rehabilitation. A holistic assessment of the relationships among the physical sizes of the transmitting and receiving coils, power transfer characteristics, and specific absorption rate in animals of a simple wireless power transfer system using two rectangular coaxial transmitting coils [9.9]. In order to build the driver, a new ripple-free input current power factor corrector (PFC) is investigated. By applying a concept called “Power Semiconductor Filter” for input filtering, the input current ripple of the PFC can be reduced by using a semiconductor device. The requirement of the differential-mode filter for the entire system can be greatly reduced [9.6, 9.7].

112613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
112613.value: 3D winding structures have been investigated. In general, more orthogonal windings can be added to tackle coil misalignment of a higher dimension. Thus, a more specific investigation into the use of orthogonal windings in both receiving coil and transmitting coil can be conducted. Although the interaction of the three-winding-to-three-winding coupling is complicated, it is expected that such coil structure could further enhance the magnetic coupling for coil misalignment. Multi-winding coil structure in wireless inductive links has the potential to be applied for powering up biomedical implants, such as retinal prosthesis, capsular endoscope, cardiac pacemaker and spinal-cord stimulator. Charging multiple devices simultaneously with a single power transmitter has recently attracted much attention, especially in the applications of wireless charging gadgets. It is valuable to explore the possibility of using transmitting side information to estimation electrical qualities of multiple receivers. Similarly, the possibility of applying the estimation algorithms to the multi-coil structures can be studied.

112613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
112613.value: The wireless inductive link consists of a transmitter, a receiver, and loosely-coupled coils. Energy is transferred between the transmitter coil and the receiver coil through alternating magnetic fields. Although many improved transmitter and receiver designs have emerged, the link efficiency is still determined by a fundamental “bottleneck” – fluctuations in the power transfer and link efficiency due to misaligned coupled coils. When the coils are coaxially orientated, the magnetic coupling between the coils and thus the link efficiency are maximal. However, if the two coils are misaligned, the magnetic coupling and the overall link efficiency will impair significantly. Although inductive links have been studied extensively during the past few decades, there have been no major advances in the coil coupling method used in today’s inductive links, as compared to the conventional approach. This project aims to make a breakthrough in the coil coupling technology by exploring the use of high-dimensional, including two- and three-dimensional, windings to provide true-omnidirectional control of the magnetic coupling between coils with greater maneuverability and flexibility than the conventional structure. Such concept allows the coils to maintain a high level of coupling, even under misalignment situation, and will bring a new perspective to the power transfer strategies.

112813.label: Project Title(Chinese)
112813.value: 矿渣材料的不收敛力学特性

112813.label: Co - Investigator(s)
112813.value: Prof Coop, Matthew Richard Prof Hu, Wei Prof Schnaid, Fernando Prof SENETAKIS, Konstantinos Prof Sitharam, T.G.

112813.label: Project Objectives
112813.value: By testing a wide variety of tailings from around the world, to establish the soil and particle characteristics that might identify a particular tailings material as being likely to have transitional behaviour. To investigate in detail how transitional behaviour affects the behaviour of tailings in both monotonic and cyclic loading and how it might influence the applicability of state parameter based design methods. To try to identify those elements of fabric that give rise to the transitional behaviour.
rows: By testing a wide variety of tailings from around the world, to establish the soil and particle characteristics that might identify a particular tailings material as being likely to have transitional behaviour.

To investigate in detail how transitional behaviour affects the behaviour of tailings in both monotonic and cyclic loading and how it might influence the applicability of state parameter based design methods.
To try to identify those elements of fabric that give rise to the transitional behaviour.

112813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
112813.value: Failures of tailings structures have caused significant loss of life, even in recent years, most notably in China where 344 people were killed between 2001 and 2009. These failures have occurred under both static and seismic loading, liquefaction of the materials within the structure being a key hazard in both cases, often exacerbating an initial failure. In part these failures may reflect local lack of control of the design of such structures, but to some degree it must also indicate a lack of understanding of the mechanics of tailings materials, which are undoubtedly made more complex by the variety of materials that are disposed of in this way. There is an increasing amount of research on tailings, addressing their behaviour under monotonic and cyclic loading. In preliminary work carried out by the applicant, a number of tailings from different locations around the world were found to have transitional behaviour, with non-unique compression paths and non-unique critical state lines, so that the behaviour is strongly related to the initial density of the material when it was deposited or created. This mode of behaviour would make uncertain how existing methods of design within a critical or steady state framework, such as those based on a state parameter, might be applied. The project brings together both expertise and sources of tailings from several countries in which large numbers of such structures are built, with the aim of investigating when transitional behaviour might be expected in tailings and the implications for our understanding of their behaviour when it does. 矿渣结构的破坏造成了重大人员伤亡损失，中国在2001年到2009年间有344人死于尾矿事故。这些破坏是由静力和动力荷载作用引起的，结构中材料液化是这两种情况下的关键破坏因素，它加剧了初始的破坏。在过去，这些破坏可以反映该种结构设计参数的缺失，但同时也在一定程度上反映了对于矿渣结构材料特性了解的缺乏，而矿渣材料的多样性无疑使之更加复杂。目前，针对矿渣的研究越来越多，包括其处于单调或者循环荷载下的力学行为。根据申请人前期对世界各地矿渣的研究，其表明部分矿渣材料有不收敛力学特性，即非唯一压缩路径和非唯一临界状态线，也就是说这样的行为与材料的初始密度密切相关。这种行为模式将会使得现有的临界或稳态框架的设计方法变得不确定，如使用的状态参数。该项目汇合了来自拥有大量尾矿结构的国家的大量材料和相关知识，旨在研究矿渣材料的不收敛力学特性及其影响。

112813.label: Realisation of objectives
112813.value: Throughout the implementation of this project on the mechanical behaviour of tailing soils and the investigation of features of transitional behaviour and their relationships with soil characteristics and fabrics, a very large number of high quality experiments was conducted and additionally, a large number of literature data were re-analyzed and compared with the experiments carried out by the principal and co-investigators of the project to draw general conclusions into the complex behaviour of tailings. The project allowed the development and establishment of a number of international collaborations between the co-investigators of the project and other research groups, which led to a high quality output of research articles appeared in international journals covering the whole range of the objectives of the project. Key articles of these international collaborations may refer to Todisco et al. (2018) and Ponzoni et al. (2017). The majority of the experiments were carried out at the City University of Hong Kong, but additional experiments which contributed invaluably to the objectives of the project, were carried out at the University of Brescia Italy, Ècole des Ponts Paris Tech (IFSTTAR CNRS) France, the University of New South Wales Australia, and the Institute of Rock and Soil Mechanics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, China. A PhD thesis by Wei Li was successfully completed at the City University Hong Kong in 2017, which comprised core component of the project deliverables and a research article by Li et al. (2018) was a prime work in comparing three tailings examined at the City University with a large number of tailings from literature studies and studies by the Co-I of the project, Prof. Schnaid. The high quality and of large volume experimental work was accompanied by analytical works to further support the outcomes of the project and obtain insights into the complex behaviour of soils understanding the role of soil characteristics and fabrics, including the probabilistic-based study by Akeju et al. (2017), the statistical-based study by Todisco et al. (2018) and the numerical study by Lopera Perez et al. (2018), which works had a direct focus on possible transitional soils or a broader objective contributing to the outcomes of the project. The volume of the experimental work and some key research articles which delivered or partly supported the project could be outlined as follows: - Study of the compression behaviour of tailing soils and the role of fabric on the mechanics of soils: Approximately a total number of more than 250 tests were conducted on more than ten different soils. - Study of the shearing monotonic and cyclic behaviour of tailing soils and the role of fabric on the mechanics of soils: Approximately a total number of more than 200 tests were conducted on more than fifteen types of soils. Key parts of these experiments (compression and shearing) appeared in the research papers by Li et al. (2018), Ponzoni et al. (2017), Todisco et al. (2018). - Investigation of the cyclic-dynamic behaviour of tailing soils and the role of fabric on the mechanics of soils: Approximately a total number of more than 100 experiments have been conducted on more than fifteen types of soils and additional analytical works have supported the outcomes of the research. Key parts of these experiments appeared in the research papers by Li et al. (2018), Todisco et al. (2018), Akeju et al. (2017) and Li and Senetakis (2017), and additional support to the project outcomes was implemented from the studies by He et al. (2017, 2018). Three major types of tailing soils comprised key materials of the project, which materials cover representative tailings around the world: a gold tailing, an iron tailing and a copper tailing. The present gold tailing represents a soil of fractal grading of finer average size in comparison to a previously studied material by the Co-I Prof. Schnaid. Due to the different grain size characteristics of these two soils, this comparison led a detailed investigation and the establishment of the role particle characteristics that may control the behaviour of tailings and their possible transitional mode and features of their behaviour in association with the objectives of the project will be outlined in section 6. From the iron tailing, three different gradings were studied representing different locations of the tailing dam; comparisons of the three iron tailings, the gold tailing and the well-graded copper tailing, led to a deeper understanding of the role of particle characteristics and tailing type into their mechanical behaviour. It was realized, based on the study by Li and Senetakis (2017), that tailing soils of fractal gradings, follow a similar mode of behaviour with other types of soils of different composition in terms of small-strain behaviour, as long as proper quantification of particle shape and grain size characteristics are encountered. This expanded the research into two different kinds of materials examined in terms of grain size characteristics; (1) gap-graded soils, where the features of transitional (or slow-convergent behaviour) were clearer, as for example in the study by Todisco et al. (2018) and Ponzoni et al. (2017). For these types of materials, apart from laboratory works including compression, shearing, and cyclic-dynamic tests, mercury intrusion porosimetry tests were also conducted in collaboration with Prof. Pereira at Paris Tech to thoroughly examine the correlation between soil fabric, slow-convergent behaviour and the investigation of the applicability of the critical state soil mechanics for given types of soils (detailed by Todisco et al., 2018). (2) Soils of fractal gradings, where features of slow-convergent behaviour could be identified, but, as will explained in section 6, different modes of testing revealed the way that fabric effects can be erased and this was supported in the project both experimentally (e.g. Li et al., 2018, Ponzoni et al., 2017, Todisco et al., 2018) and analytically with statistical approaches (e.g. Todisco et al., 2018). Particularly for smaller to medium strains, a probabilistic framework was developed by Akeju, Senetakis (Co-I) and Wang (PI) (Akeju et al., 2017) which is the first work of its type in soil mechanics research with broader impact and applicability. For soils of fractal gradings, throughout the experimental study, there was provided the chance to expand the project investigating other types of materials with more similar or different characteristics in comparison to tailings, so that (i) more general conclusions can be drawn with broader impact in geotechnical research and practice and (ii) through the comparisons of a broader range of soils with the tailing ones, finer conclusions could be drawn and understand the whole set of parameters that control the behaviour of tailing soils so that the objectives of the project were successfully delivered on firm basis. Complex patterns of testing in both smaller and larger strains were implemented and advanced instrumentation and techniques were applied, for example three-dimensional bender element instrumentation, so that the quantification and understanding of fabric effects could be clearer.

112813.label: Major findings and research outcome
112813.value: It could be impossible to summarize the large number of outputs of the study in association with the main objectives of the project in a few lines, even though a general overview has been presented in section 5. Some of the key elements of the delivered outcomes are therefore discussed in this section. The comprehensive study on different types of tailing soils, including both experimental and analytical studies, as well as the investigation into a wide range of soils in terms of particle characteristics and fabrics, led to important outcomes: given types of soils have a clearer transitional (or slow-convergent) mode of behaviour, for example soils of the gap-graded type or even soils of fractal grading of finer particles (Objective 1). However, this slow-convergent behaviour was more evidently shown in compression and that the application of shear stresses could erase this mode of behaviour (Objective 2). Key studies into these observations were conducted by Li et al. (2018), Todisco et al. (2018) and Ponzoni et al. (2017). In practice, this means that the initial fabric will dominate the behaviour within typical geotechnical engineering pressures that a tailing dam will possibly experience. This questions, within the expected pressure levels, the applicability of the critical state soil mechanics framework as highlighted by Todisco et al. (2018) and Ponzoni et al. (2017). As examined by Li et al. (2018) and Ponzoni et al. (2017), a soil of finer size, in comparison to a same type of material but coarser, may prevent particle breakage, however, as the aforementioned studies showed, this would not affect the applicability of the critical state soil mechanics framework as long as much larger strains are applied, but it will control the behaviour when the shear stresses are less dominant. Based on key studies by Li et al. (2018), Todisco et al. (2018) and Li and Senetakis (2018), it was revealed that tailing soils show fairly isotropic behaviour and that the feature of non-convergence is not associated with possible differences of initial void ratios but it is a real behaviour of soils (Objective 3).

112813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
112813.value: For future studies, it worth to be investigated the role of time effects on the mechanical behaviour of tailings and whether these effects could play a role on potential non-convergent behaviour, which was not studied in the project as well as to expand the investigation from the very small scale (e.g. tailing grain contact response) to the scale of element soil sample. Because a high quality and of large-volume database has been developed based on experiments of a broad range of soils of variable characteristics, focused studies such as the two possible topics mentioned before, can be conducted easier with reference to the available element test results.

112813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
112813.value: Understanding of the engineering behaviour of tailing soils is of major interest in civil infrastructure with important environmental and economical implications. Previous experience on a large number of failures of tailing dams, which caused fatalities and irreversible environmental, economical and social problems to societies, has shown that it is possible that these failures are related not only with the technical and geometrical characteristics of these structures and their construction design, but also with the poor understanding of the mechanical behaviour of tailing soils. So that, the present project contributes to the scientific and engineering communities to understand all the important features that control soil behaviour, targeting tailing soils, which advances the better prediction of the response of tailing dams and their safer performance. In this project, a large number of soil types were tested including different tailings from around the world. A number of high quality collaborations was achieved between different universities and academics, which led to an impactful output of scientific works. These works contribute to the enhancement of our knowledge and understanding on the engineering behaviour of tailings.

113513.label: Project Title(Chinese)
113513.value: 基於部件組裝的日常物體三維幾何和結構的重建方法

113513.label: Project Objectives
113513.value: To turn consumer-level depth cameras like the Kinect system to powerful personal 3D scanners; To help users easily construct high-quality digital 3D models of real-world objects from low-quality scan acquisition; To reconstruct a complete geometry of the underlying object from highly noisy, incomplete 3D scans with the help of the corresponding RGB images under the same viewpoints; To recover the underlying part-level structures of real-world objects from single- or multi-view scan acquisition that essentially contains unorganized points and/or pixels; To develop bottom-up approaches that are able to create new structures by automatically assembling existing parts in a small-scale shape repository with respect to input scans; To examine the issues related to 3D scanning and modeling of multiple objects, and explore applications such as interactive shape modeling and indoor scene modeling.

113513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
113513.value: 3D scanning is one of the most effective ways for 3D modeling, which is at the heart of computer graphics and visualization. The growing popularity of fast, easy-to-use, low-cost depth cameras (e.g., the Microsoft Kinect) presents new acquisition possibilities and makes it possible for everyone to digitize 3D objects at home. However, the resulting raw scans are often highly noisy and incomplete. Hence, a faithful reconstruction of the underlying 3D geometry is rather challenging even for the state-of-the-art techniques, let alone understanding its semantic structure. This work gets inspirations from the recent advancement of assembly-based 3D modeling, which is designed for artist-driven, open-ended 3D modeling. Our key idea is to let a computer (serving as a virtual artist) utilize acquired scans from depth cameras to automatically guide and constrain a process of part assembly. This poses an interesting but challenging research problem given the exponentially growing space by shape synthesis via part composition. We present a promising framework by heavily exploiting geometric priors for individual parts and their mutual relations exhibited in the shape repository. It results in a novel approach for recovering high-detailed 3D geometry from low-quality scan acquisition of everyday objects. Unlike existing surface reconstruction technologies, which are limited to low-level geometry reconstruction, our framework naturally enables high-level shape understanding and allows the creation of new semantic structures with respect to the acquired data. The produced structures can directly benefit applications like structure-aware shape editing and synthesis. In short, the proposed framework will turn consumer-level depth cameras to powerful personal 3D scanners and allow quick conversion of low-quality object scans to high-quality 3D digital models with semantic structures. The output of our framework can be directly fed into a wide range of applications, for example, semantic indoor modeling, augmented reality, reverse engineering and rapid prototyping etc. We are confident that we can complete the project and deliver the expected outcomes. We have had extensive research experiences in the field of shape analysis, which we believe have paved the way for the proposed ideas. We expect that the new project will follow the success of our current projects and make continuous contributions to both research and industry. 三維幾何建模是圖形學的一個核心問題。三維掃描是行之有效的幾何建模技術，但是該技術主要被專業人士使用。這幾年，隨著低價、快速、易用的深度相機的普及，讓一般用戶把家用物體三維數字化變得可能。然而，廉價的深度相機產生的數據通常含有很大的噪聲並且經常有數據丟失的現象。 因此，從這樣的數據中要很好的恢復出三維幾何來是很有挑戰性的，更不用說要理解有語義的結構了。 此項目是受最近才開始發展起來的基於部件組裝三維建模方法的啟發。這些方法原本是被設計用來做有藝術家驅動，開放式的三維建模。我們工作的主要想法是讓電腦來充當虛擬藝術家的角色，用來自深度相機的數據來自動引導和約束部件組裝過程。這是一個很有意思的課題，但同時有具有挑戰性。最大的挑戰主要來自由部件組裝構成的幾何空間是跟部件數目成幾何級別增長的。為了解決這個問題，我們提出盡可能的使用每個部件的幾何先驗知識以及部件間的相互關係，這些信息都可以通過分析幾何部件的數據庫來得到。這個方法把從低質量的掃描數據中恢復出高細節的幾何模型變得有可能。另外，不同於以前的曲面重建的方法，我們提出的框架還能夠允許做有語義的形狀理解，對根據數據自動生成新的有語義的結構是很有幫助的。這些產生的結構可以直接被運用到多個應用中，比如結構感知的形狀編輯和合成等。 簡言之，我們提出的框架可以讓一個消費級的深度相機變成一個功能強大的三維掃描儀，能夠快速地從低質量數據中恢復出高質量、帶有語義結構的三維模型來。從我們框架產生的模型可以直接輸入到很多應用中，例如室內建模、增強現實、反向工程和快速成形等。

113513.label: Realisation of objectives
113513.value: We have achieved all the objectives. ++ Objectives 1-2 ++ To make consumer-level depth sensors like Microsoft Kinect for better acquisition of real-world objects, we have introduced a saliency-aware volumetric fusion approach for acquiring 3D objects in real time [Journal 11]. While the objects in the resulting scans are of better quality than those by traditional Kinect fusion approaches, they are represented in unorganized point clouds and their segmentation is unknown. To focus more on the modeling of individual objects, we developed an interactive segmentation interface for extracting semantic objects from 3D scans [Journal 9]. We contributed a mechanism of automatic view suggestion to make interactive segmentation of large-scale scenes more efficient. ++ Objectives 3-5 ++ We developed bottom-up approaches for 3D modeling by part assembly (Objective 5), either interactively or automatically. In the work of [Conference 3], we present SweepCanvas, which provides a sketch-based in-context modeling tool for quick prototyping on 3D scans by consumer-level depth sensors. We use swept surfaces as basic primitives (building blocks) and exploit the structural information in the 3D scans of existing objects to interpret input 2D sketches. Users can sketch and assemble new swept surfaces to interactively create 3D concept designs on top of existing scenes. Towards the synthesis of a more detailed, complete geometry of an object (Objective 3), in [Journal 1] we proposed a method to build 3D structured mechanical collages by assembling mechanical parts with respect to a coarse proxy model, which can be either designed by artists or reconstructed from 3D scans. We employ some graphic design guidelines such as variety and unity to make resulting assemblies visually structural. To introduce semantic part-level structure (Objective 4), we have developed a part-assembly-based approach for semantic segmentation and labeling of freehand sketches by exploiting the known segmentation and labeling information in existing 3D models [Journal 3]. This can be easily extended to handle edge maps of scanned real-world objects to get their part-level structures. The above mentioned works have focused on in-class synthesis of 3D models by reusing the parts that belong to the same object category. We have further explored cross-class geometry and structure synthesis under the bottom-up part assembly framework (Objective 5). The main challenge is how to still achieve functionally plausible and structurally valid synthesis results given the possibly much larger shape space. To address this key issue, we have experimented various additional cues, including reference examples [Journal 5], support and stability [Journal 8], human poses [Journal 10], when assembling parts from objects of different categories. ++ Objective 6 ++ We have shown that the developed assembly-based modeling techniques can benefit various applications, including indoor scene synthesis, intelligent arrangement of graphic elements, smart image tracing, and font synthesis. Our part assembly idea has been used in [Journal 7] to achieve structure-adaptive shape editing for man-made objects. By re-combing objects instead of object parts, we developed a structure-guided interior scene synthesis technique [Journal 6]. We successfully applied the idea of global interpretation [Journal 3] for automatic refinement of sketches roughly traced over images [Journal 2]. Inspired by the graphic design rules used in [Journal 1] and the structural information inference from 3D scans [Conference 3], we also developed two intelligent interfaces for arranging graphic elements as 2D parts [Conferences 1 and 2]. The key idea is to first infer geometric relations between parts and then enforce such relations to get a well arranged layout. Our part assembly idea has also been used for synthesizing a complete font given the glyphs for a given small set of letters [Journal 4]. We learn the assembling rules from hundreds of existing fonts and use them to re-assemble the parts of the input glyphs to create the glyphs for new letters.

113513.label: Major findings and research outcome
113513.value: We developed the bottom-up part assembly framework and explored part assembly in different granularity levels and different dimensions, benefiting various applications. In the project we have successfully demonstrated that the framework of part assembly is very powerful for 3D modeling [Journals 1 and 8; Conference 3]. By properly picking and placing existing parts, we are able to create high-quality 3D models from low-quality models like proxy models or 3D scans. Part assembly can be done at various granularity levels to create new parts [Journal 1], objects [Journals 5, 7, 8, 10], or scenes [Journal 6]. For the synthesis of objects in the same object class [Journals 3, 7, 8], our task of part assembly can be relatively easily achieved by switching parts of the same part labels. However, this task is more challenging for cross-class object synthesis, i.e., when synthesizing new models by re-combing parts from existing objects of different classes. We have shown that simply using geometric cues are not enough, and we have to exploit additional cues such as human pose and support & stability to restrict the feasible shape space [Journals 8 and 10]. The part assembly idea can also be applied in spaces of different dimensions. While our focus is more on 3D modeling, we have applied the idea of part assembly to 2D parts (for font synthesis [Journal 4] and graphic elements arrangement [Conferences 1 and 2]). Its benefit for the analysis of 1D sketches has been demonstrated in two applications for semantic segmentation and labeling of freehand sketches [Journal 3], and sketch beautification [Journal 2]. The project led to in total 14 publications, including 11 journal papers and 3 conference papers. Among them 11 papers were presented at the top conferences and journals in the graphics and HCI fields (the rankings below are based on Google Scholar Metrics): - Journals 2 and 3: in ACM Transactions on Graphics (the best journal in the graphics field); presented at SIGGRAPH or SIGGRAPH Asia (the best graphics conferences); - Journals 1, 8 and 9: in IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics (No. 2 in graphics); - Journals 4, 7 and 11: in Computer Graphics Forum (No. 3 in graphics); - Conference 2: in ACM CHI (the best HCI conference); - Conferences 1 and 3: in ACM UIST (No. 4 in HCI).

113513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
113513.value: Assembly-based 3D modeling is essentially data driven. We have mainly focused on using purely geometric approaches to identify possible relations between parts so that the synthesized models are structurally valid and functionally plausible. In [Journal 4], we took a learning-based approach, which learns a distribution over hand-crafted features for flexible typeface synthesis. In recent years, it has been proved that deep learning is able to achieve the best performance for various tasks. It would be very interesting to explore how deep learning can be used in our scenario to make part assembly based shape analysis and synthesis perform even better.

113513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
113513.value: In this project we have explored bottom-up part assembly approaches for shape analysis and synthesis, at the levels of both geometry and structure. The key idea is that given a set of existing parts, we properly select and place them together so that the resulting assemblies become structurally valid or even functionally plausible new shapes. We demonstrated its use for synthesizing 3D models by using parts from objects from the same or different categories. We examined different constraints, including human poses, support and stability, reference examples, and target shapes represented as coarse models (acquired by consumer-level depth sensors or freehand sketches). We also explored part assembly in different granularity levels and different dimensions. The proposed part assembly approaches have been demonstrated for various applications, including 3D scanning using consumer-level depth sensors, sketch-based 3D modeling, indoor scene synthesis, pose-driven shape modeling, semantic segmentation and labeling of freehand sketches, smart image tracing, font synthesis, and intelligent arrangement of graphic elements. This research project led to more than ten publications published in top journals and conferences in the computer graphics and human-computer interaction areas, one keynote speech, one Best Paper award, and two patents.

114013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
114013.value: The proposed project aims to develop a novel analytical model for studying the multistable characteristic of thin-walled shells prestressed by using a self-controlling and self-monitoring smart system. Previous studies have showed that shell stability properties are determined by its initial shape, and not more than two stable equilibrium configurations can be achieved for most of shells. This research will investigate a smart control system which makes typical shells, including isotropic shells, to have more than two stable equilibrium configurations. First, a nonlinear finite element approach will be established to analyze the multistable behavior of shells embedded with piezoelectric patches, taking into consideration the effects of electro-mechanical coupling, large deformation, and snap-through behavior. Secondly, a feedback control algorithm will be developed to achieve multistable characteristics of shells subjected to residual stresses which are induced by the active and sensory response of piezoelectric actuator/sensor patches. Meanwhile, combined with the developed feedback control algorithm, an optimization algorithm will be derived to model a particular distribution of residual stresses which will lead to two or more desired stable equilibrium configurations. The feedback control gains for the closed loop feedback control will be optimised to ensure achieving a desired stable configuration. It is worth noting that, so far, no application of the self-powered piezoelectric actuators/sensors for multistable characteristic was reported in literature, and the proposed research will result in a new type of multistable structure. 壳结构的稳定平衡状态是由初始几何形状决定的，一般不会多于两个。本项目拟开发一个新颖的智能控制模型，用于设计新型的薄壁壳结构，使其具有多于两个的稳态特性。首先建立一个非线性的有限元智能模型，研究力-电藕合，大变形及屈曲跳跃等特性的影响。其次，开发压电反馈智能系统，优化设计增益矩阵，从而得到特定的残余应力分布，该残余应力分布能实现薄壁壳结构的多稳态平衡构型及所需要的稳定平衡构型。

114013.label: Realisation of objectives
114013.value: 1) Nonlinear numerical models based on finite element method have been formulated for bistable mechanisms of thin-walled shells with coupled electro-mechanical characteristics of piezoelectric sensor/actuator patches. The numerical models show that the attached piezoelectric patches have considerable influence to the stable configurations. However, external inputting energies are compelling required to hold the designed residual stress field for specific stable configurations. 2) An analytical formulation combined with a fractional-order time derivative damping model has been formulated for the large amplitude free and forced vibration response of carbon nanotubes (CNTs)/fiber/polymer laminated multiscale composite beams. 3) A nonlinear numerical model combined with feedback control algorithm is formulated for bistable shells using piezoelectric actuator/sensor based smart system. Genetic algorithm is also combined for the formulated numerical model to find the optimal residual stress field generated from the smart system, which is determined by the gain matrix, for targeted stable configurations. 4) The residual stress field generated from the smart system is based on the actuation from piezoelectric actuator, which continuously consuming external inputting energies. To spare the continuous energy consumption, a new method to achieve bistable and multistable shells with designable features is proposed by using nanotechnology, Surface Mechanical Attrition Treatment (SMAT), on isotropic metallic plates. The residual stress field left in the nanostructured shells from localized treatments determines the two or multiple stable configurations, which can be controlled and designed. 5) Currently, 6 journal papers have been published and one journal paper (Materials & Design, IF: 4.364) is under second review in a revised version. 6) Three students with dissertation focusing on bistable shells have completed their studies and obtain their Master Degrees. One student with dissertation titled as “Theoretical and Experimental Study of Multistable Shells Developed by SMAT” has completed his study and obtained his Doctor Degree.

114013.label: Major findings and research outcome
114013.value:  1. Systematic experimental and numerical study of bistable snap processes for anti-symmetric cylindrical shells has shown that the initial mid-plane transverse radius and ply angle are two key factors that affect bistable behaviors in the same environmental conditions, which is accordant with theoretical predictions, whereas the number of plies and longitudinal length of the shell only influence on the snap load and stress distribution. The angle of embrace is demonstrated of no influence on bistable performance of anti-symmetric cylindrical shells [1]. 2. A new method to achieve bistable and multistable isotropic metallic shells of designable feature has been proposed and studied in this project. The original idea is to achieve different bistable and multistable properties through the generated residual stress fields by using localized stimulation from the accumulated plastic deformation during the nanocrystallization process and the largely increased elastic deformation ability of the nanostructured shells. 3. An improved interpolating complex variable moving least squares (IICVMLS) method is proposed for numerical simulations of structures, in which a complete basis function and singular weight function are used to form a new basis function through the orthogonalization process. And a new shape function which has the property of Kronecker δ function is derived to build the interpolating function. Combining the IICVMLS method with specific problems, an improved interpolating complex variable element free Galerkin (IICVEFG) method is obtained with directly satisfied essential boundary conditions [6]. Compared with other non-interpolating meshless methods, the IICVEFG has higher accuracy and efficiency. The proposed IICVEFG can be used to deal with the large deformation analysis of bistable structures. 4. An analytical formulation combined with a fractional-order time derivative damping model has been developed to conduct a comprehensive study on the large amplitude free and forced vibration response of carbon nanotubes (CNTs)/fiber/polymer laminated multiscale composite structures [2]. The analytical formulation can be used to investigate the vibration between two equilibrium states of a bistable structure. 5. Three patents have been filed in USA and China for a developed technique to manufacture bistable or multistable structures.

114013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
114013.value: The developed bistable and multistable isotropic metallic shells, which have good stabilities and designable configurations, are potentially applied in aerodynamic fields, such as for airplane wings, automobile’s morphing surfaces, etc. Energy is only required to trig the transition among different configurations. Currently, the transition system for the developed bistable and multistable shells is under research. When the transition system is finished, the full aerodynamic response of a multistable structure mimicking a morphing wing will be conducted in the wind tunnel. The ability of adjusting aerodynamic performance using different stable configurations of multistable shells will be accurately measured. Besides, the transition system will be combined with feedback control system in order to make sure that the actuated multistable shell holds the targeted specific stable configuration.

114013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
114013.value: This research project aims to develop a new method to achieve novel structures that can hold two or multiple equilibrium configurations of designable feature without external supports or consuming inputting energies. Through a localized process using nanotechnology, surface mechanical attrition treatment, which is conventionally used for improving material properties, a special residual stress field is left in nanostructured shells and enable the processed shells to hold alternative stable configurations without external supports or inputting energies. Energies are only required to trig transitions among different stable configurations. As manufacture parameters can be fully controlled, the stable configurations of the proposed bistable and multistable shells can be designed for specific functions. It is believed that the achieve bistable and multistable shells are valuable for aerodynamic fields, such as morphing wings, morphing car surfaces, and other shape morphing related areas.
