114113.label: Project Title(Chinese)
114113.value: 分布式网络化系统的故障分析：诊断、控制和恢复

114113.label: Project Objectives
114113.value: to investigate the fault diagnosis problem of DNSs, in which a distributed fault detection and isolation technique will be proposed; to design a NFTC scheme for DNSs, which should be implemented at the selected nodes with optimal control effect; to develop a fault recovery scheme to keep the collaborative performance of DNSs after isolation of the failure nodes.
rows: to investigate the fault diagnosis problem of DNSs, in which a distributed fault detection and isolation technique will be proposed;
to design a NFTC scheme for DNSs, which should be implemented at the selected nodes with optimal control effect;
to develop a fault recovery scheme to keep the collaborative performance of DNSs after isolation of the failure nodes.

114113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
114113.value: A distributed networked system (DNS) consists of a large number of small, inexpensive agents deployed over a vast region, in which each agent is capable of collecting, processing information and communication with neighboring agents. For instance, many real-world engineering systems including sensor networks and Autonomous Underwater Vehicles can be well described by DNS. Node collaboration is the key for the success of distributed networked systems (DNSs) due to the fact that each node itself is limited by communication range, power, and processing ability. Although DNSs have been extensively applied in practical work, the distributed behavior of the DNSs do bring some essential difficulties in theoretical research. In particular, as the DNSs began to be implemented for critical tasks such as military or power system applications, the risk of network failures became more of a concern. Unfortunately, node fault and link failures generally bring undesirable effects on the stability and performance of DNSs; Thus, developing network fault diagnosis, control and recovery techniques are necessary for the response to the increasing complexity and safety demand of real-world DNSs. It is highly desirable to exploit effective protocols and methods for the fault detection and control to maintain the stability and performance of the DNSs. The project aims: - to detect and isolate the fault of nodes and link failures of the DNSs; - to develop network fault-tolerant control (NFTC) design techniques for the compensable node/link failures to maintain the performance of the DNS. - to design a fault recovery scheme for the noncompensable faults to retrieve the performance of the DNS. The theoretical results generated in this proposal, if well accomplished, will lay a solid foundation for the development of a wide range of fields,including coordination of sensor networks and formation control of unmanned robots. In particular, the development of fault detection and isolation techniques, network fault-tolerant control as well as fault recovery schemes for DNSs would be an important step to improve the reliability of practical DNSs. 分布式网络化系统是由分布在广大区域上数量巨大的多智能体组成。这些多智能体体积小、价格便宜，有能力收集、处理数据，并且和能和周围智能体进行通信。现实中，许多工程系统，如传感器网络和水下自动机器人系统，都可以被归类为分布式网络化系统。由于每个节点本身受限于通讯范围、电量和处理能力，节点之间的相互协作是分布式网络化系统能成功运行的关键。 尽管分布式网络化系统在实际当中已经得到了广泛的应用，但其分布式行为也为理论研究带来了许多困难。特别是，当系统被布置去执行重要任务，例如军事或者电网应用等，产生网络故障的风险就必须考虑。不幸的是节点故障和链接失败往往会对整个系统的稳定和性能造成不良影响。因此，研究网络故障的诊断、控制和恢复对实际应用中结构越来越复杂，安全要求越来越高的分布式网络化系统是十分必要的，亟需研究出有效的协议和方法来检测故障以及保持系统的稳定性和性能。 本项目研究目标是：  在分布式网络化系统中检测出节点故障和链接失败，并将其从系统中隔离出来；  对于可以补偿的节点或链接故障，研究网络化容错控制器的设计方法来保持系统性能；  对于不能补偿的故障，研究故障恢复方案来重新维持系统性能。 本项目所产生的理论结果，如能顺利完成将会为一系列应用研究，如传感器网络的协同以及机器人编队控制等方面奠定坚实的基础。特别是，所研究出来的故障检测和隔离技术，网络故障容错控制和故障恢复方案将为改进分布式网络化系统的可靠性迈出重要一步。

114113.label: Realisation of objectives
114113.value: The objectives of the project have been fully achieved. (1) Preliminary works on Distributed Network Systems (DNS) have been set up. The work related to communication delays , quantization parameters, distributed optimization have been investigated. The above work in [1-4] has built up a strong foundation for studying various issues in multi-agents . (2) Realization of Objective 1: Fault diagnosis problem of DNSs are investigated in the project. A distributed state estimation performance is proposed in [5]. Based on this performance requirement, the state estimators are designed for a distributed heterogeneous system based on sampled data measurements. A new performance index for distributed state estimator is proposed of which the effect of the sharp changes of fault is also taken into consideration. In this paper, the required performance for the state estimation for each node in the heterogeneous distributed system can be achieved. Further, an estimation approach in [6] has been proposed to construct a fault estimator for the signal transmission faults occurred in the process of the two-target tracking in distributed sensor networks. (3) Realization of Objective 2: Design various Network Fault-Tolerance Control (NFTC) schemes for DNS and multi-agent systems. Different types of control methods have been designed for various faulty systems: (a) sampled-data approach for heterogeneous Distributed Systems with fault[5], (b) fault-tolerance consensus for multi-agent systems using distributed adaptive protocol[6], (c) fault reconstruction design for distributed sensor networks[7], (d) adaptive fault-tolerant control scheme for Markovian Jump system[8], (e) passivity based fault-tolerance control for quantized coordination[9], (f) consensus control for autonomous Under Water Vehicles (AUVs) under imperfect information caused by communication faults[10]. (4) Realization of Objective 3: Different fault recovery schemes have been set up in the above NFTC control design. Various consensus recovery methods to nonlinear multi-agent systems have been developed for the cases in 3(a)-(f). In particular, different schemes are designed for the failure of nodes which lead to many communication issues. For examples, based on partial information in various channels in (c), some useful schemes are developed for sensor networks. Some practical simulations have been applied and presented in the project[7]. In addition, an adaptive fault-tolerance scheme in (d) is developed for Markovian Jump system with actuator faults, nonlinearity and external disturbances[8]. By on-line estimating the loss of effectiveness of actuators faults and the bounds of Euclidean norm of nonlinearity function, the proposed adaptive backstepping controller can compensate these effects completely, and the stochastic stability of the fault closed-loop system is guaranteed. Further, by extending the idea in [8], the online updating parameters are then used to develop a distributed adaptive protocol in [6]. This approach has the advantage to compensate the fault effects and the uncertainty effects in the leaderless multi-agent system. As a result, the consensus problem is then recovered. Moreover, in this project, passivity based fault tolerant control for coordination using two types of quantizers is investigated[9]. Firstly, a fault tolerant coordination scheme with logarithmic quantizers is designed using passivity property. Furthermore, another fault tolerant coordination scheme is constructed by using uniform quantizers which makes the convergence set to go to a bounded set. Thus, these conditions provide a deep insight to the cases when the coordination under imperfect communication environment. Finally, a consensus recovery control for AUVs under imperfect information caused by communication faults has been investigated in [10]. (5) In this project, one PhD student, Dr Shun Chen, has been trained and he graduated in 2015. A total ten papers have been published to fulfill the objectives of the projects. During the research period, the PI worked with more than ten researchers from different institutes to complete the tasks. Different research ideas have been generated from different groups through discussions when they visited Hong Kong. The project is considered to be successful to realize all the objectives.

114113.label: Major findings and research outcome
114113.value: Initially, we studied some research work in DNS which provides a strong background for the team to investigate various fault models. Publications [1-4] are produced on various research issues in DNS during the preliminary stage. In addition, four conference papers were presented in the 33th Chinese Control Conference on Multi-agent Systems in 2014. Finally, the project produced 6 papers [5-10] on the fault control and recovery problems to realize the objectives. Here is a summary of the major findings. (1) Preliminary works on Distributed Network Systems (DNS) have been investigated. The work related to communication delays [1], quantization parameters [2], distributed optimization [3,4] have been investigated. The above work has built up a strong foundation for studying various issues in multi-agents. (2) Various Network Fault-Tolerance Control (NFTC) and recovery schemes for DNS have been designed for multi-agent systems: (a) Sampled-data approach for heterogeneous Distributed Systems [5]. A performance index for distributed state estimation is proposed. A useful tool for fault analysis is established. (b) Fault-tolerance consensus for multi-agent systems using distributed adaptive protocol [6]. Based on the local state information of neighboring agents, a distributed updating protocol gain is developed. It leads to a fully distributed adaptive fault-tolerant leader-follower consensus. (c) Fault reconstruction design for distributed sensor networks [7]. Two sets of estimator designs for distributed sensor networks in multi-tracking under signal transmission faults due to uncertain environment is developed. Two industrial examples have been illustrated the effectiveness of the theory. (d) Adaptive fault-tolerant control scheme for Markovian Jump system [8]; The exact knowledge of actuator faults are totally unknown,and an adaptive scheme is set up to solve the problem. The work in [8] is not for DNS, nevertheless it forms a basic idea for [6]. (e) Passivity based fault-tolerance control for quantized coordination [9] is developed. This work focus on the security aspect of the coordination control under fault due to attacks. The quantization function is discontinuous, hence non-smooth analysis is used in the paper. A fault-tolerant coordination scheme with logarithmic quantizers is designed using the passivity property. (f) Consensus control for autonomous under water vehicles (AUVs) under imperfect information caused by communication faults [10] has been developed. A fault model has been set up which affect the communication signal. Thus, new idea has been established to monitor the performance of the UAV. This is a new consensus recovery approach to nonlinear multi-agent systems under imperfect information.

114113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
114113.value: The work can be further extended to safety issues when the multi-agent systems are under attacks. A new proposal has been written and submitted based on some new ideas generated from this research projects. To recover the system under different types of faults is an important research problem, new distributed schemes are required under different topological structure. Thus, based on the recovery concept in this project, a new event based fault recovery scheme is needed after isolation of failure nodes. A new event-triggered scheme for DNSs is required to rebuild new link and recover the consensus goal. To conclude, this project leads us in a great potential for further development of the research of event-based control and filtering design for DNSs.

114513.label: Project Title(Chinese)
114513.value: 多邊普適網絡服務的高效穩定匹配算法

114513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
114513.value: 本项目将研究全新的多邊普適網絡服務的高效穩定匹配算法MUNS,受限于网络带宽与设备限制。我们将MUNS看成一个含不同类型节点的两方（数据服务器-用户终端）或三方（数据源-服务器-用户终端）匹配结构。这些节点将自适应进行连接，对实时数据流（如视频流）等进行采集、存储、优化传输到用户终端。我们的主要目的是探索匹配理论及研究设计实时、分布式算法以解决用户服务质量与MUNS系统资源受限这一主要矛盾。理论研究挑战是找出稳定的匹配的最大个数算法并达到Pareto Optimality（帕累托最优). 我们预计这项项目的研究成果将填补无线网络流媒体系统匹配的理论与算法空白并取得实际系统设计的经验。

114613.label: Project Objectives
114613.value: The overall aim of this research is to investigate the impact of the Joint Practices Notes (JPNs) 1 & 2 on the use of prefabrication and on construction waste reduction level in Hong Kong High-rise buildings.The detailed objectives of this study are to: Compare the use of prefabrication in terms of types of precast elements and volume before and after the implementation of the JPNs 1 & 2; and after the revision of JPNs in 2011. Assess and compare the environmental benefits of using prefabrication in buildings with conventional construction methods. Assess the construction waste reduction potential by using prefabrication in high-rise buildings and examine the impact of the revised JPNs on the use of prefabrication and waste reduction levels. Discuss and examine the existing building regulations and incentives to promote the use of prefabrication in Hong Kong and construction waste reduction.

114613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
114613.value: Construction activities have significant and irreversible effects on the environment, and generates large amount of waste. In Hong Kong, as in many countries the disposal of construction waste has become a severe social and environmental problem. Prefabrication has been identified as a solution to reduce the generation of construction waste arising from design and construction phases. In recent years, the government has implemented incentive schemes, the Joint Practice Notes 1&2, with gross floor area exemptions granted for building development employing green and innovative building technologies and prefabrication. These Joint Practice Notes were recently revised in 2011, modifying the maximum area allowed for exemption when using prefabricated walls. This research project will attempt to assess the impact of the Joint Practice Notes on the use of prefabrication in high-rise building and its waste reduction level. In this research project, data will be collected and analysed , using combination of quantitative and qualitative methodologies such as questionnaire survey, detailed case studies of recently completed buildings in Hong Kong (including site observations), and face-to-face interviews. The triangulation between results will allow validation of the collected data. This research could significantly promote the aspiration towards a more environmentally responsible and sustainable building industry in Hong Kong to achieve a healthy built environment and efficient use of resources. 建築建設的過程製造了大量廢料，對環境已經做成了無可挽救的影響。跟許多國家一樣，香港有大量建築廢料要處理，已經形成了嚴重的社會及環境問題。預製組件已經被證實為一種可在設計及建造期間減少產生建築廢料的方法。近年，政府實施了一些獎勵計劃—聯合作業備考第一、二號，當中提出豁免計算總樓面面積以鼓勵業界設計時加入環保及創新的樓宇建造技術及預製組件當中提出豁免計算總樓面面積以鼓勵房地產開發時採用環保及創新的樓宇建造技術及預製組件。該備考在二零一一年重新修訂，並更改了因使用預製組件而獲得的豁免面積。這次的研究將會評估聯合作業備考對高樓使用預製組件及其減廢的影響。此次的研究會透過用問卷調查、詳細地研究近期完成的香港樓宇(包括實地考察)和親身訪問的方法收集資料及數據，再用定量和定性兩種方法作出分析，相互補充，從而確認收集所得來的資料的可靠性。此項研究有望可大力推動香港建造業，使他們對環境更有承擔及可持續地發展，從而成功打造一個健康的建築環境和有效地使用資源。

114613.label: Realisation of objectives
114613.value: Realisation of objectives With regards to the first, second and fourth objectives, the impact of the Joint Practices Notes (JPNs) 1 & 2 on the use of prefabrication and on construction waste reduction level in Hong Kong High-rise buildings were assessed. The data collection process consisted of a survey and individual face-to-face interviews which targeted various professionals in the construction industry, a database and detailed case studies analysis. The survey aimed to measure the frequency of use of different precast concrete elements, and the degree of impact and effectiveness of government policies and certification systems promoting the use of prefabrication in private housing projects in Hong Kong. The findings from a survey and interviews revealed that most incentives were effective in promoting prefabrication– especially the original JPNs (Joint Practice Notes). However, overall prefabrication adoption decreased due to the revised JPNs and the introduction of a 10% GFA cap by Practice Note for Authorized Persons-151. This study also revealed that precast façades were the most frequently used precast element granted GFA exemptions; the least being precast balconies and precast volumetric bathrooms. The database and detailed case studies aimed to (1) compare the use of Non-structural External Prefabricated Wall (NEPW) before and after the implementation of the original and the revised JPNs; (2) to quantify the construction waste reduction potential by using prefabrication in high-rise buildings and to examine the impact of the revised JPNs on the use of prefabrication and waste reduction levels. The database consists of 22 recently completed or almost completed high-rise residential buildings in Hong Kong. The data was collected using online sale brochures. After analysing the design on each project, there are 8 projects and 14 projects following JPNs 2001 & 2002 and 2011 respectively. For comparing the impact of prefabrication between the original JPNs and the revised JPNs, the exempted GFA of the projects were analysed. According the APP151 (Buildings Department, 2011c), the total GFA exemption is combined by (1) Disregarded GFA under Building (Planning) Regulations 23 (3) (b), (2) Green Features under JPNs 1 and 2, (3) Amenity Features, (4) Other Exempted Items and (5) Bonus GFA. For Green Features under JPNs 1 and 2, the exempted items included: (1) Balcony, (2) Wider common corridor and lift lobby, (3) Communal sky garden, (4) Acoustic fin, (5) Wing wall, (6) wind catcher and funnel, (7) Non-structural prefabricated external wall (NPEW), (8) Utility platform and (9) Noise barrier. For the detailed case studies, an investigation of 5 recently completed high-rise residential projects in Hong Kong, from the public, the semi-private and the private sectors was conducted. The detailed case studies attempted to gather data regarding the present practices of the industry in using prefabrication in high-rise residential buildings. The detailed case studies provided information based on actual details of building projects as well as precise quantitative data of existing industrial practices, like construction waste quantities, material quantities, prefabrication level, etc. The case studies also included face-to-face interviews to validate the data collected. The data of total waste generated during construction, the types and amount of precast elements and formworks were collected. All waste data were collected by contractor from monthly waste flow table. The construction waste generation was calculated with the same method from Jaillon et al. study in 2009. The collected data is then compared with the projects construction under JPN 2001 & 2002 from Jaillon et al. study (2009), average waste quantity of private and public sectors were 0.23 and 0.13 respectively. The findings from the database and detailed case studies revealed that the use of NPEW have been decreased 61.34% (per GFA exemption) since the revised JPNs and the use of curtain wall have been straightly increased (698.73%) as there is 200mm thickness allowance, which is more than precast façade 50mm. The GFA exemption 10% cap has also affected the portion of GFA exempted from green feature (26.53%). The waste quantities of private and public projects have been reduced 30% and 1% respectively compared with Jaillon et al. study (2009). Since the prefabricated component is mainly precast façade, the waste generated may be affected by other reason, for examples: increase the use of steel framework and increase the use of BEAM-Plus. Waste issue is still a concern due to the following reasons: (1) the limited site area for waste sorting and (2) the limited recycling company. With regards to the third objective, the quantification of the GHG emissions and major environmental impacts during construction phase of high-rise buildings in Hong Kong were assessed. The study compared the GHG emissions from material extraction to the construction phase of recently completed building projects using prefabrication with conventional construction methods. The findings revealed that a potential reduction of GHG emissions of about 10% was achieved when using precast concrete construction when compared with in-situ construction. Due to limited time (research study time versus construction phase duration), long and detailed data collection process and data availability (confidential data), the study was confined to the investigation of high-rise buildings from the private sector. Major impact categories for environmental impacts were: (1) human toxicity, (2) marine ecotoxicity, (3) freshwater ecotoxicity, (4) freshwater eutrophication, (5) metal depletion, (6) fossil depletion and (7) climate change. The findings revealed that reductions in these major environmental impact categories were achieved by adopting precast concrete construction when compared with in-situ construction: human toxicity (-11%), marine ecotoxicity (-9%), freshwater ecotoxicity (-9%), freshwater eutrophication (-14%), metal depletion (-6%), fossil depletion (-21%) and climate change (-26%). As far as the fifth objective is concerned, the study examined existing building regulations and incentives to promote the use of prefabrication in Hong Kong and construction waste reduction. In addition, this study assessed the key hindrances of adopting prefabrication and provided recommendations for promoting prefabrication in Hong Kong. 22 hindrances were identified in the literature and classified into 6 groups. A questionnaire survey and face-to-face interviews were conducted. The most significant hindrances were Inflexible for design change, Lack storage space on site, Long lead-in time, Long design time, High initial cost and High total cost. Based on the findings of the survey and interviews, 5 recommendations were proposed to promote the usage of prefabrication in Hong Kong: (1) Just-In-Time philosophy, (2) BIM technology, (3) Potential government measures, (4) Encouragement of design and building procure; and (5) Increase the consumer’s confidence. The overall study demonstrates the effectiveness of current government incentives-especially the original JPNs to promote prefabrication and may be further developed to direct future policies and good practice with the goal of a healthy built environment, efficient use of resources, and a more sustainable building industry. The existing building regulations and incentives although efficient may not be sufficient alone to fully reduce construction waste mainly due to limited site area for waste sorting and limited recycling companies. This study shows that the industry is raising the awareness on monitoring and reducing construction waste generation; however a the adoption of life cycle thinking, material life cycle and circular economy are major considerations to promote sustainable built environment and efficient use of resources.

114613.label: Major findings and research outcome
114613.value: The goal of this research is to investigate the impact of government policies on the use of prefabrication and on construction waste reduction level in Hong Kong High-rise buildings. The study included two surveys, face-to-face interviews, a database and detailed case studies analysis. The findings revealed that most incentives were effective in promoting prefabrication – especially the original JPNs (Joint Practice Notes). However, overall prefabrication adoption decreased (less 61% use of Non-structural External Prefabricated Wall (NEPW) due to the revised JPNs and the introduction of a 10% GFA cap by Practice Note for Authorized Persons-151. A steep increase (699%) of curtain wall use was noted. Precast façades were the most frequently used precast element granted GFA exemptions; the least being precast balconies and precast volumetric bathrooms (Paper 1). The waste quantities of private and public projects were reduced by 30% and 1% respectively compared with Jaillon et al. study (2009). Since the prefabricated component is mainly precast façade, the waste generated may also be affected by the increase in steel formwork use and BEAM-Plus. Waste issue is still a concern due to the following reasons: (1) the limited site area for waste sorting and (2) the limited recycling company (Paper 3). Other hindrances mentioned by respondents were Inflexible for design change, Lack storage space on site, Long lead-in time, Long design time, High initial cost and High total cost (Papers 1&3 and Conference papers 2&4). The study also compared the GHG emissions from material extraction to the construction phase of recently completed building projects using prefabrication with conventional construction methods. The findings revealed that a potential reduction of GHG emissions of about 10% was achieved when using precast concrete construction when compared with in-situ construction (Paper 4, and Conference papers 1&3). The overall study demonstrates that although the existing building regulations and incentives may not be sufficient alone to fully reduce construction waste mainly due to limited site area for waste sorting, limited recycling companies and the lack of life cycle thinking. This study shows that the industry is raising the awareness on monitoring and reducing construction waste generation; however the adoption of material life cycle and circular economy are major considerations to promote sustainable built environment and efficient use of resources (Papers 1-3).

114613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
114613.value: This research attempted to provide extensive quantitative and qualitative data on the impact of government policies on the use of prefabrication and on construction waste reduction level in Hong Kong High-rise buildings. The study included two surveys, face-to-face interviews, a database and detailed case studies analysis. This provides original data and significant information for the building industry in Hong Kong and overseas, thus promoting awareness on construction waste reduction, prefabrication and life cycle thinking. Based on the research findings, the existing building regulations and incentives may not be sufficient alone to fully reduce construction waste mainly due to limited site area for waste sorting, limited recycling companies and the lack of life cycle thinking in the building industry. This study shows that the industry is raising the awareness on the monitoring and the reduction of construction waste generation; however the adoption of material life cycle and circular economy are major considerations to promote sustainable built environment and efficient use of resources. The adoption of zero waste building industry and material life cycle are highly recommended as the production of new building materials, construction activities, and the management and disposal of construction waste have significant impact on carbon emissions and climate change.

114713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
114713.value: We have witnessed the explosive growth of online social networks, such as Facebook, Twitter, Sina Weibo (micro-blog), and so on. Online social networks provide users with new platforms for social interaction, communication and information sharing and have become an important media for information dissemination. For example, governments use online social networks to announce new policies, companies to promote new products, and organizations or politicians to disseminate campaign messages. However, the understanding towards the information diffusion process in online social networks is still very limited due to the complexity the networks and the diversity of users. The objectives for this project are threefold: 1) Develop a deterministic mathematical model to characterize the information diffusion process in online social networks. This model should include both spatial and temporal dimensions that describe how information is diffused over time and social distance. 2) Design minimal cost information diffusion algorithms based on our proposed model. The research problem is to find a minimum set of source nodes to post a piece of information in the network such that at least a given percentage of users will eventually be influenced by the information. 3) Design time-sensitive information diffusion algorithms that disseminate real-time or time-sensitive information in online social networks. 社交網絡為用戶提供了新的社會互動、溝通和信息共享平台，並已成為一個重要的信息傳播媒體。然而，由於網絡的複雜性和用戶的多樣性，對在線社交網絡的信息擴散過程的理解還是很有限。本項目主要有以下三個目標：1）制定一個確定性的數學模型用來描述在線社交網絡的信息擴散過程； 2）基於我們提出的模型，設計最低成本的信息擴散算法。主要問題是找到一組最少的源節點來發佈一個信息塊，使得至少有一定量百分比的用戶會受到該信息的影響；3）設計時間敏感的信息傳播算法來傳播在線社交網絡中的實時信息或時間敏感信息。

114713.label: Realisation of objectives
114713.value: 1) Developed a model to measure impact in social media by using the dissemination model of flu and Ebola virus. The result was presented in IEEE Globecom 2015. 2) Developed a new routing scheme by using social network relations. The performance evaluation has shown the efficiency (in terms execution time) and low cost (in terms of network messages) of the proposed scheme. The result was presented in IEEE ICNC 2015. 3) Proposed a seamless virtual machine migration scheme for cloud data centers. This scheme provides a load-balanced computing platform for large scale social networks. The result was published in IEEE Trans on Parallel and Distributed Systems. 4) Investigated security issues for mobile devices and for the home devices. This study is essential for developing social network systems on mobile devices. We also studied the algorithms to maximize the capacity of multi-radio wireless networks.

114713.label: Major findings and research outcome
114713.value: 1) Given the scale and diversity of users in social networks, it's very difficult to analyse users' behaviors in social networks. We developed a suite of sampling methods that sample users' tweets in social networks to understand and predict the impact of social events. This work allows us to understand the characteristic of the social network by using limited amount of computing resources and efforts. 2) Many routing algorithms have been proposed for mobile ad hoc networks, but, little work has been done on utilizing social networks to improve the efficiency and reliability of mobile ad hoc networks. We proposed a new routing scheme (Social Relation Opportunistic Routing, SROR) that utilizes social relations of users to help deliver wireless messages. Experimental results have shown that the proposed SROR scheme can deliver messages in shorter delay and more reliably. 3) We discovered a new virtual machine (VM) migration scheme by using "named data networking" concept. That's, the communication among VM doesn't based on traditional IP addresses. Instead, it uses "names of the data". This method makes data access not relying on IP addresses, but on the names of accessed data, which makes data access location transparent and thus significantly simplified the procedures of VM migrations in large data centers. This scheme facilitates the efficient data processing and computing for large scale social networks.

115113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
115113.value: Increasing life expectancy and reduced mortality is leading to a significant increase in the aging population in Hong Kong, with a total of 941,300 elders living there in 2011. The proportion of elderly residents is projected to rise still further from 13.3% in 2011 to 26.5% in 2031. To tackle this problem of rapid aging, the HK government’s main policy platform is ‘aging in place’ (HKSAR 2011, 2012). However, only half of all elders benefit from the governmental policy through public and subsidized housing, with 46% still living in private domestic (PD) housing with diversified environment and facilities (Census Statistics Department 2009). As developers normally concentrate on producing affordable housing for adults to maximize profit, at present no purpose-designed PD units have been developed for elders. Indeed, inappropriate facilities and living environment reduce elders’ Quality of Life (QoL), leading to health and safety problems. The physical living environment is a recognized dimension of QoL (World Health Organization QoL Assessment [WHOQOL] Group 1998a), and is likely to be particularly important for domestic elders. Because of a decline in their health and mobility, elders spend most of their time at home and rely on facilities and facilities management (FM) for support with physical and biological problems, and to maintain psychological well-being. Although there is a Universal Design Guidebook for general residential development in HK (HKHS 2010a), there are no specific guidelines for designing and managing PD housing for elders based on an integrated FM study covering the construction, physical, social and psychological disciplines. There is an extensive literature on FM, caring environmental design, post-occupancy evaluation, building maintenance, and QoL for adults in general and elders in particular, but little research integrates all these aspects in the context of PD housing for elders. The purpose of this study is to enhance the QoL of elders in PD housing through FM. Its objectives are: (1) to factorize the FM components in PD housing and QoL indicators for elders; (2) to establish FM-QoL relationships for elders in PD housing; (3) to develop an integrated FM-QoL model; (4) to verify the model using longitudinal data; and (5) to propose FM guidelines for enhancing QoL for elders in PD housing. The findings will promote the development of a proactive assessment of FM in PD housing, and enhance the QoL of elders across society through their application to urban planning to create a more elderly-friendly community. 115113.label: Major findings and research outcome
115113.value: The results indicate that the following FM components are predictive of an elderly person’s QoL: space, colour, furniture and fixtures, lighting, temperature, ventilation, acoustics and doors and windows. Architecture The present study reveal that space (F1) significantly influences four out of the five domains of QoL: physical health, social relationships, living environment and the overall QoL of elderly residents of PD buildings. Weak muscles and joints influence the size of the required turning spaces within an elderly person’s flat. Small turning spaces – especially in a flat of irregular shape – cause inconvenience for an elderly resident when bathing, visiting the toilet and moving from one room to another within his/her home, particularly for an elderly person who needs to use a wheelchair. Colour (F3) is another important indoor FM component that significantly influences the psychological health of the elderly. Fixtures (F4) such as storage cabinets are normally designed to be of maximum height (from floor to ceiling) in order to increase the storage capacity, but this constitutes a problem for the elderly in their daily life as their reach is limited. Moreover, small spaces with limited room for furniture (F4; e.g., chairs for sitting on in the living room) discourage the elderly from inviting friends and neighbours to visit them and affects the opportunities for engaging in leisure activities within the home. Building services Three out of the five building services components significantly predict the QoL of the elderly respondents. As a result of a decrease in their sensitivity to light, the visual acuity of elderly people is reduced. To offset the impaired vision of the elderly and to create a pleasant living environment for them, good lighting (F5) is essential. Natural light supplemented by artificial light is the best choice for elderly people, as this creates a pleasurable home environment that induces positive feelings in the elderly. High-rise buildings are built close to each other, owing to the limited amount of space for residential developments in Hong Kong. Both natural and mechanical ventilation should be exploited to improve the overall health and QoL of the elderly residents. On the other hand, excessive temperatures (whether hot or cold) can significantly endanger the health of the elderly. The death rate of the elderly during the winter, in fact, increases due to cardiovascular and respiratory diseases resulting from temperature variations (Woodhouse 1992). Supporting facilities The results also show that acoustics (F10) influence an elderly resident’s overall QoL, physical health, psychological health and satisfaction with his/her living environment. Due to a building’s age and financial constraints on maintenance of the flats, water taps and door hinges, for example, may produce noises that constitute a nuisance to the elderly. This affects the satisfaction of elderly people with their physical home environment. In addition, a decline in the physical strength and energy of the elderly creates a difficulty for them in opening doors and windows (F13). Insufficiently wide doors with stiff handles and windows that are hard to open may lead to depression and negative feelings in elderly residents.

115113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
115113.value: The impact of indoor FM components on the QoL of the elderly might also be influenced by factors not considered in the present study. Such factors as the age of a PD building, an elderly resident’s income, the size of an individual flat and the health status of an elderly person might mediate the complicated relationships between the indoor FM components and the QoL of an elderly person. These factors should therefore be examined in subsequent studies in order to provide sustainable and affordable housing for the elderly. The elderly can be categorized into three groups: the able-bodied, those who need a walking aid (such as a walking frame) and wheelchair users. The space requirements and the appropriate size of storage cabinets differ for these different groups. For instance, the turning space required by an able-bodied elderly person is not the same as that required by an elderly person who uses a walking frame or a wheelchair. Similarly, the reachable height and depth of storage cabinets vary. Further studies could conduct a comprehensive investigation of specific indoor FM components – such as kitchen cabinets (fixed at different heights), wardrobes, bathrooms/toilets and so on – as they affect different groups of the elderly. The findings of the present study have practical implications concerning the FM components in PD buildings. However, a triangulation method using qualitative data (such as interviews and site measurements) for cross-validation with the quantitative data could lend more substantial support to the findings of the present study. Interviews give detailed insight into the respondents’ points of view, while site measurements supply accurate, objective information about current facilities. Together, these different types of data can enhance our understanding and may eventually lead to an enhancement of the QoL of elderly people within their living environments.

115113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
115113.value: The rate at which the population is ageing increases the magnitude of the challenge of providing private domestic buildings with facilities meeting those needs of the elderly occupants that arise from their changing health condition. This study aims to examine the relationships between indoor facilities management (FM) components and the quality of life (QoL) of elderly people residing in private domestic buildings. A questionnaire based on an extensive literature review was distributed among elderly respondents in order to assess their level of satisfaction with 13 indoor FM components and five QoL domains e namely overall QoL, physical health, psychological health, social relationships and their living environment. In all, 348 questionnaires were completed by elderly respondents drawn from the 18 political districts of Hong Kong; the data were analyzed using reliability tests, Pearson correlation and multiple regression analysis. The results reveal that (1) the respondents' overall QoL was significantly affected by ventilation and space; (2) their physical health was predicted by space, doors and windows, and temperature; (3) their psychological health was affected by furniture and fixtures, lighting, acoustics, and doors and windows; (4) their social relationships were influenced by furniture and fixtures and space; and (5) their level of satisfaction with the living environment was affected by space, lighting, furniture and fixtures and acoustics. It is recommended that architects, interior designers, building services engineers and facilities managers include adequate turning spaces in the design of flats for the elderly; and that they pay attention to the brightness and hue of lighting, consider the micro-climate in the orientation of new buildings, incorporate sound insulation materials in walls, install on doors and windows lever handles that require minimal force and increase the width of doors in flats for elderly residents.

115213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
115213.value: After the 2003 outbreak of severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), people in Hong Kong began paying more attention to the hygiene of toilets. Although we have known for some time about potential human exposure to flushing-associated water droplets in toilets, very little is known about the aerosolization and deposition of flushing-associated pathogens and their implications for public health, particularly in areas with poorly designed toilet systems or high frequency use public toilets, such as those in Hong Kong. Solid waste from individuals suffering intestinal or urinary colonization by pathogenic microorganisms may contain a huge number of bacteria or viruses. Washroom users can be infected by either primary exposure, through the inhalation of contaminated aerosols, or secondary exposure, through contact with contaminated surfaces. There has been very little systematic research on minimizing exposure risks. Preliminary results show that ultraviolet light of 254 nm wavelength (UV-C) has disinfection capabilities in indoor environments, although no study to date has considered on the role of toilets in possible spreading of infection. Given that the existing body of knowledge is far from complete relative to the potential importance of the topic, our proposed work aims to bridge the knowledge gaps in our understanding of pathogen exposure during toilet flushing and suitable mitigating measures. The focus will be on investigating the effects of such toilet system parameters as bowl design, flushing mechanisms, water flow rate, and water pressure, such physical parameters as feces consistency, and such environmental factors as the ventilation system on the emission of and exposure to contaminated aerosols. Another key aim is to examine the disinfection effectiveness of UV-C sources, i.e., upper-room ultraviolet germicidal irradiation (UVGI) and localized UV-C developed by the PI. Both experimental and numerical approaches will be adopted. A custom-built toilet system will be installed in a controlled chamber, and common intestinal pathogens will be tested. The emission factors for the modeled feces will be measured for the first time. Field measurements will be carried out in real toilets. Airborne and surface samples will be collected under various testing scenarios and controlled conditions. Based on the measured emission characteristics, a numerical tool will be developed to predict the transport of pathogens and disinfection effectiveness. The effectiveness of UV-C devices will also be tested in real toilets. The output of this work will be applicable in a wide range of contexts, including exposure risk control and the optimization of UV-C installations.

115213.label: Realisation of objectives
115213.value: 1. To measure the emission factors and study influential factors affecting the emission of contaminated aerosols during toilet flushing (i.e., different toilet systems, bowl designs, water pressures, water flow rates, artificial stool consistencies, and environmental conditions). To correlate between droplet concentration and emission factors. A tailor made set-up has been designed and fabricated in the PI’s lab. Pathogen emission factor has been measured. The results have been published in a respectful journal Indoor Air in 2017. Details conclusions can be referred to the publication which is also attached in this report. The salient conclusions are summarized below. A pilot study was carried out to measure the emission strength of airborne pathogens. It is the first study systematically quantifying airborne pathogens emission for toilet flushing. It investigated the two most popular flushing systems, flushometer and cistern systems, at two different water pressures (400 kPa and 200 kPa) and tank heights (95 cm and 46 cm) and tested three types of bacteria (Staphylococcus epidermidis, Escherichia coli and Pseudomonas alcaligenes) representing small-, medium- and large-sized pathogens. Flushing-generated airborne pathogen was evidenced. Emission strength was expressed in terms of number of airborne microorganisms per first flush. It was also noted that pathogen emission and bacterial size were negatively correlated. The emission strength of S. epidermidis was statistically greater than that of E. coli and P. alcaligenes in the high pressure (p = 0.002) and low pressure (p = 0.001) conditions, respectively. For all three bacteria, the emission strength under high pressure was statistically greater than that under low pressure: S. epidermidis (p < 0.001), E. coli (p < 0.05) and P. alcaligenes (p < 0.001). The strengths recorded under high pressure were almost double those recorded under low pressure. For E. coli tested in the high tank height and low tank height scenarios, the respective CFU results were very low. As similarly low or even lower CFU results were anticipated for P. alcaligenes, only the high pressure and low pressure scenarios were tested. Flushing-generated airborne pathogen was evidenced. Emission factor was expressed in terms of number of airborne microorganisms per first flush. It was also noted that pathogen emission and bacterial size were negatively correlated. Finally, in all flushing conditions the emission strength of S. epidermidis was greatest, followed by E. coli and then P. alcaligenes. This paper also highlights the need for greater concern over the transmission via toilet flushing of aerosols containing pathogenic organisms, which poses particular for the immunocompromised, children and the elderly. Finally, our findings also imply that a cistern tank design is preferable respect to pathogen generation. 2. To investigate the degree of contaminated aerosols generation and surface contamination inside a toilet. The temporal profiles of the different-sized droplets generated during toilet flushing were recorded using an optical particle counter. The results can be found in a paper published in Indoor Air (2017, attached in this report) and a manuscript submitted for Indoor Air (Dec, 2018). An important finding was up to 300,000 airborne particles were measured by flushing with flushometer while 15,000 for cistern tank. All these particle sizes ranged from 0.3 to 10 micrometer. The significant different could be attributed to the flushing mechanism. Atomization energy notably influenced droplet and bacterial emission. For surface contamination study, four 90 mm Petri dishes were placed around the toilet seat (referred to submission of Indoor Air, Dec 2017). They were all at the same level of the bowl surface. The results showed that the distribution of bacteria settled mainly at the rim of the toilet. 3. To measure the disinfection effectiveness of upper-room UVGI and localized UV-C under various conditions. A manuscript has been submitted to Indoor Air (Dec, 2017). This manuscript evaluated ultraviolet waveband C (UVC) disinfection efficacy of flushing-generated pathogen-laden aerosols by localized disinfection system at two different sites (surface and airborne). Three types of bacteria were chosen: S. epidermidis (ATCC #12228), E. Coli (ATCC #10536) and S. typhimurium (ATCC #53648). Two power rating of localized UVC systems were tested: 5W and 10W. Each with a UVC tube and a ballast housed in a water-resistant clear Perspex was made. Single-stage bioaerosol impactors (Thermo Scientific) were installed to collect airborne samples at heights of 130 cm, 90 cm, and 40 cm for the high (ASH), middle (ASM), and low (ASL) level air sample collections, respectively. The localized device was installed below the rim of the toilet bowl. Then three stages of experimental measurements were performed. At the first stage, the three types of bacteria were used to test the disinfection performance of the 5W localized UV-C lamp. At the second stage, 10W localized UV-C system was used. For the final stage, only E. coli was selected for testing the disinfection efficacy of UR-UVGI. For all three stages, air and surface samples were taken for analysis. Moreover, as ozone is a by-product of UV-C emission and a harmful pollutant, emission of this gas in a confined environment such as a toilet becomes a critical health concern.31 We therefore measured ozone concentrations with an ozone monitor (Model 205, 2B Technologies). Very high disinfection efficacies ranging from 76% to 97% for bacteria-laden aerosols at source of emission were observed, and 53% to 79% for surface samples by localized systems were observed. The localized system was further compared with an upper room ultraviolet germicidal irradiation (UVGI) for E.Coli. The localized UV system performed 5 times and 2 times as good as the UR-UVGI for airborne and surface samples respectively. 4. To develop a computational model to predict pathogen transmission from toilet flushing with and without UV-C disinfection devices. A computational geometry with the dimensions equal to the experimental set-up was formulated. There are three issues needed to be resolved; the boundary conditions of emission and air velocity. The emission factor and the air velocity measured by the experiments were used as boundary conditions. The final issue was the killing effect. In order to model disinfection, susceptibility of the bacteria under UVC must be obtained first. A journal paper has been published in Aerosol Science & Technology (see attached). Five bacteria were tested and the results were inputted to a computational model. The Renormalization Group (RNG) k-ε turbulence model was applied in present work. Enhanced wall function was applied for the near wall region, as the maximal y+ is less than 8.4 in the near wall region. The magnitude and direction of air velocity was set in inlet boundary, respectively. Zero diffusion flux condition was applied at outflow boundary. No-slip conditions were performed at all solid walls. The airborne concentration between the experiments and modeling results were compared and good matches were found. 5. To measure the transport of contaminated aerosols and effectiveness to reduce the contamination by using UV-C devices in real toilets. Samples were taken in two real residence’s toilets. A 5W localized system (details refer to manuscript submitted for Indoor Air, Dec 2017) was used for a week for each site. Airborne and surface samples were taken. Each day two air samples and 5 surface samples were collected in the evening. It was observed that the microorganism airborne concentration and surface density were significantly reduced.

115213.label: Major findings and research outcome
115213.value: Upon completion of this project, some salient findings are observed: Abundant droplets were generated during flushing toilet. Even a single flush, up to 300,000 numbers of droplets were emitted. Airborne pathogens was also evident. Experimental results showed that airborne pathogens were collected airborne. The numbers depended on a variety of factors such as tank height, water pressure and pathogen sizes. This study found emission strength and bacterial size to be negatively correlated, which is valuable information for estimating the risks associated with small viruses or large bacteria. UV C is very effective for disinfection microorganisms. Inferring from the this laboratory results, it was observed that localized UV performed much better than upper-room UVGI. Finally, it found a cistern tank design to be the preferred toilet flushing option because of its minimal generation of potentially infectious small aerosols. Research outcome. The results have been published in two archival journals. 1. Emission strength of airborne pathogens during toilet flushing. Indoor Air. Accepted 1 July, 2017, DOI: 10.1111/ina.12406. 2. Experimental and numerical study of the performance of upper-room ultraviolet germicidal irradiation with the effective Z-value of airborne bacteria. Aerosol Science and Technology. Vol 51, Issue 10, 1123-1134, 2017. The following manuscript has been submitted to the journal Indoor Air on early Dec, 2017. A Pilot Study on the Disinfection Efficacy of Localized UV on the Flushing-Generated Spread of Pathogens.

115213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
115213.value: The work is completed very successfully. We understand more fundamental issues which can help us to further develop a better disinfection device for toilet. The PI is conducting more experiments to test more bacteria to establish a larger database. It will help to develop a portable UVC device with sufficient UVC intensity for common pathogens found in toilet environments. The current UVC device is good but with the advancement of electronic technology, the device can be made significantly smaller. The localized system can be put forward for actual testing. The numerical tool developed can be further used to assess indoor air quality for real toilets.

115213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
115213.value: The public commonly regards toilets as “hot spots” of microorganisms. Aerosolized droplets are generated during the toilet flushing process, and the “splashing” of these droplets is a common occurrence in poorly designed toilets (those that are overpressurized or have an excess water flow). If a toilet user suffers from intestinal or urinary pathogenic microorganism colonization, the aerosolized droplets will be contaminated by these microorganisms. Washroom users can be infected by either primary exposure, through the inhalation of contaminated aerosols, or secondary exposure, through contact with contaminated surfaces. This study investigated pathogen emission through toilet flushing. A localized UV disinfection system was also proposed. The emission factor and disinfection efficacy were measured experimentally. Inferring from the results, airborne pathogen emission is evident and very high disinfection efficacy was observed for the localized disinfection system. Using the experimental results as boundary conditions, modeling results were matched well with the experimental results. The findings of this work provide valuable information to the general public. It significantly improves our fundamental understanding of infection risk in toilets and efficiency of UV-based disinfection devices.

115413.value: 大運量客運系統是民族經濟發展的基本組成部份，而有砟軌道是全世界最流行的大運量客運系統。研究人員已經在無損檢測和有砟軌道安全上做了大量的研究。目前檢測鐵路軌道的方法很全面。用於檢測鐵軌的水平，對齊，軌距和起皺的方法快速而又有效。然而，鐵路道砟損傷診斷仍嚴重依賴於目視檢查和有損中心抽樣檢驗。顯然，目視檢查對於檢測“表面”的損傷表現良好。而對於隱藏的損傷（如位於軌枕受力區域底下或者道床砟肩的道砟損傷），這些損傷會影響軌道的穩定性並且使軌道的工作性能惡化，要通過目視檢查檢測這些損傷，即使可能，也是及其困難的。當鐵路道砟有損傷，用來支撐軌枕的道砟的粒度和剛度會相應減小。這會改變鐵路-軌枕-道砟系統的動態特性。所以，通過測量系統的振動和求解識別位於軌枕底下道砟粒度分部的逆問題來診斷位於軌枕底下道砟的損傷是可能的。在這個方案投入使用之前，必須克服一些困難。第一，由於鐵路道砟的應力應變關係是非線性的，基於測量的固有頻率和振型的模型修正的方法不適用，必須研發基於時程控制非線性的模型修正的方法。第二，參照系統的基準測量數據難以獲得。第三，由於模型誤差以及測量噪聲導致逆問題的結果非常地不確定。擬建項目將克服這個困難，並且制定切實可行的基於錘擊測試沿著貝葉斯概率方向的道砟損傷診斷的方法。這個方法旨在給工程師以及檢查員在目視檢查中提供關於軌枕底下道砟的粒度分佈有價值的信息。

115413.label: Realisation of objectives
115413.value: All objectives were achieved. For Objective 1, a series of linear and nonlinear models for capturing the vibration characteristics of the rail-sleeper-ballast system was developed. In some of the classes of models, the reduction in ballast sizes is considered as the drop of ballast stiffness values (in this study, this is treated as railway ballast damage). For the nonlinear ballast models, time-domain model updating method is developed for the calculation of the reduction in ballast stiffness due to ballast damage utilizing a set of measured vibration data (e.g., from impact hammer test) of the in-situ sleeper. For Objective 2, the classes of models developed in Objective 1 are employed to detect the reduction in railway ballast size (i.e., railway ballast damage) utilizing measured vibration data following a time-domain approach. It must be pointed out that the time-domain method for railway ballast damage detection is very new. Most existing methods from the literature follow the modal-domain (i.e., making use of measured natural frequencies and mode shapes). Under the situation of large amplitude vibration, it was found that the mechanical stiffness of railway ballast is nonlinear. As a result, frequency and modal domain methods become very difficult if not impossible to be applied. The contribution of the research project in the development of time-domain methods for railway ballast damage is an important contribution to the railway industry. In this Objective, the Bayesian method was not employed. The model updating problem was solved by using probabilistic numerical optimization algorithm. The evolutionary algorithm is adopted to ensure the optimization process will be not easily trapped by local minimums. The basic idea is to divide the optimization process into different generations (iterations steps). At the first generation, points (models in the parameter space of interest) were randomly generated following a uniform distribution. The objective function value (i.e., the discrepancy between the measured and modeled responses) for each point was evaluated. In the next generation, the points will low objective function value will be discarded, and new points will be generated (following a given Gaussian distribution) using existing points with high objective function value. The points discarding and generating processes will be repeated until the stopping criterion was fulfilled (i.e., the improvement in objective function values in several generations are smaller than the pre-defined tolerance). For Objective 3, a tailor-made Bayesian model updating (utilizing Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) simulation) was developed for railway ballast damage detection. Owing to the high uncertainties associated with the mechanical properties of railway ballast, the corresponding model updating problems are usually unidentifiable in nature. In the proposed method, the MCMC simulation was employed for generating samples in the important regions of the parameter space for the approximation of the posterior probability density function (PDF) of ballast stiffness (and so as to identify the ballast sizes). For Objective 4, impact hammer tests were carried out in both the in-door test panel and field tests (with in-kind support from MTR). It must be pointed out that the field test data was employed only for model updating for identifying the railway ballast stiffness as it is not possible for the PI to artificially simulate damage onto existing railway tracks of MTR. Therefore, the measured data for the purpose of railway ballast damage relies on the in-door test panel, which is a segment of ballasted track with 8 sleepers under a well-controlled environment (the temperature and humidity can be controlled by the air-conditioning system). The series of impact hammer tests in the in-door test panel, artificial ballast damage can be simulated by replacing normal sized ballast particles at a given region (under the target sleeper) by small-sized ballast particles. The smaller the size of ballast particles, the larger will be the ballast damage extent.

115413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
115413.value: The Bayesian method in this research project was developed for railway ballast damage detection under large amplitude vibration (e.g., train induced vibration). It is possible to extend the idea for the model updating of the train-track vibration system. The identified train-track model may have many important applications. For example, it may be used for railway track damage detection based on measured vibration data on the train and/or the track; for vibration control of the train; for controlling train induced vibration on surrounding structures. With the findings in this project, the PI successfully obtain another GRF – Ballasted track safety monitoring under operational conditions by Bayesian model updating of the coupled train-track system (CityU 11242716).

115413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
115413.value: A mass transit system is an essential component of a region’s economic growth, and ballasted tracks are the most popular mass transit system worldwide. The current methods for monitoring railway tracks are comprehensive. Fast and efficient methods are available for inspecting railway level and alignment, rail gauges and corrugation. Clearly, visual inspection is good at detecting surface damage. Hidden defects (e.g., damaged ballast under a sleeper loading area and/or ballast shoulder), which can affect track stability and deteriorate riding quality, are extremely difficult if not impossible to detect through visual inspection. When railway ballast is damaged, its size and stiffness in supporting the sleeper are reduced. This alters the vibration characteristics of the rail-sleeper-ballast system. Therefore, it is possible to detect ballast damage under a sleeper by measuring the vibration of the system and solving the inverse problem for identifying the ballast size distribution under the sleeper. This research project developed a practical ballast damage detection method based on impact hammer tests following the Bayesian probabilistic approach. The method aims to provide valuable information on ballast size distribution under a sleeper to engineers and inspectors during their visual inspections.

115813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
115813.value: Characterization technology of human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs) has been under research extensively and advanced rapidly in the past decades. One motivation is due to its many important applications including tissue regeneration and cell-based therapies, which are highly dependent on self-renewal and potency such that tissue development and auto-arrangement in human body can be achieved via the differentiation to various cell lineages. It is widely believed that the formation of human skeletal tissues from hMSC differentiation can be regulated under precise control of microenvironment. The cell behaviors (including differentiation) under different microenvironments are yet highly undetermined. Since the last decade, researchers have discovered that human stem cells respond very sensitively to both the biochemical and mechanical factors. Therefore, a cell analysis system is essential to quantitatively characterize the stem cell behaviors in multiple combinations of microenvironments. However, requirement of the conventional continuous culture and analysis systems for large quantities of growth media, reagents, cell samples and manpower has pushed the move toward microfluidics – the miniaturization and chip-based automated control of fluidic operations. In this project, we propose to develop a universal high-throughput microfluidic platform containing multiple independent culture chambers to provide unprecedented control over various mechanical and biochemical conditions required to simulate the hMSC differentiation. In essence, this proposed platform is developed for long-term hMSC culture to support the cell differentiation and subsequent tissue formation with better medium handling, such as mixing, humidification and medium replenishment. This platform fabricated by multilayer elastomeric microchannels can dynamically adjust biochemical growth parameters such as medium composition, substrate protein deposition and dissolved oxygen level. To regulate the mechanical environment including substrate stiffness, we integrate each chamber in the platform with a micropost array, in which the substrate stiffness can be tuned by dimensions of the microposts. The external shear stimulus can be regulated by the medium flow rate. Further, we will also develop strategies to conduct different analysis techniques using optical microscopy in order to characterize the hMSC responses under different microenvironments, e.g. cell type, spatial distribution of intracellular molecules, and arrangement of differentiated cells. Together, this microfluidic platform with control of multiple microenvironmental factors functions not only as a very powerful, inexpensive tool to study the biochemical and mechanical effects to cell behaviors, physiology and differentiation of hMSCs, but also as a universal high-throughput stem cell characterization platform that has the potential to induce breakthrough in stem cell research. 人體間充質幹細胞（hMSC）的醫學應用及其表徵技術在過去的幾十年間發展迅速，而當中包含了組織再生和細胞相關的新療法。有賴於這種幹細胞的各種細胞譜系分化能力，受損的人體組織得以實現自我重生以及生理功能的恢復。科學研究發現人體幹細胞對於其周遭生化和物理環境的反應非常靈敏。有見及此，醫學者普遍認為細胞環境的精確調節可以控制hMSC的分化以形成人體骨骼組織。然而，在不同環境下幹細胞的反應（包括細胞譜系分化）還有待檢驗和量化。為達到細胞個體的系統定量表徵，細胞微環境的多種不同組合的高通量並行調控和分析是必須的。傳統細胞學所要求的大量培養基，試劑，細胞樣本和其涉及的人力資源已經變得難以滿足這種科技的高度需求。因此，微流體相應地得以迅速發展而邁向『微流體芯片的細胞培埴和分析操作自動化』。 在此科研議案，我們建議開發一種通用的高通量微流體芯片。高通量是指此芯片中包含多個獨立的培養腔，模擬hMSC生長和分化所需的各種物理和生化條件，提供了前所未有的可控度。從技術而言，這芯片是基於多層微通道的弹性体製程。從本質上講，這個平台達到更為優化的培養液處理以提供指定細胞譜系分化和緊隨的人體組織的形成過程。此芯片可以隨意調整生化生長要素，如培養基成分，底物蛋白沉積和溶解氧水平；同時此芯片更可調節細胞的物理環境，包括基板的剛度。我們將設定每一個芯片的培養腔中的基板微支柱陣列，其中微支柱的尺寸能夠調控基板的相應剛度；而培養液流速可激活細胞對於水流剪力的刺激。此外，我們更會應用當今細胞學的不同分析技術。光學顯微鏡可用作表徵不同的細胞環境下的反應，例如分化後的細胞類型，細胞內分子的分佈和排列的量化分析。總括而言，這個可同時控制多個微環境因素的高通量微流體平台不僅是一個功能強大且廉價的通用細胞研究工具，當中研究結果能導出的hMSC生理和分化反應與其生化和物理細胞環境的相互關係更有可能對於幹細胞研究的新突破作出貢獻。

115813.label: Realisation of objectives
115813.value: In this research, we have reported a high-throughput microfluidic device for on-chip cell culture and analysis applications. The device was capable of assessing cell morphology, colonization density and spatial arrangement of cells throughout cell growth. This device could obtain quantitative cellular characteristics in terms of shape, distribution of cell viability, and proportion of the key cell types. Furthermore, the scalable architecture of the multiplexed platform enabled the monitoring of multiple culture samples subjected to different environmental factors, reducing the extensive experimental efforts of the conventional laboratory settings. Having a microfluidic tool to study the complex and dynamic environmental conditions driving cell-layer/tissue formation, further characterization of cell population growth may deepen our understanding of the tissue development mechanisms. As the device can be also applied to general cell culture and analyses, this work opens the door for extended bio-applications, including screening mechanisms to guide the tissue formation through techniques such as small molecule promoters/inhibitors and surface chemistry modifications.

116013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
116013.value: Facing the urgent need of reducing the greenhouse gas emission and increasing the efficiency of electricity utilization, traditional power delivery network is unable to cope with the new requirement. Renewable energy resources like solar PV panels and wind turbines are being integrated into the power grid network. In addition, the installation of roof-top PV panels and small wind turbines becomes popular in residential households. These additional energy sources become distributed energy sources and they will inject energy into the power grid. For the existing power grid systems, almost all of them are designed to delivery electricity to consumers. However, the renewable energy sources cause the power flow in the grid no longer in one direction. The renewable energy resources connected to the power grid results in a more advanced and complex power grid – smart grid. For the traditional power grid system, the control is usually achieved through a dedicated communication system, typical one is the SCADA (Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition) framework. With smart grid, the control and co-ordination of various stakeholders creates a complicated scenario. New distributed energy sources can be introduced as required and they must communicate with the central control system in form of “Plug and Play” manner. All these new installations must communicate with the central control station such that their operation conditions and status can be monitored and analyzed so as to avoid disaster happening. The intermittent nature of renewable energy sources and changing power demand pattern has a profound impact on the smart grid. The success of the smart grid relies on an advanced communication infrastructure with support for security and real-time communication. To study the impact of communication latency to the operation of smart grid, a co-simulator incorporating the power system simulator and communication network simulator will be developed. This co-simulator allows user to vary the architecture of the communication network for studying the latency effects. The objectives of this project are as follow: 1. To develop a co-simulator that incorporates the power system and communication network for simulating the operation of the smart grid. 2. To incorporate the IEC 61850 and 61400 communication standard to the DER (distributed energy resource) for realistic operational analysis 3. To develop agents to cater for different types of event handling. 各國政府正致力於減低溫室氣體排放以及提升電能使用效率，按步加強整合太陽能，風力等分佈式可再生能源，逐漸減少使用化石燃料發電。與此同時，國外民居亦開始流行安裝獨立房頂式太陽能板和小型風力電機，以降低長遠的電力開支。 大量的分佈式能源使傳統的電力系統轉化爲一個更先進和複雜的系統 - 智能電網。這些分佈式能源將會以“即插即用”的方式隨時接入電網，並與控制中心取得聯系。新接入的能源點必須透過通訊網絡，向控制中心反饋其運作狀態及接收調配命令，以確保電網整體運作正常。 分佈式能源具有間歇性與供電量不確定性等特點，成為智能電網建設中的一大挑戰。成功的設計必然倚仗於可靠的網絡架構，為監控中心提供實時及安全的通訊環境。本計劃的目的在於建立一套整合通訊與電力系統的智能電網模擬軟件。為未來研究通訊延遲對智能電網的影響提供合適的工具平臺。 本項目目標包括： 1. 建立一套聯合模擬軟件，整合電力與通訊系統兩方面，對智能電網的運作進行模擬分析。 2. 在通訊模擬方面加入對國際電工協會對變電站自動化標準IEC-61850的支持。 3. 開發應用於處理不同智能電網事件的電腦代理人。

116013.label: Realisation of objectives
116013.value: Three objectives have been set for this research project. Objective 1 is to develop a co-simulator platform for smart grid with communication capability. A co-simulator has been successfully implemented. The co-simulator consist of a commercial power system simulator software package PSCAD, a commercial network simulator software package OPNET, and an open source multi-agent platform JADE. The three software package are written different computer languages and students have spent huge efforts to interface them together. This package allow system designers to enter the smart grid power network and various communication infrastructure to examine their operation stability and also allow to find out potential catastrophic event. It also allow system designers to design a smart grid with compromises on system scale and implementation cost. The co-simulator design is also in compliant to IEEE HLA standard for which allows various simulation software package running on different computer to achieve logical time synchronization. This feature is particular import for eliminating the inaccurate simulation results caused by the latency induced by the messages passing within various software packages. Since co-simulator engine is written JAVA language, we wish to design the simulator that can accept JAVA language program without modification required. We have implement the DecompositionJ simulation framework (DEterministic, COncurrent Multi-PrOcesssing SImulaTION for Java programs) which enables direction-execution simulation of target program using compiler-based source-to-source transformation and a purposely designed runtime library. The framework is compatible with any JVMs that comply with the Java speciﬁcations, and does not require modiﬁcations on the target program code. This DecompositionJ simulation framework has been compared with other simulation frameworks against benchmark suite and the results proved that DecompositionJ only slow down by 98.9%, whereas other simulation frameworks are with 100-1000 times slow down. This demonstrate our simulator is extremely efficient. Objective 2 to incorporate the IEC 61850 standard to the co-simulator. We have successfully integrated the IEC61850 GOOSE messaging framework to the co-simulator. Since the co-simulator is able to observe all the events and messages within the network communication, the performance of the protection scheme can be evaluated in detail by analyzing the event timing, level of trip current, and voltages at different location of the smart grid. By using the co-simulation, the smart grid can be easily optimized before field deployment, which largely enhances the reliability of the smart grid. The capability of using IEC61850 standard has been simulated based on a smart grid with generator and distributed energy resources. For a faults occurred in a network, all the substation and circuit break actions can be observed in detail. The service restoration sequence allow designer to refine the power network design in order to achieve utmost performance. Objective 3 is to develop agents to cater for different types of event handling. To warrant the reliable operation of smart grid, power supply restoration is extremely important in case of faults occurred in transmission network. Fault Location Agent, Isolation Agent, and Service Restoration Agent have been developed to assist the co-simulator to examine the detail actions for power supply restoration. All agents are developed in JAVA and under JADE platform. All these program are them imported to DecompositionJ for incorporating into the co-simulator. Again all the events can be observed through the inter-communication messages among various software packages. We have also study the effects of integrating electric vehicles (EVs) to the smart grid. Since EV batteries can be considered as an energy resource, simulation results has demonstrated that it help to shorten the time to recover the voltage level when performing restoration. When EV perform charging (G2V – grid to vehicle), it draws power from the grid and this may cause a huge demand and the power network may be able to support. Intelligent algorithms has been developed to schedule the EV charging process in an orderly manner, with different price strategies. Simulation results demonstrate that the load profile can be smoothed to eliminate exceeding large demand. On the other hand, the EV owners can also “sell” energy to the operator when the load demand is high. However, the operator must devise an attractive price to encourage EV owners to participate in the selling. Algorithm has been designed to cater for this “buying” and “selling” with a win-win scenario.

116013.label: Major findings and research outcome
116013.value: Since different simulator is running according to its own timeline, this can cause unpredictable results in smart grid since the event handling can be all wrong if common timestamp is missing. Therefore time synchronization has been solved by introducing the IEEE HLA standard to the co-simulator design (Conference paper 1). It has been discover that the delays can actually cause wrong event execution sequence and hence produce different results. This finding is included in the manuscript (1) for publication referred journal. Simulation software run time is usually very long. The DecompositionJ direct simulation frame has been implement to execute the co-simulator and the run time overhead is only 98.9% for the benchmark suite test, while others are 100 to 1000 times slow. This finding is included in the manuscript (2) for publication referred journal. With the large number of electric vehicles (EVs) connected to the power network, their batteries are consider to be energy sources. Simulation has demonstrated that these battery power help to restore power in a shorter time when fault occurs, and different communication channel pose different delay time (see conference paper 5). This is important information for designer to refine the communication infrastructure. The IEC 671850 standard is mainly for protection concern and has been integrated into the co-simulator. In conference paper (4), it demonstrates that the protection action sequence against fault can be traced in detail. This allow designer to simulate different kinds of faults for examining the robustness of the network. With large number EVs connected to the power network, the power network must be able to adapt its operation to avoid EV charging power beyond the generation and this require intelligent algorithms to coordinate the charging operation. On the other hand EV owners are encourage to “sell” electric to operators during high demand. Algorithms have been developed to help both operators and EV owners to contribute to stable smart grid operation with win-win scenario (see journal papers 1 and 2). 116013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
116013.value: We will continue to implement more details on IEC61850 standard to cater for a more detail study on smart grid protection issues.

116013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
116013.value: Smart grid is now being implemented in many developed countries in order to using green energy, for examples solar and wind energies, to reduce the pollution caused by fossil fuel (oil and coal). When more households install solar panel and wind turbines to generate electricity and connect to power grid, this can cause power supply fluctuation and hence becomes instable, and may eventually leads to power outage. The smart grid infrastructure include power planets, transmission systems, substation, distributed energy resources and communication network. The reliable operation of smart grid is largely relied on the communication among various components. However, the huge traffic in public network can cause delay in information exchange. Since various components will act independently according to the information received, if the delay is too long these components may not respond exactly according to event handling sequence and eventually the entire system may not be able to restore to its desirable topology. This co-simulator is to facilitate the designer to examine the smart grid topology before deployment. The advantages are (i) to ensure the design is able to deliver stable power supply to public, and (ii) also to avoid potential catastrophic events happened when faults occur.
