116113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
116113.value: 當今，半導體製造工業佔據著全球高科技工業的重要地位，也是最大的組成部份之一，其市場規模超過2500億美金。其中，基於矽的微電子產品佔據著主導地位。作為最廣泛應用的半導體材料，人們對矽的電子性能和光電性能已開展了大量深入的研究。但同時，矽也是一種優異的機械材料。一個典型應用便是基於矽的集成時鐘芯片。具體來說，即是將微電子器件與精確振動在特定頻率的高性能機械部件（矽諧振器）結合起來產生時鐘信號的一種器件。 儘管如今，基於矽諧振器的產品已經開始進入市場，但其潛力還未遠充分開發。通常，這種諧振器是通過狹小的間隔產生的靜電力來驅動。間隔越窄，機械能和電能的耦合越緊密，驅動的效率就越高。可是，考慮在大規模加工狹小間隔的實際工藝限制，這種驅動方式效率不高。因此，爲了實現可靠并可重複進行的大規模生產，我們需要研究高效驅動矽諧振器的替代方案。矽諧振器所面臨的另一個挑戰是如何降低器件的溫度敏感性。相較而言，矽的機械性質的溫度敏感性要大大高於石英。 本研究提議針對上述的這些挑戰，在同一矽諧振器工藝平臺上提出整體解決方案。本項目將採用嵌入在諧振器中的耗盡層（常見於矽半導體器件中）來作為高效換能器。這種換能器不僅用於驅動器件產生振動，同時將振動機械能轉換為可檢測到的電訊號并輸出。耗盡層在半導體器件中極為常見，其電氣特性早已被人們所熟知并寫入了教科書。相比之下，人們對於耗盡層作為產生力的驅動器以及將振動轉換為電流的轉換器之瞭解還較為粗淺。簡言之，耗盡層產生了一層電介質，其厚度相較于可以實際加工的空氣間隔要窄得多。因此，提供了更高的機電轉換效率。同時，耗盡層的產生將改變半導體的本身性質，從而改變器件的溫度敏感特性。 我們的首要目標是開發一套加工工藝將耗盡層嵌入矽諧振器中，并通過合理設計，使其能夠驅動器件諧振在聲波橫向傳播模態（輪廓模態），同時測量出振動訊號。接下來，我們將構建可靠模型來增進對於耗盡層作為機電換能器性能的認識。基於這些成果，我們將研製高階輪廓模態諧振器，使其諧振頻率能夠達至特高頻頻段（UHF）。 基於初期的理論計算，仿真模擬，以及我們對矽諧振器設計經驗，我們有信心實現上述的研究目標。本研究對於科學和技術方面的重要性，將有助於推動矽諧振器研究的突破。

116113.label: Realisation of objectives
116113.value: Objective 1: We have been able to fabricate PN diodes embedded in the device layer of an SOI wafer. The device layer is patterned to form a 3D structure and released by HF etching. We showed through experiments that the PN diodes after the release step retain their rectification functions. Objective 2: We have developed models to describe the transduction mechanism of the PN diodes embedded within the device layer based on the proposed topology whereby the PN diode is on the surface of the silicon device layer. We have also developed models to relate the effect of doping (involved in the creation of PN diodes) on the temperature dependence of frequency. Objective 3: We have demonstrated higher order contour mode resonators using AlN-on-Si around 300 MHz with an impedance less then 50 ohms. AlN-on-Si was chosen as an alternative to the piezojunction effect in PN diodes for such high frequencies due to the weak transduction and particularly high feedthrough at high frequencies.

116113.label: Major findings and research outcome
116113.value: We have found in the course of developing the fabrication process side effects that have not been covered in the literature such as etching of regions that been ion implanted. This appears to have had an effect on the efficiency of transduction. We have been able to demonstrate that the PN junctions retain their rectifying function at the end of the fabrication process. Passivation of the junctions was not possible to be adopted in the process as the passivation layer (typically oxide) would be etched away in the release step. This results in rather large leakage. From discussions with the few in the world who have attempted this very challenge of applying the piezojunction effect in resonators, feedthrough emerges as a practical challenge for high frequencies and it is difficult to accurately distinguish the piezo-junction effect from the piezo-resistive effect in characterizing resonators.

116113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
116113.value: To reach the high frequencies proposed in this project, we have used AlN-on-Si which has been shown to be highly promising whereby both low impedance and high quality factor can be achieved particularly as we scale up the frequency. The process has become more mature, allowable greater reliability of samples fabricated for testing towards validating novel structures.

116113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
116113.value: PN diodes are well-known for their use in semiconductor devices. In contrast, their application to micromechanical devices has hardly been explored. This includes their processing in line or compatible with existing semiconductor process technology. This project attempts to fill this knowledge gap by developing the underlying process, testing the functionality of the relevant structures as well as the limitations and challenges involved.

116413.value: The overarching goal of the proposed project is to investigate the relationships between ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB), ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA) and nitrite-oxidizing bacteria (NOB) in a freshwater biofilter that oxidizes ammonia to nitrate through both culture-dependent and culture-independent genomic analyses. We tested the response of the nitrifying community at relatively low ammonia and nitrite concentrations (0.2 to 1.5 mM) that are typically encountered in a small-scale aquarium setting. Interestingly, we noted that the half-saturation constant (Ks for NH4+), maximum growth rate (μmax), and lag duration were different when both AOB and NOB were together compared to when each guild was present alone. This suggests that the synergistic relationships between the two guilds influence the physiological responses. Metagenomic sequencing enabled the successful recovery of two nitrifier genomes, including the first draft genome of Nitrobacter vulgaris. Overall, we have obtained a detailed mechanistic understanding of the synergistic interactions between AOB and NOB in freshwater biofilter systems and the objectives of the project have been achieved. Through this project, a doctoral student has been trained and a number of undergraduate students have joined the research group to gain research experience.

116413.label: Major findings and research outcome
116413.value: The results from this project have been published (Section C). The concept that nitrogen in wastewater can be a resource was reviewed in the manuscript of Sales and Lee (2015). The review highlights the fact that the nitrogen and carbon in wastewater should not be treated as waste but as useful resources and microbial processes have important roles to play in the waste-to-resource paradigm shift. The manuscript of Cai et al. (2017) contains the main results of this study. A culture-dependent enrichment approach was adopted in this study. The nitrifying community was obtained from a biofilter in a freshwater aquarium that typically received a relatively low concentration of ammonium. Initially, ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB), ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA) and nitrite-oxidizing bacteria (NOB) were present. After 15 months of enrichment in defined medium with 500 μM of ammonium (over 60 transfers, 1:10 dilution), AOA was unintentionally eliminated gradually, likely due to the ammonium concentration applied, and only AOB and NOB were left in the community. This was confirmed by both 16S rRNA gene sequencing and metagenomic sequencing. Another enrichment was developed where NOB were eliminated by the addition of chlorate. This enrichment was designed to study the physiological response of AOB when NOB were absent. The physiological responses of the enrichment cultures with AOB and NOB fed ammonium or nitrite and the cultures with AOB but without NOB fed ammonium were tested. The range of ammonium and nitrite concentrations (50 to 1,500 μM) tested was designed to be relatively low. We found that the growth rate (μmax), half-saturation constant (Ks for NH4+), and lag time showed a strong dependence on the synergistic relationships between the two guilds. When AOB and NOB were together μmax was higher, Ks was lower and the lag time prior to the commencement of nitrification was shorter. The growth of the AOB and NOB in each culture was assessed with quantitative PCR (qPCR) and we noted there was a decoupling between the growth of AOB and nitrification activities. The growth rates of AOB and NOB were elevated with a higher bicarbonate concentration as the carbon source. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing and 16S rRNA gene sequencing were applied to query the genomic content and metabolism of the nitrifiers and the community structure of the community. Through genome reconstruction, Nitrosomonas-like AOB and Nitrobacter-like NOB were identified in the cultures. One of the draft genomes was Nitrobacter vulgaris, whose genome has not been reported previously and was reported for the first time in this study. Interestingly, Nitrobacter-like NOB are typically found in environments with a high nitrogen content such as wastewater, and not found in a relatively low nitrogen environment such as aquaria. Hence, the Nitrobacter-like NOB found in the enrichment likely have a high growth rate and short generation time to enable it to be competitive in an oligotrophic environment. Genome comparison with other nitrifiers was conducted and a complete set of genes in the metabolic pathways of carbon fixation, citric acid cycle, and acetate metabolism were found, similar to other genomes in the same genus. Overall, the significance of the results in this study is that they demonstrate the importance of synergistic interactions between AOB and NOB to enhance nitrification and metagenomic sequencing can identify the key functional players in a microbial community.

116413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
116413.value: Nitrogen compounds such as ammonia, nitrate and nitrous oxide are environmental pollutants of concerns as they can degrade soil, water and air quality. In an enclosed aquatic environment, ammonia is toxic to aquatic life and hence, it must be oxidized to nitrite and subsequently to nitrate as part of the nitrification process via bacteria. One form of the nitrification reaction involves two separate guilds of bacteria, ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB) and nitrite-oxidizing bacteria (NOB), working together to convert ammonia to nitrate. In this study, we studied the interactions between AOB and NOB to convert ammonia to nitrate in a freshwater biofilter at a relative low ammonium concentration. We determined that when AOB and NOB were together, the physiological responses of ammonia conversion to nitrate were much improved compared to when each one of them was present separately. This indicates that their synergistic partnership is vital for the nitrification process. We further determined the genomic content and metabolism of the nitrifiers via high-throughput sequencing, and the draft genome of Nitrobacter vulgaris was obtained for the first time. Overall, we have developed an in-depth understanding of the synergistic interactions between AOB and NOB and the results obtained would be useful to engineers for manipulating the microbial community present in biofilters to enhance the effectiveness of nitrification.

116613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
116613.value: With a land mass of 1,104 km2 and a population of seven million people, Hong Kong is one of the most densely populated areas in the world. Any fire occurring in this city may incur severe consequences, including substantial property losses and fatalities. After each fire is extinguished, a fire investigator must establish the cause of the fire. In this exercise, determining the origin and strength of the fire is extremely important as it can help the fire investigator to establish whether the fire was due to an accident or arson. The identified cause of the fire may also trigger the implementation of additional preventive measures in the building or even the upgrading of statutory requirements. Traditionally, a fire investigator carries out the task according to his/her professional experience rather than a holistic scientific approach. In this study, we propose to develop an intelligent approach that will facilitate the investigation of fires. The engulfing fire and smoke spewing out from the fire compartment reveal the burning of a variety of fire sources, such as synthetic materials, that are commonly found in domestic dwellings. In most cases, these materials do not burn cleanly and thus generate large amounts of soot. The amount of soot in the smoke can be significant. Some of these soot-rich gases congregate and are deposited on the walls of the compartment, leaving a blackened pattern on the walls after the fire has been extinguished. This soot deposition pattern is unique to each fire scenario, thus acting like a fire ‘fingerprint’ that can be used to reconstruct the origin and strength of the fire. It is theoretically possible to use computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to reconstruct a similar soot deposition pattern by trying different combinations of fire strengths and locations. However, relying solely on CFD to determine the fire strength and origin is not considered practical, as each simulation requires extensive computational resources. We propose an alternative approach to identifying the fire origin and strength. First, a knowledge base will be established by collecting fire data from fire experiments, fire accident records and CFD simulations. Second, an intelligent model will be developed and trained to simulate the highly nonlinear behaviour between the soot deposition pattern and the fire origin and strength. This intelligent system will be an efficient tool to assist fire investigators in estimating the origin and strength of fires in field investigations. 香港陸地面積為1,104平方公里，人口達700萬人，也是世界上人口最稠密的地區之一。在這個城市發生任何火災都可能會產生嚴重的後果，包括重大的財產損失及傷亡。每場火災被撲滅後，火災調查員必須評估火災的起因。在這評估中，確定火源的位置及強度是非常重要的，因為它可以幫助火災調查員確定火災是否是出於意外或縱火。確定起火原因，也可能會在預防措施方面提新建議，把該建築物的法定防火要求進一歩升級。傳統上，火災調查員執行任務是根據他/她的專業經驗，而不是一個全面的科學方法。在這項研究中，我們提出制定一個智能的方法，它將有利於火災的調查。在火災中，火舌及濃煙噴湧過程可以揭示火源及合成材料的背景資料。在大多數情況下，這些材料在不完整地燃燒，從而產生大量的煙塵。在煙霧中的煙塵量是可以非常顯著的。這些氣體帯着豐富的煙灰將聚集並沉積在起火室的牆壁上，火災被撲滅後牆壁上留有燻黒的圖案。這煙灰燻黒的圖案模式是獨特的，每個火災場景，就像指紋一様，可以用於重建火源的位置及強度。使用計算流體動力學(CFD)，通過嘗試不同的火勢強度和位置的組合，重構類似的煙灰沉積圖案，這在理論上是可能的。然而，僅僅依靠CFD確定火災的強度和來源不太實際的，每次電腦模擬需要大量的計算量。在此我們提出了一個替代的方法來確定火源和力量。首先，利用已往火災實驗數據、火災事故記錄和CFD模擬火災數據收集建立知識庫。其次，開發和訓練智能模型，以模擬煙塵沉積模式和火源信息之間的高度非線性行為。這種智能系統將是一個有效的工具，以協助火災調查人員在火災現場調查評估火源位置及強度。

116613.label: Realisation of objectives
116613.value: Objective 1 - The theoretical soot-deposition model developed by Talbot et al. has been implemented in the Fire Dynamic Simulator (FDS) which is a CFD freeware developed by NIST and widely adopted in different fire engineering studies in the world. Numerical simulations were carried out to simulate the fire and smoke development and also the soot deposition on walls. The mass of soot per unit area of the wall is used to represent the quantity of soot deposited on the walls. Objective 2 - CFD simulation with different room sizes and fire heat release rates were performed to generate data for training of the artificial neural network (ANN). The simulation results showed that the soot deposition on wall did not clearly indicate the soot boundary demarcating the upper hot gas layer and the lower cold air layer. We adopted a statistical approach to determine the soot boundary between the hot gas layer and the cold air layer based on the soot pattern deposited on walls. Since the soot boundaries are usually simple and smooth in nature, we used quadratic equation to fit the soot boundaries on walls. The parameters of the quadratic equations were used as the inputs of the artificial neural network model while the output of the model is the fire location. Objective 3 - Typical Multilayered Perceptron (MLP) model was adopted for correlating the soot boundaries on walls and the location of the fire inside a compartment. Single hidden layer was adopted in the MLP model. The number of hidden neurons of the hidden layer was determined by rule-of-thumb and verified by sensitivity study. Leave-one-out approach was adopted to evaluate the performance of the trained MLP model. It was found that the error in fire location prediction is within 0.8m with 95% confidence. Objective 4: We collected data from a simple experiment. The trained MLP model was applied to the experimental data. The reconstruction of the fire bed location was considered reasonably.

116613.label: Major findings and research outcome
116613.value: From this research project, we found that the soot deposited on walls may not provide a clear soot boundary demarcating the upper hot gas layer and lower cold air layer. In practice, a statistical approach should be adopted on the soot pattern deposited on walls to estimate the soot boundary which is in fact quite smooth in nature. Therefore, quadratic equation can be used to fit the soot boundaries to provide sufficient features for correlating with the fire bed location. Artificial neural network, due to its capability in solving complex problem, is adopted to simulate the highly nonlinear correlation between the parameters of the quadratic soot boundaries and the fire location. It has been proven to be feasible to reconstruct the fire location from the soot patterns deposited on wall by using artificial neural network.

116613.value: This research can be further extended to train the artificial neural model with data collected from different geometries and different fire strength of the fire compartments to increase the applicability of the model.

116613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
116613.value: After extinguishing a compartment fire, one of the major task of fire investigation is determining the location of fire. Previously, the investigations were subjectively conducted by experienced investigators according to their professional knowledge and experiences. This research propose a scientific way to reconstruct the fire location according to the soot patterns deposited on the walls of the fire compartment. We used computer simulations to create different soot patterns on walls in different room sizes and fire strengths. The soot patterns were used to train an intelligent model to learn the correlation between the soot patterns and the fire locations. The trained artificial intelligent model can then be used in fire investigation to estimate the fire location according to the soot patterns deposited on walls after fire extinguishment. It can provide an objectively judgement to the fire investigators for their references in their fire investigation works.

117213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
117213.value: For a wireless communication system, the antenna is a very important part because it directly affects the signal transmission and reception. Recently, the dielectric resonator (DR) antenna (DRA) has been studied extensively due to a number of advantages including its low loss, small size, low cost, and ease of excitation. The complementary antenna is an important topic. It consists of electric and magnetic currents from which useful and interesting radiation patterns can be obtained. A number of complementary antennas have been realized using the slot and dipole antennas, but all of them are bulky in the structure and/or complicated in the feed. In this project, a novel DRA design concept that involves both electric and magnetic currents is proposed for the first time. The electric and magnetic currents are obtained from the small ground plane and the DR resonant mode, respectively. This new kind of DRA, named as complementary DRA, is very compact in size with a very simple feed. In this project, the complementary DRA will be used to design quasi-isotropic and unidirectional antennas (quasi-isotropic antennas are considered because it is very difficult, if not impossible, to obtain a truly isotropic antenna). The quasi-isotropic antenna is useful in some applications such as radio-frequency identification (RFID) systems because it has good coverage of signal at different angles. For DRAs, however, only broadside and omnidirectional radiation modes have been investigated and no quasi-isotropic radiation pattern has been generated thus far. In this project, compact quasi-isotropic antennas are designed using complementary DRAs. Wideband versions will also be provided for wideband wireless systems. Two kinds of unidirectional antennas will be designed using complementary DRAs, namely the lateral and boresight unidirectional DRAs. The design technique of the former will be applied to the dualfunction glass-swan DRA which simultaneously serves as an indoor decoration and the antenna of a wireless router. For the boresight case, the design technique will be used to suppress backward radiation of a broadside-mode DRA. This is very useful especially when a small ground plane is needed for a compact design. Wideband designs will also be provided for both kinds of unidirectional DRAs. In addition, circularly polarized boresight unidirectional DRAs will be covered for different needs. For each antenna, simulations will be done using ANSYS HFSS and verified with measurements. Also, a guideline will be given to facilitate the design. 在無線通信系統中，天線是一個非常重要的組成部分，這是因爲它能夠直接影響信號的傳輸和接收。最近，介質諧振器天線由于其損耗低，體積小，成本低，易于激勵等衆多優勢，已被廣泛研究。 互補天線在天線研究領域是一個重要課題。它的基本原理是通過天線電場和磁場電流之間的互補，使其獲得實用有趣的輻射方向圖。一些互補天線通過縫隙和偶極子天線相結合的方式已被實現。然而，這些天線體積較大且/或饋電方式複雜。在這個項目中，我們首次提出一種牽涉電場和磁場電流的介質諧振器天線設計概念，其電場和磁場電流分別從天線地板和介質諧振模式當中獲得。這種新型的介質諧振器天線，我們命名爲互補介質諧振器天線，它具有結構緊湊且饋電簡單的特點。在這個項目中，互補介質諧振器天線將被用來設計准各向同性和單向天線（這裏考慮准各向同性天線是因爲實現真正的各向同性天線非常困難）。 准各向同性天線能夠很好地覆蓋不同角度的信號，這個特點使其可以應用在某些通信系統，如射頻識別系統。然而，迄今爲止，對于介質諧振器天線的研究只局限于寬邊和全向輻射模式，其准各向同性輻射模式並沒有被調查過。在這個項目中，互補介質諧振器天線將用來設計緊湊的准各向同性天線。寬帶的准各向同性天線也將被研究，以滿足寬帶無線系統的需求。 我們將利用互補介質諧振器天線來設計兩種單向天線，即橫向天線和軸向天線。前者的設計技術將被應用在玻璃天鵝介質諧振器天線之中。所述玻璃天鵝介質諧振器天線具有雙重功能，既可作爲室內裝飾物，同時可以作爲無線路由器的天線。對于軸向天線，我們將重點研究如何抑制介質諧振器天線寬邊模式的後向輻射。這個研究是極具意義的，尤其對于一個緊湊的天線設計而言，其通常需要一個小地板，而使用小地板往往會引起較大的後向輻射。在這個項目中，寬帶的橫向和軸向介質諧振器天線也將被研究。除此之外，研究範圍將覆蓋圓極化的單向介質諧振器天線，以滿足各種實際需要。 我們將利用ANSYS HFSS對上述天線進行仿真，並且通過實驗以驗證仿真結果的准確性。此外，我們將提供設計准則以方便天線的設計。

117213.label: Realisation of objectives
117213.value: Objective 1 Investigation of quasi-isotropic dielectric resonator antennas (DRAs) The quasi-isotropic DRA has been investigated successfully. In this design, a small ground plane is utilized to obtain an electric dipole, which combines with the equivalent magnetic dipole of the broadside TE111 mode of the DRA to generate quasi-isotropic fields. The antenna can be matched easily by tuning the excitation probe. Its results have been summarized in the first paper of Part C. Objective 2 Investigation of lateral unidirectional DRAs A compact unidirectional ring DRA with lateral radiation patterns has been studied successfully. Its unidirectional patterns have been obtained by combining an equivalent horizontal magnetic dipole of the DR HEM11δ+1 mode with a vertical electric dipole located at the center of the DR. A demonstration has been given by designing a 2.4-GHz prototype, with reasonable agreement between the measured and simulated results. The results of this part have been summarized in the second paper of Part C. A second lateral unidirectional DRA with a very small ground plane has also been investigated successfully. In this case, the small ground plane simultaneously works as an excitation patch that excites the fundamental TE111 mode of the DRA to obtain an equivalent magnetic dipole. By combining this equivalent magnetic dipole with the electric dipole of the probe, a lateral radiation pattern can be obtained. The results have been summarized in the fourth paper of Part C. The first and second lateral unidirectional DRAs are linearly polarized (LP) designs. A circularly polarized (CP) lateral unidirectional DRA has also been investigated successfully. It requires two sets of CP far fields that have complementary patterns. The first set was obtained using the DR TM01δ and TE01δ+1 modes. For the second set, the CP DR-loaded slot antenna is used, which is realized by cutting a cross slot in the ground plane. A prototype was fabricated and tested at 2.4 GHz, and the measured results agree reasonably well with the simulated results. The results have been given in the fifth paper of Part C. Objective 3 Design of lateral unidirectional glass-swan DRA using the result of (2) An attempt was made to design a lateral unidirectional glass-swan DRA. The unidirectional design requires an equivalent magnetic dipole and an equivalent electric dipole. The equivalent magnetic dipole has been obtained by centrally exciting the glass-swan DRA with a slot, but it failed to obtain a good omnidirectional pattern of an electric dipole due to the asymmetry of the swan structure. It was tried to tune the length and position of the feeding probe but the radiation pattern is still not omnidirectional. We are still solving the problem. As a result, this part has not been completed. Objective 4 Investigation of boresight unidirectional DRAs Both LP and CP unidirectional DRAs with compact ground planes have been investigated successfully. Both designs make use of the broadside DR HEM11δ mode to obtain the required equivalent magnetic dipoles. The required electric dipoles are provided by the currents on the small ground planes. To demonstrate the idea, both LP and CP unidirectional DRAs operating at 2.4 GHz were designed, fabricated, and tested. Reasonable agreement between the measured and simulated results has been obtained. The results have been summarized in the third paper of Part C.

117213.label: Major findings and research outcome
117213.value: (a) Quasi-isotropic DRA A parametric study of the quasi-isotropic DRA was done to examine the effects of the various design parameters. Also, it has been found that the difference between the maximum and minimum field strengths of the quasi-isotropic radiation pattern is 5.6 dB. The difference can be reduced to 3.4 dB by using a narrower ground plane and higher dielectric constant. It can be very close to the theoretical limit of 3 dB. The results of this part have been summarized in the first paper of Part C. (b) Lateral unidirectional DRAs (i) Compact unidirectional ring DRA with lateral radiation patterns A prototype of the unidirectional ring DRA has been designed at 2.4 GHz. Our design has a measured 10-dB impedance bandwidth of 12.1%, 15-dB front-to-back-ratio (FTBR) bandwidth of ~4.0%, maximum realized gain of 3.88 dBi, and maximum antenna efficiency of 93.69%. A wideband version has been designed in 3.5-GHz WiMax band using the higher-order HEM11δ+2 mode of the DRA. A prototype was fabricated and measured, and the measurement agrees reasonably with the simulation. As compared with the original design, the wideband version has much wider measured impedance and FTBR bandwidths of 43.6% and ~14%, respectively. The results have been summarized in the second paper of Part C. (ii) Unidirectional DRA with a very small ground plane A prototype of this unidirectional DRA for 3.5-GHz LTE applications has designed and measured. It has been found that the unilateral DRA has an FTBR ratio of over 15 dB across the entire LTE band. It has also been found that by tuning the probe length, good match with a front-to-back ratio of higher than 15 dB can be easily obtained over frequency range of 3.25-3.89 GHz. The results have been shown in the fourth paper of Part C. (iii) CP lateral unidirectional DRA A prototype of the CP unidirectional DRA was designed, fabricated, and tested in 2.4-GHz WLAN band. Its measured results agree reasonably well with the simulations. It has been found that the measured 3-dB AR passband (4.9% bandwidth) entirely falls within the measured 10-dB impedance passband (9.43% bandwidth). Also, the maximum measured antenna gain and efficiency of the antenna are 2.58 dBic and 89.2%, respectively. It has been found that the measured FTBR is at least 13.9 dB across the 2.4-GHz WLAN band. The results have been presented in the fifth paper of Part C. (c) Design of lateral unidirectional glass-swan DRA This part has not been completed because it fails to obtain the omnidirectional radiation pattern due to the asymmetric structure of the swan. The finding is that the unidirectional pattern is highly sensitive to the omnidirectional field of the required electric dipole. (d) Boresight unidirectional DRAs A prototype of the LP boresight unidirectional DRA has been fabricated and measured. It has been found that the measured impedance and FTBR bandwidths are 14.5% and 10.1%, respectively, giving a usable frequency band of 10.1% (2.30–2.55 GHz). It has also been found that the measured FTBR, maximum gain, and maximum antenna efficiency are 33 dB (at 2.43GHz), 5.09 dBi, and 93.6%, respectively. A prototype of the CP design has also been fabricated and measured. It has been found that the measured overlapping bandwidth of the impedance, axial ratio, and FTBR is 6.1% (2.4-2.55 GHz). Across the overlapping bandwidth, the measured maximum gain and efficiency are given by 4.28 dBic and 94.4%, respectively.

117213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
117213.value: In this project, only single-band unidirectional DRAs have been investigated. Since dual- and multi-band systems are popular in wireless communications, the investigated designs can be extended to dual-/multi-band designs to meet the need of modern wireless systems. To do this, we need to have an equivalent magnetic current and an electric current with dual-/multi-band responses. This can be done by using a dual-/multi-band DRA and probe for the magnetic and electric currents, respectively.

117213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
117213.value: Over the last two decades, the dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) has received much attention due to its small size, low loss, low cost, and ease of excitation. In this project, a novel DRA design concept that involves both electric and magnetic currents is investigated for the first time. This new kind of DRA, named as complementary DRA, is very compact in size with a very simple feed. It is used in this project to design quasi-isotropic and unidirectional antennas. The quasi-isotropic antenna is useful in some applications such as radio-frequency identification (RFID) systems because it has good coverage of signal at different angles. For DRAs, however, only broadside and omnidirectional radiation modes have been investigated and no quasi-isotropic radiation pattern has been generated. In this project, compact quasi-isotropic antennas are designed using complementary DRAs. Wideband versions are also provided for wideband wireless systems. Two kinds of unidirectional antennas are designed using complementary DRAs, namely the lateral and boresight unidirectional DRAs. Wideband designs are also provided for both kinds of unidirectional DRAs. In addition, circularly polarized boresight unidirectional DRAs are provided for different industrial needs. For each antenna, simulations are done using ANSYS HFSS and verified with measurements. Guidelines are given to facilitate the designs.

117713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
117713.value: 有越來越多的關注建築物的能源消耗和對環境的影響。近年，淨零能源建築的概念已經獲得了廣泛的關注，成為國際化的目標，用以幫助緩解能源的枯竭和環境的惡化。一般淨零能源建築的設計策略是涉及建築物最小化的能源使用,這往往需要通過很多的節能措施和生產可再生能源來滿足最小的能源需求。在亞熱帶的香港，大部分在商業樓宇的能源,是用於佔總建築電力消耗約四分之三的空調和電燈照明來創做舒適的熱和視覺建築環境。這表明，空調和照明系統是在商業樓宇最節省大量電力的兩個關鍵領域。太陽能和風能已被確認為可以在香港大規模應用,產生可持續的，取之不盡，用之不竭，清潔和安全的能源。透過建築圍護結構來限制炎熱夏季增熱和冬季熱損失的方法,包括保溫,熱質量，窗口/玻璃窗和屋頂綠化，提高在炎熱夏天的溫控器設置，利用自然通風在流通領域，變風量的空調系統，風機變速驅動器,變速泵及性能係數高的製冷機組都是減少冷卻負荷的節能措施。使用高效節能燈具的調光控制和適當的採光方案,可以舒減照明能源。自然光可以減少電力需求和電力照明的顯冷負荷。高層商業建築屋頂面積有限，半透明和不透明的建築集成光伏,細小的太陽跟踪光伏和微型風力發電機,都是適合安裝在這個地方的可再生能源設施。半透明建築集成光伏電池板可被認為是提供電力，減少太陽熱量吸收及提高採光計劃的玻璃系統。太陽能跟踪器，可以將光伏電池板不停迎著太陽而獲得最大的太陽輻照度和發電輸出,微型風力發電機安裝在自然通風的地方，可提高整體的性能。建議項目將研究所有這些節能措施和可再生能源設施,達至實現淨零能源建築。這項工作將包括實地測量，數值方法和計算機模擬及探討在能源，環境和成本的好處。研究結果將有助於建立一個可持續的，健康性，舒適性的宜居城市。

117713.label: Realisation of objectives
117713.value: To establish performance databases for various RE applications and energy-efficient schemes under actual operating conditions using systematic field measurements The design strategies for a net zero energy building generally involve the minimization of energy use through more energy-efficient measures and generation of renewable energy to meet the minimal energy needs. Field measurements are the most accurate method for obtaining reliable data under actual conditions for analysis and evaluation. Proper lighting controls integrated with daylighting have a strong potential for reducing energy demand in commercial buildings. On-site measurements of the daylight illuminance in atrium corridors were undertaken. Based on the measured daylight availability, the lighting energy reduction and number of switching were simulated and evaluated. The correlation between the percentage of lighting energy savings and the number of switch offs was developed. The study can give an alternative to estimate the electric energy savings from the selected number of switch offs based on the various photoelectric switching controls. The solar energy harvested by photovoltaic (PV) technologies is recognized as sustainable and environmental friendly renewable resource. Nowadays, building integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) which consists of PV panels mounted on the opaque parts of the building facades for generating electricity would be an effective technology for electricity production and building envelop heat gain reduction. However, the sun positions, temperature and solar irradiance vary with the weather, season and time of a day, which make the standard test conditions rarely occur in practice. It is necessary to evaluate and estimate the performance of PV system in operation according to field measurements. As a well-developed artificial intelligence algorithm, the artificial neural network (ANN) is effective in analyzing the inter correlation between different variables. Based on the data being measured in Hong Kong, a model was developed to correlate the PV efficiency with other simultaneously recorded parameters including the solar radiation on the surface of PV panel, the temperature of PV cell, and the incidence angle of sunlight to the PV panel to indicate the PV operating conditions. The correlations being developed by ANN were applied to determine the year-round power output for the horizontal, vertical, tilted and sun-tracking PV systems. To use the measured data to develop numerical approaches and computer codes for modeling and simulating various RE facilities and energy-efficient schemes Meteorological readings and output energy data are essential to study the technical performance in terms of efficiency of various active solar energy applications. Technical data including solar radiation received, output power generated, air temperature, global temperature and the solar panel temperature were recorded. Artificial neural network was adopted to mimic the nonlinear correlation between the climatic variables and the system efficiency. Sensitivity analysis was conducted for evaluating the significance of individual input variable. The results were used to develop typical weather files for building energy studies and simulate the long-term energy performance for solar energy system. The findings on daylight-linked lighting controls and active solar systems were employed for modeling and simulating various energy-efficient schemes and RE facilities in zero energy buildings. To integrate the appropriate energy-efficient schemes and RE systems for designing NZEBs using computer simulation techniques The global irradiance on a horizontal plane consists of two differently featured components, namely the direct and diffuse irradiance. The two components are essential to the estimation of solar irradiance in arbitrary surface directions, obstructed environments and interior spaces for building energy simulation, and may affect the photovoltaic system analysis. In absence of hourly horizontal diffuse irradiance, the most common approach is to correlate the diffuse fraction with other readily available variables in simple regression equations. An appropriate approach was to use the technique of machine learning that extracts knowledge from the available data set and estimates the relationship between diffuse fraction and other readily accessible variables. The importance of meteorological variables in predicting diffuse fraction were analyzed by the algorithm of Boosted Regression and logistic regressions were developed to predict diffuse fraction using the identified important variables. Typical weather-year data representing long-term climatic conditions are essential for computer simulation studies and numerical analyses of building energy performance, daylighting schemes, and renewable energy applications. Weather data crucial to net zero energy building study include temperature (dry bulb and wet bulb), solar radiation (global, direct and diffuse), outdoor illuminance (global, direct and diffuse) and wind (direction and speed) recorded by the Hong Kong Observatory and our measuring station were collected for establishing the required weather data for computer simulation. In many parts of the world, the solar radiation and daylight illuminance data taken from surfaces of interest are not always readily available. Without direct measurement, the data can be predicted from empirical models based on geographical variations and meteorological parameters. Recently, the International Commission on Illumination has adopted a list of 15 standard skies. Each standard sky represents a unique, well-defined sky radiance and luminance pattern expressed by mathematical equations that can use to compute solar irradiance and daylight illuminance on inclined surfaces and variously oriented vertical planes. An issue is whether the sky conditions can be correctly categorized. Machine Learning techniques have been effectively used for predicting solar radiation and daylight illuminance and classifying the standard skies. Such approaches could be globally adopted and useful to compute the required climatic data for renewable and sustainable developments and energy-efficient building designs. To examine the energy, cost, thermal, visual and environmental aspects of NZEBs There are many immediate adverse effects on the environment such as emissions of greenhouse gases and pollutants. Semi-transparent and opaque building–integrated photovoltaics affect the building envelope designs in terms of visual and thermal aspects. The barriers to adopt renewable energy facilities include high initial costs, long monetary payback period and relative low efficiency. The operating performance of a building integrated photovoltaic system in Hong Kong was studied. To achieve zero energy, it is essential to learn the building demands and PV energy production with the accessible energy saving techniques and the available PV installation space on the building envelop. The study involves applying energy saving techniques that cooperate together. Building-energy simulation programs are appropriate design tools to depict the trade-off between various design alternatives. The annual and monthly building energy requirements and renewable energy generations were modeled by comprehensive computer simulations. The findings showed that zero energy school and office buildings could be achievable in hot and humid climate areas. The CO2 emission reduction, the embodied energy and greenhouse gas payback periods were predicted. The economic issue of the BIPV system with the concept of net present value and internal rate of return was determined. Daylighting is an important sustainable design strategy for alleviating problems in energy use climate and pollution, and for improving health, visual comfort and green building development. Natural daylight enters internal spaces largely through window openings that provide a visual connection between interior and exterior environments, and brighten the internal spaces. The calculation of the daylight illuminance for a given position in a building is a key step in daylighting designs. The merits and limitations of the approaches on DF determinations and proposes appropriate ideas to ameliorate and simplify the mathematical procedures for interior daylight estimation were evaluated. The architectural and daylighting design implications were discussed.

117713.label: Major findings and research outcome
117713.value: The correlation between the lighting energy savings and the number of switch offs was evaluated. The findings can estimate the electric energy savings from the selected number of switch offs from the various photoelectric switching controls which should be widely applied in day-lit areas of NZEB. (Journal paper 1) The importance of variables in predicting the hourly horizontal diffuse irradiance were identified by the algorithm of Boosted Regression Tree (BRT). The work showed a possible approach to interpret the results of machine learning for logistic regression equation development. (Journal paper 2) The calculation procedures explicitly illustrate the interdependency of various daylight parameters. The calculation tools can be used to analyze the daylight-linked lighting controls, fenestration systems, daylighting devices, shading facilities and visual comfort aspects. (Journal paper 3) An extensive review on solar radiation and daylight illuminance models and sky classification was conducted. It has been found that, ML tools would be an appropriate technology for estimating the basic solar energy parameters and conduct sensitivity analysis for individual meteorological variables. Logistic regressions could be made based on the importance of the identified parameters to compute the basic solar irradiance and daylight illuminance. Then, the available climatic data could be employed to classify the skies. With identified CIE skies, the comprehensive solar irradiance and daylight data could be found, to be used for further study and analysis. (Journal paper 4) A study of the energy performance and efficiency features using ANN techniques for a PV panel was conducted. The findings support the argument that the efficiency of the PV system is a function of the input solar irradiance, panel temperature and air mass. (Conference paper 1) The utilization of PV system is worthwhile for energy generation and carbon emission reduction as the payback periods were found below the life span of most present PV systems and investments can be profitable for the great power tariff escalation potential and low local interest rate. (Conference paper 2) An artificial neural network (ANN) was built to predict the efficiency of photovoltaic panels in operation conditions. The model was applied to the year-round hourly weather data of Hong Kong to estimate the hourly efficiency and energy output of different PV installations. (Conference paper 3) Using computer simulation techniques, the energy expenditures for a low-rise (Conference paper 4) and a high-rise (Conference paper 5) were estimated.

117713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
117713.value: It is very difficult to design a zero energy building. Cooling requirements in commercial buildings are quite high and electric light fittings are always turned on even when the lighting is not required. Solar radiation through fenestration provides the majority of the building envelope’s cooling load which contributes over one-third of the cooling requirement. Proper daylighting schemes can lower electricity expenditure in lighting. Semi-transparent building integrated photovoltaic panels can provide electricity and apposite to daylighting schemes that enhance visual comfort, reduce peak electrical and façade cooling demands, and conserve building consumption. Double-skin façade (DSF) in an effective façade design. The external walls can respond dynamically to varying ambient conditions incorporating a range of integrated sun-shading, natural ventilation and thermal insulation devices. When the cavities provide a pace for positioning the thin-film solar cell, such solar façade would be a typical semi-transparent BIPV application. Low ambient temperature can improve the PV system performance and this the PV modules would be quite suitable installed in the air cavity of the DSF to achieve excellent energy performance. For further development, the key variables are changed parametrically in calculations so that the appropriate design criteria can be selected according to the desired energy outcomes.

117713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
117713.value: The design strategies for a net zero energy building (NZEB) generally involve the minimization of energy use through various energy-efficient measures and the generation of renewable energy (RE) to meet the minimal energy needs. In subtropical Hong Kong, most of the energy used in commercial buildings is used to create a thermally and visually comfortable environment, specifically air conditioning and electric lighting. Proper daylighting schemes can reduce the energy used in lighting. Natural light can help reduce the electrical demand and the sensible cooling load from electric lighting. For high-rise commercial buildings with limited roof areas, semi-transparent and opaque building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV) are appropriate RE facilities. Semi-transparent BIPV panels can be used as glazing systems that provide electricity, reduce solar heat gain, and enhance daylighting schemes. Solar trackers can turn the PV panels so that they always face the sun for maximizing the generation of electricity. The study examined the use of these energy-efficient measures and RE facilities in creating NZEBs. The work included field measurements, numerical approaches, and computer simulations. The benefits in terms of energy, the environment, and costs were investigated. The findings contributed to the establishment of a sustainable, healthy, comfort, and livable urban environment.

117913.label: Project Objectives
117913.value: In a multi-core system where each voltage cluster can adjust speed independently, if jobs are already physically assigned to cores, we will use optimal speed curves in different cores to merge into either an optimal or an approximate optimal speed curve for the whole voltage cluster. If the jobs are only logically grouped together, with the obtained preliminary results when jobs have the same arrival time and deadline, we will further study how to compute optimal schedules when both the number of cores in each cluster and the number of clusters are input variables. We will try to either prove the problem to be NP-hard or find polynomial time algorithms to solve the problem. When memory energy consumption is considered without the speed changing flexibility, we will first explore the single core system and then extend to multi-core system with all the jobs preassigned. We will consider different granularity for power management in memory systems. The most coarse-grained management is to consider the whole memory as a single unit to turn on and off, while the finer-grained approach controls the power states of individual memory banks independently. We aim to characterize the optimal structure of the min-memory-energy scheduling and design approximation solutions with proved guarantees, if some variants of the problem are NP-hard.

117913.value: 近年來綠色計算的興起反映了人們為可持續發展而節約能源的決心。電腦硬件技術的進步在開發新型處理器的同時也為研究節能調度帶來了更大的挑戰。在本項目中，我們計劃展開帶有存儲結構的多核可調電壓系統中的節能調度研究。在多核系統中，如果所有的核都用同一個電壓會消耗太多的處理器能量，而允許每個核單獨調節電壓在硬件實現方面又會引入太多的代價，因此，兩者間的一個折中便是採用有多個電壓​​區域的多核結構，使得每個區域本身可以自由調節速度，而處於同一區域的核在同一時間只能採用相同的速度。比如Intel就已經開發了一個具備這個特性的48核芯片，其中有6個電壓區域，每個區域8個核。當任務已經分配完畢時，我們試圖找出最優調度的特性，而當任務還未分配時，我們也計劃研究如何分配最節能。 除了處理器的能耗之外，另一個主要的能耗元件就是存儲設備。研究者已經發現保持存儲結構處於激活狀態耗費的能量佔存儲結構總耗能相當大的比例。因此，如何執行任務來減少存儲結構處於激活狀態的時間成了一個很重要的研究課題。在理論計算機領域，已經有學者研究瞭如何最大化單處理器的空閒時間。在該情況下，此空閒時間等價於存儲設備的空閒時間；在實際系統領域，學者們則提出了一些啟發式算法來決定存儲設備的開關。但是對於多核系統共享一塊存儲的情況，如何把來自不同處理器的空閒時間聚在一起則是一個尚未有學者解決的問題。另外，當存儲本身也有層次結構時，問題便會變得更加複雜。對不同的存儲結構提出有理論保障的方法既具挑戰，又值得研究。 完成這個項目對於理解一個更完全的計算系統中的節能問題會有很大的幫助，也有助於加速節能算法真正的在操作系統中實現。

117913.label: Realisation of objectives
117913.value: Objective 1: In a multi-core system where each voltage cluster can adjust speed independently, if jobs are already physically assigned to cores, we will use optimal speed curves in different cores to merge into either an optimal or an approximate optimal speed curve for the whole voltage cluster. We considered scheduling different clusters separately and derived approximation algorithms with proved guarantee. We could carry out merge operation starting from the highest speed block (using that speed for all the other cores and then delete the already finished jobs). However, this way of merging can only produce heuristic solutions (we discovered some instance where such a process cannot generate the optimal solution) whose approximation ratios are very difficult to achieve. Objective 2: If the jobs are only logically grouped together, with the obtained preliminary results when jobs have the same arrival time and deadline, we will further study how to compute optimal schedules when both the number of cores in each cluster and the number of clusters are input variables. We will try to either prove the problem to be NP-hard or find polynomial time algorithms to solve the problem. When the number of cores in each cluster and the number of clusters are variables, we designed dynamic programming algorithms and greedy algorithms whose running time depend on those variables. More specifically, when either of the two numbers is a constant, our proposed algorithm is in polynomial time. The major results for the above two objectives are published in IEEE TPDS. We also have a follow up work focusing on temperature instead of energy which won the CODES+ISSS best paper award in 2014. The journal version appears in IEEE TC. Objective 3: When memory energy consumption is considered without the speed changing flexibility, we will first explore the single core system and then extend to multi-core system with all the jobs preassigned. We will consider different granularity for power management in memory systems. The most coarse-grained management is to consider the whole memory as a single unit to turn on and off, while the finer-grained approach controls the power states of individual memory banks independently. We aim to characterize the optimal structure of the min-memory-energy scheduling and design approximation solutions with proved guarantees, if some variants of the problem are NP-hard. We consider the memory as a whole to turn off and on. We obtained algorithmic results to minimize the common active time of all the processors and got the results published in DATE and TAMC. When turning off memory is further combined with DVS capability, we also obtained some interesting results and got it published in DATE also. When the granularity becomes finer, we later studied a model where each core has its own memory which could be turned off if all its jobs use the general shared memory. We proved the NP-hardness results and use ILP to formulate the problem with or without preemption. We further use LP rounding to derive approximation algorithms. The results for this part is published in RTSS and the journal version is recently accepted by IEEE TC.

117913.label: Major findings and research outcome
117913.value: For objective 1 and 2, we considered scheduling different clusters separately and derived approximation algorithms with proved guarantee. When the number of cores in each cluster and the number of clusters are variables, we designed dynamic programming algorithms and greedy algorithms whose running time depend on those variables. More specifically, when either of the two numbers is a constant, our proposed algorithm is in polynomial time. The major results for these two objectives are published in IEEE TPDS (Journal No.2). We also have a follow up work (Conference No.6) focusing on temperature instead of energy which won the CODES+ISSS best paper award in 2014. The journal version appears in IEEE TC (Journal No. 13). For objective 3, we consider the memory as a whole to turn off and on. We obtained algorithmic results to minimize the common active time of all the processors and got the results published in DATE (Conference No.4) and TAMC (not in Part C). When turning off memory is further combined with DVS capability, we also obtained some interesting results and got it published in DATE (Conference No.3) also. When the granularity becomes finer, we later studied a model where each core has its own memory which could be turned off if all its jobs use the general shared memory. We proved the NP-hardness results and use ILP to formulate the problem with or without preemption. We further use LP rounding to derive approximation algorithms. The results for this part is published in RTSS 2016 (Conference No. 10) and the journal version is recently accepted by IEEE TC. Applications in other scenarios like data transmission share similar nature as the memory model and we obtained results which are published in IEEE JSAC (Journal No. 1) and INFOCOM (Conference No. 5).

117913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
117913.value: One further direction to pursuit is to prove the approximation ratio of the merging process for optimal speed curves from different processors. We showed that this merging process cannot generate optimal solutions but did not prove how good the solution will be. About the memory-CPU tradeoff, we could have a intermediate level of granularity where cores are split into partitions and each partition has its own locally shared memory. How to derive schedules which could achieve low memory energy consumption will be a potential direction to follow.

117913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
117913.value: Energy saving is always a major concern for chip designers. Among different energy saving technologies, Dynamic Voltage Scaling is one of the most important which makes energy saving possible by adjusting execution speed of processors when they are executing jobs. Current technology further allows many CPU cores to be put on the same chip, thus creating an architecture called voltage island, where cores in the same island can only use the same speed at any specific time. This architecture combines the local voltage scaling where each individual core could adjust its speed independently and global voltage scaling where all the cores share the same speed. How to schedule jobs in an energy efficient manner is important and challenging for this architecture. On the other hand, memory is another major power consumer. For a globally shared memory, it can be turned off to save energy when no job is using the memory. Therefore, finding a schedule which can maximize the time that memory could be turned off is very important. Furthermore, if memory has hierarchies, then more energy could be saved. Finally, if DVS is considered together with the memory, we designed algorithms which can save even more energy.

118013.label: Project Objectives
118013.value: We will study channel estimation techniques for large MIMO systems. Channel estimation in a system with a large number of channel coefficients involves high complexity, and estimation errors may be inevitable due to the so-called pilot contamination phenomenon. We will seek low-cost channel estimation algorithms with improved accuracy. Conventional multi-user detection techniques require reliable channel state information (CSI). Otherwise, such detection techniques cannot fully separate the signals received from different users. We will explore new methods based on iterative detection techniques. We will place the emphasis on finding low-complexity solutions, since this is vital for large MIMO systems to be practically realizable. Most existing MIMO transmission schemes based on, e.g., singular value decomposition or space-time coding, either assume perfect CSI at transmitter (CSIT) or no CSIT at all. They are not efficient if partial CSIT is available. A desirable scheme should be able to exploit the advantages of the available CSIT and, at the same time, be robust against possible CSIT errors. We will devise such schemes based on a joint forward error control (FEC) coding and linear pre-coding strategy. Due to channel estimation errors, it is difficult to avoid cross-user interference via multi-user coordinated beamforming on the down-link. We will study a BS cooperation approach to improve signal quality on the down-link. To keep complexity low, we will focus our attention on systems with local CSIT information. We will develop joint coherent transmission and simple multi-user coordination techniques that are suitable for large MIMO systems.

118013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
118013.value: Wireless data traffic has been growing at an exponential speed in the past decade, largely due to the proliferation of smart phones and tablet computers. Reducing cell size is a conventional way to support this growth, but deploying new base station (BS) sites can be very costly in many situations. Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technology potentially provides an alternative solution. A MIMO system involves multiple antennas mounted at both transmitter and receiver, and has long been identified as a promising technology for future cellular systems. A large MIMO system refers to one involving many (tens or even hundreds of) antennas, typically at the BS side. The large MIMO concept has recently attracted considerable research interest. In principle, a large MIMO system provides a large degree of freedom and can potentially achieve very high capacity. However, there are many challenges that must be addressed in order to realize large MIMO systems. Channel modeling, antenna design, and asymptotic capacity analysis are active research topics, but there are also many open issues at the system design level. In particular, channel state information (CSI) is a crucial issue for large MIMO systems. It has been revealed recently that the so-called pilot contamination effect imposes a limit on CSI accuracy in large MIMO systems. This has serious consequences for system design, since many existing transmission and detection techniques rely on accurate CSI and so may not work well in the presence of CSI errors. There are transmission schemes, such as space-time coding, that do not require CSI at the transmitter (though they still need reliable CSI at the receiver for detection). However, such schemes cannot make full use of the available degrees of freedom in a large MIMO system. In this project, we will study system design techniques for large MIMO systems. We will develop new strategies for channel estimation, up-link and down-link transmission, error control coding and linear pre-coding. In recent years, we have worked on many aspects related to MIMO systems and we will exploit this accumulated experience to make real progress on the challenging issues in large MIMO systems. Our main aim is to develop low-cost but efficient solutions for large MIMO that will be useful in practice.

118013.label: Realisation of objectives
118013.value: The objectives of this project are summarised as follows: (1) a solution to the pilot contamination problem, (2) low-cost CSI estimation in multi-user environments, (3) joint decoding and channel estimation techniques, and (4) multi-user cooperative beamforming and pre-coding. Objective (1) is the core of this project and has been well achieved. We developed a data-aided channel estimation (DACE) technique that can efficiently reduce the pilot contamination problem in large MIMO systems. Its features of low-cost and high performance have been investigated analytically and numerically in journal publication [1]. The main idea of DACE is that partially detected data can be utilized to provide the function of pilots. The correlation among data is naturally low, and thus DACE can alleviate the pilot contamination problem caused by the correlation among pilots. This work has attracted notable attention in the research community. It has received 67 Google citations so far. Our work is also successful related to objective (2) on channel estimation in multi-user systems. Journal publication [1] provides both single-user and multi-user analysis and simulation. It is shown that DACE is efficient for both cases. We derived the achievable rate of time varying channels and analyzed multi-user detection performance in journal publication [3], based on the interleave division multiple access (IDMA) principle. We developed a decentralized multi-user transmission scheme in journal publication [5], in which each user only needs to know the state information of its own channel and none of other users. This greatly reduces the overhead in the backhaul for distributing global channel state information. We are particularly excited by our recent findings related to objective (3) on joint decoding and channel estimation in large MIMO systems. We developed novel detection algorithms based on turbo compressed sensing in journal publications [2][4][6]. This work turns out very fruitful. Turbo compressed sensing was originally designed for MIMO receivers, but it leads to a more intriguing discovery of the so-called orthogonal AMP (OAMP) algorithm, as published in reference [OAMP’17] below. We found that OAMP has a more broad range of applications beyond communications. Recently, OAMP has been studied by many researchers in the signal processing community for image signal processing. The related work in reference [OAMP’17] has received 31 Google citations so far. Strictly speaking, OAMP is a following-up work of this project and has been supported by other projects. Nevertheless, the work on turbo compressed sensing in this project laid down the foundation for OAMP. Finally, for objective (4), we studied a low-cost statistical water filling technique that requires only partial CSIT for pre-coding in the up-link conference publication [1]. We also devised a solution to the down-link using a so-called Hermitian pre-coding technique conference publication [2] that requires only local channel state information of each bas station, yet it can provide the cooperation gain involving several adjacent base stations. I would like to mention that in journal publications [1] and [2], project number 118014 is acknowledged mistakenly. This results from a typo in journal publication [2] and later the same acknowledgement was copied to journal publication [1]. (I have no project with project number 118014.) I apologise for this careless mistake. Reference [OAMP’17] Junjie Ma and Li Ping, "Orthogonal AMP", IEEE Access, vol. 5, no. 1, pp. 2020 – 2033, Jan., 2017.

rows: We will study channel estimation techniques for large MIMO systems. Channel estimation in a system with a large number of channel coefficients involves high complexity, and estimation errors may be inevitable due to the so-called pilot contamination phenomenon. We will seek low-cost channel estimation algorithms with improved accuracy.

Conventional multi-user detection techniques require reliable channel state information (CSI). Otherwise, such detection techniques cannot fully separate the signals received from different users. We will explore new methods based on iterative detection techniques. We will place the emphasis on finding low-complexity solutions, since this is vital for large MIMO systems to be practically realizable.

Most existing MIMO transmission schemes based on, e.g., singular value decomposition or space-time coding, either assume perfect CSI at transmitter (CSIT) or no CSIT at all. They are not efficient if partial CSIT is available. A desirable scheme should be able to exploit the advantages of the available CSIT and, at the same time, be robust against possible CSIT errors. We will devise such schemes based on a joint forward error control (FEC) coding and linear pre-coding strategy.

Due to channel estimation errors, it is difficult to avoid cross-user interference via multi-user coordinated beamforming on the down-link. We will study a BS cooperation approach to improve signal quality on the down-link. To keep complexity low, we will focus our attention on systems with local CSIT information. We will develop joint coherent transmission and simple multi-user coordination techniques that are suitable for large MIMO systems.

118013.label: Major findings and research outcome
118013.value: Our major findings are summarized as follows: (1) We developed a data-aided channel estimation (DACE) technique that can efficiently reduce the pilot contamination problem in large MIMO systems. The new technique is of low-cost and has demonstrated excellent performance (journal publication [1]). (2) We derived the achievable rate of time varying channels in journal publication [3] and developed a decentralized multi-user transmission scheme in multi-user environments in journal publication [5] which requires only local channel state information. (3) We developed novel detection algorithms based on turbo compressed sensing journal publications [2][4][6]. This work revealed a more intriguing discovery of the so-called orthogonal AMP (OAMP) algorithm. OAMP is potentially applied to a broad range of applications beyond communications, for example image signal processing. (4) We studied a low-cost statistically pre-coding technique that requires only partial CSIT initially conference publication [1] in the up-link. We also devised a solution to the down-link using a so-called Hermitian pre-coding technique conference publication [2].

118013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
118013.value: The outcomes of this project have attracted attention from both research community and industry. We are currently working together with several companies on the applications of DACE and IDMA in future 5G systems. We noticed that IDMA has been extensively studied by several leading companies in the world in their proposal for 5G standard, including Nokia, Samsung, ZTE, MediaTek, Intel and InterDigital. We have also secured a sum of HK$600,000 from industry for a joint research proposal under the research impact fund (RIF). The proposal was submitted to UGC in March 2018. In the future, we will continue our study on applications of DACE and IDMA in 5G. In particular, massive machine-type communication (mMTC) has been identified as a key service for 5G. The overheads in the RACH (random access channel) procedure used in 4G, which is to establish centralized control and acquire upfront channel state information, are a heavy burden for mMTC. Decentralized control is a more preferred alternative. DACE and IDMA become particularly attractive in decentralized environments since they allow gradual and progressive improvement of channel state information. However, complexity of DACE, even though it is much lower than other alternatives, is still a concern. We will devote our research effort in the future along this direction.

118013.value: We developed a data-aided channel estimation (DACE) technique that can efficiently reduce pilot contamination in large MIMO systems. 118213.label: Project Title(Chinese)
118213.value: 台风边界层风场特性研究及在结构设计和风工程应用

118213.label: Co - Investigator(s)
118213.value: Prof Cao , Shu-Yang Ms Song , Li-Li Prof Tamura, Yukio Prof XIAO, Yiqing

118213.label: Project Objectives
118213.value: Typhoons occur frequently in Hong Kong and Guangdong. The proposed simultaneous observation of wind data during typhoons—in Hong Kong, through anemometers at 51 meteorological stations, four Doppler radars and three sodars, and in Guangdong, through nine radars and numerous anemometers installed at more than 40 meteorological towers—will provide valuable information on typhoon-generated wind characteristics over different terrain conditions. Such information is scarce, and new measurements will be very useful for the wind resistant design of buildings and structures. There is considerable uncertainty regarding typhoon structure, particularly a lack of information on profiles for wind over land from tropical cyclones, as required for the design of high-rise structures in typhoon-prone regions. The adoption of a mobile facility containing a vehicle-mounted Doppler radar and three portable meteorological towers with wind monitoring systems will enable the measurement of wind profiles at or close to typhoon landfall locations. This is expected to provide valuable information on the boundary layer wind structure in the eye-wall regions of strong typhoons. Such information will be very useful in clarifying the unknown aspects of typhoons within the atmospheric boundary layer. An intensive analysis of the measured wind data will be performed to obtain statistical information on wind speed profiles and the wind and turbulence parameters that will be used to evaluate the adequacy of theoretical and empirical models and to develop new models. The analyzed results will be presented with respect to various terrain roughness conditions and the different stages of the typhoon’s life cycle. Apart from the vertical profiles of mean wind speed, gust envelop profiles will also be proposed for application in codes and standards. Wind tunnel tests will be conducted to study the effect of topography on wind speed profiles and the effects of the scaling of topographical models. The field measurement results will be used to verify the accuracy of wind tunnel testing data from models with various scales and to clarify the appropriate topographical model scale range that can provide credible results. In particular, this project aims to clarify an important issue in wind engineering: whether small-scale topographical models can be used to evaluate wind flow fields for subsequent modeling at a larger scale to estimate wind effects on structures. The combined field and model test study will thus enable a thorough assessment of the effects of terrain roughness and topography on wind speeds profiles and turbulence properties to further the understanding of the boundary layer wind structure of a typhoon upon landfall and its interaction with topography. The assessment of wind loads on buildings and structures requires a detailed knowledge of the approaching wind characteristics. Hence, a comparative study of the wind characteristics during typhoons with respect to monsoons will be conducted to clarify the differences in the wind speed profiles and turbulent characteristics of these winds. Investigations will be performed to evaluate the adequacy of the codes of practice and to improve structural designs for the effects of typhoons. Some guidance or recommendations for the wind-resistant design of high-rise structures in typhoon-prone regions will be proposed. It is anticipated that the outputs of this project will supply very useful information for amending the existing Hong Kong wind code.

118213.label: Major findings and research outcome
118213.value: The objectives of the project have been fully achieved, including: (1) Observations of wind fields within the atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) have been carried out using numerous anemometers, Dopoler radars and sodars at a number of meteorological stations in Hong Kong and in Guangdong during tropical cyclones, monsoons and thunderstorms. (2) Analysis of the measured wind data were performed to obtain statistical information on the wind and turbulence parameters as well as profiles of wind speed and direction. The analyzed results, which were presented with respect to various terrain roughness and topographical conditions and the different stages of the typhoon’s life cycle, were used to evaluate the adequacy of theoretical and empirical models and to develop new models. A data-driven scheme was proposed for standardization of raw wind speed data under complex terrains/topographic conditions, which overcomes the limitations of the existing methods. Correction factors for about 50 meteorological stations in Hong Kong were established, which provide accurate estimation of wind speed over different terrain conditions. (3) Wind tunnel testing was conducted to study the effect of topography on wind speed profiles over Cheung Chau Island and Waglan Island in Hong Kong. Several different geometric scaled models were used in the wind tunnel testing. The field measurement results were used to clarify the appropriate topographical model scale range that can provide credible results. (4) A new numerical modelling methodology was proposed for numerical simulation of wind flows over complex terrains using proper imposition of boundary conditions and tuning of the kε model. The topographic features of complex terrains were investigated by applying the new approach while the cross comparison was made between the numerical results and the wind tunnel experimental data and field measurements. It was confirmed that the new approach was capable of simulating the horizontally homogeneous atmospheric flows and reproducing the decrease of turbulence kinetic energy in the ABL. (5) Comparative studies of wind characteristics in typhoons with respect to monsoons and thunderstorms were conducted. In particular, the differences of gust factor and profiles of wind speed of these winds were clarified. (6) The boundary layer wind characteristics during landfall typhoons and their impacts on two super-tall buildings in Hong Kong and two skyscrapers in Shenzhen have been investigated. The observations of winds at several meteorological stations and by structural health monitoring systems installed in the buildings during several typhoons were analyzed. The structural dynamics properties and serviceability of the super-tall building under typhoon condition were investigated to evaluate the impacts of extreme climate events on skyscrapers.

118213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
118213.value: The results generated from this project provide useful information for the design of high-rise structures in tropical cyclone-prone regions. Meanwhile, they are also valuable for calibrating codes of practice and incorporation into useable wind tunnel modeling and numerical simulation. In addition, the research output of the project will be useful to national and local policymakers in formulating typhoon disaster mitigation regulations and implementing mitigation strategies.

118213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
118213.value: Typhoons are one of the world’s most destructive natural disasters. Thus, understanding the boundary layer wind structure of typhoons and investigating their wind characteristics are vital to disaster mitigation and structural design in typhoon-prone areas. This project aims to obtain reliable and valuable wind data from a variety of sources to investigate the wind characteristics within the atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) during typhoons for use in structural design and wind engineering application. The comprehensive field measurements of wind speeds and atmospheric turbulence characteristics during typhoons provide a fundamental improvement of knowledge in boundary layer wind structure, wind climate, typhoon wind characteristics, wind field modeling and design wind loads for Hong Kong and the surrounding regions. Wind tunnel tests are conducted to investigate the effects of terrain roughness and topography on ABL flow fields, and the field measurements are used to verify the accuracy of the results from topographical models with various scales. Furthermore, this study explores if there is a need to design structures for the effects of typhoons and the incorporation of such effects into structural design for Hong Kong and the typhoon-prone regions of mainland China. This project provides valuable information for the development of design standards and the verification of wind tunnel testing techniques.

To investigate the improvement of Li ion transport number by the incorporation of boron contained Lewis acid into the SPE matrix. To investigate the decoration of SPE films with nanoparticles that correspond to the different electrode surfaces, by applying the ultrasonication method that has recently been proven feasible in our laboratory for the decoration of electrospun fibre mats. 118313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
118313.value: 作为一种典型的储能设备，锂电池（固态电解质型）对当前能源经济的作用不言而喻。它们在可携带电子设备中的应用已经取得了相当骄人的成绩，然而在其他要求更严格领域的应用似乎并不是那么令人满意，例如在动力汽车上的应用。研究人员已经认识到，全固态聚合物电解质内在的问题是限制锂离子电池在这些领域应用的关键原因。这些问题包括：（1）全固态电解质有低的离子导电性和差的机械性能（例如差的抗拉强度）；（2）电解质内可迁移的锂离子数量偏少；（3）电解质与电极间固-固界面的接触较差。因而，对于普通的聚合物基的固态电解质（例如聚氧化乙烯基的电解质）而言， 当前的主要的挑战是去开发既具有高的离子导电性又有好的机械强度的电解质材料。然而这是一个矛盾的问题，因为高的离子导电性经常要求聚合物主链（例如聚氧化乙烯）柔韧且具有非晶结构，但这些特征往往会导致机械性能变差。为了解决这个问题，在这个项目中，我们提议去制备一种梳子状的共聚物，这种共聚物拥有交联的主链和短的柔性侧链（例如聚乙烯醇型的侧链）。交联的聚合物主链能够赋予固态电解质膜好的机械性能，而柔性的侧链能够保证好的离子导电性。此外，路易斯酸也会被添加到电解质膜中去增加可迁移的锂离子数量。另外，为了加强电解质膜和电极之间的相互作用， 我们也提议利用纳米粒子去修饰电解质膜的表面，这些纳米粒子将会很好地与电极材料匹配以便全面提升电池性能。 基于近来我们实验室开发的改进的超声方法，纳米粒子对电解质膜的修饰很容易被实现。 最后，锂盐浓度，聚乙烯醇链长和密度，路易斯酸含量和超声等实验参数对电解质的离子导电性和电池寿命的影响将在这一项目中被全面调查。

118313.label: Realisation of objectives
118313.value: Comb-like polyethylene glycol (PEG)-based copolymer electrolytes with given crosslinking density are synthesized using PEG as the main chain segments (denoted as MC-PEG), methoxy polyethylene glycol (MPEG) as side chain segments (denoted as SC-PEG), and hexamethylene-1,6-diisocyanate homopolymer (HDI trimer) as bridging and/or crosslinking agent. The effects of molecular weight of MC-PEG and SC-PEG on Li ion conductivities of the copolymer have been examined. A self-supporting comb-like Si-PEG copolymer with flexible Si–O–C bonds in the main chain and pending short PEG chains as the side chain was synthesized to improve the low temperature performance and overcome the quandary between good mechanical and electrochemical properties of the polymer electrolyte in lithium-ion batteries. A composite cathode material containing LiFePO4 nanoparticles encapsulated by PEG-based polymer electrolyte (coated LiFePO4) are prepared in order to increase the interfacial contact area between SPE and cathode materials.

118313.label: Major findings and research outcome
118313.value: The electrospinning technique has been employed to developed nanofibres and nanoparticles with various morphologies [3, 4, 5]. The ultrasonication method has also been used to decorate polymer foam and and fibre networks with carbon nanotubes and particles [5, 2]. A in-situ monitoring technique has been developed to determine the diffusivity in polymer films using confocal laser scanning microscopy [1]. Comb-like polyethylene glycol (PEG)-based copolymer electrolytes with given crosslinking density are synthesized, and the effects of molecular weight of MC-PEG and SC-PEG on Li ion conductivities of the copolymer have been examined [9]. Subsequently, a self-supporting comb-like Si-PEG copolymer with flexible Si–O–C bonds in the main chain and pending short PEG chains as the side chain was synthesized to improve the low temperature performance and overcome the quandary between good mechanical and electrochemical properties of the polymer electrolyte in lithium-ion batteries [6]. The poor contact between the cathode and the solid polymer electrolyte (SPE) is one of the primary causes for the low specific capacities of lithium ion batteries. In this work, a composite cathode material containing LiFePO4 nanoparticles encapsulated by PEG-based polymer electrolyte (coated LiFePO4) are prepared in order to increase the interfacial contact area between SPE and cathode materials [8].

118313.value: In this study, the comb-like copolymer electrolytes with controlling cross linking density has been demonstrated to be viable solid polymer electrolytes (SPE). To further explore and develop of SPE, the use of inorganic lithium garnets particulate to form composite electrolytes are definitely worth investigating.
