118413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
118413.value: 蛋白質的功能酶，抗體，傳感器，運輸，在無數其他角色中，他們是活的生物體中發現的重要分子。這些功能可以通過比較蛋白的分子結構研究。通常模擬為三維坐標的集合的距離矩陣，以促進比較的蛋白質分子。目前的辦法比較模型患有高時間複雜性和缺乏履約擔保。最近，特徵提取方法允許蛋白質結構更簡潔的表示形式（結構片段库） ，產生更高效的算法調心蛋白。與此同時，蛋白質研究的亞結構域結構的進化關係，以及蛋白質分子動力學設計的新舉措設置允許調查。我們提出了一個簡潔的模型的結構信息中提取蛋白質結構域蛋白質的研究，並使用所提取的特徵。我們的模型不同於現有模型的一個方面，而現有模型的表現力有限，在代表非本地殘留物是他們的訂單之間的約束，我們的模型載編碼順序無關的結構關係，在多個片段。 我們研究模型。我們首先考慮結構調整的高效算法。初步研究顯示，利用我們的指紋圖譜蛋白質結構模型，可以得到更準確的路線，而不引入任何運行時開銷。此外，模型自然產生的一個變體的距離的基於矩陣的結構的對齊問題 - 普遍認為是NP，由於其相似的子圖的同構問題的問題。新的問題的初步分析表明存在一個多項式時間的解決方案。通過從溶液中獲得的見解，更好的結果可能是結構調整問題可能在其他如DALI距離矩陣。 第二個問題是我們的新模型所編碼的蛋白質結構，基本的進化或功能單位或域研究的碎片。當前SCOP和CATH數據庫的維護一個數據庫這些領域的人類專家，分類。從我們的模型拍攝的片段構成的層次結構，可以用來獲得進化或功能的操作，我們希望用來定義結構之間的距離，以及在蛋白質科學領域的一般使用。 第三個問題，我們考慮設計的蛋白質結構預測問題的更好的模型。現有的從頭計算方法是低效的尋找近天然結構。這個效率低下的主要因素是在探索一個大的搜索空間不可能的候選人。研究通過我們的片段庫生成的空間結構之間的關係，我們希望能設計出更好的移動設置非冗餘的分子動力學。此外，它可能是未能代碼能源的產品進入片段隱式，以減輕一些依賴於能量函數計算。 這個項目的預期產出，包括高質量的研究刊物，算法，模型軟件，用於結構調整，結構預測，博士生的結構演化和培訓。

118413.label: Realisation of objectives
118413.value: We treat fragments as abstract features, First of all, this allows for more flexibility in performing structural searches. Our abstraction of a contact library takes further advantage of such an abstraction by encoding the global information of structures which fragments are unable to capture. we have defined a contact group and constructed a comprehensive library according to contact group, called a ContactLib, of contact groups to use as fingerprints for all existing protein structures. Then, we have proposed an indexing technique for ContactLib, which can be applied to neighbor contact group retrieval. We let a contact group refer to a small collection of residues that may have high density of contacts among the residues in a protein. As two residues in contact should not be far apart, we require all residues to be located within a sphere. The position of each residue here is represented by its Cα atom. A local contact group models contacts within a protein structure fragment, and a remote contact group could involve two or more structure fragments. Due to chemical and physical constraints within a limited sphere space, it is rare for a contact group to contain a large number of fragments. Hence, we define a contact group as a set of residues represented by the respective Cα atoms of either a single fragment with l1 residues, called local contact group, or a set of fragments with l2 residues, called remote contact group, such that all the Cα atoms are located within a sphere of radius r. To enable succinct and realistic representation of protein structures through the construction of a meaningful library of structural features, we have designed two types of structural features, one type is local contact group, and the other type is to capture the remote contat group. We are able to represent a protein structure with these local structures. Hence, a structure can be modeled into a bit vector, in which each local and remote structure is modeled as a bit. To solve theoretical and practical problems in protein structural alignment through the library, we compute two-bit vectors and assigned the different weight between two vectors, with which we can calculate the distance between structures. The weights are assigned by linear programming. By the above approach, we have also developed a distance function between two structures. In addition, we have incorporated the sequence similarity into our distance function. We have parameterized the distanced between two protein sequences As each structure is represented by a bit vector, we apply the Maximum likelihood phylogenetic tree method to build the protein structures into a tree. This tree is compared with the SCOP classification, We have applied the local structures into our FALCON program. Promising results are obtained. In addition, we have applied the developed techniques into the next generation sequence studies, which enables us to study the peppers, and also the mixture samples in forensics.

118413.label: Major findings and research outcome
118413.value: Protein alignment is a basic step for many molecular biology researches. The BLOSUM matrices, especially BLOSUM62, are the de facto standard matrices for protein alignments. However, after wide utilization of the matrices for 15 years, programming errors were surprisingly found in the initial version of source codes for their generation. And amazingly, after bug correction, the "intended" BLOSUM62 matrix performs consistently worse than the "miscalculated" one. In this paper, we find linear relationships among the eigenvalues of the matrices and propose an algorithm to find optimal unified eigenvectors. With them, we can parameterize matrix BLOSUMx for any given variable x that could change continuously. We compare the effectiveness of our parameterized isentropic matrix with BLOSUM62. Furthermore, an iterative alignment and matrix selection process are proposed to adaptively find the best parameter and globally align two sequences. Experiments are conducted on aligning 13,667 families of Pfam database and on clustering MHC II protein sequences, whose improved accuracy demonstrates the effectiveness of our proposed method. We have proposed the Context-Based Dependency Network (CBDN), a method that is able to infer gene regulatory networks with the regulatory directions from gene expression data only. To determine the regulatory direction, CBDN computes the influence of source to target by evaluating the magnitude changes of expression dependencies between the target gene and the others with conditioning on the source gene. CBDN extends the data processing inequality by involving the dependency direction to distinguish between direct and transitive relationship between genes. We also define two types of important regulators which can influence a majority of the genes in the network directly or indirectly. CBDN can detect both of these two types of important regulators by averaging the influence functions of candidate regulator to the other genes. In our experiments with simulated and real data, CBDN outperforms state-of-the-art approaches for inferring gene regulatory network. CBDN identifies the important regulators in the predicted network: TYROBP influences a batch of genes that are related to Alzheimer’s disease; ZNF329 and RB1 significantly regulate those ‘mesenchymal’ gene expression signature genes for brain tumors. The above methods were first designed for protein structures, and in which we hope to find the most important amino acid in a structure Besides, we have applied the maths model to trans-omics data analysis, which is the only plants we can obtain trans-omics datasets. Lastly, we have applied the method developed to the mixture of samples from forensic applications.

118413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
118413.value: In this project, we have developed new distance functions for protein structures, and we applied them to different datasets. We will carry a careful study of different distance functions for different datasets. For example, we found researchers often adopted 1-|Pearson correction| to measure the distances between two proteins, or two genes, which is not metric. We should modify it into a more reliable version. Deep learning has changed the fields of machine learning fundamentally. We would apply our succinct representation of the protein structures with deep learning. At this moments, all the ab initio protein structure predictions methods suffer from the energy function. We would study the possibility to model the energy function by neural net implicitly. We hope to send out two more manuscripts on this projects.

118413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
118413.value: In this project, we have proposed a succinct representation of protein structures. A protein structure is also considered as a rigid 3D object, and it is represented as a collection of 3D points. With this representation, immediately, when we compare two structures, we met several issues. First, we need to find the correspondence between points of two different structures, and also we need to define the distance function. We propose to use a collection of predefined substructures to represent problem structure. Each substructure is represented by one bit. If a structure contains a substructure, the bit is one, and otherwise, it is zero. Then we can represent a protein structure into a fix sized bit vector, With this bit vector, we can solve different problems related to protein structures. In this project, we have also applied the developed techniques to next-generation sequencing data analysis,

118513.value: 由于淋巴瘤癌细胞易扩散到淋巴瘤病人的脾、肾、骨骼与神经系统等组织，因此，淋巴瘤病人有极大的生命危险。开发一种灵敏且专用于早期淋巴瘤检测的方法，对于治愈淋巴瘤病及研究其他癌症疾病起到重要作用。淋巴瘤是淋巴细胞癌变后的细胞，而淋巴细胞是来自人类免疫系统的白细胞。研究来自病人的淋巴瘤细胞临床病理特征，对于探究病人的恶性肿瘤病理特性至关重要，同时也有利于医生选择合适的治疗方案与对病人个性化治愈效果进行预测。淋巴瘤有众多类型，治愈淋巴瘤的方法包括靶向药物疗法、化学疗法、放射疗法与骨髓移植。经上述治疗后，淋巴瘤病人的存活率取决于淋巴瘤病史、淋巴瘤病类型及淋巴病的发病阶段。然而，临床研究表明，患同种淋巴瘤的不同淋巴瘤病人对同种靶向治疗药物呈现差异性的治疗效果。因此，研究人类淋巴瘤细胞的特性，如细胞的表明粗糙度与硬度，对于研究细胞病理学特性及采用合适的治疗方案起到重要作用。然而，由于来自病人骨髓的淋巴瘤细胞样本中含有大量的血红细胞，因此，难以从中获得淋巴瘤细胞。 目前，临床医学中尚未有可有效分离淋巴瘤细胞与血红细胞的成熟方法。现有的细胞筛选方法，包括流式细胞仪与密度梯度离心法，均难以从骨髓中可靠并大量的分离出淋巴瘤细胞。在这个项目中，我们在与医生的合作研究基础上，最终开发出一种可实现高吞吐量及高纯度的淋巴瘤细胞筛选方法，完成淋巴瘤细胞与血红细胞的快速分离，并为临床环境下淋巴瘤细胞病理学特征的医学研究提供技术支持。我们将在未来三年完成如下重要研究：1)研究基于光诱导电液动力学的淋巴瘤细胞与血红细胞快速分离平台(细胞操控速度可实现100 μm/s)；2) 通过对生物流体溶液介质参数的实验研究，优化溶液介质，确保光诱导电液动力学筛选淋巴瘤细胞的过程中长时间保持细胞活性；3) 研究细胞理论模型及多物理场仿真，从理论上揭示光诱导电液动力学与细胞形态学及电机械特性之间关系。为完成上述研究，光诱导电液动力学芯片将与商用的微流控部件及计算机算法实现集成，同时建立一套可实现淋巴瘤细胞与血红细胞自动化筛选的光诱导电液动力学平台。

118513.label: Realisation of objectives
118513.value: All objectives outlined in the proposal were achieved and are discussed below. Objective 1. Demonstrate an automated OEK platform that is capable of automatically generating DEP force and electro-thermal motion in a specialized OEK microfluidic device. In order to apply an AC electric field across the optically-induced electrokinetics (OEK) chip, part of the a-Si:H thin film on the bottom ITO-glass substrate was etched to establish an electrical connection. Specifically, a 5 mm ×8 mm area of a-Si:H was patterned through standard photolithography and dry-etching (using the Oxford Plasma Lab 80 etching system) with 2% oxygen, 12.5% CF4 gas, with a 30mTorr etching chamber pressure, and 6-minute plasma exposure. The chip was then rinsed and cleaned with acetone and DI water before being dried by nitrogen gas. The microfluidic chamber, into which the cells and solution were injected, has a height of ∼60 μm. This microfluidic chamber between two ITO-glass substrates was constructed by using a patterned polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) thick film or a double-sided tape as a spacer. The OEK chip was fixed on a three-dimensional digital translation platform to accurately regulate the spatial movement of the OEK chip. To create the optically-projected patterns, a commercial graphics software package was employed to generate the virtual electrodes with any desired geometrical configurations, which were projected onto the lower surface of the OEK chip via a commercial LCD projector coupled with a computer. The manipulation and separation processes of the cells were observed and recorded using a charged coupled device mounted on a microscope. In addition, a condenser lens fixed between the LCD projector and the OEK chip, was used to focus and collimate the optical pattern onto the OEK chip. In order to power the OEK chip to perform cell separation process, an AC bias potential, supplied by a function generator was applied to the transparent ITO glasses, which are located at the top and bottom of the OEK chip. Objective 2. Demonstrate automatic separation of B-lymphoma cells and RBCs using the OEK platform. The red blood cells (RBCs) were obtained from volunteers and the samples were centrifuged at 1000 rpm for 5 min at 4°C. Then, the supernatant was discarded and the remained RBCs were resuspended into 1 mL of the isotonic solution for a second round of centrifugation using the same parameters. Then, the collected RBCs were resuspended into 1mL of isotonic solution for further experiments. The Raji cell line was obtained from Dr. Xiubin Xiao of the Affiliated Hospital of Military Medical Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China. The Raji cell line was cultured in Roswell Park Memorial Institute culture medium supplemented with 10% (v/v) fetal calf serum, 1% penicillin (v/v) (100 U/mL), and 1% streptomycin (v/v) (100 μg/mL) at 37°C in a humidified atmosphere of 5% CO2. In order to achieve standardized and comparable cell separation results using the proposed OEK chips, 1 mL of Raji cells suspension with a concentration of 1×106 cells/mL was spiked into 1 mL of RBCs suspension to obtain various cell ratios. For our experiments, RBCs concentrations of 1×107 cells/mL and 4×107 cells/mL were used to achieve cells ratios (Raji cells: RBCs) of 1∶10 and 1∶40, respectively. The resulting cellular mixture of RBCs and Raji Cells were loaded into the OEK chip cell separation experiments. We experimentally demonstrated rapid separation of Raji cells from RBCs by using dynamic ODEP force on the cells. The separation of these cells with two different concentration ratios was achieved by using two optically-projected lines (one dynamically moving and one fixed) that generate negative ODEP force of different magnitudes on the cells. Objective 3. Perform parametric experimental studies to find optimal biofluidic media that allow rapid separation of target cells (i.e., ~100um/sec movement of cells) and, at the same time, extend the viability of cells in the same media. In order to allow the rapid separation of Raji and red blood cells, investigations of cell adhesion phenomenon inside an OEK chip were performed. For example, 200 experiments were carried out to observe the adhesion behavior of ∼18, 000 cells. The experimental results showed that only ∼10% “free cells” of the Raji cells could be freely transported by ODEP force if only the isotonic solution is used. According to some researchers, the adhesion force between a-Si:H surface and mammalian cells are in the order of nanonewtons, while the ODEP force is in the order ranging from tens to hundreds of piconewtons, and hence, this adhesion force between the Raji cells and the a-Si:H surface should be minimized in order to effectively manipulate the Raji cells. In this study, we have found that adding different concentrations of bovine serum albumin (BSA) into the isotonic solution was very useful in reducing the adhesion force between the Raji cells and the OEK chip surface, i.e., when BSA was added into the isotonic solution the affinity force between the cells and the a-Si:H substrate of the OEK chip, was clearly reduced. We have investigated cell-to-substrate adhesion behavior as a function of the BSA's concentration in the isotonic solution. We have found that the cell-to-substrate adhesion could be quite significantly decreased, i.e., with 90±3% of the cells being easily transported when 0.2% (wt) BSA was added to the conventional isotonic solution. Furthermore, the measured liquid conductivity of the optimized isotonic solution was 1.3×10−2 S/m and also met the liquid conductivity requirement necessary to enable the OEK chip to perform well. Objective 4. Explore theoretical models to elucidate the underlining relationship between the optically-induced electrokinetics force fields and the morphology and electrical properties of the cells. There are several optically-related electrokinetic forces generated in an OEK chip, including DEP force and forces on a particle caused by ACEO- and ACET-induced flows. To enhance the experimental performance of the separation of the two types of cells, experimental conditions were set up such that the DEP force dominated in the separation process with a specific applied voltage frequency across the upper and lower substrates of an OEK chip. Hence, estimating the competing electrokinetics forces in the OEK chip as a function of the applied AC electric field across the fluidic medium is very important for this project. Numerical solutions estimating the velocities for the two types of cells (RBC and Raji) induced by the AC electrokinetics forces (i.e., DEP, ACEO, and ACET), as a function of the applied frequency, were obtained by using an FEM method. The simulation results indicate that within a specific frequency range, the ACEO or ACET may affect the DEP force-based separation process. For example, the ACET force in the frequency range of ∼70 kHz to ∼500 kHz is much higher than that in the frequency range of ∼7 kHz to ∼60 kHz, and thus may affect the cellular properties due to the increased temperature in the fluidic medium. Hence, a frequency in the range of ∼7 kHz to ∼60 kHz, which induces an nDEP force, is selected to conduct the separation experiments in this study. We note that Raji cells were modelled as shell-core particles and RBCs were modelled as single-shell oblate ellipsoids in the numerical studies.

118513.label: Major findings and research outcome
118513.value: The key purpose of this study is to verify the capability of using optically-induced electrokinetics (OEK) technique to separate Raji cells from red blood cells (RBCs), and potentially provide a new automated and label-free technology for cell separation and purification. Through the funding of this project, we have constructed an experimental system that consists of an image acquisition system to observe the cell separation process, and a pattern generation system to generate the virtual electrodes which are projected onto the lower surface of the OEK chisp by a LCD (liquid-crystal display) projector. Since there are much more RBCs in a blood sample than white blood cells, we have focused the current study on only Raji cells and RBCs. We simulated the blood sample of lymphoma patients by spiking the Raji cells into the RBCs sample from volunteers and then perform the cell separation experiment in this study. Although the size of the Raji cells is similar to the white blood cells, theoretically optically-induced dielectropheresis (ODEP) force can be still applied to discriminate them due to their inherently different dielectric parameters (i.e., membrane/cytoplasm/nucleus permittivity and conductance), which will result in the different direction and/or magnitude of ODEP force exerted on them. We have shown that using dynamically moving virtual electrodes to induce negative ODEP force of varying magnitudes on different cells can indeed separate Raji cells and RBCs in an optically-induced electrokinetics (OEK) chip rapidly. Polarization models for these two types of cells, which reflect their discriminate electrical properties, were established. Then, the cells' differential velocities caused by a specific ODEP force field were obtained by a finite element simulation model, thereby established the theoretical basis that the two types of cells could be separated using an ODEP force field. To ensure that the ODEP force dominated the separation process, a comparison of the ODEP force with other significant electrokinetics forces was conducted using numerical results. Experimental results showed that these two types of cells, with different concentration ratios, could be separated rapidly using externally-applied electrical field at a driven frequency of 50 kHz at 20 Vpp. In addition, we have found that in order to facilitate ODEP-based cell separation, Raji cells' adhesion to the OEK chip's substrate should be minimized, i.e., the appropriate bovine serum albumin concentration in an isotonic solution to reduce cell adhesion while maintaining suitable medium conductivity for electrokinetics-based cell separation was also investigated.

118513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
118513.value: Through this project, we experimentally demonstrated rapid separation of Raji cells from red blood cells (RBCs) by employing dynamic optically-induced electrokinetics OEK forces on the cells. The separation of these cells with two different concentration ratios was achieved by using two optically-projected lines (one dynamically moving and one fixed) that generate negative optically-induced dielectrophoretic force of different magnitudes on the cells. We think that further work should be carried out to investigate the viability of different cells under OEK forces. Currently, there is no gold standard technique in hospitals worldwide to efficiently differentiate lymphoma cells from a much larger population of RBCs. Therefore, additional work should also be performed to compare this OEK-based technology to established technologies, i.e., FACS (fluorescence activated cell sorting) and cell separation by centrifugation, in order to determine the through-put and effectiveness of these technologies. Our team will continue to collaborate with the Shenyang Institute of Automation (Chinese Academy of Sciences) and medical research organizations in China to seeking funds from sources such as the National Science Foundation of China, Hong Kong Research Grants Council, and Shenzhen Science and Technology Innovation Commission in order to carry out the future work described above.

118513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
118513.value: Lymphoma patients have a significant risk of life-threatening complications arising from both the spreading of infections and metastasis of the cancer cells to other organs such as the spleen, kidneys, bones, and the nervous system. Therefore, finding a sensitive and specific early detection method for lymphoma is critical to saving lives and improving our understanding of other types of cancers. The ultimate aim of our research team is to develop an integrated high-throughput and high-yield cell-extraction technology for obtaining lymphoma cells from bone marrow, and allow medical researchers to examine the pathology of the lymphoma cells in clinical environments. In this project, we collaborated with medical scientists to apply optically-induced electrokinetics (OEK) technology to efficiently separate cancerous B-lymphocytes and red blood cells. The following major objectives were achieved in this project: 1) developed an OEK platform to allow rapid separation of lymphoma and red blood cells; 2) performed parametric experimental studies to identify suitable biofluidic media that allowed effective separation of the cells using OEK, while also allowed cells to survive after the OEK process; 3) explored theoretical models and multi-physics simulations to elucidate the relationship between OEK forces and the morphology and electrical properties of the cells.

118613.label: Project Objectives
118613.value: To develop a novel spatial transformation based non-isomorphic sensing model for motion tracking and analysis: Boolean compressive infrared sensing model. This model can serve as a compressive sampling means for both wide and narrow infrared fields. This implies that human motion can be sensed to provide more effective and rich cues for motion tracking and analysis. To establish the analysis and design methodologies of coverage scalable and sensing efficient Boolean compressive infrared sensing for human motion sensing. We will study the issues of coverage scalability and sensing efficiency in Boolean compressive infrared sensing. Hierarchical Boolean compressive infrared sensing will be investigated for achieving the scalable visibility coverage and fulfilling the multilevel sampling resolution requirements. The sensing efficiency analysis and design will be conducted for the Boolean compressive infrared sensing with structured sparsity, which can benefit the development of low-cost and lightweight, compact and modularized PIR sensor arrays. To explore lightweight methodologies and algorithms for data-to-object associations and motion inferences for multilevel motion tracking over both narrow and wide fields. To support motion tracking in both narrow and wide fields, we will study multilevel motion tracking based on motion sensing at multilevel granularities. This includes the tasks of exploring lightweight methodologies for data-to-object association and motion inference with hierarchical compressive infrared sensing model. To construct a synergistic motion analysis framework of integrating global and local motion analysis from complementary perspective for resolving the ambiguity due to grouping interactions. Based on multilevel motion tracking, synergistic motion analysis will be conducted to integrate the global and local motion inferences from complementary perspective, which can contribute to resolving the ambiguity due to grouping interactions.

118613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
118613.value: Motion tracking and analysis is an important topic to study in automated human tracking for surveillance and many other applications. This proposal aims to study and develop a systematic and hierarchical motion sensing approach for advanced surveillance and the related applications. We propose a flexible and generic non-isomorphic sensing model for this purpose. The rational of the new sensing paradigm will be investigated by exploring the physically implemented compressive sampling with the visibility modulated pyroelectric infrared (PIR) sensor arrays. We will study the issues of coverage scalability and sensing efficiency of Boolean compressive infrared sensing. In particular, the hierarchical Boolean compressive infrared sensing will be investigated for achieving scalable visibility coverage and fulfilling multilevel sampling resolution requirements. The sensing efficiency analysis and design will be studied for the compressive infrared sensing with structured sparsity, which can benefit the development of low-cost and lightweight, compact and modularized PIR sensor arrays. To track motions in both narrow and wide fields, we will study multilevel motion tracking based on motion sensing at multilevel granularities. This includes the tasks of exploring lightweight methodologies for data-to-object association and motion inference with hierarchical compressive infrared sensing model. Based on the multilevel motion tracking, synergistic motion analysis will be pursued to integrate the global and local motion inferences from complementary perspective, which can contribute to resolving the ambiguity due to grouping interactions. 运动跟踪对于监控等应用是非常重要的。本项目旨在研究一多层次传感和多用途模型以适应此应用。此新传感方式将利用压缩取样传感器阵列，以探讨及增强其传感效率。为达到所需传感分辨率，本项目将探讨多层布尔压缩传感。在分析和设计中，将利用此间结构的稀疏性， 以便开发轻便低价便携及摸块化的传感器阵列。为实现在宽窄域多用跟踪，所开发的多层运动跟踪将基于红外压缩传感进行运动推恻。基于此多层跟踪的运动分析将互补式利用局部及全局推恻以解决物体间互相作用所至的不确定性。

118613.label: Realisation of objectives
118613.value: During the studies in this project, extensive studies were conducted on compressive sensing and motion tracking in relation to the project objectives. Related to compressive motion sensing, a novel appearance model using sparse representation and online dictionary learning techniques was developed for visual tracking. In this approach, visual appearance is represented by sparse representation [J2]. Online dictionary learning strategy is used to adapt the appearance variations during tracking. The sparse representation and online dictionary learning is unified by defining a sparsity consistency constraint that facilitates the generative and discriminative capabilities of the appearance model. As the method is insensitive to partial occlusions, a target can be effectively recovered from the corruptions using the sparse coefficients with respect to the learned sparse bases containing local appearances. Also the method can be efficiently implemented for tracking and is robust as the outliers can be eliminated via evaluations of the likelihood between the observations and the model. In studying motion sensing, a new method [J1] was developed to measure the 3D data of an object with a new projecting-imaging model based on fringe projection profilometry. Based on this model, the problem is studied on how the uncertainty of the relevant parameters would affect the 3D measurement accuracy, with relative error and sensitivity analysis provided. Experiments show that the proposed method can achieve good performance. In relation to complex motion tracking and analysis, some new invariants for space motion trajectories were studied, which benefit effective motion trajectory tracking, matching and recognition [J3,J4,J5]. A robust estimation of the integral invariants is formulated. The proposed integral invariants exhibit many attractive properties such as noise insensitivity, computational locality, and uniqueness in representation, in addition to being invariant to transformation groups. This will benefit effective motion tracking and analysis.

118613.label: Major findings and research outcome
118613.value: In this project, we studied the issues in compressive sensing in motion sensing. In this regards, sparse representation is adopted for motion sensing and tracking, with special attention on issues in robust tracking with modeling based on structured sparse representation. As the method is insensitive to partial occlusions, a target can be effectively recovered from the corruptions using the sparse coefficients with respect to the learned sparse bases containing local appearances. Implementation was conducted for flexible structured sparse representation to enhance the tracking performance. In studying motion sensing, a new method is developed to measure the 3D data of an object with a new projecting-imaging model based on fringe projection profilometry. With this model, the problem is studied on how the uncertainty of the relevant parameters would affect the 3D measurement accuracy, with relative error and sensitivity analysis provided. Related to motion tracking, efforts are paid to complex motion tracking for human motion tracking and activity modeling and recognition. We develop a hierarchical modeling approach for multiple motions with multiple trajectories. Experiments show that tracking and recognition of complex motions like human actions can be facilitated by the developed approach. The proposed invariant trajectory descriptor exhibit many attractive properties such as noise insensitivity, computational locality, and uniqueness in representation, in addition to being invariant to transformation groups. This will benefit effective motion tracking and analysis.

118613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
118613.value: In this project, we studied the issues in motion sensing to provide efficient way for complex motion analysis and recognition. In studying compressive sensing, a sparse representation scheme is developed for motion sensing and tracking. As this method is insensitive to partial occlusions, a target can be effectively recovered from the corruptions. As a result, it provides a way to achieve robust tracking to enhance the tracking performance in many practical applications like security surveillance. The fringe projection method developed in 3D data acquisition provides a way for high accuracy 3D measurements. This method can be useful in general 3D measurement applications 3D object model acquisition. In studying human motion tracking, a hierarchical modeling approach is developed for motion trajectory description. This method has many attractive properties such as noise insensitivity, and uniqueness in representation. This method can be used for tracking complex motions like human actions, and will thus be useful for activity recognition and behavior monitoring in security surveillance. Furthermore, the motion description approach is useful in robot motion reproduction for auto-programming through learning by demonstration (LbD). We have plan to propose a following up project in this regard.

119213.value: 供應鏈治理與效益：交易前沿分析

119213.label: Project Objectives
119213.value: Develop a transaction-embedded supply chain frontier modeling framework to generate a unified measure which incorporates both production and transaction costs into supply chain efficiency assessment. Exemplified with a transaction-embedded manufacturer-retailer supply chain, we introduce inter-stage and inter-firm transaction of a supply chain, which is characterized by a transaction function with non-manufacturing transaction attributes as independent variables, as a “modulator” in between the manufacturer and the retailer. We examine and identify supply chain transaction attributes and characteristics, and obtain dynamics and analytics of supply chain transactions, including governance and organization structure (e.g. vertical integration and horizontal specialization) in terms of contract coordination, risk diversification, and infrastructure governance. Develop methodology of transaction embedded supply chain efficiency assessment under different two-stage supply chain governance structures and different contract structures. Expanding from current supply chain incentive literature (which is largely based on output factors, such as output quantity and selling price), we obtain supply chain coordination characteristics with the presence of inter-firm transaction costs, which are found to be non-smooth and nonlinear, with which we explain how transaction costs affect supply chain overall performance, in terms of coordination, productivity and governance efficiency. Conduct numerical and simulation tests to examine and verify how supply chain transaction costs together with production input factors affect supply chain composite frontier (which is defined as maximized production output with minimized production input costs plus transaction costs). We plan to conduct intensive and extensive simulation facilitated sensitivity analysis on how production input factors (e.g., material and utility prices) interact with supply chain composite frontier and then overall supply chain efficiency. Then, we run numerical tests to verify and validate the TESCF model with numerical comparisons on the impacts of different port (inter-stage) governance structures (e.g., centralized governance of Singapore Port versus decentralized governance of Hong Kong Port) on overall performance of a supply chain.

119213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
119213.value: We propose to advance a theory of supply chain transaction cost, which incorporates inter-stage transaction characteristics into supply chain coordination as a necessary measure of supply chain efficiency. Currently supply chain performance has been measured by firm-based output productivity conditioned on newsvendor-type supply chain coordination (e.g., coordination of supplier-manufacturer and manufacturer-retailer supply chains), largely leaving out the aspects of inter-stage transaction cost. According to transaction cost economics (TCE) by Williamson (2008), transaction cost constitutes an intrinsic measure of supply chain performance. For example, the cost of implementing a revenue-sharing contract, a form of transaction cost that is excluded from supply chain modeling, is found to be the key factor that has limited practical adoption of a coordinated revenue-sharing contract (e.g., Cachon and Lariviere 2005). On the other hand, a price-only retailer-supplier contract, which is shown to be non-coordinated, is popularly adopted in practice. It has been argued that these findings can be interpreted by inter-stage transaction costs, which will be theorized and characterized in the proposed project. Nevertheless, supply chain inter-stage performance depends on whether and how transaction costs, including that of logistics, infrastructure and governance, interact with production output measures. There is a critical need for a unified assessment framework of supply chain efficiency, with which the following research questions can be addressed: 1) how supply chain efficiency can be fully measured by a unified measure which incorporates both production and transaction costs into supply chain performance assessment; 2) how supply chain governance structure affects supply chain efficiency under different governance structures and different contract structures; 3) how supply chain transaction attributes, together with production input factors, affect supply chain composite frontier (which is defined as maximized production output as a function of minimized combined costs of production and transaction). We develop a transaction-embedded supply chain frontier (TESCF) model of a retailer-supplier supply chain, so as to address the research questions raised above. We begin with obtaining analytical properties and characteristics of TESCF model. Our initial analysis of the TESCF model indicates the non-smooth and nonlinear nature of supply chain transaction cost, concurring with the conjectures of transaction cost economics, to which rigorous derivations and characteristics will be obtained in this project. We then conduct extensive numerical tests to verify the TESCF model and its properties and characteristics. 我們提出一個供應鏈交易前沿的理論，將供應生產單位之間的交易特徵作為供應鏈效益的必要指標引入供應鏈的協調機制。而目前供應鏈績效的度量不包括供應單位之間的交易成本和相互關聯因素。根據Williamson (2008)提出的交易成本理論(TCE), 供應鏈運作中交易成本比不可少。比如，一個盈利分享供應鏈合同的實施中的財務監管審計成本（一種交易成本）在目前供應鏈模型中均未包括。然而在實際中這種成本有誰承擔的問題嚴重妨礙了合同的執行。 至今為止，還缺乏一個統一的供應鏈效益評審機制框架能解決以下關鍵研究問題：1）如何測量生產成本和交易成本對供應鏈效益的綜合影響；2）供應鏈治理結構在不同的合同結構下對供應鏈效益的影響；3）供應鏈中交易和生產的綜合優化結構如何設計和規劃？ 這就是本項目要研究解決的核心問題。 我們先建立一個包含交易的供應鏈前沿模型，並推導出其解析性質和特徵。由於供應鏈交易運作本身的離散和隨機性使得供應鏈前沿具有複雜的非平滑與非線性特徵，從而供應鏈前沿模型的解析求解難以獲得。我們計劃進一步研究推導出供應鏈生產-交易綜合前沿的動態機制和解析性質，並對其進行數值和計算分析、檢驗和實證。

119313.label: Realisation of objectives
119313.value: In this project, we propose to investigate the nature of tags and topics in UGO and develop new techniques for tagging UGO data. We have made significant progress in our research and have more than achieved what I had proposed in development of techniques for tagging data to enable users to share UGO. We have several papers published in leading international journals and conferences. For example, we have a a paper published a paper in Pattern recognition in which we reported our techniques for robust graph matching, and our paper on tagging of video sequences have been accepted by IEEE Trans. on Cybernetics. Our recent paper, "Story Co-Segmentation of Chinese Broadcast News Using Weakly-Supervised Semantic Similarity" is currently being revised for publication in IEEE Trans on Pattern Analysis and Machine Learning; in this paper we precent a tagging mechanism for Chinese broadcast news using MRF and weakly-supervised affinity graph model and have broken the ground for segmenting and tagging video contents. This paper presents lexical story segmentation, a new approach to automatically tagging stories on the same topic from multiple Chinese broadcast news documents. Unlike topic tracking and detection, our approach needs not the guidance of well-trained topic models and can consistently segment the common stories from input documents. We are able to extend the classical cosine similarity by mapping the observed words distribution into the latent semantic space, which leads to a generalized lexical cosine similarity measurement. Extensive experiments on benchmark dataset validate the effectiveness of our story tagging approach. Using deep learning we have also developed a motion modeling approach to analyzing video contents. We propose a heterogeneous multi-task learning framework for human pose tagging from monocular images using a deep convolutional neural network. This system learns human poses in a deep network architecture which in turn provides an effective motion tagging and categorization. This method is able to converge to a good solution. Our initial results have been very encouraging. We have reported our research results in International Journal of Computer Vision.

However, as it is well known throughout history that any invention was the result of seemingly simple twiggings, from the first wheels to Google. I'm now applying for several patents with a main focus on commercial development of intelligent, automated tagging of user data which provides hierarchical tagging information seamlessly associating user data over a plethora of and widely different memory formats and devices, and computational platforms, most notably, data centers and cloud. With this approached and many other new ideas that I have proposed recently will help ameliorate user experience in the big data era.

119313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
119313.value: Just about everyone these days has huge data that are scattered over numerous very confusing, transparent, magic, and occasionally mythical places on earth; and the matter has become dramatically serious. Although you are more likely feeling happy with the search results provided by Google, you would be most likely frustrated finding yourself spending long hours trying to figure out some data that you think you have somewhere in the magic box somewhere around the cloud or in one of your devices, the feeling of being lost in your own data is like the feeling of the digital Alzheimer: the more you store the more you find yourself at a loss, and you store more, ad infinitum. This project is an initial investigation to use advanced techniques in machine intelligence to develop a functional system for automatically tagging user data, which will help the user navigate aimfully and effectively in the labyrinth of the data so that the user, YOU, may feel emancipated from the tyrant of your own data.

Knowledge-based event reasoning: Developing techniques for the online detection of complex and generic events on large Internet video recordings. The key issues include the knowledge-based modeling, reasoning, and indexing of events from a large number of imperfectly detected concepts for videos. Recounting of video content: Researching techniques for the automatic generation of textual and visual descriptions that evidence the presence of an event in a video clip. System development: Developing a framework that demonstrates the scalable detection of previously unknown events in videos with recounting capability.

120213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
120213.value: With the massive growth of Internet videos, intensive research efforts have been devoted to concept annotation, particularly the learning of audio-visual classifiers for annotating video archives with textual words (or semantic concepts). Based on the current technologies, indexing a video archive with hundreds of elementary concepts for text-to-video search in a narrow domain (e.g., for broadcast videos) and with some restrictions (e.g., only handle queries with text words that are not out of concept vocabulary) is feasible, as evidenced by the annual TRECVID benchmark evaluation. Despite the progress, querying videos with text words beyond concept atoms, for example an event of making a cake, in a large Internet video archive remains a difficult problem. The challenge comes from the fact that the event is generic – a general description that can refer to wide varieties of cakes and ways of making them, and complex – involving activities such as flouring, baking, and freezing. Training an event-specific classifier for “making a cake” is difficult unless there are abundant training examples that adequately cover all cases; and more importantly it is not scalable with the fact that Internet videos can contain any possible scenes and events. With most Internet videos uploaded together with the amateur tags, the difficulty of answering event-oriented queries could be lower. However, the amateur-tags are used to be error-prone and not specific. Searching generic events based on textual tags is known to be limited – in the way that it becomes the users’ responsibilities to explore the long list of returned videos for getting the right hits. This project aims to address two challenges: event detection – identify videos and localize the segments containing events that are previously unknown by a search system; event recounting – narrate the audio-visual evidences of how a video relates to an event by generating short textual descriptions with illustrative thumbnails. The former addresses an issue of modeling and reasoning of event knowledge from a large number of noisily tagged concepts, while the latter explicates the reasoning process to textual sentences. The major goal is to research techniques that enable the search of complex and generic events that beyond the current concept classifier learning can handle, and recount the reasoning process for fast video browsing that beyond the current video summarization techniques can offer. Both issues are of great value to Internet video searching and content monitoring. 隨著網絡視頻的迅猛增長，大量的研究精力投入在了概念標註上，特別是通過學習聽覺-視覺分類器來用文本（或語義概念）標註視頻的方法。基於目前的技術和TRECVID年度評價基準，用數百個基本概念在一個狹小的領域（例如，廣播視頻）索引視頻資料，有限制地（比如，只處理詞典中文本的查詢）進行“文本-視頻”搜索是可行的。 儘管取得了一些進展，然而對大規模網絡視頻檔案，用原子概念以外的文本進行視頻檢索，例如製作蛋糕，仍然是一個困難的問題。其主要挑戰來自事件的通用性：通用的事件描述可以指代多種蛋糕和不同製作方法；事件的複雜性：即使簡單事件也可能涉及復雜的過程，如磨粉，烘烤，以及凍結。除非有大量並且完備的訓練實例，否則為每個事件（比如，製作蛋糕）單獨訓練分類器是非常困難的；更重要的是，這種方法不具有擴展性，因為網絡視頻可能包含任意的場景和事件。對於大量在上傳時就有業餘標籤的網絡視頻，處理面向事件的查詢難度會低一些。然而，這些業餘標籤很容易出錯，而且往往不夠具體。利用文本標籤搜索一般性事件是有限的，用戶必須從冗長的返回結果中找到他們想要的視頻。本項目旨在解決兩方面的挑戰：事件檢測，找到相關視頻並定位事件發生的片段；事件敘述：用簡短的文本和縮略圖說明返回的視聽資料如何與查詢的事件相關。前者需要基於大量嘈雜概念標註進行建模和推理，而後者則以文本句子的形式闡明這個過程。本項目主要研究目前概念分類器學習不能處理的複雜通用事件搜索技術，以及當前視頻歸納技術難以提供的快速視頻瀏覽與敘述技術。這兩者在網絡視頻搜索和內容監控上都很有價值。

120213.label: Realisation of objectives
120213.value: This project aims to address issues in large-scale multimedia event detection and recounting. The scenarios being considered include 100-example, few-example and zero-example event detection. The main studies include object pooling techniques [MTA 2016, TMM 2018] and blind late fusion [IJMIR 2016] for event detection, and evidential localization for event recounting. Most of the experiments are conducted on TRECVid MED datasets, which consist of more than 8,000 hours of videos. We have actively participated in TRECVid benchmarking evaluation during years 2014 to 2016, yielding excellent performances in both multimedia event detection and recounting [TRECVid 2014-2016]. Objective-1: Large-scale elementary concept learning We started the project by constructing our home-made concept bank, where the concepts were crawled from ConceptNet ontology based on the events pre-defined by TRECVid MED and MediaEval Affect task. With these concepts, we studied issues in sampling of training examples and learning of classifiers. The training examples were obtained from three major sources: Flickr, YouTube and the research collection provided by TRECVid. The selection of training examples was conducted semi-automatically, where human operators were involved in verifying the sample labels automatically tagged by machines. With the examples, our major effort is devoted to address the problem of cross-domain data shift, by leveraging the knowledge graph mined from ConceptNet to holistically adjust the output scores of classifiers based on their contextual relationships. The adjustment of concepts was formulated as an optimization problem based on CRF (conditional random field). Using the refined concept scores, we further trained SVM for event detection [IJMIR 2016]. Later, due to advancement of deep learning and availability of large concept banks such as ImageNet, we switched our focus on leveraging of large concept banks for learning event classifiers. The concept banks include SIN-346 and RC-497 based on two development sets released by TRECVid, ImageNet-100 and ImageNet-Shuffle-12998, FCVID-239 and Sport-487, and Places-205. In total, these banks form more than fifteen thousand concepts of different granularities (low, mid and high-level concepts) covering objects, scenes and actions. As the concept banks are with different natures, the classifiers are trained using different techniques including ResNet-50, GoogLeNet, 3D convolutional network and SVM. In addition, different features such as fc7 and pool5 spatio-temporal features are extracted from the networks for event classification. Objective-2: Knowledge-based event reasoning Different techniques were developed depending on scenarios. For 100-example and 10-example event detection, our studies were mainly to address the issue of object composition and interaction. As most approaches directly extract and pool frame-level features from deep convolutional network (DCNN) for classifier learning, rich object information is overlooked or even omitted during this process. This is mainly because DCNN is trained with single-label classification and tends to highlight only the largest object in a frame. To deal with this problem, we first proposed object-level pooling technique by detecting regional objects from frames based on selective search algorithm. Each object is then scaled and fed into DCNN for the extraction of fc7 features. Object information is modeled by max pooling of features across objects and frames [MTA 2016]. In the experiment, our technique outperformed both frame-level pooling and spatial-pyramid pooling. Later, instead of adopting max pooling of fc7 features, we studied VLAD for more effective coding of object composition. Specifically, pool5 features which spatially correspond to the receptive fields of video frames are extracted for encoding. A pyramid of features is sampled from pool-5 layer and then encoded with VLAD for SVM classifier learning. The technique is named as Object-VLAD for VLAD encoding of regional objects [TMM 2018]. In the experiment, Object-VLAD significantly outperformed state-of-the-arts techniques, including VideoStory, on MED-2014 dataset for both 100- and 10-example detection. The major problem of Object-VLAD is speed efficiency because every regional object needs to be fed into DCNN for feature extraction. We have studied RPN (regional proposal network) for this problem, where feature map is shared by multiple objects in a frame. The new technique is about 18 times more efficient than Object-VLAD in the expense of detection accuracy which drops by 2% of absolute mAP. As there are no training examples in zero-example detection, the techniques rely heavily on reasoning based on knowledge graphs (i.e., ConceptNet and WordNet) and concept banks. We formulated the problem as query-to-concept mapping, where the task is to reason relevant concepts that jointly interpret the meaning of query for event detection. Different from conventional ad-hoc video search, unfortunately, knowledge graphs are not always helpful and instead introduce noisy concepts. Furthermore, the number of concepts being selected for query interpretation can significantly affect detection performance. We studied two approaches to deal with these problems. The first approach is by evidential pooling of clips (or shots) for measuring the similarity between a video and query event. Specifically, the idea is to localize clips that show evidences of event from a lengthy video and involve only these clips in query answering. The approach was found to be effective in suppressing wrongly selected concepts, making the results insensitive to the number of selected concepts [ICMR 2016]. The second approach is by word2vec representation of query and selected concepts. Specifically, a new approach, named as incremental word2vec, was proposed to incrementally add concepts to word2vec representation till query is optimally interpreted. The approach can also effectively deal with query drift problem and reported the best result on MED-14 dataset [ToMM 2017]. Objective-3: Recounting of video content We proposed three techniques for video recounting: sentence generation based on knowledge graph [IJMIR 2014], visual snippet narration based on Object-VLAD [TMM 2018] and evidential localization [ICMR 2016]. The first approach is based on a knowledge graph extracted from ConceptNet, which provides 26 of different relationships to connect different concepts (e.g., verb, noun) into parse trees. Based on a set of predefined grammar rules, parse trees are merged for sentence generation. The second approach is based on Object-VLAD where a decoder is designed to extract salient information from VLAD encoding as evidential frames and objects to explain why a video is retrieved. The third approach is directly based on localization of evidential clips for recounting, and the study focus is on the minimal number of clips and frames required to explain search results and enhance user browsing experience. The experiments shown that Object-VLAD is effective in retrieving evidential frames compared to other existing techniques. Objective-4: System development Based on the work done, we have developed a system pipeline for participation of TRECVid MED and MER tasks during years 2014-2016. The system considers not only deep visual features, but also hand-crafted motion trajectories, speech, OCR and audio signals. Comprehensive study was conducted to evaluate the performance of late fusion of multi-modal features on this task [IJMIR 2016]. The ability to leverage multi-modality features with right fusion strategy led us to be the top-1 performing team in TRECVid 2015 MED 100-example, 10-example and zero-example tasks. With the employment of Object-VLAD in the system, we continued to be the top-2 performing team in the predefined and ad-hoc MED tasks of TRECVid 2016. In addition, we also achieved good performance in video recounting, where our result was rated as top-2 for the measure “evidence quality” in the subjective evaluation of TRECVid 2014. Due to strong performance, we were selected for orally presenting our works in TRECVid workshop during years 2014 to 2016.

120213.label: Major findings and research outcome
120213.value: A challenge in this project is modeling of object composition and their interaction in a lengthy video for event detection and recounting. We approached this problem from rich multi-modal features to rich semantic concepts and to object information. Multi-modal features are known to complement with each other in boosting search performance. Nevertheless, integration of features by itself is a problem and improper fusion can easily cause performance fluctuation. Our study on blind late fusion led to the proposal of JRER measure for this problem [IJMIR 2016]. Through intensive simulation, we concluded that JRER is a robust fusion method for 100-example event detection task. The limitation of multi-modal features is that most features are hand-crafted, for example, SIFT and improved motion trajectory (IDT). The extraction of these features, especially IDT, is computationally very expensive. Convolutional neural network (CNN) bring news thought to this problem. CNN scales up the number of concept classifiers to tens of thousands and the extraction of features is efficient for classifier learning. The performance using 15K concept classifiers based on CNN alone is already close to the fusion result of all multi-modality features. The proposal of Object-VLAD [TMM 2018] led to even higher performance where single feature based on ImageNet-1000 concepts outperforms all the approaches implemented throughout the projects in both 100-example and 10-example scenarios. The advantage of Object-VLAD is that the encoded feature can be easily decoded for video recounting. Nevertheless, feature encoding in Object-VLAD is considered computational expensive. The recent work based on RPN has significantly sped up feature encoding with slight sacrifice in detection accuracy. The main problem of zero-example detection is query drift, which results in the research question of how to decide the right number of concepts for query interpretation. In this project, we have successfully proposed two effective algorithms, evidential pooling and incremental word2vec, to deal with the query drift problem. The key idea of evidential pooling is to localize a small number of evidential clips for feature pooling, which alleviates the negative effect caused by contextually relevant but non-evidential concepts. The evidential clips can also be directly used as visual snippets for event recounting. The drawback of evidential pooling is heavy memory consumption due to the requirement of frame-level concept indexing. Incremental word2vec is a more efficient way of dealing with query drift problem and led to state-of-the-art performance on MED-2014 dataset. However, the result is not interpretable for event recounting.

120213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
120213.value: Object relationship: The current project encodes object composition and interaction in videos, but the relationship between objects are not explicitly modeled. Consequently, near-miss events are difficult to be distinguished based on the current approach. Considering object relation for event detection is intuitive. By the time when this project was carried out, the challenge comes from the lack of training data to model the spatio-temporal interaction between objects. Until very recently, several large datasets are publicly released for visual relation detection. Utilizing these datasets for encoding of object interaction is a promising research direction. Cross-modal attention and embedding: The zero-example detection is based on the methodology of query-to-concept mapping. An advantage is that search result is interpretable, by showing the evidences that concepts are present. An alternative way is by mapping videos and queries into a shared embedding space. Along the learning of embedding space, attention mechanism can be injected to adaptively highlight query-relevant content and make search result explainable. In a recent experiment, we have shown that embedding feature manages to outperform query-to-concept mapping when there are sufficient training examples for certain types of queries. Therefore, it is worth exploring the pros and cons of both methodologies for this problem.

120213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
120213.value: The project has successfully addressed the challenge of multimedia event detection and recounting in a large video archive of more than 8,000 hours of videos. The project has developed various techniques for three detection scenarios: 100-example, 10-example and 0-example. Particularly, Object-VLAD, which effectively encodes object composition in a video, shows superior detection performance in both 100-example and 10-example event detection. The encoded feature can be efficiently unrolled to provide evidence for video event recounting. A faster version of Object-VLAD is also developed, which is 38 times faster with slight sacrifice in detection accuracy. In 0-example event detection, two new techniques, evidential pooling and incremental word2vec, were developed to address the query drift problem – a fundamental problem in the search paradigm of query-to-concept mapping. The outcome is that, by evidential pooling, the detection result is less sensitive to the number of selected concepts. A by-product is that the result is explainable by showing clips where concepts present. Incremental word2vec leverages the latest deep learning result for optimal way of selecting concepts, which show state-of-the-art result for zero-example event detection. Finally, the works developed from this project have demonstrated strong performance in TRECVid video benchmarking activities during years 2014 to 2016.

120413.label: Realisation of objectives
120413.value: Three-dimensional (3D) microsystems were designed and fabricated with different dimensions, layouts, and interconnecting ports for cell migration study. Reversal nanoimprint technology was developed with simultaneous ultra violet exposure and surface treatments for molds and substrates for the 3D platforms. The migration of adherent cells has been demonstrated to be influenced by surface topography of substrates. However, the knowledge on cell migration directionality is limited. We have developed patterns that can affect the direction of cell migration. Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) patterns consisting of dots, gratings, and semicircles were fabricated in Si and transferred onto PDMS substrates. The results indicate that MC3T3-E1 mouse osteoblast cell migration directionality can be controlled by the designed patterns. Cells elongated and aligned with the gratings, and the migration paths of the cells appeared to be guided by the grating pattern. Interestingly, more than 88% of the cells cultured on these patterns were observed to reverse their migration directions at least once during the 16 h examination period. Most of the reversal events occurred at the corners and the ends of the pattern, suggesting these localized topographical features induce an abrupt loss in directional persistence. Moreover, the cell speed was observed to increase temporarily right after each directional reversal. Focal adhesion complexes were more well-established in cells on the angular gratings than on flat surfaces, but the formation of filipodia appeared to be imbalanced at the corners and the ends, possibly leading to the loss of directional persistence. This study describes the first engineered cell culture surface that consistently induces changes in the directional persistence of adherent cells. This will provide an experimental model for the study of this phenomenon and a valuable platform to control the cell motility and directionality, which can be used for cell screening and selection. Asymmetrical patterns in the cell culture substrates were used to control cell migration behaviors. Three patterns, named “Squares”, “Grating”, and “Arcs” were fabricated, representing different levels of rotational asymmetry. Using time-lapse imaging, we systematically compared the motility and directionality of mouse osteoblastic cells MC3T3-E1 cultured on these patterns. Cells were found to move progressively faster on “Arcs” than on “Grating”, and cells on “Squares” were the slowest, suggesting that cell motility correlates with the level of rotational asymmetry of the repeating units of the pattern. Among these three patterns, on the “Arcs” pattern, the least symmetrical one, cells not only moved with the highest velocity but also the strongest directional persistence. Although this enhanced motility was not associated with the detected number of focal adhesion sites in the cells, the pattern asymmetry was reflected in the asymmetrical cell spreading. Cells on the “Arcs” pattern consistently displayed larger cytoplasmic protrusion on one side of the cell. This asymmetry in cell shape determined the direction and speed of cell migration. These observations suggest that topographical patterns that enhance the imbalance between the leading and trailing fronts of adherent cells will increase cell speed and control movement directions. Our discovery shows that complex cell behaviors such as the direction of cell movement are influenced by simple geometrical principles, which can be utilized as the design foundation for platforms that guide and sort cultured cells. On a microgrooved substrate, cells migrate along the pattern, and at random positions, reverse their directions. We have demonstrated that these reversals can be controlled by introducing discontinuities to the pattern. On “V-shaped grating patterns”, mouse osteogenic progenitor MC3T3-E1 cells reversed predominately at the bends and the ends. The patterns were engineered in a way that the combined effects of angle- and length-dependence could be examined in addition to their individual effects. Results show that when the bend was placed closer to one end, migration behaviour of cells depends on their direction of approach. At an obtuse bend (135°), more cells reversed when approaching from the long segment than from the short segment. But at an acute bend (45°), this relationship was reversed. Based on this anisotropic behaviour, the designed patterns effectively allowed cells to move in one direction but blocked migrations in the opposing direction. This study demonstrates that by the strategic placement of bends and ends on grating patterns, we can engineer effective unidirectional switching gates that can control the movement of adherent cells. The knowledge developed in this study could be utilised in future cell sorting or filtering platforms without the need for chemotaxis or microfluidic control.

120413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
120413.value: Regulated cell migration is an essential process in multicellular organisms. For instance, embryonic development is accompanied by precisely controlled collective cell movements. The migration of cancer cells within the tumor microenvironment plays crucial roles in metastasis, and the therapeutic interventions of these cell movements can prevent cancer cells from spreading. In this project, we developed and fabricated a series of related topographical patterns on a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) surface with different degrees of rotational symmetry, dimensions, and layouts. These patterns were of such a dimension that cells were not entrapped in valleys between the repeating units. The migration behaviors of mouse osteoblastic MC3T3-E1 cells on these patterns were systematically analyzed. Detailed characterizations of cell migration speed, direction, path, area, and organization of focal adhesions (FAs) and cytoskeletons on these patterned platforms were reported. As complex cell behaviours are influenced by engineered platforms with different patterns, the results could be utilised as the design foundation for platforms that guide and sort cultured cells.

120513.label: Project Title(Chinese)
120513.value: 命名數據網絡的線速數據包處理

120513.label: Project Objectives
120513.value: Design memory efficient hardware-based name tables to support packet forwarding in the Named Data Networking architecture. Design real-time name lookup methods. Design efficient procedures to handle update requests to the name tables.
rows: Design memory efficient hardware-based name tables to support packet forwarding in the Named Data Networking architecture.
Design efficient procedures to handle update requests to the name tables.

120513.label: Realisation of objectives
120513.value: The three objectives of this research project are fully achieved. There are three major issues in the name lookup in NDN packet processing. 1. Names can have arbitrary length. Hence, name lookup is more complex than the conventional IP-address lookup where an IP address has fixed length. 2. The sizes of the name tables in NDN routers are much larger than the IP forwarding table in conventional TCP/IP router. The expected sizes of the FIB, PIT and CS tables are multiple millions, whereas the size of today’s IP forwarding table is about 0.5 million entries. 3. NDN requires stateful packet processing, i.e. the processing of an incoming packet depends on the packets that have previously arrived at the router. As a result the PIT and CS tables require per-packet update. We have designed high-speed and memory efficient hardware architectures for the implementation of the FIB, PIT and CS tables. We obtain a FIB with 10 M name prefixes from Tsinghua University. A hardware FIB lookup engine has been designed that can achieve lookup rate of 98.6 million searches per second. This lookup rate is much better than previous results that can achieve lookup rate of 34 to 63 million searches per second. Another advantage of our method is that incremental updates to the FIB will not interrupt on-going lookup operations. In the previous methods, lookup operations need to be suspended during FIB updates. One of the major challenges of the hardware lookup engine for PIT and CS tables is that the system should support per-packet update. We have also proposed to add one more lookup table in the hardware accelerator called the name ID table (nidT). The nidT stores all the name IDs of the pending interest packets in the PIT. When a new interest packet is received and the requested object name can be found in the nidT, then the router can find out the forwarding decision without looking up the FIB. The design of the CS tables is closely related to the hardware architecture of the cache store. A two-level cache architecture has been proposed. The leve-1 (L1) cache is implemented using high speed DRAM, and the level-2 (L2) cache is implemented using large capacity solid state drive (SSD). The L1 and L2 caches have separate lookup tables. The L1 CS table is fully integrated with the PIT, and the L2 CS table is integrated with the nidT. This design option can reduce hardware implementation cost, and streamlines the overall packet processing.

120513.label: Major findings and research outcome
120513.value: One journal paper has been published, and a second journal paper is under review. W. Yu, D. Pao, “Hardware accelerator to speed up packet processing in NDN router”, Computer Communications, Vol. 91-92, pp. 109-119, Oct. 2016. W. Yu and D. Pao, “Hardware accelerator for FIB lookup in Named Data Networking”, Microprocessors and Microsystems, under review, 2018. We have designed hardware accelerators to speed up packet processing in high-speed NDN router. We can only find 1 published paper on the hardware implementation of FIB lookup. However, the authors of that paper have not provided the details of their FPGA design, implementation parameters, and analysis of the lookup rate. In this research, we have designed a hardware FIB lookup engine. For proof of concept, our method is implemented on a virtex-7 FPGA. Implementation details and performance analysis are given. The lookup rate of our method is 98.6 million packets per second (MPPS), which is much higher than other published methods. Our method supports incremental updates to the FIB without interrupting the on-going lookup operations. The lookup rates of previous methods using multithreading techniques or GPU are between 34 MPPS and 63 MPPS. A disadvantage of software methods, in particular GPU based methods, is that lookup operations need to be suspended during FIB updates. Hence, the actual lookup rate may be considerably lower than the peak lookup rate. Our proposed hardware design of the PIT and CS tables is the first hardware-based implementation method. The major challenge of the design of PIT and CS tables is the per-packet update requirement. In general, the lookup tables are pre-computed and uploaded to the hardware device. As a result, the update rate is very limited. In our method, the controller only needs to submit an update command with the data item to be inserted or deleted from the hardware table to the FPGA. The hardware will carry out the required operations without automatically. Moreover, the update operations will not interrupt the on-going lookup operations. Previous studies that use software implementation can only achieve packet processing rate of below 2 MPPS. Our method can sustain a throughput of about 60 MPPS. This improvement is very significant.

120513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
120513.value: One of the distinctive features of NDN that may potentially offer great improvement in communication efficiency is the provision of in-network caching. Data packets retrieval in NDN is name-based. This means that data traffic in the network can be cached in the local CS of network nodes, and the cached data packets can be used to satisfy future requests in a much faster manner. It is generally believed that the required size of the CS is in the order of TB. A CS with multiple TB capacity can only be implemented using 2-level memory architecture based on today’s memory technology. The I/O bandwidth of the secondary storage device is much lower than the aggregated data rate of a high-speed router. The operation characteristics of the storage device would demand a centralized caching strategy to be used. To make the best utilization of the in-network cache, the content provider needs a good strategy to decide how to allocate the contents to the CS of network nodes. This would be an important topic for future research.

120513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
120513.value: Named Data Networking (NDN) is a promising information-centric network architecture for the future generation Internet. Since the inception of the idea in 2010, NDN has attracted significant attention from the computer network community. Numerous research studies on various aspects of NDN have generated very fruitful results. Software testbed and prototypes have been made available for research and development. However, research study on the hardware design of high speed NDN router is still in the infant stage. Our research makes significant contribution to the physical realization of NDN network. We address the key issues of packet processing in high-speed NDN routers. Design of the lookup tables in NDN router is much more difficult than the counterpart in TCP/IP router. The sizes, variable-length search keys, and per-packet updates to the lookup table are the major issues that the hardware design needs to overcome. Our method for FIB lookup out performs other published methods. Our design is the first hardware-based implementation of the PIT and CS lookup tables published in the literature.
