120813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
120813.value: In the past two decades, bulk metallic glass (BMG) has gradually evolved from a scientific curiosity to a family of engineering materials which possess unique combinations of properties and find applications as functional materials as well as structural materials. Such developments are resulted from numerous empirical investigations of properties augmented by innovations in the processing technologies which make full use of the casting and thermal plastic behaviours of BMG. Recently, with the better understanding of the size-dependent properties of BMG, applications on length scales from 1 nm to several mm, such as micro-electromechanical systems (MEMS), etc., are considered the most promising. The principal investigator (PI) of this proposed research noticed that the possibility of high throughput and low cost production of systems or components in such length scales by thermal plastic forming makes BMG especially suitable for making terahertz passive components. Terahertz technology is a rapidly developing field and brings applications like high precision spectrum detection, super resolution imaging, and high performance communication, etc. Terahertz radiation lies between infrared and microwaves and has wavelength in the order of 10 μm to mm. Passive devices for guiding and manipulating THz radiation therefore contain features in similar length scales. Currently, most of such devices are fabricated by micromachining of silicon or by moulding of polymer. Silicon devices are brittle and the process is expensive, while the long-term dimensional stability of polymers is not satisfactory. We therefore propose to develop the thermal plastic processing technology for producing high aspect ratio structures with BMG with the precision necessary for high performance terahertz devices. Another challenge for thermal plastic forming of BMG is to produce nanoscale surface patterns or structures on a metallic glass thin film. If that can be done with high precision and good reproducibility, the complex procedures involving photolithography for producing nano-electromechanical systems (NAMS) may be replaced by the relatively simple process of nano-imprinting of metallic glass thin film. The second objective of this proposed research is therefore to develop a reliable and reproducible nano-imprinting process for MG thin film. Both of these proposed objective will have tremendous potential for application but they are hitherto not investigated and reported extensively. When this proposed project is successfully completed, it is anticipated that the thermal plastic processing windows for some suitable metallic glass materials will be unambiguously identified for producing practical terahertz devices with BMG and for imprinting nanostructures on metallic glass thin films. 近年隨著對大塊金屬玻璃的特性跟尺寸的關連加深了認識，將金屬玻璃應用到微機械系統吸引到科研及工程界更多關注。此外，利用熱塑性加工技術，可以發展出高效率及低成本的方法將金屬玻璃生產出太赫兹（terahertz)頻譜的器件。太赫兹科技為一急速發展的範疇。由它引申出來的應用包括高精度光譜儀，超高解像影像系統以及高速通訊技術等。太赫兹輻射介乎紅外線與微波之間，而波長為10微米至數毫米。相關器件之特徵長度亦在同一範圍。這類器件現時主要以矽或塑料製造。但矽非常易碎而且加工方法昂貴。而塑料長期的穩定性不理想。所以我們在這研究計劃建議用金屬玻璃通過熱塑性加工去製造形狀尺寸及精度都符合太赫玆應用要求的器件。假若進展順利，研究組會嘗試在金屬玻璃薄膜上壓印出微機械系統，並確定可行的加工參數範圍。這兩組技術將會有極大應用前景，並能令金屬玻璃有更廣的應用。

120813.label: Realisation of objectives
120813.value: During the project period, the PI and the research team carried out systematic experiments on fabrication of BMG devices with geometry suitable for terahertz or sub-terahertz applications. The materials properties of BMG and metallic glass thin film samples subjected to thermo-mechanical treatments similar to those for thermoplastic forming were characterized. The details of the work done for realization of the project objective are described in the following. Based on published data of optical properties of metals [1] and the geometry of viable terahertz high-pass filters [2], a device geometry, which was expected to exhibit characteristics of a high-pass filter, was designed and fabricated with Zr55Cu30Al10Ni5 BMG. The process involved both suction casting and thermoplastic forming of the BMG alloy. The BMG filter faithfully reproduced the geometry of the copper mould cavities array. The fabrication method is much easier and at substantially lower cost compared with the current techniques involving inductively-coupled plasma dry etching technology. The surface finish is comparable to or better than that of Si filter. The silicon filters are typically very fragile, whereas BMG filter has higher strength and toughness. The scanning electron micrographs of the copper mould cavities, the BMG filter we fabricated and the model Si filter are shown at the end of this report. These works were done to address Objective 1. [1] M. A. Ordal, R. J. Bell, R. W. Alexander Jr, L. L. Long, and M. R. Querry, Applied Optics 26, 744-752 (1987) [2] Y. C. Chen, T. R. Tsai, J. P. Chu, H. Sung, J. S. Jang, and H. Kato, Applied physics express 5, 012201 (2012) Zr46Ti26Ni28 thin film metallic glass (TFMG) samples on glass were prepared by sputtering. The effects of annealing on mechanical properties of the TFMG were studied using nanoindentation, nanoscratch and Rockwell indentation tests. The hardness of the TFMG increased with annealing due to formation of nanocrystals. The thin film exhibited good adhesive strength and scratch resistance annealing. The Zr–Ti–Ni thin film metallic glass is potentially suitable for applications in high strength micro parts and protective coating. The results obtained also helped to define the processing window for thermoplastic forming of the TFMG. This part of the work was done to address Objective 2. Several promising Zr-based BMGs and Mg-based BMG were prepared and tested under conditions similar to those for thermoplastic forming. If the thermoplastic fabrication processes for the devices can be carried out in air instead of vacuum or protective atmosphere, the cost can be substantially reduced. Furthermore, Mg-based BMGs have lower glass transition temperatures than those of Zr-based ones, and this feature will facilitate easier thermoplastic forming. The high temperature deformation behaviours of Mg67Zn28Ca5 metallic glass and its composites were studied. Glassy Mg67Zn28Ca5 exhibits the best superplasticity and thermal stability compared to its devitrified composites. These results help to define the processing window for thermoplastic forming of the Mg-based BMG and its composites. The oxidation at or around glass transition temperature as well as aqueous corrosion behaviour of several promising silver-doped Zr-based BMGs were studied. Alloying with silver improved the corrosion resistance substantially but it slightly accelerated oxidation in air at temperatures around Tg. Minor Ag-alloying in Zr-based BMG may be suitable for thermoplastic forming and is highly resistant to environmental attack during processing and applications. These two sets of experiments were done to address Objective 3. The results of the above research activities are described in more details in Section 6.1 and published in SCI journals as well as reported in a conference, as detailed in Section 8 and 9. All the objectives had been thoroughly addressed and achieved completely.

120813.label: Major findings and research outcome
120813.value: Mg-based BMGs typically have lower Tg (~ 400K) compared with Zr-based ones (~ 750K). This feature may facilitate easier thermoplastic forming. The high temperature deformation behaviours of Mg67Zn28Ca5 metallic glass and its composites were studied. The strain rate sensitivity m for Mg-based BMG can approach 1, but all the composites have lower strain rate sensitivity (0.17). Glassy Mg67Zn28Ca5 exhibits the best superplasticity and thermal stability compared to its devitrified composites. These results help to define the processing window for thermoplastic forming of the Mg-based BMG and its composites. The results were published in an international refereed journal (item 1 in Part C, Section 8). The oxidation at or around glass transition temperature as well as aqueous corrosion behaviour of several promising Zr-based BMGs were studied. The addition of silver into a ternary Zr-Co-Al BMG was found to improve the corrosion resistance substantially but it slightly accelerated oxidation in air at temperatures around Tg. The results indicated that there is an optimal amount of silver that can be added to the Zr-based BMG in order to form an alloy that is suitable for thermoplastic forming and is highly resistant to environmental attack during processing and applications. The results were published in an international refereed journal (item 2 in Part C, Section 8). The effects of annealing on mechanical properties of Zr46Ti26Ni28 thin film metallic glass were studied using nanoindentation, nanoscratch and Rockwell indentation tests. Its hardness progressively increased from 6.2 GPa to 11.1 GPa when annealed at 450 ºC. It also exhibited good adhesive strength and scratch resistance after the annealing treatment at 400 ºC. The annealing-induced nanocrystals contributed to the superior mechanical properties. The Zr–Ti–Ni thin film metallic glass is potentially suitable for applications in high strength micro parts and protective coating. The results were published in an international refereed journal (item 3 in Part C, Section 8). Owing to some communication problems with the collaborators in Taiwan, the acknowledgement to the RGC was missing in this paper. Since the function of terahertz devices depend on the electrical and/or magnetic properties of the materials, the PI therefore also worked on the correlation between the composition and the atomic scale cluster structures as well as the magnetic properties of Co-based BMGs. It was found that BMGs with even minor composition differences could exhibit substantial differences in properties, including magnetic properties. The results were presented in an international conference. (Part C, Section 9) Based on published data of optical properties of metals and the geometry of viable terahertz high-pass filters, a device geometry, which was expected to exhibit characteristics of a high-pass filter, was designed and fabricated with Zr55Cu30Al10Ni5 BMG. The process involved both suction casting and thermoplastic forming of the BMG alloy. The BMG filter faithfully reproduced the geometry, with rather high aspect ratio, of the copper mould cavities array. The fabrication method is much easier and faster than silicon wet etching and the surface finish is comparable to or better than that of Si filter. The silicon filters are typically very fragile, whereas BMG filter has higher strength and toughness. The results have not yet been published and the PI is considering patent application for the fabrication processes.

120813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
120813.value: From the outcomes of the project, there are several aspects that can be further developed or explored. The results on the thermal stability, oxidation resistance and thermoplastic behaviours of several series of BMG revealed that the alloy systems were viable for fabrication of micro- or nanoscale devices through thermoplastic processes. In order for the alloys to be adopted for fabrication of terahertz devices, investigation of the optical properties, viz. the electromagnetic properties of the alloys in the terahertz range, must be conducted to provide key materials characteristics for optical devices design. Furthermore, the fabrication processes described in the last section can be further developed for producing other terahertz devices with more complex geometry. Another possible development of the research is the integration of such devices into micro-electromechanical systems through thermoplastic forming, which is a much cheaper and faster process compared with chemical or ion etching methods, of components on metallic glass thin film.

120813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
120813.value: Terahertz technology is a rapidly developing field and brings applications like high precision spectrum detection, super resolution imaging, and high-performance communication, etc. Currently, most of such devices, which have features with high-aspect ratio, are fabricated by micromachining of silicon or by moulding of polymer. Silicon devices are brittle and the process is expensive, while the long-term dimensional stability of polymers is not satisfactory. The PI of this project developed the thermal plastic processing technology for producing high aspect ratio structures with BMG with the precision necessary for high performance terahertz devices. In this project, several bulk metallic glass alloy series were prepared and were through treatments similar to those involved in thermoplastic forming. The resulting structures and properties were characterized so that the viable processing window were identified. In order that the forming technology could be applied to thin film metallic glass as well, similar sets of experiments were also carried out for a series of thin film metallic glass deposited on glass substrate by sputtering. The results were useful for development of components in micro-electromechanical systems. In a nutshell, the results obtained in this project can contribute to the low-cost manufacturing of terahertz devices and will help the advancement as well as widespread applications of the related technologies.

121513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
121513.value: Dielectrophoresis (DEP) is regarded as one of the most non-invasive mechanisms for batch manipulation of dielectric particles. In this proposed project, we will conduct a dielectrophoresis research beyond the two-dimensional lab-on-a-chip spatial environment and investigate an automated technique for batch manipulation of cells for constructing intricate, three-dimensional (3D) cellular patterns with a novel electrode-integrated structure. The proposed spatial cell manipulation and microassembly technique will permit the development of 3D cell structures fulfilling both the physical (e.g. cell density and defined 3D geometry) and the biological (e.g. cell viability) requirements, which is currently a great technical challenge in the field of tissue engineering. The following three important issues will be addressed in this proposed research. First, we will design a multi-layer, multi-electrode structure that will enable effective biological cell assembly. Through modeling and computational analysis, we can optimize the design parameters of the 3D electrode architecture and its micro-electrode layers and thereby, the resulting electric field gradient for automated spatial manipulation of cells. Second, we will implement a microfabrication technique to construct the multi-layer electrode structure with high design complexity. This electrode must be fabricated from a bio-compatible, yet conductive material with layers of dielectric coating. Due to the unique requirements, it is not practical to manufacture the structure with conventional rapid prototyping techniques. Hence, we propose to use the combined micromolding and robotic microassembly technique to construct the 3D electrode. Third, we will evaluate the electrode structure as a 3D engineered scaffold for cell incubation in tissue engineering. Novel strategies such as the incorporation of specially designed voltage waveform shapes and the dispersion of micro-scale particulates will be investigated to maximize the initial distribution of cells within the scaffold. A 3D culture environment will be established for optimal cell growth. Studies will be carried out to characterize the density and the viability of cells on the scaffold, which provides important insights to the 3D cell assembly and culture applications. Our proposed dielectrophoresis-based cell manipulation and assembly technique can precisely define deposition locations in the scaffold with maximal initial seed cell density, allowing high-quality artificial tissues grown on the scaffold. Success of this research will facilitate the new development of artificial tissues and organs for transplantation purposes. 在此項目中，我們將研製一種新型的電極組裝式結構來實現錯綜複雜的三維細胞分佈,從而探索一種基於三維空間的細胞批量操作的自動化技術。該技術將同時滿足物理上（如：細胞密度及確定的三維空間形狀）和生物上（如：細胞的存活率）的要求，這在當前生物組織工程領域內還是一項重大的技術難題。另外,該研究還能夠實現細胞在支架中的精確定位以及最大密度的初始分佈，其成功將促進人造組織在支架中的高品質生長，從而有助於針對器官移植的人造組織及器官的發展。

121513.label: Major findings and research outcome
121513.value: 1. Design a millimeter-scale electrode structure that enables manipulation and assembly of cells into a 3D pattern through dielectrophoresis. We have successfully developed a millimeter-scale scaffold structure that can enable automated manipulation of cells in 3D via dielectrophoresis. Each layer has a dimension of 15 mm × 15 mm with a thickness of 500 μm, and serves for two purposes of providing a platform for cells to adhere and an electrode for electric field generation. To generate the required electric fields in the three-dimensional spatial domain, alternating voltage is supplied to the adjacent layers of the structure. After stacking multiple layers together, a 5 × 5 array of interconnected rectangular micro-wells (pores) is established within the scaffold structure for cell attachment and nutrient exchange. The effects of the voltage input on the resultant cellular pattern were examined and discussed. Viability test was performed after the patterning operation and the results confirmed that majority of the cells remained viable. After 7 days of culture, 3D cellular patterns were observed through SEM. The results suggest that this scaffold and its automated dielectrophoresis-based patterning mechanism can be used to construct artificial tissues for various tissue engineering applications. 2. Fabricate and assemble a multiple-layer, bio-compatible electrode structure through the assistance of a robotic micro-manipulator. We then fabricated a multi-layer electrode scaffold to assemble biological cells into a 3D pattern. Through establishing electric fields via this multi-layer structure, the cells in the medium become polarized and are attracted towards the interior part of the structure, forming 3D cellular patterns. To fabricate such a 3D multi-layer electrode scaffold, we utilized the laser cutting technology to cut stainless steel into a precision structure with integrated micro-tips. Layers of the structure were then stacked together forming the 3D scaffold. Experimental results show that this multi-layer structure was capable of manipulating different types of biological cells examined through dielectrophoresis. We further developed an approach to automatically locating and pairing biological cells using a holographic optical tweezers system, where a robotically controlled optical tweezers functions as a special manipulator to transfer cells automatically. Experiments were performed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the robotic micro-manipulation approach. 3. Examine dielectrophoresis-based cell assembly with enhanced DEP force, and characterize the density and viability of the cultured cells on the engineered scaffold. We designed and examined a novel scaffold that can automatically seed cells into multi-layer honeycomb patterns for bone tissue engineering application. The scaffold incorporated dielectrophoresis for non-contact manipulation of cells and intrinsic honeycomb architectures were integrated in each scaffold layer. When a voltage was supplied to the stacked scaffold layers, three-dimensional electric fields were generated, thereby manipulating cells to form into honeycomb-like cellular patterns for subsequent culture. The biocompatibility of the scaffold material was confirmed through the cell viability test. Experiments were conducted to evaluate the cell viability during DEP patterning at different voltage amplitudes, frequencies and manipulating time. Three different mammalian cells were examined and the effects of the cell size and the cell concentration on the resultant cellular patterns were evaluated. Results showed that the proposed scaffold structure was able to construct multi-layer honeycomb cellular patterns in a manner similar to the natural tissue.

121513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
121513.value: Further development of the research will be a new type of 3D-printed scaffold that utilizes dielectrophoresis to active cell seeding and patterning. This scaffold will adopt a concentric-ring design that is similar to native bone tissues, be fabricated with a commercial 3D printer. Polylactic Acid (PLA) may be selected as the material for the printer and the fabricated scaffold is coated with gold to enhance the conductivity for DEP manipulation. This new type of 3D-printed scaffold with cell seeding mechanism offers a new and rapid approach for fabricating engineered scaffolds that can arrange cells into different patterns for various tissue engineering applications.

121513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
121513.value: In this project, we have successfully addressed several important issues for 3D cell manipulation and patterning with a novel engineering scaffold structure. This structure incorporates dielectrophoresis as the non-invasive manipulation method to enable automatic seeding and patterning of biological cells with high efficiency. To enable batch manipulation of the cells, the millimeter-scaled multi-layer structure is supplied with a voltage input to generate electric fields in the three-dimensional domain, polarizing the cells to construct 3D cellular patterns on the structure. The design is then utilized to mimic the 3D geometry of a native tissue. While the conventional practice is unable to control the cells distributed on the scaffold, this scaffold utilizes DEP as the mechanism to manipulate cells toward the intrinsic architecture of the scaffold, thereby forming honeycomb-like cellular patterns on different layers for culture. Experiments are conducted and the results show that the proposed multi-layer DEP manipulation mechanism is capable of patterning the millimeter-scale structure with high cell density. On the basis of the experiments conducted, the proposed scaffold can be used to pattern a wide range of cells into honeycomb-like cellular structures. The integrated DEP-based cell patterning technique could enhance cell seeding for the development of high quality artificial tissues.

121713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
121713.value: While mobile cellular systems are evolving towards the fourth generation, today’s research on radio resource management (RRM) is still based on the traditional Gaussian interference model, which is accurate only when there is a large number of co-channel interferers and no dominant interferer. While such an assumption is valid in traditional cellular systems with large channel reuse factor, its efficacy is questionable in next-generation systems that have universal channel reuse. This project aims to establish a new paradigm for RRM by adopting the non-Gaussian interference model. It can be envisaged that RRM based on a more realistic interference model can lead to better system performance. Existing works on RRM for cellular systems are mostly based on the protocol layering principle, which separates the network layer from the lower layers. Packets transported by different wireless connections are typically treated as indivisible units. In next-generation cellular networks, which support broadcasting service and allow the use of relay nodes, the layering principle may not be a good design philosophy. Network coding, which allows packets from different connections to combine with each other, has been shown to offer throughput benefits, for example, in the two-way relay channel. While many research works confirm the advantages of network coding in various simple wireless channels, it is unclear how network coding should be used in a complex wireless environment and how much benefit can be obtained from the overall system perspective. This project aims to address this challenging issue by designing RRM schemes for cellular systems with network coding operations. The major functions investigated in the RRM design of this project are channel allocation, power control, and user association. The objective of the proposed RRM problem is to minimize the overall system radiated power, while guaranteeing each user’s quality-of-service requirement. The first step of this project is to build a unified framework for the RRM problem, including accurate modeling of interfering signals, the existence of relay nodes, and the operations of network coding. The second step is to apply optimization tools and mathematical techniques to analyze and solve the RRM optimization problem. The last but most important step is to devise distributed RRM algorithms with low computational complexity and small signaling overhead. The performance and convergence properties of the proposed algorithms for practical implementation will be analyzed and evaluated. 移動蜂窩系統正朝著第四代發展，然而當前關於其無線資源管理（RRM）的研究還是基於傳統的高斯干擾模型，即假設同頻干擾服從高斯分佈。高斯干擾模型成立的條件是同頻干擾的用戶數目很多且沒有主導的干擾。傳統的蜂窩系統擁有較大的信道復用因子，因此能夠滿足這些條件，但下一代蜂窩系統將通用所有信道，高斯干擾模型未必準確。本項目的目標就是採用更接近實際條件的非高斯干擾模型，為RRM問題建立一套新的範例。可以預見的是基於新模型的RRM設計必能帶來更好的系統性能。 現有的針對蜂窩系統RRM的工作大部份都基於協議分層原則，也就是把網絡層和其它底層分開考慮，並且傳送于不同無線鏈接的數據包通常被認為是不可分割的單元。但下一代蜂窩網將支持廣播服務和使用中繼站，分層原則未必是一個好的設計理念。相反網絡編碼技術允許不同鏈接的數據包相互結合，已經被證明能夠帶給吞吐量好處，例如，提高雙向中繼信道的吞吐量。儘管許多研究已經肯定了網絡編碼在各種簡單的無線網絡中的優勢，我們仍舊不清楚在一個複雜的無線環境下，網絡編碼該如何應用及它能帶給整個系統多大的好處。本項目的另一個目標是解決這個具有挑戰性的問題，為運用網絡編碼的蜂窩系統設計RRM的方案。 在本項目里，RRM的設計內容主要包括三個部份：信道分配，功率控制和用戶聯盟。研究的目的是最小化整個系統的發射功率，並且保證每個用戶的服務質量要求。項目的第一步是為RRM問題建立一個統一的框架，考慮的元素有干擾信號的準確建模，中繼點的引入和網絡編碼的應用。第二步是運用優化工具和數學技巧分析和解決RRM的優化問題。最後但最重要的一步是設計分佈式的RRM算法，具備運算複雜度低和信令開銷小的性質。這些提出的算法在實際實現中的表現和收斂特性也將會被分析和評估。

121713.label: Realisation of objectives
121713.value: The objectives have been satisfactorily achieved. We have established an optimization framework for RRM in heterogeneous cellular systems. The framework is based on the theory of potential game, which supports distributed optimization of the use of resources. It is modeled for 5G LTE-Advanced systems, but the methodology is general and can be applied to future cellular network architecture with different optimization criteria. Based on the framework, we have designed distributed algorithms for resource optimization of 5G LTE-Advance systems. The problem of joint user association, channel allocation and power control is formulated mathematically, and cast into our optimization framework. Simulation results show that our designed algorithms can utilize the available resources in an efficient manner. In addition to the above framework, we have considered other cellular network scenarios. In particular, we have considered the wireless broadcast problem. In this setting, it is advantageous to apply the concept of network coding. A new coding algorithm has been designed, which is able to minimize the packet delivery time to a group of users. This algorithm is also generalized to a relay-assisted wireless broadcast scenario. Besides, its performance can be further enhanced by adopting a cross-layer approach when performing network coding. The superior performance of all these algorithms have been evaluated and demonstrated. Overall, the objectives have been achieved, and the project outcomes have been published in five top journal papers and several conference papers.

121713.label: Major findings and research outcome
121713.value: An optimization framework for RRM in mobile celluar networks has been designed. It is based on the theory of potential game, which support distributed operation of the network. Besides, the framework can adapt itself to various system optimization targets, such as proportional fairness and sum rate maximization. We have demonstrated the effectiveness of this optimization framework when applied to 4G LTE-Advanced cellular systems. The framework is extensible, and is expected to be applicable to future generations of cellular systems. Based on our designed framework, we have investigated the joint optimization of user association, channel allocation, and power control for both eICIC and FeICIC in LTE-Advanced heterogeneous networks. Distributed algorithms under such a framework have been proposed. We demonstrate via simulations a 64% gain on energy efficiency achieved by eICIC and another 17% gain on energy efficiency achieved by FeICIC. We also show that FeICIC can bring other significant gains in terms of cell-edge throughput, spectral efficiency, and fairness among user throughputs. Moreover, we propose a downlink scheduler based on a cake-cutting algorithm that can further improve the performance of the optimization algorithms compared with conventional schedulers. Besides, we have considered the wireless broadcast problem with side information in users. We have proposed several network coding algorithms for this problem under various settings. For erasure broadcast channels, we have proposed a new linear sparse network code. For Gaussian broadcast channel, a cross-layer approach is adopted, and we have proposed a new concept called quality-aware instantly decodable network coding. For relay-assisted erasure broadcast channel, a joint scheduling and network coding solution is proposed. We have also considered the multiple unicast problem with coded packets in user cache. The problem is a generalization of the well-known index coding problem. A new algorithm is proposed and simulation results show that it outperforms some existing algorithms.

121713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
121713.value: The project outcome has the potential to be further developed such that the results can be applied to cellular systems that utilize more advanced technologies including multiple antennas and advanced multiple access schemes.

121713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
121713.value: Radio resource management plays an important role in the design of mobile cellular systems. As the architecture of cellular systems becomes increasingly complex, it becomes a challenge for system engineers to design new resource management schemes to efficiently utilize available radio resources including frequency spectrum and transmitter power. In this project, we have established a general optimization framework based on the theory of potential game. Under this framework, radio resource can be optimized in a distributed way, which means that each base station can optimize the user of resources independently without much communication with other base stations. Such a distributed operation is scalable and can quickly adapt to the fluctuation of wireless channels.Simulation results show that our proposed methods allow radio resource to be optimized efficiently. Besides, we have also considered the use of network coding to support multiuser transmissions. Various network scenarios have been considered and corresponding network coding algorithms have been proposed. The performance gains of these algorithms have been demonstrated by computer simulations.

122013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
122013.value: The power network, from generation to transmission and distribution to consumption, will undergo the same kind of architectural transformation in the next decades that computing and the communication networks have gone through in the last two. The smart grid network has hundreds of millions of active endpoints. These are not merely passive loads as are most endpoints today, but endpoints that may generate, compute, communicate, and actuate. They will create both a severe risk and a tremendous opportunity: an interconnected system of hundreds of millions of distributed energy resources introducing rapid, large, and random fluctuations in power supply and demand, voltage and frequency. Such deployments create stronger demands and highly variable (in time and space) operating conditions than those experienced in current networks and indeed a key challenge is how to optimize these smart grid networks. A fundamental challenge of a smart grid is: to what extent can moving energy through space and time be optimized to benefit the power network, say to charge electric cars? The power flows become less predictable and the network now has to adapt to the network users instead of the other way around. In this project, we will study power flow optimization problems that consider important features in smart grid such as network connectivity, energy storage and electric vehicle charging. In these problems, when feasible equilibria exist, it is not known if the equilibrium is unique. Our recent investigations showed that the optimal power flow solution is unique in certain network topologies. This is a somewhat surprising result, as equilibrium is known to be non-unique in the general case. It motivates a complete characterization of the network topologies with unique equilibria. Our approach is a novel use of powerful mathematical tools such as differential topology, convex relaxation and optimization theory. This theory-driven approach has three distinctive characters. First, it demonstrates a novel way to characterize a long-standing problem which brings forth new intellectual and practical considerations. Second, it enables new algorithms that are much faster and have lower complexities than state-of-the-arts to be designed. Third, it is a building block for time-dependent power flow optimization problems that are applicable to large-scale storage integration and electric vehicle charging networks. This project will make significant profound contributions to power flow optimization theory. Its impact is even larger on its applicability to modern electric power smart grids as society's reliance on sustainable energy continues to expand tremendously. 在過去幾年來，計算和通信網絡已經進行了更新換代。在未來的幾十年，電網（包括從發電到輸電和配電到消費）也將進行同類改造。尤其是智能電網的發展，將具有數百萬活躍端點。其端點不像今天只是被動的負載，而是具備計算能力、溝通能力以及再啟動能力的智能端點。此項技術存在一個嚴重的風險並創造了一個巨大的機會：一個相互聯繫的具有數百萬分佈式能源資源的系統，需要快速的調整電力供需關係，自適應的調整輸送電壓和頻率。這樣的部署將帶來更有效的需求，同時也在時間和空間上加入了很大的變數。與經驗豐富、技術成熟的現行網絡相比，一個極為關鍵的挑戰就是如何優化此新一代智能電網。換句話說，智能電網的一個基本挑戰就是：通過將變化的能量在空間和時間上進行優化，將會在何種程度上有利於電網。比如，對於大量的電動汽車充電，將會使目前網絡的供電流量變得難以預測，因此需要調整電網以適應未來網絡中不同需求的用戶。 在本項目中，我們將研究智能電網中最為重要的功能。比如網絡連接、儲能以及電動汽車充電功率流等的優化問題。在這些問題中，當可行的分配均衡存在時，平衡的唯一性難以確定。我們最近的調查表明，在某些網絡拓撲結構下最優潮流的解決方案是獨一無二的。這是一個令人驚奇的發現，因為作為平衡方案在一般情況下都是非唯一的。因此，我們能夠構建一個完整的網絡拓撲結構表徵與獨特的均衡。我們擬採用強大的數學工具，諸如微分拓撲、凸鬆弛和優化理論等。這一理論為導向的方法有三種獨特的方面：首先，它展示了一種新的方法來描述一個長期存在的問題，帶來了新的知識和實際的考慮。其次，它使新的算法更快、同時具有藝術設計的較低複雜性。第三，它是隨時間變化的潮流優化問題，適用於大規模存儲整合和電動汽車充電網絡的構建。本項目將在功率流最優化理論方面做出重大而深遠的貢獻，滿足社會依賴可持續能源的需求，繼續大幅擴大現代電力智能電網的適用性。

122013.label: Realisation of objectives
122013.value: The scope of the investigation undertaken in this GRF Project includes proposing a differential topology approach and convex relaxation framework to analyze optimal power flow and electric vehicle energy storage optimization problems that are relevant to smart grids. We also analyze the design of power flow algorithms and energy storage algorithms to charge electric vehicles during off-peak hours and to use the electric vehicle batteries as flexible energy storage tools during peak hours. We study how to overcome the non-convexity hurdles in these power flow optimization problems in order to obtain global optimal solutions and to design efficient algorithms and network protocols. We also prove theoretical analytic results, make computational evaluation, and make initial progress in developing electric vehicle charging algorithms based on mobile computing software. The project work has realized the objectives and led to the publication of three top-tiered journals in this area, e.g., IEEE Transactions on Power Systems, IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications, IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Signal Processing etc. Notably, all the project objectives have been achieved successfully and one Ph.D. student was trained under this GRF project and will graduate in November 2015. In addition to We have also developed experimental methodologies and conducted extensive experiments to evaluate the effectiveness of our proposed algorithms in the smart grid and worked on real-life data obtained from a micro-grid belonging to a California utility. Part of this work was also selected for presentation by the PI at the U.S. National Academy of Engineering China-America Frontiers of Engineering Symposium.

122013.label: Major findings and research outcome
122013.value: We have analyzed how to solve optimal power flow problems that are typically hard to solve due to the non-convexity properties. In particular, we propose a novel use of differential topology and convex relaxation methods to the classical optimal power flow problem as well as its modern version that incorporates smart grid features such as dynamic energy storage and electric vehicle network connectivity. Our results on the differential topology and convex relaxation approach were used to tackle the classical optimal power flow problem and were published in the IEEE Transactions on Power Systems (2015). We provided a full characterization of the network topology that guarantees uniqueness of the global solution as well as a computationally fast fixed-point algorithm, and the project output satisfies Objective 1.We then extended this work for a new formulation that incorporates smart grid features such as energy storage that require new techniques for optimizing power flow and energy storing. These were published in the IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Signal Processing (2014), special issue of smart grid. In particular, we developed a joint optimization of power flow and hybrid-storage integration in a time-dependent power flow optimization problem using optimization decomposition theory and to use the Lagrange dual solution as prices to indicate the threshold of energy charging, and the project output satisfies Objective 2. This in turn leads to a valley-filling algorithm that can smooth the workload for electric vehicle charging, and the project output satisfies Objective 4. We then generalize these work and algorithm design for more general energy storage capacities and these results are published in the IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications (2014) with the project output satisfies Objective 3. As this more general setting is more difficult to solve, we have developed offline optimal algorithms that can be used as benchmarks together with a heuristic dynamic programming algorithm we have proposed thus satisfying Objective 3 and 4. We have also developed experimental methodologies and conducted extensive experiments to evaluate the effectiveness of our proposed algorithms in the smart grid and worked on real-life data obtained from a micro-grid belonging to a California utility.

122013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
122013.value: There are further potential for further development of the research for applications to power grids that have both alternating currents and direct currents flows. Even though our results in this GRF project are more applicable to resistive network setting for micro-grids, the convex relaxation techniques are also applicable to alternating currents. For example, the second-order cone programming convex relaxation developed in the IEEE Transactions on Power Systems can be extended to a semidefinite programming relaxation that has more optimisation variables. The challenge is however to design distributed algorithms that converge fast, as semidefinite programs are hard to decompose and solve in a decentralised manner. Thus, the proposed course of action may be to design suboptimal heuristics inspired by our methodologies and develop performance bounds that can provide some form of optimality guarantees.

122513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
122513.value: In modern cities, natural gas is a major source of fuel for heating and cooking. In a high-rise building, an external piping system, which is erected along the external walls of the building, is used to deliver gas to each household unit. Risers are short pipes that connect the external piping system to kitchens and bathrooms through the building concrete wall. According to recent statistics provided by Towngas, over 14 million household units in China have such risers. Risers are prone to corrosion due to water leaks into the concrete wall. Corrosion often occurs in the sections of risers that are inside the concrete wall. Conventional inspection methods have failed to effectively detect the covered corrosion. The continuous degradation of corrosion may result in riser rupture. Consequently, serious gas leaks may occur and cause explosion. Incidents of sudden explosion caused by ruptured risers happened and killed a number of people. Hence, subjecting risers to safety inspections is a prime concern for every city. The goal of this proposal is to design an effective means to detect corrosion that often occurs in through-wall risers. Ultrasonic guided (UG) waves have recently become popular in the research on detecting defects in buried pipes because UG waves have low energy attenuation and are capable of long-length inspections using only a single transducer. However, the application of UG waves in risers is difficult. First, the surface of a riser is usually coated and partially encased in thick concrete, causing serious energy attenuation on the emitted UG waves. Second, the scattering of reflected UG waves generated by a corroded area is nonlinear, increasing the complexity of defect characterization. Third, risers are usually short in length, with both ends connected to elbows. The reflected waves generated by the elbows may overlap with those that are truly generated by defects. To overcome these difficulties, we propose the designs of a novel sensor called T-MsS, which is a torsional-mode-based magnetostrictive sensor embedded with flexible thin-film coils and smart-materials, an innovative nonlinear inspection approach and an advanced signal processing method named optimized matching pursuit. With the help from these innovative designs, the physical extents of a riser’s corroded area can be determined. Hence, an early warning can be issued after performing a quantitative analysis on the corroded riser. The maintenance staff can then arrange proper remedy to avoid the occurring of catastrophic gas explosion triggered by a ruptured riser. 現代都市中，天然氣是家庭取暖和烹飪所需的重要燃料來源之一。天然氣輸送管線系統主要沿高層建築外牆鋪設以向用戶輸送天然氣。連接外部管線系統與廚房、浴室等天然氣使用終端的短、直管道稱作立管，立管一般需穿過混凝土牆體。依據港華燃氣公司提供的最新統計數據顯示，中國有超過1400萬戶家庭通過立管結構獲取天然氣。由於受混凝土墻體滲水等因素影響，埋入牆體的天然氣立管易因潮濕而產生腐蝕，腐蝕部位也常發生在埋置入混凝土牆體的區段，而常規檢測方法難以有效檢測該類腐蝕缺陷。立管腐蝕缺陷的不斷擴展將導致管導破裂而造成天然氣洩漏，由此引發爆炸事故造成人員傷亡的報導屢見不鮮。因此，天然氣立管的安全隱患檢測是市政工程中關注的熱點問題之一。本研究計劃即立足于發展一種有效的檢測方法及手段，實現對穿牆立管的有效缺陷檢測。 近年來，超聲導波（UG）技術被廣泛研究和應用于麥迪管道的缺陷無損檢測，其主要優點是UG在管道中能量衰減較小，通過單一傳感器即可實現長距離管道缺陷檢測。但將UG技術應用于天然氣立管檢測時存在以下難題：(1) 立管表面塗層和部份埋置入混凝土牆體的結構特徵将導致UG在立管中傳播時發生嚴重衰減；(2) 管道腐蝕處的UG散射信號与腐蝕幾何形貌間存在非線性關係，缺陷定征較為複雜；(3) 天然氣立管長度较小且兩端通常與彎管連接，彎頭部位的反射信號可能與缺陷信號發生重疊而進一步增加信號分析難度。為了解決上述難題，提出一種新型智能傳感器結構和一種基於優化匹配追蹤算法的信號處理方法，其中新型智能傳感器（T-MsS）基於磁致伸縮效應工作，包括智能材料与嵌入式柔性印刷感應線圈，可在立管中激勵產生扭轉模態UG。採用這兩種創新設計或方法，有望實現腐蝕缺陷幾何尺寸的定征和評估，由此建立管健康狀況早期預警機制，支持維修人員適時實施管道維修措施，避免天然氣立管破裂而導致災難性的爆炸事故。

122513.label: Realisation of objectives
122513.value: All objectives have been completed as expected. For objective 1, the completed research tasks can be divided into two parts. The first part is the finite element (FE) simulation. Based on the results generated by FE simulation, they indicated that the concrete wall did absorb a significant part of the emitted ultrasonic guided wave (UGW)’s energy. Nonetheless, they also showed that part of the UGWs could travel through the wall-covered section to the other section of the pipe that was located out of the building wall. We also found that when some of UGW signals were travelled to the entry and the end of the concrete-wall’s section, some UGW wave mode conversions were generated and embedded in the reflected UGW. In conclusion, the results obtained from FE simulation shows that the UGW has the ability to penetrate through the entire length of pipe even part of it is covered by concrete wall or soil. The second part is the design of the proposed MsS (magnetostrictive effect) sensor. The MsS was designated as a torsional-mode sensor so that it can emit UGW signals that are propagating along the shell of the inspected pipe by using torsional motion. The advantages of using torsional wave mode for inspection include it has a steady group velocity within a wide spectrum of frequency and is more sensitive to circumferential type of defects. The MsS was implemented by using the material that has high magnetostrictive property wrapped around by our solely invented flexible print coils. To generate the required static magnetic field, a patch that was made out of the material was being magnetized along its circumferential direction. To produce the required dynamic magnetic field, alternative current was allowed to pass into the coils that were pre-printed in a piece of thin film (flexible printed coils). With the direction of static magnetic field made to be perpendicular to the direction of dynamic magnetic field, the MsS became a torsional mode sensor (T-MsS). To further increase UGWs energy used for inspection, multi-layer of flexible print coils were made so that more current could pass through the coils and then produced larger dynamic magnetic field. Consequently, much higher UGWs energy can be emitted by this new T-MsS sensor. The completed research task of objective 2 includes the design of a chirp signal as the emitted tone-burst signal for the novel T-MsS sensor. UGW can be highly dispersive. It means that the wave signal shape changes as the waves propagates in a distance. This change in signal shows itself in reduction of amplitude and spread of the signal in time domain. In order to detect defects, an excitation UGW signal or the so-called ‘tone-burst signal’ must be emitted with minimum time spread so that the probable echoes from the defects will not be overlapped to each other and maintained minimum noise. Meanwhile, according to the dispersion curves, there are a number of modes that can be emitted at different center frequencies. Due to the characteristics of different extent of defects, each UGW signal reflected by a particular size of defect will be excited by a particular resonant frequency. In order to increase the sensitivity in detecting different sizes of defects, an R-L-C (resistance-inductance-capacitance) circuit was designed to turn the sensor to emit UGW mode at different center frequency. By adjusting different values of R, L and/or C, different frequency bands could be produced. However, the process in tuning the R-L-C circuit to a particular center frequency is tedious and time-consuming. Hence, we employed a faster tuning method by using a chirp signal to emit the UGW wave mode at different frequency band. The chirp signal is a broadband signal that can produce different frequency band at different time intervals. Hence, the desired UGW wave mode can be triggered at a particular center frequency that can match with a particular resonant frequency generated by a special type of defect at different time intervals. With the help of such chirp signal, multiple sizes of defects were detected at different time intervals. When using UGW in pipe defect detection, the true defect related signals may be overwhelmed by noise, undesired wave modes and irrelevant signals, making the defect’s signal difficult to be revealed instantly from the time waveform of the reflected UGW signals. Such problems have been solved by the completing the research tasks listed in objective 3 through the development of two advanced signal processing techniques. The first one is the continuous wavelet transform (CWT) that has the novel idea of using the emitting tone-burst signal as the mother wavelet of CWT instead of the conventional Morlet wavelet. The second one is the matching pursuit technique. To minimize the appearance of noise and undesired wave modes, the CWT with the tone-burst signal as the mother wavelet was used. The result shows that noise and undesired wave modes were substantially minimized by using such method. However, the irrelevant signals caused by the UGW wave dispersion characteristic could not be removed. Hence, the second matching pursuit technique was designed and used to estimate the dispersion effects by statistical methods. It created a dictionary by hosting a number of different scenario of temporal UGW waveforms for the purpose to match with the possible dispersive UGW waveforms. Once the matching was successful, then this technique could predict the dispersion degree in every point of the raw UGW signals and then minimize such irrelevant signals generated by the effect of wave dispersion. With the help of both advanced signal processing techniques, the true defect related UGW signals were extracted and be easily revealed from the raw signals that contain noise, undesired wave modes and irrelevant signals. All of the above designs and methods were verified by conducting laboratory and on-site tests by using real wall-covered pipes as required by objective 4. Both the results obtained from laboratory and on-site tests proved that the emitted UGW did penetrate through the section of concrete wall and travel to other section of the pipe that was located outside of the building wall. For on-site test results, the received UGW signals were less polluted by the reflections of the concrete wall as compared to that obtained from the wall-covered pipes used in the laboratory tests. The main reason is that for the on-site tests, the concrete wall was treated as having infinite length and without any physical boundary of wall. Whilst, for the pipes tested in the laboratory, due to the physical shell of the circular concrete wall, they all had a physical boundary. Hence, during the laboratory tests, the reflections generated by the boundary of concrete wall were collected by the receiver and made the received wave signals very difficult to be interpreted. Whilst, in the results obtained from the on-site tests, part of the UGW propagating energy leaked into the wall was continuously propagating to the lengthy wall. The wave energy that was reflected by the content of wall was too weak or very small in amplitude. Hence, the UGW signals collected from on-site tests were less affected by those UGW signals reflected by wall and the true signals reflected by defects were easier to be extracted as compared to that were collected during the laboratory tests.

122513.label: Major findings and research outcome
122513.value: For objective 1, the innovative T-mode magnetostrictive sensor (T-MsS) specially made for inspecting building pipes has been designed. The MsS is built by using material that has high magnetostrictive property and our solely invented flexible print coils. Based on the results obtained from the simulation and experiments, the T-MsS can emit UGW signal in T-mode to detect defects occurred in pipes. The amplitudes of the generated UGW signals can be increased substantially by having up four layers of flexible printed coils and by increasing the number of coil lines in each flexible print coil layer. For objective 2, a broadband type of chirp signal has been implemented to emit the UGW wave mode at different frequency band. The chirp signal is a broadband signal that can produce different frequency band at different time intervals. The purpose is to replace the classical R-L-C circuit used to manually tune the center frequency of the emitted UGW signal. Tuning the R-L-C circuit manually is a tedious and time-consuming work. With the help of the chirp signal, manual tuning is not necessary as it can generate a wide spectrum of different frequency ranges at different time intervals. Hence, the sensitivity in detecting different sizes of defects has been enhanced by having such chirp signal. For objective 3, two advanced signal processing techniques have been developed to minimize remove noise, undesired wave modes and irrelevant signals embedded in the collected raw UGW signals. We invented the novel idea of using the UGW’s tone-burst signal as the mother wavelet of CWT technique. Such novel technique proved to greatly improve the signal-to-noise ratio of the reflected UGW signals by substantially minimized noise and undesired wave modes. The matching pursuit technique proved to minimize the irrelevant signals caused by UGW’s dispersive characteristics. After purifying the raw UGW signals by these two techniques, the true defect related signals can be easily revealed and its location in the tested pipe can be accurately determined. Finally raw UGW signals reflected from in-serviced pipes that were partially covered by building wall were collected using the new T-mode MsS and then analyzed by the two advanced signal processing techniques. The on-site tests’ results proved that the two techniques could minimize noise, undesired wave modes and irrelevant signals. Hence, the true defect related signals became easier to be revealed even though the defects were occurred inside the concrete-covered of the tested building pipes.

122513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
122513.value: Common types of UGW sensors, such as piezoelectric or magnetostrictive sensors, are used to emit and receive reflected UGW signals. These sensors, however, must be physically mounted on an inspected object. That is, an access point must be available for mounting the sensor on the inspected object. In real situations, however, many objects are partially covered by other structures or moving during operation. Hence, physical sensors cannot be mounted on them. Moreover, undesired disturbance could be induced due to the ringing of physically mounted sensors, which attenuates the UGW energy used for inspection. Recently, a new type of UGW sensor that uses laser has been proposed. The laser-based UGW sensors offer a non-contact inspection method and can measure the UGW signals propagating in all directions. They can also rapidly examine the entire inspected object via laser scanning. Hence, the direction of further development will be focused on the design of such non-contact and portable laser-based UGW system. The proposed research action will firstly apply the system on inspecting thin beams. After the success in testing, then the inspected objects can be expanded to thin plates made of composite materials, building pipes, train bodies etc. The potential in application is huge.

122513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
122513.value: Riser’s pipes are essential infrastructure in any city for supplying and distributing water, gas, chemicals etc., to various households and industries. Due to the pipe risers often buried or located in the areas with rugged environment, it is susceptible to various kinds of defects. If these defects cannot be found at early stage of development, then they may deteriorate to leak and eventually result in a fatal rupture. Leaky or ruptured risers may result in serious pollution to the environment, causing huge economic loss and even human casualties. A past incident of sudden water pipe rupture causing serious traffic problem and over 500,000 people did not have water to use due to unexpected water suspension. A fatal gas explosion took place in Hong Kong causing 2 deaths and 7 injuries and seriously damaging the basement of a residential high building. The reason of the explosion was the leakage of gas from underground pipelines. The generated outcomes of this project is an effective and reliable pipe inspection technique that can guarantee reliable identification of early defects occurred in building risers, reliable defect severity estimation and most importantly, provide early warnings prior to fatal riser rupture.

122713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
122713.value: Smart materials which provide rapid responses to mechanical and magnetic stimuli hold the promise for future generations of sensors and actuators. Magnetic shape memory (MSM) alloys which exhibit such responses can transform a wide spectrum of transducer technologies in diversified fields such as aerospace, automotive, underwater navigation, biomedical, surveillance and consumer electronics. Compositional and microstructural design of MSM alloys with desired magneto-mechanical responses hinges on having a fundamental understanding of the strong magnetoelastic coupling in this class of materials. We propose an experimental study to determine the nature of magnetoelastic coupling in MSM alloys. The experimental approach will be based on in-situ neutron scattering experiments under a combined magnetic field and mechanical load, complemented by real space imaging with spin-polarized scanning electron microscopy. The approach will be applied to a prototypical Ni-Mn-Ga single crystal alloy, where the combined effects of stress and magnetic field on the structural stability and magnetoelastic behavior will be investigated. The proposed study will elucidate physical insights underlying the strong magnetoelastic coupling in MSM alloys, thereby providing guidance in the design of new materials for sensor and actuator applications. Experimental characterization of magnetoelastic coupling will also provide a benchmark for testing predictions by first-principles calculations or phenomenological theories in MSM alloys. 對力場和磁場的作用提供快速響應的智能材料決定了未來數代傳感器和執行器的命運。滿足這些優異性能要求的磁性形狀記憶合金能為傳感器科技帶來一系列的革新。這些革新將體現在形形色色的領域，如航空航天，汽車，水下導航，生物醫藥，監視和消費電子產品。具備所期待的磁-機械響應性能的磁性形狀記憶合金的成分和結構設計取決於從根本上對這類材料磁彈性耦合效應的深入理解。我們提議通過實驗研究探明磁性形狀記憶合金的磁彈性耦合的本質。實驗將以結合了磁場和力場的原位中子散射實驗為主要研究手段，同時輔以自旋極化掃描電子顯微鏡的真實空間成像技術。該研究方法將被應用於典型的鎳錳鎵單晶合金。應力場和磁場的結合對於該合金結構穩定性和磁彈性行為的影響將被深入研究。所提議的研究將闡明隱藏在磁性形狀記憶合金強磁彈性耦合效應當中的物理內涵，因此為應用於傳感器和執行器領域的這類新型材料的設計提供綱領性的指導。針對磁彈性耦合的實驗檢測將為第一性原理計算或唯象理論基於磁性形狀記憶合金的預測提供參照和基準。

122713.label: Realisation of objectives
122713.value: This project was designed to determine the nature of magnetoelastic coupling in ferromagnetic shape memory alloys (FSMAs). Smart materials which provide rapid responses to mechanical and magnetic stimuli hold the promise for future generations of sensors and actuators. FSMS which exhibit such responses can transform a wide spectrum of transducer technologies in diversified fields such as aerospace, automotive, underwater navigation, biomedical, surveillance and consumer electronics. We proposed an experimental study to determine the nature of magnetoelastic coupling in FSMAs. The experimental approach is based on in-situ scattering experiments under a combined magnetic field and mechanical load, complemented by real space imaging with spin-polarized scanning electron microscopy. The approach was applied to a prototypical Ni-Mn-Ga single crystal alloy, where the combined effects of stress and magnetic field on the structural stability and magnetoelastic behavior was investigated. The proposed study shed light on physical insights underlying the strong magnetoelastic coupling in MSM alloys, providing guidance in the design of new materials for sensor and actuator applications. The project has been well executed overall. (1) The neutron diffraction experiment under a combined magnetic field and mechanical load has been realized to determine the response of twin variants and rotation magnetic moments. The experiment was carried out at the Australian Center for Neutron Scattering, using the WOMBAT instrument. A small precision load-frame was purposely built by Mr. Yubin Ke, a PhD student in my group. To differentiate the rotation of magnetic moments and twin reorientation, polarized neutron diffraction had to be used. This was perhaps one of the most challenging scattering experiments one can imagine, involving the use of polarized neutrons and under combined mechanical load and magnetic field. The experimental results are being summarized and is prepared for publication. (2) Unfortunately, the experiment with spin-polarized scanning electron microscopy could not be carried out, because the instrument at Oak Ridge National Laboratory was out of commission. We had reported this problem in our mid-term report, but unfortunately the problem lingered and the instrument remained inaccessible, even though the samples had been prepared. This was a situation out of our control. Fortunately, since it was meant to be a complementary experiment, it did not affect other parts of the project or the fundamental understanding of the magneto-elastic coupling. Instead, we spent part of the project efforts to develop a real-space phase field model combining Landau–Lifshitz–Gilbert equation and time-dependent Ginzburg–Landau equation to investigate the evolution of ferromagnetic domains and martensitic twin structures in FSMA at different length and time scales. The model is designed to help interpret the neutron diffraction data under complicated conditions of combined mechanical load and magnetic field. (3) The project was supported by three personnel over different period of times. a. Dr. A. Pramanick, Research Fellow b. Dr. Honghui Wu, Postdoctoral Fellow c. Mr. Yubing Ke, part-time PhD student They have received unique training and ample experience on the use of neutron scattering. One of our earlier experiments were carried out with high-energy synchrotron X-ray diffraction, where we measured the kinetics of twin-boundary motion in Ni2Mn1.14Ga0.86. The temporal evolution of twin variants, which occurs through twin boundary motion under a magnetic field, was directly determined from a change in intensities of X-ray diffraction peaks. It was determined that twin boundary motion occurs through a thermally-activated motion over a distribution of energy barriers which exhibit characteristics of short-range disorders. This is in contrast to the conventional models, which consider only a single switching time constant or single energy barrier for twin boundary motion in FSMAs. The findings from this work could help achieve more deterministic control in smart devices having FSMA components. This work was published in Physical Review Letters (vol. 112, p. 217205, 2014). During the application of a magnetic field in FSMAs, there are simultaneous rotation of magnetic moments and reorientation of twin variants. However, resolving the rotation of magnetic moments and reorientation of twins, although critical for design of new materials and devices, has been difficult to achieve quantitatively with current characterization methods. At the same time, theoretical modeling of these phenomena also faced limitations due to uncertainties in values of physical properties such as magnetocrystalline anisotropy energy, especially for off-stoichiometric FSMA compositions. Using in situ polarized neutron diffraction, we measured directly the extents of both magnetic moments rotation and crystallographic twin-reorientation in an FSMA single-crystal during the application of magnetic fields. In addition, high-resolution neutron scattering measurements and first-principles calculations based on fully relativistic density functional theory have been employed to determine accurately the magnetic anistrotropy energy for the compositionally disordered alloy of Ni2Mn1.14Ga0.86. The results from these state-of-the-art experiments and calculations are self-consistently described within a phenomenological framework, which provided quantitative insights into the energetics of magnetostructural coupling in FSMAs. Based on the current model, the energy for magnetoelastic twin boundaries propagation for the studied alloy was estimated to be ~150 kJ/m3. This work was published in Phys. Rev. B (Volume 92, 134109, 2015) Magneto-mechanical coupling effects in ferromagnetic materials offer a great opportunity to manipulate magnetic properties through stress loading, which has potential application in spintronic and nonvolatile memory devices. Understanding the magneto-mechanical coupling mechanism necessitate simultaneously characterization of underline structure and magnetization evolution, which remains a longstanding experimental challenge. As we had planned, a neutron diffraction experiment was carried out under a combined mechanical load and magnetic field, using polarized neutron beam, to reveal the coupled twin reorientation and magnetic moment rotation process of Ni-Mn-Ga ferromagnetic Heusler alloy. Stress-induced magnetization change was attributed to the magnetic moment rotation and a variance of moment per unit cell under magneto-mechanical loading. A linear correlation was established between magnetic moment rotation and stress-induced twin reorientation. The change of ordered moment was found to depend non-linearly on the lattice strain during mechanical loading. Aside from scientific findings, our experiments establish a new method for in-situ characterization for structure and magnetization. This work is currently summarized for publication. Since the spin-polarized scanning electron microscopy instrument was not available, we have devoted part of the project efforts to develop a real-space phase field model combining Landau–Lifshitz–Gilbert equation and time-dependent Ginzburg–Landau equation to investigate the evolution of ferromagnetic domains and martensitic twin structures in a ferromagnetic shape memory alloy at different lengthscales. Both domain and twin structures were obtained by simultaneously solving for minimization of magnetic, elastic, and magnetoelastic coupling energy terms via a nonlinear finite element method. The model was applied to simulate magneto-structural evolution within a nanoparticle and a bulk single-crystal of the alloy Ni2 MnGa, which are subjected to mechanical strains. It is shown that a nanoparticle contains magnetic vortex structures within a single twin variant, whereas for a bulk crystal both 90-deg and 180-deg domain structures are present within multiple twin variants. This work has been published in J. Appl. Phys. (Volume 120, 183904, 2016).

122713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
122713.value: The purpose-built precision load-frame is unique and can be used in conjunction with a magnetic or electric field. This device will be of great utility for investigation of novel materials response under combined mechanical load and electric or magnetic fields. The phase-field model established under this project is being further developed to study the effects of combined load and magnetic field, and to examine dynamics response of the material. This model will prove to be very useful in the design of future ferromagnetic shape memory alloys.

122713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
122713.value: Smart materials which provide rapid responses to mechanical and magnetic stimuli hold the promise for future generations of sensors and actuators. Ferromagnetic shape memory alloys exhibit such responses and have been considered for a wide spectrum of transducer technologies in diversified fields such as aerospace, automotive, underwater navigation, biomedical, surveillance and consumer electronics. The physical mechanism underlining the shape memory effect is the coupling between the magnetic moments and crystal lattice orientation. The former can be controlled by a magnetic field, whereas the latter by a mechanical load. In this project, we have realized an experiment in which a mechanical load and a magnetic field can be applied at the same time. This allows us to examine the competition between mechanical load and magnetic field. Quantitative measurements were performed with polarized neutron diffraction. At the same, we developed a predictive model based on phase-field modeling. The model will be benchmarked with neutron diffraction and synchrotron experimental results and applied to the design of new smart materials.

122813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
122813.value: The load-carrying capacity of driven piles in crushable, coarse-grained soils remains a topic with many uncertainties in geotechnical engineering. The source of uncertainty comes from a lack of a full understanding of the mechanisms that control pile penetration into the soil and pile setup with time after installation. Despite a significant amount of experimental work dedicated in this field, current design methods adopted by the pile industry may not be fully reliable and often have difficulties in capturing the behavior observed in the field. This deficiency is important for a metropolitan city like Hong Kong, where crushable soils such as highly weathered, decomposed granites or volcanics are found. In this proposal, we propose a comprehensive investigation of the time-dependent load-carrying capacity behavior of driven piles in crushable granular soils using a coupled discrete-continuum modeling approach with experimental calibration. The detailed micromechanics underlying the pile-soil interaction will be handled by the Discrete Element Method (DEM) while the wider region of foundation soil away from the pile will be modeled using the Finite Element Method (FEM) or Finite Difference Method (FDM). The major goal of the proposed research is to develop an in-depth understanding of the grain-scale mechanisms that control the pile capacity under the influence of particle breakage during pile installation and soil ageing after installation. The outcome of this research will be a significant advancement of knowledge of the pile capacity behavior in crushable, coarse-grained soils in both short-term conditions following pile installation and long-term conditions following pile setup. The benefits of this research come from an improved understanding of the time-dependent pile capacity behavior, especially of the processes, physics and mechanisms at the soil grain scale. This improved understanding will translate into an enhanced ability of engineers to make more economic designs of pile foundations, particularly in incorporating critical, complex soil behavior such as grain crushing, interface friction degradation, soil creep and soil ageing. It is expected that the improved pile foundation designs will lead to more construction cost savings in Hong Kong and worldwide in the future. 可破碎粗粒土中，打入桩的承载力研究仍然是岩土工程中一个充满不确定性的课题。这种不确定性源自对桩的打入过程以及打入后桩的时间效应的机理缺乏充分的认识。尽管有大量的试验支撑，目前被工业界采用的桩基设计方法可能不是完全可靠的，而且现有的方法很难捕捉到在现场观测到的一些现象。这种不足对于像香港这样，发现了诸如强风化分解的花岗岩或者火山岩这类的可破碎土的大城市来说是非常重要的。 在本方案中，提出了一个在可破碎颗粒土中，考虑打入桩的承载能力和性能的时间效应，采用耦合的离散-连续建模方法及试验对比的详细研究方案。桩-土相互作用的微观力学机理将通过离散元（DEM）来模拟，而离桩身较远的地基土将用有限元(FEM)或者有限差分法(FDM)来模拟。研究的主要目标是对颗粒尺寸上在桩打入过程中颗粒破碎及成桩后土老化对桩承载力的影响机理有更深入的了解。 本研究的预期成果是对在可破碎粗粒土中，成桩后桩的短期及长期承载性能的认识有重大进展。研究的效益源自对桩承载性能的时间效应有更好的理解，特别是对土颗粒尺寸级别的过程、现象和机理有更深入了解。这种认识上的进步将提高工程师设计出更加经济的桩基础的能力，尤其是面临诸如颗粒破碎、界面摩擦衰减、蠕动及老化等危险、复杂土性时。在未来，这种桩基设计理论上的进步在香港和全世界将节约更多的建设成本。

122813.label: Realisation of objectives
122813.value: All the objectives have been fully achieved. Objective 1 is achieved by constructing a 3D DEM model of crushable sands using the parallel bonded cluster technique. A detailed study on the micromechanical behavior of crushable sands was conducted using the DEM model. The agglomerates have diameters varying between 0.7 ~ 2.0 mm, with the composing uniform elementary ball diameter being 0.2 mm. Parallel bonds are installed at all the contacts existing between the balls to form the porous agglomerate. The advantage of the parallel bond model against the contact bond model, which was widely used in previous DEM studies on particle crushing, is that it simulates a finite piece of cement between two balls providing a rotational resistance. To achieve the statistical variation of the fracture strength, 0, 10% or 20% of the elementary balls are randomly removed from each agglomerate generated. The influence of the percentage of balls removed on the distribution of fracture strength is carefully investigated. Meanwhile, an advanced coupled FEM-DEM model is also established recently using the cohesive interface element and the effect of realistic particle morphology is considered in this model to simulate particle crushing. In the context of FDEM, solid fracture was simulated by the failure cohesive interface elements (CIEs) with geometric zero-thickness by defining a traction-separation damage law. The sand particle was discretized into discrete solid tetrahedral elements. The 6-node CIEs were then embedded between the edges of each pair of adjacent tetrahedral elements. Therefore, the solid fracture occurs on account of the failure of CIEs, while the tetrahedral bulk elements are deformable but unbroken with linear elastic mechanical response. The constitutive response of the bulk elements can be easily obtained based on the finite element analysis in Abaqus Standard. Objectives 2 and 3 have been fully achieved by establishing a sophisticated large-scale DEM model of pile-soil interaction and performing a comprehensive parametric study of pile penetration to assess the effects of initial soil state parameters, pile size/scale and penetration rate on the pile capacity. The DEM model is made up of a rectangular container filled with a well-compacted, poly-dispersed assembly of round particles and a CPT-shaped model pile pushed gradually into the granular foundation at the middle of the box. The bottom wall is set to be frictionless but the right wall is assigned a high friction coefficient of 0.9 to minimize any relative slip between the particles and the wall. The granular material is composed of rigid disks with diameters uniformly varying between 0.6 mm and 1.2 mm. To accommodate particle breakage in this study, we define a crushable zone with a size of 2B (W) × 27B (H) surrounding the pile. In this crushable zone, particle breakage is allowed by the disintegration of agglomerates which are made of parallel-bonded particle clusters. A study was also made to determine the type of interface shear boundary condition that best describes the model pile interface behavior. This was achieved by developing 2D DEM models of interface shear test under CNL, CNS and CV conditions with crushable particles, and comparing the simulation results of model pile with interface shear test. The CNS boundary condition is modeled by a servomechanism which controls the velocity of the upper wall. Objectives 4 has been fully achieved by establishing a rate process theory (RPT) based contact creep model in DEM and making an in-depth investigation of the particle-scale creep behavior using the proposed model. In LIGGGHTS, we adopted a Hertz contact model and incorporated RPT into the model for the creep simulation. The normal force has two terms, namely, a spring force and a viscous force. The viscous part of the normal force is due to the dissipation of energy from the velocity loss during particle collision, which can be described using the coefficient of restitution, e. When e = 0, the two particles do not move apart after the collision, but instead they coalesce; when e = 1, the two particles rebound from one another with the same relative speed at which they approach. The viscous force is useful for draining the kinetic energy when preparing the sample, and approaches zero under quasi-static loading. Particle rotation, as an important microscopic deformation mechanism, is known to affect the macro-mechanical behavior of granular materials. Thus, an additional rolling resistance model was also applied. By taking advantage of treating the contact as a continuously distributed system of normal and tangential springs, the rolling resistance model does not introduce additional material parameters. Particle breakage was also included in the model by adopting a probability-based particle replacement approach. The validity of the model was demonstrated by comparing the simulation results with published experimental data of oedometer tests. Objectives 5 and 6 have been well achieved by incorporating the RPT-based model into the large-scale DEM model of pile-soil interaction and performing a comprehensive parametric study of pile setup to assess the effects of initial soil state parameters, pile size/scale and penetration rate on the pile capacity. In order to simulate small particle sizes in an acceptable computational time, a particle refinement method, which is similar to mesh refinement in FEM, is adopted. The soil foundation is divided into 7 regions. The radius of region I and the thickness of region II are 4.8 mm and 6.8 mm, respectively. The thickness of region III-VII are set in an incremental manner. The granular material in region I is composed of crushable agglomerates with diameters uniformly varying between 0.6 mm and 1.2 mm. The diameter of balls in region II-VII are set in the same incremental manner, in which the ratio of D50 for an outer region to that for an inner region is 1.414. The gradual increase in particle diameter is to ensure that small particles will not migrate into the voids between the adjacent larger particles. The effects of vertical stress field, initial porosity, particle strength and rolling resistance on the penetration resistance were investigated to demonstrate the high capabilities of the model in reproducing many facets of the soil mechanics during the installation process seen in the physical tests. Through the incorporation of the probabilistic particle fracture model into large-scale 3D DEM models, the stress-strain behavior of the DEM material was first characterized by means of the numerical direct shear tests. The volumetric response during shearing becomes much more contractive as the particle strength is decreased. The effects of vertical stress field, initial porosity, particle strength and rolling resistance on the penetration resistance were investigated to demonstrate the high capabilities of the model in reproducing many facets of the soil mechanics during the installation process seen in the physical tests. Then, the piles were fixed for setup. After setup for 80 s of simulation time, the shaft resistance of the driven pile gains about 5%. This positive gain in capacity with time is due to the increase contact number due to rearrangement of particles, soil homogenization and the dissipation of stress concentration.
