122813.label: Major findings and research outcome
122813.value: Through the careful construction of the pile-sand interaction model and the application of a series of DEM analysis techniques, we presented a detailed and in-depth discrete-continuum study on the pile penetration mechanism, elucidating the effects of and interplay between the in-situ vertical stress field, soil crushability and void ratio on the penetration behavior (Wang and Zhao, 2014). Attributed to the unique capability of DEM in providing all particle-scale data, this study offers rich insights into the micromechanical processes and mechanisms underlying a range of penetration behavior that was known to be scientifically and practically important but not fully understood yet. Notable examples include the semi-constant tip resistance profile at larger penetration depths in high-crushability sands which is caused by significant particle breakage prevailing against the in-situ stress, and the strain reversal behavior after the passing of the tip which is caused by the principal stress rotation. These and many other novel insights have advanced our understanding of the pile monotonic penetration mechanism in crushable sand. On the basis of the previous study, further effort was made to deepen the stress analysis of the pile and the sand mass. Success is achieved in unraveling a unique penetration mechanism within a homogeneous sand mass which is independent of the pile penetration depth (Liu and Wang, 2015). Furthermore, a 2D DEM simulation study was made to elucidate the role of normal boundary condition in interface shear test for the determination of skin friction along pile shaft (Wang et al., 2017). In parallel with the numerical study, an experimental investigation on the static fatigue behavior of sand particles was also made (Liu and Wang, 2018). For the creep study, the rate process theory (RPT) was incorporated into a Hertz contact model for the creep simulation. An approach for modeling particle breakage was proposed, considering particle strength variability described by Weibull distribution and particle size distribution of fragments meeting a fractal condition. Stress redistribution and fabric change were revealed by tracking the normal contact force, the tangential contact force and the number of contacts. In order to unravel the effect of particle breakage on the creep behavior, creep tests with and without particle crushing during the creep stage were performed for comparison (Liu et al., 2018).

122813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
122813.value: Considerable potentials exist for the further development of the research. Based on the DEM findings about the pile penetration mechanism, particularly the depth-independent penetration mechanism, we may endeavor to establish a universal theoretical or analytical model for the pile penetration behavior, which could be very valuable and applicable for the pile industry. Strong development in the RPT-based contact creep model for the elucidation of creep effects on a wide variety of granular soil behavior is also demanded, especially under the triaxial shearing condition and the field condition of pile installation. In addition, the effects of pile installation methods (e.g., driving or jacking) on the pile capacity and setup behaviors are also worth investigation.

122813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
122813.value: This project made a fundamental investigation of the pile capacity behavior during the monotonic driving in to a crushable sand using the DEM and FEM modeling methods. The short-term pile capacity behavior (i.e., during and immediately after the installation process) and the long-term pile capacity behavior (i.e., long after the installation process due to soil creep and aging) were carefully studied and their underlying micromechanical mechanisms are elucidated. The significance of this project is to showcase the high capability and advantage of a numerical model to reproduce a wide range of realistic soil behaviors observed in the physical or field tests of pile installation and thus demonstrate the value and potentials of such a modeling approach in the future application in the pile industry.

122913.label: Project Objectives
122913.value: To quantify the interference level caused by co-resident VMs to different types of covert channels. Following our preliminary results, we will further quantify and approximately model the relationship between the total interference jointly caused by multiple co-resident VMs to CPU L2 cache based covert channels. For other types of covert channels, we will identify the key factors which will affect the interference to each type of covert channel and quantify the relationship between the interference and the key factors. We will also propose a framework to calibrate the interference model on different cloud platforms. To design VM provisioning solutions so that the interference on each server is sufficiently high to thwart any potential covert channel attack while the resource utilization is maximized. The newly added dimension of interference makes the VM provisioning problem different from the conventional multi-dimensional bin packing models. We will first identify the sufficient conditions for the interference requirement and then develop efficient VM provisioning solutions. To design VM re-provisioning solutions so that the interference on each server can remain sufficiently high with the dynamic arrival and departure of VMs. To this end, we will also need to consider the overhead of VM migration and the option of adding cloud service provider’s dummy VMs. To design VM provisioning solutions so that the VMs from tenants with conflicts of interests are also protected against indirect covert channel attacks. Indirect covert channel attack exists when there is an information flow path from the victim VM to a third-party VM which is co-resident with the adversary VM. In this project, by introducing the concept of safety distance measured by the length of the information flow path between two VMs, we aim to design VM provisioning solutions so that the safety distance between two VMs with conflicts of interests is longer than a threshold and the resource utilization is high.

122913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
122913.value: Virtualization is one key enabler of cloud computing, which, however, is also a double-edged sword. It may cause information leakage of a user or application which deploys virtual machines (VMs). Information leakage may happen through a so-called covert channel between a victim’s VM and an adversary’s VM when they are placed on the same server, which we refer to as direct covert channel attacks. Information leakage may also happen between two VMs even when they are not placed on the same server, which we refer to as indirect covert channel attacks. The latter risk exists when a victim’s VM communicates with a third-party VM which is co-resident with an adversary’s VM on another server. This project aims to investigate the behaviors of various covert channel attacks and to develop counter measures. Specifically, we propose to mitigate the effectiveness of various direct and indirect covert channel attacks through strategic VM provisioning, a novel approach that does not sacrifice the resource utilization or change the hypervisor and guest OSs. Our preliminary experiments have shown that on a server, the activities of additional co-resident VMs (other than the victim and adversary VMs of a covert channel) can generate significant interference to the covert channel, causing an attacker to experience a high error rate when trying to recover information through the covert channel, and thus mitigating the effectiveness of direct covert channel attacks. This project proposes to conduct intensive and comprehensive experiments on different cloud platforms to quantify and profile the interference caused by the co-resident VMs. Based on the understanding of the interference, we will then study how to provision and re-provision VMs so that, while maintaining high resource utilization, the interference from the co-resident VMs to any potential covert channel is also sufficiently high. For indirect covert channel attacks, we have observed that the risk of information leakage is smaller when there is a longer information flow path between a victim VM and an adversary VM. This project will study VM provisioning so that the VMs with conflicts of interests are placed as “far” as possible, a supplement to the protection provided against direct covert channel attacks. In summary, we aim to protect vulnerable VMs subject to covert channel attacks at the high level through VM provisioning. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first attempt to systematically study VM provisioning to thwart direct and indirect covert channel attacks. 虚拟化是云计算的一个重要支撑技术，同时也是一个双刃剑。它可能引起布置在虚机上的应用或用户信息泄露。 信息泄露可能通过布置在同一个服务器上的两个虚机间的隐秘信道发生，我们称之为直接隐秘信道攻击。信息泄露也可能发生在不同服务器上的两个虚机间， 我们称之为间接隐秘信道。当受害者的虚机与另一个服务器上的虚机通信，而该虚机与攻击者的虚机在同一台服务器上并且它们之间可以建立一个隐秘信道，通过间接隐秘信道造成的信息泄露就可能发生。本项目旨在研究不同隐秘信道攻击的行为以及相应的应对措施。具体说来，我们提出一个创新的虚机分配方法达到降低各种直接或间接隐秘信道的有效性的目的。所提出的方法既不会牺牲资源的利用率，也不需要修改虚拟机监视器也不需要修改虚机所在服务器上的操作系统。 我们的前期实验显示在一台服务器上，除了受害虚机与攻击虚机以外的虚机的操作能对隐秘信道产生很大的干扰，一次降低直接隐秘信道的有效性。本项目提出在不同的云平台上研究并量化共存的虚机对隐秘信道的影响。基于这样的量化工作，我们研究如何对虚机进行分配与再分配使得在不牺牲资源利用率的情形下，在任何服务器上，其他虚机能对任何两个虚机间的可能的隐秘信道产生足够高的干预。 对间接隐秘信道的攻击，我们观察到当从受害受害虚机到攻击者的虚机之间的信息流的路径越长，信息泄露的风险越低。本项目将研究虚机分配的策略使得有可能产生隐秘信道的虚机尽量放在信息流路径长的服务器上。 总的说来，我们旨在从虚机分配的角度保护易受隐秘信道攻击的虚机。据我们所知，本项目是第一个试图从虚机分配的角度降低直接和间接隐秘信道攻击的工作。

122913.label: Major findings and research outcome
122913.value: Objective 1 is to quantify the interference level caused by co-resident VMs to different types of covert channels. In journal paper [1], we studied the impact of different bystander workloads on L2 cache covert channels. We then built a theoretical model and conducted experiments to quantify error rates that a bystander brought to an L2 cache covert channel under different memory access frequency and working set size. In journal paper [6], we systematically measured all types of covert channels’ capacity and impact factors for the capacity of all types of covert channels. In conference paper [1], we studied the cloud platform (hardware and software)’s impact on the capacities of different covert channels. Objective 2 is to design VM provisioning solutions so that the interference on each server is sufficiently high to thwart any potential covert channel attack while the resource utilization is maximized. In journal paper [1], we proposed an efficient virtual machine provisioning algorithm which achieves the balance of tradeoff between resource utilization and error rate. In conference paper [4], we proposed a generic VM provisioning solutions which achieves high resource utilization and ensures low information leakage risk. Objective 3 is to design VM re-provisioning solutions so that the interference on each server can remain sufficiently high with the dynamic arrival and departure of VMs. In carrying the project, we found that hypervisor scheduling can decide the information leakage risk of all types of timing based covert channels. Thus, we turn our focus to be how to quantify the information leakage risk under a given hypervisor scheduling and how to integrate VM provisioning and scheduling together in conference paper [4]. This proposed solution will not change the security level when VMs dynamically join or leave the system. Objective 4 is to design VM provisioning solutions so that the VMs from tenants with conflicts of interests are also protected against indirect covert channel attacks. In conference paper [4], we allow a user to specify its security level and design VM provisioning solution so that the co-resident VMs from different tenants will have at least the security levels that they specified. Besides the four objectives, we also studied the covert channels on cloud storage and smartphones. The work has been published in journal papers [2][5] and conference papers [2][3]. We have studied other related information leakage issues using network coding in journal paper [3] and encryption in journal paper [4].

122913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
122913.value: In carrying out the project, most results have been tested in public clouds. Our further development will be to design tailored solutions to mitigate the covert channels in different platforms.

122913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
122913.value: Virtualization is one key enabler of cloud computing, which, however, is also a double-edged sword. It may cause information leakage of a user or application which deploys virtual machines (VMs). Information leakage may happen through a so-called covert channel between a victim’s VM and an adversary’s VM, by leveraging the imperfect hardware isolation between VMs, such as CPU cache, memory bus, I/O bus, and cloud storage. In this project, we have systematically studied the risk of information leakage of various covert channels between VMs on different cloud platforms. We have quantified the capacity of various covert channel, proposed VM provisioning algorithms and mitigation solutions to reduce the risk of information leakage brought by covert channels. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first attempt to systematically study VM provisioning to thwart covert channel attacks.

123013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
123013.value: 在本项目中，我们将要设计关于框架整理及家谱比较的算法。 基因组的比较是计算生物学中的一个重要领域。随着基因组测序技术的发展，越来越多的有机体已经被测序出来。一个有趣的现象是，很多相关的基因组不完整，并且越来越多的基因组是以contig的形式被公布。在本项目中，我们将研究关于框架整理问题的算法。 重建特定种群或物种之间的进化关系是进化生物学中的一个重要问题。对于物种的进化，传统上用进化树来表达。对于种群之间的关系，可以用家谱来表示。在本项目中，我们将要设计关于家谱比较的算法。

123013.label: Realisation of objectives
123013.value: We have developed algorithms for pedigree comparison problem. We studied three different models for pedigrees where every leafof the pedigree is unique labeled. The three models are the maximum pedigree isomorphism problem, the maximum paternal-path-preserved mapping problem and the minimum edge-cutting mapping problem. For the maximum pedigree isomorphism problem, we prove that the problem is NP-hard and give a fixed-parameter algorithm for the problem. For the maximum paternal-path-preserved mapping problem, we give a dynamic-programming algorithm to find the mapping that preserves the maximum number of paternal paths between the two input pedigrees. For the minimum edge-cutting mapping problem, we prove that the problem is NP-hard and give a fixed-parameter algorithm with running time O(n(2.14)k), where n is the number of vertices in the two input pedigrees and k is the number of edges to be cut. This algorithm is useful in practice when comparing two similar pedigrees. For the zreo comparison problem, we propose the first fixed parameter algorithm for EBD(1, 2). Using a dynamic programming approach, we design an algorithm to solve EBD(1, 2) with running time O(4sn2) and space O(4sn), respectively, where n is the number of gene families, and s is the maximum number of genes (minus 1) located between two copies of a gene family in the second genome. Our algorithm can also be used to compute the maximum adjacencies between two genomes. Simulations on real data have verified the effectiveness of our algorithm. The algorithm has been implemented in C++. We also developed a software package is available upon request.

123013.label: Major findings and research outcome
123013.value: The exemplar breakpoint distance problem is motivated by finding conserved sets of genes between two genomes. It asks to find respective exemplars in two genomes to minimize the breakpoint distance between them. If one genome has no repeated gene (called trivial genome) and the other has genes repeating at most twice, it is referred to as the (1,2)-exemplar breakpoint distance problem, EBD(1, 2) for short. Whether there exists a fixed parameter algorithm for this problem has been open for many years. In this paper, we propose the first fixed parameter algorithm for EBD(1, 2). Using a dynamic programming approach, we design an algorithm to solve EBD(1, 2) with running time O(4sn2) and space O(4sn), respectively, where n is the number of gene families, and s is the maximum number of genes (minus 1) located between two copies of a gene family in the second genome. Our algorithm can also be used to compute the maximum adjacencies between two genomes. Simulations on real data have verified the effectiveness of our algorithm. The algorithm has been implemented in C++. We also developed a software package is available upon request. Reconstruction of ancestral relationships among genera, species and populations is a core task in evolutionary biology. At the population level, pedigrees have been commonly used. Reconstruction of pedigree is required in practice due to legal or medical reasons. Pedigrees are very important to geneticists for inferring haplotype segments, recombination, and allele sharing status with which disease loci can be identified. Evaluating reconstruction methods requires comparing the inferred pedigree and the known pedigrees. Moreover, comparison of pedigrees is required in studying relationships among crops such as maize, wheat and barley, etc. In this project, we discuss three models for comparison of pedigrees, the maximum pedigree isomorphism problem, the maximum paternal-path-preserved mapping problem and the minimum edge-cutting mapping problem. For the maximum pedigree isomorphism problem, we prove that the problem is NP-hard and give a fixed-parameter algorithm for the problem. For the maximum paternal-path-preserved mapping problem, we give a dynamic-programming algorithm to find the mapping that preserves the maximum number of paternal paths between the two input pedigrees. For the minimum edge-cutting mapping problem, we prove that the problem is NP-hard and give a fixed-parameter algorithm with running time O(n(2.14)k), where n is the number of vertices in the two input pedigrees and k is the number of edges to be cut. This algorithm is useful in practice when comparing two similar pedigrees.

123013.value: In this project, we studied two problems, the exemplar break-point distance problem and the tree comparison problem. We have designed efficient algorithms for those two problems. We also developed a software package for the first problem. Besides, we have studies other important problems in computational biology such as predicting protein functions by using unbalanced random walk algorithm on three biological networks, protein–protein interface prediction based on hexagon structure similarity, haplotype assembly, and exploring consensus RNA substructural patterns using subgraph mining, etc.

123313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
123313.value: 最近由研究者个人开发了基于车道数量出法的数学规划方法去为独立和多个连续路口的信号控制做设计。按照惯例，交通流量和路口几何大小需要作为输入信息。本研究将结合路口信号控制和络网几何一并做设计。车辆可行的路线按他们不同的出发地和目的地的位置将取决于城市的网络几何和路口的连接状况，车道的用途和车道上方向指示的标记是允许道路使用者在行车线道上转动方向的。城市网络的实际性能取决于所有用户车辆经历的总延迟和列队长度。良好的路口设计是路网连接好坏的重要因素。该设计的问题是一个复杂的数学问题，数学问题的性质是非线性(和非凸性) 。研究者提出一个三阶段的方法去解决最优化问题。第一级网络配置将被视为从上游路口到下游的路口可行方向的设计。在第二阶段，从个人车道用法，车道标志线所表示的二进制类型的变量在个别路口的信号设置的模式和方面将被确定。这些可以做成一个网络进行详细的计算和评价。第三阶段将是基于一组优化的信号时序，包括偏移，周期时间，和其他信号时序。此外，基于路径的流量均衡分配网络与实际车辆排队发展的特殊考虑将迎刃而解。它可以防止下游车辆堵回上游路口。三个阶段的问题就解决了优化算法的过程，涉及到遗传算法，分支定界技术标准的，牛顿的基于梯度的优化算法。 研究结果将能够提高信号控制网络的实际设计，在城市路网，上游路口到下游路口相距甚近，更好的几何设计，车道用法和车道上转动方向，更好的交通信号控制设置适当的序列和精确的信号定时，整体更少的延迟和更短的车辆队列一定会实现。

123313.label: Realisation of objectives
123313.value: For study objective 1: In the journal paper entitled "Lane-Based Optimization for Macroscopic Network Configuration Designs" published in July 2017 collects the new formulation for extending the lane-based junction optimization concept to optimize the network link connectivity by setting up different lane markings on approach lanes. And these lane markings permitting turns at individual intersections can be connected by series of (upstream) intersection to (downstream) intersection from an origin node down to a destination node forming a set of feasible (vehicle movement) paths. If the users' given OD pattern is non-empty, the new design approach must ensure at least one feasible path connecting the first upstream intersection (where the origin node is located) and the last downstream intersection (where the destination node is located). So on and so forth, the signalized network configuration could be constructed and optimized to realize the study objective 1. For study objective 2: The two published journal papers entitled "Lane-Based Optimization for Macroscopic Network Configuration Designs" and "Refining Lane-Based Traffic Signal Settings to Satisfy Spatial Lane Length Requirements" published in July 2017 define (i) traffic signal settings including green duration times and traffic signal cycle length, spatial queue lengths, lane saturation flow rates, assigned lane flows, assigned path flows as key continuous variables and (ii) lane markings, existence of paths serving OD demand flows and order of traffic signal displays as key discrete variables (containing both binary and integer). These variables are to constitute the junction geometries and to support traffic signal controls. In the new formulation, users' given OD flow patterns are key inputs and assigned path flows and assigned lane flows are being governed as flow conservation requirements ensuring that the exact demand flows are able to distribute onto network lanes (or links). From the study results in which a 4-signalized intersection network has been modeled and multiple path choices moving across different intersections and approach lanes to reach destination nodes (from origin nodes) have also been modeled, it is found that the users' given OD demand flows would be able to split to use different paths (i.e. network links/lanes) through the supports of respective lane markings to arrive destination nodes (from different origin nodes). To achieve the flow conservation requirements and to balance the assigned lane (or path) flow intensities, the reserve capacity of the network OD matrix is optimized. Any deviation from the optimized lane flow assignment results, the equilibrium performances of all the modeled intersections would not be achieved. And the optimization problem is formulated as a Binary-mix-integer-linear-programming (BMILP) problem for satisfying the study objective 2. For study objective 3: Having formulated successfully the new lane-based signalized network design problem into a BMILP in study objective 2, P.I. and the research assistant helpers have utilized a commercial package with a standard GUROBI solver to solve the network design problem modeled by TRANSYT 14. The numerical results have been successfully obtained and reported in the publications mentioned above. For the numerical signalized network model, a 4-intersection with 2-approach and 2-exit lane problem with 4 OD pairs requires 405 binary variables, 212 continuous variables, and 1,955 linear governing constraints. The BMILP problem takes less than 5 minutes to be solved. All individual lane marking arrows for all individual intersections are optimized so that the signalized network configurations are also optimized to let through the users' given 4x4 OD demand flows. With additional spatial queue length requirements for modeling short lanes (with limited vehicle holding capacities), then the solution process needs to undergo multiple stages until optimal traffic signal settings are converged to minimize or even avoid (if possible) overflowing along all approach lanes. To verify the effectiveness of the optimized traffic signal settings mainly to reduce the long cycle time to allow more frequent changes of the right-of-way for the conflicting traffic movements, a VISSIM simulation model has been applied to simulate the resultant mixed discrete-continuous traffic signal settings demonstrating the effectiveness to avoid overflowing in a numerical example.

123313.label: Major findings and research outcome
123313.value: 1. By introducing a common flow multiplier to scale a given network OD matrix, the demand flows could be adjusted across an urban signalized network. This effect would also influence the turning flow intensities across all individual signalized intersections within the network. It is found that the optimized path flows and lane flows could be varied until they all match the given OD flow pattern for conservation. It is well-established that turning flows from different intersection approaches at individual signalized intersection could affect the designs of lane markings and traffic signal settings. Their interactions have been successfully modeled using new mathematical constraints and reported in a journal paper entitled "Lane-Based Optimization for Macroscopic Network Configuration Designs" published in July 2017. 2. In the numerical experiment using a 4-signalized intersection with 2 approach and 2 exit lanes network, it is found that different path flows (not evenly distributed across utilized lanes) have been optimized to satisfy the flow conservation constraints. For heavy OD pairs, more than 1 path flow is found. It reveals that the new design method is capable to balance and share the actual loadings (incoming traffic flows at an intersection). These findings have been reported in a journal paper entitled "Lane-Based Optimization for Macroscopic Network Configuration Designs" published in July 2017. 3. When traffic lanes connecting upstream and downstream signalized intersections are short with limited holding capacities, traffic signal settings and lane marking patterns should be well integrated and co-operated to prevent overflowing. When the lane-based model adopting an unrealistic point-queue system is enhanced by taking actual queue development, queue lengths, and lane holding capacities into considerations, it is found that operating long cycle times should be discouraged. Shorter cycle times should be operated to allow more frequent changes of right-of-way for conflicting traffic movements so as to avoid overflowing. This has been documented in a journal paper entitled "Refining Lane-Based Traffic Signal Settings to Satisfy Spatial Lane Length Requirements" published in July 2017.

123313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
123313.value: 1. For the lane-based design framework, the optimization model designs the best set of lane markings and traffic signal settings for practical implementations. However, whether or not all users or drivers will strictly follow the settings is uncertain. Operators set up the rules (of the game) inside a signalized network to try to achieve optimal performances. If users and drivers do not follow the rule, the expected optimal performances must not be achieved. To reduce such discrepancies, large scale traffic surveys and continuous system monitoring must be conducted to collect the actual implementation outcomes for further analysis and refinements. If sufficient information is collected to generate a big database, then further evaluations and analysis of the big data become viable to repair the potential deviations from the operators' expectations and road users' patterns. In the study, our mathematical model introduces some fine-tuning parameters and sensitivity factors to modify the model outputs. By further minimizing the errors between the model outputs and observed outcomes, the model developed in the study could be enhanced for higher efficiency and accuracy.

123313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
123313.value: Traffic signal settings are important aspects of urban traffic controls. Proper lane marking arrows painting on ground showing allowable turn directions for drivers are even more significant to influence the overall performances of every signalized intersection within an urban network. To permit road users or drivers to make series of turns in consecutive intersections is the land marking design which is critical for road users or drivers from different origin nodes to arrive their respective destination nodes efficiently. The study has introduced new design constraint sets to ensure the given OD demand flow pattern can be distributed onto different approach lanes at signalized intersections satisfying the path flow and lane flow conservation requirements. Traffic signal settings are also optimized to ensure all individual signalized intersections within an urban network are performing well.

123613.label: Project Title(Chinese)
123613.value: 22纳米CMOS工艺的静电放电的防护

123613.label: Project Objectives
123613.value: This project aims at exploring the ESD protection strategies for the 22 nm CMOS technology. We shall focus on the designs of SCR-embedded LDMOS structures based on the 22 nm CMOS process, so as to achieve a small on-state resistance, narrow operation windows and high-robustness ESD protection clamps for advanced CMOS circuit applications. We shall conduct a statistical study on the distributions of the dielectric breakdown, of the drain punchthrough and of the threshold voltage of MOS devices fabricated using the 22 nm technology, so as to determine the ESD design window. We shall investigate the ESD strike on the dielectric breakdown, on the charge trapping and on the leakage current characteristics of the high-k gate dielectric film. We shall investigate the robustness and other reliability issues like the leakage current characteristics, the charge trapping and the multiple zapping-induced robustness degradation etc., of the proposed structures.

123613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
123613.value: Electrostatic discharge (ESD) is one of the major causes for the fatal failure of electronic components. The transient electrostatic voltage generated by a human body or by a machine may exceed several thousand volts, a value which is large enough to instantly melt the metal interconnects in an integrated circuit (IC) and to produce thermal runaway of a semiconductor material. ESD often strikes on a component during its manufacturing, transportation, during the assembly process on a printed circuit board, as well as during the daily operation of an electronic product. Consequently, many efficient ESD protection devices have been developed to secure the operation and to enhance the robustness of electronic products. However, with the newly developed 22 nm fabrication technology for the next generation of CMOS ICs, a number of new challenges came up. The 22 nm transistors are known to be operated at much smaller voltages because of their thinner gate oxide and their shorter gate length, which make these devices more vulnerable to various ESD-related damages. Lower voltage operation conditions require new ESD protection devices that must be still as robust as those used in the previous technology nodes. This narrowed design window would impose the development of some new device structures. The present work aims at developing some novel ESD protection devices/schemes for the 22 nm technology applications. We shall focus on structures based on silicon-controlled rectifier (SCR), with some low-voltage triggering schemes and electric field redistribution techniques to achieve a high robustness and high-efficient ESD protection. 靜電放電是導致電子部件致命性失效的主要原因之一。由人體或機器產生的瞬態靜電的電壓可高達数千伏特,这足以在瞬間把集成電路中金屬互聯層熔斷以及導致半導體材料熱逃逸。靜電放電通常發生在器件的製造、運輸，印刷電路板裝配，以及電子產品的日常操作中。因此，目前已研製出許多有效的靜電放電（ESD）防護器件，以保障電子產品的操作及增強其穩固性。然而，對於新一代互補型金屬-氧化物-半導體（CMOS）集成電路而言，新的22 nm 工藝制程面臨著諸多新挑戰。由於其极薄的柵氧化層厚度、更短的柵溝道長度、更低的工作電壓，這導致其更容易受到各種靜電放電現象導致的損害。低電壓工作條件也要求新一代的ESD保護器件必須保證與此前技術節點中的防護器件一樣的稳固和可靠。此外,在較小的設計窗口條件下,更需要开發出新型的器件結構。我們的研究目标旨在為22 nm 工藝開發一些新型ESD防護器件及方案。我們將着重研究基於可控矽整流器（SCR）結構结合一些低壓觸發方案及電場再分布技術，来實現稳固和高效的靜電防護方案。

123613.label: Realisation of objectives
123613.value: The device size of CMOS technology continues to be downscaled further which leads to some reliability issues as the scaled devices are less robust again thermal and high-voltage stresses. In addition, electrostatic discharge (ESD) from human body or during transportation become ever serve for the new mobile applications and the more frequent man-machine interaction in modern electronic products. These bring us additional challenges for the integrated circuit design other than the performance enhancements. This project aims at exploring the ESD protection strategies for the 22 nm node CMOS technology. We focused on the designs of SCR-embedded LDMOS structures based on the 22 nm CMOS process. This project has conducted quite comprehensive study on various scheme for implementing suitable ESD clamp within the specified design windows for the CMOS technology under 28 nm nodes. The downsizing of CMOS technology into the decananometer range has called for the redesign of the ESD protection devices because of the constraints of lower operation voltage and smaller breakdown voltage of the ultrathin gate oxide. The first attempt was on the exploration of the characteristics and the limitations of Zener-diode based electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection schemes used in earlier electronic products. The designs were implemented with the conventional epitaxial silicon substrate with traditional VDMOS process. Layout dependent characteristics were investigated which provides useful information for the diode string-triggered silicon controlled rectifier (SCR) ESD protection structure [1]. Vacuum capacitor/vacuum transistor with extremely high breakdown field may be potential devices to be used for ESD protection/extreme condition has been briefly explored [2] although it is still not a compatible process of main stream technology at present. Focusing on the smaller ESD design windows, high robustness, and high area efficiency and mainstream CMOS process, Silicon-Controlled Rectifier (SCR) based structures seem to be the most promising approaches. We revisited various schemes proposed earlier in particular the ways to lower the trigger voltage of SCR and then proposed some new approaches to tune the SCR trigger voltage and holding voltage to meet the new technology requirements. The first attempt on this aspect is to trigger the SCR with Lateral Diffused Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (LDMOS) [3]. Results show that the safe operating area of LDMOS shrank pronouncedly due to the walk-in of trigger voltage caused by the weak spot filament created/grown near the drain region under some ESD strikes. Yet this issue can be solved by isolating the drain. However, the structure is still not robust enough when they were operated at higher temperatures. More promising structures we found were the GGMOS embedded SCR and diode string triggered SCR [4-5]. We had proposed a double-snapback silicon-controlled rectifier (DS-SCR) by embedding a gate-grounded NMOS (GGNMOS) structure [4]. By validating with real fabricated samples and TCAD simulations, the double snapback mechanism enables a lower trigger voltage and high holding voltage which meet the design windows as specified by the 28 nm CMOS process. Further geometrical parameter tunneling may make the design be suitable for shorter gate length. Another promising structure is still based on SCR with additional snapback but using a two-dimensional diode string to trigger the SCR [5]. This scheme significantly lower the trigger voltage which make the SCR be suitable for the narrowed ESD design window. Compared with the GGNMOS triggering scheme, diode trigger method required much larger silicon area. A smart design is to direct the triggering current to both longitude and lateral directions through the parasitic diodes and the P-Well. It saves the chip area for realization while maintaining sufficient triggering current. Optimization was done by varying several device parameters and the best ESD robustness obtained was over 53 mA/μm which was about 65% larger than that of a simple SCR with using the same technology and similar size. Comprehensive studies on the characteristic degradation due to non-fatal ESD strike had been conducted. By applying weak ESD strikes on drain and gate electrodes of the transistors, the transistors do not break down but the multiple strike can lead to significant threshold voltage and subthreshold slope degradation [6-7]. The degradation behaviors are different for source-drain and gate strikes. These results could be explained in line with the charge trapping in the gate dielectric and the generation of channel hot carriers. These observations have great practical implication and shed new light to the ESD study. In particular, a CMOS circuit with excellent ESD robustness by adopting the specified ESD protection scheme may still be damaged by a sequence of non-fatal ESD strikes which was not considered to be able to damage the circuit and was not taken into account in designing the ESD protection circuits. A model regarding this issue is yet to be developed. Additional technical implication is that specified design windows may need to be revised in order to take the non-fatal ESD-induced degradation into account. We are completing a technical paper based on these results and will be submitted for publication soon.

123613.label: Major findings and research outcome
123613.value: The works have yielded two practical ESD protection structure designs based on SCR, 2D diode triggered SCR, and GGNMOS triggered SCR which are readily applicable to real IC protections with 22 to 28 nm CMOS technology. Further design window narrowing is possible by adjusting the geometry structure and doping concentration. This work has led to five technical papers being published in international peer-reviewed journals. Yet it may have more significant scientific values and should have some technical impacts are the observation of device characteristics degradation due to non-fatal multiple ESD strikes. We have been working on the theories and models during the last phase of this project. Two additional papers on this topic are under preparation. 123613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
123613.value: Although TSMC has already put 7 nm process for production, the mainstream technologies are still 14 nm and 22 nm in particular for I/O and interfacing circuits. The ESD protection schemes for these circuits are still quite primitive. There are still lots of reliability and ESD issues need to be overcome. It is proposed that the next generation device structure should be gate-all-around (GAA) nanowire transistor. The ESD characteristics of this kind of structure are yet to be explored. We had conducted electrical characterization on this device structure and found some abnormally characteristics of GAA nanowire transistors. As the gate lengths as well as the source/drain doping level were well beyond the punchthrough conditions, we ascribed this observation to the charge transport along the corners/boundaries of the nanowires. Temperature dependent characteristics were also investigated. Corners and surfaces of the nanowires thus play an important role for ultra-short nanowire transistors and that calls for shape of nanowire optimation for device design. Our next research plan is to study the ESD reliability of this kind of transistors. We believe that the corner effects should help to improve the ESD reliability of the devices.

123613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
123613.value: Electrostatic discharge (ESD) is one of the major causes for the fatal failure of electronic components. The transient electrostatic voltage generated by a human body or by a machine may exceed several thousand volts, a value which is large enough to instantly melt the metal interconnects in an integrated circuit (IC) and to produce thermal runaway of a semiconductor material. As the transistor size is reduced, i.e., with thinner gate oxide and shorter gate length, the devices are more vulnerable to various ESD-related damages. Meanwhile, ESD protection become harder because of the smaller operation window for allowable voltage range. This work aims at developing some novel ESD protection devices for the 22 nm technology applications. By lowering the triggering voltage of a silicon-controlled rectifier with a diode string or a gate-grounded MOS transistor, a second snapback characteristic was obtained. The new characteristics of ESD clamps with smaller trigger voltage and holding voltage meet the design window specifications and provides a high robustness ESD protection with less silicon area. We further observed significant characteristic degradations when a MOS device is exposed to a series of non-fatal multiple ESD strikes. This observation have some technical implications on the design window specifications.

123813.label: Project Objectives
123813.value: To develop a novel technique for the study of liquid lubrication in bio-tribology. To quantify the growth of the protein adsorption layer on surfaces lubricated by synthetic synovial liquids. To delineate the growth characteristics of the non-uniform adsorption layer of the protein from synthetic synovial fluids, and to explore the possibility of protein adsorption control in the tribological design of artificial joints. To describe the lubricating effects of the complex synovial lubricating film, that consists of a fluid layer and an absorption layer. To present a theoretical model that describes the synovial liquid lubrication in the regime of thin film lubrication with incorporation of the adsorption layer.

123813.value: 本申請專案主要研究人工植入體摩擦學的基本問題，以改善它們的服役壽命。目前人工植入體面臨的主要挑戰是保證足夠的壽命避免病人再次進行手術。人工關節失效的原因比較複雜。一個主要因素是承載面的磨損和損壞。這是一個必須解決的摩擦學問題，包括改善潤滑和減小磨損。近年，在材料學領域完成了大量的研究，但潤化機理方的研究卻有所忽視。 在自然關節潤滑中，蛋白質的吸附扮演重要角色。但在薄膜潤滑條件下，有關人工關節液吸附膜的形成機理，我們並不是特別清楚。研究人員做了大量的工作去探究有關蛋白質的吸附及其對假體材料摩擦學性質的影響，這些研究主要沿兩個方向獨立進行。一個是從物理化學和熱力學的角度研究關節液蛋白吸附的基礎問題，其工作條件不同於真正的關節。第二個方向是由摩擦力和磨損的測量來評價蛋白質吸附膜的效應。實際上，對真正潤滑條件下的吸附膜進行描述可以更深入地理解上述摩擦和磨損的測量結果。但是，上述兩條獨立的研究路線並不能做到這一點，甚至有時是互相矛盾的。因為吸附膜的性質由潤滑的條件決定。本項工作將致力於將兩方面的研究融合。它的創新性在於實現真正潤滑條件下蛋白質吸附膜和關節液潤滑的測量。 本研究組已經成功地開發了新的面接觸油膜光學測量系統。面接觸是低副的，恰好和關節的接觸相仿。系統中一個接觸面是透明的圓盤，有利於光干涉的測量和接觸面的即時觀察。已完成的人工關節滑液試驗表明蛋白質在材料表面的吸附是非均勻性的和選擇性的。這些領人鼓舞的前期結果，導出本項目繼續進行詳細和系統研究的必要。建立能夠同時確定吸附膜厚度和折射率的光學測量方法。主要研究吸附膜的生長規律，及通過實驗和理論研究闡述人工關節滑液的潤滑機制。 本專案的關鍵點為：(a) 建立新的試驗方法，實現折射率和膜厚的同時測量，進而定性和定量地評價吸附膜的形成和分佈；(b) 闡明接觸條件和關節滑液的成分對滑動表面蛋白質吸附的影響；(c) 改進假體植入設計和材料開發策略，優化蛋白潤滑效應，減小磨損。我們相信通過本項目獲得的新技術及知識能夠應用在與蛋白質吸附相關的領域。長遠看，本項目將貢獻於假體表面科學及化學的研究創新，以及通過使用類蛋白油品添加劑發展低速摩擦副的潤滑新技術。

123813.label: Realisation of objectives
123813.value: (Objective 1) This study mainly made use of an optical slider-on-disc test rig to simulate conformal sliding contacts of artificial/nature joints. A two-medium approach was proposed to estimate the adsorption film thickness. In this approach two mediums (air and water) are employed to produce two different optical path lengths for a wedge purposely set between the slider and the disc, and the thickness of the adsorption film can be obtained readily. An electrochemical workstation has also been incorporated into the test rig to get the electric signals to assess the corrosion process. However, the two-medium approach can only be used off-line to get the adsorption film thickness, and lots of sliders have to be employed for measurement of adsorption film thickness vs. time. To realize on-line measurement of the adsorption film, another approach was proposed with two stripes of thin Cr film coated near the two side-edges of the slider. The Cr stripes serve as a reliable reference and the shift of the fringe on the steel surface due to the growth of the absorbed protein layer can be detected by comparing to the same order dark fringe formed on the Cr surface. Hence, the optical thickness of the absorbed protein layer can be obtained. (Objectives 2 and 3) The present project successfully characterizes the protein adsorption on the slider surfaces. The updated test rig and the proposed two-medium approach enable measurement of adsorption film growth under different speeds, loads and slider inclinations. Generally under thin fluid film lubrication, the synthetic synovial fluid (the BSA aqueous solution) shows adsorption films in two modes. One is a continuous thin layer at the inlet area and the other is discrete protein aggregates on other area. The present measurement was well correlated to the observation of SEM and optical microscopy. For further understanding the formation mechanism of the adsorption film of proteins, the compositions of the film were characterized by relative atomic concentration of elements versus depth from the surface detected by XPS. And it is demonstrated that corrosion, which appears firstly at the inlet side of the slider, is responsible for the observed adsorption patterns. The protein adsorption under impact conditions have also been studied by a ball-on-disc contact. The results showed that the adsorption film thickness of the protein under dynamic impact is much higher than that under static conditions. It has been revealed that the adsorption film building is better on the metal ball (hydrophobic disc) surface than that on the ceramic ball (hydrophilic disc) surfaces. The globulin has better adsorption performance than albumin. (Objective 4) With the slider-on-disc test rig, the hydrodynamic lubrication film of the simulated synovial fluids can be measured at different speeds and loads, showing that the film thickness increases with increasing speeds and decreasing loads. In the meantime initial corrosion was detected optically. Corrosion potentials and corrosion currents were recorded by the electrochemical station, revealing some intrinsic characteristics of the synergistic interactions among lubrication, corrosion and adsorption. The lubricating effect of the adsorption layer was studied in a dry contact, and it was revealed that a low friction could be achieved. (Objective 5) In the present study, not only adsorption layer but also surface corrosion were simultaneously observed and the slider surface is re-profiled accordingly. This re-profiling effect was checked by a parallel-plane sliding configuration. However, no new lubrication mechanism was found. Thus, this project has not done much in the theoretical modeling work.

123813.label: Major findings and research outcome
123813.value: 1. New approaches for the measurement of adsorption films The main apparatus used in this project is an optical slider-on-disc test rig, which was developed by my research team. However the existing version of the test rig is incapable of measuring adsorption film and cannot be applied to the present project. This project then proposed two approaches for adsorption film measurement, both of which make use of the optical path lengths to infer the adsorption film thickness under off-line and on-line situations. With these new approaches, the adsorption film growth can be measured and some intrinsic characteristics have been recognized. (Presented in conference paper [2]) 2. Growth of the protein adsorption layer and corrosion on surfaces lubricated by synthetic synovial liquids. The formation of adsorption layer of synthetic synovial fluids (BSA+PBS solutions) and corrosion behaviours under hydrodynamic lubrication conditions was uncovered. It was found that corrosion on the steel slider surface grew from the inlet first and then to the outlet and quick corrosion occurred at high sliding speeds. Corrosion was found to promote protein adsorption. Two types of protein adsorption, namely, continuous thin layer and discontinuous protein aggregate, were generated on the slider surface. The morphological features and chemical structure of the slider surfaces were analyzed using SEM, AFM and XPS. Results showed that the protein adsorption is spread over the steel surface heterogeneously. The films are apparently characterized by two layers. The top layer is in the form of protein agglomerates embedded in a gel-like matrix, and the bottom layer contains Cr+3/Fe+2/Fe+3-rich passive oxides. The organic-inorganic composite films can work as a solid lubricant to reduce friction. (Journal paper [2] and conference paper [2]). Moreover, corrosion potentials and currents were recorded by the electrochemical station, and the dependence of corrosion on speeds and loads were revealed. Growth of the protein adsorption layer was studied in a ball-on-disc contact under conditions of cyclic loading derived from the gait of human beings. It was found that impacting enhances protein adsorption. It has been revealed that the adsorption film building is better on the metal ball (hydrophobic disc) surface than that on the ceramic ball (hydrophilic disc) surfaces. At the same time, it was found that the adsorption film thickness was not related to the concentration of a single protein, and the globulin has better adsorption performance than albumin. 3. Synergetic interaction among lubrication, corrosion and adsorption. In this study it has been recognized that the lubrication behavior of synovial fluids could be influenced by the synergetic interaction among lubrication, corrosion and adsorption. The film thickness increases with increase in speed and decrease in loads. And the geometry of contact surfaces can be modified by corrosion at micro-scale so that the thin film thickness could be changed. On the other hand, the lubricating effect of the adsorption layer was studied by friction measurement in dry contact, and it was revealed that a low friction could be achieved. (Some details can be found in conference paper [1] and journal paper [2], and conference paper[1] won the Best Paper Awards in the 2014 International Conference on Engineering Tribology Technology). 4. A numerical solver to computation transient hydrodynamic lubrication. A two-dimensional numerical solver was successfully developed for the current testing condition-a hydrodynamic lubricated slider contact with an incompressible isothermal Newtonian lubricant. (Journal paper [1]).

123813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
123813.value: As the result of nature evolution, the joint of human beings/animals performs excellently as a natural bearing. Different mechanisms have been put forward to clarify the joint lubrication. Nevertheless not much is known about how the synovial liquid lubricates the joint. The water in the synovial liquid is a poor lubricant, and proteins therein are believed to contribute to the lubrication. In the present project, the featured custom-made test rig enables the study of lubrication of the aqueous protein solutions from the view point of synergetic interaction of lubrication, protein adsorption and corrosion. However the present data about the synergetic interaction was limited, in particular the dependence of the micro-corrosion on the lubrication parameters and the protein types. Therefore continuous investigation is expected, and the potential of the custom-made slider-on-disc test rig in the study on lubrication of synovial liquids deserves to be explored.

123813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
123813.value: Engineers lubricate machines with oil, but nature lubricates creatures with water. Usually pure water is poor in lubrication, but with added-in proteins it can lubricate tribo-pairs well, such as the synovial liquid, which is a water-based solution with proteins in human beings’ joints. Understanding how synovial liquid works is very important for articulating implants, synthetization of environment-friendly lubricants and development of bio-medical devices as well. Existing work assessed synovial liquids mostly from the view of wear and friction. There is knowledge vacancy about the behavior of synovial liquids in the regime of thin film lubrication, which is believed to be one of the dominating mechanisms in joint lubrication. The present project examines protein adsorption and lubrication of synthetic synovial liquids under full film lubrication conditions. For this purpose an optical tribometer was successfully developed with incorporation of new approaches to quantify protein adsorption film growth. The heterogeneous adsorption of protein on surfaces has been characterized in terms of both chemical components and morphological features, and synergetic interaction mechanism of adsorption, corrosion and lubrication has been proposed.

123913.label: Project Objectives
123913.value: CCA-Secure Leakage Resilient Encryption Tolerating Higher Leakage Rate – Most of the existing leakage resilient encryption schemes are CPA-secure (i.e. security against chosen plaintext attack). There are some generic methods for transforming CPA-secure encryption schemes to CCA-secure variants. The feasibility of applying similar generic methods onto leakage resilient encryption schemes is yet to be investigated. Furthermore, this objective is also to construct CCA-secure leakage resilient encryption tolerating higher leakage rate than existing ones, which, as of this writing, can only achieve 1/6 as the leakage rate. Highly Efficient and Practical Leakage Resilient Encryption and Digital Signature – In this objective, we target to construct leakage resilient encryption and digital signature schemes which have less computational complexity, shorter ciphertexts/signatures, shorter public keys, or fewer elements in the set of system parameters, when compared with existing ones. We target to build leakage resilient encryption and signature schemes which could be efficient enough for even portable and lightweight devices such as smart cards, where side-channel attacks are more likely to be launched on these devices. Leakage Resilient Cryptographic Variants – Though leakage resilient encryption and digital signature are the two most prominent topics in public key cryptography, there are many other important cryptographic primitives that should be investigated under the information leakage adversarial models. In this objective, we target to study the construction and security analysis of leakage resilient cryptographic variants such as attribute-based encryption, group signature, oblivious transfer, optimistic fair exchange, concurrent signature and a few related primitives.

123913.label: Major findings and research outcome
123913.value: There have been some results found in the literature on leakage resilient concurrent signatures for two communicating parties. However, it is unknown on how a corresponding security model and a provably secure scheme can be constructed if the setting is extended to multi-parties, namely, between three or more parties. In the paper on Extending Concurrent Signature to Multiple Parties, we formalized the multi-party concurrent signature and proposed a security model, and we further proposed a scheme which can be shown secure in the model we defined. We later further enhance the security of the scheme, and in paper Concurrent Signature without Random Oracles, we obtained a new concurrent signature scheme which can be proven secure in the standard model. In the paper CP-ABE with Constant-Size Keys for Lightweight Devices, we investigated and proposed an efficient ciphertext-policy attribute based encryption (CP-ABE) scheme which has low computational complexity and at the same time, supports partial keying information leakage. The result was further enhanced in another paper of us on Traceable CP-ABE: how to trace decryption devices found in the wild, in which we showed that a malicious user can be detected and identified even if the entire key is leaked regardless the leakage is by accident or in purpose. In the paper, we also proposed a black-box version which allows the public to identify a malicious user even if the secret keys are intentionally hidden in some kind of decryption devices or blackboxes.

123913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
123913.value: Our work can further be extended and it is worth investigating how to achieve similar set of features using lattice-based cryptographic techniques. The advantage of using lattice-based techniques instead of pairing-based ones as we used in this project is that the resulting schemes will have the potential of being proven secure under the post-quantum cryptographic era.

123913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
123913.value: The research results obtained under the support of this grant advanced our understanding on achieving higher security assurance under the scenarios where part of the secret keys of a cryptosystem has been compromised or leaked. This type of scenarios is very practical as the reverse engineering techniques nowadays are getting more and more advanced. Adversaries can recover part if not all of the secret keys of a cryptosystem through online and/or offline reverse engineering. The work we have done under the support of this research grant helps formalize the adversarial capabilities incurred by reverse engineering, and also contributes on devising new cryptographic techniques which can deter the reverse engineering. One of the main contributions of our work is to establish a theoretical foundation on the cryptanalysis and cryptographic techniques related to reverse engineering such as side channel attacks. We have made advancements on concurrent signatures as well as attribute-based encryption.

124013.value: 核能来自裂变或聚变中子的动能.不幸的是，动能还创建了核反应堆的功能材料和结构材料的损坏,包括障碍的人分开的有害辐射。很好地理解损伤积累过程中是必不可少的缓解反应堆材料的问题，这种方式创建的，负有直接后果反应堆寿命。这是一个问题的影响的成本核能和公众安全的重要途径。虽然最初的损坏和积累机制发生在原子尺度纳米/微微秒的特征时间，发生在反应堆损伤效应的体现在空间微米，时间尺度的天，周，年，甚至几十年，积累的尺寸与无穷小概率事件发生的天文数字。这就要求模型能够的连接宏观原子尺度机制的破坏作用。基于速率理论模型 平均场描述场面占优的，因为初期。但是，由于平均场采用近似，微观结构的发展空间相关的功能不能轻易建模。相场模型已制定研究相分离的形态材料中提供了一个机会来克服这个主要缺点，至少在原则上。既然这样，几个重要的问题还没有得到解决之前，这个方法可以有效地应用于模拟辐照损伤积累的影响。要解决这些问题是一个任务我们提供给承担的这项提议。

124013.label: Realisation of objectives
124013.value: The all-important issue that needs to be addressed in the phase-field model of void development is the correct void precipitation mechanism to use. In this regard, existent phase-field model has an obvious problem, which is the unphysically high vacancy concentration required for voids to precipitate. We traced this problem to the assumption, implicit or explicit, that void nucleation is a result of spinodal instability. The fact is, spinodal decomposition is not the only mechanism, nor is the mechanism used in conventional irradiation damage models to achieve void precipitation. Indeed, within classical nucleation theory, void nucleation occurs at much more realistic concentrations via the thermal decay of the metastable solution. In this project, we explained why it is incorrect to base the phase-field model on the spinodal instability instead of the classical nucleation theory, in which the nucleation barrier is to be overcome stochastically. The needed stochastic formulation is fundamentally different from existent deterministic phase-field model. We derived this formulation for the first time. We tested this scheme by comparing the predicted void densities at different temperatures with the existing results.

124013.label: Major findings and research outcome
124013.value: The application of phase-field modeling to void formation and growth under irradiation is analyzed. Here our focus is on the energy of the diffuse interfaces of the void system, which is customarily modeled by a Ginzburg-type gradient energy term with a parameterized coefficient. To correctly emulate the kinetics of void formation, the corresponding free-energy change is calibrated against the classical nucleation model, where the void–matrix boundary is well defined. We find that the gradient-energy coefficient may be conveniently treated as a constant independent of void size, even for voids down almost to the atomic size. We also find that the diffuse void interface in phase-field simulation has to be treated on an ultrafine spatial scale to reproduce the void energetic characteristics and growth behavior derived from the sharp boundary approach. Numerical calculations found that the developed phase-field model reproduces reasonably well the dynamical behavior of an individual void, well-known from the rate-theory treatment of void evolution. However, ultrafine characteristic spatial scales of the void-metal diffuse interface present a challenge to numerically efficient modeling of the evolution of a void ensemble under irradiation.

124013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
124013.value: Results of this project provides a firm basis for the mesoscopic-scale modeling of irradiation damage, linking the continuum phase-field model with the classical nucleation theory via many-body dynamics in a stochastic approach.

124013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
124013.value: Nuclear energy is derived from the kinetic energy of fission or fusion neutrons, which unfortunately also creates damage to the functional and structural materials making up the nuclear reactor. A good model of the damage accumulation processes is essential to mitigating reactor materials problems created this way, which bears direct consequence to issues that affect the cost of nuclear energy and public safety in a major way. Although the initial damage and accumulation mechanisms happen in the atomic scale with characteristic times of nano/pico-seconds, the manifestation of in-reactor damage effects occurs in spatial dimensions of meters through time scales of years, or even decades, through the accumulation of astronomical numbers of events occurring with infinitesimal probabilities. This calls for models capable of linking the macroscopic damage effects to atomistic scale mechanisms under a hostile environment of high stress and high temperature. The present project resolves a important issue in the mesoscopic modelling efforts in this area.

124113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
124113.value: Externally-bonded (EB) fibre reinforced polymer (FRP) is currently one of the most popular technologies for the rehabilitation (strengthening/repair/retrofitting) of concrete structures, largely due to its advantages in construction convenience. However, engineers and building authorities could be reluctant to use FRP due to concerns about its material brittleness and temperature sensitivity (including toxic gas emission under fire), along with the difficulties involved in bonding. Recently, the principal investigator (PI) collaborated with a material scientist (Co-I Lu) to successfully develop a strengthening scheme using a new type of nanomaterial – the surface mechanical attrition treated (SMAT) stainless steel sheet. The SMAT sheet is thin (about 1 mm), but has the high strength, lightweight, corrosion resistance and consequent construction convenience advantages of FRP while retaining the ductile nature of steel. It possesses the advantages of both steel and FRP while avoiding their weaknesses, which makes it an ideal material for structural rehabilitation. Because the SMAT sheet is so thin, the normal method of fastening steel plate with bolts is often insufficient, as the bolts can cut the thin sheet, providing insufficient dowel action for interfacial bonding. However, another mechanism – friction – can be used to supplement the interfacial bond in this case. Frictional bonds, such as friction-type steel joint connections, can be very strong. In fact, the PI has developed a highly effective friction dominant bonding system for FRP-concrete interfaces. A similar friction-based bonding technology can be used to enhance the SMAT sheet-concrete interface to provide a strong, robust, yet ductile interfacial connection. Such a connection will be applicable not only to SMAT sheets, but also to general high-strength yet thin and ductile reinforcing materials developed for future use. The main objective of the proposed project is to develop such a bonding system and its associated design methodology. Joint shear tests will first be conducted to identify an effective joint design and obtain test data for bond characteristics. The test results will then be used to develop the joint governing bond-slip relationships. Using the bond-slip relationship, design equations and guidelines for SMAT sheet strengthened RC beams can be derived from existing composite theory. Subsequently, RC beams strengthened with SMAT sheet will be tested to validate the efficiency of the new retrofitting system and accuracy of the developed design theory. 由于施工的方便，FRP是目前结构加固的常用材料。因为它的脆性和温度敏感性，以及与混凝土的粘结困难，工程师们对它却有所保留。最近，申请人与合作者吕坚教授合作，用SMAT钢板加固结构。SMAT材料具有钢材和FRP的优点，同时又避免了他们的缺点。这使它成为一种理想的结构加固材料。因为该材料较薄，一般用于钢板锚固的方法会割裂材料而不能适用。然而，另外一种粘结机理 - 摩擦 – 在此时可以用来增加粘结强度。因为摩擦强度可以很大，例如钢结构中的摩擦连接。申请人最近研发了一种高效的依靠摩擦的FRP粘结技术。该技术也能运用到SMAT钢板上，以达到增强粘结，提高延性的目的。其实该原理也可以运用到其它的高强高延性的片材上。所以本项目的目的是开发一种适用于高强薄片材料的一般粘结技术以及相应的设计方法。单剪试验将用来寻找一种合适的节点设计，以及确定界面的粘结特性。试验结果将用来建立一般粘结滑移关系。然后用复合结构力学的一般方法建立设计公式和方法。最后用加固结构试验来检验该方法的效果并用来验证所研发的设计理论。

124213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
124213.value: The multi-disciplinary research team consisting of researchers with expertise in robotics and automation, and biomedical and clinical research is proposing to develop a nano robotic manipulation system to conduct in-situ investigations of cell membrane receptors that are directly related to hypertension. The proposed nano robotic system will enable us to directly manipulate and sense cells in a nano and physiological environment. Results from this effort will be an invaluable resource for biomedical and clinical research, and generate a wealth of important insights/knowledge of biological relevance that will lead to the development of novel drug targets/drugs and therapies for the hypertension and other disease indications. The research and development of robotic and automation technologies are facing great challenges presently in discovering new directions to move beyond half a century successful development. It is apparent that nano robots, especially bio-nano robots are in a competitive edge to break new grounds and operational innovations in the development of robotic and automation technologies. In addition, the highly-regulated and fast-paced pharmaceutical industry has been challenged with increasing demands for development of new innovative health care products, drugs and therapies for both humans and animals on a reduced cost base. The long term objectives of this proposed research directly address these demands by: (i) developing robotic tools with capabilities of visual and haptic display, chemical, physical and biological sensing and manipulation in nano biological environment; and (ii) using such robotic tools for the investigation of dynamic and complex interactions between membrane proteins at the single molecular level. The results of this effort will cast profound scientific impact on the development of new robotics and automation technologies which would enable us to sense, manipulate and assemble in nano and biological environment. Furthermore it will provide "game-changing" technologies to revolutionize biomedical research and drug discovery via innovations. This proposed research is built upon existing collaborations between the team members and the recent advances in atomic force microscopy, robotics, computer, nanotechnology, and biomedical sciences. Upon successful completion and execution of this proposed research, we will be uniquely and competitively positioned to achieve our long term objectives. The development of bio-nano robotic and automation technologies will advance biomedical research, leading to development of drugs that target therapies for unmet disease indications. This will in turn mark a leap forward in biomedical research, and ultimately improve the health and life quality of mankind. 由機器人與自動化領域以及生物醫學與臨床領域的研究人員組成的多學科交叉研究團隊計劃開發一種納米機器人操作系統，該系統將針對與高血壓疾病直接關聯的細胞膜受體進行原位研究。該納米機器人系統具備在納米與生理環境下直接對細胞進行操作以及感知的能力。該研究成果將會對生物醫學與臨床領域帶來不可估量的推動作用，同時，該研究將為治療高血壓以及其他疾病的新型藥物與靶點開發提供嶄新的思路。 在經歷了半個世紀的成功發展后，針對新方向的探索上，機器人與自動化技術的研究與開發正面臨巨大的挑戰。顯然，目前在機器人與自動化開發領域內，納米機器人尤其是生物納米機器人的研究正處在學科的最前沿并給整個學科帶來創新以及突破。另外，由於對新型健康護理產品、藥物以及治療方法的需求以及對成本降低的需求正在提升，高度集中以及快節奏的製藥行業正面臨越來越多的挑戰。本研究的長期目標將會滿足以下需求：（i）開發納米生物環境下具有視覺以及觸覺界面，并具備化學、物理以及生物檢測以及操作能力的機器人技術；（ii）利用該機器人技術，在單分子尺度上對細胞膜表面蛋白間動態而複雜的相互作用進行研究。該研究成果將會對新型機器人與控制技術的開發產生深遠影響，使我們可以在納米生物環境下完成感知，操作與組裝。此外，該系統將會帶來改變行業規則的影響力，給生物醫學研究與藥物開發行業帶來一次全新的革命。 本提議的研究建立在工作組成員已經建立的合作基礎，以及近年來原子力顯微鏡技術、機器人技術、計算機技術、納米技術與生物醫學等領域的發展與進步上。憑藉該研究的成功執行與完成，我們將處於獨特且具有競爭力的有利位置并達到我們的長期目標。生物納米機器人與自動化技術的開發將會對生物醫學研究產生極大的推動，為尚未解決的疾病提供靶向治療開發。該研究將會推動生物醫學研究更加快速的發展，同時最終提高人類的健康與生活質量。

124213.label: Realisation of objectives
124213.value: In the project, an AFM based nano robotic system was developed with the aim to manipulate and study biological objects at high resolution (Objective 1). By functionalizing the AFM tip with specific antibodies, the nanorobot is able to identify specific types of receptors on cells’ membrane (Objective 2 and 3). By locally updating the AFM image based on interaction force information and objects’ model during nanomanipulation, real-time visual feedback is obtained through the augmented reality interface. The AFM based nanorobotic system offers several advantages and capabilities for studying structure-function relationships of biological specimens. As a result, many biomedical applications can be achieved by the AFM based nanorobotic system. A prototype of an AFM based nano robotic system was developed, which includes 2 subsystems: the AFM system and augmented reality environment. The AFM system is the main part of the nanorobotic system and designed for imaging and manipulation. The augmented reality environment provides the operator a real-time interactive environment to view the real-time AFM image, directly control the tip motion and receive the force feedback of the tip and sample interaction through a haptic joystick. The real-time visual display is a dynamic AFM image of the operating environment, which is locally updated, based on the real-time force and the local scanning information as well as the object’s behavior models. The AFM nano robotic system was developed from the Bruker BioScope Catalyst that has a special designed scanning head that can be used to image biological samples in liquid. The closed-loop scanning head with a maximum XY scan range of 100 m X 100 m and a Z range of 7 m is connected to an AFM controller and the main computer. The AFM controller is responsible for running the main control program and providing an interface for users to change control parameters and view real-time data. A signal access module (SAM) provides an interface for external devices to access the AFM controller signal. Peripheral devices including an optical microscope and a charge-coupled device (CCD) camera are connected to the system. The inverted optical microscope and the CCD camera help the operator to locate the tip and adjust the AFM laser gun and also search for interesting areas on the biological sample. The augmented reality interface is implemented in a computer equipped with a haptic device. Through the signal access module, the cantilever deflection signal can be directly sent to the A/D convertor card inside the computer. The augmented reality environment provides enhanced media for the operator to view the real-time videolized AFM image and feel the force feedback during nanomanipulation. The videolized real-time visual display is a continually dynamic AFM image of the operating environment. With the development of the AFM based nanorobotic system, their applications in biomedical areas were demonstrated. Studies of neuronal morphogenesis under stimulation of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors were conducted by AFM imaging. A representative AFM height image of live SH-SY5Y neuronal cells was obtained and the corresponding cross-sectional height profile indicates that the height of the cell was approximately 3 μm. Since the cell was relatively soft, the cell membrane was deformed by the AFM tip during the scanning and the deformation information of the entire cell was obtained from the deformation image and the cross-sectional deformation profile. The average deformation of the cell was about 250 nm. In the project, we applied AFM-based nanorobots to characterize and quantify biological binding interaction. AFM measurement showed the specific unbinding force between anti-AT1R antibody and AT1R was in the range of 50 - 120 pN. This investigation provides new avenues for mapping AT1R on living cells. In order to study the mapping of the angiotensin II (Ang II) receptor, functionalization of AFM tip was developed. Briefly, AFM tips (DNP-10, Bruker Nano, USA) were cleaned by ethanol solution and exposed to ultraviolet light for 30 mins. Then, they were immersed into 1% v/v (3-mercaptopropyl)-trimethoxysilane (MPTMS) / toluene solution, and the mixture was incubated for 2 hours. A thiol terminated monolayer was incorporated on the AFM tip surface by reaction with MPTEM. Washing with toluene for 3 times, the tips were placed in 1 mg/ml Maleimide-PEG-NHS (Nanocs Inc., USA) which dissolved in chloroform. The linker composed 45 PEG units with the length was in the range of 8-12 nm, which would benefit to recognize antigens and promote specific binding events. After 2-hours incubation, the tips were rinsed with fresh chloroform. Next, we transferred them to 0.4 μg/ml anti-AT1R antibody solution for 30 mins to attach AFM tips with the AT1R antibodies by covalent bonds, which would ensure the strength was larger than the interaction between antibodies and AT1R. Finally, the antibody functionalized tips were immersed in phosphate buffer solution (PBS), and the tips were preferred to be employed immediately to avoid degeneration in long time preservation. AFM-based molecule detection has been introduced for investigating special molecules unbinding interactions. Interactions between anti-AT1R antibodies and AT1R were monitored on the H295R cells. Considering the antibody-receptor dissociation force is usually quite small, commercially available cantilevers with a low spring constant (DNP-10 D) were used. Antibody used here was corresponding to human Angiotensin II Type 1 Receptor amino acid 1-100 at N terminal. During the nanoindentation process, it may bind to the extracellular part of AT1R once the AFM tip contacted with the sample surface. Delay time of 1 s was needed between the tip approach and retraction process to increase the contact time of the antibodies and the receptors. Subsequently, the tip began to retract. When the unbinding event occurs, a deflection shift could be obtained upon cantilever retraction from the surface of cell membrane. The typical retraction curves were shown in Fig. 4, and the unbinding events were labeled by arrowheads. During the retraction process, the cantilever deflection shift was caused by the unbinding event between anti-AT1R antibody and AT1R on the cell surface. And the deflection signal could be directly converted into a force by deflection sensitivity calibration. By performing and recording numerous approach-retraction cycles, antibody-receptor disassociation force could be calculated. Force-distance curve analysis indicated that the unbinding force between anti-AT1R antibody and AT1R was in the range of 50-120 pN. The unbinding events were distributed in the range of 0.5 μm-2.5 μm from the contact point between the tip and the cells. It is likely possible that the AFM tip stretched several receptor units. Unbinding forces of antibody-receptor were collected and analyzed from the force-distance curves, which were obtained on the living cell membranes. In the complex dissociation process, the AFM cantilever detected a rupture signal. After stretching from cell surface, force curves with single jump or multiple jumps were observed. This deflection shift should be caused by breaking noncovalent interactions include electrostatic forces, hydrogen bonds, van der walls forces and hydrophobic forces occurs in the specific binding. With the successfully development of the AFM-based nano robotic manipulator, it can be used to study biological cells. Besides, the functionalized nano end effector enables the specific detection on specific target efficiently. The advancement of the system would bring a lot of possible biological study in different aspects.
