124213.label: Major findings and research outcome
124213.value: With the development of the AFM based nanorobotic system, it enables direct micro/nano manipulation of target through visual display. An AFM cantilever can be considered as a nano end effector. The deflection signal of the end effector can be directly sent to a computer for further processing in the augmented reality environment. This provides enhanced media for the operator to view the real-time AFM image and feel the force feedback during nanomanipulation [J1]. Major applications of using the developed system in biomedical areas were demonstrated. For example, studies of neuronal morphogenesis under stimulation of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors were conducted by AFM nanorobot [J2]. To study the morphogenesis of SH-SY5Y cells under stimulation of NMDA receptors, AFM images of normal and NMDA treated cells were obtained and compared, respectively. The surface of the NMDA treated neuron was relatively rough and many protuberances appeared and aggregated in the soma. Another application is related to the study of Amyloid peptide beta (Aβ) which is the main component of the amyloid plaques present in the patient brains of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) [J3][J4]. The AFM nano robot allows us to monitor the Aβ1-40 aggregation process and directly obtain structural characteristics in an aqueous environment without any special treatment. The result of Aβ1-40 incubated in HBSS may offer a new direction for cytotoxicity and cell mechanical property test. Aβ1-40 oligomers, the most toxic formation, were apparent in all of the culture system after several hours of growth. Therefore, this study will be helpful to guide the Aβ1-40 analysis in cellular level, as well as to identify the cytotoxicity mechanism of Aβ1-40 in the cell culture solutions. Specific molecular recognition between antibody and receptor on cell membrane plays a central role in biological research. We applied AFM nano robot to characterize and quantify binding interaction between anti-AT1R antibody and AT1R on H295R cells [C3]. We functionalized the AFM tip with this anti-AT1R antibody via covalent bond. Thus, during the nanoindentation process, it may bind to the extracellular part of AT1R once the AFM tip contacted with the sample surface. In the detection process, the complex dissociation force between the antigen and antibody could be monitored as a rupture event in the cantilever retraction process. Understanding antibody-receptor recognition binding on cells may facilitate molecular recognition. This investigation provides new avenues for mapping membrane protein on living cells.

124213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
124213.value: After the invention of AFM, it is considered as a powerful nanotool to investigating the surface information, measuring the forces between probe and sample. The advancement of this project brings the new capability to the system to interact the target biological object in real time. Further development such as smaller cantilever with superior response time makes it possible to directly observe dynamic process of bimolecular interactions, such as instability of microtubules and beta amyloid assembly in supported lipid bilayer. In the further research, the nano robot can be employed to monitor the dynamics damage of plasma membrane and cytoskeleton disassembly induced by Aβ42. Unlike electron microscope, AFM can be applied to study biological molecules in living organisms without special treatments. As most AFM modes can work well in fluid, a ligand can be tethered to the AFM tip to study a targeted receptor on a substrate. When the functionalized probe was brought to approaching the surface of substrate, ligand–receptor bond is formed. Subsequently, AFM tip is retracted from the surface which breaks the non-covalent bond between ligand and receptor. The unbinding force of receptor–ligand can be calculated from force–distance curve recorded by AFM nano robot.

124213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
124213.value: The significance of this project is to development a nano robotic system which is based on the atomic force microcopy. The nano robotic system enables manipulation of biological target at microscale and nanoscale level. As the roboic tip approaches the target, force between the target and the tip causes the deflection of the cantilever. This kind of deformation can be monitored and converted to mechanical information and force feedback information. Thus, it allows us to apply an accurate force to sample surface, which makes AFM as a promising tool to characterize biomaterials including tissues, cells and proteins. For example, AFM-based measurement can be used to evaluate a risk of some diseases via special biomarkers. Previous research found that Angiotensin II type 1 receptor is a principle effector molecule in maintaining blood pressure etc. In this case, the system can be applied as a promising tool to determine the spread of Ang II in living cells. It allows us to quantify the express of this membrane protein according to spatial distribution. With the significant different of cellular response measured by the nano robot, we can calculate density of AT1R and distinguish abnormal cells from healthy cells.

125013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
125013.value: Ultraviolet radiation (UV) exposure is an integral part of our solar spectrum and is a leading cause of skin cancer worldwide. However, small amounts of UV radiation are needed to aid production of Vitamin D in the human body. As such, UV radiation can be both helpful and harmful to the human population. UV radiation levels can be affected by many parameters with one being the level of shade and scatter conditions in the environment in question. When that environment is a large high-rise city, the level of UV radiation needs to be assessed over the entire cityscape and continually throughout the day. Large buildings cause significant shading and scattering effects for UV radiation. Often areas within the city are shaded for extended periods of time during the day whereas some areas may receive continual direct sunlight. These levels are expected to change dramatically throughout the year when the solar zenith angles change as well. For a city worker or someone who lives in this environment, his UV exposure levels may be quite low during winter months certainly compared to countryside or low-rise environments. Very little work has been performed in this area and we plan to assess these UV levels in Hong Kong city and compare UV exposure levels to Hong Kong countryside environments. We also plan to investigate the high-rise environments in two other countries for comparison. Cities of interest include Manhattan, New York, US, which is a similar high-rise city to Hong Kong and also Sydney, Australia, where the cityscape is slightly lower but higher UV levels are known to occur. To achieve these measurements we plan to use our newly developed technique using radiochromic films whereby measurements can be performed over an entire day period in many different sites in an effective manner. We also plan to further investigate other new and novel methods for UV dosimetry in these environments. The radiochromic films are a unique method for UV evaluation and provide the appropriate method for data collection. The use of handheld solid-state detectors would not be appropriate for such experiments as they would need to be positioned at each site for the day, requiring hundreds of meters and the cost would be incredibly excessive. We will employ our radiochromic film technique and perform hundreds of simultaneous measurements within the cityscape to provide a unique dose map of UV exposures. 紫外線是太陽光譜的一部分，也是導致皮膚癌的主因。然而，人體需要少量的紫外線輻射以幫助生產維生素D，因此，紫外線輻射對人類有益亦有害。紫外線輻射水平受到許多參數影響，包括遮蔭和散射的狀況，一個高樓城市的紫外線輻射水平評估，必須覆蓋整個城市並且是經整個日間內持續測量而作出的。大型建築物造成明顯的遮蔭和散射，一些地區會受到長時間的遮蔭，而另一些地區則可能會受到持續陽光直射，這些紫外線輻射水平亦會隨著一年四季太陽天頂角的改變而出現顯著的變化。在這樣的環境中居住或工作的人，在冬季所接受較低的紫外線水平，甚至可跟低樓城市環境或郊區相比。這方面的研究非常少，因此我們將會評估在香港市區內的紫外線水平，並跟香港郊區的紫外線水平作出比較。我們應用輻射變色膠片新開發的技術，可以有效地在許多不同的選點及在整個日間內持續進行這些測量。我們亦會進一步探索其它創新的方法來測定在這些環境中的紫外線放射量。輻射變色膠片提供了一個獨特而適當的方法以收集及評價紫外線數據。這樣的實驗如採用手持式固態探測器是不可行的，因為每個選點每一天都需要一台探測器，整個實驗就需要數以百計的手持式固態探測器，成本會變得無法承擔。我們將採用輻射變色膠片的技術，同一時間進行數以百計的測量，以提供一個獨特的紫外線照射劑量圖。

125013.label: Realisation of objectives
125013.value: During the first reporting period, we mainly focused on the first two project objectives: (1) Develop a new method for analysis of UV exposure in a city high-rise cityscape environment; (2) Initial investigations to optimize the detector for measurement and analysis of UV exposures; The Gafchromic EBT and EBT2 films we previously explored for ultraviolet (UV) dosimetry had already been superseded by the Gafchromic EBT3 films in the market, which had designs different from the previous versions. As there were no data or information regarding solar UV dosimetry available for this new EBT3 film, we had to start from scratch. In that reporting period, solar (UVA + UVB) exposure was assessed using the EBT3 film. The coloration change was represented by the net reflective optical density (Net ROD). Through calibrations against a UV-tube lamp, operational relationships were obtained between Net ROD and the (UVA + UVB) exposures (in J cm−2 or J m−2). The useful range was from ∼0.2 to ∼30 J cm−2. The uniformity of UV irradiation was crucial for an accurate calibration. For solar exposures ranging from 2 to 11 J cm−2, the predicted Net ROD agreed with the recorded values within 9%, while the predicted exposures agreed with the recorded values within 15%. Project objectives (1) and (2) were 100% achieved. After achieving the first two project objectives, we had the necessary tool for real-life measurements of UV exposures to work on the third project objective: (3) Measure UV exposures in differing high-rise city areas to produce UV exposure maps for detailed analysis; We measured the diffuse solar (UVA + UVB) exposures at various sites on the campus of City University of Hong Kong. Our data showed that the recorded UV exposures varied significantly with the amount of sky which could be "seen" by the films. For each measurement position, one film was placed horizontally and the other one was erected vertically. The angle of elevation h for the edge of an overhang at each measurement position was given by tan(h) = y/x where y was the vertical distance between overhang edge and measured point, while x was the horizontal distance between overhang edge and measured point. The data measured with horizontal EBT3 films could be either fitted with straight lines or 2nd order polynomial functions, while the data measured with vertical EBT3 films could all be fitted with straight lines. Project objective (3) was 100% achieved. During the second reporting period, we mainly focused on the project objectives: (4) Evaluate how buildings, reflection surfaces, concrete etc. in a high-rise city affect UV scattering and irradiance; (5) Compare UV exposure levels in the high-rise area to low-rise and countryside regions during the same time period; through computer simulations supported with satellite and surface measurements. We performed computer simulations to "predict" the UV exposures in some modeled city high-rise cityscape environments. In particular, we studied the reduction of solar UV radiation due to urban high-rise buildings. We used models (a radiative transfer model coupled to a building shading model), together with satellite and surface measurements, to study the un-obstructed and obstructed UV environments in Hong Kong. Seasonal patterns of the erythemal UV exposure rates were governed by solar zenith angles, seasonal variations of aerosol loadings and cloud effects. The radiative transfer modelling results agreed with measurements of erythemal UV exposure rates and spectral irradiances in UVA and UVB ranges. High-rise buildings and narrow road width (height to width, H/W, ratios up to 15) reduced the modeled total UV (UVA+UVB) radiation and leave 10% of the un-obstructed exposure rate at ground-level at noon. No more than 80% of the unobstructed exposure rate was received in the open area surrounded by 20-storey buildings. Our modelled reduction of UVB radiation in the urban environment was consistent with similar measurements obtained for Australia. However, our results in more extreme environments (higher H/W ratios) were for the first time reported, with 18% of the unobstructed exposure rate remained at the ground-level center of the street canyon. We have also developed a coupled model to capture the spatial and temporal variations of the changes in UV exposure rates due to the obstruction effects of buildings. The variations of solar total UV (UVA + UVB) exposure rates in different areas in Hong Kong during summer months were measured and relevant model predictions were evaluated. The maximum pedestrian-level total solar UV exposure rate was less than the un-obstructed exposure rate at any time, attributing to the prevailing reduction in the diffuse solar radiation due to the obstruction effects of distant buildings. Comparing with the measurements, our coupled model well captured the spatial and temporal variations of the reduction of UV exposure rates. By measurements, large reduction in the solar total UV exposure rate down to 12% of un-obstructed exposure rate due to the building obstruction effects was found, agreeing with our previous simulation results and results from an Australian megacity. On the other hand, building reflection from reflective curtain walls could have magnitude of 23% of the un-obstructed solar total UV exposure rate at the ground level. Project objectives (4) and (5) were 100% achieved.

125013.value: (a) The feasibility of using Gafchromic EBT3 films for assessing solar (UVA + UVB) exposures was explored. The coloration change was represented by the net reflective optical density (Net ROD). Through calibrations against a UV-tube lamp, operational relationships were obtained between Net ROD and the (UVA + UVB) exposures (in J cm−2 or J m−2). The useful range was from ∼0.2 to ∼30 J cm−2. In particular, the recorded solar (UVA + UVB) exposures changed with the angle of elevation for the edge of an overhang at each measurement position. The findings were reported (in peer-reviewed journal publication [3] in Part C). (c) We studied the reduction of solar UV radiation due to urban high-rise buildings. We used models (a radiative transfer model coupled to a building shading model), together with satellite and surface measurements, to study the un-obstructed and obstructed UV environments in Hong Kong. The radiative transfer modelling results agreed with measurements of erythemal UV exposure rates and spectral irradiances in UVA and UVB ranges. 125113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
125113.value: Bug localisation is one of the most difficult tasks in program development. Ineffective bug localisation severely affects the development schedule to serve users. As energy efficiency is becoming a prime concern in the implementation of many programs, problematic performance issues of programs are increasingly intolerable by users. This situation places heavy stress on the developers to locate performance bugs in software programs. On the other hand, real-world software applications such as MySQL, Chrome, and Thunderbird are all multithreaded. Effective fault localisation techniques should be applicable to locate faults in multithreaded programs. Both static and dynamic bug localisation techniques have been proposed. They either use predefined patterns to mine the source code of the program or contrast between executions with performance problems against executions without such problems to correlate program entities to performance anomalies. These techniques could not adequately handle applications suffering from performance issues with unseen patterns nor do they work well when the notion of executions with problematic performance issue is fuzzy or changes over time even for the same application. Unfortunately, the list of such patterns could be endless, and the same pattern may identify a true performance bug in one application but produce a false positive for another, as one size typically cannot fit all. Moreover, the distinction between executions with and without performance problems could be unscientific, because executions without performance bugs may still exercise the same fragment of code that causes performance issues in other executions. In this project, we propose to develop a novel performance bug localisation framework for multithreaded programs. It does not use any pattern and does not need to distinguish executions with and without performance issues. Our framework is based on trend estimation and curve formulation over a set of executions to identify the code locations that cause problematic performance behavior. To the best of our knowledge, no prior project by other researchers ever proposes to investigate performance bugs or other types of bugs in this direction. This project will provide a framework for the developers to combat against the performance issues of the programs that they are developing or maintaining. 缺陷定位是程序開發過程中最困難的任務之一。低效的缺陷定位往往嚴重影響到程序開發的進展，以致耽誤用戶使用程序的日程。由於能源效益正成為許多程序開發中的首要關注因素，用戶越來越難以容忍性能有問題的程序。這種情況使開發人員在定位軟件的性能缺陷時承受很大壓力。另一方面，現實生活中使用的應用軟件，例如MySQL，Chrome和Thunderbird，都是多線程的。因此，有效的缺陷定位技術須能適用於多線程的程序。 目前已提出的缺陷定位技術既有靜態的，也有動態的。現存的技術或者使用預定義的模式來挖掘程序的源代碼，或者通過比較沒有出現性能問題的正常執行和已出現性能問題的非正常執行，來尋找性能異常與程序實體間的關聯。可是，這些技術並不足以處理程序中含有未知模式的性能問題。同樣，如果程序執行中是否存在性能問題這一概念很模糊，甚或同一程序的性能問題會隨時間變化的話，這些技術就不能勝任。更可惜的是，這類預定義的模式不單可以是無窮無盡，亦未必能適用於所有程序。因為同一個模式即使可用於識別某一程序中的真性能缺陷，用於另一程序卻可以產生誤報的結果。況且，分辯程序中有否出現性能問題的標準可能並不科學，因為程序執行時即使沒有出現性能問題，依然有可能運行了含性能缺陷的程序代碼片段，而該片段郤能在其他執行時導致性能問題。 在此項目中，我們倡議研發一個創新的並適用於多線程程序的性能缺陷定位框架。此框架既不使用任何預定義的模式，也不需要區分出正常執行和有性能缺陷的執行，而是通過預計一系列程序執行的趨勢和製訂相關的曲線，以定位引致性能缺陷的代碼。據我們所知，朝著此方向探討如何定位代碼中的性能缺陷甚或其他類別的缺陷，尚屬首次。此外，本項目提出的框架，將有助於開發人員在程序開發和維護的過程中，抗衡代碼的性能缺陷問題。

125113.label: Realisation of objectives
125113.value: We are pleased to report that the three objectives of this project have been realised. With regard to the first objective, we have investigated, proposed and developed a number of techniques for the detection and localisation of program bugs with respect to various aspects of performance issues that occur in the execution of multithreaded software applications. Our developed techniques include program execution profile analysis, testing strategies formulation, detection of concurrency bugs, as well as prioritization techniques that improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the tasks for exposing and locating bugs. We have also developed empirical frameworks for integrated and holistic evaluation of the implemented techniques. With regard to the second objective, we have developed a novel general model-based approach to the localisation of program bugs that lead to performance issues. Our approach is based on the fundamentally different strategy of curve fitting and trend estimation over program executions with performance data. With regard to the third objective, we have implemented prototype tools to demonstrate the feasibility of our framework. We have also conducted many experiments with commonly used empirical benchmark subjects as well as real-world large-scale multithreaded software applications. Our empirical analysis and controlled experiments have validated the effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed techniques and approaches in terms of various measures such as memory overhead and bug detection and localisation rates. More details are as follows. Performance issues are commonly due to the concurrency nature of executions of multithreaded programs with bugs such as semantic bugs, atomicity violations and data races. Static detectors may help to reveal and locate performance bugs in small multithreaded programs, but they are not scalable. Dynamic detectors predict and then examine execution instances that may exhibit errors, but often only few of them are caused by real bugs. To address this problem, we developed a family of similarity-based techniques to more accurately locate candidates of execution instances that manifest real bugs. Our empirical analysis confirmed that our techniques can significantly improve the bug detection rate, and identified several members of our family of techniques that can be more effective than the prior best techniques reported in the literature. Mainstream data race detectors either use the happens-before (HB) approach that aims at sound race detection or the locking discipline (LD) approach that aims at efficiency improvement (often at the expense of precision), or use a hybrid approach of both HB and LD. We developed a new context-based strategy for hybrid race detection that can effectively reduce the length of memory access history to improve the efficiency of memory utilization. Moreover, we developed a general empirical framework and conducted a controlled experiment on a set of commonly used benchmark suite and real-world applications to comprehensive evaluate various memory access history reduction strategies for hybrid race detectors. Analysis of program executions requires monitoring the sequence of code in the execution profile, which could accumulate to a huge set of historical records, rendering the required computation for evaluation very expensive with unsatisfactory performance. To alleviate this issue, we developed a new path analysis algorithm to query on a customised data structure that consolidates the set of executions of the same program to compute the execution frequencies of paths, where higher counts indicates incurring higher performance costs, to aid debugging the performance issues in multithreaded programs. One frequently researched set of techniques for exposing and locating program bugs is called spectrum-based fault localisation (SBFL). SBFL techniques assess the suspiciousness of program locations based on the code coverage data. The effectiveness of SBFL techniques primarily relies on the accuracy of their fault (bug) localisation formulas. We conducted a study of a suite of SBFL techniques at both the abstraction levels of source and instruction code in the context of a known theoretical hierarchy of bug localisation effectiveness. Our results complement theoretical analysis and enlighten directions for further work in the area. Once bug localisation techniques identify a bug, the programmer will apply fixes to remove the bug. However, bug fixes themselves could introduce new bugs or side effects, or the bugs could manifest in other scenarios overlooked by the programmer. To revalidate a "bug-fixed program", we proposed a similarity-based regression testing methodology that manipulates thread schedules to coordinate suspicious thread interleavings between program versions, based on the notions of similar execution contexts of events and bug signatures. We conducted experiments to illustrate the potential of bug interleaving adaptation across versions. Multithreaded programs are popularly implemented as parts of web services to harvest the performance gain due to multicore technologies and cloud computing systems. We performed literature review and systematic mapping studies on testing these software applications in diverse scenarios. We developed a technique to generate ensemble fault localisation formulas which recommend candidates of code segments of a service responsible for the observed failures. Our framework generates a subset of such ensemble formulas that are statistically more effective than their component SBFL formulas. We also studied the detection of bugs in multithreaded programs deployed in mobile devices and smart TVs. Moreover, we performed experiments to examine whether different factors would consistently affect the effectiveness of bug detection in both the average and adverse scenarios. Furthermore, insights from our studies have contributed to our formulation of a family of meta-level strategies to test multithreaded programs, which use historic data on detected races to adaptively select a transformed version of the program to be subject to the next round of race detection. We validated our strategies through a large-scale experiment on real-world programs with data race bugs, showing that the cost-effectiveness of detecting such bugs can be significantly enhanced. Both static and dynamic bug localisation techniques have been proposed to address performance issues in multithreaded programs, but existing techniques cannot handle performance anomalies with previously unknown patterns and cannot work well if the idea of performance anomaly is ill-formed or exhibit temporal variations for the same program. To address this limitation, we developed a new model-based approach for locating bugs that lead to performance issues. Our approach is based on curve fitting and trend estimation over program executions with performance data. Finally, to evaluate our developed techniques and frameworks, we have designed and implemented a number of prototype tools, some built atop existing ones while some were realized as cloud-based services. Overall, we have performed extensive experiments and empirical analyses with promising results using well-recognized benchmark suites, industrial-strength widely-used real-world multithreaded software applications, as well as datasets from other repositories and sources, as reported in journal and conference publications.

125113.label: Major findings and research outcome
125113.value: Our investigation has found improvements to the current state of detectors and locators of bugs in multithreaded programs that lead to performance issues in various aspects. Our work has produced outcomes of a number of better and new techniques that achieve significant performance enhancements in multithreaded programs in terms of various measures such as memory overhead and bug detection and localisation rates. Our framework of techniques and studies include program execution profile analysis [J5], testing strategies formulation [J1,J2,J4,J6,C1,C3,C6, C9], detection of concurrency bugs [J3,J7,C4,C7,C11,C14], rate of bug localisation [J8, C2,C10,C12], bug detection of multithreaded programs deployed in service-oriented systems [J2,J7,C8,C10], mobile devices [C9] and smart TVs [J6], as well as prioritis-ation techniques [J1,J2,C1,C6,C8] that improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the tasks for exposing and locating bugs. We also developed a new and fundamental strategy based on curve fitting and trend estimation over program executions with performance data [C5]. Our key insight is that the longer a multithreaded program executes when invoking a candidate buggy program entity, the more likely it is that the execution is associated with performance anomaly [C5]. Our strategy is distinctly different from the existing static or dynamic pattern-matching techniques which are limited in their ability to handle performance anomalies with previously unknown patterns and the scenarios when the idea of performance anomaly itself is ill-formed or temporally varying for the same program. We have also extended work on the popular class of techniques called spectrum-based fault localisation (SBFL) which assess the suspiciousness of bug presence in a program entity based on code coverage profiles. Our work has resulted in better understanding of the accuracy of SBFL formulas in the contexts of different code abstract levels [C2], different versions of program codes and test suites [J8,C10], and different means of analysis [C12]. We have implemented a set of tools, some built on top of existing ones [J3,C7] and some custom-built and deployed as cloud-based services [J7,C4]. We conducted extensive experiments that demonstrate the feasibility of our framework and the effectiveness and efficiency of our developed techniques with promising results. Our empirical analyses have been performed on well-recognized benchmark suites, industrial-strength real-world software applications, as well as datasets from other repositories and sources [J1,J2,J3,J8,J9,C5,C6,C10,C12,C13,C14].

125113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
125113.value: Our work has developed techniques and tools to offer execution-log-based dynamic analysis as cloud-based services. Our work is general and can be extended to handle a variety of programming languages used in multithreaded applications, or to support the use of intelligent learning or data-intensive analytic approaches to cover different settings or options of program execution analysis for precise bug detection and localisation. Our implementation of the newly proposed path analysis algorithm to query on a customised data structure involves a sequential process which leaves room for performance improvement as further work. The ideas can also be extended to include unstructured yet more informative elements of interrelated program execution records to enhance its capability of concurrency analysis. Our empirical framework of analyzing different bug localization formulas that underpin various spectrum-based fault localization (SBFL) techniques can be expanded to investigate the effect of other constraints and contexts on their accuracy relations and practical effectiveness. Further work can also apply SBFL techniques to regression testing for detection and removal of performance bugs in context-dependent (such as location-based or energy-aware) multithreaded programs deployed in mobile devices.

125113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
125113.value: Multithreaded programs are notoriously difficult to debug due to the added dimension of the concurrency nature of their executions. Moreover, many of these bugs manifest themselves as problematic performance issues that severely affect their practical applications. This project has investigated various state-of-the-art techniques and tools for the detection and localisation of bugs in multithreaded programs that may lead to performance issues. We have developed a number of techniques and empirical frameworks to improve existing work in various aspects, including a more efficient program path analysis algorithm, a family of similarity-based techniques to more accurately locate candidates of execution instances that manifest real performance bugs, and validation of accuracy relations among statistical bug localisation formulas in certain contexts. Furthermore, we have developed a new performance bug localisation framework that distinguishes problematic program executions with performance issues from normal ones using a statistical curve fitting and trend estimation strategy which is fundamentally different from existing ones. We have implemented the corresponding tools, some of which are deployed as services in a cloud computing platform for higher performance gains. We have also performed experiments to validate the effectiveness and efficiency of our techniques in various contexts and scenarios with promising results.

125313.label: Project Objectives
125313.value: To investigate an automatic and systematic composition method of evolutionary algorithm portfolio. Derive a set of benchmarks that reflects the world. To investigate other interesting extensions of MultiEA.

125313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
125313.value: Evolutionary algorithms (EAs) are versatile black box optimization techniques. There is no need to know the mathematical form of the optimization objective function. Hence it is applicable to search landscapes which are non-differentiable, non-smooth, plagued with large number of deceptive local optima, or simulation based functions, which cannot be easily solved by conventional techniques. EAs also offer the possibility of co-operating with traditional techniques in a memetic computing framework. Finally, it is applicable to multiple objective (MO) problems which are less amendable to conventional techniques. However, there is very little study on how a portfolio of EA may synergistically interact to give even better performance. In this research, a novel automatic and parameter-less EA portfolio composition method is advanced. Our method will compose a portfolio of one or more algorithms that would give the best average performance. It gives an answer to which algorithms and the number of algorithms that should be in the portfolio, and allow the special case of one algorithm. Moreover, the constructed portfolio is guaranteed to have better average performance than any individual algorithm. Finally, this approach will output good portfolio type algorithm that is more stable than individual algorithms! Next, we investigate the problem of how to derive a suite of benchmarks that reflects the world, an extremely important topic within evolutionary computation. We propose a novel solution to this problem using the idea of reality measures. Researchers will now have a measure that they can use to justify the degree that their EAs are useful to the real world problems. This measure will be the first of its kind in evolutionary computation. Finally, we extend our method in novel ways based on the results of the above. Two important extensions are to MO problems and algorithms that permit restart. These will deliver more powerful portfolio type EA algorithms that solve real world problems more effectively.

125313.label: Realisation of objectives
125313.value: The three objectives are achieved. On objective 1, an automatic and systematic composition method is reported that generates an algorithm portfolio which is better than a standalone algorithm. On objective 2, a systematic way to generate a set of unbiased benchmark problems is reported. It reflects the real world scenario that for any algorithm, there usually exists some problems for which the algorithm is better than the rest. It also serves to shift the focus from winning benchmarking competitions to investigating algorithm characteristics on problems. On objective 3, a multiobjective algorithm portfolio is reported. Better algorithm variants for various scenarios are also reported.

125313.label: Major findings and research outcome
125313.value: On objective 1, an automatic method for composing portfolio is reported [J2, J stands for journal publication]. It automatically constructs a portfolio which is better than any single standalone algorithm, if one exists, and report none if it does not exist. It assumes that the problem set is known and the problem distribution is known. The composing method uses a novel algorithm portfolio, known as MultiEA [J3]. A synergy effect that explains why sometimes a portfolio is better than a standalone algorithm is also reported in [J3]. When the problem set is unknown, a novel algorithm called Sequential Learnable Evolutionary Algorithm (SLEA) is reported in [C4, C stands for conference publication]. It uses the idea of case-based reasoning to map the normalized convergence curve of an unknown problem to the most similar known problem, and hence the best algorithm for the unknown problem. It contributes as a novel algorithm selection method. It works well on unknown problems it has never seen. Recently, a Bayesian reasoning method [C6] is reported to improve its performance as the number of runs is increased. Normalized convergence curve is a type of algorithm based sampling. Recently, an experimental study is conducted that suggests that this sampling strategy is better than unbiased sampling [C8]. On objective 2, a novel method for finding synthetic benchmark functions that only one algorithm finds easy and all other algorithms finds difficult (and also vice versa) is reported in [J5]. Unlike existing works, statistical guarantee is given. It is used to find the synthetic analog of a real world problem for which an algorithm excels. It is also used to construct an unbiased benchmark set that does not favour any algorithm. This serves to shift the focus of striving for winning in benchmark competitions to investigating algorithm characteristics. The method has recently been applied to construct an unbiased knowledge base for SLEA [C5]. Recently, a more theoretically correct statistical guarantee is reported in [C7]. On objective 3, a multiobjective algorithm portfolio is reported in [C1]. An improved differential evolution variant is reported in [J1]. A new non-revisiting algorithm that alleviates the memory storage of search history while maintaining performance is reported in [C3, J4]. A new history-driven algorithm for handling dynamic fitness is also reported [C2].

125313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
125313.value: We plan to investigate whether an unbiased benchmark set can reveal key characteristics of the problem which is shared by real world problems. If so, the problems generated by the methodology in [J5, C7] may give new insights on why an algorithm works well on a real world problem. This is an important problem from both the theoretical and practical viewpoint. We also plan to investigate alternative predictive measures that use knowledge effectively but are computationally feasible. This would improve the performance of both algorithm portfolio and algorithm selection methods. Also, there are other interesting extensions of MultiEA that should be investigated more deeply. They would be addressed in our future research.

125313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
125313.value: In engineering optimization, frequently the mathematical form is unknown and it is costly to sample the problem landscape. Evolutionary algorithms are effective to find good solutions to this type of problems. In this research, an automatic way to compose an evolutionary algorithm portfolio is reported. It is guaranteed to give a portfolio that is performing better than any single evolutionary algorithm when one such portfolio exists. Using such a portfolio thus increases optimization effectiveness. A new algorithm portfolio, MultiEA, is also reported which dynamically selects the most effecive algorithm within the portfolio as the optimization goes on. However, such a composition method, or any other alternatives, must work on the premise of optimizing performance on a given benchmarking set. While one can use various benchmarking sets, there is no guarantee that the set is reflective of what the real world is like. This research proposes another way to generate benchmarking sets that are unbiased - does not favour any algorithm. It discovers new previously unknown benchmark problems that an algorithm is good at, shedding light on when an algorithm will be performing well in the real world. It also shifts research focus from winning benchmarking competitions to studying algorithm characteristics.

125513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
125513.value: 本項目基於光誘導介電泳（ODEP）與顯微視覺技術，採用三維細胞動力學模型分析方法實現癌細胞的自動識別。細胞動力學分析和識別是生物技術研究領域，如診斷測試，細胞篩選以及免疫診斷的基礎。而光誘導介電泳技術不需要複雜的微電極製備，可以動態生成虛擬微電極，有助於細胞的快速並行操縱與分類。顯微視覺結合光誘導介電泳技術可以實現三維細胞動力學分析，通過視覺算法分析由顯微鏡CCD所獲取的細胞圖像序列，根據細胞運動的精確估計，完成細胞動力學模型，並在理論分析的基礎上實現癌細胞識別和評估標準建立。項目將通過實驗與數值仿真，實現並解決以下基本問題：1）定制光誘導介電泳平台，實現癌細胞的識別; 2）採用顯微視覺方法，實現細胞在介電泳力場中的運動跟踪以及細胞的三維動力學模型分析; 3）深入了解癌細胞在介電泳力場中的自旋轉機制，並通過實驗和仿真進行交叉驗證。

125513.label: Realisation of objectives
125513.value: Our team has realized all project objectives as stated in the original application. Described below are the techniques used to realize these objective. 1. Model the 3D cell rotation electrokinetics phenomena, including AC electro-osmosis and light-induced electrothermal forces, during the cell motion under the ODEP force field. A multiphysics simulation corresponding to AC electro-osmosis and thermocapillary flows on a photosensitive substrate (optically-induced dielectrophoresis, i.e., ODEP, microfluidics chip) was conducted using COMSOL. Study of the thermocapilliary flow phenomenon is especially important because the temperature gradient induced in the ODEP chip may potentially damage the biological sample. In order to study the internal temperature distribution of an ODEP chip, transient solutions calculated by a finite element method software (COMSOL) were obtained. To match the experimental conditions, the temperature change of the microscope objective with time measured by an infrared (IR) camera was imported into the simulation model. The simulated temperature distribution and the transient changes of the ODEP chip and the photoconductive substrate were consistently matched with the experimental results. Based on these simulations, we can acquire accurate temperature distribution of the liquid inside the ODEP chip. When we add the cell models into this simulation, the cells temperature distributed in different areas in the ODEP chip could be obtained. For example, the maximum temperature difference of cells with diameter of 20 μm around the illumination area can be as high as 0.7 oC and decrease from the middle area of a light spot to the surrounding region. This temperature gradient will induce thermophoretic in cell, influencing the molecular movement across the cytoplasm. The temperature gradient along the ODEP chip will also influence cell viability and activity located in different positions of the chip. Therefore, for biological applications, the light patterns used in an ODEP chip are required to be properly designed such that heat generated in the ODEP will satisfy the biological cellular requirements; the temperature gradient should also be decreased in order to minimize the negative effects such as thermophoretic. A heat sink or a stage temperature controller may be required, in which case, a reflective ODEP system where the projected light images for manipulation of cells is focused by the objective of the optical microscope. 2. Developed and optimized algorithms to automatically isolate and calculate the rotation speed of Melan-A cells (and other cancer cells) from microscope video images in real time. Cell self-rotation in a dielectrophoretic (DEP) force is about its rotation axes along the direction of an electric field. Therefore, the self-rotation motion which projects to the image sensor plane is just 2D motion. Compared with DEP, cell rotations activated by an optically-induced dielectrophoresis (ODEP) system is not about its yaw axes along the chip surface. In order to estimate the 3D rotation motion, we have developed an optical flow algorithm to track the cell rotation speeds and also their translational trajectories. Optical flow is the pattern of apparent motion of objects, surfaces, and edges in a visual scene caused by the relative motion between an observer and the scene. The optical flow methods estimate the motion between two image frames which are taken at times t and t+Δt at every patch position. The brightness constancy assumption was used in our work. We have used the ODEP platform to collect sequences of ordered images, which allow the estimation of cell motions as either instantaneous image velocities or discrete image displacements. The viewing direction of the cell is denoted by the radial unit vector, so a local two-dimensional coordinate system on a sphere consisting of two orthogonal tangential unit vectors can represent the optical flow components u and v. The cell rotation speed estimation is calculated based on the fact that the translation and rotation cause fundamentally different flow fields, described as the 2D optical flow velocity components Vu and Vv. A full description of the computerized algorithms developed with our collaborators can be found at http://www.mdpi.com/2072-666X/8/9/282/htm. 3. Characterize the limit-of-detection of Melan-A concentration in cells as a function of applied ODEP parameters and the resulting rotation speed, and cross-correlate the level of Melan-A detected in a cell via ODEP-induced rotation with the stage/grade of the melanoma. The phenomenon of self-rotation observed in naturally and artificially pigmented cells under an applied linearly polarized alternating current (non-rotating) electrical field has been investigated. The repeatable and controllable rotation speeds of the cells were quantified and their dependence on dielectrophoretic parameters such as frequency, voltage, and waveform was studied. Moreover, the rotation behavior of the pigmented cells with different melanin content was compared to quantify the correlation between self-rotation and the presence of melanin. Most importantly, macrophages, which did not originally rotate in the applied non-rotating electric field, began to exhibit self-rotation that was very similar to that of the pigmented cells, after ingesting foreign particles (e.g., synthetic melanin or latex beads). We envision that this discovery will enable the development of a rapid, non-intrusive, and automated process to obtain the electrical conductivities and permittivities of cellular membrane and cytoplasm in the near future. 4. Determine the physical mechanism behind Melan-A rotation and develop a finite element-method (FEM) based model for this mechanism. We have developed an FEM-based model to elucidate the mechanism behind the self-rotation of Melan-A and other cancer cells under an AC dielectrophorectic field. Specifically, we have demonstrated that mouse cells comprising of Melan-a cells, RAW 267.4 macrophage cells, peripheral white blood cells and lymphocytes, can be manipulated in an ODEP device with appropriate DEP parameters. Our ODEP device generates a non-rotating electric field and exerts a localized DEP force on optical electrodes. Hitherto, we are the first group to report that among all the cells investigated, Melan-a cells, lymphocytes and white blood cells were found to undergo self-rotation in the device in the presence of a DEP force. The rotational speed of the cells depended on the voltage and frequency applied and the cells' distance from the optical center. A possible mechanism for explaining this new observation of induced self-rotation based on the physical properties of cells has been formulated and will be published in the near future. We believe that this rotation phenomenon can be used to identify cell type and to elucidate the dielectric and physical properties of cells.

125513.label: Major findings and research outcome
125513.value: Through the funding of this project we have achieved the following research outcome: 1. We have shown that the self-rotational behavior of a cell can be accurately characterized from a video of many cells undergoing different motions by using micro-vision analysis algorithms. For example, we have developed an image-matching-based automated algorithm capable of accurately determining the self-rotational speed of cancer cells in an optically-induced electrokinetics-based microfluidic chip. To automatically track a specific cell in a video featuring more than one cell, a background subtraction technique was used. To determine the rotational speeds of cells, a reference frame was automatically selected and curve fitting was performed to improve the stability and accuracy. Results show that the algorithm was able to accurately calculate the self-rotational speeds of cells up to ~150 rpm. 2. The motion trajectory of a cell can be also determined by a micro-vision image analysis algorithm, which enables a comprehensive analysis of cellular kinetic behaviors. We have developed an algorithm that was successfully used to simultaneously analyze the self-rotational and translational motions of cells with non-uniform structure. In all experiments conducted, individual cells of interest were correctly tracked. No human intervention was required for the kinetics extraction algorithm, except for the assignment of the cell of interest in the first video frame. The algorithm exhibited good robustness and accuracy even if the cell of interest exhibited non-uniform self-rotation. 3. The calculation of the self-rotational speed is theoretically irrelevant to the speed of translational motion, but a high translational speed may make the tracing of the cell of interest difficult. In this case, a high frame rate is helpful. The main limitation of this algorithm is that it can only handle cells whose images are different at different self-rotational angles, but this is the general situation for flat and spherical cells. 4. The developed algorithms have also been shown to be potentially beneficial to the development of new label-free biomarkers for characterization of cellular state, discrimination of different kinds of cancer cells in heterogeneous populations, and potentially many other bioengineering related applications. It is envisioned that the image analysis methods developed in this project can be used in conjunction with other microfluidic rotational techniques, such as structure based, acoustic based or optical based cell rotation techniques.

125513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
125513.value: Potential applications for the algorithms developed in this project include separating different kinds of cancer cells in heterogeneous populations, discriminating normal cells from cancer cells, and characterization of the morphological and electrical properties of cells. We proposed to extend the current work to the measurement of single-cell mass and use a cell's mass as physiological indicator, i.e., based on a cell's mass, we can determine wether a cell is dead or alive. We propose to create a parallel, single-cell biophysical characteristic measurement platform that can detect several types of mass-related features in a single cell, and more than 10,000 cells per hour, providing a throughput that is 20 times higher than that achieved with micro-resonator-based approaches. We will apply for a RGC grant to develop a platform that can simultaneously manipulate the individual motion of cells and measure their diameter, volume, density, mass, buoyancy density, and buoyancy mass based on their sedimentation trajectory. We intend to show that the measured mass-related parameters will significantly change during the death of a single cell induced by different types of drugs.

125513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
125513.value: We have developed a novel cancer cell characterization and identification method based on 3D cell kinetics analysis using micro-vision. As an application example, we used this method to non-invasively determine cell membrane capacitance and conductance, which are intrinsic information correlated with the cellular dielectric parameters and morphology of the plasma membrane. These parameters have been used as electrophysiological biomarkers to characterize cellular phenotype and state, and they may have many associated clinical applications. Single cell membrane capacitance and conductance were determined by using the optically-induced dielectrophoresis (ODEP) microfluidics chip developed in this project and a single layer of the shell-core polarization model. 3D finite-element analyses of the positive/negative ODEP forces generated in the microfluidic chip were performed which provided a theoretical validation of the feasibility of this approach. The crossover frequency spectra for cancer cells such as Raji cells and MCF-7 cells were experimentally investigated by using a micro-vision based motion-tracking technique. The different responses of these cells to the positive and negative ODEP forces were studied under different liquid conductivities by automatic observation and tracking of the cellular trajectory and texture. This new technique allows the determination of single cell membrane dielectric properties that yields statistically significant data.

138213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
138213.value: Spatial point data consist of a number of randomly distributed points on the plane or in space. The “points” may be any objects of negligible size relative to the study region, and the focus of interest is typically on the distributional properties of point locations. Spatial point data are frequently encountered in manufacturing processes. For example, defective pixels on display panels/camera sensors (CCD or CMOS), surface defects on semiconductor wafers, nanoparticles in composite materials, etc. These “points” exhibit complex spatial patterns. They are quality characteristics having a crucial impact on the final product quality and process yield. In addition, they hold valuable information about the product manufacturing processes. Exploitation of such information they contain can be utilized for process monitoring and fault diagnosis. Rapid development of advanced image-based inspection systems has made possible the in-line inspection of spatial point data in manufacturing processes. However, due to the lack of quality control methodologies in related areas, inspection of such data is mostly carried out in primitive forms: human visual inspection and simple control charts counting the total number of points. The rich information contained in spatial point data has largely been left untapped. Although some prior work on analysis of point data can be found in other application areas such as biology, ecology, epidemiology, astronomy, etc., they have very different focuses of interest and have no concern over the critical issues in the context of manufacturing quality control. This project aims to develop systematic statistical quality control methodologies for spatial point data in manufacturing, by fully exploiting the rich process information they contain. Advanced algorithms will be developed, tested and validated through real manufacturing processes. Quantitative characterization of point distributional behaviors will be proposed, upon which process monitoring procedures for variation reduction and fault pattern detection methods for root cause diagnosis will be investigated. In this project, we will also extend our analysis from traditional two-dimensional point distribution to a much more challenging three-dimensional quality inspection problem which has rarely been studied in exiting literature. The successful completion of this project will deliver novel techniques targeting at the pressing issues of statistical quality control for manufacturing processes with spatial point data as vital quality characteristics. The proposed methods will be validated and implemented in real applications. 空間點數據由一組在二維平面或者三維空間中隨機分佈的點構成。在工業製造過程中經常可以見到這類數據(如半導體晶圓片上的瑕疵或合成材料中的納米顆粒等)。它們包含了有價值的產品製造過程信息。我們致力於研究針對製造過程中空間點數據的統計質量控制方法。我們將對針對空間點分佈行為進行量化描述，并基於此提出過程控制和故障診斷的方法。此外，我們會將傳統的二維空間點分佈研究擴展到更具挑戰性的三維質量控制問題中。

138213.label: Realisation of objectives
138213.value: The four objectives of this project have been fully achieved. (1) We have successfully developed a novel statistical model to quantify the characteristics of the spatial point patterns. The model is used as a foundation to build more efficient and effective monitoring schemes to automatically detect the variations in the point patterns. The monitoring scheme has been compared with existing ones and achieved superior results. (2) Based on the model, a diagnostic algorithm is developed to identify the root of the variation from the point patterns. It is able to independently analyze the characteristics of point patterns at multiple spatial scales. The method has been tested to produce outstandingly accurate diagnosis results. To the best of our knowledge, this is by far the only rigorous method developed for such a purpose. (3) We have developed a method to link the raw data (in the form of 2D images) to the spatial point distributional characteristics in the 3D space. By this method, we are able to accurately assess the property of 3D point patterns by using multiple 2D images. (4) All the above methods developed are verified by extensive numerical simulations, as well as real data from a nanocomposite material.

138213.label: Major findings and research outcome
138213.value: (1) Development of a statistical model to quantify the characteristics of the spatial point patterns. (2) A diagnostic algorithm is developed to identify the root of the variation from the point patterns. (3) Development of a method to link the raw data (in the form of 2D point pattern images) to the spatial point distributional characteristics in the 3D space. (4) Four journal papers have been published/accepted so far, one more working paper is being prepared for submission. Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
138213.value: Spatial point data consist of a number of randomly distributed points on the plane or in space. The “points” may be any objects of negligible size, and the focus of interest is typically on the distributional properties of point locations. Spatial point data are frequently encountered in manufacturing processes. For example, defective pixels on display panels/camera sensors, surface defects on semiconductor wafers, nanoparticles in composite materials, etc. These “points” exhibit complex spatial patterns. They are quality characteristics having a crucial impact on the final product quality and process yield. In this project, we developed systematic statistical quality control methodologies for spatial point data in manufacturing. Advanced pattern monitoring and variation root cause identification algorithms have been developed, tested and validated through real manufacturing data from a nanocomposite material fabrication process. We have also extended our analysis from traditional two-dimensional point distribution to a much more challenging three-dimensional quality inspection problem by using a model to link the 2D image data with 3D quality properties. Tools developed in this project have significantly advanced the statistical process monitoring and control for manufacturing processes with spatial point data as vital quality characteristics.

138313.label: Major findings and research outcome
138313.value: Based on the support of this Early Career Scheme project, the PI is capable to conduct research studies of developing data mining and computational intelligence knowledge for addressing emerging problems in energy engineering including the modeling, operations scheduling, as well as design and planning of the hybrid energy systems. The PI has closely collaborated with industrial partners to collect massive volumes of industrial data for studying the proposed research problems. The PI has introduced novel data-driven approaches for accurately modeling each major components in the hybrid energy systems as well as new computational intelligence approaches for efficiently solving the optimization problems in scheduling operations of the hybrid energy systems. The PI also proposed new mathematical models for well design and planning the layout and configuration of the hybrid power system by considering real data. The feasibility and effectiveness of all methodologies proposed in this research project have been rigorously validated by both of theories and industrial data. The PI demonstrates the advantages of the utilization of the data-driven approaches and computational intelligence methods in addressing emerging challenging problems in energy area. Besides research publications, the PI also successfully trained two Ph.D. students and successfully supervised the final year projects of over 6 undergraduate students. Details research findings and outcomes please refer to Part C.

138313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
138313.value: Due to the rapid growth of energy system data collected nowadays, the capability of the traditional data mining and computational intelligence approaches in analyzing big energy data becomes limited. To accommodate the era of big data, it is meaningful to investigate deep learning schemes and parallel computational frameworks based on previously proposed data-driven approaches. In addition, past researches majorly discuss about the SCADA data collected from energy systems. The recent development of smart sensors has enabled the collection of various data including images, acoustic signals, videos, etc. More advanced data-driven approaches capable to generate insightful knowledge through analyzing the fusion of various types of data becomes another interesting research direction.

138313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
138313.value: This project focuses on developing novel framework of integrating data mining methods and computational intelligence approaches to better model, optimize, and plan the complicated hybrid power systems so that more efficient and economic performance can be generated. Such data-driven approaches enable the adaptive modeling of energy systems and accurate tracking of their variations over their life-cycle. The study of the optimization of operations of hybrid power systems based on their data-driven models demonstrates the feasibility of generating more practical schedule of operating individual power generation units. Moreover, the design and planning of the hybrid power system by incorporating real data and computational intelligence offers a more realistic solution for constructing new power systems. Overall all, research outputs in this project form a solid platform for studying more advanced and intelligent methods for future smart energy systems.

138413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
138413.value: Applying wireless technologies in biomedicine for implant communications has become popular recently. Implantable devices including micro camera, pH sensor, electro sensor, and pressure sensor help to identify a recessive condition, disease, or an injury by evaluating the symptoms and signs presented by a patient. Many researches put efforts to develop implantable devices in capsule size or even smaller for surgery with minimal invasion. However, there is a trade-off between the size of device and the capacity of energy storage. A larger size of battery provides more durable electric energy for device operations but takes up enormous volume. Removal of the battery is the most effective way to miniaturize the size of those implants; nonetheless, an external wireless power supply is required. Conventional techniques of wireless power transfer (WPT) for medical implants employ loop antennas to induce voltage at the receiving coil of the implant. This technique limits the operation in a near-field range and has a drawback in sensitivity of the implant orientation. If the implant moves slightly far away from the transmitting antenna, the link efficiency of power delivery weakens. Similarly, if there is a mismatch between the implant orientation and the antenna, the link efficiency reduces significantly. These are the fundamental constraints of loop antennas for wireless powering of implants. In this project, we plan to develop new transmitting antennas for WPT for implant communications. Firstly, we will investigate a mid-field WPT. With the introduction of mid-field operation, the distance of power transfer between the transmitting antenna and the receiver can be increased. Secondly, we will propose circularly polarized (CP) wave propagations for enhancing the link quality. The link efficiency achieves a noticeable advantage for an arbitrariness of implant orientations when the CP wave is used. We will design wideband CP transmitting antennas for improving the link quality of the system. Thirdly, we will carry out a study of tissue loadings effect on the transmitting antennas. Finally, we will design two array structures for enlarging the effective communicating coverage of the implants and power focusing delivery. The ultimate goal of this project is to devote an emerging antenna technology to biomedical application, particularly in implant communications. The proposed techniques contribute to the WPT that enables medical implant communications to be more robust, stable and reliable. 無線通信技術應用於生物醫學植入通信已成為近年的研究熱點。可植入裝置包括微型攝像機，pH感測器，電化學感測器和壓力感測器，這些裝置可以通過評估患者的症狀和體征表現，從而幫助確定患者的隱性遺傳病和具體病情。在醫療植入通信應用中，傳統的無線電力傳輸技術使用環行天線，通過植入體的接收線圈產生電壓。這項技術只局限于近場區之間操作，同時，植入體對方向具有敏感性的缺點。當植入體輕微移動而遠離發射天線時，通信連絡的效率將減弱。同樣，如果植入體方向和體外天線不匹配，連絡效率將顯著下降。 在本項目中，我們將對植入式通信的無線電力傳輸應用提出一種新的天線技術。首先，將研究無線電力傳輸技術。利用本課題提出的新型天線使接收器的通信距離增加。其次，我們將研究圓極化波的傳播從而提高連絡品質。當圓極化波應用時，位於任意方向的植入體的連絡品質都會顯著提高。最後，我們將開研究人體組織對發射天線的影響。本專案的最終目標是將一類新型的天線技術應用於生物醫學中，特別是應用於植入式通信中。提出的天線技術不僅對無線電力傳輸具有科學意義，而且可被應用於醫療植入通信。

138413.label: Realisation of objectives
138413.value: (For objective 1) This objective is to analyze the field distribution and penetration from a transmitting antenna to an implanted receiving antenna. A PhD student, Mr. Wei LIN, under my supervision has completed this task of study. Part of this research findings have been presented at IEEE international conferences and reported in one chapter “Reconfigurable Antennas for Biomedical Application” of his PhD thesis entitled “Reconfigurable Antennas for Emerging Wireless Communication Systems”. From obtained simulated and experimental results, we confirmed that using magnetic field penetration is the most promising way to deliver maximum signals to implanted devices. Among many types of antennas, we investigated that the external transmitting antenna realized by slot, patch and dielectric resonator antennas are desirable candidates for implant communications in its mid-field range; while loop antennas are the excellent candidates for near-field implant communications. In addition, we discovered that polarization is one of key factor to ensure the quality of implant communications between transmitting and receiving antennas. Circular polarization (CP) can give an advantage for orientation freedom of the receiving antenna of the implant; while polarization reconfigurability can further enhance the maximum signal quality between the transmitting and the receiving antennas. Therefore, we introduced and developed several new circularly-polarized antennas and new reconfigurable (polarization and pattern) antennas for achieving the defined objectives 2 and 3. (For objective 2) This objective is to develop new CP antennas for improving transmission efficiency in on-body and implant communications. Based on the study from objective 1, we confirmed that the use of CP can give significant improvement for the link efficiency between transmitting and receiving antennas. We have designed several wideband CP antennas. Firstly, we invented a low-profile conical-beam CP antenna. This work, published in the IEEE Transaction on Antennas and Propagation 2014, suggested a new methodology of CP generation by combing radiations from a single E-dipole and multiple M-dipole current sources to achieve a wide CP bandwidth. Secondly, we introduced a rotated-stair dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) published in the IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters 2015. This work exhibited a simple configuration of DRA excited by a single aperture to obtain the wide CP bandwidth. Thirdly, we developed a wideband reconfigurable CP antenna published in the IEEE Transaction on Antennas and Propagation 2015. This antenna is an enhanced version of our multiple current sources design published in 2014. The proposed antenna in 2015 combined a controlled power distributed network and a reconfigurable network such that it can realize left- and right-hand polarizations efficiently. Because of the aforementioned inventions, my PhD student, Mr. Wei Lin, received the young scientist award at the IEEE TECON2015. He has completed his PhD degree last year and is currently a postdoc working in the University of Technology Sydney. (For objective 3) This objective is to study the human loading effect to transmitting antennas mentioned in objectives 2. The investigation found that the transmitting antennas were sensitive to the human loading. Operating frequency, impedance, and radiation would be altered when the antennas were put closer to the human. To compensate the loading effect from the human, we introduced reconfigurable technology applying to the transmitting antenna design. A set of reconfigurable antennas including patch (published in APS 2016), slot (published in iWEM2016), and dipole antenna published in a journal entitled “Multi-polarization reconfigurable antenna for wireless biomedical system”, IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Circuits and Systems, vol. 11, issue 3, pp. 652-660, Jun. 2017. This work reported an integration of multi-dipole and multi-slot antennas for improving the wireless link quality in implant communication network. We were the first research group to demonstrate multiple polarizations to the implant communications with experimental validations. Two invited talks, namely, “Reconfigurable multi-slot antenna for bio-medical applications” (EuCAP2016) and “Polarization reconfigurable multi-slot antenna for body-centric network” (iWEM2016) were presented on this state-of-the-art antenna invention.

138413.value: This research successfully developed a set of circularly polarized antennas for improving the communication link between transmitting and receiving antennas in biomedical applications. To further enhance the communication quality, the research investigated and introduced polarization and pattern reconfigurable technologies to the body-centric wireless communication (BWC) network.
