138513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
138513.value: With the advancement of information and computing technology, large-scale image datasets are being exponentially generated today. Along with such data explosion is the fast-growing challenge to efficiently and effectively store, maintain, and share them from data owners to a large number of data users. Cloud, with its robust yet economical computing resources, provides a promising platform for hosting such image management systems. However, for the image service outsourcing paradigm to become truly successful, there are still fundamental and critical challenges yet to overcome. Firstly, because the cloud is a public environment operated by external third-parties usually outside the data owner/users’ trusted domain, the outsourcing design has to be privacy-protecting and sometimes mandatorily provide legal compliance to various privacy regulations. Secondly, due to the high-dimensionality and large-scale of the image datasets, it is both necessary and desirable for the image service design to be as efficient and less resource-consuming as possible, in order to keep the cloud economically attractive. To address these fundamental challenges, we propose to investigate and prototype a novel secure image service outsourcing architecture that aims to exploit techniques from different domains and take security, complexity, and efficiency into consideration from the very beginning of the service flow. Particularly, we propose to research our service design under the compressive sensing framework, a recent data sensing/sampling paradigm known for its simplicity of unifying the traditional sampling and compression for image acquisition. Data owners only need to outsource compressed image samples to cloud for reduced storage overhead and simplified local sensing. We will explore a privacy-preserving image recovery service, where data owners/users can securely harness the cloud as a central hub responsible for image recovery from sample processing on demand, without revealing information on either the image samples or the recovered image content. With more and more image samples centralized to cloud, we further investigate a privacy-preserving content based image retrieval service, which allows users to selectively retrieve encrypted image samples from cloud without revealing their private interests. The proposed service designs will naturally interoperate and significantly boost the wide application spectrum of “secure computing outsourcing”. The research result can be easily adopted by a diverse set of industrial applications like MRI in health care system, remote sensing in geographical system, and even military image sensing in mission critical contexts. The project will also contribute to the educational plan, including curriculum development, undergraduate/graduate student training and research mentoring. 随着科技的发展，当前越来越多的大规模图片数据随之应运而生。这种大规模数据的爆炸增长也引发了一大难点问题：如何快速有效的存储，维护这些数据，并且支持在数据拥有者和大规模用户之间的快速分享？云计算，通过其可靠且经济的租用计算资源，为支持这种大规模图片管理系统的提供了理想平台。然而，要使得这种图片服务外包的模式真正为大众所接受，我们仍然有一些至关重要的难点问题必须要解决。首先，由于公有云平台是第三方维护的，其并不在数据拥有者和用户的可信范围内，因此外包设计必须要能保护用户数据隐私。而且保护数据隐私也满足了某些相关隐私法规条例的强制要求。第二，由于图片数据集通常是高纬数据且规模特别大，安全图片服务外包的设计必须要能占用资源尽量少且效率尽量高，只有这样才能保持云端资源消耗低的特点。 为了解决这些基础困难问题，我们在该课题中探索一个全新的安全图片服务外包的系统原型架构。该架构的设计将利用到跨知识领域的技术集，并从设计的一开始就将服务的安全性，复杂度，有效性考虑在内。具体来说，我们将在压缩感知的技术框架下设计该服务架构。压缩感知是一种新近发展起来的数据获取/抽样，恢复的技术。它能将数据获取和压缩合二为一，从而实现一个简单统一的采样过程。在这个框架下，数据拥有者只需要将压缩感知后的图像采集数据外包到云服务中心，以此来节省云端的数据存储，也能降低本地的采样系统的复杂度。在此基础上，我们将首先探索一个保护隐私的图片数据恢复服务。数据拥有者和用户可以安全的利用云服务平台作为处理中心，按需的要求云平台将图像采集数据直接恢复成原始图像。在这个过程中，图像采集数据和恢复的原始图像都不应该泄漏用户的数据隐私。其次，考虑到越来越多的图像采集数据被上传到云平台，我们进一步考虑如何实现一种基于隐私保护的图片获取服务。用户可以选择性的从云平台获取加密过的图片或者图片采集数据，并且仍然不泄露图片的隐私。上述两种基于隐私保护的图片恢复和获取服务能够很好的耦合，并能极大的推广安全计算外包在各种领域的应用。预期的研究成果也可预见将被广泛采纳于各种工业界的应用中，比如医疗系统中的磁共振图像，地理信息系统中的遥感信息获取，以及在各种关键任务下，比如军用场景，的图像感知应用。该课题的成果也能应用于教育计划中，包括新的课程设计，本科生研究生的知识体系训练，以及研究能力的培养。

138513.label: Realisation of objectives
138513.value: The mid-term progress has been reported before, with publications at IEEE-TIFS, IEEE-INFOCOM-2014, and IEEE ICDCS-2014. Below, we briefly conclude major achievements of the project objectives. #### Realisations of objectives 1, 2, 3, and 5. ##### Harnessing Encrypted Cloud Data for Secure Image Sharing In storage outsourcing, highly correlated datasets can occur commonly, where the rich information buried in correlated data can be useful for many cloud data generation/dissemination services. In light of this, we design a secure and efficient cloud-assisted image sharing architecture for mobile devices, by leveraging outsourced encrypted image datasets. Different from traditional image sharing, the proposed design aims to save transmission cost from mobile clients, by directly utilizing outsourced correlated images to reproduce the image of interest inside the cloud for immediate dissemination. Despite the obvious benefits, how to leverage the encrypted image datasets makes the problem particular challenging. We first develop a secure and efficient index design for the client to securely find from the encrypted image datasets the candidate selection pertaining to the image of interest for sharing. We then design two specialized encryption mechanisms for secure image reproduction inside the cloud directly from the encrypted candidate selection. We formally analyze the security strength of the design, and experimentally evaluate the performance. These new findings are published in IEEE-INFOCOM-2015. ##### Achieving Secure Image Recovery via Outsourcing Linear Programming Cloud enables economically promising paradigm of computation outsourcing. However, how to protect customers confidential data during the computation is the major security concern. Focusing on secure image recovery services in compressive sensing, we investigate secure outsourcing of widely applicable linear programming (LP) computations. Our design explicitly decomposes LP computation into public LP solvers running on the cloud and private LP parameters owned by the customer. The resulting flexibility allows us to explore appropriate security/efficiency trade-off via higher-level abstraction of LP computation than the general circuit representation. Specifically, by formulating private LP problem as a set of matrices/vectors, we develop efficient privacy-preserving problem transformation techniques, which allow customers to transform the original LP into some random one while protecting sensitive input/output information. To validate the computation result, we further explore the fundamental duality theorem of LP and derive the necessary and sufficient conditions that correct results must satisfy. Such result verification mechanism is very efficient and incurs close-to-zero additional cost on both cloud server and customers. Extensive security analysis and experiment results show the immediate practicability of our mechanism design. These new findings are published in IEEE-TC. ##### Secure Image Feature Extraction in Cloud With the continuous growth of image and multimedia data, there is a growing need to outsource such computational intensive image feature detection tasks to cloud for its economic computing resources and on-demand ubiquitous access. However, private data exposure could become the major concern. Along the direction, we study how to securely outsource Scalar Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT), one of the most important local feature detection algorithms broadly employed in different areas. We analyze and model the privacy requirements in outsourcing SIFT computation and propose Secure Scalar Invariant Feature Transform (SecSIFT), a high-performance privacy-preserving SIFT feature detection system. In contrast to previous works, the proposed design is not restricted by the efficiency limitations of current homomorphic encryption scheme. In our design, we decompose and distribute the computation procedures of the original SIFT algorithm to a set of independent, co-operative cloud servers and keep the outsourced computation procedures as simple as possible to avoid utilizing a computationally expensive homomorphic encryption scheme. The proposed SecSIFT enables implementation with practical computation and communication complexity. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that SecSIFT performs comparably to original SIFT on image benchmarks while preserving the privacy efficiently. These findings are reported at ACM-MM-2014 and ACM-TOMM. #### Realisations of objectives 1, 4, and 5. ###### Secure and Fast Indexing for Privacy-Assured Healthcare Monitoring Health related multimedia data is being exponentially generated from healthcare monitoring devices and sensors. Coming with it are the challenges on how to efficiently acquire, index, and process such a huge amount of data for effective healthcare and related decision making, while respecting user’s data privacy. We design a secure cloud-based framework for privacy-aware healthcare monitoring systems, which allows fast data acquisition and indexing with strong privacy assurance. For efficient data acquisition, we adopt compressive sensing for easy data sampling, compression, and recovery. We then focus on how to secure and fast index the resulting large amount of continuously generated compressed samples, with the goal to achieve secure selected retrieval over compressed storage. Among others, one particular challenge is the practical demand to cope with the incoming data samples in high acquisition rates. For that problem, we carefully exploit recent efforts on encrypted search, efficient content-based indexing techniques, and fine-grained locking algorithms, to design a novel encrypted index with high-performance customization. It achieves memory efficiency, provable security, as well as greatly improved building speed with nontrivial multithread support. Comprehensive evaluations on Amazon Cloud show that our encrypted design can securely index 1 billion compressed data samples within only 12 min, achieving a throughput of indexing almost 1.4 million encrypted samples per second. Accuracy and visual evaluation on a real healthcare dataset shows good quality of high-value retrieval and recovery over encrypted data samples. These findings are reported at IEEE-TMM. ###### Privacy-Assured Similarity Retrieval over Millions of Encrypted Records One essential component in privacy-preserving CBIR services is the similarity-based retrieval. While in encrypted domain, searchable symmetric encryption (SSE) has been studied extensively for exact-match queries on encrypted records, situations for encrypted similarity queries remain to be fully explored. We investigate the problem of privacy-assured similarity search over millions of encrypted high-dimensional records. Our design employs locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) and SSE, where the LSH hash values of records are treated as keywords fed into the framework of SSE. As direct combination of the two does not facilitate a scalable solution for large datasets, we then leverage a set of advanced hash-based algorithms including multiple-choice hashing, open addressing, and cuckoo hashing, and craft a high performance encrypted index from the ground up. It is not only space efficient, but supports secure and sufficiently accurate similarity search with constant time. Our designs are proved to be secure against adaptive adversaries. The experiment on 10 million encrypted records demonstrates that our designs function in a practical manner. The findings are reported at ESORICS-2015. ###### Generalized Pattern Matching String Search and Multi-Keyword Ranked Search over Encrypted Cloud Data In addition to similarity search, we have also conducted extensive research activities on generalized pattern matching string search, and multi-keyword ranked search over encrypted cloud data. For the former, we propose a secure design that allows users to specify their search queries by using generalized wildcard-based string patterns. It gives users great expressive power in specifying highly targeted search queries. Two most commonly used pattern matching on encrypted data, the substring matching and the longest-prefix-first matching are both supported. For the latter, we first establish a set of strict privacy requirements, and then choose the efficient similarity measure of “coordinate matching,” i.e., as many matches as possible, to capture the relevance ranking of data documents to the search query. Security designs that achieve various stringent privacy requirements in two different threat models are developed. These findings are reported at IEEE-INFOCOM-2015 and IEEE-TPDS.

138513.label: Major findings and research outcome
138513.value: The project has the follow major findings and research outcome. - Developed a new privacy-aware cloud-assisted healthcare monitoring method. Compared to prior arts, the proposed design leverages compressive sensing, and can effectively process the ever-growing healthcare data and simultaneously protect data privacy, while maintaining low overhead at sensors. The result was reported at IEEE INFOCOM 2014(Part-C-9-[1]). - Developed a new privacy-preserving image-centric social discovery method. The proposed design helps compare and quantify similar images over encrypted domain so as to conduct privacy-preserving image similarity based recommendations in social media sites. The result was reported at IEEE ICDCS 2014 (Part-C-9-[2]) and IEEE TDSC(Part-C-8-[6]). - Developed new methods of harnessing encrypted data in cloud for secure and efficient image sharing from mobile devices. We observe that for mobile image sharing, it's possible to directly utilize outsourced correlated images to reproduce (partially) images of interest inside the cloud, so as to save the transmission cost and enjoy immediate image dissemination. Our initial efforts along the direction showed how to achieve the above benefits by leveraging encrypted cloud image datasets. The result was reported at IEEE INFOCOM 2015(Part-C-9-[3]) - Developed new methods for privacy-preserving image feature extraction in cloud computing. The proposed designs enable the outsourcing of a local feature detection algorithm, Scalar Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT), to be executed at cloud. It protects the private image data while saving the cost of the image computation task. Our efforts were reported at ACM Multimedia 2014(Part-C-9-[4]) and ACM TOMM(Part-C-8-[6]). - Developed new methods for secure optimization computation outsourcing, with the case study of linear programming and convex optimizations. Such engineering optimization problems are commonly used in many domains, and often demand large computation resources. How to outsource them to cloud with protection of data input/output and result integrity is a challenging task. Our findings with two specific case designs were reported at IEEE TC(Part-C-8-[2]) and IEEE TIFS(Part-C-8-[3]). They are beneficial to privacy-preserving image recovery services in this project. - Developed new methods for encrypted search under a number of new contexts not studied by prior arts, primarily including multi-keyword ranked search, generalized pattern matching string search, similarity search over high-dimensional data records. Besides, how to enable secure and fast indexing to handle the challenge of high data velocity has also been studied. These efforts are beneficial to the privacy-preserving CBIR services in this project, and were reported at IEEE TPDS(Part-C-8-[1]), TMM(Part-C-8-[5]), IEEE INFOCOM2015(Part-C-9-[5]), ESORICS2015(Part-C-9-[6]), IEEE MSN2015(Part-C-9-[7]).

138513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
138513.value: There are a number of research directions worth further development. 1) Further development could be sought after by extending the proposed service architectures for secure image service in the cloud settings to other cloud application domains, such as cloud media center storing and distributing encrypted video files, or cloud based remote healthcare monitoring systems with privacy guarantees. Both scenarios are related to (but also different from) the proposed research settings, and have seen growing interests from both academia and industry for the services adoption. 2) Great potential also lies in the efforts to extending the privacy-preserving content-based retrieval services into other application contexts, like privacy-preserving recommendations and mobile user targeting. Compared to current research, more application specific characteristics could be leveraged so as to achieve better performance, and potentially rich functionality support. 3) For integration with multiple cloud service providers, it would be interesting to transform the proposed research into a secure middleware between client and different cloud service providers. The client interacts with the secure middleware for privacy-preserving image services outsourcing. The secure middleware could leverage multiple cloud providers for abundant resources and the service scalability, while being privacy-preserving and making everything transparent to the client.

138513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
138513.value: As large-scale image datasets are being exponentially generated today, there is the growing challenge to efficiently store, maintain, and share images in privacy-preserving manner via the cloud platforms. To address the challenges, the research in this project employs compressive sensing technologies as the starting point. The proposed designs satisfy the needs of image service outsourcing, yet keeps outsourced image data always private against unauthorised access. In addition, the proposed research ensures that the extra security overhead brought to cloud remains economically acceptable. Specifically, two services are developed: 1) privacy-preserving image recovery services, where cloud resources can be harnessed for image recovery from compressed samples, without exposing either the image samples or the recovered image content. 2) privacy-preserving content based image retrieval service, where users can selectively retrieve encrypted image samples from the cloud without revealing the private interests. Both services have potential to push forward the secure adoption of cloud, reducing the concerns of unauthorised data leakage, either from outside attacks or from financially-incentivised insiders. The research can find wide application scenarios, such as remote healthcare monitoring systems, remote sensing, etc. It serves solid stepping-stones for further research along the direction of secure computing outsourcing.

138613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
138613.value: Cerebellum is an important brain region which coordinates muscular control for smooth and accurate motor movement. Damage to the cerebellum, as a result of various medical conditions, impacts everyday life of the patients and there is still no complete cure to the neurological disorders. It has also imposed a significant cost to the healthcare system. With advances in fundamental neuroscience and computational technology, implantable biomimetic neuroprosthesis that are capable of restoring brain function has become possible as a therapeutic tool to neurological disorder. In this project, we propose to develop a realistic cerebellum neuroprosthesis which can operate in real-time. We will also address issues that may contribute to more efficient neuroprosthesis in the future. The ultimate goal of this proposed study is to develop a realistic cerebellar prosthetics based on the cerebellum-mediated eyeblink conditioning. This proposal will first address the system configuration appropriate for developing an efficient neuroprosthesis implant by using a biologically plausible cerebellar computational model. We will test if a neural controller, which adaptively adjusts the output of the neuroprosthesis, can lead to more flexible and more efficient configuration for constructing such neuroprosthetic device. The model will then be programmed into an implantable prosthetic device for real-time in vivo testing. To achieve high-speed computation as well as fast and flexible prototyping of a large-scale neural system, we will implement the model into a FPGA-based chip to be interfaced with a multichannel recording system. The device will be tested on awake rats using traditional eyeblink conditioning protocol. We will examine if cerebellar-dependent motor learning function can be restored by the implant. Furthermore, another important question to address in the current study is to investigate the chronic interaction between the biological neural network and the prosthetic implant. We postulate that the potential neural plasticity induced through chronic interaction with the prosthetic device, particularly in an impaired neural network, has important implication for developing future rehabilitation therapy. This proposed study will demonstrate the feasibility of a realistic cerebellar neuroprosthetics for real-time simulation and in vivo operation. The device will feature its biological plausibility as well as generality for future extension to incorporate other motor tasks. This study will also provide new insight to empower future neuroprosthesis development for rehabilitation purpose. 小腦的主要功用為協調肌肉運動的控制。小腦的損害影響患者的日常生活，但現今仍然沒有完全根治的方法，而且亦導致龐大的醫療保健成本。隨著基礎神經科學和電腦技術的進步，植入仿生神經假肢將有可能恢復腦功能並成為新的治療神經系統疾病的手段。 在這個項目中，我們計劃開發一個實時自適應的小腦神經假肢，在動物試驗中研究如果利用這小腦假肢來恢復相關的行為學習障礙。利用高效 FPGA 芯片, 並配合一個以小腦真實結構的數學模型, 我們將開發一實時運算系統, 用以控制植入式小腦神經假肢的運作。在大鼠行為實驗中，我們將測驗神經假肢在對恢復運動控制及學習機能上的效作。此外，我們將研究長時間人工植入物對生物神經網絡的影響。我們希望本計劃的研究成果能對未來的神經義肢康復治療的發展提供新的見解。

138613.label: Realisation of objectives
138613.value: The realization of the project objectives can be divided into the computational and experimental parts. For the computational part (Objectives 1 and 2), we have successfully developed a high performance hardware platform for simulation of large-scale cerebellum neural network model. We have developed a frame-based Network-on-Chip (NoC) hardware architecture for implementing ~100k neurons underlying the cerebellum granular layer network for passage-of-time (POT) representation in FPGA. POT is critical for robust timing coordination of muscles to achieve smooth motor control. The computational speed can achieve to 25.6 ms for simulating 1 sec real world activities. It is also highly scalable (with apparently no slowdown with 10 times more cells) and power efficient. The neural system of interest mainly consists of two types of neurons, granule cells and Golgi cells. This NoC system allows for arbitrary connectivity between Golgi cells and granule-cell clusters. Each processing element is connected to a router through which the action potentials are communicated. The routers are connected together in a mesh topology. When a Golgi cell produces an action potential the interface fetches a list of destination granule-cell clusters from memory, an individual packet is generated to be sent to each of these destinations within the network. The connectivity of the neural network can be updated by adjusting the contents of the memory. To inspect the state of the model the network-on-chip is also responsible for transmitting information externally. When a Golgi cell produces an action potential, a ‘Golgi Message’ packet is also transmitted to a specialist processing element. This processing element buffers all received packets and transmits these packets to a PC. This allows for a user to review the state of each Golgi cell at any time. Our simulation results showed that the FPGA implementation agreed very closely with the software simulation. We have compared the performance of our design with 3 alternative approaches previously proposed for implementing spiking neural network. The CPU implementation is the original software running on Intel Quad Core with 8GB of RAM under the Ubuntu operating system. The GPU implementation was programmed with CUDA. We also tested an alternative digital implementation to a NoC by using a bus between processing cores. In addition to its higher computational speed, our FPGA-based NoC approach clearly demonstrates its outstanding scalability compared with the other approaches in that computation time remains almost constant even if the network size increases by an order of magnitude. We have later completed the implementation of the cerebellum-mediated delayed eyeblink conditioning (DEC) model by adding Purkinje cells (PKJ), deep cerebellar nucleus (DCN) and inferior olive (IO) to the network. A special learning module was also designed to implement long-term depression (LTD) and long-term potentiation (LTP) to realize the learning of such motor control. This module provides efficient resource usage and guarantee no system overflow occurs even with long simulation. For experimental part (Objectives 3 and 4), we have showed a proof-of-concept in vivo demonstration of an integrated cerebellar neuroprosthetic system capable of reproducing the delayed eyeblink conditioning (DEC) based on the above mentioned NoC implementation of cerebellum model on FPGA. An artificial cerebellar spiking neural network model, which models the biological network structure and neural population, was implemented on FPGA for real-time simulation. The neuroprosthetic system was able to elicit conditioned eyeblink with various interstimulus intervals (ISIs) upon repeated pairing of an audio conditioned stimulus (CS) and eyelid airpuff unconditioned stimulus (US). Our system can be potentially generalized for more cerebellum-mediated learning functions. WE used this FPGA cerebellum system for neuroprosthetic application in a rat-FPGA hybrid in vivo experiment. We have established a communication protocol to stream neural signal between the FPGA cerebellum and the data acquisition and stimulation system in real time. Multi-unit neuronal activities were recorded from the pontine nucleus (PN) and inferior olive (IO), which have been shown to relay CS and US signals to the cerebellum respectively. Data acquisition was performed by the Cerebus System (Blackrock Microsystems LLC, USA). Spike detection and sorting were performed online within this system. Neural spikes were extracted by the Cerebus C++ SDK (unit index and timestamps) and were streamed to the FPGA cerebellum model (implemented on a Xilinx Kintex-7 KC705 evaluation board) via the User Datagram Protocol (UDP) at 1kHz. This communication rate ensured no distortion in data transmission and also defined the simulation speed of the cerebellum model such that the simulation time step was 1ms. The FPGA cerebellum model computed the DCN activities (which determine the motor output of eyeblink) in real time based on these recorded PN and IO spikes following the DEC model. The FPGA board was set to run at 31.25MHz clock, such that it completed calculation for each time step of 1ms within 64µs. The output DCN spikes from the FPGA board were used to trigger a stimulus isolator (ISO-Flex, AMPI, Israel). The DCN-triggered stimulus was then delivered to the animal via an electrode bundle implanted in the facial nucleus (FN). Adult male Sprague-Dawley rats were used in the rat-FPGA hybrid experiments. We tested the system with interstimulus interval (ISI) of 100ms, 250ms, and 500ms on multiple days’ experiments. Response pattern of PN and IO for different ISIs which were quite similar. Despite the variability, a general increase in CR% through training was observed for all the three ISIs tested. The overall increase in CR% was consistent with other conditioning experiments. The peak DCN firing rate generally increased with CR% over learning. The progress of learning was also reflected in temporal DCN firing and the blink response. We show that DCN became more active with more CS-US pairing as LTD strengthened. We also show that at the beginning of experiments, No Blink or Shaking Eyelid was observed in the majority of trials. But as training continued, more Weak/Strong Blinks were observed. These results validated learning of CR in both neural and behavioral levels. Our project has shown that our FPGA cerebellum can be a potential neuroprosthetic tool for restoring motor function in damaged cerebellum.

138613.label: Major findings and research outcome
138613.value: The key outcome of this project is the development of a powerful computational platform for real-time simulation of large scale cerebellum spiking neural network model in an efficient and scalable manner. We demonstrated its functionality for simulating model behavior as well as for in vivo neuroprosthetic application. The modularized design of our platform considered the neural processor, neuron-to-neuron connectivity and synaptic plasticity. These components are generic for a neural network and our design can be readily adapted for a modified network to investigate new neuroscience question. These works have led to collaborations with research groups in UK (Dr. Patrick Degenaar and Dr. Terrence Mak) and Japan (Dr. Soichi Nagao and Dr. Tadashi Yamazaki). Our results have been reported in IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Circuits and Systems (Luo et. al. 2016) and Journal of Neural Engineering (Xu et. al. 2017). We have also presented some of our preliminary findings in IEEE EMBC 2014 and ISIC 2014. Along the way in terms of investigation of neuroprosthetic application, we have also developed new algorithm for EMG-based hand gesture classification for prosthetic application using convolution neural network. We have shown a self-recalibrating classifier that can be automatically updated to maintain a stable performance over time without the need for user retraining. Our results suggest that the proposed system can be a useful tool to facilitate long-term adoption of prosthetics for amputees in real-life applications (Zhai et. al. 2017).

138613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
138613.value: A highly efficient computational platform has been developed for simulating large scale neural network model. This tool can be used for studying new neural components and new plasticity of the cerebellum system effectively. Our modularized system allows one to readily extend the model to incorporate these new components without compromising the computational speed. Furthermore, our system may also be used to study learning behavior that occurs in long term. Learning that occurs in weeks or months would require a high speed computation platform such as the system we developed in this project to realize feasible investigation. Finally, our system may be translated into ASIC platform for portable and more power efficient implementation in realistic application on longer experiments.

138613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
138613.value: Damage to the cerebellum, as a result of various medical conditions, impacts everyday life of patients and there is still no complete cure to neurological disorders. Neuroprostheses that can functionally replace the damaged neural circuit have recently emerged as a possible solution to these problems. However, the neural system such as the cerebellum is very complex which comprises of many neuron cells and extensive network connectivity, and mimicking it requires huge computing power. This is not possible with common desktop computer and would require careful design for a highly efficient simulation platform to realize. Using the hardware FPGA technology, we have developed a computational platform that is high speed, power efficient and scalable. This platform can mimic the computation of the cerebellum neural network in real-time such that it may replace a damaged cerebellum and restore the lost capability of learning motor task in these brain-damaged animals. This capability has been validated in animal experiment on a simple but important motor learning behavior in this project. The outcomes of our study may provide a new useful tool for building future neuroprosthetic to improve living quality of these brain-damaged patients.

138713.label: Project Objectives
138713.value: To develop a new layer-by-layer biomimetic structure in seeking of enhanced crack-resistance. The new structure is inspired by the gradually changing mechanical behavior through natural enamel-DEJ-dentin structure. To investigate the viscosity-related failure mechanism of the layer-by-layer biomimetic structure with multi-scale mechanical experiments. State-of-the-art microscopes such as AFM and SEM will be utilized to observe and characterize the fracture topographies. To develop a mechanistically-based computational framework to predict the viscosity-related strength and fatigue life of the structure. The model will then be backtested and validated by comparing with the experimental results. The validated model could provide guidance to the future design of crack-resistant biomimetic structures.

138713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
138713.value: Abstract Nature develops crack-resistant structures. One example is the natural teeth which are formed by enamel, dentin and dentin-enamel-junction (DEJ) (Figure 1a). Although small cracks could generate in the brittle enamel, most of them are arrested at the enamel-dentin interface (Figure 1b). Bulk failure of the teeth is therefore prevented. More dramatically, the structure could survive millions of cycles of occlusal loading with the existence of these cracks [Lin et al., 1994; Imbeni et al., 2005; Chai et al., 2009]. Inspired by the remarkable crack-resistance of natural teeth, many efforts were devoted to develop multilayer structures that are formed with hard top and durable substrate [Lawn, 2002; Lawn et al., 2004; Lee et al., 2002; Huang, et al., 2007a, 2007b]. However, this biomimetic endeavor encounters long-standing difficulty. Although having similar structures, none of the man-made multilayers could provide crack-resistance that is comparable to nature teeth. This difficulty is caused by many reasons. Lack of guidance upon structural design and inadequate information about failure mechanisms are among the most important ones. In this project, a novel layer-by-layer biomimetic structure will be developed by learning from the comprehensive microstructure of natural teeth. In the new structure, material properties will change gradually from top to bottom and there will be no distinct top or substrate layers. The gradually changing structure has the potential to minimize the stress concentration and crack driving force in the structure [Hauber, 2009; Hill and Lin, 2002; Hill et al., 2002]. Then, viscosity-related failure mechanism of this new structure will be investigated. Mechanical experiments will be performed under macro-, micro- and nano- scales to explore the modulus, viscosity, fracture toughness and other physical response of the structure. State-of-the-art microscopes such as atomic force microscope (AFM), scanning electron microscope (SEM) and transmission electron microscope (TEM) will be adopted to characterize the fracture surfaces and crack paths. In addition, non-linear finite element analysis (FEA) will be carried out to simulate, verify and promote the design. A successfully validated computational framework could provide guidance to the future design of crack-resistant layer-by-layer structures. The project will not only benefit the development of new dental structures, but also provide a light-weighted and tougher layer-by-layer structure for a broader class of engineering devices such as wind blades, printed circuit boards and automobile parts etc. The methodologies used in this project could also benefit the research and development on diversified biomimetic projects. 大自然能制造出抗裂結構。由牙釉質，本釉交界層（DEJ）和牙本質構成的天然牙齒是一個很好的例子（圖1a）。雖然小裂紋容易在牙釉質中形成，但它們大都能被本釉界面成功阻擋（圖1b）從而避免牙齒的整體破壞。更加了不起的是，該結構能夠在有裂紋存在的情況下繼續承受上百萬次的咀嚼循環載荷[Lin et al., 1994; Imbeni et al., 2005; Chai et al., 2009]。被天然牙齒卓越的抗裂性所激勵，人們努力研制由堅固頂層和耐用底層所構成的多層結構[Lawn, 2002; Lawn et al., 2004; Lee et al., 2002; Huang, et al., 2007a, 2007b ]。然而，這種仿生學方面的努力非常困難。雖然擁有相似的宏觀結構，但人造多層結構的抗裂性無法和自然牙齒媲美。該問題的原因多種多樣。缺乏對結構設計的指導和對破壞機理研究不足是兩個重要原因。 學自天然牙結構完善的微觀結構，本項目致力於開發一個新的多層仿生結構。為了減少應力集中和裂紋驅動力，新結構的材料性能將自上而下逐漸變化，避免明顯的頂層或底層 [Hauber, 2009; Hill and Lin, 2002; Hill et al., 2002]。本項目將研究和粘性相關的斷裂機制。宏觀、微觀和納觀的力學實驗將提供結構的模量、粘度、斷裂韌性和其他物理響應。先進的顯微技術如：原子力顯微鏡（AFM）、掃描電子顯微鏡（SEM）和透射電子顯微鏡（TEM）將表征斷口和裂紋路徑。此外，將采用非線性有限元法（FEA）來模擬、驗證和改進設計方案。一個被成功驗證的計算框架將會為未來的抗裂多層結構設計提供指導。 本項目將開發一個新的輕韌多層結構。它不僅適用於牙科，而且可被廣泛使用於多種工業器件如：風力發電葉片、印刷電路板和汽車零部件等。本項目采用的方法論也普適於其他仿生學研發。

138813.label: Project Objectives
138813.value: To develop a robust nano-fatigue testing platform based on the commercially available DMD device, with reasonably low-cost, high performance and reliability. By establishing the protocol for driving and programing the tilting movement of individual micro mirrors with calibrated cyclic loading and geometry, this platform should be readily available for characterizing the fatigue behavior of various 1-D nanomaterials. To perform high cycle tensile fatigue tests on single crystalline gold and nickel nanowires as well as multi-walled carbon nanotubes with diameters ranging from tens of nanometers to hundreds of nanometers; to probe the size effect in fatigue life and failure mechanisms for metallic nanostructures and carbon nanotubes, with the assist of in situ SEM imaging and post-test high resolution TEM (HRTEM) analysis. By choosing 1-D nanomaterial samples with appropriate geometries, such as metallic nanowires or multi-wall carbon nanotubes with larger diameters, to explore the potential of the platform in high cycle torsional fatigue testing---it might be noted that, at small scales, torsion is a long-desired loading geometry but has not been realized yet for 1-D nanomaterials; to study the fatigue behavior for nanowires/nanotubes under torsional cyclic loading. By taking the advantage of DMD’s inherent characteristics for DLP projection, to perform nano-fatigue tests without electron microscopes (sample pre-clamped via FIB); the successful implementation of this objective will lead to the next sub-objectives: (4a) to explore the possibility for high throughput experiments, i.e., to perform multiple nano-fatigue tests at the same time by monitoring their corresponding pixels through DLP projection display; (4b) the environmental effects (such as temperature, humidity) on the fatigue behavior of single crystalline metallic nanowires. (Optional) To develop a laboratory course module for creative design and use of commercial MEMS devices (e.g. DMD) for unconventional engineering applications, as well as to teach the current state-of-the-art MEMS technology by using DMD as an example and DMD-based DLP development kit as a creative lab demo system. (see Education Plan for more details)

138813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
138813.value: Despite extensive research into the mechanical properties of one-dimensional (1-D) nanomaterials, such as metallic/semiconductor nanowires and carbon nanotubes, for the past two decades, experimental data on the fatigue behavior (i.e. the changes in properties resulting from cyclic loading) of these 1-D nanostructures have rarely been reported. This is largely due to the critical challenges on performing quantitative mechanical testing on such exceedingly small samples with consistent repeated loading. Recently, MEMS (microelectromechanical systems)-based testing platforms have emerged as powerful and versatile tools to interrogate low-dimensional micro- and nanostructures, and a number of MEMS devices have been successfully developed to investigate the mechanical strength and plastic deformation for various kinds of 1-D nanomaterials. However, the dynamic characterization for important fatigue behavior, which ultimately limits the ability to achieve the full potential of nanowire/nanotube-based devices in numerous engineering applications, especially flexible electronics and bio-integrated electronics, remains highly challenging, mainly due to the inherent limitations of existing MEMS designs. Here, instead of designing a dedicated MEMS device, we propose to adopt a commercially available MEMS product---DMD (Digital Micromirror Device, by Texas Instruments) for the development of a novel nano-fatigue testing platform, and to study the high-cycle fatigue behavior of metallic nanowires and carbon nanotubes. Originally designed for Digital Light Processing (DLP) as a sophisticated light switch, DMD is essentially millions of hinge-mounted microscopic mirrors which can be individually deflected +/- 12 degrees for several thousand times per second (up to 32kHz). Through the electrostatic force attraction, the deflection of each micro mirror can be controlled by changing the binary state of the underlying CMOS memory cell, to realize the cyclic tensile or torsional loading onto the sample. The small footprint of DMD chip also makes it’s capable for “in situ” testing---to perform experiments inside a scanning electron microscope (SEM) for observing the deformation process; on the other hand, by taking advantage of DMD’s own characteristics, it’s possible to monitor fatigue testing status directly by optical projection, without the need of electron microscopes, which may facilitate the study of biomaterials and tissues as well as the environmental effects on fatigue behavior for 1-D nanomaterials. We believe that the implementation of this proposal will not only offer some key insights on fatigue behavior of 1-D nanomaterials, but also stimulate interest among researchers in exploring other potentials in existing MEMS designs, as well as developing even more capable MEMS-based platforms for cross-disciplinary, unconventional engineering and research applications. 在過去的二十多年裏，盡管大量的研究致力於一維納米材料（例如金屬/半導體納米線和碳納米管）的力學性能，實驗上關於這些一維納米結構的疲勞性質（即多次循環加載而導致的材料損傷）的觀測和數據仍然極度缺乏。很大程度上，這是因為對於如此之細小的納米尺度樣品進行持續恒定的力學加載並定量測試其力學性能變化的難度很高。最近，基於MEMS（微電機系統）的測試平臺逐漸展示出其用於低維度微納米材料性質研究的巨大潛力。一系列專屬MEMS器件被開發出來並成功用於對多種一維納米材料的力學強度和塑性變形機制的研究。然而，對於在實踐應用中至關重要的材料疲勞性質的動態表征---這將從根本上決定基於納米線/納米管的器件在各種工程應用中能否展現其全部潛力---卻依然困難重重，很大程度上在於已有的MEMS設計本身所具有局限性。因此，相較於專門設計一種新的MEMS測試器件，我們決定另辟蹊徑，采納一種已有的商業化MEMS產品---DMD（數位微鏡面元件，美國德州儀器研發）而發展出一套新型納米疲勞測試平臺，並用以研究金屬納米線及碳納米管的高循環疲勞性質。 原本設計作為一種復雜的光學開關用於數字光處理，DMD本質上是數百萬個在鉸鏈上固定並能以每秒數千次（高達32kHz）的頻率傾轉+/-12度角度的微型鏡面陣列。通過靜電吸引力，每個微鏡面的獨立傾轉能通過改變位於其下的CMOS記憶單元的二進位狀態來控制，並實現對在其表面上固定的樣品的拉伸或扭轉循環加載。並且，由於其本身的小尺寸，DMD芯片也使得極具有吸引力的“原位測試”變得可能---也就是說，允許實驗在掃描電子顯微鏡腔體內實現：一邊進行疲勞測試，一邊實時觀察材料損傷的過程。另一方面，通過利用DMD本身用於光處理的特性，我們將可能使用光學放大投影來實現對於微納米樣品疲勞測試狀態的實時監測，而不必依賴於電子顯微鏡設備---這也將大大有利於對生物材料和生物組織，以及對一維納米材料在環境效應下疲勞特性的相關研究。 我們相信，該項目的成功執行將不僅僅對一維納米材料的疲勞性質提供一些關鍵的認識，它也將激發科研同仁對於探索其它已有MEMS器件設計之潛在應用的興趣，並且開發出更具有潛力的MEMS測試平臺用於各種交叉學科以及非傳統的工程和科研應用。

138813.label: Realisation of objectives
138813.value: 1. The Digital Micromirror Device (DMD)-based high cycle fatigue testing platform has been successfully established. By this platform, we have tested various kinds of 1D nanomaterials in cyclic loading modes: Despite that DMD is a commercial device, to use it for the desired nanomechanical testing purpose remains of challenge. Experimentally, after removing the cover protective glass lid on the DMD chip (which was a great challenge), we can access the mirrors directly under microscopes. Inside the DMD is a micro-electro-mechanical system (MEMS) consisting of hundreds of thousands of over one million of tiny switchable micro-mirrors with two stable states. Upon the electrode potential, the mirror could be electrostatically attracted to address electrodes with the largest electrostatic field potential when bias/reset voltage was applied. Then, we use a micromanipulator probe station with a sharp tungsten microprobe to pick up individual nanowires and place them onto the designated location at DMD. The movement of each individual micro-mirrors can be programmed and controlled by using a customized Digital Light Processing (DLP) development kit. The tilting movement of individual micromirror could be used to apply mechanical loading on the nanowire attached on mirrors. The flipping rates of the micromirror could be up to 32,000 Hz, an attractive feature for high cycle testing. With the assist of finite element method (FEM) and selectively clamping the 1D nanomaterial samples with respect to the different micro-mirrors, the tensile strain amplitude could be changed and quantified. Due to its small footprint and the cable-remote controlling mechanisms, we put this platform into SEM for in situ SEM fatigue testing after successfully tested under optical microscope in ambient environment. Overall this work has been published in the leading journal of mechanics “Extreme Mechanics Letters” titled “Digital Micromirror Device (DMD)-based High-Cycle Tensile Fatigue Testing of 1D Nanomaterials”. 2. We have successfully demonstrated the application of this platform for tensile fatigue testing on various 1D nanomaterials at a quantitative manner: For example polymer nanowire (polyurethane) was clamped on the DMD with four micromirrors at flat state around it. During the first half of the testing cycle, the micromirror at the upper right corner was flipped to positive 12º while the lower left one was flipped to negative 12 º, which result in the nanowire being stretched with strain about 15.5% and moving upwards. Then the pose of the two micromirrors switched at the second half of the testing cycle quickly, which result in the nanowire being stretched with strain about 14.7% and moving downwards. Repeating the process alternatively would induce a cyclic tensile loading on the nanowire. After ~287,500 cycles’ test, the polymer nanowire fatigued. To quantify the strain/stress distribution of nanowire under tension, finite element method (FEM) modeling was adopted. We used commercial software (ANSYS) to simulate the deformation behavior of nanowire driven by the tilting movements of DMD. Therefore, the concept of high frequency fatigue test for nanowires based on our DMD platform has been clearly demonstrated. The main achievement obtained in this objective has been detailed in our Extreme Mechanics Letters paper. Other parts of achievements can be reflected in our Experimental Mechanics paper titled as “Low-Cycle Fatigue Testing of Ni Nanowires Based on a Micro-Mechanical Device” and Science Advances paper titled as “Approaching the ideal elastic strain limit in silicon nanowires”, in which we used another MEMS-type device (PTP) for the low-frequency cyclic testing of metallic and semiconductor nanowires. 3. We have successfully performed the qualitative torsional fatigue study on 1D nanomaterials by this fatigue test platform: The challenging but desired torsional deformation of nanowires could be realized by aligning the sample along the tilting axis of the micromirrors. The maximum twisting angle of the sample could be totally 24°, when two mirrors were fully tilted toward the opposite directions. The effective torsion gauge length also depended on the distance between the two glue clamping positions. The strain distribution of the tested sample under torsion was also simulated by the finite element method (FEM) modeling strategy. The FEM analysis can precisely quantify the fatigue strain limit of the nanomaterial and give an in-depth investigating of their failure mechanisms during the torsional loading. Specifically, we demonstrated the torsional twisting of a silver nanowire with diameter ~100 nm and gauge length ~25 μm by 12°. During the test, the micromirror at the upper left corner was fixed, while another micromirror at the lower right firstly flipped to positive 12°, and then flipped to negative 12°. Repeat of this process can induce the torsion loading on the nanowire. The nanowire hasn’t failed after more than one million cycles of loading. On another Ag nanowire with the gauge length reduced to ~1 μm, a torsional fatigue behavior was observed after ~432,000 cycles’ loading. The main achievements obtained in this objective have been published in journal Micromachine titled “Digital micromirror device (DMD)-based high-cycle torsional fatigue testing micromachine for 1D nanomaterials”. 4. We successfully demonstrated that this platform can work without SEM, being working under optical microscope, as well as via DLP display. In addition, due to the millions of micro-mirrors, we also demonstrated the possibility for high throughput fatigue testing experiments of this DMD device by successfully aligning multiple Ag nanowires array in the DMD devices. Due to the millions of micro mirrors on a single chip which can be operated individually and independently, we could potentially test them at the same time after dispersing, aligning and clamping many individual nanowires under different micromirror configurations and different gauge lengths. Monitoring of the fatigue status can also be achieved via the DMD pixel brightness changes in parallel. Therefore, high-throughput nanofatigue testing can be potentially performed by this platform with very low cost, and thus speed up the depicting of the whole picture of fatigue characteristics by testing a large quantity of individual 1-D nanomaterial samples at the same time. We can also test many samples with varied chemical compositions, such as metallic glasses or high entropy alloys with different atomic compositions, to identify the best alloy compositions with highest fatigue life performances. This approach can be very helpful for “Materials Genome” research. The related achievements can be reflected in our Micromachine paper titled “Digital micromirror device (DMD)-based high-cycle torsional fatigue testing micromachine for 1D nanomaterials”, and our Scanning paper titled “Recent Advances on In Situ SEM Mechanical and Electrical Characterization of Low-Dimensional Nanomaterials”, as well as the newly published Extreme Mechanics Letters paper. 5. We have developed a laboratory course module for creative design and use of commercial MEMS devices for unconventional engineering. We bought a used DLP projector and dissembled it for the class teaching purpose. The feedbacks were very good. We improved our DMD-based laboratory module for better teaching of the latest MEMS technologies in some of the PI’s undergraduate courses, and trained several undergraduate students in our lab for part-time research throughout the successfully implementation of the project. Our work has been invited to show in the CityU Discovery Festival 2015 with PhD student Chenchen Jiang.

138813.label: Major findings and research outcome
138813.value: Through the research of this project, we successfully applied the commercially available digital micromirror device (DMD) into a fatigue testing platform for various kinds of 1D nanostructures (see our Extreme Mechanics Letters paper). The DMD-based platform is proved to be suitable for high-cycle both tensile and torsional fatigue testing of individual nanowire. By applying cyclic tensile tests on different nanowire samples with varied mechanical characters and geometries, the advantages and feasibility of this platform, such as stable high cyclic tensile straining, low cost, versatile for in situ tests under microscopes, were demonstrated. We also verified that fatigue can exist in nanomaterials (see our Experimental Mechanics paper) About the torsional fatigue testing, we also demonstrated its feasibility by characterizing the high-cycle fatigue behavior of several nanowires with different diameters and shear strains (see our Micromachine paper). More importantly, the small footprint of the DMD was proved to be small enough for in situ SEM testing, which is highly desired for observing the deformation and failure processes to construct the useful microstructure-property relationship, and possibly revealing the underlying mechanisms of nanostructure fatigue behaviors. With the millions of micro mirrors on a single chip, high-throughput fatigue tests of multiple specimens at the same time can be also achieved for statistical analysis, which presumably allow the prediction of fatigue life of these 1-D nanosized building blocks for their real device applications. Due to the commercial availability of the DMD and millions of micromirrors available on a single chip, this platform could offer a low-cost and high-throughput nanomechanical solution for the uncovered torsional fatigue behavior of various 1D nanostructures. For the relatively low-cyclic nano-fatigue testing, we also built up a micro-mechanical device (MMD)-based low cycle in situ SEM tensile fatigue testing platform with the assistance of a picoindenter, which can fulfill the quantitative low cycle fatigue testing with various kinds of 1D nanostructures. Based on the MMD-based low cycle cyclic tensile testing platform, we observed the ultra-large elasticity behavior on pristine single crystalline Si nanowires (our Science Advances paper). With our in situ SEM nanomechanical characterization platforms, the mechanical properties of several typical metallic, polymer as well as semiconductor nanostructures has also been studied through both experimental and theoretical strategies for their cyclic deformation behavior. These size-dependent and unusual mechanical behaviors are reported in details by other published academic journal papers (such as Science Advances, Journal of Applied Physics, Scanning, Acta Mechanica).

138813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
138813.value: The further development regarding to this project is the development of high throughput fatigue testing platform based on the current DMD-based high cycle fatigue testing platform, as well as the investigation on the influence of environmental impacts on the fatigue properties on low dimensional nanomaterials. The possibility is because that there are millions of independent movable micromirrors on a single DMD chip, all of them can be well controlled by a customized DLP development kit, therefore it’s particularly suitable for high-throughput testing of various 1-D nanomaterial samples for the statistical analysis of their fatigue characteristics. This approach can be very helpful for “Materials Genome” research. Due to the small footprint of the DMD, it can be used under both vacuum inside the SEM and ambient environment under an optical microscope. With the design of a dedicated testing kit with adjustable temperature and humidity, the environmental influence on the fatigue properties of low dimensional nanostructures can be further investigated. Besides, with the development of sample fabrication and transferring techniques of recently hot two dimensional (2D) materials, like graphene, MoS2, etc., fatigue behavior investigation can be expected to extend to such 2D materials’ mechanics based on our DMD-based fatigue testing platform.

138813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
138813.value: Fatigue, or the progressive and localized structural damage that occurs when a material is subjected to cyclic loading, is a commonly encountered mode of failure in materials that ultimately limited their device stability and lifetime. At nanoscale, fatigue behavior of nanomaterials was found to also exist and critical for numerous nanomechanical applications involving dynamic deformation processes, such as in flexible electronics devices. In this project, instead of designing a new device, commercial digital micromirror device (DMD) has been successfully adopted to develop a cost-effective platform for investigating the high-cycle fatigue responses of individual nanowires under both tensile and torsional modes, due to its ultra-high actuation frequency (up to 32,000Hz). In addition, the millions of independent movable micromirrors on a single DMD chip make our platform particularly suitable for parallel high-throughput testing of nanomaterials for statistical analysis. The experimental data obtained in this project provides some key insights on the nanomechanical behavior of metallic, semiconductor and polymer nanowires. This micromachine solution, together with the other nanomechanical testing solutions developed in this project, could also inspire the design and development of novel MEMS-based micromechanical testing systems for other kinds of nanoscale materials, such as recently emerging 2D materials (e.g. graphene).

138913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
138913.value: 網絡動力系統由多個交互的智能體或子系統組成。同單智能體相比，網絡系統通過協調控制可以更加靈活有效地完成指定任務。網絡系統協調控制的概念由現實生活中的一些基本問題啟發而來，如機器人組協調問題和無人機編隊問題。近年來，有關網絡化系統分佈式協調控制問題的研究層出不窮，例如一致性問題、編隊問題及蜂擁問題。但在大部份已有文獻中， 網絡化系統都是由單積分器、雙積分器或線性系統等簡單的動態智能體組成。而現實生活中，網絡化系統多由帶有任意不確定項的非線性動力模型組成，如未知環境中的移動機器人網絡，或在領導者軌跡未知情況下發生蜂擁行為的微型飛行器組。 本項目將研究由帶有未知參數的非線性智能體組成的網絡化系統的自適應協調伺服問題。此問題包括以上提到的一致性、編隊及蜂擁問題。本項目會將伺服理論的應用從單一動力系統擴展到一組相互連通的動力系統，開發新的方法以解決由復雜的非線性動力模型和系統的不確定性帶來的技術性問題，并且為領導者軌跡未知的伺服問題建立可解性條件。此項目的理論結果將用于研究有領導者的移動機器人組的自適應一致性問題，以及其他實際控制器的設計問題。

138913.label: Major findings and research outcome
138913.value: A number of critical and fundamental issues in the field of networked control systems have been investigated. In particular, the adaptive coordinated servomechanism problem for networked systems with each agent dominated by a dynamical model with unknown parameters has been studied. Effective control strategies have been developed to handle networked systems in more practical settings with less restrictive assumptions. A new framework has been developed to deal with the adaptive coordinated servomechanism problem for uncertain networked systems. Then the framework has been applied to solve the adaptive coordinated servomechanism problem for uncertain networked systems in output feedback form and strict feedback form with unknown control direction. These two classes of nonlinear systems have been the most fundamental yet critical nonlinear systems in the area, which a large number of practical systems can be formulated into. To address the coordinated servomechanism problems of networked systems, same problems for single nonlinear systems with uncertainties and unknown exosystem have also been studied. With the developed framework and results in single nonlinear systems, the problems of networked nonlinear systems can be handled. On one hand, the assumptions in previous results such as the parameter uncertainties are sufficiently small or their boundaries are known a priori have been removed. On the other hand, almost all previous works on coordinated control of networked systems assume that the dynamics of the exosystem are exactly known so that its trajectory can be utilized in controller design. Applying the developed framework and control strategy, this unrealistic assumption has also been removed. Finally, the application of the developed control strategies to important engineering problems such as coordination of networked mobile robots and tracking control of ships have also been investigated.

138913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
138913.value: A number of results have been obtained and published regarding the adaptive coordinated servomechanism problem for uncertain networked systems. Nevertheless, many intriguing problems in coordinated control of networked systems are worth investigating. For example, so far we have assumed the communication network is time invariant, while in many cases in practice the network might be changing from time to time. This is of great importance considering the application of the developed control strategies. It has been one of our recent interests and could be one of the future research focuses.

138913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
138913.value: Coordinated control of networked systems is largely motivated by fundamental applications in the real world ranging from coordination of a group of mobile robots to formation of a team of unmanned aerial vehicles. A basic feature of coordinated control of networked systems is that a controller for each subsystem can only use information from itself and its neighbors. The coordinated servomechanism problem includes many existing interesting problems such as consensus, formation, and flocking as well as swarming and rendezvous as its special cases. This research project has investigated the adaptive coordinated servomechanism problem for networked systems with each agent dominated by a dynamical model with unknown parameters. Effective control strategies have been developed for more practical networked systems such as those systems subjected to unknown external disturbances and/or with parameter uncertainties. A number of restrictive assumptions required in most previous results that are rarely satisfied in practical networked systems have been removed. The outcome of this research project can significantly enhance the feasibility, functionality and flexibility of control systems.

139013.label: Project Title(Chinese)
139013.value: 在绿色建筑中通过整合策略以提升设计单位的市场绩效

139013.label: Project Objectives
139013.value: This research aims to investigate and test the potential of integration as a strategy for design firms to enhance performance in Hong Kong's green construction market. The objectives are to: develop and test a conceptual framework to increase design firms’ performance through design, social, supply chain and customer integration (integrative factors) in green advantages (costing savings, green quality and innovation); investigate the extent to which integrative factors lead to higher green advantages; examine whether green advantages lead to better design firms’ performance; and establish a decision support system to enable a design firm’s performance and green advantage to be predicted. Regarding the decision support system, it will enable design firms to confirm and adjust their practices to enhance performance in Hong Kong’s green construction market, as well as their special capabilities in integration implementation. Design firms will glean information in three aspects: (i) green advantages, (ii) critical integration strategies to enhance performance, and (iii) important practices to achieve integration in Hong Kong’s green market.

139013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
139013.value: 'Green Building' is strongly encouraged by Hong Kong’s government. The development of green building provides expanding opportunities for Hong Kong’s design firms. To survive and develop in Hong Kong's green construction market, design firms have to identify appropriate strategies to enhance their performance, while the core is to adopt integration approach to provide environmental-friendly product. Inspired by strategic management principles, design firms should utilize integration to create advantages in market, thereby achieve good performance. In this project, integration is of four dimensions: design integration (via integrated design), customer integration, supply chain integration, and social integration. Design firm advantages consist of cost savings, green quality, and innovative production. As design firms attempt to create their integrated environments, two problems emerge from the inherent separation of design and production stages of construction industry. Firstly, in the context of create advantages, will a high level of “design integration” lead to higher levels of “customer integration” and “supply chain integration”, and thereby create competitive position in market? Secondly, what is the role of integration based on no-economic activities (social integration in this project), in creating integration environment? To address above problems, this research aims to investigate and test the potential of integration as a strategy for design firms to enhance performance in Hong Kong's green construction market. The objectives are to: (i) develop and test a conceptual framework to increase design firms’ performance through design, social, supply chain and customer integration (integrative factors) in green advantages (costing savings, green quality and innovation); (ii) investigate the extent to which integrative factors lead to higher green advantages; (iii) examine whether green advantages lead to better design firms’ performance; and (iv) design a decision support system to enable a design firm’s performance and green advantage to be predicted. The population of this study are building design firms in Hong Kong, who deal with developers, contractors, government regulatory bodies, users and materials suppliers. Simple random sample method will be employed to select building design firms that have designed green building projects in Hong Kong. The data collection instrument will be a structured questionnaire, utilizing email survey and face-to-face interviews. Structural equation modeling will be adopted to develop and test the models. A decision support system for practitioners and academics on how to enhance integration, and finally to achieve good performance in Hong Kong's green construction, will be developed. 香港政府大力推进绿色建筑，相应不断扩大的绿色建筑市场为香港的设计公司提供了更多发展机会。绿色市场中生存和发展，要求设计公司采用适当的策略提高公司绩效，其核心是采用整合方法以提供绿色产品。受到策略管理原理的启发，设计公司应该利用整合策略创造市场优势，从来提升公司绩效。在此项目中，整合有四个纬度：设计整合，客户整合，供应链整合，以及社会关系整合。设计公司的优势包括：成本节省，绿色质量，和创新产品。 由于建筑行业与生俱来的设计和生产阶段的分隔，设计公司在创建自己的整合环境时，会面临两个问题。第一，在获得市场优势时，设计的高程度整合一定会带来高度的客户整合和供应链整合吗？并由此确立市场竞争地位？第二，以非经济性行为为基础的社会关系整合在创造整合环境中的角色是什么？ 为解决以上问题，此项目的主要目的是研究并测试整合策略对于提高公司在香港绿色建筑市场中的绩效的潜能。具体目标有：i) 建立并检测用于提升公司绩效的概念模型；此概念模型通过设计-社交-供应链-客户等因素的相互作用获取绿色优势；ii) 研究以上各因素的相互作用与公司绩效间的量化关系；iii) 检测绿色优势与公司绩效的关系；iv) 设计并测试一套供设计公司使用的决策支持和预测体系。 此项目的目标人群是香港的建筑设计公司。随机样本的方法将用来选取那些有参与绿色建筑设计的香港设计公司。信件调查和面对面采访的数据通过问卷来收集。概念模型将通过结构模型进行模拟和分析。最终的决策支持和预测体系将帮助香港建筑业界人士用于提高公司在绿色建筑市场中的绩效 。

139013.label: Realisation of objectives
139013.value: Acknowledgment: This research is made possible by the Hong Kong General Research Fund [RGC 139013 (i.e. 9041988)]. The four objectives are realized, and the relative results were published in 1 A+ journal paper (Ling and Li, 2016) and 2 Conference papers (Li, 2016; Li and Ma, 2017), supported by RGC 139013 (i.e. 9041988). In brief, these four objectives are realized through applying reasonable research methodology and adopting appropriate data analysis methods. In particular, literature review, pilot study, questionnaire survey, t-test and correlation methods were adopted to achieve the objectives. 1. In particular, the 1st objective to develop and test a conceptual framework to increase design firms’ performance through design, social, supply chain and customer is realized by using methods of literature review and pilot study. Literature review was used to identify both components and structure of the conceptual framework, while pilot study to assess and polish the conceptual framework was adopted to improve the feasible and reasonable of the conceptual framework. In literature review, theories of integration strategy, competitiveness and relative business models were reviewed to identify the components of the conceptual framework. In particular, Porter’s generic competitiveness strategy and integration strategy were reviewed in details. The structure of the conceptual framework, mainly presented by the connections between actions/practices, advantages and firm performance were established by reviewing literatures on nature and structure of business models. In brief, in this conceptual framework, components are design integration, social integration, supply chain integration, customer integration, advantages and firm performance. Pilot study was carried out between PI and expert to assess the feasibility and reasonability of the components and the structure of conceptual framework. Following experts’ suggestions, component of social integration, one of the components proposed through literature review, was internalized as partial practices of other three components, including design integration, supply chain integration and customer integration. In addition, green advantages are suggested to be operationalized as cost leadership, differentiation and focus after refined literature review and pilot study. Results are published in Ling and Li (2016). 2. The 2nd objective to investigate the extent to which integrative factors lead to higher advantages is realized by using questionnaire survey and t-test method. Questionnaire survey was carried out to collect the data from design firms who operating in green market. The questions in questionnaire are coming from the conceptual framework. The questions were organized into three sections, including general information, actions/practices taken and performance achieved. The t-test of the mean was carried out to check whether the sample data were significantly different from the population mean (μ). For each measurement item, the null hypothesis (Ho: μ ≤ μo) that the variable was equal to or below the population mean and the alternative hypothesis (H1: μ > μo) that the variable was above the population mean were set out. The t-test was performed on each of the measurement to determine if the firms are competitive in each area, on each of actions/practices to check the extent to which each of the actions/practices was adopted to a significant extent. In total, 3 out of 20 critical practices are not effective to achieve advantages of cost leadership, differentiation and focus. 2 of these 3 practices are from supply integration, and the other one is from customer integration. In particular, design integration practices contributes to both cost leadership and differentiation; supply chain integration contributes to cost leadership; customer integration contributes to both cost leadership and focus. The results are reported in Ling and Li (2016). In addition, the implementation of design integration, which is one part of the 2nd objective, is further studied and reported in Li (2016). In particular, critical activities to carry out design integration is further studied. The results highlighted the importance of reconfiguration of design chain and the reduction of costs in operation in integration process. 3. The 3rd objective to examine whether green advantages lead to better design firms’ performance is realized by conducting Pearson’s correlation analysis. The correlation coefficient was used to determine whether there is any evidence of statistically significant association between these variables. Correlation coefficients (r) can take on only values ranging from −1 (perfect negative relationship) to +1 (perfect positive relationship). 3 out of 7 aspects of firm performance are not significant. In particularly, advantages of cost leadership and differentiation contribute a lot to firm performance in providing competitive productive, client satisfaction, public image and speedy delivery. Advantage of focus makes no contribution to firm performance. Furthermore, in terms of enhancing product quality and public image, differentiation is more effective than cost leadership. While in delivery design in a speedy way, cost leadership is most effective. 4. The 4th objective to establish a decision support system to enable a design firm’s performance and green advantage to be predicted is realized by propose a business model (Ling and Li, 2016). The structure of this business model is referring to Morris et al. (2005)’s business model structure that addresses six components: value-offering factors, market factors, internal capability factors, competitive strategy factors, economic factors and personal factors. Information of (i) green advantages, (ii) critical integration strategies to enhance performance, and (iii) important practices to achieve integration is reorganized in the business model to determine (i) the value to be created, (ii) the market to be targeted, (iii) the internal capability to be applied, (iv) competitive position to be established, (v) the money to be made. In addition, some of the risks to apply integration in the project is also further studied (Li and Ma, 2017).

139013.label: Major findings and research outcome
139013.value: Major findings and research outcomes are: 1. Social integration is not a critical integration strategy adopted by Hong Kong (HK) design firms in HK market. This is found by using pilot study. Experts with relative experience in HK green market mentioned that social integration may be important in doing project in Mainland China market by mainland design firms. However, this kind of integration may not be applicable due to HK’s market normally following west competitive mechanisms in previous years. Correspondingly, in establishing conceptual framework (see Ling and Li, 2016), social integration is not organized as one component, but is operationalized as partial of the other three components. 2. In terms of achieving advantages, the design firms focus more on differentiation rather than cost leadership. And this is mainly through supply chain integration and design integration. Design firms give a lot of emphasis on supply chain integration with the intention to provide unique design products. In another word, the integration with supplier is neither to cut suppliers’ prices nor to offer low prices for their services. In obtaining design integration, reconfiguration of design chain and investment of superior design technology are adopted, though these will increase the cost greatly. 3. In terms of competitive performance in market, design firms emphasize design quality, client satisfaction and good public image. Targeting at narrow market to offer special products and services help them to keep existing customers for unique features met. Design firms obtain competitiveness by increasing the size of customers attracted by the niche products provided. 4. Although reconfiguration of design chain plays critical role in establishing design integration, supply chain integration, customer integration, through which advantages and competitive performance can be achieved. The implementation of this practice is not easy, especially in tradition project context. Li (2016) identified that people-oriented, task-oriented, contract-oriented barriers should be removed to set up the new design chain. Li and Ma (2017) further suggested that the benefits of integration can only be realized through the efforts of legal system, owner, government, project participants and professional bodies.

139013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
139013.value: The 1st major finding in 6.1 deserves further studies on the dynamic role of “social integration” in diverse project context. Previous researches done by PI have realized that “social integration” among participants can lead to good design performance, thereby enhancing design firm’s business performance in construction market. But other researches also implied that project performance may be impacted by project variables varying in diverse project context. Based on these, it is necessary to study the business effects of “social integration” by using contingency theory. The 4th major finding in 6.1 deserves further studies on the how to remove the barriers in delivering integration. Though the benefits of integration have been identified in this research, which are supported by previous research results, new risks may emerge in realizing the benefits in implementation. These new risks may result from these necessary integrations which are too new to current practitioners. Based on these, it is necessary to study the risk mechanism in integrated project delivery.

139013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
139013.value: Hong Kong (HK) design firms hope to be competitive in green design market. Since green design can only be achieved through integration among all participants, which is different from the practices taken previously. Therefore, it is necessary for design firms to adopt integrative practices to cultivate this integration. However, as a business unit, design firms should be very clear about which kinds of integrative practices can bring profits to them, thereby making up the cost resulting from delivering these new practices. HK design firms can use integration if they are focusing on providing unique and innovative design to fulfill certain design market’s requirements. At the same time, existing customers and new customers will follow design firms that their reputations and images in publics will be very high. In doing so, design firms should focusing more on superior design, technology and quality, which are critical to offer extra value to customers. Since integration process is different from the traditional one, design firms should reconfigure their design chain, thereby reorganizing the relation with their suppliers and redefining the services they provided.

139113.label: Project Objectives
139113.value: To connect structural behavior of material interface at different length scales by studying the interfacial fracture mechanism, using advanced composites and cementitious materials as a representative system. To understand how the interface between advanced composites and cementitious materials interacts with the surrounding moisture from an atomistic perspective, which leads to the change in mechanical properties in a much larger length scale in continuum regime. To study the effect on high temperature on the bulk materials of advanced composites and cementitious materials, and their interface using an atomistic approach together with a nanoscale experimental technique. To develop a multiscale analysis technique that combines molecular dynamics simulation and finite element method such that the applicability of molecular dynamics simulation can be seamlessly extended to mesoscale structure.
