139113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
139113.value: Material interface is present in various applications ranging from nanoscale components, such as thin films in circuit boards, to macroscale structures, such as adhesive bonding in civil infrastructures. In many engineering applications, the integrity of the interface under various environmental conditions is critical to the performance of the entire material system. Thus, considerable efforts have been devoted to developing mechanics approaches for understanding interfacial fracture and debonding mechanisms. Analytical and empirical approaches based on classical methods are generally limited in predicting crack propagation at the interface when chemical effects are involved. Molecular dynamics simulation appears to be a potential and robust approach enabling us to study the material interaction at nanoscale which can capture the possible physical and chemical interactions along the interface, and hence such approach is particularly useful for investigating the complex interfacial fracture under the moisture and temperature effect, i.e. the durability of the bonded system. Water molecules may attack the weak bonds at the interface, or alter the molecular structure of substrates, resulting in weakened adhesive and cohesive strengths. In some cases, such as structural strengthening application, debonding failure can lead to disastrous results. This proposed research is motivated from the broad engineering applications of organic-inorganic material systems which require an accurate prediction of the mechanical properties in various length scales. The objective of this research is first to under the material behavior in the vicinity of the interface at different length scales, using advanced composites and cement hydrates as a representative system, and then linking these length scales through a multiscale framework eventually allowing us to connect the atomistic level development to the macroscale engineering analysis, with the consideration of moisture and temperature effects. It is envisioned that the proposed work will introduce a new paradigm in engineering analysis of complex systems in a similar manner that the finite element method has once provided the opportunity for powerful analysis of structures. Development of this methodology will bring a broader impact to the civil engineering community, ensuring public safety against unanticipated failure due to debonding. Also, such methodology can be extended to general organic-inorganic systems including the bond between a temporary replacement crown and enamel. Knowledge and approach developed in this project will be integrated into education via course curricula and made available for public through PI’s website. Every effort will be made to involve undergraduate and female students in the conduct of the proposed research. 在現代科技中，材料介面的研究已被廣泛運用。從奈米級元件到巨型結構，從電路板中的薄膜到建築物構造間相互的黏合，皆可見其蹤影。研究指出，在許多機械工程的應用中，材料介面在各種環境條件下所呈現出的狀態與完整性，往往是判讀此素材整體效能的主要依歸。於是，大量資源不斷投入相關的研究，致力於以力學的角度來理解介面間各種斷裂和剝離。傳統的分析和實證法在涉及化學效應的實驗中，都被局限於僅能預測介面上裂紋的擴展。面對此種困境，分子動力學模擬逐漸成為另一個更具潛力且穩健的做法。分子動力學模擬能在研究介面互動的實驗中，以奈米規模的精準度，捕捉到介面間可能的物理和化學性質的相互影響。因此，在研究複雜的濕度和溫度的影響下的各種介面斷裂，是相當有用的。（例如：鍵合系統的耐久性。因為水分子可能會阻斷介面上較弱的鍵結，或是改變基底物質的分子結構，造成了黏著和凝聚力量的弱化，而其導致的介面間黏結的剝離破壞，在某些結構加強的應用實例中，所造成的後果往往是不堪設想的。） 此項研究的動機，是為了提供一個能在不同尺度條件下，準確預測工程中有機、無機材料的介面，在力學性能上的表現的方法。我們以高科技複合材料間接合劑的液化作為樣本系統，探討其介面在不同尺度條件下的表現情形，並將水分和溫度的影響列入考量，在多尺度框架下將來自不同環境條件的實驗數據交互運算，以得出結果，進而達到將原子量級的發展應用在工程上宏觀分析的目的。就如同有限元素法曾在結構分析中佔有一席之地，此研究項目將有望成為工程複合系統分析中一個新的範例，並可藉由其研究成果，避免介面間意外的剝離與碰壞，除了可以確保公眾安全，還可為土木工程界帶來更廣闊的影響。

139113.label: Realisation of objectives
139113.value: Objective 1 has been achieved completely. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations have been conducted for advanced composites materials and cementitious materials. Coarse-grained (CG) model of cementitious materials (i.e. C-S-H) has been used to interpret the nano-scale behavior at the meso-scale level. Some more CG models for advanced composite materials has also been constructed. Objective 2 has been achieved completely. A better understanding on the failure mechanism of the interface between advanced composites and cementitious materials has been obtained through the MD simulations and appropriate CG models. In general, the interface becomes in the presence of the surrounding moisture. An in-depth investigation on the chemistry between advanced composites and cementitious materials has been made. Objective 3 has been achieved completely. The study of temperature effect has been conducted through both simulation and experiment. It is found that an increase of temperature results in a weakened interface between advanced composites and cementitious materials in general. The experimental part has also been completed so that the comprehensive picture of the temperature effect can be obtained. Objective 4 has been achieved completely. In order to eliminate limitations of MD simulations, a multi-scale simulation scheme combing cohesive finite element method (CFEM) and MD simulation has been conducted. In this simulation scheme, variation of material microstructure and micro-properties is described by MD at atomistic scale. Based on the atomistic information from MD, the structural behavior of interface can be modeled by CFEM. The material information described at different scales is transferred seamlessly. The effectiveness of proposed multi-scale simulation scheme has been verified by a case study of concrete-epoxy interfacial crack.

139113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
139113.value: The knowledge developed in this project is a fundamental step for understanding complex fracture behavior in the organic-inorganic material system at molecular level and contribute to the understanding at the macro-level design. Application and development for other type of substrates at larger scale is possible and this will help ensure public safety against unanticipated failure. In addition, this research has a strong intellectual component with potential to significantly advance scientific knowledge in the multi-disciplinary areas of fracture mechanics experimentation, molecular dynamics simulation for fracture, and environmental effect in bi-material systems, involving polymeric and silica materials. This research forms the basis for the development of a new engineering and design paradigm for the solution of complex engineering problem.

139313.value: 石墨烯是一種二維六邊形碳晶格結構，由於其具有突出的性能如高載流子遷移率以及獨特的能帶結構,作為可用於高性能納米設備的新型材料得到了越來越多的關注。石墨烯的電子性能主要是由其原子組態決定，因此，在石墨烯的加工過程中，對石墨烯被切的幾何形狀、切割方向以及切割位置進行精確控制就具有極其重要的意義。但是，傳統的納米加工工藝，如電子束曝光技術，無法在原子尺度上對石墨烯結構進行精準控制。 本研究的主要目標是開發一種集成解決方案，利用一個試驗平台同時完成對石墨烯的成像以及圖形化，使得被加工的石墨烯結構具有所需的性質。該研究中將要開發的機器人平台借助了基於原子力顯微鏡技術的高解析度表徵與機械操作能力，以及局部陽極氧化（LAO）工藝的蝕刻能力，將會提供對石墨烯進行原子解析度成像、高精度操作、圖形化以及蝕刻、以及電子性能表徵等功能。為了達到這一目標，我們將會解決以下幾個問題：1）實現原子解析度的成像以供細節表徵並判斷石墨烯晶格結構；2）開發原子力顯微鏡系統以及力/位移控制策略以利用原子力顯微鏡探針實現對石墨烯結構的精確操作與切割，同時將局部陽極氧化工藝與機械切割法結合，實現對石墨烯結構的圖形化與蝕刻。通過控制沿著特定晶格方向進行切割，我們將獲得具有納米級別寬度並具有特定幾何形狀的石墨烯納米帶；3）理解切割過程對形成的石墨烯納米帶的影響並建立相應的模型對幾種輸入參數進行描述，通過該模型可以判斷輸入電壓、切割力、以及最終石墨烯結構的幾何方向對該結構的影響與作用；4）研究加工與圖形化後石墨烯結構的電子特性，並將試驗結果與電子能帶結構模型理論相關聯。 與其它傳統複雜並且難以重複的製造過程不同，本研究提出的新系統將會高效的製造出具有所需電子特性的石墨烯結構並將其裝配成功能化的納米設備。最終，本研究提出的裝配平台將會進一步被開發成自動化石墨烯製造設備。該研究的成果不僅會帶來多學科間交叉創新，更將解決石墨烯可能作為感測器、電晶體、太陽能電池以及顯示器等產品走向實用與商業化過程中所面臨的加工難度這一障礙。

139313.label: Realisation of objectives
139313.value: Atomic force microscope (AFM) is a powerful tool for imaging and patterning various nanomaterials at the nanoscale resolution. Atomic resolution imaging by AFM has been achieved by various operation modes like contact mode, tapping mode and lateral force mode. In our experiments, we found friction force image is a simple and quick technique for identifying the crystalline orientation of graphene and contact mode was used. The contact mode image was taken with the scan angle perpendicular to the AFM cantilever, so that friction forces between the tip and surface result in lateral forces that twist the cantilever, measured as a lateral deflection, based on which the atomic resolution friction image of graphene was obtained. To improve the image quality for atomic resolution imaging, fast Fourier transform filter was conducted to filter out the high-frequency noise. The filtered friction image clearly reveals the lattice pattern of graphene. Lattice resolution images of graphene could be obtained reproducibly at high scan rates, making their acquisition comparatively rapid. This makes it feasible to use this technique for rapid identification of the orientations of graphene. Besides atomic resolution imaging and crystalline orientation identification, in-situ nano-patterning of assembled graphene could also be conducted by employing AFM. Nanostructures like holes and trenches can be potentially fabricated with well-defined dimension by AFM. The AFM-based nanopatterning system was developed, which mainly has three parts: the optical microscope for observing sampling, AFM scanner head to conduct nanolithography and sample stage. The patterning process can be roughly divided into two methods. The first method is developed using the force-controlled nanomechanical cutting by applying normal force to break the carbon-carbon bond of graphene. The applied force can be calculated by multiplying the spring constant and vertical deflection of AFM probe. This method does not involve chemical reaction or irradiation, and the intrinsic property of graphene will not be affected. Voltage-controlled local anodic oxidization (LAO) cutting is another method for the AFM-based nanopatterning. By applying negative voltage between the conductive tip and graphene surface, local oxidation is produced by the strong electric field and the selected region of graphene can be etched away. The oxidation process occurs near the AFM tip. By tuning the normal force and LAO voltage, nanoscale trenches can be achieved on the graphene surface. By combining atomic resolution image and nanolithography, AFM provides potential capability to fabricate graphene nanoribbon with desirable width and crystal orientation or edge structure. Nanopatterning by AFM has several advantages. First, the width, crystal orientation and edge structure of graphene can be precisely controlled based on the AFM imaging and manipulation at atomic resolution. Second, dynamic observation of cutting process is achieved through AFM, which allows the modification of cutting parameter so as to obtain the desired structure. In addition, repeatable and consistent nanopatterning of graphene with desired electronic property can be realized. Moreover, the changes of electrical properties of graphene can be monitored after the AFM patterning process. For the force-controlled nano-mechanical cutting, we experimentally investigated the influence of cutting force, cutting direction, cutting speed and substrate materials on the resulted feature of cutting trenches. In the experiment, the AFM tip was controlled to contact and scratch the surface of the graphene sample. As mentioned before, the applied force on the graphene was obtained based on the spring constant of the AFM cantilever and the corresponding deflection signal. By gradually increasing the applied normal force from 40 µN to 120 µN, octagon patterns were patterned on graphene and it was found that only when the normal force was larger than 60 µN, the graphene could be cut. Therefore, the critical load was 60 µN. The corresponding width of trench was ~ 200 nm. The measured critical load was much larger than the previously reported values for suspended graphene ( 1.6- 2.8 µN). We ascribed the difference to the underlying substrate, which supported the graphene samples. In addition to the mechanical cutting, AFM based LAO cutting could be performed by applying bias voltage. The tip voltage can be controlled by the built-in controller of the AFM system and the graphene was electrically grounded by manually connecting it with the sample stage (ground). Since the distance between the AFM tip and graphene was very small, a strong electric field could be induced. The distribution of the induced electric field was simulated. One striking feature was the obvious broadening of the electric field and the full-width and half maxima could be as high as a few hundred of nanometers, implying a wide cutting trench. We then experimentally study the influence of LAO voltage, cutting speed and cutting force on the trench features. First, the cutting trenches were generated by under different LAO voltages, but the constant cutting speed of 0.5 µm/s and cutting force of 0.13 µN. The results showed that the trench was cut on the graphene when the LAO voltage was larger than -5 V. Therefore, the threshold LAO voltage should be ~ 5V. The corresponding applied force was smaller than cutting force in the mechanical cutting. Clearly, by applying LAO voltage, the required cutting force can be decreased. The width of the trenches under different LAO voltages was measured. The trench width increased proportionally to the LAO voltage and the value (from 90 nm to 400 nm) was larger than that obtained from the mechanical cutting. This was attributed to the broaden distribution of electric filed induced between the tip and graphene. Besides LAO voltage, it was found that cutting speed had large influence on the trench width. By increasing the cutting speed from 0.05 µm/s to 5 µm/s, the trench width under the same LAO voltage significantly deceased. Increasing the cutting speed would decrease the LAO time for graphene along the cutting trench. Therefore, the degree of oxidization was decrease, resulting in smaller trench width. Also, the threshold voltage gradually increased with higher cutting speed from 4 V to 7V. Compared with force-controlled nano-machanical cutting, the required cutting force was much smaller. However, the LAO voltage and cutting speed influenced each other, making it difficult to obtain the optimal cutting parameters. Moreover, since the LAO cutting process relied on the chemically oxidization, the stability was worse than the nano-mechanical cutting. The oxidization process introduced oxygen group to the edge of the cutting trench and this process may degrade the properties of pristine graphene. Therefore, the electrical property of graphene before and after the LAO cutting was investigated. The gate-dependent transfer curve of graphene was measured before and after the LAO cutting to study the doping effect of LAO cutting on graphene. Multiple trenches were created by LAO cutting and the edges of the trench were supposed to contain oxygen groups. The gate-dependent transfer curves were measured during the cutting process. As the number of trenches increased, the transfer curve gradually shifted to larger positive voltage, indicating higher p-doping level. The Dirac voltage shifted from 8 V to 20 V. The corresponding Fermi level shift was from 0.15 eV to 0.24 eV. We attributed this to the introducing of electron-withdrawing group (oxygen group) on the edge of cutting trenches. Previous studies showed that the addition of oxygen groups caused significant p-doping effect, which is consistent with our experimental results.

139313.label: Major findings and research outcome
139313.value: An atomic force microscope (AFM)-based robotic platform has been developed with atomic resolution imaging ability and nano-patterning function for graphene-based devices (ref J2-J4). Atomic resolution image of graphene was realized, based on which the crystalline orientation of graphene could be determined. Nano-patterning of graphene could be conducted in force-contrlled nano-mechanical cutting mode and local anodic oxidation (LAO) controlled cutting mode. It’s was found that, for nano-mechanical cutting, the substrate materials has large influence on the minimum required cutting force for graphene (ref J4). Soft substrate materials lead to smaller required cutting force than hard substrates (ref J4). For graphene on SiO2, the minimum required cutting force is ~ 60 µN. The dimension of the cutting trench depended on the cutting direction because of the non-uniform geometry of AFM tip, while the cutting speed showed no influence on the cutting resolution, making fast pattering application possible. By controlling the cutting parameters, graphene trench with width down to 50 nm was achieved. Besides nano-machenical cutting, LAO cutting was realized by biasing the tip and graphene with controlled LAO voltage. The required cutting force was much smaller in LAO cutting and it was usually below 1 µN. As the LAO voltage increased, the cutting trench increased too, and the trench width was in the range of 100 nm to 800 nm. The minimum required LAO voltage changed with the cutting speed. Increasing the cutting speed would decrease the LAO time for graphene along the cutting trench. Therefore, the degree of oxidization was decrease, resulting in smaller trench width. Overall speaking, both nano-mechanical cutting and LAO cutting could successfully pattern graphene with controlled geometry and dimension. The nano-mechanical cutting involved no chemical reaction. Therefore, the property of pristine graphene could be preserved. For LAO cutting, oxygen groups were introduced to graphene, causing doping effects on graphene and adding possible bonding sites for functional groups for various sensing application. Depending on the application, both nano-machnical cutting and LAO cutting could facilitate the development of graphene-based devices.

139313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
139313.value: By patterning graphene into nanoribbons, nanopores, quantum dots and nanomeshes, the energy gap of graphene could be possibly controlled. This could benefit the development of filed effect transistors, photodetector, bio-sensors and gas sensors. More importantly, the developed AFM-based robotic platform is capable of selectively introducing oxygen groups on graphene. By controlling the degree of oxidization, the energy gaps could be possibly tuned. Moreover, those oxygen groups could act as strong binding sites for bio-agents or gas molecules, leading to high-sensitivity detectors.

139313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
139313.value: An atomic force microscope (AFM)-based robotic platform has been developed. The imaging capability of the platform enables us to see individual atoms in graphene and determine the crystalline orientation of graphene. After that, by using the AFM probe as nanoscale surgical knife, large graphene could be cut into various small patterns like nanoribbons, nanopores quantum dots and nanomeshes. Since the electrical properties of graphene are highly dependent on its dimension and geometry, the performance of graphene based electronics could be potentially optimized, leading to high-performance detectors for various applications.

139413.label: Project Title(Chinese)
139413.value: 高性能门控III-V族平行纳米线阵列MOSFETs

139413.label: Project Objectives
139413.value: Synthesize III-V nanowires (e.g. InAs, GaAs and InGaAs) with controlled chemical composition, diameters and length, surface morphology, structural and electronic transport properties, and then fabricate wrap-gated nanowire parallel array MOSFETs on Si. This would provide preliminary nanowire device structures for the subsequent studies. Utilize the low-frequency noise characterization of nanowire devices to investigate the effect of different nanowire surface treatments and various high-k dielectrics on the dielectric/nanowire interface properties. This yields the optimized surface treatment and dielectric deposition scheme for the reduced resulting interface traps. Investigate the influence of nanowire dimensions and active device area on the interface trap density of nanowire devices. This not only provides the trap dynamics of devices but also enables a more accurate device design such as the selection of nanowire diameter and device area. Assess the impact of different gate electrodes with different work functions and gate biases to study the subsequent threshold and noise characteristics of nanowire MOSFETs. This finding will be useful to further control the threshold voltage and minimize the intrinsic noise level. Evaluate the ultimate device performances and reliabilities (e.g. the DC stability and high-frequency responses) with the optimized transistor design such as the NW dimension, high-k dielectric and gate electrode, etc. The aim is to develop a versatile and powerful technology platform to quantify the wrap-gated nanowire MOSFET device characteristics, which can provide design guidelines to further optimize and enhance the transistor performances.

139413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
139413.value: 在过去的几十年来，半导体器件缩放已经成为了电子业技术发展的主要驱动力。正如2011年半导体领域国际技术路线图（ITRS）的预测，为了满足缩放的需求，具有纳米结构的非平面型器件（如纳米线）以及III-V族材料很快将与传统的硅技术相结合来提高其性能，包括具有更高的场效应迁移率、更好的栅静电以提供传输更高的驱动电流。例如，最近问世的第一个拥有高迁移率In0.53Ga0.47As平行纳米线阵列隧道的门控III-V 族MOSFETs，这种器件具有更优良的电学性能，并且能够对抑制短沟道效应进行有效的控制。当然，在制备基于III-V族纳米线的商业化电子产品之前，还有很多关键的问题需要解决。而如何使纳米线晶体管具有稳定的设备特性和极低的固有噪音则成为最大的挑战。然而，由于III-V族纳米线具有平面硅结构所不具备的异常高的比表面积和活性晶面，因而纳米线器件的电子性能对纳米线的表面以及存在于纳米线隧道和栅极绝缘层间的晶面缺陷表现出很高的敏感性，这点对于门控纳米线器件来说尤为显著。因此，控制缺陷以及通过发展其他的方法来减少对设备性能和稳定性的影响显得尤其重要却具有挑战性。本方案中，我们将采用低频噪音测试，这是用于检测电子器件的质量及其稳定性的一种非常灵敏的表征手段。通过应用InAs、GaAs以及InGaAs晶体纳米线为典型的二元、三元高迁移率III-V族纳米线材料集聚于硅衬底上，目的是制备门控平行纳米线阵列MOSFETs，通过一系列优化设计以及系统的噪音研究（从优化高-κ电解质，纳米线尺寸的研究，到栅电极的选择）来进一步提高器件的性能和稳定性。最终，我们的研究将扩展到建立一个多样化且强大的技术平台，在未来的电子领域通过互补I-V和噪音表征为纳米线器件的性能优化提供指导。

139413.label: Realisation of objectives
139413.value: In this project, we have successfully accomplished all the objectives with 100% of completion. Particularly, we have established the synthesis technique (i.e. solid-source chemical vapor deposition) to obtain various III-V nanowires (NWs), such as InAs, GaAs and InGaAs, etc, with regulated chemical compositions, geometries, crystallinity, surface morphologies, electrical characteristics and so on (Objective 1). For example, the catalytic effect is systematically investigated in these NW growths, including Pd, Au, Ag and Ni catalyzed GaAs, InGaAs and GaSb NWs. Interestingly, the small diameter catalyst seeds usually lead to the efficient NW growth with the better crystallinity, whereas the large seeds result in the defective NW synthesis with kinked morphologies and twinning defects. Importantly, the obtained III-V (e.g. InGaAs) NWs can be fabricated into high-performance wrap-gated NW field-effect transistors (FETs) using standard sputtered Al2O3 layers as gate dielectrics, as opposed to the typically utilized atomic layer deposited thin film materials (Objective 1). The wet-chemical surface passivation of NW device channels completed before the dielectric deposition is observed to considerably relieve plasma induced defect states on the NW surface. At the same time, we also employed the low-frequency noise (LFN) characterization to evaluate different NW surface treatment and various high-k dielectric materials on their dielectric/NW interface properties and fabricated III-V NW device performances (Objective 2). First of all, the current normalized spectral densities (CNSD) is measured, demonstrating the LFN measurements detailed from the drain of NW devices. Remarkably, the CNSD for each set of biasing conditions, NW treatment and various dielectrics follows closely to the 1/f exp(γ) dependency. Especially in this dependency or also known as McWhorter model, the exponent γ designates the relative dielectric and interface traps uniformity with depth. It is not surprised that the noise follows closely to the number fluctuation theory here, indicating that the LFN is mainly attributed to variations in the carrier concentration triggered by trapping and detrapping at and/or within the dielectric material. In any case, among many trials, the Al2O3 dielectric in combination with the NW surface chemical passivation of aromatic thiolate (ArS-)-based molecular monolayers would deliver the reduced traps for the optimized channel dimensions and electrical device performance of fabricated InAs NWs (Objective 3). Furthermore, the influence of different gate electrodes with different work functions and voltage bias on the device threshold voltage and other performance data is assessed (Objective 4). For instance, when all the conditions are optimized with the Al2O3 dielectric layer thickness of 12 nm deposited homogeneously around the NW and 5 nm Ti/90 nm Al deposited isotropically as the wrap-gate electrode, the device reveals excellent electrical performances with a high ON/OFF current ratio of ~2E6, an impressively low sub-threshold slope of 80 mV/decade and a peak field-effect electron mobility of ~1600 cm2/(Vs) at the source/drain bias of 0.1 V at room temperature, in which these values are comparable or even better than the ones of state-of-the-art NWFETs reported in the literature. In order to fully understand their device reliabilities, the electrical bias stress test is performed and found that all the NW devices display very stable characteristics for extended durations of electrical bias with a threshold voltage shift of less than 0.25 V, which is in a distinct contrast to other film-thin transistors (TFTs) (Objective 5). This enhanced reliability is anticipated to be due to the single crystalline nature of our III-V NWs, optimized NW/dielectric interface properties, such as dangling bonds, defect creation and charge traps. In summary, we have developed and fabricated wrap-gated III-V NW based thin film transistors on Si with the investigation of their detailed LFN behavior. Such measurement can be effectively used to evaluate the NW device characteristics and to determine the density of interface states existed in the devices. In this regard, utilizing these techniques, we can establish a versatile and powerful technology platform to assess the impact of these interface states and to optimize the device design to further achieve the further performance and reliability enhancement for the wrap-gated NW devices.

139413.label: Major findings and research outcome
139413.value: In this project, there are several key findings, which lead to 12 high-impact journal publications (1 Advanced Materials, 1 ACS Nano, 1 Small and 1 Scientific Reports, etc) as well as 6 presentations at different international conferences (4 invited talks). In specific, as reported in Journal of Materials Chemistry C 2017 (Cover Article), the catalytic effect is evaluated systematically in the chemical vapor synthesis of various III–V NWs, involving Au, Pd, Ag and Ni catalyzed GaAs NWs, InGaAs and GaSb NWs. Surprisingly, the small diameter catalyst seeds are found to lead to the efficient NW growth with the better crystallinity, while the large seeds would lead to the slower NW synthesis with kinked morphologies and twinning defects. More importantly, the small catalyst nanoseeds are observed to induce the higher solubility of group III precursors due to Gibbs–Thomson effect, which does not only enable the effective III precursor diffusion for the higher growth rate, but also generate the epitaxial growth of NWs from catalysts contributing to the low activation energy and better crystallinity. Moreover, once the high-quality III-V NWs are obtained, we explore different NW device structures, geometries and surface treatment, etc, for the enhanced performance. For example, as reported in Scientific Reports 2015, we adopt a hybrid approach, combining the well-established sputter deposition to attain high-quality and conformal Al2O3 dielectric layers as well as the pre-deposition surface passivation of NW channels by self-assembly sulfur-containing monolayer in the device fabrication of InGaAs wrap-gated NW FETs. The high-k gate dielectric of Al2O3 layer is sputter-deposited uniformly around the NW channel. The pre-sputtering chemical passivation by (NH4)2S is also utilized to minimize the detrimental effect of the plasma induced surface/interface defect trap states on the NW channels. After passivation, the InGaAs device exhibits excellent electrical properties, which is comparable to or even better than state-of-the-art ALD enabled wrap-gated FETs. As shown in ACS Nano 2015, further improvement could be achieved by using the aromatic thiolate (ArS−) based molecular monolayers as the surface modification of NWs in this wrap-gated device fabrication, since this ArS− surface processing can not only decrease the amount of surface traps for the better mobility but also induce the surface electronic charge to move the device threshold voltage positively. In summary, all these major findings are significant, which would bring forward the deployment of wrap-gate III-V NWs for high-performance next-generation electronic devices.

139413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
139413.value: Although there are many significant findings produced from this work, there are still several major areas required for the further study of these wrap-gated III-V NW devices. For example, all the current investigations are focused only on the high-electron-mobility n-type III-V NWs, such as InAs, GaAs, InGaAs; however, explorations of high-hole-mobility p-type III-V NWs (e.g. GaSb) are inevitably needed to achieve high-performance complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) NW devices and circuits. In this case, it is necessary to examine the effect of different NW surface treatments and various high-k dielectrics on the dielectric/nanowire interface properties of p-type NWs for the reduced resulting interface traps and the enhanced NW device performance. Another one is to further explore large-scale utilization of these wrap-gate NW devices for electronic circuits. Since impressive electrical performances have been demonstrated with individual wrap-gate n-type NWs and their small-scale parallel arrayed film devices, it still requires a scale-up to shoot for large-scale applications, including to fabricate different large-area circuit components (e.g. ring oscillators, random number generators and others). All these further works would push forward the substantial technological development of wrap-gate III-V NWs for practical applications.

139413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
139413.value: Due to their excellent properties, III-V compound semiconductor nanowires (NWs) have been widely considered as ideal alternative device materials for high-performance electronics. For example, the first wrap-gated III-V metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs) with a high-electron-mobility InGaAs nanowire parallel array channel have been recently demonstrated for their superior electrical performances and effective control in suppressing the short channel effect. However, there are still significant challenges to fabricate III-V NW based devices with minimized surface and/or interface traps existed between the NW channel and gate dielectric. Therefore, it is essential to control these defect states and to develop methods to quantify their impact on the device characteristics and stabilities. In this project, we have established the catalytic engineering technique to obtain high-quality III-V NWs and the surface chemical passivation scheme to alleviate the influence of NW surface states on the corresponding NW device performance. Utilizing the conventional device fabrication and characterization techniques, we have successfully fabricated high-performance wrap-gated III-V NW devices, which exhibit the superior performance data. All these would indicate the technological potency of employing these wrap-gate III-V NWs for next-generation electronic devices.

139413.value: In this work, we have successfully synthesized high-quality III-V nanowires, including high-electron-mobility GaAs, InAs and InGaAs, as well as to obtain the wrap-gate nanowire device utilizing the optimized surface chemical passivation and conventional device fabrication technique. When fabricated into transistors, these nanowires with minimized surface state and traps exhibit the superior electrical performances. Because of these interesting properties and impressive device characteristics, we have then established many fruitful collaboration with other research groups worldwide, including Wuhan University, National Laboratory for Infrared Physics, Shanghai Institute of Technical Physics, Institute of Process Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences, and etc to further develop the potential applications of these nanowires for other practical utilizations. All these trainings have not only provided them early research exposure at the cutting edge of materials science, but also help accelerating the project forward at a faster step.

139613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
139613.value: Building-integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) systems with photovoltaic (PV) modules installed in the cavity of a double-skin façade (DSF) are becoming popular. However, buildings with a DSF have difficulties complying with fire safety codes in some countries. When a building catches fire, burning PV panels can contribute to an already very hazardous environment. In some cases, cutting off the electricity generated by PV panels has proved problematic, and vast quantities of toxic gas have emitted from burning PV panels and associated combustible components. Although PV cells at roof level are stable under normal building fire temperatures, their behaviour during fires when they are installed in the cavity of a DSF is unknown, as the air temperature in a DSF cavity can be very high when it is located next to a flashover room fire. Furthermore, large amounts of PV modules are typically installed in BIPV systems. The major aim of this project will be to conduct a thorough investigation of the fire hazards of BIPV systems with DSFs. The thermal environment in a façade cavity when the interior glass pane is broken due to a flashover fire in a room adjacent to the façade will be examined using scale model experiments and full-scale burning tests on part of a BIPV system with a DSF. The results will be applied to investigate the possibility that the selected PV modules and the combustible accessories installed in the façade cavity will ignite. Samples of the crystalline and thin-film silicon PV modules commonly used in BIPV systems will be selected to examine their behaviour in big post-flashover room fires. The heat and smoke emitted from PV modules exposed to experiment-based radiative heat fluxes will be evaluated by a cone calorimeter. The smoke-potency fractional exposure dose will also be measured. The spread of the smoke and heat emitted from the burning PV modules installed in the façade cavity will then be examined. A real-scale model of part of a BIPV system with a DSF will be constructed to justify the results of the thermal environment in scale modelling experiments. Mathematical models of heat and mass transfers, including computational fluid dynamics, will be combined with the experimental results to achieve the integrated understanding necessary to provide fire-safe BIPV systems with DSFs. Appropriate fire protection, firefighting and rescue strategies for BIPV systems with DSFs can then be recommended. 光伏建筑一体化系统（BIPV）得到越来越广泛的应用。 此系统配备墙体安装光伏模块（PV）的双层幕墙（DSF）。然而在一些国家，安装此类双层幕墙的建筑很难符合消防安全法规的规定。当建筑物发生火灾，燃烧的光伏电池板会恶化已经非常危险的火灾环境。在某些情况下，很难切断光伏电池板所产生的电力，同时燃烧的光伏电池板会排放大量的有毒气体及可燃成分。通常情况下，安装在在屋顶上的光伏电池板在一般建筑火灾温度下是稳定的。如果相邻房间发生轰燃，电池板的温度双层幕墙墙体中间的温度会非常高。此时很难预测安装在双层幕墙墙体中间的光伏电池板会发生何种现象。与此同时，越来越多光伏组件被安装于光伏建筑一体化系统中。 本项目将主要研究应用此类双层幕墙的光伏建筑一体化系统的火灾隐患。本项目将进行小尺寸及全尺寸模型试验。试验场景主要为安装双层幕墙的相邻房间发生轰燃且双层幕墙的内层玻璃破裂的情景。试验结果可应用于评估所选用的光伏模块及其附件的可燃性。试验选用光伏建筑一体化系统中常见的结晶和薄膜硅光伏模块，测试其在大型后轰燃房间火的稳定性。试验采用锥形热计量仪测量光伏模块在试验用辐射热通量下产生的热及烟气及其扩散模式。并通过试验确定产生烟气所需要的临界辐射热通量值。随后本研究将在配备双层幕墙的光伏建筑一体化系统的全尺寸模型上进行试验研究。全尺寸模型试验结果将和小尺寸模型试验结果进行对比验证。结合热量和质量传导的数学模型、流体力学模型和试验结果，可以全面了解双层幕墙光伏建筑一体化系统所需要的消防安全指标。研究结果可为双层幕墙光伏建筑一体化系统的防火，灭火和救援等方面提供参考。

139613.label: Realisation of objectives
139613.value: Fire hazard of photovoltaic (PV) modules installed in the façade cavity of double-skin façade (DSF) of building-integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) system was studied in this project with all objectives achieved: 1. To examine the fire environment encountered by PV modules installed in a façade cavity Real-scale burning tests on a DSF structure were carried out at a remote site in China. The DSF rig was burnt under a fire scenario identified earlier. A post-flashover room fire of 1.6 MW heat release rate using gasoline was burnt adjacent to the façade cavity. Flame spread pattern out of the openings in the flashover room fire to the glass façade was studied. Air temperatures next to the façade skins were measured to study the characteristics of the window plume. Further, a 1/10 scale model of the above DSF rig was constructed. A small fire room with a 1.6 kW propanol pool fire of diameter 7 cm was put adjacent to the model. Transient air temperatures near the interior and exterior façade skins were measured. Vertical air channel flow in a narrow façade cavity was observed. The hazard scenario identified for DSF fire due to window plume was then applied to study the effect on PV modules. A mathematical model was then developed based on the physical modeling results and numerical simulation with Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) to study whether window plume from a room fire to the DSF cavity would attach to the façade skins. The net lateral pressure on the plume was calculated with results justified by experimental studies with part of a DSF rig constructed earlier and numerical simulations. 2. To examine the smoke emitted from burning PV modules commonly used in BIPV systems Fire behaviour of two commonly used polycrystalline silicon PV modules labelled as A and B were studied. The chemical compositions of the two PV samples were analysed by the Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy with justification by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy results. Sample A was a silicate product with polyurethane adhesive, and sample B has epoxy resin and is likely to have flame retardant as claimed. Thermal analysis by heating the samples was carried out using thermogravimetric analysis and thermogravimetric analysis coupled with infrared spectroscopy. The fire behavior was then studied by a cone calorimeter under radiative heat fluxes from 10 kWm-2 to 70 kWm-2. Time to ignition, peak heat release rate, total heat released and peak carbon monoxide concentration were determined from the cone calorimeter tests. Three key parameters on flashover propensity, total heat release rate, and lethal concentration of the fire effluent emitted to produce death in 50% of test animals deduced from the peak carbon monoxide concentration were then calculated for ranking the thermal and smoke hazards. The values of flashover propensity and total heat release rate were found to be large only when the PV samples were exposed to higher radiative heat fluxes over 35 kWm-2. The thermal hazards of the two PV samples are low, at least during the early stage of a fire. However, smoke risk of burning PV materials is very high. When a building catches fire, burning PV panels can contribute to an already very hazardous environment. More importantly, vast quantities of toxic gases are emitted from burning PV panels. 3. To examine how heat and smoke emitted from burning PV modules spread in a façade cavity As illustrated in studying window plume in the above objective 1, the hot flame and smoke coming out of a flashover room fire to the facade cavity can act at the PV panels and ignite them easily. Note that large amounts of PV modules would be installed in BIPV systems. Therefore, flame and smoke trapped in the DSF cavity while burning PV panels can give a very hazardous environment. Physical full-size and scale modeling experiments on the fire hazards on part of the BIPV system with DSF were carried out. Fire behavior of selected samples of the polycrystalline silicon PV modules in cone experiments was examined in big postflashover room fires. Real-scale burning tests on a DSF structure were studied under the window plume scenario identified. A post-flashover room fire of 1.6 MW heat release rate using gasoline was burnt adjacent to the façade cavity. Flame spread pattern out of the openings in the flashover room fire to the glass façade was studied. Air temperatures next to the façade skins were measured. Experimental studies on 4 cases with and without PV panels were arranged. In each case, 4 PV panels were installed on the shaft model wall opposite to the chamber model with a vertical facade facing the cavity. The window plume observed was then compared with those deduced earlier from numerical simulations. PV membrane burnt out within the area of temperature higher than 500oC. Glass layer fell out within the area of temperature higher than 900oC. Gas temperatures of cases with PV panels inside the DSF cavity was much higher than the cases without PV panels. Burning PV panels inside the DSF cavity tended to aggravate the fire hazard scenario. Scale modeling experiments on that part of BIPV-DSF rig were conducted. Different façade cavity depths were adjusted. One, two and four propanol pool fires of diameter 7 cm were arranged in the model room to give heat release rates of 1.6 kW, 3.2 kW and 6.4 kW, corresponding to about 0.0625 MW, 0.125 MW and 0.5 MW fires in the real-scale model. Air temperatures in the scale model due to these scale model pool fires were assumed to be the same as in full-scale experiments. 4. Summary PV modules are installed in some modern buildings for generating renewable energy. When a building catches fire, burning PV panels can contribute to an already very hazardous environment. Research results from the above confirmed that trapping flame and smoke generated from burning PV materials in DSF cavity due to the window plume would give a very hazardous fire environment. The identified hazardous scenario should be considered in determining fire safety provisions for BIPV systems with DSF. Note that very few full-scale burning tests were reported in the literature on BIPV-DSF fires due to resource limitations. Such an experimental study on real-scale BIPV fires is very useful to the fire community in designing green architectural features. In summary, all objectives proposed in the submitted proposal were achieved in this completed project.

139613.label: Major findings and research outcome
139613.value: Two journal and five conference papers were already published from this project at this moment. A PhD student was registered with thesis to be submitted in 2018. Major findings are: • Window plume from a room fire to the cavity of a double-skin façade A simple model was developed to calculate the net lateral pressure on the plume. Based on this theoretical steady-state model, window plume from a room fire ejected to the DSF cavity was studied by both physical modeling experiments and numerical simulations using CFD. Both experimental and simulation results show that for a given cavity width, heat release rate and geometry of the window opening are the two key factors in determining the plume trajectory. Comparisons between the plume trajectories based on temperature field and based on velocity field were carried out. • Fire behaviour of combustible components of photovoltaic panels Two common polycrystalline silicon PV samples were selected with their chemical composition analysed by the Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy with justification by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy results. The fire behavior was then studied by a cone calorimeter under different radiative heat fluxes. The thermal hazards of both PV samples are low, at least during the early stage of a fire without flame acting directly on the sample. However, smoke hazard from burning PV panels is high even though only carbon monoxide was considered in toxicity study. The hazard due to smoke generated from burning such PV materials is strongly recommended to be taken into consideration in designing fire safety provisions for PV-integrated buildings. • Building-integrated photovoltaic system fire with double-skin façade In contrast to PV models at roof level which are stable under normal building fire temperatures, their behaviour during fires when installed in the façade cavity of BIPV-DSF system should be watched carefully. This was confirmed by physical full-size and scale modeling experiments on part of the BIPV system with DSF in this completed project. A model rig with an 8 m tall vertical shaft model and a 2 m tall combustion chamber was built in a remote site of China. Samples of the polycrystalline silicon PV modules commonly used in BIPV systems were selected to examine their behaviour in big postflashover room fires. Experiments on BIPV were carried out with a 3.5 MW gasoline pool fire placed inside the chamber.

139613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
139613.value: Building-integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) systems with photovoltaic (PV) modules installed in the cavity of a double-skin façade (DSF) are becoming popular. Burning PV panels in a building fire would lead to very hazardous smoke environment as indicated by cone calorimeter test. Fire hazard must be assessed thoroughly for determining fire safety provisions for BIPV with DSF. As demonstrated in this project, heat and smoke emitted by burning PV in the DSF cavity would spread upward with air entrained at lower levels and then trapped in the façade cavity. Very few full-scale burning tests were reported on BIPV in the literature. Such a qualitative study on real PV fires in cavity of DSF would clearly indicate the hazard behind. More PV panel samples should be further studied. The scientific aspects of BIPV system fires should be explored to design workable fire safety provisions and appropriate firefighting and rescue strategies. New physical fire scenarios can be observed and included in hazard assessment. Appropriate fire protection strategy, including smoke extraction, detection system and suppression by appropriate water or gas systems should be determined by further studies to have safe green architectural BIPV-DSF system.

139613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
139613.value: Building-integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) systems with photovoltaic (PV) modules installed in the cavity of a double-skin façade (DSF) are becoming popular. Behaviour of PV modules installed in the façade cavity of DSF in a fire was explored in this project by analytical study, physical scale modeling tests, full-scale experiments and numerical simulations. PV modules commonly used in BIPV systems were selected to examine their behaviour in big post-flashover room fires. The hot window plume coming out of a flashover room fire acting on a DSF cavity can ignite the PV panels. The heat and smoke emitted from PV modules exposed to radiative heat fluxes were evaluated by a cone calorimeter. Very few full-scale burning tests were reported on BIPV in the literature due to resource limitations. Computational fluid dynamics was applied to justify the experimental results to achieve the integrated understanding necessary to provide fire-safe BIPV systems with DSFs. The air movement induced by a fire in the façade cavity of a BIPV system would facilitate smoke spread. Appropriate fire protection, firefighting and rescue strategies for BIPV systems with DSFs can then be recommended based on the research results. Firefighters must be provided with special personal protection equipment.

139713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
139713.value: Carotid atherosclerosis is a major cause of thrombosis and subsequent emboli, which may block one of the cerebral arteries, causing ischemic stroke. Most strokes associated with carotid atherosclerosis can be prevented by lifestyle/dietary changes and medical/surgical treatments. Effects of different treatment strategies are required to be validated in clinical trials. Traditional clinical trials use incidence of vascular events, stenosis and intima-media thickness to evaluate the severity of carotid disease. These trials must be very large in order to demonstrate the treatment effects statistically. Therefore, there is a critical need for sensitive biomarkers for serial monitoring of atherosclerosis. A sensitive, non-invasive 3D imaging technique allowing plaque visualization and quantification will play a vital role in the development of such biomarkers, which may ultimately be used clinically to tailor individual treatment decisions through improved monitoring of treatment response. With the ability to generate 3D carotid images, 3D ultrasound has allowed the development of biomarkers such as total plaque volume and vessel wall volume. However, plaque dimension alone cannot identify the local change in plaque. To address this issue, we developed a method to construct a 3D map to display local vessel-wall-plus-plaque thickness change (VWT-Change) on a point-by-point basis for each artery. Unfortunately, the map depends on the 3D geometry of the carotid wall, which is highly subject-dependent, precluding quantitative comparisons of VWT-Change distribution between subject groups. This proposal describes a technique for mapping VWT-Change computed for different subjects on a standardized 2D carotid atlas, with which the VWT-Change distribution of subjects belonging to different treatment groups can be directly compared. We propose to develop algorithms that utilize the information available on the atlas to: (1) construct two novel biomarkers based on feature selection analysis. A feature is a single VWT-Change measurement at a point on the atlas. The first biomarker is the average VWT-Change over all selected feature points, and the second is based on a discriminant analysis technique between treatment groups. Since regions with selected feature points exhibit greater plaque response difference between treatment groups, we hypothesize that these biomarkers are more sensitive than existing biomarkers; and (2) identify subjects who do not respond to a treatment sufficiently and subjects who experience rapid plaque progression. We hypothesize that these subjects can be identified even in a small pilot clinical study because of the increased sensitivity provided by the carotid atlas. We will validate these hypotheses using images from several clinical studies. 頸動脈硬化是引起血栓和血栓栓子的主要因素，而血栓及血栓栓子會導致腦動脈堵塞繼而引起缺血性中風。大部分與頸動脈硬化有關的中風都可以通過生活或飲食習慣的改變以及用藥物或手術來預防。但是，我們首先需要考慮如何對臨床試驗中不同治療方案的療效進行評估。傳統的臨床試驗通常採用血管意外的發生率，血管的狹窄和內膜中層厚度來估算頸動脈疾病的嚴重性。爲了顯示不同治療方案的效果有著統計顯著性的差異，這樣的評估方法需要大量的臨床試驗。靈敏、非侵入式三維成像技術可將斑塊顯示出來並量化。這些技術將會在生物標記發展中發揮著至關重要的作用。新的生物標記最終改善對治療反應的監控，在臨床上為每一個患者提出一套具有針對性的治療方案。 3D超聲技術具備生成3D頸動脈圖像的能力，允許了我們研發出諸如全斑塊體積和血管壁體積這樣的生物標記。然而，單靠斑塊大小的量度，儘管可以直接測量斑塊變化，並不能定位出斑塊的局部變化。為了量化斑塊變化的三維分佈，我們在血管壁的每一點上定義了一種新的度量去量化“管壁斑塊厚度變化”。但是，從不同患者中得到的二維動脈圖具有不同的形狀。因此，我們只能進行一些定性的和主觀的空間比較，而不能進行定量和客觀的評估。 本研究提出一種新技術將不同患者的管壁與斑塊厚度的變化分佈映射到一個已標準化的2D頸動脈圖集。通過該標準化的2D頸動脈圖集，我們可以對屬於不同治療組的患者的管壁與斑塊厚度的變化分佈進行直接比較。為了充分利用這些圖集裡蘊含的信息，我們還提出一些新的算法：（1）基於特徵點選擇分析的技術，提出了兩種新的生物標記。一個特徵點就是在圖集上一個點的管壁與斑塊厚度的變化的測量值。我們提出的第一種生物標記是所有篩選出來的特徵的管壁與斑塊厚度變化的平均值；第二種生物標記是基於不同治療組之間的判別分析之上。由於包含這些所選特徵點的區域對不同治療組間表現出更大的斑塊響應差異，我們可以合理假設這些生物標記比現有的生物標記更加敏感。 （2）去有效地鑑別出對某種治療方案無反應的患者以及那些正經受斑塊快速惡化的患者。得益於這種新的頸動脈圖集不斷提高的敏感性，我們假設這些患者儘管在小規模的試點臨床研究中也能得到有效判別。最後，我們將通過從多個臨床研究中得到的圖像來檢驗這些假設。

139713.label: Realisation of objectives
139713.value: Note: this section cites publications listed in Part C. The citations are peer-review journal articles listed in Section 8 unless otherwise stated. Objective 1 has been successfully accomplished. We have developed and published a number of algorithms for generating the carotid atlas. Ref. 7 introduces an algorithm based on the steepest descent of description length to optimize correspondence of 3D points on the carotid surfaces of different subjects. The algorithm was validated by a phantom study and an in vivo ultrasound study. Ref. 9 introduces an algorithm that generates conformal (angle-preserving) 2D standardized carotid maps. Ref. 2 introduces an algorithm generating 2D standardized maps that are approximately conformal. This algorithm was developed before the improved version described in Ref. 9 and was applied to investigate the correlation between geometric parameters extracted at each point of the carotid surfaces and the wall shear stress (WSS), which was established as an important hemodynamic parameter linked to the development of carotid atherosclerosis. Ideas developed in carotid atlas construction have been adopted and expanded in the generation of atlases of other anatomic structures. Ref. 3 and Conference Publication 2 introduce a framework developed for the evaluation of local segmentation accuracy and variability of the cerebral ventricle surfaces segmented from 3D ultrasound images. Such evaluation requires the development of a cerebral ventricle atlas that establishes point-by-point correspondence of the cerebral ventricles for a group of subjects. The atlas generation technique was described in Ref. 3, which is a more advanced version than that introduced in Conference Publication 2. Objective 2 has been successfully accomplished. In fact, the algorithm developed in this project was better than that originally described in the ECS proposal. The originally proposed biomarker that measures the mean vessel-wall-plus-plaque thickness change (VWT-Change) specific to regions of interest identified by a feature selection algorithm was described in Ref. 5 and was evaluated in a cohort including ex-smokers and never-smokers with normal airflow measurements. In Ref. 5, we showed that measurements of this biomarker were significantly higher in ex-smokers than in never-smokers. This investigation shows the ex-smokers were associated with a more severe atherosclerosis and were exposed to a higher stroke risk even though all subjects in this cohort do not have an airflow limitation. This result establishes a link between early, sub-clinical smoking-related respiratory abnormalities and carotid atherosclerosis for the first time. However, the feature-selection-based biomarker has two major limitations. First, feature selection returns a binary distribution on the 2D map, which identifies whether each point in the 2D map is included in the ROI. Points not selected were not involved in the computation of the region-based biomarker, but may still provide important information in the difference of VWT-Change distributions in the two groups. Second, the mutual-information-based feature selection algorithm is a forward sequential searching algorithm that adds features one at a time without an objectively defined stopping criterion. The lack of a termination criterion produces variability in the feature-selection-based biomarker as the average VWT-Change is a function of the size of the ROI over which the average was taken. In Ref. 8, we introduced a biomarker based on a weighted average, which, while emphasizing regions with the more prominent difference between treatment groups, takes all points in the 2D map into consideration. Since all points are considered, the new biomarker does not vary with the number of points involved in the calculation of the average VWT-Change. The results presented in Ref. 8 shows that the new biomarker is more sensitive in discriminating subjects treated with Vitamin B from the control group. The sample size required by the new biomarker to establish the effect of Vitamin B in carotid atherosclerosis progression/regression is 70-80% lower than existing biomarker, thereby potentially contributing to lowering the cost and the duration of clinical trials aiming at establishing effects of new treatment options. Objective 3 was successfully accomplished with the introduction of a biomarker based on the graph-based random walk framework and a novel similarity function in Ref. 6. The proposed biomarker was validated by 3D ultrasound images acquired from a placebo-controlled trial investigating the effect of a lipid-lowering drug known as atorvastatin. In Ref. 6, we showed that the proposed biomarker was 14 times more sensitive than the mean VWT-Change in discriminating responsive and unresponsive subjects. Other developments in this project involve the introduction of arterial segmentation and registration algorithms. Although the development of these algorithms was not explicitly specified as objectives in the proposal, they are required in the generation of the carotid VWT-Change maps, which are pre-requisites of all objectives in the proposal. Ref. 11 introduces a direct three-dimensional sparse field level-set algorithm for plaque segmentation, which is an improved version of the algorithm developed in Conference Publication 5. Ref. 1 introduces an arterial segmentation algorithm focusing on improving segmentation accuracy by adjusting the initial contour fed into a surface deformable model. It was shown in the paper that more accurate initial contours produced by the adjustment operators lead to significant improvement in segmentation accuracy. Related concepts have been adopted in ultrasound prostate (Ref. 4) and breast lesion (Ref. 10) segmentation. Note: The acknowledgement section was inadvertently missed out in two conference publications intimately related to this project (Conference Publications 5 and 6). For this reason, this grant was not properly acknowledged in these two conference publications and we apologize for this oversight.

139713.label: Major findings and research outcome
139713.value: Since carotid atherosclerosis is a focal disease that predominantly occurs at bifurcations, biomarkers based on local plaque change was hypothesized to be more sensitive in assessing the progression and regression of carotid plaques in therapeutic clinical trials, thereby reducing the sample size required to demonstrate the statistical significance of treatment effects. A major contribution of this project was the development of a vessel-wall-plus-plaque thickness change (VWT-Change) quantification framework to provide a consistent assessment of local vessel wall and plaque burden progression/regression in the carotid arteries of a population. Specific contribution involves (i) the development of carotid atlases to adjust for the inter-subject variability in vascular geometry and (ii) the development of simple and sensitive biomarkers to quantify the degree of VWT-Change for each patient. The techniques developed in this project have been applied in (i) assessing the effect of Vitamin B for atherosclerosis (Ref. 8). The sample size required to establish statistical significance of the effect of Vitamin B treatment was 70-80% lower than existing 3D carotid ultrasound biomarkers; (ii) assessing the difference in the vessel-wall-plus-plaque burden in ex-smokers and never-smokers (Ref. 5). In this subclinical population, vessel wall volume was not able to detect the difference in vessel-wall-plus-plaque burden whereas significant difference was detected by our VWT biomarkers; (iii) quantifying the response of patients treated by a strong dose of atorvastatin (Ref. 6). A graph-based biomarker we developed was 14 times more sensitive than the mean VWT-Change in discriminating responsive and unresponsive subjects. The framework has a major impact in reducing the sample size and the duration required to establish statistical significance of novel treatments for atherosclerosis, thereby reducing the cost of clinical trials. In addition, the intersubject variation of treatment response is common. The more sensitive VWT-Change biomarkers introduced in this project will allow for earlier identification of patients that do not sufficiently respond to treatments. Once identified, alternative treatment strategies can be administrated to these patients.

139713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
139713.value: The current project focuses on the constructing sensitive biomarkers based solely on local VWT-Change. We hypothesize that incorporating local volumetric changes and textural change of plaque would lead to another leap in the assessment of new therapies for atherosclerosis. We are carrying out studies to investigate the validity of this hypothesis.

139713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
139713.value: Carotid atherosclerosis is a major source of blood clots, which travel downstream and may block one of the cerebral arteries, causing ischemic stroke. Most strokes associated with carotid atherosclerosis can be prevented by lifestyle/dietary changes. Therefore, parallel to the development of new therapies, there is a critical need for sensitive biomarkers for serial monitoring of atherosclerosis. Since carotid atherosclerosis is a focal disease that predominantly occurs at bifurcations, biomarkers based on local or region-based plaque change measurements were hypothesized in the project proposal to be more sensitive in assessing the progression and regression of carotid plaques in therapeutic clinical trials. We developed 3D ultrasound imaging tools to quantify local vessel-wall-plus-plaque thickness change (VWT-Change) over a treatment period and showed that biomarkers proposed based on local VWT-Change measurements are more sensitive than global volumetric measurements of the vessel wall and plaque volumes. As the sample size requirement and the cost for establishing treatment effects in a clinical trial have been significantly reduced by the introduction of these carotid biomarkers, many proof-of-principle studies can be performed for novel treatment options before a more costly study involving a larger population is held to validate the results.

140213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
140213.value: 學界對顧頡剛疑史辨偽工作以至其治學操守均褒貶不一。但有關論述較局限於顧 氏漫長生命歷程中的某些孤立時段和學術片段。要對顧氏其人其學有客觀、深入 的了解，實需從兩方面知識背景着手：近世域外學術與中國學術、思想資源的複 雜互動(尤其是近代日本學術與中國學術)，「五四」重估傳統價值與現代中國學 術知識轉型的關係。無前者，固不知顧氏乃至現代中國學術知識之體系及其主體 性；無後者，亦無以知顧氏與現代中國學術的發展方向及其自我更新求變的複雜 過程。此外，不可忽視的還有顧氏建立學術事業的職志及其構造學術社群的用心。 否則，顧氏的學術生命和現代中國的學術特質將無從深論，遑論走出疑古時代、 重建中國學術體系。本研究將從多角度透視顧氏的知識體系、學術事業與生命情 懷；並以之為視角，觀察中國疑古傳統在走向近代的過程中如何與域外知識觀念 契接，從而促進學術的轉型和再生展。相關研究將有助於了解傳統思想資源與新 知識的建立及傳播的深層關係。

140213.label: Major findings and research outcome
140213.value: 顧頡剛是1920年代古史辨運動的領軍人物，以激烈反傳統而著稱的史學家。但在1930年代，基於日軍侵略中國、蒙古將繼滿洲宣佈脫離中國而獨立的民族危機，他不再倡言疑古辨偽的反傳統學術思想，同時放棄掉「為學問而學問」的治學理念。取而代之的是，他出於抗戰主張和參與救國的政治活動，使學術研究發揮切合時需的功用，以喚醒國人團結救亡為首務。異於昔日集矢攻擊儒學道統的虛構性，他因抗日救國之故而從民族學、文化風俗學、邊疆史地考證等諸方面召喚國人的民族文化意識，致力於建構中華民族的統一性及同一性；這可看作是顧頡剛因應世變而有其「重光國史」、「轉步國運」(借用錢穆之語)的新學術事業。總言之，本研究成功和深入地從顧頡剛於救亡危機下，向學界闡明顧頡剛的思想在前後究竟發生了什麼樣的變化以及他怎麼樣地實踐他的新學術目標。

140213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
140213.value: 1.將繼續關注顧頡剛思想的多元性和流變性 2.將繼續釐清顧頡剛與北京學界的人事交割以及在1930年代以來與左翼史學陣營的思想互動 3.將繼續探究顧頡剛學術思想轉型帶給中國史學界的影響

140213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
140213.value: 本研究嘗試向學界/讀者闡明，顧頡剛在1920年代因“古史辨”運動而名滿天下，並且其一生的學業功績都被普遍認為是在於透過古史辨運動而推倒傳統學術思想、重造中國文化傳統。然而，他的這一思想或事業只是他生命中的一個片段，更不是固滯不變的。本研究嘗試說明其前有所承，後亦有所變。當然，在發展和變化的過程中，他的思想世界也曾發生矛盾，而學術創造方面也必須面對時代帶來的種種局限。總之，本研究試圖重估顧頡剛的學術影響力和歷史價值，並超越或褒或貶的視角還原其史家形象。

140313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
140313.value: The rise of China has been reshaping the world’s political economy. Since its economic reform in 1978, China has been seen as driving the ‘race to the bottom’ competition amongst developing countries and exerting a negative impact on global labour standards (A. Chan, 2003). In recent years, scholarly work on Chinese labour has been dominated by two distinct strands. The first strand is influenced by the tradition of institutional analysis and has made trade unions as the centre of inquiry. The second strand reflects the sociologists’ concern and focuses more on the management’s control and labour resistance in workplace (‘labour regime’). These two strands have started to pay attention to common themes, such as the rising patterns of migrant workers’ protests, but they still have different emphases. While the primary interest of the institutional analysis scholars lies in the role of trade unions and state authorities in mediating labour conflicts (A. Chan, 2011; Chen, 2010; Gallagher, 2005), the framework of class formation has been introduced by the sociological strand to discuss labour protests (Lee, 2007; Chan and Pun, 2009; Leung and Pun, 2009; Pun and Lu, 2010). This has left an important research gap in the field: what is the impact of labour protest on the institutional settings of the Chinese industrial relations? While our previous and ongoing research has suggested that the waves of strikes have exercised pressure on the party-state to introduce a policy framework that emphasizes on workers’ collective rights, essentially collective bargaining and trade union reform (C. Chan, 2010; Chan and Hui, 2012; forthcoming), we know little about the implementation of these initiatives and their impact on power relations in the workplace after the strikes. This research endeavors to fill this intellectual gap. On the one hand, it assesses the extent to which labour resistance has shaped the institutions regulating the workplace labour relations; on the other, it evaluates the effectiveness of the party-state’s attempt to mediate labour conflicts via the new regulations and mechanism. Drawing upon Burawoy (1985)’s insights on two forms of labour regimes in industrial capitalism—despotism and hegemony, this research will examine the potentials and limitations of workers’ activism in transforming the despotic labour regime within the new regulation and policy framework. Also, by comparing two major export-oriented cities in southern and eastern China, Shenzhen and Suzhou respectively, the role of the local state and local regulations in workplace relations will be explored. 中國的崛起​​重塑了全世界的政治經濟。自中國在1978年推行經濟改革以來，中國被認為是在發展中國家之間推動「向下競爭」（race to the bottom），並對全球勞工標準造成負面影響（A. Chan，2003）。近年，對中國工人的學術研究被兩個種類主導。第一類受制度分析影響，把工會視為研究的重心。第二類反映了社會學家的關注，把焦點放在工作場所內管理層的控制及工人的反抗（「勞動體制」）。這兩類研究漸開始關心相同的主題，例如移民工抗爭的發起模式，但他們仍有不同的側重點。制度分析學者的主要興趣在於工會和國家機在調解勞工糾紛的角色（A Chan，2011；Chen，2010；Gallagher，2005），社會學的研究則引進了階級形成的框架探討勞工抗爭（Lee，2007 ；Chan and Pun，2009；Pun and Lu，2010）。他們在這個研究範疇中留下了一個重要的空隙：工人抗爭在中國勞資關係的製度環境有何影響？我們以往及目前的研究提出多次工潮對於政府構成了壓力，迫使國家推行強調工人集體權利的政策框架，尤其是集體談判和工會改革（C. Chan，2010；Chan and Hui，2012；待出版） ，我們對於這些政策的落實和他們在罷工後對工作環境的權力關係的影響仍所知甚微。本研究旨在填補上述的學術空隙。一方面，本研究檢視工人抗爭在何等程度上形塑了各種管理工作場所勞工關係的製度；另一方面，本研究亦評核政府透過新的規條和機制調解勞工糾紛的效用。借用Buraway（1985）對工業資本主義下兩種勞動體制的洞見－－專制（despotism）和霸權（hegemony），本研究將檢視工人運動在新規條和政策下轉化專制式的勞動體制有何潛力和限制。另外，透過比較兩個在華南及華東的主要出口向導城市（分別是深圳和蘇州），本研究將探討地方政府及其政策在規範工作場所勞動關係上扮演的角色。

140313.label: Realisation of objectives
140313.value: The objectives of the project have been well achieved. As we stated in our proposal, the first stage of this research was sponsored by the Chiang Ching-kuo Foundation for International Scholarly Exchange through the project 'Changing Labour Regime in China? A Study of Workplace Relations in Suzhou'. The most important objective of this project was to study the impact of workers' collective actions on workplace relations. We found that strikes and NGOs activism have exerted much more impact in the city of Shenzhen ( or Pearl River Delta in general) than Suzhou (or the Yangtsz River Delta). Therefore, we used case studies in Shenzhen and other cities in the PRD to demonstrate the scope and limits of labour activism in influencing labour policies, industrial relations framework and workplace relations under the current political-economic context. Meanwhile, we compared different geographic areas and stages of development to show that the local state and its industrial policies have a significant role in shaping working conditions, labour relations and labour activism.

140313.label: Major findings and research outcome
140313.value: Our research has produced many journal articles and book chapters on the impact of workers collective actions on a wide range of issues, such as collective bargaining (Chan and Hui, 2014), trade union reform (Hui and Chan, 2015), labour legislation (Hui and Chan, 2016), state strategies (Chan and Hui, 2017) and labour regulatory regime (Chan, 2014). In terms of the differences between Suzhou and Shenzhen, we found that: 1) The tradition of Town and Village Enterprises from 1980s has laid a solid foundation for Private Domestic Owned Enterprise and thus has protected workers in Suzhou better than their counterparts of Foreign Owned Enterprise workers in Shenzhen; 2) The industrial park model, which was originated from Suzhou, involves a high level government to collect land from the peasants, destroy the village houses, and transformed the peasants into proletarians by offering them apartments and social security. In Shenzhen, the urban village (cheng zhong cun) has played a significant role in nurturing NGOs and strike activism. In Suzhou, however, the space of traditional village has been totally destroyed and the space of NGO and workers’ activism has also been constrained; 3) While labour NGOs in the PRD are mainly supported by organizations in Hong Kong, grassroot NGOs in Suzhou does not have such geographic advantage and have to turn to the local government for support. But more importantly, the government in Suzhou has reached out much further than their counterparts in the PRD in monitoring NGOs and other civil society actors.

140313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
140313.value: Our research focused on labour intensive manufacturing industries in the PRD and YRD. With the trend of industrial relocation to the inland provinces, and state's policies to promote industrial upgrading, it is important to extend the empirical research to other parts of the country and to high-tech industries and service sector.

140313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
140313.value: Since its economic reform in the 1980s, China had been seen as driving a ‘race to the bottom’ amongst developing countries and exerting a negative impact on global labour standards. Poor working conditions in the country have triggered workers’ collective unrest and demands for better wages and treatment; the government has been compelled to take serious measures to contain the unrest, including the implementation of the Labour Contract Law in 2008. This research has studied the impact of labour protest on the institutional settings of the Chinese industrial relations. On the one hand, it assesses the extent to which labour resistance has shaped the institutions regulating the workplace labour relations; on the other, it evaluates the effectiveness of the party-state’s attempt to mediate labour conflicts via the new regulations and mechanism.

141613.label: Project Objectives
141613.value: To compare the effectiveness of common physical activities and traditional Chinese martial arts training for reducing children’s reactive and proactive aggression at Pretest (Time 1), Posttest (Time 2), and one-year follow-up study (Time 3). Compared to the corresponding scores of reactive and proactive aggression at T1, Hypothesis 1a: children in Control groups I and II show no change at T2 and T3. Hypothesis 1b: children in Experimental groups I and II show a similar level of reduction in reactive and proactive aggression, which is less than that of children in Experimental group III but more than children in the two control groups at T2 and T3. Hypothesis 1c: children in Experimental group III show the most significant reduction in both reactive and proactive aggression among the three experimental groups at T2 and T3. To test the mediating effects of children’s anger arousal, impulsivity, and self-control on reducing the reactive aggression of children in the three Experimental groups (see Figure 1). For children in the three Experimental groups, Hypothesis 2a: martial arts training directly reduces their anger arousal, and impulsivity, and improves their self-control. Hypothesis 2b: with the reduction of anger arousal, and impulsivity, children’s reactive aggression is further reduced. Hypothesis 2c: with the improvement of self-control, children’s reactive aggression is further reduced. To test the mediating effects of children’s narcissism, callous-unemotional (CU) traits, and empathy on reducing the proactive aggression of children in the three Experimental groups (see Figure 2). For children in the three Experimental groups, Hypothesis 3a: martial arts training directly reduces their narcissism and CU traits, and increases their empathy. Hypothesis 3b: with the reduction of narcissism and CU traits, children’s proactive aggression is further reduced. Hypothesis 3c: with the increase of empathy, children’s proactive aggression is further reduced. To identify the intervention effects of traditional Chinese martial arts training at different stages of Times 1, 2, and 3. For both reactive and proactive aggression of children in the three Experimental groups, Hypothesis 4a: scores at T2 are significantly lower than those at T1. Hypothesis 4b: scores at T3 are significantly lower than those at T2.
