157013.label: Major findings and research outcome
157013.value: The most significant research outcomes of this project include the following publications, which can be found in Part C: “Human Rights and the Literary Self-Portrait: Vann Nath's A Cambodian Prison Portrait: One Year in the Khmer Rouge's S-21”; “Iterations of War and its Literary Counterforces: Vaddey Ratner’s In the Shadow of the Banyan and Kosal Khiev’s Why I Write”; “Buried History and Transpacific Pedagogy: Teaching the Vietnamese Boat People’s Hong Kong Passage”; “‘To the Intellectuals of the West’: Rithy Panh’s The Elimination and Genealogies of the Cambodian Genocide”; “Alice Munro Country and Refugee Havens.” Through attention to an understudied archive of transnational Asian literature, film, and culture that takes up the afterlife of the Cold War in Cambodia, this project has undertaken the work of re-centering the refugee’s testimonies and knowledges that have been historically been disavowed, forgotten, and neglected. After over four decades have elapsed since the Khmer Rouge era, Cambodians have acquired a degree of psychological space and distance from the traumatic past that is often necessary for artistic experimentation to take place. This distance, coupled with a general acceptance by the international community that Cambodian refugee testimonies were not fabricated tales, has allowed Cambodian authors to begin to approach the past with more imaginative flexibility. While not one aesthetic form or genre can adequately capture the heterogeneity of this new movement, Cambodian transpacific critique is decidedly more experimental in its engagement with the testimonial form. Beyond a simple recounting of the past, testimony forms a part of the strategy for survival, healing, and reconciliation. For the refugee, testimony is about recounting one’s first-hand experience of state violence, displacement, and resettlement; it is also about reclaiming compromised self-hood and about making appeals to asylum nations for opening its borders. In the context of an ongoing global crisis in which refugees have become increasingly mistrusted, surveilled and criminalized, regarded as threats to national security or homogenized objects of humanitarian pity, this project has stressed that we have an urgent responsibility to attend to the complex personhoods articulated in the art and life stories of survivors and refugees. Oriented toward social justice, Cambodian transpacific critique works to counter the increasing global compassion fatigue and stigmatization of refugees in the contemporary era. These narratives attest to the complicated inner lifeworlds of refugees, imagining futures, aspirations, and relations of coexistence beyond the paralyzing traumas of the past.

157013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
157013.value: Building on my first project’s investigation refugee narratives, my next project will shift the focus to the global politics of refugee sponsorship. The project will attend more closely to written and filmic accounts of Western sponsors and humanitarians involved with the refugee resettlement process. If a sponsor can be variously defined as “one who assumes responsibility for some other person or thing,” what does sponsorship mean in the context of global refugee crises from the Cold War to the present? Theorizing the politics of refugee sponsorship within a transnational framework, The Will to Sponsor will assemble an archive of refugee sponsorship stories (government archives, memoirs by sponsors, documentary case studies, and refugee literature) that illuminate the complex political, affective, and discursive entanglements of global refugee sponsorship. Some preliminary ideas for this research project are outlined in my forum contribution, “Alice Munro Country and Refugee Havens,” which appears in the recent special issue of Canadian Literature, and in the autobiographical essay I contributed for website Compassionate Canada, which can be found here: https://compassionatecanada.wordpress.com/2015/09/07/y-dang-troeung-hong-kong/.

157013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
157013.value: This research project considers how Cambodian diasporic life stories (as found in testimonials, literature, and film) serve as a rich site for understanding difficult questions about justice in the aftermath of genocide: What is the relationship between healing, reconciliation, and life stories? How are notions of trauma read differently across cultural, national, gendered, and generational divides, and what are the implications of these epistemological differences for thinking about justice? What is the relationship between healing, reconciliation, and life stories? This study has explored how diasporic life stories not only bear witness to a truth beyond what is empirically verifiable, but also have a creative license to imagine potential futures beyond the trauma, a creativity that is not as readily available in anthropological, sociological, and legal texts. The project engages in the global conversation among survivors, oral historians, literary and film scholars, human rights activists, and policy makers about how life stories can and are being mobilized in the collective work of reconciliation. This project serves as a timely scholarly intervention in the context of the contemporary global refugee crises, demonstrating what can be learned from past historical traumas and from those who have survived them.

157413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
157413.value: Previous research has suggested that men who endorse more traditional constructions of masculinity are less likely to engage in healthy behaviour. Men suffer more severe chronic health conditions, have higher mortality for all leading causes of death, and die younger than women in many modern societies around the world. The issue of gender difference in mortality is an issue of strong international resonance as we cope with population ageing across the globe. However, a number of key questions regarding individual differences and cultural differences in the construction of masculinity and the impact on male health behaviour remain unanswered. Masculinities and approaches to health are diverse and complex, with significant variations across cultural contexts. There is a dearth of research focusing on the meanings and relationship between diet, health and food among men. This is an important topic particularly in light of the current ‘crisis’ in men’s health and the role of lifestyle factors, such as diet and illness prevention. Critically, the majority of the existing research related to constructions of masculinity is derived from cross-sectional studies in Western populations on selected aspects of health behaviour. The proposed project will explore how factors such as ethnicity, employment, educational level, socioeconomic status, sexual orientation, place of birth and social context influence the kind of masculinity that men construct and contribute to differential health risks among men in Hong Kong, using a cohort of Hong Kong Chinese, mainland Chinese, South Asian, and white males residing in Hong Kong. The project will employ a mixed methodology focus groups and survey to examine constructions of masculinity and health-related behaviour among different cohorts between the ages of 18 and 79 years.

157413.label: Realisation of objectives
157413.value: The present study was unique in its bicultural and cross-cultural examination of men’s help-seeking behaviour in Hong Kong, examining how constructions of masculinity impact on men’s help-seeking behaviour. The study has identified differences in the help-seeking approaches of Chinese, Western and South Asian men in Hong Kong. Some of the most striking differences have been observed between Western and Chinese men, both in their attitudes towards health and help-seeking. While Chinese men (regardless of mainland or Hong Kong Chinese) were more proactive in their help-seeking behaviour, Western men were more strongly influenced by a hegemonic masculine culture which seemed to prevent these men from showing an open concern with their health and taking a more proactive stance with health protective behaviour. On the other hand, Chinese men were much more proactive in their health and help-seeking behaviour, some of this behaviour can be seen to be influenced by their cultural values, and specifically the emphasis on filial piety, which meant that Chinese men felt a strong sense of duty towards looking after their family, which they perceived they needed to be in good health to do so. In this way it can be seen that cultural values have an influence on constructions of masculinity which in turn go on to influence the health and help-seeking behaviour of these men. The PI is currently in the midst of drafting a paper comparing constructions of masculinity across the three groups of men recruited; this paper will be the first of its kind in comparing constructions of masculinity across three diverse cultural groups. To date the PI has successfully executed two qualitative manuscripts; one of which is in press and one is currently under review. In the near future this funded project will have three publications that will be directly related to this research project. In addition to this, the PI has disseminated findings from the project at three international conferences which have contributed to broader theoretical debates within the field of health psychology regarding men’s health and health behaviour.

157413.label: Major findings and research outcome
157413.value: The study identified clear differences in pathways to help-seeking and healthcare among men in Hong Kong. Much of the current literature centres on white heteronormative ideologies of masculinity and as such the present findings are insightful in their revelations of constructions of masculinity among non-white male populations. In the past little attention has been paid to cultural variations in masculinity, whereas this was very much the focus of the present study. Clear pathways of help-seeking were identified among Chinese men who were very much influenced by cultural values. Chinese men were proactive in looking after their health and were comfortable to discuss their health and illnesses with others, while Western men were less proactive in looking after their health. While Chinese men shared their health concerns with their wives and families this was something Western men frowned up. Western men were more comfortable with sharing their health concerns only with their male friends, and would share health information with their partners in more strategic ways, such as to gain more sympathy or ‘get the dinner cooked for me’. An important motivator for good health among the Chinese men was filial piety whereas for Western men an important motivator was looking good. While a widespread endorsement of hegemonic masculinity was observed in Western men, the same was not observed among Chinese and South Asian men. Among Western men, help-seeking was embraced when it was perceived to impact on their masculinity, for example, when related to sexual performance. Whereas Chinese talked of the importance of looking after their own health in order to better look after their families, demonstrating the influence of cultural values such as filial piety on the health behaviour and attitude of individuals.

157413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
157413.value: The PI is hoping to extend the development of this research by examining the influence of cultural values on the help-seeking behaviour of men and women in relation to psychological help-seeking. Based on the findings of the present project, the PI has just applied for GRF funding to examine the relationship between gender norms, gender role conflict and attitude towards professional help-seeking in Hong Kong.

157413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
157413.value: Clear pathways of help-seeking were identified among Chinese and British men in Hong Kong. Chinese men were proactive in looking after their health while British men were less so. An important motivation for good health among Chinese men was filial piety; men talked of looking after their own health to better look after their families and discussed how concern to prevent family worry was a motivator to become healthier. Chinese men talked of sharing their health worries and concerns with their wives and partners, whereas British men were much more reluctant to share their health concerns with their partners, while friends were an important source of sharing for British men in Hong Kong. Chinese men viewed this problem-solving behaviour as positive, while British men viewed this problem-solving with their wives in more negative ways.

157513.label: Project Objectives
157513.value: To describe dynamic changes in inter-city passenger access and intra-city business agglomeration patterns for the past 10 to 15 years by computing macro-scale network and micro-scale location indicators based on graph theory and urban economics, which enables us to analyze global city cases as "nodes" and "places" in a topological manner. To examine the marginal impacts of inter-city passenger access changes on intra-city business agglomeration patterns by establishing the regression models for multivariate longitudinal micro-geographic data over the past 10 to 15 years in Hong Kong and selected global cities, which allows us to grasp the node-place characteristics of global cities in an empirical way. To highlight international experiences with the significance of HSR terminal development along with airport improvement projects in global-status cities’ urban development processes by comparing their indirect access changes and agglomeration impacts in dissimilar backgrounds, which helps us identify generalizable state practices and market responses across different countries and regions. To explain the question of whether business agglomeration impacts around inter-city transportation terminuses are truly generative, representing net increases in economic productivity or are pecuniary and redistributive in nature, simply transferring economic activities from suburban business locations to central business districts, which is useful for researchers and policymakers to introduce territorially more efficient and equitable regional transportation investment and local economic development programmers in other global-status cities and newly developing regions in China.

157513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
157513.value: In recent years, High-Speed Rail (HSR) development programs have increasingly been introduced, funded and implemented along with airport improvement programs in American, European and Asian city-regions, including Hong Kong and Mainland China. Such intercity/interregional/international transportation investments are often justified not simply based on their direct passenger benefits but rather their indirect development benefits conferred around first-tier cities’ terminal stations. Despite the increased importance of HSR in public policy and urban planning, its net benefits and spatial impacts remain questionable, due in large part to the paucity of empirical knowledge about the combined effects of intercity railway development and airport improvement projects and the complexity of polycentric and redistributive economic development processes in global-status cities. This research attempts to illustrate dynamic changes in “inter-city access” and “intra-city agglomeration”, so-called node-place characteristics of global cities, by computing a set of macro-geographic network and micro-geographic agglomeration indicators for the last 10 to 15 years and examine the marginal impacts of inter-city railway and airway network changes on intra-city business agglomeration patterns by running regression models for multivariate longitudinal macro- and micro-geographic data in Hong Kong and selected global cities (e.g., Tokyo, Los Angeles and New York). Empirical findings derived from this international case analysis will be fruitful for both scholars and professionals to have better understandings of the spatial transformation processes of global city-regions on the basis of urban theory and development practice. In particular, our study will shed light on the question of whether HSR terminal development projects (e.g., West Kowloon Terminus in Hong Kong, Figure1) accrue inter-city access and intra-city agglomeration benefits dominantly in a central business district at the expense of suburban business centers or lead to polycentric city-regional development largely accompanied by airport capacity improvement schemes (e.g., Hong Kong International Airport Master Plan 2030). The evidence on inter-city transportation network evolutions and intra-city business agglomeration impacts in the past decade could help us make more efficient and equitable transportation investments and land use policies in “transitional” Chinese and other Asian city-regions for the next decades. 近年来，高铁已经得到了普遍的关注和认可。美国，欧洲和亚洲的许多区域，包括香港和中国大陆都积极的引进，资助和实施高铁项目。这种夸区域的交通投资不仅需要考虑乘客的需求，还要考虑高铁终端对于该地区经济的影响。尽管学术界越来越关注高铁的发展，高铁项目所带来的收益以及对城市空间的影响并不明晰。这方面的实证研究显得尤其复杂：它不仅要考虑到现有铁路和机场等交通网络的影响，还要考虑多中心城市的复杂性以及在开发过程中所产生的效益分配。 本研究试图说明“城际连接”和“城市内部集聚”的动态变化，也就是全球城市的节点场所特征. 通过运用计量回归方法对过去10-15年间高铁在香港和几个国际都市（东京，纽约，洛杉矶）所产生的宏观地理网络和微观地理聚集效应进行分析，来论证城市间的轨道交通及机场交通网的改变对于城市内部商业聚集效应的影响。 本实证研究通过对于国际都市的案例分析，将会让学者和专业人士更好的理解国际都市及区域的空间转换过程. 这个研究着重揭示高铁终端发展是否会导致城市间的更好连接，是否会增强城市商业区的聚集，以及这种聚集是否会以伤害郊区商业的发展为代价，并导致多中心的城市发展. 这些结论将会指导未来在中国和亚太其它地区的高铁投资，使得未来的高铁发展能够更好的结合土地规划，最终导致更经济，集约，有效，以及平衡的区域发展。

157513.label: Realisation of objectives
157513.value: Firstly, this research described complex and dynamic changes in inter-city passenger access and intra-city business agglomeration patterns within Hong Kong, Wuhan (China), Tokyo Metropolitan Region (Japan), and Northeast Corridor (United States) by analyzing geographic datasets on intra-city transportation networks and cross-industrial employment location with the model of node-place development. The geographic analyses based on urban economics and network theories was successful in capturing the dynamism of contemporary city formation in a topological way. In particular, this study illustrated the fact that rapid changes in inter-city and intra-city transportation networks were accompanied by “de-industrialization” – a drastic industrial restructuring process from manufacturing-based to service-based economies – in China, Japan, and the United States for the last 10–15 years. Secondly, this research further examined the intra-city influences of rail network changes on business agglomeration shifts and/or urban economic performance by running several multivariate regression models for land values and labor productivity by industrial sector on different scales across Wuhan (on a site-scale), Tokyo (on a municipal scale), and Northeast Corridor (on a metropolitan scale). Note that the case of Wuhan was added to this research for this objective, as Hong Kong’s HSR project was delayed and is still under construction in December 2017. To have local evidence, we have to wait for the completion and operation of HSR in Hong Kong. In essence, the capitalization effects and/or productivity gains relevant to major railway network extensions within Wuhan, Tokyo, and Northeast Corridor appeared to be statistically significant in contemporary business sectors (e.g., office, finance, producer services), regardless of geographic scales. Thirdly, this research summarized international implications based on a range of quantitative descriptions and empirical findings from Wuhan, Tokyo, and Northeast Corridor. Although the cases possessed dissimilar urbanization scales and spatial development strategies, this study found that there were internationally generalizable practices in last-mile service and land use coordination, accompanied by business relocation and productivity gains in knowledge-based industrial sectors. Particular, “local entrepreneurialism” plays a critical role in raising public capital funds and maximizing private capital gains for accessibility around inter-city transportation facilities along with special economic zones. The inferences are of particular importance for land use rezoning and economic development practices around the on-going HSR project in Hong Kong. Lastly, the question of whether business agglomeration impacts around inter-city transportation terminuses are generative or redistributive in nature still remains inclusive, as the empirical analyses on employment relocations, land values, and productivity gains presented mixed results within Wuhan , Tokyo, and U.S. Northeast Corridor (and no evidence on the case of Hong Kong). 157513.label: Major findings and research outcome
157513.value: This research produced four large sets of quantitative studies on the influences of HSR terminal development accompanied by airport improvement programs on spatial reconfiguration and its economic performance by applying a “node-place” model for selected global cases – Hong Kong, Wuhan, Tokyo, and U.S. Northeast Corridor. The first set sheds light on Hong Kong's urban transformation pattern associated with the Hong Kong International Airport development in 1998 (and partially the on-going HSR project) from a spatial analysis that estimates: the last-mile costs between the international terminal and local origins/destinations; the residential profiles of major estates along the airport access line; and the effects of airport access times and costs on cross-industrial agglomeration patterns. These empirical results were presented at the 54th ACSP Annual Conference in 2014. The second set examines the intra-city relationships between HSR locations, metro extensions, and land leases in Wuhan. A set of spatial autoregressive models are tested to estimate the intra-city influences of inter-city accessibility changes on land lease prices for 2004–16 around three HSR stations and along four metro lines. The results reveal that significant premiums appeared on land leases for commercial and residential uses in 1–2 km of the upgraded city-centre HSR station and in 1km of the metro stations connected to the new city-fringe HSR station during the years after the train services came into operation. This case study is currently under review as a full article for publication in "Regional Studies." The third set scrutinizes the intra-metropolitan associations between intra-city accessibility, employment density, and labor productivity using data from 267 municipalities in Tokyo. Results of the spatial models for value added per worker infer that labor productivity outperforms in the municipalities that afford low city-airport access and egress costs by intermodal transportation systems and attain high urbanization economies across high-tech, knowledge-, and service-intensive industries. This geographic study is also under review as a full article for publication in "Regional Studies." The fourth set measures changes in intra-city railway network and business agglomeration patterns using geographic datasets from Boston, New York, Philadelphia, and Washington DC along the US Northeast Corridor. Moreover, a set of panel data analyses are applied to examine the associations of changes in inter-city employment accessibility across the 15 industrial sectors with metropolitan-scale economic productivity in the Northeast Corridor for 2001–14. Another manuscript is currently prepared as a full article for publication in "Transport Policy" (or "Transportation").

157513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
157513.value: There are three possible directions for further development of the research. First, follow-up research needs to be conducted for the case of Hong Kong during the post-project period of HSR, which should be compared to the empirical evidence on Hong Kong’s intra-city economic geography from the pre-project period. Second, the empirical findings presented by this research were derived from topological information. Thus, it will be value-added to combining emerging big data on both inter-city and intra-city travel flows into the hieratical transportation systems and urban agglomeration datasets used for short-term spatiotemporal analyses. Third, more micro-geographic datasets on socioeconomic profiles, housing rents, and household incomes have to be incorporated into the empirical analyses on megaprojects and macro-geographic transformation to discuss the issue of state entrepreneurialism and the potential of welfare capitalism for truly competitive and sustainable regional development.

157513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
157513.value: Multibillion-dollar public spending in inter-city transportation, including high-speed rail (HSR) and hub airport terminals, has progressively been adopted by policy makers as an economic stimulus. Despite the importance of safeguarding such megaprojects and their wider economic impacts, little has been reported about dynamic changes in inter-city transportation access and intra-city business location worldwide. This research attempts to grasp the influences of HSR terminal development accompanied by airport improvement programs on spatial reconfiguration and its economic performance from selected global cases – Hong Kong, Wuhan, Tokyo, and U.S. Northeast Corridor. Although the four global cases have dissimilar geographic scales and industrial structures, the empirical findings obtained from a set of spatiotemporal analyses on network evolution, employment relocation, and economic performance commonly implies that the region-wide impacts of multibillion-dollar infrastructure investment depend heavily on intra-city land use coordination and inter-modal transportation connectivity in local contexts. This study concludes that entrepreneurial city governments play a critical role in allocating public resources and capture private gains for accessibility enhanced around inter-city transportation hubs, such as in-city HSR and airport terminals.

158513.label: Project Title(Chinese)
158513.value: 政府部門自主是否一把雙刃劍？探究政府部門自主與機構腐敗及績效的關係

158513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
158513.value: New Public Management reforms in recent decades have been based on the assumption that delegating autonomy to government agencies brings about improvements in organizational performance. This presents an ‘accountability dilemma’ problem, which indicates a trade-off between performance and accountability. That is, when government is more inclined to improve organizational performance with increased autonomy, bureaucrats’ accountability can be compromised resulting in the increased likelihood of bureaucratic corruption. Based on this ‘accountability dilemma’ problem, this project will examine how bureaucratic autonomy, which refers to the exemption of constraints on the actual use of decision-making competencies, influences performance as well as corruption of administrative agencies. Research findings to data are equivocal, based on case studies or survey data, and thus we attempt to conduct the first large-sample statistical analyses with systematic data sets over time. In this study, bureaucratic autonomy will be divided into three dimensions: legal autonomy refers to the extent to which the legal status of the agency prevents the government from altering decision-making competencies; structural autonomy is defined as the extent to which the agency is shielded from influence by the government through lines of hierarchy; and financial autonomy refers to the extent to which the agency does not depend on governmental funding. To achieve the goals, we will develop unique data sets that measure organizational autonomy, performance, corruption, and relevant variables (e.g., organizational and managerial attributes) from multiple time points. With time-series data, we will conduct statistical analyses to test the causal relationships of autonomy with performance and corruption. Furthermore, our data will be helpful in extending our current models by enabling future research to investigate what conditions (e.g., organizational structure and management strategies) enhance or weaken the causal relationships. The South Korean central government is an ideal location for this project, as it provides uniquely and systematically externally-audited, archival, and survey data of autonomy, performance, corruption, and other relevant variables. Such data are not available elsewhere. The Korean government has collected these data annually since 2006. Moreover, this research will be conducted by scholars whose research specialties include organizational performance (Jung, Rainey), organizational autonomy (Oh, Rainey), and appropriate methodological skills (Jung, Rainey, Oh). The research outcome will contribute to the theory development of bureaucratic autonomy, corruption, and performance by investigating the causal relationships. Furthermore, the findings are expected to help policy-makers, public employees, and scholars in many countries promote wide-ranging debates on designing and implementing administrative reforms. 近數十年間眾多的新公共管理改革主要基於一個假設，就是政府權力下放，讓機構自主可以改善機構績效。不過，當政府提升機構的自主性以改善其績效時，政府部門的問責可能會受到影響，導致官僚腐敗的可能性增加。由此可見，政府部門自主衍生出要績效還是要問責的「問責困境」。 基於這個「問責困境」的問題，本研究主要探討政府部門自主（意指實際使用決策權力不受限制）如何影響績效以及導致行政機關腐敗。然而，從個案研究及數據調查所得的結果仍然難以看清彼此的關係。因此我們嘗試進行第一次大規模有系統的數據收集及統計分析。在這項研究中，政府部門自主將包括三方面：法律自主，指機構具備能阻止政府更改其決策能力的法律地位；結構性自主，指機構可以免受政府通過內部架構而影響的程度；財務自主，就是機構不依賴政府資助的程度。 在這項研究中，我們將開發獨特的數據集以測量不同時間機構的自主、績效、腐敗，以及有關變數（如機構及管理的屬性）。有了這些在不同時間收集的數據，我們會進行統計分析，測試自主與績效及腐敗的因果關係。這些數據將有助擴大現時的模型，日後可以進一步研究甚麼情況（如組織架構及管理策略）會加強或減弱這因果關係。 南韓中央政府是進行這項研究的理想地點，因為南韓政府能提供獨特及系統化，並且經過外部審計、整理入檔，關於機構自主、績效、腐敗及其他相關變數的調查數據。南韓政府自2006年已開始每年搜集這些數據。其他地方實在難以找到如此齊備的數據。此外，將會負責這項研究的學者均是專長於機構績效、機構自主，以及相關的研究方法。 調查結果將有助於政府部門自主、腐敗與績效因果關係的理論發展。同時，研究結果亦有助其他國家的決策者、公共部門員工及學者就設計及實施行政改革進行更廣泛的討論。

159313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
159313.value: 本課題 計劃對政府政策，社會態度，歷史遺産 綜合作用下的 民族宗教多樣性進行研究。本課題的設立基于項目負責人廣泛的學術研究， 包括宗教與國家的關系，對東南亞的深入了解，和最近獲得的對香港的宗教形勢的專業知識。 在未來四年的時間裏，本人計劃對馬來西亞，新加坡和香港的宗教少數族裔進行比較 並專注于穆斯林和佛教徒團體。馬來西亞人口由60%穆斯林，19%佛教徒和9%的基督徒組成。新加坡人口則包含42%佛教徒，15%穆斯林和5%基督徒。在香港，主要的宗教信徒爲佛教徒佔人口總數21%，11%基督徒和3%穆斯林信徒。 將香港和新加坡進行比較的原因顯而易見（兩地在城市般大小的領土，可控的民主制度， 人口以中國人為主，世俗國家具有相似性）. 馬來西亞則是一個以伊斯蘭教爲國教，以馬來族爲主要民族的大國。另外，這三個地方都曾經受英國殖民統治，有助于多民族、多宗教群體的塑造。 但是自從殖民時代以來，馬來西亞和新加坡就將對民族和宗教多樣性的“管理”作爲其政策的關鍵方面 （盡管有不同的優先事項和結果）。而在香港，在1997年回歸中國後的法律框架中，則只起草了一項關于宗教自由和反民族歧視的法律。鑒于對于亞洲和西方國家來說，宗教間和民族間的關系仍然在政策層面非常重要，對理解法律和社會行爲是如何促進（或者阻礙）一個多樣的並且多元的社會的形成具有重要意義。 圍繞著Michael Peletz關于多元主義即“被賦予合法性”的多元性的觀點，本課題擬就 合法性機構的所依賴的基礎是什麽的問題進行研究。政府是否應該建立一個清晰有力的法律框架用于保護少數公民的權利？公民是否應當通過每個人對差異性的承認和尊重來證明他們的公民精神的成熟？ 本課題的研究目的將通過對關于宗教自由的法律規定和實踐的綜合的深入分析來實現。本課題將利用民族誌素材，訪談和多媒體資源，評估關于多元主義（合法的多元性）的社會實踐。然後這些數據將在歷史角度進行分析，而國家獨立的轉型時期將被予以特別關注。

159313.label: Realisation of objectives
159313.value: Whilst Singapore has advanced a state-directed form of management of diversity (inspired by the core concern of maintaining inter-religious and inter-racial harmony), Malaysia has forsaken such priority in name of retaining a government-directed policy for Malays’ primacy; it is important to note here that although Malay identity is framed as Muslim identity this does not imply that other Muslims (regardless of their racial identity) enjoy the same privileges; similarly, it is not even being bumiputra (indigenous people, “sons of the soil”) that marks Malays as privileged as Sabah-Sarawak bumiputras and peninsular Malaysia’s orang asli are also excluded, unless they convert to Islam. It is thus a combination of ethnic and religious identities that shapes the policy. Although it is a stretch to define Singapore a well-integrated diverse society (i.e. a pluralistic society) - as civil society groups (especially Malay, Indian, and migrants’ groups) frequently point to discrimination - it is out of doubt that Singapore makes a better effort than Malaysia towards achieving some form of national unity. Much should be however said about the stereotyping of ethnic groups (commonly referred to as CMIO - Chinese, Malay, Indian, Others) and their respective religious identities. Such fixities create major complications for those who wish to cross the ‘standardized’ boundaries. Hong Kong is a late comer to the “management of diversity” table as it is still ignoring the issue of population diversification; all policies relevant to “ems” (ethnic minorities) are not targeting social integration (in education, employment accessibility, social mobility, etc) nor catering for their religious needs (limited mosque space, for example) but rather to providing support to access basic social services. In terms of religious freedoms and rights, the fact that Hong Kong’s indigenous population by and large sees and perceives religion as a not-so-important aspect of life influences the way that employers, for example, relate to Indonesian domestic workers’ need for their personal religious performative space. This is reflected in the law, as discrimination on the basis of religious beliefs is not protected in its own right but only as an indirect implication of racial discrimination

159313.label: Major findings and research outcome
159313.value: The research, engaging with the relationship between race and religion, pursued a macro-level analysis of the legal and social status of minorities in Malaysia and Singapore, with a focus on constitutional rights, education policies (civics, religion, and language), acceptance of diversity, and grass-roots initiatives interfacing with diversity within the broader scheme of diversity-related policies (multiculturalism, interfaith dialogue, multiracialism). Singapore, Malaysia and Hong Kong appear to be divided societies. In Singapore inter-racial and inter-religious harmony - often translated as multiracialism, but never understood as multiculturalism or legitimation of differences - is considered necessary for national stability, and thus acceptance is embraced, at least in the public sphere. Malaysia’s increasing distrust of the government - a phenomenon tangible in urban areas and amongst the middle class, educated circles, the same environment in which surveys and “inter-communal” initiatives take place - is also translated in disillusionment towards “multiculturalism”, government policies such as 1Malaysia and calls for national unity as PR stunts. But the Hong Kong administration stands alone in its denial of diversity and the apparent absence of awareness of the stakes involved when ignoring the need for inclusive policies - or at least diversity management. None of the realities investigated depicts an integrated, inclusive, accepting, “pluralistic” society, or a sustainable model of citizenship for nations with a diversified population. But as much as one might dislike Singapore’s micro-managing policies, PAP’s paradigm of forced harmony surfaces as a better stepping stone than segregation, institutionalised hierarchies, and layering (currently present in both Malaysia and Hong Kong, albeit in different degrees). Yet, forced juxtaposition of racial groups (housing, GRCs et al.) should be seen as a means, not an end in itself. The issue of a national language-based education is fraught with contradictions, as it can be seen as either an element for social cohesion and national unity, but also as eradicating local identities. Thinking in terms of religious communities, the shaping of a “neutral” moral education curriculum comprising (updated and verified) materials on all religions present in the territory, a module compulsory for everyone and possibly with exams - so to be taken seriously by pupils and parents alike, but also to undermine the spread of stereotypes - could be a solid first step in instilling knowledge as a tool for understanding and thus a further move towards acceptance. Isn’t citizenship itself a form of social engineering?

159313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
159313.value: This research has stimulated very interesting questions relating to how colonial legacies impact on current policies and how nation-building processes - no matter how distant or near in time - still hold a strong impact on social relations. Much research is still to be done on the ways in which Hong Kong - both in terms of society and government - relates to its diverse minorities, both ethnic ones and religious ones. Besides the narrower scope of Hong Kong’s own development, another interesting case study which is only now emerging as such, is Burma/Myanmar, as there too colonial legacies - and specifically British colonial legacies, as in Singapore, Malaysia and Hong Kong - are playing a key role on the ways in which the newly formed government is managing its ethno-religious minorities.

159313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
159313.value: Hong Kong brands itself as Asia’s World City, but does it mean that anyone will feel at home there? Is diversity celebrated here, or is it treated as a hindrance? This research project has investigated the status of religious minorities in Hong Kong comparatively to Singapore and Malaysia, other two highly diversified societies in the region. The key finding of this research has been that none of these locales seems to have overcome their colonial legacies. The British, in each of these places - and notably also in Burma/Myanmar and India - advanced very structured classification policies based on race and religion; its derivative social layering was reflected in the marginalization of minorities, whether in terms of ethnicity and/or religion, at the time of shaping post-colonial nation-states. Multicultural policies emerged world-wide in the 1970s onwards, and one could understand Singapore’s and Malaysia’s difficulties in absorbing such “western” concepts so early in time, but Hong Kong, which emerged from colonial domination at a later stage, has demonstrated both the disadvantage of having had less time to experiment ways to overcome such marginalization, as well as having missed the opportunity to learn from the mistakes of its cousins, Malaysia and Singapore.

159413.label: Project Objectives
159413.value: To provide a deeper understanding of the socio-legal reasons for the phenomenon of “hospital chaos making” in the context of the Chinese medial negligence dispute resolution system; To expose and analyze the characteristics of the three major ad hoc medical negligence mediation mechanisms operating in China; To examine the quality of the three major ad hoc medical negligence mediation mechanisms in China; To explore the practical constraints that each ad hoc medical negligence mediation mechanism faces in operation in China; To provide the necessary and feasible recommendations to improve the Chinese medical negligence mediation system; To contribute to broad theoretical discourse on alternative dispute resolution in medical negligence and the theory of dispute system design from the socio-legal perspective.

To expose and analyze the characteristics of the three major ad hoc medical negligence mediation mechanisms operating in China;
To examine the quality of the three major ad hoc medical negligence mediation mechanisms in China;
To explore the practical constraints that each ad hoc medical negligence mediation mechanism faces in operation in China;

To contribute to broad theoretical discourse on alternative dispute resolution in medical negligence and the theory of dispute system design from the socio-legal perspective.

159413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
159413.value: Medical negligence disputes become a real and ongoing threat to social stability and social cohesion in China. Improper resolution of medical negligence disputes causes the already frail physician-patient relationship worse in the country. Although litigation is always available to solve medical negligence cases, the Chinese victims of adverse medical events are reluctant to resort to it due to a number of reasons, mainly including low successful rate on the part of the plaintiff, low amount of awarded compensation, high cost in time and expenses, inconsistent and unpredictable judicial decisions. Patient victims are even more reluctant to rely on administrative authority to resolve disputes because they heavily doubt the neutrality of administrative authority given that more than 90 percent of hospitals in China are public and subsidized by the government. Instead, patient victims or their family members commit acts of duress, insult and violence against the alleged negligent health care providers for the purpose of recovering compensation, which is popularly called “hospital chaos making” (Yinao) in China. Since 2005 the hospital chaos making events have increased significantly in number cross the country and become a waking nightmare for the Chinese health care providers. Medical staff in some hospitals even wore helmet at work in order to protect themselves from physical attacks by hospital chaos makers. It is important and imminent to provide an effective alternative dispute resolution system to both patient victims and the alleged negligent health care providers so as to stop hospital chaos making and to prevent the physician-patient relationship from further deteriorating in China. In effect there are mainly three different types of ad hoc medical negligence mediation mechanisms operating in the current China. They are (a) people’s mediation of medical disputes, (b) medical mediation operated by insurance companies, and (c) medical mediation provided by domestic arbitration commission. But how these ad hoc medical negligence mediation mechanisms are running in reality and whether they are able to provide an effective dose to solve medical negligence disputes remain far from clear. This project will perform an empirical legal research into the three ad hoc medical negligence mediation mechanisms in Beijing, Shanghai and Shenzhen to examine their effectiveness and to suggest improvements in resolving medical negligence disputes in China. 当前，医疗过失争端已成为威胁中国社会稳定和团结的现实因素。医疗事故争端的不当处理使得本已脆弱的医患关系更为紧张。尽管诉讼是解决医疗过失案件的通常途径，然而中国医疗不良事件的受害人并不愿意通过诉讼方式解决争端；其主要原因包括原告胜诉机率较小，获得赔偿的数额偏低，诉讼时间和金钱成本较高，以及司法判决缺少统一性和可预见性。受害人更不愿意依赖行政权力来解决医疗过失争端。中国百分之九十以上的医院是获得政府资助的公立医院，受害人极度怀疑行政机构在处理争端时的中立性。因此，医疗不良事件的受害人以及家属往往通过威胁、侮辱、暴力对待医疗服务人员的方式以获得赔偿。这种普遍现象在中国被称为“医闹”。自2005年起，全国范围的医闹事件数量激增，从而成为中国医疗服务人员的噩梦。部分医院的医务人员甚至带着头盔工作，以防止受到医闹者的暴力伤害。为停止医闹、避免医患关系进一步恶化，为医疗不良事件的受害人和被怀疑具有过失的医疗服务人员提供一种有效的争端解决机制，既迫切、又重要。 当前中国存在三类医疗过失调解机制，即医疗过失争端的人民调解、保险公司主持的医疗过失调解、及仲裁机构下设的医疗过失调解。然而这三种医疗过失调解机制在实践中是如何运行的、它们是否能够成为解决医疗过失争端的有效途径，仍不明朗。本研究项目拟对北京、上海、深圳的三种不同的医疗过失调解机制进行法律实证研究，以探究各种机制的有效性、并且提出改进中国医疗过失争端调解机制的具体方案。

159413.label: Realisation of objectives
159413.value: The project objectives have been achieved as my publication under the project thoroughly discusses the features of the three major medical mediation mechanisms operating in China and the main functions that the medical mediation system is intended to play in the context of Chinese intense doctor-patient relationship. The effectiveness and quality of medical mediation in practice are analysed and assessed in detail. Moreover, suggestions for improving Chinese medical mediation are provided for further consideration by lawmakers and health administrations. The publications have been shared with some local legislatures and health administrations of Mainland China.

159413.label: Major findings and research outcome
159413.value: The major findings include but not limited to the characteristics of the three major models of medical mediation operating in the current China and the socio-legal reasons for them, that is, all medical mediations indeed share the common aims to cope with the phenomenon of “hospital chaos making” and a very intense relationship between physicians and patients in the setting of medical negligence disputes in China. The research also finds that Chinese medical mediation mechanisms are deliberately designed to achieve such aims, which renders medical mediation in China different and unique compared to the counterpart in other jurisdictions. The research also finds out a number of weaknesses and practical problems arising from the practice of medical mediation and suggests that mediator quality and selection, mediation process, assistance of experts, quality of mediatory intervention and participation of the insurers are five aspects that the future reform of Chinese medical mediation system should focus and address.

159413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
159413.value: Potentially, this project can be developed by looking into how medical liability insurers can play a more active and efficient role in resolving medical negligence disputes in China and provide legal reform proposals in this regard.

159413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
159413.value: Medical negligence disputes and medical chaos have been a serious socio-legal problem in China. This project comprehensively discusses three different models of medical mediation mechanism operating in the current China and evaluates their functions in dealing with medical chaos and improving the doctor-patient relationship. More importantly, this project analyses the practical problems arising from the practice of medical mediation and provides suggestions for improvement. The findings of the project not only helps various stakeholders to have a better understanding of the current Chinese medical mediation system, but also provides the lawmakers and health administrations with useful suggestions for legal reform of the medical mediation system in China.

159613.label: Project Objectives
159613.value: To document through visual and ethnographic means Tai Hang’s residences in terms of space, material, aesthetics, and behavior. To map diverse household practices and ideals relative to diverse types of domestic spaces. To unravel materiality’s expression of and support of divergent household practices and ideals.
rows: To document through visual and ethnographic means Tai Hang’s residences in terms of space, material, aesthetics, and behavior.
To map diverse household practices and ideals relative to diverse types of domestic spaces.
To unravel materiality’s expression of and support of divergent household practices and ideals.

159613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
159613.value: In recent decades, Hong Kong has experienced significant changes in housing with concurrent economic development and cultural, societal, and demographic shifts. Scholars (Bourdieu, 1979; Miller, 1997; Silva, 2010; Daniels, 2010) have established that ethnography of domestic architecture, material culture and practices is a fruitful way of analyzing values and power: gender and kinship relations in family, the change of ideology, the dictates of property developers and the government, and objects’ power in framing our worldview and shaping everyday practices. Nevertheless, local studies on housing have not yet adequately addressed the underlying dynamic relationships among materiality, agency, and power, and have tended to limit their focus to architecture and design (Rooney, 2003; Lee, 2010), realist photographic representations of homes (Wu & Canham, 2009; Wolf, 2009; Choy, 2010) and historical overviews of Hong Kong housing (Leung, 1999; Yeung & Wong, 2003). No one to date has used visual ethnography to examine the relationships among materiality, agency, and power in Hong Kong’s domestic spaces, where residents engage in dialectical processes of “making” home. To help fill this research gap, the current study uses a visual-ethnographic perspective to examine relationships among materiality, individual agency, and social relations in domestic spaces in Tai Hang. Tai Hang, a small area sandwiched between Causeway Bay and Tin Hau, is notable for its different types of residential buildings: late 19th-century Hakka stone houses, pre-war tong lau (“tenement houses”), post-war tong lau, multi-story public-housing estates, and affluent high-rise residences. These dwellings’ structural properties vary significantly in their physical dimensions, spatial organization, and aesthetic characteristics, expressing and supporting Tai Hang residents’ wide range of life-styles. In documenting through visual and ethnographic means Tai Hang’s residences in terms of architecture, material, space, aesthetics, and behavior, this study seeks to (1) map diverse household patterns, practices, and ideals relative to diverse types of domestic spaces visually and ethnographically; and (2) unravel materiality’s expression of and support of divergent household patterns and ideals. The current study mainly uses visual ethnographic methods, including photo-taking, photo-elicitation interviews, interviews, observation, and participatory photography and video recording of Tai Hang residents’ everyday practices. Ethnographic methods are employed to study residents’ ideas, values, and emotional sentiments of “home” and their everyday behavior in context. 經濟、文化和社會不斷發展變更，香港的居住環境也隨著整個社會結構一直改變。學者們(Bourdieu, 1979; Miller, 1997; Silva, 2010; Daniels, 2010) 認為，藉著觀察研究一個地方的居住建築、物質文化與家庭裡的行為模式，我們可以了解社會的權力分怖、價值觀、家庭裡的性別親屬關係、意識影態的改變、地產發展商和政府的運作。然而，過去有關本地住屋的研究，大多關注於香港的住屋歷史 (Leung, 1999; Yeung & Wong, 2003) ，住宅建築和設計方面(視覺上)的探討(Rooney, 2003; Lee, 2010) ，及用寫實的影像呈現出來 (Wu & Canham, 2009; Wolf, 2009; Choy, 2010) ，並未有人用影像民族誌的形式去探討物質、個體與社會的互動關係，及港人如何以物質建構｢家｣的感覺、理念與價值觀，及相關的日常家居生活行為。 為了填補之前研究的空白，是次研究將以影像民族誌的形式，研究大坑的住宅，從而了解物質、個體與社會的互動關係。大坑位處銅鑼灣和天后之間，是一個住宅建築極多樣化的小區，如：建於十九世紀的客家石屋、戰前或戰後唐樓、公共屋邨以至高密度豪宅，也能在大坑找到。這些不同年代興建、不同住宅空間佈置、及不同建築特色的住宅，為大坑帶來多樣化的生活方式。 本研究主要使用影像記錄及田野工作的方法，包括：拍照、圖片引述訪談、訪問、觀察、錄像拍攝去記錄大坑住宅及居民的家居生活，從而分析1)家庭的模式、運作及觀念，與居住環境的關係; 及2) 物質如何呈現及支持不同生活模式及價值觀。

159613.label: Realisation of objectives
159613.value: Objective 1: to document through visual and ethnographic means Tai Hang’s residences in terms of space, material, aesthetics, and behavior. 100% achieved. Since the study aims to explore respondents’ experiences over their dwelling environment, domestic ideals they embrace, the ways they make home, as well as their everyday home-making and domestic practices, I used different methods to explore residents’ activities, meanings and senses over Tai Hang plain as a dwelling environment and their homes. As a resident of Tai Hang for six years, I regularly sat down in residents’ favorite sitting arrangement along Wun Sha Street to observe residents’ acts and to converse with them. I contacted Tai Hang Residents’ Welfare Association and held a semi-structured group interview with seven Tai Hang long-term residents there. In the interview, one had provided particularly rich information and he became one of the respondents of the individual interview and home visits. Other respondents were recruited through mailing invitation letters, referrals and snowball methods. In total, the study was conducted with 12 households, with a total of 22 respondents. I did home visits and asked respondents to introduce their home and home activities; I conducted semi-structured interviews with respondents in their home about their housing history, their past and present experiences of living in Tai Hang, their perception of dwelling environment quality, their future housing option, the choice of the particular housing type for dwelling, the length of living in present dwelling unit and the changes (including space rearrangement and major renovation) made, the idea of aspired ideal home, home décor, and the everyday home-making practices, etc. Informants then gave home tours, which are filmed, during which we talked about spatial and objects arrangement, home décor and domestic practices. Informants also introduced their precious objects and their lived practices, such as the consultation of feng shui (Wang, Joy, Sherry, 2013), etc. In cases where permission was given, informants’ daily domestic lives were also observed. I also used walk-along methods to walk through some respondents’ favorite places in Tai Hang. The choice of using unstructured interviews and walk-along methods in addition to semi-structured interviews (group and individual) is because the individualized descriptions used by respondents cannot be found in quantitative research. To visually document the respondents’ residences faithfully, the data will be put on a web archive (in both Chinese and English), including a section on Tai Hang housing history to provide contextual background to the research. The main framework of the web archive was built and details of all individual cases were uploaded. The website titled "Making Home: Tai Hang" address is: http://taihang.scm.cityu.edu.hk/#tc A manuscript about the methodological issues of visual ethnography and the design rationale of the website was submitted to the renowned international journal Qualitative Research. For details, please refer to the submitted manuscript titled “Engaged Critical Browsing: Hong Kong Home Culture Presented in Hypermedia” in the section “Research Output.” The website Making Home: Tai Hang has also been selected and featured in two festivals: 1. the renowned IDFA DocLab Online Database (http://www.doclab.org/2016/making-home-a-visual-ethnography-of-tai-hang-domestic-space/). 2. International Image Festival, XII Media Art Monographic Show, 9-13 May 2016 at Centro Cultural y de Convenciones Teatro los Fundadores. http://www.festivaldelaimagen.com/en/2016/129-versiones-anteriores/2016/3332-mediaart-2016 Please refer to “Research Outputs” for details. Objective 2: To map diverse household practices and ideals relative to diverse types of domestic spaces. 100% achieved. The study was conducted with 12 households, with a total of 22 respondents. Out of these 12 households, four are long-term residents (lived in the area for over 30 years); four are mid-term residents (8-12 years); and four are newer residents (around or less than 6 years). They also live in diverse private housing types: one in pre-1930s tong lau, three in post-WWII tong lau, two in 8-12 storey buildings, and six in high-rises (two in the plain and four up the hills). Besides the different building types, the respondents are living in different household types (single household, couples without children, nuclear family, and extended family) of various lengths (from two years to more than 60 years since they were born), and different forms of housing (nine are owners and three are renters). Respondents also vary in age (household head from thirty-something to seventy-something) and monthly income (from HKD 2,390 taken from Old Age Living Allowance under the Social Security Allowance Scheme to over HKD 200,000). I integrated Gibson’s affordances and Bourdieu’s habitus and explore parents’ ideas about learning and leisure and the actual domestic leisure children (between three to seven years old) consume in association with socioeconomic status. It is found that parent informants have similar reservations about local education regardless of socioeconomic status. Nevertheless, their different socioeconomic and cultural backgrounds contribute to their different involvement in children’s learning and leisure through their use of the domestic setup, television and computing devices, and toys. Materials at home are indicative of the respondents’ daily life and projected values. For example, parents from middle-class nuclear families strongly prefer developing their children’s reading habits over watching TV, and they therefore either opt for additional power switches on the TV set or forego a TV set altogether, in order to limit the children’s access to television programs. Through leisure, middle-class parent informants transmit certain emotions, values, skills, behavioral dispositions, and tastes to their children, which coincide with institutional approaches to learning. The study finds that children’s domestic leisure is largely patterned by materials (domestic setup and leisure-induced appliances), practices (TV and mobile computing usage and toy selection and play) and social structure, and thus links considerably to children’s disparity in academic achievements and attitudes towards learning. The paper titled “Habitus, affordances, and family leisure: Cultural reproduction through children’s leisure activities” was published in the international journal Ethnography. Objective 3: to unravel materiality’s expression of and support of divergent household practices and ideals. 100% achieved. Using an agential realist approach, I analyzed three cases of older women’s homes and their material-discursive practices at home diffractively. The three older women live in diverse private housing—pre-war tong lau, post-war tong lau, and a modern building. I argue that the entanglement of materialities, discourses, and subjectivities in home as a site of cultural action contributes to Hong Kong older women’s divergent subjectivities. I wrote a manuscript and I argued that three homes’ structural-spatial configurations materialize Hong Kong’s patrilineal and male-dominated family system and these three older women also perform a set of (house)wifely duties that link to the maintenance of the male-dominated family system. Nevertheless, the material-discursive configuration of home enfolds with other mundane but significant discursive-material agential actors, such as clutter, and the entanglement produces conditions of possibilities, though exclusionary, for reconfiguring older women’s contested and disunified performances and subjectivities. The manuscript titled “Home and the Materialization of Older Women’s Divergent Subjectivities in Hong Kong” was submitted to the journal Journal of Gender Studies (see the section research output).

159613.label: Major findings and research outcome
159613.value: The visual ethnographic research analyzes power in relation to materiality (these homes’ structural-spatial configurations) and social structure, and the study produces the following research outputs. First, the study integrates Gibson’s affordances and Bourdieu’s habitus and finds that children’s domestic leisure is largely patterned by materials (domestic setup and leisure-induced appliances), practices (TV and mobile computing usage and toy selection and play) and social structure, and thus links considerably to children’s disparity in academic achievements and attitudes towards learning. The paper titled “Habitus, affordances, and family leisure: Cultural reproduction through children’s leisure activities” was published in the journal Ethnography. Second, I use agential realist approach to analyze three older women’s homes and their material-discursive practices diffractively and provide a fresh angle on the study of home culture. The three homes’ structural-spatial configurations materialize Hong Kong’s patrilineal and male-dominated family system, and these older women also perform a set of “normal” (house)wifely/motherly duties that link to the maintenance of the male-dominated family system. Nevertheless, the material-discursive configuration of home enfolds with other mundane but significant discursive-material agential actors, such as clutter, and the entanglement produces conditions of possibilities, though exclusionary, for reconfiguring older women’s contested and disunified performances and subjectivities. The manuscript titled “Home and the Materialization of Older Women’s Divergent Subjectivities in Hong Kong” was submitted to Journal of Gender Studies. Third, ethnography is also a process of creating and representing knowledge about society, culture and individuals. I create a website “Making Home: Tai Hang” (http://taihang.scm.cityu.edu.hk/index.php#en) to represent research findings. By representing participants’ domestic world through four layers of interpretation (splash and introductory pages, panoramic photography, audio vignettes of participants-researchers’ micro-narratives on objects, and database), employing specific media, and utilizing multiple interconnections among media via hypermedia applications on our website, I aim to produce engaging yet critical and reflexive ethnographic knowledge on Hong Kong home culture and hypermedia knowledge representation. The manuscript titled “Engaged Critical Browsing: Hong Kong Home Culture Presented in Hypermedia” was submitted to Qualitative Research. Fourth, the website Making Home: Tai Hang was selected and featured in two festivals: 1. IDFA DocLab Online Database (http://www.doclab.org/2016/making-home-a-visual-ethnography-of-tai-hang-domestic-space/). 2. International Image Festival, XII Media Art Monographic Show, 9-13 May 2016 at Centro Cultural y de Convenciones Teatro los Fundadores. http://www.festivaldelaimagen.com/en/2016/129-versiones-anteriores/2016/3332-mediaart-2016

159613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
159613.value: In studying home cultures in Tai Hang, it is found that older women from different sociocultural background perform roles as homemakers and caretakers if they live with family members, and enjoy little family support if they live alone. However, no local research has researched on the relationship between older women’s subjectivity and home culture. Further research should therefore be done on this aspect. The home environment can be further analyzed, especially Tai Hang is experiencing gentrification. The concept of gentrification has evolved for fifty years. As a process of class neighborhood upgrading, local literature describes effects of gentrification and residents’ different meanings of gentrification. Recently, some local groups organize community activities and artists do socially engaged works with non-government organizations to enhance residents’ sense of community in the process of gentrification. Further research can be done to explore these activities.

159613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
159613.value: “Making Home: A Visual Ethnography of Tai Hang Domestic Space” is a visual ethnographic research about “homes” in Tai Hang. In Tai Hang, there are different types of residential buildings (pre-war tong lau, post-war tong lau, and high-rise affluent residences). The research studies Tai Hang domestic space visually and ethnographically. The research intersects visual ethnography, material culture, family studies, Hong Kong culture and web archiving, which have not been done by any local research. The study finds that: (1) finds that children’s domestic leisure is largely patterned by materials (domestic setup and leisure-induced appliances), practices (TV and mobile computing usage and toy selection and play) and social structure, and thus links considerably to children’s disparity in academic achievements and attitudes towards learning; (2) the entanglement of material-discursive configuration reconfigure older women’s contested and disunified performances and subjectivities; (3) the study creates a website “Making Home: Tai Hang” (http://taihang.scm.cityu.edu.hk/index.php#en) to produce engaging yet critical and reflexive ethnographic knowledge on Hong Kong home culture via hypermedia applications on the website.

160013.label: Realisation of objectives
160013.value: 17α-ethinylestradiol (EE2), a synthetic pharmaceutical compound, is present ubiquitously in sediments and aquatic ecosystems worldwide. EE2 is chemically similar to the natural female sex hormone 17 β-estradiol (E2) and mimic biological actions of E2. Given that EE2 is a potent E2 agonist and more stable in water as compared to the synthetic E2, EE2 (Cat. No. E4876, Sigma-Aldrich Pty. Ltd) was used to replace E2 as representative estrogen endocrine disruptive chemical (EEDC) for the exposure experiments. For Objective 1 (completed), a range finding study was first conducted to determine the effective sublethal concentrations of EE2 using the established fish model Oryzias melastigma. The findings support the use of two environmental realistic EE2 concentration at 33ng/l (low) and 113 ng/l (high) to evaluate the concomitant impacts of EE2 on immune competence and reproduction in both male and female medaka. (1) Three sets of EE2 exposure experiments were conducted, considering sex-specific induction, adaptive and recovery responses on immune suppression (immune marker gene expression, leukocyte numbers, host resistance assay HRA, and immune competence index ICI) alongside with reproductive impairment (estrogen responsive gene expression, fecundity, fertilization success, hatching success, and reproductive competence index RCI) in medaka in vivo. (2) Experiment 1 was aimed to determine if short term exposure (7 days) to EE2 could induce immunosuppression and reproductive impairment in fish. Experiment 2 was aimed to determine if EE2 induced immunosuppression and reproduction impairment were persistent or adaptive during chronic exposure to EE2 (21 days). Experiment 3 was aimed to study recovery of fish immune function and reproductive performance after depuration (7 days) from long term EE2 exposure. (3) Host resistant assay (HRA) against pathogenic bacteria E. tarda was conducted for experimental fish according to the standard operating procedures described in Ye et al. (2016). Plasma and liver were sampled from both the EE2 and CTL fish (for all the three experiments) (i) prior to and (ii) 3 days after bacteria injection, which are equivalent to the immune resting state and immune active state, respectively. Liver samples were used for molecular analyses (genes/proteins) and measurement of leukocyte abundance (see objective 2 below). Post infection fish mortality was monitored for 14 days and fish survival were compared between EE2 and control groups for both male and female, separately. (4) The immune competence index (ICI) was calculated based on the survival curve date obtained in HRA for determination of the hazard ratio (HR), using the well-established Cox Proportional Hazard model. The EE2 group (33 or 113 ng/L) was set as the covariate for the different sex and experimental regime. The ICI was calculated as the reciprocal value of the HR (EE2 group versus control group) in Ye et al 2018; where “EE2” is specific EE2 group contrasting to control, sex is either male or female fish; when -1 < delta ICI < 0: fish in the EE2 group have higher immune competence compared to the control; when 0 < delta ICI < 1: fish in the EE2 group have lower immune competence compared to the control; when delta ICI = 0: all groups show a similar immune competence. (5) The reproductive competence index (RCI) was developed to indicate reproduction performance of EE2-exposed fish relative to the control fish, considering the key reproduction endpoints that could potential affect the number of F1 offspring. The RCI of EE2-exposed male fish was calculated based on fertilization success and hatching success. The RCI of EE2-exposed female fish was calculated based on fecundity and hatching success using the formula derived in Ye et al 2018; where FC is the fecundity, FS is the fertilization success and H is the hatching success at the time point when the control group reached a hatching success ≥ 90% to take a potential delay in hatching into consideration; “i” is the day of experiment, “j” is the EE2 treatment group, “ct” is the control group, “d” is equal to 3, the three days (d1 to d3) when eggs were collected for calculation of RCI at each time point: (i) D7: day 6-8; (ii) D21: day 19-21; (iii) D28: day 26-28; when -1< delta RCI < 0: fish in the EE2 group have higher reproductive function compare to the control; when 0 < delta RCI < 1: fish in the EE2 group have lower reproductive function compared to the control; when delta RCI = 0: all groups show a similar reproductive function. For Objective 2 (completed), in addition to studying change of C3 gene/protein, the central component of the complement system, as stated in the original proposal, additional hepatic immune genes (NGS and RT-qPCR) and plasma immune proteins (proteomic analysis) were included to provide a comprehensive understanding on the underlying molecular pathways. A further step was taken to unravel the cleavage cascade of C3 in medaka plasma and its response to EE2 exposure as well as bacterial challenge. Moreover, the immunomodulatory action of EE2 on medaka was further assessed by change of blood leukocytes (lymphocytes and granulocytes abundance) using DiOC6(3) staining and flow cytometry. (1) A total of 18 key immune system activation genes in the liver of male and female marine medaka were identified by next generation sequencing NGS (Ye et al., 2016). These genes were grouped into (i) “immune receptors” (7 genes) to detect pathogens, (ii) “immune mediators” (5 genes) to induce multiple humoral and cellular immune responses and (iii) “immune effectors” (6 genes) to resist and eliminate the invasion of pathogens (2) High EE2 concentration exposure could significantly suppress multiple immune genes in male and female medaka (the immune resting state, without bacteria challenge). Yet, no fish mortality was found in both sublethal EE2 levels (33 ng/L and 113 ng/L EE2), indicating that the EE2-induced gene expression changes were not lethal in the absence of pathogens. (3) The detrimental impact of EE2 on fish survival was augmented rapidly upon bacterial infection (the immune activated state), particularly in male fish. The suppression of immune genes at the immune activated stage can be directly link to elevated post infection fish mortality. (4) Two modes of EE2-induced deregulation of immune gene expression have been identified in this study: (i) EE2-induced deregulation of immune genes during the immune resting state, which was maintained upon bacterial infection. This comprises the immune receptor tlr3 in both sexes and five genes (immune receptor tlr5, tlr5s; immune mediator c3, myd88; immune effector lyz) in male fish. (ii) EE2-induced deregulation of immune genes at the activated immune state only. This was only seen for the two immune effector genes hep1 and hep2 (downregulated) upon high EE2 exposure in male fish. (5) For C3 and other key immune proteins analysis, a two-dimension gel electrophoresis (2DE) and nanoLC-tandem mass spectrometry (MS) protocol was developed to screen, identify and quantify plasma proteins for fish (Dong et al., 2017a). While the abundance of C3 protein species was not different between male and female medaka, the exposure of both sexes to EE2 induced a redistribution of C3 fragments, cleavage and post-translational modification of C3 could be altered by EE2 treatment in males (C3dg down; C3g up) (Dong et al 2017b).

160013.label: Major findings and research outcome
160013.value: The present study investigated sex-specific immunomodulatory action of EE2 alongside with reproductive impairment in medaka. Female fish (with a high endogenous E2) exhibited a non-monotonous response to EE2 exposure. A low concentration of EE2 (33 ng/L) could induce hormesis (immune enhancement), enable adaptation (restored reproduction) and even boost females resistance to bacterial challenge after abatement of EE2. However, a prolonged exposure to high concentration EE2 (113 ng/L) not only impaired immune function, but also perturbed females recovering from reproductive impairment, resulting in a persistent impact on the F1 generation output. Thus, for female fish, the EE2 exposure concentration (not the EE2 dose) is most critical in determining the impacts of EE2 in vivo. Conversely, male fish (with low endogenous E2) are far more sensitive than females to the presence of low levels of exogenous EE2 in water. A dose-dependent relationship was distinct for EE2-mediated biological responses (ICI and RCI). It was also evident in male fish that direct contact of EE2 is essential to sustain impairments of immune competence and reproductive output as well as deregulation of hepatic immune genes in vivo. Downregulation of C3 and TLR3 (both sexes) and TLR5 together with lymphocytes reduction (in male) were directly associated with enhanced post-infection fish mortality in EE2 exposed fish. Proteomic analysis also revealed highly sexually dimorphic plasma immune proteins in medaka. EE2 induced pronounced sex-specific changes in the plasma proteome, with the male plasma composition clearly becoming “feminised”. In male fish, reduction of C3dg was the only C3 cascade component which was responsive to the EE2-treatment alone and in the combined EE2 and bacterial infection treatment. The plasma of female fish in response to the combined treatment was characterized by a stronger decrease of C3 intermediate b-chain proteins and increased quantities of the C3/C3b protein compared to the EE2- or bacteria-treatment individually. Furthermore, expression of plasma C1q subunit B (C1Q), an initiating factor of the classical complement pathway, was found higher in males and was suppressed in both sexes in response to EE2 and bacterial challenge. The findings shed light on potential development of immune biomarkers (i.e. C3, TLR3 genes and C1Q, C3 protein breakdown products) for early diagnosis/prognosis of immunotoxicants in fish, which are useful for environmental monitoring and aquaculture management. The present study highlights the importance of a parallel evaluation of immune function and reproduction in fish (both sexes, separately) when assessing the risk EE2/EEDCs in aquatic ecosystem.

160013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
160013.value: The present study has substantiated the detrimental impacts of EE2 on immune competence of directly exposed F0 individuals and reproductive output of F1 in fish. Further development and validation of immune biomarkers identified in this study are needed, which is highly meaningful and useful for environmental monitoring and aquaculture management. Recent studies in mammals and fish have reported that ancestral exposure to environmental estrogens (including EE2) could impair reproductive fitness of offspring beyond F1 to F3. Based on the current findings, parallel assessment of EE2/EEDCs induced immune dysfunction alongside with reproductive impairment should be further investigated in multigenerational scale (beyond F3) to evaluate the potential long term impacts of EEDCs in the environment. It is scientifically significant to decipher the impact of ancestral paternal and maternal exposure to EE2 on transgenerational reproductive and/or immune impairments in the unexposed offspring (≥ F3). A systematic and comprehensive study is needed to determine the critical windows and EE2 exposure scenarios that can trigger multigenerational impairments of reproduction and/or immune function in the unexposed offspring in F3 and beyond. The underlying genetic and epigenetic mechanisms should be explored.

160013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
160013.value: This study is the first to demonstrate sex-specific immunomodulatory action of EE2 alongside with reproductive impairment in fish (vertebrates). In females, a low concentration of EE2 (33ng/L) could induce immune enhancement, enable adaptation (reproduction) and even boost fish resistance to bacterial challenge after abatement of EE2. A prolonged exposure to high concentration EE2 (113ng/L) not only impaired female immune function, but also resulted an irreversible decrease of F1 reproductive output. Conversely, males (with low endogenous estrogen) were more sensitive than females to exogenous EE2 and responded to EE2 in a dose-dependent manner. Moreover, direct contact of EE2 is essential to sustain impairments of immune competence and reproduction as well as deregulation of hepatic immune genes in males. Conceivably, impaired immune competence poses an immediate treat on the survival of F0 population, while impaired reproduction can directly affect F1 output. The present findings highlight the importance of concomitant evaluation of immune competence and reproduction in fish (both sexes separately) when assessing the long-term risk of EE2/EEDC in aquatic environments. Furthermore, a suite of hepatic immune genes (C3, TLR3) and plasma proteins (C3, C1Q) were identified, characterized and quantified, which are potential molecular biomarkers of immune impairment in fish.
