160213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
160213.value: Heart diseases such as myocardial infarction (MI) and ischaemic heart disease affect millions of patients worldwide. The damaged myocardium becomes necrotic, forms a noncontractile scar which integrates poorly with the remaining myocardium, and leads to poor recovery. Hence the formation and degradation of scars represent potential targets for therapeutic interventions. Tremendous efforts have been made to find out how to unlock the regenerative capacity of the mammalian heart and develop effective cell-based therapies for treating heart diseases. Encouraging reports have shown that neonatal mice possess robust ability to regenerate, new cardiomyocytes can be derived either from endogenous cardiac myocytes or from a noncardiac myocyte progenitor population such as the epicardium. However, before we can achieve the ultimate goal of functional recovery, we need to overcome three hurdles, namely, the inadequate number of newly formed cardiomyocytes, the persistence of a collagenous scar and the lack of neovascularization. These processes are potentially interlinked because the damaged heart needs to maintain the mechanical barrier and perform its physiological function. Zebrafish possesses unparalleled ability to regenerate the complete heart following scar forming injuries. Work on the anatomical, cellular and molecular events in this model organism has identified the formation of new cardiomyocytes from the intact part of the heart, and the importance of the epicardium which envelops the heart. My laboratory has identified a mutant line of zebrafish which shows a delay in the regenerative process, and also shares important features with mammalian heart repair. This mutant line offers an opportunity for us to investigate two potentially interlinked events, namely, the degradation of the collagenous scar and the formation of a conducive environment in the injured site for the repopulation by newly formed cardiomyoctyes. This unique animal model offers the potential to test drugs which can accelerate these two important processes, and thereby opening new therapeutic targets for the awakening of regenerative potential in adult human hearts.

160213.label: Realisation of objectives
160213.value: The formation and degradation of scars represent potential targets for therapeutic interventions in humans. In this project, we have focused on the zebrafish mutant Breakdance as a suitable animal model to develop potential strategies to enhance the degradation of scar and the epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). The zebrafish mutant Breakdance is one of the most reported mutants on the erg (ether-a-go-go-related) gene and presents an AV block and LQST in the embryonic stage. We previously observed delayed heart regeneration in this mutant while the wild type zebrafish completed heart regeneration following cryoinjury and resolved the collagenous scar almost entirely. In this project, we used the bre mutant to decipher the dynamics between the arrival of newly formed cardiomyoctyes in the neovascularised subepicardial region and the progressive degradation of the collagenous scar. We have found unexpected difference between the enzymatic activities, transcription and protein levels of matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) in the Breakdance mutants and the wild type zebrafish. In other words, we found that the Breakdance mutant has lower levels of enzymatic activities, less transcriptions and translations of the MMPs. We have completed the three objectives in the zebrafish Breakdance mutant by assessing the scar degradation, the epicardial EMT and neovascularization, and screened for known drugs such as cisapride in accelerating the scar degradation and EMT processes. In addition, we have developed an improved methodology of surface ECG recording and reported QTc values of Breakdance as 572ms. In addition, our improved version of surface ECG showed that bradycardia occurred in Breakdance with a heart rate of 87.4 bpm and indicated the lower cardiomyocyte excitability due to ion channel disorder. Instead of a 2:1 AV block in the embryonic Breakdance, we found that the mutation on the potassium ion channel did not affect atrial ventricular conduction in the Breakdance adults. Our work describes the cardiophysiology of this adult mutant and facilities the study of human congenital LQTS and the function of ion channels in heart regeneration. In order to isolate the defects of the potassium channels from the observed MMP abnormalities, we mimicked the Breakdance conditions in the wild type by first using a broad spectrum MMP inhibitor GM6001. Surprisingly, we found the heart regeneration process is delayed when MMP activities have been inhibited during the first 7 days post-cryoinjury, when the inflammatory process is taking place while the process of tissue remodelling has yet to initiate. We then designed experiments based on what is known about the roles MMPs in inflammation to decipher the specific roles of MMPs in the process of inflammation and resolution. First, we have established the dynamics of leukocyte recruitment in the injured areas. We detected the recruitment of neutrophils and macrophages (as determined by the k-values using a transgenic zebrafish fish Tg(coro1a:EGFP; lyz:dsREd) kindly provided by Zilong Wen from HKUST. The fastest recruitment of neutrophils happened during the first 0.5 days post cryoinjury (dpc) while the second fastest recruitment period happened between 0.5 to 1.0 dpc. In other words, the peak of recruitment of neutrophils happened within the first 24 hours after cryoinjury of the heart. The dynamics of the macrophage recruitment shared a similar pattern. The numbers of neutrophils and macrophages, both peaked at 1 dpc, declined on the next 7 days to reach the basal values. Interestingly, the transcription of the chemokine genes cxcl8 and ccl2 also peaked at 1 dpc and returned to basal level by 4 dpc. To verify the importance of the chemokines in this model of MMP-inhibited heart regeneration, we used recombinant CXCL8 and CCL2 proteins to rescue the delay in heart regeneration. We found that the combined actions of recombinant chemokines could rescue the the inhibition of leukocyte recruitment and delay in the resolution of the collagen scars in zebrafish treated with the MMP inhibitor GM6001. Using specific inhibitors of different MMPs on their respective actions to modify the dynamics of leukocyte recruitment in the cryoinjured hearts, we have identified the pair of MMPs involved are MMP-9 (a gelatinise) and MMP-13 (a collagenase). We then prepared recombinant CXCL8 and CCL2 proteins and investigated the enzymatic digestions of these two chemokines by the zebrafish MMP-9 and MMP-13/ We found that MMP-9 and MMP-13 both cleaved the CXCL8 at the same site. More importantly, the digested CXCL8 chemokine has a higher chemotactic activity than the intact counterparts in an in vivo and an intro models of leukocyte recruitment. To our surprise, there is no cleave site for MMP-9 and MMP-13 in the recombinant CCL2. This observation shows a key difference between zebrafish and mammals, as MMP-cleage of CCL2 in mammals will inactivate this chemokine. In other words, the lack of MMP-cleavage sites in the zebrafish CCL2, resulting in the lack of inactivation despite the increased MMP enzymatic activities, will mean that the recruitment of macrophages will be sustained in the injured area.

160213.label: Major findings and research outcome
160213.value: Our first publication on the improved surface ECG methodology has shown that the mutation on the potassium ion channel did not affect atrial ventricular conduction in the Breakdance adults. Nonetheless, we have established a useful methodology to enable us to correlate the observed cardio physiology with the various stages of heart regeneration in wild type and mutant zebrafish adults. This enabling technology can be easily implemented by other laboratories. Our second publication on MMPs has several novel findings. 1) The requirement of MMPs during the inflammatory phase of heart regeneration (as shown by broad spectrum inhibitors) leukocyte recruitment represents one of the mechanisms of MMP-mediated heart regeneration (as shown by our rescue experiments using exogenous chemokines) 2) the specific requirement for MMP9 (a gelatinase) and MMP13 (a collagenase) during the inflammatory phase (as demonstrated by the use of a specific MMP9/13 inhibitor) 3) the first demonstration of MMP9 and MMP13 cleaving and activating CXCL8 in zebrafish 4) the lack of an MMP cleavage site in zebrafish CCL2, which is unlike its mammalian counterpart. In summary, we believe that we have identified previously unreported roles of MMPs in mediating leukocyte recruitment in the first phase of zebrafish heart regeneration. In other words, we have contributed to the mechanistic understanding on the difference between a vertebrate model of heart regeneration. More importantly, the process of inflammation and leukocyte recruitment have many identifiable drug targets and could well have FDA approved drugs for this aspects. Our work described here will hopefully add to the arsenal of drugs for the better management of cardiovascular patients.

160213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
160213.value: Our work on the improved surface ECG methodology is versatile and robust. It describes the cardiophysiology of this adult mutant and facilities the study of human congenital LQTS and the function of ion channels in heart regeneration. The open access format of publication will make this methodology an enabling tool for the community to use. In other words, correlating electrophysiology with various treatment regimens will help scientists to improve on the screening of cardiac drugs. More importantly, our methodology can enable the community to better detect cardiac toxicities from drugs or pollutants. We have shown the importance of chemokines and inflammation in rescuing observed delays in heart regeneration. This represents a less well known aspect on the management of cardiovascular patients. Currently, many patients with cardiovascular diseases are concurrently treated with inflammatory drugs. We hope that our observation will inform clinical studies such that we can improve on patient management.

160213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
160213.value: Using zebrafish mutants with heart abnormalities, we have deciphered the important interactions between two important processes, namely the inflammatory and tissue remodelling processes. With an elaborate range of experiments, we have identified the specific enzymes and the specific chemokines involved. More importantly, we have reported, for the first time, a key difference in the dynamics of leukocyte recruitment during the inflammatory phases of zebrafish and mammalian. In our hands, we have shown that the lack of enzymatic cleavage site in the zebrafish chemokine CCL2, preventing this chemokine being inactivated by enzymatic activates, might explain the difference in the leukocyte recruitment and dispersal in the zebrafish and mammals. We envision this mechanistic difference between the zebrafish and mammals can help other scientists and clinicians to develop novel strategies of cell-based therapy by augmenting the endogenous repair with combinatorial treatment of cellular and chemical interventions. This proposal will lay the foundation of a novel concept of regenerative medicine, whereby the endogenous tissue process is being treated as bioreactors to drive the recruitment and dispersal of leukocytes during the inflammatory and resolution phases of the cardiac repair. As many patients with cardiovascular diseases also require inflammatory drugs, our data might support patient management too.

160513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
160513.value: The assessment of population exposure to selected environmental contaminants is crucial to the understanding of their risk posed on public health. Environmental endocrine disrupting chemicals (EDCs) have aroused particular concerns around the world as a number of these compounds, e.g. bisphenol-A (BPA) and tetrabromobisphenol-A (TBBPA), are ubiquitously present in our daily appliances. The conventional way of estimating the extent of population exposure to contaminants via measuring their levels in human tissues is resource-demanding and difficult to carry out. A new approach has emerged in recent years that analyzes drug residuals in municipal wastewater to assess the usage (and abuse) of pharmaceuticals in the community within the wastewater catchment. This concept of Sewage Chemical-Information Mining (SCIM) has greatly simplified community-wide monitoring and should also work for the estimation of population exposure to environmental contaminants as well. In order to do so, specific molecular markers in municipal sewage, that are collectively excreted by the community within the sewage catchment, have to be identified. In this project, we targeted eight mono- and di-conjugated glucuronide and sulfate metabolites of BPA and TBBPA as potential candidate markers for the SCIM-based estimation of population exposure to BPA and TBBPA. These conjugates are well established Phase II metabolites of the EDCs. Although most of their authentic standards are not commercially available, our research group has already established the procedures for their chemical synthesis and purification. Our preliminary results have also demonstrated the correlation between their levels in human urine and those of their parent EDCs in human blood. Nevertheless, much more work is needed to ascertain their feasibility as molecular markers for SCIM-based community-wide human exposure assessment. Thus, a SCIM-based evaluation of these metabolites will be conducted to study the correlation between their levels at the household sewage sources and their corresponding levels in the urine and blood samples collected from voluntary donors within the wastewater catchment. Municipal wastewater from up to four catchment areas in Hong Kong will be involved. Results generated from our studies can be generalized for nation-wide and international population exposure and public health assessments of these environmental endocrine disrupting chemicals. 要評估環境污染物對公眾健康構成的風險， 我們需要一個有效的估量方法。環境內分泌干擾物（EDCs ）已經引起世界各地的關注，譬如雙酚A（BPA ）和四溴雙酚A （TBBPA ） ，是普遍存在於我們的日常用品, 家電及個人電子產品中。要估計這些環境內分泌干擾物如何影響公眾健康，傳統的方法是通過測量其在人體組織中的水平，從而揣算其對整體人口健康的影響。這些方法一般都需要耗費大量的資源資源，所以不易開展。近年來出現的一種新的方法，檢測在城市污水中殘留的藥物，從而評估社區內濫用藥物的情況。這個污水化學信息採集（ SCIM ）概念，非常有效地簡化了社區濫藥的監測。這一概念，同樣可應用於監測在特定的社區內的人口所接觸環境污染物的程度。為了做到這一點，我們需要找出在城市污水中跟這些環境內分泌干擾物相關的分子標記物，來進行監測。在這個項目中，我們將會利用八個雙酚A和四溴雙酚A的共軛葡萄糖醛酸和硫酸鹽代謝物作為這些環境內分泌干擾物的分子標記。 這些內分泌干擾物的次期代謝物，不容易得到。而我們的研究小組已經建立了將它們化學合成和純化出來的程序。我們的初步結果也證實了它們在人的尿液裡的水平是跟在人體血液中的內分泌干擾物有著很大的相關性。但這距離能用於監測社區人口跟環境污染物的接觸水平，還有很遠的路。這個研究計劃的目的，就是要建立這一套SCIM監測系統。我們將在香港挑選多達四個集水區，收集家庭污水, 尿和血樣本進行分析，從而建立系統

160613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
160613.value: The Pearl River Estuary (PRE), located in the Pearl River Delta (PRD) region, southern China, is one of the largest estuaries in South-east Asia. Similar to most estuaries worldwide, PRE is a highly productive ecosystem and has significant economic (e.g. supporting over 120 million people in PRD) and ecological (e.g. providing important habitats and nursery grounds to many organisms) functions. However, rapid urbanization, coupled with economic and industrial growth in PRD has resulted in environmental degradation, threatening the survival of two common marine mammals, namely, finless porpoise (Neophocaena phocaenoides) and Indo-Pacific humpback dolphin (Sousa chinensis), which reside in Hong Kong waters. These cetaceans are vulnerable to anthropogenic impacts and environmental changes due to their long life span, relatively low reproductive rates as well as their habitat preference for estuarine and shallow coastal waters. Although there is some data on population trends, food sources and habitat utilization of these cetaceans for the past decades, there is a significant gap in our knowledge on how the population trends, food sources and habitat utilization of these cetaceans may have been influenced by environmental changes (e.g. El Niño Southern Oscillation) and anthropogenic impacts (e.g. overfishing, environmental pollution, and coastline reclamation). The teeth of cetaceans grow continuously. As teeth grow, new layers are deposited to the interior of the tooth, together with the assimilation of trace elements from their environment. These growth layers can, therefore, act as “time capsules” representing a life-time “record” of diet and foraging patterns of the cetaceans. As both finless porpoise and humpback dolphin have long life spans of over 30 years, the teeth of the adults can provide a long-term record for backtracking changes in their food sources and habitat use, and pollutant exposure. This information can be used to elucidate possible relationships to fluctuations in the environment over the same time period. It is possible to quantitatively measure landscape changes (e.g. land use pattern and coastline morphology) in the PRD by comparing current and past satellite images (e.g. since 1970s). By making use of the teeth samples of stranded cetaceans (since 1970s) as biological time capsules, this study aims to trace back and investigate how historical environmental (e.g. weather) fluctuations and landscape changes may have influenced (1) the population trends, (2) exposure dynamics of inorganic contaminants (e.g. heavy metals), and (3) food source and habitat utilization of finless porpoise and Indo-Pacific humpback dolphin, in PRD. 珠江口位於華南珠江三角洲地區，是東南亞最大的河口之一。與世界的大部分河口相似，珠江口是一個高生產力的生態系統，具有顯著的經濟（如，支撐了珠江三角洲超過1.2億的人口）和生態功能（如，給許多生物提供了重要的棲息地和育苗場）。然而，快速城市化以及經濟和工業的增長已導致環境退化，正威脅著江豚 (Neophocaena phocaenoides) 和印度太平洋駝背豚（中華白海豚, Sousa chinensis）這兩種常見的、棲息於香港水域的海洋哺乳動物的生存。這些鯨豚類由於壽命長、繁殖率比較低以及偏愛棲息於河口和沿海淺海水域，因此很容易受人為活動和環境變化的影響。 儘管過去幾十年裡有相關於這些鯨豚類種群趨勢、食物源和棲息地利用的資料，但對於其如何受到環境變化（如，厄爾尼諾南方濤動）和人為活動（如，過度捕撈、環境污染和海岸線填海）影響，我們的認識仍存在明顯的缺口。 鯨豚類牙齒是持續生長的。當牙齒生長時，新層沉積到牙齒內部，同時同化環境中的微量元素。因此這些生長層可以作為“時間囊”，“記錄”鯨豚類攝食和覓食模式的生命時間。由於江豚和中華白海豚壽命超過30年，因此它們成年的牙齒可為回溯食物來源、棲息地利用變化以及污染物暴露量提供長期記錄。這些資訊可用於闡明同時期環境波動間可能存在的關係。 通過比較當前與過去的衛星圖像（如， 70年代以來的衛星圖像），可定量測量珠江三角洲景觀變化（如，土地使用模式和海岸線形態）。本研究通過使用擱淺的鯨豚類牙齒樣品作為生物時間囊，旨在追溯和調查歷史環境波動（如，天氣）和景觀變化對珠江三角洲江豚（1）種群趨勢、（2）無機污染物暴露動力學（如，重金屬）以及食物來源和棲息地利用造成的影響。

160613.label: Realisation of objectives
160613.value: Teeth are metabolically inert structures that preserve chemical variations which may be related to the environmental history experienced by toothed marine mammals. To date, all the collected specimens have been processed and all the analyses completed to address the objectives of this study. Specifically, tooth sections were prepared and used for analyses including age determination for demographic analysis (objective 1) and determination of trace elements (objectives 2 and 3) in the tooth samples. In addition, soft tissues of the marine mammals were also subjected to the analyses of stable isotopes (objective 2) and contaminants of concern (objective 3). Objective 1: In a parallel study conducted by our Co-I, Dr Shiang-Lin Huang, demographic parameters for the Indo-Pacific humpback dolphins, Sousa chinensis, were estimated based on a life-table constructed using data from stranded animals in the Pearl River Estuary (PRE). Abundance estimates and individual based Leslie-matrix model were used to predict the population fluctuation by factoring in parameter uncertainty and demographic stochasticity. This study estimated a continuous rate of decline of 2.46% per annum for the humpback dolphin population (Hung et al. 2012). The present study used the same methodology to predict the population fluctuation of finless porpoise, Neophocaena phocaenoides, in the PRE. Our preliminary findings showed that the finless porpoise population is declining over the past years. Objective 2: Marine mammal muscle tissues, collected from 2009 to 2015, were analyzed for stable carbon and nitrogen isotopes to investigate habitat use and trophic pathway utilization by cetaceans in the PRE. Stable isotope models were used to elucidate the species and ontogenetic variations of trophic pathways and niche segregation of marine mammals and other top predators (e.g. sharks and rays) in the PRE. In addition, powder samples micro-milled from each growth layer group (GLG) of individual tooth sections of Indo-pacific humpback dolphins were analyzed using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometer (ICPMS). Intensity ratios of 14 detectable trace elements (Ba:Ca, Sr:Ca, Mn:Ca, Cu:Ca, Zn:Ca, Cd:Ca, Pb:Ca, Fe:Ca, Li:Ca, U:Ca, Mg:Ca, Na:Ca, K:Ca) were measured along the GLGs of tooth sections. The data generated were used to determine the sex and ontogenetic variations in habitat preference. Based on the trace element profiles of teeth, multivariate analyses showed that the trace elements in humpback dolphin varied significantly with sex and age groups. In particular, as the bioavailability of barium (Ba) in water decreases with increasing salinity, Ba can be used to track the habitat use or migratory pattern in marine mammals. Based on the trace element profiles of teeth of Indo-pacific humpback dolphin, Ba:Ca was significantly higher in adult female dolphins, indicating that female dolphins might spend longer period in estuarine habitats (with lower salinity) to give birth and rear their pups; and the lower levels of Ba:Ca in juvenile male and pre-adult dolphins indicated that they might migrate to open water (with higher salinity) to forage and mate. Objective 3: Levels of trace elements (Ag, As, Cd, Co, Cr, Cu, Hg, Mn, Mo, Ni, Pb, Sb, Se, Ti and Zn) were measured in the liver and prey samples of stranded finless porpoises (Neophocaena phocaenoides) and the levels in the samples were in order of Zn > Hg > Cu > Se > Mn > Cr > As > Mo > Ag > Cd > Ti > Pb > Ni > Co > Sb. Concentrations of most of the trace elements detected in the liver samples were declining during the past decade. In contrast, increasing levels of As, Cr, Mo and Ni were observed in the samples from 2004 – 2014, however, our study only reveals a statistically significant temporal trend in As concentrations in the finless porpoise over the past ten years. Over the past decade, several groups of chemicals of emerging concern (CECs) have attracted great attention worldwide because of their potential hazard to the environment. We have estimated the levels of CECs in the habitat of these vulnerable species and assessed the potential adverse effects arising from these substances. Briefly, elevating levels of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) were observed in the surface water samples from Pearl River Estuary (PRE), and these results were in good agreement with the increasing trend of PFASs in blubber samples over the past ten years (Lam et al., 2016), suggesting that production and use of PFSAs were in high demand in this region. In addition, toxicological studies of CECs have shown that exposure to organophosphate flame retardants (OPFRs) has the potential to cause neurological and systemic effects in aquatic organisms.

160613.label: Major findings and research outcome
160613.value: The demographic parameters for the finless porpoise, Neophocaena phocaenoides, were estimated based on a life-table constructed using data from stranded animals in the PRE. Our findings showed that the finless porpoise population is declining. Trophic level of the Indo-Pacific humpback dolphin and finless porpoise was the highest among all the top predators. Although humpback dolphin and finless porpoise had different foraging range and prey sources, they both mainly relied on pelagic food chains (i.e. pelagic fishes and/or cephalopods), which were consistent amongst all age groups (juvenile, pre-adult, and adult). This was also confirmed by stomach content analyses. The size of the trophic niche of finless porpoise has been increasing over the years, which may be related to environmental changes and/or trawling ban in recent years. Based on the trace element profiles of teeth, multivariate analyses showed that the trace elements in humpback dolphin varied significantly with sex and age groups. Based on the trace element profiles of teeth of Indo-pacific humpback dolphin, Ba:Ca was significantly higher in adult female dolphins, indicating that female dolphins might spend longer period in estuarine habitats (with lower salinity) to give birth and rear their pups; and the lower levels of Ba:Ca in juvenile male and pre-adult dolphins indicated that they might migrate to open water (with higher salinity) to forage and mate. Our study indicated that both trace elements and CECs accumulated in the soft tissues of porpoise collected from the PRE. Most of the trace elements detected in the liver samples showed a declining trend. One exception is that our study shows a statistically significant increasing trend in As concentrations in finless porpoises over the past decade. A number of manuscripts are being prepared based on the above results. In this study, we have also measured the levels of CECs in the habitat of these vulnerable species to assess the potential adverse effects arising from these substances (Kwok et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2015a and b). Apart from an increase in concentrations of certain PFASs in water, a recent investigation further reveals significant increasing trends of PFASs in the cetacean blubber samples collected in the past ten years (Lam et al., 2016), indicating that the use and production of PFSAs has been increasing in their habitats. Recent toxicological studies of CECs have shown that exposure to OPFRs has the potential to cause neurological and systemic effects (Wang et al., 2015a and b).

160613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
160613.value: The size of the trophic niche of finless porpoise has been increasing over the past years, which may be related to environmental changes and/or the trawling ban introduced since January 2013. Further monitoring and studies are needed to determine the reasons. Our studies demonstrated that organophosphate flame retardants (OPFRs) can accumulate in marine animals, and exposure to OPFRs can cause neurological and systemic effects (Wang et al., 2015a and b). However, information on the occurrence and environmental fate of these chemicals is scarce in this region. The impact of OPFRs on the local marine ecosystem in general and marine cetaceans in particular, deserves further investigation.

160613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
160613.value: Pearl River Estuary (PRE) is among the fastest growing regions of China. A decline in marine mammal populations in PRE is evident from the present and previous studies. In this study, ecological niches and prey sources of Indo-Pacific humpback dolphin and finless porpoise were determined using stable isotope and stomach content analyses. Both marine mammal species occupy the highest trophic levels among all the top predators in the PRE. The marine mammals had different ecological niches (foraging range/prey sources) and shared different resources with other top predators in the PRE. The trace element profiles in the tooth sections of humpback dolphin showed that adult female dolphins might spend longer periods in the estuary (e.g. to give birth/rear their pups), whilst juvenile male and pre-adult dolphins might migrate to open waters to forage and mate. A study on environmental contaminants including trace elements and chemicals of emerging concern (CECs) further revealed increasing trends of arsenic and per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) in the blubber samples of porpoise from 2004 – 2014, suggesting the presence of potential contamination sources of these chemicals in the PRE.

160713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
160713.value: Mechanical allodynia and hyperalgesia are primary symptoms of trigeminal neuropathic pain (TNP). An enhanced responsiveness of nociceptive neurons in the spinal trigeminal nucleus(SpV) has been well demonstrated. However, the mechanisms underpinning the transition of acute into chronic pain remain unclear. fMRI studies have shown enhanced activation of SpV, thalamus and anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) in the patients with TNP suggesting a dysfunction of the brainstem sensory components and higher brain pain centers. We hypothesize that tonic orofacial afferent nociceptive inputs to the SpV and ACC enhance synaptic transmission, and induce synaptic plasticity. The heightened synaptic transmission leads to a reduction in the pain threshold. We optimize the infraorbital nerve chronic constriction injury (IONCCI) model and the behavioral testing conditions to create stable allodynia for 6 weeks. Electrical physiological recording in in vivo will be performed to characterize an increase in synaptic transmission, e.g., activity-dependent plasticity (long-term potentiation,LTP); in the trigeminal ganglia (TG)–SpV, and medial thalamus (MT)–ACC synapses in TNP state. Elvax containing tetrodotoxin (TTX), a local nerve blockade, will be implanted into the nerve injury area. Immediate following nerve injury Elvax-TTX prevents the increase in the MT–ACC synaptic transmission as well as allodynia. However, the same nerve blockade during the later phase (10 days after nerve injury) failed to prevent long-term tactile allodynia and ACC–LTP. This is the first evidence that cortical plasticity may be intimately developed during the initial phase of trigeminal neuropathic pain. The roles of ACC, and NMDA receptors subtypes in modulating ACC-LTP and later phase of allodynia will be clarified. The changes in NR2B, NR2A, CaMKII expression will be detected by Western blot. It appears that the enhancement of synaptic glutamatergic transmission in the TG to SpV play a role to transmit and amplify nociceptive inputs and aggravate symptoms of TNP. Whereas higher brain center facilitation, e. g., ACC-LTP may be required for maintaining of neuropathic pain in the later phase. Further, we will demonstrate that reactive astrogliosis is involved in thalamo-ACCsynaptic plasticity. In the last phase of our experiment, we will focus on genetic silencing the gene expression of NR2B in the ACC to prevent the later phrase of allodynia. Understanding changes in the CNS processing in human surrogate models of TNP should contribute to a better understanding of the neurobiology of chronic facial pain disorders, and facilitate the identification of potential therapeutic targets in the brain cortex for humanTNP. 机械异常性疼痛和痛觉过敏是三叉神经性痛（TNP）的主要症状。在TNP中，脊髓三叉神经核（SPV）痛觉神经元反应增强已经得证明。然而，从急性过渡到慢性疼痛的机制仍不清楚。功能磁共振成像研究表明TNP患者SpV，丘脑和前扣带皮（ACC）活动增强，表明脑干感官元件和更高的大脑疼痛中心存在功能障碍。 我们推测，到达SpV及ACC的过多的口腔颌面部痛觉传入可增强突触间传递，诱发突触可塑性。我们优化了眶下神经慢性缩窄性损伤模型和行为学测试条件，创造出可维持6个星期的稳定的痛觉异常模型。通过在体电生理记录鉴定突触传递增加，例如，在TNP状态下，三叉神经节（TG）到SpV及内侧丘脑（MT）到ACC突触间活性依赖可塑性（长时程增强，LTP）改变。神经损伤后立即植入含河豚毒素（TTX）的Elvax，一种局部神经阻滞剂，可阻止MT-ACC突触传递的增加，以及痛觉异常。然而，在后期阶段（神经损伤后10天）同样的神经阻滞未能阻止长期触觉异常和ACC-LTP。这是皮层可塑性在三叉神经疼痛的初始阶段形成的第一个证据。我们将阐明NMDA受体亚型在调节ACC-LTP和后期阶段异常性疼痛中的作用，并使用免疫印迹法检测NR2B，NR2A变化和CaMKII的表达。我们认为TG-SpV突触间谷氨酸传递增强，可放大痛觉传入和加重TNP症状。而更高的大脑中枢的易化则可能作用于维持后期的神经性疼痛。 此外，我们将证明反应性星形胶质细胞参与MT-ACC突触可塑性。在实验的最后阶段，我们将重点放在ACC中NR2B基因表达沉默，以防止后期的痛觉异常。 了解TNP动物模型中枢神经系统的改变将有助于更好地理解慢性面部疼痛的神经生物学机制，并利于识别TNP在大脑皮质中潜在的治疗靶点。

160713.label: Realisation of objectives
160713.value: The project objectives have been achieved 1. Mechanical nociceptive behavior In the present study, the rats undergone chronic gut suture ligation of the ION, consistent with previous observations, showed a long-lasting stable mechanical allodynia for a period of at least 4 weeks. It is widely believed that plastic changes in the synapse are vital for information storage in the brain. TTX implanted during the early stage, immediately, after ION-CCI surgery showed a stable head withdrawal pain threshold of 6-7 g over a period of 30 days and shown better pain relief during the first 30 days which does not significantly differ from the presurgery head withdrawal threshold and sham group. These results indicate that local release of TTX can minimize the pain transmission from the injured region and provide significant relief from mechanical allodynia. 2. Decision making deficit in ION-CCI rats The results from the 60-min RGT test for the experimental groups: sham-operated rats, ION-CCI rats and TTX treated ION-CCI rats were compared using Mann-Whitney U test for significant difference. Rat gambling task showed that ION-CCI led to an increase in the proportion of poor decision-makers, and decrease the proportion of good decision-makers. 3. Early TTX treatment prevented decision making impairment in ION-CCI rats Directly implanting an Elvax-TTX immediately at the ION lesion site completely suppressed the lesion-induced allodynia, and rescued the decision-making deficits induced by chronic TNP. 4. Electrophysiological recordings of the nociceptive responses of SpVc neurons The SpV caudal neuronal firing rate were significantly increased in response to gradually increased orofacial mechanical pressures compared with those of sham rats. 5. Facilitation of basal synaptic transmission at the TG-SpVc synapses in ION-CCI rats The ION-CCI rats showed markedly enhanced LFP response evoked by TG stimulations compared with that of sham rats. A clear left shift of the I/O curve was observed in ION-CCI rats, suggesting long-lasting potentiation of TG-SpVc synaptic transmission after constructing trigeminal nerve. This result was consistent with the increased SpVc neuronal spontaneous firings and the increased response to orofacial nociceptive stimuli in ION-CCI rats in present studies and previous publications. 6. Induction of LTP-like plasticity at the TG-SpVc synapses was blocked in ION-CCI rats. In sham rats, HFS to the TG induced a robust and long-lasting LTP-like increase in LFP amplitude in the SpVc in response to the TG stimuli (400 μA, evoked about 50% of the maximum LFP amplitude) compared with the baseline level, reflecting the potentiation of the TG-SpVc pathway. In contrast to sham rats, HFS to the TG failed to facilitate the induction of LTP-like plasticity in ION-CCI rats. These observations suggest that the induction of LTP-like plasticity in the TG-SpVc synapses was blocked in the CCI states. It appears that, in the CCI state, transduction signals in the TG-SpVc synapses are not available for subsequent electrical recruitment, suggesting that the synaptic strengthening occurring in the CCI state engages signal transduction pathways that are in common with those activated by electrical stimulation. 7. Impaired within-SpVc spike-field phase synchrony after chronic injury of ION To further investigate intrinsic neuronal processes of chronic trigeminal neuropathic pain in spinal trigeminal nucleus; in particularly, to explore neural oscillations and synchronization within SpVc and between SpVc-SpVo, multiple-channel electrophysiological recording was performed in both caudalis and oralis of spinal trigeminal nucleus. A significant reduction of within-SpVc SFC in low-frequency range was observed during spontaneous condition in ION-CCI rats compared to that in the sham treated rats. Further, to investigate the spike phase distributions at any given frequency, phase locking analysis was performed between SpVc single units and its ongoing LFP oscillation. The Rayleigh’s test was computed to check for significance of single-unit phase-locking. Taken together, these findings indicate a loose coordination of spike timing with the local theta oscillation in chronic ION-CCI rat model. 8. Desynchronization between SpVc and SpVo in ION-CCI rats Next, to explore the alteration of functional connectivity in SpVc-SpVo network, we computed SFC between SpVc neurons and SpVo field potential. Similarly, the SFC values between SpVc neurons SpVo LFP at both spontaneous and nociceptive conditions were computed, significant difference between sham and ION-CCI rats was observed in both spontaneous and nociceptive conditions. Our data showed synchronization between SpVc and SpVo theta oscillations was reduced in ION-CCI rats. The detailed results described above were showed in the Part C attachment “Figures”. 9. Reduction of spike-field coherence and phase-locking between ACC spikes and basal lateral amygdala (BLA theta in ION-CCI rats) Averaged percentages of phase locked neurons show a significantly decrease in ACC single-unit spikes phase-locking to BLA theta band field potential in ION-CCI rats compared to that in sham rats 10. Disrupted BLA-ACC synchronization and information flow in ION-CCI rats Cross-correlation analysis of theta-filtered LFP recorded in the BLA and ACC revealed a reduction of synchronization in theta band in ION-CCI rats compared to sham rats. 11. Characterization of ACC Astrogliosis in ION-CCI Rats We first checked the expression of glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and S100 calcium-binding protein beta (S100β) in chronic visceral pain and ION-CCI rats, both of which are sensitive and reliable markers of astrocytes that respond to CNS damage and disease. Immunohistochemical staining of GFAP+ and S100β+ cells showed thicker processes and larger, more densely stained cell bodies in CCN rats similar with the visceral hypertensive rats (Cell Reports 2017, see Part C attachment). In addition, western blot analyses of protein expression in the ACC showed increases of GFAP in CCI rats. These observations indicate development of reactive astrogliosis in the chronic ION-CCI rat model. 12. Exogenous l-lactate supply into ACC facilitates decision-making performance in rats. lactate infusion rescues ACC long-term potentiation and repairs the impaired spike phase-locking in the rats chronic pain. Supported by this funding the paper “Astrocytic L-lactate Signaling Facilitates Amygdala-Anterior Cingulate Cortex Synchrony and Decision-making in Rats” has been published in Cell Reports. 2017 https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2211124717316327?via%3Dihub

160713.label: Major findings and research outcome
160713.value: Infraorbital nerve chronic constriction injury (ION-CCI) has become the most popular chronic trigeminal neuropathic pain (TNP) injury animal model which causes prolonged mechanical allodynia. Accumulative evidence suggests that TNP interferes with cognitive functions, however little is known about the underlying mechanisms. The aim of this study was to investigate decision making performance as well as synaptic and large-scale neural synchronized alterations on spinal trigeminal nucleus (SpV) circuitry in rats with TNP. Rat gambling task showed that ION-CCI led to an increase in the proportion of poor decision-makers, and decrease the proportion of good decision-makers. Directly implanting an Elvax-TTX immediately at the ION lesion site completely suppressed the lesion-induced allodynia, and rescued the decision-making deficits induced by chronic TNP. Electrophysiological recordings showed long-lasting synaptic potentiation of LFP in the trigeminal ganglia (TG)-SpV caudalis (SpVc) synapses in TNP rats. High frequency electrical stimulation of the TG induces long-term potentiation (LTP) in the TG-SpVc pathway in normal rats, but was occluded in the TNP state. Multiple-channel electrode recordings revealed that spike-field coherence and phase locking were reduced within the SpVc, meanwhile theta (4-10 Hz) synchronization between SpVc and SpV oralis (SpVo) was disrupted in ION-CCI rats. These findings provide the first documentation that orofacial allodynia and decision-making deficit are associated with alteration of synaptic plasticity on TG-SpVc synapses, as well as disruptions of spike-field coherence within SpVc and synchronization between SpVc-SpVo in rats following trigeminal nerve injury. (see part C attached file "M" and "figures"). We characterized impairments of long-term potentiation and spike-field coherence in the basolateral amygdala (BLA)-ACC network in association with a decision-making deficit in rats with chronic pain visceral hypersensitivity (part C attached files) and ION-CCI rats. Further, we showed that ACC-reactive astrogliosis and activity-dependent impairment of lactate release occur in chronic pain rats. Exogenous lactate supply rescues chronic-visceral pain- caused impairments of ACC phase locking and decision making, which can be mimicked by optogenetic activation of ACC astrocytes (Cell report https://doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2017.11.012). Currently, manuscripts are prepared using data collected from ION-CCI rats.

160713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
160713.value: Our large-scale electrophysiological recordings in Basal lateral amygdala (BLA)- anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) circuitry in free-moving animals during a decision-making task indicate that chronic trigeminal neuropathic pain (TNP) reduces the phase locking and synchronization, thus affecting the information flow between the higher brain regions necessary for cognitive functions. Myelination is critical for information flow between region and myelin plasticity is an important feature for learning. This feature of myelin plasticity is affected in diseased conditions such as chronic pain, chronic stress and in neurological disorders. Recent our studies in rodent models suggest global methylation in the prefrontal cortex is affected in neuropathic pain. In this study we showed that myelination and oligodendrocyte progenitor cells are affected in chronic TNP in the ACC regions. In further study we plan to show that promoting myelination (Clemastine) can facilitate recovery of decision-making performance in chronic pain rats, and further increase in BLA-ACC synchrony in the brain network in TNP rats.

160713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
160713.value: Infraorbital nerve chronic constriction injury (ION-CCI) has become the most popular chronic trigeminal neuropathic pain (TNP) which causes prolonged mechanical pain. Accumulative evidence suggests that TNP interferes with cognitive functions, however the underlying mechanisms are not known. Human and animal studies consistently suggest that chronic pain interferes with cognitive function. Brain fMRI studies have shown enhanced activation of spinal trigeminal nucleus, anterior cingulate cortex, basolateral amygdala (BLA) and thalamus in the patients with trigeminal neuropathic pain, suggesting a dysfunction of the brain stem sensory components and higher brain regions. It is surprising that there has been no experimental animal model to study chronic oral facial pain related and cognitive deficits, and little is known about the underlying mechanisms. We performed Rat Gambling Task showed that CCI led to decrease the proportion of good decision-makers and increase in the proportion of poor decision-makers. Multiple-channel electrode recordings revealed that showed long-lasting synaptic potentiation of LFP in the trigeminal ganglia-SpV caudalis synapses in TNP rats. Further, administration of Riluzole, an approved neuroprotective agent activating glutamate reuptake, at the late phase, suppressed mechanical allodynia but failed to rescue the decision-making deficits. Hence, early pain relief treatment is important for recovering from pain related cognitive impairments.

160813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
160813.value: 化療藥物所致周圍神經病變（ CIPN ）是一種嚴重的藥物副作用，紫杉醇和長春新堿等常用於治療卵巢癌、乳腺癌以及胃癌的藥物都可導致CIPN。CIPN由周圍神經損傷引起，會造成不可逆的感覺及運動功能的損傷，如麻木，痛覺異常，肌肉無力和癱瘓，這時候醫生往往會停止使用這些藥物。周圍神經（含有神經纖維束的條索狀結構）將我們的大腦和脊髓（中樞神經系統）與肢體和器官連接起來，為大腦傳遞資訊。通常情況下，受損的周圍神經會慢慢再生，但CIPN病人的周圍神經很難再生，導致損傷持續存在。目前，接受紫杉醇或長春新堿療法的患者，超過一半罹患不可逆轉的CIPN，但是卻仍然沒有預防CIPN的有效措施 。因此，開發潛在的CIPN治療措施是十分迫切的 。 那麼，怎麼才能夠預防癌症患者罹患CIPN？方法之一是增強神經元的內在生長能力，減少周圍神經損傷對神經元的影響。我們進行了一項研究來解決這個問題，在這個研究中，我們找到了生長相關的基因--熱休克蛋白（ Hsp） 27 。我們發現， 在嚴重的周圍神經損傷後，Hsp27可以促進感覺和運動功能的恢復，在小鼠模型中，Hsp27還可以預防I型糖尿病神經病變的發生發展。更重要的是，我們的資料初步顯示，過度表達人類Hsp27的周圍神經元可以抵抗紫杉醇和長春新堿對神經突觸的抑制，使突觸能夠生長延伸（從周圍神經元投射組成神經纖維）。根據這些研究，我們認為Hsp27很可能可以有效的預防和治療CIPN 。 在這項研究中，我們希望利用CIPN動物模型來證實這一假說。 CIPN動物模型在小鼠體內再現了類似人體內的環境，被廣泛用於CIPN的防治研究中。我們使用的動物是過度表達人類Hsp27的小鼠，給它們注射紫杉醇和長春新堿，進行動物行為學研究，進而評估小鼠感覺和運動功能的恢復。同時，我們會使用高解析度原子力顯微鏡來檢測CIPN模型動物細胞，研究Hsp27對神經元細胞的保護機制。我希望通過這項研究證明Hsp27對CIPN的防治作用，最終能夠在化療中引入FDA批准的Hsp27激活因子用於預防CIPN ，讓癌症患者在接受化療時，免於遭受藥物對神經系統的副作用，提高患者的生活品質。

160813.label: Realisation of objectives
160813.value: All Objectives were fully accomplished. Figures and Reference list are in Part C: Section 12 Other Impact. Objective 1.1: To examine temporal dynamic of sensory recovery in CIPN induced hHsp27 Tg mice: We proposed to examine if overexpressing human (h) heat shock protein (Hsp) 27 specifically in neurons protect CIPN mice from developing mechanical allodynia, thermal allodynia, and demyelination (1-4). Adult hHsp27 transgenic (Tg) and littermate (LM) male mice were intraperitoneally (i.p.) injected with paclitaxel (taxol) or vincristine (VCR) to generate CIPN symptoms, and divided into three groups including saline, LM+taxol/VCR, and Hsp27 Tg+taxol/VCR (n=10-16/group). hHsp27 prevented the development of mechanical allodynia measured by manual and electronic von Frey tests, when compared with saline control mice after treated with taxol (Fig.1A-B) and VCR (Fig.2A-B). LM mice developed cold allodynia significantly while hHsp27 Tg mice did not exhibit cold allodynia (Figs.1C & 2C). Loss of Intra-epidermal nerve fiber (IENF) in hind paw skin is correlated directly with the development of allodynia (2, 5). Restoration of IENF improved the symptoms (2, 6). Drastic loss of IENF was detected in LM mice but IENF were largely preserved in hHsp27 Tg mice after treated with taxol (Fig.3A-B) and VCR (Fig.4A-B). We performed electrophysiology studies to examine sensory nerve conduction in tail caudal nerve to validate behavior and histology studies. Caudal sensory nerve action potential (SNAP) was measured as it was directly correlated with the extent of mechanical allodynia in CIPN animals (3, 7). SNAP amplitude and nerve conduction velocity (NCV) recorded from hHsp27 Tg mice returned to control levels although both recording values remained significantly lower in LM mice after treated with taxol (Fig.3C-D) and VCR (Fig.4C-D). We assessed axonal degeneration by quantifying axon number and diameter one month following taxol and VCR treatments. Total number of axons remained unchanged in the sciatic nerve in taxol-treated animals (Fig.5). Interestingly, number of axons reduced significantly in VCR-treated LM mice but restored to saline control level in hHsp27 Tg mice (Fig.6). The number of small diameter axons increased significantly (Fig.7A-B) accompanied by reduction of mean axon diameter in toluidine blue semi-thin section of sciatic nerve from taxol-treated LM mice (Fig.7C). However, we did not detect alternation of axon diameter in VCR-treated mice (Fig.8). Myelin basic protein (MBP) is a predominant protein on the myelin sheath (8). Loss of MBP results in demyelination and reduction of NCV (9). MBP quantification showed that hHsp27 overexpression protected against taxol- and VCR-induced demyelination (Figs.9-10). These observations were confirmed by ultrastructure morphometry analysis using transmission electron microscopy (TEM) in which aberrant myelin was observed in LM+taxol/VCR mice but not in hHsp27 and control mice (Fig.11-12). We noticed prominent swelling of mitochondria in sciatic nerve of taxol- and VCR-treated mice, while hHsp27 Tg mice exhibited normal mitochondrial morphology (Fig.13-14). Our ongoing studies further extend the mitochondria research to examine the expression profile of mitochondrial fusion (Drp1 and Fis1) and fission (MFN1, MFN2 and Opa1) involved in mitochondria dynamics. Three out of five fusion/fission mRNA expressions was remained unchanged in the sciatic nerves of hHsp27 Tg+taxol mice, compared with controls (Fig.15A). We validated the downregulation of MFN2 protein expression by Western blot analysis (Fig.15B). Taxol is well-known to induce excessive microtubule acetylation. High level of acetylated tubulin was detected in LM+taxol mice only demonstrated the protective effect of hHsp27 overexpression (Fig.15C). Further studies are required. We next investigated the underlying mechanism of hHsp27-induced protective effect. Increased numbers of dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons undergoing apoptosis was detected by TUNEL assay (Fig.16A-B) along with activation of caspase 3 in LM+taxol mice only (Fig.16C-D). The DRG neurons were protected from apoptosis and no activation of caspase 3 was detected (Fig.16). We observed similar neuroprotection in VCR-treated animals as measured by TUNEL assay (Fig.17). We proposed to perform a sciatic nerve crush after treated with taxol/VCR to assess sensory (Objective 1.1) and motor function recovery (Objective 1.2). LM mice recovered much slower than hHsp27 Tg mice after taxol (Fig.18A) and vincristine (Fig.19A) treatments measured by pinprick assay, and the daily sensory recovery of hHsp27 Tg mice was comparable to controls. Similar to the systemic effects of taxol and VCR in above studies, LM developed CIPN-induced allodynia which was mostly relieved in hHsp27 Tg mice as measured by electronic Von Frey (Figs.18B-C & 19B-C). We performed additional works (not included in original proposal) including SNAP and NCV recordings, total axon and axon diameter quantification, MBP qualification, detail TEM analysis of demyelination and mitochondrial morphology, mitochondrial dynamic, microtubule acetylation, TUNEL and caspase 3 activity. Objective 1.2: To examine motor functional recovery and functional synapse formation in CIPN induced hHsp27 Tg mice: After sciatic nerve crush, we examined motor functional recovery by a battery of motor behaviour tests. hHsp27 Tg showed significant motor function recovery when compared with LM+taxol/VCR in toe spreading reflex and grip strength (Figs.20 & 21). All treatment groups showed similar sciatic function index (SCI) and rotarod test results during the recovery since both tests are more commonly used for assessing motor coordination (Figs.22 & 23). We next performed electromyography (EMG) recording during the course of recovery to assess functional synapse formation following injury, which allows the detection of functional neuromuscular synaptic transmission at the target distal muscles. Compound muscle activated potential (CMAP) of gastrocnemius muscle was evaluated on a weekly basis after treatments. CMAP amplitude in the hHsp27 Tg+taxol/VCR mice were maintained at a comparable level to the saline-treated mice (Figs.24A & 25A). Motor nerve latency was calculated to reflect the delay in motor recovery in LM+taxol and LM+VCR mice (Figs.24B & 25B). Objective 1.3: To investigate the effects of chemotherapy agents on synaptogenesis by in vitro co-culture assay: Animal and clinical case studies reported motor deficits during chemotherapy (10-14), we aim to assess the effect of chemotherapy agent on synaptogenesis. As mentioned in the mid-term report, it was time consuming to outline the contours of HEK-NLG-1 positive cells manually from thousands of cells with weak synapsin signal. We therefore using in vivo model to assess synaptogenesis by quantifying the formation of synapse at motor endplates. Motor functional recovery depends on successful nerve terminal and muscle reinnervations, and eventually the formation of functional neuromuscular junction (NMJ) at the motor endplate (15-18). We showed that the functional synapse formation was completely restored in hHsp27 Tg+taxol/VCR mice at a comparable level to controls (Figs.26A-C & 27A-C). We also performed weekly EMG recording to confirm the observation in NMJ studies. CMAP values in hHsp27+taxol/VCR were gradually returned to control levels but LM groups remained below the baseline levels (Figs.26D & 27D). Objective 2: To investigate the underlying mechanism of Hsp27 protection by using atomic force microscopy (AFM): This objective is completed by publishing in Nanomedicine: Nanotechnology, Biology, and Medicine with co-PI Dr King Lai (CityU) (19). We submitted current proposal in Nov 2012 with pilot live cell AFM imaging data generated by Dr Lai’s group. By that time, several papers published based on live cell AFM imaging, we therefore decided to submit the manuscript using the data generated directly from current grant and accepted for publication in March 2014 with additional data generated for revision during the course of study.

160813.label: Major findings and research outcome
160813.value: Current study examines the potential of Hsp27 as a therapy for CIPN, our results showed that Hsp27 could be one of the top candidates. We demonstrate for the first time that forced expression of hHsp27 protects the CIPN animals from developing CIPN associated peripheral neuropathy after treated with two commonly-used chemotherapy drugs paclitaxel and vincristine in clinically relevant animal model of CIPN. We confirm the protective effects observed in hHsp27 transgenic mice by multiple approaches including animal behavior, electrophysiology, and histology. Ongoing studies demonstrate the association between Hsp27 and mitochondria dynamics which requires further investigation. We also hypothesize that the regenerative capacity of CIPN patients would be affected due to the accumulation of chemotherapy drug. We show that forced expression of hHsp27 prevents the delayed in function recovery and demyelination after peripheral nerve injury in animals treated with chemotherapy drug. We therefore reviewed the major inhibitory molecules in regulating axonal regeneration. This study was published in a special issue of Experimental Neurology, and future studies should focus on the therapeutic roles of these inhibitory molecules in CIPN. Further investigation is required to uncover the underlying mechanism of Hsp27 protective effect, which can provide new insight into potential therapeutic interventions. Our ultimate goal is to identify small molecules that activate Hsp27 gene expression under physiological conditions for potential drug development. At molecular cell level, we demonstrate chemotherapy drug affects the regenerative capacity, cell mechanical properties and cytoskeleton of primary sensory neurons directly. At single cell level, we are able to detect how vincristine alters the cell mechanics such as roughness and stiffness of live adult mouse DRG neurons significantly, with the aid of atomic force microscopy. The major finding was published in a prestigious Nanomedicine journal. Two papers were published in top Journals in the area of Neuroscience. One of my PhD students (Chine) is directly involved and trained in current studies. We presented the work in the largest Neuroscience Meeting in the US for three consecutive years. I also present the major findings generated from current studies as invited talks. Chine was selected and invited to share his work that generated directly from current study in the section of “Young Investigator Oral Presentation” during the HK Neuroscience Meeting in 2016.

160813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
160813.value: We demonstrate the substantial beneficial effects of hHsp27 forced expression on CIPN mice; however, detail mechanism underlying the protective effects of Hsp27 requires further study. Our pilot studies indicate that mitochondrial and microtubule dynamic might play crucial roles in protecting the hHsp27 transgenic mice from developing CIPN symptoms. Further studies could be performed to modulate mitochondria fusion and fission (i.e. inhibitor) aiming to reverse the CIPN symptoms. Tubulin deacetylation is mediated by histone deacetylase (HDAC) plays a key role in axonal regeneration. Our data show that the level of acetylated tubulin return to basal level in hHsp27 transgenic mice, which indicates that the association of hhsp27 with tubulin acetylation that requires further studies. We believe that that our in vitro and in vivo system could be used for screening new and existing chemotherapy agents that might cause CIPN. Future studies will be to perform a high throughput small molecular library screening for Hsp27 to identify FDA approved small molecules which activate Hsp27 expression under physiological conditions. The ultimate goal is to delivery small molecule which can activate Hsp27 expression to enhance axonal regeneration and functional recovery in CIPN patients and treat other neurodegenerative diseases.

160813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
160813.value: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is a common side effect associated with anti-cancer drugs such as paclitaxel and vincristine for treating ovarian, breast and stomach cancers. Around 50-60% of cancer patients develop CIPN when treated with paclitaxel and vincristine, which stop them to continue the life-saving therapy. CIPN in patient is characterized by sensory (allodynia) and motor function impairments (muscle weakness and coordination). There is currently no cure for treating CIPN. Current proposed study aims to address this important question by examining the potential of a small heat shock protein (Hsp) 27 as a therapy for CIPN. We show that overexpression of Hsp27 greatly improve the CIPN symptoms in animal model confirmed by animal behavior tests, electrophysiology and histology analysis. We also develop a cell-based platform for screening new and existing chemotherapy drugs that cause CIPN. We believe that current study provides new sight into the development of potential therapy to CIPN. Future study should focus on performing high throughput small molecular library screening for Hsp27 to identify FDA approved small molecules which activate Hsp27 expression under physiological conditions. The cancer patients could carry on the life-saving chemotherapy without suffering neurological side effects, which greatly improve patient’s quality of life.

160913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
160913.value: Coral reefs are high biodiversity habitats currently under threat worldwide by a variety of factors, including global climate change, sedimentation due to surface runoff, chemical pollution and commercial overexploitation. Among chemical pollutants, herbicides have been found to affect coral health by interfering with the symbiotic relationship between corals and zooxanthellate algae, resulting in coral bleaching. Recently, exposure to sunscreen products was also reported to cause coral bleaching, but the causative toxin remains unknown. The major active ingredients of many sunscreen products are organic ultraviolet (UV) filters, a group of nearly 50 chemicals belonging to 15 chemical classes and having a wide variety of chemical properties. Organic UV filters are used in sunblock, cosmetics and other products in order to protect against the effects of prolonged sun exposure and to add stability to product formulations. These compounds may enter aquatic environments directly through recreational activities such as swimming and snorkeling, and indirectly after washing or bathing via wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) or wastewater releases. Our recent work has investigated the occurrence and distribution of organic UV filters in the Hong Kong environment in sediment and WWTP effluents, and we have found that several organic UV filters can be found in sediments from Victoria Harbor and in effluents from five major WWTPs in the city, indicating that these compounds are released and occur in the local environment. Due to their ecological importance in marine systems, corals are protected in Marine Parks and Reserves in Hong Kong, and several species are further protected under the Protection of Endangered Species of Animals and Plants Ordinance, but there is little information available on the effects of organic UV filters and sunscreens in local coral species. This study therefore aims to (1) investigate the occurrence of organic UV filters in surface waters in Hong Kong in order to more accurately estimate coral exposure to these compounds; (2) assess the toxicities of these compounds in juvenile and adult life stages of several species of corals found in Hong Kong as well as more widely in Southeast Asia; and (3) assess the toxicities of these compounds in combination with increasing ocean temperature using a mesocosm approach. The results of this study will provide information on the risks posed to corals by commonly used organic UV filters that can be used in future management and conservation of coral species both in Hong Kong and in the Asia-Pacific region.

160913.label: Realisation of objectives
160913.value: Surface water samples were collected prior to the commencement of the project period from various cities around the world; the samples were analyzed and the results were published in Tsui et al. (2014). A second manuscript on sediment concentrations of these compounds in Hong Kong and Tokyo Bay was published in 2015 (Tsui et al. 2015). These analyses addressed Objective 1 and part of Objective 4. The larval and adult coral toxicity tests were initiated in collaboration with our Co-I at the National Museum of Marine Biology and Aquarium (NMMBA) in Taiwan. Four benzophenone (BP) compounds (BP-1, -3, -4 and -8) were tested in larvae and adults of two coral species, Pocillopora damicornis and Seriatopora caliendrum. Larval tests were carried out for 14 days and measured the effects of the tested compounds on survival, larval settlement/desettlement, bleaching rates and photosynthetic efficiency. Adult (nubbin) tests were carried out for 7 days and measured the effects of the tested compounds on survival, bleaching rates, polyp extension, photosynthetic efficiency and zooxanthellate density. The tested concentrations ranged from environmentally-relevant levels to very high levels (0.1 to 1000 ug/L). S. caliendrum, a species found throughout the Coral Triangle, is closely related to another species included in the original proposal (S. hystrix) and can be readily cultured at NMMBA, and thus it was included in the study. Our results showed that both larval and adult P. damicornis were less sensitive to the effects of organic UV filter exposure than S. caliendrum larvae and adults. Effects on S. caliendrum larval settlement and bleaching rates were observed at the high end of the tested concentrations (100 and 1000 ug/L), though some effects occurred at 10 ug/L for some of the tested compounds. Likewise, the adult exposures with S. caliendrum showed that the tested BP compounds affected bleaching rate, polyp extension and photosynthetic efficiency at 100 and 1000 ug/L. A manuscript is currently in preparation. Activities in the second reporting period focused on testing additional organic UV filters and commercial products (Objective 2) and preparing for and initiating the mesocosm exposures (Objective 3). Two additional organic UV filters, ethylhexyl methoxycinnamate (EHMC) and octocrylene (OC) were tested in adult P. damicornis and S. caliendrum nubbins at concentrations ranging from 0.1 to 1000 ug/L using the same endpoints as in the benzophenone exposures. As in the benzophenone tests, EHMC had the strongest effects on S. caliendrum at 1000 ug/L, with high mortality and other physiological effects observed in these nubbins. EHMC showed very minor effects in P. damicornis nubbins, supporting the idea that this species is less sensitive to organic UV filter exposure. Exposure to OC had only minor effects on both coral species, and any observed effects occurred only at the highest concentration tested, indicating that this organic UV filter is less toxic than the other compounds tested to date. A manuscript is currently in preparation. A commercial sunscreen product was also tested to determine its effects on the nubbins of these two coral species. The selected product contained 7% EHMC and 3.6 % OC for skin protection. The product was applied to the hands of volunteers after pre-washing with methanol and MilliQ water. Volunteers then soaked their hands in containers of seawater for 20 minutes to mimic swimming activity. The seawater was then tested in a dilution series and the nubbins were exposed to the various dilutions for 7 days; the same endpoints were measured as in the previous nubbin exposures. The results for both species showed that the commercial sunscreen product had very strong effects on all of the tested endpoints in both species. Rapid bleaching was observed in the more concentrated treatments, and mortality was also observed in many of the treatments. The concentrations of OC and EHMC were confirmed analytically and found to be 30 µg/L and 400 µg/L, respectively, neither of which was found to be toxic in the single-compound coral exposures. The commercial sunscreen product tested contains many chemicals in addition to organic UV filters, and it is therefore likely that the observed effects are due to a combination of ingredients in the product, but the identities of these toxic components could not be determined. These results completed the work under Objective 2. The toxicity thresholds obtained from the experiments conducted for Objective 2 were used to more accurately assess the risk of organic UV filters to corals in Hong Kong based on surface water concentrations measured under Objective 1. These assessments complete Objectives 1 and 4. The results of these assessments are being prepared for publication. The final set of experiments was based on the 60-day mesocosm exposures which aimed to mimic environmental exposure to a mixture of organic UV filters both in the absence and presence of global climate change-related elevated temperature stress (Objective 3). Nubbins of three coral species, S. caliendrum, P. damicornis and Montipora aequituiberculata, were exposed in the mesocosms to a mixture of 12 organic filters (BP-3, BP-4, BP-1, BP-8, EHMC, OC, amiloxate, enzacamene, avobenzene, ethylhexylsalicylate, homosalate, and octyl dimethyl-p-aminobenzoic acid) at a concentration of 200 ng/L, a level which was chosen based on the levels measured in the studies described for Objective 1. The exposure concentration was verified analytically throughout the 60-day exposure period. The corals were exposed to the organic UV filter mixture alone or the organic UV filters mixture + elevated temperature (30°C), in addition to a solvent control. Mortality, bleaching and polyp retraction were measured daily as in the previous experiments, and growth was also measured on days 14, 30 and 60 of the exposure. Once the exposures were completed, the remaining nubbins were used to measure gene expression of oxidative stress- and detoxification-related genes and enzyme activities, and for chemical analysis to determine bioaccumulation of the tested compounds. The nubbins in the solvent control appeared healthy throughout the 60-day exposure period. Bleaching (37.5%) and death (12.5%) of S. caliendrum were observed in the UV filter mixture treatment, while the other two coral species were unaffected. In the UV filter mixture + heat treatment, 100% bleaching and mortality of S. caliendrum and 100% bleaching and 50% mortality of P. damicornis were observed. These results are notable because previous experiments had shown that P. damicornis was much more tolerant of UV filter exposure than S. caliendrum, but the introduction of heat stress in addition to the chemical exposure caused strong effects. M. aequituiberculata also bleached (50%) and showed a thorough polyp retraction response (100%) in the combined chemical + heat stress treatment. Nubbin growth of all three coral species in the combined treatment was also significantly reduced. The results of the gene expression and enzyme activity measurements showed that oxidative stress was induced in the corals under the combined stress treatment, partly explaining the observed bleaching and mortality. These results indicate that organic UV filters at environmental concentrations caused bleaching and death in a sensitive coral species, S. caliendrum, while the combination of these two conditions caused these effects in more tolerant species, P. damicornis and M. aequituiberculata. The only part of the work under Objective 4 that remains to be completed is the bioaccumulation assessment for the coral nubbins, which is currently ongoing. Once the chemical analysis is finished, all of the results will be incorporated into a manuscript for publication later this year.

160913.label: Major findings and research outcome
160913.value: This research demonstrated that organic UV filters occur ubiquitously in the marine environment, including in beach areas and non-beach areas. Among the studied locations, Hong Kong waters contained the highest number of compounds at the highest concentrations. Initial risk assessment showed that these concentrations in Hong Kong could pose a risk to local organisms. These results were published in Tsui et al. (2014), listed in Part C. A method was developed for measuring organic UV filters in sediments, and these compounds were quantified in sediment samples from Hong Kong and Tokyo Bay. The results of the sample analysis showed that higher concentrations of hydrophobic organic UV filters were detected. There is limited toxicity data available for the effects of these compounds in benthic organisms, but a preliminary analysis showed that the sediment concentrations measured posed a risk to marine snails. These results were published in Tsui et al. (2015), listed in Part C. Toxicity testing was carried out on six organic UV filters to determine effects thresholds for these compounds in Coral Triangle coral species. The results of this testing showed that most of the compounds were not toxic within the ranges at which they occur in the environment. However, toxicity testing of a sunscreen product showed that diluted water washed from the hands of volunteers who had applied the product caused bleaching in the tested corals, indicating that other components of personal care products could have a mixture effect. These results will be published in two papers later this year, one for benzophenones and the second for octocrylene, ethylhexyl methoxycinnamate and the commercial product (both He et al., listed in Part C below). A mesocosm approach was used to assess the toxicity of a mixture of 12 organic UV filters at an environmentally-relevant concentration to three Coral Triangle coral species. The toxicity of the mixture alone was tested, as well as the combined effects of the chemical mixture and elevated seawater temperature. The results showed that organic UV filter exposure exacerbated the effects of elevated temperature in terms of coral growth, bleaching and mortality. These results raise concern regarding environmental coral exposure to organic UV filters given that sea surface temperatures are predicted to continue to increase as global climate change impacts intensify. These results will be published in a paper to be submitted later this year (He et al., listed in part C below).

160913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
160913.value: The results of the studies conducted under this GRF grant indicate that organic UV filters may be an important chemical stressor to corals. Coral reefs around the world are already under increased stress due to coastal development, nutrients, ocean acidification and global climate change. Recent severe and large-scale bleaching events in coral reef systems including the Great Barrier Reef underscore the extent to which corals are under threat. The finding of the work carried out under Objective 1 has already helped to inform a field study of organic UV filter exposure in Hong Kong corals published this year (Tsui MMP, Lam, JCW, Ng TY, Ang PO, Murphy MB, Lam PKSL. 2017. Occurrence, distribution and fate of organic UV filters in coral communities. Environ. Sci. Technol. 51:4182–4190). This work also led to an SRG grant to investigate the environmental occurrence of chlorinated organic UV filter breakdown products in Hong Kong seawater, wastewater treatment plant effluent and swimming pool water, including toxicity testing of these compounds using in vitro bioassays. This work is currently wrapping up, and a manuscript will be submitted for publication this year.

160913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
160913.value: Organic ultraviolet (UV) filters are common ingredients in cosmetic and sunscreen products. After these products are used, they are washed off and into the sewer system through bathing or laundering, or washed into the environmental directly during aquatic recreational activities. The research carried out for this grant first investigated whether these compounds are present in seawater and sediment in various locations around the world. The results showed that some organic UV filters could be found in seawater and sediment from the US, Japan and Hong Kong, with the highest concentrations measured in Hong Kong. Based on these results, we wanted to know if these compounds posed any toxicity risk to coral reefs, as many coral reefs around the world are tourist destinations and tourists often use products containing organic UV filters when they visit coral areas. The results of toxicity testing on three coral species showed that organic UV filters in an environmentally realistic mixture worsened the effects of increased seawater temperature, a known impact of global climate change. Overall, the results of this research show that organic UV filters occur widely in the aquatic environment and that the risks they pose to corals may warrant concern.
