199213.label: Major findings and research outcome
199213.value: The results of multilevel analyses across two field studies and one experimental study revealed a three-way interaction pattern, demonstrating that supervisor emotional exhaustion was positively related to abusive supervision only when subordinate performance and supervisor self-monitoring were low. In addition, our results showed that abusive supervision was positively related to subordinate deviance and this supervisory behavior mediated the relationship between supervisor emotional exhaustion and subordinate deviance (but not subordinate performance). Subordinate performance, rather than as an outcome, functioned as an additional factor moderating the exhaustion-abuse linkage. The interactive effect of supervisor exhaustion and subordinate performance and the mediating relationship were particularly salient when supervisor self-monitoring was low. Based on these results, we have produced a journal article published at a high-quality journal (Journal of Organizational Behavior) and two conference papers that were presented at the Annual Conference of the Society of Industrial and Organizational Psychology in 2014 and the Annual Conference of the Academy of Management in 2015.

199213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
199213.value: Future research could expand the present model by considering other moderators. For example, fundamental goals and needs as important motivational factors that may buffer the negative consequences of resource deprivation (Halbesleben et al., 2014). Organizational sanctions, for example, may raise the personal costs associated with abusive behavior for supervisors themselves (cf. Inness et al., 2008). If these costs exceed the resources required to withhold abusive supervision, even exhausted supervisors confronting a low-performing subordinate may find it worthwhile to restrain their aggressive impulses. Future research that explicates how organizational sanctions should be designed and implemented to achieve this effect would be highly interesting, potentially offering tangible instruments for organizations striving to act against abusive supervision. Besides, future studies could consider the relationship between emotional exhaustion and other supervisory behaviors and leadership outcomes such as supervisors’ logical reasoning, information processing, decision-making, and their overall leadership effectiveness (Schmeichel, Vohs, & Baumeister, 2003). Finally, future research may benefit from a more dynamic perspective by uncovering how differing supervisor exhaustion levels (e.g., during periods with higher vs. lower job demands) may trigger oscillations in subordinates’ abuse perceptions over time.

199213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
199213.value: When supervisors experience work stress and excessive job demands and thus feel emotionally exhausted, they are more likely to exhibit abusive behavior. Such destructive supervisory behavior may produce detrimental impact on subordinates. The main contribution of this study is to increase our understanding of the origins of abusive supervision. Our results suggests that supervisors may perceive lower subordinate performance as a source of provocation and frustration that can trigger aggressive impulses and supervisors higher on self-monitoring are more motivated to avoid abusive supervision even when they experience emotional exhaustion and face a relatively low performing subordinate. This study expands our knowledge by (a) highlighting supervisors’ resource deficits at work as a critical instigator of hostile supervisory behavior and (b) illustrating that the role of such deficits may differ markedly between distinct subordinates and supervisors.

199613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
199613.value: Both shrinkage estimation and high dimensional factor models become increasingly popular in econometrics and statistics during recent years. On the one hand, the shrinkage estimation is a method that tends to shrink estimates towards zero. It is especially useful when the model has a large number of unknown parameters that demonstrate sparsity, namely, many of the parameters are zeros. Various shrinkage estimators are developed so that the estimators will be exactly zeros for unknown zero parameters and will converge to the parameters' true values for unknown nonzero parameters. This means that the shrinkage method allows people to conduct estimation as if they know the true model in advance. This is known as the oracle property. On the other hand, factor models are commonly used in macroeconomics and finance where the data sets have large cross section and time dimensions. Usually, it is technically cumbersome to directly estimate high dimensional models. The factor model assumes that the high dimensional data are driven by a small number of common factors and many idiosyncratic noises. In many applications, a few common factors can explain a substantial amount of variation in high dimensional data sets. Hence, factor models provide a useful way of conducting dimension reduction which leads to low dimensional models without loss of important information. This project will propose a shrinkage type of estimator for high dimensional factor models so that model selection and factor loading estimation can be accomplished simultaneously. In a conventional factor model, unobservable factors are estimated by principal components (PC), and then the number of factors is determined by some information criteria. Subsequently, factor loadings are estimated by conventional OLS, given the PC estimates of factors. The advantage of the shrinkage estimation method is that it can combine the selection and estimation into one step. Also, the literature mainly focuses on determining the number of factors, which is a special case of model selections in factor models. In contrast, we will deal with more general model selection problems based on the oracle property of the shrinkage estimator. For example, we can select the overidentifying restrictions for the factor-augmented VAR models. We will propose a class of shrinkage estimators, establish their asymptotic properties, and provide the conditions under which these estimators can select the correct model with a probability converging to one. The finite sample performance of the proposed estimator will be explored using Monte Carlo simulation. 近年來，壓縮估計和高維度因數模型在計量經濟學和統計學文獻中變得越發流行。一方面， 壓縮估計是一種將估計值向零壓縮的估計方法。這種方法對有大量未知係數且具有稀疏性的模型來說尤為有用。所謂稀疏性，即很多參數為零。多種壓縮估計量被發展出來，它們可以將未知的零參數恰好估計為零，同時可以收斂到未知非零參數的真實值。這意味著壓縮估計方法可以使人們在進行估計的時候，有如預先知道真實的模型一般。這就是為人熟知的先知性質。另一方面，因數模型被大量應用於宏觀經濟學和金融學中，而這些領域的資料通常同時具有較高的橫截面維度和時間維度。通常情況下，直接估計高維模型存在著一定的技術難度。因數模型假定高維資料由少量的共同因數和大量的特質干擾項所推動。在很多應用中，使用少量的共同因數便可以解釋高維資料中相當一部分的波動。因此，因數模型提供了一種降低維度的方法，它可以將模型簡化到低維度而不損失重要的資訊。 這個專案將提出一個針對高維因數模型的壓縮估計量，其可以同時完成模型係數的估計和模型的選擇。在傳統的因數模型中，不可觀測的因數通常由主成分分析來估計，而因數的個數則由資訊準則來確定。因此，在給定由主成分估計的因數的情況下，模型中的係數是由傳統的最小二乘法來估計的。壓縮估計方法的優勢在於其可以把模型選擇和估計在一步操作中完成。另外，現有文獻主要是關注於決定因數的個數，這只是因數模型中模型選擇問題的一個特例。與之不同的是，我們將在壓縮估計量的先知性質的基礎上，處理更一般的模型選擇問題。例如，我們可以選擇因數增廣的向量自回歸模型中的過度識別約束條件。我們將提出一類壓縮估計量，建立其漸進性質，並得出在什麼樣的情況下，這些估計量能夠以趨近於1的概率選擇出正確的模型。我們將使用蒙特卡羅模擬來研究所提出統計量的有限樣本性質。

199613.label: Major findings and research outcome
199613.value: This project develops an adaptive group lasso estimator for factor models with both global and group-specific factors. The global factors can affect all variables, whereas the group-specific factors are only allowed to affect the variables within a certain group. We propose a new method to separately identify the spaces spanned by global and group-specific factors and develop a new shrinkage estimator that can consistently estimate the factor loadings and determine the number of factors simultaneously. The asymptotic result shows that the proposed estimator can select the true model specification with probability approaching one. An information criterion is developed to select the optimal tuning parameters in the shrinkage estimation. Monte Carlo simulation confirms our asymptotic theory, and the proposed estimator performs well in finite samples. In an empirical application, we implement the proposed method to a data set consisting of Europe and U.S. macroeconomic variables and detect one global factor, one U.S. specific factor, and one Europe specific factor.

199613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
199613.value: The method can be extended from the current static factor setup to a dynamic factor setup. Specifically, the orthogonality condition holds for the innovations of the factor processes instead of the factors themselves. In addition, the model can be generalized from the current two-level factor structure to more than two levels. For example, we can consider global factors, regional factors, and country factors. These are interesting topics for further development.

199613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
199613.value: This project develops a shrinkage estimator for factor models with global and group-specific factors. I considered a factors model with both global and group-specific factors. Specifically, the global factors can affect all of the variables in the data set, whereas the group-specific factors can only affect variables in certain groups of variables. I proposed a shrinkage estimator that can simultaneously determine the model specification and estimate the global and group-specific factors and their factor loadings. I prove that the proposed method can select the true model specification with a probability approaching one as the sample size increases. In addition, the estimators of the factors and factor loadings are consistent in the sense that they become more and more accurate as the sample size increases. I conducted vast simulation experiments. The results show that the proposed method can choose the true numbers of global and group-specific factors with very high probabilities in reasonably large samples. The estimator can also span the spaces of underlying factors with high accuracy. The proposed method can be applied to big data with multi-level factor structure. For example, I use an empirical application to illustrate how to apply my method to Europe-U.S. macroeconomic data.

As for the (linked) Objectives 4 and 5: while the present adaptive time-stepping method yields satisfactory results, we are still working on refining it, by using as the basis a posteriori error estimates for the collocation solutions (ideally, by employing an $hp$ approach in which both the local stepsizes and the local degrees of the piecewise polynomials are variable). 200113.label: Major findings and research outcome
200113.value: The analysis of quenching solutions for Volterra-Hammerstein integral equations, (as described on page 8 of the application) , i.e. conditions under which global solutions exists and conditions under which the solutions quench in finite time, has been fully carried out (cf. Z.W. Yang and H. Brunner, Quenching analysis for nonlinear Volterra integral equations, Dyn. Contin. Discrete Impuls. Syst. Ser. A Math.}, 21 (2014), 507-529; see also Section 3.3 in H. Brunner, Volterra Integral Equations: An Introduction to Theory and Applications, Cambridge University Press, Cambridge/UK, 2017 for a summary of the main results). The analogous quenching analysis of piecewise polynomial collocation solutions for such quenching problems is also complete, and a corresponding paper (with Z.W. Yang, Harbin Institute of Technology) is currently in revision. Dr Yang and I are currently completing work on the computational implementation of these collocation schemes, in particular regarding the use of adaptive mesh selection and the application to Volterra-Hammerstein integral equations arising as mathematical models (see also Example 9.2.14 in the above monograph, and the references). The mathematical technique underlying the adaptive stepsize selection is based on the analogous one for approximating solutions of nonlinear Volterra integral equations that blow up in finite time (see the paper by Z.W. Yang and H. Brunner, Blow-up behavior of collocation solutions to Hammerstein-type Volterra integral equations, SIAM J. Numer. Anal., 51 (2013), 2260-2282). Concrete large-scale numerical simulations remain to be carried out.

200113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
200113.value: As mentioned in Section 6.1, the computational implemention of our collocation schemes to concrete mathematical models (which often arise from initial-boundary-value problems of linear diffusion equations with nonlinear boundary conditions) is still work in progress. We expect to complete this by early 2019.

200113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
200113.value: Finite-time quenching in semilinear diffusion problems (semilinear parabolic partial differential equations) and related nonlinear Volterra-type integral equations describes a certain singular behaviour of solutions: the solutions tend to a finite limit in a finite time T_b but their time derivatives become infinite at that time. Since such nonlinear problems cannot in general be solved explicitly, one is interested in numerical schemes generating approximations that exhibit the same behaviour. Of particular interest is the approximation of the quenching time T_b. The aims of this proposal are (i) to establish the theory of quenching (and non-quenching) for nonlinear Volterra integral equations, and to design and analyse collocation schemes based on piecewise polynomials.

200513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
200513.value: We developed an analytical technique capable of detecting 0.2 ppb of lead colloids in drinking water and atto-moles of trace elements in laser printed inks. This technique has sensitivity comparable to laser-excited atomic fluorescence (LEAF). Yet unlike LEAF when one wavelength only excited one transition, it induced numerous analytes to fluoresce with one single excitation wavelength. Multi-analyte fluorescence was intriguing. We believe the process was as follows. A nanosecond laser pulse vaporized the sample. The atoms in the dense plume interacted strongly. That resulted in the smearing of their energy levels. This was especially severe for highly excited states. Photoexcitation to these smeared levels was therefore non-selective. As the plume expanded, the atom-atom interaction diminished and the photoexcited species behaved like isolated atoms again. They decayed radiatively to emit sharp spectral lines. So far, our experimental observations were consistent with the general ideas of our model. We now plan to elucidate the details by examining four key steps of the process. First, we will analyze the plume creation step and design ways to minimize optical interference while maximize volatilization. Second, we will study the absorption of the excitation laser beam by the dense plume. We will use various excitation wavelengths to map the smeared energy levels. Third, as the plume disperses, we will do time-resolved spectroscopy to track the metamorphosis of energized molasses to well-defined excited analytes. We will try to design and engineer the product states. Fourth, we will characterize the analyte spectral emissions, both their intensity and line shape, and tailor them for spectrochemical analysis. Ultimately, we aim at making ppb and atto-mole sensitivity an everyday performance. Our analysis required little sample preparation, could be carried out rapidly in real-time, and featured a host of capabilities associated with laser beams, such as good spatial and temporal resolution for in-situ and non-contact sampling. We have applied it to matrices ranging from metals through ceramics to plastics. We have observed signature emissions from numerous elemental and molecular analytes. A technique with this combination of sensitivity and versatility is unheard of. The simultaneous capture of signals from multi analytes, including trace components, will present vast chemometric opportunities for the classification of complex samples. This can be real-time tissue identification during laser ablative surgery, or bio-agent screening in the field. The application horizon is beyond imagination. 我們早前開發了一種分析技術，能夠檢測飲用水中0.2 ppb的鉛微粒和打印機墨粉中atto-mole的痕量元素。這種技術的靈敏度媲美激光誘發原子熒光 (LEAF)。然而，它不受制於LEAF的“一個波長，激發一態” 的限制。它用一個波長就能誘發眾多樣品的熒光。多体熒光這現象當然耐人尋味。我們猜想過程是如下的。一個激光脈衝將微量的物質蒸發成氣團。開始時，這氣團密度很高。原子們甚為接近，互相影響，把相互的能級變得模糊。這情況於較高的激發態致為嚴重。由於原子能級模糊了，光激發就變得無選擇性。隨著氣團擴散，原子間的相互作用減弱，原子能級亦從模糊回復銳利。原子團又再如獨立的原子般。它們的發射譜線又再變得清楚和尖銳。 迄今，我們的觀察和上述的構想大體是一致的。但其中的細節未盡清楚。我們現在計劃闡明整個過程的四個關鍵步驟。我們首先研究氣團的產生，一方面要減少同生的背境光，另方面要盡量使樣品氣化。第二，我們需要研究氣團吸光的情況。我們將會使用各種不同波長的激光來激發模糊了的能級。第三，隨著氣團的擴散，我們會迅時觀察其光譜的變化，以求達至最佳的原子態。第四，我們會研究樣品的發射譜線，包括其強度和形狀，務求塑造最宜分析用的樣品光譜。我們最終希望ppb和atto-mole的靈敏度垂手可得。 用我們的方法，樣品不需特別準備。又可進行快速的實時分析。更可利用激光的特性，包括空間和時間的高分辨率，進行遙距原位採樣。這些年來，我們分析了不同的樣品，包括金屬、陶瓷以至塑膠。亦觀察到眾多元素和分子的光譜訊號。一種技術，能如此靈敏，又廣能應用，是聞所未聞的。用此技術，我們可以同時探測多個原素，包括痕量的。再透過數據處理和分析, 可把複雜的樣品分類和鑑定。試想，用於激光切割的手術時，可實時鑑定纖維組織。用於化武戰場上，可實時確定化武種類。這技術的應用面，廣闊得超乎想像。

200513.label: Major findings and research outcome
200513.value: There are five major findings, 1. The mechanism of ArF laser-induced-fluorescence (LIF) of ablation plumes, or plume-LIF (PLIF) for short, can neither be plasma emissions nor photofragmentation fluorescence (see Wang 2016). 2. The PLIF mechanism is shown to involve dense matters. According to that model, the dense nascent plume has energy structure resembling bands, especially for the higher energy states. Absorption of energetic ultraviolet photons is therefore nonselective. As the plume disperses, the excitation energy is channeled to electronic excitation energies of the atomic and molecular fragments. Their fluorescence gives rise to the fingerprint signal of the analytes (see Wang 2016). 3. Ultraviolet lasers at both 193 nm and 213 nm are effective (see Cai 2015). 4. PLIF has tremendous analytical potential for ultra-trace and ultra-micro simultaneous analysis of multi-analytes by optical means (see Wang 2016). 5. We demonstrated its application in the analysis of Chinese artworks, specifically, the nondestructive analysis of Chinese black inks on xuan papers (see Cai 2016).

200513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
200513.value: Huge potential for ultra-sensitive nondestructive analysis. A company specialized in artwork authentication is founded based on this research.

200513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
200513.value: Ultraviolet laser light can induce dense plumes to fluoresce, a phenomenon that can be exploited for very sensitive and nondestructive material analysis. This project elucidated the basic science of that phenomenon and pointed directions for its optimization. One application example is the chemical analysis of Asian artworks for conservation and authentication purposes.

200813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
200813.value: 毛細電泳是一種重要的生物分子分離技術，本項目書通過減少焦耳熱和提高檢測信號，以改善毛細電泳的性能和靈敏性。 如果需要對某種生物分子進行生物分析和醫療檢測，將其与其它生物分子分離是一個重要的步驟。在微流控分離系統中，生物分子通常會進行熒光標記以便識別分離信號。如果分離系統的通道橫截面比較大，分離信號比較容易觀測，但很容易產生焦耳熱，而焦耳熱會影響分離的效率和重複性。如果減小通道橫截面，焦耳熱減少，但信號觀測則變得困難。為了解決這個問題，本項目書建議利用金屬納米材料的熒光增強效應來提高分離觀測信號。由於金屬納米材料，特別是金和銀納米材料，具有等離子共振特性，當受到入射光的激發後，金屬納米材料附近的電場被增強，進而使得附近的熒光分子的發光強度得到增強。這種現象已被廣汎應用于生命科學。 為了將金屬納米材料的熒光增強性質應用于毛細電泳分離系統，需要解決的問題是如何將金屬納米材料整合到微流控通道內部。本項目書建議利用局域斜入射物理沉積方法在通道內部製備金屬納米材料，該方法可以解決現有方法的一些困難，比如通道橫截面大小受到限制，需要進行複雜的金屬納米材料和通道的對準等等。本項目書計劃先將金屬納米材料製備到微流控通道內部，對其熒光增強效果進行表徵，進而進一步將該研究應用于DNA分離。 香港有兩百多間診所，大部分從事生物分析和醫療診斷。本項目書利用金屬納米材料的熒光增強性質，可促進低成本高效率的生物分子分離技術，以及相關行業的產業化進程。

200813.label: Realisation of objectives
200813.value: 1. Fabricate capillary electrophoresis microchannel with decreased cross section to reduce Joule heating Capillary electrophoresis (CE) microchannel with 1.5 μm width has been fabricated through optical lithography. 2. Develop the localized oblique angle deposition (LOAD) methods for metal nanostructures integration into capillary electrophoresis microfluidic system SiO2 and Ag nanorods (NDs) have been grown on the sidewalls of CE microchannel through LOAD method. The corresponding scanning electron microscope (SEM) images can be found in the 2013 μTAS conference manuscript. 3. Explore metal enhanced fluorescence (MEF) effect of Ag nanorods deposited in microchannels MEF enhanced CE experiment for amino acids separation is performed by placing Ag NDs on sidewalls of microchannels. Three fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC) labeled amino acids Gln, Gly, and Ser have been separated in the above Ag NDs integrated CE device. The fluorescence intensity increases by 6 folds after the amino acids enter the region with Ag nanorods. The results have been presented in the 2013 μTAS conference. A more systematic study on the solution-based MEF property of the Ag NDs arrays has been performed in terms of their morphology, orientation, absorption and scattering. When the height of the sandwiched solution is 20.8 μm, the effective enhancement factors are calculated as 292 and 505 with respect to Si wafer for Ag NDs at the nominal thickness T = 2000 nm and 3000 nm, respectively. In addition, a multilayer of SiO2 NDs/Ag NDs is integrated with a CE device and the optical detection of amino acid separation is improved by 6.5 fold with the microchannel depth of 10 μm. This result has been published on Nanotechnology. Ag Zigzag NDs (ZNRs) have been fabricated at different temperature and their MEF property has been investigated by detecting biotin-neutravidin reaction and DNA hybridization. Ag ZNRs with folding number Z=1, 3, 5, 7 are fabricated on the flat substrates at the substrate temperature T=0 °C and 25 °C. Biotin-neutravidin interaction is firstly explored with the Ag NRs based MEF. As a result, the enhancement factors 1 (EF1s) generally increases with the increasing folding number and the maxima EF1, 14 fold, is obtained at Z = 7, where EF1 is defined as the ratio between the integrated FL intensity on Ag NRs and that on the Ag film reference. While there is no big difference in EF1 between the ZNRs deposited at the same folding number but different substrate temperature, due to the most similarity in their structures. To sensitively detect the DNA hybridization, Ag ZNRs at Z = 7 are chosen as the optimal structure. Furthermore, an underlayer of Ag film with a thickness of 500nm is deposited on the substrate prior to the Ag ZNRs growth to promote stronger plasmonic coupling and thus produce higher signal enhancement. A piece of Ag film is treated with the same procedure for comparison as well. As planned, single-stranded oligonucleotide is immobilized on the Ag ZNRs and the hybridization is detected by using the Alexa 488 labelled complimentary target oligonucleotide. As a reference, 3μl Alexa 488 labelled target solution at the concentration of 1.0×10-5M is sandwiched between a piece of Si wafer and cover slip for FL measurement. There is no neutral density (ND) filter for the reference while a 16x ND filter is used for the Ag ZNRs sample. Obviously, a much significant FL signal has been observed from the Ag ZNRs surface. We define EF2 as the ratio between the integrated FL intensity per excited molecule on Ag NRs and that on the Ag film reference. Through a quantitative calculation, the maximum EF2 is 28.28 at T = 25°C. Further, detection limit of the target DNA has been determined as 1.0×10-14M, i.e., 0.01pM. This result has been published on Biosensors and Bioelectronics. 4. Carry out DNA separation in MEF assisted capillary electrophoresis microfluidic system As planned, SiO2 NDs will act as a sieving mattress in CE microchannel for DNA separation. To achieve effective separation, a large mesh size and a small sieving opening are preferred. To this end, we have put great efforts in fabricating SiO2 NDs to fully fill out the channel. We have first tried the device without photoresist (PR) layer and observed the growth of SiO2 NDs step by step through three sequential LOAD depositions. After the first LOAD deposition, the curvature of the edge of the SiO2 film on the device top is smaller than that of the side wall. According to the mechanism of LOAD, the SiO2 film at the opening will grow faster than those NDs on the side wall. Therefore, the opening has been closed before SiO2 NDs fill out the channel. Then we have tested the device with PR layer. After the LOAD deposition, the PR layer, SiO2 NDs grown on PR side walls and SiO2 film on the top surface could be removed. However, the remaining tilting SiO2 NDs stick out of the channel and form an uneven device surface, which is not desirable for the subsequent PDMS bonding. Another try is to firstly remove PR layer and SiO2 film after 1st LOAD deposition. Since there has already some SiO2 NDs at the opening, the subsequent SiO2 film will not grow faster than those NDs in the channel. This is the best structure we have obtained so far. However, the device surface still has some bumpers and the SiO2 NDs bundle together after the acetone treatment. Two DNAs, lambda and T4, have been separated in the above SiO2 filled rectangular CE microchannels. Laser has been used to excite the YOYO®-1 nucleic acid stain bound to DNAs. It takes almost 2 minutes to achieve the separation and the resolution is not high. The possible reason is that the mesh size is not larger enough and there is still large opening in the SiO2 NDs seizing mattress. Also, we encounter some technical problems. Since the device surface is not smooth, the bumpers cause the serious leakage of the device after PDMS bonding. After comprehensive consideration, we have decided to change the strategy and will directly use Ag NDs as both the seizing mattress and fluorescence enhancer for DNA separation. In the work of the Ag NDs assisted CE separation for DNA, Ag ZNRs with folding number Z=3 are fabricated on flat substrate, sonicated into buffer, and injected into CE microchannel. The randomly orientated Ag ZNRs act as both seizing mattress and fluorescence enhancer. The typical electrophoregrams of lambda DNA and T4 DNA using 1cm long devices under different voltages shows that these two DNAs have been completely separated within half minute. Sieving performance has been evaluated using theoretical plate numbers, migration time and resolution. For 50V to 150V, a higher migration speed of DNA molecules was unveiled with the increase of voltage, due to the high electric force. The resolution, R_s=2Δt⁄((W_1+W_2)), which is the distance between the two peaks scaled by their average width at base, increases under higher field strength due to the more concentrated bands and higher fluorescent intensity. The plate number somewhat keeps unchanged for T4 DNA under different voltage schemes, while for lambda DNA, the plate numbers doubles when the voltage applied declines to 50V. These values are comparable to those reported DNA sieving devices and the control experiments are in progress. The above results have been summarized into a manuscript.

200813.label: Major findings and research outcome
200813.value: We have first explored the metal enhanced fluorescence (MEF) property of Ag nanorod (ND) arrays, made by localized oblique angle deposition, in a microfluidic-based capillary electrophoresis (CE) system. By measuring the fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC) solution sandwiched between the Ag NDs and a piece of cover slip, the enhancement factors are found as 3.7 ± 0.64 and 6.74 ± 2.04, for a solution thickness at 20.8 μm and 10 μm, respectively. If only consider the excited fluorophores, the corresponding effective enhancement factors are revealed to be relatively close, 259 ± 92 and 340 ± 102, respectively. Further, a multilayer of SiO2 NDs/Ag NDs is integrated with the CE device. At a microchannel depth of 10 μm, an enhancement of 6.5 folds is obtained for amino acids separation detection. Please refer to publication 1 in part C. To explore the MEF effects of different morphology of Ag NDs, Ag zigzag nanorod (ZNR) arrays have been studied for biomolecule-protein interaction and DNA hybridization. By changing the folding number, a 14-fold enhancement factor (EF) is obtained for biotin-neutravidin detection. The optimal folding number is decided as Z=7, owing to the high scattering intensity of Ag ZNRs. Further, Ag ZNRs deposited on a layer of Ag film have been introduced to the DNA hybridization and a significant signal enhancement has been observed through the fluorescence microscope. Through a detailed quantitative EF analysis, which excludes the enhancing effect from the increased surface area of ZNRs and only considers the contribution of MEF, an EF of 28 is achieved for the hybridization of two single-stranded oligonucleotides with 33 bases. Furthermore, a limit of detection is determined as 0.01pM. Please refer to publication 2 in part C. Two DNAs, lambda and T4, have been separated in the SiO2 NDs filled CE microchannel, though the resolution needs improvement. Then, Ag ZNRs with folding number Z=3 are fabricated on flat substrate, sonicated into buffer, and injected into CE microchannel, to act as both seizing mattress and fluorescence enhancer. The typical electrophoregrams of lambda DNA and T4 DNA using 1cm long devices under different voltages shows that these two DNAs have been completely separated within half minute. Sieving performance is comparable to those reported DNA sieving devices. Please refer to publication 3 (in preparation) in part C.

200813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
200813.value: Metal enhanced fluorescence (MEF) of Ag nanostructure arrays made by oblique angle deposition has been verified and applied to various research fields such as amino acid separation, biomolecule-protein binding, DNA hybridization and separation. Since fluorophore labelling is the most commonly used technique for signal detection, Ag nanostructure arrays with MEF property can find more applications such as immunoassays, biomolecule manipulation, and etc. Meanwhile, fluorescence detection is straightforward and can be easily integrated with portable instrumentation. Therefore, Ag nanostructure arrays based MEF device has great potential in use of daily diagnostics in clinics or fast bio-detection at the ports. Further, microfluidic system plays an important role in bio-analysis due to the advantages such as low usage of samples, easy control of bio-reaction and convenient integration of analytical processes. By decorating the microfluidic channels with either metallic or oxide nanostructures, the microfluidic system is good for real-time detection even with low volume of target analytes, or versatile development of Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems by adding more functionalities.

200813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
200813.value: DNA and protein are the fundamental subjects in many biological or diagnostic analysis, such as gene therapy and virus detection. In many cases, people need to separate different DNAs or proteins into individual ones, so that the thorough analysis of their property and function can be performed. Capillary electrophoresis (CE) is a commonly used technique to separate DNAs or proteins, where an electric field is applied to a microchannel and the injected mixture of biomolecules will move with different speed due to the difference in charges. One problem of the traditional CE device is that the buffer solution in the microchannel usually acts as a resistor. Thus, the Joule heating is generated and harmful for the separation. One solution is to minimize the cross-section area of the microchannel to reduce the current. At the same time, to avoid the difficulty in observing the signal from the decreased CE channel, the fluorescence intensity emitted by the fluorophore labeled on biomolecules needs to be enhanced. This project introduces a simple physical vapor deposition to place Ag nanorods into CE microchannel and they are able to enhance the fluorescence intensity, without sacrificing the separation performance.

201113.label: Project Objectives
201113.value: To elucidate the transformation profile, including mechanisms, by which acesulfame is degraded by photo-catalytic reactions with TiO2 and UV irradiation; To identify individual transformation intermediates and photo-degradation products of acesulfame using liquid chromatography-quadrupole-time-of-flight (LC-Q-TOF) and liquid chromatography-electrospray ionization-ion trap (LC-ESI-IT) mass spectrometry; To broaden the eco-toxicological database for a comprehensive risk assessment of acesulfame in aquatic compartments.
rows: To elucidate the transformation profile, including mechanisms, by which acesulfame is degraded by photo-catalytic reactions with TiO2 and UV irradiation;

To identify individual transformation intermediates and photo-degradation products of acesulfame using liquid chromatography-quadrupole-time-of-flight (LC-Q-TOF) and liquid chromatography-electrospray ionization-ion trap (LC-ESI-IT) mass spectrometry;
To broaden the eco-toxicological database for a comprehensive risk assessment of acesulfame in aquatic compartments.

201113.label: Realisation of objectives
201113.value: The stated project objectives have been completely and satisfactorily achieved. To begin with, we successfully developed a liquid chromatography/ion trap mass spectrometric (LC/MS) method for tracking of the transformation products (TPs) generated from the photodegradation of acesulfame (ACE). The chemical structure of individual TPs were established by using liquid chromatography/quadrupole-time-of-flight (LC/Q-TOF) mass spectrometry. In the work, we identified altogether 16 TPs upon photocatalytic degradation of ACE. Transformation mechanisms and pathways were established. TPs were collected and lyophilized for initial embryotoxicity study. ACE TPs displayed an augmented toxicity relative to the mother compound in embryo development. The results here further emphasize that ACE should be paid close attention not only because of its widespread application, ubiquitous occurrence and persistence in the aquatic systems but also because TPs generated by photocatalytic processes using UV-C and TiO2 are even more toxic than the original compound.

201113.label: Major findings and research outcome
201113.value: Artificial sweeteners have been recognized as emerging contaminants due to their wide application, environmental persistence and ubiquitous occurrence. Among them, acesulfame (ACE) has attracted much attention. After being discharged into the environment, ACE undergoes photolysis naturally. In the present study, ACE photodegradation behavior and identity of its transformation products (TPs), critical to understanding ACE’s environmental impact, were thoroughly investigated. We used a laboratory simulation study in examining ACE TPs and pathways under UV-C photolysis in the presence of TiO2. Photodegradation products of ACE were isolated and analyzed using the LC/Q-TOF-MS coupled with LC Ion Trap MS in the MSn mode. Out of the sixteen TPs that identified, our results show six new TPs that have not been previously identified. The molecular structures and transformation pathways were proposed. Further embryotoxicity tests showed that ACE TPs at the low g L-1 level produced significant adverse effects in tail detachment, heart rate, hatching rate and survival rate during fish embryo development. The identification of additional TPs with proposed transformation pathways of ACE, the increased toxicity of ACE after photolysis, and the fact that the accumulation of ACE TPs is increasingly likely make ACE contamination even more important.

201113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
201113.value: The present study provided critical information about the environmental fate of ACE upon catalytic photolysis. The generated TPs were found with higher toxicity than the original sweetener. Further studies on the environmental distribution, bioavailability, and biological effects of the TPs must be undertaken to ensure a comprehensive evaluation of the risks these chemicals pose to the natural environment. More importantly, a satisfactory removal approach for water treatment must be developed to properly and safely remove ACE and its TPs in the open aquatic environment.

201113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
201113.value: Of all artificial sweeteners, acesulfame of domestic sewage origin has the highest occurrence in environments worldwide. Indeed, the alarmingly high levels of acesulfame in finished drinking waters has upscaled acesulfame contamination to a global water crisis. From our present research data, it strongly suggest that transformation of acesulfame under catalytic photolysis (similar to prolonged exposure to sunlight in open environmental conditions) produces a suite of even more stable transformation products (TPs). After short-term and prolonged exposure of these TPs to zebrafish embryos, the embryotoxicity has been demonstrated. The entire set of transformation pathway, mechanism and toxicity data constitute a database for a comprehensive environmental risk assessment and spark novel insights that can guide further research toward improving waste treatment and, ultimately, our environment.

201213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
201213.value: 目前，許多智能材料以及分子和納米機器採用可激活的分子開關。為了適應未來的發展智能材料用於生物醫學目的的需要，結合分子開關和生物活性分子的特性，應該考慮（1）能夠在體外和在體內被激活， （2）分子的特異性，和（3）毒性。在這項建議我們打算構建新的生物活性，來自（ 1 ）大環內酯類機械互鎖輪烷的系統 - [n]輪烷，含有生物活性的大環內酯類藥物分子環可以被激活，和（2）超順磁性氧化鐵納米粒子與合適的多孔表面共價連接或物理誘捕的大環內酯類輪烷。合適的大環內酯類抗生素或免疫分子是利福平，雷帕黴素（西羅莫司），與環孢素A，將與多胺/聚銨或聚酰胺進行混合獲得最結合匹配的輪烷。 輪烷的親和力特性在溫滴定量熱測定。熱力，超聲或酶能激活輪烷內的大環內酯分子，選擇性釋放到受感染的器官，為的是減少體內大環內酯類毒性和耐藥性。我們突破性的建議作為特定的大環內酯類釋放療法和MRI診斷造影劑，能夠帶來更複雜的智能納米材料的設計和用途更廣泛的治療。

201213.label: Realisation of objectives
201213.value: All four objectives have been successfully achieved. We have featured novel drug rotaxanes by investigating high binding affinities between selected macrolides and bioactive linear-shaped compounds. A new [2]pseudorotaxane DB24C8-1-H·PF6 with dibenzo[24]crown-8 (DB24C8) crown ether-dibenzylammonium (1-H·PF6) binding which was formed by slippage approach at different solvents and temperature, had been isolated and characterized by NMR spectroscopy and mass spectrometry. The [2]pseudorotaxane DB24C8-1-H·PF6 was stable at room temperature. The dissociation rate of [2]pseudorotaxane DB24C8-1-H·PF6 could be tuned by using different stimuli such as triethylamine (TEA)/diisopropylethylamine (DIPEA) and dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO). In particular, the dissociation of [2]pseudorotaxane DB24C8-1-H·PF6 by an excess of TEA/DIPEA base mixture possessed a long and sustained, complete dissociation over 60 days. Other stimuli by DMSO possessed a relatively fast dissociation over 24 h. Organic rotaxane presents new directions toward controlled drug delivery. By combining molecular switches and biomimetic catalysts, fluorescence and pH-responsive switching along with the exclusive selectivity of dual catalytic reactions are demonstrated. A newly designed [2]rotaxane catalyst containing an anthracene group was used to visualize the catalytic reaction process upon switching the macrocycle. We have chemically modified and incorporated rotaxanes onto magnetic-responsive nanoparticles. A hybrid composite made up of superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoshells encapsulating the anticancer drug doxorubicin and bound together by poly(vinyl alcohol) was developed. Transcatheter arterial delivery in an in vivo liver tumor model led to embolization of the liver tumor blood vessels. Embolization was followed by disassembly of the composite. The nanoshells were then able to pass through the leaky tumor vasculature into the tumor tissue, thereby leading to slow and sustained release of the drug. As well as being relatively noncytotoxic, the composite was responsive to magnetic resonance imaging, thus making it a potentially useful theranostic agent. We have evaluated cytotoxcities of drug rotaxane nanoparticles and their derivatives and to facilitate magnetic resonance imaging diagnosis and stimuli-triggered macrolide release therapeutics.

201513.label: Project Title(Chinese)
201513.value: 高步次橢圓算子的熱核

201513.label: Project Objectives
201513.value: To extend the complex Hamilton-Jacobi theory to high step subelliptic operators. We will extend the complex Hamilton-Jacobi theory developed by Beals et al. [13] to make it suitable for subelliptic operators of steps higher than two, including some associated modifications of the action function and the volume element. To construct the heat kernels for high step subelliptic operators. We will apply the complex Hamilton-Jacobi theory to derive explicit formulas for the heat kernels of high step subelliptic operators, such as the step three Grushin operator and the subLaplacian on Engel group. We will also investigate some physical models, such as the quartic oscillator and double well potential. To derive the small time and large time asymptotic expansions for subelliptic heat kernels. We will apply the saddle point method (the method of steepest descent) to the integral representation of the heat kernel to derive a full asymptotic expansion for small time, in order to obtain asymptotic formula for the subRiemannian distance and the index theorems for subelliptic operators. The large time asymptotics of the heat kernels are closely related to the spectral zeta functions, and using integration by parts or the Mellin transform technique we will derive asymptotic expansions of the subelliptic heat kernels as the time tends to infinity.

201513.value: 次橢圓算子出現在許多分析與幾何問題的交叉口--這些領域包括冪零李群理論，多複變中的強擬凸區域，具退化擴散過程的概率理論，次黎曼幾何，控制論，布朗運動，以及量子力學的半經典分析。過去的幾十年中，許多數學家對次橢圓算子進行了廣泛深入的研究，其中有許多工作涉及到這些算子的基本解或熱核的構造。然而，現有大部份研究成果是有關於二步算子的，比如海森堡群上的次拉普拉斯算子，二步的 Grushin 算子及球上的次拉普拉斯算子。 以海森堡群上的次拉普拉斯算子為例，這是一個二步的次橢圓算子。現存有幾種不同的方法來構造其熱核，這些方法包括概率方法，擬橢圓算子技巧，傅利葉變換，隨機分析，路徑積分以及幾何方法。然而，所有這些方法都不適用於高步次橢圓算子的構造。 因此，一個有趣的問題是如何給出高步（大於二步）算子的熱核的顯式表達式，這是在本研究課題中考慮的問題。高步次橢圓算子包括三步 Grushin 型算子，Engel 群上的次拉普拉斯算子和Martinet 算子。我們首先將從推廣現有的處理二步算子的幾何方法（亦即哈密爾頓-雅克比理論）到高步算子。之後，我們會將此方法應用到三步 Grushin 算子和 Engel 群上的次拉普拉斯算子。在得到三步 Grushin 算子的熱核之後，我們會將該結果應用到一些重要的物理模型，比如四次振盪子及雙勢壘模型，的研究中。

201513.label: Realisation of objectives
201513.value: We have achieved all the three project objectives. With collaborations with coauthors and by independent investigations, we have established the general Hamilton-Jacobi theory, that is suitable for higher step operators and obtained the desired formulas of the heat kernels. Heat kernel asympototics are also studied for typical subelliptic operators. These results are addressed in the publications listed in this report. The PI has invited collaborators and researchers in the related areas for short-term visits and discussed the problems of this project, including Professor Der-Chen Chang of Georgetown University, USA, Professor Peter Greiner of the University of Toronto, Professor Ovidiu Calin from Eastern Michigan University, and Professor Jingxue Yin from South China Normal University. The PI has visited collaborators at the overseas institutes for discussing problems related to the project. Such visits include the University of Tokyo, Tokyo Science University, Academia Sinica, National Tsinghua University, etc.

201813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
201813.value: 為了解決和探討實際問題，往往需要構建一個涉及帶有條件的微分方程的數學模型。這樣一個模型的傳統的數值解法一般是將我們感興趣的區域按其關係分成一些有網格組成的小區域來進行的。而我們這個應用和計算數學研究項目的重點則是，是否可以用非網格的方法來解決我們的數學模型。 儘管一些景觀，汽車或飛機可能有一些網格化的美學訴求，但不幸的是，網格的建立在許多計算方面都是一個“瓶頸”。因此，雖然實際計算可能只要很短的時間，但要具體應用到複雜的幾何形狀上去網格卻可能需要數天或數週的時間。所以，最近出現了大量在對不使用網格的這類新的計算方法，即無網格方法，的研究。自2000年以來，這個項目的研究者在無網格方法的相關算法理論和的應用上面多了大量的工作。主要的研究目的就是希望開發一種新的算法，可避免任何網建設和利用自適應過程，同時也為了方便用戶尋求一個強大和高效的計算解決方案的數學模型。 對於由Kansa引入的關於時間獨立的線性偏微分方程模型來說，其無網格非對稱技術有一個很重要的缺失，那就是在解的收斂性上缺少堅實的數學根基。這個項目的建立也是希望為科學和工程學領域提供一個穩定的數值算法，並且可以對有約束的最小二乘Kansa方法在理論和算法上有所發展。理論部份是通過對該無網格方法解的近似度及收斂速度來確定其有效性；在應用方面，則會提供實例來驗證理論部份對此算法高效及先進性的證明。進一步的一些合適的技術，如自適應數據點細化，自適應貪婪算法，也將會在無網格數值分化計劃中發揮重要的作用。

201813.label: Major findings and research outcome
201813.value: Though Kansa methods are very successful in a large variety of applications for engineering and science, there were no proven results about it for over 10 years. After many unsuccessful attempts to establish such a foundation, it was revealed that there are extremely rare cases where the original approach can fail because the underlying linear system can be singular. In order to ensure solvability, we proved that overtesting is required. Next,we found a partial answer to the convergence of overdetermined Kansa formulations. Our precious analysis was carried out based on the continuous and discrete maximum norms. We showed that the max-norm minimizer of a residual functional converges to the exact solution at the optimal speed. On one hand, it was nice to finally have a convergence theory for Kansa methods. On the other hand, the nonlinear nature of this formulation cannot be handled effortlessly and required a specially designed adaptive algorithm. In this project, we attempted to extend the theories to the least squares minimizer and numerically verified in extended precision arithmetic that the least-squares minimizer also converges at the optimal rate. Recently, we worked out the necessary assumptions for a class of weighted least-squares algorithms to be convergent. Our main contribution here is the proof of an inverse inequality for kernels in bounded domains. We robustly showed the conditions on the RBF, trial centers, and collocation points for our proven error estimates to apply. This allows us to theoretically justify if Kansa methods are suitable for the given problem. The research results on convergence analysis of Kansa methods were recently accepted for publication in SIAM J. Numerical Analysis. The newest result was a block-greedy algorithm. The main challenge is that the greedy strategy does not generalize to block form in a trivial way. Therefore, to properly select multiple rows and columns in each iteration, we propose some economic ways to select/preselect rows and columns. Then, we deploy expansive algorithms on small submatrices to make final selections. By designing with complexity in mind, every iteration of the block-greedy algorithm can be interpreted as a combination of Householder reflections and the Gram-Schmidt process. Other features are added to improve accuracy and robustness. Most importantly, the new algorithm significantly reduces the computational cost from the previous by one order of magnitude. This work was published in SIAM J. Scientific Computing.

201813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
201813.value: The work of theory development does not stop at PDEs on regular domains. Having the inverse inequality proven, we successfully extended our convergence theory to meshfree methods for solving PDEs on manifolds. This yields a rigorous convergence proof for the Orthogonal Gradient Method in literature. Our next project is to understand how to properly apply spatial overtesting and develop new robust formulations for solving parabolic PDEs. Its success will further benefit all practitioners by providing theoretically correct formulations to set up Kansa methods for solving a wider class of PDEs in computational sciences.

201813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
201813.value: Mathematical models or differential equations are meaningful only if they can somehow mirror the overly complicated real world. Similarly, numerical methods are useful only if they can produce approximations guaranteed to converge to the outcome that the mathematical model predicts. It could take tens of years for some good numerical strategies to mature and become a well-established class of numerical methods with a complete and rigid theoretical framework. Take the finite element method as an example. It waited for a quarter of a century to get its rigorous mathematical foundation. This project established some theoretical foundations for the unsymmetric radial basis function (RBF) collocation method, which is also known as the Kansa method in the community. This approach requires no re-formulation of the PDE and no triangularization. As long as one knows how to program for an interpolation problem, it only takes minutes to understand and code up something for the Kansa method. Since invented, the Kansa method has been widely used in vast numbers of applications in physics and engineering. As Kansa methods gain popularity, this work also provide ways to stably solve the resulting severely ill-conditioned linear systems.

201913.label: Realisation of objectives
201913.value: In this funding period, we have successfully achieved all of the project objectives regarding the exploration of substitutionally inert octahedral iridium(III) complexes as direct inhibitors of tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α). Firstly, we have designed and synthesized a series of novel octahedral iridium(III) complexes as selective TNF-α protein−protein interaction modulators. We explored the effect of incorporating different substituents such as halogen, nitro, aliphatic and/or aromatic groups to various positions of the ancillary ligands in order to optimize the steric, electronic and/or lipophilic properties of the complexes. Furthermore, we synthesized novel cyclometallated iridium(III) complexes containing expanded aromatic C^N and N^N donor scaffolds in order to form effective Van der Waals and hydrophobic interactions with the protein−protein interaction surface of the TNF-α dimer. We first tested the effect of the complexes at inhibiting TNF-α-induced NF-κB activity in a human hepatocellular carcinoma cell line (HepG2) using the luciferase assay. The most potent complex exhibited the highest ability to inhibit TNF-α induced NF-κB luciferase activity, with 61.5% inhibition at 10 μM. Based on above experimental results, the efficacies of the “hit” metal complex against the TNF-α interaction was further optimized by modification of the organic ligands around the metal center. A series of iridium(III) complexes were designed as structural analogues of most promising complex. Some complexes contain the same C^N ligand as most promising complex but vary in the nature of the N^N ligand, while other complexes carry the same N^N ligand of most promising complex but possess different C^N ligands. The inhibition effect of NF-κB cell signaling pathway of the complexes was then evaluated by investigating IκBα serine phosphorylation levels using Western blotting. IκBα phosphorylation was decreased after co-treatment of cells with the complexes in a dose-dependent ways. The results showed that these complexes could inhibit TNF-α-induced NF-κB activity in transfected HepG2 cells. We presume that the decrease of IκBα phosphorylation is due, at least in part, to the inhibition of TNF-α activity by the complexes. And then we utilized the complexes for their inhibition on TNF-α−TNFR binding in vitro. An enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay was performed to verify whether the complexes were targeting TNF-α−TNFR binding in the cellular NF-κB signaling assay. The isolated corresponding C^N and N^N ligands showed negligible TNF-α−TNFR inhibitory activity, indicating that the assembly of the ligands into an intact complex is essential for biological activity. These results suggest that the observed in cellulo effects exhibited by the complexes could be attributed, at least in part, to its inhibition of the TNF-α−TNFR protein−protein interaction. Furthermore, we synthesized enantiopure Λ and Δ to investigate the effect of stereo-chemistry on biological potency according to a method reported by Meggers' group. The isomers were characterized by circular dichroism, and their potency was investigated by AlphaScreen assay and ELISA. The results showed both enantiomers dose-dependently inhibited the TNF-α−TNFR interaction, with Λ complex again being more potent than Δ complex. The results from this project have led to multiple publications in peer-reviewed journals, such as Journal of Medicinal Chemistry, Chemical Communications, Chemical Science, Biosensors and Bioelectronics, Scientific Reports and other journals. Our expertise in the field of metal-based drug discovery has also been recognized by recent review articles in high impact factor journals (Coord. Chem. Rev., 2016, 319, 25; Chem. Sci., 2015, 6, 871; Dalton Trans., 2016, 45, 2762).

201913.label: Major findings and research outcome
201913.value: In this funding period, we explored the effect of incorporating different substituents such as halogen, nitro, aliphatic and/or aromatic groups to various positions of the ancillary ligands in order to optimize the steric, electronic and/or lipophilic properties of the complexes. Moreover, we synthesized novel cyclometallated iridium(III) complexes containing expanded aromatic C^N and N^N donor scaffolds in order to form effective Van der Waals and hydrophobic interactions with the protein−protein interaction surface of the TNF-α dimer. To achieve this goal, we have synthesized a number of octahedral iridium(III) complexes bearing different C^N and N^N ligands which are designed to target TNF-α and then investigated their TNF-α-induced NF-κB activity in a human hepatocellular carcinoma cell line. Afterwards, a series of iridium(III) complexes were designed as structural analogues of the most promising complex. The most promising complex inhibited the TNF-α−TNFR protein–protein interaction as revealed by an ELISA test. Moreover, the complex inhibited IκBα phosphorylation in a dose-dependent fashion in cells. Structure−activity relationship analysis indicated that the presence of the pbt C^N ligand and the arrangement of methyl groups on the tm-phen N^N ligand were important for biological potency. Moreover, the iridium(III) center plays a critical role in organizing the structure of the bioactive metal complex, as the isolated ligands were found to be completely inactive. Overall, the results indicated that the novel iridium(III) complex was a potent inhibitor of the TNF-α−TNFR protein−protein interaction in vitro and in cellulo (J. Med. Chem. 2016, 59, 4026). Furthermore, we have also designed and synthesized cyclometallated iridium(III)/rhodium(III) complexes as other protein−protein interaction inhibitors. For instance, we developed an iridium(III)-based irreversible protein–protein interaction inhibitor of BRD4 as a potent anticancer (Chem. Sci., 2015, 6, 5400). We also firstly reported organometallic p53/hDM2 protein−protein interaction inhibitor (Oncotarget, 2016, 7, 13965). Moreover, we reported the inhibition of TLR1/2 dimerization by enantiomers of metal complexes (Chem. Commun., 2016, 52, 12278). Furthermore, we developed an enantiomeric iridium(III) metal-based compound inhibition of the Ras/Raf interaction and repression of renal cancer xenografts in vivo (Chem. Sci., 2017, 8, 4756). Furthermore, our expertise in DNA-based luminescence sensing assay has been recognized by recent review articles in high impact factors journal (Coord. Chem. Rev., 2016, 319, 25; Chem. Sci., 2015, 6, 871; Dalton Trans., 2016, 45, 2762).

201913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
201913.value: The discovery of novel iridium(III) complexes as direct inhibitors of TNF-α could further the development of more potent organometallic complexes as protein–protein interaction inhibitors. Previously, we investigated the inhibitory activity of the complexes in cellulo, and showed their superior ability to inhibit TNF-α induced NF-κB activity compared to the positive control compound. Based on our successful in vitro and in cellulo results, the complexes are not further investigated as anti-inflammatory agents for the potential treatment of TNF-α-associated diseases in this stage. In the future, we can also investigate the inhibitory activity of the complex in an animal model in vivo, potentially developing the lead iridium(III) complexes as anti-inflammatory agents for the potential treatment of TNF-α-associated diseases.

201913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
201913.value: In this project, we synthesized a number iridium(III) complexes as selective TNF-α protein−protein interaction modulators. Among these complexes, the most potent complex was identified after investigating their TNF-α inhibitory activity in a human hepatocellular carcinoma cell line. We then prepared a series of iridium(III) complexes as structural analogues of the lead complex, and identified the most potent complex after a second round of screening. This complex showed the TNF-α−TNFR protein–protein interaction in an ELISA test, and also inhibited IκBα phosphorylation in cells. We found that the activity of the iridium(III) complex was dependent upon the organization of the bioactive metal complex by the iridium center. In summary, all the data indicate that these complexes represent a promising scaffold for the further development of more potent organometallic TNF-α inhibitors. In the future, these complexes could further be developed as anti-inflammatory agents for the potential treatment of TNF-α-associated diseases.

202013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
202013.value: Contrast enhancement is one of the major tasks in image processing. The purpose of image contrast enhancement is to increase the visibility of images and to make them more suitable for other image processing applications and analysis. Histogram equalization is one of the well-known methods for enhancing the contrast of images due to its simplicity and comparatively better performance on different kinds of images. The idea is that a transformation function is applied to an input image such that the contrast of the transformed image is enhanced. Existing histogram equalization methods do not distinguish the image pixel values in different pixel locations, their performance may cause some unexpected distortions in practice. Several variational formulations of histogram equalization have been proposed and studied in the literature. In these formulations, either a mean brightness constraint is not considered or the differences among pixel transformations at the nearby pixel locations are not studied. The main aim of this proposal is to develop a histogram equalization algorithm for image contrast enhancement. Our idea is to propose a variational approach containing an energy functional to determine a local transformation such that the histogram can be redistributed locally, and the brightness of the transformed image can be preserved. In order to minimize the differences among the local transformation at the nearby pixel locations, the spatial regularization of the transformation is also incorporated in the functional for the equalization process. In the variational problem, we consider both the H1-norm regularization and the total variation regularization of the transformation in the model. The existence and uniqueness of their minimizers of the two proposed models will be studied and analyzed. Moreover, the alternating direction method is developed to solve the two proposed models. Its convergence and performance will be analyzed and evaluated respectively by testing for a wide range of image types in different image processing applications. Applications of variational methods to color images and high dynamic range images will be considered, studied and analyzed. We extend and develop our variational histogram equalization model (i) in the CIE LCH color space to enhance color image contrast, and remove unnatural appearances including color missing and visually disturbing artifacts; and (ii) in the generation of a high dynamic range image from a low dynamic range image through spatial regularization and range regularization. 對比度增強是在圖像處理的主要任務之一。目的是提高圖像的可見性，並使其更適用於其他圖像處理應用程序和分析。均衡化是一個簡單增強對比度的圖像方法，它在不同類型的圖像的表現也相當不錯。它的原理是利用一個變換函數應用到輸入圖像來增強圖像的對比度。現有的直方圖均衡化方法不區分的圖像中的像素值不同的像素的位置，其表現在實踐中可能會造成一些不是很好圖像結果。在文獻中，一個平均亮度約束或不同附近的像素位置像素的轉換之間的研究並沒有分析。 這個提案的主要目的是開發一個圖像對比度增強的直方圖均衡算法。我們的想法是提出一個變分方法能不同附近的像素位置像素的轉換的直方圖，以及轉換後的圖像的亮度可以約束。為了盡量減少改造的差異，在附近的像素之間的差異位置，空間也納入了正規化的改造功能均衡過程。在變分方法上，我們同時考慮H1範數正和全變差正改造該模型。兩項模型的存在性和唯一性將會研究和分析。交替方向法開發解決， 收斂性和性能將會進行分析。 我們會在不同的圖像測試和評估新的變分方法。 彩色圖像和高動態範圍圖像中的應用變分法將會研究和分析。我們會研究直方圖均衡模型（i）在CIE LCH顏色空間，以提高彩色圖像的對比度及（ii）在一種高動態範圍圖像的產生，從低動態範圍圖像通過空間的正規化和範圍正規化。

202013.value: The objectives of this project are achieved by developing variational models and efficient algorithms for energy functionals in historgram equalization. This model has been proposed and studied in [Output #1,2,4,7]. Both theoretical [Output #2,3,7] and experimental results [Output #1,2,4,7] are analyzed and reported in several publications to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed models. In the reported publications [Output #1,2,3,4,5,6,7], we have used image data sets to show how the proposed models and algorithms can work for different applications (including color images and high dynamic range images) and the performance of the proposed models and algorithms is better than the other testing methods.

202013.label: Major findings and research outcome
202013.value: In [Output #2], we develop a histogram equalization algorithm for image contrast enhancement. The basic idea is to propose a variational approach containing an energy functional to determine a local transformation such that the histogram can be redistributed locally, and the brightness of the transformed image can be preserved. The H1-norm and TV norm regularization of the local transformation is employed into the functional for the equalization process. In [Output #1,4], we generalize this framework to expanding the bit-depth and tone mapping for other image processing applications. In [Output #1,3,7], we analyze the proposed variational models by showing the existence and uniqueness of the minimizers of the two proposed models. Theoretical results for convergence analysis of the proposed numerical methods are established to support the proposed model. In [Output #5], we further study the total variation based nonlinear restoration problems in high-dynamic ranging imaging. The nonlinear least squares data-fitting is required in the formulation and analysis. By using the proposed framework, a cartoon-plus-texture image decomposition method for blind deconvolution is published in [Output #6].

202013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
202013.value: In the work, we study models for histogram equalization. It is interesting to extend to a a spatially variant total variational model to correct chromatic aberration that causes false color artifacts near edges in captured images. In general, it may be difficult to find chromatic regions for image processing correction. The idea is to use histogram equalization model for detection and and make use of spatially variant model to control the gradient and intensity matching between the red and blue color channels and the green color channel at the edges.

202013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
202013.value: Contrast enhancement is an important task in image processing. Image contrast enhancement is to increase the visibility of images and to make them more suitable for other image processing applications and analysis. The principle of intensity-based methods is that a transformation function is applied to an input image such that the contrast of the transformed image is enhanced. Histogram equalization is one of the well-known methods for enhancing the contrast of images due to its simplicity and comparatively better performance on different kinds of images. In this research, the perceived distribution (histogram) of gray-levels in an image should be uniform. Our main research contribution is to propose and develop optimization methods to determine a local transformation such that the histogram can be redistributed locally instead of globally. Therefore, the model can preserve more local image details and make the enhancement according to such details of an input image. We can deal with by using the cumulative distribution function of the normalized histogram of the image pixel values. In this project, we successfully study and analyze such new histogram equalization models and present interesting theoretical results for further mathematical development and application results for the other possible applications in image processing.

202213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
202213.value: This study will use cores to develop a detailed later Pleistocene (several hundred thousand years) diatom-based environmental/climatic history for the Koora Graben and for the Lake Magadi Basin in the southern Kenya Rift. Currently, there are no long and continuous environmental records. The use of cores from two different basins, within 10 km of each other, should help to discriminate between regional climatic signals and tectonically-induced local environmental changes. The project will also relate these data, in turn, to existing outcrop-based sedimentary records from the Olorgesailie Basin. This latter area has a rich mammalian record and is archaeologically world-famous for its Acheulian and Middle Stone Age tool assemblages, which have shed considerable light on past hominin activities. However, there are problems of continuity at Olorgesailie in terms of the environmental record, which incorporates detailed changes reconstructed from lake and wetland sediments, punctuated by breaks associated with the development of terrestrial/fluvial conditions. These latter depositional breaks are also the parts of the sequence that tend to be associated with the stone tools. The challenge is to develop a better understanding of these breaks in the record so that hypotheses on the role of climate change in driving human physical and cultural evolution can be more fully tested. This broad aim also falls within the remit of the Hominin Sites and Paleolakes Drilling Project (HSPDP), which is carrying out a co-ordinated study of five major hominin sites in East Africa. HSPDP will supply this project with samples from a long core (several hundred meters) from lake Magadi that will cover much of the MSA and upper Acheulian. The Smithsonian Institute (Olorgesailie Geological Field Group) will also be supplying two cores from the Koora Graben that have already been recovered (55 m and 135 m long) for work under this proposal. The PI is closely involved with both organisations. In order to obtain highly detailed environmental records the target drilling sites have been selected at locations with well-developed lacustrine sedimentary sequences where environmental archives should be best developed. The Koora Graben sediments have never been studied previously. The Magadi deposits have been investigated in outcrop, especially from a chemical sedimentology viewpoint, but apart for one eight-meter-long core there is no continuous record. This research will focus on developing a diatom stratigraphy, supported by data on mineralogy and a chronology based on a variety of dating techniques (14C, 40Ar/39Ar and U/Th). 本研究透過分析岩石核心樣本所取得的數據，來編寫南肯亞裂谷加廸湖盆地及Koora裂谷在更新世（Pleistocene）晚期，矽藻生長的環境及氣候歷史。現存有關該地區的環境紀錄不但數量少，而且缺乏連貫性。這研究正補充了當中的空白。使用的岩石核心樣本來自兩個相距十公里的取樣點，這兩個樣本有助於分辨地區性氣候變化與地殼活動所導致的環境改變。 本研究所得的數據會與肯亞盆地現有的沉積岩紀錄對照。肯亞盆地是世界著名阿舍利文化（Acheulian）和石器時代中期的考古場地，蘊藏著非常豐富的哺乳類動物紀錄。然而，該盆地亦同樣缺少有連貫性，而且包含湖泊和濕地沉積物細微變化的環境紀錄。這個不足，同時亦打斷了對陸地及河流情況變化的紀錄。環境紀錄的殘缺不全影響了我們對早期人類使用石器工具的演變的了解。 本研究除了為上述的空隙補白，更會在宏觀的層面上加深氣候改變對人類進化的作用的了解。此項目同時與一個在東非進行，名為‘古人類遺址與古湖鑽探項目’（HSPDP）的項目配合。HSPDP會為本研究提供在加廸湖鑽取，長約數百米的岩石核心樣本。再者，Olorgesailie地質考察組會為本項目提供兩個取自Koora裂谷，55米至135米長的岩石核心樣本。本項目的主要研究員同時密切地參與上述的兩個組織中。 鑽探岩石核心樣本的地點是擁有完好湖泊沉積次序的地區。這樣才能透過解讀岩石樣本來找出詳細的環境變化。本項目是對Koora裂谷沉積物的首次研究；而對加廸湖沉積物的研究亦深入到岩層的八米以下。利用各種不同的技術（14C, 40Ar/39Ar 和U/Th）所取得的礦物學數據；輔以年代學資料，本研究將會建構一個矽藻的地層學。

202213.label: Realisation of objectives
202213.value: Three long cores were obtained in collaboration with the Olorgesailie Drilling Project and the Hominin Sites and Paleolakes Drilling Projects. These cores are 164 m long in the Koora Basin and 135 m and 194 m long in the Magadi Basin. Koora Basin core sampling was carried out in March 2014 in Minneapolis, where the core had previously been sent after recovery. The two Magadi cores were drilled in the Lake Magadi Basin in July 2014 and sampled at the LacCore storage and analysis facility in Minneapolies in January 2015. Cores from both the Koora Graben and Lake Magadi Basin have been fully analysed for diatoms and has been logged in detail by the PI and a PhD student. Magadi samples also yielded excellent pollen and geochemical records that date back about one million years, which was not expected when the project was originally put together. Both Owen and the PhD student have presented the results at several conferences in the USA and Europe. The project has therefore achieved all of the objectives, with additional new data also generated. In particular, we have developed detailed diatom stratigraphies (Objective 1) as well as pollen and geochemical records. These data have been used to generate environmental records for the southern Kenya Rift that allow the recognition of climate and environmental change and the influence of tectonism (faulting, basin fragmentation, rising geothermal fluids and CO2 gas phases) on the preserved core stratigraphy (Objective 2). These environmental histories have been related to changes from Acheulian to Middle Stone Age toolkits (Objective 3) and, in addition, to mammal extinctions in the area. The results have been integrated with data from other HSPDP members in developing the environmental records further (Objective 4).

202213.label: Major findings and research outcome
202213.value: Diatoms in the Koora core and large parts of the Magadi sequences are dominated by a variety of planktonic Aulacoseira, Cyclotella and Thalassiosira. Species comprising these genera and other planktonic, benthonic and epiphytic taxa preserve a detailed record of lakes that fluctuated in depth, extent and chemistry. The data document the presence of freshwater and saline lakes as well as wetlands. Diatom transfer functions from the Koora and Magadi basins indicate that these water bodies fluctuated widely in conductivity between ~200 to >20,000 μS cm−1, with pH changing between about 7.5 and 11.5. The palaeolakes also periodically exceeded diatom tolerance limits and intermittently dried out. Pollen are generally lacking in the Koora basin sediments, but deposits in the Magadi core contain common pollen that document a wide range of habitats, including forests, woodlands and grasslands that could have supported the presence of hominins and their activities in the region. Fungal spore data support pollen inferences and indicate periods when large mammals might have been common. The data indicate progressive aridiﬁcation since about 510 thousand years ago (ka). This long-term drying trend was interrupted by many wet-dry cycles, with the greatest variability developing during times of high eccentricity-modulated precession. Intense aridiﬁcation between 455–325 ka is apparent in both the Magadi pollen record and the Koora diatom data, with relatively persistent arid conditions after 250 ka and through to the present. The transition to arid conditions coincides with the Mid-Brunhes Event and partially over-laps with mammalian extinctions in the South Kenya Rift between 500–400 ka. The 455–325 ka arid phase developed between the period when the last Acheulean tools in the South Kenya Rift are reported and prior to the appearance of Middle Stone Age artefacts, by at least 325 ka and took place close to the ﬁrst appearance of humans around 315 ka elsewhere in Africa. Our data suggest that increasing mid-late Pleistocene aridiﬁcation may have been a driver in the physical and cultural evolution of H. sapiens in East Africa.

202213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
202213.value: The research is directly related to two major international projects: the Olorgesailie Drilling Project and the Hominin Sites and Paleolakes Drilling Projects that are attemptoing to relate environmental change to human evolution for differeing time periods over the last four million years. These records are being developed from six basins in Ethiopia and Kenya, with results starting to appear for each basin. Future collaborative work will involve the integration of these datasets in order to better understand the driving processes behind hominin evolution. Meetings of the different groups take place annually, with the next scheduled for January 2019 at which time the focus will shift from individual basin records to the integration of the large datasets generated.

202213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
202213.value: Previous research hypotheses have related human evolution to climate change. However, most of the theories lack detailed evidence for a direct relationship between climate and human development. This research shows that there has been a gradual increase in aridity since about 500,000 years ago with a major change developing in environments after about 430,000 years ago. Intensely dry conditions in the Magadi and Koora Basins can be linked to mammal extinctions and changes in the types of stone tools used in the southern Kenya Rift. The information generated suggests that climate changes have had an important influence on human cultural and physical evolution.

202413.label: Major findings and research outcome
202413.value: About objective 1: In [7], we derive some reduction procedures on the Laplacian, signless Laplacian and normalized Laplacian characteristic polynomials of a graph respectively. In [6], we consider how the normalized Laplacian spectral radius of a non-bipartite graph behaves by several graph operations. As an application, the largest normalized Laplacian spectral radius of non-bipartite unicyclic graphs with fixed order and girth is determined. Moreover, the largest and the smallest normalized Laplacian spectral radius among non-bipartite unicyclic graphs with fixed order are also determined, respectively. In [3], we investigate the behavior on the second normalized Laplacian eigenvalue (called normalized algebraic connectivity) when the graph is perturbed by separating an edge. This result can be used to determine the minimum value of normalized algebraic connectivity of trees and unicyclic graphs. As an application, in [4] we classified six classes of trees whose normalized algebraic connectivity are the same within the class. Using the result and techniques represented in [7] we determined the minimum normalized algebraic connectivity of unicyclic graphs with fixed girth. About objective 2: Normalized Laplacian energy (also called Randic energy) is the sum of absoluate value of eigenvalues subtracting by 1. Normalized Laplacian Estrada energy is a variation of Randic energy. In [1], some bounds for normalized Laplacian Estrada energy af a graph in terms of its vertex number, maximum (or minimum) degree are obtained, some inequalities between In [8], we established new upper and lower bounds on the Randic energy of a graph in terms of its structural parameters, such as the vertex number, the general Randic index, the rank of its adjacency matrix, etc. In [2], we obtained some new upper and lower bounds on the normalized Laplacian spectral radius for connected graphs, triangulation graphs and maximal planar graphs, respectively.
