202713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
202713.value: Recently, a team of researchers from HKU, UCSD, Marburg and HKBU conducted experiments of pattern formation in open geometry by controlling the motility of bacteria via a synthetic circuit [C. Liu et al., Science 334, 238 (2011)]. The work opens up a novel route to pattern formation in autonomous systems without invoking external guidance. It has been shown that the Fisher-Kolmogorov type equations that implement the density-dependent diffusivity of an active species correctly reproduce the stripe patterns seen in the experiments. However, a number of important theoretical issues have been left unanswered so far. In this project, we construct and analyze a three-species continuum model that takes into account the delayed response of bacterium to its environment. The multi-species model is expected to give a more accurate description of the microscopic process that gives rise to the front instability and stripe formation. Traveling wave solutions to the continuum equations will be worked out and their stability against small perturbations analyzed. The cyclic generation of new stripes during the colony expansion will be investigated numerically. Build on this model, we will examine the robustness of the pattern formation process against variations in cell motility, either transient (due to protein copy number fluctuations) or genetic (due to mutations). We will also investigate whether presence of a residual chemotactic component in bacterial movement significantly alters certain key aspects of the pattern formation process. The study will yield a better understanding of the robustness of the proposed pattern formation scheme and the conditions that need to be fulfilled for it to work. It will not only enable a closer comparison between the modeling and experimental results, but also open up new directions of research for the active matter community. 最近，香港大學，加州大學聖地牙哥分校，瑪律堡大學和香港浸會大學的一個研究團隊進行了一項有趣的合成生物學實驗，用人工設計的分子線路控制細菌的運動，進而使菌落生長出可控的二維斑圖 [C. Liu等人，科學334， 238 （2011）] 。這項工作為無需外部引導的自發斑圖構建開闢了一條新的途徑。研究表明，從描述菌落生長的Fisher - Kolmogorov方程出發，引入隨細菌密度增加而降低的擴散係數，便可重現實驗觀測到的條紋圖案。然而，一些重要的理論細節尚未得到滿意的解答。在這個項目中，我們將構造和分析一個包含細菌內部狀態對環境滯後響應的三態模型 。多態模式可以區分細菌個體的狀態差異，從而更準確地描述菌落前沿出現不穩和條紋的動力學過程 。 我們將找出連續性方程的行波解，並分析其對小擾動的穩定性。運用數值方法，我們將研究群落擴展時週期性生成新條紋的過程。在此模型的基礎上，我們將研究斑圖對細胞運動差異的魯棒性，包括由細胞內蛋白質的拷貝數變化引起的暫態漲落或或由突變引起的遺傳性差異。另外，實驗中採用的菌種可能具有殘餘的化學趨向性，其對斑圖形成一些關鍵環節的影響也將是該專案的一個研究內容。這項研究將對斑圖的魯棒性及其形成的條件建立更深入和完整的認識 。它不僅通過更細緻的模型說明相應實驗的重要細節，也可以為活性物質的研究開闢新的研究方向。

202713.label: Realisation of objectives
202713.value: As stated in the original proposal, the main aim of the study is two-fold: i) a microscopic theory of the sequential pattern formation in the engineered bacterial system that in particular incorporates effects arising from delayed response and variable motility among individual cells; ii) an understanding of the robustness of pattern formation through motility control in the presence of the effects mentioned above. Significant progress has been made in both fronts as detailed below. Expanded models with internal cell states (objectives 1&4) — The phenomenological two- and three-component models introduced in our previous work is able to capture key features of stripe formation under density-dependent motility control. Through the course of this project, we came to a deeper understanding of the drawbacks of this class of coarse-grained particle models. On the biophysics side, they do not allow for systematic incorporation of single-cell data for improved predictions. On the mathematics side, they tend to exhibit certain pathological features associated with a sharp motility function, particularly near the onset of the patterning process. To overcome these difficulties, we constructed expanded models by introducing an internal state variable for each particle/cell, i.e., the CheZ protein concentration that directly control the duration of run and tumble intervals. The synthesis and degradation rates of the protein are set by the local AHL concentration and the rate of cell division, respectively. The robustness of the pattern formation process can then be studied through the dynamics of CheZ which serves as a master integrator of cellular and environmental perturbations. We have studied various versions of the expanded model both numerically and analytically. On the numerical side, it is difficult to handle a continuous distribution of CheZ values so we restrict the number of internal states to two or three. In the 2-state model, cells with a high CheZ value are motile while the ones with a low CheZ value are immotile. The forward and backward conversion rates between the two populations are chosen to be a function of the local cell density. In the 3-state model, there is an intermediate population where cells are motile but CheZ expression has stopped. The turnover rate of CheZ in these cells is set by the rate of cell division. Numerical simulations of both models show stripe formation when the suppression of cell motility happens sufficiently fast as the cell density increases. On the analytic side, through collaboration with Prof. Min Tang at Shanghai Jiaotong University, we have constructed partial differential equations for the mean cell density as a function of its spatial coordinates and internal state. Prof. Min Tang’s group developed numerical algorithms to solve the PDEs, and have used the model to study the dependence of front speed and pattern wavelength on the speed of individual cells as well as the turnover rate of CheZ within each cell. They also made the interesting observation that, while the turnover rate of CheZ does not affect significant the wavelength of the pattern, it has a very strong effect on the density profile of the stripes behind the front. A slower turnover rate allows cells to continue to diffuse even when they are well inside the expanding colony. This suggests that the initial instability that leads to cell density oscillations takes place at the very frontal region. We are currently investigating this issue further. Onset of density oscillations in the expanding colony (objectives 2&3) — Identifying the stability limit of a steadily propagating front turns out to be a much harder problem than demonstrating the existence of oscillatory solutions. Through pains-taking numerical studies, we have established the existence of a localized mode that undergoes a Hopf bifurcation at the transition point from stable to pulsating fronts. We have also provided a detailed description of this mode, including its spatial profile and temporal oscillation period. Our numerical experiments indicate that the continuous transition scenario through a Hopf bifurcation is likely limited to the situation when the motility function is sufficiently smooth. This indicates possibly two types of transitions leading to the striped phase, one is first order as described in the 2012 PRL paper by X. Fu et al., and one is continuous as we investigated here. The continuous transition scenario seems to match better the experimental radial profiles. The above results were obtained by numerical diagonalization of a discretized eigenvalue problem. In the model considered previously, the diffusion term is complicated as the cell motility is set directly by the local AHL concentration. In the expanded model, cell motility is set by its internal CheZ concentration which makes it easier to handle the linear stability equations analytically. To find the mode localized at the frontal region that drives the instability, we have devised a WKB method to analyze the eigenvalue problem. This work is still in progress. The above results are currently in the form of research notes and student thesis. The first part involving model construction and numerical investigation has been completed. Publications have been delayed by our desire to combine the theoretical work with experimental results from Dr. Chenli Liu and Xiongfei Fu’s group at SIAT in Shenzhen. We will have the manuscript ready and submission in six months and report to the RGC accordingly. The second part on the localized mode at the propagating front needs further simplification. We will intensify our efforts in the coming months to bring the work to a fruitful conclusion.

202713.label: Major findings and research outcome
202713.value: Construction of motility switching models that show pattern forming behavior — Our previous work has focused on a “particle” model where the diffusivity of individual particles is set directly by a diffusing chemical AHL. The “cell” model developed in this work treats the diffusivity of a cell as an internal dynamic variable (a function of the intracellular CheZ protein concentration). The rate of change of this variable is determined by the process of gene expression and cell division. This class of models are closer to the biological reality and also allows more quantitative aspects of the pattern forming process, such as the linear dependence of stripe wavelength against front velocity, to be explained. It can also be applied to a number of other situations such as gene expression change through cell-cell contact. Simulations of the model have indeed confirmed predicted behavior, i.e., pattern formation in respective parameter regions. The flexibility of the model allows different aspects of experimental design to be incorporated, such as maximum and basal CheZ expression level, etc. Work is in progress for detailed comparison with experimental data to be completed and reported. Onset of the pattern-forming process — The theory for the onset of instability of a stable traveling front is incomplete in our previous work. In the current project, we carried out a tour-de-force linear stability analysis and identified a localized mode whose eigenvalue develops a positive real part at the onset of patterning. This puts the patterning transition into the category of Hopf bifurcation typical of low-dimensional nonlinear dynamical systems, despite the fact that we are analyzing a PDE system with infinite many degrees of freedom. Ongoing work aims at tackling the eigenvalue problem from the analytic side using methods such as the WKB. This is the first time that an instability through a localized mode at the propagating front in Fisher wave problems is clearly demonstrated. The mechanism is generic and can be applied to related problems.

202713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
202713.value: A few years ago, a team led by colleagues at HKU conducted experiments of pattern formation in open geometry by controlling the motility of bacteria via a synthetic circuit [C. Liu et al., Science 334, 238 (2011)]. The work opens up a novel route to pattern formation in autonomous systems. In this project, we construct and analyze a new class of models that take into account the delayed response of bacterium to its environment. The “cell” model gives a more accurate description of the intracellular process that gives rise to the front instability and stripe formation. Numerical studies of the expanded model indeed give rise to growth patterns when the density-dependent switching rate of the cell motility is sufficiently fast. Furthermore, the mathematical structure of the new model allows for a more thorough analysis of the onset of oscillatory colony expansion. Through the project, we have gained a better understanding of the robustness of the proposed pattern formation scheme and the conditions that need to be fulfilled for it to work. It not only enables a closer comparison between the modeling and experimental results, but also opens up new directions of research on pattern formation in cell populations.

202813.label: Project Objectives
202813.value: We begin by further studying the nonlinear energy stable schemes. It is known that the phase field models satisfy a nonlinear stability relationship called gradient stability, usually expressed as a time-decreasing free-energy functional. This property has been used recently to derive space and time discretization schemes that inherit the nonlinear stability relationship of the continuous model. As the gradient stability plays an important role in time adaptively, better understanding in this direction is desired. Several adaptive time stepping strategies will be studied in this project. It is observed for many theoretical models the energy functionals decay with time quite smoothly except at a few 'critical' moments. Therefore, how to detect these critical moments become important: if this can be done then variable time steps can be arranged in a sensible way. In this project, we will explore effective ways to detect these critical time levels in the process of numerical simulations. It is also important to establish some fundamental theory for the adaptive time-stepping schemes. The theory will help us to understand some basic principles in developing and implementing the time-adaptive strategies. The proposed project is also partially relevant to this challenging problem.

202813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
202813.value: Phase field models have become an important tool to simulate many important physical problems, such as simulating crystal growth, thin film growth, and multi-phase flow interactions. The relevant phase-field methods are capable of computing topological changes such as splitting and merging, and thus have been applied successfully to multi-component fluid flows involving large interface deformations. The typical governing equations for the phase field models are of Cahn-Hilliard type, which involves a small positive parameter, strong nonlinearity and higher-order derivatives in space. These difficulties require careful study of the numerical discretization methods. Another feature of the phase filed computations is long time simulations, which make the standard (small) constant time-stepping approach difficult due to rounding errors and computational resource constraints. If both the solution dynamics and the steady-state solutions are required, it is desirable to use some time-adaptive strategies which allow to use small time steps in a few critical time levels (where the solution properties such as energy may change rapidly) and larger time steps in other time levels (where solution varies quite slowly). This project is to give a systematic study on the adaptive time-stepping approaches for the phase-filed equations. The goal is to obtain highly efficient adaptive methods for the phase-filed simulations. 相場模型在很多重要的實際問題的仿真模擬中起到非常重要的作用，這些問題包括晶體增長、多相流體相互作用等。 相場模型可以解決流體變化中的拓撲結構變化，比如分離或相融。相場模型中常見的方程是Cahn-Hilliard型方程，它包括了小參數、強非線性和空間的高階導數。這些數學上 的困難增加了數值計算方法的困難，特別是時間方向上高效離散方法上的難度。相場問題在不同的時間區域有不同的時間尺度，我們需要根據物理解的變化強度自適應地採用不同的時間步長。這一研究課題就是要系統地研究相場問題的自適應時間步長選取，以期導致高效快速相場模擬計算方法。

202813.label: Realisation of objectives
202813.value: The first objective of the project is to further studying the nonlinear energy stable schemes. It is known that the phase field models satisfy a nonlinear stability relationship called gradient stability, usually expressed as a time-decreasing free-energy functional. This property has been used recently to derive space and time discretization schemes that inherit the nonlinear stability relationship of the continuous model. As the gradient stability plays an important role in time adaptively, better understanding in this direction is desired. This has been fully investigated in this project. One of the main findings in this direction is the successful characterization of the stablization size for semi-implicit spectral methods to phase field equations. The up-to-date theoretical explanation of the numerical stability relies on the assumption that the derivative of the nonlinear potential function satisfies a Lipschitz-type condition, which in a rigorous sense, implies the boundedness of the numerical solution. In this peoject,we remove the Lipschitz assumption on the nonlinearity and prove unconditional energy stability for the stabilized semi-implicit time-stepping methods. It is shown that the size of the stabilization term depends on the initial energy and the perturbation parameter but is independent of the time step. The corresponding error analysis is also established under minimal nonlinearity and regularity assumptions. This paper is published recently by SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis [D. Li, Z. Qiao, and T. Tang, Characterizing the stabilization size for semi-implicit Fourier-spectral method to phase field equations, SIAM J. Numer. Anal. 54(3) (2016), 1653-1681.] The second objective of this project is to study adaptive time stepping strategies. It is observed for many theoretical models the energy functionals decay with time quite smoothly except at a few 'critical' moments. Therefore, how to detect these critical moments become important: if this can be done then variable time steps can be arranged in a sensible way. In this project, we planned to explore effective ways to detect these critical time levels in the process of numerical simulations. Our main result is to study long-time numerical simulations for phase field problems using adaptive time stepping strategies. More precisely, a high-order and energy stable scheme is developed to simulate phase-field models by combining the semi-implicit spectral deferred correction (SDC) method and the energy stable convex splitting technique. The convex splitting scheme used is a linear unconditionally stable method but is only of first-order accuracy, so the SDC method can be used to iteratively improve the rate of convergence. However, it is found that the accuracy improvement may affect the overall energy stability which is intrinsic to the phase-field models. To compromise the accuracy and stability, a local p-adaptive strategy is proposed to enhance the accuracy by sacrificing some local energy stability in an acceptable level. The proposed strategy is found very useful for producing accurate numerical solutions at small time (dynamics) as well as long time (steady state) with reasonably large time stepsizes. Numerical experiments are carried out to demonstrate the high effectiveness of the proposed numerical strategy. The paper is also published in an SIAM journal [X. Feng, T. Tang and J. Yang, Long time numerical simulations for phase-field problems using p-adaptive spectral deferred correction methods, SIAM J. Sci. Comput. 37 (2015), A271-A294.] The third part of the project is to establish some fundamental theory for the adaptive time stepping schemes. The theory will help us to understand some basic principles in developing and implementing the time-adaptive strategies. The current project is also partially relevant to this challenging problem. Part of the findings in this direction was published in SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis [Z. Qiao, T. Tang and H. Xie Error analysis of a mixed finite element method for the molecular beam epitaxy model, SIAM J. Numer. Anal. 53 (2015), 184-205.] This paper investigates the error analysis of a mixed finite element method with Crank-Nicolson time-stepping for simulating the phase filed model. It is proved that the semidiscrete and fully discrete versions of the numerical schemes satisfy the nonlinearity energy stability property, which is important in the numerical implementation. Moreover, detailed analysis is provided to obtain the convergence rate.

202813.label: Major findings and research outcome
202813.value: In this project, we have made systematic investigations on the adaptive time adaptivity for the phase field simulations. Several adaptive time stepping strategies are proposed, and relevant theoretical properties on the numerical schemes, based on a nonlinear stability relationship called gradient stability, are analyzed. The study in this project indicates that adaptive methods in time are very useful for obtaining fast and accurate numerical solutions. We also study a related efficient time discretization, i.e., fast and stable explicit operator splitting methods for phase-field models. With proper time splitting, the efficiency of the numerical algorithms can be significantly enhanced. See Y. Cheng, A. Kurganov, Z. Qu and T. Tang, Fast and stable explicit operator splitting methods for phase-field models, J. Comput. Phys. 303 (2015), 45-65.

However, more studies are needed to gain deeper understanding for convergence on time-adaptivity.

202813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
202813.value: In the summer of 2011, US President Obama announced the Materials Genome Initiative (MGI) for Global Competitiveness. This new initiative calls for major efforts to significantly advance three areas of research: multiscale computational materials science, open source cyber infrastructure for data management, and an integrated approach combining computation and experiments to accelerate the development of advanced materials. A phase field model is a mathematical model for solving interfacial problems. It has mainly been applied to material sciences, as many important engineering materials are designed by controlling their phase transformations and microstructure evolution. To obtain meaningful results for the phase field models, efficient and accurate numerical methods become very important. This research project aims to provide a useful tool in obtaining numerical solutions for the phase field modles.

203013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
203013.value: Polo-like kinase 1 (Plk1), involved in many key steps throughout mitosis, is found to be of great important in cancer treatment since its activity appears to be limited to mitosis in proliferating cells. However, the lack of selective small-molecule inhibitors of the kinase remains a major obstacle to further elucidate its precise functions. For instance, using anticancer agents that target microtubules may engender various adverse effects partially because of the diverse functions of microtubules in the cell. To date, only few small molecules can show the very specificity to Plk1 for imaging and inhibition. It is self-evident that the enhanced understanding of Plk1 activities will considerably favour the design and imple¬mentation of future experiments in the research, preclini¬cal, and clinical settings, adding muscle to our war against cancer. Although decent prognosis can be achieved by these small molecules, such chemosensors (i.e. BI 2536) are not without disadvantages: broad emission bands, short luminescence lifetimes (~ns) and ease of photo-bleaching. In contrast, lanthanide complexes, in this regard, do surpass all their counterparts, having large Stokes shifts, sharper fingerprint emission peaks, longer emission lifetimes (~ms) and higher photo-stability. Our blueprint includes the cyclin-specific lanthanide complexes with particular peptides and chromophores that can be excited in the near infra-red region via multi-photon excitation, and, above all, be Plk1-specific. Our research team is experienced in lanthanide coordination chemistry, spectroscopy, peptide chemistry and in vitro biological applications, as justified by our previous publications on responsive luminescent lanthanide materials towards various biological tasks in solution/in-vitro. To further support our work, we have performed several proof-of-concept experiments to consolidate our proposal: (1) synthesis of a Plk1-specific europium complex with tailor-made synthetic peptides that could be excited linearly and by two-photon(s) to give responsive fingerprint europium emission; (2) molecular docking shows our complexes can fit in the Plk1; and (3) they are all cell permeable and available for in-vitro imaging. This proposal will pave the way for the development of a new generation of lanthanide complexes conjugated with responsive chromophores and Plk1 specific peptides as dual probes – imaging and anti-tumor. It is hoped that the success in research could also lead to the success in practice, thereby providing more powerful tools (especially available to combine multi-photon and time-resolved technology) to get a more complete picture of the role of Plk1 kinase. 樣激酶家族(Plk1)涉及到有絲分裂中的多個重要步驟，通過抑制其在有絲分裂中的活性可以影響細胞增殖，這對癌癥治療具有重要的意義。然而，激酶特異性小分子抑製劑的缺乏仍然成為闡明它精確性能的主要障礙。例如，以微管為靶向的抗癌試劑可能會造成多種副作用，這其中一部份原因在於微管的多樣性功能。迄今為止，只有為數不多的小分子對Plk1的成像和抑制作用具有非常顯著的特異性。不言而喻的是，增強對Plk1活動的理解將有助於設計并實現未來的實驗研究，包括臨床前和臨床上的，進而為抗癌戰爭添加一臂之力。 儘管這些小分子可能會實現一些預測，但這類化學傳感器(i.e. BI 2536)並非沒有缺點，如發射帶寬、螢光壽命短(~ns)、易於光致漂白等。相比而言鑭系化合物明顯勝出，它具有大的斯托克位移、尖銳的指紋發射峰、長的螢光壽命(~ms)以及強的光穩定性。我們的目標在於合成週期蛋白特異性的鑭系化合物，這一化合物同時連有特定的肽及發色團，并通過多光子產生近紅外激發，最重要的是，對Plk1的特異性。 從之前發表的相應發光材料用於各種生物學方面的應用來看，我們的研究團隊富於鑭系配位化學、光譜學、肽化學以及體外生物學應用方面的經驗。爲了進一步支持研究工作，並對研究方案進行鞏固，我們採用了一下幾項概念驗證：(1) 採用特製的多肽化合物合成對Plk1特異的銪化合物，該化合物同時能被線性激發并通過雙光子產生相應的銪的指紋發射；(2) 分子對接結果表明該化合物適用於Plk1；(3) 所有化合物都具有細胞滲透性並能夠進行體外成像。 本方案將為開發新一代連接有相應的發色團以及Plk1的特異性肽以實現其雙功能(成像和抗癌)的鑭系化合物奠定基礎。我們希望研究上的成功能推動實踐上的成功，並由此為Plk1激酶角色的完整描述提供更強大的工具(尤其是兼顧多光子和時間分辨技術)。

203013.label: Realisation of objectives
203013.value: For objective 1, twenty lanthanide based complexes and nanomaterials have been synthesized and well-characterized by NMR and HPLC (lanthanide complexes), TEM and FTIR (nano-materials). All these lanthanide complexes/nanomaterials have been ligated with tailored peptides for targeting cell cycle regulatory proteins via newly developed method. (Org. Biomol. Chem., 2014, 5876; Chem. Commun., 2014, 6517) They have shown high reaction yield (>50%) and emission quantum yields (10%) in the aqueous solution with near-infrared excitation. For objective 2, six short peptide sequences are synthesized and have shown a strong binding with PBD in Plk1. The binding affinity of these peptides have been estimated by dynamic simulation (in theory) and isothermal titration calorimetry (in experimental). Among the six sequences, namely P1- PLHSpT , P2- PLHSD , P3-GGPLHSpT, P4-GGPLHSD, P5-GGPLHSpTGGRrRk and P6-GGPLHSDGGRrRk. P1, P2 and P3 have shown a stronger binding affinity to Plk1. These three peptides conjugated with lanthanide complexes or upconversion nanomaterials shows the interruption of G2-M cell cycle phrase during the mitosis in cancer cells specify and induced the apoptosis. (J. Mater. Chem. B, 2015, 2624) For objective 3, the emission lifetime of the proposed lanthanide complexes/nanomaterials conjugated with peptides upon binding with targeted protein(s) have been measured. The responsive lanthanide emission bands and lifetime are observed. It has shown that the peptide coated with nanoparticles emitting a long lifetime bright visible light under near infrared excitation could be an ideal material for achieving termination and visualization of cancer cell simultaneously. We have been used five water soluble, cyclen based europium complexes with various number of same antenna - :2-methyl-4-(2-(4-propoxyphenyl)-ethynyl)pyridine (L) from objective 1 and done the comprehensive studies on their solution state structure, photophysical and in vitro properties. The ligand/metal ratios in these five complexes are 4 (Eu-4L), 3 (Eu-2L), 2 (Eu-o-2L and Eu-p-2L) and 1 (Eu-1L). The hypersensitive europium emission from five complexes have been recorded and correlated to their symmetry. The 1H-NMR, high resolution mass spectra do not provide a definitive distinction between Eu-o-2L and Eu-p-2L, but room and low-temperature Eu3+ luminescence can give a clear identification. The Eu-4L demonstrated the impressive europium emission quantum yield in aqueous solution (~16%), but the Eu-3L with overall two positive charge perform the best energy transfer efficiency. All five complexes are nontoxic in vitro, and cell permeable, however only Eu-4L shown the promising emission in vitro with energy transfer upon protein binding. (RSC Adv., 2015, 13347) For objective 4, we have to evaluate the performance of new delivery systems in-vitro. Plk1 has appeared to be a promising target for the development of new anti-cancer agents. The polo box domain (PBD) of Plk1 serves as an excellent target for the inhibition of Plk1 activity. For this reason, we have rationally designed some multifunctional lanthanide-doped unconverted nanomaterials for this application. Specifically, we aimed to create novel nanomaterials that could carry Plk1 specific peptides into cancer cells and cause Plk1 inhibition, and at the same time, allow direct NIR imaging and monitoring. NaGdF4: Yb3+, Er3+ (NaGdF4) and BaGdF5: Yb3+, Er3+(BaGdF5) nanoparticles of two different sizes (60 nm and 10 nm, respectively) were prepared followed by conjugation with Plk1 specific peptides (-P1 = PLHSpT, -P2 = PLHSD, and -P3 = GGPLHSpT) to generate novel nanomaterials. Systematic and comparative studies of the nanomaterials prepared were carried out with structural morphology and phase composition, upconversion photophysical properties, cellular uptake efficiency, cytotoxicity, tumor selectivity, and the Plk1 binding affinity and inhibitory potency were also examined in details. The experimental results obtained showed that various nanomaterials prepared have achieved our original dual-function aim of anti-cancer activity and NIR imaging. Among the novel bio-conjugated nanomaterials investigated in our study, NaGdF4-P1, demonstrated a potentially system for future development. NaGdF4–P1 emerged as the best candidate for Plk1 binding and imaging and it could effectively exert cell cycle G2/M arrest and thus tumor inhibition both in vitro and in vivo. It is also worth noting that NaGdF4-P1 is selective in its mode of action and no anti-growth effects on the normal cells lines used in this study were observed. (J. Mater. Chem. B, 2015, 2624 and Chem. Commun., 2014, 6517)

203013.label: Major findings and research outcome
203013.value: Polo-like kinase 1 (Plk1) is a major serine/threonine protein kinase which regulates vital mitotic events such as centrosome duplication, spindle assembly and chromosome separation. Overexpression and aberrant activities of Plk1 can be detected in various different types of cancer. The unique polo box domain (PBD) pocket is an excellent drug target for Plk1 binding and inhibition, so multifunctional lanthanide-doped upconverted nanomaterials and Plk1 specific peptides are designed for imaging and inhibition of cancer growth via targeting Plk1. We have considered the size and shape effect of nanomaterials to the Plk1 in terms of its binding affinity, imaging and cancer inhibition. For the size effect: NaGdF4: Yb3+, Er3+ (NaGdF4) and BaGdF5: Yb3+, Er3+(BaGdF5) nanoparticles of two different sizes (60 nm and 10 nm, respectively) have been thin-coated with Plk1 specific peptides (-P1 = PLHSpT, -P2 = PLHSD, and -P3 = GGPLHSpT) to prepare novel nanomaterials. The comparative studies looking at cellular uptake, anti-cancer activity and imaging properties were then carried out. The experimental result supports our assumption that the nanomaterials prepared could successfully deliver Plk1 specific peptides into cancer cells and induce Plk1 inhibition while simultaneously allowing direct NIR imaging and monitoring. From the NaGdF4–Pn and BaGdF5-Pn nanoparticle series prepared in this study, NaGdF4–P1 emerged as the best candidate for Plk1 binding and imaging. NaGdF4–P1 can effectively exert cell cycle G2/M arrest and thus selective tumor inhibition both in vitro and in vivo. Thus, it offers a potentially interesting system for the development of new cancer therapies. (J. Mater. Chem. B, 2015, 2624) The shape effect of our same-sized hybrid nanomaterials conjugated with two different Plk1 specific peptides had been investigated in terms of their photophysical properties, cellular uptake efficiency, and selective inhibitory effect towards cancer and normal cells. The results obviously demonstrate that our spherical -NaGdF4@SiO2-P1 achieve the best performance when it comes to in-vitro imaging, G-2 phase cell arrest and hence cell cycle inhibition. (Eur. J. Inorg. Chem., 2014, 4539) Furthermore, in the molecular level – biocompatible lanthanide complexes, Plk1 or EBNA1 specific lanthanide complexes have been synthesized with strong binding and the inhibition of these overexpressed cancer protein function in vitro, being a potential luminescence labelling and anti-cancer agent with high hopes. (Org. Biomol. Chem., 2014, 5876; Chem. Commun., 2014, 6517) Their photophysical properties have been analyzed in the aqueous solution. (RSC Adv., 2015, 13347)

203013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
203013.value: This study represents one of the few examples where systems have been developed capable of both Plk1 inhibition and simultaneously direct near infrared imaging and monitoring of cancer cells by lanthanide complexes/nanomaterials. Such application improves considerably the signal-to-noise ratio for the Plk1 imaging. The peptide in this project doesn't only served as the vector, but also functions as a workable specific inhibitor. In the near future, we are going to investigate the in vivo behaviors of the complexes/nanomaterials system generated from this project, i.e. pharmacokinetic studies, biodistribution, in vivo acute, sub-chronic toxicity and in vivo anti-cancer efficacy in the patient derived xenografts mice models from different cancer patients. There are increasing interest in the establishment of PDX models for various cancers by investigators in academic/pharmaceutical research, in order to improve the development of effective therapeutics. In addition, the limitation of the fluorescence microscopy is the penetration in the tissue for in vivo studies. Positron Emission Tomography (PET) can offer deeper tissue imaging signal, but lack of cancer selectivity. The combination of peptide sequences with PET imaging seems to be the solution. With the support of this project, the PET imaging agents for specific cancer diseases are initiated. (Inorg. Chem., 2016, 6839)

203013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
203013.value: Peptides are considered as potential drugs due to their specific mode of actions and low requirement of dosage for treatment nowadays. However, their physical and chemical instability have hampered their effectiveness in therapeutic applications. Upon conjugation with our biocompatible lanthanide complexes/nanomaterials, target-specific peptides can be designed that resist from enzyme degradation and/or detrimental biological environments, and their solubility would also be increased. In this project, we have shown the possibility of the combination of lanthanide luminescence and peptides as imaging probes for cancer – via harmless near infrared excitation and emission, especially for one of the most important kinases in human beings – PIk1. This work does offer the first insight into whether the lanthanide complexes/nanomaterials matters their bio-interactions for further biomedical research. In summary, this study represents one of few examples where systems have been developed for both imaging and inhibition of tumor growth and will be a new direction for diagnostic testing employed for selecting targeted therapy.

203313.label: Major findings and research outcome
203313.value: A series of solution-processable, electroactive metal-containing polymers have been prepared which represent a new class of cathode-active, charge-storage materials for rechargeable batteries. The spectroscopic and redox behavior of these new organometallic polymers were investigated. New poly(fluorenylethynylene)s with ferrocene moieties (PFFAL1 and PFFAL2) and metallo-copolymers bearing different mole ratios of ferrocene and triphenylamine pendants (PVFVM1 and PVFVM1-1) were synthesized and characterized. The morphologies and electrochemical performances of the polymer-composed cathodes were studied by SEM, cyclic voltammetry and galvanostatic charge-discharge test. PFFAL1-composed electrode retained over 90% of the initial capacity after 100 cycles at 10 C and PFFAL2-based cathode exhibited a stable discharge capacity of 73 mAh/g at 1 C, which is close to the theoretical value (82.3 mAh/g) (paper 1). The composite electrode based on PVFVM1 exhibits an initial specific discharge capacity of 102 mAh/g, which corresponds to 98% of its theoretical capacity (104 mAh/g). (paper 4). Metallopolyynes with ferrocenyl pendants were studied for their cathode-active materials with good cycle life (paper 5). Besides, these metal-containing polymers were shown to exhibit resistive-type memory effect useful for information storage. PFFAL1 and PFFAL2 exhibit nonvolatile resistive switching behaviors. Single layer devices (ITO/polymer/Al) based on PFFAL1 exhibited the characteristics of "write-once read-many times" (WORM) memory effect, while PFFAL2 showed the flash memory behavior. The ITO/PFFAL2/Al memory device shows a high ON/OFF current ratio of 1000 to 10000, a low switch-on voltage of -1.0 V, a long retention time of 1000 s and the large read cycles up to 10000, which is superior to other reported ferrocene-containing memory systems (paper 6, highlighted as journal back cover). A series of non-conjugated ferrocene-containing copolymers FcCP1-FcCP3 with triphenylamine, benzothiazole or phenothiazine unit were synthesized via radical polymerization. They exhibited flash memory behaviour with a bistable conductive process, where FcCP1 showed a large ON/OFF current ratio of 1000 to 10000 with a low threshold voltage of -0.6 V. The work was recently submitted to J. Mater. Chem. C (paper 13). Control of the redox and charge transport properties of other metal-based systems was also investigated for use in future molecular design (papers 7-8). Some organic precursor polymers were also made which can be further derivatized to other organometallic systems in the future (papers 2, 3, 9). The results also contribute partly to the content of the review articles in Chem. Soc. Rev. (highlighted as journal back cover), Polymer. Chem. and Top. Curr. Chem. (papers 10-12).

203313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
203313.value: The following areas of research work can be further developed in the future: (1) Extension of the work to other redox-active metal chromophores. (2) Enhancement of the performance of the batteries and memory devices.

203313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
203313.value: A series of solution-processable, electroactive metal-containing polymers have been prepared which represent a new class of cathode-active, charge-storage materials for rechargeable batteries. The spectroscopic and redox behavior of these new organometallic polymers were investigated. The capacities of these organometallic rechargeable cells fabricated with metallopolymers were evaluated. On the other hand, these metal-containing polymers were shown to exhibit resistive-type memory effect useful for information storage. The present work fills in a relatively under-investigated area of organic batteries and memories and would provide a new impetus to the creation of some technologically useful materials and systems for both energy and information storage.

203613.label: Project Title(Chinese)
203613.value: 分裂方法的收斂速度分析

203613.label: Project Objectives
203613.value: Establish a worst-case convergence rate for the Douglas-Rachford splitting method, in the generic setting of finding a zero point of the sum of two maximal monotone set-valued operators. Establish sharper convergence rates for the Douglas-Rachford splitting method, in specific settings such as separable convex optimization problems and monotone variational inequalities --- e.g. the local linear convergence for the alternating direction method of multipliers, when it solves a quadratic programming model or a general separable convex optimization model. Establish a worst-case convergence rate for the Peaceman-Rachford splitting method, in the generic setting of finding a zero point of the sum of two maximal monotone set-valued operators. Establish sharper convergence rates for the Peaceman-Rachford splitting method, in specific settings such as convex optimization problems --- e.g. the sub-linear or linear convergence rates for some alternating linearization schemes for general nonsmooth separable convex optimization models.

203613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
203613.value: Operator splitting methods play a fundamental theoretical and algorithmic role in various areas of scientific computing, and have inspired many efficient numerical algorithms in different applications. The numerical efficiency and some theoretical progress on this type of method have long been witnessed in diversified areas, but research on their convergence rates is in its infancy. In this project we will focus on the context of convex optimization, and intensively investigate the convergence rates of some fundamental operator splitting methods. For these methods, we will estimate their worst-case convergence rates in generic settings, and sharper convergence rates in specific settings. 算子分裂方法在很多科學計算問題的理論和算法方面都發揮著至關重要的作用。很多解決不同應用問題的有效數值算法都是由算子分裂方法而來。在不同的領域里，有很多文獻討論算子分裂方法的數值有效性和一些相關的理論問題；然而有關這類算法的收斂速度方面的研究卻很少。本項目將以凸優化問題為目標，重點研究一些基本的算子分裂方法的收斂速度。對於這些方法，我們將估計它們在一般情形下的最壞收斂速度和在特殊情形下的更快的收斂速度。

203613.label: Realisation of objectives
203613.value: All the proposed objectives are well achieved, and some more results beyond are obtained.

203613.label: Major findings and research outcome
203613.value: The major findings of this projects are convergence rate results for some fundamental operator splitting methods such as the Douglas-Rachford and Peaceman-Rachford schemes. More general discussions are also done in the proximal point framework. Analysis is conducted in both the operator and specific convex optimization contexts. Both the sublinear convergence rate for the generic operator and convex optimization contexts and the linear convergence rate for some special cases are obtained. Some results are proved for the first time in the literature such as the counter example showing the divergence of direct extension of the ADMM for a multi-block separable convex minimization model, the divergence of the Peaceman-Rachford scheme, and the unified analysis framework in terms of the proximal point algorithm for several operator splitting methods. Completion of this project has lead to 13 research papers, most of which are published on flagship journals in optimization and operations research areas.

203613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
203613.value: Results obtained in this project are the foundation of some future work such as the extension to some special nonconvex scenarios. The mathematical tools developed in this project, particularly the analysis framework based on variational inequality and contraction techniques, can be potentially used for our research in the future. The prediction-correction framework for convergence analysis developed in this project can also be used later. Moreover, some ideas used for algorithmic design in this project can be used for tackling other more complicated problems in our future research. A special technique is using proximal regularization with smaller proximal parameters, or correction step with larger step sizes, to ensure the convergence of various splitting methods based on the augmented Lagrangian method.

203613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
203613.value: Some classic operator splitting methods have been very widely used in the literature and recently found more and more applications in various areas. Convergence rates of these methods, however, were not very well known despite of their popularity and extremely efficient numerical performance. This project had been focused on the convergence rate analysis for some most important operator splitting methods. Some new results were obtained in this project in this regard; and some of them were obtained for the first time in the literature. Some analysis frameworks have been developed for analyzing the convergence rate for some operator splitting methods; and some efficient numerical algorithms with provable convergence and verifiable efficiency to applications were designed in this project.

203913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
203913.value: The rapid growth of the world economy and population has created a great impact on the earth’s water cycle and water resources. Moreover, intensive human activities, such as the clearance of forests and expansion impermeable surfaces, have also made our living environment vulnerable and susceptible to extreme weather conditions. The hydrological cycle is a complex process. A better understanding of rainfall-runoff responses is a key issue for preventing and reducing natural disasters and for the better use of water resources. In an aridzone, runoff from mountainous region is essential for the survival of human settlements in the lower reaches. The rainfall-runoff often shows an unstable spatio-temporal pattern, largely due to variations in mountain topography. Because of water shortage and its influence on settlements, regional water resource studies often form a focus of hydrological modelling. Fewer investigations have looked at rainfall-runoff events, which may cause devastating consequences due to the poor water holding capability of the environment. As is common with geographical problems, an understanding of the rainfall-runoff process also closely relates to the investigation scale. This study, therefore, will investigate methods for multi-scale hydrological modelling that are suitable for aridzone applications in China’s west. A 3-dimensional terrain-based hydrological process model will be developed by integrating a multi-scale digital terrain model with a topological flow-path network model, which is capable of representing complex hydrological processes by a set of flow tubes perpendicular to contours at a given investigation scale. Thus, the water movement over a 3-dimensional surface can be simplified and modelled to one dimension. Then a conventional one-dimensional formula in fluvial hydraulics can be linked to the flow path segments for dynamic event-based simulations. A software platform will be developed to implement the proposed spatio-temporal models to establish a ‘test-bed’ for the analysis of impacts of environmental variables and scales, and for better understanding about the hydrological processes in the aridzone of western China. Answers will be sought for fundamental research questions in the aridzone hydrology including: (1) the topographic control on the spatio-temporal distribution of rainfall-runoff in the mountainous region, (2) the relationship between the runoff and other environmental variables in the aridzone, (3) the process of flow generation and convergence corresponding to rainfall events over a small catchment, and (4) the impact of scales of data and analysis on the hydrological modelling outcomes. 當今世界經濟的快速發展和人口膨脹對地球水迴圈和水資源造成了極大的影響，諸如森林砍伐和不透水層擴張等強烈的人類活動，使得我們的生活環境日漸脆弱，比以往更容易受到極端天氣條件的傷害。 地球水迴圈是一個複雜的過程。對降雨——徑流響應機理更好的把握是減災防災、合理利用水資源的關鍵。特別是在乾旱區，源自山區的徑流是下游人類和動植物生存的基本條件。山區地形地貌在很大程度上影響著降雨——徑流過程，通常顯示不穩定的時空分佈。由於水資源的匱乏及其對人類活動的決定性作用，目前，乾旱區水文模型的研究大多以區域水資源為研究重點，而對於由於環境持水能力低下而造成的災害性降雨——徑流事件的深入研究，則未受到應用的重視。 和其它地理學問題相同，降雨——徑流過程的研究也同樣存在著研究尺度問題。所以，本研究致力於深入研究適用於中國西部乾旱區的多尺度水文模型，其核心內容是建立以數位地形模型為基礎的三維水文過程模型，在整合多尺度地形模型基礎上建立流線網路拓撲模型。該模型可以將複雜的三維水文學過程在給定的任意尺度上表達為垂直於等高線的“流管”的集合，從而將三維空間上的坡面水流過程簡化為一維空間的上下游拓撲關係。這樣，傳統一維空間上的水力學模型和計算公式就可以耦合到流線網路上的各個線段，從而實現動態時空類比。本研究將據此建立時空類比的軟體實驗平臺，用於分析和模擬各環境要素和尺度對水文學過程的影響，以期得到對中國西部乾旱區水文學過程更好的理解。 本研究擬對下列乾旱區水文學基本的科學問題做出回答：(1)地形對山區降雨——徑流時空分佈的控制；(2)乾旱區徑流和其它環境要素的關係；(3)小流域降雨事件的產流匯流過程；(4)資料和分析尺度對水文過程模擬的影響。

203913.label: Realisation of objectives
203913.value: The project aims to investigate methods for multi-scale hydrological modelling that are suitable for aridzone applications in China’s west. A 3-dimensional terrain-based hydrological process model has been developed by integrating a multi-scale digital terrain model with a topological flow-path network model, which is capable of representing complex hydrological processes by a set of flow tubes perpendicular to contours at a given investigation scale. The water movement over a 3-dimensional surface can be simplified and modelled to one dimension. Then a conventional one-dimensional formula in fluvial hydraulics can be linked to the flow path segments for dynamic event-based simulations. A software test platform has been developed to implement the proposed spatio-temporal model to provide a basis for the hydrological process simulation. Objective 1: To investigate a method that integrates the scale-adaptive TIN-based terrain analysis and a topological flow-path network models for the analysis of rainfall-runoff processes. A particle-set hydrological model has been developed and implemented in an open-access platform for open-testing. The model, based on a S-DEM (Scale-adaptive DEM) and a FPN (Flow-path Network), provides a scale-adaptive model to provide a hydrologically-sound surface for simulation. The continuous hydrological processes are simulated by the movement of a set of discrete particles according to the hydraulic parameters and theorems. The principles, optimization and preliminary implementation methods have been published (Chen, et al., 2014; Zhang, et al. 2017). Objective 2: To investigate a method for integrating a sensor network and remotely sensed data for monitoring rainfall and runoff response in local catchments of an aridzone. A number of weather/hydrological stations have been installed in mid-Tianshan Mountains and continuous recording of rainfall/runoff parameters have been maintained for more than three years. Hourly fieldstation rainfall/runoff data have been compiled for several rainfall/runoff events for the testing of hydrological response to rainfall. Five field sites and a large catchment area were used to test methods of water balance change detection and hydrological responses using remote sensing, especially the GRACE satellite data. Changes of regional hydrological cycle because of climatic change and their impacts on hydrological responses have been investigated. Findings are reported by journal articles (Huang, et al., 2015, 2016; Hu, et al. 2017). Objective 3: To integrate distributed hydrological models with the scale-adaptive terrain analysis methods for simulating spatio-temporally uneven rainfall-runoff events and estimating regional water. This objective is achieved by the implementation of the methods developed by Objective 1. A software source code and sample data has been made available for open access at GitHub (https://github.com/funtry/particle-set) as a part of journal article submission (currently under review).

203913.label: Major findings and research outcome
203913.value: 1) A particle-set hydrological model (PHM) has been developed and implemented for the simulation of rainfall/runoff processes. The PHM is scale-adaptive (i.e. self-adaptive to application demand on scale), capable of dealing with uneven rainfall distribution, and ready for adoption of conventional hydrological methods (Chen, et al., 2014; Zhang, et al., 2016). 2) Regional water cycle and its responses to climate change has been investigated using remote sensing in two aspects: the regional climate change evidences and indicators (Hu, et al., 2017) and change of terrestrial water storage and related hydrological parameters (Sun and Zhou, 2015; Huang et al., 2015, 2016). 3) A prototype high-performance implementation of PHM has been developed for the simulation of hydrological responses at local and regional scales (Zhang, et al., under review).

203913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
203913.value: 1) Real-time simulation of rainfall/runoff processes based on high-performance cloud computing to allow in-time prediction of hydrological events such as sudden flood in ungauged mountainous areas. 2) Establishing computation models for predicting rainfall/runoff induced natural hazards, such as mud-floods and landslides, 3) Developing real-time spatial data acquisition and integrated data processing to incorporate data from weather RADAR, field stations, and sensor networks to support early warning for preventing and reducing the impacts by natural disasters.

203913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
203913.value: This project has developed a practical hydrological model that support multi-scale applications and spatio-temporal simulation of rainfall/runoff processes. The model employs a scale-adaptive digital terrain analysis approach to extract a flow-path network model from digital elevation model according to the demand of application scale. The model is capable of simplify complex 3-dimensional distributed hydrological models to an one-dimensional and highly efficient computational model to allow real-time simulation of rainfall/runoff processes. Investigations have been conducted to apply the model at local and regional scales, together with remote sensing technology, to achieve better understanding about water cycles and its response to climate change in the aridzone of China's west.

204013.label: Project Title(Chinese)
204013.value: 高維資料中的一些假設檢驗問題

204013.label: Project Objectives
204013.value: We propose a test statistic to deal with the two-sample Behrens-Fisher problem. Unlike existing methodologies, the test is scalar transformation invariant, which is a necessary requirement for any test statistic. Due to plug-in estimation for the variance for standardization, we propose a bias correction to get the limiting null distribution tractable. In this project, the number of covariates would reach n^2 or even n^3, where n is the sample size. For the generalized linear regression model, we suggest a test based on the weighted square of the conditional residual, given several linear combinations of covariates. In this case, the dimension reduction structure allows us to avoid the curse of dimensionality, so a large number of covariates can be handled when nonparametric estimation is involved for the conditional residual. For testing the existence of random effects in an ANOVA mixed model, we propose a test based on the difference between an estimator of variance that is only consistent under the null and an estimator that is consistent under both the null and an alternative. Further, we also construct a test for the hypothesis in which only some of the random effects are zero. The tests are extended to handle the case where the number of fixed and of random effects are large. Further, to assess the efficacy of the proposed methods in practical applications, we shall conduct extensive simulation studies and analyze a number of real data problems.

204013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
204013.value: In this project, we investigate three testing problems for regression models when the dimensionality of the covariate vector is large, even larger than the sample size. The problems are: the two-sample Behrens-Fisher problem; model checking for parametric regression models; and testing for the existence of random effects in an ANOVA mixed model. Unlike existing tests in the literature, the new test for the two-sample Behrens-Fisher problem is scale-invariant. For the models with a dimension reduction structure, we suggest a dimension reduction test for the parametric regression models, and a difference-based and a trace-based test for the existence of random effects. There appears to be no previous research discussed in the literature for the last two problems with large dimensionality. Clearly, this research project investigates some important problems in statistical inference when there are many predictors, and the new methodologies and theories developed in the course of the project will have a lasting impact on statistical science. 在這個專案中，當協變數的維數甚至大於樣本量時，我們考慮三個回歸模型的檢驗問題。這些問題為：兩樣本Behrens-Fisher問題；參數回歸模型型檢驗；ANOVA混合模型的隨機效應的存在性檢驗。不同于現有檢驗，對兩樣本Behrens-Fisher問題的檢驗是刻度不變的。對有降維結構的模型，我們提出一個降維檢驗。對隨機效應，我們提出基於離差和跡的檢驗。對大維數問題，文獻中沒有後兩個問題的檢驗。顯然，這個專案研究一些統計推斷中重要問題，新的方法論和理論對統計科學有著持續的影響。

204013.label: Realisation of objectives
204013.value: For this project, there are three topics, but the first two topics are very important in statistics. First, the hypothesis testing for two sample problem when the dimension is ultra high. There are a number of proposals in the literature. However, there is a big issue in many methods for test statistics construction: the test statistics are not scale invariant. In other words, when the scale of variable changes, the test would give a different conclusion. Thus, in our method, we tried to avoid this undesired property and then proposed the test that is scale-invariant. This paper has been published in Statistica Sinica, a decent journal in statistics. Second, for model checking for regressions, there are two main methodologies: local smoothing methods by using nonparametric estimation and global smoothing tests that are based on empirical processes. Local smoothing is sensitive to frequency models, but less powerful in general, while global smoothing tests can have better ability to detect smooth alternative models, but theer is no tractable distribution to be used for critical values determination. We then introduced an adaptive-to-model concept in hypothesis testing such that the test can adapt underlying models under the null and alternative hypothesis and then has tractable distribution to determine critical values with higher power. The paper has been published in JRSS B and people appreciated this effort. A referee even thought this was a substantial constribution in this field. The test for the existence of random effects is also a useful method in the ANOVA model. Further, the methods have been examined through numerical studies for their performances.

209813.label: Project Title(Chinese)
209813.value: 構建生物化學與生物分子自由能模擬中聯繫電子和原子核量子世界的多尺度橋樑

209813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
209813.value: Biochemical and biomolecular free-energy simulations, involving DNA, RNA, and protein macromolecules, can provide us with useful new insight into the (reaction) mechanisms behind bio-systems. The range of applications/implications can be from the origin of life and biocatalysis to biotechnology and rational drug design. Particularly, if the simulations can be performed at multiple scales and based on first principles in classical, quantum, and statistical physics, e.g., density functional theory (DFT) for electronic scale, path integral (PI) for nuclear scale, and Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics for phase-space scale, then oftentimes the computational results can make accurate predictions of numerous important physical quantities (e.g., nuclear tunneling and zero-point energy, electronic correlation energy, isotope effects, free-energy profile, binding energy, pKa value) for guiding experiments. In short, the current focus of DFT-PI methods in the literature is on optimizing the numerical algorithms Separately in electronic, nuclear, and phase-space scales. These methods are of particular importance because once the free-energy samplings are converged, then the exact quantum free-energy profile is obtained at some DFT-PI level of theory. However, given the computing power available nowadays, the practical level of theory for constructing the potential-energy surface in path-integral simulations still cannot be DFT, e.g., standard DFT B3LYP/6-31G(d) level could take ~two-million years to get a converged quantum free-energy profile using one processor. By contrast, the focus of this proposal is Not on Existing DFT-PI levels of theory. Instead, the goal of our method is to create a series of brand New intermediate levels of theory, which systematically connects both electronic and nuclear quantum worlds, i.e., to create a “multi-scale bridge” Unifying all existing levels of theory. Using this “bridge”, which is a complementary approach that can take advantages of current methods in the literature, we would generate a quantum free-energy profile at a New level of theory in between some of existing ones, and in accordance with the available computing power. The additional computational cost should be ~5% of the conventional approach. Preliminary results are remarkable, lowering the risk of this proposal. Particularly, after thorough tests on the “strength”/accuracy of our new “bridge”, including comparing our results with those calculated by other methods and with experimental results measured by, e.g., our two collaborators: Nobel Laureate Prof. Roger Kornberg via theorist Prof. Xuhui Huang at HKUST, and Prof. Michael Harris, we believe many theorists and experimentalists would use our new “bridge” for getting valuable new information on their bio-systems. 生物化學與生物分子(包括DNA、RNA和蛋白質等大分子)自由能模擬能夠為我們提供有關生物系統(反應)機制的有用的新見解。應用和涉及範圍從生命起源和生物催化到生物工程和合理藥物設計。特別是，如果模擬能夠在多尺度上執行並且基於經典、量子和統計物理中的第一性原理，如：電子尺度的密度泛函理論(DFT)，原子核尺度的路徑積分(PI)，以及相空間尺度的蒙特卡羅/分子動力學，那麼通常情況下計算結果能夠對很多重要的物理量作出精確的預測，如：核隧道效應及零點能，電子關聯能，同位素效應，自由能勢能面，束縛能，pKa值等，從而對實驗提供指導。簡而言之，目前DFT-PI方法的研究重點集中於分別在電子、原子核和相空間尺度上優化數值計算方法。一旦自由能取樣成功收斂，在某些DFT-PI理論水平上就可以得到確切的量子自由能勢能面，因此這些數值計算方法是非常重要的。然而，考慮到當前的實際計算能力，在路徑積分模擬中構建勢能面理論的實際應用還無法達到DFT水平，如：應用單個處理器在標準的DFT B3LYP/6-31G(d)水平上得到一個收斂的量子自由能勢能面分佈將需要大約二百萬年的時間。相比之下，本提案的重點不在於既有的DFT-PI理論方法，我們的目標是構建一系列嶄新的中等層次理論將電子和原子核量子世界系統地連接起來，也就是說，構建一個將所有既有水平的理論統一起來的“多尺度橋樑”。它是一種利用當今現有方法的互補方式，運用這一“橋樑”，我們能夠得到介於某些既有理論水平之間的新的量子自由能勢能面分佈。並且這一過程與可行的計算能力相適應，其額外計算成本約為傳統方法的5%。初步結果非常顯著，降低了本提案的風險性。特別地，我們會對新“橋樑”的“能力”/準確性進行全面測試，包括將我們的結果與其他方法計算得到的結果進行比較，以及與我們的兩個合作者[諾貝爾獎獲得者Prof. Roger Kornberg(經由香港科技大學的理論學家Prof. 黃旭輝)和Prof. Michael Harris]的實驗測量結果進行比較。通過比較，我們相信許多理論學家和實驗學家都可以應用我們的新“橋樑”得到關於其研究的生物體係有價值的新信息。

209913.label: Project Title(Chinese)
209913.value: 基于有效介质理论在人工材料中的电磁力密度的计算

209913.label: Project Objectives
209913.value: Present an effective medium theory to efficiently compute EM force density, where one only needs the succinct effective medium fields, not the detailed discrete model fields. Generalize existing effective medium theory to calculate the partial derivative of effective permittivity and permeability with respect to the strain (for solid) and density (for fluid). 209913.label: Major findings and research outcome
209913.value: Object illuminated by light experiences a light induced stress and pressure. Such pressure and stress are small compare to the binding forces in real materials. But for artificial materials, the binding force may not be large, and thus the electromagnetic stress may play an important role. We find that the stress depends not only on permittivity and permeability, but also on the underlining lattice structure. We have considered solid-like and fluid-like materials, and developed an approach to handle them. In short, we have developed the computation algorithm, we have verified it, and we have applied it to several cases.

210813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
210813.value: Synthesizing close interactions between articulated characters and objects is an important research topic with a wide range of applications including movies, character animations, computer games, and robotics. Despite the high demand for it, automatically synthesizing movements through existing methods remains impractical nowadays. The main problem lies in the conventional representation of character states, which is based on joint angles/positions. Because spatial relations between body parts are not encoded in such a representation, switching from one posture to another using existing methods (such as motion interpolations and motion planning) requires intense random sampling and collision detection in the state space. As a result, most close interaction scenes are still designed manually by experienced animators. Due to the nature of manual editing, reusing movements in different conditions is not only difficult, but also inefficient and costly. In this project, we propose a new framework for systems that automatically analyze and synthesize movements involving close interaction between the body parts of one or multiple articulated characters (such as dancing and wrestling) or between characters and objects (such as carrying luggage). We address the problems mentioned above by proposing a new representation that is based on the spatial relationships of different body parts, where the postures of the characters are described by their relative position and orientation with respect to adjacent entities in the scene. This new representation offers strong abstraction power and a high degree of adaptability. Motion that is captured from the interactions of one subject with other entities can easily be applied to characters and objects of different sizes, geometries, and topologies. The motion data obtained using different subjects and objects can be interpolated and concatenated as long as the spatial relationships are similar. Using this new representation, we will build a system that automatically synthesizes novel movements for the new condition using the training data. The system will be able to learn and synthesize movements that involve close interactions much more efficiently, without any artifacts such as penetrations and body part pass-throughs, compared to existing methods that is based on joint angles. As a result, the system is applicable for various applications, such as computer animations and computer games. It can also enhance research on imitation learning, where robots mimic human movements and adapt them to its own body size, topology and geometry. 製作人體緊密互動動作是一個重要的研究課題，具有廣泛的應用性，當中包括電影、角色動畫、電腦遊戲和機器人等，但以現有的方法自動地製作人體緊密互動動作仍然是不能實行的。主要的問題在於常用的人體表示法以關節角度/位置為基礎，因為肢體之間的空間關係並不能以上述的方式表示，當從一個姿勢切換到另一個姿勢的時候，使用現有的方法（如運動插值法、運動規劃等）需要使用大量的隨機抽樣和碰撞檢測。因此，緊密互動動作仍然由經驗豐富的動畫師手動設計，以致在不同情況及環境下重用這些現有的動作變得困難，減低工作效率和提高成本。 在本項目中，我們提出一個新的框架自動地分析和製作人體緊密互動動作，當中涉及一個或多個人物之間（如舞蹈和摔跤）或人與物體之間（如背著行李）的緊密互動。我們提出一種基於空間關係的表示法解決以上提及的問題，新的表示法根據在場景中相鄰的身體部位及物體的相對位置和方向描述它們的緊密互動。這個新的表示法提供了強大的抽象能力和高度的適應性，令現有的動作能輕易地套用於不同尺寸、幾何結構和拓撲結構的人偶中。 透過利用本項目提出的表示法建立動作製作系統，我們能夠以空間關係類似的運動數據作訓練集，並自動地製作新的人體緊密互動動作。該系統將能更有效地學習和製作涉及緊密互動的動作，並可應用於不同領域中，如計算機動畫和計算機遊戲等。它也可以提高模仿學習、機器人模仿人類的動作和適應他們自身的尺寸、拓撲和幾何等領域的研究。

210813.label: Realisation of objectives
210813.value: Upon completion of this projects, all of the objectives are realized completely. The outcomes of the research are published in 5 research papers, including 2 referred journal papers and 3 referred conference papers. The details of the achievement are as follows: For Objective 1), we proposed a new multi-resolution spatial-relation based representation, called “Spatial Relations of Human Body Parts (SRBP)”, for handling close interactions among characters, objects, and the environment. Such representation encodes the local relationship of body parts in proximity to represent motions in different classes. SRBP is intuitive and easy to interpret - the larger the SRBP value, the more the body parts interact. In addition, poses captured from subjects with different body sizes can be represented and compared using the same SRBP representation. Experimental results show that our proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art skeleton-based approaches on classifying and retrieving motions on benchmark databases. For Objective 2), we proposed several methods for analysing and synthesizing close character-character and character-environment interactions efficiently. For motion analysis, we proposed a classification framework based on the SRBP representation (discussed above) for classifying 3D human interactions. Experimental results show that our method works better than existing methods on benchmark databases. In addition, we further proposed a reliability-aware classification framework to further improve the classification performance when handling noisy 3D data (such as those captured from depth sensors). To cope with the noisy input posture, we design a set of reliability measurement to evaluate how reliable the tracked joints are. The more reliable joints then contribute more in a max-margin classification system, which is used to classify postures of different context. Our framework allows a smart environment to understand what the user is doing from the noisy data obtained by Kinect. Due to the improved accuracy, the system can even classify the subtle difference between performed postures, such as interacting with the environment by operating. Such a method can facilitate the analysis of close interactions as occlusion occurs very often in close interactions and results in noisy motion data. To facilitate further research in the field, the posture database created in this research will be made available to the public. Up to now, such a kind of database is not openly available. The comprehensive database consists of more than 8000 3D postures for different behaviours such as working at an office desk in sitting and standing postures, together with the source 3D depth images and colour images obtained from the depth camera. It is also carefully annotated with information of the behaviour, such as the nature of the movement and the potential health risks. Experimental results show that our method outperforms the state-of-the-art approaches on benchmark datasets. For motion synthesis, we first proposed a local motion planning algorithm for character animation. We focus on motion planning between two distant postures where linear interpolation leads to penetrations. In this paper, we propose a method to solve this problem by composing an energy graph where distances between different body parts are taken into account. Smooth motions are calculated as geodesic lines between the start and end nodes on the energy graph. Based on this concept, we form the motion planning problem between two arbitrary postures of a human skeleton character as a Boundary Value Problem (BVP). Besides the boundary conditions, the formulation of the BVP needs to consider three factors: (1) Physical plausibility, for instance, there should be no penetrations. (2) Smoothness. (3) Incorporation of user control. First, we construct an energy graph that meets these requirements. Next, we develop an iterative algorithm to compute the geodesic line between the two postures. Finally, we project the motion function onto a constraint manifold incorporating factors such as physical constraints and additional user control. Our method can be integrated into current keyframing techniques. It also has potential applications in motion planning problems in robotics. To improve the performance on synthesizing close interactions, we also proposed a multiresolution approach to speed-up Interaction Mesh based editing framework. The new approach takes the advantage of the temporal redundancy of human motion and using paralleling programming techniques (both on CPU and GPU) to accelerate the performance of the Interaction Mesh motion editing framework by introducing the idea of multiresolution optimization in the temporal domain. We first produce a multiresolution structure of the motion by extracting keyframes from the original motion. A coarser version of the motion is first computed by solving a smaller scale spacetime optimization by optimizing the keyframes. Next, starting from the motion computed at the coarser level, the fine details of the motion between the keyframes are adjusted by solving another series of smaller scale spacetime optimization problems. Our multiresolution approach improves the convergence of the optimization problem and thus speeds up the motion adaptation process. In addition, the highly parallelizable nature of our approach enables the motion to be edited on-the-fly interactively when playing back the animation. Our approach has many advantages compared to existing motion editing techniques that can handle close interactions. Using our method, the user can interactively change the sizes of the characters and also edit the postures during close interactions, which makes the method suitable for animators to edit and produce animations. As we compute the movements by solving linear problems, we can easily impose constraints such as ZMP and physical constraints. Experimental results show that the quality (in terms of smoothness) retargeted motions are comparable to those generated using Interaction-mesh while the computation time is significantly reduced. As a result, our method can be applied to interactive applications such as motion editing and online control of humanoid robots.

210813.label: Major findings and research outcome
210813.value: As explained in Section 5.3, several representation and frameworks have been proposed to achieve the project objectives during the course of this project. In particular, the outcomes of the research are published in 5 research papers, including 2 referred journal papers and 3 referred conference papers. For motion analysis, the SRBP representation shows how close interactions can be described based on the volumetric mesh structured computed from body parts. This is a new perspective to represent human postures in motion classification. The outcome of the SRBP is published in VRST2015. In the proposed reliability-aware classification framework, we found that taking into account the reliability of each feature in the motion data can improve the classification performance. In particular, we compute the optimal weight for each of the feature in the motion data according to the reliability measurement. By this, the classification performance can be boosted significantly. The outcome is published in CVIU in 2016. For motion synthesis, we proposed a framework to solve motion planning between two postures as a Boundary Value Problem. We assume that the solution is a bounded continuous function on an energy graph. By this, a fast constrained bidirectional motion planning method is further proposed. To further incorporate user control, we project the motion function to a constraint manifold. Experimental results show that our method can synthesize collision-free in-between motion when interpolating two different key postures without using any collision handling processes. The outcome is published in IEEE TVCG in 2015. We also proposed a multiresolution approach for solving spacetime optimization problems efficiently. We applied our method to retarget motions of closely interacting characters based on the design of the Interaction Mesh framework [Ho et al. 2010]. Experimental results showed that our method consistently outperforms the original Interaction Mesh framework in terms of motion quality and computational efficiency. We further showed that the highly parallelizable nature of the multiresolution model enables motion retargeting on-the-fly when playing back the animations and near-realtime performance can be achieved. The outcome is published in VRST2014.

210813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
210813.value: One of the interesting potential further development of the research is applying the motion synthesis techniques in controlling humanoid robots in highly constrained environment as well as closely interacting between multiple robots / human-robot interactions. Out proposed methods can handle close interactions efficiently. Such as advantage can reduce the computation time required for motion synthesis/planning and more computation power can be reserved for controlling the robot at action level to control the robots more smartly. Another important direction is to combine the developed approaches with data-driven approaches to further improve the results. For example, the naturalness of the synthesized motions can be learned from existing motion data. That includes using machine learning techniques to learn the human motion manifold and make use of such a manifold in motion synthesis.

211513.value: 在車載Ad Hoc網絡(Vehicular ad hoc networks，VANETs)用于建立车辆和车辆之间，以及车辆和道路设备（roadside equipment）之间的通讯链接。下一代的VANETs可以支持各种各样的应用，包括道路安全、智能交通、移动信息化、各种基于位置的商业应用。 交通安全是VANETs的一个根本的要求。现有两种策略：流量控制（traffic control）和紧急通知（emergency notification）。流量控制是一种预防性的策略，它通过控制交通信号的调度来控制车流量。但考虑到通过瓶颈路段车的总数保持不变，这种策略并不能根本性的解决问题。相对比，紧急通知是一种事后反应的策略。但危险情况发生时，遇险车辆广播出紧急信号以通知所有附近的车辆。然而，广播（broadcasting）在VANETs是一个很有挑战性的问题。这是由于车辆时高速行驶的，并且网络的拓扑随时变化。现有的广播算法有以下的局限性：1）不能同时应用到高速公路和城市地区；2）不能应用于双向多车道的情况；3）不能应用于稀疏拓扑结构的VANETs。 本项目的目的是设计一种VANETs的分布式流量控制和导航系统。它将支持：1）把车辆导航到少车流的路段从而实现分布式的流量控制；2）能克服以下所述局限性的有效的紧急通知；3）各种基于位置的服务和娱乐应用。我们将VANETS的信息根据它们的优先级划分成以下4类：紧急通知信息、实时路况信息、有严格响应时间要求的请求信息、没有严格响应时间要求的请求信息。我们设计一种基于优先级的广播算法。该算法有效的利用VANETs中多信道的特点以实现信息传递的高效性。我们还将设计一种基于机会的（opportunistic）传递模式，是的该广播算法能够应用于稀疏拓扑结构的，甚至是不连通的VANETs。最后，我们设计一个智能导航系统。在该系统中，装载电子地图的车辆在行驶过程中可以动态地交换实时路况信息。这些信息将用于实时地更新电子地图。这样，车辆将可以被导航到最优的路径，比如到达目的地花费时间最少的路径。我们提出的分布式流量控制和导航系统在下一代VANETs中将可以平衡道路流量、提高交通效率、并潜在地保护人民的生命安全。

211913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
211913.value: Semiconducting polymers are expecting to find applications in polymer-based light-emitting diodes (PLEDs) and organic photovoltaic (OPV) cells.[1-2] Development of polymeric electronic devices, however, is hampered by the presence of defects that can act as charge traps. The presence of these traps lead to undesirable losses. Electrical energy is wasted in form of heat rather than light for PLEDs; in an OPV cell, solar energy is wasted as in form of heat, too, as traps act as recombination centers for charge carriers. Further improvement of polymeric devices, therefore, requires a deeper understanding of these defects. This proposal outlines an extremely sensitive technique, known as photothermal deflection spectroscopy, for measuring the subgap optical absorptions of semiconducting polymers and their bulk heterojunction blends. Measurement of subgap absorption can lead to the identification of traps, and provide direct measurements of their energetic positions, distributions, and densities. The outcome of this proposal should lead to better understanding of defects in polymeric semiconductors. Minimization of these defects (by, e.g., intentional doping) should reduce loss in PLEDs and OPV cells and lead to devices with improved performances. 備受注目的半導聚合物可應用於發光二極管及有機光伏電池(OPV)。但是,缺陷的存在卻阻礙了聚合物電子器件的發展，缺陷引致能量損失，令發光二極管或光伏電池耗電而發熱。為進一步改善聚合物器件的性能，有必要更深入地了解這些缺陷引起的陷阱態。此建議概述一個極為敏感的技術，即光熱偏轉譜，用於測量半導體聚合物和它們的本體異質結的共混物的亞能隙光吸收。測量亞能隙吸收令我們識別陷阱，並提供他們的能量位置，分佈和密度的直接測量。這個建議的結果會令我們更好地理解聚合物半導體的缺陷，此外，故意摻雜於分子發光二極體及OPV電池可減少能量消粍，並提高這類器件的性能。
