211913.label: Major findings and research outcome
211913.value: 1. We performed a detailed investigation to correlate trap densities to OPV device performance in the archetype BHJ of PTB7:PC71BM with different donor-acceptor (D-A) weight ratios. Photothermal deflection spectroscopy (PDS) is used to quantify the trap density. Starting with pristine PTB7, addition of small concentration of fullerene increases the electron trap density and lowers the electron mobility. When the D-A weight ratio reaches 1 : 0.1, fullerene percolation occurs. There is an abrupt drop in trap density and simultaneously a six orders of magnitude increase in the electron mobility. Furthermore, the fill factors of the corresponding photovolatic devices are found to anti-correlate with the trap density. This study reveals that electron trapping is the key limiting factor for un-optimized BHJ solar cells in low fullerene regime. [Ref. 1: Adv. Energy Mater, DOI: 10.1002/aenm.201602360 (2017)] 2. Traps can sometimes be reduced with a suitable dopant. In this study the dopant is in the form of a ternary element in some representative BHJs. To amplify the effect of traps and the positive role of the dopant, we made thick film BHJ cells. We show that about 200nm thick BHJ cells (with a ternary element) can be fabricated that retain 90% PCEs of the optimized thin film cells. The ternary component is p-DTS(fbtth2)2. Without p-DTS(fbtth2)2, the binary thick film devices have PCEs of 6.3%, 7.4% and 3.2%. With p-DTS(fbtth2)2, the corresponding BHJs have markedly improved PCEs of 7.6%, 8.3% and 3.9%, respectively. The results are more than 90% the PCEs of the optimized binary BHJs. Addition of the ternary component enhances hole mobility and suppressed band tails disorders as revealed by PDS. Our results suggest the p-DTS(fbtth2)2 behaves as conducting bridges in between two neighboring polymer segments. [Ref. 2: Adv. Electr. Mater. DOI:10.1002/aelm.201700007 (2017)] 3. Our PDS setup has also generated a number of collaborative researches on perovskite-based organic semiconductors. Details are provided in Part (C).

Development of polymeric electronic devices, however, is often hampered by the presence of defects that can act as charge traps, leading to undesirable waste heat. Further improvement of polymeric devices, therefore, requires a deeper understanding of these defects. This proposal succeeded in implementing a very sensitive optical technique, known as photothermal deflection spectroscopy (PDS), for measuring the subgap optical absorptions of semiconducting polymers and their bulk heterojunction blends. We employed PDS and identified the origin of charge traps in several imporatant polymer-based OPV cells. 212313.label: Project Title(Chinese)
212313.value: 穩健的信息融合技術及其在視頻監控中的應用

212313.label: Project Objectives
212313.value: To study and develop a dependency model for information fusion in which the fusion algorithm is distribution-free; To study and develop an outlier handling algorithm for the information fusion model developed in (1); and To study and generalise the information fusion model incorporating dependency modelling and outlier handling developed in (1) and (2) from training data to query data.
rows: To study and develop a dependency model for information fusion in which the fusion algorithm is distribution-free;
To study and develop an outlier handling algorithm for the information fusion model developed in (1); and
To study and generalise the information fusion model incorporating dependency modelling and outlier handling developed in (1) and (2) from training data to query data.

212313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
212313.value: While surveillance video camera networks have been installed in public areas in many countries, the development of intelligent video software technology lags far behind that of the associated hardware. Surveillance video processing has thus become a research topic of great interest in the computer vision and pattern recognition community over the last decade because of a number of potential applications such as human behaviour understanding, person identification from videos, event detection for video retrieval and gait-based criminal investigations. However, all these applications are very complicated. It may be difficult to achieve a good level of accuracy using a single piece of information from a video recording. Instead, it has been shown that combining different pieces of information from the same or different video recordings could significantly improve accuracy. Combining multiple sources of information to solve computer vision and pattern recognition problems was proposed in the 1980s, and has been successfully applied in character recognition, biometrics, image retrieval, event detection and social media data analysis. While encouraging results have been reported in the literature, existing fusion algorithms do rely on strong assumptions concerning information dependency and data distribution. However, most surveillance video based applications do not satisfy all these assumptions. In turn, fusion performance will be degraded, and the degree of degradation will depend on the level of deviation from these assumptions. As a result, existing information fusion algorithms cannot perform at a consistent level. We have conducted a simple experiment that shows that performance can be degraded by 30%. This robustness issue must be resolved to deploy fusion methods in practical applications. To address the forgoing robustness issue arising in information fusion, the proposed project will develop a distribution-free dependency model. The proposed dependency model does not require that the pieces of information to be fused are independent of each other and does not assume any data distribution. To reduce the distribution estimation error introduced by the presence of outliers, the model learning process will incorporate an outlier handling procedure. The proposed project will also investigate how to generalise the fusion model learnt from training data to query data by minimising the maximum mean discrepancy. The proposed project will develop a new theory and algorithm for robust information fusion. The theory and algorithm to be developed will be generic in nature and will be applicable to computer vision and pattern recognition applications, as well as to other domains.

212313.label: Realisation of objectives
212313.value: The three listed objectives have been realized satisfactorily along three main directions. With respect to the first objective, we have developed a new framework to model dependency based on probabilistic properties of posteriors without any assumption on the data distribution. Making use of the range characteristics of posteriors, the fusion model is formulated as an analytic function multiplied by a constant with respect to the class label. With the analytic fusion model, we give an equivalent condition to the independent assumption and derive the dependency model from the marginal distribution property. In this way, any algorithms developed under this framework will be distribution-free. With respect to the second objective, in order to detect outliers from data, we have proposed a new method to detect reliable data (samples) and remove unreliable data for fusion. The rationale is that unreliable may contribute negative effect to fusion process. To achieve this, we have proposed a new joint sparse representation model for robust feature-level fusion. The proposed method dynamically removes unreliable features to be fused by employing the beauty of sparse representation. With respect to the third objective, by using the above-mentioned results, we have successfully combine the distribution-free dependence model and unreliable data detection, and applied to face recognition, action recognition and visual object tracking.

212313.label: Major findings and research outcome
212313.value: To achieve the objectives stated above, we have investigated and researched different approaches for developing distribution-free and robust dependent model in order to increase the robustness of information fusion, as stated in the proposal. After analyzing limitations in existing fusion methods, we discover two key factors affecting the performance and robustness of a fusion model under different data distributions, namely (1) data dependency and (2) fusion assumption on posterior distribution. Considering these two factors, we developed a new framework and an analytic fusion model to model dependency based on probabilistic properties of posteriors without any assumption on the data distribution. With the analytic fusion model, we give an equivalent condition to the independent assumption and derive the dependency model from the marginal distribution property. Since the number of terms in the dependency model increases exponentially, the Reduced Analytic Dependency Model (RADM) is proposed based on the convergent property of analytic function. Finally, the RADM optimal coefficients are learned by incorporating label information from training data to minimize the empirical classification error under regularized least square criterion. We have also applied RADM to face recognition and action recognition. These research findings have been reported in International Journal of Computer Vision [1]. To solve the outlier issue, we have proposed to extract reliable samples for fusion while unreliable samples will be removed so as to increase the robustness of the fusion model. Along this line, we have proposed a new joint sparse representation model for robust feature-level fusion. The proposed method dynamically removes unreliable features to be fused using the beauty of sparse representation. In order to capture the non-linear similarity of features, we extend the proposed method into a general kernelized framework, which is able to perform feature fusion on various kernel spaces. This method has been applied to visual tracking application and robust tracking performance is obtained. Both the qualitative and quantitative experimental results on publicly available videos show that the proposed method outperforms both sparse representation-based and fusion based-trackers. The preliminary version of this idea has been published in IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition [2] while the journal version has been published in IEEE Transactions on Image Processing [3]. Further working along the line, we have proposed an unified feature learning framework which simultaneously exploits both the representation capability and the discriminability of multiple features. It has been reported in International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence [4].

212313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
212313.value: A distribution-free model for information fusion framework namely analytic fusion model, has been developed in this project. While the proposed model is theoretically sound, we could only develop a reduced model as the number of terms increases exponentially. Along this line, one of the future work is to develop a “smart” method to find the complete model. With the advancement of CPU, hardware implementation may become feasible. While the proposed method has been applied to different computer vision applications, the computation time is relatively long. Another direction of this research is to develop a CPU implementation of these fusion methods. As such, real-time practical applications can be realized.

212313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
212313.value: It is well know that the performance of using multiple experts (information fusion) to draw a conclusion is better than that based on one single expert. This idea was proposed more than three decades ago in the areas of pattern recognition and machine learning. While many methods were proposed along this line, there are some assumptions in these methods. That means, the performance of existing methods will be very good if the assumptions are valid. Otherwise, the performance may degrade dramatically. In order to overcome this limitation, this project has successfully developed a new information fusion framework in which no assumption is required. The proposed framework is also deployed in different computer vision and pattern recognition applications, including face recognition, action recognition and visual object tracking. The results are encouraging. These research findings have been published in two top-tier journals and two top-tier conferences.

212613.label: Realisation of objectives
212613.value: A major goal in systems biology is to develop appropriate computational models that are able to integrate various experimental data for dissecting biological complexity in transcriptional gene regulation. To address this challenge, we combine cis-regulatory logics and transcriptional kinetics to develop a biologically plausible model. Theoretically, TFs can form many logics in gene regulation, but in reality, only a few of them become the driving force in a biological process. LogicTRN has the ability to identify the dominant logics in an accurate and high-throughput way. In LogicTRN, the change of gene expression is defined as a function of TF-binding occupancies and kinetic parameters. Unlike existing integrative analyses that treat gene expression and TF-DNA binding as two separate processes, our approach puts these two types of data into one single model, which is more biologically meaningful. In this project, we had faced one obstacle, that transcriptional kinetic function is essentially nonlinear, which makes it difficult to develop computational methodologies. Therefore, we adopted Taylor expansion to convert the nonlinear kinetic function to a polynomial function. The usage of the polynomial function provides a general mathematics form to simultaneously involve different regulatory logics. By assuming each logic has a probability of being involved in regulating a target gene, we are able to construct the model equation. Solving the model equations can lead to a determination of the TF logics. One challenge in developing LogicTRN is that the number of combinatorial logics increases drastically as more TFs are involved. To make it more computationally feasible, we converted the full model into a pairwise-logic model. The pairwise-logic model only identifies the dominant two-TF logics and thus can greatly reduce the model's complexity. Gene expression-based methods assume correlation among genes can imply regulatory relationships (between regulators and their targets) or co-regulation (targets that are regulated by the same regulator). TF-DNA binding-based methods, on the other hand, identify the TFs that can bind to the target genes. Both methods are generally less accurate comparing to the third one. Existing integrative methods normally using filtering approach to combine the gene expressed based methods and TF-DNA binding-based methods. That is, using TF-DNA binding methods in the first step to include those gene bound TFs only, and then apply gene expression-based methods to derive the TRN, or vice versa. These approaches didn’t consider the mechanistic relationships between TF-DNA binding and gene expression during the biological process. Unlike existing integrative analyses that treat gene expression and TF-DNA binding as two separate processes, LogicTRN puts these two types of data into one single model, which is more biologically meaningful. In LogicTRN, the gene expression is defined as a model equation of TF-DNA binding status, all possible TF interaction logics, and associated kinetic parameters. Solving the model equation can thus lead to the determination of the dominant TF regulatory logics and all the kinetic parameters. We have evaluated LogicTRN using simulation, comparison and application studies, and the results not only show their consistency with existing knowledge but also demonstrate its ability to accurately reconstruct TRNs in biological complex systems.

212613.label: Major findings and research outcome
212613.value: In summary, LogicTRN is a systematic approach developed based on the well-established theories of cis-regulatory logics and transcriptional kinetics, which provides an efficient way to directly infer TF–TF interactions in regulating target genes. (1) In this study, the regulatory relationship among the transcription factors (TFs) as well as the interplay among target genes and multiple TFs, underpinning the gene expression regulation has been inferred. (2) The regulatory TF-logics for any given target gene can be well identified from the dynamic gene expression data and TF-DNA binding data through this integrative LogicTRN model. (3) In biological complex systems, accurate reconstruction of the underlying TRNs is also plausible with the help of those well-predicted TF-logics. (4) The results are consistent with existing knowledge. (5) A major goal in systems biology is to develop appropriate computational models that are able to integrate various experimental data for dissecting biological complexity in transcriptional gene regulation has been achieved.

212613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
212613.value: (1) Application of LogicTRN shows its ability to identify TF targets and to reconstruct TRNs. (2) The derived networks are able to explore the nature of transcriptional gene regulation with biological meanings, which are consistent with previous experiments. (3) Through simulation and comparison studies, the LogicTRN model shows its reliability and robustness in capturing TF regulatory logics and identifying targets of TFs, and in constructing TRNs. (4) This method has been applied to analyze data sets representing the estrogen-induced breast cancer and human-induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived cardiomyocyte (CM) development. (5) Applications in human breast cancer and the hiPSC-derived CM development demonstrate consistency between the identified TF gene regulation and the previous experiments. (6) With increasing number of dynamic high-throughput data of gene expression and multiple regulator binding signals, the LogicTRN method would provide a powerful tool in interpreting the dynamics and complexity of transcriptional gene regulation. (7) In the future, it should be possible to extend our method to cover gene regulation by other regulators. The integrated approach should help researchers develop accurate model transcriptional relationships among molecules in a biological system as a whole, thus permitting a greater understanding of complex biological processes associated with development, ageing, and disease.

212613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
212613.value: LogicTRN is an algorithm to identify the dominant TF regulatory logics acting on given target genes during a specific biological process. The identified TF logics can show how TF work collaboratively in regulating their target genes. Based on the TF logics, the transcriptional gene regulatory networks can be reconstructed.

240213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
240213.value: This project will research the 'Berita Singapura' ('Singapore News') documentary film series produced by the Singapore Ministry of Culture and Cathay Film Services between January 1963 and October 1969. The 'Berita Singapura' series comprises eighty-six short 16mm films held at the Audiovisual Collection of the National Archives of Singapore (NAS). The series was shown on TV Singapura, and in cinemas in Singapore, Malaysia, Borneo and the UK, during the 1960s. In addition to the films, this project will also research written primary documents related to 'Berita Singapura' produced within the Ministry of Culture Publicity Division and Film Sub-Committee; the Singapore Broadcasting Division; the Singapore Film Unit and TV Film Unit, and the Ministry of Finance. The archives of the NAS Oral History Collection, Cathay Organization, current Singapore broadcasting station MediaCorp TV, and 'Straits Times' newspaper will also be researched where relevant. The 'Berita Singapura' series was produced during a period of turmoil in Singapore and was personally commissioned by the first Prime Minister of Singapore, Lee Kuan Yew, in late 1962. In 1963 Singapore declared formal independence from Britain and also joined the Federation of Malaysia. In this context of uncertainty, radical change and risk one of the key tasks facing Lee Kuan Yew and his People's Action Party was to forge a sense of national unity and identity from an ethnically and religiously divided population; and both TV Singapura and 'Berita Singapura' were established in early 1963 in order to help accomplish that. However, because there were only 2,400 TV sets in the city in 1963, 'Berita Singapura' became the paramount audiovisual means through which the government's objectives were to be achieved. 'Berita Singapura' continued to play this pivotal role after the expulsion of Singapore from Malaysia in 1965, and up till 1969. This makes 'Berita Singapura' of considerable historical value. This project also develops from three previous short research trips to compile information on official film-making in Singapore. As a consequence of these, the PI already possesses a number of relevant primary materials; providing the project proposed here with a substantive research underpinning. In addition, this project is also supported by the PI's recent research and publications on the official film in Malaysia, Singapore and Hong Kong. The research project proposed here will constitute an important and original study of this significant and previously unresearched series of films. 本研究計劃的對象是一部名為“新加坡新聞 （Berita Singapura）”的系列紀錄片，該片由新加坡文化部和國泰影業（Cathay Film Service）於1963年1月至1968年10月聯合出品。該系列紀錄片包含68卷16毫米短片，現藏於新加坡國立音像檔案館（Audiovisual Collection of the National Archives of Singapore NAS）。該片在1960年代在新加坡電視台（TV Singapura）和位於新加坡，馬來西亞以及英國的影院公映。 除了電影之外，本計劃同時研究一些與該紀錄片有關的文字資料。這些資料涉及如下機構：新加坡文化部及其下屬的電影委員會；新加坡廣播局（Singapore Broadcasting Division）；新加坡電影部門以及電影電視部門（Singapore Film Unit and TV Film Unit）;以及新加坡財政部（Ministry of Finance）。此外，研究者還計劃在如下機構中搜尋相關資料：新加坡國立檔案館的口述史收藏（NAS Oral History Collection），國泰集團，以及當下的新加坡傳媒集團如MediaCorp TV和海峽時報（Strait Times）等媒體。 “新加坡新聞”系列紀錄片產生於一個新加坡歷史上的動盪時期，該片由新加坡首任總理李光耀在1962年親自下令拍攝。1963年新加坡宣布獨立，同時加入馬來西亞聯邦。在這個充滿動盪和激變的時刻，李光耀及其人民行動黨面臨的核心任務是在一個充滿著宗教和種族分隔的社會中建立起國家認同。“新加坡新聞”系列紀錄片的攝製就是為了滿足這一目標。然而，由於在1963年新加坡只有不過2400台電視，該紀錄片遂成為政府實現其國家認同目標的重要工具。這部紀錄片公映直到1969年，期間新加坡退出馬來西亞聯邦。因此，“新加坡新聞”系列紀錄片的歷史價值不容低估。 本研究計劃還源於研究者先前三次對新加坡官方電影的田野經歷。基於此，PI已經掌握了一定數量的第一手研究資料，這些都為本計劃打下了堅實的基礎。此外， PI近期對馬來西亞，新加坡和香港官方電影的研究和出版工作同樣有力的支持了本計劃的展開。 以上所述的研究計劃具有原創性和重要的意義，可以增進我們對這部十分重要卻研究不多的系列片的理解。

240213.label: Realisation of objectives
240213.value: Objectives 1-5 have been realized fully, and a good understanding of how Berita Singapura came into being, and what the series consisted of has been attained. A research trip lasting one month was made to the National Archives in Singapore, where the majority of the episodes of Berita Singapura were viewed. During this trip analysis of paper archival records was also undertaken, and copies of relevant material were taken. Objective six was also realized in terms of learning how Cathay Film Services related to the Singapore government. However, and this also relates to objective 4, because the Berita Singapura series deliberately hid its source in the Ministry of Culture, no credits appear on the films, making it difficult to know who the individual film-makers were, though the producers: Hodge and Wright, are known. In terms of objective seven, most of this has been achieved. However, there has been a delay in completing everything because of funding difficulties. Whilst RGC agreed this as a 12 month project only funding of six months was provided to employ an RA. This was insufficient to realize project objectives. Therefore, the PI had to spend considerable time/energy in finding other sources of funding to fund the RA for the duration of the project. Eventually, the RA was able to be employed for 11 months, with the PI having to find roughly the same amount of funding as provided by RGC. Nevertheless, the project 'Report' was written up, and is available on the research programme website. The website itself has also undergone significant expansion, in collaboration with the University library, and all the primary data emanating from the Berita Singapura project will eventually appear on the website. The website now contains thousands of pages of archival material, scanned and cross-referenced. The new website is http://digital.lib.hkbu.edu.hk/documentary-film. Collaboration is also taking place with colleagues in Dartmouth College, USA, over enhancement of this, and a conference will be held next May at HKBU entitled 'Digital Humanities and the Historical Record'. Representatives from Dartmouth will speak at the conference. The Berita Singapura project will also be presented at the conference. The 'Catalogue of research resources mentioned in objective 7 has been folded into the project 'Report', and has therefore been achieved, The objective of publication in a journal has been superseded by the fact that the PI managed to secure two book contracts for the material(see section 6.1).

240213.label: Major findings and research outcome
240213.value: Outcomes: 1. An edited anthology (Aitken and Deprez editors) contracted from Edinburgh University Press, entitled 'The Colonial Documentary Film in South and South-East Asia'. Material from this Berita Singapura project will appear in a chapter entitled 'The People's Action Party of Singapore and Berita Singapura'.The book will appear in 2016. 2.Single-authored (Aitken) research monograph contracted from Palgrave Macmillan entitled 'The British Official Film in South-East Asia: Malaya/Malaysia, Singapore and Hong Kong', in which a chapter entitled 'Berita Singapura and Hong Kong Today' will appear. This book will also appear in 2016. 3. Conference presentation. 12,000 word paper on Berita Singapura: IBSSS, Global Symposium on social Sciences, Bali, May 2015. Conference presentation was entitled ‘A Study of the 1960s Singaporean Official Film Series Berita Singapura'. The PI also served as Panel Chair, Media and Communications Panel, at this conference.. major findings include the following: 1. During the 1960s PAP government succeeded in establishing an authoritarian-capitalist one-party state in Singapore that was reliant upon public-relations output to stifle dissent. 2. This involved the ‘engineering of consent’ through suppression of political opposition, use of legal/police systems, control of the media, censorship, and use of pro-regime public-relations material such as Berita Singapura. 3. The major function of the films was a distractive rather than informational one. 4. Films made on political matters rarely informative/critical - mainly focused on the personalities involved, most prominent being Lee Kwan Yew 5. Despite PAP rhetoric of multi-racialism, films portray a modernising nation outside of racial difference 6. Rhetoric in the Berita Singapura films always positive - rarely posed problems without then detailing solutions to those 7. Technically, films are simply made, with a standard editing and filming technique 8. The fact they are short, and presented in segments, also places limitations on their ability to deal in depth with any subject – they do not generate problematics. 9. Berita Singapura covered final period of the film units based in ex-British colonies 10. In 1969, with television arriving, there was little for the Singapore government to gain by renewing the contract for the series The Berita Singapura role then taken up by Television Singapura in 1969. A study of the Berita Singapura series provides insight into the way that the transition from colony to post-colonial state was effected in Singapore. The Singapore government insisted on close oversight of the series and used it to promote PAP policies. In effect, it became an authoritarian series superintended by an authoritarian government.

240213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
240213.value: This research project into Berita Singapura was a discrete project which has now been accomplished. However, the research will be combined with other studies of colonial film-making appearing in the two contracted books that the PI is involved with, one of which is an anthology featuring contributions by different authors, and comparisons will be made at that point and generated by this. The chapter in the Palgrave Macmillan monograph will also specifically compare Berita Singapura with the colonial film series 'Hong Kong Today' (1966-73), made by the Hong Kong Film Unit. This chapter will focus on the similarities/differences between two official film series produced by authoritarian states, though ones very different from each other: the Crown Colony of Hong Kong and post-colonial Singapore. In the 18,000 word Introduction to the Palgrave monograph the films of Berita Singapura will also be compared to the earlier films made by the Malayan Film Unit during the Malayan Emergency (1948-60), in order to arrive at conclusions on similarities and differences. A future conference on colonial film-making is planned, to be held at HKBU after the appearance of the monograph and the anthology, at which material on this project on Berita Singapura will be presented.

240213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
240213.value: Berita Singapura provides a detailed and illuminating insight into events occurring at the end of the British Empire in South-East Asia. The series also provides insight into the continuing British presence in post-colonial Singapore, and how that affected media and communication. The documentation around the series, and the films themselves, also provides insight into the sort of tensions and difficulties involved in continued relations between the old colonial power and the new postcolonial state. Berita Singapura also reveals the hostility of the PAP government in Singapore to the old colonial regime, and the films also showcase the major PAP policies, relating to areas such as housing development and race relations. Berita Singapura reveals the extent to which the PAP, and Lee Kwan Yew in particular, were determined to control the flow of information, and the extent to which relations with the Commonwealth became increasingly important to Singapore after the expulsion from Malaysia in 1965. This research is of value in analysing, for the first time, a major and substantial series of official films which was the most important vehicle for dissemination of PAP policies and information flow to the people of Singapore during the 1960s.

240413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
240413.value: The development of sociology arose through the historical experiences of the French Revolution, the European Industrial Revolution and European and American urbanization. The intellectual and technical development of sociology during the twentieth century was similarly undertaken in American and European institutions. This particular background of geographic location is necessarily associated with cultural predispositions, preoccupations and limitations. At the same time sociology as a discipline has universalistic pretensions, assuming that it can be applied to social processes and social structures at all times and places. This outlook is encouraged by the global hegemony of ‘metropolitan’ research and scholarship associated with internationally dominant political and economic power. A number of researchers have argued for the recognition of local and indigenous scholarly traditions in the further development of social science in order to overcome the limitations of the perceived ‘Euro-centricism’ of much current sociology. This is particularly evident in Chinese cultural areas where endeavours to sinicize sociology have been undertaken during the last half century. This has included the development of sociological theory founded on Confucian philosophy. This strategy is not inappropriate as all sociology has a philosophical foundation and Anglo-American sociology is often analyzed and promoted in terms of its distinctive philosophical bases. The difficulty with a Confucian foundation of sociology is its limitation in explaining only Chinese cultural formations whereas the rationale for sociology as a ‘science of society’ is that it can explain social processes and social structure irrespective of the cultural complexion of the society subjected to sociological investigation. There is another indigenous Chinese philosophical tradition which arguably has broader application than Confucianism that the PI of this proposed research has already demonstrated has general relevance to sociological analysis. This is the tradition founded on Daodejing, a work extensively discussed by philosophers but neglected by sociologists. The proposed research is to support and advance the research already begun by the PI in examining the relevance of the Daodejing for the development of sociological theories concerning action, power, self, interest and social structure that are not only distinctive but complement and augment mainstream sociology in crucial ways. In this manner a philosophical basis for the development of sociological theory, drawn from Chinese traditions but demonstrably of general relevance in theory building, stands as a genuine alternative to much mainstream theorizing. In this manner the overall competence of sociology is enhanced and its universalistic aspirations realistically encouraged. 社會學的發展與法國革命ˎ 歐洲工業革命以及歐洲同美國城市化之進程密不可分˳ 美國同歐洲雖然地處不同大陸, 卻擁有相似的文化習性ˎ 思維方式及相關的局限性, 所以二十世紀在美國同歐洲的大學及研究機構中社會學理論與研究方法的發展頗為相似˳ 另外, 社會學作為一門學科自居具有普遍適用性, 即其理論與方法在任何時候ˎ 任何地域, 適用於不同的社會過程及結構˳ 這種觀點尤其得到全球權利中心研究界及與國際政治和經濟勢力有聯繫的學術界的支持˳ 有些學者提出為了進一步發展社會學, 本土與土著學術傳統應該得到承認, 以此克服目前社會學以歐洲為中心的現象˳ 中國文化在這方面已做出了相應的努力, 特別是上半個世紀,中國學者展開了社會學中國本土化活動, 其中包括提倡社會學以儒學為基礎的活動˳ 社會學以儒學為基礎這一方式並不具有普遍適用性, 因為任何社會學都有其特殊的哲學基礎, 盎格魯–美國社會學採用的分析手段是與其特殊的哲學基礎密不可分的˳ 以儒學為基礎的社會學局限於僅僅能解釋中國文化現象, 而作為'社會之科學' 的社會學其理性在於不管文化有何種複雜性, 通過社會調查, 其社會過程及結構都可得以解釋與分析˳ 另一個中國本土哲學傳統則比儒學具有更廣泛的適用性, 那就是道德經, 此研究項目的主研究員已經證明了道德經 在社會學分析上具有普遍適用性˳ 道德經 雖已得到哲學家們的廣泛注意, 卻為社會學家們所忽視˳ 此項目的主研究員已經開始研究道德經 在行動ˎ 權利ˎ自我ˎ利益及社會結構方面能否推進社會學理論, 此項目將繼續推進主研究員已經著手進行的研究˳ 此研究項目立意新穎獨特, 並將以對主流社會學理論加以關鍵性之補充與擴展而作出貢獻˳ 借鑒中國傳統作為哲學基礎以發展社會學理論, 展示其構建理論的普遍性, 將為主流社會學理論化提供另一種可能性˳ 由此而來, 社會學理論的分析及解釋能力則會得以進一步加強, 另外, 社會學離其追求普遍適用性的理想則又更接近了一步˳

240713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
240713.value: Healthy eating is important to everyone in every country, and its absence brings about considerable social and economic burdens. Twenty-two percent of primary school students in Hong Kong were obese in 2008-09. This obesity rate demonstrated a significant increase when compared to the 16 percent in 1997-98 (Hong Kong SAR Government, 2010). Mainland China also faces the issue of child obesity. The obesity rate among mainland children under the age of 15 increased from 15 percent in 1982 to 27 percent in 2004 (Lau, 2004). Problems such as obesity have raised questions about how the healthy eating message can best be communicated to young people. Effective health communication should be based on a sound knowledge of young people’s attitudes toward healthy eating and the cognitive psychology involved in health communication. This study will investigate Hong Kong and mainland Chinese adolescents’ intention toward healthy eating. The Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) is used as the theoretical framework to examine how the intention to engage in healthy eating is affected by attitudes, perceived behavioral control and subjective norms related to healthy eating. Variables in addition to the conventional TPB variables will include perceived barriers, self-efficacy, past healthy eating behavior, and behavioral knowledge. The Hong Kong part of the study was conducted in 2012. This project seeks funding to conduct the mainland China part of the study. The research builds on the investigators’ previous work in this area and will make significant theoretical and practical contributions to the understanding of adolescent eating habits in Hong Kong and mainland China. The proposed study will be the first to apply the Theory of Planned Behavior to predict the effects on healthy eating in a Chinese society. Applications of the Theory of Planned Behavior and the associated Theory of Reasoned Action are commonplace in western countries, but the theory has been applied less often in a Chinese context. There is evidence to suggest that for some behaviors predictions may vary depending on the social and cultural settings (Bagozzi et al, 2000). How would the theory apply to the adoption of healthy eating behavior in China? Although the focus of this research is on the theoretical contribution, given the magnitude of the obesity problem in Hong Kong and mainland China the results of the study will also be of practical importance in assisting parents, educators and policy makers in designing health communication strategies for adolescents.

240713.label: Realisation of objectives
240713.value: The funded project builds on the investigators’ previous work in healthy eating and attempts to make significant theoretical and practical contributions to the understanding of adolescent eating behaviors in Hong Kong and Mainland China. The Hong Kong data was collected with funding from a Faculty Research Grant of Hong Kong Baptist University. We planned to collect data in Shanghai and Chengdu. However, we encountered problems in Chengdu because we lost touch with our initiate contact. We established a new contact who could assist us in data collection from Jilin, Changchun. The final sample size of 635 was very close to the planned sample size of 640. All the measures used in the project, including attitudes, subjective norm, perceived behavioral control, self-efficacy, perceived barriers, and behavioral intention demonstrated good Cronhach’s alpha coefficients. To test the validity of the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) in a Chinese cultural context, we adopted a series of multiple regressions for data analysis. We prepared a manuscript and submitted it to the Journal of International Consumer Marketing. One reviewer requested the use of SEM for data analysis. As both investigators were not trained in SEM, we hired a final year PhD student to analyze the data using it. The data analysis took about three weeks. Afterwards, we spent some time in model selection. We finally decided on the most appropriate model and revised the paper accordingly. The revised manuscript was accepted. It was published online and the printed copy will soon be published. Based on the results of EFA and the subsequent CFA results to achieve an adequate fit, we arrived at the following changes in the original proposed model: 1. Two items of attitude were removed because CFA results did not achieve an adequate fit. 2. Four items of interpersonal subjective norm were removed because CFA results did not achieve an adequate fit. 3. Two of the three items of perceived behavioral control were removed because of their cross-loading on behavioral intention. 4. Two items of perceived barriers that did not fit the CFA model were removed. The remaining item of the perceived behavioral control was combined with four items of perceived barriers (reversed in direction of coding) to form a new measure of perceived behavior control. 5. Two self-efficacy items were removed because of an inadequate fit to the CFA results. What we learned from the SEM was that the two constructs “perceived behavioral control” and “behavioral intention” had large overlapping in explained variance. So did the concepts “perceived behavioral control” and “perceived barrier”. Furthermore, the self-efficacy scale demonstrated a high predictive power of behavioral intention. These findings pointed to the direction that “perceived behavioral control” and “perceived barrier” can be combined into one single construct. As self-efficacy proved to be a significant predictor of behavioral intention, the evidence supported the use of an expanded Theory of Planned Behavior to predict healthy eating intentions with self-efficacy as an additional predictor. It also provides insights into the design of intervention measures and programs. The validity of the Expanded Theory of Planned Behavior in a Chinese context among adolescent respondents was tested and reported. Therefore, the first objective was achieved. In the SEM analysis, adolescents’ intentions to practice healthy eating was found to be related to all four proposed predictors, including subjective norm from the media, self-efficacy, attitude toward healthy eating, and perceived behavioral control. The findings also revealed that the effect of subjective norm on behavioral intention was stronger among the participants who scored high in past behavior. Furthermore, the effect of self-efficacy on behavioral intention was stronger among the participants who scored low in past behavior. Regarding the moderating effect of gender, the results showed that subjective norm was positively related to behavioral intention among males but not females. Moreover, the attitude toward healthy eating was found to be positively related to behavioral intention among the females, but not males. We therefore conclude that behavioral intention was moderated by past behavior as well as by gender. Therefore the second objective was achieved. Comparing the results from the two sub-samples obtained in Hong Kong and China, we found some differences. Mainland Chinese adolescents had significantly higher healthy eating intention than Hong Kong adolescents. For the TPB and additional variables, mainland participants had a significantly higher level of healthy eating attitudes, perceived behavioral control, and perceived social norms, and a lower level of perceived barriers than Hong Kong participants. So, the third research objective was achieved. As a result, all the three project objectives were achieved fully. We presented the results of the Hong Kong/China comparison at the 21st International Conference of the International Association for Intercultural Communication Studies (IAICS), Hong Kong, July 15-18, 2015. Several conference attendants found the results interesting. However, they also commented that the differences between the China and Hong Kong samples were insignificant. The data collected from China indicated that the respondents had positive attitudes toward healthy eating. We would like to explore how they perceived healthy foods and unhealthy foods. We conducted a focus group study to explore the perception of healthy and unhealthy foods among adolescents. One manuscript was accepted for publication after three rounds of revision. Another manuscript was being prepared. With the additional qualitative data and one manuscript accepted for publication, we would consider that we over-achieved our objectives.

240713.label: Major findings and research outcome
240713.value: A study was conducted to test an expanded Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) in predicting healthy eating intention among adolescents in Shanghai and Jilin in mainland China. Two variables (perceived barriers and self-efficacy) were added in the TPB. A purposive sampling design was adopted to select schools, then students. Altogether 635 adolescents completef a structured questionnaire about healthy eating. Results of confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling supported the structural validity of the proposed expanded model, with attitude toward healthy eating, subjective norm, perceived behavioral control, self-efficacy, and perceived barriers as predictors of behavioral intention. Confirmatory factor analysis suggested that selected items of the perceived behavioral control and perceived barriers should be combined to form a new measure of perceived behavioral control. The new measure of perceived behavioral control and self-efficacy was found to be more important than attitude and subjective norm in predicting healthy eating. Past behavior and gender were significant moderating variables. The effect of subjective norm on behavioral intention was stronger among respondents who scored high in past behavior. The effect of self-efficacy on behavioral intention was stronger among respondents who scored low in past behavior. Furthermore, subjective norm was positively related to behavioral intention among males but not females. Attitude toward healthy eating had positive correlation with behavioral intention among the females, but not males. Results from China were compared to results obtained from a previous study conducted in Hong Kong. Mainland adolescents showed more positive attitudes toward healthy eating, and perceived a higher level of social norms about healthy eating. They also perceived a lower level of barrier of healthy eating than Hong Kong respondents. Mainland Chinese adolescents demonstrated a higher intention to eat healthily. Perceived barrier was a significant predictor of behavioral intention for Hong Kong respondents, but not for mainland Chinese respondents. There is a need to conduct further studies to explain such differences. As behavioral control and self-efficacy were found to be the two most significant variables in predicting intention to engage in healthy eating, the study points to the importance of fostering an environment where adolescents can make healthy food choices. Facilitating greater behavioral control and self-efficacy could be accomplished by teaching adolescents how to prepare time-saving healthy snacks/meals, raising their awareness of healthier food choices, providing positive support at home and school to reward healthy eating, and ensuring that healthy food choices are available.

240713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
240713.value: The research can be further developed to predict healthy eating among the adult population. Ajzen (2015) argued that the age and gender variables can be modeled as a background factor in the Theory of Planned Behavior. We can investigate whether age and gender have a direct effect on behavioral intentions, or on behavior. We can also investigate if the effects of age and gender are mediated by attitudes, subjective norms, or perceptions of controls. The current study is able to inform the design of health intervention initiatives to encourage healthy eating among adolescents in Hong Kong and mainland China. The PI was granted a Quality Education Fund to work with Dr. Judy Siu of Hong Kong Polytechnic University to design a school-based intervention program to encourage healthy eating among adolescents. The design of the invention initiatives was grounded in the research findings from the Hong Kong study. The QEF project was completed in May 2016. A similar project can be done in mainland China. 240713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
240713.value: The overweight and obesity rate among mainland Chinese children under the age of 20 was 18.8 percent in 2013. This study investigated mainland Chinese adolescents’ intention of healthy eating. The Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) was used as the theoretical framework to examine how the intention to engage in healthy eating is affected by attitudes, perceived behavioral control and subjective norms. Additional variables including perceived barrier and self-efficacy were added to the theoretical model. Results indicated that perceived behavioral control and self-efficacy were the most important variables for predicting adolescents’ intention to eat healthily. Attitude toward healthy eating was a significant predictor of healthy eating intention among girls while subjective norm was a significant predictor of healthy eating intention among boys. The results imply that there is a need to empower adolescents with the knowledge necessary for and skills of making healthy eating choices. There is also a need to make the environment conducive to healthy eating. Parents and educators as socializing agents can create the norm that healthy eating is considered smart and trendy. Innovative and interactive communication efforts can be designed to change adolescents’ attitude toward healthy eating.

240813.label: Project Objectives
240813.value: To shed new light on property ownership and property transfer in Chinese lineage villages through an unprecedented examination of the extensive and complete set of land and house title deed records. The findings will provide strong and detailed evidence of a complex and multifaceted system of property inheritance and management other than the male-only inheritance pattern commonly suggested by the lineage literature. To complement the literature on Chinese customary mortgages by paying due attention to: (a) the role and significance of corporate/ancestral estates and kinship ties in securing their members’ financial needs and making profits from loans; and (b) the characteristics of interest payments and the time of redemption. The findings will enhance our understanding of the significance of kinship in financial activity at the village or trans-village level. To suggest as a new research direction the examination of an existing but overlooked set of archives/documents (land and house title deeds) providing rich and accurate information that reveals and even predicts the continuity of and changes in corporate single-surname villages in Hong KOng's New Territories in the past, present and future. To comprehensively reveal the management of property transformations in local kinship organizations that accepts or normalises very diverse arrangements in respond to changing circumstances or to strike the balance between individual rights and collective interests.

240813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
240813.value: Single-surname lineages are commonly found in Hong Kong’s New Territories. They largely share the following features: members tracing their descent from a common ancestor, bearing an identical surname, and occupying a common residence in a walled village or territorially well-defined settlement; sons instead of daughters holding descent status; practicing the patrilineal rule of property inheritance; and owning corporate holdings (at the family and lineage levels) which serve to protect the welfare and interests of members and to maintain the tradition of collective worship and its associated identity. Thus, it is essential to maintain the patrilineal inheritance of land and village houses to perpetuate the existence of such localized corporate lineages. The New Territories have undergone a major process of rapid transformation since the 1970s, mainly due to the trends of urbanization and modernization and to the impacts of colonial administration and policy related to the customary and statutory rights of lineage villagers. Under these changing circumstances, to what extent has the rule of patrilineal inheritance been strictly observed or occasionally violated in such localized corporate lineages? What changes have taken place in the meanings and forms of ownership, management, and transfer (sale and succession) of land and village houses, both individually owned and corporately owned, in colonial and post-colonial regimes? How have the complicated and symbiotic relationships between gender (in)equality in property rights, lineage customs, and communal identity been (re)defined in response to changing circumstances? The proposed study will seek to answer the above under-researched questions by embarking on a pioneering examination of land and house title deeds giving a complete record of ownership, mortgages and transactions from 1905 onwards. By investigating deeds owned by three selected major corporate lineage villages in the New Territories—the Tang lineage of Ha Tsuen, the Liu lineage of Sheung Shui and the Man lineage of San Tin—a large set of cases will be collected and analyzed systematically. This archival study, which will be coupled with in-depth interviews of lineage villagers, will reveal a substantial variety of forms and patterns of property rights, property management practices, ownership, and property transfers over the last 100 years, and their associated hegemonic or contested meanings. The findings will complement existing lineage studies that demonstrate only a single pattern of patrilineal inheritance, thereby shedding new light on the continuity of and changes in New Territories lineages in the colonial and post-colonial regimes from a property rights perspective. 單姓宗族村落在香港新界隨處可見。它們有著以下的共同特徵: 成員來自同一祖先、擁有同一姓氏、聚居同一地方、男姓成員擁有繼嗣權、財產以父-子繼嗣方式承傳、在家和族的層面均擁有嘗產來保障成員福祉、維持集體祭祀活動、以及成員之間的認同感。因此，維持土地和房屋的父-子承繼方式，是延續本地宗族村落的重要手段。 由1970年起, 都市化、現代化、以及殖民地政策, 對新界宗族村落有著顯著的改變。有鑒於此，父-子承繼方式是否得以維持、或者在可時被摒棄? 對於在殖民和後殖民時期, 個人和家族財產的業權、管理和轉讓(出售和繼承)有著甚麼意義和形式上的轉變？性別(不)平等、財產權、宗族傳統、以及集體認同之間的複雜、共生關係如何在變遷的社會、經濟、政治環境中被重申定義？ 是次研究，分析新界宗族村落由1905迄今的土地和房屋產權、抵押和轉讓來解答上述問題。通過調查廈村鄧族、新田文族、和上水廖族擁有的產業契約，得以收集大量個案並作出有系統的分析。是次檔案研究，附以深入的面談，能掀示過往百多年產權、管理和轉讓的不同形式及規律，以及它們的多層和富爭議性的意義。研究成果能補充現有宗族研究所陳述的單一父系繼嗣方式，因為以產權角度來切入，能對新界宗族在殖民、後殖民時代的延續和變遷有新的了解。

240813.label: Realisation of objectives
240813.value: This research project achieved to identify and examine all land lots and house lots owned by the Liu lineage in Sheung Shui, the Man lineage in San Tin, and the Tang lineage in Ha Tsuen in the New Territories of Hong Kong during the period 1905-2015. Liu lineage Man lineage Tang lineage Total No. of lots no. of Land lots 2826 5151 2384 10361 no. of house lots 2750 1049 1025 4824 As the above table shows, a total of 10,361 land lots and 4,824 house lots were identified. By making use of Block Crown Lease, Lot Index Plan, Land Register and Memorial documents, the research team successfully collected all kinds of transactions during the research period 1905-2015. These transactions include mortgage, sale, succession, division, assignment, appointment of manager, and appointment or removal of trusteeship. Based on these, we have established two databases: one is on mortgage and another on transfer. The first database includes all details of mortgage loan (either land/house or both as collateral), namely, the identity and address of lender and borrower, the date of transaction, the amount of loan, the length of mortgage, the loan interest, the time of redemption, and the form of payment. All these information captures or provides a detailed picture and substantial cases of formal moneylending activities of the Liu lineage of Sheung Shui (1179 cases of land mortgage and 197 cases of house mortgage), the Tang lineage of Ha Tsuen (314 cases of land mortgage and 82 cases of house mortgage) and the Man lineage of San Tin (1026 cases of land mortgage and 104 cases of house mortgage). Based on a comparative analysis of all these mortgage cases (2902 in total) amongst the three lineages, we have substantially revealed patterns and characteristics of Chinese customary mortgages in rural communities under colonial administration and changing socio-economic circumstances. The project objective no. 2 has been achieved. The second database is composed of all transactions of both land and house. Information include time and frequency of transfer, the natures of transfer, the identity of buyer(s), seller(s) or inheritor(s). The following table indicate number of transaction records of land and house. Liu lineage Man lineage Tang lineage Total No. of cases land transfer cases 4631 6164 4315 15110 house transfer cases 1886 2189 1794 5869 Drawing from these data, we achieved to substantively reveal a holistic, longitudinal picture and, more importantly, patterns of transfer and management of land and house in Chinese lineage communities. Since land and house are two major constituents of Chinese lineage as a corporate kinship organization and patrilineal inheritance is adopted to maintain the integrity of closely-knit agnatic community, the data we collected provide solid and rich information about stringency, laxity, or flexibility of patrilineal inheritance rule in regulating property transfer to strike the balance between individual rights and collective interests. In so doing, the continuity of and changes in corporate single-surname village in rural Hong Kong will be clearly demonstrated. Project objectives no. 1, no. 2 and no. 4 have been achieved.

240813.label: Major findings and research outcome
240813.value: 1. Regarding mortgage issues, we have found that: (a) a century-old Chinese customary mortgage practice (dian) was no longer popular in the New Territories under British colonial rule, whereas another one (diya), which was not legalized in imperial times, has become a dominant form in a colonial regime; (2) non-kin people and institutions also played an active role in moneylending activities; (3) borrowers did not receive concessionary interest rate from kin moneylenders; (4) cash instead of crop was a common form of interest payment; (5) a certain number of female moneylenders were found in moneylending activities in rural communities; and (6) land was more popular than house as collateral in the mortgage loan. 2. Regarding property transfer and management, we have found that: (1) in the transfer of house, agnatic kins are largely found to be inheritors or buyers; whereas in land transfer, a large number of buyers were non-kin people; (2) there are a few cases of widows as the sole administratrix or beneficiary of her deceased husband’s estate; (3) a customary practice of forming corporate estate (by putting land or house in trust in the name of ancestor, association or deity) was no longer common; and (4) the frequency of transfer of land was much higher than that of house.

240813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
240813.value: A comparative study of mortgage practices and property transfer and management between lineages in the New Territories of Hong Kong and lineages in Taiwan in the early 20th century will be an interesting and pathbreaking research project. This proposed research attempts to reveal how Chinese customary practices in terms of collateral loan as well as property transfer and management had been shaped by different types of colonial administration (British rule in Hong Kong [1898-1997] and Japanese rule in Taiwan [1895-1945]). To the best of my knowledge, land records in Taiwan during Japanese occupation are very detailed and well preserved. Therefore, this comparative study is highly feasible to have many influential findings and to develop many insightful arguments.

240813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
240813.value: This research project aims at revealing patterns and characteristics of some Chinese customary practices in terms of collateral loan as well as property transfer and management in Chinese lineage communities in rural New Territories where such closely-knit settlements are dominant. The findings provide substantial evidence to evaluate the impacts of British colonial administration on some century-old Chinese customs, the value and roles of kin and non-kin ties in different types of transactions or transfer, the role and status of women in family division and moneylending activities, and the stringency or flexibility of male-only inheritance rule. Through this comparative study, changes and continuities of Chinese lineage communities in rural Hong Kong have been clearly revealed and delineated.

240913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
240913.value: This research project seeks to examine the political influence of the Protestant churches in Hong Kong. Specifically, this research will use Paul Djupe and Christopher Gilbert’s theory of religious influence on political behavior to investigate how the social context of the Protestant churches facilitates the development of socioreligious subcultures inside and outside formal church structures, and how the membership in these subculture units opens up organizational channels that build social networks and transmit political information, leading to enhanced rates of political participation. The subject of study is the 23 member churches/ denominations of the Hong Kong Christian Council, in which include 262 churches in Hong Kong. This study will use both survey and interview as research methods for a full test of the effects of the Protestant churches on the political behavior of their members. The research findings will provide a clearer understanding of the contributions of the Protestant churches to sustaining civil society in Hong Kong. The theoretical significance of this research project is that, it will explicate a theory of church-centered influences on political behavior based on contextual analysis, which will advance the study of religion and politics in Hong Kong. Regarding the practical significance, it will provide a specified model of how voluntary associations expose individuals to political information and norms, which will help us to understand how public opinion is formed and why people participate in politics. 這個研究計劃考察基督新教教會在香港社會政治上的影響。具體而言，這個研究以Paul Djupe和Christopher Gilbert的宗教影響政治行為的理論作為架構，查考基督新教的社會脈絡如何促進教會正規架構內部和外部的次文化，以及教會成員如何在次文化的單位中建立組織渠道去發展社會網絡和傳遞政治資訊，使得政治參與率的上昇。這研究計劃將會以香港基督教協進會中的23個成員教會和宗派作為研究對像，其中包括共262間教會。這個研究會同時採用問卷調查和面談的方法，測量基督新教教會對其信徒的政治行為的影響。研究結果將會為基督新教教會支撑香港公民社會的現象提供一個清晰的解釋。這個研究計劃在理論上的意義，在於從處境分析的進路去闡明教會影響政治行為的理論，從而提昇香港在宗教與政治的研究。在現實意義方面，這個研究會提供一個特定的模型，幫助我們理解志願團體如何影響個人的政治的行為和規範、公眾輿論如何形成，以及為何人們會參與政治。

241113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
241113.value: 本研究項目的對象是劉晨阮肇奇遇這個在中國文學史上有著重要影響的文學主題的衍變發展，論述其淵源及其在三至十三世紀期間的改編情況。 這個文學傳統的原始故事見於南朝宋劉義慶的《幽明錄》。故事敘述劉阮二人入山迷路，邂逅二女。十日後，二人思歸，但被女子強留數月方得離去；出山後方知人間已歷七世。 劉阮故事成為後世文學改編所本並形成一個文本群落。這些文本的體裁包括詩詞、小說、戲曲等體裁。本研究通過對比分析論證，探討原故事中的元素如劉阮角色以及某些情節在後世文本中的改編發展。研究涵蓋的時代為二世紀至十三世紀，所涉文類包括志怪小說、民俗傳說、傳奇、道經、詩詞、戲曲等；研究重點主要有涉及修辭、詩律、宗教、民俗、政治、情色文學、飲食文化、時空轉移等方面的議題。

241113.label: Realisation of objectives
241113.value: Objective 1: The project has achieved this objective by researching the understudied literary tradition and, through communication with scholars, publicized my findings of the research. Objective 2: The project succeeded in exploring and evaluating a wide range of methods of literary adaptation and, by the establishment and analysis of the theme paradigm as planned, arguing that the theme underwent different adaptive methods in different historical and cultural backgrounds. Objective 3: The research successfully identified and evaluate how certain cultural elements such as dinning made to the uniqueness of the literary tradition. This was done in an extensive search for evidence and in-depth analysis of it. We argue that the spatiotemporal displacement was mainly ascribed to the unique effect of the consumption of "magical food." Objective 4: The project achieved this goal by employment of new angle and methodology. By identifying a traditional theme but researching in an innovative method, the research has drawn attention from audience in the US and the Chinese speaking world. For example, the rereading of Li Bai's poem of Mt. Tiantai from a perspective of "transcendence seeking" yielded new inspiration for the analysis of the imagery and textual variants of the poems in question.

241113.label: Major findings and research outcome
241113.value: The first part of the research discusses how prevalent dietary beliefs contributed to the literary motif of spatiotemporal displacement in narratives written in early medieval China (approx. 2nd–5th centuries CE). In the otherworldly realm as seen in these kinds of narratives, time elapses significantly faster than the real world. The chapter focuses on the tale about Liu Chen 劉晨 and Ruan Zhao 阮肇, the main subject of the research project, and examines how peach and sesame enabled the two fellows to survive in this realm of different spatio-temporal dimension, as well as how these magical ingredients underpin the process of fantasy in this narrative and in other similar ones. The second part of the research discusses two poems by Li Bai (701-12) written on his visits to Mount Tiantai. It solves a textual crux of a poem and examines his political thought in relation to his Daoist belief. Through the discussion of the image of the great peng bird in relation to Mt. Penglai, one of the three mythological sacred mountains in Daoist lore, this chapter offers a clear outline of his state of mind when he was about to accept the imperial summon (in 742) for a position at the court of Emperor Xuanzong. The third part examines the shared sentiments and enlightenments of Yuan Zhen (779–831) and Bai Juyi (772–846) as reflected in their exchange poems entitled “A Spring Outing in A Dream.” It identifies the Liu Chen and Ruan Zhao tale as a provenance of an early Tang tale, Roaming to the Grotto of the Fairies, as well as Yuan and Bai’s writing on Yuan’s romantic past. In their respective (auto)biographical representations, Yuan expresses his romantic nostalgia while Bai turns the discourse into a lesson on Buddhist enlightenment. The last part studies Liu Yuxi’s (772–842) treatment of the Liu-Ruan tale in his poems written while in exile. Liu apparently adapts Tao Qian’s version of the Peach Blossom Spring adventure but also initiates some significant changes. The locale (in modern Hu’nan) where Liu was exiled patently inspired Liu to write about Tao Qian’s Peach Blossom Spring, but our poet to some extent integrates the two tales in his political satire. The imagery of the wonderland becomes a platform for Liu to play with a variety of thematic elements, such as accidental intrusion in the “paradise,” Daoist lore, and spatiotemporal displacement.

241113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
241113.value: The GRF project has given rise to a clear picture of my long-term project. I submitted another application under the category of “continuation” for my planned book project in 2015 and 2016, respectively. As the four draft chapters are under revision, they yield inspiration for further research, for which I have planned four other chapters. Below is a tentative table of contents of this entire book project: Introduction: Liu Chen and Ruan Zhao and the Quest for the Wonderland Ch 1: Magical Food and Spatiotemporal Displacement in Early Chinese Narratives Ch 2: The Peng Bird and Penglai: Li Bai on Mt. Tiantai Ch 3: Another Day in Paradise: Liu Yuxi and the Peach Blossom Spring Ch 4: Remembrance of the Grotto: Bai Juyi and Yuan Zhen on Liu-Ruan Ch 5: The Nymph in Love: Liu-Ruan in Late Tang and Five Dynasties Poetry Ch 6: “Songs of the Grotto Nymphs Sending off Master Ruan Home”: the Feminine Lovesickness in Song Ci-poetry Ch 7: Liu-Ruan’s Ordeal and Religious Conversion in Yuan, Ming, and Qing Dramatic Re-creations Ch 8: Liu Chen and Ruan Zhao’s Time-travel to Classical Japanese Literature Conclusion Upon completion, I will submit the manuscript to a major publisher for publication.

241113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
241113.value: Nature: The project is a study of the formation of a literary tradition and its later developments. By looking into its intellectual and literary backgrounds, we reconstruct the making of Liu Chen and Ruan Zhao’s otherworldly adventure, and in what ways this tale was adapted to later, various literary genres such as poetry, drama, and folklore, with new motivation, content, and reference. Significance: The tale in question underwent a long process of adaptation, assumed a new metaphorical content and aesthetic value in each adaptive work, and formed a very important tradition; nonetheless, a comprehensive in-depth study has yet to appear. The project is intended to fill this lacuna by bringing in fresh insights and research methodology in its dealing with this body of texts, which have never been systematically analyzed and studied. Value: The anticipated outcomes of the project make significant impacts in relevant fields such as literary studies, religious studies, and cultural studies. The conference presentations delivered on different occasions have called attention from scholars in relevant fields in the USA, Mainland China, and Taiwan. The publication of the monograph, which is under preparation, will make a solid contribution to relevant fields and exert its long-term influence.

241313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
241313.value: The Honda strike in May 2010 triggered worker protests across China. Encouragingly, almost half the strikes reportedly concluded with some form of collective bargaining (CB) occurring between management and workers, and a pay raise. Nevertheless, the emerging form of CB in China differs from its counterparts in industrialized countries in important ways. While it constitutes one of workers’ collective rights in the West, exercised through trade unions in an institutionalized setting, CB in China has thus far remained largely spontaneous and scattered. Although local governments and trade unions have come to recognize its ability to resolve industrial conflicts and have begun promoting it, enormous uncertainties stand in the process of institutionalizing CB, as it may engender changes in power relations within factories. This project aims to understand the contexts, processes, actors, and impact on labor relations of emerging CB practices in Chinese factories. Specifically, it seeks to accomplish the following goals: To examine the socioeconomic context that gives rise to CB in China and explain why it becomes increasingly important for labor disputes resolution in the workplace. To explore whether strikes and CB increase workers’ awareness of collective rights and how workers were organized and represented during the CB process, without the presence of trade unions, and assess the long-term implications of CB for China’s labor movement. To investigate the attitude of local governments and trade unions toward CB and their attempt to regularize it, and assess the effect of different models of bargaining (i.e., government-driven, union-driven, and strike-driven bargaining) across the regions. To explore the bargaining process and the patterns of interaction among concerned parties, i.e., governmental agencies, trade unions, worker representatives, and employers, and explain the factors that shape the result of bargaining. As the current theories on CB is based on western experiences, the project stands to make a novel contribution to the CB literature by revealing the socioeconomic and institutional settings in which CB arises, and its actors, processes, mechanisms and outcomes. The project will advance our understanding of the development of the Chinese labor movement in light of workers’ growing awareness of collective rights and the role of trade unions facing workers’ rising demand for genuine representation. This research will also extend our understanding of the changing state-labor relations by exploring how the state’s response to CB shapes the constraints, as well as opportunities, facing China’s labor movement in the years to come. 2012年5月本田汽車廠工人罷工觸發了中國自市場改革以來最大的罷工潮。令人鼓舞的是，約半數的罷工導致了集體談判，工人的漲薪要求得到滿足。但是。正在中國出現的集體談判與西方工業化國家的集體談判在許多方面有很大不同。在西方，集體談判是工人基本的集體權利之一，通過工會來實施，得到制度保障。而在中國，集體談判是自發的，在一些工廠零散發生。 雖然有些地方政府和工會已經意識到集體談判對於解決工業沖突的重要性，正在試圖推動這一做法，但建立集體談判制度的過程仍然存在著巨大的不確定性，畢竟，集體談判的實施會對企業勞資權力關系產生重大影響。 此研究項目意在理解正在中國工廠出現的集體談判的背景、過程、行動者和影響。具體而言，本項目試圖達至以下目標： 審視集體談判興起的社會經濟背景，解釋為何集體談判對解決勞動爭議變得日益重要。 探索罷工和集體談判是否增強工人的集體權利意識，工人如何在無工會幫助的情況下，在集體談判過程自我組織並在談判桌尋求有效代表；評價集體談判對勞動關系發展的長遠意義。 調查地方政府和工會對集體談判的態度以及他們如何試圖使之規則化，評價不同地區的不同集體談判模式（即政府推動型，工會推動型和罷工推動型）。 探索談判過程和不同行動者（即地方政府，工會，工人代表，罷工群體和雇主）的互動模式，解釋何種因素決定談判的結果。 現存有關集體談判的文獻主要是以西方經驗和實踐為基礎的。本項目通過揭示中國集體談判獨特的社會經濟和制度背景以及由此產生的行動者，過程，機制和結果，力圖對現存文獻有所貢獻。本研究還將從工人權利意識的出現和工會角色變化的角度，來加深對中國工人運動發展的認識。最後，通過觀察國家對工人罷工和集體談判的應對，本研究將拓展對中國國家-社會關系變化的理解。

241613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
241613.value: The Shang (16th-11th cent. BC) and Zhou (1045?-221 BC) dynasties, the heyday of Bronze Age China, have grown increasingly vivid to scholars in the past several decades due to the excavation of many important bronze vessels, in addition to the more than 10,000 inscribed bronzes already extant. All these bronzes provide us with concrete accounts and direct information about critical events in early China. However, the inscribed bronzes also pose endless challenges to our understanding of the remote past in terms of the divergence in readings of inscriptional characters, interpretation of the contexts, attribution of the donors, and chronology of their production. Scholars have contributed a tremendous scholarly literature analyzing these bronze objects and the contents of these inscriptions. This research has been published in various different sources and media around the world, and hence made difficult to locate. Although there are a number of publications dealing with the diverse readings of certain major bronze inscriptions (See references), many of them need to be updated to include more recent studies, and some of the most important objects have never been treated comprehensively. There is an urgent need for a series of books to synthesize the research on important inscribed bronzes to date. To satisfy this need, this project purports to organize a number of international scholars who specialize in bronze inscriptions and paleography to collaborate in the compilation of book manuscripts, each treating one or one group of important bronze vessels. Aiming to deal eventually with most of the important inscribed bronzes, this project, which comprises about 15 volumes with treatment of approximately 20 odd pieces dated to the Western Zhou, is merely the first stage, and we hope that it will provide a sound base and an authoritative reference for international research on Zhou history. The obvious significance of this project has attracted interest of three prestigious publishers in China, namely Shanghai Renmin （上海人民）、Shanghai Guji （上海古籍）and Zhongxi Shuju（中西書局）. As PI, I would conceive my roles in the proposed project as follows: 1. Organizing a team of international specialists on bronze inscriptions and coordinating with researchers to work on different bronze objects. 2. Designing the formats, patterns and styles of the book manuscripts with Co-I and other compilers. 3. Compiling or co-authoring one or two of the book manuscripts in the series. 4. Finalizing the manuscripts by other authors and refining them to be ready for publication.

241813.label: Project Title(Chinese)
241813.value: 夜間社會學:中國夜經濟對公共空間,社會政治觀,和社會分層的影響

241813.label: Project Objectives
241813.value: To examine how local Chinese residents resist, reclaim, and negotiate the gentrified urban spaces of jiubajie (nightlife districts). To investigate the sociopolitical values of individuals who consume commercial nightlife in China. To examine how nightlife consumption practices in China reinforce as well as disrupt hierarchical socioeconomic structures.
