244513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
244513.value: The second round of public consultation on the review of Obscene and Indecent Articles Ordinance (Cap 390) (COIAO) ended in mid-July 2012, debates regarding the obscure mechanism of Obscene Articles Tribunal (OAT) in defining “obscenity” and “indecency” within images, in the context of the image itself, derived publication and display. The status and execution power of OAT have been criticised of censoring renowned Western artworks, mostly nude paintings and sculptures. The Principal Investigator (PI) observes the tension between legal definition, and nudity and eroticism as a common genre in the visual arts, albeit its contexts and significance differ. Such tension is not caused solely by legislation but the confronted conservatism towards the perception of human bodies versus those look to revisit and expand such perception. Indeed the classification made by OAT fail to convince certain sector within the local community, while it prompts closer to the problem of existent conservatism across the secondary and tertiary art curriculum, as well as a more interactive platform of the value of nude and/or erotic art. A more focused discussion, and hence research is needed in collecting views and reflection from the local cultural and art circle on the various threshold and development of nude and/or erotic in the Hong Kong context, so as to enable a bottom-up platform for the art practitioners and the public to access and respond to more concrete examples. The proposed project works to fill in the gap of the online database from OAT, it is and would be for administrative record as it would “only record the classification results, the cross-reference number and the description of the articles” and the PI reckons it would cause further confusion, and that is in which an “unofficial” database built by academic(s) and art practitioners should come into place. 香港政府於2012年7月中旬完成《淫褻及不雅物品管制條例》第二階段公眾諮詢，然而當局尚未就何謂「淫褻」及「不雅」圖像作清晰的指引或定義。不僅其定義有欠清晰，過往淫褻物品審裁處於處理西方藝術品的準則亦備受文化界批評。東西方藝術素有男女胴體的圖像，當中包含文化意象的更不計其數，當局若單憑作品中人裸露與否而將其評定為「不雅」或「淫褻」將有損創作及表達自由。 有見及此，本硏究會從不同角度剖析本港對裸體及情色圖像之接受尺度，並透過收集各位地數據及先例，與本地藝術家及相關團體進行硏究及訪問，繼而從民間及文化藝術從業員角度出發，尋求一個能權衡文化藝術從業員及公眾兩者權益的方案；並就硏究所得建立網上資料庫，當中包含不同圖像及法律資訊以供公眾參考。該資料庫會於非官方或民間渠道發放，務求公眾在條例修訂前後能在官方渠道以外有一全面及學術性的支援。

244513.label: Realisation of objectives
244513.value: To investigate how nude and erotic art is displayed and received in Hong Kong, the team conducted a literature review of the relevant laws that govern the control of obscene and indecent articles in Hong Kong, including the statutory framework and case law. In reviewing the cases, the team studied the relevant legal judgments to understand how the law is applied in practice. In addition, the team also reviewed the newspaper commentaries and articles reporting on the case to gauge media and public sentiments on the issue. At the same time, the team collected images of the nude/erotic art involved in the relevant cases, as well as nude/erotic art of the artists that we interviewed and examples of nude/erotic art that has been exhibited in Hong Kong to enable a more solid basis for our discussion. To enable a bottom-up approach to discussion, the team distributed a survey for art teachers and art students in secondary and tertiary education. The surveys are distributed online and the response rate is low, which could also be attributed to the fact that this is a rare topic in the local education sector. The survey, which focuses on the content of Hong Kong art education, is complemented by the team's interviews with Hong Kong artists, which is an important component of our research. The team has interviewed nine artists whose works involve nudity or erotic contents. Despite the small sample size of our surveys and interviews, they help shed light on the issues and different perspectives that arise and therefore, has potentials in opening up the discussion in this area, including the defining line for obscene and indecent articles and the covering of debatable content in Hong Kong art education. The combination of both qualitative and quantitative research methods help lay the foundation for a contextual analysis of censorship. The importance of context is highly relevant under the legislation and the purpose of our literature review is to better understand the legal and factual background of a case, which is supplemented by the relevant reports and commentaries in newspapers and journals for a more balanced analysis. In the interviews, the artists were provided with the relevant contextual background of the cases and to comment on them. The team believes that a discussion on this topic will only be more valid with the contextual understanding of a case.

244513.label: Major findings and research outcome
244513.value: While the Obscene Articles Tribunal has often been criticised for being arbitrary and its lack of consistencies, our research suggests that this is due to a lack of understanding and awareness of the contextual background of the case and the legislation that governs the control of obscene and indecent articles. The importance of context is confirmed by the Office for Film, Newspaper and Article Administration, the body that regulates the standards of decency, which reiterates that they will consider the dominant effect of an article as a whole. In the reporting of cases that involve arts and nudity, the newspaper commentaries tend to be one-sided and do not aid understanding of the law. Our findings also highlight the challenges and shortcomings of obscenity laws, which the government public consultation has referred to. However, our research argues that the real problem lies in the concept of the local community standard, which is one of the factors used to determine whether or not an article is obscene or indecent, and the illusion that a common community standard can be reached on issues relating to obscenity and indecency. Our findings on the survey, despite the small sample size, suggests that the question of what is art differs, even amongst art teachers. The response also indicates the importance of context in the area of art education and the factors that will influence the teaching include the religion beliefs of the school, the age and gender of the students. The interviews with artists provide a different perspective to the issue as they shed light on the factors they would consider in appraising a work of art. Nonetheless artists may differ on the issue of what is or is not erotic or obscene. However, they tend to be more open-minded towards nudity and eroticism due to their educational training and exposure to western influence. The findings are reported in journal articles, one of which has been published in 2015 in the Hong Kong Visual Arts Yearbook. The other has been submitted for publication.

244513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
244513.value: There is potential for further research into the changing attitudes towards arts and nudity in Hong Kong, the potential for using alternative dispute resolution methods in resolving disputes involving controversial works of art and to broaden the discussion to include contemporary works of art that might be controversial because of the sensitivity of the issues involved, not merely nudity and eroticism.

244513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
244513.value: This research evaluates the law that governs obscenity in Hong Kong and how they are applied in practice and in cases involving works of art. The objective of the research is to highlight the challenges of identifying the boundary between art and obscenity by providing a contextual analysis of censorship. Instead of focusing on how obscenity and indecency should be defined, the research argues that the challenge lies in defining the context of the case, specifically the concept of the local community standards in determining the question of what is or is not obscene. This research questions whether the tribunal and court is the best forum to resolve issues involving nudity and eroticism in arts and explores alternative methods to resolve disputes involving controversial works of art. This is significant in the context of contemporary art and with art moving into public space, which not only brings art closer to the public but may also give rise to conflicts.

244913.label: Project Title(Chinese)
244913.value: 體感遊戲對久坐兒童的有氧運動能力，體力活動及運動自我效能的干預研究

244913.label: Project Objectives
244913.value: To determine the effect of a prescribed active video game intervention on children’s aerobic fitness compared to usual PA. To determine the impact of AVG on children’s PA levels, screen time consumption, exercise-related self-efficacy, competence to be active and enjoyment.
rows: To determine the effect of a prescribed active video game intervention on children’s aerobic fitness compared to usual PA.
To determine the impact of AVG on children’s PA levels, screen time consumption, exercise-related self-efficacy, competence to be active and enjoyment.

244913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
244913.value: Background: 22% of Chinese primary children are catgorized as overweight/obese and currently, they are doing very little exercise [1]. Sedentary behaviors such as children's screen time (TV viewing, non-active video games) are thought to be a major origin of this outcome. Information communication technology provides a platform to activate more physical interaction betwwen the children and the screen. This AVG may be able to replace the traditional non-active video games [2]. However AVG studies are still providing mixing results on this research question and need more scientific evidence. Aims: To determine the effect of a prescribed AVG intervention on children’s aerobic fitness compared to usual PA. Primary outcome: Exercise capacity (maximal oxygen uptake; VO2max) assessed with a 20-meter shuttle run field test at 12 weeks. Secondary outcomes: VO2max at 24 weeks, change in objective measured PA assessed at 12- and 24 weeks and self-reported exercise-related self-efficacy, screen time consumption, competence to be active and enjoyment. Design: A standard two-arm parallel, single-blinded, randomized control trial Participants: Chinese primary students will be recruited from schools in Hong Kong. Inclusion criteria: 1) Aged 10-12 years old; 2) Play video games ≥ 2 hours/week; 3) have no contraindications to perform PA. Intervention: Children randomized to the intervention will participate in an AVG intervention three times per week for 12 weeks, in addition to their usual activity levels. Each exercise session will last 60 minutes and the research team will prescribe updated active video games consistent with moderate-vigorous intensity. Control: The control group will continue with usual PA alone and will not receive the AVG intervention. Sample size: 80 participants will provide 90% power at 5% level of significance to detect a group difference of 3 ml/kg/min in change of peak VO2max from baseline to the end of intervention period, assuming a standard deviation of 4 ml/kg/min. Analysis: All analyses will be conducted using SAS version 9.2 and R version 2.14.0, following the principle of Intention to Treat, with all randomized participants. Repeated measures mixed model will be used to investigate the intervention effect on primary and secondary outcomes, adjusting for baseline characteristics and correlation between repeated observations. Significance: This will be the first study to provide definitive evidence for the impact of a prescribed AVG intervention on physical fitness and PA levels. If effective, this research will provide much needed evidence to inform health professionals how to incorporate technological approaches to enhance health-promoting behaviors. 中文摘要: 研究背景：現在香港有22%的小學生是超重或肥胖，他們很少進行運動[1]。久坐行為，比如看電視和玩靜態電子遊戲被認為是造成這種現狀的一個源頭。資訊通信技術為兒童和電子螢幕提供了身體互動的平臺—體感遊戲。它有可能取代傳統的電子遊戲[2]。但是關於這個研究問題，目前體感遊戲的研究結果並不一致，需要更多的研究來得出結論。 研究目的：研究體感遊戲對於久坐兒童有氧運動能力的干預效果。 主要測量指標：最大攝氧量（通過20米折返跑測試估計） 其他測量指標:體力活動水平（通過動作感應器進行客觀測量），運動自我效能，靜態螢幕活動時間, 運動競爭力及享受運動水平。 研究設計：標準兩組平行隨機對照實驗研究。 研究參與者：香港小學學生 入選標準：: 1) 10-12歲; 2) 每週玩電子遊戲的時間大於2小時; 3) 無進行體力活動的身体病症 干預內容：參加者將被隨機分配到體感遊戲組和對照組。體感遊戲組將在平時的體力活動基礎上進行為期12個星期，每星期三次的體感遊戲干預，每次持續60分鐘。研究團隊將為他們提供中等強度水準的最新的體感遊戲。對照組將繼續進行他們平時的體力活動而沒有任何體感遊戲干預。 樣本量：80名參加者能夠提供90%的把握度，在5%的顯著水準上來探測3毫升/千克/分鐘的最大攝氧量的組間差，當假定標準差為4毫升/千克/分鐘時。 資料分析：所有的資料分析將通過軟體SAS（9.2版本）和R（2.14.0版本）進行。分析將遵照意向性分析原則。重複測量混合模型將用於探測主要測量指標和其他指標的干預效果，基線指標和重複測量指標間的相關強度將被控制。 研究意義：本研究將為體感遊戲干預對有氧運動能力和體力活動水平的影響提供確定的證據。如果干預研究是有效的，本研究將為健康工作者提供有用的資訊及科技来加強人們的健康行為。

244913.label: Realisation of objectives
244913.value: According to the intervention study, the results demonstrated that compared to the control group, significant increases were found in the intervention group in VO2max (mean and 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.58 (0.74, 2.42) ml/kg/min), objective moderate-to-vigorous PA (6.73 (1.70, 11.76) min/day) and total physical activity (PA) (27.19 (9.33, 45.04) min/day) but not for BMI. No significant differences in PA task efficacy, barrier efficacy, and enjoyment were observed. This 12-week school-based AVG intervention could improve Chinese children’s aerobic fitness and PA level. These findings indicated that AVG could be used as an alternative means to engage Chinese children’s PA in school setting. However, the treatment effects of AVG on PA-related psychological correlates and body composition need more investigation. To conclude, the two objectives of the research project are achieved. This interventio study is an important study to provide definitive evidence for the impact of a prescribed AVG intervention on physical fitness and PA levels. Based upon these findings, we have produced significant evidence to inform health professionals how to incorporate technological approaches to enhance health-promoting behaviors among Chinese sedentary children.

244913.label: Major findings and research outcome
244913.value: Major findings are: Intervention effects on aerobic fitness Significant increases in VO2max were observed at post-test both within two groups. Children’s VO2max within the intervention group increased from 42.93 (SD: 1.47) ml/kg/min at baseline to 45.21 (SD: 2.15) ml/kg/min after intervention, while increased from 42.62 (SD: 1.75) ml/kg/min at baseline to 43.38 (SD: 2.36) at post-test within the control group. Compared to the control group, children in the intervention group had higher VO2max at post-test (t = 3.61, p = 0.001). For the effect of the 12-weeks of PA intervention using Xbox 360, significant group difference was found for VO2max in the intervention group compared to the control group (mean (95%CI): 1.58 (0.74, 2.42), F = 13.24, p < 0.001). Intervention effects on physical activity No significant differences were detected for total PA and MVPA at baseline. The significant increases in total PA and MVPA were observed at post-test within the intervention group (total PA: t = -5.40, p < 0.001; MVPA: p < 0.001) but not within the control group (Table 2). Compared to the control group, children in the intervention group had higher total PA at post-test (t = 2.15, p = 0.035). No significant difference in MVPA was detected at post-test across groups. Significant differences were observed for PA in favor of the intervention group (mean (95%CI) for average daily total PA: 27.19 (9.33, 45.04), F = 9.19, p = 0.003; mean (95%CI) for average daily MVPA: 6.73 (1.70, 11.76), F = 7.09, p = 0.009). Intervention effects on psychological variables There were no significant differences in the tested psychological variables (i.e. task-efficacy, barrier-efficacy, enjoyment) at baseline. Compared to the change in the control group, participants in the intervention group had increased PA task-efficacy (mean (95%CI): 0.54 (-0.27, 1.34)) and enjoyment (mean (95%CI): 0.13 (-0.13, 0.39)), and decreased PA barrier-efficacy (mean (95%CI): -0.23 (-0.64, 1.12)). At post-test, all the measures showed health-beneficial trends although the differences did not achieve statistical significance (PA task-efficacy, F = 1.76, p = 0.189; PA barrier-efficacy, F = 0.30, p = 0.584; PA enjoyment, F = 0.99, p = 0.322). Regarding the research output, please refer to Part C.

244913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
244913.value: Based upon the present findings, the researcher has further developed another research proposal entitled "Intervention effect of active video game on mental health, physical activity level and psychological correlates in adolescents with depression". Since the anxiety and depression of Hong Kong children and adolescents have been increasing in recent years, the researcher would like to employ the active video games to investigate if there is significant and positive impact on the children with mental problem.

244913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
244913.value: Objective: The present research sought to determine the effect of a school-based AVG intervention on Chinese sedentary children’s aerobic fitness, physical activity (PA) level and PA-related psychological correlates including task-efficacy, barrier-efficacy, and enjoyment. Method: Eighty 8-11-year-old Chinese children (55 males) were recruited from one Hong Kong primary school and were allocated at random to either an AVG intervention or control group. Children in the intervention group played an AVG Xbox 360 twice per week during after school, each for 60 minutes over 12 weeks in duration. The control group received no intervention. Results: Compared to the control group, significant increases were found in the intervention group in aerobic fitness and total PA time but not for body mass index (BMI). No significant differences in PA task efficacy, barrier efficacy, and enjoyment were observed. Conclusion: A 12-week (60min x twice per week) school-based AVG intervention can improve Chinese sedentary children’s aerobic fitness and PA level. These findings indicated that AVG could be used as an alternative means to engage Chinese sedentary children’s PA in school setting. However, the treatment effects of AVG on PA-related psychological correlates and body composition need more investigation.

245913.label: Project Title(Chinese)
245913.value: 從中央制度到地區教化： 十五世紀至十六世紀期間朝鮮王朝禮儀政策與中國古禮傳播的關係

245913.label: Co - Investigator(s)
245913.value: Dr Fan, Wing Chung Prof Kong, Byung Suk

245913.label: Project Objectives
245913.value: 通過整理朝鮮國典中的古禮材料，包括朝鮮開國後二百年間所頒行的《朝鮮經國典》、《朝鮮大典》和《國朝五禮儀》，分析朝鮮中央政府襲用《周禮》、《儀禮》、《禮記》和《文公家禮》等古禮文獻材料，從而制定出具體的政治措施，藉此推動地方基層實行古禮制度。 根據《朝鮮王朝實錄》和朝鮮地方志研究朝鮮境內的地理特徵，分析它們在古禮傳播上帶來的影響，特別是由南北地區之間所形成的地域性差異，如何導致朝鮮中央政府改變其施政初衷，由推行禮制傳播轉變為採用地方教育宣揚儒家教化。 根據《朝鮮王朝實錄》、《韓國禮學叢書》、《韓國經學資料集成》(《禮記》部分)和朝鮮儒生的生平資料，包括《行狀》、《墓誌》和《傳奇》，分析朝鮮王室和當時士人如何整合本土風俗和古禮儀之間的差異，並按照他們的親身體驗和他人實踐的結果，評論在地方基層中推行禮制的可行性。 在《韓國歷代文集叢書》、《新增東國輿地勝覽》和《東國文獻備考》中，探討朝鮮地方基層採用朱熹《增損呂氏鄉約》宣導儒家的倫常教化，並收集朝鮮本土的宗族契約和鄉約刊本，分析鄉老宿儒如何把禮義內容納入鄉約條文和鄉校課程中，藉此探討朝鮮基層在地方教育上接受古禮的播遷。

245913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
245913.value: 朝鮮王朝(1392-1910A.D.)是在執掌朝鮮半島命脈的歷代政權當中，最能夠反映中國古代禮儀在韓國傳播的朝代，它也是最重視地方禮儀植根的朝鮮中央政權。十五世紀至十六世紀期間，朝鮮中央政府在全國各地制定和推行了一些政治措施，目的是促進中國禮儀制度在地方組織中的傳播，使社會基層從踐行禮制的過程中，接受和履行傳統儒家的倫理價值觀，貫徹執行由立國初期《朝鮮經國典》所訂下來的禮治政策。本計劃研究在朝鮮王朝立國後的二百年間，中央政府在國內推行的政治措施是否取得古禮傳播的成效，分析當時韓國境內的傳統習俗、地理環境、經濟結構、戶籍人口和自然氣候等地域差異性，如何導致朝鮮王室改變其政治策略，由最初根據中央立法規定地方組織實行禮儀制度，到後來逐步由古禮儀式改變為禮義的播遷，在地方教育中宣揚倫理教化，並頒令各地鄉老宿儒宣讀鄉約，指導社會基層遵行儒家倫常綱紀，使他們從根本上理解行禮的意義，進而根深蒂固地接受古禮的薰陶。

245913.label: Realisation of objectives
245913.value: 1.本計劃考察出朝鮮王朝通過中國古禮制定的地方禮儀政策，有以下方面： (1)朝鮮太祖3年(1394)，鄭道傳根據《周禮》寫成《朝鮮經國典》，這是第一部朝鮮王朝的國家法典，反映儒家禮治精神在朝鮮法典中的滲透。當中採用“以禮入法”和“禮主刑輔”的立法標準，建構禮、法、刑三者關係，賦予國家實行禮治的法律效力和刑罰約束力，為地方禮儀的推行提供法治基礎。 (2)朝鮮建國初年，全國郡縣設置“留鄉所”監察制度，目的是透過地方品官議論，糾正鄉土風俗，扶正倫常。其次是制定“五戶一統”戶籍制度，憑恃鄰里之間互相監察，勸戒鄉民嚴守禮儀，維護人倫綱紀。 (3)《國朝五禮儀》在朝鮮成宗6年(1475)成書，這是朝鮮王朝第一部禮典。它傳承《家禮》禮儀，並按照中國古禮分類，分為吉、凶、賓、軍、嘉五禮，除了提供朝鮮王室禮儀外，也有專門為地方大夫、庶人撰寫的禮儀篇目。例如《州縣春秋祭社稷儀》、《開城府及州縣養老宴儀》、《鄉飲酒儀》、《鄉射儀》和《大夫士庶人喪儀》等。 (4)朝鮮地方官員有在其管轄地區內舉行禮儀制度。例如朝鮮英祖2年(1726)10月22日，慶尚道清道郡舉行了鄉飲酒禮儀式，由當地郡守尹鳳九策劃和舉行，屬於朝鮮郡級地方政府主導的禮儀活動，這是朝鮮地方禮儀傳播的一個重大發現。 2. 本文分析出朝鮮八道有不同的地理特徵，導致各道儒家文化的傳播存在強弱差異。朝鮮知識份子認為“下三道”的地理環境遠勝北方諸道，所指的是南方忠清道、全羅道和慶尚道，當地儒家文化氣氛濃郁，崇尚禮讓，具有儒家文化地理版圖的特徵。從文獻記錄中已能夠揭示出各道禮儀政策成效不一，但要進一步深入研究，便須要進行田野考察。《新增東國輿地勝覽》記載慶尚道內官方設置的地方禮儀場所，包括客館、小學堂、祈雨所、社稷壇、城隍祠、厲壇、鄉校、鄉射堂和射廳等，它們發揮起地方禮儀傳播的功能，但基於田野考察沒有設定在本計劃內，故在缺乏經費支持下，無法到當地考察。 3. 本計劃揭示出朝鮮本土風俗與中國古禮有不少抵觸之處，特別是「男歸女家」的婚俗習慣，導致中國婚儀未能完整地在當地實行；其中，文廟制度是最能夠反映這種現象。朝鮮知識份子從認識到接受文廟禮儀，繼而在地方鄉校興建文廟，遵行釋奠禮，主祀孔子及中國賢儒。但他們認為，古韓國歷代王朝同樣有不少名儒，與中國諸儒地位等同，理應在文廟中置放神位，供後人祭祀。因此，朝鮮王朝按照朝鮮師承譜系，重新整理從祀人物，在地方文廟中推行具有本土特色的祭祀制度。 4.朝鮮王朝在中宗12年敕令頒行《呂氏鄉約》，成為朝鮮時代地方禮義播遷的主要途徑。本計劃查找出由於各地士人具備解讀儒家典籍能力，兼有實踐禮儀的知識，故在各地頒行《呂氏鄉約》，兼且融合朝鮮風俗和傳統契約，撰寫適合朝鮮本土社會的鄉約內容，以便鄉人廣泛施行。

245913.label: Major findings and research outcome
245913.value: 1.對於朝鮮民族而言，古禮播遷除了是對東傳儒家文化的吸收外，也是藉此機會建構自身文化傳統，證明本土禮教程度已達到華夏水平，而在“去夷”的民族意識上，不再承認東夷身分。〈高麗、朝鮮詩作中的《春秋》「華夷觀」〉、〈政治決策與禮義認同〉 2.朝鮮王朝要求一種根深柢固的文化植根，在地方古禮播遷上，朝鮮知識份子認為不可以勉強鄉民遵行古禮儀式，所以，他們採用鄉約的傳播形式，首先令鄉民明白儒家的禮義精神。〈士人流動與朝鮮鄉約頒行〉 3.朝鮮知識份子掌握了儒家知識傳播的主動權，例如清道士人通過地區性的禮儀活動，與位處周邊的士人互相接觸和交流，實踐鄉飲酒禮儀，其意義不但實現了中國古禮在朝鮮鄉土社會中的播遷，也反映地方知識份子是古禮傳播的重要媒介。〈朝鮮王朝地方性的禮儀活動〉 4.文廟制度提供朝鮮王朝建立祭祀先儒的傳統，使他們與華夏諸儒等齊，促成東國先儒學統的出現，也達致朝鮮道統的傳承。〈文化接受者的身分認同〉

245913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
245913.value: 1.慶尚道區域性研究：慶尚道具備禮儀文化傳播條件，刻劃出古禮在朝鮮鄉土社會中播遷的動態圖景，以及對周邊鄰國在儒家文化上的輸出。 2.韓國本位研究：我們可以轉換視野，觀察朝鮮民族文化內部發展的脈絡，以及在中、韓文化不同歷史背景對照下，古禮播遷的不同面貌。 3.跨學科研究：地理空間是文化傳播的元素，它擁有的物質條件愈是理想，就愈能夠建構合適的地理環境。因此，研究儒家文化的傳播，須要具備跨學科知識，作綜合性討論。

245913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
245913.value: 朝鮮王朝採用「儒教立國」的治國方針，通過制定地方禮儀政策，把中國古禮傳播至鄉土社會。可是，由於知識份子才具備閱讀漢字的能力，加上朝鮮本土風俗習慣的差異，鄉民大多沒法遵行禮儀。因此，朝鮮王朝在全國頒行鄉約，與禮儀同步而行。本計劃考察出朝鮮慶尚道是禮儀傳播中心所在。根據現存朝鮮文獻資料的記載，傳播禮儀的文化輸出者，他們的籍貫主要來自慶尚道，當地是朝鮮半島的文教發源地。可見，慶尚道有進一步研究的價值。

247313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
247313.value: This research seeks to investigate the capacity for ethics in current food practices in Hong Kong. The current system we use to produce, distribute and consume food has shown itself to be increasingly unsustainable. Broadly speaking, ethical food practices aim to combat the negative effects of industrialized food production and consumption driven by efficiency and profitability. Academic engagement in this area has tended towards policy outcomes such as classification standards (e.g. organic, fair-trade) or consumer behaviour. While this is necessary, the solutions are often reduced to a labelling practice thus limiting the capacity for ethics. This research extends the scope of understanding in a new direction by focusing on how ethical behaviour is enabled or constrained by the contacts within which food is practiced. The project will look at the way food is bought and sold; how cooking is shared and reciprocated; what are the attitudes towards eating and what networks of relationships in the community are sustained. Ethical practices bring people together and challenge the sense of alienation and individualism promoted by neo-liberalism. The social impact of these practices goes beyond the individual and contributes to creating a more cohesive society. Four sites of interest have been chosen to represent different models of production and consumption. This includes farmers’ market, wet market, supermarket and a local eatery which grows its own food. Detailed interviews will be conducted with growers and sellers, traders and shoppers, cooks and eaters. Field notes, participant observation, transcripts of interviews will contribute to the main empirical data. The theoretical analysis will draw from philosophy and cultural theory, in particular de Certeau and Lefebvre for their work on everyday life. This will be furthered by Serre’s theory of the parasite as an investigation into the ontology of material practice of food as a generative and constitutive force that exemplifies the capacity of ethics. The outcomes generated in this project will contribute to the fields of food studies and cultural studies. By extending the theoretical understanding of ethics exemplified through food practices, the results of this project will shed light on questions of sustainable development and social cohesion. This will be beneficial to policy makers and other researchers working in the area. Detailed case studies based in Hong Kong will also provide exposure to the local scene, which is currently absent in the field. This knowledge will be disseminated through conferences, journal articles and book chapters.

247313.label: Realisation of objectives
247313.value: Project Objective 1 This project has examined 4 sites of food production, distribution and consumption to assess its claim and capacity for ethical food practices. Each model offered a particular take on ethics revealing certain limitations which move the investigation forward. The first site was an organic vegetable stand at the Yata supermarket. This site offered an example of how ethical food consumption focuses on the offer of “organic” vegetables, highlighting its merit of being “good” and “clean” in its production phase. However, this model does not challenge the limitations of large scale production and distribution. Staff at point of distribution often has no knowledge of the produce and were unable to inform customers of the origin or process of production. Consumers are also unaware of what “organic” actually represents and treats it as a brand affecting a limited attitude change. The second site was Chan Fai Kee, a vegetable trader which has been running for three generations. The investigation documented the rise and fall of the vegetable trade in Hong Kong and demonstrated the demand for organic vegetables due to increasing food scares in China. This case study demonstrated the problematics of certification mentioned above. “Organic” certification often requires a lengthy and expensive process which smaller producers could not afford. The balancing act of sourcing organically produced vegetables and produce that carries the organic certification are often brought into question at the wet market stall. This demonstrates the limitation of certification methods as the call for ethics. The third site is farmers market, the project investigated Island East market and the central Star Ferry Pier market. This model demonstrates the benefit of a shorter production-distribution-consumption cycle as local farmers are able to sell direct to consumers. This model to a certain extent side-steps the issue of “organic” certification as trust is somewhat established by the direct connection. However, further investigation with a local farmer revealed that the ethical claims of supporting “local” production is marred by the heavy overhead charges which adds to the burden of both producers and consumers. The final site is a local eatery in Fotan. This dai pai dong differs from the rest in its vicinity as the production-distribution-consumption cycle is almost self-contained. The family farm in Ching Yuen provides the vegetables to its eatery in Hong Kong. The localized but cross-border model offer an alternative site to investigate the capacity of ethics outside of certification and infrastructural limitations. The micro-practices of food preparation, consumption and waste pointed to an area of investigation which goes beyond previous models. Objective 2 Based on the empirical evidence generated from case studies mentioned above, this project has critically evaluated commonly received notions of “ethics” in food practices, challenging the limitations of usual indicators of “good” “clean” and “fair”. This in turn allowed the project to reconfigure ethics as a means and not an end. Ethics in this new configuration is understood as a mode of operation which articulates a set of relationships. This extended the investigation into the micro-practices of food and opened up the everyday as a site of critical examination. The qualitative ethnographic field notes detailed actions that have been engaged in alternative models of food production, distribution and consumption which lend itself to a critical reflection through the works of Michel de Certeau, Ben Highmore, Michel Foucault and Henri Lefebvre. In addition to this, the project has also experimented a new theoretical paradigm based on Michel Serres’ work on the Parasite. This theoretical move has allowed the research to encompass a larger set of questions that takes into account the entangled relations of food practices and indicates further areas of research. Objective 3 The two years of fieldwork involved identifying and establishing contact with local stakeholders to gather data on the local community of food practitioners. The situated case study of a local organic farmer documented a wider set of political, socio-economic influences which exceeded the initial hypothesis of what market driven imperatives entail. In addition to the unsustainable methods of large scale food production, local land policy changes, contestation of land ownership and management are set against a the city’s continual urbanization. Objective 4 “Towards a Parasitic Ethics” has been successfully published with the Cultural Studies journal Theory, Culture and Society. This is a Tier 1 journal and during the process of publication, PI has been invited to speak about the project twice in Australia (see next section for details). Further publication based on continual research is still underway. Overall, this GRF funded project has been successful in allowing the PI to establish an overview of current food practices and models as well as establish contacts and informants in the field. There has been 2 major challenges in the process. First, data from private companies is almost impossible to gather. In the instance of Yata supermarket, the case study has been paired with Chan Fai Kei to offer a comparative analysis focusing on the politics of certification methods. Second, the hiring of an appropriate Research Assistant has proven challenging. The needs of the project are varied and ethnographic research requires training and experience. The PI has therefore provided intense supervision and training for the RA and oversaw much of the process.

247313.label: Major findings and research outcome
247313.value: This research has established an overview of food practices and movements in Hong Kong, an area which is under researched in the local context. This overview details 4 models of food production, distribution and consumption supplemented by qualitative case studies to demonstrate the important role of micro-practices of food. These case studies document the intersection of between lives and institutional environments which makes visible the conditions which limits and facilitates ethical practices. The theoretical reflection based on empirical data offers a grounded evidence-based model with which to think through the cultural practices of everyday life in its relation to ethical food practices. In addition to the qualitative case studies where individual tactics in dealing with food allow for positive radiating effects on the community (a definition of ethics in this project), these cases have furthered the inquiry into the acts or moments which facilitate such ethical practices. The focus on the individual’s relation to the social maps a larger network of relationships, one in which the interdependencies of actors have been foregrounded.

247313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
247313.value: The empirical research also prompted further investigation into the larger context of urban development in Hong Kong. Further areas of investigation have been identified and the research questions scaled up to the level of the city. Informed by the findings of this research, investigation into the wider Hong Kong food system has been developed into another successful GRF grant.

247313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
247313.value: It is widely understood that the current way we produce, distribute and consume food is unsustainable, and many alternative food movements that have emerged in the last decade all lay claim to be an ethical solution to our current problem. This research critically evaluates these models and asks what it is that makes food practices ethical. Through investigating a series of food production and consumption models, this project shifts our attention away from labels and certification, and focuses instead on the everyday practices that create and strengthen networks that create impacts that benefit the community. The Hong Kong case study contributes to the global discussion of our food systems and offers a unique case study for comparison. The research question undertaken in this project can be scaled up to the city level and address the wider issue of food security. The question of how food comes to our tables is not just a question of healthy living, but one that affects the city’s capacity to face shifts in our global and local food chain.

247713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
247713.value: 在全球化日益加劇的年代，很多不同觀點、創意，以及最佳實踐案例等也在全球範圍內廣泛傳播；而諸多在發達經濟地區醞釀的創意或者政策，往往不經檢驗或者考量就開始在中國被接納并實踐。文化/創意城市就是其中一個典型的流動政策。目前為止，學術界對於此類現象尚未有一個系統的批判的考察。 聯合國教科文组织做发起的“创意城市网络“或许是一个极好的案例。在中国，深圳率先于2008年正式获接纳并授予 “设计之都”的称号。 上海和北京则尾随其后，分别于2011和2012年加入网络。尽管北京无可厚非地拥有更强大的艺术家团体，而深圳和上海的领先或许暗示着其领导团体更加积极的融入世界网络。这种塑造创意城市的风潮正席卷更多的中国城市。 与北京不同的是，很多中国城市未必拥有足够的艺术家或者文化因素， 因此陷入盲目的投机的寻找另类文化的竞争中。在这个过程中，跨地区组织开始出现，组织各类论坛以供跨地区、跨国界咨询机构、城市决策者互相交流。 当外国先进经验被介绍给中国城市的同时，一些中国自己的最佳实践案例也开始被推销到国外。 在此研究中，我们的研究问题在于：文化城市这个政策是如何借助根系网络传播，以及这个全球流动的政策如何与本地环境相遇、集聚而形成本地化的文化城市模式。此项研究主张批判的看待这个现象，探讨政策流动与在地化的政治经济性质。也就是说，我们将研究文化城市这个流动的概念，是通过何种渠道流通到中国并在本地环境内物质化，以及这个本地化后的模式如何被政策化，或许，被推销到国外。 此项研究将深圳和上海置于全球化网络中进行比较研究。以德勒兹的“集聚”概念作为研究方法，我们致力于寻找一种研究方法平等地对待此过程中的语言与物质要素。

247713.label: Realisation of objectives
247713.value: Objective 1, 2 and 3: These three objectives concerns the scholarship on geography of knowledge production and its politics - the first is to accumulate empirical data, the second is to provide analyse of power relations emerged from this process, and the third is to develop a methodological framework for similar studies. All objectives have been achieved, but it is necessary to acknowledge that the power relationship is always contingent therefore my analyse has to be delimited in the cultural city discourses and practices that were territorialised in chosen Chinese cities from 2010 to 2016. In other words, mobility and territorialisation of cultural cities discourse, as illustrated by my publications, are situated in the political-economy circumstances after Deng, in particular, policy making guided by “Three Represents”, “Harmonious Society”, and “Soft Power”. That said, the more recent development under the umbrella of “China Dream” and “Silk Roads” are still at its preliminary stage (pls see my paper “Heritage Sovereignty: Authorization, Territorialization, Engaging the Making of Silk Road” on the journal “Territory, Politics, Governance”). I will then address what I have achieved regarding the three objectives. Given that the three objectives are interrelated, I will first address my framework (Objective 3) and my data collected (object 1) and my findings derived (objective 2). Objective 3: I follow the post-structuralist school and follow the procedural approach to study how different concepts, policy, practice is constructed with political, economic, cultural and social interests, through negotiations, contestations and collaborations of various actors. Assemblage is the major method I use, and I very much pay attention to the politics of assemblage. It is exactly because of my attention to politics of assemblage that my framework is to explore how new power relations, in form of scale, is constructed through negotiations of various stakeholders. The boundary of various actors is always in process of forming, stabilising and parting, therefore always porous. Objective 1: data collected include three major cultural city discourses and practises: cultural city and cultural trade, music cities, and heritage cities. Cities chosen for study include Shenzhen, Beijing, and Xi’an. Objective 2: in Authoritarian China, globally mobile cultural city policies, practices and strategies are visible in local policy, star fast-policer sellers were invited to China, however, mobility of ideas and policy-makers must be situated in the domestic re-configurations of scale (scalar and territorial). As such, keywords appear in local policy, only after they are screened and approved by cultural bureau and then mobilised to different cities by the propaganda system. Objective 4 is achieved through collaboration with local scholars and institutions in social-science, talks and reports have been delivered to relevant institutions.

247713.label: Major findings and research outcome
247713.value: In Authoritarian China, globally mobile cultural city policies, practices and strategies are visible in local policy, star fast-policer sellers were invited to China, however, mobility of ideas and policy-makers must be situated in the domestic re-configurations of scale (scalar and territorial). As such, keywords appear in local policy, only after they are screened and approved by cultural bureau and then mobilised to different cities by the propaganda system. The book (Wang, June, Tim Oakes, and Yang Yang, eds. 2016. Making Cultural Cities in Asia: Mobility, assemblage, and the politics of aspirational urbanism. London Routledge.) entails two major parts, each is a collection of policy mobility cases studied by two different approaches - one by the Political Economic Approach and the other by Post-structural approach. It is however cautioned that, there is no one homogenous Asia, and cases of mobility is to be studied with a relational manner. The chapter (Wang, June. 2016. "Assemblage Urbanism." In The Wiley Blackwell Encyclopedia of Urban and Regional Studies, edited by A. M. Orum. London: Blackwell.) and the paper (Wang, June. online first. "Relational heritage sovereignty: authorization, territorialization and the making of the Silk Roads." Territory, Politics, Governance:1-18. doi: 10.1080/21622671.2017.1323004.) illustrate the framework of politics of assemblage, knowledge and territoriality. The paper (Wang, June, and S.M. Li. 2017. "State territorialization, neoliberal governmentality: the remaking of Dafen oil painting village, Shenzhen, China." Urban Geography 38 (5):708-728. doi: 10.1080/02723638.2016.1139409.) demonstrate how is the nature of art district defined in Chinese cities and how the mobility (de-territorialisation) of varying population segments is mobilised after neoliberal value of deserving citizen is normalised. It argues that the case might shed light on the plural meaning of territory, not just as land for economic calculations, or just as terrain for political strategies, but more (Elden, 2010). Drawing on interrogations into the triangle of government–population–territory revealed by the Dafen experience, the paper argues that neoliberal rationality not only generates calculated policies to create and expand the all-encompassing domain of economy, but above all serves the political project that endeavors to produce the state space. The paper (Wang, June. online first. "Relational heritage sovereignty: authorization, territorialization and the making of the Silk Roads." Territory, Politics, Governance:1-18. doi: 10.1080/21622671.2017.1323004.) examins the heritage nomination process of ‘Silk Roads: Chang’an-Tianshan Section’, interrogates the politics of assemblage, knowledge and territory. In particular, it explores how a cultural route offers space for international and local experts as well as political and economic organizations to collect, compare, categorize and reassemble sites/places, historical episodes, and technical knowledge to legitimize an imaginary territory with new power relations in the present. The relationality of heritage sovereignty pushes for more serious attention to be paid to the politics of assemblage and the ongoing process of power–territorialization reconfiguration.

247713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
247713.value: Policy mobility itself is an always changing process, contingent and dynamic, therefore, always worth continuous attention. Out of the three strategic policies/practices, cultural trade and heritage cities are of priority, given the promotion of Silk Roads project and Belt and Road Initiatives. In particular, it is worthwhile to observe mobility of idea and policy-makers between south-south countries.

247713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
247713.value: This research explores why some urban development policies, best practices are so popular and spread to different cities in China. Behind this is power relationship when idea, knowledge and know-how, serve the search for new spatial fix by different stakeholders. This research examines how culture-related ideas are situated in city policies like five-year plans and how is it implemented, and how is the consequences.

247813.label: Project Title(Chinese)
247813.value: 中國城市汽車保有及時間運用建模：從家庭時間和資金分配的角度

247813.label: Project Objectives
247813.value: To develop a household time and money allocation-based model to examine households’ decisions on car ownership; To apply the household time and money allocation-based model to analyze the features of households’ decision on and the determinants of car ownership in urban China; To study the impacts of plate-number-based traffic rationing policies on car ownership and household time and budget allocation in urban China.

To study the impacts of plate-number-based traffic rationing policies on car ownership and household time and budget allocation in urban China.

247813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
247813.value: The economic miracles of countries such as China and Brazil have led to explosive growth of private car ownership. The rapid growth in motor vehicle fleets has resulted in serious problems like traffic congestion and air pollution. In response to these problems, the so-called plate-number-based traffic rationing policies, which restrict the usage of cars with certain plate numbers on specific days, have been implemented in Mexico City, Beijing and other cities. The existing literature on car ownership may help answer some of the problems faced by the developing countries. However, the scale of car ownership growth observed in China and other developing countries today and the types of response policies adopted deserve research efforts, which may improve our understanding about car ownership. Equally important, we think that the existing car ownership studies can be extended along a different direction. Existing studies mostly treat car ownership as questions of whether to own or how many to own; to our knowledge, hardly any study considers car ownership as a household expenditure commitment competing with other long term decisions such as employment commitments and housing choices. We believe that car ownership should be studied from the point of view of household time and money allocation. This research project is proposed to: a). Develop a household time and money allocation-based model to analyze households’ decision on car ownership. The model will incorporate households’ consideration of income earning, spending patterns and the time allocation of individual household members. Variables on government traffic rationing policies will be included in the model; b). Collect data on car ownership, car usage, time use and households’ socioeconomics to calibrate the model and study the features of households’ decision on and determinants of car ownership in urban China; and c). Study the impacts of plate-number-based traffic rationing policies on car ownership and the resulting time and budget allocation. This proposed research will contribute to the literature with a new perspective and a modeling approach that links car ownership decision with other household long run decisions. The study will also enrich the literature on determinants of car ownership with new evidences from China; a country that has recently entered the motorized era. Finally, this study will provide evidences on how the plate number–based traffic rationing policies impact on car ownership. Findings of this research will be of highly relevance for policy making. 中國和巴西兩國經歷了經濟奇蹟，導致私家車保有量爆炸性增長，然而其快速增長面臨著交通阻塞及空氣污染等嚴峻問題。針對這些問題，墨西哥城、北京等城市已實施限制某些車牌在特定日子通行的政策。關於車輛保有量問題，現有的文獻可能有助於回答發展中國家所面臨的一些困境，但現今我們觀察到在中國和其他發展中國家的汽車保有量在大規模增長，各地採取相應措施各出其謀，這些現象仍然很值得我們付出研究的努力以提高對汽車保有的理解。同樣重要地，我們認為現有的關於汽車保有的研究可以沿著不同的方向延伸。現有的研究大多把重點放在是否擁有、擁有多少這兩個方面；據我們所知，幾乎沒有研究把汽車保有問題看作是家庭開銷的決策如就業和住房抉擇等這些家庭長遠決策一般。我們相信研究汽車保有問題應從研究家庭時間和資金分配的角度出發。 這個研究項目建議：1）建立一個基於家庭時間和資金分配的模型來分析家庭保有汽車問題。這個模型將納入家庭對收入的考量、消費模式和各家庭成員時間分配這些資料；同時，政府交通配給政策將作為變量包含其中。2）收集汽車保有量、汽車使用率、時間支配和家庭社會經濟這些資料來校準模型並研究中國城市中家庭保有汽車的決定因素。 3）研究基于車牌的交通限行政策對汽車保有量和由此產生的時間和預算分配的影響。 此研究方案將為文獻提供新的視角和建模方法，把保有汽車與家庭其他長遠的支出計劃連繫；同時為文獻提供更多來自中國這個剛進入機動時代的關於汽車保有決定因素的新的證據。最後，該研究將為基于車牌的交通限行政對汽車保有的影響提供證據，其研究結果將與政策的制定高度相關。

247813.label: Realisation of objectives
247813.value: The objectives of this research project have been fully realized: We have developed a theoretical model to analyze households' decisions concerning car ownership. The model applies the game-theoretic approach to capturing household members’ interactive decision-making mechanism and links household members’ short-term time allocation decisions to long-term car ownership decisions. It theoretically and methodologically advances the studies on car ownership and extends the application of houdehold time allocation models. We have also collected data on car ownership and car usage as well as two-day activity-travel diaries from about 800 households involving more than 1800 individuals in Beijing. This database not only supports the emprical investigation of this research project, but also offers plenty of opportunities for further empirical studies on car ownership and car usgae as well as activity-travel research in general. The theoretical model has been empirically applied to predict car ownership and examine interactions between car ownership and household time allocation. It has also been used to assess the impacts of plate-number-based vehicle usage rationing policies on car ownership and time allocation to travel and daily activities. Results show that the model can be applied to evaluate the car ownership impacts of car usage rationing policies. In addition, we have also conducted some empirical studies concerning the determinants of car ownership and car usage as well as travel behavior in Beijing Further, we have extended the car ownership model to include other long-term household decisions such as residence and employment, so that interactions between car ownership and other household long-term decisions as well as between long-term and short-term choices are fully accounted for.

247813.label: Major findings and research outcome
247813.value: This research project has generated a number of important research outcomes and findings. We have developed a game-theoretic model to study auto ownership decisions from the point of view of household time allocation. The model explicitly considered interactions between spouses in long-term household car ownership decisions and short-term time allocation to daily activities. Car ownership decision was formulated as a Nash bargaining problem in the upper level with husband and wife involved in decision-making, while time allocation decision was considered as a generalized Nash equilibrium problem in the lower level incorporating spouses’ interactions concerning activity participation. The model theoretically and methodologically advances the studies on car ownership and extends the application of houdehold time allocation models. The theoretical model has been empirically applied to assess the impacts of plate-number-based vehicle usage rationing policies on car ownership and time allocation to travel and daily activities. We found that when car rationing intensified from free to full restriction, the total car ownership within the sampled area increased slightly at first and then decreased continuously after reaching a peak point. Another finding was that the changing rationing degree had a significant impact on household members’ travel time, minor impact on time allocated to subsistence and recreation activities, and almost no impact on maintenance activity participation. We have also investigated the mediating effects of car ownership in the connection between the built environment and travel behavior using a framework of integrated structural equation model and discrete choice model. We found out that car ownership may mediate the impacts of the built environment on travel behavior and higher population density and employment density may reduce the likelihood of choosing car for trip making. These research findings have been and will be reported in academic papers. The research project has so far led to 7 academic papers mostly published in top international journals including Transportation (impact factor: 2.633), Transportation Research Part A (impact factor: 2.609), Transportation Research Part B (impact factor: 3.769), and Transportation Research Part D (impact factor: 2.341) (please refer to Part C of this report). We are expecting more publications from this research project in the coming few years. Research findings of this project have been reported and publicized in a number of important international conferences including the 14th International Conference on Travel Behaviour Research held in London and the 3rd Symposium of the European Association for Research in Transportation held in Leeds, U.K.

247813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
247813.value: The game-theoretic modeling approach developed by this research project can be applied to other households' decisions involving interactions between household members and between short- and long-term decisions. We have extended the model to include other household long-term decisions such as residential location choice and employment decisions and developed a model to analyze household housing and car ownership decisions. We will also further extend the research to investigate the interactions between household long-term decisions such as housing choice and car ownership decisions and examine the implications on daily travel. Another direction of extension of the current research project is to investigate the inter-generational trends in car ownership and travel behavior. This has resulted in a new GRF research project funded in 2016.

247813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
247813.value: This research project was proposed to address some of the questions related to the explosive growth of car ownership observed in some countries today and the types of response policies adopted, which cannot be answered by the existing knowledge. We applied the game theory approach and developed a car ownership model, which considers car ownership as a household expenditure commitment competing with other household expenditure choices. The model incorporates households’ income earning, spending patterns and daily time allocation of individual household members. Variables on government traffic rationing policies are included in the model. The model has been empirically calibrated by data collected in Beijing applied to analyze the impacts of plate-number-based traffic rationing policies on car ownership. This research project contributes to the literature with a new perspective and a modeling approach that links car ownership decision with daily time allocation and trip making behavior of household members. The modeling approach developed by this project can be applied to examine the impacts of government policies on car ownership, for example, how the plate-number-based vehicle usage rationing policies implemented in a number of cities will influence car usage and car ownership if relevant data will be available.

248013.label: Project Title(Chinese)
248013.value: 中西交融協奏曲: 音樂曲種，文化融和與民族標記的探討

248013.label: Project Objectives
248013.value: I will explore the notion of hybridization as a national signifier in 30 fusion concertos and works from related genres, as well as audience reception based on discourse and ethnography. I will formulate an aesthetic of musical hybridization drawing on Bakhtin in order to demonstrate how cultural dialogue shapes the new genre. I will describe the important distinction between hybridization and hybridity in the larger hybrid discourse, casting fusion concertos at the intersection of new crossover musical genres and postcolonial politics. I will compare the composition, reception, and cultural/aesthetic justifications of the earliest Chinese-Western fusion instrumental or vocal works before 1949 to those written in the later twentieth or early twenty-first centuries. I will seek publication of my research findings in three to four journal articles.

248013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
248013.value: This project analyzes the emergence of a new international orchestral genre shaped by Chinese culture, called the “fusion concerto,” for Western orchestra and Chinese solo instrument. The research will be focused on the nature of the genre in terms of Chinese-Western hybridization and signifiers of national traditions. These concertos reflect important cultural-historical trends in modern Chinese society now having an impact outside of China, and they present striking new developments to the scholar of musical genres by combining symbolic aural and visual images of the “traditional” Chinese solo instrument alongside the Western orchestra. The study of musical hybridity that results must focus not only on East-West/colonial-postcolonial power relations and the discourse of cultural identity, but also on individual artistic creative processes. The body of over 400 concertos dates back to the 1930s. I will consider approximately forty of these works as I address four main issues: 1) how and why composers create hybrid genres, how audiences receive fusion concertos, and how we interpret the works as national signifiers; 2) how specific aesthetics of musical hybridization apply to generic expectations and how cultural dialogue shapes the new genre; 3) how important distinctions between aesthetic and ideological approaches in the hybrid discourse cast fusion concertos at the intersection of new crossover musical genres and postcolonial politics; 4) how the composition, reception, and cultural/aesthetic justifications of fusion concertos before 1949 compare musically, politically, and culturally to works written since 1980. This is the first study to analyze the fusion concerto repertoire as an embodiment of hybridization in China’s new national music. It explores theoretical, aesthetic, and ethnographic concepts of hybrid forms, cultural identity, and global consumption that dominate contemporary cultural discourse in areas experiencing East-West crossover. The methodology includes musical score-recording collection and comprehensive database compilation that will index by category these key contexts. I then analyze smaller groups of works in writing individual journal articles, assessing a deeper level of interaction between genres, hybridization, audience reception, and national signification in contemporary Chinese composition. In view of the presence of musical and national symbols, the new genre represents a tangible marker of Chinese-global cultural patterns. Most importantly, this study will have value for understanding the rapidly changing cultural profile of Hong Kong, which has been a center for fusion concerto composition and performance. It, therefore, makes a significant contribution to the areas of cultural hybridity, ethnomusicology, and contemporary Hong Kong-China studies. 這份報告分析了一種受中國文化影響的新國際管弦樂曲風，稱為“交融協奏曲”，由中國傳統樂器獨奏配以大型西方交響樂團演奏。這項研究主要就中西文化融和的影響及民族傳統的表現兩方面探討此曲種的性質。這些協奏曲反映著重要的歷史文化趨勢: 近代中國社會的影響及至海外， 它們結合“傳統”中國獨奏樂器配以西方交響樂團所象徵的聽覺和視覺形像，為音樂曲種學界帶來了觸目的新發展。音樂雜糅的研究不應只集中於中西/殖民前後的權力轉移和文化認同的論述，更應注意個人的藝術創作過程。 超過400首這樣的協奏曲可以追溯到20世紀30年代；我會就大約四十首作品帶出四個主要問題：1）作曲家是如何和為何創建混合曲式、觀眾如何接受交融協奏曲以及我們如何把這些作品傳釋為國家的標記; 2）音樂風格交融之美學如何達致觀眾對 "協奏曲" 的期望，與及在文化交流上如何塑造這種新曲式; 3）交融協奏曲深受交叉文化和後殖民政治的影響，美學和意識形態上的重要區別如何在新曲式反映; 4）在1949年以前的交融協奏曲是如何作成，接收和文化/審美的理由，將會與1980年後的作品從音樂，政治，文化方面作出比較。 今次是第一次研究分析交融協奏曲劇目是中國的新民族音樂文化融合的化身。本研究探討了理論，審美，人種學的概念，在東西文化的融合是體驗了在融合形式，文化認同以及全球消費量上是主宰著當代文化。方法包括樂譜和錄音記錄的收集和全面的數據庫編譯，從關鍵的索引類別上下文。然後我會在期刊文章分析小部份音樂作品，在中國現代作品上更深層次上評估音樂曲種，文化交融，觀眾的認受性和民族意義。 在音樂和民族象徵上，這種新的曲種代表了中國和全球化的標記。更重要的是，這項研究將會更深入了解香港在文化上急劇的轉變，成為創作和演奏交融協奏曲的中心地帶。因此，在文化糅合，民族音樂學和香港當代中國研究領域的提供了一個重大貢獻。

248013.label: Realisation of objectives
248013.value: This project has been particularly successful in achieving its objectives over the course of the research. From its solidified theoretical base coupled with ongoing archival research and extensive score analysis, this study has informed the genre and cultural studies discourses. It has analyzed a tangible subgenre that has rapidly emerged from the postcolonial context in recent decades, demonstrating one way in which China has adopted a Western concerto genre to serve its own pursuit of a new national music. This experimental pursuit has, in turn, contributed to the formation of a new international subgenre. With a refined analysis of how language, culture, and history mix from the standpoint of literary genres, I have been applying it to new Chinese genres in a variety of instrumental and vocal media. I have achieved all of the five project Objectives nearly to 100%, with only Objective 5 still nearing completion. I have published two book chapters and submitted one journal article for peer review (recommended by reviewers for publication with revisions). I have also presented related conference papers and made invited presentations, as well as performing experimental works that have been viewed or heard by Hong Kong and international audiences. Objective 1 100% achieved - I have exceeded original expectations in my overall collection, listing, and assessment of fusion concertos from the past century. I have expanded my fusion concerto database with numerous categorical descriptions for over 30 works. I have broken these works down according to historical background, performance and score features, programme notes, performers, and critical reception. From this database, I have further analyzed smaller groups of works for the published chapters and submitted journal article, as well as for presentations and performances. My analysis focused on the eight main yangbanxi “model dramas,” as well as works by Aaron Avshalomov, Chan Hing-Yan, Gao Weijie, Xian Xinghai, He Luting, Alexandre Tcherepnin, Tan Dun, Chen Yi, Ma Shuilong, Wang Jianmin, and others. In these works, I assessed the many ways in which hybridization acts as a national signifier in the fusion concerto repertoire, focusing on 1) the incorporation of concerto and non-concerto generic features (using different structures, dramatic forms, and media), 2) the classification of solo and orchestral instruments, and 3) the use of texts and non-musical, cultural attributes as a reflection of historical forces driving their composition. I also described audience reception to works in Shanghai from before 1949 and during the Cultural Revolution, as well as in newer works of recent decades. Objective 2 100% achieved - Applying Mikhail Bakhtin’s writings, on literary genres, I have formulated an aesthetic of musical hybridization and applied it to the understanding of generic expectations as new Western forms were mixed with Chinese theatrical, instrumental, and folk forms. I have adopted Bakhtin’s notions of heteroglossia, polyphony, and hybridized genres to demonstrate how musical-cultural blending reflects changing historical backdrops in China from the early twentieth century to the early twenty-first century. In one book chapter, I applied Bakhtin in demonstrating how cultural dialogue shaped new musical-dramatic genres – in the case of The Great Wall and various versions of Bai Mao Nü and Shajiabang, which mixed Western and Chinese instruments. I have also shown how the intersection of politics, genre, and national culture across textual boundaries has resulted in the fusion concerto as a “politicized hybrid genre” marked by an era of national crisis. In another submitted article, I have shown how the concept of polyphony describes musical, literary, and cross-cultural overlap as manifest in the earliest fusion concerto experiments by Bakhtin’s Russian contemporary Aaron Avshalomov, who was active in Shanghai before 1949. Avshalomov’s concerto was the first major step in shaping the fusion concerto genre. Objective 3 100% achieved - I highlighted the distinction between the aesthetic notion of hybridization, as promoted by Bakhtin, and the concept of postcolonial hybridity as advocated by cultural theorists, such as Homi Bhabha, with the idea of “politicized hybrid genres” that I introduced in my chapter on The Great Wall and the yangbanxi “model dramas.” In this chapter, I demonstrated how the phenomenon of Chinese and Western musical elements (hybridization) being scored together in compositions with concerto features, but being carried out for political purposes (hybridity) has re-occurred at different times over the past century. In a separate article and presentations, I further described its occurrence in fusion concertos, dramatic works, and choral repertoire in the decades preceding and following the Cultural Revolution, where artistic hybridization is set against the historical backdrop of postcolonial hybridity. Objective 4 100% achieved - I have completed this objective, which has resulted in the publication of two book chapters, one journal article, multiple presentations, and multiple performances. I have compared the composition, reception, and cultural/aesthetic justifications of the earliest Chinese-Western fusion instrumental and vocal works before 1949 to those written in the later twentieth or early twenty-first centuries. One chapter considered dramatic works in pre-1949 Shanghai as a precedent to works of the Cultural Revolution. Another framed the overall repertoire of the past century in terms of timbral experimentation resulting from historical forces that brought different cultures into contact. Further archival research from pre-1949 Shanghai resulted in the journal article submission relating to piano works and vocal works composed by Russian and Chinese composers that have had a continuing impact on hybrid musical development in the PRC to today. My own participation in an important Hong Kong premiere of a Chinese-Western experimental work in 2016-2017 has effectively tied all of these elements together in practice-led research as a reflection of ongoing historical change in China. Objective 5 95% achieved – I have published two book chapters in volumes by prestigious publishers (University of Michigan and Palgrave MacMillan) that 1) analyze national signifiers and audience reception of fusion concertos according to instrumental classification, and 2) cast the fusion concerto genre formation as a direct result of interactive hybridization (as described by Bakhtin) and postcolonial hybridity processes, encapsulating historical movement as artistically designed, “politicizd hybrid genres.” I also submitted an article “A New Multivoiced World: Bakhtinian Polyphony and the First Chinese-Western Fusion Concerto,” which has been reviewed and recommended for publication (pending revisions) in a first-tier musicology journal. Revisions and review are scheduled for late 2017 and early 2018.

248013.label: Major findings and research outcome
248013.value: The major research findings involve five areas relating to genre, hybridity, and fusion concertos: 1) compositional features - having indexed the earliest fusion concertos and categorized their novel approaches; 2) political-aesthetic discourse and experimental compositions - having contextualized the compositions within the historical backdrop of twentieth-century China, especially 1930s Shanghai, and the pursuit of musical modernization; 3) vocal-instrumental interaction – having discovered and analyzed Chinese vocal styles used as source materials for early fusion concerto experimentation; 4) trends in new Chinese national music and new global concert music - having described how contemporary trends in national identity relate back to early twentieth-century movements and outward toward current global interaction; 5) concepts of genre and hybridization - having closely analyzed and described theories originally applied to literary genres and adapting them interactive musical languages. I have applied my findings from the current research project in the publication of two book chapters: “Musical-Dramatic Experimentation in the Yangbanxi: A Case for Precedence in The Great Wall,” in Listening to China’s Cultural Revolution: Music, Politics, and Cultural Communities, edited by Paul Clark, Pang Laikwan, and Tsai Tsan-Huang. London: Palgrave MacMillan (November 2015), pp. 189-212; and “Spanning the Timbral Divide: Tradition, Multiplicity, and Novelty in Chinese-Western Fusion Concerto Instrumentation,” in China and the West: Representation, Reception, and Reception, edited by Hon-Lun Yang and Michael Saffle, University of Michigan Press. (March 2017), pp. 186-204. I have also applied them in submission and provisional acceptance of an article “A New Multivoiced World: Bakhtinian Polyphony and the First Chinese-Western Fusion Concerto,” in the Journal of Musicological Research (in review). Further application of findings has been made in “Stylistic Development and Hybrid Genres in Chinese Choral Music” presented at the American Choral Directors Association National Conference (2015) and in “Fu Lei and the ‘Grand Chinese Evening’: Intransigence and Boundless Hope for China’s Musical Future” presented at the CHIME international conference in Geneva (2015), as well as at invited presentations at the Graduate Institute of Musicology at National Taiwan University (2014), the international symposium “Fu Lei and His World” at theFu Lei Research Center in Shanghai (2016), and at the 10th World Symposium on Choral Music in Seoul (2014). The research has informed my own performance of new Chinese-Western works, such as the newly commissioned, semi-staged cantata “Hong Kong Odyssey” at the 2017 Hong Kong Arts Festival, on RTHK Radio 4 (2016), and BBC Radio 3 "In Tune" (2016).

248013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
248013.value: The study of fusion concertos in relation to modern Chinese history and musical development has naturally branched out into related vocal, instrumental, and dramatic genres, all of which came into being via experiments in mixing Chinese and Western forms during the revolutionary period before 1949. I have just submitted a new GRF proposal on the topic of “Chinese Music in Revolution: Ideology, Factionalism, and Nationalism as Cross-Cultural Modernity.” The research will focus on ideology, political factionalism, and nationalism relating to Chinese-Western symphonic, choral, and dramatic works by Chinese and foreign artists in Shanghai, Yan’an, and other war-torn areas. These issues illuminate a critical intersection of politics and performance amidst national crisis that has transformed the artistic landscape. The emergence of Chinese-Western forms demonstrates how cross-cultural contact affected debates on modernity among key players in China’s artistic-political arena before and after establishment of the People’s Republic. This study is the first to examine, from a cross-cultural perspective, the performers, writers, and political factions that created China’s new national musical and drama while being engaged in revolutionary struggle.

248013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
248013.value: The research project describes one of the new musical forms that developed in China over the past century. Modern Chinese music is built on combining traditional styles with Western models that were imported in the early twentieth century. My project looks at a special set of works that combine Chinese and Western instruments on the concert stage. These works can be seen and heard all over China today, and they are an important symbol of the new Chinese identity. I have researched the history that led to these kinds of works and I have analyzed them in musical and cultural terms. Since much of modern China was born out of internal conflict and war with outside powers, these works, numbering in the hundreds, are a valuable tool for seeing how new culture is created from distant traditions. If we think about China’s growing stature in the world today, we need to know how and why it developed beyond just political and economic terms. The ways it mixed foreign and Chinese cultures into new modes of performance helps us better understand the nature of China’s relationship to the rest of the world in the twenty-first century.

248613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
248613.value: Albeit the global trend of corporate social responsibility, most Hong Kong corporations continue to do business as usual, not making substantive efforts to explore whether and how they might enhance social well-being and win the trust of the average citizen. A case in point is the 08 May 2012 announcement by China Light and Power that its rates will rise 40% by the end of 2015 due to an estimated 250% hike in fuel costs. In response, several Legislative Council (Legco) members have recommended restructuring Hong Kong’s electricity sector. Adopting this recommendation is risky, chiefly because of the lack of evidence that electricity market competition would result in reliable service at just and reasonable rates. Moreover, restructuring is costly, time-consuming, and irreversible, as evidenced by experience worldwide. A reversible, low-risk, low-cost alternative is regulatory reform to establish a public service commission (PSC) that would hold public hearings to allow various stakeholders (e.g. ratepayers and environmentalists) to examine the evidence presented by utilities in their rate increase applications. Commonly used in North America, public hearings would generate the information that would enable the PSC to make its decisions based on findings of fact and conclusions of law. Furthermore, the PSC can investigate policy proposals that would greatly affect consumers (e.g., renewable-energy procurement, vehicular electrification, large-scale energy efficiency improvement, a smart grid to improve asset utilisation and system operations, and alternative ratemaking mechanisms). Our proposed research focuses on estimating the demand by residential users for a PSC in Hong Kong for the following reasons. First, low-income families are most affected by electricity rate increases. Second, residential users are relatively homogenous, thus simplifying our survey development and data collection. Finally, absent residential support for a PSC, the idea is dead on arrival at the Legco. The proposed research enriches the research in public administration and law by determining if there is a strong demand for regulation based on electricity users’ willingness-to-pay (WTP) for a PSC’s service. It innovatively uses the contingent valuation survey method to elicit WTP for the unpriced service of an independent regulator. It determines how the support for the PSC may vary by its funding source (private vs. public funding). If a low support for the PSC is largely due to the poor residents’ inability to pay, it should be publicly funded to reflect that its service would benefit all Hong Kong residents. 儘管履行企業社會責任已成為全球趨勢，大多數香港公司繼續以往常方式經營業務，沒有作出實質性的努力，探索應否和如何能增進社會福祉和贏得公民的信任。一個典型的例子是中華電力有限公司2012年5月8日宣佈，2015年底電價將上調40%，原因是燃料成本估計上升250%。幾個立法會議員作出回應，建議重組香港的電力部門。採納這項建議是有風險的，因為沒有證據證明電力市場競爭會帶來可靠的服務，以及公正和合理的價格。此外，世界各地的經驗表明，重組電力部門是昂貴、耗時和不可逆的。 一個可逆、低風險、低成本的替代方案是進行監管改革，建立一個「公共服務委員會」(public service commission)，舉行公聽會，讓各種利益相關者 （例如繳納電費者代表和環保主義者），審視申請提高電費的理據。公聽會是北美國家常用的方法，讓委員會獲取資訊，以建基於事實的證據和法律來作決定。此外，「公共服務委員會」可以審議對消費者產生重大影響的各種政策建議(例如可再生能源採購、車輛電氣化、大型能源效益改進項目、改善資產利用率和系統操作的智慧電網，以及收取電費的各種機制)。 我們的研究重點，是估算電力的住宅使用者對香港設立「公共服務委員會」的需求。主要考慮如下：第一，低收入家庭最受電費增加影響。第二，住宅使用者是相對單一的，可簡化我們調查和資料收集的設計。最後，倘若缺乏住宅使用者的支持，設立「公共服務委員會」的建議是不可能獲得立法會考慮的。 此研究項目測算電力使用者對設立「公共服務委員會」的支付意願 (willingness-to-pay)，以確定公眾是否強力支持其成立，這將增進公共行政和法律領域的研究成果。「獨立監管者」是一種沒有價格的服務，此項目創新地應用「意願調查方法」，找出公眾的支付願意。此研究還會確定公眾對「公共服務委員會」的支持，是否因其資金來源 (私人與公共資金) 而出現差異。如果公眾對「公共服務委員會」支持不足的主因是貧困居民無力支付，那就應該以公帑資助，以彰顯其服務能讓所有香港居民受益的性質。

248613.label: Major findings and research outcome
248613.value: The project's major findings appear in: Woo, C.K., Y.S. Cheng, A. Law, J. Zarnikau, S.T. Ho, H.Y. Leung (2015) " Consumer Support for a Public Utilities Commission in Hong Kong," Energy Policy, 76, 87-97. The paper's abstract contains the following findings. Hong Kong’s electricity service is superbly reliable and price-reasonable when compared to those of the major cities in the OECD countries. Based on the rate of return regulation in the U.S., the current scheme of control agreement (SCA) regulating the two local integrated investor-owned utilities (IOUs) will expire in 2018, thus offering an opportune time to consider proposals to modify or replace the SCA. The proposals made to date range from minor modifications of the SCA to electricity market restructure. These proposals, however, overlook two important aspects of regulatory governance: transparency and public involvement. This paper estimates consumer support for the proposal to establish a Hong Kong public utilities commission (HKPUC) to improve the current regulatory process. Based on the responses collected in mid-2014 via a face-to-face survey of 1,100 Hong Kong residents, we find that at the 1.5% bill surcharge, about 70% the respondents are estimated to support an HKPUC. Thus, there is sufficient consumer support for a financially viable HKPUC. The policy implication is that Hong Kong should consider the possibility of establishing an HKPUC prior to the 2018 expiration of the current SCA. The paper makes the following contributions. First, to the best of our knowledge, this is the first documented evidence of consumer support for a proposed PUC, thus enriching the literature on public utility regulation. Despite the analysis of the election of PUC commissioners and the creation of consumer advocates, there is little empirical evidence that directly points to consumer support for a PUC. Second, it is shown that an estimated 70% of consumers would be willing to incur a 1.5% surcharge on their electricity bills to pay for a PUC, thus indicating a proposed HKPUC’s public acceptance and financial viability. Finally, the paper informs the possible development of provincial PUCs in China, the world’s second-largest economy, where regulatory governance remains weak for its electricity industry.

248613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
248613.value: The next major step is to convince the stakeholders that a HKPUC is necessary to improve the regulatory transparency and fairness for the electricity industry's shareholders and consumers. This echoes the recommendation of the Consumer Council’s 2014 report on Hong Kong's electricity future (http://www.consumer.org.hk/website/ws_en/news/press_releases/2014120401.html)

248613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
248613.value: Hong Kong’s average electricity rate in 2012 was HK$1.025/kWh, which is relatively low when compared to the rates of the major cities of the OECD countries. Hong Kong’s electricity service is superbly reliable, thanks to the vast capital expenditures made under the Scheme of Control Agreement (SCA), which will expire in 2018. A series of proposals made before the 2008 signing of the current SCA suggest restructuring the electricity industry, instituting periodic reviews of the SCA’s permitted return on assets, and implementing performance-based regulation. However, these proposal overlook the possibility of establishing a Hong Kong Public Utilities Commission (HKPUC) to remedy the lack of transparency and public involvement in Hong Kong’s regulatory process. This project estimates consumers' support for a proposal to establish an HKPUC. As the proposed HKPUC has yet to occur, we adopt the contingent valuation method (CVM) to design and implement a face-to-face survey of 1100 Hong Kong residents to gauge the HKPUC's public support and acceptance. Based on the responses of 1,100 respondents collected in mid-2014, our key finding is that public support for an HKPUC is about 70% of the respondents when the surcharge is equal to 1.5% of their electricity bills.
