248813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
248813.value: This multifaceted and interdisciplinary project brings together three researchers of very different backgrounds to address issues pertinent to the role of music in migration, cross-cultural contacts, and transculturation, anticipating many of the features of globalization. The ‘port of last resort’ - Shanghai - became a Russian diaspora in the East, home of hundreds and thousands of Russian refugees in the 1930s, among them were many musicians who used music for various purposes – from community building to making ends meet. The main objective of this project is to formulate a theoretical framework to unravel how the émigré Russian musicians interacted with the larger Shanghai community during the interwar period through their musical activities. Drawing on the construct of actor-network, the project hopes to reveal how music is used by different actors/actants in their negotiation for space, identity, nationhood, and livelihood, which contributed to Shanghai’s metropolitanism on the one hand and Chinese modernity on the other. Treating Shanghai’s musical scene as a big network with many smaller networks, the project will examine three communities, the Russian community with a focus on social clubs, the international community represented by the Shanghai Municipal Orchestra, and the Chinese community, focusing on Chinese students of Russian pedagogues, each forming a network of its own, but all linked by Russian musicians who were the key actors and through whom connections were made to other actors/actants. Two case studies of Russian composers who had close connections with the Chinese community and whose works showed Chinese influences are included to illustrate the reciprocal nature of links in a network. Though findings of this project are likely to corroborate the notion that music has the power to unify people and breaking down boundaries, they will challenge the generally accepted view that the émigré communities in Shanghai lived in self-contained enclaves that had little connection to the local Chinese population. Moreover, they will introduce Russian musicians who in most cases are completely forgotten due to their émigré status. Furthermore, the theoretical framework formulated will open up new grounds in the study of music and diaspora, particularly regarding music’s role in cultural contacts and transculturation. The resulting publications will be pioneer studies to address such a topic and affiliated concerns. Last but not least, such a study provides a historical perspective for a deeper understanding of the impact of immigration and multi-culturalism on a society’s socio-cultural texture. 在二次世界大戰期間，上海成為成千上萬俄僑的東方居所，這些俄羅斯難民有為數不少的音樂家，他們不單以音樂謀生，更以此作社區建設。這多元和跨學科的研究項目匯集了三位背景各異的研究人員，從而探討俄羅斯音樂家的音樂活動和上海各國社區的關係，以行动者网络理论 (actor network theory) 去解構音樂對遷移、文化交流、文化互化、及全球化進程所作出的貢獻，亦揭示音樂在民族及身份認同及上海大都會化所扮演的角色。該研究項目把上海音樂圈視為一個大的網絡，其中包括了許多較小的網絡。研究重點放在三個社區網絡，一為俄羅斯社區及其俱樂部的音樂活動，二為上海公共租界工部局樂隊所代表的國際社區及其中的俄羅斯樂手，三為中國社區，針對俄羅斯教育家在培訓中國學生的關鍵角色。此外，研究還包括兩個曾在上海生活、其作品受中國元素影響的俄羅斯作曲家的實例，以此說明網絡的互惠性質及密切關繫。這個項目的研究結果能引證音樂的力量，其統合性能打破民族界限；亦挑戰上海難民自成一角、對當地社會少有貢獻的固有觀點。此外，研究所帶出的理論框架，有助音樂和散居、音樂文化交往和文化互化的研究，研究的結果亦提供了一個歷史角度去反思文化多元對中國音樂文化現代化的影響。

248813.label: Realisation of objectives
248813.value: The objectives proposed have been realized. The project results in a tri-author volume by the three investigators submitted to the University of Hawaii Press. The volume consists of seven chapters, a preface and an epilogue. Objective 1 is realized in the introduction of the volume. It presents the theoretical framework of the ‘network’ from various perspectives, including Actor Network Theory, diaspora, and migration study to examine the subject of this research, the impact of Russian musicians and musical activities in Shanghai. Objective 2 is realized in the first part of the volume. Chapters 1 and 2 focus on the Russian community and its inner workings. Chapter 1 opens up with an advertisement of musical activities at a Russian restaurant, signalling the complexity of Russian identity. The chapter discusses the social-cultural nature of Shanghai’s Russian emigration. It explicates who the Russian émigrés were, where they came from, what views they held regarding their motherland and their cultural heritage, what challenges they confronted in the process of displacement, how they met with the difficulties arising from emigration, and finally, what happened to them with the founding of the PRC in 1949. The next chapter opens with a newspaper report of a Russian New Year ball beginning the discussion about different forms of Russian musical activities. First, it traces the activities of various Russian organizations that often seem to be related to the diaspora, but were typically more than that. It shows that: 1) these music organizations were quite diverse, and many of them were fairly short-lived; 2) musicians’ attitudes fluctuated and whether one was cosmopolitan or diasporic is often difficult to define; and 3) even if these émigré music societies were meant to be diasporic, serving émigrés’ needs, they were often of interest to non-Russians of Shanghai, their musical activities becoming cosmopolitan in nature. Finally, the chapter argues that many of the musical activities of the Russian community served to reach out to other communities, accounting for Shanghai’s prosperous musical scene and cosmopolitan soundscape in the interwar period, introducing Shanghai to western musical idioms, sometimes never before seen. Objective 3 is realized in the second part of the volume. Chapters 3 to 5 discuss Russian musical activities from the perspective of Shanghai’s international community and Chinese community by focusing on two cultural pillars: the Shanghai Municipal Orchestra and the National Conservatory of Music. Chapter 3 opens with Tcherepnin’s commendation of the SMO (hereafter the SMO), which employed many Russian musicians as players and soloists. While detailing how many Russian musicians actually served in SMO, the chapter also reveals how unfairly they were often treated. Despite the occasional tension between the SMO conductor Mario Paci and some of the Russian musicians, it argues that the availability of the Russian musicians and the music-loving Russian community were crucial for the success of the SMO, which in turn, became a tool of power negotiation for the Russian community. Chapter 4 begins with a newspaper report of a special Russian concert of the SMO, through which the chapter looks into SMO’s concert programs, unraveling the contributions made by the Russian musicians as well as the economic motivation behind the Russian-inclined programming of the SMO. Chapter 5 opens with a photo of the Russian pedagogue Boris Zakharov and his two Chinese students, through which to explore Russian musicians’ activities at the National Conservatory of Music. In addition to identifying Russian educators and their respective students, the chapter analyzes their relationships as reconstructed from Chinese musicians’ memoirs and writings. Finally, it demonstrates the Russian musicians’ profound impact on the development of Chinese musical performance through tracing the accomplishments of Russian pedagogues’ Chinese students. Special attention is given to the performances of these students with the SMO, which were often viewed by Chinese with a nationalistic sentiment, a sense of triumph, as the institution was once a colonial icon, inaccessible to Chinese. Objective 4 is realized in the third part of the volume. Chapters 6 and 7 consist of two case studies of Russian émigré composers, moving the focus from the émigré community and social constructions to individuals. This part reflects on the cultural and human contacts encountered in the process of migration, and the ways in which individuals moved between different cultures in their creative work. Chapter 6 opens with a Chinese student’s impression of Tcherepnin playing his Chinese-flavored compositions, treating Tcherepnin as an actor moving between different networks. While the four sets of his piano compositions from 1934 to 1937, namely the Piano Study on the Pentatonic Scale (without opus), and then Op. 51, Op. 52, and Op. 53 are products of “translation,” a result of Tcherepnin’s treading outside the Russian network and forming connections with intelligentsia of the Chinese community. His Chinese connections in turn had consequential impacts on the future networks he was going to partake. He left his first wife and patron to be together with the Chinese pianist Lee Hsien-Ming he met at the National Conservatory. This forced him into a new path in which his migratory Russian émigré identity faced new kind of influences. Most importantly, his new Chinese networks gave him the opportunity to inspire Chinese students to search for a musical language that would create a synergy of Chinese and Western elements. This had a profound impact on Chinese musical development in the twentieth century. Chapter 7 opens with an article on the SMO concert “Grand Chinese Evening” introducing the Russian-Jewish émigré composer Aaron Avshalomov. In contrast to Tcherepnin, Avshalomov, who came from a very different background, engaged in different Shanghai networks for more than a decade. His experimentation in synthesizing Chinese and Western musical as well as dramatic elements in his works and his attempt to symphonicize Chinese music were unprecedented acts with profound implications. Through looking into some of his works that could also be regarded as a different form of “translation” due to their innovations, this chapter unravels the different networks surrounding them. Most of all, it also assesses the implications of the composer’s endeavor on the developmental trajectory of contemporary Chinese music. Objective 5 is examined in all the chapters, and the closing epilogue provides a further examination of the issue raised. It revisits music’s role in diaspora by highlighting how music connected individuals and communities in Shanghai, thus proposing a new understanding of diaspora against the classic one. Then, it reflects on the importance of the study in contributing to ‘relational musicology’, not only in the volume’s subject matter, but also the collaborative approach adopted by the investigators. Last, it looks into how politics in both the ex-USSR and the PRC had led to the ‘disappearance’ of the Shanghai Russian émigrés in dominant discourse of Russian and Chinese prior to the 1980s, and then how the study of Sino-Russian music relations is taking a new turn in recent years. Objective 6 is self-explanatory as evident in item 9 of the report. Objective 7 is self-explanatory as evident in item 8 of the report.

248813.label: Major findings and research outcome
248813.value: The research outcome of the project is the tri-author volume entitled Networking the Russian Diaspora: Russian Musicians and Musical Activities in Interwar Shanghai. The volume shows the impact of migration on both the immigrants and the hosting country. We revealed how the Russian émigrés struggled to survive in Shanghai, and how they gradually built a diaspora in which music played an important role. But unlike other diasporas in which the practice of music from home functioned to foster solidarity among its members, the role of music in Shanghai’s Russian community was complex. Our research suggests that music let Shanghai’s Russian émigrés reach out rather than shrink back. For example, Russian choirs and the Russian opera, as testified by many primary source accounts, did not just serve the Russian community but were also enjoyed by audiences of the international and Chinese communities. In fact, a few of such performances even afforded Chinese musicians performing opportunities that helped China nurture its first generation of highly successful Western music practitioners who since became leading musical figures such as the pianists Ding Shande and Wu Leyi. The fact that the Shanghai Russian community transcended diaspora boundaries was evident in its impact on the city’s Municipal Orchestra. Accounting for more than 50% of the SMO’s players, Russian musicians were also frequently featured as soloists in the orchestra’s regular concerts as well as in its special Russian concerts. These musicians were also crucial in large-scale choral concerts deployed by the SMO director Mario Paci to bring Shanghai’s different musical communities together with an array of political, cultural, and economic motivations. Most important of all, Russian pedagogues affiliated with the National Conservatory have left an indelible mark on Chinese musical development, they being responsible for producing the first generation of renowned Chinese performers who went on to become leading musical figures of China in the second half of the twentieth century. We also note that layers of identities are embedded in different émigré composers’ works. The works of Tcherepnin and Avshalomov readily raise questions about the theoretical usefulness of existing discourse on diaspora and identity. Even the cosmopolitan works of Aksakov illustrate the elusiveness of what a Russian émigré identity should be. While there might have been a perceived “Russian cultural identity” in concrete or in imagination in the diaspora, cultural encounters inevitably lead to new hybrid identities of the individuals as well as their cultural manifestations.

248813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
248813.value: In the process of researching, the principal investigator of this project has come across a large volume of interesting materials that can be used as the basis of future projects. There are two areas that can be further developed. The first area concerns a large amount of information pertinent to Chinese musicians who were students of Russian pedagogues. The second area concerns the concert programs of the Shanghai Municipal Orchestra, of which more than half of its members were Russian and its concert heavily dependent on Russian soloists and Russian works. As an outgrowth of the current project, the investigator has applied for an HKBU internal grant to research on Chinese ‘star musicians’, examining how the training they received from their Russian pedagogues paved their way for their success in musical performance. Furthermore, the investigator also tried to take advantage of the concert programs of the Municipal Orchestra by investigating what Western music concerts meant to Shanghai audience in the early twentieth century by drawing on the notion of middlebrow.

248813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
248813.value: This project treads mostly uncharted territory. Interdisciplinary in nature, it incorporates musical, cultural and diaspora studies into a social history of cosmopolitan Shanghai, bringing together fields of musicology, ethnomusicology, social history and cultural and migration studies. It takes the view that music is not merely about musical texts, compositions and notes, but also about musicians and performances delivered through various types of institutions and material objects such as concert advertisements and programs, but also reviews, revealing identity and power negotiations. The research reveals the importance of music in the formation of Russian émigré culture. It also shows how Russian musicians and musical activities played a part in shaping the dialogues between Chinese and Western music. Furthermore, it demonstrates the impact of cross-cultural encounters on both Russian and Chinese communities. The Russian émigré composers’ synthesis of Western and Chinese elements have become models and inspirations for the next generation of Chinese composers, paving the way for the development of Chinese new music and Western inter-cultural music that would further flourish throughout Asia and other parts of the world after the second half of the twentieth century.

249213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
249213.value: Rising HIV rates among men who have sex with men (MSM) in Hong Kong have led to calls for a better understanding of the situation and contributing factors. Of particular concern are local gay youths (ages 18-25), especially those who meet partners online, because studies have suggested that they are more likely to report higher rates of unprotected sex—the behavior most likely to transmit HIV—and less likely to be exposed to existing HIV prevention programs (Tsui & Lau, 2010; PRiSM, 2012). At present, however, we know very little about the factors that may hamper consistent condom use by gay Hong Kong youths and whether the use of social networking technologies has necessarily played a role in their risk behaviors. Social networking technologies can facilitate high-risk behaviors by offering users a quick and easy means of filtering large numbers of potential partners with similar preferences (Benotsch, Kalichman, & Cage, 2002; McFarlane, Bull, & Rietmeijer, 2002). Gay youths make easy targets for those seeking unprotected sex because their relative inexperience and poor sexual communication skills, including avoiding the topic altogether, puts them at risk when negotiating condom use (Molitor, Facer, & Ruiz, 1999). Furthermore, at their developmental stage, they may not hold pre-determined categorical intentions about condom use and may be ambivalent about or open to unprotected sex if the perceived risk of HIV transmission is low. Recently, the popular emergence of geosocial networking mobile apps (Grindr, Jack’d, Manhunt, etc.) among gay Hong Kong youths has ignited speculation that the use of these apps—which enable users to instantly locate and connect with others nearby—might be fueling HIV risk behaviors (see ‘A deadly dating game’, China Daily, September 2012). Taken together, there is a pressing need to ascertain the impact of social networking technologies on gay Hong Kong youths’ sexual practices. A clearer understanding of how they use and perceive social networking technologies as well as the potential benefits and risks involved is central to effective intervention efforts with this subgroup during a critical period in their social development. Using sexual scripting theory, this mixed-methods study will examine whether and how social networking technologies shape the cultural understandings, interpersonal communication, and personal desires of gay Hong Kong youths in relation to sex and relationships. The knowledge gained in this project will be channeled directly into HIV prevention efforts that foster the resilience and well-being of gay Hong Kong youths. 香港男男性行為愛滋病病毒感染率的上升喚起關注其促成原因，尤其對年齡介乎十八至二十五歲透過網上結識伴侶的香港男同志青年特別關注。過往研究指出，在網上結識伴侶的男同志會有更高機會進行不安全性行為，即他們更有可能傳播愛滋病病毒，和較少機會接觸現有的愛滋病預防項目 (Tsui & Lau, 2010; PRiSM, 2012)。然而，我們不了解有什麼因素會影響香港男同志青年持續使用安全套的習慣，以及使用社交網絡技術對他們的風險行為是否扮演一定的角色。 社交網絡技術為使用者提供一個快捷和方便的渠道，以有效搜羅大量擁有相似喜好的潛在伴侶，從而促進了高危行為(Benotsch, Kalichman, & Cage, 2002; McFarlane, Bull, & Rietmeijer, 2002)。男同志青年很可能被那些尋求不用安全套進行性行為者視為輕易目標，原因是他們的經驗相對不足和不善於對性關係的斡旋，包括完全避免有關話題，使得他們在商討使用安全套時成為風險的一群(Molitor, Facer, & Ruiz, 1999)。此外，按他們的發展階段，如果他們認為愛滋病病毒傳播的風險低，他們可能沒有預先明確地決定使用安全套的意向，或可能對使用安全套感到矛盾，因而進行不安全的性行為。最近，地理社交網絡移動應用程式廣受男同志青年歡迎(Grindr, Jack’d, Manhunt, 等)，這令人猜疑使用這些移動應用程式能夠即時找到並連接附近其他人，可能會助長愛滋病病毒傳播的風險行為。 綜合而論，我們迫切需要澄清社交網絡技術對香港男同志青年性行為的影響。要清楚了解他們如何使用及理解社交網絡技術，以及其潛在利益和風險對這群體在發展社交能力的關鍵時期擔當一個重要並有效的干預力度。 此研究從性的劇本理論探究社交網絡技術如何塑造香港男同志青年有關性與關係的文化理解、人際溝通和個人慾望。同時，此研究亦探討使用社交網絡技術對促進更安全性行為的溝通和推廣預防愛滋病病毒項目的潛力。在此研究中所獲得的知識將會對預防愛滋病病毒傳染發揮直接的指導作用，以及提升男同志青年的順應力和健康。

249213.label: Realisation of objectives
249213.value: Over 300 gay Hong Kong youths participated in this research through in-depth individual interviews, focus group discussions, and a questionnaire survey. Objective 1: This research addressed gay Hong Kong youths' motives of using gay social networking applications and how specific characteristics of the platforms influence their associated gratifications. Participants reported various styles of sexual communication occurring online and offline, shedding light on the potential and limits of social networking technologies for facilitating safer-sex behaviors. The findings show the relationships between frequency and history of gay apps use, and number of recent condomless sex partners in relation to different gratifications sought from gay apps (i.e. surveillance, social, sex, relationship). Objective 2: Interviews examined the sociocultural norms governing online interactions and offline relationships to understand gay Hong Kong youths’ satisfactions and frustrations when pursuing sex and romance on social media. Survey findings confirmed the prevalence of gay Hong Kong youths' sexual and romantic motivations for using gay apps. Objective 3: Interviews examined gay Hong Kong youths’ risk perceptions and risk-reduction practices through a cultural lens and they are shown to be influenced by cultural scripts and interpersonal dynamics. Consequently, sexual practices with varying degrees of risk are adapted in different sexual contexts or with different partners. Intuitive and probabilistic risk assessments were adopted by gay Hong Kong youths when arranging for and during a sexual encounter. Social networking technologies tend to facilitate intuitive risk assessment. Survey findings further indicate that gay Hong Kong youths were more likely to report inconsistent condom use with regular partners and condomless internal ejaculation, attesting to the symbolic values of interpersonal trust with regular partners. Objective 4: The research findings inform us that HIV prevention should focus on longtime app-users and heavy Grindr users; since social gratification is a common underlying motive for apps use, health educators can appeal to users’ social inclusion and validation needs in order to attract and engage with a large segment of apps-users. Objective 5: Findings were presented at leading international communication studies conferences (NCA and AEJMC). Community stakeholders were invited to attend a talk organized to report the project findings. Journal articles resulting from this project were also shared with the Department of Health, AIDS Concern, and The Boys' & Girls' Clubs Association of Hong Kong to inform their work with young gay men. Further contributions include participation in the Community Stakeholders' Consultation Meeting for the Development of Recommended HIV/AIDS Strategies organized by the Advisory Council on AIDS.

249213.label: Major findings and research outcome
249213.value: Firstly, in Yeo and Fung (2015) (see Part C), this project indicates that the challenge for health intervention lies in the inconsistent condom use of young men who have sex with men (YMSM) in Hong Kong despite their high level of HIV-related knowledge. YMSM described using condoms, HIV testing and abstaining from anal sex as measures undertaken to prevent HIV infection. However, sociocultural norms and expectations pertaining to ‘0’ (docile, bottom) and ‘1’ (assertive, top) roles and trust between partners complicate the consistent implementation of risk-reduction measures. Influenced by heteronormative and romantic beliefs, condomless anal sex and internal ejaculation hold symbolic meanings – exclusivity, commitment, intimacy, possession – for YMSM, which override health concerns. Secondly, in Yeo and Ng (2015) (see Part C), this project shows that inconsistent condom use (ICU) and condomless internal ejaculation (CIE) during anal sex was fairly common among app-using YMSM in Hong Kong. Frequent users of Grindr and Jack’d, were less likely to report anal sex, and hence ICU, with regular and non-regular partners, respectively. Sexual partnering via apps doubled the odds of ICU with both regular and non-regular partners. The odds of ICU with regular partners also increased with relationship status but reduced for those who never had STI/HIV testing. With nonregular partners, YMSM’s likelihood of ICU increased with more recent partners and drug use, but reduced with group sex. The odds of receptive CIE increased with alcohol consumption, non-exclusive relationship, and more recent partners, but reduced with group sex and older age. For insertive CIE, the odds increased with bisexual YMSM, exclusive relationship, and longtime apps-use. Finally, in Yeo and Ng (August 2015; see Part C), this project informs the theoretical debate concerning the impact of social networking technology on sexual risk behaviors. Finding sexual partners was not a high priority for using gay apps; surveillance, relationship, and diversion motives were more important. App-use frequency, sex motive, and sexual sensation seeking predicted more total sex partners (TSP) while surveillance motive predicted fewer TSP. None of these variables, however, directly predicted condomless sex partners (CSP). Sexual sensation seeking in interaction with sex or diversion motive predicted both TSP and CSP. Despite lacking significant association with sex motive or sexual sensation seeking, app-use frequency was a stronger independent predictor of TSP. While frequent app use may facilitate more app-met sexual partners, there was no evidence that apps use promote riskier sexual behavior with those partners.

249213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
249213.value: Future studies should assess the generalizability of the findings to see whether gay and bisexual men of other age groups would also readily adopt established cultural scripts of heteronormativity and romance in their sexual practices. Moreover, besides heteronormativity, further research should examine how other social structures such as class and changing socio-political contexts may influence young gay men’s sexual practices. Since the cross-sectional data of the survey prevents any assessment of the temporality of events or inferences about causality, future work could adopt a longitudinal study of new app-users to compare the total number of sex partners and number of condomless sex partners when users begin using the apps and at regular intervals thereafter, and capture any fluctuation in the frequency of use and the perceived importance of the different types of apps-use motives since the beginning of apps use. In addition, the present study did not consider other means of meeting sexual partners and is, therefore, unable to assess the comparative rates of sexual partnering and condomless sex partners. Beyond comparisons of sexual behaviors, future studies should examine the extent to which social networking mobile apps serve as a functional alternative to more traditional means of making social connections.

249213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
249213.value: This project has examined the sexual practices of young men who have sex with men (YMSM), who are fast becoming the most at-risk group of HIV infection in Hong Kong, particularly those who use gay social networking mobile applications (apps). This research found that although YMSM exhibit considerable awareness and concern about HIV infection, condomless anal sex and internal ejaculation hold symbolic meanings derived from heteronormative and romantic beliefs that override health concerns. HIV prevention messages should speak to such sociocultural norms. This research has also identified meaningful differences among YMSM who use gay apps. Notably, YMSM identifying as bisexual, those in a relationship, and longtime app-users are more likely to engage in sexual risk-behaviors. Alcohol consumption and drug use had adverse impacts on YMSM’s sexual decision-making. Overall, this research debunks the notion that the primary motive of using these apps is sex, and that these apps fuel sexual risk-behaviors. The findings indicate that sex-seeking is not a high priority for apps use as compared to the motivations for relationships, distraction, and checking out other MSM nearby. While frequent apps use facilitates more app-met sex partners, this research found no evidence that apps use promote condomlesss anal sex with those partners.

258513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
258513.value: The proposed project investigates how the intersection of structural factors and agency of various actors in migrant families in South China reconstructs parenthood in a separated-family situation. Mass internal migration in China since the 1970s has given rise to the issue of left-behind children, who have become a serious social problem in Mainland China and attracted both public and academic attention. Previous studies on this topic have mostly focused on the behavioral and psychosocial problems of left-behind children caused by their physical separation from their parents. The agency of migrant parents and their parental practices in childrearing have not been discussed, although transnational parenting has become a fast-growing topic in the studies of international migration. Existing literature on transnational parenting focuses on maternal experiences. The role of migrant fathers and the collaboration between migrant parents and substitute caregivers of left-behind children in childrearing are understudied. Meanwhile, current discussions of Chinese parenthood concentrate on the impact of Confucian culture, the rural-urban divide and the increased education level of parents on parenthood construction. The influence of internal migration on parental practices has not been discussed, although migration greatly affects people’s lives in both urban cities and rural villages. In order to fill these gaps, this project will adopt a multi-sited and multi-voice design to investigate: (1) how the interaction among migrant parents, left-behind children and substitute caregivers of left-behind children reconstructs the meaning of parenthood for migrant workers in South China; (2) how the structural factors (migration, gender ideology, Chinese culture, the penetration of information and communication technologies) shape the process of trans-local parenting practices. This project will have the following contributions: (1) it deepens the theoretical discussion of parenthood by demonstrating how the interaction of various structural factors and the diversified agency of different actors in trans-border families shapes parental practices from afar; (2) it enriches the discussion of migrant parenting and trans-border families by investigating both migrant fathers and migrant mothers and examining both the care givers and the care receivers; (3) it enriches the discussions of the meaning of parenthood in Chinese societies by revealing how mass migration challenges traditional Chinese understanding of parenthood and provides new opportunities for migrant parents to reconstruct parenting ideologies; (4) the multi-sited and multi-voice research design will provide important methodological implications for studies of migration and trans-border families in both China and elsewhere.

259213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
259213.value: This project examines the intersection of concepts of race, nationality and citizenship in the British empire through the history of Anglo-Chinese Eurasian communities between 1830 and the 1960s. Although Eurasians were the most controversial peripheral group in treaty port China and colonial Hong Kong, there are very few published studies of Anglo-Chinese communities and individuals. This project fills this gap by exploring the lives and careers of Eurasians in Hong Kong, China and imperial Britain. Ultimately, this research will disentangle the complex relationship between race, nationality and political and professional status in the empire world. This project breaks new ground by investigating the international history of mixed-race communities in the context of the British empire. By focusing primarily on three major port cities – Hong Kong, Shanghai and Liverpool – this study identifies the connections forged between different sites of empire by Eurasians while also examining how local contexts informed their political and professional identities. Therefore, the research outputs, which include a monograph and a related website, will contribute new perspectives on Chinese, British, and global history. Furthermore, debates about the supposed dangers of Sino-foreign encounters ran through the empire world, and the tangible product of these fears can be found in the anti-Chinese exclusion policies of Canada, Australia, the United States and South Africa. This study demonstrates how the experiences of Eurasians in China and Hong Kong can elucidate this empire-wide discourse and its impact on policy-making. There are four intertwined strands to this research, which brings together social, cultural and political approaches to studying the past. Firstly, the project will examine cultural representations of Eurasians in popular literature and film and the ways in which these portrayals expressed imperial disquiet about racial mixing. The second theme is Eurasian childhoods, with a particular focus on education. Thirdly, the project will explore the professional and social statuses of Eurasian individuals. Finally, British immigration policy and the journeys of Eurasians to Britain will shed light upon the influence of imperial racial discourse on definitions of nationality. 本研究以跨國歷史的視野，探討香港、上海及利物浦三地之中英混血族群在1830-1960年代間的生活與事業，並疏理英帝國下的種族、國籍與公民身份等問題。其中加拿大、澳洲、美國及南非等地的反華情緒與移民政策亦將成重心，以申論種種話語對帝國政策的影響。有關的著述目前仍付闕如。本計劃不止填補空白，並可進而提供剖析中國、英國及全球史的新取徑。

259213.label: Realisation of objectives
259213.value: The PI, with the help of two senior research assistants and undergraduate students trained in archival research using project funds, has achieved the project objectives through the collection and consultation of thousands of pages of archival materials collected during five source acquisition trips to repositories in London, Liverpool, Shanghai, and Hong Kong. This extensive archival work has enabled the PI to produce research outputs which, in addition to making a theoretical intervention, are richly empirical. This distinguishes the research outputs produced by this project from the existing book-length publications on the history of Eurasians, which use published materials such as memoirs as their major source material. To date, the project has produced; two articles (one published and one under review) comprising approximately 23,000 words; six papers presented at international conferences and one public lecture; a prosopographical dataset detailing mixed marriages and the baptisms of Eurasian children on the China coast, which will be made available online in December 2019 (objective 5); a 5,000-word article (draft) on the children of Chinese sailors and white women in Liverpool and London, pitched at a general readership. The dissemination plan promised to ‘make progress’ towards a monograph. Accordingly, the PI has produced a book proposal (under review) for a mid-length 30-35,000-word monograph scheduled for completion in November 2019 and two draft chapters for a full-length monograph, which be combine the findings of this project with those of a current project on the history of marginal foreigners in Asian colonial port cities (objective 5). Objectives 1-4 promised to make conceptual and empirical interventions in the social history of foreign communities on the China coast and in the histories of race, nationality, and mobility in the wider British empire. These objectives have been achieved in the project’s research outputs, both completed and in progress. A peer-reviewed book chapter published in December 2016, examines the ways in which being Eurasian enhanced or impaired international mobility. It examines Eurasian experiences of travel between China and other parts of the wider British empire in order to show how they were highly mobile, drawing on transnational family ties to make frequent journeys for professional or personal reasons. The liminal status of Eurasians meant that they could negotiate strict nationality laws in order to obtain British passports and circumvent anti-Chinese immigration laws in the British Dominions and the United States in order to make long-distance relocations. However, these movements of marginal peoples prompted the development of more exclusive national categories in the early twentieth century, which were more strictly policed on the China coast in response to the Nationalist Government’s promulgation of its own Chinese nationality laws. A second journal article, under review at the Journal of Imperial and Commonwealth History, examines the experiences of Eurasian and other marginal European children in the Shanghai Municipal Council’s schools. It shows how Eurasian children were a nexus for discussions about the intersection of race, class and national sentiment, demonstrating how the schools attempted to mould children from diverse national backgrounds into both loyal Shanghailanders and imperial Britons. The PI is currently writing a short monograph (see attached proposal) which uses the colourful biography of a Hong Kong-born Eurasian man, Lawrence Kentwell, as a window into elucidating broader issues related to Eurasian history, particularly mobility between different sites of the British Empire in an age of anti-Chinese exclusion laws, Eurasian anti-imperialist activism, the employment prospects of Eurasians, and the intersection of racial and national identities. This book highlights the ramifications of anti-Chinese exclusion laws, which are usually considered in their national contexts, on the lives of individuals on the China coast, while also considering how fears of racial ‘mixing’ born out of the situation on the China coast fed into these policies. Contrary to the narrative of Eurasians as cultural and economic intermediaries between Chinese and European interests that dominates much of the existing scholarship, this book shows how some Eurasians chose to assert a Chinese identity for political reasons, while the professional and family lives of many others were intertwined with those of other marginal foreigners. A shorter article (4,000-5,000 words) currently in preparation, examines the socio-economic features of and political response to the tight-knit, visible, and geographically contained communities of Eurasian children in Liverpool and London in the early twentieth century, whose status was politicized by popular and parliamentary condemnation of women who married Chinese seamen. Divergences from the original project objectives 1. In response to the PI’s finding that Eurasians did not usually form distinct communities on the China coast but rather led lives that were deeply intertwined with those of other ‘foreign’ families born in Asia, the PI will combine some of the material acquired during this research into a full-length monograph along with the findings of an ongoing project on the history of marginal foreigners in Asian colonial port cities. The PI is currently preparing a shorter monograph which, as described above, is solely devoted to the life stories of Eurasians and their broader implications for imperial history. 2. Due to the technical expertise required in order to attract a significant online readership, the PI has decided to make available data collected during the project on an existing online platform rather than creating an original website. Two datasets containing biographical data collected from treaty-port marriage and baptism records held in the UK National Archives and the Lambeth Palace Library will be made available on the HKBU Library’s History in Data website after this platform is overhauled later this year. This data will be of use to both academic historians and members of the public researching their family history. 3. Although the PI completed five of the planned source acquisition trips, it was not possible to undertake the final trips. This is because a high-risk pregnancy, maternity leave and the health problems of the PI’s infant twins which meant that she could not travel outside of Hong Kong to conduct research during the last 18 months of the project. However, this did not significantly impair the project outcomes and the project team have collected a sufficient material to sustain not only the research outputs detailed above, but also further outputs planned for the next six months as detailed in section 6.2.

259213.label: Major findings and research outcome
259213.value: The research outputs, both completed and in progress, detailed above together constitute the first wide-ranging empirical study of Eurasians on the China coast and in Britain between the mid-nineteenth and the mid-nineteenth centuries. Previous studies have focused on narrowly-defined events or communities of Eurasians, mostly located in Hong Kong, while the only book-length history considers Eurasians in the Asian American context and is based mainly on published sources and memoirs. Three principal features of this project set its findings apart from its predecessors: 1) The extensive archival sources collected from archives in the UK, Hong Kong and Shanghai, which form a rich empirical foundation for the project’s published outputs; 2) The chronological range of the research (c. 1850-1960), which has enabled the PI to assess change and continuity in the political and social status of Eurasians; 3) The situation of the experiences of China-coast Eurasians in the broader history of the British empire. The project makes several major conceptual and empirical interventions: 1) Besides demonstrating how the liminality of Eurasians could enable them to make long-distance journeys that circumvented anti-Chinese immigration laws in the British Dominions and the United States, this research highlights a different type of imperial mobility: travel through regional networks which connected together East and Southeast Asian colonial port cities into an integrated arena of opportunity for Eurasians and other marginal people on the China coast. 2) Discussions about the liminal political status of Eurasians and Anglo-Chinese on the China coast influenced broader debates about the inclusivity or exclusivity of imperial subject status and contributed to the tightening up of British nationality law and its implementation in places on the edges of empire. 3) Although several studies of Hong Kong Eurasians exist, this project is the first to examine the contours of Eurasian lives in the Chinese treaty ports and Britain. One major finding is that, in contrast with other colonial sites such as India or Singapore, there was no clearly-defined Eurasian community with a separate political status in the treaty ports. Although prejudice against Eurasians was widespread among treaty-port elites, the professional and family lives of Eurasians were inextricable from those of other settlers. 4) In all three locations, discussions about the welfare and potential of Eurasian children were a nexus for all the above concerns about the intersection of race, nationality, citizenship, mobility and the extent and limits of colonial responsibility towards marginal Europeans.

259213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
259213.value: The PI is continuing to produce research based upon the sources collected during this project, including a monograph as described in the attached book proposal, which will be completed by the end of 2019. Currently, the PI is writing a short feature article (c. 4,000-5,000 words) pitched at a general educated readership on the distinctive features of communities of Eurasian children in Liverpool and Britain and the ways in which these communities stimulated public debate and government policy about immigration. The findings of this project continue to inform the PI’s long-term research plans. One of the major findings of the project, that Eurasians in the Chinese treaty ports did not form a distinct community but rather were personally and professionally intertwined with the lives of other marginal ‘foreigners’, has informed the PI’s current GRF-funded project on marginal Europeans in East and Southeast Asian port cities. The findings from both projects will be combined in a single full-length monograph. Furthermore, the PI intends to develop a new project on the history of citizenship, nationality, mobility and race on the edges of the British empire, which arises from the findings of this project.

259213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
259213.value: This project gives voice to the thousands of non-elite people of mixed Chinese and European ancestry who, despite constituting a large proportion of ‘foreign’ residents on the China coast between the mid-nineteenth and mid-twentieth centuries, have remained mostly hidden from view. Using a broad range of archival sources from the UK, China and Hong Kong, this project sheds light upon both the distinctive features of Eurasian identities in the Chinese treaty ports, Hong Kong, Liverpool and London. For instance, Eurasians in the Chinese treaty ports differed from mixed-race communities in Hong Kong, Britain or in other colonial sites because they neither belonged to a separate political category, nor did they form a distinct communal identity. Instead, their life experiences and cross-regional movements were embedded in a web of family and professional connections which spanned all marginal foreigners in the treaty ports. By contrast, in Liverpool and London Eurasian children formed visible and geographically contained communities in the early twentieth century. Above all, this research demonstrates how discussions of the national status and extent of colonial responsibility towards Eurasians on the China coast fed into broader debates about the inclusivity and exclusivity of imperial subjecthood in the wider British empire.

259913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
259913.value: The promises of growth and innovation offered by creative industries have found their way into policy initiatives around the world. In Asia, recent years saw South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong and Singapore implement plans to integrate arts, technology and business in order to ensure their future places in the region. China is no exception. To date, academic studies on the Chinese experience have focused on how the global discourse of creative industries is translated to local practices. Some go further and ask if a‘Creative China’ would lead to a more open and free society. This project responds to these questions from a unique perspective. It takes the increasing inter-connectedness between Hong Kong and Mainland China as its starting point. It fills a research gap by asking: how and how far have members of Hong Kong’s creative class impacted on China? More specifically, it does so by conducting an empirical study on the creative brain drain from Hong Kong to Mainland China. In 2008, Leung Man-tao, an influential intellectual in Hong Kong, published an article highlighting the post-millennium phenomenon that increasingly more people from the local arts and cultural sector have responded to the threats and opportunities brought forward by the‘Rise of China' and shifted their base from Hong Kong to Mainland China. They took up creative jobs in China, particularly in the print media; some also opened spaces such as galleries or cafes targeted especially at the new creative class in urban China. Leung's article has sparked off intense public discussions over the future of Hong Kong’s creative industries and the likely impact on China. As yet, no academic study has been conducted on the phenomenon. Following ten Hong Kong creative professionals who have relocated to Shanghai and Beijing, this project has the following objectives: 1/ To chart the emergence and trajectory of the creative brain drain and to document their narratives; 2/ To examine what they have experienced and actually done in the creative outputs they have delivered; 3/ To examine what they have experienced and actually done in the creative spaces they have opened; 4/ To synthesize insights gained from 1-3 for theoretical reflection and policy implications; 5/ To publish four academic articles; and 6/ To use knowledge thus gained for community dissemination and tertiary education purposes. Multiple qualitative research methods (in-depth interviews, participant observation, archive research and textual analysis) will be employed.

259913.label: Realisation of objectives
259913.value: In 2008, Leung Man-tao, an influential intellectual in Hong Kong, published an essay with an alarming title: ‘Confessions of Someone from the Last Generation of Hong Kong Cultured People’. Citing a handful of well-known film-maker, designer and writers who shifted their career base to mainland China, Leung foregrounded what he observed as a ‘reality of the market, reality of the society’ – professionals from Hong Kong’s arts and cultural sectors have increasingly responded, on the one hand, to the limitations the city had to wrestle with and, on the other, the opportunities brought forward by the ‘Rise of China’; they moved. They took up creative jobs and projects in China. Informed by this phenomenon, this project concerns one practice of creative class, namely mobility, which in turn feeds into the global competition of ‘creative cities’ to try their best to attract and retain talented creative workers. Implied in this line of thinking and policy initiative is a two-thronged belief: on the one hand, creative workers, unlike many other resources for growth, can be and are indeed mobile; on the other, certain places bear particular appeal to them and they respond by moving there. The question remains, ‘what are the primary push and pull mechanisms behind migration of talent and the creative class?’. Given the lack of studies in the Chinese experience, this project is first and foremost exploratory in nature. Empirically driven by a case embedded in something else, or more, than work and place, namely Sino-Hong Kong dynamics, this project contributes theoretically to current understandings of creative class mobility. A total of 12 creative workers were recruited. While half of them were direct acquaintances of mine or friends/acquaintances of theirs, the rest were introduced to me through other sources (for instance, a colleague introduced a former student). Efforts were made to secure a better balance of gender and age ratio. Parallel to this consideration, there were two major requirements concerning the recruitment of respondents. First, for reasons mentioned earlier, their professions should fall under what the DMCS would prescribe as creative work. Second, they would see themselves doing such creative work. Here, I adopted a bottom-up approach; I used the term ‘creative industries’ while liaising with possible respondents and when they agreed to take part, I assumed they agreed to be seen as creative worker. The 12 respondents thus recruited include 9 males and 3 females, born between 1952 and 1992. They work in a variety of creative professions, ranging from music, design, magazine, and advertising, to art and cultural events administration. I have deliberately refrained from defining a priori which creative industries would be covered. This ‘looseness’ corresponded to the goal of the current inquiry, namely to explore and map the field of studying creative class mobility in contemporary China – a field which is characterized by a lack of similar research. At the same time, the other starting point of the current inquiry, which relates to issues of mobility, was the Sino-Hong Kong dynamics. Consequently, respondents were recruited primarily because of where they were from, not what they did. My fieldwork consisted of two months in Beijing and Shanghai, respectively in 2014 and 2015. All respondents indicated their written consent to participate in this inquiry and allowed their real names to be used. I conducted at least one in-depth semi-structured interview with each respondent (usually about an hour), at the venue(s) preferred by the respondent. I would typically open the interview with asking them the factual aspects of leaving Hong Kong, such as when, where to, and for what. I would then follow up on the motivation details of their mobility, focusing on why they moved, why to mainland China, and why the current base of Shanghai or Beijing. While the first half of the interview covered their lives leading to the move, the second half continued to probe into their encounters and experiences after they moved. Guided by this rough questioning logic, I stayed alert to their verbal and non-verbal responses and improvised follow-up questions on potentially illuminating but un- or under-articulated points. Insights drawn from the fieldwork contribute to three journal articles: on what they had to say about why they moved and why they moved there (revised and resubmitted to Eurasian Geography and Economics); on their post-migration work experiences, especially in the particularities of creative practices in mainland China (accepted and published by China Information); and on the affective dimension of their migration (being prepared for a special issue for International Journal of Cultural Studies). In short, I argue that creative class mobility should not be configured only with work or only with place. We need to take into account many other vectors: the geopolitical, the intersectional, the contingent, the circuituous, the aspirational, the precarious, the ethical, and the affective. Meanwhile, tentative findings from the project were presented at New York University-Shanghai Campus， University of Melbourne and Hong Kong Baptist University. Furthermore, they were also incorporated to my teaching on Chinese creativity, and a new course is under preparation accordingly. The project also engendered the opportunity for undergraduate training in the form of a documentary recording the migratory experience of the 12 creative workers. The documentary is meant for pedagogical purposes.

259913.label: Major findings and research outcome
259913.value: While existing scholarship on creative class mobility is largely configured by concerns with employment situations and place attractiveness, the current study of mobility supplements it by drawing insights from a specific case of Hong Kong-mainland China mobility. Its major findings contribute to three articles. 1/. Revised and resubmitted to Eurasian Geography and Economics: On the one hand, this inquiry has noted the importance of the geopolitical context in their migration narratives when some of the respondents explain their reasons for moving to mainland China not only in relation to work and place, but also to their wish to do things which are driven by the Sino-Hong Kong dynamics. On the other hand, what the respondents have to say about their trajectory points to the need to pay attention to categories intersecting their creative employment such as gender and age; to the often contingent, rather haphazard nature of their migration; and to the possible longer migratory trajectories that are characterized by circuitousness. 2/ Accepted and published by China Information: Like many fellow creative workers, my informants moved northwards to pursue better career opportunities. But they also wanted to do something more. Some of them managed. At the same time, their stories were punctuated with disappointments, frustrations and continuous adjustments, categorized into what I call the precarious and the ethical. The findings of this inquiry pose questions on the hypothesis, the hype and the hope of creativity in China. (Pls see PDF of the published article in Part C.) 3/ Being prepared for a special issue for International Journal of Cultural Studies: As this article is still at its preparatory stage, not much can be said in details. Tentatively speaking, it will focus on the affective dimensions of creative class mobility as experienced by the 12 creative workers from Hong Kong to Shanghai and Beijing. The entanglements with their love lives, their friendships, their families, and the general feeling of not at home are understudied in creative class scholarship.

259913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
259913.value: Building on this research project, I can envisage a number of follow-up studies. I will name three of them. 1/. Gender: This project does not specify gender as an important parameter to study creative class mobility either in general, or from Hong Kong to mainland China in particular. The interviews, however, do point to gender-specific experiences, which deserve further investigation. 2/ Return: This project focuses on creative ‘brain-drain’, namely outflow from Hong Kong. As indicated by the interviews, some of them do contemplate a possible return to the city. In fact, I know of some other creative workers who have done so after staying in the mainland for some time. In addition to studying their decision to leave Hong Kong, it would be interesting to continue studying why some decide to return and what their experiences are. 3/ Longitudinal: This project examines experiences now and then. What would their experiences be, say, in 5 year’s time? A longitudinal study on the same group of migrants would offer more insights on their long-term experiences.

259913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
259913.value: This project studies a particular case of creative class mobility, namely from Hong Kong to Shanghai and Beijing. Given that existing scholarship on creative class is largely based on Western experience, this project contributes to understanding of creative workers and their mobility in a Hong Kong-Chinese context. From the narratives of the 12 creative workers included in this inquiry, they have moved northwards mainly because of better career prospects, not due to the attractiveness of the cities concerned. This finding poses questions on one dominant assumption proposed by Richard Florida and adopted by many urban planners and policy makers, namely cool cities attract talents. Furthermore, this inquiry finds geopolitical context should be taken into account when understanding creative class mobility, while age, gender, family background and personal trajectory are equally significant in shaping creative workers’ choice of employment location. At the same time, creative workers also articulate their aspirations of working in mainland China, which are often compromised by unpredictable behaviours of the state and the investors. In the end they are all wrestling with ethical concerns. This, as well as other personal concerns, in turn also call for a better understanding and care of the affective sides of creative migrants.

260413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
260413.value: 絞股藍（GP ），也稱為絞股藍，是中國傳統的中藥，用於治療包括癌症在內的各種疾病。使用分子和蛋白組學的方法，我們已經在細胞和動物模型研究出絞股藍總三萜皂甙和其中兩種純化合物（GPG and GPO）的抗癌果效 [該研究獲得GRF 07-09和CRF 09-11基金資助]。 GP的總皂苷（GPS）有效地抑制腫瘤細胞的生長。有趣的是， GPS的抑制作用需要正常細胞共同培養。在大腸癌小鼠模型， GPS治療腸息肉減少了40％。這些發現提供了強有力的證明GPS具有抗癌特性。 腸道微生物區系在健康和疾病中起著重要的作用，尤其是在藥物代謝。然而，主機菌群的生態系統的認識仍然模糊。但是, 最近的研究發現腸道菌群的調製可以顯著影響寄主的代謝表型，能量平衡，疾病狀態及藥物反應。我們最近分析和比較GPS對腸道菌群的變化和裸鼠移植瘤的影響，並發現GPS是能夠轉換帶瘤的裸鼠的菌群從生態失調到正常狀態。有了這些令人鼓舞的結果，為進一步闡明GPS藥物的作用，我們將探討中藥材，以GPS為例, 如何影響腸道細菌的組成，以及是否這些特定的微生物群反過來改變寄主生態. 實驗將會採用Apcmin/+大腸癌小鼠作模型. 我們已經在細胞模型証實了GPS和GPO的抗癌的效果。此建議的項目，我們相信將提供中藥如何影響寄主與腸道菌群, 並作為以中國傳統醫學（中醫）為基礎的藥物研究的先驅。從這個研究項目將為GP皂甙作為治療和預防癌症推進一大步。

260413.label: Realisation of objectives
260413.value: Gut microbiota is significantly associated to individual’s health and diseases, including cancer. Saponins have raised considerable interest for their health-promoting effects and preventive roles in various diseases. In this funded project, we address questions on how ingested herbal medicines, such as Gynostemma pentaphyllum (Gp) affect the composition of the bacteria population in the gut, and how that in turn affects the host’s gut microenvironment and responses to the drug. To the end of the project, we have successfully achieved two main objectives of the proposal, namely to demonstrate the impacts of GpS on gut microflora in both healthy and cancer- bearing animal models. We further defined the signature changes in the gut microbiome associated with Gp saponins protective effect in Apcmin/+. In addition to the investigation of the gut microbiota under the influence of GpS treatment, the inflammatory and cancerous biomarkers in the host gut epithelial were revealed with significant novel findings.

260413.label: Major findings and research outcome
260413.value: 1. The anti-cancer effect of Gynostemma pentaphyllum saponins in the ApcMin/+ mouse model. We demonstrated that GpS alone or in combination with 5-FU could significantly reduce the number and size of intestinal polyps in ApcMin/+ mice. The proteomics and bioinformatics analyses suggested that the anti-cancer effect of GpS might be mediated through the upregulation of Prdx1 and Prdx2, suppression of Ras, RAF/MEK/ERK/STAT, PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling and modulation of JNK/p38 MAPK signaling. 2. GpS induced differential changes of gut microbiota in non-tumor and tumor grafting athymic nude mice. In this study, we analyzed the fecal microbiome of nonxenograft and xenograft nude mice treated with GpS. The fecal DNAs were analyzed using enterobacterial repetitive intergenic consensus (ERIC)-PCR and 16S pyrosequencing methods. This study, for the first time, characterizes the properties of gut microbiome in nude mice responding to tumor implant and drug treatment. We also demonstrate that GpS can potentially regulate the gut microbial ecosystem by increasing the number of symbionts. 3. Dietary saponins of four medicinal herb exert prebiotic-like effects on gut microbiota in healthy C57BL/6 mice This study demonstrated the impact of saponins on gut microbiota in mice. Real time qPCR showed that some known beneficial bacteria were enhanced in the treatment groups. Importantly, Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, a bacterium associated with human intestinal health, was stimulated by GpS treatment in a time-dependent manner. This study, for the first time, demonstrated that the health-promoting effects of dietary saponins might be through the manipulation of the gut microbiota. 4. GpS enhance beneficial bacteria, decrease sulfate-reducing bacteria, modulate inflammatory intestinal microenvironment and exert cancer preventive effects in ApcMin/+ mice Study showed that GpS treatment significantly reduced the number of intestinal polyps in a preventive mode and boosted the beneficial microbes. More importantly, GpS feeding strikingly reduced the sulfate-reducing bacteria lineage, which are known to produce hydrogen sulfide and contribute to damage the intestinal epithelium or even promote cancer progression. In the gut barrier of the mice, GpS increased Paneth and goblet cells, up-regulated E-cadherin and down-regulated N-cadherin. In addition, GpS treatment also improved the inflamed gut epithelium of the mice by upregulating the anti-inflammatory cytokines while downregulating pro-inflammatory cytokines. Intriguingly, GpS markedly stimulated M2 and suppressed M1 macrophage markers, indicating that GpS altered mucosal cytokine profile in favor of the M1 to M2 macrophages switching, facilitating intestinal tissue repair.

260413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
260413.value: The findings from this project strongly demonstrate that GpS remarkably improved the diseased intestinal epithelium of ApcMin/+ mice through the modulation of the gut microbiota, downregulating the pro-inflammatory and upregulating the anti-inflammatory molecules. Such properties pointed the potential of GpS to be developed as cancer preventive health supplement. In addition, we also revealed, for the first time, that herbal saponins can function as prebiotic in regulating gut microbiota to the benefit of the host. Our pioneer works provide first hand evidence for the impact of herbal saponins on the gut microbial ecosystem and new insights into the possible mechanisms for their cancer preventive effects. Such health beneficial effects of GpS may apply to alleviate other chronic elements associated with inflammatory intestinal environment.

260413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
260413.value: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the leading causes of cancer deaths in the world. The colon has been described as a “bioreactor”, containing the greatest amounts of bacteria. Recent evidence has demonstrated the crucial role of commensal microbiota in the development of CRC. In order to investigate the responses of commensal microflora to cancer and anti-cancer jiaogulan saponins (GpS), we adapted colorectal ApcMin/+ mice for the thesis project. For further understanding the interaction between gut microbiota, herbal saponins and cancer, we also adapted athymic nude mice with immune deficiency into our study. The key findings are listed below: 1. This study, for the first time, characterizes the properties of gut microbiome in nude mice responding to tumor implant and drug treatment. We also demonstrate that dietary saponins such as GpS can potentially regulate the gut microbial ecosystem by increasing the number of symbionts. Interestingly, this regulation of the gut ecosystem might be in part responsible for or contribute to the anticancer effect of GpS. 2. This study, for the first time, demonstrated that the health-promoting effects of dietary saponins might be through the manipulation of the gut microbiota to the benefit of the host. Our findings strongly indicated that herbal saponins have great potential to be developed as prebiotics for human health. 3. GpS might reverse the host’s inflammatory phenotype by increasing beneficial bacteria, decreasing sulfate-reducing bacteria, and alleviating intestinal inflammatory gut environment, which might contribute to its cancer preventive effects.

260613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
260613.value: 肥胖已經成為了公共健康危機。肥胖人群較易患上多種疾病，例如心血管疾病、二型糖尿病、高血壓、中風及多種癌症，所以增加能量消耗和控制肥胖是必要的。 脂肪細胞分為兩種，分別為白色脂肪細胞和褐色脂肪細胞。白色脂肪細胞專門儲存化學能量，而褐色脂肪細胞則將能量轉化成熱量。解耦連蛋白1（uncoupling protein 1, UCP1）是一種特異存在於褐色脂肪細胞線粒體的內膜蛋白，負責生熱作用過程中呼吸鏈的解耦連。然而，肥胖人群中幾乎不存在活化的褐色脂肪或只有低的生熱作用。 使白色脂肪細胞表達UCP1及其他褐色脂肪細胞的表型和特性，稱之為「褐變」。它由腎上腺素的刺激和環氧合酶（cycloxygenase, COX）活性所調控。天然無毒的草本提取物產生褐變作用，會成為引人注目的抗肥胖策略。我們初步的資料顯示：肉桂提取物（CE）能夠在體外（i）使3T3-L1白色脂肪細胞表達褐色脂肪細胞的典型多彩表型和UCP1；（ii）在db+/+db, m+/+db的皮下脂肪組織以及（iii）飲食誘導肥胖（diet-induced obesity, DIO）小鼠中分離的皮下脂肪細胞中表達UCP1。此外，去甲腎上腺素同樣誘導來自體內的皮下脂肪細胞表達UCP1。而且，（iv）CE能增加和db+/+db, m+/+db和DIO小鼠的`皮下脂肪組織的環氧合酶2（COX2）表達；COX2選擇性抑制劑能減少CE誘導的UCP1表達；（v）在脂質沉積研究中 ，我們發現潛在的前列腺素可能介導CE在皮下脂肪細胞中的褐變作用。 總的來說，我們猜想CE信號在皮下通過COX2和β腎上腺素通路上調UCP1、介導褐變作用。為驗證這一假說，我們計畫（1）檢測COX2（和/或COX1）是否介導CE的褐變作用；（2）驗證我們識別的前列腺素介導的CE褐變作用。此外，我們還計畫（3）驗證β腎上腺素通路是否介導CE的褐變作用。我們同樣將會檢測一個替代通路，即CE中活性物質-肉桂醛直接活化暫態受體電位A1（Transient Receptor Potential A1，TRPA1）通道，從而產生褐變作用。 我們將進行CE褐變作用的進一步體內研究，以及其在肥胖小鼠新陳代謝中的作用。

260613.label: Realisation of objectives
260613.value: We have achieved Objective 1, 2 and 3. We found that cinnamon extract (CE) induced typical brown adipocyte multiocular phenotype in 3T3-L1 adipocytes. The treatment also increased brown adipocytes markers and reduced white adipocytes markers in the 3T3-L1 adipocytes. In ex vivo studies, we found that CE increased brown adipocytes markers in the subcutaneous adipocytes isolated from db/db mice and diet-induced obesity (DIO) mice. However, CE did not significantly affect UCP1 expression in the adipocytes isolated from perinephric adipose tissue and epididymal adipose tissue. β3-adernergic receptor (β3-AR) antagonist reduced the CE-enhanced UCP1 expression, suggesting an involvement of the β3-AR. Oral administration of CE significantly increased UCP1 expression in the subcutaneous adipose tissue and reduced the body weight of the DIO mice. CE also increased COX2 expressions in white adipocytes; and COX2 inhibitor reduced the CE-enhanced UCP1 expression. Our data also suggest that different components in the CE such as catechin and chlorogenic acid also increase UCP1 expression but not necessarily mediated by COX2 activity. We have tested if prostaglandins (PG) were responsible for the CE-enhanced UCP1 expression. Our data suggest that PGD2 and PGE2 are not able to significantly increase UCP1 expression in the white adipocytes.

260613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
260613.value: Since cinnamon is a natural non-toxic herb, we will further examine other anti-obesity effects of cinnamon. Our studies will provide solid scientific evidence to suggest that cinnamon can be a natural remedy to reduce obesity.

260613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
260613.value: Browning is the process of inducing brown adipocyte phenotypes in white adipocytes which are therefore called brite cells. Increasing brite cell helps to increase energy expenditure which can reduce obesity. Consumption of natural and non-toxic herbal extracts that possess the browning effect is an attractive anti-obesity strategy. In this study, we examined the browning effect of cinnamon extract. We found that the extract increased uncoupling protein 1 expression in subcutaneous adipocytes and reduced the body weight of the diet-induced obesity mice. Our data suggest that cinnamon extract has a browning effect in subcutaneous adipocytes, which can be a natural non-toxic herbal remedy to reduce obesity.

261113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
261113.value: 類風濕關節炎是一種以多關節滑膜炎症性病變為特徵的慢性全身性自身免疫性疾病。在香港成人中發病率較高，約為0.35%。滑膜炎持久反復發作，可導致關節內軟骨和骨的破壞，關節功能障礙，甚至殘疾。給患者和社會都造成嚴重的經濟負擔。 類風濕關節炎骨破壞機制被認為是骨重建過程中破骨細胞骨吸收增強而成骨細胞骨形成減弱所致。然而，至今對於類風濕關節炎骨破壞仍無有效的治療措施。即使是通過積極的治療去遏制關節骨破壞的進展，已有的損傷性病變仍然得不到有效修復，只有非常有限的骨損傷位點有新骨形成。這表明在炎症和骨侵蝕局部，成骨細胞介導的骨形成功能受損，從而造成總體上的骨丟失。 已有研究提示：在炎症性關節炎的局部骨破壞部位，成骨細胞的中晚期分化及成熟、骨礦化功能受損。但是目前具體的分子機制仍然不明。因此，有必要深入研究，為未來開發新的骨修復藥物提供實驗依據。 近來，專案組發現一個新的細胞內負性調控因數——酪蛋白激酶2相互作用蛋白-1（CKIP-1）。其能通過與Smurf-1相互作用，增加後者的活性從而發揮負性調控成骨細胞中晚期分化及礦化的作用。我們最新的研究也發現：在類風濕關節炎患者關節置換標本中CKIP-1的表達異常升高，而Smad1和骨鈣素的表達顯著下降。在類風濕關節炎動物模型關節局部成骨細胞內，CKIP-1表達也持續升高，與骨破壞增強和骨形成降低密切相關。此外，體外實驗發現，前炎症因數TNF-α、IL-1、IL-6能促進成骨樣細胞CKIP-1的表達。據此，我們提出以下假說：成骨細胞內CKIP-1高表達可能是類風濕關節炎骨破壞局部成骨細胞成骨功能受損的關鍵因素之一。 為證明上述假說，本專案選用既往已製備成功的成骨細胞靶向性CKIP-1核酸遞送系統干預膠原誘導關節炎動物模型，採用關節炎評分、顯微CT、組織病理、骨形態計量、及免疫組化等方法分析干預後小鼠在關節炎發病、骨小梁結構、骨破壞、骨形成及成骨細胞分化狀態等方面的變化，以期闡明成骨細胞內CKIP-1在類風濕關節炎骨破壞局部骨修復中的作用，並為臨床開發具有真正意義上的骨修復藥物提供新的靶標。

261113.label: Realisation of objectives
261113.value: For this whole research project, 1. We have evaluated the arthritis severity of collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) mice treated with osteoblast target delivery system encapsulated CKIP-1 siRNA ((DSS)6-liposome-CKIP-1 siRNA) (hereafter, CKIP-1 siRNA) by a graded scale; 2. We have quantified the bone architecture of CIA mice treated with CKIP-1 siRNA by microCT measurement; 3. We have examined the bone erosion of CIA mice treated with CKIP-1 siRNA by histology analysis; 4. We have measured local osteoblastic bone formation of CIA mice treated with CKIP-1 siRNA by bone histomorphometry analysis; 5. We have investigated the markers specific to the stages of osteoblast differentiation of CIA mice treated with CKIP-1 siRNA by immunohistochemistry, we have also detected the osteoblastic CKIP-1 levels by laser capture in combination with Q-PCR, respectively. Up to now, we have completed all the projects objectives.

261113.label: Major findings and research outcome
261113.value: Major findings: During previous research period, we have found that arthritis score was significantly decreased in CKIP-1 siRNA-treated CIA mice when compared to mice treated with (DSS)6-liposome-non sense siRNA (hereafter NS), (DSS)6-liposome (hereafter VEH) or PBS. In addition, we have also found better organized microarchitecture and a higher bone mass in CKIP-1 siRNA-CIA mice compared to NS-, VEH-, or PBS-treated mice (Please refer to 2015 annual report). Further, we have found that the bone erosion score in CKIP-1 siRNA treated-CIA mice was remarkably decreased compared to those treated with NS, VEN or PBS after treatment. The dynamic bone histomorphometric analysis showed that the values of MAR and BFR/BS were significantly higher in CKIP-1 siRNA-treated group when compared with three control groups after treatment (Please refer to 2016 annual report). During this research period, we have found that the level of CKIP-1 mRNA was significantly downregulated in osteocalcin positive cells of CKIP-1 siRNA-treated CIA mice after treatment. We have also found more ALP positive cells and osteocalcin positive cells in CKIP-1 siRNA-treated CIA mice compared to three control groups (http://systembioinfo.org/hxj/annual%20report.pdf). 261113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
261113.value: In this study, we have found that inhibition osteoblastic CKIP-1 could effectively attenuate articular bone erosion and promote bone repair in mice with collagen-induced arthritis, which would provide a potential target CKIP-1 to augment osteoblast-mediated bone formation toward repairing articular bone erosion during progressive rheumatoid arthritis. In further study, we will investigate the therapeutic effect of osteoblastic CKIP-1 inhibition in a collagen-induced non-human primate arthritis model so as to facilitate our findings to clinical translation.

261113.value: Based on the experimental data, it has been confirmed that osteoblastic CKIP-1 inhibition could attenuate bone erosion and promote bone repair in collagen-induced arthritis mice. The significance and value of the research is to provide a novel target CKIP-1 to augment osteoblast-mediated bone formation toward repairing articular bone erosion during progressive rheumatoid arthritis.

262013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
262013.value: 全世界每年大約產生13億頓市政垃圾，其中30-50%（香港約40%）是廚餘垃圾。廚餘垃圾填埋佔用了寶貴的土地，並且釋放甲烷氣體導致溫室效應。厭氧消化是處理廚餘垃圾的可行選擇，因為在回收能源的同時還能減少其填埋量。傳統單相厭氧消化容易發生產酸和耗酸的不平衡，使得反應器運行不理想，從而降低了甲烷產生效率。兩相厭氧消化的設計中，從物理上將產酸相（酸化/乙酸化）和耗酸相（甲烷化）分開，使得分別優化兩相反應器，提高運行效率和反應器穩定性的優點得以發揮。然而，兩相厭氧消化的甲烷產生量並沒有比單相高很多。碳守恆分析發現約20%的碳從產酸反應器中以二氧化碳的形式放出。文獻資料表明，產酸相氣體包含大量二氧化碳和氫氣。我們假設將產酸反應器的氣體轉移到產甲烷相；在產甲烷相同型產乙酸菌和利用氫產甲烷菌可以利用二氧化碳和氫氣產生乙酸或甲烷，因此總的產甲烷量會提高。影響代謝途徑的主要因素包括pH值、酸積累和反應器頂空氫氣的濃度。對這些因素之間的相互影響的研究尚不充分，一些相關文獻往往只報導了主要微生物類群的變化，並沒有將這些條件變化和代謝途徑的遷移聯繫在一起。應用宏基因組學和轉錄組學的方法可以揭示影響不同酸化產物，比如脂肪酸和溶劑以及在不同操作和反應器環境下代謝途徑遷移的所有微生物類群和其功能屬性。因此，本計畫旨在探究（i）利用先進的宏基因組學和轉錄組學揭示兩相厭氧消化產酸反應器中微生物之間的相互作用；和（ii）影響滲濾液（第二段產甲烷反應器的食物）品質的因素對甲烷產量以及減少二氧化碳釋放的潛力的影響。利用宏基因組學開發的技術，可以通過調節運行以及反應器環境鎖定特定的代謝產物，因此該研究具有以生物能源不同領域技術為科學依據發展成高效厭氧消化的潛力。

262013.label: Realisation of objectives
262013.value: The project achieved its target as proposed as three different objectives. The objective 1 aimed to study the metabolic pathway during off-gas diversion from LBR to UASB reactors to correlate with the microbial diversity and functions. This was successfully achieved by comparing the control system without LBR-offgas diversion and treatment with LBR-offgas diversion to UASB. The results provided a clue that off-gas diversions benefit the hydrogen production pathways and accumulation of desirable volatile fatty acid (e.g. butyrate) for methane production in second stage UASB system. The microbial population dynamics were distinct between the treatment, while they coincide with the acid accumulations and speciation’s results. Especially, the Syntrophobacteria was dominant during the organic acid productions in LBR-with offgas diversion to UASB. Whereas, the Lactobacilli was dominated in the control system. Notably, the gas transfer system had very specific microbial diversity and community interactions that of control system and was found interesting. The metatranscriptomic analysis has also been completed for control system to compare with treatment as discussed in below section (under objective 3). In objective 2, the aim was to improve the biogas yield by regulation of offgas diversion and leachate exchange dynamics from LBRs to UASBs. First, the study established that the offgas diversion improved the biogas yield upto 10% than control system. With leachate exchange, the biogas yields further improved upto 40%. Further to improve the efficiency and yield, the leachate qualities were differed by changing the off-gas diversion rates by maintaining different head space pressures in LBRs and compared with control system. The treatment that had maximum off-gas diversion rate (was achieved using 3.3 psi head space pressure) solubilized more of organics by improved hydrolysis-acidogenesis process in LBRs. This subsequently improved the biogas (and methane) yields. To follow-on, the objective 3 considered to test the LBRs gas composition as a parameter to regulate the hydrolysis-acidogenesis process under 3.3 psi pressure regulation conditions in headspace. The interesting finding from this experiment and objective was that the low hydrogen partial pressure (0.04%) was provided more soluble products and carbon conversion rates. This was possible due to more electron flux towards the carbohydrate conversion processes to produce methane that was evident from the electron flux and metabolic pathways. Also, the metatranscriptome study revealed that the gene regulations were different between control system and treatments. There are ~2700 and ~2600 genes were up- and down-regulated in treatment, compared to that of control system, respectively. Overall, the study achieved the target of improving the biogas (and methane) yield by altering the system conditions and the results are supported by microbial diversity analysis, electron flow theories and metatranscirptomic studies
