262013.label: Major findings and research outcome
262013.value: The four major findings from this research study are; (a) Offgas diversion from LBRs improve the biogas (and methane) yield in UASB, was demonstrated as a novel strategy. Through this approach, the biogas (and methane) yield could be improved upto 10% than control system. (b) Pressure regulation of 3.3 psi in head space of LBRs found more feasible and reliable approach to achieve high rate of acidogenic off-gas as well as the volatile fatty acid productions for subsequent methanization in UASB. (c) The LBRs offgas composition influences the degradation rate and metabolic pathways were evident from the electron flow calculations. Thus the gas composition in LBRs also key to regulate the better process conversion and biogas yield was found novel. (d) The microbial diversity and interactions were found distinct between the control and treatments. Thus we could able to identify the beneficial microbes that favor the butyrate production pathways during hydrolysis-acidogenesis of food waste in LBRs and no such data reported elsewhere.

262013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
262013.value: This path-finding research provided many interesting research directions for developing new research proposals for upcoming funding schemes and also for international collaborative research fund applications developments. The specific research scopes/directions that need to be addressed are; (a) Understanding the metabolic pathways in UASB reactor during off-gas diversion and leachate regulation to explain the improved biogas (and methane) yields (b) Effect of CO2 pressure and its percentage in head space of LBRs in regulation of metabolic pathways and subsequent methane yield in UASBs. These two scopes will be really interesting to study to further improve the efficiency of the two-phase anaerobic digestion system for food waste treatment. The first scope will provide the better clue to understand the microbial interactions in UASB that support 40% higher methane yields. The second scope will help to understand the key role of CO2 in buffering the LBRs. If it’s sequestered in LBRs, this will lead to develop a new process to bio-refine the biogas from UASB. Therefore, off-gas from UASB can be diverted to LBRs for low cost biogas purifications during sequential operations.

262013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
262013.value: Food waste treatment to produce bioenergy is an important research area for Hong Kong that produces ~3600 tones every day and simply disposed-off in landfills. Instead it could be used to produce more bioenergy that can benefit our society. But, food waste treatment by conventional anaerobic digesters (single-stage system) found difficult due to their operational limitations and space requirements. Alternatively, a two-stage system will be used that required less space and more controlled process that could treat 2-5 times more food waste than conventional digesters. During two-stage system operations, there is a loss of energy as CO2 and H2 from stage-1 reactor. This affects the overall energy intensity and process economics. To overcome the problem, this research proposed a new concept of utilizing this gas from stage-1 reactor to produce methane in stage-2 reactor. The study was successfully demonstrates that the bioenergy could be improved up to 40% by using this approach. The path-finding study also provided a clue that the specific group of microbes facilitated this high-energy yield and this technology could be feasible to use in the field.

262213.label: Project Title(Chinese)
262213.value: Extra Large G Protein 2 (XLG2) 在植物免疫反應中起作用的分子機理

262213.label: Project Objectives
262213.value: We will carry out detailed molecular characterization of XLG2 protein to reveal whether it binds to modified and/or unmodified histones. We will also determine whether XLG2 undergoes nucleocytoplasmic shuttling in response to pathogen infection and whether XLG2 accumulation is controlled by AtPUB2 and AtPUB4, two E3 ubiquitin ligases which were previously identified as putative XLG2-interacting proteins from our yeast two hybrid screen. We will perform in vivo co-immunoprecipitation assay to identify additional XLG2-interacting proteins which should also help to shed light on the molecular function of XLG2. We will carry out a RNA-Seq experiment designed for genome-wide identification of transcript isoforms which might result from alternative transcription start sites or alternative pre-mRNA splicing. The experiment aims to reveal the possible role of XLG2 in defense-associated promoter switching at the genome scale.

262213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
262213.value: later人體細胞具有為數眾多的異三聚體G蛋白，細胞外信號分子通過結合質膜上的G蛋白偶聯受體和異三聚體G蛋白，將信號傳遞給下遊的效應蛋白並最終產生生理應答。植物如擬南芥中只有極少數基因編碼G蛋白亞基，但G 蛋白仍參與多種植物生物學過程。目前在植物中鮮有G蛋白下遊效應蛋白被鑒定出，對於 G蛋白如何調控各種生物學過程仍然知之甚少。 在擬南芥中除了經典的G亞基GPA1外，還有三個特別的類G-alpha蛋白，分別為XLG1、XLG2和 XLG3。它們的羧基末端與G-alpha相似，而氨基末端的400多個氨基酸殘基只在植物XLG蛋白之間高度保守。之前本研究組鑒定出XLG2作為正調節子調控植物的防衛反應，然而它如何調控防衛反應仍有待於解答。 XLG2定位於細胞核，這不同於其他的主要定位於細胞質的G蛋白。序列分析表明其氨基末端具有一個類PHD/FYVE的鋅指結構域，緊接其後的序列與人類TRIM24蛋白的PHD-Bromo結構域具有相似性，該蛋白通過識別組蛋白修飾來調節轉錄。最近另一個研究組報道，XLG2蛋白能與DNA結合蛋白RTV1相互作用，RTV1和能參與染色體重塑的VRN1蛋白具有相似性。我們還發現，過量表達XLG2導致防衛相關基因異樣轉錄本的富集，這可能是由於使用了選擇性啟動子。本課題組和其他課題組的初步研究表明，XLG2極有可能是通過識別特異的組蛋白修飾，從而選擇不同的防衛相關基因的啟動子來進行轉錄調控的。本研究中我們將運用分子生物學、功能基因組學和遺傳學等方法，試圖闡釋XLG2的功能，以及XLG2介導的信號通路，拓展我們對G蛋白的認識。

262213.label: Realisation of objectives
262213.value: Objective 1. We will carry out detailed molecular characterization of XLG2 protein to reveal whether it binds to modified and/or unmodified histones. We will also determine whether XLG2 undergoes nucleocytoplasmic shuttling in response to pathogen infection and whether XLG2 accumulation is controlled by AtPUB2 and AtPUB4, two E3 ubiquitin ligases which were previously identified as putative XLG2-interacting proteins from our yeast two hybrid screen. It was previously reported that XLG2 is localized in the nucleus. We found that XLG2 and XLG3 are localized both on plasma membrane and the nucleus whereas XLG1 is primarily localized on plasma membrane. Pathogen infection did not lead to an obvious change to their subcellular localization patterns. XLG2 was predicted to have a PHD/FYVE-like zinc finger domain with some similarity to the PHD-Bromo domain of TRIM protein that recognizes modified lysine in histones. It raises a possibility that XLG2 might also interact with histones. We did an in-planta co-immunoprecipitation experiment using transgenic plants expressing XLG2-FLAG-GFP fusion protein. The co-IPed proteins were identified by mass spec. However, histones were not among the pulled-down proteins, arguing against XLG2 being involved in recognizing histones. PUB2 and PUB4, two E3 ligases, were found to interact with XLG2, raising a possibility that PUB2 and PUB4 might act as negative regulators of XLG2 by targeting XLG2 for degradation. If the hypothesis is valid, it is expected that the pub2 pub4 mutant might accumulate a higher level of XLG2. We found that XLG2 level was not significantly changed in the pub2 pub4 mutant. Instead, we found that the pub2 pub4 mutants displayed very similar phenotypes to those of the xlg1/2/3 triple mutant (see the next section), indicating that PUB2 and PUB4 are not negative regulators of XLG proteins. More likely, PUB2 and PUB4 are required for function of XLGs. We found that PUB4 likely catalyzes protein mono-ubiquitination (Wang H et al, 2013, Plant Physiology). Our results suggest that PUB4 might regulate XLG function by mono-ubiquitination. Objective 2. We will perform in vivo co-immunoprecipitation assay to identify additional XLG2-interacting proteins which should also help to shed light on the molecular function of XLG2. We carried out yeast two hybrid screens, co-immunoprecipitation, and BiFC for identification and verification of proteins that interact with XLG1, XLG2, or XLG3. All three XLGs were found to interact with PUB2 and PUB4. However, previously the xlg mutants were not found to show any phenotype similar or opposite to that of pub4, raising a doubt on whether they are involved in the same pathway. The xlg1/2/3 triple mutant previously reported carried an xlg1 weak allele. We obtained an xlg1 knockout allele and used it to generate a new xlg1/2/3 triple mutant. The new triple mutant displays similar phenotypes to those of the pub4 mutant and the pub2 pub4 double mutants, including retarded growth, tapetal cell enlargement, defect in pollen release, and enhanced root growth. These xlg triple mutant and the pub4 mutants were found less sensitive to seedling growth inhibition caused by exogenous cytokinin treatment, indicating that XLGs and PUB4 are required in the cytokinin response. These results were published in a recent Plant Physiology paper (Wang Y et al, 2017) XLG2 was recently reported by another group to interact with RbohD, an enzyme that catalyze production of hydrogen peroxide, to regulate ROS production triggered by pathogen infection. We also found that both XLG2 and XLG3 interact wtih RbohD and the xlg triple mutant is defective in pathogen/elicitor-induced oxidative burst, indicating that the XLGs are required for RbohD and perhaps also other Rboh proteins. Another putative XLG2-interacting protein identified from the co-IP experiment is an arginine-rich splicing factor. The xlg triple mutant was previously found to be slightly more susceptible to P. syringae whereas the pub4 mutant showed no significant difference in pathogen susceptibility compared to wildtype. We pretreated plants with an elicitor such as flg22 to prime the defense response and then infected the plants with P. syringae, the xlg and pub4 mutants showed a defect in the defense response priming: as the mutants were less capable of defending themselves against the pathogen infection compared to wildtype following the priming treatment. This defect might be due to the mutants’ inability to produce ROS triggered by flg22. Objective 3. We will carry out a RNA-Seq experiment designed for genome-wide identification of transcript isoforms which might result from alternative transcription start sites or alternative pre-mRNA splicing. The experiment aims to reveal the possible role of XLG2 in defense-associated promoter switching at the genome scale. XLG2 and XLG3 are localized in the nucleus in addition to plasma membrane, suggesting they have a role in nuclei. We hypothesized that the XLG nuclear function might be related to RNA splicing and/or alternative transcription initiation/termination site selection. Transcriptome sequencing was carried out to test the hypothesis. We used the xlg triple mutant and wildtype plants with or without pathogen infection for extraction of RNA samples for transcriptome sequencing. It was found that in the plants infected with p. syringae, the xlg triple mutant displayed aberrant splicing patterns of many pathogen-responsive genes. In addition, usage of alternative transcription initiation sites were also found for some genes in the xlg mutants. The mechanism on how the xlg mutation alters splicing patterns or transcription initiation site selection remains to be elucidated.

262213.value: • All three XLGs (XLG1, XLG2 and XLG3) were found to physically interact with PUB2 and PUB4 based on the results from the yeast two hybrid screen, BiFC, and in vivo co-immunoprecipitation. • XLG2 and XLG3 are localized on plasma membrane and in nuclei whereas XLG1 is primarily localized on plasma membrane. There is no obvious evidence that their subcellular localizations changed in response to pathogen infection. • The xlg triple mutant displays similar phenotypes to those of the pub4 mutant and the pub2 pub4 double mutants, including retarded growth, tapetal cell enlargement, defect in pollen release, and enhanced root growth. These xlg triple mutant and the pub4 mutants were found less sensitive to seedling growth inhibition caused by exogenous cytokinin treatment, indicating that XLGs and PUB4 are required in the cytokinin response. • The above results were published in Plant Physiology (Wang et al, 2017) • XLG2, XLG3, and PUB4 all form a complex with RbohD. The xlg triple mutant and the pub4 mutant are defective in pathogen/elicitor-induced oxidative burst and in defense priming induced by elicitor (flg22). • Transcriptome sequencing data revealed differences in RNA splicing patterns and transcription initiation site selection for many defense related genes between the xlg triple mutant and wildtype, suggesting a role of XLGs in RNA splicing and transcription initiation site selection.

262213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
262213.value: The XLG proteins have been found to be important players in various developmental and physiological pathways in plants, further expanding the roles of the heterotrimeric G proteins in plant processes. Our findings raise the following questions. 1. How are XLGs involved in RbohD-mediated ROS production?. Our current hypothesis is that following recognition of pathogen by a pattern recognition receptor (such as FLS2), FLS2 activates a kinase (such as BIK1). BIK1 then phosphorylates XLGs which in turn interact with and activate RbohD. 2. The exact role of XLGs in nuclei remains largely unknown. If XLGs are involved in alternative splicing or transcription initiation site selection, what is the underlying mechanism? 3. The xlg mutation causes insensitivity to cytokinin. Again, the underlying mechanism is unknown. Could the defect in the cytokinin response be due to the defect in ROS production?

262213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
262213.value: Many genes in animals encode components of heterotrimeric G proteins and they play very important roles in various physiological and developmental pathways in animals. In plants, there is only a single canonical G-alpha gene. However, plants have three unique G-alpha-like proteins, XLG1, XLG2, and XLG3. The molecular and biological functions of the XLGs remain largely unknown. This project aimed to use genetic, molecular, and genomics approaches to understand the functions of the XLG proteins in plant biological processes. We identified several proteins that interact with XLGs. XLGs and its interacting proteins PUB2 and PUB4 were found to be involved in the response to cytokinin, in tapetum development and male fertility, and in production of reactive oxygen species which plays an important role in plant immunity. XLGs might transduce the defense signaling pathways to regulate gene expression.

289713.value: WRKY轉錄因子防禦機制及擬南芥多倍體的雜種優勢研究

rows: Identification of differentially expressed WRKYs in Arabidopsis allotetraploid and its progenitors in response to biotic stresses
The kinetics of WRKY gene expression changes in related Arabidopsis polyploids and hybrids in response to biotic inducers

289713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
289713.value: Heterosis or hybrid vigor describes the development of superior traits in progeny from crosses between two different species. Although this phenomenon is commonly used for improving yield and quality of agricultural crops, the genetic and molecular mechanisms surrounding hybrid vigor remain elusive. Genetically, several hypotheses have been used to explain the basis of heterosis. This includes the dominance, overdominance, pseudo-overdominance, and epistasis models. In an interspecific cross between a synthetic autotetraploid Arabidopsis thaliana (At4) and a natural autotetraploid Arabidopsis arenosa (Aa), a genome-wide change in gene expression was detected in the synthetic Arabidopsis suecica allotetraploid hybrids (Allo733) when compared to the progenitors. Increased biomass, starch accumulation and disease resistance were observed in Allo733 when compared to its parents. The availability of these related Arabidopsis species and the establishment of the synthetic allotetraploids thus provide an excellent and tractable genetic system for studying the mechanism of hybrid vigor. WRKY transcription factors are a family of plant-specific transcriptional regulators involved in diverse plant signaling pathways such as pathogen responses, abiotic stress responses, seed development and senescence processes. The ability of plants to develop multiple interconnected pathways to cope with the constant changes of environments and to fend off their attackers is vital for their successful survival and propagation. Therefore, modulation of defense regulatory pathways could contribute to the improved vigor in the allotetraploids. The goal of the proposed research is elucidate the molecular mechanism of heterosis through studying the evolution and modulation of WRKY factors upon genome divergence and hybridization in the related Arabidopsis autotetraploids and allotetraploids. To achieve this, we will first examine the kinetics of WRKY expression in the related Arabidopsis species and allotetraploids. The epigenetic and genetic control of WRKY genes expression upon biotrophic pathogen (Pseudomonas syringae) or chemical (salicylic acid) treatment over different time intervals will be analyzed. Using biochemical and genetic approaches, we will further dissect possible protein-protein or protein-DNA interactions among homologous AtWRKY and AaWRKY factors or between WRKYs and their target promoters. The proposed studies are expected to provide insights to the mechanisms of heterosis and further our understanding in the modulations of defense response pathways in allotetraploid hybrids. In addition, knowledge gained will have potential application in crop biotechnology. 雜種優勢泛指兩個不同物種之間的雜交後代能發展出優良性狀。這種現象廣泛應用於提高農作物產量和質量，然而其遺傳分子機制仍是有待商榷。在基因遺傳學上，數個假說被應用來解釋雜種優勢的機製,包括顯性、不完全顯性、偽顯性、以及上位性模型。由合成四倍體 Arabidopsis thaliana（At4）與天然四倍體 Arabidopsis arenosa（Aa）所合成的擬南芥異源四倍體(Allo733)中，其基因表達變化可從基因組層面上檢測獲得。相比其親本，Allo733有較高生物量，澱粉積累和抗病能力。這些相關的擬南芥物種及其合成異源四倍體研究為雜種優勢的機理提供了優秀和較易掌握的遺傳系統。WRKY轉錄因子隸屬植物具專特性的轉錄調控因子家族之一，它們涉及信號轉導，這包括病原體反應、非生物脅迫反應、種子發育和衰老等過程。植物能演變出多個相互關聯的途徑以應對不斷變化的環境與及攻擊者，這對植物能成功生存以及繁殖有著重要的角色。因此，調節防禦機理可對異源四倍體的作出貢獻。本研究目的建議通過研究擬南芥同源四倍體和異源四倍體之間的WRKY轉錄因子的演化及調製，從而箇中闡明雜種優勢的分子機理。在實踐時，我們首先監定WRKY轉錄因子在相關的擬南芥物種和其四倍體中表達的動力學。在表觀遺傳和遺傳學上，通過植物病原假單胞菌(Pseudomonas syringae)以及化學(水楊酸)處理，繼而分析WRKY轉錄因子在不同時段的表達變化。使用生化和遺傳的途徑，我們將進一步解剖其潛在蛋白質與蛋白質(同源AtWRKY和AaWRKY因子)，以及其蛋白質與DNA(WRKYs和它們的目標啟動子)之間的相互作用。此研究建議預計將為我們對雜種優勢的機制提供進一步的知識，並讓我們對異源四倍體在防衛機制上有更一步的了解。再者，所獲得的知識將對農作物之生物技術上有著潛在的應用價值。

289713.label: Realisation of objectives
289713.value: The overall goal of this project is to use an Arabidopsis polyploid system to gain new insights to genome interaction and heterosis in plant defense. The two specific objectives are: (1) Identification of differentially expressed WRKYs in Arabidopsis allotetraploid and its progenitors in response to biotic stresses; and (2) The kinetics of WRKY gene expression changes in related Arabidopsis polyploids and hybrids in response to biotic inducers. During the project period, we have identified several WRKY transcription factors that showed differential expression and responses against the bacterial pathogen, Pseudomonas syringae (Pst). These included the group I WRKY33, three closely related group IIa WRKYs (WRKY18, WRKY40, WRKY60), the group IIb WRKY6 and group III WRKY53. In addition to Pst treatment, we have also further characterized the effect of salicylic acid (SA) on the expression dynamics of WRKY 18, 40, 60 respectively. Among these identified WRKYs genes, we have decided to focus on the three closely related WRKY18, 40 and 60 and performed additional analyses in characterizing the mechanisms and their contribution to improved defense responses in the Arabidopsis allotetraploids. Achievements of project objectives To summarize the major findings for the projects, we have quantified and compared the growth performance of the related Arabidopsis polyploids (A. thaliana, A. arenosa and A. suecica). Consistent with their growth phenotypes, the resynthesized A. suecica allotetraploids (Allo) showed an overall higher growth performance and resistance against Pst infection when compared to either of the parents. Since WRKY transcription factors are one of the major regulators for transcriptional reprogramming during plant defense, we have thus investigated their expression among these Arabidopsis polyploids. Among the WRKY transcription factors, the closely related WRKY18, 40 and 60 have been shown to share redundant but important roles in defense. WRKY18 was found differentially expressed between A. thaliana (At4) and A. arenosa (Aa) while additive expression was evident in the Allo. Expression of WRKY40 was similar among all tetraploid species. In contrast, differential expression (between At4 and Aa) and non-additive repression (in Allo) patterns were observed for WRKY60. Upon infection with Pst, a rapid non-additive induction of WRKY18 and WRKY40 expression was detected in the allotetraploids when compared to the progenitors. Slower induction kinetics and lower induction peaks were observed for these WRKYs in the progenitors when compared to the allotetraploids. In contrast, WRKY60 showed higher induction kinetics in At4 than in Aa or Allo. Moreover, although WRKY60 was induced upon pathogen challenge in the allotetraploids, it is non-additively repressed when compared to the progenitors. In addition to Pst treatment, plants were treated with 1mM SA and similar rapid induction of WRKY18 and WRKY40 was observed in the allotetraploids at 2 hours post treatment (hpt). In At4, WRKY60 was differentially induced and expressed after 8 hpt when compared to Aa. The expression of WRKY60, however, was not induced in the allotetraploids or in Aa upon SA treatment. Therefore, these data suggested a more rapid induction of WRKY18 and WRKY40 in the allotetraploids when compared to its progenitors under stress conditions. To elucidate the relative expression of the homoeologous WRKY alleles upon the treatments in the allotetraploids, a cleaved amplified polymorphic sequences (CAPS) analysis was used. Upon Pst or SA treatment, both AtWRKY18 and AtWRKY60 were found to express at a higher level when compared to their Aa homoeologs in the allotetraploids. In contrast, AaWRKY40 showed a higher expression when compared to the AtWRKY40 allele in the allotetraploids. Since PATHOGENESIS-RELATED1 (PR1) is a common marker for SA responsive gene, its expression dynamics was also compared among the related tetraploid species. Under normal condition, PR1 is differentially expressed between At4 and Aa and non-additively repressed in the allotetraploids. Upon SA treatment, differential expression and upregulation of PR1 expression was observed between At4 and Aa. Although PR1 expression is lower in the Allo when compared to At4, non-additive upregulation of PR1 was observed in the allotetraploids when compared to the MPV. Moreover, when compared the PR1 expression fold change upon SA treatment, a higher and faster PR1 induction was observed in the Allo and it peaked at 8 hpt. In contrast, both At4 and Aa showed a lower and a delayed PR1 induction that peaked at 12 hpt. Therefore, these data supported a rapid induction of WRKYs and PR1 in the allotetraploids could contribute to the improved defense when compared to the progenitors. The observed preferential expression of WRKYs could help to modulate defense-signaling pathways through differential affinity/ strength of protein-protein interactions occurred in trans, hence transcriptome in the hybrids. Therefore, we assayed the homodimeric and heterodimeric interactions among these WRKYs using an in vitro split-LUC complementation assay by transiently expressing combinations of N-LUC and C-LUC fusion of the target WRKY in tobacco. Results showed that preferential cis-¬homodimer (e.g. AtWRKY18-AtWRKY18 > AtWRKY18-AaWRKY18) and trans-heterodimer (e.g. AtWRKY18-AaWRKY40 > AtWRKY18-AtWRKY40) formations exist between WRKY18 and WRKY40. These preferential protein-protein interactions are consistent with the observed preferential homoeologous alleles expression in the allotetraploids upon Pst or SA treatment. In addition, AaWRKY60 showed a preferential heterodimeric interaction with either WRKY18 or WRKY40 when compared to AtWRKY60. Moreover, when transiently expressed these combinations of split-LUC constructs in the corresponding wrky18 or wrky40 mutant in A. thaliana, consistent with their preferential interactions, the cis-homodimer (e.g. AtWRKY18-AtWRKY18) induced a higher level of PR1 expression than the corresponding trans-interacting homodimer (e.g. AtWRKY18-AaWRKY18). Therefore, these data support an alleles regulation and interaction model for improved defense in the allotetraploids. The differential regulation, expression kinetics and preferential interaction of the homoeologous alleles from the two parental genomes in the allotetraploids act in concert to shape the transcriptome for improved defense signalling. By understanding the preferential WRKYs expression and interactions, it could guide the selection of parental lines in molecular breeding. Conclusions In summary, we have achieved the aims outlined in both project objectives and have identified several WRKY candidate genes that showed differential expression in the Arabidopsis allotetraploids under biotic stresses when compared to the two progenitors. Moreover, further investigations of the selected WRKY18, 40 and 60 in terms of their protein-protein interactions and functional consequences (on PR1 expression) have provided further insights to the contribution of homoeologous alleles expression and interaction towards improved defense responses in the allotetraploids. In addition to presentations at international conferences, a manuscript is being prepared for publication to conclude the findings from the funded projects.

289713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
289713.value: For further development, we have since submitted a proposal to extend our research effort in characterizing the growth performance and defense in the resynthesized allotetraploids at physiological level. Once these physiological parameters are established, they will facilitate the identification of important components or pathways contributing to the heterotic phenotypes development in the allotetraploids at the molecular level. Since we have showed that the homoeologous WRKY18 and WRKY40 were preferentially expressed in the allotetraploids upon Pst-induced stress and SA treatment as well as their preferential interaction in transient assays, we will extend our research to further elucidate their roles in mediating the gene regulatory networks in Arabidopsis upon stresses by creating “hybrid mimic” lines through expressing the homoeologous proteins in A. thaliana. ChIP-seq and RNA-seq will be used to characterize the altered regulatory networks mediated by the preferential trans-heterodimers between AtWRKY18 and AaWRKY40 at a genome-wide scale. Results obtained will provide further mechanistic insights into the role of homoeologous genomes interactions in hybrids and their contribution to improved disease resistance in allotetraploids.

289713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
289713.value: Most domesticated crop species were created as hybrids for superior and desirable traits. However, with climate changes and global warming, the development of new hybrids is essential to ensure food security. When two genomes of related species are brought together in the hybrids, epigenetic and genetic change at the genome level could affect their overall developmental programming. In addition, allele expression from the two parental genomes in the hybrids could alter downstream protein-protein interactions and transcriptional outputs. The results obtained from this research project have provided a molecular mechanism behind improved defense responses in hybrids by studying the expression and protein-protein interaction among members that belong to a class of important transcription factors (WRKY) with major roles in plant defense. In plant breeding, one of the major goals is to increase disease resistance of plants for better yield and performance under different environmental conditions. Through understanding the preferential WRKYs expression and interactions that are beneficial for altering downstream targets for better defense, it could guide the selection of parental lines (different cultivars) in molecular breeding for hybrid crops.

291213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
291213.value: 一家公司的股票，除了在本國股市上市交易外，也在海外市場掛牌交易，稱之為異地上市。異地上市的益處很多，包括可以進入更大和更深的資本市場，分散股權，增加股票流動性等。一般來說，異地上市的股票是先在不發達的市場上市，再到發達市場譬如美國上市。但是，近幾年來，不少公司先後在美國自願除牌，也有一些公司是先在發逹的海外市場上市，再回過頭來在本國股市逆向掛牌上市。 在本研究裡，我們會關注兩個逆向上市的獨特個案：中國公司首先在香港上市，然後再回頭內地Ａ股市場上市；以色列公司先在美國交易所上市，後來又回到持拉維夫交易所上市。 我們會研究逆向異地上市會不會對現有的海外股東產生負面影響。集中關注率先上市的海外市場，可以讓我們從另一個角度審視異地上市的益處。具體來講，我們會研究股價的長期表現，看逆向異地上市會不會影響現有股東財富，以及公司的營運狀況是否會改善。我們也會研究公司逆向異地上市是否因財政緊拙所造成。接下來，我們會集中研究公司逆向異地上市後兩點：一，股價是否更具訊息，以及股票在海外市場的流動性有否改變；二，股票異地上市後，海外市場的整體市場效率有否改變。 本研究涵蓋了美國，香港，中國大陸和以色列四個市場。本研究預計會有兩大政策上的啟示：一，本地的市場再小，也會有存在價值，不會為海外大的資本市場所吞噬；二，如果逆向異地上市是受負面因素，如享受海外上市地位的溢價或逃避本地嚴厲的法規監管等推動，那麼，逆向異地上市不但會對海外市場的股東，而且也會對本地市場的股東產生負面效應。

291213.label: Major findings and research outcome
291213.value: We study how the information and trading environments of Hong Kong-listed Chinese companies (H-share firms) change once the companies return to the China A-share markets for listing. We examine the stock price synchronicity, liquidity commonality, and stock liquidity after dual-listing and investigate three channels related to possible changes. We find that added A-share analyst coverage influences the stock liquidity, but not the price synchronicity or liquidity commonality. Moreover, Qualified Direct Institutional Investors’ trading affects price synchronicity, liquidity commonality, and stock liquidity while Qualified Foreign Institutional Investors’ trading affects price synchronicity and liquidity commonality, but not stock liquidity.

291213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
291213.value: Our study contributes to the literature on cross-listing by investigating the changes in information and trading quality in the setting of Chinese A- and H- dual-listed firms, where firms first list on the developed Hong Kong market and then dual-list on the less developed domestic A-share market. Our study also has implications for financial-market regulators. In addition to dual-listings of H-share firms in China, the QFII and QDII programs and the Shanghai–Hong Kong Stock Connect have been opened to allow limited cross-market access. Regulators generally take trading volume and market liquidity as indicators of the market’s development, researchers raise concerns over the close connection between Hong Kong and China’s stock markets. Although it is always contended that market integration should lead to more efficient information flow by allowing investors to trade and engage in arbitrage more economically in different markets, our study reveals another side of the story. Market integration may result in more trading, more trading does not necessarily lead to a more efficient market. If market liquidity stems from a decrease in informed trading, the market’s reputation will deteriorate in the long run.

292113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
292113.value: 由看似無關的事情引起的一種情緒，可以於服務失誤的情況下影響消費者的歸因傾向嗎？二零一二年九月十日，日本政府宣佈從「私人業主」手中購買尖閣列島，引發中日之間的衝突及敵意。中國民眾的憤怒於全國可見；民眾砸壞日本汽車，到日本大使館外抗議，甚至任何對日本的提及都予以怒火。從北京市工商局的最近資料中，可看到消費者對各行業的投訴數字於二零一二年九月有顯著的上升，達到1605封投訴信件，而二零一二年八月只有 1129封投訴信件。(來源: http://www.baic.gov.cn) 同樣地，導致福島核電廠嚴重損毀的東日本大地震，可能對消費者歸因傾向的影響格局具有平行的效果。九級地震與隨之而來的海嘯，令核電廠反應堆的冷卻系統失效，導致核幅射洩漏及核電廠三十公里範圍內成立起疏散區。中國民眾對核幅射洩漏感到驚慌失措，很多人囤積基本物資以應付日後可能出現的食物短缺及安全問題。我們取得了北京市工商局在二零一一年初的投訴資料。有趣地，資料顯示於地震發生後左右投訴數字顯著下降，可比較二零一一年二月的6741宗投訴，以及二零一一年四月的5390宗投訴。(來源: http://www.baic.gov.cn) 我們推測，尖閣列島事件誘發的憤怒情緒增加了消費者歸咎日本公司的傾向。但是，福島核電廠事故引發的恐懼就可能減少了消費者歸咎公司的傾向。如果這些直觀推論為真，它們顯示出由無關的事情引起的偶然性情緒，能夠影響消費者於服務失誤當中的歸因傾向。我們認為這項潛在的發現能夠提高我們對消費者對服務失誤的反應的認識，以及拓寬我們對情緒在服務情形中角色的知識。這項建議中的研究將會探討這兩項重要議題。 根據認知評估論，我們提出兩個常見偶然性情緒（憤怒及恐懼）可產生不同的歸因傾向。具體來說，一位憤怒的旁觀者，在觀察一宗影響另外一位消費者的服務失誤時，會更可能歸咎於服務提供者（即公司）；而一位恐懼的旁觀者，在觀察一宗影響另外一位消費者的服務失誤時，會更可能歸咎於受影響的消費者（即該名遭遇服務失誤的消費者）。而且，應對策略將會作為情緒對歸因傾向影響的中介變數。雖然真實市場數據為我們的論點提供了初步支持，我們將提出五項研究以進一步測試我們的建議。

292113.label: Realisation of objectives
292113.value: Most research on the effects of emotional reactions to a misfortune assumes that attributions of responsibility for the event (either to oneself, to others, or to the external circumstances) elicit different emotional reactions and that these reactions determine behavior. In contrast, there are possibility that attributions are often a consequence of people’s emotional reactions to a situation rather than a determinant of them. For example, individuals who happen to feel angry at the time they have a negative experience may attribute the cause of the experience to others and this attribution may stimulate action against the perpetrator. In contrast, individuals who experience fear might be uncertain about the cause of the event and to feel out of control, leading them to avoid the situation rather than confronting it. The effects of these emotional reactions may occur independently of the events that have risen to them. We investigated this possibility. In the situations we considered, participants were induced to feel either angry or fearful at the time they encountered a service failure. We found that persons who felt angry would attribute responsibility for the situation to the service provider and that this attribution would lead them to register a complaint against the provider. In contrast, we found that people who experienced fear at the time they encountered the situation would be uncertain of the cause of the event, decreasing their likelihood of complaining. We also found the moderating role of cognitive load for the proposed effect, which provided further support for our conceptualization and advances our understanding of incidental emotions.

292113.label: Major findings and research outcome
292113.value: Consumers’ incidental emotional state at the time they encounter a service failure can affect their likelihood of complaining about the failure and their willingness to patronize the service provider again. Whereas incidental anger increases consumers’ disposition to complain about a service failure, incidental fear leads them to react less negatively to the service failure than they otherwise would. This was true both when a service failure was personally experienced, and when it was only observed. These effects are mediated by the impact of incidental emotions on cognitive appraisals of the situation, and moderated by the cognitive load among the consumers.

292113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
292113.value: Prior research (Keltner, Gruenfeld, & Anderson, 2003) indicated that different power levels were associated with the incidental emotions of anger and fear. That is, people with high power tend to become angry easily, whereas people with low power more easily become fearful. It is conceivable that people with high power are relatively more likely to blame the service provider in service failures that they experience or observe. Several factors (e.g., social status, company-customer relationships) can lead to different levels of consumer power. To this extent, the proposed investigations suggest service failure recovery strategies that managers might use to deal with different types of consumers. Furthermore, many studies have found that both music and color can arouse different emotions (e.g., Schulkind, Hennis, & Rubin, 1999; Valdez & Mehrabian, 1994). Based on similar logic, it is possible that environmental settings such as music and color would lead to consumer emotions arousal and this would potentially influence their perception toward a service failure. This would be an interesting direction for future research.

292113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
292113.value: Customers’ disposition to register a formal complaint about an inferior product or poor service is often mediated by attributions of responsibility. However, the anger or fear that people happen to be experiencing for totally irrelevant reasons can also influence this disposition. Two field studies and four laboratory experiments indicate that when people feel angry at the time they encounter a service failure, they are more likely to blame the service provider for the failure and more likely to register a complaint. When they experience fear, however, they are uncertain about the cause of their misfortune and decrease their negative reactions relative to conditions in which fear is not experienced. The effects of these incidental emotions are evident both when a service failure is personally experienced and when it is only observed. These effects are eliminated, however, when individuals do not have the cognitive resources available to assess the reasons for the service failure and the conditions surrounding it.

292313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
292313.value: Teams are critical to an organization’s success, especially in modern day Hong Kong. But teams today must also be creative. Indeed, creativity is recognized as a critical means to create meaningful, lasting value for organizations and their stakeholders in today’s dynamic environment (Zhou & Shalley, 2008). Knowing how to increase and to sustain creativity is a challenge for project leaders and supervisors, and many teams fail to realize their full potential. An important ingredient in team creativity, hitherto under-explored, is emotion. Amabile and her associates (2005) have showed that creative attempts are emotionally charged. Sometimes team members working together feel inspired and experience new and useful insights, but they may also get stuck and feel frustration and even hostility during their interactions. The questions that we address in this research are: What are the emotional processes underlying team creativity? How can team leaders help to translate emotion into energy for team creativity? How can they help team members to work collectively for creative synergy? Although there is increasing interest in exploring how emotions in teams may serve as assets or liabilities for team creativity, the existing literature is piecemeal and has yielded mixed results. Moreover, neither emotion nor creativity is stable over time. Much of the existing research uses cross-sectional survey designs or one-time experiments which preclude the study of temporal variation in emotions and creativity within teams over time. We know from our earlier research (To, Fisher, Ashkanasy & Rowe, 2012) that moods account for some of the variation in how creative individuals are from day to day. Like individuals, teams may have good days and bad days in terms of how they feel and how creative they are. The purpose of the research outlined in this proposal is to explore dynamic relationships between collective emotion and team creativity, together with a unique set of boundary conditions hypothesized to condition whether teams turn their emotional energy to creative purposes. We will employ Experience Sampling Methodology and multilevel modeling to study dynamic team processes over time. In summary, teams are not always at their creative best. Understanding how team creativity varies over time, and the factors affecting these fluctuations, provides a lever for leaders and managers to capitalize on emotion as a resource for improving creative performance. 在隊工中如何充份發揮團隊創意是一個重要的課題。有時候，隊員合作無間，互相啓迪激勵，創意如泉；有時候，合作出現分歧，甚或敵對。創意過程充滿高高低低，也充滿喜怒哀樂。如何能把隊員的情緒轉化為創意的能量，正是這研究項目的主要目的。現存有關情緒和創意的文獻大多零散，其中不乏矛盾的研究結果。我們的目標是探求團隊情緒如何影響隊員的創作力: 在何種情况情感可化作創意之能量；何時情感反成負累? 我們將採用"經驗樣本方法學" 來研究在團隊中情緒和創意的互動。

292313.label: Realisation of objectives
292313.value: Our first objective was to propose and test an integrative framework regarding the link between group affect and team creativity. This objective has been fully achieved in three aspects together. First, an earlier theoretical paper based on our GRF proposal has been presented in the symposium of “Innovation and Creativity in Teams” at the Academy of Management Conference (Orlando, 2013). The audiences including a few leading scholars in the research area found our work to be interesting, and we received useful feedback from them for our idea development. Second, a conceptual paper (To, M. L., Tse, H. H.M., & Ashkanasy, N. M. 2015. A multilevel model of transformational leadership, affect, and creative processes in work teams. Leadership Quarterly, 26: 543-556) has been published in the Leadership Quarterly. In this paper, we propose an integrative multilevel framework of the links between affect and creativity in teams. A core proposition of our model is to explain how group affect may trigger creative processes in teams, and how leadership behavior may moderate the relationships. This addresses an important, yet understudied, phenomenon at work. Third, a total of three empirical studies have been conducted in order to test the affective influences on team creativity. Please see the details below. Our second objective was to investigate the conditional indirect effects of group affect on team creativity via task elaboration. Based on existing conceptualization and operationalization, we developed and validated a scale of task elaboration evidence from three empirical studies. Item examples are available upon request. First, a longitudinal survey (Study 1) of our project has been completed. This study involved over 50 student project teams with over 300 team members. Participants were working on a required semester-long team project in which creativity – generation of novel and useful ideas to a problem – was set as a key requirement for assessment. To collect the longitudinal data with the repeated measures, we obtained four weekly reports on group affect, task elaboration, and self-reported team creativity during each week. This design helped to capture the most meaningful weekly team experiences and interactions and variation of these experiences over time. Moderator variables (such as identification, reflexivity, transactive memory system, and etc) were also measured in the one-off survey of this study. A second study (with 105 student project teams) was conducted. These project teams were working on a research project required by a research method course. Again, this study involved group affect, task elaboration, moderators ( (such as identification, reflexivity, transactive memory system, and etc), and team creativity. In this study, we obtained external ratings of team creativity. A third study (involving 65 R&D teams in China) was conducted. This was also an longitudinal survey with the multi-wave multi-source design. As in the first two studies, this third study involved group affect, task elaboration, moderators, and team creativity. In this study, we also obtained external ratings of team creativity. These three studies come together provided meaningful results in support for conditional indirect effects of group affect on team creativity via task elaboration. An earlier manuscript was submitted to the Academy of Management Journal, and we received useful feedback from reviewers. Based on the feedback, we are working on a new paper version targeted at the Journal of Applied Psychology. In this regard, we consider a substantial achievement (80%) of Objective 2. Our third objective was to provide insights for scholars and practitioners to better understand team dynamics, and how to capitalize on group affect as a resource to foster creativity in teams. As mentioned in our previously progress projects, we had extended our work to consider the effects of different manifestations of group affect. Specifically, informed by our research discoveries and advice from an additional co-author (well known as a leading scholars in the area), we extended our scope to consider the two core manifestations of group affect. Specifically, we investigated not only the influence of group affective tone (mean affect shared by individual members) but also group affect diversity (variance of individual members' feelings). The manifestations of group affect are expected to explain group dynamics and team creativity more comprehensively. In our working paper mentioned above, we found support that mean group affect interacted with group affect diversity to influence team creativity via a team process. This indirect effect was moderated by team context (i.e., transactive memory structure). This provides insights for scholars and practitioners who wish to understand team dynamics more comprehensively, and how to capitalize on group affect to increase team creativity. Together with the progress made for Objective 1 and 2, Objective 3 is considered completed in this regard.

292313.label: Major findings and research outcome
292313.value: The increasing popularity of project/group-based structures in organizations is due to their value in delivering timely and creative outputs, though not every project team lives up to these expectations. Project teams often lack an established approach to guide member interactions and knowledge sharing, though team creativity requires the exchange of unique or even opposing information and perspectives among team members. It is not surprising that creative processes are full of ups and downs, and are charged with and by emotions. In some occasions, team members may converge into similar or homogeneous feelings (e.g., all feel excited!). In some other occasions, members can feel quite diversely from each other, with some feeling enthused and positive and others feeling worried or disheartened. Given such a scenario, the question arises as to how members’ feelings (convergence and divergence) might be related to project teams’ creativity. Why are some project teams able to harness the resources and energy associated with positive and negative affect to improve team processes and creative output, while other teams fail to do so? Our research based on our GRF proposal contributes to answer the above questions. Specifically, in our working paper under preparation (see Part C), we demonstrated that group affect (i.e., the interaction of affective convergence and affective divergence) played a role in promoting team creativity via enhanced task elaboration (members' exchange, discussion, and integration of task-relevant knowledge and information). This paper also contributes to understanding of the boundary conditions of the mediated relationships. This paper is targeted at the Journal of Applied Psychology. Moreover, in our conceptual paper published in the Leadership Quarterly (please see Part C), we put forward a multilevel view of research on affect and creativity in teams and to address how contextual factors (leadership behaviors) may moderate the affect-creative process relationships at different levels. By conceptualizing affect and creative behavior as multilevel constructs embedded in teams, this integrative model is important because it explains how the affect-creative process relationship can coexist at multilevel. This holds potential to provide a deeper understanding as to produce performance in team creativity ultimately. Finally, the longitudinal approach we adopted in two studies (see Section 5.3 above) has the potential to demonstrate the temporally dynamic, varying nature of group affect and its relationship to variation in creativity within project teams over time. This addresses calls to move beyond the “group statics” approach to true group dynamics.

292313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
292313.value: We note that the correlational design we used does not allow definitive conclusions about causal relationships between group affect, team processes, and team creativity. However, support for a causal impact of affect on creativity can be found in decades of laboratory research in which affect has been manipulated and subsequent creativity measured. Although our predictions draw on this body of theory and are consistent with these mechanisms, we admit that the affect-creativity links can be reciprocal. For example, while a negative group affect may boost members' collective effort to be creative, a successful progress of team creativity could also help to produce a positive state shared by the members. In this sense, team creativity is a collective affect-regulation mechanism that might help to shift a negative group affect to the positive one. That is, being creative collectively may serve to enhance members' collective emotional wellbeing, which may in turn increase teams' sustainable creativity and performance. Future research may extend our work to investigate the reciprocity.

292313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
292313.value: Collaborative efforts of members in project teams are recognized as an important creative asset for organizations. Promoting joint efforts to achieve creative outcomes is a challenge, especially given that team creative efforts are often emotionally-laden. We know that people prefer to work with similar others who share their feelings, so promoting a shared feeling among group members would seem, at least on the surface, to help team functioning including creativity. However, maintaining emotional convergence over time (such as keeping every project member happy) is perhaps not managerially practical and may in fact rob teams of valuable resources or increase the chances of groupthink. Our work suggests that, under the right conditions, diverse affective states among team members may also benefit team creativity. As our work suggests, whether group affect (homogeneity and/or heterogeneity) may increase team creativity or not depends on team contexts and resources (e.g., team reflexivity, a team's knowledge structure, etc) that help teams manage their affective dynamics. With effective resources in operation, team members may translate their affective energy and resources into creative breakthrough through the process of task elaboration, i.e., a task-focused process of idea exchange and integration among team members.

292413.label: Project Objectives
292413.value: Build upon the conventional predictive regression model, we improve on the existing estimation methods when the predictive regressor follows stationary first-order autoregressive process where its innovation is correlated with the innovation in the predictive regression. Due to the success of autoregressive approximation as shown in theory and simulation results in approximating a wide class of time series processes, we extend the conventional predictive regression models by allowing the predictive regressor to follow processes that are either stationary, nonstationary or long memory with or without breaks. Distribution of the t-statistic for the coefficient of the predictive variable will be derived. Its size and power will be compared with the existing test statistics through simulation. The performance of our estimators will be illustrated through theoretical proof, a set of Monte Carlo studies in which the predictive variables follow various kind of processes, two simulation settings that mimic annual and monthly excess stock return, and empirical studies using the data in Welch and Goyal (2008).

292413.value: 「預測回歸」 是一個時間序列的回歸︰用滯後時間序列的變量去解釋另一個變量。此等回歸常用於金融回報預測及其變量的預測性。例子包括用落後的股息收益率來預測股權溢價使。傳統的估算方法都會導致係數的估計不準確︰原本可能不相關的變量變成相關。當樣本不大而且滯後變量是比較有高度持久性的時候，這個情況尤其嚴重。此項目提出一個以「科克倫 - 奧克特」的系統為基礎嶄新的估計方法去估計「預測回歸」中的係數。這個估計方法有三個優點。第一，無論變量是靜止的，非平穩的或有長期記憶過程的，它都能準確估計係數。第二，就算時間序列裡有大轉變，此方法也能處理。第三，這個估計方法很簡單，用的只是對「預測回歸」的殘餘作出「自回歸過程」的分析，其序可以一般的信息標準選擇。我們比較了三個方法。第一，用「科克倫 - 奧克特」方法去掉滯後變量內的序列相關性，並把它的殘餘也放在「預測回歸」中。第二，若雙方變量都是非平穩的，就直接用「科克倫 - 奧克特」方法於「預測回歸」中，去掉雙方的序列相關性。第三，可兩度用「科克倫 - 奧克特」方法方法於「預測回歸」中。由於係數的t統計量隨t分佈，一般應用者都很容易做此類分析。一系列模擬金融數據特性的蒙特卡洛研究亦支持這項方法。我們將會比較其他方法的表現並用以預測股權溢價。

292513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
292513.value: Both strategy and entrepreneurship research has documented the importance of social networks to the survival and growth of new ventures (e.g., Baum et al., 2000; Stuart et al., 1999; Yli-Renko et al., 2001). It is through these networks that new ventures acquire information and resources to shape a firm’s strategic choices and mobilize resources conducive to the firm’s growth. However, extant studies have primarily taken a static view and considered a firm’s networks more as given, rarely discussing how networks develop and evolve. Organizational lifecycle theory suggests that as firms progress from emergence toward growth, they require new and additional resources to support continued expansion (Churchill & Lewis, 1983; Dodge et al., 1994). This dynamic nature of firm resource needs suggests that a more dynamic approach to understanding the firm’s social networks is required. Only with such a dynamic view, entrepreneurs can understand how their firms can better respond to the changing competitive environment and how to increase their firms’ success possibility. To fill the gap, this project is designed to conduct a longitudinal study on the evolution of social networks in new ventures with three specific research objectives. First, based on both qualitative and quantitative examination, we hope to map out the evolution of a new venture’s social networks from its emergence. We propose that along the growth of a new venture its networks tend to evolve from path-dependent towards intentionally managed ones (Hite & Hesterly, 2001). Second, to address the bottom-line importance of firms’ network transition, we will take lead to operationalize new ventures’ path-dependent and intentionally managed networks and examine the effect of timely network transition on venture performance. Finally, we aim to integrate the research about entrepreneurship and social networks to identify and test a group of key entrepreneurial and strategic contextual factors that facilitate the network evolution. Our research will make multiple contributions. It will enrich entrepreneurship literature by identifying the evolution pattern of new ventures’ networks and testing the proposed impact of such evolution on venture performance. This project will also extend social networks literature by taking a dynamic view of firm networks, and methodologically contribute to the literature by proposing and validating measures of path-dependent and intentionally managed networks. More importantly, it will pay attention to the factors fostering the evolution of firm networks, while the antecedents of firm networks in general have been underdeveloped in the social network literature. 戰略和創業領域的研究都強調了社會網路對新創企業生存和發展的重要性 (e.g., Baum et al., 2000; Stuart et al., 1999; Yli-Renko et al., 2001) 。新創企業通過這些社會網路獲取其戰略選擇所依賴的資訊和資源，也通過調動這些資源促進企業的成長。然而，現有研究主要採取了一種靜態觀點，常常將企業的社會網路當作已知事實，很少討論社會網路是如何發展和演化的。組織生命週期理論認為，企業在從創立到發展的過程中需要通過獲取新的、額外的資源來支持其持續擴張(Churchill & Lewis, 1983; Dodge et al., 1994) 。企業資源需求的這種動態本質要求我們從更加動態的視角來理解企業的社會網路。這種動態的視角可以説明創業者瞭解企業如何能更好地應對不斷變化的競爭環境以及如何提高企業成功的可能性。 為了填補這一研究空白，本研究將開展關於新創企業社會網路演化的縱向研究。本研究的目標有三個：首先，基於定性和定量檢驗，我們希望能夠描繪出一家新創企業從創立開始其社會網路的演化。我們認為，隨著一家新創企業的發展，它的社會網路傾向於從‘路徑依賴’型向‘蓄意管理’型演化（Hite & Hesterly，2001）。第二，為了探討公司網路轉變對企業績效的重要性，我們將率先操作化新創企業的‘路徑依賴’型和‘蓄意管理’型網路，並檢驗前者向後者的及時轉變對企業績效的影響。最後，我們將整合有關創業和社會網路方面的研究，針對影響二者間轉化的一些關鍵的創業和戰略因素展開實證分析。 本研究的貢獻體現在幾個方面。通過識別新創企業的社會網路演化路徑和檢驗這種演化對企業績效可能產生的影響，本研究將豐富有關創業的文獻。本研究也將推進和延展社會網路的相關研究：理論方面我們從動態的視角研究企業網路，實證方面我們提出並將驗證‘路徑依賴’和‘蓄意管理’兩種型態的網路。更為重要的是，本研究將會關注促進企業網路演化的因素，這將極大彌補目前社會網路研究中關於企業網路前因研究的不足。

292513.label: Realisation of objectives
292513.value: As explained in the mid-term report, according to the reviewers’ comments and considering the time constraints and budget limit, the major goals of the project have been turned to the study of intra-team network development within the TMTs, rather than the social networks of the firm as originally proposed. This is confirmed with the information collected from our preliminary study done with some founding teams who consistently highlight the critical role of founding teams in the evolution of the new ventures and the even more important role taken by the CEOs who lead the TMT in making all strategic decisions that determine the direction of the ventures. Actually, both qualitative data and literature review results support our view on the importance of examining the dynamics of social networks embedded in the founding teams. We do make some good progress in studying the interrelationships among TMT members including their coordination in teamwork, their consensus and how the team leader and team structure impact the TMT process which in turn influence the TMT effectiveness as well as the overall performance of new ventures. With the second round survey data collected, we are able to go for more in-depth analysis of the TMT dynamics, CEO’s role in initiating and facilitating the TMT coordination work in promoting the growth of the new ventures. With the try of unpacking the micro-mechanism of this CEO-TMT dynamics, we also consider other traits of the CEO and TMT members that facilitate the emergence or cultivation of such CEO roles to make the ventures successful. Overall, with the revised objectives, we are able to thoroughly examine how the CEO-TMT interface impacts the TMT effectiveness and finally the new venture success. With the two round survey data, we are able to test on our proposed theoretical model based on the relational view, to unpack the influence of a novel CEO trait, i.e., CEO tertius iungens orientation, in improving the coordination among TMT members and enhancing their work efficiency through communicating more and engaging in multi-tasking (i.e., polychronicity). We are also able to take further look at an important team dynamics, i.e., TMT strategic consensus, and analyze it impacts the decision makings by the TMT which finally determines the firm innovation. In summary, we believe our successful completion of the project by achieving all these goals help to add to the knowledge of CEO/TMT, from both micro- and macro- perspective, in entrepreneurial firms.

292513.label: Major findings and research outcome
292513.value: As the strategic decision makers and key leaders of the entrepreneurial firms, the top management teams (TMTs) which are led by the CEOs take an extremely important role in directing the new venture towards right direction so as to survive and develop further. Despite the progress of research on CEO’s role in managing the TMT and some aspects such as the traits of CEO including personality and values have been examined, the role of CEO in bridging and coordinating the TMT members has been rarely investigated, despite the fact that the intra-team dynamics of TMT do determine the effectiveness of this teamwork at the top. Therefore, identifying and then focusing on this CEO’s role which is manifested by the CEO’s networking orientation (specifically, the construct of tertius iungens orientation), we examine and find that such a CEO is more likely to enhance the level of communication among TMT members which further facilitates the polychronicity of the TMT, enabling firm growth when TMT perceive growth opportunities from the focal industry. This empirical study, based on the survey data collected from 141 technology-based new ventures is now being revised and resubmitted to Organization Science. With a valid sample of 101 single founders, we also find that need to belong a key motivational source for the development of this CEO networking orientation and behavior which is positively related to the new venture’s performance. This positive relationship is higher when the key managers working with the founder are also high in need to belong. A related study then finds the determinant role of founder need to belong on tertius iungens orientation is contingent on the venture’s product development stage, further detailing the contextual effect of new venture development in soliciting the networking behavior of the founding CEOs. The findings have been reported in the manuscript being invited to submit to Entrepreneurship Theory and Practice. Overall, the series of CEO-TMT interface related research help us to better understand how CEOs personal traits and leadership impact the TMT process which further improved the organizational outcomes.

292513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
292513.value: As reported above and in the previous report, the data collected for this project cannot be ideally longitudinal due to time and budget limitation. Although we have tried to collect two-wave data from the same sampled firms, the second wave data collection are more about the outcome variables. Therefore, it is hard to obtain information for observing any evolutionary pattern of the firm. Recognizing this constraint, and based on the information obtained from our interviews on some founding CEOs and TMT members; we adjust our original objectives from studying firm level social network evolution to the study of founding teams, to observe the intra-team dynamics and how CEOs influence the dynamics. Focusing on the intra-team network and coordination in the current project, we think inside- and outside- TMT networking behaviors by TMT members are to be examined in more depth and the interaction of them can be explored as well, for instance, CEO s high on networking orientation may not only be good at bridging among TMT members but also connecting them to the external stakeholders. Other CEO traits or skills related to this such as social skills or interpersonal competency can be examined as well in the future.

292513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
292513.value: Top managers, under the leadership of the CEO, make the strategic decisions collectively and this is critical for the firm. For new ventures, top managers face even more challenges due to the extra demand from the business environments such as higher level of competition and limited resources. Therefore, the top teams from new ventures are to make decisions faster to grasp opportunities so as to win the competition in the marketplace. Our findings from this project show that the founding CEO, especially his personality and trait is key to the efficient teamwork of the TMT. More specifically, CEOs who are high in need to belong are more likely to exhibit networking and bridging behaviors, to facilitate the communication among the TMT members. High frequency of communication among TMT members will eventually lead to higher efficiency of their teamwork, including their engaging in multi-tasking, which in turn facilitate the growth of the firm, if they can perceive the growth opportunities in the focal industry. Our findings highlight the importance of certain CEO trait and provide references to investors for their making the IPO related decisions. We also provide direction for selecting and training of senior executives in new ventures.

292713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
292713.value: In today’s dynamic and turbulent business environment, it is becoming increasingly untenable for a single firm to sustain its competitiveness by merely relying on its own firm-specific resources, routines and processes. Absorptive capacity, defined as the ability to utilize external knowledge through three sequential processes of exploratory, transformative, and exploitative learning, is regarded as one of the most important constructs in organizational research; and its impact on firm performance has been one of the central research themes (Cohen and Levinthal, 1990; Zahra and George, 2002; Lane et al., 2006; Lichtenthaler, 2009). However, in a recent review, it is argued that we still do not fully understand this absorptive capacity-performance relationship (Volberda et al., 2010). For example, the empirical findings of the absorptive capacity-performance link remain largely inconclusive and divergent, ranging from a positive relationship (Lichtenthaler, 2009) to a negative relationship (Jansen et al. 2005). Therefore, the proposed study seeks to address the following two critical questions: 1. Does absorptive capacity have a direct impact on firm performance? 2. If not, do marketing and managerial capabilities mediate the relationship between absorptive capacity and firm performance? This study contributes to the existing literature in four substantive ways. First, as an alternative explanation to the inconclusive and divergent findings on the absorptive capacity-performance link, this study, using a dynamic capabilities perspective, advances the research by demonstrating that absorptive capacity is a necessary but insufficient condition for firm performance. Second, the proposed study will empirically investigate the mediating roles of two key operational capabilities: marketing capabilities and managerial capabilities, in the relationship between absorptive capacity and firm performance. It is expected that the findings will provide support to the theoretical prediction that the performance impact of absorptive capacity has to be realized via operational capabilities. Third, this study contributes to the existing literature by investigating whether market and technological turbulence may enhance the effect of absorptive capacity on operational capabilities and moderate the effects of operational capabilities on firm performance. Finally, this study contributes to the research by using a sample of manufacturing SMEs in a non-R&D context in an emerging economy, China. Lane et al. (2006) urged that future research should empirically investigate absorptive capacity in non-R&D contexts in a multi-dimensional approach with a focus on small firms. China, the largest emerging economy, offers an appropriate research venue for such a study since fast-changing environments are typical of an emerging economy. 在今天動態和動盪的商業環境中，單個企業僅僅依靠其自身的企業特有的資源,程式和流程，以維持其競爭力正變得越來越艱難。吸收能力定義為利用外部知識的能力，通過三個連續的過程：探索，變革和剝削性的學習. 它被視為組織研究中最重要的理論之一。其對企業績效的影響一直是重要的研究課題（Cohen和Levinthal，1990; Zahra和George， 2002; Lane等，2006年和Lichtenthaler，2009年）。然而， 在Cohen和Levinthal（1990）的開創性研究二十年後的今天，我們仍然不完全理解吸收能力和績效之間的關係（ Volberda等，2010）。吸收能力和績效之間關係的實證研究結果，基本上沒有定論，眾說紛。從成正比的關係（ Lichtenthaler ，2009）到負比的關係（ Jansen等人， 2005）都有 。因此，本研究旨在解決以下兩個關鍵問題：1 。吸收能力是否足以對企業績效有直接的影響？ 2。運營能力是不是在吸收能力與企業績效之間起到仲介的作用？ 本文對現有文獻在四個方面有實質性的貢獻。首先，對基本上沒有定論，眾說紛紜的吸收能力和績效之間關係研究結果提供一種解釋。 本研究應用動態能力理論，旨在證明吸收能力是企業績效的一個必要但非充分條件。從而推進這一領域的研究。第二，本研究將實證研究兩個運營能力：營銷能力和管理能力，在吸收能力與企業績效之間發揮仲介角色。我們相信，調查結果將我們的理論預測提供支持。即，吸收能力對績效的影響是通過運營能力作為仲介得以實現。第三，這項研究通過專門調查市場和技術動盪可能加大吸收能力對運營能力的影響和其可能加大運營能力對企業績效的影響，從而對這一研究領域作出貢獻。最後，通過用來自新興經濟體的中國製造業的非研髮型的中小企業作為一個樣本，推進這一領域的研究。 Lane等（2006）敦促未來對吸收能力的實證研究，應該採用一個多維的方法，把研究重點放在非研髮型的小企業上。中國，這個全球最大的新興經濟體，為本研究提供了一個適當的場所，因為瞬息萬變的環境是新興經濟體的典型特點。

292713.label: Realisation of objectives
292713.value: The initial results from the data collected so far show that objectives have been fully supported. The key contribution that there exist a mediation model in which absorptive capacity has an indirect impact on firm performance has been supported by the preliminary data collected from various sources. One of the papers related to the project shows that marketing capabilities and managerial capabilities do mediate the impact of absorptive capacity on firm performance. A journal paper is being prepared for Research Policy and to be submitted soon. Another related paper benefiting from the theoretical model of this project shows that in the context of social enterprises, absorptive capacity also has an indirect effect on a social enterprise's financial performance.

292813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
292813.value: The recurrent reports of broad-based ethical transgressions such as corporate scandals (e.g., Lehman Brothers), embezzlement, accounting frauds, insider trading, and dubious business practices have sparked a heated debate on the role of corporations in society. Calls from consumer pressure groups, trade associations, and government regulatory bodies all highlight the need for more attention to business ethics and corporate responsibility to our community at large. Consequently, over 90% of the Fortune 500 companies have explicitly exhibited CSR initiatives (Luo and Bhattacharya 2006). Although those ethical corporate leaders are keen on developing a corporate climate for CSR, frontline employees may not care about it. The realization of CSR not only requires a commitment from the management but also the heartfelt support of frontline employees. To ensure an effective implementation of CSR, it is necessary to understand how the social responsibility climate (SRC) and ethical leadership of the firm are received and internalized by its frontline employees and, in turn, how their performance will be impacted. Despite a large body of literature testifying the outcomes of CSR practices at firm level, the effects of CSR on employees at individual level remain a big knowledge void. This proposed project endeavors to fill this knowledge gap by understanding the effects of the SRC and ethical leadership on frontline salespeople, particularly on their work meaningfulness perceptions and performance. We seek to unveil the psychological mechanisms explaining how CSR enhances salesperson performance through their perceptions of work as a calling, their customer orientation, and their sense of work meaningfulness. This project also aims to contribute to the methods of CSR research by advancing the operationalization of the CSR construct. CSR, by nature, is a continuous practice over time rather than a one-shot deal. We therefore contest that the “static” CSR operationalization in conventional cross-sectional research in the extant literature is incapable of truly reflecting the nature and effects of CSR. Taking into consideration that the impacts of CSR are dynamic and unfold over time, we propose a three-wave multiple time-point design with a latent growth modeling approach (Ng, Feldman, and Lam 2010). We plan to recruit frontline salespersons and make use of their companies’ sales records to test our research model. In doing so, we hope to demonstrate that CSR is a source of opportunity for employee well-being, performance, and competitive advantage. 一篇又一篇關於企業廣泛不道德/違法行為(如雷曼兄弟事件般的醜聞、監守自盜、會計詐騙、內幕交易，以及其他可疑的行為 )的報導引發起企業於社會中角色的激烈討論。 從不同消費權益組織、以至商會及政府規管機構的呼籲中可見商業道德及企業責任的提倡對於社會是必須要的。因此，超過9成財富世界500強的企業均把他們對於企業社會責任所實施了的措施明確的列了出來。 雖然這些有心的商界領袖立志提倡企業社會責任的風氣，但前線員工所想的未必也是一樣。企業社會責任的實現不單只需要依賴管理層的支持，前線員工的真心支持也是十分重要的。為了確保企業社會責任的有效實施，我們須了解前線員工如何看待社會責任風氣和良心領導管理，兩者對他們工作表現又有何影響。過去雖有大量關於企業社會責任措施如何影響企業的研究文獻，但關於企業社會責任措施如何影響員工本身的研究則還是一個未有廣泛探討過的項目。 本建議項目旨在研究社會責任風氣和良心領導管理如何影響前線員工，尤以對他們工作意義的自覺和工作表現兩方面為重。我們旨在探發企業社會責任如何透過令員工認知工作對自己是一種召喚、他們的顧客導向、工作意義的自覺等心理因素之機制調控來達致提升銷售人員表現之目標。 本建議項目亦旨在對企業社會責任的研究方法作出貢獻，尤以改善建構企業社會責任的操作化。企業社會責任本身就是持續不斷而非單一的事項。因此，我們反對傳統橫斷性研究中企業社會責任操作化的「不變」；這些傳統的研究並未能充分反映企業社會責任的本質與真正效果。考慮到企業社會責任的效果與顯現是與時並變的，我們提出了三浪幅多時點隱藏性發展的模型方案。我們計劃招攬不同的銷售人員並以他們的銷售業績來測試我們的研究模型，藉此展示出企業社會責任於員工福祉、員工表現，以致企業競爭優勢方面也是一重大的機遇。

292913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
292913.value: I examine the information content of the option-implied covariance between jumps and the diffusive risks of individual stocks in the cross-sectional variation of future returns. This study is the first investigation that studies the predictive power of implied covariance for expected cross-sectional stock returns. The implied volatility that is derived by the jump-diffusion model of Merton (1976) assumes that there is zero correlation between jumps and diffusive volatility. Although there is no significant relationship between the level of implied covariance and the expected return for a stock, this paper indicates that the difference between realized volatility and implied covariance (RV-ICov) can predict future returns. The results demonstrate a significant and negative association between the expected return and the realized volatility-implied covariance spread in both the portfolio level analysis and the cross-sectional regression study. A trading strategy of buying portfolio with lowest RV-ICov quintile portfolio and selling with highest generates positive and significant returns. This RV-ICov anomaly is robustly persistent after controlling for size, book-to-market value, liquidity and systematic risk proportion. 我研究股票的跳躍和擴散風險之間的協方差 (ICOV) 的期權隱含的的信息內容未來橫截面的收益變化。這是第一項研究隱含協方差的預測股票收益率的能力。默頓（1976）模型得出的隱含波動率中跳躍和擴散波動之間的相關性認為是零。雖然隱含協方差和股票的預期回報之間沒有顯著的關係，本文指出實際波動率和隱含的協方差差異（ RV - ICOV ）可以預測未來的回報。在這組合層面的分析和橫截面回歸協方差傳播研究結果，表現出顯著預期收益和實際波動率和隱含的協方差差異的負相關關係。購買RV - ICOV最低的五分之一組合和銷售最高的五分之一組合的交易策略中，產生顯著的回報。此RV – ICOV在控制價格賬面價值比率、流動性、系統性風險的比例後，其回報仍異常強勁持久。

292913.label: Major findings and research outcome
292913.value: Major Findings 1. I examine the information content of option-implied covariance between jumps and diffusive risk in the cross-sectional variation in future returns. This paper documents that the difference between realized volatility and implied covariance (RV-ICov) can predict future returns. The results show a significant and negative association of expected return and realized volatility–implied covariance spread in both the portfolio level analysis and cross-sectional regression study. A trading strategy of buying a portfolio with the lowest RV-ICov quintile portfolio and selling with the highest one generates positive and significant returns. This RV-Cov anomaly is robust to controlling for size, book-to-market value, liquidity and systematic risk proportion. 2.I also derive the option-implied volatility allowing for nonzero correlation between price jump and diffusive risk to examine the information content of implied diffusive, jump risks and their implied covariance in the cross-sectional variation of future returns. This study documents a strong predictive power of realized volatility and correlated implied volatility spread in the cross section of stock returns. The difference of realized volatility with the implied diffusive volatility, jump risk and covariance can forecast future returns. These anomalies are robustly persistent even after controlling for market, size, book-to-market value, momentum and liquidity factors. 299913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
299913.value: The observed continuation (momentum) of stock return over shorter to intermediate horizons of six to 12 months and the observed reversal of stock return over longer horizons of three to five years have posted challenge to the view of market efficiency in traditional finance theory and puzzled financial economists over the past 3 decades. These effects are found across industries, in alternative asset classes, and in stock markets internationally. The associated investment strategies not only provide statistically and economically significant profits but the profitability also does not seem to vanish after the initial discoveries. While the current literature has provided various rational and behavioral explanations, these explanations seem not to be able to keep up with the vast amount of empirical findings made available to the literature recently. This research fills this gap by providing a novel and unifying explanation and empirical analysis to (1) understand the empirical term structure of information contained in past stock returns about future returns, specifically the effects of short-term return momentum, intermediate-term momentum and long-term reversal, (2) further examine whether and how the components of the term structure, especially short-term momentum and long-term reversal, are related, (3) clarify the unexplained relation between return momentum or reversal and corporate asset growth, and (4) synthesize the stylized cross-sectional and time-series determinants of return momentum and reversal. My explanation is based on the empirical continuation versus reversion of corporate asset growth measured over different horizons and the investor behavior of preferring growth style. 340613.label: Project Objectives
340613.value: In order to empirically examine the dilemmas of transitional justice and their purported impact, the investigators of this project will: • devise a survey questionnaire and a set of attitudinal vignette-based survey experiments among Myanmar people, including minority groups, in which respondents will express their attitudes toward truth, justice, reconciliation, trust, and which will allow us to examine their predictors; devise vignettes describing variations of real-life situations; the vignettes will manipulate proxies for transitional justice, including truth-revelation, investigation, reparation, amnesty, conditional amnesty, apology, and confession, and respondents will be asked to assess their impact on reconciliation, justice, forgiveness, and trust; • analyse these experiments by using appropriate statistical techniques in SPSS or Stata. In order to disseminate the results of the project, the investigators will: • write a co-authored book on prospects for transitional justice in Myanmar and submit the manuscript to a university press in the United States, United Kingdom, or Hong Kong; • write two research papers and submit them to SSCI journals, such as The British Journal of Sociology, Journal of Contemporary Asia, International Journal of Transitional Justice, Law & Society Review, etc.; • present their results at two international conferences, such as annual meetings of the Law & Society Association, Collaborative Network on Law & Society in East Asia, International Association of Political Psychology, World Society of Victimology, International Studies Association etc. • present their results in two local conferences, such as Hong Kong Sociological Association (the PI) and Hong Kong Political Science Association (the CI). • Seek additional funding for the project from Lingnan University.
