359313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
359313.value: How does legislative deliberation in liberal democracies differ from that in authoritarian/semi-democratic regimes? How does democratization affect the quality of legislative deliberation? More broadly, what are the determinants of the quality of legislative deliberation in an authoritarian/semi-democratic regime? To answer these important questions about deliberative politics, this project applies a revised version of the Discourse Quality Index (DQI) developed by Steenbergen et al (2003) to assess and explain the quality of deliberation in Hong Kong’s legislature between 1950 and 2012. Political science scholarship has long highlighted the significance of deliberation to effective functioning of a democratic political system and legislature is a particularly important deliberative institution. The existing studies, however, have two major weaknesses. First, they mainly focus on deliberative politics in western democracies, ignoring authoritarian and/or democratizing regimes. As Leib and He (2006) argue, deliberation has become increasingly popular in authoritarian countries like China. Second, the existing research on legislative deliberation is based on data on a single or a few legislative terms. Without examining longitudinal data, this line of research therefore has overlooked the impact of socio-political changes on the quality of legislative deliberation. The case of Hong Kong can make important theoretical and empirical contributions to the study of deliberative politics in legislatures. Through analyzing the legislative deliberation on crucial public policies from 1950 to 2012, this project allows us to study the impact of political changes, specifically democratization, on the quality of legislative deliberation. Has democratization enhanced or undermined the quality of legislative deliberation? If so, why and how? Hong Kong has an (soft) authoritarian political system. The Chief Executive is elected by a 1,200-member Election Committee, and the majority of its members are pro-China figures or businessmen. However, the legislature has undergone partial democratization since the mid-1980s. Before 1985, all the Hong Kong legislators were appointed by the colonial governor. In 1985, indirect elections were introduced, through which the business sector and professionals elect their representatives to the legislature (functional constituencies [FCs] members). In 1991, direct elections were introduced, through which each citizen casts one vote (geographical constituencies [GCs] members). By 2004, all legislators were elected either through geographical or functional constituencies. How has this unique electoral system affected deliberation quality within the legislature? Does deliberation quality vary between the GC members and FC members? More broadly, has the presence of an un-democratically elected Chief Executive influenced legislative deliberation? 立法會的議事在民主政治下跟在獨裁和半民主政治下有什麽不同的地方? 民主化會如何影响立法會的議事質素? 有什麼因素會影响獨裁和半民主政治下立法會的議事質素? 為了回答以上關於議事政治的重要問题, 本研究將應用由Steenbergen 等学者所發明的研討質素指標 (Discourse Quality Index: DQI) 來評估與解釋香港立法會從一九五零年至二零一二年間的議事質素。 香港立法會的案例對於研究立法會議事政治將带來重要的理論和實踐貢献。透過分析香港立法會對重大的公共政策的議事，本研究將幫助我們了解政治轉變，特别是民主化，對立法會的議事質素會带來什麼影响? 民主化會提高还是會減低立法會的議事質素? 香港是一個半民主的政治體制。行政長官由一個1200人组成 (大部份成員是親北京的政治人物和商人) 的選舉委員會選舉產生。立法會由八十年代中期开始民主化。到二零零四年，所有的立法會議員都由地方選舉/功能组别選舉產生。这種獨特的選舉制度會否影响立法會的議事質素? 地方選舉產生的議員的議事質素會否跟功能组别選舉產生的議員不同? 一個不是由民主選舉產生的行政長官會否影响立法會的議事質素?

359313.label: Realisation of objectives
359313.value: All five objectives stated in the proposal were achieved. Objectives 1 to 4. To fulfil Objectives 1 to 4, I studied legislative deliberations on six rounds of political reforms in Hong Kong from 1984 to 2015. The first concerned the introduction of functional constituency elections to the legislature in 1985. The second focused on the introduction of direct elections to the legislature in 1991. The third concerned legislative reforms introduced by the last colonial Governor Christopher Patten. The fourth focused on reforms of the Chief Executive and legislative elections in 2005. The fifth discussed the expansion of more democratic elements in the legislature in 2012. The last focused on the Chief Executive Election in 2017. I conducted detailed content analyses of the speeches delivered by all the legislators during the resumption of Second Reading Debate on the aforementioned six rounds of political reforms. The first debate took place in 1984 when the legislature was undemocratic (all legislators were appointed by the colonial Governor). The second to the last debates happened in the context of gradual democratization of the legislature, as appointed members were gradually phased out and replaced by directly-elected and functional constituency members. Applying Steiner et al's 'Discourse Quality Index' (2004), I examined the quality of legislative deliberation on the above six political reforms, whether and how democratization could affect the quality of legislative deliberation, and the major determinants. I am currently writing an article based on the above study and will send it to an international peer-reviewed journal to be considered for publication. Related to the above research, I examined whether legislator gender will affect the quality of legislative deliberation. To answer this question, I conducted detailed content analyses of the speeches delivered by the legislators during the resumption of Second Reading Debate on all the bills during the 2012-16 legislative session. Specifically, I investigated whether female legislators were more likely to be respectful to their colleagues than male legislators, and whether male legislators were more likely to be disrespectful than their female counterparts. This article will be submitted to the journal Politics & Gender to be considered for publication. Apart from the aforementioned two projects, I also conducted detailed content analyses of the deliberations on important bills in Hong Kong's legislature from the 1970s to 2015. I am planning to write a book based on the findings of the content analyses. Objective 5. To investigate the behavior of legislators in Hong Kong, I examined the extent to which Hong Kong's female legislators represented women's interests from 1970 to 2012. The study finds that after the introduction of legislative elections, female legislators were more likely to represent women’s interests than male legislators. Apart from gender, the study also finds that political orientation of a legislator significantly affected legislator policy priorities. Liberal legislators proposed significantly more motions related to women’s interests than conservative legislators. Finally, the study highlights that as the legislature was transited from an undemocratic to a semi-democratic body, legislators were significantly more likely to propose motions related to women’s interests. This study has been published in Journal of Legislative Studies (Issue 1, 2017, pp. 44-70). The title of the article is 'Do female legislators have different policy priorities than their male colleagues in an undemocratic/ semi-democratic legislature? The case of Hong Kong'

359313.label: Major findings and research outcome
359313.value: My first paper investigates the behavior of legislators in Hong Kong by examining the extent to which Hong Kong's female legislators represented women's interests from 1970 to 2012. The study finds that after the introduction of legislative elections, female legislators were more likely to represent women’s interests than male legislators. Apart from gender, the study also finds that political orientation of a legislator significantly affected legislator policy priorities. Liberal legislators proposed significantly more motions related to women’s interests than conservative legislators. Finally, the study highlights that as the legislature was transited from an undemocratic to a semi-democratic body, legislators were significantly more likely to propose motions related to women’s interests. This study has been published in Journal of Legislative Studies (Issue 1, 2017, pp. 44-70). The title of the article is 'Do female legislators have different policy priorities than their male colleagues in an undemocratic/ semi-democratic legislature? The case of Hong Kong' In the second paper, I applied Steiner et al's 'Discourse Quality Index' to study the quality of legislative deliberation on six major political reforms in Hong Kong between 1984 and 2015. The content analyses show that as the legislature experienced gradual democratization, the quality of legislative deliberation in terms of 'participation', 'respect for counter-arguments and legislators with opposing viewpoints', and 'justification for demand', experienced a decline. This finding has serious implications for democratization and the prospect of democracy in Hong Kong, given that effective deliberation is important to democracy. In the third paper, I find that in Hong Kong legislator gender has affected the quality of legislative deliberation. Both male and female legislators did not show any significant difference in terms of respecting the colleagues who had opposing viewpoints and the counter-arguments of their colleagues. However, male legislators had used more disrespectful language against their colleagues who had opposing viewpoints and the counter-arguments of their colleagues.

359313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
359313.value: Further research can address: (1) whether the quality of legislative deliberation on other important bills in Hong Kong also experienced a decline, when the legislature experienced gradual democratization (2) compare the case of Hong Kong with Taiwan, which underwent the process of democratization between the 1980s and the 2000s. We can conduct a longitudinal research on the quality of legislative deliberation in Taiwan's legislature and investigate whether democratization had any impacts on the quality of legislative deliberation.

359313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
359313.value: This project is the first longitudinal study of the quality of legislative deliberation in Hong Kong in the context of gradual democratization. Given that effective deliberative capacity is central to any democratic system, a comprehensive understanding of the quality of legislative deliberation and its determinants is important for us to examine the prospect of democratization in Hong Kong. The results of this project may serve as a guide for politicians, the government or other interested parties when they are pursuing democratic reforms in Hong Kong.

359613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
359613.value: The status of intuition in philosophical methodology has recently come under heavy scrutiny. Intuition plays a dominant role in the argumentative practices of philosophers; however, an increasing number of empirical studies have begun to show that intuition is highly variable, and potentially deeply unreliable. A variety of defenses of intuition have been offered, as well as a variety of arguments proposing restriction or abandonment of the use of intuition. The proposed research project aims to elucidate and challenge several of the dominant assumptions adopted on both sides of this debate. There are three crucial questions which must be answered before the status of intuition as a philosophical tool can be properly assessed. The first concerns the nature of intuition itself. Though appeals to intuition are often easy to spot, there is little agreement as to what an intuition consists in. My own view is that the term ‘intuition’ does not in fact pick out a unified mental phenomenon at all – instead, it covers a wide range of deeply heterogeneous mental states. If this is indeed true, it makes the evaluation of intuition’s epistemological status much more complex. The second question concerns the targets of philosophical inquiry. An investigation of knowledge might aim to illuminate the boundaries of our commonsense concept of knowledge. Alternately, it might aim to characterize some mind-independent, ‘natural’ phenomenon. I argue that viewing the aim of philosophy in the first sense makes appeals to intuition more justifiable, but that it fails to adequately capture philosophical practice. The second option fits more closely with actual practice, but makes the position of intuition much more tenuous. The third question concerns the epistemological standards that our assessment invokes. Simple reliability based assessments (i.e., intuition is acceptable if and only if it is reliable) have been the default; however, defenders of intuition have pointed out that intuition’s errors are not obviously more frequent than those of perception. My own position is that the epistemological assessment of intuition must be sensitive to features beyond mere frequency of error; it is possible to accept that intuition is on the whole reliable, while simultaneously questioning its suitability to play a central role in philosophical theorizing. The stances I advocate on these three methodological questions lead to the following view: intuition cannot be dispensed with entirely, but there may be a need to substantially reform our current philosophical practices. 直覺(Intuition)在哲學方法(philosophical methodology)上的地位近來受到徹底的仔細檢視。直覺一直以來在哲學討論中扮演一個主導性的地位；但是，越來越多的經驗研究(empirical studies)顯示直覺是變化不定(variable)，而且可能極不可靠(unreliable)。種種不同的論證主張直覺的運用(use of intuition)應該受到限制或屏棄，另一方，亦有不少論證為直覺提供辯護。本研究的目的在於闡釋和質疑，有關直覺的討論中，幾個主導正反雙方的假設。 要評定直覺作為哲學工具(philosophical tool)的地位，必先回應三條關鍵的問題。第一條問題關注直覺的本質(nature of intuition) 。雖然直覺的運用一般都相當容易確認，但對於直覺由甚麼構成，卻很少有一致的意見。我認為「直覺」一詞實際上並非指向一個統一的心靈現象(a unified mental phenomenon)，而是一系列不同的心靈狀態(mental states) 。如果這個觀點是真確的，則會令有關直覺在知識論中的地位的評估(the evaluation of intuition’s epistemological status)變得更加複雜。 第二條問題關注哲學探究的目的(targets of philosophical inquiry)。有關知識的研究，其目的可能是為了闡明我們日常生活中知識這個概念的界限(the boundaries of our commonsense concept of knowledge)，另外，亦可能是為了描繪一些獨立於心靈的「自然」現象(mind-independent, ‘natural’ phenomenon) 。我會論辯，在第一個意義下理解哲學研究的目的會令直覺的運用更加合理，但卻未能符合慣常的哲學探究方式；第二個意義更加接近慣常的哲學探究方式，但卻會令直覺在哲學中的地位變得更薄弱。 第三條問題關注評估直覺時在知識論上所採用的準則(epistemological standards)。對直覺的評估一般都以可靠性(reliability)為預定的準則（即，直覺會被接納，當且僅當，直覺是可靠的），但辯護者指出直覺出現誤差的頻率並不明顯地多於感知(perception)。我認為對於直覺在知識論上的評估(the epistemological assessment of intuition)，必需顧及誤差頻率以外的因素；我們可以認可直覺在大體上是可靠的，同時質疑它是否合適在哲學理論建構上扮演一個重要的角色。 基於我在以上三條問題的立場，我認為：直覺不能被完全屏棄，但卻有需要重整我們現時的哲學探究方式。

359613.label: Realisation of objectives
359613.value: The ultimate output of the grant has been a series of papers, rather than the initially proposed book. There are several reasons for this. First, an important new development arose within the intuitions literature (namely, the large reaction to Herman Cappelen’s recent book “Philosophy without Intuitions”) which caused me to rethink my core positions in the area rather dramatically. Given my changing views, I decided to rework the planned contents of the book, to write initial versions of the core book ideas up in article form in order to organize my thoughts, and then finally to return to tie all the ideas together into a coherent whole. Finally, during this same period, I received several invitations to contribute to journal special issues, edited volumes, and conferences related to intuition and metaphilosophy – this led me to further focus on developing the project ideas in paper format for inclusion in these venues. Thus, at current, the published work arising from the project is wholly in article format. It was my hope that I could also complete a book draft which would synthesize the material in these papers within the grant period, thus fulfilling the original objective as stated – however, this was ultimately too ambitious and the draft is yet to be completed. In part, I believe that I made the mistake of overcommitting myself during the project period, by accepting five separate invitations to submit papers to special issues/edited volumes (two of these are still under preparation – the others are the Oxford studies paper, the Epistemic Pluralism paper, and the Inquiry paper listed in part C), plus an invitation to edit a volume for a series on experimental philosophy (another of my output papers in part C is a contribution to this edited volume – I have not listed the volume itself as a research output). As an early career researcher, I am not yet accustomed to receiving regular invitations for contributions, and this led me to difficulty in properly managing my project load and commitments. The invitations seemed to me to be excellent opportunities to work through the issues I was grappling with for the book (and I do in fact believe they were) – but they led to neglect of a book draft itself. Relatedly, I should also note that I further erred by not including grant information on the first two output articles from the project – as this was my first grant, I was not yet familiar with proper procedures for grant work (I had no exposure to grants during graduate school, as they are not as common in philosophy as they are in other fields). This also led to some confusion on my part as to how to properly report my output during my midterm progress reports (indeed, I’m still not sure I’ve gotten everything right!). Ultimately, however, I have produced what I believe to be a very substantial output during the grant period – nine published and accepted papers, two of which are in top ten journals in my field (both with acceptance rates of approximately 10%). The contents of the papers I have completed during the grant period are deeply interrelated, and the papers when taken as a whole present what I believe to be a coherent, comprehensive picture of the role of intuition in philosophical inquiry. I do still plan to synthesize the material into a book, and have a fair amount of written material towards this goal, but it is currently in several different partial drafts and outlines, and fairly far from a readable state. I continue to struggle with fully fitting the different pieces of my view together, and currently the book draft has been lowered in priority due to the two additional invited contributions I have promised to complete. As for the specific objectives I initially proposed in the grant application, the papers do, I believe, fully address objectives 2 and 3: the nature of intuition is explored in the Inquiry paper, the Philosophical Studies paper, and the Thought paper; the targets of philosophical inquiry are explored in the paper for the Bloomsbury volume, and to a lesser degree in the Philosophical Studies and Inquiry papers; the epistemological standards question is taken up in the Australasian Journal paper, the Epistemic pluralism paper, and the Oxford Studies in Epistemology paper. Though I have not produced a book, the material I have produced does at least partially fulfill objective 1: the paper in Thought serves as an overview of the current state of the intuition debate which is suitable for specialists and non-specialists, and the Philosophical Studies paper similarly provides an overview for a smaller portion of that debate (namely, the literature surrounding Cappelen’s work mentioned earlier). Unfortunately, none of the currently published output material substantially addresses my original objectives 4 and 5. One of my papers currently in preparation partially deals with historical issues in this area – namely, Carnapian explication and its relation to the use of intuition in philosophy. However, that paper is not complete (I have not listed it as an output, since I have not completed a full draft at current). Other research I have performed on these objectives will eventually be incorporated into the book draft, but is not currently substantially incorporated into any written output. Outside of the explicitly proposed objectives, the work I have completed during the grant period has been immensely formative with regard to developing more mature and complete philosophical views; I have, I believe, substantially improved upon the positions I held in my dissertation. My future work will build on this foundation.

359613.label: Major findings and research outcome
359613.value: The primary research output for the grant consists in nine published and accepted papers, dealing with related topics surrounding the use of intuition in philosophy. The unifying theme of the papers is that the metaphilosophical literature has operated with a dramatically oversimplified picture of philosophical methodology, and that as a result neither side of the ‘intuition debates’ (that is, ‘pro-intuition’ vs ‘anti-intuition’) is wholly in the right. The best characterization of our current methodological situation, I argue, is moderate – there is need for improvement, but the core methods of philosophy need not be discarded. Among the primary claims I argue for in these papers are as follows: first, intuition is not a single ‘type’ of mental state, but many; second, philosophical methodology is much more complex than mere ‘appeal to intuition’, involving a variety of expert skills that are obscured by current focus on intuition; third, that philosophy employs (or should employ) much higher epistemic ‘standards’ than ordinary intellectual activity; and fourth, that the goal of philosophy is, in most cases, not best characterized by the idea of ‘conceptual analysis’ as a purely descriptive enterprise of characterizing ‘our own concepts’. Each of these claims appears repeatedly across the papers – for instance, the paper ‘the intuition deniers’ makes use of the first, second, and third claims to analyze the significance of a recent view according to which philosophers do not rely on intuition in philosophy. In many cases, I motivate these theses by analogy with the sciences and the methodology in place in fields like psychology. Each of these nine articles contributes to a view according to which intuitions are in fact used as evidence - but not to the degree standardly claimed; and according to which intuitions genuinely do provide good evidence – but not as good as would be needed to justify a complacent attitude in the fact of the findings of experimental philosophy. The upshot of this position is that we are in more or less the same position as most other intellectual fields – we must struggle with the effects of various cognitive biases on our efforts at inquiry, and we must develop methods to mitigate those biases. The existence and importance of said biases to academic method are, for instance, obvious in fields like experimental psychology – but practitioners rarely conclude that they doom the methods of the discipline. The same attitude is warranted in philosophy.

359613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
359613.value: I currently have two papers in preparation that are directly related to the grant topic – both deal with the idea of conceptualizing our philosophical goal in terms of ‘conceptual engineering’ (a prescriptive project) rather than ‘conceptual analysis’ (a descriptive project). One of these is for an invited contribution to a special issue of Synthese, and the other is for a special issue of Philosophical Psychology. As noted in section 5.3, I do still plan to develop the papers written during this project (as well as the ones in preparation) into a full book. I have been working on a draft of this book for quite some time, but it has been pushed somewhat ‘in the background’ as I developed my positions primarily in article format (partially due to the volume of contribution invitations I received within the last few years). As this is my first book-length project subsequent to my dissertation, I have found myself struggling with organization and ‘flow’ for the larger-scale project – I am still working out how to make the various parts of the book ‘fit together’. The book and the two final in-prep papers will be my primary research focus for the coming year.

359613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
359613.value: Philosophy has long been understood as a discipline which places special evidential weight on intuitions – immediate judgments which occur in the absence conscious reasoning. We intuit, for instance, that such-and-so action is wrong, or that such-and-so scenario does not count as genuine knowledge. Within the last few decades, however, substantial experimental evidence has indicated that these intuitions may be subject to many worrying biases – they are apparently affected by cultural background, gender, emotion, personality type, and more. Some philosophers have reacted by claiming that current philosophical methods have been proven unreliable; others have protested that these studies present no challenge. My work presents a more moderate approach to the philosophical significance of these studies, drawing largely on analogies with scientific methodology. I argue against several misconceptions of philosophical methodology which I claim have led the literature on intuition in the wrong direction. The standard view of philosophy as relying primarily on ‘appeal to intuition’ is wrong – the story is much more complicated. Studies on intuition do not seriously threaten our core philosophical methods, I conclude – but they do show that there is a need for greater care, and the implementation of procedures to minimize or correct for cognitive biases.

359813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
359813.value: Today’s booming digital-media technologies permeate our culture, education, work and daily lives. Recent studies show that a majority of digital age learners worldwide are experienced producers of new literacies involving media content and are active participants on the Internet, whereas their teachers may not be. Despite abundant literacy research related to traditional print-based literacy before the 1970s, followed by educational literacies after the 1970s and digital-media and new literacies latterly, research into the effects of new literacies in formal settings in the Asia-Pacific region, especially with reference to university students, remains limited. This proposed study extends current research by investigating groundbreaking possibilities and synergies for new literacies as leverage points for academic literacies for university students in digital humanities through creative expression, performative arts and popular culture. It explores the interface between formal and non-formal learning environments enhanced by Web 2.0 tools within an Asian cultural setting with biliterate and trilingual university students in an English-as-a-second-language (ESL) learning context. The proposed study will draw on social learning and sociocultural perspectives that take into account recent research findings. It argues that principle-based acculturation and reflection, as based in discipline engagement and transfer enhanced by the Web 2.0 tools in multiple contexts, has the potential to bridge the gap between academic and new literacy practices in formal and non-formal settings. The study also aims to foster social learning and the “participatory cultures” critical for the development of “efficacious learning” amongst university students, encouraging them in the process to become full participants and responsible media-producers. Informed by an earlier small-scale pilot study, the present study will employ a mixed-method research design in a two-phase longitudinal format over three years. It will utilize quantitative, analytical and case study methods to gather rich data through guided practice from a variety of formal and non-formal settings, employing innovative technologies including mobile learning tools and virtual platforms. The major outcome will be a better descriptive and explanatory framework for new literacies as leverage for academic literacies in an Asian context than has hitherto been possible. Accomplishing this goal will provide important insights into how university students can be better prepared for the application of new literacies to their adult lives in the 21st century. 今天的數碼媒體技術相當發達，並已滲透到我們的文化、教育、工作及日常生活之中。最近的研究表明，世界大部份生活在數碼年代的學生，是有經驗的新媒體素養——包括媒體內容——的製造者, 也是互聯網的活躍參與者，而他們的老師卻未必如是。在素養研究方面，除了1970年代前有足夠的對傳統印刷素養的研究，以及1970年代後對教育素養、數碼媒體及新媒體素養的研究外，有關新媒體素養在亞太地區正式場合上應用的研究，特別是其對大學生影響的研究，依然有限。 這個擬議在目前研究的基礎上，延伸探討新媒體素養繼續開創的可能性及其協同效應——通過創意表達、表現藝術和流行文化，讓新媒體素養成為大學生在數碼人文學術中的槓桿點。此研究是探討Web 2.0工具在亞洲文化背景下，及大學生在兩文三語並以英語作為第二語言的學習環境中，如何增強正式與非正式學習的對接。 本研究會從社群學習與社會文化的視角出發，利用最近的研究成果。本研究認為，原則導向的文化滲透和反思，由於建基於Web 2.0工具對學科參與及轉移的增強作用，因而在正式或非正式的場合中，有縮短學術及新媒體素養之間差距的能力。本研究同時致力於培養社群學習，以及對大學生發展“有效學習”非常關鍵的“參與文化”，並在此過程中鼓勵他們全情投入，成為負責任的媒介製造者。 基於早前一個小型試驗性質的研究，本研究會採用一個為期三年、分兩階段的縱向混合研究模式。它會利用案例、分析及定量研究，通過在正式或非正式場合的指導性實踐，去收集數據，並會應用最新科技，如流動學習工具及虛擬平台。 本研究主要的成果，在亞洲迄今未能成氣候的環境下，形成一個更好的框架去描述和解釋新媒體素養，並讓其影響學術文化界。以及為二十一世紀的大學生，該如何為在未來的工作和生活中應用新媒體素養做更好的準備。

359813.label: Realisation of objectives
359813.value: The three-year ECS project (Jan 2014 to Dec 2016) was completed fruitfully with an extension which ended officially on June 30, 2017. The project configured the efficacious learning mediated by new literacies to foster the academic literacies important for academic success, with undergraduate students in the digital humanities (in this case, English) from an Asian cultural perspective. The 3 project objectives were reinterpreted through the following 5 research questions. Project objective 1: Develop a new theoretical paradigm that describes and explains new and academic literacy practices of university students in the Hong Kong context. RQ1. What are the existing perceptions and practices of new literacies enhanced by Web 2.0 tools in higher education in Hong Kong? Project objective 2: Investigate the principles and procedures related to new literacy practices as leverage points to enhance academic literacies across formal and non-formal settings, in and out of the classroom, and across borders for global English. RQ3 (original question number in the ECS proposal). In what specific ways can the new literacy practices in multiple subfields of contemporary English studies afford leverage points for academic literacies in formal and non-formal settings? Project objective 3: Analyze and evaluate the impact of the new literacy practices on student literacy practices and global identities longitudinally. RQ2. What is the impact of new literacy practices enhanced by Web 2.0 tools on student learning outcomes related to literacy development in formal setting? RQ4. Does awareness of the issue in (RQ3) have any sustainable impact on student literacy development and practices beyond the formal setting? RQ5. What critical factors might shape the successful leverage of new literacy practices for academic literacies enhanced by Web 2.0 tools in higher education in Hong Kong? To accomplish the project objectives, a total of 39 of the proposed 40 student participants were recruited from 4 English courses at the PI’s home university, with 1 participant-initiated withdrawal due to a change of university (N = 38). Within the project period, various data were collected from the participants (see table below). To further inform the project objectives, supplementary data were also collected from additional sources, including (1) from the students who attended the English courses taught by the PI during the project period; (2) through a large-scale literacy survey conducted and tracked annually with the 2013 cohort of undergraduate students throughout their four-year bachelor’s degree program of study (2014-2017) and the 2014 cohort of students over their first three years of study (2015-2017). Researchers kept observation notes over 3 terms. The paradigm capitalizes the key concept of “efficacious learning” of new literacies (Lankshear & Knobel, 2011, p. 252) to describe and explain new and academic literacy practices of university students in the Hong Kong context. The major principles of efficacious learning found in the study reflect a strong participatory culture, involving active participation, collaboration, distributed expertise and learner autonomy. The theoretical paradigm of efficacious learning has been put forward in two forthcoming journal articles (Hui, in press a; in press b). Ongoing analysis is currently underway. As regards objective 2, the study’s results showed a variety of leverage points, including “academic literacies,” “collaboration,” “creativity,” “learning in coursework and assessment” and “communication and socializing” (RQ3, see Hui, in press b). Broadly speaking, the project’s findings of leverage points have addressed the challenge of filling the everyday/academic literacies gap (Alvermann & Hinchman, 2012) in literacy research in the following principal ways. Firstly, it goes beyond the predominant focus on the school context to explore new literacies in higher learning situations in various academic contexts (Lea & Street, 2006) and in an English language learning environment (Thorne, 2008) from an Asian cultural perspective. Secondly, it addresses the problems of the academic literacies — often criticized as an overly prescribed, pre-determined and decontextualized form of knowledge, individualistic problem-solving style, and non-committing innovation (Gee, 2007) — to foster efficacious learning through social learning and participatory culture in the networked English community (Rice, 2006). Thirdly, it alleviates some methodological problems such as the short-term, mainly single-course nature of studies, assumptions of literacies as monologic and binary, and technology as a neutral tool that is in isolation from the users, purposes of use, literacy practices and contexts (Wilber, 2008). The mixed-methods structure of the study within the disciplinary engagement (i.e., English) in the Hong Kong cultural and linguistic environment offers novel and rich contextual evidence to construct meaningful interpretations in new literacies research. The third and final objective regarding the effects of new literacy practices on academic performance (RQ2) has been disseminated in a forthcoming journal article (Hui, in press a). In summary terms, the study’s empirical results showed significant positive associations between participants’ perceived effects of new literacies and academic achievements, concerning particularly “academic literacies” and “collaboration;” and between their digital engagement levels and the scores of the assessment tasks, involving especially the interactive and collaborative discourse. These results inform how “efficacious learning” fostered by new literacies can transform the academic literacies essential for academic success (Project objective 1). Regarding the issues of awareness (RQ4) and crucial factors (RQ5), the study’s empirical results showed that participants who demonstrated different digital engagement levels would seem to be differently proficient in leveraging new literacies for enriching discipline-based academic results. In particular, participants with a strong participatory culture seem more capable of utilizing the positive effects of new literacies to foster academic benefits than those who are less digitally engaged. Participants who were more digitally engaged would seem to be more capable of transforming the affordances to navigate between conventional and new literacies, which in turn leads to relatively more favorable academic achievements. The relevant study’s findings have been reported in a forthcoming journal article (Hui, in press a). Under-achievements and follow-up plan: While the PI completed the data collection within the scope of the proposed project timeline, the PI did not have enough time to analyze a wide range of unanalyzed research data collected from the ECS project. For example, statistical analysis of the large-scale survey data sets and qualitative analysis concerning the qualitative data of the principles (RQ3), and crucial factors and identities (RQ5) are currently underway. The findings of these analyses will convey a fuller and richer picture of how academic literacies are leveraged through the efficacious learning of new literacies. Additional 2-3 manuscripts are underway based on these unanalyzed research data. The writing topics include the tracking of the literacy practices of two undergraduate cohorts admitted in 2013 and 2014 respectively over 4 years, and in-depth analysis of discourses and case studies. The PI will make every effort to accomplish the aforementioned unfinished tasks generated directly from the ECS project in the coming months or 1-2 years, if and when the PI finds a faculty position in another UGC-funded university elsewhere in Hong Kong.

359813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
359813.value: The study configured the efficacious learning mediated by new literacies to foster the academic literacies important for academic success, with English major undergraduate students from an Asian perspective. The study’s results have addressed the challenge of filling the everyday/academic literacies gap (Alvermann & Hinchman, 2012) in literacy research and contributed useful insights into the changing English, language and linguistic studies. Firstly, the learning principles for new literacies are common to students’ lifestyle habits as a way to advance academic literacies, which are deemed essential for academic success. This in turn may enhance efficacious learning beneficial to all learners to become more critically and academically literate and responsible participants in the digital humanities. Secondly, active engagement in reflective practices of new literacies to enhance domain-specific knowledge could encourage learners to become more independent and engaged in performative and cultural curricular areas within and beyond the tertiary English education context. Thirdly, curriculum development in the areas of pedagogy and assessment would need to accommodate student expectations and the diversity of digital trends and styles in learning and teaching, which are becoming increasingly digitalized, distributed and negotiable in the co-construction of meaning involving learning artifacts, social relationships and collaborative processes.

390113.label: Realisation of objectives
390113.value: We have collected the data on cases of repeated fraud in China and obtained preliminary results on the determinants of repeated fraud. However, we encountered a serious estimation problem --- distinguishing between the fraud commission and fraud probabilities for multiple fraud cases (which is different from the single time event). The distinction is very important as it will have very different implications on the interpretation of our results. However, existing studies in finance and statistics have not offered a guideline for us to solve this problem. When we worked on the project, we find some interesting and important results on labor market consequences of securities fraud to independent directors. Our research team decided to finish a paper on that issue first while we are looking to the solutions to our estimation problem. We eventually published the paper in the Journal of Business Ethics.

390113.label: Major findings and research outcome
390113.value: We investigate the regulatory sanctions imposed on independent directors for their firms’ financial frauds in China. During the period 2003-2010, 302-person-time independent directors were penalized by the regulator (the CSRC), and the two stock exchanges. Our results are summarized in the following points. 1. The independent directors with accounting experiences are more likely to be penalized by the CSRC, though they do not suffer more severe penalties than do the other sanctioned independent directors. 2. The independent directors suffer less severe penalties than do the insider directors. These results are consistent with the hypothesis that the sanctions on independent directors are tied to their assumed responsibilities. 3. Following a regulatory sanction, penalized independent directors experience a significant decline in the number of other board seats held. However, they can gain board seats in better quality firms. 4. Interlocked firms that share penalized independent directors with the fraud firm do not suffer from a valuation decline. In sum, our results suggest that regulatory sanctions have not triggered further sanctions on the penalized directors in the labor market but they have, instead, created a disincentive for these directors to serve on the company boards of high risk firms. We explain the disincentive effects by way of the damage to the penalized directors’ career goals and personal reputation and the direct financial costs created by fines.

390113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
390113.value: Our study identifies two aspects for further research and development. We indicate some cautions that should be exercised when generalizing our findings. Our results are obtained under China’s unique institutional framework. In particular, there is a lack of demand for good quality independent directors due to the concentrated ownership and weak law enforcement. The impacts of the regulatory sanctions are very likely to be different if there is an effective demand for good quality directors in other markets. Future studies are needed to examine this issue in the markets with effective demand for good quality directors. Secondly, it is possible that the regulatory sanctions may be useful in inducing other non-penalized directors to provide better services. How the regulatory sanctions will alter the incentives of non-penalized directors and the overall quality of the services provided by independent directors are important issues that we will put in future research. [Note by the Office of Research Support] Sadly the PI passed away in 2016 and this report was written by the Co-I Dr Sonia Wong.

390113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
390113.value: China has attempted to secure good conducts from independent directors by employing regulatory sanctions as disciplinary devices. We examine the Chinese experience to offer some new insights on the effects of regulations as a complementary institutional arrangement to monitor the independent directors. We find that the regulatory sanctions on independent directors are lighter than those imposed on the inside directors (Chairman, CEO, CFOs and non-independent directors). Independent directors with accounting backgrounds are more likely to be sanctioned by the regulator. We also examine the consequences of the regulatory sanctions on the functioning of the board labor market. We find that the penalized independent directors experience a decline in board seats held but also have a shift in quality of board memberships from poorer firms to better firms. Overall, our results suggest that the regulatory sanctions have not triggered the labor market to further punish the penalized independent directors but have created an incentive for directors to leave the boards of high risk firms. Similar to China, many emerging markets are also plagued by serious agency problems between minority shareholders and have instituted an independent director system to mitigate the agency problems. Our results should have resonance for these emerging markets.

390913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
390913.value: Negative Brand Publicity and Consumer Attributions: The Moderating Influence of Corporate Brand Dominance and Individual Thinking Styles 品牌負面曝光事件與消費者歸因：企業品牌顯著性及個體思維方式的調節作用 摘要： 品牌資產被認為是公司所擁有的最重要的資產之一。像瑕疵的/危險的產品（如：豐田汽車的突然加速）或不道德的商業行為（如：蘋果的富士康加工廠裡惡劣的工作條件）這樣的負面曝光事件很可能會損害品牌資產。在一個日趨全球化的市場裡，消費者對品牌負面曝光事件的處理可能變得越來越複雜，這就迫切需要調查品牌負面曝光事件如何影響消費者的反應，以及如何影響消費者對負面曝光事件進行解釋的歸因過程。 本研究的主要目的是調查企業品牌顯著性對兩種不同類型，即與性能相關的（如：產品缺陷）和與價值相關的（如：不道德的行為）品牌負面曝光事件的歸因過程的影響。企業品牌顯著性是指公司的品牌在產品溝通中的能見度。我們預測品牌顯著性可能會在負面品牌曝光事件對消費者歸因的影響中起到仲介作用。一個具有高水準的企業品牌顯著性的公司可能會在因為負面事件而受到責備的過程中得到保護。此外，我們還將檢驗個體思維方式的角色，因為我們期望企業品牌顯著性的仲介影響對分析性思維方式者和整體性思維方式者會有所不同。整體性思維方式者更可能看重基於外部情境的負面曝光事件的解釋並傾向于形成與公司無關的歸因。與此相反，分析性思維方式者則不太可能看重情境因素並傾向于形成與公司相關聯的歸因，這可能會極大的影響顧客對負面曝光事件反應。 我們設計了一個概念框架，包括了兩種主要的負面品牌曝光事件類型對消費者關於因果歸因和可控性歸因的影響，而企業品牌顯著性和個體的思維方式在理論上作為兩個關鍵的調節因素。此外，消費者的品牌評價、公司評價和購買意願作為其歸因過程的結果變數。我們期望與性能相關的和與價值相關的負面品牌曝光事件會顯著的影響消費者的判斷和對負面事件的歸因。歸因過程的複雜性會取決於研究所涉及的各個變數，即不同類型的負面曝光事件、企業品牌顯著性和個體的思維方式之間的相互作用。我們將採用實驗設計和問卷調研的方法來對假設及概念模型進行檢驗。實驗設計的主要目的是檢驗與消費者歸因形成相關聯的關鍵要素，而問卷調研是為了增強對所提出概念模型中的各種關係的理解。 通過將負面曝光事件分為兩種主要類型，擬進行的研究為了解消費者歸因和負面品牌曝光事件的關係提供了一個新的視角。我們希望在消費者對性能相關的和價值相關的負面曝光事件的反應中得到重要的管理啟示。預期的新發現可會豐富現有關於負面曝光事件及品牌溝通的相關營銷理論。

391113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
391113.value: Information asymmetry can threaten the availability of external financing to a firm when there is a separation of ownership and control. As a result, corporations have incentives to devote resources to communicate with various market participants. These activities have been broadly referred to as investor relations (IR). According to the 2010 Guidelines on Best Practices of IR issued by the London Stock Exchange, IR refers to “the ongoing activity of companies communicating with the investment community”. It is a “part of stock market life” and is essential for “attract(ing) and retain(ing) investment funds” (London Stock Exchange, 2010, p.2). The stated objective of IR activities is to reduce information asymmetry between corporate insiders and outsiders. Nevertheless, the effects IR activities have on information asymmetry are theoretically unclear. To begin with, insiders may not have the incentive to reveal accurate information to market participants. Depending on insiders’ incentives, IR can be a useful information-provision vehicle, a window-dressing tool, or even a market manipulation device. Moreover, the effects of IR activities also depend on how the information communicated via IR activities is used by investors and analysts. IR activities may lead to excessive stock volatility if investors react to the information with cognitive biases and analysts use their information advantages for insider trading and market manipulations. Existing empirical studies on IR activities have focused primarily on mature markets where legal frameworks are relatively well-established and investors are more sophisticated than those in the emerging markets. We plan to extend the literature by examining how IR activities affect information asymmetry in China – the biggest emerging market. We will focus on two types of IR activities, namely, the accessibility of corporate insiders to minority shareholders and corporate private meetings with analysts and institutional investors. Corporate accessibility to minority shareholders is the starting point that enables two-way communications between corporate insiders and outsiders. The effects of corporate private meetings with analysts and institutional investors have recently received substantial attention from scholars and regulators in the US but no study has examined this issue for emerging markets. We will manually collect data on these two types of IR activities and then formally test how they are related to information asymmetry. We believe that the proposed study will contribute to economics and finance knowledge as well as to help inform regulators and market participants about the IR activities and corporate governance of China’s listed firms 當公司股權和控制權分離，信息不對稱會威脅公司外部融資的獲得。於是，公司有動機在與不同市場參與者的溝通上投入資源。這種行爲被稱爲“投資者關係活動”。依據倫敦證券交易所發布的投資者關係維護行爲指南，“投資者關係活動”是指“公司與投資者群體持續溝通的行爲”。這種行爲是“股票市場活動的一部分”，並且對於“吸引和維持投資者資金的投入”十分重要（倫敦證券交易所，2010，p.2）。 投資者關係活動的目標是減少公司內部和外部人員的信息不對稱。然而，投資者關係活動對於信息不對稱的效應在理論上亦不清晰。首先，公司內部人員沒有動機向市場參與者公布准確的信息。基於公司內部人員的動機，投資者關係活動是一個重要的信息供給，或一種修飾工具，甚至是一種操縱方法。而且，投資者關係活動的效應同樣依賴於投資者和分析師如何對發布信息的解讀。如果投資者對於信息的反應具有認知偏誤，或者分析師利用信息優勢進行內幕交易或者市場操縱，投資者關係活動可能導致股價異常波動。 已有的針對投資者關係活動的實證研究主要集中於成熟市場，其法律框架相對規範，投資者保護相對新興市場更加成熟。我們計劃研究在中國——最大的新型國家——投資者關係活動如何影響信息不對稱，進而拓展已有研究的深度。我們會集中分析兩種投資者關係活動，即公司內部人士對於小股東接觸的回應，以及公司私下對於分析師和機構投資者的個別會面。公司內部人士對小股東接觸的有效回應，是公司內部人士與外部投資者雙向溝通的起點。而公司私下對於分析師和機構投資者的會面情況最近吸引了美國學者和監管者的關注，但是迄今沒有研究針對新興市場的情況。我們會手工收集兩種投資者關係行爲的數據，檢驗其同信息不對稱的關係。我們認爲本研究對於經濟學和金融相關領域具有學術貢獻，同時有助於監管者和市場參與者理解中國上市公司的投資者關係和公司治理。

391113.label: Major findings and research outcome
391113.value: The first paper as listed in 5.3. examines whether corporate accessibility is a signal of the severity of agency problems among the Chinese publicly listed firms. It is find that the firms providing corporate accessibility to outsiders are associated with less serious agency problems and better future firm performance. The research suggests that a firm's observable decision to provide corporate accessibility can be used to detect the hard-to-observe agency problems of the corporate insiders. The paper has received a revise and re-submission invitation from the Review of Accounting Studies. The revision has completed and the paper will be resubmitted in December 2017. The second paper listed in 5.3 examines the relationship between corporate accessibility and firm crash risks. It is find that the firms providing corporate accessibility to outsiders are associated with lower crash risks. The results suggest that corporate accessibility facilitates private communications with various market participants, which in turn reduces the possibility for corporate insiders to hide bad news from market participants. The paper has been presented at several major and prestigious conferences, which include 2016 FMA (European) meeting, 2016 FMA Annual meeting, 2017 CICF. The research team is now trying to incorporate the comments received from the conference participants. It will be submitted to a journal for review very soon.

391113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
391113.value: The research team will strive to get the above two papers published at prestigious journals. On the other hand, the research team of the second paper believes that corporate accessibility may also help to mitigate the information asymmetry and consequently mitigate investor sentiment effects. As a result, a new project will be launched to examine this issue.

391113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
391113.value: This project examines whether a publicly listed firm's investor relation (IR) activities can contain valuable information about a firm's fundamental conditions and whether these activities can reduce information asymmetry and improve the firm's information environment. We find that the willingness of a firm to provide effective communication with outsiders contain valuable information on the hard-to observe agency problems. Furthermore, IR activities can reduce information asymmetry as evidenced by the reduction in crash risks. IR activities have become increasingly common practices for publicly listed firms. Our research contributes to the literature by introducing a novel measure of corporate accessibility (the willingness of a firm's to respond to emails and phone calls from market participants) to capture the effective IR activities. We find that corporate accessibility can be a good device for detecting agency problems. The signaling effect of corporate accessibility can help investors to avoid investing in bad firms. It also helps regulators to better allocate their regulatory resources. Furthermore, our findings on the effectiveness of IR activities in reducing information asymmetry also provide guidance for publicly listed firms to plan their investment in IR activities.

399813.label: Project Title(Chinese)
399813.value: 基於變動年金動態研究下的最優消費和投資選擇

399813.label: Project Objectives
399813.value: The first objective focuses on how human capital interacts with financial assets in the variable annuity account and how the interaction changes the variable annuity policyholder’s behaviors, including asset allocation and consumption choices. I expect to find a human capital effect and a GMDB effect on the insured’s optimal decision. The second objective is to check if the guarantee options add value to the contract even if the term life policy is available. The third objective is to study insurance policyholders' optimal behaviors in a utility-based incomplete market framework. The policyholder actions are used to price the option after replacing the realistic probabilities with risk-neutral ones. The fourth objective is to contribute to this discussion by evaluating consumers' willingness to pay for GMDB protection in utility framework with a term insurance policy available. The fifth objective is to develop a multi-dimensional trinomial lattice in numerical analysis.

399813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
399813.value: Variable annuities are insurance contracts which provide periodic payments to the policyholder, usually after a deferment period. Their benefits are based on the performance of the underlying bond or equity portfolio. Condron (2008) reports that "more than $1.35 trillion was invested in variable annuities in the United States." Individuals buy variable annuities for many reasons. They are tax-deferred and protect the policyholder from outliving his assets during retirement. In addition, insurers offer various forms of option-like guarantees which provide protection against the downside risks of the subaccounts. A typical example of an option-like feature is Guaranteed Minimum Death Benefit (GMDB), which provides the beneficiary a lump sum amount upon the insured's death. GMDB helps protect the policy's beneficiary from negative market movements. Many papers discuss GMDB riders. The previous literature applies risk neutral optimality that presupposes the worst case from the insurer's perspective. From the insurer's perspective, GMDBs are able to be traded and hedged. Therefore, the worst thing is that the GMDB prices the largest under the risk neutral measure. The policyholders want to maximize the utility not the GMDB prices, so the worst case under risk averse optimality is not the worst case under risk neutral optimality. In this proposed project, we plan to extend existing literature by examining the insured’s optimal asset allocation and consumption choices in a variable annuity with a GMDB clause featuring partial withdrawals by using a utility-based approach and furthermore investigating how to price and hedge the GMDB contracts. This is a very meaningful area of study because China is planning to develop variable annuity scheme since 2011. We expect this project will contribute some value to both academic knowledge and China’s insurance industry. We will develop a model and try to answer the questions raised above. In the model, the insured gets utility from consumption and has bequest motives. We include the effect on asset allocation from both savings (accumulation) and dissavings (consumption). We also reflect bequest motives by including the utility of the recipient of the policyholders guaranteed death benefits. We derive the optimal transfer choice by the insured, and furthermore price the GMDB through maximizing the discounted expected utility of the policyholders and beneficiaries by investing dynamically in the fixed account and variable fund and withdrawing optimally. The study contributes to academic knowledge as well as gives industry a different perspective in the consideration of pricing and hedging variable annuity products.

399813.label: Major findings and research outcome
399813.value: Two papers have been developed. Paper One: The Effect of Labor Income and Health Risk on the Optimal Choices and the Valuation of Guaranteed Minimum Death Benefits We examine the effect of labor income and health risk on the optimal choices of policyholders with Guaranteed Minimum Death Benefits embedded in Variable Annuities. These choices are determined in the context of a utility-based life cycle model including bequest motives and optimal term life purchases. We then determine risk-neutral prices from the perspective of the issuing financial institutions. In contrast to previous studies which do not include income and health risk, we find that very risk-averse policyholders in weak job markets would be willing to pay the risk-neutral price in order to receive these benefits. This occurs because an unemployed individual with a low account balance would be unwilling to pay for term insurance, but has precommitted to pay the now small GMDB fees in exchange for the death benefits. Paper Two: The Demand for Annuity and Long-term Care Insurance Individual retirees face two important risks: rising health care costs and increased life expectancy. Health shocks and longevity risk are inherently connected since death represents the end state in an individual’s health state transition process. A longer life expectancy can be attributed to a prolonged time span during which the individual stays healthy, i.e., compression of morbidity (Fries 2005), or associated with a relatively more increase in the length of an unhealthy state, i.e., expansion of morbidity (Olshansky et al. 1991). A third hypothesis (the dynamic equilibrium theory) points to an overall stable relative length of unhealthy life expectancy. There is still no consensus in the literature on which pattern truly captures individuals’ evolution of health states. In this paper, we use a life-cycle model to investigate how the health state transition process affects an individual’s demand for long-term care insurance and life annuity, in addition to other standard investment products such as bonds and stocks. Our paper contributes to the existing literature in several ways. First, we develop a dynamic multistate transition model where the transition probabilities depend on age and calendar time. Second, we answer the question as to what is the demand for long-term care insurance and life annuity under the compression, expansion and dynamic equilibrium hypothesis, respectively.

399813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
399813.value: Currently, I have presented these two papers in some international conferences, e.g. the Annual Meeting of American Risk and Insurance Association 2016, the Annual Meeting of Longevity 2016 and the Annual meeting of Asia-Pacific Risk and Insurance Association 2017. We have received some comments. We are revising and polishing the papers and going to submit them to some academic journals.

399813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
399813.value: Our research will have significant implications for life insurance companies and for policymakers. In paper one, we examine when and why variable annuity policyholders are purchasing GMDB options. In paper two, we investigate the impact of longevity risk and health care shocks on an individual’s retirement planning. These two risks are often intertwined with each other and impose great challenges on financial budgets for the aged population after their retirement. This outcome has economic implication to any aged populations, like Hong Kong, as to retirement product design and retirement portfolio choice.

399913.label: Project Objectives

399913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
399913.value: Authoritarian leadership is defined negatively in the extant literature and shows negative effects on subordinates and subsequently, organizations. For this reason, it is puzzling that this dysfunctional leadership style is still prevalent in Chinese societies after decades of industrialization and modernization despite rapid development of Chinese firms. A simple conclusion that authoritarianism is negative seems unable to account for these observations. The proposed project seeks to address this research gap by extending my previous work on the duality of authoritarianism leadership. Integrating classical Confucian thought and theorizing in developmental and educational psychology, I theorized and found that authoritarian leadership could be differentiated into two dimensions. The directive-achieving dimension is a directive and controlling style that has an achievement and training focus, whereas the autocratic dimension, the prior conceptualization of authoritarian leadership, is solely concerned with domination. Findings based on Chinese samples confirm that directive-achieving and autocratic leadership have positive and negative effects on subordinates, respectively. Extending this line of research, this project aims to further validate the newly identified directive-achieving leadership concept with two major objectives. First, it contrasts the different learning mechanisms of subordinates that transmit the effects of directive-achieving leadership and relevant developmental practices from Western literature which overlap with the training focus of directive-achieving leadership. Directive-achieving behavior occurs in a hierarchical context with the emphasis on achievement and continuous improvement, which is conducive to persistence and depth of exploration within a few scopes specified by the leader. On the other hand, the egalitarian nature of general development practices may be conductive to flexibility and width of exploration. Based on the dual pathway to creativity model which posits that creativity can be achieved by persistence or flexibility, I proposed that directive-achieving leadership and general development practices are positively related to creativity as well as job performance through these two qualitatively different mechanisms, namely, persistence and flexibility, respectively. My second objective is to examine the effects of directive-achieving leadership across cultures. The concept of directive-achieving leadership originated from the indigenous research of China, a high power distance culture. To fully validate this style as a universalistic leadership concept, this project seeks to examine its effects across cultures varying in power distance. If directive-achieving leadership turns out to be important even in the low power distance cultures, it would provide a good example of how Chinese indigenous research can contribute to universal theorizing. 現有文獻對威權領導的定義是負面的。然而對中國文化的深入分析表明簡單地把其歸納為一種負面的領導是不全面的。通過整合儒家思想和相關理論，我提出並發現一種正面的威權領導—規誨領導。 該課題旨在進一步檢驗這個新的概念。第一個目標是區別規誨和變革領導對下屬學習機制的影響。根據創新的雙重路徑模型，兩種領導通過分別影響思維韌性和彈性從而影響下屬的創新和工作績效。該課題擬在不同權力距離文化中檢驗規誨領導是否具普世性。

400213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
400213.value: This project studies the geometry of the Homological Mirror Symmetry (HMS) conjecture which was proposed by Fields Medalist Maxim Kontsevich in his 1994 ICM address. Mirror symmetry is a duality between two different physical theories which give rise to the same predictions about nature. Mathematically, it predicts deep yet mysterious connections between seemingly very different geometries on a manifold and its mirror. Hence understanding the geometry of mirror symmetry will lead to a broader comprehension of different geometric structures. Kontsevich's HMS conjecture can be viewed as an algebraic and categorical formulation of mirror symmetry. It states that the Fukaya category (symplectic-geometric) of a manifold is equivalent to the derived category of coherent sheaves (algebraic-geometric) of the mirror, and vice versa. In the last 18 years, mathematicians have been striving toward settling the conjecture. Indeed, much evidence has been found and it was verified in numerous examples. Nevertheless, we are still lacking a proper understanding of the geometry behind this conjecture. On the other hand, Strominger, Yau and Zaslow proposed in 1996 a geometric explanation for mirror symmetry. Their proposal (the SYZ conjecture) has attracted a lot of attention since then and has proved to be very promising. The main objective of this proposal is to pursue a geometric understanding of the HMS conjecture via the SYZ proposal. The PI plans to construct a geometric Fourier-type functor which realizes the equivalences of categories asserted by the HMS conjecture, making use of the SYZ construction. A major step in this construction will be defining the transformation on morphism spaces and higher A-infinity operations. The PI also plans to investigate the transformation of higher rank holomorphic bundles over toric varieties, understand the correspondence between matrix factorizations and Lagrangian torus fibers, and study the HMS for toric Calabi-Yau manifolds to see how the wrapped Fukaya category comes in. We will also apply our construction to understand various geometric phenomena in mirror symmetry, such as how instanton corrections (i.e. disk counting) arises in Floer theory, why the quantum product in Floer cohomology is corresponding to the classical product in Dolbeault cohomology on the mirror side, and whether the mirror map coincides with the change of variables which appears in the HMS equivalences. These are all questions of central importance to mirror symmetry. 本項目研究由菲爾茲獎得主Maxim Kontsevich在1994年世界數學家大會中所提出的同調鏡對稱猜想的幾何。 鏡對稱是兩個給出相同自然現象但原本不同的物理理論之間的對偶現象。在數學上，它預測流形和它的鏡像上完全不同的幾何之間的深邃而神秘的連接。理解鏡對稱的幾何可令我們對不同的幾何結構有更廣泛的理解。 Kontsevich 的同調鏡對稱猜想可以被看作是鏡對稱的一個代數和範疇描述。它提出一個流形的Fukaya範疇（辛幾何）應該等價於它的鏡像上的凝聚層的導出範疇，反之亦然。在過去的18年中，數學家一直致力解決這個猜想。事實上，很多證據已被發現，它亦在無數的例子中被驗證。儘管如此，我們仍然缺乏對這猜想背後的幾何的一個適當的理解。 另一方面，另一位菲爾茲獎得主丘成桐和他的合作者Strominger和Zaslow在1996年提出一個鏡對稱的幾何解釋。他們的建議（ SYZ猜想）自那時開始已吸引了不少關注，而且亦已被證明是非常有說服力的。本項目的主要目的正是通過SYZ猜想給出同調鏡對稱猜想的幾何意義。 在這個項目中，PI計劃利用SYZ猜想來構造一個幾何傅立葉型的函子來實現同調鏡對稱猜想所斷言的等價關係。在這種構造中，一個重要步驟將是確定如何定義映射空間和高A-無窮操作的變換。PI還計劃探討高階全純束在環面蔟的變換，了解矩陣分解和拉格朗日的圓環纖維之對應關係，以及研究環面卡拉比-丘流形的同調鏡對稱猜想與如何引進包裹Fukaya範疇。 我們也將應用我們的構造試圖了解鏡對稱的各種幾何現象，例如瞬子修正如何出現在Floer理論上，為什麼Floer上同調的量子乘積是對應於鏡像流形上的古典Dolbeault上同調，以及鏡像映射是否等於同調鏡對稱中出現的變量變換。這些問題都是在鏡對稱的研究中都是至關重要的。

400213.label: Realisation of objectives
400213.value: The first objective of this project was to construct a geometric Fourier-type functor which realizes the equivalences of categories asserted by Kontsevich's HMS conjecture. The PI and collaborators succeeded in constructing the desired functor for all toric Calabi-Yau surfaces and some examples of toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds. More precisely, for any toric Calabi-Yau surface, which is a crepant resolution of the quotient of C^2, and certain toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds including any small toric Calabi-Yau 3-fold, we constructed a geometric Fourier-type functor using SYZ transforms, and proved that the functor induces an equivalence between the derived category of coherent sheaves over the toric Calabi-Yau manifold and the derived wrapped Fukaya category of the mirror (which is a noncompact Calabi-Yau manifold having the structure of a conic fibration). In particular, this gives the first complete computation of the wrapped Fukaya category of a 6-dimensional Liouville domain, which is neither a product of lower dimensional manifolds nor a cotangent bundle, and implies new results on Bridgeland stability conditions on Fukaya categories of 6-dimensional symplectic manifolds. The PI would like to extend our results to the higher dimensional case. But one main obstacle is the lack of a construction of good Lagrangian sections. In the two and three dimensional cases, we made use of Abouzaid’s tropical localization to construct nice Lagrangian sections of the SYZ fibrations which are fibered over curves in the base of the conic fibration. We were also able to show that these Lagrangian submanifolds split generate the wrapped Fukaya category. However, we still do not know how to construct suitable Lagrangian submanifolds in the higher dimensional case. The second objective of this project was to understand various geometric phenomena, such as quantum corrections in morphism spaces and the change of variables formula, which arise in the HMS conjecture. The PI and collaborators were able to accomplish this goal for all the examples we discussed above. Indeed the SYZ transforms only define the functor on the object level, and the HMS equivalences were proved by computations on both sides. This is not desirable because we would also like to see how morphisms can be transformed using SYZ. But in our concrete examples, after doing the computations explicitly, it is not hard to guess how the functor should be defined on the morphism level. Still, we would like to have a more intrinsic way to define the functor, and this is the direction on which the PI plans to make more progress in the next project. The third objective of this project was to use SYZ transforms to give explicit geometric correspondences between Lagrangian cycles in a manifold and holomorphic cycles (such as coherent sheaves, matrix factorizations) in the mirror. This was done for the correspondence between Lagrangian sections and holomorphic line bundles for all toric Calabi-Yau surfaces and certain toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds including all the small toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds, in works of the PI and collaborators. The PI has also asked one of his MPhil students (Mr. Shun-Wai Chung) to study SYZ transforms for Aganagic-Vafa branes in toric Calabi-Yau manifolds. One interesting phenomenon for these examples is that the holomorphic disks with boundaries on the Lagrangian itself now play an important role in defining the SYZ transform. Put in another way, this means the SYZ transform does not produce the correct mirror if it does not take into account the quantum corrections coming from the Lagrangian brane itself. This does not happen for the previous examples due to some topological reason which rule out such quantum corrections. The PI is currently investigating SYZ transform for more general branes, in particular, for Lagrangian multi-sections and Lagrangian submanifolds with more nontrivial topology. The goal is to understand how quantum corrections affect the construction of SYZ transforms in general.

400213.label: Major findings and research outcome
400213.value: By applying the PI’s previous work on SYZ construction of the mirrors for toric Calabi-Yau manifolds, the PI and collaborators have succeeded in constructing a geometric Fourier-type functor using SYZ transforms to realize the equivalences between triangulated categories asserted by Kontsevich's Homological Mirror Symmetry conjecture in this project. More precisely, for any toric Calabi-Yau surface and any small toric Calabi-Yau 3-fold, we proved that the geometric functor we constructed gives an equivalence between the derived category of coherent sheaves over the toric Calabi-Yau manifold and the derived wrapped Fukaya category of the mirror (which is a noncompact Calabi-Yau manifold having the structure of a conic fibration). This in particular gives the first complete computation of the wrapped Fukaya category of a 6-dimensional Liouville domain, which is neither a product of lower dimensional manifolds nor a cotangent bundle, and we also obtain some new results on Bridgeland stability conditions on Fukaya categories of 6-dimensional symplectic manifolds. For a general toric Calabi-Yau 3-fold, we have computed the wrapped Floer cohomology of the SYZ mirror of its structure sheaf and show that it is isomorphic (as a ring) to the ring of holomorphic functions. This are new examples on computation of wrapped Floer cohomology and symplectic cohomology, which were known in only a handful of examples.

400213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
400213.value: As we mentioned above, our results should be generalized to higher dimensional examples. What we need is a construction of Lagrangian sections which can generate the (wrapped) Fukaya category. This would require new techniques. But the recent work of Gross-Matessi on a more topological construction of Lagrangian sections seems quite suitable for generalization to higher dimensions. On the other hand, it is very important and interesting to look at SYZ transforms for other types of Lagrangians, more general than just Lagrangian sections. One class is Lagrangian multi-sections, whose SYZ mirrors should give holomorphic vector bundles over the mirror space. One may also consider Lagrangians which are fibered over subspaces of the base of the SYZ fibration, whose SYZ mirrors should produce coherent sheaves over proper subvarieties in the mirror space. Finally, the metric aspects of the geometry of SYZ transforms are largely unexplored. This is significant because taking into account the metrics could provide us more refined information which is not quite accessible by the homological approach. One interesting question is the relation between special Lagrangians and solutions of the (deformed) Hermitian Yang-Mills equation on the mirror side. The PI is currently working on these problems in a subsequent project.

400213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
400213.value: Mirror Symmetry was discovered by String theorists in the early 1990s. It predicts that there is a highly nontrivial and mysterious equivalence between the Symplectic Geometry of a space and the Complex Geometry of a completely different space. This led to numerous surprising and deep mathematical conjectures. Since its discovery, mathematicians have been striving to understand the geometry of Mirror Symmetry. A breakthrough came in 1996 when Strominger, Yau and Zaslow proposed that Mirror Symmetry should be understood as a geometric Fourier transform. Lying at the heart of the SYZ conjecture is the role played by quantum corrections, which is the key to explain the miraculous power of Mirror Symmetry. Our geometric proofs of Kontsevich's Homological Mirror Symmetry (HMS) conjecture using SYZ transforms is an important step in the study of quantum corrections and Mirror Symmetry. Our results provide important insight on how cycles are being transformed under Mirror Symmetry and explain the geometry behind the HMS conjecture.

400313.label: Project Objectives
400313.value: The main objective of the proposed study is to develop useful statistical methodologies for the analysis of nonstationary, heavy-tailed and/or long-memory time series, and to study the limiting distributions of the underlying statistics for statistical inference. In particular, we propose to establish a unified approach to study the weak convergence results of various models, which previously had to be dealt with in a case-by-case manner. The second and equally important goal is to establish the higher-order asymptotics of the corresponding limiting results obtained in Objective 1. It is well known that limiting distributions only constitute the first stage of asymptotic inference. To further understand the underlying properties, higher-order asymptotics are required so that both powers and sizes can be evaluated. Furthermore, higher-order asymptotics provide useful tools for model selection and quantile calculation. As the asymptotic results involve evaluating the nonstandard limiting distributions of stochastic integrals of generalized stochastic processes with random jumps and/or fractional Brownian motions, which is computationally challenging, we aim to develop efficient algorithms to compute these procedures in real time. Using the asymptotic results established in the proposed study, we will develop efficient numerical procedures that can be applied empirically. As finance is a rapidly developing discipline, it is crucial that pioneering research results be incorporated into the pedagogical front in a timely fashion. Because practitioners are faced with the challenge of handling operational risks that are nonstationary in nature, the successful completion of this project will lead to a deeper understanding of these statistical methods, which will enhance the applicability of nonstationary time series to risk management and other disciplines.

400313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
400313.value: The recent surge of activity in risk management and financial econometrics has led to a huge demand for non-standard statistical procedures to be developed for the modeling of nonstationary and non-regular time series. In general, these types of time series belong to the area of critical phenomena, in which non-standard asymptotics are the rules rather than the exceptions. It is now generally accepted that the dynamic nature of diverse physical and financial phenomena requires one to take into account the ever-changing nonstationary, heavy-tailed and long-memory behavior. Throughout the past two decades, a cascade of theoretical research on the inference of non-stationary and heavy-tailed time series has been developed. In the course of these developments, it was found that many of the standard tools in asymptotic theory are not applicable and that there is a need to develop new ideas of weak convergence under different topologies. In general, the weak convergence technique used in the finite variance case is very different from the infinite variance case, which in turn is drastically different from the long-memory case. With the concerted efforts of many scholars, it is now high time to assemble these results in order to offer a more comprehensive treatment of the asymptotic theory for critical phenomena. One major objective of the proposed study is to pursue a comprehensive treatment of these asymptotic theories, from which we expect to derive new insights into these crucial phenomena. Establishing the weak convergence of the relevant statistics constitutes only the first stage in the asymptotic inference. To understand the properties of the test statistics, one also needs to consider higher-order asymptotics so that both the powers and sizes of the test can be calibrated. Recently, Chan and Ing (2011) established a negative moment bound for the Fisher’s information matrix of a general time series, which provides the critical component for developing the higher-order asymptotics, including but not limited to model selection, quantile calculation, and size and power evaluations. The second objective of this study is to extend the idea of moment bounds to general non-stationary time series and to apply the moment bounds in the model selection of non-stationary time series. Although many of these theoretical results are highly technical, it is expected that further understanding of the numerical underpinnings will be realized in this study, from which relevant practical implications can be derived. 非平稳的时间序列式临界现象的其中一个特例。处理這種现象要利用非一般的大样本理论。近年的金融風暴特显了非平稳的时间序列在金融和计量经济中的应用。 這研究计划有两个重要目标。首先，我们会發展相关的弱收敛理论。在临界现象下，一般的弱收敛是不适用的。一套新的统一弱收敛要重新建立。 另外一个重要目标是要發展有关的高阶的大樣本漸近理论。极限分布只是第一步。要研究验证和漸近信用区间，我们要知道进一步的高阶的大樣本漸近结果。而近期 Chan and Ing (2011) 有关 Negative Moment Bounds 的结果正好提供了这方面的背景。这研究计划会把这类结果推到非平稳的时间序列上。为模型选择和大樣本理论提供了前瞻的技术和结果。
