400313.label: Major findings and research outcome
400313.value: The major finding of this proposal is to develop a unified weak convergence theory to conduct statistical inference for nonstationary and heavy-tailed,time series models. In particular, by making use of weak convergence of Brownian motions and Levy processes, limit distributions of various statistics can be constructed and testing the adequacy of the models can be performed. Further, by means of numerical integration methods, new algorithmes have also been developedto handle the non-standard asymptotics that involve Brownian motions and Levy processes. The collected research outcomes not only offer an entirely new way to analyze nonstationary and heavy-tailed phenomena in financial time series, but also to other disciplines such as network traffic, internet data, and e-commerce. Important research findings from this project were reported in major international conferences and published in premiere refereed journals and books, as stipulated in Part C: Tables 8 and 9.

400313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
400313.value: As weak convergence techniques are general in nature, the results obtained in this proposal can be used in many other contexts. In particular, by establishing the limit distributions of various statistics of nonstationary and heavy-tailed time series, results from this project offer a novel way to analyze time series with jump behaviors, which is of huge potential interest in financial risk management. The techniques developed in this project can be applied both to the long-memory and nonlinear cases with heavy-tailed innovations. Finally, in areas such as financial risk management and network engineering, where heavy-tailed and long-range dependence are rules rather than exceptions, results of this project offer a useful alternative to the traditional methods for conducting statistical inference.

400313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
400313.value: All of the major objectives have been realized in this project. By virtue of the weak convergence techniques, advances in model estimation and calibration can now be efficiently conducted. This will bring significant impacts in modeling important features not only for nonstationary time series, but also for heavy-tailed series where jump behaviors are common as in the case of portfolio management and network traffic. In particular, the first three objectives achieved in this proposal offer a platform and new direction that will lead to important advances in the pursuit of modeling financial data. In addition, by developing numerical algorithms in evaluating the limit distributions involving Brownian motions and Levy processes, many of the statistics can now be computed, which would enhance their applications in various disciplines. Finally, by publishing relevant papers and monographs in the field of risk management and statistics as reoirted in Part C, important research developments can be disseminated to practitioners timely and effectively.

400813.value: 交錯間斷Galerkin方法的快速解法

400813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
400813.value: The aim of this project is to develop and analyze a class of fast solvers for the linear algebraic systems arising from the staggered discontinuous Galerkin discretization of partial differential equations. Recently, the staggered discontinuous Galerkin methods have been developed for a large class of partial differential equations, including the wave equations, the convection-diffusion equations, the Maxwell's equations and the Stokes system. The success of the staggered discontinuous Galerkin methods is based on an innovative construction of a staggered triangulation as well as a stable pair of finite element spaces defined on it. This staggered continuity property naturally preserves the local and global structures of the partial differential equation being approximated as well as gives a conservative flux without introducing numerical fluxes and penalty parameters in contrast to standard discontinuous Galerkin methods. Due to these unique advantages of the methods, they have great potential to be used for many realistic applications. The use of these methods will typically result in a large linear algebraic system which is computationally intensive to solve by direct methods. In respect of this issue, we have some recent advances in the development of fast solvers for scalar elliptic equations with great success. However, the development of fast solvers for other types of equations is still open. In this project, we will develop a class of fast iterative solvers for the staggered discontinuous Galerkin discretizations of the curl-curl equation and the Stokes system. Moreover, we will provide a rigorous mathematical analysis for the condition numbers of the methods. We will also conduct careful numerical studies to test the performance of the methods. The proposed research will provide a class of iterative solvers that can efficiently solve the equations considered with the number of iterations independent of the problem size. Our recent research of fast solvers for the scalar elliptic equation has shown that these methods perform very well. Thus, there are incentives to further develop our methodologies for other kinds of partial differential equations, in particular, the curl-curl equation and the Stokes system. The results of the proposed research will significantly advance the state-of-the-art knowledge of fast iterative solvers for linear algebraic systems arising from the discretization of partial differential equations, as well as provide some efficient and parallelizable solvers for many realistic scientific applications. 本課題的主要目的是開發和研究線性代數系統的快速解法。這些線性代數系統出自偏微分方程的交錯間斷Galerkin離散化過程。 最近，交錯間斷Galerkin離散化方法被應用在多種類型偏微分方程的求解過程中，包括波動方程，對流傳導方程，馬克斯維爾方程組和斯托克思系統。其成功的主要原因是構造創新的交錯三角形剖分和相應的穩定有限元空間組。這種交錯的連續性很自然的保持了原有偏微分方程的區域以及整體結構，並且相比標準間斷Galerkin離散方法，它可以在不引用人為流量和參數的情況下保持流量守恆。基於這些獨有的優勢，這種新方法很可能將被廣泛的運用在實際應用中。在使用中，我們通常需要求解大型線性代數系統，如果直接求解的話運算量過大將會成為問題。好消息是近日在標量橢圓方程的快速求解方面有很大突破。但是，對於其他類型的方程如何快速求解還有待研究。 在這個課題中，我們將會研究開發快速迭代算法，並應用在交錯間斷Galerkin離散化求解旋度方程和斯托克思系統中。我們還會通過嚴謹的數學分析給出條件參數。最後進行數值實驗來檢測其應用效果。 本課題將會給出一類高效率求解的迭代算法，並且迭代次數不依賴於問題規模大小。我們最近的研究表明這類方法可以快速求解標量橢圓方程。因此，我們也有興趣繼續學習研究這類算法，推廣應用到其他類型的偏微分方程，特別是旋度方程和斯托克思系統。文中提及的研究結果將會大幅度提高偏微分方程離散化中線性代數系統的迭代解法的技術發展水平，並且也為許多其他實際應用問題提供了高效的替換算法。

400813.label: Realisation of objectives
400813.value: The proposed objectives are the design of efficient preconditioners as well as their mathematical analysis, and they are satisfactorily achieved. In the design of the preconditioners, the PI considered the framework of domain decomposition method. In particular, Schwarz, BDDC and FETI-DP methodologies are considered as a way to precondition the discretized linear system. One of the key components is the choice of the coarse degrees of freedom. For the discontinuous Galerkin methods considered in the project, there is an advantage that the degrees of freedom related to the grid vertices are decoupled, and only the degrees of freedom on the edges are coupled via the two adjacent elements. This fact greatly simplifies the choice of coarse unknowns. In particular, one can choose a common degree of freedom on an edge or face as coarse unknowns. The next important ingredient is a stable decomposition property. This property is also related to the choice of coarse degrees of freedom. Proving the stable decomposition property is in general a challenging task. Nevertheless, we have successfully shown that our proposed methods lead to a stable decomposition using the coarse spaces. Finally, we have implemented the proposed methods and conducted some numerical tests and validate our methods. We have performed extensive studies numerically. Our results show that the proposed preconditioners are very robust, and confirm the theoretical results.

400813.label: Major findings and research outcome
400813.value: We will summarize the major findings in the project. First of all, for systems involving complex media with many scales and high contrast, classical preconditioning techniques, which use one degree of freedom per coarse region in the global coarse space, fail as the condition numbers depend highly on the heterogeneities and contrast. Thus one needs to enrich the global coarse space in order to obtain a robust preconditioner. It is known that polynomial space is not a good choice as the resulting coarse space will have a large dimension. In the project, we develop a novel adaptive choice of coarse space. The main idea is to use local spectral problem, which gives dominant modes in the local region. To obtain our coarse space, we set a tolerance, and then use all eigenfunctions corresponding to the eigenvalues that are smaller than the given tolerance. Then we show that the resulting conditioner is very robust, and performs independently with the coefficients. Secondly, we have found that the design of the local spectral problems for coarse face and edge are very crucial. More precisely, for the face spectral problem, we need to use harmonic extensions and energy minimizing extensions in order to obtain a robust condition number bound. For the edge spectral problem, this is more tricky. In our work, we design a spectral problem which is based on some energy minimization on a neighbourhood having a given edge. The resulting condition number is very robust.

400813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
400813.value: There are rooms for further development. In particular, a large class of applications results in huge nonlinear systems. Existing techniques are not directly applicable for nonlinear problems. To design effective and efficient domain decomposition techniques for nonlinear problem is a big challenge. One possible way is to construct some local nonlinear eigenvalue problems for the constructions of adaptive coarse spaces. By using such coarse spaces, one can develop robust domain decomposition ideas for nonlinear systems.

400813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
400813.value: The aim of the research is to develop a class of fast methods for solving large-scale scientific problems. In practical scenarios, one needs to solve systems with a large number of unknowns, and solving these problems require significant amount of computational times by classical techniques. In the proposed research, the PI developed some fast strategies for solving these problems. These strategies are based on the domain decomposition idea. In particular, smaller problems are solved in parallel, and the solutions of these small problems are suitably combined in the global solve. The resulting iterative scheme provides a very efficient way to solve large scale problems. The findings in the project have very great impacts in basic science research as well as realistic scientific applications.

400913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
400913.value: The functions of biomolecules, such as protein and RNA, are largely determined by their structures and structural dynamics. While performing the biological functions, biomolecules may undergo reversible transitions between alternative structures, which are called different conformations. Conformations with lower free energy are more stable, but the transition between different conformations is complicated. The energy landscape of a conformational space often consists of multiple low-energy wells separated by high-energy barriers that hinder cross-barrier conformational changes. Understanding the energy landscape is crucial for understanding many complex processes, such as protein-protein interaction, RNA-folding, and protein-folding. Existing experimental techniques for studying conformational changes have difficulty to provide dynamic information of conformational changes at atomic resolution. Molecular Dynamics and Monte Carlo computer simulations can complement these experiments at the atomic level. However, they can only simulate the dynamics of biomolecules at the nanosecond timescale, which is far away from the timescale of microseconds or longer for real biological conformational changes. Some computational methods, such as Markov state models, have been proposed to bridge this gap. However, how to elucidate the energy landscape from the computer dynamics simulations remains unclear. In this proposal, we will use a Bayesian model-based approach to analyze the discretized trajectories from computer simulations as an effort to elucidate the energy landscape. A family of models and accompanying computing algorithms are proposed to automatically partition the conformational space into an unknown number of clusters, which are ideally corresponding to separated energy wells, and study the relationship between clusters. Unlike traditional clustering methods, here we propose probabilistic generative models for the pairwise co-occurrence count data summarized from multiple trajectories, and provide new Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithms to infer both the number of clusters and the cluster labels in the form of posterior distribution. Preliminary experiments on both synthetic data sets and a real biomolecule system called the Alanine dipeptide have shown the accuracy and efficiency of our approach. The results developed in this project will provide a new way to integrate the trajectory data computer simulation and elucidate the complex energy landscape of biomolecules. This will be very helpful for structural biologists, biochemists and drug designers. The developed approach, with some adaption, may also be applied to general pairwise data in order to detect the structure of a population, e.g., detecting academic cliques from citation data, detecting related books or movies from sales data, or detecting friend circles from social network data. 蛋白質和RNA等生物分子的功能在很大程度上取決於它們的結構和其不同可能結構間的動態變化。一個生物分子的結構空間的自由能分佈並不均勻。具有低自由能的穩定結構被自由能高的不穩定結構所形成的壁壘隔開，使得不同結構之間的跳轉關係往往很複雜。對分子自由能格局的研究是理解許多複雜的過程（如蛋白質間的交互、RNA折疊和蛋白質折疊）的關鍵。 現有實驗技術很難提供在原子層面的結構動態信息，所以基於計算機模擬的方法被廣泛採用以做補充。然而當前計算機分子模擬能達到的時間尺度限於納秒級，遠不能達到實際生物分子結構變化過程所需的微秒級。雖然相關研究人員已經嘗試一些方法以彌補該差距，但是尚未解決如何從計算機分子模擬數據學習出結構空間的能量格局的問題。 在這項研究計劃中，我們將用基於概率模型的貝葉斯方法，從大量並行的計算機分子模擬產生的離散結構間的跳轉數據中推算結構空間的能量格局。我們將為該問題設計新的統計模型和相應的計算算法。該算法將對分子的結構空間根據能量狀態自動分區。 該研究將提供一個新的用來整合計算機分子模擬產生的軌跡數據的聚類方法。這將對結構生物學家、化學家和藥物設計師非常有幫助。該方法經過改造，也可被用於分析一般的成對數據。

400913.label: Realisation of objectives
400913.value: All five objectives are fully achieved. For the first objective, we developed the block-wise Poisson partition model for clustering conformational trajectory data. The transition observed on the trajectories is summarized to a count matrix. The transition within a cluster corresponds to a block along the diagonal line of the count matrix, where the counts are assumed to be from a Poisson distribution. Off-diagonal blocks correspond to the transition between different clusters, where the counts are from Poisson distributions of different parameters. The second objective is achieved by an advanced Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm. The cluster labels are updated using a Gibbs move. The number of clusters are updated using two moves: an Metropolis-Hastings move mimicking the Chinese restaurant process to create or delete a single-member cluster; a collapsed Gibbs move to divide or merge current clusters. The algorithm is efficient to explore the posterior distribution of the number of clusters and cluster labels. For the third objective, synthetic datasets from the generative model and the benchmark real data from the molecular dynamics simulation of the biomolecule alanine dipeptide is used to evaluate our method and compare with existing methods PCCA and MPPA. The fourth objective is achieved by the detail analysis of two biomolecules: Ala-dipeptide and Villin HP35 double mutant Nle/Nle. Detail landscape pictures in the angular planes are provided. The fifth objective is achieved by publishing related methods and their applications, and sharing related software codes online. All clustering results of Ala-dipeptide and Villin HP35 double mutant Nle/Nle are also shared via the Internet. We not only fulfilled all the above five objectives, but also introduced a second clustering model based on a tree structure for handling molecular dynamics trajectories from a different perspective. More specifically, we introduced the conditional angle partition tree to elucidate the landscape of the conformational space according to local structure characteristics.

400913.label: Major findings and research outcome
400913.value: (Note: Journal papers listed in Part C/Section 8 are cited here according to their order in the table of Section 8) As planned by the project, we investigated on clustering methods for partitioning the conformational space of biomolecules. Although we only proposed to provide one such model, we eventually developed two methods for partitioning the conformational space: one based on a Poisson model [10] and another based on a tree model [9]. Related computing problems are also investigated and solved [2]. To deepen the research, we also investigated how to apply these models and computing algorithms in other settings [1,4,6,8] and how other clustering methods can be used for this project. During this process, we proposed some other clustering methods which eventually not efficient for clustering the conformational space, but efficient in other settings [3,5,7]. The major findings and research outcomes at the algorithm side include several new or improved clustering methods, including the Poisson partition model [10], the conditional angle partition tree [9], the Chinese Restaurant Process [8], HMM [7], the finite mixture model [5], and the mix-effect model [3]. Important general problems of clustering methods are also investigated. For example, [2] provided a better solution to solve the label switching problem during Bayesian clustering inference. At the subject side, we not only used the developed methods of this project to solve the conformational space partition problem [9,10], but also applied these methods in embryonic gene expression analysis [1], gene network inference [4], branch point detection [5], multiple sequence alignment [6], methylation analysis [7] and multinomial distribution inference [7]. The application of our new clustering methods on biomolecular conformational spaces resulted in findings which advanced our understanding of the biomolecules. The results in [9] and [10] showed that local angles play a crucial role in determine the clustering structure of the conformational space. Our clustering results of both Ala-dipeptide and Villin HP35 double mutant Nle/Nle are of higher quality than previous results.

400913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
400913.value: At the application side, the models and computing methods produced by this project can be applied for many similar clustering problems. In the new era of big data, there is an increasing demand to form hypothesis from datasets, where clustering methods can be used to check the pattern and facilitate the forming of hypothesis. Especially, when only the transition among a space is observed, our methods for clustering conformations can be directly applied. At the methodology side, the conditional angle partition tree model raised a challenge for probabilistic inference in some cases. We will continue revising the model and improving its computing performance.

400913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
400913.value: The structural dynamics of a protein determines how it functions, thus studying the modularity of the structural space of a protein is important. We developed new clustering models and related computing algorithms to cluster the structural space of a protein based on structural transition data. Both computer simulation and real applications showed that our methods performed well. The results provided new vision for structural biology studies. Directly applications of our methods in biomedical studies include but not limited to drug design, enzyme study and fundamental molecular process. Furthermore, our methods can also be applied to general pairwise data in order to detect the structure of a population, e.g., detecting related books or movies from sales data, or detecting friend circles from social network data.

401013.label: Project Objectives
401013.value: It is proposed to study the dimension of orthogonal projections and slices of self-similar and self-affine sets and measures along concrete directions. In the literature, there have been some partial results for the projections and slices of self-similar sets satisfying the strong separation condition. Our focus will be on general self-similar fractals and certain self-affine fractals. It is proposed to further study the dimensional properties of almost all self-affine sets and measures. The focus is on the dimension of projections of arbitrary subsets and arbitrary measures in symbolic spaces under the coding maps associated with almost all self-affine IFSs. The Renyi dimension of almost all self-affine measures will be further investigated.

401013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
401013.value: The dimension (with its various definitions) of fractal sets and measures is among the most important characteristics in fractal analysis. It often relates to different features of geometric and dynamical structures of the underling sets and measures. So far the explicit dimensional formulas have been obtained in the literature for non-overlapping self-similar sets and measures, and a few classes of self-affine fractals. It remains a challenging problem to estimate the dimension of other families of self-similar and self-affine fractals, as well as the dimension of the orthogonal projections of fractal sets and their intersections with lines and planes. In this proposal, the Principal Investigator will study some dimensional properties about typical self-affine fractals. Morover he will study the dimension of slicing sets and measures of fractals along concrete directions, and will study the validity of dimension conservation principle for general self-similar sets and certain affine sets. The study of this project will lead to a better understanding of the dimension theory of fractal sets and measures. 維數在分形集合與測度的刻畫研究中起著至關重要的作用。它和這些集合與測度的幾何與動力系統結構密切相關。對於非重疊的自相似集與自相似測度，以及一類特殊的自仿分形，人們已得到具體的維數公式。然而對於一般自相似及自仿分形，以及它們截集及正交投影，其維數的估計還是一個困難的問題。在該項課題中，我們將研究典型自仿分形的維數性質，分形集合與測度截集及投影性質， 以及維數守恆律。這些研究將加深我們對分形維數理論的理解。

401013.label: Realisation of objectives
401013.value: In this project, we mainly investigate the dimension of fractal sets and measures under two kind of projections: orthogonal projections in the Euclidean space and the projection from the symbolic space to the the Euclidean space under the coding map (associated to certain iterated function systems.) In the first situation, the classical Marstrand theorem states that the Hausdorff dimension of the orthogonal projection of a planar set (or measure) to a line along typical directions admits a simple formula. As listed in our first objective, it is an important and interseting question to analyze how the Hausdorff dimension changes under concrete orthogal projections. For this item, we consider the orthogonal projection of a family of planar random self-similar/self-affine measures (the so-called Mandelbrot random measurea) onto its x-axis or the y-axis. Besides obtaining the precise formulas of the Hausdorff dimension of the projected measures, we also obtain the precise dimension formula for the correspoding fibre measures. Moreover, we conduct the multifractal analysis for this projected measures. We obtain the precise formulas for the Renyi-dimension (a variant of L^q spectrum) and the dimension spectrum, and verify the multifractal formalism in the largest range of q>0. In the second situation, inspired by the classical projection theorems on the Hausdorff/packing dimensions under the orthogonal projections, we succeed in proving that under the coding map asscociated to a typical affine IFS, the Hausdorff dimension and the packing dimension of the projected sets and measures are constant, and morever we are able to provide the precise dimension formulas in terms of singular value functions. In particular, we can provide a criteron to classfisy all those measures on the symbolc space so that their projections under the typical coding maps are exact dimensional. Besides the above results, inspired by the dimension theory of Bedford-McMullen self-affine sets, we develop the theory of weighted thermodynamic formalism in topological dynamical systems. We also develop the dimension theory of random covering sets in Riemann manifolds, and prove a continuity property of Falconer's dimension formaula for typical self-affine sets, which resolves an open conjecture in fractal geometry. Overall we have achieved the major parts (around 90%) of our original objectives. A further understanding of the box-counting dimension and Renyi-dimension of projected sets and measures on typical self-affine sets is expected. This might be achieved by extending the methods developed in this project as well as by using some idea of Howroyd in his previous work on the box-counting dimension under orthogonal projections, and we hope to check this possible approach in the further investigations.

401013.label: Major findings and research outcome
401013.value: In [1] we study the pressure function of certain sub-additive potentials generated by a tuple of real square matrices (the so-called singular value functions over matrices). By applying the multiplicative ergodic theorem and the sub-additive thermodynamic formalism, we prove that the pressure function depends continuously on the matrices. As a consequence, we prove that Falconer's dimension formula for typical self-affine sets depends continuously on the linear parts of the generating IFSs of those self-affine sets. This gives a confirmative answer to a longstanding open conjecture in fractal geometry. In [2], motivated by dimension theory of self-affine sets with grid structures (including the Bedford-McMullen carpets and its high dimensional generalizations), we define the notion of weighted topological pressure and weighted topological entropy for factor maps between abstract topological dynamical systems. The main result of this work is the establishment of the so-called weighted variational principle, namely, the weighted topological pressure is equal to the supremum of the sum of the weighed measure-theoretic entropies and the Lyapunov exponents over invariant measures. This not only extends the classical variational principle by Ruelle and Walters, but also extends the previous works on the dimension of invariant sets and measures on the d-torus under diagonal expanding maps. In [3], we study the dimension of random covering sets in Euclidean spaces or on Riemann Manifolds. The origin of the random covering sets goes back to the early work of Borel on random covering sets by arcs. In this work we consider the random covering sets generated by a sequence of arbitrary open sets, or more generally, measurable sets with positive Lebesgue density. Applying potential theory and geometric measure theory, we provide the precise dimension formula for the Hausdorff and packing dimensions of these random covering sets. In [4], we investigate the various dimensions of the projections of arbitrary sets and measures in the symbolic space under the coding map associated to a typical affine iterated function system. We prove that for typical translation vectors (with fixed linear parts of the IFS), the Hausdorff dimension (as well as the packing dimension) of the projections of these sets and measures are constant and can be expressed into different formulas in terms of singular value functions. It exploits deep connections to the classical projection theorems on Hausdorff and packing dimensions under orthogonal projections. In [5], we consider the orthogonal projection of a family of planar random self-similar/self-affine measures (the so-called Mandelbrot random measurea) onto its x-axis or the y-axis. Besides obtaining the precise formulas of the Hausdorff dimension of the projected measures, we also obtain the precise dimension formula for the corresponding slicing measures. Moreover, we conduct the multifractal analysis for this projected measures. We obtain the precise formulas for the Renyi-dimension (a variant of L^q spectrum) and the dimension spectrum, and verify the multifractal formalism in the largest range of q>0.

401013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
401013.value: Dimension theory of fractal sets and measures plays a crucial role in fractal geometry and dynamical systems. It has close connections to many subjects in mathematics, such as geometric measure theory, harmonic analysis, combinatorics and probability theory. In this project, we study the dimension properties of fractals under different projections, e.g. orthogonal projection in Euclidean spaces and projection from symbolic spaces under coding maps. We obtained precise dimension formulas for projected sets and measures on almost all self-affine sets, and projected random planar measures on co-ordinate axis, and random covering sets on smooth manifolds. These works lead to a better understanding of dimension theory.

401113.value: 在固體中尋找馬約拉納費米子

401113.label: Project Objectives
401113.value: Single band vs multiband effect in experiments. In regard of the factor that in realistic experiments a lot of bands (4 – 8 bands using realistic experimental parameters) have been cut by the chemical potential, the single band model thus is insufficient to full explain the experimental observations. We will study the emergence of MFs in the multiband condition using the tight-binding model, in which the pairing is independent of the dimension of the system, thus can overcome the major difficult in the standard k∙p model. In the tight-binding model the disorder effect, including the uncorrelated disorder and correlated disorder, can be readily incorporated in our theoretical framework. We expect the multiband model can lead to a better understanding of the experimental observations, especially the height of zero-bias peak which is much smaller than the expectation value of 2e2/ℏ. Detection of MFs by coupling to quantum dots, and non-destructive measurement of MFs. It is still a great challenge in experiments to unambiguously identify the existence of MFs. We expect to identify the MFs and explore the properties of MFs using standard quantum transport method. Although the MFs in theory is neutral in charge, it can still be measured using the charge transport. The noise spectrum provide important basis for us to understand the properties of MFs in solid state systems, which is also crucial for future device applications. We also want to study the non-destructive measurement of MFs using the same method, so the MFs after identification can still be used for topological quantum computations. Decoherence of MFs interacting with the environments. In principle the MFs are robust against local disturbance because the information is encoded in degenerate ground states. However, in realistic systems the degeneracy is not exact, therefore a lot of sources in solid state systems, including the temperature effect, electron-phonon interactions and phase fluctuations of the superconductors, may lead to decoherence of MFs. These effect can lead to finite lifetime of MFs, hence is essential for the future device applications. The exploring of decoherence of MFs in realistic system therefore become crucial for the future solid state based topological quantum computation. Searching of MFs in new materials. The semiconductor is by no means the only system that support MFs. There are a lot of new materials that may support MFs. We will explore the possible MFs for semiconductor in contact with MgB2, which is a standard two-band s-wave superconductor, and unconditional d-wave superconductor. We will also study the emergence of MFs in topological insulator. The Andreev bound states in these systems will be explored because these bound states can be directly measured using standard quantum transport method.

401113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
401113.value: Recently, it has been proposed that conventional semiconductor nano-structures in proximity to the s-wave superconductors may support Majorana Fermions (MFs) when the Zeeman field exceeds some critical values. Here the Zeeman field is used to break the time-reversal symmetry so as to create the equivalent p-wave type pairing in the pseudo-spin basis. The basic conclusions hold for both electron and hole doped semiconductor. These proposals have spurred widespread interests, and some exotic signatures that may related to the present of MFs have been observed in different groups. In this project, we focus on several important topics related to the realization of MFs in solid state systems. (i) In realistic experiments the chemical potential cut a lot of bands, thus the single band approximation may not be used to interpret the experimental observations. We will try to understand the experimental data using tight-binding model for electron and hole doped nanowires which work well even in the multiband regime. We will also study the disorder effect on the emergences of MFs. (ii) Searching and detecting the MFs by coupling them to external quantum dots. Some pertinent results have already been obtained along this direction. We will also study the nondestructive measurement of MFs via quantum charge transport, which has already been demonstrated for conventional qubits. (iii) Decoherence processes of MFs interacting with the environments. Although the MFs in principle is immune to local disturbances, in realistic solid state systems the degeneracy of the ground states may be lifted by finite coupling between MFs, therefore there are a lot of sources, such as electron-phonon interactions, temperature effect, phase fluctuation of the superconductor et al, that can influence the lifetime of MFs. The decoherence processes of MFs are very important for the future application of MFs. (iv) Searching of zero-energy MFs in some new materials, including MgB2 (a two band superconductor with Tc ~ 40 K), unconventional d-wave superconductor and topological insulators. For the high Tc superconductor we expect the minigap of the MFs become very large thus the MFs can live at much higher temperature. We will also study the Andreev bound states in these new systems which can be directly measured using quantum transport method. This project aim to explore some fundament problems related to the realization, detection and application of MFs using the solid state systems. 401113.label: Realisation of objectives
401113.value: 1. New platform to realize the Majorana zero mode (MZM) using exotic pairings. The topological superconducting phases have to be realized using p-wave pairing. An important formula to realize the p-wave pairing can be written as soc+zeeman+s-wave ≈p-wave, where the spin-orbit coupling (soc) term can be find in various semiconductor materials without inversion symmetry, and the surface states of topological insulators. These topological phases can only be realized under strong Zeeman field much larger than the pairing strength. To overcome this difficulty, we consider the possible realization of MZM using semiconductor -- Fulde–Ferrell–Larkin–Ovchinnikov (FFLO) hybrid structure. The phase boundary is determined by the chemical potential, pairing strength, center-of-mass momentum Q carried by the Cooper pairs and the direction of the magnetic field. Thus this model provides some more controlling parameters to realize the topological phases. To investigate the possible signature for FFLO superconductor, we have examined the Andreev reflection for a Y junction in proximity to FFLO superconductors [2]. We show that these pairings are still p-type, although some high angular momentum states are involved [3]. We find strong coupling between the edge modes and the extended bulk states in the gapless regime [3]. These phases are characterized by Pfaffian and/or Chern number. 2. Coupling between MZMs and conventional qubits and their decoherence process. The MZMs are protected by topology, thus are believed to be robust against external decoherence /dephasing. However, the MZM itself can’t be used to realize universal quantum computation. We consider the coupling between MZMs and topological superconducting qubits and propose a general scheme to realize many-body entangled states encoded in the topological qubits. These states are robust against decoherence and dephasing when the temperature is much lower than 30 mK, which is estimated with realistic experimental data. We have also investigated the coupling between MZMs and quantum dots, in which the MZMs can be manipulated and read out by standard transport techniques [5]. The quantum dot and the superconducting qubit systems, nowadays, are regarded as two most promising platforms for the realization of quantum computations, and coupling between MZMs and these two systems should be an important direction in future. 3. Large Chern numbers in multiband systems. In all the previous investigations, the Chern numbers carried by the topological superconducting phases equal to ±1. We find that the large Chern numbers can be realized using a multi-band model by considering a nanowire with large lateral sizes, in which the chemical potential occupy more than one bands. The problem is that the order parameters in each bands are totally undetermined, thus a lot of parameters are involved in the determination of the total phase diagrams. To simplify this problem and to protrude the large Chern number phases more clearly, we investigate the large Chern number phases in a simplified bilayer systems, which are coupled by interlayer tunneling t. This model can be realized using two coupled semiconductor quantum wells or two layers of Fermi gases. This picture is essentially equivalent to the case with multi bands occupation (Ref. 6), with only two more controllable parameters. We find that during the topological transitions from Chern number C = 2 to C = 1 to C = 0, jumps of spin polarization at zero momentum are expected due to band inversion. We have also examined the similar physics for two coupled nanowires in Ref. 6, which yields the similar conclusion; since in D class phase, the topological index in 2D and 1D are all defined by integer Z. 4. Disorder effect in MZMs. The MZMs can be realized using semiconductor nanowires, however, it is still in debate that whether the observed signatures are indeed from MZMs. We examined the fate of MZMs in a nanowire in proximity to a s-wave superconductor. The fluctuation in chemical potential, Zeeman field and and pairing phases are all considered in our simulation via a tight-binding model. We find that the MZMs are robust against all kinds of disorders and the edge states can be observed in a wide range of disorder strength in the topological phase regime. Disorder will not contribute to new peaks at zero energy. The topological phase is characterized by Pfaffian. To understand the robustness of these edge states, we employ the high order perturbation theory to understand the splitting of MZMs from direct coupling between the edge states and all the extended bulk states. We show that the coupling between particle and hole bands are canceled exactly thus the zero energy states can be survived even in strong disordered environment. We have also examined the similar issue in the disordered Fermi-Hubbard model by self-consistent calculation, which yields the same conclusion. 5. A new mechanism for topological FFLO superfluids and topological Floquet phases. We show that the inversion symmetry breaking is essential for the development of FFLO phase in ultracold atoms in the presence of in-plane Zeeman field and spin-orbit coupling [4]. The finite momentum is not resulted from competition between BCS pairing and magnetism, thus represents a new mechanism for finite momentum pairing. In the topological regime, the edge states can support zero energy MZMs in some parameter regime. By quenching of the Zeeman field, the dynamics of the superlfuids, after a sufficient long-time evolution, may enter the topological Floquet phase regime, in which the order parameters oscillate periodically. In this case, the quantum states should be described by Floquet theorem [7]. We unveil this phase and figure out the corresponding phase diagram by large-scale self-consistent numerical simulation. Finally, we have also examined the interesting physics in the Fermi-Hubbard and Bose-Hubbard models using exact numerical methods [11]. Detection of MFs by coupling to quantum dots, and non-destructive measurement of MFs. It is still a great challenge in experiments to unambiguously identify the existence of MFs. We expect to identify the MFs and explore the properties of MFs using standard quantum transport method. Although the MFs in theory is neutral in charge, it can still be measured using the charge transport. The noise spectrum provide important basis for us to understand the properties of MFs in solid state systems, which is also crucial for future device applications. We also want to study the non-destructive measurement of MFs using the same method, so the MFs after identification can still be used for topological quantum computations.

Decoherence of MFs interacting with the environments. In principle the MFs are robust against local disturbance because the information is encoded in degenerate ground states. However, in realistic systems the degeneracy is not exact, therefore a lot of sources in solid state systems, including the temperature effect, electron-phonon interactions and phase fluctuations of the superconductors, may lead to decoherence of MFs. These effect can lead to finite lifetime of MFs, hence is essential for the future device applications. The exploring of decoherence of MFs in realistic system therefore become crucial for the future solid state based topological quantum computation.

Searching of MFs in new materials. The semiconductor is by no means the only system that support MFs. There are a lot of new materials that may support MFs. We will explore the possible MFs for semiconductor in contact with MgB2, which is a standard two-band s-wave superconductor, and unconditional d-wave superconductor. We will also study the emergence of MFs in topological insulator. The Andreev bound states in these systems will be explored because these bound states can be directly measured using standard quantum transport method.

401113.label: Major findings and research outcome
401113.value: 1. New platform for the realization of topological phases and Majorana Zero modes (MZMs). We show that these zero energy modes can be realized in semiconductor and Fulde–Ferrell–Larkin–Ovchinnikov (FFLO) superconductor hybrid systems, in which the topological phases and associated MZMs may be realized with much weaker external magnetic field. We have discussed the corresponding physics and their mechanisms in solid materials and ultracold atoms. 2. Coupling between the MZMs and the conventional quantum qubit. We consider the coupling between MZMs and superconducting qubits and propose a generic way to realize multi-partitie entangled states with the topological qubits mediated by the superconducting bus. In the hybrid systems between quantum dots and MZMs, we have discussed the detection of MZMs using conventional quantum transport techniques in quantum dots. 3. Robust of the Majorana qubits under the disordered environment. We demonstrate that the topological superconducting phase is robust against disorders and the zero energy edge modes can be survived in a wide range of disorders. We try to understand this result using the higher-order perturbation theory, in which contribution of energies from particle and hole branches to the edge states are exactly canceled, thus the MZMs are robust. 4. Topological superfluids and topological Floquet States. The in-plane Zeeman field can break the inversion symmetry and give rise to FFLO phase, which represents a new mechanism for finite momentum pairing in superconducting phases. Topological gapped FFLO phase can be realized in this model. After the quenching of the Zeeman field, topological Floquet superfluids can be developed, in which the order parameter oscillates periodically in time. Topological phases with large Chern numbers can be realized in this Floquet phase regime. 5. Many-body effect in the Hubbard models and phase diagrams. We examine the fate of Cooper pairs in the spin-orbit coupled Fermi-Hubbard model using density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) method, in which we show that in some proper parameter regimes the coexistence of BCS pairing and FFLO pairing may be realized. This phase can even be realized in two spatial dimensions. We find that this coexisting phase can not be understood from conventional mean-field theory.

401113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
401113.value: Since the first experimental realization of Majorana zero modes (MZMs) in Kouwenhoven’s group in TU Delft, nowadays, at least eight groups have claimed signatures for MZMs in various systems, including the semiconductor nanowires as well as topological insulators. Technology giants, such as Google and Microsoft in US and Alibaba and Huawei in China, also have invested a great number of money in this field, trying to realize the quantum computations. It is still indefinite who will out the so-called quantum supremacy in future? The topological quantum computation is regarded as a possible and promising candidate to realize this supremacy. In this sense, the consistent supporting from the government about topological phase transitions and topological computations should be necessary and important in future. The investigations carried out in this project has shed new light on the properties of the topological qubits. Moreover, the proposal for the coupling between topological qubits and flying qubits is quite likely to be realized in experiments due to the progresses achieved in superconducting qubits and MZMs.

401213.label: Project Title(Chinese)
401213.value: 寻找二级关联系统的基态序参量的新方法

401213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
401213.value: The concept of order parameter is of fundamental importance in the condensed matter physics. The nonvanishing value of the order parameter at a long distance characterizes a symmetry-breaking phase in many-body systems. In traditional approaches, to study the ground state properties of a quantum many-body system, people usually introduce a certain order parameter, then study its correlation function to witness the existence of long-range order. Such an order parameter strongly depends on the physical intuition of the investigator, hence might be wrong in some cases. Due to the quick development in quantum information theory, many concepts and methods from the information science have been applied to study the phenomena in the condensed mater physics. Quite recently, we found that the spectra of quantum mutual information can tell us all the possible correlations in the ground state of quantum many-body systems. We then proposed a new scheme to construct order parameter explicitly from the spectra of the quantum mutual information. This scheme provides us an opportunity to find the accurate order parameter of the ground state. In this proposal, we are going to the apply the scheme to the two-dimensional strongly correlated systems. Since the two-dimensional Hubbard and t-J models play very important roles in the field of high temperature superconductivity, we will take them as examples in this proposal. In the traditional approaches to these systems, people usually need to assume a special order parameter to obtained the self-consistent equations, hence some special orders might be missed in the approach. By analyzing the spectra of the reduced density matrix used to calculate the mutual information, we plan to study the all possible correlations and orders existing in the ground state of the models. The critical behavior of the mutual information (as a measure of total correlation) will be studied too. In the new approach to construct order parameters, no knowledge of symmetry of the system is required, we hope it can help us to find new novel phases that cannot be found via the traditional method. We expect that our proposal will shed new lights on our understanding on the electronic and magnetic properties of superconductivity states in doped antiferromagnets. 序参量的概念在凝聚态物理中基本而又重要。在量子多体系统中，长距离上不为零的序参量表示某种对称破缺相。在传统的理论中，为了研究量子多体系统的基态性质，人们通常先引入某一个序参量，再来研究相应的关联函数来确定是否存在长程序。如此引入的序参量通常依赖于研究者的物理直觉，因为在有些情况下可能出错。 由于量子信息理论的发展，许多信息科学中的概念与方法已被应用到凝聚态物理中来。最近，我们发现，对一个量子多体系统来讲，量子互熵的谱就可以告诉我们其基态中所有可能的关联。于是我们提出了一个新的方案——通过量子互熵的谱来构造序参量。此方案为我们提供了寻找正确的序参量的一个方法。在这个研究计划中，我们准备把这方案应用到二维强关联系统中去。由于二维哈伯德模型和t-J模型在高温超导领域的重要性，在该计划中，我们打算以它们两者为研究对象。在传统的方法中，人们常常需要假定一个特定的序参量来获得自洽方程，所以会可能忽略掉某些重要的信息。通过分析约化密度矩阵的谱，我们计划探寻在这些模型的基态中所有可能存在的序和关联，同时探讨互熵的临界形为。 在构造序参量的新方案中，由于不需要假定任何对称性，我们希望它可能帮助我们发现传统方法不能找到的新的物理相；为我们理解掺杂超导态的电磁学性质提供新的思路。

401413.label: Project Title(Chinese)
401413.value: 用中心自旋退相干探測環境中的時間域相變

401413.label: Project Objectives
401413.value: Systematically studying universality classes of time-domain phase transitions. The model systems will be chosen from the ferromagnetic and anti-ferromagtic Ising models, XXZ models, and dipolar coupling systems, which have rich structures of universality classes in conventional phase transitions. We will employ exact solutions for certain exactly solvable models (e.g., one-dimensional Ising models and XX chains), carry out numerical simulations for finite-size systems using Bethe ansatz (for one-dimensional XXZ chains) or exact diagonalization, and use the renormalization group theory to analyze the critical behaviors in the time-domain and to determine the universality classes. We will study the effects of quantum fluctuation in quantum models where the bath Hamiltonian does not commute with the probe-bath coupling. We will employ one-dimensional Ising or XY chains under transverse fields to investigate the time-domain phase transitions in quantum models. These models are exactly solvable. Finite-size scaling of the critical phenomena. In realistic experiments, the central spin decoherence has to be studied in finite-size baths. While the bath can be sufficiently large to approximate the thermodynamic limit, it is important to understand the finite-size scaling of the critical behavior. The finite-size scaling at the critical points is also an important critical feature to classify the universality classes. We will increase the size of the spin baths to investigate how the coherence approaches zero differently at different sides of the time-domain phase transition point and calculate the related critical exponents. Design and simulation of realistic physical systems for experimental observation. We will design and simulate realistic physical systems, which will be chosen from small molecules for liquid-state nuclear magnetic resonance, trapped ions with controllable interactions, spin arrays on surfaces probed by nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond, and spins of atomically positioned phosphorous donors in silicon, according to the experimental progresses in these systems. We will simulate the effects due to disorders and control errors.

401413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
401413.value: 自旋的量子相干性會被環境中的噪聲破壞。此中心自旋退相干效應是以自旋為基礎的量子技術的一個關鍵問題。對中心自旋退相干的研究經歷了四個發展階段： (1)理解其微觀機制, (2) 用動力學去耦抑制退相干, (3) 應用於噪聲譜和磁探測, 以及 (4) 應用於探測環境中的多體物理。相變是多體物理的一個主題。在研究中心自旋退相干時, 申請人和合作者發現了一類新的相變現象，即時間域相變。他們發現中心自旋退相干在時間演化過程會經歷一個非解析點，即相變點 [Phys Rev Lett 109, 185701 (2012)]。該發現不但帶來新的物理概念也對自旋共振譜帶來新的應用。 對時間域相變的研究還處於起步階段。此效應還只在一些特定鐵磁系統發現。目前還不清楚該效應有多普適以及如何劃分該相變的普適類。 為實驗觀測所預言的效應也需要設計和模擬實際的物理系統。 在本項目中，我們用不同自旋庫模型系統地研究中心自旋退相干中時間域臨界現象的普適特性。我們將考慮熱漲落和量子漲落的不同效應。為促進有關實驗研究, 我們將研究臨界點附近的有限尺寸標度性質，並設計和模擬實際物理體系。 本項目所需要的理論工具已經相當成熟，包括可解模型的精確解、一維模型的Bethe假設解、有限系統的嚴格數值模擬、以及用於普適類的重整化群理論。在設計和模擬實際物理體系的時候，我們會考慮液態核磁共振分子系統，具有可控相互作用的離子阱系統， 用金剛石中氮-空位缺陷探測的表面自旋陣列，以及矽裡面按原子分辨率排列的磷施主雜質等等。所以這類系統的結果和量子態都有實驗證實其可控性。我們也將研究系統構成和控制中的誤差效應。 對發現的時間域相變的深入研究將開創一個新的相變研究領域也將開發一個磁探測的新方向。臨界時間可以類比臨界溫度。本項目的研究也有機會揭示時間和溫度這一對自然界中最基本的物理量之間的深刻聯繫。

401413.label: Realisation of objectives
401413.value: We reports on an experimentally realizable approach to analytic continuation of thermodynamic functions to the complex plane of physical parameters and thence a new type of phase transitions that would not be observable if the physical parameters are restricted to be real numbers. We show that the quantum evolution of a system from thermal equilibrium, due to the complex quantum phase factor, is equivalent to a partition function with complex physical parameters. The quantum evolution is in principle experimentally realizable and under certain circumstances is directly related to the probe spin decoherence or quantum quench dynamics. This finding opens the door to a vast wonderland of physics in the complex plane of physical parameters. In particular, a new type of phase transitions is revealed by the distinct features of quantum evolution, which is confirmed by the topological features of the renormalization group flows of the complex parameters. This work was published as [Wei et al, Scientific Reports 4, 5202 (2014). Phase transitions in the complex plane of physical parameters]. In this work, Objectives 1, 2 & 3 are addressed. We rigorously establishes the holographic principle in equilibrium thermodynamics. We demonstrate that the holography is an underlying principle in equilibrium thermodynamics, a most important foundation of physics. We prove that the thermodynamics of a system at any point of an area in the complex plane of a physical parameter is fully determined by the partition function along the edge of the area. This principle is shown universally applicable to all physical systems, being fermions, bosons, spins, or their mixtures. The thermodynamic holography opens up new possibilities for studying many-body physics, making the impossible now possible - the physical properties of a system in a parameter regime where the measurement in experiments or calculation in theories is difficult or even impossible now may be obtained from the properties for parameters where the measurement or calculation can be readily carried out. This is especially useful for studying strongly correlated systems and thermodynamics of nano-systems. The work was published as [Wei et al Scientific Reports 5, 15077 (2015). Thermodynamic holography]. Objective 1, 2 & 3 are addressed. We proposed NV spin systems coupled to a mechanical resonator to realize a many-body systems and investigated the thermodynamics of the system in the complex plane. This work was published as [Wei et al, EPJ Quantum Technology 2, 18 (2015). Magnetic ordering of nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond via resonator-mediated coupling]. Objective 4 is addressed. In collaboration with the USTC group, , based on our previous discovery that the quantum coherence of a probe spin coupled to a many-body system is equivalent to the partition function of the system with complex physical parameters [Phys Rev Lett. 109, 185701 (2012)], we made the first observation of Lee-Yang zeros, more than 60 years after they were theoretically discovered. This experiment conceptually completes the picture of thermodynamics and statistical physics. We also demonstrated the Lee-Yang zero measurement as a powerful approach to studying many-body physics. With the measured Lee-Yang zeros, we reconstructed the free energy of the interacting spin system and obtained the phase transition temperature, both of which are in excellent agreement with theoretical predictions. This work was published as [Peng et al, Physical Review Letters 114, 010601 (5 January 2015). Experimental Observation of Lee-Yang Zeros]. Objective 4 was addressed.

401413.label: Major findings and research outcome
401413.value: We made the first observation of Lee-Yang zeros, more than 60 years after they were theoretically discovered. This experimental work, in collaboration with USTC group, is based on our previous theoretical discovery that the quantum coherence of a probe spin coupled to a many-body system is equivalent to the partition function of the system with complex physical parameters [Phys Rev Lett. 109, 185701 (2012)]. This experiment conceptually completes the picture of thermodynamics and statistical physics. We also demonstrated the Lee-Yang zero measurement as a powerful approach to studying many-body physics. With the measured Lee-Yang zeros, we reconstructed the free energy of the interacting spin system and obtained the phase transition temperature, both of which are in excellent agreement with theoretical predictions. Extension from the real axis to the complex plane has played revolutionary roles in mathematics and physics, with famous examples like introductions of in mathematics and probability amplitudes in quantum mechanics. Our observation of Lee-Yang zeros will appeal to the general audience by the possibility of generalizing thermodynamics to the complex plane of physical parameters. [Output 8.3] We rigorously establish the holographic principle in equilibrium thermodynamics. The holographic principle, most well known in optical hologram, has proven to be a fascinating, profound relation in a wide range of physics fields, from optics to many-body physics to quantum gravity to string theories. We demonstrate that the holography is an underlying principle in equilibrium thermodynamics, a most important foundation of physics. We prove that the thermodynamics of a system at any point of an area in the complex plane of a physical parameter is fully determined by the partition function along the edge of the area. This principle is shown universally applicable to all physical systems, being fermions, bosons, spins, or their mixtures. The thermodynamic holography opens up new possibilities for studying many-body physics. [Output 8.5] We discovered an experimentally realizable approach to analytic continuation of thermodynamic functions to the complex plane of physical parameters and thence a new type of phase transitions that would not be observable if the physical parameters are restricted to be real numbers. We show that the quantum evolution of a system from thermal equilibrium, due to the complex quantum phase factor, is equivalent to a partition function with complex physical parameters. This finding is of immediate interest to the study of quantum decoherence in environments, quantum quench dynamics of cold atoms, and quantum engines. [Output 8.1]

401413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
401413.value: The analytic properties of partition functions or free energies fully determine the thermodynamics of a physical system at thermal equilibrium. This picture has been a mathematical cornerstone of thermodynamics and statistical physics since the seminal paper published by T. D. Lee and C. N. Yang more than 60 years ago [Phys. Rev. 87, 404 (1952)]. However, access to the singularity points in the complex plane has not been regarded possible since the physical parameters are always assumed as real numbers. In this project, we discovered an experimentally realizable approach to analytic continuation of thermodynamic functions to the complex plane of physical parameters and thence a new type of phase transitions that would not be observable if the physical parameters are restricted to be real numbers. We rigorously establish the holographic principle in equilibrium thermodynamics. We made the first observation of Lee-Yang zeros, more than 60 years after they were theoretically discovere, in collaboration with USTC group. This experiment conceptually completes the picture of thermodynamics and statistical physics. We also demonstrated the Lee-Yang zero measurement as a powerful approach to studying many-body physics.

401613.label: Project Title(Chinese)
401613.value: Fuglede問題及分形上的調和分析

401613.label: Project Objectives
401613.value: We propose to study the Fuglede problem on self-similar tiles and integer tiles. We will investigate the structure of these tiles as certain product forms. It amounts to factorizing the mask polynomials into some tractable components, and the zeros of the factors will provide a natural way to handle the spectral problem. It is known that in many cases, one cannot expect $L^2(K, \mu)$ to have an exponential orthonormal basis. We consider relaxing this to exponential Riesz basis or Fourier frame. The problem is particularly interesting for a continuous singular measure that is not a spectral measure (like the standard Cantor measure or the Hausdorff measure on the Sierpinski gasket). So far very little is known in that direction. We will expand the scope of this spectral analysis so as to connect it with other developments in fractal analysis, for example, the fractal Phancherel formula, the convergence of non-harmonic series, Cauchy transform of self-similar measures and its boundary behavior.

401613.label: Realisation of objectives
401613.value: In the 70's, Fuglede raised a well-known conjecture that a bounded set $K$ is a tile if and only if it is a spectral set (i.e., existence of an exponential orthonormal bases in $L^2(K)$). In the turn of the century, the conjecture was proved to be false in $R^s$ for $s geq 3$ by Tao. However the problem still poses challenging questions for $R^s$ for $s leq 2$, and for some variations of the setting. In this project, our first objective was to study the structure of a special class of tiles that are generated by iterated function systems of similitudes (or affine maps). We showed that on $R^1$, the tiles can be described by the modulo product-forms, a notion introduced by us (the PI and his collaborators), and their properties were studied in detail. The higher dimensional analog is more difficult, we found new techniques to deal with certain basic cases, and some unexpected results were discovered. We also investigated the spectral property of such tiles by making use of the product-forms. We verified Fuglede's question holds on some cases in $R^1$. In another development, we studied the spectral property of the self-similar measures as well as the Moran measures, and proved some interesting results.

401613.value: (Note: the reference in the following are in Part 7, Peer-reviewed journal publications) Let $T(A, D)$ be self-similar sets generated by a pair $(A, D)$, where $A$ is a matrix of expanding similarity and has integral entries, and $D subset R^s$ is a finite set, called digit set. A fundamental question in the theory of fractal tiling is to understand the structure of $D$ so that the self-similar set is a translational tile. In our previous work (reported in RGC project 401309), we classified such $D$ in $R^1$ as some sort of modulo product-forms. Continuing this work, in [3] we gave explicitly expression of the modulo product-forms $D$ for $A= p^n q$ where $p, q$ are distinct primes, this improved the previously known case that $A=p^n$ or $pq$. For higher dimensional spaces, there was no precedent result on the structure of the tile digit sets other than the case $|det A| =p$ where $p$ is a prime. In [5] we made a head start to consider the case that $A =pI$ in $R^2$ where $p$ is a prime and I is the identity matrix (hence $|det A| =p^2$). We classified the tile digit sets by making use of the zeros of the mask polynomial, together with a recent result of Iosevich {it et al} on factorization of sets in $Z_p x Z_p$. Although it is a very special case, the conclusion and techniques are quite different from the situation in $R^1$, this may lead to some new development. In [4] we investigated the spectral properties of self-similar tiles $K$ in $R^1$ through the product structure of the associate digit sets. We showed that the tiles from the strict product-forms and the associated modulo product-forms are spectral sets. The converse question is much harder, we gave a pilot study for the self-similar sets generated by arbitrary digit sets with four elements. We made use of the zeros of the Fourier transform of the tile, and verified Fuglede's conjecture for this special case. 401613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
401613.value: We have certain success in classifying the structure of the self-affine tiles and tile digit sets on $R^1$. There are few results for the higher dimensional spaces. Our pilot study in [5] in $R^2$ projects some new insight for future development. For the spectral property, the same comment as the above also holds for higher dimensional spaces. Moreover we have extended our consideration outside the self-similar measures [2]. It will be interesting to find other specific classes of measures to have the spectral property. Another important direction is to relax the exponential orthogonality basis requirement to be an "exponential frame" or an "exponential Riesz basis", which will be a very challenging project.

401613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
401613.value: A translational tile is a set such that the space can be covered by its translates with no overlap; a spectral set is a set that admits an exponential orthonormal basis. They were conjectured to imply each other. In this project, we investigated a special class of self-similar sets that are generated by the iterated function systems, they are fractals in nature. We gave conditions for them to be a tile, and study whether they are spectral sets in the spirit of the conjecture. We also extended our consideration to the self-similar measures as well as some non-self-similar measures and inspect their spectral property.

401913.value: 辛幾何與規範場論中的TQFT

401913.label: Project Objectives
401913.value: In a series of papers [KLT], the proposer and her collaborators recently established the long-conjectured equivalence of (Ozsvath-Szabo's) Heegaard and Seiberg-Witten Floer homologies. We would like to extend this result by comparing invariants for 4-dimensional cobordisms on both sides. Relate the invariants for closed 4-manifolds in Seiberg-Witten and Heegaard Floer theories.

401913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
401913.value: The PI proposes to continue her study on the relation between gauge theoretic invariants and Gromov-type invariants under the framework of Taubes’s proof of “Seiberg-Witten equals Gromov''. In a series of papers joint with Taubes and Kutluhan [KLT], the PI proved the equivalence of four corresponding flavors of Seiberg-Witten Floer homologies with Heegaard Floer homologies. In another joint work with Taubes [LT], the proposer established the equivalence of a certain version of Seiberg-Witten Floer homology with the ``periodic Floer homology” for mapping tori. According to Atiyah's TQFT (topologial quantum field theory) principle [A], the natutual next step is to extend these results about 3-manifolds to 4-manifolds and cobordisms. 本計劃預定研究及比較辛幾何與規範場論中的TQFT. 在一系列與 Taubes 合作的論文中，計劃提出者證明了Seiberg-Witten Floer 和 Heegaard Floer homologies 的等價性。按照 Atiyah TQFT（拓樸量子場論）的原則， 下一步是擴大有關三維流形的這些成果到 4-cobordisms。

401913.label: Realisation of objectives
401913.value: The PI has essentially established the equivalence of the parallel TQFTs in Heegaard Floer and the Seiberg-Witten theories. (These include both Objectives.) The body of the proof of the main equivalence theorems constitutes a paper still under preparation ("Seiberg-Witten and Heegaard Floer invariants for four-manifolds"; expected length 80 pages). The analytical foundation is provided in a separate long paper "From Seiberg-Witten to Gromov: MCE and Singular Symplectic Forms" (151 pages). The technical results contained in the aforementioned paper are far more general than what is required for the equivalence theorems and are expected to have broader applications; for example, they are also used in other ongoing and planned research of the PI. The progress of the project was delayed by the preparation of the technical paper "From Seiberg-Witten to Gromov: MCE and Singular Symplectic Forms", which took longer than expected. In addition, a significant amount of time was spent on revising the series of preprints HF=HM I.-V. that are prequels to this project. In particular, a large part of HF=HM V. is rewritten and new material is incorporated, making it 80 pages longer. Some of the new materials are relevant to this project. In the still-ongoing course of writing the paper "Seiberg-Witten and Heegaard Floer invariants for four-manifolds", minor issues may arise which we believe can be easily addressed.

401913.label: Major findings and research outcome
401913.value: It is shown that, as conjectured, the equivalence of the Seiberg-Witten Floer homology and the Heegaard Floer homology proven in the series of paper HM=HF I.-V. extends to an equivalence of TQFTs. For closed 4-manifolds with b^+>1, the Seiberg-Witten invariant is shown to be equal to Ozsvath-Szabo's 4-manifold invariant. A simplified version of the main result in the technical paper "From Seiberg-Witten to Gromov: MCE and Singular Symplectic Forms", very roughly speaking, states the following: Let X be a 4-manifold with cylindrical end, and let v be a generic harmonic 2-form on X in a non-torsion cohomology class such that it is asymptotic to the Hodge dual of a Morse-Novikov 1-form on at least one of X's ending 3-manifolds. Consider Seiberg-Witten equations with perturbations of the form rv^+ plus some other less significant terms. Given a sequence of solutions corresponding to an increasing, unbounded sequence of r satisfying certain topological constraints, there exists a chain of certain types of weighted pseudo-holomorphic subvarieties satisfying corresponding constraints.

401913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
401913.value: As already mentioned, the paper "Seiberg-Witten and Heegaard Floer invariants for four-manifolds" which contains the proof of the equivalence theorems is still under preparation. In the course of writing, minor issues may arise which we believe can be easily addressed. Results from the technical paper "From Seiberg-Witten to Gromov: MCE and Singular Symplectic Forms" are used in other ongoing projects of the PI. We will also look for other applications of these results.

401913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
401913.value: Taubes’s idea of relating the gauge-theoretic Seiberg-Witten invariants and the Gromov-type invariants have wide implications in both low-dimensional topology and symplectic geometry. Though the closed-manifolds-versions of these relations have been largely known for more than ten years, due to substantial technical difficulties, its Floer-theoretic versions have only begun to be understood recently. Several equivalence theorems relating Seiberg-Witten-Floer homologies with "Gromov-type" Floer homologies have been established: E.g. "HM=ECH" (Taubes); "HM=PFH" (Taubes and the PI); "HM=HF" (Kuluthan, Taubes and the PI). Applications of such equivalence theorems include Taubes's celebrated proof of the long-standing Weinstein conjecture for 3-manifolds, and new obstructions to symplectic embeddings introduced by Hutchings. One of the major outcomes of this project is an extension of the "HM=HF" theorem to closed 4-manifolds and 4-dimensional cobordisms. (In comparison, extensions of "HM=ECH" and "HM=PFH" to TQFTs are still open problems, though the Hutchings-Taubes's proof of the Arnold chord conjecture makes use of some initial steps of a putative extension of "HM=ECH" to certain 4-dimensional cobordisms.) While the invariants from the Heegaard Floer theory side are much more computable, their counterparts in Seiberg-Witten theory are more intrinsic in many aspects. This, for example, has been exploited by D. Ruberman and his coauthors.

402113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
402113.value: 以过渡金属络合物催化二氧化碳的氢化，形成甲酸，所得到的高催化效率堪称均相催化成功的典范。没有毒性，来源丰富的二氧化碳，在这一过程中变成有机工业原料，对经济，对环境都有很大的好处。这些反应的机制，特别是其中的溶济作用，却至今未有完全弄清楚。在本项目中，我们将以分子团蔟的方法，逐个加上溶剂分子，以量子化学与第一原理动力学，模似溶剂分子对反应物及催化机制的影响，为更有效催化剂的设计，提供依据。

402113.label: Realisation of objectives
402113.value: We first observed that there were problems discrepancies between previous theoretical studies, as different mechanism was proposed and the enhancement in sc-CO2 was not really explained. By a detailed comparative study on L4RuH2, with L being either PMe3 or the bidentate dmpe, we have been able to resolve these discrepancies and put our understanding of catalytic mechanisms on a firmer foundation. It is unnecessary to evoke the presence of coordinately unsaturated complexes as intermediates. The first reaction step is the same for both ligands: direct hydride abstraction by CO2 to form a formate ion coordinated to Ru, L4RuH(OOCH). For both catalysts, it is possible to substitute a Ru-P bond by a Ru-O bond, which makes the formate ion bidentate, in the form of L3RuH(η2-OOCH). The experimentally observed differences between the two catalysts are largely explained by the difference in this reaction step. In the case of (PMe3)4RuH2, this step is endothermic by 7.8 kcal/mol in energy. With a PMe3 completely dissociated, the energy increase is partially compensated by an increase in entropy, so that the overall free energy change is less endothermic. There is a significant presence of L3RuH(η2-OOCH), which makes the subsequent H2 insertion easier. One of its Ru-O bonds could be substituted by H2, followed by metathesis between H2 and OOCH, both coordinated to Ru, and leading to the formation of HCOOH, with a barrier of 19.4 kcal/mol. It is the rate determining step in the overall process. In the case of (dmpe)2RuH2, this step is endothermic by 14.5 kcal/mol. The formation of η2-formate complex leaves a dmpe ligand half-dissociated, but still attached to Ru, providing no entropy gains. The overall free energy change is as endothermic as the energy, reducing the presence of the η2-formate complex. H2 insertion must proceed via trans-(dmpe)2RuH(OOCH), by directly inserting H2 between Ru+ and OOCH-, and its barrier of 21.6 kcal/mol makes it the rate determining step. The η2-formate complex still plays a significant role, not as an intermediate for H2 insertion, but as an intermediate through which cis-(dmpe)2RuH(OOCH) could be transformed into its more stable trans isomer, which is more amenable to H2 insertion. The comparison between PMe3 and dmpe complexes of Ru dihydride is an example that in a multi-step catalytic reaction the advantage for one step could be a disadvantage for the next step. While CO2 insertion is facile and produces a more stable product for (dmpe)2RuH2, the subsequent H2 insertion is relatively more difficult. In contrast, while CO2 insertion is less facile and produces a less stable product for (PMe3)4RuH2, the subsequent H2 steps are relatively easier. For both catalysts, H2 insertion is the rate determining step. Overall, (PMe3)4RuH2 is a better catalyst. The comparison also points to a mechanistic factor for the enhancement of a catalytic reaction under supercritical conditions: when the production of a key intermediate involves a step of complete dissociation, the increase in translational and rotational entropy could make the free energy more favorable and provide a significant boost under supercritical conditions, as the rotational and translational movements are less inhibited by solvation. For (PMe3)4RuH2, the formation of the η2-formate complex involves the complete dissociation of a PMe3 ligand, and the process is enhanced in scCO2. In contrast, for (dmpe)2RuH2, the formation of the η2-formate complex leaves a dangling dmpe attached to Ru and no entropy increase, and the process is not enhanced in scCO2. Such a consideration should be valid for other catalytic reactions as well, since it is based on the general nature of a dissociation process and of supercritical conditions. We then proceeded to solve the long standing problem that additives could greatly enhance the catalytic rate, and model the details of the underlying solvation effects. For the CO2 hydrogenation catalyzed by (PMe3)4RuH2, there are hydrogen bonding interactions around the Ru−H bonds when protic additive molecules, such as H2O, MeOH, and HNMe2, are the additive. But such interactions alone do not change the catalytic mechanism or lower the overall barrier significantly. Significant changes come at the final elimination step of the first catalytic cycle. When the product formic acid is removed, one of the additive molecules aggregated around the Ru−H bonds and the coordinated formate ion/formic acid is well positioned to fill the empty coordination site, producing (PMe3)3RuH2L, with L=H2O, MeOH, or HNMe2. Such energetically unstable intermediates could then react readily with the abundant CO2, starting a new catalytic cycle. The overall barrier is lower significantly when (PMe3)3RuH2L is the catalyst, because the relevant intermediates are higher in energy. In other words, it’s the elevation of TDI, rather than the lowering of TDTS that makes (PMe3)3RuH2L a better catalyst. The salient feature of the promotion effect by protic additives is that the presence of thermodynamically unfavorable intermediates can be enhanced by the aggregation of additive molecules around the reactive site of the catalyst molecule. The larger promotion effect by MeOH and HNMe2 than by H2O is due to the higher solubility of MeOH and HNMe2 which makes the aggregate of additive molecules around the reactive sites larger. CO2 hydrogenation catalyzed by (PMe3)4RuH2 in sc-CO2 is a good example of the high efficiency that could be achieved by homogeneous catalysis. But its high TOF in the presence a protic additive is actually due to the structural inhomogeneity around its reactive polar site which is the favorable for the aggregation of protic additives. Such restricted channels for polar molecules are quite common in organometallic complexes, which often contain polar bonds and less polar organic ligands. It produces an inhomogeneous structural environment that could be advantageous for the design of better catalysts. We also studied catalytic mechanism for the CO2 Hydrogenation catalyzed by an Ir-PNP complex, which is one of the best reported so far, and performed in aqueous solution. The electropositive and electronegative centers of H2O molecule and Ir-PNP complex are identified. H2O molecules are added to the Ir-PNP complex one by one to construct the solvation model. The hydrogen bond network and the stabilization energy are examined. Based on these results, the most stable structure is selected for the catalytic cycle analysis. Afterwards, each reactant is consecutively added to the Ir-PNP complex by constructing theoretical molecular model. The variation in mechanisms is systematically studied, by considering the effect of de-aromatization, and the presence or absence of hydroxide ion. All the intermediate structures are identified and relative energies of each step are calculated. Lots of data are generated in this part, and we are still working on putting them into a coherent picture.
