402113.label: Major findings and research outcome
402113.value: With a comparative study by density functional theory on two catalysts, (PMe3)4RuH2 and (dmpe)2RuH2, with dmpe=Me2PCH2CH2PMe2, we are able to clarify the similarity and difference between them, and provide a consistent account for all the experimental observations reported, including the kinetic models, the cis to trans transformation of (dmpe)2RuH2, and the significant enhancement of catalytic rate in supercritical CO2 for (PMe3)4RuH2 and its lack thereof for (dmpe)2RuH2. The crucial difference between the two mechanisms involves the formation of an intermediate, in which a formate ion binds to Ru as a bidentate ligand. When this step results in the dissociation of a ligand, the reaction rate is enhanced under supercritical conditions, due to the increase in entropy, which should be a valid consideration for other catalytic reactions as well. With combined AIMD and DFT calculations and explicit treatment of the protic solvent molecules, we are able to account for the accelerated reaction rate observed in the landmark CO2 hydrogenation catalyzed by (PMe3)4RuH2 in supercritical CO2 when H2O, MeOH, or HNMe2 is added. A thermodynamically unstable yet dynamically favorable active intermediate could be produced by the inhomogeneity of solvent distribution around the catalyst, rather than initiated by ligand dissociation. It takes place at the end of the first catalytic cycle, when the product is eliminated. The empty site is immediately filled by one of the additive molecules aggregated around the reaction center, even when the intermediate complex is unstable, producing a transient and more active catalyst. It suggests a new way to exploit the structural inhomogeneity around an organometallic complex for the design of better catalysts. By systematically varying the number of water molecules and the de-aromatization on the Ir-PNP catalyst for CO2 hydrogenation, we demonstrated importance of considering the contribution of solvent H2O in the catalytic model. In agreement with experiment, the best catalytic rate is achieved after de-aromatization has taken place in the presence of hydrated hydroxide ion.

402113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
402113.value: Catalytic CO2 hydrogenation is still a very active research area, with ongoing search for better and cheaper catalysts. Our results have elucidated the mechanistic aspects of model reactions, providing insights and impetus for future experimental and theoretical works in this area.

402113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
402113.value: The hydrogenation of CO2 holds the promises to turn a cheap and abundant gas in the atmosphere into a feedstock in chemical industry. The process needs a catalyst. By molecular modeling, we have studied the underlying mechanisms and the effects of solvation dynamics on these reactions. It provides fundamental understanding to design and search for better catalysts.

402413.value: 視覺信息在我們的日常生活中扮演了重要的角色。隨著圖像獲取技術的進步，視覺信息現時可用數字圖像有效表示。數字圖像處理廣泛應用在物理、計算機視覺、醫學成像等領域。許多圖像處理問題都與圖像的幾何和幾何形變相關，因此發展有效的幾何手段來解決這些圖像問題是至關重要的。在本項目中，我們著眼於建立三種圖像處理問題的幾何模型：1. 圖像配准；2. 影像壓縮；3. 影像高清化。 這項研究主要分爲兩部分。在第一部分，我們的興趣在於發展圖像配准和影像處理的高效算法。對於圖像配准，我們將會研究四個特定的問題。我們首先將發展噪聲或者扭曲圖像的配准方法。這將有助於配准醫學圖像或者氣流扭曲圖像。其次，我們所感興趣問題是尋找一種匹配特征點的配准，同時盡可能地保持局部幾何信息。許多配准問題可以用基於特征點匹配的算法來解決，以得到圖像之間能夠一致匹配特徵的一對一的空間配對。理想情況下，我們將希望得到一個匹配特征點的配准，同時盡可能地保持遠離特征點處的局部幾何信息。爲了節省存儲空間，最好能有一種緊致的方法來表示配准。基於這些考慮，我們將發展算法來計算特征點匹配的幾何模型，並且能夠保持局部幾何信息同時具有稀疏表示。第三，我們計劃發展用於分片常數圖像的快速配准方法。我們將探索利用三角網格表示數字圖像的可能性。我們將開發基於區域的配准算法，這將能大大降低問題的規模。最後，我們將會探索高維圖像的特征點匹配問題，例如三維體積醫學圖像。對於這個目標，我們考慮將基於二維擬保角框架的特征點匹配方法擴展到一般的高維圖像。 對於影像處理，我們將專注於發展用於影像壓縮和影像高清化的幾何模型。我們的目標是開發算法獲取更高清的影像同時使用較少的存儲空間。在本項目中，我們考慮的幾何算法基於控制運動矢量場的幾何扭曲，以達成視頻超分辨率和視頻壓縮的目標。 此外，在研究的第二部分，我們將會應用這些算法到實際問題當中。更具體地，我們將應用我們的配准算法來配准和復原氣流扭曲圖像。算法也將用於動態對比度增強的磁力共振影像的運動補償。最後，我們將應用我們的特征點匹配算法到心臟運動模擬。

402413.label: Realisation of objectives
402413.value: In this project, we have three main objectives. The PI has tackled each proposed problems successfully. Details are as follows. Objective 1: Our first objective is to design and implement mathematical models for different image registration problems. The PI has successfully achieved this goal. There are several tasks involved in this objective. Firstly, the PI has successfully developed an effective algorithm for high-dimensional (n-d) landmark-matching image registration. The quasiconformal registration algorithm for 2D images has previously been developed by the PI. However, the model cannot be applied to general n-d image data. In order to extend this idea to higher dimensional domains, we have proposed a geometric quantity, called the n-D dilation, which measures the local geometric distortion of the n-dimensional mapping. We then proposed a variational model, which finds a n-D landmark-matching mapping between two images minimizing an energy functional involving the n-D dilation. To speed up the optimization process, a multigrid method has been applied. Experiments have been extensively carried out to compute landmark-matching registration between high dimensional domains (such as 3D medical image data). Results show that the method is an effective registration model. Another task is to sparsify piecewise constant images so that image registration can be speeded up. To achieve this goal, the PI has developed an effective algorithm to triangulate a piecewise constant image. An image can be represented by a coarse mesh and values are defined on each triangular faces based on the intensity values of the image. With the triangulated images, we have incorporated the quasiconformal registration model to obtain an efficient landmark-matching registration algorithm, called TRIM. As the triangulated images consist only of small amount of vertices, the quasiconformal registration is fast. Experimental results show that the proposed TRIM algorithm is efficient and can obtain accurate registration results. Besides, we have also proposed to obtain the triangulated image representation of a piecewise constant image by a segmentation algorithm based on quasiconformal mappings. A template mesh is warped to the original image using a suitable quaiconformal map. Different regions of the template mesh are deformed to segment the image into various partitions. The proposed model can also enforce the topological constraint, so that the image is accurately segmented. Experimental result shows that the developed quasiconformal registration model is effective for segmenting the image into regions, which are discretised as triangular meshes. Furthermore, we are interested in developing mathematical models for the restoration and registration of distorted images. The PI has successfully developed mathematical models to achieve this goal. More precisely, the PI has developed a variational model for the joint subsampling and restoration of the distorted image sequence. An optimal subsample of the image sequence capturing the same scene of the image is collected with which a clean image is restored. An efficient optimization method has been developed to solve the variational model. With the restored images, registration between distorted images can be effectively obtained. In addition, we have developed a quasiconformal based model to restore the turburlence distorted images. A reference image is extracted and the geometric distortion of the image is removed using the quasiconformal theories. Experimental results demonstrate that the developed quasiconformal based model can handle the restoration of degraded image with very large geometric distortion, with which image registration can be effectively carried out. Objective 2: The second objective is to develop algorithms for video processing using the Beltrami coefficients. In this project, we have successfully developed different algorithms for video processing using quasiconformal theories. Using the Beltrami coefficients, we can effectively represent and manipulate deformations between images. Consecutive images of a video are often similar up to deformations. By manipulating the deformations between images of a video, we can easily process and compress a video. Using the Beltrami coefficients, we can easily estimate the motion vectors between images using the least number of image frames of a video. To achieve this goal, accurate estimation of the motion vector field is necessary. Using the TRIM algorithm, we can estimate the motion vector fields from a limited number of registered image frames by interpolating the Beltrami coefficients (instead of interpolating the coordinate functions of the motion vector field). The interpolation of the deformation is much better and hence the estimation of the motion vector field is much better. The residual image between the original image frames and the interpolated frames are very sparse, thanks to the accurate estimation of the motion vector field. Experimental results show that the method is effective for video compression. Another task is to enhance the image frame from a lower resolution video. Given an image frame from a video, its adjacent frames provide extra information to enhance the quality of the image frame. To achieve this goal, variational models have been developed, which simultaneously search for the most useful subsample of frames for the enhancement and obtain a high-quality image frame from the subsample of frames. Different fidelity and regularization terms have been proposed to handle various situations, such as noisy frames or frames with large geometric deformations. Results show that our developed models are effective for enhancing an image frame from a low-quality video. Objective 3: Our third objective is to apply the developed algorithms to practical applications. With our developed algorithms, we have applied them for different real applications. More specifically, our developed algorithms for the restoration and registration of distorted image sequence have been successfully applied to restore a latent image from a turbulence-distorted video, such as surveillance video degraded by atmospheric turbulence. The developed algorithms are also effective for removing unwanted geometric distortion by registering the image frame to a reference image frame. Besides, the TRIM algorithm provides an effective solution to estimate the motion vector field between image frames and can be represented by the Beltrami coefficient. A smooth motion simulation can be done by interpolating the Beltrami coefficient representing the registration map between two image frames.

402413.label: Major findings and research outcome
402413.value: In this project, we have developed various mathematical models for image and video processing, which have resulted in 3 published papers and 2 submitted papers (under revision) in different applied mathematics journals. Details are as follows. (1) Development of variational models for the image processing of distorted images: To restore and register distorted images, we have developed variational models for the joint subsampling and restoration of the distorted image sequence [4]. An efficient algorithm has been developed to solve the optimization problem. With the restored images, image registration can be carried out. (2) Quasi-conformal based models for tackling distorted images with very large geometric distortions: To handle distorted images with very large geometric distortions, we have developed Quasi-conformal based models to remove large geometric distortions in the degraded image. Geometric deformation is represented by Beltrami coefficients [5]. A reference image is extracted and the geometric distortion of the image is removed using the quasiconformal theories. (3) Development of TRIM algorithm: We are also interested in sparsifying piecewise constant images so that image registration can be speeded up. To achieve this goal, we have developed an algorithm to triangulate a piecewise constant image. An image can be represented by a coarse mesh and values are defined on each triangular faces based on the intensity values of the image. By incorporating the quasiconformal registration model with the triangulated image, a fast landmark-matching registration algorithm, called TRIM, has been developed [2]. (4) Obtaining triangulated images based on a quasiconformal segmentation model: In [3], we have developed a segmentation algorithm based on quasi-conformal mapping, which can be used to obtain a triangulated image representation. A template mesh is warped to the original image using a suitable quaiconformal map. Different regions of the template mesh are deformed to segment the image into various partitions. (5) Development of mathematical models for high-dimensional (n-d) landmark-matching image registration: In [1], we have developed an algorithm for high-dimensional (n-d) landmark-matching image registration. This extended the 2D quasiconformal registration model the PI has previously developed. More specifically, the n-D dilation, which measures the local geometric distortion of the n-dimensional mapping, has been proposed. With the n-D dilation, an optimization model has been developed to compute the n-D image registration. Multigrid method and alternating minimization scheme are used to solve the optimization problem.

402413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
402413.value: There are two areas for further development of the research. Details are described as follows. (1) Extension of TRIM algorithm to general three-dimensional images: Currently, the TRIM algorithm for fast landmark-matching image registration is implemented for 2-D images. The algorithm can be useful if it can be extended to general three-dimensional images. Using a similar idea, we will explore the possibility to overlay a coarse mesh to the 3D image whose values on each vertices are determined by the intensity values of the image. (2) The variational models for the joint subsampling and restoration of the distorted image sequence do not consider the image deblurring problem. In practice, an image under geometric distortions also suffers from image blur. From the Beltrami coefficients representing the geometric distortions, we will explore the possibility to extract the blurring kernel, so that image deblurring can be incorporated into the variational models.

402413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
402413.value: In this project, the main goal is to develop geometric models for different image and video processing problems. We have explored three research directions: 1. Design algorithms for different image registration problems; 2. Develop algorithms for different video processing problems; 3. Applications of the algorithms to practical problems. We have successfully developed mathematical models for the above three goals. For image registration, we have developed algorithms to sparsify an image by a coarse triangulated image. By sparsifying the images, fast algorithm for landmark-matching image registration has been developed. We have also developed models for the restoration of distorted image sequence. With the restored images, registration of degraded images can be carried out. In addition, we have developed an effective algorithm for n-dimensional landmark-matching image registration. As for the second goal, we have successfully developed different algorithms for video processing using quasiconformal theories. We have developed algorithms to process a video by manipulating deformations between image frames. Different variational models have also been developed for enhancing an image frame from a low-quality video. Our developed algorithms have shown to be useful in various practical applications, such as the restoration of turbulence-distorted image sequence and motion correction.

402613.label: Project Objectives
402613.value: To synthesize and characterize a series of N-heteroacene derivatives, which are rationally designed for applications in organic thin film transistors (OTFTs) and organic photovoltaics (OPVs). To characterize these N-heteroacene derivatives to determine their molecular structures and electronic structures. To study molecular packing and crystallization of the proposed molecules aiming to find the relationship between molecular structures and supramolecular structures in the solid state. To fabricate OTFTs from the proposed N-phenylated N-heteroacenes and to achieve high field effect mobility with the highly crystallized semiconductors from N-phenylated N-heteroacenes. To fabricate OPVs using the co-crystallized p-type and n-type silylethynylated N-heteroacenes as a new type of p-n heterojunction. To characterize the device performance of the OTFTs and OPVs and to elucidate the fundamental links between molecular/supramolecular structures and device performance.

402613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
402613.value: 將氮原子插入到並苯這一類直線型稠環芳烴的骨架中就產生氮雜並苯。繼並五苯之後，氮雜並五苯及其衍生物成為一類新的有機半導體材料，在有機薄膜晶體管中表現出優異的性能，因而得到越來越多地關注。在我們關於氮雜並五苯分子的開創性研究的基礎上，在此我們提出一項研究計劃，從兩個新的方向來探索氮雜並苯。有機薄膜晶體管和有機太陽能電池是兩種基本的有機電子元件。這項計劃致力於研究和這些器件有關的兩個重要問題。 這項計劃研究的第一個問題是有機半導體材料在薄膜中的結晶性。這是一個影響有機薄膜晶體管性能的關鍵因素。在有機薄膜晶體管研究中一個廣為人知的難題是儘管紅瑩烯的單晶保持了有機半導體材料的場效應遷移率的最高紀錄，但是由於紅瑩烯在普通薄膜中結晶度很低因而場效應遷移率也很低。與此相關，我們最近發現氮-苯基化的氮雜並五苯，與其並五苯類似物不同，很容易在真空蒸鍍得薄膜中結晶，從而在薄膜中表現出較高的場效應遷移率。在這一發現的基礎上，我們設計了紅瑩烯的氮雜類似物。我們預期這些新的分子容易形成結晶的薄膜。對這些分子的研究將有助於理解紅瑩烯為什麼在薄膜中不易結晶。 這項計劃研究的第二個問題是有機太陽能電池中的分子組裝。這是一個影響有機太陽能電池能量轉化效率的關鍵因素。到目前為止，能量轉化效率最高的有機太陽能電池一般包括一個體異質結。這個體異質結是一個電子給體（即P-型半導體）和電子受體（即N-型半導體）相互交織的網絡，具有納米尺度的微觀相分離，從而有利於激子的擴散、電荷的分離與傳導。為P-N異質結設計和測試新的超分子組裝結構對於發展更高效的有機太陽能電池十分重要。我們初步研究了矽烷基炔基化的氮雜並五苯的共晶。在此基礎上，我們提出一種新的P-N異質結。這種異質結包含了共結晶的P-型和N-型的矽烷基炔基化的氮雜並五苯，可以視為納米尺度的微觀相分離的一種極端情形。它不僅具有分別傳導空穴和電子的通道，而且提供分子水平上的給體-受體介面。 這項研究計劃的成功實施將有助於開拓新的思路來設計有機半導體材料和器件,為發展高性能有機薄膜晶體管和有機太陽能電池開闢新的途徑。

402613.label: Realisation of objectives
402613.value: We have successfully realized almost all the objectives as detailed below. 1. We synthesized a series of N-heteroacene derivatives and π-extended N-heteroacenes containing a four-membered ring. 2. We studied the molecular structures and electronic structures of these new compounds using experimental and computational methods. 3. We studied molecular packing of N-heteroacene derivatives and π-extended N-heteroacenes in the solid state. We investigated the supramolecular structures of the novel p-n solid solutions of silylethynylated acenes (p-type) and silylethynylated N-heteroacenes (n-type) with an emphasis on the relationship between molecular and supramolecular structures. 4. We applied N-heteroacene derivatives and π-extended N-heteroacenes as organic semiconductors to fabricate organic thin film transistors (OTFTs), and achieved a state-of-art n-channel OTFT exhibiting field effect mobility as high as 11 cm2/Vs. 5. We fabricated organic photovoltaic solar cells (OPVs) using the solid solutions of silylethynylated acenes (p-type) and silylethynylated N-heteroacenes (n-type) as a new type of p-n heterojunction. 6. We characterized the device performance of the OTFTs and OPVs, and compared the performances of a p-n solid solution and a microphase-separated p-n blend in ambipolar OTFTs. From a study on the dependence of electron mobility on temperature, we observed a negative temperature coefficient of electron mobility and found that the grain boundaries in organic semiconductor films played an important role in determining band-like or thermally activated hopping transport mechanism for OTFTs.

402613.label: Major findings and research outcome
402613.value: Through this project, we developed new organic semiconductors based on N-heteroacenes and π-extended N-heteroacenes, fabricated high-performance n-channel organic thin film transistors (OTFTs), studied charge transport mechanism in high-mobility n-channel OTFTs, and explored a new concept of blending p- and n-type organic semiconductors for applications in ambipolar OTFTs and organic solar cells. The most important finding from this project is a state-of-art n-channel OTFT exhibiting field effect mobility as high as 11 cm2/Vs and an observation of a negative temperature coefficient of electron mobility, an indication of band-like charge transport, from this device (Advanced Materials, 2016, 28, 5276). The key characteristic of high-performance OTFTs is a high field effect mobility, which enables organic electronic circuits with sharp turn-on and fast switching for a variety of applications in light-weight, low-cost, flexible and wearable electronics. The electron mobility achieved here set a record for solution-processed n-channel OTFTs at the time of publication. It is also found that the grain boundaries in organic semiconductor films play an important role in determining band-like or thermally activated hopping transport mechanism for OTFTs. Another major finding from this project is that silylethynylated pentacene (p-type) and tetraazapentacene (n-type) form solid-solution crystals, which are conceptually different from either microphase-separated donor-acceptor heterojunctions or stoichiometric donor−acceptor complexes. It is found that this solid solution functioned as an ambipolar semiconductor, whose hole and electron mobilities could be conveniently tuned by varying the donor-acceptor ratio in the solid solution (ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces, 2015, 7, 28019). This project led to publication of 5 primary research articles and 1 review article in decent peer-reviewed journals as well as 3 invited presentations at national and international conferences. Moreover, two PhD students received training from this project. These outcomes are detailed in Part C.

402613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
402613.value: The state-of-art n-channel organic thin film transistors (OTFTs) as realized by this project suggest that N-heteroacenes and, more generally, linearly shaped N-rich polycyclic heteroarenes are a very promising design for n-type organic semiconductors with even higher electron mobility. The research on new organic semiconductors based on this design is in progress in our laboratory. The fact that silylethynylated pentacene and tetraazapentacene form solid-solution crystals suggest that p- and n-type semiconductors with similar molecular shapes can form p-n co-crystals, which can be regarded as a molecular level heterojunction. We propose to investigate photo-induced charge separation and transport in novel co-crystals of p- and n-type organic semiconductors for applications in organic electronic devices.

402613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
402613.value: With the financial support from this General Research Fund, we developed new organic semiconductors on the basis of N-heteroacenes and π-extended N-heteroacenes, fabricated organic electronic devices achieving a state-of-art n-channel organic thin film transistor (OTFT), studied an important question in organic semiconductor physics, and explored a new concept of blending p- and n-type organic semiconductors for applications in ambipolar OTFTs and organic solar cells. The findings from this project help to better understand structure-property relationship for organic semiconductor materials and devices. This project led to publication of 6 research articles in decent peer-reviewed journals as well as 3 invited presentations at national and international conferences. Moreover, two PhD students received training from this project.

403113.label: Project Objectives

403113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
403113.value: 珠江沖淡水在近岸水域形成一個浮羽流，並在夏季西南風的作用下從河口向東輸運，影響香港近海水域環境。珠江的沖淡水攜帶內陸營養物質和微量元素到近岸海域，對近岸的海洋生態系統產生影響。珠三角擁有世界上最密集的人口，在經濟和社會快速發展中發揮了重要作用。然而，隨著上游地區經濟的快速發展，越來越多的無機和有機物質，包括各種沉積物，生活污水和污染物傾倒於珠江水中，河水受到嚴重污染，水質越來越惡化，大大威脅了沿岸海水的生態環境 。珠江沖淡水的水質和生物物理、化學特性主要受浮羽流的動力過程如羽流環流、鋒面過程、混合等因素控制。強斜壓浮羽流可以顯著影響香港沿海的海洋環流。深入研究珠江沖淡水浮羽流動力學特征有助於理解香港沿海水域的複雜的生態系統。因此，珠江羽流的動力學調查與研究對更好地了解香港近岸的生態環境系統和增進香港沿岸水域的數值預測是非常重要的。然而，由於沒有足夠觀測研究資料，我們一直對珠江浮羽流的物理過程了解甚少。在本項目中，我們將進行詳細的珠江浮羽流的動力學研究，並將回答如下有關浮羽流的動力學問題： 1）珠江浮羽流的結構對風驅動力和沿岸流是如何響應的？根據動力學和物理特性，如何分類珠江沖淡水浮羽流？ 2）在夏季西南風和徑流的作用下，珠江浮羽流具有什麼樣的特征？在珠江沖淡水區域，浮羽流的層化和混合具有什麼樣的特征？ 3）在超臨界或亞臨界條件下，什麼是珠江浮羽流鋒面的動力學特性? 珠江浮羽流鋒面混合具有什麼樣的特征？ 本項目的研究側重於取得珠江浮羽流動力學的新結論。通過觀測，得到新的現場數據，為香港有關政府部門所用。研究成果會使我們深入地了解珠江沖淡水對香港沿海水域生態系統的影響效應。本項目的研究結果也有助於了解河流沖淡水浮羽流系統在其他類似地區的過程。

403113.label: Major findings and research outcome
403113.value: 1) A cruise survey of the Pearl River plume during southeasterly and southwesterly winds, two typical wind patterns in summer in Guangdong coastal waters, is reported. Numerical model simulation results suggest that there is a sub-tidal, anti-cyclonic recirculation bulge on the west side out of the estuary mouth under southeasterly winds, showing a re-circulating plume in the near-field. When the wind changes to the southwesterly, however, the re-circulating plume vanishes. The distinct, supercritical tidal plume front occurs with southeasterly winds prevailing in spring tide due to the strong advection in the tidal plume (Pan et al., 2014). 2) Cruise observations reveal that strong mixing appeared in the bottom layer on larger ebb in the estuary. Numerical model simulations show that inside the estuary and in the near-shore water, the mixing is stronger on ebb than on flood. The mixing generation mechanism analysis based on modeling data reveals that bottom stress is responsible for the generation of turbulence in the estuary, for the re-circulating plume area, internal shear instability plays an important role in the mixing, and wind may induce the surface mixing in the plume far-field (Pan et al., 2016). 3) The detachment of low salinity water (LSW) from the Pearl River plume plays an important role in cross-shore transport of the nutrient-rich plume water. Numerical modeling results show that the LSW detachment appears under a pulsed southwesterly wind. In the plume region, upwelling develops under the forcing of the pulsed southwesterly wind, which transports high salinity bottom water to the surface layer, leading to appearance of high salinity water in the surface layer off the Pearl River estuary mouth (Chen et al., 2016). 4) Satellite images from the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) show that there was a belt of turbid water appearing along an upwelling front near the east coast of Guangdong. Numerical modeling results are consistent with the satellite observations. The dynamical analysis suggests that geostrophic equilibrium dominates in the upwelling front and plume areas, and the baroclinicity of the upwelling front resulting from the horizontal density gradient is responsible for the generation of the strong jet, which enhances the far-reaching transport of the terrigenous nutrient-enriched water of the Pearl River plume (Chen et al., 2017).

403113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
403113.value: We will continue to study the dynamics of the Pearl River plume using the cruise-conducted data and the numerical model simulations. The several topics will be addressed including interaction between the tide and wind that could affect the plume dynamics, the mixing dynamics in the plume front, and the role of eddy-flux on the dispersion of the Pearl River plume water in coastal waters.

403113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
403113.value: The discharge of the Pearl River forms a buoyant plume in coastal waters, which is transported eastward from the river mouth and occupies Hong Kong near- and offshore waters, driven by southwesterly winds in summer wet, high-flow season. The river discharge carries inland nutrients and micro-elements into the coastal water area, facilitates a rich primary production area in the Pearl River plume region. In this project, based on the cruse observation data and numerical modeling, we explore the dynamics of the Pearl River plume, study the dispersion of the plume water in coastal waters, and clarify how the Pearl River plume water mix with the causal waters. The results can enhance our understanding of impacts of the Pearl River plume on ecosystem of the Hong Kong coastal water, and contribute to regional management efforts.

403413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
403413.value: The aim of this project is to develop a high-throughput and sensitive assay for quantitative profiling of plasma/serum amino acids by matrix assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight/time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF/TOF MS). Quantitative amino acid profiling is a useful tool for diagnosis of various diseases and for monitoring patients’ nutritional status. Currently, its clinical applications, especially in newborn infants, are limited by its throughput and the amount of plasma/serum sample required for generating reliable results. MALDI-TOF/TOF MS is a sensitive and high-throughput technology. Hence, it may provide a feasible solution to release these limitations. However, technical hurdles exist when applying MALDI-TOF/TOF MS to reliable quantification of small molecules. We have a long-standing interest in applications of MALDI-based MS to quantification of biomolecules. Recently, our group has shown that the major technical hurdles faced by MALDI-TOF/TOF MS-based quantification of small molecules can be overcome by i) using graphitized carbon nanoparticles as matrix, and ii) using a novel MS analysis method - parallel fragmentation monitoring (PFM). By using citrulline, which is a non-essential amino acid, for proof-of-concept, we have demonstrated that our novel method is robust and quantitative. Our subsequent preliminary experiments have suggested that the sensitivity of the current PFM method can be further improved by using other carbon-based nanomaterials. Our preliminary data have also indicated that the PFM method should be applicable to quantifications of other amino acids. In this project, we intend to systemically examine the effects of the types of carbon-based nanomaterials and the amount of sodium chloride on detection sensitivities and fragmentation efficiencies for 6 representative amino acids. On the basis of these finding, we will develop a multiple PFM method for high-throughput and sensitive quantifications of these 6 amino acids in a single assay. Based on our recently published PFM method and the sound preliminary findings, this project represents a natural extension and also continuation of our work. Data on applications of MALDI-based MS and carbon-based nanomaterials to quantitative analyses of small biomolecules have been limited. Results of this project should provide useful foundations for future applications of MALDI-TOF/TOF MS to qualitative and quantitative analysis of amino acids as well as other biomolecules. Furthermore, we expect that this project will result in a high-throughput and sensitive method that requires less than 5 uL plasma/serum for quantitative profiling of amino acids. Ultimately, this method creates new opportunities in clinical applications of quantitative amino acid profiling, especially for neonatal clinics.

403513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
403513.value: In the century of data, the analysis of massive data sets commonly arise in diverse fields of sciences, ranging from computational biology and health studies to financial engineering and risk management. The challenges of high dimensional data analysis have significantly motivated the development of new statistical methodologies and techniques. The Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR)-controlling procedure is an effective method to deal with large-scale simultaneous testing problems when the test statistics are independent and corresponding $p$-values are known. The aim of this proposed research is to further develop the method for multiple hypothesis testing and to develop related asymptotic theory. The research will focus on (i) FDR-controlling procedure under dependence, (ii) developing a procedure to control FDR for many-to-one comparisons, for multiple pairwise comparisons and for large scale tests on correlations, (iii) control simultaneously the false discovery rate and non-discovery rate, and (iv) studying moderate deviation asymptotic theory for related test statistics. 在大数据时代, 许多科学领域通常需要分析大规模数据,如计算生物学,健康研究, 金融工程和风险管理. 高维数据分析中遇到的挑战显著的推动了新的统计方法与技术的发展. 当检验统计量独立且p-值已知时, Benjamini-Hochberg 错误发现率控制方法是处理大尺度假设检验问题的一种有效的方法. 这项研究的目的是针对多重假设检验发展进一步的方法以及相关的渐近理论. 这项研究将主要集中于(i) 相依情形下错误发现率的控制, (ii)发展错误发现率的控制方法, 用来处理多对一比较, 多重两两比较以及大尺度相关性检验, (iii) 同时控制错误发现率及未发现率, (iv) 研究相关统计量的中偏差理论.

403513.label: Major findings and research outcome
403513.value: In Liu and Shao (2014), we first developed a procedure for controlling the false discovery rate (FDR) under dependence and prove that when the population has the finite 4th moment and the dimension m and the sample size n satisfy log m = o(n^{ 1/3}) , the Benjamini and Hochberg method (B–H method) controls the false discovery rate (FDR) and the false discovery proportion (FDP) at a given level α asymptotically with p-values estimated from N(0, 1). However, a phase transition phenomenon occurs when log m > c n^{ 1/3}. In this case, the FDR and the FDP of the B–H method may be larger than α or even converge to one. We also proposed a regularized bootstrap correction which was shown to be robust to the tails of the distributions. In Shao and Zhou (2016), we developed a new randomized concentration inequality and establish a Cramér type moderate deviation theorem for general self-normalized processes which include many well-known Studentized nonlinear statistics. In particular, a sharp moderate deviation theorem under optimal moment conditions is established for Studentized U-statistics. Cramér type moderate deviation theorems quantify the accuracy of the relative error of the normal approximation and provide theoretical justifications for many commonly used methods in statistics. In Chang, Shao and Zhou (2016), we established sharp Cramér-type moderate deviation theorems for Studentized two-sample U-statistics in a general framework, including the two-sample t -statistic and Studentized Mann–Whitney test statistic as prototypical examples. In particular, a refined moderate deviation theorem with second-order accuracy is established for the two-sample t -statistic. These results extend the applicability of the existing statistical methodologies from the one-sample t -statistic to more general nonlinear statistics. Applications to two-sample large-scale multiple testing problems with false discovery rate control and the regularized bootstrap method are also discussed. In Chen, Shao, Wu and Xu (2016), we established a Cramér-type moderate deviation result for self-normalized sums of weakly dependent random variables, where the moment requirement is much weaker than the non-self-normalized counterpart. The range of the moderate deviation is shown to depend on the moment condition and the degree of dependence of the underlying processes. The result was applied to multiple testing and construction of simultaneous confidence intervals for ultra-high dimensional time series mean vectors.

403513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
403513.value: Controlling the false discovery rate and establishing a Cramer type moderate deviation theorem are two very important topics in high dimensional statistical analysis, especially in the age of big data. The PI and his team will continue to work on these topics in the future, in particular, on controlling simultaneously the false discovery rate and the non-discovery rate.

The challenges of high dimensional data analysis have significantly motivated the development of new statistical methodologies and techniques. The Benjamini-Hochberg false dis- covery rate (FDR)-controlling procedure is an effective method to deal with large-scale simultaneous testing problems when the test statistics are independent and corresponding p-values are known. In this project we have further developed the method for multiple hypothesis testing for dependent test statistics, developed a procedure to control FDR for many-to-one comparisons, for multiple pairwise comparisons and for large scale tests on correlations. 403613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
403613.value: Cases of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), a metabolic disorder in connection with high blood sugar level, have been escalating sharply in wealthy society worldwide. At present, optimal blood sugar control can be difficult to achieve even by a combination of therapeutic agents and the major side effects are weight gain and low blood sugar level. About 85% of T2DM patients are overweight or obese. Now, the main challenge in pharmaceutical industry is to develop novel molecules that control blood sugar level and also inducing weight loss or at least preventing further weight gain. Sodium glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) is an enzyme responsible for the glucose reabsorption in the kidney and its inhibition has been proposed as a novel therapeutic strategy for diabetes treatment. Naturally occurring but metabolic unstable phlorizin, a glucose-like molecule, was shown to be a SGLT inhibitor. Prompted by this, synthetic and stable glucose-like molecules are being developed by pharmaceutical companies and some have finished phase III clinical trials. However, none of these SGLT2 inhibitors could inhibit more than 50% of renal glucose reabsorption in humans. Structurally, a synthetic SGLT2 inhibitor is composed of 2 parts: the glucose part and a hydrocarbon portion (aglycon). The present proposal studies the construction of carbocyclic analogues of phlorizin. That is, to replace the glucose part in phlorizin by a pseudo-sugar (carbasugar) moiety to give stable SGLT2 inhibitors. In our preliminary studies, a pseudo-aryl glucoside 7 was made (see main proposal). Recently, a Japanese pharmaceutical company reported the construction of the same molecule 7 which was shown to be a potent SGLT2 inhibitor. Our research approach has therefore been proved viable. This research proposal will continue to investigate the construction of carbocyclic analogues of phlorizin in which the pseudo-sugar is connected to the hydrocarbon via a carbon or a nitrogen linkage. All the synthetic molecules will be tested for SGLT2 inhibition properties. These are the objectives of our present research. The successful research results will form the basis of a general approach for the construction of aryl pseudo-glycosides and will allow the bioactivity of these synthetic chemicals to be studied. In summary, our research results are (a) important for the advancement of the science of synthetic organic chemistry, (b) useful for the chemical industry which may employ our synthetic method for the preparation of related substances of pharmaceutical interests, (c) contribution to the discovery of new anti-diabetic agents. 糖尿病2型（ T2DM ），是一種高血糖的代謝疾病，在全球富裕社會中已經增加很多例子。目前，即使有治療劑的組合, 最佳的血糖控制是難以實現的. 主要的副作用是體重增加和低血糖水平, 大約85％的糖尿病2型患者是超重或肥胖的。現在，製藥行業面臨的主要挑戰是開發新的分子，控制血糖水平，使患者減肥，或至少防止進一步的體重增加。 鈉葡萄糖共轉運2 （ SGLT2 ）是一種酶，在腎臟中的葡萄糖的重吸收負責其抑制已被提出作為用於糖尿病治療的一個新的治療策略。天然存在的，但代謝不穩定的根皮苷，葡萄糖分子，被證明是一種SGLT抑製劑。提示，合成和穩定的葡萄糖分子正在開發的製藥公司和一些已完成III期臨床試驗。然而，沒有這些SGLT2抑製劑能抑制超過50％的人類腎糖再吸收。在結構上，一種人工合成的SGLT2抑製劑是由兩部分組成：葡萄糖部分（糖苷配基）的烴部。 本提案研究碳環類似物的根皮苷的建設。即，由偽糖（ carbasugar ）部分，得到穩定的SGLT2抑製劑，以取代在根皮苷的葡萄糖部分。在我們的初步研究，偽芳基葡萄糖苷7 （見主要建議） 。最近，日本製藥公司的報告被證明是一種有效的SGLT2抑製劑同一分子7的建設。因此，我們的研究方法已被證明是可行的。本研究建議將繼續，調查偽糖被連接到通過碳或氮鍵的烴的碳環類似物的根皮苷的建設。所有的合成分子將被測試SGLT2抑制性能。這些都是我們目前的研究目標。 成功的研究成果將形成基礎為芳偽甙建設的一般方法，並允許這些人工合成的化學物質的生物活性研究。總之，我們的研究結果是： （一）有機合成化學重要的科學進步，（B）可用於化學工業中，可以採用我們的製合成方法製作相關物質.（三）有發現新抗糖尿病藥物的貢獻。

403613.label: Realisation of objectives
403613.value: Palladium-catalyzed coupling reactions have been used extensively in the synthesis of many important pharmaceuticals. It serves as a powerful method to synthesize new compounds which are not readily accessible by traditional synthetic transformations. Recently, we discovered a potent and selective inhibitor of the transporter protein sodium-glucose cotransporter 2. It is a carbasugar which contains a metabolically stable C-O bond. We postulate that the syntheses of their analogues including aryl-carbosugars and amino-carbasugars could provide important insights into the structure– activity relationship (SAR) of these inhibitors, thereby aiding the development of carbasugar SGLT2 inhibitors as antidiabetic and antitumor agents. Carbasugars are carbocyclic analogues of carbohydrates, in which the endocyclic oxygen atom of the sugar core was substituted with a methylene unit. Based on our previous experience, aryl pseudo-C-glycosides, in which a C(sp2)–C(sp3) bond replace a C–O bond, could be superior carbasugar SGLT2 inhibitors as they possess higher stability due to the presence of a “dual C–C linkage” . Towards this research goal, we have developed a concise and stereodivergent synthetic route towards some novel carbasugar analogues of dapagliflozin. The key step involves a mild, regioselective, and stereospecific palladium-catalyzed allyl-aryl coupling reaction which has been underexploited in the synthetic community. A chemoselective diimide reduction was also critical to our synthetic route. Notably, this synthetic study revealed unexpected structure-activity relationship (SAR) of carbasugar SGLT2 inhibitors, and also enabled the discovery of the highly potent and selective inhibitor. A cellular 14C-α-methyl-D-glucopyranoside (14C-AMG) uptake assay was used to evaluate the SGLT2/SGLT1 inhibitory activities of our carbasugar analogues of dapagliflozin. In general, the β-C series were more active than the α-C series, hinting that the β-configuration at C-1 is critical for the inhibitory activity. However, within the β-C series, the cyclohexane analogue showed only a moderate SGLT2 inhibitory activity and only 20-fold SGLT2/SGLT1 selectively; whereas the cyclohexene analogue showed a nanomolar SGLT2 inhibitory activity and more than 400 fold SGLT2/SGLT1 selectively. The excellent potency and selectivity of the cyclohexene analogue towards SGLT2, together with its enhanced stability (as a result of its dual C-C linkage), suggested that it is a highly promising lead compound for further optimization as a clinically useful SGLT2 inhibitor. Another piece of unexpected SAR information came from the activity profiles of aryl pseudo-O-glycosides beta-O series, in which an exocyclic oxygen atom connects the carbasugar and aglycone moiety. We found that this subtle change in spatial connectivity is detrimental to the activity of carbocyclic analogues of dapagliflozin, as suggested by the dramatic loss of inhibitory activity in the beta-O series. In addition, we performed in silico docking analysis by fitting different ligands into a homology model of SGLT2. The ligand binding pocket of SGLT2 is shaped by the hydrophobic residues Phe98, Tyr290, and Trp298, together with hydrogen bond donors/acceptors such as His80, Glu99, and Asn10136, 37. We found that the diarylmethane moiety in both the cyclohexane and cyclohexene analogues stacked perfectly with the aromatic ring of Tyr290, resulting in strong π-π stabilizations. There are also extensive hydrogen bonding interactions between the carbasugar hydroxyl groups and His80, Glu99, and Asn101. Although the hydrogen bond network of the cyclohexane and cyclohexene analogues closely resembles each other, the distorted chair conformation of the cyclohexene allowed an additional hydrogen bonding interaction between the primary hydroxyl group and Ser287, thus leading to an enhanced binding affinity of the cyclohexene analogue. Our computational modeling also revealed that pseudo-O-glycoside is a poor ligand of SGLT2. The exocyclic oxygen atom in aryl pseudo-O-glycoside effectively disrupts the π-π interactions and also withholds the carbasugar core from forming an extensive hydrogen bond network, resulting in the observed lack of SGLT2 inhibitory activity of aryl pseudo-O-glycoside. With the assistance of computational modeling, this SAR study has provided important insights into the ligand space of carbasugar SGLT2 inhibitors, thereby guiding the future exploration of these inhibitors as novel anti-diabetic agents. In addition, recent studies have suggested additional beneficial effects of SGLT2 inhibition, such as reducing body weight, blood pressure, cardiovascular and renal events, which helped to uncover the hidden therapeutic potentials of our novel carbasugar SGLT2 inhibitors. Our study will therefore guide the future design and syntheses of carbasugar SGLT2 inhibitors, thereby unlocking their potential as novel diabetes therapeutics and beyond. Later on, amino-carbasugars were also investigated. Amino-carbasugars are biologically important compounds. For example, valienamine and acarbose were shown to exhibit strong glycosidase inhibitory activities. Despite their biological importance, their syntheses remain challenging and are usually lengthy. The synthetic hurdle has prevented amino-carbasugars from being developed into valuable drug candidates. The targeted aminocarbasugars and the carbocyclic analogues of sergliflozin and dapagliflozin contain a C-N bond, which is not easily accessible by traditional synthetic transformations. Thus, palladium-catalyzed arylation is ideal for such a challenging transformation. The beta-hydride elimination of the [LnPd(NHAlkyl)Ar] intermediate is a potential complication which may lead to the epimerization at C1 on the carbasugar core. However, we envisioned that, with judicious choice of ligand and reaction conditions, the undesired beta-hydride elimination pathway could be suppressed. Based on this strategy, we have developed a novel synthetic avenue towards the syntheses of these biologically active amino-carbasugars using a palladium-catalyzed arylation of a polyhydroxylated carbocyclic amine as the key step. The arylation reactions showed completed chemo- and disastereoselectivities. This synthetic strategy enabled the short and convergent syntheses of these optically pure amino-carbasugars without any epimerization. A cell-based 14C-a-methyl-d-glucopyranoside (14C-AMG) uptake assay was used to evaluate the SGLT2/SGLT1 inhibitory activities of the six novel amino-carbasugars. The amino-carbasugar analogue, the carbocyclic aza-analogue of Sergliflozin, was found to be a highly selective and potent SGLT2 inhibitor. Its IC50 value is 1.9 nm, thus showing that it is as potent as its aryl O-pseudoglycoside counterpart. It also demonstrates an over 3000-fold SGLT2/SGLT1 inhibitory selectivity. Surprisingly, another amino-carbasugar analogue showed almost no SGLT2/SGLT1 inhibitory activities, even though it consists of a beta-delta-glucose-configured core and the aglycone of Dapagliflozin. This brief SAR study revealed that the amine functionality and the distal aromatic ring must be positioned at the ortho-position of the amino group to show a high SGLT2 inhibitory activity. In line with the SARs in aryl O-pseudoglycosides, the didose-configured amino-carbasugar was also inactive, thus suggesting that the inversion of the stereocenter at C5 is not tolerated in carbasugar SGLT2 inhibitors. However, the allylic amine carbasugar analogue showed nanomolar inhibitory activity (5.5 nm) and high selectivity (>1700-fold), despite the fact that it adopts a distorted chair conformation. Overall, two of these amino-carbasugar compounds turned out to show strong SGLT2 inhibitory activity in a cell-based glucose uptake assay. This arylation reaction also enabled the syntheses of conformationally distinct amino-carbasugars, thereby allowing study of their SARs and guiding the future design of clinically valuable drug candidates. The results of the aforementioned works have been published in two high-impact peer-reviewed journals Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. and Scientific reports. The manuscripts have been attached in this report, Part III.

403613.label: Major findings and research outcome
403613.value: In this research project, we have developed a short and convergent synthetic route towards some small-molecule SGLT2 inhibitors by a chemo- and diastereospecific palladium-catalyzed arylation reaction. Selective inhibition of the transporter protein sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) has emerged as a promising way to control blood glucose level in diabetes patients. The newly developed process enabled the discovery of two highly selective and potent SGLT2 inhibitors, thereby paving the way towards the development of carbasugar SGLT2 inhibitors as potential antidiabetic/antitumor agents. In addition, we have developed a concise and stereodivergent synthetic route towards some novel carbasugar SGLT2 inhibitors, featuring an underexploited, regioselective, and stereospecific palladium-catalyzed allyl-aryl coupling reaction. This synthetic strategy, together with computational modeling, revealed the unexpected SAR of these carbasugar SGLT2 inhibitors, and enabled the discovery of a highly selective and potent SGLT2 inhibitor.

403613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
403613.value: We have already identified several potent SGLT2 inhibitors as potential antidiabetic and antitumor agents. With the streamlined synthetic route and SARs of these carbasugar SGLT2 inhibitors, we envision the further exploration of this new family of SGLT2 inhibitors as antidiabetic/ antitumor agents. We have already filed patent for the scientific discovery. Further collaboration with company can boost the progress of drug development.

403613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
403613.value: According to the International Diabetes Federation, more than 550,000 individuals in Hong Kong suffered from diabetes in 2015; the majority of them had Type 2 diabetes. Current treatments are imperfect, and are associated with many side effects. For example, the Metformin treatment may cause nausea, vomiting, and diarrhoea; while insulin therapy may cause low blood sugar, resulting in headache, rapid breathing, and fast heart rate. As mentioned in the ‘Global Report on Diabetes’ issued by World Health Organization (WHO) in 2016, diabetes is an important public health problem, one of the four priority non-communicable diseases targeted for action worldwide. Therefore, research and development for new treatments are needed. In this research endeavor, we used an inexpensive and readily available raw material, gluconolactone, to create these drug-like chemical compounds. A low-cost chemical synthesis methodology was also adopted. Thus, the cost of making these compounds is remarkably low. We also demonstrated that the new compounds are very effective in inhibiting glucose reabsorption by using cellular models, with the molecular target of these compounds being sodium-dependent glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2). These inhibitors have a promising potential to develop as new antidiabetic agents for treating Type 2 diabetes.

403813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
403813.value: When dilute gases of identical atoms are cooled down to temperatures merely a millionth of a degree above absolute zero, the effects of quantum mechanics become dominant. For bosons, they undergo the Bose-Einstein condensation phase transition, which was first realized in 1995. This exotic phase has deep connections with a range of important physical phenomena, such as superconductivity. Compared with other physics systems, the dilute atomic quantum gas system is much easier to control, thus offers us a great opportunity to investigate quantum systems with great flexibility and cleanness. The magnetic Feshbach resonance, commonly used to manipulate the inter-particle interactions, is the workhorse for studying varies interaction driven phenomena in quantum gases. In this project, we propose to further extend the capability of this technique by combining light standing waves with the magnetic field. The success of this project will lead to quantum gases with submicron resolution spatially modulated interactions, which has been largely out of reach so far. Two major side effects: the light induced loss and dipole force will be minimized with the two-photon molecular “dark state” scheme and by choosing bound-bound transitions near the “magic wavelength” where the polarizability is near zero. We expect that with our proposed work the interaction strength modulation can be situated with unprecedented flexibly. It can be used to tackle existing physics problems as well as creating new model systems to enhance our understanding of fundamental quantum physics. In a first example scenario, atoms in the nodes and antinodes of the standing waves will have attractive and zero interactions, respectively. For a quasi 1-D sample, such interaction modulation may induce the output of an atomic soliton train laser, which can be utilized as a non-dispersive atom interferometer source. In another scenario, the local interactions are all repulsive but with interlaced stronger and weaker strengths. This will cause density modulations and spontaneous pattern formations. High resolution spatial and rapid temporal modulation can also be implemented simultaneously with the proposed setup to induced non-equilibrium behavior of the condensate. With the PI’s many years experience on cold molecules and our new group’s current progress, including the achievement of an Rb BEC and the observation of Feshbach resonances, we are confident that the proposed work can be completed successfully. Findings from this project will further broaden the horizon of ultracold quantum gas research and improve our knowledge of quantum fluid under different conditions. 當由全同粒子組成的稀薄氣體被冷卻到接近絕對零度時，量子效應就會開始支配其性質，如果是玻色子，它們就會發生玻色-愛因斯坦凝聚相變。這種在1995年首次實現的相變與許多重要的物理現象，如超導現象等，都有深刻的聯繫。相比其他的物理體系，原子的稀薄量子氣體更加容易操控，因而它很快成為了一種更加靈活和乾淨的研究量子體系的載體。 在量子氣體研究中，磁場引起的Feshbach共振是在研究由相互作用驅動引起的物理現象時，用來調節粒子間相互作用必不可少的手段。在本課題中，我們計劃將磁場的Feshbach共振和光的駐波結合起來實現對粒子間相互作用的亞微米尺度空間調製。根據已有的研究，實現這一技術的最大障礙是光致損耗和光偶極力的影響，為了克服這些困難，我們將借助分子能級的雙光子“暗態”來減少激發態散射的影響，並選用極化率接近零的分子躍遷來消除光偶極力。 我們提出的這一方法可以用來更加靈活的實現相互作用的調製，它既可以被用來研究已有的物理問題，也可以用來創建新的量子物理模型體系。例如，結合磁場和光的駐波，我們可以在波節和波腹分別實現吸引和零相互作用，在準一維情況下，可以由此用來誘導輸出原子孤子序列激光器，它可以被用作無色散的原子干涉儀的粒子源。由於光場可以輕易的實現快速的時間調製，我們提出的方法也可以用來實現相互作用在時間和空間中的同時調製，由此可以研究非平衡態量子氣體的性質。 這一方向充分結合了項目負責人在冷分子領域的經驗和本研究小組的現有條件，最近，我們已經成功實現了銣原子的凝聚體並觀測到了磁場誘導的Feshbach共振，因此我們相信本課題提出的工作可以成功完成。我們的這一研究將進一步擴展超冷量子氣體的研究領域，並提高我們對不同情況下量子流體的認識。

403813.label: Realisation of objectives
403813.value: The main goal of this project is to create and study ultracold quantum gas with spatially modulated interactions. We plan to achieve this by combining a magnetic Feshbach resonance with light control. Near the Feshbach resonance, when the threshold of the colliding pair of atoms is in the vicinity of a bound level in another collision channel, the interaction between atoms can be tuned at will. With light coupling the bound level to another level in the excited state, the resonant condition of the Feshbach resonance can then be tuned. If the light is a standing wave with periodical maximum and minimum, then the atom-atom interaction can be tuned periodically as well. We started this project in January 2014. During the 3 years period of this grant, we successfully finished all the proposed technical objectives. As the grant supported is substantially less than we asked for, we had to use home-built electronics and lasers. The result is satisfactory, but it took us longer time. With these improvements, we achieved the following goals: 1) the high field was stabilized to less than 10 mG fluctuation at 1000 G. Now we the narrow Rb 1007 G Feshbach resonance can be resolved without problem. 2) We built the diode laser for high field imaging; the high field imaging was successfully demonstrated. 3) We also built an offset locking system, which has allowed us to phase-lock two diode lasers for two-photon spectroscopy with high resolution. We then performed the one-photon PA with optical trapped Rb gases. We were able to recover multiple photoassociation resonances which have been reported before. However, the resonance near 790 nm can only be observed with very high laser intensity. As a result, the atom cloud was heated up too quickly for further investigations. We believe this is due to the much weaker transition. Meanwhile, as 790 nm is just in between the D1 and D2 line, the off resonant scattering is severe with high intensity. In order to move forward, we have tried to use a strong PA resonance which allowed us to use less laser power to address the excited state. With this, we were able to observe some amount of shift of the Feshbach resonance. However, the result was not repeatable. We believe this is due to the fluctuation of the magnetic field and the relatively broad linewidth. Since the bound state causing the Feshbach resonance has a very small binding energy, the 10 mG field fluctuation and the laser linewidth actually have a significant influence on the experiments. Unfortunately, further improve the magnetic field stability to much less than 10 mG at the 1000 G field turned out to be a big challenge. The laser linewidth was measured to ~ 500 kHz. To further narrow it down will require a very different technique which typically involves a high finesse optical cavity currently not available. We then decided to explore other systems which can be manipulated with light but with less stringent technical requirement. Our idea is to try to do the experiments at low magnetic field so that controlling its fluctuation to below 10 mG is easy. In one of the experiments, we looked at the spinor gas system of Rb. The spin oscillation in spinor gases is determined by the spin-exchange interaction and its completion with the second-order Zeeman effect. Using light at appropriate polarization, an effective light induced magnetic field can be created. This can then be used to control spin dynamics. As shown below in Fig. 1, we observed coherent spinor dynamics in thermal Rb spin-1 and spin-2 gases. This result was published in Physical Review A. We noticed that, in combination of the small DC magnetic field, it is possible to use the light induced magnetic field to tune and control the spin dynamics. As the width of the resonance is on the order of 100 mG, to observe significant effects, the light induced B field should be at least 10 mG. Under this kind of condition, the light intensity is smaller then the previous case, but the heating is still there. Nevertheless, it should be possible to investigate spinor dynamics with spatially varying magnetic fields. To seek for systems allowing low loss manipulation with light, we turned to the spinor system consisting of two different atoms: spin-1 Na and spin-1 Rb. In this kind of spinor mixture, the interspecies spin dynamics is determined by the spin-exchange interaction and its competition with the total magnetic Zeeman energy. Furthermore, there are multiple possible spin exchange channels. In the first experiment, we focused on the process Rb|0>+Na|-1>↔Rb|-1>+Na|0>. The Zeeman energy different between the two sides have a zero at about 1.7 G. Near this B field, we observed coherent spin oscillations between Rb and Na. In addition, we also observed the shift of the resonance position by the light induced magnetic field. Our results in this work were published in Physical Review Letters. While the light induced B field in the above work was generated by the optical trap laser, we have started to explore the possibility of using an individual laser at 790 nm. Here, since the linear Zeeman effect can affect the heteronuclear dynamics, a very small light intensity can generate significant effect. As a result, the loss is minimized. Fig. 3 shows the preliminary result for the Rb|0>+Na|0>↔Rb|1>+Na|-1> which has a resonance at 0.8 G without the light induced magnetic field. With the light on, the spinor resonance is to 2.2 G. Further investigations, including the possibility of applying a standing wave to generate spatially modulated spin dynamics, are currently going on.

403813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
403813.value: While the original plan of manipulating the Feshbach resonance with light didn't work as well as planned, the heteronuclear spinor mixture system does show great promise. We will explore more along this direction in the future. The physics in the new scheme will focus more on the control of the spin dependent interaction, which is much smaller than the mean-field interaction. The main advantage of this scheme is the low loss since very small change of the energy scale has significant influence on the spin dynamics. The preliminary result is already very encouraging and its extension to a standing wave following similar idea in our proposal seems to be straightforward. This is a rather new system, but we already noticed several theoretical works discussing possible physics to be explored with similar settings. Especially, the possibility of connecting this system to topological defects in the spin degree of freedom is very attractive. We hope to continue our exploration along that line.

403813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
403813.value: In dilute gas of ultracold atoms, the seemingly weak inter-atomic interactions can actually bring many exotic properties, such as the superfluidity, to the system. A major theme in ultracold physics is to manipulate the interaction of atoms to realize different quantum behaviors. Many ground-breaking results have been achieved in the last two decades along this line. This proposal aims to explore the combination of magnetic Feshbach resonance and light wave to generate condensates with spatially modulated interactions which have been predicted to lead to many interesting phenomena. However, after the first stage of investigations, we realized the light induced heating is too severe to realize our original idea. We thus turned to the much smaller spin dependent interaction and try to control the spin dynamics with light. We observed, for the first time, coherent spin oscillations between two different atomic species. We further realized control of the spin oscillations with laser light induced magnetic field. We are currently investigation the possibility of generating spin dynamic with spatial modulations with standing wave of light. Our works opened a new avenue for ultracold mixture physics. Further investigations may lead to deep connections with topics like topological physics.

404213.label: Major findings and research outcome
404213.value: We have developed polymer coated biocompatible and biodegradable magnesium (Mg) with a controllable corroding rate inside the human body so that they can be used for for bone fracture fixation. Namely, we have developed several procedures to coat Mg/Mg alloys surfaces with a thin layer of biodegradable polymer. Although such a coating reduces the long-term corrosion rate, it also prevents the short-term quick release of beneficial growth-stimulating Mg++ ions after orthopedic operations. In order to meet these conflicting short- and long-term requirements, we have composited a certain type and quantity of Mg salts into a polymer coating for implants such that these salts can properly percolate inside the polymer matrix to form bi-continuous phases of polymer and salt during the coating formation on the Mg/Mg alloy surface. In the first few weeks following an orthopedic operation, the dissolution of these embedded salts controllably releases Mg++ ions and produces the inter-connected channels to regulate the long-term corrosion rate of the underneath Mg/Mg alloys. Our objectives have been accomplished.

404213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
404213.value: The know-how gained in this study to prepare coated Mg/Mg alloys with different dissolution and corrosion rates can be further used in preliminary animal tests and future orthopedic applications.

404213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
404213.value: Biocompatible and biodegradable magnesium (Mg) and its alloys possess excellent potential as orthopaedic implant biomaterials because a) they have similar mechanical properties to natural bones; and b) magnesium ions (Mg++) are known to promote the growth of new bone. However, Mg/Mg alloys corrode inside the human body too fast. To overcome such a fast corrosion of Mg, people had tried to coat Mg/Mg alloys surfaces with a thin layer of biodegradable polymer. Although such a coating reduces the long-term corrosion rate, it also prevents the short-term quick release of beneficial growth-stimulating Mg++ ions after orthopedic operations. In order to meet these conflicting short- and long-term requirements, we have composited a certain type and quantity of Mg salts into a polymer coating for implants such that these salts can properly percolate inside the polymer matrix to form bi-continuous phases of polymer and salt during the coating formation on the Mg/Mg alloy surface. In the first few weeks following an orthopedic operation, the dissolution of these embedded salts releases Mg++ ions in a controllable fashion and produces the inter-connected channels to regulate the long-term corrosion rate of the underneath Mg/Mg alloys. The outcomes of this study not only shed light on how inorganic salts are percolated inside a polymer during their phase separation, but will also have direct implications in a rational and novel design of orthopedic biomaterials for implants. The success of this proposed study illustrates how important to combine polymer chemistry, physical characterization and biomedical tests and applications together. Our future is multidisciplinary.

404413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
404413.value: 造物主創造了讓人歎為觀止的分子建築體來實現精妙的化學和生物學功用，比如多酶複合物。這些合計長久以來啟發著合成生物學家來設計多酶組裝體，從而實現最優的催化效率。比如，在蛋白質或者DNA骨架上的酶的模組化組裝成功控制了控制代謝流。然而，已報導的這些方法面臨兩個局限。第一，酶的組裝體限於線性結構；其二，組裝體可能分解。 最近我們探索了一個新的策略，被稱為“結合誘導交聯”。受到酶反應的啟發，我們成功設計了幾個不同的蛋白-多肽對。這些蛋白-多肽對的相互作用誘導了一個分子間的硫醚鍵的形成。這類反應是特異性的、快速、自發，而且是彼此正交的。因此，這些蛋白-多肽反應對能夠用作樂高單元來在合成的多肽骨架上組裝個體的酶。此外，我們也可通過控制多肽骨架的結構而實現構建不同結構的多酶複合物。 甲基萘醌類化合物的生物合成把分支酸轉換為維生素K2。這一合成途徑在細菌中極其重要。參與這一途徑的每個酶都已經克隆且被詳細研究了。然而把這些酶組裝成多酶複合體是否能夠大大提高底物的轉換仍然是個迷。為了回答這一疑問，我們計畫把共價樂高單元應用於雙酶和三酶複合物的組裝。我們可以形成樹枝狀的共價多酶組裝體。通過分析多酶組裝體的底物轉換，我們可以回答在甲基萘醌類化合物的生物合成中空間組裝是否能夠影響代謝流。 本課題的成功進行需要化學合成和生物實驗兩方面的技能。我們在這兩方面都有多年的經驗。我們的初步實驗也證明本計畫是高度可行的。本課題的成功，一方面可以提供蛋白工程師一整套新的工具，另一方面可以首次揭示多酶複合物中的酶的空間組裝怎樣影響代謝流。我們有信心按期完成。

404413.label: Realisation of objectives
404413.value: Both objectives have been fully realized upon the completion of this project. More specifically, we successfully developed a set of four protein covalent reactions that are fully orthogonal with each other. We then demonstrated the construction of Y-shaped protein complexes by covalent crosslinking reactions. Next, enzymes in menaquinone biosynthesis pathway MenD, MenH and MenF have been assembled into multi-enzyme complexes that can catalyze the sequential reaction from chorismic acid to SHCHC. We demonstrate that the assembled enzymes show much higher production yield of the product than un-assembled free enzymes. Also the intermediate level is significantly reduced. This proves spatial arrangement of the cascade biocatalytic enzymes can improve metabolic flux. This then presents the first example that utilizes bioconjugating protein reactions for multienzyme assembly.

404413.label: Major findings and research outcome
404413.value: This work developed a very novel method for covalent protein reactions, using the concept "proximity-induced reaction" and specific protein-peptide interactions that are prevalent in nature. By installing a mindfully selected electrophile in the selected position of the peptide and engineering a cysteine residue at specific position of the protein target, we realized site-specific conjugation reaction to four different proteins. These four pairs of conjugation reactions showed impressive orthogonality towards each other, making it feasible for a Lego-type of covalent assembly. We demonstrated a use of this technique where four pairs of the reactions were used to construct a Y-shaped covalent protein assembly. This is the first trial towards the use of this strategy for multienzyme assembly. Also, we used menaquinone biosynthetic enzymes for assembly of three enzymes and fully demonstrated the substrate channeling effect, with lower concentration of intermediate, and higher production of the product. One key paper from this work was highlighted on the cover of an ACS journal, and the other one highlighted in a review paper. Because of this work, we were invited to write a review article to introduce this novel chemistry and its applications to the community. I was invited to multiple international conferences to present this work. A total of four PhD students received training under this project, with two graduated with PhD during the period.

404413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
404413.value: Covalent site-specific reactions and multienzyme complex construction, two objectives in this project have expanded and evolved to two research directions in my lab, site-specific reaction inside cells and structural basis of multienzyme catalysis. For example, we are now exploring the application of cysteine site-specific reaction to a broader range of biological contexts. For the second direction, we have formed multienzyme complexes inside cells and demonstrated a drastic increase of the biosynthesis of valuable chemicals. Both directions have led to a series of funding applications. We will also seek potential commercial use based on the techniques developed from this project.

404413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
404413.value: Like we play Lego game, which employs the concept of plug-and-play and free assembly into different architectures, we now can use protein units and peptide linkers to do a covalent reaction-based Lego assembly. This fuses science with engineering, and opens a new dimension in a variety of applications. One of the exciting applications is to assemble enzymes that catalyze sequential steps in a reaction, as catalytically active "Lego" assemblies.

404513.value: 旋转热湍流中边界层动力学及Ekman输运的实验研究

404513.label: Project Objectives
404513.value: To investigate the Ekman layer dynamics by measuring the instantaneous three-dimensional (3D) flow field directly. The thickness of the Ekman layer will also be measured. To measure the thickness and the spatial structures of thermal boundary layer. To study how boundary layers affect the global flow properties. To investigate the flow state transitions (i.e. from rotation-controlled to non-rotating regimes) with respect to the relative thicknesses of the measured Ekman and thermal boundary layers. To study how boundary layers affect the global flow properties. 404513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
404513.value: Rotating Rayleigh-Bénard (RB) convection is a simplified but relevant model to study the fundamental effects of rotation on convective flows, which is not only of scientific interest but also important to the understanding of related phenomena in the planets and stars. One major open question is to understand the transition among different flow states. Although there are growing evidences suggesting that boundary layers play an important role in determining the flow dynamics and thus controlling the transition among the different regimes, the debate on this issue is still ongoing and far from conclusion. This is especially so in view of the fact that experimental works on this issue remain limited. Ekman pumping is an important process that is responsible for the active influence of boundary layers on the flow properties far away from the boundaries in rotating flows. However, its highly complex dynamics has not been systematically studied experimentally. The scarcity of experimental data concerning boundary layer dynamics and its associated effects in rotating RB convection has prompted the proposed investigation. In this project we will make direct measurements of both the thicknesses and the spatial structures of the thermal boundary layer and of the three-dimensional Ekman layer in rotating RB convection, the latter has never been measured experimentally. These results will be connected to the global heat transfer measurements to understand the regime transition behavior. In addition, a modified Lagrangian particle tracking technique will be used to study the transport behavior in Ekman pumping process, by measuring the local heat flux, particle accelerations and dispersions simultaneously, which is a unique feature of the proposed project. The obtained results should enable us answering how boundary layers affect the flow dynamics and also to provide a dynamical picture of Ekman pumping. 作为一个研究旋转效应对热对流的基本影响的简化模型，旋转瑞利-伯纳德对流(Rayleigh-Bénard convection)吸引着人们广泛的科学兴趣，并对帮助理解各类星体中的相关现象发挥着重要作用。在对该系统的研究中，其中一个非常重要却悬而未决的问题是理解不同的流动状态之间是如何转变的。尽管有越来越多的证据表明边界层在决定流体动力学中有着重要作用从而控制了不同状态之间的转变过程，但关于这个问题的争论仍然存在，而且实验方面的工作还相对缺乏。事实上，在旋转流体中，边界层对流场性质的影响主要是通过埃克曼(Ekman)输运这一重要过程来实现的。然而，由于其动力学的复杂性，该物理过程还没能得到系统的实验研究。 在本课题中，我们不仅会测量旋转瑞利-伯纳德对流中温度边界层的厚度和其空间结构，还会在实验上第一次直接测量埃克曼边界层的三维结构。这些结果将会和传热效率的测量结果结合在一起，去理解不同流动状态之间的转变过程。此外，一套经过改进的拉格朗日(Lagrangian)粒子示踪系统将被用来研究埃克曼输运过程，包括局部热流的传输、粒子的加速度和传播扩散等。这是本研究的一大特色。我们期待这些结果能够回答在旋转热湍流中边界层如何影响流场的动力学特性这一重要问题，同时也让人们对埃克曼输运的动力学过程有一个清楚的认识。

404513.label: Realisation of objectives
404513.value: We have successfully constructed a rotating Rayleigh-Benard turbulent convection apparatus with a rotating speed of up to 240 RPM. With this apparatus, we can conduct rotating RB convection experiments with the varying range of the Rayleigh number from 1e8 to 1e12, and the Ekman number from 1e-4 to 5e-9. Both heat transport and optical measurements can be made. Our heat transported measurements have shown that within certain parameter range, Ekman pumping effect can indeed enhance the heat transfer efficiency, the Nusselt number. We also obtained the three dimensional velocity field (3D). The instantaneous velocity field shows how plume structure evolves as the rotating frequency increases (or the Ekman number decreases), i.e. they change into highly confined vortex columns that span the entire cell height. By measuring the thermal boundary layer and the momentum boundary layer directly, our results also reveal a crossing between the two boundary layers when the Ekman number decreases. This crossing is further found to be responsible for the optimal enhancement of heat transfer efficiency in rotating RB convection. We also made the first experimental study of the influences of the thermal boundary condition on turbulent thermal convection.

404513.label: Major findings and research outcome
404513.value: Our study of the vortex dynamics has shown the existence of global clustering of vortices in space, while dynamically the motion of vortices exhibit random motion. We further found the existence of universality in scalar transport enhancement among three systems: Rotating Rayleigh-Benard Convection, Confined Rayleigh-Benard Convection, and Double Diffusive Convection. We found that all of the three systems exist the competition between stabilizing force and unstabilizing force, and the stabilizing force provides either a static or dynamics confinement to the respective turbulent flows. Furthermore, an optimal transport enhancement exists that correspond to the optimal coupling between suction action and scalar fluctuation in the boundary layers. In the case of rotating RB convection, this corresponds to the generation of maximum Ekman pumping effect. Out comparative experimental study between the fixed temperature and fixed heat flux thermal boundary conditions in turbulent thermal convection has revealed that the differences in the boundary condition lead to rather unexpected changes in the flow dynamics. It is found that, surprisingly, reversals of the large-scale circulation occur more frequently under constant temperature than under constant heat flux, despite the fact that in the former its flow strength is larger than that in the latter. Our results not only show which aspects of the thermal boundary condition are important in thermal turbulence, but also reveal that, counterintuitively, the stability of the flow is not directly coupled to its strength. Our experimental study has shown that a minute amount of polymer additives can significantly enhance heat transport in the bulk region of turbulent thermal convection. The effects of polymer additives are found to be the enhancement of coherent heat fluxes and suppression of incoherent heat fluxes. The enhanced heat transport is associated with the increased coherency of thermal plumes, as a result of the suppression of small-scale turbulent fluctuations by polymers. The incoherent heat flux, arising from turbulent background fluctuations, makes no net contribution to heat transport.

404513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
404513.value: In the future, we plan to explore the long-time dynamics of the vertex columns. The effect of centrifugal force, which has been neglected in most studies of rotating convection, will be investigated. There are evidences that this effect may be important in certain situations. We also plan to study rotating RB convection in non-idealized situations such as the rotation axis is not aligned with the system's symmetry axis.

404513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
404513.value: Convection phenomena exist ubiquitously in geophysical and astrophysical systems, such as in the core and atmosphere of planets and in star. As almost all planets and stars are rotating objects, understanding convection under rotation is therefore essential to our understanding of the many properties of planets and start. It is very common in nature and engineering settings that, in addition to a driving force, a system is also subjected to a stabilizing force. For a highly nonlinear system, the presence of the stabilizing force may induce surprising phenomena. Our study therefore reveals a universal mechanism underpinning scalar transport enhancement in the several different types of turbulent flows including rotating convection. The ability to understand similar phenomena occurring in different systems under a unified framework has been a hallmark of physics research. The present study of stabilizing-destabilizing flows provides one such example and may therefore inspire work on other systems.
