409813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
409813.value: The aim of this project is to develop the Virtual Substitution Scan (VSS) method for efficient lead optimization. Lead optimization is a key step in structure-based drug discovery, where compounds identified from an initial screening, i.e., the leads, are modified chemically to improve their activities. In the past, computational methods have played an increasingly important role in lead optimization. Prior to any chemical synthesis, free energy calculations can be performed to predict whether a certain modification, such as substituting a hydrogen with a chlorine (H→Cl), will enhance the activity of the lead. The results are then used to guide the subsequent, more expensive chemical synthesis. Nevertheless, existing free energy methods tend to be resource-intensive and time-consuming — calculating a single chemical substitution usually takes days, or even weeks, on dozens of central processing units (CPUs). As lead optimization frequently requires hundreds of substitutions to be evaluated, the high computational cost has severely limited the application of free energy methods. Experienced in free energy calculation and enhanced sampling methods, we will develop VSS into an efficient and easy-to-use lead optimization tool. Through a single round of VSS calculation, we will evaluate all the possible substitutions of aromatic hydrogens by small functional groups. Following its development, we will implement VSS in the open-source program VMD to make it available to the entire drug discovery community. Finally, we will demonstrate the applicability of VSS through optimizing inhibitors of a novel enzyme target in anti-tuberculosis drug discovery. Our method can produce accurate results at a fraction of the computational cost of existing techniques. Apart from its application in anti-tuberculosis drug design, VSS can be used to guide the lead optimization efforts on many other targets. In particular, the open-source nature of our implementation allows VSS to be used in academic drug discovery targeting a variety of neglected diseases, which predominantly impact people in China and other developing countries. 本项研究旨在增强电脑辅助药物优化设计的效率。 药物优化是基于结构的药物设计中重要的一环。在进行化学合成之前，通过结合自由能的计算，我们可以预测某种对药物结构的变化，例如将一个氢原子变为一个氯原子，是否会带来更高的活性。这类计算的结果可被用来指导接下来的化学合成。然而，现有的结合自由能计算方法对计算资源和时间都有很高的要求－－计算一个位点通常需要十几个CPU运行数天。我们旨在研究开发一种便于应用且高效的计算工具，可一次性完成对所有位点上较小的功能团的计算。基于开源的VMD软件，我们的工具可以被学术界的用户免费使用。我们还将在一个抗结核菌的目标蛋白上测验及应用我们的工具。

409813.label: Realisation of objectives
409813.value: As stated in the above objectives, this project revolves around developing a single-step FEP calculation method for the rapid scan of small functional group substitutions. The first two objectives (the development and implementation of our method) has each been fully achieved. Specifically, we have developed the virtual substitution scan (VSS) method for 12 small substitutional groups, exceeding the previously proposed 8 groups. We have implemented our method as a plugin of the popular visualization and analysis package VMD and has made it publicly available online (https://github.com/YingChihChiang/VSS). Apart from these tasks proposed in the original project, we further expanded our theoretical study of the single-step FEP method based on results obtained during the completion of objective 1. More specifically, during the VSS method development, we noticed an unexpected large error in the calculation involving groups like -OCH3. Motivated by the need to understand and eliminate this error, we thoroughly analyzed the VSS performance and found that the error can be largely reduced through adopting a ghost ligand potential that includes not only the bonded, but also the non-bonded energy terms. Once this 'full' ghost ligand potential is used, the calculation gives considerably improved performance without the expensive angle sampling. This result is not only applicable to our VSS calculation but also applies for other single-step FEP methods in general. Further expanding from our VSS calculation efforts, we also implemented an enhanced sampling method, namely, the GaMD method, into the program NAMD. These results have been summarized in the three publications attached at the end of this report. Regarding objective 3, which involves the application of the developed method, we are only now beginning to perform the calculation on the protein targets, although we did finish a preliminary test on a model protein, the lysozyme. This under-achievement of objective 3 is mainly due to the unexpected large VSS error on certain functional groups as described above. We spent a considerable amount of time understanding and eliminating the source of this error, which, as noted earlier, has produced deeper insight into the single-step FEP method and generated an additional publication (the second attached paper in Part C). This publication was only finished recently (Dec 2016) and we have just begun to apply our method on calculations involving protein targets.

409813.label: Major findings and research outcome
409813.value: 1. We developed the Virtual Substitution Scan (VSS) toolkit as a plugin of the open-source visualization and analysis software VMD. Based on the single-step free energy perturbation (sFEP) method, VSS enables the user to post-process a plain MD trajectory for a fast free energy scan of substituting aryl hydrogens by 12 different small functional groups. Dihedrals of the functional groups are sampled explicitly in VSS, which improves the performance of the calculation and is found particularly important for certain groups. Overall, the computational cost of VSS is found to be only a fraction of the corresponding multi-step FEP (mFEP) calculation, while its results agree reasonably well with those of mFEP, indicating that VSS offers a promising tool for rapid free energy scan of small functional group substitutions. See the first attached paper in Part C for details. 2. We applied our VSS method to elucidate and eliminate one source of error in sFEP calculations. We demonstrated that the accuracy of sFEP could be significantly affected by the vibration of bond angles, traditionally considered as ‘rigid’ degrees of freedom and kept fixed during sFEP. We further revealed that this unexpected contribution from angle vibration arose from adopting a ghost ligand potential containing only bonded terms. Once the intramolecular non-bonded interactions were included, the error upon substituting aryl hydrogen by -OCH3, for instance, dropped from 3 kcal/mol to around 0.5 kcal/mol. Along with the work described above, this study paved the way for using sFEP and plain MD to conduct rapid, first-round search for chemical modifications that optimize the binding of a ligand towards its target receptor. See the second attached paper in Part C for details. 3. We implemented an enhanced sampling method, GaMD, into the program NAMD. Radiating from our own method development of VSS, we also contributed to the implementation of the enhanced sampling method Gaussian accelerated molecular dynamics (GaMD) into the widely used program NAMD. See the third attached paper in Part C for details.

409813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
409813.value: How to render sFEP calculations even more efficient and accurate is an important and ongoing research subject that calls for further investigation. Based on our VSS method, the PI and the first author of the aforementioned publications, Dr. Chiang, Ying-Chih (soon to be a Newton Scholar at U. Southampton), plan to continue working in the theoretical method development on this subject.

409813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
409813.value: The rapid expansion of our computing power has produced ever longer computer simulations of various biomolecules. In particular, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations ranging from hundreds of nanoseconds to microseconds or even milliseconds have become increasingly common. To promote the “recycling” of these plain MD simulations, we developed the Virtual Substitution Scan (VSS) toolkit as a plugin of the open-source visualization and analysis software VMD. Based on the single-step free energy perturbation (sFEP) method, VSS enables the user to post-process a plain MD trajectory for a fast free energy scan of substituting aryl hydrogens by 12 small functional groups. Results from this project indicate that VSS offers a promising tool for rapid free energy scan. Furthermore, VSS results have suggested a best combination of ghost ligand potential and dual topology setting, which offers a general strategy to improve the accuracy of sFEP calculations.

409913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
409913.value: The project aims at studying the Boltzmann equation with dynamic screening effect, arising from plasma physics and describing the time evolution of quantum gas particles, with focus on well-posedness of the Cauchy problem as well as qualitative and quantitative properties of solutions. The Boltzmann equation established in 1872 is the cornerstone of collisional kinetic theory. Its importance lies in bridging a link between the reversible molecule mechanics and the irreversible macroscopic procedure manifested by the celebrated H-theorem. The classical Boltzmann collision operator for a rarefied gas is quadratically nonlinear with possibly singular cross sections depending only on the relative velocity and the deviation angle. On the other hand, for a plasma which generally exists in universe, some additional physical mechanisms such as quantum effect and dynamic screening must be taken into account, leading to some variants of the equation. Among them, it is Balescu who first derived in 1961 a Boltzmann-type equation with dynamic screening effect. The most distinct character compared to the classical case is that dynamic cross sections depend on unknown distributions in a complex way and does not enjoy the factorization property even at equilibrium. The fundamental question in kinetic theory is global existence and uniqueness of solutions. Indeed tremendous progress has been made by many people on the classical Boltzmann equation in different settings, such as weak renormalized solutions and classical solutions around Maxwellians. Particularly, an almost satisfactory theory has been realized for the spatially homogenous problem, even with physically singular cross sections. However, to our knowledge, nothing is known for the Boltzmann equation with dynamic screening. The main purpose of the project is to investigate the behaviour of the special screening collision kernel without the factorization property, and establish well-posedness theory for the nonlinear Cauchy problem as used in those classical frameworks. We attempt to develop new techniques and approaches to treat the problem, at least in perturbative regime where we have been working in the field of kinetic theory for the classical Boltzmann equation. The classical Boltzmann integral is meaningless for the Coulomb interaction between charged particles. Though, the integral with dynamic screening derived by Balescu is convergent. The research results of the project are expected not only to bring out new understandings of the mathematical theory of kinetic plasma but also to justify the physical model in an appropriate setting. 本项目旨在研究等离子物理学中描述量子气体粒子时间演化的具有动态屏蔽效应的玻尔兹曼方程，主要关注的是柯西问题的适定性及解的定量和定性的性质。 在1872年建立的玻尔兹曼方程是带碰撞的动力学理论的基石，其重要性在于它在可逆的分子力学和不可逆的宏观过程之间建立了一个桥梁关系，例如著名的H定理。稀薄气体的经典玻尔兹曼碰撞算子是二次非线性的，它依赖于粒子间碰撞的相对速度和偏转角。另一方面，对于宇宙中普遍存在的等离子体，一些额外的物理机制也必须考虑，比如量子效应和动态屏蔽效应，这些将诱导出一些经典方程的变体。其中，Balescu 在1961年首次导出了带有动态屏蔽效应的玻尔兹曼类型的方程。它同经典情形相比较最不同的特征是动力散射截面以一种复杂的方式依赖于未知分布函数本身，甚至在平衡态处也不具有经典情形可分离的性质。 动力学理论中最基本的问题是解的全局存在性和唯一性。事实上，人们已经在经典玻尔兹曼方程的各个方面取得了巨大的进展，比如弱正规化解和Maxwellian附近的古典解。特别地，空间齐次问题，甚至在奇异散射截面的情况，几乎已有满意的理论。 然而，关于带有动态屏蔽效应的玻尔兹曼方程的研究还是一无所知的。 这个项目的主要目的是研究没有分离性质的特殊的带屏蔽效应的碰撞核，并且建立一套类似于经典框架下的非线性柯西问题的适定性理论。我们尝试发展新的技术和方法来解决该问题。至少在扰动的框架下，我们一直致力于有关经典玻尔兹曼方程的动力学理论相关领域的研究。 在带电粒子的库伦力相互作用下，经典的玻尔兹曼积分是毫无意义的，但由Balescu 导出的带有动态屏蔽效应的碰撞积分是收敛的。我们期望这个项目的研究结果不仅能给等离子体动力学理论的数学研究带来一些新的理解，而且也期望能在一些适当的情形下验证物理模型。

409913.label: Realisation of objectives
409913.value: First of all, let us focus on the first part of the main objectives. Indeed, we have derived a Boltzmann-type collision operator. In the classical case, the Boltzmann collision kernel depends only on the relative velocity and the derivation angle between the pre-collisional and post-collisional relative velocities. Compared to the classical case, the newly derived Boltzmann collision kernel is a non-negative function of the projections of the pre-collisional velocities onto a given interaction direction. Even though there is such difference, the Boltzmann-type collision operator enjoys some similar properties as in the classical situation including the collision invariants, macroscopic conservation laws, and entropy-entropy product inequality. In order to establish the perturbation theory around global Maxwellians as in the classical case, one has to first provide an equivalent description of the Dirichlet norm of the linearized collision operator, namely, to derive an optimal coercivity estimate. Recently, the non-cutoff Boltzmann operator in the classical case has been well studied by different research groups, and the key point is to either give an equivalent characterisation of the triple norm in terms of the upper bound and lower bound of the Dirichlet norm, or introduce a new norm additionally taking into account the property of the fractional diffusion of the collision operator. We are in the same situation to carry out all the similar analytical procedures. On the other hand, we also have found out that due to its different feature, the collision frequency of the Boltzmann-type operator around global Maxwellians behaves differently as for either hard or soft potentials in the classical sense, namely, it is continuous and strictly positive for any finite velocity but decays to zero as velocity goes to infinity. In the mean time, we also found out that the collision kernel itself admits a set of singularity as in the classical angular non-cutoff case, but singularities only occur along some curves which tends asymptotically (not exactly) toward the curve where the derivation angle is zero. Such new feature of the collision kernel makes it much more difficult to analyse the coercivity of the linearized operator. In terms of a delicate decomposition of the collision integral, we have succeeded figuring out the singularity of the collision kernel so as to give the coercivity of the linearized operator in a velocity weighted function space. It seems that the velocity weight function is necessary in order to compensate the degeneracy of the collision frequency in the large-velocity domain. Next, we focus on the second and third parts of the main objectives, that is whether or not one can further develop a similar global-in-time existence theory in perturbation framework in the spatially homogeneous or inhomogeneous settings as in the classical case. The problem has been only partially answered in some modelling cases. As mentioned in the project, the new Boltzmann-type collision operator is derived from a much more complicated collision operator (SB) with the screening effect in the Coulomb potential case, namely, there are four kinds of collision operators (SB), (SL), (B) and (L), where (L) is the limiting model of either (B) or (SL) which is also the limiting model of (SB). An important fact is that the collision integrals for all three models (SL), (B) and (L) turn out to be divergent in the Coulomb potential case. However, the collision integral is convergent in the model (SB) which has been used to derive our new model in this project. It is surely an interesting and challenging problem to rigorously justify the involving limiting procedures for different collision models, but such task is quite beyond the scope of this project. What we have tried to understand is concerned with two related collision models, one is the Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system which is often used to describe the motion of plasmas with self-consistent forcing, and the other is the relativistic Boltzmann equation for soft potentials in order to understand the quantum effect in the model (SB) where the collision kernel depends on the velocity distribution function itself. Indeed, we have established the global-in-time existence of solutions for both models in perturbation framework. For the Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system, the main concern is to consider the effect of the self-consistent potential force on the dynamical behavior of solutions, where we have treated the proof in a more general analytical setting with a given time-periodic ions density. Particularly, the same result can be obtained if the Poisson kernel is replaced by the Bessel potential which actually corresponds to a kind of screening effect in plasmas considered in this project. It seems necessary to further understand the relation between the model (SB) and the Vlasov-Poisson-type collision model, in order to capture the dependence of the collision kernel of (SB) on the unknown function. For the relativistic Boltzmann equation with soft potentials, our main concern in this project is to understand the velocity-weighted estimates on the collision operators. The analysis is well-known either in the hard potential case or for the polynomial weight in the soft potential case. We have developed some new hybrid estimates for the nonlinear terms in the relativistic context. We hope that these techniques can be carried out to treat the model with the screening effect considered in this project.

409913.label: Major findings and research outcome
409913.value: 1. We have derived a new Boltzmann-type model, studied the linearized collision operator through the Radon transform, and found out the coercivity estimate on the Dirichlet norm. See Item 1 in Section 8 of Part C. 2. We have studied the spatially inhomogeneous perturbation theory by considering the effect of the Poisson or Maxwell equation on the global dynamical stability instead of directly treating the dependence of the collision kernel on the velocity distribution function with the screening effect. The models under consideration include the Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system and the Vlasov-Maxwell-Boltzmann system for soft potentials, see Item 2 and Item 4 in Section 8 of Part C. 3. We have studied the spatially inhomogeneous perturbation theory by considering the quantum or relativistic effect instead of directly considering the screening effect. The main concern is to treat the soft potential which induces the degeneracy of the linearized collision operator in the large-velocity domain. The global-in-time existence has been established in a velocity-weighted function space, and the main issue is to understand the effect of the exponential velocity weights on the analysis. See Item 5 in Section 8 of Part C. 4. To expect to develop a global well-posedness theory of the classical Boltzmann equation or the Boltzmann-type equation under consideration of this project, we have found out a new analytical framework to treat a class of general initial data. This research topic can be independent of the current one, because it is concerned with a much more general perturbation theory we may devote ourselves to studying in another project. See Item 3 and Item 6 in Section 8 of Part C.

409913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
409913.value: The mathematical study of the model derived in this project is quite few in the literature, so we believe that any kind of research in this direction should be a progress. Particularly, it should be much more interesting to consider the non-dimensional model with two physical parameters taking into account the quantum effect and the grazing effect, and further investigate the even informal limiting procedures between different kinds of models in the Coulomb potential case.

410113.value: 同态加密方案的复杂性理论基础

410113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
410113.value: Homomorphic encryption schemes allow for privacy preserving but meaningful public computation on encrypted data. Schemes that support homomorphic evaluation of simple functionalities like addition or multiplication have been known for more than a decade. More recently, breakthroughs in lattice-based cryptography have led to proposals of cryptographic schemes that support homomorphic evaluation of arbitrary functionalities of bounded depth, and even unrestricted (efficient) functionalities. Unlike ordinary (non-homomorphic) encryption whose security can be argued from generic computational hardness assumptions, the known homomorphic schemes require specific assumptions such as hardness of finding discrete logarithms in cyclic groups or short vectors in lattices. Should these assumptions turn out wrong the schemes would be broken. We propose to study both the security and implementation of homomorphic encryption schemes from a complexity-theoretic perspective. Regarding security, we recently showed that encryption schemes supporting homomorphic evaluation of parity cannot be proved NP-hard to break via general reductions. We give evidence the complexity class that captures the security of such schemes is statistical zero-knowledge and outline an approach for proving such a statement. We also consider the possibility of "non-black-box" proofs of security for homomorphic encryptions in which homomorphic evaluation of the distinguishing algorithm could be used to an advantage. Regarding implementation of homomorphic evaluations, we seek to explain why homomorphic evaluation of general functionalities appears to be an inherently complex process. We give partial evidence for the complexity of homomorphic evaluation in the form of constant-depth functionalities that cannot be homomorphically evaluated in constant depth and propose extensions of this argument to other complexity theoretic settings in which explicit lower bounds are known. We also consider conditional hardness proofs, as well as a possible relation between the complexities of pseudorandom functions and homomorphic encryptions. Finally, we propose a study of the relative complexities of homomorphically evaluating a single functionality, somewhat homomorphic encryption, and fully homomorphic encryption. We believe this study will help develop firm theoretical foundations for homomorphic encryption schemes, which are largely missing. 同态加密方案在保护隐私的同时, 允许公众对加密的数据进行重要的计算。支持同态计算简单功能如加法或乘法的方案已经在十多年前被人们所知晓。最近，基于格的密码学的研究领域的突破导致了一些支持同态计算有限制深度的功能，甚至是无限制深度（高效）的功能，的方案的提出。普通的（非同态）加密方案的安全性可以用一些一般计算难度的假设来论证。与此不同的是， 同态方案需要一些特定的假设，例如在循环群寻找离散对数或在格中找到短向量的难度假设。如果这些假设被证明是错误的，那么这些方案的安全性也将被破坏。 我们建议从复杂性理论的角度来研究同态加密方案的安全性以及实现。在安全性方面，我们最近研究显示，一般规约方式无法证明支持同态计算奇偶函数的加密方案的安全性是NP困难。另外，我们给出这类方案的安全性被统计零知识这一复杂类所概括的证据并概述了一个证明这一说法的方法。 在同态计算的实现方面，我们尝试解释为什么同态计算一般功能似乎是一个复杂的过程。对于同态计算的复杂性，我们给部分证据——常数深度的功能无法在常数深度被同态计算； 并且提出这一论点在其他已知的明确的下界的复杂性理论情况的扩展。我们也考虑有条件的难度证明，以及伪随机函数和同态加密的复杂性之间可能的关系。 最后，我们提出的研究单一功能的同态计算，有些同态加密，完全同态加密之间的相对复杂度。我们相信这项研究将有助于推进坚实目前不足的同态加密方案的理论基础。

410113.label: Realisation of objectives
410113.value: The published works largely address the objectives of this proposal. We showed that the complexity assumptions necessary not only for homomorphic encryption but also for many natural one-way functions fall in the class NP intersect coNP (also resolving an open problem in the area that was the result of incomplete previous work by other authors) [C1]. We gave a concrete complexity model in which homomorphic evaluation is impossible, but there are plausible proposals for public-key encryptions [C3]. The study of the learning with rounding and learning with errors problem concerns concrete tools used in proposed implementations of homomorphic encryption [C2]. Specifically the objectives have been addressed as follows: Specifically the objectives were addressed as follows: Objective 1: The hardness of learning with errors assumption, which serves as the foundation of all existing schemes has been thouroughly investigated [C2]. As part pf his M.Eng. thesis [T] Yik Hin Sham studied the applicability and limitations of known algorithms for this problem. Other works we did unveiled differences between complexity of ordinary and homomorphic encryption [C1, C3]. Objective 2: We now understand that homomorphic encryption schemes can be broken with the help of an NP intersect coNP oracle. On the other hand they can be based on the learning with errors problem which resides in this class (but is not complete for it) [C2]. We know that implementations of homomorphic encryption require higher complexity than ordinary encryption [C3]. Objective 3: We proved that some of these inefficiencies are inherent, and we gave some improvements in reductions in the LWE/LWR setting that are used for this purpose [C2]. We also studied the complexity of basic cryptographic functionalities like secret reconstruction, in part with an eye towards more efficient homomorphic implementations [C4, C5]. Objective 4: Our work uncovers a theoretical gap between ordinary and homomorphic encryption, but we did not find any distinguishing feature between homomorphism that supports a given functionality and full homomorphism. There is still a gap between theory and practice in this setting [C1]. Note: [C1]-[C5] refer to the conference publications in the order in which they are listed. [T] refers to Yik Hin Sham's M.Phil. thesis.

410113.label: Major findings and research outcome
410113.value: Our results clarify the conceptual underpinnings of homomorphic encryption, but also of ordinary secret-key encryption. The conclusions are negative: They indicate that current methods of basing these types of cryptography on NP-hardness are unlikely to succeed [C1]. We give a concrete complexity-theoretic model in which homomorphic encryption is impossible, but some form of public-key encryption exists under plausible assumptions [C3]. We also study the provable security of concrete tools used in the construction of homomorphic encryption (the LWE and LWR assumptions) [C2] as well as the complexity of basic cryptographic primitives that may be of interest for homomorphic evaluation (secret sharing schemes) [C4, C5].

410113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
410113.value: There is still a large gap between the theory and practice of fully homomorphic encryption: While the theoretical foundations are strong, implementations are still quite slow. This project gives some indication as to why this gap may be inherent in theory, but does not quite explain the barriers that arise in concrete implementations. Coming up with new theoretical foundations that address this gap is a challenge for the future.

410113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
410113.value: Homomorphic encryption is a powerful form of cryptography that allows untrusted servers (i.e., "clouds") to carry out tasks without learning any useful information about them. This project studies the theoretical foundations of this powerful proposal and unveils some of its limitations, partly explaining why this technology is yet to become practical.

410213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
410213.value: 由于資源的不足，非急診手術的長期等待已成爲公費醫療體系的一個嚴重問題。如何尋找有效的解決方案，是政策制定者及服務提供者的重要目標。在衆多的政策方案中，公私營醫院合作(PPP)是很多地區考慮及采用的方案之一。盡管PPP，或者更一般的，多醫院合作，確實有可能更有效地利用資源從而減少病人的長期等待，很多與此有關的問題還需解決。比如，如何最優地分配合作群體中的資源? 如何在衆多的約束條件下最優地規劃手術時間? 如何公平合理地在各醫院間分擔費用或分享利潤? 本項目的主要目標，就是開展一個深入的研究，探索上述有關的問題，以尋找合作中的資源最優利用和分配方案。 我們的研究將采用合作博弈和隨機調度的概念和方法，以科學嚴謹地處理多醫院的合作問題。我們將會建立三層模型:（i）多醫院合作體系中的長期資源最優規劃;（ii）考慮病情嚴重程度及緊急手術優先的短期非緊急手術排序；（iii）費用及利益分享，以保證公平及穩定的合作。盡管PPP及多醫院合作是普遍認可的政策方案，我們用合作博弈結合隨機調度的研究，是一個新的方嚮。我們將必須探索攻克許多新的具挑戰性的難題。我們預期這一研究項目將對醫療服務管理的理論和應用做出重要的貢獻。

410213.label: Realisation of objectives
410213.value: First, we develop a surgical capacity sharing model in an integrated hospital system, to facilitate capacity sharing and allocation for elective surgery. In this model, there are multiple hospitals. Each of the hospitals has its own surgical capacity and surgery groups, and faces random demands. The problem is to find the optimal allocation of surgery capacities among multiple hospitals so as to maximize the expected total profit for all the hospitals. We formulate the problem as a stochastic optimization problem and develop an algorithm to find the optimal allocation of surgical capacities. In addition, we develop a model to formulate the mutual referral process in a health care system involving a city hospital and a community hospital, and derive the optimal mutual referral strategy between them. We also develop two contracts (i.e., FFS-CS and P4P-CS) and show that both contracts coordinate effectively, regardless of the scale of the system. Second, we develop a scheduling model for elective surgery operations in an operation theater that also treats emergent patients with priority when they arrive randomly. We consider both short-term and long-term scheduling problems. For the short-term problem, the number of the patients for elective surgeries is fixed, all waiting at time zero for operations, and the objective is to find the optimal policy that minimizes the expected total waiting time for all surgery operations. For the long-term problem, the patients requiring surgeries of different types arrive randomly, and the objective is to find the optimal policy that maximizes the expected total benefit of completing the operations of all patients in waiting. For both problems, we derive the optimal policies based on the theory and techniques of stochastic scheduling and open bandit processes. Third, we develop a cooperative-game model among multiple hospitals to distribute profit and cost for surgery capacity sharing, using the notion of the core of cooperative games. We first assume that the demand is always larger than the supply. In this case, we formulate the problem as a deterministic linear programming (LP) problem. We prove that the core is nonempty and use the duality theory to find an imputation in the core. Then, we consider the general case where the demand is random and can be either larger or smaller than the supply. In this case, we formulate the problem as a stochastic LP problem. We apply the strong duality theory to show the non-emptiness of the core and suggest a way to find an element in the core. In summary, we have provided the models and solutions for all the three objectives we raised in this project. The objectives have been satisfactorily realized.

410213.label: Major findings and research outcome
410213.value: First, we develop a model to formulate the mutual referral process in a health care system involving a city hospital and a community hospital, and derive the optimal mutual referral strategy between them. We consider the subordination situation as a benchmark as well as the subcontracting situation. We develop two contracts (i.e., FFS-CS and P4P-CS) and show that both contracts coordinate effectively, regardless of the scale of the system. We also discuss four extreme cases and find that some of them can coordinate the health care system under certain circumstances, whereas others cannot. Through numerical examples, we discuss the applicability of the coordinating contracts and further find that FFS-CS outperforms P4P-CS in terms of applicability. The research findings have been published in International Journal of Production Research. Please refer to Part C for details. Second, we study the scheduling of elective surgeries in an operation theater that also treats emergent patients with priority when they arrive randomly. We first consider the short-term problem of finding the optimal policy to determine the order of all surgery operations in waiting. Then, we consider the long-term problem of determining the optimal policy to select the elective surgeries to operate. We derive the optimal policies for both problems. The research findings are reported in our working paper “Optimal Schedule of Elective Surgery Operations Subject to Disruptions by Emergencies”. We are revising it and plan to re-submit it to Naval Research Logistics soon. Please refer to Part C for details. Finally, we study two problems of surgery capacity sharing and cooperation in an integrated hospital system. First, we consider the optimal allocation of surgery capacities among multiple hospitals. We formulate the problem as a stochastic optimization problem and develop an algorithm to find the optimal allocation. Second, we study the cooperative games among the hospitals. We first assume that the demand is always larger than the supply, and prove that the core is nonempty and use the duality theory to find an imputation in the core. Then, we consider the general case and apply the strong duality theory to show the non-emptiness of the core and find an element in the core. The research findings were presented in ICSSSM 2016 and form Ms. Min Luo’s PhD thesis. Please refer to Part C for details.

410213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
410213.value: Due to insufficiency of capacities, prolonged waiting for elective surgical procedures has become a problem of great concern in countries that maintain publicly funded health services. In this project, we apply the concepts and methodologies of operations research and cooperative games to rigorously address three important issues in elective surgery planning and scheduling with inter-hospital cooperation. The progress we have made is encouraging but is just a start. We believe that there are many other interesting and important issues on this topic that deserve future research. For example, what is the role of the government in designing incentive schemes (e.g., subsidy) for promoting inter-hospital cooperation? How to utilize the various data the hospitals have, together with the emerging machine learning and analytics techniques, to make better planning and scheduling decisions? What is the benefit (and cost) of data sharing among multiple hospitals? More generally, besides capacity and data, what else the hospitals can (and should) share which can increase the entire social welfare (especially in the era of sharing economy)?

410213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
410213.value: Due to insufficiency of capacities, prolonged waiting for elective surgical procedures has become a problem of great concern in countries that maintain publicly funded health services. Seeking effective solutions to tackle this problem is an important goal for both the policy makers and service providers. Among various policy initiatives, public-private partnership (PPP), or more generally, inter-hospital cooperation, is one that is actively considered and adopted in some regions. In this project, we address three important issues in elective surgery planning and scheduling with inter-hospital cooperation: 1) optimal capacity allocation in an integrated system with multiple hospitals; 2) optimal surgical case sequencing, considering the relative seriousness of each waiting case and the uncertainties due to emergency cases; and 3) profit and cost distribution schemes, to ensure the fairness and therefore the stability of cooperation. To address these issues, we apply the concepts and methodologies of operations research (e.g., linear programming and stochastic scheduling) and cooperative games to develop rigorous mathematical models and provide optimal or tractable solutions. The research output of this project is expected to make significant contributions to the theory and practices of health-care service management.

410713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
410713.value: Terahertz (THz) technology has many unique and important applications. Although there are advancements in recent years, the technology has not been widely deployed. Primarily, this is due to the immaturity of the technology and the associated high cost of the equipment. Here, we propose to investigate the world first’s metamaterial thin film based THz bolometer array, which is low cost and operable at room temperature. Recently, an ultra-broadband visible-to-infrared absorber has been demonstrated, and a broadband, omnidirectional, and polarization insensitive THz absorber has been proposed by one of the co-PIs. By means of magnetic polaritons, this metamaterial absorber is very efficient in absorbing the incoming radiation and converting it into heat. Built upon these breakthroughs, we will now focus on fabricating an absorber at the THz range. Utilizing this new ultra-broadband THz absorber, we will design and examine the performance of a new THz bolometer and its companion bolometer array – MOTH bolometer array. The proposed MOTH bolometer comprises a THz metamaterial absorber integrated onto an isolated layer of heat-sensing element (HSE). Because of the heat generated by the absorber, the resistance of the HSE will be altered. In order to prevent the generated heat from escaping into the surrounding materials and to enhance the sensitivity of the MOTH bolometer, we will make use of a silicon anisotropic etch to isolate the individual MOTH bolometer from the silicon substrate. For the HSE, we will explore three types of materials: pure metal, polysilicon and crystalline silicon. Since the metamaterial consists of either gold or silver, it is a simple process to add an extra layer for the metallic HSE, which offers a very wide dynamic range of detection. Both polysilicon and crystalline silicon provide better sensitivity owing to the exponential temperature dependency of the electron concentration in the conduction band; however, the dynamic range may be limited. During the readout of the bolometer array, unexposed dark MOTH bolometers will be used to compensate for the self-heating effect generated by the biasing current in each MOTH bolometer. Low noise circuit design techniques will be employed to design the readout integrated circuit for the MOTH bolometer array. With this MOTH bolometer array, we will be in a unique position to realize a room temperature THz imaging system, which has many applications, for example in security screening at the port of entry, and in medical imaging for the detection of early stage skin cancer. 太赫茲科技是被認為有潛在的廣泛應用價值。但是因為太赫茲源及探測器均非常昂貴，且體積龐大，應用上並不方便。近來有報導通過用超材料製成的寬帶紅外線吸收體可以接近完全的吸收紅外線並把其能量轉為熱能。基於相同原理，本課題擬利用超材料製成太赫茲吸收體並將其產生的熱能用温度提升來量化，以作為一個太赫茲探測器。此技術優點是可以在硅材料上製造超材料，並可同時結合硅材料上的温度探測電路。因此造出來的太赫茲探測器可以體積小、適合於製造成像元件，並可用於安全檢查或醫學成像等用途。

410713.label: Realisation of objectives
410713.value: A prototype thin-film THz absorber has been designed, simulated and fabricated. Simulation results show that it would have the absorbing capability at the THz frequencies targeted. We measured the time-domain spectroscopy of absorber response. There were absorption peaks at 0.06THz, 1.08THz, and 1.16THz in all the chips that were taken from the same wafer. SEM pictures of the device array and the single device have been taken. The original plan was to dissect the devices and measure the thicknesses of each individual layer under the SEM in order to get their accurate physical dimensions because the simulation of the device performance will need accurate physical size measurements. However, when the postdoctoral fellow, Dr. Zhang Zhongxiang, was preparing to execute this part of the experiments, he was invited by a start-up company in Shenzhen to start a business on optical equipment. He could not resist the offer and resigned from the project to undertake the business. Hence this part of the development was suspended. However, the most difficult part of the complicated device fabrication has already been successfully finished. Hence it is considered that 90% of this item has been completed. The knowledge that we obtained in developing the broadband THz absorber has triggered us to develop a solution to the important problem of antenna decoupling in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technology for communications systems at lower frequencies. We introduced an LC low-pass π network perform the antenna decoupling. Comparing with existing decoupling techniques, the proposed method provides a wideband but compact solution. Furthermore, a generalized one-fit-all scheme is justified to implement the decoupling network with an antenna independent core network. By adjusting a few external components, the same core network can be applied to different antenna pairs with different coupling levels and antenna form factors. We have implemented four design examples to demonstrate the proposed decoupling network. In all cases, the decoupling network significantly improves the isolation between two antennas over a wide frequency band while maintaining the intrinsic matching bandwidth of the antennas. We have identified to use vanadium oxide, VOx, as the heat sensing element and used sputter deposition to integrate it with the THz absorber structure. Its heat sensing characteristics were about to be measured by a series of controlled heating experiments by electrically heating it and measuring its temperature response. However, for the same reason of the postdoctoral fellow’s leaving the project, this part of analysis has been suspended as well. After his resignation, there were not enough time and funding left to train up a qualified research assistant for this specialized and sophisticated job. The unspent amount was returned to RGC. But the fabrication of the heat sensing element and integration of it with the absorber structure have been completed. Hence we consider 60% of the work associated with this part of the project has been completed. In studying the heat sensing element, we discovered a new smart temperature sensing technique in CMOS integrated circuits. The sensor is based on a resistor for temperature sensing and a time-to-digital converter for producing digital outputs. An on-chip RC-based simple oscillator is used as the clock source of the sensor. The period of the proposed oscillator tracks the time output of the sensing circuit so that its variation due to RC spread does not affect the temperature sensor’s final digital output. The sensor has the distinct advantage that from sensing temperature to generating digital output codes all the functions are integrated on-chip without needing any off-chip references, particularly a precise clock signal. With a two-point calibration, the sensor achieves a small error that is within −1.9/+1.21 degrees Celsius over a temperature range from 0 degree Celsius to 100 degrees Celsius. The third objective stated in the original proposal, namely, designing and characterizing a low noise readout integrated circuit for use with the MOTH bolometer, which was dropped after the project was approved, has been added back to the project after the change of the PI. This objective has been fully realized. We have designed, simulated, fabricated and characterized an integrated low-noise low-power analog-to-digital converter (ADC) that can be used for the readout of the MOTH bolometer. The readout ADC is a type of transconductor-capacitor (Gm-C) modulator based ADC. We have discovered a new architecture and a new circuit for the readout ADC. The prototype ADC is fabricated in a 0.18-um CMOS process. It has been fully characterized. Measurement results show that it achieves a 75 dB signal-to-noise ratio and 79.8 dB dynamic range over a 100-kHz bandwidth. Operating from a 1.8-V supply, it consumes only 222.5 uW. The prototype readout ADC has demonstrated the principle of the new Gm-C Delta-Sigma architecture. It has also demonstrated in experiments that the proposed merged input-feedback Gm circuit consumes very low power while achieving a low noise and a high linearity. The prototype shows that the proposed architecture and circuit are clearly a direction towards better power efficiency, lower noise and higher linearity for Gm-C modulator based readout ADCs. While the achieved performance meets the demand for our MOTH bolometer, the readout ADC can also be applied in a wide range of other systems that require readout electronics.

410713.label: Major findings and research outcome
410713.value: We have successfully designed, simulated, and fabricated a thin film THz absorber integrated with a heat sensing element which was deposited by sputtering VOx on the absorber structure. All of the processes have been actually completed. The project has triggered the successful development of an effective and practical method to solve the difficult problem of interferences between antennas in MIMO technology for communications applications. The method is an antenna decoupling network that employs an LC low-pass π network. It has two distinct advantages, namely, a wide decoupling bandwidth and compactness for the resulted device. A rigorous mathematical proof is provided. The findings are published in outcome item 8.1. The project has discovered a new low-noise read-out ADC architecture that achieves the best power efficiency of its kind. A new circuit and new architecture have been proposed. A prototype has been designed, simulated, fabricated and characterized. Experimental results have proven the distinctive low-noise and low-power advantages of the proposed read-out ADC. The findings are published in outcome item 8.2. This project also proposed a fully-integrated and self-contained smart temperature sensor, the first of its kind in the world. It not only is a solution for low-cost temperature sensing applications but also demonstrates in a fundamental way that a temperature sensor can operate without any external references at all. The results are published in outcome item 8.3. The project has also nurtured two Ph.D. students to graduate. They are Dr. LI Daxiang and Dr. LIU Jingjing, whose works are related to the design of readout electronics and the thin-film fabrication process respectively.

410713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
410713.value: The developed low-noise readout electronics finds applications in other areas such as wireless communications and particle detectors in accelerator experiments. Based on our developed technologies in this field, we will explore opportunities to collaborate with the Physics department in CUHK, which is a member of the Large Hadron Collider experiments in European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN), to develop radiation-tolerant, low-noise and low-power electronic readout integrated circuits for the future upgrade of the ATLAS (A Toroidal LHC ApparatuS) detector in CERN.

410713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
410713.value: This project has investigated on the materials, fabrication and readout electronics for a broadband THz absorber and its companion bolometer array. A thin-film THz absorber has been fabricated and experimentally demonstrated to be able to absorb radiation energies at THz frequencies. A suitable material, namely, vanadium oxide has been found for use as the heat sensing materials for integration with the THz absorber at room temperature. The project has also led to three discoveries that are closely related to the theme of the project. The first one is a new circuit architecture for the readout electronics which produces digital outputs. The new circuit architecture achieves a very low noise level whiling having the highest power efficiency of its kind. The second discovery is a compact antenna decoupling technique to improve the performance of multiple-input multiple-output antennas used in communications systems. The third discovery is a world’s first all-integrated CMOS temperature sensor that does not require any external references. In summary, this project lays a foundation for realizing room-temperature THz imaging systems for applications ranging from security screening at the port of entry to medical imaging.

411113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
411113.value: Financial institutions knit a complex network. They interconnect with each other directly through active borrowing-and-lending activities and holding significant amount of marketable securities against each other. In normal times, this network helps the institutions diversify their idiosyncratic risks to achieve an efficient allocation of economic resources. However, under crisis conditions, this network can be easily turned into a conduit that propagates failures at one or several institutions to the entire system. Further complicating the matter is a second layer of interconnectedness of the institutions, indirectly via the market. The asset fire sale by a distressed firm will create a significant negative externality for the rest of the system. As the recent financial crisis reveals, these two, direct and indirect but mutually enhancing, channels play an important role in the development of systemic risk. This subject is also highly relevant to the banking regulation policies and practices in Hong Kong and the Great China region, as many structural problems have been accumulated and concealed in the unprecedented growth of the region over the last two decades but will certainly surface as important sources of systemic risk. The proposed research aims to develop a network-based approach to modeling and analyzing systemic risk, in particular studying how defaults spread through the entire financial system. Our approach will enable explicit modeling of the level of interconnectedness via a closely matched network configuration. It will characterize analytically how the topological structure of a financial network and the market liquidation of assets interact with each other; and, via optimization algorithms, specify the nonlinear dynamics by which a crisis forms and cascades. Results from our proposed study will contribute fundamental understandings and insights into financial systemic risks, along with practical tools to support the design of banking stress tests and to help regulators monitor closely those critical institutions in the network and setup ``fire walls'' to prevent cascading failures. 金融機構形成一個複雜的網絡體系。 它們通過兩條主要的渠道相互關聯。 其一是直接的借貸和相互持有對方的資產。 在平常時, 這個網絡幫助金融機構分散個體風險以達到經濟資源的有效配置。可是在爆發危機時, 這個網絡會演變成將一家或數家機構的破產風險傳導到全行業的通道。使得問題變得更爲複雜的是這些機構通過市場的不直接的關聯。 一家瀕臨倒閉的公司甩賣資產可能會給全網絡的其他公司造成負面的外部效應。 正如近年發生的金融危機所揭示的那樣，這兩條渠道相互促進，在系統性風險的形成中扮演的重要角色。這個課題對於香港以及大中華地區的金融監管的政策和實踐也高度相關。近二十年的高速發展所積累和掩蓋的結構性問題，隨著中國經濟的增速放緩，會日益突出並成爲系統性風險的重要來源。 本研究著眼於發展一套基於網絡模型的方法來模擬和研究系統性風險，特別是研究個體的破產風險如何演變成全金融體系的危機。我們的方法是通過網絡構造對金融體系的關聯性建立模型。它能夠定量的刻畫出金融網絡的拓撲結構如何與資產清算相互作用，並且通過優化算法的方法，詳細闡明金融危機形成和傳播的非綫性機制。我們的研究將有助於對金融系統性風險的基礎研究。與研究伴隨產生出的實務工具將支持銀行體系壓力測試的設計，並幫助監管機構監測網絡中的重要機構和設立防火墻阻止風險傳播。

411113.label: Realisation of objectives
411113.value: 1. The principal formulates the interconnectedness in a financial network, more explicitly, the interbank liability network and the market liquidity, through an optimization problem with equilibrium constraints. This new formulation, in conjunction with some existing network recovery methods, can be used to estimate the true banking network configuration. Objective 1 in the original application are successfully achieved. 2. Aiming to solve the above optimization problem, the principal develops a partition algorithm to characterize analytically how the topological structure of a financial liability network and the market liquidation of assets interact with each other to form a massive contagion of defaults. By performing sensitivity analysis on the outcome of the optimization problem, the principal identifies two key contributors to financial systemic risk, the network multiplier and the liquidity amplifier, and to discern the qualitative difference between the two, confirming that the market liquidity effect has a great potential to cause system wide contagion. Objective 2 in the original application has been successfully addressed. 3. In addition, the research synthesizes the above two factors into a Katz centrality-like metric to measure the system’s resilience against external shocks. The metric is computed from the banks’ net worth that are marked to the market, enabling an explicit estimation of the contagion probability of a specific group of banks. In this way, the investigation produces a measure of systemic risk. Objective 3 in the original application has been successfully achieved.

411113.label: Major findings and research outcome
411113.value: There is one major research outcome related to this project. The principal published one paper (Research output 1 in Part C) in the journal of Operations Research, the flagship journal in the area of operations research, based on the findings summarized in the research objectives. In that paper, we formulate a constrained optimization problem that incorporates both channels of risk, and exploit the problem structure to generate the solution (to the clearing payment vector) via a partition algorithm. Through sensitivity analysis, we are able to identify two key contributors to financial systemic risk, the network multiplier and the liquidity amplifier, and to discern the qualitative difference between the two, confirming that the market liquidity effect has a great potential to cause systemwide contagion. In addition, part of the fund was used to support two related researches (Research outcomes 2 and 3 in Part C). The first one is to propose an importance-sampling based Monte Carlo method to obtain unbiased estimators to evaluate expectations involving random variables whose probability density functions are unknown while their Fourier transforms have explicit forms. It provides an efficient approach to evaluating financial derivatives. The second one studies the design of contingent convertible bonds, a form of debt that converts to equity as a bank approaches financial distress, and their incentive effects in mitigating systemic risk.

411113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
411113.value: The principal will continue the investigation stemmed out from this research project to investigate the dynamic of systemic risk. A particular near-term objective is to construct a general equilibrium model to enhance the understanding of how the financial network evolves over time and to develop analysis tools in assessing the effectiveness of various regulatory policies.

411113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
411113.value: This funded research develops a network-based approach to modeling and analyzing financial systemic risk, in particular studying how defaults spread through the entire financial system through the interbank liability exposures and the market liquidity. The methodology derived from the investigation leads to analytical metrics of interconnectedness to characterize how the topological structure of a financial network and the market liquidation of assets interact with each other to form the nonlinear dynamics of a crisis. Results from this study contribute fundamental understandings and insights into financial systemic risks, along with practical tools to support the design of banking stress tests and to help regulators monitor closely those critical institutions in the network and setup “fire walls” to prevent cascading failures.

412313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
412313.value: In recent years, we have seen a dramatic increase in the number, the size, and the variety of social networks (e.g., Twitter, Facebook, Friendster, MySpace, Cyworld, etc.). Social networks are affecting more and more of the daily life of the modern world. There are also many other networks, such as mobile and communication networks, collaboration and citation networks, transportation networks, financial and marketing networks, WWW and Internet, chemistry and bio-informatics networks, neural networks, etc., which are all closely related to our life. Effective analysis of these networks is beneficial to both individuals and the society. Some possible applications of such analysis include viral marketing, fraud detection, network traffic planning, spam detection, financial portfolio selection and biochemical studies. For example, it has been found that the histograms of triangle numbers of web hosts can be used to detect web spam; another application of triangle counting is an indicator of the role of a user in a community [7]. Cliques are important in social network analysis [30]. Cliques in the market graph represent stocks of similar financial instruments[8]. Distance querying can tell us the closeness of two individuals in a social network, cheapest travel plan, and web page similarity in a web graph. The proposed research focuses on large-scale network analysis (we are interested in networks, represented as graphs, consisting of billions of vertices and edges). We will study a number of fundamental problems in network analysis at different conceptual levels. The solutions to these fundamental problems are crucial for effective network analysis, and they are also building blocks of advanced techniques for network analysis. Therefore, efficient solutions to these problems are vital for analysis of massive networks. Hong Kong is a major city in China that embraces the newest technologies and this gives an extra edge to its business and finance systems. In both business and non-business sectors, there exist a lot of social networking datasets and other network datasets for useful analysis. We believe that our project will have a strong impact on the advancement of the above mentioned technologies, and make contributions to the success of reaping the most benefits from such technologies, towards the interests of Hong Kong. 近年來, 各種社交網絡（如 Twitter，Facebook ， Friendster的， MySpace等）的數量, 大小，在急劇增加。社交網絡正在影響著越來越多的現代世界的日常生活。也有許多其他的網絡，如手機和通信網絡，協作和引文網絡，交通網絡，金融和營銷網絡， WWW和互聯網，化學和生物信息網絡，神經網絡等，這些都是和我們的生活密切相關。這些網絡的有效分析對個人與社會是有益的。這種分析的一些可能的應用包括營銷，欺詐檢測，網絡流量規劃，垃圾郵件檢測，金融投資組合的選擇和生化研究。 例如，已經發現，可以用來檢測網頁垃圾郵件的網絡主機的三角號的直方圖;三角計數的另一種應用是在一個社區的用戶的作用的一個指標。派系是重要的社會網絡分析 。派系代表股票在市場上圖類似金融工具 。距離查詢可以告訴們在社交網絡中，最便宜的旅遊計劃去從一個位置到另一個網頁在Web圖形相似的兩個人的親密程度。從一個節點到另一個可達識別語義網中的對象之間的關係是非常有用的，在蛋白質相互作用網絡，並在基因調控研究中的監管網絡。 我們所提出的研究主要集中在大型網絡的分析, 我們感興趣的, 是由十億頂點和邊表示為圖形的網絡。我們將研究在不同的概念層次網絡分析中的一些基本問題。這些根本問題的解決方案，對有效的網絡分析是至關重要的。因此，對這些問題的有效的解決方案對大規模網絡的分析至關重要。 香港是中國的主要城市，最新的技術對其業務和財務系統是一個額外的優勢。在業務和非業務部門，存在著大量的社會網絡數據集和其他有用的分析網絡數據集。我們的項目將提供各種大型的社交網絡數據集的分析, 對香港在互聯網上的用戶以及移動用戶提供優質的應用程序/服務。我們相信，我們的項目將對上述技術的進步有一個強烈的衝擊，使從這些技術中收穫的成功，對香港的利益作出貢獻。

412313.label: Realisation of objectives
412313.value: In our proposal, we highlight 3 conceptual levels in the analysis of massive networks. The three levels are from simple to complex components. The first level is called the vertex level, and it is about the basic graph components of the vertices and edges. The second level is about simple graph structures such as triangles and cliques which are made up of only a few vertices and edges each. The third level is about more complex and bigger graph components such as clusters, which may consist of a substantial number of vertices and edges. We have made progress in the study of efficient algorithms for the computation of important problems in each individual level. We summarize the findings in the following. (1) At the vertex level, we have completed the following studies: A most basic problem related to individual vertices would be the distance computation. Algorithms known for smaller graphs are not adequate for large networks. Our study about this leads to a hop doubling technique for effective indexing that can handle large scale-free networks. This work is published in the following: -- Hop doubling label indexing for point-to-point distance querying on scale-free networks (VLDB 2014) Next we enrich the nearest neighbor search in large networks with keywords and improved on previous result by returning exact solutions instead of approximate solutions, while remaining scalable to large networks. The result is reported in the following publication. -- Exact top-k nearest keyword search in large networks (SIGMOD 2015) Another important problem involving the linkage of vertices in a cost-effective way is the well studied minimum spanning trees. To this end, we consider the more complex but realistic situation where the graph contains temporal information about the start and end time of each edge. We propose an efficient algorithm for this problem in the following work. -- Minimum spanning trees in temporal graphs (SIGMOD 2015) An important type of large scale network is online social networks. The difficulty involved is that the vertices or edges of such social networks are often accessible only via expensive API calls. To avoid searching the entire network, random walk technique is employed in the basic operation of estimating the number of edges with a target label, and this study resulted in the following work: -- Counting edges with target labels in online social networks via random walk (ApWeb 2017) In many applications, the similarity between two vertices is needed, and one well studied metric is called simrank. The computation of simrank is costly and typically approximate results are extracted by random walk. We consider a solution by a new indexing method and show that we can handle dynamic data in the following work: -- READS: a random walk approach for efficient and accurate dynamic simrank (VLDB 2017) (2) At the pattern level, the study considers small components of the given massive network, such as triangles, network motifs, cliques etc, we have made the following studies: -- Distributed maximal clique computation (2014) -- Rectangle counting in large bipartite graphs (2014) -- Counting edges and triangles in online social networks via random walk (2017) (3) At the component level, we have results of the following studies: Information dissemination is about how information spread in a social network. It is noted that information spreads readily within communities and in the following work we introduce a mechanism of identifying communities and applying the community structures in estimating the spread of information. -- Community based information dissemination (2015) Another important component based problem about massive networks is the problem of subgraph querying. Although this is a well studied problem, a known problem is that there are typically too many matchings in the result set, and previously known solutions return many results and still not all results are considered and there are a lot of overlapping in the resulting subgraphs, making it not very helpful to the users. Our study shows that we can instead return top-k diversified subgraphs in the result. A new algorithm is proposed to this end which is shown to be highly effective and we have a theoretical guarantee on the result quality. The study is reported in the following publication. -- Diversified Top-k subgraph querying in a large graph (SIGMOD 2016) In the above study, the following works consider parallel and distributed computation: -- Distributed maximal clique computation (2014) -- k-balanced sorting and skew join in MPI and MapReduce (2014) -- Distributed maximal clique computation and management (2016) Although we have produced a lot of results in the above studies, we have not been able to make a balanced study of the three levels. We a more biased towards the first two levels and less work is accomplished at the third level. The reason being that even at the first basic level, many important issues and problems need to be examined. While at the highest level, it is found that the study about communities in a network faces a major obstacle about the ground truth. It is quite impossible to verify if any result we obtain is truly a community and also the information dissemination problem is plagued with artificial models of influence that are not verifiable and are inconsistent. Another area where we have limited work is the use of massively parallel systems since there is hardly adequate hardware for support. We would leave this item to future work when we can secure sufficient funding for the required hardware.

412313.value: ** At the vertex and edge level, we consider the problems of shortest path or distance querying, the top-k nearest keyword search problem, minimum spanning tree problem, and the simrank computation on massive networks, and the estimation of labeled edge counts in online social networks. The studies are reported in the following: -- Hop doubling label indexing for point-to-point distance querying on scale-free networks (VLDB 2014) -- Exact top-k nearest keyword search in large networks (SIGMOD 2015) -- Minimum spanning trees in temporal graphs (SIGMOD 2015) -- READS: a random walk approach for efficient and accurate dynamic simrank (VLDB 2017) -- Counting edges with target labels in online social networks via random walk (ApWeb 2017) ** At the pattern level, we consider the maximal clique problem, rectangle counting in bipartite graphs, and triangle counting in online social networks. 412313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
412313.value: For future work, there can be more study to link up the three levels. Also the use of parallel and distributed computing for massive speed-up can be investigated. With social networks, the issue of privacy is of significant concern, and it may be necessary to incorporate privacy preserving mechanisms in all of the studies problems.

412313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
412313.value: As massive networks are gaining much influence on many sectors of business, and public interests, the analysis of such networks is found highly useful. They are helpful for network maintenance, marketing, information searching, etc. In this project, we tackled many fundamental problems in the analysis of massive networks, including shortest path, nearest neighbor search, estimation of statistical measurements of the network, counting basic components in the network, clique computation, to community mining and subgraph querying. The results in the project can help to facilitate the above mentioned applications, in terms of efficiency and result quality.

412413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
412413.value: The aim of this proposal is to investigate the chemical and toxicological characterization of personal exposure of PM2.5 in Hong Kong and to explore the strength of the associations between personal PM2.5 exposures with indoor and outdoor concentrations. Since we typically spend most of our time (80-90%) in indoor microenvironments, focus on fixed ambient monitoring measurements to assess personal exposure risks is of limited value. As the health effects of urban air pollutants may not be caused solely by their concentrations at fixed outdoor air monitoring sites alone and personal exposures is determined by the subjects' exposure to both indoor and outdoor environments. Thus, characterization of indoor, outdoor and personal exposure levels to PM2.5 (and their chemical compositions) are critical for conducting accurate exposure assessment. In addition adverse health effects of PM2.5 may be derived from oxidative stress initiated by the formation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) at the target cells, making PM-associated ROS generation the focus of much attention in ongoing efforts to understand the mechanisms of such effects. Therefore, reliable scientific data on the levels of personal exposures of PM2.5 and the bioreactivity of different PM2.5 samples in association with their chemical characteristics (elemental carbon [EC], heavy metals, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons [PAHs] and phthalates) are essential in the efforts to evaluate the potential effects on human health. Moreover, the developments of personal exposure models for PM2.5 are critical for long-term risk assessments and at the same time offer effective means of estimating personal exposures (PE) to PM2.5 without the logistical difficulties of personal sampling. Currently, only limited local personal PM2.5 exposure data is available in Hong Kong and this research will be able to contribute to the better understanding how indoor/outdoor environments affect personal exposure. It will also provide data to support an epidemiological study investigating potential health effects of PM2.5 pollution in Hong Kong. 本項目旨在調查香港個體暴露PM2.5的化學和毒理學特徵，探究PM2.5人體暴露與室內外污染物濃度的關聯性。一般情況，我們80-90 %的時間是在室內度過，因此利用室外大氣環境監測結果評估個體暴露風險的做法顯然效果很有限。暴露於城市大氣污染而引發的健康問題並非單一的由室外固定採樣點捕獲的大氣污染物導致，而是來源於室內外多種環境暴露的共同作用。因此，室內外及人體暴露PM2.5的特徵及其化學組成對準確進行暴露評估十分必要。另外，PM2.5的負面健康效應可能來自靶細胞中活性氧分子（ROS）形成過程而產生的氧化應激，讓研究與ROS產生相關的顆粒物成為人們不斷努力理解與備受矚目的焦點。因此，關於PM2.5人體暴露水平的可靠科學數據及PM2.5中不同化學成分（如元素碳EC，重金屬，多環芳烴PAHs及鄰苯二甲酸酯等）的生物活性對於評估PM潛在的健康影響非常重要。另一方面，PM2.5人體暴露模型的發展對於長期風險評估而言至關重要，同時這也針對人體暴露採樣困難的問題，提供了行之有效的估算PM2.5人體暴露的一種手段。截至目前，香港PM2.5人體暴露的數據資料非常有限，本研究將為室內外大氣污染對人體暴露影響的理解做出貢獻，為針對香港PM2.5污染的潛在健康效應而開展的流行病學研究提供數據支持。

412413.label: Realisation of objectives
412413.value: The objectives of this study were realized by analyzing the personal exposures, outdoor and residential indoor levels of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and corresponding hazardous components (elemental carbon (EC), polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and phthalates) from adult subjects in Hong Kong. In addition, a seasonal program of in transit microenvironments measurement was also conducted for further analysis. Identical sampling equipment, operating procedures, and questionnaires were used throughout the study period. Information about subjects spent in indoors, outdoors and performed activities were collected by using time-activity diaries. Standard operating procedures were applied for all subjects and field procedures. A comprehensive quality assurance (QA)/quality control (QC) protocol was established to ensure comparability between collected data. The above mentioned PM2.5 samples were further determined by different toxicity assays. Cell viability test was applied to assess the cell viability after exposure. Lactic dehydrogenase (LDH) (Abcam, Cambridge, MA, USA), 8-isoprostane (Cayman, MI, USA), and interleukin 6 (IL-6) (BD Biosciences, USA) were used to determine the levels of cytotoxicity, oxidative stress, and inflammation in cell supernatants after exposure, respectively. Correlation analysis was performed to identify the correlation between (1) cytotoxicity, oxidative stress and inflammation and (2) chemical species. The targets were completed successfully. Direct measurement of PM2.5 via personal monitoring is the most accurate exposure assessment method currently available. However, to evaluate the exposures at population level is often burdensome, time consuming and expensive. Therefore, indirect measurements via a combination of personal activity diaries and different indoor/outdoor microenvironment concentrations can be a useful alternative. Personal exposure concentration is a function of concentrations within various microenvironments in addition to the time spent in these microenvironments. The modeled PM2.5 personal exposure results were evaluated and further adjusted with the measured concentrations. All of the targets have been accomplished on schedule. The outcomes were published in peer-reviewed journals. More results will be anticipated and expected for further articles submissions in due course.

412413.label: Major findings and research outcome
412413.value: Higher PM2.5 levels were observed in Hong Kong compared to other studies in the United States and Europe. For the majority of subjects, personal PM2.5, organic carbon (OC), EC, PAHs, and phthalate exposures demonstrated significant seasonal variation (p < 0.001) with higher exposure levels in winter but lower levels in summer. During the study period, relatively higher personal and indoor PM2.5 levels were identified compared to outdoors. Evidences confirm that indoor PM2.5 is a main determinant factor for the total personal PM2.5 exposure. The overall results suggest that outdoor PM2.5 (including OC, PAHs, Phthalate components) from fixed sampling locations may not be suitable proxies for personal exposures in human health studies. Further evidences showed that personal exposure to OC significantly correlated with LDH and IL-6; indoor OC was associated with 8-isoprostane. The result suggests that cell viability reduction and increases in LDH, IL-6, and 8-isoprostane levels could occur due to OC, PAHs, and phthalate exposure in PM2.5 after combination of all sample types. The research outcome can be summarized as below. 1) Personal monitoring for PM2.5 was conducted for healthy adults living and working in different areas of Hong Kong between July 2014 and March 2015. Higher heavy metals exposure levels were observed in winter than summer. There was no significant seasonal variation of EC in personal PM2.5. Additional factors that could influence personal exposure to PM2.5 mass and their components (e.g., EC and elements) were duration at home under indoor environment, in transit and indoor cleaning activities (Chen et al., 2018). 2) Concurrent outdoor and personal PM2.5 monitoring was conducted between July 2014 and March 2015. Outdoor PM2.5 mass concentrations were retrieved from the Hong Kong Environmental Protection Department (HKEPD) Air Quality Monitoring Network. Results suggest that season (p = 0.02) and occupation (p < 0.001) were significant factors that could influence the relationships between outdoor PM2.5 concentrations and personal exposure to PM2.5 mass concentrations. Outdoor PM2.5 mass was a dominant indicator (R2 = 0.39, p < 0.01) and the most significant contributor (~77.5%) to personal PM2.5 exposure (Chen et al., 2018). 3) Indoor air pollutants such as PM2.5 in 55 households for elderly residents in Hong Kong were characterized during summer and winter in 2016-2017. Higher concentrations were observed for indoor PM2.5 in winter than summer. The determinant factors for indoor PM2.5 concentrations were from incense burning and cooking. (Tong et al., 2018).

412413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
412413.value: Our results suggest that bioreactivity of PM2.5 vary by particles composition and sample types. Limitation of our study includes lack of exposure data on elemental species and water-soluble secondary organic aerosols. External validity of these findings is limited to healthy adults in Hong Kong only. A substantial number of repeated personal monitoring is recommended to elucidate the time sequence of pollution effects on human health endpoints.

412413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
412413.value: Relatively higher personal PM2.5 levels were found in Hong Kong compared to other personal exposures studies in the United States and Europe. Significant seasonal differences (p < 0.01) were shown in personal exposures with higher levels in winter but lower in summer. Moderate to strong correlations were shown between personal and outdoor PM2.5 concentrations. Season and occupation are the factors determining the strength of personal-ambient associations. Relatively higher personal and indoor PM2.5 levels than outdoors were found during the study period. Indoor PM2.5 concentration is a main determinant for total personal PM2.5 exposure. Outdoor PM2.5 (including OC, PAHs and Phthalate components) concentrations from fixed sampling locations may not be satisfactory proxies for personal exposures in human health studies. OC concentrations in personal exposures and indoors samples correlated with bioreactivity indicators (LDH, IL-6 and 8-isoprostane). Cell viability reduction and increases of LDH, IL-6, and 8-isoprostane levels were observed due to exposure to OC, PAHs, and phthalate components.

412513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
412513.value: The aim of this project is to build a virtual operative anatomy system facilitating surgeons in learning 3-D anatomy in the thoracic cavity, and to develop a virtual environment for the training of pulmonary thoracoscopic skills. Training of video assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) has been more prevalent in all structured training programs globally in the field of cardiothoracic surgery. Thoracoscopic surgery is a complex procedure, which is highly restricted in the views of operative field; it is essential to train the surgeon to learn how to observe and distinguish normal and pathological anatomies. Minimally invasive interventions in thorax are considerably different from that in abdomen due to the presence of the thoracic bony cage (formed by sternum and ribs) which only provides a narrow intercostal space for procedures. It is essential for a thoracic-surgeon to possess a firm knowledge of thoracoscopic anatomy and possess high degree of surgical skills before one operates on a patient. Current training on human cadaver or pig models only provides learning of the normal or animal anatomy and there is a call for more lifelike training with pathological conditions. This research will be using virtual reality (VR) with reference to a database of ultra-high resolution virtual human thoracic cavity datasets for the learner to interactively localize and dissect in the virtual space; three-dimensional (3-D) images with preoperative information on the vascular system, esophagus, trachea, lungs, lymph nodes, skin, and bones will be provided and coupled with real-time dexterous touch feedback. Surgical site can be extremely complicated as it might be close to the surface of the beating heart, major big artery or vein, which involves large soft-tissue deformation (self-changing or during poking/grasping) as well as bleeding (when cut). Research challenges in this project include photorealistic visualization, time-critical force rendering, and interactive biomechanical models for soft tissue and blood interaction as well as intelligent skill assessment. To summarize, this is a joint project between a pioneer VR development team and a leading thoracoscopic surgery team in Hong Kong. We aim to construct a training system with a simulated pulmonary thoracoscopy, in real-time to the virtual patient’s thoracic cavity on a simulated endoscopic navigation practicing dissect skill on a life-like mannequin with pathologies. The proposed system is anticipated to strengthen and compensate existing thoracic-surgical education and training as well as to become a training standard for existing and future surgeons.
