412513.label: Realisation of objectives
412513.value: In this project, we have built a virtual operative anatomy system facilitating surgeons in learning 3-D anatomy in the thoracic cavity, and developed a virtual environment for the training of pulmonary thoracoscopic skills. Key research and development issues addressed in this project include multimodal medical image (e.g., MRI, CVH data, etc) segmentation and visualization on the desired areas, 3D anatomical model reconstruction and optimization from the segmented volume data, automatic anatomical structure labeling for medical images, interactive interface to display anatomical images from arbitrary positions and angles. In our developed prototype, the High Definition Television (HDTV) surgical images as well as the ultra-rich CVH color textural volume is presented to user, while providing a VR based thoracoscopic-related surgical environment. We have designed a series of deep neural networks (3D FractalNet, densely connected ConvNets, deep contour-aware network, deep cascaded networks, 3D convolutional network, hybrid loss guided convolutional network， 3D deeply supervised network) to automatically segment and detect various desired areas and organs. In addition, we have proposed a novel algorithm called projection-embedded BYY algorithm (pBYY) to make the learning process of Gaussian mixture model (GMM) more stable, which has achieved good results on color image (e.g., color CVH cryosectional images) segmentation. We have developed an efficient method to estimate the noise level from a single image, and proposed a two-stage method to remove its contained noise. We have proposed a new medical image smoothing method based on non-local patch grouping and filtering. The proposed method can better preserve prominent structures and visualize fine images. We have proposed to reduce speckle noise in ultrasound images using feature asymmetry anisotropic diffusion (FAAD). The proposed approach is an adaptive diffusion process that can preserve the image features while suppressing the noise by incorporating a local phase-based edge detector, called feature asymmetry (FA), into the forward-and-backward diffusion. We have employed vortex filaments in grids scheme to efficiently simulate intensive and finely detailed virtual environment. We have proposed an efficient segmentation-based framework for the automatic generation of transfer functions for better visualization. We firstly over-segment the intensity-gradient histogram of the input volumetric data into a set of patches according to their intensity and gradient magnitude. We then cluster these patches according to the spatial information of the voxels by leveraging a hierarchical clustering method. Finally, the resultant image is automatically generated based on the hierarchical clusters by employing appropriate opacity and color transfer functions. The proposed method takes both intensity-gradient values and spatial information into account and hence can achieve promising visualization results. We have proposed an effective framework to extract the anatomical model from the segmented medical volume data (e.g. CT, MRI, CVH). We take advantage of the piecewise consistent property of the two normal fields (i.e., facet and vertex normal fields) and propose an effective framework in which they are filtered and integrated using a novel method to guide the mesh denoising process. The method consists of three steps: vertex classification, bi-normal filtering, and vertex position update. The classification step allows us to filter the two fields on a piecewise smooth surface rather than a surface that is smooth everywhere. Based on the piecewise consistence of the two normal fields, we filtered them using a piecewise smooth region clustering strategy. To benefit from the bi-normal filtering, we design a quadratic optimization algorithm for vertex position update. Our algorithm achieves higher quality results than current approaches on surfaces with multifarious geometric features and irregular surface sampling. We have presented a novel approach to better preserve morphological features. We first develop a labeling process to distinguish staircases from geometric features and then eliminate them by a staircase-sensitive Laplace filter. To reduce the noises, we approximate local morphology by fitting vertex and their neighborhood using biquadratic Bezier surfaces. Finally, we formulate an optimization of local spatial quadrics (LSQ), which can yield a compact mesh in which each triangle is tangent to the underlying surface and hence the morphological features are well preserved. We have proposed a novel method to do labeling for medical images in which anchor points and textual label layout are automatically determined. First, we compute the anchor points of tissues which are very representative. Second, rather than using optimization method to solve this problem, we transform the label layout problem to a one-to-one mapping problem and develop our mapping algorithm to solve it. Our method can produce an even and non-overlapping label layout. We have developed an easy-to-use anatomy learning system with a 3D printed human body and a 6DoF tracker, to let users explore anatomical structures at arbitrary positions and angles for surgical path planning in real time. Slice images and labels are real-time calculated and displayed as users move the tracker on the plastic model at arbitrary positions and angles. This system can be used in the human anatomy education and research as well as other applications such as surgical planning.

A summary of major findings are given under the following categories: Medical image visualization and segmentation – • In [J03], we propose a novel algorithm to make the learning process of Gaussian mixture model more stable, which has achieved good results on color image (e.g., CVH data) segmentation. • In [J04], we propose to reduce speckle noise in ultrasound images using feature asymmetry anisotropic diffusion. • In [J05], we present an efficient 3D fully convolutional network equipped with a 3D deep supervision mechanism to segment volumetric medical images. • In [C02], we propose an efficient segmentation-based framework for the automatic generation of transfer functions for visualization. • In [C03], we propose a semi-automatic approach to segment liver tumor from CT volume. • In [C06], we propose a 3D FractalNet for volumetric segmentation of cardiovascular MRI data. • In [C07], we propose a densely connected ConvNets for the 3D segmentation of cardiovascular MRI data. • In [C9], we propose a deep contour-aware network to segment glands from histology images. • In [C11], we propose a 3D convolutional network to segment whole heart. • In [C12], we propose a hybrid loss guided convolutional network to segment whole heart. • In [C14], we propose a 3D fully convolutional network to segment intervertebral disc. • In [C16], we propose a Bayesian nonparametric approach to recover the noisy matrix, i.e. noisy image, based on only a small number of observed entries. • In [C17], we propose a novel two-stage method to remove noise from a single image. Specially, we employ the Dirichlet model to automatically cluster similar patches in a group, and then derive a new filter to remove the contained noise. • In [C18], we propose an efficient statistical method for the noise level estimation from a single image. Geometrically reconstruction and optimization – • In [J01], we solve the morphology-preserving problem of anatomical structures. This method is able to preserve the morphology of anatomical models. • In [J02], we propose an effective framework to guide the mesh denoising process. The method can be directly extended to post-process 3D medical models. • In [C04], a personalized reconstruction of organs with various deformations has been proposed based on biomechanical modelling. Anatomical structure labeling – • In [C01], we propose a novel method to do automated labeling for medical images in which anchor points and textual label layout are determined. • In [C05], we propose a joint learning model for the localization of anatomical structures. • In [C10], we propose a cascaded networks for the mitosis detection. • In [C13], we propose a deep regression networks for the mitosis detection. • In [C15], we propose a 3D ConvNets for the pulmonary nodule detection. Anatomy learning system and interactive interface – • In [C08], we propose an efficient tissue-tissue interaction scheme for soft tissue interaction in virtual surgery.

412513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
412513.value: In our future work, we aim to conduct more in-depth system evaluations and refinements, and extend our system to other video-assisted surgery applications. Such a virtual training circumstance can deliver the trainee high fidelity experience of virtual operative anatomy for learning video-assisted thoracoscopic lung surgery skills and assess the quality of learning surgical procedure. Our proposed course of actions include – • Collaborate with surgeons and physicians for further evaluation and refinement of our existing prototypes. • Provide software licensing for educational purpose and beta testing. • Search for industrial collaborators for technology transfer in the area of virtual video-assisted thoracoscopic lung surgery and virtual operative anatomy learning. • Continue to seek new research grants to further our research in virtual reality anatomy and surgical simulation.

412513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
412513.value: Training of video assisted thoracoscopic surgery has been more prevalent in all structured training programs globally in the field of cardiothoracic surgery. Thoracoscopic surgery is a complex procedure. It is essential for a thoracic-surgeon to possess a firm knowledge of thoracoscopic anatomy and possess high degree of surgical skills before one operates on a patient. Current training on human cadaver only provides learning of the normal anatomy and there is a call for more lifelike training with pathological conditions. In this project, we have built a virtual operative anatomy system facilitating surgeons in learning 3D anatomy in the thoracic cavity, and developed a virtual environment for the training of pulmonary thoracoscopic skills. The deliverable in this project is the first virtual environment which provides real-time operative photorealism in presenting thoracoscopic-related surgical anatomy by fully exploiting the HDTV surgical images as well as the CVH color textural volume. Such a virtual learning environment can deliver the trainee high fidelity experience of virtual operative anatomy for learning video-assisted thoracoscopic lung surgery skills and assess the quality of learning surgical procedure. Our project deliverable is able to generate a truly repeatable skill learning platform with no need to practice on real patients.

412613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
412613.value: This project proposes to develop a lab-in-droplet bioassay strategy implemented on a power-enabled lab-on-a-disc (LOAD) platform. The proposed approach aims to resolve major design issues that have prevented widespread adoption of LOAD by the bioassay industry. Although LOAD has been recognized as an attractive device solution for low-cost multi-assay applications because of its pump-less operation using centrifugal force, there is a critical drawback due to the lack of physical access to the disc while it is in rotational mode. This makes it impossible to perform common bioassay steps such as real-time flow control, sample heating and precise monitoring of assay conditions within the LOAD platform. To resolve the above problem, specifically the proposed approach has two key features: (i) droplet-in-oil bioassays with movement of droplets purely actuated by density difference between the aqueous droplets and its surrounding oil medium, thereby achieving small sample consumption and precise mass transport; (ii) introduction of electrical power to the rotating disc, thus enabling a multitude of on-chip real-time bioassay functionalities without any stop-go interruption. This project will first implement an integrated LOAD system containing three layers including (i) a disposable polymer disc containing the microfluidic components; (ii) a printed circuit board coupled to the polymer disc for providing local temperature control, electromagnetic valve actuation, droplet manipulation and signal transduction; (iii) a split-core transformer for non-contacting power coupling to the rotating platform. The team has demonstrated a first-generation power-enabled LOAD prototype for allergy screening and DNA amplification. The proposed project aims to develop new on-chip microfluidic components, namely (i) droplet generation devices; (ii) rotation and electromagnetic actuated gate valves; (iii) droplet sorting valves; (iv) dielectrostatic/ultrasound actuators for droplet mixing; (v) micropillar/micropore flow-through chambers for droplet-based bio-detection. These basic microfluidic components, working under direct control from the circuit board underneath, will perform the bioassays as desired. By dividing the disc into many small sectors, one can readily scale the LOAD device for conducting multiple tests on a single specimen. A unique commercial merit of this strategy is that users only need to install one common reader system, while the disposable LOAD device is custom-designed according to assay requirements. This project has impact in many biotechnology sectors such as low-cost point-of-care DNA or protein based diagnostics and high-throughput single cell studies. While the demand for better healthcare at reduced costs is growing rapidly in Hong Kong and worldwide, this project may offer solutions to alleviate the situation. 該項目提出了一種基於液滴生物測定技術的新型離心力微流控系統。該系統應用於非接觸式電耦合離心力微流控晶片（LOAD）平臺。該專案在基於晶片實驗室（LOC）的許多技術領域具有獨特的優勢。典型的晶片實驗室運用泵浦可以實現樣品液的流動，然而離心力微流控晶片上的離心力使液體在整個晶片範圍具有自動流動的特性，使其最適合於低成本的應用。特別地，該裝置具有兩個重要的特徵：（1） 該生物測定方法基於含水試樣和它周圍油介質的密度差導致的液滴運動，從而實現精確的物質運輸；（2） 通過為旋轉的離心力微流控晶片引入電源，晶片上多數即時生物測定功能可在不間斷的情況下執行。 該項目將首先完成一個集成的離心力微流控晶片，共三層：（1）包含微流組件的一次性聚合物圓盤；（2）與聚合物圓盤相連的印刷電路板，可提供包括局部溫度控制、電磁閥動、液滴操縱和信號檢測和傳輸的功能；（3）分離鐵芯式變壓器，將非接觸電信號耦合到旋轉平臺上。 我們已經收集了初步資料來展示如何運用電耦合離心力微流控晶片方法進行過敏症篩選和DNA擴增。至此，該項目致力於發展新型片上微流元件，即（1）液滴產生腔；（2）用旋轉和電磁驅動閥門操縱液滴；（3）運用閥門將分離的液滴排列進入不同流道；（4）液滴凝聚制動器；（5）基於液滴的生物測定微柱形/微氣孔溢流腔。這些由底部電路板直接控制的基本微流元件是集成生物測定所需要的。甚至可以將若干生物測定元件放在同一離心力微流控晶片設備上來完成單一樣品的多重檢驗。該方法的一個獨特的商業優勢是使用者僅需購買一個離心力微流控晶片讀取系統，一次性的離心力微流控晶片可以根據試驗要求定制。 該項目影響著許多生物技術應用，例如低成本床邊檢測DNA或者蛋白質的診斷裝置和高通量單細胞研究。當前香港和世界範圍都非常需要在降低成本的情況下提供更好的保健服務，基於該專案的新型生物分析技術將為此提供解決方案。

412613.label: Realisation of objectives
412613.value: The primary goal of this project is to develop centrifugal microfluidics for low-cost point-of-care bioassays, with droplet-in-oil as a new strategy for highly flexible sample processing and manipulation. Within the course of this project, we have focussed our efforts on two areas: (i) droplet-in-oil strategy in centrifugal microfluidics for sample processing and signal detection; (ii) demonstration of practical bioassays based on LOAD. The electrical power-enabled active centrifugal microfluidics system, or so-called active lab-on-a-disc (LOAD), that we previously reported has been shown to be very effective baseline platform for a wide range of bioassay functionalities. Within this project, we have successfully demonstrated full sample-to-answer operation of our LOAD platform for several healthcare applications, namely cell-based allergy testing and drug screening and nucleic acid based detection of drug allergy and infectious disease including Mycobacterium tuberculosis (TB) and Acinetobacter baumanii (Ab). This technological output from this project has opened a new direction for low-cost point-of-care detection of bacterial infectious diseases with fast turnaround time. The effort has led to a journal publication in Biosensors and Bioelectronics. As a continuation of this effort, we are currently working with the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) of The Prince Edward Hospital (PWH) through Dr Czarina Leung to develop a complete proof-of-concept LOAD system for point-of-care monitoring of 5 infections, namely Enterobacter aerogenes, Enterococcus faecalis,Bacteria, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, commonly found in the ward. Validation results are expected to come out in February 2017. On the topic of droplet-in-oil, this project has produced a new strategy based on Euler forces generated from angular acceleration of spinning during centrifugal actuation. This technique is found to be effective in selecting the delivery channel of the droplet, thus leading to the possibility of “logical” manipulation of droplets in which the droplet can be accurately driven into a selected channel at any Y-junction. This will ensure the outcome of delivering one droplet to each chamber within an array for conducting many droplet-based bioassays in parallel. With our electricity-enable LOAD system, we can perform localised heating suitable for the reaction requirements of each of the chambers. This effort has produced one journal publication (in preparation, aiming to be submitted to Lab Chip), one Chinese patent and one conference paper. Through this project, we have made significant progress in the development of a complete LOAD system for clinical use. As mentioned previously, we have produced a practical system for use in ICU. Recently (25 November 2016), we have co-organised a one-day seminar for 35 high school students to receive practical experimental experience on identifying genetically modified papaya fruits through screening their DNA. We adopted the loop-mediated nucleic acid amplification (LAMP) technique, which requires a constant temperature of 60-65 deg C for amplify the target DNA strands with an accuracy within 0.5 deg C. This requirement puts our LOAD approach a favourable choice because of the availability of electrical power. Our team developed 7 LOAD machines for the event. The machines were shown to be useful for conducting the DNA tests. We used disposable polymer discs fabricated from a mould. The material cost was low enough to make the LOAD approach a real competitor for practical low-cost point-of-care DNA tests. Within this project, we have accumulated extensive knowledge on the development of centrifugal force based microfluidics, particularly those related to bioassays that requires active heating. We have published a review article on this topic. Apart from new LOAD techniques, this project has provided the opportunity for developing a new centrifugal microfluidics strategy called lab-in-a-tube. We have further expanded the concept of electrical-power enabled operations to the test tube environment. This way we can make use of the extremely high spinning speed, up to 100,000 rpm, available from common centrifuges. The so-call motor-assisted chip-in-a-tube (MACT) has brought in a wide range of real-time sample processing and signal detection capabilities. With MACT one can effectively complete a bioassay in any commercially available centrifuge. Based on this work we have produce one publication in Lab Chip and one US patent (filed). On the objective of developing new devices based on droplet-in-oil centrifugal microfluidics, the remaining tasks include (i) strategies for performing fusion of two droplets as required for conducting bioassays; (ii) production of cell-containing droplets; (iii) extraction of DNA based on the droplet strategy. We have not been able to make strong progress on these tasks primarily due to the lack of suitable personnel. It has been difficult to recruit personnel who are experienced enough in both engineering and biochemistry for conducting the work. We are currently actively recruiting a new research student to continue the droplet-in-oil work, which has very strong application potential for the next generation of microfluidics. Given more time, we are quite confident that the effort will lead to high impact outcomes. In light of the growing trend of personalised medicine, the demand for high-throughput screening of nucleic acids is definitely the way forward. Drop-in-oil centrifugal microfluidic, which offers the merits of low-cost, low sample consumption and highly parallel multiplexed screening tests, is an effective solution for addressing the market requirements.

412613.label: Major findings and research outcome
412613.value: A major outcome of this project has established a medical device platform for low-cost and point-of-care analysis of biomolecular species. We have successfully demonstrated a complete power-enabled lab-on-a-disc system for nucleic acid based analysis of biological samples. The use of centrifugal forces offers the advantage of pump-less operation while sample actuation forces are available anywhere within the disc surface. Since centrifugal forces are linearly proportional to radius and spinning speed, one has very accurate control on the size of the actuation force. In addition, another very useful attribute of centrifugal microfluidic is the use of capillary valves, which operate under the influence of surface tension as the sample fluid passes over a sudden expansion of the microchannel width. These passive valves conveniently provide a scheme for controlling the sequence of motion of sample fluids in the microfluidic system as required. This effort has produced two journal publications in Biosensors and Bioelectronics and Lab Chip, which respectively report sample-to-answer diagnosis of bacterial infections and in-line spectrophotometry for protein sensing. With the introduction of electrical power while the disc is still spinning mode, all kinds of intricate control processes can be implemented. All on-disc operations are no longer in the passive mode. Active operation mode is particularly useful for the case of droplet-in-oil systems, as capillary actions do not play a significant role in droplet manipulation. Through this project, we have demonstrated a mechanism for digital generation and manipulation of droplets in a centrifugal microfluidic chip. We have filed one Chinese patent. And a Lab Chip manuscript is now under preparation. A third outcome of this project is the inception of an active “lab-in-a-tube”, or so-called motor-assisted chip-in-a-tube (MACT), approach for conducting bioassays in a 3-dimensional multi-layered centrifugal microfluidic device. The concept incorporates a motor within the instrument, which can change the direction of the centrifugal force relative to the chip surface in order to produce force vectors in any direction within the 3-dimensional coordinates. The work has led to the publication of a Lab Chip paper and a patent (US and Chinese).

412613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
412613.value: This project has potential for further development in the directions of applied research and commercialisation. The project PI has identified a research student, who shall be starting in August 2017, to continue the droplet-in-oil experiment. The focus will be on the study of droplet manipulation and mixing under the inertial force actuation as compared to conventional flow actuated movements. Centrifugal force is primarily generated through density difference between oil and water, which is entirely different from the case of water droplet being carried by a stream of oil inside the microchannel. Our aim is to explore the possibilities of using inertial forces to obtain highly accurate parameters of the contents in the droplets, which may provide information about the bio-activities inside. Another direction that the project team is actively pursuing the possibility of commercialising the active LOAD concept for bioassay applications. The team now has established a start-up company called ATSPIN to develop such instruments.

412613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
412613.value: In this project, we have successfully developed an active power-enabled lab-on-a-disc (LOAD) system for conducting bioassays. Although the LOAD approach has been recognized as an attractive solution for low-cost multi-assay applications because of its pump-less operation, a critical drawback exists because of the lack of physical access to the disc while it is in rotational mode. This makes it impossible to perform many common bioassay steps such as real-time flow control, sample heating and precise monitoring of assay conditions within the LOAD platform. With the availability of electricity from our active power-enabled LOAD, many of such sample processing requirements are resolved without much difficulty. Meanwhile, another new concept called the droplet-in-oil scheme as demonstrated through this project, also offers the benefits of small sample consumption and precise mass transport. The outcome of this project has impact in many biotechnology sectors such as low-cost point-of-care DNA or protein based diagnostics and high-throughput single cell studies. While the demand for better healthcare at reduced costs is growing rapidly in Hong Kong and worldwide, this project may offer solutions to alleviate the situation.

412713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
412713.value: 本研究项目的主要目的是设计、分析和实施关于动态频谱共享的新的市场机制和分布式协议。 无线频谱是一种稀缺资源，因而通常被分割成为不相重叠的频段而授权给不同政府和商业实体长期使用。这种分配方法有效地保护了授权用户免受未授权用户的干扰，但同时也导致许多频段的实际利用率较低。解决这一问题的方法是允许授权和未经授权的无线用户之间以不同优先级进行动态的频谱共享。目前干扰缓解和微小区技术的发展使得频谱共享在技术上已经可以实现。但另一方面授权用户通常没有足够的经济上的动力去共享频谱资源。因此我们需要设计创新的市场机制来实现无线频谱共享的双赢。此外我们还需要设计分布式协议来方便用户之间协调频谱共享。 在这个研究项目中，我们计划回答以下四个关于频谱共享的关键问题： （一）什么样的市场机制可以为授权用户提供适当的经济激励并对无授权用户实现差异化服务？ （二）用户如何在竞争激烈的环境中使用动态变化的资源实现想要的QoS？ （三）如何鼓励用户在有限的网络信息下实现有效的协调？ （四）如何使得用户在不同类型的频段间实现无缝的自由切换？ 本项目的第一和第二带头人在分布式无线资源分配的优化，博弈论和网络经济学上具有较强的专业知识和成功的合作经验。该项目还获得了相关领域的业界合作伙伴的大力支持。该项目的研究成果能够帮助我们更深入地了解动态频谱共享的的机遇和挑战。

412713.label: Realisation of objectives
412713.value: We are pleased to report that the project team has achieved all project objectives, through collaborations with many top researchers around the world. This project is theoretical in nature. We have designed and analyzed a wide range of market mechanisms and distributed protocols for dynamic spectrum sharing and wireless resource sharing. We have used methodologies including auction theory, pricing theory, noncooperative game theory, bargaining theory, mechanism design, nonlinear optimization, and graph theory. The application scenarios include government spectrum allocation, cognitive femtocell management, TV white space management, wireless data offloading, user-centric resource sharing, dynamic power control, and social-aware spectrum sharing. We have designed flexible hybrid mechanisms that provide strong incentives of sharing for both licensed users and enable differential services for unlicensed users. We have proposed resource sharing schemes that enable users to achieve the desired QoS in a competitive environment with dynamically available resources. We have designed incentive mechanisms that effectively induce coordination among users with limited network information and bounded rationality. Overall, we have achieved a deeper understanding of opportunities and challenges of the large-scale dynamic spectrum sharing. Results related to this projects have appeared in 3 monographs, 2 book chapters, 18 top IEEE Transactions, journals and magazines, and 22 international conference papers. This project also trained 5 PhD students and lead to two Best (student) Paper Awards. The detailed summary is given in Part C.

412713.label: Major findings and research outcome
412713.value: We study how mobile users can switch between licensed and unlicensed spectrum bands and effectively offload the traffic to reduce the stress on the cellular networks. This is related to journal publications 3, 5, 14, 15, 16, and 17, conference publications 2, 8, 9, and 14. We study how the regulator should allocate spectrum resources among licensed and unlicensed spectrum bands to balance the income and the users' utility. This is related to journal publication 1. We study how the radio resources should be allocated among femtocell networks to achieve efficient communications. This is related to journal publication 2. We propose contract and information market models for TV white space networks, for the effective shared usage of the TV spectrum by unlicensed devices. This is related to journal publications 4, 7, 10 and 13, conference publications 6, 11 and 15. We propose an effective revenue sharing mechanism that incentivizes the primary users to effectively share the spectrum resources with the secondary users. This is related to journal publication 6. We analyze several user-provided wireless networks and propose effective incentive mechanisms for the users to fairly share their limited communication and energy resources with each other to achieve an enhanced overall network performance. This is related to journal publication 8, conference publications 3, 13, 16, and 17. We propose a simple yet effective power control algorithm based on location recommendations for wireless ad hoc networks. This is related to journal publication 9 and conference publication 1. We explore the effective social-aware spectrum sharing using graph theory and matching theory. This is related to journal publications 11, 12, and 18. We use behavioral economics to understand the investment and resource access behaviors of mobile operators and users in both cellular and cognitive radio networks. This is related to conference publications 4 and 10. We propose several resource allocation and incentive mechanisms for effective use of spectrum and wireless resources in mobile crowd sensing and crowdsourcing. This is related to conference publications 5, 7, 12, 18 and 20. We explore economic mechanisms to more effectively utilize the spectrum of WiFi and share the unlicensed spectrum with LTE-U services. This is related to conference publications 19, 21, and 22.

412713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
412713.value: This research project has been successfully concluded and related research outputs have been published. In the future, it is possible to further develop more advanced learning-based spectrum sharing and co-existence mechanism, by taking advance of the recent advancements in reinforcement learning and combining with the extensive spectrum dynamic availability measurement data.

412713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
412713.value: Wireless spectrum is a scarce resource, and historically it has been divided into chunks and allocated to different government and commercial entities with long-term and exclusive licenses. This approach protects license users from harmful interferences from unauthorized users but leaves little spectrum for emerging new services and leads to low spectrum utilization in many spectrum bands. The way to turn “spectrum drought” into “spectrum abundance” is to allow dynamic and opportunistic spectrum sharing between licensed and unlicensed users with different priorities. In this project, we answer the following key questions in a shared spectrum environment: (a) What kind of market mechanism can provide proper incentives for licensed users and enable differential services for unlicensed users? (b) How can users achieve the desired QoS in a competitive environment with dynamically changing resources? (c) How to encourage coordination among users with limited network information and bounded rationality? The output of the proposed research leads to a deeper understanding of opportunities and challenges of the large-scale implementation of dynamic spectrum sharing.

412813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
412813.value: Since the early 2000s, the cooperative control or coordinated control of multi-agent systems has become one of the central control problems. The cooperative control of multi-agent systems includes but is not limited to such problems as consensus/synchronization, formation, rendezvous, flocking, and swarming. These problems arise from such applications as the coordination of mobile robots, mobile sensor networks, formation of unmanned flight vehicles, etc. What distinguishes the control of a multi-agent system from the control of a conventional system is that a control law for a multi-agent system is usually distributed in order to achieve a coordinated global objective while satisfying communication constraints. The past decade has witnessed a tremendous expansion on the research of multi-agent control systems. However, so far most results are limited to homogeneous linear systems without subjecting to uncertainties and external disturbances. Recently, the PI has developed a framework called cooperative output regulation for linear multi-agent systems which is capable of achieving asymptotic tracking and disturbance rejection in a linear uncertain heterogeneous multi-agent system. The problem formulation includes the leader-following consensus and formation of linear multi-agent systems as special cases. In this project, we will further extend this framework to nonlinear uncertain heterogeneous multi-agent systems. This framework consists of two steps. The first step will convert the cooperative output regulation problem for a given nonlinear multi-agent system into a global stabilization problem of a distributed augmented system composed of the given multi-agent system and a distributed internal model. In the second step, the distributed augmented system will be further globally stabilized by a distributed control law. What makes our problem challenging is that even if each agent of the multi-agent system is single-input, single-output and time-invariant, the augmented system is always multi-input, multi-output. Moreover, in order to satisfy the time-varying communication constraints, we can only employ a distributed time-varying control law instead of a centralized time-invariant control law. We will overcome these difficulties by seeking a distributed internal model and establish specific stabilization techniques applicable to multi-input, multi-output, and time-varying uncertain nonlinear systems. Also, we will apply this framework to a few practical cooperative control problems such as the mobile robot coordination, and formation of spacecraft systems in a more realistic setting. The success of this project will not only enhance our capability to handle various cooperative control problems for practical nonlinear multi-agent systems, but also significantly advance control techniques for multi-input, multi-output uncertain nonlinear uncertain systems. 自21世纪初, 多智能体的协同或者协调控制问题已经成为控制界的中心问题之一.多智能体的协同问题涵盖了趋同,编队,蜂拥,群聚等问题.这些问题在机器人的协同控制,无线传感网络,无人驾驶机的编队等实际应用中应运而生. 有别于传统的控制问题, 由于存在通讯限制, 多智能体系统的控制器必须是分布式的. 在过去的十年间, 多智能体的控制研究已取得巨大进展. 然而,到现在为止,大部分的结果还仅限于齐次线性系统, 而且还假定这些系统不含不确定性,也不受外部干扰. 最近,我们提出了一个求解线性多智能体系统的协同输出调节的框架. 该框架可同时解决线性多智能体系统的渐近跟踪,抑制干扰等问题,而且还允许这种线性多智能体系统含不确定参数,甚至允许每个子体系统具有不同的结构. 线性多智能体的有领导者的趋同和编队问题只是协同输出调节问题的特例. 在本项目中,我们考虑将该框架推广到不确定性非线性异构多智能体. 该框架由两个步骤构成.第一个步骤是将非线性多智能体系统的协同输出调节问题转化成分布增广系统的全局镇定问题,而这个增广系统由原来的多智能体系统和分布式的内模组成. 第二个步骤是设计一个分布式控制器来全局镇定这个增广系统. 在这过程中, 我们遇到的技术上挑战有: (1) 即便每个多智能体的子系统是单输入单输出的, 增广系统也是多输入多输出的;(2) 由于存在时变的通讯限制, 我们必须设计一个分布式时变控制器来解决我们的问题,而不是一个集中式的时不变控制器. 为克服这些困难, 我们将寻求设计分布式的内模并且开发可全局镇定多输入时变不确定性非线性系统的工具. 我们还会将这些结果应用于机器人的协调控制,航天器的编队等实际控制问题. 该项目的成功实施不仅有助于非线性多智能体系统的实际应用,而且能大大地提高关于带有不确定性参数的多输入多输出非线性系统的控制技术.

412813.label: Major findings and research outcome
412813.value: 1. We have extended the framework for handling the cooperative output regulation problem for linear multi-agent systems to nonlinear uncertain heterogeneous uncertain nonlinear multi-agent systems. This framework consists of two steps. The first step converts the cooperative output regulation problem for a given nonlinear multi-agent system into a global stabilization problem of a distributed augmented system composed of the given multi-agent and a distributed internal model. In the second step, the distributed augmented system will be further globally stabilized by a distributed control law. What makes this problem challenging is that even if each agent of the multi-agent system is single-input, single-output and time-invariant, the augmented system is always multi-input, multi-output. Moreover, in order to satisfy the time-varying communication constraint, we can only employ a distributed time-varying control law instead of a centralized time-invariant control law. We have overcome these difficulties by seeking a distributed internal model and establish specific stabilization techniques applicable to multi-input, multi-output, and time-varying uncertain nonlinear systems. The major results are reported in the following papers: Y. Su, and J. Huang, “Cooperative global robust output regulation for nonlinear uncertain multi-agent systems in lower triangular form,” IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control, Vol. 60, No. 9, September 2015, pp. 2378 – 2389. T. Liu and J. Huang, “Cooperative output regulation for a class of nonlinear multi-agent systems with unknown control directions subject to switching networks” IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control, Vol. 63, No. 3, March 2018, pp. 783-790 2. We have further applied our general framework to two interesting cooperative control problems of multi-agent systems. The first one is the leadless and leader-following consensus problem with connectivity preservation of uncertain Euler-lagrange multi-agent systems. The major findings are reported in one journal paper and one conference paper. The second one is the Leader-following attitude control of multiple rigid spacecraft systems via unit quaternion-based output feedback control. The major findings are reported in two journal papers and one conference paper coauthored with Prof. Cai. Additionally, we have extended our study to the output regulation problem for both linear time-delay systems and linear time-delay multi-agent systems. This finding will pave the way for further studying the cooperative output regulation problem for nonlinear time-delay multi-agent systems. The major findings are reported in 4 papers with my then PhD students Dr. Lv and Dr. Yan, respectively.

412813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
412813.value: So far we have focused on continuous-time systems. We will further consider discrete-time multi-agent systems later. Also we will consider implement our control law using the event-triggered control method so that the control law can be implemented in a digital platform efficiently.

412813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
412813.value: Over the past decade, the cooperative control or coordinated control of multi-agent systems has become one of the central control problems. The cooperative control includes but is not limited to such problems as consensus/synchronization, formation, rendezvous, flocking, and swarming. These problems arise from such engineering applications as the coordination of mobile robots, mobile sensor networks, formation of unmanned flight vehicles. In this project, we have established a general framework for handling the cooperative output regulation problem for nonlinear uncertain multi-agent systems. This framework consists of two steps. The first step converts the cooperative output regulation problem for a given nonlinear multi-agent system into a global stabilization problem of a distributed augmented system composed of the given plant and a distributed internal model. In the second step, the distributed augmented system is further globally stabilized by a distributed control law. Moreover, we have applied this framework to a few classes of important nonlinear multi-agent systems including nonlinear systems in output feedback form, feedforward form, and normal form, and to a few practical cooperative control problems such as the mobile robot coordination, and attitude control of multiple spacecraft systems.

412913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
412913.value: Shape editing is a popular operation in the design of engineering components using computer-aided design (CAD) systems. Although there are tools for deforming or editing polygon mesh models, they are not adopted for editing CAD models of engineering components. This is because most existing deformation techniques deform a 3D model without considering its effects on the functional features of the component. For example, a straight hole may be bended in a deformation process. However, this hole may have to be fitted to a shaft such that the deformed shape is not acceptable. There are some works on preserving surface details in the deformation of a polygon mesh. These approaches mainly retain the visual appearance of the object and provide no guarantee on retaining the functional features of the component. There are also some works on preserving shape features specified by edges of a model. Nevertheless, edges are not enough for specifying engineering features (e.g. the flatness of a surface is not constrained even if the boundaries edges are coplanar), and hence is not sufficient for controlling the shape of engineering components. This research is to develop an approach for the shape editing of CAD models such that functional features of the models are not affected. This approach will allow user specified shape features to remain unaffected while their locations and orientations may be modified in the editing process. For example, two shafts modeled as cylindrical features attached to a casing may be restricted such that their axes must be parallel to each other and the cylindrical surfaces have to remain cylindrical while the casing is deformed. In this research, a scheme for representing functional form features in a CAD model will be developed. In order that the proposed approach can be used for models constructed with trimmed NURBS surface which is widely adopted in existing CADCAM systems, an approach will be developed to convert trimmed NURBS surfaces to a form suitable for the shape editing process. Algorithms will be developed to maintain the continuities of the converted surfaces in the shape editing process. An optimization technique will also be developed to obtain an optimal shape of the component such that the given constraints are satisfied. It is expected that the results of this research will provide an important design tool for the design and development of complex engineering components and forms a basis for further automating the product design process. 形狀編輯普遍應用於計算機輔助設計。雖然現有不少網格模型編輯工具, 這些工具都未能應用於計算機輔助工程設計。因為這些變形技術未有考慮形狀改變對組件工能的影響。例如，一個直孔在編輯過程中變成彎曲的筒道，然而，這直孔可能是一軸孔，因此不可以彎曲。雖然有不少硏究在變形的網格上保留原有細節，這些方法主要保留物件的外觀視覺效果，對保留組件的功能特性，並沒有保證。有硏究利用模型的邊緣線匡表示及保留形狀特徵，然而，邊緣線匡未能全面表示各種工能特徵 (例如，邊緣線匡不可能表示一表面是否平坦)，因此不足以控制工程部件的形狀。 這項研究就是要開發可保留CAD模型功能特性的形狀編輯方法。這方法將容許用戶指定的形狀特徵在形狀編輯中不受影響，而這形狀特徵的位置和方向，則可被修改。例如，在修改一個連接著兩個筒狀軸蕊模形的殼體時，這兩個軸蕊必須保持平行，而圓形的筒狀軸蕊亦必須保持圓形。這項研究將開發功能特徵的表示方法。為使這方法可用於現有CADCAM系統中被廣泛應用的Trimmed NURBS 曲面，這項研究將開發能轉換Trimmed NURBS 到適合形狀編輯的表示法，亦會開發在編輯過程中能保持曲面連續性的算法，以及開發優化技術，優化組件在滿足各種限制下的形狀。本研究的結果將提供一重要的設計工具，適合開發複雜的工程部件，更可成為進一步產品設計自動化的基礎。

413113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
413113.value: Large-scale 3D reconstruction is one important task in computer vision. It is developed quickly with its significance in many practical applications in building and street modeling and rendering. Typical examples include Google Earth and Microsoft Virtual Earth, in which 3D structures are formed and visualized. Automatic 3D reconstruction finds its foundation on structure-of-motion (SfM), which is a useful set of techniques to recover sparse 3D correspondences of an object or scene in multiple frames during motion and to estimate camera trajectories in the 3D space. Without using SfM, automatic 3D reconstruction could be difficult, if not impossible, to accomplish. Dense images and common videos contain a lot of geometrical and structural information. They provide vital clues for SfM. The traditional way to perform video SfM is to track feature points continuously in multiple frames considering temporal relationship among them. These schemes could be influenced by many factors, as will be detailed later in this proposal. In this project, we will revisit and systematically study this problem given our extensive experience in this field, mainly to address a few challenging issues for feature point tracking and eventually to construct a complete and reliable system. One such problem is that feature tracking is sensitive to occlusions, lighting condition change, possible image noise, and significant movement, which easily make tracked points being dropped. Therefore, feature tracking in long sequences is generally not very stable and can be distracted. The second problem is on how to efficiently detect and match common features over non-consecutive subsequences. Its significance for SfM has been demonstrated on quite a number of examples in prior work. Third, in a large scale scene, efficiently registering multiple videos to a unified coordinate system is difficult, considering inevitable error accumulation. These issues exist in prior work following the line of feature tracking and could seriously hamper SfM from being applied to large-scale scene modeling. This project devotes to addressing these fundamental issues that commonly affect SfM and advancing the framework in terms of robustness and efficiency. Our research will eventually profit 3D structure estimation regarding correspondence establishment among features for connecting and non-connecting frames, general optimization framework definition, structure consistency constraint enforcement, and real-time performance achievement. A broad spectrum of applications, e.g., scene understanding and recognition, can be benefited as well. 大尺度3D重建是計算機視覺中的一個重要任務。因其在建築物、街道建模及渲染等實際應用中，具有重大意義，近年來發展迅速。Google地球（Google Earth）和微軟虛擬地球（Microsoft Virtual Earth）是兩個典型的粒子，它們可以實現3D結構的重建和顯示。自動的3D重建建基於SfM（structure-of-motion）技術。SfM包含了一系列有用技術，從多幀圖像中，恢復稀疏的3D物體或場景的匹配，以及估計相機在3D空間中的軌跡。沒有SfM技術，自動3D重建會是一大難題，即使不是無法解決。 連續圖像或者影像中，所包含的豐富的幾何以及結構信息，是SfM技術的重要依據。傳統的基於影像的SfM依賴於連幀圖像中的特徵點跟蹤，通過時域連續性來實現。但是，這一方法的準確度受多個因素制約（這些因素我們將在本計劃書后半部份詳細講述）。在本項目中，依賴於我們在該領域已有的豐富經驗，我們將對本問題先進行一個系統審視，然後解決特徵點跟蹤方法中的一些難點問題，最終搭建一套完整可靠的3D重建系統。 我們要解決的第一大問題是，現有特徵點跟蹤方法對於遮擋、光線變化、圖像噪聲和顯著運動的敏感性，這使得所跟蹤的特徵點易於丟失。由此導致在長序列影像幀中，特徵點跟蹤變得不穩定，甚至於偏移。第二個問題是，如何高效率的檢測和匹配不連續子序列中的特徵點。這一問題的重要性已經在很多前人的工作中提到。第三，大尺度場景中，多個影像快速配準到統一的座標系統。問題的難點在於，大尺度和多影像的條件下，累積錯誤不可避免。上述問題的存在，使得基於特徵點跟蹤的SfM技術不能直接應用於大尺度場景建模。 本項目將著重於解決這些影響SfM準確度的重要問題，進一步提升SfM技術的可靠性和效率。我們的工作包括，連續和不連續影像幀中的特徵點匹配的研究，該問題的一般優化框架的定義，時域結構一致性約束的引入，以及實時算法的實現。這些最終都將有益于3D結構重建。除此之外，一些其他應用，如場景理解和識別，也將受益于我們的技術。

413113.label: Realisation of objectives
413113.value: The first objective is to investigate new schemes to reliably extend tracked feature lifetime in connecting frames. We found it is closely related to the vulnerability of feature tracking to object occlusions, illumination change, noise, and large motion, which easily causes occasional feature drop-out and distraction. This problem makes robust feature tracking from long sequences challenging. To address this issue, we proposed consecutive point tracking to detect and match invariant features in consecutive frames. A matching strategy is proposed to greatly increase the matching rate and extend lifetime of the tracks. Then in non-consecutive track matching, by rapidly computing a matching matrix, a set of disjoint subsequences with overlapping content can be detected. Common feature tracks scattered over these subsequences can also be reliably matched. The new two-pass matching strategy is very effective. The first-pass matching is the same as our prior method, which uses SIFT algorithm with RANSAC to obtain high-confidence matches and remove outliers. In the second pass matching, we first use the inlier matches to estimate a set of homographies with multiple RANSAC procedures. To handle illumination change, we estimate global illumination variation between images by computing the median intensity ratio between matched features. The two-pass matching can produce many long tracks. Each track has a group of descriptors. They are similar to each other in the same track due to the matching criteria. We compute average of the descriptors over the track, and denote it as track descriptor. This strategy is very effective to achieve our first goal. For the second objective to propose new models to match features that are not in adjacent frames, we match features distributed in different subsequences, which is vital for drift-free SfM estimation. If we select all image pairs in a brute-force manner, the process can be intolerably costly for a long sequence. A better strategy is to estimate content similarity among different images first. We propose a non-consecutive track matching (NCTM) method to address this problem. There are two steps. In the first step, similarity of different images is coarsely estimated by constructing a symmetric match matrix storing overlapping confidence between images. We quickly estimate the initial matching matrix, which first uses hierarchical K-means to cluster the track descriptors and then compute the similarity confidence of frame pairs by counting the number of potentially matched tracks that are clustered into the same leaf node. For acceleration, we only select long tracks that span 5 or more keyframes to estimate overlap confidence. In our experiments, for the “Desktop” sequence, the initial match matrix estimation only takes 1.08 seconds, with a total of 5, 935 selected feature tracks. Because we exclude track self-matching, the diagonal band of estimated match matrix has no value. Our method handles dense image sequences, unlike FAB-MAP that assumes sparsely sampled ones. When applying FAB-MAP to the original “Desktop” sequence, no loop is detected. So we manually sample the original sequence until common points between adjacent sampled frames are no more than 100. This generates 26 sampled frames. In the second step, with the initially estimated match matrix, we select the frame pairs with maximum overlapping confidence to perform feature matching, and update the match matrix iteratively. Matrix estimation and non-consecutive feature matching are benefitted from each other to simplify computation. Finally, we developed a new SfM system based on our findings and research outputs in feature management. Our method can be naturally extended to handle multiple sequences. Given one or multiple sequences, we first split long ones, making each new sequence generally contains only 1000-3001 frames. The split neighboring sequences can contain some overlapping frames for reliable matching. Then we apply our feature tracking to each segment , and estimate its 3D structure and camera motion using a keyframe-based incremental SfM scheme. The major novelty is that we use known intrinsic camera parameters, and simply select an initial frame pair that has sufficient matches and a large baseline to start SfM. For each sequence pair, we use the fast matching matrix estimation algorithm to estimate the rough match matrix such that related frames in any two different sequences can be found and common features can be matched. Then we use the segment-based SfM method to efficiently recover and globally register 3D points and camera trajectories. With the independently reconstructed sequences and matched common tracks, we align them in a unified 3D coordinate system. For a long loopback sequence, error accumulation could be serious, making traditional bundle adjustment stuck in local optimum. It is because the first a few iterations of bundle adjustment aggregate accumulation errors at the joint loop points, which are hard to be propagated to the whole sequence. To address this problem, we split each sequence into multiple segments - each is with a similarity transformation. Only these transformations and overlapping points across different segments are optimized. We name it segment-based bundle adjustment. To summarize this part, our method remarkably improves structure-from-motion regarding its practicality and theory. All objectives stated in the proposal have been achieved successfully with these new methods. Our established system is state-of-the-art in this community.

413113.label: Major findings and research outcome
413113.value: Our major finding and outcome are multifold. First, we proposed a fine-grained recognition system that incorporates part localization, alignment, and classification in one deep neural network. This is a nontrivial process, as the input to the classification module should be functions that enable back-propagation in constructing the solver. Our major contribution is to propose a valve linkage function (VLF) for back-propagation chaining and form our deep localization, alignment and classification (LAC) system. The VLF can adaptively compromise the errors of classification and alignment when training the LAC model. It in turn helps update localization. This work was presented in CVPR 2015. Second, for the multi-view stereo component, automatically computing high-quality dense depth information from captured images/videos is still quite difficult. We proposed in 3DV 2014 a novel semi-automatic multi-view stereo system, which can quickly create and repair depth from a monocular sequence taken by a freely moving camera. One contribution is a novel multiview stereo model incorporating prior constraints indicated by user interaction, which makes it possible to even handle Non-Lambertian surface that surely violates the photoconsistency constraint. Users only need to provide a coarse segmentation and a few user interactions, our system can automatically correct depth and refine boundary. Third, for automatic object finding, we proposed an object clique potential for semantic segmentation. Our object clique potential addresses the misclassified object-part issues arising in solutions based on fully-convolutional networks. Our object clique set, compared to that yielded from segment-proposal-based approaches, is with a significantly smaller size, making our method consume notably less computation. Regarding system design and model formation, our object clique potential can be regarded as a functional complement to local-appearance-based CRF models and works in synergy with these effective approaches for further performance improvement. This appears in ICCV’15. Further in CVPR 2016, aiming at simultaneous detection and segmentation (SDS), we proposed a proposal-free framework, which detect and segment object instances via mid-level patches. We design a unified trainable network on patches, which is followed by a fast and effective patch aggregation algorithm to infer object instances. Our method benefits from end-to-end training. Without object proposal generation, computation time can also be reduced. In experiments, our method yields results 62.1% and 61.8% in terms of mAPr on VOC2012 segmentation val and VOC2012 SDS val, which are stateof-the-art at the time of submission.

413113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
413113.value: The potential for further development is as follows. The parameters can be easily set in our system because most of them are not sensitive and use default values. The most important parameter controls the strength to mark outliers during feature tracking. The proposed two-pass matching works best if the scene can be represented by multiple planes. For a video sequence with dense frames, this condition can be generally achieved because image transformation between two consecutive frames is small for viable approximation by one or multiple homographies. We note even if the scene deviates from piecewise planarity, our second-pass matching still works as rectified images are close to the target ones. Our method may be not suitable for wide-baseline sparse images where the number of matches by first-pass matching is too small. Addressing this issue thus naturally becomes our further work. In addition, our ENFT method greatly helps SfM, and considers feature tracking on non-deforming objects by tradition. It will be developed to handle more dynamic objects. Although the proposed method is based on SIFT features, there is no limitation to use other representations for further acceleration. We will research along this line.

413113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
413113.value: Large-scale 3D reconstruction finds many practical applications. It primarily relies on structure-from-motion (SfM) algorithms to first estimate sparse 3D features and camera poses given the input of video or image collections. Compared to images, videos contain denser geometrical and structural information, and are the main source of SfM in the movie, video and commercial industry. A common strategy for video SfM estimation is by employing feature point tracking, which takes care of the temporal relationship among frames. We have presented a robust and efficient non-consecutive feature tracking (ENFT) method for robust structure-from-motion, which consists of two main steps, i.e., consecutive point tracking and non-consecutive track matching. Different from typical sequential matchers, e.g., KLT, we use invariant features and propose a two-pass matching strategy to significantly extend the track lifetime and reduce the feature sensitivity to noise and image distortion. The obtained tracks avail estimating a match matrix to detect disjointed subsequences with overlapping views. A new segment-based coarse-to-fine SfM estimation scheme is also introduced to effectively reduce accumulation error for long sequences. The presented ENFT-SFM system can handle tracking and registering large video datasets with limited memory consumption.

413213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
413213.value: With the advent of Web 2.0, social, location, and behavior data on the Internet resulting from mobile and social computing are expanding at a very rapid rate. These data are often characterized by their sparsity, heterogeneity, veracity, dynamism, velocity, and voluminosity, etc. Even though there is already a large body of research work on various big data issues, we will continue need novel ways to handle and process big data. Although the content of these social, location, and behavior data is an important source to extract valuable information and knowledge for researchers and industrialists, we are finding that the contextual information that are either explicitly or implicitly associated with these data are of paramount importance and have only been investigated with more fervor and rigor recently. In this proposal, we plan to investigate ways to process contextual social and behavior information by providing a theoretical framework and by designing practical learning algorithms that are capable of processing these big data. More specifically, our project will focus on developing factorization-based learning framework and tackle the following important issues: (1) to develop and to derive theoretical contextual high-order factorization-based learning models to extract the knowledge embedded in these data; (2) to provide scalable algorithms and convergence analysis of the algorithms for the proposed learning models; (3) to apply the proposed learning models and algorithms to recommendation in location-based social networks. 隨著Web 2.0的出現，在互聯網中的移動計算和社交計算下產生的社交、位置、和行為數據正在以極快的速度擴張。這些數據通常具有稀疏性、異質性、真偽性、動態性、快速性和海量性等。儘管目前已經有大量關於大數據相關的研究工作，我們仍需要新的方式來操作和處理大數據。 雖然這些社交，位置和行為數據的內容是一個重要的為研究者和企業家提取有價值的信息和知識的來源，但是我們發現，這些數據中顯式的或隱藏的情境信息極為重要，而且近年來被熱烈和嚴格的調研。 在這份項目書中，我們計劃通過提供理論框架和設計可用於大數據處理的實用學習算法調研處理社交和行為情境信息。具體而言，我們的項目將集中於開發基於分解的學習框架，並解決以下幾個重要問題：（1）制定和推導高階基於分解的學習模型，用於提取嵌在這些數據中的知識；（2）為提出的學習模型提供可擴展的算法和收斂性分析；（3）將提出的模型應用於具體的實際應用，如基於位置的社交網絡的推薦;等。 我們相信這項工作具有巨大的價值，不僅對香港很有利，其重大意義還影響任何在大數據世界中有興趣工作的人。

413213.label: Realisation of objectives
413213.value: We highlight a few key and major findings that help to realize our objectives to develop matrix factorization-based and other scalable machine learning approaches to unify social, location, and temporal information in recommender systems. In addition to the matrix factorization framework, we have also used other machine learning approaches, e.g., semi-supervised learning, game theoretic models, latent factor models, etc. in a wide range of applications such as multilingual information retrieval, crowdsourcing, community detection, feature selection, link recommendation, metric learning in distributed machine learning systems, etc. In a number of work, we have also provide detailed analysis of convergence rate, regret bound, etc. in order to demonstrate the performance of these proposed algorithms. In the following, we summarize a selected set of publications to illustrate how these work satisfy the proposed project objectives. Maximum margin semi-supervised learning with irrelevant data, Neural Networks 70 (2015) 90–102, Haiqin Yang, Kaizhu Huang, Irwin King, Michael R. Lyu. To tackle scalable contextual learning techniques, we have explored from the Semi-supervised learning (SSL) perspective, which is a typical learning paradigms training a model from both labeled and unlabeled data. One of the problems is that the unlabeled data may contain irrelevant data to the labeled data. To tackle this problem, we develop a maximum margin model, named tri-class support vector machine (3C-SVM), to utilize the available training data, while seeking a hyperplane for separating the targeted data well. Our 3C-SVM exhibits several characteristics and advantages. Budget constrained non-monotonic feature selection, Neural Networks 71 (2015) 214–224, Haiqin Yang, Zenglin Xu, Michael R. Lyu, Irwin King. Feature selection is an important problem in machine learning and data mining. We consider the problem of selecting features under the budget constraint on the feature subset size. Traditional feature selection methods suffer from the ‘‘monotonic’’ property. That is, if a feature is selected when the number of specified features is set, it will always be chosen when the number of specified feature is larger than the previous setting. This sacrifices the effectiveness of the non-monotonic feature selection methods. Hence, in this paper, we develop an algorithm for non-monotonic feature selection that approximates the related combinatorial optimization problem by a Multiple Kernel Learning (MKL) problem. Leveraging Social Connections to Improve Personalized Ranking for Collaborative Filtering. CIKM 2014: 261-270. Recommending products to users means estimating their preferences for certain items over others. This can be cast either as a problem of estimating the rating that each user will give to each item, or as a problem of estimating users’ relative preferences in the form of a ranking. Using social connections to better estimate users’ rankings of products is the task we consider in this paper. We develop a model, SBPR (Social Bayesian Personalized Ranking), based on the simple observation that users tend to assign higher ranks to items that their friends prefer. We perform experiments on four real-world recommendation data sets, and show that SBPR outperforms alternatives in ranking prediction both in warm- and cold-start settings. Exploiting Game Theoretic Analysis for Link Recommendation in Social Networks. We explore game theoretic approach for link recommendation in social networks. There are few works considering how to combine game theoretic analysis and machine learning models. Therefore, we study the problem of Exploiting Game Theoretic Analysis for Link Recommendation in Social Networks. Our goal is to improve link recommendation accuracy via leveraging the power of Network Formation Games into machine learning models. We present two different approaches to solve this problem. First, we propose a three- phase method that straightforwardly combines game theoretic analysis with machine learning models. Second, we develop a unified model, BPRLGT, that incorporates Network Formation Game into a Bayesian ranking framework for link recommendation. Improving Latent Factor Models via Personalized Feature Projection for One Class Recommendation. In this paper we propose a novel personalized feature projection method to model users’ preferences over items. Specifically, for each user, we define a personalized projection matrix, which takes the place of user-specific factors from existing mod- els. This matrix describes a mapping between items’ factors and users’ preferences in order to build personalized preference models for each user and item. The proposed personalized feature projection method is quite general and existing latent factor models, for example, can be cast as a special case. Probabilistic Matrix Factorization With Active Learning For Quality Assurance In Crowdsourcing Systems. Currently, quality assurance in crowdsourcing systems highly relies on redundancy of answers provided by multiple workers with varying expertise; however massive redundancy is very expensive and time-consuming. Active learning is a learning approach to achieve certain accuracy with a very low cost, and thus a number of previous works adopted active learning in crowdsourcing systems for quality assurance. However, previous works do not consider the varying expertise of workers for various task categories in real crowdsourcing scenarios. In our paper, we propose ActivePMF (Probabilistic Matrix Factorization with Active Learning) for TaskRec (a task recommendation framework) to learn a factor analysis model for quality assurance in crowdsourcing systems. Exploiting k-Degree Locality to Improve Overlapping Community Detection. Community detection is of crucial importance in understanding structures of complex networks. In many real-world networks, communities naturally overlap since a node usually has multiple community memberships. One popular technique to cope with overlapping community detection is Matrix Factorization (MF). However, existing MF- based models have ignored the fact that besides neighbors, “local non-neighbors” (e.g., my friend’s friend but not my direct friend) are helpful when discovering communities. In this paper, we pro- pose a Locality-based Non-negative Matrix Factorization (LNMF) model to refine a preference-based model by incorporating locality into learning objective. Distributed Information-Theoretic Metric Learning in Apache Spark. Distance metric learning (DML) is an effective similarity learning tool to learn a distance function from examples to enhance the model performance in applications of classification, regression, and ranking, etc. Most DML algorithms need to learn a Mahalanobis matrix, a positive semidefinite matrix that scales quadratically with the number of dimensions of input data. This brings huge computational cost in the learning procedure, and makes all proposed algorithms infeasible for extremely high-dimensional data even with the low-rank approximation. Differently, in this paper, we take advantage of the power of parallel computation and propose a novel distributed distance metric learning algorithm based on a state-of-the-art DML algorithm, Information-Theoretic Metric Learning (ITML). Fast Relative-Error Approximation Algorithm for Ridge Regression. Ridge regression is one of the most popular and effective regularized regression methods, and one case of particular interest is that the number of features p is much larger than the number of samples n, i.e. p >> n. In this paper, we propose a fast relative-error approximation algorithm for ridge regression.

413213.label: Major findings and research outcome
413213.value: Although factorization-based framework is quite effective in recommender systems, we have developed other machine learning approaches such as maximum margin semi-supervised learning, latent factor models, metric learning, game theoretic approach, etc. to handle scalable learning. Moreover, we have used different types of data, e.g., cross language corpuses, social network, community, crowdsourcing, etc. The significance of the proposed project lies in the development of new scalable machine learning algorithms to support better and more effective matrix factorization and other techniques that are being used not only in recommender systems but other applications. This theoretical part of the research provides guidance on performance analysis for algorithmic convergence, bounds, etc., while the practical part of the research work provide algorithms for more effective and efficient computation in a number of applications. These contributions to the technical community propels further research better theoretical as well as algorithm development for the future. 413713.label: Project Objectives
413713.value: To perform ground research in system level privacy loss metrics and full integration of constraint propagation in Distributed CP algorithms. The work is needed since modeling can affect privacy loss during the constraint solving process, and interacts most succinctly with constraint propagation to affect execution efficiency. To investigate the impact of modeling/design choices with respect to different measures of efficiency. In particular, we consider consistencies of constraints within an agent and those distributed over agents. We would also study the effect of the induced topology of the constraint network. To investigate efficient ways of incorporating (soft) global constraints into distributed constraint satisfaction and optimization algorithms. The main issue is effective and efficient algorithms for constraint propagation in terms of privacy loss, communication costs and network loadings.

413713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
413713.value: 約束規劃 (CP) 在很多工業應用和計算機科學中被成功應用，例如調度、配置、裝箱問題、運輸路徑、圖的佈局等問題。另一方面，在人工智能領域，多智能體模式出現的原來越頻繁，從而引起大家去解決分佈式計算環境下的問題的研究，但同時也帶來了新的挑戰。在這種情況下，無論是對滿足或者優化問題，分佈式約束編程是處於這兩種重要領域的交叉點。 現在我們要考慮的問題是如何建模，這是為了讓分佈式約束編程問題能在現實生活中廣泛的和有效的部署一定要解決的一個瓶頸。在集中約束規劃中，建模包括了確定問題的決策變量和表述關於這些變量的約束。制定一個能快速解決的的模型通常需要大量的經驗和專業知識。分佈式約束規劃的建模問題更為複雜在另外兩個方面：通信成本和隱私。在過去的十年中分佈式約束求解已經取得了很大的進步，但他們的重點主要在算法本質上。該項目的目的是填補分佈式約束編程建模空白。我們著重解決網絡拓撲結構對於用不同方式（保密性，計算能力，網絡負載）去衡量其效果時的影響，根據規格來模型自動生成，搜索和啟發式跟建模的相互作用，以及一些建模技巧。 我們的目標是給分佈式應用建模者一些實際指引。我們希望能夠（a）對在建模過程中的理論和出現的問題的更深度的認識及（b）發展新的軟件工程方法和技術去高效的建模和最終模型自動化生成。擬建項目對於把分佈式約束推理技術在實際中應用是很重要的第一步。此項目也將促進和加強香港和西班牙合作者之間的合作關係。

413713.label: Realisation of objectives
413713.value: In the following, our citations are based on Research Output in Part C of this report. To fulfill Objectives 2 & 3, we [C3] propose to maintain soft arc consistencies in each subproblem, so that variable assignments during search are also considered in consistency enforcement. As a result, we can explore more value pruning opportunities and thus further reduce the search space. Gutierrez and Meseguer introduce an extra copy of cost functions in each agent, so that search and consistency enforcement are done asynchronously. Our contribution goes further maintaining soft arc consistencies in each subproblem during search, so that (i) search and consistency enforcement are done asynchronously, introducing some extra copies of cost functions; (ii) the induced overhead caused by backtracking and undoing assignments and deletions is minimized. The asynchronicity requirement and different cost measurements require us to introduce novel techniques over those used in centralized CP. Experimentally, we show the benefits of our proposal on benchmarks usually unamenable to solvers without consistency. Distributed constraint solving are useful in tackling constrained problems when agents are not allowed to share his/her private information to others and/or gathering all necessary information to solve the problem in a centralized manner is infeasible. With these two limitations, distributed algorithms solve the problem by coordinating agents to negotiate with each other. However, once information is exchanged during negotiation, the private information may be leaked from one agent to another. To fulfill Objective 1, we [C2] propose and design a framework based on Valuation of Possible States (VPS) to evaluate how well a distributed algorithm preserves the totality of all private information on the entire system when solving distributed constraint optimization problems, by allowing the uses of different aggregators aggregating agents' individual privacy loss. Two classes of aggregators: idempotent aggregators and risk based aggregators are proposed. We further proposed generalized inference rules to infer privacy loss of individual agents. We implement our work on four distributed constraint solving algorithms: Synchronous Branch and Bound (SynchBB), Asynchronous Distributed Constraint Optimization (ADOPT), Branch and Bound ADOPT (BnB-ADOPT), and Distributed Pseudo-tree Optimization Procedure (DPOP). Preliminary experimental evaluations on two benchmarks, Distributed Multi-Event Scheduling Problem (DiMES) and Random Distributed COP, comparing the four algorithms are performed. Resolvent-based (Rslv) andMinimum conflict set (MCS) nogood learning are popular techniques to prune search space in distributed search. We observe that the nogoods generated by Rslv nogood learning may have redundant conflict value assignments, which are not needed. To fulfill Objectives 2 & 3, we [C1] propose two new techniques: Unique nogood First Resolvent-based (UFRslv) and Redundant conflict value assignment Free Resolvent-based (RFRslv) nogood learning. By removing conflict value assignments that are redundant, these two new nogood learning techniques can obtain shorter and more efficient nogoods than Rslv nogood learning, and consume less computation effort to generate nogoods than MCS nogood learning. We implement the new techniques in two modern distributed constraint satisfaction algorithms, nogood based asynchronous forward checking (AFCng) and dynamic ordering for asynchronous backtracking with nogood-triggered heuristic (ABT-DOng). Comparing against Rslv and MCS on random distributed constraint satisfaction problems and distributed Langford's problems, UFRslv and RFRslv are favourable in number of messages and NCCCSOs (nonconcurrent constraint checks and set operations) as metrics. In addition, we [C5] also investigate how to maintain and propagate nogoods recorded from restarts efficiently. It builds on reduced nld-nogoods introduced for restarts and increasing nogoods introduced for symmetry breaking. Our work shows that reduced nld-nogoods extracted from a single restart are in fact increasing, which can thus benefit from the efficient propagation algorithm of the incNGs global constraint BnB-ADOPT+ is a solving algorithm for Distributed Constraint Optimization Problems (DCOPs) that optimizes a global utility function composed of joint utilities of subsets of agents. Each agent executes a copy of the algorithm, which communicates with the other agents using three kinds of messages: VALUE, COST and TERMINATE. To fulfill Objectives 1 & 2, we [J1] consider the reduction in communication requirements of BnB-ADOPT+ (reducing the number of messages) made possible by not sending out every COST message. This lazy strategy sends out only those COST messages that satisfy some extra conditions (in contrast to the eager strategy of the original BnB-ADOPT+ that sends out a COST message as soon as some change has been produced). Interestingly, this lazy approach combines nicely with soft arc consistency maintenance, producing an algorithm that uses fewer messages than any of these approaches taken separately. Regarding ENCCCs, experimentally we observe a slight variation that does not harm performance. While most of search-based algorithms for optimal DCOP solving assume a single variable per agent, many DCOP instances could be more appropriately modeled with several variables per agent. There are several approaches to transform a DCOP instance with several variables per agent into another instance with one variable per agent, on which existing algorithms could be applied. To fulfill Objective 1 & 2, we [C7] present a hybrid approach by taking privacy loss into account that combines two of these transformations. Interestingly, our method can be connected with enforcing soft arc consistency during search, a technique that has been shown beneficial for search-based DCOP algorithms. Using BnB-ADOPT+ as the solving algorithm, preliminary experimental results on DCOP random instances indicate that this hybrid approach provides clear advantages over the two transformation approaches taken in isolation, and confirm also the benefits of soft arc consistency enforcement in this context. Outside of the objectives, we also address another important modelling issue/technique, which is symmetry breaking for pruning search space. Both dynamic and static symmetry breaking methods are considered. We [J2] propose a dynamic method, Recursive Symmetry Breaking During Search (ReSBDS), for efficient partial symmetry breaking. ReSBDS can break extra symmetry compositions, but is carefully designed to break only the ones that are easy to identify and inexpensive to break. We present theorems to guarantee the soundness and termination of our approach, and compare our method with popular static and dynamic methods. When the variable (value) heuristic is static, ReSBDS is also complete in eliminating all interchangeable variables (values) given only the generator symmetries. In [C4], we give the first formal characterization of the pruning behavior of ParSBDS and its improved variants. Introducing the notion of Dominance Completeness (DC-ness), we show that ParSBDS and variants eliminate the symmetry group of the given subset of symmetries if the resultant search tree is DC, and give an example scenario. Unfortunately, building a DC tree is not always possible. We propose two search heuristics with the aim of having more nodes dominated and thus also pruned during search. In terms of static symmetry breaking, we propose a new total ordering, reflex, as basis of a new symmetry breaking constraint that collaborates well among themselves as well as with Precedence constraints, thereby breaking more composition symmetries in partial symmetry breaking. An efficient GAC filtering algorithm is presented for the reflex ordering constraint. We propose the ReflexLeader method, which is a variant of LexLeader using the reflex ordering instead, and give conditions when ReflexLeader is safe to combine with the Precedence and multiset ordering constraints.
