413713.label: Major findings and research outcome
413713.value: The project produces 2 journal, 6 conference and 1 workshop papers, the majority of which appear in top venues in the area of Constraint Programming and Artificial Intelligence, including IJCAI, AAAI, AAMAS and CP. 2 MPhil and 1 PhD students are also trained via the topics in the project. As such, our research group is recognized as one of the leaders in the modeling research in the area. Conference publications C2 and C3 were published before the project commencement date. In the updated proposal submitted to RGC in April/May, 2013, I have already declared that work had already commenced right after original proposal submission and some related research findings would have been published in the upcoming conferences before project start date. Referring to Section 5.3, the major findings include the following. First, we adopt and adapt techniques from Weighted Constraint Satisfaction to help design the consistency enforcement algorithms in the BnB-ADOPT+ search method, which results in drastic reduction in search space and significant increase in solving efficiency. We also propose an effective lazy messaging strategy by not sending out every COST message. The method combines nicely with soft arc consistency maintenance, producing an algorithm that uses fewer messages than any of these approaches taken separately. Second, we also came up with a privacy loss framework based on Valuation of Possible States (VPS) to evaluate how well a distributed algorithm preserves the totality of all private information on the entire system when solving distributed constraint optimization problems, by allowing the uses of different aggregators aggregating agents’ individual privacy loss. Third, we came up with ways of utilizing nogoods in speeding up the ABT, AFC and restart-based families of search algorithms. Fourth, we also investigate the privacy and efficiency issues of multiple variables per agent, and present a hybrid approach by taking privacy loss into account that combines two of possible transformations of several variables per agent into another instance with only one variable per agent. Interestingly, our method can be connected with enforcing soft arc consistency during search, a technique that has been shown beneficial for search-based DCOP algorithms. Fifth, we also show how to break more composition symmetries in dynamic methods and introduce a new total order for a better static symmetry breaking method.

413713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
413713.value: The project has helped to identify the major research issues of modeling in distributed constraint satisfaction and optimization. Our results have also built the ground work on consistency enforcement algorithms, privacy loss, modeling multiple variables per agent, efficient use of nogoods and symmetry breaking for additional research. Each direction contains myriad of opportunities for further work.

413713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
413713.value: Constraint Programming (CP) finds success in many walks of industrial applications and computer science, such as scheduling, configuration, bin packing, transport routing, diagram layout, just to name a few. On the other hand, the multi-agents paradigm has firmly emerged in recent years in the Artificial Intelligence community, giving rise to distributed problem solving but also posing new challenges in a distributed computing environment. In this context, Distributed Constraint Programming, be it satisfaction or optimization, finds its crossroad at the intersection of these two important endeavours. The problem at hand is that of "modeling", which is a bottleneck that must be tackled before distributed constraint programming problems can be widely and effectively deployed in real-life applications. The results of the project identify important research issues in effective model transformation, privacy preservation/loss and efficient solving algorithms, and provide ground results for further work in this important area.

413813.label: Project Objectives
413813.value: [Exploiting parallelism to achieve high read performance]: We plan to formulate a deduplication-aware chunk placement problem. That is, by carefully distributing deduplicated chunks across different storage nodes, we aim to minimize the reading time of each deduplicated file. [Adapting deduplication to workload heterogeneity]: We plan to design deduplication mechanisms that are adaptive to heterogeneous workloads, while providing read/write performance guarantees. [Data availability and recovery with erasure codes]: We provide fault tolerance for metadata and deduplicated data using erasure codes, with redundancy based on the number of shares of each chunk. 413813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
413813.value: We are living in an information age that is overwhelmed by massive data. It is thus paramount to develop scalable and reliable storage technologies to store an ever-increasing scale of data information. We explore a well-known technique called deduplication to eliminate the storage of redundant data and reduce the operational cost of storage management. To make deduplication widely applicable, we must provide both performance and dependability guarantees. Specifically, the performance requirements include high read/write performance, high storage efficiency, and low memory usage; and the dependability requirements include consistency between metadata and data, availability and recovery in the presence of failures, and security in the presence of attacks. Furthermore, deduplication technologies must be deployable with low-cost commodity hardware configurations that are available to general users, so as to minimize the operational cost of storage management. In this research, we propose to design and implement novel deduplication methodologies on a large-scale, distributed cloud file system, with an objective of providing both performance and dependability guarantees. Specifically, we propose a technique called reverse deduplication, whose key idea is to shift the fragmentation to old data while maintaining the sequential layout of the latest data. Our preliminary studies demonstrate the performance effectiveness of reverse deduplication using real-world virtual machine image workload. Using reverse deduplication as a building block, we propose to conduct extensive performance and dependability studies on how to feasibly enable deduplication in cloud file systems, subject to the limited resource constraints of commodity hardware configurations. Our ultimate goal is to identify new design principles for deduplication, supported with realistic prototype implementation and extensive experiments. The contribution of this research will provide practical deduplication methodologies for organizations to reduce the operational cost of managing massive data in a scalable and reliable manner. Our research also addresses the challenges of putting deduplication in wide deployment using low-cost commodity hardware configurations. We have sought indication of interest of collaboration in this project from both academia and industry such as University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) and Huawei Technologies. 我們生活在一個被海量數據淹沒的信息時代，因此開發可擴展和可靠的存儲技術便為重要。在此項目中，我們探討重複數據刪除，以消除冗餘數據的存儲，從而降低存儲管理的營運成本。為了使重複數據刪除技術廣泛適用，我們必須同時提供性能和可靠性保證。具體而言，對性能的要求包括高讀/寫性能，存儲效率高，和低內存佔用; 可靠性要求包括數據的一致性，出現故障的情況下的可用性和恢復能力，與抵抗安全攻擊。此外，重複數據刪除技術必須能應用在低成本的商品硬件配置上，以盡量減少存儲管理的營運成本。 我們提出在這項研究中，為大型分佈式雲文件系統設計和實現新穎的重複數據刪除方法，並同時提供性能和可靠性保證。具體來說，我們提出反向重複數據刪除技術，其關鍵思想是把碎片問題轉移到舊的數據，而保持最新數據的連續性。我們的初步研究顯示，在真實虛擬機映像數據上，反向重複數據刪除能達到性能效益。利用反向重複數據刪除技術作為基礎，我們建議進行廣泛的性能和可靠性研究，就如何切實在有限的資源商品硬件配置下，啟用重複數據刪除雲文件系統。

413813.label: Realisation of objectives
413813.value: (i) Objective 1 [Exploiting parallelism to achieve high read performance]: We identify the problem that deduplication inevitably leads to unbalanced data placement across storage nodes, thereby degrading read performance. We formulate a combinatorial optimization problem, and propose a greedy, polynomial-time Even Data Placement (EDP) algorithm, which identifies a deduplication-aware data placement that effectively achieves read balance while maintaining storage balance. We evaluate the EDP algorithm through extensive evaluations and testbed experiments. Our findings are published at IEEE IWQoS’15 (acceptance rate = 22/89 = 22.5%), a premier conference in QoS research. (ii) Objective 2 [Adapting deduplication to workload heterogeneity]: We extend our work on RevDedup (previously published as a workshop paper at APSys) to provide a complete deduplication solution that differentiates hot and cold data. Our observation is that hot (cold) data tends to be read more (less) frequently. Our RevDedup system carefully combines the inline and out-of-line deduplication approaches, such that the read performance of hot data is maintained, while the storage efficiency is maintained by deduplicating the cold data. We conduct extensive testbed experiments on real traces. Our findings are published at ACM Transaction on Storage (TOS) in 2015. Note that TOS is the most prestigious journal in storage systems research. We further demonstrate how to exploit workload similarity to mitigate the encryption key generation overhead in our previously proposed rekeying-aware deduplication storage system, while preserving deduplication effectiveness in storage savings. Our findings are published at ACM Transaction on Storage (TOS) in 2017. (iii) Objective 3 [Data availability and recovery with erasure codes]: Our Even Data Placement (EDP) algorithm (see above) is formulated in erasure-coding-based setting. Thus, we maintain fault tolerance when we perform deduplication-aware placement under EDP. The detailed formulation is in our IEEE IWQoS’15 paper. We further conduct an in-depth simulation-based analysis to evaluate how the storage reliability is affected due to deduplication. We show that deduplication consistently reduces the damage of sector errors due to intra-file redundancy elimination, but potentially increases the damages of whole-disk failures if the highly referenced chunks are not carefully placed on disk. We also propose a deliberate copy technique to improve storage reliability. Our findings are published at IEEE IISWC 2016 (acceptance rate = 21/69 = 30.4%) and IEEE Transactions on Computers. (iv) Objective 4 [Security for deduplication]: We propose a new secret sharing scheme called Convergent Dispersal, which carefully combines deduplication, fault tolerance, and security in a unified design. The idea is to augment the existing secret sharing schemes by replacing the random key with a deterministic cryptographic hash that is derived from the message itself. Thus, the secret shares of identical messages are still identical, thereby allowing deduplication. Our findings are published as a workshop paper at USENIX HotStorage 2014 (acceptance rate = 15/57 = 26.3%), a full paper at USENIX ATC 2015 (acceptance rate = 47/221 = 21.3%), and a magazine paper at Internet Computing 2016. Note that USENIX ATC is a prestigious conference in computing systems research. Since enterprises and individuals increasingly outsource their data management to cloud storage, it is critical to provide security guarantees for cloud storage. We study the security issues in cloud storage that deploys encrypted deduplication, which combines encryption and deduplication in a seamless manner to achieve both data confidentiality while preserving storage efficiency. We design and implement REED, in which we support rekeying and dynamic access control in encrypted deduplication storage using a variant of the all-of-nothing transform primitive. The findings are published as a conference paper at IEEE/IFIP DSN 2016 (acceptance rate = 58/259 = 22.4%) and as a journal paper at TOS 2017. Furthermore, we identify new inference attacks that cause information leakage in state-of-the-art encrypted deduplication systems by carefully adapting the classical frequency analysis attack and provide insights into designing leakage-resistant mechanisms for encrypted deduplication. Our work is published at IEEE/IFIP DSN 2017 (acceptance rate = 49/220 = 22.3%). Note that this work is one of the three nominations for the Best Paper Award at IEEE/IFIP DSN 2017.

[Security for deduplication]: We identify new threat models and propose security mechanisms for a deduplication-based cloud file system, while ensuring that the performance overhead incurred by the proposed security mechanisms is minimal.

413813.label: Major findings and research outcome
413813.value: We explore several areas of research to improve the current deduplication storage design with better performance and dependability guarantees. (I) Read performance of deduplication storage Inline deduplication storage generally suffers from low read performance due to chunk fragmentation. We propose RevDedup [TOS 2015], which carefully takes into account workload properties and combines the inline and out-of-line deduplication approaches, such that the read performance of hot data is maintained, while the storage efficiency is maintained by deliberately deduplicating the cold data. Extensive testbed experiments show that RevDedup achieve both high read and high write performance. (II) Reliability in deduplication storage We study the reliability issues of deduplication storage. We propose EDP [IWQoS 2015], which evenly balance the data layout of erasure-coding-based deduplication storage to maintain load balancing. In addition, we present an in-depth simulation analysis to accurately quantify the reliability impact when deduplication is deployed [IISWC 2016, TC]. We show that deduplication consistently reduces the damage of sector errors due to intra-file redundancy elimination, but potentially increases the damages of whole-disk failures if the highly referenced chunks are not carefully placed on disk. We also propose a deliberate copy technique to improve storage reliability. (III) Security in deduplication storage We present several secure deduplication storage systems to provide security guarantees for deduplication storage. First, we present CDStore [HotStorage 2014, USENIX ATC 2015, Internet Computing 2016], which builds on a novel design called convergent dispersal that augments the existing secret sharing schemes with the deduplication capability. Second, we present REED [DSN 2016, TOS 2017], in which we support rekeying and dynamic access control in encrypted deduplication storage using a variant of the all-of-nothing transform primitive. Finally, we identify new inference attacks that cause information leakage in state-of-the-art encrypted deduplication systems by carefully adapting the classical frequency analysis attack and provide insights into designing leakage-resistant mechanisms for encrypted deduplication [DSN 2017].

413813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
413813.value: We believe that deduplication will be widely deployed in outsourced storage for high storage efficiency. How to provide security guarantees for deduplication storage becomes a critical issue. Existing studies in the literature have limited investigation on deduplication-based outsourced storage. Our recent work at DSN 2017 shows that existing secure deduplication designs are vulnerable to frequency analysis. Future work includes: (i) an in-depth study of how advanced inference attacks can compromise deduplication storage, (ii) a design of secure deduplication storage system that is provably secure against inference attacks, (ii) a prototype implementation of secure storage systems with performance guarantees.

413813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
413813.value: Deduplication is a well-known compression technique that can effectively eliminate content-level redundancy and hence achieve high storage efficiency. We explore several areas of research to enable efficient deployment of deduplication storage with performance and dependability guarantees. Our research specifically addresses three aspects of deduplication storage: read performance, reliability, and security. Our results will enable storage system practitioners to effectively deploy deduplication and understand the design trade-offs among performance, dependability, and storage efficiency achieved by deduplication. Our findings have been published in prestigious conference and journals.

414113.label: Project Title(Chinese)
414113.value: 基於主導極點追踪和取消的快速瞬態低壓差穩壓器之發展

414113.label: Project Objectives
414113.value: To investigate the generation of a non-tracking and controllable low-frequency zero for the pole-zero cancellation with the dominant pole in low-dropout regulator. To investigate and develop a low-frequency zero which is able to track the dominant pole in most of the loading conditions. To develop a fast transient low-dropout regulator with the proposed dominant-pole tracking and cancellation technique.

To investigate and develop a low-frequency zero which is able to track the dominant pole in most of the loading conditions.
To develop a fast transient low-dropout regulator with the proposed dominant-pole tracking and cancellation technique.

414113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
414113.value: Low-dropout regulator (LDO) is a well-accepted power-supply circuit for both analogue and RF modules in IC systems since it is an accurate, ripple-free and low-noise power regulator. Transient errors of a LDO such as overshoots and undershoots under rapid changes of loading and supply conditions should be minimized. In order to improve the transient performance of LDO, in the past decade, the research works on LDO were mainly focused on the internal feedback stability and the feedback loop bandwidth since a wider loop bandwidth results in faster transient response, as well as less transient errors on the regulated voltage. In the typical LDO design, a large off-chip capacitor at the output of LDO is used to achieve good stability by dominant-pole frequency compensation. Although this large off-chip capacitor does help to maintain the voltage regulation under rapid line and load transient changes, the dominant pole is always located at very low frequency. The loop bandwidth, which is controlled by the dominant pole, is always limited, and it cannot be extended substantially even though more power is applied to the internal circuits. This situation disables further enhancement on the transient response. In order to retain the advantages of using the large off-chip capacitor and obtain a substantial extension of the loop bandwidth simultaneously, this project aims at developing a dominant-pole tracking and cancellation technique for LDO. The ultimate goal of this project is to substantially improve the transient response of LDO by the proposed idea and to prove the proposed concept by experimental results. Moreover, since the location of the dominant pole is load-dependent, the development of the dominant-pole tracking method in different loading conditions is the main focus and key challenge of this project. 低壓差穩壓器 (LDO) 是一種準確、無紋波和低雜訊的電源穩壓器，所以被廣泛使用於集成電路的模擬及射頻模塊上的供電電路。LDO的瞬態誤差，如負載及電源狀況快速變化下造成的過衝及欠衝等，應盡量被減少。為了提高LDO的瞬態性能，在過去的十年中，研究工作主要集中於內部反饋的穩定性及反饋迴路的頻寛，因為更寛的迴路頻寛能促使更快之瞬態反應，以及穩定電壓上更少的瞬態誤差。 在典型的LDO設計中，於LDO的輸出端的設置一枚較大的外置電容有助利用主導極點頻率補償來達到良好的穩定性。雖然這枚大的外置電容確實有助於保持快速電壓及負壓瞬態改變下的電壓調節，但主導極點始終位於非常低的頻率。因為迴路頻寛是由主導極點所控制，所以迴路頻寛會被限制，即使內部電路耗電更多亦不能令其大幅伸延。 為了保留大外置電容的優點，同時獲取迴路頻寛的大幅伸延，這項目旨在發展用於LDO之主導極點追踪和取消技術。這個項目的最終目標是利用提出的技術大幅提高LDO的瞬態響應，和利用實驗結果來證明提出的概念。此外，由於主導極點會因負載而改變，在不同負載條件下的主導極點追踪方法將會是此項目的主要焦點及關鍵挑戰。

414113.label: Realisation of objectives
414113.value: The project has been successfully completed. All objectives have been achieved. Several structures of low-dropout regulator to improve transient response have been developed. The proposed structures have been investigated and the impacts towards the transient response have been studied as well. During the development of the proposed low-dropout regulators, several required circuit techniques and structures have been investigated, optimized and developed. They are 1. A CMOS low-dropout regulator with dominant-pole substitution –To extend the loop bandwidth of a low-dropout regulator for faster transient response, the dominant pole is cancelled by a low-frequency zero. This low-frequency zero is created by the proposed current multiplier circuit which is embedded into error amplifier. The feedback control loop is thus modulated. The experimental results show the improvement. This work has been reported in IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics. 2. Fast error amplifier designs with proposed signal- and transient-current boosting technique – To enhance the small- and large-signal responses of the error amplifier for low-dropout regulator, a circuit structure called signal- and transient-current boosting (STCB) has been developed. The preliminary version of STCB has been published in IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems I. An improved version which has a much simpler circuit structure then has been proposed and reported in IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits. 3. Application of STCB to two-stage design – With the success of STCB development, two two-stage structures have been developed to improve classical Miller compensation. The works have been reported in IEEE Transactions on VLSI and International Journal of Circuit Theory and Applications. 4. Other structures of low-dropout regulator – There are several regulators developed and they have been reported in some journals and conferences. After completed the project, it is found that a dominant-pole cancelled low-dropout regulator, which is one of the developed regulators, is sufficient to improve the transient response. The tracking idea provides minor improvement.

414113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
414113.value: A potential area of development is to investigate the possibility to apply the low-frequency zero for the compensation in switch-mode regulator design. However, in this case, multiple zeros are needed to cancel the complex poles in the feedback.

414113.value: In this project, a more reliable power-supply circuit has been developed. The developed circuits reduce the overall cost and size of future electronic devices significantly. The outcome of this project would provide impact to the future portable devices.

414313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
414313.value: Transportation is one of the industrial sectors most impacted by global climate change. Governments are recognising the urgency of development of transport policies for sustainability. In this project, we would like to explore the design and planning of urban transit alternatives that capitalise on electric cars and other environmentally-sustainable transport technologies now available. With zero tail pipe emissions, electric vehicles can significantly reduce city air pollution and create a greener environment. The challenge in the wide-spread adoption of electric vehicles is the availability of re-charging stations and the re-charging time. On-demand public transit has also gained popularity in many cities. On-demand public transit combines the servicing of customers with similar routes in the same vehicle. Each passenger still gets point-to-point service with only short detours incurred. Unlike traditional buses with fixed routes and schedules, on-demand transit vehicles go into service only when requested, and thus do not waste time and fuel when driven with no passengers. Hence, on-demand public transit is an eco-friendly and efficient form of transportation. In this project, we investigate the impact of the use of electric vehicles on route planning and operations of on-demand transit systems. The Dial-a-Ride Problem (DARP) consists of designing vehicle routes and schedules for users who specify pick-up and drop-off requests between origins and destinations. We have made some preliminary study of a variant of the static Dial-a-Ride problem using electric vehicles (DARPEV), which aims to minimize the total vehicle-distance travelled subject to meeting all advanced customers' requests, and constraints on vehicle capacity, pickup/ delivery time-window, customer ride-time and battery-charging restrictions. Using electric vehicles limits the vehicle travel time between battery recharges. With restricted charging locations, and the requirement that charging must be done with no customers "in-service", the battery-charging constraints significantly complicate the problem. Our preliminary investigations indicate that even very small problems (with only a few vehicles of small capacity and dozens of passengers) are already beyond the capabilities of off-the-shelf software for mixed integer programs. In this project, we will investigate model and algorithm development for static and dynamic variants of DARPEV, to enable on-line operations of realistic scale for on-demand transit. We will also investigate robust solution approaches for the stochastic DARPEV. The insights obtained in studying these DARP variants would help to build an integrated planning model for location of charging stations and on-demand transit request management. 全球氣候變化與運輸交通息息相關，各國政府都意識到可持續發展的交通政策的迫切性。 本研究探索如何設計一個以電動汽車和其他環保運輸技術運作的公共交通系統。 電動汽車可以減少城市空氣污染，有助於環保，但由於電池運行時間有限和充電站網絡不完整, 電動汽車尚未普及。另一方面， 一些城市已經試圖引入按需公共交通系統 --- 為預約客戶提供點對點服務，但把時間和路程相近的乘客以同一車輛運載。相對於傳統的公交車，按需系統沒有固定的航線和時間表，沒有乘客時不操作，不會浪費時間和燃料，因此是一個環保和高效的運輸模式。 按需運載系統也被稱為電召問題（Dial-A-Ride Problem）。據我們初步的研究，使用電動車輛的電召問題（DARP-ElectricVehicles）相比上顯著更複雜。基於車輛容量約束，啟程/交付時間窗口，客戶乘坐時間和電池運作時間限制，充電地點和充電時間的局限性，和其他服務的要求，即使是只有幾輛車和數十名乘客的小問題，已經超越現有混合整數規劃軟件的能力。 我們將研究DARPEV的靜態和動態模型及求解算法，並且探討隨機DARPEV模型的穩健解決方案。這個研究得到的見解，將有助建立按需公交系統之綜合規劃和管理模型。

414313.label: Realisation of objectives
414313.value: To achieve the project objectives, we first conducted a comprehensive literature survey on dial-a-ride problems. This gave us a good background as to the effectiveness of the various methodologies. The literature survey has been published in Transportation Research Part B: Methodological. We then developed models and algorithms for the static and dynamic dial-a-ride problems with electric vehicles. This required the adaptation of the models and methods for solving vehicle routing problems. A mixed-integer linear programming model was proposed. This model incorporates realistic problem features, including users' requests, time windows, vehicle capacity, energy consumption, battery capacity, and max ride time. A tabu search heuristic was developed to solve the problem. Compared with an exact method branch-and-cut algorithm implemented by a state-of-the-art optimization solver CPLEX, the performance of the tabu search approach was satisfactory but required significantly less computational time. We refer to Chapter 2 of the attached Ph.D. thesis for the details of the model and algorithm. To investigate the stochastic nature of public transit systems, we collaborated with a major local public transit company and utilized their data regarding the network infrastructure and transportation activities for modeling. An optimization was developed for real-time re-scheduling and a simulation model of the public transit network, where vehicle travel times were stochastic, was developed for performance evaluation. The optimization model was solved in the dynamic environment of the simulation model, and the benefits of re-optimization were evaluated. Robustness of the solution approaches was examined. The findings have been published in Transportmetrica B: Transport Dynamics and presented at two international conferences. The planning of locations of electric vehicle charging stations requires the understanding of the users' demands. We incorporated spatial factors into classic location models and derived insights into the selection of those locations. The findings have been published in Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies. We also conducted other relevant research studies, including location model development, competition in public transit services, and passengers' travel recommendation systems. The findings have been presented at international conferences and published in the respective conference proceedings.

414313.label: Major findings and research outcome
414313.value: We reviewed 86 papers on dial-a-ride problems published in the period of 2007 - 2017. We found that static and deterministic problems are the most popular, where little research has been done on dynamic or stochastic problems. There is a need to address these problems for practical purposes. Trends and research gaps such as green transportation, disruption management, staffing issues, and competition between on-demand transportation service providers were identified. We then developed a mixed-integer linear programming model DARPEV, with realistic features such as users' requests, time windows, vehicle capacity, energy consumption, battery capacity, and max ride time. We developed a Tabu Search algorithm for solving the optimization problem. Its performance was comparable to a branch-and-cut approach implemented by a state-of-the-art optimization solver CPLEX, but its solution time was much shorter. For real-time implementation, solution time is crucial and therefore the heuristic approach is recommended. We also considered dynamic and stochastic public transit systems. We collaborated with a major local public transit company and utilized the data regarding their network infrastructure and transportation activities for our studies. We developed an optimization model for integrated vehicle and driver scheduling. A simulation model based on their transit network, which captures also travel time uncertainty, was developed. The optimization model was solved to guide decisions in the dynamic environment of the simulation model. The optimization frequency could be adjusted for more/less responsive rescheduling. We found that our re-optimization approach could lead to better performance, such as gains in revenues, higher service coverage, and reduced drivers' overtime. Solution times were in seconds such that near real-time implementation is possible. We also studied an electric vehicle charging location problem and considered users' demands in the location models. Three classic location models -- the set covering model, the maximal covering location model, and the p-median model -- were studied. We found that p-median model was more effective among the three in the sense that its suggested charging stations are more accessible to points with higher demands. The solutions of p-median models are relatively robust when the number of charging stations increases incrementally. The major findings have been published in three key journals in transportation, two of which were leading journals in the field: Transportation Research Part B & C. The Ph.D. dissertation, titled "Metaheuristics for Solving Variants of Vehicle Routing Problems," presents parts of the findings. We also conducted other relevant research studies, including location model development, competition in public transit services, and passengers' travel recommendation systems. The findings have been presented at international conferences and published in the respective conference proceedings.

414313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
414313.value: In recent years, the numbers of users and vehicles in on-demand public transportation systems have increased significantly. The problem size of such decision-making problem is also expected to grow exponentially. There is a need to develop much faster computational algorithms for deriving solutions for real-time implementation. Meta-heuristics can be explored or tailor-made for speeding up the computations. Another possible research direction is that the DARPEV model we developed considers only a single service provider but, in reality, there can be multiple public and private operators. Their competition or collaboration will change their individual dispatch decisions. A game theory approach may be suitable to address the problem. Finally, the emerging technology of autonomous vehicles is a hot topic nowadays. Its impact on future public transportation systems will also be an interesting research area to investigate.

414313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
414313.value: In this project, we studied the design and planning of on-demand transit systems enabled by electric vehicles. We developed mathematical models which incorporate features of the operations of electric vehicles, such as constraints on battery capacity and battery charging requirements. A heuristic method was developed to solve the optimization problem. Our computational results show that the performance of this heuristic approach was comparable to an exact algorithm implemented by a state-of-the-art optimization solver but required significantly less computational time. We also collaborated with a major local public transit company and utilized their data regarding their network infrastructure and transportation activities for developing models. An optimization was developed for integrated vehicle and driver scheduling. A simulation model based on the real network and travel data was developed for evaluating the performance of our approach. The optimization model was solved to guide re-scheduling decisions in a dynamic environment. Our computational experiments demonstrate the benefits of our approach, including gains in revenues, higher service coverage, and reduced drivers' overtime. We also incorporated spatial factors into location models for the selection of electric vehicle charging stations. A comparative study of three classic models for the location problems was conducted.

414413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
414413.value: Deciphering gene regulation is a core research topic of computational biology and biomedical sciences with direct impact on life understanding, bio-engineering and medical applications. It is costly to determine high-resolution 3D structures of the regulatory protein-DNA interactions, namely Transcription Factor (TF) and Transcription Factor Binding Site (TFBS) bindings. From abundant binding sequences available, we have opened up a new direction of discovering associated TF-TFBS patterns, many of which are highly predictive binding rules and verified as binding cores according to the expensive 3D structures and Protein Binding Microarrays (PBM) results. In this proposal, we further formulate the novel and inexpensive methodology to discover more underlying rules of TF-TFBS bindings, and more importantly, validate it with in vitro experiments and develop high impact Bioinformatics applications. The four main tasks are as follows: (1). Formalized associated TF-TFBS pattern discovery will be incorporated directly with subtype analysis on high-throughput data as a framework, to discover general binding rules and regulatory mechanisms. We have studied residue varying subtypes which suggest intriguing biological meanings, and have been developing quantitative models to effectively shortlist associated patterns which are verifiable binding cores as shown in our initial results. (2). Protein-DNA (TF-TFBS) binding energy modeling is critical for docking and homology modeling. Generalized associated TF-TFBS binding rules will be employed to enrich the information beyond 3D structures for the energy model optimization. (3). Advanced gene regulatory network (GRN) inference modeling, such as time-delayed causality, will be enabled by incorporating the TF-TFBS patterns as well as other information to alleviate the problem caused by limited samples such as expression time series. (4). To complement available high-throughput data, in vitro experiments will be performed to validate the computational predictions for cases important to diseases and human. The project has high impact in bioinformatics research of protein-DNA interactions, high relevance and potentially significant contributions to biomedical applications and new biological insights. 破譯基因調控一直是計算生物學和生物醫學科學的核心研究課題，這直接影響對生命的理解，促進生物工程和醫療應用計算生物學的發展。可是，透過高分辨率實驗去確定調節蛋白質與基因的相互作用之三維結構，即轉錄因子（TF）和轉錄因子結合位點（TFBS）綁定，成本高昂。從大量已有的結合序列數據，我們已經為相關轉錄因子與轉錄因子(TF – TFBS)模式發現問題開闢了新的方向。在我們所發現相關轉錄因子與轉錄因子模式中，有許多規則具有高度預測能力，有部份模式更能由三維結構及蛋白質結合微陣列（PBM）的結果獲得證實。 在此計劃書中，我們進一步制定創新的和廉價的方法去發現更多轉錄因子與轉錄因子綁定規則，並透過試管實驗中進行驗證，從而開發具影響力的生物信息學應用程式。四項主要任務如下： （1）形式化相關轉錄因子與轉錄因子模式發現方法將被納入在高通量定序技術數據的亞型分析框架，以發現普遍綁定規則和基因調控機制。我們先前研究了能產生多款殘留物的亞型，提供了令人感興趣的生物學意義。我們也建立了量化模型去揀出相關的可結合核心模式。據我們的初步驗證結果顯示，模型能有效地揀出相關的可結合核心模式。（2）蛋白質與基因, 即轉錄因子與轉錄因子, 結合能量建模在對接和同源建模極之重要。歸納相關轉錄因子與轉錄因子綁定規則將提供比三維結構更豐富的信息，更能用於解決能量模型優化問題上。（3） 利用先進的基因調控網絡（ GRN ）推理模型，如時間延遲因果關係模型，將轉錄因子與轉錄因子模式以及其他相關信息，突破樣本不足的限制。（4） 為了彌補高通量定序技術的數據的不足，重要的人類疾病將有體外實驗中去驗證計算預測。 這專案對生物資訊學研究的蛋白質與基因之間的相互作用、 高相關性和生物醫學的應用程式和新的生物見解潛在着重大貢獻。

414413.label: Realisation of objectives
414413.value: The revised project objectives have been fully achieved. This project helps our group to gain significant experience in TF-TFBS pattern analyses. The results have been published in refereed international conferences and prestigious journals. During the presentation of the papers (C1-C5) in the conference, we acknowledged this grant which supports our research. The three project objectives have already been achieved to 100%. The details are as follows: (1). To formalize associated TF-TFBS pattern discovery into generalized rules and binding mechanisms, and to study various subtypes using high-throughput data In order to achieve the first objective, we proposed novel association rule mining approach, statistical clustering approach, and random forest approach [C2, J1, J2, J13]. On the algorithmic aspect, we developed a new model to represent Protein-DNA binding known as Protein DNA Co-Occurring Aligned Pattern Clusters (APCs), which are more compact than one-to-one pattern associations but detailed enough to allow site-specific variants. The flexibility comes from the capability to include gaps and wildcards in the pattern representations. We also developed an efficient algorithm to quantitatively discover Protein-DNA Co-Occurring APCs from Protein-DNA binding sequences. We have defined Co-Support Measure and Forward-Confidence Measure to order a set of Protein-DNA Co-Occurring APCs. On the biological aspect, we discovered two new Protein-DNA binding cores supported by homology modeling, which validates our predictions in 3D structures. When the score is low, the tool will then apply homology modeling to find their close matches in PDB to attain new chemically feasible binding cores. In term of computational performance, our algorithm obtains binding cores with higher precision using much shorter runtime (about 1,600x faster) than that of its contemporaries, discovering candidates that do not co-occur as one-to-one associated patterns in the raw data. Later, an improved binding affinity prediction method was developed by adding the information from low-quality structural and interaction data with the help from random forest [J6, J9]. Our experiments showed that machine learning-based scoring functions are remarkably more accurate than empirical scoring functions because machine learning-based scoring functions can assimilate data better. In order to establish quantitative models, the input data needed to be normalized so as to retain the important biological relevant signals in the data set. Therefore, novel normalization methods were proposed [J10]. (2). To apply the associated TF-TFBS (protein-DNA) binding rules on energy modeling in computational docking In this objective, we applied the enhanced models obtained in objective 1. We integrated the enhanced models into two downstream applications. Our system attempts to optimize candidate ligands in accordance with click chemistry and thus ensures chemical synthesizability. To achieve this, novel genetic operators were introduced so as to preserve some drug-like properties. The applications include anti-cancer drug identification and novel inhibitors at the CDK2 [J3, J4]. Another study on colorectal carcinoma also led us to the discovery of the inhibiting effect of adapalene on the activity of cyclin-dependent kinase 2 [J7]. At the same time, our existing drug discovery platform has been extended and enhanced [C5, C1, C3, J8]. Another drug was discovered for bladder carcinoma [J11]. Furthermore, repurposing of indacaterol and canagliflozin can also treat EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors-resistant lung cancer. (3). To explore and exploit the incorporation of the rules in gene regulatory network (GRN) inference One problem in gene regulatory network inference is that even with high throughput technology, the available time series expression data was still very limited compared to the network size. However, existing methods make the convenient but unrealistic assumption of causal sufficiency, i.e. all the relevant factors in the causal network have been observed and there are no unobserved common cause. To alleviate these problems, we proposed to decompose large network into small subnetworks without prior knowledge of the decomposition. We also allowed the presence of hidden common cause(s) and small delays among the causal steps in the new model. Results show that our proposed algorithm improves the GRN inference performance of using either CLINDE or DD-lasso alone on the large network, with statistical significance, and is robust to different variances and slight deviation from Gaussian distribution in error terms [C4, J5]. We have demonstrated the potential of our algorithm on small YEASTRACT subnetworks using limited real data.

414413.label: Major findings and research outcome
414413.value: (1). To formalize associated TF-TFBS pattern discovery into generalized rules and binding mechanisms, and to study various subtypes using high-throughput data To achieve the first objective, we proposed novel association rule mining approach, statistical clustering approach, and random forest approach [C2, J1, J2, J13]. On the algorithmic aspect, we developed Protein DNA Co-Occurring Aligned Pattern Clusters (APCs), which are more compact than one-to-one pattern associations yet detailed enough to allow site-specific variants. On the biological aspect, we discovered two new Protein-DNA binding cores supported by homology modeling. Later, an improved binding affinity prediction method was developed by adding the information from low-quality structural and interaction data with the help from random forest [J6, J9]. (2). To apply the associated TF-TFBS (protein-DNA) binding rules on energy modeling in computational docking In this objective, we implemented two downstream applications. The applications include anti-cancer drug identification and novel inhibitors at the CDK2 [J3, J4] and the discovery of the inhibiting effect of adapalene on the activity of cyclin-dependent kinase 2 [J7]. Our drug discovery platform has been further extended and enhanced [C5, C1, C3, J8]. (3). To explore and exploit the incorporation of the rules in gene regulatory network (GRN) inference We proposed a new algorithm to learn GRN given a small amount data. Results show that our proposed algorithm improves the GRN inference performance of using either CLINDE or DD-lasso alone on the large network, with statistical significance, and is robust to different variances and slight deviation from Gaussian distribution in error terms [C4, J5].

414413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
414413.value: In the future, we would like to improve the efficiency (i.e. precision, recall, and computation speed) of our docking programs by inventing new data-driven scoring functions. Besides, given a promising software in identification of cancer drugs, we will like to extend our study to advance the drug design and find out what drugs may suppress metastatic cancer.

414413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
414413.value: We have developed many computational tools to analyze the biomolcules in our body (such as proteins, RNAs, and DNAs) and the drug molecules. The computational framework produced models which capture the inter-relationship among these molecules, such as protein-ligand binding energy estimation. These models are better than the existing in terms of execution speed, the capability to adding existing knowledge, and the capability to model a set of relevant knowledge. The tools invented in this project have been shown to identify novel drugs in suppressing and potentially curing some types of bladder carcinoma and lung cancer.

414513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
414513.value: The most critical capability in achieving good portfolio performance is certain kind of prediction power for future rates of return of the risky assets. We never over-emphasize the importance of the forecast ability for a volatile market. The current dominant approach in the practice has been to use a variety of forecasting models dictated by historical data. However, believing that the past pattern will persist into the future could be philosophically wrong. Millions of people participate in financial markets, and financial events are heavily driven by people's expectations of the future. Thus portfolio decisions should also take into consideration the forward-looking information that is implied by the financial market, when possible, in addition to the backward-looking information from historical data. Due to the characteristics of options, the option prices contain rich information about the future rates of returns for underlying risky assets. While the investigation of implied moments, especially implied volatility, already leads to many promising results, the study on implied distributions is still thin. More importantly, the issues of how to integrate implied distributions into portfolio selection as another source to estimate the future rate of return and how to derive the optimal portfolio policy accordingly are basically open. This proposed project aims to develop a formal framework to develop implementable solution methodology to feed the information from different channels into the dynamic decision making process in deriving a better adaptive portfolio policy. The first main task to attain the overall objective of this research is to develop a term structure for implied distribution. By filling the missing piece of the implied forward distribution by associating it with a suitable term structure of the implied volatility function, our research will establish a unified framework for the term structure of implied distributions. Our next main task is to consider a general multi-period mean-risk model and to derive (sub)-optimal policy in the presence of continuous updating of the implied distribution by developing some approximation solution schemes. On the other hand, precisely specifying the distribution of the asset returns is often impossible. The reality is that we live in a world mixed with ambiguity and risk. This recognition brings up a necessity for us to consider the robustness of portfolio choice when dealing with uncertainty in the implied distribution. By allowing ambiguity in the implied distribution of asset returns, our research on robust portfolio selection aims to achieve good worst-case performance.

414513.label: Realisation of objectives
414513.value: While predicting the future return distributions always represents the most compelling challenge in investment, any underlying distribution can be always well approximated by utilizing a mixture distribution, if we are able to ensure that the component list of a mixture distribution includes all possible distributions corresponding to the scenario analysis of potential market modes. Adopting a mixture distribution enables us to: (1) reduce the problem of distribution prediction to a parameter estimation problem in which the mixture weights of a mixture distribution are estimated under a Bayesian learning scheme and the corresponding credible regions of the mixture weights are obtained as well; and (2) harmonize information from different channels, such as historical data, market implied information and investors' subjective views. We develop in our research a novel portfolio selection framework with a feature of double robustness in both return distribution modeling and portfolio optimization. We further formulate a robust mean-CVaR portfolio selection problem to deal with the inherent uncertainty in predicting the future return distributions. By employing the duality theory, we show that the robust portfolio selection problem via learning with a mixture model can be reformulated as a linear program or a second-order cone program, which can be effectively solved in polynomial time. A crucial issue in VaR-based portfolio selection models is how to estimate VaR values of portfolio as a function of portfolio weights. We investigate in this research a portfolio optimization methodology using nonparametric Value-at-Risk (VaR). When adopting nonparametric Value-at-Risk (VaR), kernel VaR and quadratic VaR, as risk measures, the resulting models are nonconvex and nonsmooth optimization problems, albeit with some special structures. We develop some specially devised block coordinate descent (BCD) methods for finding approximate or local optimal solutions. Computational results show that the BCD methods are efficient for finding local solutions with good quality and they compare favorably with the branch-and-bound based global optimal solution procedures. Recognizing the importance to reduce the impact of parameter estimation error on the optimal portfolio strategy, we integrate a set of parameter sensitivity constraints into the traditional mean-variance model. The resulted optimization framework is a quadratic programming problem with nonconvex quadratic constraints. By exploiting the special structure of the nonconvex constraints, we propose a convex quadratic programming relaxation and develop an efficient branch-and-bound global optimization algorithm with a lower dimension than the original problem dimension.

414513.label: Major findings and research outcome
414513.value: The most challenging task in financial optimization is how to make decision while lacking the exact knowledge of the future uncertainty under some subjectively selected risk measure which in turn dictates corresponding "appropriate" investment guidance under such situations. We carry out research in this project how to deal with uncertainty in the model building for financial decision and how to solve the resulting nonconvex optimization problems (Output: 1, 5 and 12) For dealing with worst-case scenarios and developing robust investment policies, we onfen invoke the downside risk measures, such as lower partial moments (LPM), VaR and CVaR. We extend in this project the static mean-LPM, mean-VaR and mean-CVaR solution methodologies to their dynamiv counterparts, thus extending siginificantly the reach of this general class of mean-downside risk framework (Output: 8, 10 and 11) The most classical approach to cope with market uncertainty is the ground-breaking mean-variance formulation. However, due to some undesired properties of using variance as the risk measure, there are significant rooms for understanding the inherent solution properties and improving the conventional mean-variance formulation. Part of the efforts in this project devote to this subtask (Output: 2, 4, 7 and 9). Market timing probably is the most important responsitive strategy in corresponding to the market information. This consideration leads to a cardinality constrained mean-variance dynamic portfolio selection problem in our project (Output: 3) Understanding investors' behavior in corresponding to his previous gain or loss in the market is critical for developing investment policies and risk management schemes for such behahior investors (Output: 6). Note some of the research outputs were first submitted for journal publication before the beginning date of the project. The revision of these research papers usually would take a few years. And these revision works were partially supported by this project.

414513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
414513.value: When having limited knowledge, although robust optimization ensures good performance in the worst case scenario, it, however, results in a very conservative policy which leads to unsatisfactory performance in normal situations. One future research topic is to develop a data mining scheme to identify market turning points in order to switch the investment policies between two modes: Nomal one and the one for market crisis.

414613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
414613.value: Above-knee prostheses are the devices that can restore locomotion of trans-femoral amputees. Research and development of intelligent prostheses have shown promising results on human gait control. However, the mobile power supply constrains greatly the development of intelligent prostheses in terms of limited endurance and inconvenient daily charging. Moreover, extra batteries and angular sensor used in the current intelligent prosthetic system would result in some issues such as low reliability and big size. On the other hand, significant amount of human biomechanical energy in the current prosthetic systems was just dissipated and wasted. In addition, magnetorheological (MR) dampers are adaptive and controllable, and would have great performance on prosthetic gait control. In this research, we aim to develop intelligent prostheses utilizing regenerative MR dampers. The prosthesis has self-powered feature and real-time controlled MR damping force to adjust the walking gait. The regenerative MR dampers have self-contained sensing and power regeneration abilities, which can convert the previously wasted biomechanical energy into useful electrical energy. The size and weight of power supply would be greatly reduced, and extra angular sensor in the current system would not be needed anymore. Great merits including no daily charging of battery, longer working time, higher reliability, more convenient installation and maintenance, reduced size and weight, would be brought for the current intelligent prosthetic systems. Prototypes of regenerative MR dampers, energy harvesting circuits, sensor fusion, and control algorithms will be developed and tested. Modeling and analysis of the regenerative MR dampers and prosthesis will be performed. The integrated system will be implemented. Human trials will be performed as well to lead to a direct evaluation of the proposed ideas and analyses. This research will provide deep physical insights on understanding different functions, and interactions between the MR prosthetic device and human locomotion. The scientific knowledge created through this project will facilitate the full realization of intelligent biomechanical devices for human and energy harvesting, and stimulate continuing research efforts in both areas. The project output will benefit the medical care and rehabilitation for trans-femoral amputees in Hong Kong, Mainland China, and all over the world. 膝上義肢是一種能夠使膝上截肢者恢復行走能力的裝置。研究及開發顯示，智能義肢對於人體行走的步態控制具有極佳的效果。然而，由於有限的使用時間和日常充電的不便，移動電源的供應限制了智能義肢的發展。另外，當前智能義肢系統所使用的外加電池和角度感應器會導致一些問題，如低可靠性和較大的體積。另一方面，在當前的義肢系統中，有大量的耗散並浪費的人體動能。另外，磁流變阻尼器具有可控及可調節性，若用於義肢的步態控制，將具有極好的性能。因此，我們將在本項目中開發使用了具有能量回收的磁流變阻尼器的智能義肢。該義肢具有自供能的特性和用於調整行走步態的實時可控的磁流變阻尼力。具有能量回收的磁流變阻尼器具有内置的自感應和發電能力，可以將原先浪費掉的人體動能轉換為有用的電能。因此，電源的尺寸和重量會大大地減小，也不再需要當前系統中的角度感應器。智能義肢系統將不再需要每日的充電，並且具有更長的工作時間、更高的可靠性、更加便利的安裝和維護、以及更小的體積和重量。本項目將開發並測試具有能量回收的磁流變阻尼器的原型、能量收集電路、感應器融合和控制算法，並將對阻尼器和義肢系統進行建模和分析。我們還將實現系統的集成，並進行人體試驗，從而對提出的方法及分析進行評估驗證。本研究將有助於深入了解不同的功能，以及磁流變裝置和人體行走的相互作用機制。項目所創造的科學知識將會促進智能生物力學裝置和能量收集技術的發展，並且促進這兩個領域的持續研究。項目的成果還將有益於香港、中國大陸和全世界膝上截肢者的醫療護理及康復。

414613.label: Realisation of objectives
414613.value: A powered ankle-foot prosthesis driven by a parallel elastic actuator (PEA) was developed. With the consideration of energy efficiency and control of prosthesis, the parallel spring mechanism was designed to imitate the controlled dorsiflexion impedance of human ankle. In that case, about 86% of the negative energy in controlled dorsiflexion (CD) phase can be stored in the parallel spring and reused in powered plantar flexion /push-off phase (PP). Consequently, the peak motor power and torque were reduced by 31% and 56%, respectively. Besides, since the parallel spring mechanism can provide the desired torque in CD phase, the motor was powered off without control in this phase. In addition, sufficient torque can be provided by the parallel spring in late CD phase, the transition between CD to PP phase was activated by the motion of subjects. It ensured more natural gait being restored. In this study, the parallel spring mechanism was implemented with a compact cam-spring mechanism. The design of cam profile for desired torque behavior was studied. Cam profile was decomposed into several parts, and each part was fitted by a quadratic Bezier curve. Noted that the friction force was considered in the cam-spring mechanism. It ensured that in CD phase, the parallel spring mechanism can imitate the desired behavior precisely. Finally, experimental results validated the design. For good practicality, the developed powered prosthesis was designed with capability to work in passive mode, because sometimes, prosthesis would be out of power because of walking in battery restricted area, long-time walking, or forgetting to charge. For practical use, two functions were desired. The first was to protect subjects falling down in CD phase, sufficient torque should be provided. The second was for avoiding foot dropping off in swing phase (SW) phase, damping torque should act on prosthesis to resist the inertial force of prosthetic foot. In the developed prosthesis, the parallel spring mechanism can provide sufficient torque in CD phase. In addition, the motor worked as a generator to supply damping torque in SW phase for avoiding foot dropping off. Besides, regenerative MR dampers have been designed. Intelligent prostheses were designed and fabricated by considering human biomechanics. Energy harvesting circuits were built; sensors and controller on the human walking gait were also developed. Models of MR dampers were developed and the design has been optimized. Gait analysis for prosthesis was performed. Finally, clinical trials were conducted for testing the performance of the developed prosthesis. The testing results showed that in powered mode, the motion curves of the sound side and prosthetic side of subjects were the closest to each other among the three studied cases: walking with original one; walking with the new one in powered mode; and walking with the new one in passive mode. In other words, the powered prosthesis can help subjects restore more symmetrical gait. In addition, when wearing the powered prosthesis, subjects’ effort for walking can be reduced by 15%, compared with the conventional prostheses. The intelligent prosthetic system was implemented, and human trials were also performed. All objectives of this project have been successfully realized.

414613.label: Major findings and research outcome
414613.value: Shape memory alloy (SMA) fiber-reinforced epoxy/aluminum matrix composite cylinders were analyzed under thermo-mechanical loadings. A robust phenomenological constitutive model was implemented to simulate martensite transformation, reorientation of martensite variants, pseudo-elasticity and shape memory effects of SMAs (see [J1] in Part C). Reversible shape adaptive panels integrated with one-way shape memory alloy actuators were analyzed to examine the effects of martensite variants reorientation. A robust three-dimensional model was implemented to simulate shape memory effect, pseudo-elasticity, and ferro-elasticity features of shape memory alloys (see [J2] in Part C). We proposed a convenient and real-time gait modeling, analysis, and evaluation method based on ground reaction forces (GRFs) measured by a pair of smart insoles. Gait states were deﬁned based on the foot–ground contact forms of both legs. From the obtained gait state sequence and the duration of each state, the human gait was modeled as a semi-Markov process (SMP). Gait analysis experiments were conducted on 23 subjects with different ages and health conditions. The results showed that gait patterns are successfully obtained and evaluated for normal, age-related, and pathological gaits (see [J3] in Part C). A magnetorheological (MR) damper was optimally designed for use in smart prosthetic knees. The objective of optimization was to minimize the total energy consumption during one gait cycle and weight of the MR damper. Based on the MR damper model as well as the prosthetic knee model, the instantaneous energy consumption of the MR damper was derived in the two working states. Then by integrating in one gait cycle, the total energy consumption was obtained. Particle swarm optimization algorithm was used to optimize the geometric dimensions of MR damper. Finally, a prototype of the optimized MR damper was fabricated and tested with comparison to simulation (see [J4] in Part C). A powered ankle-foot prosthesis with nonlinear parallel spring mechanism was developed. The parallel spring mechanism was used for reducing the energy consumption and power requirement of motor. To achieve that goal, the parallel spring mechanism was implemented as a compact cam-spring mechanism that was designed to possess human ankle dorsiflexion stiffness. Experimental results showed that the cam-spring mechanism can mimic the desired torque characteristics in loading process precisely. Finally, the developed prosthesis was tested on a unilateral below-knee amputee. The testing results showed that the peak power and energy consumption of motor are decreased by about 37.5% and 34.6%, respectively. (see [J5] and [J6] in Part C)

414613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
414613.value: Although significant results (6 journal papers and 6 conference papers, patent applications in China and US, etc.) have been obtained from this completed project, the terrain identification for powered lower limb prostheses should be further investigated. A suitable pattern recognition algorithm should be developed to process the input signals so as to identify the terrain. The terrain identification system should be implemented in the developed powered lower limb prostheses. More clinical trials on both below-knee and above-knee amputees should be conducted to evaluate the performances on different terrains.

414613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
414613.value: In this research, a powered ankle-foot prosthesis driven by a parallel elastic actuator (PEA) was developed. With the consideration of energy efficiency and control of prosthesis, a cam-spring mechanism in the PEA was designed to reproduce the impedance of human ankle. To obtain desired torque behavior, the cam profile generation was studied. With this design, the peak motor power and torque were decreased by 31% and 56%, respectively, compared with direct drive system. Besides, the powered prosthesis was designed to be workable in passive mode. The parallel spring mechanism can provide sufficient torque to avoid falling down, and the motor can work as a generator for providing damping torque to resist the inertial force of prosthetic foot. Finally, clinical trials were performed to test the performance of the developed prosthesis. Subjects’ gait and metabolic cost were both measured. Experimental results showed that when walking with the developed powered prosthesis, subjects have more symmetrical gait, lower metabolic cost as compared with conventional prostheses. The scientific knowledge created through this project will facilitate the full realization of intelligent prostheses. The project output will benefit the medical care and rehabilitation for amputees in Hong Kong, Mainland China, and all over the world.

414713.value: To investigate the application of iterative algorithms to solve the joint problem of multi-parameter estimation and channel decoding "optimally" in PNC systems. 414713.label: Realisation of objectives
414713.value: For this project, all three objectives have been met, with some research outcomes extending beyond the original three objectives. Altogether, 12 journal publications and 6 conference publications are associated with this project (publication list at the end of this section). With respect to objectives 1 and 2, we have succeeded in setting up an EM-BP framework to solve for the optimal solutions and practical solutions to joint parameter estimation and channel decoding in physical-layer network coding (PNC) systems. We further extended the framework to the multiuser detection problem (not just PNC). Our results were reported in a number of international journal and conference publications (references 1 to 10 below). Major findings related to objectives 1 and 2 are elaborated in Section 6.1. With respect to objective 3, we successfully developed a TCP/IP compatible PNC prototype on a software-defined radio platform. Standard TCP/IP applications, such as web browsing and video conference, can run on top of our PNC network. This is a significant achievement in that we are the first team that moves PNC from theory to practice to that extent: as far as we know, PNC prototyping efforts at several other research labs around the world have not demonstrated a real-time PNC system running real applications. This success requires us to reduce the complexity of our frameworks in objectives 1 and 2 so that they can be implemented on our software-defined radio platform. Publications with implementation ingredients and experimentation are references 11 to 14 below. Findings related to objective 3 are elaborated in Section 6.1. Going beyond objectives 1, 2, and 3, we also studied several non-PNC systems that, like PNC systems, also exploit signal/interference cancellation techniques (references 15 to 18 below). 414713.label: Major findings and research outcome
414713.value: Cited references are with respect to the Reference List at the end of Section 5.3 Summary of Main Outcomes with respect to Objectives 1 and 2: PNC channel decoding is different from conventional multi-user channel decoding: specifically, the PNC relay aims to decode a network-coded message rather than the individual messages of the users. Channel estimation in PNC is particularly challenging because of 1) the overlapped signals of multiple users; 2) the correlations among data symbols induced by channel coding; and 3) time-varying channels. In this project, we successfully combined the expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm and belief propagation (BP) algorithm on a unified factor-graph framework to tackle these challenges. In this framework, channel estimation is performed by an EM subgraph, and channel decoding is performed by a BP subgraph that models a virtual encoder matched to the target of PNC channel decoding. Iterative message passing between these two subgraphs allow the optimal solutions for both to be approached progressively. Extensive simulation results demonstrate the superiority of our PNC receivers over other PNC receivers [1,2]. Besides the EM-BP approach, we successfully constructed complexity-reduction signal processing methods to tackle multipath issues and symbol misalignment issues in PNC systems [4,5,6]. In addition, the construction of advanced complexed-symbol PNC systems were reported in [7]. The applications of PNC beyond two-way relay channels were investigated in [8, 9, 10]. Going beyond PNC systems, we leveraged the new insight obtained from the above studies in the design of multiuser detection systems, in which a receiver aims to decode all the individual messages simultaneously transmitted by multiple users [3]. Summary of Main Outcomes with respect to Objective 3: We successfully made our PNC prototype TCP/IP compatible, so that standard TCP/IP applications, such as web browsing and video conference, can run on top of our PNC network (see youtube demo “https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ghv0MsfHFFs”). In addition, we implemented PNC prototypes to explore the use of PNC in mobile networks. In addition wireless networks, we also explored optical networks that employ PNC in which joint channel estimation and signal detection are required. Through this work, the first optical PNC system prototype has been implemented and demonstrated. The results were reported in the Photonic Technology Journal [14]. Works that involve experimentation on PNC prototypes were reported in [11 – 14]. Note: The work of two publications reported here began soon after the result of this proposal was made known in July 2013 (i.e., after we knew that this proposal successfully obtained the funding), and before the official start date of Jan 2014, because we wanted to be ahead in this competitive research field. The slightly later start date allowed us to gather our resources for a more organized pursuit of the objectives. All publications listed, however, were accepted after the start date of Jan 2014, and much of the work done to revise these papers into forms acceptable to the reviewers/editors were done after the official start date of this project. The majority of the papers attributed to this project were submitted and published after the official start date.

414713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
414713.value: In the midterm report, we mentioned that through the work of this project, we discovered a generic signal processing problem -- relevant not just to PNC systems, but many other communications and engineering systems -- that has not been tackled by other researchers: namely Soft Fast Fourier Transform (SFFT). We discovered this problem because SFFT can potentially be integrated into our overall framework of joint parameter estimation and channel decoding to further improve performance. Although not part of the core objectives of this project, we have further devoted attention to the investigation of SFFT since the midterm report. Our further investigation indicated that the complexity of SFFT could increase exponentially as SFFT size increases. Specifically, the complexity of computing the message on each edge increases exponentially as the number of stages in FFT (log N where N is the FFT size) increases. Although analysis indicates that the complexity can be reduced somewhat (since some message components can be derived directly from other message components without computation), the overall complexity still remains large. Going forward, a very interesting issue to work on is complexity reduction of SFFT, given that SFFT can be very useful in many applications beyond that of this project.

414713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
414713.value: This work investigated Iterative Algorithms for Multiple-Parameter Estimation and Channel Decoding in Physical-Layer Network Coding (PNC) Systems. PNC was originally proposed in 2006 by the research group of the principal investigator of this project. The key idea of PNC is to turn a nuisance in wireless communications, interference among wireless stations, into useful signals that can boost the throughput of wireless networks. Since 2006, PNC has developed into a subfield of network coding with a wide following in the wireless community. For a complete PNC system, the incorporation of channel coding is essential to ensure reliability in information transmission. PNC channel decoding, however, is different from channel coding in conventional communications systems in several respects. Furthermore, channel estimation in PNC, another key component for practical PNC, is particularly challenging due to the overlapped of signals and interferences. This work tackles these two key problems by constructing a new framework for channel estimation and channel coding in PNC systems. In addition, a first-of-its-kind TCP/IP compatible PNC prototype has also been successfully implemented on a software-defined radio platform to demonstrate feasibility. Overall, this project contributed significantly to the theoretical understanding and practical feasibility of PNC, moving it a step closer to reality.

414813.label: Project Objectives
414813.value: Develop an approach to propagate motion of the leader robot of the group to all the followers on-line so as to avoid pre-planning/giving of the desired trajectories for all the robots; Formulate the image-based formation control of multiple robots, and design a formation controller for a group of nonholonomic mobile robots using visual feedback from their cameras capturing features on the leader robots; Investigate the stability and robustness of the developed controller under the nonholonomic constraints using the Lyapunov theory and computer simulations; and Implement the developed controller and examine its performance by experiments on a group of nonholonomic mobile robots.

414813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
414813.value: Formation control is a problem of controlling a group of mobile robots to move in a desired formation. For its many potential applications in civil and military areas, formation control has been one of the most popular topics in robotics and automation for years. Existing approaches mainly control position errors between neighboring robots with the condition that the desired trajectories of all the robots are planned beforehand. However, in many real applications the group leader plans the global motion on-line and all the other robots just follow its motion and know nothing about their desired trajectories. Moreover, few existing controllers take into account the nonholonomic constraints. To mimic human formative walking, in this project we will develop a new framework for formation control of nonholonomic mobile robots using image-based visual feedback. Like what human does in formative walking, a robot will use its eye, i.e. a camera, to monitor some features on its leader robot and then control projections of the features to the positions on the image plane that yield the desired formation between the robots. Instead of planning the desired trajectories of the robots, an innovative concept called reference propagation will be developed to propagate motion of the group leader to the followers on-line. Furthermore, on the basis of the scheme we will design an image-based formation controller for nonholonomic mobile robots. Asymptotic stability of the developed method under the nonholonomic motion constraints will be investigated by Lyapunov theory. Experiments on a group of nonholonomic mobile robots will be conducted to validate the controller to be developed. The research outputs will contribute to the advancement of robotics and technology development in Hong Kong as well as the rest of the world. 機器人編隊控制是控制一組機器人按照指定的隊形一起運動。因其在軍事和民用領域的廣泛潛在應用，機器人編隊控制一直是機器人和控制領域的研究熱點之一。目前所研發的控制方法主要是在所有機器人的目標軌跡都知道的情況下控制機器人的相對位置關係。但是在實際應用時，一般是領隊機器人線上規劃其軌跡而其他機器人則跟蹤其運動。此外，很少研究考慮到移動機器人的非完整約束。為了模仿人們的編隊行走，本專案將研發基於視覺回饋非完整約束移動機器人編隊控制的新理論框架和演算法。與人們編隊行走時一樣，機器人將利用它的眼睛觀察它跟蹤的機器人的特徵點，通過控制特徵點的位置實現編隊運動。為了回避機器人的運動規劃，我們將提出一個全新的目標軌跡傳遞法把領隊機器人的目標運動逐個傳遞給其他機器人。在此基礎，研究非完整約束機器人的編隊控制演算法並利用李雅普理論分析控制系統的穩定性。為了驗證所研究控制演算法的有效性，將利用一組機器人開展實驗研究。本研究對機器人技術發展及香港的科學創新有很重要的意義。

414813.label: Realisation of objectives
414813.value: The objectives have been fully achieved as detailed in the following: (1) We developed a new framework for imaged-based leadering-following formation control of nonholonomic mobile robots using visual feedback from on-board cameras. The motion of the leader is propagated to the following robots on-line using an image-based formation representation. Moreover, this new framework formulates the leader–follower kinematics in the image space so that the measurements of the global positions of the robots can be avoided. In this framework, feedbacks from the sensors are employed to design observers that estimate the positions and/or velocities of the mobile robots. (2) Based on the new framework, a visually servoed controller has been developed to control formation of nonholonomic mobile robots without directly measuring positions of the robots. This controller employs an adaptive algorithm to estimate positions of the robots on-line by fusing visual information with odometry and inertial measurements. We have proved the stability of the controller and carried out the simulations. The results have been published on IEEE Trans. on Automatic Control. (3) We further developed a controller for formation tracking of a leader-followers mobile robot system. In addition to the positions, the controller also estimates the linear velocity of the leader using visual feedback so that the formation control can be done even without mutual communication. The proposed formation tracking controller enabled the robots to track desired trajectories while maintaining the formation. By using the Lyapunov stability theory, we conducted a rigorous stability analysis and proved the global stability of the combined observer–controller closed-loop system. Both simulations and experiments were conducted to validate the performance. The work led to publications in IEEE Transactions on Robotics and etc. (4) We have investigated distributed control of leader-follower formation of nonholonomic mobile robots. In most of the existing leader-follower formation control schemes for nonholonomic mobile robots, having access to the full state of the leader is a requirement. However, due to limitations in communication bandwidth and range, it is real that the information of the leader is available only to a subset of followers. Hence, we proposed a new distributed leader-following formation control strategy based on the distributed estimation of the leader’s states. Moreover, the coordination error between a pair of interacting robots is explicitly used in the control design to weaken the dependence on the estimated state of the leader and hence to enhance the decentralized nature of the proposed control scheme. The stability and convergence of the system are analyzed mathematically and the experiments using unicycles were conducted to verify the good performance. (5) We further studied the self-repairing problem in formation control of mobile robots. A self-repairing algorithm has been developed to maintain synchronisation or formation of networked mobile robots when some of the robots fail to function.
