414813.label: Major findings and research outcome
414813.value: The major findings and research outcomes are as follows: (1) An image-based formation controller for nonholonomic mobile robots without the need of measuring the global positions of the robots: The controller fuses the visual information with the odometry or inertial sensors to estimate the positions of the robots on-line. Therefore, the formation tracking control can be achieved without direct measurement of the positions. The work has been published in IEEE Trans. on Automatic Control (paper 2) (2) An image-based formation tracking control of nonholonomic mobile robots without position and velocity measurements: An adaptive algorithm was proposed to estimate the position and linear velocity of the leader using visual information. The formation control is formulated as a problem in the image space. The work led to a publication in IEEE Transactions on Robotics. (paper 3) (3) A distributed formation controller for nonholonomic mobile robots: Given the reality that the leader's motion information is available to a small number of followers, the controller estimates the position and linear velocity of the leader using an observer in a decentralised manner. The work led to a publication on IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering. (paper 4) (4) A self-repairing algorithm for maintaining synchronisation of networked mobile robots when some robots fails. This algorithm plans on-line the optimal repairing paths for the robots so as to maintain the network topology. The work is to be published on IEEE Transactions of Systems, Man, and Cybernetics: Systems. (paper 5) (5) Extension of the algorithms/controllers to image-based formation control of networked robot manipulators: The controller makes it possible to control cooperative tracking of networked manipulators in the task space without measuring the task velocity. We proved the stability of the system with uncertain dynamics and communication delay using Lyapunov functions. Two papers have been published. (paper 6 and 1). (6) Stability analysis of the controllers using Lyapunov functions, and verification of the controllers by both simulations and experiments.

414813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
414813.value: Further research could be carried out as follows: (1) Improvement of the robustness of the controllers to noises in visual measurements: The research did not consider the visual noises in the controller design. Coping with the image noises is an important issue to be solved. (2) Controller design when the dynamics of the robots is taken into account: The proposed controllers are designed based on kinematics of the mobile robots only. When the weight of the robot is large, the inertial forces must be considered in order to stabilise the system.

414813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
414813.value: In this project, we investigated formation control problems of nonholonomic mobile robots. To address the challenges in measuring global positions of the mobile robots, we formulate the problem in the image space so that direct measurement of the positions can be avoided. An adaptive algorithm or observer is designed to estimate the positions on-line from the sensory information, in particular the visual feedback. The research outputs include (1) the design of an image-based controller for the leader-follower formation control problem of nonholonomic robot without measuring their positions, (2) an image-based controller for formation tracking control of the robots without the position and velocity measurements; (3) a distributed formation controller in the presence of communication limitations; and (4) a self-repairing method for networked nonholonomic mobile robots. The stability of the controllers was theoretically analysed by Lyapunov functions, and their superior performance was further verified by experiments. Compared to our approaches, existing formation controllers work under the assumption that the positions of all the robots are available, while this assumption is hardly satisfied in real applications. Therefore, the research work made important contributions to formation control of nonholonomic mobile robots.

415013.label: Project Objectives
415013.value: Develop sampling theory and parallelized random walk algorithms to explore "local structures" (e.g., connectivity among a small group of friends) in an OSNs. This is important for applications such as identifying network homophily or community detection. Develop mathematical theory and sampling methods to calculate the "information content and its distribution" in large scale networks. This is important because one can accurately determine the information replication level, and so to device the proper caching scheme for quick information delivery. he technical challenges are : (a) Provide a provable sampling theory for "unbiased estimates" on the distribution of performance metrics, i.e., as we sample more nodes, estimate will converge to the true measure. (b) Since we consider networks which are inherently large in scale, this implies that there is a huge storage and I/O cost in storing and processing the data. We will develop "efficient compression algorithms" for strong the data set and de-compressing for retrieving them. (c) Explore theoretical foundation to quantify the convergence on the random walker in calculating various performance metrics. Although the convergence rate depends on the type of networks and applications, but the "Markov chain mixing time" results can be use to quantify convergence rates.

415013.value: 近年來，有一個新興的科學領域被稱為網絡科學。這一領域的目標是了解網絡的互連結構和不同的底層動態特性。物理學家，生物學家和社會學家在這一領域已有一些早期作品。然而，在過去的幾年中，計算機科學家研究的算法和架構問題，在網絡科技領域的興趣亦同時增長。這是因為計算機科學家和工程師要所面對許多大型網絡，例如，互聯網，萬維網(WWW），以及在線的社交網絡如Facebook或Twitter。 上述網絡有一個共同特點，就是它們是非常大規模。例如，2012年3月，有大約22.8億用戶在互聯網上>和430億索引的網頁。對於網上流行的Facebook或Twitter等社交網絡，每個大約有5億用戶。一個普通的用戶在Facebook擁有大約250個朋友（最多5000的朋友），而頭用户（Lady Gaga)的Twitter用戶中，有超過3千萬的追隨者。通常情況下，人們可用一些圖論方法（例如，定向或無向圖），建模形和代表這些網絡。這些網絡意味著我們要有一個巨大的存儲和計算方法來處理這些大圖。因此，我們迫切需要開發新的方法，算法，存儲或壓縮方法，...等，這樣才可以處理這些圖形的動態。 這個研究項目的目的是開發新的理論，算法和計算架構，以便探索這些大規模網絡的信息。讓我們先考慮一個例證。例如，我們要確定在Facebook所有用戶（例如，從城市的用戶比例$ X$）的地理分佈的概率密度函數。一個簡單但昂貴的計算方法是枚舉所有在網絡中的節點（或用戶）後，我們訪問所有節點，每個節點提取的元信息，並提交總結。然而，更有效的方法是我們可考慮在圖上隨機遊走。這相當於做在網絡上的信息的採樣。當然，技術挑戰性的問題是給裝置採樣算法，給出了一個無偏分佈。 我們認為在這個研究項目中有一些有趣的應用: (1) 開發新的隨機遊走和採樣算法 (2) 制定正式的抽樣方法來表徵在線社交網絡內容分佈 本研究的目的是開發大型網絡的數學理論和算法，探索信息, 和其應用。

415013.label: Major findings and research outcome
415013.value: There are # of major findings: - Some previously proposed exploration techniques (e.g., depth first search or breath first search), turn out, to generate erroneous results, more important, these errors CANNOT be corrected. This was shown in our publication Part C, 8-2, 8-4 and 8-5, as well as Part C, 9-1 and 9-3. - Our algorithms can guaranteed that the information we try to explore and collect will have "unbiased results", in other words, we have a theoretical guarantee of our results. 415013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
415013.value: Given the popularity of online social networks, web-blogs and web-based transaction systems, it is becoming important for researchers and engineers to develop efficient and effective way to explore information. The challenge is that given the massive amount of information, how can we only examine a small percentage of data and still be able to find the information accurately. Previous proposed methods consider an exhaustive search, which is very expensive because it may take a long time (weeks, years) to get the result, while other previous research proposal consider naive sampling but these techniques were found to have errors and more important, these errors can't be removed by post-processing. We are the first to develop an online sampling algorithm which can accurately and effectively explore information in large scale networks (e.g., Facebook) with massive amount of data.

415113.label: Project Objectives
415113.value: Localization of quality bottlenecks via mining platform-generated trace logs: This task aims at investigating how to exploit the huge volume of platform-generated trace logs to help designer understand system performance and locate fine-grained performance anomalies. Firstly, performance profiling and fine-grained anomaly detection approaches are proposed. Then, performance anomalies are detected via system behavior mining employing the large volume of platform-generated trace logs. Tolerance of faults via exploiting platform-generated QoS information: This task will design adaptive and reconfigurable fault tolerance strategies for distributed platforms via mining the platform-generated QoS information. Online learning algorithms will be investigated for incremental update of the fault tolerance strategy. Moreover, since different users may observe quite different QoS performance on the same service, we will also design personalized user-centric fault tolerance strategies via mining server-side and user-side QoS information of service components. Migration of services via investigating platform-generated service relationship: This task will investigate service invocation relationship as well as QoS of service components for making optimal service migration. Firstly, initial deployment of services is studied by exploiting the large volume of available platform-generated service data (e.g., service invocation graphs, QoS of the physical machines, etc.). After that, several dynamic service migration strategies will be investigated

415113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
415113.value: In the modern IT era, service computing has attracted worldwide attentions as a pervasively deployed technique with the support of large-scale distributed systems, such as cloud applications, Internet-of-Things, and many other domains. In these emerging service platforms, various platform-generated data are so huge and complex that they become difficult to process with existing software. The targeted platforms often involve complex structures, and the big data generated from these platforms are typically graph-based, heterogeneous, of multiple data types, dynamic and incomplete. Due to the fast increase of system size and the associated enormous volume of platform-generated data, investigating service quality engineering in the presence of massive system and application data is an inevitable challenge. Examples of platform-generated big data include trace logs, quality of service (QoS) information of service components, software status, service invocation graph, etc. The platform-generated big data cover four unique dimensions: volume, velocity, variety, and veracity. Exploring the unique characteristics of platform-generated big data present an excellent opportunity for researchers to revolutionize service quality engineering. To fully unfold the potential of platform-generated big data, developing innovative techniques to effectively process large quantities of data within tolerable elapsed time is required. This project will therefore comprehensively investigate service quality engineering via modeling and exploiting platform-generated big data. To attain this goal, four tasks will be conducted in this project. The first three tasks investigate three corresponding types of platform-generated big data respectively (namely, platform-generated trace logs, QoS of service components, and invocation relationship among service components), while the last task implements the proposed algorithms. More specifically, we will first localize service quality bottlenecks via mining the platform-generated trace logs. Then, tolerance of faults will be achieved by exploiting platform-generated QoS information. After that, migration of services will be investigated via studying platform-generated service invocation relationship. Finally, large scale research data will be collected and a service quality engineering toolkit will be implemented. This project can be seamlessly deployed in both industrial and academic communities for building high quality service systems. 415113.label: Realisation of objectives
415113.value: All the project objectives have been either completely achieved or exceedingly achieved. We have studied the logging statements of modern platforms in the first place. We design a “learning to log” framework, which aims to provide informative guidance on logging during development. A tool called LogAdvisor is developed to automatically learn the common logging practice from existing master codes and suggest logging places to developers. LogAdvisor achieves 0.84+ accuracy on all evaluated datasets. We also design machine learning and data mining techniques to help localize the quality bottlenecks. We design a framework to help semi-supervised learning with both relevant and irrelevant data. Besides, we also investigate feature selection techniques, which is crucial in various log mining tasks. First, we develop an algorithm for non-monotonic feature selection that approximates the related combinatorial optimization problem by a Multiple Kernel Learning (MKL) problem. Second, we propose a greedy interaction feature selection algorithm based on gradient boosting. Moreover, we study the combinatorial pure exploration (CPE) problem in the stochastic multi-armed bandit setting, where a learner explores a set of arms with the objective of identifying the optimal member of a decision class. We present general learning algorithms which work for all decision classes that admit offline maximization oracles in both fixed confidence and fixed budget settings. We prove problem-dependent upper bounds of our algorithms. Our results show that the proposed algorithms achieve the optimal sample complexity (within logarithmic factors) for many decision classes. To improve the fault tolerance via platform-generated QoS information, we design various QoS prediction approaches for Web service recommendation. First, we propose a novel spatial-temporal QoS prediction approach for time-aware Web service recommendation, where a sparse representation is employed to model QoS variations. This approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods with more than 10% improvement on the accuracy of temporal QoS prediction. Second, we present a highly credible approach, called reputation-based Matrix Factorization (RMF), for predicting the unknown Web service QoS values using QoS data from both reliable and unreliable users. Besides, we conduct an overview about service fault tolerance for highly reliable service-oriented systems. Moreover, we investigate the fundamentals of touch operations as biometrics by justifying their distinctiveness and permanence, and verify that touch biometrics can serve as a promising method for continuous and passive authentication. To help develop incremental update of the fault tolerance strategy, we also design a kernelized online imbalanced learning algorithm with fixed budgets. By using this method, we can control the number of support vectors without sacrificing model performance, and restrict the fluctuation to attain smooth updating. We also propose techniques for better migration of services via investigating platform-generated service relationship. Specifically, we design an entropy-based service selection technique with uncertain QoS values for mobile cloud computing. It uses intervals instead of fixed values to represent QoS of services, and enables developers to specify their QoS requirements in a more simple way. Besides, we design an online dynamic provision algorithm to minimize operational cost in hybrid clouds. Our approach can address the real-world challenges where no a priori information of public cloud renting prices is available and the future probability distribution of user requests is unknown. To make better usage of service invocation relationship, we also investigate recommendation algorithms. First, we unify explicit response models and PMF to establish the Response Aware Probabilistic Matrix Factorization (RAPMF) framework. This approach can capture the response patterns of users and adjust the recommendation results accordingly. Second, we propose a unified model that combines content-based filtering with collaborative filtering, harnessing the information of both ratings and reviews. With the information embedded in the review text, we can alleviate the cold-start problem. Furthermore, our model is able to learn latent topics that are interpretable. With these interpretable topics, we can explore the prior knowledge on items or users and recommend completely “cold” items. Moreover, we also study community detection algorithms for better service migration. First, we propose a preference-based nonnegative matrix factorization (PNMF) model to incorporate implicit link preference information. Our model maximizes the likelihood of the preference order for each node by following the intuition that a node prefers its neighbours than other nodes; and overcomes the indiscriminate penalty problem in which non-linked pairs inside one community are equally penalized in objective functions as those across two communities. Second, we propose a Locality-based Non-negative Matrix Factorization (LNMF) model to refine a preference-based model by incorporating locality into learning objective. By discriminately treating these two classes of non-neighbors, our model is able to capture the process of community formation.

415113.label: Major findings and research outcome
415113.value: Totally 1 book, 7 journal papers and 10 conference papers have been published, all acknowledging the support of this grant. These publications cover the project’s objectives in various aspects. We describe the resulting outcomes as follows. (We use [J1] label to refer to journal publication [1], and [C1] label to refer to conference publication [1], etc. Note [J8] is a book publication.) The first objective focuses on the localization of quality bottlenecks via mining platform-generated trace logs. First, we systematically investigate the problem of the localization of quality bottlenecks and the platform logging mechanism. Specifically, we study the logging strategy of master platforms developers, and develop a LogAdvisor to help developers make informed logging decisions [C7]. Moreover, machine learning methodologies, such as semi-supervised learning approach [J4], general multi-armed bandits learner with combinatorial structure [C5], feature selection techniques [J5, C2] are also investigated, which can be employed to localize quality bottlenecks. The second objective focuses on tolerance of faults via exploiting platform-generated QoS information. To understand the fault tolerance techniques with QoS information, we conduct a survey of service fault tolerance techniques for highly reliable service-oriented systems [J3]. Besides, we investigate spatial-temporal QoS prediction approach [J6], reputation-based personalized QoS prediction approach [J7], framework of telerobot in space [C1], touch biometrics-based authentication [C3], kernelized online learning approach [C6], which can help design fault-tolerance techniques. Moreover, a book [J8] has been published to comprehensively introduce our QoS prediction and evaluation approaches. The third objective attempts to study the migration of services via investigating platform-generated service relationship. Towards this end, we propose an entropy-based service selection technique with uncertain QoS values [C10]. Besides, to minimize the operational cost for service providers, we design a dynamic resource provisioning approach with delay-aware optimization [J1]. Moreover, we also extend the problem to model-based collaborative filtering [J2], recommendation [C4], community detection [C9, C8].

415113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
415113.value: In this project, we have investigated service quality engineering via modeling and exploiting platform-generated big data, including localization of quality bottlenecks, tolerance of faults, and migration of services. Various data mining and machine learning techniques are employed, such as collaborative filtering, classification, feature selection, matrix factorization, online learning, imbalance handling, and so on. For future research, we can design and implement a toolkit that contains the service quality engineering techniques. Besides, we can collect platform-generated data and release online. This would allow our service quality engineering techniques to be reproduced and employed by researchers and practitioners.

415113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
415113.value: We have designed and implemented various approaches to ensure or enhance the reliability of modern systems by employing the large amount of data generated. These approaches mainly cover localization of quality bottlenecks, tolerance of faults, and migration of services. This project enables developers of modern systems to build reliable systems, such as cloud computing systems. The proposed techniques allow developers detect the anomalies of the system, further locate the quality bottleneck inside the system, automatically fix the problem, and so on. This project promotes the design and development of reliability engineering of modern systems, and employs the large volume of data generated. Moreover, it facilitates the ongoing research in the big data era.

415313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
415313.value: 目標 這個項目的目標是搭建第壹個高性能且不需要校准算法的太赫茲時域光譜橢偏儀系統 項目背景 在研究太赫茲透射光譜的應用,以及太赫茲信號記錄的時候,我們需要知道樣品厚度。由于生物樣品厚度的不均勻性，其厚度通常是不確定的。此外,暴露于環境空氣中可能會使樣品脫水，從而影響樣品的厚度。如果樣品厚度不精確，在測量和計算太赫茲信號的時候，光譜的准確特性就會降低。克服這個問題的方法之壹是使用太赫茲時域光譜橢偏儀,它在准確計算樣品厚度的同時測量太赫茲信號。這將使太赫茲光譜在空間和時間上都具有精確計算的特性 項目簡介 橢偏儀是壹項在光頻段深受認可的技術。爲了讓這項技術很好的工作,需要使用高性能的偏振器將s和p偏振方向的分量分開。然而,在太赫茲波段,現有的偏振器還不能滿足這個要求。校准算法能彌補非理想太赫茲偏振器的不足。對于這個問題,目前國際上只有少數研究組嘗試搭建壹個太赫茲橢偏儀系統。我們設計了壹種迄今爲止性能最爲優越的太赫茲偏振器。因此,我們計劃制備這個太赫茲偏振器，並將其整合到太赫茲橢偏儀系統中，進而開發第壹個高性能且不需要校准算法的太赫茲橢偏儀系統。這個項目將是把在光頻段標准橢偏儀技術應用到太赫茲波段所需要的基本突破。 項目意義 鑒于我們研究團隊多學科專長，包括太赫茲成像,太赫茲光譜,光學設備制造,醫療成像，我們有條件制備出第壹個高性能且不需要校准算法的時域光譜橢偏儀系統。這將極大地推進太赫茲光譜和成像在諸多領域的應用,尤其是生物醫學成像。

415313.label: Realisation of objectives
415313.value: Objective 1. We have designed and fabricated a high-extinction ratio and low transmission loss thin-film terahertz polarizer based on our work published previously. The polarizer is based on a bilayer aluminium grating structure enables tailoring of the extinction ratio and the transmission characteristics. The experimental verification shows that the extinction ratio is maintained over 50dB and the transmission losses is below 1dB in the effective 0.2-1.1 THz. Due to the bandwidth limitation of the experimental system, frequencies above 1.1 THz provides limited signal to noise ratio which is below the extinction ratio of the device, therefore the device property cannot be well resolved. However, a good match between the experimental and simulation results allows us to further analyse its performance at higher frequencies and of different structure dimensions. We simulated the performance of the device as a function of pitch distance when fixing the spacing at 2 µm, and an extinction ratio above 63dB with transmission loss below 1dB (i.e. transmission coefficient >89%) for 0.3 - 2THz can be achieved with a grating spacing of 2 µm and pitch of 4 µm, which has been beyond our expectation. Therefore we were able to fabricate a new bilayer terahertz polarizer with the optimized dimension for the ellipsometry experiments. Objective 2. We have built a fiber-based terahertz emitter and a fiber-based terahertz detector with multiple dimensional adjustability, including synchronous rotation. The established emitter and detector can be linearly adjusted in three-axis dimensions and precisely tilted to optimize the beam focus. The synchronous rotation allows independent polarization control of the beam generation and detection. Objective 3. We have built a THz Time-domain spectroscopy system with free incident angle adjustment for highly flexible THz ellipsometry measurements. As mentioned in objective 2, a new fiber-based emitter and detector were assembled in a multiple-axis holder with a rotator to precisely control the polarization state. The high extinction ratio (ER) bilayer polarizer is installed on the 3-D printed adaptor and adapted to the detector to provide a perfect linear polarization detection. Two free-standing terahertz polarizers from MicroTech Inc. provided less extinction ratio but larger aperture for controlling the incident polarization state and selecting the components of the reflected beam. The whole emitter axis can be freely tuned from -90° to +90°, covering all the incident angles necessary for ellipsometry measurements and can be easily changed to transmission geometry when setting at 0°. Objective 4. We have developed acquisition software using LabVIEW for the THz ellipsometry system. The software provides both rapid scan mode for fast signal preview and step scan mode for precise signal detections. The software allows settings of the moving waiting time of the delay line and the integration time constant, providing an accurate time-position control and a high signal-to-noise ratio. We also developed a novel processing algorithm for accurate ellipsometry data analysis. We have experimentally verified the algorithm as a highly accurate method for ellipsometry: it greatly reduces the error sensitivity on the polarizers and provides highly accurate phase information. The initial results of the algorithm have been accepted by the IRMMW-2017 conference and will be further optimized and submitted to a journal soon. Objective 5 We have measured different phantom samples by the ellipsometry system, including standard low-absorption crystal quartz, high-absorption Glabervel glass. Our results show that the established ellipsometry system and the corresponding processing algorithm provide greatly improved accuracy compared to the existed publications. The result of high-absorption glass and biomedical samples also demonstrate that ellipsometry shows its merits on high-absorption samples and provides much less restrictions on sample preparations. Objective 6 We have successfully used our established system with the developed acquisition software and processing algorithm for measuring some biomedical samples of porcine muscle and skin. These samples are both very difficult to measure in transmission geometry due to their high absorption and the difficulty of cutting them into very thin slices. Sample preparation for the ellipsometry system is much easier as long as a flat surface of samples can be provided. Porcine muscle and skin samples were wax-embedded and cut to provide an optically flat surface. The samples were measured under 63° incident angle, which is expected to be close to the Brewster angle of the sample to provide a good contrast between the reflected s- and p- components. The incident polarization state was set to 16° to the p- direction according to our developed algorithm to reduce the error sensitivity on the polarizers. Reflected s- and p- components are measured with a 13° polarization direction being detected as well for phase correction, according to our developed algorithm. The resulting refractive index and absorption coefficient are calculated according to Fresnel’s equations.

415313.label: Major findings and research outcome
415313.value: In this project we have completed the setup and establishment of a THz ellipsometry system. The system provides all the characteristics necessary for ellipsometry measurements, including all fiber-coupled antennas, free incident angle adjustment, multi-dimensional control of the emitter and detector with precise rotation ability, three precisely aligned polarizers for polarization control and multi-dimensional sample holder for accurate reflection adjustment. We have also developed acquisition software and data analysis algorithm for ellipsometry measurements. The software provides accurate signal acquisition and the algorithm has been verified as an accurate method for data processing. We have also used our elipsometry system, acquisition software and processing algorithm for sample measurements of different types, including biomedical samples. We have finished all the fundamental work for the system and metrology parts of this project and have achieved very promising results which will have great impact in the terahertz community as well as the ellipsometry community. This project has an output of 9 journal papers and 12 international conference proceedings. These publications relate to different aspects of the project, such as developing optical components to help build the THz ellipsometry system (journal papers 1 and 4); developing algorithms for more accurate and faster data acquisition (journal papers 5, 8 and 9); and investigation of biomedical applications (journal papers 2, 3, 6 and 7). Our future work will focus on in-vivo measurements using the ellipsometry system (e.g. hand skin measurements). Compared to ex-vivo samples, the challenge will be to to perfectly align the THz beam on to the subject and keep the subject perfectly stable for the whole measurement.

415313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
415313.value: We plan to further develop our research to the applications of in-vivo measurements. In vivo-measurements on human subjects can only be performed in reflection geometry. However, traditional substrate-based reflection measurement has unavoidable contact problem, while non-substrate based reflection geometry cannot provide correct phase reference. Ellipsometry is a promising technique which solves both the contact and phase problem by its self-reference characteristics. We will work on the design and fabrication of a suitable holder for in-vivo subjects and then optimize the system to allow in-vivo measurements. The holder will be carefully designed and to provide multi-dimensional adjustment to allow precise focus control. The system will also be optimized to provide space for placing in-vivo samples. Corresponding data processing methods will also be developed. We will also develop the project to facilitate thin-film sample measurements. This type of measurement requires accurate phase measurement, multiple incident-angle measurements and more complicated data processing. The system is basically ready for this type of samples and we believe we are able to get some promising results soon.

415313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
415313.value: Terahertz (THz) ellipsometry is a challenge due to the need for high quality broadband polarisers operating at THz frequencies – polarisers at visible frequencies are much more established. In our project we have investigated several aspects of THz ellipsometry including developing THz devices, devising algorithms, building and calibrating a THz ellipsometry system and measuring biomedical samples of interest. In particular, we have designed and fabricated our own polarisers to meet the needs of our THz system. We have also developed various algorithms to improve the accuracy of THz spectroscopy including a novel method for establishing and aligning a THz ellipsometry system and for calibrating ellipsometry signals for precise THz ellipsometry measurements. Our method is a significant improvement as our resulting THz ellipsometry system achieves far greater accuracy compared to previous publications.

415413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
415413.value: Cells in many biological tissues are required to sustain large mechanical forces. Cells in such loaded conditions experience mechanical damages regularly, compromising their plasma membranes and cytoskeletons. If not repaired in a timely manner, these damages would lead to cell death and tissue failure. The cellular self-repair of the damaged plasma membrane follows a cascade of well-orchestrated molecular events. It is hypothesized that there exist damage thresholds beyond which the cellular self-repair mechanisms would not suffice to cope with the imposed challenge. It is likely that such damage thresholds would depend on cell type, loading conditions, and environmental contexts. In situations where damage exceeds the self-repair capacity of the cells, the damage becomes irreversible and cells apoptosis and tissue necrosis would follow. Once the threshold is passed, additional local and nonlocal resources plus other extrinsic conditions would need to be in place to support a much longer process of cellular and tissue regeneration. Cells are subject to oxidative stress in many situations, as normal metabolic activities commonly involve many redox processes. Cells in oxidative environments often need to continue to sustain mechanical loading. The overall goal of this project is to study the mechanics of cell damage and repair under oxidative stresses that are physiologically threatening. We will focus on the damage and repair biomechanics of C2C12 myoblasts and fused myotubes, and 3T3-L1 pre-adipocytes under various oxidative conditions. This study addresses a number of key issues in presure ulcers due to epidermal loading, involving deep muscle and fat tissues. This is a persistent clinical problem in rehabilitation medicine faced by millions of persons with physical disabilities. To deliver controlled quantifiable dosages of biophysical damages to the cells in-vitro, we will use both laser photoporation and direct microindentation. To simulate the oxidative challenges, we will subject the cells to various concentrations of hydrogen peroxide for different durations. We will study the associated cell mechanics using an atomic force microscope. To understand the kinetics involved, we will monitor the changes in the intracellular Ca++ and reactive oxygen species concentrations, and in the biomarkers associated with cell damage, repair and viability. We will integrate our experimental in-vitro results into a computational model on a multiphysics multiscale theoretical platform, so as to articulate our understanding coherently and quantitatively. The proposed cell culture study ties in well with our animal studies in GRF project (523810) and our theoretical studies in GRF project (521812). 很多生物组织的细胞须要面对庞大的机械力. 在这种载荷下, 细胞经常受到破损, 损及细胞膜及细胞骨格. 若不及时修复, 破损可导致细胞死亡及组织损毁. 细胞膜破损的自我修复涉及一连串紧密的分子过程. 可假设破损若超过某一临界, 自我修复将不足驹应付. 这个临界非常可能随不同细胞, 载荷, 及环境因素而改变.当破损超过细胞的自我修复能力临界, 破损成为不可逆转, 随来是细胞凋亡及组织坏死. 当破换超过临界後, 细胞须要更多的外援及更长的过程才能再生. 细胞在正常的新陈代谢中常要面对氧化的压力. 就算如此, 细胞仍要继绩承载不同的机械力. 这项目的最高目的是研究在氧化威胁下细胞的破损及修复. 我们会集中研究不同氧化条件下C2C12成肌细胞及肌融合管状细胞的破损及修复. 这研究要处理皮肤受力作用下在深层肌肉中所引起的压疮问题. 这是数以百万设计肢体残疾人仕要面对的复康问题. 我们会用光学成洞及直接的微压头方法提供可量化的生物物理破损. 我们会以不同浓度的H2O2及不同长短时间仿拟不同程度氧化环境. 我们会以原子力显微镜测试细胞力学. 透过追踪细胞内钙离子及ROS浓度, 及相关生物标记来了解所牵涉的动态过程.我们会以一个多物理多尺度的理论平台综合这项目不同的实验结果, 以达至一个可量化, 互相吻合的理解.

415413.label: Realisation of objectives
415413.value: Objective 1: To determine the damage thresholds of the C2C12 cells by characterizing their dose-dependent damages by laser photoporation and direct micro-indentation, and their subsequent self-repair kinetics. (Research Outputs # 3, 4, 6) We measured the compressive damage threshold of C2C12 myoblasts. Spherical indentation was applied onto a layer of agarose gel (3 mm thick) covering a monolayer of myoblasts. Cell damage was recognized by using a cell membrane damage assay, propidium iodide. The spatial profile of the measured percentage cell damage was correlated with the radially varying stress field as determined by finite element analysis to estimate the compressive stress threshold for cell damage. Damage threshold was measured in term of the combinations of stress levels and durations causing ~10% cell death, which was ~3x natural cell death. Damage threshold followed an inverse sigmoidal relation between compressive stress level and duration. We measured the damage thresholds of myoblasts under prescribed compressive strains (15% and 30%) and shear strains (from 0% to 100%). A flat plate was used to apply a uniform compressive strain and a radially increasing shear strain on disks of gelatin–methacrylate (GelMA) hydrogel with myoblasts encapsulated within. The percentages of cell death were estimated with propidium iodide and calcein AM staining. Results suggested that cell death depended on both the level and duration of the applied strain. There seemed to be a non-linear coupling between compression and shear. We monitored the damage evolution after single myoblasts were individually subjected to femtosecond (fs) laser photoporation on their plasma membranes. A well characterized tunable fs laser was coupled with a laser scanning confocal microscope. The post-damage wound evolution was documented by real-time imaging. The fs laser generated a highly focused hole at a targeted site of the myoblast plasma membrane. The initial hole size depended on the laser dosage in terms of power and exposure duration. Myoblasts showed difficulty in repairing holes with initial size beyond certain threshold. Within the threshold, holes could apparently be resealed within 100 s under the normal condition. Objective 2: To investigate in the C2C12 cells their biomechanical changes and the corresponding changes in their biomarkers of cellular damages and self-repairs after different oxidative exposures. (Research Outputs # 1, 2, 5, 12) We examined various effectors of the Rho signaling pathway, which has been shown to play a key role in the control of cell mechanics. H2O2 decreased the cell stiffness in a dose-dependent manner, caused cell death, and reduced the RhoA expression that was accompanied by down-regulation of α-actin, cytoskeleton-membrane linker proteins (ezrin–radixin–moesion proteins), and focal adhesion. Modulating the Rho signaling by using a Rho activator partially restored the cell stiffness, enhanced the cell viability, and decreased the intracellular ROS level. We studied how the regulatory proteins of actin polymerization could be up- or down- regulated in the presence of oxidative stress. We showed that in chronic oxidative stress, cofilin was up-regulated, thus favoring actin de-polymerization, while thymosine-beta-4, a cofilin competitor, was down-regulated. However, after brief oxidative exposure, cofilin was down-regulated. The patterns of changes with chronic versus brief oxidative exposures were consistent with cell stiffness measurements using AFM. We documented the postdamage morphological changes of the C2C12 myoblast cell bodies and nuclei after femtosecond laser photoporation targeted at the plasma membrane. In normal conditions, the cell bodies underwent significant shrinkage after single-site laser photoporation on the plasma membrane. However for the cells bearing hydrogen peroxide oxidative stress beforehand, the cell bodies showed significant swelling after laser photoporation. The post-damage morphological changes of single cells were more obvious after chronic oxidative exposure than that after acute ones. We used the same femtosecond laser to nano-scissor cytoskeletal actin stress fiber within myoblast and studied the subsequent viscoelastic retraction to assess cytoskeletal pre-tension. We applied this technique to study the effects of oxidative stress on the cytoskeletal mechanics. Our results suggested that after brief exposure to oxidative stress, the cytoskeletal actin stress fibers tend to be pre-stressed significantly more. In addition, it was also noted chronic exposure to oxidative stress apparently could increase the internal friction in the cytoskeletal rheological processes. Objective 3: To study the damage thresholds of the C2C12 cells by photoporation and micro-indentation and the corresponding changes in their biomarkers of cellular damages and self-repair kinetics after different oxidative exposures. (Research Outputs #3, 4, 6) This objective was pursued in conjunction with Objective 1. Cell damage under micro-indentation and shear depended on both the level and duration of the applied stress / strain, following an inverse sigmodal relation. Chronic oxidative stress compromised the capability of muscle cells to withstand compressive and shear damages, while short oxidative stress enhance such capability. A femtosecond (fs) laser was used to generate a highly focused hole on the myoblast plasma membrane. Bigger holes were obtained in the myoblasts after oxidative pretreatments. In chronic oxidative conditions, more myoblasts could not have their holes resealed. In contrast, brief exposure to oxidative stress apparently could promote resealing in myoblasts. Objective 4: To explore the potential of enhancing cellular regeneration after damage beyond the self-repair thresholds through co-culturing the cells with macrophages. We mechanically damaged myoblasts with macrophages in proximity and observed little interaction between these cells in our co-culture model with apparently no myoblast regeneration. In the lack of any positive results after months of various attempts by a PhD student, we decided to explore other alternatives, namely the preventive use of surfactant poloxamer-188 and intermittent vibration. Our alternative approaches led to our research outputs #8, 10, 11. Objective 5: To construct a multiphysics multiscale computational platform to theoretically integrate these in-vitro results to hypothesize a coherent quantitative understanding of the mechanics of cell damage and repair. (Research Outputs #7, 9) We conducted a finite element (FE) analysis of how oxidative stress induced changes in the actin cytoskeletal structure affected a myoblast’s capability to resist damage under compression. A confocal-based cell-specific FE model was built to parametrically study the effects of stress fiber density, fiber cross-sectional area, fiber tensile prestrain, as well as the elastic moduli of the stress fibers, actin cortex, nucleus and cytoplasm. The results showed that a decrease in the elastic moduli of both the stress fibers and actin cortex could increase the average tensile strain on the actin cortex–membrane structure and reduce the apparent cell elastic modulus. Assuming the cell would die when a certain percentage of membrane elements were strained beyond a threshold, a lower elastic modulus of actin cytoskeleton would compromise the compressive resistance of a myoblast and lead to cell death more readily. This model was used with a Weibull distribution function to successfully describe the extent of myoblasts damaged in a monolayer under compression. We used COMSOL to simulate the compressive stress distribution and the diffusion of biowastes in a semi-3D buttock finite element model. In vitro results showed that biowastes collected from cells damaged under prolonged low compressive stress were more toxic (as compared to brief high compressive stress) and could compromise the capability of normal myoblasts to resist mechanical damages. In-silico results showed that higher biowastes diffusion coefficient, higher biowastes release rate, lower biowastes tolerance threshold and earlier timeline of releasing biowastes would cause faster propagation of tissue damage. This study highlighted the importance of biowastes in the development of deep tissue injury to clinical pressure ulcers under prolonged skeletal compression.

415413.label: Major findings and research outcome
415413.value: Cell damage under micro-indentation and shear depended on both the level and duration of the applied stress / strain, following an inverse sigmodal relation. Chronic oxidative stress compromised the capability of muscle cells to withstand compressive and shear damages, while short oxidative stress enhance such capability. (3,6) AFM results showed that short oxidative exposures increased cell stiffness, but that long exposures made the cells softer. The turning point took place somewhere between 1hr and 2hrs of oxidative exposure. Such stiffness change was mediated via the Rho signaling pathway and involving actin filaments depolymerization associated with the down-regulation of thymosin beta 4, and up-regulation of cofilin2 and profilin1. (1, 2) We used a confocal-based cell specific finite element model to show that a decrease in actin cytoskeletal elastic modulus could reduce the elastic modulus of the cell, increase the average tensile strain on the actin cortex-membrane structure, and compromise the compressive resistance of a myoblast. (7) A femtosecond (fs) laser was used to generate a highly focused hole on the myoblast plasma membrane. Bigger holes were obtained in the myoblasts after oxidative pretreatments. In chronic oxidative conditions, more myoblasts could not have their holes resealed. In contrast, brief exposure to oxidative stress apparently could promote resealing in myoblasts. Changes were also observed in the rheology of the cytoskeletal stress fibers and overall cell morphology. (4, 5, 12) The biowastes released by cells damaged under prolonged low loading were more toxic than those released by cells damaged under brief high loading. Using a computational model of a human buttock seated on an elastic cushion, we simulated the significant effects of such toxic biowastes on the propagation of deep tissue ulcers. (9) We mechanically damaged myoblasts with macrophages in proximity and observed little interaction between these cells in our co-culture model with apparently no myoblast regeneration. In the lack of any positive results, we decided to explore other alternatives, namely the preventive use of surfactant poloxamer-188 and intermittent vibration. With poloxamer 188 (P188) pre-treatment, muscle cells could maintain their compressive damage threshold in oxidative environments. Actin polymerization dynamics remained stable. Ability to reseal membrane damage was preserved. P188 pretreatment apparently help muscle cells retain their mechanical integrity in oxidative environments. (10) Application of 35 Hz, 0.25 g intermittent vibration during prolonged compression decreased the compression-induced oxidative damage and muscle breakdown in aged mice. A possible explanation is that the anti-oxidative defense could be maintained with intermittent vibration during compression. (11)

415413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
415413.value: A natural extension of this study is to monitor the intracellular redox status of cells real-time during prolonged loading till they ultimate death. We have begun some pilot studies to explore the correlation between cell viability and such mechanically induced intrinsic oxidative stress.

415413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
415413.value: Deep tissue injury due to prolonged excessive loading can lead to clinical pressure ulcers. We assessed the duration-dependent damage thresholds of muscle cells in compression and shear using myoblasts in-vitro, and studied the effects of oxidative stress on such thresholds. We examined the effects of oxidative stress on cytoskeletal polymerization and used AFM to study the corresponding changes in cell stiffness. We used femtosecond laser to evaluate how oxidative stress affects the pre-tension in the cytoskeletal fibers and the ability of cells to repair submicron-pores on their plasma membranes. Using a confocal image based finite element model, we simulated the effects of the biochemically compromised cytoskeleton on the tensile strain in the cell membrane when the myoblast was subjected to compressive loading. Our findings also suggested interesting implications of damage vulnerability when cells were exposed to biowastes released from other damaged cells in their neighborhood, or when cells were subjected to prolonged oxidative exposures, such as during chronic inflammation. We examined the protective effects of a surfactant cell membrane stabilizer poloxamer-188 and of intermittent vibration on pressure-induced deep tissue ulcers.

415513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
415513.value: Speech disorders affect all aspects of life and the general well-being of the individual. Dysarthria is among the most common speech disorders associated with motor control and affects millions worldwide. Possible etiologies are diverse, leading to different dysarthric types. Their motor impairments have global effects on speech production. Acoustic manifestations include hoarseness in voice quality, imprecise articulation, excessive nasalization and disordered prosody, all of which reduce speech intelligibility. These manifestations are complex – the dysarthric types cannot be distinguished by disparate sets of dysfunctional speech features. The dysfunctions also exhibit intra- and inter-speaker variability. To gain a better understanding of dysarthria, we are faced with the challenge of analyzing its complex and variable manifestations in speech acoustics. Treatment of dysarthria typically requires a speech pathologist to devote individualized attention to a subject’s speech and conduct perceptual assessment to classify the type, characterize the severity, evaluate the intelligibility, devise intervention strategies and monitor progress. This is a costly process. Also, perceptual assessments are susceptible to inconsistencies due to human subjectivity and biases due to listeners’ learning effects. This situation calls for data-driven, computational techniques that can analyze the complexities of dysarthric speech objectively and automatically. Automation can also enable speech pathologists to treat a larger dysarthric population in need. Existing research in computational analysis of dysarthric speech predominantly focuses on automatic intelligibility assessments to achieve high correlations with human judgments. Major languages include English, Dutch, etc., with a paucity of work for Chinese. We need to design and collect a Chinese corpus to support our research. We propose to develop a phonologically-motivated framework for computational acoustic characterization of error patterns in dysarthric speech. We will leverage the parsimonious description of speech segments afforded by distinctive features (DFs), which have correlates in both articulatory and acoustic domains. We will develop automatic speech recognition techniques for detection of DFs from the speech signal, which also enables efficient analysis of a large amount of speech data. Corpus-based analysis and comparison between the DF-based representations of normal and dysarthric speech will elucidate problematic articulatory gestures that cause errors and reduce intelligibility. Articulatory problems identified can inform the development of intervention strategies. Investigations in both English and Chinese will enable better understanding of the language-specific and language-independent aspects of dysarthria. DFs offer a unique advantage here due to their language-independent nature. Our findings will benefit the large population of dysarthric speakers, especially the Chinese-speaking dysarthric community. 语言障碍影响生活的各个方面。构音障碍是最常见的言语障碍，影响世界各地数以百万计的人。可能的原因是多种多样的，导致不同的构音障碍的类型。他们的神经障碍对语言产生多种影响， 包括音质嘶哑，发音不正确，过度鼻音化和韵律无序等，所有这些都降低语音清晰度。 同时，这些声学特征会复杂地混合出现，并有基于个别说话人及说话人间的变化。为了更好的理解构音障碍，我们面临着分析复杂的， 可变度高的语音声学特征的挑战。构音障碍的治疗通常需要一个语言病理学家对病人的语音作出个人化的听觉评估，描述障碍类型，严重程度，可懂度，及制定干预策略和监测进展 -- 这是一个昂贵的过程。同时，听觉评估会受主观性及对病人的熟悉程度影响。 这种情况需要数据化驱动的计算技术，可以客观地，自动化地分析大量的语音，也能帮助言语病理学家治疗更大的构音障碍的人群。现有的构音障碍研究，主要集中在自动化的可懂度评估，与个人的判断能达到颇高的相关性。主要的语言包括英语，荷兰语等，缺乏针对中文的研究。我们需要收集语料来支持我们的研究，设计一个以音韵学为中心的框架，针对构音障碍引起的语音错误做出声学特性的计算。我们将利用音韵学区别性特徵（DFs）简洁的描述语音段中相关的发音及声学特征。我们将开发的语音识别技术对大量数据作出有效分析和DFs检测。我们会分析和比较正常及障碍语音的语料，致力于阐明问题发音的声学特征，从而帮助设计干预策略。基于英文与中文的比较和研究，我们将能够更好地了解构音障碍语音在单一语言中和跨语言的特性。DFs的语言独立性对于语音的描述提供了一个独特的优势。我们的研究结果将造福患有构音障碍的人群。

415513.label: Realisation of objectives
415513.value: We have designed and collected a Chinese dysarthric speech corpus that include over 30 speakers. We designed the stimuli to include a range of speaking styles including single word, short sentence, paragraph and conversation, as well as articulatory tasks. These tasks can help isolate specific articulatory or performance characteristics, e.g. ability in pitch control. The task structure references the Frenchay Dysarthria Assessment. Overall the recording prompts cover all Cantonese initials and finals in the Jyutping system, as well as combinations with lexical tones. We have also designed the full set of equipment for recording setup, and recording can be conducted in any quiet meeting room. The impaired movement of muscles due to dysarthria often leads to utterances that have prolonged pause intervals, slow speaking rates, poor articulation of phonemes, syllable deletions, etc. These present challenges towards the use of speech recognition technologies for automatic processing of dysarthric speech data. Based on the English TORGO dysarthric speech corpus, we developed a strategy to recover from performance degradation in automatic phonetic forced alignment on dysarthric speech, as compared with normal speech. The strategy locates long pauses in dysarthric speech and used these as anchors. Then speech recognition for word lattice outputs is applied to recover the time-stamps of the words in disordered or incomplete pronunciations. By verifying the initial alignments with word lattices, we can obtain reliably aligned segments. These segments provide constraints for new alignment grammars and can improve the alignment quality and hence transcription quality. This proposed strategy obtained improved alignments for most dysarthric speech data, based on TORGO, while maintaining good alignments for non-dysarthric speech data. The strategy is generalizable to other dysarthric speech corpora. We proposed the Distinctive Feature (DF)-based Framework to identify problematic articulatory patterns of dysarthric speakers. The identification of such problematic articulatory patterns aims to assist speech therapists in developing intervention strategies. The framework includes 21 distinctive features covering the articulators and manners of articulation. We also created a specially category of “unspecified” DF, to accommodate feature spreading in continuous speech. We have developed a suite of DF detectors based on neural networks (multi-layered perceptrons), one for each DF, which can then automatically detect the DF vectors corresponding to each phone in a spoken utterance. Hence we are able to analyze each subject’s speech by comparing the DF based on the canonical phone, DF based on manual annotation and DF based on automatic detection, which enables us to observe the DF errors. The Pearson correlation of DF substitution error rates between automatic detection and manual annotation averages 0.7 across DFs. If we consider the average DF error rate across subjects, the correlation between automatic detection and manual annotation is at 0.9. We have full achieved the project objectives as proposed.

415513.label: Major findings and research outcome
415513.value: We have designed and collected CU DYS – the Chinese University Dysarthric speech corpus for Cantonese. The design rationale references the Frenchay Dysarthric Assessment for the English language. We cover all the Cantonese initials and finals in Jyutping, and their combinations with lexical tones. This design and collection processes are documented in a paper in the proceedings of INTERSPEECH 2015. Since the impaired movement of muscles for speech production leads to utterances with prolonged pause intervals, slow speaking rates, poor articulation of phonemes, syllable deletions, etc., it is challenging to work on automatic analysis of dysarthric speech data. We addressed the problem of forced alignment using speech recognition techniques. We developed alignment grammars (by focusing on long pauses as anchors, followed by word lattice-based recognition) which can improve the alignment and transcription quality for most dysarthric speech, while maintaining good alignments for non-dysarthric speech data. This work is also published in the proceedings of INTERSPEECH 2015. We have developed a Distinctive Feature (DF)-based framework to capture problematic articulatory patterns of dysarthric speech in terms of DFs, which aims to assist speech therapists in developing intervention strategies. A neural network (NN) based system is trained with non-dysarthric speech data for DF recognition. Feature detection in normal speech achieves a correct rate of 85.7%. Performance decline for dysarthric speech ranged from 1% to 3% for mild cases, 4% to 7% for moderate cases, and 7% to 12% for severe cases. We also observed that the DF disagreement patterns are consistent with the analyses of a speech therapist. This work is published in the proceedings of the ISCA Workshop on Speech and Language Processing for Assistive Technologies, 2015. A pilot phonological analysis of dysarthric speech was conducted and published in the International Symposium on Chinese Spoken Language Processing 2016 The DF framework covers 21 distinctive features covering the articulators and manners of articulation. Together with the full suite of NN-based DF detectors, we are able to automatically analyze DF errors. The Pearson correlation of DF substitution error rates between automatic detection and manual annotation averages 0.7 across DFs. If we consider the average DF error rate across subjects, the correlation between automatic detection and manual annotation is at 0.9. This work was published in the IEEE International Conference on Acoustic, Speech and Signal Processing 2016.

415513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
415513.value: We have collected a very valuable asset of the Cantonese dysarthric speech corpus from subjects with this speech disorder. This is, to the best of our knowledge, the most systematically designed and largest dysarthric speech corpus to date. This corpus will be able to support many other investigations in the future, such as speech recognition of disordered speech, voice restoration, etc. We believe that this line of research is extremely important for addressing the needs of subjects with the communicative disorder of dysarthria, and will also illuminate our understanding of other related speech disorders. We will be conducting future research in disordered speech recognition and voice restoration.

415513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
415513.value: Speech disorders affect all aspects of life and the general well-being of the individual. Dysarthria is among the most common speech disorders associated with motor control and affects millions worldwide. To gain a better understanding of dysarthria, especially in the linguistic context of Hong Kong, we have designed and collected CU DYS, the Chinese University DYSarthric speech corpus in Cantonese. To the best of our knowledge, this is the most systematically designed and largest dysarthric Cantonese speech corpus to date. Treatment of dysarthria typically requires a speech pathologist to devote individualized attention to analyze a subject’s speech. This is a costly process. Hence we have developed a data-driven, computational framework that can analyze the complexities of dysarthric speech objectively and automatically. This new Distinctive Feature (DF)-based framework can describe problematic articulatory patterns of dysarthric speech in term of DFs. We have also developed a full range of DF detectors (based on neural networks) to support the framework and enable automatic analysis of spoken utterances. We also verified that the detected DF patterns are consistent with the analyses of a speech therapist. We believe that such a framework can potentially enable speech pathologists to treat a larger dysarthric population in need.

415613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
415613.value: Gastrointestinal (GI) disorder is one of the most common diseases in human body. The GI cancer rate and death rate are approaching those of the number 1 killer: lung cancer. Endoscopy is the most frequently used clinical procedure for detection of the GI cancers at their early stages. Wireless capsule endoscopy, during which the patients just swallow a capsule-shaped camera with wireless image data transmission, has been proved to be a convenient, non-invasive and relatively effective way to examine the whole GI tract. However, the size and power limitations of the current capsule endoscope can only perform image-based examinations without any therapeutic functions. To unleash the potential power of the device and to fulfill the need of therapeutic functions, we propose to develop a modular wireless capsule endoscopic robotic system with three capsular modules: imaging module, drug delivery module and battery module, which can be assembled into a therapeutic robotic system to achieve the functions of externally controlled GI track examination, medicine spray, and additional power supply. Each module has a permanent magnet at one end and an electromagnet with iron core at the other end to form the reversible linkage. The attraction of the magnet in one capsule and the oppositely charged iron core in another will make the two modules connect. The modules will be disconnected by changing the electromagnet iron core polarity to repel the connected module to release the linkage. In addition, the drug delivery module is used to spray medicine at the desired locations identified by the imaging module, and the battery module provides extra power supply as a backup device. This proposed therapeutic modular robotic system is able to perform more functions than the traditional examination capsule endoscopy. It facilitates better endoscopy that is easy, safe, and comfortable for the patients to use, with added useful functionality. In addition, the proposed research will provide a platform that enables further development with more complicated functions and operations, such as biopsy and small tumor removal etc. 腸胃道不適是人類最常見病之一。腸胃道癌症發病率和死亡率正在快速逼近第一殺手肺癌。內窺鏡是檢查早期腸胃道癌變的有力手段。通過口服進入體內的無線膠囊內窺鏡技術成就了病人的無痛、無傷檢查，深受歡迎。但目前商用無線內窺鏡膠囊由於體積和供電等限制，只能做檢查而沒有任何治療功能。本項研究旨在研發一個具有精確投放藥品等簡單治療功能的模塊化多體無線膠囊內窺鏡機器人系統。該系統包括三個模塊：內窺鏡視覺模塊、精確藥品投放模塊、以及附加供電電池模塊。三組模塊組合後通過外部遙操作，完成腸胃道檢查、精確藥品投放、以及附加供電功能。模塊之間的連接和斷開有模塊上兩極處的電磁開關控制。這個模塊化系統具備了傳統內窺鏡的簡單治療功能，同時又兼備無線膠囊內窺鏡的無痛、無傷檢查功能。這個能夠提供治療功能的簡單、安全、舒適的模塊化無線膠囊內窺鏡技術不但成就了病人的無痛、無傷檢查和簡單治療，還為下一代可提供腸胃道病理採樣和無創傷去除腸道內癌變組織的功能開發建立了基礎和平台。

415713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
415713.value: 网络信息论研究如何将 Shannon 的点对点通信理论 [1] 拓展至多用户网络的情形。由于与无线通信的建模密切相关，加性高斯噪声信道模型在网络信息论里有着非常特殊的地位。事实上，这一领域的大部分研究者仅专注于这一特殊模型，而不是更一般的无记忆设定。 网络信息论有着大量悬而未决的基本问题，而过去五年里，项目负责人一直专注于其中一些问题。事实上，近几年项目负责人的大部分工作着重于更一般的离散无记忆广播信道，并且取得了一些不平凡的重要进展，参见《网络信息论》 [2] 第五、八章。最近，受离散无记忆设定下的一些技巧启发，项目负责人成功地解决了加性高斯噪声模型下的一个非常重要的公开问题：在需要传输私人及共同信息的要求下，判定两用户矢量（即 MIMO）高斯广播信道的容量区域 [3]。该项工作的主要意义不仅仅在于它解决了上述问题。事实上解决问题的方法非常新颖：它不依赖于熵幂不等式、Fisher 信息量，或者是最小均方估计的一些等价形式，而是采用了一个分解不等式以及高斯分布在旋转变换下的不变性。这是一组更简单的方法。采用这些方法，不仅能更简单地证明已有的结果，还能得出新的结果。在该项目提议里，通过深入研究这种新方法，我们期望解决一些其他的采用加性高斯噪声设定的基本问题。 其中一个基本的加性高斯噪声情形就是两用户高斯干扰信道，其容量区域四十年来尚未解决。这一信道模拟了一个常见的场景：两组发送接收者通过一个共享媒介作点对点通信，导致互相干扰。人们感兴趣的核心问题是判定容量区域，即能够可靠地传输的码率对的集合。最近，该问题已有显著进展：[4] 文作者将容量区域的估计精确到1比特以内；[5,6,7] 三文作者独立地计算了一些弱干扰情况下的最优码率和。 在高斯干扰信道这一问题上，项目负责人目前已经与 Max Costa 一起工作超过一年。对于特定的弱干扰情况（信道参数在初始值附近且严格涵盖上述 [5,6,7] 三文），当输入为高斯分布时，我们精确地计算出 Han-Kobayashi 内界。我们初期的工作事实上得出了一些新的观察以及有希望推动进一步探索的方向。这些观察表明，参数空间包含了很多不同的位面，而这在此前尚属于未知。在该项目提议里，项目负责人期望通过结合 [3] 里提出的证明高斯分布最优性的技巧，来考察这些有希望的研究方向。 总而言之，该项目提议旨在采用 [3] 里提出的方法来研究加性高斯信道模型的容量区域。特别地，作者期望首先专注于采用 [8] 作出的令人激动的观察来研究干扰信道，然后再研究其他高斯信道模型。具体而言，重点在于通过拓展高斯信道模型里的新方法和新工具来得出精确的结果。

415713.label: Realisation of objectives
415713.value: The objective of the proposal was to understand in broad terms the optimal extremal distributions in additive Gaussian noice settings of network information theory. Indeed, more often than not, Gaussians turned out to be extremal distributions and this had been previously shown using the famous Entropy Power Inequality of Shannon and Stam. The project was the result of the discovery of a novel method to establish the optimality of Gaussian distributions and use it to establish the capacity region of a broadcast channel setting (published in 2014), for which he received the prestigious 2016 IEEE Information theory society paper award. Researchers, including the PI, then observed that this new method had similarities to some methods used in functional analysis, especially those by Lieb, Carlen, etc. The methods exploited an invariance of the gaussian distribution and the functional to a "doubling" operation though the mechanics of proving optimality was much simpler using the information theoretic tools as opposed to the previous arguments and relied on the Skitovic-Darmois characterization of Gaussians. The discovery of this connection and the subsequent pursuit of this became the subject of a parallel investigation by the PI. The purpose of this proposal was to investigate the Gaussian interference channel, another central problem in multiuser information theory, and see if anything can be said about the optimizers. The initial approach to this problem was to obtain a better understanding of the genie based approach that had been used recently (in the relative age of the problem) to derive the sum capacity in a subset of the weak interference regime. Towards this end, the PI defined a class of discrete-memoryless interference channels with very weak interference and used the genie based approach to derive the sum-capacity of a sub-class by building on the genie approach. More significantly, the PI also showed that there are regimes where the genie approach will fail to meet the conjectured sum capacity, i.e. treating interference as noise. These results are related to Objective 1 (and indirectly Objective 2) of this proposal. Motivated by the Gaussian interference channel, the PI started looking at maximizing the weighted sum-rate of a sub-class of channels with very weak interference called the Clean Z-interference channels. This study immediately yielded huge dividends as we were able to isolate examples where the Han-Kobayashi region for the interference channel was strictly sub-optimal thous solving problem that had been open for three decades. This counterexample was obtained by using temporally correlated input distributions or what is called multi-letter expressions. This result implied that, for the Gaussian Z-interference channel, the functional involved did not directly satisfy the naive tensorization property and hence evene the new method cannot be used to imply the Gaussian extremality. Further, it became apparent that one need to consider multi-letter expressions with Gaussian signaling and see if this improved the achievable region for the Han-Kobayshi region. In 2016 and 2017 we were able to show that this did not lead to any improvement for the Z-interference channel and finally in late 2017 we were able to show it for the entire Han-Kobayashi region. This is related to Objectives 2 and 3 of this proposal. This result also sheds light on potentially new ideas that can be used to show Gaussian optimality. We also dsicovered an enhanced Genie based outer bound that unified all previous outer bounds to the Gaussian capacity as well as discrete channels. This became the central element of the doctoral thesis of Sida Liu. Finally while studying the extremal distributions for degraded broadcast channel in the fading case, we could show that Gaussian were not extremal and this can be either demonstrated by using mixture of Gaussians or using Hermite Polynomials. This is related to Objective 4. In Summary, the study of the problems outlined in this proposal had led to resolution of long standing open problems and in rekindling connections between information theory and functional analysis. Reasons for not complete realization of objectives: Objective 1. Sum-capacity has only been realized for a partial class of very weak interference channels. But novel approaches were developed towards this end. Further we also demonstrated that the approach we developed would not answer in the entire regime. We made significant progress on the problem, yet there are some not resolved regimes. However the progress we made, we believe make significant progress in our understanding for this long-standing problem. Objective 3: This has been done in parallel by other researchers, some building on our work. So, we cannot claim that we solved the problem by ourselves. Objective 4: We showed that Gaussian signaling is not optimal. This sub-optimality can be demonstrated by either considering a mixture of Gaussians or by using Hermite polynomials. There is a simple capacity achieving expression, so the question is to find the extremizing distribution. After the sub-optimality of Gaussian distribution was shown, our hope was to get a distributional equation satisfied by the optimizer. This is still a work in progress. In summary, we marked under achieved if other people were involved in achieving the objective or there are some remaining aspects to be solved even though we made significant progress in solving these central problems. Notes: I wish to note that I have oftentimes acknowledged the grant using 2150785, which is the internal CUHK bursar's code of this grant due to my misunderstanding of the numbering convention. In one of the paper (2014) I completely missed acknowledging any grant. I am really sorry about that absent-mindedness.

415913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
415913.value: Visual quality assessment (VQA) is very important in image/video applications, such as image/video compression, quality monitoring during transmission, watermarking, advertising, and archiving. VQA aims at evaluating the perceptual quality of the image/video after processing. The VQA can be achieved by subjective and objective means. Subjective VQA involves many subjects (or viewers) giving opinion scores on the perceptual quality of the images/videos being assessed. On the other hand, an objective visual quality metric (VQM) can be derived based on the subjective scores obtained by the subjective VQA methods. Mean square error (MSE) and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) are widely adopted as benchmarks for objective measure of subjective quality, since they are simple to implement. However, they cannot accurately depict the perceptual quality of the visual signals. Therefore, many researchers have devoted their efforts to developing new VQMs for not only evaluating the quality of the visual signals but also guiding the corresponding image/video applications. Retargeting methods have recently been proposed to meet the display requirements of different communication devices, such as PC, tablet, mobile phone, etc., which are ubiquitous in our everyday life. However, since different displays are of different resolutions, retargeting methods must be employed to adapt the same visual signal for display on different devices. This poses new challenges for VQA to ensure a good perceptual quality of the retargeted signal when displaying on these different devices. To evaluate the perceptual quality of the retargeted images, a subjective quality database for retargeted images will be constructed with a large collection of images of different contents and resolutions, generated by using all existing retargeting methods. In order to ensure reliable and unbiased results, an online subjective evaluation platform will be set up, where viewers from different cultures and regions of the world are asked to perform the subjective evaluation via the Internet. The subjective scores collected will be analyzed to obtain an accurate subjective value for each retargeted image. Next, an accurate visual quality metric (VQM) for the retargeted images will be developed by jointly considering the shape distortion and content information loss of the retargeted image. These two distortions will be studied and characterized. How to combine them together with the HVS properties in the VQM formulation will be investigated. Finally, the VQM will be validated using our constructed subjective retargeted image quality database. 視覺質量評價在圖像/視頻的應用中非常重要，比如圖像/視頻壓縮，傳輸過程中的質量監控，數字水印，廣告，以及儲存。視覺質量評價目的在於衡量處理後的圖像/視頻的質量。我們可以通過主觀以及客觀的方法來衡量圖像/視頻的質量。主觀的方法需要很多的參與者（觀察者）通過觀看圖像/視頻給出相應圖像/視頻的質量分數。而另一方面，客觀的質量評價方法可以基於主觀方法所得到的主觀圖像質量分數進行開發。均平方差以及峰值信噪比是最被廣泛採用的客觀基準質量評價方法。其原因在於這兩種客觀方法易於實現。但是他們不能準確的描述視覺信號的質量。因此，很多的研究工作者致力於開發新型的質量評價方法，不僅可以評價視覺信號的質量，而且可以指導相應的圖像/視頻的應用。 縮放方法最近被用於顯示圖像/視頻，以適應於不同的通訊設備不同顯示屏幕的要求，例如個人電腦，平板，移動手機。這些通訊設備現在已經普及於人們每日生活中。但是，因為不同的通訊設備有不同的顯示分辨率。因此，縮放方法用於將同一視覺信號顯示在不同分辨率的通訊設備上。這對現在的質量評價方法提出了新的挑戰。如何將縮放的圖像以很好的質量顯示在不同的通訊設備上。 為評價縮放圖像的質量，我們需要構建一個由縮放圖像組成的主觀質量數據庫。這個數據庫由一個大規模的不同內容以及不同分辨率的圖像組成，其中的縮放圖像由業界開發的縮放方法產生。為了保證可靠以及無偏差的主觀質量，我們將開發一個主觀實驗的平台。其中來自不同的文化背景，世界不同地區的參與者將通過互聯網進行主觀測試。所搜集得到的主觀質量分數經過分析以標識每一幅縮放圖像的主觀分數。 進而，我們將針對縮放圖像開發一款精確的視覺質量評價標準。這個質量評價標準將聯合考慮圖像的形狀失真以及內容信息的失真。這兩種失真都會被學習以及刻畫。我們將進一步研究如何將這兩種失真與人眼視覺系統的特性結合在一起。最後，這個主觀質量評價標準將在我們構建的主觀數據庫上被測試以及驗證。

415913.label: Realisation of objectives
415913.value: Objective 1: To construct a subjective retargeted image database with a large number of images which are retargeted into different resolutions with different image retargeting methods. A subjective quality database for retargeted images has been constructed with a large collection of images of different contents and resolutions, generated by using all existing retargeting methods. The images are categorized into four classes according to attributes such as 'face and people', 'clear foreground object', 'natural scenery', and 'geometric structure'. There are altogether 57 source images in which frequently encountered attributes are included. In this database, only two retargeting ratios, i.e. 50% and 75%, are employed to generate the retargeting images. There are ten state-of-the-art candidate retargeting algorithms in comparison, i.e., cropping, scaling, seam carving, optimal seam carving and scale, non-homogeneous warping, scale and stretch, shift map, multi-operator, energy-based deformation and streaming video. For each original image, only three retargeted images are manually selected among all the 20 possible retargeted results for the database. The retargeted image database can be accessed via the link: http://ivp.ee.cuhk.edu.hk/projects/demo/retargeting/index.html. Objective 2: To build an online subjective testing platform to measure the perceptual quality of the retargeted images, where the subjects’ agreement will be examined and the subjective scores processed to generate the final subjective quality index for each retargeted image. An online subjective testing platform to measure the perceptual quality of the retargeted images has been built which is accessible via the same link as the retargeted image database given above. The user interface of the online subjective testing platform shows the source and the retargeted images side-by-side on a visual display. The quality scales are labeled as “Bad”, “Poor”, “Fair”, “Good” and “Excellent”, which range from the lowest to the highest perceptual quality index. During the subjective evaluation, the subjective values are recorded in numerical values. The participants select the appropriate quality index based on their own judgement. In order to reduce the effect of the viewer fatigue, the 171 retargeted images are divided into two sessions. The first session contains 69 images, while the second one contains 102 images. For each session, it will take the viewer about 10–20 min to accomplish the subjective testing. The order of the image pairs (the source image and the retargeted image) is randomly arranged which varies for each participant. In order to avoid the contextual and memory effects on the participants’ judgement of the quality, the retargeted images which are generated from the same source image will not be presented consecutively. Furthermore, in order to prevent the scaling effect, the source image and the retargeted image must be displayed in their native resolution. All the subjects participating in the subjective testing are students having normal vision (with or without corrective glasses) and have passed the color blindness test. For the first session, 15 viewers who are experts in image processing participated in the subjective test. In the second session, each image was rated by 34 participants, with 18 viewers who are experts in image processing. Objective 3: To analyze the subjective scores on the retargeted images, and characterize the shape distortion and content information loss attributes that affect the subjective quality of the retargeted image. The results are processed to obtain the mean opinion scores (MOS) of all the retargeted images. Furthermore, the histogram of the MOS scores is plotted graphically. It is observed that the perceptual qualities of the retargeted images in the database span the entire range of visual quality and exhibit good perceptual quality separation. Also, it demonstrates that the subjective study samples a range of perceptual quality in an approximately uniform fashion, which results in a good separation. The distortions introduced during the retargeting process are mainly categorized into shape distortion and content information loss. The shape distortion measurement is critical in the evaluation of retargeting image perceptual quality. We studied the performances of different shape descriptors, such as PHOW, GIST, MPEG-7 descriptors, EMD, for evaluating the perceptual quality of the retargeting images, which are examined using our public image retargeting subjective quality database. Experimental results demonstrated that most of the shape descriptors can hardly capture the characteristics representing the quality of the retargeting image, but the global shape descriptor GIST presents significant performance gains. Moreover, by combining the measurements from content information loss, a better performance is obtained. Objective 4: To derive a perceptual model that combines the shape distortion and content information loss together, and to develop a quality metric for evaluating the retargeted images. Next, we turned our attention to quality evaluation of images under content-adaptive retargeting, in which the sizes of the images may differ from each other. It is known that shape distortion and content information loss are two main factors in the evaluation of the retargeting quality. In this study, a region-based scheme is proposed to evaluate the shape distortion and information loss caused by retargeting. We tested the proposed algorithm on the public database RetargetMe. Experiments demonstrated that this region-based quality assessment algorithm outperformed other schemes based on pixels. We further developed a novel no-reference quality assessment (NR-QA) method for retargeted image based on the rank learning approach. Firstly, image features for each retargeted image are extracted, which should not only represent the image characteristics but also be sensitive to the retargeted distortions. Specifically, the image feature should be able to capture the shape distortions, which are the commonly encountered distortions of the retargeted image. Based on the extracted image features, the rank learning method is employed to train a model to discriminate the perceptual quality of the retargeted image. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively depict the perceptual quality of the retargeted image, which can even perform comparably with FR quality assessment methods.
