415913.label: Major findings and research outcome
415913.value: 1. A subjective quality database for retargeted images has been constructed with a large collection of images of different contents and resolutions, generated by using all existing retargeting methods. The retargeted image database can be accessed via the link: http://ivp.ee.cuhk.edu.hk/projects/demo/retargeting/index.html. 2. An online subjective testing platform to measure the perceptual quality of the retargeted images has been built, where the subjects can access and evaluate the subjective quality of a retargeted image with reference to the source image to provide a subjective score which can then be used to generate a subjective quality index for each retargeted image. The subjective testing platform is accessible via the same link as the retargeted image database given above. 3. The subjective scores of the retargeted images were analyzed. It was observed that the scores span the entire range of visual quality and exhibit good perceptual quality separation. The distortions introduced during the retargeting process are mainly shape distortion and content information loss. It was found that the global shape descriptor GIST can capture the shape distortion characteristics well, and when combined with the content information loss, the performance is enhanced. A journal paper (Section 8, paper #1) and a conference paper (Section 9, paper #1) based on the research findings were published. 4. A region-based (instead of pixel-based) perceptual model that combines the shape distortion and content information loss together was derived. It outperformed all other pixel-based schemes. A novel no-reference quality assessment (NR-QA) method for retargeted image based on the rank learning approach was developed. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively depict the perceptual quality of the retargeted image, which can even perform comparably with full-reference (FR) quality assessment methods. A journal paper (Section 8, paper #2) and three conference paper (Section 9, paper #2, #3 and #5) based on the research findings were published.

415913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
415913.value: Content-aware image retargeting adjusts images to arbitrary sizes and preserves visually salient content. Previous algorithms formulate the problem in terms of either pixel level or mesh level structures, deforming salient objects inconsistently. To improve retargeting quality and reduce complexity, a patch-wise method to generate sparse image grids based on visual saliency and gradient magnitude should be used. Some preliminary work has been done by optimizing three energy functions to warp the grids and generate retargeted images (See Section 9, paper #4). In content-aware image retargeting, many types of deformation inconsistency occur resulting in shape distortion, deformation artifacts and content information loss, which degrade its perceptual quality. The deformation inconsistency occurs at different levels of the retargeted images. Due to the inaccurate alignment between the original and retargeted images, previous methods only focus on pixel-level and patch-level fidelity analyses and fail to detect the deformation inconsistency. The alignment algorithm can be improved and the retargeting process formulated as a three-level representation. Based on the analysis of this three-level representation, both the fidelity measures and inconsistency detection can be combined to determine the final retargeting quality (See Section 8, paper #3).

415913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
415913.value: Retargeting is the enabling technology that makes it possible for one to view the same digital content using different devices. For example, you can watch the same movie on your smartphone, tablet, laptop, or PC, even though the displays are of different resolutions. The trick is to scale the resolution of the original movie to that of the display device. There is a whole host of retargeting techniques for image and video. However, the overriding objective is to preserve the semantic content of the image/video while maintaining its subjective quality. In this respect, the subjective quality evaluation of the retargeting image/video is of paramount importance since the human viewer is the ultimate assessor. The project investigates the factors affecting the subjective quality of retargeted images. A subjective quality metric has been formulated and validated using our subjective image retargeting database built purposely for this project. Based on the subjective quality measurement, the retargeting algorithm can be fine-tuned to suit the particular application and display device.

416113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
416113.value: The aim of this project is to conduct research to improve the energy efficiency of successive approximation register (SAR) analogue-to-digital converters (ADCs). ADCs are the bridge between the analogue real world and the exponentially expanding digital world. Among different types of ADCs, SAR ADCs are unmistakably important due to their high energy efficiency and amazing versatility. The state-of-the-art SAR ADCs are often at the frontier of the ADC energy efficiency map. The overall energy efficiency of SAR ADC is mostly determined by the energy efficiency of one of its blocks: the (usually capacitive) digital-to-analogue converter (DAC). A capacitive DAC consumes energy only when its capacitors switch. Significant progress has recently been made in reducing the DAC switching energy for SAR ADCs. In the proposed project, we will investigate four new techniques to further improve the DAC switching energy efficiency for SAR ADCs. In our theoretical analysis, two new techniques have the potential to consume 62% less switching energy for 10-bit ADCs compared with the previous best technique using the same unit capacitor size and reference voltage. They also perform better in terms of differential nonlinearity. We will choose two the new SAR techniques for realization in CMOS technologies. The two prototype chips are designed for different applications, one for medium-bandwidth (~1MSps) biomedical signal acquisition and the other for wide-bandwidth (~100MSps) high-definition video signal acquisition. This research will enable many of the devices that use the proposed techniques to improve their overall power efficiencies, and thus contribute to a greener environment. 此項目旨在提高逐次逼近式模擬 - 數字轉換器（SAR ADC ）的能源利用效率 。 ADC是模擬的現實世界和以指數式擴展的數字世界之間的橋樑。在不同類型的ADC中， SAR ADC以其高能效和多用途性尤其重要。最先進的SAR ADC的往往處在ADC能源效率地圖的最前沿。 SAR ADC的整體能源使用效率主要取決於其數字模擬轉換器（DAC ）（通常是電容性的）的能源效率。電容式DAC只在當它的電容開關時才消耗能量。最近在降低SAR ADC的DAC開關能耗已取得重大進展。 在此項目，我們會研究四項新技術，以進一步提高了SAR ADC的DAC的開關能源效率。在我們的理論分析中，其中兩項新技術有可能減少62%的開關能耗（與以前的最好技術在使用相同大小的單元電容和相同參考電壓並基於10位元ADC下相比較) 。這些技術也會有更好的微分非線性。我們將選擇其中兩項新技術在CMOS工藝上實現。兩個原型芯片將面向不同的應用，其一為中等帶寬（～1MSPS ）生物醫學信號採集應用，另一為寬帶寬（～100MSPS ）高清晰度視頻信號的採集應用。 這項研究最終應可應用於不同的電子設備，以提高它們的整體電源效率，從而有助於環保。

416113.label: Realisation of objectives
416113.value: Objective 1 has been fully achieved. We have conducted a theoretical analysis of the energy efficiency of the proposed four new SAR ADC switching techniques, and the theoretical results have been validated by behavioural simulations in Matlab. The results of the proposed SAR switching techniques are briefed below. The proposed SAR ADC switching scheme No.1, named as SAR ADC with LSB-down, has been shown to consume a switching energy less than the conventional SAR and the split-MSB SAR, but higher than those of the set-and-down SAR and the Vcm-based SAR. The proposed SAR ADC switching scheme No.2, named as SAR ADC with split-MSB and LSB-down, has been shown, compared the previously most efficient technique (the Vcm-based SAR), to consume less energy in the LSB transition while retaining the same energy in other bit transitions. Its additional advantage in differential nonlinearity is also validated by behavioural simulations. The proposed SAR ADC switching scheme No.3, named as SAR ADC with split-MSB and charge recycling, has been shown to be able to improve the switching energy by 60% compared to the previously most efficient technique (the Vcm-based SAR) for a 10-bit resolution under the condition of the same unit capacitor size. It also offers better differential linearity than other SAR techniques under the same capacitor mismatching conditions. The proposed SAR ADC switching scheme No.4, named as SAR ADC with a unit capacitor array, has been shown to be as efficient as the proposed SAR ADC switching scheme No.3, but provides even better linearity performance. However, its switching decoding scheme is far more complex than other approaches. Objective 2 has been fully achieved. Based on the outcome of objective 1, we have picked the proposed second (split-MSB and LSB-down) and the third (split-MSB and charge recycling) techniques to realize two energy-efficient SAR ADCs in a low-cost 0.13um CMOS process. Both ADCs have sampling rates of 1.1-MSps and resolutions of 10 bits, suitable for applications in low-power multi-channel electroencephalograph signal acquisition systems. The SAR ADC with the proposed split-MSB and LSB-down switching scheme reduces the area and switching energy by 50% and 87% compared with the SAR ADC with the conventional binary weighed array (BWA) switching scheme under the same unit capacitor value. Moreover, capacitor matching requirement is relaxed by 75% for a given mismatch condition. The project proves the high power efficiency of the proposed scheme with a prototype SAR ADC designed and fabricated in a 0.13um CMOS process. The prototype consumes 23.2uW under a 1-V analog supply and a 0.5-V digital supply. It achieves a measured signal-to-noise-plus-distortion ratio (SNDR) of 55.2dB and an effective resolution bandwidth up to 1.1MHz when it operates at 1.1MSps. The figure of merit (FoM) is 44.1 fJ/conversion-step, which, when normalized to the unit capacitor size, was among the best at the time of reporting. The SAR ADC with the proposed split-MSB and charge recycling technique exhibits a 95% reduction in switching energy, a 50% reduction in capacitor area, and 30% reduction in nonlinearity compared with the conventional SAR ADC with BWA switching scheme with the same unit capacitor size and matching condition. The improvement in the switching energy consumption is the best among reported SAR ADC switching techniques. The prototype SAR ADC consumes 15.6uW from a 0.5-V digital supply and a 1-V analog supply. It occupies a chip area of approximately 0.84mm2 with a unit capacitor value of 30fF. Measurements show that it achieves an SNDR of 55dB, a spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) of 60.8dB for an input near the Nyquist frequency (worst case). The corresponding FoM is 31.8fJ/conversion-step. At its publication time (2015), the FoM, when normalized to the unit capacitor size, was the best in the world. The high power efficiency of the proposed SAR ADC switching technique with split MSB and charge recycling has therefore been proven. Objective 3 has been fully achieved. We have investigated a wide-bandwidth medium-resolution energy-efficient SAR ADC for realization in a CMOS process. A 16.5-MSps 12-bit pipelined SAR ADC has been designed in a 0.18um CMOS, which is targeted for high-quality video signal acquisition. The ADC is composed of the first stage of a 6-bit SAR ADC and the second stage of a 7-bit time-to-digital converter. The SAR stage applies the proposed charge recycling switching technique. From simulations, the ADC consumes only 290uW power from a 1-V single supply. The achieved effective-number-of-bits (ENOB) is 11 bits. The corresponding FoM is 8.17fJ/conversion-step, which is among the best in the world at this sampling rate and resolution range.

416113.label: Major findings and research outcome
416113.value: The project has discovered four new capacitor switching schemes that have advanced the power efficiency of SAR ADCs. The first SAR switching scheme discovered is the LSB-down switching scheme. It can be applied on top of any existing differential SAR switching schemes to halve the area of its capacitor array and the switching energy consumption. When applied in the existing power-efficient Vcm-based switching scheme, the method achieves 93% less switching energy and 75% less chip area with the same linearity performance, compared with the conventional BWA switching scheme. The theoretical analysis and behavioural simulations of this technique are reported in the output item 8.3. The second SAR switching scheme discovered is the split-MSB with LSB-down scheme. With a typical resolution of 10 bits, it is capable of reducing the area and switching energy by 50% and 87% compared with the conventional BWA scheme. Moreover, capacitor matching requirement is relaxed by 75% under a given capacitor mismatch condition. The project proves the effectiveness of the technique with a prototype 1.1-Msps 10-bit SAR ADC fabricated in a 0.13um CMOS process. The theory, circuit designs and experimental results of this new scheme are detailed in the output item 8.2. The third SAR switching scheme discovered is the split-MSB with charge recycling. It combines the above two switching schemes but introduces a never-before-used step of charge recycling that boosts the power efficiency. With a typical resolution of 10-bits, it is capable of reducing the area, switching energy and differential nonlinearity by 50%, 95%, and 30%, respectively, compared with the conventional BWA scheme under the same unit capacitor value and matching conditions. The project proves the effectiveness of the technique with a 1.1-Msps 10-bit SAR ADC fabricated in a 0.13um CMOS technology. The SAR ADC achieved the best energy efficiency (normalized to the unit capacitor size) in the world at the time of publication. The theory, circuit designs and experimental results are detailed in the output item 8.1. The fourth SAR switching scheme discovered is the reverse Vcm-based scheme. It is capable of reducing the switching energy by 98.4% compared to the conventional BWA scheme. This tri-level scheme removes the need for a Vcm-driver and any associated power consumption. A new reset scheme is also proposed to reduce the energy consumption incurred in the reset phase in every sample. Outcome item 9.1 details the theory, designs, and simulation results of this scheme.

416113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
416113.value: The SAR switching scheme that was discovered the latest in the project, i.e., the reverse-Vcm switching scheme, has been shown in theory and simulation to be the most power efficient one, capable of reducing the capacitor switching energy by 98.4% compared to the conventional BWA scheme while eliminating the power associated with Vcm driver and reducing reset energy. However, it is not yet realized in silicon to prove it with experimental results. Therefore, a further development of the research is to realize an SAR ADC with the reverse-Vcm switching scheme in a CMOS process. A low supply voltage and custom-made tiny capacitors can be applied to assist achieving high power efficiency.

416113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
416113.value: SAR ADCs are important due to their high power efficiency and a wide spectrum of applications. Improving the power efficiency is a never-stopping quest of researchers, and can enable some new power-conscious electronic products. The power efficiency of SAR ADCs is largely determined by the power efficiency of their capacitor switching schemes. In this research, we have developed four new switching schemes that have advanced the power efficiency of SAR ADCs. We have designed and fabricated two medium-speed and medium-resolution SAR ADCs in a low-cost CMOS technology. These chips are suitable for multi-channel EEG signal acquisition applications. The experimental results from these chips have verified the high power efficiency for two of the proposed switching techniques. They achieved the best energy efficiency at the dates of publications. We have also validated the two other techniques by transistor-level simulations. To highlight a specific achievement, we proposed to apply the concept of charge recycling in the SAR ADC switching process to save the power consumption. The charge recycling technique can be widely applied in future generations of SAR ADCs that are embedded in many power-conscious electronic devices to prolong the battery time and to reduce energy waste.

416213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
416213.value: Rapid advances in electronic and optical technologies have led to extensive use of broadband RF and optical signals in communications, sensors, and instrumentation. Effective approaches for the monitoring and processing of such high-bandwidth signals are very desirable. The conventional electronic measurement approach suffers from the high cost and limited availability of high-speed devices and circuits. The measurement is also susceptible to electromagnetic interference. An ultimate solution to boost the measurement capability is to exploit the intrinsic bandwidth and parallelism of optics in signal monitoring and processing. Out of the various approaches, wavelength-division processing has demonstrated unique advantages that leverage on the maturity of wavelength-division multiplexing technology in fiber communications. Many needed active and passive devices and modules are available at low cost. There are however few reports on wavelength-division signal processing, partly due to the complexity and stringent requirement of the optical transmitter that needs to be specially designed for the purpose. In this proposal, we aim at demonstrating new and efficient transmitters that produce high-repetition-rate short pulses at interleaved wavelengths. We further investigate their use in the sampling of broadband optical and electrical waveforms, as well as in multichannel processing of digital optical communication signals. The optical source will first be recognized using an actively mode-locked quantum-dash semiconductor laser driven optically at ~ 40 GHz. The compact and integrable device will generate thermally stable, low-jitter, and low-chirp pulses through a dispersion-managed external cavity that enables self-seeding with time- and wavelength-interleaved pulses. We will compare the transmitter performance with one realized from spectral slicing of a supercontinuum produced by actively mode-locked fiber laser pulses in a nonlinear fiber. The fiber supercontinuum source benefits from a larger saturated output and a broader bandwidth. By introducing proper delay times to pulses centered at different sliced wavelengths, the interleaved output can reach a repetition rate up to hundreds of GHz. The output will be applied for real-time sampling of both an arbitrary optical waveform in a nonlinear medium and an RF waveform in an electro-optic device. Applications in dynamic optical performance monitoring and in a digital coherent receiver will be pursued. We will also explore multi-channel regeneration of optical communication signals based on serial processing with the interleaved pulses in a fiber optical parametric amplifier. Finally, we will investigate practical limitations of our processing approach including the scalability in the number of wavelengths, the signal bandwidth, and the data rate. 電子和光學技術的快速發展，引起寬帶無線電頻信號和光信號在通信、傳感器和儀器技術領域的大量應用。有效地監控和處理高帶寬信號的方法是非常需要的。傳統的電子測量方法受到高速器件和電路的可用性和高成本的限制，而且其測量還容易受到電磁場干擾。爲了提高測量性能，根本解決方案就是要開拓固有的帶寬和充分利用並行光學的特性來對信號進行監控和處理。 在眾多方法之中，波分信號處理憑借波分複用技術在光纖通信應用的成熟度，已經顯示出其獨特的優勢。許多所需要的有源和無源器件和模塊的已經能以低費用來獲取。但是，還是很少有關於波分複用信號處理的報告，在一定程度上是由於為達到這目的所特別設計的光發射器具有複雜性和要滿足嚴格的要求。在這個提案中，我們的目標是展示全新而有效的發射器，產生高重複率的波長交織短脈衝。我們還將進一步研究其在寬帶光學和電學波形的採樣和多通道數字光通信信號的處理上的使用。光源將首先採用以40 GHz頻率光學驅動的主動鎖模quantum-dash半導體激光器來實現。這個小型集成的裝置會產生熱穩定，低抖動，低啁啾的脈衝，通過色散調控的外腔，使得所產生的時間和波長交織的脈衝能夠實現自激注入。我們將在性能上對比該發射器與另一種通過切割超連續譜的方法所實現的發射器，而該超連續譜是由主動鎖模光纖激光器產生的脉衝通過非線性光纖所生成的。光纖超連續譜光源的好處在於其更大的飽和輸出和更寬的帶寬。通過在擁有不同中心波長的脉衝中引入適當的延遲時間，時間與波長交織的脉衝輸出便可以達到高達數百GHz的重複率。這脉衝輸出將被應用在非線性介質中任意光波形和在電光設備上無線電頻信號波形的實時採樣。同時，我們還追求該脉衝在動態光學性能監測和數字相干接收機方面的應用。我們也將探討基於串行處理的利用交織脈衝在光纖光學參量放大器再生多通道的光通信信號的情況。最後，我們將研究我們的處理方法實用性上的限制，包括波長數，信號帶寬和數據速率的可擴展性。

416213.label: Realisation of objectives
416213.value: 1. To design and investigate efficient optical transmitters for the generation of tunable time- and wavelength-interleaved pulses beyond 40 GHz repetition rate. We have successfully completed the design and have built tunable optical transmitters that performed up to 100 GHz using time- and wavelength-interleaved optical pulses. The transmitter can produce 4x10GHz, 8x10GHz, and 10x10GHz outputs. The generation relies on spectral slicing of a supercontinuum source seeded by a 10-GHz actively mode-locked fiber laser in a dispersion-flattened highly nonlinear fiber, followed by appropriate group velocity dispersion in a standard singlemode fiber. The uniformity of the temporal spacing is limited by the non-zero dispersion slope of the singlemode fiber over a wide wavelength range. To address the issue, we propose two solutions based on either increasing the input pulse rate or using non-uniform wavelength spacing of the pulses to improve the temporal uniformity. The purity of the electrical spectral characteristics is influenced by both the uniformity of the pulse amplitude and the optical pulse shape. Both effects have been thoroughly studied. Furthermore, the fractional temporal Talbot effect has been applied to provide repetition rate multiplication of the optical pulses. In particular, we have demonstrated a new technique using preceded binary intensity modulation before the Talbot effect takes place to achieve tunable multiplication. 2. To demonstrate the use of time- and wavelength-interleaved pulses for ultrafast real-time sampling of optical and/or RF waveforms. To evaluate the pulses for sampling application, we performed measurement on properties including time-bandwidth product, phase noise, and time jitter. The measured time-bandwidth product of 0.78 to 0.82 indicates a slightly chirped output which can be improved by spectral filtering and optical phase adjustment. By integrating the phase noise from 100 Hz to 1 MHz carrier offset, we obtain a time jitter of 2.04 to 3.42 ps that is limited by the 10GHz actively mode-locked seed fiber laser in the generation of the pulse source. Consequently, the sampling performance is relatively poor and results in undesirable distortion. To sample optical waveforms, we apply ultrafast four-wave mixing process in a nonlinear fiber. We investigate the use of stimulated Brillouin scattering to control optical phase matching and improves efficiency and bandwidth of the mixing process. During the sampling process, we observe that the signal distortion can be suppressed by applying Raman amplification in the fiber. By optimizing the operating parameters, we have succeeded in achieving 16 dB reduction in the second harmonic distortion component. The mechanism of improvement is the suppression of parametric pump depletion through Raman amplification in the fiber. In addition, we also demonstrate crosstalk mitigation in polychromatic sampling in which the signal is replicated to increase the effective optical sampling rate. 3. To investigate the use of wavelength-division sampling architecture for dynamic monitoring and detection of coherent signals, and to explore multichannel processing of optical communication signals with time- and wavelength-interleaved pulses. We have completed the design and built the setup for the generation, processing, and detection of coherent communication signals. The setup has been used to investigate QPSK and 16-QAM modulation formats up to 32 GBaud. Multichannel processing has been realized using fiber-optic parametric amplification (FOPA) as described in our proposal. We also investigate phase sensitive amplification. By applying nonlinear scattering processes including stimulated Brillouin scattering and stimulated Raman scattering, we are able to control the optical phase and improve the optical gain in the signal processing. The crosstalk is also suppressed between multiple channels at different wavelengths. As a result, the receiver sensitivity is improved. Furthermore, the saturation characteristics of Raman amplification has been investigated. Optical phase conjugation has been successfully demonstrated for optical OFDM signals consisting of 256 subcarriers with QPSK encoding, and 8-point cyclic prefix. Serial-to-parallel data processing involving time and wavelength interleaved pulses been demonstrated using time lens approach assisted by Raman amplification. To miniaturize the setup on the monitoring and detection of coherent signals, we have completed the design, fabrication, and characterization of novel photodetectors based on graphene integrated on silicon nitride waveguides. We have successfully developed photodetectors integrated with rib and slot waveguides, as well as with ring resonator cavities.

416213.label: Major findings and research outcome
416213.value: On the generation of high-repetition-rate optical pulses for optical signal processing and communications, we have investigated different approaches based on resonating cavity based [C11] and cavity-less schemes [C15]. The seed pulses have been multiplied up to ~ 80 GHz using the fractional temporal Talbot effect in an optical fiber. Programmable repetition-rate multiplication has been realized without changing the fiber length [J17, C13]. In addition, time- and wavelength interleaved pulses can also be generated by time lens processing using four-wave mixing in a nonlinear fiber. Uniformity of the processing has been improved by applying Raman amplification [J18, C14]. To perform ultrafast real-time sampling, we first characterized the time- and wavelength-interleaved pulses. It is observed that the timing jitter is relatively large and is limited by the actively mode-locked fiber laser source. Optical sampling is performed using ultrafast four-wave mixing [J1, J7, J15]. The processing bandwidth and efficiency have been enhanced by controlling the phase matching between the interacting waves [J13, C9]. By applying Raman amplification, the second harmonic distortion is greatly suppressed by 16 dB through the compensation of pump depletion [C8]. To further increase the effective sampling rate, we apply polychromatic sampling by copying the input signal waveform to different wavelengths. The associated crosstalk has been mitigated again by applying Raman amplification [J19, C16]. A coherent communication system has been built and was able to operate at 32 GBaud with 16-QAM data modulation [C15]. To perform multichannel processing, we investigate the use of fiber optical parametric amplifier and its crosstalk suppression [J2, J3, J5, J10] and extend our study to phase sensitive amplification [J4, J11]. We have also investigated optical phase conjugation for optical OFDM signal compensation [J6, C8] and high-performance wavelength multicast of coherent communication signals [J19, C12]. A serial-to-parallel data conversion scheme has been demonstrated to convert serial data to parallel outputs at different wavelengths using Raman assisted time lens processing [J18, C14]. Finally, we also investigate miniaturization of the setup by designing, fabricating, and characterizing on-chip waveguide photodetectors integrated with 2-D graphene materials for improved responsivity [J8, J9, J12, C10].

416213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
416213.value: In achieving the objectives of ultrafast optical sampling and multichannel optical processing as stated in Objectives 2 and 3, we observe that the performances of four-wave mixing and optical parametric amplification can be significantly enhanced by applying backward Raman amplification in the fiber. The parametric pump depletion is reduced and the crosstalk among multiple channels is suppressed. Therefore, we have submitted a GRF proposal on Raman-assisted optical processing to investigate the mechanism and to understand the physical constraints. The proposal was subsequently funded by RGC. The optical coherent communication system built in the course of running this project was assembled by pieces of components and equipment borrowed from different laboratories, companies, and universities. Its performance in terms of data rate, noise, and stability is relatively poor. To further investigate and support research projects that can make use of such a facility, we have worked with colleagues in CUHK Information Engineering Department and Hong Kong Polytechnic University to submit a preliminary proposal to the Collaborative Research Fund. The preliminary proposal has been shortlisted by RGC in 2017. We are in the process of preparing a full proposal to build an advanced lightwave testbed for the photonic community in Hong Kong.

416213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
416213.value: In the era of big data, there is much need to process vast amount of signals in the information network. Optical processing scheme benefits from its ultrafast performance, transparence to data formats, data rates, and communication protocols, as well as electromagnetic interference immunity and potential for low power consumption. To take full advantage of optical processing, we have investigated new optical processing tools based on advanced optical pulse sources and processing schemes. Our results demonstrate that with specialized design of high-speed pulse sources and processing conditions, we can effectively increase the processing capability in reducing undesirable signal distortion and increasing the processing rate through multichannel processing. The results are of crucial significance for future development in high-speed instrumentation and optical communications.

416413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
416413.value: 距離幾何中一個基本問題就是在給定維數的空間中進行定位。針對這問題的其中一個傳統辦法就是進行凸鬆弛，因它有很好的理論基礎，並能給出高效和精確的算法。我們在這項目裏提出以非凸最優化的方法去考慮上述的定位問題，原因是非凸的模型能更準確地刻畫原來的問題。我們的目標是要提出高效的多項式時間算法，並研究新的非凸模型對圖論裏面剛度理論的意義。本項目的成果將對定位問題的理論和算法有著突破性的影響。

416413.label: Realisation of objectives
416413.value: In this project, we first resolved a fundamental conjecture in linear algebra and compressive sensing by establishing a perturbation inequality for concave functions of singular values (such as the Schatten quasi-norm). A well-known consequence of this result is that it provides necessary and sufficient conditions for low-rank matrix recovery, which includes the fixed-dimensional localization problem as a special case. This significantly advances our understanding of the theoretical properties of Schatten quasi-norm regularization in localization and allows us to achieve Objective 1. Next, we achieve Objective 2 by designing algorithms for two highly practical localization problems - time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA)-based source localization under non-line-of-sight (NLOS) conditions, and TDOA-FDOA (frequency-difference-of-arrival)-based multiple source localization. The former arises frequently in indoor localization scenarios, while the latter is key to locating signal-emitting targets by formation-flying satellites. For both problems, we designed Schatten quasi-norm regularized semidefinite programming (SDP)-based algorithms, and the computational results showed that our proposed approach outperforms those in the literature. Lastly, we conducted a theoretical analysis on the optimization geometry of the classic TDOA-based source localization problem. Although the problem is well known to be non-convex, we proved, for the first time, the surprising result that when the measurement noise power is not too large, the likelihood function is actually strongly convex around a neighborhood of the maximum-likelihood estimator (MLE). This implies that properly initialized first-order (resp. second-order) methods, which generally are computationally less expensive than SDP, can converge linearly (resp. quadratically) to the MLE. This provides a theoretical justification on why first- and second-order methods for solving the TDOA-based source localization problem tend to perform well in practice and allows us to achieve Objective 3.

416413.label: Major findings and research outcome
416413.value: The major findings of this project have already been summarized in Sec. 5.3 above. They have led to the publication of two journals articles - one in Applied and Computational Harmonic Analysis and one in IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing (both are top-ranked in their respective fields) - and two conference articles - one in the 2016 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing (ICASSP) and one in the 7th IEEE International Workshop on Computational Advances in Multi-Sensor Adaptive Processing (CAMSAP).

416413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
416413.value: Our findings suggest several directions of future research. First, it would be interesting to develop first- or second-order algorithms to solve Schatten quasi-norm regularized SDPs, as existing interior point methods for solving such problems do not scale very well. Second, the TDOA-FDOA-based multiple source localization problem can be formulated as a mixed-integer quadratically constrained quadratic optimization problem. Currently, the convex relaxation for this problem relaxes both the integer variables and the continuous variables. However, given the advances in mixed-integer conic optimization, it is worth investigating the practicality of solving a mixed-integer conic relaxation of the problem, as such an approach can yield better solution quality than the convex relaxation approach. Third, it would be interesting to see whether other localization problems possess nice geometry that allows them to be solved more efficiently by first- or second-order methods. The outcomes of this study will contribute to the rapidly growing literature on the analysis of structured non-convex optimization problems.

416413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
416413.value: In this project, we studied the design and analysis of algorithms for locating targets based on distance/frequency measurements. Such problems arise frequently in practice, such as indoor localization and the localization of signal-emitting targets by formation-flying satellites. The outcomes of this research project provide fast and reliable solutions to various localization problems and have potential implications in search and rescue, tracking and surveillance, route planning, etc.

416713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
416713.value: In this proposal, we propose to model the complex web image collection with a novel automatically generated graph structure, called visual semantic complex network (VSCN). The nodes on this complex network are clusters of images with both visual and semantic consistency, called semantic concepts. They are connected based on the visual and semantic correlations. Multiple fundamental structures of the complex network will be studied for the VSCN, including the small world behavior, concept community, in-degree distribution, hub structures, and isolated concepts. It not only helps us to better understand the web image col-lections at a macroscopic level, but also has many important practical applications. We propose to study two application examples using such a visual network: content-based image retrieval and image browsing. 在本项目中，我们提出了一种新型的自动生成的网络图形结构来模拟复杂的互联网图像集合，称为视觉语义复杂网络（VSCN）。这个复杂网络的节点由视觉和语义都很相似的图像集群构成，称为语义概念。它们的连接是基于视觉和语义相关性。复杂网络的多种基本结构将被用来研究VSCN，包括小世界现象，概念社区，连接度分布，枢纽结构，和孤立概念。它不仅可以帮助我们更好地在一个宏观的层面了解互联网图像集合，还有许多重要的实际应用。我们会研究这种可视化网络的两个应用实例：基于内容的图像检索和图像浏览。

416713.label: Realisation of objectives
416713.value: All the objectives of this project have been realized successfully. (1) We developed a new approach to model the complex web image collections with an automatically generated graph structure called visual semantic complex network (VSCN). The nodes on this complex network are clusters of images with both visual and semantic consistency, called semantic concepts. These nodes are connected based on the visual and semantic correlations. Our VSCN with over 33 thousand concepts is generated from a collection of 10 million web images. A great deal of valuable information on the structures of the web image collections can be revealed by exploring the VSCN, such as the small-world behavior, concept community, in-degree distribution, hubs, and isolated concepts. It not only helps us better understand the web image collections at a macroscopic level, but also has many important practical applications. We also present two application examples: content-based image retrieval and image browsing. Experimental results show that the VSCN leads to significant improvement in both the precision of image retrieval (over 200%) and user experience for image browsing. (2) We also explore the application of this new network concept to other application domain, such as exploration of music. We introduce MIL: a music exploration prototype which integrates music (M), image (I), and lyrics (L), for efficiently visualizing and browsing music collections. MIL utilizes a novel structure, music semantic graph (MSG), to organize music collections in a hierarchical way by leveraging lyrics and acoustic cues of music. Each node of MSG corresponds to a music concept and is associated with a cluster of music tracks. MIL offers users a novel way to efficiently explore and scan music collections by using lyrics and image information. In addition, the proposed prototype supplies an easy-to-use interface to visualize MSG hierarchically. The user study shows that our prototype can effectively and efficiently help users to browse, search, and scan music collections. (3) We continue to enhance the content-based image retrieval capability of VSCN through exploring more advanced features to represent images. We conducted studies on semantic image segmentation, which is an important task in computer vision. Semantic segmentation aims at assigning each pixel in an image with a semantic label, such as tree, sky, person. To this end, we propose a novel deep layer cascade (LC) method to improve the accuracy and speed of semantic segmentation. Unlike the conventional model cascade (MC) that is composed of multiple independent models, LC treats a single deep model as a cascade of several sub-models. Earlier sub-models are trained to handle easy and confident regions, and they progressively feed-forward harder regions to the next sub-model for processing. Convolutions are only calculated on these regions to reduce computations. The proposed method possesses several advantages. First, LC classifies most of the easy regions in the shallow stage and makes deeper stage focuses on a few hard regions. Such an adaptive and ‘difficulty-aware’ learning improves segmentation performance. Second, LC accelerates both training and testing of deep network thanks to early decisions in the shallow stage. Third, in comparison to MC, LC is an end-to-end trainable framework, allowing joint learning of all sub-models. (4) We found that a lot of web-images are not pre-labeled with human-provided annotations. This makes learning a deep model impossible if we were to employ the conventional supervised learning scheme. To extend the capability of VSCN to learn from unlabeled web images we explore the possibility of unsupervised learning. Attributes offer useful mid-level features to interpret visual data. While most attribute learning methods are supervised by costly human-generated labels, we introduce a simple yet powerful unsupervised approach to learn and predict visual attributes directly from data. Given a large unlabeled image collection as input, we train deep Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to output a set of discriminative, binary attributes often with semantic meanings. Specifically, we first train a CNN coupled with unsupervised discriminative clustering, and then use the cluster membership as a soft supervision to discover shared attributes from the clusters while maximizing their separability. The learned attributes are shown to be capable of encoding rich imagery properties from both natural images and contour patches. The visual representations learned in this way are also transferrable to other tasks such as object detection. We show other convincing results on the related tasks of image retrieval and classification, and contour detection. (5) Lastly, we try to enhance web image browsing using VSDN. Browsing may get ineffective if the initial query is ambiguous. In our new work, we attempt to improve the human-computer interaction through the use of natural language conversation. The ability to ask questions is a powerful tool to gather information in order to learn about the world and resolve ambiguities. In this study, we explore a novel problem of generating discriminative questions to help disambiguate visual instances. Our work can be seen as a complement and new extension to the rich research studies on image captioning and question answering. We introduce the first large-scale dataset with over 10,000 carefully annotated images-question tuples to facilitate benchmarking. In particular, each tuple consists of a pair of images and 4.6 discriminative questions (as positive samples) and 5.9 non-discriminative questions (as negative samples) on average. In addition, we present an effective method for visual discriminative question generation. The method can be trained in a weakly supervised manner without discriminative images-question tuples but just existing visual question answering datasets. Promising results are shown against representative baselines through quantitative evaluations and user studies.

416713.label: Major findings and research outcome
416713.value: As research outcome, 3 journal papers and 5 conference papers are published. IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (PAMI) is the best journal on computer vision and machine learning. 5 papers were published on the top conferences on computer vision and multimedia (CVPR, ICCV, and ACM MM). In this project, we proposed a novel visual semantic complex network to model the complex structures of a web image collection (paper in Part C.9 No. 1). We studied multiple fundamental structures of complex networks, which reveal some interesting facts about the VSCN. They not only help us understand the huge web image collection at a macroscopic level, but are also valuable in practical applications. Two exemplar applications show that exploiting structural information of the VSCN not only substantially improves the precisions of CBIR, but also greatly enhances the user experience in web image search and browsing. We showed an application of VSCN on music exploration and visualization (paper in Part C.9 No. 2). In particular, we proposed music semantic graph, a music browsing and scanning prototype, for organizing a music collection by utilizing lyrics and audio features. Based on our proposed MSG, we developed a user-friendly interface to present the hierarchical semantic structures among a music collection. Our next work aimed at improving the representation capability of VSCN through semantic image segmentation (paper in Part C.9 No. 5, and in Part C.8 No. 3). Specifically, Deep layer cascade is proposed in this work to simultaneously improve the accuracy and speed of semantic image segmentation. Our subsequent effort was dedicated to allowing VSCN to learn from images that are not labeled (paper in Part C.9 No. 3). That allows VSCN to improve its representation extraction capability from time to time. We proposed an unsupervised approach to deep learning discriminative attributes from unlabeled data. The input of our system is natural images. The output is a compact list of attributes in the form of binary codes. The resulting visual attributes and features are found to capture strong semantic meanings, and are transferrable to several important vision tasks. Lastly, we enhanced the capability of web image browsing by introducing an additional modality in human-computer interaction. In particular, a user not only can browse images through the manoeuvring image collections using mouse clicks, the user can pinpoint the right images by conducting a natural language conversation with the image browsing application (paper in Part C.9 No. 4).

416713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
416713.value: In our study, we found that deep learning performs exceedingly well on representation learning in comparison to other hand-crafted feature-based approaches. We will further pursue this research direction to develop more powerful deep learning-based methods on other computer vision problems. We also found natural language important for visual understanding and retrieval, we will continue to work on this direction.

416813.label: Project Title(Chinese)
416813.value: I/O高效的大規模社交網絡特性提取算法

416813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
416813.value: A social network refers to a graph that captures information about the social behavior of human beings. Such a network may range from a traditional "call graph" to a modern "friendship graph" at Facebook. Scientists of multiple disciplines are eager to understand the characteristics of social networks, as part of our eternal endeavor to reveal the essence of human communities. As a common feature, however, social networks grow with time. For example, as of 2011, the social network at Facebook contains more than 721 million active users (a.k.a. vertices), and over 69 billion friendship edges. If each edge is represented by 2 integers, the entire graph occupies over 550 giga bytes of storage, which significantly exceeds the memory capacity of a commodity machine. As a consequence, most existing algorithms for computing graph characteristics in memory become intolerably slow (on disk-resident graphs) due to a phenomenon known as "memory thrashing". Motivated by this, the proposed project aims to design I/O-efficient algorithms for extracting characteristics of massive social networks. As a direct outcome, the project is expected to produce timely softwares that are geared to significantly facilitate the analysis of gigantic social networks. 社交網絡實際上是一個捕捉了人類社交行為信息的圖。這樣的網絡的範圍可以從傳統的“調用圖”到現代的在Facebook上的“朋友關係圖”。不同學科的科學家們都希望能夠理解社交網絡的特性，作為我們一直為之奮鬥的目標的一部分，從而揭示人類群體的本質。然而，社交網絡通常具有隨著時間的推移而增長的特性。例如，截至2011年，Facebook上的社交網絡包含了超過7.21億個活躍用戶（又稱作頂點）和超過690億表示朋友關係的邊。如果用2個整數表示每一條邊，那麼整個網絡將會佔用超過550GB的存儲空間，這明顯地超過了目前一般計算機的內存容量。因此，目前大多數適用於在內存中計算圖特性的算法都會面臨著“系統顛簸”的現象（因為这样巨大的圖只能存放在硬碟中），從而使得算法效率大大地降低，甚至到了讓人無法容忍的地步。基於這樣的問題，本項目旨在設計適合I/O的高效的大規模社交網絡特性提取算法。而作為本項目的一個直接成果，本項目希望能夠製作一個適時的软体，從而更方便有效地分析大規模社交網絡。

416913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
416913.value: 摘要： 矽懸空薄膜波導（SMW）是一種脊形光波導，可以製作在具有亞微米厚度的矽薄膜芯片上。其加工方法類似於傳統的絕緣體履矽脊形波導的製作，但需要利用各向異性的濕濁刻法，局部地去除掉波導下面的氧化埋層。最近的研究顯示，這種高折射率對比度的納米結構可以感受到來自於輻射壓強和電致伸縮的機械力，目前已報導了超過104 N/m2的壓強。在高折射率對比度的波導中，輻射壓強理論上可以對受激布里淵散射（SBS）產生一萬倍的增強，但是，這種現象尚未在實驗中觀測到。在光學光纖中，人們已經證實，對於連續光甚至皮秒脈衝光，電致伸縮效應在克爾非線性折射率變化中具有顯著的作用。這裡我們首次提出了對矽懸空薄膜波導非線性光學性質的實驗研究。我們將設計並製作不同尺寸的矽懸空薄膜波導，開展對受激布里淵增益譜和傳導聲波諧振的研究。並利用～50皮秒光脈衝進行自相位調製的測量，從而驗證克爾效應是否在這種結構中得到了增強。對於高折射率對比度納米尺寸的波導，最近的研究還表明，其他的三階非線性光學效應，如受激拉曼散射，在這種結構中將得到2.5倍的增強，這一點也將在本工作中進行驗證。本工作的目的是為了更好地理解納米尺度高折射率對比度波導的非線性光學性質。我們將設計製作並優化具有最大光學非線性效應的矽薄膜波導，除了對傳統的後向受激布里淵散射進行測量，同時也會對前向受激布里淵散射進行研究，而這一點正是這種亞波長納米結構所特有的性質。我們同時也將比較非線性折射率在懸空波導和傳統脊型波導中的不同。此項工作有望開闢矽懸空波導在非線性光子學中的眾多新應用，包括，利用單波長泵浦產生多波長光輸出的矽波導，可調節延時，以及光波導隔離器等。

416913.label: Realisation of objectives
416913.value: The first objective involving the design and fabrication of silicon suspended membrane waveguides and associated passive waveguide elements was 100% completed. We designed and fabricated waveguide grating couplers[1,2] , suspended waveguide directional couplers [5] and fully suspended slot waveguides [5], suspended disk resonators [7] and fully suspended ring resonators [8] within this project. The second objective involving the measurement of third order nonlinear effects including kerr nonlinearities and stimulated Brillouin scattering in suspended waveguides was also 100% completed. We measured a small enhancement in Kerr nonlinearity of fully suspended silicon waveguides [3,9], and a somewhat larger enhancement by placing MoS2 on top of the silicon waveguides [4]. The enhancements were theoretically modelled and a small contribution (about 5% enhancement). Kramers Kronig analysis revealed that the small gain and loss from stimulated Brillouin scattering at stokes and antistokes wavelength respectively could account for the experimentally observed enhancement [10]. Optical gain from stimulated Brillouin scattering in a silicon ring resonator was also measured for the first time [6]. The third objective to develop applications of nonlinear silicon suspended membrane waveguides was addressed with the development of suspended silicon slot waveguides for enhanced refractive index sensitivity in gas sensing [5], and the demonstration of optical gain from stimulated Brillouin scattering in ring resonators [6]. This third objective is rather open ended but it is deemed completed given the practical time frame of the project. 416913.label: Major findings and research outcome
416913.value: We designed and fabricated silicon suspended membrane waveguide grating couplers[1,2] , suspended membrane waveguide directional couplers [5] and fully suspended silicon slot waveguides [5], suspended disk resonators [7] and fully suspended ring resonators [8] within this project. We measured a small enhancement in Kerr nonlinearity of fully suspended silicon waveguides [3,9], and a somewhat larger enhancement by placing MoS2 on top of the silicon waveguides [4]. The enhancements in the suspended membrane waveguide were theoretically modelled and a small contribution (about 5% enhancement) was attributed to the confinement of phonons and electriction. Kramers Kronig analysis revealed that the small gain and loss from stimulated Brillouin scattering at stokes and antistokes wavelength respectively could account for the experimentally observed enhancement in Kerr nonlinearity [10]. Optical gain from stimulated Brillouin scattering in a silicon ring resonator was also measured for the first time [6]. We demonstrated applications of suspended silicon membrane slot waveguides for enhanced refractive index sensitivity in gas sensing [5], and the demonstration of optical gain from stimulated Brillouin scattering in ring resonators [6] points to the future possible nonlinear optical amplifiers and Brillouin lasers. The research project involved the participation of three several students, and one MPhil student. One of the more senior students (K. Xu) who helped in device design at the start of the project won the Hong Kong Insitution of Science Young Scientist Award 2014 (Engineering Science Category). Two other PhD students (W. Zhou and Y. Zhang) who were the first authors of several papers in this project are expected to complete their theses in 2018.

416913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
416913.value: There is potential to further develop the integrated suspended membrane waveguide gas sensing platform, with the advantages of longer interaction lengths and high intensity within the suspended slot waveguide. This may open up high sensitivity Raman spectroscopy for identifying different gases using the nonlinear integrated waveguide platform. There is also potential to exploit the optical gain from stimulated Brillouin scattering for high resolution integrated optical spectrum analysers.

416913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
416913.value: The project advanced the understanding of the physics of suspended membrane silicon waveguides and demonstrated the practical implementation of integrated silicon suspended membrane devices. We showed that the suspended membrane waveguides had higher refractive index nonlinearity and could support stimulated Brillouin scattering for optical amplification. These advances can potentially find applications in gas sensing and integrated spectrometers.

417213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
417213.value: Generating electrical power from natural or environmental sources, such as ambient vibrations, would give self-powering capability to a sea of wireless sensors and portable devices. Vibrations are omnipresent in machines and structures, allowing their energy harvesting on a continuous basis. Vibration-based energy harvesters require minimal maintenance and can be employed in hostile and inaccessible environments, making them especially attractive for applications in structural health monitoring and geological remote sensing. But, in flexural structures such as long cables of a suspension bridge, vibrations are widely spread throughout the structures, and they have significant energy spectrum only in the low frequency range. This type of energy source poses great technical challenges in energy harvesting. Existing vibration harvesters mainly rely on piezoelectric elements in resonate motion amplification, which has an inherently narrow operating bandwidth. Furthermore, little consideration is given on energy scattering by wave propagation in the underlying vibrating structure. Thus, the conventional piezoelectric harvesters are yet practical in real-world applications on flexural structures. The overall objective of this project is to develop a class of wideband piezoelectric harvesters suitable for low frequency vibration energy harvesting on flexural structures, specially targeted for self-powering applications of remote sensors on long cables, beams, and plates. The harvester has a distinct 2-DOF design with stretch-thin-beams, which results in three unique characteristics: (1) wide-bandwidth and higher power generation, stemming from stiffness nonlinearity, resonance interference and the use of more efficient piezoelectric mode; (2) doubling power efficiency and further widened bandwidth by absorbing energy flow in both rotational and translational motions; and (3) formation of locally-resonant “stop-bands” to trap the flexural waves at low frequency range, so their substantial energy is converted to electricity by the harvesters which have matching dynamic bandwidth. The project aims to address all major issues for the development of this innovative technique, including design, micro-fabrication, dynamic analysis, experimental validation and practical implementation. It is expected that this investigation would yield a novel vibration energy harvesting technique that can be applied to a wide class of flexural structures in a real-world environment. The capability of the low frequency range power generation is of great interest for structural health monitoring, geological remote sensing, and military devices. The advanced technology will make a significant contribution to Hong Kong, particularly in the technology development, manufacturing and production of the systems, and deployment for infrastructure monitoring and geological sensing.

417213.label: Realisation of objectives
417213.value: The overall objective of this project is to design and develop a class of wideband flexural beam structures with 1-DOF or 2-DOF for low frequency vibration energy harvesting, specially targeted for self-powering applications of remote sensors on long cables, beams, and plates. During the project period, we started to address those major issues by the development of wideband flexural structures, including design, micro-fabrication, dynamic analysis, experimental validation and practical implementation. A primary task is to develop piezoelectric harvesters with wide bandwidth at the low frequency range. We have investigated three cases of theoretical and practical importance: (a) a single force-only harvester periodically attached, (b) an array of force-moment harvesters, and (c) a periodic beam array attachment. Our focus has been on maximum matching of the bandgap effect with the harvester’s dynamic bandwidth for maximum vibration trapping and power generation. We explored the structural feature such as concentrated mass to assign resonance harmonics of the vibration. The second and third eigenfrequencies can be tuned to be integer times of the first eigenfrequency separately or simultaneously using one or two concentrated masses attached on the original cantilever probe. The existence of concentrated masses modifies the boundary conditions and generates the continuity conditions. The analysis fundamental of this methodology is the Euler-Bernoulli beam theory. And it was found that two concentrated masses can provide more frequency ratio combinations than one mass. Frequency response spectrum shows that the response peaks of cantilever after tailoring exactly coincide with selected harmonics orders. However, large frequency tailoring range needs heavy mass, which will lower the fundamental frequency. We then investigated the structural optimization to amplify harmonics response of beam structures. The mechanical model is a step cross-sectioned probe. Original cantilever probe is divided into three steps, in which the cross-sectional width of symmetric top and bottom steps is the design variable, while the medium step is unchanged. Optimization constraints are the integer ratios between eigenfrequencies, and the objective is to maximize the first eigenfrequency. Shape sensitivity is derived using the material derivative and the classical adjoint method, and the steepest ascent algorithm is utilized to solve the optimization problem. Beam model based finite element method is incorporated into the structural dynamic analysis of cantilever beam with variable cross section. Numerical examples with single and multiple frequency constraints are investigated. Selected resonance frequencies are assigned in accordance with specific integer harmonics, thus enhancing the response significantly. In order to validate the modeling results, we then applied microfabrication technique to micromachine the harmonic probes, and the experimental results are systemically evaluated as well. One- layer variable-width and three-step cross-sectioned harmonic probes are designed, respectively. The design is based on a commercial silicon probe, and structural optimization framework is utilized to figure out the optimal probe pattern. Focused ion beam (FIB) milling technique is employed to micromachine the probes according to the optimization design. Single and two harmonics assignment are achieved through the validation of probe's resonance frequency measurement on the AFM system. Probe design with step cross section is proved to provide more resonance harmonics choice, compared with one-layer variable-width design. The fabrication cost of the harmonic beam probes is also benchmarked. It is notable that silicon is a piezoresistive material without piezoelectricity, hence, another layer of piezoelectric material need to be coated, such as ZnO or PVDF (polyvinylidene fluoride polymer) to realize the piezoelectric beam. Within the framework of this project, we have also studied an Euler–Bernoulli beam periodically suspended with separated force-resonators and moment-resonators. Specifically, we investigate the low-frequency band-gap structure of flexural wave propagation in the LR (locally resonant) beam with 1-DOF and 2-DOF. The transfer matrix method for a unit cell in the beam is used in conjunction with Bloch’s theorem. The method allows us directly to calculate the dispersion curves and to characterize the frequency band structure. Our results show the rich dispersion properties of the LR periodic structures, especially the super-wide band-gaps at an optimal separation distance. Furthermore, we present a characterization on the frequency axis of the conditions for transitions between the four types of dispersion regions. Our numerical findings testify that wide band-gaps can be tuned more flexibly in vibration-wave-based practical applications. Besides, we explored the feasibility of generating vibration using electromagnetic fields by tethering a tiny magnet on the beam-like flexible structures. The results was striking, which show varied vibration modes can be achieved with control. The use of a flexible link enables the beam-like structures to exhibit two different vibration modes by tuning the input frequencies of the applied oscillating magnetic field with uniform field strength. When the input frequency is below 15 Hz, the head and tail show similar and large vibration amplitudes, and the net centrifugal force mainly contributes to the forward propulsion of the beam in fluid. While with high input frequencies (i.e., larger than 30 Hz), the flexible link can filter away high-frequency signals to efficiently avoid the passive vibration of the nonmagnetic portion of the head. Simultaneously, the magnetic tail vibrates with relatively large amplitude and generates forward propulsion force for the robot. To understand the whole-body-vibration and tail-vibration behaviors, an analytical model has been developed. Moreover, propulsion performances of this beam-like robot, i.e., the propulsion force and swimming velocity, are characterized on the substrate–water interface. Finally, we demonstrate two-dimensional manipulation of tiny objects by utilizing the two vibration modes of the robot. Based on the results, we have published several journal and conference proceeding papers. Some results were also presented in the international conferences. There were no major problems.

417213.label: Major findings and research outcome
417213.value: The major finding and research outcomes are mainly from the following aspects. - We explored the structural feature such as concentrated mass to assign resonance harmonics of the vibration. The second and third eigenfrequencies can be tuned to be integer times of the first eigenfrequency separately or simultaneously using one or two concentrated masses attached on the original cantilever beam. - We systematically investigated the structural optimization to amplify harmonics response of beam structures. The mechanical model is a step cross-sectioned beam probe. Surface and bulk micro-machining techniques (e.g. Focused Ion Beam, FIB) were implemented for fabrication of the flexible beam structures so as to develop the vibration based piezoelectric havester. We have published two journal papers and two conference proceedings accordingly. - Within the framework of this project, we have also studied an Euler Bernoulli beam periodically suspended with separated force-resonators and moment-resonators, which has potential for the development of piezoelectric flexure beam for harvester. The results were also published in two journals. - We studied the feasibility of generating multi-mode vibration using electromagnetic fields by tethering a tiny magnet on the beam-like flexible structures. The results indicate that varied vibration modes can be achieved based on the structural design, and such an approach has high potential for the actuation of soft robot in a controllable fashion.

417213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
417213.value: On the one hand, the realization of the objectives yields a novel vibration-based energy harvesting technique that can be applied to a wide class of flexural structures in a real-world environment. The capability of the low frequency range power generation is of great interest for structural health monitoring, geological remote sensing, and military devices. And, on the other hand, the mechanical vibration with multi-modes can also be used to remotely acutate soft robotic devices, which provides an interesting means for actuation and control of soft robots. The PI's lab will continue to explore the potentials of utilizing mechanical vibration for tiny, untethered robotic devices with enhanced functionalities.

417513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
417513.value: The PI proposes to study the fundamentals of bio-mimic superhydrophobic surfaces and to apply the surface structures for improving the performance and reliability of silicon solar cells. In high-performance silicon solar cells with multifunctional surfaces, features like light trapping, water-repellent and self-cleaning are usually highly desired. These properties require superhydrophobic surface coatings, ultra-low reflectance, UV stability and mechanical robustness, which are not all currently available. Superhydrophobicity, known as the "Lotus Effect" that mimicks the surface of natural lotus leaves, has an ultra-low surface energy (high contact angle) and a self-cleaning capability. It can be achieved through micro- and nanostructure designs and suitable hydrophobic treatments on the surface. In order to realize the multifunctional bio-mimic superhydrophobic surfaces for solar cell applications, fundamental understanding on the surface physics and chemistry in both micro- and nanoscale, high-throughput/low-cost fabrication technologies for nanostructures, and the surface hydrophobic passivation techniques are imperatively needed. In this work, the PI proposes to develop multifunctional superhydrophobic coatings on silicon semiconductor surfaces. These coatings could improve photovoltaic device efficiency by (1) achieving low reflectance and thus enhanced light absorption through surface light-trapping structures, (2) keeping the surface clean throughout the fabrication and packaging processes of the device, and (3) reducing charge carrier recombination through surface passivation. The PI first will conduct fundamental studies on the effects of the surface micro/nano structure on "superhydrophobicity". The structured micro-/nano-surfaces will be fabricated through (1) wet chemical (metal assisted) silicon etching, (2) photolithography/plasma etching, and (3) sol-gel processing in order to generate controlled geometrical shapes, structure diameter, pitch, and height. The relation between light scattering and surface roughness will be investigated. To achieve enhanced light absorption by solar cells, a hierarchically structured silicon surface is proposed which is expected to achieve both superhydrophobicity and broadband anti-reflection by gradual modulation of the index of refraction on the surfaces. Finally the surface passivation will be investigated to reduce surface charge recombination and achieve optimized photovoltaic cell performance. This work will improve the fundamental understanding of superhydrophobicity and superoleophobicity achieved via micro- and nano-structured surfaces. It is of great significance to apply hierarchically structured surfaces for self-cleaning purposes. The technologies developed here can not only contribute to the research of reliable and high performance solar cells, but also be widely used to achieve self-cleaning function of other surfaces, such as covering glass for solar panels and building windows. 本項目將研究仿生超疏水表面的基本原理，並且將該技術應用到矽太陽能電池方面以期改善它的效率和穩定性。高效率的矽太陽能電池具有多功能的表面，如果將一些新的性質例如光捕獲、防水、自清潔等加入該多功能表面將會進一步改善電池的性質。這些新性質的建立是超疏水錶面塗層、超低的光反射、紫外穩定和機械強度的綜合作用，在目前的技術條件下還無法同時獲得。超疏水錶面，也就是大家說的“荷葉效應”其實是模仿自然界裡荷葉的表面，這種表面具有超低的表面能（很高的接觸角）和自清潔的能力。目前，可以通過微納結構的設計和對錶面進行合適的疏水處理得到超疏水錶面。為了實現多功能仿生超疏水錶面在太陽能電池上的應用，以下技術知識是必須的：微納結構表面的物理和化學知識，高產出而且廉價納米結構的製備技術，疏水錶面鈍化技術。在本工作中，PI打算研究矽半導體表面的多功能超疏水塗層。這些塗層很可能從以下幾個方面改善光伏器件的效率（1）利用具有光捕獲的表面結構達到減少反射和增強光吸收的目的（2）在整個的製備和封裝過程中保持表面的清潔（ 3）通過表面鈍化減少電荷激子的複合。首先，PI將開展表面微納結構對超疏水性質影響的基礎研究。微納結構表面可以通過以下幾個方法製備（1）濕法化學矽刻（金屬輔助）（2）光刻/等離子刻蝕（3）溶膠-凝膠過程，並且通過這些方法調控微納結構的幾何形貌、結構尺寸、距離和高度。其次，該工作也將研究光散射和表面粗糙度之間的關係。為了達到增強太陽能電池光吸收的目的，多級結構的矽表面是一個很好的選擇，我們不僅希望該表面具有超疏水的性質，還希望通過逐漸調控表面的折射率使其具備寬帶增透的性質。最後，我們將探究表面鈍化技術是如何降低表面激子復合和優化光伏電池性能。該工作也將進一步深化對具有微納結構的超疏水和超疏油表面的基本理解。通過製備多級結構而達到自清潔的目的是非常重要的。這些技術不僅有助於研究高性能太陽能電池的可靠性，也將在太陽能電池板的覆蓋玻璃和建築門窗等領域的自清潔表面廣泛應用。

To obtain fundamental understanding of the relationships among the surface hierarchical structure, the related superhydrophobicity and the micro three-phase contact line, and to identify the origin of contact angle hysteresis, which is responsible for the self-cleaning effect of superhydrophobic surfaces.

417513.label: Major findings and research outcome
417513.value: -We have developed a silver (Ag) nanoparticle-assisted HF/HNO3 etching process to generate hierarchical silicon structures, which consist of zigzag-oriented nanowires grown on micron-sized pyramids. Furthermore, we observed a strong dependence of the nanowire morphology on the etching conditions and provided theoretical explanations to the phenomenon. (Manuscript #1) -We have carried out further analysis on the structure-property correlations based on the tunable hierarchical structures. The superhydrophobicity of the hierarchical structures was systematically characterized, and well correlated with a theoretical model related to transitions between the Wenzel and Cassie contact states. Furthermore, we studied the light trapping process on the hierarchically textured silicon surface combining optical measurements with simulations. The relative trends of optical reflectance of the hierarchical silicon surfaces agree well with the simulation results. (Manuscript #1 and Ph.D. thesis of SL Shen) -We have introduced copper(I) thiocyanate (CuSCN) on as an interfacial layer to improve the performance of silicon nanowire (SiNW) -based solar cells. The CuSCN layer was placed between the SiNW and PEDOT: PSS (a p-type polymer) layers to improve the junction quality by reducing surface recombination. With the improved interface morphology and reduced charge recombination, the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of the solar cells has been dramatically improved. (Manuscript #2) -We have further investigated the polarization and charging processes at the silicon/water interface, with the aim of exploring the application of the structured silicon in electrochemistry. We compared silicon (100) and (111) surfaces through both theoretical and experimental approaches. As compared to the silicon (100) surface, the silicon (111) surface shows much better charging/discharge capability in aqueous electrolytes, in particular at high scan rates. (Manuscript #3) - Besides the work at CUHK, we collaborated with Yun Chen et al. at Georgia Institute of Technology to further expand the metal-assisted chemical etching method to fabricate texture silicon surfaces. Two new approaches have been developed. The first one is alternating Metal-Assisted Chemical Etching method for fabricating kinked Si NWs with controlled 3D geometry. By the use of multiple etchants with carefully selected composition, one can control the number of kinks, their locations, and their angles by controlling the number of etchant alternations and the time in each etchant. The second one is diffusion Controlled Metal-Assisted Chemical Etching Method for fabricating zigzag Si NWs. By tailoring the composition of etchant to change its diffusivity, etching direction, and etching time, various zigzag NWs can be easily fabricated. (Manuscript #4-6)

417513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
417513.value: The success of the project shows that the hierarchical silicon surfaces with water-repellent and self-cleaning properties could be highly desired for improving the performance and long-term reliability of electronic and photonic devices. To fully utilize the hierarchical structures, new materials should be researched to better match with the complex silicon surface structures, and film deposition processes have to be optimized accordingly to ensure high quality film morphology for each device layer.

417513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
417513.value: Crystalline silicon has long been established as the material of choice for the microelectronics industry. In order to enhance the functionality and broaden the applications of crystalline silicon, this project focuses extensive research efforts on creating micro-/nano-structures on silicon surface and exploring their applications on the energy storage field. This project studied the superhydrophobic and light trapping properties of hierarchical silicon surfaces combining experimental characterizations with theoretical calculations. To better utilize the silicon nanostructures in silicon solar cells, we introduced CuSCN as an interfacial layer between n-type silicon and p-type hole extraction layer, and achieved significant performance improvement for the solar cells. Furthermore, we studied and compared the interface charging/discharge processes of on silicon (100) and (111) surfaces in an aqueous environment and explored the related application in electrochemical devices. These findings not only provide material strategies to further improve silicon based electronics devices but also help to broaden the applications of crystalline silicon in energy storage and many other areas.

To study the binocular single vision of human vision system.
