417913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
417913.value: With the wide popularity of 3D (more precisely, stereoscopic) movies, 3D display devices, such as consumer 3D television, become more accessible to the general public. While the dual display (left and right views) doubles the visualization space, existing 3D movies only offer stereopsis. Psychologists found that the human visual perception can fuse two views with difference, not just in disparity, but also in contrast and luminance, while still able to form a stable single percept unconsciously. Such non-linear fusion takes place in our brain and is more powerful than the linear blending of the two views. As existing displays are mostly low-dynamic range, images may usually either too “flat” (in order to visualize all small-scale details) or lack of details (in order to exhibit the large-scale regional contrast). Utilizing the perception behavior of binocular single vision and visualizing different visual content on the two views (e.g. one exhibits higher contrast and the other exhibits fine details), it is possible to enrich the visual experience of audiences that is not feasible with a single-view low-dynamic range display. The question is whether a stable single percept can be formed. Note that annoying binocular rivalry (continuous alteration between the two views) can be resulted, if the two views are too different. In this project, we propose to design and develop the fusibility prediction models for stereoscopic images and videos. With these models, we can guide the synthesis of the two views of binocular images and videos in order to enrich the audiences’ visual experience, without triggering any visual discomfort. The major challenge of the project is how to quantify the fusibility. Note that existing study, mostly in psychology, is qualitative and most study assumes the disparity is absent. Our project will be the first computational model on predicting the fusibility of stereoscopic content. The videos synthesized by the proposed framework will be the first set of 3D movies that offers not only stereopsis, but also binocular single vision. By solving these challenges, we believe the outcome (the knowledge, publications, and algorithms) from the proposed project should motivate further study along the direction of binocular vision fusibility. Besides, the developed algorithm should be directly applicable in film industry to produce visually enriched stereoscopic movies, without the cost of upgrading any existing display hardware. This shall provide a technological edge to film makers to attract more audiences. 隨著3D（確切地說是立體）電影的廣泛普及，一般大眾也能更容易的接觸到3D顯示設備，比如消費類3D電視機。儘管雙視圖（左視圖與右視圖）顯示將可視化空間擴大了一倍，但現有的3D電影只局限於立體視差。心理學家發現，人類的視覺感知不僅可以自發地融合兩個視圖的視差，同時還能融合對比度和亮度的差異，從而形成一個穩定的單一認知。這種非線性的融合是由我們的大腦自覺產生的，遠強大過兩個視圖的線性合成。 由於目前的顯示設備大多是低動態範圍成像，圖像往往不是太“平面”（為展現所有小範圍的細節），就是缺少細節（為展現大範圍的區域對比度）。利用雙眼單一視覺這一認知行為，可以在兩個視圖中呈現不同的視覺內容（例如一個視圖呈現高對比度，另一個呈現細節）。相比於單視圖的低動態範圍成像，這種呈現方式將大大豐富觀者的視覺體驗。雙視圖顯示的關鍵在於是否可以形成穩定的單一認知。需要注意的是，如果兩個視圖差異過大，會導致令人不悅的雙眼競爭（兩個視圖不停的交替呈現）。在這個項目中，我們計劃設計並開發立體圖像與視頻的融合度預測模型。有了這個模型，我們就可以在不引起任何視覺不適的前提下，引導合成雙眼圖像與視頻的兩個視圖，從而豐富觀者的視覺體驗。 這一項目遇到的主要挑戰在於如何量化融合度。需要提到的是，現有的研究集中在心理學領域且均為質性研究。另外，這些研究大多假設雙視圖之間不存在內容差異。這一項目將會開創性的首次提出預測立體內容融合度的計算模型。通過提出的系統框架，我們將能合成第一批既有立體視差又能單一視覺化雙眼不同內容的3D電影。解決挑戰之後，我們相信項目的成果（知識，學術文章和算法）將會促進雙眼視覺融合方向的進一步研究。此外，研發的算法應能直接應用於電影產業，無需用資金升級任何現有顯示設備，即可製作出視覺效果更加豐富的立體影片。這將為電影製作人提供前沿的技術優勢，從而使電影能吸引更多觀眾。

417913.label: Realisation of objectives
417913.value: Our visual system can unconsciously fuse the visual content acquired by our left and right eye in a non-linear fashion. This binocular fusion has been found to be a non-linear combination of luminance, contrast, and color. Such non-linearity is crucial as it means our binocular fusion could be substantially different from (and usually more informative than) the simple linear blending of two images. In other words, the more difference the left and right views are, the higher chance our brain can acquire more visual information. However, there is a limit on such visual difference, if it is exceeded, our brain cannot form a stable vision and this is called binocular rivalry. The primary goal of this project is to study this fusibility limit, and design the reliable and accurate models for fusibility prediction, so that we can synthesize pairs of images or videos with computer programs. The context of binocular fusion is usually considered in Panum’s fusional area. In computer science terminology, it is a local neighborhood, i.e. an image region. Both contour fusion (agreement of salient edges), and contour and region contrasts (agreement in color and contrast) have to be accounted during the fusibility prediction. Contour fusion relies on the accurate edge identification. This is why in the early phase of the project, we need to design a reliable salient edge detection. This result has been applied on an illumination-invariant pattern recognition application and published in [J02]. We have successfully applied the first fusibility prediction model to enrich visual content by synthesizing a pair of images from a given input image. The idea is to generate two images with different contrast and brightness to maximally preserve the visual elements in the input image, without breaking the fusibility limit, hence prevents triggering the binocular rivalry. We have filed patents based on this idea to United States [P01] and Chinese patent offices [P02]. In our first attempt of modeling the fusibility prediction, we adopt a very tight requirement in avoiding binocular rivalry. As mentioned before, whether the two corresponding point in two views agree to each other, it is dependent on the agreement of contour and contrast in a local neighborhood (fusional area). In other words, each corresponding pixel pair between left and right view, we need to evaluate whether they are fusible or not. In our first version of fusibility prediction model, the model declares the two views are infusible whenever a single pixel in two views disagree. The advantage of this design is that it can reliably to prevent the binocular rivalry. However, it is also too conservative, and limits the possible solution. Even the audiences do not perceive any binocular rivalry, the model still rejects the image pair. In our second attempt of fusibility prediction design, we relax such hard constraint, make a soft constraint. Instead of straightly rejecting image pair that slightly disagrees, we try to minimize the disagreed regions during the image pair synthesis. This approach allows us to enlarge the solution space, and offer wider range of results. We have put this model in practice in our application of visual sharing with colorblind. The result is promising and we also presented the work in the prestigious conference, ACM SIGRRAPH 2016 held in United States. The work is published in top journal ACM Transactions on Graphics [J01]. To extend the work from image to video content, we need to simultaneously preserve the fusibility constraint, and the temporal consistency. This further limits the solution space. To solve this problem, we formulate the problem as an objective function that tries to optimize the fusibility constraint and temporal consistency. We follow the blind video temporal filtering approach in this formulation. However, the original blind filtering approach is designed for monocular video. In our case, we need to process dual video channels and the problem is more challenging. We successfully solve it and applied to colorblind visual sharing problem. The work has been submitted to IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics. At the time of preparing this report, our paper is under revision. To evaluate our models, we conducted user study at the final stages. Through the user study, we are able to evaluate the reliability and accuracy of the proposed models. Moreover, the collected data from user feedback is also used to fine tune the parameters of the models. For instance, the user data can be used to tune the ratio between the multiple constraints (e.g. fusibility and temporal consistency) in different applications in order to achieve the best results.

417913.label: Major findings and research outcome
417913.value: To facilitate the reference to related publications, each journal, conference paper and patent listed in Sections 8, 9, and 11 is labeled with a unique ID, e.g. [J01], [C01], or [P01]. Please refer to the field “Title” for the ID. 1. We have designed a structure line extraction method that is resistant to various image noise and illumination interference. With this, it can better extract the contours (edges) from both left and right images, and hence better alignment of contours in stereoscopic image/video. This technique has been extended to a recognition application and published in a journal [J02]. 2. Our fusibility predictor can measure the chance of binocular rivalry (i.e. stable fusion cannot be formed). However, the initial design is very conservative and limits its solution. So we relax the requirement and formulate the problem as a minimization of overall discomfort value. This offers us more possible and visually acceptable solutions. We have improved the fusibility metric to make the visual experience more stable and more solution can be obtained. We have filed the static image version of our method to apply for a US patent [P01] as well as a Chinese patent [P02] (Section11). At the time we prepared this report, we have already been granted with the US patent [P01]. 3. With the improved fusibility predictor, we apply it to a visual sharing application, in which it allows both colorblind and normal vision audiences to share the same visual content. We achieve this via the binocular display. The left and right images are separately presented to the eyes of colorblind to form a stable fusion in their brain. This is possible only because we have a reliable fusibility predictor developed in this project. Our work has been published in the prestigious conference ACM SIGGRAPH 2016 and the top journal ACM Transactions on Graphics [J01]. 4. We further extend the ability of the fusibility predictor to video by extending the image visual sharing with colorblind to video content. We reformulate the blind filter operator (originally designed for monocular video) to our binocular colorblind-sharable video. We submit the work to IEEE Transaction on Visualization and Computer Graphics. At the time of preparing this report, the paper is under revision. 5. We also attempt to transfer the developed technology to industrial application. We have applied the funding of CUHK Technology Start-up Support Scheme for Universities (TSSSU). Our application has been shortlisted at the time of preparing this report.

417913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
417913.value: Further development: In this project, we attempted to predict the fusibility of binocular vision. With the fusibility predictor, we are able to embed more visual information into the binocular display setting, e.g. 3D TV, head-mounted display of modern VR entertainment devices. However, the fusibility prediction model alone may still reject results that do not trigger binocular rivalry. We believe one reason is that our current design does not account for the visual attention. If the visual attention model is accounted, we believe more accurate fusibility prediction can be achieved. Course of action: We believe more study should be done in the direction of visual attention modeling. By developing more sophisticated quantitative models for visual attention, more accurate visual model can be obtained. Currently, researchers have been attempted to adopt the deep learning approach to train neural networks model in identifying the visual saliency. This is promising direction and we are also currently looking into it.

417913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
417913.value: While nowadays binocular display devices such as 3D television, VR head-mounted display, have been widely adopted and already produced at consumer-level, the dual display channels are only used for visualizing one kind of binocular vision behavior, stereopsis. Human visual system accepts much more difference between left and right views. By utilizing this, we can present much more visual content to audiences, without modifying the existing display hardware (low dynamic range displays). The key to achieve this is to accurately and reliably predict the fusibility limit of human vision system. This project serves as a start in this research direction. The developed models can immediately applied in multiple applications. We have also demonstrated its usage in generating more vivid visual content and colorblind sharable images. The immediate impact of our work is that it is possible to produce visually enriched visual content for bluray distribution or even multiple video channel broadcast.

418213.label: Project Title(Chinese)
418213.value: 微結構親水-疏水表面沸騰換熱極限的研究

418213.label: Project Objectives
418213.value: The PI will design and fabricate a series of micro-devices that consist of alternatively patterned large microchannels and micro pin fin arrays on silicon substrates. The device surface will be made mainly hydrophilic with regularly distributed hydrophobic patches. Extensive boiling experiments will be performed on the microfabricated devices to systematically investigate how boiling heat transfer behavior is affected by porosity, viscous drag, capillary pressure, surface wettability, and nucleation site density, etc. Through systematic experiments, we will identify the key factors limiting the critical heat flux and enhance the boiling heat transfer limits by strategically engineering the microstructure and surface properties of heated surfaces.

418213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
418213.value: 本項目旨在於通過策略性地設計加熱表面的微結構及表面特性來探索臨界熱流密度現象的機制進而提高沸騰換熱極限。本項目將系統研究具有可調微結構表面的沸騰換熱行為並從根本上理解納米尺度汽泡的異相成核。 加熱表面的泡核沸騰利用流體具有大的汽化潛熱的特點，是一種高效的傳熱機制，已在發電和製冷設備中得到了廣泛的應用。研究表明特定工質在給定飽和壓力下的最大熱流密度存在一個實際極限，稱為臨界熱流密度。例如水在大氣壓下的臨界熱流大約為100 W/cm^2。儘管已對臨界熱流現像開展了大量的研究，幾十年來臨界熱流密度值基本上保持不變，迄今仍未對造成臨界熱流密度的確切機制達成共識。因此，有必要明確限制臨界熱流密度的重要因素，並對加熱表面的結構和表面特性進行優化設計，以提高沸騰換熱的性能。 為了解決上述問題，本項目擬對一系列具有交替微通道及微針翅陣列的微加工表面進行沸騰換熱實驗。表面的特定區域將被塗上一層聚四氟乙烯以便建立疏水的補丁；而表面的其他區域則將沉積一層二氧化矽以提高親水性。通過這個獨特的設計，我們將系統地探討沸騰換熱行為如何受孔隙度、粘性阻力、毛細管壓力、表面潤濕性和成核密度等因素的影響。 臨界熱流密度限制了沸騰換熱設備安全操作的最大功率。本項目的研究將提高我們對造成臨界熱流密度機制的基本認識，加熱表面的策略性設計可能顯著提高沸騰換熱性能，這將大大提高工作效率並對發電和製冷工業的安全有深遠影響。

418213.label: Realisation of objectives
418213.value: We have fully accomplished the objectives of the proposal. - We have designed and fabricated a series of microstructured hydrophobic-hydrophilic surfaces with controlled wettability and nucleation sites to explore the pool boiling heat transfer limits. The sample surface has three main features: (1) micropillar arrays, (2) central cavities, and (3) water channels. Micropillar arrays are designed to be the capillary structure to supply water from large water channels to central cavities. Teflon is coated on the surface of the central cavities to enhance the effectiveness of those cavities as nucleation sites. For a systematic comparison, a total of eight types of samples with different surface coatings and cavity sizes have been fabricated. Si-type samples (Si70 and Si110) with the bare Si microstructures are fabricated to serve as the reference samples. O-type samples (O70 and O110) with the whole surface coated with SiO2 are designed to have a good wettability. T-type samples (T70 and T110) with Teflon-coated cavities and Si microstructures are designed to have easy-to-activate nucleation sites, while TO-type samples (TO70 and TO110) with Teflon-coated cavities and the SiO2 coating on the remaining surface are designed to have both good wettability and easy-to-activate nucleation sites. Two cavity sizes are considered for each type of samples. The number in the sample label, for example, Si70, represents the cavity size. - Inspired by the liquid droplet wetting studies, we have developed a novel approach to achieve effective and controllable nucleation sites. Each nucleation site is designed to be a cavity with hydrophobic micropillar arrays. The micropillar arrays are carefully designed to achieve the Cassie wetting so that the cavity can effectively trap gas and evolve as a nucleation site in the pool boiling environment. The boiling samples with the number of nucleation sites ranging from 1×1 to 8×8 are designed and fabricated to study the correlation of boiling curves and number of nucleation sites. - Extensive boiling experiments were conducted on all the boiling samples fabricated in this project. A testing device was designed and manufactured to heat up the sample during the boiling process and meanwhile measure the boiling curves. Before the experiment, the sample was bonded onto the Cu block (embedded in the testing device) by using the soldering tin. Then, the testing device was placed in a quartz chamber. The deionized water was filled into the chamber and heated up to the saturation temperature (~100oC) by using a hotplate. Degassing was carried out for 30 min before the experiment. A high-speed camera is placed at the side of the chamber to record the boiling process and a high-intensity LED light source is used to illuminate the view field. - Through systematic experiments, we have studied the effects of surface wettability, easy-to activate nucleation sites, cavity size, and number of nucleation sites on the critical heat flux and heat transfer coefficient of pool boiling.

418213.label: Major findings and research outcome
418213.value: - We systematically examined the boiling behavior of microstructured hydrophobic-hydrophilic surfaces. Our results reveal that excellent critical heat flux up to 231.5 W/cm2 is attainable only when the surface has good wettability but is free of easy-to-activate nucleation sites. However, with the presence of easy-to-activate nucleation sites on the boiling surface, only limited critical heat fluxes can be achieved irrespective of the surface wettability, suggesting a suppression effect of nucleation sites on the critical heat flux. Based on the previous experimental observation of the dynamic network-like wetting pattern at high heat fluxes, a wetting-deterioration mechanism is proposed to explain the suppression effect of easy-to-activate nucleation sites on the critical heat flux. Easy-to-activate nucleation sites continuously generate bubbles that pose a large flow resistance for the liquid to wet the hot surface and thus lead to early dry-out. (Publication on International Journal of Thermal Sciences) - We developed a novel approach to achieve effective and controllable nucleation sites in the pool boiling environment. Each nucleation site is designed to be a cavity with hydrophobic micropillar arrays. The micropillar arrays are carefully designed to achieve the Cassie wetting so that the cavity can effectively trap gas and evolve as a nucleation site in the pool boiling environment. Compared to traditional nucleation sites with hole-shaped cavities, these Cassie-wetting nucleation sites own unique advantages including easiness of activation and reliability of enduring harsh boiling perturbations. A correlation of boiling curves and number of nucleation sites is obtained by systematically examining the pool boiling performance of surfaces with different numbers of nucleation sites. (Manuscript under review)

418213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
418213.value: The success of the project shows that easy-to-activate nucleation sites can effectively enhance the heat transfer coefficient but will suppress the critical heat flux in pool boiling. On the other hand, Cassie-wetting cavities can work as effective nucleation sites in the pool boiling environment. Extended from this project, next we will use similar designs to study how baseline pinning affects the bubble departure shape in nucleation boiling. Till now, different bubble departure shapes have been observed in the literature, however, consistent explanation is still lacking. In our next project, we will fabricate boiling samples that consist of a hydrophobic Teflon patch with a Cassie-wetting cavity on silicon substrates. The Cassie-wetting cavity will serve as the nucleation site. The size of the hydrophobic Teflon patch will be varied in a large range to investigate the effect of baseline pinning on the bubble departure shape. The project will be completed within six months. The sample fabrication will be conducted in July-September, 2018. Then, boiling experiments will be performed in October-December, 2018.

418213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
418213.value: In this project, we have systematically studied the effects of surface wettability and easy-to-activate nucleation sites on the pool boiling heat transfer performance. Our project revealed that excellent critical heat flux can be achieved on boiling surfaces with good wettability but free of easy-to-activate nucleation sites. Nucleation sites can effectively enhance the heat transfer coefficient but will suppress the critical heat flux in pool boiling. Our research provides guidance on how to design boiling surfaces with high critical heat flux and high heat transfer coefficient, respectively. On the other hand, we developed a novel approach to achieve easy-to-activate nucleation sites by Cassie-wetting cavities in pool boiling. A correlation of boiling curves and number of nucleation sites is proposed by systematically examining the boiling behavior of samples with number of nucleation sites ranging from 1×1 to 8×8. The design of the Cassie-wetting nucleation sites will also allow us to study the single bubble dynamics and the interaction between bubbles in nucleation boiling.

418613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
418613.value: This proposed research aims to explore the feasibility and key design features of a versatile, autonomous marine research and observation vessel possessing long endurance and low environmental impact. Research into the observation and exploration of the marine environment has recently attracted much worldwide attention. There are numerous requirements for autonomous marine investigation robots, a few significant applications being advance warning of devastating tsunamis (as in Asia in 2004), observation of oil spills (as in the Gulf of Mexico in 2010), surveillance of pirate activities in the Gulf of Aden and the recent boat collision at Hong Kong in 2012. However, due to the vastness of the oceans, it is extremely difficult to reach the specific location of such a robot vessel for the purposes of energy replenishment and real-time remote control. Self-sustainability and autonomy are two key research issues for the realistic application of such sea robots. We propose to conduct research into the design of a vessel designated ‘Sustainable and Autonomous Robotic Vessel’ (SARV) for long-term and long-distance operation at sea. Our research will be mainly focused on four aspects of SARV’s design: (1) a self-trimming sail and self-steering mechanism to enable the vessel to minimize the energy required for motion control; (2) dynamic modeling and analysis of the vessel’s dynamic behaviour in varying conditions, aiming at speeding up the convergence of the motion of the rudder and sail by an indirect control strategy; (3) harvesting of renewable energy and management for sustainability (how to predict energy consumption as well as future energy harvesting requirements; how to ensure there is sufficient energy to sustain its operation); (4) motion control and navigation: how to take account of winds and water flow to ensure a successful mission. The proposed research will lead to an understanding of how to design SARV to fully utilize the energy found in the marine environment, in order to achieve its targeted objectives. It will provide insight into the design of an excellent type of CO2-neutral transportation tool. It will make SARV capable of long-term deployment without maintenance and provide support, not only to Hong Kong's maritime agencies but also to marine exploration for the nation and the world as a whole. 418813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
418813.value: Partial Element Equivalent Circuit (PEEC) is a very popular numerical modeling technique for high-speed electronic circuit design. Recently, a new formulation including the radiation effect has been introduced to the technique. This new formulation makes use of the concept of generalized complex inductance to correctly account for the radiation effect but without violating the conventional definition of capacitance. With this new formulation, equivalent circuit models obtained from the PEEC analysis will consist of real-valued capacitors and complex-valued inductors. In this research, a method for deriving a concise and physically intuitive circuit from such a radiating PEEC model will be investigated. The method will be based on the Y-to-Δ network transformation to eliminate all “un-important” internal details of a given raditing PEEC model. The resulting circuit will be highly concise and simple. This effectively gives a concise circuit representation to a full-wave electromagnetic structure. Therefore, for a given radiating structure, if its concise circuit representation is available, one can easily identify which circuit component influence the overall radiation performance most. Consequently, the specific layout feature of the structure corresponding to this component can be modified accordingly to improve the performance. The exactly way to perform the network transform is one key aspect of this research. With this circuit network representation for radiation problems, the design and modeling of radiating structures and systems becomes more efficient with higher integrity. In other words, the overall design process can be speeded up significantly. In fact, a very attractive application of the proposed research is on integrated antenna design. Since modern wireless devices require small-size integrated antennas of better efficiency and more complex in shape, sophisticated antenna design tools are becoming essential. This is where the proposed research can play a critical role. 部分元等效電路（ PEEC ）是一個非常受歡迎的數值模擬技術用於高速電子電路設計。最近，一個新的輻射效應提案已被引入到該技術。這新提案，在沒有違反電容的傳統定義下，利用廣義電感的概念來正確解釋輻射效應。這項研究將會從這樣一個輻射性PEEC模型來推一個算簡潔而直觀的物理電路來模擬輻射導體。該方法將會基於Y-Δ網絡改造，以消除所有“不重要”的內部細節，由此產生的電路將是非常簡潔和簡單的。這能有效地給出一個簡潔的電路來表示一個全波電磁結構。由於現代無線設備需要小尺寸的集成天線，複雜的天線設計工具是不可少的。擬議的研究可以在這方面發揮關鍵作用。

418813.label: Realisation of objectives
418813.value: 1. A full-wave formulation of PEEC that can separate out various radiation components of a radiating structure on layered substrate has been successfully developed. The approach is to formulate the Green's functions into three distinct parts: i) quasi-dynamic component, ii) surface waves, and iii) higher-order effects (e.g. lateral waves). In this objective, an accurate radiation model for the partial element equivalent circuit (PEEC) technique is introduced for modeling of microstrip structures. By making use of the proposed concept of generalized complex inductance, an accurate decomposition of the radiation resistance for a small dipole on microstrip substrate is derived for the first time using PEEC. Using the semi-analytical Green’s functions for microstrip substrates, the imaginary part of this complex inductance can be shown to represent a frequency-dependent resistance containing contributions from spatial radiations (spherical and lateral) and surface waves (cylindrical). Hence, depending on how the structure of interest is divided into meshes, an equivalent circuit network of “distributed” radiation resistances can be obtained. 2. A model-order reduction technique that can produce a concise circuit model for a radiating structure has been successfully developed. The technique is based on the Y-to-delta transformation to simplify a given circuit. A new circuit reduction algorithm for generating physically meaningful equivalent circuits for electrically small structures is proposed in this objective. It makes use of the generalized Y-to-Δ transformation as well as features unique to partial element equivalent circuits (PEECs) to perform the reduction process. For a given partial element equivalent circuit, insignificant nodes are removed one by one in a prioritized order according to both user-specified cut-off frequency and threshold value. By having the freedom of choosing these parameters, this algorithm provides users an option to make a trade-off between accuracy and simplicity of the final reduced circuit. Since the generalized Y-to-Δ transformation can keep all mutual couplings intact, the order-reduced circuit should correctly capture all physical essences of the structure being modeled. 3. The efficiency-oriented design methodology for integrated radiating structures has not be successfully developed since the concise circuit models obtained from Objective 2 are not guaranteed to be positive in value. This leads to a concern of negative circuit components without physical meaning. Attempts have been tried to understand the reasons for the appearance of these negative components. However, conclusion has not been drawn before the project period ends.

418813.label: Major findings and research outcome
418813.value: This research leads to a novel circuit reduction algorithm for generating physically meaningful equivalent circuits. The algorithm is based on a unique model-order reduction (MOR) technique. In this work, rigorous derivation of the new MOR technique is comprehensively introduced. In the derivation, the equivalent diagrams are also presented for supporting explanation. Two experimental tests are given to validate the accuracy of the new algorithm. Based on the theoretical and experimental investigations, the new algorithm introduced in this paper can help to improve the design and analysis of electrically small multi-conductor structures without degrading accuracy.

418813.value: A possible direction for further research is to extend the current algorithm for three-dimensional structures. To do this, a three-dimensional formulation of PEEC is needed.

By using the unique mathematical formulation developed in this project, radiating structures can be transformed to a equivalent circuit. With such a circuit representation, insights of the structures can be obtained, leading to a more efficient design process.

419413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
419413.value: 该项目研究量子和经典通信的复杂性。过去二十年目睹了量子计算快速发展，包括理论上发现高效的量子算法和协议，和在试验中不同的实施方案，如被最近2012新物理学奖认可的基于离子阱和光子实验的快速进展。通信复杂性研究计算一个分布式的输入的函数值的最低所需要的通信量。由姚在1979年提以来，它一直在理论计算机科学中最重要的领域之一，因为它与很多领域如算法设计，复杂性理论，组合数学，代数等的密切联系。XOR函数是一类重要的函数，其中包含了如Equality，Hamming Distance等基本重要函数，但其私有随机SMP模型通信复杂度仍是未知的。 XOR函数有一些明显的对称性结构有待了解如何被充分利用。在这个项目中，我们计划研究量子和经典通信的复杂性XOR函数的上下界‘。 上界：有几个函数的量子通信复杂性仍是未知数。我们的目标是确定这些通信的复杂性。我们也注意到，高效的协议预留算法和数据梗概通常有一个亲密的关系。鉴于这种动机，我们的目标是设计协议不仅在通信，而且在计算上高效。我们已经构造对称的XOR功能与最佳的通信复杂度的协议，但时间高效的量子协议。我们的目标是实现计算高效的经典协议。我们也计划研究非对称XOR的函数，如线性阈值函数和矩阵函数，在这上面我们已取得了一些局部的结果。 下界：证明通信复杂性的下界是核心问题也是具有挑战性的问题，所以下界方法紧性至关重要。Lovasz和Saks于1988年提出的Log-rank猜想通信复杂性研究的圣杯，但它也是出了名的难题。该项目旨在对XOR函数进行研究，这个猜想依然很难，但似乎是可做的。我们提出了一些新的具体办法，并计划使用最近发展的加性组合数学和布尔函数的傅立叶分析等工具。这些方法的研究将对一般猜想给出启示性的意义，并加深我们的理解布尔函数的傅立叶频谱的理解。

419413.label: Major findings and research outcome
419413.value: We discovered a number of efficient protocols in both classical and quantum communication complexity models, in various computation modes. Some are for specific functions such as Hamming Distance problem and rank decision problem, some are for classes for functions, such as symmetric XOR functions, LTF functions, XOR functions with small GF[2] degree, etc. We proposed a new measure called linear rank, and linked it to the famous Log-rank conjecture. We also studied some of its properties. The results are published in leading conferences.

419413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
419413.value: We can continue the line of interesting research and try to prove the whole Log-rank conjecture for XOR functions. It's a very challenging task, but we've made significant progress which sheds a light on this long-standing open question.

419413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
419413.value: This project aims to study a long-standing open question in communication complexity, a measure of the minimum amount of communication needed to compute a function with distributed inputs. In this project, we managed to prove the conjecture for some large classes of functions, by designing efficient communication protocols in various communication models. 439013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
439013.value: This proposal is directed to the studies of the electronic properties of bulk and nanostructured red phosphorus, with the aim of exploring their applications in solar water splitting cells. Although early theoretical work has predicted red phosphorus as an elemental amorphous semiconductor, its electronic properties have rarely been investigated until a recent study that demonstrates red phosphorus as a promising photocatalyst for water splitting. In such an application red phosphorus is particularly advantageous because of its low-cost, chemical simplicity, broad spectral absorption and suitable band edge alignment with the hydrogen reduction potential. Nevertheless the current performance of the red phosphorus based cells is still limited, largely due to (1) the lack of understanding on its electronic properties and (2) the non-optimal morphology of the material. In this proposal we will tackle both challenges. First, we seek to understand the mechanisms that govern the charge separation, transport and recombination processes in the bulk and surface of red phosphorus. In order to decouple these electronic processes from the surface chemical reactions in photoelectrochemical cells, we will focus on the electrical and spectroscopic characterizations of solid-state red phosphorus films and devices, including field-effect transistors, photodiodes and lateral photoconductors. In particular, charge modulation spectroscopy and transient photocurrent spectroscopy will be introduced to probe microscopically the charge localization (trapping) in red phosphorus. The physical origins of charge recombination will be interrogated with impedance spectroscopy and transient photovoltage measurements. Quantitative analysis on the characterization results will be performed through device modeling. Secondly, we will fabricate red phosphorus nanostructures to enhance its surface area for charge separation. Nanowires will be produced using a vapor–liquid–solid deposition process. Compact or mesoporous thin shells will be grown on nanowire surfaces to (1) reduce the recombination of photogenerated carriers and (2) improve the surface chemical stability. The core-only and core-shell red phosphorus nanostructures will be studied using the aforementioned characterization techniques, thus revealing the impact of nanostructuring on the electronic properties of red phosphorus. The work will be finalized with the implementation of the nanostructured red phosphorus into photocatalytic cells. The correlation between the electronic processes in the material and its photocatalytic performance will be established. We believe the proposed research will not only shed light on the physics of an important elemental semiconductor but also provide a very useful and comprehensive testing platform to evaluate other novel photocatalytic semiconductors such as elemental sulfur and black titanium dioxide. 本項目旨在揭示塊狀和納米結構紅磷的電學性質，從而促進其在光解水產生氫氣中的應用。最近的研究發現紅磷表現出半導體特性，可以作為光催化材料，而且在光照下產生的光生電子可以分解水產生氫氣。紅磷的半導體能帶結構，理論上已進行了預測，但其光學方面性質知之甚少。作為光催化產氫材料，紅磷具有諸多優點，例如：價格低廉，成分簡單，具有較寬的太陽光吸收範圍。不過，目前為止，其光催化的效率仍較低。主要原因是由於（1）對其光學性質的了解不足和（2）材料的形貌也尚未優化。 在此項目中，我們將著力於這兩個問題。首先，我們將通過系列測試揭示紅磷內部和表面的電子分離，轉移及復合的過程。通過對紅磷的薄膜及測件的光學及光譜學測試，分析其表面化學反應的電學過程。例如，借助於場效應晶體管，光電二極管，光電導體測試。此外，利用電荷調製光譜和瞬態光電流光譜探測紅磷的電荷離域性質（電子復合中心）。還將藉助阻抗光譜和瞬態光電壓測試探明其電荷複合的物理起因。同時通過器件建模進行定量分析。 其次，我們將製備納米結構紅磷來提高其比表面積，從而促進光生電荷的分離。將採用氣相-液相-固相​​沉積的方法製備紅磷納米線。通過在納米線表面再製備一層緻密或者介孔的材料，以期降低紅磷光生載流子的複合機率和提高其化學穩定性。借助於前面所提及的表徵方法，分析納米結構對於紅磷光學性質的影響。 本項目最終將應用納米結構的紅磷於光解水體系中，確立電學性質與光催化性能的關係。我們相信此項目的開展不僅有利於了解元素型半導體的物理性質，而且將提供一個非常有效而且全面的測試方法以評估其它新型光催化半導體體系​​，例如元素硫及黑色二氧化鈦。

439013.label: Realisation of objectives
439013.value: The objectives have been achieved with modified methodologies. Firstly, for the characterization of the electronic properties of red phosphorus (RP), although we are able to make thin films and nanostructures of red phosphorus films and integrate them into photodiode structures, we found the high leakage current and poor electrode contact prevent the accurate analysis of the intrinsic electronic properties of the material. Instead, we found the study can be done using conductor and electrochemical cell structures. We therefore primarily did the mechanistic studies using these two structures. Conductivity of RP films in water and under different ambient atmosphere were investigated. Moreover, we studied the density of states of pure RP by density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The combined theoretical and experimental approaches allow us to propose models to explain the electronic properties (e.g., density of states, charge carrier doping, and carrier mobility) of RP, its interaction with different gas molecules and its heterojunction with metal oxide particles. Secondly, throughout this project, we have set up a testing platform combining impedance spectroscopy, photocurrent spectroscopy and gas responsivity measurement to study the properties of RP and its heterojunction with metal oxide particles. Thirdly, we have developed a facile process to synthesize amorphous RP@TiO2 core-shell nanoparticles using a low temperature solvothermal reaction. The nanoparticles can be used to make efficient photoelectrochemical cells for water splitting. We also improved the vapor-liquid-solid (VLS) growth process by introducing a glass wool between the substrate and source RP powder in the growth tube. We found that the glass wool can largely filter out the large sized RP clusters and leave the film deposited on the substrate highly uniform. Another interesting observation is that the glass wool can serve as a 3D skeleton to grow needle-like red phosphorus fibers during the VLS process. This greatly increases the surface-to-volume ratio of red phosphorus and leads to excellent water-splitting performance, as proved by the collaborator of this project (Yu et al. Angewandte Chemie, 128, 9732). Fourthly, we investigated the morphological features of the RP and RP@TiO2 core-shell nanosctructures through optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, transmission electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction, and analyzed their chemical states using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The optical properties of the samples were studied by UV-vis absorption and photoluminescence measurements, while the electronic properties (defect density, Fermi level, electron spin resonance) were characterized via impedance analysis and electron paramagnetic resonance measurements. These studies enabled us to understand the surface defect effects on charge transfer and band alignment at the RP/TiO2 heterointerface. Finally, based on the fundamental findings, we optimized the material processing process to tune the defect density and energy levels of RP/TiO2, and used the material as photoanode in photoelectrochemical cells. The water splitting properties of the RP@TiO2 hybrid film were investigated, and a champion photoelectrochemical performance was achieved, outperforming previously reported electrode materials made with crystalline RP nanorods and RP-based hybrids.

439013.label: Major findings and research outcome
439013.value: 1. Owing to its optimal energy band position, red phosphorus (RP) has been considered as a promising elemental semiconductor for achieving simultaneous light-induced water oxidation and reduction. However, the photoelectrochemical performance of RP is limited by rapid charge recombination, low-charge carrier mobility, and poor water oxidation and film-forming capabilities. In this study, we explored the material strategies to address these limitations by developing a facile process to fabricate amorphous RP@TiO2 core-shell hybrid films. We found that the amorphous RP@TiO2 hybrid films annealed at low temperatures (e.g., 200–300 °C) in nitrogen exhibited significantly enhanced anodic photocurrent as compared to pure RP and pure TiO2 films due to a combined effect of enhanced visible light absorption and efficient heterointerface charge separation. Through a systematic characterization combining electronic, optical and electrochemical measurements, we found that the high density of Ti3+/oxygen vacancy complexes in amorphous TiO2 created a defect band above the valence band of RP but below the water oxidation potential, thereby inducing a quasi-type-II band alignment in the amorphous RP@TiO2 hybrid films; such electronic structure endowed amorphous TiO2 with a “hole leaky” feature to separate and transport the photogenerated holes from RP nanoparticles to exhibit an enhanced photoanodic performance. (Publication#1) 2. In this project we also investigated the gas-responsive electronic properties of amorphous RP (a-RP) by combining experimental characterizations with theoretical calculations. We found that a-RP films exhibited an amphoteric character for detecting both oxidizing and reducing gas molecules through variations in their electrical resistance. In particular, a-RP was found to be particularly promising for detecting NO2 at room temperature with excellent sensitivity, selectivity as well as a fast response–recovery speed. A unique sensing feature of a-RP toward NO2 was identified, which was associated with the extension of P–P bonds upon NO2 chemisorption. A physiochemical model was proposed to elaborate the synergistic effects of the P–P bond extension and Langmuir isotherm adsorption on the gas sensing processes of a-RP. These results elucidate the critical electronic and gas adsorption characteristics of a-RP. (Publication #2) 3. With the characterization platforms set up by this project, we were also able to conduct research in other nanostructured materials based devices (Publication #3 and #4). The studies achieved high-sensitivity room-temperature operated mid-infrared photodetectors and revealed the impact of indium diffusion at the ITO/active layer interface of memory devices.

439013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
439013.value: Scalability and efficiency are both important to realize hydrogen production with red phosphorus based photoelectrochemical cells (PEC). In this project we demonstrated a technique that can produce a large quantity of active materials that can exhibit the best PEC performance among reported red phosphorus based cells. However, compared to other PEC materials, the efficiency is still limited. Further development should be focused on developing scalable and safe nanostructuring techniques to reduce the size of the red phosphorus particles while still allowing for good electrical connections between individual nanostructures.

439013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
439013.value: Owing to its optimal energy band position, red phosphorus (RP) has been considered as a promising elemental semiconductor for achieving simultaneous light-induced water oxidation and reduction. Through this project we have developed a facile fabrication process to prepare RP@TiO2 hybrid film-based photoanodes of PEC water splitting, and systematically studied the working mechanism of the hybrid structure and its performance dependence on the fabrication conditions. The hybrid stratagem in this study demonstrates a scalable production method for creating hybrid nano- and microstructures in PEC electrodes, and it could be extended to other elemental semiconductors (e.g. sulfur and black phosphorus) and address issues such as poor film formation and low charge separation efficiency. Also, while black and blue phosphorus (both allotropes of elemental phosphorus) have recently been widely explored as an active material of electronic devices, amorphous red phosphorus (a-RP), a much cheaper and readily available phosphorus allotrope, has seldom been investigated as an electronic material and their gas sensing properties have never been studied. In this project we investigated these properties of a-RP by combining experimental characterizations with theoretical calculations.These results elucidate the critical electronic and gas adsorption characteristics of a-RP.

439113.label: Realisation of objectives
439113.value: The overall objective of this project is to design, fabricate and characterize new prototypes of remotely controlled helical swimming microrobots for electrical stimulation of biological cells with high precision. During the project period, we started to address the first objective on the controlled fabrication of ferromagnetic ABFs from metallic ribbons. A facile and general manufacturing batch process has been developed. And then the microstructure and mechanical properties of the ABFs have been investigated by using SEM, micromanipulators, and so on. Our study indicates that the metallic helical ribbon is mechanically stable with high elasticity. We successfully fabricated Ti nanocoils with different tilting angles of the substrate, and studied the optimized deposition parameters for the formation of a helical microstructure. Based on the same experimental approach, we also successfully fabricated Ni nanocoils with different tilting angles of the substrate. Standard photolithographic patterning processes were applied for the patterning of metal ribbons with different orientation on the substrate, and hence, helices with tuned geometrical parameters such as pitch, helicity angle and chirality were successfully achieved in a controllable fashion. On the other hand, 3-axis electromagnetic coils setup were constructed for the generation of rotating magnetic field for magnetic actuation of the ferromagnetic helical structures. We have developed a new method to precisely control the electrical current that flow through the electromagnetic coils, and we are currently applying a US non-provisional patent on this technology via ORKTS at CUHK. Our experimental results indicate that corkscrew motion of the ferromagnetic nanocoils can be generated when the input field frequency is sufficiently high. Whereas, when the frequency is reduced to a certain range, strong wobbling of the helical swimmer can be observed. The dynamics behaviour of the varied swimming motion of the ferromagnetic helical swimming (i.e. Ni nanocoils) under the rotating magnetic field is similar to that shown in the previous publications of magnetic helical swimming microrobots. And then, we had designed the helical microstructures with two tails. Due to the fluidic interaction between the neighbouring coils, the propulsion force can be adjusted. Interestingly, the hydrodynamics simulation results indicate that when the crossing angle of the two helices (with the same chirality) reaches some critical values, the propulsion force and the swimming direction can be reversed, which can significantly influence the swimming behaviour of the helical microswimmers. After we investigated the electric properties of the metallic ribbons and the electromagnetic coupling of the alternating magnetic field with the magnetic swimmers with varied configurations, their performance for targeted energy delivery to cells and the understanding of electrostimulation were conducted. In order to perform the targeted energy delivery, radio-frequency alternating magnetic field was applied, and the simulation works were also conducted. Within the framework of this project, three primary research contributions are shown as follows. First, a facile approach for the fabrication of ABFs from pure ferromagnetic metal materials has been developed. Conventional photolithography and low-cost thin film evaporation technique were utilized for the batch fabrication of the helical devices. In comparison to ABFs prepared by other methods, this new approach will significantly simplify the fabrication procedure. The second contribution is that the swimming performance and magnetic control of f-ABFs using a rotating magnetic field has been characterized and optimized. And the third contribution is electrical-magnetic coupling effects of the ferromagnetic microrobots and their interactions with the biological cells have been studied. Based on the results, we have published 30+ papers in the journals and conference proceedings, including the work in the top-tier journals, such as Science Robotics, Nature Communications, IEEE Transactions on Robotics, Soft Robotics, and so on. Some key results were also presented/disseminated in the international conferences and/or workshops. It is remarkable that our published works had been highlighted in the RGC YouTube Channel, Nature News, Science News, CNN, and many international and local media (Please see the details in part C, and the full list is available in PI's lab). Overall, there were no major problems on achieving the objects of the project.

439113.label: Major findings and research outcome
439113.value: The major finding and research outcome from this projects have been published in several top-tier journals, including Science Robotics (AAAS), Nature Communications, IEEE Transactions on Robotics, Soft Robotics, and so on, and some of them were also presented in international conferences and/or microrobotics related workshops. - Experimental analysis and simulation work were conducted to understand the dynamics of helical swimming microrobots in fluid. The swimming performances of helical microrobots with different numbers of helical tails and optimized designs for swimming and magnetic control were studied by using scaled-up prototypes. Furthermore, we have found that the helical swimmer with two tails may change its propulsion direction due to the hydrodynamic interactions with the fluid. - We used scaled-up helical swimming microrobots to understand the swimming performance of helical swimming microrobots with different surface coating. The results indicate that the coating will influence the fluidic drag induced by the fluid, hence will impact the propulsion significantly. Part of the results was presented in 2016 IEEE International Conference on Biomedical Robotics and Biomechatronics (BioRob 2016). - We have investigated the optimized shape of the helical microrobots for electromagnetic response. The optimized mechanical properties of the magnetic swimmers with high elasticity were also investigated. Some results were published in the top robotics journal "Soft Robotics" in 2018. - An invited review article about current status and potential applications of magnetic swimming micro-/nanorobots was published in the journal "Chinese Science Bulletin" in 2017. One year later, an editorial article was published in the journal "Quantitative Imaging in Medicine and Surgery" by PI's group about in vivo tracking and localization of micro-/nanorobots. - One US non-provisional patent application is on-going in PI's lab via ORKTS at CUHK, entitled “Method for Control Optimization of Multi-axis Electromagnetic Coils”, which provides a new method to precisely control the input current of the electromagnet, so that the magnetic field can be controlled accurately. - PI's lab has developed biohybrid helical swimming microrobots, which multi-functionalities. The key results were published in the prestigious robotics journal "Science Robotics", and it was also highlighted in Science News and the RGC YouTube Channel (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l2NQfgW8tSQ). Based on this work, we have also established good relationship on doing collaborative research with our partners from the University of Manchester for the development of magnetic swimming microrobots for biomedical applications. - PI's lab has also investigated the collective behaviour of varied magnetic swimmer which is necessary for the targeted delivery of drug and energy. Both simulation and experimental work were conducted. The collective behaviour of the microrobot swarm were also studied in varied biofluidic media. The work was published in Nature Communications, IEEE Transactions on Robotics, IEEE Transactions on Mechatronics, and Advanced Functional Materials, in 2017 and 2018.

439113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
439113.value: As we could see from our recent publications that the development of magnetic micro- and nanorobots for clinic applications have drawn lots of attention nowadays. Though several interesting properties of the magnetic microrobots have been systematically investigated including the materials and controlled fabrication, their swimming performance, and collective behaviors, the studies for in vivo applications are yet to be adequately investigated. Therefore, the future work on the microrobots for in vivo applications could be conducted from the following aspects, such as in vivo tracking, biodegradability and cytotoxicity of the microrobots, targeted drug/energy delivery in vivo, and the control of the microrobots in physiological (dynamic) conditions. We are working on those key aspects for the design and development of medical microrobots.

439113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
439113.value: Four decades ago, Howard Berg from Harvard University discovered that Escherichia coli bacteria propel themselves by means of rotating helical-shaped flagella. As researchers continue to investigate this unique method of low Reynolds flow locomotion, the appreciation of their elegant design has begun to inspire engineered systems for applications in micro-/nanorobotic drug delivery platforms in vitro and in vivo. While it remains a daunting task to replicate bacterial 45-nm-diameter motors, the use of low-strength rotating magnetic fields to externally power the microrobots removes the need for an onboard motor, power supply and bearing between the helical tail and the body. Instead, the focus lies on the challenging fabrication of three-dimensional helical structures at micro-/nanoscale. To date, several approaches have been reported to fabricate magnetic helical micro-/nanorobots with comparable dimensions to E. coli, in which the nanoribbons are lithographically patterned and self-assembled to form a helical shape. As bio-inspired microrobots, while these magnetic-torque-driven helical agents, have shown several advantages including precision motion control and a high swimming velocity, their morphologies, functionalities and embodied intelligence are yet to be adequately addressed for minimally invasive medicine. This project pave the way on design and development of multi-functional helical swimming microrobots for such research purposes.

439513.label: Project Title(Chinese)
439513.value: 大規模數據分析的稀疏優化算法和應用研究

439513.label: Project Objectives
439513.value: We will develop a suite of efficient algorithms for solving large-scale sparse optimization problems, especially for problems with multiple regularization terms. We will provide theoretical foundations for these algorithms such as proofs of their global convergence, rate of convergence and iteration complexity for epsilon-optimality. We will apply the developed algorithms to solve very large-scale and challenging problems from compressed sensing, machine learning and statistics such as robust PCA, sparse PCA, sparse inverse covariance selection, latent variable graphical model selection, stable principal component pursuit and compressive principal component pursuit. We will implement a variety of software packages for solving real applications of sparse optimization that can be used in different areas such as statistical learning, machine learning, finance and image processing.

We will provide theoretical foundations for these algorithms such as proofs of their global convergence, rate of convergence and iteration complexity for epsilon-optimality.

We will apply the developed algorithms to solve very large-scale and challenging problems from compressed sensing, machine learning and statistics such as robust PCA, sparse PCA, sparse inverse covariance selection, latent variable graphical model selection, stable principal component pursuit and compressive principal component pursuit.

We will implement a variety of software packages for solving real applications of sparse optimization that can be used in different areas such as statistical learning, machine learning, finance and image processing.

439513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
439513.value: 在現代的高維數據分析領域，我們正面臨著大規模和完全稠密的數據。我們很難用傳統的方法來分析這些數據。然而，在許多問題中，大規模，完全稠密的數據通常有特殊結構如稀疏低秩結構。稀疏優化是一個新近開發的工具對數據進行分析和提取完全稠密的數據的稀疏信息。這方面的研究，主要由於最近出現的壓縮傳感及相關問題而引起廣泛關注。 壓縮傳感可以使用較少的觀測數據來恢復可壓縮的信號（或低秩矩陣），從而對於數據採集非常昂貴的問題提供突破口。然而，壓縮感知的潛在影響不能沒有有效的優化算法，以及可以處理非常大規模和密集的數據的應用算法實現。雖然這些問題的凸鬆弛可以重新表示成線性規劃，二階錐規劃或半定規劃的問題，但是解決這些問題的傳統方法在這裡是不適用的，因為問題通常規模龐大，包含密集的數據。因此，如何解決大型稀疏優化問題變得非常具有挑戰性。 我們這個項目的主要研究目標是：（一）制定一套高效的算法求解大規模稀疏優化問題，尤其是對於多個正規化項的問題; （二）為這些算法提出理論基礎，比如證明這些算法的全局收斂性，收斂率和迭代複雜度； （三）應用這些算法來解決非常大型和具有挑戰性的問題，包括壓縮傳感，機器學習和統計領域的問題; （四）為這些不同領域的應用問題提供快速的程序軟件包。

439513.label: Realisation of objectives
439513.value: This project has led to 11 journal papers and 1 conference paper. In all these papers the funding number was explicitly acknowledged. Results in these papers well achieved the objective of this project. In this project, the PI designed a series of algorithms that solve large-scale sparse optimization problems, and analyzed their convergence properties. For problems with multiple regularization terms, the algorithms are also successfully designed and the convergence was analyzed. These theoretical results cover global convergence, convergence rate and iteration complexity. All objectives were achieved successfully. The algorithms studied in this project have been applied to solving problems arising from bioinformatics, image processing, signal processing and computer vision.

439513.label: Major findings and research outcome
439513.value: Major findings and research outcome of this project include: 1. We give sufficient conditions for guaranteeing the convergence of multi-block ADMM and analyze the convergence rate. (Ref [1,7,10]). 2. Studied inertial ADMM and inertial PPA algorithms and applied them to solving image processing problems. (Ref [8,9]). 3. Studied Lq-quasi-norm regularization problem, and apply it to solving signal processing problems (Ref [6]). 4. Studied variants of ADMM algorithms and analyzed their convergence properties ([4,12]). 5. Designed algorithms for the following problems: bioinformatics ([2]), distributed network ([3]), image denoising ([11]). 6. Studied stochastic approximation algorithm for solving general nonlinear programming problem ([5]).

439513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
439513.value: Potential for further development include: 1. Research results in this project indicate that multi-block ADMM converges under certain conditions. How to further weaken these conditions can be a further direction. 2. Inertial technique can accelerate some algorithms like ADMM and PPA. It will be interesting to extend the results to nonconvex problems. 3. Stochastic algorithms deserve further investigation. How to design a practical algorithm for stochastic nonlinear programming is very important.

439513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
439513.value: Sparse optimization plays a very important role in data analysis. In this project, we designed various algorithms for solving sparse optimization problems, and provide theoretical foundations for them. These algorithms are shown to be suitable for solving problems in bioinformatics, signal processing, image processing and so on.

439713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
439713.value: Advances in communication technologies change the way people communicate. For example, Internet brings together people who do not know each other before hand to engage in discussion of a certain topic. With cyber-physical systems, they also make daily life more convenient. People can make seamless payment using stored-value smartcard or auto-toll devices. One indispensable feature in these systems is privacy. However, perfect privacy may be abused, e.g., vandalism in discussion forum, money laundering, etc. Anonymous credential offers a cryptographic authentication mechanism that aims to provideaccountability and privacy at the same time. They are useful in applications which just require a proof of certain attributes such as membership, instead of positive identification of the user. Normally, the users remain anonymous, yet they are still accountable for their actions after authentication, by the means of anonymity revocation. Years of research efforts have been made on balancing between privacy and accountability, which is also the main theme of this proposal. Firstly, we aim to improve real-world anonymous credential realizations, such as Microsoft’s U-Prove, which does not support revocation without compromising untraceability. We aim to develop a new, efficient, and modular mechanism for revocation. Techniques developed will also benefit other anonymous credential systems. Secondly, we are particularly interested in application of anonymous credentials technologies in supporting privacy-preserving electronic payment. Realizing privacy-preserving payment systems is closely related to the problem of striking a balance in privacy and accountability which is the main focus of this work. The final focus of this proposal is on anonymous blacklistable credentials for the Internet, which a trusted party for ensuring privacy is often absent. Apart from blacklisting bad behaviour, rewarding user contribution via reputation score is equally important. Existing mechanisms either requires costly authentication process or a timely evaluation of all authenticated sessions to see if blacklisting is required. We aim to propose a new framework to resolve all these problems simultaneously. Improving any of these areas will make an impact on potentially millions of users worldwide. Underlying these key thrusts is privacy-enhancing cryptography, which the PI has been actively working on in recent years. The PI has also close collaboration with driving forces of anonymous credential systems such as Microsoft Research, Intel, and NTT R&D. The completion of this proposed project will result in new cryptographic building blocks and new paradigms of constructing cryptographic anonymous credential systems, which have a broad impact on cryptography, distributed systems, and privacy research communities. 通信技術的進步，改變了人們的溝通方式。例如，互聯網促進網上討論、儲值卡有助快速付款。在這些系統中不可缺少的一環是私隱。然而，私隱可能會被濫用，如破壞論壇、洗黑錢等。 匿名憑證可同時確保驗證的可問責性及私隱性。一般情況下，用戶保持匿名；需要時，他們的匿名性會被撤銷，從而要對自己的行為負責。 這項目主要是平衡私隱性和問責性，目標包括：一、改善現有系統，如目前並不支援撤銷的Microsoft U-Prove；二、保護電子付款的私隱性；三、在不用信賴任何人底下，支援獎勵及黑名單的匿名憑證。

439713.label: Realisation of objectives
439713.value: 1) Part of the literature survey has been presented in my various invited talks and my two postgraduate courses (detailed in "Other impact"). 2) Our preliminary work led to a paper entitled "Accumulators and U-Prove Revocation" in Financial Cryptography (FC) 2013. With our proposed accumulator, we proposed new applications of accumulators, including time-bound anonymous authentication (IEEE-TIFS 2015) and authenticated multi-pattern matching (AsiaCCS 2016). An accumulator is a cryptographic primitive which can accumulate $n$ elements while supporting constant-size zero-knowledge (non-)membership proof. Different from traditional blacklist approach of using accumulator which accumulates the blacklisted users, our first work in TIFS uses the accumulator to incorporate a time limit for revocation due to credential-expiry. The second work uses the accumulator to authenticate pattern matching result from a third party holding the pattern database. We need a new technique to support efficient (non-)matching proof that patterns which do (not) match the query. While some existing accumulator support non-membership proof, using it naively will require enumerating and proving all possible pattern-strings resulted from the query are absent, which is clearly inefficient. Multi-pattern matching found applications in virus scanning and intrusion detection in particular, if some matchings are maliciously omitted, it can lead to undetected intrusion. We also utilize a new notion of accumulator known as positional accumulators (and other tools) to build a very powerful tool (computation-trace indistinguishability obfuscation) which allows us to do many cryptographic tasks in the parallel RAM model. We consider the objective achieved for discovering new applications of accumulators in practical applications. One difficulty related to this objective is that one of my co-authors left his original institution which further complicated the already inconvenient remote collaboration in extending our result. 3) For (a), apart from the FC 2015 paper described in the mid-term report which provides a handy tool for equality testing and may find applications in linkable e-cash, we study a bigger goal of transferable and "combinable" anonymous credentials in general. The preliminary results were reported as an invited talk "Functional Credentials for Internet of Things" in ACM-IOTPTS 2016. We also initiated the study of "Multi-Key Homomorphic Signatures Unforgeable under Insider Corruption", which is under submission. For (b), as in the mid-term report, we broadened our scope to consider physical attacks on secret credential/keys. Our works are published in Cocoon 2016, AsiaCCS 2015 and 2014. The first is about when we do not sure which 1 of 2 implementations is indeed secure, how to achieve security against chosen-ciphertext attack (CCA) in public-key/identity-based encryption (IBE), both notions are useful for group signature. The second considers the security of signature/IBE under active attacks like fault-injection. The last aims to hold the user who leaked the credential accountable. For (c), we have identified a possible implementation flaw of Trusted Platform Module (TPM) 2.0 signature when used for anonymous authentication as described in the mid-term report. We broadened our scope to consider privacy-preserving payment settlement for cyber-physical systems in general. E-cash by itself can only preserve privacy for withdrawal/spending of e-coins but not whether one has paid enough e-coins while not leaking the amount. New ideas/paradigms are needed to circumvent this seemingly unachievable goal. The result is still under submission. For (d), our results are published in NSS 2016 ("Privacy Preserving Credit Systems"). Our systems can hide the user expenses from the bank while preserving most features of current credit-card systems. Our first system is relatively lightweight which only uses group signatures and e-cash systems. The core idea is all users commit to the spending and settle the payment later both by group signatures. The bank will open the signatures associated to any unsettled (i.e., without the corresponding later payment) spending. However, all users have the same payment due date. Our system resolves this issue with anonymous transferable e-cash systems and non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs. One difficulty for (b) and (c) is that experiments on real-world hardware are expected, while our team mostly work on the theory/software side. We are now involving other researchers in wireless networks and cyber-physical systems. We consider the objective achieved. Beyond the published results, (a) gives a solid theoretical foundation of what kind of functionalities and security requirements can multi-key homomorphic signatures achieve, and (c) suggests a new paradigm of privacy-preserving payment. 4) For (a), which is on proposing and realizing a new framework for anonymous credentials with reputation and revocation support, we have eventually proposed two new frameworks and completed two manuscripts. The titles are omitted here for better preserving the anonymity of future submissions which are often required. We consider the frameworks are promising improvements and the objective achieved. Yet, the above two papers require "major revision" after submission to a journal. One difficulty is that the teams involve external collaborator or (former) undergraduate students who can no longer invest enough time to continue the revision, especially on the prototype and experiments. It is also generally difficult to recruit research assistants who can quickly learn the cryptography theory behind and help with the implementation. For (b), we started some general research in lattice-based cryptography and outsourcing computation as described in the mid-term report. Specifically, we proposed real-hidden identity-based signatures in FC 2017. This is a major improvement since the seminal work appeared in FC 2007. In short, it addresses a catch-22 problem of preserving anonymity while ensuring accountability. An opening authority (OA) of a group signature scheme can open a signature and reveal its true signer. Not only the secret key of the OA but also a member database (cf. a public-key repository) is often required for this opening. This "secret members list" put the anonymity of members at risk as each of them is a potential signer. The seminal schemes did not fully resolve this issue since they require a computationally-expensive procedure for the opening. Our work resolves this issue. 5) For (a), we start with the proposals of a new general primitive of all-but-one dual projective hashing in ACNS 2014 (which found application in CCA-security), a new practical dual-receiver encryption scheme in CT-RSA 2014 (with escrow as one of the major features), and new distributed signature schemes described in the mid-term report (CT-RSA 2014 and full version in Theoretical Computer Science 2015). Specifically, we proposed two new generic constructions of sanitizable signature in ESORICS 2016. While being a privacy-oriented primitive which considers the accountability of sanitizer, this work also proposed a new primitive called rerandomizable tagging and a new construction of accountable ring signatures based on structure-preserving encryption. This funding also supported the study of Tao ZHANG. His Ph.D. thesis is titled "Contribution to Structure-Preserving Cryptography and Accountable Privacy". One of the major results is another structure-preserving primitive which is currently under submission. For (b), a core primitive in the work of "Password-Controlled Encryption with Accountable Break-Glass Access" appeared in AsiaCCS 2016 is an identity-based encryption with an anonymous secret key issuing (ASKI) protocol. We also proposed "A Framework of Multi-Authority Attribute-Based Encryption with Outsourcing and Revocation" in SACMAT 2016. While the paper did not study ASKI, the proposed abstraction may lead to an easier generic construction of an accompanying ASKI protocol. We also have a manuscript on "Exponent-inversion Signatures and IBE under Static Assumptions" under submission. In particular, it discussed new anonymous credential systems and new traitor tracing system which can hold the user who leaks the secret key accountable.

439713.label: Major findings and research outcome
439713.value: *TIFS14: anonymous credentials with timestamp embedded for natural revocation with O(1)-size transcript by accumulators; *TCS15-WWWCQLD (+ CTRSA14): a distributed signature scheme for signers represented by a monotone access structures, and its extensions; *TC16 (+ Infocom14): a systematic way to construct provable data possession protocol from any secure network coding protocol; *Inscrypt14-LCC: extend the notion of lattice trapdoors the ring setting with careful justification; *Inscrypt14-ZC: identified a possible implementation flaw of TPM 2.0 signature application when the same signing algorithm and the signing key are re-used; *CTRSA14: formally proposed soundness of dual-receiver encryption with applications in complete non-malleability and more; *Cocoon16: how to ensure security by combining two implementations when only an unknown one among them is secure; *AsiaCCS15: study and achieve security against related-randomness attack (which generalizes the known related-key attacks); when the randomness used in different invocations of the cryptographic algorithms are related. *AsiaCCS14: a black-box-tracable identity-based broadcast encryption from fingerprint codes; *ACNS14: a simple construction of all-but-one-loss trapdoor functions and a generic construction of chosen-ciphertext-attack secure deterministic encryption in the standard model; *ESORICS14: securely outsourcing variable-exponent variable-base exponentiations in one untrusted program model; *CNS14: securely outsourced arithmetic circuits using additive/multiplicative homomorphic encryption in two non-colluding cloud model; *FC15: a primitive which encoded message can hide information about the plaintext, but still supports equality test between encoded messages and plaintext; with application in privacy-preserving collaborative filtering; *ITCS16: cryptography in the parallel random-access-machine model is possible; *AsiaCCS16-ZZCZZ: multi-pattern matching, which compares a large set of patterns against a given query string, can be outsourced with verifiability; *AsiaCCS16-ZCS: a two-factor scheme involving a user-chosen password and the master public/secret key pair, the master allows break-glass access, yet is held accountable when it does so; *SACMAT16: a semi-generic construction of multi-authority attribute-based encryption with outsourcing and revocation; *Mycrypt16: an alternative definition of anonymous communication under mass surveillance, a modular construction and specific optimizations; *NSS16: credit-card systems that hide the expenses of individual users from the bank, while the bank can make sure the expenses are settled; *ESORICS16: two generic constructions of sanitizable signatures with unlinkability such that no one can link sanitized message-signature pairs of the same document; *FC17: a group signature scheme such that the open authority can learn the real signer of a normally anonymous signature without the need for storing a membership database;

439713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
439713.value: Some works such as the papers appeared in Infocom 2014 (later IEEE Trans. Computers 2016), ITCS 2016, SACMAT 16, the invited talk in IoTPTS 16, and a pre-print first uploaded to IACR ePrint Archive 2016 form the preliminary work and foundations for two later GRF grant proposals, yet, unfortunately they are not funded. Nevertheless, some parts of the research plans laid out by these two proposals are still ongoing. The cryptographic techniques in ensuring accountable privacy in general also found application in other cryptosystems. In particular, it is useful for one of the objectives in my GRF proposal this year (result not yet known by the time of the internal deadline for this report). Thanks to this funding, there are also a number of ongoing works to be submitted and under submissions. We will further develop those.

439713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
439713.value: Anonymity is a basic human right. Yet, perfect anonymity might be abused. This research investigates what can be possible, i.e., a right balance between anonymity and accountability. It is possible that anonymity can be preserved without affecting other security requirements. As one example, in payment systems, a transaction will not be traceable to the original payer, yet the payer cannot double spend the electronic cash (which is a series of 0 and 1 and can be freely copied after all) and the recipient is guaranteed to get the payment. For another example, users can have a credential which allows them to login to some services anonymously, yet, they can still have their actions affecting the reputation score stored in their credentials, and can be eventually banned if the user has done "too much harm" under the anonymity protection. This requires not only a careful definition of multiple security requirements, but also dedicated designs of cryptographic schemes which achieve a set of seemingly contradictory requirements simultaneously. This study presents results in this regard. Hopefully, it makes our society one step further in enjoying the nice services brought by information technology, without compromising user privacy and without worrying privacy will be abused.
