439813.label: Project Objectives
439813.value: The overall goal of the proposed research is the development and characterization of an aberration-corrected NLO endomicroscope prototype. The endomicroscope will be capable of operating in both two-photon excitation and confocal mode at an adjustable frame rate between 1 to 30 frames per second. The in-plane field of view is 400 x 400 μm2 with a depth penetration between 200-500 μm. When operated at low frame rates, i.e. 1-2 fps, the endomicroscope will have a lateral (in-plane) resolution and axial (out-of-plane) resolution of 1.0 μm and 2.0 μm, respectively. The essential elements of NLO endomicroscope include: (1) microactuators, (2) micro-scanners, (3) aberration-corrected compact lens, and (4) control and electronic system. The technical objectives which define the criteria for the success of this research are follows: We will use the stress-stiffening concept to develop two frequency-tunable micromirrors and related microfabrication processes that enable the fabrication of an integrated compact scanning optical bench. The micromirror’s resonant frequencies will be adjustable between 3kHz ± 250Hz and 1kHz ± 100Hz respectively. Both mirrors will have a mechanical scan angle of 6 degrees (required to achieve the proposed work volume). We will understand the physics and develop parametric models to demonstrate the performance improvement of a micro-device with integrated electrostatic comb-drive and electrothermal actuators. The parametric models will be used to guide the device design/optimization, and to predict the micro-device’s performance. We will model, design, and fabricate a hybrid lens of 1 mm diameter in size. The hybrid lens will integrate a refractive surface and an optimized diffractive surface into a single lens. The focal point shift, a measure of chromatic aberration, for a parallel incoming light of wavelengths between 400nm to 800nm will be less than 1.5 micron. (A typical GRIN lens of 1 mm diameter has a focal point shift of 25-30 micron.) We will develop proper fixation and assembly methods to integrate and align the micro-scanner and micro-optics on a scanning optical bench. The optical scanner will have a work volume of 400 x 400 x 400 μm3 and a bandwidth of 3 kHz for its fast axis. Proper control techniques will be implemented to the micro-scanner to eliminate the unwanted dynamics. We will characterize the optical performance of the prototype NLO endomicroscope, including sensitivity, lateral/vertical resolution in both confocal and two-photon mode. Tasks directed at achieving these objectives are described in the “Research Plan and Methodology” section.
rows: The overall goal of the proposed research is the development and characterization of an aberration-corrected NLO endomicroscope prototype. The endomicroscope will be capable of operating in both two-photon excitation and confocal mode at an adjustable frame rate between 1 to 30 frames per second. The in-plane field of view is 400 x 400 μm2 with a depth penetration between 200-500 μm. When operated at low frame rates, i.e. 1-2 fps, the endomicroscope will have a lateral (in-plane) resolution and axial (out-of-plane) resolution of 1.0 μm and 2.0 μm, respectively. The essential elements of NLO endomicroscope include: (1) microactuators, (2) micro-scanners, (3) aberration-corrected compact lens, and (4) control and electronic system. The technical objectives which define the criteria for the success of this research are follows:

We will use the stress-stiffening concept to develop two frequency-tunable micromirrors and related microfabrication processes that enable the fabrication of an integrated compact scanning optical bench. The micromirror’s resonant frequencies will be adjustable between 3kHz ± 250Hz and 1kHz ± 100Hz respectively. Both mirrors will have a mechanical scan angle of 6 degrees (required to achieve the proposed work volume).

We will understand the physics and develop parametric models to demonstrate the performance improvement of a micro-device with integrated electrostatic comb-drive and electrothermal actuators. The parametric models will be used to guide the device design/optimization, and to predict the micro-device’s performance.

We will model, design, and fabricate a hybrid lens of 1 mm diameter in size. The hybrid lens will integrate a refractive surface and an optimized diffractive surface into a single lens. The focal point shift, a measure of chromatic aberration, for a parallel incoming light of wavelengths between 400nm to 800nm will be less than 1.5 micron. (A typical GRIN lens of 1 mm diameter has a focal point shift of 25-30 micron.)

We will develop proper fixation and assembly methods to integrate and align the micro-scanner and micro-optics on a scanning optical bench. The optical scanner will have a work volume of 400 x 400 x 400 μm3 and a bandwidth of 3 kHz for its fast axis. Proper control techniques will be implemented to the micro-scanner to eliminate the unwanted dynamics. We will characterize the optical performance of the prototype NLO endomicroscope, including sensitivity, lateral/vertical resolution in both confocal and two-photon mode.
Tasks directed at achieving these objectives are described in the “Research Plan and Methodology” section.

439813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
439813.value: This research aims to generate the scientific and technological knowledge required to (1) design next-generation microscale precision scanning devices for in vivo procedures, and (2) develop new systems and methods for high resolution, non-invasive optical imaging. Specifically, we will develop compliant mechanism based micro-actuation and high-speed scanning technologies and new aberration-corrected lenses that enable the construction of a multimodal nonlinear optical (NLO) endomicroscope with subcellular resolution and an adjustable frame rate, e.g. 1-30 frames per second. Although greatly researched, to date none of the NLO endomicroscopes have demonstrated comparable performance to their macroscale versions, i.e. two-photon or confocal microscopes. This is mainly attributed to (1) the non-optimized light delivery from a light source to a specimen and the use of gradient index (GRIN) lenses as objective lenses that generate significant chromatic aberrations, and (2) the insufficient range and speed of current microscale scanning/positioning devices and technologies. Presently, state-of-the-art NLO endomicroscopes have approximately 10% of the required scan volume at a much slower frame rate, achieving a resolution of approximately 2/10 µm in lateral/axial directions, versus 0.2/0.6 µm for a macroscale scanning confocal system. This research will first tackle the technical issues by (1) developing new micro-scanning/actuation technologies and endoscopy-optimized frequency-tunable micromirrors, and (2) developing and custom-fabricating a millimeter-sized hybrid lens that combines a refractive surface and a diffractive surface in one single lens element for chromatic aberration and field curvature correction. These technologies will then be used to develop a compact multi-axis scanning optical bench for the construction of a NLO endomicroscope. Upon completion, the endomicroscope can be readily used to perform simple in vivo biological studies; for example, to track cells in internal organs including the spleen, the mesenteric lymph node, and the kidney. The developed scanning devices, compact aberration-corrected lenses and NLO endomicroscope may impact both engineering and medical fields. For example, the frequency-tuning concept enables the micromirror to operate at a more flexible frequency range with increased precision and a wider variety of applications. The NLO endomicroscope, with improved resolution, frame rate and field of view, will significantly impact the diagnosis, staging, and treatment of various early epithelial cancers (such as colorectal, esophageal, and cervical cancers), for which real-time tissue imaging to a depth of a few hundred microns may suffice. 本項目意在探索實現活體實時高分辨率內視顯微鏡的技術與方法。近年經過了大量的研究和實踐，內視顯微鏡的性能得到了許多提升，但是由於光源傳導尚未優化，自聚焦透鏡色差以及微掃描器件性能較弱等原因，使得目前非線性光學內視顯微鏡難以望非線性光學顯微鏡（如雙光子顯微鏡）之項背。當下最先進的非線性光學內視顯微系統的性能也只有普通非線性光學顯微鏡的十分之一，其能夠獲得的橫向分辨率只有2微米，軸向分辨率只有10微米，於普通非線性光學顯微鏡橫向0.2微米，軸向0.6微米的分辨能力相距甚遠。另外由於微掃描器件的性能限制，非線性光學內視顯微系統只能在低速掃描情況下獲得十分之一於預期掃描體積內的掃描成像。為了解決這一難題，本項目將研究微掃描器件設計的新方法，並設計可以修正色差和場曲的混合型內視成像透鏡，最後將兩者結合在一起，應用到原型機的設計與組裝之中。最後通過追跡內臟（如脾臟，腎臟，淋巴結等）內細胞遷徙過程的方式驗證系統性能與新方法的實用性。

439913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
439913.value: 這項研究的目的是開發模擬軟骨細胞外基質（ ECM ）的生物材料支架並研究其對人骨髓間充質幹細胞（ hMSC）的初始軟骨，隨後肥大分化和組織礦化的作用。 骨關節炎（OA ）是人關節軟骨的逐步退化所導致的一種疾病。最近的一項研究發現，約10％的50歲及以上的香港人口有膝關節骨性關節炎的症狀。這表明骨關節炎是香港以及世界各地的殘疾的主要原因之一。目前的治療包括關節置換術和軟骨鑲嵌有各種限制，如有限的壽命，缺乏供體組織和疾病傳播的潛在風險。基於幹細胞的軟骨組織工程或再生醫學，是一種很有前途的治療骨性關節炎的方法。由於其多能性和容易獲得等優點，骨髓間充質幹細胞（hMSCs）已成為用於軟骨修復的重要細胞來源。然而在首先分化為軟骨細胞後，hMSCs的繼續分化為肥大細胞導致軟骨的大量礦化。這個問題現在被確認為是使用hMSCs廣泛進行臨床軟骨修復的一個主要障礙。 軟骨細胞外基質（ ECM ）分子已被證明具有調節幹細胞軟骨分化的作用。我們提議開發包含多種ECM分子的水凝膠支架。這項工作的新穎之處在於三個方面。首先，以往的研究很少調查ECM分子對hMSC肥大的效果。其次，獨特的生物材料的水凝膠支架允許我們對每個ECM分子的貢獻進行系統性參數化研究。最後，還沒有研究調查水凝膠支架上的ECM濃度梯度對軟骨肥大和基質礦化的影響。 此項目將幫助引導生物材料支架的仿生化設計。從這項研究結果不僅會促進間葉幹細胞在軟骨修復上的使用，但也將有助於發展幹細胞治療支架修復其他結締組織包括骨，肌腱/韌帶，半月板和椎間盤。

439913.label: Realisation of objectives
439913.value: We have successfully achieve all the objectives in this project. In this project, we synthesized crosslinkable ECM biopolymers including hyaluronic acid (MeHA), chondroitin sulfate (MeCS), and collagens (COL) for fabricating biomimetic hybrid hydrogels containing selected cartilaginous ECM molecules of defined dosage (Objective 1). To evaluate the efficacy of ECM components in regulating stem cell chondrogenesis and hypertrophy, the hMSCs encapsulated in hydrogel constructs were assessed on day 7 and day 28. The majorities of the encapsulated cells in all groups (MeHA+Col, MeHA+MeCS and MeHA) remain viable and are distributed uniformly in the hydrogels after 7 days and 28 days of culture. These data show that these biopolymer-based hydrogels support cell viability during long-term culture. On day 7, the hMSCs in the HA hydrogels that contain collagen or CS (“MeHA+Col” and “MeHA+MeCS”) exhibit the upregulated expression of aggrecan mRNA compared to those in the pure HA hydrogels (“MeHA”). The “MeHA+MeCS” group and the “MeHA+Col” group show a higher level of type II collagen gene expression than the “MeHA” group. On day 28, according to the RT-PCR analysis, the expression of both type 10 collagen (Collagen 10) and matrix metallopeptidase 13 (MMP13), two key markers of chondrocyte hypertrophy, are down-regulated in the “MeHA+Col” and the “MeHA+MeCS” group compared to that in the “MeHA” group. More specifically, the expression of type 10 collagen is decreased in the “MeHA+Col” and the “MeHA+MeCS” group compared to the “MeHA” group, respectively. And the expression of MMP13 has decreased in the “MeHA+Col” and the “MeHA+MeCS” group compared to the “MeHA” group, respectively. These data suggest that the ECM hydrogel support the differentiation of the encapsulated stem cells during long term culture. We employed these biomimetic hydrogels to investigate the effect of the ECM molecules on the chondrogenesis and hypertrophy of encapsulated hMSCs (Objective 2). These biomimetic hydrogels decouple the function of each cartilaginous ECM component and allow the contribution of each component to be evaluated systemically. We found that the hyaluronic acid (HA) hydrogels containing type I collagen (MeHA+ Col) upregulate the deposition of PGs of hMSCs after being cultured in the chondrogenesis and hypertrophy condition in vitro and subcutaneous study in vivo. However, the HA hydrogels containing chondroitin sulfate (MeHA+MeCS) promote the deposition of proteoglycans (PGs), while suppressing the calcification of hMSCs encapsulated when compared with the control HA hydrogels. Specifically, when normalized by the sample wet weight, the quantification of GAGs shows that the hMSCs-laden hydrogel constructs of the “MeHA+Col” and the “MeHA+MeCS” groups possess higher GAGs content than those of the “MeHA” group. This quantification of cartilaginous matrix content is based on analyzing one third of each sample from three parallel hydrogel constructs cultured under the same condition. Consistently, the Alcian Blue and Safranin O staining of the histological sections show more accumulation of GAGs in both the “MeHA+Col” and the “MeHA+MeCS” groups than in the control group after 28 days of in vitro culture. The calcium content decreases in the “MeHA+MeCS” group compared with that in the “MeHA” group. Von Kossa staining shows more calcium distribution around the periphery of the sectioned samples . Immunohistochemical staining against type II collagen of the histological sections of the “MeHA+Col” and the “MeHA+MeCS” groups also shows more substantial and distributed ECM deposition in the intercellular space compared to that in the “MeHA” group. Based on the pixel intensity measurement using Image J software, staining against type II collagen in the “MeHA+Col I” and the “MeHA+MeCS” groups is 72% and 56% higher than that in the “MeHA” group. Type I collagen expression remains low in all the three groups. We further conjugated sulfate groups to HA. These sulfated HA exhibit significantly slower degradation by hyaluronidase compared to the wild type HA likely because of that sulfation reduces the available HA octasaccharide substrate needed for the effective catalytic action of hyaluronidase. Moreover, we found that the sulfated HA significantly improved the protein sequestration, thereby effectively extending the availability of the proteinaceous drugs in the hydrogels. In the following in vitro study, we demonstrated that the sulfation exerted no negative effect on the viability of human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs). Furthermore, the sulfated HA promoted the chondrogenesis and suppresses the hypertrophy of hMSCs both in vitro and in vivo. Moreover, animal research demonstrate that the sulfated HA hydrogels avert the cartilage abrasion and hypertrophy in the animal osteoarthritis joints. When these biopolymers were dispesed in these biomimetic hydrogels with a spatial gradient, differential effect on stem cells encapsulated in different regions of the hydrogels can be observed (Objective 3). Stem cells showed enhanced expression of chondrogenic and decreased hypertrophic marker genes in regions where chondroitin sulfate is present, leading to increased cartilage matrix depositiona and suppressed calcificaiton content. We evaluated the effect of the ECM hydrogels on the chondrogenesis and hypertrophy of hMSCs in vivo by implanting hMSCs-laden hydrogels subcutaneously in nude mice. The GAG quantification data show that the hydrogel constructs of the “MeHA+Col” group and the “MeHA+MeCS” group possess a much higher level of GAG deposition than those in the “MeHA” group when normalized by the DNA content. Furthermore, histological sections of both the “MeHA+Col” and the “MeHA+MeCS” groups exhibit more intense Alcian Blue and Safranin O staining compared to the control “MeHA” group, and this is consistent with the GAG quantification data. The result of calcium quantification shows a trend of reduced calcification in the “MeHA+MeCS” group although no significant difference in calcium content is detected between these groups. Immunohistochemical staining on the histological sections of the implanted hydrogels shows a result which is consistent with that of the in vitro study. More specifically, the staining against type II collagen and CS in both the “MeHA+Col I” and the “MeHA+MeCS” groups is more intense than that in the “MeHA” group, thus indicating more deposition of cartilage-specific matrix in these two groups.These findings will provide valuable guidance on the design of hydrobel biomaterials for repair composite tissue involving multiple tissue types defects such as osteochondral lesions.

439913.label: Major findings and research outcome
439913.value: In research output paper No.2 and No.3, we developed hybrid hydrogels containing selected cartilaginous ECM molecules of defined dosage. We employed these ECM hydrogels to investigate the effect of the ECM molecules on the chondrogenesis and hypertrophy of encapsulated hMSCs. These hybrid hydrogels decouple the function of each cartilaginous ECM component and allow the contribution of each component to be evaluated systemically. We found that the hyaluronic acid (HA) hydrogels containing type I collagen upregulate the deposition of PGs of hMSCs after being cultured in the chondrogenesis and hypertrophy condition in vitro and subcutaneous study in vivo. However, the HA hydrogels containing chondroitin sulfate promote the deposition of proteoglycans (PGs), while suppressing the calcification of hMSCs encapsulated when compared with the control HA hydrogels.

439913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
439913.value: These findings demonstrate the potential of tuning the recipe of cartilage-specific biopolymers incorporated into the hMSC-laden hydrogels to modulate the extent of maturation and calcification of the engineered cartilage. The findings of this study will not only help guide the design of hydrogels for spatially presenting influential ECM molecules but will also facilitate the development of composite tissue implants for the repair of interfacial tissue defects in vivo. These hydrogels can be further developed into injectable materials for minimally invasive surgery. We can are currently adding self-reactive groups to these biopolymers which will also spontaneous gelation of the hydrogel after injection into in vivo defect sites.

439913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
439913.value: The microenvironment of the extracellular matrix (ECM) plays a key role in directing the viability and subsequent differentiation of the encapsulated stem cells by the specific integration between the hydrated biomolecules and cell surface receptors. Herein, we developed a hydrogel platform based on hyaluronic acid (HA) that presents cartilage ECM molecules as a form of developmental cues. The hybrid hydrogels were generated by coupling photo-cross-linkable HA with selected cartilaginous ECM molecules including chondroitin sulfate (CS) and type I collagen (Col I), and we studied the decoupled function of these cues in regulating the initial chondrogenesis, subsequent hypertrophy, and tissue mineralization by hMSCs. The quantification results also show that glycosaminoglycans accumulation increases in the hybrid hydrogels containing cartilaginous ECM molecules, both in vitro and in vivo. We hypothesize that these additional ECM components in the HA hydrogels further regulate the hMSCs chondrogenesis and hypertrophy by coordination. The understanding obtained in this study may guide biomaterial scaffold design, thereby facilitating manipulation of the differentiation and mineralization of induced hMSCs for application in the repair of different musculoskeletal defects.

440713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
440713.value: Youth unemployment has become a global issue. Traditional studies on unemployment, including those on youth employment, primarily focus on the impact of objective employment status and neglect the importance of one's subjective estimate of finding employment. Employability, a relatively new concept defined as subjective perception of the possibility of finding employment, has therefore been introduced (Berntson & Marklund, 2007) and has attracted increasing research attention. It has been argued that employability has diverse impacts on individuals. However, there has been very limited research on employability of unemployed youth. Moreover, no study has been conducted to examine the development of employability, and its impacts on psychological health, job search behavior, and attitudes associated with social stability among unemployed youth in Hong Kong. A two-wave longitudinal study is proposed to examine the antecedents and consequences of employability for Hong Kong unemployed youth. Following the conceptual model proposed by Fugate, Kinicki, and Ashforth (2004) and our preliminary findings (Chan & Au, ongoing), it is predicted that unemployed youth who are more adaptable, self-directed, better-educated and skillful, and who have more social capital will perceive that they can find employment more easily than those who are lower in these dimensions. Moreover, according to the social identity literature (Tajfel & Turner, 1979), unemployed youth who perceive a higher level of employability will believe they are more likely to improve their socioeconomic status and move up the social hierarchy. In turn, they will have better psychological health and exhibit stronger job search intensity. To the extent that they exhibit stronger job search intensity, in the long run they will receive more job offers, which should enhance their perceived likelihood of improvement in socioeconomic status and psychological health, and reduce their negativity toward the rich, a social phenomenon that has attracted increasing attention from different disciplines. Furthermore, the impact of employability is expected to be more pronounced among unemployed youth who face more family and financial obligations. In sum, the proposed research will investigate the antecedents and consequences of employability among unemployed youth in Hong Kong. Conceptually speaking, it will examine the validity of a framework of youth employability that integrates previous findings on this topic. From an applied perspective, our results will help formulate public policies and effective intervention for enhancing unemployed youth's employability which, in turn, positively influences their psychological health and employment opportunities, as well as their attitudes toward the rich. 青少年失業已成為國際性議題。傳統上，有關失業問題的研究，包括青少年失業，主要集中於就業狀況的客觀影響，而忽略了個人對求職主觀估計的重要性。因此，「就業能力」(Employability; Berntson & Marklung, 2007) 這一個較新的概念在近年吸引越來越多的研究關注。就業能力定義為就職可能性的主觀看法。有學者認為就業能力對個人有不同範疇的影響。然而，只有少數研究針對探討失業青年的就業能力。再者，目前還沒有研究探討香港失業青年就業能力的發展變化及其對心理健康、求職行為和社會穩定性相關態度等的影響。 本建議書將採用二波段的縱貫性研究法，以研究香港失業青年就業能力的前因和影響。根據Fugate, Kinicki 和Ashforth(2004)提出的概念模型和我們初步的調查結果 (Chan & Au, ongoing)預測，適應力、自我導向性、教育程度較高、擁有較高技能和「社會資本」(social capital)的失業青年會認為自己較其他在這些層面得分較低的人更容易找到工作。此外，根據「社會性認定」(Social Identity)的文獻 (Tajfel & Turner, 1979)，認為自己就業能力較高的青年相信他們更有可能改善他們的社會經濟地位和在社會階層中上移。繼而，他們會有更好的心理健康及表現出更高的求職強度。長遠來看，他們將獲得更多的就業機會，進而提高其對社會經濟地位和心理健康改善的可能性的主觀看法，並減低仇富的心理。消極仇富這個社會現象已引起不同的學科越來越多的關注。此外，我們預計就業能力會對肩負着家庭和經濟重担的失業青年起了更明顯的影響。 總括而言，本研究計劃會探討香港失業青年就業能力的前因後果。從概念層面上，研究將測驗結合了以往關於青年就業能力調查結果的概念架構的效度。從應用層面上，我們的研究結果將有助於制訂公共政策和有效的干預，加強失業青年的就業能力，繼而提昇他們的心理健康和就業機會，以及改變他們對富人的態度。

440713.label: Realisation of objectives
440713.value: To empirically examine each of our three major objectives, we successfully collected data from 359 unemployed youth in Hong Kong, across two waves of data collection with 9 months apart (out of 533 participants at Wave 1; a retention rate of 67.4%). Participants, all aged between 16 and 27 years old and had been unemployed for at least 3 months prior to the survey, were recruited from diverse channels, ranging from employment service, community service, and youth service centers, to a couple non-governmental organizations (NGOs) in the community. We also approached young people in job fairs, and made announcements about our study in online forums. Further, we asked our participants to invite their acquaintances who were eligible for our study to participate. In our statistical analyses, we excluded 104 individuals who had decided to go back to school at Wave 2, leaving us 255 individuals. Among them, a majority of 56.7% remained unemployed at the end of the project. That is, out of the 533 unemployed participants at Wave 1, only 110 of them were confirmed to secure a job 9 months later, signifying the potential severity of the problem. At any event, our interpretation below is based on analyses of the completed responses from 255 individuals. Objective 1: The proposed study on Hong Kong unemployed youth will examine whether adaptability, career identity, human capital, and social capital are determinants of their sense of employability. Our Reply: Path analytic results generally provide full support to our four hypothesized antecedents of sense of employability. Specifically, we found that boundaryless mindset (a measure of adaptability), career self-efficacy (a measure of career identity), work experience (a proxy of human capital), and social support (a measure of social capital) all significantly contributed to Hong Kong unemployed youth’s sense of employability. Although not directly predicting employability, proactive personality (another measures of adaptability), identity awareness (another measure of career identity), education (proxy of human capital), and networking (another measure of social capital) were all linked with correlates of employability. Proactive individuals appear to perceive themselves as upwardly mobile. Those who are retrospective in thinking about their career and/or have abundant informational support from their career networks exhibit higher job search intensity. Also, highly educated persons tend to enjoy high income in the future. Taken together, we can conclude that proactive personality, identity awareness, education, and networking are also significant concerns of unemployed youth, and should not be ignored in the relevant research. In sum, we have gathered empirical evidence to support our four hypothesized antecedents of sense of employability. Objective 2: It will also investigate whether the impacts of employability on the three important outcomes (i.e., job search intensity, psychological health, and negativity toward the rich) are mediated by individuals’ perceived upward mobility. Our Reply: Empirical support for Objective 2 is mostly positive, as mediation analyses provide support for two of the three consequences. Specifically, we hypothesized that the effects of employability on the three outcomes would be mediated by individuals’ perceived upward mobility. First, path analytic results reveal that employability was indeed positively related to perceived upward mobility and high perceived mobility was linked with high job search intensity. Bootstrapping procedures were then employed to examine the strength of the mediation effects. Results demonstrate that perceived mobility indeed mediated the association between employability and job search intensity (indirect effect = .04, p = .019). Perceived upward mobility was also found to be positively associated with psychological health. Moreover, bootstrapping analysis confirms that perceived mobility mediated the employability – psychological health linkage (indirect effect = .05, p = .014). However, the proposed mediation effect of perceived upward mobility on the employability – negativity toward the rich link was not supported. Counter to our hypothesis, perceived upward mobility was weakly but positively associated with negativity toward the rich (i.e., the more upwardly mobile and employable our unemployed youth perceived, the more negative they were toward the rich). Moreover, bootstrapping analysis fails to confirm the mediation effect. We are somewhat puzzled by the positive association between perceived mobility and negative attitudes toward the rich. Intuitively (and as hypothesized), if unemployed youth think they are unemployable and cannot move up the social hierarchy, they may exhibit heightened negativity toward people with high SES, perceiving them as, for example, hypocritical. In contrast, if unemployed youth think they will get employed and can improve their SES, they may not display such negativity. Our findings reveal the opposite. One potential explanation is that the above reasoning may be applicable to individuals in general. However, our particpants mostly remained unemployed (56.7%) throughout the research period. For those who perceived themselves as upwardly mobile (e.g., maybe they were educated), they might feel particularly “trapped” because they were still unable to secure a job, as compared to those who didn’t perceive much upward mobility and remained unemployed. Sch individuals might also be more cynical toward those who already possess higher social status, or the rich. We believe this piece of finding is interesting but complicating, and have been conducting additional analyses to examine how this association (between perceived mobility and negativity) may vary across different groups of youth (e.g., those went back to school vs. those remained unemployed vs. those secured a job). We are also comparing our findings here with data that we are gathering in our other projects with the negativity toward the rich measure. To sum up, our findings provide support to two of the three proposed mediation effects under Objective 2. And we are exploring ways to disentangle the surprising association between perceived upward mobility and negativity toward the rich, through more statistical analyses of the current dataset as well as comparisons to additional data in our other projects with the negativity toward the rich variable. Objective 3: It will examine whether employability affects their psychological health, job search behavior, and negative attitudes toward the rich over time. Our Reply: Similar to the results addressing Objective 2, our findings generally provide support for Objective 3. The impact of perceived employability on job search intensity and psychological health was found to be positive over time. Most interestingly, job search intensity in turn was found to significantly predict participants' income earned at Wave 2 (those who remained unemployed would have zero income). In other words, the concept of employability can indeed exert impact on some concrete measure such as employment status (i.e., getting employed or not) and income level, providing further validation of the importance of such a concept in unemployment research. This finding is deemed particularly meaningful because previous research has mainly focused on employment status (dichotomous yes—no measure). However, the above patterns of result did not apply to negativity toward the rich. As discussed in our reply to Objective 2, the association between upward mobility and negativity toward the rich is weak but positive. And we believe the association is much more complicated and awaits further research scrutiny as mentioned above. To conclude, our study has addressed most of our research objectives, and has also raised interesting questions for further investigation. Even though our sample might not be truly representative, the finding that most of our participants remained unemployed during the research period of about a year points to the importance of research on unemployed youth.

440713.label: Major findings and research outcome
440713.value: Our study generated some interesting, but also complicating findings, on unemployed youth. First, we managed to generate empirical support for our model that adaptability, career identity, human capital, and social capital are determinants of their sense of employability. Such findings bear conceptual and applied implications. First, they generally corroborate Fugate et al.’s (2004) proposal that in addition to human capital, psychosocial attributes of adaptability, career identity, and social capital are also critical to the sense of employability. Second, extant literature (McArdle et al., 2007; Gowan, 2012; Koen et al., 2013) has not reached consensus on the operationalization of antecedents of employability. Our findings suggest that empirical research can operationalize them in terms of boundaryless mindset, career self-efficacy, work experience, and social support, respectively. Third, intervention programs targeting local unemployed youth can then focus on these antecedents in their program design and assessment of unemployed individuals. Moroever, our findings confirm the mechanism of how the sense of employability affects employment outcomes such as psychological health and job search behavior over time, through the mediating roles of perceived upward mobility. First, these mediation effects bear interesting implications. Youth unemployment has been linked to social unrest as unemployed youth often report that channels for upward mobility are stifled (The Economist, 2011). However, psychological research has overlooked the construct of perceived upward mobility (Jetten et al., 2008). Our findings reveal that employability signifies perceived upward mobility. Relatedly, perceived mobility mediates the positive employability – job search intensity association, providing an account for the impact of employability. Furthermore, unemployed youth with higher job search intensity tend to obtain higher income jobs in the future. This finding demonstrates the impact of employability on actual, quantifiable outcomes. Based on these major findings, we submitted a paper to Career Development International, the oldest journal in the field of career development research, and received a revise-resubmit decision from the editor (see the first attachment in Part C). In view of the positive comments, we believe that we can address them satisfactorily and publish this first paper of the project. We also presented our findings in various international conferences. As mentioned above, there are some other very interesting findings that are unexpected and worth pursuing, particularly the one on negativity toward the rich among such youth. We are now drafting another paper on this topic (see the second attachment in Part C which outlines the content of this working paper).

440713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
440713.value: We attempted to extend and place youth unemployment research in a social context by examining: (a) the mediating roles of perceived upward mobility, and (b) negativity toward the rich as one important outcome of job search behavior. No prior research has linked youth unemployment, or unemployment research per se, to such societal oriented variables. Whereas we have gathered empirical support for the importance of perceived upward mobility, the findings on negativity toward the rich are far from conclusive. Future research should examine if/how youth unemployment may be linked to negative social attitudes such as negativity toward the rich. Future research should also examine factors that may moderate the main effects reported in our study. Another stimulating finding is the sizable number of unemployed participants (around 30%) choosing to return to school. Longitudinal, career development research should be conducted to examine key factors (e.g., career indecisiveness, resilience personality) affecting such young adults' (aged 18 to 27 in our study) career decision when facing unemployment. Practically, such decisions will have significant implications for the allocation of our educational resources. Again, more research is needed to better-understand their career choice, especially the type of education they prefer (e.g., vocational vs. traditional tertiary education).

440713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
440713.value: Youth unemployment is pervasive worldwide, with important societal implications. Recent youth unemployment rates was 12% in the U.S. (U.S. Department of Labor, 2016) and higher than 10% across Europe (Maguire, 2015). Similar figures (aged between 15-19: 15%; between 20-24: 8%) were observed in Hong Kong (HK Census and Statistics Department, 2016). We thus aimed to examine antecedents and consequences of Hong Kong unemployed youth’s sense of employability. We successfully collected data from 359 unemployed youth across two waves of survey, 9 months apart (out of 533 participants at Wave 1). Our analyses confirm that adaptable personality, career identity, human capital, and social capital are major determinants of employability. Moreover, employability was found to significantly affect employment outcomes such as psychological health and job search behavior (i.e., job search intensity and future job income) 9 months later, through the mediating roles of perceived upward mobility. Conceptually, these findings highlight the importance of examining individuals' psychological states in job search research, i.e., whether individuals perceive they have the abilities/resources to secure a job, and whether individuals perceive they are upwardly mobile and remain hopeful. Practically, intervention programs targeting unemployed youth can focus on enhancing antecedents of employability, given its strong explanatory power.

440913.label: Project Title(Chinese)
440913.value: 以超句法線索分析漢語句子

440913.label: Project Objectives
440913.value: The language-specific properties of Chinese make it a unique arena for sentence parser development. Instead of relying exclusively on words and their syntactic tags, a set of supra-syntactic clues including word order, pre-/post-verbal asymmetry, function words, animacy, semantic proximity and grammatical weight will be annotated to provide further hints for parsing purposes. Most traditional statistical parsers rarely consider the shape of subtrees, which are dominated by nodes in relevant treebanks. As a consequence, a noun phrase (NP) with a complicated structure is treated the same as an NP that dominates only one word. In this research, we will devise several tree shape features. We will use these features to predict phrase boundaries and their syntactic tags and to resolve critical ambiguity issues during the early parsing stages. Inspired by the insights of k-best parsers, we will co-train the supra-syntactic clues in three promising and complementary machine learning algorithms. A parser will be devised that combines predictions from the three algorithms and generates a collective decision. This approach will reduce a possible addiction to any single algorithm that may produce vague or obscure predictions during parsing. Most Chinese parsers are ported from some of the major English parsers, which rely primarily on lexical information such as words and their POSs. However, porting a state-of-the-art English parser to Chinese usually achieves a lower F-score (Petrov et al., 2006; Petrov & Klein, 2007). This performance is even worse in the absence of error-free word segmentation and POS tagging. It is thought that using an English-based linguistic parsing model to parse Chinese sentences is likely to hide the many interesting and unique features of the Chinese language. While there are many linguistic and structural differences between the two languages, we will pursue a novel approach using supra-syntactic clues along with lexical information and explore further possible parsing strategies, especially because the performance of parsers ported for Chinese seems to be plateauing.

440913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
440913.value: 本研究的目的是提高漢語句子剖析質量。語言學家觀察得到，讀者在了解漢語句子時，會結合一些超句法線索，例如，動詞前後的不對稱性，虛詞，有生性，語義貼近度和語法重量等。然而，現今漢語句子剖析系統，主要借鑒英語語言系統所顯示的特質，來作句子分析，而忽略漢語句子的獨特性。在這個項目中，我們將利用已研發的剖析器，在以下各方面進行優化。（一）註釋多種在語法外的句法線索，（二）制定一些樹形狀特徵及證明它們對了解句子結構是有裨益的，及（三）制定一個機器學習原則，綜合從不同線索所得出的剖析判斷，並進行集體裁決。本項目將對這剖析進行一個全面的檢討評估，以確定其統計意義。同時，以兩個在線的漢語剖析器作為對比，並進行深入的評價。

440913.label: Realisation of objectives
440913.value: In this research, we have devised a sentence parser that scans and analyzes Chinese input texts in multiple passes. In each single pass, the parser will build up an interim parse tree, working incrementally in a bottom-up manner. Unlike other parsing techniques, such as shift-reduce parsing and its derivatives, during the interim parse tree construction, every levels from terminal to the root will be subject to two classifications, (i) sentence chunking; (ii) phrase recognition. The sentence chunking is to predict the right chunking point that lies between two adjacent phrases. The second classification is to figure out the appropriate syntactic structure for the chunks, such as noun phrases. The recognition applies the grammar rules and its neighboring context to build up the interim parse tree. A collection of various heterogeneous context features, such as their POS tags, head words, weight in a chunk, animacy and super-sense, their co-occurrence, have been defined and annotated. In addition, a set of attributes that depicts the shapes of subtrees quantitatively has been devised. They include span ratio, aspect ratio, node coordinates and their degree of skewness. As a consequence, these features gauge the complexity of a parse tree node and have the capability to differentiate a complicated node with a simple one. The above feature extraction is the process of translating print into parsing hints by rapidly recognizing its unique linguistic traits. It is analogue of our human brains that can elicit the key language features spontaneously in reading. The role of feature extraction in sentence parsing is irrefutable, however, it does not suffice on its own. In this research, we capture the regularity indicated by the supra-syntactic clues and we believe that regularity can be easily spotted using the latest inductive learning techniques. We have applied decision trees (DT) and support vector machines (SVMs) in both sentence chunking and phrase recognition. The outcome of the sentence chunking is a binomial distribution. Each has its own Boolean value, either a chunking point or not. For phrase recognition, it is a multiclass or multinomial classification problem. For example, at POS level, the chunk is predicted to be an NP, -> NP. We take advantage of the latest version of C4.5 (Quinlan, 1994) with its default pruning ratio. We adopt the boosting with 10 trials. As observed in the dataset, each discrete attribute may have more than 10 possible values, particularly in the multinomial classification. We apply the discrete value subsets option (-s) to eliminate the undesirable side-effect of fragmentation of data during the construction of the decision tree. For the SVM model, we apply the C-support vector classification (C-SVC) with a typical radial basis function (RBF) kernel with default parameters. The classifier is under a standard Library for Support Vector Machines (Chang & Lin, 2011). During training, we set the tolerance of the termination criterion to 0.001. Both the DT and SVM algorithms apply their diverse types of discernment to the tasks of chunking and phrase prediction. However, none of these algorithms can achieve a perfect prediction when applied in isolation. The algorithms may provide two feasible predictions, or sometimes vague or even contradicting predictions. In our study, an ensemble technique is applied in combining the algorithms in a meta-level classifier and building up the parser. First, we divide our context features into three heterogeneous and mutually independent subgroups. Instead of training all three subgroups to form a single gigantic classifier, we produce six different base-level classifiers, both for sentence chunking and phrase recognition, from the two learning algorithms, in the hope that they will produce a highly accurate prediction. At the same time, we apply the meta-decision tree (MDT) that learns to combine predictions from the six different base-level classifiers (Ženko et al., 2001). Basically, the rationale of the MDT is quite similar to that of the other base-level decision trees, such as CART, except that each leaf node of the MDT indicates the base-level classifier that will be adopted for prediction. In other words, the target class feature assigned to the leaf node of the MDT determines which base-level classifier should be triggered. For each level in the parse tree construction, we produce multiple derivations and sprout more than one possible phrase structures up to its higher level. All the possible sprouts are being kept track of in a parse chart. The final optimal parse will be resolved in a top-down mode under the chart parsing technique. On top of the existing template to evaluate the parser using two standard Treebanks as shown in last annual report, we have conducted a further evaluation in resolving a real-world application. Financial text streams are more than just collections of isolated documents, in that they exhibit the traits of collective intentions and actions. These text streams contain prominent hints for investors, as they convey many expressions of sentiment drawn from the public. Such texts are thus helpful in evaluating our parser in sentiment analysis. In this evaluation, we obtained collections of financial news that were posted between September 9, 2014 and March 24, 2015 on a Hong Kong financial website called Finet. This site is one of the most influential newswires and is an authorized newspaper agency in both English and Chinese for the region. Two major collections of texts were included: (i) dailies, which included daily financial news from various newspapers along with all scheduled/unscheduled announcements and (ii) blogs, which contain comments/advices from a group of expert analysts who are eager to provide their insights of the current and future markets in print. The total number of words in the collections is 12 million. As the broad-coverage of the financial Chinese text corpus like this, there are, not surprisingly, a lot of out-of-vocabulary (OOV) words without any POS and sense tags. In this evaluation, our tagging of an OOV in financial texts is based on two major categories of linguistic features, namely morphological and co-occurrence similarity features. The morphological features describe the intrinsic clues in word formation. That is, how words are formed from their smaller constituents. Co-occurrence similarity features are used to uncover the collocations between the word OOV and some key linguistic clues in a corpus. This is based on the hypothesis that words with similar meanings tend to be bundled with linguistic-alike neighbours to form similar listemes (Chan et al., 2015). All sentences in the textbase are parsed using our Chinese parser. Further examination is conducted whether the positive and negative moods expressed in the parsed texts correlate with the closing price of the Hang Seng Index (HSI), a major stock market index in the region. With the aid of a sentiment lexicon, our parser using supra-syntactic clues and complementary machine learning algorithms dissects both the recursive and non-recursive phrasal structures. This parser is capable to identify the subtle polarity shift when aggregating phrasal polarity scores to determine the overall sentence polarity, while it is completely ignored in most learning-based sentiment analysis approaches.

We will use these features to predict phrase boundaries and their syntactic tags and to resolve critical ambiguity issues during the early parsing stages.

Inspired by the insights of k-best parsers, we will co-train the supra-syntactic clues in three promising and complementary machine learning algorithms. A parser will be devised that combines predictions from the three algorithms and generates a collective decision. This approach will reduce a possible addiction to any single algorithm that may produce vague or obscure predictions during parsing.

Most Chinese parsers are ported from some of the major English parsers, which rely primarily on lexical information such as words and their POSs. However, porting a state-of-the-art English parser to Chinese usually achieves a lower F-score (Petrov et al., 2006; Petrov & Klein, 2007). This performance is even worse in the absence of error-free word segmentation and POS tagging. It is thought that using an English-based linguistic parsing model to parse Chinese sentences is likely to hide the many interesting and unique features of the Chinese language. While there are many linguistic and structural differences between the two languages, we will pursue a novel approach using supra-syntactic clues along with lexical information and explore further possible parsing strategies, especially because the performance of parsers ported for Chinese seems to be plateauing.

440913.label: Major findings and research outcome
440913.value: A Chinese parser that is based on the collection of heterogeneous features has been trained and tested using the English and Chinese Penn Treebanks (Marcus et al., 1993). Buoyed by the chart parsing technique for resolving the optimal parse tree, as mentioned in above section, the overall parsing performance of our English and Chinese parsers have achieved an F-score of 87.96% and 85.61% respectively. Although the F-score for state-of-the-art English parsers lies between 87 and 89%, it is noteworthy that the performance of our Chinese parser is rather encouraging. For instance, Bikel (2004) obtains an F-score of 81.2% in parsing Chinese sentences. The detailed result can be found in Chan & Chong (2017). To study the usability of our Chinese parser in a real-world application, we have applied the parser in financial texts analytics. As in any other real-life linguistic applications, one of the most important obstacles is to identify the large amount of Chinese out-of-vocabulary (OOV). In the research, we provide an approach to unlocking POS tags of the OOV. The tagging in financial texts is based on two major categories of linguistic features, namely morphological and co-occurrence similarity features. Interested readers can refer to the literature for a detailed technical discussion (Chan et al., 2015). In the financial text analytics, we hypothesize daily positive and negative mood indices, which are rendered by the parser, can provide some clues on the changes of the stock market index. To test this hypothesis, we apply a well-known econometric technique, the Granger causality analysis (GCA), to the two time series against the HSI. Granger, a Nobel Laureate in Economic Sciences, argues that causality in economics can be tested by measuring the ability to predict the future values of a time series by using the prior values of another time series. We have demonstrated the mood indices generated by the parser, with the aid of a sentiment lexicon, do have Granger-cause any effect on stock index. These results provide grounds for belief that the sentiments detected from the finance-related texts by the parser are not random. They are helpful for analyzing the trends in financial markets (Chan & Chong, 2017; Chan, in press).

440913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
440913.value: Chinese texts have become more readily available due to the proliferation of postings to the Internet and the ever-increasing demand for transparency in business, humanities, social or political contexts. All these texts have always been an important resource to demonstrate the wisdom of crowds. However, given the complexity of Chinese language as well as the profundity of its linguistic structures, it is usually a great challenge to capture the syntactic structures, or the underlying sentiment in the texts in this era of big data. There is at least one possible remedy, which may overcome some shortcomings of traditional methods of sentence parsing. After the revival of neural networks (NN), the concept of deep learning is pervasive, in large part, due to the technological advancement of the graphics processing unit (GPU) or Google AlphaGo. For instance, the recurrent neural networks (RNNs) employ a large number of hidden layers to extract features automatically from ordered sequences of words. The information stored non-symbolically in the weights of the RNNs captures the time-varying real-valued activation and the highly non-linear relationships. Even though the concept of deep learning reignites the controversy between classicists and connectionists, the deep learning using RNNs to memorize the recursive and hierarchical grammatical structures may be a good challenge for sentence parsing.

440913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
440913.value: There are at least two main factors that distinguish our work from others. First, we have provided a novel approach to developing a language parser. This parser integrates various heterogeneous context features in refining the detection of chunking points and recognizing phrases by using an ensemble machine learning technique. A parse tree resolution algorithm is proposed to resolve the possible ambiguous or incomplete structures when multiple derivations are propagated from the terminal level. The parser is language-independent and can be easily adapted to different languages, such as in English and Chinese. Second, to demonstrate that the parser is applicable to real word applications, a sentiment assessment heuristic is applied to assign the polarity of a text based on the phrase structures rendered from its parse tree. Several evaluations using movie review dataset and financial text streams are examined. Our statistical tests using twelve million words of financial texts attest to the significance of the parser. Our approach provides a means of identifying sentiments amid the complex and unstructured qualitative data derived from various text genres such as breaking news, news groups, blogs and tweets. The parser can help investors to deal with data in a way that eases their cognitive limitations.

441113.label: Project Objectives
441113.value: In the past few months, we have developed a more general framework for an integrated meMO and moME analysis. We call this approach VS (Variable System). Consequently, we need to examine the performance of this approach with measured variables first. Then, we will extend the method to the case of latent variables.

Consequently, we need to examine the performance of this approach with measured variables first. Then, we will extend the method to the case of latent variables.

441113.label: Realisation of objectives
441113.value: In social science research, moderated mediation and mediated moderation have become increasingly popular for studying the relationship between different variables. Generally speaking, moderated mediation (moME) occurs when a mediation process, X-->M-->Y, varies at different levels of one or more moderators W. Mediated moderation (meMO), on the other hand, occurs when the moderation effect of the moderator (W) on the relationship between the independent variable (X) and the dependent variable (Y) is transmitted through one or more mediators M. In theory development, both moME and meMO can offer researchers a more sophisticated representation of their research hypothesis. Empirically, however, researchers often have difficulty analyzing these models. This is because moME and meMO were shown to have the same underlying statistical model. Under the traditional interpretations, moME and meMO are simply “two sides of the same coin”, and therefore it is very difficult for one to differentiate the two processes from a statistical point of view. Furthermore, as the underlying statistical models of moME and meMO are complex and the correct specification of these models usually requires advanced statistical skills, testing moME and meMO effects is often a demanding task for applied researchers. In this project, the objective was to develop a general framework for an integrated meMO and moME analysis. In particular, we have achieved the following three goals: (1) We proposed an alternative specification for meMO that allows us to differentiate the two processes, on both conceptual and statistical level. Conceptually, this alternative specification of meMO provides an intuitively meaningful representation of the process that is different from its moME counterpart. Statistically, it offers meMO a unique statistical representation that is no longer identical to moME. Consequently, this alternative specification of meMO helped us resolve the long existing issue on “how to differentiate moME and meMO?”. (2) Based on the ideas derived from the alternative specification for meMO, we further extended the method to a general case that includes moME, meMO, and other conditional path models. We called this integrated method the Variable System (VS) approach. In our definition, a variable system depicts the relationships between the variables. The central idea of the VS approach is to transform a conceptual model of theoretical interest into a statistical system of variables, which is typically a path analytic model that can be fitted to the observed data and tested by structural equation modelling (SEM). In other words, the VS approach essentially consists of two major steps. Step 1: Model Transformation. A conceptual model of theoretical interest is transformed into a statistical working model (i.e., the path model) according to a set of model transformation rules. Although these rules were originally developed for the meMO analysis, they are general enough to cover a wide range of different models one would normally have in social science research. This includes, for example, a moderated mediation model with multiple mediators aligned in serial or parallel, or a second-order moderated mediation model in which the moderator itself is further moderated by another variable. Step 2: Model Fitting. The statistical model generated in Step 1 is analysed by SEM for parameter estimation and model goodness-of-fit evaluation. Traditional methods for model fitting are usually regression-based and the model parameters are estimated by separate regression models using least squares. In contrast, the VS approach is SEM-based and the model parameters are estimated simultaneously using maximum likelihood or generalised least squares. Another distinctive feature about the VS approach is that the SEM analysis is able to provide the overall model goodness-of-fit statistics, which are important and useful information for model evaluation and comparison. Using real examples, we demonstrated that two competitive conceptual models (one is meMO and another is moME) would give rise to two different statistical working models with different estimated parameter values as well as goodness-of-fit statistics under the VS approach. In contrast, the traditional methods provided identical results for these two models, confirming their inability to differentiate the two processes properly. Hence, the VS approach can help eliminate the need of choosing one process over the other arbitrarily. Rather, researchers can evaluate and compare different model hypotheses empirically by the model goodness-of-fit statistics and the tests of the meMO and moME effects. (3) To many researchers, model transformation (first step) is challenging because it demands advanced statistical skills and careful manipulation of the variables such as the creation of an interaction term between the antecedent variable and the moderator, or the specification of the relationships between the interaction term and its source variables. More importantly, as the complexity of the conceptual model increases, this transformation step would become increasingly tedious and difficult. To make VS approach more accessible to applied researchers, we developed a computer software program, VS for Windows, to implement the proposed procedure. This program runs on Windows with the R system for statistical computing, which implements the lavaan package. Users only need to specify the conceptual model in the VS program and the program will automatically transform the model and run the SEM analysis accordingly. Specifically, this VS software program (1) transforms the conceptual model into SEM working model; (2) generates a VS dataset that includes all the key variables and their interaction terms as needed in subsequent SEM analysis; (3) creates additional parameters and model constraints for testing the conditional direct and indirect effects of theoretical interest; (4) runs the SEM analysis of the specified model; and (5) prepares an output file with all major results summarized in a readable format. The software is available for free download at https://www.psy.cuhk.edu.hk/research/lab/quantlab/vs. What's next? We are now extending the VS approach to models with latent variables (see section 6.2, point 1 for details). Ideally, our plan is to make the basic VS approach for measured variables accessible to the field first, before we promote the method for latent variables. We admitted that the original title of the project was somehow misleading, given the revised objectives that were approved in 2013 (see section 5.2). If possible, we should have changed the project title to make it more consistent with what had been done in this project.

441113.label: Major findings and research outcome
441113.value: (1) An integrated approach for the analysis of mediated moderation (meMO), moderated mediation (moME), and other general conditional path models was proposed. This approach, known as Variable System (VS), involves two basic steps. First, a conceptual model of theoretical interest is transformed into a statistical working model according to a set of model transformation rules. Second, the statistical model is analysed by structural equation modelling for parameter estimation and model goodness-of-fit evaluation. In the literature, traditional methods typically described meMO and moME as two processes that share the same underlying statistical model, of which meMO is either interpreted as "meaningless" or "a special case of moME". Unlike the traditional methods, the VS approach provided an alternative formulation for meMO, and made the two processes conceptually and mathematically differentiable from each other. A manuscript titled “VS: An alternative approach for the analysis of mediated moderation” has been conditionally accepted for publication in Psychological Methods, subject to minor language editing. (2) A self-developed computer software program, VS for Windows, has been developed to implement the aforementioned VS approach (Chan, Kwan, & Choi, 2017). This program runs on Windows with the R system for statistical computing (R Development Core Team, 2015) that implements the lavaan package (Rosseel, 2012). To facilitate users' application, we also prepared a user manual for the program. The package is currently available for free download at https://www.psy.cuhk.edu.hk/research/lab/quantlab/vs. (3) An index of weak invariance of mediation (Iw) was invented to examine the validity of the moderated mediation effect. Given a mediation process X-->M-->Y, a two-stage moME occurs when the paths X->M and M->Y are simultaneously moderated by W and S, respectively. In the literature, an index of moderated mediation was recommended to quantify the strength or magnitude of this moME effect. However, we showed that a spurious moME effect may sometimes be concluded under certain atypical model conditions (AMC). The index of weak invariance of mediation can help us rule out the possibility of concluding a spurious moderated mediation effect through the examination of AMC numerically. A manuscript titled "Integrating moderation models into a moderated mediation model: An index of weak invariance of mediation to detect spurious moderated mediation effects" was prepared and it will be ready for submission in June 2017 after final editing.

441113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
441113.value: (1) We are now extending the VS approach to models with latent variables (factors). Specifically, a three-step procedure will be adopted. In Step 1, given a conditional process model with latent variables, we will compute the factor scores for the latent variables based on confirmatory factor analysis. In Step 2, the latent variables that appear in the original conditional process model will be replaced by their corresponding factor scores, leading to a modified model with observed variables only. This modified model will then be transformed into a statistical working (path) model according to the transformation rules described in the VS approach. In Step 3, structural equation modelling will be applied for analyzing the statistical working model concerned. Simulation studies will be conducted to examine the empirical performance of this three-step procedure. (2) Concerning the VS program, we will continue to add new features to the system. These include, for example, flexible data input format such as SPSS system file, multiple group analysis, and parameter constraint option. (3) We will explore the relationship between the VS meMO model and the two-level regression model proposed by Yuan, Cheng, and Maxwell (2014). Initial analysis suggested that these two models are largely identical and the two-level model can be considered as a special case of VS meMO.

441113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
441113.value: Moderation and mediation analysis is an useful analytical technique in psychological research. Generally speaking, moderation occurs when the relationship between the independent variable (X) and dependent variable (Y) varies as a function of the moderator variable. Mediation, on the other hand, occurs when the effect of X on Y is transmitted through an intervening variable. However, the relationship between the variables is sometimes more complicated and a simple moderation and mediation model may fail to describe the underlying psychological process adequately. Consequently, psychologists are motivated to consider a more general theoretical framework that combines moderation and mediation, which is commonly regarded as moderated mediation (moME) or mediated moderation (meMO). Although there exists different methods in the literature for the analysis of moME and meMO, these methods have problems in differentiating the two processes, either conceptually or mathematically. In this project, an integrated approach, known as Variable System (VS), was proposed for the analysis of meMO and moME. Unlike the traditional methods, the VS approach offered an unique solution to the problem by allowing one to differentiate meMO and moME, both conceptually and mathematically. To facilitate applied researchers to implement the proposed procedure, a free software program, VS for Windows, was developed.

441313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
441313.value: Guangdong province in South China is dominated by a sub-tropical monsoon climate which is characterized by significant seasonal and interannual variations. Fluctuations of precipitation driven by the intrinsic nature and variability of Asian Monsoon may cause meteorological droughts of varying severity, extent, and duration mainly in the winter and spring seasons in Guangdong, which has been repeatedly the case over the past decade. Droughts have caused a variety of problems and threats which can seriously hamper the rapid socio-economic development, such as water shortage, salinity intrusion, water quality deterioration, and etc. However, hydrological research has focused more on the flood and water logging issues in the water rich region like Guangdong over the years and less attention has been paid to investigate the water shortage problems which can be caused by both natural and human factors. The proposed study aims to characterize the spatio-temporal patterns of droughts which will be represented by an integrated drought assessment system, to find out and understand the climatic driving forces behind, and to analyze how the society should respond to the drought hazards. We will employ both traditional hydrological analysis techniques using statistical methods as well as innovative approach to integrating the temporal and spatial domains of drought hazards using GIS tools. Efforts will be made to compare the hydrology and climatology of drought hazards in Guangdong with other regions of the world that share similar climatic characteristics. This integrated study of meteorological and hydrological droughts will enable us to not only advance the state-of-the-art of drought research in a warm and humid monsoon climate region, but also produce many results and findings of great importance for sustainable management of water resources in the Guangdong province. 廣東省位於中國華南地區，主要受亞熱帶季風氣候控制，具有明顯的季節和年際變化特徵。自然界的降水波動和亞洲季風的變化會造成不同程度、不同面積和不同持續強度的氣象乾旱，尤其是在春季和冬季，這在過去的幾十年裡時有發生。乾旱造成的威脅已經嚴重影響了社會經濟的快速發展，帶來了各種各樣的問題，比如水資源短缺、鹽潮入侵、水質惡化等等。近年來，大多數的針對水資源充裕地區的水文研究都側重于洪水和水浸問題，只有少數的研究是關於由自然和人類共同導致的水資源短缺問題。本課題主要致力於研究乾旱的時空分佈特徵，通過構建綜合的乾旱評價體系，找出造成乾旱的氣候引子，並分析應對乾旱災害的策略。採用基於統計方法的傳統水文分析技術和地理資訊系統等新方法對乾旱的時空特徵進行分析，並將廣東省的水文和氣候乾旱與其他類似氣候地區進行比較。這種對氣象水文乾旱的綜合研究，不僅有助於提升濕熱季風氣候地區乾旱的研究水準，同時對於廣東省水資源的可持續管理也具有積極作用。

441313.label: Realisation of objectives
441313.value: The overall objective of this project is to characterize the spatio-temporal patterns of droughts which will be represented by an integrated drought system, to find out and understand the climatic driving forces behind, and to analyze how the society should respond to the drought hazards. Through hydrological and meteorological analyses, as well as socio-economic assessment of drought risk and vulnerability in Guangdong Province, we have successfully produced many findings to address four key research questions: (1) what are the characteristics of spatio-temporal distribution and severity-frequency of meteorological droughts in Guangdong? (2) what climatic drivers and factors have caused the reduction in rainfall in recent decades and how? (3) how do the reduced rainfall and possibly increased evaporation influence the basin water budget and low-flow regimes? and (4) How human and institutional responses to droughts affect the effectiveness of mitigation measures and policies? First, the study has focused on characterizing the changing properties of droughts in both time and space in Guangdong province. Univariate and bivariate frequency analysis of drought duration and severity using Copulas were conducted to investigate the spatial distribution of droughts based on the joint probability distribution in Guangdong province. The quartiles descriptive statistical approach and spatial interpolation were used to map the spatial frequency distribution for the marginal distribution and joint occurrence probability of drought duration and severity. Clusters analysis was employed to characterize the regions with the same exceedance probability and their spatial variations. We also used standardized precipitation-evapotranspiration index at a 3-month time scale to characterize droughts and applied Copula functions to derive transition probability matrix of the Markov chain to classify six drought statuses. Secondly, we analyzed the response of moisture circulation to the daily evolution of India-Burma Trough (IBT) and the modulation of disturbances along the South Asian waveguide to seek a potential precursor of winter precipitation over South China, using daily observational precipitation and reanalysis data from ERA-Interim during 1979–2012. We employed the Hybrid Single-Particle Lagrangian Integrated Trajectory (HYSPLIT) model to trace the trajectories of air parcels released over Southeast China during 01Apr 2012–31 Mar 2013 and three typical regional long-lasting heavy rainfalls. The model’s ability in detecting the transport routines and sources of moisture supplied to Southeast China was evaluated. We also applied a combination of Ward’s and k-means clustering to a 3-month Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI-03) during 1961–2012 to identify 8 divisions of homogeneous drought variation throughout China. A greater meridional gradient appeared over East China (6 divisions) than over West China (2 divisions). Dissimilarities in the temperature range, precipitation amount, and length of the dry/wet season among the 8 regions supported our division scheme. Thirdly, we developed an Integrated Water Resources Vulnerability Index (IWRVI) based on the typical regional water resources vulnerability indicators, including water resources demand and supply indicators, land use indicators, population and GDP indicators and so on in terms of Water Withdrawals to Availability (WTA), Exposure and Sensitivity. Based on IWRVI, the spatio-temporal patterns of water resources vulnerability show that PRD regions, such as Guangzhou, Foshan, Dongguan, Shenzhen, and Zhongshan are the most vulnerable areas to drought hazards, the southeast regions such as Shantou and Chaozhou second, southwest slightly vulnerable, while the mountainous regions in broadly north part of Guangdong the least vulnerable. Further temporal pattern analysis has revealed that the conditions of most vulnerable regions are getting worse and that the coverage of most vulnerable area is expanding. Fourthly, we assessed the water resources risk in 2020 based on joint occurrence probabilities and water resources vulnerability in terms of two exceedance probabilities types and nine combinations of drought duration and severity. Spatial drought risk patterns at gridded scale show that the Pearl River Delta region, especially in Guangzhou and Foshan, will be at the highest level of risks, Shenzhen and Dongguan second. Leizhou Peninsula should pay attention to the risk caused by extreme physical droughts. Besides, Shaoguan regions in Northern part of Guangdong with low water resources vulnerability present a relative high risk compared to other neighboring northern areas due to the high physical occurrence of droughts. The combination of the drought hazards physical characteristics with the water resources vulnerability index system makes the drought risk assessment system a useful and important tool for sustainable management and adaptation of water resource resilient to the changing climate and socioeconomic development in Guangdong province. To extend our investigation of droughts in Guangdong to cover the Pearl River Basin and the whole China, we adopted a multivariate approach to analyzing regional frequency of droughts in China. The regionalization of droughts was carried out using Fuzzy C- Means (FCM) clustering technique and also multivariate L-moment method. Besides, copula was used to estimate regional joint probability in terms of drought duration and severity. Evaluation of uncertainty in the joint probability curves was conducted using the Bootstrap resampling technique. We evaluated the future changes in floods and water availability which may cause droughts across China under representative concentration pathway 2.6 (RCP2.6) and RCP8.5 by analyzing discharge simulations from the Inter-Sectoral Impact Model Intercomparison Project (ISI-MIP) with the consideration of uncertainties among global climate models (GCMs) and hydrologic models. Our study of the response of long-term water availability to more extreme climate in the Pearl River Basin shows that increase in inter-daily variability of precipitation and temperature not only triggers more intensive hydrologic extremes, but also causes considerable impacts on long-term water availability. Sixteen climate scenarios were designed to separate overall changes of precipitation and temperature into two aspects: (1) change in monthly mean and (2) change in inter-daily variability. Runoff of the Pearl River Basin was simulated by the variable infiltration capacity (VIC) model under these scenarios.
