441313.label: Major findings and research outcome
441313.value: The project has generated many research findings with important scientific merits and practical significance as reported in the publications given in Part C. These outputs contribute to enhance our understanding of the spatio-temporal patterns and climatic drivers of and societal responses to droughts in a water-rick region like Guangdong Province and the Pearl River Basin, which has been a less studied topic compared to flood research. Chen et al. (2016) shows that higher probability of occurrence of seasonal droughts after the occurrence of more severe seasonal droughts, and extreme drought in winter tended to persist with higher probability till spring, whereas extreme drought in autumn might not probably last to winter. Furthermore, our study also indicated high probability of occurrence of droughts in southeast parts of the Pearl River basin during spring to winter. Thus, droughts in the Pearl River basin are subject to lengthening duration, particularly in the southeastern part of the basin. Chen et al. (2017) indicates that: (1) the exceptional drought lasts about 1.5 months and the abnormally dry lasts about 3 months; (2) it takes about 3.5 months for the exceptional drought status to be recovered to no drought while about 1.7 months for the abnormally dry status to be recovered to no drought; and (3) generally, there is a moderate drought in 0.5 year, a severe drought in 1 years, an extreme drought in 1.5 years, and an exceptional drought in 3.5 years. Further, the results of our study indicated higher risk of drought in the southeast part of the Pearl River basin and these regions are densely populated and economically developed, especially in the Pearl River delta. In addition, the west part of the Pearl River basin has also been identified as a region with a higher risk of drought. Li et al. (2017) exhibits that moisture circulation in response to the India–Burma Trough (IBT) is part of the zonally oriented wave trains along the South Asian waveguide, but it persists longer and migrates farther eastward than other lobes. Cyclonic moisture transport enhances the moisture supply to south China as a strong IBT develops, and shifts eastward abruptly after the peak of IBT with enhanced precipitation shifting from southwest to southeast China. This response is a joint effect of synoptic, intraseasonal, and interannual components that show similar wave train structures, whereas slight differences still occur.

441313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
441313.value: China faces many water challenges, not only in the arid and semi-arid regions in north and northwest, but also in the water rich regions in the south. Given the rapid increase in water demand, massive human activities and particularly the changing climate, hydrological and climatological studies to support water resources management are becoming more and more important. This is the fifth RGC project on the regional hydrological analysis and modeling in the Pearl River Basin/Delta and Guangdong Province in South China over the past 18 years. Through these and other projects, we have built up an extensive hydrological and meteorological database of the Pearl River Basin and the whole China. Based on our experiences and data availability, we consider excellent potentials in further developing our research in the following two directions: (1) to strengthen our studies of climate change impacts on hydrological cycle and water hazards, especially the increasing frequency and intensity of extreme events, and (2) to expand the study area from the Pearl River Basin to the whole China, especially the arid regions in western China. Our research findings will continue to provide important scientific support for enhancing water security and sustainability at both regional and national levels.

441313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
441313.value: Drought is a major natural hazard with chronic damages affecting society, economy, and environment of large areas, even those not located in the arid and semi-arid regions. Guangdong province is generally dominated by a humid and subtropical monsoon climate. The plenty of annual rainfall usually does not cause any water shortage in terms of annual total water availability. However, seasonal and interannual variations of monsoon climate do cause substantial and sustained reduction of rainfall in the dry seasons (from October to next March, usually only less than 20% of the annual rainfall) and dry years (up to half and even two-thirds of drop in annual rainfall). Over the years dry climate in some years has caused enormous socio-economic and environmental impacts in Guangdong and Hong Kong, such as severe threat to water supply, salinity intrusion, water quality deterioration, and navigation. Therefore, we have conducted a comprehensive study of drought hazards in Guangdong province, which carries important practical significance given the increasing evidences of hydrological alterations and uncertainties caused by climate change and human perturbation. This study has characterized the spatio-temporal patterns of droughts as represented by an integrated drought system, examined the climatic driving forces behind, and analyzed how the society should respond to drought hazards in different parts of Guangdong.

442113.label: Project Objectives
442113.value: 將計劃主持人親自到各地圖書館抄錄及複印的材料整理，編成《王念孫、王引之稿本、抄本、校本資料彙編》。 整合中、臺兩地圖書館所藏王念孫論韻的稿本、抄本，析述當中所示先秦兩漢典籍韻腳以及同部之字的材料，重組王氏古韻分合理論構建的次弟。再與近人古韻分部比較，以觀王氏古韻分部的得失。 比勘《方言疏證補》、《廣雅疏證．釋草》的稿本、抄本與刻本的內容，考訂其文字異同，還原其撰述的最初形式。 梳理六種經王氏父子校訂過的古籍所見文字校勘、詞義訓解的材料，從校勘、訓詁角度考論王氏父子校治個別古籍的實績及局限，並藉新的材料總結二人研究古籍的成就，用以校訂今人對相關古籍部分詞句的誤解。 上載研究成果至本計劃的網頁(http://www.wangniansun.net)，提供交流的平台，促進王氏之學的研究。

442113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
442113.value: 王念孫、王引之是清代傑出的訓詁學家、校勘學家，他們對古漢語形音義以及對先秦、秦漢古籍的研究成果，至今仍普遍為學者肯定與採用。然而由於材料所限，學者對王氏父子的研究，多局限在《廣雅疏證》、《讀書雜志》、《經義述聞》、《經傳釋詞》等已經刊刻的著作。為了解決目前有關王氏之學的研究在材料上的局限，我們在2010年開展了「新見王念孫古籍校本研究計劃」，整埋並研究了八種經王念孫親手批校的古籍，成果甚豐。本計劃在此基礎上，進一步將範圍擴大，擬將現藏中、臺圖書館善本書庫的王念孫、王引之學術著作之稿本、抄本八種，以及新近發現的經王氏父子親手批校的古籍校本六種整理研究。 這十四種新材料的內容涉及王氏父子在音韻學、訓詁學、古籍校勘與訓釋等方面的研究成果，大部分從未對外公布，是極為重要且數量可觀的珍貴材料，有待開發研究。本計劃期以三年時間，分階段將十四種材料輯錄整理，編成《王念孫、王引之稿本、抄本、校本資料彙編》，並與王氏父子已經刊刻的著作比較研究。本計劃將藉新材料，理解王念孫古韻分部及合韻理論的形成過程、王引之撰述《廣雅疏證》卷十之實況以及王氏父子對《周禮》、《焦氏易林》、《說文解字通釋》、《孫子注》、《楚辭》、《北堂書鈔》等古籍的校治工作，並嘗試探論王氏父子治學之異同乃至二人學術著作權等學術史問題，相關研究成果亦會按時上載至計劃之網頁，冀能繼續開拓研究王氏之學的新里程。 Despite their preeminence as semanticists and textual critics whose scholarship is still relevant to this day, the Qing scholar Wang Niansun and his son Wang Yinzhi have been little studied outside the contexts of their hitherto published works, namely Guangya shuzheng (《廣雅疏證》), Dushu zazhi (《讀書雜志》), Jingyi shuwen (《經義述聞》) and Jingzhuan shici (《經傳釋詞》). This is largely due to the lack of research materials. The problem has been partly addressed with the study of Wang Niansun’s critical editions of eight ancient titles under the “Research Project on the Newly-discovered Ancient Texts Collated by Wang Niansun” that commenced in 2010. To further expand this corpus of raw materials, this two-year project is proposed to collate and study another fourteen works by the two scholars, eight of which are currently in the form of manuscripts or copies housed in libraries in Mainland China and Taiwan and the other six are newly discovered critical editions of ancient titles. Mostly unpublished previously, these fourteen titles will be compiled into Wang Niansun Wang Yinzhi gaoben chaoben jiaoben ziliao huibian (《王念孫、王引之稿本、抄本、校本資料彙編》A Compendium of Manuscripts, Copies and Critical Editions by Wang Niansun and Wang Yinzhi) to provide otherwise unavailable materials for further research on the two Wangs’ contribution to phonology, semantics, textual criticism and annotation. Other research efforts will include a comparative study of the two scholars’ published works, reconstruction of Wang Niansun’s re-categorization of ancient sounds and rhymes, reconstruction of Wang Yinzhi’s production of juan 10 to Guangya shuzheng (《廣雅疏證》), and the pair’s textual criticism of Zhou li (《周禮》), Jiaoshi yilin (《焦氏易林》), Shuowen jiezi tongshi (《說文解字通釋》), Sunzi zhu(《孫子注》) , Chuci (《楚辭》) and Beitang shuchao(《北堂書鈔》). Attempts will also be made to compare and contrast the two scholars’ scholarly pursuits and to tackle the issue of authorship between them in the context of academic history. To facilitate further studies on the two Wangs, these outputs will be progressively uploaded to the project’s website for easy access.

442113.label: Realisation of objectives
442113.value: 本計劃的主要目標，是分階段將十四種材料輯錄整理，編成《王念孫、王引之稿本、抄本、校本資料彙編》，並與王氏父子已經刊刻的著作比較研究，藉新材料，理解王念孫古音分部及合韻理論的形成過程、王引之撰述《廣雅疏證》卷十之實況以及王氏父子對《周禮》、《焦氏易林》、《說文解字通釋》、《孫子注》、《楚辭》、《北堂書鈔》等古籍的校治工作，並嘗試探論王氏父子治學之異同乃至二人學術著作權等學術史問題，相關研究成果亦會按時上載至計劃之網頁，冀能繼續開拓研究王氏之學的新里程。申請本計劃之前，計劃主持人從2010年開始分階段到兩地圖書館，親自翻閱了大部分材料，同時已經收集了四種材料，分別是：北京國家圖書館收藏的王念孫《方言疏證補》王國維抄本、《王石臞先生文稿》稿本及臺灣中央研究院傅斯年圖書館收藏的王引之《廣雅疏證．釋草》稿本、《王氏父子音韻手稿》抄本。在為期三年的計劃期間，計劃主持人先後到北京、南京、武漢、臺北等地圖書館，借鈔其他的稿本、抄本、校本，將原書、原件所見王氏父子親手用墨筆、朱筆所寫的批校札記如實過錄，同時將抄錄所得的資料輸入電腦，編製成《王念孫、王引之稿本、抄本、校本資料彙編》(以下簡稱《彙編》)。完成《彙編》的編輯工作後，我們隨即對個別稿本、校本、抄本進行了逐條疏證、考釋的研究，考證這些新材料所見古音理論、文字校勘、詞義訓解、章句分合等材料，比對《廣雅疏證》、 《讀書雜志》、《經義述聞》、《經傳釋詞》等已經刊行的著作，同時參考前人對相關古籍的研究成果，藉此梳理王氏父子的案語、校改、校記，分析王氏父子研究相關課題的得失，最後將研究成果以學術會議論文及專書的形式公布。同時，我們重視學術成果的交流與分享，把新材料盡快公布，正是本計劃的研究目標。因此，我們分階段把已經發表的學術論文等研究成果 上載至本計劃的網頁。

梳理六種經王氏父子校訂過的古籍所見文字校勘、詞義訓解的材料，從校勘、訓詁角度考論王氏父子校治個別古籍的實績及局限，並藉新的材料總結二人研究古籍的成就，用以校訂今人對相關古籍部分詞句的誤解。
上載研究成果至本計劃的網頁(http://www.wangniansun.net)，提供交流的平台，促進王氏之學的研究。

442113.label: Major findings and research outcome
442113.value: 在三年的研究時間裏，計劃主持人完成所有抄錄稿本、校本、抄本的工作，並將資料輸入電腦，編製成《王念孫、王引之稿本、抄本、校本資料彙編》(以下簡稱《彙編》)。我們將數量較多，學術價值較大的材料，分別撰寫成四篇學術會議論文，分別在中國上海、中國天津、南韓首爾、日本神戶舉行的國際學術會議上宣讀。這些研究成果主要有： 第一、 本計劃收集的王念孫論韻材料甚豐，其中以《韻譜》、《合韻譜》份量最多，也最為重要。我們整合了王念孫論韻材料，利用「《經義述聞》、《讀書雜志》研究計劃」所得的《〈經義述聞〉、〈讀書雜志〉古音資料彙編》，同時借用近人研究古韻的成果，衡量王氏研究古韻的得失，成果見Part C/9/2。 第二、 本計劃收集的王氏父子稿本、抄本材料，部分雖然已經刊刻成書，但內容頗有出入，可資考訂文字的異同。如《方言疏證補》，本計劃收集的王國維抄本與通行的《遺書》排印本，文字詳略頗有不同，我們仔細比對研究後，得出抄本更接近原著的結論，成果見Part C/9/1。 第三、 我們將本計劃編纂的《彙編》與本計劃策劃人主持的「《經義述聞 》、《讀書雜志》研究計劃」編纂的《〈經義述聞〉、〈讀書雜志〉訓詁資料彙編》相互比較，並從方法學角度，論證了王氏父子校讀古籍的科學性，成果見Part C/9/4。 第四、 我們利用校本的材料深入探討部分與王氏相關的學術問題，如有關「高郵王氏四種 」著作權的問題，我們根據本計劃收集的王氏父子的稿本、校本、抄本等新材料，再論《經義述聞》、《讀書雜志》的著作權問題，成果見Part C/9/3。 第五、 我們將研究成果分階段上載本計劃網頁。 第六、 本計劃的階段性成果，將以《王念孫、王引之稿抄校本古籍研究》為題，由上海古籍出版社在2018年出版。

442113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
442113.value: 本計劃主持人在長達十年的研究實踐中，一方面累積了大量的研究材料，一方面對王氏父子校治先秦秦漢古籍的方法有較深入而全面的掌握。近三十年由於考古發現而出土大量先秦秦漢文獻，當中涉及字形辨識、詞義訓釋的問題、疑難可謂觸目皆是，如果我們可以借助本計劃所得的研究成果，即利用王氏父子校釋古書的實績，當有助解決今人在研究出土文獻時遇到的語言文字的問題。準此，本計劃主持人將以「王念孫、王引之校治古籍成果與出土先秦秦漢文獻互證研究」為題申請2018/19年度的GRF計劃。

442113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
442113.value: 王念孫、王引之是清代傑出的訓詁學家、校勘學家，他們對古漢語形音義以及對先秦、秦漢古籍的研究成果，至今仍普遍為學者肯定與採用。然而由於材料所限，學者對王氏父子的研究，多局限在幾部已經刊刻的著作。本計劃將現藏中、臺圖書館善本書庫的王念孫、王引之學術著作之稿本、抄本八種，以及新近發現的經王氏父子親手批校的古籍校本六種整理研究。這十四種新材料的內容涉及王氏父子在音韻學、訓詁學、古籍校勘與訓釋等方面的研究成果，大部分從未對外公布，是極為重要且數量可觀的珍貴材料。我們可以藉這些新材料，理解王念孫古音分部及合韻理論的形成過程、王引之撰述《廣雅疏證》卷十之實況以及王氏父子對《周禮》、《焦氏易林》、《說文解字通釋》、《孫子注》、《楚辭》、《北堂書鈔》等古籍的校治工作，並嘗試探論王氏父子治學之異同乃至二人學術著作權等學術史問題，相關研究成果亦會按時上載至計劃之網頁，冀能繼續開拓研究王氏之學的新里程。

442213.label: Project Title(Chinese)
442213.value: 影響學生對學校科學的興趣之因素：一項混合方法研究

442213.label: Project Objectives
442213.value: To identify the ‘catch’ and ‘hold’ instructional strategies that can induce Hong Kong students’ situational interest in school science. To construct measurement scales to measure students’ individual interest and situational interest experiences in school science. To develop and validate a theoretical model for analyzing the key factors affecting student interest in school science.
rows: To identify the ‘catch’ and ‘hold’ instructional strategies that can induce Hong Kong students’ situational interest in school science.
To construct measurement scales to measure students’ individual interest and situational interest experiences in school science.
To develop and validate a theoretical model for analyzing the key factors affecting student interest in school science.

442213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
442213.value: Student interest is an important variable in science education. However, research has repeatedly confirmed that students become less interested in science classes when they move from junior to senior grades. This proposed study seeks to fill this gap in science education literature by pinpointing why this happens, thus paving the way for pedagogical intervention strategies. Despite agreement among policy-makers, school teachers, parents, and educational researchers about the importance of students’ interest in school science as a subject, it has not been easy for these stakeholders to improve students’ interest in school science lessons and their behavioral tendencies to learn science. Although various intervention strategies have been tried by educational researchers to improve student interest in school science, such as active participation in extra-curricular science activities, implementation of inquiry teaching, and the use of a science-technology-society (STS) approach to curriculum design, the results are inconclusive or conflicting. A hindrance to progress is that there are no empirically validated models in science education literature that can be used by stakeholders to analyze the key factors affecting student interest in school science. Building on previous research evidence, the study will use qualitative and quantitative methods to develop a model of the factors affecting student interest in school science and empirically assess its validity. The study will be conducted in three phases in Hong Kong secondary schools. In the first phase, qualitative interview data will be collected from 60 junior secondary students, who be asked to describe the nature of their interest or lack thereof in school science and the factors to which they attribute this. Special attention will be paid to the distinction made in Psychology between individual interest and situational interest. Teacher interviews, parent interviews, and classroom observations will be conducted to triangulate student interview data. The second phase will aim to hypothesize a theoretical model by synthesizing the interview data and findings of past research studies. Finally, during the third phase, questionnaire items will be constructed to collect quantitative data from 1,500 students to test the validity of the hypothesized model by structural equation modeling techniques. Students’ loss of interest in science at around the age of eleven is a pervasive phenomenon, yet existing literature can fully account for neither cause nor remedy. By understanding the problem, this research hopes to take an invaluable step towards teaching and learning in science that is more engaging and effective for Hong Kong students. 學生的學習興趣是科學教育中的重要變項，然而多項研究發現學生對科學課的興趣有隨升上高年級而遞減的趨勢，本研究試圖探究導致此現象的原因，為進行相應教學干預做準備。 雖然教育決策者、教師、家長及教育研究者一致認為學生對科學科的興趣至關重要，但多項干預措施收效不佳，如課外科學活動、探究教學法、“科學－科技－社會”課程設計等，而且干預策略效果不一甚至相互矛盾。導致這種困境的其中一個原因，就是在科學教育文獻中缺乏一個可以分析影響學生科學科興趣的模型。 為彌補這一空缺，本研究將結合使用質化和量化的方法建立一個學生學習科學課興趣的模型，並檢驗其效度。研究將分三個階段在香港中學開展。第一階段擬收集質化資料，此階段將訪問60名初中生有關其所持或欠缺科學課程興趣的性質並進一步訪問其歸因，研究者將特別注意區分個體興趣及情境興趣。此外，研究者將收集教師訪談、家長訪談及課堂觀察的資料，以便對學生訪談資料進行三角互證。研究第二階段將結合第一階段所獲資料與過往研究結果初步建構理論模型。第三階段將對此理論模型進行實證檢驗，介時將向1500名學生發放問卷，並對問卷資料進行結構方程模型分析。 學生普遍在11歲左右對科學課漸失興趣，但已有研究尚未能全面地解釋這一現象或提出補救方案。本研究試圖解開這一謎題，以提升香港科學課堂教學的吸引力及成效。

442213.label: Realisation of objectives
442213.value: In this study, a mixed-methods design was used to address the three objectives. The first objective was fully achieved in the first year of the study. Multiple sources of data were collected to provide triangulation. The ‘catch’ and ‘hold’ instructional strategies were identified by analyzing the qualitative data from four sources: student interviews, parent interviews, teacher interviews, and classroom observations. Three secondary schools of different bands participated in the qualitative part of this study. Interviews were conducted with 60 Secondary 1-3 students (mean age = 13.5 years, SD = 1.01, 34 boys, 26 girls) with different levels of science achievement. They were selected from 18 science classes in the three secondary schools, with two classes for each grade level per school. A semi-structured interview protocol was used to investigate how students describe the nature of their interest or lack of interest in learning science as a school subject and the factors to which they attribute their interest or lack of interest. The 60 students were interviewed individually. Below are examples of interview questions: To what extent would you say you are interested in science lessons? Why are you interested (or not interested) in science lessons? What sorts of things does the science teacher do that can instantly catch your attention during a science lesson? Why? What sorts of things does the science teacher do that help you hold your attention or interest during a science lesson? Why? Semi-structured interviews were subsequently conducted with the science teachers (n = 12) teaching the 18 classes. Two classroom observations per teacher were conducted to gather data on teachers’ pedagogical variations that caught or held students’ interest for studying science as a school subject. A total of 48 parents were also interviewed face-to-face in schools or on the phone. Analyses of the qualitative data revealed that the triggers of situational interest in science lessons included laboratory work, information and communication technologies, unusual teaching or learning aids, and games or competitions. The sources of triggered situational interest included hands-on, novelty, and pleasant feelings. In this study, triggers of situational interest refer to the curriculum content, teaching methods, learning activities, or environmental conditions in regular science lessons, which can serve as stimuli to “catch” fleeting attention instantly from many students. Sources of triggered situational interest are the attributes of the triggers, which cause the elicitation of students’ situational interest in regular science lessons. For example, laboratory work is often a powerful trigger of situational interest due to the involvement of hands-on activities. Information technologies such as computer games and videos can trigger many students’ situational interest because they like to participate in novel and funny learning activities. To “hold” students’ situational interest in science lessons, teachers should provide some supporting conditions for maintaining students’ situational interest, including personal relevance of science content, out-of-classroom hands-on activities, interesting learning contexts, social involvement, and feelings of success. These findings were presented at the annual conference of the British Educational Research Association held in September 2015 in Belfast. In the second year of the study, the second and third objectives were fully achieved. A total of 15 questionnaire items were constructed to measure students’ individual interest in school science (e.g., “Science lessons in school are interesting”, “I like science more than any other school subject” “I generally have fun when I am reviewing science contents”), individual interest in science (e.g., “I am interested in thinking about science-related problems shown on television or in newspapers” “I am interested in reading information about science” “I am interested in visiting science museums”), and situational interest while learning science at school (e.g., “I like to attend science class more when I myself do science experiments” “I am more attentive in class when my teacher illustrates science concepts with daily life examples” “It is an exciting way to learn science when my teacher explains science contents using Internet information or videos”). Students were asked to rate each item on a 6-point scale (from 1 = strongly disagree to 6 strongly agree). I constructed these items based on the qualitative research findings and adapted some items used in the PISA 2006 project. Reliability tests and confirmatory factor analysis of the quantitative data indicated that the student data were of high reliability and good construct validity. The final theoretical model quantitatively compared five factors affecting students’ individual interest in learning science as a school subject: situational interest while learning science at school, individual interest in science, science self-concept, grade level, and gender. Individual interest in learning science as a school subject can be defined as a relatively stable and enduring personal preference toward learning science at school for intrinsic and/or instrumental reasons, whereas situational interest is environmentally triggered in a science class, short lived and experienced by many students. Individual interest in science refers to a relatively stable and enduring interest in science that students bring to classroom. Science self-concept refers to students’ beliefs about their general or overall competence to study science in school. The quantitative data were collected from 591 Hong Kong Secondary 1 – 3 students using a questionnaire. They were selected from 12 schools by a stratified random sampling scheme (313 boys, 278 girls, mean age = 13.3 years, SD = 1.06). The questionnaire survey was administered by their science teachers or a research assistant. Names of students and schools were not collected to ensure anonymity. Structural equation modeling was applied to test the theoretical model. Bayesian analysis in the AMOS software indicated a well-fitting model (posterior predictive p value = .50). The model explained 93% of the variance in students’ individual interest in learning science as a school subject.

442213.label: Major findings and research outcome
442213.value: Bayesian analysis found that the strongest factor affecting students’ individual interest in learning science as a school subject was their science self-concept (posterior mean = .43), followed by individual interest in science (posterior mean = .32) and situational interest while learning science at school (posterior mean = .27). Grade level and gender were found to be weak factors. Thus, researchers should pay attention to the relative importance of these five factors when designing and implementing intervention strategies for enhancing students’ individual interest in learning science as a school subject. Hong Kong science teachers need to consider the close association between science self-concept and individual interest if they want to motivate their students to learn science at school. These findings and their important implications for secondary school science education were presented at the annual conference of the Australasian Science Education Research Association held in June 2015 in Perth. A manuscript has been submitted for publication in the International Journal of Science Education. It has been revised based on the reviewers’ comments and the revised version is now under review.

442213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
442213.value: The generalizability of the 5-factor model to other countries remains to be determined. The student interviews in the first phase of the study were semi-structured and student responses were likely affected by the Hong Kong education system and the Chinese culture. As a result, one or two factors may need to be added to the model before it can be applied to other education systems and cultures. One additional factor that may be missing is the type of achievement goals that students adopt in a science course. Harackiewicz et al. (2000, 2002) found that mastery goals positively predicted students’ interest in an undergraduate psychology course whereas performance goals and work avoidance goals did not. Future research on the factors affecting students’ individual interest in learning science as a school subject could include specific interview questions to explore whether mastery goals are equally relevant to science education in the secondary school.

442213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
442213.value: Various strategies have been tried by researchers to improve students’ interest in school science, but the results are inconclusive. A hindrance to progress is that there are no empirically validated models in science education literature that can be used by stakeholders to analyze the key factors affecting students’ interest in school science. In the first year of this study, qualitative interview data were collected from a sample of Hong Kong Secondary 1 – 3 students. They were asked to describe the nature of their interest in learning science at school and the factors affecting their interest. Teacher interviews, parent interviews, and classroom observations were conducted to cross-check student data. In the second year of the study, a theoretical model was developed based on the qualitative findings. Five factors affecting students’ interest in learning science as a school subject were included in the model. No previous science education researchers have compared the relative importance of those five factors in a single study. A questionnaire was constructed and quantitative data were collected from a new sample of Hong Kong Secondary 1 – 3 students. Results indicated that the model provided a good fit to the student data.

442813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
442813.value: 主流認知及老年學學術文獻揭示了正向情緒的影響：隨着年齡增長，人們的認知處理會偏好處理正向刺激訊息，多於負向或中性刺激訊息。雖然此現象在記憶學、注意力、及神經科學各方面上已進行研究，但科學界對它的成因依然未有共識。以上提及認知偏好是在研究 社交情绪選擇性理論 的實驗時發現的。社交情绪選擇性理論 認為，當人隨著年齡增長時，人們會偏好處理正向刺激訊息，由於這些訊息會影響到個人情緒，正向情緒的影響也會隨之出現。老年人的認知處理會偏好集中於正向刺激訊息，這些訊息也對老年人來說是特別有意義的。然而，後來的研究常常把此情绪影響歸於情緒調節的效果：老年人更加注意和/或處理正向訊息，因為這樣做讓他們心情良好。這情緒調節的效果也正正解釋了老年人在面對種種的衰老和退化時，為何仍可以保持心靈健康。 在此實驗中，我們的目標是要澄清跟年齡有關的正向情绪影響的成因是以情緒意義為目標還是以情緒調節為目標。注意力（固定時間和瞳孔擴張）會用眼球追踪技術來衡量。 實驗一會啓動參加者以情緒意義為目標（譬如幸福感的目標）和以情緒調控為目標（譬如享樂主義目標），並測試當中的年齡差異及他們對於情感面部表情（生氣，快樂，悲傷，中性）的注意力（固定時間和散瞳）。 實驗二會把香港實驗參加者與美國實驗參加者作出比對。相方均以情緒意義為目標的參加者（譬如文化價值）與以情緒調控為目標（譬如享樂主義目標）。居於波士頓（美國）和香港（中國）的年輕和年長的成年人將觀看有關不同文化價值（美國或中國有關）及效價（正與負）的圖片。假若與年齡有關的正向情绪影響是因爲情緒調控，我們可以預料老年人會較年輕人更注意正向圖片。假若年齡有關之正向情绪影響是因爲以情緒意義為目標，老年人相對年輕人會更注意文化價值相關的圖片。 此外，實驗將對兩個可能性進行評估。實驗一將研究情感識別準確率。實驗二將研究情緒變化。這些措施使我們能夠測試年齡相關注意力能否預測更好的情緒質量。

442813.label: Realisation of objectives
442813.value: To address Objective 1, we conduct two studies. In Study 1a, 59 young adults (MAge = 20.2) and 66 old adults (MAge = 70.2) were recruited. To examine age-related positivity effect, participants were presented with facial expressions that displayed positive and negative emotions, and an eye tracker tracked their attention toward these expressions. To examine the contributions of emotionally meaningful goals vs. emotion regulatory goals, participants’ eudaimonic goals and hedonic goals were measured. In addition, we also manipulated the closeness of the facial stimuli as a within-subject factor by telling the participants that the targets shared many (little) similarities with themselves. If prioritization of emotionally meaningfully goals leads to the positivity effect, older participants, relative to younger participants, would pay more attention to facial expressions of close than non-close targets, regardless of valence, and these age differences would be more pronounced among those who endorse eudaimonic goals more. Conversely, if prioritization of emotion regulatory goals leads to the positivity effect, older participants, relative to younger participants, would pay more attention to facial expressions of positive than negative emotions, regardless of perceived closeness of the targets, and these age differences would be more pronounced among those who endorse hedonic goals more. In Study 2, US participants (121 older adults (Mage = 69.22) and 105 younger adults (Mage = 19.48) and Hong Kong participants (65 older adults (Mage = 72.09) and 96 younger adults (Mage = 19.75) were recruited. To examine the age-related positivity effect, participants were presented with positive and negative pictures, and their attention towards these expressions was tracked. To examine the contributions of emotionally meaningful goals vs. emotion regulatory goals, we manipulated the cultural relevance of the pictures. If emotionally meaningful goals lead to the positivity effect, older adults from both cultures would pay attention to culturally relevant pictures regardless of valence. In contrast, if hedonic goals are at stake, older adults, compared to younger adults, would pay attention to positive pictures, regardless of cultural relevance. To address Objective 2, participants in Study 1a (described above) were asked to recognize the emotion that each facial expression displayed. Age by perceived closeness by valence interactions on emotion recognition was then tested. In addition, another study (Study 1b) was conducted to test recognition memory of these emotions. In Study 1b, 25 young adults (M = 22.48 years), 25 young-old adults (M= 67.56 years), and 25 old-old adults (M = 80.24 years), and 25 participants with moderately severe Alzheimer’s disease (M=84.28 years) were recruited. Participants were presented with positive and negative pictures and their recognition memory performance of the emotions displayed in these pictures after a 15-min delay were assessed. To address Objectives 3, 45 older adults (age ranged from 60 to 84 years) from Study 1a reported their social network composition by completing the Social Convoy Questionnaire twice over a 2-year period (Study 1c). The associations between their attention toward positive vs. negative facial expressions and changes in the number of close vs. non-close social partners in their social networks across the 2-year period were examined. Moreover, participants’ self-construal was measured as a potential moderator. Study 2 also addresses Objectives 3 and 4. We induced negative mood among US and Hong Kong participants. In addition to tracking their attention to those positive and negative pictures, their mood after viewing each picture were recorded by self-report measures. We tested whether the age-related positivity effect (indexed by attention preference for positive pictures over negative pictures) might be associated with more positive mood changes over time. We also examined the cultural differences in this effect by comparing US and Hong Kong participants.

442813.label: Major findings and research outcome
442813.value: Results from Study 1a revealed that compared with younger adults, older adults gazed more at emotional facial expressions of close than non-close targets, regardless of valence. This age difference occurred to a greater extent among those who endorsed eudaimonic goals more. These findings suggest that the age-related positivity effect is attributable to prioritization of emotionally meaningful goals instead of hedonic goals. These findings are written up in Research Output #6. In terms of the consequence of positivity effect on recognition and memory of emotions, Study 1a did not find systematic age differences in emotion recognition as a function of specific emotions. Yet, it found that compared with younger adults, older adults were better able to recognize the emotions of close social targets than non-close social targets. Study 1b further revealed that healthy old-old adults showed the same pattern of recognition memory of different emotions as older adults with Alzheimer’s disease, with whom they shared similar chronological age but showed differences in cognitive functioning. These results suggest that the age-related positivity effect in recognition memory of emotional stimuli is likely a goal-relevant process that is not limited by cognitive degeneration (Research Output #1). In terms of the consequence of positivity effect on emotion regulation, results from Study 2c revealed that more attention toward negative emotions (anger and sadness) was related to longitudinal decreases in the number of older adults’ emotionally close social partners, and this effect was only observed among older adults with a higher level of interdependent self-construal (Research Output #2). This suggests that among older adults, particularly those who value social relationships (as indexed by higher interdependent self-construal), showing the positivity effect (i.e., paying less attention toward negative emotions) is adaptive for the emotional quality of their social networks. When examining the differences between US and Hong Kong participants in age-related positivity effect, we proposed two theoretical approaches: a) using age as a proxy of cognitive and neural changes, and then test whether cultural differences in cognition diminish or magnify with these changes (Research Output #3 and #4); b) merging cross-national data sets to test the generalizability of aging-related phenomena (Research Output #5). Empirically, results from Study 2 revealed that when participants’ negative mood was induced, US participants showed an attention bias towards positive images while Hong Kong participants didn’t show this positivity bias; however, paying attention towards positive images didn’t help US participants buffer against the induced negative moods, but it led to more positive mood changes among Hong Kong participants (written up into Research Output #7). These findings lead us to argue that the age-related positivity effect may have two parts: (1) whether people cognitively process age-related positive stimuli to a greater extent with age (“preference”) and whether doing so leads to more positive consequences (“effectiveness”). Our findings suggest that US Americans show the former kind of the positivity effect while Hong Kong Chinese show the latter kind.

442813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
442813.value: In this project, we investigated how manipulation of two stimuli properties (valence and relevance) moderated younger and older adults’ attention as measured by the eye-tracking technique. In the next project (funded by a GRF that is a continuation of this grant), we will extend this line of research to memory. This extension is important because attention and emotional are two interdependent, but distinct processes, with attention representing the encoding phase and memory the retrieval phase of cognitive processing (e.g., Downing, 2000). Although the age-related positivity effect has been found in both attention and memory, they show different effect sizes (Murphy & Isaacowitz, 2008). In addition, studies that included both attention and memory measures usually did not find the positivity effect on both measures (e.g., Murphy & Isaacowitz, 2008; Reed et al., 2014). All of these suggest that the underlying mechanisms for the age-related positivity effect on attention and memory might be different. Moreover, one study of the new project will employ the ERP technique to examine the latency that the age-related positivity effect shows up. As stated above, we found in this project that healthy old-olds and their same-age peers with Alzheimer’s disease showed the same pattern of age-related positivity effect. This helps us to narrow down the cognitive mechanisms for the effect. But it remains unclear as to whether this age-related positivity effect is automatic or deliberate. If it is automatic, then varying the properties of the stimuli (i.e., making it positive or meaningful) should be enough to enhance the cognitive processing of older adults. Alternatively, if the effect requires deliberate cognitive control, then older adults would need cognitive resources (e.g., not being distracted) to allow their top-down goals to enhance their cognitive processing. The ERP technique will allow us to address this question.

442813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
442813.value: The mainstream literature on cognition and aging has revealed a positivity effect: With age, people increasingly show preferential cognitive processing of positive stimuli relative to negative or neutral stimuli. Although the manifestation of this effect has been studied in the areas of memory, attention and neuroscience, its exact cause is under debate. Findings from this research project suggest that the age-related positivity effect is attributable to prioritization of emotionally meaningful goals instead of hedonic goals. Furthermore, the age-related positivity effect has important implications for emotion recognition, emotional memory and emotional regulation of older adults. It is associated with memory bias towards positive emotions and maintenance of emotionally close social partners. Finally, there are cultural differences in the age-related positivity effect. Compared with their younger counterparts, older US Americans showed a more positive attention bias when viewing emotional images. Hong Kong Chinese did not show these age differences. Yet, attending to positive images was associated with more positive mood changes among older Hong Kong Chinese relative to their younger counterparts. US Americans did not show these age differences.

443013.label: Project Title(Chinese)
443013.value: 痛楚現象學：自然主義與社會建構主義之間

443013.label: Project Objectives
443013.value: The central objective is to publish a set of four papers (either journal articles or chapters in Anthologies), which would offer a development a phenomenology of pain, conceived as as a distinct philosophical position and a distinct methodological standpoint in pain research. It is to be regretted that to this day, such a phenomenology remains to be worked out. Just as in classical phenomenological studies, so in contemporary analyses as well, the phenomenon of pain appears only at the margins of theoretical interest. The second objective is to trace the historical development of the phenomenological analyses of pain. I would like to show that phenomenology of pain originates in the debate between Carl Stumpf, Franz Brentano, and Edmund Husserl on the question regarding the intentional status of pain-experience. I would also like to address the further developments of the phenomenology of pain in the works of Max Scheler and F.J.J. Buytendijk. Another important objective is that of resolving the fundamental contradiction that lies at the heart of contemporary pain research: pain is conceived as both a natural and a socio-historical phenomenon. As seen from a phenomenological point of view, while the first attitude is a case of naturalism, the second one is a case of historicism and culturalism. One of the fundamental goals of classical phenomenology was that of overcoming the either/or between these alternatives. Building on phenomenological principles, I would like to show how the abandonment of both standpoints generates a novel methodological and ontological basis to conceptualize the phenomenon of pain. The final objective is to think through some of the fundamental implications entailed in the phenomenology of pain. Although our experience of pain is lived as a holistic unity of sense, the popular conceptualizations of pain suffer from severe fragmentation. The currently popular identification of the physiological body as the subject of pain, and the over-medicalization that follows it, constitute a disturbing consequence that follows from this fragmentation. Yet the real subject of pain is not the physiological body (Körper), but rather the lived-body (Leib), taken along with its concrete immersion in the lifeworld. This realization carries profound implications for medical practice: it places an ethical demand to resist over-medicalization by privileging (when possible) therapeutic treatment.

443013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
443013.value: A GRF grant would enable me to devote the next two years to a research project on the phenomenology of pain. Such a project is called for by four main reasons: 1) the regrettably marginal significance of pain research in phenomenology; 2) the illegitimate assumption that the naturalistic analyses have generated a full-fledged account of pain-experience, 3) the false conjecture that naturalism and social constructionism are the only possible standpoints in pain research, 4) the unfortunate fact that to this day, pain remains without an appropriate definition. My project would focus on a deep-seated ambiguity that underlies contemporary pain research. While the natural sciences tend to identify pain as a natural phenomenon, the dominant trend in the socio-historical sciences is to address pain as a socio-historical construction. Recognizing that the two approaches are incompatible, pain analysts often concede that questions regarding the role that biology and sociology play in shaping pain-experience constitute one of the greatest puzzles in pain research. The central goal of my research project is to offer a solution to this dilemma. I would like to argue that 1) a solution cannot be found as long as naturalism and social constructionism are assumed to be the only possible methodological standpoints in pain research and insofar as pain is not recognized as a stratified phenomenon. 2) Although it is not uncommon to admit that pain is a multilayered phenomenon, the available analyses cannot solve the problem at hand because they do not question the methodological and ontological basis that underlies them: these analyses are either naturalistic or socio-constructivist. 3) The distinctive characteristic of the phenomenological method lies in its capacity a) to suspend the ontological assumptions that underlie the naturalistic and the socio-constructivist standpoints and b) to disclose the manifold strata that constitute the sense of phenomena such as pain. Phenomenology accomplishes the first goal by performing the transition from the natural to the phenomenological attitude. It can also accomplish the second goal and disclose the different strata of sense that make up the full texture of experience we identify as pain. 4) By offering an account of pain constitution, phenomenology could generate a compelling solution to the outlined dilemma. The solution would suggest that the natural and the socio-historical analyses of pain are complimentary in that they address different ontological strata that compose the full-fledged phenomenon of pain. 摘要：本人倘能成功申請優配研究金（GRF）的撥款，未來兩年內將投放心力於一項關於痛楚現象學的研究計劃。需要進行這項研究的原因有四：（1）在現象學中，關於痛楚的研究乏善足陳，殊為可惜；（2）一直有一誤解，就是以為建基於自然主義的分析，足以全盤解釋痛楚經驗；（3）此外，還有一個缺乏論據的想法，就是奉自然主義和社會建構主義為研究痛楚的圭臬；（4）不幸地，痛楚至今仍未有一個合適的定義。 本人的研究計劃會集中討論一個深層的歧義，而這個歧義正成為了當代痛楚研究的基礎。自然科學傾向將痛楚定為一自然現象；與此同時，社會歷史科學的主流則認為痛楚是一社會－歷史的建構。分析痛楚的人士也意識到，上述的兩個取向互不相容，因此他們不得不承認，生物學和社會學對模塑痛楚經驗究竟擔當了什麼角色，成為了痛楚研究中的一大懸案。 本研究計劃的核心目標，是為上述的兩難困境提供一解決方案。本人的論點是：（1）假如自然主義和社會建構主義繼續被奉為研究痛楚的圭臬，而痛楚繼續不被視作一個多層次的現象，則上述的兩難困境不可能解決。（2）雖然「痛楚是一多層次的現象」這個論述已普遍被接受，然而，現存的分析並不能解決目前的難題，因為這些分析並無反詰其自身背後的方法論上、本體論上的基調──不是立足於自然主義，就是植根於社會建構主義。（3）以現象學的方法研究痛楚，獨特之處在於這套方法可（a）終止自然主義和社會建構主義立場所賴以為基礎的種種本體論上的假設；以及（b）開顯構成現象的感官知覺／感官知覺現象──例如痛楚──的多個層次。現象學藉由將自然科學的態度引導向現象學的態度，以達至目標（a）；現象學亦可完成目標（b），開顯感官知覺的不同層次之後，這些感官知覺即構成我們稱為「痛楚」的整全經驗。（4）藉由提供痛楚的構成，現象學可以提出一個有力的方案以解決前文所述的兩難。這個方案建議：在痛楚的研究上，自然分析和社會歷史分析是可以相輔相成的，因為兩者實際上各自回應了不同的本體論上的層次，而這些層次正好構成了整全的痛楚現象。

443013.label: Realisation of objectives
443013.value: 1. I exceeded my central objective as far as the number of publications is concerned: Instead of publishing four, I published five articles in philosophy journals and/or anthologies. 2. “Pain and Intentionality,” addresses the question of the historical development of phenomenological reflections on pain in the greatest detail. Here I pay special attention to Brentano’s, Stumpf’s and Husserl’s contributions, and especially with regard to the intentional status of pain-experience. “Max Scheler and the Stratification of the Emotional Life” and the conference presentation, “Max Scheler’s Philosophy of Pain” address Scheler’s phenomenology of pain in detail. “The Spectacles of Pain and Their Contemporary Forms of Representation” and “Phänomenologie des chronischen Schmerzes und ihre Auswirkungen auf die Medizin“ pay special attention to Buytendijk’s contribution. Finally, “The Pathos of Time: Chronic Pain and Temporality,” “Pain and Intentionality,” and “The Spectacles of Pain and Their Contemporary Forms of Representation” present a careful study of the central issues in contemporary pain research. 3. I addressed the relation between pain as a natural and socio-historical phenomenon in “Pain and Intentionality,” where I argued that pain is a stratified phenomenon. I maintain that natural and socio-historical sciences address one and the same phenomenon (i.e., pain), although at different strata of its phenomenality. The same issue was of importance in “Max Scheler and the Stratification of the Emotional Life” and in the conference presentation, “Max Scheler’s Phenomenology of Pain.” 4. “Phänomenologie des chronischen Schmerzes und ihre Auswirkungen auf die Medizin” (“Phenomenology of Chronic Pain and Its Implications for Medicine”) and “The Spectacles of Pain and Their Contemporary Forms of Representation” directly address the fourth objection — the ethical implications entailed in the phenomenology of pain. The first of these papers deals with issues concerning medicalization and the biomedical mode of pain-treatment. The second paper addresses the ethical implications that follow from the excess and proliferation of violent imagery. I also dealt with this set of issues “Phenomenology of Pain and Its Implications For Medicine” – the invited lecture, which I delivered at Leuven University. As far as the distinction between Leib and Körper in the context of pain research is concerned, my conference presentations, „The Lived-Body as the Subject of Pain: Some Reflections on Husserl’s Ideas II” as well as “A Husserlian Phenomenology of Pain” directly dealt with these themes.

rows: The central objective is to publish a set of four papers (either journal articles or chapters in Anthologies), which would offer a development a phenomenology of pain, conceived as as a distinct philosophical position and a distinct methodological standpoint in pain research.

The second objective is to trace the historical development of the phenomenological analyses of pain. I would like to show that phenomenology of pain originates in the debate between Carl Stumpf, Franz Brentano, and Edmund Husserl on the question regarding the intentional status of pain-experience. I would also like to address the further developments of the phenomenology of pain in the works of Max Scheler and F.J.J. Buytendijk.

Another important objective is that of resolving the fundamental contradiction that lies at the heart of contemporary pain research: pain is conceived as both a natural and a socio-historical phenomenon. As seen from a phenomenological point of view, while the first attitude is a case of naturalism, the second one is a case of historicism and culturalism. One of the fundamental goals of classical phenomenology was that of overcoming the either/or between these alternatives. Building on phenomenological principles, I would like to show how the abandonment of both standpoints generates a novel methodological and ontological basis to conceptualize the phenomenon of pain.

The final objective is to think through some of the fundamental implications entailed in the phenomenology of pain. Although our experience of pain is lived as a holistic unity of sense, the popular conceptualizations of pain suffer from severe fragmentation. The currently popular identification of the physiological body as the subject of pain, and the over-medicalization that follows it, constitute a disturbing consequence that follows from this fragmentation. Yet the real subject of pain is not the physiological body (Körper), but rather the lived-body (Leib), taken along with its concrete immersion in the lifeworld. This realization carries profound implications for medical practice: it places an ethical demand to resist over-medicalization by privileging (when possible) therapeutic treatment.

443013.label: Major findings and research outcome
443013.value: This research project traced the historical development of the phenomenological analyses of pain. I demonstrated that a forgotten controversy between Brentano and Stumpf over the status of the so-called feeling-sensations (Gefühlsempfingen) marks the origins of the phenomenology of pain. My research shows that Husserl’s early resolution to this controversy in the Logical Investigations and his further reflections on pain in Ideas II lead to the realization that pain is a highly stratified phenomenon. My research also demonstrates that there are four fundamental strata that compose the phenomenon of pain. Pain can be conceived as (1) a stimulus (2) a feeling state, (3) an emotion (4) a spiritual experience. My research shows how such a fourfold stratification of pain provides one with the resources needed to resolve one fundamental puzzle in contemporary pain research. The operative assumption that underlies pain research suggests that pain is both a natural and a socio-historical phenomenon. Yet insofar as pain-research rests on naturalistic methodology, it cannot justify how pain can be conceived as a socio-historical phenomenon. So also, insofar its methodology is based in social constructionism, it cannot demonstrate that pain is a natural phenomenon. Phenomenology enables one to dissolve this dilemma on the basis of the insight that pain is a stratified phenomenon: while naturalistically oriented sciences address pain as a stimulus and a feeling-state, socio-historically oriented sciences address pain as an emotion and a spiritual experience. My research addressed the ethical significance of the phenomenology of pain. I show that the subject of pain is not the body, conceived physiologically, but the person, conceived phenomenologically. So as to demonstrate the significance of this finding, I focused on pain as a de-personalizing and a re-personalizing experience. My research also addressed the role that time plays in chronic pain. My research led to a paradoxical finding. Chronic pain locks the patient within the field of the living present, which is cut off from all painless past and painless future. Nonetheless, this field of living present is inseparable from the effects of implicit memory and implicit anticipation. Finally, the GRF grant also enabled me to offer a phenomenological account of symbolic violence. I showed that symbolic violence derives from the unconscious desire to liberate itself from pain’s destructive effects. This unrealizable project of liberation can take three forms: it can aim to express the inexpressible, escape the inescapable, or transfer the non-transferrable.

443013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
443013.value: On the basis of the research I have conducted while working on this research project, I hope to be able to write a monograph on the phenomenology of pain. My monograph is provisionally titled Phenomenology of Pain: Its History, Methodology and Significance. Here my goal would be to demonstrate that contemporary pain research suffers from three fundamental shortcomings. It suffers from a methodological flaw (it is grounded in contradictory assumptions), historical deficiency (it remains cut off from its own heritage), and from a deficiency of relevance (it remains unclear what philosophy of pain can contribute to pain-research). Building my case on the basis of the research I have conducted while working on this research research project, I aim to argue that: 1) phenomenology of pain clarifies a number of central conceptual distinctions in philosophy of medicine. 2) It provides an eidetic clarification of pain and shows that it is a highly stratified phenomenon. 3) By recognizing that the subject of pain is the person, and not the body, phenomenological investigations lead to the recognition of the ethical and therapeutic significance of dialogue in pain-research.

443013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
443013.value: This research project resulted in five articles and five conference presentations. Through these research outcomes, the project accomplished five central goals: 1) It provided a groundbreaking study of the historical development of the phenomenology of pain. 2) It showed that this historical research is by no means only of historical significance. Rather, it provides the means needed to overcome some of the central puzzles that lie at the heart of contemporary pain-research. In particular, it shows how pain-research undertaken in natural science relates to pain-research undertaken in the socio-historical sciences. 3) This research project demonstrated that the phenomenological analyses of pain are of profound ethical significance for medicine. In this regard, it is crucial not to overlook that the subject of pain is not the body, conceived physiologically, but the person, conceived phenomenologically. 4) This project also demonstrated the highly significant role that the experience of time plays in chronic pain. It led to the recognition of the significant role that implicit memory and implicit anticipation play in chronic pain. 5) Last but not least, this project also addressed the exposure to the pain of others and showed how this exposure can be conceived as the origin of ethical responsibility.

443213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
443213.value: 摘要 此項目研究生活在香港的南亞裔和東南亞裔中學生的第二和第三語文學習動機（即廣東話，普通話和現代書寫中文），以及他們作為少數民族學生的身份構建。具體而言，此研究考慮語言學習動機和身份認同如何在語言課堂中建立，如何在歷史ˎ 文化傳承以及廣泛的社會話語中被塑造。 移民學生給本地學校和社會帶來的語言ˎ 文化和種族的多樣性已經廣泛地被教育領域所認知。然而，研究者表明，在教育籌畫中，移民學生的母語和文化知識在很大程度上被忽視；移民學生經常被認為是一些社會和教育問題的來源，他們在就學和未來的職業選擇中往往要面對語言ˎ 文化和社會挑戰 (Hue, 2008)。過往的研究還表明，語言障礙和在當地的社會化進程加劇了這些學生在學業上ˎ 情感上和社會化中的困難，並限制了他們在求學中的選擇多樣性 (Kennedy, 2011)。來自于南亞裔和東南亞裔的少數民族學生的數目在香港逐年增加，政府頒佈了反種族歧視法規以確保給予這些學生平等教育。儘管如此，這些學生面臨的身份構建的挑戰以及他們的多樣的語言學習需求如何被滿足仍然是一個急需研究的領域。 個體的語言學習動機與他們的身份認同密切相關 (Gu, 2009a, Norton, 2000)。此項目採用質化研究方法，追蹤調查三所招收大量少數民族裔學生的本地中學中這些學生的學習經歷。收集資料的手段包括：採訪，觀察，檔分析和課堂話語分析。被追蹤調查的學生的背景將具有多樣性：印度裔，尼泊爾裔，巴基斯坦裔，菲律賓裔，和泰裔。這些背景的少數民族學生同時也構成在香港的非西方的少數民族學生人數的大多數(Census and Statistics Department, 2007)。 此項目建議的對於塑造和影響語文學習動機和身份構建的因素的多層次調查（包括：社會話語環境，實施的教育政策，學校文化，被研究者的歷史，和微觀層面下的師生以及同伴之間的互動）將在很大程度上豐富現在的研究文獻。此外，通過研究確認這些少數民族裔學生的語言學習和身份認同需求，此專案將有助於為教師ˎ 學校的管理者和政策制定者提供有效建議，從而為這些學生建立一個文化支撐性的學習平臺。同時，此專案也將建議學生如何提高他們學習英文和中文的動機，如何在學習和社會環境中利用他們的語言和文化資源，為自己獲得更多的發言權和優勢，並獲得平等機會。

443213.label: Realisation of objectives
443213.value: The five project objectives have been fully achieved in the following ways: 1. Research has been done to investigate the second language(s) leaning motivation and identity formation among ethnic minority students among ethnic minority students. In specific, a qualitative study, adopting structural equation modelling, has been conducted to evaluate a motivational model which subsumes some hypothesized links between L2 ideal self (a re-conceptualized notion of L2 motivation), acculturation to the mainstream society, acculturation to the heritage culture, and learners' intended effort to learning the mainstream language as an L2 among immigrant students in a host context. Data was collected from 390 secondary students with ethnic minority backgrounds in Hong Kong. It is found that L2 ideal self (L2 motivation) has a direct effect on intended effort and an indirect effect through the acculturation to mainstream culture. It is also found that parental encouragement contributes to intended efforts both directly and indirectly via impacting L2 ideal self. The findings imply that promoting ethnic minority students' Chinese language ideal self would help construct their bicultural identity. The findings has been published at System: • Gu, M. & Cheung, D. (2016). Ideal L2 self, acculturation, and Chinese language learning among South Asian students in Hong Kong: A structural equation modeling analysis. System, 57, 14-24. (SSCI, impact factor: 1.400; Five-year IF: 1.848) 2. Research has been done to examine the extent to which these motivations and identities are interrelated and are historically, contextually and socially constructed. In specific, two studies have been conducted. 1) A qualitative study has been conducted to explore how ethnic minority students in Hong Kong secondary schools discursively construct their identities in relation to culture, heritage, and social discourse. It finds that the ethnic minority students negotiate their identities within multiple positioning from parents, school, and the broader social discourse on minority languages and cultures. It also finds that they construct contradictory language ideologies when attempting to legitimate their heritage languages and to illegitimate the status of Chinese in the social context. The findings indicate that the participants tend to establish an essentialized cultural difference between their heritage culture and host culture. It argues that fixed and stereotyped views towards language practices and culture may lead to antagonistic relations between the ethnic minority students and locals, and become obstacles to their socialization and integration into the mainstream community. The implications for establishing a flexible and relational view on cultural differences and language use are explored. The findings have been published at Asia Pacific Journal of Education: • Gu, M., Mak, B., & Qu, X. (2017). Ethnic Minority Students from South Asia in Hong Kong: Language Ideologies and Discursive Identity Construction. Asia Pacific Journal of Education. DOI: 10.1080/02188791.2017.1296814 (SSCI, impact factor: 0.531) 2) A study has been done to investigate the complex interplay between religion, gender and marginalization among a group of Pakistani schoolgirls in Hong Kong. It is found that the participants experience multiple marginalization and develop various strategies against disadvantageous positions. It is also found that, while the Pakistani girls attempt to extricate themselves from the gendered practices in their heritage culture and its customs that marginalize and confine women, they simultaneously seek to establish an Islamic or Muslim identity that differentiates them from local girls. It argues that, while mainstream culture has, to a certain extent, released Pakistani girls from the oppression and pressure of religion and customs, they have not been provided sufficient guidance to realize their dreams, making the release temporary and uncertain. The implications of the findings and directions for future research are discussed. The findings have been published at Ethic and Racial Studies: • Gu, M. (2015). A complex interplay between religion, gender and marginalization: Pakistani schoolgirls in Hong Kong. Ethnic and Racial Studies, 38(11), 1934-1951. (SSCI, impact factor: 1.07; Five-year IF: 1.425) 3. Research has been done to explore the measures which will help these students become more motivated to learn second language(s) and move beyond homogeneous social networks. In specific, a qualitative study has been conducted to investigate the language ideology of a groups of Chinese language teachers working in Hong Kong’s secondary schools when they teach ethnic minority students. Drawing on interview data, this study reports on how these teachers’ language ideologies are in accordance/discordance with dominant discourse, and in what ways their ideologies impact their teaching approach and attitudes towards the students’ heritage language and culture. Key findings indicate that instead of promoting homogeneity as a prerequisite for success, the teachers hold a pluralistic language ideology and outline the potential for ethnic minority students to become linguistic and cultural brokers between the heritage communities and mainstream society. An inconsistence was found between the teachers’ positive language attitude towards heritage language and their self-distancing from the heritage language learning and use in school contexts. The findings implied that teacher education courses could enable teachers, as active agents, to re-negotiate the separate language ideology of the language policy at the macro level, deconstruct it in classroom settings and develop knowledge and beliefs to challenge and resist the ideologies that sustain the marginalisation of heritage language and culture. The findings have been published at International Journal of Bilingual Education and Bilingualism: • Gu, M., Kou, Z., & Guo, X. (2017). Understanding Chinese language teachers’ language ideologies in teaching South Asian students in Hong Kong. International Journal of Bilingual Education and Bilingualism. DOI:10.1080/13670050.2017.1332000 (SSCI, impact factor: 1.338; Five-year IF: 1.271) 4. Methodologically, the above journal publications have adopted both qualitative and quantitative methods, and utilized such different analytical tools as narrative analysis, content analysis, and structural equation modeling, among others. Analytically, these studies have explored L2 motivation and identity construction among ethnic minority students from multiple levels. The impact of Michelle’s research occurred through engagement with the academic community and the public via publications at high-impact journals, books, workshops, invited talks, seminars, interviews and plenary speech. 5. The above research outputs have generated suggestions that can guide teachers, school administrators and policy makers in establishing a supportive environment for language learning by these students, and help them to understand better how these students can be helped to utilize their multicultural and multilingual background to empower themselves in the host context in order to gain equal opportunities.

443213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
443213.value: Building on the PI’s this GRF project on ethnic minority students’ second language(s) learning motivation and identity construction, further research can be conducted to explore the effects of family socialisation on second-generation adolescents’ acculturation, academic identity construction and L2 learning. Thus, it will contribute to an underdeveloped area in research literature by presenting, from a historical perspective, the conflicts and dilemmas to be found in immigrant adolescents’ acculturation, identity formation and language learning.

443213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
443213.value: This project has contributed to the literature by proposing a multi-level investigation of the shaping effects of social discourses, existent educational policies, school culture, participants’ histories, and the micro-context of teacher-student and peer interactions on the construction of language learning motivation and identity among South Asian and South East Asian minority students. By addressing their diverse language learning and identity needs, this project helps to inform teachers, school administrators and policy makers how to establish a culturally responsive and supportive learning environment for these students, and how the students themselves can, on the one hand, enhance their learning motivation in respect of English and Chinese languages, and utilize their linguistic and cultural resources to empower themselves in the host context and gain equal opportunities, on the other.

443613.label: Project Objectives
443613.value: • To examine the HKE pronunciation of 40 first year fully residential CUHK university students who are native speakers of Cantonese from Hong Kong; • To describe and compare the consonant and vowel inventories of the participants to establish which vowels and consonants are categorically (100%) or near-categorically (90% or above) used in a required environment (e.g., as in /t/ as the first sound of ten and /d/ as the first sound in den). This analysis will enable the PI to establish a common vowel and consonant inventory for the participant; • To identify vowels and consonants that in variation for one or more participants. For example, some participants may pronounce /l/ as /n/ as in the word nine for line. This analysis will enable the PI to examine the prevalence of variation for each identified feature within the participant population; • To investigate how often, when and why this variation occurs; • To examine the impact of various factors on HKE pronunciation (including variation). These factors are drawn from previous research and may include: o Gender o Social networks – primarily Cantonese, primarily Mandarin, primarily English, mixed social networks o Educational background (primary and secondary school: EMI, CMI, international) o Preference for a variety of English – e.g., American English, British English, Hong Kong English, Australian English, if known o Linguistic experience (e.g., age of English learning, age of Cantonese learning, primary language(s) used at home, other languages learned – when, how, proficiency) o Linguistic constraints, such as syllable stress, previous and following linguistic environment • To analyze data both via descriptive (e.g., frequency counts) and inferential statistics (e.g., loglinear regression via VARBRUL) to examine the frequency and probability of the individual and group use of a specific sound (e.g., /l/ or /n/) when there is variation; • To set the ground work for follow-up research on a wider population of participants, in particular for future research on the linguistic development of the participants across time (e.g., Year 2, Year 3, Year 4) with particular focus on those students who have non-Cantonese speaking roommates and/or join an overseas exchange programme; • To disseminate the results of this project via several articles, which will be submitted for publication in journals such as World Englishes, English World-Wide, English Today, Language Variation and Change, and other respected journals in the area of applied linguistics.

443613.label: Major findings and research outcome
443613.value: The project had a number of significant findings regarding the phonological features of Hong Kong English. Firstly, the project established that a number of phonological features of English - /t,d/ deletion, TH-fronting, as well as /l/ - /n/ conflation - exist in Hong Kong English. Importantly, the project uncovered a number of previously unstudied patterns in each type of variation, finding that both linguistic (previous and following linguistic environment, syllable position, lexical conditioning) and non-linguistic (gender, proficiency, medium of education) impact use and variation in these features. The study also examined whether these patterns of linguistic variation were specific to Hong Kong English or similar to patterns observed in other Englishes, and thus likely to be universal or general across all varieties of English. The study found that some patterns of variation in HKE - TH-fronting and /t,d/ deletion - were similar to patterns found in other varieties of English, indicating that HKE operates under similar constraints to other varieties of English and that these patterns of variation are language-internal (and not specific to influence from Cantonese). Other patterns, such as /l/ - /n/ conflation, are specific to HKE due the influence of Cantonese, as Cantonese also has /l/ - /n/ conflation. The project also provided insight into how English is used - at school, home, and with peers - among tertiary students in Hong Kong. It is the first study to date to examine the construct of the native speaker in relation to the acquisition and use of English in Hong Kong and as such, provides important insight into the evolving role and status of English in Hong Kong (and Asia).

443613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
443613.value: The data set is very rich and there are many further areas of exploration. The PI will continue to analyze features of the sound samples, including a focus on the production of the final /r/ (rhoticity) after vowels, a feature of American English that is increasingly emerging in the English of Asia. The PI will also examine the use of the pragmatic marker 'like', which like rhoticity, was found to be a feature of the English of some of the participants, and is also likely to be influenced by increasing exposure to the American English media. The project will also finish the analysis of the 30,000 words that use /l/ or /n/, to wrap up the analysis of /l/ - /n/ conflation in HKE. Other pronunciation features such as /w/ - /r/ - /v/ variation, will also be examined in further analyses of the data.

443613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
443613.value: The project uncovered patterns in the use of pronunciation features in Hong Kong English (HKE). In specific, the study examined whether HKE is similar or different to other varieties of English in terms of use of different linguistic features, and why or why not. The study found that TH-fronting (the production of the initial sound in 'three' as /f/ so it sounds like 'free') exists in HKE, and is more common among males than females. It appears to be lexically constrained (it occurs on specific words, and not on all words that start with the TH sound). These patterns are similar to those found in other varieties of English, including Scottish and British English. The study also found that HKE has /t,d/ deletion (deletion of the final /t/ or /d/ sound in words like 'just' or 'and') similar to many varieties of English worldwide, and that similar linguistic and social constraints operate on /t,d/ deletion in HKE as in other varieties of English. The key insight from these analyses is the finding that HKE is a rule-governed variety that operates under similar linguistic and social principles as other more well-established varieties of English including American and British English.

443713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
443713.value: In the Ming dynasty (1368-1644), the Li people were known to have occupied large tracts of southwestern Guangdong and practically the whole of Hainan Island (Hainan province since 1988). Over time, the area they occupy has contracted to the Five Finger Mountain on Hainan and areas to its south and west. Even on Five Finger Mountain, the last vestiges of the Li way of life have all but disappeared. Since the 1980s, in the interest of alleviating poverty, the government has relocated Li villages and introduced to villagers new agricultural forms and social amenities. Gone are the days when Li people tattooed their bodies and practised slash-and-burn agriculture. How should one record the passing of Li culture and how might that be understood? Is it the replacement of a “tradition” by “modernity”? Does the story of the disappearance of Li culture capture the history of the Li? From what I have learnt of the Li people from the Ming dynasty, I think the history of the retreating Li-occupied territory must be separated from that of the transformation of lifestyle. Lifestyle was being changed over centuries: from the Ming dynasty, Li people were sitting for the imperial examination. Yet, because the Li had been thought about as people who were outside the bounds of the state, observers from the Ming onwards have looked upon particular features of Li lifestyle as indicative of their indigenous status. They seek out such features in their ethnographic study to prove the continuation of the Li tradition. The disappearance of the last vestiges of Li lifestyle promotes the view that “modernity” has finally replaced “tradition”. Rather than studying the disappearing “traditional” lifestyle, this project tracks the history of Li people over a period within living memory to see what has happened to them as a people. It is hypothesized that many Li people retain their Li identity even as they negotiate their lifestyles through Li and non-Li (including Chinese) societies. Over the years, the penetration of government created many intermediaries, some of whom carry the markers of the state as much as their Li persona. Through prosopography, this project will reconstruct the history of people in the Baisha area of Five Finger Mountain, including some who would have experienced the Baisha uprising of 1943, to see how the transformation of life style, in fact, might have enforced the image of the permanence of a Li tradition. 在明代的海南，黎族遍佈全島。在其後的歷史演變中，黎族逐漸集中到五指山及其周邊地區。 今天，即使在五指山地區，黎族的生活痕跡也處於消失之中。自1980年代開始，隨著扶貧的推行，政府逐漸將黎村從深山之中遷移出來，並把新的農業技術與社會方式帶入到這些村落之中。黎族的習俗，比如紋身和刀耕火種都已漸漸消失。 那麼，我們如何來記錄這種消失中的黎族文化，並理解它？這是“現代”對於“傳統”的取代嗎？還是，黎族文化的消失本身就是黎族歷史的一部分？ 博士論文期間，我研究明代的黎族史。我認為黎族邊界退往五指山的歷史與黎族生活的消失是需要分開探討的問題。從明代開始，黎人就已經參與到朝廷的科舉考試當中。因為黎族被視為王朝的化外之人，因此明朝以後，觀察者，挑選了一些生活方式的特徵來代表他們原著民的身份。在民族學的研究中，也尋找這些特徵去證明黎族傳統的存續。於是，黎族生活方式的消失引致一個觀點，“現代”最終取代了“傳統”。 與那些討論“傳統”生活方式消失的研究不同，本項目從黎人的記憶中追溯黎族的歷史；去看作為一個民族，他們怎樣變化。本項目持這樣的假設，許多持有黎族認同的人其實是長期穿梭于黎與非黎的生活方式與社會之中。在漫長的歲月中，政府的滲入創造了許多中間人，他們可以是黎，他們同樣也可以表達國家的意願和身份。通過集體傳記，包括1943年白沙起義親歷者的傳記，本項目將重構五指山白沙黎族的歷史；並探討生活方式的改變，是否有可能是強化了黎族有一個長期維持的文化與傳統的形象。

443713.label: Realisation of objectives
443713.value: For this project, I visited Hainan seven times, mostly along the east coast of the island and going up to Wuzhishan from that side. When I discovered the history of Wang Zhaoyi, whose experience illustrates vividly changes in the indigenous elite and politics among the Li, I also visited the area that at one time came under his control, which was located towards the eastern slope of Wuzhishan. I must have spoken to more than 100 local people, some of them at length. One of them, in particular, having served as headman in his group when he was still a child, gave me important insights into the published ethnographic reports on the Li which were written in the 1950s. I think I have succeeded to reveal some aspects of the history of the Li that had not been apparent in the published literature, and by doing that, I have come up with an account of the transformation of their lives, as I can document from both interviews and documentary sources, and relate those transformations to the process whereby the state gradually gained ascendancy. I think I have completed the objectives I set out in my application. Some time into my research, I singled out two important aspects of that history for detailed study. One of them had to do with the use of writing among the Li, most of whom for most of their history up to recent times were illiterate. I chose to examine the question of the impact of writing in relation to their religious practices as far as I could observe them myself. The other aspect of my research has to do with the displacement of slash-and-burn agriculture by paddy farming high up on Wuzhishan and how that converged with the presence of the state from the late Qing into the 1950s. This became quite a complex story. On the one hand, tracking the biographies of historical persons from both oral and written sources, I could document that from the last decades of the nineteenth century, high up on Wuzhishan local people coming in from Ledong county lower down on the mountain had been introducing paddy farming. At the same time, Hainan was caught up in late Qing politics when, after the Sino-French War of the 1880s, Governor General of Guangdong and Guangxi Zhang Zhidong stationed the troops he had sent fighting in Indo China to Hainan. The “road building” activities of General Feng Zicai left vivid memories on Hainan. He did not really build roads, the Qing government was building the telegragh, and it reached into Wuzhishan. Also at the same time, missionaries had reached the area. Thanks to General Feng’s grant of land in return for the missionaries saving his troops from epidemic, a Presbyterian church was set up in the area. To consolidate his grip on the area, General Feng purged the Li leadership, but in just another generation, Li people who had gone to school at the Presbyterian Church, and from there to training in Guangzhou, that is to say, people such as Wang Zhaoyi, a new leadership had come up in Wuzhishan.
