443713.label: Major findings and research outcome
443713.value: I wrote three papers for publication, two of them have already appeared, and one of them has been accepted for publication. In my first published paper, I trace how religious ceremonies conducted by specialists known as geba (male) and babone (female) were gradually being displaced by ceremonies in which writing played an important part. I followed the ceremonies that they conducted to pacify the gods of thunder, in which male and female gender came to be very obviously asserted. I also took part in a ceremony to celebrate the hunt, in which not only the religious specialists, but the various headmen (shaoguan) each played a decisive role. I saw religious texts being introduced, and how the use of the texts changed the nature of rituals. The use of Chinese ritual texts implies that the specialist possessing them belongs to a larger religious movement that goes beyond the Li communities. In places, I could observe hybrid practices, part Li, part Chinese. Among the villages at the foot of Wuzhishan, I found collective ancestral halls and genealogies, which show very obvious indications that the local people were beginning to adopt practices as might be found in Han people’s lineages. In my other paper, I unravel the history of the practice known as hemu (collective acreage) in the 1950s, said to have been the continuation of primitive forms of land ownership. Although the Li leadership of Wuzhishan by the 1930s was very different from their traditional headmen and was introducing paddy farming, all the while, the headmen’s tradition had continued, especially in regard to farming ceremonies. The new leadership clashed with the Guomindang in the 1940s at a time when the Japanese had occupied part of Hainan. After the Baisha uprising of 1943, some of that leadership joined the Chinese Communist Party on Hainan. During land reform, the new leadership promoted the impression that the Li had continued the “primitive” practice of the hemu that was earmarked by farming ceremonies. Meanwhile, the Guomindang in their nation building effort had been promoting the Li as an ethnic group. The politics, therefore, conspired to shield the history of paddy farming on Wuzhishan from the public gaze.

443713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
443713.value: I am glad I documented some aspects of Li culture while it is so rapidly being changed, but I do not see Li studies as a primary focus of my overall research interests. I am interested in how the state and its ideology interact with local society. In this respect, I have studied the lineage in the Ming and the Qing in southwestern Guangdong, Jiangxi lineages from the Song to the Ming, the history of secret societies, the boat people and how moving ashore had changed their culture, and, so, for me, future research has to do with institutional transformation connected with the state and how individuals came to be caught up in the process. I have obtained my next RGC grant, beginning 2019, to study the Ping-Liu-Li uprising, which, I believe is very much another instance of such transformation. This Hainan project has moved me in the direction of the twentieth century, and Ping-Liu-Liu will be another step which will contribute eventually to an understanding of how the Ming-Qing state impacted local society in ways that were different from the Republican state.

443713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
443713.value: Up to the Ming dynasty, the Li people occupied not only the central mountain, Wuzhishan but also parts of the plains. By the nineteenth century, they were found largely in the Wuzhishan area. They practiced slash-and-burn agriculture and lived under headmen who were known to the Qing government. By the last decades of the nineteenth century, the Qing government’s stationing of troops on the mountain, the efforts of missionaries to provide school education, and the introduction of paddy farming had given rise to a leadership committed to commercial development. The new leadership came to be drawn into the Japanese invasion in the 1940s, internal war between the Chinese Communist Party and the Nationalist Party, while, at the same time, an increasing public awareness of the Li people’s indigenous ethnicity was promoted by campaigns that attempted to educate them. In the national context, the indigenous character of the Li people became more well-known than their economic transformation. However, opening the Wuzhishan area to outside influence has eroded traditional ways of life. A very significant change was introduced by writing. The increasing use of writing in religious practices was gradually replacing indigenous religious rituals in which texts had played no part.

443913.value: 世傳歙縣「許氏幼科」主要人物許豫和（１７２４－約１８０５）終生執業邑城，主治幼科，而兼及婦，內，其臨症用藥，無論對患者病家之施治或醫士同仁之對質，均可為觀察所謂新安醫者活動與徽州人口福祉提供難得案例．曾遺醫著七種，《熱辨》一卷，《治驗》一卷，《怡堂散記》二卷及《散記續編》一卷．此四帙五卷之內容，絕大部份為其幼科臨症之論說，處方及案紀錄．此二年之研究計畫即欲以此微觀記錄出發，佐證籍屬新安之歷代名醫，或執業新安之他科醫士，尤以彼等對熱症，治驗，用藥等散記，核對其他地方相關醫論，醫方，醫案之所呈，對新安幼醫或近世中國地方醫療與地方醫說，醫派之形成得一具體而實之案例．據此類文獻，踨跡之考核，而思地方醫療，人口健康與家族興衰間之訊息消長．

443913.label: Realisation of objectives
443913.value: As stated in the original project proposal, the importance of this research lies in the first-hand study on the pediatric career of Dr. Hsü Yü-ho (許豫和, 1724–1805). With an in-depth textual analysis on the texts he left (called “seven titles from Dr. Hsü’s Pediatric Clinic” 許氐幼科七種), we were able to document the clinic he operated in the town center of the She (歙) district of the Hui-chou (徽州) prefecture in Anhui during the eighteenth century, thus to reconstruct a specific case of an actual local physician at work as a sub-specialist. Even though this GRF project (Project No.: 443913; Project Title: Records of a Local Pediatrician: The Life and Practice of Dr. Hsü Yüho (1724–1805) of the She (歙) District in Huichou during the Ch’ien-Lung Era) had been altered from a three-year to a two-year undertaking (2014.01 – 2015.12), this PI of the project decided not to revise, lessen, or in any manner decrease the “project objectives” as conceived. The following is an item by item report on these 5 objectives as per original application: 1. Investigation on the medical genealogy of Dr. Hsü Yü-ho had been completed. His professional training as a local pediatrician from the Lower Yangtze Valley region firmly established. Furthermore, this case record from the eighteenth century is connected with this researcher’s accumulated knowledge on the birth and development of pediatric medicine since the Southern Sung dynasty (1127–1279), through the Ming (1368–1644), to reconstruct the longitudinal evolution of how such a textual-academic and clinical-technical expertise had been made to be passed from one generation to the next. An article in English was completed, entitled “The Becoming of a Specialist: A Social Portraiture of the Pediatrician in Late Imperial China,” to be published in the Journal of Asian Medicine. 2. In reconstructing Dr. Hsü’s daily operation, as a local pediatric clinic during the Ch'ien-Lung period in She district of Hui-chou, disease patterns of infants and children were examined closely case by case. These diagnostic notes and pharmaceutical prescriptions from Dr. Hsü in addition to being analyzed on their own, such as his laborious discussion on “feverish diseases (熱辨)” which becomes a separate topic of research paper both in Chinese and in English, had also been compared with established understanding of pediatric deliberations (醫論), prescriptions (醫方), and case records (醫案) in the past. Which allows for a systematic re-examination of received knowledge on pediatric diseases and health care for children in the late imperial period, as demonstrated on the new release of this author’s book-length publication, chapter by chapter. 3. Which leads to the examination and write up of the impact of Dr. Hsü’s pediatric services upon children’s health, as it constitutes best in the way of integrated and renewed understanding and assessment of Chinese pediatric knowledge and treatment to major categories of child diseases and discomfort. Such were the re-addressed health problems of the young in the new monograph of Linking Publishing (聯經出版社) addressing to the critical path to successful breeding and extension of Chinese families, clans, and lineages known to Chinese history (Publication title: “幼醫與幼蒙: 近世中國社會的綿延之道”) Which includes chapters on neurological (驚), nutritional problems (疳), vomiting (吐), diarrhea (瀉), and dietary tract problems, as well as the infamous rage of acute and most lethal infectious diseases (痘疹). Other endemic problems such as skin diseases, poisoning, and parasites were also discussed in their respectively related categories. 4. The wider implication of Dr. Hsü’s work in the Lower Yangtze region during the Ch'ien-Lung period can be best gauged in the vocational contribution of such a middle echelon pediatric practitioner in supporting and sustaining the daily needs of the families of the region. Which was then part of the social mechanism and professional service to the successful or not-so-successful service to China’s perennial need to physically perpetuate its family line. Toward the end of this two-year research, its results had led to a realization that such an assessment needs best be done in considering this pediatric service, of which Hsü served was a best example but only part and parcel of a larger picture of medical services to family reproduction. Which therefore led to the designing and organization of this PI’s third and latest GRF submission to bringing in the third and last element of such a Chinese reproductive engine into this historical account: namely that of male medicine (男科), which served together with pediatrics (幼科) and gynecology (婦科) to meet the popular demand in literally planting the seeds (種子), propagating the sons (宜麟), and broadening the offsprings (廣嗣). This then is a project called: “Male Medicine and Reproduction in Late Imperial China.” (submitted for assessment in 2018 – 2020, RGC Ref No. 14600117) 5. The evaluation of the working relations between this reading, thinking, writing pediatric specialist Dr. Hsü with his nurturing also demanding clientele of the affluent scholar-official and merchant community from the Hui-chou region and the late imperial Lower Yangtze area has been greatly facilitated and deepened with this two-year project but not completed exhaustively. This investigation on the relevance of any specialist knowledge to the daily wellbeing of the general population is now being further pursued with this PI’s current GRF project on the other end of the human lifestyle, namely aging (Project Title: “Aging in Late Imperial China: Advice and Practice,” 2016-2017, RGC Ref No. 14605615). This two-year project presently executed half-way (completing the first year, 2016) continues to document and explore the actual material conditions behind medical and health care services of this region (as represented by the She district of Hui-chou in pediatrics and Su-chou of the Chiangnan region in old age care, both in the eighteenth century). We may now safely conclude that the socio-cultural network, the sizable reading, printing, consulting, paying audience and customer group indeed had been the pre-supposed sociological and economic condition for the existence and sustainability of such a specialized knowledge, skill, and service. The chain effect of this on-going cultural-social reproduction indicated that a certain guaranteed “marketability” had been in existence certainly since the Southern Sung dynasty (1127–1279) as it grew and expanded in the Ming period (1368-1644). Its climax during the high Ch’ing era (second half of the seventeenth through the first quarter of the nineteenth centuries) allowed for the surfacing of a case such as Dr. Hsü Yü-ho’s performance and recording at the She intersection of Hui-chou which is by no means a historical accident. What appears in the first instance to be a fortunate discovery of an accidentally survived manuscript for the uncovery of the details in Chinese medical history turned out at the end to be no accident at all. Which thus proves for itself the intrinsic value of the academic outcome of this two-year project as it had structurally been conceived in the first place.

443913.label: Major findings and research outcome
443913.value: The major finding of this project was the discovery and reconstruction of a local Chinese pediatrician at work in the eighteen century. This research outcome then enables us to go back and connect with scattered information we had gathered but were unable to organize systematically, to re-examine how a specialist such a traditional Chinese pediatrician had been produced ( see the article on “Becoming a Specialist”) as the training evolved over the centuries. Which lied behind the sociological possibility of family and lineage reproduction, as well as the economic phenomenon of growth, expansion, and prosperity in the China proper during the early modern period (sixteenth to nineteenth century). Demographic explosion was merely one of the better-known result falling out of such an “achievement.” Specifically within the specialized field of Chinese medical history, armed with the detailed accounts from this particular case, this researcher was able to “revisit” all the monographic studies accumulated over the past two-plus decades, to deepen, add to, strengthen, also revise and adjust the finer details and nuances in the accepted knowledge on Chinese pediatric history and history of children’s diseases and health. After due consideration, it is decided that, though cut short of a three-year full length grant, the research outcome of this two-year GRF project should be presented in a Chinese monographic publication with the same academic press (Linking Publishing台北聯經出版, 台北市基隆路一段180號4樓) which won its acclaim in releasing previously the two prize-winning books by this same author (幼幼-傳統中國的襁褓之道 (1995) and安恙: 近世中國兒童的疾病與健康 (1999) which broke academic grounds and establish the scholarly field of Chinese pediatric history and history of child health in the first place. Moreover, it is decided that this newest release in both digital and hard copy revisions shall be complemented with ample illustrations in full color and black and white from herewith never disclosed museum collections and other sources, of the social, cultural portraiture, artistic representation and other earlier images related to children’s lives.

443913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
443913.value: At the completion of this two-year research project, it becomes clear that one of the key questions to be pursued is to investigate on how in the Lower-Yangtze valley region, of which Hui-chou is a core part and outstanding example, Chinese lineages and clans had been successfully maintained during the late imperial period. Although falling outside of the immediate scope of this current project, after systematic archival and bibliographic search, this researcher decided to prepare another GRF project on “reproductive culture” of this region, especially as revealed by the sub-specialty of “male medicine (男科),” which needs to be studied together with traditional Chinese “pediatrics (幼科)” as documented here, and “gynecology (婦科),” as scholars came to understand. This realization and effort resulted in a newly submitted GRF project, entitled “Male Medicine and Reproduction in Late Imperial China.” (RGC Ref No. 14600117, 2018-2020) The result of which will produce in published trilogy and other peer-reviewed journal articles and conference papers, better appreciated with its completion in three years.

443913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
443913.value: Chinese medical history is documented by “scholarly doctors,” we know little about ordinary doctors in daily operation. Due to the print culture in Hui-chou, we have the notes of Dr. Hsu Yu-ho (1724-1805) and are able to reconstruct the case of a child doctor who devoted his whole life to children’s diseases and health care of the very young in one county for 60 years. With earlier research, against this discovery, we can reconstruct how such doctor was educated and trained by other specialties, as he built his reputation and clinic on the streets of the town of She (歙邑). With the “random notes (散記),” compared with his medical discourse in “feverish diseases” (熱辨), we establish the regional and seasonal character of the disease patterns (called “epidemic,” some “endemics”). With which we further reconstructed the sociological profile of the patients (their age, gender, family background, health conditions). Historians may then consider this against the socio-economic development of the region at this period to understand how the well-being of a Chinese locality had been maintained with the service of a local doctor, at the time when Chinese population exploded during the eighteenth century.

444213.label: Project Objectives
444213.value: Characterizing the Unit of Conscious Focus: Evidence from the Access Repetition Advantage Using the “access repetition advantage”, I will characterize the unit of conscious focus (i.e., explore what subsets of memorized information can be accessed together as a unit). The Boolean map theory (a) states that the unit of information that can reach conscious focus at one time is a Boolean map and (b) implies that this unit is neither an object nor a perceptual group (Huang, 2010a). Specifically, I will use the access repetition advantage paradigm above to test the following prediction: If an item is used in one task, then in a subsequent task, the response time for this item and for another item in the same Boolean map would be equally fast and the response time for both of these items would be faster than for other items that are not in that particular Boolean map, regardless of whether they belong to the same object (or group) or not. Object- or Group-based Effect on the Capacity Limit of Visual Working Memory I will explore whether objecthood/grouping has any effect on the overall capacity of VWM. The overall capacity limit of VWM consists of a few Boolean maps. Therefore, like in visual attention (Huang, 2010a), this capacity limit should not be affected by object structure/grouping within the stimuli. In other words, there should be zero object- or group-based effect on the capacity limit of VWM. Exploring the Nature of Memory Compression I will explore the nature of changes when memories of features are compressed based on statistical regularities. In memory compression, there is a critical difference between “memorizing pair labels” and “memorizing actual colors”: If only pair labels (but not colors) are actively represented in VWM, then when a task requires knowledge about colors, extra processing time will be required to retrieve the colors from long-term memory. This extra retrieval time implies that access to compressed colors should be considerably slower than access to uncompressed colors. Exploring the Role of Long-term Familiarity I will explore the potential role of long-term training in memory compression. In both the original study of Brady, Konkle, and Alvarez (2009) and our pilot experiment, the statistical regularities were learned in a mere 20 to 30 minutes. Therefore, one may imagine there could be a fundamental change in the underlying mechanism if the statistical regularities (e.g., color pairs) were acquired over a much longer training period (e.g., 20~30 hours). How Access affects the Maintenance of Visual Working Memory I will explore whether access to and maintenance of a subset of VWM are equal. Specifically, I will examine whether (a) access to a subset causes it to be better maintained in VWM and (b) maintenance of a subset is necessarily implemented by accessing it.

The Boolean map theory (a) states that the unit of information that can reach conscious focus at one time is a Boolean map and (b) implies that this unit is neither an object nor a perceptual group (Huang, 2010a). Specifically, I will use the access repetition advantage paradigm above to test the following prediction: If an item is used in one task, then in a subsequent task, the response time for this item and for another item in the same Boolean map would be equally fast and the response time for both of these items would be faster than for other items that are not in that particular Boolean map, regardless of whether they belong to the same object (or group) or not.

Object- or Group-based Effect on the Capacity Limit of Visual Working Memory I will explore whether objecthood/grouping has any effect on the overall capacity of VWM. The overall capacity limit of VWM consists of a few Boolean maps. Therefore, like in visual attention (Huang, 2010a), this capacity limit should not be affected by object structure/grouping within the stimuli. In other words, there should be zero object- or group-based effect on the capacity limit of VWM.

Exploring the Nature of Memory Compression I will explore the nature of changes when memories of features are compressed based on statistical regularities. In memory compression, there is a critical difference between “memorizing pair labels” and “memorizing actual colors”: If only pair labels (but not colors) are actively represented in VWM, then when a task requires knowledge about colors, extra processing time will be required to retrieve the colors from long-term memory. This extra retrieval time implies that access to compressed colors should be considerably slower than access to uncompressed colors.

Exploring the Role of Long-term Familiarity I will explore the potential role of long-term training in memory compression. In both the original study of Brady, Konkle, and Alvarez (2009) and our pilot experiment, the statistical regularities were learned in a mere 20 to 30 minutes. Therefore, one may imagine there could be a fundamental change in the underlying mechanism if the statistical regularities (e.g., color pairs) were acquired over a much longer training period (e.g., 20~30 hours).

How Access affects the Maintenance of Visual Working Memory I will explore whether access to and maintenance of a subset of VWM are equal. Specifically, I will examine whether (a) access to a subset causes it to be better maintained in VWM and (b) maintenance of a subset is necessarily implemented by accessing it.

444213.label: Realisation of objectives
444213.value: The objective 1 is “Characterizing the Unit of Conscious Focus: Evidence from the Access Repetition Advantage”. Using the “access repetition advantage”, I characterized the unit of conscious focus (i.e., explore what subsets of memorized information can be accessed together as a unit). The Boolean map theory (a) states that the unit of information that can reach conscious focus at one time is a Boolean map and (b) implies that this unit is neither an object nor a perceptual group (Huang, 2010a). Specifically, I used the access repetition advantage paradigm to test the following prediction: If an item is used in one task, then in a subsequent task, the response time for this item and for another item in the same Boolean map would be equally fast and the response time for both of these items would be faster than for other items that are not in that particular Boolean map, regardless of whether they belong to the same object (or group) or not. These experiments have been completed. The results are consistent with my initial predictions. A subset of the results is now part of a manuscript entitled “Unit of Visual Working Memory is Better Characterized as a Boolean Map than an Object or a Perceptual Group”. The objective 2 is “Object- or Group-based Effect on the Capacity Limit of Visual Working Memory”. Here, I explored whether objecthood/grouping has any effect on the overall capacity of VWM. The overall capacity limit of VWM consists of a few Boolean maps. Therefore, like in visual attention (Huang, 2010a), this capacity limit should not be affected by object structure/grouping within the stimuli. In other words, there should be zero object- or group-based effect on the capacity limit of VWM. These experiments have been completed. The results are consistent with my initial predictions. A subset of the results is now part of a manuscript entitled “Unit of Visual Working Memory is Better Characterized as a Boolean Map than an Object or a Perceptual Group”. During this process, some parts of the results lead me to explore the relevant question on the correlation between different dimensions in visual working memory. For example, when you are asked to remember both the colors and shapes of a set of items, are you more likely to remember the shape of an object if you remember its color, and vice versa? I have systematically tested this question. The results are now reported in a manuscript entitled “Are Memory Representations for Object Features Independent or Integrated? A Unified Account for Conflicting Findings”. The objective 3 is “Exploring the Nature of Memory Compression”. Here, I explored the nature of changes when memories of features are compressed based on statistical regularities. In memory compression, there is a critical difference between “memorizing pair labels” and “memorizing actual colors”: If only pair labels (but not colors) are actively represented in VWM, then when a task requires knowledge about colors, extra processing time will be required to retrieve the colors from long-term memory. This extra retrieval time implies that access to compressed colors should be considerably slower than access to uncompressed colors. These experiments have been completed. The results are consistent with my initial predictions. The results have been reported in a manuscript entitled “Chunking in working memory via content-free labels”, which is now “in press” in the journal “Scientific reports” and will be published very soon. The objective 4 is “Exploring the Role of Long-term Familiarity”. Here, I explored the potential role of long-term training in memory compression. In both the original study of Brady, Konkle, and Alvarez (2009) and our pilot experiment, the statistical regularities were learned in a mere 20 to 30 minutes. Therefore, one may imagine there could be a fundamental change in the underlying mechanism if the statistical regularities (e.g., color pairs) were acquired over a much longer training period (e.g., 20~30 hours). These experiments have been completed. The regularity-based advantages were moderately larger than the original report of Brady, Konkle, and Alvarez (2009). I also tried a few further tests on these trained subjects and see whether the long-term familiarity makes a difference on automaticity of the responses, conscious awareness of the processes, etc, and found no obvious changes. To assess the effects of long-term familiarity, I have also repeated the set of experiments in objective 3 with letters which can make short words (HI, BY, ME, GO). The results are consistent with those in objective 3 and have also been included in the manuscript entitled “Chunking in working memory via content-free labels” (in press, Scientific reports). The objective 5 is “How Access affects the Maintenance of Visual Working Memory”. I explored whether access to and maintenance of a subset of VWM are equal. Specifically, I tried to examine whether (a) access to a subset causes it to be better maintained in VWM and (b) maintenance of a subset is necessarily implemented by accessing it. The results are consistent with my initial predictions. A subset of the results is now reported in a manuscript entitled “Attentional Competition between the Encoding and Maintenance of Information in Visual Short-term Memory”. During this process, some parts of the results lead me to explore the relevant question on the time-course of the cueing in visual working memory. I have systematically measured this time-course and compared it with that of perceptual cueing. The results are now reported in a manuscript entitled “No Immediate Attentional Selection in Visual Working Memory”. To summarize, in all the 5 objectives, I have found evidence that are consistent with the Boolean map account: the unit of visual working memory is a Boolean map, not an object. This research question (the unit of visual working memory) is fundamentally important for our understanding of human cognition and perception, and these set of results have important implications because they challenge the standard view of object-based account. Unfortunately, I have encountered extreme difficulty in publishing these results, something that has never happened in my academic career before. As mentioned above, I have prepared five manuscripts. So far, I have only successfully published one of them in Scientific Reports. Three of them are now under review, and I am still working on thoroughly revising one of them. I suspect that this unusual difficulty is faced because I am challenging the standard view in this field. I remain very confident that these papers will make important contributions after they are ultimately published.

444213.label: Major findings and research outcome
444213.value: When we temporarily retain some information in our working memory, what is the data format of these memory representations? In various lines of experiments, I have found evidence that these representations are organized in the unit of Boolean maps. This Boolean map account contradicts the standard view that these are organized in the unit of “objects”. The Boolean map and objects are compared side by side in various ways. For example, I have found that memory performance drops when an object include different parts that have to be represented by multiple Boolean map, and that memory performance does not drop when multiple objects can be represented in one single Boolean map. This research question (the unit of visual working memory) is fundamentally important for our understanding of human cognition and perception, and these set of results have important implications because they challenge the standard view of object-based account. Unfortunately, I have encountered extreme difficulty in publishing these results, something that has never happened in my academic career before. As mentioned above, I have prepared five manuscripts. So far, I have only successfully published one of them in Scientific Reports. Three of them are now under review, and I am still working on thoroughly revising one of them. I suspect that this unusual difficulty is faced because I am challenging the standard view in this field. I remain very confident that these papers will make important contributions after they are ultimately published.

444213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
444213.value: Of course, the first thing I will do next is to try to publish the four above-mentioned manuscripts. After they have been successfully published, I will do some further tests with other important research questions in this area, such as the division of representational resource (slot vs. resource models). One thing that is particularly promising is the notion of content-free labels. Given the computational load, it seems likely that this should be a commonly used strategy in human cognition and perception. However, this has not been explicitly addressed in the field. I will try to see whether this notion can be applied to other theoretical framework and/or empirical findings in this field.

444213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
444213.value: When we see things in front of us and are asked to temporarily remember them. We can only remember a very limited amount of information. This is called visual short-term memory. What is the unit (or data format) on which our short-term memory is limited? The standard view in the field suggests that the unit is “object” and we can generally remember 3-4 objects. In this project, I challenge this view and argue that the unit is defined as a Boolean map: the linkage between a set of locations and one feature per dimension. In many situations, these two accounts made different predictions. For example, when we try to remember multiple-color objects, object theory predicts that we can remember a constant number of objects (colors in them) regardless of how many colors are in these objects, whereas Boolean map theory predicts that we can remember only a constant number of colors. In this and many other situations, the two theories have been compared and the Boolean map theory has been supported, whereas object theory has been rejected.

444313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
444313.value: In 2006-07 a revised version of Virtual Trainer (VT) system was developed to foster exercise participation and compliance. An improved 2nd version was launched since October 2011 and currently serving closed to 10,000 registered citizens of Hong Kong (as at September 2012). Although initial data shows the VT system is useful for improving exercise participation, actual exercise engagement was not guaranteed due to the nature of self-reporting exercise record online. To ascertain accurate exercise engagement, measurement of actual physical activity (PA) engagement is important. Such PA measurement should take advantage of the VT system that allows automatic PA detection and be transmitted to the VT server for immediate feedback and evaluation. Hence, the purpose of this study is to develop an automatic PA measuring and reporting system which applies infrared sensor and EKG with telemetry technologies, as well as mobile apps that enable PA data uploading to the VT server (3rd version of VT). To evaluate the effectiveness of the revised VT program with the integration of the automatic PA measuring and reporting system, approximately 100 healthy adults will be invited to engage in an intervention program as prescribed by the 3rd version VT program (i.e. automatic PA reporting) for 3 months. Another 100 matched users will be recruited for engaging 2nd version VT (i.e. self-report PA) for comparison, also a third group of 100 matched subjects will be recruited as controls (no VT). Pre- and post- health and fitness evaluation data, including heart health risk estimation, obesity level, estimated aerobic fitness, flexibility, and muscular fitness will be assessed from the VT program on-line, for all 3 groups. Exercise compliance over the 3-month period will be examined from the automatic exercise log of the VT program (a Scheduler Program). The maintenance effect will also be assessed 3 months after the intervention. 於2006-07年度一修改版的虛擬教練(VT)系統被推出來提升市民的運動參與。於2011年10月VT第二版本推出直至2012年9月已有接近一萬名香港市民在使用。儘管初步的數據顯示VT系統在提高運動參與上十分有效，但由於系統依賴參加者自行到VT網站滙報運動參與進度，因此不能保證參加者所滙報運動參與是真確的。為了要確認參加者所滙報運動參與是真確，實際的體能活動(PA)測量是非常重要的。這種PA測量應該利用VT系統允許自動化的PA檢測和傳送到VT伺服器，以能作出即時PA參與記錄、評價和回饋。因此，本研究的目的是開發一個自動PA測量和報告系統，該系統會選用遙測技術傳遞由透過紅外線和/或心電傳感器所探測到的心率反應，來量化PA量，並遙距傳送到流動電話的應用程式，再轉載到VT伺服器(VT第三版本)。為了評估融合了自動PA測量和報告系統的VT第三版本的成效，約100名健康成年人會被邀參與VT第三版本的幹預計劃(即自動PA測量和報告)3個月。另外100匹配用戶將從事第二版VT(即自我報告PA)作比較，還有第三個對照組別(沒有VT)將另招募100市民作比較。VT線上測量的健康和體適能評測數據將會於幹預計劃前及後搜集，包括心臟健康風險估計，肥胖程度，估計有氧體能，肌肉適能與柔軟度。運動參與率會透過VT系統內的運動參與記錄來作出分析。計劃3個月後亦會進行運動行為改變的維持評估。

444313.label: Realisation of objectives
444313.value: 1. Objective #1 has been fully achieved. A revised VT system, the VT3, and its affiliated mobile app (both Android and iOS) were developed. Extensive additions and modifications were made in the revised VT system and its affiliated mobile app, below is a summary of the significant developments. A. Integration of a heart-rate detection device with the VT3 system: A heart-rate watch, Mio-Alpha, was identified and was successfully integrated with the VT3 system. Mio-Alpha makes use of optical sensor (a type of infra-red sensor) to detect changes of blood flow underneath the skin due to the beating of the heart and therefore, detects heart-rate. B. Automatic physical activity (PA) measuring and reporting: When used in conjunction with the Mio-Alpha watch, the heart-rate data is updated in time through the VT3 mobile app and transferred to the VT3 online system. Consequently, VT users do not need to take the initiative to perform the time-consuming procedures of measuring and reporting PA data; the revised VT3 system performs these functions automatically. C. Immediate progress evaluation and feedback: With the detected heart-rate data, the VT3 mobile app immediately computes PA performance indicators using formulae embedded in programming. Performance indicators such as calorie expenditure, average/maximum PA heart-rate and time spent in target exercise heart-rate zone are calculated. Therefore, real time PA progress evaluation and feedback is provided to users. 2. Objective #2 and #3 were fully achieved. Subjects were recruited to participate in a 3-month VT intervention study (and 3-month maintenance). To recruit subjects, potential subjects answered a screening questionnaire through several ways, i.e. street interviews, distribution of screening questionnaire through CUHK Mass Mail, Sik Sik Yuen centers and SportiHealth (online media) Facebook page. A total of 1,300 screening questionnaires were collected and 261 subjects met the study criteria (sedentary 912  health limitation 696  not smartphone / apps users 468  consider for joining health promotion program 261). All suitable subjects were contacted through phone call and/or whatsapp and were invited to participate in the VT intervention study, and were randomly assigned into either VT3, VT2, or Control groups. As a result of the recruitment effort, 119 subjects were retained, with 53 participated in the VT3, 38 in the VT2, and 28 were control subjects. Results are presented in Section 6 below. 3. A few difficulties were experienced during the project period and are summarized below. a. Due to severe cut of the project funding (70.3% cut down to $359,000 from the original 1.2 million proposed), we did not have sufficient fund to develop our own heart-rate detection device. We spent an extra of 12-month time to investigate existing suitable heart-rate detection device and then tendering for an I.T contractor to develop the mobile apps. Extra time was then needed to solicit other additional funding to support the VT apps development. b. The VT3 system development fell behind for another ~12 month due to delayed work progress of the I.T contractor. c. Due to the limit of funding incentives were not provided to participants which greatly affect the intervention compliance rate. Out of 261 eligible subjects, 53 VT3 participants completed the intervention; for VT2 only 38 participants, whereas only 28 Control were retained (with pre- and post evaluation).

444313.label: Major findings and research outcome
444313.value: The data set entered into the final analysis included 53 VT3, 38 VT2, and 28 control, yielding a total of 119 participants. For exercise compliance of this inactive adults, the weekly moderate to vigorous physical activity (MVPA) level as measured from the International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ) for VT3 group changed from 212.60 (195.78) met-mins to 644.40 (522.19) met-mins, and maintained at 566.40 (505.92) met-mins; for VT2 group, the weekly MVPA changed from 365.33 (87.85) to 949.33 (882.65) and maintained at 1,112.40 (759.40) met-mins; whereas for control, the weekly MVPA were changed from 91.75 (79.65) to 316.00 (343.73), and maintained at 396.25 (536.95) met-mins. Two-way (groups x times) repeated measure ANOVA found significant TIME effects (p< .01) with no interaction effect (p> .05). This result suggested that all three groups improved their physical activity level after the 3-months intervention, but the changes between the three groups were similar. Which means, regardless VT treatments or control, all participants increased their physical activity levels at a similar fashion. However, it is noted that the increase in MVPA was double for the VT groups (~400-600 met-mins) then the control (~200 met-mins). The slight increase for control may probably due to the education received by simply filling out the questionnaire. The non-significant interaction was probably due to the small in sample sizes. When comparing for the level of exercise training that the two VT group participants complied with the exercise prescriptions offered by the VT system, the mean compliance for VT3 was 42.05% (42.49) whereas the for VT2 was 34.69% (20.85) and was not significant difference (p> .05). However, when comparing those participants who complied for more than half (i.e. 50%) of the exercise prescription, there were only 25% in VT2 participants but 40% in VT3 participants (p<.05 Chi-square test). This result suggests that the VT3 may provide slightly better incentive than the VT2 group for encouraging exercise compliance. We also found that the high compliance group reported greater improved in physical activity knowledge for health and exercise prescription than the low compliance group (p<.05), and rated higher in psycho-behavioral elements of the VT program design (p<.5). For improvement of health-related fitness, for all VT participants, repeated measure ANOVA found aerobic fitness (VO2max) and push-up improved at p< .05 level, whereas the sit-up test improved at p< .01 level. All other health-related fitness (sit-and-reach, blood pressure, stress level, and body mass index) did not change much (p> 0.5). No differences were found between the VT2 and VT3 groups. Over 50% of VT3 participants (57.9%) felt that their health condition was better than before after intervention, as compared to 41.2% for VT2 and 50% for control. In conclusion, the VT project that integrates interactive website and mobile apps would provide better incentive for exercise participation, although the improvement in PA level and fitness are subtle, but seems to be attractive to participants in terms of exercise compliance and maintenance. With the addition of heart rate detection founction as in the VT3 program in this study, add little effects to the existing VT2 system (where no heart rate detection and feedback is available).

444313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
444313.value: 1. Currently, there are three exercise prescriptions in the VT3 system (weight-control; cardiovascular health; general fitness) targeting the general, inactive adult population of Hong Kong with no apparent health issues. For future development, exercise prescriptions for other chronic diseases could be programmed in the VT system, e.g. hypertension, diabetes, osteoporosis and etc. Further research can be conducted with chronic diseases patients to investigate VT system’s effectiveness on improvement in health-related fitness, exercise compliance and maintenance. 2. Technology is fast evolving, especially in the industry of wearable exercise detection devices. New products with new functions are introduced to the market at a fast pace. VT system must be revised continuously in the future to keep up with advances in technology. 3. With the VT3 system established, there are two types of collaborations to be explored. A. Industry collaboration: As mentioned in point #1 and #2, the VT3 system possesses an immense potential for further technological development. Collaboration with I.T Research & Development industry partners would be crucial for the realization of development. B. Organization collaboration: In VT dissemination campaigns from previous projects, collaboration effort were made mainly with education institutions (secondary schools and universities). Partnership with organizations would assist the implementation of VT into a different sector such as the workplace, where the intervention target would be non-active office workers, providing them the tool to assist in the combat of sedentary lifestyle.

444313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
444313.value: The Virtual Trainer 3 (VT3) system is an improved system with the addition of the automatic physical activity detection and reporting wearable device (heart rate watch and mobile apps) to the existing Virtual Trainer 2 (VT2) system where only an exercise promotion website and mobile apps are provided. This study compared the exercise compliance and improvement of health-related fitness between VT3, VT2 and those of control, after a 3 months intervention period and another 3 months of maintenance period. A total of 119 sedentary adults (53 VT3 vs 38 VT2 and 28 control) completed this study. Results revealed that, after 3 months of intervention, both VT2 and VT3 participants increased their exercise compliance by 400-600 met-mins moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) whereas the control increased by 200-300 met-mins. The improvement for VT2 and VT3 was similar. Such PA improvement was able to maintain 3 months after the cessation of the intervention. Health-related fitness, in particular the aerobic fitness (estimated VO2max), push-up and sit-up performances, were also improved but no difference between VT2 and VT3. The high compliance participants reported better increase in physical activity knowledge and attitude, as compared to low compliance group. It is concluded that the VT system is a promising system for motivating exercise complaince.

444513.label: Realisation of objectives
444513.value: Objective one was satisfactorily completed. Previous reports have mentioned that funeral guides and bulletins, both local and western, were collected, and content analyses were conducted to study the rites which are suppressive of/indifferent to/facilitative of the bonds. To enhance the credibility of the findings, stakeholder check was done by inviting three ordained pastors from three different local denominations to comment on and suggest revisions to the interpretations and conclusions offered by the researchers. It was revealed that, among other findings, funeral guides and funeral arrangement-on-paper across different denominations mostly but subtly stress the cutting of the bond between the living and the dead with many ritual means which are temporal, textual, and linguistic, for example: temporally by focusing on the belief in future resurrection and the idealization of the past of the dead, thus implying the non-presentness of the dead; textually by making the gracious God and the survivors rather than the dead as the centers of the funeral liturgy; linguistically by referring to the absence of the dead in the funeral process. Yet, some of the means are found to be denominationally unique. For example, some independent churches are less restrictive in this theological stance, among them some even take singing selected hymns as a service done to the dead. All the pastors who helped in the stakeholder check agreed that their denominational traditions do take discontinuation of the bond between the living and the dead as theologically correct, and the liturgical arrangements do imply and actually lead to cutting the bond, although they suggested that those arrangements were not set up with an intention to cut the bond. Some of the findings were presented to an international conference held in HK in June 2014, an international conference held in Washington DC in March 2016, and written into a monograph. Objective two was satisfactorily completed. The PI and a Co-I have attended a total of 7 Daoist funerals and 13 Protestant funerals. Daoist texts were consulted, and Daoist funeral masters were also consulted on the site, to check the textual meanings of the rites and the meanings as they were practiced in the funeral process. Due to some practical difficulties, photos instead of videotape of the process were taken. Field notes were taken and a fieldwork journal was kept. Data collected were discussed and interpreted by the PI and Co-I. The observations were largely guided by the framework provided by Albrecht (1999) and Bolton and Camp (1986-87): observing the ritual time, ritual space and the objects in the space, ritual identities and roles, ritual sight, ritual sounds and language, and ritual actions and behaviors and gestures. The eight funeralization rituals as suggested by Bolton and Camp were taken as the focus of analysis along the dialectic of inclusion and marginalization of the dead from the living. Comparing to the Protestant rituals in every stage of the funeral process, Daoist death rituals were found to be very rich and explicit in encouraging the bond between the living (including the funeral masters, the survivors and the ritual participants) and the dead. Actually the dead is served and rescued in the Daoist ritual process, and because of this ritual purpose the Daoist practice does not require the participants to understand the meanings of the rites, while the Protestant practice mostly assumes that the participants must understand the meanings in order to truly participate in the liturgies. Besides, some aspects of indigenization of the Protestant rituals were identified. For example, the Daoist offering incense to the dead, which is a funeral rite to serve the dead, surely would not be practiced in Protestant funerals. However, in some Protestant funerals that the researchers have attended, the participants were requested to perform a ritual of presenting flower to the dead (represented by the dead’s photo) right after they arrived at the funeral hall. Close analysis revealed that the two rituals have a number of similarities in their ritual forms, while there are also differences which were interpreted as originated from their different anthropology: Christian body-soul dualism vs. Daoist embodied soul. Some of the findings were presented to an international conference held in Washington DC in March 2016, a keynote speech at a conference held in London in July 2017, and written into a monograph and the paper accepted by journal Practical Theology. Objective three was satisfactorily completed. 11 ministers from various local denominations, 10 bereaved and 12 relatives were interviewed. Data were transcribed and analysed. Due to some practical difficulties, stakeholder check of data interpretation could not be done with the bereaved and the relatives. Instead, trustworthiness of the interpretation was to some extent ensured by involving the PI and RA to do the data coding and interpretation (in case of considerable disputes, Co-Is would be invited to render a verdict). Among the findings, it was interesting to note that not a few ministers showed discrepancies between what they regarded as theologically correct and how they practiced in pastoral situations in the area of encouragement and suppression of the continuation of the bond between the living and the dead. Using Helen Cameron's framework of four voices of theology, these were taken as a dissonance between one's espoused and operant theology, which to some extent would in some cases cause stress in funeral ministers. Besides, by adopting a discourse analysis to the transcribed data, it was found that those bereaved who were more culturally Chinese (e.g., received little or no western education, early socialization proceeded in Mainland China, older, etc.) did not show significant symptoms of complicated grief even though the continuing bonds that they were keeping with the deceased would traditionally be classified as involving illusions and hallucinations; this phenomenon is quite different from that which found in the English speaking world (Field and Filanosky 2010). This has implications to the indigenized understanding of the notion of continuing bonds. Some of these findings were presented to an international conference held in HK in June 2014, an international conference held in Washington DC in March 2016, and written into a monograph. Objective four was completed satisfactorily. An extensive literature research on death rituals in various periods of the history of Christianity has been done. This research was guided by the works of Rowell (1977), Geary (1994), Davis (1999), Koslofsky (2000), AlexandreBidon (2005), Jones (2007). It was discovered that in the long history of Christianity, separation between the living and the dead were not always normative. There were even rituals taught and practiced during the early church period that took for granted the continuation of the bond between the living and the dead. Historically, the turning point happened in the midst of the Reformation, due to the prolonged theological debates about purgatory, as well as some topographical reasons concerning the burial sites. Some suggestions on the early church rituals being contextualized in the contemporary Protestant world were made at some occasions (such as during some public lectures delivered by the PI). Some of these findings were presented to an international conference held in HK in June 2014, an international conference held in Washington DC in March 2016, and written into a monograph.

444513.label: Major findings and research outcome
444513.value: Depth interviews with a sample of mourners/relatives revealed that: • All expressed the use of externalized Continuing Bond (CB). • Quite different from findings in the West, the use of externalized CB did not show any significant association with poor adaptation to bereavement. • Certain popularly held Protestant beliefs in life after death, especially when these beliefs were raised to the consciousness level of the Protestant informants, seemed suppressive of CB. • Among the younger, more educated Protestant informants, and those whose relatives' death was more dramatic, the three forces—psychological needs of CB, Chinese cultural imaginations about CB, Protestant imaginations about CB—underneath the informants' CB experience seemed to be in conflict. All these findings were presented to the 6th International Conference on Religion & Spirituality. Some of them were analysed in the monograph, and the 10th International Conference on Grief and Bereavement. A journal paper is under preparation. Depth interviews with a sample of Protestant funeral ministers revealed that: • While most of the informants tended to suggest that CB was theologically incorrect, it was found that the more ecumenical the denomination where an informant was from, the more open his/her attitudes toward CB would be. • For those who were strict in regarding CB as theologically incorrect, discrepancies between their espoused theology and operant theology were detected. In pastoral situations, these discrepancies often expressed as cognitive dissonance, and the resolution of the dissonance mostly followed the general paths of resolution of stress in other cases of cognitive dissonance. All these findings were presented to the 6th International Conference on Religion & Spirituality. Some of them were presented and analysed in the monograph, and the 10th International Conference on Grief and Bereavement. Practical Theology of a Dialogue between Christian Traditions and Empirical Sciences: Since there were many death rituals in the earlier Christianity (before the Reformation Era) that contained the components of CB, it was found that it would be theologically/ pastorally fruitful to engage a historical theological study (from early church to medieval time) of death rituals with the psychology of CB, and religious studies in religious healing rituals and Daoist funeral rituals. The theology of Pastoral Presence could effectively served as a bridge for practical theologians to navigate between the concerned theories and practices (the Monograph included this idea). An interfaith spiritual care based on "interfaith hospitality" was suggested. These ideas were explored in the paper presented to the BIAPT conference, and the paper accepted by the journal entitled Practical Theology.

444513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
444513.value: This research engaged the Christian ritual traditions in dialogue with the Daoist death rituals and the social scientific studies of continuing bonds. Findings revealed that it could be extended to a study of interfaith spiritual care. The present research preliminarily proposed that the model of interreligious hospitality be applicable to interfaith spiritual care. The modern notion and practice of hospitality has a tradition tracing back to the Greco-Roman world. Indeed, hospitality has strong roots in the history of Christianity, and in the Hebrew culture. Hospitality is also regarded as a moral virtue in many Asian cultures and religions, and is certainly a virtue found in Chinese cultures. In the passing decades, hospitality has received much scholarly attention across different disciplines and in various contexts. For example, we have Derrida's deconstructionist approach to hospitality , Lévinas' political theology of hospitality, Ricœur's linguistic hospitality, Kaufman's intellectual hospitality, Yong's inter-religious hospitality, Elvey's ecological hospitality, and pastoral hospitality, and so on. Yet, there are other models of interfaith spiritual care being discussed in the West. The PI is now planning to submit a GRF proposal to launch an investigation into the effectiveness of various tested models of interfaith spiritual care in Chinese cultural context.

444513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
444513.value: This project is an investigation into the Protestant death rituals in the context of bereavement studies with reference to the mourner-dead continuing bonds (CB) in Chinese setting. It revealed that Chinese were more prompt to the practice of CB which has been taken as sinful by the church. However, scientific studies reveal that the need of CB may be at the root of one’s psycho-spiritual core. This project, which includes a historical theological study of Christian death rituals, a cross-cultural study of funeral rites, and a practical-theological correlational study of the two, reveals that there could be ample space for Protestantism to accept CB. PI argues that this practical theology of death rituals is of high value, for various local studies indicate that Protestants comprise well above 10% of the HK population. Moreover, since it is common that Protestants in the non-Western world are members and relatives of non-Christian families, such revised Protestant death rituals done for Protestant dead are presumably healing to the non-Christian mourners. So, in terms of bereavement care, the project is not only significant to the church, but also to any mourners who are facing the death of their beloved who passed away as a Protestant.

444813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
444813.value: This project proposes the exploration of the newly unearthed documents to the study on the social issues and political conflicts in the frontier regions during the Qin and Han periods (221B.C. to A.D.220). As reflected in the Qin and Han standard histories, many ethnic groups inhabited in the Han frontier, like the nomadic people of Xiongnu in the northern and northwestern China, the tribes of Qiang in the western China and tribes of Luo Yue in the southern China. Both political and cultural conflicts happened when Han government imposed the imperial laws and decrees, as well as Confucian rites on these ethnic groups. Recognizing the diversity of multi-ethnic groups and the uniqueness of socio-cultural environment of the frontier regions, historian noted that there were conflicts between the Han and the indigenous population during the assimilation process. Considering the tensions and antagonizes between the ethnic groups and Han people, this project intends to have a thorough understanding on the political and social situation in the Han frontier. The proposal writer will explore concrete cases recorded in newly unearthed documents, namely the wooden slips from Juyan 居延, Jianshui Jinguan 肩水金關 and Xuanquan 懸泉. For comparative purpose, the author will also investigate the Qin documents from Liye 里耶 and the collection from Yuelu shuyuan. This research holds that the process of establishing a unified empire was a long term development. Empirical evidences exhibited that there were a lot of socio-political obstructions and cultural barriers in such a vast empire. The issues of eliminating cultural plurality or preserving regional peculiarities and local uniqueness were the significant aspects in the course of building up the Han Empire. Han government imposed institutional devices to assert political unity, but it did not imply the existence of a cultural uniform empire simultaneously. Therefore, social and cultural diversities were the prominent phenomena in Han China. In brief, this project will greatly enhance our understanding of Han China of the following significant aspects: i. The ruling strategy of Han rulers in response to the social and political conflicts; ii. The nature and the crux of the social incidents and ethnic conflicts between the Han and ethnic minorities in the frontier region; iii. To confirm that social and cultural diversities were the prominent phenomena in Han China. 本計劃利用新出土的秦漢簡牘文書，探討秦漢（公元前221年-公元220年）邊陲地區的社會和政治衝突問題。傳統的正史材料都記載秦漢邊境地區居住了許多少數民族。這些族群包括北部和西北部的匈奴游牧民族，西部的羌族種落，以及中國南部地區的駱越部落等等。每當帝國對這些族群實行嚴格的管控，例如實行秦漢的律令和儒家禮儀規範時，民族之間的政治制度、社會組織和文化內涵的差異就會造成種種的衝突。史學家指出，由於邊區民族的多樣性和獨特的社會文化環境，他們在漢化過程中，漢族和外族之間往往產生許多衝突和對抗，本研究項目擬對漢邊境的政治和社會形勢進行透徹的探討。作者將利用出土的居延漢簡、肩水金關漢簡和懸泉置漢簡的具體案例，以及其他簡牘材料，例如里耶秦簡和嶽麓書院藏的秦簡作為主要的分析材料。作者認為秦漢帝國要建立一統的帝國，其過程是漫長的，具體的歷史證據顯示當中的社會和政治障礙、文化藩籬不是一時一刻可以克服。徹底掃除多元文化性，抑或維護地區的獨特性，是統治者在建立一統帝國過程中的重要抉擇。雖然漢政府在邊陲地區推行了種種的制度，以期達至一統的政治，但這不意味文化一致的帝國就能夠建立起來，因此，社會和文化的多樣性是建立漢帝國期間的突出現象。 簡言之，本計劃提高我們對漢代中國的了解： （一）漢帝國統治者實行何種統治策略，以回應邊區的社會和政治衝突； （二）邊陲地區漢人與少數民族的社會和種族衝突的性質和癥結所在； （三）確認社會和文化的多樣性是漢代的突出現象。

444813.label: Realisation of objectives
444813.value: After two years of study on the project, Social and Political Conflicts in the Frontier Regions of the Qin and Han Empires (221B.C. to A.D.220): An Exploration on the Wooden Documents from Juyan, Jianshui Jinguan and Xuanquan, I have attempted to analyze concrete cases related to social and political conflicts among indigenous people, community and local officials by scrutinizing wooden documents excavated in Juyan, Jianshui Jinguan and Xuanquan site, etc. My first article, 懸泉置漢簡的羌人問題——以《歸義羌人名籍》為中心〉(On the Qiang People: A Discussion of Guiyi Qiangren Mingji Based on the Wood Slips Excavated at Xuanquanzhi Site) , was published in 九州學林 Chinese Culture Quarterly. This paper analyzed concrete cases related to political social and control of the indigenous people in Xuanquan, Dun Huang Jun 敦煌郡. I have focused on the documents Guiyi Qiangren Mingji which were the registers of surrendered Qiang people after the campaigns of Han armies in the Hexi 河西 region. Once the surrendered Qiang people declared themselves in Han register, they were under the rule of Han Empire. Compare with the formats and specific contents between the registers of Guiyi Qiangren Mingji and the household register from Liye Qinjian, the author held that the surrendered Qiang people were vested in Han Empire and became ordinary people under the rule of Han administrative system in the frontier. This undated register indicated these Qiang people subjugated under Han Empire and complied with Han law, received the protection from Han Empire. The implementation of population registration application reflected Han Empire secured his rule and administration in the Dun Huang Jun. My next article肩水金關漢簡的趙地戍卒 (The Zhao Soldier Recorded in Bamboo Slips of Han Dynasty Found in Jianshuijinguan), published in 邯鄲學院學報 Journal of Handan College in December 2014. This paper investigated the execution of countrywide conscription to the Juyan and Jianshui regions in order to maintain frontier security. I have studied the recruitment of conscriptions from the Zhao Marquis region and they were stationed at the beacon towers in military fortress with strategic values at Jianshui Pass and Xuanquan site. The Zhao warriors had long been recognized by their tactics and braveness in the battlefields by Chinese historians. Although these Zhao conscriptions were not qishi 騎士 cavalry, these garrison were mechanical device that ensured frontier safety. Besides sending conscriptions to the Han border, in order to achieve political stability and control of the indigenous people in Xuanquan, Dun Huang Jun 敦煌郡, Han established the institution of “Dependent state” to control over those newly claimed areas. Han administrated these chiefdom leaders though the“dual political system” that not only having Qin-State-appointed bureaus like Administrator守, Assistant 丞 and Captain 候, but also retaining the king, now being degraded as Marquess 侯, and royal court of the submissive regime. This dual political system reduced hostility and conflicts among Han and mon-Han people and eventually created a relatively stable sociopolitical environment in the frontier. Please refer to my manuscript, “秦至西漢屬國的職官制度與安置模式 The Bureaucracy and Settlement Pattern of Dependent States 屬國during the Qin and Western Han Dynasties” (co-authored with my Research Assistant, Mr. Tong Chun Fung) As indicated in the Liye manuscripts, Qin Empire established and institutionalized the executive and administrative officers during the territory expansion. I have discussed the role of Li Cao 吏曹 bureau of personnel and the wei 尉Commandant in personnel matters. These officers in county level acted important functions in suppressing local resentments and insurrections from the bottom of society, to seize and redistribute local resources. The legal provisions from Yunmeng Qin Jian, Liye Qin Jian and Zhangjiashan Han Jian indicated that wei (尉 Commandant), probably the xian wei (Prefecture Commandant) were authorized to exercise the power of appointment and removal of Division Heads and Clerks in relevant to legal provisions. In view of the correspondence archives, ordinances and specific personnel cases, Commandant was given the authority to award/to remove aristocratic rank from people, called-up conscription and labor corvée during Qin and early Han periods. The “wèizúlǜ 尉卒律” from Yuelu Academy sheds new lights on the election of senior inhabitants to be the li dian 里典 in the local districts with priority given to people held xiajue 下爵 (aristocratic ranking orders below 不更 bugeng “no conscript service”). Commandant in the county level managed a number of “ji 計 account books” including population, agricultural garrison and public resources. Another investigation on the Qin bureaucratic system was the division of labor and administrative coordination between guan官 and cao曹 organization in the Qin county. I and My Research Assistant, Mr. Tong Chun Fung, published a paper, titled里耶秦簡所見秦代縣行政中官、曹組織的職能分野與行政互動—以校計、定課為中心 The Division of Labor and Administrative Coordination between Guan官 and Cao曹 Organization in the Qin County Administration attested in the Liye Manuscripts. We try to categorize of Qin county organization into guans官 and caos曹. The former served as functional organizations that assumed responsibilities of compiling accounting reports and appraisals, while the latter were complementary organizations auditing the accounting reports and appraisals which guans had prepared. In other words, there was a division of labor between guan and cao. The Qin government tightly monitored the daily operations and capability of division head and clerks. Through the cao system, the foreman clerk (lingshi令史) who in charge of cao would audit the accounting reports from the respective guan, in accordance with books (buji簿籍) and invoices (quan券) submitted from guans beforehand. The lingshi would draft an auditor's report, which was then called a“record of account (jilu計錄)”and then submitted to the Commandery. The auditing and appraisal system were part of regular assessment on individual bureaucrats. Depend on the result of assessment, those dedicated to his duty would get promotion and derelict officials would be demoted. The second objective of this project is to analyze the crux that caused the social and political conflicts. I believe that social and political conflicts in the frontier region came from a series of complicated factors. It is subjective and emotional to reach to one single reason. Different ethnicity, different cultural background and variety of customs, even different dialects and languages, also these constituted a breeding ground for potential conflicts. Xiongnu and Qiang people were nomadic people. The herders’ livelihoods were differed from the farming culture of Han people. The surrender and the attachment of Xiongnu and Qiang people in Han Commandery would easily lead to hostilities and conflicts between Han and non-Han people. In order to resolve the ethnicity problem and to retain nomadic tradition, Han Empire introduced the dual political scheme by the establishment of the “dependent states system” in the new territories. My articles addressed how Qiang people searched their identity, how Qiang people integrated into Han Empire through the registration system. But the system of chányú 單于 which was the chief constituent of the Xiongnu society remained unchanged. The charisma of the traditional nomadic society continued to serve as the spiritual leader of the indigenous peoples. In brief, ethnicity problem, nomadic livelihood, indigenous political values were the relevant issues in connection with the crux that caused the social and political conflicts in the frontier region Han Empire.

444813.label: Major findings and research outcome
444813.value: The topics I have done during the report period, included the ruling mechanism of Qin-Han Jun-Xian system and the “Interior Vassals-Exterior Vassals” system. All these are in connection to the two objectives, either the concrete cases on administrative mechanisms or on the explanation to the crux that caused the social and political conflicts. - the Hu Cao戶曹 and its operations in the Jun-Xian system reflected from the bamboo slips of Liye Site; - the Li Cao 吏曹 bureau of personnel and the Commandant’s role in personnel matters, in particular on the appointments of yuanshi 掾史 division head and Clerks in Qin prefecture; - the bureaucracy and settlement pattern of Dependent States 屬國during the Qin and Western Han Dynasties, which deal with ethnicity problem, nomadic livelihood, integration of non-Han into Han Empire; - an investigation on the recruitment of Zhao conscriptions in the Jianshuijinguan which were one of the mechanical device that ensured frontier safety and prevent potential conflicts; - Han Empire was comprised of multi- ethnic groups. The expansion of territory of the empire eventually in need of restructuring international order and the social hierarchy among various ethnic groups; former Han and the Xin Dynasty introduced the idea of “Interior Vassals-Exterior Vassals” 內臣 nèichén—外臣 wàichén System which was characterized by a deliberate categorization of different dependent countries and minority groups in accordance with their submission levels. The differentiation between interior vassals-exterior vassals was reflected in the obligations, tributes and political hierarchy under the international order of Han Empire. -But Wang Mang王莽 has attempted to revolutionize the system of Interior and Exterior Vassals through implementing the five peerage ranks 五等爵 of Zhou dynasty. Under Wang Mang's new order, degradations had been imposed upon both the interior and exterior vassals. Xiongnu suffered the most radical humiliation of degrading to count 伯. His status from exterior vassal was degraded to interior vassal that converted Xiongnu into complete obedience to Han. These measures had enraged many ethnic minorities and resulted in severe revolts. Cautious about the failure of Xin, the Latter Han ruler had restored the “Interior Vassals-Exterior Vassals” system, and has ultimately transformed Xiongnu into the interior vassal of empire. The changing of ruling system and the reconstruction of international order may be the crux that caused the social and political conflicts.

444813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
444813.value: I shall continue and expand in-deep on the research in connection with the social and political conflicts from the frontier regions to the inner Commanderies of Han China. With the release on the newly unearthed bamboo and wooden manuscripts dated at the Eastern Han Dynasty, like the archives excavated in the Wuyi 五一 Square Site, and the collection from Dongpailou 東牌樓 Site in Zhangsha, as well as the collection of Yuelu 嶽麓Academy, these documents exert stimulation on new questions and research areas. Some of their evidence deepened our knowledge on current researches. I have paid attention on Statutes on Abscondence (亡律 wanglu) from the manuscripts of Yuelu 嶽麓Academy. We find that the escape from legal and fiscal responsibilities were common in both Han and non-Han societies. The evidence from Wuyi Square sheds new light on “manyi 蠻夷” activities in south China, probably Yue people, most likely is related to the Luoyue 駱越 people in Jiaozhou 交州 Region, for example the rebellion of Zheng Ce 徴側 and Zheng Er 徴貳. I shall follow-up and further explore the above-mentioned topics in the next project.

446213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
446213.value: Uncertainty is ubiquitous in decision making with geographical information. It might be due to randomness in data acquisition and processing, or it might arise from vague judgment with fuzzy connotations or imprecision with interval values. Furthermore, the uncertainty-laden data might not be normally distributed as assumed by most error models. Complicating further the uncertainty problem is nonlinearity of the transfer function, which is generally assumed to be linear, that we use to propagate uncertainty from inputs to outputs. Therefore, it is necessary to have a comprehensive and rigorous framework within which uncertainties of various kinds can be analyzed and propagated through operations in geographical information system (GIS). The overall objective of the proposed research is to develop a general framework for the analysis and propagation of various types of uncertainty in GIS. We will build into the framework novel and powerful methods for uncertainty propagation when the transfer function is nonlinear, with linearity as a special case, and the inputs and outputs are multi-dimensional, with single input and single output as a special case. A user-friendly system will be developed for the implementation of the general framework and the associated algorithms. An evaluation system will also be developed to provide guidelines for the choice of methods for effective and efficient propagation of uncertainty in GIS operations under different situations. A series of numerical and real-life applications will be made to assess the efficacy and applicability of the framework and the related methods. The proposed research will advance the research frontier and applications of uncertainty analysis in GIS. 对于决策分析，地理信息中的不确定性普遍存在，部分源自于数据获取与处理过程中的随机性，又或是由对区间数表示的模糊含义或不精确性进行的模糊判别引入。此外，正如大部分误差模型所预先假定的那样，不确定性数据可能并非正态分布。更深一步考虑，针对不确定性问题中将不确定性从输入传播到输出的转移函数，一般假设为线性的，在这里我们研究更为复杂的非线性函数。因此，在地理信息系统 （GIS）中，对于不确定性的分析及其如何通过各种GIS操作进行传播等问题，构成一个全面且严谨的框架至关重要。该项研究计划的主要目的是对GIS中不同种类的不确定性的分析和传播研究形成一个系统的框架，在该框架下，我们将提出一些有效的新方法，用以解决当转移函数为非线性时的不确定性传播问题，其中线性的情况作为特例给出；同时解决了输入与输出均为多维情况下的传播问题，其中一维的输入输出情况同样作为特例。然后将该框架及其相应的算法延伸出一套体系，完善研究问题，与此同时建立一套评估体系，用以指导不同情形下如何选择有效的不确定性传播方法。最后将给出一系列的实际数值应用，用以评价所提框架下各种方法的有效性与实用性。该项研究计划将会推进GIS中不确定性的研究前沿，并拓宽其应用领域。
