453513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
453513.value: Dementia is a major and global health problem characterized by progressive cognitive degeneration and a high level of dependence and disability. Family caregiving for this group of sufferers is burdensome and leads to poor health outcomes of the caregiver themselves. Research in this field has adopted the stress appraisal and coping model to explain the health impact of dementia caregiving. Little attention has been paid to how such an appraisal and coping process evolves synergistically with the intrapsychic, interpersonal and contextual factors in affecting the caregiver’s health. The aim of this study is to address this research gap, and to articulate and test an integrative model which will enable the more accurate prediction of health outcomes for caregivers of Chinese dementia sufferers. Based on an integration of theories in stress and coping, ecological system and human development, the hypothesized model captures the synergistic transaction between the stress appraisal and coping process with the various intrapsychic, interpersonal and contextual factors in predicting the health impact of dementia caregiving. We propose a sequential explanatory mixed method study and aim at recruiting 275 primary caregivers of Chinese dementia sufferers from three non-government organizations which provide carer support services. A trained research assistant will conduct face-to-face interview using questionnaires on level of stressors, stress appraisal (perceived burden and gain), coping strategies, relationship with care recipient, relevant cultural values (filial piety and familism), perceived social support, intrapsychic attributes (neuroticism and sense of coherence), and health outcomes (quality of life and depression). We use advanced statistical methods to examine how well the collected data support the hypothesized model in predicting the health outcomes of the caregivers. Then, the research assistant will further invite 30 primary caregivers among the recruited participants who have diverse health outcomes to take part in a more in-depth individual interview. The purpose of the interview is to seek understanding on how and why the identified predictive factors influence the health of primary caregivers. This project will advance the knowledge by generating a theory-driven and evidence-based predictive model to explain the health impact of dementia caregiving. Such a model can inform the development of health risk assessment for primary caregivers and the caregiver support service. The ultimate impact is to benefit not only the caregivers themselves, but also the dementia sufferers and society at large, which will be spared the additional fiscal burden of dementia patients being taken into formal care early. 腦退化症是一種主要及全球性的健康問題，病者的認知功能會逐漸退化，令其活動功能缺損，日常生活需要依賴他人協助。照顧腦退化症病人並不簡單，對照顧者的健康亦構成負面影響。過往相關的研究，多著重探討照顧者如何評估及應付相關壓力。照顧者個人的內在精神、人際關係及情境等因素，在他們評估及應付壓力時的協同發展過程卻甚少關注。本項目旨在提出此研究缺口，透過建議及測試一綜合式模型，從而更精確預測華人腦退化症病人的家庭照顧者健康。研究假設的模型將融合「壓力及適應」、「社會生態系統」及「人類發展」三大方面的理論，涉及個人內在精神、人際關係及情境等多種因素，探討它們如何與壓力評估及應付協同發展，及對家庭照顧者健康的影響。 本研究將採用順序及解釋性的混合設計模式，於三間現為腦退化症照顧者提供支援服務的非政府機構，邀請275名主要家庭照顧者參與。一名曾接受培訓的研究助理將以面談方式，利用問卷搜取受訪者的相關資料，包括：壓力程度、壓力評估(感到的負擔及得著)、應付方法、與患者的關係、相關文化價值(孝道與家庭觀念)、獲得的社會支援、內在精神狀況(神經過敏及心理一致感)、及健康狀況(生活質素及抑鬱)。所蒐集的數據將透過高階的統計方法，審核上述假設模型於預測照顧者健康的準確性。此外，研究助理亦於參加者當中，邀請30名健康狀況較多樣性的人士，再進行深入的個人訪談，了解他們如何看待及解釋為所確定的預測因素對其健康之影響。透過提出以理論及實證為本的預測模型，此項目將可豐富現時對腦退化症病人的家庭照顧者的健康相關知識。同時，更有助發展以主要家庭照顧者及其支援服務為對象的健康風險評估。除了家庭照顧者外，本研究對腦退化症病人及整個社會亦有重要影響。長遠而言，腦退化症病人可望避免不必要地被提早接受正規護理，社會於此方面的財政負擔亦能減輕。

453513.label: Realisation of objectives
453513.value: The first objective was fully achieved. We hypothesized that the stress appraisal (caregiving gain/ burden) and coping (composite coping) process is the core mechanism to predict the caregivers’ health outcomes. Various contextual (i.e. dementia symptom severity, social support, expressed emotion, filial piety and familism), and intrapsychic factors (i.e. neuroticism, sense of coherence) are postulated to mediate their effects on health through this stress appraisal and coping process. Structured interviews were conducted to 400 family caregivers of dementia sufferers (mild/ moderate/ sever dementia = 34.2%/ 56.2%/ 9.2%). Their mean age was 58.2 (SD=12.9), with about 80% were female. About 40% were spousal caregivers and the others were mainly children caregivers. The Short Form-36 Health Survey (SF-36) showed that about 42% and 36% of family caregivers had poor physical and mental health respectively (i.e. physical (PCS)/ mental (MCS) component scores < norm value of 50). About 71 % perceived moderate to high level of caregiver burden. By using path analysis with structural equation modelling approach (LISREL 8.8), the goodness-of-fit of the initial hypothesized model was not adequate to explain the PCS and MCS of the caregivers (chi-square value 2 =94.9, degree-of-freedom df=19, p<0.001; RMSEA=0.101; SRMR=0.06, NNFI=0.86, CFI=0.96). Guided by the modification indices of the subsequent models, three theoretical plausible paths were added to and one insignificant path was dropped from the initial model. The goodness-of-fit indices (2=41.0, df=17, p<0.001; RMSEA=0.06; SRMR=0.03, NNFI=0.95; CFI=0.99) indicated good data-model fit. According to this final model, the effects of all exogenous variables (including the symptom severity, contextual and intrapsychic factors) on caregivers’ physical and mental health outcomes were mediated by the endogenous variables associated with the stress appraisal and coping process. In particular, caregivers who handled more disturbed dementia symptoms (standardized path coefficient, β=0.195, p<0.001), with poorer emotional relationship with the care recipients (β=0.326, p<0.001) and lower social support (β=-0.180, p<0.001), and be more neurotic (β=0.205, p<0.001) appraised the caregiving situation as more burdensome, whereas those with better emotional relationship with the care recipient (β=-0.304, p<0.001) appraised more caregiving gain. Caregivers with a stronger sense of coherence (β=0.154, p<0.01) and less strong belief on familism (β=-0.171, p<0.001) were more likely to use positive rather than negative coping. More active coping, in turn, mediated the effects of more positive (i.e., gain) and less burdensome stress appraisal on PCS (β=0.285, p<0.001) and MCS (β=0.542, p<0.001). Comparing with caregiving gain, the effect of caregiving burden through coping style on caregiver health was more dominant (β=-0.592, p<0.001 vs β=0.181, p<0.01). Furthermore, neuroticism also had a significantly negative direct effect on MCS (β=-0.439, p<0.001). The second objective was fully achieved. In-depth interviews were conducted with 30 family caregivers who reported relatively poor, moderate or good health on the SF-36 component scores, the findings are consistent with the predictive model, and further explain why the model constructs influence health. By using a priori coding system based on the hypothesized model, three major themes are identified. i) Coping as a response to stress appraisal that influences health This theme describes the significant role of stress appraisal and coping in influencing the health of family caregivers. In the within-case analysis, consistent pattern was observed that family caregivers with poorer health had more negative appraisal on the caregiving situation. They described it as too persistent and demanding which drained out their energy and life opportunities. Some caregivers regarded it as the most adverse life situation without an outlet. Senses of hopelessness and powerlessness were dominant, and the progressively increasing disability of the care recipients added further uncertainty to their future. Negative coping strategies including losing their temper to the care recipients, overeating, use of alcohol, and seeking access to institutionalization were common among this group. Some of them even expressed the desire to simply escape from the caregiving situation and suicidal ideation. Fatigue, sleeping problems, feeling blue, loneliness and social isolation were reported by this group. As for the caregivers with better health, even though they perceived the situation as burdensome, they were more able to report the gain from caregiving. They cherished the opportunities to continue the companion with the care recipients and reciprocate to their love in the past. Some caregivers described a sense of role-accomplishment and gratification from their success in acquiring the skill competence to manage dementia. Some children caregivers also appreciated that the caregiving experience provided them a chance to act as a role model to demonstrate filial piety to their own children. For this group, they were more likely to accept the situation and to deploy more attention to the residual function and minute improvement of the care recipients. They were more motivated to explore active and creative strategies to engage the care recipients in day-to-day life. Successful emotional regulation strategies such as acceptance and let go, positive thinking, religious coping, and remain hopeful were reported for use to cope with the stressful caregiving. ii) Appraisal of caregiving situation is socially constructed at dyadic and family levels. This theme describes the conditions which influenced the stress appraisals of the caregivers. The results indicated that the stress appraisal was heavily shaped by the dyadic interaction and the family dynamic. For dyadic interaction, problematic behavioural symptoms of the care recipients were consistently described by the caregivers as most disturbing. However, more negative appraisal was reported from caregivers who interpreted those symptoms as problematic personal characters, poor self-control and irresponsible behaviours of the care recipient. They were more likely to criticize and scald the care recipients and became more hostile in the dyadic interaction (i.e. high level of expressed emotion). Such negative emotional expression, in turn, renders the caregivers to feel guilty and frustrated, and resulted in more negative appraisal of the caregiving situation. On the other hand, caregivers who interpreted the behavioural symptoms as a disease process and were more empathetic and creative to comfort the care recipients reported more gratification about their skill competence in handling the symptoms and promoting the well-being of the care recipients. As for family dynamic, emotional and social interactional support in form of appreciation, encouragement and caring behaviours from family were repeatedly mentioned by caregivers as most rewarding. They perceived the caregiving situation as bringing the family together with increase cohesiveness and functionality. Conversely, those who lack of family support negative appraise the caregiving situation as helplessness and frustration. iii) Coping style as shaped by personal value and life orientation, This theme described how caregiver’s personal system shaped the coping styles of family caregivers. In particular, caregivers who held a stronger belief on familism perceived themselves as having greater obligation to protect the family’s interest. They were more likely to be stressed out by scarifying their social life and health for assuming the full caregiving responsibilities. The situation would be even worse if the other family members did not share the same value system. On the other hand, caregivers who demonstrated more confidence in making sense and managing the caregiving situation (i.e. sense of coherence) are more motivated in trying out creative methods to cope with the caregiving difficulties, and be more optimistic and hopeful in anticipating their future caregiving role responsibilities. In conclusion, the qualitative findings are in high coherence with the identified predictive model and explained how the model constructs shaped the caregivers’ health.

453513.label: Major findings and research outcome
453513.value: This study identified a predictive model to explain the health outcome of family caregivers of persons with dementia. The effects of caregiving stressor, contextual factors (including familism, social support, expressed emotion) and intrapsychic factors (sense of coherence, neuroticism) on caregiver physical and mental health were mediated by the stress appraisal (i.e., caregiving gain or burden) and coping process. In particular, caregivers who handled more dementia symptoms (β=0.195, p<0.001), with poorer emotional relationship with the care recipients (β=0.326, p<0.001) and lower social support (β=-0.180, p<0.001), and be more neurotic (β=0.205, p<0.001) perceived the caregiving situation as more burdensome, whereas those with better emotional relationship with the care recipient (β=-0.304, p<0.001) perceived more gain from the caregiving experience. Caregivers with a stronger sense of coherence (β=0.154, p<0.01), and less strong belief on familism (β=-0.171, p<0.001) were more likely to use active coping. Of note, active coping further mediated the effects of caregiving gain and caregiving burden and had significantly positive direct effects on both physical health (β=0.285, p<0.001) and mental health (β=0.542, p<0.001). Furthermore, neuroticism also had a significantly negative direct effect on mental health (β=-0.439, p<0.001). Qualitative findings enrich the model. Caregivers who perceived the situation as persistent, demanding, painful, powerless and hopeless were more likely to use negative coping strategies such as overeating, alcohol consumption, blaming the others, escaping from the situation and even suicidal thoughts. Poor health outcomes including fatigue, sleeping problem, feeling blue, loneliness and social isolation were reported. On the other hand, those perceived the caregiving situation as an opportunity to reciprocate the care recipients, increase family function, and personal growth managed the stress with problem-focused copings and positive thinking, and resulted in better health. Furthermore, this stress appraisal and coping process was evolved from the intra-psychic and contextual environment of the caregivers. Whereas stress appraisal was found to socially constructed by the dyadic interaction and the family dynamic in responding to the dementia caregiving, coping style was found to be shaped by the caregivers’ personal value and life orientation. In particular, familism was found to impose a strong obligation on the caregivers to shoulder all the caregiving responsibilities and inhibited effective help-seeking. On the other hand, caregivers who demonstrated more confidence in making sense and managing the caregiving situation are more motivated in trying out creative methods to cope with the caregiving difficulties, and be more optimistic and hopeful in anticipating their future caregiving role responsibilities.

453513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
453513.value: This study has developed a theory-driven predictive model to explain the health of family caregivers of persons with dementia. The model implies that interventions which promote positive aspects of caregiving [PAC or perceived gain], sense of coherence, dyadic emotional relationship may enhance effective coping and the health of the caregivers. In connection with this, following actions were taken: - A strength-based intervention protocol which targeted at enhancing positive appraisal of the caregiving situation, sense of coherence, and caregivers’ health was developed. Funding has been secured from the General Research Fund 2016/17 to examine its health effects on family caregivers. - An integrative review on 40 studies was done to develop a model to predict PAC for persons with dementia. The work has been submitted to the International Journal of Nursing Studies for consideration of publication. A research proposal for this model testing was submitted for the GRF2017/18. - A study to validate the construct of emotional relationship between care dyads of dementia in Chinese was completed, and its health impact on caregivers were identified. The work has been disseminated in national and international conferences, and the investigation team is now developing strategies to improve the dyadic relationship in dementia caregiving.

453513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
453513.value: With the drastic increase in the dementia population in Hong Kong, family caregiving becomes a crucial informal care resource to relieve the disease burden. Sustaining this valuable resource relies on effective interventions to optimize role adaptation and health of the caregivers. This study addresses this agenda by generating a theory-driven and evidence-based model to delineate and explain the mediating mechanism of caregiving experience and the caregivers’ health. This model provides conceptual guidance on how to mobilize the intrapsychic and contextual resources of caregivers to better support their stress appraisal and coping process and, thereby, optimize the health outcomes. Besides, the findings have also yielded important service implications by highlighted the roles of positive aspects of caregiving, sense of coherence, dyadic emotional relationship in promoting effective coping and optimizing the health of family caregivers. Such information is crucial to catalyze the paradigm shift from ‘reducing limitations’ to ‘optimizing personal and interpersonal strengths’ in developing caregiving support services. In line with this, a strength-based intervention protocol developed for this purpose has been communicated to the service partners of the investigator team. Ongoing efforts is placed on developing strategies to optimize positive caregiving experience, and to nurture a better dyadic relationship.

453713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
453713.value: The aim of this project is to detect oil-spills using satellite Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data in coastal waters of Hong Kong and in the northern South China Sea, and to investigate the potential impact of oil-pollution on phytoplankton-blooms in coastal waters. Ecological disasters caused by oil-spills result in enormous damage to the marine environment and great costs for clear-up operations. Being transected by major international lanes, the Pacific and Indian Oceans are among the busiest in the world. Thus, monitoring the oil-pollution in this region is of great importance to protect the region’s marine ecosystem. SAR imagery will be used as it is independent of weather conditions and capable of detecting dark-spots on the sea surface and coastal waters. SAR images (e.g., Radarsat-2, Cosmo-Skymed, HJ-1C and HY-3 SAR) will be employed to detect dark-spots, determine major features of oil-slicks and distinguish real oil-slicks from look-alikes. Level-set method and wavelets will be applied to segment dark-patches from single-polarimetric SAR data. Multi-polarimetric SAR behavior of oil-spills will be especially studied to improve the capability of distinguishing oil-spills from biogenic look-alikes and low-wind areas. One-class classification will be applied to determine optimum features distinguishing real oil-slicks from look-alikes by taking the advantage of single-polarimetric and multi-polarimetric SAR information. In addition, optical satellite MODIS (Moderate-Resolution-Imaging-Spectroradiometer) and ASTER (Advanced Space-borne Thermal-Emission and Reflection-Radiometer) images in cloud-free conditions will be used as supplementary data to assist in the interpretation of oil information detected from SAR images over the coastal waters. In the northern South China Sea, oil-spills are often correlated with shipping or pipeline routes and with oil platforms. Historical in-situ measurements and MODIS & ASTER data will also be collected to investigate coastal phytoplankton-blooms and relate these blooms to oil-pollution. We believe this is the first time that satellite data has been used to study the impact of oil-pollution on Hong Kong’s coastal phytoplankton-blooms. The outcomes of this study include publications in peer-reviewed journals and evidence-based reports that will support coastal assessment and decision-making. The findings can also be applied to several important fields of research, including the preservation of the coastal ecosystem, sustainable tourism and the understanding of coastal ecological health, with particular reference to increasing oil-spills. Additionally, Hong Kong is typical of many coastal areas in the tropics, and therefore the implementation of this project can usefully serve as a model for other tropical coastal regions elsewhere in the world. 457413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
457413.value: Aim The proposed project focuses on grassroots philanthropic tourism (GPT) in rural China, and aims to (1) map out the characteristics (forms, operations, and activities) of GPT in rural China; (2) explore GPT’s influence on participants; (3) understand GPT’s influence on rural communities; (4) investigate GPT’s influence on civil society development; and (5) discuss GPT’s challenges and future development. Background Philanthropic tourism has emerged in China as a grassroots movement. Urban residents participate in various philanthropic activities while traveling in rural areas. They have a great potential to promote social and economic development in rural areas, as well as to strengthen civil society in China, through resource mobilization, service provision, encouraging civic participation, and establishing new voluntary organizations. Systematic knowledge regarding philanthropic tourism in China is lacking. Although there are studies on voluntourism (that is, volunteer tourism) in developed Western countries, voluntourism and philanthropic tourism differ in terms of mission, format, and influence. While voluntourism is led by commercial travel agencies or established non-profit organizations (NPOs), and may include a large variety of non-profit activities, philanthropic tourism in China is largely grassroots and involves almost exclusively public-interest initiatives, such as education promotion, and environmental protection. Hence, to understand philanthropic tourism in China, and to maximize its benefits to society, we cannot rely solely on the framework of voluntourism, but rather we have to investigate the local situation. Thus, we are proposing to conduct this ethnographic study on GPT in rural China. Project Description To achieve the research goals, the study will utilize both online and offline ethnographic methodologies. We will collect formal and informal organizational documents to explore the demographic and program characteristics of the GPT organizations. Online and offline participant observation will be used to investigate GPT organizations’ operations, as well as the behavior of individual philanthropic travelers who do not belong to a GPT organization. Online and offline interviews will be conducted to understand the GPT participants’ motivations and personal gains, as well as the organizational leaders’ perceptions of current challenges and future directions. Rural residents influenced by GPT will also be interviewed to explore their perceptions of GPT’s impact. Significance The findings of the proposed study will not only help us understand GPT, and maximize its benefits to society, but also fill an important knowledge gap in the field of volunteerism and non-profit studies. This explorative qualitative work will become the basis for future quantitative investigations. 在中國內地，公益旅遊正以一種草根運動的形式蓬勃發展。城市居民在前往偏遠農村旅遊的同時，參與各種慈善公益活動。他們對偏遠農村的社會與經濟發展有巨大的推動潛力。同時，由於他們廣泛地動員資源，提供服務，鼓勵公民參與，且建立新的社會團體，他們也有可能對中國內地公民社會的發展有著積極的影響。然而，針對中國內地公益旅遊的系統知識卻十分貧乏。雖然西方發達國家已經有一些關於志願旅遊（即在旅遊中從事志願活動）的研究， 可是志願旅遊和公益旅遊在使命、形式和影響上都有很大的不同。志願旅遊通常是商業旅遊機構或者非營利機構所開發的專案，可以包括許多不同的活動；而中國內地的公益旅遊卻大部分是草根的，而且基本只從事慈善公益事業，例如，扶貧、支教、環保。 因此，要瞭解中國內地公益旅遊，將其有益影響最大化，我們不能只依賴志願旅遊的理論框架，而必須親身到當地去調查情況。所以，我們設計了這個民族志研究專案，來研究中國草根公益旅遊(GPT) 。本研究有五個目標：（1）描述GPT的特點（形式、運作、活動）；（2）探索GPT對參與者的影響；（3）瞭解GPT對偏遠農村社區的影響；（4）通過對GPT組織發展過程的研究，調查GPT對中國公民社會發展的影響；以及（5）討論GPT所面臨的挑戰和未來的發展機遇。 為達上述目標，本研究將會採用網上和網下的民族志法。我們將搜集正式與非正式的檔，以探索GPT組織的形態與專案特徵。我們也將採用網上與網下的參與式觀察來研究GPT組織的運作，以及那些不隸屬於任何GPT組織的自由旅遊者的行為。我們還將採用網上與網下的訪談來瞭解GPT參與者的動機和收穫，以及GPT組織領導者對目前GPT所面臨的機遇與挑戰的看法。此外，我們將採訪農村居民，以瞭解他們眼中GPT的影響。 本研究的結果不但有助於加深我們對GPT的瞭解，最大限度地發揮其對社會的正面影響，還可以填補一個志願旅遊及非營利領域的重要知識空白。這個探索性的質性研究將成為未來量性研究的基礎。

457413.label: Realisation of objectives
457413.value: 1. Based on the initial 32 organizations identified in the PI’s dissertation, an exhaustive snowball sample of GPT (grassroots philanthropic tourism) organizations has been conducted to identify other organizations. Finally, we found 163 organizations that are involved in philanthropic tourism, and 101 are of grassroots background. The demographic characteristics of these organizations, as well as their level of development have been mapped out. We have identified six different types of GPT organizations, namely, outdoor activity clubs, philanthropic tourism companies, charitable organizations with rural field work projects, social enterprise, gap year services, and volunteer teaching organizations. These organizations are involved in four major areas of work, including: poverty alleviation, education promotion, environment protection, and rural development. Some organizations are working in multiple areas. In addition, using a bottom-up coding strategy, we identified the major organizational strategies/approaches that these organizations use to achieve organizational missions & goals. Thirty-seven approaches in seven different domains have been mapped out, which were classified into 4 levels based on their level of interaction/engagement with the participants and local residents. The first level is direct cash and/or in-kind donation to the needy people. The interaction with beneficiary is low. In the second level of activities, volunteers are involved, and members of the organizations start to build collaborative relationship with the beneficiaries (e.g. volunteer teacher programme in remote rural villages). The third level of approaches utilize community asset-building or participatory-charity concepts (e.g. rural cooperatives). The service recipients are encouraged to participant in the programme and their contributions and potentials are recognized. The fourth level brings “charity advocacy” into activities. These approaches aim to link the external resources with the needy community. They may use charitable fundraising and crowdfunding through social media. 2. Online and offline observation and in-depth interview were utilized to understand the GPT groups’ influence on participants. We found that GPT participants in China are a more diverse group than those described in the Western literature. While the Western literature focused on individuals who participates in short-term or long-term programs organized by established organizations, our observations in China identified individuals as organizers of different programs. Moreover, besides urban individuals who travel to remote rural areas, we have also identified rural migrant workers, who decided to go back home to organize programs that attract urban tourists. For some of these people, GPT is an eye-opening experience, which leads to more understanding of various social problems. For some other people, GPT is an opportunity to start a social business which benefit themselves, as well as their community. 3. Offline observation and in-depth interview were utilized to understand the GPT groups’ influence on rural community. We conducted two field trips, travelling along with GPT organizations to remote rural areas. The two sites we visited are both located in Sichuan province. The first site, Yaan is a city suffered a level 7.0 earthquake in April 20th 2013, we traveled there to observe a social enterprise which helped residents to establish cooperative groups, selling agricultural products online and organizing home-stay for tourists. The organization runs a series of GPT program that aims to attract urban tourists. Inspired by the GPT organization’s work, some local residents who had previously migrated to the city came back to set up businesses in the village. The second site, Butuo village is located in Ta-liang Mountains. Local residents, mainly from the Yi ethnic group are facing various social problems. The GPT organization from Guangdong province, brought donors and volunteers to Butuo village to help with local education. The organization has successfully established some schemes to promote education for local girls and young women. The programs have changed local residents’ attitudes towards education for girls. From these two examples, we can see that GPT organizations can make various positive impacts on rural communities. 4. Online and offline observation and in-depth interview were utilized to understand GPT’s influence on the Chinese civil society. We have analyzed the level of developed of a sub sample of the GPT organizations. We have identified four levels of developed, described the characteristics of each developmental level, and discussed factors that facilitate or hinder organizational development. The results have been published in: Zhou, H. (2015) Mapping the Level of Development of Grassroots NPOs in China, Voluntas: International Journal of Voluntary and Nonprofit Organizations, doi: 10.1007/s11266-015-9612-0. We are in the process of analyzing the full sample. Moreover, we visited five provinces, seven different cities and more than 20 GPT organizations to conduct in-depth interview. We also collected various online documents, such as forum discussions, and online diaries. We are analyzing these data to further investigate GPT organizations’ operations, and their perceptions of philanthropic tourism. We are preparing a paper on the construction of grassroots philanthropy in the Chinese cyberspace. Additionally, because many of the organizations in our sample use online mobilization. We have collected data on their behavior on social media. The paper has been published: Zhou, H., & Pan, Q. (2016). Information, Community, and Action on Sina-Weibo: How Chinese Philanthropic NGOs Use Social Media. Voluntas: International Journal of Voluntary and Nonprofit Organizations, 1-25. doi: 10.1007/s11266-016-9685-4. A follow-up paper “Adoption and Use of Social Media: Chinese nonprofits in the Web 2.0 Era” on the same topic was presented at the 2016 ARNOVA conference. The paper has been revised and renamed as “Blogging with a Mission, Blogging within a System: Chinese GONGOs, CONGOs, Grassroots, and Student Organizations on Weibo”. It has been submitted for publication and is currently under review. 5. Our data shows that GPT in China face various challenges. At the policy level, in the past, many GPT organizations could not gain legal nonprofit status. Currently however, because the central government is evaluating local governments based on how many registered NGOs they have in their jurisdictions, local governments at various levels organize programs to “incubate” grassroots groups. Some of the GPTs are much annoyed by these programs, as the various trainings and sharing sessions are eating up their precious time. At the organizational level, we observed that there is divide between those that desire to become formal nonprofits and those that want to remain grassroots. Those that desire to become formal nonprofits lack capacity to do so, while those that desire to remain grassroots are providing programs with questionable quality. We have discussed with the organizational leaders to see how these challenges could be addressed. Some of the organizations are now working with the research team on program evaluation and program development. We have also teamed up with the NGO 2.0 project to provide training to organizations.

457413.label: Major findings and research outcome
457413.value: We identified 163 philanthropic tourism organizations operating in various jurisdictions of China. The majority of them (62.0%) are of grassroots background (GPT). Over 60% are unregistered groups. Among them charitable organizations with rural field work project is the most common type, occupying more than half of the sample (62.4%). The main area that GPT organizations work in is rural education promotion. Data suggests that GPT organizations in China are still at an early stage of development. The vast majority of them are engaging in resource mobilization activities, such as donation and volunteer assistance. Using the scoring system we developed (paper 2 Part C), we found that most of the GPT organizations are still at stage one (amateur do-gooders) or stage two (star-up charities). We have identified motivations to participate in GPT, including altruistic motivations (e.g., supporting an important cause), utilitarian motivations (e.g., enhancing human capital), and social motivation (e.g., extending social networks). Participants reported that they have gained various benefits from GPT, such as getting to know a new culture, getting a sense of achievement, develop the ability to survive in the mountains, and prepare for future entrepreneurship. GPT organizations have made positive impacts on the local community. GPT initiatives organized by both the social enterprise and the charitable group in post-earthquake Yaan city and in ethnic-minority-occupied Butuo village, have made significant influence on the resourceless communities. Through participating in the initiatives, the villagers enhanced their sense of belonging to the community, have their traditional cultural recognized and were empowered to take control of their own future. By utilizing existing resources, skills, and experience within the community, the capacity of the community could be greatly enhanced, leading to better quality of life and sustainable development. The leaders and practitioners shared their opinion on the challenges and opportunities for GPT (Conference 1& 2, Part C). Financial sustainability seems to be the biggest problem, and they also admit these communities are unattractive by commercial tourism agencies, which provide them space to conduct charity programs or do business. In addition, they claimed they may also win support from the government as long as they could provide quality service to marginalized rural communities. While searching for GPT online, we developed a side-project to study their behavior on Sina-Weibo. We found that organizations share using Weibo to sharing information, build community and call for action (Paper 3 & 4, conference 3 & 4 Part C)

457413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
457413.value: In order to use our research findings to benefit the GPT organizations and the rural community, we have established collaborative relationship with several of the GPT organizations, helping them with program evaluation and program development. We have also established a research and training collaboration with the NGO 2.0 project (China University of Science and Technology, and MIT). In this new research collaboration, we will work with more grassroots organizations, including the GPT organizations, assessing their needs, and helping them to better mobilize resources from the society. Additionally, because many of the organizations in our sample use the Internet to mobilize resources and promote their programs, we have developed a new research area focusing on grassroots organization and new media. In our new project, we will identify how new technology is being used by NGOs, and how new technology influences the work impact of the nonprofit sector, as well as its relationship with other sectors in the society.

457413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
457413.value: This study is the first to map out the development of grassroots philanthropic tourism (GPT) in China. The study identified the major types of GPT organizations, the main areas and approaches of their work, and the potential benefits it may have on the participants, the rural community and the Chinese civil society sector. We argue that GPT is a new form of social development program, a new type of volunteering, and a new way of social participation. It not only brings resources from the city to the poverty-stricken rural areas, but also enhances the communications and interaction between the urban and rural areas. Currently, GPT faces challenges, but also have many opportunities. Using our findings, practitioners in the field can develop programs to help GPT organizations to maximize their benefits to the community.

458413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
458413.value: The aim of this study is to apply and extend the “local climate zone” (LCZ) classification to a high density city by focusing on the Hong Kong urban scenario, and to gain a better scientific understanding on the effects of high-density/compact urban building construction and development on their local climate. Since the late-1940s, fast urbanization has not only brought new urban immigrants, but has also gradually physically changed the urban spaces. It is well observed that differences in the urban morphology and geometry of sites can modify their local climatic conditions, and even form unique climatic features. Thus, describing the physical surface properties of sites in a scientific and precise way is important and necessary for urban climatic analysis, and subsequent application into urban development and town planning. In 2009 Iain Stewart and Tim Oke developed a comprehensive approach of LCZ classification by using a standardized and quantitative way to present the physical surface properties of sites and their local climate features (Stewart & Oke, 2009 & 2012). Studies have been done for low-density cities in Sweden, Canada and Japan. However, there has been no study yet to test and apply the LCZ method to high-density high-rise cities with complex topography. The whole classification system may underestimate the effects of high-density high-rise urban developments on their local climate, indeed the existing knowledge of LCZs needs to be extended for application to mega cities. And thus Hong Kong provides a good test of such conditions for the LCZ system Firstly, the proposed study will collect site metadata of urban morphology and land cover through field surveys with up to 30 local sites being visited. Secondly, on-site spot field measurements will be carried out to capture spatial variations in the local thermal environment. Thirdly, the study will employ the ENVI-met model simulation to get a comprehensive understanding of the thermal environment of each survey site. Then, the collected data and simulation results will be analysed to examine the effects of high-density urban development on the local climate and to develop a LCZ for Hong Kong. The research will contribute to scholarly understanding of the effects of high-density urban developments on their local climatic conditions. In practice, the findings will provide planners and governments with a useful and quantitative reference of high density sites and their local climatic features, which could guide them to create better climatic spatial planning for mega cities.

458413.label: Realisation of objectives
458413.value: For testing and applying the LCZ concept to high density cities by focusing on the Hong Kong urban scenario and its local climate, developing a new dataset for the LCZ of Hong Kong based on the collected data, and also providing a standard set of planning parameters of each defined sub-class of LCZ of Hong Kong for urban planners and government officials to guide and improve their design and decision making, the objectives have been achieved. In the first step, world-wide cases on the LCZ studies are reviewed to choose and develop a raster-based GIS method for Hong Kong high density urban environment. In the second step, urban planning information in 2009 version were collected from the Planning Department of Hong Kong Government and remote sensing images from 2013-2015 were also collected. Both sets of data are integrated and calculated in the GIS for conducting sensitivity test and analyzing urban morphological characteristics. Then, based on the findings of second step, LCZ classifications are developed and the corresponding map is also generated (Zheng, Y., Ren, C., Wang, R., Xu, Y., and et al, 2016; Wang, R., Ren, C., Cai, M., Xu, Y. and et al, 2016). For investigating the relationship between high density urban developments and its local climate, up to 30 sites will be selected to conduct on-site field surveys, field measurements and simulation studies, “How much, what and where” questions on Hong Kong high density urban development and its local climate will be answered, the objectives have been achieved. Air temperature, wind speed, relative humidity and globe temperature of 87 locations were measured. Furthermore, mean radiant temperature (Tmrt) was also calculated from a numerical modeling –SOLWEIG. The simulation results show that geometry plays an important role in intra-urban differences in summer daytime Tmrt (Lau, K., Ren, C., and Ng, E., 2016). Based on the collected data and information, physiological equivalent temperature (PET), a thermal comfort index and heat stress were also calculated to analyze the thermal comfort conditions. Both numerical simulation and geographical mapping approach were used for the estimation of the microclimatic spatial distribution pattern. Results show that the influence of urban morphology on the microclimatic spatial distribution is strong (Shi, Y., Ren, C., Zheng, Y. and Ng, E., 2016). Further climatic-design and applications were conducted to demonstrate the possible design strategies for improving living conditions of high density urban environment (Zheng, Y., Shi, Y., Ren, C. and Ng. E., 2016).

458413.label: Major findings and research outcome
458413.value: This study has presented a raster-based GIS method to develop a local climatic zone map for high density cities by using Hong Kong as a case study. Both numerical simulation and geographical mapping approach were used for the estimation of the microclimatic spatial distribution pattern. Furthermore, thermal comfort and heat stress study were conducted to understand the effect of urban geometry on local people. Results show that the influence of urban morphology on the microclimatic spatial distribution is strong. Further climatic-design and applications were conducted to demonstrate the possible design strategies for improving living conditions of high density urban environment. Four journal articles and three referred conference papers have been published based on this study. Two invited papers from Urban Climate are under review now. (See attachments in Part C)

458413.value: In this study, apart from using a raster-based GIS method, a satellite image –based method is also adopted to develop a local climatic zone map for Hong Kong. (Wang, R., Ren, C., Cai, M., Xu, Y. and et al, 2016). The cross-comparison study between two methods were conducted to understand their limitations and accuracy performance. Then, the learned experience can be introduced and applied to other high density cities, like those in the Pearl River Delta Region of China.

458413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
458413.value: This study proposes a raster-based GIS method to develop a local climatic zone map for Hong Kong and to analyses the impact of urban geometry on local urban climatic conditions. The study employs on-site measurement, numerical simulation and geographical mapping approach to estimate the microclimatic spatial distribution pattern. Furthermore, thermal comfort and heat stress analysis is conducted to understand the effect of urban geometry on local people. The results show that geometry plays an important role in intra-urban differences in summer daytime in Hong Kong. Thus, architects and urban designers should consider and understand more urban climatic information and situations when they are doing design. A case of climatic-design and application is conducted to demonstrate the possible design strategies for improving living conditions of high density urban environment.

458913.label: Project Title(Chinese)
458913.value: 香港亞熱帶紅樹林濕地生物圈-大氣的溫室氣體交換

458913.label: Project Objectives
458913.value: To quantify the magnitude of the annual biosphere-atmosphere exchange of greenhouse gases, including CO2 and CH4, from a subtropical mangrove ecosystem in Hong Kong; To investigate the diel, seasonal and inter-annual variability of CO2 and CH4 fluxes from the mangrove wetland; and To examine the influence of environmental parameters on the temporal variations of CO2 and CH4 exchange between the atmosphere and the mangrove ecosystem.

To examine the influence of environmental parameters on the temporal variations of CO2 and CH4 exchange between the atmosphere and the mangrove ecosystem.

458913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
458913.value: This proposed study aims to investigate the magnitude and environmental controls of the exchange of greenhouse gases, including carbon dioxide (CO2) and methane (CH4), between the biosphere and the atmosphere in a subtropical mangrove wetland in Hong Kong. Mangroves form one of the most carbon-rich types of forest in the tropics as well as being one of most productive ecosystems of the world. While mangroves are generally long-term sinks of atmospheric CO2, they are also potentially a large source of CH4 which is a very potent greenhouse gas over the short term. Thus, quantifying both the net CO2 uptake and CH4 emissions is essential for determining the overall contribution of mangrove ecosystems to atmospheric radiative forcing and climate change. The micrometeorological technique has numerous advantages over the biomass inventory and chamber approaches in estimating the net ecosystem exchange of greenhouse gases, but it has rarely been employed in mangrove wetlands compared to other ecosystems. Given the paucity of research on the overall biosphere-atmosphere exchange of greenhouse gases in mangrove ecosystems, this study intends to use a micrometeorological approach to: (a) quantify the annual net exchange of CO2 and CH4 from a subtropical mangrove wetland in Hong Kong; (b) investigate the temporal variability of mangrove CO2 and CH4 fluxes at the diel, seasonal and inter-annual time scales; and (c) examine the influence of environmental parameters on the temporal variations of CO2 and CH4 exchange between the atmosphere and the mangrove ecosystem. An eddy covariance system consisting of a sonic anemometer and fast response gas analyzers will be set up in the Mai Po mangrove forest to measure the net ecosystem exchange of CO2 and CH4 quasi-continuously and non-invasively for three years. In addition, ancillary measurements of various environmental parameters will be made to assist in the interpretation of flux data. The results obtained in this proposed study will shed light on the role of subtropical mangroves in mitigating climate change, and provide baseline data for assessing the impacts of mangrove degradation and restoration on contemporary CO2 and CH4 fluxes. Moreover, the relationships established between gas fluxes and their environmental controls can be used to optimize management practices to minimize the adverse climatic impacts of mangroves, as well as parameterize biogeochemical models of mangroves to predict the effects of perturbations on greenhouse gas fluxes. Furthermore, the long-term flux data set generated can be used for collaborative regional and global synthesis of ecosystem carbon exchange. 本計劃以香港一亞熱帶紅樹林濕地為研究地點，旨在調查溫室氣體﹝包括二氧化碳及甲烷﹞在生物圈與大氣間交換的強度及環境控制因子。 紅樹林是熱界地區其中一種含碳最高的森林，也是全球其中一個生產力最高的生態系統。雖然紅樹林長期而言一般為大氣中二氧化碳的匯，但它們也有潛力成為一個龐大的甲烷源。由於甲烷短期是個強效的溫室氣體，因此在評估紅樹林生態系統對輻射強迫力及氣候變化的整體貢獻時，有需要同時量化二氧化碳的淨吸收及甲烷的釋放。微氣象法在估算生態系統溫室氣體通量上，雖比生物量調查法及箱法有很多優勢，但它很少被應用於紅樹林濕地上。 由於至今仍缺乏關於紅樹林生態系統生物圈與大氣間溫室氣體通量的研究，本研究旨在透過微氣象法以：﹝甲﹞量化香港一亞熱帶紅樹林濕地二氧化碳及甲烷的年淨通量；﹝乙﹞調查紅樹林二氧化碳及甲烷通量在日夜、季節及年際的時間變化；及﹝丙﹞調查環境因子對紅樹林二氧化碳及甲烷通量時間變化的影響。本研究會於米埔紅樹林設立一套包括聲波風速計及氣體分析儀的渦度相關系統，用三年時間連續及非侵入性地測量溫室氣體通量。另外，本研究亦會測量一些輔助環境參數以協助通量數據的詮釋。 本研究所得的結果有助進一步了解亞熱帶紅樹林於緩解氣候變化的角色，及提供重要的基線數據以評估紅樹林退化及復修對二氧化碳及甲烷通量的影響。另外，本研究建立的氣體通量及其環境控制的關係，能協助優化紅樹林管理以減低其對氣候的不良影響，及設定紅樹林生物地球化學模型的參數以預測干擾活動對溫室氣體通量的影響。本研究所建立的長期通量數據庫亦可用於生態系統碳通量區域及全球性的綜合分析。

458913.label: Realisation of objectives
458913.value: This project had three main objectives, which had to be addressed by primary data collected by an eddy covariance system established in a subtropical mangrove ecosystem in Hong Kong. Since the proposed study site was located in a Site of Special Scientific Interest, approval had to be sought from relevant authorities for establishing an environmental monitoring tower. The whole process took longer than expected, owing to various technical and administrative challenges of setting up a tall tower on very soft sediments that could comply with the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance. Our team eventually overcame all the hurdles and successfully established the eddy covariance tower in early 2016. Since then, we were able to measure the exchange of CO2 and CH4 quasi-continuously at our mangrove study site for more than two years, and subsequently used the high-frequency data to produce an estimate of the annual budgets of CO2 and CH4 fluxes in the subtropical mangrove ecosystem. Also, using the unique, large data set collected by our half-hourly flux measurements, we were able to examine the temporal variability of CO2 and CH4 fluxes at multiple temporal scales, ranging from diel changes over a 24-hour period, seasonal changes over a full year, to inter-annual changes over two study years. Furthermore, based on the high temporal resolution data set of various environmental parameters that we measured simultaneously with gas fluxes in the field, we were able to identify the key biophysical drivers of the temporal variations of CO2 and CH4 exchange in the subtropical mangrove ecosystem.

458913.label: Major findings and research outcome
458913.value: We found that our subtropical mangrove site on one hand was a significant CO2 sink sequestering about 758-890 g CO2-C m-2 year-1 over the study period, while on the other hand was a net CH4 source emitting about 11 g CH4-C m-2 year-1. Hence, the overall climatic impacts of mangrove wetlands should take into account the exchange of both CO2 and CH4 with the atmosphere. CO2 flux showed a clear diurnal pattern, with the maximum gross primary production and net CO2 uptake being observed at noon. CH4 flux also a distinct diurnal trend with a higher emission from noon to late afternoon. Seasonally, we found that our mangrove had a greater mean net CO2 uptake during the dry season than wet season, in contrary to the conventional wisdom that ecosystems would sequester more atmospheric CO2 in the wet seasons owing to a greater availability of sunlight and moisture. This was partly because of a significant increase in ecosystem respiration during the warmer wet season that led to considerable CO2 loss, as well as an increase in salinity during the dry season that supported greater photosynthetic activity of mangrove plants. We also observed a significantly higher mean CH4 emissions during the wet seasons than the dry seasons in our mangrove site, possibly because of a higher temperature and lower salinity that supported CH4 production. We observed inter-annual variability of CO2 fluxes in our mangrove sites, with annual CO2 flux in the second year being about 15% lower than the first year, in response to changes in temperature and solar radiation. In contrast, inter-annual variations of CH4 fluxes were rather small. We found that light intensity, air temperature, salinity, tidal level and vapor pressure deficit played a role in governing temporal variations in CO2 flux, while soil temperature, salinity and tidal level would control the variations in CH4 flux. These findings have been presented in a number of international conferences, and the results of CO2 fluxes have been published in Agricultural and Forest Meteorology, a top journal in the field of forestry (Liu & Lai, 2019).

458913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
458913.value: Our research has generated a unique and valuable data set of CO2 and CH4 in subtropical estuarine mangrove ecosystems. We are sharing our data set with the international flux community to work collaboratively on data synthesis work over a broader spatial scale to examine the large-scale variability of greenhouse gas fluxes among global wetlands. We also hope to continue operating our eddy covariance tower as far as practicable to generate a long-term flux data set, which would be useful for examining the temporal changes in ecosystem functions and evaluating the influence of different kinds of disturbance events on mangrove carbon fluxes. Our data set of ecosystem-scale CO2 and CH4 fluxes could also stimulate further work in investigating the process-level greenhouse gas dynamics in various ecosystem components of mangroves.

458913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
458913.value: This study examine the magnitude and controlling factors of CO2 and CH4 exchange between the subtropical mangrove and the atmosphere. Our results showed that mangroves were able to remove CO2 from the atmosphere in mitigating climate change, but at the same time emit CH4, another potent greenhouse gas, into the atmosphere in contributing to climate warming. Understanding the relative rates of CO2 uptake and CH4 release is thus essential for thoroughly assessing the role of mangrove wetlands in affecting our future climate. Also, the rates of CO2 and CH4 fluxes in mangroves were found to vary considerably over time from diurnal to seasonal scales. The temporal variations of CO2 and CH4 exchange in mangroves were controlled by various environmental factors, such as light intensity, air temperature, water salinity, and tidal level.

459013.label: Project Title(Chinese)
459013.value: 在學校正規教育中實施建構式網上遊戲化學習：教師促進策略設計為本研究

459013.label: Project Objectives
459013.value: To design teacher facilitation strategies in implementing COGBLe in formal curriculum teaching in different classroom contexts; To enact, analyze, and revise the strategies through authentic classroom implementation; To construct principles (meta-design) and practices (contextual-based) of teacher facilitation in implementing COGBLe in formal curriculum teachings in school education.
rows: To design teacher facilitation strategies in implementing COGBLe in formal curriculum teaching in different classroom contexts;
To enact, analyze, and revise the strategies through authentic classroom implementation;
To construct principles (meta-design) and practices (contextual-based) of teacher facilitation in implementing COGBLe in formal curriculum teachings in school education.

459013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
459013.value: The aim of this proposed study is to develop teacher facilitation principles and practices for constructivist online game-based learning (COGBLe) when it is adopted in formal curriculum teaching in school education. The study is set against the backdrop of the pervasive discussion of harnessing online games for providing school-aged students with new constructivist learning opportunities. The focus of the domain has placed largely on exploiting online games into another type of technology-enhanced student-centric environment. Teacher facilitation is usually absent in the process of COGBLe. Although constructivist education emphasizes an active, self-regulated student role, literature spells out that teacher support is always a vital component inside. There should be no exemption to COGBLe. Upon the theoretical foundation, we proposed VISOLE – Virtual Interactive Student-Oriented Leaning Environment, a teaching framework for implementing COGBLe in formal school education. We also developed a multi-player online game, Farmtasia, for teaching a four-week theme-based module, Agriculture, in the formal curriculum of senior secondary Geography education in Hong Kong. In this study, we will adopt a design-based research paradigm. Upon our previous work of VISOLE, we (researchers) will collaborate with practitioners (teachers) to investigate what and how teachers should do in order to facilitate their students in COGBLe. Data collection with mixed-methods will span two years, involving three Geography teachers and their classes respectively from three different secondary schools from three different academic bands in Hong Kong. Adopting VISOLE as an initial teaching framework, each of them will teach their students the four-week Agriculture module with Farmtasia in two consecutive school years. During the study, according to our ongoing analysis and their formative experiences as a COGBLe facilitator, we and the teachers will work together to design, enact, and refine their strategies for facilitating their students in COGBLe in authentic classroom contexts. The iterative cycles of analysis and refinement will enable us to develop teacher facilitation principles (meta-design) and practices (context-based) for implementing COGBLe in formal curriculum teaching in school education. Prior scholarship has ignored largely the facilitation role of teachers in COGBLe. We address that shortfall. The proposed study will contribute to what and how teacher should do in order to facilitate their students in the course of COGBLe in formal curriculum teaching settings. It will advance the knowledge of adopting COGBLe in formal school education, which is of theoretical and practical significance to research on appropriating online games for educational use. 本研究的目的是為在學校正規教育中實施基於建構主義的網上遊戲化學習（Constructivist Online Game-based Learning，簡稱COGBLe）提出教師促進的原則和實踐策略。 以網上遊戲為學生提供新的建構式學習機會是當今資訊科技敎育領域其中一熱點。然而，相關的研究大多著重如何利用更新的技術將網上遊戲開發成為另一種以學習者為中心的自主學習環境，而在COGBLe的過程中，教師的促進作用經常被忽略。儘管建構主義強調主動的、自我導向的學生角色，但它同時指出教師的支持也是關鍵的組成部分，在COGBLe中也不例外。在理論研究基礎上，我們提出了「虛擬互動學生為本學習環境」（Virtual Interactive Student-Oriented Learning Environment，簡稱VISOLE），將它作為在學校正規教育中實施COGBLe的教學框架。另外，我們跟據香港高中地理科其中以農業為主題的四星期正規課程，開發了一個建構式網上遊戲「農場狂想曲」（Farmtasia）。 本研究中，我們將採取設計為本研究範式。基於已有的VISOLE研究經驗，我們（研究者）將與實踐者（教師）協作來探究教師們「應做什麼」和「如何做」才能促進學生們在COGBLe中的學習。本研究將以混合方式進行為期兩年的數據收集，研究對象為香港三個不同學術等級的中學的三名地理科教師和他們所授課的班別。每一位教師都會採用VISOLE作為一個初始的教學框架，在連續兩個學年裡，用Farmtasia來教授相關的正規課程。在研究過程中，根據持續的分析和教師作為COGBLe促進者的形成性體驗，我們將會與教師一同設計、實施和優化他們的策略以促進學生的學習。分析和優化的循環能夠幫助我們發展出教師促進的原則和實踐策略，以支持在學校教育的正規課程教學中實施COGBLe。 以往學術研究忽視了教師在COGBLe中的促進作用；我們將彌補這個的缺陷。本研究有助發掘在正規的課程教學情境中，教師「應做什麼」以及「如何做」以促進學生進行COGBLe。研究結果將有助發展COGBLe在學校正規教育中的應用，同時對於網上遊戲用與教育的研究具有重要的理論和實踐意義。

459013.label: Realisation of objectives
459013.value: The project objectives were fully achieved. We employed the four-stage design-based research (DBR) methodological approach (design, enactment, analysis, and redesign) with two iterative cycles to carrying out this project. The research participants included three secondary school teachers and 296 Grade-11 students. - Design We initially designed a pedagogic framework, VISOLE (Virtual Interactive Student-Oriented Learning Environment) to integrate COGBLe into formal learning and teaching in school education, emphasising the importance of teacher facilitation components, scaffolding and debriefing, respectively before, during and after the course of COGBLe. This framework is composed of three phases. In Phase 1, the teacher scaffolds students with initial abstract knowledge related to the subject matter that the game intends to cover. The pedagogic activities in Phases 2 and 3 are crossed together. Phase 2 engages students in COGBLe in which they shape the development of the “virtual world” therein. All tasks in this “world” are authentic and open-ended in nature. Students should acquire new knowledge on their own from other additional learning resources in order to accomplish the tasks. Moreover, after the completion of each gaming round, they are required to write a short journal to reflect on what they have learned. In Phase 3, the teacher observes students’ gaming at the backend and extracts cases taking place in the game for debriefing students during and after the course of gaming. With the VISOLE framework, we developed an online multiplayer game based on the Agriculture module in the Grade-11 Geography curriculum in Hong Kong. To support students to do the reflection during Phase 2 of VISOLE, a blogging gadget was embedded into the game. After each round of gameplay, it will pop up to remind students to do reflective blogging. Also, to facilitate teachers to conduct the debriefing work during Phase 3 of VISOLE, a teacher console for retrieving students’ gaming data was integrated into the game system. Teachers can use the console to observe and capture students’ game-play proceedings in the form of video playback. - Enactment Secondary schools in Hong Kong are categorised into three academic bands based on their students’ academic achievement. Bands A, B, and C are respectively the top, middle, and bottom bandings. In this DBR, we collaborated with three Geography teachers respectively from the three different school bandings to implement COGBLe in their teaching practice in two consecutive school years. Initially, the 16 teachers who had participated in our early pilot study were put into the selection scope. Finally, three female teachers were selected because: (i) they were teaching at different school bandings; (ii) their academic background and years of teaching experience were similar, (iii) the number of students in their Geography classes were comparable, and (iv) the three schools were using the same Geography textbook. For writing convenience, School A and Teacher A, School B and Teacher B, as well as School C and Teacher C are used to denote the corresponding schools and teachers at Band A, Band B, and Band C. The first enactment (in the first research cycle) was conducted in the school year of 2014. Adopting VISOLE as an initial pedagogic framework and the game, Teachers A, B, and C implemented COGBLe to teach their Grade-11 classes in 2014 the Agriculture module. The number of student participants was 99 (34 from School A, 32 from School B, and 33 from School C). During the first enactment, we carried out the control manipulation, i.e., each teacher also taught another Grade-11 class (i.e., a control group) the same module with the usual textbook-based teaching approach. The number of student participants in the control manipulation was also 99 (34 from School A, 32 from School B, and 33 from School C). The second enactment (in the second research cycle) was conducted in the school year of 2015. Adopting the optimised VISOLE framework and the revised game (see the Redesign section), Teachers A, B, and C again implemented COGBLe to teach their Grade-11 classes in 2015 the Agriculture module. The total number of student participants in this enactment was 98 (35 from School A, 32 from School B, and 31 from School C). During both the Enactment stages, we closely observed the implementation process in Schools A, B, and C. At the end of the Enactment stage in each cycle, in each school we conducted a knowledge test. The validity of the test and marking scheme was scrutinised by a review panel composed of nine in-service Geography teachers possessing 10 to 16 years of teaching experience. - Analysis Apart from analysing the quantitative data collected via the knowledge test in each research cycle, we carried out in-depth interviews with the teachers and students to understand more about their experience in facilitating/ pursuing COGBLe right after the first and second Enactment stages. The further collected qualitative data were useful for triangulating the effectiveness of the teacher facilitation strategies implemented and optimised in this DBR. We leveraged Maxwell’s qualitative analysis approach supplemented with Creswell’s thematic development technique of theme layering and interrelating to analyse the qualitative data. - Redesign The Redesign stage took place right after the end of the Analysis stage in the first research cycle. On the technical aspect, we integrated a number of non-player characters (NPCs) into the game as “virtual mentors” (e.g., Orchardist, Agricultural Biochemistry Specialist, etc.) to scaffold non-gamer students in the gaming process. The existence of these new NPCs in the game can be “by default” or “by injection” through the teacher console in a timely manner. Also, the blogging gadget in the game was revamped to support both text-based and audio-based blogging. The revised game was pilot-tested before the second enactment. On the pedagogic aspect, we discussed the findings obtained in the first research cycle with the three teachers. Then, we worked together to derive new interventions for optimising the existing facilitation strategies in VISOLE in accordance with their school settings.

459013.label: Major findings and research outcome
459013.value: 1. Impromptu gaming, arbitrary gaming and halt gaming are three common impeding phenomena emerging from the implementation process when COGBLe is adopted in the context of formal schooling [Research Output 1]. Students’ gaming experience, gaming interest, examination orientedness, and emerging emotion are the factors leading to these impeding phenomena. 2. Scaffolding and debriefing are the two important theoretical principles for deriving teacher facilitation strategies when COGBLe is adopted in the context of formal schooling [Research Outputs 3 and 5]. 3. The VISOLE (Phase 1: Scaffolding; Phase 2: COGBLe & Reflection; Phase 3: Debriefing) is a useful meta-design framework for framing what and how teachers should do in order to optimise students’ COGBLe process [Research Outputs 3 and 5]. 4. The effectiveness of using virtual mentors (non-player characters) to scaffold non-gamer learners in the course of game-based learning is desirable [Research Output 4]. The term “non-gamer learners” refers to students who have no or very little prior experience and interest in online gaming. 5. Specific teacher facilitation practices are needed to optimize the VISOLE framework in different school settings [Research Output 5]. In a high academic-achieving class, the practices include (i) equipping students with the gameplay knowledge via in-class practice and flipped video; (ii) activating all virtual mentors for scaffolding students throughout the game; (iii) assigning the gaming and blogging tasks as formal assignments for formative assessment; (iv) providing students with just-in-time encouragement for releasing their frustration and anxiety. In a middle academic-achieving class, the practices include (i) leveraging gamer students’ proficiency to support non-gamer students in launching the game; (ii) injecting the virtual mentors into the game in a just-in-time manner; (iii) allowing students to do either text-based or audio-based blogging; (iv) facilitating group-based discussion in which students share their gaming and learning experience. In a bottom academic-achieving class, the practices include (i) video-recording the scaffolding lessons and putting the clips onto the web for students’ self-access; (ii) de-activating all virtual mentors in the game; (iii) asking students to do audio-based blogging; (iv) inviting students to share their ongoing gaming strategies in front of the class. 6. The idea of harnessing COGBLe in formal schooling is still novel in Hong Kong [Research Output 2]. It is important to formulate effective strategies to (i) introducing this educational innovation into pre-service and in-service teacher training programmes and (ii) addressing teachers' concerns about adopting this educational innovation in practice with articulated support.

459013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
459013.value: The Hawthorne effect is a possible limitation of this research. There is a need for further investigating the substantiality of the pedagogic effect of VISOLE (as well as the formulated teacher facilitation strategies) on the participating students when they learn with VISOLE again. Then, it will involve developing more VISOLE games for teaching other modules in the Geography curriculum, or even other topics in other subjects. Using non-player characters (NPCs) as virtual mentors to scaffold students is proved to be effective in this project. However, to avoid lowering the "playability" of the game, it is worthy of further technical research effort on making the NPCs more "intelligent" with AI technology, so that they will only appear at critical moments and in a just-in-time manner during the gameplay (rather than manually injected by teachers). The idea of harnessing COGBLe in formal school education in Hong Kong or many Asian countries is still novel. For example, most teachers in Hong Kong are "non-gamers" and hesitate about the pedagogic effectiveness of COGBLe. It is important to further study effective approaches to (1) introducing COGBLe into pre-service and in-service teacher training programmes and (2) addressing teachers' concerns about adopting COGBLe in practice with articulated interventions.

459013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
459013.value: The integration of COGBLe into formal school education and the importance of teacher facilitation in the process of COGBLe have received very little attention in the field. This project alerts the researchers to the gaps, as well as addressing the shortfalls. Specifically, it answers two important questions—(i) what and (ii) how school teachers should do when implementing COGBLe in the context of formal curriculum teaching and learning. It contributes to the development of principles and practices of teacher facilitation in COGBLe and advances the knowledge of harnessing COGBLe in school education. The research findings provide: - game-based learning researchers and educational game developers with scholarly and pragmatic insights into designing games for integrating COGBLe into formal teaching and learning, as well as framing pedagogic strategies for implementing their COGBLe initiatives in different school settings; - teacher educators (of both pre-service teacher education and in-service teacher professional development) with a practical reference and a real example for formulating pedagogic training that prepares teachers to adopt COGBLe in teaching and learning in practice; - education policy makers and school administrators with an empirical basis for formally supporting and introducing COGBLe into teaching and learning of statutory school curricula.
