459213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
459213.value: This Project aims to analyze the mitigation of constitutional problems between Hong Kong and Mainland China since July 1, 1997, with special emphasis on the role of the Committee for the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region under the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress (NPCSC-CBL) – the constitutionally-sanctioned body to perform just this function. Enacted in accordance with the Sino-British Joint Declaration of 1984, the Basic Law unprecedentedly provided for the absorption of Hong Kong – a long-time British dependency, international financial center and common law jurisdiction, into the People’s Republic of China – the world’s most populous country and last major Communist Party-state. Although implementing the Mainland’s preferences for sovereign unity, the provisions of the Basic Law safeguarding civil liberties and promising universal suffrage elections have inspired an alternative concept of constitutional order supported by the senior courts, opposition parties, and large numbers of citizens. In light of these developments, this Project devotes its attention to the CBL, the official constitutional connective issues between the two jurisdictions. The CBL is an important yet operationally secretive body, whose opinion the NPCSC is obligated to consult whenever it wishes to invalidate Hong Kong legislation, extend Mainland laws to Hong Kong, and interpret, and even amend the Basic Law. Surprisingly, no article or book has ever been dedicated to the study of the CBL in its own right, and in dispersed commentaries, scholars sharply disagreed on its importance: on the one hand, it has been accused for being a pawn of the regime; on the other hand, it has been recognized as being influential in publicly shaping the meaning of the Basic Law and injected common law knowledge into the NPCSC’s own decision-making. Addressing this gap of the literature, this Project seeks to uncover, empirically and inter-disciplinarily, the role of the CBL by bringing the insights from the economic analysis of law and positive political economy literatures to develop a stylized principal-agent theory to explain and predict the CBL’s trajectory, and then providing it with evidential support through research interviews and a comprehensive review of primary and secondary materials. This Project will yield important insights on how to minimize cross-border constitutional friction, and on the prospects of entrenching constitutionalism in China. 本計劃旨在分析自一九九七年七月一日起，香港與中國大陸之間的憲制問題的緩解，並著重研究全國人民代表大會常務委員會香港特別行政區基本法委員會在此所扮演的角色。根據一九八四年的中英聯合聲明所制定的基本法，史無前例地，促成了作為世上人口最多的國度和最後一個主要的共產黨國家的中華人民共和國，對長期身為英國海外領地、國際金融中心、普通法管轄區的香港，行使主權。基本法的條款，既落實中國對主權統一的主張，亦保障香港的公民權利和承諾推動普選；後者衍生了一種與中國理解不同的，但廣為高級法院、反對黨、大批市民所支持的憲制概念。基於上述發展，本計劃將聚焦於作為連結兩地憲制事務的官方組織的基本法委員會。基本法委員會是一個重要但神秘的機構；全國人大常委有義務在發回香港法例、延申全國性法律到香港、解釋或修改基本法前，諮詢其意見。然而，現有文獻卻意料之外地沒有集中討論此機構。學者們卻在散佈在其他文獻有關基本法委員會的討論，對其重要性產生嚴重的分歧。有指基本法委員會不過是政權的傀儡，同時也有意見認為，委員會對公眾了解基本法的意義上角色舉足輕重，並且為全國人大常委的決策過程注入了普通法的元素。有見及此，本計劃將嘗試從實證和跨學科研究的角度了解基本法委員會的角色，並以法律經濟學、實證政治經濟學的原理，建構相關的主理人／代理人理論、訪談和對主要和次要資料全面分析等方法為理論提供證據支持。本計劃有望為減少兩地憲制磨擦、在中國建設憲政，提供新視角。

459213.label: Realisation of objectives
459213.value: Objective 1: Constitutional problems between Hong Kong and Mainland China mainly revolve largely around electoral reform toward universal suffrage. Both sides to the democratization dilemma of Hong Kong share an overarching interest in avoiding the total breakdown of coordination, yet tensions persist over their clashing preferences for which particular outcome – more or less electoral competition – they ought to converge on. This project has demonstrated the shortcomings of the Basic Law as a coordination device and has examined the strengths and weaknesses of the three major focal point generators in the Basic Law framework: the Hong Kong courts, the Basic Law Committee (CBL), and the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress (NPCSC). It posited that the unilateral and uncompromising injection of its preference for uncompetitive elections into Hong Kong’s constitutional law pivotally contributed to the waning of the NPCSC’s focal power; after all, no focal point can elicit acquiescence from those thoroughly hostile to its essence. Regarding the Umbrella Movement, this project highlighted the roles played by the above three bodies in achieving (or not) some convergence of expectations amongst the disputants. It has illustrated how the Umbrella Movement was the fallout of a coordination failure stemming from a hardening of strategies on both sides, and from a collapse of the focal power of the NPCSC and its Decisions. The surprisingly bloodless winding-up of the Umbrella Movement practically resulted from the intervention of the prestigious High Court not the CBL. The electoral reform process in Hong Kong is now a stalemate, which may not last indefinitely, however, given the erosion of the coordinating power of the Basic Law and of NPCSC Decisions as their psychological salience as focal points in constitutional conflicts diminishes with the growing propensity of both sides to act uncompromisingly. The saga of the Umbrella Movement indicates that Beijing will not offer any substantial concession toward electoral competition in Hong Kong, even in face of unprecedented popular mobilization. In the absence of any viable focal points, it is unlikely that the Chinese Party-state and Hong Kong community, the latter of which increasingly showing localist or even separatist tendencies, will be able to avoid converging on the worst of all outcomes in their coordination. All things being equal, chances of a constitutional breakthrough will remain low, and that the political stalemate will stick for the foreseeable future. Objective 2: This objective is largely met. During the drafting of the Basic Law, even several Hong Kong drafters apprehended a need to prevent the NPCSC interpreting the Basic Law at will, lest Hong Kong’s autonomy be compromised. China’s lack of a constitutional court moved Hong Kong intellectuals to seek out an independent institution that could fulfill such a role. Victor Sit, then-senior lecturer of Geography at the University of Hong Kong, was in January 1986 among the first Hong Kong public figures expressly to propose to the establishment of a “Hong Kong Basic Law Committee” to participate in interpreting Basic Law provisions relating to the Chinese central government with finality. By April the same year, the relevant subgroup of the Drafting Committee had begun to conceive of a “special committee” consisting of Hong Kong members but under the National People’s Congress to do just that. By December 1987 a consensus appears to have emerged amongst the drafters that the NPCSC should be obliged to consult the CBL before rendering important decisions regarding the Basic Law. According to drafter Rayson Huang, the Committee was meant to countervail, in case of conflict, the Basic Law’s overarching emphasis on “One China”. The perception became ascendant in Hong Kong that the CBL was a means to protect the region’s autonomy with a new jurisprudence that would join up the divergent common law and socialist traditions of both sides. Enthusiasm in Hong Kong for the CBL waxed so great that mainland drafters were forced to reject explicitly the most aggressive proposal of all, to legally obligate the NPCSC to adopt each and every recommendation made by the CBL. After the 1989 Tiananmen Square Incident, there emerged suggestions for the CBL to function as a European-style constitutional court consisting of an equal number of mainland Chinese and Hong Kong judges. The final text of the Basic Law vests the CBL with four formal competences to be consulted by the NPCSC in four significant domains of possible conflict between Hong Kong and Beijing. Objective 3: This objective is largely met. This project demonstrated that the CBL epitomizes a prototypic form of constitutional supervision in China. But it turned out that China’s top leadership has taken the narrowest interpretation of the legal provisions on the CBL, seeing the Committee as nothing more than an ordinary non-permanent work committee. And yet such narrow interpretation of the CBL’s role, as well as full control over its composition, has yet to prevent state leaders from delegating greater discretion to the Committee. Being barred from conducting public hearings, publishing its proceedings, and staffed by individuals most of whom are not full-timers, the CBL has not been given any opportunity to produce any focal opinions on the Basic Law as a cohesive corporate actor. And the Committee appeared to have never been given the requisite time and resources to hammer out substantial opinions separately from drafts already prepared by the NPCSC. Besides, many CBL members have never sought to distinguish themselves from partisan politicians or NPCSC bureaucrats. No introspective understanding is in evidence that they ought to abstain from taking part in controversial public debates, lest they be drawn into taking sides. Indeed, the lack of public visibility, a cohesive corporate identity, and dedicated full-time members are key obstacles that must be addressed and eradicated by any serious proposal for a workable Constitutional Supervision Committee in China. Objective 4: This objective is largely met. The role of the CBL in various Interpretations and during the Umbrella Movement has been documented by the research outputs of this project. It was suggested that there was no room for the emergence of any custom tilting the NPCSC towards endorsing every recommendation made by the CBL. Objective 5: This objective is moderately met. The core insight of this project is that the only way for the CBL to play an enhanced role in mitigating cross-border tensions is for it to become a salient focal point for coordination. Whilst a minimalist role is not indefensible as a matter of black-letter law, the marginal position of the CBL in mitigating mainland China-Hong Kong constitutional tensions in many ways represented a lost opportunity for experimenting with constitutional supervision: the CBL has not even been used as a device to give politically motivated Basic Law Interpretations greater procedural and legal legitimacy. And if China is unwilling to experiment with constitutional enforcement with the CBL in Hong Kong, there is a strong possibility that it will not, in the foreseeable future, be willing to entertain any proposals for a specialized constitutional body, even one with highly circumscribed powers. After all, “One Country, Two Systems” has long been utilized by Beijing as a field laboratory to test novel ideas and policies before they are applied to mainland China. The conclusions of this project are thus pessimistic.

459213.label: Major findings and research outcome
459213.value: The protracted constitutional conflicts between the Chinese state and Hong Kong society over the pace and form of democratization have become a source of political instability. This project analyzed these dynamics by analyzing the two sides as locked in a coordination dilemma: both have important common interests to coordinate with each other, but both rank in divergent ways their preferences for and against introducing competitive electoral arrangements into Hong Kong. It was shown how the unwillingness of either side to compromise has caused the gradual breakdown of coordination as focal points like the Basic Law have eroded, culminating in the Umbrella Revolution of 2014, the largest and longest-lasting popular movement in Hong Kong history. The bloodless ending of the Movement is chronicled, along with the persistence of political stalemate in this highly anomalous polity, known throughout the world for its combination of genuine civil liberties with authoritarian rule. Recurrent proposals to establish a constitutional supervisory committee have been pertinaciously rejected in spite of widespread recognition of the Chinese Constitution’s ineffectiveness. And yet, the Hong Kong Basic Law Committee has long epitomized in practice a prototypic form of constitutional supervision. Vested with quasi-judicial competences, the Committee seemed destined for a central role under the “One Country, Two Systems” arrangement. The tight secrecy imposed on its proceedings and the suppression of its potential to act consistently and with a distinct identity have decisively undermined the Committee’s ability to modulate constitutional tensions by way of coordinating expectations of the Basic Law’s proper meaning. The experience of the Basic Law Committee reveals the recalcitrance of the Party-state toward constitutional interpretation by any specialised body, even one whose powers are heavily circumscribed and whose membership is tightly controlled.

459213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
459213.value: This project uncovered the potential of using the law and coordination perspective to study Hong Kong constitutional dilemmas and the roles that the CBL and the courts can play in promoting conflicting parties to converge on mutually beneficial outcomes. The PI will further develop this approach in a number of follow-up articles.

459213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
459213.value: Generally speaking, this project is about the constitutional disputes between members of Hong Kong society and the Chinese government after 1997. Although both sides are keen on preserving Hong Kong's stability and prosperity, each of them has a different view on the pace of electoral reform, among others. In particular, this project focused on the Committee for the Basic Law under the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (CBL), which uniquely consists of an equal number of Hong Kong and mainland members, and which should be consulted every time an important constitutional decision has to be made. It discovered that the CBL could have played a useful role in coordinating constitutional disputes by generating salient focal points for disputing sides. And yet Beijing has taken a narrow reading of the CBL's power, subsuming it as part of its political decisionmaking process, giving it no special prominence in the resolution of constitutional dilemmas. The CBL's lack of consequential power is therefore a lost opportunity in the One Country Two Systems experiment. This project suggests that as both sides hardened their positions in the aftermath of the polarizing Umbrella Movement, the prospect of successful coordination under focal points like the Basic Law, the Standing Committee, and the CBL is dim.

459413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
459413.value: Chinese courts have shifted their priorities away from adjudicatory justice towards mediatory justice since 2003. As a result, an increasing number of cases accepted by the courts are settled, rather than adjudicated. However, a high settlement rate does not necessarily indicate the success of the program. What is the legitimacy of judicial mediation? What are the main goals and values of judicial mediation? How is the policy shift toward mediation reflected in the actual judicial practice? How do we evaluate the success of the current judicial mediation program in China? These and other questions relating to judicial mediation in China need to be answered in order to have a well-informed and reasoned understanding of the current Chinese promotion and practice of judicial mediation. This project is set to stimulate ideas for the construction of an effective judicial mediation system in China, based on a combination of theoretical analysis and empirical study. First, it will investigate the current status of judicial mediation through documentary study. Second, the theoretical analysis will be tested by empirical evidence, through on-site investigations at three basic courts in different regions of China at different stages of economic developments. A series of interviews will be conducted with judges in order to obtain detailed and first-hand knowledge on the actual practice, successful experience and existing obstacles of China’s current judicial mediation program. Last, it will analyze the results of empirical findings and develop a theoretical framework of judicial mediation in China. This project fits timely with China’s social needs. The implications of this project will be significant, not only for policy-making and judicial practice but also for academic research. It will make important contribution to the construction of a theoretical framework of judicial mediation in China. The research findings will provide the Chinese authorities with theoretical basis for assessing the effects of civil justice reform and finding the institutional legitimacy of courts, all of which is of great significance in their long-term policy making. Lastly, the research findings will have important impacts for the mediation developments in Hong Kong, in light of its current civil justice reform. Given the important role of China in the world arena, the Chinese model of mediation can provide important reference for the development of ADR and restorative justice in other jurisdictions. 2003年以来，中国法院的司法实践由审判正义向调解正义转换。因此，法院受理的大量案件以和解结案，而非审判结案。2013年8月，在最高法群众路线教育实践活动领导小组会议上，最高人民法院院长周强已指出片面追求结案率、调解率等指标的弊端。我们需要重新冷静的审视司法调解在中国当今社会的作用。司法调解的合法性是什么？司法调解的主要目的和价值是什么？政策上对于调解的态度转变是如何反应在司法实践中的？如何评估当前司法调解实践？我们需要回答以上和其他关于中国司法调解的问题,以更全面、客观的了解中国的司法调解实践。 这个研究项目企图通过理论和实务的研究，激发关于如何在中国建立有效的司法调解机制的一些想法。首先，调研者计划通过文献研究了解当前中国司法调解的现状。其次，调研者计划通过实证调查来审视理论分析的结果，实地考察三个在不同地区、处于不同经济发展阶段的法院。通过对法官的面对面采访来了解司法调解的实际操作情况、成功经验和现有问题。最后，调研者会分析实证考察的结果，并以此为基础来提出建设司法调解理论框架的主张。 这个研究项目密切结合中国当今的社会需求。其研究结果会对政策决定、司法实践和理论研究都有重要意义。该研究会为建设中国司法调解的理论框架作出重大贡献。研究结果可以为中国的权威对于法院的合法性认识提供理论基础，这对于他们的长期政策决定有着重要作用。最后，研究结果也会对香港当今的民事正义改革下调解的发展提供宝贵的素材。由于中国在世界舞台上发挥着重要的作用，中国的调解模式也可以为其他地区的替代式争端解决和恢复性正义的发展起到借鉴作用。

459413.label: Realisation of objectives
459413.value: The overall objectives of the project have been achieved. On the basis of a comprehensive literature review, the PI and her RA conducted on-sight investigations in June-July 2016 and conducted semi-structured in-depth interviews more than 30 judges from Xiamen Siming People's Court, Beijing Haidian People's Court, Beijing Chaoyang People's Court, Xian Intermediate People's Court, Xian Lantian People's Court and Xian Fanta People's Court. The above courts are selected because they represent divergent geographic locations (including Central and Western center-city as well as Southeast coastal area), and covers three different economic zones, so that the sample is reasonably representative of the current judicial mediation status in China. Most of the courts investigated are basic people’s courts, which represent 76.9% of the judicial personnel and 89.28% of accepted cases in courts at all level. We also interviewed judges from intermediate people’s court in order to test if there are any differences in the attitudes and practice of judicial mediation among different levels of courts. There is a reasonable diversity of seniority, years of experience and gender amongst the interviewed judges, so that the risk of bias is minimized. Some of the interviewed judges have at least ten years of experience in judicial mediation, who will be able to comment on the difference of judicial practice before and after the policy shift toward mediation in 2003 from their personal experience. Our research trip initially experiences some challenges, as such visits of an international nature have to be arranged from higher level of administration, even though the courts we contacted were interested in receiving us. Through several months of coordination, through the PI’s professional and personal contacts, through assistance of Beijing High People’s Court and Supreme People’s Court, and through the assistance of Liaison Office of the Central People's Government in the Hong Kong, all of our intended visits have been arranged, which generated satisfactory outcomes. Based on a combination of theoretical and empirical analysis, we have obtained detailed and first-hand knowledge on how judicial mediation actually works in China. The theorization of mediation practice appears to be challenging, given that the practice varies significantly based on individual’s personal experience and types of cases. We have attempted to overcome this challenge by (i) making a summary of over a hundred mediation cases (mostly from the published mediation cases), and (ii) summarizing the personal experiences shared by interviewed judges, in order to identify commonly used techniques and strategies and specific techniques and strategies adapted to specific types of disputes, so as to tease out some useful models of "best mediation practices". We have also identified existing obstacles of China’s current judicial mediation program based on the literature survey and on-site interviews. Apart from practical insights from judges who are front liners of judicial mediation practice, we have also interviewed the officials from the Legal Reform Office of the Supreme People’s Court, so as to get a better insight of the status and trends of judicial mediation in China from a national policy perspective. Based on the above empirical findings, and drawing on experiences in other jurisdictions, we have made proposals to improve judicial mediation system and put forward ideas to develop a theoretical framework of judicial mediation in China.

459413.label: Major findings and research outcome
459413.value: Since 2004, the Party and the courts have shifted their priority from adjudicatory back to mediatory justice, in line with the party-state commitment to a “socialist harmonious society”. The change of policy towards judicial mediation caused a steady increase of the percentage of civil cases that are concluded by mediation. The combine effect of the political pressure on court, the appraisal mechanism and sense of honor of judges, caused irrational competition in mediation rate in some court. Our research finds that there has been a conscious reflection on the “mediation heat” since the new director of SPC Zhou Qiang assumed office, and a more balanced approach is proposed. Judges are required to correctly handle the relationship between mediation and judgment. Judges should only prioritize mediation when the parties are willing to mediate and there is a chance to solve the dispute through mediation. The scope of mediation is limited to the family and neighborhood disputes, the disputes that lack clear law and regulation and situation when strictly application of the law may lead to unjust result. Furthermore, for those cases parties are unwilling to mediate and there is a need to provide guidance to the society, the court should prioritize judgment. Such a balanced policy approach seems to have affected the judiciary practice. Most of the interviewed judges expressed that they no longer feel the pressure to push for a settlement as a result of the policy change. Whether they have a preference towards mediation now mainly depends on the nature and type of the cases and the relationship and attitudes of the parties. Mediation at the appeal court appears to be more difficult when parties tend to focus on one disputing issue and have both intensified their positions after the first trial. The judges’ preference is also influenced by the individual’s personal background: the more senior judges with more life experience than legal training tend to have a strong preference towards mediation; while more junior judges who came only a few years after school with a strong legal training tend to prefer adjudication. Through on-sight investigations and face-to-face interviews, the PI has identified common elements required for a successful mediation, values of mediation, common techniques and strategies used by the judges during mediation, the typical process and outcomes of judicial mediation in China. Drawn on the experience from other jurisdiction and discussions with the judges and officers at the SPC, the PI also made proposals to improve the mediation system in China, to develop judicial mediation in the context of a comprehensive Multiplex Dispute Resolution System, to provide systemic accreditation and training of mediators, to explore innovative programs through pilot projects such as commission mediation, Specially-Invited Mediation, e-Mediation. The implications of China's experiences and lessons for Hong Kong's civil justice reform have also been discussed.

459413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
459413.value: The research findings can also have useful implications for judicial mediation programs in other jurisdictions. The PI has now moved to McGill University and has established some contacts with judges in Quebec, where interesting civil justice reform is taking place recently. She intends to expand this research by making a comparison between judicial mediation in China and that in Quebec.

459413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
459413.value: This study examined the current status of judicial mediation system in China, based on a combination of theoretical analysis and empirical study. On the basis of a comprehensive literature review, interviews with more than 30 judges from six courts located in three different cities, as well as interviews with the Supreme Court of China (“SPC”), the study finds that there a conscious reflection on the “mediation heat” since the new director of SPC Zhou Qiang assumed office, and a more balanced approach is proposed. Such change in policy has also affected the judicial practice, so that individual judges feel that can make a choice between mediation and adjudication based on the nature and type of disputes, as well as the attitudes and relationship of the parties. Their preference is also influenced by their personal background and trainings. The study further identified useful techniques and strategies in judicial mediation based on the successful experiences, and also made proposals to improve the judicial mediation system in China in the context of a comprehensive Multiplex Dispute Resolution System. Such research findings are significant, not only for policy-making and judicial practice but also for academic research.

459713.label: Project Title(Chinese)
459713.value: 政治公民參與在社交媒體的使用 —— 香港公民研究

459713.label: Project Objectives
459713.value: To derive an understanding of how Hong Kong citizens are using social media in their everyday lives, especially focusing on the domain of political and civic engagement. To develop a conceptually and empirically informed account of the role of social media in the development of political attitudes and values among citizens. To develop a conceptually and empirically informed account of the role of social media in the development of political attitudes and values among citizens.
To examine the impact of social media use on political and civic participation.

459713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
459713.value: The use of social media in Hong Kong has risen sharply in the past few years. By 2012, over half of the population was using the social network site (SNS) Facebook, a technology that has altered the way many people form relationships, communicate, and get information about politics and current affairs. One area in which SNSs has made an impact is in political and civic engagement. Hong Kong has in recent years witnessed several instances of citizen-initiated mass engagement, such as the movements against the Queen's Pier demolition and against the construction of the Express Rail Link, which were facilitated, to some degree, by SNSs. This continued in 2012 as people used SNSs to share information, express opinions, and gather support for actions related to the anti-national education protests and the Legislative Council Elections. The outcomes of these activities had varying degrees of success, but they highlight the utility of social media to bring together people with common views, provide a space for sharing information, and mobilize different kinds of actions with the aim of influencing government policy. Nevertheless, little research has been done in Hong Kong about the role of SNSs in facilitating people’s political and civic engagement. This project examines the dynamics of social media use, the development of political attitudes and values, and their impact on citizens’ political and civic participation. More specifically, it asks: • How and why are Hong Kong citizens using social media for political and civic engagement purposes? What characteristics differentiate users and non-users? • How does the use of social media affect the way citizens get information about politics and current affairs? What proportion of their news consumption comes from social media relative to other news channels? • How does the use of social media influence political attitudes and values, such as belief in one’s ability to influence society and political interest? • How do these attitudes and values influence citizens’ political and civic engagement? This project has high levels of social significance given the prominent use of social media in Hong Kong and its potential to increase participation in actions that can affect government policy and bring about social change. The findings can inform and be compared with similar research undertaken by overseas scholars in countries at different stages of democratic development to that in Hong Kong, and help identify similar and idiosyncratic uses of social media.

459713.label: Realisation of objectives
459713.value: Overall, the three objectives set out in this project have been achieved, as evidenced by the body of outputs the project has generated (documented in Part C). Objective #1 In particular, we now have a deeper understanding the ways Hong Kong citizens use social media for political and civic participation, encompassing both conventional political participation as well as non-conventional participation. Example: 1. Different uses of Hong Kong’s most popular social media platform (Facebook) Chan, M. (2016). Social Network Sites and Political Engagement: Exploring the Impact of Facebook Connections and Uses on Political Protest and Participation. Objective #2 This was achieved by synthesizing and integrating different theoretical models in the communication and psychology literature, and testing them empirically in different contexts (e.g. Hong Kong, Taiwan, and China). For example, variants of the cognitive mediation model, communication mediation model, OSROR, and SIMCA models were tested and were empirically shown to explain the process in which social media engenders and develops political attitudes, which subsequently affect participation tendencies. Examples: 1. Applying the SIMCA model from psychology and integrating it with social media: Chan, M. (2017). Media Use and the Social Identity Model of Collective Action: Examining the Roles of Online Alternative News and Social Media News. 2. Applying the OSROR model from political communication Chan, M., Chen, H.-T., & Lee, F. L. F. (2017). Examining the roles of mobile and social media in political participation: A cross-national analysis of three Asian societies using a communication mediation approach (Objective #3) Finally, the body of research clearly demonstrate that social media does have substantive influence on political and civic participation through its provision of information and connections with public actors that can mobilize citizens to act, particularly in elections and protests which occurred during the study period. Examples: 1. Examining voters’ willingness to talk on social media about elections Chan, M. (2018). Partisan strength and social media use among voters during the 2016 Hong Kong Legislative Council election: Examining the roles of ambivalence and disagreement. 2. The role of social media among Hong Kong youth in participating in the Umbrella Movement Lee, F. L. F., Chen, H.-T., & Chan, M. (2017). Social media use and university students' participation in a large-scale protest campaign: The case of Hong Kong's Umbrella Movement.

459713.label: Major findings and research outcome
459713.value: The body of output form this project has generated some core insights about the role of social media in Hong Kong and its influence Hong Kong politics and society. The key findings can be summarized as follows: - Social media has a positive impact on political and civic participation for the general population AND young people, such that greater use generally leads to more engagement. The stereotype that social media is used predominately only by young people is not supported from this project, which shows very high levels of social media use among the general population in their everyday lives. - Yet, different types of social media use have different kinds of effects. This is because social media is not only a source of information like traditional media, but also a networking and participatory media where individuals can make their voices heard among their own network of friends. - The key theoretical contribution of this paper then is identifying and testing the various mechanisms in which social media can influence participation through diverse pathways, such as through social media news or personal expressions on social media. Overall, because of this project we now have a clearer understanding of the role of social media in Hong Kong politics and civic life, and the conditions in which social media could influence political attitudes, which can then engender participatory behaviors.

459713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
459713.value: There is much potential for further research in the area of social media use and political and civic life in Hong Kong. Two avenues are worthy of further investigation. First, the completed project by and large focused on the “positive” outcomes of social media use, such as engendering greater citizen participation in conventional politics. Less emphasized are the potential “dark side” of social media use for politics as it can lead to the rise of “filter bubbles” and “echo chambers” where only congenial information is shared among one’s social network, which can ultimately contribute to greater opinion polarization. This is particularly relevant in Hong Kong since many experts and scholars agree that Hong Kong society has increasingly become more polarized. Second, more work can be conducted on the effects of mobile media and communications in political and civic life, especially with the role of smartphone messaging apps such as WhatsApp, which is widely used in Hong Kong for close-tie communications. For the first avenue mentioned above, I have already submitted a GRF proposal for the 2019-2020 funding cycle, titled “Personal communication networks, partisan communication and social polarisation: A study of Hong Kong using a curated flows approach”.

459713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
459713.value: This project examined the role and impact of social media use among Hong Kong citizens and its impact on political and civic participation in Hong Kong. In general, the use of social media among citizens is very high compared to the rest of the world. For example, Facebook has around 60% penetration. The body of studies in this project show that social media serve a variety of functions: as a source of information about politics and public affairs, a platform for political expression, and a virtual network in which to connect with one’s friends. These in turn influences citizens’ political attitudes and subsequent participation in conventional and non-conventional political activities, such as elections and protests.The body of studies improve our theoretical understanding of the various mechanism that integrate to predict citizen participation. More practically, it provides organizations, such as political institutions, interest groups, and activist groups, insights on the conditions in which social media may accentuate or attenuate participation tendencies.

460113.label: Realisation of objectives
460113.value: Objective 1: Identification of the motor switch interacting partners By a combination of pull-down and mass spectrometry analysis, our team has identified two interacting partners of flagellar motor switch complex. Specifically, they are FliM-spermidine synthetase (SpeE) and FliY-FliN-methionine adenosyltransferase (MAT) complexes. Their direct biophysical associations have also been confirmed by co-expression and co-purification. We have further purified FliM-SpeE complex for crystallization study and resolve its structure at atomic level. The crystal structure of FliM-SpeE was determined to a resolution of 2.7Å by molecular replacement, with R/R-free refined to 17.75% and 21.5%, respectively. The crystal structure of FliM-SpeE complex reveals that the interaction between FliM for SpeE is dominated by electrostatic interactions and hydrogen bonds spanning across the beta-strand 1-2 region of FliM and the N-terminal beta-strand domain of a SpeE subunit. Key residues involve in the formation of salt bridges and hydrogen bonds were validated by site-directed mutagenesis and pull-down assays. Additionally, we characterized the binding kinetics of FliM and SpeE by isothermal titration calorimetry. The binding constant of FliM and SpeE was in the micromolar range, and the calculated stoichiometric ratio was 0.43, consistent with the crystal structure that one FliM interacts with a SpeE dimer. In line with the pull-down results, the binding affinities of FliM with SpeE mutants was assessed and our results indicated that the formation of FliM-SpeE complex was abolished when one of the salt bridge or hydrogen bond interactions is interrupted. It appears that this binding mode provides the ability of ready response to the external stimuli and motility regulation in a subtle way. Further characterization of the FliM-SpeE interaction revealed that H. pylori SpeE is a pseudoenzyme and does not carry any enzymatic activity in spermidine synthesis, suggest that H. pylori SpeE is functionally distinct from spermidine production. H. pylori may instead employ the alternative pathway for spermidine synthesis which is dominantly exploited by other human gut microbes. We further showed that SpeE was well expressed in H. pylori wild type strain, indicating that SpeE is not a redundant protein and may carry specific biological function, likely as a motility regulator as demonstrated in our FliM-SpeE study. This part of findings has been published in Biochemical Biophysical Research Communication (2017). Soon after our BBRC paper was published, we received comments from Prof. Anthony Michael (U of Texas) - “This is an excellent paper and you have done a great service to the polyamine community by showing that this protein is not a spermidine synthase. I am very impressed by the analytical rigour you have used in the analysis of this "Pseudo-aminopropyltransferase". Objective 2: Characterization of the functional relationship of FliG-VacA interaction Previously, we have isolated VacA as a binding partner of FliG by in vitro pull-down assay. To understand the biological importance of their interaction, our team has constructed a fliG-null strain and vacA-null strain in H. pylori. Comparison of the expression level of VacA in the wild type and fliG-null strains did not show significant difference. We also compared the secretion of VacA and CagA to the infected gastric cancer cells, and no significant difference was detected when vacA gene was deleted in the H. pylori genome. It is likely that the binding between FliG and VacA has no influence on VacA stability and secretion. Interestingly, our results from bacterial motility assays showed that vacA-null strain displayed a greater migration diameter, suggesting that the flagellar motor was in counter-clockwise bias or the motor was at a higher rotational speed. It is possible that VacA, like SpeE, may behave as a modulator to control the balance between clockwise/counter-clockwise switching. On the other hand, the in vivo interaction of FliG and VacA was confirmed by a combination of in vivo cross-linking and co-immunoprecipitation. Objective 3: Molecular interaction of FliG-VacA complex We have constructed various FliG truncated fragments to map the interaction of FliG and VacA. Our results showed that the C-terminal domain of FliG was necessary for VacA binding. This result was also supported by the mass spectrometry of FliG-VacA cross-linked product. Cross-linking of residues Lys 268/269 at helix 3 of the FliG C-terminal domain and Lys 322 of VacA p33 domain were identified. Our earlier study proposed that the symmetrical torque generation process during clockwise and counter-clockwise directions may relate to the two-fold flipping of the FliG C-terminal domain that interact with the stator. Here, the cross-linked residues in FliG we identified are in close proximity to the charged ridge that interacts with the stator. It is possible that binding of VacA alters the association of FliG with the stator during rotational switching. We attempted to purify recombinant FliG-VacA complex for structural study. Unfortunately, the protein complex was not stable, and the amount and homogeneity of the complex were not sufficient for crystallization studies. The results also suggest that unlike FliM-SpeE, the binding affinity of FliG-VacA is not strong. Currently, we apply gradient density centrifugation to obtain small amount of FliG-VacA complex for electron microscopy study. Objective 4: Validation of motor switch interacting partners Our team has successfully applied in vivo cross-linking to confirm the biological relevance of FliM-SpeE interaction identified in Objective 1. To understand the biological importance of SpeE in flagellar motility, we created a speE-null strain in H. pylori. We found that deletion of SpeE did not affect flagellar formation, however, clockwise rotation bias was induced as shown by bacterial swimming assays. We also analyzed whether speE-null mutant retained the ability to respond to chemo-attractant and repellent using supplemented soft agar chemotaxis assay. Our results indicates that response of speE-null strain to attractant Urea and repellent HCl was comparable to that of the wild type, suggesting that SpeE has no association with chemotactic responses. Proper association of FliM and FliG is required for rotational switching. To better understand the functional implications of FliM-SpeE interaction, we compared the binding interfaces of FliM-FliG with that of FliM-SpeE. The two binding interfaces partially overlap, particularly at residue D148 of FliM, which is involved in salt bridge formation with K105 in SpeE and with K194 in FliG. We hypothesized that FliM-SpeE interaction may disrupt FliM-FliG binding. The results from in vitro competitive pull-down assays confirm the structural findings that binding of SpeE to FliM interferes FliG interaction. Interestingly, by a combination of protein sequence conservation analysis and pull-down assays using FliM and SpeE orthologues in E. coli, our data suggest that FliM-SpeE association is unique to Helicobacter species. Findings from Objective 1 and 4 were published (Zhang et al., Molecular Microbiology, 2017).

460113.label: Major findings and research outcome
460113.value: In this study, we report two novel non-chemotaxis regulators of the flagellar motor in H. pylori. They are putative spermidine synthase SpeE and vacuolating cytotoxin VacA. Through a combination of molecular genetics, behavioral analyses, and structural biology approaches, we further demonstrate the in vivo and in vitro biophysical interactions of FliM-SpeE and FliG-VacA. Both SpeE and VacA are essential for wild-type motility, specifically for the proper balance of motor switching. Results from the motility assays suggest that knockout of SpeE led to clockwise rotational bias while knockout of VacA induced counter-clockwise bias. Furthermore, our FliM-SpeE co-crystal structure reveals that atomic basis of the motor regulatory mechanism. SpeE dimer binds to FliM with micromolar binding affinity, and their interaction is mediated through the b1’ and b2’ region of FliM middle domain. The FliM-SpeE binding interface partially overlaps with the FliM surface that interacts with FliG and is essential for proper flagellar rotational switching. By a combination of protein sequence conservation analysis and pull-down assays using FliM and SpeE orthologues in E. coli, our data suggest that FliM-SpeE association is unique to Helicobacter species. Additionally, results from the crosslinking and mass spectrometry show that VacA may control motor performance by modulating the association of the FliG C-terminal domain with the stator in the symmetrical torque generation during rotational switching. Interestingly, our work also uncover that H. pylori SpeE is a pseudo-enzyme with no detectable catalytic activity in spermidine synthesis. Analysis of H. pylori genome further suggests that similar to other human gut microbes, H. pylori may employ the alternative route of spermidine synthesis. Taken together, it appears that beyond chemotaxis, microbes develop their own protein repertoire to regulate motor performance. Our work presents two new models of motor regulation through binding to FliG at the upper C-ring, and FliM at the middle C-ring. Both of which are well known to be critical for motor behavior. The crystal structure of FliM-SpeE has been deposited to PDB (ID: 5X0Z). Our findings on FliM-SpeE were presented by a PhD student in the BLAST meeting in Jan, 2015 (selected for stage presentation) and published in Biochem Biophys Res Commun (2017) and Mol Microbiol (2017). The PI has also been invited to deliver a talk in an international meeting to present the findings.

460113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
460113.value: Our work has revealed for the first time the post-assembly regulation of the flagellar motor in H. pylori. Specifically, it is linked to a pseudoenzyme spermidine synthase SpeE in spermidine biosynthesis. The crystal structure of FliM-SpeE complex we obtained will provide a structure-guided study to investigate the mechanistic underlying the regulation of this nano-device. Additionally, our findings also indicate that H. pylori may employ the alternative pathway for spermidine synthesis, which is dominantly exploited by other human gut microbes. Since the motor performance is tightly associated with cell adhesion and biofilm formation, taken together the results from the FliG-VacA interaction studies, our work has opened up a new line of study for the development of antimicrobial agents against H. pylori infection. New collaborations with Prof. Wah Chiu (Baylor College of Medicine, US), Prof. Zhang Qinfen (Sun Yat-sen University, China), Prof. Yuan Junhua (University of Science and Technology of China, China) and Prof. Wu Yilin (CUHK) are established. There are several lines of investigation underway, these include 1) x-ray crystallography and cryo-EM studies of H. pylori flagellar motor (WC and ZQ), and 2) biophysical characterization of the motor performance of H. pylori flagellar motor using wild type, speE-null and vacA-null strains (YJ and WY).

460113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
460113.value: The bacterial flagellum is an essential virulence factor in many bacterial pathogens. The flagellar motor switch complex, which is typically composed of multiple copies of FliG, FliM and FliN, plays a critical role in the flagellar synthesis and motor functions. This project aims to investigate the regulation of motor performance in gastric pathogen H. pylori. Our group has identified the direct interactions of FliM with a pseudoenzyme spermidine synthetase SpeE, and FliG with vacuolating cytotoxin VacA. Interruption of SpeE or VacA gene in the H. pylori genome did not affect flagellar formation. However, the two null strains displays rotational bias. From the crystal structure of the FliM-SpeE complex, we proposed that the binding of SpeE to FliM disturbs the association of FliM with FliG that is required for proper flagellar rotational switching. On the other hand, we mapped the interaction of VacA to the C-terminal domain of FliG, suggesting that VacA may modulate the symmetrical torque generation during bidirectional switching. Our findings uncover two novel protein factors for the post-assembly regulation of the flagellar motor and provide new concepts for the development of therapeutic agents against H. pylori infection, and for the design of tunable nano-machine.

460713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
460713.value: 乳腺癌是女性最常見的惡性腫瘤，在香港在2010年造成561人死亡。該項目將研究一個壓制乳癌的基因，PTEN. 在超過23％的乳癌, PTEN是受到抑制。這項建議會揭示PTEN基因抑制腫瘤的新機制，並揭露乳癌擴散的基因。 腫瘤抑制基因是維持細胞穩態的關鍵，他們的壓制會觸發不受控制的增殖和擴散。這樣的一個腫瘤抑制， PTEN基因能夠壓制乳癌，子宮內膜癌，和腦癌。 生化方面, PTEN能分解磷脂酰肌醇[ 3,4,5 ]三磷酸（PIP3）。PTEN的功能關鍵於它能夠粘住細胞膜的蛋白。PTEN利用一個PDZ-BD的蛋白結構域將PTEN運輸到細胞和細胞的連接點。 擾亂乳癌細胞交界處的完整性和上皮細胞形狀的損失是晚期癌症的標誌。在Cowden綜合徵（CS)，PTEN PDZ-BD結構域在乳癌，皮膚癌，和甲狀腺癌被刪除。PTEN PDZ-BD的損失可能破壞細胞交界處的完整性和誘發上皮細胞轉化。 要探索PTEN PDZ-BD在腫瘤進展中的作用，我們的實驗室已經研製一種 小鼠缺乏PDZ-BD的結構域。這種小鼠類似CS的患者。這項建議將調查這個小鼠是否更容易發生乳癌。 這小鼠會與一種乳腺癌的模型交配。發病，腫瘤大小和肺擴散的程度，將進行比較。此外，腫瘤細胞的分離和其相對的增殖，遷移和誘發腫瘤的能力進行比較。此外，在腫瘤細胞的緊密連接，缺乏PDZ- BD的生化和功能特性將被確定。 PTEN抑制乳腺腫瘤的進展沒有完全解決。雖然腫瘤細胞交界處的完整性是至關重要的，所涉及的分子機制並不清晰。我們的小鼠模型將一個接近生理條件下解決這些關鍵問題的癌症生物學。產生的結果，將加強我們了解乳房腫瘤抑制基因的監管機制。此外，在細胞交界處發現的新蛋白將用於研製治療癌擴散的標靶藥物。

460713.label: Realisation of objectives
460713.value: Refer to paper submitted in Section 8 Part C for figures. Objective 1 Pathological examinations of mammary glands were performed for 8-month-old virgin mice different genotypes, including Pten+/+, Pten+/- and PtenΔPDZ/-. The pathological grading scheme ranges from normal (0 score) to diffuse carcinoma (15 score), and covers different stages of mammary carcinogenesis. Each mammary gland was graded based on the highest pathological lesion being observed, and the grading score for each animal was averaged by all the glands being examined. Results showed that no significant difference was observed between Pten+/- and PtenΔPDZ/- mice. Objective 2 To investigate the effects of PTEN PDZ-BD (abbreviated as PDZ-BD) on mammary tumorigenesis, we crossed the PtenΔPDZ-BD mice with MMTV-PyMT breast cancer model. KO mice have significantly shorter tumor free survival time (Figure 3A), as well as increased total tumor weight compared with WT or HET mice (Figure 3B), though tumor incidence per animal was comparable across the three genotypes (Figure 3C). Histology of tumor tissue revealed adenocarcinoma like structures for WT, HET and KO (Figure 3D). Pathological examination showed that tumor tissues from KO mice exhibited a greater degree of high grade histological features, such as more pleomorphism, larger nuclear size, and more frequent mitoses; while tumors from WT mice showed more benign features, including glandular differentiation, smaller nuclear size, and more regular and fewer mitoses. Overall, KO mice show increased tumor burden in model, which indicates that PTEN PDZ-BD indeed contribute to the tumor suppressive function. Whether PTEN PDZ-BD also participated in metastasis was investigated by counting lung metastases. Results showed that KO mice exhibited more extensive lung metastasis (Figure 4A), and stratification of the data showed that a significant larger proportion of KO mice have more extensive lung metastasis (>5 metastatic nodules) as compared to WT mice (Figure 4B). Meanwhile, although HET mice did not have significantly elevated tumor mass compared to WT mice, they indeed showed a higher tendency to have lung metastasis than WT mice. This indicates that heterozygous loss of PTEN PDZ-BD may be more important for breast cancer metastasis than for primary cancer growth. Objective 3: We have established 4 to 5 independent primary cultures from mammary tumors in PTEN PDZ-BD WT, HET, and KO genetic background. We do not detect altered PTEN subcellular localization (Figure S1A) in KO tumor cells. Also, by transwell migration assay and scratch wound assay, KO tumors did not display greater motility that the WT counterpart (not shown). Additionally, KO breast cancer cells did not show higher proliferation based on measurements of Ki67staining (Figure S1C). Therefore, PDZ-BD is dispensable for either PTEN localization, protein expression, and migration in MMTV-PyMT breast cancer. As for their tumorigenic potentials, it is important to clarify whether the enhanced tumor burden observed is due to the loss of PTEN PDZ-BD in cancer cells or in the tumor microenvironment. To test this, primary WT or KO mammary tumor cells were orthotopically injected into either WT or KO mice. As shown in Figure 3E, KO tumor cells induced greater-sized tumors than WT tumor cells when injected in either WT or KO mammary fatpads. Overall, the orthotopic allograft model indicates that the loss of PTEN PDZ-BD in breast cancer cells promotes tumor growth in the MMTV-PyMT model. Furthermore, the role of PTEN PDZ-BD in cells within the tumor microenvironment may not have a prominent role in suppressing mammary tumorigenesis. Objective 4: We have established 4 to 5 primary cultures from mammary epithelial cells and mammary tumors in PDZ-BD WT, HET and KO genetic background. The activation states of the PI3K-AKT pathway did not show significant difference in KO mammary epithelial cells (Figure 2C) nor in KO mammary tumors (Figure S1B). The tumor suppressive functions of PDZ-BD in the MMTV-PyMT breast cancer model may involve other mechanisms independent of the phosphatase activity of PTEN. We, therefore, conducted, extensive immunogold staining of PTEN by transmission electron microscopy in an attempt to examine if PDZ-BD is required for TJ localization. After considerable efforts, we were not able to demonstrate significant difference in PTEN localization to the epithelial junction by this approach. We also attempted to identified novel complexing proteins in mammary epithelial cells by conventional biochemical purification steps using PTEN fusion protein but failed to capture novel interactors using this strategy. Objective 5: Whole mount staining of mammary glands from 5-week-old virgin mice revealed no significant difference in normal branching and numbers of end buds in PDZ-BD KO mice when compared to WT. These results indicate that PDZ-BD is not involved in regulating mammary gland morphology (Figure 1A and B). H&E staining on mammary gland sections from 4-month old virgin mice (Figure 1C). Although ductal morphologies were similar among WT, HET and KO, the average ductal sizes for KO and HET were significantly increased compared to WT (Figure 1D). Therefore, PTEN PDZ-BD regulates ductal size in adult animals. Three-dimensional (3D) culture of mammary epithelial cells was performed using Matrigel to reconstruct mammary organoids in vitro. When the diameter of the spheroids was measured, a significant increase in the diameter could be observed in KO mammary epithelial cells (Figure 2E). This data is consistent with the observation of greater ductal diameter of mammary glands, and suggests involvement of PTEN PDZ-BD in regulating the size of mammary ducts in vivo and spheroid in vitro. To investigate whether PTEN PDZ-BD deletion could disrupt cell polarity or cell junctions, immunofluorescence analysis was performed on 3D mammary spheroids. Observations showed, tight junction marker ZO-1, apical-basal polarity markers integrin-β1 and GM130, and cadherin marker E-cadherin were all intact in WT, HET and KO organoids (Figure 2D). Therefore, PTEN PDZ-BD is not required for establishing and maintaining junctional integrity and apical-basal polarity of primary MMEs. Objective 6: Since the effect of PTEN PDZ-BD on mammary carcinogenesis does not appear to be mediated through tight junction (TJ). Search for novel TJ interactors for PTEN PDZ-BD will be futile. To determine the underlying mechanism, transcriptome analysis was performed to compare WT and KO tumor cells. 327 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) genes were detected with 302 genes downregulated, and 25 genes up-regulated (Figure 5A). Gene Ontology analysis showed that the most common classifications were protein binding, cytoskeleton, and calcium signaling (Figure 5B). The majority of the 20 most downregulated genes are related to muscular functions, for example muscular cytoskeletal proteins myosin, troponin, and smooth muscle actin (Table S3). Cell types within normal mammary or mammary tumor tissue possessing muscular characteristics consist mainly of myoepithelial cells, myofibroblasts, or vascular smooth muscle cells. RT-qPCR validation analysis showed that myoepithelial cell markers, rather than myofibroblast or smooth muscle cell makers, are significantly downregulated in KO tumor tissue (Figure 5D). By IHC analysis, myoepithelial cell markers, TRP63 and α-SMA (ACTA2), both showed decreased staining in KO tissues as compared to WT tissues (Figure 6A and B). Myoepithelial cells have been regarded as a natural tumor suppressor for breast cancer. Besides, lower expression of myoepithelial markers, like KRT5, KRT14, TP63 and NGFR, in invasive breast cancer was associated with poorer patient prognosis, supporting the tumor suppressive nature of these genes (Figure 6D). Therefore, the decreased expression of the myoepithelial markers in KO breast cancer tissues may cause the enhanced tumorigenicity in MMTV-PyMT model.

460713.label: Major findings and research outcome
460713.value: We have identified previously unknown function of the PDZ-BD of PTEN in both normal mammary epithelial cells and during mammary tumor development. In normal mouse mammary epithelial glands, PTEN PDZ-BD does not play a major role in overall ductal morphology, branching, and terminal end bud size. Instead, it is involved in controlling the homeostasis of the lumen size in adult mammary duct. Consistent with this finding, three-dimensional spheroid cultures confirmed this finding as primary mammary epithelial cells lacking PTEN PDZ-BD have greater sphere diameter. Interestingly, spheroids from PTEN PDZ-BD still retain the apical-basolateral polarity commonly found in normal mammospheres suggesting that PTEN PDZ-BD is not involved in regulating tight junction integrity as would have been expected. Also unexpected is that PTEN PDZ-BD does not appear to exert negative control on the PI3-K/AKT signaling event. Overall, the phenotype of PTEN PDZ-BD knockout in normal mammary epithelial cells is very subtle. During mammary tumor development, the role of PTEN PDZ-BD as a tumor suppressing motif is more evidenced. Specifically, mice lacking PTEN PDZ-BD promoted MMTV-PyMT mammary carcinogenesis by having shortened latency of onset, greater tumor mass, and more malignant phenotypes. By orthotopic mammary tumor induction model, the observed tumor promotion is not because of the contribution from the tumor microenvironment. Furthermore, the number of lung metastasis is significantly higher in mice lacking PTEN PDZ-BD. However, the tumor suppressive effects of PTEN PDZ-BD are not correlated with the suppression of PI3K signaling. Instead, we observed a significant downregulation of myoepithelial markers in both KO primary breast cancer and orthotopic allografts, indicating PTEN PDZ-BD may participate in myoepithelial differentiation of breast cancer cells. Overall, our finding suggests that PTEN PDZ-BD plays a tumor suppressive role in a murine model of breast cancer, and the mechanism may involve dysregulation of myoepithelial differentiation in breast cancer cells.

460713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
460713.value: We envisage the following two areas to be of interest for further development. 1. Role of PTEN PDZ-BD in regulating spindle pole movement - van Ree et. al. reported the interaction between PTEN PDZ-BD with Dlg-1at the pre-mitotic centrosomes (Nat. Cell Biol. 2016 18:814-21). Coupling of a kinesin protein, Eg5, to the PTEN-Dlg-1 complex is important for spindle pole motility. The knockout of PTEN PDZ-BD was shown to cause asymmetrical spindles and missegregated chromosomes leading to aneuploidy and predisposition to cancer. This finding is consistent with our data showing the knockout of PTEN PDZ-BD can promote mammary tumorigenesis. Future studies may evaluate if the greater mammary tumor formation observed in our case is actually due to chromosome missegragation. 2. The link between PTEN PDZ-BD and myoepithelial markers - our transcriptomic analysis revealed the downregulation of myoepithelial markers in mammary tumors lacking PTEN PDZ-BD. The underlying mechanism is not clear as to how PDZ-BD can regulate gene expression. Future studies may explore the nuclear function of PTEN PDZ-BD by isolating direct interacting partners that may play a role in gene transcription. Furthermore, the tumor suppressive role of individual myoepithelial marker genes will be evaluated in human breast cancer cell lines.

460713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
460713.value: During breast cancer development, the loss of the entire PTEN tumor suppressor protein is a common event. However, which portion of PTEN can mediate tumor suppressor function is not clear. We uncovered that a protein-protein interaction domain of PTEN can suppress tumor initiation, progression and metastasis. Normally, this domain only plays a minor role in determining the size of a mammary duct. Assigning a tumor suppressor function to this domain in PTEN is a significant finding as this will justify the search for the binding partner(s). Also, our finding will drive more research into finding novel strategies to either restore or strengthen the binding between this domain and its binding partners in breast cancer. The funded project is of value as a major manuscript is currently under review. Furthermore, we have established a new collaborative effort with Prof. Ui Soon Khoo, an experienced breast cancer pathologist at the Department of Pathology at the University of Hong Kong based on this funded project. More importantly, this GRF funding has allowed the training of an talented PhD student, Yan Mingfei.

460913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
460913.value: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) rupture is a very common sport injury resulting in an unstable knee. As a ruptured ACL does not heal, ACL reconstruction (ACLR) is the standard treatment to restore knee function. The surgical procedure of ACLR involves the use of a tendon graft to replace the ruptured ACL. Surgeons drill bone tunnels on distal femur and proximal tibia, insert the tendon graft through the bone tunnels and secure the graft in place. Poor graft healing is the major cause leading to ACLR failure and excessive knee laxity, because the graft tissue is weakened with decreased mechanical properties under hostile micro-environment at early healing phase, which never return to the original level. Glycyl-histidyl-lysine tripeptide copper complex (GHK-Cu) is a well-known activator of tissue remodeling, which is used in many skin products. In the last GRF project, we found that GHK-Cu can enhance graft incorporation and improve restoration of knee laxity. However, repeated intra-articular injections of GHK-Cu at post inflammatory phase may bring unnecessary tissue responses, and graft weakening at intra-articular mid-substance was still evident. Therefore, we propose to develop a product to reduce graft weakening in ACLR, by a bioactive coating on tendon graft with controlled delivery of GHK-Cu. We have shown that a protective coating on tendon graft can reduce the extent of graft deterioration at early stages after ACLR. In this research project, a biodegradable thermo-sensitive hydrogel (which remains as liquid at room temperature and forms gel at body temperature) will be developed to encapsulate GHK-Cu and apply on tendon autograft or allograft to improve the healing outcomes of ACLR. As there are over 1200 ACLR in Hong Kong per year, with over 200,000 ACLR in US per year and probably millions in the world; our study will not just benefit the patients Hong Kong but worldwide. 前十字韌帶(ACL)撕裂是常見的運動創傷，會使膝關節變得不穩定。由於撕裂的ACL不能自行修復，ACL重建手術(ACLR)是恢復膝關節功能的標準治療方法。重建手術會利用肌腱移植物取代撕裂的ACL。骨科醫生會在股骨遠端和脛骨近端鑽出骨隊道，然後把肌腱移植物穿過並固定於隊道內。不過，移植物一般都不能好好癒合，其力學性能在癒合早期的惡劣環境下會變差，從而導致膝關節鬆弛，令傷者無法恢復原來的運動能力。 藍銅勝肽(GHK-Cu)是一種常用於皮膚產品的組織重構活化劑。在上一個受資助的優配研究計劃中，我們發現GHK-Cu能促進移植物植入骨隧道裡，並改善膝關節的鬆弛程度；但是重覆注射GHK-Cu到膝關節內會引發不良反應，使移植物在關節腔內的中間部份變弱。初步研究發現，在移植物上塗上生物活性塗層，能在癒合早期減輕其弱化情況。在這個研究項目中，我們將開發一種可生物降解的熱敏水凝膠(室溫時呈液態，當溫度升至體溫時則凝結成膠狀)把GHK-Cu封裝，然後把含GHK-Cu的水凝膠塗上自體或同種異體的肌腱移植物上。透過調控GHK-Cu在手術後緩緩釋放，傷者在術後的恢復也許能進一步得到改善。現時香港及美國每年各有多於1200 及20,000 宗ACLR手術，推算全世界甚至可能有過百萬人需要進行ACLR。 我們的研究將會有助香港以至全世界ACL撕裂的病人早日康復。

460913.label: Realisation of objectives
460913.value: All work related to the 3 objectives has been completed. Objective 1. This part aimed to fabricate thermo-sensitive hydrogels based on mPEG-PLGA-Box block copolymer for bioactive graft coating in subsequent in vitro and in vivo experiments. Thermosensitive hydrogel mPEG-PLGA BOX gel was successfully fabricated by our collaborators in Taiwan. Two batches of hydrogels were synthesized in Taiwan and sent to Hong Kong. The gel was reconstituted in PBS to achieve an aqueous solution at 15, 25, or 35%. Due to batch-to-batch variation, the time taken for gel reconstitution in batch 2 is longer than in batch 1 (14 days vs 1 day on average). However, the temperature-sensitive gelling properties are not affected. At 4°C, the gel solution remained as liquid form. Upon transfer to 37°C, the solution gelled within 1 min. Objective 2. This part aimed to encapsulate GHK-Cu in the bioactive coating gel and investigate the release kinetics. Results were obtained from 3 parts of work, including (A) in vitro study of GHK-Cu encapsulation, release and gel degradation, (B) in vitro study of the characteristics of the hydrogels on harvested tendon grafts, and (C) in vivo study of gel coating durability. In part 2(A), GHK-Cu was encapsulated in the mPEG-PLGA BOX gel and the concentration of the polymer with optimal encapsulation efficiency of GHK-Cu was investigated, followed by investigation of release kinetics and gel degradation. GHK-Cu was added to 15 wt%-, 25wt%- and 35wt%-copolymer aqueous solution (n=3 per group). After gelation, the hydrogel was incubated in PBS at 37°C with constant shaking. Encapsulation efficiency was calculated by measuring GHK-Cu in the washings immediately after the gels were formed. The amount of GHK-Cu was measured by spectrophotometry at 620 nm. On day 0 (initial washings), 3, 6, 13, 20 and 30, the supernatants were removed and replaced by 37°C fresh PBS. The amount of GHK-Cu and mPEG in the supernatants were measured to calculate GHK-Cu release and gel degradation. The gel degradation was shown in terms of the mPEG level in the washings. The washing was first underwent alkaline hydrolysis by NaOH, which released mPEG from copolymer. The washing was then treated with barium iodide. The mPEG formed complex formation with barium iodide. The mPEG level was measured and calculated from the absorbance of the resulting solution at 540 nm. In part 2(B), in order to investigate the spatial and temporal release of drugs in vivo in the subsequent part (C), anti-mouse IgG-FITC was used as a visualizing agent to assess the thickness of coating and its evenness. Before in vivo part, the FITC-IgG loaded gel degradation and FITC-IgG release kinetics were investigated in vitro. Flexor digitorum longus tendons were harvested by longitudinal medial incision on the heel of 12-week-old male Sprague-Dawley rats. The tendons were coated with 35% mPEG-PLGA BOX gel pre-loaded with FITC-conjugated tag by a coating device with a bore of 1.2 mm. The coated tendons were incubated in vitro in PBS at 37 °C. A continuous study on Day 1, 7, 14, 21, 28, 30 and 35 (n=3 per time-point) was used and the gel volume remained and release of FITC-IgG were investigated. Gel coating was examined under microscope in whole amount and in frozen section. Polarized light illumination was used to visualize collagen fibers in tendon and hydrogel coating was revealed by green fluorescent signal of FITC. The gel volume remained was measured by the mPEG level on the washings using the same hydrolysis mentioned in the part A. The FITC-IgG release was measured by quantifying its fluorescent signals. In part 2(C), the durability of hydrogel and release of FITC-IgG were investigated in vivo. Anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) was performed in 12 week male SD rats (n=3 per time-point) flexor tendon graft as described in our previous report (Fu, 2013). The tendon graft harvested from rat was coated with mPEG-PLGA BOX gel. To allow even coating, the coating procedure was performed twice. The procedures of passing tendon graft through bone tunnels were slightly modified, so as to minimize gel loss on tendon graft. Instead of passing whole tendon graft from exit of femoral tunnel, the tendon was put in intra-articular space and the 2 ends were routed through femoral and tibial tunnels respectively. On Day 1, 7 and 14 post-operatively, the rats were euthanized and the tendon grafts were harvested. Frozen sections of the tendon grafts were prepared for examination of residual gel coating under polarization and fluorescent microscopy. Objective 3. In this part, the effect of GHK-Cu bioactive coating on healing outcome after ACLR was studied in a well-established rat model of ACLR. Since the procedures of gel coating on graft and graft fixation method to prevent gel loss was standardized in part 2 (C), we proceeded to compare the effects of GHK-loaded gel coating on tendon graft with gel coating only and untreated control on ACLR healing outcome. GHK-Cu at 0.3mg/ml or 3mg/ml was loaded to the reconstituted 25% mPEG-PLGA BOX gel. Graft coating was performed as in part 2 (C). After ACLR, rats were sacrificed at week 2, 6, and 12 post-operatively for assessment of healing outcome. Mechanical tests, including static knee anterior posterior laxity test and graft pull-out test was performed according to our established protocol at week 12 post-operation to assess restoration of knee stability and tendon graft strength respectively (n=8 per group). Histology using routine H&E staining was performed to evaluate graft degeneration, graft incorporation, and bone tunnel healing (n=4 per group). Since no significant difference in AP laxity and graft pull-out force was found between all treatment groups (more details in “6.1 Major finding” below), an additional group with BOX gel coating loaded with 100mg/ml GHK-Cu was included to evaluate its effects on ACLR healing (n=8 for mechanical test, n=4 for histology). In our previous studies, 6 weeks post-op could best reveal the difference in mechanical properties, so in this study a time point of week 6 post-operation was chosen in this additional group for comparison with control group.

460913.label: Major findings and research outcome
460913.value: In part 1, thermosensitive hydrogel mPEG-PLGA BOX gel was fabricated for subsequent experiments. In part 2(A) , 35% gel exhibited highest encapsulation efficiency (94%) as compared to 15% gels (p=0.003). For all gels, significant initial bursts were observed on Day 1 and most GHK-Cu was released after Day 6. GHK-Cu release in 15% gels was significantly faster than 25% and 35% gels (p<0.001). Gel degradation was evident on Day 3 and almost half of the gel (~30 - 50%) was still retained on Day 30. There was no significant difference in gel degradation among the gels (p=0.139). In part 2(B), coating of 35% FITC-tagged mPEG-PLGA gel on tendon grafts resulted in a thin and even gel layer as revealed by polarization and fluorescent microscopy on whole mount and frozen sections. Significant initial burst was observed on Day 1 post-op and 90% of FITC-IgG was released after 35 days. Gel loss was evident on Day 7 and exhibited gradual loss until Day 35. In part 2(C), FITC remained on graft on Day 14 post-operatively. An even coating can be observed. FITC-IgG release had a burst on the Day1, which remained consistent till Day 14. There was significant gel degradation on Day 1 post-operatively but no significant degradation was observed between Day 1 and 14 post-operatively. The above results were reported in 3 conferences, and 1 full paper will be re-submitted to peer-reviewed journal. In part 3, at 12 weeks post-ACLR, among the 4 groups (untreated control, BOX gel only, 0.3 and 3mg/ml GHK-Cu in BOX gel), there was no significant difference in knee AP laxity as well as failure load of the graft-bone complex (p=0.111, 0.396, ANOVA). On the contrary, at 6 weeks post-ACLR, graft coating using higher dose at 100mg/ml GHK-Cu loaded BOX gel resulted in significantly improved knee laxity (p<0.001, Scheffe post-hoc test) as compared to saline control from previous study (p=0.004, ANOVA). However, at 6 weeks post-op, as compared to 4 repeated injections of 3mg/ml GHK-Cu (from previous GRF project), 100mg/ml GHK-Cu BOX gel graft coating (in this study) did not showed further improved knee laxity and graft strength (p>0.05, ANOVA). Histology showed that using this effective dose of 100mg/ml GHK-Cu BOX gel coating, at 6 weeks post-ACLR, as compared to the gel coating only, there was enhanced graft incorporation to the surrounding bone, including the presence of fibrocartilage zone and sharpey’s fibre.

460913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
460913.value: After collecting data from the current study, drug encapsulation and release kinetics using the mPEG-PLGA-BOX gel was better characterized. Apart from loading small molecules such as GHK-Cu, the BOX hydrogel will be further used in 3 other projects. In a proposal submitted for Health and Medical Research Fund (HMRF), we aim to study the effect of controlled release of platelet-rich-plasma (PRP) in a rat model of ACLR. PRP has been used to promote repair in wide range of orthopaedic disorders. However, the treatment effects varied due to the difficulties in localization and retention of PRP. In the study, we are trying to mix BOX hydrogel with PRP and put in the site of ACLR. In another ongoing project, BOX gel is mixed with PRP for ACL partial tear. We expect the effects of PRP will be further enhanced with the use of the BOX gel as a controlled delivery system. We also plan for further studies to characterize retention of PRP-loaded BOX gel following injection in rat. The proposal has been submitted for ITF to Innovation and Technology Commission. With the ongoing and proposed work, we hope BOX gel can be used as controlled delivery system in orthopaedics.

460913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
460913.value: Anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) is the standard surgery to restore knee stability after ACL rupture. Current biological modulation includes bioactive factors were given either during operation or after operation by intra-articular injections. As drug clearance from knee joint is fast, to tackle the slow process of tendon graft remodeling, a delivery system that allows localized and sustained drug release is highly desirable. This study aimed to develop a controlled delivery system to carry bioactive molecules for enhancement of graft healing following ACLR. Previously we showed that repeated intra-articular injections of a GHK tripeptide-copper complex (GHK-Cu) transiently improved repair following ACLR. In this study, to localize drug for sustained release, GHK-Cu was encapsulated in temperature-sensitive hydrogel (mPEG-PLGA-BOX gel) for graft coating, and high encapsulation efficiency was achieved. We have established a standardized protocol to coat the tendon graft. In vivo durability of hydrogel for at least 14 days post-operation suggested that the hydrogel was suitable for delivering bioactive factors targeting at early healing processes. Following ACLR using GHK-Cu hydrogel graft coating, animals exhibited better knee stability at 6 weeks post-op, potentially due to improved tissue remodeling. The delivery system can be used to carry other bioactive factors for ACLR.

461013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
461013.value: 聚丙氨酸疾病是由於人類基因組編碼丙氨酸的核酸序列延伸所致。至今，研究發現有九種疾病與丙氨酸（alanine）鏈的延長相關。大多數聚丙氨酸（polyA）疾病蛋白是轉錄因子，調節細胞中基因轉錄。帶有延長聚丙氨酸鏈的蛋白主要定位於細胞質，表明延長的聚丙氨酸疾病蛋白核質運輸失去平衡，聚丙氨酸疾病蛋白的轉錄能力也因此受到牽連。以上研究結果表明延長的聚丙氨酸疾病蛋白錯誤定位於細胞質引起轉錄能力損傷，最終導致細胞功能紊亂，進而疾病發生。因此，我們假設延長的聚丙氨酸蛋白核質運輸失衡導致其錯誤定位於細胞質。我們前期的實驗結果顯示延長的聚丙氨酸鏈是一種新的核輸出信號（nuclear export signal; NES），通過一種全新的核輸出通路介導蛋白出核。經生化分析，我們堅定出真核翻譯延伸因子1A (eukaryotic translation elongation 1 alpha; EEF1A) 參與延長的聚丙氨酸介導的蛋白出核。此發現可使我們繼續研究延長的聚丙氨酸疾病蛋白錯誤定位於細胞質的機制。本研究預運用生物化學（細胞組分分析和免疫沉澱），細胞和分子生物學（蛋白定位的共聚焦顯微圖像分析，小片段干擾RNA (siRNA) 篩選和基因過表達）以及遺傳學方法（過表達或RNA干擾基因於基因敲入的果蠅模型）來研究此全新的蛋白出核機制。結合多種學科的研究方式有利於我們研究延長的聚丙氨酸疾病蛋白細胞定位的機制。此延長聚丙氨酸鏈出核的研究可以為聚丙氨酸疾病治療提供幫助。
