461013.label: Major findings and research outcome
461013.value: Polyalanine (polyA) diseases are caused by the expansion of GCN trinucleotide repeats in the disease genes encoding polyA amino acid tract in the disease proteins. Expansion of alanine tracts has been shown to cause several human pathological conditions, including congenital malformations and/or mental retardation. Eight of nine polyA diseases are caused by expansion of the polyA tract in transcription factors. Previous studies demonstrated that wild type unexpanded polyA proteins localize to the cell nucleus while expanded polyA disease proteins primarily localize to the cytoplasm. The mislocalization of expanded polyA disease proteins causes impairment of their transactivation activity, leading to gene transcriptional dysregulation. In our study, we showed that expanded polyA tract possesses nuclear export activity. Further, we identified eukaryotic translation elongation factor 1 alpha 1 (eEF1A1) as a novel interacting protein of expanded polyA-containing protein. Knockdown of eEF1A1 expression suppressed the nuclear export of expanded polyA-containing protein, and restored the transcriptional function of expanded polyA-containing transcription factor. We also found that the SoxNeuro protein, Drosophila ortholog of the human Sox3 protein, exhibited toxicity in an in vivo Drosophila model when it is fused with a polyA tract. The knockdown of Ef1a48D expression, the fly ortholog of eEF1A, attenuated the toxicity.

461013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
461013.value: This work demonstrates nuclear export activity in expanded polyalanine (polyA) tract, and we uncovered the function of eEF1A1 in mediating nucleocytoplasmic export of expanded polyA domain-containing proteins. Our present work would provide novel insights into understanding the pathogenesis of polyA diseases. This study demonstrates that eEF1A1 regulates the subcellular location of expanded polyA proteins and is therefore a potential therapeutic target for combating the pathogenesis of polyA diseases.

461013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
461013.value: Proteins that are resided in the cell nucleus play essential roles in controlling gene functions. When these nuclearly-localized proteins become misplaced in other cell compartments, such as the cytoplasm, they can no longer support particular functions of the cell nucleus. This will lead to cell malfunctioning and diseases. Patients who suffer from polyalanine (polyA) diseases present several human pathological conditions, including mental retardation. Eight of the nine polyA disease proteins are localized to the cell nucleus. Our research findings demonstrate that an expanded polyA domain causes the cytoplasmic mislocalization of these disease proteins, and this in turn results in defective gene regulation. This research finding emphasizes the importance of maintaining certain essential proteins in the cell nucleus, otherwise critical nuclear activities, such as gene transcription, would be perturbed.

461113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
461113.value: Bone healing takes place in the case of bone fractures, bone defects or in orthopedic surgery. Inadequate medical treatment may lead to impairment of bone regeneration and, ultimately, delayed union or non-union. Enhancement of fracture healing is therefore a desirable objective, in order to reduce or avoid such consequences. Currently, bone grafting, physical intervention, gene therapy, stem cell therapy and growth factor treatments are being developed to enhance bone healing. However various problems have been reported, such as long treatment time, ectopic bone formation, risk of infection and limited sources of donor bone or stem cells. Delivering effective orthobiologics with low cost and minimal complications remains a great challenge. It has recently been seen that natural products derived from medicinal herbs have great potential as biologics in bone healing. Osthol, an anabolic small molecule, is reported to alleviate osteoporosis and stimulate osteoblastic differentiation. In this project, we hypothesize that osthol enhances bone formation in fracture healing. The objectives of this study are to investigate: 1) the optimal dosage of osthol on enhancement of bone formation in fracture healing and 2) the optimal route of administration of osthol on fracture healing This study is significant, in that shed light on knowledge of natural small molecule on enhancement of fracture healing and results in reduction of related complications and shortened periods of hospital treatment. It may also reduce the occurrence of delayed union or non-union of fracture bones and related loss of working ability and low quality of life. 骨傷癒合發生在骨折，骨缺損或者骨科手術過程。不適當的治療，可能會造成骨再生能力損傷，從而導致延遲癒合，甚至不癒合的後果。因此為了減少或者避免這類情況發生，促進骨折癒合成為我們追求的理想目標。現今，研究人員已經開發了骨移植、物理干預、基因、幹細胞以及生長因子治療等多種方法來促進骨傷癒合。然而包括治療時間過長，異位骨形成，感染幾率增加和供體骨或者幹細胞來源有限等各種問題時有報導。 所以發展廉價並且帶來最少併發症的骨性生物製劑仍是一個巨大挑戰。 近來研究發現來自草藥的天然產物有很大潛能開發成為幫助骨傷癒合的生物製劑。蛇床子素是個具有合成作用的小分子化合物，據報導蛇床子素可緩解骨質疏鬆並刺激成骨分化。我們假設蛇床子素能促進骨折癒合中的骨骼形成，本課題旨在研究：1）蛇床子素用於促進骨折癒合中骨形成的理想劑量以及 2）蛇床子用於骨折癒合治療的最佳給藥途徑。 本課題的意義在於揭示天然小分子產物對骨折癒合的促進作用來減少相關併發症及縮短住院治療時間。同時，減少延遲癒合和不癒合的發生，從而緩解隨之相關的喪失工作能力和生活品質降低的問題。

461113.label: Realisation of objectives
461113.value: To study the effect of optimal dosage of osthol on enhancement of bone formation in fracture healing, mouse femoral open fracture model was performed with air pen driven oscillating saw on 12-week-old male C57BL/6 mice. Oral osthol reagent was freshly prepared by suspension with distilled water with 0.5% (v/v) Tween 80; and injectable osthol regent was prepared by dissolution with saline with 10% (v/v) DMSO and 5% (v/v) Tween 80. Three serial oral dosages of osthol including 5mg/kg (low group), 20mg/kg (middle group) and 50mg/kg (high group) together with solvent control were tested to find out the optimal dosage of osthol for bone augmentation. Fracture healing status of control and treated mice was assessed with plain radiology, molecular imaging, micro computed tomography (micro CT) and biomechanical testing. Osteogenic related gene expression profile in callus tissue was assessed with immunohistochemistry (IHC) and real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR). Serial plain radiographs from week 1 to week 4 of oral control and three osthol-gavage groups of were captured, analyzed and compared. Callus formation and structure in low group showed very similar healing pattern as control group. Whereas in middle and high group, the callus size at week 3 was apparently reduced compared to size at week 2, which was much smaller than that of control and low group. Quantification of the area and pixel intensity in region of interests (ROIs) of callus of was used to analyze callus volume and mineral density in callus. Callus tissue area in middle and high group were significantly smaller than that of control group by 43.65% and 36.17% respectively at week 2 and 3. The intensity of callus region at week 2 in both middle and high group was slightly higher than average control value with a statistical significance of p<0.05. Since middle and high dose of osthol did not have significant difference, middle dose (20 mg/kg/day) was selected as the optimum dose and applied in further assessments. Reconstruction of micro-CT slices allowed a visual evaluation and comparison of bony callus in control and osthol-treated (20 mg/kg) mice. In control group, there was large gap between bony bridge in callus at week 2; and the newly-formed bone had not fully bridged until week 3. Whereas for osthol group, higher proportion of bone in callus was observed at week 2. At week 3 fractured site had already be completely covered by newly formed bone; and at week 4 the fractured bone was further remodeled and restored to original shape. MicroCT 3D radiographical results were generally consistent with the results from plain radiography. Callus total volume (TV) identified the volume of newly formed tissues; low density callus bone volume (BVl) identified the volume of newly formed mineralized tissue; tissue mineral density (TMD) measured volumetric density of calcium hydroxyapatite (CaHA) in total tissue; bone mineral density (BMD) measured volumetric density of CaHA in mineralized tissue (bone). BVl/TV value of osthol group was significantly higher than control at week 2 and 3 by 45.27% and 15.87% respectively. TMD values of fractured femur were markedly raised in osthol group at all three time points; BMD of treated mice was also significantly higher than control at week 3 and 4. Since radiographic evaluations were not able to identify cartilage and other soft tissues, histological sections of fractured bone were conducted to show both cartilaginous and bony tissue. Histomorphometric results showed the bony callus area in osthol group was significantly larger than control group by 20.96% while the cartilaginous callus area was much smaller by 64.82% at post-operation week 2. The bone tissue area in treatment group became smaller than control and the cartilaginous tissue almost diminished from callus at week 3. In vivo fluorescent imaging of neo-bone formation was detected and generated with two Osteosense (Os) probes Os680 and Os800 at week 2 and 3 respectively. Positions of new bone formation could be mapped in living animals by fluorescent signals, and bone growth rate was quantified and compared between control and treatment groups. Once femur was fractured, high fluorescent signals could be detected around callus at post-operation week 2 and 3. Rectangular region of interest was middle one-third the length of femur including callus region. The signal intensity of operated bones was quantified and normalized by contralateral ones. The ratio of fluorescence intensity at week 2 was dramatically increased by 80.72% after treated with osthol; the value dropped at week 3 but was still 25.95% higher than control value. Bone mechanical test was conducted at the end point of the experiments to test the bone strength of healing femur at week 4. Results demonstrated that osthol gavage significantly enhanced maximum load of fractured bones by 36.42% compared to vehicle control ones. Meanwhile, maximum load of contralateral femurs was increased by 10.76% but without a significant difference. Expression level of osteogenic markers were assessed with IHC and compared between control and treatment group at week 2. BMP-2 mainly expressed in osteoblastic cells surrounding woven bones. ALP specifically expressed around hypertrophic cartilaginous tissues and newly formed bone tissues. OCN expressed throughout the whole callus which highly expressed in osteogenic cells but also found in bone matrix. In osthol-treated group, expression of BMP-2, ALP and OCN were all observably more intense than those in control group. Overall expression levels of osteoblastic and osteoclastic related marker genes were measured with qPCR of the whole callus. Osteoblastic gene ALP, OCN and Osx in osthol-treated group was 3.30, 3.06 and 4.41 folds respectively compared to control group, however BMP-2 level of osthol group were not significantly changed probably because relatively low total amount of expression. Expression levels of osteoclastic genes in treatment group were not notably changed.

461113.label: Major findings and research outcome
461113.value: During the period of this study, we investigated the effects of osthol on bone fracture repair in C57BL/6 mice subjected to transverse femoral fractures. Results demonstrated that osthol treatment enhanced degeneration of hypertrophic cartilage and bony union during reparative stage without significant interfering on remodeling process. Bone formation rate of the treatment group was almost two-fold of control group at post-operation week 2 during callus ossification. Osthol promoted endochondral ossification via upregulation of maturation osteogenic marker genes ALP and Col-X in chondrocytes; and enhanced osteoblastic bone formation via upregulation of BMP-2, OCN and ALP in osteoblastic cells. This part has been published (Zhang 2016). We published a review paper that summarized multiple biological and pharmacological activities of osthol and give an overview of the underlying mechanisms. We suggested that the mechanisms of multiple pharmacological activities of osthol were very likely related to the modulatory effect on cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) and cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) levels (Zhang 2015). Based on this hypothesis, we studied the osteopromotive action of osthol on mouse osteoblastic MC3T3-E1 cells and explored the interaction between osthol-induced osteopromotive effect and cAMP elevating effect. Osthole treatment promoted osteogenesis in osteoblasts by enhancing alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity and mineralization. Oral gavage of osthole enhanced fracture repair and increased bone strength. Mechanistic study showed osthole triggered the cAMP/CREB pathway through the elevation of the intracellular cAMP level and activation of the phosphorylation of the cAMP response element-binding protein (CREB). Blockage of cAMP/CREB downstream signals with protein kinase A (PKA) inhibitor KT5720 partially suppressed osthole-mediated osteogenesis by inhibiting the elevation of transcription factor, osterix. In conclusion, osthole shows osteopromotive effect on osteoblasts in vitro and in vivo. Osthole-mediated osteogenesis is related to activation of the cAMP/CREB signaling pathway and downstream osterix expression. The findings are published (Zhang 2017)

461113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
461113.value: Osteoporosis is a worldwide major public health problem along with the aging of population. Osteoporotic fracture treatment has particular difficulties for high rate of implant fixation failure and increased non-union risk caused by delayed bone formation. Numerous previous studies have proven that osthol exerts anti-osteoporotic effect by restoring bone mineral density in animal models. We have found that osthol showed in vivo osteoanabolic effect to promote new bone formation in mice fracture healing process. Therefore, osthol may be a promising potential anabolic agent for treatment of osteoporosis and osteoporotic fracture. We plan to explore the pharmacological effect of osthol on ovariectomised osteoporotic fracture in female mice model in future study. Ovariectomy are performed on 16-week female C57/BL mice, femoral osteotomy are conducted two months later after develop postmenopausal bone loss. Mice are orally administrated with osthole in the presence or absence of bisphosphonates treatment. Since experimental evidences have suggested that bisphosphonates administration may have negative effect on bone healing process. We plan to evaluate the effect of osthol on bone mass recovery and bone healing in osteoporotic fracture; and to test the drug interaction of osthol and bisphosphonate.

461113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
461113.value: Bone fractures are the most common orthopedic problems. Although our body repairs broken bone naturally, the healing process takes months or even years, depending on severity of injury and complications. Osthol is a naturally derived bioactive compound isolated from medicinal plant Cnidium monnieri (L.) Cusson. This herb is commonly applied by traditional Chinese medicine practitioners for bone strengthening. In this study, we investigated the effect of osthol on bone fracture repair using femoral open fracture model in mice. A transverse fracture was created at the middle of femur with saw. Operated mice were given osthol solution or solvent alone by oral gavage or injection every day since postoperative week 1. Oral intake of osthol promoted bone formation during reparative phase and hence accelerated the whole bone fracture healing process in terms of plain radiography, micro-computed tomography, histological analysis and molecular imaging. Osthol may be a promising natural supplement that facilitates bone healing and benefits bone health.

461213.label: Realisation of objectives
461213.value: The goal of our study is to examine the involvement of β-defensins and their interaction with the CCR6 receptor in regulating sperm motility. We sought to achieve the goal with two specific aims: 1) to investigate the co-localization and possible protein-protein interaction between different β-defensin family members and CCR6 receptor on sperm; and 2) to investigate the effects of different β-defensins on the types of sperm motility elicited and the involvement of CCR6, and the possible underlying mechanisms. In Aim 1, we have first identified a number of β-defensins from the literature and Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database that are shown to be expressed in male and female reproductive tract. We then screened the expression of these β-defensins and found that β-defensin 1 (DEFB1) is expressed in the epididymis whereas β-defensin 119 (DEFB119) and its mouse homolog/ortholog β-defensin 19 (DEFB19) is expressed by the epithelial lining of the female reproductive tract. These β-defensins were selected for subsequent experiments. Since CCR6 receptor is known to interact with β-defensins, we have examined the protein-protein interaction of candidate β-defensins with CCR6 receptor by co-immunoprecipitation. Our results showed that both DEFB1 and DEFB119 could bind to CCR6 receptor on sperm. Immunofluorescence staining further demonstrated the co-localization of DEFB1 and CCR6 in the midpiece of sperm. (Detailed results have been published in Science Translational Medicine, Diao, et al. 2014, see attached paper). Together, our results showed that multiple β-defensins expressed in the reproductive tract could interact with the CCR6 receptor on sperm. In Aim 2, we have investigated the effects of candidate β-defensins on different forms of sperm motility and the possible underlying mechanisms. We mimicked the release of candidate β-defensins from epithelium by recombinant β-defensins. We have also attempted to deplete candidate β-defensins by neutralizing antibody treatment. Our results showed that treating sperm with recombinant DEFB1 did not affect sperm motility whereas DEFB1 neutralizing antibody significantly decreased sperm motility. On the other hand, recombinant DEFB19/DEFB119 treatment significantly increased sperm motility. These results suggest the differential roles of DEFB1 and DEFB19/119 on sperm motility. Since β-defensins are well recognized for their antimicrobial activity, we speculated a dual role of β-defensins in sperm. Indeed, we found that interference with DEFB1 function decreases both motility and bactericidal activity in normal sperm. The interaction between DEFB1 and CCR6 in sperm triggers Ca2+ mobilization that is important for sperm motility. Interference with CCR6 function also reduces motility and bactericidal activity of normal sperm. Notably, DEFB1 only modestly increase the intracellular cAMP level, suggesting that DEFB1-induced Ca2+ mobilization is independent of the cAMP pathway. DEFB1 also modestly promotes hyperactivated motility but has no effect on acrosome reaction. We went further than the proposed objectives, not only to elucidate the underlying mechanism of DEFB1 but also reveal a common defect in DEFB1 in male infertility associated with both asthenozoospermia (sperm with weak motility) and leukocytospermia (sperm with presence of high number of leukocytes due to infection), indicating a dual role of DEFB1 in defending male fertility. We demonstrated that the level of DEFB1 in sperm from infertile men exhibiting either leukocytospermia or asthenozoospermia, both with reduced motility and bactericidal activity in sperm, was found to be much lower compared to that of normal fertile sperm. Treatment of the patient's sperm with recombinant DEFB1 markedly restored DEFB1 expression, bactericidal activity, sperm quality (including % motility and forward motility) and egg-penetrating ability in sperm from both asthenozoospermia and leukocytospermia patients. The results from this part of the proposal suggested that treatment of defective sperm with recombinant DEFB1 protein may be a feasible treatment method for male infertility associated with poor sperm motility and genital tract infection. (Detailed results have been published in Science Translational Medicine, Diao, et al. 2014, see attached paper) We went on to investigate the role of DEFB119 on sperm motility in human sperm. We showed that recombinant DEFB119 treatment increases both sperm motility and hyperactivated motility and alters swimming parameters. The DEFB119-induced sperm motility can be inhibited by a neutralizing antibody against the CCR6 receptor, suggesting the involvement of CCR6 receptor in mediating the effect of DEBF119 on sperm motility. The results from previous experiments have suggested the differential roles of DEFB1 and DEFB119 on sperm motility. In corroboration to this idea, the molecular mechanisms underlying the regulation of sperm motility by DEFB1 and DEFB119 are different. We showed that DEFB119 also induces Ca2+ mobilization through binding to CCR6 receptor. However, the amplitude of Ca2+ mobilization is higher than that induced by DEFB1. Moreover, DEFB119 significantly increased cAMP level in sperm, suggesting the possible involvement of cAMP pathway in mediating the effect of DEFB119 on sperm motility, which may be accounted for the observed differential effects between DEFB119 and DEFB1 on sperm motility. (Manuscript in preparation, see attached abstract) Taken together, our results indicate that different β-defensins from male and female reproductive tract can both bind to the CCR6 receptor on sperm and regulate different forms of sperm motility that are essential for fertilization.

461213.label: Major findings and research outcome
461213.value: Our study has uncovered the differential roles of DEFB1 and DEFB19 (mouse)/DEFB119 (human) in regulating different forms of sperm motility and their underlying mechanisms. We have shown that DEFB1 is required for the maintenance of sperm motility whereas DEFB19/DEFB119 triggers hyperactivated motility. We have also demonstrated the involvement of CCR6 receptor in mediating the effect of both β-defensins on sperm motility. We have further shown that both DEFB1 and DEFB19/DEFB119 triggers Ca2+ mobilization where the effect of DEFB19/DEFB119 is stronger than that of DEFB1. (Manuscript in preparation, see attached abstract) The effect of DEFB1 on sperm motility together with its well-recognized antimicrobial activity has led to our discovery of a dual role of DEFB1 in defending male fertility, defects of which is associated with asthenozoospermia and leukocytospermia. Importantly, we further revealed that recombinant DEFB1 treatment significantly rescued the sperm parameters associated with both cohorts of patients, suggesting the potential implication of recombinant DEFB1 treatment as a feasible treatment method for male infertility associated with poor sperm motility and genital tract infection. (Detailed results have been published in Science Translational Medicine, Diao, et al. 2014, see attached paper).

461213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
461213.value: Various members of the β-defensins family are also known to be expressed in the female reproductive tract apart from the male reproductive tract. The presently discovered differential effect of DEFB1 and DEFB119 on sperm motility suggests that they may play different roles on sperm functions during the sperm transit through the male and female reproductive tract; i.e., β-defensins, such as DBEF119, released from the female reproductive tract may affect other sperm functions essential for fertilization. We have started a follow-up study to examine the role of β-defensins in sperm chemotaxis, a guided process for sperm to swim towards the egg. The discovery that deficient DEFB1 underlies male infertility associated with poor motility and genital tract infection together with the rescue effect of recombinant DEFB1 treatment on critical sperm parameters in sperm from patients suggested that DEFB1 is a promising target for the diagnosis and therapy of male infertility. We are currently exploring the association of other β-defensins with male and female infertility.

461213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
461213.value: Sperm motility is essential for the migration of sperm and thus fertilization. However, how sperm motility is initiated, maintained and hyper-activated in male and female reproductive tracts is poorly understood. Previous studies have shown that the involvement of β-defensin family, a group of small antimicrobial peptides, in the initiation of sperm motility. In this study, we have demonstrated that DEFB1 and DEFB119, which are expressed in the male and/or female reproductive tract, play differential roles in maintaining sperm motility and inducing hyperactivated motility. The effects of both β-defensins on sperm motility are mediated by the CCR6 receptor on sperm. DEFB1 and DEFB119 trigger different levels of calcium mobilization that may be attributed to cAMP-independent and dependent pathway respectively. Furthermore, we have demonstrated that deficient DEFB1 underlies male infertility associated with poor motility and genital tract infection. More importantly, recombinant DEFB1 treatment significantly improves critical sperm parameters, including motility and fertilizing capacity, in sperm obtained from infertility patients. Taken together, our results reveal critical and differential roles of β-defensins in different forms of sperm motility through their interaction with the CCR6 receptor on sperm, defects of which may underlie male infertility associated with poor motility and genital tract infection.

461513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
461513.value: The aim of this project is to determine the impact of deep vs light anesthesia on perioperative outcomes in high-risk patients undergoing major surgery. Millions of high-risk patients worldwide receive general anesthesia for major surgery every year. However, the optimal depth of anesthesia for these patients is currently unknown. Traditionally, deep anesthesia is commonly provided to avoid awareness during surgery and to reduce consequent stress response. However, recent cohort studies, as well as data from our own, reported a 20% increase in morbidity and mortality among high-risk surgical patients who received deeper rather than lighter anesthesia. Monitoring systems that use the electroencephalogram, such as the bispectral index (BIS), are now widely available to assess depth of anesthesia. In a number of studies, we have demonstrated that BIS monitoring can be used to target specific anesthetic depths during surgery and is useful in assisting anesthesiologists to optimize drug administration. In this pragmatic study, we plan to determine the appropriate depth of anesthesia for patients with significant comorbidities, using intraoperative BIS monitoring. We propose to carry out an international, randomized controlled trial to compare the effect of deep vs light general anesthesia on all-cause mortality in 6,500 high-risk patients at 12 months after major surgery. Secondary outcomes include disability-free survival, unintentional awareness during anesthesia, analgesic requirements, wound infection and postoperative cardiac complications. The findings of this study may be of considerable social and economic significance. If our study confirms that deep anesthesia contributes to serious postoperative complications, this finding should lead to a change in anesthetic practice around the world. 461813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
461813.value: There are ethnic differences in the prevalence of obesity and its related illnesses between Caucasians and Asians, within Asian populations, and within populations of the same ethnicity in different geographic locations. The unique dietary habits and food cultures of each ethnicity, which affect the postprandial oxidative stress (POS) may explain some of the ethnic or cultural differences in the prevalence of chronic disease. There are scanty data on the effect of diet or meal types on POS in ethnic Chinese population. Available trials in Caucasians have mainly used the artificial solid or liquid ‘meals’ approach which is incompatible with the real-life situation. This one-year randomized crossover study is proposed to compare the changes of POS after consumption of meals from different cultures in healthy Chinese adults, using a ‘real-life, cultural meal’ approach. We hypothesize that the changes of POS differ with meals from different cultures. Four cultural meals are chosen, namely Southern Chinese, Northern Chinese, American, and South Indian, based on the known prevalence of chronic diseases between Caucasians, Chinese and Indians, and within the Southern and Northern Chinese population. Thirty-four healthy and non-obese Chinese adults will be recruited. Four one-day studies separated by at least seven days will be conducted. On each study day, after an overnight fast, subjects will consume one of the cultural meals, allocated to them in random order. A catheter will be placed in a vein in the forearm for blood draws at pre-meal, 2, 4 and 6 hours postprandial. Urine samples will also be collected. After the pre-meal blood draw, subjects will consume the test meal within 20 minutes. No other foods or beverages will be consumed during the 6 hours postprandial period, except water. Postprandial changes of biomarkers of oxidative stress in blood and urine, as well as changes in blood glucose and lipid profiles will be measured. On the first test day, data on demographics, lifestyle, anthropometric parameters and blood pressure will be collected. The study does not aim to examine the effect of single nutrient component on POS. From the public health perspective, a ‘real-life, meal type’ approach is preferred over a single nutrient approach since people consume meals with combinations of various nutrients, and using a meal type approach is more relevant to the public. Findings from this study are expected to further inform the public about the healthier cultural meal types. 文獻指出不同種族的肥胖及相關疾病發病率各有不同，而不同種族的獨特飲食習慣及文化對餐後的氧化壓力所造成的影響亦有所不同，餐後的氧化壓力是形容當我們進食含高脂肪及/或碳水化合物的餐膳後體內所產生的氧化壓力變化。文獻指出當餐後的氧化壓力愈高，肥胖及相關疾病的風險會愈高，這或可解釋種族之間肥胖及相關疾病發病率的差異。文獻中很少記載有關中國人餐後的氧化壓力的數據。到目前為止，大部份有關餐後氧化壓力變化的研究只限於以白人為研究對象，而且大部份以提供人工化固體或流質餐膳為主，因此未能反映現實生活的餐膳進食情況。 這個為期12個月的隨機交叉研究希望利用『現實生活餐膳進食情況』的模式，比較中國健康成年人進食不同文化菜式的餐後氧化壓力變化，從而初步了解不同文化菜式對餐後氧化壓力變化的影響。研究假設不同文化菜式對餐後氧化壓力變化的影響會有所不同，基於文獻有關不同種族的肥胖及相關疾病發病率的數據，本研究會選定四個不同文化的菜式，包括廣東菜、中國北方菜、美式菜及南印度菜作為研究菜式。 研究將招募34名合資格參與本研究的中國藉健康成年人，研究人員會為參加者安排4天的測試，每次測試須相隔最少一週。參加者須在測試前一晚開始禁食，而在測試當日，參加者會因應隨機抽樣結果於30分鐘內進食其中一款特定菜式，包括廣東菜、中國北方菜、美式菜及南印度菜。研究人員將於進餐前、以及進餐後的2、4及6小時為參加者進行4次抽血及收集4次尿液樣本，除清水外，參加者在測試進行的6個小時內不可進食其他食物及飲料。研究人員會為參加者量度進餐前、以及進餐後的2、4及6小時血液及尿液中氧化壓力指標，和血糖、血脂及高敏-C反應蛋白的變化。在篩選檢查當日，參加者亦須完成一份有關個人資料及生活習慣的簡短問卷，以及量度身高、體重及血壓等。 本研究的設計不是著眼於探討單一營養素對餐後氧化壓力變化的影響，而是希望透過『現實生活餐膳進食情況』的模式，初步了解不同文化菜式對餐後氧化壓力變化的影響。研究結果將有助教育公眾認明及選擇較健康的菜式。

461813.label: Realisation of objectives
461813.value: The study was completed as scheduled. All key milestones as well as expected deliverables have been achieved. A total of 55 participants were screened for eligibility and 33 of them were eligible and completed the study. Data on these 33 subjects were included for final data analysis. The objective of the project was to investigate and differentiate the postprandial changes in biomarkers of oxidative stress including plasma allantoin and urine F2-isoprostanes (F2-IsoPs) after consumption of meals from different cultures in healthy Chinese adults. Our study was able to demonstrate significant differential effects of four meal types from different cultures, namely Cantonese, Northern Chinese, South Indian and American on postprandial oxidative stress (POS) in healthy adults. Our data showed that mean plasma allantoin concentration was significantly increased (p<0.05) for all meals at 2-hours after ingestion, levels peaked at 4-hours and declined by 6-hours post-ingestion, though baseline levels were regained only with the Cantonese meal. The magnitude of postprandial increase in plasma allantoin concentration was smallest with the Cantonese meal and greatest with the American meal. There was less marked differences in postprandial changes in urine F2-IsoPs across meals, but urine F2-IsoPs concentrations were significantly increased (p<0.05) for each meal during the 6-hour postprandial period. There were differential meal effects on the postprandial changes in plasma glucose and triglyceride concentrations. Postprandial triglyceride levels significantly increased (p<0.05) for all meals except for the Cantonese meal. Plasma high-sensitivity C-reactive protein did not change with time or meal type.

461813.value: The objective of the project was to investigate the postprandial changes in biomarkers of oxidative stress including plasma allantoin and urine F2-isoprostanes (F2-IsoPs) after consumption of meals from different cultures in healthy Chinese adults. Our study was able to demonstrate significant differential effects of four meal types from different cultures, namely Cantonese, Northern Chinese, South Indian and American on postprandial oxidative stress (POS) in healthy adults. Our data showed that mean plasma allantoin concentration was significantly increased (p<0.05) for all meals at 2-hours after ingestion, levels peaked at 4-hours and declined by 6-hours post-ingestion, though baseline levels were regained only with the Cantonese meal. The magnitude of postprandial increase in plasma allantoin concentration was smallest with the Cantonese meal and greatest with the American meal. There was less marked differences in postprandial changes in urine F2-IsoPs across meals, but urine F2-IsoPs concentrations were significantly increased (p<0.05) for each meal during the 6-hour postprandial period. An abstract with the preliminary findings of postprandial plasma glucose response to various cultural meals were accepted and presented as a poster presentation in the 9th Asia Pacific Conference on Clinical Nutrition. A manuscript will also be submitted to an international peer-reviewed journal.

461813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
461813.value: Compared to previous studies, our multiple cross-over study had a relatively large sample size and included common and accurate biomarkers of oxidative stress. We also used a ‘real-life, mixed meal’ approach with test meals reflecting the typical portion and the major features of different cultures. Our findings would therefore be much more useful and translational to individuals consuming mixed meals in a free living environment as compared to previous studies using laboratory or experimental settings. However, our study has several limitations. First, we did not measure the antioxidant and the polyunsaturated fatty acid level of the test meals and did not include measures of biomarkers of antioxidant capacity, specific apolipoproteins (e.g. apoB48 particles) as well as functional endpoints (e.g. endothelial function) that are of public health relevance. Further studies should include markers of antioxidant levels. Second, our study sample was healthy and normal weight individuals and predominated by female participants. Previous studies have suggested that postprandial responses vary with sex, BMI status, ethnicity as well as metabolic status. Therefore, future studies are suggested to compare the change of POS in these specific groups. Moreover, our results were based on only one single meal in the morning. The effect of consecutive meals on postprandial changes in oxidative stress remains to be explored. Besides, in view of increasing evidence to suggest that diet could affect the microbiota, the microbiota component could be considered in future investigations.

461813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
461813.value: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are the major causes of death and disability. One of the important causal factors underlying the development of NCDs is postprandial oxidative stress (POS), and this is known to increase after intake of food. However, which meal types that induce the most, or least, level of POS is uncertain. This study compared the changes of POS after consumption of meals from different cultures, using a ‘real-life, cultural meal’ approach. Four cultural meals were chosen, namely Cantonese, Northern Chinese, American, and South Indian. Thirty three healthy non-obese Chinese adults were recruited and consumed each meal in random order on four separate days. Changes of biomarkers of POS and other biochemical parameters in blood and urine were measured. Our study showed that change of POS was smallest in the Cantonese meal whereas it was greatest in the American meal. The latter possibly due to its relatively large meal size and high total fat, carbohydrate as well as sugar content in comparison to the other three meals. This study further provides information to inform the public about the healthier meal types and supports the notion of using a dietary basis to explain for the difference in the prevalence of NCDs.

461913.label: Realisation of objectives
461913.value: The primary goal of the study targets at characterizing the brain activation patterns of the three psychological paradigms (self-reflection, rumination and stimulus independent resting state) that may potentially differentiate the clinical state, trait and course of illness of depressive disorder. We thus design functional MRI experiments to compare the activation/deactivation and functional connectivity pattern of cortical midline structures under experimental conditions (self vs non-self; rumination vs distraction) OR resting state default brain activities, in association with different clinical phases of major depressive disorder (first onset current depressive state, recurrent illness with current depressive state, OR currently remitted with past depressive episode) and control subjects (not currently depressed and no lifetime history of depression). Our secondary goal aims at comparing anatomical and dynamic differences in brain level responses under the two experimental conditions (self-reflection and rumination), given the potential shared default mode network from prior studies that examine either psychological condition alone. Over the entire funding period and the no-cost extension period ( 38 months), a total of 90 participants, of which 45 were depressed patients in different stages of illness (first-onset, with past episodes currently in relapse, and with past episodes currently in remission) and 45 were matched healthy controls, were recruited. All of them underwent the functional MRI experiments that demand attention to self/ others and general stimulus presented in block and event-related designs, rumination induction paradigms along with two sets of resting scans before and after the task activation experiments. The inclusion of clinical subjects across the spectrum of lifetime and current major depressive disorder and their matched controls allow comparison of the activation/deactivation brain states related to self-reflection, rumination and resting state connectivity between healthy state and different stages of diseases.

461913.label: Major findings and research outcome
461913.value: Subjects' characteristics: Of all 90 participants, 74 of them were female, which constituted 80.4% of entire sample. In terms of education level, most of the subjects, reported they had secondary school level, which accounted for 66.3% in this study. Independent sample t-tests were conducted to make comparison of the depression symptom scores (Beck Depression Inventory) obtained from clinical subjects and their healthy controls. Generally, there was a significant difference in the scores for clinical group (M = 21.73, SD = 14.00) and healthy group (M = 4.54, SD = 4.32), t(89) = 7.65, p < .001. Specifically, t-test for different case-control conditions were carried out to investigate the difference between different clinical groups and their matched control counterparts. Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) scores of Group A subjects (M =29.43, SD = 12.16) were significantly higher than their healthy controls (M = 6.33, SD = 4.76), t(27) = 6.83, p < .001. For Group B (M = 29.13, SD = 10.64) and matched healthy subjects (M = 3.40, SD = 4.24), significant difference in BDI scores was observed, t(28) = 8.71, p < .001. Besides, it was indicated that subjects in Group C (M = 8.06, SD = 5.67) scored higher in BDI than the control subjects (M = 3.94, SD = 3.62), t(30) = 2.45, p < .05. In general, the self reference tasks induce brain activation states in cortical midline structures that are differentiable from non-self reference tasks, and the observation is consistent across different experimental designs using event-related or block design, suggesting the validity of the psychological experiment. Exploratory studies suggest the activation pattern are consistently different between depressed patients and healthy subjects irrespective of the clinical status of depressed subjects i.e., first onset, recurrent but in remission and recurrent in relapse. The clinical utility of self-reflection paradigm in assessing severity and prognosis of depressive illness can be further explored in future studies. Manuscripts are in preparation for submission to international journals on human brain mapping. The target journals include Neuroimage, Journal of Affective Disorder, Psychological Medicine and Biological Psychiatry.

462013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
462013.value: 肝炎是肝癌（HCC）的隱藏病因,累積証據顯示全身炎症反應在腫瘤的重要預後角色。過往十年，不同個人組別，包括我們的團隊，確認在肝癌病人多樣循環細胞激素預後能力。C反應蛋白與中性粒細胞與淋巴細胞比值等發炎替代成為肝癌獨立預後因素。這些數據建議循環發炎標記數可提供更多獨立於傳統分期的預後資料。 即使臨床人員可取得血清標別，循環發炎標記應用在臨床情况仍有限。當中有多個原因:第一，即使個別標記能預測肝癌整體生存率，亦可能發炎過程及預後與多過一個標記有關。現今沒有大型研究同步評估肝癌一系列發炎標記的預後。結果每個循環標記互動不清晰。第二，與在肝癌預後，發炎標記與現行分期數據不足。第三，與西方比較，更多湧現數據指出亞洲肝癌有獨有的臨床特點和預後。所以有研究需要去善用發炎標記於臨床應用上。初期數據顯示兩種循環發炎細胞激素、interleukin-6 and -10作為獨交預後因素，一個以這兩個標記及支援向量機方法可會增加BCLC及CUPI分期的預後價值。

462013.label: Realisation of objectives
462013.value: Objective 1: To determine the individual ability of a panel of circulating inflammatory markers for prognostication of HCC Patients The study population came from a prospective cohort of patients recruited in the multi-disciplinary hepatoma clinic at the Prince of Wales Hospital from January 2009 to December 2012. Part of the cohort has been reported in previous studies. The diagnosis of HCC was made in accordance with the guideline established by the American Association for the Study of Liver disease.34 The management of HCC was decided by a multidisciplinary team consisting of hepatobiliary surgeons, medical oncologist and interventional radiologists. The composition of the cohort, archival of of serum samples as well as this study itself have all been approved by the Joint Chinese University of Hong Kong-New Territories East Cluster Research Ethics Committee. Clinical parameters and staging system All patients consented to assessment of clinical data and acquisition of blood samples for research purpose at the time of consent. Consented patients underwent evaluation by clinical investigators to record the baseline demographics, clinical parameters, and laboratory parameters including liver, renal and hematological function and serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP). Tumor staging was decided immediately after availability of laboratory data according to the Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) system. At the time of consent, both serum and plasma samples were obtained from each subject and archived for future research. The outcome and survival of each patient were followed up routinely in the clinic. Overall survival was defined from the time of surgery to the time of HCC-related death, or last follow-up if death had not occurred. Measurement of circulating markers The serum cytokine concentrations of serum inflammatory markers were determined by the Human Cytokine Array 41-plex and Human Neurodegenerative Disease 1-plex assays (Eve Technologies, Alberta, Canada). In brief, 50 μL of serum samples were incubated with color-coded polystyrene beads conjugated with capture antibodies where each type of bead specifically identified one kind of cytokine. A total of 42 serum cytokines were measured, namely the epidermal growth factor (EGF), FGF-2, eotaxin-1, transforming growth factor-alpha (TGF-α),G-CSF, FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3 ligand (Flt-3L), granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF), fractalkine, interferon alpha 2 (IFNα2), interferon gamma (IFNγ), chemokine (C-X-C motif) ligand 1, IL-10, monocyte chemotactic protein-3 (MCP-3), interleukin 12 p40 subunit (IL-12p40), macrophage-derived chemokine (MDC), IL-12p70, platelet-derived growth factor–AA dimer (PDGF-AA), IL-13, platelet-derived growth factor–BB dimer (PDGF-BB), interleukin 15 (IL-15), soluble CD40 ligand (sCD40L), IL-17A, IL-1RA, IL-1α, IL-9, IL-1β, IL-2, IL-3, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-7, IL-8, IP-10, MCP-1, MIP-1, MIP-1, RANTES, TNFα, TNFβ, VEGF-A and CRP. The bead-bound analytes were then detected by a second antibody for production of a fluorescent signal. This was run through a multiplex suspension array system (Bio-Plex 200; Bio-Rad Laboratories, CA, USA) which measured the amount of fluorescent signal produced from each of the beads. The fluorescent signal detected is proportional to the amount of target analyte and was quantified relative to a standard curve. Each serum sample was measured in duplicate with the average value used in the study. The laboratory personnels who conducted the assay were blinded to the study objectives and clinical data. The entire cohort was randomly divided into training and validation cohorts. A multivariate analysis with the Cox proportional hazard model was conducted to analyze the prognostication of each marker in the training cohort. The objective 1 was 100% completed. Objective 2: To develop a model based on combination of circulating inflammatory markers for prognostication of HCC Following the findings of independent markers in the multivariate analysis in the training cohort, an inflammatory model was built up to predict survival of patients. The prognostic performance of the novel model was evaluated by the following: (1) homogeneity within classification (differences in survival time among patients classified in the same group); (2) discriminatory ability (greater differences in survival time among patients in different groups); and (3) monotonicity of gradients (mean survival time in a more favorable group is longer than in a less favorable group). The likelihood ratio test was applied to evaluate the homogeneity and monotonicity. The Harrell’s concordance index (c-index) was calculated by bootstrapping with 100 resamples to estimate the discriminatory ability. All statistical analyses were performed by R version 3.02 (R Foundation for Statistical Computing, Vienna, Austria). A 2-tailed P-value <0.05 was regarded as statistically significant. The prognostic performance of the novel model was validated in the validation cohort of the study. The Kaplan-Meier method was used to estimate the survival rates for different groups. The equivalences of the survival curves were tested by log-rank statistics. The Cox proportional hazards model was employed for survival analyses. The objective 2 was 100% completed. Objective 3: To evaluate the performance of combined model of circulating inflammatory marker and clinical tumor staging system for prognostication of HCC The staging systems, namely, the BCLC system, CUPI system and CLIP score, were determined in each patient at the time of diagnosis. The values of markers with independent prognostication were studied in each stage system to evaluate if there is any additional prognostication offered by the marker. A multivariate analysis with the Cox proportional hazard model was conducted to analyze the prognostication of each marker in the each staging system for HCC. The objective 3 was 100% completed.

462013.label: Major findings and research outcome
462013.value: 1. Baseline characteristics were summarized in Table 1. 2. Interleuk-8 (IL-8) was the most potent prognostic factor in the univariate analysis. Factors including the neutrophil (Spearman rho 0.502, p<0.001); IL-17a (rho 0.610, p<0.001), IL-6 (rho 0.531, p<0.001) and TGF-α (rho 0.523, p<0.001)] were strongly correlated with IL-8 and hence excluded from the multivarite analysis to minimize multicollinearity. Similarly, TNF-α was correlated with FGF-2 (rho 0.566, p<0.001) and IFN-γ (rho 0.628, p<0.001), so both FGF-1 and IFN-γ were also excluded in the multivariate analysis. Total seven markers were finally evaluated in the multivariate analysis, which showed that albumin [hazard ratio (HR) 0.95, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.91-1.00; p=0.032], CRP (HR 1.11, 95% CI: 1.04-1.18; p=0.003) and IL-8 (HR 5.82, 95% CI: 3.20-10.18; p<0.001) were independent prognostic factors for overall survival (Table 2) 3. To make the three independent prognostic markers, namely IL-8, CRP and albumin, readily applicable in clinical practice, these markers were transformed into dichotomous forms instead of continuous variables. The cutoff values of albumin <35 g/L and CRP ≥10 mg/dL were referenced from the original IBI 12, while the cutoff of log(IL-8) ≥1.8 was determined by a receiver operator characteristic curve. To make sure that these three dichotomous parameters were prognostic indicators which were independent of tumor stage, a separate multivarite analysis was conducted, which persistently showed that log(IL-8) ≥1.8 was an independent prognosticator together with CRP ≥10 mg/dL and albumin <35 g/L in the training cohort (Table 3). A novel inflammatory index was constructed on the basis on IBI, with 1 score given for each factor when the subject has albumin <35g/L, CRP≥10mg/dL or log IL-8≥1.8, respectively (Table 4). The summation of score from these dichotomous values of albumin, CRP and log IL8 will give rise to a score ranging from 0 to 3. 4. This novel inflammatory index (known as modified IBI in subsequent discussion) could divide the cohort into four arms of patients with different overall survival (P<0.0001; Figure 1). The respective median overall survival for score 0, 1, 2 and 3 was 68.3, 10.0, 4.4 and 2.0 months. The performance of the new index was also validated in the validation cohort (Figure 2) with median overall survival in score 0, 1, 2 and 3 of 36.2, 15.6, 5.3 and 1.5 months respectively. The prognostic performance of modified IBI was superior to other existing inflammatory indices in terms of homogeneity likelihood ratio and c-index (Table 5). 5. Finally, it was found that both IL-8 and CRP could offer additional prognostic information in BCLC, CUPI and CLIP (p<0.0001) (Table 6). For the tables and figures, please refer to section 11.

462013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
462013.value: Future works should be focused to 1. Validation of the novel modifified inflammation-based index (IBI) in other cohorts of HCC. 2. Study the clinical and therapeutic implications of the modified inflammation-based index in pateints with advanced HCC 3. A more accurate stratification of systemic inflammation with the modified IBI may help identify responders for immunotherapeutics in HCC, and this hypothesis may be studied in clinical trials with paired serum samples in the future.

462013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
462013.value: This study has studied the level of mutiple markers in the blood of patients with liver cancers. It was found that three blood markers, namly higher interleukin-8 level, higher C-reactive protein level and lower level of albumin, are associated with worse outcome in patients with liver cancer. When combining these three factors in a scoring system, it was found that this scoring system could stratify the outcomes of patients with high accuracy. These markers also have additional meaning on existing staging systems of liver cancers.

462613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
462613.value: Lung cancer, 80-85% of which is non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC), is the leading cause of cancer deaths in the world including Hong Kong. One major factor that contributes to the high mortality is due to the failure to detect the tumor at the early stage, resulting in the tumor being unresctable by the time of diagnosis. Our results have shown that the levels of 15-lipoxygenases (15-LOXs) and their metabolite 15(S)-hydroxy-eicosatetraenoic acid (15S-HETE) and 13 (S)-hydroxyoctadecadienoic acid (13S-HODE) were significantly reduced in NSCLC cancer tissue samples compared with lung non-cancer tissues. To determine the role of 15-LOXs, 15S-HETE and 13S-HODE in the development of lung cancer, we monitored their levels in smoking carcinogen NNK-induced mouse lung tumorigenesis. All tumors induced by NNK were pathologically confirmed to be NSCLC. The mouse model results confirmed the data obtained in human and further revealed that the reduction of 15S-HETE and 13S-HODE predated the occurrence of lung tumors. In order to determine whether 15S-HETE and 13S-HODE can serve as early biomarkers for lung cancer, we measured the levels of both molecules in 99 serum samples obtained from patients with NSCLC. As expected, serum 15S-HETE and 13S-HODE were markedly reduced in NSCLC, compared with normal healthy subjects. Moreover, we found that the concentrations of these two molecules in serum were positively correlated with their levels in the lung cancer tissues. The above data strongly suggest that serum 15S-HETE and 13S-HODE may serve as early biomarkers for the diagnosis of NSCLC. In this proposal, we plan to prospectively monitor serum 15S-HETE and 13S-HODE in heavy smokers with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), with aim to develop them as the early diagnostic biomarkers for NSCLC. This prospective study will be performed in a cohort of heavy smokers with COPD from three teaching hospitals in southern China. 15(S)-HETE和13(S)-HODE用於早期診斷合併有慢性阻塞性肺病的肺非小細胞肺癌的研究 目前低劑量螺施CT(LDSCT)被認為是一種最為有效早期檢測肺腫瘤的方法，但是，它有一些不足之處，例如高假陽性率及誤診。我們近來的研究顯示15(S)-HETE和13(S)-HODE水平在肺癌明顯地降低，且在動物肺癌形成的實驗中，此兩種分子的降低可發生在肺腫瘤形成之前，這個結果提示這兩種分子可能是早期診斷肺癌的指標。因此，我們計劃對15(S)-HETE和13(S)-HODE在肺癌的診斷價值進行評估。眾所周知，吸煙與慢阻肺病（COPD）是導致肺癌發生的主因，所以，本研究將在重度吸煙的COPD人群中展開監測血中15(S)-HETE和13(S)-HODE水平。本研究結果將會幫助產生一個早期肺癌的診斷方法, 提高早期肺癌診斷率。

462613.label: Realisation of objectives
462613.value: Totally 409 smokers with COPD were recruited from 3 major hospitals in Hong Kong and Guangdong for this study. Patients were followed up every 6 months for body check-up and lung screen for NSCLC. Blood samples were taken every 6 months and the levels of 15S-HETE and 13S-HODE were measured by ELISA kits. In addition to 409 smokers with COPD, we have also collected blood samples from 337 healthy subjects and the levels of 15S-HETE and 13S-HODE were also determined as controls. We have found 9 NSCLC cases in 409 smokers with COPD and the levels of 15S-HETE were significantly reduced before NSCLC was diagnosed. However, the levels of 13S-HODE were not obviously changed. Though the number (409) of smokers with COPD recruited is more than 250 subjects proposed in the application, we note that some patients did not show up for the schedule follow-up and the dropout rate is 28.17%. Also a significant number of cases have not been followed up to 5 years because in the 1st year, only 111 cases were recruited. Since the development of NSCLC is a very slow process, a long period (10 years or more) of the follow-up should greatly enhance the value of this study.

462613.label: Major findings and research outcome
462613.value: 1. The level of 15S-HETE (but not 13S-HODE) in blood is decreased around 6-12 months before NSCLC is diagnosis. We monitored 15S-HETE in 409 smokers with COPD for up to 5 years and found that NSCLC was developed in 9 patients. Significantly, the level of 15S-HETE in blood was obviously reduced about 6 - 12 months before NSCLC was diagnosed. Therefore, 15S-HETE is a potential early diagnosis biomarker for NSCLC occurred in smokers with COPD. The relevant results were presented in 2 international conferences (See Part C, Figure 1). 2. Our in vitro cultured cell experiments have demonstrated that the exogenous or endogenous 13(S)-HODE and 15(S)-HETE (especially the latter) can functionally inhibit NSCLC likely by activating PPARγ. The restoration of 15-LOXs activities to increase the production of endogenous 15(S)-HETE and 13(S)-HODE may offer a novel research direction for the molecular targeting treatment of smoking-related NSCLC. The relevant results have been published (Please see Part C: Cancer. 2015;121 Suppl 17:3130-45). 3. Air pollutant fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is experimentally a lung-tumorigen and it can work in a way similar to smoking carcinogen NNK to cause lung tumorigenesis via reducing 15-LOX metabolites 13(S)-HODE and 15(S)-HETE, particularly the latter. The relevant results were presented in an international conference (See Part C). 4. Early studies have shown that the reduction of 15-LOXs can promote FOXP3 (Diabetes. 2008;57:199) and we confirmed it in NSCLC cells. Thus, we have tested the function of FOXP3 in NSCLC and demonstrated that FOXP3 can promote the growth of NSCLC via stimulating cancer cell stemness and the Wnt-b-catenin/Notch1 signaling pathways. The relevant results have been published in two papers (Please see Part C: Mol Cancer. 2017;16:124. Ther Adv Med Oncol. 2019;11:1758835919855228).

462613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
462613.value: 1. Though smoking and COPD contribute to the development of NSCLC, NSCLC will eventually develop in only a small number of smokers with COPD (about 2-8%). Furthermore, lung carcinogenesis is a chronic process (probably 10 - 50 years). Therefore, one major limitation of this study is that the follow-up period (up to 5 years) is too short. A longer period (10 years or more) of the follow-up should greatly enhance the value of this study. 2. Another limitation of this study is that the follow-up frequency (every 6 months) is low. We initially would like to follow up patients every 3 months. However, clinically the follow-up period for patients in the hospitals involved is very 6 months. If the plan of every 3 months is executed, much more funds are needed to change the clinical schedule (financial supports for clinical doctors, nurses and relevant clinical tests). However, such an amount of funds is beyond the current funding model. 3. This study will also be benefited by recruiting more cases, for example 1000. 4. It will be idea if we can develop a mechanism to prevent or reduce the dropout. A certain amount of financial aid to patients may work.

462613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
462613.value: Although many diagnostic methods for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) have been developed, the early diagnosis of NSCLC is far from satisfactory. Early detection of NSCLC is very critical because if NSCLC can be detected at the earlier stage, most of cases can be cured via surgical resection of the tumor. Among various metabolites in NSCLC, we have discovered the changes in certain metabolites from 15-lipoxygenases (15-LOXs) in the very early stage of lung tumorigenesis. These diagnosis-potential metabolites included 15(S)-hydroxy-eicosatetraenoic acid (15S-HETE) and 13(S)-hydroxyoctadecadienoic acid (13S-HODE). By following-up the high risk population, 409 smokers with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) for upto 5 years, NSCLC developed in 9 patients. Significantly, we found that the level of 15S-HETE (but not 13S-HODE) in blood was markedly decreased around 6-12 months before NSCLC was diagnosis. In cultured cell systems, we have demonstrated that 15(S)-HETE could functionally inhibit the growth of NSCLC via targeting several molecular pathways including cancer cell stemness and the Wnt-b-catenin, Notch1 and PPARγ signalings. In conclusion, the reduction of 15S-HETE predates the clinical diagnosis of NSCLC, making it a potential early diagnosis biomarker for NSCLC occurred in smokers with COPD. 15S-HETE can functionally inhibit the growth of NSCLC.

462713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
462713.value: The aim of this project is to identify and functionally characterize long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) associated with human pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). PDAC is aggressive and the existing therapeutic approaches are ineffective. Early investigations have identified critical molecules such as Kras, p16, p53 and DPC4 associated with the development and progression of PDAC. Despite progress in developing therapeutic strategies, overall survival of patients has little improvement for the past 20 years. Therefore, it is of urgent significance to identify novel therapeutic targets. Advance in RNA sequencing technology unravels massive amount of non-protein coding RNAs. LncRNAs, with length generally over 200 nucleotides, possess key biological functions including histone-codes establishment, genomic imprinting and dosage compensation. Accumulating evidence suggests that dysregulation of lncRNAs heavily contributes to the pathology of cancers. However, the role of lncRNAs in PDAC remains largely unexplored. We have been attempting to identify critical lncRNAs associated with PDAC. By lncRNA microarray, we identified lncRNAs differentially expressed in human PDAC tumors compared to adjacent non-tumor tissues. Our results indicated a distinct upregulation of HOTTIP, HOTAIR, nc-HOXB9-186+ and downregulation of AK311005 in PDAC samples. Similarly, HOTAIR has been previously reported to be overexpressed in PDAC. However, the dysregulation of the other three lncRNAs in cancer has not been reported. We first showed that HOTTIP was frequently upregulated in PDAC cell lines and primary tumors. We further showed that HOTTIP may play critical roles in PDAC because siRNAs targeting HOTTIP dramatically inhibited PDAC cell growth. The gene expression microarray identified a subset of genes responsive to depletion of HOTTIP in PDAC cells. Similarly, we observed an inhibition of PDAC cell growth after we knocked down the potential HOTTIP target genes CHI3L1, CLIC5 and CYB5R2. Targets including CYP26B1 and CLIC5 were regulated along the canonical HOTTIP-HOXA13 pathway, whereas our preliminary data suggested a novel non-canonical pathway of HOTTIP to directly transactivate genes in PDAC cells that possess critical functions. Based on the inspired promising result, we intend to 1) characterize the role of HOTTIP in PDAC; 2) delineate the HOTTIP regulatory pathway and identify PDAC-associated HOTTIP targets; 3) investigate the clinical implication of HOTTIP pathway in PDAC. The role of AK311005 in PDAC will also be characterized. Knowledge gained from this project will reveal the roles of lncRNAs in PDAC and potentially lead to new diagnostic and therapeutic targets. 本課題的目的是鑒別與胰腺導管腺癌相關的長鏈非編碼核糖核酸（lncRNA）並進行功能分析。以往的研究表明Kras, p16, p53, DPC4與胰腺癌的發生發展密切相關。儘管在治療上取得了一些進展，胰腺癌病人的整體存活率在過去的20年沒有改變。因此迫切需要鑒別新的治療靶點。lncRNA的長度一般大於200核苷酸，在多種生物進程中起了非常重要的作用。越來越多的證據表明lncRNA失調對腫瘤發生起了重要作用。然而，lncRNA在胰腺癌中的作用仍有待研究。 利用基因晶片技術，我們找到了在人胰腺癌腫瘤組織和鄰近正常組織差異表達的lncRNA。我們的結果表明HOTTIP, HOTAIR, nc-HOXB9-186在胰腺癌中顯著上調。已有的研究已經證實HOTAIR在胰腺癌中顯著上調。然而其它lncRNA的失調仍未見報導。我們的實驗證實HOTTIP在胰腺癌細胞株及腫瘤組織中高表達。針對HOTTIP的siRNAs顯著抑制胰腺癌細胞生長。基因表達晶片結果找到了一些受HOTTIP調控的基因。 基於前期研究的結果，我們計畫1）分析HOTTIP在胰腺癌中的功能；2）解析HOTTIP調控通路及鑒別胰腺癌相關的HOTTIP靶分子；3）研究HOTTIP通路在胰腺癌中的臨床意義。本課題的研究成果將揭示胰腺癌中lncRNA的功能並有可能發現新的診斷及治療靶。

462713.label: Realisation of objectives
462713.value: 1 To characterize the role of HOTTIP in PDAC. We analyzed the expression profiles of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) by microarray in 4 pairs of PDAC tumor and paired non-tumor tissues. We focused on lncRNAs which were dysregulated in all 4 patients. We observed the up-regulation of HOXA transcript at the distal tip (HOTTIP) in PDAC tumor. We profiled HOTTIP expression in a panel of PDAC cell lines (PANC-1, SW1990, Capan-2, PANC0403, CFPAC-1 and BxPC-3), compared with non-tumorigenic human pancreatic ductal epithelial cells (HPDE). We found that HOTTIP was significantly up-regulated in PDAC cell lines. In addition, we observed that HOTTIP was up-regulated in PDAC tumor tissues, compared adjacent non-tumor tissue. This suggested that HOTTIP may promote PDAC development. Therefore, we knock-down HOTTIP by siRNA, and knock-down efficiency was validated by qPCR. Depletion of HOTTIP significantly inhibited the growth and invasiveness of PANC-1 and SW1990 cells. Also, depletion of HOTTIP promoted cell apoptosis and gemcitabine sensitivity. Then, we attempted to study the oncogenic role of HOTTIP in PDAC through overexpressing HOTTIP in HPDE cells. As expected, overexpression of HOTTIP promoted cell growth in HPDE cells. Collectively, we found that HOTTIP plays an important role in PDAC carcinogenesis through promoting cell growth and invasion, developing gemcitabine resistance, and inhibiting apoptosis. 2 To delineate the HOTTIP regulatory pathway and identify PDAC-associated HOTTIP targets. After characterizing the role of HOTTIP in PDAC carcinogenesis. We further elucidated the molecular mechanism in HOTTIP-mediated PDAC development. To identify HOTTIP targets, we knock-down HOTTIP and performed microarray. We focused on dysregulated targets which have been reported in cancer development; i.e. CYB5R2, SULT1A1, CYP26B1, CLIC5, CHI3L1 and UCP2. Chitinase 3-like 1 (CHI3L1), a secreted glycoprotein, plays an important role in carcinogenesis. Up-regulation of CHI3L1 promoted cell proliferation, invasion and drug-resistance in various cancers, including colorectal cancer, glioma, and papillary thyroid carcinoma. Chloride intracellular channel 5 (CLIC5) promotes cell proliferation in prostate cancer and functions as metastatic marker in breast cancer. CLIC family member CLIC1 is also expressed in PDAC tumors and prostate cancer, and promotes cancer proliferation. Uncoupling protein 2 (UCP2) protect colorectal cancer cells from apoptosis. However, UCP2 functions as tumor suppressor in glioma through mediating mitochondrial retrograde signaling. Their roles in PDAC development are fully understood. The retinoic acid metabolic enzyme cytochrome P450 26B1 (CYP26B1), which is a member of phase I metabolic enzyme, is reported to be involved in oncogenesis in oral squamous cell carcinoma and colorectal cancer through the development of drug resistance via retinoic acid signaling pathway. Sulfotransferase (SULT) is up-regulated during oncogenesis and are associated with cancer survival in gastrointestinal cancer. In this study, we found that CYP26B1, CYB5R2, CHI3L1, SULT1A1, CLIC5 and UCP2 were up-regulated in PDAC tissues and cell lines, and were positively correlated to HOTTIP expression. Importantly, CYB5R2 and CLIC5 promoted cell proliferation; CHI3L1 was involved in cell invasion; CYP26B1 and SULT1A1 were responsible gemcitabine resistance; and UCP2 inhibited cell apoptosis. Collectively, our results demonstrated that CYP26B1, CYB5R2, CHI3L1, SULT1A1, CLIC5 and UCP2 played important roles in PDAC development. Previous studies demonstrated the role of HOTTIP in gene regulation. HOTTIP complexes with adaptor protein WDR5 and methyltransferase MLL1 to drive gene activating H3K4me3 at the promoter. Through chromosome looping, HOTTIP is brought close to nearby HOXA cluster to activate HOXA13. HOTTIP-HOXA13 axis is frequently involved in carcinogenesis. Therefore, we investigated whether these HOTTIP were also regulated under HOTTIP-HOXA13 pathway. We discovered the downstream targets of HOTTIP-HOXA13 axis; CHI3L1, CYP26B1, CLIC5 and UCP2. We found that HOXA13 promoted the expression of its targets via binding to their promoters. Also, depletion of HOXA13 by siRNA inhibited the expression of CHI3L1, CYP26B1, CLIC5 and UCP2. Therefore, we suggested that CHI3L1, CYP26B1, CLIC5 and UCP2 were regulated under canonical HOTTIP-HOXA13 pathway. Meanwhile, our research revealed the novel roles of HOTTIP in promoting PDAC development, apart from regulating gene expression through HOXA13 axis. Since CYB5R2 and SULTIA1 were not sensitive to HOXA13 knockdown, they may be the non-canonical targets of HOTTIP. Since HOTTIP formed complex with WDR5 and MLL, resulting in activation of HOXA genes through H3K4 trimethylation, we hypothesized that CYB5R2 and SULT1A1 were under the regulation of HOTTIP/WDR5/MLL complex. First, we observed the occupancies of HOTTIP, WDR5, MLL1 and H3K4me3 at the promoter of CYB5R2 and SULT1A1. Their enrichment levels were up-regulated in PDAC cell lines. Also, knock-down of MLL and WDR5 significantly inhibited the expression of CYB5R2 and SULT1A1. These results suggested that HOTTIP may activates distant genes such as CYB5R2 and SULT1A1, even in other chromosomes, instead of nearby HOXA gene clusters. Many studies in the past focused on HOTTIP-mediated carcinogenesis through regulation of nearby HOXA gene cluster. The novel regulatory pathway, which was demonstrated by our group, suggested that chromosome looping may not be the sole mechanism for HOTTIP-mediated gene regulation. 3 To investigate the clinical implication of HOTTIP pathway in PDAC. We measured the expression of HOTTIP and its targets (CYP26B1, CYB5R2, CHI3L1, SULT1A1, CLIC5 and UCP2) in PDAC tumor tissues, which were obtained from Prince of Wales Hospital, Hong Kong, by both qPCR and ISH. We observed that they were significantly up-regulated in PDAC tumor tissues, compared adjacent non-tumor tissue. In addition, we observed strong correlation between HOTTIP level and the expression of its targets. These results indicated that HOTTIP-regulatory pathway could be reflected in the patient PDAC tumors. Since our findings demonstrated that HOTTIP played an important role in PDAC development, we attempted to investigate the regulatory mechanism of HOTTIP. Bioinformatics analysis revealed that several miRNAs regulated HOTTIP expression through direct interaction. Among those potential targets, we focused on miR-424 and miR-497, which are oncogene and tumor suppressor respectively in many cancers, including PDAC. We hypothesized that miR-424 and miR-497 regulated the expression of HOTTIP through direct interaction to HOTTIP in PDAC. Overexpression of miR-424 by transfecting the miRNA mimics significantly up-regulated HOTTIP expression. As expected, transfecting PDAC cells with miR-497 mimics and inhibitors gave opposite results. Overexpression of miR-497 by miRNA mimics degraded HOTTIP, while inhibiting miR-497 promoted the expression of HOTAIR in PDAC cells. In addition, RNA immunoprecipitation analysis showed that HOTTIP bound to the miRNA effector Ago-2 in PANC-1 cells. This suggested that HOTTIP was regulated by miR-497 and miR-424 in Ago-2 dependent manner. Collectively, we found that miR-497 was the post-transcriptional suppressor of HOTTIP, while miR-424 was the novel modulator in regulating HOTTIP expression in PDAC. Our findings suggested that miR-497 and miR-424 can be a novel therapeutic target in modulating the HOTTIP level in PDAC. Restoration of miR-497 and miR-424 that inhibited HOTTIP may be a potential therapeutic for PDAC.

462713.label: Major findings and research outcome
462713.value: The long non-coding RNA HOXA transcript at the distal tip (HOTTIP) is frequently up-regulated in various cancers, including pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). HOTTIP complexes with adaptor protein WDR5 and methyltransferase MLL1 to drive gene activating H3K4me3 at the promoter. Through chromosome looping, HOTTIP is brought close to nearby HOXA cluster to activate HOXA13. HOTTIP-HOXA13 axis is frequently involved in carcinogenesis. In this project, we found that HOTTIP plays an important role in PDAC carcinogenesis through promoting cell growth and invasion, developing gemcitabine resistance, and inhibiting apoptosis. We identified the downstream targets of HOTTIP-HOXA13 axis: CYP26B1, CLIC5, CHI3L1 and UCP2, which were responsible for gemcitabine resistance, cell proliferation, cell invasion and resistance of apoptosis in PDAC. Importantly, we identified the novel oncogenic mechanism of HOTTIP in PDAC. HOTTIP/WDR5/MLL complex directly bound to CYB5R2 and SULT1A1, which were in other chromosomes. The resulted H3K4me3 promoted the expression of CYB5R2 and SULT1A1, which promoted cell proliferation and gemcitabine resistance respectively in PDAC. This direct interaction between HOTTIP and CYB5R2 or SULT1A1, without the involvement of HOXA13, demonstrated that HOTTIP-HOXA axis was not the sole mechanism of HOTTIP-mediated carcinogenesis in PDAC. In addition, we first to showed that HOTTIP was regulated by miR-424 and miR-497 in PDAC. miR-497 was aberrantly inhibited in various cancer, such as renal carcinoma and angiosarcoma. In PDAC, miR-497 was also down-regulated and was associated with poor prognosis. As a tumor suppressor, miR-497 inhibited cell proliferation, gemcitabine sensitivity, angiogenesis and metastasis. Notably, different from miR-497, we discovered miR-424 as the novel modulator in regulating HOTTIP expression in PDAC. Up-regulation of miR-424 promoted carcinogenesis in various solid tumors. Our findings suggested that miR-497 and miR-424 can be a novel therapeutic target in modulating the HOTTIP level in PDAC. Knock-down of miR-497 promoted the expression of HOTTIP, while knock-down of miR-424 degraded HOTTIP. Therefore, in this project, we demonstrated that miR-424 modulate the expression of HOTTIP, while miR-49 inhibited HOTTIP. Collectively, miR-497 and miR-424 can be a novel therapeutic target in modulating the HOTTIP level in PDAC.

462713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
462713.value: In this project, we demonstrated a novel mechanism of HOTTIP-mediated PDAC carcinogenesis. Importantly, we illustrated the mechanism which explains why HOTTIP is up-regulated in gastrointestinal cancer, including PDAC. We found that miR-424 modulates the expression of HOTTIP, whereas miR-497 inhibits HOTTIP expression. These findings suggested that miR-497 and miR-424 can be a novel therapeutic target in modulating the HOTTIP level in PDAC. Recently, we developed a high through-put screening method to discover small molecule miRNA modulator. A report is constructed by cloning miRNA sequence into firefly luciferase system. High through-put drug screening is performed by adding drugs to the cells with miRNA reporter, followed by measurement of luciferase activity. An increase or decrease in luciferase activity suggested the effect of drugs on miRNA’s activity. This screening method may be used in developing novel miR-497 modulator and miR-424 inhibitor, which in turn inhibited HOTTIP in gastrointestinal cancer.

462713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
462713.value: HOTTIP is up-regulated in various solid tumors, but its role in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains unclear. We found that HOTTIP promotes PDAC cell growth, invasion and developing drug resistance. Apart from canonical HOTTIP-HOXA13 pathway, in which HOTTIP activates nearby HOXA13 gene, we identified novel mechanism in HOTTIP-mediated carcinogenesis. In this mechanism, HOTTIP interacts with genes in other chromosomes and promotes their expression. In addition, we identified novel downstream targets: CYB5R2, SULT1A1, CYP26B1, CLIC5, CHI3L1 and UCP2, which also play an important roles in cancer development, under these canonical and non-canonical mechanisms. Importantly, we discovered a novel mechanism in regulating HOTTIP expression in gastrointestinal cancer. We found that miR-424 promotes HOTTIP expression, while miR-497 inhibited HOTTIP. These finding can lead to the drug development in modulating the expression of miR-424 and miR-497, which in turn inhibits HOTTIP expression and cancer growth.

462813.label: Realisation of objectives
462813.value: The project had the six objectives. The project went well and all the experiments were conducted as originally planned in the proposal. We had completed the six objectives as expected (100%). In brief, we used hamsters as a model to investigate the effect of sesamin on plasma cholesterol, finding that sesamin was effective in reducing plasma total cholesterol and LDL cholesterol. Such cholesterol-lowering activity of sesamin was mediated by its inhibition on cholesterol absorption via down regulation of gene expression of NPC1L1, ACAT2, MTP and ABCG5/8. We also compared the cholesterol-lowering activity of sesamin with β-sitosterol, finding it was less effective than β-sitosterol because the latter had strong inhibition on cholesterol absorption. The project was productive and we have published three papers in the mainstream journals of food/nutritional science field.
