462813.label: Major findings and research outcome
462813.value: One abundant compound present in sesamin seeds is called sesamin. The present study was to (i) investigate the plasma cholesterol-lowering activity of dietary sesamin; (ii) examine the interaction of dietary sesamin with the gene expression of sterol transporters, enzymes, receptors and proteins involved in cholesterol metabolism. and (iii) compare plasma cholesterol-lowering activity of sesamin with that of beta-sitosterol, a nutraceutical for management of blood cholesterol in hypercholesterolemia patients. Major findings: (1) Dietary sesamin was effective in reducing plasma cholesterol in a dose-dependent manner in hypercholesterolemia hamsters. When sesamin was added into diet at 0.5%, plasma total cholesterol could be reduced by 25% compared with the control. (2) Dietary sesamin down-regulated gene expression of intestinal Niemann-Pick C1 like 1 protein (NPC1L1), acyl-CoA: cholesterol acyltransferase 2 (ACAT2), microsomal triacylglycerol transport protein (MTP), ATP-binding cassette transporters sub-family G member 5 and 8 (ABCG 5 and 8). All these proteins, enzymes and transporters involved in the cholesterol absorption. (3) Dietary sesamin could up-regulate hepatic cholesterol- 7α-hydroxylase (CYP7A1) while it down-regulated hepatic 3-hydroxy -3-methyl-glutaryl-CoA (HMG-CoA) reductase and liver X receptor alpha (LXRα). (4) Plasma cholesterol-lowering activity of sesamin could increase the excretion of total fecal neutral sterols in a dose dependent manner, mediated by mediated by promoting the fecal excretion of sterols and modulating the genes involved in cholesterol absorption and metabolism. (5) Dietary sesamin was less effective than beta-sitosterol in reducing plasma cholesterol even though it was potent in decreasing plasma cholesterol compared with other natural compounds

462813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
462813.value: Current medicines including statins and cholestyramine in treatment of hypercholesterolemia suffer from some side effects. There is a growing interest in using functional foods and nutraceuticals to manage the hypercholesterolemia. The future study in this direction (1) shall focus on the synergistic effect of sesamin with these medicines in order to reduce the amount of drugs used by the patients, thus minimizing the side effect caused by statin or cholestyramine; (2) shall conduct a clinical study to see the finding in the animal experiment could be translated into humans.

462813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
462813.value: High blood total cholesterol (TC) is a risk factor for coronary heart disease (CHD). Cholesterol in blood is mainly present in two lipoproteins namely low-density lipoprotein (LDL) and high-density lipoprotein (HDL). Research has clearly demonstrated that when TC and LDL cholesterol (LDL-C) are abnormally elevated, cholesterol and other lipids may build up in the walls of arteries, causing atherosclerosis and leading to development of CHD. In contrast, HDL helps remove cholesterol from the arteries and transports it back to the liver for elimination. Thus, high concentration of HDL cholesterol (HDL-C) is protective against CHD. Sesame seeds are rich in sesamin, a natural compound. The present study was to investigate plasma cholesterol-lowering activity of sesamin and the underlying mechanism by which why dietary sesamin could reduce plasma cholesterol. It was proved that sesamin was effective in decreasing blood cholesterol. The mechanism was that sesamin could inhibit the cholesterol absorption by down-regulating the gene expression of these transporters, enzymes and proteins involved in cholesterol absorption.

463013.label: Major findings and research outcome
463013.value: 1. A protocol to assemble customized TALENs for generating targeted genome modifications in zebrafish was established. (Research Output #1 and #2). 2. Using this system, we have systematically generated zebrafish mutant lines lacking either the kiss or kissr genes. Spermatogenesis and folliculogenesis as well as reproductive capacity are not impaired in all of these mutant lines, demonstrating that the kiss/kissr systems are dispensable for zebrafish reproduction. These data provide genetic evidence supporting a multifactorial strategy for the neuroendocrine control of reproduction in fish. This strategy of reproduction in zebrafish is also demonstrated in the knockout of the gonadotropin releasing hormone gene. (Research Output #3 and #4). 3. We have also established both the LH beta-subunit (lhb) and LH receptor (lhr) knockout zebrafish lines. Both homozygous lhb and lhr mutant male fish are fertile. On the contrary, homozygous lhb mutant females are infertile, whereas homozygous lhr mutant females are fertile. Folliculogenesis is not affected in either lhb or lhr mutants, but oocyte maturation and ovulation are disrupted in the lhb mutant, whereas only ovulation is affected in the lhr mutant. Differential expression of genes in the ovary involved in steroidogenesis, oocyte maturation, and ovulation was found between the lhb and lhr mutants. These data demonstrate the essential role of LH signaling in zebrafish oocyte maturation and ovulation, and support the notion that LH acts through the FSH receptor in the absence of LH receptor in zebrafish. This in vivo evidence demonstrates, for the first time in any vertebrate species, that LH signaling is indispensable in female reproduction but not in male reproduction. (Research Output #5). 4. An ar knockout zebrafish line was established. Homozygous ar mutant male fish with smaller testis size were found to be infertile when tested by natural mating. Intriguingly, a small amount of mature spermatozoa were found in the ar mutant fish. These mature spermatozoa could fertilize healthy oocytes by in vitro fertilization, albeit with a lower fertilization rate. Moreover, the expression levels of most steroidogenic genes in the testes are significantly elevated in the ar mutants. In contrast, the levels of estradiol and 11-ketotestosterone are significantly decreased in the ar mutants, indicating that steroidogenesis is defective in the mutants. Furthermore, the protein level of LH beta in the serum decreases markedly in the ar mutants when compared with the wild-type, probably due to positive feedback from the diminished steroid hormone levels. (Research Output #6).

463013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
463013.value: Using this project, we have successfully achieved the project objectives and obtained definitive in vivo data to unveil the roles of the target genes on the control of reproduction in zebrafish. The rather surprising results of the knockout of the kiss/kissr genes as well as the gonadotropin releasing hormone gene in producing no reproductive phenotypes have led to the discovery of the multifactorial control strategy of reproduction in teleost. Whether this works through a compensation mechanism via altered expression of other genes or through a different regulatory network (e.g. in parallel instead of in series) of the control genes warrants further investigations. The realization of the very different mode of LH signaling in controlling male and female reproduction in teleost as compared to that in mammals is another interesting finding that warrants follow up investigations. These discoveries have immense implications for the aquaculture industry in which reproductive manipulation of the cultured species constitutes an important approach. These aspects will be further exploited in subsequent studies.

463013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
463013.value: The goals of this project are to obtain zebrafish mutant lines of our target genes in order to systematically analyze their functional roles in the control of reproduction in zebrafish, to study the reproductive abnormalities of the mutant fish, and also to investigate whether such abnormalities could be rescued by replacement of the appropriate hormonal factors. Using zebrafish as a convenient in vivo model amenable to genetic manipulations, results obtained from the present proposal will greatly enrich our current understanding on the control of reproduction in vertebrates. In addition, this study also demonstrates the unsurpassed efficiency and convenience of our improved TALENs system in producing targeted mutagenesis in zebrafish. This platform would have much wider application values beyond the present study. The adoption of this platform to knockout genes in other species would have immense implications in both basic and applied research. Furthermore, the high mutation efficiency achieved by our improved TALENs system provides unprecedented opportunities to perform gene knock-in studies as well.

463113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
463113.value: Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis (AIS) is the commonest disabling three-dimensional spinal deformity of unknown etiology affecting adolescent girls. Severe AIS can be associated with significant cosmetic and functional morbidity and the currently available treatments have significant limitations. AIS was shown to be associated with generalized low bone mineral density (BMD) which could persist beyond skeletal maturity and was found to be a significant prognostic factor for curve progression. Our recent researches utilizing Quantitative Ultrasound (QUS) and high-resolution peripheral quantitative computed tomography (HR-pQCT) have also demonstrated significant alterations in bone quality (bone micro-architecture, volumetric BMD) in AIS. More recently, our pilot study revealed a higher percentage of low-mineralized bone in AIS, together with an abnormal pattern of bone mineral density distribution, indicating their abnormal bone mineralization status. Taken all together, with the observations of lower BMD and early evidence of abnormal bone mineralization, it is important to further define their relationship and look into the actual bone mineralization process in AIS versus normal controls. We hypothesize that bone matrix mineralization is abnormally low in AIS and the abnormality could contribute to the observed osteopenia and abnormal bone quality that might be associated with the etiopathogenesis of AIS. We plan to conduct a case-control study on bone biopsies taken intra-operatively from AIS and age-matched controls. At the tissue level, histomorphological and micro-architectural analysis on bone biopsies will be performed to evaluate the quantitative status of bone mineralization. Additional molecular and cellular assessments tests will be conducted on bone tissue and osteoblast cells cultured from bone biopsies. Specific markers of bone formation, resorption and mineralization activities would be included to understand better their relative contributions to the observed abnormal bone mineralization. The study if granted could help to consolidate our hypothesis on the presence of abnormally low bone matrix mineralization in AIS from histomorphological, histomorphometric-microarchitectural, cellular and molecular functional aspects. The results of this study will enable further understanding on the possible role of abnormal bone mineralization in the etiopathogenesis of AIS. This will open up further possibilities of developing new molecular or functional markers of bone mineralization in the prediction of occurrence and progression in AIS and provide more informed evidence-based clinical diagnostic and personalized treatment of AIS. In the long run, it is hoped that prevention of occurrence or progression of AIS with abnormal bone quality can be initiated through direct non-invasive interventional treatment of the abnormalities in the bone mineralization etiopathogenetic pathways. 青少年特发性脊柱侧凸患者的骨矿化作用是否存在异常？ 摘要 青少年特发性脊柱侧凸(adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, AIS) 是一种最常见的三维脊柱畸形，青春期女性多见，至今病因不明。严重的侧突畸形可显著影响患者的外观和功能，但是目前治疗方法仍有诸多的局限性。 目前发现AIS患者存在全身广泛性的低骨量，并且可持续存在甚至到患者骨骼成熟；有研究认为低骨量是预测AIS侧突进展的一个重要因素。我们近期通过定量超声(quantitative ultrasound, QUS)和高分辨率外周定量计算机断层扫描(high-resolution peripheral quantitative computed tomography, HR-pQCT)技术，发现AIS的骨质量（骨微结构和材料骨密度）存在显著改变 ；同时我们最新的试验性研究显示，AIS中低矿化骨组织比例较高和骨密度分布异常，提示AIS存在骨基质矿化异常。综合考虑AIS的低骨密度和早期矿化异常的表现，我们认为进一步研究其彼此间的联系，以及比较AIS和正常人之间的实际骨矿化过程的差异将具有十分重要的意义。我们推测，AIS的骨基质矿化可能异常降低，进而导致低骨量和异常骨质量的发生，而这可能与AIS发生发展有关。 病例对照研究。通过术中对AIS患者和与其年龄匹配的对照组取骨组织活检，在组织学层面，我们将对骨的组织形态和微结构进行分析，定量评估矿化状态；分子学和细胞学层面的评估将通过相关骨组织试验和原代成骨细胞培养来完成。同时，我们也将通过对骨形成、吸收和矿化方面相关特异性标志物的检测，探讨其与AIS的异常骨矿化之间的联系。如果申请获得资助，该研究将进一步证实我们目前在骨的组织形态学、组织形态计量学-微结构和细胞分子功能学方面建立的关于AIS中存在骨基质矿化降低的假设；其研究结果能更好地解释异常的骨矿化作用可能在AIS发病机制中所起的作用；这也有助于在骨的矿化方面，发现新的预测AIS发生发展的分子或功能学标记，同时也有助于为AIS的循证医学临床诊断和个体化治疗提供更多的信息。从长远来看，我们期待通过对引起异常骨矿化的相关通路行直接的非侵入的干预性治疗，预防或治疗伴有低骨量的AIS的发生或发展。

463113.label: Realisation of objectives
463113.value: Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis (AIS) is a three dimensional spinal deformity occurring during pubertal period. The etiopathogenesis remains unclear, therefore current treatment regimes, including bracing and surgical correction, are targeting the pathoanatomical changes. Low bone mass is one of the proposed mechanisms underlying the etiopathogenesis of AIS, and is found to be an independent prognostic factor for curve progression. However, at the time of the submission of this proposal, the causes of low bone mass in AIS was elusive as there were only as few indirect evidence via serological study on bone formation and resorption markers, and the lack of bone histomorphometric analysis with AIS and matched controls bone tissues. The trabecular bone biopsy in both the AIS and control group were not taken as a separate procedure but rather as a part of the standard surgical procedure of the operated patients that require bone harvesting for bony fusion. This approach allowed us to obtain bone biopsy at the same bone site from age- and ethnic-matched control subjects which is believed to be the first attempt in AIS-related study. With extensive efforts, we have managed to collected the targeted number of bone biopsies from 60 AIS and 20 control subjects as planned. For technical and practical consideration, we further divide all the samples randomly into three portions for the following three in depth studies 1) micro-computed tomography (μCT) and histomorphometric analyses, 2) primary culture, and 3) RT-PCR study. Objective 1 of this study is to study the bone micro-architecture and the status of bone mineralization at bone tissue level. μCT analysis provided significantly higher resolution and details on the bone micro-architecture then the peripheral quantitative CT (pQCT) and the HR-pQCT. Apart from primary analyses by the built-in algorithm, we also extended our investigation through the collaboration with Prof. Edward X. Guo from Columbia University in New York to further characterize the micro-structure and connectivity individual trabecular plates and rods with individual trabecula segmentation (ITS) based morphological analysis , and to study the mechanical property with finite element analysis. Our static bone histomorphometric analysis showed more osteoid volume in AIS bone, supporting our hypothesis of an abnormally low systemic bone mineralization. To evaluate the status of mineralization, we conducted energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) which could provide additional information on the proportion of two major minerals in bone, i.e. calcium and phosphorus, and their ratio. We one of the few groups using this newly installed EDX system in the School of Biomedical Sciences CUHK. We are delighted to contribute to the development of the standard protocol for the determination of calcium and phosphorous composition and their ratio in human bone tissue samples. The findings showed in general, AIS had slightly lower bone volume fraction and specific bone surface, which was manifested as higher trabecular separation and lower trabecular number. ITS results further revealed predominant change in rod trabecular bone volume fraction, rod trabecular number, and rod-rod junction density. The overall deranged trabecular plates and rods led to a trend of lower apparent modulus in AIS when compared with Controls in both homogeneous and heterogeneous FE models. The ratio of calcium to phosphorus (RCa/P) , widely accepted for assessing the status of bone mineralization was found lower in AIS. EDX scanning also showed significantly lower RCa/C in AIS, suggesting decreased mineralization that was in agreement with the presence of more osteoid in histomorphometric analyses. Objective 2 of this study aimed to study the osteogenic and osteoclastogenic activities of primary osteoblasts and osteoclasts culture, respectively. We isolated the primary osteoblasts from bone biopsies. For the primary culture of osteoclasts, we isolated the progenitor cells from peripheral blood collected in the early morning before operation and subjected to ficoll separation. Subsequent cellular functional assessments were conducted according to well-established protocols as planned. The trabecular bone biopsies were subjected to total RNA extraction for the determination of expression level of bone formation related mRNAs. We extracted the total RNA from the whole bone biopsies rinsed thoroughly with DEPC-PBS, instead of from osteoblasts isolated from decalcified bone with laser micro-dissection because RNA degraded considerably after a series of decalcification and dehydration processes. At tissue level, AIS bone biopsies was found to express significantly less Runx2, but more Spp1 and TRAP when compared with Con. ALP and CTSK mRNA level in AIS were numerically lower in AIS, while Col1 level was slightly increased in AIS numerically. To validate if these changes also happening in osteoblasts, we measured the expression level of these mRNAs in primary osteoblasts culture and found similar trend.

463113.label: Major findings and research outcome
463113.value: Our results from objectives 1 and 2 provided new insight into the abnormal bone quality in AIS. By comparing bone biopsies from AIS patients and matched controls with similar skeletal and sexual maturity, anthropometry and femoral neck BMD Z-score to control confounding effects, we found significantly higher trabecular separation, thicker trabecular plates and lower rod-rod junction connectivity, and together with the lower calcium content and numerical reduction in apparent modules in AIS, which could be attributed to differential down-regulation of Runx2, and up-regulation of Spp1 and TRAP. In summary, this is the first comprehensive study providing direct evidence of unique pathological changes at different bone hierarchical levels which hitherto were undefined in AIS [2]. As it has been widely reported that 30% of AIS subjects had osteopenia, defined as femoral neck BMD Z-score ≤ -1 determined by DXA. The results of this funded project led to a speculation that non-osteopenic AIS might also exhibit different degrees of abnormal bone mass and quality which could not be clearly delineated by DXA. Therefore, in parallel to this study at bone tissue level, we also conduced case-control cross-sectional study to compare the bone mineralization and micro-structure of 257 AIS and 187 age- and gender-matched normal controls with HR-pQCT [1]. After adjustments of age, cortical area and vBMD, and trabecular number and separation continued to show statistical significance. Both the osteopenic and non-osteopenic AIS subgroups revealed significant abnormal bone quality parameters from that in the control group after adjustments of age and aBMD with multi-linear regression analysis. This study specifically defined the abnormal profile of bone quality in the osteopenic and non-osteopenic AIS for the first time. Collectively, these two studies suggest the presence of abnormal systemic bone metabolism in AIS, and also laid the groundworks for other subsequently granted GRF (Ref. No.: 14116415 and 14135016) and NSFC/GRF (N_CUHK416/16) funded projects.

463113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
463113.value: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive ex vivo study providing direct evidence of previously undefined unique bone microstructure, mechanical property, mineralization and local gene expression profile in AIS with matched-controls at bone tissue level, which could shed light on future mechanistic and therapeutic studies via targeting on the bone metabolism and mineralization pathways. One important research direction is from the serendipitous discoveries of structurally and functionally abnormal osteocytes in AIS. Osteocytes, the longest living cell comprise over 90% of mature bone cellular components have now been shown to be actively involved in regulating bone homeostasis and mineralization via interacting with osteoblasts and osteoclasts through its unique lacuno-canalicular network. We hypothesize that the morphological and functional abnormalities in osteocytes in AIS could be resulting from an abnormal reduction in Dmp-1 and SOST expression acting through the Wnt/β-catenin signalling pathway and manifest phenotypically as abnormal osteopenia, bone mineralization and bone microarchitecture thus affecting the mechanical bone strength and contribute to the initiation/progression and etiopathogenesis of AIS. A series of serological, histological, cellular and molecular experiments are undergoing to reveal the biological function of osteocytes in AIS.

463113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
463113.value: In this project, we have conducted successfully a series of scientific studies based on the objectives we set in the proposal with accepted publications in highly recognized journals in the field and presented in regional and international prestigious professional conferences. In general, with different assessment approaches, we found that the bone mass and quality are different between patients with AIS and non-AIS volunteers. The finding of this proposal has opened new research direction to further studies on the causes and mechanism underlying the documented abnormal bone mass and quality in AIS which will shed light on future development of novel prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic strategies in preventing the occurrence or progression of the scoliosis deformity via targeting on the bone cells and bone mineralization pathway in AIS through timely non-invasive intervention.

463213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
463213.value: 源自菌菇的具生物活性的多糖(含β-葡聚糖)有廣泛的免疫調節活性及低副作用的優點，是很有前途的抗腫瘤佐藥。據文獻報導，一般認為菌菇類β-葡聚糖的免疫調節過程是多通路，多途徑，多靶點的，然而其具體機制尚不完全明確。現有關於菌菇類β-葡聚糖的免疫調節活性以及其結構-活性之間的關係的研究相對匱乏。目前該領域研究最大的缺陷是缺少以結構明確的菌菇β-葡聚糖純品作為標準，且對不同來源的純β-葡聚糖在發揮免疫調節過程中牽涉到的細胞表面受體相互作用及信號轉導通路的對比仍未得到很好的闡明。本項目擬從幾種具代表性的蘑菇和真菌中分離的一系列結構明確的β-葡聚糖純品為標準，對比這些β-葡聚糖對人免疫細胞（單核細胞源的巨噬細胞）的免疫調節活性的分子機制。本研究深層意義是將初步在細胞水準上闡明菌菇β-葡聚糖調節免疫的結構-活性之間的關係，並為後續在動物水準乃至臨床研究提供適當的標準品以推進其在腫瘤治療中的應用。此外，本研究的結果還能為進一步合成具有優選免疫調控活性的β-葡聚糖提供重要的依據。

463213.label: Realisation of objectives
463213.value: Since the submission of the last progress report on February 2015, we have continued on the work of Objective 1 to purify native mushroom β-glucans and their structural elucidation. In addition to the alkali-soluble β-glucans and water-soluble polysaccharide-protein complexes from the mushroom sclerotia of Pleurotus tuber-regium (PTR) and Polyporus rhinocerus (PR), we have also included a number of β-glucans from other sources including yeast, bacteria, seaweed and cereal as references to provide a wider spectrum of chemical structure in terms of the molecular weight and β-glycosidic linkages for the study of the structure-function relationship. The detailed chemical structures of all these β-glucans were characterized by chemical, spectroscopic, chromatographic and microscopic techniques. In summary, a highly branched heteropolysaccharide-protein complex with 45.7 % polysaccharide and 44.2 % protein isolated from PRW was found to be a β-D-mannoglucan with its backbone containing →1)-D-Glcp-(4→, →1)-D-Glcp-(6→ and →1)-D-Manp-(2→ residues with a molar ratio of 5:4:6 and having terminal D-Glcp as side chain with a degree of branching of 0.62. Three fractions of β-glucans isolated from PR including PRA1 and PRA-2A and PRA-2C had similar structure which were hyper-branched β-glucans with a backbone composed of →1)-D-Glcp-(3→ linkages and side chains having the major branching points at the O-6 positions with a degree of branching (DB) of 0.89, 0.87 and 0.89, respectively. The non-PR and non-PTR sources of  β-glucans were found to have the following chemical structure : for barley (cereal) β-glucan was a linear β-(1,3)-(1,4)-glucan; for carboxymethyl (CM)-curdlan (bacteria) and native curdlan were linear β-(1,3)-glucan while laminarin (seaweed) and yeast β-glucan were β-(1,6)-branched β-(1,3)-glucan with a DB of 0.3 and 0.16, respectively. The molecular weight of these non-mushroom β-glucans determined by GPC was as follows: 4378.6 kDa for CM-curdlan, 3270.6 kDa for curdlan, 444.2 kDa for barley β-glucan, 9.5 kDa for laminarin, and 2.2 kDa for yeast β-glucan. In the last progress report, we have mentioned the in vitro immunomodulating effects of mushroom polysaccharides on antigen-presenting cells (APCs) derived from human monocytic leukemia-derived cell line (THP-1) with regard to expression of surface maturation markers, cytokine release and specific binding to cell surface receptors in relationship to Objective 2. In the present completion report, we have focused the comparison of the immunomodulatory activities of the PR and PTR β-glucans with those from the non-mushroom ones on both murine and human macrophages as well as human peritoneal blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). In brief, In vitro immunomodulatory studies showed that the alkali-soluble β-glucan from PR (PRA), the water-soluble hyper-branched heteropolysaccharide from PRW (PRW1), CM-curdlan, curdlan and yeast β-glucan could significantly activate murine macrophage RAW264.7. Specifically, PRA treatment significantly induced NO and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production as well as the morphological changes in RAW264.7 cells. PRA significantly up-regulated phagocytic activity of RAW264.7 cells evidenced by increased uptake of FITC-labeled dextran. PRA treatment also markedly enhanced the secretion of cytokines including CTACK, G-CSF, MCP-1, MIP-1α, MIP-2, RANTES, sTNFRI TIMP-1. The activation of murine macrophages triggered by PRA was associated with activation of iNOS, NF-κB, ERK and AKT. PRW1 significantly induced nitric oxide (NO) production and stimulated morphological changes in RAW264.7 cells. PRW1 treatment enhanced the release of a variety of cytokines including G-CSF, GM-CSF, IL-6, IL12p40/70, MCP-1, MCP-5, MIP-1-α, MIP-2, RANTES, sTNFRI and TNF-α. Mechanistically, PRW1 treatment triggered ERK phosphorylation to activate macrophages in a short period of time (within 15 min) and significantly increased the expression level of inducible NOS (iNOS) after 6 h. In addition, CM-curdlan, curdlan and yeast β-glucan exhibited immunomodulatory effects on human peritoneal blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) by inducing cytokine production including GM-CSF, GRO, IL-6. To address Objective 3, we have done a structure-function relationship study by comparing the in vitro immumomodulatory effect between structurally-characterized mushroom and non-mushroom β-glucans on macrophages. It was found that the β-(1,3)-glucans showed macrophage-activating effect while mixed linkage β-(1,3;1,4)-glucan did not. For β-(1,3)-glucans, both the linear and the branched structure as well as the molecular weight and water solubility affected the activation of the macrophages. These results give insights into the structure-activity relationship of β-glucans, allowing a better design of immunotherapeutic β-glucan for future clinical trials. The novel PRW1 and PRA derived from mushroom sclerotia are potent immuno-stimulator and further in vivo investigations using animal models on their effects towards human immune cells are necessary to evaluate their application for cancer immunotherapy. The above results obtained since the last progress report were reported in a paper published in the Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry 2016, 64, 3206-3214 and contained in a PhD thesis (published in July 2016) titled “A Comparative Study of the in vitro Immunomodulating Effects of Structurally Well-defined β-glucans in Macrophages”. By and large, the 3 project objectives have been achieved as planned and the results obtained can basically fulfil our original aims for the project. We expect follow-up work to be carried out in the near future to achieve our long term goal of applying the mushroom beta-glucans in clinical studies.

463213.label: Major findings and research outcome
463213.value: Novel β-glucans were isolated and structurally characterized from mushroom sclerotia. In particular, a water-soluble highly branched heteropolysaccharide-protein complex and three alkali-soluble hyper-branched β-glucans were obtained from the mushroom sclertoium (peer-review paper by Chen et al., 2015). We have also demonstrated the immunomodulatory activities of these mushroom sclerotial polysaccharides towards human immune cells including antigen-presenting cells (APCs) derived from human monocytic leukemia-derived cell line (THP-1) with regard to expression of surface maturation markers, cytokine release and specific binding to cell surface receptors. These polysaccharides can also induce the production of nitric oxide and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, cytokines as well as the morphological changes in RAW264.7 cells.macrophages (conference papers 2014 and 2015; peer-review paper by Liu et al., 2016). The structure-function relationship of β-glucans for in vitro immunomodulatory activities on immune cells was established. We have focused the comparison of the immunomodulatory activities of the mushroom β-glucans with those from the non-mushroom ones on both murine and human macrophages as well as human peritoneal blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). It was found that pure β-(1,3)-glucans showed macrophage-activating effect while mixed linkage β-(1,3;1,4)-glucan did not. For β-(1,3)-glucans, both the linear and the branched structure as well as the molecular weight and water solubility affected the activation of the macrophages (student PhD thesis by Chaoran Liu, 2016).

463213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
463213.value: Bioactive polysaccharides derived from mushrooms with beta-glucans in particular have a wide range of immune regulation with low side-effects and have the potential to be an adjuvant in cancer therapies. Based on the literature, it is generally recognized that the immunomodulation of mushroom and fungal beta-glucans is a multi-channel, multi-level, multi-target process with its mechanisms being still not fully understood yet. There is at present a lack of detailed knowledge in the immunomodulatory effects of mushroom and fungal beta-glucans and their structure-activity relationship. The present project has successfully obtained some purified mushroom and non-mushroom beta-glucans that have diverse structural features to be used for a comparative structure-function relationship study of the molecular mechanisms of their immunomodulatory activities in human immune cells (monocyte-derived macrophages) as well as murine macrophages. The present findings have provided significant insights to the mechanism involved in the immunomodulatory actions of the mushroom beta-glucans in cell line models. In addition, they would also provide crucial information for the synthesis of tailor-made beta-glucans that have optimum immunomodulatory activities. Potential target therapeutic agents derived from these mushroom beta-glucans could be used for future translational research in animal studies or clinical trials for cancer therapies in the long run.

463613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
463613.value: The aims of this study are to identify the binding molecule in colorectal tumor blood vessels and develop a biomarker and a drug target to enhance chemotherapy. Using phage display biopanning technology, our previous study identified a small peptide (CTPSPFSHC) termed TCP-1 that specifically bound to blood vessels of tumors induced orthotopically by a mouse colon cancer cell line (colon 26) but not to other tissues or subcutaneous colon 26 xenograft in mice. The same peptide also binds to blood vessels in human colorectal cancers (CRC) but not to adjacent normal tissues. These findings suggest that there is a specific binding site in tumor blood vessels. With these findings, identification of this molecule could have significant clinical implications in the treatment of CRC. In this regard, the binding molecule could be a specific biomarker for CRC and used as a molecule for drug targeting during chemotherapy. Our preliminary data also showed that the same binding capacity of TCP-1 was found on the cell membrane of colon 26. With this important information, we shall use TCP-1 to pull down the binding molecule from these membranes, in order to identify and also define the properties of this molecule. The identity of this binding molecule will be confirmed in the colon tumor vasculature in animals and humans. This molecule will be a guide for CRC treatment using TCP-1 as a carrier for anticancer drugs in targeted drug therapy. In this study, we shall employ tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-alpha) which has been identified to have potent anti-angiogenic activity but possess severe systemic toxicity. Recently, tumor vasculature targeting therapy has been playing an increasing role in chemotherapy. We shall couple TCP-1 with TNF-alpha using recombinant technology in the hope that new anticancer agents for CRC could be developed. This TCP-1/TNF-alpha could also enhance the efficacy of other clinical anticancer drugs, e.g. 5-fluorouracil, oxaloplatin and irinotecan through destruction and removal the vascular barrier and/or stabilization of the tumor vascular system. These novel therapeutic strategies will not only enhance the anticancer action of TNF-alpha on tumor blood vessels but also produce synergistic effects with other anticancer drugs together with lower systemic toxicity. This could greatly increase the viability of chemotherapy in humans. Identification of the binding molecule for TCP-1 at tumors is useful for targeted and guided therapy for CRC. This serves as a good example for personalized medicine in cancer patients. 本研究旨在鑒定腫瘤血管靶向多肽在腫瘤血管上的特異性結合受體，並將其運用到結腸直腸癌的圖像檢測和靶向治療上。前期研究中，我們發現TCP-1多肽能特異性地靶向小鼠原位結腸直腸癌組織的腫瘤血管，而非其他組織或皮下種植的結腸癌細胞。此外，TCP-1多肽還可以特異性地結合人的直腸結腸癌的血管，而對正常組織沒有明顯親和性。這些發現表明腫瘤血管上存在特殊位點可以特異性地結合TCP-1多肽。這個特殊結合位點的鑒定將會對結腸直腸癌的圖像檢測和靶向治療有很好的指導意義。初步實驗結果還顯示，TCP-1多肽同樣可以與Colon-26癌細胞的細胞膜結合。基於此，我們將利用蛋白質交互作用沉澱試驗技術分離鑒定TCP-1多肽在腫瘤血管細胞膜上的結合靶點。腫瘤新生血管已經成為選擇性抗腫瘤藥物研究的熱門靶點之一。腫瘤壞死因子具有較強的抗血管增生的活性，然而在臨床應用中卻表現出嚴重的副作用。我們利用重組技術，耦合TCP-1多肽和腫瘤壞死因子配體，以期開發出新的抗結腸直腸癌藥物。TCP-1多肽和腫瘤壞死因子耦合配體可以通過破壞腫瘤血管結構，增加其通透性及改變其穩定性，來增強其他化療藥物的效用。這種新的靶向給藥手段不僅可以增加腫瘤壞死因子的抗腫瘤活性，並且可以與化療藥物產生協同功效，同時也有效降低化療藥物的副作用。因此，分離鑒定TCP-1多肽在腫瘤血管上的特異性結合位點將對靶向治療直腸結腸癌產生積極意義，也會為癌症病人的個體化給藥提供依據。

463613.label: Realisation of objectives
463613.value: Objective 1: It was largely achieved, except the development of antibody for binding molecule (reasons stated below). (1) Identification of binding site in colon 26: Using the pull-down assay combined with MALDI-TOF-MS, we identified the band that appeared in the TCP-1 but not in the control peptide, which was about 36-38 kDa and found to be annexin A2. (2) Confirmation of the binding molecule in cells and human CRC tissues: To validate annexin A2 as the targeted molecule for TCP-1, we performed the immunoprecipitation assay using commercial annexin A2 antibody, and knockdown assay using annexin A2 siRNA in SW1116 (a TCP-1 homing human colorectal cancer cell). Western results showed that there was no clear band at 36-38 kDa, and this might be due to the biotin-TCP-1 which was not a good primary antibody. We then validated the results using knockdown assay with annexin A2 siRNA. siRNAs for the control, and annexin A2 were synthesized according to the manufacturer’s manual. Knockdown of annexin A2 markedly reduced TCP-1 binding ability in SW1116 when compared with the scramble siRNA treatment. Furthermore, we demonstrated that TCP-1 and annexin A2 were highly co-localized in human CRC and colon adenoma tissues. It was found that TCP-1 could home to 54% of human CRC (71 patients) and 62% adenoma (8 patients) tissues, which makes TCP-1 and Annexin A2 a great potential as CRC diagnostic agents and TCP-1 as drug carrier for CRC treatment. Undone: Development of antibody for the binding molecule We identified the binding site for TCP-1 on CRC likely to be annexin A2, a well-known protein that was highly expressed in various types of cancer including those in colons and stomachs. To date, numerous antibody products have been developed for detecting annexin A2 through western blot, immunoblot and other applications. Therefore, it is unnecessary for us to develop a specific antibody for this molecule. Objective 2: It was largely achieved, except the long-term drug treatment with TCP-1 conjugate in CRC model and in vivo depletion of cytokines or cell subsets in animal study (reasons stated below). (1) Coupling TCP-1 with TNFα and its cytotoxicity: TNFα and TCP-1/TNFα were prepared by recombinant DNA. The in vitro cytotoxic activities in L929 cells suggest that conjugation of TCP-1 with TNFα has no obvious effect on the cytotoxic property of TNFα. These data indicate that TCP-1 peptide does not significantly affect folding, oligomerization, or binding to TNFα receptors on cell membrane as well as its functional cytotoxicity on cells. (2) Assessment for the anti-angiogenic action of TCP-1/TNFα conjugate in CRC: As TCP-1 is targeting tumor blood vessels and TNFα is known for its anti-angiogenic effect, coupling of these molecules could have significant anti-angiogenic effect against tumor growth. Results showed that a single dose of 5 μg of TNFα produced a slight vasculature injury. In contrast, the same dose of TCP-1/TNFα resulted in a more obvious tumor vascular damage and significant reduction in microvessel density in tumor tissues at 24 hours after treatment when compared with other groups. TUNEL assay also showed that TCP-1/TNFα induced more apoptosis in tumors and associated blood vessels. Consistently, the levels of cleaved caspase-3 were higher in the TCP-1/TNFα group than the TNFα or PBS alone group. Our study also showed that short-term treatment with TNFα or TCP-1/TNFα groups did not show a significant loss of body weights (<5% of body weight). TCP-1 has a potential to deliver TNFα as an anti-angiogenic and proapoptotic agent to exert antitumor effect in CRC. (3) Antitumor activity of TCP-1/TNFα in combination with 5-FU in the orthotopic CRC model: Using a smaller dose approach for both 5-FU and TNFα, a single injection of 5-FU (20 mg/kg) slightly decreased tumor growth. When combined with TNFα or TCP-1/TNFα (1 ng/mouse), it significantly decreased tumor growth. TCP-1/TNFα showed more antitumor effect than TNFα alone in the combined treatment (P<0.01). Systemic toxicity test on loss of body weight and blood cell count was determined. There was no significant changes on these parameters. As the major pharmacological action of 5-FU and TNFα was on apoptosis in tumors, the antitumor action of TCP-1/TNFα + 5-FU through this biological effect was examined. As expected, TCP-1/TNFα + 5-FU had the highest number of apoptotic cells (P<0.05), disclosing that TCP-1/TNFα produced a synergism with 5-FU in the induction of apoptosis in cancer tissues. It was further confirmed with the induction of cleaved caspase-3 and PARP. As 5-FU has been reported to inhibit cell proliferation by inducing G1/S phase arrest, we also examined the inhibitory action on cancer cell proliferation by measuring the expression of Ki67. TCP-1/TNFα markedly potentiated the inhibitory effect of 5-FU on cell proliferation in tumors when compared with TNFα (P < 0.05). Mechanistic studies TCP-1/TNFα increased tumor blood vessel normalization Low dose of TCP-1/TNFα (1 ng/mouse) increased the number of blood vessels with open lumen and significantly increased 5-FU level in tumor tissues. This may explain the synergistic effect between TCP-1/TNFα and 5-FU in our orthotropic CRC model. The microvessel density showed no significant difference in all groups, indicating that unlike the high dose, TNFα or TCP-1/TNFα at low dose did not affect angiogenesis in tumors. They whether combined with or without 5-FU, all markedly increased the coverage of mature desmin+ pericytes and reduced the coverage of immature PDGFRβ+ pericytes, suggesting a normalization of tumor blood vessels by these agents. This could increase vascular perfusion, which was proven by more FITC-conjugated lectin found in tumor vessels after treatment. Such effect was more prominent in the TCP-1/TNFα + 5-FU group. TCP-1/TNFα significantly improved 5-FU infiltration in tumor mass We determined if TCP-1/TNFα could increase 5-FU infiltration into tumors using the HPLC approach. We had optimized all the experimental conditions in this method. Results showed that 2-hour pretreatment with TCP-1/TNFα (1 ng/mouse) significantly increased 5-FU level in tumor tissues after treatment. This may mainly explain the synergistic antitumor effect of TCP-1/TNFα and 5-FU in our cancer model (detailed information referred to Lu L. et al, Journal of Controlled Release 2015). TCP-1/TNFα enhanced antitumor immunity CD3+CD8+ lymphocyte levels in tumors were increased in low-dose TCP-1/TNFα (1 ng/mouse) with/without 5-FU groups. This action was probably due to the normalization of tumor blood vessels to enhance antitumor immunity. The medium dose of TNFα (1 µg/mouse) inhibited blood CD34bright CD45dim hematopoietic cell levels, whereas conjugation with TCP-1 restored the hematopoietic cells loss (P<0.01), indicating that TCP-1 could alleviate the side effect of TNFα on immunosuppressive action on bone marrow. However, both doses of TCP-1/TNFα alone did not affect tumour growth, and 5-FU did not affect the immune response of TCP-1/TNFα in tumors, suggesting that the immune responses and anti-tumor effect have no direct association. Undone: 1. Long-term drug treatment of TCP-1 conjugate in CRC model, 4 injections will be given and evaluating for the antitumor action of TCP-1 conjugate. It was unexpected that tumor outgrew after the second injection of agents. We needed to stop the long-term evaluation process on the agents to comply with the animal ethics governed by CUHK and Department of Health regulations. 2. In vivo depletion of cytokines or cell subsets in animal study: The direct association between the immune regulation and anti-tumor action by TCP-1/TNFα, or its combination with 5-FU had no significant association. This type of work was not further pursued in the study.

463613.label: Major findings and research outcome
463613.value: 1. In the current project, TCP-1 could home to more than 54% human CRC and 62% adenomas tissues. Using the pull-down assay and the gene knockdown approach, we further identified that annexin A2 could be the target binding molecule for TCP-1 in CRC. This result was further validated in cells (SW1116), and also in human CRC and adenoma biopsies. These findings provide solid evidence that TCP-1 could be an effective tool for the diagnosis and drug carrier for targeted therapy in CRC. 2. We successfully conjugated TCP-1 peptide with an immune cytokine, such as TNFα using recombinant DNA technology. Its antitumor action and mechanisms of action on CRC were further evaluated. 3. TCP-1 could deliver TNFα to tumors to produce anti-angiogenetic action. In this regard, we demonstrated that targeted delivery of TNFα by TCP-1 conjugation enhanced the therapeutic action of TNFα (at high dose 5 μg/mouse) through damaging tumor vasculature and reducing microvessel density in tumor tissues. This action was evidenced by acting through the induction of apoptosis in tumors through upregulation of cleaved caspase-3 and PARP levels in tumor tissues. In addition, the systemic toxicity of TNFα on bone marrow was also significally reverted by TCP-1 conjugation. 4. Unlike the high dose, much lowed dose of TCP-1/TNFα (1 ng/mouse) did not provide direct anti-angiogenic affect, instead reversely increased tumor blood vessel normalization in cancer tissues. With this unique biological action, the agent elevated the levels of pro-apototic chemotherapeutic agent (5-FU) and immune cells (CD8+ cytotoxic lymphocytes) through increased perfusion of vasculature, into tumor mass. These overall actions resulted in a synergism between the therapeutic effects of TCP-1/TNFα and a chemotherapeutic agent like 5-FU in the treatment of CRC. With this low dose of TCP-1/TNFα and significant antitumor action, such biological preparation should have good potentials to be developed as an effective adjuvant chemotherapy in cancer patients. 5. With these findings we are in the active stage to join hand with the partners in Beijing to study the pharmacokinetic profile of TCP-1 and also enlarge our patient sample size with a sense of multi-center approach to consolidate the clinical applications of the peptide as a chemodrug carrier and diagnostic for CRC treatment. For more detail information, please refer to our publication: Lu L. et al, Journal of Controlled Release 2015.

463613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
463613.value: 1. TCP-1 peptide could home to 54% of human CRC tissues and 62% of colon adenoma tissues. In this respect, this biological preparation is useful not only for the diagnosis of cancer, but also for the identification of CRC at its pre-cancerous stage. On the therapeutic side, those patients with positive signal on the binding molecule annexin A2 in their cancer tissues, TCP-1 and its therapeutic conjugate would be the most appropriate targeted therapeutic agent to these patients. As such TCP-1 is a good diagnostic tool and personalized medicine for CRC treatment. 2. In addition, we should extend the usage of TCP-1 both as diagnostic and therapeutic agents in gastric cancer (GC) patients, as it exhibited a similar binding capacity as in CRC mouse model. The therapeutic effects of TCP-1/TNFα on gastric cancers is being validated in orthotropic gastric cancer model, including tumor vascular normalization, infiltration of chemotherapeutic drugs such as 5-FU, oxaliplatin, irinotecan, etc. 3. We should also extend the usage of TCP-1 to targeted delivery for other immunotherapeutic agents, such as IFN gamma and IL-36 to evaluate their therapeutic efficacy in GI cancers. Indeed, we have positive therapeutic response with TCP-1/IFN gamma conjugate in CRC mouse model.

463613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
463613.value: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the third most common cancer in the world. It ranks number one among all cancers found in Hong Kong. Standard chemotherapy like fluorouracil (5-FU) although remains the mainstay of drug treatment to prolong patients’ survival at stage II and III CRC in high doses, it defintely causes many and sometime intolerable side effects. Increasing drug infiltration into tumors with targeted therapy might be the solution to overcome this problem. In the current project, we firstly validated that TCP-1 peptide could target annexin A2 in human cancer cells and tissues. It also selectively delivered bioactive agent like TNF-alpha through this binding molecule in CRC. In addition, TCP-1/TNF-alpha conjugate exhibited multiple biological functions, including anti-angiogenic and apoptotic actions at high dosage, and increase in tumor vascular permeability and consequent promotion of 5-FU and immune cells infiltration into tumors at much lower dosage. We also demonstrated that TCP-1 peptide was able to home to 54% (38/71) human CRC tissues and 62% (5/8) colon adenoma tissues, suggesting that TCP-1 and its binding molecule annexin A2 could be developed as diagnostic agents for CRC and suitable for personalized medicine to achieve optimal outcomes with less systemic toxicity in chemotherapy.

464013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
464013.value: 在海洋中，海平面和海洋環流過去和當前的變化不斷影響生物的基因流，從而導致種群的分化。不同物種遺傳間隔的一致性提供了其進化歷史和種群關聯的觀點。然而，不同物種間的差異常常被發現，而且出現這些差異的原因都歸於不同海洋生物生活史的多樣性。特別是，大多數海洋動物的浮游幼蟲階段，預計會促進基因的交流以及消除歷史性隔離的信號。然而，最近對現有證據的統合分析，得到的結論含糊不清；並且，在很多情況下，浮游幼蟲期與遺傳分化程度的相關程度並不高。分子標記的選擇、有效種群大小的變化、非均衡的FST值，以及成體的生境需求，都被提出會對預測的關聯性和實際的遺傳結構帶來重大影響。然而，很少有實證研究分析這些因素的影響，而大多數的研究只關注浮游幼蟲期的影響。為了闡明特異的生境在塑造遺傳結構中的作用，使用多位點的方法對多個生境的物種進行親緣地理學的比較研究是非常必要的。 在本研究計劃中，我們將考察十二種短尾蟹類的親緣地理格局。這十二種短尾蟹類分佈在東亞三個不同的沿海棲息地（每個棲息地四種）：潮間帶的岩石海岸、沙質海岸和河口的紅樹林泥灘。我們將使用線粒體COI基因、核基因內含子位點和高變微衛星位點，以估計種群之間的遺傳分化。有效種群大小和分歧事件的時間會以聚結模型的框架分析序列數據來估計，而微衛星位點可為當前種群的關聯提供更加翔實的信息。多分子標記的綜合分析，將使我們能夠捕捉歷史和當前的基因流水平信息。我們將進一步測試使用近似貝葉斯計算，同時分析不同物種之間親緣地理學間隔的差異。根據研究結果，我們可以確定在同一棲息地具有不同浮游幼蟲期的物種（因此具有不同的預期擴散能力）是否顯示相同的遺傳結構模式。本研究成果將填補生物性狀如何影響種群關聯的知識空白。這對於了解和預測全球性進程於不斷變化的世界帶來的影響，以及設計以知識為基礎的保護措施，均具有無法估量的價值。此外，本研究會促進我們理解東亞海洋生物的分化歷史和近期種群的關聯。

464013.label: Realisation of objectives
464013.value: The three objectives were basically realized. We have examined the phylogeographic patterns revealed by mitochondrial COI and nuclear NaK intron markers of 12 intertidal crab species inhabiting four different habitats (exposed rocky intertidal, sheltered rocky shores, sandy shores, and estuarine mangrove mudflats) from three to six sampling sites in East Asia per species. For one sandy shore species, Ocypode ceratophthalmus, we extended the sampling to include 35 sites throughout the entire Indo-Pacific region to comprehensively investigate its phylogeography over a broader geographic scale. Our first objective was to test if mangrove-inhabiting species demonstrate a higher level of population genetic differentiation than rocky shore and sandy shore species attributed to lower concurrent gene flow and thus preservation and/or amplification of signals from historic isolation. We found that while two exposed rocky intertidal crabs and one sheltered rocky shore species exhibited no population structure suggesting a high level of gene flow among the populations, marked population genetic differentiation was observed in the remaining species inhabiting sheltered rocky shores, sandy shores, and mangroves. Hence, we fully achieved this objective by showing that adult habitat requirement plays a role in shaping the genetic structure of intertidal crabs in East Asia. For the second objective, comparison of the phylogeographic patterns revealed several common biogeographic breaks shared among a few, but not all, of the sympatric crab species. These biogeographic breaks are associated with regional oceanography and disjunction of habitats that, theoretically, could impact all species in common. Therefore, the different phylogeographic patterns revealed indicate diverse biotic response to these factors. For the third objective, the mitochondrial and nuclear markers generally show congruent phylogeographic patterns. Coalescent analyses based on mismatch distribution and Bayesian approach using seven of the species similarly revealed that the studied species underwent recent population expansion during mid- to late-Pleistocene and that their populations were not markedly affected by the last glacial maximum. Despite the best of our effort (including multiple field visits and collaboration with local scientists), we could not obtain enough samples for some species in some locations for unbiased approximate Bayesian computation; therefore we did not perform this analysis. Nonetheless, common biogeographic breaks shared among several crab species were evident as aforementioned, without the need of performing approximate Bayesian computation.

464013.label: Major findings and research outcome
464013.value: We observed prominent difference in the phylogeographic structures of the 12 coastal crab species despite similarities in their pelagic larval duration, ocean currents experienced and sampled ranges (Ip, CUHK M.Phil. thesis 2014; Kawasch, University of Regensburg B.Sc thesis 2014; Bader et al., submitted; Schubart, unpublished data). In general, crabs inhabiting more exposed coastal habitats (i.e. intertidal rocky shores) exhibited no/less population structure, suggesting higher population connectivity in these species. By contrast, crab species living in more sheltered/disjointed habitats (i.e. mangrove, sandy shores, and sheltered rocky shores) usually showed more marked genetic structure, indicating stronger impact of oceanographic conditions and/or historical events on these species. We found biogeographic breaks shared among some, but not all, of the sympatric species. For instance, we observed significant genetic differentiation between Hong Kong and Taiwan populations of all three mangrove crab species, but this pattern was not observed in other species (Ip, CUHK M.Phil. thesis 2014; Schubart, unpublished data). Moreover, a north-south partition in the East China Sea was observed in two Hemigrapsus species inhabiting sheltered rocky shores, highlighting the influence of freshwater outflow of the Yangtze River in restricting their dispersal. This pattern was also observed in a soft shore barnacle (Fistulobalanus albicostatus) that we also sampled during field trips for this study (Chang et al., 2017). The disparity of phylogeographic patterns observed among species could not be explained by pelagic larval duration and ocean current circulation. The current comparative study thus underscores the importance investigating the effect of other life history traits on population genetic structure. This study also discovered four new/cryptic species in the study region. This reveals underestimated biodiversity in Asia and provides further implications for management strategies of conservation of biodiversity and understanding of speciation events in Asia. Moreover, by extending the sampling to include 35 sites throughout the entire Indo-Pacific region for one of the sandy shore species, Ocypode ceratophthalmus, we found that peripheral isolation plays an important role in shaping evolutionary history of this species (Ma et al., submitted). Particularly, secondary dispersal of divergent lineages from the Central Pacific contributes to the high diversity found in the Indo-Australian Archipelago. Thus, the Centre of Accumulation hypothesis best describes the evolutionary and demographic history of this species best. Our coalescence analyses revealed that the seven species have experienced demographic expansion in mid- to late-Pleistocene before last glacial maximum (LGM) and maintained stable effective population sizes through the LGM. This is a situation in contrast to many studied organisms, which had experienced post-LGM expansion (Ip, CUHK M.Phil. thesis 2014). It was unclear why the LGM did not exert any effects on the demographic histories of the crab species. The studied species might have persisted through the LGM regionally. The South China Sea was not greatly contracted during low sea level in the Pleistocene; hence the populations in the region might not be much affected by the reduction of habitat. This finding calls for more study on the demographic history of various East Asian coastal fauna to better understand the biological impact of global climate changes.

464013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
464013.value: While our study revealed that crabs’ adult habitat requirements influence population connectivity and that common biogeographic barriers exist in East Asia, the precise mechanisms are still obscure. In order to better understand how adult habitat determines genetic connectivity between populations, a multi-locus approach with the employment of more variable markers (e.g. microsatellites) shall be undertaken in a smaller geographical scale to scrutinize the larval dispersal kernels of crabs inhabiting different environments. The study of brachyuran larval biology and behavior of the species would help us better understand their specific adaptive responses. More oceanographic studies in East Asia are also required to examine the nature of biogeographic barriers in this region. Besides, our genetic analyses also discovered four potential cryptic/new species. We are working with collaborators to examine their morphology to properly describe these species. These works will lead to the revision of the classification scheme and better understanding of the driver of biodiversity of multiple brachyuran genera.

464013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
464013.value: This study examined the distribution of genetic diversity of 12 crab species inhabiting four different coastal habitats: exposed rocky shores, sheltered rocky shores, sandy shores, and estuarine mangrove mudflats, in East Asia. We found that genetic diversity of crabs inhabiting rocky shores (particularly the exposed ones) tend to be more evenly distributed throughout the studied area in East Asia, indicating high level of population connectivity in these species. By contrast, species that inhabit sandy shores and mangroves show more marked population genetic differentiation. Our study thus bridged the knowledge gap about how biological traits affect population connectivity. Our comprehensive genetic analyses of crabs from multiple regions also revealed the presence of potential new cryptic species and illuminated on the processes driving species diversification in the marine realm. Our finding will therefore be of immeasurable value to the understanding and predicting the consequences of global environmental changes and the design of knowledge-based conservation measures.

464613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
464613.value: Embryonic stem cells (ESC) and induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC) have great potentials for studying early embryonic development, establishment of disease models, and development of regenerative medicine. However, current methodologies can only induce ESCs/iPSCs to differentiate into heterogeneous population in vitro. Elucidation of the molecular mechanism underlying early stage ESC lineage commitment is necessary for improving the efficiency of directed differentiation, which is critical for harnessing the full potential of ESCs/iPSCs. Therefore, in this proposal we would like to investigate the exact molecular events involved in early neural induction of ESCs. Inhibition of BMP and TGFβ signals are essential for neural induction during early embryogenesis and ESC differentiation in vitro. However, how BMP/TGFβ inhibition triggers emergence of the earliest neural cells remains unclear. The incomplete characterization of these processes is due to the transient activation of multiple cellular events, heterogeneity of the culture, and restrictions associated with the use of animal models. In our preliminary work, we have set up a platform for inducing and maintaining primitive neural stem cells (pNSC) from mouse ESCs, and identified a group of early neural genes which is up-regulated in pNSCs. Our data provided valuable clues to investigate how BMP and TGFβ inhibition promotes the early neural induction. In this project, we will investigate the functional interactions between the genes that are differentially expressed in response to BMP/TGFβ inhibition and the early neural genes that are up-regulated in pNSCs. First, we plan to identify binding targets of Smad family members, which immediately acts downstream of BMP and TGFβ signals, on a genome-wide scale. Second, we will identify immediate responsive genes by comparing normal ESC with those treated with BMP/TGFβ inhibitors over a time-course analysis. Finally, we plan to study the cellular function of genes which are common in above two assays using shRNA-mediated silencing and cDNA overexpression approaches, followed by real-time PCR analysis. This study will generate valuable data and provide insights into the molecular mechanism that governs the transition from pluripotent ESCs/iPSCs to early neural cells. In a long term, the in-depth understanding of neural induction potentially facilitates the establishment of an efficient methodology for generating homogenous and safe NSCs for therapeutic transplantation. 摘要： 胚胎干細胞（Embryonic stem cells，ESC）及誘導性多能干細胞（induced pluripotent stem cells，iPSC）都具有在體外無限增生及分化為各類體細胞的潛能；這對研究早期胚胎細胞的分化，在細胞水平建立疾病模型，以及發展再生醫學都具有極其重要的價值。但是，現有的方法僅能誘導多能干細胞（包括ESC和iPSC）分化為混雜的細胞群體。因此，進一步研究和揭示ESC早期分化的分子調控機制是提高定向分化誘導效率、促進干細胞發展和應用的關鍵。本課題將就ESC早期分化的分子調控機制，主要是最早出現的向神經細胞分化的調控，進行深入研究。 抑制BMP 及 TGFβ 信號是早期胚胎及ESC向神經分化的最關鍵因素。 但是，這一現象背后的具體分子調控機制還不清楚。這主要是由於早期分化進程快，細胞數目少， 動物試驗在這一時期受到極大限制，ESC體外分化又呈現混雜和不穩定的特性。 申請者從事ESC/iPSC研究多年。在前期工作中，我們建立了從小鼠ESC分化為早期初始神經干細胞（primitive neural stem cells, p-NSC）的技術平台， 並且鑒定了一組在這一時期高表達的基因。 這些數據對於研究BMP 及 TGFβ 信號抑制與早期神經分化誘導的關系提供了極具價值的線索。 本課題將圍繞p-NSC 高表達基因對BMP 及 TGFβ 信號抑制的反應，及其與BMP 及 TGFβ 信號下游基因的調控關系，對早期神經分化誘導分子調控機制進行探索。1）課題將通過對染色質免疫共沉澱實驗數據進行分析，鑒定BMP 及 TGFβ 信號下游的功能基因；2）課題將以小分子化合物在ESC中抑制BMP 及 TGFβ 信號，再以基因芯片分析技術分析比較所引起的基因表達的變化，並由此鑒定ESC中BMP 及 TGFβ 信號所調控的下游基因；3）對第一部分與第二部分所鑒定基因的交集， 即ESC中BMP 及 TGFβ 信號直接調控的下游基因，進行功能分析：以RNA干擾技術及過表達等實驗方法分析其在早期神經分化誘導中的作用。 該項研究將進一步揭示早期神經分化誘導的分子機制，有利於進一步建立更高效的方法在體外誘導ESC向神經細胞的定向分化。

464613.label: Realisation of objectives
464613.value: Inhibition of bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) and tumor growth factor-beta (TGFβ) signaling is required for neural development in early embryos as well as for neural commitment of embryonic stem cells (ESCs) and induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs). However, the exact molecular mechanism by which BMP/TGFβ modulates early lineage specifications and BMP/TGFβ inhibition triggers the emergence of earliest neural cells remain obscure. In this project, we aim to investigate the early molecular events underlying neural induction and identify genes that are activated/suppressed directly by BMP/TGFβ inhibition. Meanwhile we examine the functional connections between genes that are responsive to BMP/TGFβ inhibition and the early neural genes which were highlighted in our previous microarray analysis, where we performed genome-wide gene expression profiling and unraveled the characteristic of primitive neural stem cells (p-NSCs) as an intermediate between ESCs and definitive neural stem cells (d-NSCs) (Tsang et al., Stem Cell Res, 2013). We first analyzed the potential BMP/TGFβ target genes in mouse ESCs through bioinformatics analysis, using published Smad ChIP-seq data, including those obtained from both mouse ESCs and differentiated cells. We first mapped the binding targets of BMP/TGFβ effector transcription factors Smad 1/5 and Smad 2/3 on a genome-wide scale in mouse ESCs, and found that the Smad-target genes in mouse ESCs include a large number of neural differentiation-related genes. We further compared this result with the ChIP-seq result from differentiated cells. The comparison analysis revealed that in total, 255 genes were bind by Smad1/5 and 962 genes targeted by Smad2/3, specifically in mouse ESCs. These include 160 bound by Smad1/5 only, 867 by Smad 2/3 only and 95 bound by both Smad1/5 and Smad2/3. Next, we compared these Smad ChIP-seq results with our gene expression profile data obtained during neural induction from mouse ESCs (Tsang et al., Stem Cell Res, 2013). We found that the expressions of Smad-binding genes are mainly changed at the d-NSC stage. While 97 Smad2/3 binding genes are upregulated, 72 Smad2/3 target genes are downregulated at the p-NSC stage. The upregulated genes include many genes that are known to play important roles during early neural differentiation, such as Sox1 and Pax6. These work have largely verified our hypothesis, and support that it is the external signaling changes, such as BMP/TGFβ inhibition drives the activation of internal genes to initiate neural differentiation from pluripotent cells (Wang et al., J Stem Cell Res Ther. 2015) In addition, to the neural induction from mouse ESCs, we have also extend our study on TGFβ to dedifferentiation of endodermal cells and endothelial cells. We found that that modulating signaling pathways including TGFβ by a cocktail of small molecules, endodermal progenitor cells could be successfully induced from somatic gastrointestinal epithelial cells and expanded in culture condition (Wang et al., Cell Stem Cell. 2016). On the other hand, we also found an microRNA miR-221, which is both a modulator and a target of TGFβ signaling, plays an important role in smooth muscle cell (VSMC) proliferation and phenotype transformation. Locally adventitial delivery of miRNA sponges can reduce miR-221 level and is promising to prevent vein graft failure (Wang et al., Int J Cardiol. 2016). Since extensive research on TGFβ has demonstrated it as a multi-tasking morphogenic signal pathway; based on the above works, we have further broadened our investigation into TGFβ functions in other contexts of stem cell differentiation or dedifferentiation. Recently, our research on hepatic dedifferentiation have yielded interesting preliminary data, and showed that hepatic progenitor cells could be induced from mature hepatocytes through a dedifferentiation processes induced by modulating signaling pathways including TGFβ (unpublished). This work has potentials to elaborate the mechanism underlying lineage specification and facilitate the generation of liver progenitor cells for end-stage liver disease treatment in clinical application. Collectively, we have completed the proposed research work, and obtained insightful understanding of BMP/TGFβ signaling during stem cell differentiation and dedifferentiation. The data and knowledge obtained through this research work will benefit our research and promote the development of new stem cell technology in future.

464613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
464613.value: A recent study employed chemicals Y-27632, A-83-01 and CHIR99021 (YAC) to convert rodent mature hepatocytes into liver progenitor cells in vitro, which is promising to provide induced liver progenitor cells in treating liver diseases. A-83-01 is a TGFβ signaling inhibitor, and CHIR99021 is Wnt signaling activator. It suggests that interplay between TGFβ and Wnt signaling may play important function in cell lineage specification as well as dedifferentiation. Recent studies also indicate that other signaling moleculars such as Hippo and MET pathways may be involved in the dedifferentiation from mature hepatocytes into progenitors. We have initiated a research work and obtained preliminary data. In the future, we will further explore the roles of related signaling pathways during YAC-induced dedifferentiation of hepatocytes, which has potentials to elaborate the underlying mechanism and facilitate the generation of human liver progenitor cells for end-stage liver disease treatment in clinical application.

464613.value: Successful establishment of embryonic stem cells (ESCs) and induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) has opened tremendous opportunity to study cell differentiation and develop regenerative medicine. In order to obtain insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying early differentiation, we have investigated the role of important signaling pathways BMP and TGFβ during the neural induction from mouse ESCs. In this research work, we have identified a number of interesting genes that are regulated by BMP/TGFβ signaling and undergo the drastic expression changes during early neural induction. These work have large verified our hypothesis, and support that it is the external signaling changes, such as BMP/TGFβ inhibition drives the activation of internal genes to initiate neural differentiation from pluripotent cells (Wang et al. Cell Stem Cell. 2016) and endothelial cells (Wang et al. Int J Cardiol. 2016). Collectively, we have obtained insightful understanding of BMP/TGFβ signaling during stem cell differentiation and dedifferentiation throughout this research work, to promote the development of new stem cell technology in future.

466313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
466313.value: Endomembrane Proteins (EMPs) are polytopic integral membrane family proteins found in in yeast, plants and mammalian cells. Structurally, most EMPs are predicted to contain a large lumenal N-terminus, nine transmembrane domains (TMD) and a short cytoplasmic tail (CT). The Arabidopsis genome contains 12 EMP members. Our recent study on the targeting and subcellular localization of AtEMP12 have demonstrated that 1) both endogenous AtEMP12 and GFP-AtEMP12 fusion localized to the Golgi apparatus in transgenic Arabidopsis plants; 2) GFP fusion at the C-terminus of AtEMP12 caused mis-localization of EMP12-GFP to post-Golgi compartments and vacuoles for degradation in Arabidopsis cells; 3) the AtEMP12 CT contained two important signals: an ER export signal (FVY) and a novel Golgi retention signal (KXE/D); and 4) this newly identified KXE/D Golgi-retention signal is both necessary and sufficient for Golgi localization of EMPs in plant cells (Plant Cell 24:2086-2104). However, the molecular mechanisms by which EMPs and other polytopic integral membrane proteins are targeted to and retained within the Golgi apparatus remain to be clearly defined. Our recent bioinformative analysis showed that the newly identified Golgi retention signal (KXE/D) is not only highly conserved in all EMPs found in yeast, animals and Arabidopsis, but this motif is also present in many other eukaryotic proteins of undefined localization. We thus hypothesize that this novel Golgi retention signal may represent a new general mechanism of Golgi targeting and Golgi retention of certain polytopic integral membrane proteins in eukaryotic cells. Therefore, the central goal of this proposal is to determine the molecular mechanisms of Golgi targeting and retention for polytopic integral membrane proteins with conserved but previously uncharacterized Golgi retention signal (KXE/D) using a combination of molecular, cellular and genetic approaches. First, to test the hypothesis that the KXE/D Golgi retention signal is conserved in eukaryotic cells, we will study the subcellular localization of selective EMPs of yeast, animal and Arabidopsis. Second, using a similar GFP fusion and transient expression approach, we will study the targeting and subcellular localization of selective polytopic integral membrane proteins containing the putative novel Golgi retention signal. Third, we will identify, through affinity chromatography and subsequent LC-MS/MS analysis, proteins that interact with this Golgi retention motif. Last, since not all Golgi-localized polytopic integral membrane proteins contain known COPI-interacting motif, we will test the hypothesis that distinct COPI-dependent and COPI-independent mechanisms are responsible for Golgi protein retention in eukaryotic cells. 内膜蛋白（EMPs）是一类在酵母、植物和动物都非常保守的含多跨膜结构域的膜蛋白。拟南芥有12个基因编码此内膜蛋白家族。以拟南芥EMP12为研究对象，我们最近的研究证明：1）内源性的EMP12蛋白和N末端GFP标记的GFP-EMP12复合蛋白在植物细胞中都定位于高尔基体；2）将GFP连接于C末端导致EMP12-GFP复合蛋白错误的定位于后高尔基体细胞器并最终在液泡降解；3）EMP12的C末端胞质部分有两个重要的蛋白分选信号，分别是内质网输出信号（FVY）和一个全新的高尔基体滞留信号（KXE/D）；4）这个新发掘的高尔基体滞留信号（KXE/D）对于植物内膜蛋白家族的高尔基体定位是必要且充分的。根据上述研究结果，我们推测这个新发掘的高尔基体滞留信号可能代表了一种新的高尔基体定位和滞留机制，而真核细胞中诸多此类高尔基体多跨膜蛋白或将依赖这个新的机制以保障它们定位于高尔基体来行使相关功能。因此，本项研究的中心目标是结合分子、细胞和遗传的手段来研究此类含有KXE/D高尔基体滞留信号的多跨膜蛋白于高尔基体定位和滞留的分子机理。

466313.label: Realisation of objectives
466313.value: Objective 1 : Previously, we identified dual sorting signals in the C-terminal cytosolic tail of Arabidopsis AtEMP12 as being essential for maintaining its Golgi localization, namely the COPII interaction motif, FV/Y, and the COPI interaction motif, KXD/E. Given that EMP homologues can be found in yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) and human (Homo sapiens) apart from plant, and the lysine-based KXD/E motif seems to be conserved in all homologues except yeast ScTMN3, we hypothesized that there is a possible conserved function of this lysine-based KXD/E sorting signal among different organisms. We cloned selective EMP homologues from Arabidopsis, human and yeast. We next generated their respective N-terminal and C-terminal GFP fusions under the control of proper promoters, and then studied their subcellular localization in corresponding native expression systems. Expression of foreign EMP homologues in hetero-expression system has also been done. We studied the localization patterns by (1) expressing various GFP-fused EMP homologues from mammals and yeast in plant cells, and (2) various GFP-fused plant and yeast EMP homologues expressed in mammalian system. All these experiments demonstrated that regardless of expression systems, the N-terminal XFP-fused EMP isoforms always localized to the Golgi, while the C-terminal XFP-fused EMPs always localized to post-Golgi compartment due to the blockage of KXD/E motif by the C-terminal fused tag. These results proved the conserved role of KXD/E motif in conferring Golgi retention of EMPs among different organisms, thus confirming our original hypothesis. These results have been published in Molecular Biology of the Cell in 2015 included in this report. Thus, we have achieved the original objective 1 fully. Objective 2: We have performed a bioinformatic search in different organisms to identify transmembrane proteins that contain the KXD/E motif located in the C-terminus exposed to cytosol. Such analysis yielded 79 membrane proteins in Arabidopsis, 91 membrane proteins in human and 22 membrane proteins in yeast that satisfy the above criteria. We next selected At1g61670 in Arabidopsis for confirmation. The N-terminal GFP-At1g61670 fusion expressed in plant cell showed punctate signals that colocalized with the Golgi marker ManI-mRFP but not the PVC marker mRFPVSR2. These results indicate that the KXD/E motif may perform a general COPI interaction function for other membrane proteins other than EMPs. Most of the analysis data have been included in an opinion article published in Trends in Plant Science in 2014. In addition, using transient expression in Arabidopsis protoplast, we demonstrated the Golgi-localization of newly cloned KXD-containing membrane protein with previously unknown subcellular localization, thus, confirming our original prediction. These results have been included in a research article published in Molecular Biology of the Cell in 2015. Thus, we have achieved the original objective 2 fully. Objective 3: Previously we showed that KXD/E motif is essential for the Golgi localization of EMP12 in Arabidopsis, owing to the binding of the motif towards the COPI coatomers to achieve its Golgi retention function. To examine whether the KXD/E motif has similar COPI binding ability among different organisms, we performed pull down assay using the synthetic peptides corresponding to the AtEMP12 cytosolic tail (CT) as a bait to isolate binding proteins from the yeast extracts, followed by SDS-PAGE and MS/MS analysis for protein identification. The wild-type AtEMP12 CT peptide, but not the mutated one, pulled out the COPI coatomer subunits β-COP and ε-COP. This binding result is consistent with our previous pull-down result obtained using Arabidopsis proteins, indicating a conserved interaction ability of KXD/E motif and COPI coatomers in different organisms. Thus, EMP proteins among different organisms achieve their Golgi localization via a dynamic interaction between the C-terminal KXD/E motifs and COPI vesicle. These results have been included in a research article published in Molecular Biology of the Cell in 2015. Thus, we have achieved the original objective 3 fully. Objective 4: To further investigate the function of COPI in Golgi retention of membrane proteins containing KXD/E motif, we employed an RNAi approach to generate transgenic plants expressing hairpin RNAi fragments against ε-COP under the control of a dexamethasone (DEX)-inducible system. The hairpin RNAi construct produced an effective knock down of both ε-COP homologues after DEX induction, and the DEX-treated ε-COP RNAi seedlings was lethal. These results proved the essential function of COPI in plant growth. We then crossed various Golgi marker lines with the COPI RNAi line for testing its effect on Golgi targeting upon DEX induction, to investigate their COPI-dependent or independent mechanisms. AtEMP12-GFP-RNIKCD, a Golgi marker containing effective COPI interaction motif at the C-terminus, showed typical Golgi localization pattern without DEX treatment. Yet, the marker was mislocalized to vacuole after DEX induction. These results proved the COPI dependence of Golgi retention of AtEMP12 in plant. To test the possible COPI-independent mechanism of Golgi localization of membrane proteins without obvious COPI interaction signals, we also crossed the DEX-inducible COPI RNAi plant with other Golgi marker plants, for example ST-YFP. Interestingly, after DEX induction, ST-YFP still localized to the Golgi but not the post-Golgi compartment like vacuole. In addition, strong ER localization of ST-YFP was detected after COPI RNAi, indicating the disassociation of Golgi stacks and the fusion between ER and the Golgi remnants. We further performed transmission electron microscopic (TEM) analysis of ultrathin sections of ε-COP RNAi seedlings processed by high-pressure freezing/freeze substitution for their effects of COPI RNAi on the morphological change of ER and Golgi. We found that there is a reduction in the number of cisternae per Golgi stack in the root cells of DEX-treated ε-COP RNAi plants. While the Golgi apparatus of non-induced cells typically contained around five cisternae, those in DEX-treated plants contained only around three to four cisternae. Apart from altered Golgi morphology, we observed many abnormal vesicle clusters resembling secretory vesicles near the Golgi remnants under DEX treatment. We also examined the cotyledon cells after DEX treatment. However, most of the Golgi became much more fragmented as compared to those in root cells, and it is difficult to detect Golgi with normal architecture. To test whether AtEMP12 was still located to the heavily fragmented Golgi remnants, we performed immunogold labeling with AtEMP12-specific antibodies. Anti-AtEMP12 labeling could be found in the fragmented Golgi structures, which are possibly ER–Golgi hybrids. We also observed gold particle labeling on MVBs, which is consistent with our previous results implicating MVBs on the pathway to vacuolar degradation of AtEMP12 upon mutation of the KXD/E motif. All these results support our original hypothesis, and have been included in a research article published in Molecular Biology of the Cell in 2015. Thus, we have achieved the original objective 4 fully. Related research: With the support of this grant to graduate students, we have also performed other related research on COPII-mediated protein trafficking and AP1-medaited vacuolar targeting in plant cells, with several publications in PNAS, Plant Cell, Molecular Plant, Current Biology, Molecular Biology of the Cell, Trends in Plant Science, Current Opinion in Cell Biology, Current Protocols in Cell Biology, and Methods in Molecular Biology , included in this report.
