466313.label: Major findings and research outcome
466313.value: 1. We have examined the subcellular localization of selective EMPs in Arabidopsis, yeast, and animal cells. Regardless of expression systems, all N-terminal GFP-fused EMPs localized in Golgi, reflecting the true localization, while all C-terminal GFP-fused EMPs mislocalized in post-Golgi compartments. These results proved a conserved role of KXD/E motif in conferring Golgi retention of EMPs among eukaryotes. 2. We have performed a bioinformatic search in different organisms to identify transmembrane proteins containing a KXD/E motif located at cytosolic C-terminus. We selected At1g61670 in Arabidopsis, where the N-terminal GFP fusion localized at Golgi but not PVC. These results indicate that the KXD/E motif may provide a general COPI-interaction function for other membrane proteins. 3. We have performed pull-down assay using synthetic peptides corresponding to AtEMP12 cytosolic tail to capture proteins from yeast extract. Such peptide pulled out COPI coatomer subunits, which agrees with our previous result using Arabidopsis proteins. These results indicate that there is a conserved interaction ability of KXD/E motif and COPI coatomers for Golgi localization maintenance. 4. We have obtained an effective hairpin ε-COP RNAi plant inducible by dexamethasone (DEX). After DEX induction, seedlings were found to be lethal, proving the essential function of COPI in plant growth. We have crossed the COPI RNAi line with various Golgi markers, whose Golgi localization were affected. We have performed electron microscopic analysis to demonstrate that Golgi morphology and cistern numbers were affected by COPI RNAi. 5. With partially support from this project, we have also trained several excellent postgraduate students working on multiple projects with very good research outputs as demonstrated by publications of their thesis work in a number of international journals. For example, we have (1) summarized methods and protocols in our labs for sharing by the plant science community via publication as protocols and methods; (2) reviewed on protein secretion pathways in plants; (3) propose the AP1 complex on the TGN mediates tonoplast targeting of membrane proteins with the dileucine motif; and (4) identify FREE1 and its suppressors in regulating vacuolar protein transport and autophagic degradation. We thus consider these publications as the research output of this grant. 6. The project has resulted in very good publications in international journals including PNAS, Plant Cell, Molecular Plant, Current Biology, Molecular Biology of the Cell, Trends in Plant Science, Current Opinion in Cell Biology, Current Protocols in Cell Biology, and Methods in Molecular Biology.

466313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
466313.value: Our studies showed that GFP fused to N- or C-terminus of EMPs could impact their subcellular localizations. Given that the functions of EMPs in plant remains largely unknown currently, further research could be done to elucidate the correlation between the function and subcellular localizations of EMPs. Correct Golgi targeting should be essential for the normal functions of EMPs. To prove this hypothesis, a direct approach would be to complement plant mutants in the corresponding EMP alleles by expressing either GFP-EMPs or EMP-GFPs to see which form of GFP fusion can rescue the mutant phenotype. This experiment could give further information on the mechanistic research of EMP functions. On the other hand, our present study also demonstrated that knockdown of coatomer by DEX-inducible ε-COP RNAi in plants causes phenotypes under electron microscopy that mimicking the effects of BFA treatment. Therefore, our DEX-inducible coatomer RNAi plants could be useful materials alternative to BFA drug treatment for further studies into the function of COPI in intracellular protein trafficking, as well as into the other physiological function of COPI in plant development.

466313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
466313.value: This GRF-funded project aims to investigate the molecular mechanism of how Endomembrane Proteins (EMPs) is targeted and retained in the Golgi apparatus of eukaryotic cells. Our results demonstrated that only N-terminal GFP fusions could truly reflect the real localization of EMPs. This observation is of essential in subcellular localization studies using confocal microscopy, as an incorrect fluorescence tag fusion could render misleading results. We also showed that KXD/E is a conserved motif in eukaryotes, which is responsible in interacting with COPI coatomers for retaining itself in Golgi apparatus.

466413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
466413.value: Malignant gliomas are the most common and lethal central nervous system cancers. Despite decades of enormous effort and advances in surgery, radiation and chemotherapy, the median survival of patients is still less than 15 months. This dismal clinical outcome makes malignant glioma a particular focus of cancer research. A thorough understanding of the aberrant molecular pathways leading to the progression of glioma is essential for the identification of new therapeutic targets for malignant glioma. Cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) is a cAMP regulated anion channel capable of conducting both Cl- and HCO3-, the mutation of which causes cystic fibrosis (CF), a common autosomal recessive disease with a wide range of severity and manifestation. While there has been recent interest in the risk of various cancers in CF patients and carriers of CFTR mutations, the biological role of CFTR in cancer development is largely unknown. Recently, we have observed that CFTR is robustly expressed in glioma cell lines and primary gliomas. In addition, we have shown that overexpression of CFTR in U87 cells promotes cell growth and inhibits apoptosis both in vitro and in xenograft models. Moreover, we have found that CFTR downregulates the expression of multiple tumor suppressors, such as p53, miR-34a and RB. These results have prompted us to propose an exciting new hypothesis that aberrant expression of CFTR promotes glioma growth through downregulation of tumor suppressor-mediated pathways, such as p53/miR-34a, leading to enhanced cell cycle progression and cell survival. Thus, CFTR has potential to be used as a novel target for glioma treatment. It is our goal in this proposal to determine the role of CFTR in the pathogenesis of glioma and to present a target that is potentially useful for the treatment of glioma. The specific aims of this project are as follows: Aim 1: To determine the role of CFTR in glioma progression by gain and loss of function studies in vitro and in vivo; Aim 2: To elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying CFTR-mediated regulation of glioma progression; Aim 3: To examine the therapeutic potential of CFTR silencing in vivo. Completion of these studies will reveal a previously undefined role of CFTR in cancer and advance our understanding of molecular mechanisms that govern glioma progression. Moreover, the findings of the proposed studies may open up a new avenue for developing therapeutic strategy against malignant glioma by suppression of CFTR.

466413.label: Realisation of objectives
466413.value: AIM1: To determine the role of CFTR in glioma progression by gain and loss of function studies in vitro and in vivo. The objective 1 proposed in the original proposal has been fully investigated and achieved. In order to assess the role of CFTR in glioma growth, we first used CFTR inhibitor to treat different glioma cell lines (U87, U138, U373 and SW1088) and determined the effect of CFTR dysfunction on glioma cell growth. Our results showed that suppression of CFTR function inhibited glioma cell growth in p53 wild type (U87) and p53 mutant (U138, U373 and SW1088) cells. In consistent with our preliminary results, knockdown of CFTR in U87 suppressed cell growth whereas overexpression of CFTR in U87 promoted cell growth. Next, we stably knockdown CFTR in SW1088 cells (Grade III astrocytoma, p53 mutated, CFTRhi). We found that CFTR knockdown in SW1088 not only suppressed cell growth, but also inhibited cell migration and invasion. In summary, CFTR promotes glioma progression and malignancy, independent of p53 status. To study the effect of CFTR knockdown or overexpression on glioma progression in vivo, we injected SW1088 control and knockdown cells subcutaneously. However, after 6 weeks of tumor cell inoculation, there are no tumor formation found. Since SW1088 is not tumorigenic, we used U87 to determine whether overexpression of CFTR promoted tumor formation in both subcutaneous and orthotopic models. Our results showed that in the subcutaneous model, the ratio of tumor /body weight were about 3 times and the ration of tumor size/body weight were more than 40 times in CFTR-overexpressing tumors than control tumors. Consistently, in orthotopic model, the tumor size and burden were significantly increased in CFTR-overexpressing-tumors compared to control cell-inoculated tumors as well. In summary, we have demonstrated that CFTR promotes glioma progression both in vitro and in vivo. AIM2: To elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying CFTR-mediated regulation of glioma progression The objective 2 proposed in the original proposal has been fully investigated and achieved. 1. CFTR suppresses apoptosis in glioma cells independent of p53 To further determine the cellular and molecular basis underlying the effect of CFTR in glioma progression, we first determined whether overexpression of CFTR promoted cell proliferation in U87 cells. The results showed that there was no significant difference in PCNA expression between CFTR-overexpressing and control U87 cells. In addition, cell cycle assay demonstrated that neither overexpression nor inhibition of CFTR regulated cell cycle progression in U87 cells. These results indicate that CFTR does not affect cell proliferation in glioma cells. Next, we evaluated whether CFTR had any effect on cell apoptosis. Our flow cytometry result showed that overexpression of CFTR suppressed apoptosis at the basal level. Moreover, overexpression of CFTR dramatically alleviated H2O2-induced apoptosis or death in U87 cells. These results indicate that CFTR-overexpressing glioma cells exhibit a survival advantage. Moreover, this effect is not related to p53 status, since CFTR suppresses apoptosis in both p53-dependent and p53-independent glioma cell lines. 2. CFTR suppresses apoptosis by upregulation of Akt/Bcl-2 pathway both in vitro and in vivo As a first step to identify the genes that might contribute to the enhanced survival capacity of CFTR-overexpressing U87, a focused real-time PCR array encompassing 84 genes associated with cell proliferation and apoptosis was used (PAHS-020C). 30 genes were upregulated and 4 genes were downregulated over 2 folds when comparing CFTR-overexpressing with control U87 cells. Among them, the most upregulated gene is BCL2. As Akt is known as an upstream regulator of Bcl2-mediated apoptotic pathway, and PI3K/PTEN/Akt pathway appears as most frequently altered signaling pathway in malignant gliomas, we speculated that CFTR might suppress apoptosis via PI3K/Akt pathway. Indeed, our western blot results showed that overexpression of CFTR enhanced the phosphorylation of AKT (p-AKT) at Ser473 in U87 cells. On the contrary, knockdown of CFTR suppressed the expression level of p-AKT in SW1088. In addition, either suppression of Akt pathway by specific p-Akt inhibitor or suppression of PI3K activity by PI3K specific inhibitor abolished the upregulation of BCL-2 by overexpression of CFTR in U87 cells, indicating CFTR regulates BCL-2 expression via PI3K/Akt pathway. Moreover, suppression of Akt activity rescued the promoting effect of CFTR on cell viability in U87. Apart from that, the regulatory effect of CFTR on PI3K/Akt pathway is validated in our xenograft model, which showed upregulated p-AKT in CFTR overexpressing-tumors compared to control tumors. Altogether, these results suggest that CFTR suppresses apoptosis and promotes glioma progression via Akt/Bcl-2 pathway. Aim 3: To examine the therapeutic potential of CFTR silencing in vivo The objective 3 proposed in the original proposal has been fully investigated and achieved. To evaluate the therapeutic effect of CFTR knockdown on glioma progression, we established U87 subcutaneous xenografts first. After 3 weeks, the mice were subdivided in 2 groups (n=10) and injected with 10 µg PEI F25-LMW -complexed CFTRsiRNA or control siRNA for a total of 5 injections. While we found a trend of tumor size reduction, there was no significant change of control and CFTR siRNA-injected tumor xenografts 2 weeks after treatment. Besides the above objectives, we have also determined the expression of CFTR in human samples. We examined the expression levels of CFTR in a cohort of tissue microarray samples which include 5 cases of normal cerebellum and 20 cases of malignant gliomas using immunochemical staining. The immunochemistry result showed the expression level of CFTR in malignant glioma is higher than that in normal brain. In all tested tumors, very weak staining of CFTR was shown in 3/20 of tumors (3/11 in female and 0/9 in male), middle intensity of CFTR was observed in 11/20 of tumors (5/11 in female and 6/9 in male), and high intensity of CFTR was observed in 6/20 of tumors (3/11 in female and 3/9 in male). There was no significant difference in CFTR staining between male and female. Of note, CFTR expression showed a relative low to middle intensity in the low grade (grade 2-3) astrocytomas compared to the high grade (grade 3-4 & 4) astrocytomas or glioblastomas. While we do not find a significant difference in the expression level between normal brain and astrocytoma, the expression levels of CFTR are significantly higher in glioblastoma patients compared to normal brain. These findings suggest that the expression levels of CFTR are significantly increased in glioblastoma and might be positively related to the grades of malignant gliomas.

466413.label: Major findings and research outcome
466413.value: Cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR), is widely expressed at the apical membrane of epithelial cells. Accumulated evidence has related the expression and function of CFTR to cancer development, but remained controversial. While malignant gliomas are the most common and aggressive intracranial tumors, the role of CFTR in the pathogenesis of glioma development is unknown. We have found that CFTR is highly expressed and exhibits Cl- channel function in glioma cell lines. Suppression of CFTR channel function or knockdown of CFTR suppresses glioma cell viability whereas overexpression of CFTR promotes it. Additionally, overexpression of CFTR suppresses apoptosis and promotes glioma progression in both subcutaneous xenograft model and orthotopic glioma model. CFTR activates Akt/Bcl-2 pathway, whereas suppression of PI3K/Akt pathway abolishes CFTR overexpression-induced upregulation of BCL-2 and cell viability. More importantly, the expression level of CFTR is dramatically increased in glioblastoma patient samples and potentially correlated with glioma grades. Taken together, our study has revealed a novel mechanism by which CFTR promotes glioma progression via upregulation of Akt/Bcl-2-mediated anti-apoptotic pathway, which warrants future investigations into the potential of using CFTR as a therapeutic target and exploring combination therapy to aim for PI3K/Akt pathway in the treatment of glioblastoma. Apart from that, with the captured funding, we have also found that CFTR is involved in various pathological conditions which are closely correlated to cancer development, such as chronic inflammation and fibrosis (Xie C et al., J Cell Physiol. 2015; Liu K et al., Oncotarget. 2016; Zhang JT et al., Sci Rep 2017;). In addition, CFTR is also involved in maintaining the ESC property (Liu ZQ et al., Cell Death Diff 2017). Most importantly, besides glioma, we have found that CFTR is also critical for the development of lung cancer and nasopharyngeal cancer (Li J et al., Int J Oncol. 2015; Tu Z et al., Oncotarget 2016). Altogether, we have revealed that CFTR is not merely an ion channel but also an important regulator of cancer development and progression with multiple signaling pathways identified.

466413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
466413.value: We have revealed that CFTR is highly expressed in glioma patients. While there is a trend of correlation of CFTR expression level with glioma grades, we did not find significant difference between astrocytoma and glioblastoma due to small sample size. Thus, we have initiated a relative large scale retrospective clinical study investigating the correlation of CFTR with malignant glioma with our collaborators in Mainland China. On the other hand, constitutive PI3K/Akt pathway activation is a hallmark of glioblastoma, however, results from clinical trials by using PI3K/mTOR inhibitors are disappointing. Therefore, identification of novel targets along this pathway is required for developing alternative therapeutic strategies to suppress this pathway in glioblastoma treatment. Our finding that CFTR regulates Akt/Bcl-2- mediated anti-apoptotic pathway, warrants future investigations into the potential of using CFTR as a therapeutic target and exploring combination therapy to target PI3K/Akt pathway in the treatment of glioblastoma.

466413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
466413.value: Glioma is the most common and most malignant of central nervous system (CNS) tumors in adults with overall poor outcome and inevitable lethality. Despite decades of enormous effort and advances in surgery, radiation and chemotherapy, the overall 5 year survival rate of high grade malignant glioma patients remains less than 5%. This dismal clinical outcome makes glioma a focus of cancer research. Here, we have found that Cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR), a cAMP-activated Cl- channel, is robustly expressed in glioma cell lines and primary gliomas. Suppression of CFTR channel function or knockdown of CFTR suppresses glioma cell viability whereas overexpression of CFTR promotes it. Additionally, overexpression of CFTR suppresses apoptosis and promotes glioma progression in animal xenograft models. Mechanically, CFTR activates Akt/Bcl-2-mediated anti-apoptosis pathway, and then promotes glioma cell survival. More importantly, the expression level of CFTR is dramatically increased in glioblastoma patient samples. Taken together, our study has revealed a novel mechanism by which CFTR promotes glioma progression via upregulation of Akt/Bcl-2-mediated anti-apoptotic pathway, which warrants future investigations into the potential of using CFTR as a therapeutic target and exploring combination therapy to aim for PI3K/Akt pathway in the treatment of glioblastoma.

466513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
466513.value: 主觀性耳鳴定義為在沒有聲音刺激之下感覺到聲音。在一般人口中，此乃常見的症狀。儘管有各種療法，但沒有持續有效的治療方法，亦沒有被廣泛接受的治療已被對照研究證明是有效的。因此，需要前瞻性對照研究，提供明確的證據，證明治療方法的成效。 實證數據表明，耳鳴的病理生理基礎是大腦中的神經活動。一般普遍接受，大多數耳鳴的形成是由於聽覺中樞神經系統的重組和過度活躍。最近的研究結果表明，耳鳴不僅是跟聽覺皮層過度活躍有關，也跟一些非聽覺的大腦區域過度活躍有關。以這些耳鳴機制的現代理論為基礎，腦刺激於耳鳴控制的應用已經開始發展。使用經顱磁刺激（TMS），可以無創性刺激腦部。許多研究已經證實在聽覺腦區進行低頻重複經顱磁刺激（rTMS）的正面效果，但只有中度的規模效應。一些初步證據顯示，刺激聽覺和非聽覺的大腦區域或僅是後者的治療效果更好。這些類型的刺激在小數患者已被證明是有效的，但尚未在隨機對照試驗中驗證。 本研究旨在探討治療耳鳴成效。我們建議進行隨機雙盲對照試驗，以測試神經導航低頻rTMS治療耳鳴的成效。為了達到足夠的統計功效，足以檢測出耳鳴治療成效的差異，本研究將招募135名患有主觀性耳鳴的受試者，並隨機分成三組： 1）真正rTMS於右背外側前額葉皮層（DLPFC），2）真正rTMS於左邊的初級聽皮層和3 ）假rTMS在左邊的初級聽皮層。 研究亦以下列四種指標進行即時及持續性的成效對比： 1) 中文版耳鳴問卷, 2) 中文版耳鳴障礙問卷, 3) 自我評估耳鳴響度; 及 4) 以心理聲學方法量度出的耳鳴響度。此研究採用治療意向分析法。透過嚴謹的隨機對照試驗設計，這項研究的結果將不僅為耳鳴管理臨床決策提供有力的證據，也有助於進一步了解耳鳴機制。

466513.label: Realisation of objectives
466513.value: In order to address the objectives, we performed a randomized controlled trial. 82 potential subjects have been screened for their eligibility for joining the study. 42 subjects met the inclusion criteria and only 16 subjects were enrolled in the study. Most subjects reported difficulty in taking leave for 10 intervention sessions in 2 consecutive weeks. Due to the small sample size, the power of the study is much lowered and so thus the percentage of objectives achievement. The 16 subjects were randomized prospectively into 3 groups: 5 subjects for real rTMS of the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) (RD), 5 subjects for real rTMS of the left primary auditory cortex (LA) and 6 subjects for sham rTMS of the left primary auditory cortex (SA). Block randomization with a block size of six and allocation ratio of 1:1:1 was used. Both the subjects and the assessors were blinded to the treatment assigned. The non-blinded staff who perform the stimulation was instructed not to communicate with the subjects about the treatment group assignment. The outcome assessments were made right before, immediately, 3 months and 12 months after the final treatment session. Outcome measures used including two self-assessed tinnitus questionnaires (the Chinese Tinnitus Handicap Inventory (THI-CH) and the Chinese Tinnitus Questionnaire (TQ-CH)), a self-rated visual analogue scale (VAS) on tinnitus loudness, and the tinnitus loudness matches at the tinnitus frequency and at 1000Hz. Assessments were done at baseline, immediate after 10 sessions of intervention, 3-month, 6-month and 12-month after intervention. Intention-to-treat analysis was conducted to handle the cases that drop out. Inferential statistical methods, such as analysis of variance and multiple regression analysis, were applied to compare the measures of the two treatment groups as well as the sham group. The effect of the intervention was measured by the standardized treatment effect size. In addition, the effect of a set of independent variables, including subjects’ age, gender, hearing level, duration, laterality, and pitch of tinnitus, with adjustment for baseline characteristics, was studied. Interactive effects, such as baseline hearing level and tinnitus distress (i.e., TQ-CH score), were also investigated.

466513.label: Major findings and research outcome
466513.value: The age of the subjects ranged from 32 to 68 (mean = 57.5, SD = 9.4) and there were 9 males and 7 females. Mean time since onset of tinnitus was 6.75 years (SD = 7.8), and 14 subjects (87.5%) had unilateral or lateralized tinnitus. Most subjects had mild hearing loss at 0.5, 1 and 2k Hz, and an average moderate hearing loss at 4, 6 and 8k Hz . TQ-CH and THI-CH total scores at baseline were similar between all three groups. The three groups were comparable in terms of hearing level, and tinnitus loudness matching. Post-intervention outcome In general, there was a decrease in the TQ-CH total score at the intervention endpoint for the LA and RD group (from 50.6 and 51.0 decreased to 30.2 and 44.2 for the LA and RD group respectively) and the score maintained at 3 months after intervention. General linear regression analysis with repeated measures revealed insignificant main effect for both time and intervention group. There was no significant interaction between intervention group and time. Similar analyses were performed on the secondary outcome measures. Reduction in THI-CH scores at the intervention endpoint was noted in the LA and RD group (from 36.4 and 42.0 decreased to 24.0 and 33.2 for the LA and RD group respectively) while there was an increase in the THI-CH score in the SA group from 38.0 to 48.3. The average THI-CH score maintained at 3 months after the intervention endpoint in the LA group but increased in the RD group. There was no significant effect for time, intervention group nor interaction effect between time and intervention. Tinnitus loudness both measured by subjective rating via VAS and psychoacoustically matched at 1k Hz were decreased in the two real rTMS intervention groups (dropped from 6.4 and 7.0 to 5.6 and 5.7 in the LA ad RD group respectively) but slightly increased in the sham control group. No statistically significant differences were found in these secondary outcome measures with both within-subject and between-subject analyses. A multiple regression was performed to predict the changes in TQ-CH scores from gender, age, hearing level, duration and loudness of tinnitus. All these variables were insignificant to the prediction.

466513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
466513.value: The major limitation of this study is the small sample size. Further research with more subjects is needed to provide clinical evidence for the implementation of rTMS for tinnitus management in clinical settings. The team will look for funding opportunities for further research.

466513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
466513.value: Subjective tinnitus is the perception of sound inside the head in the absence of acoustic stimulation. It is a common condition in the population and is associated with variable severity and symptom response. Low frequency repetitive transcranial stimulation has been proposed to be used in tinnitus management. However, there is no standardized procedure or protocol in using such method. In this project, we investigate the immediate and long-term treatment effect of two stimulation sites: left primary auditory cortex and right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. Our results showed both groups have improved tinnitus distress and loudness but further research in more subjects is needed.

466713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
466713.value: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is one of the most common neurodegenerative disorders incapacitating millions of patients world-wide. The eventual cause of PD is the degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc), leading to motor system impairment, while mitochondrial dysfunction, elevated oxidative stress and abnormal accumulation of alpha-synuclein protein are regarded as major pathological events. The exact reasons of the selective vulnerability of SNc neurons are still not fully understood. Despite this, a number of symptomatic therapeutic approaches are available, including levodopa treatment and surgical deep brain stimulation. However, these currently standard therapeutic paradigms are not disease-modifying in nature and there is still no effective cure for the disease. Therefore, neuroprotective strategy represents an important research direction in the treatment of PD. Strong evidence has been found to suggest that abnormally accumulated iron is one of the major factors underlying neuronal damage in many genetic and idiopathic neurodegenerative disorders, including PD. Thus, understanding the mechanism of iron homeostasis and its relationship with the pathological hallmarks of PD is important and of clinically relevance. Towards this goal, with support from a previous GRF grant, we have already shown that hepcidin, a newly discovered iron-regulating hormone, plays a central role in brain iron homeostasis by regulating the expression of iron transport proteins in the central nervous system. Hepcidin administration has also been shown to be effective in lowering brain iron content in iron-loaded animals. Based on these foundation discoveries and other encouraging preliminary data from our laboratory, here we hypothesize that over-expression of hepcidin would be beneficial to PD. In the present proposal, we will exploit a novel adenovirus construct developed in our laboratory in impeding the progression of PD. The study will be based on the well-established animal and cell models of this disorder. A full battery of physiological, pathological and behavioral markers will be used to assess the efficacy of the treatment paradigms. In addition, we will elucidate the mechanisms underlying the beneficial effect of hepcidin, particularly on the role of iron regulation and its impact on oxidative stress, mitochondrial function and alpha-synuclein protein. If adenovirus hepcidin administration can modify the progression of PD, then gene therapy as well as small molecule drugs that can induce hepcidin expression would become feasible therapeutic approaches. The results will therefore open up a new direction in the search of novel and effective therapeutic strategies to treat millions of sufferers of this disease. 帕金森病（Parkinson's disease, PD）是最為常見的神經退行性疾病之一，全球範圍內患者達數百萬。帕金森病主要由於中腦黑質多巴胺神經元死亡最終導致運動系統障礙。線粒體異常，氧化應激和alpha-synuclein蛋白聚集為主要病理特征。而位於黑質的神經元相比其他部位的神經元特別容易受到損傷的原因尚不清楚。目前，帕金森病常見的治療方式包括左旋多巴胺藥物治療，深部腦刺激等，然而這些治療方式以緩解症狀為主，不能扭轉病理過程和治愈該病，因而以神經保護為策略的治療是帕金森病治療的一個重要研究方向。廣泛的研究均證實，異常的鐵聚集是包括PD在內的眾多遺傳和原發神經退行性疾病神經元損傷的主要因素之一。因此，闡明鐵代謝平衡及其與PD主要病理標誌之間的關係具有重要的基礎和臨床意義。為實現這一目標，我們在上一個GRF基金的支持下，成功揭示了鐵調素通過影響鐵轉運蛋白的表達而在中樞神經系統的鐵代謝平衡中佔據重要地位。鐵調素是一種新發現的鐵調節激素，我們的研究表明，鐵調素能有效地降低鐵過載動物模型中的腦鐵含量。在這一發現和我們實驗室其他已有實驗結果的基礎上，我們提出了鐵調素腦內過表達可以緩解和治療PD的假設。在本項目中，我們將探究我們實驗室構建的表達鐵調素的腺病毒對帕金森病程的影響。利用公認的帕金森病動物和細胞模型，我們擬測量帕金森病的一系列生理、病理和行為指標，以評估該治療的有效性。在這一基礎上，我們將進一步探討鐵調素對鐵代謝、氧化應激、線粒體功能和alpha-synuclein聚集等方面的影響，作為基因治療、分子治療的理論基礎，為找尋帕金森病新的有效治療方法開啟新的方向。

466713.label: Realisation of objectives
466713.value: Objective 1. To determine the potential of adenovirus-hepcidin as a promising disease-modifying agent based on well-established animal models of PD. We have successfully constructed the adneovirus-hepcidin, characterised it and tested its usability in over-expressing hepcidin in the intact rodents. Furthermore, in different well-established models of Parkinson's disease in rodents, we determined the effect of adenovirus-hepcidin in alleviating Parkinsonian motor symptoms and confirmed its neuroprotective effects by various parameters. Thus, we have fully realised this objective. Objective 2. To elucidate the neuroprotective mechanism of adenovirus-hepcidin by studying its action on iron accumulation, thereby suppressing reactive oxygen species generation and alpha-synuclein aggregation. To elucidate the neuroprotective mechanism of the adenovirus-hepcidin, we conducted a series of experiments focusing on the action on iron accumulation, reactive oxygen species level and aggregation of alpha-synuclein. We confirmed the multiple effects of hepcidin in these processes. Furthermore, to gain further insight into the underlying mechanisms, we explored the effect of hepcidin on mitochondrial dysfunction. Therefore, not only that we have fully realised this objective, and also extended the scope of study.

466713.label: Major findings and research outcome
466713.value: The major objectives of the proposal are to determine the potential of adenovirus-hepcidin as a promising disease-modifying agent in Parkinsonism, and then to elucidate the underlying neuroprotective mechanism. Our hypothesis is that by targeting abnormal iron homeostasis and related pathogenic processes in Parkinsonism, over-expression of hepcidin is therapeutically beneficial. In Sprague Dawley rats, in addition to a model of iron-overload, two chronic models of Parkinson's disease were produced by rotenone and 6-OHDA administration. Intracerebroventricular or midbrain substantia nigra injection of an adenovirus-hepcidin, an adenovirus carrying a scramble sequence (Ad-blank, as a control) or saline was conducted to study the effect of hepcidin replenishment. In vitro models of Parkinson's disease were produced by treating SH-SY5Y cells with rotenone or via alpha-synuclein plasmid transduction. Our result show that hepcidin ameliorated motor deficits of Parkinsonian rats assessed by a comprehensive set of motor behavioural tests, including catalepsy test, rotarod test, stepping test and ladder rung test. Immunohistochemical staining for tyrosine hydroxylase revealed neuroprotective effect of hepcidin on dopaminergic neurons, in iron-overloaded, rotenone- and 6-OHDA-treated rats. Furthermore, iron was found to accumulate in the substantia nigra in 6-OHDA- and rotenone-treated rats, with accompanying disruption of various iron transport proteins. These effects were all rectified by treatment of adenovirus-hepcidin. Hepcidin also suppressed rotenone- and 6-OHDA-induced oxidative stress, through quantification of different markers. Further elucidation of the therapeutic mechanism revealed that hepcidin protected rotenone-induced mitochondrial damage via decreasing iron content. In addition, rotenone-induced alpha-synuclein accumulation in the substantial nigra and SH-SY5Y cells was reversed by hepcidin. Together, the findings of the present project suggest that iron homeostasis dysregulation, and the associated oxidative stress, mitochondria dysfunction and alpha-synuclein accumulation are important factors in the pathogenic process of Parkinsonism induced by rotenone and 6-OHDA. Hepcidin replenishment, which can be effectively achieved by administration of adenovirus-hepcidin, is proved to be an effective means for eliminating these abnormalities in which iron homeostasis plays a critical role.

466713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
466713.value: Our results have confirmed the efficacy of viral-based strategy in up-regulating central hepcidin, which can protect dopaminergic neurons known to degenerate in Parkinson's disease, achieving therapeutic effect. Based on these findings, follow-up work can be adopted to 1) further study the role of hepcidin in the manifestation of Parkinsonian symptoms in patients and animal models, and 2) find strategies to facilitate translation of the findings to clinical setting. New project proposals could be put forward for these follow-up projects.

466713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
466713.value: Parkinson’s disease, characterized by dopaminergic neuron loss in the midbrain substantia nigra pars compacta and motor impairment, is the second most common neurodegenerative disease incapacitating millions of patients in the world. However, the exact causes of the degeneration of substantia nigra neurons are still obscure. There is strong evidence that abnormal iron accumulation in the substantia nigra is one of the major causes of neural degeneration in Parkinson's disease. Our study has shown that hepcidin, a newly discovered iron-regulating hormone which controls iron homeostasis in the central nervous system, could help alleviate the symptoms of Parkinson's disease. We demonstrated the feasibility of up regulating hepcidin exploiting a virus-based strategy, and have also elucidated the mechanism of action. Our results have the potential to be translated to clinics helping the rapidly increasing population of Parkinson's disease patients.

466913.label: Realisation of objectives
466913.value: 1. Objective 1: Using normal 16HBE14o- cells and primary human bronchial epithelial (HBE) cells, we have characterized the mRNA and protein expression patterns of heme oxygenases HO-1 and HO-2 using real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) and Western blotting, respectively. Inflammation in the bronchial epithelia was induced by exposing the cells to poly-L-arginine (PLA), a surrogate for the major basic protein (MBP), thereby damaging these epithelia and inducing inflammation. Damage of the cells by PLA leads to the release of nucleotides into the extracellular medium, and the extracellular nucleotides, such as ATP, UTP and UDP, stimulate the secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines (e.g., IL-6 and IL-8) in an autocrine or paracrine fashion. The expression patterns of the P2X and P2Y receptor subtypes were determined in the 16HBE14o- cells and primary HBE cells by Western blotting. In addition, we have determined whether the following would up-regulate HO-1 and HO-2 mRNA and protein expression in the 16HBE14o- and primary HBE cells: (i) activation of the P2X and P2Y receptors by ATPgammaS (a non-hydrolyzable analog of ATP) and UTP; (ii) carbon monoxide (CO) released from CO-releasing molecules (CORMs); and (iii) PLA. 2. Objective 2: Using Fura-2 microspectrofluorimetry in 16HBE14o- cells and primary HBE cells, we have characterized the inhibitory effect of CO released from CORM-2 on P2Y receptor-mediated increases in the intracellular calcium concentration ([Ca2+]i). We examined the differential inhibitory effect of CO on receptor-mediated calcium release and/or on the influx component. The effect of CO on D-myo-inositol-1-phosphate (IP1; a surrogate of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate [IP3]) production was quantified to monitor the effect on the activation of the P2Y receptor, which is a G protein-coupled receptor. We also determined the inhibitory effect of CO on non-receptor-mediated store-operated calcium entry (SOCE) induced by the inhibition of sacro-endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase (SERCA) by thapsigargin. Using calcium measurements and a PKG activity assay, we assessed the involvement of the soluble guanylate cyclase/cGMP-dependent protein kinase G (sGC/PKG) pathway in the inhibitory process of CO on P2Y receptor-mediated calcium signaling. We have examined the effect of CO on P2Y receptor-stimulated calcium signaling and short-circuit current (ISC), which is an index of electrogenic ion transport, by simultaneously monitoring fluorescence signals and ISC in a polarized epithelium. The effect of CO on forskolin-stimulated cAMP levels and ISC was also examined. 3. Objective 3: We have determined the effect of CO on PLA or P2Y receptor activation on the release of two pro-inflammatory cytokines, IL-6 and IL-8, in the 16HBE14o- cells and primary HBE cells. CO was introduced to the cells using either CORMs (CORM-2 and CORM-3) or induction of HO-1 expression by hemin to produce CO endogenously. The anti-inflammatory role of the HO-1/CO axis was verified using either an HO-1 siRNA knockdown approach or a specific HO-1 inhibitor. We assessed the involvement of the ERK1/2 mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), p38 MAPK and NF-κB pathways using Western blotting. This study has demonstrated for the first time that the expression and function of the HO-1/CO axis is an anti-inflammatory component in the human bronchial epithelium. The expression and function of the HO-1/CO axis was mediated by opposing effects on the pro-inflammatory pathway that was activated by the P2Y receptors. We believe this study fulfilled the three objectives.

466913.label: Major findings and research outcome
466913.value: Expression patterns of HO-1 and HO-2, and P2X and P2Y receptors: HO-1 and HO-2 mRNA were both expressed in the 16HBE14o- cells, and HO-2 levels were higher than HO-1. Both the 16HBE14o- and primary HBE cells had higher protein expression levels for HO-2 than HO-1, suggesting HO-2 was the predominant and constitutively expressed isozyme. The P2X4, P2X5, P2X6 and P2X7 receptor subtypes were expressed in the 16HBE14o- cells, while only P2X6 and P2X7 were expressed in primary HBE cells. Both the 16HBE14o- and primary HBE cells expressed the P2Y1, P2Y2, P2Y4 and P2Y6 receptor subtypes. The mRNA expression of HO-1 and HO-2 could be up-regulated when the cells were exposed to PLA, but only HO-1 protein expression was up-regulated. Activation of the P2X and P2Y receptors by ATPgammaS up-regulated HO-1 mRNA and protein expression in the 16HBE14o- cells. CO released from CORM-2 up-regulated HO-1 protein expression in the 16HBE14o- and primary HBE cells. CO regulation of calcium signaling pathways, and calcium-dependent and cAMP-dependent Cl- secretion: CORM-2 increased both [Ca2+]i and IP1, which was inhibited by phospholipase C inhibitor U73122. In contrast, the P2Y2/P2Y4 receptor-mediated intracellular Ca2+ release and influx induced by UTP were inhibited in by CORM-2. CORM-2 did not affect the SOCE induced by thapsigargin. The inhibitory effect of CORM-2 on UTP-induced calcium increase was abolished with a sGC inhibitor, ODQ, or a PKG inhibitor, KT5823, suggesting the involvement of sGC/PKG signaling in this process. CORM-3 inhibited forskolin-evoked increases in cAMP levels and ISC, and it also inhibited the P2Y2/P2Y4 receptor-mediated increases in calcium signals and ISC in polarized 16HBE14o- epithelia. We found similar results when CO gas was used. CO anti-inflammatory effects: HO-1 protein expression was induced by hemin, an HO-1 inducer, and HO-1 expression could be knocked down by siRNA technology in both cell types. Hemin significantly suppressed the PLA- and nucleotide-induced release of IL-6 and IL-8. The inhibitory effects of hemin were attenuated by SnPP, an HO-1 specific inhibitor, or hemoglobin, a CO scavenger. The HO-1 siRNA knockdown abolished the inhibitory effect of hemin on the release of IL-6 and IL-8. These findings suggest an important anti-inflammatory role for endogenously produced CO. Exogenously applied CO via CORM-3 also inhibited nucleotide-induced IL-6 and IL-8 release. CO inhibited p65 NF-κB and ERK1/2 MAPK phosphorylation but not p38 MAPK in the primary HBE cells, suggesting the anti-inflammatory effect of CO was mediated by inhibiting these two signaling pathways.

466913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
466913.value: We have demonstrated that in human bronchial epithelia, HO-1 is an inducible isoform in response to cellular damage by cationic proteins, PLA and the activation of P2X and P2Y receptors. To further study the anti-inflammatory role of the HO-1/CO axis in human bronchial epithelia, a stable HO-1- knockdown human bronchial epithelial cell line has been established using lentiviral vectors. In the future, it will be important to measure the real-time changes in CO levels inside living cells in the presence of CORMs and to correlate the CO levels with biological activities. In collaboration with colleagues from Department of Chemistry, CUHK, we will develop a selective fluorescent probe for the detection of CO, either endogenously produced by HO or through release from CORMs. The detailed cellular mechanism(s) underlying the inhibitory effect of CO on cAMP formation and ion channels (e.g., apical CFTR Cl- channels or basolateral cAMP-dependent K+ channels) responsible for transepithelial Cl- secretion will be explored. We expect to submit either a GRF or HMRF grant proposal in 2018/2019.

466913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
466913.value: The purinergic receptor, P2Y, is expressed in the apical and/or basolateral membranes of virtually all polarized epithelia to control the transport of fluid and electrolytes. A recent discovery suggests that P2X receptors are also expressed in epithelial tissues, and the expression levels of both of these receptors are up-regulated in inflammatory diseases. We have demonstrated for the first time that the anti-inflammatory effect of carbon monoxide (CO) or CO-releasing molecules (CORMs) observed in the respiratory system might result from the inhibitory effect of CO on calcium signaling pathways that are mediated by the P2Y and/or P2X receptors. The effect of CO on these pathways affects the ion transport and immune functions mediated by the purinergic receptors that are expressed in the bronchial epithelia. Thus, CO might act as an important regulator of calcium homeostasis and electrolyte transport and thus the height of airway surface liquid in human airway epithelia. These findings help further explain the function of CO in many physiological and pathological conditions. This information will be relevant to the potential clinical use of CO or CORMs for treating airway inflammatory diseases, which could lead to additional therapeutic applications such as treatments for airway inflammation by targeting purinergic receptors.

467613.label: Major findings and research outcome
467613.value: Background: Women after menopause are prone to osteoporosis, and most pharmacologic treatments for treating osteoporosis are anti-resorptive agents. Currently, hormone replacement therapy is the major treatment that prevents bone loss in women. In the light of this, there is an urgent need to develop a novel strategy using genuine bone anabolic agents to deal with the established osteoporosis. Hence, effects of simvastatin (a HMG CoA reductase inhibitor), alone or in combination with vitamin D, and the underlying mechanisms involved of bone anabolism, in vitro and in vivo, in ovariectomized (OVX) mice were examined. Methods: Osteoblasts were harvested from sham and OVX mice, incubated with simvastatin (1, 3 and 10 nM) and 1α,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 (1,25(OH)2D) (1, 3 and 10 nM), alone or in combination. OVX mice were orally administered (daily, 3 months) with simvastatin (0.01 mg 10g-1), alone or in combination with vitamin D (0.05 µg 10g-1). Results: Simvastatin (10 nM) plus 1,25(OH)2D (10 nM) (≥ 7 days) increased p-HMG CoA reductase and HMG CoA reductase expression in osteoblasts of sham and OVX mice. A reduction of the expression of most bone anabolic / transcription factors measured was detected in osteoblasts of OVX mice compared with sham. Simvastatin plus 1,25(OH)2D elicited a concentration- and time-dependent increase of most bone anabolic biomarkers measured, with a greater magnitude of increase in OVX mice. Consumption of simvastatin plus vitamin D resulted in the restoration of reduced serum Ca2+ levels of OVX mice. Combined drugs consumption increased the failure load / stress and stiffness of femurs, and improved the micro-structure of the L-5 lumbar vertebra of OVX mice. Serum undercarboxylated osteocalcin (ucOC) and insulin levels were increased and reduced, respectively, in OVX mice and the altered ucOC and insulin levels were reduced (unOC) / enhanced (insulin) after combined drugs treatment. An atrophic structure with a lower insulin expression was detected in sections of the pancreas of OVX mice which were reversed after combined drugs consumption. Conclusions: Our results illustrate the bone anabolic effects of simvastatin plus vitamin D in treating oestrogen deficiency-associated osteoporosis. A manuscript based on the results of this proposal has been submitted to Frontiers in Pharmacology and revision is underway as requested by the Journal Reviewers.

467713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
467713.value: 順鉑聯合紫杉醇作為標準化療方案用於治療卵巢高級別漿液性癌已有15年之於，但此方案往往只是暫時控制疾病的發展，治療結束後疾病還會復發。因此，急需研發新的方案來提高治療效果。最新研究發現一種由放療和化療引起細胞免疫原性死亡的特殊現象。研究員觀察到放化療殺死的腫瘤細胞會激發抗腫瘤免疫反應，從而清除殘餘的腫瘤細胞。我們的前期研究已經發現紫杉醇可以誘導釋放引起人和鼠卵巢高級別漿液性癌細胞免疫原性死亡的關鍵因數，包括鈣網織蛋白（CRT），高遷移率族蛋白1(HMGB1)，和ATP。同時，我們還發現紫杉醇能誘導卵巢高級別漿液性癌細胞合成趨化因數CCL2（通過CCR2受體趨化樹突狀細胞），以及暴露F-actin配體（壞死細胞受體的特殊配體，DNGR-1）。然而，順鉑並無這些特徵。基於這些研究結果，我們假設紫杉醇能夠通過誘導合成CLL2和暴露F-actin配體而引起卵巢高級別漿液性癌細胞免疫原性死亡。為了進一步驗證該假設，我們將會進行以下研究1）通過體內免疫原性試驗測試紫杉醇是否可以誘導卵巢高級別漿液性癌細胞免疫性死亡；2）觀察紫杉醇是否通過TLR4-NFkB信號傳導通路誘導卵巢癌細胞合成釋放CCL2，CCL-2上調是否會趨化樹突狀細胞從而介導抗腫瘤免疫反應；3）觀察紫杉醇是否可以促進卵巢癌細胞F-actin的聚合作用，以及卵巢高級別漿液性癌細胞免疫原性死亡是否需要通過DNGR-1暴露F-acin配體位點。紫杉醇誘導卵巢高級別漿液性癌細胞免疫原性死亡的研究成果將會提示選擇化療聯合免疫療法（例如啟動樹突狀細胞）作為治療卵巢高級別漿液性癌首選方案。聯合療法有可能提高腫瘤細胞的清除率，因此可降低卵巢癌病人的死亡率。另外，通過研究CCL2和F-actin如何參與紫杉醇誘導細胞免疫原性死亡將會深入影響抗腫瘤治療方案的設計。

467713.label: Realisation of objectives
467713.value: Objective 1: To study if paclitaxel induces immunogenic cell death in high-grade serous ovarian cancer cells Paclitaxel induces molecular characteristics of immunogenic cell death in mouse ovarian cancer cells To investigate the chemotherapy drugs induce CALR and ERp57 surface exposure in ovarian cancer cells, cell surface CALR and ERp57 was examined in dying (but not dead) ID8 cells after treatment with cisplatin, carboplatin or paclitaxel by flow cytometric analysis and confocal microscopy. Our results showed that treatment with paclitaxel, but not cisplatin or carboplatin, induced CALR and ERp57 exposure on the plasma membrane surface of dying ID8 cells. Next we investigated if the chemotherapy drugs induce HMGB1 release in ovarian cancer cells. Soluble HMGB1 was examined in conditioned media of ID8 cells after chemotherapy drug treatments by ELISA and Western blot analysis. Our results showed that high levels of HMGB1 were detected in the conditioned media of ID8 cells after treatment with paclitaxel, cisplatin or carboplatin. The levels of HMGB1 release in dying ID8 cells seems to be correlated to the levels of cell death. Secretion of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) is another characteristic of immunogenic cell death. Autophagy is essential for the immunogenic release of ATP from dying tumor cells. Here the levels of autophagy in mouse ovarian cancer cells after chemotherapy drug treatments were examined by CYTO-ID® autophagy detection kit. Our results showed that high levels of autophagy were detected in dying ID8 cells after treatment with paclitaxel, but not cisplatin or carboplatin. ATP secretion was also examined in the conditioned media of dying ID8 cells by ATP detection assay. Our results showed that high levels of extracellular ATP were detected in dying ID8 cells with treatment with paclitaxel, but not in cisplatin or carboplatin. Take together, our results indicate that paclitaxel, but not cisplatin or carboplatin, induces molecular markers of immunogenic cell death in mouse ovarian cancer cells. Paclitaxel induces antitumor immunity in syngeneic mouse model of ovarian cancer We are now using a vaccination experiment in syngeneic mouse ovarian cancer model (intraperitoneal ID8 tumor in C57B/L6 mice) to investigate if treatment of paclitaxel, but not cisplatin or carboplatin, induces antitumor immunity in mouse ovarian tumor. Since the growth rate of intraperitoneal ID8 tumors in mice is long (up to 3 months per experiment), the progression of our in vivo experiments is slow. Objective 2: To study if paclitaxel induces CCL2 in ovarian cancer cells through TLR4-NFκB signaling, and if the up-regulation of CCL2 recruits dendritic cells for paclitaxel-mediated antitumor immunity After obtaining this funding, two similar projects were reported. One reported that chemokine CCL2/chemokine receptor CCR2 signaling axis is essential for recruitment of functional antigen-presenting cells into tumors upon chemotherapy (Ma Y et al., Cancer Res. 2014). The other publication reported that IκBξ is a transcriptional key regulator of CCL2 (Hildebrand DG et al., J Immunol 2013). Therefore, we shifted our attention to study the molecular mechanism of how paclitaxel induces immunogenic cell death and antitumor immunity in ovarian cancer. Paclitaxel induces immunogenic cell death and antitumor immunity in ovarian cancer through toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) signaling Paclitaxel induces molecular characteristics of immunogenic cell death in mouse ovarian cancer cells via cancer cell-autonomous TLR4 To investigate the molecule mechanism of how paclitaxel induces immunogenic cell death in ovarian cancer cells, we studied the innate immune receptor toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) since TLR4 is a receptor for paclitaxel. Wild type mouse ovarian cancer ID8 cells express high levels of endogenous TLR4. We generated several isogenic derivatives of ID8 cells that lack Tlr4 expression (Tlr4-/-) by CRISPR-Cas9. The absence of Tlr4 gene and TLR4 protein expression in the knockout clones was confirmed by qRT-PCR and Western blot analysis. When we investigated the molecular characteristics of immunogenic cell death that triggered by paclitaxel treatment in the Tlr4 KO clones. We found that the paclitaxel-induced CALR and ERp57 surface exposure, HMGB1 release, and ATP production were diminished in the TLR4 KO clones when comparing to the wild type ID8 cells. These results indicated that paclitaxel induces markers of immunogenic cell death in mouse ovarian cancer cells is dependent on cancer cell-autonomous TLR4. Paclitaxel induces antitumor immunity in syngeneic mouse model of ovarian cancer through cancer cell-autonomous TLR4 We are now using a vaccination experiment in a syngeneic mouse ovarian cancer model (intraperitoneal ID8 tumor in C57B/L6 mice) to investigate if treatment of paclitaxel induces antitumor immunity in ovarian cancer through cancer cell-autonomous TLR4. Objective 3: To study if paclitaxel induces the polymerization of F-actin in ovarian cancer cells, and if the exposure of F-actin is required for immunogenicity of paclitaxel-induced cell death through DNGR-1 F-actin surface exposure involves in paclitaxel-induced immunogenic cell death and antitumor immunity Paclitaxel, but not cisplatin or carboplatin, induces surface exposure of F-actin in mouse ovarian cancer cells through TLR4 DNGR-1 is a C-type lectin homodimeric innate immune receptor that detects the presence of dead cells. Recently, F-actin was found to be an evolutionarily conserved damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) recognized by DNGR-1. The interaction of F-actin and DNGR-1 involved in cross-presentation of dead cell-associated antigens by dendritic cells. To investigate if F-actin is as DAMP in paclitaxel-induced immunogenic cell death in ovarian cancer, we first examined surface exposure of F-actin in mouse ovarian cancer ID8 cells after chemotherapy drug treatments (cisplatin, carboplatin, or paclitaxel) by flow cytometric and immunofluorescence staining analysis. Our results showed that treatment with paclitaxel, but not cisplatin and carboplatin, induced cell surface exposure of F-actin in dying ID8 cells. Moreover, release of F-actin from dying mouse ovarian cancer cells was investigated by detecting soluble F-actin in conditioned media by Western blot analysis. Notably, high levels of soluble F-actin were detected in conditioned media of dying ID cells after treatment with all chemotherapy drugs (cisplatin, carboplatin, and paclitaxel), indicating that the release of F-actin from dying tumor cells is not specific to particular chemotherapy agent. Next, we further investigated if paclitaxel induces surface exposure of F-actin in ovarian cancer is dependent on cancer cell-autonomous TLR4. ID8 cells with Tlr4 KO were treated with paclitaxel. When comparing to wild type ID8 cells, the paclitaxel-induced F-actin exposure was diminished in the Tlr4 KO clones. On the other hand, the release of F-actin was detected in the dying Tlr4 KO clones after treatment with paclitaxel, suggesting that the release of F-actin is not dependent on TLR4 signaling in tumor cells, it rather related to the cell death rate. By the way, we also investigated actin filament polymerization in mouse ovarian cancer cells after paclitaxel treatment by detecting expression levels of G-actin and F-actin. Our results showed that treatment with paclitaxel induces higher levels of F-actin/G-actin ratio in wild type ID8 cells as well as in the Tlr4 KO clones. These results indicated that paclitaxel induces actin filament polymerization in dying ovarian cancer cells is independent of TLR4 signaling, and possibly is related to its ability to inhibit microtubule depolymerization. Paclitaxel mediates antitumor immunity in syngeneic mouse model of ovarian cancer through F-actin and DNGR-1 interaction We are now using a vaccination experiment in a syngeneic mouse ovarian cancer model to investigate if treatment of paclitaxel induces antitumor immunity in ovarian cancer through the interaction of F-actin and DNGR-1 in the ovarian tumor microenvironment.

467713.label: Major findings and research outcome
467713.value: Besides its cytotoxicity by microtubule stabilization, we discovered chemotherapy drug paclitaxel induces immunogenic cell death and antitumor immunity in ovarian cancer. Using syngeneic mouse model of ovarian cancer, we showed that paclitaxel induces immunogenic cell death and antitumor immunity in ovarian cancer through cancer cell-autonomous TLR4. Moreover, we found that surface exposure of F-actin in dying ovarian tumor cells functions as damage-associated molecular pattern in paclitaxel-mediated immunogenic cell death, and the interaction between F-actin on cancer cells and DNGR-1 on dendritic cells is essential for paclitaxel-mediated anitumor immunity in ovarian cancer. In conclusion, we found that chemotherapy drug paclitaxel induces antitumor immunity in ovarian cancer through immunogenic cell death that mediated by TLR4 and F-actin. We are preparing a manuscript for submission to an international peer-reviewed journal.

467713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
467713.value: Based on our finding on paclitaxel-induced immunogenic cell death and antitumor immunity in ovarian cancer, we extended our research to explore the mechanism of recurrence of ovarian cancer after chemotherapy. Our preliminary results suggest that paclitaxel-mediated immunogenic cell death in ovarian cancer cells triggers cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL)-mediated antitumor response, which contributes to the high initial response rate of chemotherapy of ovarian cancer. Notably, we found that a key cytokine for CTL antitumor response, known as interferon-gamma (IFN-γ), up-regulates programmed cell death 1-ligand 1 (PD-L1) in a majority of human and mouse ovarian cancer cells in vitro, while failure of IFN-γ-mediated PD-L1 induction was found in a minority group of human ovarian cancer cell lines with defective IFN-γ signaling. Given that PD-L1 is a ligand of programmed cell death-1 (PD-1) negative regulatory immune checkpoint, we hypothesize that the tumor immunosuppression, which was induced by paclitaxel-mediated antitumor immunity via IFN-γ and PD-L1, contributes to the development of ovarian cancer recurrence. Based on our findings, we proposed the underlying mechanism involves 1) CTL triggered by paclitaxel-mediated immunogenic cell death induces up-regulation of PD-L1 in ovarian tumor cells via IFN-γ; and 2) IFN-γ-mediated induction of PD-L1, in turn, suppresses the antitumor immunity and thus contributes to the relapse of ovarian tumor. This proposed project was also supported by GRF in 2015 (14109515; Study of PD-L1-mediated tumor immunosuppression that contributes to ovarian cancer recurrence).

467713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
467713.value: Our study discovered a novel molecular action of chemotherapy drug paclitaxel in ovarian cancer. We found that paclitaxel not only kills the ovarian tumor cells by microtubule stabilization. Paclitaxel also causes an immunogenic cell death that triggers antitumor immunity in ovarian cancer. Therefore, our results suggest a combinational therapy using chemotherapy and immunotherapy for ovarian cancer.

468013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
468013.value: Phospholipid binding domains play important roles in mediating cellular signaling processes by controlling the trafficking of membrane-associated proteins. The C2 domain is one of the most diverse phospholipid binding domains and has been well characterized in the animal system. However, the functions of plant C2-domain proteins are relatively unknown. We have cloned and characterized OsGAP1, a novel C2-domain protein in rice, which binds to phospholipids and interacts with OsYchF1, an unconventional G-protein. We have also demonstrated through gain-of-function tests that OsGAP1 is a positive regulator of plant defense and abiotic stress responses. Using X-ray crystallography, we have solved the structure of OsGAP1 to a high resolution of 1.63 Å. Based on the 3-D structure and sequence alignment, we performed site-directed mutagenesis and successfully identified the clusters of residues in the C2 domain that are required for phospholipid binding and interaction with YchF proteins. Building on this information, the proposed study aims at analyzing the mechanism of function of the C2 domain in OsGAP1 in detail. Our specific objectives are: (1) to establish a protocol for dissecting the functions of the different regions of OsGAP1; (2) to study the role of phospholipid binding in the function of OsGAP1; (3) to study the mechanism of interaction between OsGAP1 and YchF homologues; and (4) to study the roles played by the unique and conserved structural regions of OsGAP1. 磷脂結合結構域能夠控制膜關聯蛋白的識別，在細胞信號的傳遞中起著重要的作用。而C2結構域作為其中最多樣的磷脂結合結構域，在動物領域研究中較為清楚，而在植物領域中的認知卻十分有限。我們在水稻中發現並克隆了一個新的C2-結構域蛋白，OsGAP1，它可以結合磷脂層，並和一個非常規的G-蛋白OsYchF1相互作用。我們通過功能添加測試證明，OsGAP1在植物的防禦和非生物逆境應答機制中是一個正向調控因數。利用X射線晶體學的方法，我們將其結構解析到1.63 Å的精度。基於其3-D結構和序列分析，我們利用點突變的方法成功地發現了在C2-結構域中和結合磷脂層及與YchF相互作用的氨基酸。基於這些資訊，這項目將會詳細解析OsGAP1中C2-結構域的作用機理。我們的具體目標是：(1) 建立一個分析OsGAP1蛋白中不同結構域的方法流程；(2) 研究磷脂結合功能在OsGAP1的蛋白功能中起的作用；(3) 研究OsGAP1和YchF類蛋白相互作用的機理；(4) 研究OsGAP1獨有且保守的結構區域的作用。

468013.label: Realisation of objectives
468013.value: (1) To establish monitoring systems to dissect the functions of different regions of OsGAP1. In our proposal, we reported that we have already obtained the crystal of OsGAP1. In this work, we successfully refined our X-ray crystallography data to obtain structural details of OsGAP1. To performed detailed analysis of the ability of phospholipid binding and activation of OsYchF1 GTPase activities in mutated OsGAP1 proteins, we have constructed 5 types of mutant OsGAP1 (clusters 1 to 5) that affected OsGAP1 binding to phospholipids and OsYchF1. Using phospholipid dot blot, we showed that mutations in clusters 2, 4, and 5 will abolish phospholipid binding while mutation in cluster 3 will weaken this ability. On the other hand, mutations in clusters 1 and 3 will abolish the activation effect on OsYchF1 GTPase activities. For functional analysis,we have successfully constructed transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana expressing these mutant proteins. Three independent transgenic lines of each mutant constructs were propagated to homozygous stage and for functional analysis. (2) To study the importance of phospholipid binding in the function of OsGAP1. Since our previous works showed that expression of native OsGAP1 in transgenic A. thaliana will enhance both plant defense responses and salt tolerance, we tested these functions in mutants (clusters 4 and 5) that have lost their abilities in phospholipid binding. Mutations in cluster 4 or 5 abolished plant defense responses caused by OsGAP1 but still retained its salt tolerance function. Therefore, phospholipid binding is essential for the plant defense responses but not the salt tolerance function of OsGAP1. (3) To study the importance of YchF homologues that interact with OsGAP1. Using similar approach as described in Objective 2 above, we tested the important of OsGAP1 interaction with YchF homologues in the function of plant defense responses and salt tolerance. Mutations in cluster 1 that have lost its ability to interact with YchF homologues abolished both plant defense responses and salt tolerance caused by OsGAP1. Therefore, interaction with YchF homologues is essential for both the plant defense responses and salt tolerance function of OsGAP1. In addition, we also used X-ray crystallography and site-directed mutagenesis to study the structure-function relationship of the OsGAP1 target, OsYchF1. OsGAP1 negatively regulates OsYchF1 which itself is a negative regulator of plant defense and salt tolerance. Our crystallographic results showed that OsYchF1 can bind to ATP and GTP, and such binding will slight change the protein structure. Binding to ATP, but not GTP is essential to the negative function of OsYchF1 in plant defense. On the other hand, binding to GTP is sufficient for the negative function of OsYchF1 in salt tolerance.

468013.label: Major findings and research outcome
468013.value: We published two important papers in the prestigious scientific journals: JBC (output paper 1) and PNAS (output paper 2). In our JBC paper, we used site-directed mutagenesis to show the significance of interactions with phospholipids and the G-protein OsYchF1 for the physiological functions of the rice OsGAP1. OsGAP1 is a plant-specific C2-domain protein, binds to phospholipids and an unconventional G-protein OsYchF1. In this research, we solved the crystal structure of OsGAP1 to a resolution of 1.63 Å. Using site-directed mutagenesis, we successfully differentiated between the clusters of surface residues that are required for binding to phospholipids versus OsYchF1, which, in turn, is critical for its role in stimulating defense responses. On the other hand, the ability to alleviate salt stress by OsGAP1 is dependent only on its ability to bind OsYchF1 and is independent of its phospholipid-binding activity. These findings will advance our understanding of this group of novel C2-domain proteins and their modes of function. They also shed light on the regulatory mechanisms of the understudied YchF-type unconventional G-proteins. In terms of application, ectopic expression of OsGAP1 will be a strategy to enhance plant resistance to pathogens and salt tolerance. In our PNAS paper, we dissected the structure-function relationship of the target of OsGAP1, the unconventional G-protein OsYchF1. It is an essential step to understand why OsGAP1 could enhance plant resistance to pathogens and salt tolerance. Unlike the conventional G proteins that only bind to GTP, the YchF subfamily possesses the unique ability to bind both ATP and GTP. In this work, we have elucidated the different conformational changes caused by the binding of OsYchF1 to ATP versus GTP by X-ray crystallography. Furthermore, by comparing the 3D relationships of the ligand position and the various amino acid residues at the binding sites in the crystal structures of the apo-form and ligand-bound versions, a mechanism for the protein’s ability to bind both ligands is revealed. Mutation of the noncanonical G4 motif of the OsYchF1 to the canonical sequence for GTP specificity precludes the binding/hydrolysis of ATP and prevents OsYchF1 from functioning as a negative regulator of plant-defense responses, while retaining its ability to bind/hydrolyze GTP and its function as a negative regulator of abiotic stress responses, demonstrating the specific role of ATP-binding/hydrolysis in disease resistance. This discovery will have a significant impact on our understanding of the structure–function relationships of the YchF subfamily of G proteins in all kingdoms of life.

468013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
468013.value: Identification of an OsGAP1 functional target, the unconventional G-protein OsYchF1, has unveiled a novel regulatory hub involving in both plant defense response and salt tolerance. While we have thoroughly analysed the relationship of the OsGAP1-OsYchF1 pair, there are still many unanswered questions related to the functional of OsYchF1. Besides binding to ATP and GTP, OsYchF1 also interacts with multiple protein partners, in which, most of them are regulators in nature. We have obtained a new GRF grant to delineate the regulatory network related to the YchF type G-proteins.

468013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
468013.value: We discovered the rice OsGAP1 protein and showed that it can enhance the hydrolytic activity of ATP and GTP in the rice OsYchF1 protein, thereby eliminating the negative functions in plants’ defense response and salt tolerance. Through X-ray crystallography and site-directed mutagenesis, we delineated the physiological significance of OsGAP1 binding to phospholipids and OsYchF1. X-ray crystallography provides a platform to “observe” such tiny molecules by hitting the crystal of the target protein with X-ray beams. To fully understand the structure and function of the unconventional G-protein OsYchF1, we again employed X-ray crystallography and site-directed mutagenesis to dissect the structure of OsYchF1. We confirmed that the OsYchF1 Protein can bind to ATP and GTP and have different effects on the defense response and stress tolerance of plants. This work has brought us closer to understand how to control this kind of switching system for regulating plant defense response and salt tolerance. Ultimately, this research can help maintain a higher agricultural productivity under adverse conditions, such as crop disease and salinity.

468513.label: Project Objectives
468513.value: To delineate the importance of Smad3-dependent cancer microenvironments in cancer growth, invasion, metastasis, and death in vivo. This will be studied in two syngeneic mouse tumor models by administering two invasive cancer cell lines (LLC and B16F10) subcutaneously and intravenously into genetically-identical global Smad3 KO and wild-type (WT) mice (C57/BL6). To investigate the regulatory mechanisms of TGF-beta/Smad3 in cancer progression by focusing on NK cell differentiation, maturation, and cancer-killing activities. Studies will examine the regulatory role of Smad3 in Id2-dependent NK cell differentiation and T-bet/GATA3-mediated NK cell maturation/activation within the cancer microenvironment of Smad3 KO/WT mice and in vitro in Smad3 KO/WT hematopoietic stem cells under TGF-beta1 and NK cell differentiation conditions. In addition, Smad3-dependent NK cell cancer-killing mechanisms will be studied in vitro. To determine the suppressive role of Smad3 deficient NK cells in cancer progression. The suppressive role of Smad3-null NK cells in cancer progression will be studied by deleting NK cells from the tumor-bearing Smad3 KO mice with the neutralizing NK1.1 antibody。

468513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
468513.value: 目前研究證明， 生长转化因子（TGF-beta）是一個強有力的腫瘤促进因子，通過腫瘤微環境以推動癌症惡化。然而，這一惡性進程的機制在很大程度上仍然還不清楚。因此，我們的研究目標是拓開TGF-beta通過腫瘤微環境以推動癌症惡化的機制。我們推測，癌症源性TGF-beta通過Smad3的依賴性腫瘤微環境而推動肿瘤的惡性進展。我們進行了初步的研究以檢驗這一假設。我們發現，小鼠缺乏Smad3可防止肺癌（LLC）和黑色素瘤（B16F10 ）癌細胞的生長，侵襲，轉移和死亡。這與自然殺傷（NK）細胞顯著上調相关。根據這些初步的研究結果，我們進一步推測， TGF-beta可能通過Smad3抑制NK細胞免疫機制而促進癌細胞的生長，侵襲，轉移。所以，本课题將应用Smad3基因敲除小鼠模型，研究Smad3依賴性微環境对癌症進展的機制。首先，我们将研究TGF-beta/Smad3对NK細胞分化，成熟/激活，並在體內和體外抗癌活性的調節作用。最後，我們將確定Smad3对NK細胞在癌症進展的抑制作用和治療潛力。我們預計，Smad3介導抑制NK細胞免疫功能可能是TGF-beta促進癌細胞的生長，侵襲和轉移的關鍵機制。更重要的是，抑制Smad3可能是一個新穎而有效的抗癌細胞治療

468513.label: Realisation of objectives
468513.value: We have made a great progress in this project with several novel and exciting findings as described below. 1. We have successfully completed the Specific Aim 1 and found that Smad3-dependent microenvironments determined the tumor progression as genetic deletion of Smad3 or inhibition of Smad3 with a pharmacological inhibitor SIS3 protected against lung carcinoma (LLC) and melanoma (B16F10) growth, invasion, metastasis, and death.These novel findings were presented in the 18th World Congress of Oncology (Greece 2013) and published in Nat Commun 2017; 8:14677 (Part 3C). A Patent on Smad3 inhibitor SIS3 has been filed and licensed to MOEXA under named Cancelex (http://www.cancelex.com/cancelex/ ). A Press conference was also held on 6 April, 2017 and this new discovery was publically released by many TV programs and newspapers with total 32 reports (see attachments 1 and 2). 2. We have also completed the Specific Aim 2 and found that Smad3 promotes cancer by suppressing NK cell immunity against cancer via a E4BP4-dependent mechanism as deletion of Smad3 or pharmacological inhibition of Smad3 increased E4BP4 on NK cells and promoted a 10-fold increase in NK cells and their anti-cancer activities. In addition, mice lacking Smad3 also caused a marked suppression on angiogenesis, activation of matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), and production of regulatory T (Treg) cells. Furthermore, Studies in GFP+ chimeric mice found that the tumor microenvironment was derived from bone marrow and reconstitution of GFP+Smad3-/- bone marrow on the tumor-bearing Smad3+/+ mice suppressed the lethal progression of cancers by restoring the NK cell immunity. 3. We have completed the Specific Aim 3 and validated the suppressive role of Smad3 KO NK cells in cancer progression. We found that deletion of NK cells from the tumor-bearing Smad3 KO mice with the neutralizing NK1.1 antibody triggered the deathly progression of melanoma. In contrast, reconstitution of GFP+Smad3-/- bone marrow on the tumor-bearing Smad3+/+ mice can suppress the lethal progression of cancers by restoring the NK cell immunity. These findings revealed a suppressive role of Smad3 in the NK cell-mediated anti- cancer immunity, which was further confirmed in vitro that NK cells lacking Smad3 exhibited much greater cancer-killing activities. 4. Importantly, this study has been extended by successfully obtaining an the Innovation and Technology Fund grant (ITS/227/15) and engineered a TGF-beta tolerant human NK cell line by silencing Smad3 in NK-92 cells for effective anticancer therapy, which has been revised in Cancer Immunology Research (Part C) with an US provisional patent application (62/446,106) filed (attachment 3). Furthermore, a new Smad3 inhibitor called self carry nanodrug-Smad3 inhibition SIS3 (SCND-SIS3) is also recently funded by ITF (ITS138/17) for the further development into the new immunotherapy drug and a novel finding of "A Novel Clec4e/Syk/NF-κB Signalling Circuit Promotes Cancer Progression by Triggering Tumor-associated Macrophage Activation" has been submited to Immunity (see Part C ). 5. Furthermore, we have also developed a novel therapy for cancer by retrieving the balance between Smad3 and Smad7 signaling with asiatic acid (AA, a Smad7 agonist) and naringenin (NG, a Smad3 inhibitor) to effectively inhibit tumor progression in mouse two mouse models of melanoma (B16F10) and lung carcinoma (LLC) by promoting NK cell development and cytotoxicity against cancer via the Id2/IRF2-dependent mechanisms. Results from this study have been submitted to Cancer Immunology Research Communications (See Part C) and an US provisional patent application (15/808,344) and a Chinese Patent ( 201711098547.X) have been filed (See attachments 4 and 5). In summary, all the objectives of this project have been successfully completed. Importantly, based on the exciting findings from this study, two ITF grants have been successfully obtained for the further development of new antitumor drugs. Totally, 3 patents have been filed with one licensed. There are also two PhD students and two Hong Kong Scholars have been recruited into this study.

468513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
468513.value: The finding of Smad3-dependent tumor microenvironment determines cancer progression is novel and important. The identification of Smad3 promotes cancer by suppressing NK cell immunity agaisnt tumor has led to the development of new Smad3 inhibitor and Smad3-silencing NK cells for anticancer immunotherapy. 468513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
468513.value: This project has been very successful with several novel and exciting findings. First, we found that transforming growth factor-beta1 promotes cancer via the Smad3-dependent microenvironments as pharmacological inhibition or genetic deletion of Smad3 can protect against invasive lung carcinoma (LLC) and melanoma (B16F10) growth, invasion, metastasis, and death. Second, we also identified that Smad3 acts by suppressing the NK cell immunity to promote cancer, which can be reversed by blocking Smad3 with a pharmacological inhibition SIS3 or by deleting Smad3 gene. Importantly, these novel findings have made a great progress to develop new drug to treat cancer by promoting the host immunity against cancer with a Smad3 inhibitor or directly by treating cancer with a Smad3-silencing NK cells. Furthermore, findings from this study also suggest that rebalancing TGF-beta/Smad signaling with a novel Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) using the combination of asiatic acid (AA, a Smad7 agonist) and naringenin (NG, a Smad3 inhibitor) may represent another novel TCM-based immunotherapy for cancer. Thus, outcomes from this study are highly significant both scientifically and clinically.

469113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
469113.value: The aim of this study is to apply the most accurate and user-friendly risk prediction model, derived from routine clinical care data, to correctly identify patients at high risk of Intensive Care Unit (ICU) delirium post cardiac surgery, in a sample of Hong Kong patients, while avoiding the burden of drug prophylaxis for individuals at low risk. Delirium is a syndrome characterized by the acute onset of fluctuating levels in severity of consciousness, attention, cognition and perception. ICU delirium is reversible but is a precursor to poor patient outcomes, such as a prolonged stay in the ICU and in hospital, persistent cognitive impairment, poor quality of life, mortality and higher healthcare costs. Although up to half of all patients are at risk of ICU delirium after cardiac surgery, it is often undetected by healthcare professionals. The local incidence of ICU delirium and its association with fast-track failure (i.e. 30-day mortality, readmission to the ICU or a protracted ICU stay longer than 48 hours) after cardiac surgery are unknown. ICU delirium after cardiac surgery can be prevented by the use of delirium risk prediction models. Despite the availability of such risk prediction models, none have been prospectively validated in the local population. Before widespread application of these risk prediction models to our cardiac surgical population can occur, the discrimination (ability of a risk prediction model to distinguish between those who develop delirium from those who do not) and calibration (agreement between the predicted risk and the observed frequency of delirium) properties need to be determined. Furthermore, an assessment is required of the potential impact on drug utilization of preventing ICU delirium by using the best risk prediction model. This study’s prospective cohort of 600 patients undergoing emergency and elective cardiac surgery will (1) determine the incidence of ICU delirium after surgery; (2) externally validate and compare the performance of two risk prediction rules for ICU delirium; (3) estimate the potential clinical consequences for drug resources of applying the best prediction rule; and (4) determine the association between ICU delirium and fast-track failure after cardiac surgery. Accurate identification of patients at high risk of ICU delirium will help healthcare professionals to recognize delirium earlier, give appropriate drug prophylaxis, reduce the risk of fast-track failure, and improve the rate of recovery from cognitive impairment and quality of life after cardiac surgery. 這項研究的目的是從常規臨床數據研發出最準確和方便使用的風險預測模型；在香港的ICU內正確地識別心臟手術後的高風險譫妄病人，同時減低低風險病人使用預防譫妄的藥物用量。 譫妄是一種急性發作的嚴重性意識，注意力，認知和感知等出現水平波動等特徵的綜合症狀。ICU譫妄是可逆轉的，但它是病人預後不良的前兆；例如延期留在ICU和醫院、持久性認知功能障礙、生活質量下降、死亡率較高和增加醫療成本。雖然達一半的病人在心臟手術後會有ICU譫妄的風險，但往往卻未能被醫護人員察覺。在本港，心臟手術後呈現ICU 譫妄的發病率及其與快速康復失敗（即 30 天死亡率，重返ICU或持續 ICU 停留超過 48 小時）之間的關聯仍屬未知。 心臟手術後呈現的ICU譫妄，可使用譫妄風險預測模型預防。儘管已有可用的風險預測模型，但是這些模型尚未在本港得以前瞻性的驗證。在廣泛應用風險預測模型於心臟外科病人之前，我們必需確定模型的區別性（能夠區分那些病人呈現譫妄）和準繩性（譫妄的風險預測和觀測頻率）。 此外，利用最好的風險預測模型，評估為防止ICU譫妄而潛在使用的藥物用量。 這項前瞻性定群研究包括600名接受急診和擇期心臟手術的病人。研究將會（1）確定手術後ICU譫妄的發病率，（2）外部驗證和比較兩個ICU譫妄的風險預測規則的表現（3）使用最佳預測規則估計藥物資源應用的潛在臨床結果; （4） 確定心臟手術後ICU譫妄和快速康復失敗之間的關聯。 精確識別高風險的ICU譫妄病人，有助醫護人員及早於病人接受心臟手術後識別譫妄，給予適當的藥物預防，降低快速康復失敗的風險，及改善病人的認知功能障礙和生活質量。
