Secondary response will be examined by pretreatment with protein transport inhibitor, Brefeldin A. Objective 2: To investigate targeted functional effectors of NR4A2 in transcription (EGR1, PPARG and NF-kappa B), cell death (ATOH8 and G0S2), inflammation (GPR84, IL-8, PTGS2 and TNF-alpha), NO regulation and chemotaxis (CAMK2G and GCH1). Expected deliverables: i. A validated network of LPS-induced transcriptional regulation as a result of NR4A2 silencing by siRNA in two human neutrophil models: (a) primary cord blood neutrophils, and (b) HL-60 differentiated neutrophils. ii. Functional disturbances in these 2 cell models, resulted from NR4A2 silencing, in terms of: a. apoptosis b. cytokine release c. chemotaxis d. activation e. NO synthesis f. ROS production Objective 3: To compare the magnitude of LPS-induced responses of NR4A2 and associated gene expressions in cord blood neutrophils of preterm neonates (gestational age 32-36 weeks), term neonates (gestational age 37-40 weeks) and peripheral blood of adults (age 25-30 years). Expected deliverables: Developmental regulation of NR4A2 downstream genes and network in neutrophils (Objective 2) secondary to LPS stimulation.

472413.label: Realisation of objectives
472413.value: All the 3 objectives were completed. A manuscript entitled: “Expressional Profile of Neonatal Neutrophils and Role of Transcription Factor Nuclear Receptor NR4A Members in Response to Bacterial Lipopolysaccharide” was submitted to the Journal of Immunology for review and publication. (Attached) Our novel findings and deliverables are described as follows: (1) Objective 1: To validate the proposed signal cascade leading to LPS-induced upregulation of transcription factor NR4A2 mediated by TLR-4, p38MAPK and NF-kappa B. We accomplished cord blood sample collection (n=36) from full-term delivery with immediate isolation of neutrophils, followed by in vitro culturing, pretreatment of various antibodies and inhibitors, and stimulation with LPS or with medium only control (CTL). Quantification of target gene expression by qPCR and western blot were performed. Our results showed that: (a) The expression of NR4A2 induced by treatment with LPS was significantly decreased (all P < 0.05) when neutrophils were pretreated with p38MAPK inhibitor SB203580 (73% reduction), and NF-kB inhibitors BAY-117082 (86%) and pyrrolidine dithiocarbamate (93%), respectively compared with the control treatment (dimethyl sulfoxide, DMSO). These data indicated that LPS-receptor binding was activated via NF-kB signals leading to NR4A2 upregulation. Pretreatment of JNK inhibitor (SP600125) did not significantly change the LPS-induced expression of NR4A2 in neonatal neutrophils. (b) A decreased expression of NR4A2 (53%; P = 0.045) in LPS-activated neutrophils after pretreatment with TLR4 blocking antibody validated that TLR4 as one of the key components of LPS receptor in neonatal neutrophils. (c) Pretreatment with protein transport inhibitor, Brefedldin A, also led to a decrease in expression of NR4A2 (51%, P = 0.006), revealing significant effect on secondary response to LPS stimulation. (d) We demonstrated that TLR4 antibody and NF-kB inhibitor reduced NR4A2 protein expression by 80 to 20%, whereas, p38MAPK inhibitor significantly reduced NR4A2 protein levels by 50% after 24 hours of LPS treatment. Our overall results showed that LPS-receptor binding was activated via NF-kB and p38MAPK signals leading to NR4A2 upregulation in neonatal neutrophils. (2) Objective 2: To investigate targeted functional effectors of NR4A2 in transcription (EGR1, PPARG and NF-kappa B), cell death (ATOH8 and G0S2), inflammation (GPR84, IL-8, PTGS2 and TNF-alpha), nitric oxide (NO) regulation and chemotaxis (CAMK2G and GCH1). (a) qPCR assays demonstrated expression of NR4A2 and targeted associated molecular signals (ATOH8, CAMK2G, ERG1, GCH1, G0S2, GPR84, IL8, NFKB1, PPARG, PTGS2 and TNF) in neonatal neutrophils. Upon stimulated with LPS for 4 hours, expressions of all these genes (except CAMK2G) were significantly upregulated (P < 0.05). Expression of CAMK2G was inhibited by LPS (P = 0.0004). The other 2 NR4A family members NR4A1 and NR4A3 were investigated for comparison, and they were also significantly induced by LPS (P < 0.05). (b) Functional assays were performed on both primary cord blood neutrophils and in the in vitro model of differentiated HL60 cells after manipulation of NR4A2 expression. Since the transfection efficiency and cell viability of siRNA transfection with primary neutrophils via nucleofection were too low for functional analysis, we adopted the strategy of overexpressing NR4A2 gene in HL-60 cells by lentiviral transduction. For comparison, we also overexpressed NR4A1 and NR4A3 and investigated their involvement in the regulation of the innate immunity of neonates. Our results showed that in DMSO-differentiated HL-60 cells, overexpression of NR4A2 significantly increased LPS-induced IL8 expression by 2 fold (P = 0.011). However, no difference was observed in chemotaxis assay and nitric oxide synthesis genes (NOS1, NOS2 and NOS3) with or without LPS stimulation. Again, no change in apoptosis and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production was observed in NR4A2 overexpressed differentiated HL-60 cells. Overexpression of NR4A1 significantly reduced chemotaxis of HL60 differentiated cells towards LPS (20%), but did not change the expression of NOS1, NOS2 and NOS3 or the number of apoptotic cells after LPS stimulation. Overexpression of NR4A1 significantly increased LPS-induced IL8 and PTGS2 expression (P < 0.05). Overexpression of NR4A3 showed a trend of reduced expression of NFKB1 in HL-60 differentiated cells upon LPS-stimulation (P = 0.066). (3) Objective 3: To compare the magnitude of LPS-induced responses of NR4A2 and associated gene expressions in cord blood neutrophils of preterm neonates (gestational age 32-36 weeks), term neonates (gestational age 37-40 weeks) and peripheral blood of adults (age 25-30 years). qPCR assays for expression of NR4A1, NR4A2, NR4A3 and associated molecular signals (ATOH8, CAMK2G, EGR1, GCH1, G0S2, GPR84, IL8, NFKB1, PPARG, PTGS2 and TNF) were performed on neutrophils from preterm and term neonates, upon stimulation with LPS. Peripheral blood neutrophils from healthy male adult volunteers were studied in parallel. (a) Expression levels of NR4A1, NR4A2, NR4A3 in neonatal (term and preterm) and adult neutrophils in response to LPS stimulation were compared. At basal level, there were significantly higher expressions of all tested NR4A members in adult compared with term neonatal neutrophils (n=8; P< 0.05), and a higher level of NR4A3 in adult compared with preterm neutrophils (P < 0.01). Exposure to LPS for 4 h increased NR4A1, NR4A2 and NR4A3 in preterm (6.47-17.28 fold), term (6.07-22.12 fold) and adult (2.39-12.85 fold) neutrophils (P < 0.05 except only a trend on NR4A1 levels in preterm infants P = 0.0621). While LPS stimulation increased NR4A1 and NR4A2 in preterm and term neutrophils to levels similar with adult neutrophils, NRA43 levels were significantly higher in adult neutrophils compared with their neonatal counterparts (P < 0.05). (b) Basal and LPS-stimulated expression levels of ATOH8, CAMK2G, EGR1, GCH1, G0S2, GPR84, IL8, NFKB1, PPARG, PTGS2 and TNF genes were quantified in neonatal and adult neutrophils (n = 8). Our data showed that basal levels of these gene expression were similar between preterm and term neonatal neutrophils whereas EGR1, G0S2, IL8, PTGS2 and TNF levels were significantly higher in adult neutrophils, compared with term (P < 0.05) and/or preterm (P < 0.01) neutrophils. All the investigated target genes were significantly LPS-regulated (P < 0.05; 0.25-65.30 fold) in term neutrophils. ATOH8, EGR1, G0S2, IL8, NFKB1, PPARG and TNF genes were significantly increased (P < 0.05; 0.18-35.22 fold), except that CAMK2G was significantly reduced by LPS in preterm neutrophils. ATOH8, GCH1, G0S2 and IL8 genes were significantly increased (P < 0.05; 4.97-15.76 fold) by LPS in adult neutrophils. LPS-stimulated expression levels of ATOH8, PTGS2, IL8 and G0S2 were significantly higher in adult neutrophils compared with term and/or preterm neutrophils (P < 0.05). There were also significant correlations between NR4A2 and NR4A3 and targeted genes (GCH, G0S2, NFKB, IL8, PPARG, PTGS2, GPR84, TNF, ATOH8) in neonatal and/or adult neutrophils. Conclusion: With these new findings, we proposed a regulatory network mediated by binding of LPS to TLR4/CD14 receptors, leading to transcription signals: NF-kB, PPARG, EGR1 which could upregulate or interlink with NR4A members and downstream functional genes of neutrophil activation, including pathways of inflammation (GPR84, PTGS2, NFKB1, IL8, TNF), nitric oxide (CAMK2G, ATOH8, GCH1) and cell death (G0S2). Comparison of NRA4 expressions and downstream signals in these different developmental windows demonstrated that the response of the NR4A gene family against bacterial infection, though demonstrable in preterm and term neutrophils, appeared to be compromised both at basal and inducible levels.

472413.label: Major findings and research outcome
472413.value: Major new findings: (a) We presented the first regulatory expression profiles of the orphan nuclear receptor NR4A subfamily members and downstream signals in human neutrophils from different developmental windows. We also demonstrated significantly lower expression at basal levels as well as post-stimulation by LPS in neonatal neutrophils, indicating possible compromised response to bacterial infections. (b) Our expressional and inhibitor studies revealed a regulatory network mediated by binding of LPS to TLR4/CD14 receptors, leading to transcription signals: NF-kB, PPARG, EGR1 which could upregulate or interlink with NR4A members and downstream functional genes of neutrophil activation, including those regulating inflammation (GPR84, PTGS2, NFKB1, IL8, TNF), nitric oxide regulation (CAMK2G, ATOH8, GCH1) and cell death (G0S2). (c) We proposed a regulatory network of gene expressions and functions in neonatal neutrophils upon challenge by Gram-negative bacterial component. Publications: (a) A manuscript entitled: “Expressional Profile of Neonatal Neutrophils and Role of Transcription Factor Nuclear Receptor NR4A Members in Response to Bacterial Lipopolysaccharide” was submitted to the Journal of Immunology for review and publication. (b) Presentation in Conference: The 57th American Society of Hematology: Annual Meeting and Exposition (5-8 Dec 2015; Orlando, USA) Gene Expressional Profile of Neonatal Neutrophils in Response to Bacterial Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and Possible Mechanism of Transcription Factor NR4A2 on the Immune Signal Cascade. (Poster no. 995).

472413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
472413.value: Infections caused by Gram-negative bacteria, such as E. Coli, Klebsiella sp. or Pseudomonas sp. are major causes of morbidity and mortality in newborns, especially in preterm infants. Due to the lack of adaptive immunity in early life, neonates primarily rely on the innate immune system to provide the first line of defense against invading pathogens. Neutrophils are the most abundant leukocytes and the earliest host responsive cells recruited to sites of bacterial infection. A comprehensive understanding of developmental regulations, signaling and functional deficiencies of neonatal neutrophils upon bacterial challenges is of paramount importance for development of prophylactic measures and intervention targets for these vulnerable infants. With the new information acquired from this study, we propose to further consolidate the regulatory network and functional implications in neonatal neutrophils regulated downstream of the NR4A family. 1. By lentiviral transduction approach, we could manipulate the expression of NR4A family and downstream genes in human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs, wiCell) differentiated neutrophil model. Loss of function would be investigated for each proposed genes except CAMK2G. Relevant functions would be studied in mature neutrophils with gene-knockout including cytokine release, neutrophil survival and chemotaxis. 2. Functional changes and downstream-proposed network can also be investigated in neutrophils isolated from NR4A knockout mice.

472413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
472413.value: Neutrophils are the major component of the host innate response at early life against bacterial infections. However, neonatal neutrophils are known to exhibit both quantitative and qualitative deficiencies, which compromise their antimicrobial and acute inflammatory functions. In this study, we investigated the regulatory pathways of the orphan nuclear receptor NR4A subfamily members and downstream signals in human neutrophils from different developmental windows. Targeted gene expressions in neutrophils from umbilical cord blood of term (>36 week gestation) and moderately preterm (32 – 36 weeks) infants as well as adult peripheral blood were quantified upon stimulation by bacterial liposaccharide (LPS). Our results demonstrated that baseline expressions of NR4A members were significantly lower in neonatal neutrophils compared with adult neutrophils. In spite of significant induction by LPS, their levels remained compromised in neonatal neutrophils. LPS-stimulated NR4A expressions were significantly inhibited by NFκB and p38MAPK inhibitors. Our overall findings suggested a regulatory network mediated by binding of LPS to TLR4 receptors, leading to transcription signals of NR4A members and downstream functional genes of neutrophil activation. A comprehensive understanding of developmental regulations of neonatal neutrophils upon bacterial challenges is of paramount importance for development of prophylactic measures and intervention targets for these vulnerable infants.

472513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
472513.value: The aim of this prospective study is to compare the prevalence of advanced adenomas and cancers in siblings of individuals with advanced adenomas compared with those of siblings of individuals without such lesions. Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the second most common cancer in Hong Kong. First-degree relatives of patients with CRC have a two-fold increased risk of colorectal neoplasms and colonoscopy screening is indicated in this high-risk group. However, there is a lack of prospective data on the risk estimates of colorectal neoplasms in relatives of subjects with adenomas. It is not clear when and how to screen an individual with a family history of adenomas. International guidelines recommend earlier and more regular colonoscopy screening of close relatives when there is a proband with an adenoma. However, this recommendation is based on limited evidence. In our CRC screening study, up to 25% of asymptomatic persons 50 years of age and above have at least one adenoma. Screening all close relatives of subjects with adenomas would require substantial manpower and health resources. Well-designed and adequately powered studies are needed to estimate the risk of colorectal neoplasms in individuals who have first-degree relatives with adenomas. We have recently shown that siblings of patients with CRC have a three-fold increased risk of colorectal neoplasms. We hypothesized that siblings of patients with advanced adenoma (adenomas at least 10mm in size, high grade dysplasia or villous histology) also have an increased risk of advanced adenomas compared with those without such family history. In this study, we intend to compare colonoscopy results in siblings of subjects with advanced adenomas to those of age- and sex-matched siblings of subjects with negative colonoscopies. The use of such a control group avoids biased estimates of the association with family history, and removes the acquired or environmental component to this association. Despite the high incidence of CRC in Hong Kong, the local health authority has not yet established a population based screening policy. The current study not only will quantify the risk of colorectal neoplasms, but also provide further evidence on whether, and when, screening should be offered to relatives of patients with advanced adenomas. This information is essential to formulate an effective CRC screening strategy in Hong Kong. Furthermore, it will provide important information to international guideline committees on screening strategies for subjects with family histories of adenomas. 此前瞻性研究的目的是比較兄弟姐妹羅患大腸癌癌前病變(癌前病變)與否，對個人患癌前病變或大腸癌病發率的影響。大腸癌是香港第二最常見癌症，大腸癌家族史增加大腸癌病變率達兩倍。高危群組應定期接受大腸鏡篩查。可惜醫學文獻缺乏針對癌前病變家族史的前瞻性研究。國際指引建議，有大腸腺瘤家族史人士應提早定期進行大腸鏡檢查，但沒有明確証實及指出撿查開展的時間與方法。跟據我們過往的腸癌篩查研究，五十歲以上健康人士有兩成半機會患有大腸腺瘤，如為大腸腺瘤患者家屬提供檢查，將需要大量人力及資源。因此我們應該就癌前病變家族史進行更精密及準確研究。 我們最近的研究發現兄弟姐妹羅患大腸癌人士患大腸癌變機會高出三倍。因此我們相信兄弟姐妹羅患大腸癌癌前病變(組織大於＋毫米之腺瘤, 發育異常或絨毛狀組織)亦癌前病變的風險因素。事次研究以年齡及性別配對癌前病變患者及健康人士之兄弟姐妹大腸鏡檢查結果，以健康人士作對比對象能減低家族遺傳，後天或環境相關影響。 雖然大腸癌在香港病發率高，但香港政府並沒有普及的大腸癌篩查計劃。此研究除了深入了解大腸癌變的因素，更為大腸癌癌前病變家屬的篩查需求及時間提供更多實証，此研究結果對本地及國際大腸癌篩查方針有著重要影響。

472513.label: Major findings and research outcome
472513.value: The prevalence of advanced neoplasia and serrated polyps (excluding small distal hyperplastic polyps) was 5.7% and 5.6%, respectively. 3.7% and 0.4% subjects had proximal and large (≥10 mm) serrated polyps, respectively. Independent predictors of synchronous advanced colorectal neoplasia were the presence of sessile serrated adenomas (OR: 4.52; 95% CI: 2.40–8.49), proximal serrated polyps (OR: 2.23, 95% CI: 1.38–3.60), large serrated polyps (OR: 59.25; 95% CI: 18.85–186.21), hyperplastic polyps (OR: 1.66; 95% CI: 1.03–2.67), three or more serrated polyps (OR: 4.86; 95% CI: 1.24–19.15) and one or more non-advanced tubular adenomas (OR: 3.58, 95% CI: 2.59–4.96). Detection of proximal, sessile and/or large serrated polyps at screening colonoscopy is independently associated with an increased risk for synchronous advanced neoplasia.

472513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
472513.value: The risk of colorectal cancer (CRC) in families of patients with CRC is well established, but it is less well defined for families of patients with adenomas. Previous studyies have demonstrated an increased of CRC in close relatives of patients with any adenoma or an advanced adenoma (AA). However, most of these studies were limited by the lack of a suitable comparison group. Therefore, we conducted a prospective, blinded, cross-sectional study to compare the prevalence of colorectal neoplasms in subjects who had a sibling with AA with that in subjects who had sibling with a normal colonoscopy. To better define the risk in siblings of patients with an AA, we chose siblings of subjects with normal colonoscopy as our controls. We included 200 siblings from 200 patients with AA (exposed siblings) and 400 siblings from 400 patients without AA (unexposed siblings) to analysis. We found that the prevalence of AA was six-fold higher in exposed siblings than unexposed siblings. Exposed siblings also had a higher prevalence of all colorectal adenomas and multiple adenomas. CRC was identified in 2 exposed siblings and none of the unexposed siblings. These data reinforce the need for screening in families when a patient has AA.

472613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
472613.value: In Hong Kong, colorectal cancer (CRC) has emerged as the second most common cancer and the second leading cause of cancer deaths. While surgery still remains the mainstay of curative treatment for CRC, most patients with advanced/metastatic disease will require chemotherapy (in particular oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy) as a palliative treatment to hopefully prolong survival. Unfortunately, a significant proportion of patients fail to respond to such treatment, and some may even experience worse outcomes as a result of drug-induced toxicities. It is therefore imperative to identify predictive markers that can help select those patients who may benefit from the chemotherapy. It is well known that epigenetic background of an individual can influence his/her response to anti-cancer therapy. Our preliminary in vitro data suggested that hsa-miR-133a (miR-133a), a novel tumor suppressive microRNA (miRNA), can sensitize CRC cells to chemotherapeutic drugs (including oxaliplatin) through increase of early apoptosis. Based on these results, we hypothesize that miR-133a is an important epigenetic regulator that modulates chemosensitivity. Restoration of miR-133a in vivo will enhance the therapeutic efficacy of oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy. Furthermore, we hypothesize that the expression levels of miR-133a in CRC are associated with clinical responses to oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy. In a series of studies using cellular and animal models, we plan to characterize the role and mechanism of miR-133a in the sensitization of CRC cells to oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy. In order to demonstrate the clinical relevance of these preclinical findings, we also plan to compare the expression levels of miR-133a in archival primary tumor/liver metastases tissues among metastatic CRC patients who responded to vs. those who did not respond to oxaliplatin treatment. The expected findings of these studies will provide new molecular insight into the mechanism of miR-133a chemosensitization effect on CRC, which may allow the development of new strategies to enhance the therapeutic efficacy of oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy. Furthermore, our studies may clarify the clinical potential of miR-133a as a predictive biomarker or ‘personalized medicine’ biomarker in selecting CRC patients for oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy, so that patients who will not benefit from the treatment can be spared from the drug toxicities and offered alternative treatments. 結直腸癌已經成為香港地區的第二大主要的新發癌症, 並且是導致癌症死亡的第二大原因。目前儘管手術切除依然是治療結直腸癌症的主要手段, 但是大多數局部晚期或轉移性結腸癌患者仍然需要依靠輔助化學治療（特別是基於奧沙利鉑的聯合化療）來預防復發及延長生命。但不幸的是,很大部分患者對此種化療手段不僅沒有產生良好應答,甚至還要承受隨之而來的藥物毒副作用。因此,尋找奧沙利鉑應答的分子預後標誌物可以説明制定合適的個體化治療方案。 表觀遺傳機制是導致抗癌藥物療效個體差異的一個重要因素。屬於表觀遺傳學範疇的微小RNA越來越獲得腫瘤研究的重視。我們的前期體外試驗顯示微小RNA分子hsa-miR-133a（miR-133a）是一個重要的結直腸腫瘤抑制分子。上調miR-133a可以增強結直腸癌細胞的早期凋亡,進而實現化學藥物（特別是奧沙利鉑）增敏的效果。基於上述發現,我們提出以下假設:miR-133a是一個增強奧沙利鉑化療敏感性的表觀遺傳調節因素。上調miR-133a可以增強奧沙利鉑輔助化療的療效。此外,我們推測結直腸癌患者腫瘤組織內的miR-133a可以作為奧沙利鉑輔助化療的預後標誌物。 通過利用一系列細胞和動物模型試驗,我們將研究miR-133a對奧沙利鉑化療增敏的分子機制。另一方面通過檢測標本庫內已有的臨床原位結直腸癌及其肝臟轉移癌組織的miR-133a表達量,我們將評估miR-133a與奧沙利鉑應答關係的臨床相關性。預期的試驗結果將有助於解釋miR-133a對奧沙利鉑的增敏機制,進而輔助制定增強奧沙利鉑藥物療效的新措施。此外闡述miR-133a作為奧沙利鉑治療轉移性結直腸癌的預後標誌物將有利於制定個體化治療方案,而且可以減輕無應答患者的痛苦和經濟負擔。

472613.label: Realisation of objectives
472613.value: Aim 1: To characterize the potential targets of miR-133a that confer chemosensitivity using 3’UTR binding assay, western blot, gene overexpression, and rescue assay. Experiment 1.1: In vitro evaluation of chemosensitization by miR-133a restoration To investigate the chemosensitization effect of miR-133a, we overexpressed miR-133a in 6 colorectal cancer (CRC) cell lines (HCT116, HCT116p53-/-, HT29, DLD1, RKO, and SW1116) and the 50% inhibitory concentration (IC50) of each cell lines was calculated by means of MTT assay. Restoration of miR-133a was sufficient to result in a 1.5 to 2.9 fold sensitization to oxaliplatin treatment in all the tested cell lines. Compared with the p53 mutant cell lines, the IC50 fold change was more prominent in HCT116 and RKO which have wild-type p53 background, suggesting that p53 status is one of the factors that influenced the sensitization effect of miR-133a. Experiment 1.2 Identification of the potential targets of miR-133a that confer chemosensitivity p53 status is associated with the cell responses to chemotherapeutic agents. Overexpression of miR-133a did not alter the mRNA expression of p53 but significantly increased the protein level of p53, indicating that miR-133a upregulated p53 protein through increasing its protein stability. It is reported that Ring finger and FYVE-like domain containing E3 ubiquitin protein ligase (RFFL) is a potential oncogene that targets p53 for degradation. Moreover, silencing of RFFL can sensitize cell responses to chemotherapeutic agents. RFFL contains an evolutionarily conserved binding site for miR-133a. To test whether RFFL is targeted by miR-133a in vitro, we attached the predicted RFFL 3’UTR binding site, as well as its mutant form to firefly luciferase reporter gene, respectively. miR-133a repressed wild-type RFFL-3’UTR reporter activity for about 49% compared with the control group (P <0.01). On the other hand, miR-133a had no inhibition effect on the mutant RFFL-3’UTR reporter activity, indicting the direct regulation of miR-133a in the 3’UTR of RFFL mRNA. Ectopic expression of miR-133a remarkably reduced RFFL protein expression for 35%, 55%, and 40% of the control group in the three cell lines, suggesting that RFFL is a bona fide target of miR-133a. To further characterize the chemosensitizing property of miR-133a to oxaliplatin treatment, we searched for new miR-133a targets that regulated the pharmacokinetics of oxaliplatin. Previous studies indicated that ATPase Cu++ transporting beta polypeptide (ATP7B), ATP-binding cassette sub-family C member 1 (ABCC1), and γ-glutamylcysteine ligase (GCLC) regulated platinum-based drugs efflux and detoxification. Notably, ATP7B, ABCC1, and GCLC contain evolutionarily conserved binding sites for miR-133a. Overexpression of miR-133a significantly suppressed the mRNA of ATP7B, ABCC1 and GCLC in two CRC cell lines: HCT116 (p53 wild type) and DLD1 (p53 mutant), indicating that the three genes could also be potential targets that contribute to the chemosensitizing property of miR-133a. Furthermore, we attached their predicted 3’UTR binding sites, as well as their mutant form to firefly luciferase reporter gene, respectively. miR-133a repressed wild-type ATP7B, ABCC1, and GCLC-3’UTR reporter activity for about 64%, 56%, and 42%, respectively (P <0.05). On the other hand, miR-133a had no inhibition effect on the mutant ATP7B, ABCC1, and GCLC-3’UTR reporter activity, indicting the direct regulation of miR-133a in the 3’UTR of ATP7B, ABCC1, and GCLC mRNA. Experiment 1.3: Effects of RFFL silencing and overexpression on chemosensitization To validate the effect of RFFL on p53 expression in colon cancer, RFFL was transiently transfected in HCT116. Overexpression of RFFL in HCT116 significantly suppressed p53 protein expression. Silencing of RFFL induced p53 and its downstream target p21 protein expression, and caused 5% increase in G0/G1 phase arrest. Moreover, RFFL-depleted cells exhibited impaired cell growth compared to control cells as revealed by MTT assay and colony formation assay. The colonies formed by RFFL knock-down in HCT116 cells were fewer than those in the control cells (P <0.05). We also found that knock-down of RFFL in HT29 (p53 mutant) could also inhibit cell growth, indicating that RFFL has a potential oncogenic function in CRC through a p53-independent manner. On the other hand, we performed the rescue experiment and found that overexpression of RFFL cDNA in HCT116 could not suppress the effect of miR-133a. Aim 2: To determine the in vivo biologic activity of miR-133a as a positive modulator for oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy using miRNA overexpression techniques and xenograft models. Experiment 2.1: In vivo evaluation of chemosensitization by miR-133a restoration Our in vivo study suggested that overexpression of miR-133a in HCT116 significantly suppressed the tumor growth in nude mice compared to the control group (P <0.01), supporting that miR-133a inhibited colon cancer growth in vivo. We further checked the miR-133a expression levels in the xenografts. The amounts of miR-133a were approximately 102-fold higher in miR-133a stable cell line than those in the control cell line group at the beginning (day 4). No significant miR-133a reduction was observed at the end of the experiment (day 34), suggesting the miR-133a expression was stable during the in vivo study period. We therefore used this model to evaluate the chemosensitization by miR-133a restoration. Nude mice have been inoculated with miR-133a overexpression cell line or control cell line. Mice was treated with oxaliplatin (15 mg/kg body weight iv) or vehicle. However miR-133a showed no significant sensitization effect in this single in vivo experiment. Factors such as drug administration time, dosage, and small sample size of the xenografts animals should be considered in future experiments. Aim 3: To investigate the association between miR-133a expression levels and the clinical responses to oxaliplatin treatment using quantitative PCR assay and statistical analysis. Experiment 3.1: Investigation of the association between miR-133a expression levels in tumor specimens from metastatic CRC patients and their outcomes to oxaliplatin treatment. We evaluated miR-133a expression level in 42 pairs paraffin blocks of tumor and adjacent normal tissues from stage IV CRC patients who had received oxaliplatin-based treatment at the Department of Clinical Oncology, Prince of Wales Hospital. miR-133a level showed no significant correlation with clinicopathologic features such as age, gender, primary cancer site (colon or rectum), and metastasis site, but was marginally associated with oxaliplatin treatment response (P = 0.052). In consistence with our previous data, miR-133a was significant reduced in tumor tissues compared with adjacent normal tissue (P <0.001). We next stratified the CRC patients into two groups based on their oxaliplatin treatment response (good response and poor response), according to the RECIST guideline. Although miR-133a showed a comparable level in normal tissues of both groups, miR-133a was demonstrated to be significantly lower in the tumor tissues from patients with poor response to oxaliplatin treatment compared with those with good response (P <0.05). The area under the ROC curve (AUC) value for miR-133a was 0.727 for prediction of oxaliplatin treatment outcomes. At a cut-off of 0.0373, miR-133a showed a relatively high specificity (79.3%) and the sensitivity was 50%. Moreover, low miR-133a expression was associated with an increased risk of cancer-related death by univariate Cox regression (relative risk [RR] 4.18, 95% CI 1.42 to 12.3, P = 0.010). After adjustment for potential confounding factors, low miR-133a level was found to be an independent risk factor for shortened overall survival in patients with stage IV CRC by multivariate Cox regression analysis (RR 4.35, 95% CI 1.46 to 12.8, P = 0.008). Kaplan-Meier survival curves showed that stage IV CRC patients with low miR-133a expression had significantly poorer overall survival based on the log rank test (P <0.01).

472613.label: Major findings and research outcome
472613.value: miR-133a expression level was significantly lower in the tumor tissues from patients with poor response to oxaliplatin than in those with good response (P <0.05). The area under the ROC curve value for miR-133a was 0.727 for prediction of oxaliplatin treatment outcomes. At a cut-off of 0.0373, miR-133a showed a relatively high specificity (79.3%) and the sensitivity was 50%. miR-133a level was marginally associated with oxaliplatin treatment response (P = 0.052). Low miR-133a expression was associated with an increased risk of cancer-related death by univariate Cox regression. After adjustment for potential confounding factors, low miR-133a level was found to be an independent risk factor for shortened overall survival in patients with stage IV CRC by multivariate Cox regression analysis (RR 4.35, 95% CI 1.46 to 12.8, P = 0.008). Kaplan-Meier survival curves showed that stage IV CRC patients with low miR-133a expression had significantly poorer overall survival based on the log rank test (P <0.01). The biologic function of miR-133a was further studied in CRC cell lines. Restoration of miR-133a was sufficient to result in a 1.5 to 2.9 fold sensitization to oxaliplatin treatment in HCT116, HCT116p53-/-, HT29, DLD1, RKO, and SW1116. The 50% inhibitory concentration (IC50) fold change was more prominent in CRC cells with wild-type p53 background. We next found that overexpression of miR-133a significantly upregulated p53 protein level but not mRNA level. Using luciferase reporter assay and Western blot, we found that miR-133a directly suppressed the oncogene ring finger and FYVE-like domain containing 1 (RFFL), a p53 E3 ubiquitin ligase, and upregulated p53 protein through increasing its protein stability. This could partially explain why the sensitization effect of miR-133a was more prominent in p53 wild type cell line. To further characterize the chemosensitizing property of miR-133a to oxaliplatin, we used target scan algorithms to identify that ATP7B, ABCC1, and GCLC, which regulated platinum-based drugs efflux and detoxification, were potential targets of miR-133a. Overexpression of miR-133a significantly suppressed the mRNA of ATP7B, ABCC1 and GCLC in two CRC cell lines: HCT116 (p53 wild type) and DLD1 (p53 mutant). We further observed that miR-133a significantly repressed ATP7B, ABCC1, and GCLC 3’UTR reporter activity, indicating that the three genes could also be potential targets that contribute to the chemosensitizing property of miR-133a. In conclusion, miR-133a was an independent predictive biomarker for stage IV CRC patient who received oxaliplatin therapy.

472613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
472613.value: In this study, we enrolled 42 stage IV CRC patients and studied the association between miR-133a level and oxaliplatin treatment outcomes. Our current data suggested that miR-133a in CRC cancer tissues was a promising biomarker for predicting stage IV CRC patients’ response to oxaliplatin-based treatments. Low miR-133a level was an independent risk factor for shortened overall survival in stage IV CRC patients by multivariate Cox regression analysis. miR-133a showed a relatively high specificity level (79.3%) and the sensitivity was 50%. Limitations of the current study include its retrospective nature and the limited number of clinical samples available for analysis. A larger prospective study with more clinical samples should be conducted to validate our study findings. In addition, more studies in different populations to validate miR-133a as a predictive biomarker for oxaliplatin treatment are required before it can be applied clinically. Finally, further studies to provide a direct comparison between miR-133a and other reported oxaliplatin treatment predictive biomarkers such as KRAS mutational status, ERCC1 expression, XPD polymorphism, should be conducted to confirm the advantages of miR-133a in prediction of oxaliplatin treatment response.

472613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
472613.value: Oxaliplatin, a platinum-containing antineoplastic agent that prevents transcription of DNA by crosslinking DNA strands, is commonly used in the treatment of colorectal cancer (CRC) in both adjuvant and metastatic setting. However, a proportion of patients may either fail to respond to oxaliplatin or subsequently develop resistance. Therefore stratification approaches are required to help select those patients who may benefit from this treatment and to avoid potential complications such as peripheral neuropathy. In this study, we have identified a significant correlation between miR-133a expression level in CRC cancer tissues and the treatment outcome among CRC patients who received oxaliplatin. Low level of miR-133a in tumor tissues is associated with poor response to oxaliplatin and poor overall survival. Subsequent experiments confirmed that miR-133a restoration could sensitize CRC cell lines to oxaliplatin in vitro. We also obtained insights into the intracellular signaling pathways regulated by miR-133a that contributed to its chemosensitization effect. In conclusion, our data suggested the potential use of miR-133a as a biomarker for predicting CRC patients’ response to oxaliplatin-based treatments.

472913.label: Realisation of objectives
472913.value: Objective 1. To generate oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs) from bone marrow pluripotent stem cells derived neurosphere. As the bone marrow pluripotent stem cells are differentiated from mesoderm, and oligodendrocyte progenitor cells from ectoderm, it is difficult to generate oligodendrocyte progenitor cells from bone marrow derived stem cells. We spent the first 18 months of this project in attempting to generate OPCs from bone marrow pluripotent stem cells. This has failed. We change strategy by establishing the immortalized human neural stem cells with Bmi-1 and TERT gene. These immortalized human neural stem cells are then differentiated to OPCs which are Olig2 and PDGFa positive. This strategy allows the generation of adequate number of OPCs for their characterization and experimental treatment of murine ICH. Objective 2. To measure the functional/histological outcomes of ICH model after transplanting OPCs into experimental ICH mice and bio-behaviors of grafting OPCs in brain. We established murine ICH model with collagenase, and transplanted the induced OPCs into the striatal ICH on the 7th day after the experimental ICH. OPCs transplantation does improve the locomotor function of ICH mouse as assessed by Catwalk gait analysis. Histological examination demonstrates that OPCs transplantation can promote the neurofilament expression of in striatum (NL-L). These results strongly suggest that OPCs treatment of murine ICH does promote a significant improvement of its locomotor function. Objective 3. To clarify whether the transplanted OPCs promotes the axon regeneration through modulating the glial scar and stimulating remyelination after ICH. To explore the molecular mechanism regulated by OPCs in the murine ICH model, we screened several microRNAs enriched in OPCs compared with NSCs by microRNA array, including miR-R27a, miR-15a, miR-30a, and miR-34a. These microRNAs may take part in the regulation OPCs differentiation in the brain. Meanwhile, we detected the expression of axon markers in the corticospinal tract of the mice by Western blot, and found that the transplanted OPCs can increase the expression of NF-L and MAP2, but had no effects on NF-M. We also stained the murine corticospinal tract with olig2, MBP and NF-L antibodies, and O4 antibody in the striatum, and found that OPCs increased the expression of NF-L, but showing no effects on other markers. It explained the mechanism of OPCs treatment of murine ICH that OPCs improve the locomotor function of ICH mice by promoting axon regeneration.

472913.label: Major findings and research outcome
472913.value: We established a protocol to immortalize neural stem cells and differentiated the neural stem cells to oligodendrocyte progenitor cells. The induced OPCs are olig2 and PDGF positive by IF. We also screened microRNAs enriched OPCs compared with neural stem cells with microRNA array, and found that miR-R27a, miR-15a, miR-30a, miR-34a are significantly highly expressed in OPCs. It is worth to explore the detail mechanism of regulation by microRNAs during OPCs differentiation. Then we transplanted OPCs into ICH mouse model, and assessed the motor function recovery by Catwalk gait system. We found that OPCs transplantation can significantly improve the motor function of mouse ICH in parameters of stand time, step cycle, swing time, and swing speed. For the mechanism exploration, we detected several neuron markers such as NF-L, NF-M, and MAP2 by Western blot, and found that the expression of NF-L and MAP2 are increased by OPCs transplantation. The immunostaining results indicated that OPCs transplantation can increase axon regeneration. We are preparing a manuscript on the major findings from this project and planning to submit to BMC Neurology for publication.

472913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
472913.value: As we have screened several microRNAs enriched in neurons, we can explore the detail mechanism and function of microRNAs in regulation of OPCs differentiation in future work. OPCs can differentiate to oligodendrocytes which form myelin to protect the electricity transmission for axon, but the source of OPCs is a limitation for the clinical therapy. In 2006, Yamanaka established a system to reprogramme the fibroblast cells to induced pluripotent stem (IPS) cells (Takahashi and Yamanaka, 2006; Takahashi et al., 2007), it is a new thought for getting OPCs. The further development of the research is to generate large numbers of OPCs from IPS which are reprogrammed from the fibroblast cells or other source cells. As most of IPS is generated with virus, so far, it is not safe to apply in clinical and is still in laboratory stage. For the course of action, we can collect the murine fibroblast cells and culture for adequate number of cells, then transfect with the four Yamanaka factors by lentiviruses, followed by culturing with embryonic stem cell medium. When the IPS are available for differentiating into the IPS into OPCs with adequate number, cell therapy for ICH model can then be further assessed for efficiency.

472913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
472913.value: In this research project, we have established the immortalized human neural stem cells with two oncogenes (Bmi-1 and TERT), for their differentiation from neural stem cells [NSCs] into oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs). We have also screened several novel microRNAs enriched in OPCs with microRNA array. Furthermore, the induced OPCs transplanted into the murine striatal ICH result in motor function improvement and increased axonal and myelin marker expression, suggestive of axon regeneration in the striatum (source of brain damage) and the descending long tract, the corticospinal tract in the medulla oblongata. The value of the research is that we have demonstrated motor function recovery by transplanting OPCs into the brain-damaged striatum, and in vivo, molecular evidence of axon regeneration. When an improved source of induced OPCs is available, this can be a new direction for cell therapy for ICH.

473013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
473013.value: 隨著全球老齡化，骨骼肌肉系統的健康（如骨質疏鬆）備受關注。預防骨質疏鬆是避免骨質疏鬆（尤其是婦女絕經後骨質疏鬆）骨折的關鍵。荷爾蒙替代療法（HRT）是預防絕經後骨質疏鬆骨丟失的一線療法。然而，長期使用HRT會增加乳腺癌和心血管疾病的發生風險。在香港和中國內地，複方中藥是防治骨質疏鬆及相關骨疾病的常用療法。在抗骨質疏鬆的眾多中藥中，富含生物活性植物雌激素的淫羊藿使用頻率最高，其治療效果在臨床前和臨床研究中均已得到驗證。 我們最近的多中心臨床試驗確證了以淫羊藿為主藥的複方仙靈骨葆膠囊治療骨質疏鬆的有效性和安全性，同時還發現了“劑量不依賴性”：高劑量組（每天12粒膠囊）與低劑量組（每天6粒膠囊，也是常規的臨床使用劑量）相比，並未產生預期的更好的治療效果。類似的現象也出現在PTH的臨床試驗中。我們最新的實驗研究為這種“劑量不依賴性”提供了線索：增加淫羊藿黃酮的給藥劑量並不能增加其活性代謝產物淫羊藿素的濃度。其原因是淫羊藿黃酮類化合物在血液中停留的時間短，迅速分佈至肝臟，後經“肝-膽-腸循環”返回小腸，被排出體外，致使其生物利用度低。我們的最新研究也揭示了淫羊藿素預防骨丟失的潛在作用機理：通過Wnt/beta-catenin和BMP信號通路促進骨髓基質乾細胞（BMSC）的成骨分化，並且通過Wnt/beta-catenin和PPARγ信號通路抑制BMSC的成脂分化。可見，提高淫羊藿黃酮治療骨質疏鬆效能的關鍵是維持淫羊藿素在血液及骨形成表面的濃度。我們的多學科團隊研發了一種新的生物技術能夠增加淫羊藿素的骨形成效能：1）增加在血液循環中的保留時間，2）使淫羊藿素靶向至骨形成表面。我們採用脂質體延長淫羊藿素在血液中的停留時間，並採用一種新型的遞送系統，6個連續的天冬氨酸-絲氨酸-絲氨酸序列（DSS6）-脂質體（自然-醫學，參考文獻45）將其靶向至骨形成表面以增強其促骨形成的效能。綜上形成我們的研究假設：新型可注射的淫羊藿素骨靶向脂質體可延長淫羊藿素在血液中的停留時間，並且增加其在骨形成表面的濃度，通過促進骨髓基質乾細胞的成骨分化抑制其成脂分化，從而增強預防骨質疏鬆的效能。 當前研究為複方中藥的臨床研究提供了科學依據，更總要的，為循證醫學及中藥現代化的進一步發展開拓新途徑。如可證實新型可注射淫羊藿素骨靶向遞送系統能有效防治骨質疏鬆，則為開發新一代“減量增效”的中藥提供堅定的基礎。我們的研究還將為節約中藥資源及中藥防治骨質疏鬆的臨床應用的可持續發展提供新策略。

473013.label: Realisation of objectives
473013.value: Up to the completion of this final report, we have finished all the in vivo and in vitro experiments. All the objectives listed in the proposal have been well achieved. To achieve the first objective (To investigate pharmacokinetics and tissues distribution of bone-forming and fat-suppression phytomolecules icaritin in the successfully developed injectable bone targeting delivery system), firstly we developed an injectable bone-targeting delivery system carrying osteopromotive molecules icaritin, then the fluorescence-labeled targeting delivery system was injected in mice and detected by the non-invasive detector IVIS. The results showed that the fluorescence signals were accumulated more condensed in bone tissue than in other tissues, and the signals in bone tissue of the targeting delivery system group was stronger and more lasting than the ones in non-targeting delivery system group. Meanwhile, we also injected the gold particles-labeled targeting delivery system into mice and traced the location on the gold particles by scanning electronic microscopy (SEM). The images of SEM have proved that the labeled targeting delivery system could deliver the content successfully to bony tissue. This double confirmed the efficiency and efficacy of the targeting delivery system in delivery the contents. To achieve the second objective (To evaluate the efficacy and safety of this novel bone targeting delivery system on prevention of estrogen depletion-induced osteoporosis in OVX mice), a series of animal experiments were performed. Firstly, we have developed the estrogen depletion induced osteoporotic mice model by processing ovariectomy (OVX) surgery on the female mice. Then the mice were divided into several groups and given different treatments including intravenous injection of targeting delivery system with icaritin. After 6 weeks of treatments, various ex vivo analysis was performed to evaluate the efficacy and efficiency of the novel targeting delivery system with icaritin in prevention of osteoporosis in OVX mice, including micro-CT scanning, mechanical tests, histomorphometry analysis, and biomarkers level etc. Results of the assessments showed that the novel targeting delivery system with the phytomolecules icaritin could effectively and efficiently maintain bone quality in both bone mass and microarchitecture, especially in the trabecular bone, by enhancing bone formation and suppressing bone resorption and adipocytes formation. To achieve the third objective (To investigate the ex-vivo underlying mechanisms associated with enhancement of bone formation and inhibition of bone marrow fat formation, an important niche of bone marrow MSCs in developing anti-osteoporosis agents), we performed cell culture of BMSCs, preosteoblasts and preadipocytes, and then process osteogenic induction or adipogenic induction respectively. mRNA and protein expression level of different markers were assessed. Our in vitro results suggested that icaritin did not work through either estrogen receptor directly or the conventional β-catenin signaling pathway, but was able to inactive GSK-3β by phosphorylating its Ser9 site regulated by increasing phosphorylation of AKT, which led to nuclear translocation of β-catenin and thus initiate osteogenesis and suppress the expression of PPARγ and C/EBP, which are key adipogenic markers.

473013.label: Major findings and research outcome
473013.value: In our study, we have proved the efficacy and efficiency of the novel targeting delivery system with icaritin in prevention of estrogen depletion induced osteoporosis in mice OVX model. More importantly, we also investigated the mechanism of icaritin in inhibiting adipogenesis and promoting osteogenesis of bone mesenchymal stem cells through regulating β-catenin signaling pathway by phosphorylation of upstream proteins, Akt and GSK-3β. The major funding has been composed as manuscript and submitted to journal ACS NANO, and now is under review. For detail information, please refer to the journal publications list in Part C. In the project, we have established collaboration with leading international universities and/or professors in this field, such as Professor Yang Zhijun in Baptist University, Professor Yao Xinsheng in Jinan University, Professor Zhou Hong in the University of Sydney and Professor Long Fanxin in Washington University etc. Also, there are several publications raised directly from this funding. Two of them have already been published, one is under review by the Journal ACS NANO and two manuscripts are under preparation. For detail information, please refer to Part C. Moreover, several papers related to this research project were delivered at many international conferences, including ORS in the US and international conferences in Hong Kong and Mainland China, highlighting that two of them were received awards (the Best Paper Awards and the Young Scientist Awards). For detail information, please refer to Part C. Finally, one PhD candidate has been trained, with the thesis under preparation for submission.

473013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
473013.value: We are aiming to develop a novel targeting delivery system with the osteopromotive phytomolecule icaritin as an alternative therapeutic strategy for osteoporosis prevention. In the current stage, we have finished the animal experiments part and proved that the targeting delivery system could improve the efficiency and efficacy of icaritin in the estrogen depletion-induced osteoporosis prevention. Since the mechanism of osteoporosis due to aging is different to osteoporosis result from estrogen depletion, whether the targeting delivery system with icaritin could still work well in aging that would be subject to future studies. If icaritin has synergistic effects with growth factors, compounds or even bone matrix minerals in the musculoskeletal system, it remains for future research as well. In the current study, we just proved that icaritin could prevent bone loss through regulating β-catenin signaling pathway by the process of phosphorylation of the β-catenin related protein Akt and GSK-3β, other elements or even other pathways may also be affected by icaritin. It is reported that icaritin also can inhibit cellular senescence pathways and therefore icaritin was assumed to be a potential candidate for senescence inhibitor. Whether this is related to bone diseases it could also be a future study direction.

473013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
473013.value: When population is getting aging, one of the major challenging health issues is osteoporosis, which means the bones are getting fragile and easy to be broken. Osteoporosis is a degenerative bone disease with slow progress, and the symptoms are too mild to be diagnosed in the early stage. However, the fragile fractures resulted from osteoporosis is associated with severe high mortality and mobility, which may also affect the quality of life severely. Since osteoporosis is a degenerative bone disease and hard to be reversed and therefore prevention is essential. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) has been widely used in China, especially south part of China, for over hundreds of years and still remains popular in our health care system. In our study, we extracted a phytomolecule icaritin from the medical herbal Epimedium which is used as the major ingredient in most of the prescriptions for treating bone diseases. The developed icaritin carrying bone targeting delivery system has been developed as a novel TCM targeting injection to modify the administration of TCM and improve its efficiency and efficacy. Our current study provides solid evidence that the novel TCM injections can help to prevent bone loss in preclinical animal models, which can be the cornerstone for further clinical application.

473713.label: Realisation of objectives
473713.value: This study was undertaken to genome-wide identification and characterization of functional long noncoding RNAs in skeletal muscle stem cells using integrated high-throughput sequencing and regulatory network analysis. In the original grant proposal, we hypothesized that functional long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) could be regulated by transcription factors (TFs), miRNAs, and form the integrated gene regulatory networks to exert their functions. Therefore, the functional lncRNAs can be computationally predicted through gene network analysis. To test the above hypothesis, we propose to conduct three aims and are pleased to report that all three aims have been successfully completed. Aim 1: To identify interplays among lncRNAs, YY1 and miRNAs in myogenesis Details have been included in the mid-term report. Aim 2: To construct lncRNA involved regulatory network and identify functional lncRNA through regulatory network analysis To fulfill this aim, we proposed lncFunNet, a computational framework by systematically exploring gene network established by utilizing high-throughput sequencing data and implemented three key consecutive modules for this framework: (i) network integration; (ii) lncRNA functional prediction and prioritization; and (iii) lncRNA functional annotation. In network integration module, we identified TF-gene interactome through chromatin immunoprecipitation with massively parallel DNA sequencing (ChIP-seq) data analysis, established miRNA-gene interactome through CLIP-Seq data analysis, and constructed gene-gene interactions through co-expression gene analysis. In lncRNA functional prediction and prioritization module, we first proposed the scoring system to evaluate the functional importance of the identified lncRNAs using Functional Information Score (FIS) and used randomized network for FIS cutoff calculation. In lncRNA functional annotation module, we adopted the approaches that associate the function of a lncRNA with its directly connected genes with known functions. We also used the KEGG pathway information for the functional annotation. Further investigation on the identified lncRNAs shows that LncFunNet identifies known functional lncRNAs in mESCs as we expected. In addition, LncFunNet uncovers novel functional lncRNAs in skeletal muscle cells; and functional lncRNAs in muscle stem cells are key motif components of integrative gene networks. Aim 3: To experimentally validate the identified interplays and characterize lncRNA functions in myogenesis. The ultimate approach for testing the accuracy of our results is to experimentally validate the functionality of the identified lncRNAs and the associated interactions. To this end, we selected 10 predicted functional lncRNAs in both proliferating myoblasts (MBs) and differentiating myotubes (MTs) muscle cells with two criteria: (i) comparatively higher FIS; and (ii) the ability to form interactions with miRNAs because miRNA binding appears to confer a higher FIS. First, we confirmed their expression profiles. All 10 of the selected lncRNAs were readily detected by quantitative qRT-PCR during muscle cell differentiation. Some were highly induced during differentiation whereas others were repressed. The differential expression dynamics of these lncRNAs indicate their diverse roles in myogenesis, for example, the lncRNAs with increasing expression during differentiation may play a promoting role in the process. Indeed, when 5 of such lncRNAs were knocked down by a siRNA oligo, C2C12 differentiation was inhibited as assessed by a Myogenin luciferase reporter assay (see attached NAR 2017 paper Fig. 6). To further validate the involvement of functional lncRNAs in three-node network motifs and their interactions, we selected Snhg1 (small nucleolar RNA host gene 1) for further experimentation. It has been reported to promote cell proliferation in non-small cell lung cancer and hepatocellular carcinoma tumorigenesis but with unexplored function in skeletal myogenesis. By our prediction, Snhg1 interacts with YY1 and miR-200b through direct binding with them to form a type I three-node FFL network motif. An YY1 binding site was identified upstream of Snhg1 TSS (6.5 kb upstream of TSS) by analyzing YY1 ChIP-seq; an Ago2 binding peak was found and four binding sites for miR-200b were predicted. Indeed, by ChIP-PCR, an enrichment of YY1 on Snhg1 promoter was detected. Furthermore, overexpression of YY1 in C2C12 increased its expression while knockdown of YY1 repressed it, suggesting YY1 binding to Snhg1 causes the increase of its transcription. This was further confirmed by cloning a 250bp fragment of Snhg1 promoter encompassing the YY1 binding site into a luciferase reporter; results from the reporter assay showed that YY1 positively regulates Snhg1 expression. To dissect miR-200b-Snhg1 regulation, as expected, overexpression of miR-200b inhibited Snhg1 expression. To further demonstrate the possibility of post-transcriptional degradation by miR-200b through direct binding, we selected the predicted binding site that resides within the Snhg1 exon 10. A 240 bp fragment encompassing the site was fused with luciferase gene; when transfected into C2C12 cells with miR-200b mimic oligos, a significant decrease of the reporter activity was observed. These experimental evidences demonstrate that Snhg1, a pro-myogenic lncRNA, is regulated by YY1 and miR-200b (see attached NAR 2017 paper Fig. 7). To strengthen the findings, we further tested another lncRNA, 9530072K05Rik which was predicted to form type I network motif by interacting with MyoD and miR-29b through direct binding. Interestingly, MyoD binding on its promoter (350 bp upstream of TSS) was found to suppress its expression; miR-29b was also found to decrease its level through binding to the 3’ end of 9530072K05Rik. Altogether these results strengthened the reliability of our network approach in inferring the lncRNA functional mechanisms. It also demonstrated the previously underappreciated complexity of interactions that lncRNAs are involved in through binding with TFs and miRNAs during the process of myogenic differentiation.

473713.label: Major findings and research outcome
473713.value: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) are key regulators of diverse cellular processes. Recent advances in high-throughput sequencing have allowed for an un-precedented discovery of novel lncRNAs. To identify functional lncRNAs from thousands of candidates for further functional validation is still a challenging task. In the original proposal, we hypothesize that functional lncRNAs are key nodes in the gene regulatory networks and their functional importance can be evaluated computationally by the integrative network analysis. To test this hypothesis three specific aims/objectives are proposed. We have now completed all the proposed work and presented a novel computational framework, lncFunNet (lncRNA Functional inference through integrated Network) that integrates ChIP-seq, CLIP-seq and RNA-seq data to predict, prioritize and annotate lncRNA functions. A paper including all the major findings “LncFunNet: an integrated computational framework for identiﬁcation of functional long noncoding RNAs in mouse skeletal muscle cells” has been published on Nucleic Acids Research (2017) (Part C8). In this paper, we first demonstrated, in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs), using lncFunNet we not only recovered most of the functional lncRNAs known to maintain mESC pluripotency but also predicted a plethora of novel functional lncRNAs. Furthermore, in mouse myoblast C2C12 cells, applying lncFunNet led to prediction of reservoirs of functional lncRNAs in both proliferating myoblasts (MBs) and differentiating myotubes (MTs). Further analyses demonstrated that these lncRNAs are frequently bound by key transcription factors, interact with miRNAs and constitute key nodes in biological network motifs. We have also conducted the experiments to validate their dynamic expression proﬁles and functionality during myoblast differentiation. Collectively, our studies demonstrate the use of lncFunNet to annotate and identify functional lncRNAs in a given biological system. The implementation of the lncFunNet framework has also been submitted as an application note to the journal of Bioinformatics (Part C8). In addition, a total of 6 publications (5 published, 1 under review) have been generated with this funding acknowledged (Part C8). Our findings were highly received when presented in international and local conferences/seminars (Part C9). Four Ph.D. students and one MPhil student were trained under the grant (PartC 10). Through this work, we have also developed active collaboration with scientists from China, Prof. Miguel Esteban and Prof. Ralf Jauch (Part C11).

473713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
473713.value: Research from our study has provided a fast and accurate platform for functional lncRNA screening. It not only increases our knowledge in the field of lncRNAs, but also enhances our understanding of molecular regulation in skeletal muscle stem cells. This may eventually lead to the identification of novel therapeutic targets for muscle relevant disease such as muscular dystrophy and Rhabdomyosarcoma. In the future, to further these findings, we plan to continue the investigation of lncRNAs in the muscle cells. (1) The research will be expanded beyond the myoblast differentiation to include the entire lineage progression of muscle stem cell during regeneration. (2) To further examine the interplay between lncRNAs and transcription factors in myogenesis using genome-wide epigenetic sequencing data.

473713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
473713.value: Recently, long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs, non-coding RNAs >200nt in length) are emerging as potent regulators of gene expression. Deregulation of lncRNA function has been associated with human diseases. Myogenesis, or formation of skeletal muscle, is a process driven by the activation and differentiation of muscle stem cells. Complex regulatory networks involving transcription factors (TFs) and microRNAs are critical for myogenesis. However, it is largely unknown the functional roles of lncRNAs in these networks. In this study, we attempt to investigate the involvement of lncRNAs in myogenic regulation and try to computationally predict and functional annotate lncRNAs at the genome-wide level through a combination of high throughput sequencing tools and computational network analysis. The significance of our study is multi-folds: (i) It is the first genome-wide study to reveal the interplays between miRNA-lncRNA and TF-lncRNA in myogenesis; (ii) Findings revealed lncRNAs as important components of gene regulatory network thus enhance our understanding of gene regulation in muscle, which may eventually contribute to the understanding of etiology behind muscle related diseases; (iii) Through this investigation, we have developed a computational framework that integrates high-throughput sequencing data with regulatory network analysis to predict and prioritize functional lncRNAs.

474313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
474313.value: Pentatricopeptide repeat (PPR) proteins are a class of proteins that have loosely conserved 35-amino-acid repeats in tandem, and are prevalent in land plants. They are implicated in RNA processing mostly in mitochondria and plastids. However, due to its large family size, functions and their ligands of many PPRs are unknown. We have cloned a PPR gene which affects seed development in maize. The goal of this research is to determine the function of this unknown PPR protein, test its potential application value in transgenic plants, and attempt to identify its interacting proteins. The results are expected to advance our understanding of the mechanism by which this PPR protein affects seed development. This PPR gene was isolated via analysis of a small kernel mutant (smk11) in maize. The smk11 mutant is a recessive mutation, producing seeds about half of the wildtype size and weight. Cloning of Smk11 by transposon tagging indicates that it encodes an E subclass of PPR protein, named PPR179. PPR179 is targeted to mitochondria. Based on existing knowledge, most PPR proteins have functions in one of the four processes, RNA editing, splicing, maturation, and translation activation. All the editing functions reported so far are associated with either PPR-DYW or PPR-E type proteins. Hence, our primary objective is to test whether PPR179 functions on RNA editing. This will be achieved by mitochondrial RNA deep-sequencing and comparison between the smk11 mutant and the wildtype. The affinity and specificity of PPR179 binding to specific RNAs will be confirmed by RNA Co-IP analysis. Secondly, latest evidence suggests that the DYW motif in PPR-DYW proteins is still likely the deaminase, which catalyzes the C-to-U editing reaction. But how a PPR-E protein recruits its deaminase remains a question. We hypothesize that it exerts its editing function by associating with an either an unknown deaminase or a PPR-DYW protein. Either way, we will use Co-IP and yeast two hybrid analyses to identify the interacting proteins. Last, considering mutation in PPR179 causes small seeds, we are interested in testing the impact on seed formation (size and weight, etc) in transgenic plants that over-expresses PPR179. Because of its large naked seeds, rich genetic resources and increasing tools, maize has been a powerful model system for functional genomics on seed development in grain crops. As a major cereal crop itself, potential application of valued genes can be directly applied to other cereal crops. 474313.label: Realisation of objectives
474313.value: We carried out the extensive experiments and key results are summarized below. Pentatricopeptide repeat (PPR) proteins have functions in one of the four processes, RNA editing, splicing, maturation, and translation activation. We identified a critical RNA editing factor of mitochondrial nad7 transcript via molecular characterization of a small kernel 1 (smk1, named as smk11 in earlier proposal) mutant in Zea mays (maize). RNA editing modifies cytidines (C) to uridines (U) at specific sites in the transcripts of mitochondria and plastids, altering the amino acid specified by the DNA sequence. Mutations in Smk1 arrest both the embryo and endosperm development. Cloning of Smk1 indicates that it encodes an E-subclass pentatricopeptide repeat (PPR) protein that is targeted to mitochondria. Loss of SMK1 function abolishes the C to U editing at the nad7-836 site, leading to the retention of a proline codon that is edited to encode leucine in the wild type. The smk1 mutant showed dramatically reduced complex–I assembly and NADH dehydrogenase activity, and abnormal biogenesis of the mitochondria. Analysis of the ortholog in Oryza sativa (rice) reveals that rice SMK1 has a conserved function in C to U editing of the mitochondrial nad7-836 site. T-DNA knock-out mutants showed abnormal embryo and endosperm development, resulting in embryo or seedling lethality. The leucine at NAD7-279 is highly conserved from bacteria to flowering plants, and analysis of genome sequences from many plants revealed a molecular coevolution between the requirement for C to U editing at this site and the existence of an SMK1 homolog. These results demonstrate that Smk1 encodes a PPR-E protein that is required for nad7-836 editing, and this editing is critical to NAD7 function in complex-I assembly in mitochondria, and hence to embryo and endosperm development in maize and rice. In conclusion, the project is well finished. In several areas, we exceeded our expectations.

474313.label: Major findings and research outcome
474313.value: 1). Identification of SMK11 function. After the cloning of Smk11 by transposons tagging and confirmation by multiple allele analysis, we predict that Smk11 functions in RNA editing in organelles based on the sequence information. Subcellular protein localization analysis using SMK11-GFP fusion revealed a mitochondrial localization of SMK11. Thus, a comparative study was carried out to analyze the mitochondrial transcripts between the mutant and WT. Sequencing of all the mitochondrial transcripts revealed that Smk11 is required for nad7-836 editing in mitochondria. Further analysis confirmed the mutation of Smk11 blocks complex I assembly, hence severely blocks the electron transfer chain in mitochondria. Further analysis of the rice ortholog Os Smk11 identified a conserved function of SMK11. 2). Characterization of the Smk11 mutant and the expression of Smk11 during seed development. We examined the mutant seed developing profile and revealed Smk11 mutation delays embryo and endosperm development. It also inhibits the differentiation of transfer cells. Smk11 mRNA was found in all the vegetative and reproductive tissues tested, relatively high in stem, pollen, silk and ear, and low in root, leaf, tassel and developing kernels. 3). Impact of over-expressing Smk11 on seed development. We attempted to transform maize with Smk11 in collaboration with Prof. JR Zhang at Shandong University, but we failed to identify reliable transgenic lines. The transformation of over-expressing Smk11 in rice is currently underway. 4). Identification of the potential SMK11 interacting proteins. Yeast two hybrid analyses identified over 200 candidates that may interact with SMK11. Three were localized in mitochondria, but further analyses by BIFC did not confirm their interaction with SMK11. Thus, it is possible that the transcript level of the SMK11 interacting proteins is very low or SMK11 does not have to interact with a partner protein to carry out its function.

474313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
474313.value: Although we failed to identify SMK11 interaction protein, it remains a question as to how a PPR-E type protein such as SMK11 carries out the deamination of specific cytidine in mRNA. The editing mechanism is worth further investigation. In addition, we revealed that a strong co-evolution of the nad7-836 editing site in mitochondria with the presence of a SMK11 homolog in the nucleus, which presents a case for further study on mitochondrion-nucleus co-evaluation.

474313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
474313.value: The Smk11 mutation causes a smaller seed phenotype in maize with arrested embryo and endosperm development. The mutation was identified to be a loss of function mutation in a PPR-E, a type of proteins with loosely conserved 35-amino acid repeats and an extension (E) domain. The function of this PPR-E named SMK11 is to edit the nad7-836 cytidine to uridine in mitochondria. Failure to editing causes dysfunction of Nad7 protein, resulting in failed mitochondrial respiration, hence arresting seed development. This was proved by analysis on the mitochondrial complex abundance and assembly where the mutant failed to assemble complex I. The rice counter part gene OsSmk11 has the same molecular function and mutation leads to small rice grain. This study cloned the Smk11 gene and identified the function in RNA editing. The failed editing also indicates the importance of that amino acid residue – leucine in protein function for electron transfer and complex I assembly. The revelation of this mutation affects seed size opens the possibility of enhancing the mitochondrial function for crop improvement.

474513.label: Project Title(Chinese)
474513.value: 中風後抑鬱的靜息態預設模式網路：一項腦功能連接的磁共振研究

474513.label: Co - Investigator(s)
474513.value: Prof Chu, Winnie Chiu-wing Prof Mok, Vincent Chung-tong Prof Wang, Defeng Prof Wong, Lawrence Ka-sing

474513.label: Project Objectives
474513.value: To investigate the effect of DMN FC on the risk of developing PSD. We hypothesize that PSD is associated with abnormal DMN FC. To investigate the effect of DMN FC on the symptom severity of PSD. We hypothesize that there is a significant correlation between abnormal DMN FC and PSD severity. To investigate the effect of DMN FC on the outcome of PSD. We hypothesize that non-remitting PSD is predicted by abnormal DMN FC at baseline. To investigate the relationship between structural abnormalities and DMN FC in patients with PSD. We hypothesize that abnormal DMN FC is correlated with the extent of acute infarcts, white matter hyperintensities (WMHs), and reduced white matter integrity, as measured by diffusion tensor imaging (DTI).
