474513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
474513.value: 1．目的 本研究旨在評估大腦默認模式網絡（DMN）功能性連接（FC）與中風後抑郁（PSD）之間的關系。 2．研究背景 大腦是由壹套廣泛分布並互相連接的網絡組成的。默認模式網絡（DMN）就是這樣的壹種網絡，由壹些在個體處于清醒靜息狀態且不受外界幹擾時較爲活躍的大腦區域構成。不同腦區（磁共振功能性連接/functional connectivity magnetic resonance imaging, FCMRI）在靜息時血氧依賴水平（Blood Oxygenation Level Dependent,BOLD）信號的關系，據說可以反映相關功能在結構上的重要相互關系。據研究報道，中風後存在功能性連接（FC）異常(Sharma et al., 2009)。因此，越來越多的研究者有興趣使用靜息態FCMRI預測中風後的康複狀況(Westlake et al., 2012)以及療效(Buch et al., 2012)。也急需大型縱向研究，以確定DMN FC 是否可以幫助對長期住院的中風幸存者、普通老年人群做出臨床醫療決定。 中風是最常見的重性神經系統疾病，每年在全世界涉及1500萬人，並給其中500萬人留下永久性殘疾。PSD是中風後最嚴重的情感障礙，涉及三分之壹的中風幸存者。抑郁與較差的短期恢複、長期康複結局，較嚴重的殘疾，認知損害，以及中風幸存者的死亡率有關。也有人主張新病因模型（Santos et al.,2009），認爲PSD的灰質、白質缺血病變破壞了大腦的情感調節機制，導致腦邊緣系統過度活躍以及隨之而來的抑郁症狀。如果該模型是正確的，檢測PSD和DMN FC之間的關系將會提供相關支持證據。 3．研究項目說明 本研究是第壹個大樣本（n=738）縱向研究，將檢測連續入院患有PSD中風幸存者的FC作用。研究結果將會給探討FC在PSD風險、症狀嚴重程度、預後的作用帶來曙光。 4．項目優勢 本研究的主要優勢是精神科醫師、神經科醫師、放射科醫師間的通力合作。多學科參與將會確保收集到綜合性的精神科、神經科、放射科科研數據，不僅著眼于當前的研究評估，而且顧及今後的研究使用，比如評估中風後其他相關精神障礙的風險因素和預後。

474513.label: Realisation of objectives
474513.value: Structural MRI examinations were performed in 1429 patients, and 417 (29.1%) were assessed at 3 months following their index stroke. Among these 417 patients, 191 (45.8%) received a functional MRI examination, of whom 67 (35.1%) had poststroke depression (PSD) and 124 (64.9%) did not. The characteristics of the final sample (N=191) were as follows: 59.2% were men, the mean age was 65.3 years, and the average education level was 7.6 years. Their mean National Institute of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), Barthel Index, Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), and Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS) scores were 4.4, 18.3, 26.5, and 5.2, respectively. The clinical characteristics of the PSD group were as follows: 58.9% were men, the mean age was 63.7 years, and the average education level was 7.7 years. Their NIHSS, Barthel Index, MMSE, and GDS scores were 5.5, 17.4, 26.1, and 9.69, respectively. In the non-PSD group, 58.9% were male, the mean age was 66.2 years, and the average education level was 7.5 years. Their respective scores were 3.8, 18.9, 26.7, and 2.7. There were no significant differences between the two groups in terms of age, sex, education level, and NIHSS and MMSE scores, except that the PSD group had a higher MMSE score (p<0.001). Among these 191 patients, 146 completed the 9-month follow-up and 114 completed the 15-month follow-up examination. The main reasons for dropouts at the 9-month follow-up were refusal to participate (N=28) and failure to access the patient (N=17). The dropout group had lower MMSE (p<0.001) and higher GDS (p=0.005) scores. The main reasons for dropouts at the 15-month follow-up were refusal to participate (N=55), failure to access the patient (N=20), and death (N=2). The dropout group had lower age (p=0.043) and higher MMSE scores (p<0.001). In the PSD group, 45 patients completed the 9-month follow-up and 33 patients completed the 15-month follow-up examination. One patient had PSD at 9 months and none had PSD at 15 months. In the non-PSD group, 101 patients completed the 9-month follow-up and 81 patients completed the 15-month follow-up examination. Two of them had PSD at 9 months and none had PSD at 15 months. Topological properties of the DMN in PSD Functional hubs in DMN. Four regions of interest (ROIs) were identified as functional hubs in patients with PSD including the left middle temporal gyrus (MTG.L.4.1), right superior frontal gyrus (SFG.R.7.6), and bilateral precuneus (PCun.L.4.1 and PCun.R.4.1), whereas six ROIs including MTG.L.4.1, MTG.L.4.4, MTG.R.4.4, SFG.R.7.3, PCun.R.4.1, and PCun.L.4.1 were characterised as functional hubs in patients without PSD. Collectively, the functional hubs of both groups were mutually located in the MTG, SFG, and PCun. Global Properties. No significant differences in global metrics were observed between the two groups at a significance level of 0.05. Nodal properties. Compared with the non-PSD group, the PSD group showed increased nodal degree (56.44±21.50 vs. 70.17±23.26, uncorrected p=0.008), increased global efficiency (0.37±0.06 vs. 0.41±0.07, uncorrected p=0.004), and increased clustering coefficient (0.13±0.03 vs. 0.15±0.04, uncorrected p=0.027) but a decreased characteristic path length (2.81±0.44 vs. 2.51±0.37, uncorrected p=0.004) in the right inferior parietal lobule (IPL.R.6.5, referring to BA39, PGa). Increased betweenness (80.32±95.78 vs. 136.66±105.58, uncorrected p=0.004), increased global efficiency (0.40±0.08 vs. 0.45±0.10, uncorrected p=0.035), and decreased characteristic path length (2.60±0.54 vs. 2.33±0.50, uncorrected p=0.035) in SFG.R.7.6 overlapped with the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) and dorsal medial prefrontal cortex (dmPFC). However, these nodal properties did not differ between the two groups after the FDR corrections. Because this is an exploratory study, we encourage further experiments to validate our findings by reporting the results without multiple comparison correction. Increased functional connections of the Default Mode Network (DMN) in PSD In the network-based statistics (NBS), three primary thresholds were applied to identify the altered functional connections at different levels of sensitivity. A more stringent threshold led to fewer connections identified but with stronger group -difference effect. Three hyper-connected subnetworks were thus generated: the first sub-network generated with the least conservative primary threshold (p<0.01) comprised 26 nodes and 44 connections, the second with the primary threshold of p < 0.005 contained 18 nodes and 24 connections, and the third, with the most conservative primary threshold (p<0.001), had 6 nodes and 5 connections. It is noteworthy that the connections in these three subnetworks overlapped with each other like a pyramid: significant functional connectivities (FCs) identified under a stringent primary threshold were all statistically significant in the NBS analysis under the less stringent primary threshold. Specifically, the following five pairs of increased FCs (PSD>non-PSD) were identified in all three hyper-connected subnetworks, indicating a strong between-group difference effect: between orbital gyrus (OrG.R.6.2) and SFG.L.7.6 (0.30±0.23 vs. 0.61±0.24), between OrG.R.6.2 and SFG.R.7.6 (0.38±0.28 vs. 0.64±0.27), between MTG.R.4.4 and SFG.R.7.6 (0.29±0.20 vs. 0.51±0.26), between IPL.R.6.5 and SFG.R.7.6 (0.40±0.26 vs. 0.65±0.21), and between OrG.R.6.2 and SFG.L.7.7 (0.27±0.19 vs. 0.48±0.27). Notably, these anatomical regions with increased FCs overlapped with or belonged to the orbital frontal cortex (OFC), dlPFC, dmPFC, ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC), MTG, and IPL. Nodes involved in these sub-networks were classified into three types: those present at three sub-networks, or two sub-networks, or only one sub-network. SFG.L.7.6, SFG.R.7.6, OrG.R.6.2, IPL.R.6.5, MTG.R.4.4, and SFG.L.7.7 were sensitive ROIs related to post-stroke depression because they were mutual nodes of three sub-networks. More importantly, these five ROIs could be considered as intrinsic functional hubs in a PSD-related sub-network indicated by relatively higher nodal degree. It is noteworthy that SFG.R.7.6 was simultaneously identified as a functional hub of the DMN in the PSD group and as a functional hub in the hyper-connected sub-network. In addition, nodal metrics of SFG.R.7.6 were also significantly different between the two groups. Collectively, these results showed a widespread hyper-connected configuration of the functional DMN in PSD and depicted several sensitive ROIs related to PSD. Lack of correlation between the network metrics and severity of PSD Only the significantly altered network metrics in previous analyses were further estimated on their correlations with the severity of PSD adjusted for age, sex, years of education, level of social support, laterality of stroke, stroke severity, number of acute infarcts, and cognitive function. However, partial correlations showed that the relationship between altered FCs, nodal metrics, and severity of PSD were insignificant, except that the FC between MTG.R.4.4 (right anterior superior temporal sulcus) and MFG.L.7.7 (left lateral BA 10, overlapped with vmPFC and mOFC) significantly correlated with the severity of PSD (r=0.48, uncorrected p=0.04). However, this significance failed to survive after multiple comparisons corrections. Summary of objectives addressed to date We were unable to recruit the targeted sample size due to a low prevalence of PSD. We had increased the sites of recruitment from one to four and extended the duration of the study for 12 months.

474513.label: Major findings and research outcome
474513.value: This study examined the topological reconfiguration of functional DMN, using NBS and graph theory, in patients with clinically significant PSD 3 months after stroke. To the best of our knowledge, we first delineated that the functional DMN in patients with PSD showed a trend to be more locally integrated in the cored hubs, such as the mPFC, IPL, and OFC, whereas the global architecture of the DMN was identical to that of patients without depressive symptoms. Alternatively, we found that compared with patients without PSD, those with PSD exhibited a wide range of increased FCs within the hubs (mPFC, OFC, IPL, and MTG) in the DMN, suggesting a functionally hyperconnected pattern in PSD. In summary, we revealed that in patients with clinical post-stroke depressive symptoms in the chronic stroke phase, the DMN exposed a trend to be more functionally integrated as marked by multiple increases in FCs within the network but to be more specialised in some cored hubs such as IPL and the dorsal PFC. Our findings implied that stroke-mediated interruption of the functional DMN topology may be associated with the risk of clinically significant PSD and thus provided vital insight into the network-based pathogenesis of PSD. The examinations of the topological alterations in functional DMN after stroke may add benefit to the identification of stroke patients at risk for late PSD.

474513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
474513.value: Further investigations are warranted to clarify whether DMN have any impact on the clinical presentation or treatment response of PSD. It would be logical to examine whether DMN might also contribute to the outcome of depression in the general elderly population. In addition, further investigations are needed to clarify whether DMN could be a target for new interventions to treat PSD, such as brain stimulation treatments.

474513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
474513.value: This study examined brain functioning in stroke survivors with depression. We found that distinct abnormal brain functioning increases the risk of depression. This finding will enhance our understanding of the underlying cause of depression in stroke. It may also facilitate further research on new treatments of depression in stroke, such as brain stimulation treatment.

474813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
474813.value: Radiation damages cancer and normal human cells. Its cumulative dosage may result in delayed complications, notably changes in the nerve and musculoskeletal systems. Radiation to the neck in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) patients causes sensory and motor impairment in oro- and laryngo-pharynx, and these patients often suffer from aspiration. The current study aims at exploring the pathophysiology of motor impairment in two muscle groups, the tongue and the suprahyoids, which have been shown in prior studies to be affected in head and neck cancer patients both locally and internationally. Two hundred post-irradiation NPC patients will be recruited from the ENT out-patient clinic of Prince of Wales Hospital and each will complete a questionnaire survey on quality of life. Swallowing outcome assessment for penetration/aspiration will be conducted via fiberoptic endoscopic examination of swallowing (FEES) as well as videofluoroscopic swallowing study (VFSS). Study of the two swallowing muscle groups will be conducted with the use of surface electromyography (sEMG) as well as ultrasonography (USG), providing a series of physiological data for the two muscle groups. Multivariate regression model will be constructed to understand the significance of each of the clinical factors, patient factors and physiological parameters on the final clinical outcome. It is expected that a more thorough understanding of the pathological process and more importantly the identification of risk factors for post-irradiation dysphagia will be achieved. Further studies in terms of defining the different techniques employed in the current study, and utilizing physiological parameters in the early identification of patients at risk will be conducted upon completion of the present study. It is hoped that we will eventually be able to design new treatment strategies for irradiation-associated dysphagia once the pathophysiology is better understood. 放射治療的輻射會傷害癌細胞以至正常細胞，其累積劑量更可能導致延遲出現的併發症，尤其對於神經系統和肌肉骨骼系統。鼻咽癌患者於頸部所受的輻射會導致頸部軟組織纖維化，從而構成口﹑咽和喉的感覺和運動障礙。這些患者可能出現食物誤墮氣管的現象。本研究旨在探索兩組吞嚥肌肉，舌（tongue）和舌骨上肌群（supra-hyoids）於運動障礙上的病理生理學，而頭頸癌患者於這兩組肌肉所受的影響在以往的研究中已證明了。二百位名曾完成放射治療的鼻咽癌患者將在威爾斯親王醫院耳鼻喉科門診診所被招募參與是次研究，參與者均需完成一份有關其生活質素的問卷。參與者將通過光導纖維內視鏡吞嚥檢查（FEESST）以及透視錄影吞嚥檢查（VFSS）接受吞嚥評估，並透過表面肌電圖（sEMG）以及超聲波（Ultrasonography）獲得兩組肌肉群的一系列生理數據。我們將利用多元回歸模型（multivariate regression model）分析各臨床因素﹑患者因素和生理參數對最終臨床結果的影響。透過本研究，我們希望加深瞭解放射治療後吞嚥困難的病理過程，並有效辨認其風險因素。本研究完成後，我們將進一步定義於研究中採用的不同診斷技術，並利用有關的生理參數儘早識別高危患者。我們希望最終能夠為接受放射治療後的吞嚥困難患者設計新的治療方針。

474813.label: Realisation of objectives
474813.value: Implementation: All the above objectives in the proposal were addressed. Subject recruitment began in early 2014 at the ENT Out-patient Clinic of the Prince of Wales Hospital (PWH). Each participant was given a fact sheet outlining the background of the study as well as a brief introduction of the instrumental examinations involved. After returning written consent to participant in the study, each participant was asked to complete a questionnaire on demographic, treatment and feeding information, and another questionnaire to collect quality-of-life (QoL) information, i.e. the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy - Naso-pharyngeal subscale (FACT-NP) (Tong, 2009). Each participant was then arranged to attend two sessions of data collection on two separate days to complete all necessary examinations. The first session was conducted at the ENT Out-patient Clinic of PWH, and involved a history-taking interview, an oral motor examination, the Fiberoptic Endoscopic Evaluation of Swallowing (FEES), a surface electromyographic (SEMG) as well as ultrasonographic (USG) measurement of swallowing. Examinations in this session involved an ENT specialist and a speech therapist. The second session was conducted at the Radiology Department of PWH, and involved the Videofluoroscopic Study of Swallowing (VFSS). Examinations in this session involved a speech therapist, a radiographer, a nurse and a stand-by radiologist. Overall achievement: The recruitment and study period lasted for 30 months, including an extension of 6 months from the originally planned period. Up to May 2016, 172 participants were successfully recruited. Among these, there were 13 patients (8%) who withdrew from the study. Quantitative physiological raw data were obtained from FEES, SEMG, USG and VFSS. QoL scores were obtained from FACT-NP. These data, together with information collected by questionnaires, were processed to obtain a list of patient-related, treatment-related, and physiological parameters for the investigation and analysis of risk factors associated with poor swallowing and QoL outcome. Problem encountered and solutions: In the initial 12 months, subject recruitment was smooth and quite a number of NPC patients showed interest to participate in the study. It was noticed that, however, the rate of subject recruitment started to drop in early 2015. This was partly due to the fact that patients who showed up in the clinic started to repeat after a long period of recruitment. To sustain recruitment rate, the project team decided to start recruiting potential subjects from another clinic, i.e. the Oncology Out-patient Clinic of PWH, which was a collaborating department in the present study. The recruitment rate improved after recruiting patients from a new source as most of these patients had regular medical follow-up at the Oncology Out-patient Clinic only, but not ENT. However, recruitment rate was still falling towards the second half of 2015. The PI then decided to apply for a half-year extension of the study in order to improve total recruitment. Eventually, our study managed to recruit 172 NPC patients within 2.5 years, which is 86% of our target sample size for the project. One of the causes of incomplete data collection of participants was the withdrawal from VFSS (i.e. second data collection session), which involved the use of radiation. Some participants showed concern of potential harmful effects from the exam and hence opted out. A fact sheet outlining all involved examinations and their possible side-effects was distributed to all participants prior to their consent to join the study. Despite such information provided, a small number of participants, especially those who did not show much concern on swallowing functions, were not keen to proceed to VFSS. Other reasons of subject withdrawal included an unmatched schedule, prolonged hospitalization, repeated default and loss of contact. Having this said, our overall withdrawal rate remained low at 8%.

474813.label: Major findings and research outcome
474813.value: One hundred and 63 patients were recruited in the study (116 males; 47 females; mean age: 57.2 years; time elapsed since treatment: 3-26 years). Thirty patients (18%) demonstrated tracheal aspiration (i.e. PAS score 6-8) on at least one consistency, whilst forty-two patients (26%) demonstrated laryngeal penetration (i.e. PAS score 3-5) on at least one consistency. Swallowing outcome (10th APCSLH, Japan, 2017): Dysphagia was defined as the presence of penetration or aspiration (i.e. Penetration-Aspiration Scale score≥3) on at least one consistency during videofluoroscopic study of swallowing (VFSS). There was significant difference between the two groups (i.e. ‘dysphagia’ and ‘no dysphagia’) in anterior hyoid displacement (p=.004), oral transit time (p=.000), pharyngeal transit time (p=.000), pharyngeal delay time (p=.000), upper esophageal sphincter opening (p=.005), and pharyngeal constriction ratio (p=.000). Binary logistic regression analysis revealed that pharyngeal constriction ratio (odds ratio=1.2, p=.022) and pharyngeal delay time (odds ratio=26.8, p=.047) were associated with dysphagia. Quality of life outcome (6th ESSD Congress, Italy, 2016): Each patient’s quality-of-life (QoL) profile was collected using the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy - Nasopharyngeal (FACT-NP). Multiple regression analysis revealed that both dysphagia severity (PAS score) (p<.001) and education level (p=.003) were significant predictors for QoL in these patients. A higher PAS score and a lower education level predicted a lower QoL. Gender, age, stage of disease, radiation technique, time elapsed since irradiation had no significant effect on QoL. Ultrasonography study (CUHK ENT Conference, 2015): B-mode ultrasonographic examination was employed in the current study to assess suprahyoid muscle movement in coronal view. The percentage increase in cross-sectional area of the geniohyoid muscle was found to correlate positively with anterior hyoid displacement during thin fluid swallows (r=0.42, p<.05). The time elapsed since irradiation was also found to correlate negatively with anterior hyoid displacement (r=-0.40, p<.05) and upper esophageal sphincter opening (r=-0.33, p<.05). Ultrasound imaging as a clinical screening tool allows direct visualization and measurement of individual suprahyoid muscles. Surface EMG study (Hong Kong Speech & Hearing Symposium, 2016): Submental muscle activities were measured during swallowing using ultrasonography (USG) and surface electromyography (SEMG). Preliminary analysis revealed a positive correlation between the change in cross-sectional area of the geniohyoid muscle as measured by USG and the submental electrical activity as measured by SEMG (r=.27; p<0.05) during thin fluid swallows. Both parameters, however, were not associated with PAS score.

474813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
474813.value: The findings of the present study revealed that the development of post-irradiation dysphagia was associated with a number of physiological parameters, most of which were related to swallowing muscle functions. By far, research work on post-irradiation dysphagia of head and neck cancer has mainly focused on the investigation of contributing factors for the occurrence of dysphagia and the efficacy of swallowing intervention for patients with symptomatic dysphagia. Limited work has been done to investigate the potential contribution of ‘neo-adjuvant’ prophylactic swallowing training on the preservation of swallowing functions and prevention of post-treatment dysphagia in this disease group. It is hypothesized that prophylactic swallowing training is effective in preventing or delaying the onset of post-irradiation dysphagia due to swallowing muscle functions.

474813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
474813.value: The current study investigated the swallowing and quality-of-life (QoL) outcome of 163 post-radiotherapy naso-pharyngeal cancer (NPC) patients. The study involved a series of physiological examinations to obtain data on swallowing performance. These examinations included radiographic, endoscopic, ultrasonographic and electromyographic measurements. Information was also collected through questionnaires regarding patients’ demographic, treatment, feeding and QoL status. These data were analyzed to identify factors that could predict the occurrence of swallowing impairments and poor QoL in NPC survivors. For swallowing outcome, it was found that impaired pharyngeal strength (or food residue in throat after swallowing) and a delayed swallowing response were associated with a higher risk of food or liquid entry into the airway, which is a cause of chest infection. For quality-of-life outcome, it was found that swallowing dysfunctions and a low education level were associated with a poorer QoL in these patients. The current study identified areas that need to be addressed in order to minimize radiotherapy-related side effects in NPC patients. Swallowing intervention should be provided by speech therapists to improve swallowing functions and minimize risk of airway aspiration from oral feeding.

474913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
474913.value: Embryonic stem cells (ESCs), derived from the inner cell mass of blastocysts, can self-renew and are pluripotent, meaning that they propagate indefinitely in culture and have the ability to give rise to all differentiated cell types in the body, including cardiomyocytes. ESCs can therefore be an excellent source of cardiomyocytes for research and future therapies. The functional properties of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes must be better understood before such cells can be used for therapeutic purposes. Calcium transients (CaTs) are important determinants of the excitation-contraction coupling of cardiomyocytes. However, regulation of CaTs in early differentiating cardiomyocytes is not fully elucidated. The renin-angiotensin system (RAS) plays a pivotal role in the cardiovascular system. Previous studies showed that exogenous application of angiotensin II (AngII), the major effector of RAS, increases the contraction amplitude and frequency of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes. However, it is unknown whether local RAS exists and produces AngII endogenously in early differentiating cardiomyocytes. In addition, the mode (intracrine, autocrine and/or paracrine) through which AngII exerts its effect and the signaling pathways that are involved in mediating the effect of AngII are largely unknown. Preliminary data from our group showed that the proteins of both AngII receptor type I (AT1R) and AngII receptor type II (AT2R) are expressed in ESC-derived cardiomyocytes. AT2R inhibitor but not AT1R inhibitor decreased both the amplitude and the frequency of CaTs. Interestingly, AT2R was found to be localized in the nucleus of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes. These novel data suggested that AngII may be produced intracellularly and act on the AT2R to affect CaTs in an intracrine fashion. However, the mechanism underlying how AngII affects CaTs is unknown. Previous studies showed that AngII activates canonical transient receptor potential isoform 3 (TRPC3) channels in various cell types while recent data from our laboratory showed that TRPC3 channels are present in ESC-derived cardiomyocytes to determine both the amplitude and the frequency of CaTs. However, it is unknown whether AngII would regulate CaTs through TRPCs in ESC-derived cardiomyocytes. The overall objective of this proposal is to investigate the role of AngII and the mechanisms underlying the effect of AngII in regulation of CaTs in ESC-derived cardiomyocytes. A combination of cell biology, molecular biology, electrophysiology and genetic manipulation techniques will be employed. This study will be crucial for understanding the complex biology of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes. This study will also be important for providing insights into the suitability of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes for future transplantation. 胚胎幹細胞來自囊胚的內細胞團，能夠自我更新和擁有萬能的特性，意味著它們可以無限地被培養，並有能力分化為體內所有的細胞類型，包括心肌。胚胎幹細胞分化出的心肌細胞能夠應用於研究和未來的治療，因此是一個很好的心肌細胞來源。要應用胚胎幹細胞分化出的心肌細胞於細胞治療法之前，我們必須更好地理解這些細胞的功能特性。 鈣瞬變是決定心肌細胞激發與收縮的聯結的重要因素。然而，我們尚未完全理解早期分化的心肌細胞是如何調節鈣瞬變。 腎素 - 血管緊張素系統（RAS）在心血管系統中起著舉足輕重的作用。以往的研究表明，外源性的血管緊張素II（RAS的主要效應器) 能增加胚胎幹細胞分化出的心肌細胞的收縮幅度和頻率。然而，我們還未知道RAS是否存在於胚胎幹細胞早期分化出的心肌細胞裡，並產生內源性的血管緊張素Ⅱ。此外，我們仍未知道血管緊張素Ⅱ是通過什麼模式（胞内分泌，自體分泌和/或旁分泌）和信號轉導途徑去導致它在心肌細胞裡的作用。 以往的研究表明，血管緊張素Ⅱ能於不同類型的細胞中激活經典型瞬時電壓受體通道3（TRPC3）。同時，我們最近的實驗數據表明，TRPC3表達於胚胎幹細胞分化出的心肌細胞中，同時能對這些心肌細胞裡鈣瞬變的波幅和頻率有著重要的影響。然而，血管緊張素Ⅱ是否通過調節TRPC3去影響鈣瞬變還是未知之數。 這個研究計劃的總體目標是研究血管緊張素II在胚胎幹細胞分化出的心肌細胞中調控鈣瞬變的角色和機制。我們會使用細胞生物學、分子生物學、電生理和遺傳操作技術以達致目標。 這該研究將對理解複雜的胚胎幹細胞分化出的心肌細胞的生物學至關重要。此外，本研究也將對胚胎幹細胞分化出的心肌細胞是否適合使用於將來的移植提供重要的見解。

474913.label: Realisation of objectives
474913.value: [Due to the required format of the present report, figures of the data cannot be shown. All data are available upon request.] Aim 1. To investigate if the local renin-angiotensin system exists in embryonic stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes. To test if the local renin-angiotensin system (RAS) is present in embryonic stem celll-derived cardiomyocytes (ESC-CMs), we first tested for the presence of individual RAS components. Co-immunostaining of angiotensin II (Ang II) and the cardiac-specific protein cardiac troponin T followed by confocal microscopy was performed on ESC-CMs. The same co-immunostaining was also performed for ESC-CMs that have been preincubated with angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor benazeprilat and/or chymase inhibitor chymostatin. While benazeprilat or chymostatin alone could not decrease the endogenous level of Ang II to a statistically significant level, co-application of both inhibitors suppressed the iAng II level. These results suggested that intracellular Ang II (iAng II) is synthesized by both ACE and chymase in ESC-CMs. Immunostaining of Ang II type 1 receptor (AT1R) and Ang II type 2 receptor (AT2R) was also performed. Our results showed that AT1R was expressed both on the plasma membrane and in the cytoplasm while AT2R was expressed in a unique, web-like pattern. Co-staining with the nuclear stain DAPI and with antibodies against SERCA2 [a cardiac specific isoform of SERCA; this was used as a sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) marker] revealed that AT2R was located on the nucleus and the SR. Recombinant adenoviruses expressing the AT1R fluorescent fusion protein (AT1R-YFP) or the AT2R fluorescent fusion protein (AT2R-YFP) were also used to infect ESC-CMs. The results confirmed that AT1R were expressed both on the plasma membrane and in the cytoplasm while AT2R were expressed on the nucleus and the SR. Taken together, our results showed the presence and the subcellular localization of different components of the local RAS in ESC-CMs. Aim 2. To investigate if angiotensin II regulates the calcium transients of embryonic stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes and if angiotensin II exerts its effect via an intracrine mode. Action potentials (APs) and calcium transients (CaTs) are important determinants of the excitation-contraction coupling of cardiomyocytes. Patch clamping and calcium imaging were performed on ESC-CMs to measure these two functional parameters. Extracellular Ang II was found to transiently increase the frequency of calcium transients (CaTs), the AP rate and diastolic depolarization (DD) slope of the APs. Preincubation of AT1R blocker losartan but not AT2R blocker PD123319 attenuated the effects of extracellular Ang II. The results indicate that extracellular Ang II positively regulates the CaTs and APs via AT1R. Next, to investigate the effect of intracellular Ang II (iAng II) on the automaticity of ESC-CMs, we have developed the dual patch clamp method in which one electrode would serve to deliver drugs to the intracellular environment of the cells, while the other electrode would serve to record APs before and after the drug delivery on the same cells. By using the dual patch clamp method, iAng II was found to decrease the AP rate and DD slope of ESC-CMs. In addition, intracellular delivery of AT2R activator C21 exerted the same effects as that of iAng II, suggesting that iAng II activates intracellular AT2R, leading to a decrease in APs in ESC-CMs. Take together, we found that extracellular Ang II positively regulates the automaticity of ESC-CMs through AT1R. On the other hand, iAng II negatively regulates the automaticity through AT2R via an intracrine mode. Aim 3. To investigate if angiotensin II regulates the calcium transients of embryonic stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes through opening the canonical transient receptor potential isoform 3 (TRPC3) channels. By calcium imaging using confocal microscopy, we found that Ang II increased the frequency and decreased the decay time of CaTs in a concentration-dependent manner in ESC-CMs. Pyr3, a TRPC3-specific blocker, attenuated the effects of Ang II on the CaTs. The results indicated that the effects of Ang II on the frequency and decay time are mediated through activating TRPC3. In Aims 1 and 2, we had several novel findings, including the presence of intracellular AT2R on the SR, and iAng II regulates the automaticity through intracellular AT2R. Therefore, we decided to focus more on this completely new pathway. By using dual patch clamp, iAng II was found to attenuate the effects of caffeine [(activator of ryanodine receptor 2 (RyR2)] on the automaticity of ESC-CMs. Furthermore, in the absence of external calcium ion, iAng II reduced caffeine-induced calcium release in ESC-CMs. These results suggested that iAng II negatively regulates the automaticity of ESC-CMs through inhibiting the activity of RyR2. Take together, we found that extracellular Ang II positively regulates the automaticity through opening of TRPC3. On the other hand, iAng II negatively regulates the automaticity through inhibiting RyR2.

474913.label: Major findings and research outcome
474913.value: Endogenous expression of Ang II in ESC-CMs. iAng II was detected in the cytoplasm of ESC-CMs. Co-application of ACE and chymase inhibitors suppressed the iAng II level, suggesting that iAng II is synthesized by both ACE and chymase. Developing CMs expressed AT1R on the plasma membrane and in the cytoplasm and expressed AT2R predominately on the nucleus and the SR. AT1R was found to be expressed both on the plasma membrane and in the cytoplasm of ESC-CMs and neonatal rat cardiomyocytes. AT2R was found to be expressed on the nucleus and the SR of these cardiomyocytes. Extracellular Ang II regulated APs in a transient manner through AT1R-dependent pathway. Exogenously-applied fluorescence-labeled Ang II was not observed to enter ESC-CMs even after being applied for 36 hours, suggesting that exogenous Ang II may act on receptors located on the plasma membrane. Extracellular Ang II transiently increased AP rate and DD slope of ESC-CMs. AT1R blocker losartan but not AT2R blocker PD123319 attenuated the effects of extracellular Ang II on APs, suggesting that extracellular Ang II acts through AT1R to increase APs. Extracellular Ang II regulated CaTs through opening the TRPC3. Extracellular Ang II increased the frequency and decreased the decay time of the CaTs of ESC-CMs in a concentration-dependent manner. Pyr3, a TRPC3-specific blocker, attenuated the effects of Ang II on the CaTs. The results indicated that the effects of Ang II on the CaTs are mediated through activating TRPC3. iAng II decreased the APs of developing CMs through AT2R-dependent pathway. By dual current patch clamp, iAng II was found to decrease AP rate and DD slope of ESC-CMs. Intracellular delivery of AT2R activator C21 also decreased the AP rate and the DD slope, suggesting that activation of AT2R would decrease APs. Since decent amount of iAng II and activation of intracellular AT2R would similarly decrease the APs, our results hinted that iAng II activates intracellular AT2R, leading to the decrease in APs in developing CMs. Effect of iAng II on the automaticity of ESC-CMs was associated with the activity of RyR2. Intracellular delivery of Ang II attenuated the effects of caffeine (RyR2 activator) on the APs. In addition, in the absence of external calcium ion, iAng II reduced caffeine-induced calcium release. These results suggested that iAng II negatively regulates the APs through inhibiting the activity of RyR2. All results described above were published in form of conference abstracts and/or papers.

474913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
474913.value: In this study, embryonic stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes were found to produce angiotensin II under basal condition. Further investigation would be conducted to investigate if different physiological (e.g. mechanical stress) or pathophysiological (e.g. high-glucose environment, atrial fibrillation) conditions would alter the production of Ang II in cardiomyocytes. Moreover, we aim to explore to develop new method [e.g. electrospray ionisation (ESI)-liquid chromatography (LC)-mass spectrometry (MS) (ESI-LC-MS)/MS method] for more sensitive and reliable detection of intracellular Ang II. In addition, in this study, angiotensin II type 2 receptor (AT2R) was found to express on the sarcoplasmic reticulum of cardiomyocytes. Importantly, activated AT2R was found to exert its downstream effect via inhibiting the calcium release from ryanodine receptor type 2 (RyR2). This is a novel pathway that has never been reported. While angiotensin II type 1 receptor has been well-studied, the signaling pathway of AT2R, especially for that of the intracellular AT2R, is unclear. Further investigation would be conducted to investigate how AT2R can inhibit the RyR2. Co-immunoprecipitation and knockdown by shRNA would be conducted to test the possible interaction between AT2R and RyR2. The signaling downstream of AT2R to inhibit RyR2 would also be investigated using pharmacological and molecular tool.

474913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
474913.value: Embryonic stem cells (ESCs) have the unique ability to give rise to all differentiated cell types in our bodies, including cardiomyocytes. ESCs can therefore be an excellent source of cardiomyocytes for research and future therapeutic applications. Angiotensin II (Ang II) plays a pivotal role in the cardiovascular system. The aim of this project was to investigate the role of Ang II on the functional properties of ESC-derived cardiomyocytes (ESC-CMs). Early differentiating ESC-CMs resemble cardiac pacemaker cells and generate spontaneous action potentials (APs). These spontaneous APs determine heart rate. In our study, using a combination of cell biology, molecular biology, electrophysiological and genetic manipulation techniques, we found that ESC-CMs synthesize their own Ang II. In addition, we found that extracellular Ang II acts via Ang II type 1 receptor to increase spontaneous APs while intracellular Ang II acts via Ang II type 2 receptor to decrease spontaneous APs. Since angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors are used clinically for the treatment of cardiovascular diseases, this study has therefore not only generated biological information concerning how Ang II acts on ESC-CMs, it has also provided important insights into the suitability of transplanting ESC-CMs on patients, especially for patients who are taking ACE inhibitors.

475113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
475113.value: In Hong Kong, the prevalence rate of asthma in Chinese school children is over 10%. Moreover, the prevalence has increased by three to four times over the past 20 years. House dust mite allergy is a prevalent cause of allergic responses. The predominant species of dust mite in most geographical regions are Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus and Dermatophagoides farinae. Exposure to house dust mite allergens in atopic patients triggers inflammatory diseases including allergic asthma, perennial rhinitis and atopic dermatitis. At present, more than 20 allergen groups have been defined based on sequence and functional homologies but additional allergen groups as well as members of known allergen groups remain to be identified. Moreover, microbes in house dust mite have been demonstrated to play a critical role in the emergence of allergic responses. However, the genome information of house dust mite is currently very limited. The constituents of endosymbiotic microbiota in house dust mite are also largely unknown. According to the preliminary work conducted to evaluate the feasibility of this project, the genome of Dermatophagoides farinae has a modest size and contains a small amount of repetitive sequences. Microbial elements previously unidentified in dust mite were also elucidated. In this study, we will focus on the sequencing of the genome, transcriptome and microbiome of Dermatophagoides farinae and Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus using the next-generation sequencing technology. The genomic and mRNA sequences of allergens will be elucidated by sequence homology using bioinformatics tools. For selected allergens that have not been characterized before, cDNA will be cloned and then proteins will be expressed. Finally, allergenic properties of expressed proteins will be investigated by immunological techniques. The deliverables of this study will provide important resources for the future identification and characterization of dust mite allergens. 475113.label: Realisation of objectives
475113.value: After the completion of the project, nearly all of the objectives have been achieved and the details are outlined as follows: Objective 1 - To determine the genome and transcriptome of D. farina and D. pteronyssinus using next generation sequencing technology Concerning the D. farina genome, after building a de novo draft assembly and applying gap filling, 4 sequencing libraries were assembled into 554 scaffolds. Separation of microbial DNA resulted in a 53.5-Mb D. farinae draft genome with 516 nuclear genome scaffolds (N50 = 187 kb) and a 14.3-kb mitochondrial genome. On the other hand, we had obtained a 66.8 Mb final assembly of D. pteronyssinus genome with 1,390 contigs and 634 scaffolds, with scaffold N50 being 194 Kb and contig N50 being 80 kb. Finally, the transcriptome of the two dust mite species were also determined for the genome annotation. Objective 2 - To predict and annotate genes in the genome and transcriptome of D. farina and D. pteronyssinus For the D. farina genome, our bioinformatics pipeline predicted 13,475, 20,165, and 14,156 gene models, respectively. Another 3,265 gene models were inferred using transcriptome sequence analysis. Altogether, 16,376 gene models were obtained, including 9,142 that were supported by RNA-sequencing results. Gene annotation with Blast2GO yielded 8,201 genes with significant hits in the NCBI non-redundant database. Among them, 5,576 were assigned at least one GO term. On the other hand, there are 13,699 genes in D. pteronyssinus annotated genome supported by RNA-Seq data inferred from Tophat-Cufflinks transcriptome analysis. On the other hand, according to the analysis by GlimmerHMM, 16,300 genes were predicted. We have also used AUGUSTUS ab initio prediction to increase the number of predicted protein. After combining the ab initio predicted genes and evidence-driven predicted genes, we predicted a total of 16,805 protein-coding genes in D. pteronyssinus. Objective 3 - To identify allergen genes in D. farina and D. pteronyssinus based on sequence homology using bioinformatics tools For the D. farina genome, we retrieved complete gene sequences and structures of 20 reported HDM allergens, including Der f1 to Der f23—except for Der f17, Group 12, and Group 19, from our assembled genome with support from transcriptomic analysis and determined their relative expression levels in adult D. farinae mites in terms of fragments per kilobase of transcript per million mapped reads (FPKM). Der f 4 is reported here for the first time. We also identified the complete sequences of 7 non-canonical allergen candidates (profilin, Alt a 6, alpha-tubulin 1, cathepsin, Mala s 6, aldehyde dehydrogenase, and enolase homologues) with amino acid sequence homology (41.5~90.5%) to experimentally validated allergens in other species. Concerning D. pteronyssinus, from the WHO/IUIS Allergen Nomenclature database, we obtained D. pteronyssinus’ known canonical allergen genes’ complete sequences from Der p 1 to Der p 24, as well as their gene structures. Specifically, there was no Der p 12, Der p 16, Der p 17, Der p 19 and Der p 22 in the database. However, we could find putative Der p 16 and Der p 22 in our high-quality genome by inferring homology from Der f 16 and Der f 22 which are known allergens in D. farinae. Moreover, we got the Der p 25 to Der p 33 gene sequences and gene structures. To extend the search of non-canonical allergens, we also screened the genome with all of the allergens from both WHO/IUIS Allergen Nomenclature and AllergenOnline allergen databases. Finally, we predicted that there are 59 protein sequences that are highly similar with other species’ allergens. This number of predicted non-canonical allergens is significantly larger than that from the draft genome of D. farinae, of which the number is only 7. This is another evidence supporting the completeness of the D. pteronyssinus genome reported in this study. Objective 4 - To characterize allergen genes by immunological techniques For the analysis of allergens in D. farinae, MALDI-TOF MS analysis of protein spots reactive to pooled sera from 20 HDM-allergic patients with our integrated-omics approach revealed four known canonical allergens (Der f 1, Der f 2, Der f 11, and Der f 14) and 12 other proteins. Based on protein size and signal intensity, we selected 6 of these 12 for production of recombinant proteins for probing of allergenicity: UQCRB-like protein, myosin alkali light-chain protein, secreted inorganic pyrophosphatase, DFP2, cofilin, and ferritin heavy-chain-like protein. Only recombinant UQCRB-like protein was strongly bound by IgE in separate serum samples from 18/18 HDM-allergic individuals and not bound by IgE antibodies in sera obtained from any of 18 non-allergic healthy controls and 7 pollen-allergic patients. The other two recombinant proteins (cofilin and secreted inorganic pyrophosphatase) yielded very weak positive responses, while the remaining three recombinant proteins did not show any IgE-binding activities. The gene encoding the UQCRB-like protein was cloned and its gene structure was mapped. An IgE-ELISA demonstrated strong IgE-binding to recombinant UQCRB-like protein in 22 (100%) of 22 mite-allergic patients’ sera. In vivo testing showed skin reactivity in 5/10 mite-allergic patients (Table E12). This novel major allergen was designated as Der f 24 by the WHO/IUIS Allergen Nomenclature Sub-committee. Similar approach was used to analyze the allergens on in D. pteronyssinus. By using Coomassie Blue stained 2D gel, we successfully separated the HDM proteins. Their molecular weights ranged from 15 kDa to 100 kDa. The results of immunoblotting from the 2D gel showed that there were 64 protein spots in the total protein of the HDM bound by specific IgE in the sera of patients with HDM allergy, numbered 1-64 in the 2D gel. All 64 proteins underwent de novo peptide sequencing by MALDI-ToF MS, then the sequenced peptides were searched against our predicted genes. Among them, 55 allergens could be supported by RNA-Seq data. The recombinant proteins of Der p 25 to 33 were successfully expressed in Orgami-expressing bacteria and then purified by Ni2+ affinity chromatography with fast protein liquid chromatography. The allergenicity of the non-canonical allergens of Der p 25, 26, 28, 32, and 33 was detected by ELISA using 26 sera of HDM allergy patients and 4 normal human sera as negative control. The results showed that the IgE binding rates of Der p 25, 26, 28, 32, and 33 were 53.8%, 61.5%, 38.5%, 46.2%, and 65.3% respectively. Therefore, Der p 33 had the highest allergenicity among the novel canonical D. pteronyssinus allergens. Objective 5 - To identify the sequences and relative abundance of potential endosymbiotic microbes using the generated genome and transcriptome data Of the ~112k genomic sequencing reads that we linked to 100 microbial species, 71k (63.4%) mapped uniquely to Enterobacter species, most predominantly to Enterobacter cloacae and Enterobacter hormaechei; Staphylococcus (17.8%) and Escherichia (4.9%) were the next most predominant genera. Bartonella accounted for only 1.7% of the reads. Our IHC experiment confirmed the abundant presence of enterobacteria in the gut of D. farinae. We examined whether the genes encoding KEGG pathway enzymes were present in the D. farinae genome or its microbiome fraction and identified four pathways wherein the majority of genes were from the microbiome: thiamine biosynthesis, and aromatic and aliphatic amino acid biosynthesis. Additionally, by combining the DNA and RNA sequence information, we determined from our draft genome that an intron is present in the 13.8-kDa D. farinae bacteriolytic enzyme.

475113.label: Major findings and research outcome
475113.value: We would like to emphasize that our findings on dust mite genomes and transcriptomes provide novel insights for development of diagnosis and interventions for inhalant allergies. The first paper generated from this project titled “The draft genome, transcriptome, and microbiome of Dermatophagoides farinae reveal a broad spectrum of dust mite allergens” has been published in the Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology (IF = 12.485; ranks 1/21 in Allergy in 2015) (Reference 1). This work was selected as the Editors' choice and commented by an editorial (Reference 2). It was also highlighted as one of the major advances in mechanisms of allergic disease in 2015 (Reference 3). Although the preliminary data was sent to Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology for publication on 29 June 2013, it had gone through four rounds of revisions and the finally accepted on 26 September 2014. The funding from the GRF grant had made a big contribution during the revision of this manuscript since the commencement of the project on 1 December 2013. Regarding the genome and transcriptome analysis of D. pteronyssinus, the second paper was just accepted by the Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology (Reference 4). References 1. 475113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
475113.value: Because of our excellent deliverables generated from this project, another General Research Fund titled “Elucidating the allergen profile and its regulation mechanism in dust mites using single molecule real-time sequencing” has been recently funded by the Research Grants Council (Project No.: 14175617; Fund Amount: HK$785,393; Duration: November 2017 – October 2019). With this support, we plan to construct complete genomes of two dust mite species by the PacBio Sequel sequencing platform. Moreover, additional allergens and regulatory regions of allergens will be identified and investigated. We will also explore new areas of dust mite genomics, including the expression of allergens in different developmental stages, the importance of miRNA in the regulation of allergen genes, the transcription factor binding sites in promoters of allergen genes and the comparative genomics of D. pteronyssinus, Dermatophagoides farina and other mites with available genomes. Concerning the characterization of novel allergens, we will express these allergens in different model systems so as to obtain active allergens for characterization using patients’ samples and cell line models. At the right time, we will seek for major funding support from the Research Grants Council so that the dust mite allergen analysis could become a major research area in Hong Kong.

475113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
475113.value: In Hong Kong, the prevalence rate of asthma in Chinese school children is over 10%. Moreover, the prevalence has increased by three to four times over the past 20 years. House dust mite (HDM) allergy is a prevalent cause of allergic responses. The predominant species of dust mite in most geographical regions are Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus and Dermatophagoides farinae. Exposure to HDM allergens in atopic patients triggers inflammatory diseases including allergic asthma, perennial rhinitis and atopic dermatitis. In this study, the genomes of these two dust mite species have been constructed and analyzed. Using advanced molecular and genomic techniques, many new allergens were discovered and characterized. It is also notable that significant differences could be found in various aspects of these two species. Finally, we unveiled the microorganism profile in the gut of HDM. Such microbes are also potential allergens for future investigation. The deliverables of this study have been highly appreciated by the international research community. In conclusion, the resources generated in this study will provide will provide tools for further identification and characterization of HDM allergens and development of diagnostics and immunotherapeutic vaccines.

476013.label: Realisation of objectives
476013.value: This project’s major objective is to develop an automatic algorithm using breath mass spectrometry data to perform prediction on clinical parameters such as urea and creatinine for renal patients. We have successfully collected chronic kidney disease patients breath mass spectrometry data in Hong Kong, and for the first time, developed an algorithm using the complete range of 200 detected breath masses to perform prediction on blood level urea and creatinine. Since the breath sample is collected in an non-invasive way, the developed method offers a novel, convenient, and efficient way to measure renal functions. The algorithm uses iterative principle component analysis and lasso method to select important compounds from 200 simultaneously measured ion mass. Finally prediction was performed on independent data set and the error rate evaluated by mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) reached 30%. In another data set of dialysis patients, we used the developed algorithm to predict the subject’s blood level creatinine and urea. And the error rate ranged between 13.2% to 24.03%, depending on which precursor ion was used. The achieved results met the goal of algorithm development, independent data validation, as well as the clinical exploration of the possibilities of non-invasive measurement for kidney disease subjects through breath mass spectrometry. The results proved the concept of conducting non-invasive clinical measurement through breath mass spectrometry for renal disease subjects. The project also produced a software that can be applied with patients breath full-scanned mass. The algorithm solved several critical issues for accurate prediction: 1. It solves simultaneous compound selection from over 200 masses when the number of subjects is smaller than the number variables. The challenge is solved by using penalized linear regression method (lasso) and the principle component analysis (PCA). 2. The algorithm solves the problem of high inter-correlatedness among full-scanned masses via iteratively subtracting information through PCA and re-evaluate through the Variance inflation factor (VIF). 3. Through the identification of important variable subsets, the algorithm provides a solution to the challenge of making accurate predictions. The project also resulted in the gain of important experience in breath analysis technology. The SIFT-mass spectrometry machine was shipped from New Zealand to Hong Kong. We learnt the installation, calibration, precursor gas supply, breath sample collection, storage, and analysis techniques. We also generated local data set of breath mass spectrometry in Hong Kong for diabetic and renal patients. Worldwide, such breath full mass scanned data for medical application is very rare and precious. These data sets and the invaluable experience laid the foundation for future translational development and clinical application using the non-invasive breath scan. Accomplishment of this project requires the collaboration of a true interdisciplinary team. We have the help of Prof. Cheuk-Chun Szeto for providing the chemistry and engineering expertise for machine installation and calibration; we also collaborated with clinical doctors and scientist Prof. Juliana Chan and Prof. Anthony HY Chung for collecting patients sample and clinical parameters. We have professional bio-statistician who is capable of conducting advanced statistical analysis as well as using computer science languages. We also relied on clinical practice administered by nurses and clinicians to ensure the data quality and patients handling. The entire team gained knowledge from each other and together generate the new medical application using full-scanned data for clinical monitoring and prediction.

476013.label: Major findings and research outcome
476013.value: We have developed an automatic algorithm to analysis full-scan breath mass spectrometry data. The algorithm and applications produced one automatic software, one United States patent, one scholar article published in Journal of Breath Research (IF= 4.17, Ranking 9/58), and one article under review in the same journal. Through the analysis of kidney disease data, we identified the metabolites that can be used to predict blood level creatinine and urea, including isoprene (mass to charge ratio- m/z 68), acetylene (m/z 26), methional (m/z 104), trichlorobenzene (m/z 180), ethyl nonanoate (m/z 185). ammonia (m/z = 18,), methanol (m/z = 33), and ethanol (m/z = 47). Based on these findings and the developed algorithm, the project started the medical application of full-scanned mass spectrometry and proved the method of making accurate non-invasive measurement using breath samples.

476013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
476013.value: In future development, with enough funding, we can purchase a breath mass spectrometry machine with full mass scan capacity and placed it in collaboration labs. More samples can be collected, and we can monitor the status of a wide range of diseases through breath analysis, including gastroenteritis and diabetes. The patent granted secured the possibility of developing the software into a new commercial medical device, which is non-invasive, convenient and fast.

476013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
476013.value: This project provides a whole new angle of clinical measurement for kidney disease patients. Current measurement of blood level urea and creatinine for kidney patients is invasive. For subjects who need constant dialysis performed every week, it is inconvenient to measure the efficacy of dialysis - subjects often do not know the urea level before and after dialysis, and when dialysis is needed. We propose to use a new device, breath mass spectrometry to analyze the exhaled breath of subjects to measure the blood level parameters. The new method is non-invasive, convenient and fast. We successfully implemented the new device and applied the developed method on local kidney disease patients; the outcome was very effective. The new t method has the potential to assist medical testing and evaluation of patient status noninvasively in real time. It opens up a new direction of medical application through analyzing a wide range of breath masses collected from exhaled breath.

476113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
476113.value: Large portion of mammalian genome was thought to be “junk” regions while only ~3% are useful in coding proteins. However, recent efforts in high throughput analyses of the mouse and human genomes have revealed that these “junk” regions are transcribed into a wide variety of non-coding RNA (ncRNA) transcripts. Long ncRNAs (>200nt in length, lncRNAs) are emerging as potent regulators of gene expression. Among them, large intergenic ncRNAs (lincRNAs) have become the focus of attention since its initial discovery in 2009. Spurring efforts have been made to identify and characterize their functions in various cells and tissues. However, it was not know whether lincRNAs are involved in skeletal muscle stem cell differentiation or myogenesis. Here we describe de novo discovery of a novel lincRNA through analyzing a combination of genome-wide chromatin mapping and transcriptome sequencing data. It appears to be transcribed from the bi-directional promoter of Yin Yang 1 (YY1) gene, thus named linc-YY1. We previously showed that YY1 is a transcription factor which silences several muscle genes and muscle relevant miRNAs epigenetically by recruiting Ezh2 containing Polycomb repressive complex (PRC2) to target promoters. Disruption of YY1 involved regulation contributes to muscle diseases such as Rhabdomyosarcoma and Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Strikingly, the temporal and spatial expression of linc-YY1 is highly coordinated with YY1 gene and itself regulated by myogenic regulator, MyoD, suggesting that it is likely a functional component of myogenic regulatory network. Consistently, knockdown of linc-YY1 in C2C12 myoblast cells by siRNA inhibited differentiation, leading us to hypothesize that it acts as a pro-myogenic factor. Further studies suggested that linc-YY1 may interact and evict YY1/PRC2 repressive complex from the target gene promoters leading to gene activation. To test the above hypothesis, four objectives are proposed which aim to discover a novel mechanism underlying the role of linc-YY1 in skeletal muscle cell differentiation and muscle regeneration in vivo. The resultant findings from this study will shed a light on the involvement of lincRNA in skeletal muscle development and identify a novel mechanism of gene regulation by lncRNAs. In the long run, this will also be helpful in understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying muscle related diseases. 在过去10年中，大量高通量基因组学平台的研究数据显示在哺乳动物的基因组中只有不到3%的序列是用来编码蛋白质的，而大量非蛋白编码序列能够转录生成不同类型的非编码RNA（ncRNAs）。有越来越多的研究数据显示ncRNA对基因组的表达调控具有重要作用。lncRNA中有一类是从基因间序列转录生成的，被称为长链基因间非编码RNA（large intergenic non-coding RNA, lincRNA）。自从2009年被发现以来，lincRNA已经成为生物医学领域研究的热点。但是lincRNA在骨骼肌干细胞分化和肌肉发育再生中的功能尚是一个空白。在这一课题中我们将研究linc-YY1在骨骼肌中的重要功能。Linc-YY1是从yy1基因的启动子区域生成。Yin Yang 1 (YY1) 是一个广泛表达的转录因子，在肌细胞分化过程中能抑制肌肉特异基因和miR-29的表达，从而起到抑制分化的作用。在成肌细胞中，YY1能结合在肌肉特异基因和miR-29的启动子区域并招募含有甲基转移酶Ezh2的抑制复合体（Polycomb Repressive Complex, PRC）和组蛋白去乙酰化蛋白HDAC1，造成靶基因启动子区域的组蛋白H3第二十七赖氨酸甲基化(H3K27me3)，从而抑制靶基因的转录。Yy1 功能的干扰会造成肌肉疾病的形成。根据预实验结果我们认为Linc-YY1可以与yy1 相互作用从而调侃其转录活性。为了验证这一假想，我们将在本课题中验证四个具体目标。如果成功，我们的结果将揭示lincRNA作用的新的分子机理。从长远而说，我们的结果为理解肌肉相关疾病的分子机理提供重要依据。

476113.label: Realisation of objectives
476113.value: In the original proposal we hypothesized that linc-YY1 represents a novel lncRNA which functions to promote skeletal myogenesis through modulating the activity of TF and epigenetic modifier. To test this hypothesis four specific aims/objectives are proposed. We are pleased to report that all four aims have been successfully implemented with favorable outcomes. Aim 1: To determine the temporal expression of linc-YY1 during myogenesis both in vitro and in vivo. We assessed its expression in various myogenesis settings. First, during differentiation of C2C12 cells, low expression of Linc-YY1 was detected in proliferating myoblasts at 50% confluence (-24hr). A significant increase was observed when the confluence reached 70-80% (0d). The expression continuously increased up to 48hrs which was then followed by a gradual decline in the late stages (96hr and 144 hr). Consistently, during the differentiation of freshly isolated satellite cells (SCs), Linc-YY1 expression significantly increased in the early stage . To further examine its expression dynamics in vivo, we employed a widely-used muscle regeneration model in which the injection of cardiotoxin (CTX) results in muscle injury and in turn induces muscle regeneration. The expression of Linc-YY1 was found to be rapidly induced starting day 1 and peaked around day 2. Consistently, higher levels of Linc-YY1 were detected in dystrophic muscles of young mdx mice (3 and 5 week) which were featured by a pathologically active degeneration-regeneration; this was not observed in limb muscles from normal wild type mice or older mdx mice (>6 week) in which the disease phenotype has subdued. Moreover, high level of Linc-YY1 was observed in limb muscles of newborn mice (age 3d, 5d and 2week) which displayed active myogenesis but decreased as the neonatal myogenesis ceased after about two weeks. The above results suggested that Linc-YY1 is associated with active myogenesis. Aim 2: To clone and characterize linc-YY1 gene. To this end, we cloned it using Rapid Amplification of cDNA Ends (RACE) which led to an 1173 nt transcript possessing a polyadenylation site; its transcriptional start site is 2,103 bp away from the first exon of YY1 and indeed generated from the opposite strand. The size was confirmed by northern blotting assay. RNA-Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (RNA-FISH) detection revealed it mainly resides in the nuclei of C2C12 myoblasts and myotubes, similar to small nuclear transcript U1. This was confirmed by cellular fractionation assay. A high enrichment of Linc-YY1 transcripts was found in nuclear extracts. Consistent with the prediction using our in-house iSeeRNA software, Linc-YY1 is predicted as non-coding by two other publicly available programs, which was confirmed by results from in vitro translation assay. Aim 3: To dissect the role of linc-YY1 in skeletal muscle cell differentiation and muscle regeneration. The early induction of Linc-YY1 during C2C12 differentiation suggested to us that it may be a pro-myogenic factor during myoblast differentiation. To test this notion, we employed loss- and gain-of-function assays. Successful knock-down of Linc-YY1 led to a delayed differentiation. Stable knockdown of Linc-YY1 using a shRNA also delayed the myogenic program over a course of 6 days. These findings confirmed that Linc-YY1 is a pro-myogenic factor during C2C12 differentiation. To strengthen the above findings, Linc-YY1 over-expression was found to accelerate the differentiation of C2C12 cells as assessed using multiple approaches as above. To extend our findings in C2C12 cells to a more physiologically relevant setting, we tested the function of Linc-YY1 in freshly isolated satellite cells. In keeping with its pro-myogenic function in C2C12 cells, knock-down of Linc-YY1 by siRNA oligos impaired myogenic differentiation of the cells whereas over-expression of Linc-YY1 improved their differentiation. These findings were further confirmed on satellite cells associated with freshly isolated single myofibers which serve as an excellent ex vivo model. Knock-down or over-expression of Linc-YY1 on the myofibers led to an inhibition or enhancement of satellite cell activities as assessed by both Myogenin and Pax7 staining. Furthermore, Treatment of regenerating muscles with siLinc-YY1 oligos led to down-regulation of Pax7, MyoD, Myogenin and embryonic-MyHC (e-MyHC, a marker for regenerating fibers) at both mRNA and protein levels. Altogether our results suggested that Linc-YY1 is a functional pro-myogenic factor in muscle satellite cells and during muscle regeneration in vivo. Aim 4: To explore the mechanisms underlying the pro-myogenic function of linc-YY1. Next, we probed into the molecular mechanisms underlying the promoting role of Linc-YY1 in myogenesis. We first tested the possibility of Linc-YY1 directly regulating YY1 transcription. Manipulation of Linc-YY1 levels by siRNA or over-expression in C2C12 cells resulted in only a modest change of YY1 mRNA or protein; it also did not modulate the levels of PRC2 components. However, since it inhibited the transcription of several known direct targets of YY1, all of which are co-regulated by PRC2, we speculated that instead of acting in cis, Linc-YY1 could bind with YY1/PRC2 complex to antagonize its transcriptional activity on these muscle loci in trans. To test this hypothesis, we performed RNA-immunoprecipitation (RIP) assay. Expectedly, IP of YY1, Ezh2 or EED from proliferating C2C12 myoblasts at 80-90% confluence (MBs) or early differentiating myotubes (MTs) pulled down significant amount of Linc-YY1. To further determine the specific interacting protein partner, we performed RNA pull down assay from native non-crosslinked cell lysates using biotinylated in vitro synthesized RNA. Contrary to our original thought that Linc-YY1 may bind to PRC2 like many other lincRNAs, the full length Linc-YY1 retrieved no Ezh2 or Suz12 and very low level of EED; however, it retrieved a substantial amount of YY1, suggesting that Linc-YY1 specifically binds with YY1. To further map the binding domain, we found that the middle domain most likely contains functional structures. Indeed, at the functional level over-expression of the middle domain but not the other two domains recapitulated the full length function, leading to the increase of YY1/PRC2 target gene expression. The above results led us to further hypothesize that Linc-YY1 binds to YY1/PRC2 repressive complex upon early differentiation, leading to its eviction from chromatins and subsequent de-repression of the previously known YY1/PRC2 co-regulated targets. To test this notion, we performed ChIP assays using chromatins from Vector or Linc-YY1 over-expressing C2C12 cells collected at 0, 24 and 48hr of differentiation. The association of YY1/PRC2 with several previously known target promoters, the enrichment of YY1/PRC2 was very high in proliferating C2C12 myoblasts and gradually declined during the myogenic differentiation from day 1 to day 2. Indeed, the over-expression of Linc-YY1 caused concurrent loss of YY1, Ezh2, Eed and Suz12 binding at all three time points on all the three promoters examined. These results suggested that ectopic expression of Linc-YY1 could evict YY1/PRC2 complex from the known target promoters, confirming its in trans function. To further answer the question how Linc-YY1 removes YY1/PRC2 complex from the target promoters, we found that expression of Linc-YY1 hampered the interaction between endogenous YY1 and Ezh2 proteins using Co-Immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) assay. Furthermore, using Chromatin Isolation by RNA Purification (ChIRP) assay, we were able to specifically retrieve substantial amount of endogenous Linc-YY1 transcripts from the target loci. Altogether the above findings provided compelling evidence to support the notion that on the known target genes Linc-YY1 functions through antagonizing YY1/PCR2 transcriptional activities in trans.

476113.label: Major findings and research outcome
476113.value: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) are transcriptional units with no protein-coding potential and emerging as potent regulators of gene expression. This study was undertaken to investigate the function of an ncRNA, Linc-YY1 in skeletal myogenesis. In the original proposal, we hypothesize that linc-YY1 represents a novel lncRNA which functions to promote skeletal myogenesis through modulating the activity of TF and epigenetic modifier. To test this hypothesis four specific aims/objectives are proposed. We have now completed all the proposed work. Our findings support the original hypothesis that Linc-YY1 is a functional non-coding RNA in skeletal myogenesis. A paper including all the findings “Linc-YY1 promotes myogenic differentiation and muscle regeneration through an interaction with the transcription factor YY1” is published on Nat Commun. 2015 (PartC8). In this paper we describe the discovery of Linc-YY1 from the promoter of the transcription factor (TF) Yin Yang 1 (YY1) gene. We demonstrate that Linc-YY1 is dynamically regulated during myogenesis in vitro and in vivo. Gain or loss of function of Linc-YY1 in C2C12 myoblasts or satellite cells alters myogenic differentiation and in injured muscles impacts the course of regeneration. Linc-YY1 may interact with YY1 through its middle domain to evict YY1/Polycomb repressive complex (PRC2) from target promoters, thus activating the gene expression in trans. In addition, Linc-YY1 also regulates PRC2-independent function of YY1. Finally, we identify a human Linc-YY1 ortholog with conserved function and show that many human and mouse TF genes are associated with lincRNAs that may modulate their activity. Altogether, we show that Linc-YY1 regulates skeletal myogenesis and uncover a previously unappreciated mechanism of gene regulation by lincRNA. In addition, a total of 9 publications have been generated with this funding acknowledged (PartC8). Our findings were highly received when presented in international and local conferences/seminars (PartC9). One Postdoc Fellow, Dr. Liang Zhou was trained under the support of this grant and he is now an Associate Professor at Southern Medical University, China. Two PhD students, Dr. Yu Zhao and Dr. Kun Sun, were also trained under the grant. Dr. Zhao obtained his PhD at 2015 and is now a Postdoctoral Fellow at Chinese University of Hong Kong. Dr. Sun obtained his PhD at 2014 and is now a Research Assistant Professor at CUHK (PartC10). Through this work, we have also developed active collaboration with scientists from China, Prof. Miguel Esteban and Prof. Ralf Jauch (PartC11).

476113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
476113.value: Research from our study not only increases our knowledge in the field of lncRNAs particularly divergently transcribed lincRNAs, but also enhances our understanding of molecular regulation in skeletal muscle stem cell behavior and skeletal muscle development. This may eventually lead to the identification of novel therapeutic targets for muscle relevant disease such as muscular dystrophy and Rhabdomyosarcoma. In the future, to further these findings, we plan to continue the investigation of lncRNAs in the muscle cells. (1) The research will be expanded beyond the myoblast differentiation to include the entire lineage progression of muscle stem cell during regeneration. (2) To further examine the interplay between lncRNAs and transcription factors in myogenesis.

476113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
476113.value: Large portion of mammalian genome was thought to be “junk” regions while only ~3% are useful in coding proteins. However, recent efforts in high throughput analyses of the genomes have revealed that these “junk” regions are transcribed into a wide variety of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs). Long ncRNAs (>200nt in length, lncRNAs) are emerging as potent regulators of gene expression. Defects in lncRNAs could lead to the development of many human diseases while the underlying mechanisms are largely unknown. Thus, lncRNAs are considered as the new frontier of biomedical research. Here in this project we for the first time identified and characterized the function role of a novel lncRNA, Linc-YY1, in skeletal muscle cell and muscle regeneration process. In the long run, we hope this will serve as a starting point for the development of new therapeutic approaches for treating muscle related human diseases.

476313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
476313.value: 非酒精性脂肪肝疾病有两种自然病程。第一种形式是单纯性脂肪肝 (SS) ，它遵循一个良性的过程。第二种形式的脂肪性肝病为非酒精性脂肪性肝炎(NASH) . NASH是一个潜在的严重状况，可以导致肝硬化，终端肝功能衰竭，肝癌。除脂肪肝外，NASH还伴有肝脏炎症和纤维化。区分NASH从SS 非常重要。目前肝活检是诊断NASH的唯一可靠的方法。然而这是一个创伤性的手段，也是一个主观的过程，受抽样误差的影响。常规MR成像可用于评估脂肪肝，但是不能帮助区分NASH和SS 。新的成像技术，如磁共振弹性成像、声辐射力脉冲成像、磁共振波谱等展现了检测肝纤维化的可能性，并在某些情况下检测脂肪性肝炎。然而，这些成像技术尚未确立区分NASH和SS 。 需要无创性和可靠的方法是区分SS和NASH 。我们最近的研究表明T1rho磁共振可以敏感地评估 胆导管结扎诱导的大鼠模型肝纤维化模型以及四氯化碳诱导的肝纤维化大鼠模型。肝脏胶原蛋白水平与肝的T1rho值增加相关。四氯化碳中毒的急性肝脏炎症可以在没有明显的纤维化时引起轻度T1rho的松弛时间增加。我们最近的健康志愿者的研究表明健康志愿者的肝T1rho值是一致，初步的临床数据表明肝硬化患者肝T1rho值增加。MR T1rho成像是一种非侵入性的技术。它不涉及注入造影剂或外部设备。然而， T1rho MRI区分SS 和NASH的作用纳什还没有被研究。 本研究旨在探讨是否T1rho核磁共振加以磁共振波谱辅助能区分SS和NASH。三个动物模型将被用于此项研究，包括：1) CCl4诱导肝硬化部分性恢复模型， 2)大鼠肝SS模型，和3)不同阶段的大鼠肝NASH模型。磁共振波谱将被用于评估肝脏脂肪含量。T1rho结果将与1 )肝组织学评分; 2)肝组织形态学措施; 3)肝脏胶原水平相比。 这项研究的结果为进一步探索成像生物标志物来区分SS和NASH 将是至关重要的。T1rho磁共振将可能成为全面的成像技术参数之一用于非侵入性的肝脏评估，因此临床实践意义重大。

476313.label: Realisation of objectives
476313.value: Together with colleague Dr Weitian Chen, a new T1rho imaging method was developed to realize the aim of this research. This new single-breath black blood T1rho imaging method allow 6-spin lock times (TSL) to be acquired in a single-breath hold of 12 seconds which removes the usual problem of residual respiratory motion even when respiratory gating is applied. This method also uses the black blood effect of 2D fast spin echo (FSE) sequence and double inversion recovery to achieve blood signal suppression. It substantially improved the liver T1rho measurement accuracy, so much so that we were able to demonstrate that the female liver T1rho value ranges between 35.07 and 51.97 ms and showed an age-dependent decrease, with younger women having a higher measurement; while the male liver T1rho value ranged between 34.94 and 43.39 ms, with no evidential age dependence. Postmenopausal women had similar liver T1rho values as men. For women, there was a trend that the liver T1rho value could be 4% to 5% lower during the menstrual phase than during the non-menstrual phase. In an animal based study with male rat biliary duct ligation (BDL) induced liver fibrosis, we were able to demonstrate that for young male rats (200–250 g) the physiological liver T1rho value was 38.38 ± 1.53 ms (range, 36.05-41.53 ms), which is similar to the human data obtained in our study (9.16 ± 2.31 ms; range, 34.94–43.39 ms). Liver T1rho value elevated progressively after BDL. On day-10 after BDL all experimental animals can be separated from normal liver based on T1rho measurement with lowest value being 42.82 msec. Day-7 and day-10 liver resembled METAVIR stage-F1/F2 fibrosis, and fibrous area counted for 0.22%±0.13% and 0.38%±0.44% of liver parenchyma area, respectively. Therefore this study provides the proof-of-principle that T1rho might diagnose early stage liver fibrosis. To assess the pathology detection sensitivity, additionally we evaluated a variant of T1rho method termed Chemical Exchange Saturation Transfer (CEST). In a human study we found that CEST imaging was able to detect the liver biochemical composition changes of after-meal status vs. over-night-fast status, thus highlighting the sensitivity of this method. In a rat experimental study, we also found that CEST T1rho imaging was able to demonstrate liver CEST measurement (APTw and GlycoCEST signals) decrease after 24 hours-fasting. Additionally, when rat liver intoxication was induced by a single intraperitoneal injection of 1 ml kg−1 body weight CCl4 and scanned before and 48 hours after CCl4 administration, rat liver APTw and GlycoCEST signals decreased from 2.46 ± 0.48 % to 1.10 ± 0.77 %, and from 0.34 ± 0.23 % to -0.16 ± 0.51 % respectively. We analyzed that while elevated T1rho was correlated with the amount of collagen deposition in biliary duct ligation induced liver fibrosis, fiber tissue is not necessarily associated with higher T1rho inherently, as shown in intervertebral disc degeneration studies. Liver fibrosis, depending on its causes, is associated with a number of complicated pathological processes, including steatosis, hepatocellular ballooning, and inflammation. Inflammation involves presence of inflammatory cells, including lymphocytes, eosinophils and neutrophils, near ballooned hepatocytes. These processes may potentially contribute to the elevated T1rho measurement. We noted that acute edema of liver caused by CCl4 intoxication was not a dominant contributor of T1rho increase. After the withdrawal of CCl4 stimulus, the lowering of elevated liver T1rho was faster than the resolve of fiber tissue deposition in rat liver. Our hypothesis and theory have been substantiated by two recent studies by independent authors. In a study by Xie et al (Korean J Radiol 2017;18:898-905), 18 healthy subjects, 18 patients with fatty liver, and 18 patients with liver fibrosis had T1rho MR imaging performed. Mean liver T1rho values in fibrotic group (52.6±6.8 ms) were significantly higher than those of healthy subjects (44.9±2.8 ms, P<0.001) and fatty liver group (45.0±3.5 ms, P<0.001), while mean liver T1rho values were similar between healthy subjects and fatty liver group. Xie et al’s results and our results jointly suggest that T1rho can differentiate liver steatosis (no T1rho elevation with fat suppressed sequence) from steatohepatitis (with T1rho elevation due to inflammation and fibrosis). In a rabbit experimental study reported by Xie Y at al (Magn Reson Imaging. 2018 May;48:34-41), non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) rabbit models was induced by feeding a varied duration of high-fat high-cholesterol diet. In addition to plain T1rho imaging, a contrast enhanced T1rho was obtained 20min after administration of contrast agent Gd-EOB-DTPA. Their results demonstrated that plain T1rho and contrast enhanced T1rho have strong association with NASH overall activity, and contrast enhanced T1rho is strongly relevant to inflammation stage. Particularly, in their model it was demonstrated contrast enhanced T1rho allow differentiation between (a) NAFLD without NASH and (b) NASH.
