476313.value: 1. To overcome the usual problem of T1rho imaging, a single breathhold black-blood imaging was developed and validated in animal liver fibrosis model and healthy human studies. This method is clinically applicable and improve measurement accuracy/reproductivity (Quant Imaging Med Surg. 2016;6(2):168-77. Quant Imaging Med Surg. 2016;6(4):353-363. SLAS Technol. 2018;23(2):179-187. Acta Radiol. 2018;59(3):257-265). 2. Physiological liver T1rho ranges have been established. The age- and gender- dependence of liver T1rho was noted (Acta Radiol. 2018;59(3):257-265/ . SLAS Technol. 2018;23(2):179-187) 3. Animal model demonstrates T1rho imaging can detect early stage (stage -1) liver fibrosis (Quant Imaging Med Surg. 2016;6(4):353-363). 4. 476313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
476313.value: 1. the contrast mechanism of T1rho for liver fibrosis has not been fully understood, this will require further studies. 2. though preliminary proof of concept studies have shown that T1rho ( and contrast enhanced T1rho) allow differentiation between liver steatosis (no T1rho elevation with fat suppressed sequence) from steatohepatitis (with T1rho elevation due to inflammation and fibrosis), further studies, particularly clinical studies, are require to confirm the initial reports. 3. further technical improvement T1rho measurement is undergoing (by colleague Dr Weitian Chen). 4. A parametric approach, such a combination with other quantitative imaging such as IVIM (Intravoxel incoherent motion), should be further explored.

476313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
476313.value: To date, noninvasive diagnostic tests available from clinical practice are not sensitive or specific enough to detect occult liver injury at an early stage. Liver biopsy is currently the standard of reference for the diagnosis and staging of liver fibrosis. However, it is an invasive procedure with several contraindications and with a risk of complications. A noninvasive and quantitative technique for detecting liver fibrosis is highly desirable. In this study, together with collaborators we developed a single breathhold black-blood T1rho imaging which is clinically applicable and improve measurement accuracy/reproductivity. We established the physiological liver T1rho ranges in general population. It is shown demonstrated that T1rho imaging can detect early stage liver fibrosis, and may allow differentiation between liver steatosis from steatohepatitis. The results obtain in this study is important for developing T1rho as a clinical tool for noninvasive assessment of early liver fibrosis.

476813.label: Project Objectives
476813.value: The objective of this experimental pathology and immunology research proposal is to elucidate the immunopathological and intracellular signal transduction mechanisms mediating the activation of basophils and dermal fibroblasts by ligands for TLR2 [Pam3Cys, PGN and LTA from S. aureus, heat killed S. aureus] and NLR member NOD2 [N-acetylmuramyl-L-alanyl-D-isoglutamine (muramyl dipeptide/MDP)]. The project will study the following in the co-culture of primary human peripheral blood basophils and dermal fibroblasts. The effects of Pam3Cys, PGN, LTA, heat killed S. aureus or MDP together with or without the dermal fibroblasts-derived and basophil-activating cytokine IL-33, on (i) the production of the essential AD-related inflammatory cytokines IL-1beta, IL-6 and IL-22, TSLP for Th2-related dendritic cells and AD-related chemokines CXCL8 and CXCL1 for neutrophils, CCL2 for monocytes, mast cells, basophils, eosinophils, CCL17 and CCL22 for Th2 cells, CCL27 and CCL18 for cutaneous lymphocyte antigen (CLA)+ T cells (ii) the production of skin-antimicrobial peptide beta-defensin-2 (BD-2) (iii) the cell surface expression of adhesion molecules such as intercellular adhesion molecule (ICAM)-1, vascular cell adhesion molecule (VCAM)-1, L-selectin, Mac-1 (CD11b) on basophils and dermal fibroblasts (iv) the adhesion of basophils onto dermal fibroblasts and (v) the basophilic degranulation for the release of histamine and superoxides. The relationship between TLR ligands and MDP mediated the activation of essential intracellular signaling molecules [extracellular signal-regulated protein kinase (ERK), c-Jun amino-terminal kinase (JNK), p38 mitogen activated protein kinase (p38 MAPK), Janus kinase-signal transducer and activator of transcription factor (JAK-STAT) and phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)-AKT and transcription factor nuclear factor-kappaB (NF-kappaB)] with the expression of cytokines, chemokines and adhesion molecules, adhesion and degranulation will be investigated. The difference in the plasma level of soluble basophil granular protein basogranulin, basophil activation upon allergen challenge, cell surface expression of TLR2 and cytosolic expression of NOD2 of peripheral basophils between AD patients and sex- and age-matched, non-allergic, normal control subjects will be investigated and compared. The AD and normal control mice will be set up for studies of (i) the ear thickness, quantitation of serum basogranulin and AD-related cytokines and chemokines (ii) the effect on ear thickness, serum level of basogranulin, cytokines and chemokines by the depletion of basophils with the treatment of specific basophil-depletion antibody (Ba103), followed by the in vivo activation with TLR2 and NOD2 ligands.

476813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
476813.value: Aim The aim of this study is to elucidate Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus)-initiated immunopathological and signal transduction mechanisms regulating toll-like receptor (TLR)2 and the nucleotide binding oligomerization domain (NOD)2-mediated activation of human basophils, the crucial effector cells for allergic inflammation by interacting with dermal fibroblasts in atopic dermatitis (AD). Project Background AD is a widely prevalent and chronically relapsing inflammatory skin disease that affects nearly 20 % of Hong Kong schoolchildren. Basophil infiltration into the skin lesions is a characteristic feature of AD. Bacterial skin infection caused by S. aureus associates with the chronic inflammation and morbidity in AD. TLR2 and NOD like receptors (NLR) are key pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) mediating inflammatory and innate immune responses by recognizing bacterial conserved molecular structure. TLR2 sensing bacterial peptidylglycans and NLR family member NOD2 sensing the muramyl dipeptide of S. aureus, together play immunopathological roles in AD. We have demonstrated the putative role of TLR in the activation of eosinophils, the interaction of eosinophils with epidermal keratinocytes, and basophils interacting with bronchial epithelial cells in allergic inflammation. However, the basophil function in AD has not been well elucidated. Brief Project Description We hypothesize that TLR2 and NOD2 are crucial PRRs of allergic inflammation in AD linking the S. aureus-mediated innate immune response with the subsequent allergic inflammation through the activation of basophils and dermal fibroblasts. The primary objective of this proposal is to elucidate intracellular signal transduction mechanisms mediating the activation of the co-culture of primary peripheral blood basophils and dermal fibroblast by ligands for TLR2 and NOD2 in term of the production of AD-related inflammatory cytokines and chemokines, anti-bacterial beta-defensin-2, cell surface expression of adhesion molecules, intercellular interaction and the induction of basophilic degranulation. Both clinical and animal translational studies will be used to confirm basophil-related TLR2 and NOD2-mediated inflammation in AD. We believe that the valuable experience we have gained over the past decade in this research area provides a firm basis for this study. Significance of Project The study is expected to identify the unique intracellular mechanisms for the S. aureus infection-mediated activation of basophils upon its interaction with dermal fibroblasts in allergic inflammation of AD, and should advance our knowledge of the immunopathological mechanisms by which infection-mediated basophil activation can trigger allergic inflammation. Its results should furnish a biochemical basis for the development of therapeutic intervention such as antibody blocking TLR2 and oligodeoxynucleotides targeting NOD2 for AD treatment. 目的： 這項研究的目的是爲了闡明金黃色葡萄球菌（金葡菌）所引起的信號轉導和免疫病理機制。即在特應性皮炎(AD)中， toll樣受體(TLR)2和核苷酸結合寡聚化結構域(NOD)2所介導的人嗜鹼性粒細胞的活化調控。在過敏性炎症中，嗜鹼性粒細胞是能與皮膚成纖維細胞發生相互作用的關鍵效應細胞。 項目背景： AD是一種廣泛流行的慢性復發性皮膚炎症，影響近20%的香港學生。嗜鹼性粒細胞浸潤到皮膚病灶是AD的特徵之一。慢性皮膚炎症和AD的發病率與金黃色葡萄球菌所引起的細菌性皮膚感染有關。TLR2和NOD樣受體(NLR)是重要的模式識別受體(PRRS)；它們通過識別細菌保守的分子結構來介導炎症和先天性免疫反應。 TLR2能識別細菌的肽聚醣，同時NLR家庭成員NOD2能識別金黃色葡萄球菌的胞壁酰二肽，在AD中兩者共同發揮免疫病理作用。我們之前已證明了TLR在過敏性炎症中的作用，如激活嗜酸性粒細胞，參與表皮角質化細胞與嗜酸性粒細胞的相互作用，以及參與嗜鹼性粒細胞與支氣管上皮細胞的相互作用。但是，在AD中嗜鹼性粒細胞的功能還不完全清楚。 項目簡介： 通過關聯金黃色葡萄球菌介導的先天免疫反應和後天激活嗜鹼性粒細胞和皮膚成纖維細胞的過敏性炎症，我們推測，在AD中TLR2和NOD2是至關重要的過敏性炎症模式識別受體。這方案的主要目的是爲了闡明，通過TLR2和NOD2配體介導外周血嗜鹼性粒細胞和皮膚成纖維細胞的共培養環境中的細胞內信號轉導的機制，從而調控AD相關的炎性細胞因子和趨化因子釋放，抗細菌β-防禦素-2釋放，細胞表面粘附分子的表達，細胞間的相互作用以及誘導嗜鹼性細胞脫顆粒。另外, 臨床和動物研究將進一步用於確定嗜鹼性粒細胞相關的TLR2和NOD2所介導的AD炎症反應。我們相信，在過去的十年中，我們在這一研究領域所獲得的寶貴經驗，將為這項研究提供了堅實的基礎。 項目的意義： 通過這項研究期望能解釋這一獨特的胞內機制，即由金黃色葡萄球菌感染介導，並能與皮膚成纖維細胞發生相互作用的嗜鹼性粒細胞的激活，從而觸發AD中的過敏性炎症；同時還能夠使人們深入認識感染介導嗜鹼粒細胞的激活而引發過敏性炎症的免疫病理機制。這研究的結果也提供了一種生化基礎, 從而幫助發展新的AD治療方案，例如利用抗體阻斷TLR2和寡核苷酸靶向NOD2來治療AD。

476813.label: Realisation of objectives
476813.value: (1) We have established the co-culture of human granulocyte basophils and eosinophils, the principal immune effector cells in allergic inflammation, with human primary dermal fibroblasts upon the activation by TLR2 ligand peptidoglycan (PGN), Lipoteichoic acid (LTA) and Pam3CSK4 (Pam), and NOD2 ligand (muramyl dipeptide/MDP). We first confirmed that human basophils, eosinophils and dermal fibroblasts constitutively expressed NOD2 (intracellularly) and TLR2 (cell surface), facilitating the efficient detection of S. aureus by these innate cells. We then found that large amounts of AD-related CXCL8, CCL2 and CCL5 were released from the co-cultured human basophils and dermal fibroblasts in the presence of S. aureus-associated NOD2/TLR2 ligands. Significant up-regulation of ICAM-1 expression on dermal fibroblasts was observed under the stimulation by NOD2/TLR2 ligands in basophil-fibroblast co-culture. Similarly, human eosinophils co-cultured with dermal fibroblasts were shown to release larger amounts of AD-related IL-6, CXCL8 and CCL4 in the presence of NOD2/TLR2 ligands, and express higher level of ICAM-1 on dermal fibroblasts. Moreover, it was found that heat-killed S. aureus (HKSA), the intact bacteria mainly recognized by TLR2, enhanced the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines/chemokines and the expression of ICAM-1 on dermal fibroblasts in both basophil- and eosinophil-dermal fibroblast co-cultures. To address the intracellular signal transduction pathways for NOD2/TLR2-stimulated activation of human baosphils, eosinophils and dermal fibroblasts, p38-MAPK inhibitor SB203580 and NF-κB inhibitor BAY11-7082 significantly suppressed the NOD2/TLR2 ligands-induced release of CXCL8, CCL2 and CCL5 in basophils co-cultured with dermal fibroblasts, as well as the increased expression of ICAM-1 on dermal fibroblasts. Results therefore suggested that p38-MAPK and NF-κB, were essential for NOD2/TLR2-mediated activation of basophils and fibroblasts. On the other hand, instead of PI3K-AKT inhibitor LY294002 and JNK inhibitor SP600125, SB203580, ERK inhibitor U0126 and BAY11-7082 extensively suppressed the release of cytokines/chemokines and the increased ICAM-1 expression on dermal fibroblasts in eosinophil-fibroblast co-culture, indicating that other than p38-MAPK and NF-κB, ERK also played an important role in NOD2/TLR2 ligands-induced activation of eosinophils co-cultured with dermal fibroblasts. Moreover, using bead-based multiplex assays, we observed elevated phosphorylated p38-MAPK (pp38-MAPK) and phosphorylated IκBα (pIκBα) in cell lysates of KU812 cells (a human basophilic cell line) and dermal fibroblasts in co-culture 10 minutes after the stimulation of NOD2/TLR2 ligands. Likewise, significantly increased pp38-MAPK, pIκBα and phosphorylated ERK (pERK) were detected in eosinophils and dermal fibroblasts in co-culture in the presence of NOD2/TLR2 ligands (Cell Mol Immunol 2016; 13: 535-550). (2) We have established the AD-liked mice model using inbred female BALB/c mice (8-week-old and 20 g weight). 2 nmol MC903 (Sigma-Aldrich Corp, St. Louis, MO, USA) in 5μl ethanol was topically applied to mice ears every other day for 14 days (Day 0 to 14, 8 times in total). Ear thickness was measured using a dial thickness gauge (Model G, Peacock, OZAKI MFG. CO., LTD, Tokyo, Japan) and recorded every other day for 16 days. Photographs of mice ears were taken on Day 16, followed by the sacrifice of mice and histological analysis of AD-skin lesions. In certain experiments, 10 μg S. aureus-associated NOD2 ligand MDP and TLR2 ligands PGN, LTA and Pam (Invivogen, San Diego, CA USA) in ethanol were also topically administered either separately or together with MC903 (2 nmol) to mice ears. Results showed that topical MC903 on the ears for 14 days induced tissue swelling, epidermal thickening, and eosinophils infiltration in the dermis layer. Strikingly, topical application of NOD2/TLR2 ligands together with the AD-inducing agent MC903 further deteriorated the AD-like symptoms, including enhanced ear swelling, more extensive epidermal thickening, and larger number of eosinophils present in the dermal layer. NOD2/TLR2 ligands treatment alone had no effects in the absence of MC903, suggesting that the deteriorating effects of NOD2/TLR2 ligands might only occur in the pre-established skin lesions wherein epidermal barrier functions were disturbed. We found that topical S. aureus-associated NOD2/TLR2 ligands further led to epidermal infiltration of eosinophils in our AD-like mouse model induced by MC903. IL-3 complex (IL-3C), a basophil-expansion agent, intraperitoneal (i.p.) treatments for 14 days significantly increased the proportions of FcεRIα+CD49b+ basophils in peripheral blood, spleen and bone marrow, as well as the blood cell counts of basophils. Meanwhile, IL-3C treatments also enhanced eosinophil pool sizes, as increased ratios of eosinophils were observed in all examined organs and systems. Significantly increased eosinophil counts were likewise found in peripheral blood. Nevertheless, IL-3C did not affect the cellular pool sizes of neutrophils, monocytes, CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cells and B cells, as well as skin/peritoneal mast cells, which confirmed the high specificity for IL-3C-mediated expansion of basophils and eosinophils. IL-3C treatments were found to deteriorate MC903-induced AD, as validated by enhanced ear swelling, more extensive epidermal thickening, and an increased number of eosinophils present in the epidermal/dermal layer. When IL-3C together with topical NOD2/TLR2 ligands was i.p. administered in MC903-treated mice, synergistic effects of basophil/eosinophil expansion and NOD2/TLR2-mediated stimulation were observed, further exacerbated AD symptoms. In these experimental groups, severe skin lesions culminated in dry skin and psoriatic ears, featured by intensely thickened epidermal and large amount of eosinophils infiltrated in epidermal and dermal layers. Together, these results unraveled a crucial role of basophils and eosinophils in the deterioration of AD in patients with S. aureus infections. By using immunohistofluorescence, dermal fibroblasts were found to be enriched in AD skin lesions. Plenty of infiltrated basophils and eosinophils were also observed in dermal layer and located in the vicinity of dermal fibroblasts, facilitating the interaction between these innate cells with adjacent fibroblasts. Consistent with the above results, similar cell distributions were observed in skin lesions of mice treated with MC903 that was co-administered with IL-3C, NOD2/TLR2 ligands, or IL-3C plus NOD2/TLR2 ligands. These results collectively suggest that, being adjacent to each other, NOD2/TLR2-stimulated basophils and eosinophils might further exacerbate AD symptoms by interacting with dermal fibroblasts. (Cell Mol Immunol 2016; 13: 535-550). (3) For clinical study, we have recruited 27 AD patients and 15 control subjects to investigate the plasma concentration of microbicidal peptide human neutrophil α-defensins (HNP) and dermcidin, the expression of bacterial toll-like receptor (TLR) and nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain (NOD)-like receptors of basophils, and plasma concentration and ex vivo induction of AD-related inflammatory cytokines and chemokines Plasma concentrations of HNP, dermcidin and AD-related Th2 chemokines CCL17, CCL22 and CCL27 were significantly elevated in AD patients compared with controls (all p < 0.05). Plasma concentrations of CCL27 and CCL22 were found to correlate positively with SCORing atopic dermatitis (SCORAD), objective SCORAD, % area affected, lichenification and disease intensity, and CCL27 also correlated positively with pruritus in AD patients (all p < 0.05). Protein expressions of NOD2 but not TLR2 of basophils were significantly down-regulated in AD patients compared with controls (p = 0.001). Correspondingly, there were lower ex vivo % inductions of allergic inflammatory tumor necrosis factor-α, IL-6 and CXCL8 from peripheral blood mononuclear cells upon NOD2 ligand S. aureus derived MDP stimulation in AD patients comparing with controls. The aberrant activation of bacterial pattern recognition receptor such as NOD2 of basophils and anti-bacterial innate immune response should be related with the allergic inflammation of AD patients (Molecules, 2016, 21, 471).

476813.label: Major findings and research outcome
476813.value: Using a typical mouse model of AD-like skin inflammation, S. aureus-associated NOD2 and TLR2 ligands were found to exacerbate AD-like symptoms, which were further deteriorated by in vivo expansion of basophils and eosinophils. Subsequent histological analyses revealed that dermal fibroblasts were pervasive in AD-like skin lesions. The co-culture of human dermal fibroblasts with basophils/eosinophils exhibited a vigorous cytokine/chemokine response to NOD2/TLR2 ligands, as well as an enhanced expression of intercellular adhesion molecule-1 on dermal fibroblasts. Basophils and eosinophils were mainly responsible for the AD-related cytokine/chemokine expression in co-culture. Direct intercellular contact was necessary for the crosstalk between basophils and dermal fibroblasts, while soluble mediators were sufficient to mediate eosinophil-fibroblast interactions. Intracellular p38-MAPK, ERK and NF-kB signaling pathways were essential for NOD2/TLR2 ligands-mediated activation of basophils, eosinophils and dermal fibroblasts in AD-related inflammation. This study provides evidence of NOD2/TLR2-mediated exacerbation of AD through activation of basophils and eosinophils interacting with dermal fibroblasts. The above results have been published in Cell Mol Immunol 2016; 13: 535-550. For clinical study of AD, plasma concentrations of microbicidal peptide human neutrophil α-defensins (HNP), dermcidin and AD-related Th2 chemokines CCL17, CCL22 and CCL27 were significantly elevated in AD patients compared with controls. Plasma concentrations of CCL27 and CCL22 were found to correlate positively with disease severity, and CCL27 also correlated positively with pruritus in AD patients. Protein expressions of NOD2 but not TLR2 of basophils were significantly down-regulated in AD patients compared with controls. Correspondingly, there were lower ex vivo % inductions of allergic inflammatory TNF-α, IL-6 and CXCL8 from peripheral blood mononuclear cells upon NOD2 ligand S. aureus derived muramyl dipeptide stimulation in AD patients comparing with controls. In this study, the defective PRR have been identified for allergic inflammatory basophils. Together with lower cytokine response upon NOD2 ligand stimulation and lower concentration of anti-microbial peptides HNP and dermcidin at local skin lesions, the local innate immune mechanisms against S. aureus could be down-regulated in AD. This may subsequently lead to enhanced S. aureus proliferation at skin lesions, and bacteria or its pattern associated molecular pattern molecules may penetrate into the blood circulation to stimulate the neutrophils and other immune effector cells-mediated innate immunity in circulation to result in increased plasma levels of HNP and dermcidin. The above results have been published in Molecules, 2016, 21, 471 and awarded the best Abstract Prize at the European Academy of Allergy and Clinical Immunology Congress 2016.

476813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
476813.value: Using AD mouse model and ex vivo co-culture systems, we illustrated a novel NOD2/TLR2-stimulated pathway to activate basophils/eosinophils by interacting with dermal fibroblasts. Together with the key role of S. aureus in AD, the results of current study depict a mechanism by which S. aureus would induce the accentuation of AD through pattern recognition receptors and innate immunity. Our results concerning the vicious effects of S. aureus on AD also shed light on implementing therapeutic interventions to eliminate S. aureus may help to alleviate AD symptoms. By moving one step forward, we are working on the damaging associated molecular pattern molecule high mobility group box 1-mediated activation of eosinophils/basophils and immunoregulatory cytokines in allergic inflammation. In clinical study, the defective pattern recognition receptors have been identified for allergic inflammatory basophils, together with the previously shown impaired anti-bacterial innate immunity for the enhanced skin bacterial infections in AD, our results provide further evidence for the elucidation of the defects of innate immunity and allow the development of novel therapeutic intervention to repair these deficiencies and reduce the allergic inflammation in AD patients. Along with this study, a large scale international collaborative clinical study of innate immunity in allergic diseases is in-going.

476813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
476813.value: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronically relapsing inflammatory skin disease that affects nearly 20% of Hong Kong schoolchildren. Bacterial skin infection caused by Staphylococcus aureus is associated with chronic inflammation and morbidity in AD. Using mouse AD model, we found that S. aureus-associated cell wall components, ligands for innate immune receptors, can exacerbate AD-like symptoms in AD mice via the activation of eosinophils and basophils, the principal effector in allergic inflammation. Using cell culture, the interaction of eosinophils/basophils with skin cells can provoke potent allergic inflammation upon bacterial infection. The cellular mechanistic study revealed that the intercellular contact and intracellular signaling mechanisms play important roles for regulating bacteria–induced allergic inflammation in AD. In clinical study, we identify and characterize the aberrant innate immunity against bacterial infection in AD patients while comparing with normal control subjects. Together, results not only help for the further evaluation of the novel cellular mechanism of allergic inflammation in AD but also provide a biochemical basis for the development of new therapeutic intervention for the treatment of allergic diseases. The results of this AD study have been published in international peer-reviewed journals and awarded the best abstract award in an international congress of allergy.

477213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
477213.value: This double-blind randomized trial aims to compare the efficacy of a proton pump inhibitor (lansoprazole) and a histamine-2 receptor antagonist (famotidine) in preventing recurrent ulcer bleeding in patients with a history of idiopathic gastroduodenal ulcer bleeding. Peptic ulcer disease is known to be caused by a bacterial infection (H. pylori) in the stomach or the use of certain painkillers (nonsteroidal anti-inflammtory drugs including aspirin). Since the last decade, peptic ulcer disease with unknown cause (idopathic gastroduodenal ulcer) has been increasingly recognized worldwide. Large-scale studies in the U.S. reported that up to 27% of patients developed recurrent ulcers without H. pylori infection or use of painkillers. In Asia, the relative proportion of idiopathic gastroduodenal ulcers has risen from less than 5% to over 20% of all peptic ulcers. In Hong Kong, idiopathic gastroduodenal ulcer is an emerging problem. We have demonstrated a 4-fold rise in the absolute incidence of idiopathic gastroduodenal ulcer bleeding between 1997 and 2000. Little was known about the natural history of idiopathic gastroduodenal ulcer bleeding. According to our series of studies, we found that recurrent idiopathic ulcer bleeding is common - 13% and 42% in one and seven years, respectively. In another prospective nonrandomized study, we found that acid suppressive drugs were more commonly prescribed to older patients with more serious comorbid illnesses, and that acid suppressive drugs failed to reduce the risk of recurrent bleeding or mortality. However, the nonrandomized study design and infrequent use of potent acid suppressive drugs may account for the treatment failure. Currently, there is no evidence-based guideline on the prevention of recurrent idiopathic ulcer bleeding. The local heath authority does not recommend long-term use of acid suppressive drugs for this emerging condition. We hypothesize that the use of potent acid suppressants (proton-pump inhibitors) will be superior to conventional acid suppressants (histamine-2-receptor antagonists) for the prevention of recurrent bleeding in patients with a history of idiopathic ulcer bleeding. Unfortunately, this important clinical question is not a precedence of pharmaceutical companies because the unpredictable study outcome may not favor their products. Irrespective of the study outcome, this industry-independent clinical trial will encourage health authorities and international guideline committees to review their recommendations for this emerging condition.

477213.label: Realisation of objectives
477213.value: Present guidelines are conflicting for the prevention of recurrent ulcer bleeding in patients with a history of Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori)–negative idiopathic bleeding ulcers, i.e. in the absence of H. pylori and a drug history of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and/or antiplatelet agents. These patients have considerable risk of recurrent ulcer complications, even years after the index bleeding. We hypothesized that a proton pump inhibitor (lansoprazole) is superior to a histamine-2 receptor antagonist (famotidine) for prevention of recurrent ulcer bleeding in such patients. For this industry-independent, double-blind, randomized trial done in one academic hospital in Hong Kong, we screened patients with a history of idiopathic bleeding ulcers. After ulcer healing, an independent staff member randomly assigned (1:1) patients who were negative for Helicobacter pylori with a computer-generated list of random numbers to receive oral administrations of either lansoprazole 30mg or famotidine 40mg daily once per day for 24 months. Both patients and investigators were masked to their treatments. The primary endpoint was recurrent upper gastrointestinal bleeding (defined as hematemesis, per-rectal bleeding and/or melena confirmed and documented by the attending doctor, or a drop in hemoglobin >/=2 g/dL, with ulcer and/or erosions confirmed endoscopically) within 24 months. The secondary endpoint was any recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding (upper, mid and/or lower) as defined according to the clinical criteria stated above. The primary endpoint and secondary safety endpoints were analyzed in the intention-to-treat population. This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, number NCT01180179. We now report the blinded interim analysis of findings at Month 12. Between June 24, 2010, and Oct 20, 2016, we enrolled 228 patients, assigning 114 patients to each study group, all of whom were included in the intention-to-treat population. The cumulative incidence of recurrent upper gastrointestinal bleeding in 12 months was 2.6% in Arm A and 6.1% in Arm B (difference in proportion = 0, 95% CI -0.03 to 0.03; p=0.20). Endoscopic ulcer recurrence rate was 1.8% in both Arm A and Arm B. No treatment-related deaths occurred during the study. This blinded interim analysis did not demonstrate any superiority of either lansoprazole or famotidine for the prevention of recurrent ulcer bleeding in patients with a history of H. pylori–negative idiopathic bleeding ulcers. Patients still had considerable risk of recurrent ulcer complications up to 6.1% despite 12 months of acid suppressive therapy. To further understand the risk factors predicting recurrent idiopathic gastroduodenal ulcer bleeding, we built a machine learning (ML) model to predict recurrent ulcer bleeding in such patients. A retrospective cohort of patients who were diagnosed to suffer from peptic ulcer from January 1, 2000 to August 31, 2016 were retrieved through the Clinical Data Analysis and Reporting System (CDARS) of the Hospital Authority (HA), Hong Kong. Demographic data, laboratory parameters, relevant diagnoses, procedures, concomitant drugs, and laboratory parameters were retrieved and studied. The primary endpoint was recurrent peptic ulcer bleeding. An idiopathic peptic ulcer ML mode (IPU-ML mode) built was validated in an independent prospective cohort of patients with index peptic ulcer bleeding from January 1, 2008 to December 31, 2015. We identified a cohort of 24,482 patients suffered from idiopathic gastroduodenal ulcer bleeding (Table 1). Recurrent ulcer bleeding developed in 4,772 patients (19.5%) at a median follow-up duration of 2.7 years; the one-year incidence rate was 12.8%. IPU-ML mode predicted recurrent ulcer bleeding in one year with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) 0.6861. With a cutoff value of 0.15, IPU-ML model achieved 90.02% sensitivity and 30.98% specificity with corresponding negative and positive predictive values of 75.63% and 56.60%, and 42.03% of overall accuracy to predict the one-year recurrent ulcer bleeding risk ≥20% in the training group. IPU-ML mode was validated in an independent prospective cohort of 1,265 patients. IPU-ML model predicted recurrent ulcer bleeding in one year with an AUROC 0.8114 in this validation cohort. With a cutoff value of 0.15, IPU-ML model achieved 92.50% sensitivity and 53.37% specificity with corresponding negative and positive predictive values of 87.68% and 66.48%, and 59.47% of overall accuracy to predict the one-year recurrent ulcer bleeding risk≥20%. A machine learning model (IPU-ML model) accurately predicts the one-year risk of recurrent ulcer bleeding in patients with a history of idiopathic gastroduodenal ulcer bleeding. This serves as an excellent tool for risk stratification and hence to provide a personalised management for such patients.

477213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
477213.value: Another General Research Fund from Research Grant Council (Project Ref: 14106917) has been funded. This new study is entitled "Prevention of recurrent ulcer bleeding in patients with idiopathic gastroduodenal ulcer: a double-blind randomised trial on misoprostol combined with lansoprazole versus lansoprazole alone (NRT_MISO Study)". This successful application was based on the current randomised trial which compares the efficacy of lansoprazole and famotidine to prevent recurrent idiopathic gastroduodenal ulcer bleeding (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT01180179). Up to 31 August 2016, we recruited 176 subjects who have completed the study period. Recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding developed in 11 (12.9%) and 12 (13.2%) patients in Arm 1 and Arm 2 respectively (P=1.000), which is unacceptably high. This is a strong piece of evidence that PPI is not the best treatment for preventing recurrent ulcer bleeding.

477213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
477213.value: Peptic ulcer disease used to be caused by a bacterial infection (Helicobacter pylori) in the stomach or the use of certain painkillers (nonsteroidal anti-inflammtory drugs or NSAIDs). However, there has been an increasing trend of peptic ulcer disease with unknown cause (idopathic ulcer) worldwide since the last decade. We have demonstrated that after these ulcers had healed, the rates of recurrent ulcer bleeding in one year and seven years were over 13% and 42%, respectively. There were no observational studies or randomized trials on the use of acid suppressive drugs (e.g. proton pump inhibitors or histamine-2 receptor antagonists) in preventing recurrent idiopathic ulcers. As a consequence, the hospital authority has not issued any guideline on the long-term use of acid suppressive drugs in patients with a history of idiopathic bleeding peptic ulcers. This double-blind randomised trial compares a proton pump inhibitor (lansoprazole) and a histamine-2 receptor antagonist (famotidine) for prevention of recurrent ulcer bleeding in such patients. Between June 24, 2010, and Oct 20, 2016, we enrolled 228 patients, assigning 114 patients to each study group, all of whom were included in the intention-to-treat population. The cumulative incidence of recurrent upper gastrointestinal bleeding in 12 months was 2.6% in Arm A and 6.1% in Arm B (difference in proportion = 0, 95% CI -0.03 to 0.03; p=0.20). Endoscopic ulcer recurrence rate was 1.8% in both Arm A and Arm B. No treatment-related deaths occurred during the study. Hence we concluded that This blinded interim analysis did not demonstrate any superiority of either lansoprazole or famotidine for the prevention of recurrent ulcer bleeding in patients with a history of H. pylori–negative idiopathic bleeding ulcers. Patients still had considerable risk of recurrent ulcer complications up to 6.1% despite 12 months of acid suppressive therapy.

477513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
477513.value: Research on cognitive aging has shown an extensive network of neurocognitive decline. The disease-state of such a decline—Alzheimer’s disease and other cognitive disorders—not only hijacks us from our consciousness and intellectual autonomy, but also burdens families and health care systems. Solutions to finding a cure must be multifaceted, focusing on both pharmacological agents and treatments post-onset of the disease on one hand, and behavioral stimulations and preventions on the other. The proposed research focuses on the latter, building upon two lines of research. First, older adults who speak two or more languages have a reduced risk of dementia and enhanced cognitive abilities. Similar positive effects have been found in older adults who engage in cognitively stimulating activities, including structured (computerized) cognitive training. Second, research in second language learning provides evidence for changes in an extensive cortical and subcortical network as a result of learning in adulthood. Interestingly, such an extensive network overlaps with the network of cognitive decline due to aging. The proposed research will seek to determine whether cognitive improvements can result from language learning. Chinese-speaking adults between 65-85 years old who do not speak English will be randomly assigned to an English learning (experimental) group, a crossword puzzles/math problems (active control) group, or a group receiving no intervention who meet only for the purpose of music appreciation (passive control) for 18 months. English learning will consist of computerized training adapted to the learning styles and practical needs of older adults in Hong Kong. Biweekly social interaction groups with native speakers will facilitate language use and induce a cohort experience for enhancing study retention. Subjects’ working memory, attention, and inhibitory control functions will be assessed via standardized tests before training, immediately after training, and 3 months after training to determine whether cognitive improvements are observed in the language learning group and whether such improvements are larger than improvements seen in the control groups. If successful, this research will provide the first evidence in a prospective study to demonstrate the cognitive benefit of language learning in later adulthood. It will naturally lead to a large-scale, longitudinal study to examine cognitive reserves and incidence of Alzheimer’s disease in a cohort of older adults who study a foreign language for a longer term to ascertain the therapeutic and prevention promise of late-life language learning. The results will not only have an impact on older adults in Hong Kong, but also their peers worldwide. 研究顯示，認知功能老化能導致廣泛的神經認知衰退。這些病態的衰退（如：腦退化症和其他認知障礙）不只威脅到病人的意識和智力自主性，更為其家庭成員和社會醫療系統帶來負擔。而尋求治癒方法則必須從多方面入手：一方面著重病後治療和輔藥，另一方面研究行為刺激和預防方案。本研究將著重探討後者，並基於兩條研究路線發展。第一，能說兩種或以上語言的老年人，其患上失智症和其他認知功能損傷的風險較低。而在參與刺激認知活動（包括電腦化認知訓練）的老年人身上，同樣的正面效果亦有出現。 第二，有第二語言學習的研究證明，在成年期學習語言，能導致廣泛的皮層和皮層下的神經網絡變化。值得一提的是，這個廣泛的網絡，跟因老化而生的認知衰退的神經網絡是交疊的。本研究將討論語言學習到底能否令認知功能得到改善。實驗中，一群以中文為母語，且不懂英語的老年人，將被隨機分到英語學習組（實驗組），或縱橫字謎／數學解難組（活性對照組），或一個不受任何干預，只作數個月的音樂聆聽的組別（被動對照組）。這裡的英語學習會是一個電腦化的訓練，並顧及香港老年人的學習習慣和實際需要。實驗組別會每兩個星期參加社交組，與以英語為母語者交談，讓他們有機會運用英語，從而提高學後保留。實驗對象的短期記憶﹑集中力和抑制控制功能會在訓練前﹑訓練後和接受訓練一段時間後，以標準化測驗得到評估，以助觀察英語學習組的認知功能有否改善，而此等改善又會否比其餘兩個對照組別的為大。假如結果屬正面，本研究將首次為未來相關的研究提供證據，證明語言學習確為老年人的認知功能帶來益處。這自然會把我們帶到一個大規模的縱觀研究，更長時間地觀察一群學習外語的老年人的認知儲備，和患上腦退化症的機率，以確定在老年學習語言的治療和預防效用。本研究的結果將不只影響香港的老年人，而是全球的老年人也能受惠。

477513.label: Realisation of objectives
477513.value: The objectives of this project have been completely achieved. We have conducted a prospective randomized controlled training study with older adults with age-typical cognitive functions. Taken into consideration of a potentially large attrition rate, our target enrollment was 120 older adults. We successfully recruited a total of 120 older adults, between 60 to 85 years of age, from community centers in Hong Kong. As the current study targets older adults before the onset of symptoms for dementia and other cognitive deficits, only participants who received a 0 on the Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) scale were included. Due to the longitudinal nature of the study, not all of the 120 participants originally recruited completed the full experimental protocol. In total, 67 individuals completed the study in its entirety and were included in the statistical analyses. Of the 53 participants who were either removed or withdrew from the study – a) eight did not satisfy the inclusion criteria; b) three did not follow experimenter instructions; and c) 42 did not complete the full experimental protocol including training and three assessments. The latter subgroup did not complete the full protocol because – a) 31 subjects found the training requirements to be too time consuming or too difficult; b) five needed to attend to home or family issues; c) six withdrew from the study without providing a reason. Participants who withdraw from the study did not differ from those who completed the study in terms of education, occupation status, housing, musical experience, or scores on the CDR or ADAS-Cog (all ps > .05). Participants were randomized into three training groups: 1) Foreign Language (FL) (N = 24) in which participants learned basic English through Rosetta Stone software, 2) Games (N = 22) in which participants played cognitively stimulating activities such as puzzles and mahjong, and 3) Music (N = 21) in which participants listened to traditional and contemporary Chinese music. All participants took part in a computer-based activity for five hours per week over a period of six months, i.e., maximally 130 training hours (26 weeks × 5 hours) in total. A minimum of 78 training hours (i.e., 60% of all the sessions) was required to be included in the final analysis. The three participant groups, FL (Mean = 113.54, SD = 11.70), Games (Mean = 112.90, SD = 6.58), Music (Mean = 112.77, SD = 11.26) did not significantly differ in total training hours [F(2, 66) = .03, p = .965]. Participants completed the computer-based training individually in one of the participating community centers. Additionally, participants within each training group met for regular social activities (usually twice a month), led by a research assistant who fulfilled the role of Social Group Leader, so as to foster a cohort experience and to aid retention. These social activities were appropriate for the cognitive stimulation of each group. For instance, FL participants practiced their developing English skills with a proficient English speaker, the games group played board games, and the music appreciation group took part in karaoke. A battery of cognitive tests was administered before (pre-training) and immediately after training (post-training) and three months after training (follow-up), including ADAS-Cog to assess cognitive impairment, Reading span (Rspan) and Digit span for working memory, Simon Task for inhibitory control, Attention Network Test (ANT) for attention, Boston Naming Test (BNT) and Category Verbal Fluency Test (CVFT) for verbal functions. Prior to training, the three groups of participants did not differ in age [F(2, 66) = .67, p = .517], education level [F(2, 66) = .70, p = .499], occupation [F(2, 66) = .32, p = .584], housing [F(2, 66) = .20, p = .817], and musical background [F(2, 66) = .01, p = .988]. Importantly, all participants received a CDR of 0 at baseline, and general cognitive abilities as measured by the Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale Cognitive Subscale (ADAS-Cog) [F(2, 66) = .18, p = .830] did not differ across groups. Results from mixed ANOVAs (3 groups x 3 time points) revealed significant main effects of time on measures of Rspan [F(2, 128) = 3.43, p = .035, = .051], BNT [F(2, 128) = 31.38, p < .001, = .329] and CVFT [F(2, 128) = 9.30, p < .001, = .127]. We did not find any significant effects of group (ps > .05), nor any group by time interactions (ps > .05). However, to evaluate whether cognitive functions change given different types of interventions, we conducted planned comparisons in each group to compare subject’s performance across time i.e. pre- vs. post-training, and post-training vs. follow-up, focusing on the three measures (Rspan, BNT and CVFT) that appeared to be sensitive to intervention. We did not observe any significant effects of training on other outcome measures (all ps > .05). FL training improved reading span from pre- to post-training [t(23) = 2.77, p = .011, Cohen's d = .746] and this improvement was maintained at the 3-month follow-up [post-training vs. follow-up, t(23) = - 1.16, p = .257, Cohen's d = - .268]. In contrast, participation in games or music appreciation did not yield significant improvements in Reading Span scores (all ps > .05). FL also led to improvements in BNT from pre- to post-training [t(23) = 2.53, p = .019, Cohen's d = .349], and performance improved significantly again from post-training to 3-month follow-up [t(23) = 3.61, p = .001, Cohen's d = . 626]. Contrastively, performance improvements only reached significance from post-training to follow-up in the game [t(21) = 2.18, p = .041, Cohen's d = .435] and music [t(20) = 4.84, p < .001, Cohen's d = .543] groups. As for CVFT, FL significantly improved performance from post-training to 3-month follow-up [t(23) = 3.04, p = .006, Cohen's d = .489]. Similarly, participation in games also improved CVFT scores at 3-month follow-up [t(21) = 2.80, p = .011, Cohen's d = .297]. In contrast, music appreciation did not yield reliable improvements in CVFT at post-training nor at follow-up (all ps > .05). Taken together, these results suggest that FL for six months is an effective means to improve cognitive functions (Objective 1). Additionally, both FL and game are beneficial in improving cognitive functions, however FL seems to improve a broader range of cognitive functions i.e. both working memory and verbal functions, and induce a larger cognitive gain i.e. larger effect size (Objective 2).

477513.label: Major findings and research outcome
477513.value: Major findings 1: The present study is the first prospective randomized controlled study to examine the potential cognitive benefit of FL training, and found FL training improved cognitive functions in older adults. The clearest improvement we saw was on measures of working memory- Reading Span [pre- vs. post-training, t(23) = 2.77, p = .011, Cohen's d = .746] and verbal functions including Boston Naming Test [pre- vs. post-training , t(23) = 2.53, p = .019, Cohen's d = .349; post-training vs. follow-up, t(23) = 3.61, p = .001, Cohen's d = . 626] and Category Verbal Fluency Test [post-training vs. follow-up, t(23) = 3.04, p = .006, Cohen's d = .489]. Major findings 2: FL training seems to be an optimal cognitive-reserve-building activity that may possess some comparative advantage over other cognitive stimulations, i.e. game and music. Replicating previous studies in which benefits of cognitively stimulating activities such as playing puzzles and games on improving cognitive abilities were found, we observed that the games group also improved their cognitive abilities as measured by BNT [post-training vs. follow-up, t(21) = 2.18, p = .041, Cohen's d = .435] and CVFT [post-training vs. follow-up, t(21) = 2.80, p = .011, Cohen's d = .297]. Though we did not find any significant group by testing time interactions in the mixed ANOVAs, we did observe evidence suggesting that FL may provide comparative advantage in improving cognition relative to games. Specifically, FL yielded a larger effect size (Cohen's d = 0.435) relative to games (Cohen's d = 0.297) when comparing post-training vs. 3-month follow-up CVFT. Moreover, training-induced benefits were only observed for FL in the working memory measures of Reading Span. Compared to FL and games, music appreciation did not result in reliable improvement in any of the cognitive measures. The research outcomes based on this project: This project contributed to the publication of 5 journal articles and multiple conference presentations on our findings associated with language learning and the brain. One article on FL and cognitive health is under review.

477513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
477513.value: This study shows positive evidence of language training, even initiated later in life, yields statistically reliable improvements in cognitive measures in older adults with age-typical cognitive functions. This finding establishes the efficacy of FL training (conducted within elderly centers) as a cognitive-reserve-building activity to counteract age-related cognitive decline and halt progression of neurodegenerative disease. Based on this experimental paradigm, we have also conducted a project with the support of the HMRF to examine whether FL can improve cognitive functions in adults with signs of Mild Cognitive Impairment. In the future, we plan to examine the effects of format and dosage of FL learning on cognitive functions, so as to maximize learning and cognitive outcomes. Specifically, we propose to investigate whether FL training via a mobile device that could occur anywhere is more effective than training confined to a desktop computer in a fixed location (an elderly center) in promoting cognitive functions. Moreover, we aim to determine if FL training via a mobile device in promoting cognitive functions is space-dependent so that six-month training may lead to better outcome than three-month training even if the number of hours (dosage) of training is the same (to be supported by HMRF).

477513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
477513.value: With the drastic increase of aging population in Hong Kong, early and effective intervention of cognitive deficits becomes imperative. We report the first comprehensive study that prospectively tests the potential cognitive enhancing effect of foreign language learning in older adults who have age-typical cognitive abilities. Because language learning engages a large brain network that overlaps with the network of cognitive aging, we hypothesized that learning a new language later in life would be beneficial. Older adults were randomly assigned to three training groups: foreign language (FL), games, and music appreciation. All were trained predominately by a computer-based program for six months, and their cognitive abilities were tested before, immediately after, and three months after training. FL and games, but not music appreciation, improved cognitive functions, moreover, FL seems to produce a larger cognitive gains than game. FL is thus an ideal training activity for older adults, not only because it provides a form of cognitive stimulation, but also it has the benefits of being meaningful (an advantage over other cognitive training approaches) and provides an avenue for acquiring an important new skill that can facilitate other aspects of life such as traveling, communication and commerce.

477813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
477813.value: This is a prospective cohort study to study the prevalence and clinical significance of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) in patients with type 2 diabetes. NAFLD is the most common chronic liver disease worldwide and affects 15-30% of the general adult population in Asia. Some patients with NAFLD would progress to cirrhosis and liver cancer. NAFLD is strongly associated with type 2 diabetes. 30-90% of diabetic patients have NAFLD. NAFLD patients with diabetes are more likely to have active steatohepatitis, advanced liver fibrosis and cirrhosis. On the other hand, NAFLD represents a state of insulin resistance and is strongly associated with coronary artery disease and various malignancies. Its association with other diabetic complications is currently unknown. Due to insufficient data, current guidelines offer conflicting recommendation on whether diabetic patients should be screened for NAFLD. The main arguments against screening include uncertainties surrounding diagnostic tests and treatment options and lack of knowledge related to the long-term benefits of screening. On the other hand, screening may identify patients with NAFLD-related cirrhosis who would benefit from liver cancer and varices surveillance. Patients with NAFLD may also be an at risk group who would most benefit from diabetic complications assessment. With new technological development, it is now possible to perform accurate liver assessment on a large number of patients at low cost. Our center has installed the state-of-the-art Fibroscan 502 machine and is among the first teams to validate its performance. Simultaneous controlled attenuation parameter and liver stiffness measurement by the machine is an accurate, reproducible and non-invasive test to assess liver fat and fibrosis. In this project, we will perform liver fat and fibrosis measurement by Fibroscan on 2035 patients with type 2 diabetes. This will provide important data on the prevalence of NAFLD and advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis in diabetic patients. We will also determine the association between NAFLD and diabetic complications through our comprehensive complications screening program. Finally, these patients will be followed up for 10 years to determine the association between NAFLD and important clinical outcomes. This study addresses the uncertainty about NAFLD screening in diabetic patients. The results will have direct influence on future guideline development and will impact on clinical practice. 這是一項前瞻性隊列研究，旨在研究2型糖尿病患者的非酒精性脂肪性肝病的患病率及臨床意義。 非酒精性脂肪肝是最常見的慢性肝病，影響亞洲15-30％的成人人口，有些脂肪肝患者會進展為肝硬化和肝癌。非酒精性脂肪肝與2型糖尿病相關密切， 30-90 ％的糖尿病患者同時有脂肪肝。在脂肪肝患者當中，糖尿病可能促進脂肪性肝炎，肝纖維化和肝硬化。另一方面， 脂肪肝代表胰島素抵抗狀態，增加冠狀動脈疾病及各種惡性腫瘤的風險。 由於數據不足，目前的治療指南並不確定糖尿病患者是否應進行脂肪肝篩查。隨著新技術的發展，現在有可能為大量病人提供脂肪肝無創檢查。我們的中心已經安裝了新型肝纖維素描，能同時檢測肝臟的脂肪含量和纖維化。 在這個研究，我們將為2035例2型糖尿病人進行新型肝纖維素描檢查。這將提供重要的脂肪肝，我們也將研究脂肪肝和糖尿病併發症之間的關聯。這項研究的結果將直接影響未來的治療發展。

477813.label: Realisation of objectives
477813.value: 1. To study the prevalence of NAFLD and advanced liver fibrosis in patients with type 2 diabetes During the study period, we screened 2119 patients with type 2 diabetes using the FibroScan machine. After excluding patients with excessive alcohol consumption, other liver diseases and unsatisfactory FibroScan examination, 1918 patients were included in the final analysis. Based on controlled attenuation parameter and liver stiffness measurements, the prevalence of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and advanced liver fibrosis in patients with type 2 diabetes was estimated to be 72.8% and 17.7%, respectively. The findings were further validated in 94 patients who underwent liver biopsy. In addition, we determined factors associated with NAFLD and advanced fibrosis. Objective 1 is thus fully realized. 2. To study the association between NAFLD and diabetic complications With FibroScan examination in a large cohort of patients with type 2 diabetes and the performance of comprehensive diabetic complications screening, we were able to study the association between NAFLD and diabetic complications including nephropathy, retinopathy, peripheral neuropathy and cardiovascular diseases. In particular, we found that albuminuria due to type 2 diabetes was increased in patients with advanced fibrosis but not steatosis. After adjusting for age, sex, other metabolic factors and medicine use, advanced fibrosis was associated with a 2-fold increase in the risk of albuminuria. This suggests that the severity rather than the mere presence of NAFLD is associated with albuminuria. The findings may explain the conflicting data from other groups on the association between NAFLD and diabetic nephropathy. The results on albuminuria have already been published in full, while manuscripts on the other diabetic complications are currently under preparation. Objective 2 is thus fully realized. 3. To study the association between NAFLD and clinical outcomes at 1 and 10 years One of the main objectives of this project is to establish a high quality clinical cohort to study the clinical outcomes of diabetic patients with and without NAFLD/liver fibrosis. Currently, the patients have been fully enrolled and are followed at the diabetes and hepatology clinics prospectively. We have now completed the Year 1 analysis of the clinical outcomes. To our surprise, patients with NAFLD were less likely to die or develop acute myocardial infarction and end-stage liver disease. In contrast, hepatocellular carcinoma and ascites were 10 times more likely in patients with advanced fibrosis. We believe the apparent inverse association between liver fat and adverse clinical outcomes may be because of the disappearance of liver fat in patients with severe liver and medical diseases. In any case, the establishment of this cohort will generate precious data on the natural history of NAFLD in diabetic patients. As described in the original proposal, these patients will continue to be followed at the clinic for 10 years for clinical events. Objective 3 is thus fully realized.

477813.label: Major findings and research outcome
477813.value: Through FibroScan screening, we found that the prevalence of NAFLD and advanced fibrosis among patients with type 2 diabetes was 72.8% (95% CI 70.7-74.8%) and 17.7% (95% CI 16.0-19.5%), respectively. By multivariable analysis, female gender, higher body mass index, triglycerides, fasting plasma glucose and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and non-insulin use were associated with increased CAP. Longer duration of diabetes, higher body mass index, increased ALT and spot urine albumin:creatinine ratio and lower high density lipoprotein-cholesterol were associated with increased LSM. Ninety-four patients (80% had increased liver stiffness) underwent liver biopsy: 56% had NASH and 50% had F3-4 disease. In addition, the prevalence of albuminuria was higher in diabetic patients with liver steatosis and those with advanced fibrosis (no NAFLD vs. liver steatosis vs. advanced fibrosis: 41.4% vs. 46.2% vs. 64.2%, p<0.001). After adjustment of potential confounders including glycated hemoglobin, hypertension and body mass index, advanced fibrosis but not liver steatosis was associated with increased risk of albuminuria (odd ratio, OR =1.52, 95% confidence interval, CI: 1.02-2.28, p =0.039) in patients with estimated glomerular filtration rate ≥60 ml/min/1.73 m2. The odds of albuminuria increased with greater severity of liver fibrosis in a dose dependent manner with the highest odds observed in patients with LSM scores ≥11.5 kPa assessed by M probe or ≥11.0 kPa assessed by XL probe (adjusted OR= 1.53, 95% CI: 1.07-2.20, p=0.021). Furthermore, we studied the Year 1 clinical outcomes of this cohort. NAFLD patients were less likely to die (2.9% vs 6.1%; P=0.001) or develop acute myocardial infarction (1.0% vs 2.5%; P=0.014) and end-stage renal disease (1.0% vs 3.5%; P<0.001). On the other hand, advanced fibrosis was associated with a higher risk of hepatocellular carcinoma and liver decompensation (1.0% vs 0.1%; P=0.009).

477813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
477813.value: As described in the original proposal, this cohort will be prospectively followed for 10 years for clinical events. This will determine the long-term prognostic significance of NAFLD and advanced liver fibrosis. In addition, with the support of the General Research Fund (Project reference 14108916), we are currently repeating FibroScan examination at 3 years. This project will determine the incidence of NAFLD and the rate of fibrosis progression in patients with type 2 diabetes. Factors associated with incident NAFLD and advanced fibrosis will also be studied.

477813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
477813.value: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a form of fatty liver associated with obesity and the metabolic syndrome. It affects around a quarter of the Hong Kong adult population. The current project aims to study the epidemiology of NAFLD in a high risk population, namely patients with type 2 diabetes. We used FibroScan as a non-invasive measurement of liver fat and fibrosis. Overall, NAFLD was found in around 70% of diabetic patients, and nearly 20% had severe liver fibrosis or cirrhosis. Both NAFLD and severe fibrosis were associated with the severity of the underlying metabolic disease. In addition, we found that liver fibrosis but not NAFLD itself was associated with diabetic kidney disease. This is an ongoing project. We will continue to follow these patients for 10 years to study the association between the liver condition and the long-term clinical outcomes.

478413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
478413.value: Arteriosclerosis is a prevalent medical problem in industrialized countries. An important feature of arteriosclerosis is vascular wall thickening in the intimal layer (or neointimal hyperplasia). Neointimal hyperplasia narrows vascular lumen, resulting in ischemic diseases such as heart failure and stroke. A key event in atherosclerotic development is an overproduction of reactive oxygen species (ROS). ROS overproduction promotes the progression of neointimal hyperplasia by stimulating multiple pathological events, including smooth muscle migration into intimal region, smooth proliferation, monocyte/macrophage and neutrophil infiltration, inflammation, vascular cell death and endothelial dysfunction. In the preliminary studies, we established an animal model and a human model of intimal hyperplasia by placing a perivascular cuff (or collar) around rat femoral artery and by culturing human saphenous vein in vitro over a 2-week period to allow neointimal growth, respectively. Interestingly, we found that numerous smooth muscle cells in the newly-formed intimal region had high TRPM2 (transient receptor potential channel isoform M2) expression. TRPM2 is a Ca2+-permeable cation channel activated by reactive oxidative species. Over-activity of TRPM2 channels is known to result in inflammatory diseases and cell death. Thus, we hypothesize that ROS-sensitive TRPM2 channels play a key role in neointimal growth (hyperplasia) and that inhibiting TRPM2 could be a means to reduce neointimal hyperplasia and arteriosclerosis. Indeed, we found that treatment of saphenous veins with a TRPM2-specific blocking antibody TM2E3 or a TRP channel inhibitor 2-APB each caused marked reduction in neointimal hyperplasia. In the present proposal, we plan to use additional approaches to verify the role of TRPM2 in neointimal hyperplasia and to explore the underlying mechanisms of TRPM2 involvement in the pathological progression of arteriosclerosis. 478413.label: Major findings and research outcome
478413.value: 1). We have verified the role of TRPM2 in neointimal hyperplasis in human saphenous vein models. The results confirmed that anti-TRPM2 antibody TM2E3 and a pharmacological inhibitor 2-APB both are able to inhibit neointimal hyperplasia in organ-cultured human saphenous veins. 2) We have confirmed the role of TRPM2 in neointimal hyperplasis using TRPM2 knockout (TRPM2-/-) mice. Perivascular cuff-based neointimal hyperplasia model was established in mice and rats. Immunostaining showed numerous TRPM2-positive smooth muscle cells in neointimal regions. ROS were over-produced and PCNA-positive proliferating cells were numerous in the neointimal regions. Importantly, the neointimal hyperplasia was substantially reduced in Trpm2 knockout. The results are published in several international journals (Ru X et al., Biochim Biophys Acta – Mol Basis Dis. 2015;1852:1360-71; Ru X and Yao X, Acta Physiologica Sinica, 2014;66:7-15; Ma Y et al., Biochim Biophys Acta – Mol Basis Dis. 2015;1582:552-9; Wang Y, et al., Stem Cells 2015;33:2973-84; Zhang P et al., Cardiovas Res 2014;104:138-46). 3) We have explored the role of TRPM2 in smooth muscle cell migration and proliferation. We used H2O2 treatment to stimulate cell proliferation and migration in the cultured rat/mouse aortic smooth muscle cells. We found that the stimulating effect of H2O2 on cell proliferation and migration was reduced by TM2E3 and TRPM2 knockout. We further identified that signaling molecules downstream of TRPM2 involves Axl and Akt.The results are published in several international journals (Ru X et al., Biochim Biophys Acta – Mol Basis Dis. 2015;1852:1360-71; Ru X and Yao X, Acta Physiologica Sinica, 2014;66:7-15; Ma Y et al., Biochim Biophys Acta – Mol Basis Dis. 2015;1582:552-9; Wang Y, et al., Stem Cells 2015;33:2973-84; Zhang P et al., Cardiovas Res 2014;104:138-46). 4) We have also explored the role of TRPM2 in leukocyte infiltration and inflammation in vascular wall. However, the results are negative. We did not see much difference in leukocyte infiltration and inflammation between wild-type and TRPM2 KO mice. The results are published in a Ph.D thesis by Zhang Jinglin (2015). We have also determined whether TRPM2 KO can alter endothelium-dependent vascular relaxation using mouse mesenteric arteries. However, the results are negative. We do not find any difference in endothelium-dependent vascular relaxation between normal mice and TRPM2 KO mice. 5) We have also studied related topics including the role of TRPC1, TRPV4, TRPC5, Orail in cardiovascular functions and obtained some interesting results. The findings are published in several journals including Nature Communications, Stem cells, FASEB J, Cardiovas Res, J Mol Cell Cardiol.

478413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
478413.value: Through this study, we found that TRPM2 is an important protein that is critically involved in atherosclerotic development. Furthermore, we have developed a functional blocking antibody TM2E3 that can inhibit the neointimal hyperplasia in atherosclerotic lesion. In future, it may be worthwhile to develop this antibody into a potential therapeutic tool for the treatment of atherosclerosis.

478413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
478413.value: Arteriosclerosis is a common medical problem in industrialized countries and has major impact on survival and quality of life. A hallmark of arteriosclerosis is vascular wall thickening in the intimal layer. Intimal hyperplasia (or thickening) is an early event in the development of atherosclerotic lesions. Intimal hyperplasia narrows vascular lumen, resulting in ischemic diseases including heart failure and stroke. In the present study, we identified a novel protein TRPM2 that plays a critical role in the progression of intimal hyperplasia using cultured cell model, animal model, organ-cultured human vessel model. We found that inhibition of TRPM2 reduced the intimal hyperplasia in animal model as well as in organ-cultured human vessel model. Our study laid the background for potential therapeutic strategy targeting at TRPM2 and its related signaling pathway. During the process, we have developed an TRPM2-specific blocking antibody that can effectively slow down the progression of intimal hyperplasia. In future, it is possible to develop this antibody into a therapeutic tool for atherosclerosis.

479213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
479213.value: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is characterized by episodes of apnea during sleep leading to intermittent hypoxia and hypoxemia and various degree of sleep disturbance. It is well known that OSA is not just a breathing disorder with metabolic consequences. The intermittent hypoxia and sleep fragmentation could lead to impaired brain functions which severely degrade performance in daily lives and work, and is one of the major causes of sleepiness and concentration deficiency-related traffic accidents. However, still very little is known about the detailed events happening in the central nervous system in OSA subjects, including the exact cause of neurocognitive deficits and the effects on different types of memory system. Furthermore, although surgery and continuous positive airway pressure, or CPAP, are useful treatments for OSA, whether long-term changes happening in the brain could be reverted is not known. These are important questions to be addressed and the answers are just beginning to be unraveled. Our team is one of the pioneers to investigate the impact, and mechanism, of OSA-associated intermittent hypoxia on neuroplasticity. With previous supports from GRF, we have provided firm evidence that the expression of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF, a member of the neurotrophin family) is reduced in an animal model of OSA and surgical replenishment of BDNF can prevent intermittent hypoxia-induced impairment in long-term synaptic plasticity in the hippocampus, a cellular index of memory formation. Such findings not only unveiled an underlying cause of OSA-associated neurological problems but also open up the possibility of treating the cognitive dysfunction by pharmacological agents. Some key issues, however, remain to be settled. In this project, which builds on our previous work, is a continuation of this line of research, we will further and fully characterize the impact of chronic IH on sleep pattern, and both long term memory and working memory functions in animal models. Furthermore, we ask exactly what happens to neuronal activities in the brain under IH treatment and the impact of a decreased BDNF on cell survival. Finally, we explore pharmacological means to upregulate BDNF level via the administration of a group of glutamate receptor modulators ampakines and also BDNF receptor activator. The results of the present project will help pin down the cause of neurocognitive problems in OSA and also pave the way for designing adjunct pharmacological treatment for OSA that targets specifically at OSA-associated nervous system malfunctions. 阻塞性呼吸睡眠暫停綜合征(OSA)是一種以在睡眠時呼吸暫停導致間歇性缺氧為特徵的睡眠呼吸疾病，並且伴隨著低氧血症和不同程度的睡眠障礙等一系列的臨床症狀。阻塞性呼吸睡眠暫停綜合征不僅對機體的代謝有一定的影響，而且其所產生的間歇性缺氧和睡眠片段化能夠導致大腦功能嚴重受損，對日常的生活和工作產生重大的影響。研究表明，間歇性缺氧和睡眠片段是由於嗜睡和注意力不集中所導致的交通事故的重要原因之一。然而，對於中樞神經系統在阻塞性呼吸睡眠暫停綜合征中病理變化，包括引起神經認知功能減退的確切原因以及其對不同記憶系統的影響，我們知道的少之甚少。雖然，外科手術和持續氣道正壓呼吸（CPAP）對於治療阻塞性呼吸睡眠暫停綜合征具有一定的效果，但是這些效果是否能夠保證大腦中這種長期的病理變化不會復發，我們仍不清楚。而這些問題正是我們急需知道答案的。在阻塞性呼吸睡眠暫停綜合征所引起的間隙性缺氧對突觸可塑性的機制研究這一方面，我們是最早進行探索的研究團隊之一。我們在之前GRF資助的課題研究中發現，腦源性神經營養因數（BDNF，神經營養因數家族的成員之一）在阻塞性呼吸睡眠暫停綜合征中表達降低，而在手術腦部補充外源性的BDNF後，它就可以防止間歇性缺氧所引起的海馬突觸可塑性能力的降低，而海馬突觸可塑性的能力通常都用來表示記憶形成的細胞基礎。這些發現不僅揭示了阻塞性呼吸睡眠暫停綜合征中神經系統問題出現的根本原因，而且也為尋求治療認知功能障礙的藥物製劑帶來可能性。然而，有一些關鍵問題仍然沒有解決。在本課題中，我們會在原有的工作基礎上，以動物模型為對象，更深入，更全面的揭示間歇性缺氧對睡眠模式、長時程記憶功能和工作記憶功能的影響。與此同時，我們也會探究在間歇性缺氧中，大腦神經元興奮性的變化以及BDNF的減少對細胞存活的影響。最後，我們通過在體注射谷氨酸受體的調節劑和BDNF受體的活化劑-ampakines，來提高BDNF的表達水準。本課題的研究成果將有助於我們瞭解在阻塞性呼吸睡眠暫停綜合征中神經認知功能障礙所形成的原因，也為研發設計出針對阻塞性呼吸睡眠暫停綜合征所引起神經系統問題的輔助性藥物鋪平了道路

479213.label: Major findings and research outcome
479213.value: We characterised the effect of chronic intermittent hypoxia on both working memory and long-term memory of the test rats, and found that while the working memory is mildly affected, spatial long-term memory of the animals is significantly affected. At the same time, sleep architecture is also disrupted by the intermittent hypoxia treatment per se. These results indicate that OSA-associated chronic intermittent hypoxia have a negative impact on neurocognitive function and sleep structure. We hypothesised that OSA-associated intermittent hypoxia impacts on neuronal function via ER stress leading to sub-lethal malfunctions of neurons. In one experiment, two weeks of intermittent hypoxia disrupted ER fine structure and upregulated ER stress markers Grp 78, caspase-12 and CHOP in the hippocampus. Meanwhile, ER stress induced apoptosis via decreased Bcl-2, and promoted reactive oxygen species production, increased malonaldehyde formation and protein carbonyl as well as suppressed mitochondrial function. In another set of experiments, by means of in vivo electrophysiological recordings via chronically implanted multi-electrode arrays in a rat model of OSA, we found that both pyramidal neurons and interneurons in the hippocampal CA1 subfield were hyper-excitable during the first week of CIH treatment, which was followed by progressive suppression of neural firing in the longer term. Partial recovery of the neuronal activities was found after normoxia treatment but only in pyramidal neurons. Learning and memory-related hippocampal theta rhythm was also diminished irreversibly in CIH. These findings correlated well to abnormalities in dendritic spine morphogenesis of these neurons. The results reveal that hippocampal neurons respond to CIH in a complex biphasic and bidirectional manner eventually leading to suppression of firing activities as well as memory-related brain rhythm. Importantly, these changes are attributed to a larger extent to impaired functions of interneurons than to pyramidal neurons. Based on the findings from previous reports of the team and also the results of the present proposal, two pharmaceutical paradigms were tested for potential beneficial effects. First, administration of ER stress inhibitors tauroursodeoxycholic acid (TUDCA) and 4-phenylbutyrate was able to rectify both functional and morphological deficits observed in the OSA model. Second, administration of ampakines, a group of small molecules that could upregulate endogenous BDNF level, was also able to alleviate neurocognitive symptoms and long-term synaptic plasticity defects in chronic intermittent hypoxia. These results indicate possible treatment of OSA-associated neurocognitive symptoms by pharmacological approach.

479213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
479213.value: Our results not only help uncover the mechanisms underlying structural and functional deficits in the hippocampus in chronic intermittent hypoxia leading to neurocognitive dysfunction of OSA subjects, the use of ER stress inhibitors and ampakines in alleviating the symptoms highly encourage further exploration of pharmacological approach as adjunct treatment for managing OSA in the clinics.

479213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
479213.value: Chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH) occurs in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), a very common sleep-disordered breathing associated with malfunctions in multiple organs including the brain. How OSA-associated CIH impacts on brain activities and functions leading to neurocognitive impairment is virtually unknown. The present study helped underpin the mechanisms underlying the emergence of neurocognitive dysfunction, in particular, memory function in OSA subjects based on an animal model study. The results pinpoint the important role of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress during intermittent hypoxia leading to both structural and functional deficits of neurons in the hippocampus. We also tested the effect of suppressing ER stress in alleviating the symptoms occurring in OSA, and support adjunct drug treatment in the management of OSA.
