479813.label: Project Objectives
479813.value: To investigate the CNS uptakes of the RS flavones and their relationships with the anxiolytic effect of RS; To further identify the role of each RS flavone in the overall anxiolytic effect of RS;
rows: To investigate the CNS uptakes of the RS flavones and their relationships with the anxiolytic effect of RS;
To further identify the role of each RS flavone in the overall anxiolytic effect of RS;

479813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
479813.value: In addition to well-reported anti-oxidative, anti-inflammatory and anti-cancer activities, the CNS effects of dietary flavonoids have started to attract biomedical research attention over the past two decades. Studies from others and us have demonstrated that flavones from Radix Scutellariae (RS) could interact with benzodiazepine binding site of the GABA type A receptor, leading to anxiolytic and anticonvulsive effects. In comparison to their reported CNS activities, the CNS uptakes of flavones following administration of either pure compound or RS have never been fully investigated, let alone the blood brain barrier (BBB) uptake mechanisms behind it. Our preliminary experiments indicated certain amounts of CNS uptake of not only flavone aglycones but also their hydrophilic glucuronides, suggesting potential transporter mediated uptake of these glucuronides across the BBB. The present study hypothesizes that RS flavones, especially their glucuronide metabolites, can be taken up into the CNS system via either passive diffusion (for flavone aglycones) or active transporters (for glucuronide metabolites of RS flavones) to contribute to the overall anxiolytic effect of RS in-vivo. The present study aims to: 1) investigate the CNS uptakes of the RS flavones and their relationships with the anxiolytic effect of RS; 2) further identify the role of each RS flavone in the overall anxiolytic effect of RS; 3) further investigate the CNS uptake mechanisms of RS flavones and their corresponding glucuronides. It is expected that by further mechanistic studies on CNS effective flavonoids, we can develop RS into an effective alternative anti-anxiety product to avoid typical side effects caused by western anxiolytic drugs.

479813.label: Realisation of objectives
479813.value: In order to explore the CNS uptake of the RS flavones, we investigated and compared brain uptake of the six studied flavones after oral administration of both RS standardized extract and single componnets. • The content (w/w) of the six bioactive marker compounds in the studied RS extract in descending order are baicalin (48.0%), oroxyloside (3.78%), baicalein (2.08%), wogonoside (1.60%), wogonin (0.40%) and oroxylin A (0.15%) as quantified by our LC-MS/MS method. • An LC-MS/MS method was also developed for simultaneous determination of the studied RS components in plasma and brain. • Brain uptake of six flavones after oral administration of RS extract at 600 & 1200 mg/kg:At the current studied doses, all the six RS flavones were identified in mice brain at pmol/mL levels, with oroxylin A (94-224 pmol/mL) and baicalin (77-134 pmol/mL) being the most abundant ones, followed by oroxyloside (20-43 pmol/mL), baicalein (18-26 pmol/mL), wogonin (9-17 pmol/mL), and wogonoside (8-12 pmol/mL). The plasma concentrations of these flavones were much higher (at nmol/mL levels) than their corresponding brain concentrations. In descending order, the abundance of plasma concentrations of the RS flavones was baicalin (6.6-10.6 nmol/mL) > oroxyloside (2.0-5.7 nmol/mL) > oroxylin A (0.28-0.71 nmol/mL) > wogonoside (0.10-0.28 nmol/mL) ~ baicalein (0.10-0.17 nmol/mL) > wogonin (0.06-0.11 nmol/mL). It should be noted that the sequence of plasma abundance followed that of the original RS flavone content, except for oroxylin A which was the least abundant flavone in RS extract but was the third most abundant flavone detected in plasma. By comparing the brain and plasma concentrations of the flavones in mice receiving 600 mg/kg of RS extract with that receiving 1200 mg/kg of RS extract, it was found that doubled dose resulted in a proportionally doubled brain and plasma concentrations. • Brain uptake of flavones after oral administration of individual components: The concentrations of the six flavones in plasma and brain at the same moler dose (52.8 μmol/kg) 1 h post drug administration to mice were compared. The plasma concentrations of these flavones were much higher than their corresponding brain concentrations. In plasma, there were two isomers (BG and BG’) identified in mice plasma after the administration of B, whereas there was only BG detected in brain. BG could be detected after administration of OA, which indicated that OA was firstly demethylized into B and further metabolized by glucuronidation. No matter aglycones or glycosides were administrated, there was only aglycone (B, OA) form detected in brain except for WG (both W & WG are detectable in brain, W>> WG), with the rank order of OA (1.307±0.703 nmol/g for OAG and 0.748±0.715 nmol/g for OA) > W (0.146±0.030 nmol/g for WG and 0.134±0.022 nmol/g for W) > B (0.053±0.031 nmol/g for BG and 0.060±0.028 nmol/g for B). The aglycone form of each flavones could not be deteced in plasma. • Brain uptake of flavones after combination administration of two anxyiolytic components B and W: It was also found that the drug combination B+W could increase the brain concentration of W (0.165±0.062 nmol/g vs 0.134±0.022 nmol/g) and WG (0.119±0.105 nmol/g vs 0.049±0.025 nmol/g) compared with the concentration when W was administrated alone, which may lead to enhanced activities for B+W. The plasma concentration of WG was increased by the drug combination of B+W (0.882±0.358 nmol/ml vs 0.192±0.071 nmol/ml, p<0.001) and BG+WG (1.196±0.585 nmol/ml vs 0.605±0.247 nmol/ml). On the contrary, the concentration of BG was decreased by the drug combination of B+W (0.372±0.106 nmol/ml vs 0.525±0.071 nmol/ml) and BG+WG (0.209±0.105 nmol/ml vs 0.982±0.369 nmol/ml). Such change in formation of WG and BG could be due to their competition in same UGT metabolisms. The anxiolytics effects of RS flavones were investigated by monitoring and comparing the time spent in the mice elevated plus maze model after oral administrations of RS standardized extract and single componnets at their equivalent doses in the RS extract. • RS extract did not demonstrate anxiolytic effect in elevated plus-maze: The effects of oral administration of vehicle, diazepam (1 mg/kg), and RS extract at two studied doses (600 mg/kg and 1200 mg/kg) on the anxiolytic behavior of mice in elevated plus-maze were conducted and compared. As a positive control, diazepam significantly increased the percentage of open arm entries and open arm time spent [F(3,71)=5.954, p<0.05 and F(3,71)=7.239, p<0.05 respectively], while decreasing the closed arm time spent [F(3,71)=7.239, p<0.05]. These results indicated the anxiolytic and locomotor depressive effect of diazepam. On the other hand, mice receiving RS extract at doses of 600 mg/kg and 1200 mg/kg (twice oral doses) did not result in a significantly different open arm entries, open arm time spent or closed arm time spent compared with that receiving vehicle control (p>0.05). Therefore, RS extract at the current studied doses did not exert anxiolytic effect on mice in elevated plus-maze model. • W and WG demonstrated similar anxiolytic effect at same molar dose: In comparison to vehicle control, diazepam and W/WG significantly increased the percentage of open arm entries and open arm time spent (p<0.001), while decreasing the closed arm time spent (p<0.001). The anxiolytic effect of W and WG were comparable when they were administrated at the same molar doses (52.8 μmol/kg). • Combination use of B with BG/W did not exert synergic anxiolytic effect: In comparison to vehicle control, diazepam and B significantly increased the open arm time spent (p<0.001 and p<0.05). The co-administration of BG or W did not exert synergic effect with B. • Anxiolytic effect of W: The anxiolytic effect of W was less than B. Although W did not significantly increase the open arm time spent compared with control, the combined use of B and WG could enhance its anxiolytic effect. Based on the absence of anxiolytic effect observed, mechanistic studies were further conducted to identify the reasons: • Role of transporter in the brain uptake of six flavones: Incubation of B, W, OA, BG, WG and OAG at 1 μM and 10 μM with HEK293/MOCK and HEK293/OAT3 cells found that there was no cell uptake of BG, WG and OAG in either HEK293/MOCK cells or HEK293/OAT3 cells, indicating no involvement of OAT3 in their brain uptake. Compared with the amount in HEK293/MOCK cells, the cell uptake in HEK293/OAT3 cells were increased for B and decreased for W and OA, indicating that B is a possible substrate of OAT3 while W/OA might serve as the OAT3 inhibitor. • Brain affinities of the six flavones: It was found that the affinity to brain of the aglycones (B, W & OA) are much higher than their corresponding glycosides (BG, WG & OAG). The Vu,brain of OA was the highest among six falvones with the rank order of OA>W>B>>OAG>WG>BG, which is consist with our findings in the in vivo brain distribution of SR flavone in ICR mice. In addition, the Vu,brain of all the aglycones (B, W, OA) ranged from 111.1±27.1 to 934.7±182.3, indicating a rather high brain uptake potential. It was concluded that the aglycones (B, W and OA) demonstrated greater brain uptake than their corresponding glycosides BG, WG and OAG. among the three aglycones, OA showed the highest affinity to the brain regardless of its limited content in RS extract. Thus, it is concluded that the lack of anxiolytic effect of RS extract is due to the high CNS uptake of OA/OAG.

479813.label: Major findings and research outcome
479813.value: Our current study explored the CNS uptake of the Radix Scutellariae (RS) flavones, namely baicalein (B), baicalin (baicalein-7-glucuronide, BG), wogonin (W), wogonoside (wogonin-7-glucuronide, WG), oroxylin A (OA) and oroxylin A-7-glucuronide (OAG) and their relationship with the anxiolytic effects. Although there are significant levels of brain uptake of the studied flavones from RS extract, the standardized RS extract (containing BG (48.0% w/w), OAG (3.78%, w/w), B (2.08%, w/w), WG (1.60%, w/w), W (0.40%, w/w) and OA (0.15%, w/w) at doses of 600 & 1200 mg/kg did not exert significant anxiolytic effect on mice in elevated plus-maze model. Our further mecahnistics studies indicated that the anxiolytic effect of RS extract is dependent on the extent of brain uptake of anxylitic components of B, BG, W and WG versus that from the antagonistic components of OA and OAG. Among the anyiolytic active components, W/WG showed less effect than that from B/BG. In addition, W and WG demonstrated similar anxiolytic activity at the samle molar dose, due to their similar pharmacokinetics resulted from the hydrolysis of WG into W after its oral administration. It was found that the combination administration of B with W could increase the brain concentration of W and WG, resulting from their competition of UGT enzyme for metabolisms, which may lead to enhanced activities for B+W. Among the six studied components, the aglycones (B, W and OA) demonstrated greater brain uptake than their corresponding glycosides BG, WG and OAG. Among the three aglycones, OA showed the highest affinity to the brain regarless of its limited content in RS extract. Thus, it is concluded that the lack of anxiolytic effect of RS extract is due to the high CNS uptake of OA/OAG.

479813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
479813.value: Our study clearly identify that absence of OA/OAG is essential for demonstration of the anxiolytic effect of RS extract. Further product development of RS extract with and without OA/OAG could be employed to serve for different therapeutic purpose related to anxiolytic activities.

479813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
479813.value: Our research on the brain uptake of flavonoids for the first time suggested that flavonoids with similar structures can demonstrated different level of brain uptake and different level of CNS effect. Due to the high affinity to brain and anxiolytic antagonist effect of OA/OAG, minimization of their contents in the RS extract is essential for its demonstration of the anxiolytic effect. Understanding the mechanisms behind this will lead to the further product development of RS extract.

489213.label: Realisation of objectives
489213.value: Till the end of the project, we have accomplished all three specific aims: 1) To examine the distribution of Plekho1 siRNA delivered by the liposome with and without the target moiety (AspSerSer)6 at cellular (osteogenic vs. non-osteogenic cells) level; 2) To test the gene knockdown efficiency of Plekho1 siRNA delivered by the liposome with and without the target moiety (AspSerSer)6 at cellular (osteogenic vs. non-osteogenic cells) level in aged male rats; 3) To evaluate the effect of Plekho1 siRNA delivered by the (AspSerSer)6-liposome on bone formation, bone mass, bone structure, bone strength and the safety for non-skeletal organs. For specific aim 1&2, twenty aged (sixteen-month-old) male SD rats were intravenously injected with Plekho1 siRNA delivered with liposome (Liposome-siRNA Group, n=10) or Plekho1 siRNA delivered with (AspSerSer)6-Liposome ((AspSerSer)6-Liposome siRNA Group, n=10). The Plekho1 siRNA was labeled with FAM (fluorescein amidite). All the rats were sacrificed four hours after the administration. To examine the distribution and knockdown efficiency of Plekho1 siRNA at cellular level in skeletal tissue, the right femur was dissected and decalcified. After that, the cryosections from the decalcified distal femur were subjected to immunostaining for co-localization of siRNA signal and osteocalcin. Thereafter, laser capture micro-dissection (LCM) in combination with Q-PCR analysis was performed for Plekho1 mRNA level in osteogenic/non-osteogenic cells as determined by osteocalcin-positive staining. For specific aim 3, 40 aged male SD rats were divided into four groups (n=10): Baseline group, Plekho1 siRNA group, Non-sense siRNA group and Vehicle group. All agents were intravenously administrated for six periodic injections at an interval of two weeks. Three months after the first administration, all rats were sacrificed. Ten days and three days before sacrifice, all rats were injected intraperitoneally with calcein green (10mg/kg) and xylenol orange (30mg/kg), respectively, to label bone formation surface. The 5th lumbar vertebrae body of each rat was collected and evaluated by micro-CT scanning. Serum was examined for liver function index and kidney function index. The left femur was fixed in 70% ethanol for un-decalcified bone histomorphometry. The right femur was evaluated by three-point bending test. The project has validated the hypothesis that silencing Plekho1 gene expression by RNAi in osteogenic cells could promote bone formation in aged men. It has helped to establish CKIP-1’s role as an important regulator of bone formation in aged male skeleton, and also provides a novel RNAi-based pharmacologic inhibitor of CKIP-1 for bone anabolic strategy to reverse age-related bone loss in aged men, thereby reducing fracture risk. 489213.label: Major findings and research outcome
489213.value: For specific aim 1&2, the immunostaining data showed numerous instances of co-localization of the labeled siRNA with osteocalcin-positive (OCN+) cells in (AspSerSer)6-Liposome-siRNA group than that in Liposome-siRNA group (Figure 1). The knockdown efficiency of Plekho1 siRNA in OCN+ cells was significantly higher when compared to that in Osteocalcin-negative (OCN-) cells in (AspSerSer)6-Liposome-siRNA group, whereas no difference was found between OCN+ cells and OCN- cells in Liposome-siRNA group (Figure 2). These evidences indicate that (AspSerSer)6 could facilitate bone anabolic siRNA specifically targeting osteogenic cells in aged, gonad-intact male rats for translation of RNAi-based bone anabolic strategy. For specific aim 3, the microCT analysis data showed better organized trabecular micro-architecture in the rats from siRNA Group compared to the rats in Baseline, Non-sense siRNA and Vehicle groups (Figure 3A). Consistently, the trabecular parameters (bone mineral density, relative bone volume, trabecular thickness and trabecular number) in siRNA group were notably higher when compared to those in other groups (Figure 3B). The bone histomorphometric analysis data showed that the bone-formation-related parameters (bone formation rate, mineral apposition rate and osteoblast surface) in siRNA Group were all significantly increased from baseline and higher than those in Non-sense siRNA and Vehicle groups, whereas the bone resorption-related parameter (osteoclast surface) was unchanged among all the groups (Figure 4). The three-point bending test showed that the ultimate load and energy-to-failure in siRNA group were both significantly higher than those in Non-sense siRNA and Vehicle groups (Figure 5). Furthermore, no obvious changes in the serum liver function index (alanine aminotransferase and asporatate aminotransferase), kidney function index (BUN), hematology parameters (total protein, hemoglobin, white blood cell, red blood cell, and platelet) were found in rats after (AspSerSer)6-Liposome-siRNA administration (Table 1). These evidences indicate that silencing Plekho1 gene expression by RNAi in osteogenic cells could promote bone formation in aged male rats. 489213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
489213.value: The current project has demonstrated PLEKHO1’s role as an important regulator of bone formation in aged male skeleton, and also provides a novel RNAi-based pharmacologic inhibitor of Plekho1 for bone anabolic strategy to reverse age-related bone loss in aged male rats. Our further development of the research is to explore the application of this RNAi-based bone anabolic strategy in human being. (AspSerSer)6-liposome is a promising targeting system for specifically delivering siRNA drugs to bone-formation surfaces and osteogenic cells that reside there, thus providing a potential solution to the bottleneck in clinical translation of RNAi-based bone anabolic therapies. Furthermore, (AspSerSer)6-liposome could conjunct with other small molecules including natural products besides the siRNA. It has a great potential to extend the bone-targeted therapy by utilizing this (AspSerSer)6-liposome system to specifically deliver the different kinds of bone anabolic agents to the bone tissue for their therapeutic use. We have started to investigate the application of this delivery system to bone-targeted therapy with other samll molecules in musculoskeletal disorders.

489213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
489213.value: (Asp-Ser-Ser)6 is a newly identified peptide selectively targeting osteogenic cells via specifically approaching bone formation surface, which has been validated as a target moiety for targeted delivery of osteogenic siRNA (e.g. Plekho1 siRNA) encapsulated within liposome in adult healthy rodents (Zhang G, et al. 2012). So, the target moiety could facilitate osteogenic siRNA targeting osteogenic cells to achieve RNAi-based bone anabolic strategy in reversing established osteoporosis. The current project has demonstrated the specific distribution of (AspSerSer)6-Liposome-Plekho1 siRNA and high knockdown efficiency of Plekho1 at cellular level in bone tissue of aged male rats. It has further shown the promising anabolic effect of (AspSerSer)6-Liposome-Plekho1 siRNA with safety in bone tissue of aged male rats. The project has helped to establish CKIP-1’s role as an important regulator of bone formation in aged male skeleton, and also provides a novel RNAi-based pharmacologic inhibitor of CKIP-1 for bone anabolic strategy to reverse age-related bone loss in aged men, thereby reducing fracture risk.

489813.label: Project Objectives
489813.value: Aim 1a: develop in silico, agent-based analogues of the human gastrointestinal tract to model drug absorption. Starting with an abstract, semi-validated prototype, we will iteratively add additional features in three key aspects: 1) physicochemical properties of drugs, 2) gastrointestinal physiologic features, and 3) interactions between formulation and luminal fluid. These will be validated against known gastrointestinal physiology in the literature, and available human drug absorption data from bioequivalent studies for a set of chemically-diverse drugs. The ISDAT may then be used to explore effects of genetic variants and complex formulations. Aim 1b: build the supporting simulation framework and graphical user interface. Aim 2: use traditional pharmacometric methods, including population pharmacokinetic models (NONMEM®) and/or physiologically-based pharmacokinetic models (SimCyp® or others) to analyze the same human data and simulated data, in parallel to Aim 1. Cross-validations between the analogues and traditional pharmacometric models increase trust and acceptance in ISDAT.

489813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
489813.value: 此項研究計畫旨在開發模擬藥物吸收道(ISDAT)，藉科學法建模和模擬來研究藥物的吸收和生物利用度。 模擬藥物吸收道採用個體為本、多層和仿生的模擬手法，以電腦軟件演算描述和模擬胃腸道的生理功能，腸道管腔液的特性，及其對吸收相應藥物的影響。透過科學法建模和模擬，我們將能綜合有關藥物吸收的知識，從而更深入暸解藥物吸收的生理機制。 完成開發ISDAT原型軟件及其相關的模擬平台後，ISDAT將能為我們模擬和預測藥物血液濃度和藥物製劑的吸收、生物利用度及生物等效性。ISDAT亦能幫助我們解答有關藥物吸收、藥物相亙作用、控釋製劑及藥物代謝酶和輸送體基因變異等假設問題。在藥物製劑的研發過程中，以ISDAT作藥物代謝動力學模擬將能合理地、有根據地預測藥物製劑在臨牀測試中的表現和藥物生物等效性，從而減低研發成本。因此，ISDAT將能成為藥物製劑研發中不可或缺的工具。

489813.label: Realisation of objectives
489813.value: The team has successfully constructed propotypical software that represent the human gastrointestinal tract during drug absorption, thus achieving our Aim 1. An agent-based biomimetic model, in silico drug absorption tract (ISDAT), was built to mimic oral drug absorption in humans. The model consisted of distinct spaces, membranes, and metabolic enzymes, and it was altogether representative of human physiology relating to oral drug absorption. Simulated experiments were run with the model, and the results were compared to the referent data from clinical equivalence trials. Acceptable similarity was verified by pre-specified criteria. A graphical user interface was developed together with the ISDAT. The ISDAT met all the pre-specified similarity criteria for both midazolam and clonazepam, and demonstrated its ability to describe absorption kinetics of both drugs. Therefore, the validated ISDAT can be a promising platform for further research into the use of similar in silico models for drug absorption kinetics. We reported back in 2016 that the team had run into problems with using physiologically-based pharmacokinetic models (e.g. SimCyp) to mimic the bioequivalence data we have. Due of the proprietory nature of these software, we were unable to parameterize or modify it to obtain acceptable fit and therefore we have determined that those software were not suitable for cross-validation. Subsequent cross-validation was conducted by comparing PK parameters obtained from ISDAT to those from the traditional noncompartmental analysis of the data. As reported in the publication, they matched exceptionally well. On top of the ISDAT, the software we developed also enabled an assembly of alternative in silico pharmacokinetic models. Of note, an In Silico Enterocyte Monolayer model was developed and used in studying enzyme-transporter interplay in an in vitro cell monolayer experiment.

489813.label: Major findings and research outcome
489813.value: The project is best represented by the ISDAT software we developed, and it is reported in PLoS ONE in 2018, entitled, "In silico drug absorption tract: An agent-based biomimetic model for human oral drug absorption. In addition, we published a review of food-drug interaction on oral drug absorption in Drugs in 2017. The software is available freely at the principal investigator's website. (http://www.pharmacy.cuhk.edu.hk/1/about-us/academic-staff/teddylam/?target=supplementary+information) Comparing the simulated profiles with our bioequivalence dataset, simulations results from ISDAT satisfied all three levels of similarity criteria for both drugs. The weighted RMSE was 0.51 and 0.92, and the weighted MAPE was 5.99% and 8.43% for midazolam and clonazepam, respectively. Calculated PK parameter values, including area under the curve (AUC), peak plasma drug concentration (Cmax), time to reach Cmax (Tmax), terminal elimination rate constant (Kel), terminal elimination half life (T1/2), apparent oral clearance (CL/F), and apparent volume of distribution (V/F), were reasonable compared to the referent values. The predicted absolute oral bioavailability (F) was 44% for midazolam (literature reported value, 31–72%) and 93% (literature reported value, ≥ 90%) for clonazepam. The abovementioned two publications, as well as numerous conference abstracts of the results from the ISDAT and in silico enterocyte model are listed in Part C of this report.

489813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
489813.value: The ISDAT represents a promising alternative modelling approach in studying the mechanisms and pharmacokinetics of oral drug absorption. Future work is suggested to further develop the ISDAT to incorporate more physiological features of the gastrointestinal tract that are involved in oral drug absorption. On the other hand, the software we developed can be alternatively assembled to model other tissues and/or organs of pharmacokinetic interests. Our in silico model of the enterocytes has demonstrated its potential. Therefore, another line of future development is to assemble the parts into a different model and use them to study pharmacokinetic behaviour other than oral drug absorption. The principal investigator is actively seeking further research funding to carry out the abovementioned future work.

489813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
489813.value: The in silico drug absorption tract (ISDAT) is a computational software that mimics the processes of oral drug absorption in humans. It is expected that the software will accelerate drug development by providing the pharmaceutical scientists better tools in understanding various interconnected mechanisms of drug absorption, and additional screening and/or predictive tools during early drug development.

490113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
490113.value: Nowadays because of the fierce competition in the global economy, many original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) outsource part of their production processes to external suppliers. By so doing, OEMs can reduce production costs and focus on their core competencies such as product design and marketing (Kakabadse & Kakabadse, 2005). It is widely believed that the trend of outsourcing will continue to increase in the near future (Stevens, 2009). This emphasizes the importance of research on outsourcing in operations management literature. A prevailing practice in production outsourcing is the so-called contract manufacturing whereby an OEM outsources its production to a contract manufacturer. In the electronics manufacturing industry, for example, many OEMs nowadays outsource manufacturing, distribution, and other related services to electronics manufacturing service (EMS) providers. In order to fulfill the production function, the contract manufacturer may need to procure certain parts and components from its suppliers that can be procured by the OEM or the contract manufacturer itself. This gives rise to a fundamental question in such a setting: should the OEM control the procurement of components or delegate this task to its contract manufacturers? In this project we propose to study the effect of competition and bargaining power on OEMs’ component procurement decisions. We will consider a three-tier supply chain that consists of two OEMs, two contract manufacturers, and two suppliers. The objective of each OEM is to jointly determine the optimal component procurement structure (i.e., delegation or control of component procurement) and its product pricing to maximize its profit. By casting our problem in a competitive setting, wherein two OEMs produce partially substitutable products, our study will offer a new perspective in component procurement decisions for OEMs. We expect to gain new managerial insights into the effect of OEMs’ component procurement decisions on all supply chain firms. These new findings will have the potential to complement and enrich the existing literature in economics and supply chain management. Our research will also have the potential to contribute to the regional economic and business development of the greater China region; this is because most of contract manufacturers and suppliers of large multi-national OEMs are located there and any change in the OEMs’ component procurement policies directly affects them. Therefore, the optimal OEMs’ component procurement policies and their effects on these firms are important topics to be investigated in the literature. 如今，由于在全球经济环境下,企业竞争激烈。许多原始设备制造商（OEM ）把他们一部分的生产流程外包给外部的供应商。 在这种举措下，OEM 可以降低生产成本并专注于产品设计和市场营销等自己的核心竞争优势 (Kakabadse and Kakabadse 2005)。这种外包模式已经被广泛地认为将在未来的几十年中延续(Stevens 2009)。因此，对外包模式的研究有着重要的学术的价值。 合同生产外包是一种普遍业界采纳的外包制造模式。例如，在电子制造行业，许多OEM 将制造、分销以及相关的服务外包给相应的电子制造服务供应商（零部件制造商）。为了能够满足生产的要求，合同制造商可能需要从其他供应商采购部分的零部件，而这些零部件本可以由OEM或零部件制造商制造。因此，以上外包模式产生了一个根本的问题：是否OEM应该控制这些零部件的采购还是将这个采购任务完全交给与其签订合约的生产商？ 在本项目中，我们计划研究竞争能力和议价能力对OEM的零部件采购决策的影响。我们研究由两个OEM、零部件制造商和两家供应商组成的三层供应链结构。每个OEM的目标是共同决定最优的零部件采购结构，即是否控制零部件的采购。此外，OEM同时需要决定其产品价格以最大化自身利润。在竞争的环境下，考虑到两家OEM生产部分可替代产品，因此我们的研究将提供一种对零部件采购决策的新视角。从中我们希望获得对所有供应链公司的OEM的零部件采购决策的管理新见解。这些新发现可补充和丰富现有的经济学和供应链管理文献。鉴于大多数大型跨国OEM的合同制造商和供应商都位于大中华地区，此外任何的OEM零部件采购策略的变化直接影响零部件制造商和供应商，我们的研究也有助于区域经济和大中华地区的业务发展。综上所述，最优的OEM零部件采购策略及其对整个供应链成员的影响是一个重要的经营管理研究课题。

490113.label: Major findings and research outcome
490113.value: This research studies the optimal component procurement strategies of two competing OEMs selling substitutable products. The OEMs outsource their production to a common contract manufacturer, who in turn needs an input from a component supplier. Each OEM may either directly procure the input from the component supplier, or delegate the procurement task to the contract manufacturer. We first analyze the OEMs’ procurement game under a non-strategic supplier whose component price is exogenously given. It is found that symmetric equilibria arise for most situations, that is, both OEMs either control or delegate their component procurement in equilibrium. Interestingly, despite the commonly-held belief that the contract manufacturer would be worse off as OEMs gain component procurement control, we show that the contract manufacturer may enjoy a higher profit. Then we study the OEMs’ procurement game under a strategic supplier who can set its component price. We find that the supplier’s strategic pricing behavior plays a critical role in the equilibrium procurement structure. In particular, in the equilibrium under strategic supplier, the larger OEM always uses delegation while the smaller OEM may use either delegation or control. By identifying the driving forces behind the OEMs’ procurement choices, this research helps explain observed industry practices and offer useful guidelines for firms’ component sourcing decisions.

490113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
490113.value: An important future extension of this problem is to explicitly model negotiations and bargaining power of different players in the model and try to figure out how power distribution in this supply chain might affect firms' decision to delegate or control their component procurement for their manufacturer's. In this study, it has been assumed that the supplier’s discount rate for its product is exogenously given. A potential direction for future research is to relax this assumption and examine how the results may change. Also it is interesting to know what would happen if we have more than one supplier and one type of input products.

490113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
490113.value: In this competitive market place, firms need to think carefully about their procurement strategies. Any reduction in input costs can make them more competitive in the market. The fact is that supply chains are becoming long, which means my manufacturer has many suppliers that have suppliers of their own and this chain is getting longer and longer. A relevant question for any firm is that do I need to care about my manufacturer's suppliers and probably directly contract with them to procure my manufacturer's input. Can this direct procurement help me in the competitive market? Our research tries to answer this question. In a simple stylized supply chain we shed some light on this question.

490313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
490313.value: Abstract Strategic human resource management system (SHRM) is one of the most crucial contextual influences on employee behavior and attitudes and has a critical influence on companies’ bottom-line performance. Surprisingly, however, little research has been done on how the hotel industry can benefit from the effective use of SHRM. In this study, we aim to advance knowledge of how SHRM can help the hotel industry in Hong Kong and the world in general achieve exceptional performance. In the meantime, research suggests that the hotel industry is an interesting context in which to study SHRM. Its worldwide growth is continually increasing; the impact of software (that is, people) on firm performance is as important as, or perhaps even more important than, hardware (that is, infrastructure); companies have to face a tension between regular and contingent employees; and the average industry turnover rate is worryingly high. The study addresses two research questions. Firstly, the extant SHRM research highlights the best fit perspective. However, understanding of this perspective remains limited and the extant work has largely focused on the horizontal fit among HR practices within SHRM and the vertical fit between SHRM and environmental factors. We are particularly interested in advancing understanding of this perspective by assessing the fit between SHRM and intra-organizational characteristics (for example, at the team level, task interdependence and team climate; at the individual level, personality and values). Secondly, an important question that deserves more research attention is why so few hotel firms actually adopt SHRM, given the obvious financial and HR returns associated with it. We aim to develop a comprehensive framework that addresses hotel firms’ opportunity, ability, and motivation to adopt SHRM. On completion of the study, we expect to have systematically advanced conceptual and empirical knowledge about how to promote the competitiveness of the hotel industry in Hong Kong in particular and the world in general through SHRM. Concrete and practical suggestions and implications for policymakers are also expected to emerge. 企业人力资源管理系统是影响雇员行为以及绩效的最重要影响因素之一。同时，研究已经证明企业人力资源管理系统对公司层面的绩效也有显著影响。有趣的是，尽管酒店行业是个人力资本密集度非常高的行业，人力资源管理方面的研究在这个行业还不是非常成熟。在这项研究中，我和我的合作者将系统研究人力资源管理在酒店行业中的作用。 与此同时，研究表明酒店行业是企业人力资源管理系统研究中一个有价值的研究领域。酒店行业正在世界范围内快速增长。软实力（人力资本）对其业内公司的绩效影响已经可以与硬实力（基础设施）等同，甚至超过硬实力的影响力。行业内的企业也普遍面临着正式员工同临时员工之间的矛盾问题。此外，人员流失率过高的行业状况也令人担忧。 本文主要着眼于研究两个问题。首先，现阶段的企业人力资源管理系统研究大多数集中于人力资源管理实践同人力资源管理系统的横向关系，和人力资源管理系统同环境因素的纵向关系这两个层面上。我们的研究则着重于提高对人力资源管理系统同组织内部特性（例如，在团队层面，任务的相互依存和团队氛围；在个人层面，个性和价值观）之间协调性的评价上。第二，另一个值得关注的问题是，尽管企业人力资源管理系统可以带来明显的财务和人力资源回报，仍然很少有酒店企业采用了系统的人力资源管理系统。我们的研究目的是通过建立一个整体的模型框架，来研究酒店公司采纳企业人力资源管理的机会、能力同动机。 在完成研究后，我们期待能够对于如何发展香港乃至世界酒店行业的竞争力有系统性的先进理论认知同实践理解，同时能够为政策制定者提供切实有效的政策参考同建议。

490313.label: Realisation of objectives
490313.value: In this project, my co-investigators and I were interested in the antecedents and consequences of human resource management (HRM) issues in the hospitality sector in particular and in the management field in general. We have successfully collected three main datasets out of this project. In the first dataset (Data 1), we collected 294 paired employee-supervisor data from two hotel properties. In the second dataset (Data 2), we collected 282 paired employee-supervisor data nested within 65 supervisors and 3 non-hotel (manufacturing) organizations. In the third dataset (Data 3), we collected 303 paired employee-supervisor data nested within 71 supervisors and 37 hotels. We collected these multiple datasets to enhance the generalizability of our findings across contexts (e.g., Chang, Gong, Way, & Jia, 2013). While such data collection schemes took us more effort in collecting data, we believe it would greatly increase our ability and confidence to draw more rigorous and informative conclusions, particularly regarding the topic of HRM. This multi-source, multi-wave, and multi-study research design could also increase the chance for us to publish our work at top-tier journals later on. With these data points, we are able to develop multiple studies to address the original research objectives at this stage, as we shall state below. Original Objective 1: Understand the fit between HRM and intra-organizational characteristics. We have fully achieved this objective. In particular, we have provided a deeper understanding on the role of HRM in the hospitality management field in particular and the management filed in general via multiple studies. Study 1. In this study (using Data 1), we examined whether individual front-line, customer-contact employees’ perceived firm HRM practices would positively affect these employees’ supervisor-rated innovative behaviour. Moreover, we examined whether these employees’ attitudes toward change and absorptive capacity would mediate the aforementioned relationship. Drawing upon prior research on the role of employees’ perceived HRM practices (e.g., Bowen & Ostroff, 2004; Liao, Toya, Lepak, & Hong, 2009), this study was one of the first studies to examine whether employees’ perceived HRM practices would affect their supervisor-rated innovative behaviour in the hospitality sector. In addition, we re-joined Hon and Lui’s (2016) conceptual call for empirical inquiries to investigate if readiness for change would mediate the relationship between its precursors (e.g., perceived HRM) and consequences (e.g., innovative behaviour). We also built upon prior work of Lowik, Kraaijenbrink, and Groen (2012) and were among the first to apply the notion of absorptive capacity, originated at the firm level research (e.g., Cohen & Levinthal, 1990), to the individual level of analysis. Overall, we extended prior pioneering research on HRM and creativity and innovation in the hospitality sector (e.g., Chang, Gong, & Shum, 2011), and addressed whether and how employees’ perceived HRM practices would affect their supervisor-rated innovative behaviour in this setting. An early version of this study has been accepted for a poster presentation at the 2017 International Council on Hotel, Restaurant, and Institutional Education. We have strengthened this paper both conceptually and empirically afterwards and now the revised study is ready for journal submissions. Study 2. In this study (using Data 2), we drew on social learning theory (Bandura, 1986) and also the recent research on leader humility (Owens & Hekman, 2012; Owens, Wallace, & Waldman, 2015) to investigate the relationships among leader humility, employees’ creative process engagement, HRM, and their supervisor-rated creativity. Leadership theorists emphasized that leadership behaviours were conducive to employee creativity. Tierney (2008: 95) particularly commented that “given the dynamic environment facing today’s organizations, a hallmark of contemporary leadership is the capacity to foster employee creativity”. Building on such arguments, in this study we revealed the complexity of how employee-rated leader humility (time 1, independent variable) could stand out and contribute to supervisor-rated employee creativity (time 3, outcome variable) via its impact on employee creative process engagement (time 2, the mediator). To the best of our knowledge, the current research was among the rare studies to investigate the cognitive mechanisms between leadership and employee creativity. Furthermore, we hypothesized and found that perceived HRM strengthened the link from leader humility to employee creative process engagement. That is, under the condition of both high HRM and humble leaders, employees were most likely to engage in creative process. This study integrated multiple lines of research and enhanced our understandings on why and when leader humility and HRM can affect employee creativity. An early draft of this study will be presented at the 2017 Asia Academy of Management Conference. Study 3. In this study (using Data 3), drawing upon the growing research on emotional intelligence (e.g., Walsh, Chang, & Tse, 2015), we assessed whether and how individual front-line, customer-contact employees’ emotional intelligence would matter to their supervisor-rated creativity (i.e., the causal chain of employees’ emotional intelligence->employees’ attitude toward change->supervisor-rated creativity). Moreover, we examined whether HRM director-rated job involvement practice would act as a firm-level contingency in strengthening the positive effect from individual front-line, customer-contact employees’ attitude toward change and their supervisor-rated creativity. This study aimed to make several contributions to the hospitality research in particular and the management research in general. First, scholars have recognized that emotional intelligence is an important individual difference that may create value for organizations. But the extant research has not systematically assessed the role of emotional intelligence in affecting individual creativity. Building upon the affect infusion model (Forgas, 2002) and the build-and-broaden theory (Fredrickson, 2001), we provided an initial effort in demonstrating the role and relevance of emotional intelligence in affecting individual creativity. Moreover, drawing upon the theory of unfreezing (Lewin, 1947), we assessed and found the role of employees’ attitude toward change in fully mediating the aforementioned relationship. Lastly, we introduced the notion of firm job involvement HRM practice and found that this practice provided a beneficial organizational context that amplified the positive effect of employees’ attitude toward change on creativity. We had finished an initial draft and are revising this draft for journal submissions. Original Objective 2: Understand the antecedents of HRM. We have partially addressed this objective. Given that we are trying to develop multiple studies to address Objective 1, so far we have not worked extensively on this objective. But we have explored the dataset and have some initial interesting findings regarding this objective. First, there is a very strong and positive association between general manager’s transformational leadership and the HRM implemented in hotels (r = .61, p < .01). Second, while general manager’s positional tenure also positively influences the HRM implemented in hotels (r = .30, p < .01), general managers’ age has a negative impact on the HRM implemented (r = -.28, p < .01). Third, absorptive capacity is positively associated with the level of HRM implemented (r = .49, p < .01). Lastly, hotels’ culture values (Tsui, Wang, & Xin, 2006) have the strongest impact on the HRM implemented in hotels (r = .84, p < .01). While such findings are largely correlational in nature, we are confident that with such initial interesting findings we could develop concrete studies later on, after we have made significant progress on studies to achieve Objective 1. (References are omitted due to the page limitation in this report; and they are available upon request and are all from premium hospitality management and management journals)

490313.label: Major findings and research outcome
490313.value: We have developed five studies and three of them have been accepted for conference presentations (i.e., Study 1, 2, and 4). Studies 1-3 have also been mentioned in Part 5.3. Study 1. In this study (Data 1), we found that employees’ perceived HRM enhanced both their readiness for change and absorptive capacity, and the latter two further enhanced these employees’ supervisor-rated innovative behavior. Furthermore, employees’ readiness for change and absorptive capacity fully mediated the impact of HRM on innovative behavior. Study 2. In this study (Data 2), we found that leader humility increased employees’ creative process engagement, and this engagement further mediated the relationship between leader humility and supervisor-rated employee creativity. Moreover, employees’ perceived HRM strengthened the positive link from leader humility to employees’ creative process engagement. Study 3. In this study (Data 3), we found that employees’ emotional intelligence enhanced their attitude toward change, and this attitude toward change fully mediated the impact of emotional intelligence on supervisor-rated creativity. Furthermore, HRM-director reported job involvement HRM practice strengthened the impact from employees’ attitude toward change and their supervisor-rated creativity. Study 4. In this study (Data 2), we found that employees’ mindfulness affected their supervisor-rated creativity via creative self-efficacy. Furthermore, we found that individuals’ competitive orientation weakened the positive effect from mindfulness to creative self-efficacy (i.e., a first stage moderated mediation model). This study contributed to the mindfulness and creativity research in several ways. First, we deepened our understandings on the role and relevance of mindfulness in organizations. Second, we provided a new perspective to understand the motives toward employee creativity via the role of a psychological process of creative self-efficacy. Third, we introduced the notion of employee competitive orientation to organizational research. An early version of this study will be presented at the 2017 Asia Academy of Management Conference. Study 5. In this study (Data 2), we found employees’ perceived HRM decreased their turnover intention via the mediating role of intrinsic motivation. Furthermore, we found that employees’ emotional intelligence strengthened the relationship between perceived HRM and intrinsic motivation. This study extended prior research in the following ways. First, this study represented one of the first attempts to investigate whether employees’ perceived HRM would affect their turnover intention. Second, based on the self-determination theory, the present study provided a novel mechanism for how perceived HRM affected employees’ turnover intention. Third, we investigated the important boundary conditions based on employees’ emotional intelligence.

490313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
490313.value: We have two planned studies out of this project (both using Data 3). First, as we mentioned in Part 5.3, we will develop a study on the antecedents of HRM in the hotel sector. We have already obtained meaningful initial findings and will develop concrete studies later on. Second, we plan to apply the recent micro-foundations perspective to understand the individual-level antecedents of firm performance outcomes. We found that individual front-line, customer-contact employees’ individual differences, such as learning goal orientation, creativity, and citizenship behaviour, had consistent and significant relationships with general manger-reported firm performance such as subjective and composite indicators and objective indicators such as revenue per available room and average daily rate of hospitality companies. My co-authors and I have applied this line of thinking in prior studies (e.g., Yao & Chang, in press). While this study is again largely correlational at this stage, we are confident that it would eventually result in a quality paper based on such meaningful initial findings and also our expertise in developing such emergence studies. Reference: Yao, F.K., & Chang, S. In press. Do individual employees' learning goal orientation and civic virtue matter? A micro-foundations perspective on firm absorptive capacity. Strategic Management Journal.

490313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
490313.value: In this project, we collected data from different sources (e.g., general managers, HRM directors, supervisors, and employees), different contexts (e.g., hotels and non-hotels) and different time lags among variables and aimed to investigate the role of HRM issues in the management of organizations (particularly hospitality organizations). First, across multiple datasets, we consistently found that HRM could enhance desirable employee outcomes such as supervisor-rated creativity or innovative behavior. HRM also significantly boosted desirable firm outcomes such as hospitality firms’ financial performance, absorptive capacity, and innovation. Second, and more importantly, we found that while HRM created a beneficial organizational context in general, it also interacted with important supervisor and employee characteristics in predicting desirable outcomes. For example, we found that HRM strengthened the positive impact of leader humility on employees’ creative process engagement and in turn creativity. We also found that firms have to provide extensive job involvement opportunities so as to get the most benefit of having emotionally intelligent front-line customer service employees in predicting these employees’ supervisor-rated creativity. All these findings are consistent with the conjectures outlined in our original research proposal. Overall, via these studies, we could significantly advance our knowledge on the value of HRM in (hospitality) management.

490413.value: Land or space in general, art, identification or title, and knowledge are dynamically non-rival, that is, their stock tends to be independent of human consumption. We refer to goods with dynamic non-rivalry as heritage good. We envision an economy of overlapping generations where humans consume both the heritage good and a perishable good that must be produced using labor. We analyze the efficiency implication of private ownership of heritage good, beginning with the case where the heritage good exists exogenously and later extending to the case where the heritage good must be created through human efforts. We show that unrestricted private ownership of heritage good leads to overproduction of the perishable good, distorted consumption pattern, and lower well-being in equilibrium, whereas restricted private ownership that limits perpetual trading of the heritage good across generations help restore efficiency. Implications for privatization (as well as nationalization) of the heritage good are discussed. We also investigate how heritage goods, when privately owned, impact trade liberalization of perishable good, how privatization of heritage good impacts trade, and how trade liberalization of heritage good affects global trade and production pattern 本项目研究动态非竞争性和所有权的问题。 动态非竞争性是指一个物品，在被前一位使用者使用后，功能保持不变， 因而不影响后一位对该物品的使用， 及使用中所带来的效用。 许多物品含动态非竞争性。 最典型的是数字世界中的信息内容， 知识， 现实生活中用于标记人，物，事的符号， 土地， 空间， 山川风景等等。 本项目研究将显示当物品含动态非竞争性时所有权中使用权和支配权的区分变得重要。 尤其是因为这些物品的所有权私有化会对社会福利产生负面的作用， 社会需要对这些物品的私有权， 特别是私有权的年限上， 加以限制。

490513.label: Project Objectives
490513.value: To develop a framework that takes into account an important dimension of blueprint quality, namely the blueprint’s ability to stand the test of time. To use this new framework to improve our understanding of the relationship between temporal quality and firms’ product line and supply chain decisions. To use this new framework to inform better policy discussions, such as the effect of free trade on intensive margin, extensive margin, and welfare; and general-equilibrium effects of various policies regulating parallel trade.

490513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
490513.value: Blueprints invariably become obsolete, and an important dimension of quality is how well they stand the test of time. Ordinary flu vaccines need to be reformulated every year due to the high virus mutation rate. High-quality vaccines are called “universal” vaccines. They are no more effective than ordinary vaccines in the first year, but remain effective for longer because they are more robust to virus mutation. Fashions become obsolete for a different reason. A design that is a year old does not give the same thrill of novelty as it did a year ago. High-quality designs are called “classic” designs. They are indistinguishable from the over-hyped ones in the short run. Only time can tell them apart in the long run. Economists have studied quality for decades, but never this temporal dimension. Such omission can lead to very misleading policy analyses. For example, when new varieties are sold at much higher markups than old ones are, it may be a sign of fast technological progress; but it may also be a sign of poor quality, rendering old varieties obsolete in a fast pace. When more new varieties are introduced into the market every year after a certain trade reform, it may be because firms have stepped up their R&D to churn out more new designs; but it may also be because firms have scaled down their investments in quality, which shortens the lifespan of old varieties and necessitates their replacement by new ones. To carefully separate these opposite forces, we need a new framework that is general enough to allow for different reasons why flu vaccines and fashions become obsolete over time, and flexible enough to allow for endogenous choices of temporal quality (i.e., the ability to stand the test of time). This project aims at providing such a new framework. We plan to use this new framework to investigate, among other things, (i) how to correctly measure welfare gains from new varieties when large inflow of new varieties may be a sign of low temporal quality, (ii) how does the concern of blueprint obsolescence affect a firm’s product line and supply chain decisions, and (iii) how does endogenous temporal quality affect our analysis of parallel trade.

490513.label: Realisation of objectives
490513.value: All of the above three objectives have been achieved. Our first objective is to develop a framework that takes into account an important dimension of blueprint quality, namely the blueprint's ability to stand the test of time. We have successfully developed such a framework, which we explain in details in Sections 2 and 3 of the article "Only Time Can Tell: Temporal Quality in Trade and Sourcing". The framework has several components. It involves a stationary economy where all consumer goods are perishable, and come in different varieties. At any time, every variety is indexed by its name as well as by its age. Consumers are identical, each has one unit of labor endowment at any moment, which is supplied inelastically. The representative consumer does not save, and at every moment maximizes a non-homothetic utility function subject to budget constraint. Within the non-homothetic utility function is an aging function, which captures how less appealing an older variety is when compared to newer ones in the eyes of the consumer. The rate at which a variety's blueprint loses its appeal is a measure of its temporal quality. We introduce a class of aging functions indexed by an aging function's corresponding temporal quality. For any temporal quality, the values of the aging functions are the same at age zero, capturing the idea that only time can tell apart blueprints with different temporal quality. At age bigger than zero, the values of the aging functions with different temporal quality start to differ. Doubling the temporal quality doubles the time required for a blueprint to suffer the same obsolescence. In essence, our framework abstracts from the reasons why a blueprint may become obsolete over time, and takes a reduced-form approach of postulating that it does and describing how fast it does. As such, our framework is actually silent on who is at fault for a blueprint becoming obsolete. An antibiotic loses its effectiveness faster when public misuse induces the development of resistance in the bacteria it targets. To the extent that public misuse of antibiotics reflects more the quality of public health policies, the temporal quality of the same antibiotics can vary across different societies, and is not completely controllable by the scientists who formulated them. Each variety is produced by a different firm who owns the variety's blueprint. Production requires only labor. As a variety ages, the firm that produces it charges a lower and lower price. Since marginal cost of production does not change, the firm's profit margin is shrinking over time as well. The representative consumer consumes less and less of it. Eventually there is a maximum age for any variety at which point profit margin vanishes, and the variety disappears from the market. This maximum age defines the variety's lifespan. There is an unbounded pool of prospective entrants into the economy. To enter, a firm must first pay a blueprint development cost. A new blueprint is developed at the same moment the blueprint development cost is paid, which immediately starts to become obsoletely gradually. Free entry implies that every firm earns zero net profit. Our framework is so tractable that closed form solutions for all the endogenous variables can be solved in terms of exogenous parameters. This allows one to perform comparative statics exercises on every endogenous variable with respect to every exogenous parameter. We illustrate this tractability in Section 3 of the article "Only Time Can Tell: Temporal Quality in Trade and Sourcing" by proving the result that the number of new varieties introduced into the market at any moment increases if firms scale down their investment in temporal quality. This highlights the importance of studying temporal quality formally, because omitting temporal quality would lead to serious misinterpretation of economic data such as the number of new varieties introduced into the market at any moment. Our second objective is to use this new framework to improve our understanding of the relationship between temporal quality and firms' product line and supply chain decisions. We provide a thorough analysis of this relationship in Section 5 of the article "Only Time Can Tell: Temporal Quality in Trade and Sourcing". There, we consider a Northern firms that are selling only to Northern consumers. They, however, can choose whether to produce at home (i.e., in the North) or in a foreign, Southern country. Producing at home incurs a higher labor cost, but a shorter "lead time" (i.e., the delay from the time a blueprint is developed to the time the first product is put on the shelf), when compared with producing in the South. Firms are heterogeneous in how efficient they are in investing in temporal quality. Our main finding is that a firm's total gross profit function satisfies a certain single-crossing property: for a firm that has already invested in a higher temporal quality, an increase in "lead time" by a given amount is not as damaging, and hence does not require as large a reduction in labor cost to restore its original total gross profit. (To understand this, one can consider the admittedly extreme scenario where the temporal quality is so low that the variety's lifespan is even shorter than the increased "lead time". In that scenario reduction in labor cost would offer little redemption.) The profound implication of this single-crossing property is that the only possible sorting pattern we can observe is that firms that are more efficient in investment in temporal quality are more likely to offshore their production, while those that are less efficient in investment in temporal quality are more likely to produce in their home countries. Our third objective is to use this new framework to inform better policy discussions, such as the effect of free trade on intensive margin, extensive margin, and welfare; and general-equilibrium effects of various policies regulating parallel trade. Our study of these issues lead to a very surprising finding, namely that within a very wide class of trade models, none of the trade policies will affect the firms' equilibrium choices of temporal quality. This finding is surprising even to us, but we document in details in Section 4 of the article "Only Time Can Tell: Temporal Quality in Trade and Sourcing". The underlying logic of this result is quite subtle (which explains why we did not see it coming), but roughly speaking it is driven by the fact that free entry and exit of firms neutralize the effects of trade policies on firms' endogenous choices of temporal quality. Although the result is not what we anticipated, it is nevertheless a significant finding, and also puts the question in our third objective into rest.

490513.label: Major findings and research outcome
490513.value: This project has developed a theoretical framework for the study of temporal quality, a dimension of quality that only time can tell. We use this framework to obtain three theoretical findings, which are briefly described below, and are documented in details in the article "Only Time Can Tell: Temporal Quality in Trade and Sourcing" (under revision at American Economic Review). Our methodological innovation also helped us to finish an earlier project, which resulted in the article "Non-Homothetic Preferences and IPRs Protection", which was subsequently published in Journal of Development Economics (vol. 109, pp. 229-239). The three theoretical findings we obtained using the theoretical framework we developed are as follows. First, we find that the number of new varieties introduced into the market can be a misleading indicator of consumer welfare. When more new varieties are introduced into the market at any moment, it may be because firms have stepped up their investments in R&D, which helps design new varieties in a faster pace; but it may also be because firms have scaled down the temporal quality of these new designs, rendering them appropriate for the market for a shorter period of time, which in turn necessitates their replacement by even newer designs. We find that a better indicator that can tell apart these two opposite cases is the total number of varieties existing in the market. Second, we compare the endogenous choices of temporal quality among firms in the richer North and firms in the poorer South. We find that Northern firms do not necessarily invest more in temporal quality vis-a-vis their Southern counterparts. They do so, however, if they have a larger advantage in marginal blueprint development cost than in total cost. We also find that this prediction is very robust, and holds regardless of how Northern countries differ from Southern ones, and how intensive they trade with each other. Finally, we find that firms with investment efficiency in temporal quality sort themselves in a way that more efficient firms invest more in temporal quality and offshore their production, while less efficient firms invest less in temporal quality and keep their production closer to home.

490513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
490513.value: There are apparently a lot more work remains to be done regarding temporal quality. For example, in our article "Only Time Can Tell: Temporal Quality in Trade and Sourcing", we conjecture that introducing endogenous temporal quality may provide a theoretical foundation for the empirical finds of shortening product life cycles over time in the marketing literature, and that product life cycle shortens more in industries where trade barriers reduce more. Formalizing and testing this conjecture should be one of the next items in this research agenda.

490513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
490513.value: Ordinary flu vaccines become ineffective after one year, thanks to the high mutation rate of virus, which necessitates introduction of new formulations every year. Scientists are developing new, higher-quality flu vaccines called ``universal vaccines''. They are equally effective as ordinary vaccines in the first year, but hopefully will remain effective for longer because they are more robust to virus mutation. In this example, there is an important dimension of quality---which we call "temporal quality''---that only time can tell. Economists have never studied temporal quality before. Such omission can result in very misleading interpretations of economic data. For example, when more new varieties are introduced into the market every year after a certain trade reform, it may be because firms have stepped up their innovation of new designs, but it may also be because firms have scaled down the temporal quality of these new designs, necessitating their replacement by even newer designs. This project develops such a new theoretical framework, which we can use to start studying temporal quality---how firms make decisions on it, how it interacts with their other decisions---and to avoid misinterpreting economic data.

490813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
490813.value: 收藏對於消費者和商家都是非常重要的。世界各地的消費者收集各種產品（如藝術品，古董，書籍，和硬幣）以尋求審美，情感慰籍或投資升值機會。商家也致力於研發收藏品以取悅消費者，增加其購買慾望，及強化忠誠度。然而，我們對於消費者如何決定收藏知之甚少。在這項研究中，我們系統地研究微觀環境對消費者收藏行為的影響。我們認為，消費者的收藏決策通常反應了一個偶然的和自下而上的過程，各種因素可能會影響消費者開始收藏的可能性。

490813.label: Realisation of objectives
490813.value: The PI and Co-Is thoroughly reviewed the relevant literature and conducted a large number of studies to address the research objectives stated in the project proposal. Our first objective was to examine whether small differences in consumers’ initial possession level affect their likelihood to start a collection. The PI and Co-Is conducted a large number of lab and field studies, pre-tests, posttests, and in-depth interviews with collectors. Our findings confirmed that the beginning of a collection is often loosely planned and triggered by situational factors. Specifically, incidentally obtaining items that belong to a collectible series often gives rise to a decision to start a collection. This is because a small number of possessions—a few more than one—represent an unjustified and, thus, unstable possession level that prompts a status change. Our research is among the first to explore situational influences on long-term goal initiation. Our paper was submitted and published in a top-tier marketing journal, Journal of Marketing. Our first objective was fully accomplished. Our second objective was to compare a piecemeal and a lump-sum manner to acquire the first few collectible items and study their different effects on collection goal setting and goal commitment. To accomplish this goal, we again conducted a series of online studies and lab experiments. Two procedures for acquiring rewards were carefully examined: a piecemeal procedure, whereby rewards are acquired gradually through repeated small efforts, and a lump-sum procedure, whereby a number of rewards are acquired all at once after a longer period of work. We showed that holding constant the total quantity of acquired rewards and the effort–reward exchange rate, the piecemeal procedure is more motivating than the lump-sum procedure because the former results in a greater sense of achievement. If the sense of achievement is curtailed by preventing people from accumulating the rewards they have earned, by providing rewards that are different from the already-earned rewards, or by breaking the association between effort and rewards, the piecemeal procedure is no more motivating than the lump-sum procedure. The effect is also diminished when consumers are satiated with the rewards. Taken together, these experiments provide converging evidence that acquiring rewards piece by piece motivates people to continue earning them. A research paper based on our findings was submitted and published in Journal of Consumer Research. Our second objective was also fully accomplished. Our third objective was to study how computationally easy and difficult progress markers affect motivation and goal commitment at different stages of the collection process. To accomplish this goal, we again conducted a series of online and lab studies. Our findings provided full support to our hypotheses. As the results of our experiments are much related to our second objective stated in this project, we also reported our findings in the aforementioned publication at Journal of Consumer Research.

490813.label: Major findings and research outcome
490813.value: In this project, we are interested in starting point of collection. Specifically, we look at how seemingly inconsequential situational factors can influence goal initiation. Our finding suggest that incidentally obtaining a small number of possessions that belong to a collectible series (paper 1), or receiving small rewards on a repeated basis (paper 2) can change people’s perception of the meaning of their current actions and lead to them to seek out more actions in order to fulfil the emerging goal, which eventually leads to a collection. This project has yielded two top-tier marketing journal publications. The first paper was published in Journal of Marketing. We show that the beginning of a collection is often loosely planned and triggered by situational factors. While previous research has typically treated collection as a top-down process, we show that collections may often reflect a bottom-up, incidental process—after a certain inflection or tipping point is reached, the likelihood of starting a collection disproportionally increases. The second paper was published in Journal of Consumer Research. In this paper, we compared two procedures for acquiring rewards: a piecemeal procedure, whereby rewards are acquired gradually through repeated small efforts, and a lump-sum procedure, whereby a number of rewards are acquired all at once after a longer period of work. We showed that holding constant the total quantity of acquired rewards and the effort–reward exchange rate, the piecemeal procedure is more motivating than the lump-sum procedure because the former results in a greater sense of achievement. Thus, acquiring rewards piece by piece motivates people to continue collecting them. Beyond the journal publications, we also distributed our research outcomes on international conferences and converted the research findings to cases for classroom teaching. Our research makes important contributions to the collection and motivation literature and has important implications for marketing practice. Additional information about publication #1: Publication #1 was accepted in the same year when the RGC grant started. This is because (1) we had already completed a series of pretests and pilot experiments and found preliminary support when we submitted the grant application (which was clarified in my original proposal), and (2) we ran more experiments after the grant application was submitted and got additional support to our hypotheses. We submitted our first draft to Journal of Marketing in November 2013. The review team asked us to run additional studies and replace some of the old ones. The majority of the studies reported in the published paper were conducted in the spring of 2014 using the current grant. The draft was accepted in August of 2014 and published in November of 2014. I acknowledged this GRF grant as the only funding source in my publication.

490813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
490813.value: Our research findings inspire the PI to continue working on projects related to collection and goal initiation. For example, based on the findings that the perceived connectedness of the different collectibles/rewards moderates the collection tipping point effect (paper 1) and the acquisition procedure effect (paper 2), the PI is currently studying how the structural characteristics of a set of collectibles (e.g. their theme clarity and representativeness) influence people’s motivation to start and continue a collection, and their likelihood to start a hobby.

490813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
490813.value: The decision to collect or start a long-term engagement is usually characterized as a top-down, goal-driven process; for example, a consumer may decide to collect teddy bears or join a loyalty program to collect rewards, which then leads to specific actions to achieve that goal. However, our findings suggest that collections may often reflect a bottom-up, incidental process—after a certain inflection or tipping point is reached, the likelihood of starting a collection disproportionally increases. As we showed in this research (paper 1), the collection decision point often occurs at the stage of possessing two or three collectible items. Two or three is the inflection point because maintaining a status quo of a few collectible items is difficult to justify – it is “neither here nor there.” We also show (paper 2) that people who received rewards piece by piece were more motivated to acquire more rewards than were those who received the same rewards in a lump-sum. Thus, when small achievements are accumulated, it leads to a journey, not a finishing line.

490913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
490913.value: The 2008 financial crisis brought great challenges to many cash stranded small and medium-size enterprises (SMEs) and increased the risk of supply chain disruption due to these firms’ inability to secure much needed financial supports. This has become a particularly serious problem in recent years for many SMEs in China. With a banking system nearly monopolized by a few state-owned banks and an immature credit reporting system, many of these SMEs can only rely on inventory-based financing—using inventory as collateral to secure loans—to supplement their needs for working capital. Motivated by our observations in China, we propose to study production and inventory management in a company that produces or orders a single product to satisfy a stream of demands in a multi-period planning horizon. The company’s ability to capture all of the demands is constrained by its limited working capital and it must rely on its inventory as collateral to secure additional loans. We propose to model the problems using both deterministic and stochastic modeling approaches. We will characterize the optimal inventory and financing decisions; investigate the interdependencies of the inventory flow and financial flow in a firm; and identify business environments in which a firm will significantly improve its profitability with the availability of the inventory-based financing. We will also collect real world data and use it to conduct a numerical study to validate the theoretical results and to potentially develop further managerial insights. Our proposed research has the potential to make significant contributions to the literature by studying a number of new multi-period inventory management problems with inventory-based financing. Furthermore, our study is also expected to contribute to the real world practices in a time when inventory-based financing has increasingly become a popular choice for companies, especially SMFs who lack credit rating or market power to obtain more traditional forms of financing such as bank credits or trade credits. Our proposed research may help these companies better understand the intricate interdependencies of inventory and financial flows, and better prepare them to manage their operational and financial risks. 2008年的金融危機給許多自有資金不足的中小企業帶去了巨大的挑戰，特別是使它們面臨供應鏈中斷的風險，因為這些公司無法獲得急需的金融支持去應付日常的運營。這已經成為近年來許多中國中小企業所面臨的一個特別嚴重的問題。同時在國內由於這些中小企業面對由少數國有銀行幾乎壟斷的銀行系統和目前尚不成熟的信用評級系統，導致他們中的很大一部分只能依靠庫存質押進行融資，具體來說就是企業通過質押一部分庫存從而取得貸款以補充其營運資金。 通過在中國的觀察，我們提出一個研究某一公司生產和庫存管理的多階段問題。該公司在每一階段都需要生產（訂購）一種單一的商品來滿足一定的外部需求。同時由於該公司運營資金有限，如果在某一階段發現其資金不足以滿足外部需求，它必須通過質押一部分庫存來獲得貸款。這裡我們提出確定性和隨機性（外部需求）兩種不同的建模方法。在研究中，我們試圖刻畫公司的最優庫存決策和相應的融資決策；探究公司內部庫存流和資金流之間的相互依賴關係；尋找特定的商業環境使得身處其中的公司可以通過庫存融資顯著提高其盈利能力。我們也將收集一些企業的實際數據，用它來進行實證研究和驗證我們的理論結果，同時進一步得到相關的管理啟示。 我們通過研究庫存質押這一特定的供應鏈融資模式，在多階段庫存的文獻研究領域將會做出一定貢獻。此外我們的研究也有望在實踐中得到運用和發展，尤其是針對國內的中小企業。在目前尚缺乏信貸評級而主要依靠傳統藉貸，比如銀行貸款或貿易信貸融資的情況下，庫存融資對它們顯得日趨重要。我們的研究旨在幫助這些企業更好地了解庫存流和資金流之間複雜的依賴性，以此更好地指導它們管理公司的運營風險和財務風險。

490913.label: Realisation of objectives
490913.value: The PI have achieved all 4 objectives in the project proposal. The PI have produced 3 papers that are based on the proposal. Specifically, two papers develop stochastic and deterministic models respectively with inventory-based financing (objective 1) and both papers study the structures of the optimal production and inventory decisions (objective 2). All three papers investigate the interdependency between inventory flow and financial flow in a supply chain (objective 3). And finally, one paper uses a set of real world data in its study of optimal production planning with inventory-based financing (objective 4). Two papers have been submitted to a high quality journal Production and Operations Management. One paper is currently in the last stage of completion and will be submitted to a scholarly journal soon.
