490913.label: Major findings and research outcome
490913.value: The three papers have provided several new findings that are significant to the literature and also to business practices. For example, we find that when the demand is stochastic, a cash-constrained company's inventory ordering policy will be significantly impacted by the inventory-based financing scheme. The firm may even strategically over-stock its inventory for the purpose of securing more capital. We also find that when a company produces multiple products, he could use the existing cycle inventory to obtained the needed additional capital. In one of the study, we find that a work-in-process inventory (a milk cow in our study) can be used as collateral to secure a more steady income for a farmer.

490913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
490913.value: The proposed project falls in an area of business practice called Supply Chain Financing which has been very active in recent years in the greater China region. It has also attracted many research scholars who study various different issues of supply chain financing. The three papers funded by this project should allow the PI to establish more credibility when working with scholars and practitioners. The PI plan to continue this line of study. In particular, the PI plan to work with the business communities more closely and identify more research opportunities in this area.

490913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
490913.value: This project study a cash-constrained small or medium firm who uses its inventory to secure additional working capital in order to capture his market demands. The most interesting aspect of the proposed research is that decision of production and financing are intricately interdependent--the production of inventory requires more working capital, but the additional capital raised through inventory-based financing requires more inventory. The research results from this project is significant in that it is among the first in the literature to consider production and inventory planning with inventory-based financing. The findings are new and useful to both research and practice communities.

491113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
491113.value: 本項研究提出一個兩階段的手機選擇模型，即消費者首先考慮是否選擇智慧手機，然後再決定選擇什麼品牌和模型。基於過去的研究，我們考慮從手機顧客的社會網路特徵、電訊服務、手機的產品屬性等三方面建立一個手機選擇的整合模型，並應用這一模型對中國某一電訊運營商的客戶手機使用資料進行實證分析。另外，我們還會做一些問卷調查或實驗來研究中國消費者智慧手機的選擇行為和影響因素，並為電訊公司和手機製造商提供更加有效的市場戰略。

491113.label: Realisation of objectives
491113.value: We developed an integrated framework of phone brand adoption model that differentiate three types of influence on product adoption: usage experience, product informational influence, social influence. These three types of influences play an important role on consumer product judgment and decision-making process. We conducted several studies to examine these three types of informational sources on product assessment and developed several models using different methods to explain the customer product adoption and consumer switching behavior. By leverage a unique transaction-level dataset from China telecom, we show that how customer use their phones has the greatest impact on their subsequent adoption process. Customers characteristics (e.g., age, gender) and a list of phone features also affect the phone brand switching phone. We demonstrate that customers’ phone brand switching is influenced by both the utilization of mobile phone (e.g., phone calls and mobile internet) and the features of their old phone (e.g., screen size, graphical display, and camera quality). In addition, we also investigate the role of innovation on brand extension in the changing mobile market. Technology advancement creates new opportunities but also many challenges to the business that are unable to adjust to the changing environment. In our study, we observe an interesting phenomenon regarding brand loyalty on smartphone adoption. When consumers switch technology from a non-smartphone to a smartphone, they are more sensitive to phone feature and less on brand. The brand loyalty is severely affected in such process of smartphone adoption, which we call it as the creative destruction of brand loyalty. In our further analysis, we find that smartphone and non-smartphone users have different decision-making processes when choosing smartphones. Smartphone users focus on their experience in using the brand they have purchased, whereas non-smartphone users are more concerned on new phone features. This result shows that new technology may break the trust and relationship structure critical in brand loyalty. When consumers assess a new product, they check if it is associated to a particular product category. After identifying the product category, they tend to transfer their perceived quality, knowledge, and experience associated with the brand of their old product to the new one in the same product category. However, if they perceive that the new product is not associated with any existing product category, transfer of brand loyalty is reduced. As a result, customers may switch to other brands for replacement. We also investigated the influence of social factors on mobile phone choice in social networks. In an empirical study based on 1.36 million customers in two medium-sized cities in western China, we assessed the manner by which network structure and dynamics interplay with the effects of social influence to facilitate the diffusion and adoption of Samsung Galaxy Note II. We conducted this study in three stages: (1) new phone model adopters are selected within our sample period and a two-layer snowball sampling of their mobile contacts is used to extract individual networks; (2) given longitudinal networks and temporal adoption behaviors, the stochastic actor-based dynamic network model is used to simultaneously determine the homophily effect on network formation and the social influence effect on adoptions; and (3) various measures of the network structure are linked to the estimated effects of social influence based on meta-analysis. We determined that the two most significant network measures related to social influence are the diversity of social connections and the time variation of network edge numbers (after controlling for network size and density). A simulation further reveals that a certain number of initial adopters is necessary to trigger positive social influence and adoption during the early stage of the diffusion process. The most significant feature of this study is the co-evolution of network formation and adoption behaviors that enable us to identify and quantify the endogenous effects of social inﬂuence.

491113.label: Major findings and research outcome
491113.value: We carried out the proposed research activities and completed three papers. The result findings of the papers are summarized as follows. The first study employs technology acceptance model (TAM) and information system theory approach, performing an in-depth quantitative analysis of customer usage and adoption behavior among mobile community to address two research questions: how and why customer switch between brands, and what are the determinants of phone brand switching. Concerning the first research question, the research finding reveals that customer purposes, characteristics, roles, and usage behavior matter. Regarding the second research questions, the study classifies mobile device into two major categories - smartphone or non-smartphone, and model customer phone switching behavior using a Markov chain framework in which the decision process only depends on the immediate past. Our research finds that customers with high usage of phone calls are more likely to switch phone than low voice calls customers. High usage mobile internet non-smartphone users are more likely to switch to smartphone in the next period. However, smartphone customers with high usage in mobile internet tend to use their current cell phone (instead of switching their phone brand) in the next period. The second paper investigates why a once successful brand demises for brand extension and how the customer perception changes during the creation and product subsequent introduction. Technology changes the way customers think and behave. Nokia dominated the non-smartphone market with high market share at that time. They did not lack technical capabilities to manufacture high quality smartphone in the new environment. The findings suggest that the failure, on one hand, is due to the firm’s resistance to change/adapt to the changing mobile market. On the other hand, it is also difficult to change a brand’s perception in the minds of customers. Once a mindset (voice call for Nokia) is made up about a brand, it is difficult to change. In particular, when customers change from a non-smartphone to a smartphone, they pay more attention to features and less on the brand. We attribute this behavior to the creative destruction of brand loyalty. The third paper investigates the effect of the dynamic network structure on social influence using network measures both at micro and macro levels. It examines the diffusion of a Samsung smartphone within a major wireless carrier in two middle-sized cities in China at three choice levels. The social influence in each social network is identified and measured using the stochastic actor-based model. Meta-analysis is then conducted to link network characteristics with social influence. Two important measures are identified as the major drivers of social influence: diversity of network connections and the standard deviation of edge numbers over time. Thus, the social influence effect is likely to occur in evenly distributed or expanding networks. Our findings also show that social influence occurs highly in networks with large size and density, abundant closure, low epidemic threshold, and high centrality of initial adopters when a new product is introduced. This study expands our understanding of the role of social influence in product diffusion by exploring individual- and network-level heterogeneities.

491113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
491113.value: We will try to develop our research further and to make a methodological advancement in the product adoption process. We will attempt to record customer historical brand adoption, usage behavior, and product advertising, and include them in the two-stage least squares regression model. The improvement will control the confounding factors associated with several brand promotional efforts as well as customer heterogeneity and alleviate the potential issues of endogeneity issues. Research in social psychology suggests that social factors, such as peer influence and network externality, have essential roles in customer decision making. Opinions of close friends may influence customer assessment of phone characteristics and decision-making process. In the ongoing studies, we collect a larger user product adoption data with user opinion (i.e., WOM communication) including products’ review valence, volume, and variance with substantial social economic variables (source strength, close proximity, and social proximity) in affecting the customer judgment and decision process. This study provides a new perspective on product adoption in social networks. Network structure information significantly complements individual demographic and local position information. The right networks must be selected based on a general network structure prior to selecting the right seeds based on personal characteristics and network positions. For future research, we will also examine a competitive scenario (e.g., Samsung versus Apple) and investigate the relationship between their network structures and adoption behaviors. Our results also provide empirical support for a new targeting strategy, which is called network-based targeting. The standard targeting strategy identifies certain individuals as targets (seeds) based on their individual characteristics and product features. However, network-based targeting suggests that companies should first consider individual network information, including peer influence and network structure, to determine the targets. Future research can further demonstrate the effectiveness of such a strategy. This knowledge will help companies to develop better targeting strategies.

491113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
491113.value: Customer adoption behavior is among the most important factors that influences the market share and profitability of a firm. The large number of new phones sold per year indicates that the replacement cycle of cell phone becomes shorter. People switch and replace their cell phone faster and sooner. The customer perceived value plays a vital role in the switching intention model. However, prior work in marketing are particularly interested in customer switching among mobile carriers, and little work has paid attention on understanding the determinants of phone brand choice. We conducted several studies using different approaches to unfold the hidden structure of switching behavior. Our findings provided insights on how phone services and features of phone influence mobile phone choice and brand switching. We provide guidance and knowledge on how mobile manufactures should design their mobile phones and manage their brands in this new digital era. We also present a warning for currently successful firms that they need to open up their innovation process and relax traditional notions of control and change at the pace of the market because the rules of branding are changing. Customers are more empowered than ever before. Technology has given consumers with more choice, reducing the power of traditional media in some markets. They have been given the power to filter irrelevant information and messages. New rules on branding are being introduced or reformed in the disruptive trends of technology. Especially, customers are also influenced by their peers regarding phone choice and adoption. We found that the two most significant network factors related to social influence are the diversity of social connections and the time variation of network edge numbers. A certain number of initial adopters is necessary to trigger positive social influence and adoption during the early stage of the new product diffusion process.

491313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
491313.value: The expectation-confirmation model (ECM) has been applied to investigate the satisfaction with and continuance of information technology (IT) after its adoption. This theory, which is based in social psychology, has already proven its applicability in the evaluation of IT post-adoption behavior. However, this project identifies a few important omissions that if modified, could improve the ECM’s theoretical validity and applicability. First, we argue that the assumption of a linear relationship between satisfaction and continuance may be inappropriate. If this linearity assumption holds, satisfied customers would choose to continue their service rather than switching to other services, as happens in reality. Second, the relationship between satisfaction and continuance/ discontinuance could be affected by other variables, either directly or indirectly. We believe that switching cost is an important variable missing in the ECM. Third, the ECM has been validated in many studies using data from continuers, but it has been insufficiently explored in the context of discontinuers. In reality, continuers and discontinuers behave differently, opting for various decision alternatives after their IT adoption. Hence, the ECM should extend its capacity to accommodate and explain the post-adoption behavior of both continuers and discontinuers. It is the objective of this project to provide insights into how the ECM could be modified to extend its theoretical applicability to both continuers and discontinuers by collecting empirical data for validation. Consequently, this project will contribute to the growing literature that examines IT post-adoption behavior and enhance our understanding of the effects of switching costs in IT continuance and discontinuance. 期望-確認模型（ Expectation-confirmation model -- ECM ）已被應用於研究信息技術（IT ）被採納後的滿意度和延續性。這一建基於社會心理學的理論，亦被證明適用於評價IT被採納後的行為。然而，我們發現這模型有幾個重要的遺漏，一旦能夠修改，可能會提高ECM理論的有效性和適用性。首先，我們認為ECM模型假設的滿意度和延續性的線性關係可能不正確。如果這個線性假設成立，滿意的客戶就應該選擇延續現有的服務，而不是好像在現實中切換到其他服務。第二，滿意度和連續/終止之間的關係可能受到其他變數直接或間接的影響。我們相信，轉換成本可能是ECM模型遺漏的一個重要的變數。第三，ECM的理論已被許多研究IT延續者的數據驗證，但它卻沒在中止群中被充分探討。在現實中，延續者和中止者的行為，選擇，和決策都有所不同。因此， ECM應該延伸其理論能力，讓它能同時解釋延續者和中止者在IT被採納後的不同行為表現。基於上述原因，本項目的主要目標是建議ECM應如何修改，並收集數據驗證我們的建議，以拓展ECM理論能同時適用於延續者和中止者。

491313.label: Realisation of objectives
491313.value: The project achieved all objectives originally designed for the study. In meeting the objectives, a research model, which differentiate the effect of switching costs on continuance and discontinuance of online service usage, was proposed. This research model is based on the expectation-confirmation model constructs from a user’s perspective. With this reference model, we introduce switching costs as a variable to investigate their moderating effect on customer (dis)satisfaction and evaluate the effect of switching cost types in the context of continued online service use. A total of eleven hypotheses, which correspond to these four objectives, were postulated. Data was collected to validate all these eleven hypotheses. The correspondence of these objectives and hypotheses are stated below: Objective 1: H1: Customer (dis)satisfaction has a positive effect on (dis)continuance intention (a). The effect follows an increasing returns-of-scale for continuers (b), but remains constant or decreases for discontinuers (c). Objective 2: H2: Switching costs have a positive effect on continuance intention (a). However, this effect is stronger on continuers who are early adopters and discontinuers who are late adopters (b). H3: Continuers and discontinuers have different perceptions of the effects that different types of switching costs have on continuance intention. H4: High switching cost has a negative, but low switching cost has a positive, moderating effect on the relationship between customer satisfaction and their continuance intention. Objective 3: H5: There is a satisfaction-continuance gap between continuers and discontinuers that widens when switching costs are low and narrows when they are high. H6: Switching cost types have different effects on moderating the relationship between (dis)satisfaction and (dis)continuance intention. H7: Continuers have more social capital than discontinuers (a). Therefore, they perceive relational costs to be more important in moderating the effect of their satisfaction with continuance intention than their discontinuer counterparts (b). Discontinuers, however, perceive financial costs to be more important in this moderation effect than continuers (c). Objective 4: H8: Perceived usefulness has a positive effect on continuance that is stronger on continuers than it is on discontinuers. H9: Perceived usefulness has a positive effect on satisfaction that is stronger on continuers than it is on discontinuers. H10: Confirmation has a positive effect on satisfaction that is stronger on continuers than it is on discontinuers. H11: Confirmation has a positive effect on perceived usefulness that is stronger on continuers than it is on discontinuers. In meeting the first objective, partial least square (PLS) product-indicator approach (PIA) approach was applied to investigate the relationship between (dis)satisfaction and (dis)continuance. Using the PLS-PIA approach, our observed variables (satisfaction and satisfaction* satisfaction) are mean-centered by subtracting the mean from every score to avoid multicollinearity. After calculating the centered indicators, the product indicators are developed by creating the possible products from the two sets of indicators. In other words, satisfaction, which is measured using four indicants (SAT1, SAT2, SAT3, and SAT4), is multiplied with the quadratic term SATi*SATj (where i, j = 1, 2, 3, 4) to create 10 product indicators. The PLS approach, which produces estimates of standardized regression coefficients for model paths, is then used to measure the relationships between the latent variables. This approach of curvilinear investigation of (dis)satisfaction-(dis)continuance suggests a significant increasing (positive) returns-to-scale satisfaction-continuance relationship between continuers. The discontinuers, however, do not have any non-linear satisfaction-continuance relationships. When continuer and discontinuer responses are combined, a significant decreasing (negative) returns-to-scale satisfaction-continuance relationship is identified. These results support the hypothesis postulated to investigate objective 1. In meeting the second objective, we performed a series of PLS analysis on switching costs and (dis)continuance. We believe that PLS is appropriate for our research as switching cost effect is a relatively unexplored topic. Furthermore, the multi-group analysis of PLS is appropriate for comparing between-group differences, which suits our research objective to compare the behavior of continuers and discontinuers. To test the effect of switching costs on continuance intention (objective 2), multi-group PLS analysis is used to compare the differences (t-tests) in the coefficients of the corresponding structural paths for continuers, discontinuers, and their combination on switching costs. The results suggest that the overall switching costs have a significant direct effect on continuance intention. The breakdown of users into continuers and discontinuers yields interesting findings. First, all switching cost types are critical to the continuance intention of continuers, but only financial cost type is significant to discontinuers. Second, switching costs are critical to continuers in their service continuance, but not to discontinuers. Objective 2 also involves the investigation of the moderation effect of switching costs on the satisfaction-continuance relationship. In testing this moderation effect, our results suggest that switching costs have significant positive moderation effects on the satisfaction-continuance relationship at both high and low switching costs. However, these findings do not align with our hypothesis that switching costs have positive and negative moderation effects on the satisfaction-continuance relationship at low and high switching costs, respectively. We believe this phenomenon is caused by staying costs. Research has demonstrated that customer’s intention to continue is not only confined to switching costs, but also staying costs. Hence, a satisfied customer who decides to stay at times of low switching costs may have to pay a price for staying. These staying costs include boredom, lack of variety, satiation, and curiosity, and may cause irrational continuance or discontinuance decisions. In other words, staying costs may counteract the effect of switching costs, thus diminishing the differential effects of high-low switching costs on satisfaction-continuance. In meeting the third objective, we split switching costs into three types – relational, financial, and procedural. Multigroup PLS analyses were then performed to test their direct and moderation effects on continuance and discontinuance. The results suggest that the three switching cost types have different moderation effects on the satisfaction-continuance relationship. Further analysis of this difference using the Tukey test reveals that relational and financial cost types have significantly stronger moderation effects than procedural cost types. These findings suggest that the procedural cost type has the smallest interaction effect with satisfaction on continuance. Our research also finds different switching cost types to have different moderation effects on the satisfaction-continuance relationship. These differential effects are found to be significant. Further analysis of this difference using the Tukey test reveals that relational and financial cost types have significantly stronger moderation effects than procedural cost types. These findings suggest that the procedural cost type has the smallest interaction effect with satisfaction on continuance. Splitting the data into continuers and discontinuers also confirms significant differential effects across these three switching cost types for both user groups. In sum, all hypotheses proposed to meet object 3 are supported. In meeting the last objective, we tested the behaviors of continuers and discontinuers on other expectation-confirmation model constructs. Similar multigroup PLS analyses were performed to evaluate the behavior of continuers and discontinuers. The results suggest that continuers and discontinuers do have different perceptions of usefulness and (dis)confirmation constructs depicted in the expectation-confirmation model. In other words, all hypotheses associated with objective 4 are supported.

491313.label: Major findings and research outcome
491313.value: Our research has three significant findings. First, the relationship between satisfaction and continuance is non-linear. Of the two user types, this relationship follows an increasing returns-of-scale for continuers, but is constant for discontinuers. Second, switching costs have a direct and indirect effect on (dis)continuance intention. Third, different switching cost types result in different effects, both direct and indirect, on the satisfaction-continuance relationship. Other than these general findings, specific findings of our hypotheses are summarized as follows: H1: Customer (dis)satisfaction has a positive effect on (dis)continuance intention (a). The effect follows an increasing returns-of-scale for continuers (b), but remains constant or decreases for discontinuers (c). H1a: Supported H1b: Supported H1c: Supported H2: Switching costs have a positive effect on continuance intention (a). However, this effect is stronger on continuers who are early adopters and discontinuers who are late adopters (b). Therefore, they perceive relational costs to be more important in moderating the effect of their satisfaction with continuance intention than their discontinuer counterparts (b). 491313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
491313.value: Our research findings confirm that switching cost, along with its types, have differential effects on continuers and discontinuers. However, our findings also demonstrate some unexpected results of switching costs. For example, early and late adopters do not exhibit differential continuance behavior when switching costs fluctuate. High switching costs also do not foster a negative effect on continuance. Hence, we believe, at least theoretically, that switching costs do not act alone, but in combination with other forces, to influence the satisfaction-continuance relationship. Such forces may include lock-in and amplification effects. In our research context, the lock-in effect is the limitation of customers to switch and the amplification effect is the augmentation of the (dis)satisfaction effect of customers on their (dis)continuance intention. In this regard, switching cost fluctuations may combine with lock-in and amplification effects to either increase or decrease the satisfaction-continuance relationship. These synergetic effects may also be influenced by the effect of staying costs, which occurs when dissatisfied customers decide to continue their services despite their dissatisfaction. Future research may include examinations of all of these effects in their investigations.

491313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
491313.value: In the context of online services, switching costs are the magnitude of the additional costs required to terminate the existing relationship and secure an alternative. These costs are not only economic, but also composed of psychological and emotional motives. Consequently, switching costs have the capacity to enrich our understanding of the (dis)continuance and the (dis)satisfaction-(dis)continuance relationship of online services. This research attempts to fill in this research gap by investigating the effects of switching costs on (dis)satisfaction and (dis)continuance intention. We believe that this research can make a few contributions to IT post-adoption literature. First, it offers additional insight into the post-adoption behavioral difference between continuers and discontinuers. Second, it offers a new complementary perspective from which to evaluate switching costs in the context of post-adoption behavior.

491513.label: Project Title(Chinese)
491513.value: 「員工感到大材小用」對企業的可能益處

491513.label: Project Objectives
491513.value: To identify the dimensionality of underemployment and develop a scale to measure it in the Chinese context. To assess the criterion validity of the underemployment scale in predicting job attitudes and performance in Chinese context. To verify the non-linear relationships between underemployment and thriving/job performance, and the mediating role of job crafting in these processes.
rows: To identify the dimensionality of underemployment and develop a scale to measure it in the Chinese context.
To assess the criterion validity of the underemployment scale in predicting job attitudes and performance in Chinese context.
To verify the non-linear relationships between underemployment and thriving/job performance, and the mediating role of job crafting in these processes.

491513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
491513.value: Underemployment occurs when a worker is employed in a job that is inferior by some standards in terms of education, pay, skill, experience, working hours or status (McKee-Ryan & Harvey, 2011). It is also referred to as overeducation, skill underutilization and overqualification in the literature. Underemployment is of critical importance nowadays. Scholars estimated that between 13% and 33% of the workforce was underemployed (see, e.g., Mavromaras et al., 2010). It was also found that underemployment might still persist during economy recovery (Ponthiere, 2008). As a result, underemployment is at the forefront of the minds of many policy makers (Erdogan et al., 2011). However, our understanding of the outcomes of underemployment was inconclusive or biased. While it is easy to associate underemployment with undesirable outcomes such as intention to leave (Livingstone, 1998), some scholars recently proposed possible bright sides of underemployment. Erdogan, et al. (2011) and Maynard (2011) argued that underemployment might create potential competitive advantages for organizations. Unfortunately, scholars who advocate this positive view neither proposed a clear theory nor concrete empirical evidence to justify their claims. Empirically, the literature only consisted of a large body of studies with mixed results, near zero correlations, or insignificant relationships between underemployment and various outcomes without clear explanations (e.g. Holtom et al., 2002; Kraimer, 2009). We argue that possible curvilinear effects may be the cause of the mixed findings. We propose a two-step process to answer the issues identified above. First, we would develop a sound unemployment scale by consolidating the eight underemployment dimensions identified in the last 10 years (McKee-Ryan, et al., 2011). Then, by integrating work role transition theory (Nicholson, 1984) and the attention activation rule (Kahneman, 1973), we propose a model that a moderate level of underemployment would lead to two positive outcomes: thriving (Spreitzer et al., 2005) and job performance. Job crafting (Wrzesniewski & Dutton, 2001) is hypothesized as the core employee coping mechanism leading to the two positive outcomes of underemployment. We will test this curvilinear mediation model using large sample data from two cities in mainland China. By testing the above curvilinear mediating relationship and the role of job crafting, we can understand the theoretical mechanism leading to the possible bright sides of underemployment. This would open up a new arena for future underemployment research. The research outcomes would have important implications for leaders and HR managers on different ways to managing talents in their organization. 受雇员工觉得自己被「大材小用」的感觉在今天的社会极为普遍，也极为重要。有数据显示有13%到33%的企业员工在工作中经常会有这样的感觉。这种「大材小用」的委屈感觉不仅出现经济衰退的时候，即使是到了经济兴旺时，这种感觉在受雇员工中依然普遍存在，目前，企业决策者非常重视怎么处理、引导这种员工的感受。 目前大部分的研究都推论，员工的「大材小用」感觉会带来各种负面影响，例如影响士气、更多抑郁情绪、更多工作不良行为更高、离职率更高等等。但是，对于「员工感到大材小用」这类课题的研究结果却与这些推论颇不一致，其结果很多是与以上推论是矛盾的、数据不显著的，或是效用值非常低的。 有鉴于此，我们提出了一个非线性的模型来解释「员工感到大材小用」和相应结果的关系。之前的研究都着重于直线关系，比如，员工的“大材小用”的感觉越高，发生各种负面结果可能性就越高。但非线性的模型是反映员工“大材小用”的感觉与相应的结果变量是曲线关系的，比如，员工“大材小用”的感觉较轻微或是只到中等程度时，这时“大材小用”的感觉是与结果正相关的，但当“大材小用”的感觉非常强烈时，这种感觉与相应结果将是负相关了。 本研究中，我们首先会检讨过去对「员工感到大材小用」的测量问题。然后，我们会提出两个「员工感到大材小用」的可能正面结果 – 「员工的干劲和喜悦感」和「工作业绩」。我们提出的中介机制是「工作重塑」。当员工感到中等程度的“大材小用”感觉时，这种感觉会促使他们重塑工作的内容、工作的意义和工作中的关系以使工作符合他们的主观愿望，这些在一定程度上自感“大材小用”的员工较之那些没有这种感觉的员工就会有更高的工作干劲和喜悦感，同时工作业绩也会更好；但是当“大材小用”感觉太过强烈时，员工就难以重塑他们的工作来改变他们对工作的感受，他们的干劲和喜悦感以及业绩就会下降。所以本研究是验证一个「员工感到大材小用」与两个结果变量的倒U型的曲线关系。 我们相信这个对「员工感到大材小用」的正面结果的研究，会有助于企业更好地管理工作能力水平不断提高的员工，更好地激发员工的潜能，让他们尽展所长，体会到工作的愉悦，并为企业做出更高的业绩。

491513.label: Realisation of objectives
491513.value: 1. We have tested and used two scales of underemployment developed in the US in the Chinese context. Items are translated and back-translated and used in our survey questionnaire. Underemployment was found to be a unidimensional construct. 2. We used the underemployment scales to predict proactive behaviors, creativity and citizenship behaviors of employees in Chinese context. Our results showed that the relationship between underemployment of task crafting was, in fact, quadratic in nature. We also found that underemployment would predict thriving of employees, although this result was not included in our final publication. Since the predictions were all significant, we have established criterion validity of the underemployment scales in China. 3. We have verified that both subjective and objective underemployment predicted job outcomes and job crafting served as the mediating mechanism. These results was published in the Academy of Management Journal, a top-tier journal in the management field.

491513.label: Major findings and research outcome
491513.value: We found two major sets of results in this research project. First, underemployment was found to affect proactive behaviors of employees through role-breadth self-efficacy. Employees who are overeducated with respect to the job requirements would have strong self-efficacy of their role breadth and would, therefore, define the job differently and have more proactive behaviors. We also found that this mediation relationship was moderated by goal orientations of the employees. The mediation effect was stronger for employees who are high in performance orientation. These results were published in the following paper: Zhang, M.J., Law, K.S. & Lin, B. (2016). You think you are big fish in a small pond? Perceived overqualification, goal orientations, and proactivity at work. Journal of Organizational Behavior, 37, 61-84. Second, underemployment was found to affect creativity and citizenship behaviors of employees through task crafting as a mediator. The relationship between underemployment and task crafting was quadratic in nature, meaning that task crafting is highest when underemployment was at a moderate level. The same results were confirmed in two surveys and a field experiment. These results were published in the following journal: Lin, B., Law, K.S., Zhou, J. (in press). Why is underemployment related to creativity and OCB? A task crafting explanation of the curvilinear moderated relations. Academy of Management Journal, published online on Jun 6, 2016.

491513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
491513.value: The research of underemployment in management is underdeveloped. Underemployment, and in particular, overeducated, is always perceived as negative and detrimental for management. The general assumption is that organizations should only hire employees who are just-qualified. Both overqualification or overemployment are bad. Our study results show that underemployment may be an asset for organizations when it is well managed. We started a new arena of research to explore the potential positive outcomes of underemployment.

491513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
491513.value: Underemployment, or overeducation in our research context, is always labeled as a poor organization practice. While firms do not like to hire applicants who are not qualified, most managers do not like to hire overeducated applicants either. The general impression is that underemployed workers are not motivated and tend to have high turnover. We started a new line of research, trying to explore some possible positive outcomes of overeducation. As the world economy slows down and more and more production processes are engaged by robots, the education level of many job incumbents are getting higher and higher. Overeducation, or employees who possess higher qualifications than are required by the jobs, is popular nowadays. We found that overqualified employees may result in more future-oriented proactive behaviors, creativity as well as citizenship behaviors. Managers may need to promote the confidence of these overeducated employees and provide a mechanism that they can craft their job contents positively. Positive job outcomes may then result.

491813.label: Project Title(Chinese)
491813.value: 整合空運貨代的貨物競價和物流規劃：隨機規劃模型和管理見解

491813.label: Project Objectives
491813.value: To obtain a thorough understanding of shipment bidding in practice. Nowadays, there are many web-based logistics platforms functioning as online logistics marketplaces (e.g. JCtrans.net, freightquote.com, cargoclix.com, freightbid.co.nz). We need to document the way these e-platforms operate and to understand the level of interactions of the participants, as well as the neutrality afforded by these e-platforms. Particular effort will be spent on examining how shipment bidding is done, how the time window is managed, how contracts are made, etc. To formulate a two-stage stochastic programming model. The model determines bidding decisions that maximize expected profit. The first stage determines the optimal portfolio of shipments, identifying new jobs to bid (and the corresponding bid prices) and the logistics planning for the portfolio. The second stage recourses the optimal logistics decisions based on bidding outcomes. The model will incorporate bidding time windows, bidding randomness, and shipping logistics decisions that are made at different stages. To develop an efficient solution procedure. Stochastic programming models are well-known to be computationally cumbersome (Higle and Wallace 2003). We propose to derive properties and bounds of the model, which are then used to design a heuristics solution procedure. We will examine the bid price of a job based on the probability distribution of competitors’ best price (Figliozzi et al. 2007). We will adopt the scenario generation methodology by Høyland et al. (2003) to generate competitors’ best price. To explore managerial insights. Using real-life data and information, we will examine behavior of critical jobs in the portfolio, formulating plausible bidding and logistics strategies. The likely issues would include how to examine variability in bidding decisions, how to identify the actual cost of shipping within the portfolio environment, and how to assess tradeoffs between bidding risks and logistics costs.

491813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
491813.value: With the success of global supply chain management and collaborative logistics, forwarders need to provide one-stop total logistics services that are integrated, reliable, and global. Also, forwarders have to routinely work with tight schedules with frequent impromptu changes and a wide variety of special requests. Nowadays, many web-based logistics platforms have been developed, enabling logistics agents worldwide to interact and to form collaborations in an effective manner. In particular, some advanced e-platforms support online bidding of shipments. With such e-platforms, forwarders can now effectively integrate shipment bidding with shipment logistics planning. Shipment bidding must be based on a portfolio concept. It needs to address the synergy between new and existing shipments. Will there be new consolidations to reduce cost? Will target delivery dates of shipments be met? Will additional resources be required? It needs to address the bid prices and their chances of success. In some e-platforms, a forwarder could place a buyout bid (getting the shipment right away) or could place an alternative bid and wait for the outcome at the end of the bidding time window. Shipment bidding could be further complicated by special requests of shippers such as using a specified airport, a particular route, a preferred logistics center, a specific treatment (e.g. temperature control), etc. Hence, a forwarder’s bidding decisions cannot be separated from shipping logistics decisions. This research proposes to determine optimal bidding decisions (new shipments to bid and their corresponding bid prices) along with optimal logistics decisions. We will formulate this problem as a two-stage stochastic programming model which optimizes expected profit with respect to shipment bidding strategies. The first stage determines the optimal portfolio of shipments, identifying new jobs to be bid, their bid prices and the logistics planning for the portfolio. The second stage recourses the optimal logistics decisions based on bidding outcomes. Decisions in the two stages are interdependent. The model will incorporate special requests of shippers, bidding time windows, respective bid prices and their chances of success. We will derive properties and bounds of the model, which are then used to design a heuristic solution procedure. Managerial insights will be explored by studying real-life problems. We will examine the tradeoffs between bidding risks and logistics costs. We will also examine the merit of different bidding strategies such as optimistic approaches and pessimistic approaches. 隨著全球供應鏈管理和合作物流的成功，貨運代理需要提供一站式整合的、可靠的及全球性的物流服務。此外，貨代需要處理緊張的時間表、頻繁的變化以及各種特殊的要求。如今，很多基於網絡的物流平台已經開發，它們使得世界各地貨代能夠以有效的方式互動和合作。一些先進的物流平台還支持網上貨物競價。有了這樣的平台，貨代如今可以有效地整合貨物競標和物流規劃。 貨物競標必須基於組合的概念。它需要解決新貨物和現有貨物之間的協同問題。是否有新的整合以降低成本？目標交付日期可否達到？是否需要額外資源？它還需要解決競標價格以及相應的成功機會。在一些網絡平台，貨代可以競拍買斷價格（立即贏得貨物），或者競拍另外的價格然後等待拍賣結束。貨主的特殊要求也會使競拍更為複雜，比如指定使用某個機場、某條航線、某個物流中心、特殊處理（如溫度控制）等等。因此，貨代的競拍決策與物流決策不能分開。 本研究將確定貨代的最優競拍決策（選擇貨物及其投標價格）以及最佳的物流決策。我們將建立一個兩階段的隨機規劃模型來優化期望利潤。第一階段確定最優的貨物組合、鎖定貨物、決定這些貨物的競拍價格以及物流規劃。第二階段在競拍結果的基礎上優化物流決策。這兩個階段的決策相互依賴。該模型還將納入貨主的特殊要求、競拍時間窗口、競拍價格以及相應的成功機會。我們將推導模型的性質及界限，然後設計一個啟發式求解過程。管理見解也將會通過現實問題得到分析。我們將考察競拍風險和物流成本之間的權衡。我們也將考察不同競拍策略（比如樂觀和悲觀）的特點。

491813.label: Realisation of objectives
491813.value: There are four objectives: • Objective 1. To obtain a thorough understanding of shipment bidding in practice. During 2013-2015, we search the internet to gain a better understanding of logistics e-platforms. Particular attention is given to e-platforms in China, where there is a very fast growth in the use of e-platforms for bidding. In fact, Dr He Wen (then a graduate student under my supervision) spent two weeks in Beijing working in Baidu company to see how biddings in e-platform typically operate. A discussion on logistics e-platform is provided in Introduction section of Paper 2: “Forwarder’s Bidding of Air Cargo Shipments: A Case Study of Revenue Management of Multiple Jobs With Synergy” by W. He, L. Leung, YV Hui, and G Chen (final version attached with new title is added). • Objective 2. To formulate a two-stage stochastic programming model. During 2013-2015, we formulate a two-stage stochastic programming model, where the first stage determines the optimal portfolio of shipments, identifying new jobs to bid (and the corresponding bid prices) and the second stage recourses the optimal logistics decisions based on bidding outcomes. The consideration of bidding time window is also incorporated. We use such a formulation in two separate papers (Paper 1 and Paper 2). Paper 1 addresses different aspects of logistics planning and Paper 2 addresses logistics planning within a revenue management setting. Paper 1 entitled “An Airfreight Forwarder’s Shipment Bidding and Logistics Planning” by L Leung, YV Hui, G Chen and W He, was developed from an earlier draft paper and is completed during this period. Based on the earlier draft, we reworked the entire second half of that paper, modeling the bidding environment within a two-stage stochastic programming framework. This paper has been published in Transportation Science (published version attached) • Objective 3. To develop an efficient solution procedure. For our model in Paper 1, the second-stage is a mixed integer problem and is NP-hard. During 2013-2015 period, we first derived an upper bound for expected profit. We then developed a two-stage heuristic algorithm, where the first-stage problem is solved by implicitly enumerating bidding decisions and searching logistics assignments during the time window, and the second-stage problem is solved by the second-echelon heuristic (for logistics assignments). The effectiveness of the heuristic is compared to another search procedure which search the solution space exhaustively; it is found that the current heuristic is able to determine solutions that are on average 0.26% below those from the search procedure but with significantly less computation time. Compared to other existing heuristics (Gendreau et al. 1996, Alonso-Ayuso et al. 2007, Döye et al. 2012), the novelty of our heuristic is that it proposes a branching method for bidding decisions that utilizes the model properties on feasibility and upper bound; it also incorporates customized moves to utilize knowledge specific to the logistics constraints. Details can be found in Paper 1. A variant of this heuristic algorithm has also been developed to solve the two-stage stochastic integer program in Paper 2. • Objective 4. To explore managerial insights of Bidding in Revenue Management within a logistics environment. During 2015-2016, we wholly concentrate on this objective. Via a reverse auction format on logistics e-platforms, airfreight forwarders often make bidding decisions on multiple shipments posted by shippers, while considering uncertain arrivals of future shipments. Many posted shipments could have synergistic aspects between them, such as routing, timing, and density compatibility. We formulate this problem as a two-period stochastic mixed 0-1 model, where bidding decisions are made on a set of shipments in the first period, while bidding outcomes and regular job arrivals are realized in the second period. We are able to identity this revenue management problem as a multi-product multi-input problem with potential interdependency in demand and interdependency in supply, as well as interdependency between demand and supply. It is the integration of revenue management and supply chain management under uncertainty on an e-platform. In this airfreight forwarding case study, forwarders acquire heterogeneous shipments via reverse auction on an e-platform. The forwarder determines best bid prices for a set of jobs while considering revenue and risk of future contracted jobs, and supply mix. This revenue management problem is a form of dynamic bid-price control, where revenue and supply information is updated for each request, selectively accepting only requests with desirable revenue while considering resource allocation. The bidding of shipments depends on the resource availability and vice versa. Via the case study, we explore the impact of different synergies on this problem. For demand synergy, we explicitly show the impact of buyout price, bundle bidding, and cross bidding dependency. For supply synergy, we show the impact of freight consolidation and use of different resource mix. We identify that for both demand synergy and supply synergy, there exists a direct effect and a decision recourse effect. There are two risk elements: bidding risk and potential arrival of future jobs. We show that there are risk sharing effect between products and inputs, and risk adjusted effect – a scaling effect on various synergies. Section 6 of Paper 2 summarizes and conceptualizes the behavior of multi-product demand synergy and multi-input supply synergy within the airfreight forwarding context. In general, via an airfreight forwarding case study, we are able to examine explicitly and in detail the impact of demand synergy and supply synergy on revenue management decisions of multiple products and multiple inputs. We incorporate two types of uncertainty typically addressed in revenue management literature, bidding and future arrival – both demand risk. We are able to identify the similarity between the two risks in terms of their impact to the decisions. More importantly, the primary objective is to conceptualize the relationship between demand synergy and supply synergy within the context of revenue management. Via numerical experiments, we show many aspects of demand synergy and supply synergy, and how they interact with each other and under uncertainty.

491813.label: Major findings and research outcome
491813.value: This research has two parts. The first examines bidding of shipments by forwarders on an e-platform. The second uses airfreight forwarder’s bidding problem to examine revenue management within a multi-product multi-input setting, where products and inputs have synergy within themselves and between them. • The first part is a technical contribution where a very complex model is formulated to represent the problem environment as close as possible. An elaborate solution procedure is also designed and is shown to be able to solve the problem effectively. This work integrates shipment bidding with logistics decisions. First, a shipment bidding and logistics planning model (mixed 0-1 LP), which addresses only buy-out bids, is formulated. Based on the properties of the model, we design a two-echelon solution procedure which determines the optimal shipment portfolio along with corresponding logistics requirements. Our computational experience shows that the solution procedure gives strong results. We then extend the model to include placing either a buyout bid or an alternative bid for a new shipment (with an estimated probability of success). The general model (a decision tree) allows forwarders to develop a bidding strategy of acquiring certain new jobs right away while placing alternative bids on others. • The second part uses the airfreight forwarder’s problem as a case study. This case study can be identified as revenue management meets supply chain management under uncertainty. The setting is multi-product and multi-inputs with demand synergy and supply synergy, and with bidding and uncertain future arrivals as the risk components. While the first part of the research is to seek an optimal solution, the primary purpose of the second part is to explain the solution, to conceptualize the relationship between demand synergy and supply synergy within the context of revenue management. We find that within a multi-product multi-input environment, there is a great deal of interaction possibilities within elements of the products and within element of the inputs, and between elements of the two groups, some of which can be subtle. Elements in demand synergy can be complementary and substitutable and elements in supply synergy can be as well. In a deterministic environment, such synergies would be fully exploited. When risks increase, these synergies can function as shock absorber, allowing optimal decisions to be more insensitive to uncertainty. But as the risk level becomes very high, many of the synergy themselves become riskier to take and would be forsaken.

491813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
491813.value: For future research, one could investigate the impact of risk on the supply side. In airfreight forwarding, it is not uncommon for forwarders to bid for airspace or for subcontracting – an example of uncertainty in availability of supplies. This would require new formulation on addressing demand risk and supply risk simultaneously, that could continue to capture demand synergy and supply synergy. Another important aspect of multiple product and multiple input revenue management is the computational difficulty in obtaining optimal solutions. One feature of this stochastic mixed 0-1 programming problem is that there are many combinations of bidding and resource mix - there would be a need to design more efficient algorithms.

491913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
491913.value: The videogame industry has grown rapidly in recent years. According to the Entertainment Software Association in the United States, the industry’s annual growth rates were above 10% between 2005 and 2009. In 2011, Americans spent $24.75 billion on video games, hardware and accessories. The great amount of revenue makes game piracy a huge concern for the game industry. One direct impact of game piracy is its effect on game sales revenue. In a report by the Computer Entertainment Suppliers Association in Japan, researchers estimate that, had all the illegal downloads on two portable game consoles (Nintendo DS and SONY PSP) they found on 114 piracy sites between 2004 and June 2009 been turned into legitimate sales, the worldwide game sales revenue would increase by 3.816 trillion yen (approximately $4.8 billion). Although the “estimated” loss was huge, the prospect of the game industry is not all gloom and doom. For one thing, not all the illegal downloads would be turned into legitimate sales. Many economists have studied the music and movie industries and found that while piracy hurts the sales of music records and movie box office, the replacement effect is significantly less than one. Also, while piracy can hurt the game sales, it boots the demand for, and thus the sales of, game consoles. In this project, I aim to collect a unique conjoint survey data from Hong Kong and China and then structurally estimate the effects of piracy on the sales of games and game consoles jointly. The structural estimates will help us understand the different pricing strategies of game console developers in response to game piracy and possibly shed light on the future direction of copyright policies. 電視遊戲市場近年不斷發展。根據美國的娛樂軟件聯會的數據，在2005至2009年期間，遊戲市場的增長率為每年10%。而在2011年，美國人花在電視、電腦遊戲軟件和硬件的總額為接近250億美元。在這利潤巨大的市場裡，盜版一直是行內的一個隱憂，其中一個是其對遊戲軟件銷售的影響。日本有研究指出，如果在114個盜版網頁內的與兩個手提遊戲機有關的非法下載都轉變為合法銷售，遊戲商的收入會上升48億美元。 不過，並不是所有非法下載都可轉變為合法銷售。很多經濟學者都發現在音樂和電影市場裡，即使執法令100人不作非法下載，只會有少於100人會轉而買正版。另外，雖然盜版令正版遊戲銷量下跌，但卻會令遊戲機的銷量上升。在這項研究中，我會在香港和中國收集問卷數據，並以計量方法分析盜版對遊戲和遊戲機市場的影響。這分析將有助我們理解遊戲機發展商的行銷策略。

492013.label: Realisation of objectives
492013.value: The first objective of this project is to develop and analyze a noncooperative model of network bargaining with endogenous matching. In our model, when a player is endowed with a trading opportunity, he strategically chooses with whom to bargain among those he shares link with. Thus, in the bargaining game, a player’s strategy has a more complex structure as in the model of Abreu and Manea (2012a, b), which substantially complicates the proof of the existence. We managed to show that a Markov Perfect Equilibrium (MPE) always exists in the network bargaining game. The existence result holds for networks with heterogeneous link values and link-specific allocation of bargaining power. Our proof proceeds by induction, making use of Kakutani’s fixed point theorem. This objective is fully achieved. The second objective is to investigate the properties (e.g., existence, efficiency and payoff equivalence) of Markov perfect equilibria of the dynamic bargaining game. This objective carries the most weight of the project. The fundamental task is to identify the conditions under which an efficient MPE exists. For the existence of efficient MPE, we established the condition of network homogeneity, that is, agents have identical link values, discount factors and proposing probabilities. We managed to show that for homogeneous bipartite networks, an efficient MPE always exists. For general homogeneous networks, an efficient MPE exists under a specific condition on the network structure. We also constructed an example showing that a homogeneous network may have both efficient and inefficient MPEs. There are still several conjectures that we cannot prove or disprove. Firstly, we conjecture that, even without imposing any extra condition, a general homogeneous network also possesses an efficient MPE. Secondly, we conjecture that when there are multiple efficient MPE, they must be payoff equivalent. Finally, for bipartite homogeneous networks, we conjecture that all MPEs are efficient. We tried different techniques in tackling these issues; in particular, we surveyed relevant existing results in graph theory in order to find useful mathematical tools. Up to now, there are still some gaps to fill. This objective is thus only partially (80%) achieved. The third objective is to generalize the model by allowing heterogeneous link values and link-specific allocations of bargaining power and to investigate the efficiency implications of these generalizations. By constructing counter examples, we show that when a network has heterogeneous link values or link-specific allocation of bargaining power, it is possible that all the MPEs are inefficient. Therefore, the condition of network homogeneity is a tight condition for the existence of an efficient MPE. This objective is also fully achieved. The fourth objective is to identify the conditions under which decentralized bargaining in networks can lead to an efficient outcome. The analysis required for achieving this objective largely overlapped with that of the previous one. Based on our analysis, we indeed identified the conditions under which decentralized bargaining leads to an efficient outcome. In particular, when focusing on MPEs of the bargaining game, we established the homogeneity condition. However, we also planned to provide an impossibility theorem showing that for some networks with heterogeneous link values, efficiency still cannot be achieved even when non-stationary subgame perfect equilibria are taken into account. Such an impossibility result would be interesting because it provides a new source of market failure and may give us new insights into the study of market competition. However, we have not been able to prove the impossibility theorem. Thus, this objective is also only partially (80%) achieved. Finally, I shall mention that the project has gone beyond its original objectives. The ideas gained from the theoretical analysis conducted in this project enabled the PI and another collaborator, Chiu Yu Ko at National University of Singapore, to revive an old project on one-to-many bargaining, which leads to another working paper.

492013.label: Major findings and research outcome
492013.value: In this project, the PI and the Co-I developed a model of network bargaining with endogenous matching, in which a randomly recognized player can choose to bargain with anyone with whom he shares a link. We first established the existence of a Markov Perfect Equilibrium (MPE) in the network bargaining game. For homogeneous bipartite networks, namely, buyer-seller networks, we showed that there always exists an asymptotically efficient MPE. The proof is constructive and proceeds by induction. We were particularly interested in the buyer-seller networks because it has greater relevance to economics. Due to some technical difficulties that we have not been able to overcome, for general networks, we only managed to show that an efficient MPE exists given a specific condition on the network structure. Our equilibrium construction is based on two classic results in graph theory, Gallai-Edmonds Decomposition Theorem and Dulmage-Mendelsohn Decomposition Theorem. We proved several lemmas concerning the evolution of the network structure after an arbitrary link is removed. These lemmas are valuable for related studies in their own right. Another important finding is that a homogeneous network may have both efficient and inefficient MPEs. This disproves our original conjecture that for homogeneous networks, all MPEs must be efficient and payoff-equivalent. Using several examples, we showed that when a network has heterogeneous link values or link-specific allocation of bargaining power, it is possible that all the MPEs are inefficient. The aforementioned theoretical findings are contained in a working paper, Decentralized Network Bargaining with Endogenous Matching, which is now being polished for submission. While working on the proofs of this project, the PI gained some new ideas on how to tackle the difficult technical issues in a suspended project of mine on one-to-many bargaining. Based on these new ideas, together with Chiu Yu Ko at NUS, we revived this project and our new working paper, Decentralized One-to-Many Bargaining, is now under review at the Review of Economic Studies. In this paper, we analyze a one-to-many bargaining situation where one active player seeks to reach agreement with every passive player on how to share the surplus of a joint project. Bargaining is conducted in a decentralized manner, that is, there is no fixed protocol and the active player decides with whom to bargain in each period. This modelling choice shares the same motivation as the endogenous matching rule in network bargaining.

492013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
492013.value: The main goal of this project is to investigate efficiency implications of endogenous matching in multilateral bargaining on an exogenously given network. Having obtained a good understanding about trading networks with homogeneous link values, we still have several open questions and conjectures regarding bargaining outcomes on bipartite networks and networks with heterogeneous link values. The PI and the Co-I are still attempting to provide answers to these questions. Another interesting direction for future exploration is to endogenize network formations. Since an agent’s payoff from decentralized trade largely depends on his position in the network, he may strategically establish or terminate some trading relationships. In the long run, the structure of the trading network is endogenously determined. An important research question is what network structures will arise in equilibrium. Our study on one-to-many bargaining can also be further generalized. More specifically, in our current paper, all agents are assumed to be perfect complements in generating a surplus of a fixed size. It is desirable to have a general framework in which agents could be either substitutes or complements. Such an extension will link our theoretical analysis to important applied research topics such as intra-firm bargaining, welfare implications of tariff negotiations, etc.

492013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
492013.value: In this project, we study how trading terms are determined through decentralized bilateral bargaining in a network economy. In many real life situations, due to economic and non-economic restrictions, such as market accessibility and technical compatibility, economics agents may trade with each other only if they are in some specific relationships. Such a market can be modeled into a network. It is both interesting and important to understand how economic agents interact in such network markets. In particular, it is important to investigate under what conditions the outcome of decentralized trading is efficient. A crucial feature and also a theoretical innovation of our model is that each agent, when having a trading opportunity, can choose whom to bargain with, among those he has relationship with. This is a plausible and intuitive modelling choice motivated by numerous real-life observations. We investigate the efficiency implications of this endogenous matching rule in the network economy. Our theoretical findings substantially deepen our understanding about strategic interactions of economic agents in network markets and provide new insights into the welfare analysis of decentralized market behavior.

492913.label: Project Objectives

492913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
492913.value: The globalization of accounting standards, reflected by the widespread adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), is one of the most important developments in accounting principles. One of the primary motives behind the worldwide adoption of one single set of high-quality accounting standards is to decrease compliance costs and reduce the inefficiencies associated with preparing multiple sets of financial statements to comply with different jurisdictional accounting requirements, and to improve investment efficiency and cross-border investment through the increased comparability of accounting information. Despite a growing literature examining the various economic costs and benefits of IFRS adoption, the question of whether mandatory IFRS adoption facilitates firms’ cross-border stock listing activities—a primary motive behind the International Organization of Securities Commissions’ proposal for harmonizing accounting standards across different jurisdictions surprisingly remains unaddressed. The objective of this study is to examine whether and how global accounting convergence affects firms’ foreign stock listing activities. Specifically, we ask the following questions: First, do firms increase their stock listing activities on overseas stock exchanges following mandatory IFRS adoption in their home countries, and what are the cross-sectional determinants of this change? Second, do firms from IFRS-mandating countries have different preference in the cross-listing venue choice post-IFRS adoption compared with their non-IFRS-mandating counterparts, and what drives the cross-sectional variations in their venue choices? In other words, we examine the effects of mandatory IFRS adoption on firms’ cross-listing activities and the related listing venue choices. 国际财务报告准则（IFRS）的广泛采用反映了会计准则的全球化，是会计原则最重要的发展之一。在全球范围内推行一套统一的高质量会计准则的主要动机之一是通过提高会计信息的可比性来降低合规成本（遵从成本），以减少为满足不同管辖会计之要求而编制多套财务报表所造成的效率损失，从而提高投资效率和促进跨境投资，最终优化全球资源配置。尽管越来越多的文献对采用IFRS的各种成本与收益进行了研究，但强制采用IFRS是否有利于企业跨境上市这一问题却仍未得到解决，而此问题却正是国际证券事务监察委员会组织倡议全球范围内统一会计准则的首要动机。本文对全球会计趋同是否影响以及如何影响企业境外上市的行为进行研究，具体分析以下两个问题：第一，强制采用IFRS后，该国企业的海外上市行为是否更多了，又是何种因素导致了这一变化？第二，采用IFRS后，在强制执行IFRS国家的企业与非强制执行IFRS国家的企业之间对于企业交叉上市地点的选择是否具有不同偏好，引起这种差异的动因又是什么？换言之，本文检验强制执行IFRS对于企业交叉上市行为以及交叉上市地点选择的影响。

492913.label: Major findings and research outcome
492913.value: Using a comprehensive dataset of international cross-listings spanning 34 (50) home (target) countries, we examine whether mandatory IFRS adoption facilitates firms’ cross-listing activities. Our results using difference-in-differences analyses show that firms that mandatorily adopt IFRS exhibit significantly higher cross-listing propensity and intensity following IFRS adoption. We also find that firms from mandatory IFRS adoption countries are more likely to cross-list their securities in countries also mandating IFRS and countries with larger and more liquid capital markets. We further find that IFRS adoption has a greater effect on mandatory IFRS adopters from countries with larger accounting differences from IFRS, lower disclosure requirements and less access to external capital prior to IFRS adoption. Our findings are consistent with the notion that mandatory IFRS adoption facilitates firms’ cross-listing activities and highlight the importance of considering the change in cross-listings when examining the capital market consequences of mandatory IFRS adoption.

492913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
492913.value: The comprehensive dataset collected in this project is being used for examining subsequent research questions. Specifically, I am extending the study on cross-listings to the delisting of cross-listings. Providing a better understanding on firms' cross-delisting is important because existing literature has done little in this topic given the difficulty in assembling such a dataset.

492913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
492913.value: The study directly tests one primary motive underlying the global convergence of accounting standards across different jurisdictions, and documents an important, yet untested, consequence of mandatory IFRS adoption: the facilitation of firms’ cross-listing activities. To the best of our knowledge, this study is the first to directly examine how mandatory IFRS adoption alters managers’ incentives to undertake cross-listings, and our findings provide new evidence that mandatory IFRS adoption has real consequences on corporate behaviors

493113.label: Project Title(Chinese)
493113.value: 消費者對具吸引力的服務人員的反應: 接近還是拒絕

493113.label: Project Objectives
493113.value: To examine both the positive and negative impact of physical attractiveness of service providers on consumer reactions by exploring the mediating role of self-presentation anxiety. To investigate the moderating role of embarrassing consumption on consumer reactions to attractive service providers. To explore the moderating role of self-construal on consumer reactions to attractive service providers in embarrassing consumptions.
rows: To examine both the positive and negative impact of physical attractiveness of service providers on consumer reactions by exploring the mediating role of self-presentation anxiety.
To investigate the moderating role of embarrassing consumption on consumer reactions to attractive service providers.
To explore the moderating role of self-construal on consumer reactions to attractive service providers in embarrassing consumptions.

493113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
493113.value: There is a widely accepted belief that attractive (vs. unattractive) service providers are able to bring about better service interactions and therefore increase consumer satisfaction and purchase intention (e.g., Ahearne, Gruen, and Jarvis 1999). Retaining attractive service providers in the non-profit sector has also been found to generate larger donations (Reingen and Kernan 1993); and a recent study has evidenced that consumers will give higher product evaluations if they simply perceive the product as having been touched by an attractive opposite-sex service provider (Argo, Dahl, and Morales 2008). In essence, consumers love attractive people, and recruiting attractive service providers has become a pervasive phenomenon. Despite the evidence showing the favorable impact on consumer reactions to attractive service providers, this may not always be beneficial. Building on the impression management literature (Schlenker 1980), there is a possibility that consumers sometimes hesitate in interacting with attractive providers. Notably, they are more motivated to present a favorable self before an attractive (vs. unattractive) opposite-sex person because they believe the latter’s evaluations of them are more important (Schlenker and Leary 1982). This higher motivation towards self-presentation may create greater social anxiety as the consumers feel unable to present satisfactory impressions in the presence of attractive providers. Therefore, we propose that when consumers’ attention in service interactions is drawn to their anxieties arising from self-presentation, they react less positively to attractive (vs. unattractive) providers. When they do not focus their attention on the anxieties, however, the reverse is true. We suggest one feature of consumption that will heighten consumer self-presentation anxiety in service interactions as being the consumption of a product that is likely to cause embarrassment (“embarrassing consumption”). Embarrassment is an awkward emotional state that threatens an individual’s desired social identity in social interactions (Miller 1996). Some products can generate greater embarrassment than others, such as condoms and those relating to weight loss. Since embarrassing consumption can bring about a negative evaluation, consumers may react less positively to attractive (vs. unattractive) providers. We also suspect this pattern will be stronger for consumers with interdependent (vs. independent) self-construal, given they are more sensitive to impression management. This is the first study to examine when physical attractiveness of service providers increases consumers’ favorable reactions and when it decreases at a first-time purchase and situated within the context of embarrassing consumption. Findings will offer valuable managerial insights into attractive (vs. unattractive) providers and Asian (vs. Western) consumer behavior. 是次研究題目探討外表具吸引力的服務人員是如何及怎樣對消費者在服務過程中產生影響。 一般人認為外表具吸引力(對比低吸引力)的服務員會更容易受顧客歡迎，及有助提升顧客對其服務的滿意度。例如最近一些研究發現，若福利機構的工作人員外表吸引，會讓人增加捐贈。亦有研究指出消費者會因為產品被外表吸引的異性服務員觸摸過而對這產品產生興趣。 儘管很多研究認為聘請外表吸引的服務員會有好處，如提高顧客對產品的購買意慾，但本硏究認為在一些情況下，外表具吸引力(對比低吸引力)的服務員反而有機會降低顧客購買產品及服務的意慾。 在印象管理的文章裡，有提及到人們面對外表吸引的異性時，會特別想得到他們的注意及留下良好印象。這種渴望有機會產生一種不敢直接面對外表吸引的異性的恐懼。因為人們會擔心自己不能在對方面前產生良好的印象。所以若當這種恐懼出現時，人們反而不會願意和外表吸引的異性接觸。 本硏究認為尷尬的消費情景(如購買生理，減肥)用品會特別容易讓消費者產生這種恐懼。這種尷尬的消費情景若聘用外表吸引的服務員可能會產生反效果。本研究將會透過一系列實驗引證以上的假設。

493113.label: Realisation of objectives
493113.value: All objectives were achieved. We conducted six studies in total to address objectives 1 and 2 and the manuscript was successfully published at the top tier marketing journal, namely, Journal of Consumer Research. We also presented the findings in one international conference and two invited research seminars. Publication: Wan, Lisa C. and Robert S. Wyer (2015), “Consumer Reactions to Attractive Service Providers: Approach or Avoid?” Journal of Consumer Research, 42(4), 578-95. Conference: Wan, Lisa C. and Robert S. In addition, we conducted another 3 studies to test the objective 3. Results supported our predictions. We found that the impacts of self-presentation concerns on people reactions to attractive individuals are more salient for people with interdependent selves than those with independent selves. We submitted the manuscript to the top tier psychology journal, namely, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. Unfortunately, the manuscript was rejected in the second round.
