493113.label: Major findings and research outcome
493113.value: Attractive service providers are often assumed to elicit favorable consumer reactions and to increase purchase intentions. However, this may not always be true. A pilot study and five field and laboratory experiments show that when a self-presentation concern is made salient, consumers react less positively to highly attractive providers than to less attractive ones. This concern can be influenced by chronic social anxiety or can be aroused by unrelated experiences that consumers have before being exposed to the service interactions. In addition, it can be activated by the type of product being sold, that is, a product that is likely to cause embarrassment. Thus, the attractiveness of a service provider can have either positive or negative effects on consumers’ reactions to a consumption experience and their consequent purchase intentions, depending on the type of product under consideration. These effects occur when the service provider is both of the opposite sex and the same sex. However, self-presentation concerns when an opposite-sex provider is attractive are driven by sexual motives whereas these self-presentation concerns when a same-sex target is attractive are stimulated by social comparison processes. The manuscript with the above findings was successfully published at the top tier marketing journal, namely, Journal of Consumer Research. We also presented the findings in one international conference and two invited research seminars. Publication: Wan, Lisa C. and Robert S. Wyer (2015), “Consumer Reactions to Attractive Service Providers: Approach or Avoid?” Journal of Consumer Research, 42(4), 578-95. Conference: Wan, Lisa C. and Robert S. Wyer (2015), “Consumer Reactions to Attractive Service Providers: Approach or Avoid,” Paper presented at the Academy of International Business Southeast Asia Regional Conference, Malaysia. Invited Research Seminars Consumer Reactions to Attractive Service Providers: Approach or Avoid, Research Seminar, Management School, Jinan University, China, 2016. Consumer Reactions to Attractive Service Providers: Approach or Avoid, Research Seminar, Department of Marketing and International Business, Lingnan University, 2014. In addition, we conducted a few more studies to test the objective 3 and found that the impacts of self-presentation concerns on people reactions to attractive individuals are more salient for people with interdependent selves than those with independent selves. We will prepare the manuscript for these findings and will submit it to psychology journal.

493113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
493113.value: We think that more research works can be done on the topic of incidental embarrassment. The majority of previous embarrassment literature has focused on individuals’ reactions to persons who are aware of the incident that created their embarrassment (e.g., Feinberg, Willer, & Keltner, 2012; Keltner & Buswell, 1997). With few exceptions (Apsler, 1975), little attention has been given to embarrassed individuals’ reactions to people who are unaware of the source of their embarrassment and the feelings they are experiencing. In fact, Goffman (1959) contended that embarrassed individuals are typically unmotivated to restore their damaged self-image when the persons with whom they interact are unaware of the incident that gave rise to their embarrassment. This conceptualization suggests that embarrassed persons’ tendency to avoid interacting with physically attractive persons would not be evident when these persons have no knowledge of the conditions that gave rise to them. In contrast to Goffman’s speculation, however, we suggest that it is possible for embarrassed people are motivated to protect their social image even when they interact with attractive non-observers. Future research can further explore the impact of incidental embarrassment on people reactions to attractive salesperson.

493113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
493113.value: We often assume physical attraction will be an advantage in life. When we go shopping and see a highly attractive salesperson, we will be more willing to spend time interacting with the salesperson and be more likely to buy the products. Past research also qualified this assumption, as evidenced by consumers’ greater satisfaction with the service and their intentions to purchase the products being sold. However, our study suggests that this may not always be true. We show that attractive salespeople can sometimes lead consumers to have self-presentation concerns about their ability to make a good impression on others. When consumers’ self-presentation concerns are heightened (i.e., in embarrassing consumption situations or consumers with chronically high social anxiety), they often avoid interacting with physically attractive salespeople, hence making it relatively ineffective for the salespeople to sell their products. These findings were published in the top tier journal and were widely reported by a variety of influential local, regional and international media outlets, spanning from Hong Kong to Australia, China, France, India, Italy, the United States and the United Kingdom. Publications that have run articles on the findings include Money, The Times, The Telegraph, Yahoo! Style, Oriental Daily News and more.

493313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
493313.value: In this project we examine the bias of the media controlled by government. While media is generally held to play a monitoring role in the corporate world, their incentives to fulfill such a function would be compromised when both the media companies and the commercial companies are controlled by the same ultimate owner, the state. Using a unique dataset from China about public companies’ clarification statements on media’s reports, we find that reports of the media, which are all owned by the state, are significantly more favorable for state-owned enterprises (SOEs) than for non-SOEs. In addition, when revenues of the newspaper’s print space are guaranteed by the government, the newspaper has significantly lower incentives to uncover negative news of the SOEs. Finally, media are significantly less likely to report bad news if the public company contributed revenues to the media company in the past. Overall, our findings shed new light on how political forces shape the function of the media. 本文研究政府控制的媒体的有偏报道。当企业和媒体被同一个所有者，政府，控制的时候，媒体的监督功能就会被削弱。实证检验支持这一假说。

493613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
493613.value: Girls in the socially conservative Islamic society face an additional obstacle to attend school because of the hesitance of some parents to send their daughters to coed schools, particularly at the secondary school level. The proposed project will estimate the effect of the availability of different types of secondary schools (whether girls-only or coed) on girls’ educational attainment in Jordan by exploiting differences in the supply of schools by type, region, and cohort. To our knowledge, this will be the first study on the role of sex-segregated schools in increasing girls’ schooling in the Islamic society. Furthermore, relying on the exogenous variation in women’s schooling induced by differences in school availability across regions and cohorts, the proposed project will also extend the investigation to the causal effect of women’s education on fertility. 伊斯兰社会中的女孩在接受教育上面临着额外的阻力由于他们的父母对于将女孩送到男女混校—尤其是中学--心存顾虑。通过研究不同类型的学校的供给区域和年代差异，本课题将估算不同类型的中学（女校或者是男女混校）的存在对约旦女孩教育程度的影响。据我们所知，这是第一个探讨伊斯兰社会中男女分校对于增加女孩学校教育影响的研究。此外，利用外生的不同地区和年代之间的女性教育程度的变化，本课题也将研究延伸到探讨女性教育对于生育的因果效应。

493713.label: Major findings and research outcome
493713.value: This research has produced three publications, all related to the topic of emotional reactions and the perception of connectedness. In the first paper (Li and Zhang 2014), we found that exposure to images of sexy women decreases male consumers’ perception of being connected to others. We also test the downstream behavioral consequences of this reduced psychological connectedness (e.g., less resource allocation and less helping). In the second paper (Zhang and Aggarwal 2015), we examine how consumers evaluate a target in the present that is positively associated with them in the past or future. We suggest that such an evaluations is affected by the perceived connectedness between their current self and temporal self, that is, the self at that particular point in time of association with the target in the past or future. A strong (vs. weak) connectedness will result in a more (vs. less) favorable evaluation of the target—be it a product, brand, or pro-social cause. In the third paper (Shen, Zhang, Krishna 2016), we show that a touch interface, such as that provided by an iPad, compared with a nontouch interface, such as that of a desktop computer with a mouse, facilitates the choice of an affect-laden alternative over a cognitively superior one. We also find some mediational support that the direct touch effect is driven by the enhanced connectedness between the consumer and the product on touch interfaces. All three papers have rich theoretical and managerial implications.

493713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
493713.value: In addition to the investigation of consumer reaction and psychological connectedness, in the third paper, we also extend our understanding of connectedness in general (e.g., the perceived connectedness between a consumer and a digital device). Future research should continue to investigate the influences of different kinds of connectedness perception: intra-personal (especially between their past self and current self), inter-personal (between the current self and another individual) and human-object connectedness.

493913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
493913.value: The aims of this project are to investigate the role and channels of equity short-selling and shorting bonds through credit default swaps (CDS) in the spread of the recent financial crisis and to examine the contagion effects across financial markets. Short-selling of stocks and the trading of CDS have often been cited as obvious causes for the escalation of the recent financial crisis. A CDS may best be thought of as an insurance contract against the default of a corporate bond or securitized debt. Buying protection in the CDS market parallels short-selling in the debt market. Existing studies typically focused separately on either short-selling or CDS trading. Currently, very liitle research is being carried out to consider the role played in the spread of financial contagion by the combination of the short-selling of equities and the trading of CDS. With comprehensive data on stocks, bonds, short sales and CDS readily available, an investigate will be carried out into whether the short-selling of equity and shorting bonds through CDS affect American (US) stocks and bonds' returns, volatilities and skewnesses respectively. Three possible contagion channels will also be studied: liquidity, risk premium and positive feedback trading channels. A portfolio-level analysis will be implemented to study the dynamic structure of contagion across financial markets given the simultaneous trading of stocks, bonds and CDS during the recent crisis. Our research will allow academics, practitioners, regulators and policymakers to better understand financial contagion in general and the impact of short-selling and CDS trading in particular. It will offer several specific and important contributions. Firstly, when combined with the existing stock and bond trading databases, newly-available records of individual short trades and CDS trading data, it will allow detailed examination of multi-faceted major financial crises. Secondly, the data will enable us to critically examine the effects of financial contagion on stocks and bonds' return, volatility and skewness. In particular, volatility and skewness measure (extreme) risk and thus provide the opportunity to identify how short selling of stocks and shorting bonds through CDS spreads the risk in the crisis. Thirdly, a deeper understanding of the impact of short-selling and CDS will provide valuable insight for those who are under pressure to restrain short-selling and eliminate over-the-counter CDS trading.

499913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
499913.value: 伦理决策的文献多年来一直由基于推理和认知过程的理论主导(Jones, 1991; Kohlberg, 1969)，近年来，越来越多的研究开始检验伦理决策中过分依赖理性和经济核算所带来的负面效应 (Monlinsky, Grant, 和 Margolis, 2012; Zhong, 2011)，以及这些模型对于解释伦理决策实践时产生的局限性 (Haidt, 2001)。与此同时，情绪在决策行为中的作用受到越来越多的关注 (Ashton-James和Ashkanasy, 2008; Seo和Barrett, 2007)，而道德直觉的研究恰好结合了以上两种趋势。道德直觉是特指与他人利益和福利相关的情绪，例如道德情绪，这种情绪在伦理决策和行为中扮演至关重要的角色。(Graham, Haidt,和Nosek, 2009; Haidt, 2003; Haidt 和Joseph, 2007). 基于道德基础理论，我们认为道德情绪对于组织情景下的伦理决策十分重要。我们将通过三个实证研究通过不同方法回答以下问题：道德情绪从何而来？为何我们看不见道德情绪？道德情绪如何帮助组织？研究一将测试道德价值观与道德情绪的内在联系，以及其如何影响伦理决策。在研究一中，我们将运用事件相关脑电位（Event-Related Brain Potential，简称ERP）技术捕捉情绪体验。研究二将测试现代商业规范对情绪的减缓作用，研究三显示道德情绪对决策质量的影响依赖于决策类型和情绪表达的情景规范。 以往的研究大多忽视了组织情景下情绪在伦理决策中的作用，而现有的理论对情绪与决策质量之间的关系也没有统一的结论，本研究将通过测试包含道德情绪的过程来填补这一空白。本研究的结论对商业实践具有重要的意义：首先，本文为组织提供了防止欺诈的决策工具，此工具之前未被充分利用，并被系统性抑制；其次，帮助组织避免道德丑闻，为培养适当伦理行为提供指导。同时，本文对教育领域也有贡献，特别是引进道德直觉以及其如何对我们对学生和未来管理者产生影响。

499913.label: Realisation of objectives
499913.value: Objective #1 was to establish the link between moral values and moral emotions in ethical decision making contexts. I examined this link in two ways: first in the study with business school students, and second, in a laboratory experiment using fMRI method. In the first study, moral emotions showed to have a robust effect on ethical decision making, regardless of individual difference in individual value preference. This was in contrast with hedonic emotions, whose role was moderated by individual value preference. In the second paper, the result suggested that superior frontal gyrus (associated with moral emotions of righteous anger and sympathy) was more likely to be activated for individuals with high fairness value. Similarly, care endorsement was associated with activation of inferior frontal gyrus (associated with moral emotions of sympathy). Together the findings from the two studies point to the role of moral values in in eliciting moral emotions, as well as its role in regulating the role of non-moral emotions in ethical decision making. Objective #2 deals with testing and demonstrating that the exposure to current business norms suppresses moral intuition. Two conference presentations made in the Academy of Management and Asia Academy of Management illustrated exactly this relationship. In the study involving business school students, those with higher exposure to business education (e.g., MBA) illustrated a higher association between emotional intention and ethical decision making. Further, prosocial values and achievement oriented values, both associated with business school exposure (lower prosocial values and higher achievement oriented values) led to stronger negative association between hedonic emotions and ethical behavior. The association between hedonic emotions and unethical decision for those with higher business exposure suggest that these individuals are less likely to use moral intuition in their ethical decision making. Objective #3 was to demonstrate when it is better to rely on moral emotions and how to promote moral intuition. In the paper involving fMRI study, subjects with activation of superior frontal gyrus (associated with sympathy) in the presence of harm being done to a 3rd party were more likely to find the unethical situation (another person being harmed) unacceptable, and this decision was made more quickly. On the other hand, middle temporal gyrus (associated anger) led to higher approval rate of an unfair treatment of another person, and a less likelihood of trying to help the victim. Together, the findings suggest when an individual is an observer of an unethical situation, relying on moral emotions lead to better outcomes (i.e., judgements and behaviors adhering to fundamental moral norms), rather than relying on general emotions such as anger. The shorter decision time in relation to sympathy also suggests that moral emotion is associated with moral intuition (a swift judgement of what is right or wrong). In the paper using business school students, we posit that moral intuition may be promoted by including moral emotions in to the business education curriculum and teaching students how to understand and respond to their gut feelings better. These findings are reported in two papers, both currently under revision and close to submission after receiving feedback from the editor and associate editor of target journals. Specifically, the paper involving fMRI study received a positive and constructive feedback after presenting to the editor of Academy of Management Discoveries (Dr. Peter Bamberger), and I am currently making a substantial revision based on his comments. The study involving business school students was sent to the associate editor of Academy of Management Learning and Education, who also provided constructive feedback to increase the chance of publishing in the journal.

499913.label: Major findings and research outcome
499913.value: The major findings from studies based on this project are threefold. First, moral emotions are more robust in predicting business school students’ ethical behavior, while other type of emotions was regulated by moral values. These findings were presented at two major international conferences, and reported in a paper that is in its final stage of revision based on the feedback from the associate editor of the target journal (Academy of Management Learning and Education). Second, disinterestedness (the extent to which a person does not have his or her interest at stake) of an unethical event is an important predictor of moral emotions, and that moral emotions predicts the content and time spent on moral judgment. These findings using fMRI methods are reported in a paper that is under a major revision based on the feedback from the editor of the target journal (Academy of Management Discoveries). Third, my doctoral student successfully defended his dissertation building on this project. In a laboratory experiment and a field study, he examined the role of righteous anger (in reaction to customer mistreatment) among service employees and found that frequency of these anger triggering events plays an important role in determining how emotions are translated into employee behaviors.

499913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
499913.value: As mentioned above, two papers are now under revision based on constructive and positive feedback from decision makers at the targeting journals. Upon completion of the revision, the papers will be submitted for peer review and consideration for publication. Mr. Sun Cong's dissertation is currently being revised for journal submission. I have another paper on moral emotions that builds on this project, examining the role of supervisor-directed moral emotions, i.e., disgust or righteous anger towards the supervisor. I have finished collecting data from managers in Mainland China, and currently analyzing the data. This paper is targeting an international peer-reviewed journal (Academy of Management Journal). Finally, my doctoral student and I will revise his dissertation for journal submission, to be under review before the end of this year.

499913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
499913.value: The findings from this project show that certain other-focused 'moral' emotions, such as sympathy or righteous anger, play a significant role in ethical decision making. Especially when an individual is not the direct victim of an unethical event, moral emotions are likely to be aroused, and they play a central role in making ethical judgment. Also, the role of moral emotion in ethical decision making is much stronger than other types of emotion (i.e, excitement, satisfaction about future gains), which was regulated by how achievement-oriented and how less prosocial an individual is. This was demonstrated through a survey data and an experiment using brain scanning.

500113.label: Project Title(Chinese)
500113.value: 平均場理論，隨機控制及偏微分方程系統

500113.label: Co - Investigator(s)
500113.value: Prof Bensoussan, Alain Prof Yam, Phillip, Sheung-Chi

500113.label: Project Objectives
500113.value: For MFGs, HJB approach was first developed in which the HJB equation becomes a coupled HJB-FP(Fokker-Planck) equation. In contrast, for the mean field type control problem, its tackling is essentially via the stochastic maximum principle approach; the main reason is that in the mean field type control problem, the state evolution is no more a standard diffusion but satisfies a McKean-Vlasov equation, which is obtained by incorporating in the drift and diffusion terms the probability distribution of its own diffusion dynamics. Therefore, the process by its own right is not a Markov process which results in the failure of the application of dynamic programming argument. Our first objective is to show that dynamic programming and stochastic maximum principle are viable with complementary advantages and limitations. We plan to reinterpret the HJB equation differently; it is not the evolution of the value function, but a necessary condition of optimality for the dual control problem; indeed, this property is rarely applied in classical control theory, but for mean field type control it becomes critical. Moreover, to the best of our knowledge, the HJB-FP approach to mean field type control leads to interesting systems of PDE which have never appeared in the existing literature. They look more sophisticated than those arising from MFGs, but we believe that they require less condition on the existence of solutions (as supported by our recent study on the linear quadratic case, see Bensoussan et al. (2012)). One of the great discoveries of MFGs is that it simplifies considerably the study of Nash differential games with a very large number of players provided that they are identical; though it is a substantial limitation from the application perspective. In reality, what we normally encounter is a mixture of different large communities but not just a single one. Our second objective is to relax this confinement. Conceptually, it leads to reducing a differential game with a very large number of players to a differential game with a finite number of players; it still remains a game and not a control problem. The price to pay is to study systems of coupled HJB-FP equations, which is much more complex than a single coupled HJB-FP equation. This mathematical challenge and the consequences in applications (e.g. in risk management) form the core of our second objective. We want to study the optimization of a combination of moments and not just an expected value (in particular the variance of the random objective function). Our third objective can also be regarded as an alternative extension of MFGs to one with inhomogeneous players; instead of coalitions, we consider a MFG with one (or may be several) major players dominant while the rest of other players can only influence others with negligible effect. This problem, being different from a Stackelberg game, has been introduced by Huang and his collaborators in the linear-quadratic case, with a recent extension to non-LQ models by Nourian-Caines. The corresponding mathematical challenge is that, because the players react to the major player action, their HJB-FP equations become conditional to the major player decision, and hence stochastic. The works mentioned above only provide a partial answer to the problem. We aim to proceed on further study in order to tackle the corresponding complete system of forward-backward stochastic PDE and DE (differential equations) arisen in the mean field games with major players.

500113.value: 自平均場博弈的概念引進以來，已在許多先進國家內被率先進行深入研究。興趣源於既是因為提出不少新的數學問題同時亦帶有多樣的應用性。平均場類型控制，跟平均場博弈有很多相似之處，是一個不同的方向。它導致新類型正倒向隨機微分方程系統的應用於非標準隨機控制問題上。我們的首要目標是提供一個統一的方法來比較這兩個研究方向和相應的解決方案。在線性二次的情況下，我們已發現可以做到一個非常有趣的比較。 我們提出的比較主要涉及到方法論上，事實上，最優控制理論主要建基在兩種研究方法：動態規劃與最大值原理。第一個方法導出哈密頓 - 雅克比 - 貝爾曼（HJB ）偏微分方程（ PDE ），第二個方法導出正倒向隨機微分方程系統。平均場博弈導出耦合 HJB- FP的Fokker-Planck方程組。另一方面，平均場類型控制問題，它主要採用隨機最大值原理的方法。我們認為重要的是，就像在傳統的控制理論中，證明這兩種方法都是可能的。此外，就我們所知， 用HJB-FP方法解平均場類型控制而導出有趣的PDE的系統是從未在文獻中出現。可以說，在一般的情況下，仍然是一個懸而未決的問題。平均場博弈取得了顯著的成功，雖然不直接是一個博弈，而是一個控制問題，當個別參與者的數量是非常大時以及每個人與他人相同, 它提供了一個非常簡單的近似納什類型的微分博弈。然而，每個個別參與者與他人相同的條件是嚴重的限制。我們的第二個目標是放棄這個限制，並探討大聯盟之間的競爭形勢。我們在這裡遇到新的系統，這是具有挑戰性的數學偏微分方程組。事實上，相比一個單一的耦合HJB- FP方程, 耦合HJB- FP方程組要複雜得多。除了大聯盟之間的競爭形勢，我們還計劃考慮有主要參與者的斯坦克爾伯格博弈。在這種情況下，由於主要參與者的影響, 每位個別參與者的控制的模式因此亦依賴主要參與者的決定。 耦合HJB- FP方程的系統同時亦變得隨機化，相應的正倒向隨機偏微分方, 到目前為止在文獻中只有部份的解決方案。在應用上，我們有興趣在風險管理方面發展，要優化的目標泛函不只是期望值，但亦考慮到其他的矩，特別是目標泛函為方差時。這些問題都不是標準的隨機控制問題，但有趣的是，它們會導致HJB- FP耦合的方程或方程組。為風險管理領域打開了卓有成效的研究方向。

500113.label: Realisation of objectives
500113.value: REALIZATION OF OBJECTIVES The objectives have been substantially achieved and extended. The first objective was to provide a unified approach to mean field game theory and mean field type control. It is important to have in mind that they are two different problems. The origin of mean field games is to consider games with an infinite number of players, as limits of games with a large number of players. This goes back to mean field theory developed in the physical sciences, whose objective is to study the interaction of a very large number of particles. Studying the problem at the microscopic level is impossible. When the number is infinite, the situation may simplify, under the major assumption that particles are identical. This is due to an averaging effect. The trajectory of each particle is then the consequence of its own evolution, as if it were in a vacuum, modified by a term, called the mean field term, which represents the aggregated influence of all particles. The density of particles in a given state then obtains this mean field term. So mean field theory is a fixed-point theory. One fixes the mean-field term and solves the problem of a single particle. The mean-field term is derived afterwards by a fixed-point argument. Mean-field games transpose the concepts to social sciences. Particles are replaced with individuals, who interact. A main assumption is to assume them identical. An important difference with particles is that individual take decisions. Therefore, the type of games they play also captures the interaction. We assume that they play a Nash game. This gigantic Nash game is replaced with a control problem for a single individual called the representative agent. The evolution of the representative agent is modified to take into account a mean field term. The objective is also modified with the mean field term. One then solves the control problem of the representative agent, and determines the mean field term by a fixed-point argument. This approach leads to a considerable simplification. A huge Nash point problem is changed into a control problem and a fixed-point argument. Since the problem of each individual is a stochastic control problem, we can write a Bellman equation for the value function and write a Pontryagin maximum principle. The Bellman equation is a partial differential equation, depending on a function, which is a probability measure depending on time. This is the mean-field term. It is itself defined as the probability measure of the stochastic optimal state of the system. This is the solution of a Fokker-Planck equation. So the fixed-point is materialized by a coupled system of P.DE, H.J.B and Fokker-Planck equations. A lot of effort has been provided towards solving this coupled system of P.D.E. One is backward; the H.J.B equation and the other one is forward, the Fokker-Planck equation. A mean-field type control problem is a control problem for a dynamic system , whose evolution is not standard. The evolution is not a stochastic differential equation, but a Mac Kean Vlasov equation. This is an S.D.E., which depends parametrically of the probability measure of its solution. Therefore, it is itself obtained by a fixed-point argument. We can still write the Fokker-Planck equation, but it is a functional P.D.E. , so a non-local P.D.E. We then write a necessary condition of optimality. This is the same philosophy as the Maximum Principle, except that we operate on the P.D.E. formulation, which is deterministic, instead of on the stochastic evolution. In this approach, the “adjoint equation” as expected from control theory turns out to look like the Hamilton Jacobi Bellman equation of Mean Field Games. It is not the same of course, since additional terms appear. Besides, its solution cannot be interpreted as the value function of a stochastic control problem. The stochastic process, which is the solution of the Mc Kean-Vlasov evolution, is not a Markov process, since the probability distribution introduces non-local links. The HJB equation turns out to be an adjoint equation for distributed parameter control equation. This interpretation remains valid in the case of standard diffusions, but it is not used since the value function interpretation prevails. This is our main contribution towards the first objective. We have shown that a system of HJB-Fokker Planck equations govern both problems, but they have different interpretations. To solve the system of HJB- Fokker Planck equations of the Mean Field type control problem, we have made use of the fact that we solve a control problem. This leads to precious a priori estimates, which helps in proving the existence of solutions. This method does not work for the system of HJB-Fokker Planck equations of mean-field games, and it contributes to substantiating the intuition that Mean field type control problems are better posed than Mean field games. This intuition is quite clear in the linear quadratic case, where we obtain Riccati equations, which are symmetric for mean field- type control problems and non-symmetric for mean-field games. For the second objective, we have obtained systems of systems of HJB-Fokker Planck equations, both for the mean-field type control and the mean-field game situations. More precisely, the mean-field type control problem becomes a mean field type differential game. We indeed have a game among coalitions, which are represented by representative agents. We have extended our method of obtaining a priori estimates, to the case of mean-field type differential games. For mean-field games of coalitions, we have been able to extend the key result of mean field games, namely the interpretation as a limit of a very large Nash game composed of identical players. The extension is the natural one. We have coalitions composed of a very large number of identical players, but the coalitions have different characteristics. The coalitions play at their level a Nash game, which is of course composed of a finite number of players, the number of coalitions. In the third objective, we consider the situation of a major player and a vast community of identical players. We have considered a Stackelberg game, between the Major Player and the representative agent of the large community. We have obtained a set of necessary conditions. To do this, we use at the level of the representative agent the formulation of control of the Fokker-Planck equation, mentioned above for the mean field- type control problems. However, the evolution of the representative agent depends on the major player state, which is random. Therefore, the Fokker-Planck equation is also random. However, since it is a forward equation, it can be written as in the deterministic case, simply with random coefficients. Since the HJB equation is backward, we cannot proceed as in the deterministic case, because the random field is not adapted. In fact, the HJB equation becomes a backward stochastic P.D.E. The Stackelberg game becomes a stochastic control problem, with a state composed of the proper state of the leader, augmented with the value function and the probability distribution of the representative agent. Introducing adjoint processes, we formulate a necessary condition of optimality for the Stackelberg game as a system of six coupled stochastic forward backward differential equations and stochastic forward back ward partial differential equations. We have studied the linear quadratic case. We cover results in the literature as particular cases.

rows: Our first objective is to show that dynamic programming and stochastic maximum principle are viable with complementary advantages and limitations. We plan to reinterpret the HJB equation differently; it is not the evolution of the value function, but a necessary condition of optimality for the dual control problem; indeed, this property is rarely applied in classical control theory, but for mean field type control it becomes critical. Moreover, to the best of our knowledge, the HJB-FP approach to mean field type control leads to interesting systems of PDE which have never appeared in the existing literature. They look more sophisticated than those arising from MFGs, but we believe that they require less condition on the existence of solutions (as supported by our recent study on the linear quadratic case, see Bensoussan et al. (2012)).

Our second objective is to relax this confinement. Conceptually, it leads to reducing a differential game with a very large number of players to a differential game with a finite number of players; it still remains a game and not a control problem. The price to pay is to study systems of coupled HJB-FP equations, which is much more complex than a single coupled HJB-FP equation. This mathematical challenge and the consequences in applications (e.g. in risk management) form the core of our second objective. We want to study the optimization of a combination of moments and not just an expected value (in particular the variance of the random objective function).

Our third objective can also be regarded as an alternative extension of MFGs to one with inhomogeneous players; instead of coalitions, we consider a MFG with one (or may be several) major players dominant while the rest of other players can only influence others with negligible effect. This problem, being different from a Stackelberg game, has been introduced by Huang and his collaborators in the linear-quadratic case, with a recent extension to non-LQ models by Nourian-Caines. The corresponding mathematical challenge is that, because the players react to the major player action, their HJB-FP equations become conditional to the major player decision, and hence stochastic. The works mentioned above only provide a partial answer to the problem. We aim to proceed on further study in order to tackle the corresponding complete system of forward-backward stochastic PDE and DE (differential equations) arisen in the mean field games with major players.

500113.label: Major findings and research outcome
500113.value: RESEARCH OUTCOME MAJOR FINDINGS AND RESEACH OUTCOME Our significant results concern the methodology. Mean field games amount to a coupled system of partial differential equations, one HJB equation and one Fokker-Planck equation. We have solved some classes of problems and considered mean-field game for coalitions, which lead to systems of systems of HJB-FK equations. Regarding mean field type control, recalling that it is a not standard stochastic control problem, one cannot expect a HJB equation in the usual sense. A major result of our project has been to show that a system HJB- FP is still valid. It looks like the one of Mean Field game theory, with differences, and different interpretation. This interpretation stems from the fact that a stochastic control problem is also a deterministic control problem for a distributed parameter system. The evolution follows a P.D.E. This requires however to limit oneself to controls which are feedbacks. The state of the system is the probability distribution of the stochastic state and follows a Fokker Planck equation. This approach is the key to obtain the system of HJB-FP equations of mean-field type control. We have developed an important application of mean-field type control, the topic of Risk Management. It is a well know drawback of standard stochastic control that risk is not addressed, because one optimizes the average of a random cost. This average will never occur. Instead, the random cost occurs, and its variance may be very large. Mean field type control theory is exactly the mathematical theory, which is needed. We have applied the methodology to problems of growth of firms, and consumer-behavior optimization. For the situation of major player and a community with a representative agent, we have extended existing results. The problem has similarities with Stackelberg games. The decision of the dominating player affects the representative agent. If the dominating player evolution depends on a noise, which is specific, the probability distribution of the state of the representative agent becomes a conditional probability. In that case, the deterministic problem of control of P.D.E becomes a stochastic control of P.D.E. We have extended our objectives, by considering the problem of the Master equation, which is a P.D.E. on an infinite dimensional space. We have shown that there are two Master equations, one scalar and one vector. The scalar Master equation allows decoupling the system of HJB-FP equations. Therefore, it provides a new insight on the study of the system of HJB-FP equations.

500113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
500113.value: POTENTIAL FOR FURTHER DEVELOPMENT AND THE PROPOSED COURSE OF ACTION There is a huge potential for further development. An important issue concerns the study of the Master equation. It begins with the study of Bellman equation in an infinite dimensional space, at least for mean-field type control problems. The infinite dimensional space is the space of probability measures. The drawback is that it is not a vector space. A nice metric exists, the Wasserstein metric, and it is conceivable to consider controlled dynamic systems, in which the state evolves in a metric space. There are also alternatives to recover the vector space environment. One is to consider probability densities. P.L. Lions has introduced a second one. To a probability measure, one associates a random variable, and one can then work in the Hilbert space of square integrable random variables. This approach seems to be the most promising. We want to explore it to a full extent, which means considering control problems directly in the Hilbert space of square integrable random variables. There are also many problems regarding major player. They can themselves compete, which amounts to coalitions with major players. A natural complement is the study of information, among players, in particular major and minor players. Finally, applications are numerous

500113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
500113.value: THE LAYMAN’S SUMMARY This theory is an adaptation of mean field theory, developed in the physical sciences, and applies to many situations of social sciences, but also to problems of large networks in general, possibly telecommunication or computer networks, large energy grids or traffic on highways. There are two theories, mean field games and mean field type control. It has been for long a source of confusion, since the theories are close but not identical, and correspond to a different background. The interesting feature is that, mathematically, there are many similarities, which it is useful to recognize, and it is important to understand the differences. Transposing the idea to social sciences means for instance, that one will consider individuals in a large community, as particles and try to identify some aggregation phenomenon. However, in social sciences, individuals are also decision makers. One meets immediately a phenomenon, which is completely new to physics. Can we aggregate decisions? Mean field games theory tries to answer positively to this question, at least accepting restrictions, which one can hope to reduce thanks to an impressive amount of research. In addition, in social sciences, there is a big heterogeneity among players, even though communities can also be aggregated.

500213.label: Project Title(Chinese)
500213.value: 非光滑優化問題的二階數值方法

500213.label: Project Objectives
500213.value: We will develop efficient second-order methods for solving nonsmooth, nonconvex minimization problems such as smoothing trust region Newton methods, Newton interior point methods. We will establish comprehensive theoretical results on convergence rate and complexity bounds for second-order methods to solve nonsmooth optimization. We will derive innovative second-order necessary conditions and sufficient conditions for local minimizers of nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization problems. We will explore more theoretical properties of smoothing functions for nonsmooth functions, such as the gradient consistency and second-order approximation. We will extensively test the proposed algorithms and compare them with the existing algorithms in terms of speed, accuracy, robustness and complexity. Real data sets will be used to test the efficiency of the new theory and algorithms.

500213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
500213.value: Nonsmooth optimization problems have many important applications in economics and engineering. Over the decades, first-order numerical methods for nonsmooth optimization problems have been well developed. Recently, with rapid development of computer hardware and software, second-order numerical methods have attracted considerable attention. For example, semi-smooth Newton methods for solving nonsmooth convex L1 regularized minimization in parallel computing environments have been developed. As is well-known, second-order methods have many advantages over first-order approaches in solving numerous smooth optimization problems in terms of speed and convergence to second-order stationary points that satisfy stronger optimality conditions than first-order stationary points. Newton's method is a typical second-order numerical method for solving smooth optimization problems, which constructs accurate quadratic approximations of the objective function by using the gradient and Hessian of the function. However, very little is known about second-order numerical methods for finding second-order stationary points of nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization problems. Newton's method cannot be directly applied to nonsmooth optimization, because the gradient and Hessian by standard definitions simply do not exist. This project aims to develop second-order numerical methods for a class of nonsmooth composite minimization problems arising from various important applications. Especially, even when the problem is non-Lipschitz and nonconvex, the proposed methods can find scaled second-order stationary points. We will establish novel concepts and theory for constructing second-order approximations. In particular, we will use smoothing approximations and subspace approximations based on the special structure of the composite functions. We will compare smoothing Newton methods with existing methods in terms of speed, accuracy and robustness. Moreover, we will derive comprehensive complexity and convergence rate analysis of second-order numerical methods that include smoothing trust region Newton methods. In contrast with the comprehensive complexity analysis for convex optimization, little theoretical complexity and convergence rate results for nonconvex optimization are known. The established second-order approximation theory, worst-case complexity bounds and convergence rate will be significant to optimization theory and algorithms. Moreover, we will apply second-order methods to important applications in imaging sciences, signal processing, variable selection and transportation engineering. 非光滑優化問題在經濟學和工程學中有許多重要的應用。在過去的幾十年裡，非光滑優化問題的一階數值方法得到了很好的發展。近年來，隨著計算機硬件與軟件的飛速發展，二階數值方法引起了人們的廣泛關注。例如，對於非光滑凸L1正則化問題，學者們開發了並行計算環境下的半光滑牛頓方法。眾所周知，在數值求解光滑優化問題中，相比於一階方法，二階方法具有諸多優勢，它不僅在收斂速度上更快，而且可以收斂到滿足更強優化條件的二階穩定點。牛頓方法就是一個典型的求解光滑優化問題的二階數值方法，它利用目標函數的梯度與Hessian陣精確地構造了目標函數的二次逼近。然而，對於求解非光滑非凸優化問題二階穩定點的二階數值方法，人們卻鮮有研究。因為非光滑函數的梯度和Hessian陣並不存在，牛頓方法不能直接用來求解非光滑優化問題。本項目旨在發展二階數值方法，以求解一類出現在各種重要實際應用中的非光滑複合優化問題。特別地，即使當優化問題是非Lipschitz非凸時，我們提出的方法仍可找到可測量的二階穩定點。我們將建立新的概念和理論來構造二階逼近。具體而言，就是利用複合函數特殊結構的光滑逼近與子空間逼近。我們還會從收斂速度、精度和魯棒性等方面將光滑牛頓方法和一些現有的方法作比較。而且，我們將給出包括光滑信賴域牛頓方法在內的二階數值方法的綜合複雜度和收斂速度分析。與目前對凸優化問題較全面的複雜度分析研究相比，對非凸優化問題的複雜度和收斂速率的理論研究成果卻極為少見。而對優化理論和算法而言，本項目預建立的二階逼近理論、最壞情況下的複雜度分析和收斂速率是十分重要的。此外，我們還將把所建立的二階方法應用到圖像科學、信號處理、變量選擇和交通運輸工程等重要的應用領域中去。

500413.value: 合成高品質石墨烯的化學氣相沉積生長機制的理論探索

500413.label: Co - Investigator(s)
500413.value: Prof Liu, Zhongfan Prof Yakobson, Boris I.

500413.label: Project Objectives
500413.value: An in-depth understanding on the graphene nucleation on various transition metal surfaces. Achieving this objective would reveal the role of the catalysts on the nucleation of graphene, especially the differences among hem and the advantages of each. With this understanding, we will learn how to avoid the simultaneous nucleation of high density graphene islands on metal surfaces, which is crucial for growing large area graphene with large single crystalline domains. A comprehensive understanding of defect healing during graphene CVD growth. This study will leads to a deep understanding on the mechanisms of graphene defect healing. Based on it, potential means of minimizing defect concentrations in synthesized graphene can be designed. Ascertaining the optimum conditions and techniques for synthesizing large area graphene with large domain size. Based on the gained knowledge in the study of #1 and #2, potential methods including seeded graphene growth, proper design of catalyst and controlling experimental parameters will be analyzed to explore the optimum condition for synthesizing high quality, large area graphene.

500413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
500413.value: 因為其奇特的性質和巨大的潛在應用價值，單層石墨烯的研究目前激起了科研界極大的關注。在所有已知的合成石墨烯的方法中，化學氣相沉積(CVD)法在合成均勻大尺寸高質量石墨烯方面有著巨大的優勢。儘管該方法在實驗上取得了巨大成功，但是隱藏在其背後的生長機制，尤其是催化劑在CVD合成過程中的所起的作用以及各種催化劑之間的差異（如: 釕, 銠， 鈀，鉑， 銥，鈷，鎳，銅等）還沒有深刻的理解。因此我們提出在從理論角度研究催化劑在石墨烯中CVD生長過程中的作用。我們主要研究對石墨烯的結構控制起關鍵作用的兩個過程：1) 石墨烯的成核過程和2) 石墨烯生長時缺陷的修復過程。我們將採用第一性原理計算研究這兩個過程，從而揭示不同催化劑之間的差異。這一研究的成功將會讓我們對石墨烯的CVD生長機制有更加深入的認識，同時也為我們以後能夠通過催化劑設計來合成均勻大尺寸高質量的石墨烯鋪平道路。

500413.label: Realisation of objectives
500413.value: With the GRF support, we have carried extensive study on the mechanism of graphene CVD growth, especially on transition metal surfaces. All the three objects are realized with great satisfactory. The results were published in leading journals. In detail: Objective #1-- An in-depth understanding on the graphene nucleation on various transition metal surfaces, was achieved by a serious density functional theory (DFT) calculations. In these studies, we systematically explored the stability of carbon clusters on various metal surfaces and nucleation barrier of graphene on different metal surfaces are calculated. Corresponding publications are: • The Structure and Stability of Magic Carbon Clusters Observed in Graphene Chemical Vapor Deposition Growth on Ru(0001) and Rh(111) Surfaces; ANGEWANDTE CHEMIE-INTERNATIONAL EDITION, 53, 14031-14035, 2014 • Formation of carbyne and graphyne on transition metal surfaces, NANOSCALE, 6, 12727-12731, 2014 Objective #2-- A comprehensive understanding of defect healing during graphene CVD growth, was partly achieved by the studies for realizing object #1, in which, we have found that topological defects, such as pentagons and heptagons, can be easily formed during the nucleation stage of graphene. Later systematic study showed that point defects, such as single or double vacancies, may also be formed during the graphene CVD growth and normally one metal atom will be embedded into a defective site. The mechanism of defect healing also been explored and our study showed that slower growth at a high temperature favors the growth of high quality graphene and properly choose catalyst is also important: Publications regarding to this objective includes: • The formation mechanism of multiple vacancies and amorphous graphene under electron irradiation, NANOSCALE, 7, 8315-8320, 2015 • The edge termination controlled kinetics in graphene chemical vapor deposition growth, CHEMICAL SCIENCE, 5, 4639-4645, 2014 • Atomistic simulation and the mechanism of graphene amorphization under electron irradiation. Nanoscale, 2014, 6, 2082. • Hydrogenation of bilayer graphene: A small twist makes a big difference, Nano Res. 2015, 8(12): 3887–3897. • Isomerization of sp2-hybridizedcarbon nanomaterials: structural transformation and topological defects of fullerene, carbon nanotube, and graphene, WIREs Comput Mol Sci 2017, 7:e1283. Objective #3-- Ascertaining the optimum conditions and techniques for synthesizing large area graphene with large domain size, was achieved by considering the mechanism of graphene nucleation, lateral expansion and defect healing procedures. It was found that Cu-Ni alloy and Pt are among the best catalysts for graphene CVD growth because of their proper chemical activities and the relatively weak interaction between graphene and the substrate. By collaborating with our experimental collaborators, we have realized the growth of inched sized graphene in a few hours and the ultrafast growth of graphene on Cu surface with the assistance of the oxygen. The publications regarding this object include: • What are the active carbon species during graphene chemical vapor deposition growth? NANOSCALE, 7 627-1634, 2015 • Evolution of domains and grain boundaries in graphene: a kinetic Monte Carlo simulation. Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 2016,18, 2932-2939. • Formation mechanism of overlapping grain boundaries in graphene chemical vapor deposition growth, Chem. Sci., DOI: 10.1039/C6SC04535A

500413.label: Major findings and research outcome
500413.value: #1. We have found that the seeded growth is a proper method for high quality large domain graphene growth because the nucleation can be avoided; #2. We propose that the Cu-Ni alloy can be used to achieve fast growth of graphene and the nozzle injection technique can be used to realize the very large area single crystal domain growth. #3. We have systematically explored the mechanism of graphene nucleation and growth via DFT calculations and MD simulations. This serious of researches lay a milestone on the CVD synthesis of graphene. #4. Via collaborations with our experimental groups, we have realized the ultra-fast growth of graphene and a few word records (the largest single graphene domain of 1.5 inch and the fastest graphene growth rate of 60 microns per second) were set.

500413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
500413.value: In the future, to extend the study and the knowledge obtained in graphene CVD growth to other 2D materials shall be very important topic to do and is easy for us to take. Another important work is to carry some experimental researches on graphene and 2D materials growth under the instruction of our theory. We have done a lot of collaborative researches with experimental groups while the experimental procedures were not controlled by us and therefore our proposed studies were not properly considered in their studies. So, to build our own experimental team is crucially important and we are looking forward for better support on them.

500413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
500413.value: The success of the project and the collaborative researches taken during the period enable human to have the largest single crystal graghene in inch size. Such a result is very important for us to realize the industrial scaled graphene application and to change our future lives greatly.

500513.label: Project Title(Chinese)
500513.value: 通過應變媒介耦合的磁致發光

500513.label: Project Objectives
500513.value: To design and synthesize hybrid material system consisting of magnetostrictive and luminescent materials. We will investigate structural properties of the system. To observe a novel phenomenon of magnetic-field induced luminescence (MIL). We will demonstrate that light-emission of the system can be modulated by low magnetic-field at room temperature. To investigate the effects of structural properties and applied magnetic-field on the luminescent characteristics. We will combine experimental observation and theoretical study to understand the mechanism of strain-mediated MIL coupling.

To investigate the effects of structural properties and applied magnetic-field on the luminescent characteristics. We will combine experimental observation and theoretical study to understand the mechanism of strain-mediated MIL coupling.

500513.label: Realisation of objectives
500513.value: 1.In order to achieve the project objective 1, a novel strategy of three-way coupling among magnetic-field, strain, and luminescence is proposed. So far, magneto-luminescence coupling may not arise directly between the two parameters in single phase material system under low magnetic-field at room temperature. In order to overcome the obstacle, we have employed a practical approach, namely strain-mediated indirect magneto-luminescent coupling in two phases where the magnetic and photon parameters arise in separate but intimately connected phases. According to the strategy, we have designed and synthesized various hybrid materials consisting of magnetic phase and luminescent materials. In particular, ZnS:Al,Cu/ZnS:Al,Cu,Mn microparticles were uniformly mixed in polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). The magnetic responsive phase consists of magnetic Fe-Co-Ni alloy particles embedded in PDMS. Finally, multiphase composites with magnetic actuator and mechanoluminescence phosphor are prepared. In order to produce efficient magnetic response, this kind of the magneto-active elastomer with composite structure has carefully been designed so as to exhibit a compromise between flexibility and magnetic permeability. The amount of deformation generated depends on the size and concentration of the magnetic particles incorporated into matrix. The design of the three components of polymer, magnetic particle and phosphor is optimized to reach a compromise between elastic module, magnetic permeability, luminescence and other requirements in the hybrid structure. Furthermore, the structure and morphology of the hybrid systems are studied using a scanning electron microscope, which shows the multiphase rods consisted of the composite of metal ion-doped ZnS microparticles with the average size of 23 μm and another composite of magnetic Fe-Co-Ni alloy particles with the average size of 100 μm mixed to PDMS. After the success of making the system, the tunable white MIL composite was further fabricated via homogenous mixing YAG:Ce phosphor with ZnS:Al, Cu piezophosphor. The (SrS, CaS):Eu phosphor paste onto the top of a ZnS:Cu-based MIL composite. This green MIL composite consisted of 16 composite rods, each with a diameter of 1 mm and a depth of 5 mm. For the element of individual multicolor volumetric MIL composite, the red phosphor paste was coated onto ZnS:Cu-based MIL composite element rod. 2.To achieve the objective 2, according to our past expertise to test the feasibility in two kinds of strain-based light-emitting devices, we found that the fabricated composite phosphors and the hybrid devices are capable of responding to different types of external stimuli (uniaxial strains of stretch, mechanical writing and piezoelectric biaxial strain, etc.), resulting in the observed white and green light emissions by the naked eyes. The stimulus excitation, resultant luminescence spectra and their relations with color properties (color coordinates, color temperature, etc.) of the white light emission have been investigated. The PI has given invited talk to report the works in an International Conference held in USA. Some results are published online in Nano Energy. With the research results, we moved forward to test luminescence of the hybrid material system triggered by magnetic field. For this goal, we have set up a system of measuring magnetic-field induced luminescence (MIL). Briefly, time-varying magnetic fields are provided by rotating NdFeB permanent magnet with a controller. The strength and frequency of magnetic field can be readily modulated through adjusting the magnet-sample distance and rotation speed of a controller. When the alternating magnetic field acts on the sample, the transient strain produced in magnetic phase can deliver to the phosphor phase and subsequently generate light recorded by optical fiber spectrometer. Finally, we successfully observed an unexplored phenomenon, namely MIL via strain-mediated coupling. Interestingly, the unusual light emissions of the material systems can be modulated in reversible and dynamical manners under the control of time-varying magnetic field as low as Hrms~ 3.5 kOe at room temperature. After the success of observing results, we have moved forwarded to achieve temporal tuning luminescence by high-frequency magnetic field. To achieve high-frequency modulation of magnetic field, a homemade apparatus was used to generate the sinusoidal magnetic field at room temperature. A pulse width modulator was used to modulate the frequency of the magnetic field. In detail, an electric motor rotates a magnet with the rotation speed controlled by a pulse width modulation module. The magnet has a strong magnetic field along its radical axis, and it is rotated around the longitudinal axis of the magnet. The applied magnetic-field strength on the composite is controlled via changing the distance between the MIL composite and the magnet. The green to blue color displayed was tuned by controlling the modulation frequency of the magnetic field. The magnetic field was set in the range of 2.5–3.5 kOe, depending on the intensity of emission required. Finally, we firstly observed tuning emission peak wavelength and color of ZnS: Al, Cu phosphors by modulating the frequency of the magnetic-field excitation. 3.To achieve the objective 3, MIL luminescent spectra are characterized in different structural systems, such as single blue, green and red-green-blue (RGB) and tunable White MIL Composites. We found that the MIL intensity increases linearly when increasing the square of magnetic field Hrms. The observed phenomena also accord with the result where the magnitude of strain is enhanced with an increase in the strength of magnetic field. Hence, more charge carriers are detrapped when increasing the magnitude and change rate of magnetic field, resulting in the enhancement of e-h recombination and MIL. In our published papers in Chem. Soc. Rev. and Adv. Opt. Mater., we have summarized the physical mechanism related the interaction between magnetic field and luminescent materials. Based on the fundamental knowledge, a preliminary MIL theoretical model was proposed to explain the observed the MIL phenomena, which can seen in Adv. Mater. (2015, 2017). Furthermore, the mechanistic investigation suggests that the observed tunable piezophotonic emission is ascribed to the tilting band structure of the ZnS phosphor induced by magnetostrictive strain under a high frequency of magnetic-field excitation. 4.In summary, we have fully realized the three objectives of the project. Particularly, 9 high-quality papers are published with acknowledgements of this project. Among them, 8 papers are published in the journals with impact factor >10, including 3 Adv Mater., 1 Chem Soc. Rev., 1 Adv. Funct. Mater., and 3 Nano Energy. One postgraduate student has been under training during this period. The student Wong Man-chung has published high-impact journal papers, including two papers in high-impact journals Adv. Mater. (IF~19) as the first author. The PI was invited to write review articles because of our research impact in this field. To disseminate our results, the PI has given invited talks in several recognized international conferences held in USA, Italy, Japan and Korea. Our works have attracted much attention and highlighted by journal covers and many media, including Views by Chief-editor of Nature Photonics and Materials Views.

500513.label: Major findings and research outcome
500513.value: 1. Through this project, we propose the term magnetic-induced luminescence (MIL) and first observe MIL phenomenon in flexible composite laminates via strain-mediated coupling. The implementations of the new concept are based on the design and fabrication of MIL composite laminates that consist of metal-ion-doped ZnS + PDMS and Fe–Ni–Co alloy + PDMS. Novel MIL phenomenon has been observed from the phosphor composites via strain-mediated coupling. Interestingly, the unusual light emissions of the material systems can be modulated in reversible and dynamical manners under the control of time-varying magnetic field as low as H rms ≈ 3.5 kOe at room temperature. (see: Part C: Journal 4,7, Conference: 3,4,6). 2. The linear relationship of MIL intensity versus f and the square of Hrms. should benefi t to developing novel MIL-based magnetic sensors when considering that good linear relationship between the output and input signals is preferred in practical application. In contrast to conventional magnetic sensors, we found that the MIL-based and magnetic nanogenerator driven ligh-emissions enjoy competitive advantages. (see: Part C: Journal 3,4,5,6, Conference: 5,6). 3. A convenient physical approach of temporal and remote tuning of light-emitting wavelength and color is demonstrated, which is greatly different from conventional methods. We found that by modulating the frequency of magnetic-field excitation at room temperature, luminescence from the flexible composite can be tuned in real time and in situ. Furthermore, some proof-of concept devices, including red–green–blue full-color displays and tunable white-light sources are demonstrated simply by frequency modulation. (see: Part C: Journal 9). 4. The above physical method could be extended to become a general strategy of tuning luminescence beyond chemical method. A new understanding of the fundamentals of both luminescence and magnetic–optics coupling is thus provided, while offering opportunities in magnetic–optical sensing, piezophotonics, mechanical energy harvesting, novel light sources, and displays. (see: Part C: Journal 1,2,3,7, Conference: 1,2). 5. We have established MIL theoretical models. In the related modeling and calculations, the total luminescence intensity of MIL is found to be related to several coupling parameters and square of magnetic field. The mechanistic investigation suggests that the observed tunable piezophotonic emission is ascribed to the tilting band structure of the ZnS phosphor induced by magnetostrictive strain under a high frequency of magnetic-field excitation. (see: Part C: Journal 4,9, Conference: 5,6).

500513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
500513.value: Since our work supported by the GRF project represents the first example of MIL materials and devices, there has been no existing data of the device's figure of merits for comparison. By analogy with EL, we define the MIL efficiency of the new type of device driven by magnetic field as η ≈ light emission output/magnetic field input strength. Up to now, the efficiency of MIL is relatively low, which is much poorer than conventional electroluminescent devices such as LED. It is much needed to improve the efficiency of MIL devices. Although some proof-of concept devices, including red–green–blue full-color displays and tunable white-light sources are demonstrated in our works, there is room to improve the tunable range and color temperature of MIL composite. Accordingly, the magnetic field and optical characterization systems should be improved and standardized in the future. In numerical modeling and calculation, more parameters of configurations, vibration characteristics, magnetic-field variations could be considered. More types of hybrid structures could be studied. More applications of the MIL based devices could be explored to show some advantages of real-time visualization of optical imaging, remote sensing without making electric contact, nondestructive and noninvasive detection.

500513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
500513.value: Luminescence is the light-emission by a substance that is supplied with some form of energy. However, the longstanding problem limits our understanding of the relationship between magnetic field and luminescence, hindering potential applications of both magnetic and luminescent materials. In this project, we propose a practical approach to design and synthesize flexible polymer composites composed of a magnetic actuator and phosphor. Magnetic-induced luminescence (MIL) is firstly shown via strain-mediated coupling, which can be modulated under a time-varying low magnetic field at room temperature. A magnetically driven light-emission pattern and a white-light source are demonstrated. Furthermore, a novel method is developed to tune light-emitting wavelengths and color by modulating the frequency of the magnetic-field excitation. The MIL intensity and wavelength can be modulated by the magnitude and excitation frequency of magnetic stimuli in a reversible and dynamical manner. Physical mechanisms responsible for the novel observations are investigated. The study provides a new insight and understanding on the piezophotonic emission mechanism. Our new finding of the luminescent materials with ability to be accessed and modulated remotely will offer opportunities for applications in the fields of magnetic optical sensing, piezophotonics, energy harvester, nondestructive environmental surveillance, novel light sources, and displays.

500613.label: Project Objectives
500613.value: To introduce the dynamic optimization of LSC system in new ''dynamic uncertainty" setting. Specially, to formulate the linear quadratic problem with volatility uncertainty (LQV) and linear quadratic problem with drift uncertainty (LQD). To develop the variational analysis, decentralized control and consistency synthesis of LQV problem in this new setting. Based on our analysis of LQV in 2., to develop the corresponding analysis of LQD which has more complicated features than LQV.

To develop the variational analysis, decentralized control and consistency synthesis of LQV problem in this new setting.
Based on our analysis of LQV in 2., to develop the corresponding analysis of LQD which has more complicated features than LQV.

500613.label: Realisation of objectives
500613.value: Dear Reviewer: Within this project period, we complete the above research objectives, and details are reported as follows. 1. We first discuss the volatility uncertainty for the large-scale complex (LSC) system. Here, we focus on the important and practical linear-quadratic (LQ) setup (actually, this is the setup proposed in our grant research proposal): the state is linear and cost functional is quadratic. Also, our research outcomes in LQ setup, provides the ``break-through" basis for further extension to nonlinear setup. As the motivation point, we first specify various real motivations of volatility uncertainty in theoretical and practical aspects. The volatility uncertainty is formulated by some $L^{2}$ integrable process (deterministic, stochastic) with integral quadratic constraint. We also discuss the related constraint scale in real examples. One real example is the uncertainty in multiplicative-noise in randomness. To this, we also discuss its connection to the financial application: for example, the quadratic hedging or portfolio selection with risk measure uncertainty, in the presence of comparative relative performance with various competitive investors in given section. In addition, parallel research attentions are posed on their counterparts of LQ drift uncertainty setting (i.e., LQD in our proposal), as our research activity complementary to LQV. We also discuss its real motivation and applications: one example is addressed in the context of unknown additive noise, and more concrete connection is linked to relative mean-variance portfolio selection but with unknown return rate (or, interest rate). Moreover, to simplify the analysis, we focus on a class of deterministic drift disturbance with quadratic constraint in continuous-time linear LSC framework. This class of disturbance has connection to financial or engineering applications. We address them in one of our research output (see J. Huang and M. Huang (2017). Robust mean field LQG games with unknown $L^2$-disturbance. SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization, 55, 2811-2840). 2. Given formulation 1, the LQV is first analyzed by robust optimization approach for hard constraint via variational analysis thus in principle, the related open-loop solution is derived. As a result, the original robust optimization is decomposed into two sequential dynamic optimization problems. As a result, some mini-max optimization problems in its finite population case, and infinite population limiting case are respectively introduced. Specially, for the inner sup-optimization problem, the related Lagrange multiplier treatment is introduced to handle this quadratic constraint but in mean-field game setup. Moreover, the decentralized (open-loop) strategy for individual agent are derived in terms of a class of symmetric forward-backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs) with undetermined mean-field limit. Based on it, the consistency condition is represented in terms of a class of non-symmetric FBSDEs where the non-symmetricity is captured by the mean-field coupling. The state aggregation technique is utilized here to derive the related consistency condition for volatility uncertainty. The well-posedness of consistency synthesis system of LQV is further investigated with indefinite cost weighting coefficients. This is very different to the standard setup in which all cost weights are positive thus the well-posedness of FBSDE is a direct consequence. We consider and compare two different methods: one is reduction method for linear FBSDEs, and the other is bridge method which can be applied to more general nonlinear FBSDE. Based on our study of volatility uncertainty with hard constraint, in this project, we also discuss the possible analysis in terms of volatility constraint which is not absolute continuous to underlying probability measure. To this end, we formulate in the $G$-expectation setup which includes various important uncertainty singular to underlying probability measure. We discuss the related closed-loop strategy and consistency-condition in terms of a new class of Riccati equation. Such Riccati equation, with general nonlinear kernel G(P), is very different to the standard Riccati equation with the standard heat-kernel representation G(P)=sigma P sigma. Along this research line, we investigate some basic cases in which our general Riccati equation admits unique solution. Our research outcome can be applied to the LSC with G-volatility uncertainty and related mean-field game analysis. In addition , some non-symmetric Riccati equation should be introduced as a sequence. We have some working paper in progress along this research direction, and plan to investigate more details in recent future. 3. Based on 2 of LQV, we continue to investigate the related LSC system with drift uncertainties in linear-quadratic setup (i.e., LQD in proposal). Here, we focus on a detailed modeling and analysis with (deterministic) drift uncertainties, in terms of integral quadratic constraint. We discuss both the Lagrange multiplier method which is very effective for hard constraint, and penalty optimization method, which is more effective for soft constraint. In former Lagrange approach, the drift uncertainty is tackled from a robust optimization viewpoint where each individual agent takes the unknown function as an adversarial player and some game-based framework is thus introduced. The related dynamics of state-average in its infinite-population limiting case is well analyzed and examined. To this end, some perturbation analysis is introduced to explore the related sensitivity behavior. Similarly, the associated consistency synthesis of LQD is also discussed in general forward-backward SDE context, and give more insights to the related decoupling (closed-loop through the Riccati equation) in mean-field setting. As a response to application proposal, the variational analysis and related duality relation are discussed which can be generalized to more general random coefficients case. Some relaxed consistency condition notation is also proposed which is more feasible to analyze the fixe-point analysis in related mean-field game (MFG). Moreover, some decoupling results are given in this mean-field FBSDE setting, and the determination of related Lagrange multiplier constant is connect to the minimization problem of optimal cost functional and semi-definite programming. As for the latter penalty approach, the model uncertainty is formulated into a robust optimization with game-base, and the soft-constraint for the drift disturbance is also introduced. To this end, the cost functional is revised by adding some new term of penalty, and the minimization problem becomes non-standard intrinsically. By incorporating the temporal evolution of the mean-field limit in an augmented state space, we study two optimal control problems in some sequential way. The robust optimization procedure is thus further combined with a consistency condition for the mean field approximation. In addition, its dependence on the initial condition is also examined and some asymptotic estimates are hence given in this situation. More importantly, due to the presence of penalty term in cost functional, the convexity property of our inner sup-optimization problem is not obvious and we propose some auxiliary dynamic problem to give the feasible criteria to test such convexity. We propose two conditions to such convexity: one is functional representation which is very concise but rather abstract. Its direct estimates should lead to some sufficient conditions for convexity; another is the introduction of some auxiliary reduced controlled problem and with :it, the convexity can be further linked to the wellposedness of given Riccati equation. Based on them, we obtain some trackable and checkable condition for positive-definite property of related quadratic functional. We also discuss the related Riccati equation system and Two-point boundary problem. As a result, we obtain decentralized strategies and verify its epsilon-Nash equilibrium properties. The related research outcomes are reported in recent publication: J. Huang and M. Huang (2017). Robust mean field LQG games with unknown $L^2$-disturbance. SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization.

500613.label: Major findings and research outcome
500613.value: According to objective 1,2,3, we have the following major findings and related research outcomes, as listed below: (i) We get the formulation of volatility and drift uncertainty, and we find that they are closed related to the robust control with multiplicative noise and additive noise respectively. Also, we found that they have clear financial and engineering applications in these uncertainty setting. (ii) We discuss the LQV, LQD in hard and soft constraint. We find the related mini-max optimization, and robust sequential optimization all relate to non-symmetric FBSDE or Riccati equation. The related decentralized strategy can also be represented by such non-symmetric system. (iii) The well-posedness of above non-symmetric FBSDE or Riccati system is intrinsically not standard, and their analysis is more suitable to be conducted by the reduction method, which is more appropriate for linear system, as in case here. (iv) Our research outcomes include various theoretical results which are reported in our publications (to be listed below) and some working paper still in progress. More detailed results will be included in these working papers and we anticipated they will be submitted soon. They will enrich our existing publication record based on this project. (v) Based on objective 1,2,3, we further make some research by-products in the following directions: one is the mean-field games (MFGs) of large-scale complex system with partial information, related research outcome is reported in the publication: Dynamic optimization of large-population systems with partial information. Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications (JOTA), 168, 231-245. Another direction is large-scale complex integral system, and related mean-field game. Its relevant research outcome is reported in the publication: J. Huang, X. Li and T. Wang (2016). Mean field linear-quadratic-Gaussian (LQG) games for stochastic integral systems. IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control, 61. 2670-2675. The third one is more specific: the controlled large-scale complex system with stochastic delayed feature. Its relevant research outcome is reported in the publication: J. Huang, N. Li (2018). Mean field games with stochastic delayed system. IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control (TAC). DOI 10.1109/TAC.2018.2798807. All three directions apply some theoretical results from our project with LQV, or LQD implicitly. For example, the well-posedness of non-symmetric linear FBSDE and Riccati equation are very important in the derivation of partial information, as stated in the first direction above. In addition, all three directions can be found important application importance in reality.

500613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
500613.value: Our research outcome provides some starting point for further extensions: for example, our current LQ outcomes can be extended to more general nonlinear LSC setting. In addition, our theoretical results give the further developments in potential practical applications, such as the related performance mean-variance decision but with return rate or risk uncertainties. Moreover, our LQV can be formulated in the singular uncertainty measure setting. This will lead to mean-field game in G-expectation framework. We conduct some preliminary investigation along this research line.

500613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
500613.value: Large complex system (LSC) and its related dynamic optimization problems are very important in theoretical and application aspects. However, in reality, various LSC models are of drift or volatility uncertainties, and such uncertainties can be formulated in either hard or soft constraints. This project formulated these uncertainties and constraints systematically. We also discuss how to design the related decentralized in such uncertainty and constraint setting.
