500913.label: Project Objectives
500913.value: Combined fs-KTRF/TA and ns-TRE/TA experiments will be done on selected mono-/di-nuclear gold(I) complexes that contain non-coordinating counterions in inert solvent or solid state to determine spectra and dynamics signatures for intrinsic excited-states and associated emission pathways as well as to examine influence of auxiliary ligand and phase condition on the dynamics and emission. Integrated fs-KTRF/TA and ns-TRE/TA studies will be performed on complexes that contain “coordinating counterions” in inert solvent to determine dynamics and spectra signatures for transient species and pathways induced by gold(I)-counterion complexation. The results will render the first direct characterisation of such species and will enable to evaluate the particular part played by counterion in the radiative and non-radiative decay of excited state systems. Parallel fs-KTRF/TA and ns-TRE/TA work will be done on selected complexes in coordinating solvent to determine how gold(I) binding to solvent may affect the nature, dynamics and emission paths of the chosen systems. These studies will provide crucial evidence for deciphering among the various competing channels the solvent specific path(s) in the excited-state decay. The results will afford direct spectra and dynamics description of the transient adduct(s) formed by gold(I)-solvent interaction. Combining the results of objectives(1)-(3) will allow construction of a comprehensive and detailed picture for emission pathways of selected gold(I) complexes; it will lead to identification of key factors that affect excited-state evolution and luminescence properties of the chosen and related complexes. The result to be produced in this project will fill in the void and advance dramatically our understanding of the photophysics and photochemistry of polynuclear gold(I) complexes. To identify and to be able to resolve in real time and at molecular level of the dynamics origin of the environmental sensitive photoluminescence and substrate-bonding interaction of these complexes constitutes a unique and unprecedented perspective of this project. Apart from the contribution to fundamental knowledge in the basic science perspective, the outcomes from this project will be beneficial to rational design and related applications. In particular, the results on the solvent and counterion specific dynamics, spectrum, emission pathways and substrate-binding reactivity may inspire development of new strategies and operation principles for (poly-nuclear) gold(I) based luminescence sensor, OLED devices and photocatalyst.

500913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
500913.value: Besides its well-known historical monetary value and widespread symbolic functions, gold, when incorporated in coordination complex, displays fascinating physical properties and rich chemistry. Gold containing complexes have attracted enormous attention in the past several decades for both the practical uses and academic interests. Among the wide variety of gold complexes, a group of poly-nuclear gold(I) complexes with bridging phosphine ligands are of particular importance because of their unique structure features and remarkable photoluminescence properties. Upon photo-excitation, these complexes display emissions that are strongly sensitive to the subtle variation in both the ligand systems and the environmental properties. As a result, they have found potential applications in a range of fields including the molecular materials of optical sensors, light emitting diodes (LEDs) and photocatalysis. However, the underlying cause of this ligand- and environment-sensitive emission has remained a challenging issue in the gold photophysics and photochemistry. The intriguing emission behaviour of these complexes has long been connected to the enhanced aurophillic interaction induced by photo-excitation but was recently considered relevant also to the inherent substrate-binding proclivity of the coordinatively unsaturated two coordinate gold(I) centre(s). Nonetheless, due to the lack of explicit evidence, little is known for certain about the precise origin of the emission. To fill in this important but largely unexplored area, herein we propose to utilise our cutting-edge femtosecond time-resolved spectroscopic techniques to perform a systematic and in-depth study on a series of prototype di- and tri-nuclear gold(I) phosphine complexes. Our integrated application of femtosecond broadband time-resolved fluorescence, transient absorption and picosecond time-resolved resonance Raman spectroscopy provide an ideal method for revealing the spectral signatures and structural fingerprints for the involved transient species and the associated dynamic transformation(s). The proposed research will enable the first direct probe of the excited state dynamics; it will allow for unraveling the excited state cascades and identifying the elementary steps responsible for the luminescence of the selected systems. The results of these studies will provide a full and explicit interpretation of, at the molecular level, the emission mechanism and render identification of governing factor(s) for the luminescence spectra of the chosen and related systems. This project is of fundamental interest from a basic science perspective, and has significant implications for many potential practical applications based on the gold(I) and poly-nuclear gold(I) complexes. 金, 除了有貨幣價值和象徵貴重的功用，它的配合物也表現出有趣的物理性質和豐富的化學變化。在過去的數十年，金配合物在應用和基礎研究方面都引起了極大的關注。多核金(I)膦橋配合物在各種金配合物中佔有特別重要的位置，它擁有獨特的結構及光致發光特性。這類金(I)配合物的發光性質隨著配體及環境的改變而顯著變化。這使得此類配合物在光學傳感器、發光二極管及光催化分子材料等領域有重要的應用潛質。然而，配體和環境如何影響這類金(I)配合物的發光特性，卻是金配合物光物理及光化學領域中一個極具有挑戰性的課題。金(I)膦橋配合物的奇妙發光特性，在早期的工作中被歸結為由光激發而導致增強的金-金相互作用而引起，但最近的研究顯示這種現象可能與金(I)擁有不飽和配位有關。不過，由於缺乏明確的證據，目前對這類金(I)配合物發光特性的確切原因所知不多。為此，我們建議利用尖端的飛秒時間分辨光譜技術，對一系列雙核及三核金(I)膦配合物進行深入並有系統的研究。我們的寬帶飛秒時間分辨熒光、瞬態吸收和皮秒時間分辨共振拉曼光譜技術，為揭示瞬態物種的結構、光譜特徵及動力學性質提供了理想的實驗方法。本項目所建議的研究，將是首次直接探測金(I)膦橋配合物的激發態動力學; 以揭示激發態的能量轉變及發光機制。本項目的研究結果，將為在分子水平闡明影響金(I)配合物的發光特性提供完整而明確的實驗證據。這對於拓展雙核及多核金(I)配合物的基礎研究與實際應用將具有深遠的影響。

Integrated fs-KTRF/TA and ns-TRE/TA studies will be performed on complexes that contain “coordinating counterions” in inert solvent to determine dynamics and spectra signatures for transient species and pathways induced by gold(I)-counterion complexation. The results will render the first direct characterisation of such species and will enable to evaluate the particular part played by counterion in the radiative and non-radiative decay of excited state systems.

Parallel fs-KTRF/TA and ns-TRE/TA work will be done on selected complexes in coordinating solvent to determine how gold(I) binding to solvent may affect the nature, dynamics and emission paths of the chosen systems. These studies will provide crucial evidence for deciphering among the various competing channels the solvent specific path(s) in the excited-state decay. The results will afford direct spectra and dynamics description of the transient adduct(s) formed by gold(I)-solvent interaction.

Combining the results of objectives(1)-(3) will allow construction of a comprehensive and detailed picture for emission pathways of selected gold(I) complexes; it will lead to identification of key factors that affect excited-state evolution and luminescence properties of the chosen and related complexes.

The result to be produced in this project will fill in the void and advance dramatically our understanding of the photophysics and photochemistry of polynuclear gold(I) complexes. To identify and to be able to resolve in real time and at molecular level of the dynamics origin of the environmental sensitive photoluminescence and substrate-bonding interaction of these complexes constitutes a unique and unprecedented perspective of this project. Apart from the contribution to fundamental knowledge in the basic science perspective, the outcomes from this project will be beneficial to rational design and related applications. In particular, the results on the solvent and counterion specific dynamics, spectrum, emission pathways and substrate-binding reactivity may inspire development of new strategies and operation principles for (poly-nuclear) gold(I) based luminescence sensor, OLED devices and photocatalyst.

500913.label: Major findings and research outcome
500913.value: We have conducted most of the experiments planned in this project. Through these measurements, expected evidences have been obtained for addressing most of the questions posed in the proposal. Our comparative fs-KTRF/TA and ns-TRE/TA study on selected mono-/di-nuclear gold(I) complexes that contain non-coordinating counterions and coordinating counterions in inert solvent and solid state that yielded explicit spectral signatures and dynamics characters for the excited-states involved. The results reveal the first fs time-resolved spectroscopic characterization for excited states of prototype gold(I) complexes and the first direct comparison of excited state dynamics in inert condition (the solid state) versus in the solvents (CH3CN and CH2Cl2) to unravel early time events that are involved in accounting for the intriguing environmental dependent photoluminescence and the varied photochemical behaviour of gold(I) complexes. The 35d*6p state, which is formed, regardless of the environmental condition, with ~0.15 ps time constant through ISC from the initially excited 15d*6p state, is viable and highly reactive, being at the same time a powerful reagent for photochemical reactions and with astonishingly strong propensity toward increasing coordination number at the gold(I) centres. These findings provide benchmark example for understanding the photophysics and photochemistry of mono-/di-/multi-nuclear gold(I) complexes.

500913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
500913.value: Based on the outcome of this project, further research will be attempted to perform more combined fs-TRF and fs-TA experiments to directly probe the dynamics and spectra of the excited-states for more selected mono-/di-/multi-nuclear gold(I) complexes.

500913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
500913.value: Following the research plan suggested in the proposal, some selected gold(I) complexes were investigated using femtosecond time-resolved fluorescence, femtosecond transient absorption and nanosecond time-resolved emission spectroscopy. The spectra and dynamics signatures for intrinsic excited-states and associated emission pathways were obtained. The solvent specific path(s) in the excited-state decay were also investigated. The outcomes of this project have led to several publications in top international journals. The research grant enables the PI to participate international conferences to give presentations including invited talk in these conferences. It also allows training of several students, at both the undergraduate and post graduated levels.

501013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
501013.value: Catalytic cross-coupling reaction has emerged as one of the most straightforward and widespread used protocols for scientists to produce amazing chemical modifications for assembling structurally unprecedented, yet materially and pharmaceutically attractive compounds. This methodology has greatly advanced the possibilities for chemists to create sophisticated molecules, in which as complex as those created by nature itself. While brilliant researchers have been remarkably adept at coming up with innovative methods for refining specific bond constructions, the establishment of these reactions into a truly general protocol by the application of simple, readily available and highly effective catalyst is still in great demand. In fact, the high diversification of catalyst, which offers excellent tunable ability, is significant to deal with various libraries of lead compound in the drug discovery processes since different molecules usually require particular fine-tuned catalysts for optimization. The improvement of current methodologies and exploration of new technologies for versatile bond construction process are of high fundamental importance. The purpose of this project are (1) to rationally design and explore a new class of simple, yet highly tunable catalyst/ ligands (and their chiral analogs) using a facile cross-assemble approach; (2) to explore new and versatile coupling partners in this type of reaction; (3) to investigate the fundamental mechanism of these new processes; (4) to study the asymmetric atropo-C-C and -C-N bond formation and their potential application in synthesizing chiral natural molecule motifs. This project is expected to explore a new field in cross-coupling reactions. The proposed study is based on our previous success in the ligand/catalyst design and synthesis, and our extensive experiences in cross-coupling and catalytic asymmetric reactions. These new areas will offer us an excellent opportunity in making a substantial advancement to the frontier of catalysis research and may help us to establish a foundation for fine-chemical industry in Hong Kong. 催化交叉偶聯反應已成為科學家化學修飾組裝結構上前所未有的，重大藥學吸引力的化合物最直接，最廣泛使用的協議之一。這種方法極大地推進創建複雜的分子化學家的可能性，那些自然界本身一樣複雜。雖然輝煌的研究者已經非常善於與創新方法提煉特定債券結構的這些反應，建立成一個真正的通用協議由簡單，隨手可及高效催化劑的應用需求仍然很大。事實上，多元化的催化劑，它提供了優良的可調諧能力，是顯著的先導化合物在藥物發現過程中的各種庫來處理，因為不同的分子通常需要特別的優化微調的催化劑 該項目預計將開拓一個新的領域，在交叉偶聯反應。建議的研究是基於我們以前成功的配體/催化劑的設計與合成，以及我們豐富的經驗，在交叉耦合和不對稱催化反應。這些新的領域會為我們提供了一個極好的機會，作出了重大的進步，催化研究的前沿，可以幫助我們在香港建立精細化工產業奠定了基礎。

501013.label: Realisation of objectives
501013.value: This is the completion report of funding 5010/13P in chemical science category. The proposed investigations of this project focused on the development of new and easily tunable phosphine ligands for under-explored cross-coupling reactions. Moreover, the unexplored/problematic cross-coupling partners, and the fundamental aspect of these issues were planned for study. The success of these proposed studies would provide a ground work for other new chiral ligands to be designed and applied to enantioselective carbon-carbon bond-forming reactions. The exploration of new series of highly tunable ligands/catalysts using a facile cross-assemble approach has been found success. In this study, we found the indolylphosphine ligands are effective to promote the direct C-3 arylation of heterocycles using the inexpensive aryl tosylates and mesylates. This finding was published in the Journal of Organic Chemistry in 2015. [J. Org. Chem. 2015, 80, 1457, one of the most cited paper in 2015, from Thomson Reuter Webofknowledge]. In fact, our success in developing indolylphoshpine ligands was recognized by the invitation to submit a review article in summing up the achievements in this area. This review was published in 2015 [Coord. Chem. Rev. 2015, 293-294, 158]. In this project, we also aim to explore new versatile coupling partners in cross-coupling reactions. Indeed, the direct aromatic C-H bond functionalization is one of the most streamlined method for incorporation of functionality to organic compounds. During the course of study, we found that the direct intermolecular C-H arylation of unactivated arenes using simple catalyst, pyridyl carbinol, was successful. This finding was published in Organic & Biomolecular Chemistry in 2014. [Org. Biomol. Chem. 2014, 12, 6820]. An extension of this work using mixed potassium alkoxide base conditions, was published in Asian Journal of Organic Chemistry in 2014 [Asian J. Org. Chem. 2014, 3, 1262]. In seeking the more inexpensive catalyst system, we develop the iron catalyst system, which allowed the S-arylation to proceed using aryl iodides as the starting materials. [Synlett 2014, 25, 2743]. The fundamental aspect of the aforementioned reactions have also been studied and investigated. In addition to the Pd and Fe complexes, as well as the transition metal-free conditions, we found our new bulky phosphine ligands were applicable to mono-selective Ru-catalyzed directed aromatic ortho-C-H bond arylation using aryl chlorides as the coupling partners. This accomplishment was submitted for publication in 2016, and appeared online in 2017. [Synlett 2017, 28, 499]. With the solid background in previous stages, we synthesized and resolved the new axially chiral phosphine ligands for the enantioselective catalysis. After extensive screening of the ligand efficacy (in terms of product yields and enanatioselectivities), we found that the new ligands were not as effective as some other reported ligands, such as BINAP and SYNPHOS. Thus, we employed SYNPHOS as the chiral diphosphine ligands in the asymmetric carbon-carbon bond-forming reactions. We found the aromatic terminal alkynes were applicable reaction partners toward the Ir-catalyzed asymmetric addition reactions. The product enanatioselectivies obtained from this asymmetric hydroalkynylation were up to 99%ee. This research outcome has been published in Advanced Synthesis and Catalysis [Adv. Synth. Catal. 2015, 357, 2345].

501013.label: Major findings and research outcome
501013.value: In this project, we established new catalyst/ligand systems for aromatic bond-construction processes. The palladium system allow the coupling of heterocycle C-H bond with aryl tosylates and mesylates, in which they are the most inexpensive sulfonyoxy leaving groups of coupling partners for phenolic compounds. Apart from the palladium system, we also developed new Fe and Ru systems for the coupling reactions. Remarkably, during the course of our investigations, we found the conditions of transition metal-free direct C-H arylation reactions. Based on the research finding of monophosphine ligand design and synthesis, we developed new series of axially chiral ligands for asymmetric carbon-carbon bond forming reactions. Although the efficacy was yet to be comparable to the state-of-art ligands such as BINAP and SYNPHOS, the Ir system allowed the product enanatioselectivies up to 99%ee.

501013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
501013.value: The methodological finding of this research project would potentially be useful in targeting unprecedented materials and drug discovery. With the new catalyst in hand, various aromatic bond-construction processes would be realized.

501013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
501013.value: This project is aim to developed new catalyst system for aromatic bond construction processes. With the financial support, we found highly efficient catalyst/ligand for this transformation. Notably, particular substrates could react even under the system of transition metal-free conditions. These findings would contribute to the synthetic sciences of assembling complex natural products, pharmaceutical intermediates and functional aromatic organic materials.

501213.value: A long-term challenge for physicists is the demonstration of quantum behaviors of macroscopic mechanical objects. Advances in solid-state nanotechnologies may provide a solution to this problem. Recently, the development of nanotechnologies has revived interests in the fundamental science of mechanical devices since the dynamics of nanomechanical resonators are expected to be determined by the laws of quantum mechanics in the near future. Nowadays, electromechanical systems at micro- and nanoscale are intensively studied owing to their extremely low threshold forces and high mass sensitivities. Such tiny sensors open the door to the study of processes at the atomic level, e.g., to measure magnetic fields induced by individual nuclear spins, forces between individual molecules, masses of individual atoms, and so on. Advances in nanofabrication techniques have opened up possibilities in the realization of new quantum devices based on nanoelectromechanical systems. Nanomechanical resonators in the form of buckling nanoscale bars with high resonance frequencies and large quality factors have potential applications in high precision measurements, quantum information processing, and controlled generation of exotic macroscopic quantum states. Meanwhile, current fluctuations in mesoscopic electrical systems far from equilibrium provide detailed insights into the nature of charge transfer beyond what is available from conductance measurements alone. Beyond mean current and shot noise, the full counting statistics refers to the probability distribution of the number of electrons transported at a given time and provides complete details of the transport process. With its measurement being realized for single quantum dots in recent experiments, the full counting statistics is also becoming an important experimental tool to examine interactions and coherence effects in nanoscale systems under out-of-equilibrium conditions. In this project, we propose to investigate hybrid quantum systems consisting of nanomechanical resonators and quantum dots. The quantum dynamics of the whole system will be quantitatively studied using quantum master equation and related approaches. We will study the full counting statistics of transport through quantum dots in the presence of nanomechanical resonators. Further extension to the case of weak Coulomb blockade with multiple electrons in the quantum dots will also be explored. The action of the quantum dots as a quantum detector on nanomechanical resonators unavoidably disturbs the system in the form of a backaction. We will evaluate this backaction effect on the quantum behavior of an nanomechanical resonator. Related electromechanical systems serving as single electron shuttles will also be studied. 501213.label: Realisation of objectives
501213.value: The dynamics of quantum systems are often affected by backactions from the environments in the form of bosonic baths. One approach for analyzing such non-Markovian effects is the quantum state diffusion equation method. We have developed a systematic approach based on stochastic differential equations for numerically solving the non-Markovian quantum state diffusion equation for an open quantum system that can be strongly coupled to an environment. As an application, we consider a real-time simulation of a spin-boson model in a strong-coupling regime that is difficult to deal with using conventional methods. We have shown that the non-Markovian stochastic Schrodinger equation can be implemented as a real-time simulation for this model, so as to give an accurate description of spin-boson dynamics beyond the rotating-wave approximation. We have further improved our systematic numerical approach for open quantum systems by developing a closely related hierarchical functional derivative approach. Backactions from the environment are exactly treated. An explicit expression for arbitrary order HFD equation is derived systematically. Moreover, it is found that for an analytically solvable model, this hierarchical equation naturally terminates at a given order and thus becomes exactly solvable. Application to electron transport in quantum dot systems is also investigated. In addition, We have found dynamical invariants for open quantum systems described by the non-Markovian quantum-state-diffusion equation. In stark contrast to closed systems where the dynamical invariant can be identical to the system density operator, these dynamical invariants no longer share the equation of motion for the density operator. Moreover, the invariants obtained with a biorthonormal basis can be used to render an exact solution to the quantum state diffusion equation and the corresponding non-Markovian dynamics without using master equations or numerical simulations. Significantly, we show that we can apply these dynamical invariants to reverse engineering a Hamiltonian that is capable of driving the system to the target state, providing a different way to design control strategy for open quantum systems. We next study the dynamics of a hybrid quantum system consisting of a superconducting flux qubit, a nanomechanical resonator and a coplanar waveguide resonator. The qubit is coupled to the waveguide resonator via their mutual inductance and to the nanomechanical resonator via a Lorentz force induced by an external magnetic field in the plane of the qubit. The degrees of freedom of the qubit can be adiabatically eliminated from the dynamical equations in the dispersive regime and this results at a controllable and strong coupling between the waveguide and the nanomechanical resonator. We deduce a strong and controllable effective coupling between the nanomechanical resonator and the waveguide resonator. Due to the strong coupling, vacuum Rabi splitting can be observed from the voltage-fluctuation spectrum of the waveguide resonator. We have also studied an optomechanical system driven by two-tone fields. We show that in the presence of the cross-Kerr effect, a bistable behavior of the mean photon number in the cavity becomes more robust against the fluctuations of the frequency detuning between the cavity mode and the control field. The bistability can also be turned into a tristability within the experimentally accessible range of the system parameters. Also, we find that the symmetric profile of the optomechanically induced transparency is broken and the zero-absorption point is shifted in the presence of the cross-Kerr effect. This shift can be used to measure the strength of the cross-Kerr effect and the asymmetric absorption profiles can be employed to engineer a high quality factor of the cavity. Related hybrid systems with qubits in the form of quantum dots are further investigated. Properties including voltage-fluctuation spectrum, counting statistics, and electron shuttling behaviors are examined. We have also studied a hybrid system of a quantum dot coupled to a nanowire with electrons in Majorana bound states or simple metallic states. Certain features in the full counting statistics are shown to depend on the presence of the Majorana bound states. In addition, we have studied the robustness of universal holonomic quantum gates against classical noise in its driving fields. Single-qubit and two-qubit gates are considered. We compare the gate fidelity under various noise sources and determine the sweet spots in the driving parameter space.

501213.label: Major findings and research outcome
501213.value: We have developed a systematic approach to study the backactions from the environments in the form of bosonic baths in open quantum systems. It is based on stochastic differential equations for numerically solving the non-Markovian quantum state diffusion equation for an open quantum system that can be strongly coupled to an environment (see publication 1). We have then further developed a closely related hierarchical functional derivative approach for enhanced computational efficiency (see publication 3). We have also studied dynamical invariants for open quantum systems which can assist the exact solution of the non-Markovian quantum state diffusion equations (see publication 4) We have studied the dynamics of a nanomechanical resonator coupled to a superconducting flux qubit and and a coplanar waveguide resonator. Properties of such a hybrid system including a vacuum Rabi splitting in the voltage-fluctuation spectrum and the reflection coefficient of the waveguide resonator are found (see publication 5). We have also studied nonlinear properties of driven optomechanical systems. We have evaluated the impact of the presence of the cross-Kerr effect on the bistable and multi-stable behaviors of the mean photon number in an optical cavity (see publication 6). We have also studied a related hybrid system of a quantum dot coupled to a nanowire with electrons in Majorana bound states or simple metallic states. Features in the full counting statistics are shown to depend on the presence of the Majorana bound states (see publication 2). More generally, we have also studied the robustness of universal holonomic quantum gates in the presence of classical noises in its driving fields (see publication 7).

501213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
501213.value: Quantum information processing is a promising research field. Our experiences attained in the project on the properties of a range of quantum information devices and their behaviors under noisy conditions are valuable. We will further investigate quantum properties of open quantum systems of interest. In particular, detailed non-Markovian dynamics and quantum control of related open systems will be focused on.

501213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
501213.value: Quantum information processing is widely believed to be essential to the next generation of computing and communication devices. Practical quantum devices are inevitably affected by environmental noises, forming open quantum systems. We have developed systematic approaches to numerical study the backactions from the environments in the form of quantized heat baths or photon baths. It is applied to a single qubit, i.e. quantum bit, open system and good numerical efficiency is demonstrated. We have also studied the quantum evolution, transport statistics and quantum control of promising building blocks of quantum computers including nano-mechanical resonators, superconducting flux qubits, waveguide resonator and their hybrid structures. Properties such as voltage fluctuations, non-linear optical responses, information fidelity are investigated under a range of driven conditions. Implementation and reliability of operations including quantum routing, logic gate and information transfer are proposed and studied. Approaches for achieving controllable and strong couplings between components are explored.

501413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
501413.value: For more than a decade, gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) have attracted considerable interest for solution-phase colorimetric deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) detection. Their unique interparticle distance-dependent optical property, with monodispersed particles appear red while aggregated particles appear purple, enables visual readout of the recognition of specific DNA sequence. Two types of AuNPs have been utilized, which are unmodified and oligonucleotide-modified AuNPs. One detection scheme using unmodified AuNPs is based on their preferential binding to single-stranded oligonucleotide recognition probe (complementary to a target sequence) over double-stranded probe–target hybrid, and the probe-bound AuNPs are stabilized against salt-induced aggregation. On the other hand, detection using oligonucleotide-modified AuNPs is commonly based on target-induced cross-linking of two sets of modified particles. Both schemes have sensitivity at nanomolar concentrations, which is not practical for direct target detection. In view of this, efforts have been devoted to their integration with enzymatic DNA amplification. Despite the resulting high sensitivity, there are two main issues that limit their widespread use. The first one is associated with oligonucleotide-modified AuNPs (being utilized in most of the reported amplification-assisted schemes) that their preparation is laborious, time-consuming, and expensive. The second one is the high risk of carryover contamination. This is caused by the fact that the incorporation of AuNPs into an amplification reaction mixture would result in enzyme inhibition, thereby necessitating post-amplification open-tube addition of unmodified or oligonucleotide-modified AuNPs. In this proposed project, our team aims at developing new colorimetric amplification-assisted DNA detection platforms using AuNPs with facile surface modification, featuring low-cost and closed-tube analysis. Two alkanethiol modifications will be employed, including 11-mercaptoundecanoic acid (MUA) and (11-mercaptoundecyl)trimethylammonium (MTA). MUA-modified AuNPs will be incorporated into loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP). Magnesium ions in the reaction mixture lead to particle aggregation due to ion-templated chelation while pyrophosphate ions produced in LAMP, which compete with MUA to bind magnesium ions, lead to particle redispersion. For other isothermal amplification strategies that do not produce significant amounts of pyrophosphate ions, MTA-modified AuNPs will be employed. These positively charged particles form aggregates with negatively charged amplicons through electrostatic attraction. The two new detection platforms enjoy the advantages of simple preparation (AuNPs treated with MUA or MTA) and instrumentation (isothermal amplification and visual detection), as well as worry-free carryover contamination control (closed-tube analysis), which are well suited for point-of-care and on-site applications. In addition, they may potentially rival fluorescence-based techniques for routine analysis, particularly in resource-limited laboratories.

501413.label: Realisation of objectives
501413.value: Objectives 1, 2, 3, 4, and 6 were fully achieved (100%) and Objective 5 was 85% achieved. The realization of each objective is stated below: Objective 1 (100%): The color change mechanisms of the three types of new gold nanoparticle probes were unraveled: (1) 11-mercaptoundecanoic acid-modified gold nanoparticles (MUA-AuNPs); (2) poly(ethylene glycol)- and 11-mercaptoundecanoic acid-comodified gold nanoparticles (PEG/MUA-AuNPs); and (3) cysteamine-modified gold nanoparticles (cysteamine-AuNPs). For MUA-AuNPs, the complexation between magnesium ions and the carboxyl groups of MUA caused particle aggregation (red precipitate; condition similar to negative sample in loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP), i.e., without target DNA sequence). On the other hand, with magnesium ions and pyrophosphate ions (condition similar to positive sample in LAMP, i.e., with target DNA sequence, pyrophosphate ions are LAMP byproduct), the gradual formation of magnesium pyrophosphate extracted magnesium ions from the originally complexed carboxyl groups, thus partial particle deaggregation (precipitate turned from red to purple). For PEG/MUA-AuNPs, PEG stabilized interparticle complexation by magnesium ions, thereby resulting in a red dispersion. With magnesium pyrophosphate (indeed with crystal formation), the complexation of magnesium ions with the carboxyl groups of MUA and pyrophosphate ions led to coprecipitation of magnesium pyrophosphate crystals and PEG/MUA-AuNPs (red precipitate). For cysteamine-AuNPs, a red dispersion was resulted with magnesium ions (electrostatic repulsion between positively charged cysteamine) while a red precipitate was resulted with magnesium pyrophosphate (electrostatic attraction between positively charged cysteamine and negatively charged pyrophosphate ion; coprecipitation of magnesium pyrophosphate crystals and cysteamine-AuNPs). Objective 2 (100%): All the three types of AuNPs (MUA-AuNPs, PEG/MUA-AuNPs, and cysteamine-AuNPs) were found to be compatible with LAMP. Specifically, with 13-15 nm AuNPs at 6 nM (clear red color for easy readout by the naked eye), there was negligible inhibition of LAMP efficiency. Objective 3 (100%): All the three types of AuNPs (MUA-AuNPs, PEG/MUA-AuNPs, and cysteamine-AuNPs) were found to be stable and resistant to nonspecific enzyme adsorption under LAMP reaction conditions. It should be noted that MUA-AuNPs and PEG/MUA-AuNPs had excellent stability in water (could be stored for months after synthesis) whereas cysteamine-AuNPs were not stable for prolonged storage (aggregation in water within a few days; freshly prepared for the stability and enzyme adsorption tests under LAMP reaction conditions). Objective 4 (100%): All the three types of AuNPs (MUA-AuNPs, PEG/MUA-AuNPs, and cysteamine-AuNPs) enabled closed-tube colorimetric detection of LAMP (first demonstration of colorimetric monitoring of isothermal DNA amplification reaction with AuNPs in closed-tube format). Consistent with the results in Objective 1, MUA-AuNPs appeared as red precipitate in negative sample and purple precipitate in positive sample, while PEG/MUA-AuNPs and cysteamine-AuNPs appeared as red dispersion in negative sample and red precipitate in positive sample. It should be noted that MUA-AuNPs featured end-point measurement while PEG/MUA-AuNPs and cysteamine-AuNPs featured real-time measurement (quantification over a wider dynamic range). Objective 5 (85%): Reaction conditions (e.g., concentrations of magnesium ions and dNTPs) were optimized to give the best contrast between negative and positive samples with all the three types of AuNPs (MUA-AuNPs, PEG/MUA-AuNPs, and cysteamine-AuNPs). Owing to the poor storage stability of cysteamine-AuNPs, specificity and sensitivity tests were only performed with MUA-AuNPs and PEG/MUA-AuNPs. Both MUA-AuNPs and PEG/MUA-AuNPs exhibited excellent specificity and sensitivity. The limits of detection for the assay platforms with MUA-AuNPs and PEG/MUA-AuNPs were 17 aM (200 copies in 20 uL) and 42 aM (500 copies in 20 uL), respectively. Objective 6 (100%): In collaboration with Tai Lung Veterinary Laboratory under Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department of the Hong Kong Government (Hong Kong's central unit for avian influenza detection), the PEG/MUA-AuNPs assay platform was successfully applied for the detection of H9 subtype from avian field samples.

501413.label: Major findings and research outcome
501413.value: Three closed-tube colorimetric LAMP assay platforms were developed in this project (first-of-its-kind closed-tube colorimetric readout of isothermal DNA amplification with AuNPs). First, MUA-AuNPs were found to be precipitated (red color) in negative LAMP sample due to particle aggregation caused by the complexation between magnesium ions and carboxyl groups of MUA. On the other hand, in positive LAMP sample, pyrophosphate ions (reaction byproduct) could lead to partial particle deaggregation due to their strong binding affinity with magnesium ions, thus the precipitate turned from red to purple. End-point readout was performed and a mild sonicated step could redisperse the precipitate for clearer interpretation. A Chinese patent was applied for this new mechanism and assay platform (details are given in Part C Item 11). Second, PEG/MUA-AuNPs were found to be dispersed (red color) in negative LAMP sample because PEG hindered the interparticle complexation (magnesium ions and carboxyl groups of MUA). On the other hand, in positive LAMP sample, PEG/MUA-AuNPs were bound to magnesium pyrophosphate crystals through complexation (magnesium ions with pyrophosphate ions of the crystals and carboxyl groups of MUA), resulting in coprecipitation of the crystals and PEG/MUA-AuNPs (red precipitate). By measuring the absorbance (520 nm; surface plasmon resonance absorption peak of AuNPs) through the supernatant with a homemade, handheld, and low-cost device, real-time monitoring of LAMP was achieved. This work was published in ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces (details are given in Part C Item 8). A US provisional patent was also filed (details are given in Part C Item 11). As mentioned in Part B Item 5.3 (realisation of objectives; Objective 6), this work has initiated the collaboration with Tai Lung Veterinary Laboratory under Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department of the Hong Kong Government (Hong Kong's central unit for avian influenza detection). One manuscript on avian influenza (subtype H9) detection is under preparation. Third, cysteamine-AuNPs were found to appear as red dispersion and red precipitate in negative and positive LAMP, respectively. Although similar behavior as PEG/MUA-AuNPs, the mechanism was different. The dispersion with cysteamine-AuNPs was due to electrostatic repulsion of positively charged cysteamine while the precipitation was due to electrostatic attraction between positively charged cysteamine and negatively charged pyrophosphate ions (thus coprecipitation of cysteamine-AuNPs and magnesium pyrophosphate crystals). Nevertheless, cysteamine-AuNPs suffered from major disadvantage of poor storage stability.

501413.value: In collaboration with Tai Lung Veterinary Laboratory under Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department, we will further test the applicability of the assay platform with PEG/MUA-AuNPs for other subtypes of avian influenza. 501413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
501413.value: Gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) possess unique optical properties that enable the detection of a broad spectrum of analytes by the naked eye, which is ideally suited to point-of-care and on-site testing. For nucleic acid detection, to date, the reported AuNP-based assay platforms had drawbacks of complicated and expensive AuNP probe preparation (oligonucleotide-modified AuNPs), complicated operation (thermocycling target nucleic acid sequence amplification), and/or carryover contamination (postamplification open-tube addition of AuNP probe). In this project, we developed three new types of AuNP probes (11-mercaptoundecanoic acid-modified AuNPs, MUA-AuNPs; poly(ethylene glycol)- and 11-mercaptoundecanoic acid-comodified AuNPs, PEG/MUA-AuNPs; and cysteamine-modified AuNPs, cysteamine-AuNPs) that enabled differentiation of negative (without target DNA sequence) and positive (with target DNA sequence) loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) samples in closed-tube format by the naked eye. Among them, the PEG/MUA-AuNPs assay platform had the best performance by virtue of real-time monitoring and long-term storage capabilities. This platform was successfully applied to avian influenza (subtype H9) detection. Given the advantages of simple and low-cost AuNP probe preparation, simple operation (isothermal amplification), visual readout, and worry-free carryover contamination control (closed-tube format), it holds great promise for a wide range of decentralized testing such as medical diagnostics, food safety monitoring, and environmental surveillance.

501813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
501813.value: Alkyl nitrates play a crucial role in controlling ozone, NOx, NOy and HOx concentrations throughout the troposphere. They are therefore important in determining atmospheric composition, radiative balance and climate change. Organic nitrates have both anthropogenic and biogenic origins. Methyl and ethyl nitrate are produced from the ocean from algae [1]. Other longer chain alkyl nitrates are associated with urban and industrial emissions [2-6], while in remote areas, nitrates of biogenic volatile organic compounds (VOCs) become significant [7]. Organic nitrates can also be produced in the atmosphere from alkylperoxy + NO reactions, as well as NO3 oxidation of unsaturated hydrocarbons. A number of recent regional and global model studies have demonstrated that vital kinetic and photolytic parameters, especially for the alkyl nitrates formed from the oxidation of biogenic VOCs (notably isoprene), are missing, preventing chemical models from describing atmospheric oxidation chemistry well and hence determining lifetimes of key greenhouse gases and surface pollutants. These parameters include their loss rate via reaction with OH and O3 and whether NOx is released in these reactions. Also, how much NOx (photochemical reactive nitrogen oxide) and how much HNO3 (photochemically non-reactive nitrogen oxide) are eventually formed from organic nitrate reactions is important in understanding the contribution of alkyl nitrates to the oxidizing capacity of the atmosphere [8]. For Hong Kong and other marine environments, Cl atom concentrations may be 10e3 higher than that of OH [9-11] . The reaction rate of organic nitrates with Cl may be an order of magnitude higher than that with OH. Therefore, the reaction of alkyl nitrates with Cl atoms, as well as OH, may play an important role in the decomposition of organic nitrates in coastal environments. In this study a combination of Photoelectron Spectroscopy (PES) and Chemical Ionisation Mass Spectrometry (CIMS) measurements will be used to determine rate coefficients of reactions with OH and Cl with key alkyl nitrates, including some isoprene nitrates, and to measure the reaction branching ratios. Also for each reaction studied experimentally, computation of the reaction surface and channel specific rate coefficients with electronic structure methods will lead to a detailed understanding of the reaction mechanism and will allow a comparison between experimental and calculated rate coefficients. The proposed work will be crucial to the understanding of the effects of biogenic VOCs on atmospheric pollution and climate change. 硝酸酯化合物對整個對流層中的臭氧，氮氧化物 NOx NOy和HOX濃度起關鍵的影響。因此它們在確定大氣成分輻射平衡和氣候變化的角色是十分重要的。有機硝酸酯的來源可分為人類活動和生物天然排放兩類。甲基和乙基硝酸酯主要源於海洋藻類的排放 。其他烷基硝酸脂與城市和工業排放息息有關 。在邊遠地區生物排放的揮發性有機物則最為主要 。硝酸酯也可由過氧烷基和 NO反應及硝酸基氧化不飽和烴而生成。 近期的區域和全球大氣化學模型計算研究顯示某些反應速率和光解率參數不足特別是現時對植物來源的揮發性有機硝酸酯如異戊二烯的相關參數所知甚少大大限制了現時大氣化學模型描述氧化過程的準確性從而影響了現時對主要溫室氣體的壽命和污染物生成的估計。這些參數包括硝酸酯與OH 和O3的反應速率反應通度與及反應有否產生NO2。此外硝酸酯反應過程最終生成多少NOx 能參與光化學反應的氮氧化合物HNO3 不能參與光化學反應的氮氧化物決定了硝酸酯對大氣層的氧化能力的貢獻[8]。在香港和其他海洋環境中氯原子的濃度可能高於OH 的10000倍。加上硝酸酯與Cl的反應速率可能是十倍高於它與OH的 反應速率。因此硝酸酯與氯原子的化學反應對硝酸酯的分解，尤其在沿海區域中，可能發揮著與OH 反應同等重要的作用。 這項研究利用光電子能譜 PES 和化學電離質譜CIMS測量硝酸酯包括一些異戊二烯硝酸酯與OH和Cl的反應速率係數並測量反應分支比。並對每個實驗研究的反應利用量子化學方法計算反應表面和特定反應通道速率從而比較實驗和計算的差異並了解詳細的反應機理。是項研究大大有助了解最主要的揮發性有機化合物對大氣污染和氣候變化的影響。

501813.label: Realisation of objectives
501813.value: Alkyl nitrates provide temporary reservoirs for odd-oxygen and play a crucial role in controlling ozone, NOx, NOy and HOx concentrations throughout the troposphere. Their lifetimes and the major reaction channel would be important in determining atmospheric composition, radiative balance and climate change. The objectives of this project is to characterise reactions of alkyl nitrate with chlorine atom and hydroxy radicals. For reactions between organic nitrates and hydroxy radicals (objectives 1, 2 and 5), theoretical calculations has been performed to study the reactions and estimate their atmospheric lifetime. Estimation of the lifetime of CH3ONO2 with respect to reaction with OH is difficult as the available room temperature experimental rate coefficients occur in two groups which differ by an order of magnitude, a lower group, at ~3x10-14 cm3 molecule-1s-1 and a higher group, at~ 3x10-13 cm3 molecule-1s-1. In this study, four reaction channels were considered: CH3ONO2 + OH  H2O + CH2ONO2 ------------ (1) CH3ONO2 + OH  CH3OOH + NO2 ------------ (2) CH3ONO2 + OH  CH3OH + NO3 ------------ (3) CH3ONO2 + OH  CH3O + HNO3 ------------ (4) For all channels, geometry optimization and frequency calculations were performed on all the reactacts, reactive complexes, transition states, product complexes, and products as well as 30 non-stationary points along the IRC at the M06-2X/6-31+G** level, while relative energies of all the stationary points (reactants, reactive complexes, transition states, product complexes and products) were improved at the UCCSD(T*)-F12 using the VTZ-F12 and VQZ-F12 basis to estimate the Complete Basis Set limit. The major channel is found to be the H abstraction channel (channel 1). The reaction enthalpy (ΔH298 KRX) of this channel is computed as −17.90 kcal mol−1. The reaction barrier of this channel is very low and the best theoretical estimate is only 4 kcal mol−1. Although the other reaction channels are also exothermic, their reaction barriers are very high (>24 kcal mol−1), and therefore these reactions do not contribute significantly to the overall rate coefficient in the temperature range considered (200−400 K). Pathways via three transition states were identified for the H abstraction channel. Reaction rate coefficients were computed for the H abstraction channel at various transition-state theory (TST) levels in single-level (using the energies, gradients and hessians from M06-2X/6-31+G** level) and improved single-level direct dynamics calculations (using energies at UCCSD level and gradients and hessians using M06-2X) at temperatures in the region of 200−400 K. A simple extrapolation scheme has been proposed to obtain the VMEP curves from the 30 non-stationary points energies which gave a better improved single-level direct dynamics TST calculations. Our theoretical computed rate coefficients and their temperature dependence suggest that the lower experimental values are favoured. These results has been published in Journal of Physical Chemistry A (Part C, item 4). Similar calculations have been extended to examine reaction of OH with two isoprene nitrates, namely 3,4-dinitrooxy-1-butene (34-1) and 1,4-dinitrooxy-2-butene (14-2)). Two channels are considered which are the OH addition and H abstraction. Our computed reaction rate coefficients for 14-2 is slightly faster than 34-1, as observed. For the reaction with chlorine atom (objectives 3, 4 and 5), theoretical study of the reaction of chlorine atom with methyl nitrate has been conducted. Similarly to the study of the reaction with hydroxy radicals, four reaction channels, with products: HCl + CH2ONO2, CH3Cl + NO2, CH3OCl + NO3 and CH3O + ClNO2, were considered. For all channels, geometry optimization and frequency calculations were carried out at the M06-2X/6-31+G** level, while relative electronic energies were improved to the state-of-the-art UCCSD(T*)-F12/CBS level. The major channel is found to be the H abstraction channel, which gives the products HCl + CH2ONO2. Specifically, the reaction barrier and reaction enthalpy of the H abstraction channel were computed to be 0.61 and -2.30 kcal.mol-1, respectively, at the highest level of calculation, while reaction barriers for the other channels are more positive and these pathways do not contribute to the overall reaction rate coefficient in the temperature range considered (200-400 K). Employing the computed highest level energy profile, rate coefficients were calculated for the H-abstraction channel at various levels of variational transition state theory (VTST) including tunneling. The computed highest VTST level (ICVT/SCT) rate coefficient at room temperature agrees very well with experimental values, which are only available at room temperature. In this connection, computed ICVT/SCT rate coefficients in the temperature range 200-400 K obtained for the first time for this reaction in this work are recommended for atmospheric modeling, which involves reactions with methyl nitrate. In addition, the enthalpies of formation, ΔHf,298K , of CH3ONO2 and CH2ONO2 were also computed to be -29.7 and 19.3 kcal.mol-1, respectively, at the UCCSD(T*)-F12/CBS level. This work has been published in the journal, Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics (Part C Item 1). The lifetime of methyl nitrate in the atmosphere is determined by loss through photolysis, reaction with OH radicals and reaction with Cl atoms, as methyl nitrate is thermally stable in the temperature range 200-300 K, and heterogeneous removal is slow because the solubility and reactivity with water is low (objective 6). The estimated daytime global average [Cl] is 1 × 10 3 atom·cm−3 in the marine boundary layer, the methyl nitrate lifetime with respect to reaction with chlorine atom is 36800 days at 300K and 249000 days at 200K. With OH, The estimated average daytime concentration of OH is 1 × 10 6 molecule cm−3, the methyl nitrate lifetime with respect to reaction with OH is estimated as 422 (300 K) and 2320 (200 K) days, respectively. Comparing with the photolysis data in the literature, therefore, under normal atmospheric conditions in the troposphere the methyl nitrate lifetimes are in the order photolysis < reaction with OH < reaction with Cl atom (Objective 6). Similar to the Cl + CH3ONO2 reaction, the Cl + HCOOH reaction is important in the atmosphere, as formic acid (HCOOH) is one of the most abundant organic acids in the troposphere. The reaction surfaces of the two H abstraction channels were computed by UMP2 and DFT (using a number of functionals) calculations. Relative electronic energies were improved to the RCCSD(T)/CBS and UCCSD(T)-F12/CBS levels. The barrier of the C-H hydrogen abstraction channel was found to be lower than the O-H hydrogen abstraction channel by ~10 kcal.mol-1. It was found that for single level direct dynamics VTST calculations, the computed rate coefficient (2.5x10-13 cm3molecule-1s-1) using the BMK functional at the highest TST level (ICVT/SCT) agrees the best with available experimental values at 298 K (1.8 and 2.0x10-13 cm3molecule-1s-1). For dual level direct dynamics calculations (RCCSD(T)/CBS//MP2 MEP), an adjusted barrier of 3.1 kcal.mol-1 is required to match the ICVT/SCT k with the experimental values. The computed rate coefficients of the Cl + HCOOH reaction over the temperature range of 200-1500K are reported for the first time (Part C, item 2). Related works: HPS is a species of interest in the interstellar medium and astrochemistry, and an important molecule for understanding the bonding in molecules composed of second row elements. Multi-reference configuration interaction (MRCI-F12) method have been performed on the X1Aʹ and A1Aʺ states of HPS, and Franck–Condon factors between the two states have been determined to simulate the LIF and SVL emission spectra. Our results supports the proposed assignments (Part C, Item 3).

501813.label: Major findings and research outcome
501813.value: Organic nitrates provide temporary reservoirs for odd-oxygen and play a crucial role in controlling ozone, NOx, NOy and HOx concentrations throughout the troposphere. Their lifetimes and the major reaction channel would be important in determining atmospheric composition, radiative balance and climate change. In this project, we characterized the reactions of methyl nitrate with chlorine atom and hydroxy radicals, the two most important oxidizing agents in the troposphere. State-of-the-art theoretical calculations have been performed to obtain a reliable estimate of the reaction rate coefficients. For both reaction partners, the hydrogen abstraction is the major channel and the minor channels have high barriers, and hence, having small contributions to the overall reaction coefficients. The computed reaction rate coefficient of methyl nitrate with Cl at 298K is 3.06 x 10 -13 cm3 molecule-1 s-1 compares well with the recommended experimental value at this temperature of 2.34 x 10 -13 cm3 molecule-1 s-1. The computed rate coefficients in the temperature range 200-400 K relevant for atmospheric conditions are obtained for the first time and can be used for atmospheric chemistry modelling involving reactions with methyl nitrate (Part C, item 1,2). In case of the reaction of methyl nitrate with OH, the rate coefficient at 298K is 1.29 x 10 -15 cm3 molecule-1 s-1, almost two order of magnitude smaller than value of the corresponding reaction with chlorine. The computed reaction rate of methyl nitrate with OH is about an order of magnitude smaller than the lowest experimental values reported in the literature. An numerical agreement can be achieved if the barrier height is lower by 2.5 kcal/mol. The barrier of the reactions studied in this project is rather low, results in numerical issues in using dual level TST in POLYRATE, a simple extrapolation is proposed and used to obtained the reaction rate coefficients using high level ab initio (UCCSD(T)/CBS) single point energies along the IRC. Our study suggested that under normal atmospheric conditions in the troposphere the methyl nitrate lifetimes are in the order photolysis < reaction with OH < reaction with Cl atom (Part C, item 4).

501813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
501813.value: The reaction rate coefficients of organic nitrates with chlorine atom is one or two order of magnitude faster than the corresponding reaction with OH. However, the average [OH] is larger than the average [Cl] making the reaction with OH being the dominant the loss of organic molecules in the atmosphere. If [Cl] increases to 10 6 atoms cm3 (an estimated upper limit), then these day-time lifetimes drop to 36.83 (300 K) and 248.7 (200 K) days respectively, which would be comparable to that of OH, thus reaction of Cl atom with various organic compounds would still play a role in the chemistry of the atmosphere and worthwhile for further study. In the two reactions with OH studied in this project, corrections of computed barrier height at the highest level is still required in order to get the agreement of computed reaction rate coefficient with experimental values. This certainly requires further examination of the reasons as OH is certainly the most important oxidant in the atmosphere.

501813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
501813.value: Organic nitrates play a crucial role in controlling ozone, NOx, NOy and HOx concentrations throughout the troposphere. Their lifetimes and the major reaction channel would be important in determining atmospheric composition, radiative balance and climate change. The reaction rate coefficients of methyl nitrate with OH and Cl at temperature range relevant to the atmosphere have been determined. Our studies suggested that photolysis is the major process for the loss of these compounds followed by reaction with OH, then Cl. These provided essential information to understand the chemistry of these organic nitrate. Employing these new kinetic data in modelling the atmosphere will revise and improve the reliability of the results obtained, which will allow a more accurate account for role of organic nitrate in the troposphere, and abundances of ozone, NOx, NOy and HOx concentrations. Currently, the best theoretical estimates of the barrier height of reaction of VOC with OH may still need further refinement to an agreement with experimental values. Improvements in theoretical methods to describe the transition state of reactions with OH may be necessary to generate reliable reaction rate coefficients for modelling.

501913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
501913.value: Spectral graph theory is a well-studied and highly applicable subject. On the other hand, spectral hypergraph theory is still in its early stage. In this project, we plan to give the tensor approach for spectral hypergraph theory a clear start. We will apply the theory and computation of eigenvalues of tensors to spectral hypergraph theory. We will give a natural and simple definition of the Laplacian and signless Laplacian tensors, and connected them with the adjacency tensor closely. We will use eigenvalues (H-eigenvalues) in the study of spectral hypergraph theory and justify this approach. We will give clear definitions of the second largest eigenvalue of the adjacency tensor and the second smallest eigenvalue of the Laplacian tensor, and investigate their applications in expander hypergraphs, quasirandomness and other hypergraph properties. We will explore the possibility to order the complex eigenvalues of the adjacency and Laplacian tensors, and investigate topics like interlacing. The spectral hypergraph theory is a new subject in applied mathematics. The tensor approach is an important new approach for this theory. The success of this research project will greatly advance the study on spectral hypergraph theory, give it a solid foundation. The success of this project will also advance the spectral theory of tensors, in particular, for symmetric nonnegative tensors and symmetric positive definite tensors. Thus, the success of this project will be significant in both spectral hypergraph theory and spectral theory of tensors. 图谱理论 是一门 研究成熟并被广泛应用的学科。另一方面，超图谱理论的研究仍处于初始阶段。 在本项目的研究中，我们将给出超图谱理论张量方法的一个清晰的起动。我们将张量特征值理论及相关计算方法应用于超图谱理论。我们将给出拉普拉斯张量和无号拉普拉斯张量一个自然和简单的定义，并且将它们与相邻张量紧密联系起来。在超图谱理论研究过程中，我们将运用特征值（H-特征值）来研究超图谱理论，并说明这样做法的合理性。我们将给出相邻张量的第二大特征值和拉普拉斯张量的第二小特征值的明确定义，并且探究这两个特征值在扩张超图、准随机超图和超图其它性质中的应用。同时，我们还要探索相邻张量和拉普拉斯张量的复特征值的排序问题及其应用。 超图谱理论是应用数学中的一个新分支，张量方法是研究超图谱理论的一种重要的新方法。本项目的成功将会极大地促进超图谱理论的研究，并且为后续研究奠定坚实的基础。同时，本项目的成功还会促进张量谱理论的研究，特别是对称非负张量和对称正定张量方面的研究。因此，本项目的成功对于研究超图谱理论和张量谱理论都具有重要意义。

501913.label: Realisation of objectives
501913.value: We established the relation between the largest Laplacian H-eigenvalue and the largest signless Laplacian H-eigenvalue of a k-uniform nontrivial hypergraph. The largest Laplacian H-eigenvalue is always less than or equal to the largest signless Laplacian H-eigenvalue. When the hypergraph is connected, the equality holds here if and only if k is even and the hypergraph is odd-bipartite. We showed that the largest Laplacian H-eigenvalue of a k-uniform nontrivial hypergraph is strictly larger than the maximum degree when k is even. A tight lower bound for this eigenvalue is given. For a connected even-uniform hypergraph, this lower bound is achieved if and only if it is a hyperstar. However, when k is odd, in certain cases the largest Laplacian H-eigenvalue is equal to the maximum degree, which is a tight lower bound. On the other hand, tight upper and lower bounds for the largest signless Laplacian H-eigenvalue of a k-uniform connected hypergraph are given. For a connected k-uniform hypergraph, the upper (respectively lower) bound of the largest signless Laplacian H-eigenvalue is achieved if and only if it is a complete hypergraph (respectively a hyperstar). We presented some inequality relations between the Laplacian and signless Laplacian H-eigenvalues and the clique and coclique numbers of uniform hypergraphs. For a connected uniform hypergraph, we gave some tight lower bounds on the largest Laplacian H+-eigenvalue and signless Laplacian H-eigenvalue related to the clique and coclique numbers, and some upper and lower bounds on the clique and coclique numbers related to the largest Laplacian and signless Laplacian H-eigenvalues. We also gave some bounds on the sum of the largest and the smallest adjacency/Laplacian/signless Laplacian H-eigenvalues of a hypergraph and its complement hypergraph. All these bounds are consistent with what we have known in the graph case. We also proved Conjecture 4.1 of Hu, Qi and Shao (2013). We first time systematically studied the directed hypergraph theory. We studied properties of the adjacency tensor, the Laplacian tensor and the signless Laplacian tensor of a uniform directed hypergraph, and presented some lower and upper bounds for the largest and smallest adjacency, Laplacian and signless Laplacian H-eigenvalues of a uniform directed hypergraph. We showed that for a uniform directed hypergraph, the smallest Laplacian H-eigenvalue is 0. On the other hand, the upper bound of the largest adjacency and signless Laplacian H-eigenvalues are achieved if and only if it is a complete directed hypergraph. We also studied circulant tensors and their applications to spectral hypergraph theory and stochastic process. In particular, we studied their applications to circulant hypergraphs and directed circulant hypergraphs. We studied some extremal problems of three kinds of spectral radii of k-uniform hypergraphs (the adjacency spectral radius, the signless Laplacian spectral radius and the incidence Q-spectral radius). We call a connected and acyclic k-uniform hypergraph a supertree. We introduced the operation of “moving edges” for hypergraphs, together with the two special cases of this operation: the edge-releasing operation and the total grafting operation. By studying the perturbation of these kinds of spectral radii of hypergraphs under these operations, we proved that for all these three kinds of spectral radii, the hyperstar attains uniquely the maximum spectral radius among all k-uniform supertrees on n vertices. We also determined the unique k-uniform supertree on n vertices with the second largest spectral radius (for these three kinds of spectral radii). We also proved that for all these three kinds of spectral radii, the loose path attains uniquely the minimum spectral radius among all k-th power hypertrees of n vertices. Owing to the sparsity of the adjacency tensor, the Laplacian tensor, and the signless Laplacian tensor of a k-uniform hypergraph, we proposed an efficient approach to calculate products of these tensors and any vectors. By using the state-of-the-art L-BFGS approach, we developed a first-order optimization algorithm for computing H- and Z-eigenvalues of these large scale sparse tensors (CEST) arising from hypergraphs. With the aid of the Lojasiewicz inequality, we proved that the sequence of iterates generated by CEST converges to an eigenvector of the tensor. When CEST is started from multiple random initial points, the resulting best eigenvalue could touch the extreme eigenvalue with a high probability. Numerical experiments show that CEST is efficient and promising. Moreover, CEST is capable of computing eigenvalues of tensors related to a hypergraph with millions of vertices. A connected k-uniform hypergraph with n vertices and m edges is called r-cyclic if n =m(k−1) −r+1. For r=1or 2, the hypergraph is simply called unicyclic or bicyclic. We investigated hypergraphs that attain largest spectral radii among all simple connected k-uniform unicyclic and bicyclic hypergraphs. Specifically, by using some edge operations, the formula on power hypergraph eigenvalues, the weighted incidence matrix and a result on linear unicyclic hypergraphs, we determined the first five hypergraphs with largest spectral radius among all unicyclic hypergraphs and the first three over all bicyclic hypergraphs. Based on the advances in spectral hypergraph theory, we explore the Fiedler vector of an even-uniform hypergraph, which is the Z-eigenvector associated with the second smallest Z-eigenvalue of a normalized Laplacian tensor arising from the hypergraph. Then, we developed a novel tensor-based spectral method for partitioning vertices of the hypergraph. For this purpose, we extended the normalized Laplacian matrix of a simple graph to the normalized Laplacian tensor of an even-uniform hypergraph. The corresponding Fiedler vector is related to the Cheeger constant of the hypergraph. Then, we established a feasible optimization algorithm to compute the Fiedler vector according to the normalized Laplacian tensor. The convergence of the proposed algorithm and the probability of obtaining the Fiedler vector of the hypergraph are analyzed theoretically. Preliminary numerical experiments illustrated that the new approach based on a hypergraph-based Fiedler vector is effective and promising for some combinatorial optimization problems arising from subspace partitioning and face clustering. Let k ≥ 2 and k be even. An k-hypergraph G on n vertices is called odd-colorable if there exists a map ϕ : [n] → [k] such that for any edge { j1, j2, . . . , jk } of G, we have ϕ(j1) + ϕ(j2) + · · · · · +ϕ(jk ) ≡ k/2(mod k). We first determined that, if k = 2q(2t + 1) and n ≥ 2q(2q − 1)k, then the maximum chromatic number in the class of the odd-colorable k-hypergraphs on n vertices is 2q, which answers a question raised by V. Nikiforov (2017). We also study some applications of the spectral symmetry of the odd-colorable r-hypergraphs given in the same paper by V. Nikiforov. We showed that the Laplacian spectrum and the signless Laplacian spectrum of an k-hypergraph G are equal if and only if k is even and G is odd colorable. The p-spectral radius of a uniform hypergraph covers many important concepts, such as Lagrangian and spectral radius of the hypergraph, and is crucial for solving spectral extremal problems of hypergraphs. Particularly, it can be applied for evaluating the importance of objects from reality. We established a spherically constrained maximization model and proposed a first-order conjugate gradient algorithm to compute the p-spectral radius of a uniform hypergraph (CSRH). By the semi-algebraic nature of the adjacency tensor of a uniform hypergraph, CSRH is globally convergent and obtains the global maximizer with a high probability.

502913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
502913.value: 質譜是一種快速、靈敏的分析工具，而電噴霧電離是質譜常用的一種電離技術。電噴霧電離主要采用毛細管引導樣品產生電離。為了避免毛細管的堵塞問題， 人們發展了固體尖端承載樣品進行電離的非毛細管電噴霧電離技術。最近幾年，隨著常壓質譜的發展，非毛細管電噴霧電離因其能直接分析復雜樣品及與傳統電噴霧電離不同的特性而引起了越來越多的關註。 近年來，我們發展了木質尖端電噴霧電離和生物組織的直接電離質譜分析。最近，我們將這兩種技術合并為固相基底電噴霧電離。固相基底電噴霧電離利用惰性材料(如：木頭，竹子，纖維和海綿)承載樣品進行電離，同時可對塊狀的樣品(如：植物組織，動物組織，蘑菇和骨頭)進行直接電離分析。固相基底電噴霧電離質譜簡單、易推廣、且能在無需或只需少量樣品預處理條件下直接分析復雜樣品。 在本項目中，我們旨在調查固相基底電噴霧電離質譜直接分析獲得的譜圖結果能多大程度表征樣品的組成成分，研究固相基底電噴霧電離的依序及耗盡電離的次序和機理，以及進一步發展固相基底電噴霧電離用於活體植物的直接質譜分析。本項目的順利實施，將有助於揭示固相基底電噴霧電離的機制以及發展簡單有效的方法用於復雜樣品的直接分析和活體樣品的實時監測。

502913.label: Realisation of objectives
502913.value: Various studies have been carried out for realization of the objectives. Six tripeptides, namely G-G-G, G-G-A, G-G-V, G-G-L, G-G-Y and G-G-F, were employed as model compounds to investigate signal response of analytes on various solid substrates including wooden tip, polyester tip and polyethylene tip, which have surfaces with different properties. These peptides have the same peptide backbone and varying nonpolar character due to differences in their C-terminal residues. A two-stage ionization was observed for solid-substrate ESI-MS analysis of the peptide mixture. At stage 1, the response of the six tripeptides was in agreement with their nonpolar surface areas, i.e., more hydrophobic peptides were detected with higher intensities. This was consistent with the result obtained with capillary-based ESI-MS and demonstrated that ionization at stage 1 was a conventional ESI process. At stage 2, a very different response pattern of the six tripeptides was observed, with more hydrophobic compounds more retained by the tips and giving less response. Our results also showed that more hydrophobic tips enabled better separation of the peptides and that hydrophobic-hydrophobic interactions were crucial for the mobility and detectability of the peptides in the tips. To further understand the relationship between surface activity of solid substrates and analytical properties, we performed surface modification of wooden tips with hydrophobic (-C18), basic (-NH2) and acidic (-SO3H) functional groups and applied various sampling methods, i.e., extractive sampling and direct loading, to comprehensively investigate the analytical properties of solid-substrate ESI-MS. Our results showed that for the direct loading method, analytes with weak interactions with solid-substrate surface could be readily sprayed out for detection. While for the extractive sampling method, analytes strongly retained on solid-substrate surface could be selectively enriched and detected, and a washing step after sample loading could effectively remove unbound components for reducing interference. These insights could aid the development of surface-modified strategies for enhancing the analytical capability of solid-substrate ESI-MS. Different solvents (e.g., polar solvents such as methanol, and nonpolar solvents such as hexane) were used to investigate the effect of solvents on signal response of solid-substrate ESI. For example, methanol, water, acetonitrile with 0.1 formic acid, acetone, and hexane were used to investigate the response of sildenafil and tadalafil in wooden-tip ESI-MS analysis of adulterated drugs in herbal dietary supplements. Good response of both sildenafil and tadalafil was obtained only with acetonitrile containing 0.1% formic acid (ACN/FA) as the solvent, indicating that the solvent served as both the extraction and ionization medium and the importance to choose a suitable solvent for the analysis. We also demonstrated that solid-substrate ESI-MS with nonpolar solvents such as n-hexane could allow detection of native proteins and protein complexes directly from raw biological samples. Mechanistic study revealed that the process involved rapid vaporization of the nonpolar solvent, temperature reduction of substrate surface, condensation of water from the ambient air, and spray ionization of the condensed water with analytes under the electric field. The fine spray with water at low temperature allowed the technique to detect native proteins, even directly from viscous samples (e.g., egg white) and solid samples (e.g., bone marrow). This sheds new insight into the sampling and ionization process of mass spectrometry and provides a technique for detection of native proteins. One of the features of solid-substrate ESI-MS is that some analytes could be ionized and exhausted in sequence. Analysis of various proteins using ESI-MS with various porous substrates was investigated in this study. Our results revealed that ESI-MS with porous substrates could allow separation of proteins based on their sizes and shapes, including separation of the same proteins with different charge states. The separated proteins could be monitored by the ESI spectra or by analysis of the proteins remained on the substrates, and the latter could also allow preparative separation of proteins. This new observation implies a potential approach for investigation of proteins. Moreover, commercial thin layer chromatography (TLC) was used for coupling with ESI-MS for sequential and exhaustive ionization of raw samples. The sorbent material of the TLC plate was found to be able to retain the interfering compounds and allow interested analytes to be extracted, ionized and detected by ESI-MS with much reduced matrix interference. Our results showed that this method could be effectively applied in direct analysis of samples containing common interfering compounds, and rapid detection and quantitation of target analytes in raw samples. New solid-substrate ESI-MS techniques, e.g., C18 pipette-tip ESI-MS, were developed in this project. C18 pipette-tip ESI-MS is simple, easy to assemble, has solid substrate with hydrophobic surface for desalting and removal of hydrophilic interferences and enrichment of hydrophobic analytes, and can produce stable and reproducible signals for quantitative analysis. We demonstrated that C18 pipette-tip ESI-MS could be used for rapid and sensitive detection and quantitation of various analytes in raw solutions. Two high throughput wooden-tip ESI-MS techniques have also been developed for automatic analysis of samples on the wooden tips and were demonstrated for analysis of herbal medicines and detection of adulterated drugs in herbal dietary supplements, respectively. Other applications of solid-substrate ESI-MS were also explored in this project, for rapid or direct analysis of various samples, including differentiation of the bulbs of Fritillaria, authentication of Gastrodiae rhizome, etc. Overall, the mechanism and further development and applications of solid-substrate ESI-MS have been systematically investigated in this project. The outcomes of this project have allowed us to obtain insight into the technique and allow its better exploitation.

502913.label: Major findings and research outcome
502913.value: Replacement of capillary with solid substrates in ESI-MS has created many new possibilities. The major findings and research outcomes in this project, as list below, allow us to obtain insight into solid-substrate ESI-MS and represent the important development of ESI-MS. 1. Surface-modified wooden-tip ESI-MS for enhanced detection of analytes in complex samples The results in this study revealed the effect of surface-analyte interactions on the analytical features and that enhanced detection of target analytes in complex mixtures could be achieved using suitable surface-modified wooden-tip ESI-MS. (Anal Chem, 2017, in revision) 2. Detection of native proteins with nonpolars solvents We revealed that solid-substrate ESI-MS with nonpolar solvents such as n-hexane could allow temperature reduction of substrate surface, condensation of water from the ambient air, and gentle ionization for detection of native proteins and protein complexes directly from raw biological samples. (Anal Chim Acta, 2017, doi: 10.1016/j.aca.2017.11.079) 3. Mobility of proteins in porous substrates under ESI conditions We revealed that proteins could be separately detected based on their sizes and shapes using porous-tip ESI-MS, which could be a potential approach for analysis of proteins and investigation of protein structures and conformations. (Anal Chem, 2016, 88, 5585–5589) 4. High-throughput solid-substrate ESI-MS Two different high-throughput wooden-tip ESI-MS techniques were developed for automatic analysis of herbal medicines and adulterated drugs in herbal dietary supplements. (Anal Chim Acta 2015, 887, 127-137; Anal Methods, 2016, 8, 6840–6846, cover story) 5. ESI-MS with TLC plates The sorbent material of the TLC plate was found to be able to retain the interfering compounds and allow interested analytes to be extracted, ionized and detected by ESI-MS with much reduced matrix interference. (J Chromatogr A, 2015, 1415, 155-160) 6. ESI-MS with C18 pipette tips Combination of C18 pipette tips with syringe and syringe pump for rapid analysis of raw solution samples by mass spectrometry was developed. The technique allowed rapid and effective enrichment and purification as well as quantification of analytes in raw solutions. (Anal Chim Acta, 2014, 844, 1-7, cover story) 7. Invited reviews for research in this project We have been invited to write two reviews on our research in solid-substrate ESI-MS, including J Chromatogr B, 2016, 1026, 2-14 and Sci Sin Chim, 2017, 47, 1365-1378.

502913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
502913.value: The study in this project reveals the mechanism of solid-substrate ESI-MS and shows that the analytical features of solid-substrate ESI-MS are different from those of conventional ESI-MS. We demonstrated that surface modification of solid substrates could be an effective strategy to enhance analytical capability of solid-substrate ESI-MS. This could be a direction for further development, particularly for rapid detection of trace targeted analytes in complex mixtures. Another potential field is to integrate some well-developed devices, e.g., solid phase microextraction (SPME) fibre, as the solid substrates to enhance the specificity and sensitivity of the technique. Some work in these aspects have been ongoing in our group.

502913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
502913.value: The mechanistic studies and further development of solid-substrate electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS) have been carried out in this project. Unlike conventional ESI-MS that uses relatively closed capillaries with inert and smooth surfaces, solid-substrate ESI-MS uses substrates with surfaces that can be porous and contain active functional groups for sample loading and ionization, and the samples on the substrates are exposed to the ambient air during the analysis. Our results revealed that the infrastructures and surface properties of solid substrates and even the ambient air could have significant effects on solid-substrate ESI-MS analysis. ESI-MS with porous substrates could allow separation and detection of proteins based on their sizes and shapes, and surface-modified solid-substrate ESI-MS enabled enhanced detection of analytes in complex mixtures. Solid-substrate ESI-MS with nonpolar solvents could induce condensation of water from the ambient air onto the substrate and allow detection of native proteins from raw biological samples. New techniques, including C18 pipette-tip ESI-MS, TLC-ESI-MS and high throughput wooden-tip ESI-MS, have been developed and extended for various applications in this project. Our results demonstrated that solid-substrate ESI-MS had different mechanism and analytical features from conventional ESI-MS and could be a powerful tool for various analytical purposes.
