503013.label: Project Title(Chinese)
503013.value: 靶向蛋白-蛋白相互作用的α-螺旋類似物的設計，合成與性能評價

503013.label: Co - Investigator(s)
503013.value: Prof Wiest, Olaf Prof Zhang, Hui

503013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
503013.value: Protein–protein interactions (PPIs) are central to most biological processes — from intercellular communication to programmed cell death — and therefore makes them interesting targets for drug discovery. However, due to the lack of deep pockets, and the large contact surfaces involved in PPIs, they are considered challenging targets. A key principle to emerge is that whilst a PPI takes place over a large surface area, usually only a few key residues that contribute the majority of the binding affinity to the interaction. Significantly, the majority of PPIs are mediated by three main recognition motifs (α-helix, β-turn, or β-strand); and synthetic molecules that reproduce key elements of these recognition motifs could lead to the discovery of small-molecule drugs to modulate PPIs. The α-helix is the most abundant secondary structural element in proteins and is an important structural domain for mediating many naturally occurring PPIs, such as assembly of the HIV gp41 fusion complex and hDM2–p53. Strategies for the rational design and synthesis of α-helix mimetics have not matured as well as other secondary structure mimetics such as β-turns and β-strands. Stable isolated peptides with defined short α-helical segment would be ideal inhibitors of macromolecular interactions. However, those with less than ~15 amino acid residues rarely adopt a defined conformation in isolation. Strategically placed covalent linkages to replace the weak (i, i+4) hydrogen bond have been shown to stabilize helical conformations in short peptide sequences. However, this approach seems limited to the N-terminal position of a short peptide. Our present studies focus on the design and synthesis of novel α-helix mimetics based on covalent H-bond replacement at an internal helical turn. In addition, the α-helicity and biological activities of the synthesized α-helix mimetics will also be investigated. The long-term goal of this research is to develop highly effective helix-mimetic-derived agents to modulate various significant protein–protein interactions, through molecular design, chemical synthesis and biological evaluation. We are directing our efforts to design of novel helix mimetics via a computational design platform, and construction of optimized structures by organic synthesis, employing strategies and methods that can be scaled up. The investigation of novel helix mimetics should have great impacts on both the synthetic and medicinal communities. 蛋白-蛋白相互作用（PPIs）在大多數的生物過程中, 從細胞間通訊到细胞程序性死亡飾演至關重要角色，因此使其成為廣泛關注的、用於藥物研發的靶標。然而，由於缺乏比較深的口袋式結合位點，以及較大的接觸面，PPI一般被認為是具有挑戰性的藥物靶標。 PPI在一個較大表面出現相互作用的時候，往往遵循一定的原則，即：通常只有幾個關鍵殘基對絡合親和力起主要的作用。值得注意的是，大部分的蛋白-蛋白相互作用是通過三個主要的識別基序（α-螺旋，β-折疊或β-鏈）來實現的。因此合成的分子若能夠複製這些關鍵的識別基序，將為開發靶向蛋白-蛋白相互作用靶點的小分子藥物提供可能。 α-螺旋結構是最豐富的蛋白質二級結構單元，介導許多天然存在的蛋白-蛋白相互作用，例如裝配的HIV gp41的融合複合物和hDM2-p53複合物等都是通過α-螺旋結構介導產生。合理設計和合成的α-螺旋模擬物與其他二級結構類似物如β-折疊和β鏈相比還遠不夠成熟。以穩定、孤立多肽形式存在的短α-螺旋結構將是大分子相互作用的理想抑製劑。然而小於15個氨基酸殘基的多肽在孤立存在的情況下很少採用定義的構象。使用共價鍵鏈接替換弱的（i，i+4）氫鍵作用可以穩定短肽序列的螺旋構象。而這種方法目前僅限於很短肽的N-端位置的修飾。我們目前的研究集中在基於共價鍵替換短肽內部螺旋的氫鍵作用，實現新型α-螺旋模擬物的設計和合成。此外針對合成的α-螺旋模擬物的α-螺旋性能和生物活性也將進行深入研究。 這項研究的長期目標是通過分子設計，化學合成和生物評價手段，開發高效螺旋模擬物，調節各種重要的蛋白-蛋白相互作用過程。我們將通過計算化學平台設計新型螺旋類似物，利用可以大量合成的有機化學手段製備和優化結構。新型螺旋類似物的研究成果對合成化學和藥物化學都將有很大的影響。

503213.label: Project Objectives
503213.value: To demonstrate the versatility of the Rh(I)/(III) manifold in designing new cross coupling reactions: For example, other electrophilic reagents such as azodicarboxylates will be investigated for catalytic couplings with aryl/alkylboronic acids and derivatives for synthesis of functionalized aryl/alkyl amines. To extend further the scope of this manifold, we plan to develop the catalytic coupling of O-alkylcarboxyl benzohydroxamic acids with diazoesters for the synthesis of isoindolinones, which are important motifs in natural products and pharmaceuticals. To develop model studies for the Rh(I)/(III) cycle in the catalytic C-N bond coupling reactions: The arylboronic acid amination reactions with O-carboxyl hydroxyamines will be employed as a model reaction; structurally defined rhodium complexes bearing the SXS sulfoxides (X = C or N) will be examined for the catalytic amination reaction. Versatile pincer ligand synthesis will be developed to build a library of ligands with diverse electronic and steric properties. To identify the key intermediates in the catalytic C-N bond coupling reactions: Pincer ligands that stabilize Rh(III) center would be selected for this study. Stoichiometric oxidative addition reactions of O-carboxyl hydroxyamines will be performed, and the corresponding amidorhodium(III) carboxylate complexes would be characterized. The subsequent transmetallation of the amidorhodium(III) carboxylates with arylboronic acids would be examined, and characterization of the arylrhodium(III) amide complexes would be pursued. To examine electrophilic C-H activation of simple hydrocarbons: Based on the pincer ligand scaffold developed in this work, we propose to study the electrophilic C-H activation of arenes with structurally defined amidorhodium(III) and / or -iridium(III) carboxylate complexes. This part of the study aims to establish the plausible reaction pathways for developing non-chelation assisted oxidative C-H amination reactions. Initially, attention will be directed to understand the regioselectivity of the arenes C-H activation; factors including influence of ligand/metal combination and substrate structures will be examined. Catalytic aminations of sp3 C-H bonds by the pincer metal complexes will also be explored.

503213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
503213.value: 碳胺化合物 (特別是芳基胺) 在藥用價值和材料應用方面有著極大的重要性，故此碳–氮 (C–N) 鍵的合成方法在有機化學領域上一直被廣泛研究。過渡金屬催化碳–氫 (C–H) 鍵氧化構建新的化學鍵反應是合成C–N鍵的有效方法之一。我組對此亦進行了大量研究。研究發現，通過鈀(I)–/銠(III)催化C–H鍵與親電性試劑 (例如 N-arylsulfonyloxycarbmates和 N-haloamines) 的交叉隅聯反應能夠有效實現芳基胺之合成。我方利用導向基團輔助方法，以Pd(OAc)2 及 [Cp*Rh(OAc)2] 為催化劑，成功於溫和反應條件下進行邻位C–H鍵的胺化和酰胺化反應。有關實驗顯示，其C–N鍵合成可能是由於金屬–氮賓衍生物所誘發的內圈芳環遷移過程。 鑑於銠(I)及銠(III)配合物具有獨特活性，我組對銠(I)/(III)催化C–N鍵合成反應進行研究，我方期待這催化系統能大大擴展可利用的隅聯試劑。最近我組初步研究顯示 [Cp*Rh(OAc)2] 能夠有效催化氧–乙酰基苯基異羥肟酸和重氮酯的 [4+1] 環加成反應，一步合成異吲哚啉酮類化合物。我方推測此加成反應應該通過1).銠(I)配合物與氮–氧乙酰基單元的氧化加成; 2).銠(III)配合物的苯基環金屬化反應; 3).環銠（III）配合物分子內的卡賓轉移; 4).關鍵的還原消除反應重新產生銠(I)配合物。另外，為了發展更有效的C–N鍵合成反應，我組將對SXS (X = C, N) 含亞配體的鉗型銠化合物進行研究。SXS鉗型配體含有-供體和-受體單元，能夠對銠(I)/(III)配合物在催化反應中起穩定作用。我組將研究上述的鉗型銠化合物於氧–乙酰基苯基異羥肟酸和重氮酯的隅聯反應的活性，及針對其活性表現和潛在限制，設計並優化鉗型配體的結構。 在非導向基團輔助但具選擇性的C–H鍵胺化反應的領域上，我組將利用含鉗型性SXS亞配體的胺基銠(III)/銥(III)化合物進行活性研究。我方將運用H/D同位素交換實驗來評估銠(III)/銥(III)配合物對芳環C–H鍵活化的能力和可能性。此外，我方會進行一系列銠(III)/銥(III)配合物和單取代芳烴化合物 (例如甲苯、苯甲醚、苯乙酮、硝基苯等) 的化學當量反應；當中其選擇性及相對活性的評估會通過產物分析、動力學檢測及計算學分析來進行。上述之研究將會對親電性芳環C–H鍵胺化反應的催化系統設計有極大幫助。 與現今流行的銠(III)催化氧化還原中性胺化反應比較，我方期望銠(I)/(III)催化系統能更有效展現其活性及大大擴展可利用的碳氫底物。通過此研究，我方希望能發展出嶄新的合成法，為可持續多樣性分子合成領域作出貢獻。

503213.label: Realisation of objectives
503213.value: In this project, we have examined some reagents containing N-X (X = halides, pseudohalide leaving groups) and N=N (azo) as coupling partners for transition metal-mediated arylation reactions. Employing structurally defined cyclopentadienylrhodium(III) complexes, we demonstrated effective arylation of azo compounds for C-N bond formation. Employing arylazocarboxylates and diethylazodicarboxylate (DEAD) as reagents, effective coupling of these azo reagents with arylboronic acids has been developed with cyclopentadienylrhodium(III) complex as catalyst. The aryl and diarylhydrazide products can be prepared in 73-99% yields (28 examples) with remarkable functional group tolerance. The molecular structure of 2-(4-methoxyphenyl)-2-phenyl-,1-ethylhydrazinecarboxylic acid ester has been established by single-crystal X-ray crystallography. To examine the involvement of the arylrhodium(III) complexes, [Cp*Rh(Ph)Br(PPh3)] complex was prepared. No N,N-diphenylazocarboxylate formation was detected by treating [Cp*Rh(Ph)Br(PPh3)] (10 mol%) with AgSbF6 (10 mol%) and phenylazocarboxylate (0.5 mmol) in DMF. This finding is inconsistent with the involvement of the arylrhodium(III) intermediate for the C–N bond coupling reaction. The versatility of using N-N bond as leaving group for C-N coupling reaction has been further explored. In this work, we successful developed the Rh-catalyzed cycloaddition of N-Boc-hydrazones with alkynes, and NH free pyrroles were obtained in good-to-excellent yields. Our study showed that the N-tert-butoxycarbonyl (N-Boc) group is critical for achieving effective pyrrole formation. Notably, using O-acetylhydroxyamine as leaving group, isoquinoline rather than pyrrole was formed as the major product. This reaction is characterized by a formal selective C(sp3)-H bond activation versus C(aryl)-H activation. The selective C(sp3)-H activation has been verified; reacting the deuterium-labeled (at the aryl group) semicarbazone with alkynes under the Rh-catalyzed conditions afforded the desired pyrrole with preservation of all the deuterium labels. In this work, we also examined the use of [Cp*CoI2(CO)] complex as catalyst for arylboronic acids coupling with O-carboxylate hydroxyamines. We began the reaction by treating O-acetylbenzohydroxamic acid (0.2 mmol), p-methoxyphenylboronic acid (0.3 mmol), [Cp*CoI2(CO)] (5 mol%), AgSbF6 (40 mol%) and KOAc (40 mol%) in DCE (1 mL) at 40 °C under an N2 atmosphere for 4 hours afforded benzanilide in 78% yield. Under the Co-catalyzed conditions, arylboronic acids containing electron-releasing and -withdrawing groups (e.g. OMe and halides) afforded the corresponding anilides in 51–78% yields. Other functionalized arylboronic acids bearing TMS, CHO, C(O)Me, CO2Me and vinyl were effectively aminated in excellent yields. Analogous amidation of 2-naphthyl, 6-methoxy-1-naphthyl and styrylboronic acids were accomplished in 54–82% yields. With phenylboronic acid as the arylating reagent, the scope of O-carbonyl hydroxylamines / amides was examined. O-Acetylarylhydroxamic acids bearing electron-releasing and -withdrawing groups (e.g. Me, OMe, Cl and Br) afforded the corresponding anilides in 55–92% yields. Other O-acetyl hydroxamic acids containing tert-butyl, 2-naphthyl and aliphatic carbamates were obtained in 7–72% yields. Facile transformations of some primary amine hydroxamic acid such as O-benzoyl (ethoxycarbonyl)methylhydroxamic acid was also achieved in 99% yield. However, no product was obtained from O-benzoyl morpholinehydroxamic acid. The key intermediates of the Co-catalyzed amidation of arylboronic acids was examined spectroscopically. ESI-MS analysis failed to reveal the formation of any arylcobalt complexes in the reaction mixture. Rather, some reactive amido complexes was characterized. It is postulated that the Co-catalyzed reaction occurs by the initial formation of Cp*Co-O-acetylhydroxamic acid adducts, followed by aryl transmetalation with the organoboron reagents. A major challenge here is to develop non-chelation assisted direction amidation of arenes. In this project, we found that some structurally defined palladium(II) complexes of N-heterocyclic carbene and 2-arylquinolines exhibit effective catalysis on regioselective arene amidations. For instance, employing [Pd(2-phenylquinoline)(OAc)]2 [X-ray crystal structure characterized] as catalyst, phthalimide as nucleophile and PhI(OAc)2 as oxidant, effective amidation of mono, di- and tri-substituted arenes afforded the corresponding N-arylphthalimides in moderate to good yields. In general, the C-H amidation occurred at the less hindered sites. Notably, high-degree of meta-selectivity was observed for arenes bearing electron-withdrawing substituents such as trifluoromethyl group. Preliminary investigation showed that the regioselectivity is directed by both electronic and steric factors of the arenes. In closing, all the objectives set out in this project have been realized.

503213.label: Major findings and research outcome
503213.value: (1) We have developed Cp*Rh-catalyzed electrophilic amination of arylboronic acids using arylazocarboxylates and diethylazodicarboxylates as reagents. The reaction occurs under mild conditions without the need for strongly basic conditions or using highly reactive organometallic reagents. Excellent functional group compatibility was achieved. The mechanism of the C-N coupling step remains unclear. Our mechanistic study revealed that the stoichiometric reaction of arylrhodium(III) complexes with the azo reagents did not afford the expected coupled products. It is postulated that reactive metallaazaziridine complexes could be the active intermediate for the C-N bond formation. This work has been published in Organic Biomolecular Chemistry. (2) We have developed chemoselective N-N sigma-bond cleavage for effective C-N bond coupling reactions. With [Cp*RhCl2]2 as catalyst, semicarbazones derived from acetophenones undergo cycloaddition reactions with alkynes to form NH pyrroles in good yields and selectivity. The cycloaddition is characterized by regioselective C(sp3)-H activation, rather than C(arene)-H activation. Notably, primary and secondary C(sp3)-H bonds react under the Rh-catalyzed conditions to afford the desired pyrroles. We observed that the NHBoc leaving group is critical for the success of the chemoselectivity. For instance, changing NHBoc to NHAc as leaving group, isoquinolines [derived from C(arene)-H activation] was formed almost exclusively (pyrrole : isoquinoline = 1 : 37). Deuterium labelling study revealed that the cycloaddition of the N-Boc semicarbazones with alkynes involves directly C(sp3)-H activation, without C(arene)-H activation. In the presence of AcOD, significant deuteration occurs at the acetophenone methyl group exclusively. A mechanism based on Rh-mediated selective enamide formation was proposed. This work has been published in Advanced Synthesis and Catalysis. (3) Azocarboxylates and O-carboxylate hydroxyamines represent a form of "activated" amines/amides for transition metal catalyzed C-H amidation reactions. In this project, we found that phthalimide undergoes direct coupling with unactivated arenes with a cyclopalladated complex of 2-phenylquinoline as catalyst and PhI(OAc)2 as oxidant. With trifluorotoluene as substrate, the arene amidations can be effected by Pd(OAc)2 alone to give the aryl amides in <20% yield over 8 hours. However, the cyclopalladated complex would catalyse the arene ambition in about 10-fold faster rate. While monoamidation products were obtained, the regioselectivity of the C-N bond formation is influenced by steric and electronic properties of the arenes substrates. Notably, meta-selective ambition was achieved with electron-poor arenes such as trifluorotoluene and ethyl benzoate. Significant primary KIE was observed, indicating that the turnover-limiting step is associated with substantial C-H bond cleavage. A manuscript summarising the results of this study is in preparation.

503213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
503213.value: Being isoelectronic with dioxygen, azocarboxylates are shown to be effective reagents for oxidative amination of arylboronic acids and semicarbazones-alkynes cycloadditions. Our investigation on the use of azocarboxylates as aminating reagents led us to postulate reactive Rh/Co amido complexes as the intermediate for the C-N bond coupling reactions. Thus, we anticipated that azocarboxylates would react with Pd(II) to afford Pd(IV) amid complexes, which would effect C-N bond coupling reactions via C-H bond activation. Our preliminary study showed that reacting arylazocarboxylate with 2-phenylpyridine with a palladacyclic complex of 2-phenylquinoline as catalysts afforded the corresponding C-N coupled product in 45% yield. We are now optimizing the reaction, and we envisioned that a new reaction platform based on azocaboxylates would be developed. Compared to other electrophilic aminating agents, azocarboxylates are more amenable for structural variation and thermally stable. This renders azocarboxylates a convenient reagent for C-H bond amidations. We recently discovered that alpha-aryldiazoacetate would undergo photo-initiated C-N bond coupling with NHPI esters by employing acid red 94 as the photocatalyst under blue LED irradiation. The coupled azo compound was obtained in up to 90% yield. This newly discovered photo C-N coupling reaction would complement the current synthetic arsenal for this important class of compounds.

503213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
503213.value: A central problem in developing synthetically versatile transition metal-catalyzed C-H bond amidation reactions concerns overcoming the N-H bond barrier for the coupling reactions. In this project, we demonstrated that azocarboxylates containing weak N-N pi-bond are viable reagent to effect amination reaction of arylboronic acids using cyclopentadienyl-rhodium(III) and -cobalt(III) complexes as catalyst. The azo coupling reaction can be extended to Cp*Rh(III)-catalyzed cycloaddition of semicarbazones with alkynes leading to pyrrole formation. The cycloaddition is characterised by regioselective activation of aliphatic C-H bonds in the presence of the more reactive aryl C-H bonds. Employing N-Boc leaving group of the semicarbazones is especially critical for the success of the cycloaddition. We also explore reactive palladium amido complex derived from reacting phthalimide with a cyclopalladacyclic complex of 2-phenylquinolines. With an oxidising agent (e.g. PhI(OAc)2), direct amidation of unactivated arenes was achieved. Both electron-rich and -poor arenes react effectively to the N-arylphthalimides in good yields. The regioselectivity is dependent on steric and electronic factors. For instance, anisole reacts to give para-amidation product, whereas benzoate afforded the meta-amidation product. The success of this exploration offers a solid foundation to develop azocarboxylates and derivatives as versatile laminating reagents for transition metal-catalyzed C-N bond coupling reactions.

503313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
503313.value: Direct alcohol acid fuel cell (DAFC), a device that able to convert chemical energy stored in liquid fuel into electrical energy continuously and effectively through electrochemical reaction, is one of the most promising candidate for future portable electronic devices and electric vehicles. Due to the high energy density, high theoretical cell potential, high conversion rate and the fact that alcohols with short carbon chain length are capable to obtain sustainably from fermentation or chemical conversion of plant based biomass, DAFC is now considered to be a green and carbon neutral energy device for the post-petroleum era. However, massive commercialization of DAFC is still hindered by the strong rely on expensive and rare platinum as electrocatalyst. In the light of this, this proposal aims to design facile and up-scalable synthetic routes towards palladium/platinum nanocomposites with coreshell or alloy structure to reduce the platinum usage while enhancing the catalytic activity and lifetime. Recently, an electrocatalyst that composed of carbon nanotubes supported surfactant free palladium nanoparticles coated with a thin layer of palladium/platinum alloys with excellent catalytic activity and lifetime was developed. This palladium/platinum composite can be easily generated with a simple synthetic protocol which is environmental friendly and easily up-scalable. The enhancement is mainly attributed to the formation palladium/platinum alloy which enhances the Pd spatial stability and CO tolerance of Pt. In contrast, a palladium/platinum coreshell nanoparticles was also prepared with highly increased surface area due to the formation of submonolayer of palladium island at the surface of platinum nanoparticles. With these two unique models of alloy and phase separated palladium/platinum metal surface, the mechanism and factors affecting the electrocatalysis towards alcohol oxidation will be investigated. A systematic study on the synthetic conditions and the corresponding effects on the catalytic properties will also be done. Apart from the catalyst itself, the effect of replacing the commonly used carbon support with nanosized metal oxides will also be studied. We believe that by introducing the nanosized metal oxides as support electrodes, it will enhance the stability and the ions exchange rate of the electrode in either acidic or basic electrolyte will be increased. It also opens up the possibility for the investigation on the development on photo-assisted DAFC. 甲醇燃料電池是一種能夠連續和有效地將存儲在液體燃料的化學能通過電化學反應轉化為電能的裝置，被認為是未來便攜式電子設備以及電動汽車的電池。由於其能量密度、電壓升和效能高，而且能夠持續地以植物生物質以發酵或化學轉化而獲得甲醇，甲醇燃料電池將成為後石油時代中一種重要的綠色碳中和的能源系統。然而，燃料電池大規模的商業化仍因依賴昂貴和稀有的鉑作電催化劑的阻礙而停滯不前。因此本提案以簡單和可擴展的方法合成鈀/鉑雙金屬納米核殼或合金結構粒子複合材料作電催化劑，以減少鉑的使用的同時提高催化劑的活性和壽命。最近，我們開發出由碳納米管組成的電極催化劑，支持無表面活性劑的鈀納米粒子後再加上一薄層鈀/鉑合金具而製成有優異的催化活性和壽命的催化劑。另外，我們亦製備出高比表面積的鈀/鉑納米核殼材料，在鉑納米粒子的表面上修飾了一亞單層鈀原子島嶼。有了這兩個獨特的合金和相分離鈀/鉑金屬表面模型，我們將能對醇氧化的電催化機制和影響因素進行調查。我們相信，通過引入作為支持電極的納米尺寸的金屬氧化物，將會進一步提高的其綜合穩定性和在酸性或鹼性電解質中的電極的離子交換速率將會增加。此研究將亦開闢光輔助燃料電池的可能性。

503313.label: Realisation of objectives
503313.value: This project mainly aims to develop two different types of specific PtPd mixed metal surface, alloy (Pd@PdPt) and phase separated (Pt@Pd) surface, that affect the activity of electrocatalytic methanol and ethanol oxidation. Synthesis and characterization of Pd@PdPt and Pt@Pd mixed-metal nanostructured electrocatalyst A facile route for the fabrication of for PdPt alloy and phase separated surface has been achieved by adopting the galvanic replacement and our newly developed ion adsorption – in situ reduction methods. For the preparation of the supported Pd@PdPt alloy surface, freshly prepared supported Pd nanoparticles were allowed to stir with Pt salt to undergo galvanic replacement. In contrast, for preparation of the supported Pt@Pd phase separated surface, freshly prepared supported Pt nanoparticles were allowed to stir with Pd halide salt to undergo halide adsorption. The adsorbed PdPt composite was washed with water to remove excess Pd precursors and then reduced either electrochemically by a potentiostat or chemically by reducing agents like NaBH4 or H2. Since the standard reduction potential of [PdCl4]2-/Pd pair (0.62 V vs SHE) is lower than that of [PtCl4]2-/Pt pair (0.758 V vs SHE), no galvanic replacement reaction between Pt and [PdCl4]2- ions takes place. Therefore, Pt@Pd/CNTs composites are suggested to adopt a phase separated state on the surface. We have successfully prepared different loading of the Pt or Pd present on the surface of the nanoparticles for both models in order to design different bimetallic surfaces for later analysis. By simply controlling the concentration of Pt precursor in the galvanic replacement or Pd precursor in the ion adsorption – in situ reduction approach, a series of different core-shell nanoparticles with different Pd to Pt ratio can be prepared. All these carbon nanotubes supported nanoparticles are having sizes ranged from 2.9 to 3.5 nm and adopting an fcc structure as suggested in the SEM, TEM and XRD analysis. With a similar total metal loading ranged from 11 to 19 wt%, this group of composite materials forms a reliable model for the surface packing comparison. Five different composites nanoparticles are prepared namely Pd@PdPt/CNTs-1, Pd@PdPt/CNTs-2, Pt@Pd/CNTs-1, Pt@Pd/CNTs-2 and Pt@Pd/CNTs-3 with XPS determined Pd-to-Pt surface ratio of 1.3 : 1, 2.2 : 1, 1 : 7.2, 1 : 2.3 and 1 : 1.5 respectively. The PdPt alloy formation was confirmed by the shift of binding energy of Pd 3d and Pt 4f peaks in the XPS. The Pd 3d peaks of Pd@PdPt/CNTs composites are positively shifted when compared with Pd 3d peaks of Pd/CNTs composite while the Pt 4f peaks of Pd@PdPt/CNTs composites are negatively shifted when compared with the Pt 4f region of Pt/CNTs composite. The negatively shifted Pt 4f peaks and the positively shifted Pd 3d peaks suggests the electron transfer from Pd to Pt at close proximity confirm the PdPt alloy formation. In contrast, Pd 3d peaks of Pt@Pd/CNTs composite are more positively shifted when compared with the Pd 3d peaks of Pd/CNTs and Pd@PdPt/CNTs composite which may suggest a different packing of Pd atoms have resulted. The CV analysis of the five different nanoparticles shown that the reduction of the corresponding Pt and Pd oxide peaks were significantly shifted from the original potential which demonstrated the success in yielding a bimetallic surface. The peak potential of all five composites is lower than the pure Pt/CNT and Pd/CNT standard which suggest that a different electrocatalytic activity is yielded upon the formation of these bimetallic surfaces. Meanwhile, the stability of the bimetallic surfaces was analyzed by the accelerated durability test through the repetitive CV analysis of the support nanoparticles to investigate their change in electrochemical active surface (ECAS). All five types of nanoparticles shown a significant depletion in the ECAS due to their surfactant free nature. A larger loss of ECAS was observed in both Pt@Pd/CNTs-1, Pt@Pd/CNTs-2 and Pt@Pd/CNTs-3 as the core of these particles are Pt metal which is normally found to be less stable in repetitive CV analysis due to leaching. While for Pd@PdPt types of particles, the Pd core showed a much higher stability which tends to retain the high ECAS of such nanoparticles. Electrochemical catalytic studies towards methanol and ethanol oxidation of Pd@PdPt and Pt@Pd mixed-metal nanostructured electrocatalyst The Pd@PdPt/CNTs catalyst displayed excellent electrochemical performance towards methanol oxidation. The specific mass activity at 0.55V on Pd@PdPt/CNTs-1 (400.2 mAmg-1) is 2.8 times of that of commercial available Pt/C (142.8 mAmg-1). Moreover, a close look at the onset potential for the methanol oxidation revealed that a negative shift of around 40mV for the Pd@PdPt/CNTs (ca. 0.117V) as compared to that of Pt/C. The enhanced electrocatalytic activity of the Pd@PdPt/CNTs could be ascribed to the synergistic effect caused by the formation of PdPt alloy. The PdPt alloy had a modified electronic structure as compared to its monometallic counterparts; thereby improvement of electrocatalytic properties resulted. It also demonstrated a high stability in the chronoamperometric study. As compare with the alloy-based catalyst, the phased separated catalysts show a significantly higher catalytic activity. It may due to the fact that the oxidation of methanol requires at least three ensemble Pt atoms for effective oxidation. For ethanol oxidation reaction, both Pd@PdPt catalysts show higher catalytic activity than monometallic Pd/CNTs and Pt/CNTs composites. The high catalytic activity of Pd@PdPt/CNTs-1 composite (5.00 mAcm-2) towards the oxidation of ethanol can be attributed to the synergistic effect due to alloy formation. In contrast, the catalytic activities of three Pt@Pd/CNTs composites are less enhanced when compared with Pd@PdPt composite. The specific area activity increases from 2.10 mAcm-2 to 2.60 mAcm-2 and then decreases to 1.94 mAcm-2 when the Pd-to-Pt surface ratio increase from 1: 7.2 to 1: 2.3 and then to 1: 1.5. With a comparable Pd-to-Pt surface ratio, Pd@PdPt/CNTs-1 composite (1.3: 1) exhibits a more superior performance than Pt@Pd/CNTs-3 composite (1: 1.5) because a better mixing PdPt alloy surface contributes stronger synergistic effect. For Pt@Pd/CNTs-3 composite, due to the adsorption of Pd onto Pt surface, fewer Pt active sites are exposed to ethanol. This different catalytic activity further indirectly confirms that the two modified catalysts have different arrangements, resulting in different catalytic activity.

503313.label: Major findings and research outcome
503313.value: A facile route to surfactant-free monometallic Pd/CNTs and Pt/CNTs composites were successfully developed respectively. Pd/CNTs composite was synthesized by hydrolysis of [PdCl4]2- ions on MWCNTs to form PdO nanoparticles followed by H2 reduction. Pt/CNTs composite was synthesized by the spontaneous reduction of [PtCl4]2- ions to Pt metal due to the electron transfer from MWCNTs in neutral aqueous solution without the need of other reducing agents. Since no surfactant is used, it provides a clean metal surface for later modification with metal precursor. A series of PdPt composite with well-controlled Pd-to-Pt ratio were synthesized two simple and up-scalable routes. The Pd@PdPt/CNTs composites were synthesized by the galvanic replacement between Pd and [PtCl4]2- ions. While Pt@Pd/CNTs composites were prepared by adsorption of [PdCl4]2- ions onto Pt surface, followed by H2 reduction. The morphology and size of the resultant materials were well characterized by HRSEM and TEM. XRD analysis shows that both Pd@PdPt/CNTs and Pt@Pd/CNTs composites adopt an fcc structure. The elemental ratio of Pd and Pt were determined by ICP-MS, EDX, and XPS. A manuscript on this part has been submitted to Nano Research. The electrochemical properties of the Pd@PdPt/CNTs and Pt@Pd/CNTs composites were characterized by CV, LSV, chronoamperometric analysis and ADT for their electrochemical activity and stability. Together with the finding from XPS, these suggest the successful preparation of the alloy and phase separated PdPt model. The electrocatalytic study of methanol and ethanol oxidation reveals that both bimetallic surfaces show comparable catalytic activities with the Pt/CNT. Amount all five composites, Pd@PdPt/CNTs-1 shows the highest activity towards both methanol than and ethanol oxidation. The stability study towards methanol and ethanol oxidation also reviews that the alloy surface performs better as compared to the phase separated counterpart. We proposed that it is due to the synergistic effect of PdPt works better when the Pd and Pt stay close together. A manuscript for this part is under submission to Nanoscale. For the photo assist oxidation exploration, due to the lack of anchoring site on the surface of the ZnO, the decoration of Pd or Pt is not very successful. Meanwhile, a parallel synthesis of gold nanoparticles attached to the Fe doped ZnO nanostars has been done to investigate the possibility in using co-reduction approach to yield the required composite material and fine tuning of the wavelength absorbed by the metal oxide. It has been published in Journal of Nanomaterials.

503313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
503313.value: Considering the precise control of Pd@PtPd composite with such simple synthetic protocol, we would like to extend the current scope of Pt/Pd mixed metal system to trimetallic systems like Pt/Au/Pd, Pt/Pd/Ru or Pt/Pd/Rh using their corresponding halide salt as the precursor. With the precise control on the formation Pd@PtPd as a core, a third metal can be introduced either through galvanic replacement or ion adsorption – in situ reduction approach. In order to pinpoint the surface structure, we would like to collaborate with atom probe facility in Oxford University to investigate the possibility in direct observation of the trimetallic layer so that a deeper understanding in the geometry and chemical composition can be achieved. For the electrocatalytic study of ethanol oxidation, we would like to further investigate how this exactly the alloy and phase separated PtPd mixed metal surface catalyze the reaction. We would try to incorporate in-situ IR and Raman spectroscopy to study the mechanism involved in such reaction. Currently, we already contact Prof. SG Sun at Xiamen University for collaboration on their facility in in-situ IR and Raman spectroscopy for investigation of this reaction.

503313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
503313.value: We successfully developed a unique approach to developing two carbon nanotubes supported platinum palladium based bimetallic catalysts, Pd@PdPt/CNTs alloy and Pt@Pd/CNTs phase-separate catalysts, using the surfactant-free monometallic Pd/CNTs and Pt/CNTs respectively as the template without using any organic surfactants. Pd@PdPt/CNTs was prepared under the galvanic replacement reaction between platinum halides ions and Pd nanoparticles. Pt@Pd/CNTs was prepared by the adsorption of palladium halide ions onto Pt surface followed by hydrogen reduction. The electrochemical studies show that Pd@PdPt/CNTs and Pt@Pd/CNTs exhibit enhanced catalytic activity towards the oxidation of methanol and ethanol when compared with Pd/CNTs and Pt/CNTs. Our study also demonstrates the surface packing of the platinum and palladium are important as the alloy surface packing mode results in higher catalytic activity and stability as compare with the phase separated counterpart. We proposed that for the platinum and palladium to work synergistically, they have to sit near to each other on the surface which is the alloy surface model. Due to its simple preparation and high activity, this composite material shows high potential towards large-scale preparation as commercial fuel cell catalyst.

503513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
503513.value: This application proposes a class of novel structured selection and estimation methods in high-dimensional models when there are natural structures in the parameter space. Analysis of high-dimensional data presents new and challenging theoretical and computational questions in statistics. Standard methods assuming the number of variables is fixed and much smaller than the sample size are not applicable to high-dimensional models. The existing variable selection methods are developed for models with a known structure. The proposed project is expected to stimulate new research directions for studying several important statistical modeling and analysis problems, which include structure estimation and variable selection in semiparametric additive models, survival analysis models and panel count data models in high-dimensional settings where the number of variables is larger than the sample size. Theoretical properties of the proposed methods in high-dimensional settings and computational algorithms will be developed. The proposed methods are expected to be able to correctly select the important groups and correctly estimate model structures with high probability in sparse, high-dimensional settings. Simulation studies will be conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed methods in different settings. The proposed methods will be applied to real high-dimensional data sets to illustrate their applications. The proposed project will yield new methods for the analysis of genomic data sets with censored survival outcome data. 本項目針對在參數空間具有自然的結構的高維模型提出一類新的結構選擇和估計方法. 高維數據分析提出了新的和具有挑戰性的統計理論和計算問題. 標準方法假設變量的數目是固定的並遠小於樣本大小, 是不適用高維模型的. 現有的變量選擇方法假設模型的結構是已知的. 擬建項目預期將激勵新的研究方向, 研究一些重要的統計建模和分析問題, 其中包括高維情況下的半參數加性模型, 生存分析模型和麵板計數數據模型的結構估計和變量選擇. 在高維情況下所提出的方法的理論性質和計算算法將得到發展. 預期所提出的方法能夠正確地選擇重要群體, 並正確估計模型結構. 為評估所提出的方法在不同情況下的表現, 模擬研究將被進行. 為說明所提出的方法, 他們將被應用到真正的高維數據集的分析. 擬建項目將為刪失生存結果的基因數據集提供新的分析方法.

503513.label: Realisation of objectives
503513.value: We have worked on all five objectives of this project. We have investigated the problem of structured selection and estimation in high-dimensional survival models when there are natural structures in the parameter space. We have proposed a semiparametric pursuit method to simultaneously identify and estimate linear and nonparametric covariate effects through a penalized group selection method with concave penalties. The estimators of the linear effects and the nonparametric component are consistent, the nonlinear effect can be successfully identified with high probability, and the estimated linear regression parameters are asymptotically normal. We have developed a modified blockwise majorization descent (MBMD) algorithm through the backtracking line search approach for model structure identification and estimation. The numerical studies have demonstrated that the proposed group penalized approaches and MBMD algorithm work well. The proposed methods can be extended to other useful models such as accelerate failure time models and additive hazards models. We have considered the multiplicative regression model, and investigated an adaptive variable selection method via a relative error-based criterion and Lasso-type penalty with desired theoretical properties and computational convenience. We have proved that the resultant estimator achieves the oracle property. An alternating direction method of multipliers algorithm is proposed for computing the regularization paths effectively. A data-driven procedure based on the Bayesian information criterion is used to choose the tuning parameters. The finite-sample performance of the proposed method is examined via extensive simulation studies. We have proposed a novel semiparametric joint model for multivariate longitudinal and survival data by relaxing the normality assumption of the longitudinal outcomes, leaving the baseline hazard functions unspecified and allowing the history of the longitudinal response having an effect on the risk of dropout. We have developed a Bayesian Lasso method to simultaneously estimate unknown parameters and select important covariates in the model. We have studied the sieve maximum likelihood estimation for a general class of hazard regression models, which include the proportional hazards model, the accelerated failure time model, and the accelerated hazards model. We have proposed semiparametric efficient estimators for the parameters that are bundled inside the nonparametric component, and established the consistency and asymptotic normality properties of the estimators. The simulation studies have demonstrated its efficiency gain over the conventional estimating equation approach. Also we have proposed a new class of semiparametric mean models that allows for the interaction between the observation history and covariates for panel count data. For inference on the model parameters, a monotone spline-based least squares estimation approach is developed, and the resulting estimators are consistent and asymptotically normal. In particular, our new approach does not rely on the model specification of the observation process. The proposed inference procedure performs well through simulation studies, and it is illustrated by the analysis of bladder tumor data. When the number of covariates involved in survival data is much larger than the sample size, we have developed several fully nonparametric independence screening procedures through different filters, and established their sure screening property with high probability. The proposed novel screening approaches can be used to effectively reduce the number of covariates in ultrahigh-dimensional survival models. In addition, we have studied self-normalized limits and moderate deviations of nonparametric maximum likelihood estimators in the current status model and presented a new procedure to construct asymptotical confidence intervals and asymptotical rejection regions of hypothesis testing for survival functions. The theoretical results can guarantee that the new test has the probability of type II error tending to 0 with exponentially decay speed. Extensive simulation studies and application results demonstrated that the proposed new methods and computational algorithms perform well. We have achieved all the objectives of this project.

503513.label: Major findings and research outcome
503513.value: For the problem of structure estimation and variable selection in survival models, we have developed penalized group selection methods that are capable of simultaneous identification and estimation of linear and nonlinear covariate effects, while most of the existing methods are designed for a known model structure. We have developed a modified blockwise majorization descent algorithm for structure estimation and variable selection. For the multiplicative regression model, we have developed an adaptive variable selection method through a relative error-based criterion and Lasso-type penalty, and established the oracle property of the resultant estimator. We have also proposed an alternating direction method of multipliers algorithm for effectively computing the regularization paths. For the problem of variable selection and estimation in joint models of longitudinal and survival data, we have proposed a novel semiparametric joint model for multivariate longitudinal and survival data. We have developed a Bayesian Lasso method to simultaneously estimate unknown parameters and select important covariates. The proposed joint modeling approach is more flexible and robust, and thus more applicable. For the problem of variable selection and structure estimation with ultrahigh-dimensional covariates, we have proposed novel nonparametric screening methods using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test statistic, the Buckley-James estimator, and Spearman rank correlation. These new screening methods are robust to model misspecification and enjoys the sure independence screening property under mild regularity conditions. In particular, the Spearman rank correlation-based screening method still works well when a response variable is observed under a high censoring rate. Furthermore, we have developed a two-step model averaging estimation procedure for improving prediction accuracy in high-dimensional survival models. Numerical studies have demonstrated the superior performance of the proposed variable screening and model averaging procedures over existing methods. For nonparametric inference of interval-censored survival data model, we have established the self-normalized Cramer-type moderate deviations and limit distribution theorems for the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator in the current status model, and presented a new procedure to construct asymptotical confidence intervals and asymptotical rejection regions of hypothesis testing for survival functions. The new test has the probability of type II error tending to 0 with exponentially decay speed. Such theoretical properties of the type II error are not generally well-studied for other competing methods. In summary, the ten research papers associated with this project have been published/accepted in international peer-reviewed journals (Annals of Statistics, Biometrics, Bernoulli, Statistica Sinica, Biometrical Journal, Computational Statistics & Data Analysis), and also presented in the international conferences.

503513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
503513.value: (1) Our approaches developed in this project will contribute to better understanding of the genetic basis of diseases, better diagnoses, and better survival prediction. (2) Our developed variable selection and structure estimation methods can be extended to dealing with high-dimensional longitudinal data models. (3) Our developed theory on the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator can be extended to the establishment of uniform convergence theory for constructing simultaneous confidence band of the unknown survival function and global tests.

503513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
503513.value: In this project, we have investigated the problem of variable selection and model structure estimation in high-dimensional survival models arising from survival studies. This research is significant in that it addresses more general situations which often occur in the real world but have not been adequately studied in the literature. A key advantage of our developed approach over existing methods is that it offers simultaneous structure estimation and variable selection. Our new statistical inference procedures are more flexible and more robust, and so more applicable. The results of this project have a significant impact because they have filled the gap in the literature on survival analysis, and are also important to practical applications in biology, economics, engineering, genetics, medicine, and public health. In particular, our new approaches may bring better understanding of covariate effects on the survival time and better survival prediction.

503613.label: Project Objectives
503613.value: To develop and optimize liquid ink with catalytic capability for electroless deposition of metals. The ink consists of delivery matrix polymer, solvent, and catalyst. To modify various flexible, foldable, and stretchable substrates with thin layers of polymer brushes, which can act as receiving matrix for the catalytic ink. To print the catalytic ink by screen printing, inkjet printing, and scanning probe printing onto polymer brush modified substrates with feature size spanning from nanometer to centimeter scales. To deposit metals such as copper, silver, nickel, and gold on the catalyzed areas via electroless deposition with controlled thickness, roughness, and resolution. To study the materials characteristics of the metal patterns, with and without repeating bending, folding, and stretching cycles. These characteristics mainly include electrical conductivity, surface morphology, adhesion, aging, and fatigue. To simulate and understand the mechanical failure of the metal electrodes under repeating bending, folding, and stretching cycles. The simulation results will be used to optimize the structures of metal electrodes including film thickness, substrate modulus, substrate thickness, pattern design of metal electrodes, and encapsulation layer. To fabricate large-area bendable, foldable, and stretchable LED arrays using the as-made metal patterns. The electrical conductivities, I-V-J curves, and the fatigue of the LED arrays and circuits will be studied.

503613.label: Realisation of objectives
503613.value: This project aims to develop metal-based flexible, foldable and stretchable conductors via self-catalytic electroless metal deposition, which are compatible with multi-scale solution-based printing technologies. In summary, all objectives have been achieved.. The detail of realisation of each objective is stated as follows. 1. To develop and optimize liquid ink with catalytic capability for electroless deposition of metals. The ink consists of delivery matrix polymer, solvent, and catalyst. Polymer-assisted metal deposition (PAMD) has been developed to deposit metal electrolessly by self-catalytic process. Anchoring polymers which can be chemically grafted on multiple flexible substrates were employed to immobilize the catalytic moieties. The inks of anchoring polymers or catalytic moieties consists of a solution or a printable paste of polymers/catalytic moieties. Part of this work has been summarized in Advanced Materials (Adv. Mater. 2014, 26, 5508-5516), and the recent progress of polymer inks has also been published in Advanced Materials (Adv. Mater. 2016, 28, 4926–4934). 2. To modify various flexible, foldable, and stretchable substrates with thin layers of polymer brushes, which can act as receiving matrix for the catalytic ink. The anchoring polymers were grafted on multiple flexible substrates via chemical grafting process includes free-radical polymerization and UV-induced cross-linking. A new photoreactive copolymer was designed and synthesized for the UV-induced grafting, which has been proved effective on various flexible substrates such as plastics, elastomers, textiles, and papers. The grafted polymers exhibit good adhesion to substrates while maintaining the flexibility of the substrates. 3. To print the catalytic ink by screen printing, inkjet printing, and scanning probe printing onto polymer brush modified substrates with feature size spanning from nanometer to centimeter scales. Multiple approaches including soft lithography molding, inkjet printing, scanning probe printing and screen printing were employed to print anchoring polymers or catalytic inks. Scanning probe printing and soft lithography molding were used for nano- to micro-scale printing, while inkjet printing and screen printing were employed for micro- to centimeter scale printing. The concentration and viscosity of the inks were optimized to fulfil the request of different printing techniques. 4. To deposit metals such as copper, silver, nickel, and gold on the catalyzed areas via electroless deposition with controlled thickness, roughness, and resolution. The conformal deposition of copper, silver, gold and nickel on the flexible substrates mentioned above has been demonstrated. The thickness of the metal film can be controlled from nanometer scale to several micrometers by adjusting the plating bath concentration and deposition time. Meanwhile, the surface of deposited metal can be very smooth that the root mean square roughness of the deposited metal on flat substrates were confined to <10 nm scale, which meets the request for bottom electrodes of organic solar cells (OSCs) and thin-film transistors (TFTs). In addition, the resolution of deposited metals was high that the obtained metal patterns were consistent with the designed patterns. Typically, the resolution is sub-10 μm for soft lithography molding, sub-100 μm for inkjet printing (with a 80 μm nozzle), and sub-500 μm for screen printing. 5. To study the materials characteristics of the metal patterns, with and without repeating bending, folding, and stretching cycles. These characteristics mainly include electrical conductivity, surface morphology, adhesion, aging, and fatigue. The electrical conductivity and surface morphology of the metal films were studied with and without bending, folding, and stretching test. The metal films exhibited very high initial conductivity (2 × 10-7 S/m for Cu), and such high conductivity almost remained unchanged after repeated stretching at 40% strain on elastomers, or repeated bending/folding on plastic substrates. In the meantime, the surface of the metal films was still intact after the bending, folding or stretching test, which has been proved by AFM or SEM characterization. The adhesion of the metals to substrates was so firm that the metals cannot be peeled-off from the substrate by the scotch tapes. In addition, the conductivity of deposited metals was stable in air. 6. To simulate and understand the mechanical failure of the metal electrodes under repeating bending, folding, and stretching cycles. The simulation results will be used to optimize the structures of metal electrodes including film thickness, substrate modulus, substrate thickness, pattern design of metal electrodes, and encapsulation layer. Finite element simulation was adopted for fully understanding of the mechanism of the metals deposited on 3D sponges during repeated stretching cycles. The simulation suggested an optimum thickness of a few hundred nanometers to a few micrometers for metal electrodes on the 3D sponges to obtain lowest strain on metals during stretching. 7. To fabricate large-area bendable, foldable, and stretchable LED arrays using the as made metal patterns. The electrical conductivities, I-V-J curves, and the fatigue of the LED arrays and circuits will be studied. The stretchable LED arrays were fabricated with the stretchable metal interconnects, and the I-V performance of the LED arrays remained unchanged after repeated stretching at a strain of 30%. Flexible LED arrays were also obtained by the application of biomimetic stretchable transparent electrodes. Apart from this, the metal electrodes fabricated via PAMD were applied to high performance yarn-based supercapacitors (311 F/g) and fully printed TFT arrays with high mechanical flexibility. Part of this work has been published on Advanced Materials Materials (Adv. Mater. 2016, 28, 4926–4934) and Nature Communications. (Nat. Commun. 2015, 6, 7260).

503613.label: Major findings and research outcome
503613.value: The major findings of the project include the development of polymer-assisted metal deposition (PAMD) as a versatile approach for electroless metal deposition on multiple substrates, the flexible and stretchable metal interconnects/electrodes, and their applications for flexible solution-processed organic solar cells (OSCs), supercapacitors and thin-film transistors (TFTs). Major research outcomes include seven peer-reviewed papers, which are published in high-impact journals including Advanced Science (1 paper), Advanced Materials (3 papers), Journal of Materials Chemistry A (1 paper), Nature Communications (1 paper), and Small (1 paper). PI has also been invited to deliver oral and keynote lectures in many international symposiums, conferences, and workshops.

503613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
503613.value: This project develops new chemistry and know-how of making soft and patterned metal conductors on different substrates. Because the metal conductors can be applied as interconnects, contacts, or electrodes of many different kinds of electronic devices such as diodes, resistors, batteries, capacitors, transistors, memory devices, etc. Therefore, we foresee that many soft electronic devices and even soft systems can be fabricated on the basis of this technology in the future. On the other hand, the fundamental materials characteristics can be further studied to understand the nanostructures of the interface between the metal and the soft substrates, including the nanoscale morphology, the distribution of stress/strain, and the optimization of the nanostructures. From a chemical point of view, there are many other suitable polymers, precursor salts and metals should be suitable for the principle developed in the project. Therefore, a third direction can be the enrichment of the chemical family.

503613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
503613.value: Conventional printable metal inks require high temperature melting of nanoparticles, which are not suitable for soft electronics where the substrates and other materials are heat sensitive. As such, the printing inks are limited to noble metals such as gold and silver. Therefore, printing metal conductors with good electrical conductivity, flexibility, adhesion to the substrate, and smoothness has been a critical challenge in the field of flexible electronics. This project addresses this challenge by developing new chemistry and printable materials for making highly flexible, foldable and stretchable metal conductors. In particular, low-cost Cu and Ni based soft conductors are successfully fabricated on a wide variety of soft substrates such as plastic thin films, textiles, and paper, through a bottom-up chemical deposition of the metal at room temperature. This fabrication is compatible with various printing technologies including screen printing, inkjet printing, and scanning probe printing. The electrodes can be used for soft electronics devices such as displays, solar cells, memory devices, and sensors etc. The research outcome has been published in 7 high impact papers and decimated through many international oral presentations.

509113.label: Project Title(Chinese)
509113.value: 吸引排斥趋化性模型的數學研究

509113.label: Project Objectives
509113.value: Substantially improve the existing global regularity results on the attraction-repulsion Keller-Segel (ARKS) model; Investigate the pattern formation of the ARKS model analytically and numerically in the full parameter regimes and discuss its important application; Develop new ideas to establish the existence and nonlinear stability of the traveling wave solutions to the ARKS model; Modify the current ARKS model so that the pattern formation can be generated in a wider parameter regime.

Modify the current ARKS model so that the pattern formation can be generated in a wider parameter regime.

509113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
509113.value: Chemotaxis is the directed movement of cells up/down concentration of a attractive/repulsive chemical concentration gradient. The prototype of chemotaxis models was presented by Kellel and Segel in 1970s, which has increasingly triggered a tremendous amount of works since then. In this project, we shall consider an attraction-repulsions Keller-Segel (ARKS) model proposed in 2003 by different authors to describe the quorum-sensing effects and the aggregation of microglia cells formed in the central nervous system in Alzheimer’s disease. Since this model does not possess Lyapunov functional, the mathematical analysis is drastically increased compared to the classical Keller-Segel model and remains open for quite a while. The first substantial progress on the global regularity of solutions was made recently by the Principle Investigator with his collaborator. In this project, the Principle Investigator will undertake more comprehensive and substantial analysis into this model to gain better understanding of the competing effects between the chemotactic attraction and repulsion, and shed light on the further development of more realistic model. The main purposes of this project consists of four components: (1) improvement of the existing analytical results on the global dynamics of solutions of the ARKS model; (2) study of the pattern formation of the ARKS model and its applications in biology; (3) the existence and nonlinear stability of traveling wave solutions to the ARKS model; (4) Amendment of the ARKS model to fill the existing gap. Our results reveal that the combination of attraction and repulsion in chemotaxis can induce the time-periodic patterns and traveling waves that cannot be produced by the classical Keller-Segel model in which the attraction and repulsion are considered separately. 趋化性指的是細胞沿著化學物質梯度方嚮的運動。自從Keller和Segel在二十世紀七十年代提出趋化性的數學模型后，大量關於趋化性模型的數學研究得以廣汎地展開。 本項目研究的是在2003年被生物數學家提出的吸引排斥趋化性模型。 這個模型能描述趋化性中的群体感应效應和老年痴呆症患者中樞神經係統中的小神经胶质细胞的聚集現象。相對於經典的Keller-Segel模型，吸引排斥趋化性模型不具備李雅普诺夫范函， 因此數學研究就非常的困難。本項目的主持人和他的合作者在2013年得到了一些關於吸引排斥趋化性模型解的全局光滑性的結果， 這也是第一個關於吸引排斥趋化性模型的數學結果。本項目研究的目的是對吸引排斥趋化性中吸引和排斥的競爭效應做更加深入和係統的數學研究， 從而為模型的進一步發展奠定理論基礎。具體的有四個目標： (1) 改進已存在的關於解的全局動態行為的數學結果； (2) 研究吸引排斥趋化性模型的模式形成以及在生物中的應用；(3) 研究吸引排斥趋化性模型的形波解的存在以及穩定性；（3）進一步發展模型， 填補存在的漏洞。 本項目的研究結果將證實趋化性中吸引和排斥的共同作用將會產生週期和行波軌道解，而經典的趨化性模型不能產生這些結果。

509113.label: Realisation of objectives
509113.value: 1. In the project, the PI systematically and comprehensively exploited the Attraction-Repulsion Keller-Segel system (ARKS) way and got many first-hand results, such as the establishment of competition index of chemotactic attraction and repulsions. This index was identified by the PI with his collaborator Hai-Yang Jin (the former Ph.D of PI) and become a criterion to determine the well-posedness or blow-up of solutions. These results have been published in Journal of Differential Equations (see Publication No. 4 in part C). Further progress has been made and relevant results have been submitted for review (see Publication No. 8 in Part C). The objective 1 has been fully achieved in these two works. 2. Study the global bifurcation and pattern formation for the volume-filling chemotaxis model which is another type Attraction-Repulsion Keller-Segel system by taking into account cell size/volume. The interesting periodic patterns are found and bifurcation processes are detailed (see Publication No. 6 and No. 7 in Part C) and Objective 2 has been fully achieved in these two works. 3. Develop some ideas like variable transformation and shifting methods to establish the existence and stability of traveling waves to an attractive chemotaxis with singular sensitivity. These results are included in Publication No. 1 and No. 3 in Part C) and the Objective 3 has been achieved in these two works. 4. The PI developed a new idea of considering the nonlinear repulsion to modify the classical Attraction-Repulsion Keller-Segel system so that the blow-up of solutions can be avoided and hence relevant pattern formation can be generated to explain the existing experimental findings (aggregative senile plaques) in the Alzheimer’s disease. This result was published in Analysis and Applications (see Publication No. 5 in Part C) wherein the Objective 4 has been fully achieved.

509113.label: Major findings and research outcome
509113.value: The major findings of this project is that we introduce numerous skillful variable transformation in different parameter regimes and identify a so-called competition index that gives a criterion for the dominance of attraction or repulsion in chemotaxis. The sign of this index number critically determines the global dynamics of the Attraction-Repulsion Keller-Segel system. With this finding, the PI together with his collaborators first achieved some results on the qualitative behavior of the Attraction-Repulsion Keller-Segel system and this results have stimulated many works subsequently. This work has been published in the journal `` H. Jin and Z.A. Wang, Boundedness, blowup and critical mass phenomenon in competing chemotaxis, J. Differential Equations, 260:162-196, 2016. Moreover the PI studied the pattern formation of the Attraction-Repulsion Keller-Segel system and found the time-periodic (rippling) pattern at the first time for the chemotaxis system, which qualitatively reproduced the ripping pattern observed in the experiment. Our results showed that classical Keller-Segel system with attraction or repulsion alone can not produce the time-periodic patterns and only three-component chemotaxis model like the Attraction-Repulsion Keller-Segel model can possibly generate the time-periodic patterns. This reveals the unique feature of Attraction-Repulsion chemotaxis model distinguishing other chemotaxis models. These results were published in ``P. Liu, J.P. Shi and Z. Wang, Pattern formation of the attraction-repulsion Keller-Segel system, Discrete Contin. Dyn. Syst-Series B, 18(10): 2597-2625, 2013’’. Through our delicate analysis on the Attraction-Repulsion Keller-Segel system, we found some defects of this model in describing the aggregation patterns and hence modify the model by introducing the nonlinear repulsive response so that the modified model has stronger applications and can generate desired aggregation patterns. These research results have been published in `` H.Y. Jin and Z.A. Wang, A dual-gradient chemotaxis system modeling the spontaneous aggregation of microglia in Alzheimer's disease, Analysis and Applications, 16:307-338, 2018’’.

509113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
509113.value: The publication No.8 in Part C was indeed a further development of our proposed research.

509113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
509113.value: This research project was concentrated on the qualitative analysis and numerical pattern simulations to the attraction-repulsion chemotaxis model where the cell movement are directed by attractive and/or repulsive signals emitted by the cells. This model was proposed to explain the localized aggregates of microglia in Alzheimer's disease (i.e. senile plaques) and hence has important applications. The mathematical studies on this kind model will reveal the mechanism of the formation of senile plaques and identify the strength/weekness of the model and provide useful clues for further development of models. The numerical simulations will help to understand to what extend the model is powerful and what roles of the system parameters will play in the pattern formation.

509213.label: Project Title(Chinese)
509213.value: 求解玻爾茲曼方程的自適應數值方法

509213.label: Project Objectives
509213.value: The mesh adaptation with the first order scheme will be investigated to obtain an efficient mesh-adaptive solver for some 2D problems, such as flow past a cylinder and pressure driven Poiseuille flows. Adaptation of the velocity space will be explored. Some theoretical difficulties will be addressed when coupling the discrete distribution functions with a different number of degrees of freedom, such as the stability and hyperbolicity of the coupled system. Double-adaption numerical method will be developed by coupling the mesh-adaption and the adaption of the velocity discretization. High order schemes will be designed and parallel computing will be implemented. These will significantly speed up our algorithm, and make it possible to perform 3D numerical simulations such as 3D cavity flow.

509213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
509213.value: This project focuses on a self-adaptive numerical method for solving the Boltzmann equation, which is the fundamental governing equation in kinetic theory. Since the solution of the Boltzmann equation is a seven-dimensional function, it is meaningful to reduce the computational cost by adaptive algorithms. This is the motivation of the PI's research. The main trust of this project is the contribution of efficient numerical schemes for the solution of the Boltzmann equation. The PI will concentrate on a “double-adaption” strategy for the Boltzmann solver, which means that both the spatial discretization and the velocity discretization will be adapted. The indicators instructing the grid variation and various coupling problems during the adaptation will be considered, to make the whole numerical scheme consistent and efficient. The resulting numerical scheme will be fully conservative. Additionally, high order numerical schemes will be developed to further explore the efficiency of the numerical method. Our purpose is to set up a mathematical simulation platform eventually leading to a better understanding of many challenging theoretical and computational issues relevant to the Boltzmann equation. 本項目主要研究求解動力學理論中的基本方程--玻爾茲曼方程的自適應數值方法。因為玻爾茲曼方程的解是一個七維函數,所以運用自適應算法減少計算中的花費十分必要。這驅動了申請人對此項目的研究。 本項目將在發展求解玻爾茲曼的高效數值格式上有所貢獻。申請人將著力研究玻爾茲曼方程數值求解器的“雙重自適應”方法。此方法不僅在空間離散上運用自適應，在速度離散上也要同時自適應處理。為了整體數值格式的一致性和有效性，項目將研究指導網格變化的指示子函數和自適應處理中的各種耦合問題。我們得到的數值格式將是完全守恒的。同時，我們還將發展高階數值格式來進一步提高項目中發展的數值方法的效率。此項目的研究目標是建立一個玻爾茲曼方程的數值模擬平臺，從而進一步深入研究其中廣泛存在的具有挑戰性的理論和計算問題。

509213.label: Realisation of objectives
509213.value: The objectives of this project have been achieved successfully. Under the support of this GRF grant, we have studied globally hyperbolic high-order moment models derived recently from the Boltzmann equation. By using the lower-order model correction, a novel nonlinear multi-level moment solver is developed for micro-flow simulations. Then, a moment-dependent relaxation time is proposed. The resulting models could produce macroscopic quantities of interest with a high-order convergence to those of the underlying Boltzmann equation as the involved moments increase. Finally, we use the the globally hyperbolic moment method to study Kramers' problem. The analytical solutions for the defect velocity and slip coefficient have been obtained for arbitrary order moment equations. Our method can accurately capture the Knudsen layer velocity profile over a wide range of accommodation coefficients, especially for the small accommodation coefficients case.

509213.label: Major findings and research outcome
509213.value: 1. To study the micro-flow problem, the high-order moment models have been derived from the steady-state Boltzmann equation with BGK-type collision term. By using the lower-order model correction, a novel nonlinear multi-level moment solver is developed. This solver improves the convergence significantly, and thus is able to accelerate the steady-state computation greatly. Please refer to the following paper for detail: Zhicheng Hu, Ruo Li and Zhonghua Qiao, Acceleration for microflow simulations of high-order moment models by using lower-order model correction, Journal of Computational Physics, 327(2016), pp. 225–244. 2. Through a relaxation time approximation of the scattering term, extended hydrodynamic models for carrier transport are derived from the semiconductor Boltzmann equation. A formula is proposed to determine the relaxation time for each moment equation, which sets different relaxation rates for different moments such that higher moments damp faster. A multi-grid solver is developed for the derived moment models to further improve the efficiency of the simulation. Please refer to the following paper for detail: Zhicheng Hu, Ruo Li and Zhonghua Qiao, Extended Hydrodynamic Models and Multigrid Solver of a Silicon Diode Simulation, Commun. Comput. Phys., 20 (2016), pp. 551-582. 3. A linearized high order hyperbolic moment system is used to model the Knudsen layer in Kramer's problem. The boundary condition is properly reduced from the kinetic boundary condition. For Kramer's problem, the analytical solutions of moment systems are derived. With the order increasing of the moment model, the solutions are approaching to the solution of the linearized BGK kinetic equation. The velocity profile in the Knudsen layer is captured with improved accuracy for a wide range of accommodation coefficients. Please refer to the following paper for detail: Yuwei Fan, Jun Li, Ruo Li and Zhonghua Qiao, Resolving Knudsen Layer by High Order Moment Expansion, submitted and under review, 2017. 4. The MMC-TDGL equation, a stochastic Cahn-Hilliard equation with a variable interface parameter is studied for multi-phase flow problems. A convex splitting scheme is developed to solve this equation efficiently. An adaptive time stepping strategy is employed for the long time simulation. See reference: Xiao Li, Zhonghua Qiao and Hui Zhang, An unconditionally energy stable finite difference scheme for a stochastic Cahn‐Hilliard equation, SCIENCE CHINA Mathematics, 59 (2016), pp. 1815–1834.

509213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
509213.value: The further development of this research is to solve micro-flow problems modeled by the steady-state Boltzmann equation with other types of collision terms, by using the developed multi-level moment solver. The high-order globally hyperbolic moment systems and their boundary conditions will be further studied for temperature jump problems and thermal creep problems based on the study on the Kramers' problem.

509213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
509213.value: In this research, the high-order globally hyperbolic moment method is employed to study the Boltzmann equation. The main trust of this project is the contribution of efficient numerical schemes for the solution of the Boltzmann equation. Adaptive multi-level moment solver is developed. High order relaxation time schemes have been proposed. The boundary layer problem, which needs a much refined mesh, has been studied with adaptive algorithm of moments increasing accordingly. With the developed adaptive and efficient numerical methods, we may be able to investigate other micro-flow problems, temperature jump problems and thermal crap problems. We could further apply our method to study multi-phase flow problems.

509413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
509413.value: 很多主流的經濟學家均認為2007-2008年的那場金融風暴是自20世紀30年代的大蕭條以來最嚴重的金融危機， 很多公司在這場風暴中倒閉股市低迷， 於是人們開展了眾多關於危機的根源與現存因素（統計上叫做協變量）的金融/經濟分析。回歸分析是探索因變量和被影響變量（統計上叫做相應變量）之間因果關係的基本統計工具。在絕大部分的統計理論和建模中，主流的方法是基於絕對誤差。然而，在許多實際應用中，相對誤差（而不是誤差本身的大小）是人們主要關注的。例如，在一些股票數據的回歸分析，比較不同股票的股價一般是沒有太大意義的，尤其是當某些股票出現和股或者分股的時候。換句話說，不同的股票有不同的單位市值，這個時候沒有考慮異質性基於絕對誤差的統計方法是不能直接適用的。 該項目將主要探索基於相對誤差為的估計和模型選擇統計方法。線性回歸模型可以算是最古老和最廣泛使用的統計回歸模型。線性回歸模型通過對數變化可以轉換成乘法回歸模型，或叫加速失效時間模型， 該模型對分析正的相應變量數據非常有效，比如壽命或者股票價格等， 而人們關心相對誤差往往是相應變量是正的時候。在現代統計科學和現代計算技術快速發展的基礎上，建立新的基於相對誤差的統計方法是及時和有意義的，這個項目的研究成果將提供有效的統計方法幫助和指導人們更好地了解事件發生的內在機制。鑑於線性模型或加速失效時間模型的重要性和普遍性，該研究項目具有深遠和根本的影響。

509413.label: Realisation of objectives
509413.value: The PI and her coauthors have delivered a number of publications to achieve the objectives in this proposed research. First, for the multiplicative regression model, the PI and her student investigated an adaptive variable selection method via a relative error-based criterion and Lasso-type penalty with desired theoretical properties and computational convenience in Hao, Lin and Zhao (2016). With fixed or diverging number of variables in regression model, the resultant estimator achieves the oracle property. An alternating direction method of multipliers algorithm is proposed for computing the regularization paths effectively. A data-driven procedure based on the Bayesian information criterion is used to choose the tuning parameter. The finite-sample performance of the proposed method is examined via simulation studies. An application is illustrated with an analysis of one period of stock returns in Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Direct extension of the relative error-based regression to group variable selection was studied in Liu, Lin and Wang (2016). The proposed group variable selection method has examined to have better performance to detect effective groups compared to some existing methods based on absolute error criteria, for example, the least squares and the least absolute deviation. Application of the method is illustrated with the body fat and the birth weight datasets. The two publications have addressed objectives 2,3 and 5. Next, in the exploration of possible extension of the relative error-based method to other regression model (objective 4), the PI’s another publication Wang, Liu and Lin (2016) addressed a popular change-point problem in relative-error regression. In particular, a nonparametric relative error-based method is proposed to detect and estimate the change point for the multiplicative regression models. The asymptotic distribution of the proposed test statistic for no change-point effect is established. We prove the n-consistency of the proposed estimator of the change point. Simulation studies demonstrate that change-point detection and estimation with relative errors perform reasonably well in many practical situations. We illustrate the method with a financial dataset. Third, the PI has got some new finding during the exploration to achieve objective 1 and 4 in analysing censored data. We observed that a relative error-based method is not very robust in the analysis of right censored data, both theoretically and numerically. To pursue robust statistical procedure, the PI and her co-authors consider a more general class of transformation models with random effects, in which an unknown monotonic transformation of the response is linearly related to the covariates and the random effects with unspecified error and random effect distributions. This includes many popular models. We propose an estimator based on the maximum rank correlation, which relies on symmetry of the random effect distribution, and establish its consistency and asymptotic normality. A random weighting resampling scheme is employed for inference. The proposed method can be easily adapted to censored and clustered data. Numerical studies demonstrate that the proposed method performs well in practical situations. Application of the method is illustrated with the Framingham cholesterol data. Moreover, we have investigated robust model-free variable screening methods in analyzing high dimensional survival data in Lin et al (2017) and Hao, Lin, Liu and Tang (2018). Last but not least, in the pursuit of the main objectives in the proposed research, the PI has published several papers related to biased sampling design and nonparametric inference of right censored data. Different from the relative error-based regression that are mostly parametric or semiparametric approaches, the PI has successfully applied a nonparametric or distribution-free rank estimation to general transformation models in the regression of response-biased sampling. With unknown error distribution, the transformation models are broad enough to cover linear regression models, Cox's model, and the proportional odds model as special cases. To the best of our knowledge, except for the case-control logistic regression, there is presently no prospective estimation approach that can work for biased sampling without modification. We prove that the maximum rank correlation estimation is valid and can be directly applied to response-selective sampling and establish its consistency and asymptotic normality. We propose an inference procedure using random weighting to avoid the complication of density estimation when using the plug-in rule for variance estimation. Extensive numerical studies with supportive evidence are presented an application is illustrated with the Forbes Global 2000 data. On the other hand, Hao, Lin and Zhao (2018) introduces a penalized nonparametric maximum likelihood estimation of the log-hazard function in analyzing right censored data. The smoothing splines are employed for a smooth estimation. Our main discovery is a functional Bahadur representation, which serves as a key tool for nonparametric inference of an unknown function. Asymptotic properties of the resulting smoothing spline estimator of the unknown log-hazard function are established under regularity conditions. Moreover, the local confidence interval of the unknown log-hazard function are provided, as well as the local and global likelihood ratio tests.

509413.label: Major findings and research outcome
509413.value: To summarize, the main finding of this research are mostly two new relative error-based variable selection and group variable selection methods, which have been examined to have better performance to detect effective groups compared to some existing methods based on absolute error criteria, for example, the least squares and the least absolute deviation. As extension of the proposed methods, a nonparametric relative error-based method is proposed to detect and estimate the change point for the multiplicative regression models. In the analysis of right censored data in objective 1, PI and her coauthors have new findings in the pursuit of robust estimation:1. a robust rank estimation for general class of transformation models with random effects was proposed and can be easily applied to censored data and clustered data; 2. a new penalized nonparametric maximum likelihood estimation of the log-hazard function in analyzing right censored data was studied. We believe the outcome of this research is significant and is of theoretical and practical values.

509413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
509413.value: We believe the idea of relative error estimation can be applied to many other places for example, for analysis of categorial data. In categorial analysis, a category with larger percentage of observations may require more accuracy of prediction in term of absolute error. This is precisely where relative error-based methodology is most useful. We shall also consider relative error-based methods in high dimensional post-selection problems. For high dimensional models (not restrictive to linear model or multiplicative models, it would be interesting to find some reasonable relative error-based estimation and inference criteria, study their theoretical problems and examine the numerical performance via extensive simulation studies. We shall definitely work along these directions and hope to find new regression methods that are useful to practitioners.

509413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
509413.value: Overall, we think the outputs of this project are sufficient and all objectives have been addressed and achieved, which might help practitioners and researchers better understand the intrinsic relationships and identify significant important variables. We are fortune to have the timely support from RGC, without which everything would not have been possible.
