509513.value: 由于传统能源的严重短缺和大规模使用矿物燃料所引发的全球变暖问题，发展可再生的清洁能源成为当务之急。利用太阳能有效产生化学燃料和电能是其中一个最有前景且可持续的解决方案之一。比如，通过光催化裂解水进行太阳能制氢就是一种从太阳光中捕获能量并将其转化成清洁能源的有效途径。另一方面，环境治理和水净化逐渐成为全世界所关注的紧急问题。光催化分解气态和液态有机污染物是其中一个极具前景且低成本的解决方案。二氧化钛和氧化锌等半导体材料经常被用作光催化剂来触发这些具体应用中的化学转化过程。然而，这些半导体有很多缺点，包括高能光吸收边缘，较低的光吸收效率和较短的载流子寿命。传统半导体光催化剂的这些缺点严重地限制了它们的光催化效率和之前所提到的应用中太阳光的使用效率。因此，为了增强光催化效率，我们必须提出全新的设计概念并合成新的材料体系。 本建议研究的整体目标是设计基于等离激元金属/半导体杂化纳米结构的新型光催化剂，使之同时具有宽光谱带吸收和有效的电子-空穴分离特性。这些杂化光催化剂将具有增强的光化学活性；其潜在机理包括利用局域表面等离激元光敏化宽带隙半导体，利用等离激元天线效应增强半导体吸收，从等离激元纳米结构传输光子到半导体以及局域加热效应。实现这种杂化光催化剂的关键挑战是设计与合成具有宽光谱带响应的等离激元金属纳米结构，并将其与具有光催化特性的半导体集成起来。与之前研究完全不同的是，本建议研究将会在单粒子级别上表征这些杂化结构的基本光学与光电特性；我们的目标是提供一个完整的图景来理解所包含的物理机理和优化光吸收及电子-空穴分离效率。作为概念验证实验，我们将会使用合成的杂化纳米结构进行光催化水裂解和有机物分解。本研究也会对很多其它更为普遍的催化反应具有指导意义，比如乙烯部分氧化成环氧乙烷，一氧化碳氧化成二氧化碳和氨气选择性氧化成氮气。

509513.label: Realisation of objectives
509513.value: We achieved the proposed project objectives by undertaking the planned research activities, with details discussed in the following. (1) We successfully carried out theoretical design and numerical calculation of several plasmonic metal-semiconductor hybrid nanostructures and predicted their near-field and far-field optical properties. Specifically, using the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method we understood the physical mechanisms responsible for the enhanced photocatalytic efficiency and surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) response in an array of TiO2-coated silver nanowires (Applied Surface Science 301, 351-357, 2014). The calculated extinction cross section and electric near-field intensity and localization well explained the enhanced light harvesting capability of the hybrid photocatalyst and its strong SERS response. The FDTD methods was also applied to theoretically interpret the surface plasmon polariton cross-coupling enhanced photoluminescence from an insulator-metal-capped rough ZnO film (the other semiconductor photocatalyst proposed in this project) which modeled the radiation power of a dipolar emitter underneath a metal film with varied surface roughness (ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 7, 23496-23500, 2015). Objective achieved. As mentioned in the mid-term report, careful evaluation made us realize that the conformal transformation optics approach initially proposed for the project seemed unsuitable for designing broadband plasmonic photocatalysts because of its intrinsic limitation - which can only be used to analytically calculate the optical properties of metal nanostructures without semiconductor coatings or design metal nanostructures with structural singularities (but apparently those singular nanostructures would not be good candidates for practical applications). As a result, in this project we mainly relied on two electromagnetic simulation codes (FDTD and finite-element method) in designing novel hybrid metal-semiconductor photocatalysts and calculating their optical properties as described above. It turned out that full-wave electromagnetic simulations were even more powerful than the conformal transformation optics approach because the simulation codes can fully take into account the size, shape and material dependence of the plasmonic response of hybrid nanostructures. (2) We developed several protocols of solution-based large-amount self-assembly techniques for large-area fabrication of novel plasmonic metal-semiconductor hybrid photocatalysts. Specifically, we developed a modified wet chemistry method to synthesize in solution a bi-functional Au@Pt core-shell nanostructure with controllable surface density of sub-5 nm Pt nanoparticles on the surface of Au nanorods (Nanoscale 6, 9063-9070, 2014). By optimizing the surface coverage of Pt nanoparticles, we were able to achieve simultaneous catalytic activity and SERS response, which consequently enabled in situ real-time monitoring of the catalytic reaction dynamics by ultrasensitive SERS spectroscopy. We also combined magnetron sputtering deposition of thin gold film, spin-coating of TiO2 layer and post-annealing of another thin gold film atop to produce a large-area, low-cost plasmonic black absorber which exhibits significant plasmon-enhanced photocurrent response under visible light illumination (Adv. Optical Mater. 5, 1600399, 2017). Recently, we combined thermal evaporation of thin gold film with self-assembly of Au/TiO2 dumbbell-shaped nanoparticles atop to fabricate a plasmonic particle-on-film nanocavity that demonstrates excellent visible-light-driven hot-carrier generation. The extracted plasmon-decay-induced hot electrons ultimately participated in the dye-decomposition chemical reaction occurring at the TiO2 surface and accelerated the reaction rate by three times (manuscript under review with Advanced Functional Materials). Objective achieved. (3) We assembled an integrated multi-functional microscopic imaging and spectroscopy system for nanoscale measurements. The system was built up based on a conventional bright/dark-field optical microscope with significant modifications for wavelength-dependent, polarization-resolved, angle-dependent single-particle imaging and spectroscopy. It was used to measure the far-field scattering spectrum and radiation pattern of single plasmonic nanostructures in order to thoroughly understand the light harvesting ability of hybrid plasmonic metal-semiconductor photocatalysts. It can also be used to measure the photoluminescence and lifetime of quantum emitters nearby a plasmonic nano-resonator. Objective achieved. (4) Using the above-mentioned multi-functional imaging and spectroscopy system together with other commercially available optical facilities, we systematically investigated the fundamental linear and nonlinear optical and optoelectronic properties of the designed and prepared hybrid nanostructures at the single-particle level. For example, we used the system to observe the polarization-resolved hybrid plasmonic gap modes in metal-film-coupled gold nanosphere monomers and dimers and revealed their physical origins in combination with electromagnetic simulations as discussed in item (1) (Nanoscale 8, 7119-7126, 2016). We further armed the system with the functionality of single-particle photoluminescence spectroscopy along comparison with single-particle scattering imaging and spectroscopy. For example, we used the system to observe the photoluminescence linewidth shrinking and intensity enhancement in the metal-film-coupled gold nanosphere monomers and dimers, and revealed that the photoluminescence response of the coupled nanostructures comes from the plasmon-decay-dominated emission (ACS Nano 11, 3067-3080, 2017), which is closely related to the generation and extraction of plasmonic hot electrons in the proposed metal-semiconductor nano-photocatalysts. Such fundamental understanding of the optical properties of those hybrid nanostructures inspired new designs of a plasmonic gold-film/TiO2-film/gold-nanoparticles black absorber and a Au/TiO2-nanodumbbell-on-film nanocavity based photocatalyst, with their photocurrent response and photocatalytic performance discussed in the following item. The wavelength-dependent photocurrent response of those hybrid photocatalysts were measured with a home-assembled photo-electrochemical cell system with which the incident wavelength can be selected and the photocurrent density measurement can be down to 10-8 A/cm2. Objective achieved. (5) We constructed an optofluidic reactor and performed organic decomposition experiments. Firstly, we experimentally demonstrated that the decomposition rates of two typical organic dyes, R6G and methanol blue (MB) were dramatically accelerated in the presence of the plasmonic photocatalyst made of TiO2-coated silver nanowires in comparison with a pristine TiO2 film under the illumination of <380 nm UV light (Applied Surface Science 301, 351-357, 2014). Secondly, we experimentally demonstrated that the above-mentioned plasmonic black absorber consisting of a 150 nm thick TiO2 layer sandwiched between a layer of random gold nanoparticles and a 200 nm thick rough gold film had an enhanced photocurrent generation under the illumination of 400-900 nm visible light, up to 20-fold enhancement as compared to that of a bare TiO2 film of the same thickness (Adv. Optical Mater. 5, 1600399, 2017). Finally, we designed and prepared the above-mentioned Au/TiO2-nanodumbbell-on-film nanocavity based photocatalyst which takes advantage of electromagnetic coupling between the gold nano-dumbbell and the underneath gold film to enhance the visible light absorption. The coupled system supports plasmon-mediated generation and transfer of the energetic conduction electrons from gold (both in the nano-dumbbell and the film) to TiO2 through two Au/TiO2 Schottky barriers and consequently participating in the chemical reaction occurring at the TiO2 surface, enhancing the dye decomposition reaction rate by three times (manuscript under review with Advanced Functional Materials). Further decoration of those plasmonic hybrid photocatalysts with sub-5 nm catalytic transition-metal nanoparticles made of platinum or palladium can dramatically enhance their photocatalytic water splitting efficiency for hydrogen generation (manuscript under preparation, beyond the revised project objective). Objective achieved.

509513.label: Major findings and research outcome
509513.value: Major findings and research outcome of this ECS research project are summarized in the following five aspects. (1) We experimentally find that integrating rationally designed plasmonic noble-metal nanostructures (such as gold and silver) with conventional semiconductor photocatalysts (such as TiO2, ZnO and Si) can significantly enhance the light absorption of the hybrid systems both in the ultraviolet (above the band gap energy of the semiconductors) and visible (below the gap energy) regions (refer to research output items 1, 7, 12, 16, 17, 19 and 20 in Part C), which consequently improves their photocatalysis and photovoltaics efficiencies. (2) Comprehensive electromagnetic simulations and far-field extinction spectroscopy reveal that the enhanced above-band-gap light absorption is due to the plasmonic near-field enhancement effect (items 1, 7, 12 and 19) while the increased below-band-gap light absorption is mediated by the visible-light-driven localized surface plasmon resonances in the metal nanostructures (items 16, 17 and 20). (3) Along comparison with optical spectroscopy results, wavelength-dependent photocurrent measurements clearly unravel that the visible-light-driven generation and extraction of plasmon-decay-induced energetically hot electrons, which can emit over a metal-semiconductor Schottky junction and thus migrate to the semiconductor surface, contributes to the enhanced visible-light absorption and consequently improves the visible-light (even near-infrared light) photocatalysis (items 16 and 17) and photovoltaics performance (items 12 and 20). (4) We also find that strongly coupled plasmonic nanostructures such as nanoparticle clusters, particle-on-film nanocavities, core-shell nanostructures, and hierarchical porous metamaterials all exhibit multiple plasmon resonance modes over the whole visible and near-infrared light region through complicated plasmon mode hybridization and near-field coupling (items 2, 5, 6, 10, 11, 13, 14, and 15). It is therefore reasonable to expect that introducing semiconductor materials in the plasmonic near-field hot spots of those metallic nanostructures can produce effective hybrid nano-photocatalysts having strong ultraviolet-visible light harvesting capability. (5) We finally find that capping plasmonic noble-metal nanoparticles made of gold or silver with catalytic transition-metal nanoparticles made of platinum or palladium can produce bi-functional core-satellite superstructures (such as Au@Pt core-shell nanostructures) which exhibit simultaneous catalytic activity and SERS response, which consequently not only accelerate the catalytic reaction rate but also realize in situ real-time monitoring of the reaction dynamics (items 3 and 4). Further integration of such bi-functional Au@Pt core-shell nanostructures with a novel photocatalyst - graphitic carbon nitride nanosheets produce a structurally asymmetric, energetically isotropic hetero-catalyst, which doubles the photocatalytic hydrogen generation rate of pristine carbon nitride (manuscript under preparation).

509513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
509513.value: With the fundamental research results obtained in this ECS research project, we proposed a down-stream, application-oriented research project to the Innovation Technology Commission (ITC, ITF Tier 3) in which we suggested to perform simultaneous surface-enhanced Raman scattering detection and photocatalytic decomposition of trace-level organic pollutants (2015, unfunded). Later on, we established connections with the Water Supplies Department of the Hong Kong SAR and BASF Advanced Chemicals Co., Ltd., which were interested in our proposal on the trace-level detection of heavy metal ions in drinking water with surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (ITF Tier 3, 2017, unfunded). We are planning to carefully modify the unfunded proposals based on the comments provided by ITC and resubmit the proposal in the near future.

509513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
509513.value: Photocatalysis has been considered as an efficient means in energy conversion and environmental remediation. For example, photocatalytic water splitting absorbs the solar light energy and generates a clean energy source – hydrogen; photocatalytic organic decomposition utilizes the sunlight energy to promote the decomposition of gaseous and aqueous organic pollutants, playing a critical role in environment remediation and water purification. Traditional photocatalysts are almost exclusively wide-bandgap semiconductors like TiO2 and ZnO, which can only absorb the UV light (covering only ~5% of the solar spectrum) to create energetic charge carriers for catalyzing oxidation and reduction reactions. Therefore, development of novel photocatalysts capable of absorbing the visible or even near-infrared solar light is particularly important for efficiently utilizing the solar energy in photocatalysis. Through carrying out this ECS project, we have designed several new plasmonic metal-semiconductor hybrid nano-photocatalysts which exhibit optical absorption extended to the visible and near-infrared region. Comprehensive optical spectroscopy and wavelength-dependent photocurrent measurements in combination with electromagnetic numerical simulations have revealed the underlying mechanisms such as photo-sensitization of wide band-gap semiconductors by localized surface plasmons, plasmonic antenna effect increased absorption of semiconductors, and transfer plasmon-decay-induced hot electrons from metal nanostructures to semiconductors, with results published in many top-tier journals.

509813.label: Project Objectives
509813.value: To study the plasmon modes in nanostructures that are effective for enhancing light emission from non-dipole nano-emitters. To predict and demonstrate novel light emission phenomena associated with non-dipole electronic transitions enhanced by plasmon resonances. To improve our limited understanding of high-resolution cathodoluminescence spectra and images from metal nanostructures. To build an intuitive theory for understanding the near-field profile of light emission from non-dipole nano-emitters.

To build an intuitive theory for understanding the near-field profile of light emission from non-dipole nano-emitters.

509813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
509813.value: Plasmonic nanostructures can strongly enhance the rate of light emission from nano-sized quantum emitters and the rate of light scattering by biological molecules, which provide great opportunities for making nano-sized photon source and biosensors of high sensitivity. Although nano-emitters are so small that they are usually modeled as dipole emitters, non-dipole contribution to the emission can be significant when they are very close to plasmonic nanostructures. The near-field profile of the resonant response electromagnetic fields in these nanostructures is crucial for these unconventional phenomena. These non-dipole near-field features of light in the nanoscale may also carry additional classical and quantum information within an ultra-small volume, providing additional degree of freedoms for compact high-speed manipulation of optical signals. In this proposal, we plan to employ an eigen-response theory to understand the light emission from non-dipole nano-emitters near plasmonic nanostructures of arbitrary shapes. Due to the complicated shapes of nanostructures and the frequency-dependent material properties, current research progress in understanding the near-field profile of light emission strongly relies on intense numerical simulations which have very low predictive power. In contrast, our theory separates the complicated geometrical effects from the material properties. Such a theory will provide a very useful guidance on how to design resonant metal nanostructures for controlling non-dipole light emission and scattering at the nanoscale. In addition to the details of near-field profile, our theory will be able to predict the total strength of resonances and quantify the contribution from each individual resonance, which allows us to study the amount of information and energy carried by each plasmon modes. Our theory will also be beneficial to the application of high-resolution cathodoluminescence characterization, which has been widely applied to semi-conductor nanostructures and is recently being extended to metallic nanostructures. We have successfully applied the theory to a few simple examples for dipole emitters. We plan to demonstrate its applications to various useful complex systems that can enhance emission from non-dipole nano-emitters. In order to have better comparison with our predictions with experiments, we will be working closely with the experimental group led by Prof. Nicholas X. Fang of Massachusetts Institute of Technology. They will fabricate samples and verify our predictions experimentally. We will also compare our results with published data. 等離激元納米結構能夠大幅提升納米量子發射源的發光率和生物分子的光散射率，為提高納米光源的發光效率和生物感應器的靈敏度提供了極大的機遇。雖然納米發射器通常被模擬為偶極發射源，但是當它們非常接近等離激元納米結構時，非偶極性的發光會變得極為重要。對於這些非傳統的發光現象，納米結構於共振時的近電磁場有至關重要的影響。這些非偶極子近場使我們能利用極小的空間攜帶額外的經典和量子訊息，以及為高速及緊密的光訊號操控提供更大的自由度。我們計劃利用特徵反應理論來理解位於等離激元納米結構旁的非偶極納米發射源的發光結構。由於複雜的納米結構和頻率相關的材料特性，目前一般對近場發光結構的研究非常依賴酷時的模擬計算，這些計算只有非常低的預測能力。與此相反，我們的理論能將材料特性和複雜的結構效應分開，這種理論將非常有效地幫助我們設計能控制非偶極性發光和光散射的共振金屬納米結構。除了詳細的近場資料，我們的理論亦能夠預測每個單獨的共振對總體反應強度的貢獻，並允許我們量化每個等離子激元模式所攜帶的訊息和能量。我們的理論也將有利於高分辨率的陰極發光特性分析，陰極發光特性分析技術已被廣泛應用於半導體納米結構，最近更被擴展到金屬納米結構的應用。我們已經成功地應用特徵反應理論於幾個簡單的偶極發射例子，我們計劃將此理論應用到各種可以提高非偶極的納米光發射的複雜系統。為了更好地與實驗數據比較，我們將與由美國麻省理工學院的 Nicholas X. 509813.label: Realisation of objectives
509813.value: All objectives have been completely realized. Details are shown in the compiled completion report. Objective 1: The objective has been fully realized. Various plasmon modes in nanostructures have been studied using the proposed eigen-response theory described on page 10 of the proposal. We first continued on our preliminary study of the dark anti-phase modes as shown in Fig. 1 of the original proposal. We found that such modes are effective in enhancing the light emission of a nano-emitter composed of an electron-beam. These preliminary results were finally published after our submission of proposal (paper #1). Using the same theory, the enhanced light emission due to the monopole and multipole plasmon modes in plasmonic nano-discs were studied after the project starts (papers #2 & #7). We have also extended our mode analysis to 2D materials (papers #3 & #4) and topological plasmonic systems (papers #5 & #6). Objective 2: The objective has been fully realized. In papers #5 & #6, we have predicted that a novel topological edge plasmon modes and plasmonic systems with parity-time symmetry can be used to enhance the light emission phenomena associated with collective electron transitions. To enhance non-dipole contribution to the light emission due to electronic transition of nano-emitters, we also studied nanostructures consisting of 3-fold rotational symmetric plasmonic particles that can enhance the mixing between dipole and non-dipole modes. The results related to the selection rule and eigen-response theory have also been published in paper #1 & #7 (which focus on the response strength for the case of fast transition electrons) and in paper #2 (which demonstrated the selection rule related to the conservation of angular momentum and conversion of the angular momentum from dipole to quadrupole). The results suggest that rotational symmetries should be controlled properly to enhance the non-dipole contribution to the light emission from the plasmonic nanostructures. In particular, the results in paper #7 have predicted that the monopole modes of a high-symmetry plasmonic nanostructure can be used to enhance the light emission associated with monopole plasmon excited by transition election beam. Objective 3 The objective has been fully realized. The project have improved our understanding of high-resolution cathodoluminescence from metal nanostructures. Results in paper #1 have shown a previously unknown phenomena that dark modes supported in bowtie plasmonic nanoantenna (which are anti-phase modes believed to have only weak photon radiation) can radiate a lot to the far field compared to the in-phase bright mode in the case of electron beam excitation. In paper #7, we have even perfected our investigation to consider a rotationally symmetric nanodisc with a hole, which can enhance the collective monopole electron oscillations. These results will have an important impact on the understanding of high-resolution cathodoluminescence spectra and images. Objective 4 The objective has been fully realized. Through this project, we have also developed an intuitive eigen-response theory to help us understand the near-field spatial dependence of the photon emission rate near nanostructures. For example, the eigen-response theory was applied to understand the light emission from graphene disks supporting dark modes which are quadrupole-like (paper #3). The team has also studied the spatial dependence of the light emission from a hybrid graphene-hBN(hexagonal boron nitride) system (paper #4). Our theory have also provided the analytical solution to the near-field light emission profile from a non-single-dipole topological plasmonic edge mode in a complex chains of plasmonic nanoparticles (papers #5 & #6). Mapping of near-field emission rate profile for the monopole emission by electron beam has also been studied in paper #7. Minor financial issue: The funding support was not enough due to the rapid inflation of salaries and student stipends. To minimize the expenses due to limited funding, the PI decided to ask his PhD student C. W. Ling to help him present some results in international conferences. The conference expenses of the PhD student was finally supported by the University through standard support of the student, which is not reported here.

509813.label: Major findings and research outcome
509813.value: The project outcomes are delivered through 7 publications. As suggested in our proposal, we continued on our preliminary work on plasmonic nanoantenna for controlling the light emission from electron beam excitation (i.e., cathodoluminescence). In collaboration with Prof. Nicholas Fang's group at MIT, the theoretical predictions of emission enhancement and novel phenomena have been verified experimentally through cathodoluminescence spectroscopy. The results together with our intuitive eigen-response theory for understanding the near-field profile of light emission from non-dipole nano-emitters have been published in several papers attached (including publications in Nano Letters, Physical Review B, Optics Letters, Optics Express listed in Part C of this report). At the last stage of the project, extraordinary light emission phenomena from monopole modes were studied. For details, please see the previous section on "Realisation of the objectives" in Part B5 and the section "List of research outputs" in Part C of this report. Findings related to light emission from novel topologically protected edge states were also presented by Research Associate C. W. Ling (also PI's PhD student graduated in 2015/2016) in international conferences such as the APS March Meeting.

509813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
509813.value: The eigen-response theory could be further extended to magnetic non-dipole modes and non-reciprocal systems where emission and absorption are not related by Lorentz reciprocity. The topological aspect of the eigen-response theory due to special spacial-temporal symmetries can be further investigated in the future. Through collaborations with Prof. Nicholas Fang at MIT, future experimental realisations of more phenomena predicted in this project are highly possible if funding support is enough.

509813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
509813.value: Plasmonic nanostructures can strongly enhance the rate of light emission from nanosized quantum emitters and the rate of light scattering by biological molecules, which provide great opportunities for making nano-sized photon source and biosensors of high sensitivity. This project has been successful in predicting novel light emission phenomena from non-dipole nano-emitters due to plasmonic resonances. In collaboration with the MIT team, we used the eigen-response theory and cathodoluminescence spectroscopy to show that there exist new light emission phenomena not known before, such as emission from different dark modes. The results may also find new applications in high-resolution characterization of nanostructures.

510113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
510113.value: In the scientific context of aerosol science and engineering where the particle formation and growth processes simultaneously take place, the particle size distribution (PSD) usually has complex shapes which exhibit bimodal features. For this identified problem, the unimodal log-normal distribution widely used in current aerosol science associated with commonly used moment methods (e.g., quadrature method of moments, standard method of moments, and Taylor series expansion method of moments) will be no longer valid. Although some researchers have attempted to use a mixture of two different unimodal distributions and then construct the moment equations, the assumption for the shape of PSD usually fails to provide the reasonable prediction accuracy. In particular, all existing methods of moments have the same limitation in that there is no general approach to reconstruct the PSD from the known moments, especially for the bimodal system. To overcome its limitation, a novel bimodal moment method (BMM) model will be proposed with the support from the newly developed Taylor series expansion technique. This BMM model, which has no prior requirement of the assumption for the shape of PSD, is expected to be able to solve the bimodal aerosol-related problems with much lower computational time and cost. The reconstruction of PSD will also be achieved by more accurate methods including priori shape function and spline-based method. This proposed novel BMM model scheme with respect to Taylor series expansion technique will also be evaluated to determine which method would be the best criteria for different aerosol dynamic processes, including nucleation-coagulation, condensation-coagulation and nucleation-coagulation-condensation processes, and for different particle morphology including the spherical and non-spherical particles. This BMM model is capable of solving complex aerosol-related problems/systems where the computational methods for aerosol dynamics models have to be coupled with complex turbulent flows. For example, the particle formation and growth in diesel exhaust plume which will be evaluated as well as the solution for the closure of moment equations when the effect of turbulence fluctuation on particle dynamics is taken into consideration. The sectional methods in terms of specific coagulation kernel will be assumed as the exact solution for solving PSD equations whose solutions will be treated as references to validate the study of this newly proposed BMM model scheme. The reliable experimental data for the evolution of bimodal aerosol system available in published papers will also be used as references to validate this BMM model. 在氣溶膠科學與技術研究領域，顆粒的生成與演化過程同時發生，從而導致顆粒的尺度譜分佈呈現雙峰分佈的複雜現象。對於這種確定問題，目前在氣溶膠科學和技術研究領域常用的單對數正態分佈的不同方法（如積分矩方法，標準矩方法，泰勒展開矩方法）不再適用。雖然不少研究學者試圖利用兩個不同對數整體分佈的聯合處理矩方程問題，但由於對顆粒尺度分佈假設的引入，使得模型計算往往出現較大的偏差或失敗。另外，目前現有的矩方法，特別是針對雙峰系統，都在從統計矩量還原尺度譜方面存在困難。為了克服這方面困難，借助於泰勒展開技術，本項目擬提出新穎雙峰分佈矩方法模型。這種新發展模型，對顆粒尺度分佈的形狀 ， 並沒有具體預先要求，有望以極少的計算量處理雙峰分佈的氣溶膠問題。對於完成顆粒尺度分佈的還原工作，將採用預先尺度譜函數和樣條方法。 這個新發展的涉及泰勒展開技術的雙峰矩方法模型，將被用來確定用以研究不同氣溶膠動力學問題的最優方案，如形核-混凝、 凝結-混凝 、形核-混凝-凝結的過程。在研究中，針對顆粒的形狀，將涉及圓球顆粒和非圓球顆粒。本項目的新發展模型，有能力處理跟進複雜湍流問題相關的氣溶膠問題，如汽車尾氣中顆粒物的生成與演化過程。 為驗證雙峰矩方法模型的有效性，分區方法將被作為精確結果對雙峰矩方法模型進行驗證。另外，已在國際雜誌發表的可靠的實驗數據也將被採用來驗證此雙峰矩方法模型。

510113.label: Realisation of objectives
510113.value: In the realization of Objective 5.2.1, a novel bimodal moment method (BMM) model scheme has been developed and used to deal with aerosol problems involving aerosol dynamics with bimodal particle size distributions. In the scientific context of aerosol science and engineering where the particle formation and growth processes simultaneously take place, the particle size distribution (PSD) usually has complex shapes which exhibit bimodal features. For this identified problem, the unimodal log-normal distribution widely used in current aerosol science and associated with the most commonly used moment methods (e.g., standard method of moments, quadrature method of moments and Taylor series expansion method of moments etc.) will be no longer valid. Although some researchers have attempted to use a mixture of two different unimodal distributions and then construct the moment equations, the assumption for the shape of PSD usually fails to provide the reasonable prediction accuracy. In particular, all existing methods of moments have the same limitation in that there is no general approach to reconstruct the PSD from the known moments, especially for the bimodal system. To overcome its limitation, a novel bimodal moment method (BMM) model scheme has been proposed with the support from the newly developed Taylor series expansion technique. A population balance equation (PBE) with simultaneous consideration of two different PSDs has been established as a first step. The transport equations of moments have then been established as a second step to transform the differential-integral PBE into ordinary differential equations (ODEs). In order to provide closures for moments, the Taylor expansion method of moments (TEMOM) has been used together with aerosol dynamic kernels as a third step. In the last step (i.e., the fourth step), the above-mentioned bimodal PBE has been coupled with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) approach to account for complex aerosol dynamics in turbulent flows. This new BMM model, which has no prior requirement of the assumption for the shape of PSD, is capable in solving the bimodal aerosol-related problems with much lower computational time and cost. Hence, Objective 5.2.1 has been completely achieved. In the realization of Objective 5.2.2, a new reconstruction method of PSD from a finite number of known moments has been modified and further developed with validations and modifications to increase the precision and stability of this method. A novel closure method which is not sensitive to invalid sets has been proposed and modified. With this new reconstruction method, PSD of agglomerate can be obtained even for a wide range or invalid of moments without having a priori shape assumption for PSD. The most obvious advantage of this PSD reconstruction method is its insensitivity to invalid sets of moments due to the usage of particular Lagrangian interpolation of moment equations. Hence, Objective 5.2.2 has been completely achieved. In the realization of Objectives 5.2.3 and 5.2.4, this newly developed BMM model has been used to study nanoparticle formation and subsequent growth due to nucleation, coagulation and condensation processes in turbulent flows coupling with large eddy simulation (LES) and a k-epsilon Reynolds averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) approaches. The spatial and temporal PSD, particle number and mass concentrations, and competition between the formation of primary and secondary particles in turbulent flows have been studied. The results show that the large coherent structures strongly affect the particle number & mass concentration distributions, and particle polydispersity. These findings verify that the coherent structures enhance diffusion in the flows and strengthen particle intermodal transfers between particles. Moreover, the dynamics of vehicle exhaust particles with consideration of the background particles (i.e., particles in the surrounding environment) have been investigated using this BMM method coupled with LES and a k-epsilon turbulence model. Both two-dimensional and three dimensional simulations have been carried out using this BMM method coupling with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) approach. The effects of vehicle tailpipe exit conditions, sulfur content and relative humidity on the evolution of exhaust particles have been investigated, respectively. The results show that the tailpipe exit velocity and relative humidity only have slight effect on the steady-state concentration or the diameter of particles in the urban atmosphere. Although sulfur content has less effect on the particle concentration, it yields the background particles with larger geometric average diameter. The numerical simulation results have also been compared with the existing relevant studies and good agreements have been obtained. Hence, Objectives 5.2.3 and 5.2.4 have also been achieved completely. In summary, despite difficulties encountered in the model establishment and improvement of the new BMM model, and its model scheme for solving complex aerosol-related problems for an early stage, all the Objectives in 5.2 have been completely achieved for this two-year funded project.

510113.label: Major findings and research outcome
510113.value: A novel bimodal moment method (BMM) model scheme has been developed and used to deal with aerosol problems involving aerosol dynamics with bimodal particle size distributions. Coupling with large eddy simulation (LES) method, this newly developed BMM model has been used to study nanoparticle formation and subsequent growth due to nucleation, coagulation and condensation processes in turbulent flows. The spatial and temporal particle size distribution (PSD), particle number and mass concentrations, and competition between the formation of primary and secondary particles in turbulent flows have been studied. The results show that the large coherent structures strongly affect the particle number & mass concentration distributions, and particle polydispersity. These findings verify that the coherent structures enhance diffusion in the flows and strengthen particle intermodal transfers between particles. Moreover, the dynamics of vehicle exhaust particles with consideration of the background particles (i.e., particles in the surrounding environment) have been investigated using this BMM model coupled with LES and a k-epsilon Reynolds averaged Navier-Stokes approaches. Both two-dimensional and three-dimensional simulations have been carried out using this BMM model coupling with computational fluid dynamics approach. The effects of vehicle tailpipe exit conditions, sulfur content and relative humidity on the evolution of particles have been investigated, respectively. The results show that the tailpipe exit velocity and relative humidity only have slight effect on the steady-state concentration or the diameter of particles in the urban atmosphere. Although sulfur content has less effect on the particle concentration, it yields background particles with larger geometric average diameter. The numerical simulation results have also been compared with the existing relevant studies and good agreements have been obtained. Moreover, a novel reconstruction method of PSD from a finite number of known moments without having a priori shape assumption for PSD has been developed with validations and modifications to increase the precision and stability of this BBM model. This new BMM model scheme has shown its capability in dealing with bimodal aerosol-related problems. It is capable in revealing the interactions and transfers between the particles in two different modes (i.e. background and exhaust particles) as well as the effect of large coherent structure on particle dynamics. Submicron fractal-like agglomerates undergoing Brownian coagulation using this BBM model was first published in the top-tier Journal of Aerosol Science. Two papers from the obtained results and findings for solving complex aerosol related problems with this BMM model scheme are under submission and preparation status, respectively. One full paper titled “Nanoparticle Formation and Growth in Turbulent Flows using the Bimodal TEMOM" has also recently been submitted to International Journal of Powder Technology for consideration in April 2017. Another full paper related to the formation and evolution of vehicle exhaust particles using this new bimodal TEMOM is also under preparation for journal consideration once the results are further consolidated.

510113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
510113.value: This novel bimodal moment method (BMM) model scheme has great potential for solving complex aerosol related problems concerning bimodal distributions. Since it is only a two-year funded project, there are room and potential for further development for this research project in future: (1) Multi-scale study of aerosol dynamics using this BMM model scheme can be further extended to multi-scale particle systems with complex or arbitrary particle size distribution (PSD). The existing developed bimodal moment method is limited to the PSDs with two different modes. However, for some complex engineering and industrial applications, such as flame synthesis of nanoparticles with multiple physical and chemical processes, the distributions of particles may be more complex. (2) More delicately designed experimental and theoretical studies in aerosol particles are highly needed to provide more numerical validations under different conditions by using this BMM model scheme and optimize the parameters of this model scheme to obtain more accurate descriptions and predictions of complex aerosol-related systems. For example, both experimental and theoretical studies are recommended to focus on the key evolution mechanisms of particles as well as the two-way or even four-way couplings between particles and fluid environment.

510113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
510113.value: This research combines the unique knowledge of numerical simulation of aerosol particles with the aid of mathematical tools and computer computations. The significance of the research is that this novel bimodal moment method (BMM) model scheme has an ability to overcome the existing limitations of unimodal and bimodal methods of moments with simpler algorithm and less computational cost (e.g., computational time and memory) compared with sectional method. The spatial and temporal particle size distributions (PSDs), particle number and mass concentrations, and competition between the formation of primary and secondary particles in turbulent flows have been well simulated and analyzed with validations. The results show that the large coherent structures strongly affect the particle number & mass concentration distributions, and particle polydispersity. The results also show that the vehicle tailpipe exit velocity and relative humidity only have slight effect on the steady-state concentration or the diameter of particles in the urban atmosphere. The increase of sulfur content, however, yields larger size of background particles. The value of this BMM model scheme lies in that it is capable of solving aerosol-related problems and systems with complex PSDs where the computational methods for aerosol dynamics models have to be coupled with complex turbulent flows.

510313.label: Project Objectives
510313.value: Proposing and establishing a methodology to treat a “compound panel” subsystem through the concept of virtual “air panel” element to deal with interfaces containing partial opening. Establishing a new Wavelet-Galerkin formulation to deal with cavities of arbitrary shape. Establishing a systematic approach to optimize the shape of acoustic cavity to be integrated into the general PTF framework. Applying the above methodology to a number of typical applications involving MPPs and carrying out systematic analyses towards in-depth physical understanding.

510313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
510313.value: Acoustic cavities surrounded by vibrating structures are commonly seen in various applications. The vibroacoustic modeling of such systems is extremely challenging in that the simulation tools should be able to cope with the complexity of the system, to reach the mid-to-high frequency range, and to offer the flexibility needed for system optimization. This project would contribute to the modeling and optimization of complex vibroacoustic systems involving structures coupled to partially open/close acoustic cavities, connected in cascade, either in parallel or in series. As a demonstration and application, systems involving Micro-perforated structures/panels (MPP) are investigated. More specifically, several key solutions to problems bottlenecking the application of existing methods will be developed. 1). Two major techniques are proposed to endow the Patch Transfer Function (PTF) approach with the ability of coping with systems containing parallel cascade subsystems and cavities of arbitrary shapes. For a partially open cavity, the aperture is modeled as an equivalent virtual air panel element, to be combined with the structural panels (either perforated or solid) to form a compound panel subsystem. For a close cavity, a Wavelet-Galerkin Method is proposed. The method is basically mesh-free and able to handle large boundary variations, thus allowing flexible and unified handling of the cavity boundaries without meshing the geometry model. 2). Benefiting from these features, an optimization approach will then be proposed to optimize the shape of the backing cavity of elementary MPP absorbers, to be integrated into the general PTF framework. 3). After validations, PTF and WGM will then be combined and applied to a few typical configurations, which are relevant to practical applications. 被振动结构所包围的声学空腔在工程上应用广泛。本课题将对此问题进行系统的研究。作为应用，将集中研究包含微穿孔板结构的系统。

510313.label: Realisation of objectives
510313.value: All objectives of the projects have been realized in a systematic way. Regarding objective 1, an equivalent virtual panel treatment was proposed to model thin apertures involved in complex vibroacoustic systems. The proposed method is capable of handling mixed separations/interfaces comprising both structural and acoustic components, allowing sound transmission both structurally and acoustically. The proposed treatment requires the aperture thickness to be sufficiently small compared to the minimum acoustic wavelength. The theoretical formulation of the virtual panel treatment is established, assessed and validated through comparisons with FEM in two typical examples. The effective thickness allowing for a satisfactory prediction using virtual panel element is established to guaranty the convergence of the calculation. Regarding objective 2, a general procedure, comprising a Wavelet-Garlerkin formulation and a so-called vertex-driven shape optimization is proposed to deal with the general problem of internal sound field prediction and the optimization of the boundary shape. It is shown that, owing to the compactly supported orthogonal property and the remarkable fitting ability, Daubechies Wavelet can be used as a global basis to approximate the unknown sound field on a relatively large interval globally instead of piecewise approximation like most of element based methods do. This feature avoids meshing the boundary of the enclosure, although vertex points are needed to define the boundary shape, whose positions keep updating during the shape optimization process. A rectangular enclosure is used as benchmark to assess and validate the proposed formulation, by investigating the influence of some key parameters involved in the formulation. It was shown that the sound pressure along the entire boundary of the rectangular enclosure can be accurately approximated without meshing. The same enclosure with an inner rigid acoustic screen is then used to reduce the sound pressure level within a chosen area through optimizing the shape of the screen, which shows the remarkable potentials of the proposed approach as a shape optimal tool for inner sound field problems. Regarding objective 3, combining the work carried out in the above two objectives, a comprehensive sub-structuring methodology based on the Patch Transfer Function (PTF) approach with a Compound Interface treatment technique, referred to as CI-PTF method, is proposed, for dealing with complex systems involving cascade open/closed acoustic cavities and MPPs. The co-existence of apertures and solid/flexible/micro-perforated panels over a mixed separation interface is characterized using a compound panel subsystem, which enhances the systematic coupling feature of the PTF framework. Using several typical configurations, the versatility and efficiency of the proposed method is illustrated. Numerical studies highlight the physical understanding on the behavior of MPP inside a complex vibroacoustic environment, thus providing guidance for the practical design of such systems. As an example, the side-branch of the silencer is treated as a combination of unit cells connected in series. It is shown that, by connecting multiple unit cells with varying parameters, the noise attenuation bandwidth can be enlarged. With MPPs, the hybrid noise attenuation mechanism of the silencer is revealed. Depending on the size of the perforation hole, noise attenuation can be dominated by dissipative, reactive or combined effects together. For a broadband sound absorption, the hole size, together with the perforation ratio and other parameters, can be optimized to strike a balance between the dissipative and reactive effect, for ultimately achieving the desired noise attenuation performance within a prescribed frequency region. The modular nature of the proposed formulation allows doing this in a flexible, accurate and cost effective manner. The accuracy of the proposed approach is validated through comparisons with finite element method (FEM) and experiments. A systematic approach based on the sub-structuring modeling principle, to investigate the effects of several typical silencer configurations and provide guidelines for possible system optimization. Through numerical examples, the effects of different internal arrangement, including the side-branch partitions, multi-chamber partitions, non-symmetric inlet/outlet, and their combined effects are investigated. Numerical predictions show good agreements with both finite element method (FEM) analyses and experiments. Investigations suggest some critical issues and possible solutions for better silencer design. Regarding the objective 4, The methodology developed above has been applied to a series of relevant engineering problems. Typical work includes the following. a). design of a series of acoustic silencing devices, exemplified by a duct silencer of various type. MPP is integrated within the design, alongside other important geometrical parameters. Optimizations were made possible thanks to the modular nature of the PTF approach. b). design of double leaf window with opening, which allows effective noise isolation and air ventilation. Again, analysis, design and optimization was conducted; c) A class of general interior noise control problems within an enclosure. Studies allows a thorough understanding on the coupling mechanism of the MPP with the surrounding acoustic medium.

510313.label: Major findings and research outcome
510313.value: On objective 1: The air aperture is modeled as a virtual panel, while the MPP is treated using an equivalent mobility method. By doing so, various combinations of flexible/rigid panels, aperture and MPP can be gathered into a single Compound Interface, allowing multi-channel transmission paths between connected domains. A series of versatile numerical modules have been developed. The convergence and accuracy of the developed numerical tools were thoroughly validated through comparisons with both analytical and experimental examples. This part of the work was published in two papers in Journal of Acoustical Society of America. On Objective 2: The proposed Wavelet-Garlerkin formulation is shown to be able to achieve high accuracy without any boundary meshing. The accuracy of the WGM strongly depends on the resolution level m and the number of Gauss integration points, and in principle also on the wavelet support length L, but to a much less extent. The proposed WGM allows global expansion and therefore allows flexible handling of the cavity boundaries in a unified way without meshing the geometry model like FEM/BEM usually does. This empowers the new approach with its superiority in acoustic mutation and shape optimization problems over other conventional simulation methods. Details were reported in a paper published in the International Journal of Applied Mechanics. On objective 3: The Compound Interface-Patch Transfer Function (CI-PTF) approach shows the efficiency and flexibility in performing system optimization. Regarding MPPs, their in-situ sound absorption was shown to be strongly dependent on the surrounding environment in which they are put in. This unequivocally advocates that MPP cannot be simply considered as a locally reactive element. Instead, it should be treated as an integral part of the whole system, for which fully coupled modeling tools as the one presented in this thesis are definitely needed. This part of work has been the object of publication in a few journals like JSV and JASA. On objective 4: As a focused class of application examples, acoustic silencers have been extensively investigated, for understanding their sound attenuation mechanisms and exploring possibilities for a better design. To achieve a desired TL performance in a prescribed frequency region, the MPP hole diameter, perforation ratio and other parameters can be optimized to strike a balance between the sound reflection and absorption. The feasibility of achieving broadband sound attenuation by using cascade sub-chambers with optimized TLs to tackle different frequency regions was demonstrated. The sub-chamber strategy was extended to generalize a multi-level silencer design approach. Its applicability was confirmed through both theoretical case studies and an experimental validation through retrofitting a mining truck muffler. This part of the work has been published in a few journals such as JSV, JASA and NCEJ.

510313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
510313.value: The proposed general analysis and optimization strategy using MPPs has started find their applications in aerospace industry through the establishment of a joint Lab with the China Academy for Space Technology. Future effort consists in finding more applications cases. Meanwhile, a good packaging of the simulation tool will also facilitate its use.

510313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
510313.value: Acoustic noise from industry, construction and transportation is the major source of annoyance in modern urban environment. It not only affects the competitiveness of the products, thus affecting the acceptance of the consumers, but also creates increasing environmental concerns in major metropolitan cities around the world. The recognition of noise as an important hazard to human health calls for advanced noise control and mitigation strategies. In-depth analyses of vibroacoustic systems are essential for the development of advanced noise control solutions. In this work, a package of efficient numerical modeling tools is developed based on the sub-structuring approach, in order to deal with complex structural-acoustical couplings among various subsystem components in a wide range of applications. A Compound Interface-Patch Transfer Function (CI-PTF) approach is proposed, highlighting its ability in handling mixed separations, such as those composed of rigid or flexible structures and apertures. Typical structural and acoustical subsystems are characterized as a few versatile subsystem modules, serving as the building blocks for constructing complex system configurations. The developed numerical tools serve as a general simulation, analysis and optimization toll for a wide range of industrial problems.

510413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
510413.value: 大數據的显著特点是數量大，速度快，種類多。大數據超過了傳統數據庫系統的處理能力。 云計算为數據管理和處理提供了豐富的計算資源和大量的並行處理能力。近些年，針對云計算資源協調和大數據處理的問題，許多項目已經付諸實施。許多編程模型已經提出，以支持不同類型的大數據應用。 在本項目中， 我們提供高層次的編程模型， 以支持各种多樣的大數據應用。 雖然現在有多個能夠處理多種數據類型的編程模型， 例如支持批處理數據 MapReduce， 支持圖數據處理的 Pregel， 支持流數據處理的 S4。 但是沒有一個模型可以支持多樣的需求和多種的大數據應用。 一些平臺提供了模型的集成，他們要求程序員費力的把一個應用分別映射到不用的模型上。如果部署到雲上，現有的模型要求程序員提前手動的配置資源，但是所需的資源會依據不同的數據處理階段動態的變化。 本項目致力於開發一個通用可伸縮的并集成大數據處理模型的框架， 使用新方法提供針對多樣的大數據應用的統一的抽象層。可伸縮性有兩層含義：允許添加新的編程模型；針對不同的數據量彈性的管理資源。我們調查發現現有的工作無法達成以上的目標。 許多挑戰性的問題需要解決。首先，由於現有的編程模型設計不同， 所以很难集成這些模型， 并提供一個統一的編程接口。其次，設計一個能夠抽象不同編程模型所对应的执行机制具有一定挑戰性。其三，爲了支持雲端資源的動態利用，本框架首先需要調查數據處理的需求，对數據類型和以及数据之上的操作进行分类。然後，我們將针对不同數據類型以及数据之上不同操作设计一個統一表达方法， 並實現一個針對不同編程模型的統一接口。 爲了支持統一的編程接口， 我們將設計一個中間件， 提供橋接不同編程模型所需的动态支持。中間件功能具体包括将應用不同的计算階段映射到不同的編程模型，对不同编程模型的作業或者任務进行調度，分析應用所需的資源并在雲上自動配置。 本項目有助於大數據應用的編程，有益于商業界，工業界和整個社會發現知識和決策。所提出的研究將會縮短大數據應用的開發週期。我們的框架將會真正实现“用多少付多少”的云計算特點，以降低应用開發者的成本。

510413.label: Realisation of objectives
510413.value: We have made efforts to identify the new requirements and challenging issues in developing big data applications. The issues are classified into various layers: requirement analysis, a general framework for big data programming, and big data applications. The framework for big data programming includes the models, algorithms and mechanisms in individual components: models mapping, jobs/tasks scheduling, resources management, and configurations. The goal of the big data programming framework is to provide new abstractions and runtime techniques with key features like scalability, fault tolerance, efficient task distribution, usability and processing speed. We first conducted a systematic literature review of new challenges and requirements on programming support for big data analytics applications. Big data programming platforms need to provide new abstractions and runtime techniques with desired features as described above. We first conducted a comprehensive survey of the requirements and classified existing big data programming platforms in different dimensions. Then, we presented the architecture, methodology and features of major programming platforms like MapReduce, Storm, Spark, Pregel, GraphLab, etc. Last, we compared existing big data platforms and discussed the need of a unifying programming framework. We proceeded to study the problem of designing and implementing a unified and efficient data-parallel system for big data analytics computations. We first identified an important observation that the computation core of many big data applications can be expressed as general matrix computations, including linear algebra operations and irregular matrix operations. However, existing parallel programming systems such as Spark do not have programming abstraction and efficient implementation for general matrix computations. Therefore, we proposed MatrixMap, a unified and efficient data-parallel system for general matrix computations. MatrixMap provides powerful yet simple abstraction, consisting of a distributed data structure called bulk key matrix and a computation interface defined by matrix patterns. Users can easily load data into bulk key matrices and program algorithms into parallel matrix patterns. We developed three key techniques in the proposed unified and efficient data-parallel system, including matrix patterns with lambda functions for irregular and linear algebra matrix operations, asynchronous computation pipeline with optimized data shuffling strategies for specific matrix patterns and in-memory data structure reusing data in iterations. Moreover, it can automatically handle the parallelization and distribute execution of programs on a large cluster. The experiment results show that MatrixMap can achieve the performance 12 times faster than Spark. On top of the abstracted matrix computation, we developed a high-level interface for network embedding in big data applications. Network embedding is increasingly employed to assist network analysis as it is effective to learn latent features that encode linkage information. Although, various network embedding methods have been proposed, they are designed only for a single network scenario. In the era of big data, different types of related information can be fused together to form a coupled heterogeneous network, which consists of two different but related sub-networks connected by inter-network edges. In this scenario, the inter-network edges can act as complementary information in the presence of intra-network ones. We proposed a method named embedding of embedding (EOE) for coupled heterogeneous networks. In the EOE, latent features encode not only intra-network edges, but also inter-network ones. To tackle the challenge of heterogeneities of two networks, the EOE incorporates a harmonious embedding matrix to further embed the embeddings that only encode intra-network edges. Empirical experiments on a variety of real-world datasets demonstrate the EOE outperforms consistently single network embedding methods in applications including visualization, link prediction multi-class classification, and multi-label classification. Using our proposed big data programming framework, we developed two big data applications: traffic congestion correlation and interactive data-streaming application. The first application focused on discovering traffic congestion correlation, which is a major concern in many cities around the world. We proposed a three-phase framework to study the congestion correlation between road segments using multi-source real world data of Beijing City. In the first phase, we extracted congestion information on each road segment from GPS trajectories of over 10,000 taxis, defined congestion correlation and proposed a corresponding mining algorithm to find out the existing correlations. In the second phase, we extracted various features on each pair of road segments from the road network and POI data. In the last phase, the results of the first two phases are input into several classifiers to predict congestion correlation. We further analyzed the important features and evaluated the results of the trained classifiers. We found some important patterns that lead to a high/low congestion correlation, and they can facilitate building various transportation applications. The proposed techniques in our framework are general, and can be applied to other pairwise correlation analysis. The second application is related to mobile interactive data-streaming applications. We aim to improve the performance of a mobile application by offloading its computation onto cloudlets and cloud. Specifically, we first proposed a fine-grained data-flow model to characterize mobile interactive data streaming applications. Then we developed a unified optimization framework that achieves maximization of the overall utilities of all mobile users, and designed an efficient heuristic algorithm for the optimal computation offloading problem, which is able to make trade-off between throughput and energy consumption at mobile devices. The results show that the overall utility achieved by our heuristic is close to the precise optimum, and our solution can significantly outperforms the single-cloudlet mechanism.

510413.label: Major findings and research outcome
510413.value: In this project, we first conducted a comprehensive survey of the requirements, gave an overview and classified existing big data programming platforms based on different dimensions. The result is published as a survey paper [J2017a]. We presented the details of the architecture, methodology and features of major programming platforms like MapReduce, Storm, Spark, Pregel, GraphLab, etc. We also compared existing big data platforms and discussed the need for a unifying framework.We studied a specific problem of identifying and discovering multi-dimension relations in complex cyber-physical integration networks [J2015]. We then designed a unified and efficient data-parallel programming system, called MatrixMap for general matrix computations [C2015] [J2017c]. MatrixMap provides powerful yet simple abstractions, consisting of a distributed data structure called bulk key matrix and a computation interface defined by matrix patterns. Programmers can define matrices at programming level and easily load data into the bulk key matrices and program algorithms into parallel matrix patterns. The experiment results showed that MatrixMap can achieve 12 times speedup comparing with Spark. For big data applications using network graphs, we proposed a method named embedding of embedding (EOE) for coupled heterogeneous networks [C2017]. the EOE incorporates a harmonious embedding matrix to further embed the embeddings that only encode intra-network edges. Empirical experiments on a variety of real-world datasets demonstrated that EOE outperforms consistently single network embedding methods in applications including visualization, link prediction, multi-class classification, and multi-label classification. We have developed two big data applications on top of the proposed framework. The first application studies the traffic congestion correlation between road segments from multiple real world data [J2017b] [C2016]. We found some important patterns that lead to a high/low congestion correlation, and they can facilitate building various transportation applications. The proposed techniques in our framework are general, and can be applied to other pairwise correlation analysis. We have further developed another application of mobile interactive data-streaming computaion [C2014]. We proposed a fine-grained data-flow programming model based on the proposed big data programming framework to characterize mobile interactive data streaming applications. We built a unified optimization framework that achieves maximization of the overall utilities of all mobile users, and designed an efficient heuristic for the optimization problem. The results showed that the overall utility achieved by our heuristic is close to the precise optimum. To provide support for programming and deploying interactive mobile applications, we developed AppBooster, a programming platform with APIs for computation partitioning, optimization and performance tuning [J2016].

510413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
510413.value: Our future work includes further development of higher-level programming support on top of the proposed model and framework so as to help ease and shorten the development of big data applications. Specifically, we will develop more advanced matrix patterns and libraries to support complex machine learning algorithms such as deep learning. Although deep leaning contains a lot of layers, they are composed of basic matrix operations. We also plan to extend the big data programming framework to implement high-level interface such as SQL and R and provide more libraries for machine learning and graph algorithms. Another direction for future research is to integrate both batch processing and real time processing together into programming framework in a harmonious way. The integration of different big data programming platforms is an open challenge with various issues related to task scheduling, resource allocation and model mapping to be resolved. It is interesting to study and implement a general big data interface which support both batch and streaming data analytics.

510413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
510413.value: Big data applications usually involve in many different algorithms, including: graph processing, machine learning and data mining. To facilitate big data applications, it is of great importance to have a unified interface and framework of above-mentioned algorithms. Although some parallel program systems have been proposed, they are limited to certain type of computation or processing algorithms and lacking general abstractions. The contributions of this project mainly lie in programming abstraction and efficient implementation of computations in big data analytics applications. First, we identify that the computation core of many big data applications can be expressed as general matrix computations. Second, we present MatrixMap, a unified and efficient data-parallel system for general matrix computations. MatrixMap provides powerful yet simple abstraction, consisting of a distributed data structure called bulk key matrix and a computation interface defined by matrix patterns. Users can easily load data into bulk key matrices and program algorithms into parallel matrix patterns. Based on the framework, we developed big data applications on traffic congestion mining and mobile data streaming computation. This project has significant values in big data analytics applications. Many applications such as urban computing, healthcare and finance can be benefited from our research outcomes.

510513.label: Project Objectives
510513.value: To examine the features and cooling capacity of PCSs that are commercially available and commonly used in Hong Kong; To identify the shortcomings of these PCSs in combating heat stress when applied in the construction industry; To design and engineer a PCS which is suitable for construction workers taking into consideration the additional requirements of the construction industry; Evaluate the effectiveness of the newly designed PCS for construction workers.
rows: To examine the features and cooling capacity of PCSs that are commercially available and commonly used in Hong Kong;
To identify the shortcomings of these PCSs in combating heat stress when applied in the construction industry;
To design and engineer a PCS which is suitable for construction workers taking into consideration the additional requirements of the construction industry;
Evaluate the effectiveness of the newly designed PCS for construction workers.

510513.label: Realisation of objectives
510513.value: Objective 1 An extensive review of commercially available and commonly used PCSs was conducted. Three basic types of PCSs, including liquid cooling garment (LCG), air cooling garment (ACG), and phase change garment (PCG), were examined. Liquid and air cooling garments are connected to external cooling devices and circulate cooled liquid or air around the human body. Phase change garments use the precooled phased change materials (PCM), e.g. ice, inorganic salt and paraffin wax, to absorb heat. PCMs are latent heat storage materials that can absorb and release heat at a roughly constant temperature (i.e. melting temperature) as it goes through solid–liquid transitions. In practice, PCG is often the most usable cooling technique because of its simple mechanism, untethered system and unpowered nature. Considering the cost, quality, availability and popularity, two kinds of commercial PCGs (Vests A and B) in Hong Kong were identified for the evaluation. Field studies were conducted in the construction, outdoor cleaning and horticulture, kitchen and catering, and airport apron service industries in Hong Kong between July and September in 2012. Workers completed questionnaires about their subjective perceptions on the two cooling vests after they had finished wear trials. Results indicated that most workers preferred Vest B because it provided better thermal comfort, usability, fabric texture (feel), and tactile comfort than Vest A. Therefore, Vest B was selected for further testing in a climatic chamber (controlled at 33°C and 75% relative humidity) to quantitatively assess its effectiveness in reducing heat strain. 12 volunteers took the wear trial. Treadmill exercise was adopted. The Physiological Strain Index (PSI), based on the core body temperature and heart rate, quantitatively describes heat strain. Vest B slowed down the rate of increase of PSI during exercise by 6.69% and accelerated the rate of reduction of PSI during recovery by 6.82%. Therefore, the effectiveness of Vest B was demonstrated by assessing qualitative comfort and usability as well as the quantitative physiological responses. Objective 2 After confirming that Vest B is more effective than Vest A, the Hong Kong Labor Department, in cooperation with the OSHC, launched the “Cooling Vest Promotion Pilot Scheme” during the summer of 2013. Approximately 1,500 sets of Vest B were distributed to 248 participating companies in the aforementioned four industries. To assess the practicability of Vest B, a questionnaire survey was conducted over a three-month period (September to November 2013). A total of 232 valid questionnaires were collected. A remarkable heat strain alleviation of 21.1% was achieved by using the cooling vest in the four industries. To identify the major shortcomings of Vest B, in-depth interviews were conducted with the participants. 169 participants agreed to be interviewed. The major shortcomings of the vest includes easily staining color, short cooling time, heavy weight, inflexibility, a lack of industry-specific design, nondurable, and thick fabric with poor permeability. Objective 3 A systematic review and meta-analysis found that PCSs with hybrid cooling sources can achieve a high cooling effect on reducing heat strain and improving performance. Referring the prototype of Vest B, a tailor-made PCS (two-layer cooling vest) with hybrid cooling sources (i.e. PCM packs and a portable ventilation unit) was designed and engineered. The new cooling vest has two layers. The inner layer cloth has high air permeability, permitting air go through to the skin surface, whereas the outer layer cloth is highly air resistant, preventing the air from escaping to the environment, thereby facilitating air ventilation around the body. The use of thin and light fabric reduces the system bulkiness and weight. 9 polyester meshed fabrics for inner layer and 12 nylon taffeta for outer layer were tested. The finally selected inner layer and outer layer fabrics are thin (0.24 mm for inner layer and 0.07 mm for outer layer), light (0.48 g/cm2 for inner layer and 0.42 g/cm2 for outer layer), anti-static, anti-abrasive, and have high water vapor permeability (1253.48 g/m2/day for inner layer and 1052.31 g/m2/day for outer layer) and UPF of 50+ (blocking 98% UVA and UVB). Eight PCM packs are evenly placed on the chest and back region of the body considering the distribution of sweat gland. Commercial products were tested for selecting the PCM with appropriate melting temperature and large heat of fusion. The selected PCM packs have a melting temperature of 28°C and heat of fusion of 131 J/g. A thermal manikin test showed that the cooling power of the cooling vest with PCM 28 is high (64.5 ± 6.1 W/m2). Additionally, PCM at 28°C can be solidified (for reuse) at room temperature with air-conditioning (20–25°C), which is conducive to the application in the construction industry. The portable ventilation unit includes a battery pack and a pair of ventilation fans. To enhance air circulation, the ventilation fans are fixed at the lower back with two openings at the upper back of the new vest. Commercial products were tested for customizing a ventilation unit with high air flow rate, light weight and long work duration. The newly customized ventilation unit exhibited higher air flow rate (20 L/s) and longer work duration (up to 7 hours) than the commercially available ones. Overall, the design considers the following features, namely, strong cooling power, long cooling duration, achieving thermal comfort, compact design without any external connections, wearing comfort and mobility, loose-fit design, different front and back design improving visibility and safety, aesthetics, and ergonomics. Objective 4 Thermal manikin tests, human wear trials in the laboratory, and field studies were conducted in sequence to evaluate the effectiveness and applicability of the newly designed PCS. The cooling power of the PCS was measured on a sweating thermal manikin in a climatic chamber (34 °C and 60% relative humidity). With combined cooling sources (i.e. PCM + Fan-on), the newly designed PCS has a much higher cooling power of 67–87 W, than Vest B (52–58 W). Laboratory experiments were conducted in a climatic chamber (37 °C and 60% relative humidity). 12 male participants were randomly assigned to the cooling and control condition. Physiological (e.g. core temperature and heart rate) and perceptual (e.g. ratings of perceived exertion and thermal sensation) responses were measured. The protocol included treadmill exercise and recovery. The major finding manifested that PCS significantly alleviated physiological and perceptual strains during the recovery period. A remarkable reduction of body heat storage by 59% and an improvement in exercise duration by 52% were achieved in the cooling condition. Field studies were conducted at the construction sites during summer. Construction workers randomly took the Cooling and Control trial. The field experiment included 14 steel bar fixing workers. Physiological (ear temperature and heart rate) and perceptual (ratings of perceived exertion and thermal sensation) responses were measured. Physiological and perceptual strains were significantly lower in Cooling than those in Control during rest and subsequent bouts of work after rest (p < 0.05). On-site questionnaire survey assessed participants’ subjective ratings of cooling effect, thermal comfort, wetness sensation, and fatigue recovery (by the seven-point Likert scale, the higher the better). A total of 143 pairs of completed questionnaires were finally collected. Subjective ratings in Cooling ranged from 4 to 6, suggesting a highly satisfactory level. In general, Cooling was rated significantly higher than Control on all the subjective items (p < 0.05).
