515313.label: Major findings and research outcome
515313.value: The parameterized remesh-free FEM has been proposed and extensively studied [1]. The salient advantages of the proposed parameterized remesh-free FEM have been summarized as: (1) It requires only one set of fine FE computational mesh and an initial mesh. New meshes can be updated by providing the new positions of the nodes of the initial mesh and one can then map back the area coordinates to the Cartesian coordinates. (2) It is avoided using a coordinates mapping technique with the help of an initial coarse mesh, which contains all the movable nodes in the fine mesh and serves as a coarse skeleton for robust mesh deformation. The simulation results have revealed that: the proposed method can be applied to analyze electronic devices. The proposed algorithm has been extended to Synchronous machines [6], power transformers [5], HTS doubly-fed flux-modulated machines [7], HTS double-stator doubly-fed wind generator [8], hybrid-flux magnetic gear [9], power electronic driven flux-modulated machines [10]. The idea of the remesh-free FEM has been applied in the optimization of the electromagnetic devices [2-3]. It also has been combined with the improved Tabu algorithm [4]. Optimal design of magnetic gears [11] and permanent magnet arrangement [15] with parameterized mesh has also been developed. The simulation results have revealed that: (1) The proposed method can be applied to both 2-D and 3-D problems. (2) The remesh-free feature renders the method very inexpensive in terms of computational time during FEM parameter sweeping analysis. (3) The scale of degree of freedom (DoF) is controlled in the proposed algorithm and it is a multi-resolution remesh-free FEM. (3) The developed method has been applied to optimizing the design of permanent magnet electric devices, which are commonly used in industrial and domestic applications. A novel magnetic vector potential (MVP) formulation with Coulomb gauge has been proposed. This formulation is easy to implement, and the resultant matrix system is symmetric and uniquely solvable. Only limited sample points are needed in the proposed algorithm and the basis of the solution space is reduced. It has been applied for solving 3-D motional eddy-current problems [12], 3-D magnetostatic problems [13], 3-D eddy-current field analysis [14] using edge elements. The simulations have been presented to showcase the accuracy and usefulness of the proposed method for practical engineering computation.

515313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
515313.value: Optimal EM designs can effectively maximize their energy conversion efficiency and minimize their cost. Optimal design algorithms which can search automatically the best EM design parameters using numerical methods are very useful in practice. Finding the best design quickly by just clicking a mouse on the computer is indeed the ultimate dream of many electrical engineers. The remeshing procedure in finite element method (FEM) usually needs to be executed thousands of times, which is very time-consuming and is also not very robust, especially for complicated problems especially 3-dimensional (3-D) applications. In the application of numerical optimization methods in engineering, finding an efficient algorithm of FEM is a big mission for researchers. In this research area, optimization of electric machines (EMs) with remesh-free FEM is still required for further research. We may develop new remesh-free algorithms which can avoid mesh regeneration in the inverse iteration steps. Meanwhile optimization algorithms which are combined with the remesh-free FEM may be improved and new optimization strategies may be developed.

515313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
515313.value: A novel remesh-free finite element method (FEM) has been developed for optimal design of electromagnetic machines (EMs). The proposed algorithm provides a novel fast and robust mesh deformation method to reduce the time needed for generating the meshes for different design parameters to accelerate the optimal shape design process. For both 2-D and 3-D problems, for nonlinear iteration steps, the FEM solutions obtained on the previous mesh are used as initial values for the next mesh and this approach accelerates the convergence rate. It is also a novel multi-resolution algorithm. Different scales of degrees of freedom (DoFs) are used in different stages of the optimization process. And the total computing time is reduced compared to traditional FEM. The proposed remesh-free FEM has been applied to the analysis and optimization of different types of EMs. The proposed magnetic vector potential (MVP) formulation with Coulomb gauge is an extension of the traditional Coulomb-gauged formulation using penalty technique. It is an improved reduced basis method (RBM) which reduces the basis of the solution space and it greatly accelerates the time-stepping solution process. The algorithm concept against computer simulation results has been verified.

515413.label: Project Title(Chinese)
515413.value: 城市污染大氣環境中烷基硝酸鹽的光化學形成及其對臭氧產生的影響

515413.label: Co - Investigator(s)
515413.value: Dr Blake, Donald Dr CHEUNG, Kalam

515413.label: Project Objectives
515413.value: To characterize the formation mechanisms, as well as the temporal variations of RONO2 in Hong Kong; To improve our understanding on the formation pathways of RONO2 under polluted urban environments; To assess the roles and interplays of RONO2 on the formation of photochemical ground-level O3.
rows: To characterize the formation mechanisms, as well as the temporal variations of RONO2 in Hong Kong;
To improve our understanding on the formation pathways of RONO2 under polluted urban environments;
To assess the roles and interplays of RONO2 on the formation of photochemical ground-level O3.

515413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
515413.value: 在氮氧化物（NOx）的存在下，碳氢化合物氧化產生硝酸烷基酯（RONO2）。他們与臭氧（O3）有著相似的光化學形成途徑。RONO2成為氮氧化物以及烷基過氧自由基和烷氧基的儲藏庫，從而影響臭氧的產生效率。RONO2的濃度在很大程度上取決於其對應的父烴的水平。液化石油氣（LPG）的使用公認會導致顯著的非甲烷烴排放。特別是丙烷和丁烷，它們分別為C3和C4 RONO2的前體物。在香港，回溯到2001-2002年，當的士及小巴首先開始使用石油氣時，RONO2的水平已相當顯著。2006年，當幾乎所有的士和小巴轉用石油氣時，丙烷和丁烷成為香港市區最豐富的非甲烷揮發性有機化合物（VOCs）種類。目前，即在公共交通領域引進石油氣11年後，預計RONO2會成為環境中VOC的一個主要成分。然而，儘管他們在揮發性有機化合物和氮化學及臭氧形成中擔當重要角色，有关RONO2來源，命運和傳輸的研究非常有限。此外，即使在第一階段的氧化，城市和區域空氣質量模型亦沒有考慮RONO2形成的細節。因此有必要更好地理解RONO2的形成以便準確地表達這些化合物在空氣質量模擬光化學機制中的過程。鑑於RONO2前體物的大量存在及其高度活躍的光化學特性，香港特別適合調查RONO2對臭氧形成的影響。通過密集採樣活動，將對RONO2，揮發性有機化合物和臭氧的日變化特徵進行分析，以檢查RONO2在污染環境下的來源，命運和傳輸。本研究將利用計算機建模，對RONO2對O3化學的影響進行全面評估。通過調查污染城市環境中的臭氧前體關係中的關鍵化學過程，本研究將有助於在香港制定有效的O3控制策略。

515413.label: Realisation of objectives
515413.value: The project objectives have been fully achieved. The achievements are shown below. * The spatio-temporal variations of RONO2 at a costal site (Tai O), an oceanic site (Da Wan shan), a suburban site (Tung Chung), a mountainous site (Tai Mo Shan) and an urban site (Tsuen Wan) were characterized by analysis of time-series of RONO2, diurnal profiles, descriptive statistics and source apportionment analysis. * The formation pathways of RONO2 in polluted urban environments and clean marine environments were explored using the measurement data and a complex photochemical box model developed by the PI's group, namely, Photochemical Box Model incorporating the Master Chemical Mechanism (PBM-MCM). * The roles and interplays of RONO2 on the photochemical O3 formation were investigated comprehensively using the observation data and the PBM-MCM model.

515413.label: Major findings and research outcome
515413.value: * The sum of C1-C5 RONO2 varied from 30.7 ± 14.8 pptv in spring to 120.7 ± 10.4 pptv in autumn, of which 2-butyl nitrate dominated with the highest average concentration of 30.8 ± 2.6 pptv at the coastal site. * The pathway of CH3O reacting with NO2 made minor contributions (11.3 ± 0.7%) to methyl nitrate formation at the coastal site. And 51.8 ± 3.1% and 36.5 ± 6.3% of the methyl nitrate was attributed to the reaction of CH3O2 + NO and to oceanic emissions/biomass burning, respectively. * Although the levels of parent hydrocarbons were much lower at the mountainous site and the oceanic site than at the urban and suburban sites, similar alkyl nitrate levels were found between mountainous and urban sites, and between marine and suburban sites regardless of the elevation difference. * Source apportionment analysis found that secondary formation was the prominent contributor of alkyl nitrates in the meso scenario, followed by biomass burning and oceanic emissions in polluted urban environments. * The alkyl nitrate levels measured at the mountainous site mainly resulted from the photooxidation of the parent hydrocarbons at the urban site during mesoscale circulation, i.e., valley breezes, corresponding to 52–86% of the alkyl nitrate levels at the mountainous site. * The reaction of alkyl peroxy radicals (RO2) with nitric oxide (NO) dominated the formation of RONO2 at both sites, and the formation of alkyl nitrates contributed negatively to O3 production. * The formation of C2–C4 RONO2 was limited by NOx (volatile organic compounds (VOCs)) when total volatile organic compounds (TVOCs)/NOx was higher (lower) than 10.0 ± 0.4 parts per billion by volume (ppbv)/ppbv at the mountainous site. * RONO2 formation led to a decrease of simulated O3, with reduction efficiencies (O3 reduction/RONO2 production) of 4–5 parts per trillion by volume (pptv)/pptv at the mountainous site and 3–4 pptv/pptv at the urban site. * The variations of simulated O3 induced by RONO2 degradation depended upon the regimes controlling O3 formation and the relative abundances of TVOCs and NOx. * Propane and n-butane were significantly lower at the marine site (WSI) in Hong Kong, whereas C3−C4 RONO2 were comparable to the suburban site (TC), mainly due to the fact that stronger oxidative capacity at WSI led to more efficient RONO2 formation. * RONO2 formation at WSI switched from VOC-limited regime during O3 episodes to VOC and nitrogen oxides (NOx) colimited regime during nonepisodes. * Unlike the predominant contributions of parent hydrocarbons to C4−C5 RONO2, the production of C1−C3 RONO2 was more sensitive to other VOCs like aromatics and carbonyls.

515413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
515413.value: The developed PBM-MCM photochemical box model can be further improved by considering more RONO2 species in the study region. Longer sampling period is strongly proposed for thorough understanding of photochemical RONO2 formation and their impact on the ozone formation in the region.

515413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
515413.value: Alkyl nitrates (RONO2) are the secondary products of hydrocarbon oxidation in the presence of NOx, and they share a similar photochemical formation pathway as O3. RONO2 concentrations largely depend on the levels of their corresponding parent hydrocarbons. In Hong Kong, the levels of RONO2 were already significant back in 2001-2002, when the implementation of LPG-fuelled taxis and minibuses began. At present, RONO2 are expected to comprise a major fraction of ambient VOC levels. Yet, very limited studies have been carried out to investigate the sources, fate and transport of RONO2. Furthermore, urban and regional air quality models do not treat RONO2 formation in detail even in the first stage of oxidation. A better understanding of RONO2 production is needed to accurately represent these compounds in the photochemical mechanisms used for air quality modeling. Through intensive data analysis, the diurnal variations of RONO2, VOCs and O3 were analyzed to examine the sources, fate and transport of RONO2 under polluted urban environments. A comprehensive assessment of the impact of RONO2 on O3 chemistry was also conducted using computer modeling. This project is of help in formulating an effective O3 control strategy in Hong Kong.

515513.label: Project Title(Chinese)
515513.value: 城市熱島動態時空模型的建立與研究

515513.label: Project Objectives
515513.value: The first objective is to define a data model characterising urban heat islands. Temperature data are obtained from satellite images. From there, UHI are extracted at different resolutions and their life cycle built by comparing successive images. An UHI is defined as a spatiotemporal object with a spatial extent (formed by a boundary) that evolves through time possessing its own thematic attributes (including temperature values obtained from raster images). Topological events and spatial changes observed on UHI are defined as objects in their own right so that the evolution of each UHI is explicitly recorded. The second objective is the development of the GIS system with the design of a spatiotemporal database storing all environmental data. A GIS client will be developed to access the database and visualise the data. Data are retrieved by passing SQL-type queries to the server. Queries can include spatial and temporal operators and apply to all classes in the database so that spatiotemporal events can be related to any environmental object.

515513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
515513.value: An Urban Heat Island (UHI) is an urban area whose temperature is higher than in surrounding rural areas. This phenomenon is mostly observed in large and dense metropolitan cities and is caused by different factors such as the concentration of high buildings limiting air circulation and building surface heat radiating and warming the air at night time. The UHI effect is particularly intense in Hong Kong and it is therefore important to understand its causes and consequences to ensure a sustainable development of the city. Estimating the UHI effect is achieved by measuring the difference in air and surface temperature between rural and urban areas from measurements on the ground and from remote sensing data. Analysing the causes of UHI can be done in a Geographical Information System (GIS) by storing temperature data in a raster layer together with other layers providing land use and other types of environmental data. Data from each layer are then correlated and analysed to establish some causality. Evolution of a phenomenon can also be studied through several snapshots but the analysis is mostly based on human observation. The dynamic nature of UHIs and other environmental variables impacting UHIs is not recorded in current GIS models and has not been considered in GIS based analysis. The objective of this project is to provide a data model which describes the dynamic behaviour of UHIs in order to derive both spatial representations and temporal representations of UHIs. Each UHI is considered as a spatiotemporal entity undergoing a series of changes and processes through time. A GIS system will be developed which records the UHI spatial, temporal and thematic attributes (i.e. the temperature). Different space and time scales will also be considered as changes to UHIs can be observed on a daily, seasonal or annual basis and can be analysed at a street block or district level. The dynamic behaviour of UHIs and other entities will be recorded in a database so that spatiotemporal analyses can be performed by querying the database. Furthermore, a geovisual analytics toolbox will be developed to allow visualisation of spatiotemporal and thematic attributes for further analysis. The system will be able to record simulated data in order to evaluate the impact of environmental change and urban development in order to better describe and understand the relationships between UHIs and their environment as well as the impact of future building development. 城市熱島是指城市區域的氣溫明顯高於周邊郊區氣溫的現象。這種現象多見於建築密集的大都市，且誘發原因多樣，例如：高層建築的集中限制了空氣環流和建築表面散熱使得晚上城市的氣溫比郊區為高。城市熱島效應在香港尤為嚴重，因此，研究其成因與影響從而確保城市可持續發展顯得格外重要。 城市熱島效應可以通過分別計算郊區與城市的氣溫與地表溫度的溫差來進行評估，而溫度資料主要有兩種來源：一是地面直接測量；二是從遙感資料中提取。利用GIS技術，將溫度資料單獨存儲在一個柵格圖層中。土地利用及其他類型的環境資料也分別存儲在不同的圖層，由於各個圖層間資料相互關聯，通過分析可以得出城市熱島效應的成因。此外，通過拍快照的方式也可以研究熱島現象的發展情況，但這種分析通常是基於研究人員的觀察。目前的問題是，城市熱島效應以及其他對城市熱島效應產生影響的環境變數的動態本質，並沒有記錄在GIS模型中，也並沒有被考慮到GIS的各種分析功能當中。 本專案的研究目的是提供一個資料模型用來描述城市熱島效應的動態時空變化。利用這種資料模型可以得出城市熱島效應的空間和時間特徵。每個城市熱島環境可以被看作是隨時間經歷著一系列變化與過程的時空實體。建立用來記錄城市熱島時間、空間以及專題屬性（例如：溫度）的GIS系統。由於對城市熱島效應的觀察可以基於日、季度、甚至年份等不同的時間尺度，也可以基於街區或縣區級等不同的空間尺度，所以不同的時間、空間尺度也將在系統中實現。城市熱島以及其他實體的動態行為將被記錄在資料庫中。這樣一來，通過查詢資料庫就可以進行時空分析。此外，系統還考慮開發地學可視分析工具箱（geovisual analytic toolbox），從而將時空和專題屬性視覺化表達，方便進一步的分析。為了更好的表達和理解城市熱島與其周圍環境的關係，以及城市熱島對未來建築發展的影響，系統將被設計為可以記錄的類比資料，以便評估環境變化與城市發展帶來的影響。

515513.label: Realisation of objectives
515513.value: During the project period, we have accomplished the objectives: 1. This study has achieved the objective to propose a GIS data model for characterizing Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect. We have developed a novel object-oriented dynamic model to reconstruct the evolutionary process of UHIs in which previous models were not capable. 2. This study conceptualizes each UHI as a two-dimensional field-object which has four properties (i.e. extent, location, temperature, and time). Then, an object-oriented data model is developed to track the dynamic behaviors of UHIs instantly, which are expressed by three types of filiations (i.e., spatial, locational, and thematic filiations) between zones at each two consecutive time instants. For each time instant, spatial filiations are defined by areal changes and topological transformations. A zone at t(i) associating with a single zone at t(i−1) makes an areal change and a zone at t(i) has association with several ones at t(i−1) corresponds to a topological transformation. As a field-object, a UHI has also both active and inactive periods connecting with each other caused by status transitions, which finally constructs a complete life-cycle. To track the continuous evolution of UHIs observed by a series of discrete thermal data, six hierarchical graphs were developed to describe their evolutionary processes in different description granularities. Based on the air temperature data collected from weather stations on an hourly basis, results suggest that our spatiotemporal data model is effective to describe the changes of UHIs and is able to reveal evolutionary trends of UHIs. Results also suggest that the model is able to detect abnormal phenomena such as significant UHIs occurring at the noon on a raining day. 3. The results have been published in several journal publications supported by this project (please refer to the list of publication in other section). 4. We have also extended the development of the GIS system with the design of a spatiotemporal database for storing relevant environmental data, i.e. research work to analysis causative factors of UHIs. By modeling the anthropocentric heat fluxes generated from vehicles for year 2015, we have found that vehicular flow is one of the most important causative factors that makes UHIs severe, especially in mega cities such as Hong Kong. This research has been published in Scientific Reports – Nature. This GIS system and the spatiotemporal database have now been further extended to the estimation of solar radiation fluxes at the 3D domain inside a complex city. The extended system has already been able to map and visualize 3D solar radiation fluxes with multiple reflection on both the rooftops, facades, and ground areas of buildings.

515513.label: Major findings and research outcome
515513.value: 1. This research has designed an object-oriented dynamic model to reconstruct the evolutionary process of UHIs. Each UHI was modeled as a spatiotemporal field-object with its own life-cycle. The dynamic behavior of an UHI was defined by a series of filiations (e.g. expansion and contraction). Results suggest that the model can effectively identify different behaviors and status of UHIs, and reveal the spatiotemporal behavior of each of them. On a daily basis, UHIs normally appear after sunset, mostly growing and merging together before midnight, becoming stable and more significant after midnight, and finally split and disappear rapidly at dawn. On a seasonal basis, UHIs expand and their intensities increase, and the daily occurrences extend during the summer seasons; while the trends are reversed during the winter seasons. 2. This research also conceptualizes each UHI as an object, which simultaneously has thematic and spatial behaviors, and develops a graph that can depict periodic life-time transitions triggered by these behaviors. Results indicate that the developed model can effectively track the spatial and thematic evolution of urban heat islands through continuous time, and revealing the periodical patterns and abnormal cases sensitively. Several findings are summarized as follows. a) UHIs have periodic evolution in the daily basis, which can be caused by anthropogenic heat (i.e. heat fluxes generated by vehicles) and particular land covers (i.e. concrete seaports surrounded by vegetation). b) UHIs have evolutionary trends over seasons. In the summer, daily occurrence of UHIs extends, daily temperature variation increases, and the areas of UHIs grow. However, the trends are contrary in the winter. It is supposed that UHI evolution is periodic in the seasonal basis. c) UHI is normally more significant in the nighttime in both summer and winter. In an abnormal situation, it can also be obvious in the daytime if it is a raining day and the previous day was sunny. d) UHIs defined in different magnitudes have different types of spatial behaviors, and heat sinks can affiliate to UHIs during particular time periods. 3. This research also developed a simple and robust cell-transmission-model to simulate all the possible cell-based origin-destination trajectories of vehicular flows over time, based on the traffic counting stations. Results show that the heat patterns have notable daily and weekly periodical circulation/pattern, and volumes of heat vary significantly in different grid cells. The findings suggest that vehicular flows in some places are the dominating influential factor that make the UHI phenomenon more remarkable.

515513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
515513.value: Another interesting study is to estimate the solar radiation and quantify its contribution to the UHIs accurately. A research has recently been conducted to further extend our developed GIS system and spatiotemporal database from this project to estimate the solar radiation at the 3D domain inside a complex city, which allows solar radiations to shine on the 3D urban areas at any given time and multiple reflections of solar radiation are considered. Multiple reflections consequentially create accumulation and dispersion of fluxes in different locations, which lead to the diversity of the solar energy hence generating diversity of micro-UHIs. Empirical evaluations through the observation of solar radiation fluxes in Hong Kong suggest that the model can estimate solar energy accurately in both spatial and temporal domains. Moreover, high computational efficiency obtained in a spatial database management system suggests that the model can be widely used to provide effective decision making.

515513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
515513.value: An Urban Heat Island (UHI) is an urban area whose temperature is higher than in surrounding rural areas. This phenomenon is mostly observed in large and dense metropolitan cities and is caused by different factors such as the concentration of high buildings limiting air circulation and building surface heat radiating and warming the air at night time. The UHI effect is particularly intense in Hong Kong and it is therefore important to understand its causes and consequences to ensure a sustainable development of the city. Modeling thematic and spatial integrated dynamic behaviors of UHIs through continuous time is vital to understand the evolution of this phenomenon and to analyze the warming trends in urban areas. However, previous studies can only track the spatial behaviors of UHI (i.e. shape and topological variation). Thus, this research designed each urban heat island as an object which has thematic and spatial behaviors simultaneously and proposed six hierarchical graphs that depicted periodic life-time transitions triggered by the behaviors. The model was implemented in an object-relational database, and results indicated that the model could track the spatial and thematic evolution of UHIs through continuous time effectively, and also could reveal the periodical patterns and abnormal phenomenon.

515713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
515713.value: Auxetic yarn is a kind of non-conventional yarn which laterally expends when stretched. When properly understood and applied in fabric structures, this kind of yarn can be exploited for a number of applications such as functional clothing with improved comfort, smart bandages with automatic drugs delivery capacity, composite reinforcement with improved interface property between fiber and matrix, etc. The most important point to the realization of the auxetic yarn is the proper design of the yarn structure and its manufacturing process. A survey of the literature has shown limited studies in this special area. Therefore, there is a need for a basic understanding of auxetic effect, mechanical behavior and manufacturing process of such yarn structure. More specifically, the project will deal with fundamental issues of the structure and mechanical behavior of auxetic composite yarn which is formed by twisting together two kinds of single yarns with different stiffenesses and diameters in a special arrangement. Based on previous works done by the applicants, a special yarn manufacturing process will be developed to produce this non-conventional yarn structure. Various auxetic composite yarn samples will be produced using different kinds of fiber materials. Both theoretical and experimental studies will be conducted to investigate their auxetic properties and mechanical behavior. As examples, auxetic composite yarns will be used to produce woven and knitted fabrics for functional sportswear, smart bandages and composite reinforcement. 負泊松比紗線是一種非常規的的紗線，它受到拉伸時側向會變粗。正確理解它的結構和特性並配合適當的織物結構，這種紗線能夠開發出一系列的應用，如改進舒適性的功能性服裝、自動釋放藥物的繃帶和能改善纖維和機體界面性能的復合材料增強體。為達到此目的，最重要的是合理地設計負泊松比紗線結構和它的加工工藝。詳細的文獻分析表明在該領域的研究非常有限。這樣，需要對這種紗線的負泊松比效應、力學特性和制作工藝有一個系統的研究。 具體地講，本項目將致力於探討由兩種不同粗細和剛度單紗加撚而成的負泊松比復合紗線的結構和力學性能的基礎性問題。基於本項目申請人先前的研究工作，一種特殊的制造工藝先開發出來用於生產這種非常規的紗線結構。然後，采用不同類型的纖維材料，生產出各種負泊松比復合紗線試樣。最後，通過理論和實驗研究來探討這些紗線的負泊松比效應和力學特性。作為實例，負泊松比復合紗線將用來生產用於功能性運動服、智能繃帶和復合材料增強的機織物和針織物。

515713.label: Realisation of objectives
515713.value: Objective 1: This objective has been totally achieved. A novel type of auxetic composite yarn structure has been developed based on an innovative concept in which two types of single yarn components with different stiffness and diameters are twisted together to form an auxetic yarn structure via a twisting process. Due to its structural feature, the new yarn structure is also called as auxetic plied yarn in our publications. In addition, the relationship between the auxetic behavior and the geometrical architecture of the auxetic yarn structure has also been successfully established based on the geometrical analyses of the auxetic yarn structure. Objective 2: This objective has totally been achieved. A twisting process has been specially developed to fabricate the newly proposed auxetic yarn structure. Based on the developed process, a prototype was designed and built. A problem was encountered during the fabrication of the prototype due to yarn input tension and self-twisting when several yarns with different stiffness are twisted together. This problem has been solved after redesign of yarn input system. An invention patent has been awarded in China mainland to protect this new technique. Objective 3: This objective has totally been achieved. A series of auxetic yarns have been successfully produced by using the self-made prototype with different soft yarns and stiff yarns. A number of structural parameters and fiber material properties were used to produce the auxetic yarns with different auxetic behavior and mechanical properties, including auxetic yarn twist, diameter and modulus of soft yarn and stiff yarn. Meanwhile, the newly fabricated auxetic yarns were also used to produce auxetic fabrics with enhanced percent open area under extension for special applications. Objective 4: This objective has totally been achieved. A series of tensile tests were first conducted to experimentally study auxetic behavior and mechanical properties of the auxetic yarns as well as fabrics made from them by using an INSTRON 5566 tensile tester. A difficulty was encountered to precisely measure the size change of the auxetic yarn structure in the radial direction during the axial extension. To solve this problem, a high resolution camera was adopted to record size changes of the auxetic yarn structure during tensile tests. Meanwhile, a special testing method was developed to observe the cross-section changes of the auxetic yarn structure under different axial tensile strains. With both the tensile tests and cross-section observations, the deformation mechanism of the auxetic yarn structure has been well understood. In addition to the experimental study, the theoretical study of the auxetic yarn structure was also conducted. Some difficulties were encountered in the theoretical study of the yarn structure due to yarn slippage effect. Based on the first geometrical model which could not well predict the auxetic behavior of the auxetic yarn structure in the initial stage of the extension, an improved model called tilt angle model was further developed. With the use of the improved model, the auxetic behavior of the auxetic yarn structure could be well predicted. Besides the geometrical models, a finite element model was also established to simulate the deformation behavior of the auxetic yarn structure under extension. All these models can be used to guide the design and fabrication of the new auxetic yarns with predefined properties.

515713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
515713.value: This research project is concerned with a systematic study of auxetic yarn structure which expands when stretched. The auxetic yarn structure is first designed and fabricated via a special twisting process. Then, its deformation behavior and mechanical properties under axial extension are experimentally and theoretically studied. Geometrical and finite element models are developed to understand its deformation behavior under tensile loading condition. The auxetic yarns made from different non-auxetic single yarns are finally used to produce woven fabrics with enhanced percent open area under extension. The significance and value of the project is to provide a basic understanding on the structure characteristics, formation principle, fabrication method and mechanical behavior of auxetic yarn structure. Thanks to its unusual properties different from conventional yarn structure, the auxetic yarn structure developed will enable new applications such as functional clothing with improved comfort, smart bandages with automatic drugs delivery capacity, composite reinforcement with improved interface property between fiber and matrix, and many other high value-added and innovative products. 515813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
515813.value: In our project, we propose to develop a new fiber which is the artificial spider case silk made of proteins obtained by engineering the genes from spiders and through wet spinning. This fiber is known as recombinant spider case silk (RSCS), will have desirable flat tensile stress-strain (FTSS) curves just like natural SCS, good strain recovery and long cyclic uses. The RSCS proteins will be designed and prepared by using optimized codon gene recombination technique. Theories will be established for the relationships among protein structure, morphology and properties of RSCS fibers, fiber spinning and post treatment processes through systematic investigations with an aim to achieve the properties for designated applications. Among 5 typical silks from orb weaving spiders, dragline has received most attention due to its extraordinary toughness while its case silks, namely, tubuliform silks, possessing FTSS properties have not yet been really valued. In fact, this behavior of silks is highly desirable, but not found in existing textile fibers. It is very useful for textile applications e.g., pressure garments and socks for diabetics, which need constant pressure under different elongations. The traditional pressure garments such as those for burn injuries and varicose vein patients with elastic fibers have inherent disadvantages that larger elongation is along with larger force, leading to an uncomfortable sensation or worsening of the condition of the wearers. Natural SCSs can give sufficient stress under an initial elongation and the stress do not vary within a large range of elongation thus can keep pressure constant without changing garment sizes. The project biomimics SCSc based on RSCS proteins with smart properties for garment applications. The fiber can automatically adapt to body shapes achieving constant pressure, while the elongation will be recovered to its original length smartly by washing for repeated uses due to its shape memory effect. This very original research can inspire a new generation of materials for various applications, particularly pressure garments and comfort wears in textiles. It is a completely-new direction for applying spider silks to different areas. The knowledge generated from the project will be useful for the production of RSCSs, which will create opportunities for industrialization of protein materials. This project can make Hong Kong a pioneer in academic research of spider case silks for textile applications, thus enhance the international influence of Hong Kong in high performance materials research and reinforce its position as a leader in textile applications. 在本專案中，我們計畫開發一種新型纖維——人造蜘蛛包卵絲。這種蜘蛛絲是通過將從蜘蛛基因中獲得的蛋白質進行濕法紡絲來制得的。這種被稱作重組蜘蛛包卵絲（RSCS）的纖維應像天然的蜘蛛包卵絲一樣具有理想的平面拉伸應力－應變曲線，良好的應變回復和較長的使用週期。這種重組蜘蛛絲蛋白是通過優化的密碼子基因重組技術進行設計和製備的。同時，我們也會對蛋白質結構，重組蜘蛛包卵絲的形態和性質，紡絲及後處理過程，運用系統觀察的方法進行理論研究，以使其達到預期應用所要求的性能。在5種典型的從圓蛛上獲得的蛛絲中，牽引絲由於其超強的韌性得到了最多的關注，然而它的包卵絲，又名管狀腺絲，所具有的平面拉伸應力－應變還沒有被真正測量出來。事實上，蜘蛛絲的這種特性正是人們所期望擁有但卻沒有在其他紡織纖維中發現的。這在紡織領域是非常有用的，比如給糖尿病患者使用的壓力服和壓力襪就需要在不同的伸長下具有持續的壓力，而傳統的壓力服如給燒傷病人和靜脈曲張患者使用的由彈性纖維製成的壓力服則具有先天的缺陷，那就是更多的伸長就意味著更大的力，這將會給患者帶來不舒適感或是使患者的情況變得更糟。而天然的蜘蛛包卵絲可以在一個初始的伸長下提供足夠的壓力，並且在一個較大的伸長範圍內，壓力不會改變，因此可以在維持服裝的尺寸不變的前提下保持恒定的壓力。仿生蜘蛛包卵絲項目是基於具有智慧特性的重組蜘蛛包卵絲蛋白在服裝領域的一種應用。纖維能夠自動的適應人體的形狀達到恒定的壓力，並且由於形狀記憶效應，纖維在經洗滌後可以智慧的回復到原始的形狀以便重複使用。 這個原創性很強的研究將會促進在多個領域中新一代材料的誕生，尤其是紡織領域的壓力服和舒適穿著概念。這是一個在不同領域中應用蜘蛛絲的全新的方向。本項目的研究成果對重組蜘蛛包卵絲的生產而言非常重要，它將會為蛋白質材料的工業化提供新的機會。本項目可以使得香港成為蜘蛛包卵絲在紡織領域學術研究的先驅者，從而進一步提高香港在高性能材料領域的國際影響力。

515813.label: Realisation of objectives
515813.value: Objective 1. To design and prepare RSCS proteins by gene synthesis and gene recombinant technology using optimized codon for achieving typical SCS tensile behavior. The gene encoding engineered eggcase silk proteins eTuSp1 were cloned, expressed and then purified in the E. coli system. TuSp1, from the black widow spider, Latrodectuss mactans, was taken as the template, in which the repetitive domain was composed of a single conserved repeat unit. Thus, single conserved oligo-nucleotide, encoded from the consensus motifs of TuSp1, was engineered with His Tag. In the stage of cloning, DNA construct was designed to produce truncated TuSp1. The eTuSp1 construct was engineered with a single repetitive unit for the following prokaryotic expression. To amplify the target cDNA, PCR with 7 forward and 7 reverse oligonucleotides were assembled into the eTuSp1 gene. The gene was optimized with condon usage table to maximize the expression. The eTuSp1 was amplified in accordance to a previously characterized TuSp1 cDNA with residues 1-161 (GenBank: AAY28947.1). Following amplification, the cDNA fragment was gel extracted and ligated into the plasmid vector pUC18-SN and subsequently transformed into E. coli. Restriction enzyme digestion and agarose gel electrophoresis were conducted to validate if the cDNA was inserted in the correct direction. Upon verification, the modified plasmid with the cDNA carried was subjected to the DNA sequence analysis. For protein induction, a 200 mL of LB was used as 10% inoculum. At midlog phase of A600 = 0.6–1, 50 mg mL-1 ampicillin was added and the protein was induced with 2 mL isopropyl-b-D-thiogalactoside (IPTG) at 37 °C for 2 h. Following induction, the bacterial cells were lysed under sonication for 20 min (10 s/10 s) using a Bandelin SONOPULS ultrasonic homogenizer. After sonication, the sample was clarified at 6000g for 5 min. The obtained supernatant was examined by Coomassie blue staining and immunoblotting. The protein was then combined with Ni-NTA agarose resin via the engineered His-tag with the purification experiment performed according to the manufacturer's instructions. Finally, the purified protein was determined by SDS-PAGE to identify the protein expressed by the clones. The resultant proteins had a molecular mass of ~15 kDa. One significant problem in this objective is the dissolution of protein. The obtained purified proteins are partly compatible in the water and very hard to be thoroughly dissolved in regular organic solvents. We have tried very polar solvents like DMSO and TFA, but the effect is no good. Eventually, HFIP (1,1,1,3,3,3-hexafluoro-2-propanol) is chosen as the suitable solvent for these proteins. Even so, it takes three days under a continuous agitation and 40 °C for the preparation of protein solution. This objective is finally successfully achieved. 2. To develop RSCS fibers by biomimic spinning method using the genetic engineered proteins. The microfluidic device was fabricated by the combination of glass and PDMS. Briefly, SU-8 was uniformly dispersed onto the clean wafer by using a spin-coating machine at 1200 rpm for 30 s. Then, SU-8 with the wafer was put in the oven for a pretreatment at 95 °C for 20 min. The channel patterns of the designed mask were transferred onto the SU-8 by photolithography method and SU-8 patterns were developed by the 1-Methoxy-2-propyl acetate. Subsequently, the PDMS slabs containing channels were prepared according to the manufacturer’s instructions. By oxygen plasma treatment, the PDMS and glass slide were quickly pressed together and then put in the oven at 120 °C for 2 h. PEEK tubes were attached to the punched holes. By mimicking shear gradients generated by the silk gland of silkworms, a microfluidic device was designed with an initial channel width decreased from 500 μm to the terminal width of 250 μm. Finally the fabrication of silk fibers was carried out in this biomimetic microfluidic chip. In the beginning, we try the wet spinning method to prepare silk fibers. One major problem is that it requires large quantity of purified proteins, which are normally quite difficult to scale up by using the gene recombinant technology. Thus, a biomimetic microfluidic chip is designed with much less amount of proteins. This objective is fully completed. 3, To study the effects of fiber spinning and post treatment processes on the morphology and properties of RSCSs. The effects of fiber spinning and post treatment. The protein was dissolved in HFIP (1,1,1,3,3,3-Hexafluoro-2-propanol) with concentrations ranging from 0.01 to 0.3 g/mL. The spinning dopes and alcoholic solvents were separately extruded by syringe pumps into different channels of the microfluidic chip. By adjusting the protein concentration and relative flow rate ratios, silk spheres and fibers can be controlled. And above the critical protein concentration for the fiber formation, different morphologies of fiber can be obtained with a circular or irregular cross section. For improved mechanical properties of fibers, the post-spin drawing procedure was conducted to reel the silk fibers at a speed of 2 cm/s, 5 cm/s or 6 cm/s under a coagulation bath containing a mixture of water and methanol (90%). The flat tensile-strain curve is found in a low reeling speed. With an increased speed, the corresponding tensile strength is also increased. This objective is well studied and previously reported silk assembly mechanism has been verified here. 4, To investigate the relationships among protein structure, morphology and properties of RSCS fibers for achieving ideal properties of the developed fibers. For this objective, we first investigate the protein structure in the solution. As reported earlier, the protein can form liquid crystalline structure on in-vivo conditions, while they possess a micelle-like structure on in-vitro conditions. By using the synchrotron radiation SAXS, DLS and TEM, the micellar structure is proved in line with the amphiphilic feature of silk proteins. As for the natural spider silks, the silk fibers obtain a subtle hierarchical structure, including α-helix, β-sheet, globules, fibrillar structure, etc. The globules existing in the silk fibers can be related with the micellar theory, in which smaller micelles can be induced to form larger globules with increased protein concentrations. The relationship from micelles, globules/micellar aggregates to final fibers has been fully explored and the underlying mechanism for the fiber assembly is verified. The protein structure is extremely critical for the final fibers. The optimization of gene condon, a well-controlled aggregation state of protein molecules and an effective biomimetic spinning system make significant contribution to an ideal RSCS fibers. Even several works have been done, the silk assembly mechanism remains unclear and it is still challenging to prepare artificial silk fibers with comparable mechanical properties as their counterparts.

515813.label: Major findings and research outcome
515813.value: In this project, we have published eight peer-reviewed journals, attended three international recognized conferences and supported one Ph.D student. Details can refer to the Part C. Major findings are summarized as below: 1, Single repetitive unit modified from spider eggcase silk proteins obtains an amphiphilic structure, which induce the formation of micelles in HFIP. This structure is evidenced by the synchrotron radiation SAXS, DLS and TEM. A biomimetic microfluidic device is designed to study the assembly mechanism of silk spheres and fibers. To replace the function of ions exchange and acidification, the desolvation of highly conserved eTuSp1 was simplified by the non-solvent induced phase separation in the absence of N-/C-terminus. Solely by addition of isopropanol, the eTuSp1 was assembled as spheres, predominantly obtaining a helical conformation. In line with previous studies, spherical aggregates were considered as intermediates and could be induced into β-sheet-rich silk fibers by the shear and elongation. 2, Different from traditional emulsification methods, we have put forward an “HFIP-on-Oil” approach for the preparation of spheres. By using the suitable surface tension and viscosity, silk spheres were assembled as rapidly as 10 s under a lubricant-based system. The fabrication of silk spheres follows the theory of solvent-induced phase separation. The obtained particles with spherical shape were mainly attributed to the interfacial emulsification and the micelle structure. With regard to the increase of protein concentration, the average dimension and size distribution of silk spheres were both increased. Evidenced by FTIR, the freshly made spheres adopted as the same helical conformation as the eTuSp1 in HFIP. And upon exposure to ethanol treatment, secondary structure of silk spheres could be effectively changed to β-sheet-rich conformation. 3, In the presence of proteinase K, ethanol-mediated silk spheres exhibited distinct degradation behaviors by the aid of CLSM, revealing a tunable enzyme-triggered drug delivery. To optimize the electrostatic interaction for lysosomal drug delivery, the spider-eggcase-silk protein was genetically engineered using 5×His Tag with a tailor-made isoelectric point of 4.8. Followed by the post-treatment, silk spheres obtained an improved mechanical integrity with compressive modulus of 9.6 MPa by AFM indentation. Significantly, the accumulative release of doxorubicin by 96 h was approximately 4.5-fold higher at pH 4.5 than that at pH 7.4. To further demonstrate this release behavior on Hela cells, within 24 h, doxorubicin-loaded silk spheres were first observed to accumulate in lysosomes and then efficiently released the payload in response to the trigger of lysosomal pH.

515813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
515813.value: This project puts forward a new direction of studying spider silks, expanding the applications of silk-based materials. In this project, we have investigated the silk spheres and fibers for functional applications. To express the genes in silkworms may scale up the production of spider silk proteins, which are significant for the garment applications. The unique flat stress-strain mechanical behavior stressed in our project will induce the generation of polymer-based case-like fibers for various applications. Moreover, a series of natural protein-derived materials can be explored for market requirements. To study the regenerated silk protein/polymer composites possessing eggcase-like behaviors may be interesting. In addition to biological method, chemical approach can be an alternative for the preparation of polypeptides to pursue more advanced properties. The theories and principles established in this project inspire the development of artificial silk fibers with tunable structures and properties. The achievements and impacts generated by the research outcome of this project lead to the development of artificial silk-like polymers or fibers by using chemical synthetic approach in the future.

515813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
515813.value: Spider dragline silk is well known because of its outstanding tensile strength and toughness. However, another task-specific spider silk, eggcase silk, is very special and draws increasing attention from the researchers. To conduct this research, namely “Study of smart fibers from recombinant spider case silk proteins for functional garment applications”, we aim to explore a smart fiber with unique mechanical properties to fill up the market gap. In comparison to current synthetic textile fibers, this fiber obtains a flat stress-strain mechanical behavior, which is considered as great potential for application of pressure garments in the treatment of burn or varicose veins. Inspired from this research project, chemical synthesis route may be a good option to fabricate eggcase-silk-like polymers with similar mechanical properties for specific applications. Moreover, physical or chemical modification toward regenerated silk fibers from silkworms can retain the similar amino acid components but solve the yield issues. This project further investigate the underlying mechanism for silk assembly, facilitating the rational design of silk-based materials prepared in a systematic and biomimetic spinning method.

515913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
515913.value: In this project, we propose to construct a novel integrated electrochemical energy conversion and storage device, consisting of a dye-sensitized solar cell (DSSC) and a rechargeable battery to achieve the hybridization of energy harvesting and storage. The integrated device is based on anodic TiO2 and Ni(OH)2 electrodes. The anodic double-sided TiO2 nanotube electrode works not only as an excellent photoanode of a DSSC but also as a lithium intercalation anode with high capacitance and excellent cycle-stability, while the anodic Ni(OH)2 electrode works as a cathode for the aqueous rechargeable batteries. In order to maximize the total energy and storage efficiency of the integrated device, the nanostructures and properties of the anodic TiO2 and Ni(OH)2 will be optimized by adjusting the processing parameters during the electrochemical anodization. Taking advantages of the metal substrate (titanium and nickel foils) and the electrochemical anodization method, the integrated device can be made flexible and can be prepared by a simple, cost-effective, and controllable fabrication process. If successful, the integrated energy conversion and storage device will show great potential for portable electronic devices. In the long term, the proposed research may provide clues to the solution to a larger scale simultaneous energy conversion and storage. 本項目拟構建一種新型的集成電化學能量轉換與存儲器件。此器件基於陽極氧化TiO2和Ni(OH)2電極，集成染料敏化太陽能電池（DSSC）和可充放電池構成能量收集和存儲混合型器件。雙面陽極氧化TiO2納米管電極不僅可做為DSSC高質量光陽極，同時亦可用作高容量和高循環穩定性的鋰嵌入陽極。陽極氧化Ni(OH)2電極用於水系可充放電池的負極。項目將通過調整電化學陽極氧化過程的工藝參數，優化陽極氧化TiO2和Ni(OH)2的納米結構與性能，從而優化此集成器件的整體能量轉換和存儲效率。此集成器件結合了金屬基底（鈦和鎳金屬箔）和電化學陽極氧化方法的優點，可製備為柔性器件，并且其製備方法簡單、成本低廉和製備過程可控。本項目的成功實施將使此集成能量轉換和存儲器件在可便攜電子器件領域表現出廣闊的應用前景，并為解決大型同步能量轉換和存儲難題提供依據和基礎。

515913.label: Realisation of objectives
515913.value: All the objectives are 100% achieved. To fabricate anodic TiO2 nanotubes with various kinds of morphologies by well-controlled electrochemical anodization: A series of anodic TiO2 nanostructures with various types of morphologies are fabricated by electrochemical anodization. The inner diameter of the TiO2 nanotubes, the wall thickness and length of the nanotubes are well controlled by the anodization conditions. The inner diameter of the nanotube is found to increase linearly with the anodization voltage and the diameter varies from 100 nm (at 40 V) to 170 nm (at 70 V). The anodization voltage is then used as a parameter to control the nanotube diameter. The thickness of the tube wall is modified by pH value of the electrolyte. The smoothness of the surface of nanotubes is adjusted by varying the viscosity of the electrolyte. The length of the nanotubes is controlled by the anodization time, which, in general, varies from a few hundred nanometers to several microns. To fabricate anodic Ni(OH)2 nanostructure by anodization on non-valve metal Ni foil: Anodization of nickel is carried out in unstirred aqueous solution containing 0.15 M H2SO4 and 0.0375 M CsCl, with platinum as the counter electrode and saturated calomel electrode (SCE) as the reference. A potential static holding for a certain time period is a crucial step to obtain the desired microstructure by anodization since Ni is a non-valve metal. After that, galvanostatic anodization is conducted. A series of anodic Ni(OH)2 nanostructures with various types of morphologies are fabricated by tuning the anodization parameters. The anodization mechanism of Ni has been studied. To assemble the integrated solar energy conversion and electrochemical energy storage device using the above fabricated anodic TiO2 and Ni(OH)2 as the electrodes: The detailed steps for the fabrication of DSSC can be summarized as follows: the as-anodized TiO2 nanotubes is first crystallized by annealing at 450°C in air for 2 h with a heating and cooling rate of 1°C·min-1. After that, the crystallized samples is soaked in a dye-containing solvent (N719 in ethanol), followed by rinsing in pure ethanol to remove non-chemisorbed dye before being assembled in solar cells, i.e., sandwiched between two electrodes (TiO2/Ti electrode and Pt-coated ITO/PEN counter electrode) with a spacer layer (25 μm thickness, SX1170–25, Solaronix) and melted at 90°C to fix the separation. The electrolyte (DMPD: 1.0M, LiI: 0.1M, 4-TBP: 0.5M, I2: 0.12M, 3-methoxy propionitrile (MePN)) is infiltrated into the cells by placing the electrolyte droplet in the cavity of the active area of the device before the device is sealed with UV epoxy. To increase the dye loading and hence to increase the power conversion efficiency, surface treatment of the TiO2 nanotube by TiCl4 is conducted. The rechargeable battery part is assembled on the other side of the anodic Ti foil after assembling the solar cell part. The rechargeable battery is composed of three components: anode, separator and cathode. The anode is the anodic TiO2 nanotubes that are directly grown on the backside of the Ti foil (the other side being using the photoanode of the dye-sensitized solar cell). Glass fiber cloth is used as the separator located on top of the TiO2 nanotube electrode. The cathode is the anodic Ni(OH)2 which is grown on the nickel foil during anodization. After placing cathode on the separator, this part will be filled with non-aqueous electrolyte (a mixed aqueous solution of 1.5 M LiOH and 4 M KOH) and finally sealed with epoxy. To optimize the performance of the device through the systematic study on the microstructure-property-performance relationship of the integrated device: The microstructures of anodic TiO2 and Ni(OH)2 are studied by SEM and TEM. Both XRD and XPS are used to confirm the crystallinity and composition of the anodic TiO2 and Ni(OH)2. The BET surface areas of anodic TiO2 and Ni(OH)2 electrodes are key parameters determining the performance of the integrated device and they are determined from nitrogen adsorption isotherms. The pore-size distribution of the TiO2 and Ni(OH)2 nanostructures is obtained from the BJH (Barrett-Joyner-Halenda) method. Cyclic voltammetry and galvanostatic charge-discharge measurement are used to characterize the anodic TiO2 and Ni(OH)2 with various nanostructures prepared by different anodization parameters as electrode for rechargeable batteries, respectively. The systematic results obtained are evaluated and feedback to the sample preparation step to optimize the preparation parameters. A conventional cell with a three-electrode configuration is used for the electrochemical characterization of the electrochemical performance. The electrochemical performance of both the anodic TiO2 and Ni(OH)2 electrodes are evaluated. They are employed as the working electrode, with a platinum sheet as the counter electrode, and SCE as the reference one. The cyclic voltammetry and constant-current charge-discharge experiments are performed in a mixed aqueous solution of 1.5 M LiOH and 4 M KOH by using an electrochemical workstation CHI 660C. AM 1.5 G illumination (100 mW·cm-2) is provided by a 300 W solar simulator (Model 69911, Newport-Oriel Instruments, USA). The integrated devices is charged under solar-illumination and galvanostatically discharged on a program-controlled test system.

515913.label: Major findings and research outcome
515913.value: • Various types of nanostructured electrodes based on anodic TiO2 nanotubes are fabricated and used as the anode for the dye-sensitized solar cells. To enhance the light harvesting, a multi-layered TiO2 nanotube/nanoparticle hybrid structure is constructed (RSC Adv. 4, 45180, 2014). A hierarchical TiO2 nanowire–nanoparticle/nanotube architecture is found to further enhance the power conversion efficiency (J.Mater.Chem.A 3, 20366, 2015). The angular dependence of a dye-sensitized solar cell is found to be reduced by coupling the photoanode to a TiO2 nanotube photonic crystal, a very attractive feature for practical applications (Nanoscale 6, 13060, 2014). By coupling an aperiodic photonic crystal to the photoanode of a dye-sensitized solar cell, we achieve nearly full-visible-spectrum light harvesting, as evidenced by both experimental and simulated results (Sci.Rep. 4, 6642, 2014). • Various kinds of Ni-based nanostructured electrodes are fabricated and used as electrodes for battery-type supercapacitors. Using a rapid thermal quenching technique, we obtain a NiO nanosponge. Although full of cracks, the NiO nanosponge electrode is robust and shows greatly enhanced cycle stability and rate performance (J.Mater.Chem.A 4, 8211, 2016). Ni@NiO core/shell dendrites are fabricated by electrodeposition in a Ni-free electrolyte, which show an ultra-long cycle life for electrochemical energy storage (J.Mater.Chem.A 4, 15049, 2016). A hierarchical Ni-Co@Ni-Co layered double hydroxide core-shell structured nanotube array electrode is fabricated by a template method using ZnO nanorod array. The synthesized electrode show excellent electrochemical performance for flexible all-solid-state battery-type supercapacitors (Adv.Funct.Mater. 27, 1605307, 2017). • Well aligned TiO2 nanotube/nanoparticle heterostructures are fabricated simply by immersing the anodized TiO2 nanotubes into water, followed by crystallization. The TiO2 nanotube/nanoparticle heterostructure can work as a three-dimensional anode with enhanced electrochemical performance lithium-ion microbatteries (Nanotech. 25, 455401, 2014). We also develop a facile technique to prepare highly porous TiO2 hybrid film on plastic substrate for flexible dye-sensitized solar cells with quasi-solid state electrolyte, employing an inorganic binder contained TiO2 paste. The obtained photoanode exhibits not only excellent mechanical stability but also improved charge transport property (J.Power Sources 271, 8, 2014). • Furthermore, we summarize the recent advances in photonic crystals for enhanced light harvesting in sensitized solar cells and fiber-type supercapacitors for wearable device applications in two review articles (J.Mater.Chem.C 3, 10665, 2015; J.Mater.Chem.A 3, 20863, 2015).

515913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
515913.value: The TiO2 nanotube photonic crystal itself can find more applications in photocatalytic reaction, smart windows and even in photosynthesis. It can be integrated with Ni-based electrode to realize more functionalities, such as the photo-assisted electrochemical reactions or electro-catalytic activities.

515913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
515913.value: Normally, the energy conversion and the energy storage are achieved in separated devices. In many cases, it might be challenging to store the converted energy. For example, it is very challenging to incorporate the electric energy (converted from wind power or solar power) to the existing power grid. In this project, we make an integrated device that can simultaneously convert the solar energy and store it as an electrochemical energy in a battery. We make use of the double-sided nature of the anodized TiO2 nanotubes on the flexible Ti foil. TiO2 nanotube layer on one side of the foil acts as the photoanode of a dye-sensitized solar cell. The other side is used as the anode of a rechargeable battery, with the anodic Ni(OH)2 as the cathode. The integrated energy conversion and storage device will show great potential for portable electronic devices. In the long term, the proposed research may provide clues to the solution to a larger scale simultaneous energy conversion and storage.

516913.label: Project Objectives
516913.value: Identification, Recovery and Matching of Extended Fingerprint Features: The key objective of this project is to identify discriminant features that can be efficiently acquired from 3D fingerprints and develop effective matching algorithms for accurate fingerprint identification. Inter and intra-class variations of newly identified features in 3D space will be studied and used to develop non-linear matching strategy, which is robust to noise and inaccuracies in the reconstruction of 3D fingerprint images. Fingerprint Identification using Photometric Stereo: Traditional photometric approaches use Lambertian surface reflectance model (as in our preliminary work/results) to construct depth of 3D surface. However the fingerprint skin is a translucent material and therefore non-Lambertaian model that can simulate the fingerprint reflectance characteristics will be developed and used to reconstruct 3D fingerprints to provide a single camera based low cost alternative for 3D fingerprint recognition. Comparative evaluation of 3D fingerprint identification performance: We will make comparative evaluation of 3D fingerprint identification performance using (low-cost) photometric stereo based and structured lighting based approach/system (available with us). Such comparisons will identify the advantages, ascertain performance verses cost trade-off while improving performance over conventional 2D fingerprint recognition. The effectiveness of new features and the matching algorithms developed in first phase will also be comparatively evaluated. Estimating Uniqueness of 3D Fingerprints using Advanced Statistical Models: This project will develop new theoretical models to ascertain the uniqueness of 3D fingerprints for the human identification. The probability of the false random correspondence between unique 3D fingerprint features will be estimated from the advanced statistical models and used to establish upper bound on the performance of the available 3D fingerprint technologies.

516913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
516913.value: Fingerprint identification is commonly used for the civilian and law-enforcement applications around the world. Traditional acquisition of fingerprint scans by pressing or rolling of finger against the hard surface (glass, silicon, polymer) or paper often results in partial or degraded images due to improper finger placement, skin deformation, slippages, smearing or due to sensor noise. As a result full potential from the fingerprints is not realized. Therefore, touchless 3D finger imaging systems have emerged to provide ideal solutions to above intrinsic problems. Such 3D approaches can also provide more accurate personal identification as rich information is available from 3D fingerprint images. The main obstacles for emerging 3D fingerprint technologies are: 1) their bulk and high cost, which mainly results from the usage of structured lighting system or multiple cameras; 2) lack of effective 3D representation models for the unique 3D fingerprint features and their matching methodology; and 3) absence of any theoretical/empirical study to ascertain the uniqueness of 3D fingerprints. The goal of this project is to make such significant advances in 3D fingerprint technologies for the real-world deployment. We will firstly design and develop a low-cost, faster, accurate and touchless 3D fingerprint identification approach by exploiting photometric stereo techniques which employs single imaging sensor. The fingerprint skin is a kind of translucent material which exhibits multiple scattering and specular reflections. Therefore, linear models are inadequate to simulate human skin and a great challenge for this project is to develop new theoretical models to accurately simulate fingerprint skin for the precise recovery of discriminant 3D features. Secondly, this project will develop 3D representation of widely employed 2D fingerprint features by recovering and incorporating minutiae depth and orientation information. Advanced capability to recover and match such extended fingerprint features will significantly improve the accuracy and acceptability of 3D fingerprint technologies that are available today. Finally, this project will develop new theoretical models to ascertain individuality of 3D fingerprints by quantifying the amount of information available in 3D minutiae representation to establish a correspondence between two 3D fingerprint images. A scientific basis for establishing the individuality of 3D fingerprints will not only result in the enhanced confidence/admissibility of 3D fingerprint identification but also establish an upper bound on the performance from the automated 3D fingerprint identification systems. The advanced biometric identification using proposed technologies will enable low-cost, faster, hygienic and more accurate identification of humans for wide range of civilian/forensic applications. 指紋識別技術在全世界範圍內被廣泛應用於民用及執法系統。在傳統的方法里，指紋圖案是通過在堅硬的平面（玻璃、硅或高分子聚合物）或者紙張上按壓而獲得的。但是由於不恰當的放置方式、皮膚變形、滑動、拖尾效應或者感測器噪聲，這種獲取方式通常會令圖像品質受損或獲取不完全。這導致了指紋識別的精確性沒有被完全體現出來。所以，非接觸式3D指紋圖像系統的出現，為以上問題提供了一個理想的解決方案。另外，此類3D方案可以提供比2D圖像更為豐富的信息，從而使個人身份的認證更加準確。 近年來出現的3D 指紋技術主要有以下幾個局限之處：（1）由於使用立體的光照及多個攝像機，其設備通常體積龐大、價格過高；（2）對於特殊的3D指紋數據，尚沒有一種特徵表示方式及匹配算法被廣泛接受；（3）沒有任何理論或實踐方面的研究可以確定3D指紋的唯一性。本項目的目標是對上述3D指紋技術的不足之處作出重大改進，使其可以在真實世界中部署應用。 首先，我們將會研究基於單個感測器的光度立體成像技術，設計并開發出一套成本低、速度快、精度高及非接觸式的3D指紋識別方案。由於指紋部分的皮膚是一種半透明的材質，俱備多重散射和鏡面反射的特性，因此線性模型并不適用於模擬3D的指紋結構。我們將開發一種新的理論模型，可以準確地模擬及重建3D的指紋結構。其次，本項目將開發出這樣一種3D指紋特徵表示方式：把重建的微細的深度及方向信息，添加到目前被廣泛使用的2D指紋特徵上，組合成全新的3D指紋特徵。本項目將開發出可以準確重建和匹配這種擴展特徵的先進算法，使得現時的3D指紋技術的準確率和實用性得到顯著提昇。最後，本項目將開發的新的理論模型以證實3D指紋的獨特性。通過量化3D指紋特徵中的詳細信息，在兩張3D指紋圖像間建立對應關係，3D指紋的獨特性可以得到證實。查明3D指紋具有獨特性的科學依據，不僅可以加強3D指紋識別的可信度，並且可以為3D指紋自動識別系統設定一個理論上的最佳性能。本項目提出的先進生物特徵識別技術，將在極大範圍內使民用及法律方面的個人身份識別系統更加低廉、快速、衛生及準確。

516913.label: Realisation of objectives
516913.value: This project was revised and approved with two key objectives. Two Co-Investigators were not involved in the project as the revised/approved project was shortened with about half of the requested funding amount. The first objectives of this project was ‘Fingerprint Identification using Photometric Stereo’. This was in fact the key objective and required us to address many problems in different phases. We firstly build photometric stereo based 3D fingerprint imaging setup as there is no such imaging setup available in the market. This task required us to devote significant efforts in the selection of camera, hardware/driver, LEDs and to develop a user interface. First objective of this project also included the development a 3D fingerprint database and this task was mandatory. This task was completed as planned and was basis of our research on the 3D fingerprint identification as there is/was no other public database for 3D fingerprint images. The first objective also required us to develop automated region of interest extraction and other pre-processing modules that are specific to the 3D fingerprint images. The 2D fingerprint images acquired to build the 3D model can themselves be used to further improve 3D fingerprint identification and such idea was also incorporated during the realization of first objective. Our first imaging setup [TPAMI 2015] incorporated seven illuminators and posed problems due to involuntary finger motions. Therefore, we modified the first setup to include colored illumination and developed finger motion detection module [TPAMI18]. In order to further speed-up the 3D fingerprint matching module, we developed tetrahedron based 3D fingerprint matching algorithm which delivered promising results and could avoid complex 3D minutiae alignment steps. Acquisition of 3D fingerprints using photometric stereo was quite successful as can be observed from the results in our published papers [TPAMI15]-[TPAMI18]. However, the Lambertian assumption made during the reconstruction of 3D fingerprints is not very accurate and therefore we made extensive attempts [TIP2019] to develop a numerical compensation model to address non-Lambertian surface influences. The compensation weights in this solution were judiciously adopted to reflect the reliability or the accuracy of the estimated reflectance. The second objective of this project was to estimate uniqueness of 3D fingerprints using advanced statistical models. This project for the first time, uniqueness of 3D fingerprint was estimated from the probability of false random correspondences between two 3D minutiae based fingerprint representation. Experimental comparisons [TPAMI2015] between false random correspondences using 2D fingerprints and 3D fingerprints were used to ascertain significant improvements in the uniqueness of fingerprint biometric when 3D fingerprints are employed for the matching. This individuality model can establish upper bound on the expected performance from 3D fingerprint systems. However, it does not consider dependencies among the 3D fingerprint features. It also did not account for errors in the localization and detection of 3D minutiae. Therefore we further improved this 3D fingerprint individuality model in by accounting for the observed variability in the 3D minutiae locations and directions. Recovery of contactless 3D fingerprints using photometric stereo required us to acquire multiple 2D contactless fingerprint images. The surface normal vectors acquired during this process can themselves be used to match 3D fingerprints. The key idea is to exclude computationally complex process for 3D reconstruction which also introduces errors in the reconstructed fingerprints. These errors are introduced as its difficult to find closed form solutions for the integration, i.e., well-known integrability problem, and mainly results from the discontinuities around 3D fingerprint ridge valley boundaries. This approach to match 3D fingerprints is detailed in [IWBF18] and achieves very promising results. Contactless 2D fingerprint images acquired during 3D fingerprint reconstruction can themselves be used for matching with contact-based corresponding 2D fingerprint images. This problem is very important as billions of contact-based 2D fingerprint images have been acquired and stored for a range of border-crossing and e-governance. This problem was also attempted and a new thin-plate spline (RTPS) model was introduced in [TIP 2018] to more accurately model elastic fingerprint deformations using splines. We further enhanced such cross-fingerprint matching capabilities using the convolutional neural network model, which is detailed in [TIFS2019]. This work, inspired by recent advanced in deep learning for biometrics [DLBook], required us to simultaneously incorporate minutiae features and the respective ridge map.

516913.label: Major findings and research outcome
516913.value: (a) This project has attempted a low-cost approach for the 3D fingerprint acquisition [TPAMI15], [TPAMI18]. Our research has shown viability of photometric stereo-based imaging to recover 3D fingerprints under Lambertian assumption. (b) A key problem with the completely contactless 3D fingerprint imaging is involuntary finger motion which can degrade the recovery of 3D fingerprints. Therefore, the colored illumination based methods and detection/correction of finger motion, as introduced in [TPAMI18], are required. (c) Key complexity in matching two 3D fingerprint minutia template is due to the required alignment of minutiae in 3D spaces. This complexity can be significantly reduced by incorporating 3D tetrahedron based matching as detailed in [TPAMI18]. (d) Fingerprint surface is essentially non-Lambertian and further work is required to recover 3D fingerprints using such non-Lambertian assumption. The numerical compensation model to address non-Lambertian surface influences in [TIP2019] can significantly help to improve accuracy. (e) The uniqueness of fingerprint biometric can be significantly improved by acquiring and matching fingerprint in 3D spaces. As detailed in TPAMI15, the probability of false random correspondence expected from matching two 3D fingerprint template is significantly smaller as compared to those using conventional 2D fingerprint templates. (f) Our theoretical estimate on the individuality of 3D fingerprints in [TPAMI2015] does not account for the errors in the localization and detection of minutiae. Therefore, further work should incorporate the uncertainty in recovering 3D minutiae to generate more accurate empirical estimate on the individuality of 3D fingerprints. (g) Success of 3D fingerprint technologies will require accurate capabilities to match 3D fingerprints with contact-based 2D fingerprints, which have already been acquired from billions of citizens in different databases. Accurate estimation on frequent deformations in contact-based fingerprint can help to significantly improve such cross-fingerprint matching capabilities as detailed in [TIP2018]. As illustrated in [TIFS2019], emerging deep learning capabilities can be successfully employed to further improve such cross-fingerprint matching capabilities. (h) 3D fingerprint data using photometric stereo generates 3D surface normal and albedo, which forms rich 3D fingerprint surface information. As detailed in [IWBF18], such 3D details can be directly be incorporated for accurate and faster 3D fingerprint identification. (i) Adverse influences from involuntary finger motion and the ambient illumination, during completely contactless 3D fingerprint imaging, are two key challenges for the deployment of photometric stereo-based 3D fingerprint sensing technologies.

516913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
516913.value: This project has made significant advanced in the development of contactless 3D fingerprint identification techniques. Despite the approval of only half of the requested funding, we have been able to create global impact by utilizing existing resources. The work and achievements in this project demonstrates that currently deployed fingerprint systems are not adequate to avail full potential from this biometric. Our team has been awarded US Patent on 3D fingerprint matching and this is applicable to any existing method of 3D fingerprint sensing. This algorithm for 3D fingerprint matching needs to be evaluated on the 3D fingerprint images acquired using other methods of 3D imaging, e.g. structured lighting or optical coherence tomography. Acquisition of contactless 3D fingerprint also generates partial 3D fingerprint images. Therefore, further work is also required to develop advanced algorithms for the partial 3D fingerprint identification. The funding approved for this project was far from being adequate and our team urgently needs resources to undertake sub-surface 3D fingerprint identification. Given the success of this project and emergence of many open research challenges, a new research project would be submitted to RGC to undertake much needed further work in this area.

516913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
516913.value: Fingerprint identification is commonly used for the civilian and law-enforcement applications around the world. Traditional acquisition of fingerprint scans by pressing or rolling of finger against the hard surface (glass, silicon, polymer) or paper often results in partial or degraded images due to improper finger placement, skin deformation, slippages, smearing or due to sensor noise. As a result full potential from the fingerprint biometric is not realized. Therefore touchless 3D finger imaging systems have emerged to provide ideal solutions to above intrinsic problems. Such 3D approaches can also provide more accurate personal identification as rich information is available from 3D fingerprint images. The main obstacles for emerging 3D fingerprint technologies are: 1) their bulk and high cost, which mainly results from the usage of structured lighting system or multiple cameras; 2) lack of widely accepted representation for unique 3D fingerprint features and their matching methodology; and 3) absence of any theoretical/empirical study to ascertain the uniqueness of 3D fingerprints or their superiority over 2D fingerprints. This project was devoted to address these challenges and made significant advances in 3D fingerprint technologies for their real-world deployment.
