517013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
517013.value: This project aims to develop lead-free potassium sodium niobate (KNN)-based multilayered piezoelectric ceramics with good and thermally stable piezoelectric properties for actuator applications. Owing to the multilayered structure, a large piezoelectric displacement can be achieved at a low driving voltage, which is essentially needed in practical applications. It is believed that a demonstration of the successful use of lead-free piezoelectric ceramics in practical applications will help to reduce the use of lead-containing piezoelectric ceramics, thereby improving the environment as well as our health. The work will focus to develop sintering aid package for lowering the sintering temperature of KNN-based ceramics as well as to fabricate multilayer actuators by co-firing the ceramics with inner electrodes. It is anticipated that the sintering aids will form a liquid phase to assist the densification of the ceramics at low temperatures. As a result, the ceramics can be co-fired with inexpensive inner electrodes such as Ag/Pd instead of platinum in fabricating multilayered structures; and thus there will be savings not only in energy but also in production cost. Moreover, the low-temperature sintering process is also beneficial in reducing the volatilization loss of the alkali elements, and thus improving the compositional homogeneity and physical properties of KNN-based ceramics. The sintering aids will be purposely selected and the sintering conditions will be elaborately designed so as to eliminate the secondary phase normally formed by the liquid. The orthorhombic-to-tetragonal and tetragonal-to-cubic phase transitions of the ceramics will also be adjusted to low and high temperatures, respectively, with the aim of attaining thermally stable piezoelectric response in a wide temperature range. It is expected that because of the good and thermally stable piezoelectric properties as well as low production cost, the lead-free multilayer actuators can be produced by industries to replace their lead-containing counterparts for various actuator applications. 本項目旨在研究開發無鉛多層壓電陶瓷驅動器的應用。基於多層結構的特性，大的壓電位移可在低電壓的情況下得以實現，這對實際應用極為有利。這工作主要研究開發可降低鈮酸鉀鈉(KNN)基無鉛壓電陶瓷燒結溫度的燒結助劑；目標是將燒結溫度降至攝氏1000度或以下，致使價格較便宜的Ag/Pd內電極可在製造多層陶瓷結構時取代鉑電極。此外，低溫燒結也可降低鹼金屬元素的揮發，節省能源，和減省生產成本。這工作也包括製造和測試多層壓電陶瓷驅動器。我們期望通過成功示範無鉛壓電陶瓷的實際應用，以推廣減少含鉛的壓電陶瓷材料的使用，從而達到保護我們的環境不受鉛的污染。

517013.label: Realisation of objectives
517013.value: Sintering aid packages have been developed for preparing lead-free KNN-based as well as BNT-based piezoelectric ceramics at low sintering temperatures. Ceramics co-sintered with low-cost inner electrodes have been fabricated and good piezoelectric properties are obtained. Layered structures have been fabricated and evaluated. The mechanism of low-temperature sintering as well as the multi-functionality of the low-temperature-sintered ceramics has also been evaluated. A complex of Cu/Ba (in a molar ratio of 71.5/28.5) has been developed as a sintering aid to lower the sintering temperature of the 0.91K0.47Na0.47Li0.06NbO3-0.09NaSbO3 (KNLN-NS) ceramics. Our results show that the complex is effective in decreasing the sintering temperature, improving the densification as well as reducing the dielectric loss of the KNLN-NS ceramics. For the ceramics added with 2.5 wt% of the complex, the sintering temperature is decreased to 1000˚C, the density is increased to ~4.4 g/cm3 and the dielectric loss is reduced to 1.0%. As the complex becomes molten at a eutectic temperature of 890˚C, the densification of the ceramics is promoted via liquid-phase sintering. Some of the Cu2+ may diffuse into the ceramics acting as acceptor dopants, and thus reducing the dielectric loss of the ceramics. However, partly due to the secondary phase and hardening effect, the piezoelectric properties of the ceramics are decreased, giving a d33 of 130 pC/N. Nevertheless, owing to the low sintering temperature and dielectric loss, the ceramics are promising for practical applications, in particular for multi-layered components. Ceramic square rods consisting of two oppositely poled layers have been fabricated as the piezoelectric vibratory gyro-sensors. The rod is electrically driven to vibrate at its bending resonance frequency. When the vibrating rod is rotated, a Coriolis force is induced, bending it in a direction normal to both the driving and rotation directions. An electronic circuit has been designed and built for analysing the detected signals to give a dc output voltage that is proportional to the angular speed. For the gyro-sensor with a length of 4 mm and a width of 0.6 mm, a good linear relationship between the dc output voltage and rotation speed is achieved in a wide range from -360dps to +360dps, and a high sensitivity of 1.11 mV/dps is obtained. Other sintering aids Li2CO3 and CuO/TiO2 have also been investigated with the aims of eliminating the secondary phase and thus retaining the good piezoelectric properties of the ceramics. Our results revealed that Li2CO3 is an effective sintering aid for lowering the sintering temperature of lead-free ferroelectric ceramics 0.93(Bi0.5Na0.5TiO3)-0.07BaTiO3 (BNTBT). A small amount (0.5 wt%) of it can lower the sintering temperature of the ceramic from 1200°C to 980°C. Unlike other low temperature-sintered ferroelectric ceramics, the ceramic retains its good dielectric and piezoelectric properties, giving a high dielectric constant (1570), low dielectric loss (4.8%) and large piezoelectric coefficient (180 pC/N). The thermal stability is also improved by deferring the “depolarization” temperature to 100°C. Our results also reveal that oxygen vacancies (generated from the diffusion of the sintering aid into the lattices) as well as a liquid phase (formed by the sintering aid at its low melting temperature) are essential for realising the low temperature sintering. Li2CO3 is also effective in lowering the sintering temperature as well as retaining the piezoelectric properties of Bi0.485Na0.485Bi0.02TiO3 (BNBiT) ceramic owing to its low melting temperature and the resulting oxygen vacancies. However, probably due to the lack of oxygen vacancies, Li2CO3 cannot retain the good piezoelectric properties of KNN-based ceramics in lowering their sintering temperatures. Therefore, another sintering aid CuO/TiO2 has been developed, and the mechanism of low-temperature sintering has been corroborated based on the experimental results. Our results revealed that a small amount (2-3 mol%) of the sintering aid is enough for reducing the sintering temperature as well as promoting the densification and improving the sinterability of 0.95K0.5Na0.5NbO3-0.06BaTiO3 (KNNBT) ceramics. For these ceramics, Cu2+ as well as Ti4+ have higher preference of substituting the B-site Nb5+ or Ti4+, and thus generating oxygen vacancies. Our results have then confirmed that oxygen vacancies as well as a liquid phase are essential for realising the low-temperature sintering. For the ceramic added with 2.4 mol% CuO/TiO2, it possesses a high density (ρ = 4.36 g/cm3), good piezoelectric property (d33 = 175 pC/N), as well as good thermal stability up to ~290°C. One of the sintering aids, Li2CO3, has been applied to fabricate Pr-doped BNTBT multifunctional ceramics with enhanced photoluminescence (PL) and good piezoelectric properties. The ceramics added with 0.25 mol% Pr and x mol% Li2CO3, abbreviated as Pr-BNTBT-Li-x, are prepared by conventional solid-state reaction method. Both Pr3+ and (part of) Li+ have diffused into lattices, with Pr3+ substituting the A-sites and Li+ substituting the B-sites. Typical PL red emissions arisen from Pr3+ are observed. Similar to BNTBT and BNBiT, Li2CO3 is able to reduce the sintering temperature of the Pr-BNTBT-Li-x ceramics to below 1000°C. Moreover, in agreement with previous studies, Li+ is also effective in enhancing the PL emissions. For the Pr-BNTBT-Li-1 ceramic, its sintering temperature is reduced by 240°C to 960°C, d33 decreases only by ~8% to 165 pC/N, while the PL intensity increases by more than 150%. Co-sintering the KNNBT-CuO/TiO2 ceramics with 70/30 Ag/Pd inner electrodes at low temperatures have been investigated. Our results reveal that due to the diffusion of Ag and Pd into the structure (as evidenced by the energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy results), the low temperature-sintered ceramics exhibit a high dielectric loss and thus poor piezoelectric properties. A new fabrication method of including one additional heating process at 1000°C has then been developed for eliminating the diffusion and thus realising the low-temperature sintering of the ceramics with good piezoelectric properties. It has been suggested that the ceramic powders can be densified to certain extent in the additional heating process, and thus the diffusion of Ag and Pd at the final sintering process can be reduced. For the ceramics co-sintered finally with Ag/Pd electrodes at 970°C, their good piezoelectric properties are retained, giving a high d33 of 168 pC/N.

517013.label: Major findings and research outcome
517013.value: Sintering aids packages such as Li2CO3, CuO/TiO2 and CuO/BaCO3 have been developed for lowering the sintering temperatures of KNN-based and BNT-based ceramics, and the mechanism of low-temperature sintering has been investigated. Our results reveal that oxygen vacancies (generated from the diffusion of the sintering aid into the lattices) as well as a liquid phase (formed by the sintering aid at its low melting temperature) are essential for realising the low temperature sintering and in particular for retaining the good piezoelectric properties. For the 0.95K0.5Na0.5NbO3-0.06BaTiO3 (KNNBT) ceramics, a small amount (2-3 mol%) of a complex of CuO/TiO2 is effective in lowering the sintering temperature to 1000°C. Besides the eutectic phase of the complex formed at ~920°C, oxygen vacancies are produced after the substitution of the B-site Nb5+ or Ti4+ with Cu2+ as well as Ti4+. As a result, the low-temperature sintering is realised. The ceramics possess a high density (ρ = 4.36 g/cm3), good piezoelectric property (d33 = 175 pC/N), as well as good thermal stability up to ~290°C. Although an additional heating process at 1000 °C is required in realising the co-sintering with Ag/Pd inner electrodes at low temperatures, the ceramics are promising for multi-layered component applications. Similarly, a complex of CuO/BaCO3 can effectively lower the sintering temperature of the 0.91K0.47Na0.47Li0.06NbO3-0.09NaSbO3 (KNLN-NS) ceramics to 1000°C. The low temperature-sintered KNLN-NS ceramics exhibit a low dielectric loss (1.0%), a high d33 (130 pC/N) as well as good actuating and sensing performances when fabricated into layer-structured vibratory gyro-sensors. On the other hand, a small amount of a single sintering aid LiCO3 is effective in lowering the sintering temperature of the 0.93(Bi0.5Na0.5TiO3)-0.07BaTiO3 (BNTBT) ceramics from 1200°C to 980°C. The low-temperature sintered ceramics possess not only good dielectric and piezoelectric properties (giving a high dielectric constant of 1570, low dielectric loss of 4.8% and large piezoelectric coefficient of 180 pC/N), but also good thermal stability with a high “depolarization” temperature of 100°C. The sintering aid is also effective in fabricating low-temperature sintered multifunctional ceramics. After the use of 1 mol% Li2CO3, a dense Pr-doped BNTBT ceramic can be fabricated at 960°C. Not only the good piezoelectric properties are retained (>90%), the photoluminescence emission of the ceramic is also improved significantly by more than 150%.

517013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
517013.value: Various sintering aid packages have been developed for sintering lead-free KNN-based as well as BNT-based piezoelectric ceramics with good and thermally stable piezoelectric properties at temperatures below 1000°C. Although an additional heating process at 1000°C is required in realising the co-sintering with Ag/Pd inner electrodes, the low-temperature sintered ceramics should find potential applications, as evidenced by the good actuating and sensing performances of the layer-structured vibratory gyro-sensors, in various multi-layered components.

517013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
517013.value: For environmental protection reasons, low-temperature sintered lead-free KNN-based and BNT-based ceramics with good piezoelectric properties as well as improved thermal stability have been successfully developed for multilayered component applications. Various sintering aid packages have been developed for lowering the sintering temperatures to below 1000°C, and the mechanism of the low-temperature sintering process has been elucidated. Oxygen vacancies as well as a low-temperature liquid phase of the sintering aids are essential for realising the low-temperature sintering and in particular for retaining the good piezoelectric properties. The low-temperature sintered ceramics exhibit not only good dielectric and piezoelectric properties, but also good actuating and sensing performances when fabricated into layer-structured vibratory gyro-sensors. Moreover, the sintering aid is also effective in enhancing the photoluminescence emissions of the ceramics when co-doped with rare-earth elements. Although an additional heating process at 1000°C is required in realising the co-sintering with Ag/Pd inner electrodes, the ceramics are promising and ready for use in various multilayered component applications.

517113.label: Realisation of objectives
517113.value: For the first objective, a methodology was developed which is able to consider marketing, affective design and engineering concerns simultaneously for defining the design specifications of new products. In previous studies, customer survey data is required to generate a measure of affective design. However, conducting a customer survey could be quite time-consuming and even expensive. To address the second objective, a multi-objective particle swarm optimization approach of mining association rules for affective design based on online customer reviews was proposed in this research. The proposed approach has two distinct advantages over the approaches developed previously. First, the nonlinear relationships between affective dimensions and design attributes can be depicted. Second, no market survey is required for generating a measure of affective design. Based on the approach, numerous association rules were generated that can be inferenced to derive a score for an affective design. For the third objective, chaos based fuzzy regression was employed to generate utility functions in which chaos optimization algorithms were adopted to generate nonlinear structure of utility functions and Tanka’s fuzzy regression analysis was adopted to address the fuzziness of survey data and determine the fuzzy coefficients of the functions.

517113.label: Major findings and research outcome
517113.value: This research is the first of its kind to propose a methodology of integrating marketing, affective design and engineering concerns for defining design specifications of new products. The proposed methodology and its implementation, and validation results were reported in the first journal paper (i.e. the first publication in Section C). To address the fuzziness of market survey data and the nonlinear relationships between product utilities and design attributes, a chaos-based fuzzy regression was employed which is able to generate nonlinear utility functions with consideration of the fuzziness of survey data. The proposed approach and its implementation results were also reported in the first journal paper. To further address both the fuzziness and randomness of survey data in generating utility functions, a novel approach, namely probabilistic fuzzy regression, was also proposed to model customer preference and generate utility functions. The theoretical aspect, implementation and validation results of the proposed approach was reported in the second journal paper (i.e. the second publication in Section C). To solve the multi-objective optimization models formulated in this research, a customized strength Pareto evolutionary algorithm II was developed which features an improved fitness assignment scheme and a new archive truncation method. The algorithm and its effectiveness were described in the third journal paper (i.e. the third publication in Section C). Quality function deployment (QFD) was adopted in this project for defining design specification. Based on the outcome of this research and the research outcome of the PI’s previous works, an intelligent QFD model was developed which is the most comprehensive and properly the most advanced one thus far. The proposed intelligent QFD model was reported in a book chapter (i.e. the fourth publication in Section C). To derive a measure of affective design, a multi-objective PSO approach for mining association rules was developed to generate association rules for affective design based on online customer reviews. Then, the rules were inferenced to derive a score (a measure) of affective design. The theoretical aspect, implementation and the effectiveness of the proposed approach were reported in the fourth journal paper (i.e. the fifth publication in Section C).

517113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
517113.value: In the proposed methodology of integrating affective design, engineering, and marketing for defining the design specifications of new products, customer preference and market status are in static forms but, in reality, they could be quite dynamic. Future work could consider their dynamic effects in the proposed methodology. In this research, probabilistic fuzzy regression was developed to generate linear utility functions only. The algorithm can be further developed to generate nonlinear and probabilistic fuzzy regression models by incorporating a chaos optimization algorithm for determining the model structure. To improve the authenticity of online reviews extracted for association rule mining, opinion spam detection can be conducted before performing sentiment analysis through style or content similarity and semantic inconsistency to detect and remove fake reviews.

517113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
517113.value: Numerous studies about product design have been conducted based on an integrated marketing and engineering approach. However, no previous studies on integrating affective design, marketing and engineering concerns for product design was reported thus far. Emotional/affective responses of customers to products have been shown important to influence customers’ decisions of purchase. In this research, a novel methodology of considering the three aspects for defining the specifications of new products was developed. Customer/market surveys were commonly used in previous studies of product design and the survey data quite often contains a high degree of fuzziness and randomness due to the subjective and inconsistent assessments of individual respondents. The fuzziness and randomness was not properly addressed in previous studies of generating utility functions. One the other hand, it was well recognized that the behavior between product utilities and design attributes is nonlinear. To address these two issues, two approaches, chaos-based fuzzy regression and probabilistic fuzzy regression, were developed in this research. The former one is able to capture the nonlinear relationships between product utilities and design attributes with consideration of fuzziness of survey data while the latter is able to generate utility functions with consideration of both fuzziness and randomness of survey data. To consider affective design in defining specifications of new products, this research developed a new approach for generating a measure of affective design. In contrast to previous approaches, no survey data is required in the new approach to generate the measure. The outcome of the project would help advance the research of integrated design and modeling of customer preference.

517613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
517613.value: 傳統地源熱泵技術需要建築場地外鉆孔, 占用大量場地並導致鉆孔初投資大. 因而, 近年來, 能量樁, 將地下樁用作地源熱泵系統換熱器,得以發展. 然而,以前的傳熱模型基於Green Function, 不能考慮混凝土樁與周圍土壤的熱物性不同,因而傳熱模擬不準. 另外, 對於樁結構, 也缺少在長期運行下的熱力分析. 因此, 本項目將研究能量樁的傳熱性能, 並研究期在長期冷熱負載運行下對樁結構和樁基的影響.

517613.label: Realisation of objectives
517613.value: The objectives can be generally divided into two parts: to investigate the thermal performance of energy pile; and to study the thermo-mechanical behavior of the pile, the soil and the pile-soil interface. As described in Objective 1, it is mainly investigating the effects of thermal properties differences on the thermal performance of energy pile. Both analytical model and numerical model can be established to study the effects. To investigate the heat transfer process in the composite medium (pile concrete and soil), the Green’s function was employed to develop the analytical model. The derivation of the 2-D Green’s function solution equation, with the auxiliary boundary value problem for Green’s function which corresponds to this composite medium problem, can be simplified as two 1-D Green’s functions. This method was applied to derive the Green’s function solution equation for a composite medium. Firstly, the Green’s function solution equations of the composite medium in the radial and vertical direction are established respectively. Then, based on the 1-D Green’s function solution equations, two analytical models are established to simulate the radial and vertical heat transfer process of the energy pile considering the thermal properties differences of pile concrete and soil. To consider the effect of different thermal properties in two dimensions, the new Green’s function is established by combining the composite medium Green’s function in the radial and vertical directions. In this way, the whole calculation domain is divided into four sub-regions. A 3-D finite numerical model was also established to validate the new analytical model. This is commonly believed to be a reliable approach to the modeling of complex heat transfer problems with arbitrary geometries in a composite medium. The soil region in the analytical model was assumed to be radially infinite, but this is difficult to simulate numerically. In numerical model, the soil domain is made sufficiently large to ensure the thermal energy released by the energy pile cannot reach the radial outer boundaries. After completion of the geometrical process, ANSYS ICEM was used to create the 3-D mesh. A zero excess temperature boundary condition was applied to the surface ground of the numerical model, which is the same as the analytical model. The numerical calculation was performed with the commercial code ANSYS CFX. By changing the thermal properties, a series of cases were then computed to validate the analytical model. This new analytical model successfully represents the different thermal properties of the pile and the surrounding soil. It has proven to be a new tool for energy pile design and evaluation. Objectives 2 to 6 are to study the thermo-mechanical performance of the pile, the surrounding soil and the pile-soil interface. Both numerical and experimental studies have been conducted to achieve the proposed research objectives. The pile-soil interface behavior under thermal loads is one of the key factors that influence the ultimate bearing capacity of energy pile and thus, the interface behavior was firstly investigated experimentally. In this purpose, a new direct shearing apparatus with temperature control (DSA_T) was designed, developed and employed. The temperature control system can simulate the heating and cooling process of energy pile. Concrete was selected as the structure material and two typical soil materials are selected. One is quartz sand and the other one is clay. The experiment campaign was divided into three parts: 1) preliminary test on soil sample, 2) interface test on sand-concrete; and 3) interface test on clay-concrete. For the first part, both the clay and sandy soil were sheared under room temperature to determine their normal soil mechanics properties. For the second part, i.e. interface test on sand-concrete, all the sand samples were sheared under dry conditions and a smooth concrete surface was applied during the test. All the prepared samples firstly experienced a consolidation process, and then a target thermal load was applied to the test chamber until the end of each shear test. Then, the sample was sheared under certain normal stress. For the interface test on clay-concrete, the loading path is basically the same with the sand-concrete test, but all the clay soil samples are run under full saturated vapor pressure conditions, and a rough concrete surface was applied during the test. From these thermo-mechanical experiments, it can be concluded that the shear failure occurs at the interface but not in the soil. Within the proposed temperature range, there is no thermal induced effect on the sand-concrete interface behavior in fully dry condition. For the clay-concrete, friction angle and adhesion strength has an increase of 24% and 63% respectively due to the high temperature compared with the case of normal temperature. Conversely, the friction properties decreased with temperature drop. The numerical study of the thermo-mechanical performance of energy pile was conducted using the commercial finite element analysis software, ABAQUS 6.13. Both heating load and cooling load was applied on energy pile to simulate the working status in winter and summer. As the short-term influence of thermo-mechanical behavior is not obvious, a long-term simulation was simulated. The model and the mesh generation were built on the ABAQUS CAE. The sensitivity to the grid resolution of this numerical model has been considered and validated. Three kinds of physical mechanisms were taken into consideration: 1) the heat transfer process from the geothermal heat exchanger to concrete pile and soil, 2) the mechanical behavior between pile and soil, and 3) the additional thermal stress induced by heat transfer. The results of the numerical model show that the temperature rise can cause thermal expansion of pile, and this deformation increases with the temperature. On the contrary, a shrinking deformation can be observed with the temperature decrease. The numerical study of the thermo-mechanical performance of energy pile shows that the thermal load induced stress not only depends on the temperature variation but also corresponds to the mechanical load applied at the pile top. The tensile stress only occurs with a limited value at the cooling condition, when there is no mechanical load. If considering the load force effect, no tensile stress was detected either in heating or cooling conditions. Under high thermal and mechanical load conditions, the local compressive stress can reach to 9.35MPa near the heat exchanger pipe at the heating condition, which is more than threefold to stress at the pile axis. The temperature rise increases the friction angle of the interface between soil and pile, and the expansion deformation also increases the normal pressure on the interface. The average enhancing ratio when energy pile operated for 15 days and 30 days under heating condition are equal to 33.39% and 34.40 %, respectively. The cooling process led to the decrease of friction angle and normal contact pressure at the interface between soil and pile, and consequently, the shear force decreases with the temperature drop. Compared with no thermal disturbance, the ultimate friction resistance of pile is weakened by 15.37%. Therefore, this variation of bearing capacity should be fully taken into consideration in the design and calculation of energy pile, especially for the friction pile. A safety factor of thermal effect should be added or considered in the design stage to ensure the pile can safely operate in the worst-case.

517613.label: Major findings and research outcome
517613.value: 1. Both analytical model and numerical model were established to examine the effect of the thermal properties difference between the pile and the surrounding soil on the thermal performance of energy pile. It was found that a large difference (three times difference in thermal capacity) in the thermal properties difference between the pile and the surrounding soil can lead up to 46.5% error in temperature response in the short-term, while the long-term effect of the difference is minimal. Therefore, it can be concluded that when there is a relatively large difference in the thermal properties between the pile and the surrounding soil, it is necessary to consider the difference to accurately predict the transient short-term temperature response of energy pile. 2. The heating and cooling loads on the energy pile can significantly affect the pile-soil interface behavior of energy pile, including the friction parameters which directly determine the bearing capacity of floating (friction) pile. A modified direct shear apparatus with temperature control was designed and manufactured for the experimental study of the effects of temperature variation on the concrete-soil interface behavior. The clay-concrete interface tests show that a normal temperature rise increased the adhesion strength of about 63% and the friction angle of about 24%, while the temperature reduction has opposite effects. On the other hand, the results of sand-concrete interface tests demonstrated that temperature changes did not have a noticeable influence on the interface behavior under cooling or heating operation. 3. A numerical model based on FEM (finite element method) was established to study the thermo-mechanical properties of energy pile. The model was validated by comparing the simulation results with in-suit experiments. The simulation results show that without head load, the axial stress has an approximately linear relationship with the changing temperature. When a certain head load is imposed on the pile, the linear relationship is only separately valid as the cut-off of zero. Also, in the studied case, a normal cooling load on energy pile led to an increase of 34.4% in the bearing capacity of energy pile, while a normal heating load resulted in a decrease of 15.37% in the bearing capacity of energy pile. Therefore, it is suggested that when heat is extracted from the ground through energy pile, the bearing capacity should be carefully examined to make sure the heating model of GCHP system with energy pile would not cause structural failure of pile foundation.

517613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
517613.value: In this project, the thermal and thermo-mechanical performance of energy pile were studied. In the research, the surrounding soil of energy pile is assumed to be saturated. Therefore, the complete research is limited in the cases where the surrounding soil is saturated or has a high degree of saturated. When the surrounding soil is unsaturated, the thermal gradients formed in the soil around energy pile would cause moisture migration. This thermally induced moisture migration is may have significant effects on the thermal and thermo-mechanical performance of energy pile. On one hand, changes in soil moisture content directly result in changes in soil thermal conductivity, which will greatly affect the thermal performance of energy pile. On the other hand, soil moisture content is also directly related with the soil matric suction, which is the most important parameter in modeling the mechanical performance of soil and pile-soil interface. Therefore, in further research, the thermally induced moisture migration should be incorporated in modeling the thermal and thermo-mechanical performance of energy pile. A simplified analytical model can be established to monitor the moisture migration due to temperature gradients. Numerical simulation can be done to study the pile-soil interface behavior considering soil moisture change.

517613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
517613.value: The ground coupled heat pump with pile ground heat exchangers is promising in reducing building energy consumption for space heating and cooling in the densely-populated urban cities. However, the thermal and thermo-mechanical behaviors of pile ground heat exchangers are not well examined and explored, which hinders the wide application of this technology. Therefore, this project tried to study the thermal behaviors of pile heat exchangers and to examine the thermo-mechanical performance of the energy pile regarding the pile-soil interface. It found that the temperature rise could cause thermal expansion of pile and a shrinking deformation can be observed with the temperature decrease. The temperature rise also increases the friction angle of the interface between soil and pile, and the expansion deformation increases the normal pressure on the interface. So, the possible variation of bearing capacity should be fully considered in the design and calculation of energy pile, especially for the friction pile. A safety factor of thermal effect should be given in the design stage to ensure the pile can safely operate. The research findings from this project can help researchers/engineers have a better understanding of the ground source heat pumps equipped with energy piles.

518113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
518113.value: In many large Asian cities like Hong Kong, with dense land uses and congested multi-modal transport systems, a large proportion of trips are made by various transit modes for different activities. For instance, the activity behaviors include the decision of whether to perform the non-work activity or not, whether to perform it during the commuting trip or, alternatively, to pursue it making a separate trip chain from home; while the travel behaviors are related to the departure/arrival time choices, location choices of the non-work activity, the mode and route choices. However, little attention has been given to the effects of various activities on travel demands particularly in congested urban areas with mixed land uses. In order to capture the impacts of various activities on travel demand, this project proposes to develop dynamic activity-based network equilibrium models and solution algorithms for estimation of travel demands by modes in multi-modal transport system. The proposed models will explicitly take into account travelers' behaviors regarding choice of activity and duration, choice of departure time, choice of destination, choice of mode and routes under generalized utility structures. The first part of the project will make use of the recent Hong Kong Travel Characteristics Survey (TCS) results to calibrate the activity and travel choice patterns. The second part will develop activity-based time-dependent network equilibrium models to solve the travelers’ activity and travel choice problems with taking account the congestion effects in multi-modal transport network. The third part will be the integration of the first and second parts of the project for estimation of travel demands by modes and parameter estimation of the activity/travel choice model with and without updated vehicle occupancy counts in the Hong Kong Annual Traffic Census (ATC). The proposed project has the potential to help the transport planners and traffic engineers understand travelers’ behaviors on activity and travel choices and their responses to congestion in the multi-modal transport systems. These issues are particularly important in most Asian cities with dense and mixed land-use development where various activity and travel choices are inter-related. The application of the proposed models also holds great promise for establishing the potential of using updated TCS and ATC data to develop/calibrate travel demand forecasting models with minimum recurrent effort and maximum coverage in the whole territory of Hong Kong. 為了更加綜合地模擬人們的日常交通出行行為，需要建立基於出行者活動的模型來將出行動機與出行行為關聯，模擬人們的出行選擇（包括出行路徑、出行方式、出發時間、換乘選擇等）及活動選擇（包括活動目的、活動順序、活動持續時間等）。本項目擬研究一系列基於出行者活動的交通模型的建立，並利用觀測數據和統計調查數據來進行模型的校準和驗證，從而準確地模擬和探究多模式交通網絡中出行者的行為，為城市多模式交通網絡的建立和完善提供理論指導和科學依據，尤其對市區擁擠的快速發展的亞洲大型城市更為重要。模型的應用潛力還具有重要的戰略和政策意義，可為大容量多模式快速交通系統的社會、環境和財政的可持續性評估提供基於出行者活動的先進模型和工具。

518113.label: Realisation of objectives
518113.value: In relation to the project objective 1, the relationships between activity duration and travel time of workers and students were calibrated with the use of the Travel Characteristics Survey (TCS) data in Hong Kong (see publication nos. (9) and (12)). An activity-based model was calibrated to quantify the temporal utility functions of the home-work-home activities of workers by time of day, while a departure time choice model was calibrated for better understanding of the home-school-home travel behaviors. In addition, a panel nested logit model was proposed for calibrating the interaction of household members’ joint activity based on the TCS data (see publication no. (13)). In the proposed model, deterministic and stochastic utilities of the household members were used to capture the observed and unobserved factors, namely, the lagged variables and the taste heterogeneity so as to represent the time dependence of intra-household interactions. In connection to the project objective 2, several network equilibrium models were proposed with consideration of both the activity and travel choices of travelers in congested multi-modal transportation networks. An activity-based network equilibrium model for scheduling daily activity-travel patterns (DATPs) in multi-modal transit networks under adverse weather conditions with different rainfall intensities was proposed (see publication no. (1)). In the proposed model, weather forecast information was incorporated for solving the individuals’ DATP scheduling problem. In addition, a within-day activity-travel scheduling model was proposed for the simultaneous determination of departure times for morning and evening commutes, together with allocations of time during the day among travel and activities undertaken at home or at the workplace (see publication no. (2)). The proposed model extended the bottleneck model to address the scheduling problem of commuters’ morning home-to-work and evening work-to-home journeys by using an activity-based approach. The properties of the model solution were analytically explored and compared with the conventional bottleneck model. Furthermore, a household activity-travel scheduling model was proposed to investigate the interactions between two household members (see publication no. (6)). Markov Decision Process (MDP) was employed to provide a framework of dynamic discrete choice process that allows the household’s decisions to have complex interdependence over time. The impact of intra-household interactions on individual’s activity-travel scheduling behavior was explicitly explored, and the variation in intra-household interactions across activity types was thoroughly examined. An activity-based network equilibrium model was also proposed for scheduling two-individual joint activity-travel patterns (JATPs) in multi-modal transit networks (see publication no. (10)). The proposed model can be used to comprehensively investigate the individuals’ activity choices and travel choices in multi-modal transit networks, including both independent ones and joint ones. To investigate the scheduling problem of transit services in multi-modal transit networks, an activity-based stochastic user equilibrium (SUE) transit assignment model was proposed (see publication no. (8)). The proposed model can be used to generate the short-term and long-term timetables of multi-modal transit lines for transit operations and service planning purposes. The interaction between transit timetables and passenger activity-travel scheduling behavior is captured by the proposed model. Other activity-based network equilibrium models were also developed to capture the interactions between land use and transportation network development together with their impacts on activity-travel choice behaviors (see publication no. (7)), to address the simultaneous optimization problem of fuel surcharges and transit service runs for energy sustainability of multi-modal transport network (see publication no. (5)) and to investigate the Braess-like paradox phenomenon in transit networks (see publication no. (11)). With regard to the project objectives 3, a maximum-likelihood method that uses multiple sources of roadside observations (link counts and/or plate scanning data) was proposed for parameter estimation of activity/travel choice models (see publication no. (3)). Plate scanning information consisted of sequences of times and partial paths that the scanned vehicles were observed over the pre-installed plate scanning locations. Multi-day observations were simulated and derived from the true parameters adopted in the choice models of activity pattern, time of the day, destination and mode. Statistical performances of this method were evaluated on a test network with different settings in qualities and quantities of roadside observations simulated from travel demand and supply model. Another maximum-likelihood method was proposed for calibrating individual’s and household’s activity-travel scheduling models (see publication no. (4)). Various model parameters were calibrated such as the parameters in marginal activity utility function and the coefficients of intra-household interactions.

518113.label: Major findings and research outcome
518113.value: As far as the project objective 1 is concerned, Travel Characteristics Survey (TCS) data in Hong Kong was adopted to calibrate the activity and travel choice relationships. The activity durations, travel times and departure times of home-work-home and home-school-home activities of workers and students were investigated by time of day, respectively (see publication nos. (9) and (12)). The TCS data revealed that the travel time to and from work obviously affected the departure time and consequently affected the duration of work. The results also showed that the travel time and its variation of home-school travel had negative influence on the departure time choice of school-home travel. The interaction of household members’ joint activity was also calibrated by a panel nested logit model (see publication no. (13)). Time dependence of joint activities between household members was found in the study. With regard to the project objective 2, various activity-based time-dependent multi-modal transport network equilibrium models were developed with consideration of activity and travel choices of travelers in congested road and transit networks (see publication nos. (1), (2), (6) and (10)). It was found that the participation of compulsory activities and the usage of subways (Mass Transit) will be underestimated if weather effects are not explicitly considered for long-term transit planning (see publication no. (1)). The demand-sensitive (with uneven headway) timetable of multi-modal transit lines was found to has larger effects than the even-headway timetable on the activity-travel schedules of trip-makers, including their activity/trip-chain choice, their activity patterns before and after work, and their daily use and allocation of activity time (see publication no. (2)). The joint activity participation would be underestimated or overestimated if the intra-household interaction for an activity is not considered (see publication no. (6)). It was also found that the joint travel benefit significantly influences individuals’ activity/travel choices. The in-vehicle travel time affects individuals’ joint activity-travel pattern choice (see publication no. (10)). Other activity-based network equilibrium models were also developed for multi-modal transit service scheduling of transit services and for development and sustainability of multi-modal transportation network (see publication nos. (5), (7), (8) and (11)). In respect to the project objective 3, a calibration approach was proposed and formulated as a maximum likelihood estimation method (see publication no. (3)). The accuracy of the calibrated parameter is, in general, satisfactory, showing the capability of the proposed method to significantly reduce biases in the activity-based model parameters that are normally estimated from household and travel diary surveys. In addition, calibration methods were proposed for individual’s and household’s activity-travel scheduling models (see publication no. (4)). Maximum likelihood method was employed to calibrate the marginal activity utility function and the coefficients of intra-household interactions. The calibration results were found satisfactory with the relative errors of most estimates within 10%.

518113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
518113.value: In this project, various activity-based time-dependent models were proposed for estimating the multi-modal travel demands and scheduling the activity-travel patterns in multi-modal transportation networks. However, most of these proposed activity-based models only consider one behaviorally homogeneous group of travelers. As the characteristics of different individuals or household members can affect their activity-travel patterns, the proposed models can be extended to incorporate multi-class household membership (i.e. one-individual household and multi-individual household) and/or different types of households such as two full-time workers with children, non-worker or part-time worker, and two retired persons. The activities can also be further categorized based on their socio-economic characteristics. The variation in intra-household interactions across activity types can then be examined at a finer level of detail. Furthermore, as activity-travel schedules on weekdays and weekends differ significantly, further study could be conducted to investigate the non-recurrent individual or joint activity/travel during weekend and/or public holidays. Logistical problem of sharing limited resources such as vehicle sharing problem can also be considered in future study to make the joint activity-travel pattern scheduling models more applicable for multi-modal transport networks in reality.

518113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
518113.value: Understanding of traveler’s activity and travel choice behavior plays an important role in long-term transit service planning, particularly in congested urban areas with mixed land uses. This research project thus aims to investigate the effects of various activities on travel demands in congested multi-modal transportation network. The activity and travel choices of travelers are simultaneously considered for estimation of multi-modal travel demands with use of available data in practice. The data from the Travel Characteristics Survey (TCS) conducted in Hong Kong in 2011 have been adopted for calibration of the relationship of the activity and travel choice patterns. Various activity-based network equilibrium models have been proposed for estimation of the travel demands in multi-modal transportation system. The proposed models explicitly take into account travelers' behaviors regarding choice of activity and duration, choice of departure time, choice of destination, choice of mode and routes by different utility functions. Traffic count data have been used for parameter estimation of the activity/travel choice model. The output of this project can help the transport planners and traffic engineers to better understand travelers’ behaviors on activity and travel choices and their responses to congestion in the multi-modal transportation systems. This can be helpful for improving the efficiency and reliability of the multi-modal transit services.

519013.label: Project Objectives
519013.value: To study the flame stability and determine the stable operation region of open gas-fired premixed flame burners burning the mixed biogas/hydrogen fuel in terms of Reynolds number and equivalence ratio of the air/fuel jet at incrementally varied extent of hydrogen enhancement. To investigate the combustion characteristics of the premixed biogas/hydrogen-fired open flame including its structure (length and feature), temperature distribution and chemical kinetics (laminar burning velocity and hydroxyl radical (OH) distribution) within the stable operation region as identified under objective (1). Effects of the major parameters including Reynolds number, equivalence ratio and percentage of hydrogen addition will be fully investigated. To investigate the thermal characteristics of the premixed biogas/hydrogen-fired flame when it is applied for the impingement heating purpose. The heat flux and temperature distributions on the impingement plate will be fully studied when it is operating within the same stable operation region. Effects of Reynolds number, equivalence ratio, percentage of hydrogen addition and burner system configurations will be investigated. To investigate the emissions of gaseous pollutants of HC, CO, CO2, and NOx, as well as particulate matters (PM) from the premixed biogas/hydrogen-fired impinging flame within the same stable operation region. Effects of the same major parameters as specified in objective (3) will be studied. Combustion and thermal characteristics of the premixed flame obtained from achieving the objectives II and III will be integrated to facilitate a thorough understanding of the formation and emission processes of the air pollutants under consideration. To address the safety issue concerning burning the mixed biogas/hydrogen fuel in domestic/commercial environments, with the aid of the results obtained from the investigations conducting under objectives (1-4). To investigate the feasibility of achieving ultra-low air pollutant emissions at the ultra-lean equivalence ratio when biogas is used as fuel, which is expected to be possible only by using the hydrogen enrichment technique.

519013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
519013.value: Due to rapid depletion of global hydrocarbon resources, there is an urgent need to seek for alternative energy sources especially sustainable green energy. Biogas, a gaseous fuel produced under the absence of oxygen by the biological breakdown of organic matter such as biomass, municipal waste, green waste and crops, may be the most feasible solution. Biogas contains essentially methane (CH4) and carbon dioxide (CO2), and is certainly a sustainable green fuel as it can be produced from waste materials. Methane is a very light gaseous hydrocarbon fuel and produces mainly carbon dioxide and water vapor when combusted with oxygen, whereas carbon dioxide is an incombustible greenhouse gas and is the major contributor to global warming. Due to the significant content of carbon dioxide, biogas is not yet a feasible substitute of the most commonly used hydrocarbon fuels including coal gas and liquefied-petroleum-gas (LPG) because of two major drawbacks: too low heating value and too high carbon dioxide content in the combustion products. These drawbacks can be overcome by upgrading biogas with the carbon-free fuel: hydrogen (H2), because of its excellent mass-basis calorific value and burning hydrogen can completely remove the toxic gas emissions of carbon monoxide (CO) and unburned hydrocarbon (HC), and the global warming gas emissions of carbon dioxide. Using hydrogen fuel in domestic/commercial gas-fired premixed burners encounters very high risk due to its highly explosive nature, very high flame temperature and unstable operation. Thus, it emphasizes the extremely importance of safety and reliability in utilizing hydrogen. The proposed project aims to fully explore the safety, stability, combustion, thermal and pollutant emission characteristics of gas-fired premixed flame burners using biogas as the main fuel enriched with a suitable percentage of hydrogen. Adding hydrogen to biogas at suitable proportion and conditions is expected to enhance combustion efficiency, thermal performance and flame reliability, and reduce pollutant emissions of the premixed flame burner operating with the identified stable operational conditions. This project is aimed to create a breakthrough in the development of an excellent sustainable green fuel as a substitute of the hydrocarbon fuels commonly used in domestic/commercial sectors in achieving total safety, improved reliability, enhanced combustion and thermal performance and a cleaner environment. The developed green technology will benefit Hong Kong most because fuels are usually consumed in urban areas of extremely high population density and the less than desirable ventilation systems in high-rise apartments in these areas. 由于全球油气资源的迅速枯竭，寻找替代能源、特别是可持续发展的绿色能源已成为目前的迫切需求。沼气主要由甲烷（CH4）和二氧化碳（CO2 ）组成，它作为在缺氧的情况下通过分解有机物质，如粪便、污水、城市垃圾、植物材料和农作物而产生的一种气体燃料，可能成为将来最可行的绿色能源，因为沼气可以从废弃物料中制取，从而是可持续发展的绿色燃料。沼气的成分之一甲烷是一种很轻的气态烃类燃料，与氧燃烧后主要生成二氧化碳和水。成分之二二氧化碳则是不可燃的温室气体。由于沼气有着较高的二氧化碳含量，目前还不能成为替代最常用的烃类燃料，例如煤气或液化石油气（LPG ）的燃料 。究其原因，一方面，沼气的热值太低，另一方面，沼气燃烧产物中的二氧化碳含量过高。然而，这些缺点可以通过将沼气与无碳燃料：氢气（H2）混合从而得到控制或克服 。沼气-氢气之混合气体的燃烧可以充分利用氢气优异的特性，如基于质量的高热值，与氧燃烧后只生成水，完全摆脱有毒气体一氧化碳（ CO ）的排放和不完全燃烧产物碳氢化合物（HC）的排放 ，以及温室气体二氧化碳气体的零排放等等。 氢气具有非常宽的爆炸极限范围，非常高的火焰温度和难于输运的特点，因此在家用或商用的预混合燃烧器中使用纯氢燃料有较高的安全风险。利用纯氢燃料首要的是保证燃料的安全性和可靠性。本课题拟针对沼气在某个适当的掺氢条件（比例）下,全面评估预混合燃烧器使用沼气-氢气之混合燃料的安全性和稳定性、燃烧、热量释放和污染物排放等方面的特征。可以预见沼气在混入适当比例氢气可以提高燃烧效率，热释放性能和燃烧器的可靠性、以及本课拟界定一些燃烧器的工况从而令到气体污染物排放降低。本项目旨在发展一种清洁的、可持续发展的绿色能源，并在开发家用和商用的传统碳氢燃料之替代燃料的领域创造一个突破口。作为绿色能源的沼气-氢气混合燃料拟具有较好的安全性、可靠性、优异的燃烧和热释放性能，以及更加环保等特点。开发此种绿色技术将造福香港，因为燃料集中消耗在人口密度大、通风不理想的市区高层公寓。

519013.label: Realisation of objectives
519013.value: 1. Experimental investigations were performed to study the flame stability and the stable operation region of open gas-fired premixed flame burners burning the mixed biogas/hydrogen fuel in terms of Reynolds number and equivalence ratio of the air/fuel jet at hydrogen enhancement of 10%, 20%, 30%, 40% and 50%. The obtained stable operation ranges in terms of Reynolds number and equivalence ratio were used throughout the whole investigation. 2. Various experimental methods including laser technology were applied to investigate the combustion characteristics of the premixed biogas/hydrogen-fired open flame including its structure (which is essentially its length and feature), temperature distribution and chemical kinetics (which is essentially its laminar burning velocity and hydroxyl radical (OH) distribution) within the stable operation region as identified under objective (1). Effects of the major parameters including Reynolds number, equivalence ratio and percentage of hydrogen addition have been fully explored. 3. Experimental investigations were performed to fully explore the thermal characteristics of the premixed biogas/hydrogen-fired flame when it is applied for the impingement heating purpose. The heat flux and temperature distributions on the impingement plate have been fully studied when it is operating within the same stable operation region as stated in objective (1). Effects of Reynolds number, equivalence ratio, percentage of hydrogen addition and burner system configurations were used as main parameters for investigation. 4. Emissions of gaseous pollutants of HC, CO, CO2, and NOx, as well as particulate matters (PM) from the premixed biogas/hydrogen-fired impinging flame within the same stable operation region were investigated experimentally and numerically. Effects of the same major parameters as specified in objective (3) have been studied. Combustion and thermal characteristics of the premixed flame obtained from achieving the objectives (2) and (3) were integrated with results obtained by performing this task to facilitate a thorough understanding of the formation and emission processes of the air pollutants under consideration. 5. The safety issues concerning the burning of mixed biogas/hydrogen fuel in domestic/commercial environments were studied with the aid of the results obtained from the investigations conducting under objectives (1-4). The results will be very significant and useful for industrial applications when biogas is commonly applied in the future. 6. The feasibility of achieving ultra-low air pollutant emissions at the ultra-lean equivalence ratio when biogas is used as fuel has been fully explored, which is confirmed to be possible by using the hydrogen enrichment technique to biofuel.

519013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
519013.value: Biogas, a gaseous-fuel produced under the absence of oxygen by the biological breakdown of organic matters such as municipal and green wastes, may be the most feasible alternative choice for the currently used hydrocarbon fuels. Biogas contains essentially methane and carbon-dioxide and is certainly a sustainable green fuel as it can be produced from waste materials. Methane is a very light gaseous hydrocarbon fuel, and produces mainly carbon dioxide and water vapor during combustion, whereas carbon dioxide is an incombustible greenhouse-gas but is the major contributor to the global warming problem. Due to the significant content of carbon-dioxide, biogas is not yet a feasible substitute of the most commonly used hydrocarbon fuels such as coal gas or liquefied-petroleum-gas because of two major drawbacks. On the one hand, heating value of biogas may be too low for applications. On the other hand, carbon dioxide content in the combustion products may be too high, which is also contributor to the problem of global warming. As a result in carrying out the present investigation, we have confidence to help the commonly use of biogas to domestic/commercial sectors by ensuring its high performance, perfect reliability and almost zero negative effect to the environment.

519513.label: Project Objectives
519513.value: Develop scheduling models for the different principal motivations of multitasking: This includes the development of models which capture the characteristics of those motivations, while ensuring those models are of reasonable computational tractability. Develop efficient solution methods for generating optimal or near-optimal solutions to the proposed models: This requires the study of the computational complexity of the solution methods, as well as the quality of the solutions generated by the solution methods. 519513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
519513.value: This research develops and analyzes mathematical models for sequencing and scheduling jobs under the influence of multitasking. Under a multitasking environment, the processing of a selected job suffers interruption from other unfinished jobs. Such an environment appears in various applications such as project scheduling, production scheduling, and scheduling of administrative tasks. There are various principal causes of multitasking in administrative and business processes. They include (1) a need for variety in work, (2) a desire to feel or appear productive, (3) a desire to demonstrate progress on different tasks or treat task owners equitably, (4) anxiety about the processing requirements of waiting tasks, (5) impatience with unavoidable delays in the currently assigned task, (6) newly arriving information or work, and (7) interruption by other routine scheduled activities. The mathematical models will be developed based on the characteristics of these principal causes. In this proposed project, we aim to analyze various aspects of the models developed. These include the solvability of the models (i.e., the development of algorithms for solving the models), the benefit of taking multitasking into consideration when the job schedule is developed (i.e., a comparison of the total cost of the multitasking scheduling problem with the problem where multitasking is ignored when the schedule is developed), and sensitivity of multitasking on the performance of the scheduling system (i.e., the effect on the total cost as the amount of multitasking increases). 這項研究開發和分析排序和調度作業於多工處理影響下的數學模型。在多工環境下，所選作業的處理遭受中斷從其他未完成的作業。這種環境下會出現在各種應用程式，如專案調度、 生產調度、 和行政任務的排程。 多工在行政和業務流程中的各種主要原因包括： (1) 在工作多樣化的需要，(2) 顯示生產力的欲望或需要， (3)證明在不同任務上取得的進展或公平地對待任各種務業、 (4) 對等待中的任務的焦慮，(5) 在當前指派任務的延誤的不耐煩、 (6) 新到達的資訊或工作，及 (7) 受到定期活動的中斷。這研究將基於這些主要原因的特點制定數學模型。 此建議專案的目標是要開發和分析各多工環境下的數學模型。這包括模型的可解性，研究作業計畫時考慮多工的好處 ，及多工處理性能調度系統的靈敏度分析。

519513.label: Realisation of objectives
519513.value: Objective 1 has been 100% achieved. We have developed scheduling models for the different principal motivations of multitasking. These include a general "scheduling with multitasking" model that enables us to capture the characteristics of several different principal motivations of multitasking, a scheduling model that specifically addresses the multitasking motivation of "a need for variety of work," a scheduling model that specifically addresses the multitasking motivation of "interruption by routine scheduled activities," and a scheduling model that specifically addresses the multitasking motivation of "a need to demonstrate progress on different tasks." Computational complexity of each of these models has been analyzed. Objective 2 has been 100% achieved. We have developed solution method(s) for each of the abovementioned scheduling models. For models that are of low computational complexity, we have developed polynomial-time algorithms. For models that are NP-hard, we have developed pseudo-polynomial-time algorithms. Objective 3 has also been 100% achieved. We have carried out computational studies to evaluate the performance of the algorithms that we have developed. We have also conducted a computational study to analyze the benefit of taking multitasking into consideration when the job schedule is developed, and to analyze how multitasking can impact the performance of the scheduling system. This study is conducted by using the abovementioned "general scheduling with multitasking model."

519513.label: Major findings and research outcome
519513.value: We have considered different scheduling models with multitasking considerations. For each of these scheduling models, we have analyzed its computational complexity and developed practical solution methods. These models and algorithms enable practitioners to incorporate multitasking into their scheduling systems. Our computational results also provide important insights to decision makers in administrative, manufacturing, and process management applications. Our findings include: (1) Multitasking can create significant and costly interruptions in scheduling problems. (2) Several scheduling problems with multitasking do not respond well to the use of solution procedures designed for the corresponding classical problems. Hence, new solution procedures are needed, especially if finding an optimal solution is important. (3) Using our models and solution methods, companies can determine how much it would be worthwhile to invest in systems or processes in order to eliminate or encourage multitasking.

519513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
519513.value: There are several future directions for research on scheduling with multitasking. First, there are additional motivations for multitasking that should be modeled stochastically. Thus, developing and analyzing these stochastic multitasking problems is an interesting future research direction. Second, job rejection is a strategy to reduce multitasking in a scheduling system. Extension of our scheduling models through incorporating job rejection decisions is another direction for future research. Third, multitasking can also be reduced by injecting additional resources into the scheduling system to reduce job processing times. Extension of our scheduling models through incorporating job crashing decisions in also a future research direction.

519513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
519513.value: Multitasking, or the interruption of a primary task by another task that is available, is something that is frequently observed and practiced. Everyday examples occur in manufacturing and service activities, health care, computer processing, business processes, and even in leisure activities and social interactions. Boredom with the task at hand, anxiety about others that are waiting, and interruption by routine scheduled activities all contribute to multitasking. Discussions of multitasking abound within the literature of behavioral psychology, operations management, cognitive engineering, and project management. The multitasking environment is unique within the scheduling literature, in that the job that is scheduled is not always the job that is processed. This is an example of “inadvertent scheduling.” This project has considered the influence of multitasking on the efficiency of some simple scheduling systems. It provides mathematical analysis of the effect of multitasking on scheduling problems that arise in these systems. Our study finds that classical algorithms typically fail to find optimal solutions in the presence of multitasking. We therefore have developed new optimal algorithms and accompanying intractability results for the multitasking environment. We have also evaluated the cost and value of multitasking, which a computational study finds to be substantial in most cases.

519913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
519913.value: 最優停時問題在科學、工程、經濟和金融投資等領域中具有重要實際應用。在過去的幾十年中該問題對帶確定系數的隨機系統已被廣泛研究和發展。然而，帶隨機系數的動態問題尚未被深入研究和發展，如金融衍生工具中的利率結構和隨機波動問題。這要求發展帶隨機系數的動態系統及其優化的科研。此項目主要研究帶隨機系數動態問題的最優控制和最優停時。發展一類新方法完全不同於當前文獻之中的帶確定系數隨機系統所得的理論結果， 並克服由隨機系數所引起之困難。更進一步將其應用於一類在財富管理中具有挑戰性且相當實際和重要的敏感性決策問題。該類模型主要幫助投資者在投資過程中選擇合理的決策和恰當的時機處理風險資產以取得一定的回報。

520213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
520213.value: The control of flow in the microcirculation is crucial to ensure blood supply to the tissues. The spontaneous time-dependent contraction and relaxation of small arteries and arterioles was observed 160 years ago and is termed as vasomotion. Vasomotion is an intrinsic phenomenon unrelated to cardiac rhythm or neural and hormonal regulation; and it works as a local control mechanism to regulate the microvascular blood flow, of which contributes to ensuring blood supply to the tissues, despite large pressure variations. Vasomotion is important for optimal blood flow and tissue dialysis and may have considerable implications in the physiology and pathology of the arterial system. In spite of tremendous studies on vasomotion, the physiological role of vasomotion is not clear. Much of our understanding is based upon direct observations of intramuscular arterioles in response to experimental stimuli through the use of intravital microscopy. There are two major questions in understanding the vasomotion mechanism, one is how it is generated, and the other is its effects on flow delivery. In this particular proposal, we will not study the cause of the various vasomotion, but to explore how different types of vasomotion affect the flow delivery. Vasomotion is likely caused by contraction of smooth muscle and is the mechanical mechanism. The branches within the microvascular network oscillate with different frequencies and amplitudes, and they would interact to optimize the fluid delivery. These interactions can not be counted properly in the traditional one-dimensional theories, but can only be understood fully in a three-dimensional numerical simulation. Therefore, we propose to study the effect of vasomotion on efficient blood delivery through three-dimensional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation. The objective is to study the effect of oscillating frequencies and amplitudes of microvessels and their interplay on the blood delivery in a microvascular network. As the first attempt, the blood is simplified as Newtonian fluid and the arterial rhythmic diameter change is simplified as moving boundary with specified oscillating frequency and amplitude based on the available measurement data. We believe our study would help to quantify the relationship between vasomotion and blood delivery in microvascular network and improve our knowledge of the physiological significance greatly. 微循環流的控制對於確保組織的血液供應是至關重要的。小動脈和微動脈隨著時間自發收縮和舒張的現像在160年前就被觀測到，稱之為血管舒縮。血管舒縮是一種與心臟律動或神經和激素調節有關的固有現象；它如同一個局部控制機構來調節微血管血流量,即使在大的壓力變化情況下也同樣有助於確保組織的血液供應。血管舒縮對於優化血流和組織透析都很重要並可能對動脈系統的生理、病理產生相當大的影響。儘管已有很多關於血管舒縮的研究,血管舒縮的生理作用還不清楚。我們所了解的大部分知識是通過使用活體鏡檢法直接觀測肌內小動脈對實驗刺激的反饋得到的。理解血管舒縮機制有兩個主要的問題,一個是血管舒縮是如何產生的,另一個是血管舒縮對流體輸送的影響。本文不研究血管舒縮的起因,而是探索各種不同類型的血管舒縮對流體輸送的影響。血管舒縮可能是由平滑肌收縮引起的一種力學機制。微血管網絡裡的各分支以不同的頻率和振幅振盪,它們會互相影響來優化流體輸送。這些交互影響無法通過傳統的一維理論來計算,只能通過一個三維的數值模擬來全面理解。因此,我們將通過三維計算流體力學(CFD)模擬來研究血管舒縮對有效血液輸送的作用。目標是研究微血管振動頻率和振幅及他們在微血管網絡血液輸送中的相互作用。作為第一次嘗試，血液簡化為牛頓流體，動脈律動的直徑變化簡化為基於可測量數據且有特定的振盪頻率和振幅的邊界移動。我們相信,我們的研究將有助於量化微血管網絡中血管舒縮和血液輸送之間的關係，並極大提升我們對生理意義的認知。

520213.label: Realisation of objectives
520213.value: 1. The effect of vasomotion on fluid distribution in microcirculation. The control of flow in the microcirculation is crucial to ensure blood supply to the tissues. The spontaneous time-dependent contraction and relaxation of small arteries and arterioles is termed as vasomotion. Vasomotion is an intrinsic phenomenon unrelated to cardiac rhythm or neural and hormonal regulation; and it works as a local control mechanism to regulate the microvascular blood flow. In spite of tremendous studies on vasomotion, the physiological role of vasomotion is not clear. As the first attempt, we investigated the effect of microvascular structure on flow delivery in microvascular bed with composite flow oscillating frequencies. In order to achieve a better understanding of the biomechanical characteristics of vasomotion, 3-D models of the micro vessel networks are developed in this work. Three models are created with progressively increased capillary density. The constructed vascular network geometry resemble quite close to a structured tree model. There are three kinds of networks in this group. Model A is the simple vascular network in which one vessel is divided into two main branches after certain lengthen from the inlet. Then each main branch bifurcates into two sub-branches, and all the four sub-branches merge back into two main branches and one at last. Model B is similar to normal vascular network, which has more cross vessel linking among the major branches based on the former one. Model C is much more complicated, and the cross links are not in a plane. The objective is to investigate the effect of capillary density and diameter on flowmotion in capillary. With increasing the vascular density as B and C models, the pressure drop across the microvascular bed decreases significantly, and the pressure decreases greatly at the sub-bifurcations. The distribution of pressure is different for different models. Due to the asymmetry of the microvessel distribution, the pressure also exhibits asymmetric distribution. The oscillation frequency of vasomotion is within 0.001–0.2 Hz. This vasomotion can mirror human body conditions and initiate the pathogenesis sequence in some diseases. In the preliminary measurement of blood flow oscillations in radial artery at the wrist, a strong power spectral density (PSD) at ~0.1 Hz was found, indicating that low frequency flow oscillations play a dominate role in radial pulse pattern. To understand the interaction between vasomotion and cardiac rhythm in radial artery, numerical simulations were carried out. It is found that the natural frequency of the system decreases with the complexity of microvasculature system, and the inlet oscillating velocity interacts with the natural frequency to generate subharmonics. As the natural frequency in the constructed vessel system can be as low as 0.37 Hz, we speculate that the natural frequency of actual microcirculation is much lower, and the mechanism of vasomotion is actually due to the interaction of cardiac rhythm and microvasculature natural frequency. These works have been published/accepted by the book series “Fluid-structure-Sound interactions and control” published by Springer. 2. Cell flowing and adhesion in microcirculation The blood flow behaviors in the microvessels determine the transport modes and further affect the metastasis of circulating tumor cells (CTCs). Much biochemical and biological efforts have been made on CTC metastasis, however, precise experimental measurement and accurate theoretical prediction on its mechanical mechanism are limited. To complement these, numerical modelling of a CTC extravasation from the blood circulation, including the steps of adhesion and transmigration, is discussed in this chapter. The results demonstrate that CTCs prefer to adhere at the positive curvature of curved microvessels, which is attributed to the positive wall shear stress/gradient. Then, the effects of particulate nature of blood on CTC adhesion are investigated and are found to be significant in the microvessels. Furthermore, the presence of red blood cell (RBC) aggregates is also found to promote the CTC adhesion by providing an additional wall-directed force. Finally, a single cell passing through a narrow slit, mimicking CTC transmigration, was examined under the effects of cell deformability. It showed that the cell shape and surface area increase play a more important role than the cell elasticity in cell transit across the narrow slit. These works have been published in Biomechanics and modeling in mechanobiology, Cell Biochemistry and Biophysics, and etc. 3. The role of microcirculation in traditional Chinese medicine Spontaneous rhythmic oscillations in microvessel diameter are known as vasomotion. Vasomotion is the intrinsic property of small arteries and arterioles and is dependent of heartbeat, respiration, or neuronal input. The skin microcirculation is an anastomotic network of vessels with many crucial functions in which the blood flow must be finely regulated and tuned in order to fulfill all the demands of the organism. The laser Doppler Flowmetry (LDF) can be used to measure dynamic changes in skin blood flow over a small area. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) considers that there exist acupoints around body which are connected by meridian, and stimulating the acupoint is a typical therapeutic technique in TCM. It was found that stimulating one acupoint could enhance the vasomotion in another acupoint significantly. We argue that the vasomotions in these two acupoints could be correlated to each other. To verify our argument, we used the laser Doppler Flowmetry (LDF) to measure the skin blood flow at two acupoints, and carried out spectral and correlation analyses. It is found that the vasomotions related to myogenic activity are quite strong at acupoints and the correlation is discernable. The vasomotion related to myogenic activity at non-acupoint is much weaker and there is no significant correlation between the acupoint and non-acupoint. This work have been accepted by the book series “Fluid-structure-Sound interactions and control” published by Springer, and one journal paper is under preparation.

520213.label: Major findings and research outcome
520213.value: The major findings are: 1. The irregular micro vasculature would decrease the flowmotion and lead to reduction of nutrient and drug delivery which is consistent with the experimental observation. 2. The more complex of the microvasculature, the lower natural frequency of the system. The vasomotion spectral band 0.01-0.1 Hz could be due to the interaction of cardiac rhythm and microvasculature natural frequency. 3. It is found that the vasomotions related to myogenic activity are quite strong at acupoints and the correlation is discernable. The vasomotion related to myogenic activity at non-acupoint is much weaker and there is no significant correlation between the acupoint and non-acupoint. 4. In microvessel, the red blood cells migrate away from the wall to the tube center, resulting in a cell-free layer near the wall and blunt velocity profile. 5. It is shown that the flow resistance increases dramatically when the red blood cells enter into the stenosis and decreases rapidly as RBCs move away from the stenosis. Particularly, for a pair of stiffer red blood cells with the initial inclination angle of 90°, the maximum value of the flow resistance is larger; while a higher flow resistance can also come from a stronger aggregation. 6. Adhesion of circulating tumor cells (CTCs) to the microvessel wall largely depends on the blood hydrodynamic conditions, in the microvessel of 15μm diameter, the CTC has an increasing probability of adhesion with the hematocrit due to a growing wall-directed force, resulting in a larger number of receptor–ligand bonds formed on the cell surface. However, with the increase in microvessel size, an enhanced lift force at higher hematocrit detaches the initial adherent CTC quickly. If the microvessel is comparable to the CTC in diameter, CTC adhesion is independent of hematocrit. 7. It is found that the endothelial surface glycocalyx layer structure significantly influences cell adhesion function, by changing the geometry of the vessel, providing more ligands to form receptor–ligand bonds, and enhancing the forward reaction rate for forming new bonds.

520213.value: The numerical model can be used to further study the tumor cell adhesion and extravasation in microvascular system. The measurement method on vasomotion can be used to further study the effect of acupoint on vasomotion variation.

520213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
520213.value: Blood flow oscillations of 0.001–0.2 Hz are called vasomotion whose physiological mechanism has not been understood. This vasomotion can mirror human body conditions and initiate the pathogenesis sequence in some diseases. We studied the mechanism of vasomotion on pressure distribution in microcirculation, the effect of acupoints on vasomotion variation, and effect of red blood cell on turmor cell adhesion in microcirculation. Our study can help to understand the physiology of vasomotion and mechanism of tumor cell metastasis, which may lead to development of new therapeutic method for tumor treatment.
