520313.label: Realisation of objectives
520313.value: Summary: After a few years of hard work by the research team of this project, all of the proposed objectives of this project have been successfully achieved. The research outcomes have primarily reflected and documented in the 11 high impact papers published in internationally well known journals (such as JGR, Journal of Geodesy, GPS Solutions, Radio Science), 3 papers that have been submitted to JGR, Journal of Geodesy, Radio Science for review, 5 national/international conference papers and presentations (including 3 full papers for international conferences), 2 PhD students received rigorous training by this project, 3 awards/honors received by two PhD students who are trained by this project. A Hong Kong scintillation monitoring facility has been successful established to support this group’s long-term research in this area. The following paragraphs have given the specific details that have been successfully achieved in this project. The most detailed results can be referred to the journal and conference papers generated from this project. For the objective 1, we have investigated the rate of change of total electron content index (ROTI) and ionospheric scintillation indices (S_4 and σ_Φ) for low latitude regions. If each individual satellite is examined, the correlation coefficient between ROTI and S_4/σ_Φ is above 0.6 on average and sometimes they can be above 0.8, as observed in the figures below. The correlation coefficients are generally stable over time but the coefficients get high values in geomagnetically disturbed or active solar activity days. Moreover, our results indicate that low elevation angle satellites generally have a weak correlation between ROTI and S_4/σ_Φ. In addition to the correlation coefficients, the ratio of ROTI to S_4/σ_Φ has also been studied. It is found that the ratio of ROTI/S_4 varies between 1 and 4. For the ratio ROTI/σ_Φ, it varies between 2 and 9. The study of the relationship between ROTI, S_4 and σ_Φ allows us to use ordinary, non-scintillation-specialized GNSS receivers to characterize ionospheric scintillation in low-latitude region such as Hong Kong. This can help save a lot of budgets as the non-scintillation-specialized GNSS receivers are widely available in regional GPS/GNSS networks such as Hong Kong’s Satellite Positioning Reference Station Network (SatRef). Because of the abundance of the availability of the GPS/GNSS network data, the quantification and description of scintillation strengths can be better and more comprehensively specified by a large number of GPS/GNSS stations, instead of 1 or 2 scintillation monitoring stations as what has been done in the past. The findings obtained from this study enable us to take advantage of the large amount of GPS data recorded by common GPS receivers (not dedicated for scintillation monitoring) to study ionospheric scintillations. It is expected that the Hong Kong SatRef will become a very valuable data source for ionosphere scintillation studies in Hong Kong and low-latitude regions. For the objective 2, a detailed description of 3-D morphology of ionospheric scintillations as well as elucidation of ionospheric density irregularities that produce scintillations of GPS L1 signal over Hong Kong (17–27°N and 109–119°E), by combining observations from ground-based (GB) and space-based GNSS receivers over a solar active period from 2014 to 2015 (Yang et al. 2018). This study for the first time presents a locally integrated analysis of occurrences of ionospheric E- and F-region irregularities/scintillations in Southeast China. A sign of coupling of E and F region during nighttime is likely revealed from COSMIC radio occultation (RO) profile data. It also suggests that the occultation GPS data in an altitude range of 70–800 km can be used to study ionospheric irregularities. Over the study region (i.e., Hong Kong), the daytime amplitude scintillations generally attributed to Es-associated irregularities, primarily occurred during the period of 16–18 LT, reaching a maximum at the June solstice (summer), and did not exhibit obvious solar activity dependence. The nighttime scintillations induced by the equatorial F-region plasma irregularities, were prominent during the period of 20–24 LT, reaching maximum activity in the equinox months (Spring and Autumn), and increasing during the high solar activity year. The E-region (70-150 km) scintillations did not exhibit obvious geographic distribution patterns within the study region. However, the F-region (>150 km) scintillations mainly occurred to the south of Hong Kong, where there are high ambient ionizations. Regarding the simultaneous observations of E- and F-region irregularities during nighttime, two interesting features have been noticed. One is the striking occurrence of the type with GB postsunset events during the postmidnight hours (00-04 LT) and around the onset time (20 LT) of F-region irregularities. The occurrences in the postsunset hours of 21-00 LT were insignificant. In 2014 (2015), out of 23 (7) RO events observed with this type, 18 (6) events were observed after midnight or near the onset time. In particular, the postmidnight occurrences (10) were salient in March 2014. Another is the observation of simultaneous E- and F-region irregularities by RO data only without GB events. This type of events was rare (8 events in 2014 and 7 events in 2015 if excluding those with data outages) and occurred throughout the postsunset hours of 20-04 LT. In the E and F regions, the ionospheric density fluctuations are well demonstrated by the variation of the RO ROTI with altitudes. For the objective 3, the scintillation impacts on cycle slips, noise, error occurrence, and particularly low-latitude positioning (particularly Real Time Kinematic, RTK) have been studied. A RTK baseline with a length of about 24 km has been studied over a total of 31 consecutive days of data in October 2015. Several conventional ionospheric error correction methods are applied to this RTK baseline to assess the scintillation effects on RTK solutions. These methods include application of the broadcast ionospheric model (Klobuchar model), Global Ionospheric Maps (GIMs), and dual-frequency ionospheric-free linear combination. The RTK positioning accuracies at different scintillation levels (i.e., quiet, moderate, and strong) is obtained. The results demonstrate that the RTK positioning accuracy degrades with the increase of scintillation levels. The positioning error is the largest in the vertical direction, and the smallest in the north direction. Under ionospheric scintillations. The 3-D RTK positioning accuracy is degraded by a 0.7~1 m (1.5~3 m) if the Klobuchar model and GIM are applied to correct ionospheric effects for the ISM receiver (geodetic receiver), and by 10-20 cm if the ionospheric-free dual-frequency linear combination is applied. For the research objective 4, a permanent state-of-the-art scintillation observation facility has been successfully established in Hong Kong. This facility currently includes two stations: one north station located on the campus of the Chinese University of Hong Kong and the south station located at the Hok Tsui peninsula, Hong Kong island. Both stations are equipped with computer and large volume of hard drivers for data storage. The south station just completed a hardware upgrade in June 2018 with the collaboration from the PI’s research partner at the University of Colorado, USA. Now the South Station is equipped with 16 hard drivers of 4-TB each. It allows us to record scintillation events and scintillation index data over a long period of time. The two GNSS-based scintillation monitoring stations have produced a large volume of valuable research data for this project’s research work as well as the future research work to be conducted by future researchers.

This level of degradation significantly restricts the application of RTK positioning services in low-latitude region during scintillation periods as the RTK accuracy requirement is usually a few centimeters. 4. An advanced, permanent state-of-the-art scintillation observation facility has been successfully established in Hong Kong. It allows us to long-term record scintillation events and scintillation index data. The GNSS-based scintillation observation facility has produced a large volume of research data for historical and future studies on GNSS, ionosphere, and their coupling effects.

520313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
520313.value: A few further research actions can be extended after the successful completion of this project. (1) The scintillation observation data collected from Hong Kong can be cross-compared with those collected from other low-latitude GNSS stations in the northern hemisphere and also in the southern hemisphere. Potentially, the results obtained from Hong Kong’s stations can be compared with those obtained from Sanya and Guangzhou, in China. In addition, the results can be compared with those from Brazil, a typical southern hemisphere low-latitude region. (2) The low-latitude scintillation phenomena can be cross-examined with those collected from high-latitude regions. Particularly interesting data would be those from the Arctic and Antarctic GNSS stations. The ionospheric scintillation has been defined as one of the PI’s three main research directions. The PI will continue to study the scintillation phenomena (both low-latitude and high-latitude) and their impact on GNSS signals, even if the project has been completed. The PI will further apply for GRF research fund to conduct a broader and deeper study in the scintillations and their impacts on GNSS.

520313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
520313.value: The ionosphere, located in the region of ~60 km to ~2000 km above the Earth surface, has a significant impact on the signals of our daily used Global Positioning System (GPS) or Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), as well as our radio communication system. The GPS/GNSS has now played an essential role in almost everyone’s daily activities such as car navigation, pedestrian navigation, and industrial land surveying. The study of ionosphere will enable us to have a better understanding its impact on GPS/GNSS signals. In some high-end GPS/GNSS applications such as land surveying where high precision results are required, such knowledge about ionosphere scintillation is crucially important, because some countermeasures have been developed to mitigate their impact on GPS/GNSS high precision applications. The ionospheric scintillation is particularly strong and active in low-latitude region. Hong Kong GPS/GNSS users, including the general public, the professional land surveyors, government employees and others, therefore suffer more impacts in their GPS/GNSS applications. This research has quantified the impact of scintillation on GPS/GNSS positioning results. More importantly, the characteristics of scintillation 3D occurrence in Hong Kong region have been studied. Some new indicators have been developed for easier characterization of scintillation using data from ordinary GPS/GNSS receivers.

520413.label: Major findings and research outcome
520413.value: In this project, we have successfully covered why-not questions on top-k, top-k dominating, SQL and graph queries. We have devised efficient and scalable algorithms for each type of why-not questions. We have implemented and tested our algorithms on real data sets and many interesting case studies were reported. For example, we have applied our algorithms on NBA data and successfully explained why Yao-Ming was not listed as the top-5 players in NBA history. We have also applied our algorithms on road networks to find where to deploy new bridges so as to achieve a maximum reduction of traffic time. We have also tested our algorithms on a variety of synthetic data and experiments show that our algorithms are scalable and efficient. Research Outcomes: 3 journal papers, 1 conference paper, and 1 Ph.D. student. This project has resulted in 2 TKDE and 1 Information Systems journal papers and 1 conference paper. The article "Answering Why-Not Questions on Top-K Queries" was a journal extension of our conference paper in ICDE 2012, which was selected as one of the best of ICDE. The extent of this project covered the revision process of that journal article.

520413.value: After decades of effort working on database performance, recently the database research community has paid more attention to the issue of database usability, i.e., how to make database systems and database applications more user-friendly? In this project, we have studied the feature of explaining why some expected tuples are missing in a query result or the so-called “why-not?” feature. In this project, we have successfully covered why-not questions on top-k, top-k dominating, SQL and graph queries. We have devised efficient and scalable algorithms for answering each type of why-not questions. We have implemented and tested our algorithms on real data sets and many interesting case studies were reported. The project has brought advancement to the area of database usability and has improved the usability of many database applications.

520813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
520813.value: In this project, optical fibre sensor system design using optical communication and signal processing techniques will be investigated. Since its first proposal by Dr Charles Kao in 1968, optical fibre technology has changed our life significantly, first, in optical communication systems and subsequently in optical fibre sensor systems. Both areas have shown significant development in recent years. Using digital signal processing based coherent optical communication systems, multi-terabit signal transmission over a single fibre has routinely been achieved. This has increased tremendously the available bandwidth to internet users globally allowing many innovative Web based applications to be realized. Optical fibre based sensor has also been used in more and more application areas including civil and structural engineering, transportation engineering and aviation industries offering many advantages comparing with its electronic counterpart including immunity to electromagnetic interference; small size and lightweight; electrical passive; ability for remote sensing and capability for multiplexing of different functionalities. Although, the idea of optical fibre sensor has been proposed long time ago, it is only recently that optical fibre based sensor has made significant progress in practical systems. This is largely due to the progress of optical communication system that has substantially lowered the cost of fibre optic components. However, in signal detection and processing, the two research areas have mainly been developed separately. In this proposal, the possibility of using signal modulation, detection and signal processing techniques commonly used in optical communication systems for realizing optical fiber sensing functions is investigated. In particular, we propose to explore the use of modulation, detection and digital signal processing techniques used for high capacity, long haul coherent optical communication system in Brillouin scattering based distributed sensor system to enable significant improvement of system performance and simplify system implementation. These include the use of different modulation formats, phase detection and polarization modulation to enhance the sensitivity of coherent detected Brillouin Optical Time Domain Analysis(BOTDA) system and the use of multicarrier technique to enhance the detection speed of a BOTDA system; as well as the use of a spread code for reducing the effect of nonlineary in a Brillouin Optical Time Domain Reflectometry (BOTDR) system. It is believed that this effort should help to bring the two research areas together thus allowing more sensing functionalities and better system performance to be realized. 此研究项目将探讨光通信及信号处理技术在光纤传感系统之应用。从高锟博士六十年代发明光纤技术开始，光纤技术已从根本上改变了我们的生活。从开始在通信领域的应用到近年在传感领域的广泛应用，光纤技术发展迅速。利用信号处理技术及相干检测技术，光纤中的超高速数据传输已成为现实。这极大地提高了互联网用户可获得的带宽从而使很多创新应用得以实现。由于其抗电磁干扰，体积小重量轻，远程监测和可复用的优点，光纤传感系统日益广泛地用于土木，交通和航空航天领域。虽然光纤传感的概念很早就被提出，直到最近一些年才用于实际系统。很大程度上这是由于光通信系统的高速发展极大地降低了光纤器件的价格。可是在信号检测及处理方面光纤通信及传感技术的研究一直相对独立地发展。在此研究项目中，我们将探讨将光通信中的调制，检测及信号处理技术用于光纤传感系统中的可能性。我们特别将研究相干长距离光通信系统中的信号调制，检测及信号处理技术在基于布里渊散射的分布式光纤传感系统中的应用。此研究将提高系统的性能及简化系统的实现。这将有效地将两个研究领域融合在一起从而使更多的功能及更好的系统性能得以实现。

520813.label: Realisation of objectives
520813.value: In the project, we have proposed and demonstrated a number of new schemes for the realization of Brillouin optical time domain analyzer (BOTDA)systems. We have realized a scanning-free Brillouin optical time domain analyzer (BOTDA) based on an ultra-fine digital optical frequency comb (DOFC) with 1.95MHz frequency spacing and 2GHz bandwidth. using the scheme, we were able to reconstruct the Brillouin gain spectrum (BGS) and locate the Brillouin frequency shift (BFS) without frequency scanning and thus can improve the measurement speed about 100 times compared with the conventional BOTDA. We have also realized a sweep-free  distributed  Brillouin  optical  time  domain  analyzer  (BOTDA)  sensor  based  on  phase  detection. Dynamic measurement with vibration up to 1KHz was demonstrated. Coherent detection using phase and polarization diversity receiver was demonstrated experimentally with improved system performance. Artificial Neural Network(ANN) was applied for processing acquired data in the BOTDA system and significant system performance improvement was obtained. Six journal papers in leading journals in the research area and 3 conference papers were published. All the objectives have been successfully achieved.

521013.label: Project Objectives
521013.value: To develop a unified framework based on the dual-tree complex wavelet transform for efficient fringe image enhancement and 3D profile reconstruction without the phase unwrapping process.
rows: To develop a unified framework based on the dual-tree complex wavelet transform for efficient fringe image enhancement and 3D profile reconstruction without the phase unwrapping process.

521013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
521013.value: Automatic 3D profilometry allows accurate measurement of objects’ 3D model (or profile) in an automatic fashion. It is an important technology that found applications in augmented reality systems, real-time motion captures, quality control for product manufacturing, intelligent robot control, and many others. Among various profilometry approaches, the fringe projection profilometry (FPP) technique is a popular choice due to its high accuracy and relatively simple system setup. In such technique, the 3D profile of an object is obtained by first projecting a fringe pattern onto the target object and then analyzing the resulting images appeared on the object surface. In theory, the FPP are applicable to real-time measurements since only one image is sufficient for reconstructing the 3D profile of an object. However, in practice, the processing time of the FPP can be rather long particularly when working in adverse environment. One of the major problems that lead to the long computation time is the bulky phase unwrapping process, which is a necessary procedures of the traditional FPP algorithms and can take over 70% of the total computation time. In fact, the computation time can be even longer if only low quality fringe images are acquired (due to noise and other artifacts in image acquisition). In this project, a new unified framework based on the dual-tree complex wavelet transform (DT-CWT) is proposed for the realization of the FPP. The new approach directly computes the 3D profile of objects from the magnitude response of the transform output without the need of phase unwrapping. It is possible due to the short support and the analytic characteristic of the DT-CWT. We consider it as a breakthrough in the problem since, as to our knowledge, it is the first time that the complicated phase unwrapping process is reported to be unnecessary in a real-time FPP procedure. In addition to this, the artifacts of fringe images can be removed in the DT-CWT domain to improve the robustness of the 3D profile reconstruction process. Since all operations are performed in the DT-CWT domain, it saves the effort of transforming back and forth as required in the traditional pre- and post- processing algorithms for fringe image enhancement. The preliminary simulation results have shown the feasibility of the proposed framework. We believe further investigation based on this framework will let us achieve a practically feasible solution for automatic real-time 3D profilometry that cannot be achieved with the existing approaches. 自動三維輪廓術可以精確測量物體的三維模型。這是一個重要的技術並己廣泛應用於增強現實系統、實時運動捕捉、產品製造質量控制、及智能機器人控制等等。由於其高精度及相對簡單的系統設置，條紋投影輪廓術在各種輪廓術之中是一個比較受歡迎的選擇。在這技術中，物體的三維模型測量是通過對目標投影的條紋圖案，然後分析在物體表面所產生的圖像而進行。理論上，條紋投影輪廓術是適用於實時測量，因為一個圖像便足夠重建一個物體的三維輪廓。然而，在實際工作環境中，條紋投影輪廓術的處理時間可以是相當長的，特別是在惡劣的環境中工作時。其中一個導致長時間運算的主要原因是在於複雜的相位展開的計算。相位展開在傳统條紋投影輪廓術中是一個必要的程序，它可以佔總計算時間70％以上。事實上，如果只有低質量的條紋圖像（由於噪聲和其他採集圖像時的問題）計算時間甚至可以更長。在這個項目中，我們提出建立一個建基於雙樹复小波變換的統一框架，用以實現實時條紋投影輪廓術。我們提議通過雙樹复小波變換的頻率幅度響應，直接計算物體的三維輪廓而不需要進行相位展開。這是可能的原因在於雙樹复小波變換有非常短的小波函數和數學解析特性。我們認為這是一個突破。因為據我們所知，這是第一次有研究提出在進行條紋投影輪廓術時不需要進行複雜的相位展開程序。此外，在雙樹复小波變換域中，我們也可進行去噪及其他影像增强程序用以提高三維輪廓重建系統的質素表現。 由於所有的操作都可以在雙樹复小波變換域中進行，這樣可以節省來回轉化的程序，此為在傳統的條紋圖像增強方法所必需的。 初步的模擬測試結果已顯示了我們建議的計算框架的可行性。我們相信在這個框架的基礎上進一步的研究將讓我們獲得實現自動和實時的三維輪廓術的實際解決方案。

521013.label: Realisation of objectives
521013.value: The objective of the project is fully achieved. In this project, a unified framework based on the dual-tree complex wavelet transform (DTCWT) has been developed for robust fringe projection profilometry (FPP). The framework first transforms the input fringe image into the complex wavelet domain. Based on the special property of fringe images in the complex wavelet domain, the noise and bias in the image are first removed. In addition, three new function blocks are developed in this project to further enhance the quality of the fringe image and simplify the phase unwrapping process. The details will be described below. Traditional FPP schemes can have large measurement errors when the target measuring object has an abruptly changing height profile. The errors are generated due to the phase unwrapping process since some of the wrapped phase data are missing in this case. The same can happen whenever the fringe image contains any discontinuities due to, for instance, occlusion, multiple objects, indirect contact between the object and the reference background, etc. To solve the problem, traditional FPP schemes adopt complex phase unwrapping algorithms, which are time consuming but still cannot guarantee a successful phase unwrapping process in the abovementioned situations. For the first part of this project, we propose a new marker encoding and detection algorithm in the DTCWT domain. The objective of the proposed algorithm is for estimating the phase order information of the fringes in order to assist the phase unwrapping process when working in the single-shot FPP environment. For the proposed method, markers, which are realized as a sequence of impulses, are added to the sinusoidal fringe projection pattern. The positions of these impulses encode the period order number of the wrapped phase. By separately estimating the period order numbers, the phase unwrapping process can be greatly simplified. The impulses and fringes are projected onto the target objects, and the resulting fringe image is analyzed in the DTCWT domain. The impulses are then extracted and decoded so that the embedded period order of the wrapped phase is obtained. As is different from the traditional marker encoding schemes, the proposed approach is applicable to objects with color texture. Furthermore, this approach is more localizable compared to the approaches using single strip marker or single point marker. It can provide the period order information not only at the center but also along the fringe pattern. Thus, it is applicable to the scene that contains several objects with sudden jumps in height. Unlike the approaches that use multiple frame patterns, the proposed scheme is applicable to dynamic applications because it requires only a single fringe pattern for the entire operation. Finally, the algorithm is not sensitive to the quality of the fringe image. The period order information can be detected accurately with noisy fringe images or images with abnormal brightness. With the period order information, we can reconstruct the 3D model of the object even when some of the fringe data are missing due to the artifacts of the fringe image or the irregularity of the object shape. Another common problem of FPP is the highlight in the fringe image. Conventional FPP methods often have difficulty in reconstructing the 3D model of objects when the fringe images have the so-called “highlight” regions due to the strong illumination from nearby light sources. Within a highlight region, the fringe pattern is overwhelmed by the strong reflected light. Thus the 3D information of the object which is originally embedded in the fringe pattern can no longer be retrieved. In the second part of this project, a novel inpainting algorithm is proposed to restore the fringe images in the presence of highlights. Different from the previous approaches, the proposed algorithm does not require special hardware and works only on a single fringe image. The new algorithm first detects the highlight regions of a fringe image based on a Gaussian Mixture model. Then a sparse representation based image inpainting method is applied to recover the corrupted fringe patterns in the DTCWT domain. Unlike the conventional inpainting methods which assume no information about the highlight regions, the proposed algorithm first estimates the geometrical structure of the fringe patterns in order to guide the iterative inpainting procedure. The restored fringe image is then used in the conventional FPP to measure the 3D model of the object. Simulation and experimental results show that the proposed algorithm is able to accurately estimate the missing fringe patterns due to the highlights and thus correct the errors in the reconstructed 3D model which can be found when using the traditional methods. As an extension to this project, we also investigated the method to improve the DTCWT in removing the bias in the fringe image. In an FPP process, the captured fringe images can be modeled as the superimposition of the projected fringe patterns on the texture of the objects (i.e. the bias). Extracting the fringe patterns from the captured fringe images is an essential procedure in FPP; but traditional single-shot FPP methods often fail to perform. Even with DTCWT, unsatisfactory results can be obtained if the objects have a highly textured surface. Besides, most existing techniques only estimate the fringe pattern but totally ignore the texture. In fact, the texture of the object is also very important in many diagnostic applications of FPP. In this part of the project, a new single-shot FPP algorithm which allows both the object texture and fringe pattern to be estimated simultaneously is proposed. The heart of the proposed algorithm is an enhanced morphological component analysis (MCA) based on DTCWT. Conventional MCA methods which use a uniform threshold in an iterative optimization process are inefficient to separate fringe-like patterns from image texture. We extend the conventional MCA by taking advantage of the low-rank structure of the fringe’s sparse representation in the DTCWT domain to enable an adaptive thresholding process. It ends up with a robust single-shot FPP algorithm that can extract the fringe pattern even if the object has a highly textured surface. The proposed approach can also obtain the object texture simultaneously in the fringe pattern estimation process, which is useful in many FPP applications. Experimental results have demonstrated the significantly improved performance of the proposed algorithm over the conventional single-shot FPP approaches. Based on the above improvements to the unified DTCWT framework, we have significantly enhanced the robustness of the FPP system and provided new functionality for 3D profile measurement. The new functional blocks for marker decoding, highlight inpainting and enhanced MCA have significantly improved the quality of the fringe image and greatly simplify the phase unwrapping process to just a direct integration of the pixels in a local region. The objective of the project is thus considered as fully achieved.

521013.label: Major findings and research outcome
521013.value: 1. We proposed a new marker encoding and detection algorithm in the dual-tree complex wavelet transform domain (DTCWT). The new algorithm provides an efficient method for estimating the period order information of the fringes in order to assist the phase unwrapping process when working in the single-shot fringe projection profilometry (FPP) environment. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm is robust to the quality of the fringe image and is lightweight computationally as compared to the original DTCWT FPP framework. It greatly improves the accuracy over the traditional FPP schemes when measuring the three-dimensional (3D) structure of objects with abruptly changing height profile. 2. We developed a novel inpainting algorithm to restore the fringe images in the presence of highlights. Different from the previous approaches, the proposed algorithm does not require special hardware and works only on a single fringe image. The algorithm is based on an iterative regularization procedure with additional geometrical sketching of the fringe pattern in the highlight regions. It serves as the initial guess and guides the iterative regularization process to converge to a result much better than the traditional approaches without the guidance. Simulation and experimental results show that the proposed algorithm is able to accurately estimate the missing fringe patterns due to the highlights and thus correct the errors in the reconstructed 3D model which are often found when using the traditional methods. 3. We developed a new single-shot FPP algorithm which allows both the object texture and fringe pattern to be estimated simultaneously. The core of the proposed algorithm is an enhanced morphological component analysis (MCA) based on DTCWT. Conventional MCA methods which use a uniform threshold in an iterative optimization process are inefficient to separate fringe-like patterns from image texture. We extend the conventional MCA by taking advantage of the low-rank structure of the fringe’s sparse representation in the DTCWT domain to enable an adaptive thresholding process. It ends up with a robust single-shot FPP algorithm that can extract the fringe pattern even if the object has a strong textured surface. The proposed approach can also obtain the object texture simultaneously in the fringe pattern estimation process, which is useful for many FPP applications. Experimental results have demonstrated the significantly improved performance of the proposed algorithm over the conventional single-shot FPP approaches.

521013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
521013.value: While the proposed techniques can effectively improve the robustness of the FPP based 3D measurement systems, they require the implementation of a few optimization processes that can be time consuming. Particularly for those FPP applications that require real-time performance, a more computationally efficient approach needs to be developed. To speed up the operation, we believe the learning approach will be a good alternative to the optimization processes used in the proposed techniques. Recently, deep neural networks (DNN) have been applied to different optimization problems and achieved significantly improved performance. Due to the regular structure of DNN, they can be easily implemented using the Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) to greatly increase the computational speed. Extending the current work to using the learning approach can be the next topic for extensive study.

521013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
521013.value: Fringe Projection Profilometry (FPP) is a popular non-contact three-dimensional (3D) measurement technology. In such technology, the 3D profile of an object is measured based on the deformation of the projected fringe patterns shown on the object surface. FPP has been used in many 3D measurement applications, such as 3D microscopy, cosmetic surgery, 3D intra-oral dental measurements, etc. The performance of traditional FPP techniques relies heavily on the quality of the captured fringe images. Unfortunately in practice, these fringe images can have different defects due to the imperfection of the working environment. The main objective of this project is to improve the robustness of FPP. By introducing three new functional units, a robust FPP is achieved that can operate effectively even when the target object has an abruptly changing height profile. It can also operate perfectly even when there are occlusions among different objects, or the fringe image has strong highlight regions where the fringe patterns are overwhelmed by the strong light. The new functional units allow the 3D structure and surface texture of the objects to be obtained simultaneously. Such function has never been achieved in traditional FPP methods and will be extremely useful to many diagnostics applications of FPP.

521813.label: Project Objectives

To investigate the relationship between 2D features and 3D features extracted from real subject scans. To propose a robust method for extracting 2D features from monocular images for human model customisation. To predict a 3D shape representation from the images of the customer and develop a deformation method for model customisation using the predicted 3D shapes. To verify the model customisation by experiments using both objective and subjective evaluations.

521813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
521813.value: Accurate 3D human modelling is the cornerstone of both 2D-to-3D and 3D-to-2D clothing computer-aided designs. Various creative and reconstructive modelling methods are reported in the computer graphics literature. However, the former approach suffers from the requirement for manual operations that are too intensive, while the latter one results in models with low dimensional accuracy. The existing methods cannot satisfy the needs of the clothing industry for human customisation, especially in terms of size accuracy. This study aims to develop intelligent modelling techniques for human model customisation based on two orthogonal-view images of the customer. The resulting models truthfully resemble the global and local characteristics of the customer’s original body shape, with realistic appearance and accurate sizes. The accuracy of the resulting models is comparable to that of scans. To facilitate high-performance clothing design, intelligent deformation algorithms are proposed to morph the precise static models into different dynamic poses. A detailed experimental plan is suggested to validate and verify the proposed human modelling and pose deformation algorithms. The proposed methods can be applied in apparel e-tailing for virtual model customisation and online fitting analysis. 精確的3D人體建模是從二維至二維（2D-to-3D）並從二維至二維（3D-to-2D）的電腦服裝設計的基石。計算機圖形學文獻中已建議過各種建構性和重建性的建模方法。但是，前者的方法要求密集的手動操作，而後者生成的人體模型尺寸精度低。由此可見，現有的方法並不能滿足服裝行業對人體模型定制的需求，特別是在尺寸精度方面。 本研究項目旨在開發基於客戶兩張正交視人像照片的智能人體模型定制的技術。所生成的人體模型將如實地重建客戶體形的整體及局部特徵，並具有逼真的外觀和精確的尺寸。所得到的模型的準確性要與掃描相若。為了驗證和核實本項目所擬議的人體建模和體型變形的算法，我們建議了詳細的實驗計劃。本項目所提出的人體建模技術可以應用在服裝網上零售，實現虛擬人體模型定制及在線試衣。

521813.label: Major findings and research outcome
521813.value: A total of five methods/systems have been created to realise automatic shape modelling and dynamic pose deformation: • The first method deals with human subjects in tight-fitting clothing. It detects body parts from front-view and side-view 2D images and then construct them to 3D models. The output of the system is customised model with precise size measurements. • The second method removes the restriction of tight-fitting clothing. It predicts under-the-clothes body profiles of the subjects based on input images where the body profiles are covered in arbitrary clothing, including tight-fitting, normal-fitting and loose-fitting clothing. • The third method applies cutting-edge deep learning technology in human-parsing to segment the human from the image background. It also improves the robustness, efficiency and accuracy of shape modelling of individuals • The fourth development applies the above modelling methods to develop a client-server system. It is a real application of the proposed automatic shape customisation technology, starting from photo taking to model customization and size extraction. • The fifth method deforms human models of various body shapes into a series of dynamic poses with realistic appearance, enabling a more comprehensive fit evaluation in the development of high-performance clothing, such as sportswear and/or functional garments. A total of 2 book chapters, and 7 journal articles plus 7 conference papers are published. One PhD student was trained under the project. One patent files, two awards of best presentations, and wide coverage of media after a press release about the research output from the project.

521813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
521813.value: After the project completion, PolyU has one press conference to announce the results generated in this project. We received very good feedback from the industry as well as academy. We see great potential to extend the current study to other field of application, taking advantages of the results obtained in this project, e.g. real time pose detection from images, human parsing, human modelling, to areas of medical or physiotherapy.

521813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
521813.value: Shopping well-fitting clothes online or making bespoke garments can be done more easily thanks to the intelligent 3D human modelling technology developed by The Hong Kong Polytechnic University (PolyU), which generates accurate sizes and shapes of individuals from two full body photographs within seconds. We have developed new and efficient methods for modelling individuals of customised sizes and shapes in arbitrary dynamic poses. These methods allow a customised model to be created completely and automatically within 5-10 seconds. The model’s size measurements and shapes, including the girth of bust, waist, hip, thigh, knee, calf and neck, as well as arm length, shoulder slope, etc., are accurate. The discrepancies in tight-fitting and loose-fitting clothing are less than 1cm and 2 cm respectively, which are precise enough to fulfil the specific requirements of the clothing industry for fashion applications and comparable to body scans.

522013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
522013.value: Pressure ulcers or pressure sores are frequent and serious complications for long term chair bound or bed bound patients. Although impaired metabolism, friction, and shear forces have been shown to be instrumental in the pathogenesis of pressure ulcers, prolonged supra-capillary pressure is proved to be the main cause of this problem [9]. Most pressure ulcers form at the area where the bony parts of body cause greatest force on the skin and tissue. Thus the weight (body mass) of individual patients is directly related to the occurrence of the pressure ulcers. Pressure ulcers leads pain, affecting health, and disrupt every aspect of the patient’s life [10]. To reduce the interface pressure on the bony prominences of the patient’s body by pressure relieving devices is a common technique for the prevention and treatment of pressure ulcers. In recent years, hundreds of pressure relieving cushions and mattress are designed and marketed. However, there are still many limitations on these existing devices. For example, pressure relieving mattress are very expensive, and the insertion of pressure relieving cushions below patients body may cause discomfort and have risk to cause friction. In addition, too much cushions around the patients would affect the patient’s appearance and dignity. To provide the patients a low cost pressure relieving devices for the prevention and treatment of pressure ulcers as well as to maintain their dignity, this project aims to design and develop a garment with a particular padding of appropriate thickness based on the body mass index of the patient. This study focuses on the study of the relationship between the padding properties, body mass index of the patients and the pressure relieving ability of the proposed garment. A scientific approach will be developed to determine the padding thickness based on the padding properties and the BMI of patient. The ultimate deliverable is the wearable garment with padding suitable for the prevention and treatment of pressure ulcers in patients at low cost. The deliverables of this project will be beneficial to over 1.7 millions of patients with pressure ulcers all over the world. 壓瘡或壓力性潰瘍是長期坐椅或長期卧床病人經常面對嚴重併發症。雖然身陳代謝失調, 摩擦及扭曲是壓力性潰瘍發病的原因之一, 但是長期性表層微絲血管受壓是這個問題的主要成因。大部分壓力性潰瘍在骨骼附近皮肉最受力的部位形成。所以每位病人的體重對壓力性潰瘍的形成有直接的關係。壓力性潰瘍帶來痛楚, 影響健康, 擾亂病人各方面的生活。壓力舒緩用品經常被用作壓力性潰瘍的預防及治療, 以減少骨骼突出部分所受的壓力。近年已有過百種壓力舒緩物品及床褥的設計在市面銷售。但是現有的物品仍有它們的不足之處。例如:壓力舒緩床褥非常昂貴, 而使用壓力舒緩物品或會引致不適及有可能產生摩擦。使用太多壓力舒緩物品亦會影響病人的外觀及尊嚴。 為了給予病人低成本的壓力舒緩用品以預防及治療壓力性潰瘍從而維護他們的尊嚴, 這項科研計劃致力於設計及研發一件合適厚度的墊料以配合病人身體質量指數。這項研究集中於觀察墊料特性、病人的身體質量指數及所研發衣物的壓力舒緩效能。得出的科學數據會根據墊料的特性及病人的身體質量指數以決定墊料厚度。最終結果將會是一整件適合用以預防及治療壓力性潰瘍墊料製作低成本的衣物。這項科研將可讓全球170萬壓力性潰瘍患者受惠。

522013.label: Major findings and research outcome
522013.value: In this study, different materials such as mattresses, foam and cushions for pressure relieving have analyzed and it was found that foam is most appropriate material for relieving pressure. To achieve the first objective, it was found that the peak interface pressure is governed by thickness and density of the foam, and the steady interface pressure is governed by thickness and support factor the foam. After ANOVA, there is significant difference of interface pressure between foam material with and without resilience when foam thickness is thin but it is not applicable when foam thickness is thick. Thus, the design of padding materials embedded in various body position shall be different in terms of hardness and thickness to provide effective prevention of pressure sores. (See the conference paper) To achieve the second objective, we investigated the main and cross-over effects among BMI, body position and supporting material properties on pressure relieving performance using univariate ANOVA and correlation analysis. It was found that body position and foam density were the main effect and BMI and body position, and body position and foam density were the cross-over effects on pressure relief. Low density foam of less than 4cm in thickness with appropriate compression modulus are best suited for pressure relief. The actual value of foam thickness and compression modules are subject to BMI values and body position. It is useful for design of supporting materials with varied BMI values and body positions to greatly reduce pressure ulcers for ailing patients. (See the Journal Paper) To achieve the third objective, we design garments with foam material with various thickness for various BMI groups for pressure relieving. A randomized control trial had conducted among 25 wheelchair-bounded users and 29 normal users as control group. It was found that there is significant different in reduction of interface pressure between two groups of users when BMI is below 18.5. Temperature change (i.e. Increasing) between the foam material and body skin is significantly different between two groups of users when BMI lies between 23 and 25. Moisture change (i.e. decreasing) between the foam material and body skin is no significant different between two groups of users. Both users’ groups felt more comfortable when they used garments embedded with foam for pressure relief. Overall, the design of garment with appropriate foam material based on appropriate BMI value could provide effective pressure relieving performance. (Journal paper is under preparation)

522013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
522013.value: This study could extend to study more supporting materials for reducing pressure sores. For example, if the curvature of supporting material fits the contour of body, it has a high chance to reduce the interfacial pressure between the body and supporting materials. Besides the factors of BMI value and body position, the rigidity of muscles would be studied whether interface pressure is changed or not when the subject is lying on supporting material. If the rigidity index is high, it is more likely to appear the pressure sores. The above-mentioned factors could improve the efficacy of using garment with padding materials for reduction of pressure sores. In addition, number of participants for trial could extend to cover more BMI values with various contours of body. Same BMI value may have different contour of body (Concave, Convex and flat) in three critical positions that pressure sores appears. If the above-mentioned contour of body is also studied, the proposed outcome is more representative for developing appropriate garment design to provide effective reduction of pressure sores.

522013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
522013.value: Pressure ulcers/sores are skin damage for people with limited mobility who suffer a long-term high pressure during lying on bed and sitting on wheelchair. It leads so painful and affect the health and life quality of people very much. Pressure ulcers/sores could ultimately lead to death. Compared with other prevention methods such as cushions and nursing cares, the garment are more economical and practical for prevention of pressure ulcers/sores. This study aims to design new garment with padding material for effectively reduction of the pressure ulcers/sores. The significance of the findings in this study is determined the thickness of padding materials with appropriate elastic moduli for prevention of pressure ulcers/sores based on user’s BMI value and their body positions which suffer a long-term high pressure. The ultimate deliverable of this project is to provide the wearable garment with suitable padding material on appropriate location for prevention and treatment of pressure ulcers/sores at low cost. It could bring some inspiration to garment designers in clinical applications as well as low cost prevention of pressure ulcers/sores for healthcare professionals. Such outcomes would be beneficial to over 1.7 millions of people with pressure ulcers/sores over the world.

522213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
522213.value: In this project, our objective is to create a framework that will facilitate the development of systems that are adaptive (adjusts to different users and environments), physical (embedded into the environment) and/or mobile (worn on the user). An example of such a system might be a wearable computing system that allows a user to interact with a pervasive computing system in his apartment, or a mobile reader that adjusts its content or display based on the user’s contextual activity and attention. In other words, we propose a human-centric framework for affective, context-aware, multimodal interaction. Unlike similar work that focuses on the interaction devices and their incoming or outgoing signals, our framework relates together all aspects of a user interaction process, including human factors such as user needs, task requirements, user affects and emotions, and physical limitations and abilities of the user, together with device details such as functionality, communications and robustness, and environmental factors. The relations between these different aspects are captured in a user-centered ontology that allows our framework to be scalable and easily extensible to incorporate new aspects of interaction as they are discovered or developed. Our project relates to the fields of human-computer interaction, context-aware computing, physical computing and wearable computing. Recent advances have made wearable/mobile and physical devices more pervasive in daily life, and new interaction devices are being introduced regularly. These advances necessitate new ways of interaction, and there has been some work in the design of frameworks to support human-computer interaction, some of it in the mobile computing context. However, most of the work has approached the problem from a technological/infrastructural standpoint, or assumed a single-user, uni-system model of interaction. By incorporating user interactions, environment attributes and the semantics of the task, we believe that our framework has the potential to offer a holistic view of human computer interaction, which will facilitate the development of more intuitive user interactions and of adaptive user interfaces. We also hope that this framework will allow us to better understand the interactions between environment, task and user affect. We believe that our framework has application potential in a number of areas, including creative design, mobile interaction, social computing, and education. In this project, we will study two application areas for our platform: an adaptive online learning platform and an assistive technology environment to evaluate our framework for completeness and correctness. 在该项目中，我们的目标是创建一个便于开发自适应的（可以适应不同的用户和环境），物理的（嵌入到环境当中）和/或移动的（穿在用户身上）系统的框架。例如一个可穿着的计算系统，它允许用户与他公寓内的一个普适计算系统进行交互。或者一个根据用户的活动和注意力调整其内容或显示的移动阅读器。 换句话说，我们提出了一个用于情感，环境感知和多模态交互的以人为中心的框架。与类似的着重于交互设备以及其输入输出信号的研究不同的是，我们的框架将用户交互过程中的所有因素都联系了起来， 包括如用户需求，任务要求，用户情绪，用户的体力和能力限制等人类因素，以及如功能，通信和鲁棒性等设备详情，以及环境因素。这些不同因素之间的联系在一个以用户为中心的本体中获得，这使得我们的框架在规模及功能上具有可扩展性，利于结合新发现和开发的交互因素。 该项目与人机交互，环境感知计算，物理计算及可穿着计算这些领域相关。技术的进步使得可穿着的/移动的和物理的设备在日常生活中更加普及，新的交互设备也在定期推出，这必将促成新的交互方式的产生。目前已有一些用于支持人机交互的框架设计，其中部分是用于移动计算的环境中。然而，这些设计大多数是从技术/基础设施的角度来解决问题，或者假设是单用户，单系统的交互模式。通过纳入人机交互，环境属性和任务语义，我们相信我们的框架有利于提出对人机交互更全面的看法，以及开发更直观的用户交互和更具自适应性的用户界面。我们同时希望该框架能使我们更好地理解环境，任务和用户情绪之间的交互。 我们相信该框架在众多领域具有应用潜力，包括创新设计，移动计算，社会计算和教育。在该项目中，我们将深入研究两个应用领域——自适应在线学习平台及辅助技术环境来评估框架的完整性和正确性。

522213.label: Realisation of objectives
522213.value: We are pleased to report that the project has been successfully completed, and all the objectives have been fulfilled. (All references to publications in the following refer to Items 8 and 9 in Part C, i.e. 8.1 refers to Paper 1 in Part C, Item 8 (Journal Papers)): Objectives 1 and 2: We investigated a number of different factors that demonstrate and impact human behaviour in interactive contexts. These include physiological signals such as heart and respiratory rate (8.3, 9.1), eye movement (9.2, 9.4, 9.5, 9.7, 9.8, 9.9), physical movement (8.2, 9.6, 9.11) the information presented on the screen (9.2, 9.4, 9.5, 9.9), mouse movements (9.4, 9.8, 9.10), facial expressions (8.1, 8.5), and user stress and other user affects (8.1, 8.3, 8.5, 9.1, 9.4, 9.8. 9.9). We also extended our techniques to look at other factors of user behaviour that are not directly related to human-computer interaction. 9.3 looks at mirroring captured human expressions onto a virtual avatar to communicate expressions to other users while still maintaining . Extending from these techniques, we applied the techniques developed to analyze human body movements, especially those which are indicative of violence (e.g., fights). These findings have been documented in 8.2, 9.6 and 9.11. Our methods have all been evaluated on real data, and shown to achieve high performance under rigorous evaluation that are designed to mimic real-world conditions. For example, instead of the randomized splits that are commonly used in validation, leave-one-subject-out validation was employed in all of our work. This makes the evaluation more realistic and fair as it better resembles the situation whereby the method is used by a new (unseen) user, who would manifest new behaviors that have not been seen before. Another example are 8.2, 9.6 and 9.11, which broke with previous methods that mainly used simulated data. Our follow-up work (in submission) has shown that the simulated data is not useful for real-world conditions – indeed, using videos of real ANIMAL fights are better for predicting human fights, rather than videos of simulated human fights! Objectives 3-5: In the process of investigating the aforementioned factors, we also analysed the linkage between these factors and the relationship between them. In particular, 9.4 described a framework that relates the spatial properties of the content on the screen, and the movement of the user’s eyes and the click of the mouse, 9.8 describes a framework that relates user stress with their eye movements and mouse movements, and 9.10 relates this to user intention, using this to predict the user’s next mouse movement (where he/she will click next). One of the biggest challenges with human behavioural analysis is the issue of unseen cases. Simply put, people are all individuals, so there will always be some variation in how a person’s internal cognitive or affective state is exhibited through his/her behaviour. In addition, it is not really possible to capture all possible cases – even the best data collection methodology will always forgo some internal state. To address this, we investigated the use of transfer learning, to exploit the similarity between different individuals to fit new, unseen behaviors or users (8.4, 8.5). This technique, in addition to making it possible to rapidly bootstrap a model to cover new types of contexts, is also useful in a real-world context as it allows for a trained, deployed model to be re-trained without requiring either the original source training data to be transferred over to the user side, or for the user data to be transferred to the source side, both of which have privacy and data security concerns. The final models integrate and relate together different human and environmental (e.g. user interface and computer state) signals and the internal human cognitive/affective state into an ontology. Since we have intentionally focused on using consumer-level, off-the-shelf-available equipment in all of our investigations, our methods are easily transferrable into applications. In particular, we have created two eye tracker applications, for the desktop (9.4) and for the mobile platform (9.7). Both have been evaluated against state-of-the-art, and (9.4) in particular received honors as a Best Paper for the prestigious CHI conference. Student Training We admitted one MPhil student, Kwok Cho Ki (Tiffany), with the funding from this project. Tiffany graduated from Hong Kong Polytechnic University and has been involved in research and publishing even as an undergraduate. During her time here, she has successfully published or significantly contributed to 6 conference publications (9.2, 9.3, 9.4, 9.10, 9.12, 9.13), including first-authored papers at IUI (9.12) and ISM (9.13). She successfully defended her thesis in November 2017 and she is now a PhD student at ETH Zurich, a top 10 ranked university. On the undergraduate research front, we were fortunate to have identified Wu You (Erin) and had the opportunity to work with her for over a year. During this time, Erin was instrumental in assisting our research, and she also contributed significantly to two papers (9.10, 9.12). She graduated with first-class honors in 2017, and is now pursuing her PhD at the University of Luxembourg.

522213.label: Major findings and research outcome
522213.value: This project has resulted in the following major findings and outcomes (all references are listed in Items 8 and 9, Part C): 1. We have empirically confirmed a linkage between human behaviour and signals such as facial expressions (8.1, 8.5), eye movement (8.4, 9.2, 9.4, 9.5, 9.7, 9.8, 9.9), physical movement (8.2, 9.6, 9.11), mouse movement (8.3, 9.1, 9.10, 9.12), heart rate and respiratory rate (8.2, 9.1), the computer interface and environment (8.4, 9.4, 9.8), such as the information presented on the screen, and human internal states such as stress (9.8) and comprehension (9.5, 9.9). In particular, we studied eye movements around different types of interaction events (mouseclicks on various targets and typing), and found evidence that the assumption of “users are looking where they click” that has been held in previous work is not accurate (9.4). This work was further extended for stress detection in an HCI context (9.8). 2. We developed an eye tracking application that, unlike other approaches, do not require any explicit calibration or specialized equipment (9.4). This application has been extended to the mobile platform (9.7). The performance of both of these applications has been evaluated and compared against state-of-the-art. 3. We developed an emotion-sharing app that allows users to communicate their own feelings while watching videos with friends and family (9.3), while preserving personal privacy. We have evaluated this application both for correctness as well as for user reception and perception. 4. We have transferred our findings to interdisciplinary problems. We developed a method that would make it possible for a mobile phone to perform vision screening, thus alleviating the need for expensive equipment. The algorithm has been evaluated for correctness and it approaches the performance obtained by medical grade equipment (9.13). We are in the process of developing it into an off-the-shelf product.

522213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
522213.value: There is growing realization in human-computer interaction that the information-theoretic model that views the human body as a channel through which the information processor (the brain) communicates with the interface is outdated. There is a realization that emotion and perception play a significant part in human cognition and performance. However, current interaction paradigms still treat the person as a static entity. There is much work in recognizing human affect, but most of this work looks at the human in one-way activities (e.g. watching movies or reading), or in interactive activities involving other humans (e.g. turn taking), but very little deals with the affective state of the user in human computer interaction. This is despite much research showing that emotion and perception play a significant role in human cognition and thus has a big impact on human performance. We thus feel that the next step should be expanding the framework to incorporate the human affect as part of the system. This project has made significant contributions towards the understanding of behavioural signals and their linkage with human internal state and computer environment, and we therefore feel that it puts us in a good position to make further contributions in this domain.

522213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
522213.value: In this project, we looked at the linkage between human signals, such as their facial expressions, eye movements, body movements and heartrate, and the link between changes in these signals and their internal states, such as their emotion or stress level, and the computer environment, such as what is being presented on the screen. We found that a user’s internal state can be revealed through his behaviour, which implies that a user’s internal state will affect his/her performance on computer tasks. Therefore, for a computer system to be truly friendly to people, it makes sense for it to be able to deduce the human internal state, so that it can accommodate and adapt. Our approaches were all proven using only consumer-grade equipment, and much of our work was done using only off-the-shelf equipment that is standard on all desktop or laptop systems. In addition, we also devised methods that make it possible to deploy a trained model, adapt it to the user, all without transferring training data between the client and the source sides. This makes good performance possible while preserving data privacy and intellectual property. These results are significant as it means that our methods are usable and practical.

522413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
522413.value: 結構健康監測（SHM）是過去二十年土木工程領域的一個重要研究課題。這一技術能夠説明追蹤結構狀態（包括材料和幾何特性）以及運行和荷載環境的變化，從而洞察結構當前和將來的性能。通過在三座纜索支承橋梁（青馬大橋、汲水門大橋、汀九大橋）安裝超過800個感測器的複雜線上監測系統，香港於上世紀90年代末建立了向業界展示SHM技術的里程碑式範例。在過去15年，本項目的首席研究員在各種場合被他的國際同行問及諸如以下的問題：該系統如何為橋梁的全壽命維護和管理提供經濟和技術裨益？感測器的存活率和經過長期運作後感測器以及資料獲取與傳輸系統的性能衰退如何？數據品質是否有衰退？如何存儲和提取海量的SHM數據?是否監測出結構損傷和異常?積累的監測數據可否用於預測式結構評估或損傷預警?當感測器的服務壽命低於橋梁的服務壽命時,SHM系統是否有效?當部分不可置換的感測器損壞時,結構健康評估的目標是否還能達到? 本研究項目不是要回答以上所有的問題。相反，通過整合和集成地利用從三座香港大橋中連續採集的15年數據，本課題旨在研究與上述問題有關的若干重要挑戰性問題。邏輯上，只有當獲得跨越很多年的監測數據並將它們用於檢驗當前世界上最先進的方法後，大部分的以上問題才有可能得到回答。本項目的研究人員已經獲得15年的監測數據用於此項研究。我們將發展從結構狀態診斷到結構狀態預測的自進化結構健康評估框架。特別地，在貝葉斯統計推理的框架體系內，將發展基於可自我更新和自我演變的數據驅動模型的結構性能診斷方法。通過一個基準研究的建立，我們將與國際同行分享在各種荷載狀態（公路荷載、鐵路荷載、季風、颱風、地震）獲得的典型的靜態和動態回應（應力、位移、加速度）監測數據以及相應的運行荷載監測數據，研究共同感興趣的問題。本項目的研究成果將為回答上述的問題以及SHM領域若干重要挑戰性問題的回答提供線索。

522413.label: Realisation of objectives
522413.value: Objective 1： An unsupervised learning method for structural damage alarming and localization of long-span cable- supported bridges using multi-novelty indices formulated by monitoring-derived modal parameters has been developed. The proposed method which requires neither structural model nor damage model is applicable to structures of arbitrary complexity. With the intention to enhance the tolerance to measurement noise/uncertainty and the sensitivity to structural damage, an improved novelty index is formulated in terms of auto-associative neural networks (ANNs) where the output vector is designated to differ from the input vector while the training of the ANNs needs only the measured modal properties of the intact structure under in-service conditions. The performance of the improved novelty index for damage occurrence detection of large-scale bridges is examined through numerical simulation studies of the suspension Tsing Ma Bridge (TMB) and cable-stayed Ting Kau Bridge (TKB) incurred with different types of structural damage. The improved novelty index is also extended to formulate multi-novelty indices in terms of the measured modal frequencies and incomplete mode shape components for damage region identification. A study has been made to enhance the damage identification capability of ANNs and PNNs (probabilistic neural networks) when applied for identification of damage incurred at bridge deck members. Research efforts have been made to construct combined modal parameters which are synthesized from measured modal frequencies and modal shape components to train ANNs for damage alarming, as well as to configure PNNs for damage localization by adapting the smoothing parameter in the Bayesian classifier to different values for different pattern classes. The performance of the ANNs with their input being modal frequencies and the combined modal parameters respectively and the PNNs with constant and adaptive smoothing parameters respectively is evaluated through simulation studies of identifying damage inflicted on different deck members of the TMB. A novel model-free data-interpretation methodology within the Bayesian framework for structural health evaluation is developed with the use of long-term monitoring data. SHM-based structural condition assessment using Bayesian linear model (BLM) and Bayesian generalized linear model (BGLM) is developed. For condition assessment of bridge expansion joints, the relationship pattern between the thermal movement of expansion joints and the effective temperature of bridge deck is quantified using BLM and long-term monitoring data. The model parameters, model error and their associated uncertainties are estimated by analytical and MCMC (Gibbis sampler) algorithms. With the established BLM, an anomaly index is defined to evaluate the failure probability of the expansion joints. Then the BLM is extended to BGLM for assessing wind-induced displacement responses of the instrumented TKB. With the monitoring data of displacement and wind during typhoons, the correlation pattern between wind-induced displacement and wind speed/direction is explored. The crucial issue of optimizing model structure is dealt with by employing Bayesian model class selection. Based on the established model, the bridge displacement responses and the associated confidence intervals under wind speed at serviceability limit state (SLS) are predicted and compared with the design allowable values for validation. Objective 2: A reliability-based approach for progressive assessment of the structural condition of bridge deck sections has been proposed and applied to the TMB with the use of long-term strain monitoring data. After extracting the live-load-caused strain components from raw measurement data, the strain sequences acquired from different structural members on the same deck section are synthesized to derive the dynamic internal forces (axial force, bending moment, and shear force) of the monitored deck section. The Weibull mixture modeling is then carried out to characterize the probability density distribution of the peaks of each internal force component, and the corresponding reliability index is obtained. The reliability index of the deck section is evaluated by considering the different internal force components in series connection. Different statistical counting methods (the sampling method, the peak counting method, and the pointwise counting method) for the selection of peak data targeted for SHM-based reliability assessment of instrumented bridges are examined and compared, through the application of the above methods for the purpose of constructing peak-stress histograms and formulating probability density functions (PDFs) by use of long-term strain monitoring data. For comparison of the three methods on a common basis, peak covering rate is defined and the relationship between the amount of peak data and the control parameter in each counting method is obtained. Based on the formulated relationship, the parameters in the three methods are determined by ensuring a certain peak covering rate, and the evaluation results of reliability index for an instrumented deck component from the three statistical counting methods are obtained and compared. With the long-term strain data collected from the TMB, the extreme stresses caused by highway and railway traffic respectively are evaluated. Characteristic values of the extreme stresses with a return period of 120 years (the design life of the TMB) are derived by an EVT-based extrapolation. Both the block maxima (BM) approach and the peaks-over-threshold (POT) approach are employed to extrapolate the extreme stresses. The characteristic values of the extreme stress extrapolated using these two methods are compared and discussed; and are further compared with the stresses generated by design traffic loads, which are computed with the help of a 3D finite element model (FEM) of the bridge. The results not only provide a site-specific estimation of the extreme traffic load effects (TLEs) for design validation and condition assessment of the bridge, but also offer a reference for the design and condition assessment of new bridges analogous to the TMB. A reliability-based framework in the context of statistical inference (both Bayesian and frequentist approaches) is proposed to evolutionarily assess bridge condition, and is verified making use of nine years of strain monitoring data acquired from the TMB. The point-in-time reliabilities of the instrumented structural components are first estimated based on the resistance model which does not consider deterioration and annual EVD of the load effects obtained from the strain data. Then the annual reliabilities are updated recognizing the fact that the structural resistance is proved continuously by load history and the EVD of the load effects is always changing. To predict the future reliability, the lifetime reliability profile is obtained considering the structural deterioration. Objective 3: A benchmark study has been launched by sharing the long-term monitoring data (acceleration, temperature, and wind speed and direction) acquired from the instrumented TKB under normal wind and typhoon conditions. Both structural finite element model and field monitoring data (in the category of source-known data and source-unknown data) have been uploaded at the benchmark study website and announced to interested researchers worldwide for collective research. The research results achieved by investigators from different countries on the same benchmark problem have been published in a special issue of an international journal - Smart Structures and Systems (Volume 17, Number 3, March 2016) with the PI being the guest editor. Another benchmark study is developed by using the long-term monitoring data of strain and displacement collected from the TMB. A wavelet-based signal processing technique, comprising de-noising, de-spiking and decomposing of signals has been proposed and verified using the benchmark data. Besides effectiveness, automation and computational efficiency of the signal processing technique are in particular studied due to the enormous amount of long-term SHM data.

522413.label: Major findings and research outcome
522413.value: 1. When the sensor configuration is appropriately designed, the reliability-based framework in the context of statistical inference is competent for evolutionary bridge condition assessment at two levels: (i) structural component level and (ii) deck cross-section level. The annual probability distributions of daily maximum load effects can be satisfactorily estimated based on the extreme value theory. The FOSM and the MCM generate consistent results in reliability estimation. The structural reliabilities of an instrumented bridge can be successively updated using Bayesian inference. It is important to update annual reliabilities considering prior service loads for existing bridges and use the updated structural reliabilities as the reference for decision making. 2. The proposed novelty index formulated in terms of auto-associative neural networks (ANNs) where the output vector is designated to differ from the input vector is much more tolerant of measurement noise than the conventional ANN-derived novelty index; more importantly, the proposed novelty index can accurately detect structural damage even when the noise level polluted in the monitoring data is different before and after damage. The extension of the proposed novelty index through formulating multi-novelty indices in terms of the measured modal frequencies and incomplete mode shape components enables the identification of damage region(s). 3. The Bayesian linear model (BLM) formulated for characterizing the relationship between the displacement of expansion joints and the effective temperature of bridge deck proves to be an efficient approach to condition assessment of bridge expansion joints in the context of Bayesian inference. The model parameters associated with their uncertainties can be accurately estimated by using Gibbs sampler, from which an anomaly index can be defined to evaluate the probability of failure of expansion joints when new measurement becomes available. Not only the mean displacements at the maximum and minimum temperatures are predicted, but also the upper and lower bounds (uncertainty level) of the predicted displacements under different confidence intervals can be obtained. 4. The Bayesian generalized linear model (BGLM) is well suited for assessing wind-induced displacement responses of an instrumented bridge. In the context of Bayesian inference, Bayesian model class selection criterion can be heuristically applied to choose the optimal model among a set of candidate models considering different explanatory variables and degrees of polynomial. With the optimally formulated model, the maximum wind-induced displacement responses and the corresponding confidence interval under the design wind speed in serviceability limit state (SLS) can be predicted.

522413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
522413.value: 1. Multi-hazard risk assessment of bridges using long-term SHM data: As bridge ages, its vulnerability to extreme events will potentially increase. Multi-hazard including strong typhoon, overloaded traffic, ship collision, and earthquake should be taken into consideration in the life-cycle safety and resilience assessment of the bridge. 2. Integration of long-term structural health monitoring data and bridge management system: To make it easy understanding for the bridge engineers and decision-makers to determine the maintenance priority and strategy, the results of bridge condition assessment are preferred to be represented in terms of bridge condition rating (BCR). Therefore, an SHM-based BCR system providing guidelines for bridge maintenance and inspection is highly desirable. 3. Establishment of a linkage to connect SHM technology, and bridge design and assessment standards: Due to the absence of information about load and structural behaviors, the existing bridge design and evaluation standards use some empirical models or measures, and they are still in the stage of semi-probabilistic stage. With the rapid development of SHM technologies and increasing applications to bridges, performance-based bridge design and assessment might be realized.

522413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
522413.value: Structural health monitoring (SHM) has become of great significance in civil engineering community over the past two decades. It is a process of tracing the changes in structural conditions (including material and geometric properties) and the operational and loading environments, which adversely affect the current or future performance of the structure. By deploying a sophisticated on-structure instrumentation system on the Tsing Ma, Kap Shui Mun, and Ting Kau Bridges, Hong Kong has established a landmark paradigm in the late 1990s to industrial and professional communities for showcasing the SHM technology. After the system has continuously acquired data over 15 years, it is high time to use the highly valuable and unique monitoring data to pursue a comprehensive study from structural condition diagnosis to prognosis. The outcomes of this project greatly facilitate the transition of various advanced SHM methods from academic research to actual practice, and help realize the structural condition/damage prognosis capability that is currently recognized as the 'grand challenge' problem in the SHM research community.

522513.value: To project and map urban and rural temperatures over Hong Kong, for the next three decades to 2039, at high resolution using thermal remote sensing images as the mapping base, along with dynamic raster modeling. To test different urbanisation parameters (Plot Ratio, NDVI, and ISI) and their optimum scale of influence using Dynamic Raster Modelling, where each pixel will change with a different warming rate at each time step (year, decade, according to its degree of urbanisation. To investigate and explain the observed exponential increase in urban temperatures in Hong Kong over the last 3 decades To examine whether the rising urban temperature trend is due to local geographical factors within Hong Kong, or if it is part of a broader pattern over the PRD region

522513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
522513.value: Hong Kong exhibits the densest urban populations in the world, averageing 60,000 persons per km², and 3000 per hectare in some districts. Hong Kong residents already suffer severe heat stress in summer, but examination of Hong Kong’s climate over recent decades indicates a worrying trend which is difficult to explain using conventional theories. Although rural temperatures have risen at approximately 0.08ºC per decade, urban temperatures have increased much faster, at 0.16ºC since 1949, and this rate of increase has itself accelerated to 0.28ºC per decade since 1980. This is surprising in that Hong Kong became a mature/saturated urban area in the early 1980s thus factors other than increased urbanization must be operating. However, it is difficult to separate the impact of greenhouse-induced climate change from urbanisation impacts because global climate models with low resolution cannot resolve the climate forcing properties of the urban environment, namely the structures. Rates of temperature change at different urban locations depend on the surrounding built environment since building materials create higher thermal load. This project is the first attempt to downscale climate change projections from IPCC models to local urban district scale, accounting separately for greenhouse-induced changes and those due to urbanisation. Past temperature trends from Automatic Weather Stations (AWS) in Hong Kong and the Pearl River Delta (PRD) region will be related to changes in parameters which represent the degree of urbanization around each station. This is represented in Hong Kong by the planning parameters Plot Ratio, Normalised Diffeence Vegetation Index (NVDI)and Impervious Surfaces Index (ISI)from multitemporal satellite images, and in the PRD by NDVI and ISI. Future plot ratios will be obtained from government departments’ listings to account for future urbanization across Hong Kong. Thermal satellite images will provide the mapping base for temperature projections by decade up 2039, using dynamic raster modeling in a GIS. Model outputs according to degree of urbanization will be computed for the whole Hong Kong territory at 30m resolution, both with and without the PRD data, and validated by back projection to year 2000. Results of back projections will confirm/indicate the PRD regional influence on climate change in Hong Kong, which may explain the exponential temperature increase over the past three decades. High resolution mapping of decadal temperatures up to 2039 across Hong Kong, as well as thermal comfort levels and wind speed requirements, will enable authorities to consider climate change in urban development and renewal projects. 世界範圍內，香港具有高密度的城市人口，其中城市人口平均爲60,000人/km2，某些區域達到300,000人/km2。夏天，香港居民一直遭受嚴重的熱疾病。近幾十年來，香港的氣象觀測數據更是顯示了一個令人擔憂的趨勢，且難以用傳統的理論來解釋。即，農村的溫度大約10年升高了0.08℃，城市溫度增加的更快，在1949年上升了0.16℃，此外1980年的增溫率達到了平均10年升高0.28℃。不同城市區域的溫度變化率受到周邊建築物的影響，因爲某些建築材料會産生更高的溫度。該項目首先使用IPCC模型對局部城市範圍開展氣候變化預測，分別解釋由綠室效應和城市化所導致的溫度變化。研究表明，由香港和珠江三角洲（PRD）的自動氣象站（AWS）所觀測到的以往溫度變化趨勢與反應站點城市化程度的參數有關，如使用建築面積比率（Plot Ratio）和來自多時相衛星影像的不透水表面指數（Impervious Surfaces Index , ISI）等參數來表示香港的城市化程度，以及使用ISI反應PRD的城市化程度。本研究將基于熱紅外衛星影像數據在GIS動態栅格模型裏輸入反應城市化程度的參數來預測2039年全香港30m分辨率的溫度分布圖，以及包括和不包括PRD範圍的溫度預測圖，幷且在該結果的基礎上往前推測2000年的溫度分布，以此對模型的結果進行驗證。2039年香港高分辨率溫度分布圖，以及熱舒適水平和風速需求，將能够敦促官方在城市發展和工程翻新方面考慮氣候變化。
