524613.label: Major findings and research outcome
524613.value: In this project, novel flow sensors based on hot-wire anemometer and FBG technology have been developed, and good results are achieved under the field test. Particularly, the proposed flowmeter that consists of a FBG written on Co2+-doped fiber and microchannels can measure the microfluidic flow with detection limit as low as 16 nL/s, which is higher than most microfluidic flowmeters. This work was orally presented at an international conference (Part C: 9.2), and reported on a journal paper (Part C: 8.2) as well. Another type of flowmeter that packaged a FBG written in SMF and several multimode fibers with large Co2+-doped area was proposed and implemented, which is capable of measuring the flow rate of hot-water and oil. The flowmeter can be heated up over 200 Celcius degree in hot oil with temperature of ~130 Celcius degree, which demonstrated the sensor’s capability in measuring flow-rate of hot oil. The prototype of this sensor was tested at PolyU and very good preliminary results were obtained. The field test was conducted at TNO, The Netherlands, and mass flow rate of up to 1750 kg/hr for oil and water was successfully measured using the flowmeter. The fiber-based sensor was demonstrated to exhibit similiar performance to commercial electrical sensors, but the fiber optic sensor possess many advantages e.g. immunity to EMI, long distance measurement, as well as high temperature environment. This work was reported on a journal Optics Express (Part C: 8.4), and presented at the international conferences on Bragg Gratings, Photosensitivity and Poling in Glass Waveguides (BGPP) in Sydney (Part C:9.3), and 25th International Conference on Optical Fiber Sensors in Jeju (Part C: 9.1). Apart from the liquid flow, the wind flow meter was implemented by writing FBG on a metal-filled microstructured optical fiber fabricated at PolyU. This flowmeter was tested at the wind speed up to 2.5 m/s, but definitely can measure even higher velocity due to the high light-heat conversion efficiency i.e. ~7.3 Celcius degree per mW in optical power. This work was reported on a journal paper (Part C: 8.5). All the research on flow meters in this project was also reported in two invited journal papers: IEEE Journal of Lightwave Technology (Part C: 8.3) and Chinese Optics Letters (Part C: 8.1). In addition to academic papers, an US patent was awarded to this technology of measuring flow speed of a fluid based on hot-fiber (Part C: 11.1).

524613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
524613.value: Further Development of the Research include 1. Investigate the packaging materials and designs to extend the measurement range of the optical fiber anemometer to beyond 3m/sec. 2. Investigate vanadium-doped optical fiber and compare its ease of fabrication compare to cobalt-doped fiber. The main advantage of vanadium-doped fiber is its low light absorption at the telecommunication wavelength of 1550 nm compare to its peak pump absorption wavelength of 920 nm - about 40X smaller. 3. Investigate the sensing performance of vanadium-doped fiber with cobalt-doped fiber in measuring hot oil flow rate.

524613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
524613.value: Singlemode optical fibers doped with cobalt are very efficient in converting light energy to heat energy. Cobalt-doped optical fibre inscribed with fiber Bragg grating can serves both as heater and as thermometer, permitting the novel optical fibre to be employed as miniature flowmeter based on the principle of thermal convection of "hot wire". Microfluidic flowmeter using a cobalt-doped fiber was successfully developed to measure liquid flow inside a 40-µm diameter micro-channel with a minimum detectable flow rate of 16 nL/s. A sensor with a higher heat capacity, based on four cobalt-doped multimode fibers surrounding an fiber Bragg grating-inscribed single mode optical fibre, was also developed to measure water and oil flow rate up to 30 L/min. The flowmeter can operate in hot oil up to 130°C and the sensor was packaged inside a stainless steel with an outside diameter of 0.5mm. The novel fiber optic flowmeter is small and can be operated more than 10 km away from the measurement unit. It is a potential candidate for the measurement of oil flow in down-holes.

525013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
525013.value: This proposal concerns the development of a low static pressure loss compact broadband reactive silencing device for use in low Mach number flow ducts, which is relevant to ventilation and air conditioning noise control in buildings. The ventilation and air condition system is a major noise source in a modernized heavily serviced building. The traditional dissipative silencers for noise control are bulky. They also result in considerable static pressure drop in the system such that more powerful fans are required to deliver the required air flow. This in turn increases the noise attenuation load of the system. Besides, the porous sound absorption materials inside the dissipative silencers become inefficient relatively quickly in the hazardous environment of the ductwork and even worse, they are not good for human health. The success of the proposed project will not only save substantial amount of energy which is currently wasted by the unnecessarily over-designed ventilation and air conditioning systems, but will also find application in areas where maintenance of a high hygienic level is required. Recent research by the principal investigator on the use of closely packed narrow side-branch tubes of appropriate length combinations to produce sound transmission loss in ducts indicates a great possibility of achieving the present proposed target. It is proposed to carry out a detailed study of side-branch array, especially when the main duct is carrying a low Mach number flow as in practical ductwork, for performance optimization. The study will be conducted mainly through experiments, but analytical and numerical analyses will also be carried out whenever possible to gain insights into the sound transmission/attenuation phenomenon. The propagation of higher acoustic duct modes will also be considered. Since it is likely that the proposed device will interact with the duct flow to produce noise, methods which can weaken such flow-induced noise radiation will be studied and tested experimentally. Apart from the targeted product development, the proposed study is also set to address the complicated acoustics-flow-structure interactions involving cavity resonance, shear flow and vortex shedding in order to enhance our fundamental understanding of the physics. The corresponding results will help advance future aeroacoustics modelling and predictions and will make a significant long term impact to the topic. 這項建議涉及與低靜態壓力損耗寬帶低馬赫數流動管道消音器研發和建築物通風空調噪音控制相關的發展。通風和空調系統是一個現代化建築的主要噪聲源之一。傳統的耗散型消音器是笨重的。它們還導致相當大的靜壓力下降，使得需要更強大的風扇才能提供所需的空氣流量。這反過來增加了噪聲消減系統的負荷。此外，多孔吸聲材料內部耗散消音效率在相對較差的管道環境中降低速度相對較快。更糟糕的是，它們是對人體無益的。對擬建項目的成功，不僅會節省大量的能源和可避免不必要的過度通風和空調系統設計，新研發的消音器也可以應用在高衛生水平的地方。 最近筆者研究工作表明採用緊密排列的窄邊適當長度的組合支管可產生聲音的傳輸損耗，目前提出的目標的實現可能性很大。這項建議提出對狹窄側枝陣列進行詳細的參數研究和它們在低馬赫數管道消音的性能優化。這項研究將主要通過實驗進行，但也將進行理論分析和數值分析，從中洞察的聲音傳輸/衰減現象機理。所提出的消音器與管道氣流的相互作用也會產生噪聲，削弱這種流動引起噪聲輻射的方法也是本研究和實驗測試的目標。 除了有針對性的產品開發，目前提出的研究的結果，可加強對解決複雜聲流結構相互作用問題的基礎物理學理解。相應的結果也將有助於推進未來氣動聲學建模和預測，必將有一個顯著的長期影響。

525013.label: Realisation of objectives
525013.value: The project was carried out both experimentally and computationally (using 3D finite-element simulation implemented by COMSOL). In the numerical part of the study, the sound transmission losses across sidebranch array(s) and the wave mechanisms responsible for the different sound transmission properties were examined in details. Experimental validation of the simulation was done with regular sidebranch arrays. Many different settings of sidebranch arrays have been tested in order to find out the best attenuation these devices can offer. In order to have a more uniform sound attenuation spectrum, methods to introduce more resonance frequencies into the device were explored. The first method was to reduce the spanwise sidebranch length to make room for installing more sidebranch arrays on one side of the duct. Arrays on opposite sides of the duct were also tested. Combinations of sidebranch array and expansion chamber were also included. The FEM simulations also allowed the visualization of the wave interactions within the duct section installed with the sidebranch arrays (with and without expansion chamber). The major wave mechanisms responsible for the sound attenuation (or sound transmission) were sought. The effects of air flow in the duct on the sound transmission losses across sidebranch arrays were investigated experimentally. The test rig was equipped with an anechoic termination to reduce sound reflection from duct exit. Sound excitation was provided by a flush-mounted loudspeaker upstream of the sidebranch arrays. Four-microphone method was used to measure the sound transmission losses. It was found that the sound transmission loss reduction due to the flow was not significant when the air flow velocity was less than 8 m/s. The maximum air flow velocity tested was 20 m/s, which was higher than those within building air ductwork in general. Two methods were derived in order to check whether the initial shear layer at the entrance of the sidebranch array was responsible for the reduction of sound attenuation. First, Perspex trips were used to move the shear layer away from the mouths of the sidebranches. Second, the array was elevated up from the duct wall. However, it was found that all these interventions did not affect much the flow-excitation behaviour, suggesting that that initial shear layer was not responsible for the reduction of sound attenuation, and neither did the vortex excitation. Further experiment was carried out to check the air pressure fluctuation within the sidebranches in the presence of both air flow and acoustic excitation to provide more insights to future research approach.

525013.label: Major findings and research outcome
525013.value: Detailed numerical study on the sound transmission loss across narrow sidebranch arrays of many different settings in the absence of flow inside the main duct is completed. The underlying wave interactions between the duct and the sidebranches and those between the sidebranches are examined. The effect of halving the sidebranch widths to incorporate more sidebranches of different lengths (thus introducing more resonance frequencies into the system) helps to provide a more uniform attenuation bandwidth in general. Having sidebranch arrays on opposite sides of the duct also enhances sound attenuation performance. It is also find that the acoustical performance of the system can be further improved by removing the separating wall between adjacent sidebranches in the spanwise direction. Introducing an expansion chamber alongside with the sidebranch array on one side of the duct improves the low frequency attenuation performance of the assembly. Experiments with a low Mach number flow within the duct were conducted as well. It is found that the sound transmission loss of the sidebranch array is not significantly affected by the flow if the flow velocity is less than 8 m/s in general. This critical velocity changes with increasing acoustic excitation magnitude. This shows that the results of FEM simulations are applicable to flow ducts in most of the building applications, unless the flow rate is very high. However, the array can still offer reasonable sound attenuation when the flow velocity reaches 20 m/s, except that some tonal noises may be heard. It is found through experiments that the initial shear layer at the entrance of the sidebranch array is not very influential to the reduction of sound transmission loss in the presence of flow. Small trippers with circular, triangular and rectangular cross-section have been used to first destroy the shear actions at the initial edge of the array and second to separate the shear layer away from the array. Such intervention can just change the overall frequency responses of the array, but the flow excitation at high flow speed still cannot be mitigated.

525013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
525013.value: It is found that the initial shear layer has very small effects on the aero-acoustics of the side-branch array. There are vorticities within the side-branches. An understanding of the relationship between flow/acoustic excitation on these vertical structures could be helpful in damping down the sound transmission loss reduction in the presence of flow (flow velocity > 16 m/s). Further investigation will be needed. Direct aeroacoustic simulation should be carried out in the future. Two-dimensional DNS should be sufficient for the purpose. The proven strong noise attenuation capacity of sidebranch array and the expected low static pressure loss should make this device very suitable for practical uses. Practical implementation is thus one of the major future actions.

525013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
525013.value: The sound transmission loss across a novel duct silencing device consists of sidebranches is studied in details in this investigation both experimentally and numerically. Various combinations of sidebranches and expansion chamber have been considered. It is shown explicitly that this device can offer broadband sound attenuation and the sound attenuation magnitude can be up to more than 10 dB. Static pressure drop across the device is also very small. Therefore, it is expected that this silencer type will find wide application in the building industry because of its high sound attenuation capacity as well as its low pressure drop (lower fan power consumption). The sound attenuation capacity of the device is reduced upon the introduction of air flow inside the main duct. However, the deterioration of this capacity is not significant when the air flow velocity is less than 8 m/s, but the sound attenuation is still maintained at reasonably good level even when the air flow velocity is increased to 16 m/s. Sound amplification is observed at limited number of discrete frequencies when the air flow velocity reaches 20 m/s. However, this air flow velocity is not common in building applications in general.

525113.label: Project Objectives
525113.value: To conduct theoretical analysis of selected yarn and fabric structures and optimize the fiber architecture design aiming at developing new fabric electrodes with stable conductivity and excellent connectivity, superior fatigue resistance as well as full integration of the active layers or strain conversion elements. 525113.label: Realisation of objectives
525113.value: The project has covered all five objectives with the following details: Objective 1. Theoretical analysis of selected yarn and fabric structures has been carried out. Various fiber architecture designs have been investigated for new fabric electrodes with stable conductivity and excellent connectivity, superior fatigue resistance as well as for the full integration of the active layers or strain conversion elements. The electrodes investigated include fabrics made from composite yarns, weaving and knitting technology. The chosen fabric electrodes have been demonstrated to be repeatedly deformed up to 30% strain for over 1 million cycles and keep their mechanical or electrical performance in the wearable piezoelectric power generators. Objective 2. High-performance and lead-free piezoelectric NaNbO3 nanowires have been synthesized , then be integrated into thin polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) composite films. In addition, PVDF-TrFE nanofiber nonwoven fabrics and NaNbO3/polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) composite thin films have been fabricated and investigated as the active layers. The molecular morphology in these active layers were examined by X-ray diffraction, SEM and HRTEM and their effects, together with orientation, volume fractions of the constituents in the composites, poling parameters on the energy conversion efficiency of the multi-layered piezoelectric power generators have been studied. Objective 3. Several types of wearable electric power generators have been fabricated with a multilayered structure with the active layer sandwiched by fabric electrodes; (2) toothed strain conversion element sandwiched by fabric electrodes; or (3) hybrid structure of piezo- and tribo-units with textile electrodes. The structures and materials of the strain conversion elements have been designed and fabricated so that a large strain or a large strain gradient can be obtained in the active layers. The stress-strain and deformation fields, piezoelectric coefficients, and physical dimension of the made devices have been studied by using finite element analysis and experimental methods. Objective 4. Energy-extraction methods of materials, rectifying circuits and energy storage have been studied aiming at enhanced power output of the wearable electric power generators, including doping with conductive nanowires or tubes in the active layers; or three dimensional fabric conducting network; or impedance-matching, double rectifying bridge for the hybrid generators. Objective 5. Two prototypes have been made and evaluated with the selected new fabric piezoelectric power generators, based on the knowledge gained and technologies described in the first four objectives. The performance requirements have been identified, including power, maximum force, the number of loading cycles. The areas for further improvement have also been determined. Currently, the generators produced a time-average power of ~100 µW, two or three order of magnitude lower than the required value.

525113.label: Major findings and research outcome
525113.value: This project represents a first step in study of fiber-based energy generators with potential applications in wearable technology and Internet of Things. Various materials, device structures, and harvesting circuits were investigated. The mechanistic study has led to the establishment of a theoretical framework for piezoelectric generators. Three most noticeable results have been obtained. First, our investigation of novel contact‐mode hybrid nanogenerators comprising cascaded piezoelectric and triboelectric units. For the first time, a theoretical analysis of the contact‐mode hybrid generator is presented to describe the relationships among transfer charges, voltage, current, and average output power in terms of material properties, hybrid generator structural parameters, harvesting, and operational conditions. The results provide a powerful tool for synthesis and selection of materials, design and optimization of the configuration, and operation of such kind of hybrid generators as well as determination of the value of external capacitor. Secondly, we have synthesized and characterized new piezoelectric composite materials, including electrospun Polyvinyledenedifluoride‐trifluoroethylene (PVDF‐TrFE)/Ag nanowire nanofibers and Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) composites with graphite nanoparticles, Polyvinylidenefluoride (PVDF)‐carbon nanotube (CNT)‐BaTiO3 nanofiber/particle nonwoven fabrics. Fibrous electrodes have been further developed. Based upon these results, we designed, fabricated and tested contact‐mode hybrid nanogenerators comprising cascaded piezoelectric and triboelectric units by using the fibrous composites materials and electrodes. Thirdly, we studied the effects of harvesting and storage circuit design and operational conditions. These efforts have resulted in characterization protocol and evaluation methods. We used the total charges transferred to storage as the key indicator of energy harvested instead of open circuit voltage and short circuit current. Parts of the results have been published in three papers of leading journals. A PhD student completed his study. Three GRF projects in textile energy harvesting systems with Prof. Tao as PI and a joint ITF project, as Co-PI, on self-powered footwear were granted.

525113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
525113.value: Although the project has yielded many new knowledge, piezoelectric composites and fibrous materials, the results have shown the power generated by the piezoelectric generators alone may not be sufficient to provide a replacement of battery in many wearable systems. Thus further investigations have been carried out to study triboelectric generators and their hybrids. A joint ITF project was applied for and granted in 2018 to extend the development for applications.

525113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
525113.value: This project represents a study of energy textiles or fiber-based energy generators with potential applications in wearable technology and Internet of Things. Various flexible, soft, robust energy materials were synthesized at room temperature via solution-based processes. Novel light, large-sized and flexible harvesting device structures and circuits were investigated. New theoretical framework has been proposed for engineering design of the devices. The results have been published in Advanced Energy Materials, Advanced Materials and Advanced Materials Technology.

525213.label: Realisation of objectives
525213.value: Overall Achievement: We have fully addressed Objective 1. We have almost fully addressed Objective 2. Realization of Objective 1: (1) A series of axial compression tests on filament-wound glass FRP (GFRP) tubes filled with compound concrete containing recycled concrete lumps (RCLs) [i.e., compound concrete-filled FRP tubular columns (CCFFT columns)] under monotonic loading was completed to examine the stress-strain behaviour of such compound concrete under FRP confinement. In addition, a series of axial compression tests on FRP-confined recycled aggregate concrete was completed to examine the effects of different forms of recycled concrete (i.e., RCLs vs. recycled concrete aggregates). Two journal papers (Teng et al. 2015; Zhao et al. 2015) reporting these two studies respectively have been published in the ASCE Journal of Composites for Construction. (2) Another series of monotonic axial compression tests on carbon FRP (CFRP) tubes filled with compound concrete was completed to further clarify the stress-strain behaviour of FRP-confined compound concrete. The CFRP tubes were formed manually via the wet layup method on a cylinder mould with fibres oriented only in the hoop direction of the column. (3) A series of cyclic axial compression tests on CCFFT columns was completed to examine the cyclic stress-strain behaviour of FRP-confined compound concrete. The test results were compared with the predictions from Lam and Teng’s (2009) stress-strain model for FRP-confined concrete under cyclic compression. (4) Finite element (FE) modelling of compound concrete was explored. The RCLs were modelled with different shapes (i.e., cubes, rotated cubes, and spheres), and different interfacial characteristics (i.e., friction, frictionless, and tie constraints) were explored to model the interfacial behaviour between the RCLs and the fresh concrete. Numerical convergence was a great challenge in the FE simulation of such compound concrete, and a dynamic solution method was employed in the FE simulation to achieve convergence. (5) A small series of axial compression tests on FRP-confined circular concrete cylinders composed of concrete segments of pre-defined shapes was completed. Finite element modelling of these specimens was reasonably successful. Realization of Objective 2: (1) A series of tests on FRP tube-Confined steel-Reinforced Compound Concrete (FCRCC) columns subjected to eccentric loading was completed; the test variables included the load eccentricity, the column slenderness ratio, the mix ratio of RCLs, and the thickness of FRP tubes. (2) An in-depth investigation into the stress-strain behaviour of FRP-confined concrete in eccentrically-loaded FRP-confined circular concrete columns was carried out using the FE approach. A journal paper (Lin and Teng 2017a) reporting this work has been published in the ASCE Journal of Composites for Construction. Based on the results of this work, a new stress-strain model was proposed to represent the behaviour of FRP-confined concrete in eccentrically-loaded columns. A journal paper reporting this work has been submitted to the ASCE Journal of Composites for Construction (Lin and Teng 2017b). (3) Theoretical analysis using Jiang and Teng’s (2012) model for FRP-confined slender concrete columns under eccentric loading was carried out to simulate responses of the test FCRCC columns. The stress-strain model for FRP-confined concrete in eccentrically-loaded circular columns proposed in this project (Lin and Teng 2017b) was used in the theoretical analysis. (4) The design equations of Jiang and Teng (2013) for the load-carrying capacity of slender FRP-confined circular concrete columns have been used to predict the test results of the FCRCC columns. This work is still in progress and will be soon completed. (5) The seismic response of FCRCC columns, which is beyond the revised scope of the project, was explored via the testing of a large-scale column subjected to the combined action of axial compression and cyclic lateral loading. A PhD student, Mr. J.K. Zhou, has been trained in this project. He is expected to submit his PhD thesis before Aug 2018. 525213.label: Major findings and research outcome
525213.value: Findings Related to Objective 1: Axial compression tests: (1) With a significant level of confinement from an FRP tube/wrap, the effect of RCLs on the properties of compound concrete is much reduced and may be largely eliminated. (2) When no FRP confinement exists, the strength of recycled concrete has a more pronounced effect on the strength of compound concrete. (3) For unconfined specimens, when the old concrete is stronger than the fresh concrete, the compound concrete is also stronger than the fresh concrete and the strength increases with the increase of mix ratio. (4) FRP confinement can significantly reduce the degree of scatter in the test results of compound concrete. (5) Jiang and Teng’s (2007) analysis-oriented stress-strain model (Eng. Struct., 29-11, 2968-2986) provides reasonably close predictions for FRP-confined compound concrete, but it tends to overestimate the ultimate axial strain for concrete confined by a very strong FRP tube/wrap. (6) Unloading/reloading cycles have little effect on the envelope curve of stress-strain responses of FRP-confined compound concrete regardless of the mix ratio of the RCLs. (7) Lam and Teng’s (2009) cyclic stress-strain model provides very accurate predictions for the unloading/reloading curves of FRP-confined compound concrete. FE modelling: (1) For unconfined specimens, the interfacial properties between the RCLs and the fresh concrete mainly affect the peak axial stress of compound concrete; the FE results obtained with the Tie Constraint option agree very well with the test results while those with frictionless interfaces significantly underestimate the peak axial stress. (2) For FRP-confined specimens, when the Tie Constraint option is used, the FE results obtained with cubic RCLs are very close to those with spherical RCLs and both are closer to the test results than those with the Friction or the Frictionless Constraint option. (3) When RCLs are modelled as cubes without any rotation, the interfacial properties have only a slight influence on the stress-strain response of compound concrete. Findings Related to Objective 2: (1) With a significant level of confinement from an FRP tube, the effect of RCLs on the load-displacement response of FCRCC columns under eccentric loading is negligible. (2) FRP confinement significantly enhances the performance of eccentrically-loaded steel-reinforced compound concrete columns. (3) Jiang and Teng’s (2012) model with the incorporation of the proposed stress-strain model for FRP-confined concrete in eccentrically-loaded circular columns (Lin and Teng 2017b) can predict well the load-displacement curves of the test FCRCC columns.

525213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
525213.value: Objective 3 in the original application (i.e., to develop a theoretical model for FRP tube-confined steel-reinforced compound concrete columns subjected to seismic loading) has been deleted as a result of funding reduction. This objective aiming to investigate the seismic response of FCRCC columns is of great value and importance and deserves further research. Actually, a large-scale FCRCC column subjected to the combined action of axial compression and cyclic lateral loading has been completed, and some preliminary findings have been obtained. A systematic study needs to be conducted in the future to reach more solid conclusions.

525213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
525213.value: A novel method of recycling demolition concrete is to directly reuse large pieces of coarsely crushed demolition concrete (referred to as recycled concrete lumps or RCLs) for direct mixing with fresh concrete in new construction, leading to what is referred to as “compound concrete”. This method avoids the complex process of recycling concrete as aggregate and other associated disadvantages. However, due to the large size of RCLs, compound concrete is much more heterogeneous than conventional concrete and the weak interfaces between RCLs and fresh concrete may also compromise its performance. A new technique has been explored by the PI’s group to improve the properties of such compound concrete, in which the compound concrete is provided with a substantial amount of confinement supplied by an external fibre-reinforced polymer (FRP) tube. This project has been undertaken to understand and model the behaviour of columns composed of FRP confining tubes filled with compound concrete. A systematic experimental study and advanced finite element modelling to extrapolate the test results have been carried out. The research has provided a solid basis for the formulation of a design procedure for FRP tube-confined concrete columns containing RCLs.

525513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
525513.value: Effective motor recovery after a stroke highly depends on the remapping of the motor centers in the uninjured motor-related brain tissue away from the lesion site in the brain through the neuroplastic process. How to help the brain re-establish the motor function in the motor-related areas is a key to the successful post-stroke rehabilitation. Without proper intervention after stroke, neuroplasticity could lead to an unexpected reorganization of motor maps in the brain. Study has been found in squirrel monkeys that stroke without any specific training resulted in shrinkage of the hand representation in the damaged hemisphere, which was accompanied by an enlargement of the representations of the elbow and the shoulder. Approximately 70% to 80% of stroke patients have upper-extremity impairment, and most of them experienced reasonable recovery at the shoulder and elbow, but limited motor restoration at the hand function. Motor imagery (MI) is a voluntary mental practice of a specific action without muscular execution, has been proposed in stroke rehabilitation since it engages largely similar neural networks as its physical execution. Brain computer interface (BCI) using electroencephalography (EEG) is a technique that utilizes neurophysiological signals originating in the brain. However, BCI using EEG on stroke patients usually apply all electrodes cover the whole-brain in order to achieve high classification accuracy. This may lead the control algorithm adapting to the current EEG pattern of the stroke patients without guiding the brain to be trained in the focalized motor-related regions, and minimize the neuroplasticity in the brain to remap the hand function. Robotic therapy can provide repetitive and task-specific practice. The BCI system can be designed to have a real-time feedback by directly control the hand movement through robotic system during MI training. The knowledge gap of current literature and research is that there has been a lack of study on the use of EEG for MI in combination with robotic therapy to improve the hand function. There is also a lack of study which examines the effects of BCI motor imagery training in focalized motor-related cluster areas after stroke. In this project we will design a control algorithm to identify the focalized motor-related clusters for hand function on each stroke patient. A real-time feedback will control the robotic hand when motor imagery is successfully identified. 525513.label: Realisation of objectives
525513.value: Twenty-four chronic stroke subjects (20 males and 4 females; mean age = 54 ± 2 years) were recruited in this project. All subjects completed a 20-session robot hand training with brain signal (EEG) recording. Paretic upper limb motor functions of stroke subjects were assessed before and after intervention by trained clinical assessors who were blinded to the intervention. Subjects were randomly assigned to two groups: (1) RobotEEG-AO Group: Motor observation and imagery during video display of biological movement with real-time EEG guidance to trigger the robot hand: observation of a video demonstrating either grasping or releasing a cup using the subject’s unaffected hand, and the video frames were flipped to pretend that the subject was observing his/her affected hand to do those hand actions. Robot hand was triggered to help hand open or grasp if suppression of Mu wave (8-13 Hz) was above 20% of Mu power during resting state, which is the average value of healthy people. (2) RobotEEG-Text Group: Motor imagery during display of text instruction of movement without EEG guidance: observation of a text instruction of hand open or grasp. EEG signals were recorded continuously and simultaneously with an amplifier (g.USBamp, g.Tec Medical Engineering GmbH, Austria) with 16 active electrodes (g.LADYbird, g.Tec Medical Engineering GmbH, Austria) during all 20-session robot-assisted hand training in both groups. Sixteen electrodes were placed over the central area according to the international 10-20 system (C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, Cz, FC1, FC2, FC3, FC4, FCz, CP1, CP2, CP3, CP4). EEG signals were referenced to a unilateral earlobe, grounded at a frontal position (Fpz), sampled at 256 Hz, and filtered with a band-pass filter (2–60 Hz) and a notch filter (48–52 Hz). All electrodes were filled properly with a conductive gel to ensure the transmission impedance remained below 1 kOhm. For the subjects who were given video display (RobotEEG-AO group), their EEG signals were processed in real time to perform EEG guidance. C3 or C4 was selected to compute Mu suppression according to the subject's brain lesion side. The Mu suppression is believed to be associated with the activation of mirror neuron system. Hence it can be used as a neural modulation feedback clue to guide the participant. The EEG signals were first converted to the frequency domain using fast Fourier transform algorithm with a Hanning window covering the EEG data during the video display (6 s). The mean power in the Mu band (8–13 Hz) for the selected electrode was calculated. Then the Mu suppression score was calculated based on the percentage of the decreased Mu frequency power during motor imagery and relative to the baseline of the Mu power at resting state. Robot hand was triggered to help hand grasp or open if the mu suppression score is greater than 20%, which is the average value of healthy subjects. Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) can be an indicator telling people the neural reorganization during the training. Sixteen subjects were selected from the twenty-four chronic stroke subjects with the requirement of having no MRI contraindications. They had MRI scans before and after the intervention with eight subjects in each group. A 3T Philips MR scanner (Achieva TX, Philips Medical System, Best, Netherlands) with an 8-channel head coil was used to acquire high resolution T1-weighted anatomical images (TR/TE=7.47/3.45 ms, flip angle=8°, 308 slices, voxel size=0.6×1.042×1.042mm3), and BOLD fMRI images (TR/TE=2000/30 ms, flip angle=70°, 37 slices/volume, voxel size=2.8×2.8×3.5mm3). Subjects were presented with a white crosshair in black background and instructed to rest while focusing on the fixation cross. The resting state fMRI acquisition lasted for 8 minutes. This project has three main outcomes to evaluate the effect of EEG biofeedback in robotic hand training with stroke subjects: (1) clinical outcome: Action Research Arm Test (ARAT) and Fugl-Meyer Assessment for upper-limb (UL-FMA) were used to evaluate the motor functions of the paretic upper limb. The assessments of each subject were conducted before and after intervention by trained clinical assessors who were blinded to the intervention. (2) Functional MRI outcome. (3) EEG outcome: Fuzzy approximate entropy of EEG reflects the condition of brain neuronal death, loss of synaptic connections, and the general effects of neurotransmitter deficiency. It has been applied as a nonlinear dynamic approach provides insights into brain damages.

525513.label: Major findings and research outcome
525513.value: The EEG outcome has been published in a peer-reviewed journal paper and attached as the first publication in part C : research output Chronic stroke subjects and unimpaired subjects were recruited to examine the differences in their EEG complexity. After training with the RobotEEG-AO, motor function of the paretic upper limb, assessed by the Fugl-Meyer Assessment-Upper Limb (FMA-UL), Action Research Arm Test (ARAT), and Wolf Motor Function Test (WMFT) improved significantly (p < 0.05). Furthermore, the EEG Fuzzy approximate entropy (fApEn) in stroke subjects increased considerably in the central area of the contralesional hemisphere after training (p < 0.05). A significant correlation was noted between clinical scales (FMA-UL, ARAT, and WMFT) and EEG fApEn in C3/C4 in the contralesional hemisphere (p < 0.05). This finding suggests that the increase in EEG fApEn could be an estimator of the variance in upper limb motor function improvement. In summary, fApEn can be used to identify abnormal EEG complexity in chronic stroke, when used with BCI-motor observation training. Clinical Outcome with twenty-four chronic stroke subjects have been analyzed and manuscript is under preparation and listed in the part C: research output After training, both groups (RobotEEG-AO and RobotEEG-Text) showed significant clinical improvement in UL-FMA (RobotEEG-AO Group: p=0.033; RobotEEG-Text Group: p=0.036) and ARAT (RobotEEG-AO Group: p=0.045; RobotEEG-Text Group: p=0.009). This indicated that robot hand training could promote the hand function recovery of the stroke subjects when the subjects used motor imagery (video or text only) to move their affected hand during the training. Functional MRI outcome showed both groups exhibited increased neuronal activation in the limbic system, the ipsilesional inferior frontal gyrus and temporal areas after the interventions during action observation. Among these regions, RobotEEG-AO group showed greater activation changes in the inferior frontal gyrus, and contralesional limbic system (hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus), whereas RobotEEG-text group showed greater activation changes in the temporal areas, and ipsilesional limbic system. Further analysis on the EEG frequency band change has been prepared as the third paper listed in the part C: research output The results showed power suppression was found in all the frequency ranges for both unimpaired and stroke subjects during action observation. Specifically, insufficient power suppression in Mu and low beta (16-20 Hz) range in the affected hemisphere was demonstrated in chronic stroke subjects. The inter-hemispheric asymmetry index of power suppression of chronic stroke subjects was significantly greater than that of unimpaired subjects in Mu and low beta ranges.

525513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
525513.value: A neurofeedback training system with combining ipsilesional and contralesional EEG signals for stroke hand rehabilitation has been developed. It is suggested that the contralesional primary motor cortex (M1) may apply a profound interhemispheric inhibitory drive to the ipsilesional M1 during paretic hand voluntary movement. This concept has been applied to transiently improve post-stroke motor function by suppression of the contralesional M1 excitability. The new control algorithm provided feedback based on suppression of the contralesional activities in the Mu frequency band (8-13 Hz) of the brainwave in order to facilitate the ipsilesional sensorimotor cortex activities simultaneously, and to further enhance the motor function. The training effectiveness of the neurofeedback training system was evaluated. The results showed robot hand training could promote the hand function recovery of the stroke subjects when the subjects used motor imagery (video or text only) to move their affected hand during the training. MRI imaging also reveal the changes in brain activities after the 20-session training on chronic stroke subjects. Further studies can develop different robot trainings on other joints in stroke rehabilitation and consider combining motor imagery and EEG analysis in their training protocol.

525513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
525513.value: This study developed a Brain Computer Interface (BCI) based stroke rehabilitation training system to assist stroke patients to recover the motor function of upper limb. In order to validate the training effect of BCI-robot hand training, two groups were set up in this study: (1) RobotEEG-AO Group: Robot hand was triggered by real-time brainwave (electroencephalogram, EEG) with videos of hand movement for action observation. (2) RobotEEG-Text Group: Robot hand was using motor imagery with text cue. The results of clinical scales showed that the stroke patients in both groups had significant improvement in the motor function of upper limb after the 20-session training. Furthermore, the brainwave complexity has been analyzed using EEG Fuzzy approximate entropy (fApEn) technique, stroke subjects has increased fApEn considerably in the central area of the contralesional hemisphere after training (p < 0.05). A significant correlation was noted between clinical scales and EEG fApEn in the motor area in the contralesional hemisphere (p < 0.05). This finding suggests that the increase in EEG fApEn could be an estimator of the variance in upper limb motor function improvement. In summary, fApEn can be used to identify abnormal EEG complexity in chronic stroke, when used with BCI-motor observation training.

525813.label: Project Objectives
525813.value: We first aim to develop realistic models for converter systems having multiple structures and multiple operating modes. Our work will address realistic systems, and hence we will focus on a few selected hybrid power conversion systems, such as photovoltaic-battery systems, multiple-input converters, wind-generator-battery systems, fuel-cell-battery systems, etc. We aim to perform detailed analysis on the models, aiming at identifying the complex behavior related to the switching of structure and operating mode under variation of system parameters (e.g., sunlight intensity variation, wind speed variation, etc.). Results will be presented in design-oriented forms that can facilitate practical design of the systems for stable operation over practical ranges of parameter variations. Finally, we aim to develop viable verification tools and experimental platforms for comparison and verifications of the models and analytical findings. These include setting up of brute-force simulations of the actual switching systems as well as construction of experimental prototypes of the hybrid power conversion systems.

525813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
525813.value: Power converters are nonlinear systems. A rich set of nonlinear phenomena have been observed in dc-dc converters, such as period-doubling bifurcation, Hopf bifurcation, non-smooth bifurcation and chaos. Among them, non-smooth bifurcation has been found in many power converter systems where the switching structure and sequence change as some selected parameters are varied. Recently, due to the attractive features of hybrid power systems (e.g., photovoltaic (PV) power generation systems), including direct energy conversion, ease of integration and low environmental impact, some hybrid power conversion systems have been developed rapidly. For localized applications in some remote areas, for example, the standalone PV power generation system, which generally consists of PV panels and storage devices such as rechargeable batteries, is more efficient and preferred over the grid-connected PV power system, as extending the existing grids to cover these regions is not always affordable. Due to the intermittent nature of some renewable sources, like solar energy, and the bidirectional energy flow for the storage devices, practical systems have multiple structrues and multiple operation modes. This project will study the hybrid power conversion system that combines the renewable energy sources and rechargeable batteries. In a typical configuration for a dc-coupled source-battery hybrid power system, the power source and the battery are connected to a dc bus through an unidirectional converter and a bidirectional converter, respectively. As the power source and the state of charge (SOC) of the battery may vary with time during a day, the system is also designed to operate with multiple structures and operation modes. Thus, the closed-loop design has to take into consideration the different modes of operation which the system assumes for different parameter values. It can thus be appreciated that the stability issue is non-trivial as the system assumes different structures in different operating modes under different ranges of parameters. Our aim here is to study the stability and dynamic behavior of the hybrid power systems. We first develop models for the system and the related control. Smooth and non-smooth bifurcations leading to instability observed will be studied thoroughly, by simulations and experimental measurements. To facilitate design, we will derive stability boundaries and present them in graphical forms in different parameter spaces and reveal how different control parameters may interact. Through this project, we aim to gather important information about the effects of control parameters on the design of hybrid power systems having multiple structure and operating modes. 本項目針對近年再生能源的急速發展及其對電力電子變換器的最新要求作出研究。為配合再生能源的隨機性，當其作為電力輸入時，電力電子變換器的工作模式會變成多結構與運作模式。在此工作模式的環境下，加上大範圍的參數變化，變換器的穩定性必須從新審視。本項目以設計為本及配合再生能源的多結構與運作模式的功率變換器，利用非線性系統理論中的分岔分析，在廣泛的實際參數空間建構分岔界面及穩定運作範圍，為工程設計提供重要的系統穩定性設計資訊與指引。

525813.label: Realisation of objectives
525813.value: The project had concluded with all objectives fully met and had gone beyond what was expected at the beginning of the project. To the first objective, we have developed a complete simulation model for multiple converters that operate in a number of operating modes depending upon the real-time circuit conditions. The system consists of basically an arbitrary set of converters, to be set for specific analysis, that contain choices from renewable sources (e.g., PV panels), battery storages, loads via VSCs, and interface with power grid, forming the so-called hybrid system. The aim is to address in particular the multiple structure that is resulted from the change of operating conditions. Selected hybrid systems containing a subset of photovoltaic-battery systems, multiple-input converters, wind-generator-battery systems, and fuel-cell-battery systems can be studied using our simulation model. The extent of the objective met is 100%, as the original plan is to produce a model that allows multiple structure system to be described systematically. Our model can do exactly this, and in fact has also gone beyond the usual point of common coupling. This extension, though unexpected, provides insightful information on robustness of a large power grid. In other words, we have produced a model that not only describes the hybrid system but also incorporates global power flow information on a large power grid. Based on this model, we constructed an analytical system for describing the dynamics of the system under any given set of parameter values. In other words, we are able to reveal the dynamic behavior of a hybrid system defined by the user and produce stability information for that system. The results are automatically organized in graphical format which facilitates review of the stability regions and in theory also different operating regimes. Moreover, our objective to reveal stability information is fully met (100%). The current status of the project has completed the information on stability only, which is the original plan, though the design-oriented presentation format can also extend to cover complete bifurcation scenarios. Thus, we consider that the project can ready offer information beyond what was originally anticipated. The final objective was concerned with the development of viable verification tools and experimental platforms. This objective was also fully met, as we have generated a full simulation program that track the cycle-by-cycle switching operation of each converter in the hybrid system. In other words, our simulation verification does NOT use the model, but uses a complete brute-force circuit simulation, which is the only viable verification for switching systems. Thus, the objective of the simulation verification tool is 100% met. Experimental platforms were also constructed for selected test systems. This is also the expected result, as we did not aim for a completely general experimental platform which is not realistic. Therefore, as illustrated in our publications, we have produced the needed experimental platforms as we originally anticipated. In summary all objectives are completely met.

525813.label: Major findings and research outcome
525813.value: Hybrid power systems are complex dynamical systems that operate with multiple modes and time-varying structures governed by real-time circuit parameters and environmental factors, such as availability of daylight for photovoltaic panels. Through the successful establishment of the hybrid system model, complex dynamical behavior can be uncovered. One major focus is the hybrid solar and storage system, which is now commonly used. We have identified the "jump" bebavior that forces the system to become unstable. Our model permits the cause of such jumping bifurcation to be revealed systematically, and the parameter region for safe operation to be accurately located. This work generates the first report on identifying the various complex jumping behavior of hybrid solar power systems that exhibit multiple operating modes. Our paper in IEEE JETCAS (vol. 5, no. 3, pp. 316-325, September 2015) provided detailed description of the model, analytical results, and experimental verifications. Besides the hybrid solar power system, we have applied the constructed model to study interacting grid-connected systems, and produced novel results in terms of the identification of complex behavior related to voltage sags and catastrophic type bifurcation. The recent paper published in IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics in 2017 gives a comprehensive description of the application approach and the voltage dip phenomenon and its causes. This paper is expected to make some significant contribution to the understanding of multiple structure converter systems. Apart from the above core findings, we also developed connectivity study of multiple input power converters and introduced a new systematic approach to synthesize such converters which are important components of multiple structure converter systems. This work has been published in the IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics in 2015 (vol. 62, no. 10, pp. 6284-6295, 2015). We have extended the model to cover a whole network and proposed a new set of parameters to assess robustness in power systems. This work, published in IEEE JETCAS (vol. 5, no. 3, pp. 456-464, September 2015), provides important propagation information on the process of cascading failure and robustness assessment criteria. Immediately after publication, this work was featured by IEEEXplore Innovation Spotlight in December 2015. The dynamic profile of smart grid global cascading failure was further investigated and a complete dynamic profile model, with novel findings on the possible failure modes, was published in IEEE JETCAS (vol. 6, no. 2, pp. 192-204, June 2017) and in IEEE JETCAS (vol. 6, no. 2, pp. 228-238, June 2017).

525813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
525813.value: In the process of pursuing the core findings for multiple structure power systems, we developed connectivity study of multiple input power converters and introduced a new systematic approach to synthesize such converters which are important components of multiple structure converter systems. This work has been published in the IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics in 2015 (vol. 62, no. 10, pp. 6284-6295, 2015), and further work toward general circuit synthesis is possible. We have also extended the multiple structure model, via a complex network approach, to cover a whole network and in particular proposed a new set of parameters to assess robustness in connected power systems. This work, published in IEEE JETCAS (vol. 5, no. 3, pp. 456-464, September 2015), provides important propagation information on the process of cascading failure and robustness assessment criteria. Further study was made on the dynamic profile and cyber coupled power systems, with preliminary results published in IEEE JETCAS (vol. 6, no. 2, pp. 192-204, June 2017) and IEEE JETCAS (vol. 6, no. 2, pp. 228-238, June 2017). Moreover, we expect to see further complex phenomena in the cyber-coupled system, which will be a practical example of the so-called cyber-physical system currently under hot pursuit.

526313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
526313.value: Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) can perform in situ real time 2D and 3D imaging of tissue structure at sub-micrometer scale, outperforming conventional ultrasound by a factor of 10 to 100. OCT has been used to image the eyes, blood vessels, nerves, and other internal body structures. The key technological enabler of OCT is the wavelength-swept laser source, the output of which is varied repeatedly over a broad wavelength range by a tunable narrow bandpass filter inside the laser cavity. If the sweeping frequency of the tunable bandpass filter equals the fundamental frequency of the laser cavity or its harmonics, the laser is Fourier domain mode-locked (FDML). In a FDML laser, the light from the previous round trip returns back to the tunable bandpass filter exactly when the sweeping tunable bandpass filter returns to the same spectral position, thus the laser no longer need to build up from spontaneous emission. Fourier domain mocking locked lasers have better noise performance, higher output power, narrower spontaneous linewidth, and can have much higher sweeping rates than conventional wavelength-swept lasers. With FDML lasers, it is possible to sweep over 150 nm of bandwidth centered at 1300 nm, to have instantaneous linewidth of tens of picometers and repetition rates of hundreds of kilohertz. Many of the research activities so far however are limited to a particular FDML laser configuration using a semiconductor amplifier (SOA) as the broadband optical gain, and continuous sweeping of the tunable bandpass filter. Other laser configurations using different broadband optical gains such as doped fiber amplifiers, Raman amplifiers, optical parametric amplifiers, and hybrid optical amplifiers etc, or discrete rather than continuous sweeping of the frequency were barely investigated. However it is well-known that other broadband optical amplifiers has better performance than SOA and discrete sweeping can result in narrower linewidth and better point spread function. Furthermore, the theoretical analysis reported so far is computational intensive and not useful as a design tool. In this project, we propose to carry out a comprehensive theoretical and experimental investigation of FDML lasers for general design and configuration. Theoretically, we will take advantage of the natural frequency and time scale in the problem and use the multiple scale analysis to delineate the various physical effects and derive systems of equation governing the evolution of the otpical pulses. Experimentally, we will study the different FDML laser designs and configurations and optimize the laser performance for different applications. 光學相干斷層成像(OCT)技術可以對活體組織進行二維和三維的亞微米量級的成像，比傳統的超聲波成像技術解析度提高10-100倍。OCT技術已經被用於對眼球、血管、神經和其他內部人體組織進行成像。在最新一代的OCT技術中，波長掃描激光器成為整個系統的技術核心。波長掃描激光器通過在激光腔內插入一個可調的窄帶濾波器，可以使輸出光在很寬的光譜範圍內重複掃描。當腔內可調窄帶濾波器的掃描頻率與激光腔的基頻或者諧振頻率相等時，激光器可以產生穩定的輸出，工作在這種狀態的激光器稱為傅立葉鎖模(FDML)激光器。傅立葉鎖模激光器腔內由於濾波器的掃描頻率與腔基頻或諧振頻率同步，在某時刻由可調濾波器濾出的光信號在經過腔內的傳輸回到濾波器時，濾波器的透射波長也經過了整數個週期正好回到光信號的波長，這樣激光信號不需要再重新從自發輻射信號建立，波長的掃描不再受到激光建立時間的限制。傅立葉鎖模激光器相比傳統的波長掃描激光器，具有低噪聲，高輸出功率，窄線寬和高掃描頻率的優點。採用傅立葉鎖模技術，可以在1300nm波段實現150nm寬的光譜掃描，保持瞬時線寬在數十pm，掃描頻率可達數百kHz。傅立葉鎖模激光器的相關研究一直局限於採用半導體光放大器(SOA)作為寬頻增益器件，採用可調濾波器對光譜做連續掃描。其他結構類型，如採用不同的寬頻光增益器件，例如摻雜光纖放大器，拉曼光放大器，光參量放大器，複合光放大器等，或採用離散的光譜掃描代替連續掃描的傅立葉鎖模激光器沒有得到足夠的研究。其他的寬頻光放大器相比半導體光放大器具有更好的性能，離散掃描也能夠獲得更窄的瞬時線寬和更好的點傳播函數(PSF)。而且，現有報導的理論模型需要的數值計算量很大，不能很好應用到傅立葉鎖模激光器的設計研究中。本項目將針對傅立葉鎖模激光器，從理論和實驗兩方面，對傅立葉鎖模激光器的設計和結構進行系統的研究。理論上，我們將從傅立葉鎖模激光器的不同本征頻率和時間長度出發，進行多尺度分析來表徵系統中的多個物理機制，構建能夠描述腔內脈衝傳輸的高效的數學物理方程。實驗上，我們將對不同類型的傅立葉鎖模激光器進行研究和優化，針對多個應用實現高性能的激光輸出。

526313.label: Realisation of objectives
526313.value: 1. Engineering the FDML lasers to optimize the laser performance: Benefiting from the rapid development of optical components in communications, we can transfer a laser signal to another wavelength which can be several tens of gigahertz away from the original wavelength with the mature single-side-band (SSB) modulation technique. Especially when the SSB modulation is cascaded by circulating the signal in an amplified fiber loop, optical frequency comb (OFC) extended to THz bandwidth can be generated from the seeding continuous wave signal after several ten times of propagation in the recirculating frequency shifter (RFS). Since the generated signals at new wavelengths have almost the same linewidth as the seeding continuous wave, the coherence length of the new signals can be very long. We proposed and successfully demonstrated a k-space linear and self-clocked wavelength scanning fiber laser source based on recirculating frequency shifting (RFS). The RFS is realized with a high speed electro-optic dual parallel Mach-Zehnder modulator operating at the state of carrier suppressed single sideband modulation. A gated short pulse is injected into an amplified RFS loop to generate the wavelength scanning pulse train. We found that the accumulation of in-band amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) noise over multiple scanning periods will saturate the erbium-doped fiber amplifier and impede the amplification to the pulse signal in the RFS loop. To overcome the degradation of temporal signal due to the accumulation of ASE noise over multiple scanning periods, we inserted a modulated optical switch into the RFS loop to completely attenuate the in-band ASE noise at the end of each scanning period. The signal to noise ratio of the temporal pulsed signal is greatly enhanced. K-space linear and self-clocked wavelength scanning fiber laser sources in 6.1/7.2 nm scanning range with 20/30 GHz frequency shifting were successfully demonstrated. The results are published in the paper entitled “Rapid, k-space linear wavelength scanning laser source based on recirculating frequency shifter,” by M. Wan, L. Wang, F. Li, Y. Cao, X. Wang, X. Feng, B. Guan, and P. K. A. Wai, in Optics Express, vol. 24, pp. 27614-27621 (2016). 2. Master equation: Theoretical treatments of FDML lasers have recently been advanced in order to help characterize and design FDML lasers. Much like standard mode-locked theories, the FDML laser theory is recast in terms of the center-frequency of the swept filter, thus providing a new center-frequency theory of the electric field envelope. However, such models are computationally difficult to work withbecause of the need to accurately resolve the extremely broad range of frequencies present in the swept frequency sources. So although the models can produce accurate modeling results, it is very inefficient for modeling FDML systems. We took advantage of naturally existing time and frequency scales of separation in order to develop an improved computational framework for modeling FDML laser output. Indeed, a high-frequency asymptotic expansion (WKB) is demonstrated to render the FDML modeling almost computationally trivial. Thus a valuable laser design tool is constructed and a deeper theoretical understanding of swept-frequency sources is achieved. The model has similar modeling accuracy but the computation time is greatly reduced. We used the simplified model for systematical investigation of the signal dynamics in the cavity. Ensemble average of the simulation results can be handled by our model. The results show that the offset frequency of the signal to the central frequency of the swept filter is varying along time. Dispersion and nonlinearity in the cavity are the reasons of such frequency offset. The model had been used in the assessment of the performacne of the novel FDML realizations in this project. 3. Connecting it all together – theory, simulation, and experiments: FFDML fiber lasers enable megahertz wavelength sweeping rate but suffer from the short coherent length. Discretization of the swept spectrum by a comb filter was demonstrated to be effective in enhancing the coherence length. We proposed a novel discretization method of the FDML signal with an intracavity intensity modulator. With the theoretical model developed in Objective 2 and numerical simulations, we found that the discretization of a linearly chirped signal can be realized with a comb filter and/or a periodically driven intensity modulator. Simulations also show that the joint applications of a comb filter and an intensity modulation to the noisy swept signal will improve the signal quality. Based on such method, we proposed a time and Fourier domain jointly mode locked fiber laser with a Fabry-Pérot comb filter and an intensity modulator in the cavity. A 50 GHz free spectral range comb filter in the Fourier domain mode locked fiber swept laser slices the spectrum into a series of comb lines and chops the swept signal into short pulses in time domain. The temporal signal is detected by a photodetector to generate a series of ultrashort pulses to drive the intensity modulator to further polish the intracavity pulses. We experimentally realized the proposed time and Fourier domain jointly mode locked fiber laser. Discrete wavelength swept laser output with a wavelength spacing of ~0.4 nm in a 41 nm sweeping range has been achieved. The scheme of discrete FDML fiber laser using intensity modulator solely is also a promising and more flexible method to replace the comb filter scheme if the synchronization of the driving signals of the FFP-TF and modulator is guaranteed with further engineering. The results are published in the paper entitled “Time and Fourier domain jointly mode locked frequency comb swept fiber laser,” by M. Wan, et al., Optics Express, vol. 25, pp. 32705-32712 (2017).

526313.label: Major findings and research outcome
526313.value: In a harmonically mode locked laser, the supermode noise peaks in the RF spectrum can be observed directly because they are separated from the driving frequency and its harmonics of the active mode locker. Using a simple theoretical model, we showed that the intensities of the supermode noise peaks will decrease if the coherence of the laser output decreases. We harmonically mode locked a Fourier domain mode locked (FDML) fiber laser to the third order. We observed that the supermode noise peak intensities decrease significantly when the detune between the sweeping frequency of the tunable filter and the cavity resonant frequency increases. It is therefore possible to use the supermode noise peaks to monitor the frequency detune of the tunable filter for auto-calibration of FDML fiber lasers. The results are reported in Output 1 of Part C. By using multi-scale analysis, we have derived an equation governing the dynamics of FDML fiber lasers which boost the simulation speed ~100 times without affecting the accuracy of the simulation results when compared to that from the full model. Point spread functions are used to characterize the simulation results for the first time. The highly efficient reduced model can be used to design and optimize the performance of FDML fiber lasers. We have proposed and successfully demonstrated a self-clocked wavelength scanning fiber laser source based on a recirculating frequency shifter (RFS) to generate linearly wavelength-stepped output. We introduced an optical switch into the RFS loop to attenuate the accumulated in-band ASE noise in each scanning period in order to generate temporal pulsed signals with high signal to noise ratio. The injected pulse seed is effectively amplified in the RFS loop. Such self-clocked wavelength scanning sources with high signal to noise ratio on both the spectrum and waveform will have potential applications in high resolution optical frequency domain ranging and imaging systems. The results are reported in Output 5 of Part C. We propose and demonstrated, through both simulation and experiments, a novel discretization method of the FDML signal using an intracavity intensity modulator. Discrete wavelength swept laser output with a wavelength spacing of ~0.4 nm in a 41 nm sweeping range is achieved. Discrete FDML fiber laser using intensity modulator solely is a flexible and promising method to replace the comb filter scheme. The results are published in Output 6 of Part C.

526313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
526313.value: In FDML fiber lasers, a long fiber delay line is introduced into the fiber ring cavity to buffer the whole wavelength sweeping signal such that the rebuilding of laser signals from spontaneous emission can be avoided. Although FDML fiber lasers have been successfully deployed in the optical coherent tomography (OCT) systems as the swept source, the performance of FDML fiber lasers and their application in OCT systems are still limited by the large instantaneous linewidth, which manifests as the high frequency fluctuations on the waveforms. The origin of the high frequency fluctuation should be investigated and methods to control the fluctuations should be developed. The supermode noise peaks can be used to monitor the frequency detune of the tunable filter. Control circuits to carry out auto-calibration of FDML fiber lasers have to be built. We have demonstrated the feasibility of using recirculating frequency shifting to realize a scanning fiber laser source. The next step is to optimize the performance of the scanning fiber lasers. The same applies to the discrete FDML fiber laser using intensity modulator.

526313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
526313.value: Frequency domain mode locked (FDML) fiber lasers were first demonstrated in 2005. In traditional wavelength swept lasers, narrowband wavelength sweeping filters are used in fiber ring laser cavities to confine the instantaneous lasing wavelength. When the filter wavelength is changed, it should stay at the new wavelength for a sufficient long period for the buildup of new lasing signal from spontaneous emission. This buildup time limits the sweeping speed of such wavelength swept laser. In FDML fiber lasers, by introducing a long fiber delay line into the fiber ring cavity to buffer the whole wavelength sweeping signal, the rebuilding of laser signals from spontaneous emission can be avoided. With FDMLs, the wavelength sweeping speed can be enhanced by one to two orders to MHz level. In this project, we developed different FDML designs to optimize the laser performance. In particular, we demonstrated a self-clocked wavelength scanning fiber laser source based on a recirculating frequency shifter to generate linearly wavelength-stepped output. We also demonstrated a novel discrete FDML fiber laser using intensity modulator. In addition, we showed that auto-calibration of FDML fiber lasers might be possible by using the supermode noise peaks to monitor the frequency detune of the tunable filter.

526413.label: Project Objectives
526413.value: Develop a smart building framework: Our framework contains data collection modules, thermal modeling modules, scheduling and optimization modules and control modules. We will clarify their tasks and relationship. Cross-disciplinary understanding on building thermal systems and human comfort: For buildings, our objective is to develop 1) the thermal model/inertia of the building heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC) system; 2) the thermal model/inertia of individual rooms; i.e., different rooms requires different amount of cooling energy at different times. These and the dynamic electricity prices etc will impact on our scheduling algorithms. For human comfort, our objective is to understand flexible human comfort tolerance. From scheduling point of view, flexible human comfort provides further opportunity in schedule adjustment that can be translated to electricity costs reduction. Electricity bill saving computing: Our objective is to comprehensively develop a set of schedules, which collectively maximize bill savings: 1) building electricity demand schedule for electricity purchase from the power market and 2) meeting schedules and room assignment schedules where meetings are scheduled at the good time and good rooms. The schedules can be deterministic, adaptive or stochastic; and we will clarify these. From smart building point of view, we will study the mismatch between bill reduction and energy conservation; and how they may balance. Evaluation and experiments: Our evaluation will be trace driven simulations. We will develop wireless sensing networks and Andriod/iOS applications to collect data for the inputs of our cross-discipline modeling and scheduling algorithms. We will publish papers, train Ph.D. students and conduct outreach activities.

526413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
526413.value: 現階段全世界都在關註節能問題。因為能耗引起的運營費用在很多領域都占據越來越大的份額。下一代智能電網的電費是實時變化的，形成動態電力市場。本項目致力於研究樓宇電費在動態電力市場下的相關問題。在樓宇中，空調系統最為耗電，也引起了廣泛的研究關註。 我們發現樓宇空調系統中有一個特殊的性質，就是熱慣量。具體來說，能量不會從空氣或者水中立刻消散。因為這種慣性，樓宇房間中的能量會被存儲。那麽我們面對動態電力市場時，可以利用此特性來在便宜的時候購入電能，用熱慣量存儲，並在更加合適的時候使用。熱慣量提供了廣泛的空間來研究樓宇房間，會議，人之間的聯系，來最大可能的降低電費消耗。 以此為目的，我們在本項目中會提出一個體系框架，進行廣泛的數據手機，並且進行物理建模，以及進行計算。我們研究在不同情況下確定性和隨機性的優化，以減少電費消耗。本項目研究跨學科。我們要進行物理建模，並且面對物理建模可能帶來的不準確。我們要研究怎樣用計算學的算法來確保這些不準確性不會影響最終算法結果的準確性。另外，我們發現減少電費消耗並不和節能一致，甚至會更多的消耗能量，我們會研究相關問題。我們的研究結果為：1）一個完整的智能樓宇體系框架，以及相應的算法，2）增加跨學科研究的研究方法，3）從智能電網的角度來說，我們提供一個具體的需求端，為智能電網的研究提供幫助。

526413.label: Major findings and research outcome
526413.value: In a smart building energy system, there are the demand side, i.e., human occupancy, human thermal comfort, energy requirement of rooms, and the supply side, i.e., the HVAC system operations, and electricity from the grid. We have made research progress in fine-grained quantification/modeling and optimization in both directions. We also have studied overall optimization of the demand side and supply side and the supporting networking architecture. First, we developed an individualized thermal comfort model. This model breaks Fanger's averaged thermal comfort model developed in 1970. Using this model building operators can break the current uniform and conservative temperature settings, which incur huge waste. This model has three parts, a participatory individualized thermal comfort model (ACM e-Energy'14), a data-driven individualized thermal comfort model (ACM e-Energy'18b), and a group model (ACM Buildsys'14). We developed a Scalable PErsonalized Thermal-Comfort platform (SPET), a hardware independent platform hosting our thermal comfort models. SPET won Techconnect Global Innovation award, 2017. The system was adopted by Henderson Ltd (see acknowledgement letter). We developed a room thermal model. With this model, we can perform precooling of rooms, thermal storage, and electricity bill optimization (RTSS'13, ACM TOSN'14). Second, we studied the operations of HVAC systema and developed a data-driven model which can quantify the chiller performance and substantially optimize the HVAC operations. We evaluated our data-driven HVAC operation with real data from three Pacific Place buildings and observed energy saving can be as much as 2.7 million per year (ACM e-Energy'18a, best paper award). Third, we studied the supporting building network infrastructure (IEEE TETC, IEEE TII'17), and we developed an IoT communication sharing architecture, which can become an efficient support for smart bulidings (ACM Buildsys'17, IEEE INFOCOM'18). We have a related study of using our building occupancy model. We developed a model that can link building occupancy with traffic congestion of nearby roads. We conducted a case study of using the ICC occupancy data to predict traffic status of West Tunnel. Our result showed that our model outperforms the traffic prediction algorithm of Google (ACM CIKM'16). We trained one Ph.D. student, Zimu Zheng with this project. He is about to complete his Ph.D. study (Objective 6 90% completed). Currently, he has first author papers in ACM CIKM'16, ACM e-Energy'18a (best paper award), and a second author paper in ACM e-Energy'18b.

526413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
526413.value: In this project, our emphasis is smart building, i.e., from the aspect of a *same* building, hosting machines of *different* vendors. We are now looking from the aspect of the machinery from the *same* vendor, e.g., chillers, pumps, across *different* building. We are looking into their operation and maintenance. The research question of this project is how to develop fine-grained control of a building, using cutting edge technologies such as IoT, data analytics, etc, so as to minimize energy/electricity bills. The fundamental research question of the road ahead is how to develop fine-grained control of the machines, using cutting edge technologies such as IoT, data analytics, etc, so as to minimize operation and maintenance costs.

526413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
526413.value: Commercial buildings are major energy consumers world wide. With the development of IoT, data analytics, machine learning, developing next generation buildings (a.k.a smart buildings) that is energy efficient, human comfort, smart grid friendly has become a major research endevour in computer science. In a smart building, human beings, rooms etc are the demand side and HVAC systems etc are the supply side. In this project, we outlined a new smart building framework to incorporate cutting edge computing technologies. Within this framework, we developed new models in both the demand side and the supply side. We developed systems and demonstrated that we can substantially save energy consumption. Some of our results have already been observed and implemented by industry, for example, our personalized thermal comfort system has been adopted by Henderson Real Estate Ltd.

526713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
526713.value: 爲了應對日益增長的能源和環境問題的挑戰，零能耗建築(NZEB)是可行的解决方案。零能耗建築是指在特定時間段內從電網需求的淨電量爲零的建築。零能耗建築主要采用可再生能源進行發電，比如太陽能、風能、生物能等。由于可再生能源發電的的不持續性和不可靠性，建築發電量常常不能滿足自身的需求。這就不可避免地造成了實時電量供需的不平衡。一個可行的解决方案是將微電網或分布式發電集成到零能耗建築中。由于微電網靈活性高，易于在社區範圍內集成可再生能源，幷且能够實現用戶參與到電力企業，因而常常被采用。 已有的零能耗建築設計優化的性能指標，比如估計淨能産生量和淨能比，通常以非耦合的方式考慮建築能源的發電和用電，沒有考慮建築實時的發電和用電的平衡性。研究人員已經意識到這些指標的使用可能會造成嚴重的問題，比如設計過大的可再生能源系統和儲能系統，從而造成初投資的增加。因此，需要有效的方法對系統設計進行優化，使用耦合的方式考慮建築實時發電和用電，從而最小化初投資。由于包含了可再生能源發電、能源儲存，以及建築與電網雙方向供電等複雜問題，已有的面向常規建築的優化控制方法不適用于零能耗建築。另外，對電網的平衡性而言，零能耗建築可能會産生積極或消極的影響，這取决于電網的實際需求情况。除了考慮建築本身的節能性，優化控制策略應該最大化積極影響，最小化消極影響。 因此，本項目將主要研究集成微電網的零能耗建築的設計和控制的優化問題，幷以香港新建的零能耗建築“香港零碳天地”爲主要參考對象。采用耦合的方法進行優化設計，旨在通過優化三個關鍵參數（可再生能源，儲熱和電力存儲）達到用最少的初期投資建造出與電網友好的零能耗建築的目的。最優化控制策略旨在通過一個多目標函數最大化對電網的積極影響，幷最小化對電網的消極影響，使得零能耗建築系統保持高能效。該項目最終將提供面向零能耗建築的優化設計和優化控制方法，使零能耗建築爲電網供需平衡作出貢獻。

526713.label: Realisation of objectives
526713.value: 1. A simulation platform is developed based on Hong Kong ZCB (Zero Carbon Building) and each component in the simulation platform is validated using real operation data. 2. The uncertainties of nZEB performance are quantified and the relationship between the probability to achieve annual zero energy balance and the design mismatch ratio is identified when the uncertainties in energy demand, renewable resources are concerned. The deterministic approach and stochastic approach, applied in sizing renewable energy system for nZEB respectively, are investigated and compared. 3. Sensitivity analysis is conducted on an optimized system (photovoltaic/wind turbine/bio-diesel generator) to investigate the impacts of the design input variations on the building performance (i.e. operation cost, CO2emission, impact on grid). 4. A comparison study is conducted on two design optimization methods for renewable energy systems in zero energy buildings, including a single objective optimization using Genetic Algorithm and a multi-objectives optimization using Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm (NSGAII). Building energy system models and renewable energy system models are developed and adopted, allowing the consideration of the interaction between building energy systems and renewable energy systems in optimization. 5. Optimal scheduling of buildings with energy generation and thermal energy storage under dynamic electricity pricing is discussed based on the real operation data collected from Hong Kong ZCB and simulation platform. A cost penalty is introduced to consider the on/off number of the active energy systems and therefore reduce their on/off switching frequencies. 6. Considering the mismatch between the energy demand and energy supply, a model predictive control (MPC)-based strategy using nonlinear programming (NLP) algorithm is proposed to optimize the scheduling of the energy systems under day-ahead electricity pricing.
