526713.label: Major findings and research outcome
526713.value: 1. A robust design method for sizing renewable energy systems in nZEB is developed concerning uncertainties in renewable resources and demand load. The proposed robust design method is applied to the planning of renewable energy system for the Hong Kong Zero Carbon Building 2. Optimal scheduling of buildings with energy generation and thermal energy storage under dynamic electricity pricing is determined using mixed-integer nonlinear programming. The optimal scheduling strategy minimizes the overall operation cost day-ahead, including operation energy cost and cost concerning the plant on/off penalty. 3. Based on sensitivity analysis, among four considered items (i.e. wind velocity, building electric load, cooling load and solar radiation), wind velocity is the key factor concerning mismatch ratio, the cost and CDE (CO2 emissions), while the building loads should be considered with high priority concerning the comprehensive performance (combined objective) of the building 4. The performances of the buildings with the renewable energy systems optimized by two methods (i.e., single objective and multi-objective) are much better than that of the benchmark building (i.e., Hong Kong zero energy building). The single objective optimization can provide the “best” solution directly for a given objective while the multi-objective optimization provides rich information for designers to make better compromised decisions. 5. A model predictive control (MPC)-based strategy using nonlinear programming (NLP) algorithm is developed for the energy systems under day-ahead electricity pricing. Significant reductions in carbon dioxide emission, primary energy consumptions and operation cost are achieved considering two types of grid-connections (i.e., selling electricity to grid is allowed/forbidden).

526713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
526713.value: 1. In the design of climate-sensitive nZEB, design options of passive design strategies and renewable energy available should be carefully considered to cater for the local climate. As a rule of thumb, the target of zero net energy is easy to be achieved for low rise buildings with less energy use intensity and large roof space for solar photovoltaic. However, the question is: can the net zero energy be achieved in high-rise buildings or buildings with high energy use intensity? 2. Optimal solutions for nZEB should take into account both system design and control strategies. Unfortunately, the complex interplay of all the intelligent systems in nZEB and various uncertainties, such as strong dependence of energy production/consumption on weather and occupants actions, challenge the conventional way of designing and operating/controlling the buildings. It is necessary to develop a generic decision tool that move the design and control of buildings toward a holistic view, ensuring a reliable, cost-effective, environment-friendly and gird-friendly building providing the living and/or working environment of good quality

526713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
526713.value: Facing to the shortage of energy, the idea of nearly/net zero energy building (nZEB), which generates the same amount of energy as they consume over a specific period (e.g. a year), takes full advantage of renewable energy and distributed energy system to address the issue of energy and environment problems effectively. The design and control strategies of nearly/net zero energy buildings (nZEB) are not straight-forward since the buildings may involve complex integration of different energy systems, such as renewable energy generations, energy appliances, energy storages and may also interact with the smart grid. It is necessary to develop effective design and control methods for nZEB comprehensively considering the effects of climate/site on design, design optimization, the uncertainties/sensitivities.

526913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
526913.value: The interest in technologies that broaden the roles and capabilities of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs)/micro aerial vehicles (MAVs) has increased rapidly over the last decade in the aeronautical engineering community. This is due to the emerging roles of these vehicles in surveillance and reconnaissance applications, such as greater accessibility to the land-slide/forest fire areas, unsurpassed by conventional light aircrafts and satellites. Active flow control based on dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) plasma actuators is one of the promising technologies in advancing the aerodynamic performance and maneuvering of UAVs/ MAVs, because plasma actuators are fully electronic with no moving parts such as flaps or ailerons; they have an extremely fast response, very low mass, and low input power. Particularly, they are flexible, so that they can be formed to various shapes and located on the air vehicles with relative ease. The project is a continuation of our earlier pilot study aiming to control actively a leading-edge vortex on a highly swept full-span delta wing at typical UAV Reynolds numbers, by means of a DBD plasma actuator supplied with a steady ac voltage (Lee at al. 2012). The smoke-wire flow visualization shows that the plasma actuator implemented on one side significantly affects the leading edge vortex structure on the other side and delays its breakdown, which enhances the lift and roll moment accordingly in the force measurements. This interesting phenomenon has not been observed in the literature before and the underlying mechanism is unclear. Therefore, the project addresses two specific objectives—(1) to understand the physical mechanisms behind this effective control; (2) to expand our previous steady excitation to periodic excitation on the full-span delta wing. Performance enhancement and effects on the vortex structures by periodic excitation will be investigated; meanwhile, operational conditions for optimum performance will be pursued, including the plasmas geometry and positions, the modulation frequency, and the duty cycle. Flow diagnostic techniques such as PIV, smoke-wire flow visualization and Pitot tube will be used to characterize the leading edge vorteies with and without control. The measured data will be analyzed in detail to gain insight into the flow physics and its consequences to the lift enhancement, drag reduction and delta wing maneuverability under control. It is envisaged that the knowledge gained from this project will provide a new solution for the optimum performance of a delta-winged UAV 在過去的十年中，航空工程界積極地關注著拓展無人駕駛飛行器（UAV）以及微型飛行器（MAV）的角色定位和功能拓展。這主要是因為與傳統的輕型飛機和衛星相比，無人機在監控和偵察方面，比如應對滑坡、森林火災等，具有極大的優勢。介質阻攔放電（DBD）等離子致動器的主動式氣流控制是一項在提升無人機/微型機的空氣動力性能方面很有前景的技術，因為等離子致動器是完全電子化的，可以不需要副翼、襟翼等移動部件；等離子致動器有極快的反應，較輕的重量和較小的能量消耗。此外，它外形不受限制，因此可以輕易地安裝在飛行器上。本項目延續了我們先前的研究，即在典型的無人機雷諾數下，旨在通過穩定的交流電產生等離子激勵（Actuation），對大後掠角三角翼的前緣渦進行主動控制 （Lee al. 2012）。先前煙線視流實驗顯示，單側的等離子致動器會顯著影響另外一側的渦結構並推遲其破裂，這相應地增大了升力和滾轉扭矩。這個特殊現象到目前還沒有清晰的物理機制解釋，也沒有在其他文獻中出現過。因此，本項目致力於兩個目標︰（1）了解造成這種現象的物理機制；（2）除了穩定的激勵，還將使用周期性的激勵用於全翼展的三角翼上並觀察其性能提升以及前緣渦結構的變化；同時，得到最優情況下的操作條件，包括等離子致動器的幾何形狀和位置，調制頻率，和放電佔空比（Duty cycle）。PIV、煙線視流和皮托管等流場觀測技術將會被用來確定前緣渦在無控制和有控制的情況下的特徵。隨後對測量到的數據做分析，進一步加深對三角翼流場在等離子致動器作用下物理變化，升力提升，阻力減少和機動性能提升的認識。最後我們期望從這個項目中獲取一個全新的可以用於三角翼無人機最優方案。

526913.label: Realisation of objectives
526913.value: In this project, dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) plasma actuators were applied on a highly-swept delta wing to control the leading edge vortices (LEVs). Experimental investigations were conducted in a low-speed wind tunnel at low Reynolds numbers. To achieve all the proposed objectives, the investigation was carried out by four steps: 1. A DBD control system was developed. It could provide both the steady and the periodic control. This system was synchronized with other measurement facilities. The characteristics of the DBD plasma actuator were studied in the quiescence air by using particle image velocimetry (PIV) and power measurement. 2. The unsteady flow phenomena of the baseline delta wing were studied in the wind tunnel. The mechanism of the quasi-periodic antisymmetric LEV interaction was explored. We found that the vortex-crossflow interaction is responsible for this LEV interaction. The frequency features of the unsteady flow phenomena were measured. 3. The steady DBD control was applied on the delta wing to examine the control effect on the global LEV structure. The smoke flow visualization showed that the DBD plasma actuator at the leading edges could significantly modify the LEV structure over the delta wing. Factors of the actuator position (fore or aft) and the operational mode (in single DBD actuator or in a fore/aft pair of actuators) were examined. Detailed PIV measurement and force measurement were conducted to correlate the flow structure modification and the aerodynamic performance. Furthermore, we found that the crossflow in the symmetric plane (interaction between LEVs) was responsible for the opposite local control effect between the symmetric and asymmetric control cases. The modified flow structure over the delta wing induced a sideslip effect, which promoted or delayed the LEV breakdown locations. 4. Periodic DBD control was applied on the delta wing. The control parameters were adopted from the baseline case and the steady control case. The experiments were conducted in a wide range of angles of attack by using the smoke flow visualization, the phase-locked PIV measurement and force measurement. Different modulation frequencies were compared. The high frequency control showed a longer (t/T) impact on the local flow structure. Whereas, the low frequency control achieved a further control state. However, the periodic control induced oscillation of the global flow structure. By increasing the duty cycle, the time-averaged control performance became better. Through this project, a DBD control technique was developed, which can provide both the steady and the periodic control. The experimental investigation clearly showed the evolutions of the flow structure under the DBD control over the delta wing and the consequences to the aerodynamic performance. The underlying mechanism of the LEV control via DBD plasma actuators was studied. In summary, all the proposed objectives of this research project have been well achieved.

526913.label: Major findings and research outcome
526913.value: 1. The steady DBD plasma actuator generated a wall-jet on the delta wing surface, with a maximum velocity of U_max≅3.2 m/s. In the periodic mode, it induced a vortices queue. The strength of vortices and the distance between them were dependent on the modulation frequency and duty cycle. 2. The DBD plasma actuators well demonstrated their feasibility of the LEV breakdown control over a slender delta wing. At a sufficient angle of attack with LEV breakdown occurring on the delta wing, the asymmetric control promoted the vortex breakdown on the controlled side, whereas, delayed the vortex breakdown location on the uncontrolled side. With the symmetric control, both LEV breakdown locations were delayed to downstream. The DBD plasma actuators at the apex showed more control authority on LEV breakdown control than those at the rear. Although the global flow structure was modified significantly in most cases, the overall lift and drag coefficients changed very little. Meanwhile, the induced moments were remarkable. 3. The control evolution at the leading edge was dependent on the angle of attack, which meant the local shear layer strength. At a low angle of attack, the DBD plasma actuator destroyed the local weak shear layer and entrained a new shear layer attaching on the leeward surface to the inboard side. At a medium angle of attack, the local shear layer was deformed to the inboard bottom. Vortices were generated in the shear layer and finally merged with the LEV. At a high angle of attack, the DBD plasma actuator promoted the shear layer to generate a new LEV at the leading edge. The new LEV further developed with the shear layer and finally dominated the flow field. 4. With the periodic DBD plasma actuator, the high frequency control showed a longer (t/T) impact on the local flow structure. Whereas, the low frequency control achieved a further control state. However, the periodic control induced oscillation of the global flow structure. By increasing the duty cycle, the time-averaged control performance became better. 5. Four journal papers and two conference presentations were published, referred to this project. Another two journal papers are under preparing. A Ph.D student has graduated by the supporting of this project.

526913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
526913.value: In this project, the DBD plasma actuator had shown its feasibility to control the flow separation over the delta wing. Therefore, further investigations will be conducted to study the control performance on bluff bodies, for the separation suppressing and drag reduction. This can improve our understanding of the DBD-based flow control technique. In practical application, this DBD technique will be installed on the real unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) to control the maneuvering.

526913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
526913.value: In this project, dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) plasma actuators were applied on a highly-swept delta wing to control the leading edge vortices (LEVs). Experimental investigations were conducted in a low-speed wind tunnel at low Reynolds numbers. The DBD actuators could significantly control the breakdown locations of LEVs and affect the moments on the delta wing. A periodic DBD control system was developed. Factors such as the position of DBD actuators, the operational mode and the periodic frequency, were examined to optimize the control performance. Through this project, our knowledge of flow physics over the delta wing was improved and the underlying mechanism of the LEV control via DBD actuators was understood. This investigation also made it is possible to apply the DBD actuator on unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs).

527213.label: Project Title(Chinese)
527213.value: 高樓高效供水管網佈局

527213.label: Project Objectives
527213.value: To develop an optimization approach for water supply network planning and design using probabilistic demand data and assuming non-uniformly distributed consumption in high-rise buildings; To formulate mathematical expressions that predict energy requirements (consumption and efficiency) in water supply networks, by taking water consumption, probable flow rate, storage variability, water loss and distributed friction loss into account; To recommend optimal water supply network designs to meet future building developments in Hong Kong; and To demonstrate a protocol useful for determining the water supply network optimization parameters in any city.
rows: To develop an optimization approach for water supply network planning and design using probabilistic demand data and assuming non-uniformly distributed consumption in high-rise buildings;

To formulate mathematical expressions that predict energy requirements (consumption and efficiency) in water supply networks, by taking water consumption, probable flow rate, storage variability, water loss and distributed friction loss into account;
To recommend optimal water supply network designs to meet future building developments in Hong Kong; and
To demonstrate a protocol useful for determining the water supply network optimization parameters in any city.

527213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
527213.value: Energy conservation through energy efficiency improvement is fundamental to sustainable development globally (United Nation 2009). In Hong Kong, however, design for energy efficient water infrastructure has been ignored and water services energy use has increased by 60% over the past 10 years (HKSAR 2011). The city’s embedded energy consumption for water supply is 1.31 kWh m3 (Cheung, Wong, Mui 2012), of which 40% is in the supply systems in buildings. As friction loss in pipelines, appliances and pumps is 4-5 times the total potential energy of water arriving at user locations in a high-rise building, future sustainable development should focus on piping network design, appliance usage patterns and water storage arrangements so as to reduce the pumping energy needed overall. High-rise housing development, a trend in densely populated cities around the world, increases water supply energy consumption and corresponding greenhouse gas emissions. There are no existing measures for high-rise buildings that systematically address energy efficiency with respect to the optimal design of a building water supply network. The development of a new energy optimization approach appropriate for random, intermittent and transient water demands and the non-uniformly distributed consumption in buildings, urgently requires a new understanding of usage patterns, water demands and occupant loads for various building types in a dense, high-rise urban environment. This proposed project aims to establish optimal designs of energy efficient water supply networks in high-rise urban environments and has two core areas: (1) formulation of mathematical expressions that predict energy requirements in building water supply networks, taking distributed friction loss, water consumption, storage variability, occupant loads, water demands and usage patterns into account; (2) recommendation of sustainable water supply network designs, optimized in terms of energy consumption in respect of various design objectives (such as materials, space) suitable for future building developments in Hong Kong. The findings will enrich our knowledge of what is needed to promote energy efficient designs in water supply networks in a dense high-rise milieu (e.g. energy benchmarking) and enable the development of optimal water supply network designs in high-rise buildings. Practical designs, which are applicable to densely populated cities outside Hong Kong, will also be recommended. 系統能源效率之改善，實乃持續發展城市的基礎，古今中外亦然。然而，高效設計，向非本港水務建設的主要考慮；過去十載，本港供水相關耗能，增加了百分之六十，達每立方米1.31千瓦小時，其中，高樓供水管網，佔約四成，比例持續攀升，而用水的勢能，卻低於百分之十，系統效率甚低，顯而易見。故高樓供水管網佈局，包括管道設計，使用模式，蓄水池的安置，對水泵的需能影響，乃是城市發展不能或缺的重要一環。 城市人口稠密，發展高樓，勢之所趨。供水耗能加增，溫室氣體排放量亦相應提高。就高樓高效供水管網的優化設計，現行並無進行有系統的研究。發展優化高樓高效模型，刻不容緩，其模型參數，相對各類高密環境水用需求的間歇、隨機、短暫和非均勻分佈特性的影響，必須重新估量。 本項目旨在建立高樓高效供水管網佈局，研究核心領域有二：（1）制定數學模型，對系統耗能分佈，進行分析。（2）對供水管網的永續發展，提供建議。研究結果將豐富我們的認知，俾能就中外各類高密環境，提供合適的高效供水管網佈局。

527213.label: Realisation of objectives
527213.value: The project is realized by 6 tasks below. Task 1 Theoretical framework formulation. A water supply network comprises a number of self-explanatory parameters which are grouped into 3 categories: (1) design constraints; (2) physical parameters; and (3) performance measures. Two example water supply networks for buildings, dominated by (a) pipe and fitting friction and (b) elevation. In these examples: the (given design) constraints are water demands, demand locations, pipe friction, pump (& drive) efficiency, appliance exit losses, and constant piping properties e.g. volume/materials; the optimization parameters are pipe radius ratio and height of intermediate tank. Mathematical expressions are formulated using a Monte Carlo model, for designing an optimal piping network that deals with probabilistic demands to minimize energy losses in the network via sizing and arrangement of storage tanks and pipes in buildings. Analytical solutions developed for a simple network are used to validate the Monte Carlo model. Task 2 Development of a dataset for water supply network designs in high-rise buildings Existing data on water supply systems surveyed in Hong Kong by the PI and Co-Is over the past 15 years are compiled and described by parametric parameters. The outcome serves the purpose of identifying the composition of various water supply network arrangements in Hong Kong in terms of water tanks, pumps, water appliances, piping routes, user demand patterns, water and energy consumption, and other physical measures of a water supply system. Some typical water supply networks in buildings are: direct supply systems, gravity supply systems, (pressurized) pneumatic tank supply systems, and intermediate gravity systems. To verify the newly compiled dataset, small-scale surveys on buildings which had not been studied before are evaluated. The parameters are tested for statistical significance. Task 3 Water demand model development A new time series model is developed for the transient water demands in a water supply network of a number of appliances that operate randomly and intermittently with unsteady demands. The appliance operation is dependent on the number of occupants being served, occupant load variation factor and per person hourly demand, which is determined from a time series demand model via Monte Carlo simulations. The model output is compared with the classical demand model output assumed in Task 1. While the demands, which are based on occupant usage patterns and appliance demand profiles, are quantified via Monte Carlo simulation, the volumetric consumption within the duration is resolved using the time series data for simultaneous demands. Alternatively, the volumetric consumption distribution can be determined. The appliance usage pattern is given, where occupant load pattern and demand patterns of individuals are sampled from the corresponding probability density functions for the appliances using Monte Carlo technique. Distribution function of the ‘per capita’ water consumption per demand of the appliance and number of usage are modeled by an occupant load model, given the occupant area ratio and apartment area respectively. Task 4 Measurements of pumping energy Pumping efficiency in 2- water supply systems (11 commercial buildings 4 residential buildings and 3 school buildings and 2 elderly care buildings) are measured against building water demands at the specific building water supply networks. During the investigation pump installations and operation records were accessed including operation and maintenance manual, installation years, cost, ratings, flow rate and pressure, drawings and other documentations. Calculations are made for electricity consumptions of water supply scenarios. Expressions of in-use pump efficiency are worked out. Task 5 Numerical simulations for sizing pipes and arranging storage tanks in supply network designs A numerical algorithm using Monte Carlo method is developed for the network demands determined in Task 1. An appliance operation at each demand end is evaluated, given a random number taken from a pseudo random number set. The algorithm is used to determine the energy loss ratio (i.e. minimum losses) for the network. This ratio and the analytical solutions is compared. The algorithm is then applied to optimize pipe radius ratios and minimize energy losses for various basic water supply networks under unsteady demands. Pressure requirements for the network are determined and compared with existing design approaches. These requirements are essential information in formulating water pumping designs in future investigations. Volumetric cold water consumption data gained is used to validate the demand model developed. As water demands are spatially non-uniform due to the mix of appliance uses and/or occupant load variations in a building, the algorithm is applied to different tank arrangements for various water demand patterns in a building to achieve energy minimization. The integral of the time series model is applied to appliance demands. The numerical algorithm, together with the demand model, is employed to determine the embedded energy use for optimal network designs. The outcome is compared with the dataset obtained. Pipe sizing practices is presented in an easy-to-use way. Task 6 Sensitivity analysis and applications Changes in design practices for pipe sizing and storage tank locations are recommended for high-rise water supply network. Sensitivity of these water supply network design parameters on the embedded energy use as well as the energy efficiency is studied. Impact of various designs on the parameter choices regarding installation/maintenance of the network is considered. Different optimal network sizes for various arrangements including modular designs for buildings/estates are evaluated with examples demonstrated. Optimal water supply network designs are worked out for building types representative of a dense, high-rise urban environment.

527213.label: Major findings and research outcome
527213.value: Design approaches of minimization of energy loss were examined at water supply networks in buildings, covered basic T-shape water supply networks, tanked gravity systems, variable speed pumping systems and intermediate-tanked systems. Mathematical expressions for energy loss optimization were proposed for water supply networks that serves uniform and non-uniform probabilistic demands. Optimized designs based on proper network pipe sizes are analyzed. Optimal pipe radius ratios and their corresponding energy implications in the network are also discussed. An energy efficiency evaluation measure for the water supply system designs was proposed and its potential applications in a typical high-rise water supply systems were demonstrated. The in-use water pump efficiency for the supply networks was accounted. Optimized replacement schedule was proposed. The outcome provides useful benchmark references not only for the water supply system designs but also for the water demand management programmes in buildings in general. Water consumptions and its patterns of variations were examined for selected buildings which had not been studied before. Water consumptions dominating process and appliances were selected for study in details. Implications regarding energy consumption and carbon emissions were discussed with indicating targets of conservations. The data provided grounds for further development of water demand models. All the results were reported in international conferences and published in academic journals as listed in reference section. One PhD student and one MEng student took part from this project training for their dissertation and thesis.

527213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
527213.value: Research fund is applied on the water demand model development. The Bayesian model updating approach that is capable of synthesizing non-uniform water demand estimates made by various existing practices and providing adjustments to those estimates in response to more accurate urban water demand forecasts. By applying the Bayesian techniques, demand estimates can be progressively updated and continuously improved as more and more data becomes available. The research findings will both enrich our knowledge of water demands and advance the development of optimal water supply network designs. Since the work will be conducted in Hong Kong context, the findings on the performance of the Bayesian model approach will apply more directly to a densely located high-rise buildings, but will likely remain relevant to water networks generally.

527213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
527213.value: This project establishes optimal designs of energy efficient water supply networks in high-rise urban environments and has two core areas: (1) formulation of mathematical expressions that predict energy requirements in building water supply networks, taking distributed friction loss, water consumption, storage variability, occupant loads, water demands and usage patterns into account; (2) recommendation of sustainable water supply network designs, optimized in terms of energy consumption in respect of various design objectives suitable for future building developments in Hong Kong. The findings will enrich our knowledge what is needed to promote energy efficiency designs in water supply networks in a dense high-rise milieu (e.g. energy benchmarking) and enable the development of optimal water supply network designs in high-rise buildings. Practical design examples, which are applicable to densely populated cities outside Hong Kong, are recommended.

527413.label: Project Title(Chinese)
527413.value: 無線感應電力傳輸的基礎研究

527413.label: Project Objectives
527413.value: Series or parallel resonant compensation circuit of the IPT transformer primary and secondary are commonly used for the effective transmission of energy between the primary and secondary windings. Therefore four possible fundamental configurations are possible. Each of the four combinations can lead to different circuit topologies. Within these topologies, operation conditions for the best efficiency and voltage or current controllability for a range of load variations will be identified. A search of operation frequency will be carried out for optimal efficiency. A search of operation frequency will also be carried out for either a near ideal voltage source or a near ideal current source for best converter controllability. A merging of the two operation frequencies using compensation technique into a single operation frequency will be carried out for the best of efficiency, controllability and load regulation with or without frequency modulation. The characteristic of each of the operation condition will be identified for subsequent research. These fundamental research results can be the foundation of the application of IPT for the subsequent objectives. The topological operation conditions of the four transformer compensation configurations are identified on the last objective. The objective here is to identify driving circuits of different switch configurations for the energy efficient integration with the compensated transformer. The primary or the secondary of the compensated transformer can be modeled as a two-port network whose input characteristic impedance can be inductive, pure resistive or capacitive. Simple switch configurations such as half-bridge and full-bridge circuit are good for driving inductive load where zero voltage switching can be achieved to improve efficiency due to the loss of switch parasitic capacitance. Class E converter circuit is a good candidate for the driving of pure resistive load without further impedance matching. The downside of using Class E converter is its lack of freedom for modulation control of power without using additional converter. The half-bridge or full-bridge circuit can also be used to drive capacitive compensated transformer by connecting in series with an addition inductor. The identified operation conditions for near ideal current source and ideal voltage source properties of the compensated transformer of objective 1 and converter of objective 2 will be further investigated for bidirectional power flow. Topological aspect of the system in terms of the coupling of primary and secondary circuit with a system of power flow in the sequence of source, modulator, and compensated transformer will be studied.

527413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
527413.value: Inductive power transfer (IPT) is an effective and safe technology to transmit energy through a short distance of free air (or non-magnetic material) without physical contact between the power source and the load. IPT has found applications in home appliances such as wireless charging of electric toothbrush and mobile phone, and induction cooker. Potential applications of the next generation IPT ranges from high power wireless roadway or static charging of electric vehicles, to small power charging of hand-held devices incorporated with near field communications (NFC in latest cell phone) and even transcutaneous charging of lifesaving human implants. No doubt, the addition of IPT to the existing technologies will improve energy saving, environmental protection, medical devices and communication technology in various aspects. Roadway charging of electric vehicles can greatly reduce pollutions due to the distributed burning of fossil fuel within cities. The direct power to the wheel of an electric vehicle can greatly improve power efficiency due to the loss in power cycles of intermediate battery storage. The incorporation of IPT technology can even be integrated and merged with existing power generation technologies, such as the elimination of brush contacts found in most induction generators widely employed in wind energy generation system to improve efficiency and reduce maintenance cost due to constantly wear and tear. A better efficiency transcutaneous power converter can greatly reduce the internal heat up of internal human tissue. Energy can be stored to and retrieved from a shielded system which is nearly impossible without IPT. However, the development of the next generation IPT comes with different challenges. IPT relies on an air-gapped loosely coupled transformer which can be modeled as a transformer with high leakage inductances needing compensation using resonant technologies. There have been much research on the use of either series or parallel resonant of the transformer circuits driven by existing power amplifiers. A fundamental research of these compensations integrated with power converter topology is still missing. The result from this proposed research can greatly enhance the efficiency and controllability of the overall IPT converter system. Specifically, this basic research will study the fundamental aspects using the perspective of power converter circuit topologies to improve the overall system efficiency, output voltage or current controllability and mechanisms for bidirectional power flows. 感應電能傳輸是一項安全、有效的電能傳輸技術。電能通過較短距離的氣隙（或其他非磁性物質），以電磁感應的方式從電源端傳輸至負載端，之間沒有物理接觸。感應電能傳輸已被應用在家用電器的非接觸供電中，例如電動牙刷的無線充電，手機的無線充電平板，或者電磁爐的感應加熱。新一代感應電能傳輸技術亦可以被應用在更多場合，例如高功率的電動汽車無線充電，或者低功率的帶有近場通信功能的手持設備的無線充電，再或者人體植入設備的無線供電。無疑，感應電能傳輸更加節能，環保，對醫療器械和通信技術等很多方面都提供了更加完善的解決方案。道路電動汽車充電能夠大大減少因化石燃料燃燒帶來的空氣污染。由於電能是直接供給行駛中的電動汽車，少了中間電能儲存環節的能量損失，提高了系統整體效率。感應電能傳輸技術，可以與現有的發電技術進行整合。例如，在大多數感應發電機在風力發電系統中廣泛應用的電刷，被非接觸的感應電能所代替，從而提高電能傳輸效率並且減少磨損，降低維護成本。對於人體植入設備而言，高效的感應電能變換器可以大大減少人體組織內部的熱量散髮。電能可以被儲存在人體內部的具有屏蔽系統的裝置內，并隨時取用。沒有了感應電能傳輸的支持，這些很難實現。然而，新一代的電能傳輸技術的發展同樣面臨的諸多挑戰。電能的無線傳輸依賴於大氣隙、低耦合係數的非接觸變壓器，其原副邊绕组具有很大的漏感，需要用諧振技術進行漏感補償。已有大量的研究使用由功率放大器驅動的串聯或者并聯的諧振拓撲，但仍然缺少對補償電路以及系統拓撲的原理性的研究。本文提出的研究成果，可以在很大程度提高感應電能傳輸的效率以及可控性。具體而言，此原理性研究將對電路拓撲分析以提高系統整體效率，對電壓或者電流的傳輸比特性進行研究，從而實現高可靠性工作，以及對雙向功率傳輸的機理進行系統研究。

527413.label: Realisation of objectives
527413.value: Objective 1. above has been almost completely fulfilled. The results are published partially in journal papers [1-4]. Four basic types of series and parallel resonant compensation circuits of the IPT transformer primary and secondary are studied for the effective transmission of energy between the primary and secondary windings. The research results have been summarized in paper [4] in this report. Within these topologies, operation conditions for the best efficiency and voltage or current controllability for a range of load variations have been identified. Operation frequency has been found for optimal efficiency. Operation frequency for either a near ideal voltage source or a near ideal current source for best converter controllability has been identified. A merging of the two operation frequencies using compensation technique into a single operation frequency has been identified with design method for the best of efficiency, controllability and load regulation with or without frequency modulation. The characteristic of each of the operation condition has been identified for subsequent research. These fundamental research results have been the foundation of the application of IPT for the subsequent objectives in journal papers [2-5] and conference paper [1]. Objective 2. above has been almost completely fulfilled. The topological operation conditions of the four transformer compensation configurations have been identified in the last objective. The objective here has been on the identification of driving circuits of different switch configurations for the energy efficient integration with the compensated transformer. The primary or the secondary of the compensated transformer can be modeled as a two-port network whose input characteristic impedance can be inductive, pure resistive or capacitive. Simple switch configurations such as half-bridge and full-bridge circuit have been proved to be good for driving inductive load where zero voltage switching can be achieved to improve efficiency due to the loss of switch parasitic capacitance. Class E converter circuit is a good candidate for the driving of pure resistive load without further impedance matching. However, our research found that it suffers from poor efficiency due to difficulty of precise tuning its resonant circuit with that from the converter compensation circuit. Its downside of lack of freedom for modulation control of power without using additional converter is also difficult to solve. The half-bridge or full-bridge circuit can also be used to drive capacitive compensated transformer by connecting in series with an addition inductor. The research results have been partially published in journal papers [2-5] and conference paper [1]. Objective 3. above has been fulfilled conceptually. The identified operation conditions for near ideal current source and ideal voltage source properties of the compensated transformer of objective 1 and converter of objective 2 have been further investigated for bidirectional power flow. Topological aspect of the system in terms of the coupling of primary and secondary circuit with a system of power flow in the sequence of source, modulator, and compensated transformer will be studied. High impact results not directly contribute to bidirectional application have been published in journals [2-5] and conference [1]. We have concluded that bidirectional operations of inductive power transfer for maximal efficiency should also consider the loading conditions of both sides that a reasonable solution to this problem cannot be completed with solely the achievements of objectives 1 and 2 above. We need some other research to complete the optimal bidirectional converter design.

528113.label: Project Title(Chinese)
528113.value: 动态RFID系统的新技术研究

528113.label: Project Objectives
528113.value: When tag population is changing, it contains three sets of tags, i.e. missing tags, remaining tags and new tags (or misplaced) in the next time slot. Keeping track of distinct sets and their sizes are valuable to design optimal ID collection protocol. Thus, the first objective is to propose efficient algorithms to estimate the cardinality of each set. Our second objective is to design efficient ID collection protocols to identify tags in each set. Once we know the missing and new tag IDs, the remaining tag IDs can be derived from the ID database. RFID system management becomes efficient without initiating the long procedure of ID collection, especially when remaining tags are the majority. Cloning attacks and blocking attacks show two opposite ways to mislead the RFID system information collection. They are not tolerable when RFID technology is used in access control or critical item surveillance, e.g., armed weapons. Our third objective is to propose new approaches to accurately detecting such attacks and identifying which tags are cloned, which range of tags are blocked. The fourth objective is to carry out simulations and real experiments to compare the proposed solutions with previous methods to validate solution feasibility and efficiency in large-scale RFID systems.

528113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
528113.value: 无线射频技术（RFID）不仅仅可以提高工业的效率，如仓储管理和目录清单管理，也能深刻影响我们的日常生活。RFID技术已经被成功应用于大范围的日常生活中，如香港的八达通卡，图书馆里的书中植入的RFID标签，美国的超过3750个沃尔玛中的标签好的商品。在香港，每一个人都用八达通RFID卡，很方便的乘坐交通工具，超市购物及进入私人住宅。 项目的目标是对RFID研究领域内的基本问题提出高效又安全的解决方案。我们重点考虑的是动态的RFID系统。面对的挑战包括动态的标签和移动的标签阅读器。要解决的基本问题包括标签数量的估计和标签的收集。不同于以前的工作，本项目将集中研究动态标签对系统性能的影响，如丢失的标签和新加入的标签。另一个要考虑的是如何使用移动阅读器来管理RFID系统，比如检测误置的标签。另外，项目将针对恶意的环境，设计安全通信的RFID协议。 为实现这些目标，项目将对动态RFID系统提出新的技术。我们将用差异性的估算方法来估计标签数量的改变，设计碰撞的和空置的对应的时间片及多哈希的时间片选择技术来降低时间片的冲突，使用矢量标志技术提高协议的时间效率，及提供匿名的方式检测恶意攻击。项目提出的新的方法能够极大的提高RFID系统性能，并满足未来RFID系统设计的要求。

528113.label: Realisation of objectives
528113.value: We have fully achieved the above listed four objectives in this project. 1. The first objective is to propose efficient algorithms to estimate the number of tags in a group (or a set). We have achieved this goal by designing new algorithms for the group information collection. Our first step is to analyze the grouping problem in the RFID system, which relates to the group tag size estimation and group ID identification. Unlike previous research on the unicast transmission from a reader to a tag, grouping provides a fundamental mechanism for efficient multicast transmissions and aggregate queries in large RFID enabled applications. We study fast grouping protocols in large RFID systems. This is a new approach because it is the first attempt to tackle this practically important yet uninvestigated problem. We proposed three protocols, starting with a straightforward solution called the Enhanced Polling Grouping (EPG) protocol. We then propose a time-efficient FIltering Grouping (FIG) protocol that uses Bloom filters to remove the costly ID transmissions. We point out the limitation of the Bloom-filter based solution due to its intrinsic false positive problem, which leads to our final ConCurrent Grouping (CCG) protocol. Two top conference papers are published to show the research result.  J. Liu, B. Xiao, S. Chen, F. Zhu and L. Chen, "Fast RFID Grouping Protocols", in Proc. of the IEEE INFOCOM 2015, Hong Kong, China, April 2015, pp. 1948-1956.  J. Liu, S. Chen, B. Xiao, Y. Wang, and L. Chen, "Category Information Collection in RFID Systems", in Proc. of the IEEE International Conference on Distributed Computing Systems (ICDCS-2017), Atlanta GA, USA, 5-8 June 2017, pp. 2220-2225. Our second step is to conduct the tag searching, which aims to determine which of a particular set of tags are currently present in the system and which are not. We design a novel technique called testing slot, with which a reader can quickly figure out which wanted tags are absent from its interrogation region without tag ID transmissions. Based on this technique, we propose two protocols to perform time-efficient tag searching in practical large RFID systems containing multiple readers. In our protocols, each reader first employs the testing slot technique to obtain its local searching result by iteratively eliminating wanted tags that are absent from its interrogation region. This work is published in a top journal paper.  X. Liu, Bin Xiao, S. Zhang, K. Bu and A. Chan, "STEP: A Time-Efficient Tag Searching Protocol in Large RFID Systems", accepted in IEEE Transactions on Computers (TC), Vol. 64, No. 11, Nov. 2015, pp. 3265-3277. 2. To the second objectives of the project, we designed an efficient distributed query processing scheme in large RFID-enable supply chain systems to manage tag IDs and related queries. We design an efficient distributed storage model by leveraging Bloom filters to save storage space and improve query efficiency. Meanwhile, we establish corresponding query processing schemes to locally support existence queries and path queries, which are two kinds of most popular queries in the supply chain management. A local query can be completed with constant time complexity regardless of data volume. One top conference paper is published to show the research result.  J. Liu, B. Xiao, K. Bu and L. Chen, "Efficient Distributed Query Processing in Large RFID-enabled Supply Chains", in Proc. of the IEEE INFOCOM 2014, Toronto Canada, April 2014, pp. 163-171. To identify tags efficiently, we design different protocols, e.g., with handheld readers (TMC2016), unknown tag identification (TPDS2015), and fast polling in a tree structure (ICPP2016). The protocols are described in top venues, as follows:  X. Liu, B. Xiao, S. Zhang and K. Cloning attacks and blocking attacks show two opposite ways to mislead the RFID system information collection. They are not tolerable when RFID technology is used in access control or critical item surveillance, e.g., armed weapons. Our third objective is to propose new approaches to accurately detecting such attacks and identifying which tags are cloned, which range of tags are blocked.

The fourth objective is to carry out simulations and real experiments to compare the proposed solutions with previous methods to validate solution feasibility and efficiency in large-scale RFID systems.

528113.label: Major findings and research outcome
528113.value: The findings from the project include efficient tag identification protocols, efficient tag information collection protocols, and efficient query processing protocols in large-scale RFID systems. The efficient tag identification protocols are able to poll tags very fast. Polling is a widely used anti-collision protocol that interrogates RFID tags in a request-response way. In conventional polling, the reader needs to broadcast 96-bit tag IDs to separate each tag from others, leading to long interrogation delay. This project takes the first step to design fast polling protocols by shortening the polling vector. Our tag identification protocols can also first verifies whether or not a responding tag has already been identified and retrieves its ID when the answer is yes, and collects the tag’s ID only when it is unidentified. Furthermore, we propose a series of protocols that can identify all of the unknown tags with high time efficiency. The efficient tag information collection protocols can collect category-related information (e.g., the brands of clothes) when a tag is put into use and associated with a specific object. We also design two protocols to perform time-efficient tag searching in practical large RFID systems containing multiple readers. In addition, we solved the RFID tag grouping problem by efficiently grouping all tags according to a given partition such that tags in the same group will have the same group ID. This project has fruitful research outcome. The research outcomes of the project have been shown in top journal and top conference papers. Top journal papers include IEEE TMC2016 (tag identification in the mobile computing), IEEE TC2015 (RFID tag searching), IEEE TPDS2015 (unknown tag identification). Top conference papers include IEEE ICDCS2017 (an efficient product category information collection when products have RFID tags), IEEE ICPP2016 (fast RFID polling to identify tags), IEEE INFOCOM2015 (fast RFID grouping) and IEEE INFOCOM2014 (distributed query processing in RFID systems). With the support of this project, one Ph.D. student, Mr. Shang Gao, has been enrolled who will graduate in 2018.

528113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
528113.value: The proposed protocols, algorithms for RFID system management has the potential to be applied in real RFID applications. The real RFID systems normally adopt the C1G2 standard. Thus, the proposed methods should be adjusted to meet the standard requirement. This could be the further development of the research results. While the methods are adjusted, how to maintain their performance efficiency will be challenging. Some proposed method, such as the distributed query processing in paper INFOCOM2014, needs no changes and can be applied to off-the-shelf RFID products directly. More research can be carried out for performance improvement and meeting current industry standards.

528113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
528113.value: Today’s RFID system has many applications with fast batch processing ability, long wireless communication range to provide no-contact and non line-of-sight operations, on-chip memory to support data write-back and secured communications. The project investigates new efficient and secure solutions in large-scale dynamic RFID systems. It advances the RFID research from a static view of RFID systems to a dynamic view, which is closer to real applications. The project outcome includes a set of new algorithms to identify tag IDs in a RFID system, new protocols to efficiently collect tag information, new mechanisms to detect and identify attacks, e.g. cloning attacks, and distributed query processing in the supply chain industry. The proposed solutions optimize system performance to achieve time-efficiency, energy-efficiency and accuracy, or get balanced results. The novel research conducted in the project can provide new insights into the development of dynamic RFID systems and has significant practical impact for the wide applicability of RFID technologies in industries and customer markets. The project research results are published in top journal/conference papers, including ICDCS2017, ICPP2016, TMC 2016, TC2015, INFOCOM 2015, TPDS2015 and INFOCOM2014.

528513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
528513.value: Long-span cable-supported bridges with twin-box girders have been constructed in recent years to enhance the stability of the bridges against flutter. Nevertheless, some of these bridges also suffer large-amplitude vortex-induced vibration (VIV) at lock-in, in which the shedding frequency of vortices from the bridge deck surface is very close to the vertical bending or pitching frequency of the bridge. Large-amplitude VIV can produce fatigue damage accumulation in structural components and reduce safety and comfort levels of road vehicles, railway cars, and pedestrians. Therefore, in the design of long-span cable-supported bridges with twin-box girders, it is essential to understand the mechanism of VIV and to predict a structure’s response to vortex shedding. VIV is a strongly nonlinear dynamic problem that appears in many engineering fields. The problem of VIV becomes more complicated in long-span bridges because it often occurs at low wind speeds, whose vortex-induced force on a small deck model is difficult to measure in a wind tunnel. Therefore, testing often requires a large-scale deck model. In the past, several semi-empirical models have been proposed for estimating vortex-induced force and vibration on long-span bridges with single-box girders, but there are few studies on VIV in long-span cable-supported bridges with twin-box girders. This research deficiency hinders the development of super-long-span cable-supported bridges to cross straits around the world. This project will first develop a wind-tunnel test technique to accurately measure vortex-induced force on twin-box girder models. The existing semi-empirical models for identifying vortex-induce force and predicting VIV will then be examined, and a new model will be advanced for twin-box girder bridges, based on the quality wind-tunnel test data. The wind-tunnel test data will also be used to investigate irregularities in the span-wise correlation of vortex-induced force. Then the developed models for vortex-induced force and its span-wise correlation will be applied in a framework for predicting the levels of VIV in full-scale bridges with twin-box girders. Finally, the framework will be validated for its feasibility and accuracy through a case study in which the field measurement VIV data from a long-span suspension bridge will be recorded using a structural health monitoring system. The findings from this project will improve our understanding of the mechanism of VIV and facilitate the prevention or mitigation of VIV through better testing, modeling and prediction in the early stages of design for long-span cable-supported bridges with twin-box girders. 近年來，分離雙箱主梁斷面因爲其優越的顫振穩定性越來越多地運用于大跨度纜索承重橋梁中。然而，當氣流流經橋梁斷面産生的旋渦脫落頻率接近于結構的竪向固有頻率或扭轉固有頻率時，此類橋梁有可能發生顯著的渦激共振。大振幅的渦激共振不僅會引起結構構件的疲勞損傷累積，危害結構的安全性，幷且還可能會影響橋面車輛和行人的舒適性。因此，在大跨度纜索承重分離雙箱橋梁設計中，理解此類斷面的渦激共振機理幷由此預測結構的渦振響應就顯得尤爲重要。 渦激共振是存在于許多工程科學領域的一個强非綫性問題。尤其是對于大跨度橋梁，研究渦激共振問題更加複雜。這表現在，對于大跨度橋梁來講，渦激共振往往發生于較低風速，此時，作用在常規比例主梁節段模型上的渦激力量值一般都非常小，這給準確測量渦激力帶來了很大困難，因此需要在較大尺度的模型上開展測力試驗。在過去的研究中，已經有一些學者針對非分離整體式主梁斷面開展研究，建立了一些預測該類斷面渦激力及渦激共振的半經驗-半理論模型，但是很少見報道給出針對分離雙箱斷面大跨度纜索承重橋梁渦激力和渦激共振的模型。目前關于分離雙箱斷面渦激力及渦激共振的研究現狀明顯阻礙了現今跨越海峽的超大跨徑纜索承重橋梁的發展。 綜上所述，本項目將首先開發一套針對分離雙箱斷面節段模型渦激力的精確測量技術，幷檢驗已經存在的渦激力模型用于描述分離雙箱斷面渦激力和預測渦激共振響應的可靠性，如有必要，將基于上述實驗得到的可靠渦激力建立新的渦激力模型；其次，利用試驗數據進行相關性分析，研究渦激力沿主梁跨向的不完全相關特性；再次，將得到的渦激力模型及其跨向相關性模型應用于橋梁結構原型的渦激共振分析中，建立分離雙箱斷面橋梁的渦振分析理論框架；最後，利用橋梁健康監測系統采集的渦振現場實測數據，可以驗證該渦振分析框架的可靠性。預計本項目得到的研究成果有益于理解渦激共振的作用機理，在大跨度纜索承重分離雙箱橋梁的前期設計中，利用上述精細化的試驗，建模以及預測方法，有益于預防或控制該類大跨度橋梁的渦激共振。

528513.label: Realisation of objectives
528513.value: Objective 1. To advance wind-tunnel techniques for the simultaneous measurement of vortex-induced forces with span-wise correlations and vortex-induced responses in one twin-box girder bridge model. A new wind-tunnel test technique was developed for the simultaneous measurement of vortex-induced forces (VIFs) with span-wise correlations and vortex-induced responses of an elastically-mounted section model of the Xihoumen Bridge, which is the world’s second longest suspension bridge with a twin-box deck and was found to suffer VIV at low wind speeds. The section model of the twin-box deck of the Xihoumen Bridge was fabricated with a scale ratio of 1:20. The model is 3.6 m in length, 1.6 m in width and 0.175 m in depth. An inner rigid frame with two longitudinal beams and four cross beams made of aluminum was used to provide sufficient stiffness to the model so that the model could move as a rigid body during the tests. To enable simultaneous force measurements at several span-wise locations of both boxes, 7 pairs of force-measuring strips were embedded in the twin-box section model. Each strip was made of light polymeric foam and some auxiliary parts that allowed the polymeric foam to be connected to the inner rigid frame through a force balance. Apart from the 7 pairs of force-measuring strips, wooden plate skins were used to cover the rest of the model surface to form the completed twin-box section model. Mini 3-component dynamic force balances were developed. These force balances have an operating rage of ±15 kg and an accuracy of 0.1%. Totally 14 force balances were installed in the model to capture wind forces on the 7 pairs of the 14 strips. Force balances were installed to directly connect the force measurement strips to the inner rigid frame. Simultaneous force measurements at several span-wise locations were enabled with this test technique. The entire section model was attached to a rigid suspending arm at each end and then suspended between the faring walls by springs. One laser displacement gauge and one accelerometer were installed on each end of the two suspending arms to record the displacement and acceleration responses of the model. During the tests, the force, displacement and acceleration were measured simultaneously. With simultaneously recorded force and acceleration responses during the tests of free-decay vibration with an initial displacement at zero wind speed, non-wind-induced forces were extracted from the total force time-histories by subtracting the inertia forces of the foam strips. The non-wind-induced damping and mass coefficients were then identified. The VIFs on the foam strips were finally extracted from the total recorded forces by subtracting the non-wind-induced forces and inertial forces on the strips. More details can be found in Zhu et al. (2017a and 2017b) Objective 2. To examine the existing semi-empirical models and, if necessary, to develop a refined or new nonlinear model for vortex-induced forces on twin-box girder bridges, together with a parameter identification method. A direct investigation on the VIFs of the elastically-mounted section model of the Xihoumen Bridge was conducted with the new wind tunnel test technique. The characteristics and span-wise correlation of VIFs on the twin-box deck under both smooth and turbulent flow fields were examined. A refined SDOF model for VIF under smooth wind flow was first proposed. The proposed SDOF VIF model included all the non-conservative motion-induced force terms. An approximate analytical solution for the maximum amplitude of VIR was then deduced based on the proposed VIF model. Furthermore, based on quasi-static assumption, the proposed VIF model was further extended to take account of turbulence wind effects by introducing a turbulence-induced positive damping term into the model. Finally, the validity of the proposed VIF model with and without turbulent wind effects was examined using the new wind tunnel test technique. The comparative results show that the proposed VIF model can effectively predict the maximum VIR of the twin-box deck under different turbulent fields with different structural damping ratios. Further details can be found in Zhu et al. (2017b). The new wind tunnel test technique enables the simultaneous measurement of VIFs on different span-wise locations and the investigation on the span-wise correlation of VIFs on the twin-box deck. The spacing of the force measurement strips allowed the investigation on VIF correlation with span-wise distances of 0.4D, 1D, 2D, 3D, 4D, 5D, 6D, 7D, 8D, 10D and 13D, where D is the depth of the model. Tests under both smooth flow and turbulent flow were conducted. The turbulent flow fields were generated by grids consisting of vertical and horizontal aluminum alloy strips. The width of the strips and the spacing between the strips were adjusted to generate turbulent flow fields with different intensity. Under smooth wind flow, the average turbulence intensity (T.I.) between the two fairing walls is about 2%. Three turbulent wind flow fields were used in this study, with T.I. of 4.5%, 7.6% and 8.0%, respectively. The maximum VIV response occurred around a wind speed of 5.25 m/s in the wind tunnel. The Reynolds number of the tests was around 5.0×104. To investigate the effects of different damping ratios on the span-wise correlation of VIF, silicon oil dampers were used to add damping on the oscillating system. The original section model system possessed a damping ratio of 0.35%. The damping ratio was increased to 0.8% with the additional damping facilities. After the VIFs were extracted from the measured force time histories, the span-wise correlation ratios, which are traditionally adopted to represent the span-wise correlation of the VIFs, were calculated. The span-wise root coherence values of the fundamental-frequency component of VIF were also computed. More details can be found in Zhu et al. (2017a). Objective 3. To refine the analytical framework for the vortex-induced response analysis of long-span cable-supported bridges with twin-box girders. A mode-by-mode VIV analysis method was developed for long-span bridges with twin-box decks under non-uniformly distributed turbulent winds. The semi-empirical model of vortex-induced forces (VIF), developed in this project and validated by direct force measurements on the elastically-mounted twin-box section model under turbulent winds, and the new span-wise correlation results were embedded in the VIV analysis method. The finite element model of the Xihoumen Bridge with twin-box deck was established. The proposed analysis method was applied to analyze the VIV of the Xihoumen Bridge. The computed VIR of the prototype-bridge was finally compared with the VIR measured on-site by a structural heath monitoring system installed in the bridge. More details can be found in Zhu et al. (2018)

528513.label: Major findings and research outcome
528513.value: (1) A new wind tunnel test technique is developed, which can simultaneously measure the VIV responses and VIFs at a set of span-wise locations on an elastically-mounted twin-box section model. (2) The fundamental-frequency VIF, which is commonly seen as the negative linear aerodynamic damping force, is the main driving force of the VIV. The triple-frequency VIF, which is usually seen as the nonlinear aerodynamic damping force, also plays an important role in VIV, but it mainly takes effect when the vibration amplitude is quite large. (3) The span-wise root coherence values of VIF are close to 1.0 at fundamental-, double-, triple- and quadruple- frequencies with maximum amplitude under smooth wind flow. (4) Within the lock-in range, the fundamental-frequency component of VIF can be viewed as perfectly correlated even with a T.I. of 8%. Outside the lock-in range, the root coherence values decay rapidly with the increase of distance. (5) A new model for VIF on bridge decks under smooth wind flow is proposed, which includes all the non-conservative motion-induced terms. An approximate analytical solution for the maximum amplitude of VIR is also deduced. (6)Based on quasi-static assumption, the proposed VIF model is further developed to take into account the turbulence effects by introducing a turbulence-induced positive damping term into the model. (7) The validity of the proposed VIF model is examined. The results show that the proposed VIF model can effectively predict the maximum VIR of a bridge deck under different turbulent fields. (8) The comparative results with the field measurements show that the proposed mode-by-mode VIV analysis method can be used to predict the VIR of long-span bridges with a twin-box deck. (9) Turbulence reduces the VIV, and the reduction effect is larger on the VIV responses with low-order modes than those with high-order modes. This suggests that turbulence may easily suppress VIV on low-frequency modes. (10) The non-uniform distribution of mean wind speed reduces the VIV responses. For long-span bridges, neglecting the non-uniform distribution of wind speed may overestimate the VIV responses. However, the effects of the non-uniform distribution of turbulence are negligible. A total of four peer-reviewed papers have been published in the top international journals. Additionally, one invited lecture and two conference papers have been presented at international conferences. The research collaboration has been established between the Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Tongji University and Harbin Institute of Technology, China.

528513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
528513.value: The new wind tunnel test technique for the simultaneous measurement of vortex-induced forces (VIFs) with span-wise correlations and vortex-induced responses of elastically-mounted section models of long-span bridges can be refined to further enhance the measurement accuracy of VIFs. More wind tunnel tests of elastically-mounted sectional deck models of various configurations and more field measurements of long-span bridges are needed to further validate or improve the proposed VIF model and the proposed mode-by-mode VIV analysis method respectively.

528513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
528513.value: Long-span cable-supported bridges with twin-box decks have been constructed in recent years to enhance the stability of the bridges, but some of these bridges suffer large-amplitude vortex-induced vibration (VIV). Large-amplitude VIV can cause fatigue damage in structural components and reduce safety and comfort levels of road vehicles, trains, and pedestrians. Therefore, in the design of long-span bridges with twin-box decks, it is essential to know vortex-induced forces (VIF) and predict vortex-induced responses (VIR). In this context, a new wind tunnel test technique was developed to directly measure VIFs at different span-wise locations of a twin-box deck model. The characteristics and span-wise correlation of the VIFs on the twin-box deck under both smooth and turbulent flow fields were investigated. A refined semi-empirical model was also developed for VIF on a twin-box deck with and without turbulent wind flow, and an approximate analytical solution for the maximum amplitude of VIR was also deduced. Finally, a mode-by-mode VIV analysis method for long-span bridges with a twin-box deck under non-uniformly distributed turbulent winds was developed. The project has been successfully completed. The findings and experiences obtained from this exercise can shed light on the design of super long-span cable-supported bridges against VIV.

528813.label: Project Objectives
528813.value: Objectives The objective of this research project is to critically review the current design models recommended for evaluating the local web buckling strength of double-coped beams. The current reinforcement details practice intended to strengthen the web of a double-coped beam will also be examined. Both experimental and analytical investigations will be made in the research study. The experimental data will serve to augment the relatively small database of test results currently available in this area. More firmly grounded design recommendations will be developed for reinforcing double-coped beams. The objectives of this research project will be accomplished by completing the following tasks: Task I Experimental investigation Full-scale beam tests will be conducted to examine the local web buckling strength and behaviour of double-coped beams with and without reinforcement. The tests will include a number of parameters such as the cope geometry (dc/D and c/D) and the effects of different types of stiffener (longitudinal and doubler plate). Tension coupon tests will be conducted to establish the stress-strain behaviour of the materials used for both the coped beam specimens and the stiffeners. Task II Numerical investigation Finite element models will be developed to simulate the structural behaviour of the test specimens. To validate the finite element model, the test results obtained from this proposed research study and from the PI’s previous preliminary study will be compared to those of the finite element analysis. The validated models will then be used to conduct a parametric study of the strength and behaviour of double-coped beams with and without reinforcement. The results of the nonlinear finite element analysis will provide further insight into the behaviour of the test specimens and will provide the data required for the development of design recommendations. Task III Examination of the current design practices and the development of a design recommendation The current design practices for double-coped beams (Steel Construction Manual (AISC) and Joints in Simple Construction: Simple Connections (SCI and BCSA)) for the design of local web buckling strength of double-coped beams and the reinforcement recommendations are based on the work of [2]. These practices will be critically reviewed based on the results of the proposed research project, and if necessary further improvement and refinement of the design practices will be proposed.

528813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
528813.value: In steel structures, the same elevation is often required for both the flanges of the secondary beams and the flanges of the main girders to satisfy architectural purposes at member intersections. For this case, the secondary beams are usually coped at one or both flanges, to avoid interference between the connected structural members, so that sufficient clearance can be provided for the connections. Because of the copes, however, the load capacities of coped beams can be substantially decreased due to the reduction of the beam depth and the removal of the beam flange(s). The local web buckling capacity of coped beams has been investigated both analytically and experimentally by a number of researchers. Their research, however, only focused on single-coped beams (either top flange or bottom flange coped). For double-coped beams (both flanges coped), only analytical study of the local web buckling strength of the beams has been conducted and no experimental evidence is available to substantiate the analytical results. It should be noted that these analytical results form the basis of the current design recommendations for evaluating the local web buckling strength of double-coped beams. In addition, experimental evidence is also lacking in proving the effectiveness of the current recommended reinforcement details for strengthening double-coped beams. The PI has conducted research (both experimental and numerical studies) on single-coped beams (with and without reinforcements). Several preliminary tests on the local web buckling strength of double-coped beams have also been conducted by the PI. The preliminary test results show that the current design recommendation is overly-conservative. Since these tests were exploratory, further work, both experimental and analytical, is required for examining the strength and behaviour of double-coped beams with and without reinforcement. The aim of this study, therefore, is to investigate experimentally and analytically the strength and behaviour of double-coped beams and to critically review current design practices for evaluating the local web buckling strength of double-coped beams. In addition, reinforcement details for double-coped beams will also be investigated. If necessary, new types of reinforcement details for double-coped beams will be developed. 對於鋼結構來說，為了滿足建築要求與結構需要，主樑與次梁的上翼緣高度通常需要保持在同一水平面上。為了避免在主次梁交接處的衝突，通常需要在主樑與次梁的節點處對次梁的部分翼緣和腹板進行‘切口’，以便為節點設計提供足夠的空間。然而由於切口的存在，切口梁在節點處的局部強度將不可避免的受到很大的影響，其中切口範圍內腹板的局部屈曲是最常見的結構破壞模式之一。雖然對於這種破壞形式的相關實驗和分析研究已經展開，但這些研究主要針對單邊切口梁，即只對一側（通常是上翼緣）的部分翼緣和腹板進行切口。對於雙邊切口梁，目前只有很有限的數值分析研究，且尚缺乏實驗的驗證。雖然一些規範提出了雙邊切口梁的初步設計建議，但這些設計方法是基於有限的數值模擬的結果而提出的經驗設計法。另外，一些規範還提出了雙邊切口梁的加固措施，但目前同樣沒有實驗來證明這些加固方法的有效性。 申請人之前對單邊切口梁進行了詳細的實驗與數值分析，並且對其加固措施進行了系統的研究。對於雙邊切口梁，申請人目前也開始了一些初步的實驗研究。初步實驗結果表明，目前雙邊切口梁的設計建議過於保守。為了更加系統的判斷與預估雙邊切口梁（未加固或加固的）的強度與失效行為，則需要更進一步的實驗與分析。因此，此項研究的主要目的是通過實驗與理論分析來評估和更新已有的雙邊切口梁腹板局部屈曲的設計方法。同時，也將對加固後的雙邊切口梁進行實驗研究，並提出有效的加固細則。

528813.label: Realisation of objectives
528813.value: In general, all the objectives of the study have been achieved. There were two experimental programmes designed to investigate the local web buckling strength and behaviour of double-coped beams with or without reinforcements. Numerical studies were also conducted to provide further insights into the structural behaviour of double-coped beams. Design recommendations for the local web buckling strength of double-coped beams were proposed. Reinforcement details for double-coped beams were also recommended. Double-coped beams without reinforcement In total, 11 full-scale double-coped beam specimens without reinforcement were conducted, covering a spectrum of cope lengths and cope depths. Local web buckling was observed as the main failure mode for most specimens. The ultimate load was found to decrease with increasing coped length and cope depth, and in addition, an increase of the rotational stiffness of the beam end connection could benefit the local web buckling capacity. In order to evaluate the applicability of the existing design method for predicting the local web buckling strength of double-coped beams, the ultimate loads of the double-coped beam specimens from the available test data, including the current test results and those previously reported by other researchers, were compared to those predicted by the existing design method. Conservative test-to-predicted ratios were generally shown, but unsafe predictions were obtained for some cases. The finite element (FE) method was used to analyse the double-coped beam specimens without stiffeners and the validated FE models were subsequently used to conduct a parametric study to further investigate the structural behaviour and strength of double-coped beams without reinforcements. The parametric study covered a spectrum of geometric and material variables including cope length, cope depth, web slenderness, and steel grade. For the double-coped beams without reinforcement, the study revealed that the main failure mode of the models was either inelastic or elastic local web buckling, and the considered parameters could evidently influence the buckling capacity. The models with short copes tended to fail by inelastic buckling accompanied by excessive shear yielding. For the models with long copes, especially for those with thin webs and high steel grades, stable post-buckling equilibrium path could be sustained after the occurrence of initial buckling. As a result, the ultimate reaction could be evidently higher than that governed by elastic buckling. In addition, stress concentration was significant near the cope corners, and the peak elastic stress concentration factor (SCF) could achieve around 2.0. Based on the numerical results, and recognising the potential limitations of the existing design method, a modified design method, taking account of the various influential factors revealed in this study, was proposed. The available experimental and numerical results showed that the modified method can effectively improve the accuracy of local web buckling design for double-coped beam connections without reinforcement. Double-coped beams with reinforcement For the study of the strength and behaviour of reinforced double-coped beams, eight full-scale tests were conducted covering a set of reinforcement types [ a) longitudinal web stiffener, b) full-depth doubler plate, and c) partial-depth doubler plate] and varying coping dimensions. Six of the specimens were reinforced by stiffeners and the remaining two specimens were without reinforcement for comparison purpose. Local web buckling was found to be the governing failure mode for the unreinforced specimens, and the presence of the considered stiffeners could effectively increase the load resistance. In particular, a pair of longitudinal stiffeners for the top cope edge was shown to completely mitigate the risk of local web buckling, and the final failure mode was tensile cracking at the bottom cope corner. When the specimens were reinforced by a full-depth or partial depth doubler plate, the occurrence of local web buckling was effectively postponed, although local web buckling was still the major failure mode governing the ultimate load. Generally speaking, from the loading capacity point of view, employing doubler plate seemed to be less effective than adding a pair of longitudinal stiffeners. The test results showed that the plastic moment capacity of the coped sections reinforced by longitudinal web stiffeners could be well mobilised. For the cases of the full-depth doubler plate, the yield moment capacity of the reinforced coped sections was not fully achieved prior to the occurrence of local web buckling. A comprehensive numerical study on the strength and behaviour of reinforced double-coped beams, with the focus on reinforcing strategies against local web buckling was conducted using the finite element method. Four reinforcement types, namely, longitudinal web stiffener (Type A), combined longitudinal and vertical web stiffeners (Type B), vertical and double longitudinal web stiffeners (Type C), and full-depth doubler plate (Type D), were considered. Through examining a suite of validated numerical models with a spectrum of cope details, it was found that the considered reinforcement types were in general effective, especially for the models with long or deep copes. Depending on the cope details and stiffener type, a series of failure modes, including local web buckling, web shear yielding, web shear buckling, tensile fracture of the bottom cope corner, and web crippling, were identified, and the effectiveness of the different reinforcement types on preventing or postponing these failure modes was discussed. A preliminary design rule for checking the capacity of the reinforced coped section was proposed, and additional analysis was performed to further evaluate the influences of varying reinforcement dimensions and lateral bracing conditions on the ultimate capacity of the double-coped beams. Based on the numerical analysis, a set of prescriptive recommendations on reinforcement details was proposed, offering a simple yet safe guidance for new design or upgrade of double-coped beam members.
