528813.label: Major findings and research outcome
528813.value: Nineteen full-scale double-coped beam tests were conducted including thirteen specimens without web reinforcement and 6 with web reinforcements. The test results showed that for the specimens without reinforcement, the primarily failure mode was local web buckling featured by clear buckling line being developed over the coped web. The cope length-to-beam depth and cope depth-to-beam depth ratios were the two important variations that affected the ultimate resistance of the specimens. The beneficial influence of increased rotational stiffness of the end-plate connection was also exhibited. For the test specimens with web reinforcement, the test ultimate load was greatly affected by the reinforcement type and coping dimensions. The presence of the three considered stiffener types was shown to effectively increase the load resistance. In particular, no local web buckling was developed when longitudinal web stiffeners were used, and the final failure mode was tensile cracking at the bottom cope corner. When the specimens were reinforced by a full-depth or partial depth doubler plate, the occurrence of local web buckling was effectively postponed. Finite element analysis was conducted to further investigate the structural behaviour of double-coped beams. For double-coped beams without stiffeners, the main failure mode of the models was local web buckling. For the models with long copes, stable post-buckling equilibrium path could be sustained after the occurrence of local web buckling. It was observed that the increase of connection rotational stiffness was beneficial for local web buckling capacity. A modified design method was proposed for better predictions of local web buckling capacity for double-coped beam connections. For the reinforced double-coped beams, four reinforcement types were considered in the numerical study. It was found that web crippling and tensile fracture of the bottom cope corner were the two typical failure modes for the models with longitudinal web stiffeners. Web crippling could be fully prevented by using combined longitudinal and vertical web stiffeners, and tensile fracture could be effectively postponed using vertical and double longitudinal web stiffeners. Web crippling was a common failure mode for the models with doubler plate. A set of design recommendations on the reinforcement details for double-coped beams was proposed. The research findings have resulted in 4 journal papers. Two of them were published in “Engineering Structures” (Section C, paper 2 and 4) and the other two were published in the “Journal of Constructional Steel Research” (Section C, paper 1 and 3). One conference paper was published.

528813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
528813.value: This study examined experimentally and numerically the strength and behaviour of double-coped beams with or without reinforcements. In general, the test programme employed to examine the local web buckling strength of double-coped beams was comprehensive and provided sufficient experimental evidence. However, it would be beneficial to conduct additional tests on double-coped beams considering the effect of connection rotational restraint and on reinforced double-coped beams with other reinforcement details such as the extension of the length of longitudinal stiffeners beyond the cope end. The recommended reinforcement details for reinforced double-coped beams are based on the results of the parametric study of a beam section with a slender web (with the maximum d/tw ratio among the available universal beams), a relatively small span-to-depth ratio (L/D = 10), and a limited range of cope details. Although the recommended reinforcement details may be safely applicable to other universal beams, it would be beneficial to expand the parametric study to consider other beam sections and cope details to verify further the proposed reinforcement strategies.

528813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
528813.value: In typical steel building frames, the same elevation of beam/girder flanges at member intersections is often required to facilitate the fabrication of flooring, decking, and ceiling systems. In this case, part of the flange of secondary beams often needs to be coped/notched at the beam ends in order to avoid interference of the connected structural members at these junctions. Depending on the structural and architectural requirements, one flange or both flanges of the beam and the affected part of the web need to be removed such that the strength and stiffness of the beam are inevitably reduced. Because of the removal of the flanges, a number of local failure modes which are not common in the case of uncoped beams may occur in coped beam connections. A comprehensive experimental and numerical study was conducted in this research project to examine the strength and behaviour of double-coped beams with or without reinforcements. Based on the test results and the corresponding numerical studies, a set of design rules were proposed to evaluate the local web buckling strength of double-coped beams. Strategies to reinforce the web of the double-coped beams were also recommended to enhance the strength of the coped end of the beams.

529213.label: Project Title(Chinese)
529213.value: 统一的非线性增广拉格朗日理论

529213.label: Project Objectives
529213.value: We will introduce a unified nonlinear augmented Lagrangian dual framework for the optimization problem where an extended real-valued function is minimized and establish the zero duality gap under relaxed conditions. We will establish equivalent conditions for the presence of an exact penalty function and establish the existence of Lagrange multipliers and augmented Lagrange multipliers. We will provide a unified numerical framework for various nonlinear augmented Lagrange methods, establish its theoretical foundation for the global convergence and carry out numerical experiments.

529213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
529213.value: Nonlinear constrained optimization is to provide an optimal strategy for the decision maker such that the designed objective cost is minimized subject to the limited resources. Barrier penalty function methods and exterior-point penalty function methods have been useful in solving nonlinear constrained optimization problems. The theoretical foundation for the rewarding application of these optimization methods is the establishment of a duality theory, including the presence of an optimal path and an exact penalty function. It has been shown that lower-order exterior-point penalty functions have a number of assuring theoretical results and some numerical advantages over the classical linear exterior-point penalty function. In this project, we will construct a unified framework of various augmented Lagrangian dual problems for the optimization problem where an extended real-valued function is minimized by virtue of a nonlinear augmenting penalty function with an open effective domain and a dual variable substitution and provide a theoretical foundation for the unified nonlinear augmented Lagrangian duality theory. We will introduce a pair of approximate perturbation conditions and establish that this pair of perturbation conditions presents equivalent conditions for the zero duality gap and the presence of an exact penalty function. We will establish sufficient conditions for the existence of Lagrange multipliers and augmented Lagrange multipliers. We will apply the obtained results to nonlinear constrained optimization problems and carry out numerical experiments. The project is of a long-term significant value, in its provision of a unified framework for barrier penalty function methods and exterior-point penalty function methods, an implication of further investigation on efficient solution algorithms for constrained optimization problems, and in the training of Operations Researchers with strong mathematical skills. 非线性约束优化是为决策者提供最佳策略，让他们能够利用有限的资源来极小化目标成本。障碍罚函数法和外点罚函数法有助于求解非线性约束优化问题。这些优化方法有益应用的理论基础建立对偶理论，包括最佳途径和精确罚函数的存在性。已经被证实，低阶外点罚函数法较之经典的线性外点罚函数法有很多确信的理论结果和数值优势。 在这个项目中，我们将对极小化一个广义实值函数的优化问题的各种增广拉格朗日对偶问题构建一个统一的框架，其中利用到开有效域的非线性增广罚函数和变量替换，并为这个统一的非线性增广拉格朗日对偶模型提供理论基础。我们将引进一对近似扰动条件并建立这对扰动条件是零对偶间隙成立和精确罚函数存在的等价条件。我们将得到拉格朗日乘子和增广拉格朗日乘子存在的充分条件。我们还将应用这些结果于非线性约束优化问题并将进行数值试验。 这个项目的长远的意义在于它为障碍罚函数法和外点罚函数法提供统一的框架、为进一步研究约束优化问题提出有效求解算法、并培养运筹学研究者的牢固的数学技巧。

529213.label: Realisation of objectives
529213.value: For objective 1, we studied penalty approaches for a semi-infinite program and a generalized semi-infinite program. We established first-order optimality conditions for semi-infinite programs by employing lower order integral exact penalty functions and in terms of a generalized second-order directional derivative. We obtained first-order optimality conditions for generalised semi-infinite programs by adopting the exact penalty function technique in terms of a classical augmented Lagrangian function for the lower-level problems of generalized semi-infinite programs to transform them into standard semi-infinite programs and by then applying our results for semi-infinite programs. For objective 2, in the case of a sharp Lagrangian, we obtained a first-order necessary condition for the existence of an augmented Lagrange multiplier for the semi-infinite programming problem and we established some first-order sufficient conditions by assuming inf-compactness of the data functions and the extended Mangasarian–Fromovitz constraint qualification. For a min-max optimization problem with quadratic functions, we showed that the global second-order sufficient condition implies the global quadratic growth condition. For objective 3, we employed a box-constrained differentiable penalty method for general nonlinear complementarity problems. We established that the solution of box-constrained penalized equations converges to that of the original problem at an exponential order. For bounded nonlinear complementarity problems we reformulated it as a nonlinear equation containing a power penalty term. We showed that the solution to the nonlinear equation converges to that of the bounded nonlinear complementarity problems at an exponential rate when the function is continuous and xi-monotone. On the other hand, under the assumptions of local weak sharp minima of order p (p ∈ [1, 2]) and a quasi-regularity condition, we established a local superlinear convergence rate for the linearized proximal algorithm. We further applied the linearized proximal algorithm to solve a (possibly nonconvex) feasibility problem, as well as a sensor network localization problem. Our numerical results illustrated that the LPA meets the demand for an efficient and robust algorithm for the sensor network localization problem.

529213.label: Major findings and research outcome
529213.value: We established first-order optimality conditions for semi-infinite programs by employing lower order integral exact penalty functions and the condition that the generalized second-order directional derivative of the constraint function at the candidate point is non-positive. We adopted the exact penalty function technique in terms of a classical augmented Lagrangian function for the lower-level problems of generalized semi-infinite programs to transform them into standard semi-infinite programs and then applied our results for semi-infinite programs to derive first-order optimality conditions for generalized semi-infinite programs. See ref [4]. In the case of a sharp Lagrangian, we obtained a first-order necessary condition for the existence of an augmented Lagrange multiplier for the semi-infinite programming problem and we established some first-order sufficient conditions by assuming inf-compactness of the data functions and the extended Mangasarian–Fromovitz constraint qualification. In particular using a valley at 0 augmenting function and assuming suitable second-order sufficient conditions, we obtained the existence of an augmented Lagrange multiplier for the semi-infinite programming problem. See ref [2]. We found that the global second-order sufficient condition implies the global quadratic growth condition. See ref [5]. We proposed a box-constrained differentiable penalty method for nonlinear complementarity problems, which not only inherited the same convergence rate as the existing l_{1/p}-penalty method but also overcame its disadvantage of non-Lipschitzianness and non-smoothness. We proved that the solution of box-constrained penalized equations converges to that of the original problem at an exponential order. We carried out the numerical experiments on the test problems from MCPLIB, and showed that the proposed method is efficient and robust. See ref [3]. We showed that the solution to the nonlinear equation obtained by applying a power penalty approach to the bounded nonlinear complementarity problem (NCP) converges to that of the original bounded NCP at an exponential rate when the function is continuous and xi-monotone. Numerical results on discretized double obstacle problems were presented to confirm the theoretical results. See ref [1]. Under the assumptions of local weak sharp minima of order p (p ∈ [1, 2]) and a quasi-regularity condition, we established a local superlinear convergence rate for a linearized proximal algorithm (LPA). We applied the LPA to solve a (possibly nonconvex) feasibility problem, as well as a sensor network localization problem. Our numerical results illustrated that the LPA meets the demand for an efficient and robust algorithm for the sensor network localization problem. See ref [6].

529213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
529213.value: We will explore structured augmented Lagrangian methods for some special classes of constrained nonlinear optimisation problems and study computational advantages of these methods. The structures may be the sparsity of the decision variables and the discontinuity of the cost function where the former has applications in statistics, compressing sensing and the later has applications in portfolio selection with transaction cost. We will investigate smoothing methods for solving these augmented Lagrangian problems.

529213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
529213.value: We established first-order optimality conditions for semi-infinite programs by employing lower order integral exact penalty functions and in terms of a generalized second-order directional derivative. We obtained first-order optimality conditions for generalised semi-infinite programs by adopting the exact penalty function technique in terms of a classical augmented Lagrangian function for the lower-level problems of generalized semi-infinite programs and transforming them into standard semi-infinite programs and by then applying our results for semi-infinite programs. In the case of a sharp Lagrangian, we obtained a first-order necessary condition for the existence of an augmented Lagrange multiplier for the semi-infinite program and we established first-order sufficient conditions by assuming inf-compactness of the data functions and the extended Mangasarian–Fromovitz constraint qualification. We established a local superlinear convergence rate for a linearized proximal algorithm for solving a convex composite program. We further applied the linearized proximal algorithm to solve a sensor network localization problem. Our numerical results illustrated that the linearized proximal algorithm meets the demand for an efficient and robust algorithm for the sensor network localization problem. We established that the solutions of penalty problems of nonlinear complementarity problems converge to that of the original problems at an exponential order.

529313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
529313.value: In recent years, with the industrial development and population growth, there is tremendous increase in global demand for energy. Energy shortage turns to be a great bottleneck constraining the development of industry and economy and even becomes the root of most regional conflicts. People have made a bunch of endeavors to alleviate the pressure from energy shortage by seeking for new energy resources (e.g. solar energy, wind energy and nuclear energy) and enhancing the efficiency of energy utilization. Batteries, as engineering electronic devices, play an important role in storing and transferring electrical energy. Developing batteries with high capacity and long cycle life would not only be of significant value to the industries like portable electronic devices, electrical vehicles and man-made satellites, but would help save energy (e.g., storing unused electrical energy) and eventually alleviate the pressure from energy shortage. High-capacity batteries entail high-capacity electrode materials. Among all candidates of anode materials, silicon stands out for its high capacity and is viewed as the most promising anode materials for the next generation lithium-ion batteries. But a major obstacle of using Si-based materials as electrode is that they experience huge (400%) volume change during the charge/discharge processes. Consequently, fracture and delamination of active electrode materials from current collector occur, resulting in loss of electric conductivity and capacity fading. To overcome this problem, many approaches have been developed. One of the feasible strategies is to modify the morphology of the current collectors. However, this approach remains in an empirical stage due to the deficiency of a comprehensive understanding of the mechanics of adhesion between Si-based electrode materials and current collector. In this project, systematic analysis is proposed to study the mechanics of the morphological effect of current collector on its adhesion with Si-based electrode materials. The aim of this project is to provide operational guidelines to the morphological design and optimization of current collectors aimed at higher electrochemical performance. The outcomes of this project would greatly promote the application of Si as the electrode materials in the next generation lithium-ion batteries. 近些年，随着工业发展和人口增长，全球对于能源的需求量显著提高，随之而来的能源短缺问题成为制约工业和经济发展的瓶颈问题，也是诸多区域冲突的根源所在。人们投入很大精力来寻找新的替代能源（如太阳能，风能，核能等）以及增加能源利用效率以缓解能源供需紧张的问题。而电池作为应用非常广的工程器件，因为其在能源存储和转换中起的关键性作用而受到广泛关注。发展高容量和长寿命的电池不仅能够极大地推动工业发展，促进其在可携带式电源、电动车、人造卫星等方面的应用，也能够有效地缓解能源紧张带来的压力。高容量电池需要具备高容量的电极材料，而硅是已知的所有负极材料中电容量最高的，也被认为是最有前景的下一代锂离子电池负极材料。然而在电池充放电过程中，硅基材料会出现接近400%的体积膨胀，这会导致活性阳极材料和集流体之间的断裂和脱层，从而严重降低电导性和电池容量。为了解决这个问题，方法之一就是通过改变集流体的表面形貌以减少和防止阳极材料的断裂和脱层。然而由于缺乏对于硅基阳极材料和集流体之间作用的力学机理的充分了解，这种方法还只处于经验阶段。在本项目中，我们的分析将集中在集流体形貌对其与硅材料间的粘附的影响上面。我们的目的是为集流体的形貌优化提供可行性的指导方案。我们的研究成果将会很大程度上促进硅基阳极材料在下一代锂离子电池中的应用。

529313.label: Realisation of objectives
529313.value: Objective 1: To quantify the interfacial toughness between typical Si-based electrode materials and Cu; to develop an applicable cohesive law and failure criterion for the adhesion between Si-based electrode materials and cupreous current collector. A series of molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were conducted to calculate the adhesion energy (toughness) between single crystal copper (current collector) and lithiated amorphous silicon electrode. We used the reactive force field potential to describe the interaction between lithium and silicon and the second-generation of charge-optimized many-body (comb) potential for copper and silicon, both of which have been proven capable of depicting the respective interatomic relationships. Due to the lack of many-body potential for the interaction between lithium and copper, the Lennard-Jones (L-J) potential is utilized to compute the site-site energy between these atoms. The parameters of the L-J potential were extracted from the fitting curve of the results calculated by density functional theory. To reduce the time and memory consumption in calculations, a small (~3400 atoms) but typical calculation system was constructed with focus on the interface between a bulk silicon electrode and a bulk single-crystal copper current collector with its contact surface being (111) plane. Both the copper current collector and the lithiated silicon are 3.07 nm in x direction and 3.54 nm in y direction with periodic boundary conditions applied in both x and y directions. In z direction, both are 2.07 nm in thickness, greater than the maximum radial cut-off distance 1.5 nm used in the calculation. Electrodes with 4 different degrees of lithiation (Li atomic fraction of 0.375, 0.529, 0.673 and 0.790, corresponding to x of 0.6, 1.08, 2.06 and 3.75 in LixSi) were investigated. During the calculation of the adhesion energy, the current collector and the lithiated electrode were relaxed separately with interfacial distance greater than 2 nm at 300 K in NVE ensemble and then moved oppositely by a distance where the potential energy reached its minimum. With the obtainment of these calculated adhesion energy (toughness), an applicable cohesive law and failure criterion for the adhesion between Si-based electrode materials and Cu current collector was successfully established. It was found that the adhesion energy (toughness) increases with the increase of the lithium fraction, implying that lithium atoms act as the binder between electrode and current collector. The more Li atoms at the interface, the greater the adhesion strength with the Cu current collector. Upon the completion of above work, the proposed Objective 1 is achieved 100%. Objective 2: To shed light on the effect of surface morphology of planar current collector on the delamination of electrode materials. To shed light on the effect of surface roughness of planar current collector on the electrochemical performance of current collector, a surface-roughened copper foil was prepared by chemically etching a Cu foil in etchant. It was found that the electrode with etched Cu current collector exhibits higher specific capacity, better rate capacity and cycling performance than that without modification. Specifically, the initial discharge specific capacity of the electrode with surface modified current collector at current rate of 0.1 C is 2680.3 mAh/g, while the electrode without modification is 1800.2 mAh/g only. The coulombic efficiency of the electrode with surface modified current collector is closer to 100%, which is higher than that of the untreated Cu current collector. The first coulombic efficiency of the electrode with modified current collector is over 93%, resulting in a lower irreversible capacity than those reported in literature. After 40 cycles, the discharge capacity of the electrode with modified current collector remains 1196.5 mAh/g versus 766.1 mAh/g for the electrode with unmodified current collector. The improved electrochemical performance can be attributed to the strong interface binding and therefore better electrical contact between the etched Cu current collector surface and the Si-based active materials, which mainly result from the surface roughness of the etched Cu current collector. Besides, we modified the surface morphology of a planar Cu current collector by depositing Cu nanowires. The diameter and length of these nanowires are approximately 0.3 μm and 5 μm, respectively. Compared to the plain Cu current collector, such new current collector with deposited nanowires was demonstrated to have better electrochemical performance. Such enhanced performance can be attributed to enhanced attachment of the Si-based active materials on the current collector and the consequent less loss of electric contact and significant improvement of the electrode cyclability. Upon the completion of above work, the proposed Objective 2 is achieved 100%. Objective 3: To obtain operational guidelines for robust adhesion between current collectors and Si-based electrode materials by optimizing the morphology of current collectors. In addition to the surface roughness and three-dimensional structure, we also theoretically investigated the effect of thickness gradient of current collector on its electrochemical performance. It was found that the if the thickness of Cu current collector has proper gradient, the interfacial shear stress between the current collector and the Si-based electrode materials can be homogenized. The optimal gradient design was discovered in theory. With the guideline of such theoretical result, a gradient Cu current collector was fabricated by using controlled chemical etching and then assembled in lithium-ion batteries for the characterization of electrochemical performance. As expected, our results indicated that gradient current collector, compared to the traditional uniform current collector, would give rise to better performance including better cyclability and higher capacity. With the attainments of above results, operational guidelines for robust adhesion between current collector and Si-based electrode material can be proposed as follows: 1. Microscopic surface roughness can improve the bonding between the current collector and electrode materials. 2. Three-dimensional nanostructure on the surface of Cu current collector would also enhance the attachment of electrode materials on the current collector. 3. Above two methods enhance the binding between electrode materials and current collector, but the intrinsic stress concentration problem has not been solved. To homogenize the stress field developed on the interface between electrode materials and current collector, a facile and practical way is to apply current collector with gradient thickness. Upon the completion of above work, the proposed Objective 3 is achieved 100%.

529313.label: Major findings and research outcome
529313.value: Current collectors with surface roughness were fabricated by using chemical etching. The obtained current collectors were found to bring better electrochemical performance to the lithium-ion batteries. Specifically, the initial discharge specific capacity of the electrode with surface modified current collector at current rate of 0.1 C is 2680.3 mAh/g, while the electrode without modification is 1800.2 mAh/g only. The coulombic efficiency of the electrode with surface modified current collector is closer to 100%, which is higher than that of the untreated Cu current collector. The first coulombic efficiency of the electrode with modified current collector is over 93%, resulting in a lower irreversible capacity than those reported in literature. After 40 cycles, the discharge capacity of the electrode with modified current collector remains 1196.5 mAh/g versus 766.1 mAh/g for the electrode with unmodified current collector. Meanwhile, current collectors coated with Cu nanowires were also fabricated by using deposition method. The obtained current collectors were also found to have better electrochemical performance compared to the traditional smooth Cu foil. Related results were published on Carbon 80 (2014) 793-798 and Scientific Reports 7(2017), 7769. The study on the interaction between Si-based electrode materials and Cu current collector began from the investigation of the interaction between Si and Cu by using MD simulation. The adhesion energy or toughness between Si and Cu was obtained. It was found that the adhesion energy (toughness) increases with the increase of the lithium fraction, implying that lithium atoms act as the binder between electrode and current collector. The more Li atoms at the interface, the greater the adhesion strength with the Cu current collector. Such Li fraction-dependent adhesion strength may be adverse for the electrical contact between electrode and current collector because cyclic lithiation and delithiation change the amount of lithium atoms, which leads to the inhomogeous distribution of lithium atoms and therefore inhomogeneous adhesion energy at the interface. Related paper is under review. However, above methods for enhancing the interface between electrode materials and current collector do not directly tackle the problem of stress concentration which is the essential problem accounting for the interfacial delamination. To homogenizing the shearing stress field developed during the lithiation process between electrode materials and current collector, current collector with designed gradient in thickness could be applied. The validity of this gradient strategies was demonstrated in both theory and experiment. Related paper is under preparation and will be submitted in a few months.

529313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
529313.value: The finding with the most promising application potential is the gradient strategy for homogenizing the stress distribution between current collector and electrode materials with large volumetric change during lithiation and delithiation process. Currently, our method for manufacturing gradient current collector relies on chemical etching which is not so controllable. In our future work, we can focus on the other manufacturing methods of current collector with controllable gradient such as mechanical polishing and three-dimensional printing. More importantly, this strategy may also apply to other interfaces in bi-material systems with strain mismatch such as thermal barrier coatings. It should be point out that the gradient thickness strategy also has a limitation. Our current solution to the gradient is only applied to the circular current collector which is often used in coin cell batteries. It may not be applied to the current collector with other shapes such as rectangular. Other strategies for homogenizing interfacial stress is needed for non-circular current collector.

529313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
529313.value: Silicon is deemed as the most promising electrode material for the next-generation lithium-ion batteries because of its extraordinarily high capacity. However, the wide application of silicon in lithium-ion batteries is impeded by its large volumetric change, which will cause a series of problems including detachment of electrode materials from current collector. In this project, we focused our attention on the modification of current collector in an attempt to improve the attachment between Si-based electrode materials and current collector. Our results indicated that current collector with rough surface or three-dimensional nanostructures would enhance the binding with electrode materials and therefore improve the electrochemical performance of lithium-ion batteries. Another strategy that we revealed to improve the bonding between the current collector and electrode materials was to eliminate the potential stress concentration by using gradient current collector. All these findings would be of great and practical values to the design and manufacturing of high-performance Si-based lithium-ion batteries.

531213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
531213.value: Quantum technology allows us to engineer devices by exploiting non-classical features of quantum mechanics such as superposition, entanglement and tunneling. One of the prominent candidates for quantum technology is quantum optical systems and networks as photons are ideal information carriers for long-distance communication and light-matter interaction is the backbone of quantum networks. As optical quantum technology relies on designing quantum optical systems and organizing quantum optical networks so as to harness quantum states of light, a systematic framework for signal processing of quantum optical systems and networks is essential for a successful optical quantum technology. The theoretical endeavor proposed in this project is of systems and control nature. More specifically we will investigate how quantum linear optical systems and networks process non-classical and classical signals along the following three directions. 1) Derive analytical forms in mathematical terms of the intensity and state of the output field of a fully quantum linear optical system driven by multi-photon states. This is useful because multi-photon states have wide applications in quantum communication, quantum computation, quantum metrology, quantum lithography and quantum cryptography, etc. A good analytical description of the intensity and state of output fields will provide a foundation for engineering multi-photon states using quantum linear systems. 2) Extend the mathematical description in part 1) to linear mixed quantum-classical systems. This will enable one to better understand and describe multi-photon state processing by optical systems involving quantum components (such as optical cavities, beamsplitters, and optical parametric amplifiers) and classical components (such as photodetectors and piezoelectric actuators). 3) Design an estimator in the form of mixed quantum-classical linear systems to estimate an unknown classical time-varying signal, and minimize the estimation error with respect to the structure of the estimator and its feedback interconnection with the quantum system driven by the classical signal. Quantum estimation of classical signals has important applications in quantum metrology, including gravitational wave detection. The proposed estimation via feedback interconnection method will provide powerful innovative tools for quantum estimation. The proposed theoretical research will help to build a rigorous mathematical framework for signal processing by quantum linear optical systems and networks. It will provide theoretical insight to the state-of-the-art research in the emerging discipline of optical quantum technology. 531213.label: Realisation of objectives
531213.value: With the financial support of this project, we have achieved all the three objectives. In addition, we have investigated several relevant research problems. 1. Analytic form of the intensity and steady-state state of the output field of a quantum system driven by continuous-mode multi-photon states. If a light field contains a definite number of photons, say n of them, then the field is said to be in an n-photon state. In addition, if the n-photon state is characterized by the pulse shapes of the photons, then the field is said to be in a continuous-mode n-photon state. When a quantum linear system is driven by a continuous-mode n-photon state, the steady-state output field state is also a continuous-mode n-photon state. By means of tensor representation and computation, we have derived the analytic expression of the intensity and state of the output n-photon field. The research results appear in Automatica as Regular Paper; see Research Output [1] and [12] in Part C. 2. A network synthesis theory for mixed quantum-classical linear systems. When a controller is designed to control a quantum system, a set of mathematical equations can be obtained. To build an actual controller, the set of mathematical equations has to be realized. We have proposed a systematic way for such realization. More specifically, if the given mathematical equations satisfy some general conditions, we can systematically decompose them into the quantum components, classical components and their interconnections. The realization is in the form of a feedback network. The research result is currently under review by Automatica as Regular Paper; see Research Output [16] in Part C. 3. Photon-atom interaction. Photons are flying qubits, and atoms are stationary qubits; thus photon-atom interaction is the backbone of quantum information processing. We have studied how a multi-level atom interact with one, two, and even three photons of continuous mode. The exact analytic expression of the output photon state has been derived. Interesting quantum optics phenomena have been observed. The research results appear in Journal such as Automatica, New Journal of Physics, and Journal of Physics A; see Research Output [6], [7], [9] and [14] in Part C. 4. Quantum filtering. Filters allow us to get information of the underlying systems. As it is in general difficult to observe an atom or some other quantum particles, it is always beneficial to design a filter that allows us to read information in quantum systems. We have proposed quantum filters for quantum systems driven by a light field which can contain an arbitrary number of photons. By means of these filters, we are able to obtain interesting physical phenomena. For example, if an atom is driven a 2-photon Gaussian state, when the frequency bandwidth of the 2-photon state is twice of the coupling rate between the atom and the 2-photon input field, the atom achieves the highest excitation probability. The research results appear in Journals such as EPJ Quantum Technology and SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization; see Research Output [2] and [8] in Part C. 5. Quantum entanglement. Entanglement is an essential resource for the realisation of quantum information processing. Therefore, it is very important to quantify the degree of entanglement for a quantum network that is designed to fulfil a certain quantum information processing task. Unfortunately, it is commonly agreed that computation of quantum entanglement is a very difficult task. We have developed tensor computational methods to efficiently compute the geometric measure of entanglement of quantum networks. The research results appear in journal such as Physical Review A; see Research Output [3], [5], and [11] in Part C. 6. Kalman canonical form is a fundamental result in classical systems and control theory as it reveals the structure of classical linear systems. We have obtain a quantum canonical form for quantum linear systems. Interestingly, in the quantum regime, the controllable/unobservable subspace and the uncontrollable/observable subspace appear in a conjugate form. Thus, they must co-exist. Moreover, if a quantum linear system is Hurwitz stable, it must be both controllable and observable. Finally, the quantum Kalman canonical form reveals several important concepts in quantum information science, such as decoherence-free subspace and quantum back-action evading measurement The research results appear in Automatica and EEE Transactions on Automatic Control as Regular Paper; see Research Output [4] and [13] in Part C. 7. Quantum memristor modeling. In 1971, Leon Chua proposed the memristor, the fourth electric element in line with resistor, capacitor, and inductor. In 2008, the company HP built the first memristor based on nano-technology. We have proposed a quantum model of memristive circuits. The research results appear in the Journal of Mathematical Physics; see Research Output [15] in Part C.

531213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
531213.value: Based on the research carried out, we plan to work on the following research problems: 1. Structural decomposition of quantum bilinear systems. Quantum bilinear systems can be used to describe the dynamics of atoms or artificial matters, it is important to describe such dynamics as photon-matter interaction is the backbone of quantum information processing. Armed with the Kalman canonical form for quantum linear systems, we plan to develop similar structural decomposition for quantum bilinear systems. 2. Time-frequency analysis of continuous-mode photon states. Photon states are useful resources in quantum information and quantum computation. Armed with the study of Wigner spectrum analysis carried out in this project, we plan to study photon states in time domain and frequency domain simultaneously, in the hope of gaining a better understanding of continuous-mode photon states. 3. Quantum feedback network driven by photon states. Feedback is fundamentally important in control engineering. Based on the study of the atom-photon interaction conducted in this project, we plan to study how a quantum feedback network regulates the dynamics of input photon states.

531213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
531213.value: Financially supported by this project, we have studied several research problems in the broad field of quantum information and control. 1. If a light field contains exactly n photons, it is in an n-photon state. Photon states are very useful resources in quantum information and computation. Thus, it is important to study how systems process photon states. We studied how a quantum linear system responds to an n-photon state. In particular, the exact expression of the n-photon state of the output field is derived. 2． Efficient quantum information process depends on effective interaction between photon with matters, such as atoms. Matters are nonlinear quantum systems. Thus, it is important to study the interaction between photon states and quantum nonlinear systems. Analytic forms of photon states after interaction are obtained. Also, the exact form of n-photon quantum filters is derived. 3. Structure determines property. We have investigated the structure of quantum linear systems. In particular, we have obtained the quantum Kalman canonical form. As Kalman canonical form is a fundamental result in classical control theory, it is quite expectable that the quantum Kalman canonical form will play a significant role in quantum control theory.

531313.label: Project Objectives
531313.value: Training data generation for perceptual transform learning – To learn a series of linear transforms for perceptual quality preserved image restoration, we must establish a training dataset. Considering the fact that natural images have very high dimensionality, the perceptual transform learning will be performed on image patches. Two strategies will be implemented to generate the training data: by using the existing image quality assessment databases, and by simulating the image restoration outputs. In each strategy, methods will be developed to estimate the subjective quality score of an image patch. Finally, a comprehensive training dataset will be established, which contains millions of image patches of various distortion types and at different distortion levels, as well as their estimated subjective scores. This dataset will be crucial to perceptual transform learning and consequently the image restoration performance. Transform learning for perceptual quality regularization – With the established training dataset, we will study how to learn the transforms to regress an image patch to its perceptual quality score. This will be a joint optimization problem of transform learning and regression, for which non-convex minimization algorithms will be developed in this project. Consequently, we will use the learned transforms to design novel perceptual quality regularization models for image restoration. Different from the existing regularization methods, the proposed models will be able to optimize explicitly the perceptual quality score of the reconstructed image. Transform learning for perceptual nonlocal regularization – Image nonlocal self-similarity is very useful to improve the image restoration results. Conventional methods often use Euclidian distance to measure the nonlocal similarity for nonlocal neighbor searching and nonlocal regularization. In this project we will learn transforms to measure the perceptual distance between patches, and present novel perceptual nonlocal regularization models for image restoration, which will lead to perceptually much more pleasant result than existing nonlocal regularization methods.

531313.label: Realisation of objectives
531313.value: 1. Training data generation for perceptual transform learning Preparing and generating appropriate training data is the foundation to learn suitable models for perceptual image quality assessment (IQA) and image quality enhancement. In this project, extensive efforts have been made to develop two large scale datasets for these purpose. With an increasing number of IQA models proposed, how to fairly compare their performance becomes a major challenge due to the enormous size of image space and the limited resource for subjective testing. Existing databases contain distorted images generated from a few dozens of source images, which however provide an extremely limited representation of real-world images. We built a database that contains 4,744 source natural images, together with 94,880 distorted images created from them. With this database, we proposed a new mechanism, namely group MAximum Differentiation (gMAD) competition, which automatically selects subsets of image pairs from the database that provide the strongest test to let the IQA models compete with each other. Subjective testing on the selected subsets reveals the relative performance of the IQA models and provides useful insights on potential ways to improve them. This work was published in CVPR 2016 as a spotlight paper [C4]. Due to the limited dynamic range of digital imaging devices, the recorded images are often under-/over-exposed and with low quality. Tradition single image contrast enhancement (SICE) methods adjust the tone curve to enhance the image but often fail in revealing image details. The SICE task can be better accomplished if we can learn extra information from appropriately collected training data. However, how to construct a training dataset of low-contrast and high-contrast image pairs for end-to-end learning is an open problem. In this project, we built a large-scale multi-exposure image dataset, which contains 589 elaborately selected high-resolution multi-exposure sequences with 4,413 images. Thirteen representative multi-exposure image fusion and stack-based high dynamic range imaging algorithms were employed to generate the contrast enhanced images for each sequence, and subjective experiments are conducted to screen the best quality one as the reference image of each scene. With the constructed dataset, a CNN can be easily trained as the SICE enhancer to improve the contrast of an under-/over-exposure image. More details can be found in [J1]. In addition, we also collected a set of test images for high dynamic range image tone mapping in [J2]. 2. Transform learning for perceptual quality regularization We have investigated and developed a few effective methods for learning based image quality enhancement, including CNN in [J1] and PCA transform in [J2]. In [J3], we investigated the construction of feed-forward denoising convolutional neural networks (DnCNNs) to embrace the progress in very deep architecture, learning algorithm, and perceptual regularization method into image denoising. Different from the existing discriminative denoising models which usually train a specific model for additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) at a certain noise level, our DnCNN model is able to handle Gaussian denoising with unknown noise level (i.e., blind Gaussian denoising). Furthermore, a single DnCNN model can be trained to tackle with several general image denoising tasks such as Gaussian denoising, single image super-resolution and JPEG image deblocking. Our developed DnCNN has become a benchmark in image denoising, and our paper [J3] has been selected as an ESI highly cited paper. Model-based optimization methods and discriminative learning methods have been the two dominant strategies for solving various inverse problems in low-level vision. Recent works have revealed that, with the aid of variable splitting techniques, denoiser prior can be plugged in as a modular part of model-based optimization methods to solve other inverse problems (e.g., deblurring). However, the study of integration with fast discriminative denoiser prior is still lacking. In [C3], we trained a set of fast and effective CNN denoisers and integrated them into model-based optimization method to solve other inverse problems. The learned denoisers not only achieve promising Gaussian denoising results but also can be used as prior to deliver good performance for various low-level vision applications. In [C6], we also presented a learning based convolutional sparse coding scheme for image superresolution. In [J7], we proposed a structural patch decomposition (SPD) to transform an image patch into three conceptually independent components: signal strength, signal structure, and mean intensity. Upon fusing these three components separately, we reconstructed a desired patch and place it back into the fused image for multiple-exposure fusion (MEF). Our method not only outperforms previous MEF algorithms on static scenes but also consistently produces high quality fused images with little ghosting artifacts for dynamic scenes. 3. Transform learning for perceptual nonlocal regularization Patch based image modeling has achieved a great success in low level vision such as image denoising. In particular, the use of image nonlocal self-similarity (NSS) prior, which refers to the fact that a local patch often has many nonlocal similar patches to it across the image, has significantly enhanced the denoising performance. By stretching the image nonlocal similar patches as vectors and putting them into a matrix, we have investigated and developed several powerful schemes for matrix transform learning based image quality enhancement. In most existing NSS based methods, only the NSS of input degraded image is exploited, while how to utilize the NSS of clean natural images is still an open problem. In [C5], we proposed a patch group (PG) based NSS prior learning scheme to learn explicit NSS models from natural images for high performance denoising. PGs are extracted from training images by putting nonlocal similar patches into groups, and a PG based Gaussian Mixture Model (PG-GMM) learning algorithm was developed to learn the NSS prior. We demonstrated that, owe to the learned PG-GMM, a simple weighted sparse coding model, which has a closed-form solution, can be used to perform image denoising effectively, resulting in high PSNR measure, fast speed, and particularly the best visual quality among all competing methods. As a convex relaxation of the rank minimization model, the nuclear norm minimization (NNM) problem has been attracting significant research interest in recent years. The standard NNM regularizes each singular value equally. However, this restricts its capability and flexibility in dealing with many practical problems, where the singular values have clear physical meanings and should be treated differently. In [J4], we studied the weighted nuclear norm minimization (WNNM) problem, which adaptively assigns weights on different singular values. As the key step of solving general WNNM models, the theoretical properties of the weighted nuclear norm proximal (WNNP) operator are investigated. Albeit nonconvex, we proved that WNNP is equivalent to a standard quadratic programming problem with linear constrains, which facilitates solving the original problem with off-the-shelf convex optimization solvers. In particular, when the weights are sorted in a non-descending order, its optimal solution can be easily obtained in closed-form. Furthermore, inspired by the reweighted sparse coding scheme, we presented an automatic weight setting method, which greatly facilitates the practical implementation of WNNM. The proposed WNNM methods achieve state-of-the-art performance in typical low level vision tasks, including image denoising, background subtraction and image inpainting. This work has been selected as an ESI highly cited paper. Further extensions of this work can be found in [J5], [C2].

With this database, a new mechanism, namely group MAximum Differentiation (gMAD) competition, was proposed to select subsets of image pairs that provide the strongest test to let the IQA models compete with each other. This work was published in CVPR 2016 as a spotlight paper. [C4] 3. We presented a feed-forward denoising convolutional neural network (DnCNNs) to handle Gaussian denoising with unknown noise level. It can also be trained to tackle with several general image denoising tasks such as Gaussian denoising, single image super-resolution and JPEG image deblocking using a single DnCNN model. DnCNN has become a benchmark in image denoising. This paper [J3] is an ESI highly cited paper. [J3] 4. We studied the weighted nuclear norm minimization (WNNM) problem, which adaptively assigns weights on different singular values. The theoretical properties of the weighted nuclear norm proximal (WNNP) operator were investigated. Albeit nonconvex, we proved that WNNP still has a global optimum. In particular, when the weights are sorted in a non-descending order, its optimal solution can be easily obtained in closed-form. The proposed WNNM methods achieve state-of-the-art performance in typical low level vision tasks, including image denoising, background subtraction and image inpainting. This work [J4] has been selected as an ESI highly cited paper. Some extensions of this work are in [J5], [C2]. 5. We extended patch based prior learning to patch group (PG) based NSS prior learning to learn explicit NSS models from natural images for high performance denoising. [C5] 6. We trained a set of fast and effective CNN denoisers and integrated them into model-based optimization method to solve other inverse problems for various low-level vision applications. [C3] 7. We presented a learning based convolutional sparse coding scheme for image superresolution. [C6]

531313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
531313.value: There are two potential improvements of the proposed methods in this project. 1. Extension to semi-supervised learning methods. The proposed methods in [J1] [J3] [C3] [C6] are basically supervised learning methods, though they are very effective. One possible weakness of these methods are their generalization capability to images whose statistics are not identical to the training datasets. In the future, we will study how to extend these methods to semi-supervised learning schemes. On one hand, this can reduce the dependency on labeled data; on the other hand, this can also improve the generality of learned models. 2. Learning methods without image pairs. In real scenarios of image quality enhancement, the paired data are difficult to obtain. One interesting idea is can we learn discriminative models without image pairs. The recent advancement of GAN networks bring good insights on this problem, and we will also investigate along this line of research.

531313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
531313.value: In this project, we investigated the problem of perceptual image restoration, and developed a series of effective methods to enhance the quality of reconstructed images. First, some model based methods, such as the weighted nuclear norm minimization (WNNM) and patch group based nonlocal self-similarity prior learning, were developed to effectively exploit the image nonlocal self-similarity for image enhancement. Second, we investigated discriminative methods, especially deep learning, for image restoration. Our developed denoising convolutional neural network (DnCNN) is one of the first CNN based image denoising methods, and it has become a benchmark in image denoising. We also trained a set of fast and effective CNN denoisers and integrated them into model-based optimization methods. The learned denoisers achieve promising Gaussian denoising results and they can be used as prior models for various low-level vision applications. Third, we built two large scale datasets to facilitate the image quality enhancement research. One is the multi-exposure image dataset with low-contrast and good-contrast image pairs, which makes discriminative learning of single image contrast enhancement possible. The other database provides a good platform for developing new image quality assessment models. Two research papers produced in this project were selected as the ESI highly cited papers.

531813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
531813.value: There has been a resurgence of interest in nuclear power generation due to the lasting high oil price and ever decreasing fossil fuel reserve. For instance, China aims to increase her nuclear power generation by 7 times by 2020. The safety issue is of the paramount importance in the utilization of nuclear energy, especially after Chernobyl and Fukushima nuclear power plant disasters. Other than natural disasters and human mistakes, the flow-induced vibration (FIV) on structures such as fuel and control rods is recognized to be one of the major contributors to the accidents and shutdown of nuclear reactors, causing up to billions dollars loss to industries. The knowledge of the FIV is far from adequate in spite of tremendous progress made in the past. Our latest numerical simulations unveil a number of aspects of one, two and four elastic cylinders in unbounded or tubular axial flow, which failed to be captured previously (Liu et al. 2012a, b, c). This project is a continuation and complementation of this work and aims to gain experimentally a relatively thorough understanding of the FIV of clustered cylinders in axial flow. Compared with previous investigations, this study has four distinct characteristics. (1) In view of the real situation in a nuclear reactor, the effect of incident flow turbulence level on the interstitial flow and cylinder response, never reported before, will be invetsigated, along with the dimensionless flow velocity (or Reynolds number) and spacing between cylinders. (2) A multi-point optical fibre Bragg grating (FBG) sensing technology will be applied for the first time to resolve the axial-flow-induced vibration of multiple degrees of freedom. The multi-point FBG sensors have many unique advantages over conventional techniques and are most suitable for the study of fluid-structure interactions. They can be used to measure the displacement distribution and various modes of vibration for any flexible cylinder or cylinders in array since the transmission of the laser beam/signal occurs within optic fibres that are bonded along cylinders. (3) The interstitial flow field between cylinders and structural vibration will be measured simultaneously to capture fluid-structure interactions. (4) A data analysis technique will be sought that could extract from experimental data the natural frequencies, effective damping ratios and modal characteristics of a structure in the presence of flow and other structures, and the non-linear effects of fluid-structure interactions. 538013.label: Project Title(Chinese)
538013.value: 生物柴油燃燒關鍵反應的從頭算化學動力學

538013.label: Project Objectives
538013.value: The overriding objectives of the proposed program are 1) To obtain accurate reaction rate constants, by using the ab inito transition-state-theory based master equation analysis, for the key reactions in the combustion of biodiesel surrogates such as saturated and unsaturated methyl esters (C5 and C11). 2) To obtain useful information and understanding on the influence of molecular structure and unsaturation of alkyl chain on the rate constants. 3) To explore theoretical methodology for high-accuracy quantum chemistry calculation of thermochemical and kinetic data for large methyl ester molecules. 4) To develop validated and predictive quantum chemistry/chemical kinetics computation platform for large molecules of biodiesel surrogates. The specific research objectives for relatively small methyl esters (C5) are 1) To obtain bench mark rate constants for the saturated methyl esters C5H10O2, such as methyl butanoate (MB) and methyl isobutanoate (MIB), and unsaturated methyl esters C5H8O2, such as methyl crotonate (MC) and methyl methacrylate (MMA). The key reactions include the hydrogen abstraction reactions from the weakest bond of these molecules by H, OH and HO2 and the decomposition and isomerization reactions of the product radicals. 2) To obtain understanding on the influence of molecular structure on the C5H10O2 kinetics through the comparison between MB and MIB. 3) To obtain understanding on the influence of double bonds through the comparison between MB and MC, and between MIB and MMA. The detailed research objectives for relatively large methyl esters (C11) are 1) To obtain bench mark rate constants for methyl decanoate (C11H22O2, MD). The key reactions include the hydrogen abstraction reactions from the weakest bond of MD molecule by H, OH and HO2 and the decomposition and isomerization reactions of the product radicals. 2) To obtain understanding on the influence of C=C double bond on the rate constants through studying the monounsaturated methyl 4-decenoate (C11H20O2). 3) To obtain understanding on the influence of C=C double bond on the rate constants through studying the polyunsaturated methyl 4, 7-decenoate (C11H18O2).

538013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
538013.value: 為解決當代能源可持續性、能源安全和氣候變化等問題，生物燃料作為一種可行的解決方案被提出。生物柴油因其許多良好的燃料特性已成為最廣泛使用的生物燃料之一。特別是生物柴油能替代石油提煉出的柴油或與之混合，直接用於柴油發動機中，只需稍微改動或者完全無需改動發動機和燃料系統。為此，大量的研究工作正投入生物柴油燃燒化學定量預測機理的發展，這也為日益普遍的燃燒能量轉換設備的計算機輔助設計所需要。 生物柴油是具有不同分子結構和物理化學特性的脂肪酸酯的混合物，因此研究其反應機理具有極大的挑戰性。脂肪酸酯分子含有12到18個碳原子的長碳鏈，通常導致極其復雜的化學反應過程，包含成千上萬可能的中間化學物質和反應路徑。因此，常用的生物柴油化學反應研究的方式是將問題簡化為研究碳鏈較短的單個替代物分子，因為其反應機理的尺寸較小。使用最廣泛的生物柴油替代物是兩種飽和的甲基酯：含有5個碳原子的丁酸甲酯和含有11個碳原子的癸酸甲酯。盡管丁酸甲酯已被應用於許多研究，但我們對其燃燒化學的理解還很欠缺。癸酸甲酯碳鏈較長，因此還未被充分的研究。此外，目前生物柴油中的甲酯通常因含有C=C雙鍵而不飽和。然而，不飽和甲酯的燃燒化學很少被研究。基於以上的考慮，本項目將研究這兩種甲酯和它們對應的不飽和分子。本項目能夠提供有用的真實生物柴油化學反應動力學信息，並且補充和改進現有的反應機理。 本項目將采用理論和計算的方法。目前理論化學和化學反應動力學的進展使得用從頭算的方式（即求解量子化學薛定諤方程）計算反應機理中每個反應的化學反應速率常數成為可能。從頭算化學反應動力學較半經驗方法能顯著提高精度，且通常能與大多數實驗精度相媲美。另外，從頭算化學動力學可以用於研究那些難以在實驗中直接測量的反應速率常數，以及實際燃燒設備中會出現但是在實驗中難以達到的溫度和壓力。 綜上所述，本項目旨在用理論的方法研究生物柴油替代物的飽和與不飽和甲酯的燃燒化學反應動力學。

The specific research objectives for relatively small methyl esters (C5) are 1) To obtain bench mark rate constants for the saturated methyl esters C5H10O2, such as methyl butanoate (MB) and methyl isobutanoate (MIB), and unsaturated methyl esters C5H8O2, such as methyl crotonate (MC) and methyl methacrylate (MMA). The key reactions include the hydrogen abstraction reactions from the weakest bond of these molecules by H, OH and HO2 and the decomposition and isomerization reactions of the product radicals. 2) To obtain understanding on the influence of molecular structure on the C5H10O2 kinetics through the comparison between MB and MIB. 3) To obtain understanding on the influence of double bonds through the comparison between MB and MC, and between MIB and MMA.

The detailed research objectives for relatively large methyl esters (C11) are 1) To obtain bench mark rate constants for methyl decanoate (C11H22O2, MD). The key reactions include the hydrogen abstraction reactions from the weakest bond of MD molecule by H, OH and HO2 and the decomposition and isomerization reactions of the product radicals. 2) To obtain understanding on the influence of C=C double bond on the rate constants through studying the monounsaturated methyl 4-decenoate (C11H20O2). 3) To obtain understanding on the influence of C=C double bond on the rate constants through studying the polyunsaturated methyl 4, 7-decenoate (C11H18O2).

538013.label: Major findings and research outcome
538013.value: 1. A two-layer ONIOM[QCISD(T)/CBS:DFT] method The ONIOM method employs a QCISD(T)/CBS method for the high-layer and a DFT method for the low-layer. We proposed and developed this method to investigate the large biodiesel molecules, (CnH2n+1COOCmH2m+1 n=1-5, 9, 15; m=1-2). The calculated thermochemistry results, energy barriers and heats of reaction, are in very good agreement with those obtained using the widely accepted high-level method QCISD(T)/CBS method, for the computational errors are less than 0.1 kcal/mol. The method provides a computationally accurate and affordable approach to the high-level theoretical chemical kinetics of large fuel molecules. This work has resulted in a peer-reviewed journal publication. (Lidong Zhang and Peng Zhang*, Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys., 2015, 17, 200) 2. High-level theoretical studies of the reactions between unsaturated methyl esters, CnH2n-1COOCH3 (n=2-5, 17), and hydrogen radical The ONIOM method was proposed and developed for the high-level single-point energy calculations of large biodiesel molecules and was validated for the hydrogen abstraction reactions of unsaturated methyl esters. The predicted energy barriers and heat of reactions were calculated by using ONIOM and QCISD(T)/CBS method, as verified by the computational deviations being less than 0.15 kcal/mol. This work has resulted in a peer-reviewed journal publication. (Lidong Zhang, Qinghui Meng, Yicheng Chi and Peng Zhang*, The Journal of Physical Chemistry A, 2018, 122, 4882-4893) 3. Theoretical kinetics study on the reactions of methyl-butanoate with hydrogen and hydroxyl radicals The chemical kinetics for the reactions of methyl-butanoate with hydrogen and hydroxyl radicals were studied theoretically with the ab initio transition state theory including of the hydrogen abstraction reaction of MB by the radicals and further investigating to search for additional significant reaction channels. Phenomenological theoretical rate constants were calculated over broad ranges of temperature (200-2500 K) and pressure (1.3 × 10-3 to 102 atm). This work has resulted in a peer-reviewed journal publication. (Lidong Zhang, Qinxue Chen and Peng Zhang*, Proceedings of the Combustion Institute 35, 2015, 481-489) 4. Spin-off projects During the study of the pyrolysis reaction of methyl oleate (C19H36O2), we encountered a problem of adopting appropriate theoretical methodology for studying radical-radical fission reactions. We overcame the problem in cooperation with Dr. Klippenstein and Dr. Harding of Argonne National Laborary and Dr. Sun and Prof. Law of Princeton University. This collaborative work has resulted in a peer-reviewed journal publication. (P. Zhang*, S. J. Klippenstein*, L. B. Harding, H. Sun, C. K. Law, RSC Advances, 2014, 4, 62951).

538013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
538013.value: In this project, we studied large biodiesel molecules and obtained accurate and reliable reaction rate constants for the key reactions in the combustion of saturated and unsaturated methyl esters from C5 to C11, using the ab initio transition-state-theory based master equation analysis. In addition, we also investigated the larger biodiesel molecules, such as methyl oleate (C19H36O2). In the project, we proposed and developed the ONIOM method for studying quantum chemistry calculation of large biodiesel molecules. The results proved the applicability of this theoretical approach for the combustion chemical kinetics of large molecules. Furthermore, this method can be used to other large molecules. This method can be adopted to study aviation kerosene, for its main components are large hydrocarbon molecules which contain more than ten carbon atoms. High-level ab initio chemical kinetics of large hydrocarbon is crucial to establish the chemical reaction mechanisms of aviation kerosene combustion. Potential difficulties associated with further development are those originating from the high-accuracy calculation of partition functions and the rate coefficient calculation of multiple-well master equation analysis. The success of the present project provided a computationally accurate and affordable approach for studying large hydrocarbon molecules in aviation kerosene.

538013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
538013.value: Biofuels have been proposed as a viable solution to contemporary challenges such as energy sustainability, energy security and climate change. Biodiesel is one of the most widely used biofuels due to its many desirable advantages, renewability, low pollution and low emission. Particularly, biodiesel can replace or blend with petroleum-based diesel for direct utilization in diesel engine without or with only minor modifications to the engine and fueling system. Correspondingly, considerable effort is currently being devoted to the development of quantitatively predictive mechanisms for biodiesel combustion chemistry, which are required by the increasing prevailing computer-aided design for combustion energy conversion facilities. The mechanism development for biodiesel is immensely challenging since biodiesel is a mixture of fatty acid alkyl ester with varying molecular structure and physiochemical properties. The study adopts theoretical and computational approach. Recent progress in theoretical chemistry and chemical kinetics enable the ab initio (means ‘from the beginning’) calculation of reaction rate constants that are required be every reactions in a reaction mechanism. In summary, the project aims to investigate theoretically the chemical kinetics of key reactions in the combustion of the proposed saturated and unsaturated methyl esters which are surrogates of actual biodiesel.

538113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
538113.value: The coast that lies at the interface between land and ocean is a zone of great instability, being particularly vulnerable to earthquakes and the associated tsunamis. In recent years several significant seismic events, including the Mw 7.3 Haiti earthquake in 2010, the Mw 8.8 Chile earthquake in 2010 and the Mw 9.0 Japan earthquake in 2011, have occurred in the coastal zones and caused devastation to the local inhabitant and economy. Since a majority of the world’s population inhabits such zones effective assessment of earthquake potential has significant societal impacts. High-resolution measurements of interseismic deformation are critical for understanding the earthquake cycle and for assessing earthquake hazard. This project is designed to employ advanced Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) to obtain such measurements. It is well-known that by jointly analyzing a set of data over the same area acquired on different dates advanced InSAR is capable of remotely sensing interseismic deformation at an unprecedented level of spatial resolution. However conventional advanced InSAR cannot hold a considerate promise for the precise retrieval of interseismic deformation in coastal zones where complicated atmospheric delay, orbital errors, and localized seasonal ground fluctuations commonly exist. Also troublesome is the displacement due to Ocean Tide Loading (OTL) whose gradient can be larger than 3 cm per 100 km in some coastal zones. However OTL displacement has not yet been carefully dealt with in advanced InSAR processing chain. Of interest in this project is to develop reliable approaches to correct and/or suppress these unwanted signals thereby precisely map the interseismic deformation in coastal zones located in tectonically active regions (e.g., west America and Taiwan). The innovation of the proposed approaches lies in full exploration of the characteristics of the InSAR signals. For example according to different spatial-temporal characteristics, a joint model that takes both the orbital errors and deformation as parameters will be designed to isolate long wavelength ground motion signal from the orbital error even in cases the two types of signals exhibit similar spatial patterns. With determined high-resolution interseismic deformation, slip rates of major faults in coastal zones can then be estimated which is the basic information for the assessment of the earthquake risk. The proposed project is highly relevant to Hong Kong which is a representative coastal metropolis. 海岸帶位於陸地和海洋之間，在地質構造上是一個不穩定區域，特別容易受到地震及其引發的海嘯的破壞。最近幾年發生的大地震，如2010年7.3級的海地地震，2010年8.8級的智利地震及2011年9.0級的日本地震，均發生在海岸帶及周邊區域，給當地居民和經濟帶來重大損失。由於世界上主要人口均居住在沿海區域，評估該區域的地震風險具有重要的社會意義。 高解析度的震間形變觀測對理解地震週期及評估地震風險至關重要。本項目致力於應用高等雷達干涉測量技術獲取震間形變觀測。眾所周知，高等雷達干涉測量技術通過分析同一區域不同時刻成像的一系列雷達數據可以以遙測的方式獲取高解析度的震間形變場。然而具體到沿海區域，傳統技術不能夠保證所獲取的形變場的精度，這是因為在沿海區域複雜的大氣擾動，軌道誤差及區域性季節性地表形變波動普遍存在于雷達信號中。另外，在沿海區域，震間形變場亦會受到海洋潮負荷位移的影響。在某些海岸區海洋潮負荷位移在100公里內的變化可以達到3釐米。然而在將干涉測量技術應用于提取震間形變時，現有方法均未考慮海洋潮負荷位移的影響。 本項目將致力於開發一系列穩健的方法來改正或抑制上述擾動信號從而精確地獲取位於地址構造活躍區的海岸帶（如美國西部及台灣）的震間形變場。方法的創新性體現在充分挖掘了雷達干涉測量信號的特徵。例如，根據信號的時間空間特徵，提出一種聯合解算模型通過將軌道誤差和地表形變作為參數可以精確地分離長波長的形變信號和軌道誤差，即使二者在空間上呈現一致的分佈模式。利用高解析度的震間形變場可以有效評估地震風險。本項目的研究亦與香港息息相關，因為香港是個典型的沿海大都市。

538113.label: Realisation of objectives
538113.value: The project involves two objectives, i.e., Precise determination of interseismic deformation in coastal zones by advanced InSAR technique using over 20 years of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data acquired from various SAR missions and Assessment of seismic risk based on high-resolution interseismic deformation measurements obtained from the first objective. The statements on how and to what extent these objects have been achieved are as follows. To achieve the first objective, we have developed a set of novel algorithms that can overcome some limitations associated with the current multi-temporal InSAR estimators therefore improve the accuracy of interseismic deformation estimation. Firstly, a joint model aiming to precisely separate the orbit error and long wavelength tectonic motion was developed and published in [1]; Secondly, we realized the residuals due to the inaccurate DEM can also distort the estimation of interseismic motion and developed a new processing strategy that can better mitigate DEM error, which was applied in mountainous areas and published in [2]; After that, we further analyzed the factors that can affect the separation of DEM error and interseismic motion and proposed some possible solutions, which was published in [3] and [4]. Fourthly, to better mitigate the atmospheric artifacts, we developed a quad-tree based model that can model the atmospheric delay adaptively according to the topographic gradient. The work was submitted to IEEE TGRS and is under second review [5]. Fifthly, we conducted a thorough test on the performance of current ocean tidal loading (OTL) models and selected the best to correct the interferograms over coastal zones. Although such a correction is important for interseismic motion mapping, in the point view of algorithm development, the process can be easily implemented and is not deserved for publication alone. As summary, we developed 5 InSAR processing algorithms for objective 1, which can well ensure an accurate estimation of interseismic motion in most cases. The joint MTInSAR model was recently patented and applied in a project on mapping deformation over extremely wide areas, which won the first award on progresses of surveying and mapping technologies. The second objective is about the application of developed algorithms for accurate interseismic mapping. We firstly tested some algorithms in mountainous areas and published them in [6], [7] and [8]. More recently we integrated these algorithms into a processing platform and processed a large amount of L band SAR data over western Taiwan to study the relationship between costal deformation and sea level rising. The results were published in [9]. Overall, the project has been well conducted and the work is closely related to the project objectives. Although we have achieved all objectives of this project, we are still working on two publications that promote the research outputs in InSAR and earth science communities. 538213.label: Project Title(Chinese)
538213.value: 量子系統在相干控制下的可達集

538213.label: Project Objectives
538213.value: Characterizing the reachable sets of open single-spin systems. Single spin is the building block for many quantum technologies, e.g., nuclear magnetic resonance(NMR), electron spin resonance(ESR) spectroscopy and various physical realizations of quantum computing. The behavior of single spin in the absence of control fields is well studied and understood, but so far there is no general theory on optimal control of single spin, only scatted studies on optimal transfers between specific states. In this project, we will characterize the reachable sets of single spin in Markovian environment, provide a general framework for optimal control of single-spin system. Characterizing the reachable sets of operators on open single-spin systems. The reachable sets of states depends on the initial state, which sometimes can be unknown, in such cases, one can study the reachable sets of operators on the system, i.e., study what kind of operations one can generate on the system. Characterizing the reachable sets of multiple coupled-spin systems. Various physical realization of quantum computing and coherent spectroscopy requires spins to be coupled with each other. In this project the reachable sets of coupled-spin systems will be studied, emphasize on open two-spin systems, three-spin systems and spin chains. Applying the results on reachable sets to solve practical optimal control problems arise in experiments. Characterization of reachable sets can provide optimal control strategies on many concrete problems in experiments, such as coherence transfer between different spins, contrast imaging, etc. The methods and tools developed in this project will be tested in the laboratory of Professor Steffen J. Glaser at the department of Chemistry and Biochemistry at Technical university of Munich.
