540413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
540413.value: Grammatical markers or functional categories (e.g. tense, agreement, articles) have been found to cause difficulty to ESL learners. This is particularly the case when it comes to the acquisition of tense by Cantonese ESL learners as it is not realized overtly in Cantonese. This proposed study of "The Role of Pedagogical Intervention: Acquisition of Tense by Cantonese ESL Learners in Hong Kong" aims to bridge the gap between acquisition theory and language pedagogy research, and will contribute significantly to both the fields of SLA and second language teaching. Findings in the literature show that functional categories are not available in the initial stage of second language acquisition. The Minimal Trees Hypothesis, for example, contends that only lexical categories (e.g. the noun phrase) are available for first language transfer (L1 transfer) in the initial state but not functional categories which will emerge gradually triggered by positive evidence in the input (i.e. accessibility to grammatical sentences in the second language). According to Chan (2008), however, TP (Tense Phrase) is in fact present in the initial state; in other words, the production of L2 may not be an accurate reflection of what L2 learners know. Thus, the challenge for teachers is to help L2 learners map forms and meaning in acquiring tense. Processing instruction, as first described by VanPatten (1991), will be adopted as an instructional intervention. Unlike traditional instruction which emphasizes learners’ output, processing instruction intends to shape the ways that learners attend to input and make connections between form and meaning. A pre-test and 3 post-tests will be administered to examine if the pedagogical intervention will lead to any significant difference in the experimental groups (Processing Instruction group, Traditional Instruction group) in the acquisition of English simple past tense. An Implicit Training group is also added to determine the effectiveness of implicit instruction. The subjects will be secondary 1 (i.e. Grade 7) students in Hong Kong. The findings of the study will be highly significant for both SLA researchers and language teachers, shedding light on a number of theoretical and pedagogical issues, including the role of pedagogical intervention in helping learners acquire functional categories, the effectiveness of processing instruction, whether explicit or implicit instruction works better, and the pedagogical implications for teaching functional categories, suggesting how teachers can select effective teaching approaches and why (and how) English teaching in Hong Kong should be grounded more firmly on linguistic principles. 研究顯示，以學習英語為第二語言的人士在語法標記或功能語類 (例如: 時態, 冠詞）的學習上面對重大困難。而正由於粵語缺乏時態的顯性標記，因此其對學習者構成的困難尤其嚴重。本研究題為“教學的干預作用：以粵語為母語的學生習得英語時態的調查研究”，旨在拉近語言獲得理論與語言教學方法研究之間的距離，對第二語言獲得以及第二語言教學兩範疇均具有著舉足輕重的地位。 根據陳美寶（2008）的研究發現，在語言習得的初始階段，時態短語 (TP) 是存在的。我們不能根據學生在學習時態上所犯的錯誤而斷定他們缺乏時態的知識。因此，我們應關注如何幫助學生運用適當的時態表達正確的意思。 本研究以一個前測及三個後測測試VanPatten (2001) 的處理指示方法 (processing instruction)；測試對象為香港的中一學生。研究將顯示處理指示對時態習得方面的有效程度，並比較隱性教學法及明示教學法兩者的有效性。此研究在理論及教學實踐上的貢獻不容忽視。

540413.label: Realisation of objectives
540413.value: This study investigates the role of classroom input in the acquisition of Tense Phrase (TP). The experimental groups consisted of 66 primary 2 students aged 7-8 in Hong Kong. They were divided randomly into 3 groups being taught using 3 different forms of classroom intervention: Processing Instruction Group (PI); Traditional Instruction Group (TI); and Implicit Instruction Group (II). A pre-test and a post-test consisting of interpretation and production tasks were administered to examine if there is any significant difference in the performance after classroom intervention. Findings of this study suggest that explicit instruction in the form of processing instruction (PI) might be an effective means to address L2 learners’ difficulty in realizing the forms in acquiring English simple past. Of the two different types of explicit instruction examined in this study, the findings confirm earlier work about the effectiveness of PI in helping L2 learners interpret and produce simple past regardless of their L1 (objectives 1 and 2). Only the PI group showed significant improvement from pre-test to post-test in the interpretation task. The TI and II groups did not improve significantly, suggesting that traditional instruction and implicit instruction are not as effective in helping L2 learners interpret the simple past. In the production task, the findings are consistent with most previous studies, in as much as both PI and TI groups made the greatest gains from pre-test to post-test. In other words, processing instruction is as effective as traditional instruction in helping L2 learners produce simple past forms. This is the first study which examined the role of listening/reading skill in addition to that of sentence/discourse-level in the interpretation of the simple past by L2 learners. Though the three experimental groups did not have significantly different performance in both listening and reading tasks in the post-test, the effect size analysis shows that learners performed slightly better in the reading interpretation tasks and the effect size is better. Concerning sentence/discourse-level interpretation tasks, statistical analyses show that improvement in the sentence-level task is much more significant than in the discourse-level task. In other words, listening interpretation tasks and discourse-level tasks seem to make it difficult for the learners to interpret simple past. This may mean that we need to first present sentence-level tasks to primary students in the initial state when acquiring English simple past before proceeding to discourse-level ones. In the structured input activities, reading tasks can also be used first before proceeding to listening ones with the increase in students’ proficiency level. Overall, the PI group outperformed the other groups in the post-test no matter in listening/reading and sentence-level/discourse-level tasks. The effect is the largest among the three groups. (objectives 1-2) Another contribution of this study is that it betters our understanding of the role of second language instruction and adds another set of findings to the literature regarding the role of explicit instruction versus implicit instruction, which has never been examined in the PI studies conducted so far (objective 2). Results of this study suggest the importance of focusing on both the forms and meaning in second language instruction. Having said that, TI, which is a kind of form-focused instruction adopted as pedagogical intervention in this study, is found to be quite useful in helping the TI group realize the form in the production task. The effect size analysis conducted shows that the effect of TI is large in helping the TI group realize the form and its effect is small in terms of interpretation. Traditional Instruction, thus, should not be condemned as in the literature and it can be used as reinforcement together with processing instruction as classroom intervention to help L2 learners realize the target form in acquiring English simple past. Though the implicit instruction group’s improvement in the reading interpretation task was not significant, the effect size analysis shows that the effect was medium, which seems to indicate that implicit instruction requiring participants to expose to the target form through reading passages might work. (objective 3) Finally, this is another study conducted with primary students including almost double the Cantonese ESL learners in each group. The results show that PI is “equally effective as an intervention with younger learners as it is with older learners” (Benati & Lee, 2008, p.174). As reported in Author (2016), English teachers in primary and secondary schools in Hong Kong have never heard of processing instruction, and their approach to teaching the simple past tend to be form-focused. Processing instruction, as found in this study and unanimously in previous studies, is an effective instructional intervention that teachers should be familiar with. To start with, teachers should understand the principles underlying L2 acquisition of English simple past: (a) the lexical preference principle; (b) the preference for nonredundancy principle; and (c) the sentence location principle. In acquiring English simple past, L2 learners tend to process lexical items as opposed to grammatical items when both encode the same semantic meaning. This means, for example, when vocabulary and verb endings compete to be noticed and processed in an utterance, the vocabulary will more likely win out. Among the grammatical items, L2 learners prefer to process non-redundant meaningful grammatical form than redundant meaningful ones. If meaning is already encoded lexically, then learners will not need to process a form. L2 learners also tend to process the items in the sentence initial position before those in the final position and those in the medial position. Thus, teachers should understand that simple past marker is a grammatical, redundant meaningful item and always located in the medial position, which poses great difficulty for Cantonese ESL learners.(objectives 3-4) Teachers should be aware that processing teaching materials must be informed by the nature of input processing, including the principles just outlined. The intervention must be purposefully designed to move learners away from inappropriate processing. While introducing structured-input activities, teachers should also observe strictly the guidelines developed by VanPatten & Sanz (1995): (a) presenting one thing at a time so that learners can map one form to one meaning more effectively; (b) keeping meaning in focus so that learners can extract meaning from the target form or structure in the structured input activities to facilitate form-meaning mapping; (c) moving from sentences to connected discourse; (d) using both oral and written input ; (e) requiring the learner to do something with the input such as agreeing/disagreeing; indicating true or false; likely or unlikely before making effective form-meaning connections; and (f) keeping the learner’s processing strategies in mind so as to help learners avoid using an ineffective processing strategy. Based on findings obtained in the study and those in the literature concerning the effectiveness of processing instruction, teachers are advised to develop language or grammar activities in a way that can help learners process input effectively, specifically learners should be able to process the target form or structure in the input to make effective form-meaning mapping. Research findings should not be limited to researchers, and the gap between SLA and L2 pedagogy should be bridged through collaboration between frontline teachers and SLA researchers. It is important for more teachers to understand how to select appropriate teaching approaches and why (and how) English teaching should be grounded more firmly on linguistic principles.(objectives 3-4)

540413.label: Major findings and research outcome
540413.value: Major findings: While the traditional form-focused approach has been condemned in the literature, findings of this study show that the traditional form-focused approach does not seem to be less effective when it comes to form production. Results of the study show that explicit instruction, specifically TI and PI, has an equal effect in helping learners produce the English simple past form in the production task. In the interpretation task, however, PI is most effective in helping learners map both the forms and meaning, in listening and reading, sentence-level and discourse-level interpretation tasks. PI as an effective means to help L2 learners map both forms and meaning should be introduced as early as in the primary level for primary students while traditional form-focused approach can also be employed as reinforcement. 540413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
540413.value: Built upon the contributions of this study, future studies could consider using eye-tracking experiments to determine what aspects of the structure learners focus their attention on during input processing. Treatment of a longer duration can also be arranged to examine if this may allow a more significant improvement in both learners’ interpretation and production of the target structure. In addition to interpretation and production tasks as always used in the literature, interview data is also crucial in revealing how learners perceive the different forms of classroom intervention and their effectiveness. More importantly, the potential of processing instruction is not limited to morpho-grammatical items. It can well be applied to different grammatical and lexical target structures so long as L2 learners use those underlying principles during acquisition that negatively affect their picking up of certain grammatical or lexical items. With heightened awareness, joint effort between researchers and teachers are encouraged to develop the potential of processing instruction in mapping forms and meaning in second language acquisition.

540413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
540413.value: This study investigates the role of classroom input in the acquisition of English simple past. Significance: 1. Of the two different types of explicit instruction examined, the findings confirm earlier work about the effectiveness of Processing Instruction (PI) in helping L2 learners interpret and produce simple past regardless of their L1. 2. This is also the first study which examined the role of listening/reading skill in addition to that of sentence/discourse-level in the interpretation of the simple past by L2 learners. Overall, the PI group outperformed the other groups in the post-test no matter in listening/reading and sentence-level/discourse-level tasks. 3. Traditional Instruction (TI), which is a kind of form-focused instruction adopted as pedagogical intervention in this study, is found to be quite useful in helping the TI group realize the form in the production task. 4. Teachers are advised to develop language or grammar activities in a way that can help learners process input effectively, specifically learners should be able to process the target form or structure in the input to make effective form-meaning mapping. As findings show that TI is as effective in promoting language production, we can first introduce input activities followed by output ones.

540813.label: Realisation of objectives
540813.value: Although the objectives of the project have been achieved by the end of December 2016, the project has encountered several difficulties which have been reported in 2014 and 2015 annual reports. Followings are the summary of the difficulties and the attempts to overcome them: (i) Research personnel recruitment Although the project starting date was 01 January 2014, different strategies have been used to recruit research personnel. It was until September 2014 that the staffing issue has started to be settled. Furthermore, 68 student assistants have been recruited to ensure the project had enough manpower for data collection. It is because most data collection could only be conducted during lunch hours (around 12:00 to 14:00). Those nursing homes were located in 3 territories of Hong Kong (i.e., Hong Kong island, Kowloon peninsula and New Territories) and covered 16 out of 18 regions. Majority of the nursing assistants were illiterate and the research personnel needed to read and go through the questionnaire on one-to-one basis. In addition, the health assessment should be conducted by 2 research personnel to ensure the accuracy. Owing to the limited availability of the research personnel, short duration for data collection in nursing homes, and illiteracy of nursing assistants, most nursing homes have to take 4 to 10 visits to complete one nursing home's data collection. Lastly, the availabilities of student assistants were uncertain because of their study schedules and tests. (ii) Nursing home recruitment We also encountered difficulty in recruiting nursing homes. Some nursing home in charges stated that they would like to participate in the study. But they did not have enough nursing assistants to work; thus they could not spare the time for them to participate in the research. Different strategies have been employed. First, a list of their contact information was downloaded from the Social Welfare Department website and invitation letters were sent by fax. Second, the officers in charge were contacted by phone or email through community health nurse networks who provide nursing care to residents in nursing homes. Third, the principal investigator promoted the study in a nursing home association, where some officers in charge met to discuss issues related to nursing homes. Fourth, the participating nursing homes referred other participants. During the data collection, we found that we could recruit more than 30 nursing homes which was proposed, sample size calculation was revised based on the consultation of statisticians. With an average cluster size of 10, a sample of 382 subjects with 40 nursing homes would be required to provide at least 80% statistical power to detect an effect size of 0.3. Considering the drop-out rate of 8%, the sample size of the study would be 415. 47 nursing homes with 516 nursing assistants have participated in the project and thus met the sample size requirement. (iii) Completion of project Due to the difficulties encountered (as explained in (i) and (ii) above), the project was about 10 months delayed. Thus, the project has applied 12-month extension. With the approval, it was completed on time on 31 December 2016.

540813.label: Major findings and research outcome
540813.value: 1. Qualitative results (refer to Part C, research output 1) Twenty-four nursing assistants (NAs) with work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs) working in four nursing homes participated in focus group interviews. Results showed that the synergistic effects of long work hours without sufficient rest, work even with musculoskeletal pain because of staff shortages, ineffective management with insufficient prework training and inadequate equipment maintenance, and an aging workforce with strong commitment to resident care played a crucial role in WMSDs among NAs. 2. Quantitative results (Partially refer to Part C, research output 2) A cluster randomized control trial (RCT) was conducted. 47 nursing homes with 440 NAs were randomised to either the multidimensional intervention (n=212) or the control arm (n=228). 2(a) Results of baseline data (refer to Part C, research output 2): Results showed that the adverse workstyle of “working through pain” was the predictor for WMSDs. 2(b) Results of RCT: Although 72 (34.0%) from the intervention and 67 (29.3%) from the control arms did not complete the whole assessment scheme, there was no significant difference in the dropout rates between the two groups. There were no significant differences between most of the demographics of the two groups at baseline, with small differences detected on the marital status and the level of physical exertion. This indicates that the randomisation was conducted properly. In this study, generalised linear modelling was employed to examine the effect of the intervention programme. Variables such as age of the NAs and type of nursing homes were also included as the covariates in the model. Results showed that the number of NAs with musculoskeletal symptoms in at least one body part differed statistically significantly before and immediately after intervention T1 (F = 5.40, p < 0.05). An increase in the level of knowledge and decrease in the level of perceived work stress and severity of WMSDs were also observed; however, no differences were found between the two groups. On the other hand, the effect of the programme on the prevalence of WMSDs also persisted across all the time points [T2 (3 months), T3 (6 months) and T4 (one year)] (F = 2.92, p < 0.05). Therefore, we can conclude that the multidimensional intervention programme targeting NAs was successful in decreasing the prevalence of their WMSDs, but its effect on other dimensions such as work stress, knowledge, and severity of WMSD was uncertain in this study.

540813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
540813.value: This project is one of the first studies in Chinese community to provide a multidimensional intervention programme targeting the occupational health of nursing assistants (NAs) working in nursing homes. Based on the study results, we can conclude that this multidimensional intervention programme targeting NAs was successful in decreasing their prevalence of work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs), but its effect on other dimensions such as work stress, knowledge, and severity of WMSDs was not detectable in this study. Further studies are recommended to examine and develop intervention elements to improve those dimensions. The results of qualitative focus group interviews indicated that there was a synergistic effect of personal and organizational factors on the development of WMSDs among NAs. This synergistic effect might lead to the development of the adverse workstyle of “working through pain”. These results should increase the awareness of the policy makers the severity of WMSDs among NAs. Appropriate resources should be allocated to improve the manpower issues and organizational facilities. In addition, this multidimensional programme can be promoted and integrated into nursing homes’ on-the-job training programmes. Furthermore, the effects of this multidimensional intervention programme are going to be reported in research papers in the future.

540813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
540813.value: Background It is well known that nursing assistants working in nursing homes are at risk of work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WMSDs). But limited studies have been conducted to develop and evaluate multidimensional training programmes to reduce WMSDs in this vulnerable group. Aim The aim of this research was to develop a multidimensional programme and evaluated its effectiveness in reducing musculoskeletal symptoms among nursing assistants working in nursing homes. Design A clustered randomized control trial was used. 47 nursing homes with 440 nursing assistants were recruited and randomised to either the multidimensional intervention or the control group. The intervention programme involved six elements: (i) 1- hour exercise training; (ii) 1-hour manual handling with ergonomic principles; (iii) 1-hour stress management with complaints handling; (iv) onsite observation and provide feedback on manual handling; (v) onsite observation and provide feedback on the use of assistive devices; and (vi) discussion with nursing home in charge about the improvement of work organization. Results The results found that the programme was effectively in reducing musculoskeletal symptoms among nursing assistants. Conclusion This study signifies the importance of multidimensional programme in reducing musculoskeletal symptoms among nursing assistants working in nursing home settings. This programme can be promoted and integrated into nursing homes' on-the-job training programme.

541213.label: Project Objectives
541213.value: To examine users’ meaning-making processes when engaging with interactive animated media objects, in connection with the various levels of understanding specified by the principle of material-based imagination (Chow and Harrell 2009, Chow and Harrell 2012). The outcome will serve as cross-reference to the interpretive analyses based on the principle. To evaluate users’ affective responses toward an interactive animated object, with reference to the temporal patterns of engagement as articulated in the notion of enduring interaction (Chow and Harrell 2011, Chow 2012). The outcome will serve as cross-reference to the theoretical underpinning of the notion. To formulate methods and build toolkits documenting users’ various levels of imaginative meaning construction and elaboration when interacting with an artifact. The outcome can be generalized as a research tool for investigating cognitive processes coupled with sensorimotor experience. To formulate methods and build toolkits reporting users’ feeling under different temporal conditions of bodily engagement with an artifact. The outcome can be generalized as a research tool for probing users’ emotional responses to a design.

541213.label: Realisation of objectives
541213.value: To study the imaginative and affective experiences of using interactive animated artifacts, we identified four existing exemplary products, most of which were selected from the corpus formed by the PI in his early book (Chow 2013), together with two newly designed artifacts. They included a mobile phone interface, a messaging web interface, an art-game, a home appliance, a recommendation system interface, and a tobacco control smart system interface. The actual products or interactive prototypes were prepared in the usability study room of our laboratory. Participants were invited to experience the use individually in a compressed period of time simulating a real-life use case scenario. During the experiment, each participant’s responses including facial expression, gestures, and bodily action were observed and documented. After the activity session, a semi-structured in-depth interview was conducted with each participant. Based on the PI and the Co-I’s early work including material-based imagination and enduring interaction, this study focuses on users’ cognitive processes at different levels, from perception, motor action, imagination, feeling, to interpretation and reflection, elicited by interactive animated artifacts during different moments of use (cf. Objective 1 & 2). The activity session was designed to let participants experience the use across different moments in hope of embodying different levels of understanding. The interview questions were also formulated to probe users’ immediate thoughts and feelings at the initial stage of use, which were mainly triggered by perception of familiar phenomena and quick feedback based on motor action, and then higher-level responses resulted at later stages of use, which were intriguingly prompted by curious, contingent changes. A protocol of cognitive processes with conceptual integration diagrams extended from Fauconnier and Turner (2002) was developed to structure and guide the interviews (cf. Objective 3 & 4). The activity session and interview for each participant was approximately two hours, taking place in the usability study room at our laboratory. Experiments were videotaped, interviews were recorded, and the conversations were transcribed as verbal data together with the observed bodily responses. These data were marked as cognitive phenomena, including perceived sensory cues for possible action, perceived feedback, familiar sensorimotor phenomena, immediate imagination and feeling, noticed contingent changes, frame-shifting for new interpretation, elaborated imagination and extended emotion, and reflection on different interpretations. Marked data were grouped into different possible imaginations, emotions, and interpretations elicited in users at different levels during different moments. Arranging these data with reference to researchers’ interpretive analyses informed a spectrum of possible outcomes enabled by each artifact at certain stage of use. For instance, the mobile phone interface featuring a descending water level provoked imagined or remembered scenarios related to leaking, time passing, counting to deadlines, or resource consumption. The last one was in line with the researchers’ initial interpretation and the designers’ intent, while the others were slightly diverted yet still sharing similar affective responses. These data spanned a spectrum, forming verisimilar narratives of the user experience of each interactive animated artifact with multiplicity. For the mobile phone interface, a simulated version was implemented on iOS, because the actual product was already discontinued by the time of this research. Twenty participants’ data were collected and analyzed. Results were partly in line with the PI’s initial interpretative analyses with unexpected insights discovered. For the messaging web interface and the art-game, the artifacts were still accessible by the time of the experiments and so directly used. Seventeen participants’ valid data were collected and analyzed. Results were partly in line with the PI’s initial interpretative analyses with unexpected insights discovered. For the home appliance, the actual product were bought and installed in the laboratory for the experiments. Six participants were initially invited, yet the results misaligned with the PI’s initial interpretive analyses and the designer’s intent, even with subsequent adjustments on the experiment design. Participants did not see the familiar phenomena at the immediate level, not to mention noticing contingent changes and taking to the higher cognitive levels. This was because the intended familiarity faded out in many participants’ minds with the changing home environment of today. The two new artifacts were designed according to the “liveliness” framework, which is built upon the PI’s early book (Chow 2013). A “lively” interactive artifact perceptually and mentally stimulates its user (i.e., material-based imagination) via embodied, emergent, and contingent behavior (i.e., enduring interaction). The notion has been further articulated with illustrative examples of lively interactive products in a conference paper (Chow 2014) (also refer to Part C 9.1). The recommendation system interface resembles a compass whose choices are distributed on various directions. The number of choices available in every step contingently changes, prompting the user to infer the reason behind them. The tobacco control system includes a smart physical case for its user to lock up the lighter like a monster in return for the avatar’s recovery. Yet, the avatar’s health status contingently changes too. For the compass-like recommendation system interface, an interactive prototype was used in the experiment. Sixteen participants were invited. Each participant first explored to turn with the compass, and then used it for different online activities, like preparing a shopping list. Interview data were collected and analyzed. Results were partly in line with the PI’s initial interpretative analyses with unexpected insights discovered. For the tobacco control system interface, an interactive prototype was used in the experiment. Six participants with different degrees of smoking habit were invited. Each participant was asked to lock up the lighter and run for a few minutes on a treadmill. They saw their avatars getting healthier initially, but then the status reverted once they unlocked the lighter. Interview data were collected and analyzed. Results were partly in line with the PI’s initial interpretative analyses with unexpected insights discovered. 541213.label: Major findings and research outcome
541213.value: For the mobile phone interface, interpretive analyses, the experiment, and the qualitative analyses of the data were published in a journal paper (Chow, et al. 2015) (also refer to Part C 8.1). The study of the messaging web interface, together with that of the mobile phone interface, was published in a conference paper (Chow 2015) (also refer to Part C 9.3). For the compass-like recommendation system interface, the study was published subsequently in a conference paper (Chow 2015) (also refer to Part C 9.2) and a journal paper (Chow 2016) (also refer to Part C 8.2) For the tobacco control system interface, the study was published in a conference paper (Chow 2015) (also refer to Part C 9.4). To sum up, this user experience study shows a kind of interactive animated artifact, as we named “lively”, whose operation evokes familiar, mundane sensorimotor phenomena, provokes emergent thoughts and feelings, prompts reflection via curious, contingent changes. The findings support the theoretical framework for the analysis, design, and evaluation of lively interactive artifacts. The framework informs the characteristics of liveliness, which is embodied, emergent, and contingent, and leads to embodied cognition-based methodology, which can be summarized in a protocol of cognitive processes and conceptual integration diagrams to sketch the cognitive operations, as a guideline for experience prototyping. Other researchers and designers can follow the methodology to investigate the possible user experiences of existing or developing interactive artifacts that are aimed at user reflection too.

541213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
541213.value: The research outcome supports the potentials of lively interactive artifacts in provoking emergent thoughts and feelings, which probably leads to user reflection. The reflection can be performed on one’s own behavior or habit (as in the case of the mobile phone interface, the recommendation system interface, and the tobacco control system interface), or on a social phenomenon (as in the case of the messaging web interface), or on a general life topic (as in the case of the art-game). All these are related to people’s mundane, everyday life, which is the center stage of today’s human-oriented design. Designing and deploying lively interactive artifacts for reflection will be a promising moderator for people’s everyday behavior and attitude. The PI has already started to work along this trajectory. One ongoing project is about designing intervention with liveliness for healthy mobile or screen media use. The other project is extending the compass-like recommendation system from the personal context to the public setting in order to broaden the variety of topics. Some preliminary studies and findings are informative and insightful for future research direction. The PI is preparing the next major research proposal of this.

541213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
541213.value: Our experiences are built upon everyday perception, action, imagination, and feeling, which may lead to further interpretation and reflection. As technology is integrated in our everyday lives, it continues to shape our experiences via many forms of designed artifacts, like mobile phones and smart products. Some of these artifacts present interfaces that resemble familiar, mundane experiences, like the digital camera featuring the sound of a mechanical shutter as functional feedback. More intriguingly designed artifacts show nuanced novelty within familiarity, in pursuit of non-utilitarian values like imagination and reflection in users. Yet, these dimensions are commonly seen as subjective to be evaluated. This research investigates the potential of interactive animated artifacts in eliciting imagination and emotion during use, from the perspectives of both researchers and users. Researchers’ interpretative analyses of a set of exemplary artifacts first inform the characteristics of potential artifacts, which help structure experiments conducted with participants on various existing or developing artifacts. Results show possible varied mental association among participants, researchers, and people at large. Researchers’ theoretically grounded projection of subjective user experiences can be combined with participants’ cases to form convincing narratives on the possible outcomes.

541413.label: Project Title(Chinese)
541413.value: 溫故知新：多角度剖析香港教育語文政策及其執行

541413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
541413.value: The emergence of English as the global lingua franca in the past twenty years has stimulated considerable scholarly interest in the various factors that have contributed to this historically unprecedented phenomenon. Standard accounts of this process posit two fundamental factors: the influence of British colonialism in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries and the dominance of the United States since the Second World War. While these accounts generally point to the centrality of American political, economic and cultural power in transforming the language’s global status, it could be argued (see Ostler, 2005) that the legacy of colonial rule is more significant because the English-oriented education systems established by the British in Asia and Africa have been instrumental in the ‘macro-acquisition’ (Brutt-Griffler, 2002) of English as a second language in the post-colonial era. The rapid expansion of English use in post-colonial societies in the past half-century helps to explain why one distinguished imperial historian regards English-medium education as the British Empire’s ‘most significant’ legacy (Brown, 1999). While imperial historians have curiously neglected to examine how and why such instruction evolved during the colonial era, these questions have inspired a substantial literature in the field of applied linguistics. One of the limitations of this work, be it from a critical ‘linguistic imperialism’ perspective (Phillipson, 1992) or from a supposedly ‘factual’ perspective (Crystal, 2003), is that it relies excessively on secondary sources rather than on data derived from systematic archival research. Noting this shortcoming, Sweeting and Vickers (2007) have called for the history of language in colonial education to be reconstructed from the bottom up through archival studies of policies and practices in particular contexts. In the case of Hong Kong, a number of studies of this nature have appeared since Sweeting and Vickers issued this call (Evans, 2008a, b, c), but as Bolton (2011: 56) points out, ‘only part of this project has been completed’ as these investigations deal only with the nineteenth century. The proposed study seeks to complete this project by examining the nature, purposes and consequences of colonial language policies and practices during a period (1902-1978) that is virtually uncharted in the literature. By bridging this gulf in the historical record, the study will provide the basis for the production of the ‘detailed historical narrative’ that Bolton (2011: 56) has identified as a research priority in the area of language-in-education policy in Hong Kong. 在過往二十年間，英語一躍而成為環球交際語的現象促使不少學者們探討構成這史無前例的現象的各種成因。這現象的基本的論述建基在兩個主要成因上：十九及二十世紀初英國殖民政策的影響及美國自二次大戰後處於主導世界事務的地位。在這兩個論述上，一般都認為美國在政治、經濟和文化領域上的主導地位促成了英語脫變為環球交際語，但不容否認，殖民地統治期間的承傳更俱影響力 (see Ostler, 2005)，因為從宏觀的語言掌握的角度來看 ，那一套由英國人在亞洲和非洲地區建立出來，以英語為主導的教育模式(Brutt-Griffler, 2002)，更能體現主導該地區的人仕在後殖民地時期吸納英語成為他們第二語言的學習過程。過往半世紀英語在外圈社會迅速膨脹的情況確有助解釋為何一位著名的帝國研究歷史學家認為，英帝國最俱影響力的承傳就是其所建立以英語為教學媒體的教育模式(Brown, 1999) 。正當研究帝國事務的歷史學家出奇地忽略了解釋有關語文政策的指令是怎樣和為何成形之際，這些問題喚起了在應用語言學上為數不少的查考工作。無論是從富批判性的〝語言帝國主義〞角度(Phillipson, 1992)或是從據稱以〝事實〞為依歸的角度(Crystal, 2003)來看，這些查考工作的一個不足之處就是它們大多倚重第二手資料作為參考的根據，而非由有系統的第一手檔案資料出發。有見及此，Sweeting and Vickers (2007) 認為應該要由檔案資料開始，透過了解某些語文政策的內容和其執行的情況，由底而上再重建殖民地教育的語文歷史。在香港，自Sweeting and Vickers的文章發表以後，一些性質相近的文章相繼就香港的情況面世(Evans, 1998a, b, c) ，但正如Bolton (2011:56) 指出，這重建工作〝只有部份的項目是完成了的〞，因為那些項目只限於十九世紀的部份而矣。本研究旨在完成上開的研究項目，希望透過探討1902至1978年間香港殖民地語文政策的本質、目的、成效和政策的執行，填補這時段裡查考上的空白。透過填補這時段的史料，本研究希望能提供素材以建立一個Bolton (2011:56) 所倡導首要建立的〝詳盡歷史陳述〞，以作為深入研究香港教育語文政策的基礎。

542013.label: Project Title(Chinese)
542013.value: 一種針對錶皮溶解水皰症的功能性服裝系統

542013.label: Co - Investigator(s)
542013.value: Dr Leung, HangMei Polly Prof Wong, Kwok-shing

542013.label: Project Objectives
542013.value: To identify the effects of proportion of Chitosan fibres and fabric structure parameters on fabric properties and establish a model for numerical simulation of skin–fabric interactions: friction and pressure. To conduct investigation of medical performance of proposed Chitosan fabric by tests on fluid drainage ability test, cytotoxicity test, skin-textile friction test, antibacterial test, wound healing activity (Animal testing). To design and fabricate the functional skin-protective apparel for both infant EB patients and young/adult EB patients in order to replace the traditional dressing and bandage and more importantly, provide protection with high level of comfort and convenience. To assess the proposed functional skin-protective apparel for clinical trial by collaborating with Tung Wah College of Tung Wah Group of Hospitals and Princess Margaret Hospital, to validate the proposed textile system.

542013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
542013.value: This study serves as a pilot study associating textile design with Epidermolysis Bullosa (ab.EB). In scholarly circles, study of EB mainly focuses on its causes and curing methods. Nevertheless, there is limited attention paid on the alleviation and prevention of the friction that may result in blister on a daily basis. This shows a need for developing daily basis caring methods and clothing for patients with EB. This study aims at developing a functional skin-protective textile system with maximum protective and wound healing activity functionality, high level of comfort and convenience that adopts advanced textile fabrication technology and fashion design skills to produce a collection of functional apparels for patients who suffer from EB. It is expected that the developed textile system will fill the multidisciplinary gaps and generate new knowledge in the form of high-quality journal papers in the field of medicine, personal protection, bioengineering, fashion design and fabrication. The findings will help the patients with EB, their family and medical personnel on a daily basis; to government, this system will not only be limited to alleviation of the inconvenience and pain brought by EB, but can contribute to the development of skin-protective textile, such as burn treatment; finally to the textile and apparel industry, the multi-functional skin-protective textile system brings a high-technology and high value-added products. 此研究是通過紡織品的特別設計從而幫助表皮溶解水皰症患者的日常治療和生活。在目前的學術研究中，表皮溶解水皰症的研究主要側重於其病症產生原因和醫治方法，而在日常患者護理方面和日常衣物的設計，研究甚少。例如，在日常生活中，表皮溶解水皰症患者常常因為服裝與皮膚的摩擦產生水泡，十分疼痛。所以，此項研究將針對這類問題，提出解決方案。此項研究的目的在於從紡織材料，結構和設計上的深入研究，為表皮溶解水皰症患者提供高度舒適方便的日常皮膚保護系統，並促進其傷口癒合。 這個研究的順利完成將填補多項學科的交叉空缺，產生新的知識領域，並可以在醫藥、個人防護、生物工程和設計製造領域發表高質量期刊論文。此項研究結果不僅可以在日常生活中幫助表皮溶解水皰症患者、患者家庭和相關醫護人員，減輕病症所引起的疼痛和不便，同時還可以向皮膚護理研究作出貢獻，例如燒傷治療。此外，此項研究還可以推動紡織品在醫用方面的發展，此項多功能皮膚保護紡織系統具有較高的技術含量和附加價值。

542013.label: Major findings and research outcome
542013.value: This project exploited triboelectric electrostatic theory to efficiently solve the existing spinning problem of chitosan fiber and establish the model of skin-fabric interactions. This technology can maximum the bio-function of chitosan fiber; strength its mechanical property; lower the production cost and provide more possibilities for production design in the end market. Based on this chitosan spinning technical breakthrough, the advantages of this biomaterial, such as wound-healing and antibacterial functions, in terms of structure capacities and layering system with properties will be not only be limited to alleviation of the inconvenience and pain brought by wound healing (EB), but can contribute to the development of skin-protective textile, such as burn treatment and decubitus. Finally, in this textile and apparel industry, multi-functional skin-protective textile system can bring up more high-tech and high added-value products. As aforementioned, this innovative spinning system contributes significantly to the medical field, especially through new product R&D, the caring for patients could be improved, and the daily caring of their family and medical personnel can be assisted as well .

542013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
542013.value: The properties of chitosan fiber were well analyzed, the unique bio-functions of chitosan material can be combined with the advantages of woven or knitted fabric in term of structure capacities and layering system with properties such as elasticity, sustainability (durable for laundering) and comfort. Thus, the application area of chitosan fiber can be broaden extremely, especially the medical industry.

542213.label: Project Title(Chinese)
542213.value: 家庭進食模式、親職方式及家庭功能對學前兒童的健康、行為及學習的角色

542213.label: Co - Investigator(s)
542213.value: Dr CHAN, Ruth Suk-mei Prof Lo, Sing Kai Dr Tsang, Sandra Kit Man

542213.label: Project Objectives
542213.value: To test a refined and expanded model of Olson and Defrain (2003) which integrates family functioning, parenting style and family dining pattern in a Chinese context. To identify the pivotal family functioning characteristics, parenting styles and family routines which influence key aspects of child development, including diet and weight status; psychosocial behaviour, as well as learning performance among Hong Kong Chinese preschool children. To identify the culture-specific and universal family and parenting factors which contribute to child health and development in physical, social and cognitive areas. To inform clinical practice and social service policy formulation on measures to promote child development and family well-being with research-based evidence.

542213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
542213.value: Health involves not just the absence of disease, but optimal physical, psychosocial and cognitive development. The early years have important influence on the child’s physical, psychosocial and cognitive development . Early childhood obesity is associated with adult obesity which is a significant health risk. Early conduct and learning problems are associated with adolescent delinquent behaviour and later learning problems. Prevention of early childhood obesity and conduct/learning problems are important public health issues. While western literature shows that family meal times are associated with children’s eating habits, weight, behaviour and learning, the existing results are mainly based on cross-sectional studies with longitudinal studies only conducted on adolescents. It is probable that these might be due to family functioning and parenting styles, which are known to be associated with child weight, eating habits, behaviour and cognitive development. However, there are no studies examining these factors (family dining pattern, parenting style and family functioning) on holistic child health (physical, psychosocial and cognitive) among Chinese children. This study is based on the model of Olson and Defrain (2003) which integrates parenting style and family functioning, but incorporates the pragmatic strategy of family dining as a family strategy for connection and context for communication, and use this revised model to examine health outcomes (physical, psychosocial and cognitive) among Chinese children. The present study adopts a holistic view of health incorporating physical, psychosocial and cognitive aspects. It employs a longitudinal design involving multiple informants and use of quantitative and qualitative data to map out the specific family features and parenting practices which influence child obesity, eating habits, psychosocial behaviour, cognitive skills and academic competence, and to test three competing hypotheses on the impact of family functioning, parenting style and family dining pattern on child outcomes. A representative group of preschool children and their parents will be recruited through multi-stage sampling in 18 districts of Hong Kong and they will be measured at three different time points, at K1, K2 and K3, using local questionnaires on child feeding practices, and other locally validated instruments with sound psychometric properties on family functioning, parenting styles, child behaviour and learning. Assessment includes reports from parents, teachers and individual assessment of children. The results will have significant implications for social, health and family policy and early childhood education professionals in terms of identification and development of strategies to promote child health and development in physical, psychosocial and cognitive aspects. 健康的定義不僅指沒有疾病,更包括體能、心理社交及智能都有最佳發展。學前時期的發展對兒童日後的體能、心理社交及智能發展十分重要。童年肥胖和成年肥胖有密切關係，而肥胖是一個嚴重的健康問題。童年的行為及學習問題亦與青少年犯罪及學習困難相關。及早預防童年肥胖、行為及學習問題是一個重要的公共衞生課題。西方文獻顯示家人共同進餐與兒童的飲食習慣、體重、行為和學習相關，但這些兒童研究大都是橫斷研究;而縱貫研究則多以青少年為主。以上發現(家人共同進餐與兒童的飲食習慣、體重、行為和學習相關)亦可能是基於親職方式及家庭功能，因這些因素都與兒童的飲食習慣、體重、行為和智能發展相關。現時並沒有探討家庭進食模式、親職方式及家庭功能對華裔兒童整體健康(體能、心理社交及智能)影響的研究。本研究設計以Olson及Defrain (2003)的模式為基礎，綜合親職方式及家庭功能，並額外加入「家庭共同進餐」作為促進家人關連及提供一個溝通的環境的實際元素，以這改良模式來探討華裔兒童的體能、心理社交及智能。本研究採用整體健康概念，包含體能、心理社交及智能方面，並使用縱貫設計，採納多個持分者資料，並搜集量性及質性數據去探討家庭特點及親職模式對兒童肥胖、飲食習慣、心理社交行為、認知能力及學習效能的影響，更測試三個有關家庭進食模式、親職方式及家庭功能對學前兒童健康影響同的假設。研究將從本港18區內以多階段方式抽樣選出學前兒童及家長作縱貫研究，透過使用本地兒童飲食調查問卷，及經過本地驗證、有良好心理測量性能的家庭功能、親職方式、兒童行為及學習量表，以及家長和老師的報告及學童測試報告收集研究數據。研究結果對識別及發展促進兒童體能、心理社交及智能健康的策略，社會、健康及家庭政策，以及學兒童教育專業人員有重大影響。

542213.label: Realisation of objectives
542213.value: Objective 1 was achieved. The expanded model of Olson and Defrain (2003) was tested in a longitudinal study involving 470 parent-child dyads. The model was tested using multilevel mediation modelling method. It demonstrated that parenting style was more closely associated with parenting practices such as frequency of mealtime television, while family functioning such as parental control was associated with family meal frequency. Family mealtime environment mediated between parenting style and child outcomes. Family mealtime environment, together with parenting style/family functioning, have important influences on child outcomes. Objective 2 was achieved. Authoritarian parenting negatively predicted child learning and positively predicted child behaviour problems whereas authoritative parenting positively predicted child learning and fruit consumption. Permissive parenting positively predicted child behaviour problems. Parental concern and parental control were also associated with child learning. More mealtime television viewing predicted poorer teacher rating of child learning; and higher frequency of mother dining with child predicted higher teacher and parent rating of child learning. Higher frequency of dining with grandparents was positively associated with meeting fruit consumption requirements but negatively associated with meeting vegetable consumption requirements. Family feeding practice was associated with children’s behaviour and their consumption of fruit and vegetables. Family feeding practice mediated between parenting style and children’s behavior. Objective 3 was achieved. Most of the research findings were consistent with the international literature, suggesting that parenting style, family functioning and family mealtime environment variables are associated with child outcomes in western and Asian cultures. The present findings also suggested that the role of father was less prominent in our sample of Chinese preschool children, and grandparents played a role in positively influencing fruit consumption and negatively influencing vegetable consumption. It was speculated that grandparents in Chinese societies tended to perceive food as an educational and emotional tool and to express their love and care through food. As a result, they preferred to buy and prepare meals based on the young children’s preference and placed few restrictions on the children’s food consumption, and young children often preferred fruit more than vegetables. Objective 4 was achieved. The study results have implications for clinical practice and social services, in terms of measures to support parents to promote the development of their children. Parent training should focus on authoritative parenting practices, and to encourage family meal frequency and healthy feeding practices among parents, in order to promote child development. At the same time, mealtime television should be discouraged.

542213.label: Major findings and research outcome
542213.value: Family mealtime environment variables were associated with child learning. More mealtime television viewing predicted poorer teacher rating of child learning; and higher frequency of mother dining with child predicted higher teacher and parent rating of child learning. Authoritative parenting style was associated with better child learning (Research output 2 and 3). Family feeding practice and parenting style were found to be associated with children’s behavior. Child behavior problems were positively associated with authoritarian and permissive parenting. Family feeding practice mediated between permissive parenting style and children’s problem behavior (Research output 2 and 3). Healthier feeding practices were associated with lower frequency of child behavior problems (Research output 2 and 3). Meeting vegetable recommendation was associated with lower frequency of dining with grandparents and positively associated with parents using more desirable parent feeding practices. Meeting fruit recommendation was associated with parents using more desirable parent feeding practices, higher frequency of dining with grandparents, lower frequency of dining with father and higher score on authoritative parenting style (Research output 2 and 3). Family feeding practices mediated the effect of permissive parenting style on child behavior problems. Parenting style was more closely associated with parenting practices such as frequency of mealtime television, while family functioning such as parental control was associated with family meal frequency (Research output 1). The present study informs clinical practice and social policy formulation. For parent education, in addition to supporting parents to develop authoritative parenting strategies, very concrete and easy-to-achieve practices such as dining more with children and enjoying each other in television-off mealtime should be introduced. It also has implications for family friendly policies to support parents to spend time with their children and have family meals together (Research output 4).

542213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
542213.value: Issues such as family routines and rituals which are broader than feeding practice, and other external factors that might have influenced the outcome variables should be further investigated. The views of both fathers and mothers should also be included to shed more light on the influence of family mealtime environment on child outcomes. Lastly, the association between neglectful parenting and mealtime television and child outcomes should be examined. The findings can potentially influence the development of parent training programs to include more emphasis on family dining environment.

542213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
542213.value: Family dining environment has important influence on child development. Less mealtime television and higher frequency of family meals have positive influences on child learning. Healthy eating practices are related to better child behavior and fruit and vegetable consumption. Authoritative parenting style facilitates fruit consumption and child learning. Authoritarian and permissive parenting leads to poorer child learning and more child behavior problems. The findings are important for parents, psychologists, teachers, social workers and health professionals. Strategies and programs should be developed to support parents to practice authoritative parenting style and healthy feeding practices. Parents should be encouraged to dine with their children and family friendly policies should be in place to support parents to spend time with their children. Last but not the least, mealtime television should be discouraged, and parents should make use of family mealtime to communicate with their children.

542413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
542413.value: Under the growing threat of environmental degradation caused by rapid industrial growth in the past three decades, industrial pollution control has become an urgent regulatory task in China. Yet many polluting enterprises are still at the threshold of minimum compliance or even non-compliance. Thus, increasing scholarly attention has been devoted to examining factors that are conducive to corporate compliance with environmental regulations. Compliance is a process through which regulated industrial enterprises abide by environmental laws and regulations. In the current literature, there is still a lack of systematic understanding of how China’s evolving regulatory settings have affected enterprises’ approaches to regulatory compliance. The proposed research seeks to perform a longitudinal and comparative study of corporate compliance styles (CCS) in China. Specifically, it will answer the following four research questions: (1) In what ways do enterprises vary in their regulatory compliance styles? (2) In what ways do enterprise-level and industry-level characteristics—such as corporate green commitment, ownership, type of industry, and connections to international buyers—affect enterprises’ compliance styles? (3) Given the evolving regulatory environment, have there been systematic shifts in compliance styles among enterprises? (4) Do regional variations in regulatory and political contexts affect enterprises’ compliance styles? These questions will be addressed by conducting questionnaire surveys and semi-structured interviews with executives of industrial plants in Guangzhou, Chengdu, and Dalian. The study will build on our earlier study on corporate compliance in the Pearl River Delta Region and environmental regulatory enforcement in Guangzhou, Chengdu, and Dalian. New data collected in the proposed research, together with data collected in previous research projects, will allow us to study (a) variations in CCS over time in the Pearl River Delta Region and (b) how regional differences in regulatory and political environments affect CCS. By drawing on new and current data on CCS and data on regulatory approaches (collected earlier in the three cites of Guangzhou, Chengdu, and Dalian), the proposed research will provide insights into the complex connections between regulatory enforcement and regulatory compliance styles. 中国在过去三十年工业迅速的增长所引起日益严重的环境恶化的威胁下，工业污染控制已成为一个紧迫的监管任务。然而，许多污染企业仍处于遵守的最低门槛或甚至不遵守。因此，越来越多学者致力于研究有利于企业遵守环保法规的因素。合规性是工业企业遵守环保法律和法规的过程。在目前的文献中，对中国不断变改种的监管情景如何影响企业的遵守法规仍然缺乏有系统的了解。 建议中的研究旨在对中国进行追踪和比较研究。具体来说，它会回答以下四个 研究的问题： （1）企业在哪些方面表现出不同的企业合规的风格？ （2）在什么样的方式企业层面和工业界别层面的特性 – 例如企业绿色承诺，所有制，行业类型，以及与国际买家的联系 –影响着企业的合规风格？ （3）鉴于不断变化的监管环境，企业之间的合规风格有否作出有系统的转变？ （4）区域监管和政治环境的差异有否影响企业的合规风格？ 这个研究会通过对在广州，成都及大连的工业企业的高层管理人员所开展的问卷调查和半去回答这些问题。这项研究将我们先前在珠三角企业合规及环保执法研究的基础上进行。在这个建议研究中所新收集的数据，再加上前期的研究项目已收集的数据，我们可以研究（一）在珠江三角洲地区企业合规风格随着时间推移的变化，及（二）区域监管及政治环境的差异如何影响企业合规风格。通过利用企业合规风格新的和现有的数据上及执法方式的数据（先前在广州，成都和大连三个城市收集的），建议中的研究将会对与监管执法和遵守法规的风格之间的复杂关联提供深入的见解。

542413.label: Realisation of objectives
542413.value: In the process of implementing this research project, we administered questionnaire surveys to enterprise management and interviewed management executives in Tianjin (replacement of Dalian), Chengdu and Guangzhou, between 2015 and 2017. Data was collected from manufacturing enterprises in the three selected cities to perform a comparative analysis of corporate compliance styles in response to environmental regulation. The survey in Guangzhou also allows us to conduct a longitudinal analysis by comparing it with the previous data collected in the Pearl River Delta (PRD) region. An analysis of these data allows us to identify various types of corporate compliance styles (Objective 1) and explore what are the organizational and industrial level factors that explain the co-existence of multiple compliance styles (Objectives 2 and 3). Combining the survey and interview data collected from manufacturing enterprises, we were also able to examine the role of regulatory uncertainty and resource availability in co-shaping the adoption of various compliance styles (Objective 4). Moreover, a cross-city analysis could be conducted to enable a comparison of corporate compliance styles across three economically advanced municipalities of China (Objective 5). Based on these analyses, we can identify and develop strategies to help both enterprises and policy-makers to promote environmental regulatory compliance (Objective 6). As this longitudinal and comparative study is built on our exploratory studies conducted in the Pearl River Delta Region earlier in 2010-2012, we used the same sets of questionnaire and interview questions for data collection in individual locations. To increase the reliability of the survey, we asked both a management executive and the environmental managers of each enterprise to complete the questionnaire. To prevent mono-method bias, we supplemented the survey with interviews of a selection of management executives and environmental managers from 8-10 enterprises in each locality. This mixed-method approach, which combined quantitative and quality research methods in a single study, helps to enhance the credibility of data analyses by allowing the triangulation of findings. The enterprise survey implementation went smoothly as we planned. During 2016-2017, three independent surveys were implemented in Guangzhou, Chengdu, and Tianjin, respectively. In Tianjin and Guangzhou, we were able to receive responses from 200 manufacturing enterprises; each includes two questionnaires completed by a top executive and an environmental manager. The survey in Chengdu achieved a sample size of 150 enterprises, each of which received two completed questionnaires. Interview data collection in Chengdu and Guangzhou were completed on schedule, in early 2017 and the following summer, respectively. In both cities, we were able to arrange interviews with 12 manufacturing enterprises. The interviews with enterprise management in Tianjin took longer to arrange. We planned five interviews in November 2017, when there is serious smog pollution in northern China. Production activities in many of the local enterprises, especially those polluting ones, are temporally suspended. During the first few interviews, we perceived that most respondents were reluctant to speak on the sensitive topic of pollution control. To assure the interview quality, we decided to postpone the rest until our collaborator finds good timing to proceed. Based on the data collected, we were able to publish four papers on corporate environmental management among manufacturing enterprises in Guangzhou and the Pearl River Delta. The first paper, entitled “Stakeholder demands and corporate environmental coping strategies in China”, came out in a 2016 issue of the Journal of Environmental Management, conceptualizes four-dimensional classification of coping strategies –formalism, accommodation, referencing, and self-determination (Objective 1), and examines how stakeholder demand and compliance capacity jointly shape these corporate environmental coping strategies and subsequently environmental protection practices (Objectives 2 & 3). The second paper, entitled “Political Commitment, Policy Ambiguity, and Corporate Environmental Practices”, appeared in a 2018 issue of the Policy Studies Journal – a top-ranked journal in public policy research – examine how regulatory factors are related to basic and proactive corporate environmental management practices in the Pearl River Delta region in China (Objectives 3 & 4). The third paper, entitled “Policy Uncertainty and Corporate Performance in Government-Sponsored Voluntary Environmental Programs”, which appeared in the Journal of Environmental Management in 2018, examine corporate compliance performance in implementing a government-sponsored voluntary environmental program (VEP) during 2004-2012 in Guangzhou, China (Objectives 2 & 3). The fourth paper, entitled “Regulatory Ties and Corporate Compliance Strategies”, which appeared in the Public Performance & Management Review in 2019, explores how regulatory ties and firm visibility shape formalism and self-determination, two distinct corporate coping strategies for complying with environmental regulatory demands (Objective 4). All four articles have important implications for both business managers and policy-makers to promote regulatory compliance (Objective 6). Since the recent completion of data collection, we have started to work on the survey data sets and compiled the interview records. The preliminary results of cross-city analyses are encouraging, indicating variations among manufacturing enterprises in terms of coping strategies towards environmental regulation, perceived institutional and stakeholder pressures, as well as internal compliance motivations and barriers to comply or go beyond compliance (Objectives 1-3). The interview data supplements the quantitative data in two ways: it resonates the survey data by showing fruitful jurisdictional variances on the examined issues; it also enriches the quantitative data analysis by revealing more dynamics and details to help interpret the survey findings, especially those less expected ones (Objectives 4 & 5). Taken together, we are confident that findings from this project have promising implications for both policy makers and business managers in environmental governance (Objective 6). To achieve this target, more rigorous data analysis with a focus on cross-city comparison will be conducted in the next few months to ensure that the results are robust and the findings reliable. We expect two to three papers to be prepared in this process for possible conference presentations and journal submissions next year (Objectives 3, 4 & 5). In the completing stages of this project, we would like to raise that doing environmental research in China is always full of political risks and uncertainties, leaving researchers without much control over the research plan and the working schedule. We hope that the UGC and its members will be considerate and appreciate our diligent efforts in achieving the originally planned objective. We are glad to have been able to complete the questionnaire surveys and interviews of management executives in three locations, albeit having replaced Dalian with Tianjin and behind schedule. Finally, we are confident that we can produce further impactful research outputs out of these data collected in the years to come.

542413.label: Major findings and research outcome
542413.value: In the process of conducting field research in the respective locations, we have leveraged on the new data collected in this project to strengthen the analyses of data collected in earlier studies. As a result, four journal papers and a few conference presentations have been conducted (put down in the progress report). The first major finding relates to the existence of multi-dimensional corporate coping strategies in environmental compliance. Drawing on survey and interview data collected from manufacturing enterprises in China between 2010 and 2012, we show that corporate environmental coping strategies can be characterized along four dimensions – formalism, accommodation, referencing, and self-determination. Enterprises adjust their coping strategies by taking into account the constraints defined by both their internal and external environments. The results also demonstrate the potential synergetic effects of state and non-state stakeholders working together in promoting better corporate environmental coping strategies and environmental practices in China. While internal compliance capacity is needed to pursue each dimension, different alignments of internal capacity and external demands affect a firm's coping strategies. Particularly, an enterprise tends to score higher on the accommodation, referencing, and self-determination dimensions when it faces stronger demands from both state and non-state stakeholders. Yet only two of the four dimensions – referencing and self-determination – are associated with stronger environmental protection practices. Compared with formalism and accommodation, coping strategies of referencing and self-determination are associated with stronger environmental protection practices. The second major finding addresses the effects of the institutional context of policy implementation on corporate regulatory compliance. We found that perception of clear political commitment to environmental protection across multiple government levels and units is positively associated with business efforts in basic environmental practices, regardless of the specific enforcement intensity. Nevertheless, a perception of clear political commitment is not related to proactive environmental practices. Conversely, a perception of policy ambiguity, in the form of confusing regulatory standards and enforcement, is negatively associated with corporate efforts in both basic and proactive environmental practices; yet, intensive inspections mitigate these negative associations with policy ambiguity. The third major finding emerges from our particular focus on differentiating between formalism and self-determination, two distinct corporate coping strategies for complying with environmental regulatory demands. Our empirical results show a U-shaped relationship between firms’ regulatory ties and their strict adherence to formal rules (formalism), and an inverted U-shaped relationship between regulatory ties and firm discrepancy in complying with regulations (self-determination). Further, the inverted U-shaped relationship is stronger among firms with less organizational and environmental visibility. The additional analysis further indicates that these relationships are particularly evident in privately owned enterprises. Our study may contribute to the public performance literature by furthering our understanding of regulatory ties as a double-edged sword in corporate compliance. The last major finding is based on our preliminary cross-city analyses. At this stage, the survey findings show significant regional variations in local manufacturing enterprises’ coping strategies with environmental regulation and their perceived institutional environment. At the same time, the ultimate performance of surveyed enterprises also strongly differs across cities, as potentially explained by local regulatory stringency and the investigated organizational factors.

542413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
542413.value: By building on our earlier studies on corporate compliance styles in the Pearl River Delta Region, our project has conducted a cross-city analysis of corporate environmental management in China. Adopting a mixed-research design, we collected a fruitful set of empirical data for in-depth analysis to answer questions relating to changes and variations in corporate compliance styles among manufacturing enterprises in China’s dynamic and diversified institutional setting. We explored whether regional variations in regulatory, political, and cultural contexts affect corporate coping strategies. Given the proven academic contributions of this study, as demonstrated by the papers published in top-ranked public policy and environmental studies journals, it is strongly desirable to conduct future research in various directions. In responding to a call for investigating organizational responses to institutional pressures as an evolving process, we may analyze overtime changes of corporate environmental coping strategy at the industrial level and extend our current framework and develop a typology of coping strategies formed by a combination of coping strategy dimensions. Also, we can apply the overall framework to a wide array of domains where businesses are subject to government regulations, such as those related to labor, workplace health and safety, and product safety. Learning from other policy settings could add theoretical insights for further developing the theoretical model in different environmental regulation contexts.

542413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
542413.value: This longitudinal and comparative study examines the dynamics of corporate compliance with pollution control among manufacturing enterprises in the industrial sector. It has produced important findings on deeper understanding of corporate compliance strategies in confronting external regulatory pressure. The concept of corporate compliance styles, consisting of formalism, accommodation, referencing, and self-determination, have helped to capture the behavioral diversity of business firms in reacting to increasingly institutional demands and their strategic stances in dealing with environmental protection issue. Such behavioral diversity is shaped by interwoven regulatory forces and societal expectations, as well as managerial capacity and readiness. We have refined our theoretical framework to disentangle these various forces that co-shape corporate compliance styles and explore the potential interactions among them. Our study has particularly focused on the role of perceived regulatory certainty and firm capacity in determining the coping strategy in the Chinese context. On the whole, our longitudinal analysis shown that practices that demand deeper integration of environmental concerns into an enterprises’ operation (e.g., ISO14001) were significantly related to demands from the enterprise’s peers (e.g., industrial association) , while the survey findings have highlighted significant regional variations in local manufacturing enterprises’ coping strategies with environmental regulation and their perceived institutional environment.

544013.label: Project Objectives
544013.value: To compile a one million word corpus of listed companies’ corporate governance reports representative of the Hong Kong financial services sector. These reports will be drawn from a representative cross-section of listed companies in Hong Kong which in turn reflect the major sectors of the Hong Kong economy. To annotate the discourse move types of each text in the corpus following the top-down corpus-based method devised by Biber et al. (2007a). This will enable a computer-mediated analysis of the sequencing of the moves and the frequencies of their occurrence. To conduct a collaborative project, which involves the researcher and professional practitioners working together to decide issues such as the representativeness and balance of the corpus contents, the appropriacy of the analytical framework, and the interpretation of the results. Findings from the project will be shared with professionals through, for example, Continuing Professional Development Seminars jointly hosted by professional bodies and the Research Centre for Professional Communication in English of the Hong Kong Polytechnic University. To analyse the specialised corpus by adopting a top-down corpus-based approach to identify and analyse discourse organisation, i.e. the moves in discourse (Biber, Connor and Upton, 2007a, 2007b; Csomay, 2007). The analysis will include the sequencing of the moves and the identification of obligatory and optional moves. To apply a top-down corpus-based approach to the entire corpus. The analyses will include the identification of key words and key phraseologies (including phraseologies which exhibit variation). To combine both quantitative and qualitative approaches to discourse studies in order to thoroughly investigate the internal discourse structure, language and intertextuality, particularly how individual moves express specific communicative functions by means of certain lexico-grammatical, and intertextual choices, and how these contribute to the overall communicative purposes of the genre. To describe the patterns of discourse organisation, lexico-grammar, and intertextuality in the genre, and to investigate the variation in these patterns. This will be done across texts within the genre and across moves in the whole corpus. The findings will be reported initially at international conferences and then submitted to international journals and edited collections.
