544013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
544013.value: The proposed project aims to compile and analyse a specialised corpus comprised of a relatively new genre: corporate governance reports. ‘Corporate governance’ is defined as “the system by which business corporations are directed and controlled.” (Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development 2008). The corpus would be a one-million-word collection of corporate governance reports. The contents of the corpus would be collected from the annual reports of companies listed in Hong Kong. The corpus will be used to describe the patterns of discourse organisation, lexico-grammar,and intertextuality in the genre, and investigate empirically the variation in these patterns both across moves within the genre and across the corpus as a whole. Corporate governance reports have become a requirement for listed companies in Hong Kong and elsewhere in the wake of massive failures in corporate governance, such as those which led to the collapse of Enron in 2001 and WorldCom in 2002, and, more recently, the money-laundering scandal involving HSBC in 2012. In Hong Kong, listed companies are now required by the Hong Kong Stock Exchange to submit interim semi-annual and annual corporate governance reports, and make these reports available on their websites. 本項目研究企業管治報告的語體特徵及詞匯語法。企業管治是指管理及控制公司的一套制度。過往有一些大型企業相繼出現企業管治問題，甚至造成公司倒閉，例如2001年的安隆公司(Enron)和2002年的世通公司(WorldCom)倒閉及匯豐銀行於2012年涉及洗黑錢的醜聞。自此，香港交易所規定在香港上市的公司須發怖中期及年度企業管治報告，並公怖於公司網站內。 企業管治報告是一較新的語體，本研究從香港上市公司年報內收集企業管治報告，制成一個專門用途語料庫, 約為一百萬字，分析企業管治報告的篇章結構、詞匯語法、及語體的互文性，並探討這些特徵於語體不同語步中的差異。

544013.label: Realisation of objectives
544013.value: 1) The one million word corpus, The Hong Kong Corpus of Corporate Governance Reports (HKCCGR) has been compiled. The reports have been collected from 217 companies listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange and are a representative cross-section of the major sectors of the Hong Kong economy. This corpus is available online with a user-friendly interface which allows users to search the corpus for words and phrases. 2) Each of the 217 corporate governance reports has been analysed qualitatively to identify the moves contained within it and the sequencing of the moves. In addition, the steps found within each move have been identified along with their sequence. The moves and steps have then been collated into sub-corpora. These sub-corpora are also available online with the same user friendly interface as that used for the main corpus. 3) The project has been collaborative in nature with the two co-investigators in advisory roles with regard to corpus collection and confirmation of major findings. The corpora are housed on the website of the Research Centre for Professional Communication in English (http://rcpce.engl.polyu.edu.hk/index.html) and Continuing Professional Development Seminars have been held (March and September, 2015) with the Hong Kong Institute for Certified Public Accountants to introduce the HKCCGR and its sub-corpora and how it might be utilised in professional contexts. 4) The qualitative analysis of the 217 corporate governance reports has led to the identification of both the prototypical sequencing of the moves, and of the steps within each move, and to the identification of the obligatory and optional moves and steps. The reasons for these prototypical features of corporate governance reports have been discussed in conference papers and are to be covered in detail in the research monograph to be published by PalgraveMacmillan. 5) Using the corpus linguistics software, ConcGram, which is the product of an earlier GRF project led by the currelt Principal Investigator, the key words and phraseologies in the HKCCGR and its sub-corpora have been identified and are discussed at length in the research monograph to be published by Palgrave Macmillan. Importantly, the key phraseologies are not simply comprised of fixed phraseologies. The ConcGram software specialises in finding all of the phraseologies (from two words up to five words irrespective of constituency or positional variation. This then means that the description and discussion of the key phraseologies is much fuller than if only fixed clusters of words were examined. 6) The combination of both qualitative and quantitative methodologies has allowed a very thorough and detailed description of the corporate governance report genre. The ways in which the internal discourse structure, language and intertextuality, particularly how individual moves express specific communicative functions by means of certain lexico-grammatical, and intertextual choices, and how these contribute to the overall communicative purposes of the genre are detailed and discussed at length in the research monograph currently under preparation and which is to be published by John Benjamins. In particular, the ways in which key phraseologies are linked to points of intertextuality are described and discussed. 7) The final objective is to arrive at detailed descriptions of the patterns of discourse organisation, lexico-grammar, and intertextuality in the corporate governance report genre and variations in these patterns. This project's significance owes much to the fact that studying variation rather then simply focusing of fixed patterns is foregrounded throughout the study. The research monograph in preparation for the publisher John Benjamins is where these patterns are explore in depth.

544013.label: Major findings and research outcome
544013.value: Work has been completed on the analysis of the one million word corpus, the Hong Kong Corpus of Corporate Governance Reports. This is the largest specialised corps of corporate governance reports currently in existence and has been made freely available online. Conference papers have been presented describing the structure of the reports (i.e. both the obligatory and optional moves and the steps found within these moves). and the key phraseologies found in the moves of the reports. Theanalysis of the lists of key phraseologies in the 23 sub-corpora and the 30 step sub-corpora has been completed and two research monograhs are in preparation to fully describe and discuss the findings and their implications. It was decided that research monographs are the best platform to fully and coherently describe the internal discourse structure, language and intertextuality, particularly how individual moves express specific communicative functions by means of certain lexico-grammatical, and intertextual choices. One monograph (to be published by PalgraveMacmillan) will describe and discuss the structure and key phraseologies and corporate governance reports. The other monograph ( to be published by Benjamins) will examine the theoretical implications of the findings and issues related to lexico-grammatical and intertextual choices. William Lee, the full-time PhD student whose PhD studentship is funded in part by the project has presented a number of conference papers related to his PhD study,

544013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
544013.value: The corpora are accessible via a user-friendly interface on the internet and so they have the potential to be interrogated and studied by others in the field. They can can also be an invaluable learning and teaching resource. The methodology adopted in this study could be replicated or adapted by others in the field to analyse genres and their associated phraseologies. Several students in the English Department at PolyU are currently using the corpora in their MA and Doctoral studies.

544013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
544013.value: The completed project has studied a relatively new genre, corporate governance reports, It has done this by collecting the reports 217 listed companies in Hong Kong and creating a one million word corpus of the reports. The reports were then examined individually to identify the moves in each report, and the steps within each move. Sub-corpora were then compiled of each move and each step found in the 217 reports. The structure of the reports was then described and discussed. All of the corpora were then analysed in terms of the phraseologies associated with the main corpus and all of the sub-corpora. Finally, the ways in which individual moves express specific communicative functions by means of certain lexico-grammatical, and intertextual choices were identified and discussed.

544213.label: Project Title(Chinese)
544213.value: 香港新競爭法：執法策略與優次行業或行為：對比分析

544213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
544213.value: This project seeks to create a reasoned and evidence-based report to assist the newly established Hong Kong Competition Commission with (1) determining the strategic objectives of the new competition Ordinance and (2) adopting an enforcement strategy to achieve the identified objectives. Hong Kong has recently enacted its first general competition law and the process of appointing the members of the Competition Commission is ongoing. Once the Commission is established its first task will be to consider the legislative intent of the Ordinance to determine its enforcement strategy and enforcement priorities. Many other competition agencies world-wide have faced these issues previously. These agencies and key international organizations have developed principles to enhance the effectiveness of enforcement subject to the constraints of the political economy environment, the legislative framework and the resources available. Working from the legislative intention manifested in Legislative Council debates, the role of competition advocacy, education, the enhancement of corporate compliance programs, and the prosecution of infractions are all aspects of the overall enforcement strategy, and the Commission will have to decide how to prioritize the use of these various tools. Enforcement strategy and priorities of the public agency will be particularly important in Hong Kong as the legislation does not provide for stand-alone private rights of action, with private enforcement being restricted to actions that “follow on” from successful public enforcement. Thus, identifying the purpose of the legislation and tailoring an effective enforcement policy is a vital task if the new Commission is to leverage the maximum benefit to the Hong Kong economy from the new legislation. The project will firstly review the academic literature, publications from national and international competition agencies to identify the legislative intentions of Australia and Singapore with regard to their competition regimes. Secondly, we will then identify and analyse their enforcement strategies. Thirdly, we will then compare the enforcement strategies of the two jurisdictions and attempt to assess their successes and failures. Both are recognised as two successful regional jurisdictions that have significant similarities with Hong Kong and may provide some useful precedents for the Hong Kong Competition Commission to consider when devising its own unique approach. A draft report containing findings and recommendations will be presented to stakeholders in Hong Kong for deliberation and the final revised report will be submitted to the Commission for its consideration. Additionally, at least one academic paper will be published in an academic competition law journal. 本研究項目旨在編撰一份理據清晰審慎的報告，以協助新成立的香港競爭事務委員會(1)釐定新通過《競爭條例》的策略目標，以及(2)採納達到上述目標的執法策略。 近期香港正式通過首項通用的競爭法，並正招聘競爭事務委員會成員。委員會成立後，其首項工作是考慮《競爭條例》的立法原意，以決定執法策略和優先次序。世界各地不少競爭事務機構也曾面對同類問題。這些機構和主要國際組織均已確立一些原則，藉以在政經環境、立法框架及現有資源的約束下，提高執法的效能。 按照立法會辯論所顯示的立法原意，整體執法策略涵蓋各個方面，包括倡導公平競爭的價值、教育、促進企業遵守法例，以及檢控違法個案，委員會須決定採用該等不同工具的優先次序。 在香港，公共機構的執法策略和工作優先次序尤其重要，因為法例並沒有賦予獨立的私人訴訟權，私人執行僅限於公共執法成功後的「跟進」行動。因此，新成立的委員會其中一項重要工作，是識別立法的目的，並按特定需求制定有效的執法政策，使香港的經濟可從新通過的競爭法例中獲取最大裨益。 本研究項目首先回顧學術文獻、全國性和國際競爭事務機構發表的刊物，以識別澳洲和新加坡競爭法的立法原意。第二，識別和分析該兩國的執法策略。第三，比較該兩個司法管轄區的執法策略，嘗試評鑑他們成功和失敗之處。該兩國與香港的情況極為相似，而且均獲讚賞為成功執行競爭法的地區，可為香港的競爭事務委員會提供有用的先例，從而設計出適合香港的獨有執行方針。 報告草案載述研究結果和建議，將交由香港的持份者商議，經修訂後的最終報告將遞交委員會審議。此外，也會在競爭法學術期刊發表至少一篇學術論文。

544413.label: Project Title(Chinese)
544413.value: 咨询专家作为知识中介:以香港及中国内地酒店与旅游业为案例的研究

544413.label: Project Objectives
544413.value: To identify the role models and typologies of consultants as knowledge brokers in the hotel and tourism industries To describe consulting as a strategy of knowledge transfer in hotel and tourism management
rows: To identify the role models and typologies of consultants as knowledge brokers in the hotel and tourism industries
To describe consulting as a strategy of knowledge transfer in hotel and tourism management

544413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
544413.value: Consultants play a unique role as knowledge brokers in a scientific community. In an accelerating demand for knowledge-based practices, consulting has not only turned into a flourishing profession, it has also served as an effective strategy for academic researchers to demonstrate practical implications of their work, for example, through spreading innovative ideas, and promoting the use of scientific research for industry, policy and development practices in their respective fields. In our prior studies on using research for industry practices (Xiao & Smith, 2007), professional communication (Xiao & Smith, 2010) and capacity-building of a scientific community (Xiao, 2011), we have highlighted the need for, and urgency of, looking into the role of consultants (both academic consultants and professional ones) in fostering knowledge-based practices in the hotel and tourism industries. Notably, as Druckman (2000a, p.1565, 2000b) alerts, “social scientist as consultant is a relatively new development; there are few consultant role models, few source books on the craft of research consulting, and virtually no courses on consulting offered in academic social science departments”. This study aims to explore and understand the roles and typologies of both academic and professional consultants in the hotel and tourism industries. Theoretically, the undertaking is to be contextualized in, and hopes to contribute to, sociologies of knowledge in pertinence to diffusions of innovation, knowledge transfer, scientific community, and communities of learning and practice. Practically, results of the study will help better understand consultant-client relationships, and eventually shed light on promoting knowledge-based practices in the planning, development, and management of hotel and tourism in Hong Kong and mainland China. Notably, this study does NOT intend to evaluate any consulting projects (either ongoing or completed). Rather, its data collection is to be completed through in-depth key informant interviews with both academic and professional consultants and their clients in the tourism and hotel industries in Hong Kong and mainland China. By focusing on issues relating to the nature and ethics of consulting as a strategy of knowledge transfer, its content and constituents, its processes and outcomes, the roles of consultants, their relationships with clients, and their contributions to diffusions of innovation and promotion of ideas for knowledge-based practices, this proposed endeavor will have achieved its objectives of identifying and describing the knowledge brokering roles and typologies of consultants in the hotel and tourism industries through refereed journal publications and conference communications. 在科学共同体中，科技咨询起着重要的知识中介作用。在日益崇尚以知识为基础的实践热潮之下，科技咨询因此成为了一种热门的职业，也成了学界向业界展示其科学研究实用价值的一种有效手段。 在我们前期开展的关于运用知识指导旅游行业实践、旅游专业知识传播、以及旅游科学共同体容量建设等课题的研究中，我们发现并提出，对旅游与酒店业科技咨询作为知识中介这一课题开展深入研究的重要性与紧迫性。正如 Druckman (2000a, p.1565, 2000b) 所言，“社会科学研究者作为咨询专家还是一种相对新近出现的现象，还很少有现成的科技咨询模式，也没有蓝本教材，在高等院校的社会科学学科/学系，更没有这类课程或专业”。 本课题的研究，旨在探索与了解，在旅游与酒店业中，科技咨询专家的类型/类别及其作用。从理论上说，本课题的研究，将主要在知识社会学的语境中展开，旨在增加对“创新思想扩散”、“知识转移”、“科学共同体”、“知行合一”等理论与概念的深入认识。其实践意义主要在于，增进对“咨询专家与客户”之间关系的深入了解与认识，并以此达到在香港及中国内地酒店与旅游发展中，推广以知识为基础的“最佳实践”之目的。 本课题拟以质性研究的方法，通过对在香港及中国内地酒店与旅游业中开展科技咨询的专家及其客户进行深入访谈，来获取课题研究所需要之信息，并在此基础上，对研究数据进行分析、解说与整理。课题的研究成果，将以学术期刊论文以及学术会议论文的形式出现。

544413.label: Realisation of objectives
544413.value: This research was conducted in the theoretical contexts of knowledge brokering and scientific communities, or the sociology of knowledge more broadly. The roles of consultants as knowledge brokers in spreading innovative ideas, and promoting the use of scientific research for industry, policy and development practices were investigated in the field of tourism and hospitality. The stated objectives of this project are two-fold: One, to identify the role models and typologies of consultants as knowledge brokers in the hotel and tourism industries, and two, to describe consulting as a strategy of knowledge transfer in hotel and tourism management. Through literature research, and in-depth interviews with hospitality and tourism consultants and clients in China, the stated objectives of the project have been fully achieved. Two refereed journal articles have been published out of this project. One paper reports on tacit knowledge spillover through academic consultants getting involved in field research in a regional tourism planning and development context in South China, whereas another offers a review and critique on this subject with a future research agenda for China tourism studies. Results of the project were also communicated through a conference presentation to the respective applied research community. In addition to theoretical implications highlighted in the agenda paper, results of the study have practical implications for policy makers and practitioners to understand the roles of consultants, the nature and ethics of consulting as a strategy of knowledge transfer, its content and constituents, processes and outcomes, consultant-client relationships, and the contributions of consulting to diffusions of innovation and promotion of ideas for knowledge-based practices. In terms of interdisciplinary potentials or questions for the future, a number of challenges could be noted. First, the organizational and/or political culture within which knowledge brokering through consultancy is to occur. Notably, this could influence the array or scope of consultant activities, and, in inter-disciplinary terms, studies into this realm could be well carried over into the political lobbying field, as the researcher at this point is likely to reach the blurring zones of decisions about where knowledge activities and associated costs are located within a tourism organization. Second, another potential challenge to this line of inquiry is where tourism academics take on the role of consultants in bidding/tendering for research projects. This is of significance for the public/private boundaries of information flows, and of implications for how, why and by whom consultants are used in tourism organizations. The third challenge is the changing/changed role of universities and their ceaseless calls for "community service", which could be seen as a function of academic entrepreneurialism and capitalism. Under the notion of public interest groups, while many institutions still have strong interest in public research, financial and political pressures may well render much of the career/service requirement of academics into monetary return for their institutions, which in a way is attestable from the recent establishment of “applied research institutes or development research institutes” in many top-tier research-intensive universities in China. Overall, the completion of this project adds to our understanding of consultants as knowledge brokers in the tourism and hospitality field, and contributes to the body of knowledge generally known as "scientific communities".

544413.label: Major findings and research outcome
544413.value: The prominence of tourism and hospitality as a field of research and practice has resulted in a proliferation of its planning, development and marketing consultancies. Contextualized within sociologies of knowledge (or scientific communities in particular), this project probes into the roles of consultants as knowledge brokers in terms of spreading innovative ideas, and promoting the use of scientific research for industry, policy and development practices with instances from the tourism and hospitality industries. Based on literature research and interviews with consultants and clients in tourism and hospitality, this study typologizes academic and professional consultants in terms of their focus, commitments, career path as well as their affinity with (or closeness to) the academy, governments, or the industry in hospitality and tourism research and practice. Notably, the consultant typologies are inclusive of government consultants (that is, entities affiliated with a government tourism office or extension units such as a think tank), academic consultants (those affiliated with an academic institution with varying levels of/commitments to consultancies), and professional consultants. Accordingly, clients could also be seen in the same light in the brokerage scenarios in tourism policy, planning and development consultancies. By project purpose, power relations, and consultant-client interactions during the process, the dualistic typology is of public-sector clients (government departments that commission a consulting project or outsource a counseling service) and private-sector clients (organizations or business entities relying on or capitalizing on professional consulting services). The study finds that consultancies in tourism and hospitality are characteristic of industry-specific contents and constituents, processes and outcomes, and consultant-client relationships. As a deliverable part of the outcome, two refereed journal articles were published. One documents academic consultants in the field of regional tourism planning and development, and the other presents a critical review and agenda for future China tourism research on this subject. A conference communication was also developed out of this project. Overall, the study sheds light on consultant roles and typologies, and contributes to the understanding of consultancy as a knowledge brokering strategy in tourism and hospitality.

In research and practice, consultants and their clients can be typologically described in terms of their focus, commitments, career path as well as their affinity with (or closeness to) the academy, governments, or the industry. The study sheds light on consultant roles and typologies, and contributes to the understanding of consultancy as a knowledge brokering strategy in tourism and hospitality.

544613.label: Project Title(Chinese)
544613.value: 全球化中的中國農村：大豆危機和日常影響

544613.label: Project Objectives
544613.value: This project aims to produce a book-length study about the far-reaching impact of the agrarian globalization on China’s rural transformation. The case of the soybean crisis is both distinctive on its own and indicative of a general trend of China’s growing food trade. Our project will examine both the severe challenges the crisis has presented for the sannong and the strategies that have been devised and experimented with. From this case, we will draw out experiences and lessons related to China’s agrarian development in globalization. The project will also shed light on the dynamics of multiple-level social responses and interventions in this case of a “crisis.” The soybean crisis has produced chain effects on communities of producers, county and provincial agrarian development planners, soybean processing plants, consumers, researchers, etc. These actors bring their own interests and perspectives to the soybean crisis, which altogether cannot be assumed to be congruent. The dynamics and effectiveness of these multiple interventions, therefore, need serious examination. We will also bring to the fore rural producers’ understanding and perspectives on globalization. Anthropological and sociological studies on China and globalization have mainly focused on the urban and industrial settings. With a few exceptions (Zhang and Wang 2011; Chan, Madeson and Unger 2009) , the small handful of studies on globalization that involve rural China have been about the effects of globalization as a mediated discourse (Lozada Jr. 2006; Wesoky 2007), often about rural-to-urban migrants (Guang 2003; Pun 2005; Yan 2008 ). In recent years, linkages between rural China and globalization have gone beyond the cultural and discursive dimension and have gained a new dimension of political economy that directly affects rural producers and their livelihood. By studying the case of soybean production and trade, our study seeks to advance the theorization of the global food system and provide a grounded examination of the issue of food security in the national and global context.

544613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
544613.value: Rural China has been facing three inter-related issues regarding rural communities(農村), agriculture(農業) and rural producers(農民), known as the sannong problem(三農問題). The sannong problem is understood as a serious enough challenge for China’s development prospect that the Chinese central government has made it the subject of its first policy decree of the year for nine consecutive years (2004-2012). So far scholarship and policy formulations on the sannong have only placed it within the national context of development. However, since China’s WTO entry in 2001, rural China has been increasingly linked with globalization. China became a net food importer in 2003. China’s food trade grew at 24% per year during 2005-2010. This situation calls for a new conceptualization of the sannong problem in the context of globalization. The proposed project will study the impact of agrarian globalization on rural China by examining the soybean crisis. Soybean has been a traditional Chinese crop. China had been a net exporter of soybean until 1995. Today China is the world’s largest soybean importer, sourcing nearly 80% of the soybean it consumes from the global market. In the meanwhile, squeezed by the massive, cheaper, genetically-modified soybeans from overseas, Chinese soybean growers have found it very difficult to sustain their production. Traditional soybean is losing ground. In this situation -- termed a Chinese soybean crisis -- Chinese small producers are confronted with an unprecedented challenge from the agro-business-dominated global food system. We propose to study how the impact of and responses to the soybean crisis shape the process of rural transformation and rural producers’ perspectives on globalization and the WTO. Following soybean as a social-economic-cultural object, we will conduct field research in Beijing and Heilongjiang, a province prominent for its soybean production, and examine local and national actors and their interventions in the soybean crisis. These include rural producers (individuals and cooperatives), village cadres, soybean processing plants, governments at county, provincial and national levels, China Soybean Industry Association, and opinion makers -- activist writers and researchers who contribute to the public discourse of the soybean crisis. We will integrate ethnography of rural transformation, discourse analysis of the soybean crisis, and political economy of China’s implication in the global food system. This study will contribute to our understanding of rural China in agrarian globalization, advance the theorization of the global food system, and have policy implications for the sannong, sustainable development and national and global food security. 中國面臨著相互關聯的農村、農民、農業問題，或稱“三農”問題。 為體現三農問題對中國整體發展的重要性，中央政府連續十年（2004-2013）就三農問題發佈“中央一號文件”。到目前為止，人們主要在中國國情的框架裡對三農問題給予學術上和政策宣導上的關注。但是自中國2001年正式加入世界貿易組織以後，中國農村和農業與全球化的聯繫不斷深化。中國在2003年成為糧食淨進口國。2005-2010年以來，中國的糧食貿易每年增長24%。這種狀況需要我們在全球化的框架下審視三農問題。本課題計畫通過研究大豆危機來考察全球化對中國農村的影響。 大豆是中國的傳統作物。1995年以前中國都是大豆的淨出口國。現在中國是世界最大的大豆進口國，中國市場80%左右的大豆源自於進口。由於受到大量、廉價、轉基因大豆進口的擠壓，近年來，傳統的大豆的種植面積連年萎縮，中國的豆農越來越難以維持他們的生產和生計，這一情形被人們稱作“大豆危機”。在這個危機中，中國的小生產者遭遇了前所未有的、來自大資本主導的國際糧食體系的挑戰。 大豆是承載社會、經濟、文化價值的作物，我們的研究也追隨大豆的這些多重意義。本課題計畫研究大豆危機的衝擊和對此衝擊的回應如何改變著中國的農村的生產和生活，以及人們對世界貿易組織的看法。在研究方法上，本課題將結合農村社會學、話語分析、以及世界糧食體系的政治經濟學。

Self-Assessment: In the main, the project has achieved its objectives. In the first place, a great amount of data has been gathered at various field sites, allowing for in-depth analysis of the relationship between agrarian transformation and food security in China. While the project focuses on the soybean crisis in Northeast China, we take a broader perspective on food safety and security that goes beyond the local and even the national context. The quantity and quality of data acquired is such that the remaining tasks mainly involve fulfilling our program of publications and presentation in a variety of venues of our research findings, as well as consolidation of our contacts to create a further agenda for study of China’s rural transformation. As with all complex projects, particularly those heavily relying on generating data through fieldwork, obstacles arise preventing the full realization of the objectives within the project period. Nevertheless, each of the four objectives have substantially been met. To the extent that some publication objectives remain unfulfilled, it is because attainment of the comprehensive data-set became possible only recently. The full utilization of the data to generate further publication, especially a monograph, can now be accomplished. It is expected that the objectives will be fully met in the post-grant period. Our research has a social impact on two levels. We now participate in efforts of scholars/activists in think tanks and NGOs. The PI is now a member of the International Panel of Experts on Sustainable Food Systems (http://www.ipes-food.org/members), a think tank led by Olivier de Schutter, former United Nations Special Rapporteur on the Right to Food and is on the International Advisory Board of the Journal of Peasant Studies, the leading journal that engages scholarly analysis of agrarian change and social movements. We have also stimulated discussion among grass-roots producers and consumers in China about alternative modes of agricultural production and consumption through creating mechanisms for intensive interchanges between academics and local producers and consumers.

544613.label: Major findings and research outcome
544613.value: 1. In the political discourse, food security (in Chinese called “liangshi anquan”, literally grain security) is a fungible concept undergoing liberalization. On the one hand, the Chinese government still asserts 95% self-sufficiency as a baseline for food security, upholding a pledge made in a 1990’s white paper about food security. However, unlike in the 1990s, the Chinese government has also narrowed the categories of “grains” that must reach 95% self-sufficiency, to the exclusion of soybeans. The narrowing of what is “secured” by policy intervention is at the same time a liberalization of food security, because food security is now less anchored on self-sufficiency, but more oriented towards market access through global trade. In our article on the soybean crisis, we examined this important shift and its implications. 2. There exists a contradiction between the national policy of food security and local-level governments’ orientation to GDP growth. Overall, food basket provinces have lower GDP rankings in China, which creates a disincentive for these provinces to contribute to national food security. Heilongjiang officials joke with chagrin that Heilongjiang is China’s Africa. Tensions exist between GDP as the measure, the telos of development and “food security” as a form of public good (the traditional saying is “min yi shi wei tian” 民以食为天). 3. As local governments are motivated to promote GDP growth, they are incentivized to support capitalist dynamics in agrarian production. This in turn has resulted in scaling up and capitalization of agrarian production and made it increasingly difficult for small farmers to sustain their production. We have discussed these contradictions and dynamics in our articles about the transition of Chinese agriculture to agrarian capitalism. 4. An astounding growth in soybean imports and the changing politics of food security have had remarkable consequences for food safety and have provoked intense reactions from both producers and consumers. Alternative food production-consumption networks and mutual aid groups are emerging, some entailing localized new social formations. We discussed these new practices in our book chapter on green social work and in the PI’s article about a newly organized ecological village in rural Guizhou. 5. Agrarian decline has provoked a new attempt by the Chinese government under President Xi for a “rural revitalization” to reach a larger goal of “ecological civilization.” Its practical implications for food security/safety are yet to be observed.

544613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
544613.value: As stated above, it is our finding that multiple contradictions exist that will impinge on the future of agrarian change and food security in China. If this project has focused on the impact of soybean imports on agrarian change in China, it is expected that with the growing liberalization of “food security” in China, agrarian dynamics will be increasingly linked with Chinese agribusiness investment globally. Soybean production and trade is one key issue in the very recent US-China trade war. It will likely result in the Chinese government making efforts to rebalance its position in the global food system. The Chinese government may especially diversify its sources of imports of soybeans to Belt & Road countries, particularly those in Central Asia and Africa. How this dynamic will impact food production and agrarian transformation in China and the global food system awaits a close examination. The PI and Prof. Barry Sautman at HKUST have already submitted a GRF proposal to further investigate the many implications of Chinese agro-business expansion in Africa.

544613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
544613.value: Using the soybean crisis as a case, we investigates contradictions and implications in defining and treating “food” in China. A legacy of food security exists that values self-sufficiency as a condition for national development, but it is increasingly mixed with new dynamics that include growing agribusiness within and outside China, as well as volatile international relations. When pressured by massive soybean imports from North/South America, Chinese farmers have to switch from familiar soybean to less familiar maize. Local governments, facing failing local soybeans, promote maize and use this opportunity to scale-up production by all means, including by attracting agribusiness to maize production. Chinese consumers react to genetically modified soybean imports with great angst and popular concern for food safety stimulates food activism and creation of alternative food networks. The value of this project is to examine positions, contradictions and debates about the relationship between food production and consumption and China’s position in the global food system. We also proposes sustainable food policies. Will the current US-China trade war offer an opportunity to re-examine China’s strategy on food security? Will recent Chinese government promotion of “rural revitalization” and “ecological civilization” have implications for food security/safety? These are questions awaiting further study.

548713.label: Project Title(Chinese)
548713.value: 企業內部資本市場有效性和內部信息質量

548713.label: Co - Investigator(s)
548713.value: Dr Chen, Peter F Dr Zhang, Ivy Xiying

548713.label: Project Objectives
548713.value: To provide initial evidence for the role of accounting information in the resource allocation function of internal capital markets. To investigate the effect of specific internal information problems, as indicated by different types of internal control weaknesses, on the efficiency of internal capital allocation. To investigate how the interaction between internal accounting information and external investment opportunity signals affects the efficiency of internal capital allocation.
rows: To provide initial evidence for the role of accounting information in the resource allocation function of internal capital markets.
To investigate the effect of specific internal information problems, as indicated by different types of internal control weaknesses, on the efficiency of internal capital allocation.
To investigate how the interaction between internal accounting information and external investment opportunity signals affects the efficiency of internal capital allocation.

548713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
548713.value: This project aims to provide initial evidence for the impact of internal accounting information quality on the efficiency of internal capital markets. The efficiency of internal capital markets refers to the effectiveness of internal capital markets in allocating capital to good investment projects and thereby improving firm value. Anecdotal evidence (e.g., Bower, 1970) suggests that there exists severe information asymmetry within internal capital markets and more specifically between corporate headquarters and divisional managers. Such information asymmetry, coupled with divisional managers’ rent-seeking incentives, may give rise to agency problems and distort the capital allocation decisions in internal capital markets (e.g., Harris and Raviv, 1998; Scharfstein and Stein, 2000; Rajan, Servaes, and Zingales, 2000). We predict that high-quality internal accounting information helps to alleviate the information asymmetry in internal capital markets, thus improving the efficiency of internal capital allocation. To measure a firm’s internal capital market efficiency, we follow Rajan, Servaes, and Zingales (2000) and use measures that are based on the investment-weighted average of divisional investment opportunity. To measure internal information quality, we use the internal control quality on financial reporting as mandated by the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX). Although internal control quality as defined under the SOX measures the quality of external financial reporting system, it also serves as a proxy for the quality of internal accounting system as firms typically use the same accounting system for both external and internal reporting (Zimmerman, 2000). The internal control system acts as a part of the soft infrastructure that governs the information-generating process for both external and internal reporting. Furthermore, the SOX-mandated internal control assessment emphasizes specific control designs and procedures (for example, segregation of duties) instead of focusing on the ex post accuracy of externally reported accounting numbers. Therefore, the internal control assessment is also indicative of the integrity of the internal management accounting system and the quality of accounting information used for internal decision-making. Both internal capital markets, which exist within conglomerate firms and business groups, and external capital markets, which include external equity markets and debt markets, play important roles in the resource allocation of a modern economy. By providing the first empirical evidence for the impact of internal accounting information quality on the efficiency of internal capital markets, we provide rare insights into the functioning of internal capital markets.

549013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
549013.value: We propose to contrast the usefulness of the two income statement classification schemes, by nature or by function, in facilitating earnings forecasting. Both U.S. GAAP and IFRS in the U.K. allow firms to use either by-nature or by-function classification scheme. However, IFRS requires firms to provide additional disclosure on the nature of expenditures when they choose the by-function scheme (IAS1). Revenues and expenses can be classified by nature (e.g. revenue, labor costs, depreciation, and utilities) and presented in a single-step format, or by function (e.g. sales, cost of goods sold, operating expenses and non-operating expenses) and presented in a multiple-step format. Each classification scheme has its advantages and disadvantages. For example, for the by-function classification, users may better predict next period’s expenses if the expenses related to continuing operations and related to discontinued operations are disclosed separately; however, for the by-nature classification, users may not be able to assess the continuation of an expense (e.g. labor costs) if part of the expense is related to discontinued operations. On the other hand, the by-function classification may be less reliable because the distribution of expenditure by function involves subjective judgment. Moreover, managers may opportunistically shift revenue and expenses around to overstate earnings from core activities. There are ample studies on the usefulness of by-function earnings components; however, no studies contrast the usefulness of these two schemes. We will first contrast the usefulness of these two schemes for a sample of US and UK firms in earnings predictability (e.g. earnings forecast accuracy). We will then evaluate if the additional requirement by IFRS for by-function scheme users (IAS1) generates a superior performance for the UK sample relative to their US counterparts. Recent anecdotal evidence of SEC pursued cases on misclassifications of income statement items also highlight the inherent problems of the by-function scheme. Therefore our study has important implication to the capital market participants and accounting policy making. 我們建議對比兩個利潤表方式，按性質或按功能，在盈利預測能力之差異。英國國際財務報告準則和美國公認會計準則允許企業使用性質或功能利潤表。然而，當企業選擇按功能利潤表, 國際財務報告準則要求企業提供額外按性質的披露。 收入和支出可以按性質分類, 即單步格式,例如收入，勞動力成本，折舊和水電費; 或按功能, 即多步格式, 如銷售，已售商品成本，經營開支及非經營開支。每個分類方案都有其優點和缺點。例如，通過功能分類，用戶可以更好地預測下一期的費用如果有關持續經營業務及已終止經營業務相關的開支被披露分開;然而，由性質分類，用戶可能不能夠評估延續部分的費用支出（如勞動成本） ，如果有關已終止經營。另一方面，按功能分類，支出按功能的分佈可能是不可靠的，因為涉及到主觀判斷。此外，管理者機會主義行為會誇大核心業務的盈利。 有充足的研究顯示按功能利潤表中盈餘組成的用處，但是，沒有研究對比按性質或按功能這兩個的實用性差異。首先，我們將對比美國和英國公司的盈利可預見性（如盈利預測的準確度）。然後，我們會評估，英國樣本選擇按功能利潤表的企業，相對於他們的美國同行, 是否優越。 近期有關SEC追尋企業利潤表項目的誤判的傳聞證據，也突出了按功能方案的固有問題。因此，我們的研究對資本市場參與者和會計政策制定具有重要的意義。

549313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
549313.value: 電子社交網絡工具——比如Facebook和Twitter——已經改變了全球的政治生態和社會準則。與此同時，社交媒體和網絡亦廣為商界所用。社交商務泛指通過社交媒體和網絡進行的電子商務活動。在這項研究中，我們將探討社交商務的採用對產品/服務質量，銷售增長，以及企業盈利的影響。社交商務的採納定義為企業正式推出支持社交互動和用戶貢獻的社交媒體技術，以協助產品和服務的採購和銷售。我們將進一步分析公司類型（服務與製造相比）和產品特性（搜索型與經驗型產品相比，技術密集型與非技術密集型產品相比），因其可能影響社交商務對企業運營和表現的作用。

549313.label: Realisation of objectives
549313.value: The project objectives have been achieved appropriately. First, we investigated the impacts of adopting social media in organizations on various firm performance indicators such as operational efficiency, innovativeness, stock returns, and profitability. Moreover, we examined how such impacts are moderated by different factors such as firm types, product characteristics, and stakeholder characteristics. Finally, we adopted and integrated different theoretical perspectives such as resource-based view, opportunity-motivation-ability framework, and social capital theory to explain our empirical findings. We overcame some difficulties to achieve these objectives. First, it is not easy to quantify the adoption of social media across a large number of firms over years. We overcame this difficulty by collecting firms’ announcements of social media adoptions via Factiva, a database containing news articles from top media outlets such as The Wall Street Journal, The New York Times, as well as hundreds of other sources. As collecting data from Factiva was a labor-intensive task due to the huge amount of information it contains, we recruited 12 student assistants to carry out this task. We also further verified our measure of firms’ social media initiatives with data from other sources. We also collected data from different sources to measure other variables. For example, we measured operational efficiency based on Stochastic Frontier Estimation (SFE) of the accounting data collected from Compustat, innovativeness based on the innovation ratings published by Fortune magazine, stock returns based on Fama-French-Carhart’s four-factor model, and firm profitability based on return on assets. An important concern about the relationship between social media adoption and firm performance is the possibility of endogeneity. In particular, it is possible that social media adoption and firm performance co-determine each other. On the one hand, firms’ social media initiatives may affect their performance. On the other hand, firms’ performance may also affect their decisions to adopt social media, leading to the possibility of two-way causality. Therefore, without taking this possible reverse causation into account, the impact of social media initiatives on performance could be overstated. Another potential source of endogeneity is the unobservable firm-specific heterogeneity. In other words, some unobservable factors may affect firms’ use of social media and organizational performance simultaneously, making the relationships between social media initiatives and these organizational outcomes biased. We addressed this endogeneity concern by employing the generalized method of moments (GMM) estimator to analyse our data and to obtain consistent results. While this estimator employs the instrumental variables techniques to deal with the endogeneity issue, it does not rely on external variables that are outside the immediate dataset to construct instruments. Instead, this estimator constructs instruments internally with the transformation of existing variables, overcoming the difficulty in obtaining exogenous instruments externally.

549313.label: Major findings and research outcome
549313.value: By collecting and combining longitudinal data from multiple sources, we obtained some interesting findings in this research, First, we found that firms’ social media initiatives have positive impacts on their operational efficiency and innovativeness, showing the ability of social media to make firms more efficient and innovative. This finding is consistent with our resource-based view, which considers firms’ social media initiatives as strategic resources for operational improvement. This interesting finding is published in Journal of Operations Management (The impact of firms’ social media initiatives on operational efficiency and innovativeness, Journal of Operations Management, Volumes 47–48, Pages 28-43). Moreover, we found that the social media initiatives-firm innovativeness relationship is moderated by stakeholder characteristics such that the impact of social media initiatives on firm innovativeness is more positive for firms with more geographically diversified stakeholders and better stakeholder relationships. This finding is in line with our social capital perspective that emphasizes the importance of social media to leverage the social capital of stakeholders to improve innovativeness. Our paper documenting this finding is currently under review in R&D Management (Social Media Initiatives and Firm Innovativeness: The Roles of Stakeholder Geographic Diversity and Relationship, R&D Management, Under review). Finally, we found that while firms’ social media investments increase stock returns and firm profitability, such increases are more positive for firms having better reputations and selling experience and technology-intensive products. This finding reveals the role of firm types and product characteristics in moderating the returns on social media investments and is consistent with our integrative perspective that combines resource-based view and opportunity-motivation-ability framework. Our paper documenting this finding is currently under review in Information & Management (Should Firms Invest in Social Commerce? An Integrative Perspective, Information & Management, Under review after second revision).

549313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
549313.value: This research represents one of the earliest research investigating the performance impacts of adopting social media in organizations and demonstrates a great potential for further development of this research direction. For example, future research can further explore the performance impacts beyond the firm-level analysis such as how adopting social media in organizations might affect individual employees’ productivity and individual customers’ satisfaction. On the other hand, while our research reveals various factors such as firm types and product characteristics that moderate the performance impacts of social media initiatives, future research can further explore some possible factors that mediate the social media initiatives-firm performance relationships, thus advancing our understanding of the mechanisms under which social media initiatives affecting firm performance. Finally, the novel theoretical perspectives adopted in our research can provide an important theoretical foundation for future research on firms’ social media initiatives.

549313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
549313.value: Moving beyond personal communications and individual interactions, social media have been increasingly used by firms for various commercial purposes, but it is not clear whether and when firms can benefit from the use of social media. Our research helps address this important question by providing an empirical investigation on the performance impacts of firms’ social media initiatives. Analysing longitudinal data collected from multiple sources, we found that firms’ social media initiatives have a positive impact on their performance in terms of operational efficiency, innovativeness, stock returns, and profitability. We also found that firms reap more benefits from their social media initiatives when they have higher reputation, sell experience and technology-intensive products, have more geographically diversified stakeholders, and have better stakeholder relationships. Moreover, our research provided novel theoretical explanations of the empirical findings by integrating different theories such as resource-based view, opportunity-motivation-ability framework, and social capital perspective. Overall, our research documents the importance of social media for commercial purposes and advances our understanding of the impact of social media on firm performance.

549513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
549513.value: 1995 年以来，在世贸组织谈判之后中国等许多发展中国家改革了其关于专利和其他形式的知识产权 (知识产权) 的法律。知识产权的日益受到关注是因为它们通过其对技术转让的影响对经济发展和贸易产生潜在影响。以前的研究发现专利改革会减少模仿等非正式技术转让方式，但会增加技术许可和外国直接投资 (FDI)等正式技术转让方式。 然而，在发展中国家，不同生产力的公司可能会对专利改革做出不同的反应，因为他们有可能选择不同的技术转移渠道。此外，对技术转让渠道的选择会进一步加剧他们在生产力上的的差异。因此，一个有趣的研究问题是发展中国家的专利改革如何影响技术转让渠道，出口和企业的生产力。 虽然以前的文献已经考虑了企业的生产力差异在贸易自由化中的角色，其在专利改革中的角色尚未加以探讨。我们的研究将填补这一空白。我们会把传统的企业的生产力差异理论（Melitz，2003年）和企业如何吸收国际技术的内生选择结合起来。这些选择反过来会影响哪些企业成为出口商。更强的专利保护有可能改变一些公司对不同的技术转让渠道的选择，从而可能改变他们的生产力及出口的可能性。此外，通过考虑选择不同技术转让渠道的企业可能面临不同的信贷约束，我们还将建立专利改革和信贷约束的联系。，我们进一步将构建中国企业的丰富的面板数据集，并开展实证估计来测试我们的理论预测。 我们的研究贡献在于以下几个方面。第一，据我们所知，这是第一个将专利改革，企业生产力会和企业对技术转让渠道的选择结合起来的研究。第二，它将提供深入了解专利改革推动生产力的转变发生的渠道。第三，这是第一个将专利改革和和不同企业信贷成本之间联系起来的研究。第四，通过结合各种来源的数据，研究将使我们能够量化中国专利改革对技术转让和出口的影响。最后我们的研究有重要的政策影响。他们将阐明专利改革如何以促进国内结构转型和工业增长。

549513.label: Realisation of objectives
549513.value: The first objective “To shed light on how patent reform in developing countries affects firms’ sorting pattern” has been fully achieved. Firm heterogeneity has been widely used to analyze trade liberalization effects. However, its role in the presence of variable IPRs enforcement has yet to be explored. We fill this gap by combining a standard theory of heterogeneous firms (Melitz, 2003) with the endogenous choices firms make to adopt international technologies. In this setting firms face different exit and export cutoff productivities than in the standard framework, leading to a richer sorting mechanism. By developing a theoretical model, we find that before patent reforms in equilibrium firms may be sorted into four groups. The least productive firms exit; the low-productivity firms choose imitation and only serve the domestic market; the medium-productivity firms imitate and sell at home but also export; and the most productive firms purchase technology from foreign firms and serve both the domestic and foreign markets. With patent reform, we have the following theoretical predictions. First, stronger IPRs increase the exit cutoff, implying that less productive firms are more likely to shut down. Second, stronger enforcement also reduces the export cutoff, meaning that a margin of strictly domestic firms are more likely to start exporting. Third, more rigorous enforcement reduces the cutoff for formal technology transfer, which implies that more firms shift from informal learning (i.e., imitation) to market-based technology acquisition. Finally, this shift toward formal TT in locations with stronger IPRs enforcement leads to enhanced productivity gains. We carry out empirical tests using Chinese firms’ experience during a period of both legal reforms and greater judicial enforcement, taking advantage of differences in the latter across provinces. The evidence consistently supports the hypotheses derived from the theory. The second objective “To investigate how patent reform in developing countries affects the channel of technology transfer” has been achieved. Stronger patent protection changes some firms’ decisions on TT channels, altering their productivities and export possibilities. Proposition 2 predicts that an exogenous increase in IPRs protection will reduce the cutoff productivity for purchasing technology from foreign firms, which will induce more licensing among high-productivity enterprises. Empirical results report the regressions examining whether non-capital goods importers in 2000 begin importing such inputs by 2004. The positive and significant coefficient in table 3 suggests that a marginal increase in win rates raises the probability of capital importation by close to one percent, which is a notable extensive-margin impact. In addition, we find the empirical evidence between patent reform and the intensive margins of capital goods importing. Both OLS estimate and IV estimate show that existing importers located in provinces with stronger IPRs protection import more capital goods. We also find that younger firms, more productive firms, foreign firms, and firms owned by Hong Kong-Macau-Taiwan investors import more capital goods. The third objective “To explore whether patent reform leads to productivity gains” has been achieved in the following two aspects. First, in the paper “Intellectual Property Enforcement, Exports and Productivity of Heterogeneous Firms in Developing Countries: Evidence from China”, we find that the shift toward formal TT in locations with stronger IPRs enforcement leads to enhanced productivity gains. As suggested in Melitz (2003), trade liberalization induces changes in cutoff productivities, leading to reallocations of market shares in favor of the more productive firms, which remain in the exporting markets. Similarly, more rigorous IPRs protection induces changes in cutoff productivities and reallocates market shares to firms continuing to trade. Second, in the paper “Trademark Protection, Quality Improvement and Exports in Developing Countries”, we find that when the southern trademark protection is strengthened by increasing the proportion of informed consumers in home country, firms in developing countries may enhance the quality of its products due to the increase in the marginal benefit of quality improvement. It becomes an exporter when the equilibrium quality improvement is greater than the minimum requirement for exporting. This improvement in quality will induce firms to increase productivity. The fourth objective “To establish a link between patent reform and credit constraints” has been achieved. In this paper we build the link among that the extent of IPRs protection, fixed exporting costs and credit constraints. The extent of IPRs protection in the developing country could affect the ability of firms to raise capital for meeting fixed export costs. Manova (2013) suggests that, relative to domestic firms, exporting firms face greater credit constraints because exporting involves additional marketing costs associated with product promotion, consumer identification, and development of distribution channels. Stronger IPRs imply that both firms engaged in legal reverse engineering and producing under a license have greater certainty about the scope of their rights, both at home and abroad. As a consequence, such firms are more likely to attract financing from credit providers. The fifth objective “To test our theoretical predictions using Chinese manufacturing enterprise data” has been fully achieved. To implement our empirical tests, we mainly rely on a comprehensive dataset that matches Chinese firms’ financial data to their trade transactions. The sample is for 2000-2006, covering the period when China joined the WTO and implemented major IPRs reforms, including increases in litigation. The dataset contains information that allows us to construct variables needed for our empirical tests, including key firm attributes and decisions regarding market entry, exit, and exporting. We also construct a measure of capital-goods imports as a proxy for formal technology transfer. To measure the IPRs environment, we follow Ang, et al (2014) and calculate, from original data, the fraction of IPRs infringement cases won by the intellectual property owners in provincial courts over the period. To control for trade liberalization effects in this period, associated primarily with China’s WTO accession, we construct industry-level import tariffs. We carry out empirical analysis using Chinese manufacturing enterprise data. The analysis comes in three parts. First, we consider basic propositions about productivity cutoffs, using cross-sectional firm-level data in separate regressions for 2000 and 2004, without reference to trade decisions. This is essentially a descriptive exercise to discover if the data support the basic model. Second, we exploit changes over this period in the inter-provincial IPRs litigation win rates to isolate the impacts of different levels of enforcement on the productivity cutoffs, in turn determining the extensive-margin effects. Third, we analyze impacts of IPRs enforcement on the intensive-margin volumes of imports, exports, and capital-goods imports, accounting for endogeneity of patent protection. The evidence consistently supports the hypotheses derived from the theory.

549513.label: Major findings and research outcome
549513.value: We have completed two papers with this research grant. First, we have completed the paper “Intellectual Property Enforcement, Exports and Productivity of Heterogeneous Firms in Developing Countries: Evidence from China”. In this paper we study how provincial-level enforcement of intellectual property rights (IPRs) affects Chinese firms’ decisions regarding exit, export, and the channels through which to receive technology transfer. Our model combines the standard theory of heterogeneous firms with the endogenous choices of those firms concerning how they absorb international technologies. We show that, in this setting, the exit and export cutoff productivities differ from those in the standard environment, leading to a different sorting mechanism. We also predict that stronger IPRs change the decisions firms make concerning their mode of technology transfer, further altering their productivity and export possibilities. We carry out empirical tests using Chinese firms’ experience during a period of both legal reforms and greater judicial enforcement, taking advantage of differences in the latter across provinces. The evidence consistently supports the hypotheses derived from the theory. Our findings provide insights into how variations in IPRs enforcement alter productivity and shed light on how stronger intellectual property rights can promote domestic industrial transformation and support both intensive and extensive margins of trade. This paper was presented at (1) Trade and Innovation Journée de conference in Paris in December 2017; (2) China Trade Research Group conference in Nanjing in November 2016. It is currently under submission. The second paper we complete with this grant is “Trademark Protection, Quality Improvement and Exports in Developing Countries”. China has been famous for infringement for many years. The infringement would affect the sales of the genuine products in China, as well as the exports from China of these genuine products to the global market. Therefore, firms’ decision on quality improvement of the genuine products would be different when facing different levels of infringement risks. In this paper we have the following findings. When the southern trademark protection is strengthened by increasing the proportion of informed consumers in home country, firms in developing countries may enhance the quality of its products due to the increase in the marginal benefit of quality improvement. It becomes an exporter when the equilibrium quality improvement is greater than the minimum requirement for exporting. A further increase in trademark protection enhances the quality of the products on the exports market. This paper if forthcoming at the World Economy journal.

549513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
549513.value: The current research can be extended in the following aspect. In the current paper we assume that the only channel for domestic firms to get advanced technology is through purchasing technology from foreign firms. As innovation capacity in China has been improved in past decades, we can consider that domestic innovation can be another channel for domestic firms to get the advanced technology. Therefore, the cutoff productivity for domestic innovations can potentially be included in the sorting pattern and we can study the impacts of patent reform on the change in the cutoff productivity for domestic innovations.

549513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
549513.value: (1) We study how provincial-level enforcement of intellectual property rights (IPRs) affects Chinese firms’ decisions regarding exit, export, and the channels through which to receive technology transfer. Our findings provide insights into how variations in IPRs enforcement alter productivity. Our model combines the standard theory of heterogeneous firms with the endogenous choices of those firms concerning how they absorb international technologies. We show that, in this setting, the exit and export cutoff productivities differ from those in the standard environment, leading to a different sorting mechanism. We also predict that stronger IPRs change the decisions firms make concerning their mode of technology transfer, further altering their productivity and export possibilities. Empirical tests based on a comprehensive dataset of Chinese firms support the model predictions. It is the first paper to show how IPRs reform affects firms’ technology transfer channel and exporting decisions in the presence of firm heterogeneity. (2) We find that firms in developing countries may enhance the quality of its products under stronger trademark protection due to the increase in the proportion of informed consumers. A domestic firm will switch to an exporter when the equilibrium quality improvement is greater than the minimum requirement for exporting.

558913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
558913.value: The notion of grammaticality is central to syntactic theories. A sentence is either grammatical or ungrammatical, and syntactic theories have been developed to account for the (un)grammaticality. But once we go beyond the pure boundary of syntax and ask ourselves how a speaker decides what syntactic form to use for a certain meaning in a certain context, grammaticality is no longer the only concern. One task that the speaker is constantly faced with is to choose the most appropriate form from all possible, grammatical forms that are allowed by their linguistic system. This is where syntax interacts with other aspects of language, such as semantics, pragmatics and phonology. In this research, we will explore these interactions through the investigation of the use of BA construction in natural contexts. Probably the most famous Chinese syntactic construction, BA construction features a preposed object NP (overtly marked by a BA morpheme), which results in a word order of SOV that is different from the canonical SVO word order of the language. Importantly, the use of BA construction is not always obligatory, as many BA sentences can be paraphrased into SVO word order without changing the meaning. Thus the question is: How will the speaker select between the BA construction and the canonical SVO word order? This question has not been fully addressed yet, although many constraints and conditions have been proposed, ranging from definiteness of object NP to disposal meaning of the sentence to presence of parallel BA sentences in previous context. While these factors may all promote the likelihood of using BA construction, it is not clear how strong their effects are, let alone how these factors interact with each other. In this research, we will make use of some recent development in probabilistic linguistics to build a corpus-based probabilistic model for predicting the use of BA construction in context. Using a large set of annotated corpus data (with at least several thousand sentence tokens), the model will try to relate the use of BA construction with various potential sources of influence. Modeling results will be compared with human subjects' performance in behavioral experiments, in order to verify the psycholinguistic basis of the model. Findings from this research will not only shed light on our understanding of how BA construction is used in natural contexts, but also contribute to linguistic research methodology and computational linguistics.

558913.label: Realisation of objectives
558913.value: The project has been completed, with all the project objectives achieved and project outcomes published or under preparation for publication. Below is a brief description of what has been achieved regarding each project objective. Objective 1: To investigate the probabilistic distribution of BA construction (and the alternative SVO sentence) in naturally-occurring Chinese text. To achieve the first objective, I first conducted a survey of BA constructions in the Sinica 10 million-word corpus, which resulted in a database of over 11 thousand BA constructions, featuring more than 1600 different verbs. I further identified four high-frequency verbs, 放 fang4, 拿 na2, 带 dai4, and 送 song4, all of which had more than 200 BA constructions in the corpus. For each selected verb, a matching SVO sentence set was constructed based on the same corpus. Both the BA sentence set and SVO sentence set were manually checked for inconsistency. Sentences unfit for the planned analysis were excluded. The final dataset for each verb consisted of between 600 and 1000 sentences. All the sentences were manually annotated for 16 properties, pertaining the verb form (complement/aspect marker), object NP semantics (e.g. animacy, pronominality, length), sentence structure (serial verb), and the context (e.g. the use of BA construction in preceding/following context, the mention of object NP in preceding/following context). Objective 2: To investigate how various factors regarding the local sentence and the context condition the use of BA construction. In specific, we will consider factors such as object definiteness, information status, verb type, presence of parallel structure, etc, as well as their interactions. To investigate what factors conditions the surface word order (SVO vs. BA), I used mixed-effects regression analysis to model the surface word order for each verb-specific dataset. In each model, the annotated properties were entered into the model as random- or fixed-effects predictors. The results showed that for all four verb models, the use of BA construction was sensitive to the length of the object NP, whether the object NP is mentioned in preceding/following context, and whether another BA construction is used in preceding/following context. Furthermore, modeling results also revealed significant cross-verb differences, especially in the nature of object NP length effect. Such cross-verb differences are rarely addressed in previous literature, and raise new questions for theoretical discussion. Objective 3: To explore the use of corpus-based statistical models in research on Chinese syntactic variation. In specific, we will explore the strengths and weaknesses of the modeling method, and how it may be generalized to the investigation of other topics in Chinese syntax. All four mixed-effects regression models greatly improved the accuracy of predicting the surface word order (compared to the baseline accuracy). In other words, when informed about 14 properties of a sentence and its surrounding context, the models are able to make much better guesses about the surface word order. To further evaluate the effectiveness of model predictions, we compared the probability of using the ba construction (as predicted by the models) with native speakers’ intuition about which word order is better. Two behavioral experiments were conducted, one for the verb 放 fang4 and the other for 拿 na2. A naturalness judgment test was used in both experiments. The participant was provided with (1) a short passage with a missing sentence in the middle and (2) two alternative sentences that could be used to complete the passage. The two alternative sentences (one of which taken from the corpus) only differed in word order and were otherwise identical. The participant’s task was to rate the naturalness (on a 10-poing scale) of each alternative sentence. 25 native Mandarin speakers participated in each experiment. The results showed that speakers’ judgment of relative naturalness between the ba construction and the corresponding SVO sentence are correlated with the models’ predictions of how likely a ba construction would be used. In other words, the ba likelihood predicted by the regression models were confirmed by experimental results with real speakers. Objective 4: To establish the connections among theoretical linguistic investigation, language usage in corpora and language processing in individuals’ mind. To do so, we will compare corpus-based results with theoretical findings in previous literature as well as results from psycholinguistic experiments. Regarding Objective 4, I examined the modeling results in depth, and compared with previous findings on word order variation in other Chinese and non-Chinese languages. One thing that I noticed is that the effects of NP weight on Mandarin SVO-ba alternation are quite different from the NP weight effects observed in other languages. SVO languages like English are known to have a short-before-long preference for constituent ordering, and verb-final languages like Japanese and Korean are known to prefer the long-before-short order. What we have seen in the Mandarin Chinese modeling data is that NP weight has a U-shaped effect on the use of ba construction which requires shifting the NP to the preverbal position. Specifically, both very short NPs and very long NPs are more likely to be used in a ba construction than NPs with medium weight. This pattern can only be explained in a production-oriented account of sentence production, where both conceptual factors and positional factors may both influence the process of sentence production. Results of the corpus-based models have been presented and published in two conference proceedings. Theoretical discussion of the results will be in the form of journal papers and book chapters. Currently, one journal paper directly borne from this project has been submitted to a peer-reviewed journal, and one book chapter is under preparation.

558913.label: Major findings and research outcome
558913.value: This study showcases the use of big data and statistical modeling methods in the study of Chinese syntax. I built four verb-specific models for predicting the surface word order alternation between SVO and ba construction. The most important theoretical finding that arises from this project is the complex effects of NP weight on constituent ordering in Mandarin Chinese. It has been shown in previous literature that SVO languages like English are known to have a short-before-long preference for constituent ordering, and verb-final languages like Japanese and Korean are known to prefer the long-before-short order. What we have seen in the Mandarin Chinese modeling data is a U-shaped effect of NP weight on the ordering of the object NP (SVO = object after verb; ba = object before verb). Specifically, both very short NPs and very long NPs are more likely to be used in a ba construction than NPs with medium weight. This pattern can only be explained in a production-oriented account of sentence production, where both conceptual factors and positional factors may both influence the process of sentence production. Results of the corpus-based models have been presented and published in two conference proceedings (Yao 2014, 2015). Both conference papers are indexed and openly accessible online through ACL Anthology and Waseda University DSpace. They are also uploaded onto the PolyU Institutional Research Archive to be accessible locally, as per the RGC policy. Theoretical discussion of both the corpus-based results and the behavioral experimental data will be in the form of journal papers and book chapters. Currently, one journal paper directly borne from this project has been submitted to a peer-reviewed journal, and one book chapter is under preparation.

558913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
558913.value: This project has the potential to be extended in a few directions. First, the modeling methodology can be applied to other phenomena of language variation in Chinese and other languages. Second, the theoretical discussion of NP weight effect on sentence production could also be further explored. For one thing, the current project has mostly used corpus data from written texts. It will be interesting to see if the same patterns of NP weight effect can be found in spontaneously produced spoken data, either from a corpus or from online sentence production experiments. Furthermore, the cross-verb differences that we observed in the current dataset are also worth further investigation.

558913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
558913.value: We know that sometimes, one message can be expressed in two or more different sentence forms. For example, in Mandarin Chinese, 小王吃了苹果 and 小王把苹果吃了 are basically identical in meaning. Does this mean that the two sentences are equally likely to occur? Or somehow one sentence is more preferable than the other in a given context? These are the questions that we investigate in this project. Using a 10-million-word corpus, we compiled a large set of sentences with different word orders (subject-verb-object, subject-BA-object-verb) and annotated more than a dozen structural and semantic features of each sentence. The annotated dataset was then used to train statistical models to predict the surface word order. Our best models can successfully predict the surface word order in more than 90% of the sentences (baseline accuracy = 68%). The modeling results also revealed interesting effects of the length of the object noun phrase on surface word order. These results illustrate the complexity of the process of sentence production, which is influenced by various different factors concurrently.
