592413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
592413.value: Development of a unified set of accounting standards has been the most important revolution in the accounting profession. Since 2005, European Union (EU) requires all listed firms to use International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS). So far, more than 130 countries have adopted IFRS. Security Exchange Committee of U.S. is also considering the convergence of U.S. General Accepted Accounting Principal (GAAP) to IFRS. This proposal will investigate the effect of mandatory adoption of IFRS on corporate liquidity management policies. In particular, we will focus on the cash management policies. Existing literature has identified several determinants of the cash management policies, including moral hazard and information asymmetry. To the extent that the introduction of IFRS mitigates the moral hazard and information asymmetry, we first test if the firms save less cash from their operating cash flow after IFRS adoption. Second, we will test how the mandatory IFRS adoption will change the valuation of corporate cash holdings. Our third test will investigate how the change in the cash saving propensity and change in the value of cash holding vary across firms, characterized by different extent of financial constraint and agency problem. Finally, our fourth test will examine the role of country-level institutional factors and attempt to identify the specific mechanisms through which IFRS adoption takes effect. Liquidity management is central to the practice of corporate finance and consumes a large fraction of chief financial officers’ time. Recent financial crisis and evidence from both empirical studies and surveys further highlight the importance of liquidity management and, in particular, cash management. This project will improve our understanding of the effect of mandatory IFRS adoption on firms’ real decision making. It should also be of interest to the managers, investors and regulators in those countries that have not adopted but are considering adopting IFRS. 發展出一套世界各國通用的財務報告準則(IFRS)是會計屆的重要變革。自從歐盟於2005年要求所有成員國使用國際財務報告準則以來, 目前已有130多個國家採用國際財務報告準則。美國的證券監督委員會也正考慮這項改革的可行性。 本研究將探究國際財務報告準則的採用對公司流動性管理，特別是對現金管理，的影響。現有文獻一般認為預防性儲蓄和委託-代理人問題是影響公司現金管理的主要因素。如果國際財務報告準則的使用弱化了公司預防性儲蓄的動機和委託-代理人問題，那麼公司是否會在國際財務報告準則採用後儲備更少的現金呢？這將是我們將要研究的第一個問題。第二, 我們將考察投資者對公司持有的現金的估值在國際財務報告準則採用後會如何變化。我們將考察在不同類別的公司中現金持有傾向和市場對現金的估值會在國際財務報告準則採用前後呈現怎樣的差別。 在此, 我們會分別用公司的財務困境/危機的程度和潛在的委託-代理人問題的嚴重性來劃分不同類別的公司。 最後, 我們會考察各國的製度因素怎樣影響公司的現金持有傾向和現金的估值在國際財務報告準則採用前後的變化。 流動性管理是公司理財的核心問題。 近期爆發的金融危機突顯了流動性管理(特別是現金管理)的重要性。我們的研究項目將有助於提高我們對財務報告準則對實體經濟問題的意義的認識。 此外, 我們的研究也將對尚未採用國際財務報告準則的國家的公司管理者, 投資者和政策, 法規的製定人有所借鑒。

592413.label: Major findings and research outcome
592413.value: We have empirically examined the laid-out research objectives in past two years. We compose a working paper out of the research proposal and we presented the working paper in a few international conferences. In the paper, we examine how firms’ cash holdings change around the mandatory IFRS adoption. Using a difference-in-differences approach, we document that the firms significantly decrease their cash holdings after the mandatory adoption of IFRS. We also find that such decrease in cash holding is more significant for firms with more precautionary savings demand and/or with more agency problems. Furthermore, we provide evidence that the country-level legal enforcement quality has an impact on firms’ cash holdings after the adoption of IFRS, implying that enforcement interacts with the changes in regulations. Additional tests show that after the change in financial reporting standard, firms decrease their propensity to save cash from operating cash flows and increase their external financing and investment. To enrich our study, we explore the impact of another event, i.e. the initial enforcement of insider trading laws around the world. This is not proposed in earlier proposal, but we find consistent effect on cash holdings (and cash savings) of the first-time enforcement of insider trading laws, in both the pooled sample analysis and subsample analysis. Overall, our findings suggest that the change in information environment affects corporate cash policies.

592413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
592413.value: The financial theory argues that the change in informational environment should impact corporate cash policies (or liquidity management policy in general). Given the importance of cash policies in financial decision-making process, it is worthwhile to explore more contexts, either at the firm-level, industry-level or economy-level, and evaluate how and to what extent the impact of the events will shape the corporate cash policies. This can be done with not only US setting, but also international or China setting.

592413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
592413.value: How much cash shall a corporate hold? If the firm holds too little cash, the firm may not have enough liquidity to deal with daily operations; if the firm holds too much cash, it is not desirable because some cash can be alternatively used to earn higher return. It is predicted that the firm will hold less cash when it can easily borrow from external investors, and the firm can borrow from external investors more easily when external investors know better about the firm. To compare the cash holdings before and after certain economic events that are supposed to mitigate the information asymmetry between corporate insiders and outsiders, such as the implementation of IFRS and the first-time enforcement of insider trading laws, the firms indeed hold less cash and save less cash.

592713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
592713.value: 研究人员最近对虐辱管理这一话题越来越感兴趣。虐辱管理是指除了身体接触外，“下属”在某种程度上感觉到管理者持续表现出的言语或非言语的敌意行为。这些虐待行为会对员工的工作带来各种负面影响。更糟糕的是，这些虐待行为可以从主管和下属之间转移至员工和顾客之间 。通过借鉴社会学习理论以及Masterson (2001)的涓滴理论，我们认为上级的虐辱管理行为与下属的虐待行为有正相关性，后者会影响员工的服务表现。此外，我们以联合函数来检验员工的服务表现与文化因素和虐辱管理的共同作用，因为这个作用最终会影响客户的满意度和忠诚度。本研究试图开发和检验一个多层的理论框架，并为理解虐辱管理在上下级中的滴入式扩散过程提供更全面的视野。

592713.label: Realisation of objectives
592713.value: All objectives have been achieved. Those achieved objectives are listed below: 1) This study has investigated the level of abusive supervision and subordinate abusive behavior in the Chinese hospitality context; 2) This study has examined abusive supervision trickle down from higher level (e.g., supervisors) to lower level (e.g., subordinates) by integrating on social cognitive learning theory and trickle-down model; 3) This study has examined the effects of abusive supervision on subordinates' service performance via the mediating role of subordinates' abusive behavior; 4) This study has also examined the moderating roles of power distance and traditional values in Chinese context mitigate the negative effects of abusive supervision on employee service performance; 5) Finally, based on the findings and results from Chinese context, this study has provided suggestions and recommendations for hospitality managers how to reduce abusive supervision and improve employees' service performance, and ultimately, enhance customers' satisfaction and their loyalty. --To test the above objectives, we collected data in hospitality companies in Beijing, China. The research team approached participants in a full-time Master program specially developed for hospitality personnel at a university in Beijing. These participants provided us the contact information of their HR managers, we then contacted the HR managers by emails and follow-up phone calls. Finally 50 HR managers from different hotels agreed to help. We asked them to recommend one functional team or department in their hotels to participate in our survey. We assured the participants that the questionnaires would be anonymous and the survey information would be kept confidential and at no time would any individual results be relayed to the hotel management or anyone other than the research team. With help from these HR managers, 36 out of 50 teams participated in the survey. With the help of HR managers, separate questionnaires were administered to team managers and subordinates. Employees were asked to answer questions about their perceptions of abusive supervision, their abusive behaviors toward others, and power distance and traditional values. Team managers were asked to rate their subordinates’ service performance. The HR managers distributed 36 survey packets to the team managers and 300 survey packets to subordinates, and the subordinates were allowed to decide whether or not they would participate in the study. Each survey packet was put in a sealed envelope which included a cover letter explaining the general purpose of the study and stating that participation was voluntary. In order to assure confidentiality and anonymity, each participant was given a unique identification code so that data collected from the subordinates and supervisors could be matched and grouped for later analysis. Respondents placed their completed surveys in a sealed envelope and returned them to a box located in the HR department of each company. We then visited each company to collect the questionnaires. The final sample consisted of 266 employees (an 88% response rate) who were supervised by 36 team managers (a 72% response rate). --We used hierarchical linear modeling (HLM) version 6.02 (Raudenbush, Bryk, Cheong, and Congdon, 2004) to test all of the hypotheses. Multilevel researchers (Hofmann and Stetzer, 1998) have demonstrated that multilevel analysis is a more appropriate method for analyzing cross-level data because such data have a nested structure (i.e., employees are nested with the organization). In other words, the work-related attitudes and behaviors of the employees may be similar because they are all working in the same organization. Therefore, we used the HLM computer package to analyze the cross-level hypotheses. --As expected, abusive supervision was positively correlated with subordinates’ abusive behavior (r = .41, p < .01) and negatively related to employee service performance (r = -.19, p < .05). As expected, subordinates’ abusive behavior was negatively associated with employee service performance (r = -.37, p < .01). Next, a measurement model was estimated by confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) to examine the convergent and discriminant validity of each variable. We first examined a four-factor model that included abusive supervision, power distance, traditional culture, and subordinates’ abusive behavior. The discriminant validity of the four constructs was tested by contrasting a four-factor model against a three-factor and a one-factor model. The one-factor model loaded all items onto a “grand” latent factor. The three-factor model combined abusive supervision and subordinates’ abusive behavior into one factor because they had the highest correlation among the four factors. The three-factor model left the other two cultural factors separate. The one-factor and three-factor models yielded poor fits of the data compared to the four-factor model. In addition, various fit indices supported the fit of the four-factor model, thus supporting the discriminant validity of the each construct. --Finally, multilevel analysis was used to test all the hypotheses. The HLM results supported Hypothesis 1 which predicts that abusive supervision is positively related to subordinates’ abusive behavior, and Hypothesis 2 which predicts that subordinates’ abusive behavior is negatively related to service performance. Then, to evaluate the hypothesized cross-level interactions, Hypothesis 3 predicts that power distance value would moderate the positive relationship between abusive supervision and subordinates’ abusive behavior, such that the relationship will be weaker when power distance is strong; and Hypothesis 4 predicts that traditional value moderates the positive relationship between abusive supervision and subordinates’ abusive behavior, such that the positive relationship will be weaker when traditional value is strong. Our results also supported the cross-level effect of Hypothesis 3 that abusive supervisory behaviors were positively related to subordinates’ abusive behavior, and this positive relationship was weaker for teams with a strong power distance values. Consistent with Hypothesis 4, abusive supervisory behaviors were positively related to subordinates’ abusive behavior, and this positive relationship was weaker for teams with a strong traditional value. --The findings of this study supported our hypotheses about the cognitive social learning process linking supervisory abusive supervision to employee service performance. And by examining the moderating effects of power distance and traditionality, this study shows that the trickle-down effect of abusive supervision is contingent on the team’s cultural climate. Specifically, based on the trickle-down effect, we found that abusive supervisory behavior was positively associated with abusive subordinate behavior. Second, abusive subordinate behavior was negatively associated with service performance. Third, the two team-level cultural values (tradition and power distance) moderated the relationships of abusive supervision with abusive subordinate behavior and service performance, such that the relationships were weaker for subordinates working in strong traditional and high power distance team culture. Fourth, in line with cognitive social learning theory, this study found that abusive subordinate behavior mediated the link between abusive supervision with subordinate service performance. --Theoretically, this study offers further insight into the relationship between abusive supervision and abusive subordinate behavior by investigating this trickle-down effect in the hospitality industry. Practically, this study provides suggestions to the managers in service and hospitality industries. Employee service quality has been regarded as a prerequisite for success and survival in today’s competitive environment. For service organizations to maintain customer satisfaction and loyalty, employee service performance is crucial. This study suggests several practical ways by which hospitality managers and organizations can decrease the effect of abusive supervision on service performance.

592713.label: Major findings and research outcome
592713.value: The findings of this study supported all our objectives and hypotheses about the cognitive social learning process linking supervisory abusive supervision to employee service performance. By examining the moderating effects of power distance and traditionality, this study shows that the trickle-down effect of abusive supervision is contingent on the team’s cultural climate. Specifically, based on the trickle-down effect, we found that abusive supervisory behavior was positively associated with abusive subordinate behavior. Second, abusive subordinate behavior was negatively associated with service performance. Third, the two team-level cultural values (tradition and power distance) moderated the relationships of abusive supervision with abusive subordinate behavior and service performance, such that the relationships were weaker for subordinates working in strong traditional and high power distance team culture. Fourth, in line with cognitive social learning theory, this study found that abusive subordinate behavior mediated the link between abusive supervision with subordinate service performance. Therefore, the above 5 objectives are all supported. Research outcome: The two papers have been published in referred journals 1) Hon, A. H. Y. & Lu, L. (2016). When will the trickle-down effect of abusive supervision be alleviated?The roles of power distance and traditional cultures. Cornell Hospitality Quarterly. 57(4), 421-433. --The trickle-down model of abusive supervision points out that the negative effect of abusive supervisory behaviors will be imitated by the subordinates and transmits along the organizational hierarchy. An important question arises herein as when and how this negative effect will be stopped or alleviated. In this study we examine the positive relationship between abusive supervisory behavior and abusive subordinate behavior, and the negative relationship between subordinates’ abusive behavior and service performance in teams from hospitality industry. Moreover, we posit that two team-level cultural values (power distance and traditional values) moderate the trickle-down effect of abusive supervision. 2) Hon, A. H. Y. & Lu, L. (2015). Are we paid to be creative? The effect of compensation gap on creativity in an expatriate context. Journal of World Business, 50(1), 159-167. --In developing countries, there is a relatively large compensation gap between locals and expatriates, which incurs a wide range of negative reactions from the former. Referring to the equity theory and reflection theory of pay, we proposed a negative association of local employees’ creativity with perceived compensation gap. We adopted a multi-level approach to examine the moderating effects of trust climate directed towards the expatriates on individual-level relationship of compensation gap and creativity.

592713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
592713.value: From our findings, we believe that abusive supervision is common in the workplace. This negative effect will transmit from the high organizational level (manager/supervisor) to the lower level (subordinate/general employee). The worst is that this negative effect could also transmit between employees (peer to peer) and between employees and customers. If this assumption is true, this will negatively affect individuals' performance as well as hamper organizations' reputation and image, at the end, it will influence service quality of the hospitality industry. Therefore, we suggest future research could focus on the trickle-down effect and model from supervisor-subordinate relationships to subordinate-subordinate or front-line staff-customer relationships. Moreover, future research should also compare our findings based on samples drawn from hospitality and service sectors to manufacturing, electronics, research and development, and other industries such as tourism sector. This will pave the way for future direction to further validate our findings as well as providing a rich but underdeveloped area (trickle-down model) in the hospitality service sector.

592713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
592713.value: The significant value of this study is that it provides theoretical insight by integrating a Chinese cultural perspective into the cognitive social learning explanation for the relationships among abusive supervision, abusive subordinate behavior, and service performance. In this way, we intended to unveil the complexity of the trickle-down model from higher level to lower level. Two cultural factors (power distance and traditionality) are found as important roles for the relationship between abusive supervision and service performance. We conclude that these cultural factors seem to be able to mitigate the relationship between abusive supervision and abusive subordinate behaviors in the Chinese hotel industry. This study tends to lead us to rethink the application and possible adaptation of western-based theories in the non-western culture; and they also suggest the value of examining these relationships in specific hospitality firms and cultural settings.

592913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
592913.value: Skip-level voice is defined as employees’ voice behavior toward higher-level and distal leaders while skipping over their direct supervisors (Detert & Treviño, 2010). This type of voice behavior may be of great value to organizations because it allows senior managers to garner important first-hand information about organizational opportunities and threats directly from frontline employees. However, little is known about its eventual consequences on the voicing employees. In particular, it is very likely that direct supervisors—who usually hear about it from a third party—will view skip-level voice behavior as an act of betrayal or “back-stabbing” (Detert & Edmondson, 2011). Given that direct supervisors have a lot of control over the career development of frontline employees, it is necessary to investigate why and when skip-level voicing will cause negative consequences for the voicing employees. To address these research questions, we draw on organization power theory (Blau, 1964; Keltner, Gruenfeld, & Anderson, 2003; Kipnis, 1976; Magee & Galinsky, 2008; Pfeffer & Salancik, 1978) to propose that direct supervisors are likely to see skip-level voice as disrespectful and a challenge, making them feel that their power standing in the organization is being threatened (Detert & Treviño, 2010; Hambrick & Mason, 1984). As a consequence, they may take revenge for voice behavior by giving the voicing employees lower performance evaluations, salary increments, and promotion opportunities over time. Moreover, the effect of skip-level voice on direct supervisors’ perception of threat may depend on (1) direct supervisors’ power stability (Cummings, 1980; Tajfel & Turner, 1979, 1986) and (2) the extent to which the direct supervisors perceive the content of skip-level voice as infringing on their authority territories (Brown & Robinson, 2011). Finally, skip-level voice may interact with these two moderators to influence employees’ career outcomes through direct supervisors’ perceived threat to their power standing. Our pilot study has provided initial evidence supporting our theoretical framework, but to fully test our model, we will use a multi-method, multi-sampling, and longitudinal research design. This will include a critical incident study to develop a scale, a cross-sectional scenario-based survey, and two independent longitudinal surveys with four waves of data collection. The longitudinal surveys will be carried out in the research unit of the largest telecommunication services company in the world and a business unit of one of the largest commercial banks in China. 越级建言是指，员工越过自己的直属上司，向上上级的领导表达意见 （Detert & Treviño, 2010）。这种建言行为对企业的管理有一定的价值，因为企业的高管可透过这一途径透过前线的一手资料了解企业面对的挑战与机遇。但是，我们不是很清楚的是，那些越级建言的员工在建言后会有什么遭遇。实际上，这些员工的直接领导往往会透过其他途径了解到下属们越级建言的行为，甚至会把这种行为视为一种对自己的背叛或是暗箭伤人（Detert & Edmondson, 2011）。因为直属上司有绝对的权力来影响下属的职业发展，我们应该从理论上对这一现象进行更深入的了解，并梳理出为什么和在什么情况下越级建言会对下属造成负面的影响。

592913.label: Major findings and research outcome
592913.value: We have conducted seven surveys to test our models. We collected time-lagged data in 4 companies in China and 3 companies in the U.S. The results supported our key propositions on managers' reactions to employee skip-level voice. Specifically, based on two time-lagged independent studies, we found that frequent skip-level voice is more likely to induce direct supervisors’ territorial defense behaviors (i.e., undermining behavior and territorial reclaiming behavior) when the voice content contains more issues that potentially shrink direct supervisors’ authority (i.e., high authority-infringement) and fewer issues that potentially expand direct supervisors’ authority (i.e., low authority-expansion). We also found that interpersonal affect functions as an important explanatory mechanism underlying the relationships between skip-level voice and direct supervisors’ territorial defense behaviors. We have presented the findings of our paper in IACMR conference in 2016. In addition, inspired by these findings, we further investigated managers' paradoxical reactions to frequency of voice and found an inverted U-shaped relationship between frequency of voice and managers' evaluations of voicers using 5 samples. We published this paper in Journal of Applied Psychology.

592913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
592913.value: The series studies conducted in this project offer fresh insight into the consequences of employee voice. The skip-level voice paper has laid an important foundation for future research on how managers from different levels react to employee voice. The paper on managers reactions to employee challenging voice is the first to demonstrate managers' paradoxical reactions to voice and provide a strong theoretical foundation for future research on the consequences of voice.

592913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
592913.value: Our research project has revealed a few very important implications for practicing managers. First, our study clearly suggests that when top managers encourage employees to voice up issues directly to them, they should seriously take into consideration the potential feelings and reactions of the voicing employees’ direct supervisors. Direct supervisors’ vengeful reactions may indeed counteract top managers’ endeavors to build a culture of voice. Second, voicing employees should be aware the content of the voiced issues may play an important role in shaping their supervisors’ reactions. For issues that may touch upon direct supervisors’ authority territory, employees should carefully and delicately convey their voice upward. The findings of our additional study has shed light on how managers react to employees' challenging voice. We demonstrated that challenging voice, such as prohibitive voice, may not be as risky as previously assumed. A moderate frequency of prohibitive voice can project a positive image to managers, even when the voicing employees are not members of the managers’ ingroup. More important, subordinates who have poor relationships with their managers should be aware that only very frequent prohibitive voice tends to induce managers’ unfavorable responses.

593113.label: Co - Investigator(s)
593113.value: Prof Denizci Guillet, Basak Dr Zhang Qiu, Hanqin

593113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
593113.value: China has emerged as the second largest luxury goods market in the world with a world market share of 25%, and is predicted to surpass Japan by 2015 as the largest market (Chinahourly, 2009; Yu, 2010). Hong Kong has a reputation for being “fashion conscious” (Chung & Fischer, 2001), attracting 90% of the luxury brand retailers in the world (Global Times, 2010). In recent years, mainland China has become the most important market for the tourism industry in Hong Kong, contributing more than 60% of the total number of tourists coming to the region (HKTB, 2010). Mainland Chinese tourists spend most of their money on shopping (60%), followed by hotel bills (14%) and meals outside their hotels (15%). Hong Kong is in an advanced position to develop itself as a preferred luxury-shopping tourism destination for mainland Chinese. However, Hong Kong should not take mainland Chinese tourists for granted because evidence (Big Weekly, 2010) has shown that Chinese luxury-shopping tourists are now moving away from Hong Kong to Europe and North America. To attract mainland Chinese luxury shoppers to Hong Kong, the region must understand the luxury-shopping destination attributes most preferred by mainland Chinese and the destination mixes they find most enticing. With this information, Hong Kong will be in an advanced position to fully develop its potential. By incorporating conjoint analysis, this study aims to understand the importance weights of the destination attributes considered by mainland Chinese choosing a luxury-shopping destination and to determine their most preferred combination of destination attributes. It is believed that this understanding will produce constructive suggestions regarding how the Hong Kong tourism industry might best develop Hong Kong as a preferred luxury-shopping destination for mainland Chinese. 中国正快速发展成为世界第二大奢侈品市场并占有全球25%的市场份额，预计将在2015年超越日本跃居世界第一(Chinahourly, 2009; Yu, 2010)。作为“时尚前沿”的香港(Chung & Fischer, 2001)，已吸引全球90%的奢侈品牌。近年来，大陆游客已占所有访港旅客的60%并成为香港旅游业最重要的目标市场 (HKTB, 2010)。大陆游客在港旅游消费支出中，60%用于购物，14%用于住宿，15%用于餐饮及其它开支。香港有望发展成为中国大陆游客首选奢侈品购物旅游目的地。然而，据媒体报道，中国奢侈品购买者有从香港转向欧洲及北美的迹象(Big Weekly, 2010) 。为吸引大陆奢侈品购买者前往香港，香港必须了解中国大陆游客最喜爱的奢侈品购物目的地的属性及其组合。基于以上信息的了解，香港才有可能发挥其竞争优势，成为大陆游客首选奢侈品购物目的地。通过结合分析，本研究将了解大陆游客考量奢侈品购物目的地属性的权重，以及发掘他们最喜爱的奢侈品购物目的地属性的组合。研究结果将对香港旅游业如何发展为大陆游客首选奢侈品购物目的地提出建设性意

593113.label: Realisation of objectives
593113.value: All the research objectives have been achieved. 1. To determine the importance weights of the destination attributes chosen by mainland Chinese selecting a luxury-shopping destination. The results of the conjoint analysis revealed the preference of mainland Chinese tourists for different destinations within the context of luxury consumption. Clear differences were illustrated between the six attributes. “Friendliness of local residents” (29.913%) and “credibility of product quality” (26.611%) were the two most important attributes. By contrast, the attribute “travelling expenses” (6.267%) was evaluated as the least important attribute. While “travelling convenience” (9.945%) and “available choices of products” (10.716%) were considered as less important, “service quality of service providers” (16.548%) were of medium importance. This may suggest that travellers value intangible attributes more than tangible attributes when choosing a luxury shopping destination. 2. To determine the most preferred combination of destination attributes among mainland Chinese. For each attribute, a part-worth utility was produced for each level and an importance value was calculated based on the part-worth utilities of the levels. Chinese tourists prefer high level of friendliness of local residents (0.63), high quality and genuineness of the luxury product provided at the destination (0.56), high service quality of service providers (0.35), large amount of available project choice (0.23), convenient access to the destination (0.21), and low travel expenses (0.13). The remaining attribute levels carry negative utility values which indicate that respondents do not prefer these options. Additional effort was made to understand the importance of different destination attributes to mainland Chinese in accordance with their demographic information. Only very few demographic differences were revealed in the One-way ANOVA test results, which reflects that the preference of Chinese travellers in choosing a luxury shopping destination is quite robust across different demographics. The differences include the following: • The importance value of “Travelling convenience” was significantly evaluated as more important by Shenzhen respondents (14.0289%) than respondents from Beijing (9.6271%, F=3.711, p=0.012). • The same importance value was also significantly higher (14.6610%) for single respondents, comparing to 11.0798% for married respondents with children (F=3.706, p=0.020). • Respondents at the age of 16-25 considered the attribute “Credibility of product quality” (16.6963%) significantly less important (F=2.784, p=0.024) than respondents at the age of 26-35 (21.9654%), 36-45 (22.5866%) and 66 or above (30.3976%). However, the difference among the latter three groups was not significant.

593113.label: Major findings and research outcome
593113.value: This study analyses the destination preferences of mainland Chinese tourists within the context of luxury shopping. The study reveals the role of trade-off in consumers’ decision making, which is seldom considered in tourism research. Conjoint analysis was found to create apparent patterns of travellers’ preference in which friendliness of local residents was found to be most important in choosing a luxury destination among Chinese travelers, followed by credibility of product quality, service quality of service providers, available choices of products, travelling convenience, and travel expenses. Theoretically, the attributes of a luxury shopping destination are developed from scratch with a mixed methods approach. The key attributes are identified with rigorous procedures to represent the main preferences of Chinese travellers in choosing a destination for luxury shopping. Practically, the results suggest some caution in the development of luxury shopping destination.

593113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
593113.value: From a theoretical perspective, the literature mainly focuses on understanding how travellers choose a travel destination. Such an understanding is mainly constructed at the individual item level without referencing the trade-offs that people usually encounter when making decisions. Although the influence of individual attributes may be important in understanding the destination choices of travellers, the results may differ from those if trade-offs are considered and thus can be biased. In addition, the attributes identified in the literature mainly refer to leisure travel, not luxury shopping. It is necessary to identify destination attributes specifically for luxury shopping, especially to understand the corresponding destination choices of Chinese travellers given their prominent role in luxury consumption. This study should contribute to the understanding of mainland Chinese preferences for luxury-shopping destinations by examining their decision-making process while considering all relevant attributes simultaneously when evaluating their importance to the set of destination choices. Nevertheless, the respondents involved in this study were from the four major cities in mainland China which may not represent the opinions of tourists from other cities, as second-tier cities. Future studies could also focus on a cross-cultural perspective to examine the different preference structures between different nations.

593113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
593113.value: By applying conjoint measurement to analyze the preferences of mainland Chinese tourists, this study examined how six particular factors of destination attributes, generated from qualitative and quantitative methods, affected tourists’ decision-making process in the context of luxury consumption. The results indicated that of these destination attributes, friendliness of local residents was the most important and travelling expenses were the least importance. Under a context highly connected with expenditure, the results still reflect the trend that tourists do not value the cost of travelling, including the relative price of luxury products, as much as other attributes in terms of destination selection. This finding implies that for luxury consumers, it is important to create a friendly and comfortable shopping environment and make customers feel like VIPs. When customers spend more than what the ordinary products and services cost, price is not the primary factor to consider. Rather, what concerns them most are the intangible aspects of shopping experiences, such as prestige, exclusiveness, and uniqueness.

593913.label: Project Title(Chinese)
593913.value: 企業對外來沖擊的反應

593913.label: Co - Investigator(s)
593913.value: Prof Ge , Ying Dr Zhu, Susan Chun

593913.label: Project Objectives
593913.value: Compiling a comprehensive dataset that merges information on manufacturing firms, their international trade transactions, and external shocks in terms of exchange rates and tariff rates Understanding firm-level responses to exchange rate shocks and tariff shocks Linking firm-level trade responses to the aggregate level changes in trade flows
rows: Compiling a comprehensive dataset that merges information on manufacturing firms, their international trade transactions, and external shocks in terms of exchange rates and tariff rates
Understanding firm-level responses to exchange rate shocks and tariff shocks
Linking firm-level trade responses to the aggregate level changes in trade flows

593913.label: Realisation of objectives
593913.value: Our original plan was to focus on firms' response to exchange rate shocks. We conducted comprehensive analysis based on the specifications described in the proposal. Unfortunately, the results do not support our hypotheses - the regression coefficients related to exchange rate terms are either insignificant or not robust across different specifications. The reason is that relative to other factors such as labor costs, exchange rates variation is too small to stand out as a key determinant of trade performance. For example, we observe very large within firm-product-destination price changes relative to very insignificant RMB appreciation/depreciation over time. This is clear in retrospect, however, I didn’t fully realize it when I wrote the proposal. Given the weak result related to exchange rate shocks, we modified our plan to examine firms’ transportation mode decisions in conducting trade. Earlier works of transportation mode decision by Hummels (2007), Hummels and Schaur (2010), and Harrigan (2010) focus on the product and destination characteristics. By focusing on firm attributes, we built a model and did comprehensive empirical analysis. We find that within the same product-destination market, high productivity firms are more likely to use air mode and the productivity effect on the propensity of using air freight is more significant when goods are exported to richer markets, when firms are engaged in global production networks, and when products are more R&D intensive. We finished a draft entitled “Transportation Mode and Exporter Heterogeneity” and presented it in several conferences. Please refer to the uploaded paper. We believe the paper is very solid already, but we want to do more. Based on further research and many useful feedbacks from the conferences, we realized that it is important to examine firms’ joint decisions on transportation mode, product quality, and different forms of transportation cost shocks. Besides that quality choice is a hot topic in recent trade literature, the incorporation of transportation costs allows the modified project to be more closely fit to the original goal of the proposal, which is to examine “firm-level response to external shocks” – shocks in transportation costs represent very important shocks in firms import/export decisions. This is consistent with Hummels (2007) that exporters paid $9 in transport costs for every $1 they paid in tariff duties. We therefore took great effort to develop a model that endogenizes firms’ decision about product quality and transportation mode (by air or by ocean). The model suggests that conditional on transportation mode, higher export prices and price are associated with lower transportation costs, and this relationship is stronger for high-productivity firms. Our empirical results support the theoretical prediction. We find that a 10% increase in air freight costs is associated with an 8% reduction in the export price with just 2% of the freight cost increase passed on to consumers. Further, compared with firms at the 25th TFP percentile, those at the 75th percentile would see an additional reduction in price by 2%. Our results are robust to controls for firms’ self-selection into different transportation modes, product competition in the destination markets, and controls for tariffs and exchange rates. We thus finished a dramatically new draft entitled “Firm Level Response to Transportation Cost Shocks”. It is worthwhile to mention that since we also include shocks of exchange rates and tariffs as controls for robustness, now this draft more closely captures the spirit of the original proposal, that is, firm-level responses to external shocks”. We believe this is a very solid paper with a nice model and very robust empirical results about an important topic in international trade. We are preparing to submit it to Journal of International Economics. It took longer than we expected to complete the project, largely due to the unexpected weak firm response to shocks in exchange rates. After modifying to the new strategy, we took extraordinary efforts to develop new models, collect new data, and work with multiple revisions before we conclude with a model and empirical results that we consider to be truly solid. I hope these efforts can be seen from the two uploaded papers and related presentations conducted in different conferences. In addition to the focus on the theme of “firm level response to external shocks”, separately I have applied the databases constructed for this project to work on related papers. Followings are two papers largely benefited from the support of this grant (that I gratefully acknowledged): (1) “Trust Premium in Global Supply Chains”, joined with Douglas Cumming, Ying Ge, and Jiaping Qiu. This is currently under review at The Journal of International Business Studies. ABSTRACT - This study provides the first analysis of the role of trust in global supply chains that involve collaborations among multiple partners. Using large panel data on products manufactured in China by multinational enterprises with headquarters in different countries and exported to European countries, we find that European trust regarding multinational headquarter countries positively contributes to the unit value of exported products. Moreover, trust premium is more prominent for more sophisticated supply chains with: (a) a heavier delegation of decisions and tasks, (b) more differentiated products, and (c) a higher level of R&D intensity. We also find a significant trust premium for source countries of imported intermediate inputs. Overall, our analysis highlights that trust plays an important role for global supply chains. (2) “From the Stock Market to the Factory Floor: The Real Effects of Financial Dysfunctions”. Joined with Warren Bailey, Zhaoran Gong, and Wilson Tong. We are preparing to submit the paper to The Review of Financial Studies. ABSTRACT- Looking beneath stock market and accounting performance, we examine the real effects of state ownership, managerial political connections, disclosure quality, and managerial expropriation on manufacturing productivity and other firm-level real outcomes for public and private Chinese manufacturing firms. In summary, despite some difficulties in conducting this project, I manage to finish a paper of high potential at the Journal of International Economics, and two papers of high potential at Journal of International Business Studies and Review of Financial Studies respectively.

593913.label: Major findings and research outcome
593913.value: Main findings of the three papers: (1) “Firm Level Response to Transportation Cost Shocks” Using the matched firm-trade data from China, we examine the firm-level response to transportation cost shocks. We develop a model that endogenizes firms’ decision about product quality and transportation mode (by air or by ocean). It suggests that conditional on transportation mode, higher export prices and price are associated with lower transportation costs, and this relationship is stronger for high-productivity firms. Empirical results suggest that a 10% increase in air freight costs is associated with an 8% reduction in the export price with just 2% of the freight cost increase passed on to consumers. Compared with firms at the 25th TFP percentile, those at the 75th percentile would see an additional reduction in price by 2%. Our results are robust to controls for firms’ self-selection into different transportation modes, product competition in the destination markets, and controls for exchange rates and tariffs. (2) “Trust Premium in Global Supply Chains” This study provides the first analysis of the role of trust in global supply chains that involve collaborations among multiple partners. Using large panel data on products manufactured in China by multinational enterprises with headquarters in different countries and exported to European countries, we find that European trust regarding multinational headquarter countries positively contributes to the unit value of exported products. Trust premium is more prominent for more sophisticated supply chains with: (a) a heavier delegation of decisions and tasks, (b) more differentiated products, and (c) a higher level of R&D intensity. We also find a significant trust premium for source countries of imported intermediate inputs. Overall, we find that trust plays an important role for global supply chains. (3) “From the Stock Market to the Factory Floor: The Real Effects of Financial Dysfunctions”. Looking beneath stock market and accounting performance, we examine the real effects of state ownership, managerial political connections, disclosure quality, and managerial expropriation on manufacturing productivity and other firm-level real outcomes for public and private Chinese manufacturing firms. Our results thus far suggest that the financial dysfunctions are typically associated with lower TFP. However, we have uncovered at least a couple of unresolved or anomalous findings. Why would “good” (that is, high TFP) firms engage in earnings management or hold high excess cash balances? We will further explore these anomalies and uncover additional unique features of the Chinese financial market environment.

593913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
593913.value: Related to the paper “Firm Level Response to Transportation Cost Shocks”, potentially we can do the following: (1) Further research to distinguish the impact of a change in product quality vs. markup on export price and export quality. (2) Further research on the impact of exchange rate shock and tariff reductions on transportation mode and export quality. We have already included them as controls in robustness. We may compile different versions of these measures, hoping to identify more significant impacts. Related to the paper “Trust Premium in Global Supply Chains”, potentially we can do the following: (1) Examine the combined impact of product life-cycle and trust on export price. According to Bilir, L. Kamran (“Patent Law, product life-cycle lengths, and multinational activity”, American Economic Review, 2014), trust plays a more important role in industry with products that have longer life cycle. There is less concern for short life-cycle products because related trade-secrets may become obsolete before infringement can succeed. Potentially we can further examine the price impact of the interaction between trust and the industry level product life-cycle measure. We expect that trust premium on export price to be higher in industry with products of longer life-cycle.

593913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
593913.value: In “Firm Level Response to Transportation Cost Shocks”, we find that more productive firms are more likely to use airplane (vs. ship) to send high price products to richer countries. Higher transportation costs, either by airplane or by ship, leads to lower export prices. This implies that good firms are more likely to be specialized in higher value and time-sensitive goods, and transportation costs play an important role in these decisions. In “Trust Premium in Global Supply Chains”, we find that when affiliates of European multinationals export their products to other European countries, higher bilateral trust translates into higher export price. This impact is more significant in trust-sensitive industries. These results suggest that promoting trust between countries is important in promoting trade. In “From the Stock Market to the Factory Floor: The Real Effects of Financial Dysfunctions”, we examine the real effects of dysfunctions such as state ownership, managerial political connections, disclosure quality, and managerial expropriation. We find that dysfunctions are typically associated with lower TFP. While financial literature typically examines the stock market impact of dysfunctions, this paper is the first to examine the real effects of dysfunction in a comprehensive way.

594613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
594613.value: 本硏究計劃審視新股上市（IPO）的活動，企業上市的決定，以及IPO的特性如何受世界各國不同的員工保護法（ EPL ）影響。過去的研究（如La Porta et al. 1997, 2000）主要就投資者的法律保障去探索其對金融市場發展的影響，一般忽略了其他利益相關者的法律保障對資本市場發展的可能影響。我們認為，既然勞動力是生產中一個重要因素，並且佔大約三分之二的經濟附加值，員工法律保障程度很可能是股權市場發展的一個重要決定因素。 勞動經濟的研究指出，雖然工資主要是一個變量，勞動力成本尚包括相關的固定成本用以招聘、培訓及解僱員工。故此，勞動力的投資不可避免地包括其調整成本，而此種調整成本在某些情況下變得特別高昂。首先，工會的介入將影響公司對勞動力投資的控制及靈活性，從而提高調整成本。其次，工會在有助益於員工及管理層溝通的情況下將對股東引入一定的代理成本。此外，在工會介入的情況下，管理層將更有動力去保持信息的不對稱，因為增加信息共享將提高工會的議價能力。 我們認為，有力的EPL加強了工會的力量，從而增加一般的調整成本以及代理成本，因此，我們預期，在一個具良好員工法律保障的國家，公司在上市時不得不支付更高的成本，從而讓更多公司對上市裹足不前。而這些較高的成本亦將反映於那些決定上市的IPO公司。本研究的主要探索問題如下： 1）員工保護法之嚴峻性是否與企業之上市決定相關聯？ 2）員工保護法之嚴峻性會否影響IPO的一般特性，如IPO的抑價現象、承銷費、承銷團的規模？ 基於各國的員工保護法的資料，以及Amadeus數據庫中存有的公共和私營公司的數據，本硏究將在國家層面以及在企業層面對上述問題作出分析，並控制一系列企業及國家層面的相關變量。 本研究是首項處理勞動力及新股上市活動相關性的考察，將有助於我們了解幾個方面的文獻。首先，本硏究有助我們了解非金融活動的利益相關者與金融活動的利益相關者如何互動。其次，這項研究幫助我們量化員工法律保護對股權融資市場的經濟意義，如 IPO抑價作為新股權融資的實際成本如何受員工法律保護所影響。此外，新股上市活動作為股權融資市場發展的一個重要晴雨表，我們的硏究結果將有助我們了解員工法律保護如何影響國家或地區性的股市發展歷程。

594713.label: Project Title(Chinese)
594713.value: 跳躍動態與跳躍風險溢價

594713.label: Project Objectives
594713.value: To propose a robust method to estimate the functions and parameters governing the jump intensity and jump size distribution To estimate the jump risk premium implied in the options prices and understand its dynamics
rows: To propose a robust method to estimate the functions and parameters governing the jump intensity and jump size distribution
To estimate the jump risk premium implied in the options prices and understand its dynamics

594713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
594713.value: Extreme events, such as market crashes, are important to market participants because they have significant impacts on the welfare of investors. Such events are modeled as jumps in the stochastic processes of asset prices. This project proposes to investigate the dynamics of jumps in asset prices, i.e., the timing and sizes of jumps. A simple and robust approach is proposed to estimate functions and parameters governing the jump dynamics. With these correctly identified functions and parameters, the jump risk premium, i.e., the price that investors pay to hedge against the risk of such extreme events, is inferred from options prices. Then, the time-series variation of the jump risk premium is analyzed. The results of this project will have important implications for asset pricing and risk management. 市場崩潰之類的極端事件對市場參與者十分重要，因為這類事件對投資者的財富有顯著影響。在資產價格的隨機過程中，這類事件用跳躍模擬。此課題研究資產價格跳躍的動態，即跳躍的時間和大小。此課題用一個簡單而穩定的方法估計有關跳躍動態的參數，並從期權價格導出跳躍的風險溢價，即投資者為規避極端事件的風險所付出的價格。此課題進而對跳躍風險溢價的時間序列上的變化進行分析。此課題的結果將對資產定價和風險管理有重要意義。

594713.label: Realisation of objectives
594713.value: To realize the first objective, we use the daily return on the S&P 500 index from 1950 to 2014 to estimate the jump dynamics of the index under the physical probability based on the methodology documented in the proposal. We estimate popular specifications of jump dynamics proposed in the literature. The jump intensity specifications include the constant jump intensity, the affine jump intensity as a function of the diffusive variance, and the autoregressive jump intensity. The jump size distributions include the normal distribution, the double exponential distribution, and the mixture of the exponential and the generalized extreme value distribution. We find that the autoregressive jump intensity fits the data better than the constant and the affine jump intensities do. The double exponential distribution works better than the normal distribution for modeling the jump sizes. A mixture of the exponential distribution and the generalized extreme value distribution further improves the fit. The improvement is due to the ability of the generalized extreme value distribution to capture the fat tail of negative jumps. For the second objective, we infer the jump risk premiums from the differences between the expected value of a jump measure under the risk-neutral probability and its physical counterpart. The jump measure under the risk-neutral probability is estimated from the S&P 500 index option prices in a model-free manner, and the one under the physical probability is estimated from the best specification of the jump arrival intensity and jump size distribution in the previous analysis. We find that the premiums of both negative jumps and positive jumps are positive most of the time, and the premium of negative jumps is larger than that of positive jumps on average. Then, we examine the dynamics of jump risk premiums using linear regressions. We regress the jump risk premiums on many widely used macroeconomic variables in the asset pricing literature, including the monthly growth rate of the personal consumer expenditures, the monthly growth rate of the industrial production, the monthly growth rate of the consumer price index, the term spread, measured by the differences in the yields on 10-year treasury bonds and 3-month treasury bills, and the credit spread, measured by the Moody’s seasoned Aaa corporate bond yield relative to the yield on 10-year treasury bonds. We also include the annual diffusive variance, and the annual jump intensity, estimated previously, since they are considered as state variables driving the asset price dynamics in the option pricing literature. We find that the jump risk premiums are high when the growths of consumption and production in the economy are low and when the credit risk and volatility are high.

594713.label: Major findings and research outcome
594713.value: We find that the model with the autoregressive jump intensity fits the S&P 500 index returns better than that with the constant jump intensity or with the jump intensity as an affine function of the diffusive variance. The autoregressive jump intensity model captures the strong clustering effects in the jump intensity process that the other specifications do not. The mixture of the exponential and generalized extreme value distribution characterizes the jump size better than the commonly used normal distribution or the double exponential distribution. The generalized extreme value distribution is especially useful in modeling the fat left tail of the return distribution. We also find that jump risks carry significant premiums which are closely related to the macroeconomic conditions. In particular, the jump risk premiums are high when the growths of consumption and production in the economy are low and when the credit risk and volatility are high. A paper based on this analysis has been presented in the Asian Finance Association Annual Conference and the European Financial Management Association Annual Conference.

594713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
594713.value: The methodology developed in this project can be applied to other major equity market indexes around the world. Some recent studies propose that jumps across many countries are mutually excited, which suggests that the jump in one country causes an increase in the conditional jump intensity of another country. The analysis in this project can be extended to include the mutually excited jumps in the autoregressive jump intensity specification. We plan to pursue the research in such a direction.

594713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
594713.value: Extreme events, such as market crashes, are important to market participants because they have significant impacts on the welfare of investors. Such events are modeled as jumps in the stochastic processes of asset prices. This study proposes a semi-parametric approach to examining jump dynamics, and finds that among popular specifications proposed in the literature, the model with an autoregressive jump intensity and a mixture of the exponential and generalized extreme value jump size distribution best characterizes the jump dynamics. This result indicates that extreme stock price movements are frequent with large magnitudes, especially for the negative jumps, and they tend to occur in clusters. The study also shows that jump risks carry significant premiums, and the jump risk premiums are high when the growths of consumption and production in the economy are low and when the credit risk and volatility are high. The result suggests that investors pay a price to insure against the jump risk because the jump risk is high when the macroeconomic condition is poor.

595013.label: Project Title(Chinese)
595013.value: 机构以及个人交易与股价崩溃

595013.label: Co - Investigator(s)
595013.value: Prof Lee, Bong Soo Dr Wang, Shu Ye

595013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
595013.value: In this project, using a unique daily institutional and individual trading dataset, we investigate the relation between stock price crashes and the trading behavior of institutional and retail investors. Specifically, first, we investigate whether the medium- and long-run crash risk−trading (and holding) relation differs for different investor groups; second, we examine whether the short-run crash–trading dynamics differs for different investor groups around stock price crash events. Our investigation relates to three strands of the literature. First, our investigation relates to the price impact literature (e.g., Kraus and Stoll, 1972; Holthausen et al., 1987). A number of studies have documented that large price changes are usually associated with high trading volumes (e.g., Gervais et al., 2001). Based on the difference of opinion (DOP) models, Hong and Stein’s (2003) predict that stock price crashes will be most pronounced around periods of heavy trading volume. We extend Hong and Stein’s prediction by conjecturing that although crash risk tends to be higher for periods with heavy overall trading volumes, the association between crashes and trading volumes could differ for different investor groups, because investors are heterogeneous. Second, our investigation relates to the theoretical prediction on the different impacts of informational and noninformational trading on stock price changes (Hellwig, 1980; Wang, 1993, 1994). In a market with asymmetrically informed investors, trades are signals of private information (Admati and Pfleiderer, 1988). Informed trading generally reduces volatility, whereas non-informed or liquidity-driven trading increases volatility (French and Roll, 1986). We hypothesize that if investor trading behavior and information asymmetry contribute to stock price crashes, the price crash-trading relation should differ for better-informed institutional investors and less-informed retail investors, and also differ for different institutional investors. Finally, our investigation relates to the investor trading behavior literature. Gervais and Odean (2001) predict that biased investors trade more (less) aggressively following market gains (losses) due to overconfidence. Odean (1999) and Barber and Odean (2000) find that investors tend to buy stocks that have recently caught their attention, and individual investors trade excessively due to overconfidence. Barber and Odean (2008) further show that the attention effect will be stronger if investors have fewer information resources. However, whether the response to crashes differs for different groups of investors in terms of the magnitude and persistence of the abnormal trading volumes, no published empirical results have been found. We investigate the dynamics between stock price crashes and trading behavior of different investor groups. 在本研究项目中我们利用一个特有的机构以及个人投资者的日交易数据库，研究股价崩溃与机构及个人投资者投资行为之间的关系。具体而言，第一，我们考察中、长期股价崩溃风险与不同投资者的交易之间的关系；第二，我们研究在股价崩溃前后短期崩溃风险与不同投资者的动态交易关系是否不同。 本研究与三类文献有关。第一，与价格影响文献有关（(例如, Kraus and Stoll, 1972; Holthausen et al., 1987)。许多研究都指出，大的股价变化通常伴随大的成交量(例如, Gervais et al., 2001)。根据“不同意见”模型（DOP），Hong and Stein’s (2003)预测，股价崩溃最可能发生在交易量巨大时期。在他们预测的基础上，我们进一步推测，尽管在交易量大的时期，股价崩溃的风险可能较高，股价崩溃与交易量之间的关系，对于不同类型的投资者可能不尽相同，因为投资者是异质的。 其次，我们的研究与知情交易与非知情交易对股价的不同影响理论预测有关(Hellwig, 1980; Wang, 1993, 1994)。在一个包含信息不对称的知情投资者的市场中，交易是内幕信息的标志(Admati and Pfleiderer, 1988)。知情交易通常降低股价的波动，然而非知情交易或流动性主导的交易则增加股价波动性(French and Roll, 1986)。我们假设，如果投资者的交易行为和信息不对称性为股价崩溃的原因，那么，股价崩溃与交易的关系，对信息较多的机构投资者和信息较少的个人投资者应该不同，对不同的机构投资者也应该不同。 最后，我们的研究与投资者交易行为文献有关。Gervais and Odean (2001)预测，由于过度自信，在市场上升（下跌）之后，有偏见的投资者交易的更具（更少）侵略性。Odean (1999) 以及 Barber和 Odean (2000) 发现，投资者倾向于购买最近引起他们注意的股票，而个人投资者会由于过度自信而过度交易。Barber和 Odean (2008)更进一步发现，投资者的信息来源越少，会越关注引起他们注意的股票。然而，就异常交易的数量和持续性而言，不同类型的投资者对股价崩溃的反应是否不同，到目前为止还没有公开发表的实证分析结果。我们考察股价崩溃与不同类型投资者的交易行为之间的动态关系。

596913.label: Project Objectives
596913.value: To introduce an innovative method known as the general-to-specific modeling with bootstrap aggregation (GETS bagging) in the specification and estimation of the models used in the Hong Kong tourism demand forecasting system (HKTDFS) (www.tourismforecasting.net) To improve the forecasting accuracy of HKTDFS with a view to providing more reliable information of the future tourism demand for both public and private sectors to assist their decision-making To incorporate GETS bagging into HKTDFS with a view to fully automating the statistical forecasting procedure To disseminate the research findings through journal publication(s).

To improve the forecasting accuracy of HKTDFS with a view to providing more reliable information of the future tourism demand for both public and private sectors to assist their decision-making

596913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
596913.value: Tourism development plays a crucial role in Hong Kong’s sustainable economic growth. Accurate forecasting of tourism demand forms a scientific and rigorous foundation for tourism stakeholders’ policy making, strategic planning and operation management, and therefore has significant economic consequences. The investigators of this project have done extensive research in advancing tourism forecasting methodologies. Their latest research output is the development of a web-based Hong Kong Tourism Demand Forecasting System (HKTDFS). Based on the general-to-specific (GETS) econometric modeling approach, HKTDFS provides accurate forecasts of tourism demand variables such as tourist arrivals, tourists’ expenditure on different product categories and the demand for hotel rooms in Hong Kong on a fully free-of-charge basis. The frequently updated forecasts have been used as key points of reference for the strategic decision making of many industry practitioners including theme parks, hotels and government agencies. Although the present methodology of HKTDFS can produce generally accurate forecasts, the consistency and stability of the forecasting performance can be further improved. In some circumstances the GETS model deduction process cannot insure that the optimal model will be reached. In other words, the decision rule for model deduction is unstable. As a result, the forecasting performance of the selected model is not the most desirable in these cases. This research is therefore designed to address these concerns by proposing a new forecasting method with a view to further improving the forecasting performance of the existing models built in HKTDFS developed by the investigators. The new method integrates a statistical technique called bootstrap aggregation or bagging into the GETS model selection process. Bagging is designed specifically to reduce forecasting errors through selecting the predictors when the decision rules are unstable. Both experimental and theoretical evidence shows that bagging can push an unstable procedure a significant step towards the goal of optimality. This research represents the first attempt to introduce the bagging technique into the tourism forecasting field, and the first attempt to integrate GETS-bagging into a web-based forecasting system. Not only does this research have its scientific merits, but also significant socio-economic impacts. We expect that it will lead to improved forecasting performance of HKTDFS. As a widely used reference point, the system will provide more rigorous support to tourism stakeholders’ strategic decision making in order to achieve sustainable development of the tourism industry and Hong Kong’s overall economic growth.

596913.label: Realisation of objectives
596913.value: The research objectives were largely achieved. For objectives 1 to 3, the research team has carried out bootstrapping estimation of the tourism demand models (bagging) using both the Hong Kong data and Australian data; and the results suggest that bagging has improved the forecasting performance considerably compared with that generated from the standard auto-regressive distributed lag modeling method. In terms of objective 4, the research team has come up with two papers (one review article and one research article). Both papers were under review/revision in the top academic journals in fields of tourism and hotel management.

596913.value: The research has generated two potential publications. First, the project reviewed extensively the latest development in tourism forecasting with a view to providing a research foundation for the current study. The review has resulted in a paper titled “New Development in Tourism and Hotel Modeling and Forecasting”, which was submitted to the International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management and has been conditionally accepted. 596913.value: The research findings of this project will help the PI to implement GETS-bagging in future forecasting projects. In particular, the PI has been carrying out a collaborative research project with the Pacific Asia Travel Association (PATA) to produce annual forecasts of tourism demand for about 40 destinations within the Asia Pacific. In order to improve the forecasting accuracy, GETS-bagging will be used in generating these forecasts with a view to improving the forecasting accuracy.

596913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
596913.value: This study introduces bootstrap aggregation (bagging) in modelling and forecasting tourism demand. The aim is to improve the forecasting accuracy of predictive regressions while considering fully automated variable selection processes which are particularly useful in industry applications. The procedures considered for variable selection is the general-to-specific (GETS) approach based on statistical inference and stepwise search procedures based on a measure of predictive accuracy (MPA). The evidence based on tourist arrivals from six source markets overwhelmingly suggests that bagging is effective in improving the forecasting accuracy of the models considered.

597013.label: Project Title(Chinese)
597013.value: 停止季度收益指导会降低机会主义的报告 行为吗？

597013.label: Project Objectives
597013.value: Does stopping quarterly guidance reduce opportunistic financial reporting of the firms, in both accrual-based and real activity-based earnings management? Does stopping quarterly guidance reduce the probability of future irregularity-driven financial restatements? Does stopping quarterly guidance improves auditors’ perception about audit risk, and therefore reduces the audit fee that is charged for the firms?
rows: Does stopping quarterly guidance reduce opportunistic financial reporting of the firms, in both accrual-based and real activity-based earnings management?
Does stopping quarterly guidance reduce the probability of future irregularity-driven financial restatements?
Does stopping quarterly guidance improves auditors’ perception about audit risk, and therefore reduces the audit fee that is charged for the firms?

597013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
597013.value: Quarterly earnings guidance, managers’ public forecasts of forthcoming earnings is a common practice among corporate US to reduce the information asymmetry between the insiders and outside investors. However, such practice has been criticized by opponents who assert that it creates a myopic focus of the investors on the short-term performance and as a result managers may resort to opportunistic reporting behavior to cater to the whim of the investors’ focus on the short-term performance (see, for example, Krehmeyer and Orsagh 2006). Some of the opportunistic reporting could be at the expense of long-term value creation activities for the shareholders. As such, there have been calls for managers to stop providing earnings guidance (see Krehmeyer and Orsagh 2006). Some firms stopped providing quarterly earnings guidance starting with Coca Cola, AT&A and others, stating by doing so, it can redirect managers’ effort and attention to long-term value creation and at the same time does not need to worry about short-term performance. A recent survey released by the National Investor Relations Institute (Johnson 2009) suggests that CFOs have slowly tried to shift investors' attention to such other metrics as expected revenue, same-store sales, or capital expenditures than earnings. In this project, we attempt to examine whether stopping quarterly earnings guidance reduces opportunistic financial reporting or not. In particular, we will focus on three measures of financial reporting quality: accrual-based earnings management, real activities management, and the incidence of irregularity-driven accounting restatements. Both accrual-based and real activity-based earnings management can help managers to achieve the desired earnings numbers, as such they are viewed as opportunistic financial reporting. Future restatements that are driven by irregularities are corrections of past misstatements in the financial reporting, and therefore is a good measure of opportunistic financial reporting. If stopping quarterly earnings guidance reduces opportunistic financial reporting, we should observe a decreased in three measures after cessation of quarterly earnings guidance. In addition, we will examine auditors’ perception regarding the relation between quarterly earnings guidance and financial reporting quality. If auditors perceive that stopping quarterly earnings guidance reduce the audit risk associated with the opportunist financial reporting, which in turn increases the probability of misstatement, a primary audit risk that auditors are concerned with, auditors will decrease audit fee after the cessation of quarterly earnings guidance. 季度盈利指导，暨经理人公开预测即将收入，是用于减少企业内部人士和外部投资者之间的信息不对称的一个常见做法。然而，这种做法已受到批评它会创建投资者的短视，以其导致的结果可能是企业管理层诉诸机会主义的报告行为，以迎合投资者的着眼于短期业绩的兴致 （例如，见 Krehmeyer 和 Orsagh 2006 年）。一些投机取巧的报告，可能会损害股东的长期价值创造活动。为此，业界曾要求管理层停止提供盈利指导 （见 Krehmeyer 和 Orsagh 2006 年）。可口可乐，AT & A 和其他一些公司，也开始停止提供每季度盈利指导，希望通过这样做，可以重新导向管理层的努力方向，致力于企业长期的价值创造，并在同一时间不需要担心短期表现。 在此项目中，我们尝试检查停止季度盈利指导能否降低机会主义财务报告。我们将分析三项度量财务报告质量的指标： 以权责发生制为基础的盈余管理、 以实际活动为基础的盈余管理和不合规范驱动的会计转述的发生率。前两个基于权责发生制和基于真正活动的盈余管理可以帮助管理层实现预期的收益数字，因此他们被视为机会主义的财务报告。由未来转述更正过去违规行为/错报的财务报告，也是度量机会主义的财务报告的好指标。如果停止季度盈利指导减少机会主义的财务报告，我们应该观测到这三项度量指标在停止季度盈利指导后减少。此外，我们将分析从外部审计员的角度，他们会不会认为季度盈利指导与财务报告质量有关系。如果外部审计员认为停止季度盈利指导减少机会主义的报告行为， 审计风险下降，那么审计费在此以后也会有所下降。

597013.label: Major findings and research outcome
597013.value: We find that investors in firms that stop quarterly guidance are composed of a larger (smaller) proportion of long-term (short-term) institutions, put more (less) weight on long-term (short-term) earnings in firm valuation, become more (less) sensitive to analysts’ long-term (short-term) earning forecast revisions, and are less likely to dismiss CEOs for missing quarterly earnings targets by small amounts relative to investors in firms that continue to issue quarterly earnings guidance. In addition, we find there is some evidence of reduction of managerial myopia in terms of a reduction in real-activities based earnings management and an increase in R&D and capital expenditure investments. The working paper is now accepted for publication by Review of Accounting Studies.

597013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
597013.value: Providing quarterly earnings guidance by managers has been criticized for creating short-term pressure on managers and inducing an excessive fixation by investors and managers on short-term performance. In this project, we investigate whether stopping quarterly guidance can reduce the myopic behavior of investors and managers. We find a reduction in short-term oriented investors as well a reduction in investors' fixation on short-term performance after firms stop guidance compared to a control group of firms who continue to provide quarterly guidance. We also find some evidence of a reduction in real activities-based earnings management and an increase in R&D investment and capital expenditure. Our study adds to the literature by providing new evidence of the benefit of stopping quarterly earnings guidance: the reduction of short-termism among investors.

597213.label: Project Objectives
597213.value: To examine how status differentials serve as disciplinary mechanisms in governing inter-firm relationships and develop a theoretical framework for this proposition. To apply the developed theoretical framework in the context of corporate takeovers. To offer practical implications for governments and firm decision-makers on developing M&A strategies.
rows: To examine how status differentials serve as disciplinary mechanisms in governing inter-firm relationships and develop a theoretical framework for this proposition.
To apply the developed theoretical framework in the context of corporate takeovers.
To offer practical implications for governments and firm decision-makers on developing M&A strategies.

597213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
597213.value: This study explores the implications of inter-firm status differentials for firm behaviors in corporate takeover transactions. I argue that the more the status differential between two firms is aligned with expectations of their roles embedded in the specific economic activity, the easier it is for them to agree on the appropriate means to reach consensus on the given transaction. I plan to test these ideas using the empirical context of the U.S. corporate takeover market. Specifically, I predict that the greater the status differential between an acquirer and a target, the more positively the market reacts to both the acquirer and the target upon the announcement of the acquisition deal, the more likely it is for the deal to be completed, and the acquirer is also more likely to achieve better post-acquisition performance. I discuss the theoretical implications of our study for corporate takeover research, status theory, and inter-firm transaction and cooperation.

597213.label: Realisation of objectives
597213.value: The three listed main objectives have been fully addressed through the investigation of this proposal. In this research, we aim to examine how inter-firm status differentials can work as a disciplinary mechanism to govern the collaboration process in inter-firm relationships. We developed a comprehensive theoretical model first and based on this framework, we collected data from the corporate takeover context. We developed specific hypotheses for this empirical setting. utilized adequate analytical methods, we found sufficient supports to our theoretical predictions. We also generated important implications for research on inter-firm relationships and social status, and also our findings have prominent implications for practitioners. Specifically, our research contributes to the field in the following aspects. First, the existing research on corporate takeover has paid much attention to the firm-level characteristics of both acquirers and targets, but to our best knowledge, limited efforts have been devoted to exploring the implications of firm status for the takeover process. Firm status is expected to affect corporate takeovers because firms are deeply embedded in social contexts and status has been suggested as one major social factor governing inter-firm relationships. This research hopes to inspire corporate takeover researchers to incorporate the construct of social status into their landscape. This study also has important implications for status research. Prior research on firm status tends to emphasize that by teaming up with low-status partners, high-status firms will suffer from a lowering of status. Nevertheless, status-heterophilous partnerships between firms are not uncommon and it is important to explore the motivations and implications behind such affiliations for both parties. Our findings show that sometimes cross-status cooperation between firms can be beneficial and high-status partners can benefit from status-heterophilous partnerships by gaining genuine cooperation from their counterparts. This should encourage researchers to examine the conditions under which firms with different levels of status can transact smoothly and benefit each other. Our research also has important managerial implications. Corporate takeovers are important drivers for firm growth and economic development. However, takeover activities are known to be full of uncertainties and the outcomes are unpredictable, with a high failure rate. To succeed in managing corporate takeover, our paper’s findings suggest that, first, senior executives should incorporate a firm’s status into their decision landscape. A firm’s status is an intangible asset. This asset not only provides opportunities and benefits when the firm is transacting with other firms, but also governs the transaction process. Second, senior managers should consider not only their firm’s absolute status, but also its status relative to that of the party with which it is transacting. For a particular takeover transaction, it is important for the two parties’ status levels to match their expected roles during the transaction, as this would significantly influence the success and outcomes of the deal. Third, our research also offers insights for other inter-firm cooperation and transaction contexts, including strategic alliances and joint ventures. When a firm is choosing a partner to build an alliance or develop a joint venture with, its senior managers should prudently consider the status differential between the two firms because this explains why the alliance or joint venture succeeds or fails to achieve the original strategic goal. Our research has generated multiple outputs, including a few top-tier or good publications. We also presented our findings in important international conferences. Overall, we believe the research objectives of this project have been well achieved.

597213.label: Major findings and research outcome
597213.value: The major findings of this project are as follows: We test our hypotheses using a large sample of takeover transactions among U.S. public firms that took place between1990 and 2008. When the acquirer has a higher status than the target, (1) markets will react more positively to both the acquirer and the target around the deal announcement; (2) the takeover is more likely to be completed, and (3) the acquirer is more likely to achieve better post-acquisition performance. This project has generated a few top-tier and good publications. I explicitly acknowledged the GRF fund support in the "acknowledgement" section of each of the publications.
