601613.value: 玻璃化轉變是凝聚態物理和統計物理中最重要的懸而未決的問題之一。當液體被冷卻至玻璃化轉變點，動力學過程不僅大幅度減慢，在時間與空間上也變得越來越不均勻。找出動力學的這種不均勻性和靜態結構之間的關聯非常重要，但是這種關聯往往卻過於細微難以被檢測到。在這裡，我們提出實驗上利用單層膠體橢球來研究玻璃化轉變並找出動力學與結構之間的關聯。我們的初步研究結果表明，當橢球長徑比足夠大時，動力學與結構之間的關聯就會浮現出來。 膠體已被證明是研究玻璃化轉變的優秀模型系統，因為單個微米大小的膠體粒子的運動軌跡可以直接由顯微鏡觀察並做圖像處理得到。至目前為止，對球形膠體粒子組成的膠體玻璃已有很多研究，成功地加深了玻璃化轉變在微觀層次上的理解。但對非球形粒子組成的膠體玻璃的研究極少。其實，非球形粒子才能更好地模擬具有各向異性的形狀或相互作用的分子。我們在由橢球組成的膠體玻璃的開拓性實驗中觀察到一個兩步玻璃化轉變：過冷液體變為取向玻璃態，再變為傳統玻璃態【1】 。我們最近的未發表的實驗進一步表明，當長徑比足夠小時，兩步轉變變為一步常規的玻璃化轉變。 本系統中的新型取向玻璃，傳統玻璃和過冷液體提供了一個理想的平台對很多問題進行研究，例如平移和旋轉的不均勻性之間有什麼區別和聯繫，以及他們是如何影響結構和玻璃化轉變的？除了玻璃化轉變，我們計劃測出二維橢球的完整相圖，包括旋轉相和向列相。此外，我們還計劃在橢球之間加入可調長程排斥力或短程吸引力，來研究粒子間相互作用是如何影響玻璃化轉變的。這將使當前的不可調系統升級為可調系統，從而大量新問題可以被研究。令人驚訝的是，大多數問尚未被計算機仿真研究，因此，我們將對實驗進行仿真。 這些開拓性實驗能夠測量非球形粒子組成的過冷液體和玻璃態中的單粒子動力學量。基於我們初步實驗中的豐富而令人驚訝的結果，未來的實驗和仿真期望能產生豐碩的成果，這對凝聚態物理有相當的重要性。

601613.label: Realisation of objectives
601613.value: We fabricated colloidal ellipsoids with various aspect ratios and successfully assembled monodispersed ellipsoids into glassy monolayers after overcame some technique difficulties. We measured the motions of ellipsoids by image processing and particle tracking, and obtained lots of high quality data which enable the study of long-time dynamics, structure and their correlations. To measure the dynamic heterogeneity in objective 1, we measured fast-translational, fast-rotational, slow-translational and slow-rotational clusters in each video frame. We also measured structural quantities including the structural entropy, the glassy structure for both translational and rotational degrees of freedom. By comparing the spatial distribution of our measured dynamic heterogeneities and local structural quantities, we found clear structure-dynamic correlations. The results were further confirmed by our simulations. Therefore the objective 1 is 100% achieved and the results were published in a top journal Nature Communications in 2014. We found that ellipsoids with aspect ratio < 2.5 can only form conventional glasses, while those with aspect ratio > 2.5 can form orientational glass at middle densities and conventional glass at high densities. We discovered distinct dynamics-structure correlations for ellipsoids with aspect ratio > 2.5 and < 2.5. We further provide the explanation for this novel phenomenon which has not been observed before. We found that the fragility depends on the anisotropy of the particles for the first time. Some of this part was published in ref.[1] and others will be in an unpublished manuscript aiming for a top journal: “Dynamic and structural critical-like behaviors of colloidal ellipsoid glass formers”. These results fulfill 90% of objective 2. We did not explore the aging of the glasses because it is very time consuming and needs continuously monitoring the sample for days during which the experimental condition can hardly maintain constant. We discovered rich critical behaviors in these glassy systems which is very important and beyond the two objectives in our original plan, hence we shift our focus to the critical behaviors. Since this GRF601613 is our only grant about glass research, it also supported our studies about three other glassy systems: (1) theoretical and simulation studies of spin glasses’ phase spaces; (2) experiments and simulations about buckled colloidal crystals composed of either PMMA and NIPA spheres which exhibit glassy dynamics; (3) glass monolayers formed by vapor deposition of silica colloidal spheres which reveals the surface relaxation modes. The research about systems 1-3 are published in Phys. Rev. E, Phys. Rev. X and Nature Communications. Phys. Rev. X is the top journal in physics. These three projects are beyond the scope of the objectives, but all about 2D glassy systems.

601613.label: Major findings and research outcome
601613.value: We discover the structural signatures for both translational and rotational dynamics in monolayers of colloidal ellipsoids by video microscopy experiments and computer simulations. The correlation lengths of the dynamic slowest-moving clusters, the static glassy clusters, the static local structural entropy and the dynamic heterogeneity follow the same power-law divergence, suggesting that the kinetic slowing down is caused by a decrease in the structural entropy and an increase in the size of the glassy cluster. Ellipsoids with different aspect ratios exhibit single- or double-step glass transitions with distinct dynamic heterogeneities. These findings demonstrate that the particle shape anisotropy has important effects on the structure and dynamics of the glass. The results were published in Nature Communications in 2014. We further found various critical-like behaviors from cluster sizes, correlations, susceptibilities and finite-size analyses, and the corresponding manuscript is under preparation. Whether and how geometrically frustrated spins or charges in clean crystals exhibit glassy dynamics remain elusive due to the lack of microscopic measurements. We employed buckled monolayer colloidal crystals to mimic frustrated antiferromagnets and measure single-spin dynamics using video microscopy. Both attractive and repulsive colloidal crystals buckled into zigzag stripes with glassy dynamics at low effective temperatures in experiment and simulation. The simple local spin configurations enable uncovering correlations among structure, dynamics, and soft vibrational modes. Machine learning analysis further reveals facilitated dynamics to be an important mechanism of structural relaxation. Moreover, our simulation reveals a similar structure and dynamics in lattice Coulomb liquids. Hence, spin-lattice coupling and long-range interaction can similarly lift degeneracy, induce a rugged landscape, and, thus, produce glassy dynamics. The results were published in Phys. Rev. X in 2017. Vapor deposition can produce ultrastable glasses which are similar to conventional glasses aged over thousands of years. The highly mobile surface layer is believed to accelerate the relaxation of vapor-deposited glasses, but its microscopic kinetics has not been experimentally observed. We study the deposition growth kinetics of a colloidal glass at the single-particle level in both experiment and simulation. We observe that newly deposited particles in the surface layer relax via out-of-cage diffusion of individual particles, while particles in the deeper middle layer relax via activation of cooperative-rearrangement regions. Such novel middle layer has not been resolved before, which cast new light on the glass relaxation during vapor deposition. The results was published in Nature Communications in 2017.

601613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
601613.value: We studied glass monolayers composed of ellipsoids [x] and vapor-deposition growth of colloidal glass monolayers composed of spheres [x]. Combining these two experiments can produce a novel and interesting experiment: a dilute ellipsoid monolayer sediment along a slightly tilted substrate can mimic the vapor-deposition growth of a glass composed of anisotropic particles. This enables the first observation of vapor-glass transition for anisotropic particles at the single-particle level. Comparing with our previous system composed of spheres, ellipsoids have measurable rotations and more types of local orders which can better mimic vapor-deposited molecular glasses and therefore should provide richer results.

601613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
601613.value: The nature of the glass transition is one of the most important scientific open questions selected by the prestigious journal “Science”. When a supercooled liquid transforms to a glass, i.e. an amorphous solid, its structure remains almost the same, but the dynamics drastically slows down. To solve this major puzzle, great efforts have been made to search for subtle structural features associated with the dynamic slowing down, and some structure-dynamic correlations have been successfully discovered in glasses composed of spherical particles. Here we discover structure-dynamic correlations in glasses composed of anisotropic particles (ellipsoids) with the single-particle resolution for the first time. Our second achievement is the observation of glassy dynamics in a crystal at the single-particle level for the first time. Such behavior has been observed in some defect-free and dopant-free molecular crystals with magnetic frustrations, but the mechanism is not clear and lacks microscopic observation. Here we observed the glassy dynamics at the microscopic level in a colloidal crystal with geometrical frustration. Our third achievement is the discovery of the novel glass relaxation modes near the glass surface with the single-particle resolution for the first time.

601813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
601813.value: This project deals with applications of geometry, probability theory and Fourier analysis in construction of heat kernels and fundamental solutions for elliptic and sub-elliptic operators. Understanding the behavior of heat kernels is an important step in the study of Riemannian/sub-Riemannian geometry. We are interested to find explicit formulas for heat kernels and fundamental solutions for both elliptical and sub-elliptic operators using different methods such as geometric, stochastic or analytic. Some of the heat kernels computed in this project can be the regarded as solutions of some Black-Scholes' type equations and might have great financial value. We will also study a sub-Riemannian version of the Poincare Lemma regarding integrability conditions of a sub-elliptic system for which the number of differential equations is less than the dimension of the space. 本計劃將會應用幾何，概率論及傅立葉分析以構造橢圓及亞橢圓算子的熱核和基本解。理解熱核的性質是黎曼幾何及亞黎曼幾何研究中的一個重要步驟。 我們的主要興趣是在於如何利用幾何，隨機及分析的不同方法求出橢圓及亞橢圓算子的熱核和基本解的明確表達式。其中一些熱核的特例可以作為某些布萊克－舒尓斯型方程的解， 因此我們的研究可能對金融學具有價值。 對一類方程的個數少於空間的維數的亞橢圓系統， 我們還會研究所對應的亞黎曼型的龐加萊引理。

602113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
602113.value: Aromaticity has been one of the most fascinating topics in chemistry. Organic aromatic compounds (for example, benzene) are well known. Formal replacement of hydrocarbyl groups in organic aromatic compounds by heteroatom groups gives heteroaromatic compounds. Heteroaromatic compounds containing a main-group element have been extensively studied. Recently, there has been much interest in the development of the chemistry of transition metal containing heteroaromatic compounds, especially six-membered aromatic metallacycles such as metallabenzenes and metallabenzynes. Although interesting, the aromatic chemistry of transition metal containing metallacarbocycles with other ring sizes is underdeveloped. Tropylium cation is a well-known seven-membered aromatic organic species. Heteroaromatics derived from formal replacement of a CH+ group in tropylium cation by an isolobal group 13 metal containing group are also known. In principle, it may also be possible to obtain analogous seven-membered aromatic metallacycles containing a transition metal fragment. However, such a possibility has not been previously explored, although interesting non-planar (and therefore non-aromatic) metallacycloheptatrienes have attracted much attention for their relevance to transition metal mediated cyclotrimerization of alkynes to give benzene derivatives. The main objectives of this proposed research are (i) to develop synthetic methods to synthesize seven-membered unsaturated transition metal containing metallacyles, and (ii) to explore their aromatic and organometallic properties. 芳香性是具有特殊化學性質的化合物。芳香性有机化合物（例如，苯）是化学家们都熟悉的的芳香化合物。把苯及苯炔分子中的基团用含杂原子的基团代替能得到杂环芳香化合物。许多含主族元素的杂环芳香化合物已被已被广泛地研究。近年来人们也对含过渡金属的杂环芳香化合物（例如，六元环的金属苯及金属苯炔）产生了兴趣。 本项目的主要目的在于发展芳香性七元金属杂环的化学。主要研究内容包括（1）发展合成七元金属杂环的方法，（2）探讨它们的芳香性及金属有机性质性質。

602113.label: Realisation of objectives
602113.value: The main objectives of the project are (i) to develop synthetic methods to synthesize unsaturated transition metal containing metallacycles and (ii) to explore properties of the metallacycles. To achieve the objectives, we have carried out the following research work. Reactions of halometal complexes with lithiated reagents have often been used to make metal alkyl complexes. We have therefore carried out reactions of dilithiated reagents with late transition metal dihalo complexes LnMX2 (e.g. PdCl2(dppe)) for the preparation of metallacycles. Oxidative addition reactions of arylhalides can give metal aryl complexes. We have explored oxidative addition reactions of various functionalized arylhalides with Pd(0) and Pt(0) complexes to prepare precursor complexes for the construction of metallacycles. In efforts to make metallacycles containing a W-C double bond, we have prepared alkyne-functionalized tungsten carbene complexes, and studied their cyclization reactions induced by photolysis or reactions with electrophiles and nucleophiles. Through the work, we have made several tungsten-containing metallacycles. Reactions of diazoalkanes and phosphorus ylides with transition metal complexes can give complexes containing an M-C double bond. We have explored the possibility of making metallacycles containing an M-C double bond by using reactions of functionalized diazoalkanes and phosphorus ylides with W, Os and Ru complexes. Interesting metallacycles such as metallaanthracynes and metallaphenanthrynes have been successfully obtained through this approach. In efforts to develop synthetic methods to make metallacycles containing a M-C triple bond, we have explored new ways to make carbyne complexes. For example, we found that the rhenium complexes such as ReH5(PR3)3 and [Re(dppm)3]I can readily react with a variety of terminal alkynes in the presence of an acid to give rhenium carbyne complexes, including ones that could be manipulated to give metallacycles. We have also developed routes to make new tungsten and osmium carbyne complexes. Metal-alkyl complexes could undergo metathesis reactions with terminal alkynes to give alkynyl complexes. We have used the strategy to make 12-membered metallacycles by intermolecular metathesis reactions of rhenium alkyl complexes bearing a terminal alkyne functional group. We have also explored the use of eletrocyclization reactions for construction of metallacycles. For example, osmabenzynes have been successfully made through electrocyclization of osmium alkynyl-allenylcarbene complexes generated by reactions of haloosmium allenylcarbene complexes with gold or copper alkynyls. To evaluate aromatic properties of metallacycles, we have calculated NICS and ASE values of various metallacycles. To evaluate chemical properties of metallacycles, we have studied their reactions with reagents such as Br2, HCl, alkene and alkynes.

602113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
602113.value: Monocyclic metallacycles with ring sizes from three to twelve atoms are now known experimentally. It is of interest to carry out detailed theoretical studies to compare properties of the metallacycles. We found that d2 Re(V) carbyne complexes can undergo alkyne metathesis reactions. It is worthwhile to study the activity of other low valent carbyne complexes for alkyne metathesis reactions. We have found that alkyne-functionalized phosphorus ylides can readily react with OsCl2(PPh3)3 to give metallacycles containing a formal osmium-carbon triple bond within the ring. It would be of interest to explore the possibility to extend the chemistry to make analogous metallacycles with other metals or a more extended structure.

602113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
602113.value: Aromaticity has been one of the most fascinating topics in chemistry. The prototype aromatic compound is benzene and many hydrocarbons are aromatic according to the Hückel electron-counting rule. Formal replacement of a hydrocarbyl group in aromatic hydrocarbons by an isolobal heteroatom group could give heteroatom-containing aromatic compounds. Recently, there has been much interest in the development of the chemistry of aromatic metallacycles derived from formal replacement of a hydrocarbyl group in organic aromatic compounds by a transition metal fragment. Although impressive progress has been made in the chemistry of six-membered aromatic metallacycles such as metallabenzenes and metallabenzynes, the chemistry of aromatic metallacycles with a ring size other than six is in general much less developed. The main purpose of this project research was to develop synthetic methods to synthesize such compounds and to explore their properties. We have successfully prepared interesting new metallacycles such as dimetalladehydro[12]annulenes, metallaanthracynes and metallaphenanthrynes.

602213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
602213.value: 近年来，有关高频金融数据的研究越来越受到人们的关注。随之也产生出各式各样的金融模型。例如，伊藤扩散模型，纯跳模型，扩散与跳混合模型等等。在实际中，如果给定一组数据，我们又如何去判定与选择哪一类模型哪？由于错误的模型选择会导致很严重的后果，所以这个问题的研究显得尤其重要。该研究项目就是围绕这一问题展开的。我们想寻找一些简单且实用的统计方法去选择合适的金融模型。 另外，我们还想研究一般的半鞅过程中波动率的研究。这些问题的研究不仅有理论上的价值，而且还有实际上的意义。

Here we investigate how to handle multiple transactions, particularly in the context of estimating the integrated volatility and integrated quarticity, which are of great interest in financial econometrics. Their performances are confirmed by simulation studies. The estimators are also applied to real-world problems.

602213.label: Major findings and research outcome
602213.value: Pure-jump processes have been increasingly popular in modeling high frequency financial data, partially due to their versatility and flexibility. In the meantime, several statistical tests have been proposed in the literature to check the validity of using pure-jump models. However, these tests suffer from several drawbacks, such as requiring rather stringent conditions and having slow rates of convergence. Here, we propose a different test to check whether the process underlying high-frequency data can be modeled by a pure-jump process. The new test is based on the realized characteristic function, and is applicable much more generally than previous tests; for example, it is robust to jumps of infinite variation and flexible modeling of the diffusion component. Simulation studies justify our findings and the test is also applied to real high-frequency financial data. The phenomenon of multiple transactions at each time point is a common occurrence for high-frequency financial data because of the heavy trading of the market and limitation of the recording mechanism. This situation has existed for many years, but has become more common in recent years because of heavier trading. Surprisingly, there have been few studies on this important issue, except for some ad hoc approaches to treat multiple transactions. Here, we investigate how to handle multiple transactions, particularly in the context of estimating the integrated volatility and integrated quarticity, which are of great interest in financial econometrics. Two approaches are proposed for this purpose, and their asymptotic properties are investigated. Their performances are confirmed by simulation studies. The estimators are also applied to some real world problems. The work represents only the first step in this direction. It is widely accepted that certain financial data exhibit long memory or long dependence, and that the observed data usually possess noise. In the continuous time situation, the fractional Brownian motion and its extension are an important class of models to characterize the long memory or short memory of data, and Hurst parameter H is an index to describe the degree of dependence. Here, we estimate the Hurst parameter of a discretely sampled fractional integral process corrupted by noise. We use the pre-average method to diminish the impact of noise and obtain the smoothed data, and estimate the Hurst parameter from the smoothed data. The asymptotic properties such as consistency and asymptotic normality of the estimator are established. Simulations for evaluating the performance of the estimator are conducted.

602213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
602213.value: In this project, we tackled problems related to high-frequency financial data. There remains many other interesting problems to be studied in our future research plan. For instance, we would like to explore how to apply some of the findings in this project to some real data problems. Also, some of the settings are still stronger than necessary, and might be relaxed in future work. The findings could also be applied in portfolio selection, and other real-life problems.

602213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
602213.value: Integrated volatility and jumps are two important aspects of financial market. Therefore there have been many studies in the literature under different settings. In this project, we studied these issues under more general and more realistic settings and obtained interesting results. These findings are of both theorectical and practical interests.

602313.label: Project Objectives
602313.value: Develop two-player R&D race models under mixed duopoly of a public firm and a private firm. The hazard rate of arrival of the innovation is dependent on the knowledge accumulation. The market uncertainty of the innovative product will be modeled by assuming that the revenue flows to the R&D firms are proportional to some stochastic fundamental state variable. We will identify the criterion of social welfare maximization for the public firm. We will apply the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman approach to derive the governing equations for the real game models with stochastic control state variables. Construct effective numerical schemes based on the policy iteration approach and Markov chain approximation techniques to find the numerical solution to the stochastic R&D game models. Special precautions will be taken to prescribe the numerical auxiliary conditions. We will examine the mathematical conditions required for the convergence of the numerical calculations. Examine how a public firm may play an important role in mitigating the problem of over-investment in R&D activities through the adoption of public policies of allowing input and output spillovers in order to achieve social optimality of R&D activities. We will also investigate how the two competing firms adopt their optimal strategies of choosing the level of R&D efforts in response to various market conditions and technological uncertainties.

602313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
602313.value: In this project, I propose two-player real stochastic game models for investigating the impact of input and output spillovers on research and development (R&D) races under a mixed duopoly of a public research institute and a private firm. The well-known common pool problem states that there will be over-investment in R&D in the events of zero input spillovers of R&D efforts and winner-take-all games. The mixed duopoly considered in our models includes a social welfare maximizing publicly funded research institute that is competing in a two-player R&D race against a profit maximizing private firm. In our proposed real stochastic game models, the stochastic revenue flow rates of the two firms generated from the innovative product are assumed to be scalar multiples of a stochastic fundamental state variable. The level of output spillover is modeled by the various choices of appropriability factors in the revenue flow rates. Assuming positive input spillovers of R&D efforts, the hazard rates of innovative success can be enhanced by the research efforts of the competing firm. The public policies can be enforced by choosing the level of input and output spillovers from the public research institute to the private firm. In addition, the level of research efforts in the public firm through government funds would be treated as a stochastic control variable in our stochastic game models. The hazard rate of innovation of the public firm is assumed to have path dependence on the accumulation of research efforts. The private firm and public firm choose the relevant optimal strategy of research effort to maximize the firm value function and social welfare, respectively. On the mathematical aspects of the project, effective numerical schemes based on the policy iteration approach and Markov chain approximation techniques will be constructed to determine the numerical solution of the stochastic game models. Special considerations will be taken in the prescription of the numerical auxiliary conditions and stability requirements in the numerical calculations. The mathematical tools adopted in the proposed continuous time stochastic control models go beyond the discrete time non-stochastic models in the existing literature on R&D races under a mixed duopoly. The proposed project aims to examine how a public firm may play an important role in mitigating the common pool problem through a rich set of public policies of allowing spillovers and subsidies in order to achieve social optimality of R&D activities. 在這個項目中，我提出了一個二人的真實隨機博弈模型，希望以此來研究在一所公立研究機構和一所私人公司的混合雙寡頭壟斷下，研發投入和成果的外溢對於研究與發展（R&D）競爭的影響。總所周知，在研發投入外溢為零並且贏家通吃的情況下，研究與發展競爭會出現常見的過度投資公池問題。在我們的混合雙寡頭模型中，我們所考慮的研究與發展的博弈競賽是由一所以最大化社會福利為目標的公共資助型研究機構和一所以最大化其公司利潤為目標的私人公司組成。除此之外，在我們提出的真實隨機博弈模型中，成功研發創新產品對兩所公司帶來的收益率是隨機產生的。這裡我們認為收益率是一個隨機的基本狀態變量的標量倍數。而成果外溢的水平則通過對收益率不同比例的專屬權來模擬。另外，我們還假設公立研究機構有著正的研發投入外溢，那麼與之競爭的公司的創新成功率也會因此相應提高。在此，我們可以通過改變公共研究機構的研發投入外溢水平和成果外溢水平來調整公共政策。同時，在我們的隨機博弈模型中，通過政府資金資助的公立研究機構的研究工作水平將被視為一個隨機控制變量。而我們假設其創新成功率會對創新研究工作的積累有路徑依賴。在以上的競爭前提下，私人公司和公立機構將分別選取相應的最優化研究策略從而最大化企業的價值和社會福利。在此項目的數學方面，我們基於策略迭代法和馬爾可夫鏈近似技術，構造了有效的數值方案用以確定隨機博弈模型的數值解。同時我們也在數值計算所需的輔助條件和穩定性上採取了特殊的考慮。在現今有關混合雙寡頭壟斷下的研究與發展競爭文獻中，我們在所提出的連續時間型隨機控制優化模型中所採用的數學工具已經超越了離散時間型的非隨機模。該項目旨在探討公立機構如何能通過一系列關於允許研發投入和成果溢出以及政府補貼等公共政策在減輕公池問題中發揮到重要的作用，從而達到研究與發展活動的社會最優化。

602313.label: Realisation of objectives
602313.value: The three objectives stated in the proposal have been well realized, as demonstrated by the publication of 3 research papers in refereed journals. Frankly speaking, there have been no under-achievements. The details of the achievements of the projects are stated below. First, we have developed a finite-time real option model with stochastic control that explores the optimal strategy of R&D effort adopted by a firm engaging in R&D in the development of an innovative product. Our R&D stochastic control model includes market uncertainty and technological uncertainty, and the firm is allowed to adopt its optimal strategy of R&D effort as control together with the right to abandon the R&D project. While most real option models on R&D assume perpetuity for simplicity of analysis, we consider the more realistic modeling where the new product is based on technologies that have a finite life span. Also, we model the hazard rate of arrival to depend on the current R&D effort and knowledge accumulation in the R&D process, so the hazard rate is nonmemoryless. We manage to present the HJB formulation of the stochastic control model in combination with the linear complementarity formulation of the optimal stopping rule of abandonment. An efficient finite difference algorithm coupled with policy iteration and penalty approximation has been developed to solve for the optimal control strategy of R&D effort. Special attention has been taken in the choice of discretization of the HJB equation so that convergence of the numerical solution to the viscosity solution of the HJB equation is guaranteed. We performed extensive numerical studies on the optimal control of R&D effort with respect to market conditions and knowledge stock. We found that when the calendar time is approaching the expiration date of the technologies, it is optimal for the firm to abandon the R&D project at any level of the profit flow rate. Hence, for finite time horizon R&D models, the right of abandonment is worthy. Taking the stochastic profit flow rate as a proxy of the market conditions, the firm increases its R&D effort with an increasing level of profit flow rate and decreasing volatility of the stochastic profit flow rate. Also, our model exhibits a phenomenon similar to the “pure knowledge effect”, where the firm may choose optimally to put off R&D effort when the knowledge stock reaches certain threshold value (though the R&D project is kept in progress). This threshold value depends on the current level of the stochastic profit flow rate. In the next stage of the project, we consider extending the existing framework of stochastic control R&D model with knowledge stock to R&D race between two competing firms. Also, we include the spillover effects of knowledge accumulation from one firm to its rival. Under a two-firm R&D race model, one has to analyze various types of strategic equilibriums to be adopted by the two firms and the associated first-mover and second-mover advantages. We have developed a stochastic control model under the setting of mixed duopoly for the R&D race with input and output spillovers. In addition, the effect of knowledge accumulation is considered so that the past knowledge stock also contributes to the hazard rate of arrival of the innovative product. We present the HJB formulation of the R&D race model and apply the finite difference scheme to solve for the private firm value and its optimal control of R&D expenditure simultaneously using the technique of policy iteration. The optimal R&D effort of the private firm increases almost linearly with the profit flow rate and decreases with the knowledge stock. However, the optimal R&D effort of the public firm does not reveal a monotonic pattern against the profit flow rate. This is because the public firm’s R&D effort is adjusted as a trade-off between acceleration of the arrival of the new product and excessive total R&D efforts expended in the society. We also performed various sensitivity tests on the optimal R&D effort of the private firm and public firm with respect to various levels of spillover rate and knowledge stock factor. We find that the input spillover rate has a relatively smaller effect on the optimal R&D efforts of both firms. However, the knowledge stock and output spillover have more significant impact on the R&D effort. We find that both firms reduce their R&D expenditure to take advantage of the past accumulated knowledge when the knowledge stock factors increase. Also, when the appreciation rate is extremely high or low, over-investment or free-rider phenomenon is observed. The public firm has its role to mitigate inefficiency of R&D expenditure by setting an appropriate level of output spillover.

602313.label: Major findings and research outcome
602313.value: We construct the stochastic control model under a mixed duopoly R&D race between the profit-maximizing private firm and welfare-maximizing public firm. In the two-person race for the random arrival of the discovery of an innovative product, we take the control variable to be the private firm’s R&D expenditure while the R&D effort of the public firm is fixed. The optimal control is determined so as to maximize the private firm’s value function subject to market uncertainty arising from the revenue flow of the new innovative product. Our R&D race model also incorporates the impact of spillovers and knowledge stocks on the hazard rate of arrival of R&D success. The numerical Markov chain approximation scheme is constructed to solve the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation of the stochastic control model via discretization of the state variables as Markov chain and policy iteration for the optimal control. We conduct various sensitivity tests with varying model parameters that analyze the effects of input spillover, output spillover and knowledge stock on the optimal control policy and value functions of both competing firms. The R&D effort of the private firm is found to be increasing with the profit flow rate. On the other hand, when the profit flow rate is sufficiently low, the optimal effort level may decrease with increasing private firm's knowledge stock and output spillover. The impact of input spillover on the optimal control policy and value functions is seen to be relatively small. Related to effective numerical techniques for solving the stochastic control model, we make comparative studies on efficiency, reliability and versatility of the Markov chain approximation approach with the usual finite difference scheme with policy iteration. We also construct effective finite difference schemes for finding the optimal R&D effort adopted by a firm that engages in R&D of an innovative product, assuming the impact on knowledge accumulation on the arrival of the new product. Moreover, we develop the real options game models that analyze the R&D competition between asymmetric firms with spillovers. Three journal papers have been published in refereed research journals that summarize the research findings from the project.

602313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
602313.value: The numerical algorithms and real options game models that were developed in this project can be applied to other economic and finance problems that involve stochastic controls in the state variables of the models.

602313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
602313.value: This project investigates the R&D activities between two competing firms on a certain technology under different market conditions. We focus on the issue where the firm may be benefited from the R&D activities by another firm so that its research capability enhances. This will affect firm’s expected R&D duration and firm’s R&D cost since better knowledge may help to reduce the cost (input spillover). Also, there may be potential profit generated from the product developed by the firm (output spillover). We consider the spillover affect the R&D activities adopted by two firms. Simple intuition may suggest that the spillover may slow down the R&D in this case because the spillover enhances the firm’s knowledge stock and this magnifies the pure knowledge effect phenomena. We also analyze how the firms’ R&D activities can be affected under the existence of competition. The competition may speed up (slow down) the R&D activities since entry of the rival firm may induce the negative (positive) externalities to the firm. Moreover, we examine how a social planner sets the corresponding social policy to maximize the social welfare.

602413.label: Project Objectives
602413.value: Our first objective is to develop a new spectral library search engine capable of handling DIA data. We will bring together SRM-like processing and subtractive spectrum analysis techniques, and develop the necessary scoring functions to maximize discrimination and minimize error. We will validate our method first on specially designed datasets of known proteins spiked into a complex background, then on data from real proteomics experiments. Our second objective is to develop new algorithms for aligning LC-MS maps of DIA data in the retention time dimension, and by doing so, simplify data analysis by focusing on differentially expressed proteins. The alignment of LC-MS maps of technical replicates can also be used to reduce noise and increase the performance of our search engine developed in Objective 1. This requires borrowing from and adapting traditional algorithms for label-free quantification, while making good use of the additional information from fragment ion spectra to aid alignment. Our third objective is to develop a full-feature and user-friendly data analysis pipeline, including automatic statistical validation, data organization and re-use through spectral library building, protein inference and quantification. We will model our software after the widely-adopted Trans Proteomic Pipeline. The software will be made compatible with all instruments, and sound software engineering practice will be applied to ensure reusability and user-friendliness of the software tools developed.

602413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
602413.value: Proteomics, which aims at the systematic identification of all proteins in a biological system, is an increasingly powerful and popular analytical approach in life science research. Mass spectrometry (MS)-based proteomics technology has grown by leaps and bounds in the past two decades, driven not only by advances in instrumentation, but also in data analysis. In a typical proteomics experiment, peptides from digested protein samples are separated and fragmented in a mass spectrometer, yielding MS/MS spectra that record the characteristic fragmentation patterns of the peptides. This information can then be used to deduce the peptide sequence by well-established computational methods. Until recently, the mass spectrometer is typically instructed to select the most abundant peptide ions eluting at any given time for fragmentation, in what is called data-dependent acquisition (DDA). While this approach has its merits, its sampling nature limits the dynamic range for quantification, and hampers its use as robust high-throughput assays for proteins. On the other hand, data-independent acquisition (DIA) methods, in which the mass spectrometer is instructed to fragment all peptide ions together or in batches, are handicapped by the difficulty in interpreting the resulting mixed fragment ion spectra. Recently, advances in instrumentation, as well as an increasing emphasis on quantification, have tipped the scale towards DIA, and interest in DIA methods has surged. Despite the obvious promise of this method to fundamentally change the field, the corresponding data analysis methods for DIA proteomics have been lacking. This proposed project will develop a spectral library-based data analysis pipeline designed for DIA proteomics, analogous to the existing sequence database-based data analysis pipelines for DDA methods. We will bring together several disparate ideas of proteomics data processing in an innovative manner, and construct an adaptable, modular, full-feature, and user-friendly data analysis pipeline. We will pursue three objectives: (i) building a spectral library search engine for DIA spectra with multi-round subtractive analysis; (ii) applying LC-MS alignment methods to simplify data analysis by removing noise and focusing on differential signals; and (iii) developing an appropriate statistical validation approach to assess the confidence of peptide identifications made from DIA methods, to complete the data analysis pipeline. The ultimate deliverable of this project is a platform-neutral and open-source alternative to vendor-specific commercial software, and a much needed data analysis solution for all types of DIA data. 蛋白組學之目的是有系統地識別一個生物系統中所有的蛋白質。在生命科學研究領域中, 這是一項日益有力和流行的分析方法。用於蛋白組學的質譜技術, 不論是儀器上的進步，還是數據分析方法的改良，在過去的二十年中有長足的發展。在一個典型的蛋白組學實驗中，消化蛋白質而成的肽樣品經過分離和碎裂，得到的串聯質譜可以通過完善的計算方法，推導出肽序列。 直至最近，質譜儀通常選擇豐度最高的肽離子來碎裂排序，即所謂數據依賴型(DDA)二質譜法 。雖然這種方法有它的優點，這樣的抽樣法限制了定量的值域，並阻礙其作為高通量蛋白質檢測的能力。反之，非數據依賴型(DIA)二質譜法，雖然所有的肽離子可以一起或分批碎裂，但串聯質譜中混雜了多個肽離子的碎片，以致難以推導出肽序列。最近，儀器的進步, 及蛋白定量的重要，使DIA方法越來越受重視。這種方法儘管有明顯的潛力，但屹今仍缺乏相應的數據分析方法。 該擬建項目將開發一個基於質譜庫方法，特別為DIA二質譜法而設的數據分析管道。我們將匯集幾個不同的想法，構建一個適應能力強，模塊化，全功能和用戶友好的數據分析管道。我們的 目標是：（i）研發一個新的質譜庫搜索引擎來處理DIA二質譜，(ii) 研發液相色譜 - 質譜的對應方法以簡化數據分析去除 噪音和突出差分信號; 及(iii)制定適當的統計驗證的方法來評估所得的肽序列的準確性，來完成數據分析管道。該項目的結果將是一個平台中立，開放源碼，適用於所有DIA的數據類型的數據分析解決方案。

602413.label: Realisation of objectives
602413.value: The captioned project has been completed with full realization of the objectives. Objective 1 Our first objective is to develop a new spectral library search engine capable of handling DIA data. As described in the mid-term progress report, our existing spectral library building and searching software, SpectraST, has been adapted to handle DIA data already. As we pursued this objective, we came to the realization that our impact will be maximized if we joined forces with other top researchers in the field, as our approaches are largely similar, namely, to adopt SRM-like analysis for DIA data. Although SpectraST can perform a “search” of DIA data as described in the proposal, we do not believe it is worthwhile to push this direction further. This is partly because the subtractive analysis idea that we thought would make a difference did not improve the result too significantly. A more important factor is user acceptance: currently, DIA data analysis has been dominated by commercial software (PeakView from Sciex, the vendor of SWATH-capable mass spectrometers) and Skyline (an open-source platform which is widely used for SRM processing and can also be used for DIA data), which has far better user interface. Instead, we believe we can make more unique contributions in the library building and assay generation step, which involves using spectral libraries to define the search space and the fragment ion signals to score a match. In this respect, we teamed up with the OpenSWATH project (http://www.openswath.org/en/latest/) led by Prof. Ruedi Aebersold in ETH Zurich, and helped build their library building pipeline using SpectraST. We have made various changes and enhancements, for instance in fragment ion selection and retention time normalization, to facilitate the integration of SpectraST in their pipeline. This work has contributed to two publications (Rosenberger et al, Scientific Data 1, 140031, and Schubert et al, Nature Protocols 10, 426-441). Although not explicitly stated as an objective in the proposal, we have also helped launch the Human SRMAtlas, as an indirect outcome of this research. The Human SRMAtlas is the largest targeted MS assay library for human, which covers almost all known human genes (with at least one gene product per gene). This work is published in Kusebauch et al, Cell 166, 766-778. These assays can be used for SRM or DIA analysis, and using this SRMAtlas, researchers can extract validated sets of transitions (fragment ions) to monitor for any given human protein, which are the input to any targeted proteomic experiments, including DIA. Our contribution is mainly in organizing the huge amount of data generated and compiling spectral libraries specifically for SRM assays by SpectraST, which is made possible by the computational advances realized in this objective. Note: RGC/GRF was not explicity acknowledged in the two indirect outputs: Schubert et al, Nature Protocols 10, 426-441) and Kusebauch et al, Cell 166, 766-778, because both were the results of a large-scale collaboration of many researchers. There was limited space to include the funding source of every author. Our contribution was through the software we developed (SpectraST) and adapted for these two projects. This was clearly stated in the text of the papers. Objective 2 In Objective 2, we proposed to develop new algorithms for aligning LC-MS maps of DIA data in the retention time dimension, and by doing so, simplify data analysis by focusing on differentially expressed proteins. In this regard, we have vastly improved our LC-MS alignment method, LWBMatch, and adapted it for DIA data. Specifically: (i) The “time warping” step, namely, coarse alignment to correct for systematic retention time shifts, has been completely overhauled to use a signal-based approach rather than the original feature-based approach. This made the software far more robust against dissimilar LC-MS runs (e.g. those collected with different chromatographic gradients). (ii) The software can now align MS2 spectra, which are acquired continuously in time on the same precursor window under DIA. This is in addition to and orthogonal to MS1 spectra, which were traditionally aligned by this type of methods. The ability to align MS2 data can provide an independent check of the MS1 alignment and potentially improve it. In our test data, we found that the best alignment derived from MS2 data is very similar to that obtained from MS1 data, and that a vast majority of “ground truth” pairs (pairs of matching peptide identifications) can be recalled accurately by either alignment, even under very different chromatographic conditions. (iii) We made use of the algorithm to align datasets acquired on the same sample, and use the alignment to reduce noise by removing peaks that are not consistently present across LC-MS runs. This is a novel application of retention time alignment and is shown to be effective, albeit as a proof of concept at this stage. (iv) To align the MS2 data efficiently, we tried different ways of combining the different “swaths” (precursor windows). We found that concatenating MS2 spectra from all swaths, and aligning the concatenated “composite spectra” using our algorithm, is able to give us accurate alignments within a reasonable time. There is no need to align different swaths separately, which is far more time-consuming. (v) To further speed up the alignment of the composite MS2 spectra, so that it is comparable to aligning MS1 spectra, we developed a novel data compression scheme inspired by image processing techniques. This dimensionality reduction method allows us to obtain MS2 alignment in comparable time with MS1 alignment, while maintaining similar accuracy. These results are published in 1 journal paper (Wu et al, Proteomics 16, 2272-2283) and 2 conference presentations (Wu et al, HUPO 2016 and Li et al, AOMSC 2017). The latter advance is now being prepared for submission as a journal publication also. Objective 3 In our last objective, we planned to develop a full-feature and user-friendly data analysis pipeline, and to make the software usable. Although we did not end up creating the whole analysis pipeline by ourselves, we took steps to ensure that our work will be used by integrating with other widely-used platforms. We have so far implemented our new algorithms in the spectral search engine SpectraST, which remains a part of the open-source and widely used Trans Proteomic Pipeline (TPP) suite of software tools for proteomics data analysis. It is also now the library building engine behind OpenSWATH, and SpectraST libraries are also made compatible with Skyline.

602413.label: Major findings and research outcome
602413.value: The research outcomes of this project were mainly the following: (i) A spectral library-based experimental design and data analysis pipeline for DIA data analysis in proteomics. This has aided the development of online databases of DIA- and SRM-based MS assays of the human proteome for use by proteomics community. (ii) A novel retention time alignment algorithm that works for DIA data and can effectively and efficiently align MS2 spectra. This led to an ability to use aligned datasets to remove noise and highlight differentially changed signals across different samples.

602413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
602413.value: Data-independent acquisition such as SWATH has become more popular in the past few years, but it remains arguably a niche technique practiced by a relatively small circle of experts. A possible future direction would be in making the method more accessible to mainstream researchers. On the other hand, there are signs that with advancing MS technology, the acquisition window gets narrower, and the main disadvantage of DIA – the high complexity of MS2 spectra – will simply go away. In other words, the line between DDA and DIA data analysis will blur and finally disappear, as DIA acquisition becomes the norm while the resulting data can be analyzed simply by traditional database or library searching, though SRM-like methods can still be used in targeted experiments. An example is a recent paper by the Sciex team: Kang et al, “SWATH-ID: An instrument method which combines identification and quantification in a single analysis.” Proteomics, doi: 10.1002/pmic.201500522 (2017). This is mainly a commercial hardware advance that cannot be pursued in an academic setting, but it should lead to opportunities for the development of open-source research software when the MS technology becomes widely available.

602413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
602413.value: Proteomics, which aims at the systematic identification of all proteins in a biological system, is an increasingly powerful and popular analytical approach in life science research, capable to delivering unprecedented insights into puzzles in biology and vexing human diseases. Technologically, this is accomplished by mass spectrometry (MS), which can sequence and quantify protein fragments (called peptides) in an extremely high-throughput manner. Recent advances in MS have led to a new way of doing proteomics experiments, called “data-independent acquisition” (DIA), which promises to have higher sensitivity and offer more accurate quantitative information. This project was conceived of to develop data analysis methods for DIA experiments, which is more challenging due to the co-fragmentation of peptides. The method developed made use of spectral libraries to define which peptides to search for, as well as to score matches more accurately by considering empirically obtained fragmentation patterns. Separately, a chromatographic retention time alignment algorithm was also developed for DIA data, which can make use of the relationship between different experiments on the same samples to facilitate data analysis. Both of these advances were integrated into popular open-source data analysis workflows and made available to the research community.

602813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
602813.value: A superconductor is a material which can conduct electricity without dissipation. However, some superconductors behave like insulators in certain respects. For example, an ordinary superconductor has a bulk band gap in electronic band language and it takes energy larger than the band gap to excite a quasi-particle in a superconductor. Recently, new types of superconductors called topological superconductors are proposed to exist. A topological superconductor is a superconductor with a bulk band gap and gapless boundary modes. The zero energy modes at the sample boundary are called Majorana fermions. Majorana fermions are interesting in two respects. First, a Majorana fermion has only half the degrees of freedom of a usual fermion. Second, they are non-Abelian particles, e.g. braiding Majorana fermions can change the quantum state of the system. Due to these exotic properties of Majorana fermions, the search for Majorana fermions is one of the central topics in condensed matter physics recently. Majorana fermions are very robust and they cannot be removed unless the energy gap of the superconductor is closed. However, in nature, many unconventional superconductors are nodal as they possess point nodes or line nodes in the bulk. The question is: can Majorana fermions exist in these nodal superconductors? The answer is positive. Moreover, these nodal superconductors support dispersionless zero energy Majorana fermions, namely, Majorana flat bands. In this proposal, we first review the development of topological superconductors which supports Majorana fermions. Second, we review Dirac fermion flat bands in nodal high Tc d-wave superconductors and iron-based superconductors. Third, the recent progress on Majorana fermions in nodal topological superconductors is reviewed. We also point out how symmetry protected Majorana flat bands and uni-directional edge states can emerge in a fully gapped topological superconductor by closing the bulk gap. In this proposal, we propose to study: 1) The Majorana flat bands and their associated surface states in a heavy fermion nodal superconductor UPt3. 2) The surface states of Cu doped topological insulator Bi2Se3 under a magnetic field. The superconducting phase of CuxBi2Cu3 is possibly a nodal phase. 3) The Majorana flat band assisted crossed Andreev reflection. 4) RKKY (spin-spin) interactions between magnetic impurities mediated by Majorana flat bands. 5) The thermal transport of nodal topological superconductors due to the edge states and the gapless bulk. 摘要： 超導體是可以無耗散導電的材料。然後，在某些方面超導體具有絕緣體的行為。例如，從能帶理論的觀點來說，一個普通的超導體具有主體能隙，在超導體中激發一個准粒子需要大於能隙的能量。 近來，有人提出一種被稱作拓撲超導體的新型超導體。拓撲超導體是具有主體能隙和無隙邊界模式的超導體。在樣品邊界的零能量模式被稱作馬約拉納（Majorana）費米子。 馬約拉納費米子(Majorana fermions)在兩個方面引人注目。首先，一個馬約拉納費米子僅有一個普通費米子的半個自由度。其次，它們是非阿貝爾粒子，譬如交錯馬約拉納費米子可以改變系統的量子態。由於馬約拉納費米子這些新奇的物理性質，對馬約拉納費米子的探索是近期凝聚態物理的中心話題之一。 馬約拉納費米子十分穩定，只有在能帶隙閉合的時候才能被移除。然而在自然界中，許多非常規超導體在能譜中有節點，因為它們可以在主體中有點節點或線節點。疑問是：馬約拉納費米子能否存在於這些有節點的超導體中呢？答案是肯定的。再者，這些有節點的超導體支援無色散的零能量馬約拉納費米子，亦即馬約拉納平能帶。 在這個計畫書中，我們首先回顧了具有馬約拉納費米子的拓撲超導體的發展。然後，我們回顧了有節點高溫超導體和鐵基超導體中的狄拉克無色散能帶。最後我們回顧了有節點拓撲超導體中馬約拉納費米子的研究進展。我們也指出了當體內能隙閉合時,有對稱性保護的馬約拉納無色散能帶和單向邊界態可以在一個完全間斷的拓撲超導體中產生。 在這個計畫書中，我們計畫研究： 1）重費米子節點超導體UPt3中的馬約拉納無色散帶及其相關表面態。 2）在外磁場影響下，銅摻雜的拓撲超導體Bi2Se3的邊界態。CuxBi2Te3的超導相是一個可能的節點相。 3）馬約拉納無色散帶影響下的交錯安德列耶夫反射。 4）磁性雜質之間由馬約拉納無色散帶傳遞的RKKY（自旋-自旋）相互作用。

602813.label: Realisation of objectives
602813.value: During the report period, the PI studied all the topics in the revised objectives. 1. The PI realized that the surface flat bands in UPt3 can be destroyed by spin-orbit coupling effects in UPt3. As a result, the flat band in UPt3 can be difficult to realize. However, the PI realized that MoS2 may support Majorana flat bands. This work is published at Phys. Rev. Lett. 113, 097001 (2014). Moreover, the PI realized that NbSe2 can be driven to a nodal topological phase which supports Majorana flat bands. This work is under review (arXiv:1604.02867). 2. The PI theoretically studied Nb doped Bi2Se3 instead of Cu doped Bi2Se3 and we proposed that Nb doped Bi2Se3 are indeed nodal topological superconductors which support Majorana surface states. This work is published in Physical Review B and selected as a Rapid Communication [Phys. Rev. B 95, 201109 (2017)]. In collaboration with experimentalists, the PI showed that Nb doped Bi2Se3 can be a nematic topological superconductor. This work is accepted for publication in njp-Quantum Materials [npj Quantum Materials (2017) 2:59 ; doi:10.1038/s41535-017-0064-1]. 3. The PI studied the crossed Andreev reflections induced by Majorana fermions. This work is published at Nature Communications 5:3232 (2014). 4. The PI studied the RKKY interaction between magnetic impurities in MoS2. This work is still in preparation.

602813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
602813.value: In this project, we studied the properties of an novel type of superconductors in which current can flow without resistance. In the past studies, people mostly focused on the charge current as electrons carry charges and result in charge currents when they flow. In this project, we study the spin current in a special type of superconductors called nodal superconductors. This type of superconductors can induce very large spin currents when electrons flow due to the Majorana flat bands on the surface of these nodal superconductors. The results of this project will guide experimentalists to create large spin currents in superconductors.

602913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
602913.value: Transition metal alkyl and aryl complexes are of interest because of their involvement as reactive intermediates in metal-catalyzed organic transformations and bio-inorganic catalysis. Early transition metal alkyl complexes have been used as precursors to organometallic complexes (e.g., carbenes) and single-site heterogeneous catalysts. Compared with the early and mid transition metal counterparts, homoleptic alkyl and aryl complexes of late transition metals, particularly ruthenium, have not been well explored. In this project, polyalkyl and polyaryl complexes of ruthenium will be synthesized and their organometallic and oxidation chemistry will be studied. High-valent ruthenium oxo-alkyl and –aryl complexes will be synthesized and their oxo-transfer chemistry investigated. Also, the use of our recently synthesized trigonal bipyramidal ruthenium(IV) tri-alkyl complexes as precursors to high-valent organoruthenium complexes will be explored. The aryl ligands in ruthenium tetra-aryl complexes will be functionalized by bromination and borylation. The resulting functionalized aryl complexes will be polymerized by metal-catalyzed carbon-carbon coupling reactions to give network materials that can exhibit interesting physical and chemical properties, e.g., gas absorption and catalysis. Metallaquinones (quinone with one oxygen atom replaced by a metal) are of interest due to the importance of quinoid compounds in chemistry and biology. In this work, metallaquinones will be synthesized by oxidation of hydroxyaryl complexes. Understanding of the bonding, structure and reactivity of metallaquinones will help design new quinoid compounds that can find applications in catalysis and materials science. 过渡金属烷烃和芳烃配合物非常有趣由于它们在金属催化的有机转化和生物无机催化反应中作为活性中间体。前过渡金属烷烃配合物已经被用作先导物来合成有金属配合物（例如：卡宾）和单一非均相催化剂。与前和中间过渡金属比较，后过渡金属的烷烃和芳烃配合物，尤其是钌，没有被很好地研究。在这个项目中，钌多烷烃和多芳烃配合物将被合成且它们有机金属和氧化化学将被研究。高价钌氧烷烃和芳烃配合物将被合成且它们的氧传递化学被研究。此外，我们最近合成的三角双金字塔钌三烷烃配合物作为先导物到高价有机钌配合物将被探索。在钌四芳烃配合物中，芳烃配体将被溴化和硼化。通过金属催化碳碳偶合反应，官能化的芳烃配合物将被聚合得到网状材料，这些材料能表现有趣的物理和化学性能，例如气体吸收和催化。由于醌化合物在化学和生物学中的重要性，金属醌（醌中的一个氧被金属取代）非常有趣。在这个工作中，通过羟基芳烃配合物的氧化金属醌将被合成。金属醌配合物的键，结构和反应活性的理解将帮助设计新的醌化合物，这些醌化合物能应用在催化反应和材料科学。

602913.label: Realisation of objectives
602913.value: The objective of this research project is to synthesize aryl and alkyl complexes of late transition metals and investigate their redox and catalytic properties. In particular, aryl complexes of ruthenium and osmium have been synthesized owing to their catalytic activity in organic oxidations. Also, 4-hydroxyaryl complexes that are precursors to metalloaquinones have been synthesized and their deprotonation has been studied. We have developed a new synthetic route to ruthenium(IV) tetraaryl complexes [RuR4] (R = ortho-substituted phenyl). Oxidation of [RuR4] afforded the first structurally characterized ruthenium(V) aryl complexes, [RuR4](BF4). The [RuR4] complexes undergo reductive elimination of biaryl and migratory insertion with nitric oxide. Also, [RuR4] can catalyze oxidation of alcohols presumably via reactive Ru aryl oxo intermediates. Bromination of [RuR4] afforded tetra-brominated [Ru(R-Br)4] that can serve as a starting material for organoruthenium polymers. The results of this study demonstrate that both the metal center and the aryl ligand in [RuR4] exhibit rich redox and reaction chemistry. We have synthesized and structurally characterized 4-hydroxyaryl complexes of ruthenium, osmium, rhodium and nickel. An in-situ generated palladium(II) 4-hydroxyaryl phosphine complex was found to undergo facile P-C reductive elimination to yield a novel phosphaquinone that has been characterized by X-ray diffraction. Currently, a paper on ruthenium and osmium 4-hydroxyaryl complexes is under preparation and will be submitted for publication soon. We have synthesized cationic palladium(IV) aryl chloride complexes supported by a tripodal oxygen ligand. The palladium aryl complexes undergo facile C-Cl reductive elimination to yield chloroarenes. This result indicates that palladium tripod complexes can find applications in catalytic halogenation of hydrocarbons. In order to model heterogeneous cerium(IV) oxide catalysts, we have synthesized a tetranuclear cerium(IV) oxo cluster supported by a tripodal oxygen ligand. Like cerium(IV) oxides, the cerium(IV) oxo cluster reacts with carbon dioxide, nitric oxide and sulfur dioxide to give the corresponding carbonate, nitrate and sulfate complexes. Our reactivity study of molecular cerium oxo cluster complexes can shed light on the mechanisms of cerium oxide catalysts. Also, we have synthesized a novel heterometallic cerium(IV)/vanadium(V) oxo cluster that is a highly active catalyst for sulfide oxidation (with a total turnover number as high as 96,600).

602913.label: Major findings and research outcome
602913.value: (i) The reductive coupling and migratory insertion of the ruthenium polyaryl complexes have been studied systematically. The ruthenium complexes can catalyze oxidation of alcohols via reactive ruthenium oxo aryl intermediates, demonstrating the potential application of ruthenium aryl complexes in catalytic organic oxidations. (ii) 4-Hydroxyaryl complexes that are precursors to metallaquinones have been synthesized and structurally characterized. A novel phosphaquinone has been obtained by P-C elimination of a reactive palladium hydroxyaryl phosphine species. The results of our work demonstrate that transition-metal-containing metallaquinones are accessible and display interesting organometallic reactivity. (iii) The first cationic palladium(IV) aryl complexes supported by a tripodal oxygen ligand has been isolated and structurally characterized. Cationic palladium(IV) aryl complexes undergo facile C-Cl reductive elimination, suggesting that such complexes can find applications in C-H functionalization. (iv) A novel tetranuclear cerium(IV) oxo cluster compound that can serve as a model of heterogeneous cerium oxide catalysts has been isolated and structurally characterized. The reactivity of this cerium(IV) oxo cluster toward small molecules and hydrogen peroxide has been studied. This is the first reactivity systematic study of a molecular cerium-oxo cluster toward small molecules. The results of this study can shed light on the mode of action of industrially important ceria-based catalysts. (v) A novel heterometallic cerium(IV)/vanadium(IV) oxo cluster that is a highly efficient and selective sulfide oxidation catalyst has been isolated. A total turnover number as high as 96,600 has been achieved for the catalytic sulfoxidation. This work shows the importance of the cerium-based oxo-metallic core in the stability of reactive vanadium alkyl peroxo active species. The result of this study can lead to development of robust bimetallic catalysts for catalytic oxidation. (vi) The first lanthanide complexes containing iodosylbenzene and iodylbenzene ligands that can undergo oxo transfer with organic sulfides have been isolated and structurally characterized. This work demonstrates that lanthanide complexes with hypervalent iodine ligands have potential applications in organic oxidation reactions, and this is an unexplored area of lanthanide chemistry.

602913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
602913.value: Organometallic ruthenium complexes with +5 or higher oxidation states are very rare. The results of our project, stabilized with bulky aryl ligands, high-valent ruthenium complexes with low coordination numbers are accessible. Therefore, further research should be directed toward the synthesis of Ru(V) or Ru(VI) aryl complexes containing multiply bonded ligands, such as oxo, imido and alkylidene. These complexes are expected to display interesting redox and organometallic reactivity, e.g. atom/group transfer and metathesis. The study of the organometallic chemistry of high-valent organoruthenium aryl complexes can lead to development of selective catalysts for oxidation, aziridination and metathesis of alkenes. Ceria-supported metal catalysts have been widely used in catalytic oxidation in industrial processes. However, the mechanisms of the metal-catalyzed oxo transfer on the cerium-oxide surface are not well understood at the atomic level. We have found that a cerium/vanadium oxo cluster is a highly efficient catalyst for sulfide oxidation, demonstrating that the cerium-oxo-metallic core is capable of stabilizing reactive metal-oxygen species. In the future, efforts should be made to develop new heterometallic Ce(IV) clusters, e.g. Ce(IV)/Ru(IV) oxo clusters, that can find applications in C-H oxidation. Toward this end, the self-assembly of Ce(IV) tripod complexes with Ru salts in aqueous media will be explored. The structure and catalytic activity of the resulting Ce/Ru cluster compounds will be investigated.

602913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
602913.value: High oxidation state transition-metal complexes with aryl and alkyl ligands are of significance because of their involvement as intermediates in metal-catalyzed carbon-hydrogen bond functionalization. In this project, aryl complexes of late transition metals such as ruthenium have been synthesized and their redox and organometallic chemistry has been studied. We have developed a new synthetic route to ruthenium(IV) tetra-aryl complexes and investigated their reductive elimination and migratory insertion. Stable ruthenium(V) aryl complexes have been synthesized by oxidation of the ruthenium(IV) precursors, demonstrating the ability of aryl ligands to stabilize ruthenium in high oxidation states. Also, we have isolated cationic palladium(IV) aryl complexes that undergo facile carbon-chlorine reductive elimination, showing the potential applications of high-valent organopalladium tripod complexes in C-H functionalization. We have synthesized 4-hydroxyaryl complexes that are precursors to metallaquinones. A novel phosphaquinone compound has been obtained by P-C elimination of an in-situ generated palladium 4-hydroxyaryl phosphine complex. Finally, cerium oxo complexes and clusters that can serve as models of heterogeneous cerium oxide catalysts have been synthesized. The reactivity study of molecular cerium oxo clusters can shed light on the mode of action of industrially important ceria-based catalysts.

603213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
603213.value: 纳米材料设计所面对的一个重要挑战是实现具有高稳定性及具备原子尺度的有序精确结构。我们设想如下策略解决这个难题：将共价键耦合反应与可逆超分子自组装结合。超分子自组装是构建复杂结构的一个主要方法，它利用非共价键作用将分子单体自动组合。但由于非共价键的强度较弱，超分子材料的缺点是稳定性低。在这个项目中，我们将共价键耦合反应与可逆超分子自组装结合来构建搞稳定性的复杂纳米结构。我们首先设计并合成多种前驱单体，这些单体附带可以发生共价耦合及配位反应的功能组。我们将探索在金（111）表面这些单体如何在铜或钯催化下发生共价偶联。在下一阶段，我们将前驱单体通过配位反应组装为有序结构，然后用催化剂激发偶联反应，最终形成共价键联系而成的结构。我们将使用这个途径在表面合成环状结构以及两维延展结构。由于整个过程非常复杂，我们会用动力学蒙特卡洛模拟获得动力学及热力学特性。我们期望这个跨学科的项目将会拓展对表面共价反应的理解，为配体模板奠定基础，并会发现设计具有高稳定性及具备原子尺度的有序精确结构的新路径。

603213.label: Realisation of objectives
603213.value: 1. Object 1 has been successfully achieved. We chose the polymerization reaction of 5,15-bis-(4-bromo-phenyl)-10,20-diphenyl porphyrin as a model system to investigate extrinsic Cu and Pd catalysts. We used STM to monitor the isothermal reaction and then determined the reaction yields, rate constants and activation energy. After depositing the molecules onto a Au(111) surface with pre-dosed Pd, periodical chains were formed with a center-to-center distance of 1.74 ± 0.04 nm for the adjacent units, indicating covalently connected polymers. Similar chains were obtained when we conducted the Cu-catalyzed experiment on Au(111) surface. As contrast, annealing the same molecules on clean Au(111) up to 453 K for 30 minutes only gave us only 1.5% covalently-linked species, which confirms the catalytic influence of Pd or Cu on this Ullmann coupling reaction. To study the reaction kinetics of C-C bond formation of 3 catalyzed by Pd, we annealed the sample at a defined temperature in 10–12 steps with 8–10 min for each. STM measurements were carried out after each step when the sample was cooled down to room temperature. The same procedure was conducted at different annealing temperatures. We found Pd and Cu result in distinct C-C bond formation yield and length distribution of the polymeric chains. Cu-catalyzed reaction always has a much higher yield and longer polymeric chains. We also investigated the Ullmann reaction on a hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) layer grown on an Ni(111) substrate using scanning tunneling microscopy (STM). We explored the catalytic activity of Cu and Pd atoms dosed with the molecular precursors. We found that the dispersed atoms of both metals efficiently catalyze the reaction, but lead to different reaction paths. 2. Object 2 has been successfully achieved. We employed three metal-coordination structures as templates to control the Sonogashira cross-coupling reactions on a Au(111) surface catalyzed by loaded Pd. We used scanning tunnelling microscopy to resolve the products formed at the successive reaction steps and identified three vital characteristics for an efficient template: high accessibility of reaction sites, structural rigidity and thermal stability. all three templates effectively suppressed homo-coupling of aryl bromides at room temperature but resulted in very different SCC yields at elevated temperatures. Comparison of the structures formed at successive reaction steps allows us to identify three key characteristics that an efficient template must have: (1) easy accessible reaction sites, (2) rigid structure and (3) being thermally stable. It is worthwhile to point out that (1) hints that the template must not cover the entire surface in order to leave accessible reaction sites. We expect that these insights will provide guidance for designing templates for other on-surface cross-coupling reactions. We believe that these results will inspire the design and synthesis of size- and shape-controlled macromolecular systems in the fast emerging field of on-surface synthesis. 3. Object 3 has been partially achieved. We have successfully fabricated covalently-linked macrocyclic and extended 2D architectures that exhibit high stability. These structures contain defects and the degree of their structural regularity needs to be improved. The main reason is the metal-coordination templates often become unstable at the covalent reaction conditions. To overcome this problem, we are working on using templates that are stabilized by stronger metal-coordination bonds. Some preliminary results show this approach is very promising.

603213.label: Major findings and research outcome
603213.value: 1. We demonstrated that cross-coupling of aryl-bromide and porphyrin-bromide takes place on a Au(111) surface in vacuo. The products are oligomers consisting of porphyrin moieties linked by p-phenylene at porphyrin’s meso-positions. The ratio of the cross-coupled versus homocoupled bonds can be regulated by the reactant concentrations. Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations were applied to determine the activation barrier. It is expected that this reaction can be employed in other aryl-bromide precursors for designing alternating co-polymers incorporating porphyrin and other functional moieties. 2. We report the self-assembly of multi-component lanthanide coordination metallosupramolecular structures on a Au(111) surface. Eu atoms coordinate with two heterotypic ligands of quarterphenyl-4,4′′-dicarbonitrile and 4′,4′′′′-(1,4-phenylene)bis(2,2′:6′,2′′-terpyridine). For carbonitrile ligand : terpyridyl stoichiometric ratios of 0.7, Eu atoms are primarily ligated in a four-fold coordination scheme. By increasing the carbonitrile ligand to reach a stoichiometry of 1.8, Eu atoms are ligated now in a five-fold coordination sphere. Two types of coordination schemes result in structures exhibiting one-dimensional and two-dimensional morphologies, respectively. This study demonstrates that the flexible lanthanide coordination sphere facilitates the rational design of metallosupramolecular architectures. 3. we employ rare-earth-directed assembly to construct a twodimensional tiling with quasicrystalline characteristics at a well-defined gold substrate. By careful stoichiometry control over europium centres and functional linkers, we produced a porous network, including the simultaneous expression of four-fold, five-fold and six-fold vertices. The pertaining features were directly inspected by scanning tunneling microscopy, and the molecule–europium reticulation was recognized as square-triangle tessellation with dodecagonal symmetry, as shown in Figure 2. Our findings introduce quasicrystallinity in surface-confined MOCNs with a nanoporous structure and anticipate functionalities that arise from quasicrystalline ordering of the coordinative spheres. 4. We loaded Cu and Pd as catalysts to study the Ullmann-type reaction on a hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) layer grown on a metal substrate. We discovered that individual diffusing Cu adatoms are the key agent for catalyzing the reaction and Pd exhibits higher catalytic activity than Cu especially at lower temperatures (<180 ̊C). Above 180 ̊C, the yield of Cu-catalyzed reaction exceeds the Pd-catalyzed one. 5. We used templates to suppress homo-coupling and enhance cross-coupling Sonogashira cross-coupling (SCC) reaction. Precursor molecules 3 form a double-row ladder structure stabilized by py-Cu-py coordination. After molecules A were dosed onto the sample, no SCC products were observed. Loading Pd onto this sample increased the yield more than 20 times.

603213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
603213.value: Most of the surfaces that have been used are metals, which strongly interact with the molecular precursors. The intimate molecule-surface interaction can be beneficial on one hand, for example, to catalyze reactions, but on the other hand, can be problematic as it reduces the molecule mobility, activates unwanted side reactions or binds side products on the surface, etc. These effects can hinder the growth of desired structures. Our results point out a strategy to circumvent these obstacles: conducting on-surface synthesis on an inert surface and controlling the reactions by selective loading metal catalysts. We expect the weak molecule-substrate interaction may render high molecule mobility. To activate the reactions, one can co-deposit metals such as Cu, Pd, Ni and Pt as catalysts.

603213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
603213.value: Conjugated 2D layer materials exhibit remarkable electronic, mechanical, optical and chemical properties. Graphene is by far the most widely studied example. After the discovery of graphene, other 2D periodic carbon COFs have been proposed. Such materials are analogues of graphene but with tailored electronic properties that may give them an edge over graphene in certain applications. Thus the successful synthesis of conjugated 2D COFs will represent a major leap towards functional 2D materials. In this project, we have demonstrated that metal templates and metal catalysts can effectively steer the on-surface reaction towards high yield and high order. These findings provide timely imputes for 2D COF fabrication.

603313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
603313.value: Organoboron compounds are useful synthetic intermediates in organic reactions with wide ranging applications from pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals to liquid crystals and conjugated materials. They are most often prepared via metal-catalyzed hydroboration/diboration or reactions of highly reactive organolithium/organomagnesium reagents with electrophilic boron species. Other synthetic methods developed recently include metal-catalyzed borylation of carbon-hydrogen and carbon-halide bonds in alkanes and arenes. Very recent research has led to new reactions related to direct conversion of carbon-halide bonds in primary, secondary and even tertiary alkyl halides to the carbon-boron bonds. Mechanistic studies of these reactions have been limited and the current understanding of metal-catalyzed borylation reactions cannot account for a number of associated phenomena. In other words, the reaction mechanisms are not well understood. In this proposal, theoretical studies via density functional theory calculations will be undertaken to explore the reaction mechanisms of these newly discovered borylation reactions. Hopefully, this research will provide guidelines for the experimental work, including the development of new catalytic processes and applications in organic synthesis. 有机硼化物是有机合成的重要中间体。在药物和材料的合成应用很广。它们的制备通常用金属催化硼氢化或双硼化反应。目前，碳氢硼化和烷基卤化物硼化开始得到重视。本计划主要是对烷基卤化物硼化的反应机理进行理论研究。由此，希望对一些重要的实验现象进行解释，从而对发展更好的催化剂提供理论基础。

603313.label: Realisation of objectives
603313.value: Objective 1: Mechanisms for borylation reactions of various alkyl halides have been systematically investigated and calculated. Insight into nickel-catalyzed carbon–carbon versus carbon–boron coupling reactions of primary, secondary and tertiary alkyl bromides has been obtained. Suggestions on improving catalytic systems have been proposed through our studies. We will need to extend our calculations to other metal-catalyzed borylation reactions. This will be done as a follow-up work of this research. Objective 2: We have extended our calculations/investigation to zinc- and base-catalyzed borylation reactions. Various factors influencing borylation reactions have been studied and examined. As mentioned above, our follow-up work will focus on calculations of other metal-catalyzed borylation reactions.

603313.label: Major findings and research outcome
603313.value: With the aid of DFT calculations, we compared and contrasted alkyl–alkyl cross-coupling with alkyl halide borylation catalyzed by nickel complexes, and successfully elucidated the differences between the two mechanisms and deduced that the rate of alkyl–alkyl crosscoupling was determined by the reductive elimination step, whereas the rate of borylation was governed mainly by the atom transfer step. The differences are due to the differing electronic properties of the two coupling reagents, especially the presence of an empty p orbital in the borylating reagent. The inability of unactivated tertiary alkyl halides to undergo alkyl–alkyl cross-coupling is mainly due to the moderately high reductive elimination barrier caused by substantial steric hindrance. (Publication (3) in Section 8) We have studied reactivities of the unsymmetrical diboron compound pinB_BMes2. New reaction mechanisms have been proposed to account for how the diboron cleaves a carbon-nitrogen triple bond and borylates alkynes. (Publications (1), (2), (4) and (5) in Section 8) We have systematically investigated the reactivities and electronic structures of boryl ligands. Insignts into how the boryl ligands mediate/catalyze various chemical transformations have been thoroughly discussed and presented. A book chapter has been written to summarize all of our findings. (Publication (6) in Section 8) Various factors influencing borylation reactions have been obtained through our investigations of other reaction systems such as zinc-catalyzed dual C-X and C-H borylation of aryl halides and potassium diboryllithate mediated deprotonation of benzene. (Publications (7) and (8) in Section 8)

603313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
603313.value: Over the years, we have witnessed important applications of metal-catalyzed borylation reactions in synthetic organic chemistry. Many new catalytic processes towards more applications continue to be developed. The insights obtained from this project contribute significantly to this expanding development. We are now focusing our research effort to understand many recently reported borylation reactions using cheap and abundant first row transition metals as catalysts.

603313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
603313.value: In this project, we've investigated issues related to transition metal catalyzed borylation reactions to give organoboron reagents, which are important intermediates in the synthesis of many pharmaceutical products. The results/insights we've obtained are useful for researchers to find better catalysts for producing the important reagents.
