603413.label: Realisation of objectives
603413.value: We first derived the functional limit distributions of the partial sum and the sample autocovariances of the short- and long-memory linear processes with GARCH (1,1) noises when the tail index α is in (0, 2), equal to 2, and in (2,∞), respectively. The partial sum weakly converges to a functional of α-stable process when α < 2 and converges to a functional of Brownian motion when α ≥ 2. When the process is of short-memory and α < 4, the autocovariances converge to functionals of α/2- stable processes; and if α ≥ 4, they converge to functionals of Brownian motions. In contrast, when the process is of long-memory, depending on α and β (the parameter that characterizes the long-memory), the autocovariances converge to either (i) functionals of α/2-stable processes; (ii) Rosenblatt processes (indexed by β, 1/2 < β < 3/4); or (iii) functionals of Brownian motions. Based this limiting theory, we studied the LSE of AR models with heavy-tailed G-GARCH(1,1) noises. When the tail index α of G-GARCH is within (0,2), it is shown that the LSE is not a consistent estimator of the parameters, but converges to a ratio of stable vectors. When α ∈ [2, 4], it is shown that the LSE is n^{1−2/α}-consistent if α ∈ (2,4), log n-consistent if α = 2, and n^{1/2/} logn-consistent if α = 4, and its limiting distribution is a functional of stable processes. In general, the limiting distributions of LSE or LAD estimators are hard to be used for statistical inferences. Based on the self-weighted LAD estimators, we developed a systematic procedure of statistical inference for the ARMA model with unspecified and heavy-tailed heteroscedastic noises. The self-weighted LAD estimators are shown to be strongly consistent and asymptotically normal. The rates of convergence of the LADE and the self-weighted LADE are n^{−1/2}, which is faster than those of LSE for the ARMA model when the tail index of GARCH noises is in (0, 4], and thus they are more efficient in this case. We further proposed a novel sign-based portmanteau test for model adequacy. As an extension of the self-weight estimation, we developed a systematic procedure of statistical inference for the heavy-tailed TAR model. We showed that the LAD of thresholds are n-consistent, each of which converges weakly to the smallest minimizer of a compound Poisson process. . We further studied the quasi-maximum exponential likelihood estimator (QMELE) of the heavy-tailed and multiple-threshold DAR models. We showed that the estimated thresholds are n-consistent, each of which converges weakly to the smallest minimizer of a two-sided compound Poisson process. The remaining parameters are root-n-consistent and asymptotically normal. A score-based test was developed to identify the number of thresholds in the model. Furthermore, we construct a mixed sign-based portmanteau test for model checking. We have accessed the performance of the asymptotic results and methods in finite samples through Monte Carlo experiments. We have applied our theory and method to study the daily stock data of Monarch Community Bancorp in NasdaqCM, KV Pharmaceutical in NYSE, Community Bankers Trust in AMEX and China Media Express in NasdaqGS, and the NASDAQ daily volume.

603413.value: This project explored the limiting behaviors of the short- and long-memory linear process of the heavy tailed G-GARCH noises, including its sample mean and ample autocovariance. We first investigated the least squares estimator (LSE) and LAD estimators of the AR/ARMA/DAR models and the short- and long- memory fractional ARIMA models when the tailed index of the G-GARCH noises is in (0, 4]. 603813.value: Abstract of research 數學中群的概念起源于物理或抽象的系統中展现的對稱性。 群的性质， 例如它們的表示，往往能在分析該系統时 起到根本的作用。对約化群， Robert Langlands 的洞察力， 推測自守形式和自守表示和數論與代數幾何的联系。 此研究项目的是为了更好的了解组成自守表示的局部表示， 及它们如何在自守表示中出现。局部表示和自守表示这两种理论有很多相似之處，这两种理论互相影響。 在最近的研究中，我曾研究p進李代數的尖形式，全局 尖形式的存在性， 及分級Hecke代數的酉表示。 这些研究導致我提出一些問題。我建議： 1.研究p進群的李代數上的尖形式，特別是支承在被稱為拓撲冪零元素的集合上的尖形式， 并研究它们和p進群上尖形式的关系。 2. 研究有Whittaker 模型的 尖自守形式存在性. 3. 研究由根系定义的分級Hecke代數的某些酉表示。特別是，找到具有非零的Dirac同調的 酉表示的例子.

603813.label: Realisation of objectives
603813.value: We discuss realization of the objectives in order descending order of percentage achieved. Objective 2 Existence of cuspidal automorphic forms which have Whittaker models This objective was 100% achieved. In collaboration with Prof. Goran the PI established a very general criterion for the existence of automorphic cuspidal representations on adelic semisimple groups which have Whittaker models. Automorphic cuspidal representations are basic building blocks in arithmetic algebraic geometry, and the existence of a Whittaker model of such a representation is a very important computational tool. Objective 1. Cusp forms supported on the set of topological nilpotent elements and relate then to cusp forms on the p-adic group. The PI directly investigated certain distributions which are natural sums of Bernstein projectors on the p-adic group SL(2), and showed that the sums have support on the set of topological unipotent elements. The support property on the topological unipotent elements means these distributions can be transferred to the Lie algebra by the exponential map. On the Lie algebra, the transferred distribution has a Fourier transform, which has a particularly easy to describe form. The 90% achievement reflect that the new phenomena is established for the group SL(2) and not larger rank groups. Ideas arising from this work then greatly influenced the preprint `An Euler-Poincare formula for a depth zero Bernstein projector' . As of April 2018 this preprint is under review for publication. Objective 3. Research on graded Hecke algebras. In connection with Objective 1, the PI and collaborator Prof. Dan Barbasch introduced new algebraic objects called Peter-Weyl Iwahori algebra which are very intimately related to Iwahori Hecke algebras. The precise relation established (in Fall 2017 and Spring 2018) after completion of the project is that for a fixed reductive group (with irreducible root system), a Peter-Weyl Iwahori algebra is Morita equivalent to the Iwahori Hecke algebra. The stated underachievement is because the new and interesting result while related to the original goal is not the original goal, i.e., finding new representations with non-zero Dirac cohomology. `

603813.label: Major findings and research outcome
603813.value: 1. In the single-authored paper `Computations with Bernstein projectors of SL(2)' the PI gave a decomposition of the Dirac delta function (at the identity element) of the p-adic group SL(2) as an infinite sum of distributions indexed by the possible depths of representations. For a given depth (which must be a nonnegative integer or half integer), the associated term has the remarkable property that (1) it is itself a finite sum of what are called Bernstein projectors, and (2) the support of the (distribution) term is inside what is called the set of topologically unipotent elements of the group SL(2). This result is very suggestive of what might be true in higher dimensions. 2. In collaboration with Prof. Goran Muić, the PI established a very general criterion for the existence of automorphic cuspidal representations on adelic semisimple groups which have Whittaker models. Automorphic cuspidal representations are basic building blocks in arithmetic algebraic geometry, and the existence of a Whittaker model of such a representation is a very important computational tool. 3. The under review paper `An Euler-Poincare formula for a depth zero Bernstein projector' is a partial follow-up of the PI's SL(2) work. The paper exhibits an Euler-Poincare presentation (over the Bruhat-Tits building of a reductive p-adic group (with irreducible root system)) of certain Bernstein projectors.

603813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
603813.value: The PI believes the research direction of the paper `An Euler-Poincare formula for a depth zero Bernstein projector' will be very fruitful in the future. The goal would be to show any Bernstein projector has a Euler-Poincare presentation (over the Bruhat-Tits building of a reductive p-adic group (with irreducible root system)).

603813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
603813.value: Groups are mathematical objects which appear whenever a physical or abstract system has symmetries. Examples of groups are all possible movements in Euclidean 3-space which preserve lengths, or all possible permutations of a finite set. Representation theory seeks to obtain a deeper understanding of groups realizing them as group of matrices. In almost all cases, there are multiple ways to realize a group as matrices. The PI's research attempts to determine all possible ways to realize certain groups (called p-adic reductive groups) in terms of matrices.

603913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
603913.value: Advance in new technology depends on several factors, one of which is our ability to design and create materials with desired properties. An active area in which physicists have been searching for materials with novel properties is quantum magnetism - the behavior of magnetic materials under extreme, quantum conditions. The present project represents a collaborative effort between groups in HKUST, MIT, Tsinghua University and Zhejiang University in this area. In this project we exploit theoretically the plausible existence of novel quantum states in magnetic systems with spin magnitude S =1 (usually called spin liquid states). Previous researches for new quantum states in magnetic materials are concentrated mainly on materials with spin magnitude S=1/2. The S=1 systems become a focus of research interests recently after the discovery of the triangular lattice material Ba3NiSb2O9 which suggested the plausible existence of a spin liquid state with novel properties. Theoretically it is expected that the nature of spin liquid states in S=1 and S=1/2 systems are very different because of the very different quantum topological (or Berry phase) effects associated with integer and half-odd-integer spins, as demonstrated by the much celebrated Haldane conjecture in one dimensional Heisenberg model and later works. We shall exploit the plausible existence and nature of spin liquid states in S=1 spin systems in some one-dimensional and two-dimensional lattice spin models including the bilinear biquadratic (J-K) model and Heisenberg models with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) type interaction. We shall study the above models in one-dimension spin chain, and in two-dimensional triangular lattice, hexagonal lattice and Kagome lattices. These models are believed to represent a rather large set of experimentally accessible materials. A combined analytical and numerical approach proposed by the principle investigator and his collaborators will be used to determine the ground states and low energy properties of these models. The major goal of the project is to search for S=1 spin liquid states with non-trivial topological characters which are potentials candidates for quantum computation. We shall compare our results with corresponding results for S=1/2 models to pin down the differences between integer and half-odd-integer spin systems. Our study will also provide new insight into the nature of general (symmetry protected) topological order in one- and two- dimensional systems, which so far, has relied heavily on results obtained from S=1/2 spin systems. 現代科技發展取決於一系列因素，其中一項是新型材料的建構。在這領域，一個活躍的研究方向是量子磁性 ─ 磁性物料在極端低溫﹝量子環境﹞下的性質。 本研究項目由科大，麻省理工、清華及浙江大學的不同研究團隊合作發動，目標是從理論上了解由自旋為一 (S=1)的磁量子組成的磁性材料的可能物質新型態。 對磁量子態的探究以往研究者主要著力於探究自旋為二份一 (S=1/2)的磁性材料，不過2011年，在一個S=1的新磁性材料Ba3NiSb2O9被發現後，S=1的磁性材料成為新的重要研究方向。理論上，由於不同自旋磁量子由貝爾相因子 (Berry phase﹞引致的不同拓樸性質，一般認為由S=1/2跟S=1磁量子產生的量子自旋液體會有非常不一樣的性質，正如霍丁(Haldane)八十年代在量子自旋縺上工作顯示。 我們將會在不同的晶體結構上探研不同的S=1量子自旋液體的存在可能性。我們將研究不同的量子自旋相互作用，包括具有四自旋相互作用的推廣海森堡模型(bi-linear, bi-quadratic Heisenberg model)，和自旋之間的Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya相互作用。研究的晶體結構包括一維量子自旋縺以及二維的三角形 (triangular)，蜂巢型 (hexagonal)及戈薇 (Kagome) 晶體結構。這些模型能描述相當大量的現存實驗磁性材料。我們將使用不同的解柝及數值辦法來研究這些模型的基態及低能激發性質。 我們項目的一個重要目標是去找尋有不尋常拓樸結構的S=1量子自旋液體，這些量子液體可望用作量子計算之用。 我們將會比較S=1/2及S=1的不同量子自旋液態的異同。在目前階段，物理學界對量子自旋液體的了解主要局限於S=1/2的磁性系統，我們的研究，將會擴大我們對量子自旋液體及(一般)拓樸態的了解。

604013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
604013.value: 液体的挥发和沸腾在我们的日常生活中随处可见。考虑一个放在固体表面上的液滴。如果固体温度略高于液体沸点，液滴会沸腾并很快挥发掉。然而，如果固体的温度远高于液体沸点，在固液之间会形成一层稳定的薄蒸汽膜。这种悬浮在蒸汽膜上的液滴称作“莱顿弗罗斯特（Leidenfrost）液滴”。此现象由德国医生莱顿弗罗斯特（Johann Gottlob Leidenfrost）在1756年首次报道。固液之间蒸汽膜的出现使得液滴不再跟灼热的固体表面直接接触。这阻止了蒸汽气泡在固体表面的成核。另一方面，由于蒸汽的热传导率远低于液体，这层蒸汽膜还起到了热绝缘层的作用。因此，液滴不再沸腾而是缓慢地挥发，其寿命得以大幅延长。 多年来，这个看似简单的“莱顿弗罗斯特现象”引起了众多科学家和工程师的关注。这很大程度上是由于工业技术应用中，灼热固体表面上的液滴挥发过程随处可见且至关重要，例如金属淬火、蒸汽发生器、喷雾干燥、核反应堆堆芯的喷雾冷却和火箭发动机喷嘴的薄膜冷却等等。近年来，由于高速和超高速摄像技术的发展以及表面处理和微机电技术的成熟，科学家们对于莱顿弗罗斯特液滴的复杂行为有了进一步的理解。同时，这些技术的进步和推广正在引领科学家们在众多科技领域中不断取得新的发现和突破。 莱顿弗罗斯特液滴的动力学牵涉质量流、自由界面运动、热传导和气液相变等多尺度多物理过程的耦合。这使得莱顿弗罗斯特现象显得及其复杂并展现出丰富、独特的物理行为。因此，对莱顿弗罗斯特现象的建模和数值模拟不仅有巨大的理论兴趣而且为当前发展中的实验研究所急需。 近来，有日本学者提出了适用于单组元流体的动力学范德瓦尔斯理论（dynamic van der Waals theory，DVDWT)。此理论能够处理不均匀温度场中伴有气液相变的两相流体动力学问题。我们通过考虑固液界面上可能发生的耗散过程，为DVDWT推导了适当的固体表面上的边界条件。通过数值模拟，我们研究了挥发性液滴在固体表面上的运动。本项目计划用DVDWT以及固体表面上的边界条件来探究莱顿弗罗斯特现象。这个理论能够为莱顿弗罗斯特现象的多个方面提供一套统一、定量和精确的数值模拟方法。例如，固液之间蒸汽膜的形成可以通过在灼热固体表面的气泡展布的两相流体动力学过程实现。蒸汽膜随时间的演化依据液滴的大小可以划分为多个不同的特征区段。微米尺度大小的莱顿弗罗斯特液滴会从灼热的固体表面一跃而起。在这一过程中，对于薄蒸汽膜的理论分析，常用的润滑近似将会失效。这使得一套统一、定量和精确的数值模拟方法显得不可或缺。

604013.label: Realisation of objectives
604013.value: For the first objective, we have numerically investigated the pool boiling of one-component fluids with a focus on the effects of surface wettability on the single-bubble dynamics. We employed the dynamic van der Waals theory, a diffuse-interface model for liquid-vapor flows involving liquid-vapor transition in nonuniform temperature fields. We first perform simulations for bubbles on homogeneous surfaces. We find that an increase in either the contact angle or the surface superheating can enhance the bubble spreading over the heating surface and increase the bubble departure diameter as well and therefore facilitate the transition into film boiling. We then examine the dynamics of bubbles on patterned surfaces, which incorporate the advantages of both hydrophobic and hydrophilic surfaces. The central hydrophobic region increases the thermodynamic probability of bubble nucleation while the surrounding hydrophilic region hinders the continuous bubble spreading by pinning the contact line at the hydrophobic-hydrophilic intersection. This leads to a small bubble departure diameter and therefore prevents the transition from nucleate boiling into film boiling. With the bubble nucleation probability increased and the bubble departure facilitated, the efficiency of heat transfer on such patterned surfaces is highly enhanced, as observed experimentally [Int. J. Heat Mass Transfer 57, 733 (2013)]. In addition, the stick-slip motion of contact line on patterned surfaces is demonstrated in one-component fluids, with the effect weakened by surface superheating. For the first objective, the dynamic van der Waals theory has been employed to model the growth of a single vapor bubble in a superheated liquid on a flat homogeneous substrate. The bubble spreading dynamics in the pool boiling regime has been numerically investigated for one-component van der Waals fluids close to the critical point, with a focus on the effect of the substrate wettability on bubble growth and contact line motion. The substrate wettability is found to control the apparent contact angle and the rate of bubble growth (the rate of total evaporation), through which the contact line speed is determined. An approximate expression is derived for the contact line speed, showing good agreement with the simulation results. This demonstrates that the contact line speed is primarily governed by (1) the circular shape of interface (for slow bubble growth), (2) the constant apparent contact angle, and (3) the constant bubble growth rate. It follows that the contact line speed has a sensitive dependence on the substrate wettability via the apparent contact angle which also determines the bubble growth rate. Compared to hydrophilic surfaces, hydrophobic surfaces give rise to a thinner shape of bubble and a higher rate of total evaporation, which combine to result in a much faster contact line speed. This can be linked to the earlier formation of a vapor film and hence the onset of boiling crisis. Liquid drops under gravity can levitate on a vapor cushion which is either sourced at the liquid-vapor interface from evaporation caused by the hot substrate below ― the Leidenfrost effect, or supplied by an upward flow injected from beneath. The lubrication approximation has been fruitfully applied to analyse the thin vapor layer between the liquid drop and the solid substrate. For the second and third objectives, we have investigated the validity of the lubrication approximation for the vapor layer under the Leidenfrost drops. This is carried out by numerically simulating systems of liquid and vapor using the recently developed dynamic van der Waals theory, in which the two-phase hydrodynamics is coupled with liquid-vapor transition. We find that the solutions derived from the lubrication approximation generally compare well to our simulation results, and the shape of the vapor layer shows good agreement. The robustness of the lubrication approximation is attributed to the common features found in the pressure variation through the vapor layer, resulting from an accumulation of vapor in the central cavity region before an abrupt escape at the thin neck region. We also find that under the drop, the pressure profile remains nearly independent of the vertical distance away from the substrate, in agreement with the lubrication approximation. However, as the evaporative region is approached near the liquid-vapor interface, appreciable deviations show up. Furthermore, by simulating isothermal drops levitating on a cushion of vapor injected from beneath, the phenomenon is found to be reasonably insensitive to the specifics of injected flow. This is still attributed to the accumulation of vapor in the central cavity region before the abrupt escape at the neck region. One of the challenging aspects of the Leidenfrost effect is the vapor layer dynamics coupled with strong evaporation. Therefore, the insensitivity observed in our simulations, which agrees with previous analytical and experimental results, can be taken as a relief for a general understanding of the Leidenfrost effect.

604013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
604013.value: (i) Since the mesh size used to resolve the diffuse interface is only a few angstroms, our simulated systems are very small, up to hundreds of nanometers. Moreover, an artificially large gravity is introduced to make the capillary length sufficiently short and thus accessible in our simulations. We hope that using the dynamic van der Waals theory, larger scale simulations of boiling phenomena can be developed. This will contribute to the study of the fundamental physical aspects of boiling. (ii) We have demonstrated that boiling heat transfer can be enhanced by patterning hydrophilic surfaces with hydrophobic patches of size comparable to the capillary length. However, the contrast in contact angle, which is necessitated by the effectiveness of such a design, can be significantly reduced by surface superheating. We propose that more effective surfaces can be engineered by combining geometric pattern with chemical pattern. (iii) We have only dealt with the dynamics of a single bubble. However, hydrodynamic interactions between bubbles may play important roles, particularly in the layer of crowded bubbles near the heating surface. It will be interesting to investigate the effects of hydrodynamic interactions on crowded bubbles near the heating surface.

604013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
604013.value: Boiling and evaporation of liquids are commonly observed in our daily life. For a liquid droplet deposited on a hot solid surface, if the solid temperature is much higher than the boiling point of the liquid, then a vapor layer is formed between the droplet and solid. A droplet levitating over a vapor layer on a hot solid surface is called a Leidenfrost droplet. Its dynamics is complicated, characterized by the coupling of mass flow, free interface motion, heat conduction, and phase change. The formation of a vapor layer marks the transition from nucleate boiling to film boiling. Numerical simulations have been carried out using a theory which describes liquid-vapor flows involving liquid-vapor transition in nonuniform temperature fields. Our simulations have shown that compared to hydrophilic surfaces, hydrophobic surfaces give rise to a much faster contact line speed for bubble growth and spreading, leading to the earlier formation of a vapor film and hence the onset of boiling crisis. Our simulations have also shown that using properly patterned surfaces can help avoid the onset of boiling crisis. These results are important to our understanding of the fundamental aspects of boiling heat transfer.

604213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
604213.value: A multi-faceted, broad-based research program in string theory, particle physics, and cosmology – the first such in Hong Kong - is proposed. String phenomenology, the proposed research focus, serves as an anchor and provides crucial links between the above key areas in fundamental physics. String theory is the leading candidate for a unified quantum theory of all the forces in nature. Thus it holds great promise of answering long-standing puzzles, from fundamental questions in high energy physics, to the origin, evolution, and composition of our universe. Progress in string theory has so far been driven mainly by theoretical considerations rather than experimental inputs, but this situation is undergoing a revolutionary change. Over the next few years, there will be a vast amount of new data from both particle physics and cosmology. With the recent discovery of the Higgs boson, the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is ready to confront theoretical ideas such as supersymmetry (SUSY) and extra dimensions. Remarkable advances in observational cosmology, such as the cosmic microwave background (CMB) measurements by current and upcoming satellite missions (e.g. WMAP and PLANCK), allow us to probe with high precision the very early universe where fundamental physics leaves its fingerprint. The observational evidence of dark energy (Nobel Prize in 2011) continues to pose great challenges for quantum gravity. This is an exciting and critical time for string phenomenology research, as these new data are providing powerful tools to test and explore physics at ultra-high energies where string and quantum gravity effects become important. The goal of the proposed research program is to bridge the gap between fundamental theory and experiment. Many outstanding issues in physics today require an integration of insights from string theory, particle physics, and cosmology - issues such as the origin of mass, the fundamental interactions in nature, the mechanism of cosmic inflation, and the nature of dark matter/energy. These issues are deeply intertwined, and their solutions are bound to have broad and dramatic experimental consequences. String phenomenology provides a fertile theoretical framework for addressing these central issues. Drawing upon methodologies and results that the PI has developed, the proposed research plan will focus on (1) constructing models of particle physics and cosmology from string theory, (2) seeking novel experimental signatures of string theory models and scenarios, and (3) developing theoretical tools to apply string theory to emerging issues in beyond the Standard Model physics and in early universe cosmology.

604213.label: Realisation of objectives
604213.value: The proposed objectives have all been successfully realized. During the funding period, we have published 15 journal articles and delivered over 30 invited talks at international conferences. The proposed objectives are deeply intertwined. Progress in one triggers advances in another. Some results we obtained have impact on several of the objectives. Here we give an overview of how the proposed project objectives are addressed: Objective 1 (Publications 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 15): We have proposed a new framework for constructing realistic string models with a genuine hidden sector (Publication 1) and constructed string theoretical models realizing this scenario (Publication 2). The phenomenological implications of this scenario were addressed in (Publication 2) and further discussed in (Publication 15). We have also proposed a mechanism to widen the axion window (Publication 4) and we constructed string theory models implementing this mechanism (Publication 5). These results have useful implications to dark matter searches, inflation, and axion physics. We have developed a framework to explain possible new resonances that can be detected at the LHC, if the inflaton field is the Higgs boson (Publication 8), thus correlating particle physics with cosmology. Objective 2 (Publications 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 15): Among the strong motivations for physics beyond the Standard Model are the existence of dark matter and the increasingly compelling framework of cosmic inflation. We designed a novel framework for the Standard Model particles to interact with dark matter (Publication 1). The correlated LHC-dark matter signatures of this framework were addressed in (Publications 2 and 15). Axion is a theoretically well motivated candidate for physics beyond the Standard Model. If their decay constant is within the right range, they can serve as dark matter and/or the inflaton. The case for axion dark matter has become more compelling in the absence of super-partner signals at the LHC. Although axion-like particles are abundant in string theory, their decay constants are widely believed to fall outside the desired dark matter and inflaton range. We designed a novel scenario motivated by string theory that involves multiple axions (Publications 4 and 5) and found that the axion decay can both be enhanced to super-Planckian values for inflation and lowered to the desired dark matter window. In Publication 8, we designed a novel scenario where the Higgs field plays the role of the inflaton, the scalar field that drives the accelerated expansion of the early universe. Objective 3 (Publications 6,7, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14): A new class of string compactifications that geometrize the desired particle physics features of the Standard Model is known as F-theory. Despite progress, the low energy effective action of F-theory compactifications has not been fully developed. We have derived some string theory corrections to the effective action of F-theory compactification (Publication 3). The corrections we obtained are important for issues such as moduli stabilization, supersymmetry mediation, and inflation. We also found stringent quantum gravity constraints on the low energy effective action of string theory (Publications 6, 7, 11, 12, 14). Our results provided further evidences of the weak gravity conjecture, and suggested that certain bottom-up approaches of physics beyond the Standard Model are not realizable in string theory. We also developed an effective field theory for spacetime symmetry breaking (Publication 8), which we applied to particle physics and cosmology (Publications 9, 13).

rows: To construct models of particle physics from string theory, and to study their physical implications and signatures.
To design novel particle physics beyond the Standard Model scenarios motivated by string theory and develop them in response to results from the LHC.
To develop novel string compactifications and derive their low energy effective actions, with a view towards their applications to phenomenological applications.

604213.label: Major findings and research outcome
604213.value: We have developed several novel scenarios of particle physics that addressed the questions: 1) what is the nature of dark matter? How do we detect them? Are there correlated experimental signatures in particle physics and cosmology that help in pinning down the composition of the dark sector of the universe? 2) what is the mechanism that generates the enormous hierarchy between the scale of gravity (the Planck scale) and the scale of particle physics (the electroweak scale), 3) what accounts for the accelerated expansion of the universe and whether quantum gravity can impose non-trivial constraints on theories of cosmic inflation and particle physics models. Here, we highlight the impact of two of our findings: 1) the work on millicharged dark matter and Stuckelberg portal (Publications 1, 2, 15) has motivated the CDMS collaboration to search for such dark matter candidates, 2) the body of work on the weak gravity conjecture (Publications 6, 7, 11, 12, 14) has influenced the CMB Stage 4 experimental community in setting their B-node target (see the CMB-S4 Science Book, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.02743.pdf). Thus, the completed project not only elucidated the theoretical foundation of fundamental physics, but also their experimental consequences.

604213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
604213.value: The research outcome of this project has opened up many new directions for future development. The completed works illustrate the power of string theory in motivating particle physics and cosmology scenarios and models, but much of the potential of string phenomenology remains to be explored. For example, it was recently pointed out by several research groups (including the PI’s) that the WGC can rule out models of particle physics that extends the Standard Model by restricting the type of neutrinos (Majorana vs Diac) and their masses as well as the masses of other new particles. Finding out whether a given low energy theory can be consistently coupled to quantum gravity has been an important research area that many researchers, including the PI, are actively pursuing.

604213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
604213.value: The proposed project is a multi-faceted, broad-based research program in string theory, particle physics, and cosmology – the first such in Hong Kong. String phenomenology, the research focus, serves as an anchor and provides crucial links between the above key areas in fundamental physics. String theory is the leading candidate for a unified quantum theory of all the forces in nature. Thus it holds great promise of answering long-standing puzzles, from fundamental questions in high energy physics, to the origin, evolution, and composition of our universe. The goal of the proposed research program is to bridge the gap between fundamental theory and experiment. Many outstanding issues in physics today require an integration of insights from string theory, particle physics, and cosmology -- issues such as the origin of mass, the fundamental interactions in nature, the mechanism of cosmic inflation, and the nature of dark matter/energy. These issues are deeply intertwined, and their solutions are bound to have broad and dramatic experimental consequences. Understanding these long-standing issues would truly advance our knowledge of how the universe works at the most fundamental level and harness the laws of Nature. The results of our findings can impact future experimental searches for new physics.

Pablo Soler, Daniel Junghans, Toshifumi Noumi, Wan-Zhe Feng were postdoctoral researchers participating in this project. 604313.label: Project Objectives
604313.value: To develop dynamic shrinkage methods for modeling time series covariance matrices; To introduce statistical methods for studying dynamic sparsity in covariance matrices; To determine the optimal order of random variables in the Cholesky decomposition; To evaluate the proposed Bayesian dynamic shrinkage and dynamic sparsity methods using forecasting errors, statistical information criteria and Bayesian tests. 604313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
604313.value: Modeling the interdependence among financial and economic variables is an indispensable part of monitoring risk and developing financial products. Identifying relationships between prognostic disease factors and numerous types of DNA has been a topic of great interest in biomedical research. It is also important to study the dependence of climate variables in both space and time. Covariance, a statistical measure used to provide information on both variability and correlation, is an important instrument employed to quantify various kinds of relationships and dependences. Therefore, it is important that researchers and decision makers in fields such as finance, biology and environmental science be provided sound models of covariance. Because the relationship between different variables depends on factors that change over time, covariance is dynamic, i.e. it is time-varying. Advances in information technology have given us a wide range of variables, but this has led to the challenge of high dimensionality in covariance modeling due to the numerous potential combinations of correlations. Dealing with the dynamic nature of covariance and its dimensionality is crucial in studying relationships between variables. The proposed study will develop statistical methods to regularize covariance patterns and simplify the exploration of dependence structures over time. We will study the effectiveness of the proposed methods in capturing the dynamic dependence of different financial variables. The findings of this project will enrich applications in fields including finance, biology and environmental studies. 金融和經濟變量之間的相互依存關係模型在監測風險和金融產品之開發上是一個不可缺少的部分。確定預後疾病因素和多種類型的DNA之間的關係一直是對生物醫學領域上一個非常有趣的研究主題。同樣重要的是研究氣候變量在空間和時間中的依存。共變異數，一個用來提供變異性和相關性信息的統計度量，是一個重要量化關係和依賴關係的工具。因此，提供良好的共變異數模型對在金融，生物和環境科學等領域的研究人員和決策者是重要的。 因為不同變量之間的關係取決於多種隨時間變化的因素，共變異數是動態的，也就是說，它是隨時間變化的。信息技術的進步給了我們廣泛的變量，但這也是導致由於許多潛在的相關性組合所帶來共變異數模型高維的挑戰。處理共變異數的動態性質和維度對研究變量之間的關係是至關重要。擬進行的研究開發統計方法規範共變異數模式及依賴結構隨著時間推移的簡化探索。我們將研究在捕捉不同金融變量的動態依賴所提出的方法的有效性。這個項目的研究成果將豐富各個應用領域，包括金融，生物和環境研究。

604513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
604513.value: Anything labeled "Organic" is supposed to have a large content of carbon atoms. Carbon-carbon bonds constitute the skeleton of the majority of organic molecules. However, the function of an organic molecule often requires the presence of heteroatoms, such as oxygen, nitrogen, sulfur, silicon, etc. These heteroatoms are typically connected to carbon atoms by carbon-heteroatom bonds. For example, carbon-heteroatom bonds widely exist in DNA molecules, proteins, carbohydrates, alkaloids, conductive polymers, and synthetic pharmaceuticals, etc. As a result, the ability to build carbon-heteroatom bonds will ultimately affect our ability to achieve and explore new functions of materials significantly. Specifically, selective formation of carbon-heteroatom bonds at the right position (chemoselectivity) of an organic molecule in a right direction (stereoselectivity) in a catalytic fashion is extremely desirable because such processes will significantly simplify further product purification, reduce energy consumption, and minimize negative impact on environment. While chemists have made significant progress towards the ideal formation of carbon-heteroatom bonds stereo- and chemoselectively, there remain numerous unsolved challenges. The goal of this project is to further advance the development of new selective carbon-heteroatom bond formation processes that are directly useful in achieving new functions, such as applications in medicines, materials, other aspects of daily life. 理論上任何標為“有機”的物體都含有較大的碳原子含量。碳-碳鍵構成了大多數有機分子的骨架。然而，實現有機分子的功能往往需要雜原子的存在（如氧，氮，硫，矽等等）。這些雜原子一般都是通過碳-雜原子鍵與碳原子相連的。例如，碳-雜原子鍵廣泛存在於DNA分子，蛋白質，碳水化合物，生物鹼，導電聚合物和合成醫藥中。所以，對碳-雜原子鍵的構架能力將會大大影響人們對新興功能分子的創造和研究能力。具體來說，以催化的方式選擇性地在正確的位置（化學選擇性）和方向（立體選擇性）形成碳-雜原子鍵非常重要，因為這樣的反應過程將大大簡化產品進一步純化，降低能源消耗和對環境的負面影響。雖然化學家已經在選擇性碳-雜原子鍵形成方向取得了顯著的進展，但仍然有許多未解的難題。這個項目的目標是進一步推進開發新的選擇性碳 - 雜原子鍵的形成過程，進而促進它們在研發新的功能分子（如藥品，材料）和日常生活其他方面的應用。

604513.label: Realisation of objectives
604513.value: In this project, we have successfully developed a range of new catalytic carbon-heteroatom bond formation processes, which have been mainly in three different areas. These processes have been achieved with (1) N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) catalysis, (2) via desymmetrization of 3-substituted oxetanes, and (3) via ligand-controlled regio- and stereo-divergent internal alkyne hydrosilylation. the objectives of this proposal have been realized as expected. (1) We have developed a range of new asymmetric fluorination, trifluoromethylation and other heterofunctionalization reactions by NHC catalysis. These reactions are all unprecedented previously. In our effort, we not only achieved good efficiency, but also tried to understand the mechanism and selectivity, which will guide further research in this area. (2) We have developed a series of catalytic asymmetric ring-opening reactions of oxetanes and related strained rings using organocatalysis. In this area, we demonstrated the first intermolecular desymmetrization of 3-substituted oxetanes. A range of nucleophiles have been demonstrated to be viable. (3) With metal catalysis, we have developed very unusual ligand-controlled regio- and stereo-divergent intermolecular hydrosilylation of alkynes with excellent selectivity control. We also did rigorous mechanistic studies to understand the origin of selectivity divergence.

604513.label: Major findings and research outcome
604513.value: In this project, we have developed the following new catalytic processes leading to synthesis of useful chiral building blocks and synthetically important structural units. (1) We developed the first general and mild hydrosilylation of thioalkynes. With [Cp*Ru(MeCN)3]+ as catalyst, a range of thioalkynes participate in the efficient hydrosilylation at room temperature with excellent regio- and stereo-selectivity. (2) An efficient asymmetric α-fluorination of NHC-enolates generated from simple aliphatic aldehydes and α-chloro aldehydes was achieved. (3) We developed the first catalytic enantioselective desymmetrization of azetidines with both excellent efficiency and remarkable enantioselectivity (4) We have demonstrated an unprecedented catalytic asymmetric intermolecular addition of o-QMs for the efficient formation of acyclic all-carbon quaternary stereocenters. (5) We have demonstrated a new organocatalytic transfer hydrogenation strategy for the efficient asymmetric synthesis of 1,1-diarylethanes, an important family of compounds with broad medicinal and agricultural applications. (6) A highly efficient enantio- and diastereoselective synthesis of dihydronaphthalenes from isobenzopyrylium ions was developed. The highly enantioenriched dihydronaphthalene products can be easily transformed to other useful molecules. (7) We developed the first general and mild hydrosilylation of thioalkynes with excellent regio- and stereo-selectivity. (8) A new general and mild catalytic asymmetric 1,6-conjugate addition process of para-quinone methides was developed. (9) We developed the first catalytic asymmetric intermolecular alcohol addition to o-QMs. It is a rare example of asymmetric hetero-conjugate additions of o-QMs. (10) We further established the first Brønsted acid catalyzed enantioselective addition of thiols to the in situ generated o-QMs. (11) A new catalytic asymmetric approach for the synthesis of chiral 1,4-dioxanes is achieved. It is a synthesis of an important scaffold of broad utility but lacking general and efficient access. (12) We developed a one-pot oxidation/cycloaddition cascade for the synthesis of 2,4-diaryl chromans, a family of useful molecules of broad utility in medicinal chemistry. Our approach involves an in situ oxidative generation of unstable o-QMs. (13) We have developed an efficient organocatalytic enantioselective intermolecular addition of naphthols to in-situ generated para-quinone methides. (14) Asymmetric opening of oxetanes is a challenging topic. Following our previous effort, in this project we achieved the first asymmetric chloride opening of oxetanes, providing expedient access of highly functionalized three-carbon chiral building blocks with excellent efficiency and stereocontrol. (15) The first intermolecular aza-Piancatelli reaction with excellent chemo-, enantio-, and diastereoselectivity under mild conditions was achieved. It provides expedient access to a wide range of highly enantioenriched 4-amino-cyclopentenone products from readily available 2-furfurylcarbinols.

604513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
604513.value: As an extension of this project, the development of additional useful catalytic carbon-heteroatom bond formation processes will continue to be our topic of pursuit in this area. In particular, we will continue to expand the utility of chiral Bronsted acids in asymmetric catalysis. Our effort in asymmetric strained ring opening, such as oxetanes and azetidines, will still be a topic for further research.

604513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
604513.value: In this project, we have discovered a range of new organic processes with excellent efficiency and selectivity. These processes are new approaches to build carbon-heteroatom bonds, which are important in our daily life as demonstrated by their potential utility in medicinal chemistry and pharmaceutical industry. These findings will not only contribute to addressing this longstanding challenges in organic synthesis, but also benefit many aspects of human life, from public health to environmental protection.

604913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
604913.value: Development of porous molecular materials such as metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) and covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is a topic of great current interest due to their anticipated high-tech applications. The preparation of crystalline MOFs and COFs, however, requires elaborate control and harsh conditions, which significantly limit their scopes in terms of materials diversity. Microporous polymers (MPPs) can afford similar properties for technological applications and enjoy such advantages as easy synthesis, light weight, and high stability. Researchers have been actively working on the development of synthetic approaches for controlling pore sizes and surface areas of MPPs directed to potential applications as gas adsorption and storage materials. However, few attempts have been made to endow MPPs with advanced functionalities such as tunable luminescence. Our research groups have discovered a novel photophysical phenomenon of aggregation-induced emission (AIE) in a series of propeller-like molecules and explored their technological applications as chemical sensors, biological probes, light emitters, etc. The propeller shape of an AIE luminogen makes it a promising building block for the fabrication of porous materials. In this project, we plan to synthesize luminescent nitrogen-rich MPPs with AIE features and widen the scope of their practical applications, in addition to gas adsorption and storage. Different types of amine-based reactions such as Schiff-base coupling, alkyne hydroamination and amidation will be utilized to construct the functional MPPs. New A2-, A3-, A4- and An-type amine monomers and B2- and B3-type aldehyde, alkyne, isocyanate, isothiocyanate and aroyl chloride monomers will be designed and synthesized. MPPs with different topological structures, pore sizes, surface areas and advanced functionalities will be prepared by different monomer combinations. Monomers with AIE characteristics will be incorporated into the MPPs to serve as luminescent indicators, while the nitrogen-containing moieties in the MPPs will serve as functional ligands to interact with different guest analytes. The properties of the MPPs will be systematically investigated and their utility in CO2 capture, chiral separation, fluorescent chemosensors, gene delivery, etc. will be explored. It is anticipated that this proposed research project will develop a variety of MPPs with novel topological structures and advanced functional properties with high potential for high-tech applications. 多孔材料的发展近年来在材料科学界得到了广泛的关注。具有高比表面积的金属有机骨架材料和共价有机骨架材料在气体储存和分离、分子吸附、传感器和催化等领域具有潜在应用。然而，晶态的金属有机骨架材料和共价有机骨架材料的制备通常需要精确控制并涉及严格的反应条件，这些制备上的困难限制了这两种材料的多样性。另一方面，微孔聚合物材料具有类似的孔隙特性，同时又享有合成简便、轻质、高热稳定性和化学稳定性，以及高比表面积等优点。科学家们已经对这类微孔聚合物材料的合成方法进行了大量的研究，并以其在气体吸附和储存中的潜在应用为导向，对材料的孔隙大小和比表面积大小进行控制。但是，针对这些微孔聚合物特殊的功能（例如发光性质等）的工作很少被报道。 我们研究组从一系列螺旋桨状的分子中发现了一种聚集诱导发光现象，并且研究了这类化合物的潜在高科技应用，例如化学传感器、生物探针、发光二极管等。在这个研究课题中，我们计划制备具有聚集诱导发光特性的富氮微孔聚合物，从而扩展它们除了气体储存和吸附以外的其他实际应用。不同类型的氨基偶联反应例如希夫碱化学、炔烃的氨基加成反应和酰胺加成反应等将会用于构筑这些功能性的微孔聚合物材料。我们将会设计和制备新型A2-、A3-、A4-以及An-型等含有多官能团的单体胺和B2-以及B3-型的醛/炔/异氰/异硫氰/酰氯等单体。具有不同拓扑结构、孔隙特性和先进功能的微孔聚合物将会通过不同的单体组合来制备。具有聚集诱导发光特性的单体将会引入到微孔聚合物结构中作为荧光指示剂，同时，聚合物中富氮的结构基元可以与不同的客体分子相互作用。我们将系统研究这些微孔聚合物的性质，并开发它们在二氧化碳捕捉，手性分离、荧光化学传感器、基因传输等领域的应用。我们希望通过这个项目开发大量的微孔聚合物材料，它们具备新型的拓扑结构、可调控的性质、先进的功能以及潜在的高科技应用。

604913.label: Realisation of objectives
604913.value: The purpose of this proposed research is to synthesis new functional monomers, search for appropriate routes for their polymerizations, study the structure-property relationships of the polymers and explore the technology applications of the new materials obtained. Through elaborate efforts in the past three years, we believe we have completed all the objectives. To achieve the objectives, we have prepared a wide variety of azides, alkynes, amines, aldehydes with different structures and functionalities, and developed efficient routes for their polymerizations. For example, we have developed a one-pot three-component polymerization of diynes, primary amines and aldehydes catalyzed by CuCl. This A3-coupling reaction could be completed in a short time, generating high molecular weight polymers in high yields. The obtained polymers were soluble and thermally stable. Some of them showed the novel phenomenon of aggregation-induced emission (AIE) and emitted intense light in the aggregate state. All the polymers showed film-forming capability and exhibited high refractive indices with low chromatic dispersions. They could function as sensitive fluorescent chemosensors for explosive detection. Four polytriazoles with small variation in either the backbone or the linking manner of the triazole were also prepared by Cu-catalyzed azide-alkyne click polymerization. Results found that a small variation in the substituent could lead to completely different absorption and emission behaviours. We also proved experimentally and theoretically that varying the substituents on the 1,4-positions of the triazole ring exerted little influence on the emission behaviour of polytriazoles. We also developed a facile and efficient approach to prepare poly(iminocoumarin)s by one-pot click polymerizations of diyne, disulfonyl azide, and salicylaldehyde or o-hydroxylacetophenone. These polymerizations possessed the advantages of both multicomponent reactions and click reactions, such as outstanding efficiency, mild reaction condition, inexpensive catalyst, and good atom economy. The obtained polymers showed distinguished and tunable refractive indices as well as good thermal stability. Due to the incorporation of tetraphenylethene moieties, the polymers displayed stronger emission in the solid state. Such feature enabled them to serve as materials for fabricating 2D and 3D fluorescent patterns with high resolution. Catalyzed by an inexpensive palladium/copper(I) system, the three-component sequential polymerizations of diynes, carbonyl chloride and optically-active amino ester salt proceeded efficiently in THF/Et3N at room temperature to afford regio- and stereoregular nitrogen-containing polymers with high molecular weights in satisfactory yields. The polymers possessed good solubility and film-forming ability, satisfactory thermal stability and high light refraction. The polymers were chiral due to the helical rotation of their chains in a preferred screw sense by the chiral pendants. Multisubstituted poly(naphthopyran)s could be readily obtained by rhodium-catalyzed oxidative polyannulation of diyne and benzoyl acetonitrile. Because of the strong intermolecular interaction between the naphthopyran units, the emission of the polymers changed in response to external stimuli such as shear force and organic vapor fumigation in the solid state. Coupled with their high thermal stability, the poly(naphthopyran)s are potential to be used as heat-resistant, photopatterning or security materials as well as prompt detectors for volatile organic compounds. We further developed a highly efficient approach to prepare poly(tetraarylethene)s with aggregation-induced emission characteristics by a one-pot one-step palladium-catalyzed three-component polycoupling of internal diynes, aryl diiodides, and arylboronic acids. This polymerization enjoyed the advantages of mild reaction condition, less costly catalyst, and a high tolerance to different functional groups. The obtained polymers possessed unique properties such as good film-forming capability, high refractive indices and good thermal stability. The obtained polymers were promising materials for fabricating well-resolved photopatterns and could serve as highly sensitive and selective fluorescent chemosensors for Ru3+ ion detection. The polymerization routes mentioned above are not friendly to the environment as they all require the use of transition-metal catalysts. With such regard, we have developed catalyst-free multicomponent polymerizations for preparing polythioamides from aromatic diynes, elemental sulfur and aliphatic diamines. The polymers were obtained in high yields with well-defined structures and high molecular weights and refractive indices. The fascinating features of these polymerizations such as catalyst-free, high atom economy, high efficiency, simple operation, and cheap monomers have met the requirements of “green” chemistry, making this methodology a promising tool for the sustainable development of sulfur-containing functional polymers. The polythioamides could emit fluorescence under UV irradiation. The intrachain and intermolecular interactions such as hydrogen bonding between the thiocarbonyl unit and amino group and n→π* interactions between the thioamide functionalities brought the sulfur and nitrogen atoms together to form “heterodox clusters”, which might serve as a new type of luminogen. The luminescence of polythioamides is anticipated to pave the way to broaden the type of biocompatible luminescent materials without conventional chromophores.

604913.label: Major findings and research outcome
604913.value: Development of new methodology for the synthesis of new polymers is a fundamental important research area in macromolecular science. In this investigation, various alkyne-based polymerization routes were developed for preparing new polymers. These polymerizations enjoyed the advantages of high efficiency, mild reaction condition, wide monomer scope and high tolerance to different functional groups. The polymers were obtained in high yields with well-defined structures and high molecular weights. They exhibited an array of functional properties such as high refractive indices, strong light emissions, chirality and photosensitivity, making them to find wide applications in optics, photonics and chemosensing. The properties of the polymers were sensitive to their molecular structures. This provided opportunities to tune their properties to meet diverse needs by molecular engineering endeavour. The investigation of their structure-property relationships provided important guidelines for the further design of polymers with new structures and properties. We also found that heteroatom-containing polymers were light-emissive despite they possessed no traditional chromophores in their structures. The formation of heteroatom clusters was presumed to be the cause for such abnormal phenomenon. As you can see in Part C of this report, more than 20 publications had arisen from this research project. Most of the papers were published in journal articles with high citation indexes. We are confident that further research in this field will lead to more fruitful result.

604913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
604913.value: Because of the rich in alkyne chemistry, many alkyne-based organic reactions are potential to be developed into useful tools for the constructing of new polymers. Thus, much remains to be done in this area. The polymers prepared in this project possessed unique structures and functional properties. Thus, they should find wide practical applications, with possibilities limited by our imaginations. For example, the poly(propargylamine)s are promising candidates for preparing organometallic materials and magnetic ceramics. They can be further functionalized by “click” chemistry to generate nitrogen-rich triazole rings for further applications. The polymeric materials with strong solid-state emission and circular dichromism signals may demonstrate circularly polarized luminescence and are promising candidates for the fabrication of high performance chiroptical devices. Because we have obtained promising results, we are still working on the development of new synthetic tools to new conjugated polymers, investigating their properties and exploring their practical applications. If we are able to get further support from RGC, we will hire experts to explore further the high-technological applications of our polymers in the fabrication of optoelectronic devices such as circularly-polarized organic light-emitting diodes and fluorescent biological probes.

604913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
604913.value: Functional polymers are important to the modern society and the development of new methods for their synthesis is an importance research area in polymer science. Herein, new methodologies based on alkyne organic reactions were proposed, which could give polymers with high molecular weights in high yields. All the polymers were soluble, showing good film-forming capability and high thermal stability. They exhibited novel properties such as strong high refractive indices, light emissions, chirality and photosensitivity, enabling them to work as sensitive fluorescent chemosensors for explosives and metal ions and generation of fluorescent photopatterns with good resolutions. Materials with such attributes are anticipated to find an array of practical applications.

605013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
605013.value: 在大自然和工業界我們常見兩種（互不相溶）液體的介面，該介面在固體表面的運動非常複雜而且尚未被完全理解。這是因為氣液介面與固體接觸所形成的三相交界線的運動受到固體表面的（物理上的）粗糙程度和（化學上的）不均一強烈影響。眾所周知，三相交界線動力學對於液體和固體表面的雜質和缺陷非常敏感。現有的理論和實驗主要關注於單個缺陷或幾個缺陷的簡單情況。這些研究都是基於理想化的條件，得到的結果不能直接適用于現實中的固體表面。現實中，固體表面的一個關鍵屬性就是具有重疊的納米尺度上的缺陷。因為缺少合適的實驗工具，直接觀測真正接近三相交界線的動力學一直是一項富有挑戰性的實驗課題。三相交界線動力學和浸潤一直是涉及多尺度的現象，為了驗證已有的理論上的想法，我們亟需對於三相交界線微觀屬性進行直接測量。 本研究計畫擬對三相交界線的耗散，浸潤動力學以及脂單層的力學屬性進行一系列系統的研究。實驗上我們將利用我們新研發的基於原子力顯微鏡的懸絲探針進行測量。在其中一組實驗中，我們將研究漲落中的三相交界線的阻尼定律。所研究的三相交界線可以形成在單純的氣液介面，或在肥皂膜中，或在表面張力可以變化的脂單層中。此阻尼定律將適用於不同液體粘度和接觸角的介面。通過精確測量這個普適的阻力定律，我們可將所得到的嚴格的物理關係用於驗證各種形式的三相交界線的微觀理論模型。在第二組實驗中，我們將測量拉抻狀態下的脂單層的彈性回應，接觸角滯後的平均值和平滑、粗糙或具有微觀結構的固體表面的動態接觸角的漲落。我們將研究固體表面從親水到超疏水的浸潤特性的變化和不同的表面張力兩者對於三相交界線鎖定和解鎖動力學的影響。對於這些屬性的準確測量可以與理論假設進行定量的對比，從而深入理解脂單層的浸潤動力學。本研究所提議的一系列新實驗將會確立一種定量的實驗方法，將以即時，高精度的方式表征很多重要並具有現實意義的氣液介面，其中包括聚合物，表面活性劑，脂類和蛋白質。 本計畫所提議的研究將是我們普遍理解二維軟物質系統的基本出發點。對於該系統的理解將為研究鐵磁疇牆，電荷密度波的鎖定和II型超導的渦流柵等隨機力場的一系列彈性動力學問題提供重要幫助。同時，本研究對於液滴、潤滑劑和鍍膜的鋪展，三次採油和多相流等實際應用課題具有重大的普適意義。

605013.label: Realisation of objectives
605013.value: To fulfill the two research objectives, we have carried out two major projects to study contact line dissipation and wetting dynamics. In one experiment, we made a direct measurement of the friction coefficient ξc of two fluctuating contact lines formed on a fiber surface when a long glass fiber intersects the two water-air interfaces of a nanometer-thin soap film. The glass fiber of diameter d in the range of 0.4–4 μm and length 100–300 μm is glued onto the front end of a rectangular cantilever used for atomic force microscopy (AFM). As a sensitive mechanical resonator, the “long-needle” AFM can accurately measure a minute change of its viscous damping caused by the soap film. By measuring the broadening of the resonant peak of the hanging fiber probe with varying viscosity η of the soap film and different surface treatments of the glass fiber, we find that the contact line dissipation obeys a universal scaling law, ξc = απdη, where πd is the contact line length, and α = 1.1 ± 0.3 is a universal coefficient independent of the change of liquid-solid contact angle. The experimental result is in good agreement with the numerical result based on the phase field model under the generalized Navier boundary conditions. The understanding of contact line friction provides a solid foundation for the further study of other liquid interfaces of practical importance, such as those coated with polymers, surfactant and lipids. In the second experiment, we carried out a systematic study of contact angle hysteresis (CAH) by directly measuring the capillary force acting on a contact line formed on a fiber surface when a long glass fiber intersects a liquid-air interface. By accurately measuring the capillary force hysteresis loop of 28 different liquids with varying surface tensions and contact angles, we find a universal behavior of the capillary force difference per unit length in the advancing and receding directions and the spring constant of a stretched meniscus by the glass fiber. The measurements of the capillary force and its fluctuations suggested that CAH on an ambient solid surface is caused primarily by two types of coexisting and spatially intertwined defects with opposite natures. The contact line is actually pinned by the repulsive defects in the advancing direction and by the attractive defects in the receding direction. With the completion of the above research projects, the two project objectives have been fully achieved.

605013.label: Major findings and research outcome
605013.value: Measurement of contact-line dissipation in a nanometer-thin soap film. The dynamics of a moving contact line (MCL) between a liquid interface and a solid surface is an outstanding problem in fluid physics and has been with us for many years. Our current understanding of the contact line dynamics in the immediate vicinity of the contact line (∼1 nm), in which molecular interactions between the liquid and solid are important, relies mainly on the results from molecular dynamic simulations. Direct measurement of the properties of the MCL in this regime is, therefore, essential to test different theoretical ideas. Our measurement of the friction coefficient ξc of the MCL was obtained at the thin film limit, in which the contribution of the bulk fluid to the viscous damping of the soap film is negligibly small. The establishment of the scaling law for ξc has several important implications. First, as a universal scaling law applicable to different fluid systems with different viscosities and contact angles, it provides a rigorous relationship which can be used to test various microscopic models for MCL. Second, it sets up an intrinsic bound for the dissipation of the MCL, which is useful for evaluating relevant molecular parameters associated with the MCL, such as the slip length for different fluids. This work was published in Physical Review E. Understanding contact angle hysteresis on an ambient solid surface. Contact angle hysteresis (CAH), where the motion of a contact line (CL) is pinned by the physical roughness and/or chemical heterogeneity on the solid surface, is an outstanding problem in interfacial dynamics. Despite of a large number of experimental and theoretical studies, one still has a poor understanding of CAH. Up to now, we do not have quantitative theoretical or experimental answer to such simple questions as how CAH is determined by the basic features of the substrate-fluid interactions. Our measurements of the capillary force and its fluctuations revealed that CAH on an ambient solid surface is caused primarily by two types of coexisting and spatially intertwined defects with opposite natures. The contact line is primarily pinned by the relatively non-wetting defects in the advancing direction and by the relatively wetting defects in the receding direction. Based on the experimental observations, we proposed a “composite model” of CAH and scaling laws, which explained the basic features of the measured hysteresis force loops. This work was published in Physical Review E.

605013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
605013.value: The understanding of contact line hysteresis and dissipation achieved through the research discussed above provides a solid foundation for the further study of other liquid interfaces of practical interest, such as those coated with polymers, surfactant, and lipids. So far we have only studied the effects of simple liquid-air interfaces and it is certainly very interesting to further extend our study to more complex interfaces of practical interest. We plan to seek additional funding to support the research in this direction.

605013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
605013.value: While liquid interfaces between two (immiscible) fluids are common in nature and industry, their motion over an ambient solid surface is complicated and not well understood. Understanding the interactions and dynamics of the contact line (CL) formed between a liquid interface and a solid surface is a fundamental issue in fluid physics and is also a concern of many industrial processes ranging from spreading of droplets, lubricants, and coatings to the extraction of oil from sandstone by injecting water. In this research we studied the CL hysteresis and dissipation and found a universal scaling law for the friction coefficient of a fluctuating CL. Our measurements of the capillary force and its fluctuations revealed that CL hysteresis is caused by two different sets of relatively wetting and non-wetting defects on the fiber surface. The contact line is primarily pinned by the non-wetting defects in the advancing direction and by the wetting defects in the receding direction. Our experiments demonstrated the importance of quantitative characterization and understanding of the physical origin of the CL hysteresis. Such an understanding opens the door to a wide variety of new experiments using a fiber surface with controlled patterns or micro-textures to study the CL dynamics.

605113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
605113.value: Achmatowicz rearrangement, an organic reaction that transform a cheap, readily available furan alcohol into a highly-valued fine chemical called tetrahydropyranone acetal (THPA), was developed originally as a general method to synthesize natural and non-natural sugar (saccharide). The tetrahydropyranone acetals (THPAs) were later been demonstrated to undergo several types of reactions that find applications in the chemical synthesis of complex natural products with high efficiency. Most of these methods rely heavily on the elaboration of only one (acetal) of the many functionalities because the chemical reactivity profile of tetrahydropyran acetal has not been fully uncovered and understood. In this proposal, we will explore the new chemical reactivity of THPAs by taking advantage of the inherent acetal and enone functionalities in a conjugated fashion, which may lead to development of some new types of useful reactions that advance the organic synthesis. The first idea of our proposal is to utilize the alkene bonded to the acetal of THPAs for a new type of carbon-carbon bond formation by a named reaction: Tsuji-Trost reaction. The enone products could be further utilized for Michael reaction to make polycyclic compounds. The second idea is to remove the oxygen (hydroxyl) of THPAs (Kishi reduction using trifluoroacetic acid and triethylsilane) under mild, non-acidic conditions by single electron transfer reagent such samarium diiodide by exploitation of the existing enone in conjugated form. In addition to the new synthetic method development, the major part of this proposal is the total syntheses of two cytotoxic natural products uprolide F diacetate (UFD) and uprolide G acetate (UGA) using Achmatowicz rearrangement as the key step to build the highly substituted tetrahydropyran with defined stereochemistry. The only difference of UFD and UGA is the protecting group on a tertiary alcohol: Acetyl for UFD; methyl for UGA. Due to the ambiguous constitutional structures and novel skeletons among the cembranoids, UFD and UGA were targeted by total synthesis, which up to now has not been achieved and may be the only solution for their structure confirmation. Our synthetic strategy features several other key transformations: Barbier type macrocyclization/lactonization, olefin cross metathesis and Morita-Baylis-Hillman reaction. The employment of these key reactions would greatly improve the synthetic efficiency for these complex molecules. Armed with this strategy, the total syntheses of both UFD and UGA could be achieved enantioselectively in only 24 steps with a single route, which comprises the first, asymmetric total syntheses of these two natural products. Achmatowicz重排，是一个将廉价易得的呋喃醇转变成高价值的精细化工品二氢哌喃酮缩醛（ DHPA ）的有机反应，最初被开发作为一种合成天然和非天然的糖（糖类）的通用的方法。二氢哌喃酮缩醛（ DHPAs ）随后被证实可以进行多种类型的反应，它们在复杂天然产物的化学合成中得到了高效的应用。然而由于二氢哌喃酮缩醛的化学反应活性信息没有被充分发现和理解，所以这些反应方法中的大多数主要依赖于众多官能团中缩醛的修饰。在这个研究提案里，我们将综合利用缩醛和烯酮的固有功能，开发一些有用的能促进有机合成发展的反应类型，进一步探索有关二氢哌喃酮缩醛的新型的化学反应。我们的提议的第一个设想是，利用二氢哌喃酮缩醛中与缩醛相连的烯烃通过人名反应Tsuji-Trost 反应完成新的碳-碳键成键。而烯酮产物可进一步通过迈克尔加成反应，用以合成多环化合物。第二个设想是，再次综合利用结构中的烯酮，由单电子转移试剂如二碘化钐，在温和的，非酸性条件下脱除二氢哌喃酮缩醛中的氧（羟基）（Kishi还原利用三氟乙酸和三乙基硅烷）。除了开发新的合成方法，本研究提案的主要部分是利用Achmatowicz重排作为关键步骤来构建高度取代的立体化学确定的四氢哌喃而最终完成两种细胞毒性的天然产物uprolide F双乙酸酯（ UFD ）和uprolide G 乙酸酯（ UGA ）的全合成。UFD和UGA的唯一的区别是叔醇的保护基不同： UFD是乙酰而UGA是甲基。因为UFD和UGA不确定的化学结构以及西柏烷类中新颖的化学骨架，但又由于这两个油状的天然产品的不适合做X-射线分析，所以全合成成为确定两者结构唯一可能的方案。更重要的是，全合成可以提供这些稀缺的天然产物的足够样品，我们就有可能合成类似物进行详细的生物活性研究。我们的合成策略含有几个关键转化：巴比尔的类型大环化反应 /内酯化反应，烯烃交换反应以及Morita-Baylis-Hillman反应。这些关键反应的运用极大地提高了合成效率，并降低了合成这些复杂的分子的挑战。一旦拥有此策略，就可以用一条合成路线只需24步实现对UFD和UGA的对映选择性全合成，这将会是这两种天然产物首次不对称全合成。

605113.label: Realisation of objectives
605113.value: Objective 1: We systematically investigated the reaction of the Achmatowicz rearrangement products and found that the bis-electrophilic reactivity could be well controlled by the reaction conditions and reagents, which allowed us to develop new synthetic methods: (a) Achmatowicz rearrangement/Heck-Matsuda arylation for the synthesis of 2,6-trans-tetrahydropyrans; (b) Palladium- or base-catalyzed oxa-[3+2] cycloaddition of Achmatowicz rearrangement products with cyclic 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds for the synthesis of polyhetereocycles of medicinal value. Objective 2: we have explored three different synthetic strategies over two years and finally developed one viable strategy for the total synthesis of the proposed structure of uprolide G acetate. However, we found that the spectroscopic data of our synthetic sample and authentic material were not consistent. After tremendous efforts on synthesis and spectroscopic analysis, we eventually confirmed the molecular structures of uprolide F diacetate and uprolide G acetate by total synthesis of three different isomers. Objective 3: both ring-closing methods (Ring-closing metathesis and Julia olefination) have been explored at a late stage of synthesis and were viable for the synthesis. In fact, the reaction conditions were found to be critical to the success of these two macrocyclization methods. Objective 4: We have achieved the first and asymmetric total synthesis of uprolide F diacetate and uprolide G acetate after 3-year continuous experimental work and many unsuccessful attempts of strategies. Objective 5: Three PhD graduate students (ZHU, Liangyu; REN, Jingyun; LI, Zhilong) working in full time on this projects have received extensive trainings in organic synthesis and become independent scientists in industry and academia.

605113.label: Major findings and research outcome
605113.value: (a) We have developed two new strategies that have been used successfully for the first total synthesis and structural revisions of uprolide G acetate and uprolide F diacetate, respectively. (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2015, 54, 627-632; Org. Lett., 2015, 17, 1966-1969.). (b) We have developed two strategies for the first total synthesis of musellarins A-C, featuring Achmatowicz rearrangement for the construction of the 2,6-trans-tetrahydropyrans. (Chem. Commun., 2014, 50, 10990-10993; Chem. Eur. J. 2015, 21, 11152-11157). The synthetic utilities of the new method for construction of 2,6-trans-tetrahydropyrans via Achmatowicz rearrangement/Heck-Matsuda reaction were demonstrated by collective synthesis of several diarylheptanoid natural products. (Synthesis, 2016, 48, 1630-1636; J. Org. Chem. 2017, 82, 1127-1135). (c) We have developed a general and efficient strategy for the construction of 6,8-dioxabicyclo[3.2.1]octane via Achmatowicz rearrangement (J. Org. Chem. 2016, 81, 2203-2212). This strategy was employed for total synthesis of 6,8-DOBCO-containing natural products including attenols A and B (Org. Lett. 2015, 17, 744-747), didemniserinolipid B (J. Org. Chem. 2014, 79, 6987-6995), psoracorylifol B, and ent-psoracorylifol C (Org. Lett., 2014, 16, 2986-2989). (d) We have developed a new method for synthesis of polycyclic heterocycles via divergent cycloaddition of Achmatowicz rearrangement products with cyclic 1,3-dicarbonyls (Org. Chem. Front. 2016, 3, 714-719). (e) We have greatly developed a new green catalytic protocol for Achmatowicz rearrangement (J. Org. Chem. 2016, 81, 4847-4855).

605113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
605113.value: Achmatowicz rearrangement is a powerful transformation that have been exploited by us for organic synthesis in the past four years. The potential for further development is attractive and we are exploring (i) synthetic methodology and applications of Aza-Achmatowicz rearrangement, (ii) Pd-catalyzed arylation of Achmatowicz rearrangement products for the synthesis of C-aryl glycosides, (iii) extension of our findings and developed methodologies to total synthesis of other families of natural products, and (iv) improvement of [5+2]-cycloaddition of Achmatowicz rearrangement.

605113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
605113.value: This project is focused on exploration of a named organic reaction called Achmatowicz rearrangement in organic synthesis because it has not been exploited in the past. After extensive experimentation, we demonstrated that it is a powerful reaction that can be used in total synthesis of complex natural products with better efficiency, scalability, and reproducibility. We also discovered some new reactivity of Achmatowicz rearrangement products, leading to development of new synthetic methodologies that are useful and effective to organic synthesis. Finally we developed a green and catalytic protocol for Achmatowicz rearrangement, which will be of importance to further applications. Our research findings make Achmatowicz rearrangement be a hot topic and new tool in organic synthesis.

605213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
605213.value: 隨著人們對理解和利用石墨烯物理性質的研究取得顯著的進展后，越來越多的人們將目光轉向了其他具有原子層厚度的二維晶體薄膜材料。其中，具有半導體性質的過渡金屬硫化物最近引起了人們最多的關注，特別是二硫化鉬。二硫化鉬單層的厚度為6.7埃，其由S–Mo–S三原子層構成。在二硫化鉬單層中，Mo 和 S之間形成很強的離子-共價鍵，然後各個二硫化鉬單層再通過范得瓦爾斯力相結合形成二硫化鉬晶體。通過減少二硫化鉬單層的數目，人們可以將原來間接帶隙的二硫化鉬晶體轉變成具有直接帶隙的二硫化鉬單層。人們研究還發現具有半導體特性的二硫化鉬單層會表現出優良的電學和光學性質。由於帶隙的存在，使得其在彌補零帶隙石墨烯不足的同時仍然具有很多石墨烯在電子和光電子應用方面的優勢之處。此外，二硫化鉬單層和石墨烯類似，都是多能谷材料。然而，和石墨烯不同的是，二硫化鉬單層具有很強的自旋-軌道相互作用，也不具有反演對稱性。這意味著它是一個可用來研究和電子能谷指數及自旋相關的基礎物理的典型體系。在本項研究中，我們將試圖通過引入單軸應力或量子限制的方法，在實驗上探索解除二硫化鉬單層能谷簡並的可能性。我們也將在該系統上深入研究人們理論預期的光誘導產生的電荷霍爾、自旋霍爾和能谷霍爾效應。本項目的順利實施將會極大促進人們對二硫化鉬單層物理性質的理解，從而為未來人們利用具有半導體特性的過渡金屬硫化物單層打下堅實的基礎。

605213.label: Realisation of objectives
605213.value: We have successfully obtained monolayer and a few layer samples of MoS2 and other two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) including WSe2, WTe2 via micromechanical exfoliation. We have employed Raman spectroscopy and atomic force microscopy to determine the thickness of the obtained samples. We have successfully fabricate these sample into field effect transistor (FET) devices using e-beam lithography. However, for FET based on monolayer samples we encounter a difficulty of achieving good ohmic contacts. We have tried to use graphene as intermediate layer for electrodes to overcome this problem but with limited success. For the fabricated FET devices, we have studied the properties of Schottky contacts which are formed at metal/semiconductor interfaces and always have large impact on the performance of FET. We use scanning photocurrent microscopy to directly probe the spatial distribution of the in-plane lateral Schottky depletion regions at the metal/2D-TMDC interfaces. We have fabricated front gate FET devices using ionic liquid as the dielectric layer in which we observe ambipolar transport behaviors. We have tried to apply uniaxial stress to MoS2 monolayer and a few layers samples using a piezoelectric actuator to study the influence of strain on the optical properties. However, the maximum strain induced by the piezoelectric actuator is rather small (less than 1%). We failed to detect any changes in the samples’ optical properties. We have studied photoluminescence (PL) of monolayer samples using circular polarized laser excitation. We can achieve valley dependent PL emission similar to that reported in the literatures. We have fabricated MoS2/WSe2 van der Waals heterostructures by polymer-free dry transfer method. We also fabricated NbSe2/WTe2 van der Waals heterostructure, which provides an ideal platform to study the interface effect in all-TMDC based superconductor/normal-metal interfaces. We have systematically studied the magnetotransport properties in exfoliated WTe2 thin films.

605213.label: Major findings and research outcome
605213.value: Schottky contacts, formed at metal/semiconductor interfaces, always have a large impact on the performance of field-effect transistors (FETs). We carried out the experimental studies of Schottky contacts in TMDCs FET devices. We use scanning photocurrent microscopy to directly probe the spatial distribution of the in-plane lateral Schottky depletion regions at the metal/2D-TMDC interfaces. This lateral depletion region length is estimated to be around several microns and can be effectively tuned by the gate and drain–source biases. Our results solidify the importance of lateral Schottky depletion regions in the photoresponse of 2D TMDC optoelectronic devices. This work has been presented in EP2DS conference, published in Nanoscale, and also been invited to present in 2D Crystal workshop. We carried out systematic magneto transport studies of a-few-layers exfoliated WTe2 thin film devices. We observed large, positive magnetoresistance (MR) in our WTe2 device (~6315 %), which show no sign of saturation up to 14 T. The results of temperature-dependent carrier density show a relative change of electron and hole concentration, implying a temperature-driven Lifshitz transition in WTe2. A quantitative analysis of the temperature and thickness dependent transport results of WTe2 demonstrates both carrier densities and mobility play significant roles in determining the magnitude and the nonsaturating behavior of MR. This work has been presented in ICPS conference and published in Solid State Communications. We fabricated NbSe2/WTe2 van der Waals heterostructure, which provides an ideal platform to study the interface effect in all-TMDC based superconductor/normal-metal interfaces. We found a resistance upturn below the NbSe2 superconducting transition temperature in the temperature dependent resistance measurements and a conductance dip accompanied with a double-peak feature in the dI/dV spectra. These features can be suppressed by increasing the measuring current. By analyzing the dI/dV spectra with BKT theory, all these results can be interpreted as the suppression of Andreev reflection at the non-transparent NbSe2/WTe2 interface. These results are included in a PhD thesis. We fabricated front gate FET devices using ionic liquid as the dielectric layer for TMDCs. We observed ambipolar transport behaviors, which allows us directly extract the energy gap of the TMDCs. We fabricated MoS2/WSe2 van der Waals heterostructures by polymer-free dry transfer method. We observed a diode like rectification behavior and studied the photo response of the diode. We found that interlayer exciton recombination process and the interlayer charge transfer process compete against each other. These results are included in an MPhil thesis.

605213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
605213.value: What we have achieved so far indicating that van der Waals heterostructures based on 2D materials are the most important issue to be explored in future. These van der Waals heterostructures can reveal entirely new physical phenomena which can lead to various functionalities. Further exploration of van der Waals heterostructures should be future actions to be taken.

605213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
605213.value: Atomically thin two dimensional crystals obtainable from layered materials are attracting great attentions for their fundamental properties and device applications. In this project, we have found that Schottky contacts in 2D field-effect transistors devices extend laterally with good photoresponse tunable by the gate and drain–source biases. This is important for its potential optoelectronics device applications. We have observed a nonsaturating and extremely large magnetoresistance in a-few-layers WTe2 thin film devices, which may have potential applications in magnetic sensors and random access memories. We also found that van der Waals heterostructures fabricated using various 2D materials exhibit many interesting properties, which should be further explored for basic properties and device applications. All these results indicate 2D materials and their heterostructures are fertile ground for discovery new physical properties and applications.

605413.label: Project Objectives
605413.value: We will study magnonic STT generation by microwaves or spin Seebeck effect. We will also study the interaction of the magnonic STT with domain walls (DWs). Due to the nonlinear nature of magnetization dynamics, DW motion will inevitably emit SWs. We will examine how SWs are emitted. Emitted SWs carry away angular momenta so that DW dynamics should also be affected. We will investigate the robustness and generality of the newly predicted DW propagation mode through DW emission. It is foreseeable that SWs emitted by one DW can mediate a DW-DW interaction after passing through another DW. This causes crosstalk in wires with more than one DWs happened in race-track memory.
