610713.label: Project Title(Chinese)
610713.value: 多視角與自由視角視頻的合作式流媒體傳輸技術

610713.label: Project Objectives
610713.value: Content Replication for Multiview Video-on-Demand: We will consider a video-on-demand (VoD) network for stored interactive multiview video streaming (IMVS). In the network, there is a remote repository storing all the pre-encoded multiview videos. In order to support a large number of users, distributed content servers are deployed close to user pools to collaboratively replicate video segments given their limited storage capacities. A client sends inter-view or temporal switching requests of segments to its local server. The server would fulfill the request directly if the data has been replicated locally; otherwise, it would contact a neighboring server or remote repository to retrieve the missing data with some access cost. Due to the special coding structure of multiview video, besides those hits and misses, we will uniquely consider “indirect hit,” where a nearby server has replicated a correlated frame and the repository supplies the differential. We will study which video segments should be replicated at each server to minimize network access cost. We have already formulated the problem, and will prove its complexity. We will propose and study powerful replication algorithms for the network. Preliminary results have shown that our approaches are promising. Collaborative Live Streaming of Free Viewpoint Video: We will consider live free viewpoint video streaming, where texture and depth of videos from multiple captured viewpoints (anchor views) are used to generate the virtual viewpoints in-between. We will study a cooperative network where peers share their anchor views to support freeview interactions, and investigate the anchor view allocation problem to minimize network cost. We will formulate the problem, prove its complexity, and design algorithms for such streaming network. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first piece of work addressing anchor view allocation problem for live free viewpoint video streaming.

610713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
610713.value: 多視角視頻是由多個通過大量緊湊分佈在相同場景前的攝像機同步拍攝的2D視頻流組合而成。在多視角視頻的點播與直播中，用戶可以根據喜好隨時切換到不同的視角觀看。而在自由視角視頻中，每一個視角可以由兩個相鄰視角組合而成。用戶主動的視角選擇可以增強所觀看到3D畫面的景深與視覺效果。多視角視頻擁有廣泛並引人注目的應用場景，如教育，醫療，體育等。 之前關於多視角視頻的研究主要集中在不同時間與視角的幀壓縮的問題上，探索相鄰時間與相鄰視角之間幀的關係。在傳統意義上，合作式流媒體傳輸主要集中在對單一視角視頻的研究，由於基本的編碼結構的不同，並不能直接擴展運用至多視角或自由視角視頻傳輸。此前並沒有關於多視角與自由視角的合作式流媒體傳輸的研究。 在這個項目中，我們對適用於多視角與自由視角視頻的合作式網絡設計與優化進行研究。為了支持高效訪問與存儲，我們使用多種幀結構對視頻內容進行編碼。這種幀結構將同一視角的連續幀封裝成為片斷，並對在一定距離內的相鄰視角根據相關性進行冗餘編碼。 我們此項研究的範圍包括高級視頻編碼，流媒體傳輸與網絡優化。它在多視角與自由視角流媒體視頻領域有著巨大的商業價值，並對於能否成功地對海量用戶提供此項服務起著至關重要的作用。基於我們多年在合作式流媒體和視頻處理領域的深厚積累，我們提出對以下問題進行研究： * 多視角視頻點播的存儲與備份：我們將研究多視角視頻的互動點播系統。利用先進的多視角編碼結構，我們提出並使用“半命中”(indirect hit)概念：由本地服務器提供相鄰視角幀，棧房(repository)提供幀差編碼。我們研究哪些視頻片斷應該被備份在本地服務器，從而減少網絡訪問消耗。在初步實驗中我們的方法有著不錯的結果。 * 合作式自由視角流媒體直播：我們將研究自由視角視頻的實時直播。我們提出一個全新的合作式網絡，使結點間可以共享視角，以支持自由視角的交互。我們研究視角分配的問題，並通過問題制定，複雜度分析與算法設計的方式優化網絡消耗。據我們所知，這是首個解決自由視角流媒體實時傳輸中視角分配問題的研究。

610713.label: Realisation of objectives
610713.value: We have achieved the objectives with much success. The following summarizes our achievements: 1) Content Replication for Multiview Video-on-Demand: We have studied, through theoretical and experimental study, the optimization of multiview VoD network, and extended it to other emerging video standards, including high-definition, cloud storage, etc. The optimization framework is applicable to VoD system in general, in order to design and deploy a scalable network. Our research is comprehensive, capturing many important parameters and factors in VoD network design. The coding structure, segment distribution and segment access have all been considered. This part of research has led to the following publications: Coding Structure and Replication Optimization for Interactive Multiview Video Streaming, IEEE Transactions on Multimedia, Vol. 16, No. 7, pp. 1874-1887, November 2014 Bucket-Filling: An Asymptotically Optimal VoD Network with Source Coding, IEEE Transactions on Multimedia, Vol. 17, No. 5, pp. 723-735, May 2015 Video Management and Resource Allocation for a Large-scale VoD Cloud, ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing, Communication and Applications (TOMM) Special Issue on Multimedia Big Data: Networking, Vol. 12, No. 5s, pp. 72:1-72:21, Sept 2016 Dissecting User Behaviors for a Simultaneous Live and VoD IPTV System, ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing, Communications and Applications, Vol. 10, No. 3, pp. 23:1-23:16, April 2014. Distributed Joint Optimization for Large-scale Video-on-Demand, Elsevier Computer Networks, Vol. 75, pp. 86-98, December 2014 2) Collaborative Live Streaming of Free Viewpoint Video: We have successfully completed the study of this objective. We have considered live streaming of recent coding standards, such as free viewpoint, multiple description, high bitrate, heterogeneous bitrates, etc. We have formulated the problems, studied their complexity, proposed novel algorithmic approaches, and experimentally validated the schemes. 610713.label: Major findings and research outcome
610713.value: Our major findings are as follows: 1) For VoD: We have studied interactive streaming for pre-encoded multiview videos. We consider distributed content servers to support large-scale interactive multiview video service. These servers collaboratively replicate and access video contents. We study two challenges in this setting: what is an efficient coding structure that supports interactive viewing and, given that, what to replicate in each server in order to minimize the cost incurred by interactive temporal and view switches? We propose efficient coding and distribution to achieve interactive view-switching, trading off storage with transmission rate. We also propose a content replication strategy that takes advantage of access locality, so that the remote repository only needs to supply the pre-encoded view differential. We formulate content replication problem and propose efficient algorithms. Both simulation and experimental results show that our approaches achieve substantially better results than other state-of-the-art schemes. 2) For live streaming: We consider, for the first time, collaborative live streaming of a free viewpoint video, where a group of users may interactively pull and cooperatively share streams of different anchor views. Beyond that, we have also considered how to distribute high bitrate video to a large group of distributed users using collaborative streaming. There is a cost to access the video from the live source, a cost to “reconfigure” the peer network, and a distortion cost due to error or view generation. We optimize the video quality given all these system parameters. We find that, if the reconfiguration cost due to view switching is negligible, the view allocation problem for freeview video can be optimally and efficiently solved in polynomial time using dynamic programming. For the other cases, the problem becomes NP-hard. We have presented locally optimal, centralized and distributed algorithms to tackle the problems.

610713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
610713.value: With our current success and fruitful results, we are currently working on the following areas: 1) From cloud to fog: To further scale up streaming, we are extending our results to fog streaming. We have already started a fog streaming project, and have conducted some experimental study on it. 2) Video data center: With the appetite for video bitrate continuing to grow, video data center needs to be designed to accommodate a large number of titles for heterogeneous devices (mobile to HDTV). We are conducting study on how to minimize data center cost while guaranteeing a certain level of service quality for a large and distributed video store. 3) Technology transfer: We will continue to develop streaming solutions to address industrial needs. The technologies can scale to a large number of users, with low cost and high efficiency. Whenever opportunities arise, the technologies will be transferred to industry for commercial adoption and system deployment.

610713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
610713.value: We have successfully completed the project, with productive results well beyond what we set off to achieve. Specifically, we have studied, for the first time, coding-replication co-design for multiview VoD system. We are also among the first to study collaborative freeview video streaming. The studies have generated much interest in the community. Besides theoretical study, we have also developed the technologies by engaging our UGs and PGs. The technologies have been transferred to industry with real commercial users (China Mobile HK, HK Jockey Club, MeiAh, etc.). This shows that our solutions are proven not only strong theoretically, but also deployable commercially. The technology has won Gold Award at the HK ICT Award in 2014, evidence of its usefulness and impacts. During the period, 2 PhDs and 6 MPhils have been graduated, who are supported in part by the funding. The funding has also been used to support UGs to conduct research with the PGs. Job opportunities and other learning experiences hence have been created.

611013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
611013.value: Ultrafine particles (UFPs) are present in indoor environments, where occupants spend most of their time. Once inhaled, such particles can penetrate deeply into the lungs and pose an elevated health risk. The airborne virus, nanometer in size, is also one type of ultrafine particles of great concern. They are responsible for the transmission of many infectious diseases, including influenza and SARS. The removal of ultrafine particles is difficult due to their very small size. Currently, high quality packed fibre filters are usually used in removing ultrafine particles. This method is both energy and material expensive. Some particles will also resuspend into the air when replacing the filter. Alternative technology in UFPs removal and airborne virus inactivation without these shortcomings is desired. Particles suspended in air will coagulate in a sound field, and this phenomenon is referred to as acoustic agglomeration. Ultrafine particles will also coagulate to form coarser particles under an ultrasonic sound field. Combining this with a lower grade filter or an aerodynamic device allows removal of ultrafine particles in a more energy and material efficient way than using the high efficiency particulate air (HEPA) filter. To enable this technology integration, modelling and characterization of the acoustic agglomeration of UFPs under realistic conditions are crucial. This project will first develop a comprehensive model to predict the UFPs agglomeration rate and the resulting particle concentration. The model will be based on a Lagrangian approach and does not assume a homogeneous particle distribution. It will also incorporate the coupling effects of different agglomeration mechanisms. The model will be verified by a series of experiments in stagnant air, a straight tunnel with airflow, and a curved tunnel with air flow. After verification, the model will be used to characterize the acoustic agglomeration in a cyclonic flow and the UFPs removal efficiency when combined with an aerodynamic device for indoor applications. This system will then be built and its performance will be tested experimentally. The feasibility of using acoustic agglomeration on the inactivation of airborne viruses combining with electrolyzed water droplets will also be studied. This airborne virus inactivation technology will not have the shortcomings of existing technologies, since it will not generate hazardous chemicals during the disinfection process or introduce disinfection by-products into room air. This technology will be highly material and energy efficient as it does not require consumable parts and will have significantly lower pressure drop than the HEPA filter. 超微粒子存在於室內環境中。住戶因為長時間處於當中，他們一旦吸入這種粒子，也因為粒子可以滲透到肺部，從而增加健康風險。空氣中的病毒是納米級的尺寸，也是超微粒子的一種，其引起的風險不容忽視。傳染性疾病（包括流感和SARS）多通過超微粒子傳播。移除超微粒子是非常困難的，因為其體積非常細小。目前，一般使用高品質的填充纖維過濾器作移除工作。這種方法無論在能量或物料消耗方面也較高昂。而在更換過濾器的過程中，顆粒亦有機會再懸浮到空氣中。若能找到替代技術應用於超微粒子的移除及空氣中病毒的滅活，又能避免以上的缺點則更理想。懸浮在空氣中的顆粒會凝聚在聲場中，而這種現象稱為聲波團聚。在聲場中，超微粒子亦可凝聚成較大的顆粒。利用這現象，在移除超微粒子方面，可以使用較低檔次的過濾器或其他氣動裝置，相對於使用高檔次的（HEPA）過濾器，能在能量及物料消耗方面更有效益。為了成功應用這項技術，移除超微粒子在現實情況下的數學模型建構、和表徵描繪是至為重要。該項目將首先研發一個全面的模型來預測超微粒子的聚集率和導致的顆粒物濃度。該模型將基於拉格朗日方法而不用假設顆粒均勻分佈。它也將考慮到不同的聚集機制的耦合效應。該模型將通過一系列實驗的驗證，包括靜止的空氣中，直線氣流的風洞中，和彎曲的風洞中。經驗證後，該模型將被用來描繪聲波團聚在旋風氣流中的表徵及結合其他氣動裝置後的移除超微粒子的效率。然後該系統將被構建，並以實驗測試其性能。聲波團聚應用於空氣中病毒的滅活的可行性研究也將進行，這個病毒滅活的技術避免出現現有技術的缺點，因為在消毒過程中，它並不產生有害的化學物質或引入消毒副產物到室內空氣中。由於它不要求耗材零件和比較HEPA過濾器具有顯著較低的風阻力，故此，這項技術在能量及物料消耗方面將更有效益。

611013.label: Realisation of objectives
611013.value: The overall project objectives have been achieved. The use of acoustics in aerosol removal technique was investigated by both experimental and numerical approaches. A comprehensive aero-acoustic model for a wide range of conditions, such as for polydispersed particles in a dynamic air flow including the coupling effect of the two nonlinear acoustic effects - acoustic streaming and acoustic radiation pressure - was developed. A three-step approach was adopted. In the first step, the acoustic field and its mean square fluctuation values were calculated. The result of the first step was inputted into the second step to solve for acoustic streaming. The third step consisted in tracking the particle's motion by a Lagrangian approach where the acoustic radiation pressure was considered. Computational simulations were conducted. Simulation and experimental results were compared to corroborate the accuracy. The three-step simulation employed produced streaming results that broadly correlated to those velocity fields obtained by the Particle Imaging Velocimetry (PIV) analyses. The particle removal ratios, equivalent to removal efficiencies in experiments, also produced trends that agreed with the physical results. During the experiments, it was found that acoustic streaming, generated by the depreciation of acoustic sound pressure near the acoustic source, had a significant effect on the deposition of aerosols, in addition to agglomeration. Ultrasound of 30kHz with a pressure level of 150dB was generated with a transducer and a radiating plate. The acoustic generator used ~150W of power, which was significantly lower than that in the literature, achieving high energy efficiency objective. The experimental rig was designed to utilize the emitted nonlinear acoustic effects by this low power acoustic generation system to agglomerate and remove aerosols by deposition on wall. The cleanable design achieved the material efficiency objective. Nonlinear acoustic effects such as acoustic radiation pressure and acoustic streaming were observed experimentally. The visualization of acoustic radiation pressure showed a clear concentration of aerosols at the nodal position of the stationary wave which was set up in the air duct. PIV showed some acoustic streaming patterns inside the air duct, causing particles to concentrate at stagnation points and deposit agglomerated onto the surfaces of the air duct. Both of these observations could be quantified by the measurement of particle size shift and particle number concentrations. Results showed that agglomeration occurred for monodisperse aerosols (nebulized by the polystyrene spherical particles). This was particularly evident when input aerosols were 2 microns where a 50% increase was observed in the size range between 8-10 microns after the acoustic treatment. Acoustic radiation pressure was modelled and showed that submicron aerosols cannot be influenced by this mechanism. Submicron aerosols were influenced by acoustic streaming. Acoustics streaming was also modelled numerically. The simulated streaming patterns showed stagnation points in the flow, which agreed with the experiments. In order to characterize the acoustic agglomeration and particle deposition in different flow conditions, e.g. straight, curved, cyclic, different aspect ratio, etc., factors that affected the removal efficiency including aerosol size, time resided in the acoustic field, aerosol size distribution and initial concentrations were studied. The acoustic residence time, which was determined by the mainstream flow velocities, the aerosol sizes and the input number concentrations were positively correlated to the removal efficiencies. An increase in the time that the particles were exposed to the acoustic field provided a higher chance for agglomeration and deposition. In addition to aerosol sizes, input number concentrations were also found to influence the system performance. In different flow geometries, the acoustic streaming patterns were different and played the key role of particle agglomeration and deposition. The position and size of the radiating plate changed the acoustic field and therefore the acoustic streaming pattern. It was shown that when the plate was positioned off-center, more aerosols were removed by higher degrees of non-uniformity and fluctuation in the flow field. The wider the radiating plate resulted in higher removal efficiencies, from 8.76%-12.21%. An analysis based on simulated acoustic streaming patterns showed that there was a positive correlation between the vorticity, derived from the acoustic streaming flow field in a given air duct geometry, and the particle deposition percentages. This correlation also agreed with the experimentally obtained particle deposition trends. With the aid of these findings, the aerosol removal system was optimized and related systems were derived. The use of acoustics has been demonstrated to be a noninvasive aerosol removal technique offering improved removal efficiencies of up to 38% for testing submicron particles with diameters of 0.3 μm. This far exceeds the performance of traditional cyclone separators currently used in the industry which are able to capture particles with a diameter of 1 μm with only 50% grade efficiency. Related researches and systems derived from this project include aerosol removal by air jet impingement, and research on the frequency effect of a sinusoidal wave in developing a personalized ventilation system. Polydispersed aerosol inputs were also investigated. Given the same concentration, an aerosol mix containing seeding particles that were larger than the test particles, removed more test particles. These types of polydisperse aerosol mixtures also removed the total number of particles more efficiently. The higher ratio between the seeding to test particle concentrations removed higher percentages of test particles. Further analysis into the particle dynamics found that the depositions were correlated with the particle size distribution and initial positions. Larger initial particles and polydisperse particles had higher ratios of area with higher deposition probabilities, when compared with smaller monodisperse particles. In order to study the feasibility of acoustic agglomeration for airborne virus inactivation and removal, polydisperse acoustic aerosol agglomeration with liquid droplets was also performed. Larger-micron aerosols (20 microns measured by Interferometric Mie Imaging, IMI, technique) were continuously generated by aerosolizing injected liquid water onto the acoustic radiating plate. The submicron aerosols were generated by the smouldering of incense which was characterized to have a count medium between 0.08-0.2 microns. Results showed that with the addition of water, a further decrease of 34% in particle number concentration was recorded. Combining this effect with the previously measured particle decreasing rate of 20% for mono-disperse submicron aerosols, the addition of water can reduce the particle concentration to 45% during acoustic agglomeration and deposition. These results suggested that the combination of larger-micron aerosols helped to agglomerate aerosols, thus the inactivation of airborne viruses combining electrolyzed water droplets is possible. The results showed that acoustics is a feasible method to be used with water droplets to remove ultrafine particles, which can be benign viruses. The effect of bioaerosol and its risk assessment were reported and discussed in a workshop in an international conference. The title of the presentation was “Bioaerosol Deposition and Resuspension” and the workshop was entitled “Disease transmission via air and fomites in crowded environment”.

611013.label: Major findings and research outcome
611013.value: The use of second order acoustics as an aerosol removal technique was proposed (Yuen et al. 2014). The work conducted in this project paved the way to realize a hypothesized technique to a physical system with an optimization framework. There are three major research outcomes: understanding the second-order acoustic effects in a proposed system, namely acoustic streaming and acoustic radiation forces; studying their effectiveness on aerosol removal; and finally developing parameters which help to optimize the performance of the proposed system. The initial hypothesis was that the proposed system designed facilitated the generation of acoustic streaming and acoustic radiation force. They were initially confirmed by visualization with photographic evidence and the PIV technique. Following such encouraging findings, experimental studies were performed to validate the effectiveness of aerosol removal by the above-mentioned mechanisms. The change in aerosol particle number concentrations due to acoustics for both first and second order acoustic-aerosol effects were investigated. It was found that under the present setting, second-order acoustic effects dominated. The inclusion of second order acoustic-aerosol effects was an advancement to the research field of acoustic-aerosol manipulation. These new capabilities extended the application range of acoustics from a previously proposed pre-conditioning agglomeration device to a standalone technology. Parametric studies were performed using the established system to develop an understanding of the conditions that influenced the system performance, quantified by the removal efficiency. Computational simulations were also conducted to complement the limitations in the experiments (Fu et al. 2015). Simulation and experimental results were compared to corroborate its accuracy. Parameters were categorized as input aerosol characteristics (Yuen et al. 2017) and acoustic field patterns (Yuen et al. 2016). It was found that removal efficiency was proportional to input aerosol particle number concentration, aerosol sizes and acoustic reside time. Polydispersed aerosols had particle-particle interactions beneficial for their removal. Acoustic streaming patterns were also found to affect the overall performance of the system. New underlying governing dimensionless parameters, near-wall vorticity magnitude and deposition cell ratios, were identified. It was found that geometrics of that provided high magnitudes of near-wall vorticity encouraged higher deposition rates by inertial impaction. Furthermore, particle initial positions were found to be a determining factor, and deposition cell ratios quantified such phenomenon. The higher the ratio, the larger the removal efficiency. Deposition was also more likely on the top half of the air duct where streaming and gravity-induced forces added in the same direction.

611013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
611013.value: The original proposed application in this project was to deal with indoor air quality. After the study, the acoustic aerosol removal system is expected to be applicable in a wide range of industries, due to its unique characteristic of non-invasiveness, for example, product recovery for pharmaceutical and food processing industries, and dried or liquid products to be recaptured from the air stream without destroying them. Thus the combination of polydisperse and poly-phase aerosols is an area to be explored. Another industrial need is related to emissions control in e.g. power stations, manufacturers and vehicle users. The systems should be tested with a high particle concentration, such as those at the exhaust of vehicles or manufacturing plants. This may also provide some design constraints, regarding the materials that may be used for high temperatures. Acoustic streaming was one of the key areas of focus in this project. It was found that the motion of submicron particles was highly related to the streaming pattern. Based on this useful fundamental knowledge obtained, further research efforts can be put into investigating the manipulation of submicron particles by acoustic effects. An UFP sorting/classifying device may be developed in this direction.

611013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
611013.value: Ultrafine particles (UFPs) are present in indoor environments, where occupants spend most of their time. Once inhaled, such particles can penetrate deeply into the lungs and pose an elevated health risk. The airborne virus, nanometer in size, is also one type of UFPs of great concern. They are responsible for the transmission of many infectious diseases, including influenza and SARS. The removal of ultrafine particles is difficult due to their very small size. Currently, high quality packed fibre filters are usually used in removing UFPs. This method is both energy and material expensive. On the other hand, particles suspended in air have been found to coagulate in a sound field. So, small particles will coagulate to form coarser particles using an ultrasonic device. By understanding this physics, a comprehensive model to predict the particle agglomeration rate and the resulting particle concentration was developed, and verified by a series of experiments in this project. The second-order airflow created by the sound field was studied and was found to be able to enhance the capturing of particles. Finally, a highly material- and energy- efficient particle removal technique based on enlarging and capturing particles using a sound field was developed.

611113.value: 用海水從尿液里回收磷的深度研究

611113.label: Project Objectives
611113.value: Develop a compact SUPR system for producing struvite from fresh urine continuously in a single reactor; Establish a mathematical model to optimize the reactor’s operation and design; Conduct a pilot scale trial of the SUPR system to further investigate its engineering feasibility and cost effectiveness.

Establish a mathematical model to optimize the reactor’s operation and design;
Conduct a pilot scale trial of the SUPR system to further investigate its engineering feasibility and cost effectiveness.

611113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
611113.value: Phosphorus (P) is essential to all living organisms. Unlike carbon, oxygen, hydrogen and nitrogen which can be obtained from air and water, the only available source of phosphorus is from mines. Although predictions vary, it is commonly estimated that 35-100% of the current P reserves will be depleted by 2100[1]. While the earth’s P reserves are rapidly diminishing, discharge of P into the environment causes algal blooms. P recovery from sewage relies upon enhanced biological P removal (EBPR) process with chemical precipitation. The EBPR process is not effective in warm climates like Hong Kong’s[2], while the chemical precipitation is costly. Sewage could be a reliable alternative P resource[3]. Urine comprises roughly 1% of sewage flow but accounts for 50 - 80% of the P load in sewage, equivalent to about 10% of mined P extraction. Therefore, source urine separation has thus been encouraged in recent years to enable possible urine P recovery (UPR)[4]. Direct reuse of urine as fertilizer is unwelcome due to concerns about endocrine disruptors and hygienic conditions[5]. Struvite formation has thus been proposed, but it involves dosing with costly alkaline magnesium chemicals[6]. Hong Kong is dominated by high-rise residential buildings supplied with seawater for toilet flushing since 1958. The high population density could provide for efficient collection of source-separated urine. The amount of magnesium in seawater is theoretically sufficient to precipitate 100 % of the P contained in urine economically. If suitable seawater-based UPR (SUPR) could be developed to recover more than 90% of the P in urine, it would benefit Hong Kong in terms of resource recovery and avoiding expansion of current biological treatment works to include EBPR in the future. The proposed study will aim at developing a system which includes 1) continuous-fresh urine flow treatment, 2) accelerated urea hydrolysis, and 3) integration of the urea hydrolysis, struvite formation and collection in a single reactor. Following an exploratory study confirming the SUPR concept, this project will focus on developing the SUPR system through following specific research tasks: 1) SUPR reactor development, 2) mathematical process modeling including urea hydrolysis kinetics, precipitation potential and precipitation kinetics, and 3) engineering feasibility and economic analysis. The system developed should not be limited to coastal cities but can also be applicable in any continental city when low-cost Mg-laden waste is available. In consideration of the ever increasing price of phosphate rock in the future, a SUPR system is worth developing.

611113.label: Realisation of objectives
611113.value: The mechanisms of phosphorus recovery from urine using SUPR reactor were extensively investigated with batch tests and mathematical model, which include chemical reaction principle exploration tests, the experimental study on the microbial effect on urine hydrolysis, and mathematical model considering both biological and chemical reactions in the SUPR system. This part of study fulfills the second objective. Based on the findings from mechanisms study, a lab-scale SUPR reactor was built up and run with different conditions for system optimization. Fresh urine and seawater were used as influent of the SUPR reactor. It was confirmed that more than 90% of phosphorus recovery from urine can be achieved in 6 hours of hydraulic retention time (HRT). This part of study realizes the first objective. Due to the odor control and urine source issue, it is very hard to realize pilot-scale SUPR reactor operation. Finally, the engineering feasibility and cost-effectiveness of the SUPR system were evaluated based on life cycle analysis (LCA) and life cycle cost (LCC) study based on the materials consumption for the lab-scale SUPR system. In addition, we also tried to use microbial fuel cell (MFC) to treat urine after phosphorus recovery to reduce the precipitation potential on the electrodes for more efficient energy and ammonia recovery. Nitrification of SUPR effluent was also investigated with good results. In summary, the objectives are well addressed.

611113.label: Major findings and research outcome
611113.value: Seawater, as an alternative source of magnesium, can be an effective precipitant for urine phosphorus (P) precipitation; The pH and ammonia concentration resulting from the ureolysis largely influence the magnesium ammonium phosphate (MAP) precipitation rate and thus the SUPR efficiency; 98% of the urine P can precipitate with seawater within 10 min when 40-75% of the urea in urine is ureolysed; In the precipitates, the P content was found to be more than 9% when the urine fraction was 40% or higher, and MAP was confirmed to be the predominant component, which can be directly applied as fertilizer in light of abundant nitrogen (N), P, magnesium (Mg), and calcium (Ca); Ureolysis extent of more than 40% and 80% were achieved in 1.5 h and 2.5 h with enriched bacteria in SUPR sludge, respectively, which makes in-situ ureolysis and phosphorus recovery feasible; SUPR reactor has a great potential to successfully recover more than 90% P in 6 h without the need for any other chemicals; The indigenous seawater bacteria played a more important role than urine bacteria in the SUPR process; The application of the urine-separation and P/N recovery/removal system requires less than 0.3% additional energy consumption and also contributes less than 1% additional environmental emissions when compared with conventional buildings; The maximum power density produced by batch model MFC and continuous flow MFC was 22.0 W/m3 and 14.2 W/m3 when the real SUPR effluent was used as the feeding solution.

611113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
611113.value: Odor control in the SUPR system during application should be carefully considered. SUPR effluent treatment with MFCs or a nitrification reactor also deserves research in the future. We conducted engineering feasibility and economic analysis only at the building level. The potential benefits to a larger system boundary, including reductions in the P & N nutrients, and organic loading on downstream wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) and subsequently the expected increase in WWTP effluent quality, are not yet considered and evaluated.

611113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
611113.value: Phosphorus can be largely recovered from urine in buildings with seawater toilet flushing by simply installing a precipitation reactor with negligible energy input. The recovered phosphorus can be directly used as a fertilizer. The application of this system can benefit cities with water and material savings. It can further reduce the energy consumption in wastewater treatment plants.

611213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
611213.value: The limited supply of fossil-fuel, the troublesome problem of nuclear waste, and the global warming linked to CO2 emission call for the rapid development of alternative/green energy, and the efficient usage of energy. Electricity generated from renewable sources offers great potential but its output is irregular although electricity is required at anytime in our daily live. These crucial energy supply issues humankind faces, along with the rapid advancement of the electric vehicles, have made it imperative to develop low cost, high capacity, long life rechargeable batteries. Lithium ion batteries have been regarded as the promising choice. Within a lithium-ion battery, the cost of the cathode material counts upto 70% of the total cost of battery materials. Moreover, the cathode mateiral is also the controlling factor determining the performace and capacity of a battery. This project explores the production of lithium ferrous phosphate particles (a promising cathode material) continuously using solution chemistry method. Specifically, hydrothermal/sovothermal and ionothermal methods that have been proven in batch mode will be examined in a plug flow continuous reactor with or without microwave heating. The effects of the precursor chemicals, the reaction temperature, reaction time, the mixing intensity, and the solvent or ionic liquid will be investigated in terms of the physical, chemical and electrochemical performances of the lithium ferrous phosphate obtained. The doping of the materials and carbon coating will also be studied by selecting proper chemicals so as to maximize the usage of the element and minimize the energy consumption during the production. The cost of ionic liquid, purity tolerance and efficient recovery process using a cyclone will also be examined. This is the chemical engineering apporach for a large scale production of the promising cathode material for lithium-ion battery for electric vehicles or energy storage. The success of this project will significantly reduce the cost of the cathode materials for lithium ion fabrication. It will also ensures the product quality by having proper process control. Thus, the batteries manufactured using this material will be more consistent leading to safer and more stable operation of large batteries. 化石燃料有限的供應，核廢料的處理和與CO2 排放相關聯的全球暖化等麻煩問題呼籲替代/綠色能源的快速發展和能源的有效利用。 可再生能源發電力具有很大的潛力。在我們的日常生活中雖然電力随时需要，但是再生電力的輸出并不規則。人類面临的這些重要能源供應問題，以及電動汽車的迅速發展，迫切需要開發低成本、 高容量、 長壽命可充電電池。鋰離子電池被視為有前途的選擇。就鋰離子電池來說，正極材料成本高達電池材料的總成本的 70%。此外，正極材料也是决定電池性能和容量的控制因素。 這一項目探討使用液態化學方法連續生產磷酸亞鐵鋰粒子 (一种有前途的正極材料) 。具體而言，它將在批次處理模式下已被驗證的水熱/溶劑熱和離子熱方法，在平推流連續反應器里進一步檢驗。同時審查微波加熱、化學前驅體、 反應溫度、 反應時間、 攪拌強度、 和溶劑或離子液體對磷酸鋰鐵的物理、 化學和電化學性能方面的影響。此外將通過選擇適當的化學品，攙雜或包覆磷酸亞鐵鋰粒子以便最大限度地实现元素利用，減少生產過程中的能耗。研究也包括離子液體價格、 純度要求和通過旋風分離器高效的回收利用。這是一種對這種對電動車及儲能領域具有前途的正極材料通過化學工程的方法進行大規模生產研究。 此項目的成功將大大減少鋰離子電池正極材料的製造成本。它還將通過適當的過程控制確保產品品質。因此，使用這種材料製造的電池將具有較好的一致性從而導致大電池更安全、 更穩定的運作。

611213.label: Realisation of objectives
611213.value: Most of the project objectives have been completed. Specifically, the experimental facility has been designed, fabricated and/or purchased with the microwave heating capability. Because the continuous process with MW heating took longer time than expected and required more funding than the figure originally anticipated, the facility is only ready in 2018. Thus, the experimental part of the synthesis and characterization were conducted with microwave heating in a microwave digester using hydrothermal/solvothermal methods. Specifically, LiFePO4 was synthesized using solvothermal method because hydrothermal would require too high temperature. The results show that 20 minutes MW heating is sufficient to achieve LiFePO4 nanoparticles with good crystallinity. With 4 hour annealing and addition of 5% carbon, the cathode prepared with the LiFePO4 presented excellent redox cycling ability with nearly 95% capacity retention after 1000 cycles under 1C current density. The Research Assistant is working on the synthesis of LiMnPO4 and LiFePO4 using ionothermal method. Also he'll conduct some experiments using the continuous flow facility to produce the cathode materials. The work will be completed in next 6 months and the publications will acknowledge RGC support.

611213.label: Major findings and research outcome
611213.value: The microwave-assisted solvothermal synthesize of LiFePO4 is investigated in the present study. Ethylene Glycol (EG) was selected as the solvent based on literature report. By varying the time scale of reaction from 5 min to 25 min, it was found that 20 min (LFP-20) has the highest cycling stability where around 85% of capacity was retained after 500 cycles and promising specific capacity of around 136 mAhg-1 under 1 C. The encouraging result is mainly due to the small particle size obtained and higher structural stability upon cycling. With proper carbon content added to LFP-20, 5 wt%, the capacity retention has increased to around 94% after 1000 cycles. It also showed excellent rate capability in which specific capacity of 142, 141.3, 139.4, 137.5, 134.8, 125.9, 112.7 mAh g-1 under the rate of 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5 and 10 C respectively. Physical, chemical and electrochemical characterization of the materials were carried out to explain the obtained results. Meanwhile, an in situ fluorination process on transition metal oxides is proposed to prepare Mn-based mixed-anion cathode materials for rechargeable Li/Na batteries. F-containing compounds, such as AF, APF6 (A = Li, Na), and fluorinated carbonate, are found to facilitate the in situ activation process by donating F- to MnO upon oxidation. A reversible capacity of 220 mAh g-1 can be obtained by activating MnO/C electrode in LiPF6-based electrolyte at room temperature at C/50 rate. The activated electrode shows decent rate capability, delivering 207, 192, and 173 mAh g-1 specific capacities at C/20, C/10, and C/5 rates, respectively. Advanced characterization techniques reveal that the reversibility is enabled by dynamic change of oxidation states and local environment of Mn. Overall, 0.8 e^- transfer per Mn is estimated in Li-ion cells based on surface- and bulk-sensitive techniques. While the practical aspect of the fluorinated electrodes prepared in an in situ way remains to be proven, this electrochemical synthesis process opens an interesting direction to design novel Li(Na)-based electrode materials showing transformational advances.

611213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
611213.value: The research assistant will continue work on this project at non-cost of RGC to complete the project objectives by using solvothermal method to synthesis LiMnPO4, ionothermal method for LiFePO4/LiMnPO4, and to produce the nanoparticles also using continuous process that is now available to the PI. Non-cost extension of this project was not applied at the end of December 2016 because the PI was in a transitional period moving from HKUST to HK PolyU. The microwave furnace was available in HKUST for the batch process. The continuous production of the nanoparticles has been designed in 2016, sent to potential engineering supplier for fabrication in May 2017. The system has now been tested by the company with all specifications met in October 2017. The tendering process has been completed in December 2017. The purchasing order has been issued to the company in January 2018. It is ready to be shipped to HK PolyU in Feb 2018.

611213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
611213.value: Lithium ion batteries are becoming very important in the energy storage and power supply for customer electronics and also large scale application such as house-hold energy storage, electric vehicles as well as the power control for the electricity grid. For the latter applications, the cheap, durable and safe batteries are desired. In this regard, lithium ferrous phosphate (LFP) has been considered good cathode material. The cost of modern lithium ion batteries is mainly from that of the cathode (>50%) material. The production condition or synthesis of lithium ferrous phosphate controls the quality and also cost of its manufacturing. Instead of using the conventionally batch process that takes more than 10 hours of reaction, the present investigation explores the possibility of synthesizing LFP with short reaction time so that it would be possible to produce it continuously which would yield products with more uniform quality. This synthesis was realized with microwave heating in 20 minutes in a properly selected organic solvent, ethylene glycol. The LFP obtained show very good crystal structure and excellent stability. Nearly 95% of initial energy capacity was found retained after 1000 cycles of charge-discharge when the cathode is made with so produced LFP and 5% carbon addition.

611513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
611513.value: According to the Green Building Council Australia, buildings consume 32% of the world’s resources, produce 40% of the waste being deposited into landfill sites, and contribute 40% of greenhouse gas emissions. Improving efficiency in consumption of energy, water and other resources in the built environment is undoubtedly considered to be one of the most sustainable and feasible measures for reducing human impacts to the environment, such as carbon emissions and energy expenditures. The built environment is moving towards sustainable development. The number of green buildings has increased worldwide in recent years. However, most of the green buildings nowadays are new construction projects which were designed as green buildings before they were built. Although the amount of existing buildings significantly outnumbers that of new buildings, study of the maintenance and renovation of existing buildings into green buildings is relatively scarce. The design and planning process for greening existing building often takes a long time and requires much human effort due to the “one-of-a-kind” nature of buildings. As the number of certified green existing buildings increases, it is beneficial to capture the knowledge gained from previous certification experience and reuse the knowledge for greening other buildings. This proposed project aims to develop a theoretical decision support framework for transforming existing buildings into green buildings. The framework development will be performed in a retrospective manner using data mining and case-based reasoning techniques. A knowledge base will be built based on the project information and certification credits information of around 1500 certified existing buildings available in the U.S. LEED (Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design) project directory. The knowledge base will also contain information about the technologies and strategies performed in those buildings, which will be collected from literature in the public domain. Association rules analysis and decision trees classification will be conducted on the knowledge base to discover the relationships among attributes such as building types, building locations, awarded certification levels, and the green technologies and strategies used. The knowledge base will then be converted into a case base to develop a case-based reasoning framework. The developed decision support frameworks will be validated by a series of case studies on several LEED certified green existing buildings. The case studies will also be used to evaluate the effectiveness of various green existing building technologies and strategies. Finally, the frameworks will be revised based on the case study results. 根據澳大利亞綠色建築委員會，建築物消耗32% 的世界資源，生產40% 被存放到垃圾堆填區的廢物，並貢獻40% 的溫室氣體排放量，故此，提高建築環境對能源、水和其他資源的消耗效率，無疑是其中一個最可持續和可行的措施以減低人類對環境（如碳排放和能源）的影響。建築環境正邁向可持續發展的方向，綠色建築的數量在近幾年於全世界不斷增加；然而，現在的綠色建築大多都是被設計成綠色建築才建的新建設項目，雖然現有建築物量明顯多於新的建築物量，對改造及營運現有建築物以達致綠色建築的研究相對較少。由於每個建築物都有獨特的本質，綠化現有建築物的設計和規劃過程往往需要很長的時間，並且需要很多人力物力；由於獲得綠色認證的現有建築物正在增加，現在我們可以捕捉以往的綠色認證經驗，並重用該些知識以綠化更多之現有建築物。這個項目旨在開發一個決策支援的理論框架，以改造現有建築到綠色建築，該框架的發展將採用數據挖掘和基於案例的推理技術，以追溯性的模式進行。基於約1500個已獲美國LEED 綠色認證之現有建築物項目，我們將建成一個項目及綠色認證分項的資訊知識庫，該知識庫也將包含在這些建築物進行的綠色技術和戰略。根據該知識庫，運用關聯規則分析和決策樹分類的技術，把建築類型、建築物地點、使用之綠色技術和綠色認證級別等屬性之間的關係發現，同時，我們建成的知識庫亦將被轉換成案例庫，以開發一個基於案例推理的框架。通過一系列的案例研究，本項目所開發之決策支援理論框架將被驗證，而這些案例研究亦會被用於評估各種綠色建築技術和策略之有效性，最後，本項目所開發之決策支援框架將於案例研究的基礎上作修訂。

611513.label: Realisation of objectives
611513.value: All the project objectives have been achieved. As for Objective 1, green building standards for existing buildings and some certified green buildings have been studied using machine learning techniques such as rule-based association rules and decision trees. Specifically, the LEED credits were studied using association rules. A measurement called the percentage of average score (PAS) was proposed to analyze how individual credits were attained in the past. As for Objective 2, a non-linear case based reasoning approach based on artificial neural network (ANN) was developed to suggest a list of target credits for new LEED projects based on similar certified cases. 1000 LEED certified cases were collected for the case base. As for Objective 3, the case based reasoning framework developed in Objective 2 has been tested and evaluated using 20 recently certified projects. The result showed a prediction accuracy of 80.75% on the LEED credit selection. The result was also compared with those calculated by commonly used linear CBR approaches: Multiple Regression Analysis, Correlation Analysis, and the k-NN approach. The accuracy calculated by these methods were between 71.23% - 77.54%, which were lower than the proposed approach. As for Objective 4, based on the rules identified in Objective 1 and the the case based reasoning framework developed in Objective 2, a web tool has been developed to help design the LEED credits for a new green building project, either of existing building or new construction.

611513.label: Major findings and research outcome
611513.value: (1) The LEED NC credits were studied using association rules. LEED credits like MRc6 (Rapidly Renewable Materials) and MRc3 (Materials Reuse) were found very rare and difficult to achieve, whereas credits like EAc1 (Optimize Energy Performance) and EAc2 (On-Site Renewable Energy) demand lots of additional effort or cost for higher points. 50 strong USGBC rules were identified and 13 new pairs of related LEED credits were developed. (2) An ANN based non-linear case based reasoning approach was developed to suggest a list of target credits for new LEED projects based on similar certified cases. The prediction accuracy of LEED credit selection was 80.75%, which was higher than other approaches. (3) The relationship between climate factors and LEED credits was studied using data mining techniques. The results showed that the achievement of some credits such as SSc4 (Alternative Commuting Transportation) and SSc7.1 (Heat Island Reduction – Non-roof) are highly related to climate factors especially the diurnal temperature range. The achievement of other credits like SSc6 (Stormwater Quantity Control), WEc3 (Water Efficient Landscaping), SSc2 (Building Exterior and Hardscape Management Plan), SSc7.2 (Heat Island Effect – Roof) and IEQc2.3 (Occupant Comfort – Thermal Comfort Monitoring) also revealed direct relationship with climate factors. (4) The numerical patterns behind the leading counties in the U.S. local green building markets and the implications of the patterns on China were studied. 39 important local green building markets in the U.S. were identified using DBSCAN algorithm. Results showed that economic features like the total personal income in the real estate market, and educational features like the number of college students can be important features for the identification of potential leading markets for green buildings. The identified optimal patterns were also implemented in the biggest developing country, China, and 20 potential leading prefecture-level cities in Chinese green building markets were suggested as the focus of development. (5) Non-linear machine learning algorithm, namely Random Forests, was used to analyze the influential features of the regional average site EUI of multi-family residential building in NYC. The AEUI of 1,322 BGs were prepared based on 3,608 multi-family residential buildings in NYC. 171 influential features describing the buildings, economy, education, environment, households, surrounding, and transportation were collected to model the AEUI. The results showed that features like the percentage of higher educated people, percentage of households heated by fuel oil, and median household income, significantly affect the regression model.

611513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
611513.value: Most findings have been published in top journals. This research has mainly focused on LEED, which is the green building standard in USA. In the future, green buildings standards in another regions like UK can be studied using similar developed methodology.

611513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
611513.value: Buildings consume 32% of the world’s resources, and contribute 40% of greenhouse gas emissions. Improving efficiency in the consumption of energy, water and other resources in the built environment is undoubtedly an important global problem. This research has studied the achievement of green building standard (LEED) credits from a large number of certified green building projects, using data mining techniques. Hidden knowledge was discovered from previous certified projects from both the bottom-up (individual project management) and top-down (city planning) perspectives. The bottom-up perspective includes analysis of LEED credit achievements in previous green building projects and development of methodology for retrieving the past case studies of similar projects, thereby facilitating the design of future green building projects. The top-down perspective includes investigation on the potential influence of climate factors on the achievement of LEED credits, discovery of the city factors that would affect the development of LEED markets, and study on the influence of demographic features and social features on the regional building energy performance on an urban scale, thereby helping designers and planners understand how to promote green building development on a regional scale. The research results will help green building design and development from both micro and macro perspectives.

611613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
611613.value: Advances in wireless communications had led to the proliferation of wireless portable devices. Currently, mobile phone penetration rate is close to 100% and most PDAs have wireless connectivity. Eventually, digital cameras, camcorders, and other portable electronic devices will have wireless communication capability. Interference among wireless devices is the major hurdle limiting further improvement in capacity and performance of future networks. One approach to address this problem is to use multiple relay stations to route signal transmitted over short range in multiple hops to reduce the total interference in the network. The other approach is to use multi-user coding strategy obtained from information theoretic study of interference channel models. Both approaches have their advantage and drawbacks. In the proposed research, we will incorporate the use of relays in interference channel and investigate several channel models which collectively better mimic the wireless multi-cell environment with relay stations. Information theoretical analysis will be performed on these channels and insights on how relay can help in practical wireless multi-cell environment will be obtained. As a result, better wireless system protocol can be design to take advantage of the interference generated by other users instead of being corrupted by the interference. 隨著無線通信領域的發展，無線便攜式設備的數目也在大幅度增加。目前，手機的普及率已經接近100%，而大多數掌上電腦(PDA)也都有無線連接功能。最終，數碼相機、攝像機和其他便攜式電子設備都會擁有無線通信能力。無線設備間的干擾是制約未來網絡容量和性能發展的主要障礙。解決這個問題的一種方法是使用多個中繼站來路由短距多跳信號，從而減少網絡中的干擾。另一種方法是使用多用戶編碼策略，該策略來源於對干擾信道模型的信息理論研究。兩種方法各有優缺點。在我們提出的研究中，我們將結合干擾信道中對中繼的使用，探索幾種能更好地模擬無線多小區中繼環境的信道模型。並且我們會對這些信道進行信息理論分析，從而獲得對實際無線多小區環境中中繼作用的深刻理解。這樣就可以利用用戶間干擾設計出更好的無線系統協議，而不是因為干擾產生通信差錯。

611613.label: Realisation of objectives
611613.value: The objectives of this project are all realised and results are published in multiple publications or being under reviewed. When we worked on objective 1 in formulating the framework of the various channel models with relay, we looked ahead to objective 3 to ensure that the framework can be incorporated in the wireless cellular network with multiple cell and relays. In this context, we identified that the framework should include wireless power relays in particular in Internet Of Things (IOTs) environment supported by wireless network. Also, to channel state information (CSI) will be increasingly difficult to be obtained and, even when obtained, may be outdated. Hence, interference channels with outdated CSI should also need to be formulated to capture the characteristics in wireless cellular network with relays. Finally, after the proposal had been submitted, there has been significant interests in taking advantage of caching content in relay or intermediate node to lessen the traffic on the infrastructure. Hence, in order for the results to be relevant to the wireless network, we formulate the channel models with cache aided relay as well. Hence, the model formulated in objective 1 include those with wireless powered relay, delayed CSI, or cache aided relay. Using the channel models derived in objective 1 in objective 2 to obtain bounds on both degree of freedom (DoF), we have generated results in capacity region and in achievable DoF. Clearly, we cannot be exhaustive in deriving all the possible combinations, but we have obtained results for the DoF of interference channel with relay, the throughput for wireless powered two-way relay channels under different relay strategies, and DoF of MIMO relay interference channel with outdated CSI. As for objectives 3, it is very challenging to apply direct information theoretic results to wireless cellular network with relays directly as these systems are highly complex. Hence, theoretical analysis using information theoretic models should provide insights and guidelines for design instead. In this context, we derived channel model that has captured the essence of the wireless network characteristics and hence the results can be used to guide wireless network design. Hence, we achieve objective 3 in this way. In particularly, we incorporate the 3 new key characteristics of wireless network in the modelling and hence results in objective 2 can be used to guide wireless cellular network design. In this sense, we have achieved objective 3 indirectly.

611613.label: Major findings and research outcome
611613.value: We have identified 3 major characteristics in the wireless network for modelling into interference channel with relay and two-two relay channels. Scheduling and power allocation for a wireless powered two-way relayed channel were studied and optimal schemes were derived that are shown to be effective. Wireless powered relay applied to MAC with different relay strategies were studied for a MAC channel using capacity region as the performance metric. Optimal schemes for scheduling and power allocations were also derived for these channel models. In studying the MIMO (Multi-Input Multi-Output) Relay Channels with outdated Channel State Information (CSI), we found that with the help fo a relay with enough antennas, the requirement for instantaneous CSI can be relaxed to the delayed CSI without sacrificing the achievable Degree of Freedom (DoF) of such channels. Moreover, we also find that the presence of relay with delayed global CSI can boost the DoF performance even when there is no CSI at the transmitters. Finally, we investigated the tradeoffs between storage and latency for a K-user cache-aided relay interference channel with a K-antenna relay when CSI is not available at the transmitter. We derived bounds on the normalised delivery time (NDT), a metric indicating the efficiency of the network.

611613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
611613.value: Further development can be done by combining these features of the networks and consider their overall effect. This research considered wireless powered relay, outdated CSI and caching aided relay separately and how they can be incorporated into interference channels and two-way relay channels. Future research can focus on combining these feature and analyse their overall effect and how to optimise such systems.

611613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
611613.value: This project has considered several newly emerged ideas and study how they can be incorporated into future wireless communication networks to increase their efficiency. These ideas include using relay that is wirelessly powered, using storage buffer in relay to reduce duplicated transmission, and lessen the overhead needed in the wireless system to monitor the real-time channel conditions for optimal performance. These ideas are considered in the context of some channel model mimicking wireless communication systems to obtain insights and guidelines in future communications system design.

611813.label: Realisation of objectives
611813.value: Smartphone applications’ energy efficiency is vital, but many Android applications suffer from serious energy inefficiency. Locating these energy problems is labor-intensive and automated diagnosis is thus desirable. This motivates us to tabulate common energy inefficiency issues and developed a framework to analyze energy inefficiency of Android apps in this project. To achieve the first objective, we collected 608 candidates from Google Play Store [17] using a web crawler. These applications have release logs containing at least one of the following keywords: battery, energy, efficiency, consumption, power, and drain. We then performed manual examination to ensure that these applications indeed were infected with energy problems and developers have fixed these problems in the applications’ latest versions (note that we did not have access to their earlier versions containing energy problems). To find interesting open-source subjects, we first randomly selected 250 candidates GitHub and SourceForge. Since we are interested in applications with a certain level of development maturity, we refined our selection by retaining those applications that: (1) have at least 1,000 downloads, (2) have a public bug tracking system, and (3) have multiple versions. We studied our collected subjects’ real bug reports, commit logs, bug-fixing patches and release logs concerning energy problems occurring to open-source and commercial Android apps. Major causes leading to energy inefficiencies were identified. With these findings, we carried out studies for the second objective and developed a framework to automatically diagnosing such energy inefficiencies. A key challenge in diagnosing energy inefficiencies at mobile applications is that the absence of a decidable criterion that facilitates effective assessment on the occurrences of such inefficiencies. We developed a technique to address this challenge. Our approach explores an application’s state space by systematically executing the application using Java PathFinder (JPF). It monitors sensor and wake lock operations to detect missing deactivation of sensors and wake locks. It also tracks the transformation and usage of sensory data and judges whether they are effectively used by the application using our state-sensitive data utilization metric. By doing so, we can generate detailed reports with actionable in-formation to assist developers in validating detected energy inefficiencies. Another key challenge is that Android applications are event-driven and highly hinge on user interactions. Their program code comprises many loosely coupled event handlers, among which no explicit control flow is specified. At runtime, these event handlers are called by the An-droid framework, which builds on hundreds of native library classes. Automated diagnosis requires: (1) generation of valid user interaction events, and (2) correct scheduling of event handlers. To address this challenge, we developed technique to analyze an Android application’s GUI layout configuration files, and systematically enumerate all possible user interaction event sequences with a bounded length at runtime. We showed that such a bounded length does not impair the effectiveness of our analysis, but instead helps quickly explore different application states and identify energy problems. We developed an application execution model derived from Android specifications. This model captures application-generic temporal rules that specify calling relationships between event handlers. With this model, we are able to ensure an Android application to be exercised with correct control flows, rather than being randomly scheduled on its event handlers. To achieve the third objective, a tool called GreenDroid was built on top of Java PathFinder (JPF), a model checker for Java programs. All three proposed project objectives were successfully completed with a set of evaluation datasets and tools implementing the proposed framework made available to the public at: - GreenDroid: The major framework that automatically detects energy inefficiencies at Android apps. The tool and evaluation dataset are available at http://sccpu2.cse.ust.hk/greendroid/. - Elite: A framework component that supplements GreenDroid to automatically detect and locate wakelocks that induce both functional and non-functional issues in Android apps. The tool and its evaluation dataset are available at http://sccpu2.cse.ust.hk/elite/toc.html.

611813.label: Major findings and research outcome
611813.value: The findings of this project were disseminated at five reputable journal articles (2xTSE, IEEE Software, IJSI, SCIS) and seven reputable conference publications (2xICSE, 2xASE, POPL, FSE and ISSTA). Two PhD students were trained. Our publication at ASE 2016 was were highly recognized by the software engineering community and received the ACM SIGSOFT Distinguished Paper award. We summarize selected findings as follows. - Although root causes of energy problems can vary with different applications, majority of them (over 60%) are closely related to two types of coding phenomena. The first phenomenon arises from missing sensor or wake lock deactivation. To use a smartphone sensor, an application needs to register a listener with the Android OS. The listener should be unregistered when the concerned sensor is no longer needed. Similarly, an application needs to acquire a wake lock from the Android OS. The acquired wake lock should be released as soon as the computation completes. The second phenomenon arises from sensory data underutilization. Smartphone sensors probe their environments and collect sensory data. These data are obtained at the cost of battery energy and therefore should be well utilized by applications. Poor sensory data utilization could result in energy waste. - Energy problems are serious. They have covered many types of Android applications and affected potentially millions of users. - It is relatively more difficult to diagnose and fix energy problems, as compared to non-energy bugs; user interaction con-texts and debugging logs can help problem diagnosis, but they require additional reporting efforts, which may not be desirable. - Two common patterns of energy inefficiencies can be identified: missing sensor or wake lock deactivation and sensory data underutilization. - Many energy-efficient mobile apps are written to adjust their behavior dynamically in response to changes in their runtime contexts (e.g., environmental conditions). We found that certain some context changes can result in unstable inconsistency detection of these changes. Such unstable detection can be effectively suppressed by pre-defined change patterns. - Over 27.2% of Android apps utilizes wake locks to protect critical computation. Computational tasks protected by wake locks are often run asynchronously and could be long running, and can bring users observable or perceptible benefits. - Eight patterns are found to commonly accountable for wake lock misuses: unnecessary wakeup, wake lock leakage, premature lock releasing, multiple lock acquisitions, inappropriate lock type, erroneous timeout setting, inappropriate flags, and permission errors.

611813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
611813.value: We hope that in future more efforts from research communities and industries can be devoted to designing useful techniques to help developers combat energy and performance bugs in their smartphone applications. We believe that energy and performance diagnosis is becoming increasingly important as mobile applications continually integrate themselves into people’s daily lives. Our findings lead to the following future work. - Extend energy inefficiency diagnosis to other non-functional issues in mobile applications. - Extend energy inefficiency diagnosis to hybrid mobile applications such as those running on top of an Android Webview component. - Automatically locate the root cause of a detected energy inefficiency and repair it accordingly. - Further enrich our current dataset with new issues found in mobile apps launched over emerging Android OS. - Extend the framework to conduct diagnosis for new Android OS. - Adapt the framework to iOS applications.

611813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
611813.value: The mobile app market is expanding rapidly. Many mobile applications are realized in an energy-inefficient or performance-ill way, seriously affecting user experience. There are a lack of powerful tools to combat energy inefficiency problems. In this project, we developed an effective framework for automated energy inefficiency diagnosis in mobile applications. We studied the characteristics of these bugs and developed automated techniques to address three major challenges: (a) how to trigger an energy bug, how to judge the occurrence of energy inefficiency, and how to determine the amount of diagnosis. We released our framework and experimental datasets to the public, and disseminate our research results in reputed research venues. Our results were well received and award-winning. Two PhD students were trained.

612113.label: Project Objectives
612113.value: To develop facile and scalable approaches to fabricate various photon management nanostructures, including nanocones, nanowell, nanospheres, nanopillars, etc. Instead of using conventional top down approaches, the self-assembly and self-organized approaches, including Langmuir Blodgett self-assembly, electrochemical etching and anodization, etc. will be explored. Meanwhile, these approaches will be combined with scalable nanoimprint, in order to achieve controllability on nanostructure ordering and periodicity. To achieve a systematic understanding on the photon management mechanism and properties of the aforementioned nanostructures. In our preliminary studies we have discovered that the photon management mechanism varies largely from structure to structure. These mechanisms include waveguide confinement, cavity confinement, light diffraction, etc., or a combination of them. In addition, the specific mechanism is also material dependent. To establish design guidelines for efficient photon harvesting structure. For photonic and optoelectronic devices, following proper design guidelines in the fabrication process can lead to favorable device performance. Based on the solid understanding of photon management mechanisms in nanophotonic structures, a set of guidelines for designing effective photonic and optoelectronic devices, particularly photovoltaic devices in this project, will be established. To implement efficient photovoltaic devices with photon management nanostructures. Demonstrating efficient solar cells based on the aforementioned nanophotonic structures is one of the key missions of the project. The design guidelines will be followed, verified and further improved with device characterization.

612113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
612113.value: Though solar energy is abundant and clean, the primary hurdles for large scale application of solar cells and modules include their low energy conversion efficiency and relatively high cost as compared to other conventional techniques for electricity generation. Reducing material usage for solar cells, e.g. fabricating ultra-thin film solar cells, can not only lead to cost reductions, but also favors photo-carrier collection. However, it also results in light absorption loss in many cases. Therefore, it is crucial to maximize material light harvesting with limited thickness. In this regard, we propose to systematically investigate nanostructures with photon management capability and explore their applications for efficient solar cells. In particular, an assortment of nanostructures, including nanocones, nanopillars, nanospheres, nanowells, etc., will be designed and fabricated with scalable self-organized methods. Their optical properties will be characterized with assistance of simulations tools. Through experiments and modeling, the promising photon management nanostructures will be identified. Furthermore, these structures will be utilized to fabricate three-dimensional thin film solar cells with significant performance improvement. These systematic studies will not only help to promote more in-depth understanding of interactions between photons and engineered nanostructures, but also shed light on rational design of novel structured solar cells as well as other optoelectronic devices. 太陽能是取之不盡和潔淨的能源，但對 於大規模的太陽能電池和模塊的應用, 主要障礙還有低能量轉換效率和比其他發電技術相對高的成本。利用超薄膜太陽能電池從而減少電池材料使用不單 能降低成本，也有利於光生載流子的收集。然而，使用超薄材料也導致在許多情況下，減低光的吸收。因此，盡量提高電池的吸光性能是至關重要。有鑒於此，我們系統地研究了納米結構對光子的操控能力，並探索其高效的太陽能電 池應用。特別地，我們設計和製造各種可大規模製造的納米結構，包括納米錐，納米柱，納米球，納米井等。我們同時亦透過電腦模擬的輔助檢測 其光學性能。通過實驗和電腦模擬，我們找出能優化光子操控的納米材料。此外，這些結構亦用來製造高性能的三維薄膜太陽能電池。這些有系統 的研究，不單能促進對光子與納米結構之間的相互作用的理解，亦有利於設計新穎結構的太陽能電池以及其他光電器件。

612113.label: Realisation of objectives
612113.value: The objectives have been accomplished. We have developed several facile and scalable approaches to fabricate various photon management nanostructures. One approach is roll-to-roll nanoimprint in conjunction with solution based anodization and etching. With this approach we have achieved nanostructures including nanopillars, nanospike, nanoconcaves, etc. We have performed systematic studies on photon management properties of these nanostructures and investigated the impact of their geometrical factors, such as height, pitch, aspect ratio, on their photon management behavior. With the understanding obtained, we are able to set up design guidelines for efficient photon management structures. Namely, how to choose structure height, pitch, and aspect ratio, in order to achieve efficient light absorption. In addition, we have successful fabricated solar cell devices on these nanostructures and the characterization results showed that with the assistance of photon management structures, device energy conversion efficiency can be improved significantly. All these results have been published on the top journals in the field.

612113.label: Major findings and research outcome
612113.value: Our major findings can be summarized as: 1. Nanoimprint can be performed on soft metal substrate with a roll-to-roll fashion. Followed by anodization in acidic electrolyte and wet etching, various kinds of nanostructures can be formed. The periodicity of nanostructures can be controlled by nanoimprint mold design, as well as anodization voltages. And the aspect ratio of the nanostructures is determined by andozation time and etching time. This is a new process to fabrication highly regular nanostructures with low cost and in large scale. 2. We have confirmed that light management capability of nanostructures not only depends on the aspect ratio of nanostructures, but also periodicity. When the periodicity is comparable to optical wavelength, the nanostructures are most efficient for light management. 3. In order to make solar cell device work efficiently, carrier collection is equally important as light management. However, for thin film solar cells on nanostructures, there is a trade off between carrier collection is equally important and light management. More light management capability normally requires higher aspect ratio nanostructures, however thin films deposited on high aspect ratio nanostructures are less uniform thus hurting carrier collection. Therefore, there is an optimal nanostructure aspect ratio to balance carrier collection and light absorption. In our work, we found aspect ratio (nanostructure height/pitch) ~0.5 can lead to the optimal device performance. 4. Beside optical property enhancement, we discovered that nanostructured substrates have better adhesion to thin film solar cell materials on top, as compared to planar substrates, due to more surface contact area. And the nanostructures can help to release stress/strain in active materials when flexible solar cells are made. This suggests that nanostructured flexible solar cells have better bendability than planar solar cells. 5. We also found that light management nanostructures can be used for solar water splitting devices as well. Solar water splitting devices are also for solar energy harvesting. It convert solar energy to hydrogen fuel instead of electricity. And nanostructures with light management capability can also improve device performance.

612113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
612113.value: This project open up possibilities for future research on these directions: 1. Combining light management structures with emerging photovoltaic materials, including organic materials for organic solar cells, and organic-inorganic hybrid perovskite materials. Particularly, perovskite material based solar cells are being developed in a fast pace recently. The energy conversion efficiency has been improved to a high level. Utilization of light management structure may potentially contribute to more performance enhancement. 2. It is worth noting that the knowledge gained in this project can benefit not only photovoltaic and solar water splitting devices, but also other optoelectronic devices including light-emitting diode (LED) and photodetectors. Therefore research on these devices can also be performed in the future, combining with the rational design of nanostructures as light management substrates.

612113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
612113.value: In this project, we have developed roll-to-roll process to fabricate nanostructure arrays with light management capability. These nanostructures have been used as templates to accommodate photovoltaic materials. We have discovered that light absorption and solar cell performance can be largely improved by using these nanostructures, subject to nanostructure design optimization. The knowledge we learned from this project can benefit not only solar devices, but also other optoelectronic devices including light-emitting diode (LED) and photodetectors in the future.
