612713.label: Project Title(Chinese)
612713.value: 快速瞬变流下的供水系统泄漏研究

612713.label: Project Objectives
612713.value: To understand the interactions between a transient wave and the flow field in the vicinity of a single leak in a pipe in order to identify the missing physics in existing quasi-steady leak relations. To study the interactions between a wave and two leaks in a pipe for different longitudinal distances between the leaks and determine the length scale below the leak-leak interaction is strong and could in practice lead one to erroneously confuse multiple leaks with a single leak.
rows: To understand the interactions between a transient wave and the flow field in the vicinity of a single leak in a pipe in order to identify the missing physics in existing quasi-steady leak relations.

To study the interactions between a wave and two leaks in a pipe for different longitudinal distances between the leaks and determine the length scale below the leak-leak interaction is strong and could in practice lead one to erroneously confuse multiple leaks with a single leak.

612713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
612713.value: Leakage in water supply pipelines is a common, costly and serious water, energy and health issue. Estimates made in 2002 in Hong Kong suggest that water loss in the supply system is 30% of the total consumption. Worldwide, the losses range from about 15 to 50%. Recently transients-based leak detection methods have been utilized in pressurized pipelines for their ability to acquire and transmit a significant range and variety of system information along the pipeline at about 1000m/s. These methods are noted for being inexpensive, efficient, and accurate for pipe leak detection, but their accuracy hinges on our ability to understand and model the wave-leak interaction. Currently such interaction is assumed to display behavior identical to steady state and do not consider the effect of the flow structures, geometry, and frequency dependency of the leak. The objectives of the proposed research are: (1) to understand the interactions between a transient wave and the flow field in the vicinity of a single leak in a pipe in order to identify the missing physics in existing quasi-steady leak relations and, thus, derive new and thermodynamically consistent head-discharge leak relation which includes the relevant flow physics, (2) to incorporate and test the newly developed head-discharge equation into an existing 1D waterhammer models, and (3) to study the interactions between a wave and two leaks in a pipe for different longitudinal distances between the leaks and determine the length scale below which the leak-leak interaction is strong and could in practice lead one to erroneously confuse multiple leaks with a single leak. Theoretical, numerical and experimental methods will be used for to achieve the objectives of the proposed research. The numerical investigation will be carried out by a three-dimensional compressible model in which the turbulence is represented by a Large Eddy Simulation model. This model is being developed as part of another research project conducted by the PI. The experimental tests for this research are carried out on the fluid transient testing facilities at the University of Canterbury, New Zealand. This facility allows for the insertion of transparent pipe sections for flow visualization and is equipped with high resolution measurement capabilities. The understanding and data gained from numerical and laboratory experiments will be coupled with the theory of extended irreversible thermodynamics (EIT) to derive a new and physically based head-discharge leak relation which will then be incorporated into an existing one-dimensional waterhammer model. 供水管道系统泄漏是一个常见的、 昂贵的和严重的水、 能源和健康问题。2002 年在香港所作的估计表明在供水系统的水泄漏损失占总消费量的 30%。在全世界，损失范围从大约 15%到 50%。最近基于瞬变的泄漏检测方法在压力管道系统中得到应用。这种方法的应用原理主要是基于瞬变流在压力管道中以大约 1000 m/s速度传播因而能够获取和传输大量的范围和类型的系统信息。这些方法被认为是廉价、 高效和准确的管道泄漏检测方法，但它们的准确性将取决于我们对水压波与泄漏的交互作用的理解和模拟能力。目前这种相互作用被假定是与稳定流完全相同的行为状态而不考虑流动结构、 系统和泄漏形状与频率等依赖项的影响。 本研究的目标是： (1) 了解瞬态波和管道里单个泄漏的相互作用，以确定现有的准稳态泄漏关系中缺少物理理解和方法。因此，可以推导出新的和热力学上一致的水头与流量的泄漏关系，其中包括相关的流体物理知识点；(2) 采用和试验新开发的水头流量关系方程，并将包含于现有的一维水击模型中；及 (3) 研究管道中波和不同的纵向距离之间的两个泄漏的相互作用，以确定在何种长度规模以下多个泄漏相互作用将是增强，并纠正在实践中将多个泄漏误认为单处泄漏的错误。理论、 数值模拟和实验方法将用于实现本研究的目标。本研究的数值模拟部分将采用三维大涡模拟模型以模拟管道中的湍流。类似模型的开发也是本首席研究员（PI） 的另一个研究项目的一部分。实验室实验部分将在新西兰坎特伯雷大学的流体瞬态测试设施上进行。这个实验设施的特点主要包括允许插入透明管部分为流动可视化，并配有高分辨率测量能力的设备。数值模拟和实验室实验所得的理解和数据并结合扩展不可逆热力学理论来推导出新的基于物理的水压流量关系，然后将这一结果合并到现有一维水击模型中。

612713.label: Realisation of objectives
612713.value: The objectives were fully realized. The interactions between a transient wave and defects have been investigated in detail (Journals: 3,4,5, 6, 7 and 8 & Conferences: 4 and 6). Using the principle of action invariance we showed that wmEm is conversed for small defects implying ∆wm / wm = ∆Em / Em , where wm and Em are the eigenfrequency and total energy of the mth mode and ∆wm and ∆Em its eigenfrequency and energy shift. The change in energy is shown to be equal to the work of the radiation pressure during the formation of the blockage. In addition, it is found that small defects reduce the potential energy, but increase the kinetic energy of all modes. For severe defects, the pipe system is decoupled into two independent subsystems. This has also for the first time revealed that Bragg resonance plays a key role in wave-defect interaction. It is shown that, if a leak is located at a maximum pressure node of a given harmonic, this mode experiences Bragg-type resonance of maximum reflection and the corresponding peak amplitude in the frequency response function (FRF) is minimum. On the other hand, if a leak is located at a zero pressure node of a given harmonic, the corresponding mode experiences Bragg-type resonance of maximum transmission and the peak amplitude in the FRF is maximum. In this latter case, the leak has no influence on the harmonic and the pipe system is equivalent to an intact system. It is shown that the pattern induced by a leak on the FRF, used in many leak detection schemes, is due to the leak interaction with the harmonics with different amplitudes. In fact, the closer the leak location to a pressure node, the higher the amplitude of the corresponding peak, and vice versa for leaks closer to stagnation points. A number of leak detection methods are discussed in light of the Bragg resonance mechanism. The friction effect is discussed and it is explained that it does not influence the leak-wave interaction mechanism explained by Bragg resonance. These insights are exploited for several distinguished leak detection methods. The trajectory of normal modes in the complex plane as a function of leak size is studied (Journal 11). The relationship of variation between normal modes and frequency response is discussed. The key parameter that represents the leak size and controls the trajectory of the normal modes is the ratio of the pipe impedance to the leak impedance. It is found that, as the impedance ratio increases from zero (i.e., no leak), each normal mode shifts towards the upper half complex plane of frequency by a leak, where the imaginary part stands for the leak induced damping of the wave. When the impedance ratio is less than the order of one, the leak induced normal mode frequency shift is negligible which supports the theory put forward by proponents of the no shift and no additional peak hypothesis. When the impedance ratio is of order one or larger, not only is the shift of FRF’s peak significant, but also new peaks appear, which supports the theory raised by proponents of the leak-induced additional peaks hypothesis. Moreover, as the impedance ratio tends to infinity, the leak behaves as a reservoir where the pipe is fully open to the atmosphere. The analysis performed in this research provides insights into the signature of a leak on normal modes and resolves a long standing controversy in the literature. Numerical schemes for one, two and three dimensional waves (Journal 1, 2, 9 and 10) have been formulated and applied. These schemes are efficient and of high order accuracy, allowing for rapid yet accurate investigation of leak-defect interaction. For the case of multiple leaks, we proved that all leaks can be identified provided that the distance between them is of the same order or larger than the shortest probing wavelength (Journal 11). For cases where the shortest probing wavelength is large compared to the distance between the leaks, separation of individual leaks in the pipe is not possible.

612713.label: Major findings and research outcome
612713.value: The major findings are as follows. First, we showed for the first time that the principle of action invariance is instrumental in studying wave-defect interaction and derived a simple, yet, compact expression that governs the this interaction (Journals: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 & Conferences: 4 and 6). In addition, we proved that the interaction between waves and defects in a pipeline obey the Bragg resonance criteria (Journals: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 & Conferences: 4 and 6). Moreover, the trajectory of normal modes in the complex plane as a function of leak size is studied (Journal 11). Numerical schemes for one, two and three dimensional waves (Journal 1, 2, 9 and 10) have been formulated and applied. For the case of multiple leaks, we proved that all leaks can be identified provided that the distance between them is of the same order or larger than the shortest probing wavelength (Journal 11). For cases where the shortest probing wavelength is large compared to the distance between the leaks, separation of individual leaks in the pipe is not possible.

612713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
612713.value: The successful completion of this project and the insights gained allowed the PI to write a GRF proposal (submitted in October 2017) aiming at understanding the interaction between a defect and three- dimensional (radial mode) probing waves in a pipe system. The results of the proposed work are expected to (i) provide insights that explain the unexpected significant shift that occurs when the Helmholtz number is of order one and (ii) lead to derivation of a leak-impedance relation valid for three-dimensional wave conditions. This objective will be accomplished using in-depth physical and mathematical analysis informed and confirmed by laboratory and field experiments. The proposed theoretical investigation comprises (i) the derivation of an analytical solution for the pressure and velocity fields with and without a leak, where an impedance relation represents pipe wall dynamics, and (ii) numerical investigations. The experimental investigation will be conducted in an existing, modern experimental pipe system at HKUST that is equipped with laboratory precision piezo-electric hydrophones capable of producing acoustic waves in the range from 5 to 50 kHz. Tests will be conducted with, and without, a leak so that frequency shifts due to the presence of leaks are evaluated. The effect of pipe wall-water interaction will be measured using high sensitivity charge accelerometers. Pressure measurements will be used to examine whether the much-used standard orifice relation represents an actual leak and, if the results indicate lack of validity, guide the formulation of a new, frequency-dependent leak relation.

612713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
612713.value: Globally we waste huge volumes of water through aging, inefficient delivery systems. Identifying deficiencies in pipes is difficult because they are buried beneath towns and cities, making them relatively inaccessible for inspection, remediation, repair, or replacement. Worldwide losses of potable water range from 30% – 40%, enough treated water to annually supply 160 cities the size of Hong Kong. Transient-based leakage detection techniques have become popular as a method for pipe leak detection in recent years due to their operational speed, ability to work online and long detection range. The accuracy of this approach hinges on our ability to understand and model the signal-leak interaction. Such interaction has been studied in detail in this research and new and novel results that are now being tested in the lab and the field have emerged. The results of the research have been published in leading journals and conferences and the PI will deliver a keynote on this topic at a conference in France. In addition, the project has helped in the training of two PhD students. Moreover, the successful completion of this project allowed the PI to write a GRF proposal (submitted in October 2017).

613113.label: Project Objectives
613113.value: We will develop a new replica placement policy which enables the distributed file system to fully explore the advantages of a data center network architecture. This replica placement policy will create a positive feedback to the network by reshaping the traffic pattern in a data center network in order to maximize the overall system performance. Given a specific data center network architecture, we will investigate the methods to organize the data pieces of a huge file in a distributed file system so that its I/O performance can be maximized. Alternatively, irrespective of the organization of data pieces in a distributed file system, we propose to tailor the corresponding network to meet the communication demands of servers by fully utilizing the most recent Software Defined Network (SDN) technology, such as OpenFlow [19]. Accordingly, we will identify the various network virtualization schemes in a SDN that can maximize the I/O performance of a distributed file system. Finally, recent researchers have concluded that the conventional TCP fails to provide satisfactory performance for data center networks in many cases including throughput, fairness and latency requirements since TCP never cares about the traffic characteristics of data centers. As a result, there is a great need in designing practical and efficient protocols which can take into consideration the data center traffic characteristics. We propose to develop a new protocol based on UDP for data center reliable transmissions which can significantly reduce traffic latency for MapReduce traffic in data center networks and provide perfect queue length control on the switch side.

613113.value: 正在积累大量数据从各种各样的来源，在工程和科学学科。例如，目前的生物信息学应用程序需要同时管理大量的数据和大量的计算。鉴于一个非常大的数据集的高维，许多研究人员的目标是在并行和分布式基础设施的开发和应用，为了支持大规模的数据分析，在数据中心。 MapReduce是一个通用的并行化的技术出现，特别是要很好地适应这项任务。 MapReduce的允许一个利用固有的并行集群计算，管理在多个节点上的一个长时间的计算过程中可能发生的硬件故障。在实践中，重要的是有一个框架，允许分布式处理大型数据集在集群计算机使用简单的编程模型MapReduce的。它必须被设计为从单个服务器扩展到数千台机器，每个提供本地计算和存储。 分布式文件系统（ DFS ）是MapReduce框架的重要组成部分。而不是依赖于硬件，以提供高可用性， DFS的设计在应用层的故障检测和处理，提供高可用性和高性能计算机集群上，其中每个服务可能会有故障。的许多架构/算法由于DFS的重要性，已提出， ，如Hadoop分布式文件系统（HDFS ） ，谷歌文件系统（GFS ） ，等等，据我们所知，很少有人能够优化系统动态性能，适应环境，他们目前居住。他们中的大多数从来不计较数据中心的流量特性 在这项建议，我们打算使用面向网络技术，分布式文件系统的性能进行优化的MapReduce ， MapReduce的大型数据分析更好的服务宗旨。我们提出了三种不同但密切相关的方法来实现这一目标。作为第一种方法，我们将开发一个新的副本放置策略，使分布式文件系统的数据中心网络架构的优势充分发掘。此副本放置策略，将建立一个积极的反馈到网络，重塑在数据中心网络的交通格局，以最大限度地提高系统的整体性能。至于第二种方法，我们建议调整相应的网络服务器，充分利用最新的软件定义网络（SDN ）技术，以满足通信需求。最后但并非最不重要的，我们建议制定一个新的协议，基于UDP数据中心的可靠传输可以实现MapReduce应用在数据中心的延迟要求，并提供更好的队列长度控制在开关两侧。

613113.label: Realisation of objectives
613113.value: We have finished the proposed objectives. First, given different data center network topologies, we studied how to store and replicate a big file into a distributed file system to optimise its I/O performance, and our approach fully takes advantage of network topologies and maximises the performance under a particular topology. Second, we leveraged SDN technique in the implementation of the routing and traffic load balancing to optimise the system I/O performance. Third, we designed a series of practical and efficient network protocols to optimise data center traffic. Specifically, we proposed flow and co-flow scheduling algorithms to reduce traffic latency for MapReduce/Spark traffic in data center networks, and we also presented optimised queue length control on the switch through active queue management (AQM).

Finally, recent researchers have concluded that the conventional TCP fails to provide satisfactory performance for data center networks in many cases including throughput, fairness and latency requirements since TCP never cares about the traffic characteristics of data centers. As a result, there is a great need in designing practical and efficient protocols which can take into consideration the data center traffic characteristics. 613113.label: Major findings and research outcome
613113.value: As the output, we have published over 15 conference and journal papers, including the best networking conference ACM SIGCOMM, which is the first home-grown SIGCOMM paper for Hong Kong. We have many findings in these published papers. For examples: 1) In conference paper No #6, we designed a practical co-flow scheduling algorithm that can greatly reduce application-level coflow completion times for MapReduce/Spark-like data parallel applications; 2) In conference paper No #2, we designed a simple yet effective solution to enable ECN (AQM) for multi-service multi-queue production DCNs which overcomes the tradeoffs by delivering both high throughput and low latency (due to optimised queue length control) simultaneously; 3) In conference paper No #5, we designed the first systematic solution for scheduling mix-flows that can reduce the 95th percentile FCT of non-deadline flows by up to 47.78% at high load compared to existing solutions while maintaining low (<5.8%) deadline miss rate. In most of these papers, we leveraged SDN technique in the implementation, and all of the the outcomes can be used to optimise the communication in distributed file systems.

613213.label: Project Title(Chinese)
613213.value: 使用蒙特卡洛方法降低运筹学模型参数估计误差

613213.label: Project Objectives
613213.value: We will develop a statistical procedure that computes a simulation-based estimator of the unknown parameter (or parameter vector) based on any two-step estimator of the system performance. Because the procedure naturally leads to a stochastic root finding problem, we will study and compare the performances of various stochastic root finding algorithms in this procedure. Suppose that the two-step estimator is a consistent estimator of the unknown parameter. We will then derive the asymptotic expansions of our simulation-based estimator and study its bias and variance and compare them to the two-step estimator. Suppose that the two-step estimator is inconsistent, especially when the data censoring is ignored. We will then show how our simulation-based estimator achieves consistency based on the inconsistent two-step estimators. We will also derive the asymptotic expansions of our simulation-based estimator and study its bias and variance. We will apply our procedure on applications from queueing theory and inventory management. In particular, we will study how to apply our approach on censored demand data and compare to other well-known inventory management policies under demand data censoring.

613213.value: The method may be applied to study bike-sharing demand data, which is a very hot topic right now. 613213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
613213.value: When the amount of data is not sufficiently large, estimation can sometimes be difficult, especially when the system performance is highly nonlinear in the unknown parameters. In this project we propose to use computer simulation as a way to generate more artificial data to supplement the real data. By combining these two sources of data together, we can estimate the system performance with much smaller bias.

613413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
613413.value: High-performance thermoelectrics, which can directly convert thermal energy into electrical energy and vice versa without any moving parts, are urgently desirable for efficient thermal energy harvesting and solid-state thermal management. Current thermoelectric applications are limited by the low efficiency of thermoelectrical materials. While little progress in improving the performance of bulk thermoelectric materials has been made in recent decades, nanostructured thermoelectric materials have shown great potential in maximizing the thermoelectric efficiency. Due to the quantum and classical confinement effects caused by the small feature size, nanostructures provide the opportunities to decouple and engineer the thermal and electrical transports. Compared with other nanostructures such as superlattices and quantum dots, nanowires, as a spatially confined one-dimensional structure, offer many advantages such as superior thermoelectric performance, low fabrication cost and convenience for characterization and integration, and are very suitable for thermoelectric applications. Compared with pristine nanowires and core-shell nanowires, 1D core-multishell heterostructures may provide more flexibility in engineering both phononic and electronic properties. The multilayer heterstructure will result in a spatially confined charge gas which experience no scattering with the interface. Meanwhile, much enhanced phonon interface scattering and phonon spectrum modification in this multilayer structure can significantly suppress the thermal transport. It is very promising to achieve a significant improved power factor as well as a substantially reduced thermal conductivity simultaneously in the core-multishell nanowires, leading to a much improved thermoelectric efficiency. We propose to systematically investigate the thermoelectric behavior of 1-D core-multishell structures with a spatially confined charge gas through both theoretical and experimental approaches. To understand the fundamental phonon and electron transport mechanism in this novel nanostructure, we will adopt a multiscale strategy, combining the first principle calculations, molecular dynamical simulations and Boltzmann transport theory, for this research. We will focus on the relationship between the core-multishell design and the quantum or classical confinement effects on electron and phonon transport. This will pave the way to tailoring the thermal and electrical properties using 1-D multilayer structure. To verify the theoretical results and improve the modeling vice versa, we will synthesize high-quality Ge-Si core-multishell nanowires with different configurations. Their thermoelectrical transport properties will be characterized using a micro measurement device over a wide temperature range. The output from the theoretical and experimental research will clarify many fundamental issues in the design, optimization and applications of thermoelectric core-multishell nanowires. 髙性能熱電材料能夠不需任何機械運動部件而將熱能和電能相互轉換，對熱能利用和熱管理具有積極意義。目前熱電應用受限于材料性能，而體材料的性能在最近幾十年提升不大，而納米材料在提升熱電性能方面展現出巨大的潛力。利用小尺度下的經典和量子約束效應，納米結構使得解耦和改變電子和聲子傳輸特性成為可能。在諸多納米結構中，納米線以高性能，低造價，方便集成和測試等特性，非常適合與熱電應用。和晶體納米線等相比，多層核殼納米線在熱電改性方面提供了更大的自由度。它可生成不受介面散射影響的約束自由電荷氣，并改變聲子頻譜和散射，從而可以同時優化聲子和電子傳輸，達到更好的熱電性能。我們計劃通過實驗和理論建模系統研究一維多層核殼結構的熱電行為，并專注于理解多層核殼結構對於聲子和電子傳輸的影響，從而為利用一維多層納米結構來改變熱和電的傳輸鋪平道路。

613413.label: Realisation of objectives
613413.value: Mr. Ruiqiang Guo was admitted as a PhD student to work on the project with the financial support from HKUST. Mr. Ruiqiang Guo has conducted atomistic simulations including molecular dynamics simulations and ab initio calculations. He received his PhD degree at HKUST in August, 2015. Mr. Daniel Villaromann obtained his bachelor's degree from HKUST in 2012 and was admitted as a PhD student to work on the development of the micro thermal bridge device for the measurement of thermoelectric properties. He received his PhD degree at HKUST in August 2017. We have developed new sets of Si-Si, Ge-Ge, Si-Ge Density Functional-Theory-based tight binding (DFTB) parameters, for the study of thermal transport properties of different Si/Ge systems. Detailed tests on the structural, mechanical, harmonic and anharmonic properties of bulk silicon and germanium, 2D silicene and germanene, silicene nanoribbon, and SiGe alloy have been conducted to verify the efficiency, accuracy and transferability of the proposed parameter sets. Comparisons with DFT, classical potentials and experimental results show that these new parameter sets can provide accurate predictions of thermal transport properties of various Si/Ge systems with a relatively low demand for computational resource. These parameter sets have been proved to be capable of describing both the Si/Ge atoms in a lattice and those on a surface, and they are expected to be applicable to other low-dimensional structures such as Si nanowires. The good balance between the accuracy, speed and transferability of these new parameter sets makes them an efficient choice for the study of thermal transport in large Si/Ge systems. Using the developed DFTB parametrizations for Si/Ge, we have explored the band structure and thermoelectric transport properties of Ge-core/Si shell and Si/Ge-core/multishell nanowires. We found that the bandgap of the Ge-core/multishell nanowires does not change monotonously with the atomic ratio: with the increase of germanium atoms, the bandgap first decreases and then increases when the Si:Ge ratio is below 3:1, and when the Si:Ge ratio reaches 1:1 the bandgap decreases again. Electron density analysis shows that hole gas can be formed in the core regime and core/shell interfaces; however, to achieve the confined hole gas, the core diameter should be larger than 1.2 nm while the shell should be thicker than 0.6 nm. For Si-core/Ge-shell nanowires, electron gas can be formed in the Ge region. Overall, the Seebeck coefficient will be improved due to the unique quasi-1D charge gas while the electrical conductivity is expected to increase as well due to the improved mobility of the confined charge gas. We also studied the thermal transport in the core/shell and core/multishell nanowires using anharmonic lattice dynamics with the developed DFTB Si/Ge parametrizations. It is found that on the interface, the phonon scattering is mainly caused by the mass variation. However, when the interfaces are between Si and Ge layers with different lattice orientations, the interfaces will be highly disordered. The distortion of the lattice structure will strongly scatter the phonons incident on the interface. Moreover, the core/multishell structure will lead to localization of phonon modes, i.e., some phonon modes will have very low group velocity and contribute little to the thermal transport. The combination of these two effects leads to a very low thermal conductivity in the core/multishell structure, indicating the core/multi-shell structure may be promising for tailoring the thermal transport properties for thermoelectric applications. For the simultaneous characterization of the thermoelectric properties of one-dimensional nanomaterials, a highly reliable and efficient thermal bridge technique was developed based on one-dimensional heat transfer and four-probe measurements. The developed micro device was fabricated using the standard micro-electro-mechanic fabrication techniques and numerical simulations were used to optimize the design parameters. The reliability of the technique was improved by using a slow voltage sweeping together with the lock-in amplification to suppress the thermal noise from the ambient environment. To eliminate the influence of radiation and improve the sensitivity, a Wheatstone structure has been used to cancel out the heat loss due to the radiation. The tests with silver nanowires, SiO2 nanowires and Si nanoribbons have proved the accuracy and reliability of the developed micro device near or below the room temperature.

613413.label: Major findings and research outcome
613413.value: 1. Two PhD students were trained and one received his PhD degree in August 2015 while the other received his PhD degree in August 2017. 2. We have published 7 articles in peer reviewed international journals . 3. New tight binding parametrizations for Si and Ge that can be used to predict the thermal and mechanical properties of various Si/Ge systems including 2D systems such as silicene and germernine have been developed. 4. Ab initio calculations show that hole gas will be formed on the interface between Si and Ge layer and a minimum thickness of 1.2 nm is needed to form free charge gas. 5. Anharmonic lattice dynamics calculations show that the core-shell structure will significantly suppress the phonon transport due to the phonon localization and diffusive scattering on the core/shell interfaces. 6. A micro thermal bridge device that can measure all the thermoelectrical properties including the Seebeck coefficient, electrical conductivity and thermal conductivity of a nanowire has been developed. A Wheatstone design has been used to reduce the thermal noise and increase the sensitivity.

613413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
613413.value: The new Si/Ge tight binding parametrizations can be used to investigate the thermal and mechanical properties of many other Si/Ge based systems such as SiGe alloy, Si/Ge superlattice, silicene ribbons, silicene/germernine hybrid 2D systems. Their high accuracy and efficiency will benefit those researches that can be difficult to conduct using the conventional density functional theory. The developed micro thermal bridge device can be used to study the thermoelectric properties of other thermoelectric nanostructures.

613413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
613413.value: In this project, we have explored the phonon and electron transport in the core/multishell nanowire structures for thermoelectric applications using the density-functional-theory-based tight binding method. We developed new density-functional-theory-based tight binding parametrizations for Si and Ge, which show excellent accuracy and transferability in predicting the thermal transport properties of various low-dimensional and bulk Si/Ge systems. We found that the core/multishell structure can introduce the charge gas confined to the Si/Ge interfaces due to the difference in work functions of Si and Ge , which will enhance the power factor of the nanowires. The layer thickness plays a role and the charge gas does not exist when the layer thickness is below 1.2 nm. The core/multiple shell structures will also cause significant interfacial scatterings and thus reduce the thermal conductivity. This indicates that core/multishell structure may be promising for thermoelectric applications. Meanwhile, we also successfully developed a micro thermal bridge device that can be used to measure the Seebeck coefficient, electrical conductivity and thermal conductivity of thermoelectric nanowires.

613513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
613513.value: Foreseeing a promising future for biomass power generation as renewable energy, relevant industries have shown keen interest into building cost effective and environmentally friendly biomass power plants. One of the main concerns about biomass combustion is its high moisture content that reduces the combustion temperature and lowers the boiler efficiency. The high moisture content in the flue gas also generates various environmental and operational problems. Drying biomass before combustion can overcome these deficiencies but on the other hand requires additional energy and capital investment. The difficulty of removing moisture from biomass is affected by many factors such as the drying medium, drying temperature, the moisture content and particle size of the feed stock. Alternatively, biomass co-combustion with auxiliary fuel such as coal can maintain a higher combustion temperature that reduces some of the difficulties caused by biofuel combustion alone. However, adding auxiliary fuel increases the fuel cost, making the combustion of biomass less cost effective. The level of drying is therefore a very important parameter, which strongly influences the economies and the feasibility of biofuel utilization. To reduce the energy cost for the drying, better integration of the drying process with the steam power system is required. For instance, a steam power plant generates steam at different pressure levels and hot flue gas from the boiler can be used to run the biomass dryers. The dryers, on the other hand, generate low grade heat in a form of low pressure steam or moist gas that can also be used for preheating boiler feed water or combustion air to the boiler. When a hot air dryer is used for biomass drying, the contaminated air after drying can be fed as the combustion air to the boiler so as to reduce the heat lost as well as the pollution. There are many other possibilities of energy or material integrations in between the two processes. The main objective of this project is to optimize the design of a biomass power plant taking into account the level of feed stock drying and the possibilities of energy and material integrations. The integration of the energy and material flows can lower energy consumption to the dryers as well as the emissions. The investigation requires modeling works of the biomass drying process, biomass combustion and the steam and power generation processes. With the models, energy and material integration study of the whole process will be performed. 在可预见未来利用生物燃料发电将变得越来越重要，但业界对生物质发电的成本效益和对环境的影响非常关注。生物燃料中的水分含量严重影响燃烧效率影响环境；降低燃烧温度，降低锅炉效率并让烟道气中的水分含量提高，还产生各种环境和操作上的问题。在燃烧之前干燥生物质，可以克服这些不足之处，但在另一方面，需要额外的能耗和资金投入。从生物质中除去水分的难度受许多因素影响，如干燥介质，干燥温度，水分含量和原料粒径的大小。另外，与辅助燃料，如煤等混燃能保持较高的燃烧温度，减少生物燃料在燃烧时所产生的问题。但是，添加辅助燃料增加的燃料成本，降低成本效益差。干燥过程的设计与干燥的深度，是一个非常重要的课题，它直接影响生物燃料利用的可行性。为了降低用于干燥的能耗，必需更好地整合干燥过程与蒸汽动力系统。例如，利用发电厂产生的不同压力的蒸汽和高温烟气为生物燃料干燥。在另一方面，干燥机产生的热气或低压蒸汽，也可以被用于预热锅炉补给水或燃烧空气。我们也可以把干燥后的热风作为燃烧空气，污染的热空气被送到锅炉燃烧，可减少热损失及污染。在这两个进程之间，能量或物料的集成还有许多其他的可能性。这个项目的主要目的是优化生物燃料电厂的设计，考虑到各种原料干燥，能源和材料集成的可能性，以降低消耗，减少排放。研究工作包括建立生物燃料干燥过程，生物燃料燃烧过程和蒸汽发电过程的数学模型。再利用这些数学模型，对全过程的能源和材料集成就进行研究。

613713.label: Realisation of objectives
613713.value: To deliver the project objectives, several probabilistic system identifications and damage detection methodologies have been developed to address the uncertainty quantification and propagation of structural dynamics problems. The objectives have all been realized and led to original contributions outlined below. With regards to the first, second, and fifth objectives, a two-stage fast Bayesian spectral density (FBSD) approach has been proposed to identify the modal parameters and to quantify their associated uncertainties using response-only measurements. This new probabilistic methodology separates the spectrum parameters (e.g., mode frequencies and damping ratios) from the spatial parameters (e.g., mode shapes) and establishes two separate identification phases, where one of them works based on the trace of the spectral density matrix and the other uses the full spectral density matrix. Using the trace of the spectral density matrix alleviates the ill-posedness of the modal identification problems and considerably reduces the computational costs. Subsequently, a mode shape assembly technique has also been developed to construct global mode shapes from the partial mode shapes, while using multiple sensor configurations. This method specifically aids to identify the modal properties of complex structures using non-synchronous partial response measurements, where the sensor configurations have only a limited number of common sensor locations. Uncertainty propagation properties of this new method are also investigated in a separate study, providing explicit formulations to account for the strong correlation existing between the modal parameters. The proposed methodologies are validated and verified through several examples using both shaking-table test data and field vibration measurements. This framework can be used to keep track of the changes occurring in the dynamical properties, which aims at identifying structural damage reliably. With regards to the first and fifth objectives, a hierarchical probabilistic framework has been developed to address the deficiencies encountered in the present model updating methodologies. It combines asymptotic approximations with Markov chain Monte-Carlo (MCMC) simulation methods to produce efficient approximations for computing the marginal posterior distributions of the quantities of interest. It also elaborates on the robustness and reliability of the estimated uncertainties and allows considering the variability of model parameters observed when using different datasets. For the first time, it has demonstrated the concept of embedding a large amount of uncertainty within the model parameters, while the present Bayesian methods attribute the uncertainties to prediction error parameters. Propagating the uncertainties according to this enhanced assessment of uncertainties provide great consistency and robustness in predictions of the output quantities of interest. Extensive numerical and experimental examples have been used to represent the accuracy and reliability of the proposed method. The mathematical formulations and computational algorithms proposed for the uncertainty quantification and propagation in time-domain model updating problems are of the fundamental contributions made under this project. With regards to the second and fifth objectives, based on the random matrix theory, a novel probabilistic approach has been proposed for the system identification and damage detection of structural systems using response-only measurements. An appealing feature of this method is that it does not involve modeling the spectral properties of the input loadings/excitations as unknown variables, whereas the present Bayesian operational modal analysis methods require adding such variables. This method is verified through a series of numerical and experimental examples using both synthetic and field vibration test data. With regards to the third and fifth objectives, a sequential Bayesian approach has been proposed to estimate the input, state, and noise covariance matrices using response-only measurements. This new approach is central to the fatigue damage prognosis methodologies since it provides an essential link to estimate the displacement history field output at both measured and unmeasured positions. The main idea behind developing this new method is to avoid the direct transmission of erroneous input estimations into the predictions of the state. The method has also been tested and verified through several numerical examples. Moreover, shaking-table tests have been performed on a prototype structure to verify the method with real vibration data. We have demonstrated that this new Bayesian-filtering method eliminates the low-frequency drifts from the estimations/predictions of the state/input and greatly outperforms the existing methods. The proposed method also offers a reliable reconstruction of local strain/stress history field outputs at both hotspot locations and entire-body of structures. With regards to the fourth objective, a novel stochastic simulation method for updating the robust reliability of dynamical systems has been developed. This new method provides insights into the first excursions problem of linear structures when they are subject to stochastic wind loads. Numerical examples are used to test and verify the effectiveness of the method. The fifth objective was realized over the verification and validation of the proposed probabilistic methodologies, for which several shaking-table tests and field response measurements have been conducted. During the experimentations, we have also worked with the new generation of wireless sensors and developed a new method to handle the synchronization errors.

Integrate high performance computing techniques to efficiently handle large-order models with a large number of degrees of freedom, localized nonlinear actions activated during operation, and stochastic loads.

Based on the Bayesian uncertainty quantification and propagation framework develop novel methods for continually tracking the health of a structure and rapidly identifying, locating and evaluating the onset of structural damage from a set of vibration measurements.

Develop methods for predicting fatigue damage accumulation in the entire body or hot-spot locations of metallic structures using response measurements collected at a limited number of measured locations. We aspire to develop methods for predicting the characteristics of the strain time histories at unmeasured hot spot locations. The estimated full strain time histories and spectral characteristics of the strains will be combined with available deterministic fatigue theories and available spectral-based stochastic fatigue theories, to generate fatigue damage accumulation maps based on actual operational conditions.

Based on the Bayesian updates of structural models and their uncertainties, robust structural reliability evaluation and prediction methods taking into account the uncertain current and future loads will be developed

A series of experiments in a controlled laboratory environment will be performed in order to investigate and demonstrate the effectiveness of the uncertainty quantification and propagation methodologies, as well as study the effectiveness of the developed structural health monitoring (SHM) techniques.

613713.label: Major findings and research outcome
613713.value: The journal papers 1 and 2, as well as the conference papers 1, 2, 3, and 4, represent the original contributions made to the uncertainty quantification and propagation of modal identification problems. This novel method separates the identification of mode frequencies and damping ratios from the mode shapes offering superior stability and convergence in the underlying Bayesian inference problem. Moreover, the journal papers 2 and 3 present the novel methodology proposed for assembling partial mode shapes according to non-synchronous response-only measurements. This new Bayesian methodology allows using an economic number of sensors to identify the dynamical properties of structures by using multiple sensor configurations. Propagation properties of this new method were studied in the journal paper 7. The journal paper 4 presents new insights on the first excursion problem of linear structures when they are subjected to stochastic wind loads. This paper elaborates on the efficiency of the present simulation methods when they are used to determine the failure domain and to estimate the reliability index. The journal paper 5 develops a new system identification and damage detection method based on the random matrix theory and the transmissibility matrix. The journal paper 6 deals with the synchronization errors produced by wireless sensors and attempts to minimize their impact on the model identification results. The conference paper 5 develops a new time-domain model updating formulation, which can consider the correlation of prediction errors. The journal paper 8, as well as the conference papers 6 and 7, present a new hierarchical probabilistic framework for time-domain model updating and response predictions. This new framework is of great importance since it also considers the variability of inference results over multiple sets of vibration data. This development considerably enhances the outcome of the present Bayesian methodologies in terms of the reliability and robustness of the estimations. Journal paper 9 proposes a novel Bayesian-filtering method for joint input-state estimation problems. This method is central to the present fatigue prognosis methodologies since it allows a reliable reconstruction of local stresses/strains.

613713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
613713.value: The future work will concentrate on the development of real-time probabilistic methods to handle the simultaneous estimation of model parameters, input forces, and the state in dynamical systems using long-term monitoring data. Nonlinear finite element model identification will shape the future studies, and the development of filter-type estimation methods for damage identification will be the next step of developing probabilistic methodologies. The application of such probabilistic tools to inter-disciplinary areas of multi-scale/multi-physics modeling problems could also be the next generation of probabilistic methods, which can effectively be addressed via the proposed hierarchical Bayesian framework.

613713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
613713.value: Structural health monitoring (SHM) methods have considerable benefits over the traditional monitoring and inspection methods and have shown great promise in practice to shape the future of smart civil structures. However, the presence of uncertainty necessitates the development of probabilistic methodologies, whereby the modeling, loading, measurement, and parametric uncertainties could be accounted for effectively. The Bayesian model updating methods developed, applied and verified under this project provide a rigorous mathematical approach to assess and manage such uncertainties. The methodologies proposed herein alleviate the need to install a large number of sensors on structures by proposing a novel method to combine non-synchronous response-only measurements obtained from multiple sensor configurations. Moreover, this project takes critical steps toward fatigue monitoring and reliability assessment of complex structures developing novel probabilistic frameworks. It also aids urban societies with the challenging problem of aging infrastructures so as to employ cost-effective maintenance strategies according to the monitoring data acquired from sensor networks.

614413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
614413.value: 我們研究一種可以用作電子紙之雙穩態液晶顯示。該顯示利用液晶扭曲向來進行快速反應，估計可以達到亞毫秒級的速度，所以該電子紙可以用於視頻顯示，比現有電子紙更有價值。我們將會以這種雙穩態液晶顯示逐漸取代現有的液晶顯示屏，以最新的技術做出可以隨時給使用者選擇切換為電子書或視頻顯示器的模式，它可以被隨意選用為低耗電量的電子書或高清平板顯示器。在電子書模式下，因為該顯示器是真正的雙穩態，並不需要電流來維持它，故耗電量甚低。在正常模式下，它可以被調較為一個普通的高清平板顯示器，以供視頻或遊戲之用。 這種技術的主要難度在於: (1) 均勻的產生高液晶預傾角，為此我們會利用納米技術。(2) 雙穩態液晶顯示的反應時間及64個灰度顯示，至今我們已製作相應特別的電極排列方法和驅動程式。

614413.label: Realisation of objectives
614413.value: It is an ambitious project. We want to produce a bistable liquid crystal display which can be used as an e-book with no power consumption, and we also want the display to be fast enough to be view in the video mode as well. Though we were successful in making a fast switching bistable display, which is a breakthrough in itself, we could not produce the same display in a large area format. The uniformity requirement is simply too demanding. It turns out that the pretilt angles of the liquid crystal molecules need to be accurate to less than 1-degree, or else the display will decay back to one of the bistable states and the display will be lost. Also, in a dot matrix situation, slight defects on the glass surface can induce a decay of the bistable states as well, making our goal nearly unachievable. We were only able to make a small 1cm size display with few pixels. However, we were able to investigate and publish a lot of results on fast switching LCD and bistable LCD. The physics of such a study is interesting as well as practical. All of these results are important for the understanding and extension of LCD beyond what is available today. Since we can produce any pretilt angle, the parameter space we can explore becomes huge. There is a lot of potential for further research and development of new LCD modes and applications. We were able to explore the application of fast LCD based on ferroelectric effect. We were also successful in making field sequential color LCD using this new effect. A good looking sample with 4” diagonal has been made, with a resolution of 300x400. This is almost what we proposed originally, but without the bistable function. So we declare that our goal has been 50% achieved. To really achieve the original goal, we need to improve our equipment greatly in order to produce the kind of accurate pretilt angles needed. That will require more funding than what we have at present. During this project period, we have published 12 journal papers and 8 conference papers.

614413.label: Major findings and research outcome
614413.value: In this research project, we worked on fast response as well as bistable liquid crystal displays. We wanted to have both properties in the same display. For the bistability part, we have been successful in making bistable bend-splay displays where the stable states are bend and splay deformation respectively. This requires a pretilt angle of about 46-degrees. We were able to generate such angles using our proprietary technology. Successful bistable displays have been made. For fast response time LCD, we were able to demonstrate very fast ferroelectric LCD, as well as bend-alignment LCD. Both are capable of sub-millisecond response times. We were able to fabricate field sequential color displays using the ferroelectric LCD mode. The field sequential color display is based on red, green and blue LED as backlight and does not require any color filter on the display to produce a full color display. We made a 4” 300x400 resolution field sequential color display together with our industrial partner who provided the high resolution active matrix backplane necessary to such a display. The demonstration unit works well and we were able to show video rate displays as proposed in this project. Unfortunately we were not able to produce the field sequential color video display using the bend mode LCD. It is because that the bend mode requires the pretilt angle to be accurate to within one-degree. It is very difficult to achieve this in a large area and high resolution situation. Nevertheless we have been very productive in terms of knowledge generation. We were able to publish 12 journal papers including several in prestigious journals such as ACS Nano and Optics Express.

614413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
614413.value: There is definitely great potential for further work. The original goal of having a fast video rate and a bistable display is still worth pursuing. We are half way there as reported. We believe that the bend-splay display, which is fast and bistable, can still be achieved. We just need to improve our equipment to provide better uniformity to the pretilt angle. As a result of this project, we also realized a field sequential color display using the ferroelectric mode LCD. This direction is worth studying further. Even though this is not a bistable technology, the demonstration of field sequential color means that no color filter is needed. This implies that the sub-pixels are not needed. This will increase the resolution of the display by 3x. In other words, it is possible to increase the pixel-per-inch density of the display. At present, there is a need for high ppi displays for VR devices. Our discovery and results developed here can be of great value for such an application. The elimination of the color filter also means substantial savings in the production cost of the LCD.

614413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
614413.value: This project deals with fabricating a bistable LCD which can function as an e-book, and is also capable of display video information. No display in the market can have both functions at present. It is obviously a very ambitious goal. At present, we were able to develop a bistable LCD which is capable of being an e-book. We were also able to develop a fast LCD capable of field sequential color, in which the color of the display is not generated by red green blue sub-pixels, but by red green blue LED backlights. We have demonstrated a nice looking 4” prototype using our new technology. This fast LCD mode can be very useful in the future to eliminate the use of color filters and in providing a high pixel per inch density display. This project has been successful in generating knowledge with the publication of 12 journal papers.

614513.label: Project Title(Chinese)
614513.value: 输入输出单调关系学习

614513.label: Project Objectives
614513.value: To extend learning with monotonicity to noisy problems where the input-output trend is not entirely monotone. To apply learning with monotonicity to more challenging problems, such as probability calibration with multiple learners.
rows: To extend learning with monotonicity to noisy problems where the input-output trend is not entirely monotone.
To apply learning with monotonicity to more challenging problems, such as probability calibration with multiple learners.

614513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
614513.value: In recent years, machine learning has emerged as one of the most successful tools in many real-world applications, ranging from robotics, bioinformatics, electronic commerce to internet technology. However, with the increasing complexities of today's computer and information systems, the underlying learning process needs to be appropriately guided and constrained so that good generalization can be expected from the limited amount of labeled data. In many applications, this can be achieved by incorporating various degrees of prior/background knowledge into the learning algorithm, and can often lead to improved accuracy and/or reduction in the amount of labeled data required. In this proposal, we consider an important form of prior knowledge, namely that the output is expected to be a monotone (either increasing or decreasing) function in one or more of its inputs. Though often ignored in many machine learning applications, this monotonicity hint is indeed commonly encountered in diverse real-world applications. For example, in breast cancer diagnosis, a tumor with larger epithelial cells is more likely to be malignant; in bankruptcy prediction, firms with poorer profitability and debt ratios are more likely to go bankrupt; in the pricing of houses, a larger house with more rooms is more likely to be more expensive. A popular learning algorithm under this framework is isotonic regression. By utilizing these monotonicity hints, not only is the resultant model more accurate and requires fewer labeled samples, this can also aid in interpretation, as a non-monotonic model may be counter-intuitive or make little business sense. However, learning with monotonicity constraints also has its own drawbacks. For example, isotonic regression can sometimes suffer from over-fitting. Besides, the input-output relationship may only be approximately monotone and thus strict monotonicity may not hold across the entire domain. The goal of this proposal to make fundamental advances to learning with monotonicity so that the above-mentioned deficiencies can be alleviated. Besides, we will enhance the applications of learning with monotonicity, and take that to a new level. For example, while isotonic regression has been successfully used in producing well-calibrated probability estimates for binary classifiers, in this proposal we will extend probability calibration to the even more challenging tasks of multilabel and multitask learning. Another novel use of isotonic regression is to apply it to learning problems with structured sparsity, in which the model parameters to be learned are required to satisfy certain monotonicity constraints. 在这份计划中，我们研究一个关于先验知识的重要形式，即当预期的输出是一个或者多个输入的单调（递增或者递减）函数。但是，单调限制下的学习过程也有它固有的问题。例如，保序回归有时会过度拟合。除此之外，输入和输出之间的关系可能只能被单调近似，因此严格单调在整个定义域上面可能不会成立。这份研究报告的目标就是减轻上面提到的问题。

614513.label: Realisation of objectives
614513.value: The use of prior knowledge can boost performance in many machine learning applications. In this project, we studied different types of prior knowledge to help learn the possibly complicated input-output relationships in machine learning. First, we consider recommender systems, which have been commonly used in e-commerce and online marketing. In particular, matrix factorization has been one of the most successful tools in building recommender systems. Traditionally, matrix factorization only uses the observed user-item feedback information. However, the user-item ratings matrix can be very sparse and noisy. In this project, we considered the use of user/item information as additional input to construct a good prior for the predicted ratings. Specifically, we extended the factorization machine (FM), which is originally designed as a general factorization model. Typically, the FM only uses pairwise input interactions; otherwise, it can easily lead to over-fitting and is also computationally expensive. The downside is that it cannot capture higher degrees of nonlinearity. In this project, we alleviated this problem by using the user/item information as additional input, and proposed a probabilistic matrix co-factorization model, which is then used in combination with a novel tree-based feature group learning mechanism. Experimental results on a number of benchmark data sets show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the state-of-the-art, particularly for predictions on cold users and cold items. Another type of prior knowledge we studied in this project is the low-rank property. In particular, we considered the task of colorizing images, which aims at recovering the original color of a monochrome image from only a few color pixels. While the low-rank assumption has been commonly used in image processing, it is often invalid on natural images for colorization because of noise and also due to the complicated pixel dependency structures in real images. In this project, instead of assuming that the whole image satisfies the low-rank assumption, we proposed a patch-based approach that divides the image into patches and then imposes a low-rank structure only on groups of similar patches. An efficient optimization algorithm based on proximal gradient descent is also proposed, which achieves significant speedup over the state-of-the-art. Experiments on a number of benchmark images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches. Yet another piece of prior knowledge that has shown to be very powerful in many applications is that data samples are often clustered. In particular, in this project, we considered this in the context of crowdsourcing. Crowdsourcing services like Amazon's Mechanical Turk have facilitated and greatly expedited the manual labeling process from a large number of human workers. Each worker can be modeled as a learner, which then provides predictions on the unobserved ratings. However, the problem is that in many real-world applications, some of these workers are spammers, and the corresponding learners may then indicate abnormally high or low probabilities for a particular class label. This makes the crowdsourced labels very noisy. We proposed a novel Bayesian model that clusters workers and items together using the nonparametric Dirichlet process priors. This allows workers/items in the same cluster to borrow strength from each other. Instead of directly computing the posterior of this complex model, which is infeasible, we propose a new variational inference procedure. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm is more accurate than the state-of-the-art, and is more robust to sparser labels. Another approach to identify spammers is by learning the characteristics of the workers. In this project, we explicitly accounted for the dedication of each worker to the task and also her expertise. Intuitively, a natural prior knowledge is that these are nearly monotonic to the quality of the provided labels, namely that if the worker is highly dedicated and also an expert, the labels she provides should be more trustworthy, and vice versa. Once the spammers are identified, their predictions can be recalibrated so that their importance in the final model can be down-weighted. The central issue then is how to estimate these from the input worker data. We developed a Bayesian mixture model for worker annotations, which learns a prediction model directly from samples to labels for efficient out-of-sample testing. Experiments on both simulated and real-world crowdsourced data sets show that the proposed method achieves significant improvements over the state-of-the-art. Instead of focusing on a particular application, the general family of kernel methods can also benefit from the use of prior knowledge. For example, prior knowledge can help the selection of a good kernel in kernel learning. In general, kernel learning can be either parametric or nonparametric. In this project, we considered nonparametric kernel learning, in which the prior knowledge, or the desired output kernel matrix for the task at hand, is specified in the form of pairwise "must-link" and "cannot-link" constraints. A must-link constraint on two input instances specifies that they should belong to the same class, while a cannot-link constraint specifies that they should belong to different classes. Nonparametric kernel learning is more advantageous and more flexible than parametric kernel learning in that it can learn the kernel matrix directly without assuming any parametric form. However, computationally, this is often formulated as a semidefinite program (SDP), which is not very scalable. In this project, we proposed the combined use of low-rank approximation and block coordinate descent (BCD). Low-rank approximation avoids the expensive positive semidefinite constraint in the SDP by replacing the kernel matrix variable with V'V, where V is a low-rank matrix. The resultant nonlinear optimization problem is then solved by BCD, which optimizes each column of V sequentially. It can be shown that the proposed algorithm has nice convergence properties and low computational complexities. Experiments on real-world data sets show that the proposed algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art solvers.

614513.label: Major findings and research outcome
614513.value: In this project, we proposed a number of improvements and extensions on the use of prior knowledge in machine learning problems where the input-output relationship can be very complicated. - We proposed the use of user/item information to construct a good prior for the predicted ratings in a recommender system. We extended the popular factorization machine by proposing a probabilistic matrix co-factorization model with the user/item information as additional input. This is then used with a novel tree-based feature group learning mechanism. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the state-of-the-art, particularly for predictions on cold users and cold items (conference paper #1). - We proposed an extension of the low-rank property, which has been commonly used as prior knowledge on images. Usually, low-rankedness does not hold exactly on natural images because of noise and complicated pixel dependencies. In this project, instead of assuming that the whole image satisfies the low-rank assumption, we proposed a patch-based approach that imposes the low-rank structure only on groups of similar image patches. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches (conference paper #5). An efficient proximal gradient algorithm is proposed to solve the optimization problem resulting from this low-rank model. Extensive experiments show that the proposed method achieves significant speedup over the state-of-the-art (conference paper #3). - We proposed using worker's dedication and expertise, which are nearly monotonic to the quality of the provided labels, as prior knowledge for identifying spammers in crowdsourcing. We proposed a Bayesian model to identify spammers, and recalibrated their prediction probabilities by down-weighting their importance. Experiments show that the proposed method achieves significant improvements over the state-of-the-art (conference paper #2). - We proposed to use the prior knowledge that users and items form clusters in crowdsourcing. We proposed a Bayesian model that clusters workers and items together using Dirichlet process priors. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm is more accurate than the state-of-the-art, and is more robust to sparser labels (conference paper #4). - We proposed an efficient approach for utilizing prior knowledge in nonparametric kernel learning. The prior knowledge is specified as pairwise "must-link" and "cannot-link" constraints. However, computationally, it is not very scalable. In this project, we proposed an efficient algorithm based on low-rank approximation and block coordinate descent. The proposed algorithm has nice convergence properties and low computational complexities. Experiments show that the proposed algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art solvers (journal paper #1).

614513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
614513.value: This project can be extended in several directions. Nonparametric kernel learning has been used for speeding up the data embedding tasks in colored maximum variance unfolding and minimum volume embedding. The solver proposed in this project can also be extended in a similar manner. For the low-rank solver proposed in this project, since it is based on proximal gradient descent, it can be accelerated for further speedup and faster convergence. Besides, as most computations are matrix-vector multiplications, they can be easily parallelized with schemes in parallel linear algebra and be used for the handling of much larger data sets.

614513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
614513.value: In recent years, machine learning has found successful applications in diverse areas of science and engineering. An important goal of machine learning is to identify the complex input-output relationships in the system under investigation. In many applications, various degrees of prior/background knowledge can be gleaned by a careful study of the domain. Once they are incorporated, the learning model can be appropriately constrained, and the effectiveness of learning is often profoundly improved. Moreover, the use of prior knowledge specific to a particular application can bias the underlying search for the best model, thus leading to better performance. In this project, we studied different types of prior knowledge to help learn the possibly complicated input-output relationships in machine learning. In particular, we considered the use of user/item information as additional input to construct a good prior for the predicted ratings in recommender systems; an extended form of the low-rank property in image processing; the clustering of workers/items and also using the worker's dedication and expertise as prior knowledge in crowdsourcing systems. More generally, we also proposed efficient methods to utilize prior knowledge in the form of pairwise "must-link" and "cannot-link" constraints to learn a good kernel in nonparametric kernel learning.

614713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
614713.value: Air pollution is a major environmental concern in Hong Kong. In his first address to Hong Kong’s Legislative Council on 17th October 2012, the new Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government, Mr. C.Y. Leung, noted the urgency of the air pollution problem, and emphasized that reduction of public health risk will be the main objective of the air quality management plan of the new administration. The impact of air pollution on the health of an individual depends on the total dose of pollutants inhaled, which depends on their concentrations in the microenvironments where the individual is exposed, and the duration of exposure. In most developed countries, data on personal exposure are available through studies of exposure assessment to air pollutants and regular time-activity studies among the population. However, such data are scarce in Hong Kong and the Pearl River Delta. In the study, we propose to develop an air pollutant related health exposure assessment system for Hong Kong. In particular, we shall first build an activity database for the various population subgroups using GPS enable mobile devices. At the same time, we shall measure the concentrations of various criteria pollutants at different outdoor and indoor microenvironments. Building on these results, we shall develop an air exposure assessment system for Hong Kong that is capable of tracking the exposure of different population subgroups to various air pollutants in Hong Kong. With such an air exposure assessment system, we can then answer questions like: Where and when do different population subgroups get most of their harmful dose of air pollutants? How would the total exposure for different population subgroups change under different air control strategies? Amongst a number of different air control strategies, which one is the most effective for reducing the overall health burden for Hong Kong's population? 空氣污染是一個香港的主要環境問題。新的香港特區行政長官梁振英先生，在他的首份施政報告中指出空氣污染問題的緊迫性，並強調政府制定空氣質素政策，會以市民健康為大前提。 空氣污染對一個人的健康的影響取決於吸入的污染物的總劑量，這取決於個人所暴露的微環境中污染物的濃度，及個人暴露時間長短。在大多數發達國家，個人暴露的數據都可以通過暴露評估研究。然而，這樣的數據在香港和珠江三角洲是不足的。 在這研究中，我們提出要發展香港的空氣污染相關的健康風險評估系統。特別是，我們應先利用移動設備內置全球衛星定位系統建立一個活動數據庫。與此同時，我們將測量各種污染物在不同的室外和室內微環境的濃度。這些結果的基礎上，我們應制定一個暴露在空氣中對香港的評估系統，能夠跟踪香港不同的人口群組各種空氣污染物暴露量。 有了這樣的空氣暴露評估系統，我們就可以回答以下問題：不同的人口群組在哪裡和什麼時候得到最多的有害空氣污染物劑量？不同的空氣控制策略將如何改變不同人口群組的有害空氣污染物暴露劑量？在眾多不同的空氣控制策略中，哪一個能最有效的減少香港人口的整體健康風險？

614713.label: Realisation of objectives
614713.value: Human activity patterns include information on demographics and data about where and how long people spend their time in different microenvironments in their daily life. By examining the available data resources in Hong Kong, we have identified two datasets which may provide useful information on people’s activity, including the “Hong Kong Population Census” by Census and Statistics Department for demographics and the “Travel Characteristics Survey” by Transport Department for traffic-related activity pattern. These datasets have been added to our activity database. In addition to getting data from exiting sources, we also explored the possibility of collecting Hong Kong citizen activity data using multiple methods and channels. For example, we designed activity survey papers to inquire the location and time that people visited during the past 24-hour and tested its feasibility under different scenarios. Our tests results showed that the accuracy and completeness of the survey highly depends on the time interval for logging their activity and the interest of the respondent. Therefore, this method may not be able to get time-intensive activity data for a mass population. With the wide spread of smart phones among the public in Hong Kong, GPS enabled mobile devices can be used to track activity-location information for a large population. We have tested several tracking softwares available on the market, and their performances on different mobile devices and microenvironments in Hong Kong. The biggest challenge of using these softwares in Hong Kong is the substantial GPS signal loss during traveling underground, on the streets surrounding by tall buildings as well as inside the buildings, which may lead to a low completeness rate of the activity data. Another concern is the fast power consuming when turn on these softwares, which may be a drawback when promoting it to the mass population. For the signal issues, we are working with people from telecom area to develop methods to retrieve individual location using both GPS signal and the telecom information between the phone and the communication cell/tower. The power concern may be overcome with the development of the high-performance battery capacity. However, they are not readily available at current stage, which may not be able to support build up a representative activity database for a 7 million city like Hong Kong. To enable the air quality measurements in the space-confined microenvironments, such as inside room and during transportation, we examined the available portable instruments/sensors on the market and selected the mostly used ones to evaluate their performance against the standard gas in lab and compared them with reference methods used in HKEPD air quality monitoring network. Based on the evaluation, we chose DustTrak (TSI Inc, MN, USA) for PM measurement and QTrak (TSI Inc, MN, USA) for CO and measurement. Both instruments are feasible to be used in the microenvironment measurement under a wide range of environmental conditions, and are able to provide comparable readings to reference methods after rigorous calibration. For NO2, however, the selected instruments failed to reproduce the calibration curve in our performance tests, due to interference of other pollutants such as O3 and the high humidity environment in Hong Kong. To overcome this issue, we have been working closely with Prof. Ning’s team at CityU to design portable sensors that may provide reasonable NO2 readings in Hong Kong. One of the challenge of using portable sensors in the field measurement is its accuracy and stability. We developed a systematic approach to diagnose instrument/sensor performance in the field measurement, including sensor calibration with reference method, daily zero drift detect and correction, as well as cross-checking among sensors before and after a cycle measurement. A standard operation procedure (SOP) is developed for each of the investigated microenvironments, including school, office, shopping mall, home, and transport, to archive high quality data. Using these SOPs, we have completed indoor and outdoor measurements in 31 schools, 5 high-rise office buildings, 1 shopping mall, 2 homes, and multiple trips on transportation. For each fixed site, we have collected approximately 0.5 million data in 1-minute resolution. These measurement data are stored in the database for further data processing and analysis get the penetration factors. The penetration factors of different microenvironments depend largely on their physical characteristics (e.g. building materials, structure), meteorological conditions (e.g. temperature, relative humidity), ventilation and filtration practice, as well as other factors related to human activity. Although the current dataset covers a wide range of microenvironments, the sample size in some of the categories are not sufficient enough to produce generalized results. For example, there are only two measurements conducted for home, which may not reflect the typical residence conditions in Hong Kong. We are seeking opportunities to collaborate with real estate developer and managers to expand our current sampling network so that we may obtain representative dataset for Hong Kong. As built upon the previous two objectives, the realization of this objective is heavily depends on the realization of the activity database and the penetration factors. Nevertheless, we have examined two state of art exposure assessment models, Air Pollutants Exposure Model (APEX) and Stochastic Human Exposure and Dose Simulation for Particulate Matter (SHEDS-PM), and assessed their applicability in Hong Kong. With sensitivity tests, we have identified and contrasted the capabilities of each method and to offer insight regarding implications of method choice. We further diagnosed that the exposure estimates are largely affected by ambient concentration, indoor air exchange rate, and time pattern, which help to identify the need and priority for collecting exposure data for objective (1) and (2). In the model evaluation process, we found that microenvironment classification embedded in the two assessed exposure models are based on the activity data collected in the U.S., which does not cover some important microenvironment in Hong Kong, such as Metro Transit System, shopping malls, and high-rise residence buildings. Based on the collected information on activity for Hong Kong citizen, we developed a 2-level Microenvironment Classification System, which provides flexibility in the selection of microenvironments and the characterization of their outdoor-indoor transit properties. This flexibility makes it readily to be applied in the context of different data availability in this city. As an integration of all the achievements in the project, the realization of this objective is heavily depends on the realization of the activity database, penetration factor database, and the localized exposure model. Based on the methods established in this project, we conducted a preliminary exposure assessment on children’s exposure to ambient O3 and PM2.5 in Hong Kong, to demonstrate the capability of the developed models in estimating the exposure for Hong Kong citizen. Due to the limited activity data available for Hong Kong citizen, we use the Consolidated Human Activity Database (CHAD) in the U.S. provides an alternative to estimate the children’s activity in Hong Kong. Three microenvironments are found to contribute to the peak exposure for children during the day. Results in this study give insights to the priority in data collection in exposure assessment and to the development of exposure abatement strategies in air quality management.
