614713.label: Major findings and research outcome
614713.value: Propose a mixed method in developing activity database for Hong Kong citizen from multiple sources channels (objective 1) We identified two data sources that may provide useful information on people’s location and their time-use pattern, including government census data and traffic survey data. Together with traditional method from paper survey and new advances in smart phone location tracking technology, we proposed a mixed method to combine, digest and fuse activity data collected from multiple sources via multiple channels. A manuscript is being prepared to demonstrate this method. Develop a systematic approach and database for charactering exposure concentrations in different microenvironments (objective 2) We developed a systematic approach on sensor calibration, data collection, data processing for exposure concentration measurement. A standard operation procedure (SOP) is developed for each of the investigated microenvironments, including school, office, shopping mall, home, and transport (W.W. Che, Lau, Frey, & Li, 2017). Our collected data shows a 20% to 70% reduction in particle infiltrations in buildings with filtering system compared to those with natural ventilations (W. W. Che, H. C. Frey, & A. K. Lau, 2015). We proposed a sequential measurement method which enables quantification of passenger exposure concentration for various transportation modes under constraints of limited instrument resources (W. W. Che, Frey, & Lau, 2016). This method was demonstrated in several studies to provide policy-relevant insights for exposure mitigation (Li, Che, Frey, & Lau, 2018; Li, Che, Frey, Lau, & Lin, 2017). For example, short-term spikes in PM2.5 concentrations were observed on MTR near train doors when doors open, indicating the inﬂow of ambient air aboveground and tunnel air underground (Li et al., 2018). In this study, 50% of the average concentrations observed in cabin during underground were contributed by the non-ambient sources related to MTR operation, such as tire and wire. Evaluate exposure assessment methods and develop a conceptual assessment model (objective 3) We evaluated the sampling schemes and modeling methods generally used in estimating exposure. Exposure simulation results are robust to the two population sampling methods evaluated, and are sensitive to the choice of method for simulating longitudinal diaries, particularly when analyzing results for speciﬁc microenvironments or for exposures exceeding a benchmark of concern (W. Che, Frey, & Lau, 2014). Our comparisons help to identify and contrast the capabilities of each method and to offer insight regarding implications of method choice. We further diagnosed the sources of variability in exposure estimates, which is to be found largely affected by ambient concentration, indoor air exchange rate, and time pattern (W. W. Che, H. C. Frey, & A. K. H. Lau, 2015). Based on the time-use pattern of HK citizens, we have developed a conceptual exposure assessment model with a localized 2-level Microenvironment Classification System for Hong Kong.  Preliminary exposure assessment on children’s exposure to ambient O3 and PM2.5 in Hong Kong (objective 4) Our preliminary exposure assessment on children’s exposure to ambient O3 and PM2.5 in Hong Kong indicate that school and in-transit microenvironment account for the hourly peak exposure on weekdays; while outdoor microenvironment accounts for the hourly peak exposure on weekends during our simulation period (1-31 October, 2011). The total exposures on weekend are generally higher than that on weekdays due to larger amount of time spent in outdoor microenvironments where the concentrations for O3 and PM2.5 are higher than indoor and in-transit microenvironments. Large reductions in children’s exposure can be expected with better control of outdoor-indoor transit of pollutants in these microenvironments.

614713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
614713.value: As an emerging field, exposure science addresses the fundamental issues of whether and how human contact with air pollutants occurs after release into the environment, and advances knowledge of the mechanisms and dynamics of events either causing or preventing adverse health outcomes. The need for exposure-related research is expanding throughout the world. The framework proposed in this project represents our best understanding of critical components in estimating the exposure for Hong Kong citizen. Warranty is granted to further investigate research questions related to each component. Cities are being instrumented with digital devices and infrastructure that produce ‘big data’. Such data enables real-time analysis of city for envisioning and enacting more efficient, sustainable, competitive, productive, open and transparent “smart cities”. How to embrace these advances in the framework to develop a better way to quantify citizen’s exposure to air pollutants is also a direction for future research. The Hong Kong SAR Government is committed to developing Hong Kong into a smart city - with the dual objective of driving Hong Kong's economic development and also improving our citizens' quality of living. We shall take the advantage in the development of smart city to validate and consolidate this framework in Hong Kong to promote more effective air pollution and health risk management, which can be demonstrated as an example for the development a smart green city. This research started by this project has been recognized by the government and the community as important. With full support of the Environment Bureau, we have since received a 46.158 million grant in September 2016 from the HSBC 150th Anniversary Charity Programme to develop a five-year Personalised Real-time Air Quality Informatics System for Exposure – Hong Kong (PRAISE-HK). More information about the project can be obtained at http://praise.ust.hk

614713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
614713.value: 6.5 million deaths (11.6% of all global deaths) were associated with air pollution in 2012, which is identified as the biggest environmental risk to health by the World Health Organization (WHO). The impact of air pollution on the health of an individual depends on the total exposure of pollutants inhaled, which depends on their concentrations in the places where the individual spends their time, and the duration of exposure. This project serves as first of its kind in Hong Kong to develop a framework with possible methods to systematically quantify population’s exposure to ambient air pollutants in their daily life. We evaluated available instruments and developed rigorous protocols for measuring microenvironmental concentrations, based on which a database is built up with indoor and outdoor measurements at 31 schools, 5 high-rise office buildings, 1 shopping mall, 2 homes, and multiple trips on transportation. We proposed a mixed method to combine, digest and integrate activity data for Hong Kong citizens. A conceptual assessment model has been developed to estimate the population exposure based on the microenvironmental concentration and localized time-activity data. Our preliminary results indicate that large reductions in population exposure can be expected with better control of outdoor-indoor transit of pollutants.

614813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
614813.value: 在過去的四十年中，集成電路產業已經顯著地改變了我們的生活方式。一個發展成熟，复杂但是可靠的工業平臺得以建立并廣泛應用于半導體製造和各種不同的領域。這些卓越的成就首先歸功於歷史上硅基互補型金屬氧化物半導體技術追隨摩爾定律不停的縮小。當金屬氧化物半導體晶體管的物理柵極長度接近原子尺寸時，獲得持續提高的性能而且不打破功耗的極限變得越來越困难。預料硅基晶體管在下個十年內會在器件結構或者開關機制上有若干根本的變革。目前，由於具備小的電子有效質量以及高的遷移速度，III-V族化合物半導體被認為是“后硅”時代n-型金屬氧化物半導體晶體管的替代品爾被廣泛地研究。來自于學術界和業界的模擬與實驗結果都展示了III-V族在邏輯電路应用的巨大潛力。 很顯然這對III-V族晶體管是一個機會，然而一個尚未解決的關鍵問題是如何把它們異質集成在硅基底上。實際上，異質集成的難題早已成為學術界一個長期的訴求。自從1980年代开始，實現III-V光學器件與先进硅基電路的單片集成已經開始推動這一問題的研究。最近對於III-V族邏輯电路應用的不斷增長的熱情再一次把注意力指向這一話題。晶圓鍵合和直接外延生長這兩種方法都在探索中。晶圓鍵合不受制于材料晶格的失配，因此可以將高質量的III-V薄膜轉移到硅基底上。但是這種方法局限於低成品率以及小尺寸III-V族基底。相較而言，直接外延生長能够借助於大尺寸硅基底良好的導熱性和機械強度，因而適合低成本大規模生產。外延生長需要考慮的問題主要是由於大的晶格失配以及熱膨脹係數和極性的差别导致的缺陷密度。

614813.label: Realisation of objectives
614813.value: To demonstrate InGaAs FinFETs, it is important to address material growth challenges and develop transistor fabrication technology simultaneously. New pattern designs are investigated, taking into account of the compatibility issues between materials growth and device implementation. The microscope picture shows the first generation of Si patterning with a “wing-like” transistor layout. The pattern are spread out in the source/drain (S/D) regions to have more materials to contact with metal pads. The top view and cross-section zoomed-in SEM images of the channel region showing the trench is widened at the access region near S/D. Growth of GaAs inside the Si trench was first performed. Prior epitaxy, the sample was dipped in a dilute KOH solution to form V-grooved Si with {111} faces. Examining the top-view and cross-section SEM images after GaAs epitaxy, respectively, two problems have been identified and addressed. First of all, the selectivity is yet to be improved, as shown by the random GaAs crystals deposited on the SiO2 mask. Secondly, we found a significant wider trench with a severe undercut after etching, which created a big cavity to be filled by GaAs. The selectivity was addressed with a surface cleaning step using a dilute HCl solution before epitaxy. The second issue was traced back to the oxide properties. With an oxide densification process using MOCVD in-situ annealing before the wet etching, the oxide lateral etching as well as the undercut is greatly alleviated. After these improvements, we were able to grow In0.53Ga0.47As using a GaAs buffer in the pre-defined V-groove regions with good growth selectivity. In the first generation of the pattern design, the transistor channel and source/drain access regions are designed to have varied width. However, this turned out to be problematic in material growth. The loading effect in selective area growth caused a big growth non-uniformity. It is also noted that, because of the varied width, the required KOH etching time is not the same. The KOH etching time that is optimal for transistor channel region to form V-shaped bottom is insufficient for source/drain. As a result, we found different etching profiles. To solve the difficulties encountered in the first generation of the pattern design, a new design with dense III-V fin-array layout was used. As shown in Fig. 6(a), periodic and dense trench recess patterns are fabricated on a SiO2 on Si substrate. This largely prevents the possibility of non-uniformity caused by loading effect in selective area heteroepitaxy. In terms of device fabrication, only one InGaAs single fin will be selected from the array. Metal contacts will be formed through contact via with large pads reside on top of the surrounding SiO2 mask. A cross-sectional SEM image shows one fin-pattern with 60nm opening. In the design, the dimension of the fin-width varies from 20 to 100 nm. With the new designed FinFET layout, we performed MOCVD selective area heteroepitaxy of dense InGaAs/InP fin stack. The growth was initiated with a thin GaAs stress relaxing layer nucleated at a low temperature of 400 ̊C. The selectively is excellent. Compared to the type-A design, the top and down fin width of type B and type C is 2× and 4× increased, respectively. We found the worst uniformity in type-C design. is 2× and 4× increased, respectively. We found the worst uniformity in type-C design. Type-A InGaAs multi-fins were selected to fabricate junctionless transistors. We observe the {111} faceting of the InGaAs layer. The interface between InGaAs and InP is distinguishable from the contrast in the image. Transistors with gate length of 400 nm and 120 nm were fabricated. The output characteristics of a 120 nm Lg InGaAs finfet. Although gate modulation is observed, the transistor can’t pinch off, resulting in a lousy Ion/Ioff ratio. Id-Vd curve subtracting drain current at Vg of -3V gives the curve. Clearly, the fabricated transistor operates at depletion mode. The gate leakage current by biasing gate and source or gate and substrate. The leakage current presented in device output characteristics is suspected to be caused by buffer leakage. There have been reports that indicate it is difficult to achieve high resistivity InP buffer grown on V-grooved Si. The conductivity of InP buffer could be resulted from Si diffusion from the underlying substrate, impurity incorporation from the oxide sidewall, or background doping in MOCVD epitaxy. If the resistivity of the underlying InP layer cannot be improved significantly, one might need to remove the InP buffer layer so that the InGaAs channel is suspended and thereby a gate-all-around (GAA) structure can be used. Additionally, compared to present triangular-shaped InGaAs crystal, it is more desirable to have box-shaped fin-structures. In summary, proof-of-concept demonstration of sub-200nm InGaAs junctionless finfets on Si substrates was achieved by leveraging the aspect ratio trapping technique. We present optimized material quality and show gate modulation in the fabricated devices. This approach shows promise to bring III-V functionality to Si CMOS chips. However, there are several big challenges remaining to be addressed, and most of them reside in III-V heteroepitaxy on Si and its compatibility with transistor integration.

614813.label: Major findings and research outcome
614813.value: By leveraging the aspect ratio trapping technique, we have achieved dense array of GaAs and InxGa1-xAs nanoridges monolithically grown on patterned Si(001) substrates. The indium fraction of the ternary InGaAs ridges can be tailored up to 57%. By combining bottom-up material growth with top-down device fabrication processes, these nano materials can find applications from FinFETs to vertical FETs and tunnel FETs. Here, the dense pattern and close space between neighboring nanoridges render it difficult to select one single nanoridge for transistor fabrication. Nevertheless, we are able to propose and experimentally fabricate a new type of GaAs-InGaAs-GaAs Fin-array tunnel diodes for proof-of-concept demonstration of their potential applications. A maximum room-temperature peak-to-valley current ratio (PVCR) of 5.4, and negative differential resistance characteristics up to 200 ˚C. The PVCR in this work is higher than most of the values reported from vertical-nanowire based tunnel diodes, substantiating the good crystalline quality enable by the defect necking effect. We also investigated aspect Ratio Trapping growth of InP and InGaAs on Si (001) substrates for nano-scale FinFETs. To demonstrate InGaAs FinFETs, it is important to address material growth challenges and develop transistor fabrication technology simultaneously. New pattern designs are investigated, taking into account of the compatibility issues between materials growth and device implementation. Type-A InGaAs multi-fins were selected to fabricate junctionless transistors. Transistors with gate length of 400 nm and 120 nm were fabricated. The output characteristics of a 120 nm Lg InGaAs finfet. In summary, proof-of-concept demonstration of sub-200nm InGaAs junctionless finfets on Si substrates was achieved by leveraging the aspect ratio trapping technique. We present optimized material quality and show gate modulation in the fabricated devices. This approach shows promise to bring III-V functionality to Si CMOS chips. In this project, we have explored MOCVD growth of GaSb and InAs nanoridge structrues on V-groove patterned (001) Si substrates. One GaSb nano-ridge transferred onto a SiO2-on-Si wafer, with a length of 15 µm and a width of 170 nm. Note that the transferred nano-ridges vary in length and are randomly distributed on the SiO2 layer. Metal contacts were able to be deposited on the wires and electrically ohmic contacts were formed. As the GaSb is a very sensitive material requiring delicate process control and the interface of high-k dielectric with GaSb is always a challenging task, achieving good transistor characteristics demands substantial more efforts and resources.

614813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
614813.value: Over the past four decades, the integrated circuits (IC) industry has drastically changed the way we live. A mature, complex yet reliable manufacturing platform is well established and applied to various applications and semiconductor products. These remarkable achievements primarily arise from the historical scaling of Si complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technology following “Moore’s Law”. As the physical gate length of MOSFETs approaches atomic dimensions, it becomes more and more demanding to attain continuously improved performance without breaking power constrain limits. Si-based transistors are expected to go through some major changes in either device structure or switching mechanism in the next decade. Currently, III-V compound semiconductors are being extensively explored as an alternative for “post-Si” n-MOSFETs, due to the low carrier effective mass and associated high electron velocity. Both simulation and experimental results from academia and industry have revealed the great potential of III-V logic technology. Despite the clear opportunity, one critical issue not yet resolved is the heterogeneous integration of III-V nMOSFETs on Si substrates. As a matter of fact, this has been a long-term pursuit of the academic community, motivated by the monolithic integration of III-V optical devices with advanced Si electronic circuitry since the 1980s. The recently increased interest in III-V logic application has directed renewed attention to this topic. Our results of this project clearly showed that is is possible and we demonstrated many proof of concept device structures for the pursue of the semiconductor IC industry.

614913.value: 應用於大規模MIMO無線網絡的多時間尺度干擾抑制技術

614913.label: Project Objectives
614913.value: Objective A: Develop a Multi-timescale Stochastic Optimization Framework We first model the interference mitigation in large MIMO wireless network as a multi-stage stochastic optimization problem by exploiting the multi-timescale structure in the underlying system random process. Such formulation allows performance bench-marking as well as derivation of low complexity solutions by exploiting specific problem structure. Objective B: Develop a Hierarchical Interference Mitigation Solution for Large MIMO Networks Based on the stochastic optimization framework developed in Objective (A), we propose a novel stochastic decomposition technique to design a low-complexity, robust and scalable algorithm to mitigate interference in large MIMO networks. Specifically, adopt distributed stochastic learning and stochastic cutting plane methods to derive low complexity solutions. We also establish technical conditions for the convergence of the distributed multi-timescale algorithms. Objective C: Applications and Performance Evaluation on LTE+ Systems under Practical Implementation Constraints We shall apply the multi-timescale solution framework and insights obtained in Objectives (A) and (B) to design practical solutions for LTE+ systems. Furthermore, we shall develop detailed system level simulation platform to characterize the potential benefits and robustness of the hierarchical interference mitigation solutions under LTE+ datapath, system configurations and constraints.

614913.value: 移動數據應用正以指數級爆發增長。據展望，未來的移動網絡將給用戶帶來如同ADSL般的高速體驗。這意味著單位面積流量要達到25Gbps/km2，也即現有無線系統的1000倍。要實現如此高的需求，無線網絡架構和技術有待重大突破。而大規模MIMO無線系統正被視為未來5G系統的一個值得期待的新模式。在大規模MIMO中，我們考慮的無線系統，相比現有系統，擁有多幾個數量級的天線數（比如100根天線）。使用大規模MIMO的關鍵動機在於：可以利用巨幅增加的空間自由度（Degrees of Freedom, DoF）來 （i） 實現用戶之間的空間複用；（ii） 抑制無線網絡中的小區間干擾。儘管大規模MIMO網絡有潛力帶來巨大的性能提升，但是實用化大規模MIMO網絡也有著很大的困難。首先，要想在多用戶MIMO系統中利用自由度增益，那麼基站需要擁有實時的信道狀態信息（Channel State Information, CSI）。然而，隨著天線數的增加，由於多小區網絡中的導頻符號的不足以及導頻污染問題，獲得這些實時的準確的CSI也越來越困難。第二，大多數應用於MIMO蜂窩網絡的干擾抑制技術（如協作MIMO，干擾對齊以及協調波束成形）都需要全局CSI（包括所有移動終端與所有基站之間的CSI）。而全局CSI在大規模MIMO網絡中很難獲得，其原因包括巨大的CSI信令負擔以及回程信令的時延（比長期演進系統（Long Term Evolution Systems（LTE））中的X2接口有10 ms的時延）。傳統的”閉環“干擾抑制技術的性能對CSI時延非常敏感。在這一項目中，我們提出一個應用與大規模MIMO無線網絡的多時間尺度的干擾抑制技術。提出的解決方案是一個新模式：既能利用大規模MIMO網絡相應的所有主要優勢，又避免了對全局實時CSI信令的昂貴需求。具體地說，每個基站的MIMO預編碼器被分為一個內編碼器和一個外子空間約束。內編碼器通過適應基站的短期本地CSI來實現多用戶MIMO的空間複用。外子空間約束則適應長期信道統計信息來把各個基站的數據流限制在已選的子空間，以實現對小區間干擾的控制。相應的優化包括求解一個多階段隨機優化問題，這一問題一般而言非常困難。但是通過利用潛在隨機過程的時間尺度的內在分離性，我們提出了一個新型隨機分解技術并獲得了低複雜度的多時間尺度解。我們提出的解擁有分層結構并能夠同時利用（i）空間複用帶來的增益；（ii）大規模MIMO系統的干擾抑制帶來的增益。同時，我們的解不需要全局CSI，因而對回程的信令時延具有魯棒性。最後，通過使用分佈式隨機學習和隨機割平面理論，我們也建立了所提出算法的隨機收斂的條件。 總而言之，本項目的結果將會為特定的低複雜度的、可擴展的且魯棒的算法提供理論和實踐基礎，而這些算法能夠完全釋放大規模MIMO在未來5G無線網絡中的巨大潛力。這些結果將會給設備供應商、未來無線標準以及學術研究帶來巨大影響力。

614913.label: Realisation of objectives
614913.value: In this project, we have successfully completed objectives A to C. In objective A, we have developed a multi-timescale stochastic optimization framework. We have studied the properties of the problem such as existence and uniqueness of solutions as well as convexity of the problem. We have also developed some important structural properties of the optimal conditions and designed iterative algorithms with convergence proof for solving the multi-timescale optimization problem based on stochastic learning methodology. The proposed solution has low complexity and provable convergence, which is very important especially for large scale problems. In objective B, we have applied the framework and the solutions in massive MIMO systems. Simulation results are promising and we can achieve significant performance gains with substantially reduced signalling overhead. The proposed solution are robust to signalling latency and this is very important for practical implementation. In objective C, we have developed LTE-based system simulation platform that can give practical performance evaluation under LTE datapath. We showed that the proposed framework can be a very useful tool as an important guideline for practical interference mitigation scheme of large-scale wireless networks.

614913.label: Major findings and research outcome
614913.value: We have obtained a robust optimization framework by separation of timescales in the control variables. Such separation of control variables is critical to exploit the underlying structure of the physical problem, resulting in more robust, scalable and practical solution for large-scale wireless networks. Such optimization framework has been applied to solve challenging interference mitigation problem for large MIMO systems. Specifically, we have obtained multi-timescale precoding algorithms that can maximize the SINR of users. By exploiting the timescale separation structure, the solution is scalable in terms of complexity and robust to signalling latency of global channel state information. As such, the solution is suitable for practical implementation constraints. We have published a total of 6 journal papers on top IEEE journals, 3 conferences papers in IEEE top conference as well as trained 2 PhD students and one postdoc fellow.

614913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
614913.value: The framework can be further applied to other challenging problems of radio resource optimization for large and complex wireless networks. As long as there is an underlying separation of timescale structure, the system should be able to benefit from the solution.

614913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
614913.value: In this project, we have developed a powerful optimization framework for the design of practical dynamic radio resource management algorithm. The solution can handle large-scale wireless network with scalable complexity and signalling overhead. In addition, the solution framework can produce a robust algorithm that is insensitive to signalling latency. The solution will be critical to enhance the adaptivity of modern large scale and complex wireless networks.

615113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
615113.value: 搜索引擎的準確度，覆蓋率，功能和速度方面在過去二十年間經歷了顯著的改善。為了幫助用戶探索與他們查詢項目相關的信息空間，一些搜索引擎除了提供匹配的網頁內容外，也展示相關的查詢和概念。例如，谷歌最近推出的知識圖，被認為是踏入下一代搜索器的一個重要起步點。例如查詢“莫扎特”，谷歌不僅提供常規的結果，亦顯示不少相關的搜索，如“莫扎特的電影”，“莫扎特傳”和“莫扎特音樂”等，以及鏈接到與莫扎特相關的各種概念（不是網頁），例如他的出生地，出生日期，父母和作品等。點擊這些鏈接，例如出生地，一個嵌入式查詢“奧地利薩爾茨堡”會把一組關於薩爾茨堡的鏈接送到用戶面前。循着知識圖的願景，這個項目研究動態查詢建議的技術。我們為了識別一個用戶在信息探索過程中的意圖和興趣，通過該用戶的相似用戶的智慧和過往經驗，提出了一個以社區為基礎的查詢推薦方法。為了向用戶提出貼切的建議，我們提出以用戶，查詢，文檔和概念構成的四部圖點擊模型，發展合作聚類算法，把四部圖中每個節點內的對象組成集群。為了得到迎合用戶長期和當前興趣的建議，我們建議研究一些方法，把用戶的興趣分為長期，臨時和當前興趣，並應付把它們納入點擊模型內所帶來的挑戰。點擊圖經集群後所得出的用戶社區，可用於（一）高質量的建議，把用戶查詢放大到特定方面，（二）多元化的建議，用戶可在他們查詢的不同方面平移，到達遠端處的有趣話題。為了解決集團化問題，即來自用戶社區的建議仍有可能與用戶的特定查詢無關，我們提出研究細化用戶群體的不同，以確保建議的相關性。我們探索細化的兩個可能維度：與該用戶的當前興趣重疊的其他用戶所進行過的搜索，和非常選擇性地點擊的用戶。最後，我們會進行績效考核，用戶研究和原型開發用以示範項目的成功。

615113.label: Realisation of objectives
615113.value: This project aims to investigate methods to model the user’s interests to make high quality and diversified recommendations to the user. Three specific objectives are listed in the proposal. We achieve the objectives fully by developing several research solutions in the project. In each research solution, we address interest modeling (Objective 1), recommendation method (Objective 2) and performance evaluation (Objective 3). Thus, in the following, we describe the research solutions and how they address these objectives. Development of Curiosity-based Recommendation System (CBRS) [C.9.1,C.10.1]: Traditional research on recommendation systems aim to model a user’s topical interests (i.e., what he/she is interested in) and recommend items that are relevant to the user’s topic interests. The drawback of this approach is that the user quickly feels bored with the recommendations because they are all similar (though not identical) to the previous recommendations. CBRS tries to measure how curious a user is. Curious users appreciate diversified recommendations because they feel excited about items they are not familiar with while non-curious users have opposed behavior. We propose a framework that considers both curiosity and relevance in selecting items to recommend to a user. The major contribution of our research is the development of a probabilistic curiosity model (PCM) that models the probability distribution of the diversity of the items accessed by the user. We apply machine learning methods to learn the curiosity level of the user and recommend items with diversity that matches curiosity level. We conducted experiments and showed that CBRS is significant better than non-CBRS methods. CBRS also shows noticeable improvement when compared to other curiosity-based recommendation methods, which model users as either curious or non-curious (a binary classification) and adjust the diversity of the recommendation in ad hoc manner whereas CBRS has a formal probabilistic foundation. Integrating social information into recommendations [C.9.2, C.9.3, C.10.2, C.10.3]: In the proposal, we argue that user communities are useful in improving recommendation quality. A user community can be formed based on the friend relationship (i.e., users explicitly connect to each other as friends) or just based on behavioral similarity (i.e., users who are not friends but are considered in the same communities implicitly based on their common access behavior). In [C.9.2], we exploit the Heterogeneous Information Network (HIN) to include both explicit and implicit of communities and use the Factorization Machine (FM) with Group lasso (FMG) to learn a model of the weights of various user-user and user-item connections in HIN. Finally, we perform evaluation using large datasets and show that the performance achieved with HIN and FMG significantly outperforms several strong baselines. As can be expected, among various relations between users and items, social connections (both implicit and explicit) are among the most effective relations in recommendation effectiveness. In [C.9.3], we propose the Social Local Model to enhance recommendation accuracy using social relations between users. From a social network, our model identifies influential users and the social networks around them, which are used to break a rating matrix into low-rank local submatrices, each of which represents a social group having similar preferences on items. We show that the application of matrix factorization to the submatrices, instead of directly to the rating matrix, produces higher accuracy. In [C.10.2], we apply community mining methods to find implicit overlapping user communities and use item-based collaborative filtering methods to obtain recommendations. The work also demonstrated the effectiveness of user communities in improving recommendation quality. Interest modeling [C.8.1]: The ability to obtain accurate and comprehensive interest profile of the users is essential for good recommendations. Most of the existing works derive the user’s interest profile through the items the users have consumed, but the number of items consumed by a user is very small (i.e., a user would read a few items among hundreds of items recommended to him/her). We argue that users’ interests are real world objects (e.g., people and events) and the relationship between the objects are important for obtaining diversified and yet interesting recommendations. We further suggest that objects and relations are embedded in various texts (primarily webpages) on the web and can be mined. Thus, we develop a system that builds a concept graph by extracting concepts and their relations from search results via a commercial search engine. We can build a concept graph of hundreds of thousands of nodes in a few days. We have studied properties of the concept graphs extracted from different commercial search engines. Prototyping: As discussed at the beginning of this section, each solution has been evaluated experimentally. In addition, we have implemented a research prototype which is a recommendation mobile app that embed some of the ideas proposed in CBRS [C.9.1]. The app tries to recommend news articles to the user. It monitors the recommended and consumed items in the user’s history. Then, it tries to make recommendations that are novel and have the proper depth and breadth to fit the user’s interest. A user study has been conducted.

615113.label: Major findings and research outcome
615113.value: We find that the novelty of the recommended items is important for arousing the user’s interest [C.9.1]. Further, different users have different levels of curiosity, leading to their different acceptance to novelty. That is, highly curious users welcome novel items, whereas non-curious users appreciate items they are familiar with. We find that with machine learning, we can learn the probability distribution of a user’s access to novel items and then adapt the recommendation to fit the distribution. This is a highly efficient and effective method. We notice that novelty in CBRS is defined based on a simple semantic schema (i.e., music tracks, artists, genres), we can expand the scope by including the users’ social connections and their various online activities (e.g., writing product reviews). By unifying all of the information in a heterogeneous information network (HIN) and applying Factorization Machine with Group Lasso (FMG) to HIN, we show that the rich semantics can improve recommendation performance significantly and that social connections are an important factor to consider in the recommendation process [C.9.2]. Both CBRS and FMG demonstrate the importance of semantics in recommendation systems. We find that a knowledge base can be constructed from efficiently by mining search results returned from search engines [C.8.1].

615113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
615113.value: In our current work (CBRS and FMG), knowledge is extracted from the applications, which means that we can only exploit knowledge available within the boundary of the application. An extension to this project is to exploit a large-scale real-world knowledge base (e.g., concept graphs developed in this project or knowledge bases publicly available on the web) in recommendations. For example, a person who like pork should not be recommended Turkish restaurants. Such knowledge is not likely to be obtainable from the user’s visit behavior. Thus, linking across applications and making the knowledge mined from an application available to other applications will likely to improve their performance.

615113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
615113.value: A recommendation system aims to recommend items that the user is interested in. Effective recommendation can be translated into high user satisfaction and increase business to websites. We investigate methods for making recommendations that can arouse the user’s interest based on how curious he/she is. The common foundation of recommendation systems is the modeling of a user’s interest on a particular item. In our Curiosity Based Recommendation System, we derive a user’s interest from his/her accessed items and the content associated with the items. Having observed the effectiveness of CBRS, we further develop a uniform framework that integrates various kinds of information captured in web applications. This include not only data about the user’s direct access to the items and content associated with the items but all kinds of information derivable for the user’s online activities on a website, e.g., social connections and product reviews written. In addition, we develop methods for constructing large-scale knowledge base to support the recommendation task and a mobile app that incorporate some of the key research ideas developed in this project.

615513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
615513.value: The deterioration of concrete structures worldwide is a major problem with civil infrastructures, and steel corrosion is a major culprit. When rust is formed, it absorbs water and expands in volume, generating internal stresses that induce cracking of the protective concrete cover. Cracks can accelerate the penetration of water and corrosive agents (such as chlorides) and continued rusting leads to concrete cover spalling. With loss of protection, the exposed steel corrodes at a significantly higher rate. The loss of steel area and bonding with the concrete eventually leads to excessive deflection and even failure of the structure. In practice, to determine the time it takes for surface cracks to reach a certain width (when major repair work needs to be performed), it is necessary to have a model that can properly consider the penetration of chemicals, the steel rusting process as well as the cracking process in the concrete cover. In this study, we propose to develop a new computational model combining boundary element and finite element techniques to analyze the propagation and opening of cracks in the concrete cover, when corrosion is caused by chloride penetration from the concrete surface. The main novelty of the work is the consideration of non-uniform rust formation around the steel reinforcement, which is the common situation in practice. In addition, we will consider several important features of corrosion-induced cover cracking, including (i) penetration of rust into the capillary pores in concrete around the steel, (ii) rust penetration into the crack once it is formed, (iii) presence of crack bridging stresses due to aggregate interlocking, and (iv) acceleration of chloride penetration due to crack formation. The developed cracking model is combined with existing models for chloride penetration and steel corrosion to form a complete computational framework for the deterioration process. To verify the computational results, experiments are performed on two kinds of concrete to obtain all the mechanical, transport and chemical parameters required for the analysis. Specimens with embedded steel are made with these concrete compositions and subjected to chloride penetration from one or two surfaces. Measured strain and surface crack opening at different times are compared to computational results. The new computational framework is a significant improvement over existing ones that can only account for uniform rusting of steel in accelerated laboratory experiments. Its development is an important step in quantifying the durability of concrete structures when steel corrosion is an issue. 混凝土結構的惡化是全球基建面對的一個重大問題, 而鋼筋腐蝕是一個主要的罪魁禍首。鐵鏽形成後會吸收水份膨脹, 產生的內應力足以令混凝土保護層開裂。裂縫可以加速水和腐蝕性物質(如氯化物)的滲透, 持續的鏽蝕導致混凝土保護層剝落,裸露的鋼筋會加速腐蝕, 破壞鋼與混凝土的粘接, 最終導致過大的變形和結構失效。 在工程實踐中，為了決定何時進行大規模維修, 需要推算裂縫達到一定寬度的時間, 因而要建立一個全面的模型, 可以適當地考慮化學品的滲透, 鋼鐵鏽蝕, 以及裂縫在混凝土保護層中的擴展過程。在這項研究中, 我們建議開發一種新的計算模型, 結合邊界元與有限元法分析因氯離子滲透引起的混凝土保護層開裂。本工作將針對非均勻鋼筋腐蝕這一個常見的情況, 同時, 計算模型會包含幾個重要的考慮, 包括（i）鐵鏽能滲透到鋼筋周圍混凝土的毛細管孔中,（ⅱ）鐵鏽能滲入裂縫內,（ⅲ）裂縫中由於集料嵌鎖會產生橋連力，及（iv）裂縫會加速氯離子的滲透。新建的模型, 可以結合現有的氯離子滲透和鋼筋鏽蝕模型, 組成一個分析惡化過程的計算框架。為了驗證計算結果，將採用兩種類型的混凝土進行實驗，量度出計算模型所需的參數, 在含鋼筋的試件上, 進行氯離子滲透, 在不同的時間測量表面應變和裂紋寬度, 與計算結果進行比較。 相對只能考慮均勻生鏽的現有計算方法, 新的計算框架是一個顯着的改善, 它的發展是量化混凝土結構鋼筋鏽蝕問題重要的一步。

615513.label: Realisation of objectives
615513.value: All three objectives have been fully achieved. The first objective is on the development of a new computational framework for the analysis of concrete cover cracking induced by steel corrosion. The framework consists of three separate modules to analyze (i) diffusion of chlorides through the concrete cover to reach various parts of the steel rebar surface, (ii) the rate of rust formation after a critical chloride is reached, and (iii) the expansion of rust and the resulting cracking process in the cover. To analyze chloride diffusion, the 2-D Fick’s equation is solved with the finite element approach for different boundary conditions representative of field condition as well as laboratory specimens. With this analysis, the build-up of chloride concentration around the steel reinforcement can be determined. When the critical chloride concentration is reached at a point on the steel rebar surface, rusting will start to occur at that particular location. After corrosion is initiated, the corrosion rate is taken to be constant so the radial loss of steel at a particular point is proportional to the difference between the current time and the corrosion initiation time. The proportionality constant is taken as a representative value from the literature. Such a simple corrosion model can capture the non-uniform distribution of rust around the steel rebar. Once the rust distribution is known, the rust is taken to expand and nonlinear fracture analysis is carried out to derive the crack length in the concrete cover and opening at the concrete surface for various amounts of steel loss (which correspond to different times). The fracture analysis is carried out with a mixed boundary element formulation. For the concrete, its external boundary (i.e., the surface of concrete member) and internal boundary (i.e., the one originally in direct contact with steel reinforcements) are described by fictitious stress elements. Cracks in the concrete cover are assumed to form along certain prescribed paths based on experimental observations. A crack will start to open at a point along its path once the tensile strength is reached, and opened cracks are modelled as displacement discontinuities. The discontinuity in displacement represents the crack opening and the crack bridging stress is related to such an opening through a softening relation. For the steel, fictitious stress elements are placed around its circumference. The rust between concrete and steel is modelled as springs with properties derived from mechanics. After imposing an initial deformation in the rust corresponding to its expansion, compatibility equations are set up so the difference in displacement between the steel surface and internal concrete surface is equal to the rust thickness after compression by the interfacial normal stress. As the lengths of cracks are not known for a particular value of rust expansion, iteration is required, and an effective numerical algorithm has been developed to obtain the solution. The second objective is related to the first, as it is on the comparison of results from the new computational approach to those from commercial finite element software. As the rust distribution is changing with time, if a conventional finite element method is employed to analyze cracking in the concrete cover, different meshes will need to be adopted at different times. To verify the accuracy of the boundary element approach described above, a few classical problems in mechanics are first analyzed with the boundary element approach to verify that the results are identical to that from the theory of elasticity. Then, we study the problem with the steel inside concrete replaced by a hole under uniform pressure. The crack development under increasing pressure is calculated and compared with that obtained from ATENA, a commercial finite element program. The results are found to be in very close agreement. After such indirect verifications, direct verification is performed by implementing a full model in ATENA, with concrete, rust and steel, as in the boundary element model. The rust thickness distribution around the steel rebar is obtained from diffusion analysis. By imposing expansion in the rust, the crack length and opening in the cover can be obtained. As mentioned above, different meshes are used for different rust distributions corresponding to various times. The process is hence very tedious so the number of data points that can be obtained is much less than those with the boundary element approach. The trend of surface crack opening (i.e., the crack width at the concrete surface) vs steel loss is found to be in good agreement between the boundary element and finite element models. The third objective is on the comparison between model predictions and test results. Two groups of concrete prisms are prepared with rebar cover of 20mm or 40mm. In one group, 5% of sodium chloride (by weight of cement) is added to induce uniform corrosion around the steel rebar. In the other group, no chlorides are mixed into the specimen. To induce corrosion, the specimens are put in contact with chloride solution. This can be achieved by immersing the lower part of the specimen into the solution, or placing a small container with the solution on the top of the prism. To accelerate the corrosion process in all the specimens, a steel mesh is placed on the surface of the prism, and electric potential is applied between the rebar and the mesh to increase the chloride diffusion rate. The current is measured continuously so Faraday’s law can be applied to calculate the total loss of steel area. During testing, the specimens are monitored by strain gauges attached to the surface. Frequent visual inspection is also carried out to detect the onset of cracking. Once cracks are found, their widths are measured at various times. At the end of the tests, specimens are broken open so the rust distribution can be observed. With values for modulus and expansion ratio of rust as well as the softening behavior of concrete taken from the literature, the relation between surface crack width and steel mass loss are calculated from the computational framework. The predicted results are found to be in good agreement with measured data during the corrosion tests. Specifically, two important trends predicted from the model are verified. Firstly, for the same mass loss of steel, when corrosion is non-uniform, as in real situations where chloride is penetrating from the surface, the degree of cracking (reflected by surface crack width) is more significant than that under uniform corrosion, which is commonly studied in the laboratory with chlorides mixed into test specimens. Secondly, while a thicker cover can delay the onset of corrosion, after the crack reaches the member surface, the surface crack width will eventually become larger for a thicker cover as the opposing crack faces are rotating away from each other. These observations, derived from both experimental and theoretical studies, give new insights to the problem of steel corrosion induced cover cracking.

615513.label: Major findings and research outcome
615513.value: A new computational framework based on both the finite element method (for diffusion analysis) and boundary element method (for nonlinear fracture analysis under rust expansion) has been developed. While the current work adopts a very simple model for the rate of rust formation after corrosion initiation, more complex models can be employed in the corrosion module, so there is high flexibility for further refinement. To verify the accuracy of the mixed boundary element approach for fracture analysis, finite element models are also set up for several cases to obtain results for comparison. With the finite element model, it is not possible to couple the time variation in rust distribution with the fracture analysis, so individual meshes have to be generated for each case. Good agreement is found between the finite element and boundary element results. A computationally efficient computational framework based on the mixed boundary element approach is hence established. The detailed derivation of the computational framework and its results can be found in Paper 1 of the list of publications. In the fracture analysis, cohesive crack is represented by displacement discontinuity. A new way to formulate the displacement discontinuity method and a new iterative algorithm to obtain the results are developed. To demonstrate the general applicability of this method to cohesive crack propagation, it is applied to several common fracture problems. Very good agreement with finite element analysis and experimental results are obtained. The results of this study are detailed in paper 2 of the publication list. Before completing the development of the new computational framework, the conventional finite element method was used to obtain insights on the corrosion-induced cracking process, and to generate results for comparison with the developed framework. In the finite element study, particular focus is placed on the difference between uniform and non-uniform corrosion. For various placements of the rebar representative of field and laboratory conditions, non-uniform corrosion will always lead to more severe cracking than uniform corrosion with the same amount of rust. The results, which are of sufficient interest on their own, are published in paper 3 of the publication list. Based on experimental studies on the cracking of concrete specimens with embedded steel rebar subjected to accelerated corrosion, measured surface crack width vs time is found to be in agreement with predictions from the computational framework. A paper on this study is currently under preparation.

615513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
615513.value: To further refine the computational framework, several additional studies can be performed. In place of the constant corrosion rate assumption, more realistic electrochemical mechanisms can be considered. When some parts of the rebar have started to corrode, the chloride threshold at other parts should increase as they become more cathodic. Also, the corrosion rate is not constant and should depend on the polarization behavior of anodic and cathodic reactions between active zones and passive zones of the steel surfaces. When cracking occurs in the cover, diffusion of chlorides is accelerated. With the developed computational framework, the computed crack lengths and openings can be fed to the diffusion module, so diffusivity of the cracked elements can be updated according to test data in the literature. Also, knowing the length and opening of each crack, the amount of rust penetrating into the cracks (and hence not inducing expansive stress) can be calculated. In most models, the cracks are assumed to be fully filled with rust. In reality, crack filling depends on the pressure acting on the rust and its flow properties. Further research on this is necessary. All the above issues are currently being studied under partial support from an industrial project.

615513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
615513.value: Steel reinforcement corrosion is a major durability problem of concrete structures. In coastal cities, it is often initiated by the penetration of chlorides. Once corrosion starts, the expansion of rust will induce cracking of the concrete cover, which will accelerate water/chloride penetration. Eventually, the cracked cover will fail by spalling, exposing steel directly to the environment. Steel corrosion is then greatly accelerated and structural safety may be affected. For the durability design of concrete structures and development of proper maintenance, an approach to predict the evolution of corrosion-induced cracking is required. The major contribution of this research project is the development of a computational framework for concrete cover cracking that properly considers various physical and chemical processes including the diffusion of chlorides through the concrete cover, the development of rusting around the steel rebar with time and the propagation of cracks due to expanding rust. Unlike most existing models that can only account for uniform corrosion around the steel rebar (which applies to laboratory specimens), the new framework can predict the cracking process under practical situations where rust distribution is non-uniform and varying with time. The improved modeling capacity is important for the quantification of durability for concrete structures.

615613.label: Project Objectives
615613.value: Designing a new pricing framework for intra-datacenter bandwidth allocation: we aim to design a new pricing framework that maximizes the resource utilization and cloud providers’ revenue. We will derive an in-depth analytical framework to understand the interplay between tenants and cloud providers, and study the price determination process in the proposed three aggregation classes using a game theoretic approach. To achieve cost dominant fairness: we define cost dominant fairness in that a tenant pays proportionally more if its applications have enjoyed better performance using more bandwidth resources. We aim to demonstrate that this is not only an attractive property to tenants, but also a step in the right direction towards optimal bandwidth utilization in cloud datacenter networks. To guarantee that our experimental observations are more convincing, traffic from multiple tenants will be produced by running real-world cloud applications such as MapReduce tasks, in addition to synthetic benchmarks.

615613.label: Realisation of objectives
615613.value: Cloud computing essentially enables multiple tenants to share resources such as CPU, storage, and bandwidth over a set of physical machines. When tenants pay for running applications in a cloud, CPU, memory and storage resources are explicitly priced in today’s public datacenters, typical in the form of virtual machine (VM) pricing. Yet, inter-VM bandwidth in datacenter networks has not been explicitly priced, and remains free of charge to the tenants. As a result, inter-VM bandwidth is usually utilized in a best-effort fashion, which makes it challenging for both cloud providers and tenants to reason about how bandwidth should be properly allocated as a scarce resource. In this project, we argue that regardless of the number of VMs a tenant has leased, each tenant should be given the flexibility to obtain a better or more predictable share of inter-VM bandwidth, which demands to be priced explicitly, and independently from VM pricing. Hence, the reserved bandwidth shares should be priced accordingly. In addition, most tenants may be content with paying more for a better than best-effort share of bandwidth instead of paying for exclusive bandwidth reservations due to the nature of elastic demands. Nevertheless, higher prices should reflect a better bandwidth allocation and usage. In another word, we believe tenants should be given the option for paying more to obtain a better and more predictable bandwidth allocation; that is say to get what one pays for. There are several challenges in allocating bandwidth fairly across competing tenants, in particular a few desirable properties need to be maintained, such as strategy-proofness, communication pattern independence, and symmetry. Surprisingly, if inter-VM bandwidth is priced explicitly, a much simpler design principle can be followed to allocate bandwidth fairly, and the aforementioned properties related to fairness can be easily achieved. We call such a design principle cost dominant fairness, which stipulates that bandwidth should be allocated based on the total cost that a tenant incurs for running its applications in a cloud, while at the same time, a tenant can opt to pay proportionally more if its applications have enjoyed better performance. With the objective of achieving the principle of cost dominant fairness, we explore the solution space of pricing inter-VM bandwidth, as well as achieving fair bandwidth sharing among multiple tenants. We have made several contributions in the realization of this project. (1), we made a strong case for pricing both guaranteed and best-effort bandwidth shares, and proposed the principle of cost dominant fairness; (2) by exploring the solution space of bandwidth pricing strategies, we designed a pricing framework for best-effort bandwidth; (3) to allocate best-effort bandwidth according to cost dominant fairness, we proposed to assign weights to each pair of VMs, determined by their individual bandwidth prices that the tenants have chosen. Based on the per-VM-pair weights assigned, we formulated the problem as a network utility maximization problem, where the objective is to achieve weighted proportional fairness among different flows subject to network capacity constraints; (4) we addressed the practical issues of billing, where discounts may need to be given to ensure that a tenant only pays for the bandwidth share that it is allocated; (5) we presented a system-level design to practically implement our proposed bandwidth allocator as a shim layer at each virtual machine, which scales naturally and is topology-agnostic. We evaluate its performance in the Mininet emulation testbed with various network topologies.

615613.label: Major findings and research outcome
615613.value: We first discussed the rational for explicit bandwidth pricing, and introduced the notion of cost dominant fairness. Since guaranteed and best-effort bandwidth shares co-exist, best-effort traffic from different tenants will need to share the residual link bandwidth at each network link, after guaranteed bandwidth shares are provisioned and accounted for. The intuition for differentiated pricing is that a tenant may wish to accept a higher price to obtain a larger best-effort share, so that better application performance can be obtained. We defined the cost dominant fairness as follows: (1) when tenants are paying the same price, their network-wide bandwidth shares should be proportional to their costs on reserving communicating VMs; (2) for tenants within different service levels, if they have incurred the same cost on reserving communicating VMs, their network-wide bandwidth shares should be proportional to their costs on inter-VM data transmission. With this definition, the cost on communicating VM reservation is reflected by the number of communicating source-destination VM pairs. We can then assign weights at a finer granularity, say, on each communicating source-destination VM pair, to achieve cost dominant fairness network-wide. Through rigorous analysis, we showed that our proposed cost dominance fairness allocation satisfy the following desired properties: (1) work conservation. This states that, if there is at least one cloud tenant who has traffic to send along a link, the link cannot be idle. More precisely, a network sharing policy is said to be work-conserving if links in the datacenter network is either fully allocated, or it satisfies all demands; (2) symmetry. This property states that the allocated bandwidth should not depend on the direction of each flow; (3) Strategy-proofness. This implies that the network sharing policy should ensure that cloud tenants cannot improve their allocations by lying about their demands. To enforce per-VM-pair weights, we have implemented our proposed bandwidth allocation algorithm as rate controlled logical at the shim layer between the VMs and the network interface. We used the Mininet 2.0 emulation testbed to evaluate the algorithm over a different topologies and configurations. In addition, we used a network bandwidth monitoring tool to measure the edge load at each network interface. Through extensive experiments and evaluation, we showed that our proposed algorithm can allocate bandwidth in a fair manner, while significantly outperforming the existing solutions.

615613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
615613.value: This project focused on the bandwidth allocation for inter-VM communications. The recent trend is to support in-memory computations in data-parallel frameworks, in which intermediate results are transmitted in different stages. Such network transfers may become the main bottleneck when we try to speed up job completion times. Existing bandwidth allocation frameworks have largely been designed as isolated solutions that focus on either computation or network performance only. Due to the lack of coordination, the utilization of computation and network resources are often unbalanced, leading to a reduced level of system throughput. We are currently working on designing and building a new network-aware bandwidth allocation framework that optimizes system throughput and balances the utilization of different resources. We plan to provide a substrate and an application programming interface (API) to support task schedulers in data-parallel frameworks both within and across geo-distributed datacenters. It will identify resource under-utilization and coordinate computation-bound and network-bound tasks in a large cluster, with the objective of deriving optimal system throughput by utilizing all types of resources. With network awareness, it will manage both network and computation resources while making task scheduling and bandwidth allocation decisions based on live analytics of cluster states.

615613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
615613.value: In this project, we advocate that a tenant should be given the flexibility to obtain more bandwidth, by pricing inter-VM bandwidth explicitly and separately from pricing VM reservations, using the notion of cost dominant fairness. It stipulates that bandwidth should be allocated based on the total cost that a tenant incurs, and a tenant can opt to pay proportionally more if itsapplications enjoy better performance. One of the highlights in this project is a thorough examination on how weighted proportional fairness can be satisfied using a distributed bandwidth allocator, based on a problem formulation using network utility maximization. Using the Mininet emulation testbed, we have shown that the proposed distributed algorithm can allocate bandwidth in a fair manner, while outperforming existing solutions with respect to fairness.

616013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
616013.value: Voting is a way to aggregate individual voters' preferences. Traditionally a voter's preferences are represented by a total order on the set of candidates. However, sometimes one may not have complete information about a voter's preferences, and in this case, can only represent them by a partial order. This has motivated work on voting with partial information, and particularly on computing the possible and necessary winners of a partial vote, and on strategies for soliciting voters' preferences. Within the general framework of voting with partial information, we propose to look at sets of questions to ask in order to determine the outcome of a partial vote. We will consider how to compute a minimal set of pair-wise comparison questions whose answers will determine the outcome of a voter, make her a winner, or a loser. We will also discuss some interesting properties about these sets of queries, prove some complexity results about them, and consider their applications in vote elicitation. 投票是一种常用的汇总个体偏好的方法。传统上一个投票人的偏好总是用一个在候选人上的完全序来表示。然而，有时候我们并不知道一个投票人的偏好的所有信息，这时候，我们只能用一个偏序来表示他们的偏好。基于这个情况，有一些关于部分信息下的投票，特别是关于计算一个部分投票的可能赢家和必然赢家的工作，还有一些关于征求投票人的偏好的策略的研究在部分信息投票的大框架下，我们计划关注在决定部分投票的结果时需要问的问题集. 我们会考虑怎样计算一个最小的两两比较查询集合，它的答案可以决定一个候选人的结果，也就是决定她是赢家还是输家。我们也会讨论一些关于这些查询集合的有趣性质，证明关于它们的一些复杂度结果，还有考虑它们在征求投票中的应用。

616013.label: Realisation of objectives
616013.value: We have successfully realised all objectives that we set out for in our proposal. We have formally defined the following three types of minimal sets of questions: minimal set of questions to ask voters so as to determine the outcome of an election, minimal set of questions to ask voters so as for a particular candidate to win the election, and a minimal set of questions to ask voters so as for a particular candidate to lose the election. We have shown the existence of these minimal sets of questions, given the exact complexity results for computing such minimal sets under many popular voting rules, and algorithms for computing them. Detailed results are reported in our AAMAS 2013 paper as well as in Ning Ding's PhD thesis. This work addresses our objectives 1 and 2. We have applied our results to Hong Kong Legislative Council Geographical Constituencies election. We formulate the election as a mostly zero-sum game, and show that while the game always has a pure Nash equilibrium, it is NP-hard to compute it. We have designed a system for computing the Nash equilibria. Detailed results are reported in our AAAI 2014 paper as well as in Ning Ding's PhD thesis. This work addresses our objective 3. We have also made part of this project into a course project for an advanced course on AI. Furthermore, Anbang Hu, an outstanding undergraduate student who had been on the Dean's List several times, worked on this project as his Final Year Thesis. Both the course project and Hu's thesis contributed to objective 3 in terms of implementation, Strategies are often implemented as computer programs. Our work reported in two of our KR 2014 papers, as well as our AIJ paper in 2016 study how to formally prove properties of computer programs using first-order theories. This opens up a new direction and relates our work with formal methods in computer science and software engineering.

616013.label: Major findings and research outcome
616013.value: We considered voting with incomplete information about voters' preferences, and looked at it mostly from the perspective of candidates. We considered what minimal information is needed to settle the election for some candidates. Towards that end, we defined three type of minimal sets of questions to query the voters in order to determine the outcome of the election: minimal set of questions to ask voters so as to determine the outcome of an election, minimal set of questions to ask voters so as for a particular candidate to win the election, and a minimal set of questions to ask voters so as for a particular candidate to lose the election (AAMAS 2013, Ding PhD Thesis). We characterise the complexities of computing these three notions of minimal sets (AAMAS 2013, Ding PhD Thesis). We then looked at the particular election model, so-called proportional representation used by Hong Kong Legislative Council Geographical Constituencies election. While the problem is in general NP-hard, it still can be solved when the number of candidates is not too large, particularly when some good heuristics are used. The results are described in our paper at AAAI'2014 as well as the PhD thesis by Ning Ding. Ding's thesis and Anbang Hu's FYT also described an implementation of the system. We then branched out: 1. proposed a translation from programs to first-order logic (KR'14 & AIJ'16) that will be used in a program verification project; 2. a model of causation for dynamic domains which can also be used in modelling agents reasons behind their preferences (AIJ'17, IJCAI'15); 3. a position system to model a planning domain (JPL'15); 4. a theoretical analysis of hard logic programs (ACM TOCL'16).

616013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
616013.value: There are several directions to continue this work: 1. In our applications to Hong Kong Legislative Council Geographical Constituencies election, we have looked at only the two party case. We started collaborating with other researchers on extending this to multi-party case, and this is an ongoing work. 2. We are continuing working on formalising and reasoning about agents' strategies. We have started work on characterising good strategies in repeated games like Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma. We have also continued our work on reasoning about computer programs.

616013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
616013.value: Voting is a way to aggregate individual voters' preferences. Traditionally a voting model requires a complete knowledge about voters' preferences represented by total orders on the set of candidates. However, sometimes one may not have complete information about a voter's preferences, and in this case, can only represent them by a partial order. This has motivated work on voting with partial information, and particularly on computing the possible and necessary winners of a partial vote, and on strategies for soliciting voters' preferences. Within the general framework of voting with partial information, in this project, we have looked at sets of questions to ask in order to determine the outcome of a partial vote. We considered how to compute a minimal set of pair-wise comparison questions whose answers will determine the outcome of a voter, make her a winner, or a loser. We also proved some interesting properties about these sets of queries, in particular, proved some complexity results about them. Furthermore, we considered their applications in vote elicitation, and in the so-called proportional representation used in Hong Kong Legislative Council Geographical Constituencies election.

616113.label: Project Objectives

616113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
616113.value: In the presence of energy crises and environmental concerns, public transport (PT) is often raised as a potential solution to mitigate such problems. It would be ideal if PT is financially sustainable without subsidy. Previous studies generally indicated that PT usage is positively related to urban development density. Hence, it is important to study the problem from an analytical perspective and ask more precisely what levels of urban density are required for what types of PT. Generally, PT takes on different forms, ranging from those with fixed-routes (FR) to those that are demand responsive (DR). Conceivably, the levels of patronage needed to financially sustain FR and DR services are different. It is valuable to ascertain for a city with a given development density and pattern, the types of PT that can achieve financial sustainability. Moreover, by integrating DR with FR services to improve the PT system as a whole, it may pave a way to attract higher PT patronage and introduce a paradigm shift in the modal choices of travelers, initiating a virtuous cycle. To bring this project into fruition, firstly, it is necessary to develop an analytical framework to model integrated FR and DR services. One issue intrinsic to DR services is to explicitly address the stochastic nature of demand, and devise an appropriate response strategy. To this end, we will draw upon the development of stochastic programs and corresponding solution strategies. Secondly, it is vital to relate the analyses of FR and DR services for different urban development densities. We envisage that corridor and spatially spread-out types of developments would have very different implications on FR and DR services. Thirdly, we will study the possibility of deploying evolutionary development strategies over time to bring up the PT modal share for regions with different development densities and patterns. The idea is to use DR services as a strategy to improve the quality of PT incrementally over time in order to prepare for the phasing-in of FR services, hence introducing regularity in service offering and at the same time achieving cost savings on a per-passenger basis. In summary, this project will draw upon recent advances in stochastic programming, both in formulation and solution procedure, and the connection between PT and land use planning. It will open up theoretically interesting, yet practically important issues in integrating the planning between urban development and financially sustainable PT. 隨著能源危機的出現和對環境保護的日益重視，大力發展公交被認為是緩解上述城市化問題的可行解決方案之一。不需要政府補貼的可持續公共交通則更為理想。研究普遍認為公交使用率與城市發展密度緊密相關。因此，有必要精確分析需要何種程度的城市密度來適用不同的公共交通方式。一般來說，公共交通有不同的表現形式，包括固定線路和需求響應型公交。顯然，維持這兩種服務經濟上可持續性的乘客上座率是不同的。對於一個給定發展密度和分佈形態的城市來說，明晰哪種公共交通方式具有經濟上的可持續性是十分有價值的。另外，通過整合固定線路和需求響應型公交來提高公交系統的服務，可以吸引更多乘客選擇公交，從而實現向公交出行方式的范式轉移，為形成良性循環鋪平道路。 為完成此項目，首先要建立分析框架，對集成的固定線路與需求響應型公交進行建模。對於需求響應型公交，關鍵問題是如何處理隨機交通需求和設計合適的的響應機制。為此，我們將運用隨機規劃的理論與方法來進行建模。其次，分析不同城市發展密度下的固定線路與響應型公交服務。不難想像交通走廊和空間上較為分散的城市發展形態需要不同類型的公交服務。再者，探討運用演化發展策略來逐步提高擁有不同發展密度與形態的地區的公交佔有率的可能性。基本思想是最初運用響應型公交來逐步提高公交服務品質，為引入固定型公交做準備，從而可以保持提供公交服務的規律性並同時達到單位乘客成本的最小化。 概括來說，該專案將運用隨機規劃建模和算法上的最新研究進展，分析公共交通與土地使用規劃之間的關係。該研究不僅會在理論上開闢新的課題，並且對整合城市發展規劃與經濟上可持續的公共交通規劃也具有實用價值。

616113.label: Realisation of objectives
616113.value: All three objectives have been achieved. 1. This project developed a framework to model integrated fixed-route (FR) and demand responsive (DR) public transport (PT) services under stochastic demand, and applied it for ferry service network design and rail-based network design. 2. This project studied the combinations of FR and DR-PT services under varying urban development densities and patterns, and analyzed their financial sustainability. The findings indicated that monocentric CBD may not be the best for FR services, whereas the approach of satellite town development, as adopted in Hong Kong, was. 3. This project studied deployment strategies of financially sustainable FR and DR-PT services for varying urban development densities and patterns. Depending on the existing levels of services and urban development densities, sometimes rail-led developments are better, and sometimes housing-led or density-led developments are better. So there is no one single type of development that is always the best. In other words, the initial conditions matter a lot in selecting the appropriate developing phasing.

616513.label: Realisation of objectives
616513.value: Audio fingerprinting is a method to represent a segment of audio content such as a song snippet or other spoken document by a fixed vector called audio fingerprint. In this research project, the PI treated an audio fingerprint as an exemplar of an audio segment and investigated adapting the current audio fingerprinting algorithm for creating audio fingerprints for acoustic units for exemplar-based automatic speech recognition (ASR). The audio fingerprinting algorithm first treats an audio segment as a sequence of images and makes use of image processing techniques to extract salient features from it which are supposed to be more resilient to noise. The features are the Wavelet coefficients on which a robust hashing method called min-hashing is performed to generate the fingerprint of the audio segment. In practice, there will be a large number of such audio exemplars (or audio fingerprints). To enable fast and efficient retrieval, locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) is used to organize the large database of min-hashed audio exemplars/fingerprints with various hash tables. The classification or retrieval decision is made by computing some distance measure through dynamic time warping (DTW) between the input audio fingerprint and all the stored audio fingerprints (which are also the audio exemplars now). In summary, the whole algorithm is designed to (1) improve the robustness of exemplar-based ASR through the use of the specific image processing techniques and the robust min-hashing method, and (2) classify or retrieve the best exemplar in the database by using LSH. As the original audio fingerprinting is not designed for ASR, every step in the original procedure had to be scrutinized and all the system settings and hyperparameters had to be re-investigated again. They included the size of audio snippets, window size, order of the Wavelet transforms, dimension of the min-hash value, number of bins and number of hash tables in the LSH database, the DTW distance metric, the choice of acoustic units, and so forth. As there were many parameters to investigate, the PI started with a comparatively small but noisy ASR task, the noisy Aurora2 digit classification. Digit classification was first tried as it is similar to the task of song retrieval for which audio fingerprinting has been shown effective. A noisy task was chosen because one of the issues the PI is investigating is robustness of the method against noise. The task was also small enough that the PI might explore the high-dimensional hyperparameter space for a good setup. Aurora2 is also a standard task and the PI may benchmark his results with others. It consists of clean utterances of continuous digits, as well as their noisy versions with additive noise or GSM filtering at different signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs). There are two training modes: clean training using only the clean data, and multi-condition training using both clean data and simulated noisy data. For comparison, the commonly used whole-digit hidden Markov models (HMMs) were constructed using the Aurora2 official configuration with 16 HMM states and 3 Gaussian mixtures per state. The HMM performance serves as a baseline for gauging the performance of our proposed method. First, the PI evaluated both HMM and the audio-fingerprint-based method with clean training --- that is, only clean utterances were used for training. It was found that the newly proposed exemplar-based ASR system using whole-digit models outperformed the traditional system based on HMM and reduced the digit classification error rate by ~50% on test data recorded by the same channel but with different types of noise, and ~37% on test data collected by a different channel. A more detailed examination of their performances at different SNRs confirm that the proposed method is robust to noise and outperforms HMM at SNRs of 5dB and 0dB, but is a bit worse than HMM at higher SNRs. Then the PI repeated the comparison by training both models with multi-condition training data. The new model now performs worse than HMM. The PI concludes that when the test data match training data (both are clean, or both are noisy), the new model does not perform as well as the traditional HMM. On the other hand, if they do not match (e.g., trained with clean data but tested with noisy data) then the new model performs much better than HMM. It means that the new model is more robust to unseen data and generalizes well, but is not as accurate as HMM in modeling the same data. The image processing technique and the hashing technique all try to smooth out the noise in the data. Although they are effective for applications such as audio retrieval, they may overdo for ASR which is a classification task that requires precise acoustic modeling. Thus, it is no surprise that when the PI further investigated the new model on Aurora2 continuous digit recognition, paving the way for large-vocabulary speech recognition, the results were again not as good as the performance of a conventional HMM system. Besides the reasons mentioned above, it is worth noting that performing recognition (not classification) with any exemplar-based system is more difficult than HMM decoding because it is not easy to perform decoding efficiently using exemplars which are segments with variable lengths as the duration of the segments also needs to be considered. More importantly, the PI believes that while song retrieval may not require precise audio fingerprints, ASR requires highly discriminative acoustic features. After investigating all the issues in our proposal objectives, the PI looked into ways to mitigate the problem. As the PI believes that the current feature extraction techniques, though producing robust features, over-smooth the features which become less discriminative for ASR, the PI spent the remaining time to search for better ways to represent the acoustic events, and the PI looked into GMM features as well as neural-net features. At that time, deep learning emerged and the PI also investigated how to derive features using deep neural networks (DNNs). Our investigation of GMM features instead led us to distinct triphone HMM modeling in which, each distinct triphone has its own HMM, under the HMM/DNN hybrid modeling framework. As a result, the distinct triphone models are more discriminative than the usual state-tied triphone models. As there can be a huge number of distinct triphones in a corpus (in the order of tens of thousands), the PI proposed a new modeling method called eigentriphone modeling. All distinct triphones are represented in the space spanned by a relatively small set of eigentriphones. The investigation of neural net features led us instead to an improved training method of DNN for ASR. We proposed the multi-task learning of DNN which produces better and more robust DNN posteriors. One may also think of a DNN as a model that ‘memorizes’ its training data. In that sense, it is a distributed representation of the input exemplars. Thus, it turns out a DNN may be a better exemplar-based model for ASR than the traditional exemplar-based acoustic models usually used in the ASR community. The PI believes further research should then be conducted using the DNN or other deep NN model such as LSTM.
