616513.label: Major findings and research outcome
616513.value: Inspired by the success of the audio fingerprinting method in large-scale song retrieval, this research project investigates a new way of performing exemplar-based automatic speech recognition (ASR) by creating audio fingerprints for acoustic units. The investigation was evaluated on the noisy Aurora2 digit classification and recognition tasks. It was found that if only clean training data were used, our newly proposed exemplar-based ASR system using whole-digit models outperformed traditional system based on hidden Markov models (HMM) and reduced the digit classification error rate by ~50% on test data recorded by the same channel but with different types of noise, and ~37% on test data collected by a different channel. The results confirm that our proposed method is robust to noise. However, the method was not as good as an HMM-based system that was trained using multi-condition training. We also implemented the method for continuous digit recognition paving the way for large-vocabulary speech recognition, but the results were again not as good as the performance of a conventional HMM system. One reason for the worse results of the new approach is that, as typical of any exemplar-based system, it is not easy to perform decoding efficiently using exemplars which are segments with variable lengths as the duration of the segments also needs to be considered. Another plausible reason is that while song retrieval may not require precise audio fingerprints, ASR requires highly discriminative acoustic features. Thus, while we were implementing our new exemplar-based system, we also investigated better ways to represent the acoustic events, and we looked into GMM features as well as neural-net features. Our investigation of GMM features instead led us to distinct triphone HMM modeling in which, each distinct triphone has its own HMM. As a result, the distinct triphone models are more discriminative than the usual state-tied triphone models. As there can be a huge number of distinct triphones in a corpus (in the order of tens of thousands), we proposed a new modeling method called eigentriphone modeling. All distinct triphones are represented in the space spanned by a relatively small set of eigentriphones (conference papers #2 and 4). The investigation of neural net features led us instead to an improved training method of deep neural network (DNN) for ASR. We proposed the multi-task learning of DNN (journal paper #1, and conference papers #1, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8) which produces better and more robust DNN posteriors.

616513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
616513.value: In the last decade, deep learning has become the most prominent machine learning technique and has found success in many areas of artificial intelligence including the area of automatic speech recognition (ASR). In some sense, a deep neural network (DNN) can be thought of as a distributed representation of an exemplar-based system: the training data (exemplars) are stored in a DNN in the form of a set of distributed weights. During decoding, a testing acoustic vector is compared with the exemplars stored in the DNN and produces a posterior score for each acoustic unit. Thus, further research should be directed to how to apply deep learning to represent the acoustic data or exemplars for ASR. For example, one direction is to train better acoustic DNNs (including the use of recurrent neural networks and convolutional neural networks). Another direction is to train end-to-end models for ASR in the form of an encoder-decoder framework that takes the acoustic events as inputs, encodes them, and directly produces the recognized words in a decoder using the properly encoded inputs.

616513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
616513.value: Inspired by the success of the audio fingerprinting method in large-scale song retrieval, this research project investigated a new way of performing exemplar-based automatic speech recognition (ASR) by treating spoken utterances as sequences of images and employing image processing techniques to create audio fingerprints for acoustic units as their exemplars. The investigation was evaluated on the noisy Aurora2 digit classification and recognition tasks. On digit classification under mismatched conditions when only clean data are used for training but both clean and noisy data are used for testing, the proposed method outperforms conventional hidden Markov modeling (HMM) method by cutting the word error rates by almost half. However, when noisy data that are similar to the noisy testing data are also used for training, the proposed method does not perform as well as the conventional HMM. It is also found that the proposed method suffers from the same problems as exhibited by typical exemplar-based ASR methods and is outperformed by conventional HMM on continuous digit recognition. The research sheds light on the strength and weakness of the audio fingerprinting approach for exemplar-based automatic speech recognition.

616613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
616613.value: Facing rising concerns over the environment and depleting oil reserves, the transportation industry is in active development of sustainable mobility systems. Car sharing (CS) is an operations model that allows multiple drivers to access a fleet of cars deployed within a service region on demand. Through shared usage, CS has the flexibility to address individual users’ mobility needs, while enabling enhanced vehicle utilization and economies of scale. Studies have shown that well-managed CS systems can help reduce car ownership. In the emerging CS industry, one-way services are gaining popularity relative to more traditional two-way services. One-way services provide users the flexibility to pick up and return cars at different locations. This enables CS services to cover a broader range of mobility needs. However, this model brings significant operational complexities, because flows of cars across zones of the service area will naturally be unbalanced, i.e., certain zones will experience shortages of cars, while others will see surpluses. To deliver high service levels, cars must be repositioned to zones with surplus stock to those in shortage. However, because cars are individual units of transport requiring drivers to be moved, they are naturally costly to reposition, unlike other transportation equipment such as rail cars and cargo containers. In this proposal, we propose to use pricing (surcharge) mechanisms to induce users to reposition cars. The major challenge is to derive the optimal dynamic temporal and spatial pricing policy that induces balanced flow, while ensuring high quality and service and maximizes revenue for the CS operator. In our proposed research, we take into account travelers’ mode and destination choice behavior and their responses to pricing. Our proposed models incorporate traveler behavior, and the dynamic interactions between demand and service units (cars) in a closed queueing system, by utilizing techniques from mathematical programming, transportation demand modeling, revenue management and stochastic analysis. Our proposed models are well-grounded theoretically and will provide practical methodologies and insights supporting pricing and operational control of one-way CS systems for practitioners. 面對環境和能源問題，可持續的交通系統正在積極發展。汽車共享允許多個駕駛者按需求使用服務區域內的車隊。汽車共享具有很大的靈活性，可滿足個別用戶的交通需求，同時能夠提高車輛的使用率。有研究表明，汽車共享有助減少汽車數量。 單向汽車共享服務正日益普及。相對較傳統的雙向服務，單向服務容許用戶靈活地選擇使用汽車的起點和終點。然而，這種模式帶來了顯著的複雜性，由於跨區域汽車流量的失衡，車輛在某些區域會出現短缺，而其他區將出現過多。然而，將車輛移動並重新佈置的成本很昂貴。在這項研究，我們建議使用定價機制，誘使用戶流量平衡，同時確保高品質和服務。 在我們所提出的研究中，我們考慮到旅客的行為模式和目標的選擇和他們的反應來定價。我們提出的模型包括旅客行為，需求和服務單位（汽車）在一個封閉的排隊系統之間的動態相互作用，利用數學規劃，交通需求模型，收益管理和隨機分析的理論。我們將提供一些實用的方法幫助業界管理單向汽車共享服務的定價和操作。

616613.label: Major findings and research outcome
616613.value: Our first key research activity was studying the service region design problem for free floating car sharing services. Car sharing firms Car2go and Drivenow/Reachnow have been gaining traction with their on-demand, free-floating model of car sharing. Unlike conventional station-based car sharing models (e.g., ZipCar), customers are free to start and end their rental trips anywhere within a defined service region in the city, with or without advance reservations. We studied the key planning question in this novel business model, namely, how to design the service region to offer extensive geographical coverage at competitive costs. In the free-floating model, demand is spatially unbalanced, due to a high proportion of one-way trips. To effectively match fleet supply with time-varying demand, the service region must be carefully designed with demand imbalance and repositioning needs in mind. We developed a practical data-driven optimization framework for the problem using distributionally-robust optimization, to ensure robustness with respect to consumers’ uncertain adoption behavior. Through analyzing this problem, we also gained insight into operations issues regarding spatial and temporal balance of car sharing demand. Calibrating the model to Car2go's operations data, we found that the car sharing service's profitability is highly sensitive to the choice of the service region. Furthermore, optimal deployment of free-floating car sharing could deliver significant environmental benefits by converting individually-owned cars into shared fleets of cleaner vehicles (e.g., electric vehicles). Our second research activity was studying the use of spatial dynamic pricing as a lever for mitigating demand imbalance. Car sharing companies, such as Drivenow/Reachnow, have been using the strategy of dynamic two-tier pricing to balance the flow of vehicles spatially. We studied the problem of optimally determining when and where to apply a surcharge on the service. Based on approximate dynamic programming, we developed a computationally-efficient algorithm for the pricing problem. Computational experiments suggested that this approach is effective, particularly, it only requires surcharges to be applied based on the origin of a trip, but not the destination, making the approach easier to apply in practice.

616613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
616613.value: The dynamic pricing problem was initially developed as part of a PhD thesis by Guangrui Ma, who graduated in 2014. Extending this work, we have solidified and enhanced the computational aspect of the algorithms and numerical experiments.

616613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
616613.value: A trend in smart city development is the rise of vehicle sharing businesses, along with the emerging sharing economy in recent years. Passenger cars make a prime candidate for sharing business models because of their low utilization rates, high fixed costs to own, and relatively low variable costs to operate. The free-floating operations model has particularly gained much attention, due to the flexibility to pick up and drop off vehicles at any location. The operations of free-float systems are challenging to manage. A key strategic planning task in free-float vehicle sharing systems is to determine the service region. On the one hand, expanding geographical coverage makes the service more attractive and encourages adoption. On the other hand, doing so entails significant operational challenges, such as the repositioning of cars to ensure availability under unbalanced demand. Our research developed data-driven methodologies to tackle key planning and operations problems for one-way, free-floating vehicle sharing systems, particularly, for the problems of service region planning and dynamic pricing to maintain high availability of service while maximizing profit. Computational experiments using actual operations data from car sharing companies concluded that our algorithms could lead to significant gains in operations efficiency for car sharing systems.

616713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
616713.value: Wireless communications is an extremely important technology which has progressed rapidly over the past decade. A main stimulant has been the development of extremely popular broadband wireless-equipped consumer products (e.g., smartphones), as well as the evolution of high-rate wireless standards (e.g., 3G/4G and Wi-Fi), providing consumers with near-ubiquitous access to a plethora of wireless data services and applications. The huge recent progress has been driven to a large extent by the advent of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technology. MIMO has now matured to the point of being incorporated into most emerging broadband wireless industry standards and products. It has become well-known however, that in real-world multi-user environments, the advantages of MIMO are strongly diminished due to inter-cell interference; a limitation that will only become more significant in the future as the density of wireless networks inevitably increase in order to keep up with strong and rising user demands. This has led researchers to look at alternative engineering strategies for supporting the rising needs of tomorrow's wireless networks. This project aims to push forward an exciting and revolutionary new paradigm, referred to as Massive MIMO, which can potentially overcome the challenges faced by contemporary MIMO, and offers a very promising solution for the future. The ultimate vision, put forward in recent breakthrough work at Bell Laboratories, is to equip base-stations with a large number of antennas (say, hundreds) and to simultaneously serve a much smaller number of users. Contrary to intuition, this can potentially overcome major limitations of conventional MIMO systems, whilst providing a significant boost in spectral efficiency and orders of magnitude savings in transmission power. Moreover, it was predicted that these gains could be achieved with very simple linear processing! The concept of Massive MIMO thus presents major opportunities and opens up a completely new design paradigm for wireless communications research and development. This area, however, is still in its infancy, and much remains to be done before the promised gains of Massive MIMO may be realized in practice. Here we outline a plan for characterizing the fundamental information-theoretic limits of Massive MIMO systems, relaxing critical assumptions which are present in most existing early contributions, to provide a more realistic characterization of the achievable performance gains. We also provide a plan to develop novel signal processing strategies for overcoming key practical challenges posed by the Massive MIMO paradigm, focusing on the design of channel estimation strategies and optimized transceivers. 在过去十年中飞速发展的无线通信技术是一项极其重要的技术。目前非常受欢迎的装备有宽带无线功能的消费产品(比如智能手机)以及高速率无线标准(比如3G/4G和Wi-Fi)的发展是无线通信技术发展的一个重要催化剂。它们使消费者可以几乎全方位地接入广泛覆盖的无线数据服务和应用。 多输入多输出技术的出现在很大程度上促使了无线通信技术近来的巨大发展。多输入多输出技术已趋于成熟，并且被大多数新兴的宽带无线工业标准和产品所采用。然而众所周知的是，在实际多用户环境中，由于蜂窝间的干扰，多输入多输出技术的优势大大削减；为了跟上急速增长的用户需求，今后无线网络密度的增长在所难免，而这个局限性只会变得更加严重。这促使了研究人员去研究替代的工程策略，以支持未来无线网络日益增长的需求。 这个项目旨在提出一个令人激动和有革命性的新模式，这就是大规模多输入多输出系统。它有潜力能克服现在大规模多输入多输出技术所面临的挑战，并为未来提供一个非常有希望的解决方案。由贝尔实验室最新突破成果提出的终极目标是，给基站装上很多根天线（比如几百根）并同时服务数量少的多的用户。与直觉相反，这样很有可能可以克服传统多输入多输出系统的主要不足之处，并在频谱效率和节省传输功率方面带来显著提高。 更进一步的是，这些增益可以通过非常简单的线性处理获取。因此大规模多输入多输出的概念带来了非常大的机会。它为无线通信的研究与开发开创了一个全新的设计模型。 但是，这个领域仍然处于初期研究阶段。 在这些大规模多输入多输出技术所带来的好处能在实际中实现之前，有很多研究工作需要完成。 在这里，我们概述了我们的研究规划，包括刻画大规模多输入多输出系统的基础信息理论极限，放宽在现有理论贡献中的一些严格假设，以提供一个对能达到的性能增益的更加实际的刻画。我们也提出了一项计划来开发新型信号处理技术，以克服大规模多输入多输出模式带来的关键的实际应用难点, 这将集中在信道估计策略和最佳无线电收发机的设计上。

616713.label: Realisation of objectives
616713.value: All key objectives have been successfully met. The project has produced numerous key contributions, and has led to 6 journal and 2 conference publications, all in leading IEEE journals or conference proceedings. Objective 1: This substantial objective was aimed at developing a fundamental information-theoretic framework for massive MIMO systems, incorporating practical effects which arise in the corresponding communication channels. The objective has been extensively addressed, yielding numerous important contributions, as we now summarize. In [Journal Paper 1], we developed a framework to characterize the performance limits of massive MIMO communication channels under slow fading conditions. This problem was addressed by introducing a new statistical framework for computing upper and lower bounds on the information theoretic capacity with linear transmission methods, in addition to accurate closed form approximations. The framework accounted for practical effects caused by interference between geographically dispersed cells, and for distributed positioning of users. This work was extended in [Conference Paper 2] to incorporate the realistic effects of channel estimation, which is a key practical issue in massive MIMO systems. In [Journal Paper 2], we addressed a different but important problem, aimed at the design and analysis of signal detection strategies in massive MIMO cognitive radio networks. In particular, [Journal Paper 2] proposed an appropriate generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT) based framework, with the resulting test statistic involving the ratio of the determinant to the trace of the covariance matrix of the received samples. A statistical analysis of this test statistic was conducted for high dimensional (massive) MIMO systems, and the design of an appropriate detection threshold was proposed. This analysis was conducted by adopting new analytical methodologies, using ideas from random matrix theory. Importantly, this analysis provided the framework for optimization and selection of an appropriate detection threshold that did not require accurate channel estimation, and allowed for the design of very simple detection rules for identifying massive MIMO signals in the presence of receiver noise. Information-theoretic performance analysis tools were also developed to account for different statistical channel characteristics of relevance to massive MIMO systems, including correlation and line-of-sight ([Journal Paper 4]), channel matrices with unbalanced variances ([Journal Paper 5]), and channel matrices with unbalanced powers in real and imaginary channel components ([Journal Paper 6]). Interesting theoretical equivalences were also established between the channels with interference (an important property of massive MIMO systems) and physical layer security ([Journal Paper 3]). Objective 2: This objective aimed to investigate the performance and feasibility of massive MIMO systems under realistic operating conditions. The objective has been extensively addressed, with the results reported in numerous publications. In [Journal Paper 1] and [Journal Paper 2], the analytical frameworks presented were used to investigate the performance of various massive MIMO communication and signal detection technologies (including those proposed by us, as outlined below in response to Objective 3) under a range of conditions. The analysis was conducted through both mathematical analysis and computer simulations. In [Journal Paper 1], and studied further in [Conference Paper 2], the proposed transmission techniques were compared with exhaustive joint network optimization methods (which are infeasible for any realistic system), and shown to achieve particularly competitive performance. More specifically, they were shown to yield almost negligible performance loss in sum rate, with substantially lower complexity. Thus, this analysis helped to suggest our proposed method as a feasible solution in practice when compared with the (typically infeasible) theoretically optimal method. For the novel detection schemes presented in [Journal Paper 2], the detection performance was evaluated based on both finite- and infinite-dimensional random matrix theory. The simple threshold design rules documented therein were demonstrated to yield high accuracy, and thus serve as useful detection strategies in practice. In addition, we investigated the performance of different important transceiver techniques in massive MIMO systems, under relevant channel fading conditions. This includes the performance analysis of MIMO MRC transceivers in correlated-Rician fading [Journal paper 4] and unbalanced-variance channels [Journal Paper 5], and under so-called Hoyt-faded conditions [Journal Paper 6]. The practical effect of carrier-frequency offsets (CFOs) for multi-carrier systems were also characterized in detail in [Conference Paper 1]. In terms of feasibility, we studied conditions on the fading statistics (correlation, line-of-sight, channel power heterogeneity, user positions, etc.), in order to achieve significant performance gains, providing insight for practical system design. Objective 3: This objective aimed to develop signal processing strategies for massive MIMO systems, considering channel estimation and transceiver techniques in particular. This objective has also been successfully addressed. In [Journal Paper 1], optimized power allocation techniques were devised based on long-term statistical channel information, which were of low complexity and simple to implement. In particular, three different strategies were proposed, based on optimizing an approximation to the sum capacity, as well as upper and lower bounds. It was found that the optimization based on the capacity approximation yielded the best sum rate performance. Moreover, this method was compared with the (impractical) joint power optimization methods, and showed to yield almost the same performance. Critically, this was achieved with little coordination between network base stations, but rather, with operating the proposed power allocation method in concert with a simple scheduling algorithm. In [Conference Paper 2], we proposed new channel estimation methods for massive MIMO systems by determining the optimal pilot length to employ, to maximize the sum rate per cell. This led to important and rather unintuitive conclusions, suggesting that for massive MIMO systems with large numbers of base station antennas, one should typically adopt pilot lengths which exceed the minimum length required to achieved orthogonality, with this optimal choice being dependent on the pilot reuse factor incorporated across neighboring communication cells. In terms of signal detection in massive MIMO systems, in [Journal Paper 2], the analytical framework developed therein was employed to design new signal detection strategies, by utilizing concepts from finite-dimensional and asymptotic random matrix theory. Specifically, simple detection thresholds were proposed for the GLRT that were shown to be accurate, and were tailored to settings encountered in massive MIMO applications, in which the signals to detect are assumed to be of full rank.

616713.label: Major findings and research outcome
616713.value: Below is a brief summary of some the major contributions in this project: (Note that [Journal Paper 3] is excluded due to space limitations): [Journal Paper 1 and Conference Paper 2]: These contributions derived expressions for the sum-rate of massive MIMO systems and proposed optimal power allocation and channel estimation strategies. Our proposed power allocation strategies were shown to bring considerable gains over equal power allocation for practical antenna configurations. For the channel estimation problem, we obtained the optimal pilot length to maximize the sum rate per cell. As an important practical result, we found that the optimal pilot length can lie above the minimum feasible value, and the gains brought by the additional training diminish as the reuse factor grows. [Journal Paper 2]: This work considered the problem of signal detection of primary user signals by a secondary user receiver in large-dimensional MIMO cognitive radio networks. The optimal detector was analyzed by deriving the moments of the generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT) statistic, yielding approximations for the false alarm and detection probabilities. We showed that the normalized GLRT statistic converges in distribution to a Gaussian random variable when the number of antennas and observations grow large at the same rate. For different practical system configurations, we obtained simple design rules for the detection threshold which demonstrated excellent performance. [Journal Paper 4]: This work derived the outage probability for MIMO maximum-ratio combining (MIMO-MRC) systems in Rician fading channels with both transmit and receive correlation. We demonstrated that for a rank-1 line-of-sight (LoS) path, the interaction with the correlation matrices may yield improved or degraded performance. The relative effect depends largely on the geometric alignment of the LoS path with the eigenvectors of the correlation matrices. Our results, in general, provided novel practical insight into how the mutual interactions of LoS and spatial correlation impacts the performance of MIMO-MRC systems. [Journal Papers 5 and 6]: These studies presented expressions for the maximum eigenvalue distribution of two important, but very non-classical and rarely studied, MIMO channels models: “Hoyt” channels and channels with arbitrary variance profiles. Both arise in contemporary MIMO systems. By adopting the new distributional results, we studied the capacity of the different channel models. We found, for example, that a variance imbalance (e.g., due to spatially-distributed nodes) can lead to a significant capacity loss, providing insight for the design of distributed communication systems.

616713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
616713.value: There are various avenues for further development; here we focus on one such direction. While the theoretical tools we have derived for correlated-Rician and Hoyt channel models are general (i.e., applying for both massive and conventional MIMO settings), our current results for channels with arbitrary variance profiles are restricted to dual-antenna configurations. As discussed in detail in [Journal Paper 6], this model presents a substantial deviation from those usually encountered in random matrix theory, since certain statistical “symmetry” properties are lost. This greatly complicates the analysis. Even for the simplest dual-antenna case, the analysis was very difficult and required the introduction of new analytical tools. An important open problem is to generalize these results to arbitrary antenna numbers, to make them applicable to generic massive MIMO systems with arbitrarily distributed nodes. New methods will be required, since the tools we developed for the dual-antenna case do not extend naturally (we gave much thought to this extension during the project). A possible strategy will be to decompose the arbitrary-variance channel as a sum of Wishart matrices, and to leverage the “condition and average” approach applied for Hoyt channels in [Journal Paper 5]. Developments along these lines requires careful consideration however.

616713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
616713.value: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna communication systems, which employ transmit and receive antenna arrays, are very important in modern wireless communication technologies, from Wi-Fi to cellular networks. Very recently, “massive’” MIMO techniques (which employ large antenna arrays) are attracting considerable attention as a means of achieving unprecedented capacity and power efficiency gains in next generation wireless systems and applications. For such systems, this project has presented new theoretical tools for characterizing the achievable capacity limits, under different scenarios and environmental conditions. We have proposed novel optimized communication technologies for maximizing performance of massive MIMO systems, such as designing novel and efficient ways for power control and for estimating the wireless channel. The new analytical theories and methods which we have proposed may be helpful for communication engineers and may facilitate the design of subsequent, more advanced communication technologies in the context of next and future generation systems.

616813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
616813.value: In the past few years, the rapid growth of the ultra-thin, ultra-light weight portable mobile devices market, like iPhones and android phones, drive the great demand of system-on-a-chip (SoC) design with increasing number of systems integrated onto a single chip. In order to prolong the battery life of the portable devices, the power supply voltages of some of the logic circuits need to scale down to sub-threshold or near the threshold voltage of the transistor to reduce the power consumption of the SoC, especially in idling and standby mode. Therefore, there is an urgent need to provide a tunable supply voltage for very low-power VLSI circuit down to 0.5V in future SoC design. The design and implementation of the required power management unit which control the supply voltages of different components inside the SoC becomes very challenging. Low-dropout linear regulator (LDO) is one of key building blocks of the power management unit. Nowadays, there are more than 20 LDOs inside the power management unit to provide different supply voltages to various components inside the SoC. The power efficiency, dropout voltage, transient response time, and chip area are the major concerns in designing the LDO. With down to 0.5-V supply voltage, the conventional LDO with analog feedback control loop will not function very well. In addition, in the future SoC design, advanced CMOS technologies below 65nm will be used and these short-channel transistors make analog circuit design very difficult. Therefore, digital LDO have been proposed in the recent years to target for this problem. Digital LDO is a LDO with a digital controlled loop instead of the analog controlled loop used in the conventional LDO. However, existing digital LDOs are not as well-developed as the analog LDOs and the performance of these digital LDOs are not optimized. One of the major issues of the existing digital LDO is the slow transient response time and large quiescent current consumption. Due to the slow transient response, the use of digital LDO in power management circuits is limited. Thus the objective of this proposal is to develop a low-power fast-transient digital LDO for SoC applications. The focus will be on how to speed up the transient response of the digital LDO without using large quiescent current. Other issues related to digital LDO performance such as stability, minimum dropout voltage, startup sequence, short-circuit protection, chip area consumption, etc. will also be explored in this project. 近年來，超薄、超輕的移動手持通訊設備，譬如蘋果和安卓智能手機市場的日益快速發展，極大拉動了片上系統設計（SoC）的需求，即將更多的系統集成在一塊芯片之上。在各種移動手持設備中，為延長電池的續航時間，其對內部邏輯電路的供電電壓往往要降至晶體管鄰近閾值電壓或更低的亞閾值區，特別是在休眠或待機模式下，以降低不必要的電路功耗。因此，近來的SoC設計對於能為超大規模集成電路提供低至0.5V可調電壓的電源管理芯片有急切的需求。 而設計並實現適應這一為SoC多個不同模塊供電的電源管理芯片要面臨很大的難度。在應用於該背景下的電源管理中，低壓差線性穩壓器（LDO）往往是關鍵的一環。正如在已推出的SoC中所展示的，其內部一般包含多餘20個LDO，以實現不同模塊的電壓轉換和調節。LDO發展已久，其設計往往要考慮多個要素，諸如能量轉換效率、輸入-輸出壓差、瞬態響應時間和芯片面積等等。然而，當其供電電壓低至0.5V時，傳統的依賴模擬電路反饋控制環路的設計技術已不再適用；而且由於低至65納米的CMOS工藝應用於SoC電源管理芯片設計，其短溝道帶來的各種副作用使得模擬電路設計更為困難。因此，近年來數字LDO應運而生，並通過數字控制環路實現傳統模擬LDO設計中模擬控制環路的功能。然而，數字LDO的發展並不如傳統模擬LDO，主要因為目前的設計偏注功能實現而性能並未得到優化。目前數字LDO性能中最嚴重的問題當屬慢瞬態響應時間和大靜態電流損耗。由於其瞬態響應很慢，數字LDO在電源管理芯片中的使用備受限制。為突破該限制，本項目旨在研發面向SoC供電的低功耗快瞬態的數字LDO，其研究重點在於如何低靜態功耗電流下實現快速的瞬態響應。此外，本項目亦將探討數字LDO設計中諸如穩定性，最小壓差，啟動順序，短路保護，芯片面積等諸多重要問題。

616813.label: Realisation of objectives
616813.value: This project is related to the development of a low-power fast-transient digital low-dropout regulator (D-LDO) for system-on-a-chip (SoC) application. In order to create a D-LDO simultaneous possessing low-power and fast-transient characteristics, three objectives needed to be addressed. For the first objective, since the output voltage of the D-LDO is an analog voltage, an analog-to-digital converter (ADC) is needed to convert the analog voltage to a digital signal before the feedback signal can be processed by the digital controller inside the D-LDO. After a series of investigations, to balance the power, speed and accuracy of the regulator, a single-bit asynchronous clocked comparator has been developed and used in the final design. In objective 2, a novel row-column-bit 3-dimensional (3D) power stage with an asynchronous multi-step switching scheme has been developed to achieve a fast load transient response time in the nanosecond range. A PCT international patent is pending. In objective 3, a complete low-power fast-transient D-LDO has been designed, fabricated and characterized. Measurement results show that its figure-of-merit is the best ever reported for a D-LDO with a large load current range of 500 mA.

616813.label: Major findings and research outcome
616813.value: The D-LDO is a newly developed dc-dc converter topology whose research started less than 10 years ago. Early D-LDO designs were not optimized and the overall performance was not as good as the conventional LDO in terms of output current resolution, transient response and power consumption. In particular, the performance in transient response and power consumption contradict each other. Some low-power D-LDOs have very slow response times while others have fast transient response but with very large quiescent current consumption. Therefore, the main goal of this project is to develop a D-LDO which has fast transient response and low power consumption at the same time. In this project, we proposed a row-column-bit 3-dimensional (3D) power stage multi-step switching scheme to speed up the response time. When there is a load transient or line transient, the power transistors in the power stage can be turned on bit-by-bit, column-by-column or row-by-row, depending on the load or supply variation, to enhance the response time. The first version of the D-LDO with an excellent figure-of-merit (the best figure-of-merit ever reported) was published in 2015 ESSCIRC [C2]. An improved D-LDO design with better boundary control was published in 2015 IEEE CICC [C3]. Both are top-tier international solid-state circuit design conferences. Part of the analysis of the 3-D Power Stage was published in 2016 APCCAS [C4]. Due to the long review process, the journal paper [J1] discussing the detailed design issues and considerations of the 3-D power stage D-LDO is just accepted for publication. Note that this paper is the same as the [J1] in the last report and the title of the paper has been changed during the peer review process. It is well known that power supply rejection (PSR) is one of the serious problems of the D-LDO. To address this issue, we proposed and developed an inverter-based LDO which can be shunted with the D-LDO to enhance the overall PSR capability. We are the first to use the inverter-based amplifier to implement an LDO. The study of the PSR began in the early stage of the research and the analytical study of PSR was published in 2014 IEEE MWCCAS [C1]. The final design of the inverted-based LDO achieving the best PSR capability at the lowest supply voltage of 0.2 V was published in 2017 IEEE ISSCC [C5], the most prestigious solid-state circuits conference in the world.

616813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
616813.value: In this project, the contradictory performance of low-power consumption and fast-transient response of the D-LDO has been addressed and a solution has been developed. However, as mentioned before, the D-LDO is a newly developed dc-dc converter topology and other fundamental issues need to be addressed. Therefore, the D-LDO is currently limited to certain applications. One of unresolved issues with the D-LDO is that the ripple voltage appears at the output of the D-LDO. Some of the ideas generated during the inverter-based LDO design may help address this issue.

616813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
616813.value: This project is related to the development of a digitally-controlled low-dropout regulator (D-LDO). The D-LDO is a new type of low-dropout linear regulator (LDO) in which a digital feedback control loop is used to regulate the output voltage instead of the analog feedback control loop in conventional LDO design. With the development of advanced CMOS technology, when the supply voltage of an integrated circuit (IC) chips drops to 0.5 V, the D-LDO can offer several potential advantages over the conventional LDO, including low sensitivity to noise, low temperature and process variations, and easy portability to other processes. However, existing D-LDO designs cannot achieve a fast transient response without significantly increasing the quiescent power consumption. In this project, this contradictory performance of low-power consumption and fast transient response of the D-LDO has been resolved. A low-power fast-transient D-LDO has been developed which can deliver 500 mA output current and achieve nanosecond response time with only 0.3 mW quiescent power consumption.

617113.label: Project Title(Chinese)
617113.value: 基於進化算法的可重構天線設計方法

617113.label: Project Objectives
617113.value: Optimization Approach: We will apply optimization algorithms to aid the design of reconfigurable antennas. We will focus on minimizing the geometric changes required in the reconfigurable antennas and minimize the number of switches that are required when reconfiguring the antenna. Multi-Port designs: In this objective we will use the results of the first objective to design reconfigurable multi-port antennas. We will initially aim for wifi and mobile phone applications and prototype the antennas to provide experimental verification of the results. Other wireless applications will later be investigated.

We will initially aim for wifi and mobile phone applications and prototype the antennas to provide experimental verification of the results. Other wireless applications will later be investigated.

617113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
617113.value: 無線通訊技術已經成為社會和生產中很多重要資訊技術的基礎。為了應對不同應用領域中的需要，針對不同頻段的多種無線通訊技術和標準已經被設計和開發出來。隨著無線通訊的各種應用之間結合得越來越緊密，能夠支持多項通信標準成為對無線通訊設備的一個重要要求。設計這類通信設備的難點在於電池使用時間、設備尺寸、基帶電路的複雜度、射頻前端的成本、互通性、和天線。而且將來可能應用的智慧無線電技術也將會使設計難度更加大。 在這份研究提案中，我們將研究能夠用於多通信標準設備的天線的設計。此種天線的主要設計難度在於要支持多個不同頻帶和不同頻寬。 現有的設計方案是為各頻帶設計獨立的天線，或者通過設計多通帶/寬頻天線來覆蓋所有的頻率範圍。但是用這兩種方法設計的天線很難滿足實際物理尺寸要求。另外一種方法是使用可重構天線，通過射頻開關原件改變天線的電氣特性，從而達到充分利用天線尺寸的目的。 通過使用新穎的可重構設計技術，科研人員過去已經提出了多種不同的可重構天線以適應各種特殊需求。 但是相比于傳統天線的設計，可重構天線的設計受到諸多因素的限制，相比之下非常複雜。因此每種可重構天線的設計都與其他的完全不同，並且需要針對性的特殊設計。 在這份研究提案中，我們將研究一種系統化的、通用的可重構天線的設計方法。我們將研究優化演算法（如基因演算法）能否協助可重構天線的設計。通過在天線設計流程中運用優化理論和算法，我們希望儘量降低射頻開關原件的數量，並且同時優化天線的性能。該方法的難點在於需要同時達到多個優化目標，因此將需要開發高效的方法來簡化優化算法。如果此項研究成功，可重構天線將得到更加廣泛的應用，對各通信設備廠商將會很有利。

617113.label: Realisation of objectives
617113.value: All objectives have been completed during the course of this research project. To meet the first objective we have developed new optimization techniques and methods. In particular we have developed an efficient approach to computing the electromagnetic properties of pixel antennas that is based on a technique which we refer to as the internal multi-port method (IMPM) [2]. This method is demonstrated to reduce computational load by around 80x as compared to conventional approaches based on full electromagnetic solvers. In addition we have performed optimization of reconfigurable antennas with the constraint that the minimum number of switches need to be utilized [2]. In [2] we have also presented single band and dual band antenna designs using this approach which compare favorably to previous work. We have also extended the IMPM technique to include the optimization of radiation patterns and this is detailed in [4] and conference paper [2] for a beam steerable antenna based on a reconfigurable pixel design. The optimization of radiation patterns is also computationally heavy and the use of the IMPM technique reduces optimization time from hours to seconds. The second objective has also been addressed and a reconfigurable MIMO optimization approach is described in the conference paper [1]. This demonstrates that the isolation requirement between ports can also be incorporated into the optimization process using the IMPM approach devised in objective 1. We have also devised a reconfigurable MIMO antenna that is dualband. In this approach special isolation structures have been incorporated into the design that are dual band. Finally in [3] we were able to simplify the design in [1] to arrive at dual-band multiport MIMO antenna for WiFi applications.

617113.label: Major findings and research outcome
617113.value: An important outcome of this research has been the development and refinement of a technique which we refer to as the Internal Multi-Port Method (IMPM) which we have detailed in journal papers [2,4] as well as conference paper [2]. This technique allows the optimization of pixel antennas to be performed efficiently and 80x faster than methods based on full electromagnetic solvers but with the same accuracy. It allows us top optimize antennas with both impedance and pattern constraints. Another important outcome is the pixel design detailed in journal paper [4] and conference paper [2]. These unique designs have demonstrated that a planar pixel design can be found which can beam steer. The uniqueness of the design is that it is thin (1 mm) while allowing beam steering ranges of +/- 30 degrees. The final important contribution is the extension of the work to multiport antennas. In particular a pixel optimization approach is demonstrated that incorporates isolation between ports. These designs have then inspired MIMO designs suitable for WiFi as described in journal papers [1] and [3].

617113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
617113.value: The potential for further research is significant. One important area is the development of optimization algorithms that perform better than genetic algorithms, In particular the use of IMPM with the pixel approach allows compact expressions for the antenna characteristics to be written and these could be used to inspire new approaches to the optimization process. Not only would they be more computationally efficient but they may also lead to better solutions that are close to the global optimum.

617113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
617113.value: The research outcome of this research has been the development of a design and optimization technique that can create new antennas for wireless communications that are more compact with enhanced performance. In addition the designs can meet the stringent requirements of modern wireless communication antennas such as multiband and multiport operation. In addition they can also meet the requirements of future 5G systems based on mm-cellular by allowing beamsteering high gain antennas to be created that are also low profile and compact.

617213.label: Project Title(Chinese)
617213.value: 能量群樁的三維離心模型試驗和數值模擬研究

617213.label: Project Objectives
617213.value: Determine the effects of temperature on the mechanical behaviour and properties of saturated, anisotropically consolidated, granular as well as fined-grained soils under drained and undrained conditions using temperature-controlled triaxial apparatus and oedometer; Extend an existing thermoelastic-thermoplastic constitutive model (ACMEG-T) to account for anisotropy and implement it in the finite element code ABAQUS; Conduct systematic three-dimensional centrifuge model tests to investigate the thermal-mechanical interaction among energy piles within a group and the influence of pile spacings; Carry out three-dimensional numerical back-analysis of centrifuge model tests and validate existing and any newly extended constitutive models.

617213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
617213.value: 目前，人類對能源的需求持續增加。統計資料表明，在過去的30年裡，25%的世界能源消耗被用建築物的空間供暖。部分發達國家已經轉而使用可再生能源，而能源地下結構是一個降低空間供暖成本的可行方案。能源地下結構的原理是基於以下事實：在地表10米以下，溫度在一年內保持相對穩定，因此地層可以被視為一種可再生的儲熱介質。在炎熱的夏季，通過使用熱泵可以將地表建築的熱量體泵入能源地下結構比如能源樁中，並將熱量存儲在地層中。而在寒冷的冬季，儲存的熱量可以被提取出來回到建築物中用於空間供暖。報導顯示，相較於傳統的加熱與冷卻系統，能源樁的使用能夠降低66%的能源消耗，並減少50%的二氧化碳排放。儘管能源樁已經有超過20年的歷史，其設計方法依然基於經驗，這是因為科研人員和工程師缺乏足夠的現場試驗和物理試驗資料來完全理解能源樁複雜的熱力學表現（包括群樁效應），並驗證他們的設計假設。更嚴重的是，僅有的針對能源單樁的物理模型試驗也給出了矛盾的結果：一些學者稱樁的側摩阻力下降高達50％，而其他科研顯示樁的承載力上升。目前為止，沒有可用的群樁物理試驗資料。 在本提議的研究課題中，將利用三維離心機模型和數值模擬手段，在加熱、冷卻並與多種力學加載耦合的條件下，研究能源樁尤其是群樁複雜的熱力學表現。此外，本方案將對土體單元進行熱力耦合加載試驗研究。基於單元測試結果並通過群樁離心機試驗結果的反分析，將改進現有的由本項目合作方開發的土壤本構模型，並植入新的有限元代碼進而探索並理解小間距能源群樁的熱力學相互作用；同時將提出新的設計指南和計算圖表，並通過正在進行的現場試驗進行驗證。本研究方案預期的發現和成果將給人類帶來顯著的社會和經濟效益。

617213.label: Major findings and research outcome
617213.value: The major findings from this project are summarised as follows: (a). The conventional assumption that the natural plane (NP) is located at the mid-depth of a floating (or called friction) pile is wrong and non-conservative. The depth of NP is governed by the magnitude of operating temperature in energy pile. (b). Floating replacement energy piles will experience ratcheting settlement during initial service stage, irrespective of whether the pile is installed in sand or clay. This is due to the thermally-induced volumetric contraction and shearing at the soil-pile interface, leading to the reduction of horizontal stress acting on the pile. Thermally- and mechanically induced contraction of clays and sands should be accounted for in design. (c). The observed ratcheting pile settlement decreases but with an increasing number of thermal cycles and it should be designed properly to minimize the service life of any structure. (d). On the contrary, only small ratcheting heave behaviour of driven floating energy piles is observed. The observed heave is likely attributed to the densification effect and particle crushing of granular soil when the pile is driven in. The major research outcomes of this project include a total of 15 joint journal and 10 joint conference papers published and one M.Phil and two Ph.D students trained. For details please refer to Part C of the report. In addition, the PI and the co-I (Professor Laloui) organized the trend-setting inaugural International Conference on Geo-Energy & Geo-Environment (GeGe2015) between 4th and 5th December 2015 at HKUST. A copy of conference proceedings was published. More details of the conference are given on the conference website: http://gege2015.org/. Moreover, the 2nd International Conference on Geo-Energy & Geo-Environment (GeGe2017) was held between 5-6 July 2017 in Hangzhou. The PI and Professor Laloui both attended the conference and delivered two keynote lectures at the conference. The 3rd International Conference on Geo-Energy & Geo-Environment (GeGe2019) will be held at EPFL in 2019.

617213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
617213.value: Although a significant numbers of physical model tests and numerical simulations of energy piles have been carried out, relatively speaking, only few full-scale tests on energy pile and pile groups are available worldwide. Clearly, more field trials should be conducted to verify new design guidelines. Moreover, the environmental impact of thermal heat dissipated in the ground by energy foundations should be investigated thoroughly to avoid adverse effects on the Earth.

617213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
617213.value: Fundamental mechanisms of single floating energy piles are investigated and understood. Ratcheting pile settlement during initial thermal cycles is identified and quantified. Remedial action is proposed. The conventional assumption that the natural plane is located at the mid-depth of an energy pile is proven to be incorrect. Temperature-dependent natural plane is revealed. New findings from this project have been published in a total of 15 journal articles and 10 conference papers. More importantly, results from this project have contributed to the first design guidelines developed on the mainland recently. This greatly promotes the use of environmentally friendly foundations on the mainland. In addition, the PI and the co-I (Professor Laloui) organized the trend-setting inaugural International Conference on Geo-Energy & Geo-Environment (GeGe2015) between 4th and 5th December 2015 at HKUST. Subsequently, the 2nd International Conference on Geo-Energy & Geo-Environment (GeGe2017) was held between 5 and 6 July 2017 at Zhejiang University in Hangzhou. The 3rd International Conference on Geo-Energy & Geo-Environment (GeGe2019) is scheduled to be held at EPFL in Switzerland in 2019. It is clear that this series of conferences has a profound impact on the sustainability of the Earth.

617713.label: Project Objectives
617713.value: We plan to perform extensive experiments with large datasets in order to identify properties of TDSPs, such as the frequency at which the TDSPs change, and the magnitude of these changes. We will study patterns of trajectories as well as groups of nodes whose shortest paths change simultaneously, and we will investigate how historical data can be used to predict current TDSPs. We will implement continuous monitoring techniques that can cope with the large number of concurrent queries and updates in real DRN systems. Our techniques will utilize historical data and previous traffic patterns to facilitate efficiency and enhance the quality of the paths, returned to the users.

617713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
617713.value: Conventional road networks are modeled using weighted directed graphs. The weight of each edge is a single value that captures its cost (e.g. travel time). Popular online applications for fastest path computation and navigation, such as Google Maps and Bing Maps, run on top of static maps, i.e. they always output the same path independent of the query time. However in real life road networks, the travel cost is not constant as it depends heavily on parameters such as traffic, weather conditions, construction works etc. Dynamic Road Networks (DRNs) capture these fluctuations of travel cost by assigning time functions (instead of single values) to edge weights. In a DRN, the fastest path between two nodes (termed Time Dependent Shortest Path - TDSP) changes over time. It has been shown by numerous studies that using the TDSP, instead of the conventional shortest path, leads to considerable savings in both fuel and commute time. This project aims at designing smart DRN services that fully exploit the available traffic information to process TDSPs and related queries. Through our collaboration with the University of Southern California we gained access to large traffic datasets for the Los Angeles road network, gathered in real-time by various agencies. The volume, the velocity and the variety of the data require Big Data approaches for data management. Our goals are twofold; first, we will perform extensive experiments with the data in order to identify properties of TDSPs (e.g., how often the TDSP between a pair of nodes changes, how previous TDSPs can be used to predict the current TDSP, patterns and groups of TDSPs that change simultaneously). Second, we plan to explore our findings in order to develop efficient continuous monitoring techniques. Specifically, we view each TDSP as a continuous query, since between the time that the query is submitted and the time that the user arrives at the destination the path may change due to sudden changes (e.g., accidents) in the traffic patterns. Given that at any instant, a system may execute thousands of such queries, while constantly updating edge weights, efficient processing techniques are essential. Moreover, historical data may be useful for enhancing the quality of the returned paths and facilitating efficiency. 傳統的道路網路使用加權有向圖建模。每邊用來描述成本（如行程時間）的權重是一個單一值。有關計算最快路徑和導航比較流行的線上應用程式，如Google地圖和Bing地圖，是運行在靜態地圖上的，即它們總是輸出獨立於查詢時間的相同路徑。然而在現實生活中的道路網路，其行程成本不是固定的，它在很大程度上取決於諸如交通情況、天氣、道路工程等參數。動態道路網路（DRN）通過為邊的權重分配時間函數（而不是單一值）來捕捉這些行程成本的波動。在動態道路網路中，兩個節點之間的最快路徑（稱為隨時間變化的最短路徑，即TDSP）隨時間而變化。大量研究表明，使用TDSP取代傳統的最短路徑，會節約相當可觀的燃料和時間。 這個項目的目的在於設計智能DRN服務，以充分利用現有交通資訊去處理TDSP和相關查詢。通過與南加州大學的合作，我們取得了大量由不同機構即時收集的洛杉磯道路網路資料集。由於資料量大，輸入和處理速度快和資料的多樣性，這都要求我們在實施資料管理時採用「大數據」的技術手段處理。我們有兩個目標；首先，為了確定TDSP的屬性，我們將對資料進行廣泛的實驗（例如，一對節點之間的TDSP多久才會變化，如何使用以前的 TDSP來預測當前的TDSP以及哪些TDSP模式和群組傾向同時變化等）。第二，我們計畫通過對研究結果的延伸，開發高效的連續監測技術。具體來說，我們將TDSP視為一個連續的查詢，因為從用戶提交查詢，到他到達目的地之間，TDSP可能由於突發事件（例如，交通意外）而發生變化。考慮到在任何時刻，一個系統可能要同時執行數以千計的查詢，而邊的權重也在不斷更新，高效的處理技術是必不可少的。此 外，歷史資料或許在提高返回路徑的品質和促進效率方面非常有用。

617713.label: Realisation of objectives
617713.value: Regarding Objective 1, our involvement with dynamic road networks led us to investigate general uncertain graphs. Query processing on uncertain graphs is based on Monte-Carlo sampling. However, sampling is not always a viable option for large graphs because: i) sampling requires generating a random number for each edge, and ii) a large number of samples is necessary to obtain a good approximation. We aim at removing the uncertainty by producing representative instances of uncertain graphs. Queries can then be processed efficiently on the deterministic instance using conventional graph algorithms. Consider for example a shortest-path query. State-of-the-art approaches to this query type perform Dijkstra expansions on multiple samples. Depending on the definition of the distance measure, expansion for some samples can be avoided or terminated early, when it cannot improve the current result. Nevertheless, the method usually has a very high cost. On the other hand, the same query in our framework can be processed efficiently by applying any deterministic shortest path algorithm on the representative. In order to achieve accuracy, the representative instance should preserve the underlying structure of the uncertain graph. Starting from the observation that the vertex degree is one of the most fundamental properties of the structure of a graph, in [C1] we conjecture that by preserving the degree of each vertex we capture the essence of the underlying uncertain graph, and thus accurately approximate other properties. In [J1], we generalize the notion of vertex degree, introduced in [C1], to the concept of n-clique cardinality of a vertex u, i.e., the number of cliques of size n that contain u. For instance, the degree of a vertex is equivalent to its 2-clique cardinality, whereas its triangle connectivity corresponds to its 3-clique cardinality. Intuitively, this generalization aims at capturing the expected structure in the neighborhood of vertices. Our extensive experimental evaluation on real and synthetic datasets confirms our conjecture: by preserving the vertex degrees and n-clique cardinality, our representative instances can also capture several structural properties of the graph, including shortest-path distance, betweenness centrality and clustering coefficient. Regarding objective 2, we focus on nearest-neighbor monitoring assuming uncertain object locations. Specifically, the positions of moving objects are modeled by a Bivariate Gaussian model. The goal is to continuously output the k-nearest neighbors with probability above an input threshold. For instance, in a taxi hailing application, a user may wish to be continuously notified about the k = 2 taxis that are closest with some probability (e.g., over 75%). Since an exhaustive evaluation would be prohibitive, in [C2] we develop heuristics based on spatial and probabilistic properties of the uncertainty model, and promptly issue approximate, yet reliable answers with confidence margins. An extensive experimental evaluation confirms that the proposed techniques can efficiently cope with numerous moving Gaussian objects under fluctuating uncertainty conditions, while also offering timely response with low error to multiple queries of varying specifications. Finally, we investigate the problem of differentially private histograms, which aims at protecting the identity of individual records from published histograms. In the context of road networks, differential privacy can be used to conceal trips of specific cars from statistical data about traffic conditions. However, the concept of privacy has general applicability in numerous applications. Existing methods focus on maximizing the utility of the histograms, which in turn minimizes the error in query results. In [J2], we first observe that there is a small set of common components across all existing methods, and that each method essentially proposes a different instantiation of each component. Then, we identify the best algorithm for each component, and propose variants that outperform the existing ones in efficiency or utility. Finally, we develop novel combinations that do not appear in the literature. Using exhaustive experiments on four real datasets with different characteristics, we conclude that there are always trade-offs in terms of utility and efficiency. Our work can serve as a guide to help practitioners engineer a differentially private histogram scheme depending on their application requirements.

617713.label: Major findings and research outcome
617713.value: Query processing in uncertain graphs is usually expensive. To facilitate efficiency, [C1] introduces the problem of extracting a representative instance from an uncertain graph. Fast deterministic processing techniques can then be applied on this representative to closely approximate the result on the original graph. [C1] proposes two methods for generating deterministic instances of uncertain graphs that capture the vertex degrees: Average Degree Rewiring (ADR) and Approximate B-matching (ABM). ADR involves two phases: first, it generates an instance with the same average vertex degree as the uncertain graph; then, it randomly rewires edges, if they lead to better approximation of the vertex degrees. ABM applies b-matching to obtain an initial instance, which then improves using weighted maximum bipartite matching. [J1] focuses on the the problem of extracting the representative instance that best preserves the expected n-clique cardinality (for n ≥ 2). We propose two algorithms based on the greedy and game theoretic frameworks. GREEDY arranges the edges in a dynamic heap and greedily inserts the one that leads to the best approximation of the expected n-clique cardinality. GAME models the edges of the uncertain graph as players of an exact potential game, and uses best response dynamics to generate the representative. In order to assess the quality of representatives, we perform extensive experiments on real datasets. Our results confirm that indeed the proposed methods, and especially GAME, approximate well various structural measures and query metrics. [C2] assumes a setting where a central server receives frequent location updates from uncertain objects, whose locations are modelled by a Bivariate Gaussian model. In addition, the server has to respond to multiple continuous k-nearest neighbor monitoring queries. A probabilistic approach with confidence guarantees is adopted to overcome the high cost of exact query processing. In order to deal with frequent updates and varying degrees of uncertainty, a novel discretization scheme quickly estimates proximity of a Gaussian pdf to the query point, offering a probability measure for their comparison. Pruning criteria eagerly discard irrelevant candidates and efficiently obtain the qualifying ones. Experiments under diverse queries illustrate that the proposed techniques generate high quality approximate solutions. Existing schemes for differentially private histograms aim at maximizing the utility of the published data. [J2] constitutes the first work that goes beyond utility, also considering efficiency. Efficiency is important when histograms are published frequently, as in the case of traffic conditions that need to be regularly updated. Towards this end, we first observe that all existing schemes consist of a small set of common blocks. We then optimize and select the best implementation for each block, determine the combinations of blocks that capture the entire literature, and propose novel block combinations. We qualitatively assess the quality of the schemes based on the skyline of efficiency and utility, i.e., based on whether a method is dominated in terms of both aspects or not. We demonstrate that the schemes derived from our novel block combinations provide the best trade-offs for time-critical applications.

617713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
617713.value: Towards the direction of uncertain graphs, we are currently working on sparsification techniques that reduce the number of edges and redistribute their probabilities in order to decrease the graph size, while preserving its underlying structure. The sparsified graph has less entropy, and can be used to approximate the result of a wide range of queries. Sparsification yields significant benefits in execution time because the cost of sampling is linear to the number of edges. Moreover, the required number of samples is proportional to the entropy, which is lower in the sparsified graph. Finally, similar to the case of deterministic graphs, sparsification reduces the storage cost, and facilitates visualization of complex networks. Towards continuous monitoring techniques, we plan to investigate additional types of queries. For instance: "When should I take a taxi to the airport in order to arrive before 5pm with probability above 0.9?". In order to answer this type of query, each edge is usually associated with a travel time and a probability distribution, which can be derived based on historical data, and updated on-line in case of unexpected events. Finally, location privacy is an important topic worth of further development. Although there are some techniques (based on private information retrieval) that can completely hide the identity and location of moving cars/users, they are too expensive to be practical. A more effective direction would be towards techniques that achieve good trade-off between privacy and efficiency.

617713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
617713.value: In the course of the project we investigated several important theoretical and practical aspects related to dynamic road networks. A main direction of theoretical work concerns the extraction of representative deterministic instances, from uncertain graphs. Towards this direction, we developed techniques to generate representatives, which capture the expected degree, or the n-clique cardinality of each node. In both cases, we have shown that the generated certain graph can be used to efficiently process a variety of queries including shortest paths, betweenness centrality and clustering coefficient. Regarding practical aspects, we have focused on nearest-neighbor monitoring of moving objects, whose exact locations are uncertain (e.g., due to inaccurate GPS measurements). The proposed techniques can efficiently manage numerous objects and long-running queries under fluctuating uncertainty conditions. Finally, we also investigated privacy aspects, and designed a general framework, based on differential privacy, that combines different components in order to maximize both accuracy and efficiency. In addition to location, the framework has a wide applicability, independently of the characteristics of the underlying data.

617813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
617813.value: Tremendous amounts of data are generated in a streaming fashion in a variety of applications, such as web and telephony networks, wireless sensor networks, social networks, and more. The continuous nature of such data has motivated the need for sophisticated data stream management systems (DSMSs), which offer efficient storage and reliable querying services to clients. Existing robust DSMSs include IBM's InfoSphere Streams, Microsoft's StreamInsight and AT&T's Gigascope. Due to the overwhelming volume of streaming data, companies may not possess, or wish to acquire, the resources for deploying a DSMS. A practical alternative is to outsource the stream storage and processing to a specialized third party service provider with strong DSMS infrastructure. Data outsourcing is a widely adopted business model that offers significant cost savings to companies, especially start-ups. Despite its merits, data outsourcing naturally raises the issue of trust. Specifically, the provider may act maliciously to increase profit, e.g., it may collude with rival companies and present fraudulent results to bias the competition, or it may shed some of the workload and only operate on a sample of the input. Even when the provider is honest, problems can arise, as it may run buggy software, or (given the scale of the problems considered), suffer errors due to equipment failure or read/write errors. This project focuses on stream authentication, which enables the clients to verify the correctness of the streaming results they receive from the provider, i.e., that they are untampered with (integrity) and up-to-date (freshness). Our goal is twofold: (i) we aim at the design of fundamental cryptographic tools for data stream authentication, which form the basis for the development of schemes for a wide range of important queries in stream outsourcing, and (ii) we target at making data stream authentication a very lightweight operation, and establishing it as a standard tool for error-checking, in a similar way to the use of checksums for reliable file transfer. 617913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
617913.value: 在生物醫學領域，根據生物細胞的形態特徵（包括大小和形狀）来提供尺寸測量，分離和同時对其力學特性的測量，指明了很多潛在的高影響力的應用。例如，檢測人體血液中的相比較於紅細胞（約7-8微米）而言尺寸較大的迴圈腫瘤細胞（約10微米），對於檢測早期癌症有重要意義。人體紅細胞膜的力學特性也可以作為反映人體健康水準的指標。 在這個專案中，我們的目標是研發出一種片上集成的小型化的光流體平臺，在最小化利用體積較大的傳統光學器件的同時使對生物細胞的光學分離和力學特性測試變為可能。在我們近來的工作和相關文獻的基礎上，我們提出利用光子晶格（即光鑷的週期排列）來作為重要的構建基礎來實現一系列的“晶片上的實驗室”的器件，包括細胞集中器件，大小差異的細胞分離器件和多級細胞拉伸器件。 專案關鍵的創新點是設計和製備一種將聚合物多模干涉波導縱向嵌入於矽襯底的結構。這種設計能使得在襯底的光學層與上方集成的流體層得到分離。波導可將光纖（從位於襯底背部的波導輸入面端射）發射的單個近紅外的光點（1064納米），在波導輸出端即微流通道的底部轉換為多個自成像（用作一個光子晶格）。產生的光子晶格將在整個微流通道的橫截面上擴散，進而所有的流體中的顆粒可以被光學分離。 我們設計波導芯層的形狀，尺寸和設置光纖出射位置來調節光子晶格。鑒於光學梯度力和流體阻力跟細胞的大小相關，因此具有不同大小的細胞可被分離到不同的運動軌跡。這裡我們尋求利用不均勻的光子晶格來實現一個集成的按大小進行分離的器件，並達到片上集成與在微米精度下不同尺寸的分離。我們還提出了利用光子晶格來週期性的拉伸單個紅細胞來測試紅細胞在光場力影響下的形變。我們會研發一種彈性光散射檢測的技術，並從散射光斑的變化及其相關聯的形變程度來讀出紅細胞的拉伸和恢復時間。

617913.label: Realisation of objectives
617913.value: Objective 1: We have successfully realized Objective 1. We have developed a fabrication process for our proposed vertically embedded polymer multimode-interference (MMI) waveguides in the university's fabrication facility. We have demonstrated SU8-filled vertically embedded MMI waveguides in the silicon substrate with the key features of a straight profile, a smooth sidewall surface, a void-free waveguide core, and smooth waveguide end-facets. We have demonstrated optical lattice generation from our fabricated SU8-filled vertically embedded MMI waveguides in microfluidic channels. We experimentally observed optical lattice patterns with numbers of mode-field maxima spanning from 4 to 10, generated on the front end-facet of rectangular-core MMI waveguides with cross-sectional widths of 27 ~ 42 micron and a length of 300 micron at 1064nm wavelength. We have studied the effect of input-coupling position offsets in the longitudinal direction on optical lattice generation from vertically embedded MMI waveguides. Though fabrication-induced dimensional errors are inevitable, optical lattice patterns can still be generated from our fabricated devices upon input-coupling at positions offset from the waveguide input end-facet in the longitudinal direction. This suggests that our technique has a high tolerance for fabrication-induced waveguide dimensional variations. Objective 2: We have partially realized Objective 2. We have experimentally demonstrated optical trapping (concentration) and guiding of microparticles and rabbit red blood cells (RBCs) using the optical lattice patterns generated from vertically embedded MMI waveguides in a microfluidic channel. We have investigated the optical guiding phenomenon of 1.1micron-radius polystyrene particles and RBCs upon a fixed injection direction parallel to one of the lattice axes. We demonstrated that microparticles and RBCs can be strongly guided along the lattice rows upon a high optical power and a reduced flow speed. Specifically, in our RBC experiments using a 5×5 optical lattice with a 6.0micron pitch, when the average optical power per lattice spot increased from ~6 mW to ~31 mW with the flow speed fixed at ~140 micron/s, we found the RBCs average lateral position deviations at the end of the lattice rows narrowed from ~1.0 micron to ~0.5 micron, suggesting a stricter guiding (concentrating). When the flow speed increased from ~80 micron/s to ~200 micron/s and the average optical power per lattice spot was fixed at ~18 mW, we found the RBCs average lateral position deviations at the end of the lattice rows increased from ~0.5 micron to ~1.2 micron, suggesting a looser guiding. In order to understand the optical potential landscapes the microparticles and RBCs encounter in optical lattices, we have numerically simulated the optical gradient force exerted on microparticles and spherical (osmotically swollen) RBCs from an array of Gaussian beams using the Maxwell Stress Tensor method in COMSOL. However, we have not demonstrated optical sorting of microparticles or biological cells, partly due to time constraints and partly due to the tight requirement of injecting microparticles at an angle relative to the lattice axes and separately collecting the sorted / rejected microparticles, which require a careful design on the microfluidic channels for injecting / collecting particles for a specific optical lattice. We are now making further attempts to investigate such a potential flow-angle-dependent optical sorting mechanism. We believe that once we find an optimum particle injection angle using a proper microfluidic channel design and an optimum lattice pattern, the originally proposed particle sorting based on particle sizes and elasticity should be within reach. Objective 3: We have partially realized Objective 3. We have experimentally demonstrated optical stretching of osmotically swollen rabbit RBCs using optical lattices generated from our fabricated vertically embedded MMI waveguides in an optofluidic chip and using a charge-coupled-device (CCD) camera for imaging-based detection of cell shape deformations. Specifically, we have systematically investigated RBC stretching by varying the optical power and the flow speed upon a cell injection angle parallel to one of the lattice axes. Based on the statistics from many RBCs (> 500 cells for each experimental parameter setting), we observed that RBCs were periodically stretched and released when passing along different rows of the optical lattice. In our RBC experiments using a 5×5 optical lattice with a 6.0micron pitch, when the average optical power per lattice spot increased from 0 mW to ~31 mW with the flow speed fixed at ~110 micron/s, we found the RBCs average maximum deformation factor increased from ~0.03 to ~0.08, suggesting a larger deformation. When the flow speed increased from ~80 micron/s to ~200 micron/s with the average optical power per lattice spot fixed at ~25 mW, we found the RBC average maximum deformation factor decreased from ~0.07 to ~0.05, suggesting a smaller deformation. We have analyzed the RBCs’ dynamics when the cells are passing through the optical lattice. We observed that when the cells were concentrated and guided along the optical lattice rows (Objective #2), they were periodically accelerated and decelerated. We observed that the cells exhibited a locally minimum speed when they were positioned slightly after an optical intensity-maximum spot, where we considered the cells were in an equilibrium state with balanced optical gradient force and fluidic force. We estimated the optical gradient force exerted on cells in the equilibrium position based on the fluidic force. In our experiments with the average optical lattice spot power increased from ~12 mW to ~31 mW and a flow speed of ~110 micron/s, we extracted the average optical gradient force of ~0.9 pN to ~4.2 pN. Based on the extracted minor axis of stretched cells of ~6.1 micron to ~5.8 micron, we estimated the RBC had a shear modulus of ~2 microN/m using a conventional static model of RBC deformation. In our current cell-stretcher configuration, we have achieved a characterization throughput of ~ 10 cells/s at an average flow speed of ~200 micron/s, which is much higher than the throughput of conventional optical cell stretchers (< 10 cells/min). In order to test the potential of our demonstrated cell-stretcher as a cell-deformation cytometer, we have characterized the deformation of healthy RBCs and unhealthy chemical-treated RBCs in response to our cell-stretcher. In our experiments, we treated RBCs using glutaraldehyde with different volume/volume concentrations from 0.0005 % to 0.002 %. We observed the deformation factor decreased from ~0.08 for untreated (healthy) RBCs to ~0.06 for RBCs treated with a chemical concentration of 0.002% upon an average optical lattice spot power of ~31 mW and a flow speed of ~110 micron/s. This is consistent with the fact that RBCs are less elastic upon a higher-concentration glutaraldehyde treatment. However, we have not demonstrated elastic-light-scattering detection for rapid characterization of cell deformations. This is partially limited by the relatively weak elastic-light-scattering signals from the cells. Besides, the scattered light will be scattered by the thick PDMS channel wall. We believe that our current scheme adopting the CCD camera-based imaging detection provides visualized information of cell deformations, which serves as a useful starting point before we further develop the technique with potentially a higher-throughput (> 50 cells/s at a flow speed of > 1 mm/s) based on the elastic-light-scattering detection using a faster linear-array detector. However, we expect that the viscous nature of biological cells (with typical mechanical response time and recovery time of ~ 0.1 s) would finally limit the flow speed allowed for cell-deformation characterization (typically in the range of tens of pN).

617913.value: 1. We have developed the fabrication process of SU8-filled vertically embedded MMI waveguides in the silicon substrate with a straight profile, a smooth sidewall surface, a void-free waveguide core, and smooth waveguide end-facets. (See Conference abstracts 1, 2, and Publication 1 (manuscript under preparation)) 2. We have designed, modeled and experimentally characterized optical lattice generation from our fabricated SU8-filled vertically embedded MMI waveguides with various cross-section profiles in microfluidic channels integrated on the top of the chip. We have adopted three-dimensional (3-D) beam-propagation method (BPM) to systematically design and numerically model the optical lattice generation from vertically embedded MMI waveguides, with various cross-sectional dimensions and various lengths, to obtain optical lattice patterns with various pitches and mode-field maximum numbers. We have found that optical lattices can be generated from vertically embedded MMI waveguides even upon fabrication-induced dimensional errors by offsetting the input-coupling position from the waveguide input-coupling end-facet in the longitudinal direction. This indicates that our technique has a high tolerance for fabrication-induced variations in waveguide dimensions. We have both theoretically and experimentally studied the effect of input-coupling position offsets in the longitudinal direction on optical lattice generation as a virtual extension of the waveguide length. (See Conference abstracts 1, 2, and Publication 1 (manuscript under preparation)) 3. We have experimentally demonstrated optical trapping (concentrating) and guiding of 1.1micron-radius polystyrene particles and rabbit red blood cells (RBCs) using the optical lattice patterns generated from the vertically embedded MMI waveguides in a microfluidic channel. We have numerically investigated the optical gradient force exerted on microparticles and spherical RBCs from arrayed optical Gaussian beams. (See Conference abstracts 1, 2, and Publication 2 (manuscript under preparation)) 4. We have experimentally demonstrated optical stretching of rabbit RBCs using optical lattices generated from our fabricated vertically embedded MMI waveguides in an optofluidic chip and using a CCD camera for imaging-based detection of cell shape deformations.
