We have distinguished between healthy RBCs and glutaraldehyde-treated RBCs based on their different shape deformations in response to the cell-stretcher. In our current cell-stretcher configuration, we have demonstrated a throughput of > 10 cells/s at a flow speed of 200 micron/s, which is much higher than the throughput of conventional optical cell-stretchers (< 10 cells/min). (See Conference abstracts 1, 2, and Publication 2 (manuscript under preparation))

617913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
617913.value: In order to further develop our on-chip optical cell-stretching technique with a higher characterization throughout and a lower memory consumption for a potentially Big-Data analysis, we will adopt the elastic-light-scattering detection using a fast linear-array detector for detecting cell shape deformations. The proposed course of action includes: (i) design and fabricate PDMS microfluidic channels with a thin channel wall and a smooth sidewall surface in order to minimize the undesirable light scattering from PDMS that may distort the weak scattering light interference patterns from cells, (ii) optimize the elastic-light-detection system configuration including the sheet-focusing of the probe laser light, the incident angle and the far-field detection position in order to measure the cell-induced interference patterns that are most sensitive to the cell deformation, and (iii) establish statistically significant datasets of the characteristics of the elastic-light-scattering far-field interference patterns from non-deformed swollen RBCs and deformed RBCs with various orientations by correlating the scattering interference patterns with the cell images simultaneously captured from a CCD camera.

617913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
617913.value: Nowadays, the ability to manipulate biological cells and characterize their mechanical characteristics potentially offers high-impact applications in the biomedical area. The mechanical properties of biological cells provide critical indicators for their health conditions. For example, various disease conditions in a human body affect the mechanical properties of red blood cells (RBCs), such as malaria infection, diabetes and hyperglycemia. Optical force-based techniques for this purpose have been under intensive research interest due to the non-invasive interaction with biological cells. However, conventional optical techniques are typically limited by bulky instruments or low characterization throughputs. In this project, we have proposed and successfully demonstrated an integrated, miniaturized optofluidic platform with minimum use of bulk optics to manipulate and mechanically characterize biological cells with a relatively high throughput, using the optical lattice generated from vertically embedded polymer-in-silicon multimode-interference (MMI) waveguides. We have demonstrated optical trapping, guiding and concentrating of microparticles and RBCs, and opto-mechanical stretching of RBCs. We have distinguished between healthy RBCs and chemically treated RBCs. Our light input-coupling technique allows a high tolerance to fabrication-induced dimensional errors to the embedded waveguides, which is relevant for practical applications. We envision this technique to pave the way for future opto-mechanical-based cell disease diagnoses.

618213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
618213.value: Recently the PI has successfully completed a RGC GRF project on the measure of instability. In the completed project, the study of the measure of instability has been carried out for both discrete-time and continuous-time LTI systems. For discrete-time systems, this topic has a longer history and has more extensive recent literature. It has been mathematically shown and physically justified that the instability of a discrete-time LTI system can be measured by the Mahler measure, the absolute product of unstable poles of the system, or equivalently by the topological entropy, the logorithm of the Mahler measure. While the existing literature has established this understanding for single input systems, our main contribution is to have shown that the same can be said for multi-input systems by using the novel vehicle of resource allocation. For continuous-time LTI systems, less is known but all indicators point to the observation that a meaningful instability measure is given by the sum of the real parts of the unstable poles. However, there were only scattered results in the literature to justify this observation. Our understanding resulted from the completed research project has strengthened this observation. Again the vehicle of resource allocation played an important role. In this proposed project, we plan to further the successful stories in the earlier project and to extend the study to deeper and wider problems. Our objectives are to find more evidence to support the use of the absolute product or the real sum of the unstable poles as the instability measure of a discrete-time or continuous-time LTI system respectively, and to find more connections between the instability measures to fundamental limitations in feedback control. In particular, it is expected that the instability measures have strong connections to the minimum communication resource needed in networked control, where the feedback signals have to be transmitted through communication channels. We plan to formulate several networked control problems whose solvability strongly depends on whether the communication resource available is sufficient with respect to the instability measure of the system. 最近，项目负责人成功完成了一项由RGC GRF资助的关于不稳定性测度的项目。该项目同时研究了离散和连续时不变系统的不稳定性测度。相对连续系统，离散系统的相关研究具有更长的历史和更丰富的文献。数学证明和物理验证表明离散时不变系统的不稳定性可以由Mahler测度（系统不稳定极点的模乘积）或者拓扑熵（Mahler测度的对数）来刻画。对于单输入系统，该发现在现有文献中已有阐述。我们的主要贡献在于提出资源分配的思想从而将该发现成功推广到多输入系统。 对于连续时不变系统，文献中认识尚少。但种种迹象表明：系统不稳定极点的实部之和可以有效地刻画其不稳定性。然而，鲜有文献证实该发现。在我们已完成的项目中，该发现得以初步证实。其中，资源分配再次发挥了重要作用。 在该拟议项目中，我们计划延续之前项目的成功经验，将相关研究推广至更深入和更广泛的问题。 我们的目标是发掘更多的事实来论证离散或连续线性时不变系统的不稳定性可以分别用不稳定极点的模乘积或实部之和来度量，以及寻找更多不稳定性度量与反馈控制本质限制之间的联系。具体而言，鉴于网络化控制中反馈信号借由通信信道传输，我们预计系统的不稳定性度量和网络化控制所需的最少通信资源具有密切的联系。我们计划提出若干网络化控制问题。我们期待这些问题的可解性取决于系统的不稳定性测度和通信资源之间的关系。

618213.label: Realisation of objectives
618213.value: For objective 1, we further strengthened the justification of the use of the absolute product or the real sum of the unstable poles as the instability measure of a discrete-time or continuous-time LTI system respectively from the following aspects: (1) we reviewed a historical perspective on optimization over polynomials and Bowen's notion of topological entropy; (2) we studied a series of optimization problems of complementary sensitivity and sensitivity functions whose optimum are all given by the absolute product or the real sum of the unstable poles; (3) we studied the networked stabilization problems under different channel models for both discrete-time and continuous-time systems and both single-input case and multiple-input case. The studies converge to the conclusion that the minimum amount of communication resource required to stabilize a linear system is given by the absolute product or the real sum of the unstable poles. For objective 2, we established more links between the instability measure and the fundamental limitations in feedback stabilization. In particular, we studied the stabilization of multi-input networked control systems over multiple fading channels in which both additive noise and multiplicative noise are present. We considered both the scenario when the channels are configurable and the scenario when the channels are fixed a priori. For the former case, channel/controller co-design was used and for the latter case, coding/control co-design was exploited. In both cases, we showed that the minimum amount of communication resource required for stabilization is determined by the instability measures of the systems. We also studied the networked stabilization over shared communication channels where a multiplexer/demultiplexer scheme is used. Again, the communication requirement was shown to be determined by the instability measure of the system. For objective 3, we have also made major initiative steps in extending the instability measure in the state feedback case to the output feedback case. It is justified partially that one possible such measure in the output feedback case is given by the optimal complementary sensitivity, which depends on both the unstable poles and zeros in rather a complicated way. We also built connections to gap metric robust control and two-port circuit theory. We modeled the uplink and downlink communication between the plant and controller in output feedback networked control systems as two-port networks, which capture the additive, inverse additive, multiplicative, and inverse multiplicative uncertainties occurring in the signal transmission process in a unified framework. Our preliminary study suggests that the examination of output feedback networked control over two-port networks will give us further insights in defining an instability measure in the output feedback case. More study is underway. Hence objective 3 is partially achieved by far.

618213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
618213.value: There is a great potential for further research. The research outcome of this project has led to two follow-up funded RGC GRF grants, 16208414 and 16201115. We expect all these research projects will lead to a deep and comprehensive understanding of the instability measure of systems and its implications in fundamental limitations of feedback control.

618213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
618213.value: Stability is a central issue in control theory. A system is either stable or unstable. However, ever since the very beginning of control theory, it has been asked how stable a stable system is. Only recently people have started to ask how unstable an unstable system is. Such questions are often associated with networked control problems and are often addressed in terms of the minimum communication resource needed in stabilizing an unstable system. An emerging discovery is that the instability measure of a discrete-time LTI system is given by the absolute product of its unstable poles, and the instability measure of a continuous- time LTI system is given by the real sum of its unstable poles. In this project, we find further evidence to support this discovery and find more connections between these instability measures and various optimal control, robust control, and networked control problems. With more such evidence and connections, the validity of the discovery is more convincing. A good understanding in the quantification of system instability will be an important addition to systems control theory.

618313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
618313.value: The amount of information in text format such as online news, Wikipedia, blogs, emails, and e-books is rapidly increasing every year. Dealing with a large amount of text data poses a great challenge to researchers. Text mining techniques, which include topic extraction, content summarization, and sentiment analysis, have been developed to help people derive high-level knowledge from text data. However, the results returned by text mining may not be accurate or relevant. Thus, many applications need human assistance to examine and understand the mining results. Visual text analytics combines text mining and visualization techniques for large text data analysis, allowing people to comprehend a huge amount of text data in intuitive ways, make accurate analysis for fuzzy patterns, and provide timely feedback for decision making in time critical situations. It leverages both the computational power of computers and the pattern recognition capability and domain knowledge of humans, and thus shows great potential. Visual text analytics is still at an early stage, and many problems have not been well addressed. With the rise of social media such as Twitter, Facebook, and Google+, visual text analytics faces new challenges. Compared with traditional text corpora, the data from social medial usually have strong social context (e.g., community, social network) and are very noisy (e.g., many meaningless or misleading posts). In this project we will focus on developing visual text analytics methods for data from social media, especially microblogging services like Twitter (or Weibo in China). We will augment text visualizations with social context for social insight and sentiment analysis. We will develop a comprehensive visual analytics system for visual guided, social-aware sampling, monitoring, and analysis of tremendous amounts of streaming posts. The completion of this project will allow people to better browse, monitor, and analyze massive text data from social media. Analysts can use our techniques to provide timely analysis to breakout news and topics in Twitter and other social media. Given that most information in the world is currently stored as text, the results from this project will benefit all kinds of users and have a high commercial value. The PI has closely collaborated with researchers at IBM and Microsoft, and some preliminary results have been published in the IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics and the ACM Transactions on Intelligent Systems and Technologies. 文本格式的數據如網上新聞，維基百科，博客，電子郵件和電子書每年都在大量增長。如何處理這些大量的文本數據給研究人員帶來巨大挑戰。人們開發了不少文本挖掘技術，包括主題抽取，內容概括，和情感分析等來幫助大家從文本數據中獲取高層次的知識。但是文本挖掘返回的結果可能不精確甚至不相關。因此很多應用都需要人力協助來辨識和理解挖掘的結果。可視文本分析結合了文本挖掘和可視化技術， 使人們能夠直觀地理解大量的文本數據，對模糊的模式做出精確的分析，並在時間緊急的情況下為決策提供及時的反饋。它同時利用了計算機的計算能力和人類的識別能力和領域知識，從而顯示出巨大的潛力。可視文本分析仍處於早期階段，許多問題還沒有得到很好的解決。隨著社交媒體如推特，臉書，和谷歌等的崛起， 可視文本分析面臨新的挑戰。與傳統的文本語料庫數據相比，社交媒體數據通常有強烈的社會內容（例如，社區，社會網絡）而且數據噪音大（例如，許多無意義或誤導性的帖子） 。 在這個項目中，我們將專註於為社交媒體尤其是微博服務如推特（或者中國大陸的微博）開發可視文本分析方法。我們將在文本可視化技術中增強社會內容，以便獲得社會洞察力和進行情感分析。我們將開發一個全面的可視分析系統以便基於視覺引導來取樣，監測和分析巨量的動態更新的文本數據。這個項目的建成將讓人們更好地瀏覽，監控和分析社交媒體產生的大量文本數據。分析師可以使用我們的技術為客戶及時分析在推特和其他社交媒體上的突發新聞和話題。鑒於目前世界上大多數信息仍然存儲為文本，這個項目的結果將使各類用戶受益，並具有較高的商業價值。 本項目負責人和IBM及微軟的研究人員合作緊密。一些初步的結果已經發表在IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics and ACM Transactions on Intelligent Systems and Technologies這兩種期刊上。

618513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
618513.value: In real-time rendering applications, there are still many scenarios in which depth-sorting is necessary or desirable. The most common is order-independent transparency or translucency. It is necessary to render semi-transparent objects in correct back-to-front (or front-to-back) order in order to correctly blend their colors and produce an accurate rendering of the scene. Therefore, rendering 3D objects in front-to-back or back-to-front order is a fundamental problem in computer graphics that has been researched extensively since the early days of computing. Depth-sorting is performed at run-time because the order of the triangles is dependent on the constantly changing viewpoint (i.e., viewer position). In this study we propose a new way of looking at the depth-sorting problem that is a significant departure from earlier sorting-based schemes. The key innovation involves designing techniques that replace the traditional runtime sorting strategy of existing algorithms with a faster triangle selection strategy. Instead of sorting triangles or fragments at run-time, given a viewpoint, a simple and very fast run-time procedure extracts triangles from an pregenerated special extended triangle list. The extracted subsequences are statically presorted by depth and contain each input triangle exactly once. Our initial results for static meshes render depth-sorted triangles from any direction with no sorting issuing a single drawing command (i.e., draw call). The proposal outlines additional applications of this initial result as well as potential directions to explore in order to extend the technique to more challenging dynamic scenes. The proposed approaches will be designed to run on high-end systems but also on legacy hardware and low end devices such as mobile phones. The initial results for static scenes on high-end graphics processors already show significantly superior performance in rendering depth-sorted static models compared to previous approaches. 按照由近到远或由远到近的深度顺序渲染三维场景中物体，是计算机图形学领域里非常基础且有意义的课题，并从计算机图形学初期一直被人们研究到现在。它在渲染中有非常多的实际应用，主要方面包括处理物体遮挡和半透明效果等。 在这份申请书里，我们提出了一项与以往排序为基础方法的截然不同的新算法。创新的关键在于用更快的选择策略来取代传统的排序策略。选择的过程发生在我们预先生成的扩大的三角形序列上，每个三角形在序列中的不同位置会有一份到几份拷贝，并用预先生成的测试平面将每份拷贝的作用空间划分。实际渲染时，根据视点和测试平面信息，我们可以快速的生成一份用于光栅化的子序列。选择到的子序列可以保证是深度排序的，且每一个三角面片处理不超过一次。

618513.label: Realisation of objectives
618513.value: We designed a basic algorithm for front-to-back rendering of static models. It was previously published in ACM Transactions on Graphics. We then started investigating the above objectives. We focused most of our effort on the objectives that we felt were the most critical for optimizing real-time rendering techniques. More specifically, objectives 1 and 3 consist of improving the efficiency triangle order generation and the final rendering for both static and animated models. One of our approaches automatically optimizes the triangle order of animated meshes with the objective of reducing overdraw while maintaining good post-transform vertex cache efficiency. This is the first work to consider overdraw reduction for animated models without resorting to runtime sorting. We show that this can significantly improve rendering time, and we hope that games and other real-time applications will employ this technique. We then further improved our static mesh ordering results by generating a set of orders very efficiently and that do not require the runtime plane test used in earlier work. As a result, the selected index buffer can be rendered directly at full speed and the approach can be easily incorporated into rendering engines. The result is unmatched in front-to-back rendering performance. This work is currently under review and we hope that it will have a lasting impact after publication. We also analysed the possibility of using hardware extensions to natively support the plane test, however this objective became less critical after we developed the improved algorithm that does no longer requires a plane test and thus can render the model directly. We also looked into volumetric and shadow extensions but found out that most of the performance benefit was on the improvements to the basic algorithm used for front-to-back rendering and translucency. We expect that to have a more lasting impact on a wide range of graphics applications. Finally, we further explored its uses in mobile hardware and found out that it results in similar performance gains in those platforms.

618513.label: Major findings and research outcome
618513.value: The two major findings were: -The first triangle reorder algorithm for selection-based front-to-back rendering of animated scenes. -A novel algorithm for front-to-back rendering of static models that does not require triangle selection sorting at runtime, and thus can render the appropriate index buffer directly at full speed. These findings for both static and animated models are widely applicable to graphics applications in general. Essentially any application that renders 3D models can in some way benefit from these contributions, either to improve rendering time of standard models or to allow for rendering translucent materials without runtime sorting. We expect that these methods will find many applications in the industry.

618513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
618513.value: We are sharing the output of this work with the graphics industry and look forward to seeing practical uses of this approach in applications, such as games, CAD, and medical visualization. We hope to work them on specialized extensions for different applications to further the impact of this work.

618513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
618513.value: Rendering the triangles of a 3D model in front-to-back order is of critical importance for two reasons: First, it improves rendering speed since occluded regions of the model need not be shaded, and second it allows for correct rendering of translucency effects. In this project, we made significant advances in reordering triangles of 3D models in order to generate these front-to-back orders. Since 3D object rendering is prevalent in computer graphics applications, reordering models using our proposed methods directly leads to significant performance improvements in a wide variety of applications without requiring significant modifications to their runtime component.

618713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
618713.value: Neuromorphic engineering is the design of computing systems based on the architecture and functional organization of the nervous system. One of the major foci in neuromorphic engineering is the implementation of visual processing, in large part because this is one of the areas that has seen the most investigation by neurobiologists, and thus, is one of the best understood areas of the brain. Biological systems use visual perception to gather information about their immediate environment. One of the goals of neuromorphic engineering is to endow robots with the same capability. Stereo vision and image motion both provide powerful cues about the geometric layout of the environment. Although neuromorphic systems for processing stereo disparity and image motion have been built, little work has been done in building systems that process stereomotion. Stereomotion, also known as motion in depth, is the motion of an object towards or away from an observer. Here, we propose to build models for the development of populations of model neurons that are tuned to different magnitudes and directions of stereomotion. 神經形態工程通過研習生物神經系統構架和功能組成以設計計算系統。如何實現視覺處理是神經形態工程領域的一個重要課題，這很大程度上是因為神經生物學家們對大腦中視覺系統工作原理探索得最多，因而也對其理解最深。生物系統使用視覺感知來獲取其周身環境信息，而神經形態工程的一個重要目標也是賦予機器人系統以同樣的能力。立體視覺以及圖像移動都為生物系統感知環境幾何構造提供了強大的線索。雖然處理立體視覺視差以及圖像移動的神經形態學系統已經被研究人員開發出來，但是研究直接處理立體圖像移動系統的相關工作較少。立體圖像移動，同時也被稱為深度向移動，表徵一個物體正在靠近或者遠離觀察者。這裡，我們提議開發一個模擬處理立體圖像移動神經元群發展過程的模型，該神經元群對於立體圖像移動的大小和方向有不同的響應。通過這一模型，我們期望實現對立體圖像移動處理系統機理的研究。

618713.label: Realisation of objectives
618713.value: Both objectives were achieved. The first objective was achieved by developing a new architecture for neural development that incorporates the concepts of sparsity and slowness in an emergent framework. While both factors had been hypothesized previously to play a role in the development of invariant feature detectors, past models hard-coded the concept of slowness. In contrast, slowness in our architecture is an emergent property that arises due to the statistics of natural inputs. We refer to this architecture as the generative adaptive subspace self-organizing map (GASSOM). It extends Kohonen’s adaptive subspace self-organizing map (ASSOM) with a generative model of the input. When exposed to binocular stimuli, this architecture learns a population of orientation, spatial frequency and binocular disparity tuned neurons. When exposed to time varying monocular stimuli, it learns a population of orientation, spatial frequency and motion tuned neurons. There are two commonly hypothesized architectures for the perception of motion in depth: the changing disparity (CD) model and the interocular velocity difference (IOVD) model. In the CD model, it is assumed that a representation of binocular disparity is extracted in a first stage of processing. Disparity encodes depth. In a second stage of processing, the rate of change of disparity (i.e. depth) is then computed, leading to a measure of motion in depth. The IOVD model also contains two stages. The first stage estimates monocular motion. The second stage looks for differences between the motion in the left and right eyes. Velocity differences imply motion in depth. Our proposed architecture also had a two stage structure. Both stages were based on the GASSOM architecture developed. In the first stage, we learned populations of units tuned to either disparity or motion using three separate GASSOMs: one for disparity and two for monocular motion (either left or right). The responses of these populations were then concatenated into a larger feature vector, which was fed into a second GASSOM. Our experimental results demonstrated that when presented with binocular images created by surfaces moving in depth, the second stage developed units that were tuned to stereomotion. The second objective was achieved by testing the learned architecture with three different classes of stimuli commonly used to characterize perception of motion in depth in psychophysical experiments: standard random dot stereograms (RDS), dynamic RDS (DRDS) and uncorrelated RDS (URDS). An RDS is created by generating a random dot pattern for the left eye and shifting it by a given disparity in the right eye. The standard RDS contains both CD and IOVD cues. The DRDS, where the random dot pattern changes from frame to frame, contains primarily CD cues. The URDS, where the random dot patterns presented to left and right eyes are different, contains primarily IOVD cues. Differences in the responses to these different types of stimuli are interpreted to indicate different degrees of reliance on the CD versus IOVD mechanism. Recently, (Sanada and DeAngelis, Journal of Neuroscience, 2014) examined the responses of neurons in the visual cortical area known as MT in response to these stimuli, and characterized the degree of motion in depth selectivity of each neuron in the population in response to each of these stimulus types. They then examined the correlation between the degrees of selectivity for the different stimulus types, in an attempt to determine the extent to which different cues were relied upon. A strong correlation between the degrees of selectivity measured in response to the RDS and the URDS stimuli would suggest a strong dependence upon the IOVD cue. A strong correlation between the degrees of selectivity measured in response to the RDS and the DRDS stimuli would suggest a strong dependence upon the CD cue. Their results suggested that selectivity was driven primarily by the IOVD cues, with a small contribution from the CD cue. However, the mechanism by which this occurs was unclear. By presenting these same stimuli to our model, we were able to replicate their results. This is significant in that it suggests that the proposed two stage architecture is a plausible model for the emergence of motion in depth in biological neural systems. In addition, we found that our results matched those of Saneda and DeAngelis only for a particular ratio of disparity to motion tuned neurons in the first stage. This is a testable prediction about the relative sizes of the populations driving motion in depth selective neurons in area MT.

618713.label: Major findings and research outcome
618713.value: One of the major developments in this work was the development of the generative adaptive subspace self-organizing map (GASSOM) model for the development of primary visual cortical cells. GASSOM formed the basis of the stereomotion model. There are several key innovations in the GASSOM model. First, rather than hard coded as in prior work, the notion of slowness is an emergent property of the GASSOM model. This not only is a more parsimonious description, but also enables the definition of slowness to adapt to the particular properties of the input. Second, the model does not require explicit segmentation of the input training vectors into separate episodes, making it more widely applicable. The GASSOM architecture was described in item 1 listed in Section 9 of Part C. The second major finding was that the GASSOM architecture can be used to learn the connectivity in a model of primary visual cortical neural units selective for binocular disparity and motion selectivity. The primary visual cortex is one of the main sources of input to area MT, which contains neurons selective for stereomotion. This was critical, given the importance of extracting disparity and motion information in the changing disparity (CD) and interocular velocity difference (IOVD) models of stereomotion perception. This finding for disparity is described in item 1 listed in Section 8 of Part C and in item 2 in Section 9 of Part C. The finding for motion is described in item 1 of Section 10 of Part C. The third major finding in this work was the two stage model that learns stereomotion selectivity. In contrast to past models of stereomotion selectivity which considered only abstractions of the real image input, our model accepts binocular image sequence input, enabling it to be run on the exact same stimuli as used in psychophysical studies of stereomotion selectivity. We were able replicate findings from measurements of real neurons with our model. This suggests that the model is a plausible candidate for the neural bases of stereomotion perception. The model was also able to generate testable predictions about the characteristics of the primary visual cortical input feeding into the motion in depth selective units found in area MT. This finding was reported in item 2 of Section 10 of Part C.

618713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
618713.value: The GASSOM architecture developed to model neural development in the course of this work can be extended in a number of ways beyond stereomotion. First, the visual representation learned by the GASSOM architecture can be combined with representations of other cues, such as vestibular and proprioceptive cues. This should enable an autonomous agent to learn how to integrate multiple cues, leading to enhanced performance. We are currently investigating this possibility in a project funded by the RGC GRF (#16211015) entitled "Neuromorphic developmental models for image stabilization." It should also be possible to extend the concept of slowness in the GASSOM architecture, which posits that stimuli close in time should be similar, to include prediction. We are investigating this in another GRF project (#16213617) entitled "The Generative Adaptive Dynamic Subspace Self Organizing Map for Sensorimotor Coordination."

618713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
618713.value: Neuromorphic engineering is the design of computing systems based on the architecture and functional organization of the nervous system. One of the major foci in neuromorphic engineering is the implementation of visual processing, in large part because this is one of the areas that has seen the most investigation by neurobiologists, and thus, is one of the best understood areas of the brain. Biological systems use visual perception to gather information about their immediate environment. One of the goals of neuromorphic engineering is to endow robots with the same capability. Stereo vision and image motion both provide powerful cues about the geometric layout of the environment. Although neuromorphic systems for processing stereo disparity and image motion have been built, little work has been done in building systems to process stereomotion. Stereomotion, also known as motion in depth, is the motion of an object towards or away from an observer. In this project, we developed a model that learned how to process stereomotion automatically, simply through exposure to the environment, much in the same way the biological neural systems develop. This architecture may lead not only to insights into biological perception, but also robots that can better adapt to novel environments.

Systematic data of the evolution of stress-strain relation, surface morphology and temperature field of the specimen will be acquired. 619113.value: The project objectives were successfully achieved through the following milestone work: 1. We have successfully designed and fabricated a cyclic tensile loading testing platform capable of both displacement- and force-controlled cyclic loading with synchronized measurements of spatiotemporal variations in surface morphology and temperature field together with the stress-strain curves of the specimen. 2. We have performed cyclic tests on NiTi SMA specimens over the frequency range of 0.0001 to 10 Hz. First-hand systematic data of the frequency-dependent spatiotemporal oscillations of the thermal and mechanical fields of the specimen were obtained for the first time. 3. 619113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
619113.value: Materials which are capable of structural phase transitions under external field, such as ferroelastic and ferromagnetic shape memory alloys and ferroelectric materials, are increasingly being used in many fields, from biomedical human artificial joints, to small-scale sensors and actuators in MEMS, to the vibration and damping control devices in small- and large-scale engineering structures. Cyclic phase transition under external periodic driving is one of the most common working modes of these materials in real service and is widely observed in various structures and systems. Under different frequencies and amplitudes of driving, the responses of the materials at different levels are directly related to the performance, fatigue and safety of the devices and therefore are always key concerns in the application. In this project, we conducted systematic experimental study on the spatiotemporal oscillations of the temperature and deformation of polycrystalline NiTi SMA under the cyclic phase transition process. Wire specimens were used in tensile tests under different deformation frequencies and amplitudes. Synchronized measurement of the temperature field, surface morphology and stress-strain histories of the specimen was performed. Theoretical analysis was performed in parallel to understand the physical process, to identify the governing parameters for the responses. The research of this project not only led to 5 international journal publications but also collaboration with a top university in china. The project is of both academic and practical importance in the performance, fatigue and failure analysis of SMA devices under cyclic loading.

619313.label: Project Objectives
619313.value: Fundamental research on image matting We will study a new approach to image matting that leverages the nonlocal principle in image matting. As will be explained, this allows for coherent pixel clusters during matte computation, which will help minimize the amount of user input and produce high-quality mattes preserving fine details in the output. Fundamental research on video matting Frame-by-frame user markups are impractical and frame-by-frame image matting does not work in video matting. The fundamental problem to solve is to produce spatio-temporally coherent clusters of moving foreground pixels. We will argue for the use of motion information, which is in contrast to the nonlocal principle applied to video denoising, by turning the notorious aperture problem in computer vision to our own advantage. Implementation and software packages While we have put online our Matlab source codes for image matting to benefit the research community, they are research codes rather than production codes. Effort will be made to produce a hardware-assisted version of KNN image and video matting to optimize performance, by leveraging off-the-shelf and state-of-the-art graphics processing unit (GPUs).

619313.label: Realisation of objectives
619313.value: The project objectives have been achieved. The image matting method we developed in our earlier CVPR'12 paper and PAMI'13 paper has been extended to the KNN Laplacian to video matting where the results were reported in our ICCV'13 paper. This paper demonstrates how the nonlocal principle benefits video matting via the KNN Laplacian, which comes with a straightforward implementation using motion-aware K nearest neighbors. In hindsight, the fundamental problem to solve in video matting is to produce spatio-temporally coherent clusters of moving foreground pixels. When used as described, the motion-aware KNN Laplacian is effective in addressing this fundamental problem, as demonstrated by sparse user markups typically on only one frame in a variety of challenging examples featuring ambiguous foreground and background colors, changing topologies with disocclusion, significant illumination changes, fast motion, and motion blur. When working with existing Laplacian-based systems, our Laplacian is expected to benefit them immediately with improved clustering of moving foreground pixels. KNN image/video matting relies on color cues for extracting the foreground matte. Currently the user needs to decide if HSV or RGB color space works best. We believe this can be automated by leveraging machine learning, and subsequently we developed a method for twoclass weather classification, focusing on labeling an outdoor image as sunny or cloudy, and the results are reported in our CVPR'14 paper. Given a single outdoor image, this paper proposes a collaborative learning approach for labeling it as either sunny or cloudy. Never adequately addressed, this two-class classification problem is by no means trivial given the great variety of outdoor images. Our weather feature combines special cues after properly encoding them into feature vectors. They then work collaboratively in synergy under a unified optimization framework that is aware of the presence (or absence) of a given weather cue during learning and classification. Extensive experiments and comparisons are performed to verify our method. We build a new weather image dataset consisting of 10K sunny and cloudy images, which is available online together with the executable. The inherent limitation that KNN matting is color ambiguities where the foreground and background colors are similar. This limitation can be readily removed with the advent of the depth cameras where the foreground and background exhibit different depths. In another CVPR'14 paper we reported our progress on depth-aware feature descriptor for video matting. We propose binary range-sample feature in depth. It is based on τ tests and achieves reasonable invariance with respect to possible change in scale, viewpoint, and background. It is robust to occlusion and data corruption as well. The descriptor works in a high speed thanks to its binary property. Working together with standard learning algorithms, the proposed descriptor achieves state-of-the-art results on benchmark datasets in our experiments. The running time is impressively short compared with existing techniques. Finally, the matlab implementation and software packages of KNN image/video matting are available at http://dingzeyu.li/projects/knn/ In fact, the technique has become so popular that various third-party implementations in other programming languages (e.g. Mython) can easily found on the WWW.

619313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
619313.value: There are several directions for further development of the pertinent research on KNN image/video matting. As evidenced by our CVPR'14 paper, leveraging the depth channel in addition to RGB in human activity recognition in a video sequence can help address the difficult video object segmentation problem, which is one direction to pursue. The other possible fruitful direction to pursue is to metabolize the recent deep learning revolution, and capitalize on deep convolutional neural network to address the image/video matting problem. While some preliminary work by other groups has been reported, the focus has been on the application aspects and quality of results, while the more difficult mathematical explanation for the efficacy of deep neural network on image/video matting is still lacking. Finally, while stable source codes and executable codes are available, making them run in real time and on mobile devices remain a challenge. This research is related to the deep learning approach mentioned above, where the research focus will be reduction on the network while maintaining the necessary quality of the matting results.

619313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
619313.value: Matting is instrumental to special effects production in TV and movies: the video matte of a moving foregound (actor) is pulled out from a video captured in a studio under controlled lighting with a constant-colored background. The extracted video matte is then keyed into another video depicting a new background scene typically generated using computer graphics software systems. This project enables high-quality image/video matting beyond TV or movie studios. Granted, existing state of the arts allow matting be done on images/videos captured by lay users in an uncontrolled environment. But their high-quality results come at the expense of a lot of user interactions and complicated techniques which are restrictive or somewhat difficult to reproduce: most methods rely on the local color-line model, or sophisticated color sampling and various forms of matte regularization. We have provided the working source codes (matlab) which is available for free in our project web http://dingzeyu.li/projects/knn/

619813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
619813.value: Advancements in silicon technology allow many processor cores to be put on single chip to form multi-processor-system-on-chip (MPSoC) for the next generation high performance computing platform. To facilitate communications among different processors in these complex systems, Network-on-chip (NoC) has been proposed [1]. Designing MPSoC with NoCs is a very complicated process. It involves solving many complex synthesis sub-problems. It needs to evaluate and compare millions different designs and select the best one. This requires fast and accurate performance models to compare the merit of different solutions. Simulation tools cannot be used for this purpose as it is too slow. Existing performance evaluation methods use queuing theory [2] or network calculus [3] to model the network performance by simple close-form mathematical formula. However the accuracy and versatility of these approaches depend on many assumptions which do not hold in real applications. Also it is difficult to extend these models to new NoC router architectures such as bi-directional NoCs [4] and speculative routers [15], which are more complicated than the traditional router. Machine learning has been extensively used in pattern recognition and artificial intelligence where it is difficult to obtain the exact mathematical relationship between the outputs and inputs directly from the problem formulation. This is similar to the NoC performance evaluation problem. However machine learning techniques have not been well-studied in previous NoC research. In this work, we propose a complete new approach for the NoC design problem by adopting machine learning. We will first develop a support vector regression (SVR) frame work [xx] for modeling the NoC average latency. Compared with the existing analytical models, fewer assumptions are needed and higher accuracy can be achieved since the learning process provides more practical inference on the properties of the data traffic in the routers. We will further extend the learning framework to model the maximum latency and bandwidth utilization to predict the worst-case performance bounds and thereby provide quality-of-service (QoS) guarantees for hard real time systems. Also, the learning techniques will be applied in router power modeling for more accurate overhead evaluation. We aim at developing a complete learning-based framework for fast and accurate estimations on all key design metrics in the optimization process. We will also use the learning techniques for optimal runtime control. Learning-based adaptive routing algorithms will be developed for optimizing the overall latency. Runtime task migration and DVFS schemes based on reinforcement learning will also be developed. 伴随着半导体工艺的不断进步和器件特征尺寸的不断缩小，越来越多的处理器核将被集成到一个芯片上而形成多核片上系统。如何有效地管理核与核之间的通信成为设计应用于下一代高性能计算的多核片上系统的一个关键问题。片上网络（Network-on-Chip）在最近被提出并带来了一种全新的片上通信方法。基于片上网络的系统能更好地适应在未来复杂多核系统设计中的时钟同步/异步，功耗，延时和可靠性等问题，从而有效地提高多核片上系统的性能。 设计一个基于片上网络的多核系统是一个复杂的综合和优化过程。它通常需要分步骤地解决一系列系统综合时的子问题。并且在应对每一个子问题时，设计者需要评估每一个设计方案（例如路由方案，布局方案等）的性能（例如延时，功耗等）， 然后再从几百万甚至几亿个方案中选择出最优的设计。因此，一个快速的模型来准确地预测每个方案的性能成为找到最优设计的关键。通常而言，基于仿真器仿真的性能预测虽然提供了可靠的精准度，但由于耗时太长而不适宜在系统综合的内部循环中使用。因此，现有的用于设计初期的性能评估模型通常是基于数学建模的方法得到的（例如排列理论模型 或者网络积分模型）。这些模型在推导时往往依赖于一些理想化的假设（例如数据包与包的时间间隔是泊松分布等）。而很多实际的应用呈现出了更加复杂的交通特性，因此这些数学模型在缩短了评估时间的同时，不可避免地降低了预测的准确度。此外，这些数学模型通常只适用于基于虚通道的或者基于虫洞交换的路由器模型，对于近期提出的一些更加复杂的片上网络架构，例如基于双向链路的片上网络或者带有投机的路由器架构, 目前还没有数学分析模型能够很好预测设计的性能。 另一方面，我们注意到机器学习已经被广泛研究和应用于模式识别，人工智能等领域。在这些领域里，一个共同的特点是很难获得一个解析的数学表达式来完整地描述输出与输入之间的关系。因此，需要利用机算计基于已有的数据来自动分析规律，并利用“学习”到的规律来对未知数据进行预测。这一点非常类似于对片上网络进行性能预测的问题。但是，迄今为止，应用于片上网络的机器学习方法还没有深入地被研究。因此，在本项目中，我们将提出一整套新的基于机器学习来预测和优化片上网络性能的方法。具体地，我们首先开发出一个利用支持向量回归（Support vector regression）来预测片上网络平均延时的模型。和之前基于排队理论的数学分析模型相比较，基于机器学习的模型来自于对实际训练数据的分析和研究，并且减少了对交通特性和路由器架构的假设，因而可以取得更高的准确度。接下来，我们还将这套机器学习的框架拓展到学习片上网络的最差延时。因为很多实时系统对每个任务的完成期限有着严格的要求（hard deadline）,因此通过对最差延时的预测，可以确保服务的质量(Quality of service)。类似地，我们还可以将机器学习的方法应用于路由器功耗和面积的建模，以达到在设计前期（综合的内部循环里），就可以有效的评估该方案所对应的硬件设计开销。通过一系列性能指标的学习，我们希望可以在系统综合时，准确的评估一个设计方案的各个指标，从而让优化程序全面地评估一个设计并且选择最好的设计方案。机器学习除了可以用在离线的性能评估以外，我们还将尝试利用机器学习来实时控制片上网络，从而进一步优化系统实际运行时的性能。具体地，我们将研究基于机器学习的自适应路由算法以优化延时特性。我们还将研究和提出基于机器学习的动态任务迁移算法以及动态电压和频率调整技术来降低系统的功耗。

619813.label: Realisation of objectives
619813.value: Network-on-Chips (NoCs) architectures have been proposed as a promising solution for complex on-chip communication problems in the era of multi-core architectures. During the design process, numerous design choices are generated. The optimal solution is selected based on the key design metrics such as the average latency, maximum delay, area and power consumption. A fast yet accurate evaluation of these metrics for each design during the design exploration becomes increasingly important. In this project we employed powerful machine learning techniques to develop an accurate and versatile NoC performance modeling and estimation framework. The first objective of the project is to develop performance-modeling techniques based on a machine-learning framework to predict the traffic flow latency to evaluate the average and worst-case NoC performance. We first worked on a generalized theoretical performance model based on advanced queuing theory to estimate the average latency of an application that mapped onto a NoC architecture. Based on the application communication traffic information and the target NoC routing algorithm, the channel and source queue waiting times are estimated using an analytical queuing model with two equivalent queues. The model works for variable packet size and general packet arrival time distribution. Then we proposed a novel approach to enhance the accuracy of the performance estimation by employing machine learning and support vector regression (SVR) techniques. The delay estimations obtained from the generalized analytical delay model are included as features during the learning process. A learning framework that uses SVR to collect training data and predict the traffic flow latency was developed. The framework was implemented based on C++ and Matlab. We ran extensive experiments using the developed model and framework on typical mesh NoC architectures. Experimental results were very promising. It improves the performance estimation accuracy over the state-of-the-art methods significantly. We also worked on the worst-case performance evaluation. We surveyed existing techniques, which are based on real-time bound analysis and network calculus. We decided to use machine learning to predict the distribution of the flow delay and could accurately estimate the percentage of flow that has a delay larger than a certain value. To improve the accuracy of the worst-case flow latency estimation, we also tried other machine learning techniques such as deep neural networks (DNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to capture the dynamic temporal behavior to model the worst-case delay of a router based on the input traffic patterns. However the impact on accuracy is not significant. For the second objective, the developed machine-learning techniques have been verified in typical small-size (4X4) mesh NoC architectures with random traffic. Later it was extended and applied on large-size (8X8 and 12X12) NoC architectures with more sophisticated traffic patterns such as transpose, tornado, bit-reversal and real-application traffic. All the experimental results show that the prediction errors are less than the existing approaches with a large speedup compared to the simulation approaches. We also did experiments on other topologies such as torus networks and the results were also promising. Besides the single-direction link mesh/torus architecture, we also developed a bi-directional link architecture based on a flit-level speedup scheme to achieve a higher throughput. For the NoC intra-router bandwidth, in addition to allowing flits from different packets to use the idle internal bandwidth of the crossbar, the proposed flit-level speedup scheme also allows flits within the same packet to be transmitted simultaneously. For inter-router channels, a distributed channel configuration scheme was developed to dynamically change the link directions. By doing so the throughput is increased and flow latency are reduced because idling data-link can be used effectively to increase the inter-router bandwidth. In addition to the basic bi-directional link architecture, we also proposed another high performance NoC router architecture using a bi-directional link with double data rate. An extra link stage between routers is added so that two flits can be transmitted in one link per cycle using phase pipelining if both routers require using the same link. In addition, to further increase the effective bandwidth, the direction of each link can be configured in every clock cycle to cater for different traffic loads from each side. We applied our SVR estimation framework on these architectures also. However the accuracy is not very high as the direction of the links between adjacent routers in these architecture is configured in real time and the static training cannot capture this dynamic reconfigurable characteristics well which results in a less accurate router performance model. For the third objective, we used machine learning and deep neural network (DNN) techniques to learn and build the latency model of the router for NoC architecture. During the process, we tried to speed up the performance of the deep neural network so as to improve the throughput of latency evaluation. We developed two techniques to speed up the performance of DNN evaluation. The first is based on the output sparsity characteristics of DNNs. A lot of the neurons in each layer of the DNN are inactive and a low overhead prediction scheme based on low rank approximation was proposed to dynamically identify those inactive neurons so that the memory accesses and the arithmetic operations associated with these inactive neurons can be bypassed to speed up the operation. This technique can be implemented in both software and hardware. Experimental results show that ~40% speedup in throughput can be achieved. Another bottleneck of the performance is the amount of memory used in the DNN model. We proposed and developed an algorithm based on hashing techniques to compress the DNN network to reduce the memory requirement for modeling. Hardware implementation technique using a block-hashing scheme was also proposed. Using these techniques can compress the weight of the network by an order of magnitude and reduce the memory requirement significantly.

619813.label: Major findings and research outcome
619813.value: We reviewed the existing approaches of predicting the performance of NoCs [Journal-3]. Existing analytical router models make many assumptions about the traffic patterns and the configurations of the router, and hence cannot be generalized for different NoC topologies and traffic patterns. Thus we developed a new analytical router delay modeling methodology that works for a variety of NoC configurations and traffic scenarios [Conf-1]. To further improve the accuracy, we enhanced our analytical model by combining the advantages of several previous models and extended it with two equivalent queues. Then we created an accurate model based on a machine learning mechanism using support vector regression (SVR). The analytical model is included as part of the features in the learning process to enhance the estimation accuracy. Experimental results demonstrated high prediction accuracy and a 100x speedup over cycle-based simulation approaches [Journal-1]. We also used this router model for worst-case performance evaluation. SVR technique was used to model the distribution of the flow delay and estimate the percentage of flow that has a larger delay than a certain value. We also explored the use of deep neural networks (DNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to capture the dynamic temporal behavior of the flow traffic to improve the modeling accuracy. However the improvement is not significant. We also tried the proposed models on other non-conventional NoC architectures. We developed two new NoC architectures based on bi-directional reconfigurable data-link. The first one allows multiple flits in the same packet to be transmitted simultaneously based on the real-time reconfiguration of the direction of the data link between two routers [Journal-2]. This architecture can improve the throughput by 50% compared with the conventional NoC architecture. To further improve the throughput, the bi-directional architecture was extended with a double data-rate reconfigurable data link. Experimental results showed that the throughput was further improved by another 50% [Journal-4]. During the creation of the router delay model, DNNs were used. To speed up the DNN evaluation, we developed two techniques. The first is to exploit the output sparsity characteristic of DNN [Conf-2]. A low rank approximation technique is used to predict the inactive neurons and then bypass their operation to achieve speedup. Up to 43% improvement in throughput was demonstrated in the experiments. The second approach used a hashing technique to compress the weight of the DNN and hence reduce the latency of memory access [Conf-3].

619813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
619813.value: The project results show that a pure analytical router delay model cannot capture the complex traffic dynamics of NoC and hence could not give accurate performance estimation. Machine learning techniques based on real traffic data training have potential to build more accurate latency model for NoC routers. In this project, the router model was built based on the features related to the local input traffic of the router only. Although this model can give good accuracy for average performance prediction for conventional NoC architecture, it still needs further improvement for architectures that use dynamic link re-configuration. Towards this end, there are two directions that can be explored to further develop the research. The first is use more sophisticated machine learning techniques that can capture the dynamic dependency. The second direction is to include more features for training the router models. Besides using the local input traffic data as features, the traffic data at the neighboring routers and even routers one or two hops away can be included. This can help to capture the latency penalty due to blocking at the downstream router. Also it will help to capture the dynamics of the data link direction reconfiguration for the bi-directional NoCs.

619813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
619813.value: Multi-core systems with network-on-chip architectures are the trend for the design of high-performance computing hardware. Designing these complex systems requires sophisticated design automation tools to explore the huge design space. Fast and accurate performance estimation models are crucial for evaluating different designs to find the optimum solution. Existing NoC performance estimation tools require too many assumptions, which impair their ability to model complex systems and hence affect the estimation accuracy. In this project, we proposed and developed a new modeling method based on machine learning techniques. Real traffic data were used to train the model to capture the complex traffic characteristics. Experiments show very promising results in prediction accuracy. Moreover, this work is probably one of the first few works to employ machine learning techniques for modeling and estimation in the domain of electronic design automation. The results of this project will stimulate interest in applying machine learning techniques in other EDA tools and algorithm development.

619913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
619913.value: Due to the highly developed information technology and sensing technology, massive amounts of data are being generated and collected constantly. In addition, the inherent complexities of various modern industries result in data of different features. Therefore, most data in our daily lives are large-scale and complex data. Traditional statistical methods cannot effectively handle the monitoring and surveillance of such data on a real-time basis. This brings new challenges and opportunities to formulate advanced statistical methodologies to better model and control the quality of modern processes or systems. New techniques of monitoring, surveillance, and quick diagnosis of abnormal activities in modern industries that produce huge amounts of complex data have become critical. The proposed research project focuses on developing statistical monitoring and diagnostic methodologies for large-scale and complex. This involves three fundamental issues: (1) online monitoring of high-dimensional data on a real-time basis; (2) simultaneous surveillance of mixed-type data that contains both numerical variables and categorical factors; and (3) off-line identification of multiple abnormalities in a large historical dataset. The central idea of the proposed research is to develop statistical methodologies to achieve efficient monitoring and diagnosis and reduce variability in modern manufacturing and service industries that involve massive amounts of complex data. The tasks will be carried out with reference to real processes where data and process knowledge are available. 由於高度發達的信息技術和傳感技術，海量數據正不斷生成和收集。此外，各種現代行業的固有特點導致數據的複雜性。因此，在我們日常生活中的大多數數據是大規模以及複雜的。傳統的統計方法不能有效在實時的基礎上處理,監測,和監督這樣的數據。這帶來了新的挑戰和機遇， 制定先進統計方法，以更好的模型和現代化質量控制, 对現代工業的大量複雜數據进行監測，監視和快速診斷的技術成為此研究關鍵。 研究項目重點为發展大規模和複雜數據的統計監測和診斷方法。這涉及三個基本問題：（1）一個實時的高維數據在線監測,（2）同時監測混合類型的數據，其中包含连续数据和离散数据,（3） 离線識別在大數據集中的多種異常。

619913.label: Realisation of objectives
619913.value: The first objective was to devise a novel online surveillance methodology for high-dimensional data. Process monitoring using multivariate quality variables remains an important and challenging problem in statistical process control (SPC). In 2015, we set up a general framework in "A General Framework for Monitoring Complex Processes with both In-Control and Out-of-Control Information," Computers and Industrial Engineering, 2015. In this work, we emphasized the use of data from both normal operating conditions and the abnormal process. The working status of the process is indicated by the probabilistic outputs of the supporting vector machine (SVM) classifier, and the multivariate exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) strategy is applied to construct the control chart. A fast diagnostic procedure can be implemented as soon as the control chart gives an alarm. The framework has been demonstrated in a hard-disk manufacturing process application. After that, we developed several (mostly nonparametric) monitoring schemes in "Monitoring Censored Lifetime Data with a Weighted-Likelihood Scheme," Naval Research Logistics, 2016, and "Statistical Process Control for Latent Quality Characteristics Using the Up-and-down Test," Technometrics, 2017. In particular, the paper "A False Discovery Approach for Scanning Spatial Disease Clusters with Arbitrary Shapes" under the same framework has received the IISE Transactions 2018 Best Paper Award. In the work, we developed a promising online surveillance methodology for high-dimensional data that can be applied to assess the outbreak of a disease. Identifying unusual events that are spatially scattered is a challenging problem that is commonly seen in a large variety of applications, including geographic disease surveillance, agriculture pest surveillance, astronomy, ecology, geography, sociology, and public health monitoring. For example, an epidemiologist is often interested in assessing the outbreak of a disease and analyzing whether it is infectious or dependent on any spatial environmental factor. The spatial scan statistic is one of the main tools for testing the presence of clusters in a geographical region. The recently proposed Fast Subset Scan (FSS) method represents an important extension, as it is computationally efficient and enables detection of clusters with arbitrary shapes. Aimed at automatically and simultaneously detecting multiple clusters of any shape, our work explores the False Discovery (FD) approach originated from multiple hypothesis testing. We show that the FD approach can provide a higher detection power and better identification capability than the standard scan and FSS methods on average. One more research breakthrough I would like to highlight is the paper by Han, D., Tsung, F., and Xian, J., "On the Optimality of Bayesian Change-Point Detection," Annals of Statistics, 2017. This result is probably one of the most important theoretical breakthroughs in the last 50 years on the strict (not asymptotic) optimality of Bayesian change-point detection since Shiryaev's fundamental work in 1963. The second objective was to develop a multivariate rank-based monitoring scheme for mixed-type complex data. We have developed solutions for the unique characteristic of large-scale and complex data in that both numerical and categorical features are involved. Research results include "Directional Control Schemes for Processes with Mixed-type Data," International Journal of Production Research, 2015, and "Rank-based Process Control for Mixed-Type Data," IIE Transactions, 2016. In this work, we assumed that there is a latent continuous variable that determines the attribute levels of a categorical variable, so that the ordinal information among the attribute levels can be exploited. This enables us to simultaneously describe and monitor continuous and categorical data in a unified framework of standardized ranks, based on which a multivariate exponentially weighted moving average control chart is proposed. This control chart specializes in detecting location shifts in continuous data and in latent continuous distributions of categorical data. Numerical simulations show that our proposed chart can efficiently detect location shifts and is robust to various distributions. In addition, we also tackled the challenges of monitoring categorical data, which include ordinal and binomial data. Examples include "Ordinal Profile Monitoring with Random Explanatory Variables," International Journal of Production Research, 2017, and "A Control Scheme for Autocorrelated Bivariate Binomial Data," Computers and Industrial Engineering, 2016. The third objective was to formulate a diagnostic approach for offline identification of multiple abnormalities. This objective was more application oriented. We have several results focusing on additive manufacturing, such as "A Statistical Transfer Learning Perspective for Modeling Shape Deviations in Additive Manufacturing," IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters, 2017, and "In-Plane Shape Deviation Modeling and Compensation for Fused Deposition Modeling Processes," IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering, 2016. At present, the shape deviation of the product hinders the application of additive manufacturing in many industries. This work proposed an in-plane compensation plan for a fused deposition modeling (FDM) process, which provided a compensation solution for a process identifying abnormalities. Mathematical models are built to predict the deviation of a 2-D shape, and a compensation algorithm is derived based on this model. With the proposed methodology, a special compensation system can be developed for an FDM machine. This system analyzes the measurement of specifically designed test products, derives a compensation plan, and modifies any 2-D computer-aided design model to increase the shape fidelity of the product. In addition to the application in advanced manufacturing, we also have results related to the service industry: "Statistical Monitoring of Service Levels and Staffing Adjustments for Call Centers," Quality and Reliability Engineering International, 2016, and "Detection and Diagnosis of Distribution Changes of Degree Ratio in Complex Networks," Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods, 2015.

619913.label: Major findings and research outcome
619913.value: Major research findings: We have proposed a general framework first, and based on that, we have developed a methodology for high-dimensional data that is applicable to many areas including geographic disease surveillance, agriculture pest surveillance, astronomy, ecology, geography, sociology, and public health monitoring. Aimed at automatically and simultaneously detecting multiple clusters of any shape, our research explored the False Discovery (FD) approach originated from multiple hypothesis testing. We show that the FD approach can provide a higher detection power and better identification capability than conventional methods for high-dimensional data. In developing a monitoring scheme for mixed-type complex data, we have made a breakthrough by assuming that there is a latent continuous variable that determines the attribute levels of a categorical variable, so that the ordinal information among the attribute levels can be exploited. This enables us to simultaneously describe and monitor continuous and categorical data in a unified framework of standardized ranks. Our proposed methodology was shown to detect location shifts efficiently and is robust to various distributions. We did not come up with a general diagnostic approach for offline identification of multiple abnormalities, as this issue is more application oriented. We did however provide solutions to both advanced manufacturing such as the additive manufacturing process and service industries such as call centers and network monitoring and diagnosis. In sum, we have achieved all project objectives by publishing 10 journal papers, mostly in top journals in our field. One paper received the prestigious IISE Transactions 2018 Best Paper Award. I would like to mention that the paper in Annals of Statistics describes one of the most important theoretical breakthroughs in the last 50 years on the strict (not asymptotic) optimality of Bayesian change-point detection since Shiryaev's fundamental work in 1963. We have also presented our research results in the INFORMS flagship annual conference in 2015, 2016, and 2017 and received very positive feedback from both academics and practitioners.

619913.value: The technical challenges on statistical monitoring and diagnosis for large-scale and complex data streams are in fact evolving because of the recent advances in real-time sensors, IOT, and big data techniqes. I and my research team will continue working this emerging area and provide real solutions that will impact on both academia and industrial practice.

In addition, the inherent complexities of modern industries result in data with different features. Therefore, most data encountered in our daily lives are large in scale and complex. The central idea of this research is to develop statistical methodologies to achieve efficient monitoring and diagnosis and reduce process/product variation in the massive amounts of complex data that modern manufacturing and service industries are producing. For example, we have developed general online surveillance methodologies to identify unusual events that are spatially scattered, which is commonly seen in a large variety of applications including geographic disease surveillance, agriculture pest surveillance, astronomy, ecology, geography, sociology, and public health monitoring. The developed monitoring and diagnosis schemes have been applied to industrial processes where data streams are big and process knowledge is available. 620813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
620813.value: The development of aerospace technology has generated a strong demand on research associated with rarefied gas dynamics. The study of rarefied flow relies heavily on computational analysis due to the technical difficulties and high cost associated with generating and conducting measurements of high speed flow in the laboratory. In the case of high speed non-continuum flow, there are additional challenges due to complicated molecular physics, such as the vibrational excitation of molecules, dissociation, ionization, and various reaction. Under rarefied flow conditions, the conventional continuum equations of gas dynamics cease to describe flow physics accurately due to the significant amounts of thermal non-equilibrium. In diatomic gases, additional rotational and vibrational non-equilibrium will be present, resulting in a state of combined translational, rotational, and vibrational non-equilibrium. The purpose of this proposal is to further develop the unified gas-kinetic scheme for the study of non-equilibrium flows. In the past several years, an accurate gas-kinetic scheme has been developed for monatomic gases and used in many rarefied flow computations. The current research is to further develop such a scheme for diatomic gases and apply it in engineering applications. 航空技术的发展有很强的对稀薄气体研究的要求。由于技术上的困难和高速气体实验测量的高成本，稀薄气体的研究越来越依赖于计算和分析。对于高速非平衡流，更多的挑战来自于对复杂的分子物理的描述，像对振动，离解，电离，和化学反应的建模。在稀薄气体的条件下，由于没有足够的分子碰撞，通常描述连续流体的气体动力学方程不再成立。对于双原子分子，除了分子平动外，转动和振动的非平衡效应也需考虑。本研究课题是进一步发展统一的气体动理学格式对非平衡流的模拟。通过之前的几年研究，我们成功构造了单原子分子的气体动理学方法，并应用于很多稀薄流场的计算。本研究是进一步把统一格式发展到双原子分子，并应用于工程计算中。

620813.label: Realisation of objectives
620813.value: Based on the Rykov and Shakhov kinetic models, we have constructed unified gas kinetic scheme (UGKS) with the inclusion of rotational degree of freedom and inelastic particle collision for non-equilibrium diatomic flow simulations. The UGKS updates both macroscopic flow variables and microscopic distribution function with the numerical fluxes across a cell interface. The flux function couples particle transport and collisions in the gas evolution process. More specifically, the physical process from the kinetic particle free transport to the hydrodynamic pressure wave propagation is recovered in the flux function. This is the most important part for the design of a multiple scale method, which can be applied to all flow regimes. The UGKS has been validated through extensive numerical tests. For example, one of the UGKS codes for diatomic gas is based on the gas-kinetic Rykov model with a Landau–Teller–Jeans-type rotational energy relaxation. The scheme has been analyzed in both continuum and rarefied flow regimes. In the continuum limit, the multiple temperature Navier-Stokes type equations can be fully recovered, which go further to the standard Navier-Stokes equations with bulk viscosity in the limit of very small flow Knudsen number. Numerically, the homogeneous ﬂow relaxation, shock structure, hypersonic ﬂow passing a ﬂat plate, and the ﬂow around a blunt circular cylinder have been tested to validate the scheme. Many analytic, DSMC, and experimental solutions have been fully recovered from the UGKS simulations. Furthermore, the UGKS has been extended to the fully ionized gases, which is applied to the plasma simulation. Here the multiscale scheme can connect the flow physics from Vlasov particle transport to the magneto-hydrodynamic evolution. Based on the UGKS algorithm, many places, such as Northwest polytechnic university, China aerodynamic research and development center, Tsinghua university, as well as HKUST, have developed 3D unified parallelization codes and applied the codes to the hypersonic flow simulations around re-entry vehicles.

620813.label: Major findings and research outcome
620813.value: With the support of RGC620813, we have conducted the following research. We developed a unified gas-kinetic scheme for diatomic gases with the inclusion of rotational degree of freedom and the inelastic particle collision. The scheme has been tested in the whole flow regimes from the rarefied free molecular flow to the Navier-Stokes solutions. Theoretically, we analyzed the corresponding macroscopic governing equations of kinetic models in the continuum flow regime and figured out the correspondence between the rotational collision time and the bulk viscosity coefficient in the continuum flow regime. The scheme has been applied to the shock structure calculation from low Mach to hypersonic ones. At the same time, the scheme was used to simulate the experimental test for the flow passing through a flat plate at Mach number 4.89. The simulation results from the gas-kinetic scheme have been compared with the experimental measurements and DSMC solutions. A 3D code is under constructing. At China Aerodynamics Research and Development Center, a 3D parallel code has been developed and the code was used in the aerospace applications for the near space flight at hypersonic speed. Under research collaboration, other 3D codes have been developed at Northwest Polytechnic University and Tsinghua University. At the current stage, the implicit and multigrid techniques for the unified gas kinetic scheme have been developed as well for steady state calculations, where the efficiency has been improved significantly

620813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
620813.value: The development of numerical algorithm for hypersonic rarefied flow is a hot research topic, which is important for the understanding of non-equilibrium flows and its close connection to hypersonic flight. The development of unified gas kinetic scheme (UGKS) for diatomic gases through this project is of a great achievement in terms of the algorithm development. The UGKS is first reliable scheme which can be faithfully used in the non-equilibrium flow study from rarefied to continuum flow regimes. The potential application of the scheme is significant. Actually, a few 3D codes in real engineering applications have been developed worldwide by using the ideas related to outcome of the current research project. Beside non-equilibrium, the hypersonic flow is also associated with high temperature. The modelling of high temperature air chemistry in hypersonic flights under highly non-equilibrium conditions is complex. A rapid increase of translational energy occurs when the gas passes through an intense shock, causing strongly coupled processes such as excitation of internal energy modes, molecular dissociation, ionization, and radiation of the weakly ionized gas. The further development of UGKS for the chemical non-equilibrium flow will be the next research topic.

620813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
620813.value: The development of aerospace technology has generated a strong demand on research associated with rarefied gas dynamics. The study of rarefied flow relies heavily on computational analysis due to the technical difficulties and high cost associated with generating and conducting measurements of high speed flow in the laboratory. In the case of high speed non-continuum flow, there are additional challenges due to complicated molecular physics, such as the vibrational excitation of molecules, dissociation, ionization, and various reaction. Under rarefied flow conditions, the conventional continuum equations of gas dynamics cease to describe flow physics accurately due to the significant amounts of thermal non-equilibrium. In diatomic gases, additional rotational and vibrational non-equilibrium will be present, resulting in a state of combined translational, rotational, and vibrational non-equilibrium. Through this project, we have developed a unified gas-kinetic scheme for the study of non-equilibrium diatomic gases and applied the scheme to the engineering applications.

620913.label: Project Title(Chinese)
620913.value: 道路限速在交通网络中的多目标分析、建模和优化

620913.label: Project Objectives
620913.value: To analyze travelers’ speed and route choices at equilibrium under a link-specific speed limit scheme by taking into account their trade-off of time costs, fuel costs, expected accident costs and speeding ticket costs; To determine speed limit schemes for multi-objective optimization of system performance from the perspectives of travel time cost, safety, emission and/or energy consumption; To design hybrid schemes of speed limit and road pricing for multi-objective optimization of system performance by making use of their different but complementary mechanisms for traffic regulation.
