620913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
620913.value: Speed limits have been employed worldwide as a straightforward way to regulate vehicular speed, thereby enhancing safety and reducing fuel consumption and emissions. Previous studies on the effectiveness of speed limits have been affluent but mostly from a local road perspective. Intuitively, if a speed limit is imposed, travelers will adapt their driving speed on the road to reduce speeding ticket risk and thus incur a longer travel time, which in turn may induce to change their routes. Therefore, a speed limit on one road can influence the flows on other roads and thus generate a new equilibrium flow pattern on the network; it is essential to choose and optimize speed limits from a network-wide perspective. This project proposes to investigate the optimal design and evaluation of speed limits for the purpose of safety enhancement, energy saving and emission reduction on general networks. The first part of the project will focus on characterizing travelers’ route choice behavior and adherence to a given speed limit scheme at user equilibrium. The subjective travel time cost, the perceived crash risk, and the perceived speeding ticket cost of travelers will be taken into account as determinant factors for their actual speed and route choices. The second part will focus on optimal design of speed limits for enhancing safety and reducing emission and energy consumption. Multiple integer levels of speed limit such as 50 or 60 km/h are considered and the resulting speed limit design problem is formulated as a bi-level discrete network design problem and solved efficiently by the latest novel methods developed by the investigator. The third part of the project will investigate hybrid schemes of speed limits and road pricing for network flow control and management. Speed limit increases travel time on a road to deter traffic flow, whereas road pricing increases monetary cost but decreases travel time by reducing traffic volume and thus increasing speed on a congested road. Their different but complementary mechanisms for traffic regulation make their integration a promising instrument to improve system performance. Given the wide implementation of speed limits around the world but only limited considerations from a system-wide perspective, the proposed research is of great importance. It provides a new perspective to look into the impacts of speed limits on traffic equilibrium and system performance in networks, and help the system planner make a better choice of speed limits for multi-objective system optimization. 道路限速作为一项能直接调节车速、提高道路安全同时减少燃料消耗和尾气排放的手段，早已在全球范围内被广泛采用。在已有的文献中，有大量对道路限速作用的研究，然而这些研究多数都着眼于局部路段。直观来看，一旦实施道路限速，出行者为了避免超速收到罚单而适当降低行车速度，这样将会导致出行者的出行时间相应延长，甚至改变出行者的路径选择行为。因此，对一条路段实行速度限制将会影响其他路段上的交通流量，从而产生一个新的交通均衡，所以我们很有必要从整个交通网络的角度出发对道路限速进行分析与优化。 该项目将会以提高道路安全、节省燃料和降低尾气排放量为目标，对交通网络中道路限速的优化和评价问题进行系统地研究。项目的第一部分将着重研究出行者的路径选择行为和其在交通均衡下对给定的限速标准的忠诚度。主观的出行时间成本、感知的车祸和超速受罚的风险是影响出行者在实际中选择行车速度和路径的决定性因素。项目的第二部分研究以提高道路安全、节省燃料和降低尾气排放量为目标的道路限速的优化问题。考虑到在实际应用中道路限速的标准多以10的整数倍的形式出现，如50或60公里/小时，我们将道路限速的优化问题改写为一个双层的离散网络设计问题，并且利用新的算法有效地解决了该问题。项目的第三部分将会研究道路限速和拥挤道路收费的混合方案在交通网络流量控制和管理中的作用。道路限速会延长出行时间、从而降低路段上的交通流量；而拥挤道路收费的作用是增加出行的货币成本，从而使路段上的交通流量相应地下降，行车速度提高，导致出行时间成本降低。这两项手段在交通网络中的影响不同，但又能互为补充，使得道路限速和拥挤道路收费的混合方案有望成为提高系统性能的有力工具。 鉴于道路限速在全世界的广泛应用以及现有文献在系统全局层次上的研究缺陷，该项目的研究具有重大意义。该项目将会为人们看待道路限速对交通均衡和系统性能的作用开辟一个新的视角，从而为系统的规划设计者在考虑以多个系统指标对道路限速进行优化时提供理论支持。

Previous studies on the effectiveness of speed limits have been affluent but mostly from a local road perspective. Intuitively, if a speed limit is imposed, travelers will adapt their driving speed on the road to reduce speeding ticket risk and thus incur a longer travel time, which in turn may induce them to change their routes. Therefore, a speed limit on one road can influence the flows on other roads and thus generate a new equilibrium flow pattern in the network; it is essential to choose and optimize speed limits from a network-wide perspective. Given the wide implementation of speed limits around the world but only limited considerations from a system-wide perspective, this project investigated the optimal design and evaluation of speed limits for the purpose of safety enhancement, energy saving and emission reduction in general networks. 620913.label: Major findings and research outcome
620913.value: Under a link-specific speed limit scheme, travelers choose driving speed and routes at equilibrium by taking into account their trade-off of time costs, fuel costs, expected accident costs and speeding ticket costs. It is found that the crash risk with homogeneous users depends on the absolute speed only, while the crash risk with heterogeneous users depends on both the absolute speed and the speed variance among the user classes. The traffic equilibrium problem can be formulated as variational inequalities and solved by an iterative Gauss–Seidel-type algorithm. Publications: Yang, H., Ye, H., Li, X. and Zhao, B., 2015. Speed limits, speed selection and network equilibrium. Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies, Vol. 51, 260–273. Effectiveness of variable speed limits (VSLs) on improving traffic flow efficiency and reducing vehicular emissions was examined in a stylized setting of morning commute where a fixed number of individuals commute from home to work on the freeway with a single recurrent bottleneck. A mechanism was developed for a VSL system to prevent the bottleneck from being activated and thus avoid detrimental capacity drop that arises at the activated bottleneck. The VSL system installed along the freeway towards the bottleneck can adjust commuters’ cruising speeds in a continuous fashion and essentially regulates the upstream flow into the bottleneck. By investigating the resulting departure-time equilibrium of commuters, it is found that the VSL system can eliminate the efficiency loss caused by capacity drop Publication: Liu, W., Yin, Y., Yang, H., 2015. Effectiveness of variable speed limits considering commuters’ long term response. Transportation Research Part B: Methodological, Vol.81, 498–519. Speed limit increases travel time on a road to deter traffic flow, whereas road pricing increases monetary cost but decreases travel time by reducing traffic volume and thus increasing speed on a congested road. Their different but complementary mechanisms for traffic regulation make their integration a promising instrument to improve system performance. A hybrid scheme of speed limit and road pricing was found to decentralize Pareto-efficient flow and speed patterns that minimize total travel time and total emissions simultaneously in a general transportation network. For any favorable Pareto-efficient solution, we established the existence of hybrid schemes of speed limit and non-negative/revenue-neutral tolls, under which the Pareto-efficient speed and flow pattern is one of the possible user-equilibrium solutions. 620913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
620913.value: High speed driving has been reported to be a contributing factor to high vehicle emissions and high fuel consumption. In view of the fact that road traffic is one of the major sources of greenhouse emissions and fuel consumption, speed limits have also been introduced to prohibit high speed driving for energy and environmental considerations in many cases. On the other hand, imposing speed limits inevitably impacts travel time or mobility. Thus it is critical to design an appropriate speed limit scheme by taking into account the trade-off between travel time, fatality rate, vehicle emissions and/or fuel consumption. This project investigated the impacts of link-specific speed limit schemes in a traffic equilibrium manner in general networks. Efficient speed limit strategies were developed for enhancing safety, reducing vehicular emission and/or saving energy consumption. Apart from improving our fundamental analysis and understanding of the impacts of speed limits in a broader context, this project provided a network-wide efficient strategy for speed limit design to enhance system performance.

621013.label: Project Title(Chinese)
621013.value: 基于群体智慧的迁移学习

621013.label: Project Objectives
621013.value: The first challenging problem is target data selection for initial labeling. In our transfer-learning framework, given a learning task with no or few labeled training data, our first objective is to design an effective strategy to select a set of data, which if labeled, could best benefit to the target learner in terms of enabling transfer learning. This set of data should maximally enable the transfer of knowledge from the auxiliary to the target domain. Different target-data selection approaches will be designed and evaluated, where the strategies will take both source domain knowledge and annotator’s ability in consideration. A number of selection strategies will be evaluated. We will evaluate the approach on text document data sets. Quality control for target data labeling is subtle. After the data selection is done, we need to distribute the selected data to crowds of non-expert annotators to label. Our second objective is to design a method that derives high quality labeled data from the crowdsourced noisy data, as using noisy annotations can degrade the task performance. We will ensure that the resulting data are associated with the correct labels even when there is few supervision from target domain. Novel strategies for data cleaning will be designed to address the quality control problem by using knowledge from both the source and the target domains. Knowledge transfer with uncertain labeling is a crucial component. Our next objective is to design an efficient and effective model for transferring knowledge to the target domain, given that the target domain data labels may still contain some noise. We need to adapt the conventional transfer learning algorithms to accommodate multiple annotators who provide uncertain labels. The learning model must be compatible with knowledge trans- fer from auxiliary. A novel model will be designed for this new transfer learning problem. Evaluation is the last unsolved problem. We will develop a prototype system for transfer learning via crowdsourcing using the context of text classification based on scalable algorithms. We will evaluate the system using many real-world text classification data sets. We will disseminate the research results in the form of high-quality publications, and make the demonstration and algorithms available in an open-source manner.

621013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
621013.value: 在许多机器学习应用中，最耗时和昂贵的任务是收集一个足够大的可靠的数据集。获得这些标签涉及昂贵的人力劳动，例如请专家们提供这样的标签。因此，如何设计一个可持续发展的模式以降低获得标签的成本，是需要解决的一个关键问题。获取数据标签是最近的一个方法是通过转移学习， 这样可以用Web和其他辅助数据可以用来作为知识转移的原数据。有研究表明，在正确使用时，迁移学习的确可以节省大量的标签，进而获得一个高素质的模型。 然而，有效的迁移学习要求目标学习领域有一些标记的数据来指导知识转移，这个初始标记的数据可以学习成功转移的关键。为此，我们建议利用的众包的方法获得人的群体智慧，来提供所需要的数据的标签，亚马逊的MTurk系统，就已经在众包上之取得了很多成功。在这一研究计划中， 一个关键的问题是设计一个数据选择策略来标记数据以提高在辅助领域的选择数据质量，以确保被迁移的知识的质量。我们需要选择一个小而有效的目标人群标签数据，但不同的数据集将导致相当不同的学习质量。我们既需要认真考虑数据迁移的质量问题， 又要考虑目标域数据的可靠性，尤其是在面对在众包过程中有可能引入噪声数据标签。 在这一项目中， 我们将使用广泛的现实世界的数据开展研究，开发和评估一个可伸缩的原型系统， 把迁移学习和众包结合起来。 并且， 我们将在基于上下文的文本分类的应用上用实验来验证我们的新算法。

621013.label: Realisation of objectives
621013.value: Crowd sourcing needs a lot of human labor to complete, and yet the accuracy of annotating the data is not guaranteed. In this project, we have developed a new method that uses transfer learning to help judge the quality of annotation results and give an accurate picture of the annotators themselves. In particular, we have accomplished the following goals: 1. We have grounded the annotation work in the field of AI planning, and developed a new technique to use transfer learning to help correct the annotations of human labelers. In this work, we combine both manual editing of the action models in planning and use the learned knowledge to help correct the labels by leveraging the knowledge from auxiliary domains. This is accomplished through target data selection and instance based transfer learning. This result has been reported in our AI Journal articles in 2014. These results correspond to the first two objectives of our project. 2. We have developed a transfer-learning based hashing method for heterogeneous objects. This task is accomplished by designing a hashing mechanism in order to find the corresponding objects to help label the data in the target domain. We have published the result in ACM KDD and ACM Transactions on KDD in 2016, which corresponds to our third objective. 3. Finally, we have successfully tested the developed algorithms and prototype systems in the context of text classification. The systems made use of transfer learning algorithms to both facilitate the noise-removal process of annotating the data and quality evaluation. These are reported in our papers published at AAAI in 2015/2016. In all, we have successfully completed all objectives set out to accomplish that uses transfer learning to help improve the quality of data annotation. We have published the results in top venues such as AAAI, KDD, and AI Journal.

621013.label: Major findings and research outcome
621013.value: We have successfully achieved our goal of developing a platform in which we can obtain high-quality data labels via crowd-sourcing and transfer learning. Our first subgoal was to choose an auxiliary set of source data to benefit the labeling of target data. To achieve this goal, we have designed an algorithm to first select source data from the vast space of available data. The auxiliary data can be used for initial labeling. In our transfer-learning framework, given a learning task of very little labeled training data, our algorithm can be used to design an effective strategy to enable data labeling and data-editor evaluation so that the best benefit can be obtained for the target learner through transfer learning. This set of data should maximally enable the transfer of knowledge from the auxiliary to the target domain. We have developed a selection strategy that determines which labels are transferred from the source to target data. In this project, we have also developed a technique to distribute the selected dataset to derive high-quality labeled data from the crowdsourced data. This allows us to use very little supervision from people in the target domain. We showed that the new algorithm allows for strong quality control by using knowledge from both the source and the target domains. Finally, we have also designed an efficient and effective model for transferring knowledge to the target domain, even though some labels contain noise. Multiple annotators can be allowed as well and the system can use transfer learning to help make the final annotations consistent with the domain knowledge. We have already developed a prototype system for transfer learning via crowdsourcing as well as experimented with a number of data sets on classification tasks. The outcome is in the form of publications as well as prototype algorithm systems.

621013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
621013.value: We will further develop the prototype system so that it can work with social data to allow the data labelling to be propagated through a social network. We plan to consider extending the crowdsourcing system to allow the system to select authors based on their capabilities.

621013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
621013.value: Crowdsourcing allows data to be labeled via cost effective and efficient means. However, crowdsourcing is prone to noise and errors due to potential diversity of data labelers. We solve this problem using transfer learning, by leveraging the quality data in related but different datasets already labeled by people. We show how to select data, how to exploit the labeling knowledge in the source data, and how to effectively transfer the labeling knowledge into the target domain data, to allow high quality and efficient labeling of the target domain data. The project solves a major problem in large-scale machine learning and data mining, that is, how to obtain high quality big data.

621113.label: Project Objectives
621113.value: Develop a microfluidic device that is capable of changing and detecting the concentration of denaturants such as urea and guanidine hydrochloride (GuHCl) in mixing time on the order of microseconds. 621113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
621113.value: 蛋白质在获寻它功能形态或构造的结构变化过程称为蛋白质折叠。蛋白质折叠是一个复杂的生物学过程，很多生理学和病理学现象都包含其中。在蛋白质从一级氨基酸序列到特定三维结构形成过程中，很多最基本的折叠步骤发生在微秒到毫秒的时间量级。研究这些早期的折叠活动对理解蛋白质折叠是怎样被发起和引导到特定折叠路径起到至关重要的作用，并且研究早期的折叠事件已然成为蛋白质折叠研究的焦点之一。为了观测早期的蛋白质折叠步骤和瞬时状态，通常需要在更短的时间量级通过改变外部环境（例如：突然稀释化学变性剂）来迫使蛋白质达到非平衡状态。然而，很多常规的混合和探测方法缺乏时间和结构分辨率，致使获得详细的快速动力学数据来阐述蛋白质折叠机制仍然是个挑战。 这里，我们融合了微流体混合和扫描双光子显微技术的优势来获取时间分辨的蛋白质色氨酸自发荧光，并以此提出了一个检测蛋白质折叠动力学的通用方法。不同于那些依赖湍流混合的停流技术和淬灭流技术， 微流体混合芯片用水力聚集的方法（层流）不仅使混合时间降低到十微秒以下，而且样品消耗量降低到皮升每秒。更重要的是，微流体混合芯片允许时间轴上的动力学活动在液体流动方向上的不同位置点上被观察到，促使它在显微系统下拥有极高的时间分辨率。由于色氨酸的吲哚发色基团荧光参数（如：光谱、光量子产率和荧光寿命）对所处的外部环境极为敏感，使得色氨酸成为理想的以及最流行的构型变化和分子内部作用力的探头之一。我们将利用时间分辨的双光子激发显微系统来获取色氨酸荧光光谱和寿命数据，以此来建立一个可以用来提取蛋白质折叠反应常数和中间态的系统构架。 我们按照这份提议的研究，发展了一个更加便利的平台用来研究蛋白质折叠问题。这个平台以揭示重要的结构折叠活动为目的，并且希望对未知的早期蛋白质折叠问题提供有价值的观点。在基础科学研究中，微流控芯片和高端的显微光谱技术的结合为生命科学交叉学科的研究跨出了重要的一步。我们期望这个提案能对检测多种生物和化学系统的动力学过程提供标准参照信息。

621113.label: Realisation of objectives
621113.value: 1. Objective 1 was fully realized. We designed and fabricated a microfluidic mixing device that can initiate a concentration jump on a microsecond timescale. The microfluidic mixing devices were developed in silicon substrate using standard lithography and fabrication technology. We established pressure control systems for device operation and measurement. We characterize the system using the diffusion limited reaction of I ions quenching Trp fluorescence. The fluid flow and concentration fields in the mixer were also simulated using Comsol Multiphysics. The device missing time was measured as ~6 ± 1 μs in both experiments and simulations. 2. Objective 2 was fully realized. The micromixer is coupled with a scanning two-photon microscopy system that records both spectra and lifetime detection of Trp fluorescence. The two-photon excitation microscopy offers two distinct merits: first, using two-photon excitation of the Trp fluorescence allows the use of a visible wavelength laser, thus the device can be built using normal glass and silicon instead of fused silica. Second, two-photon excitation is restricted to a tightly focused detection volume with a high degree of rejection of out-of-focus background fluorescence. Thus the combined technique is capable of probing the intermolecular distance change with temporal resolution at microsecond level and structural resolution at Angstrom level, and the use of two-photon excitation enables us to more broadly explore FRET with a spectrum ranging from near UV to visible wavelengths. 3. Objective 3 was fully realized. We applied single value decomposition (SVD) and global analysis to analyze the results, and all of the obtained data were analyzed using customer-built programs in MATLAB. For example, the changes of the Trp fluorescence decay rate along the cytochrome c refolding time course reveals the conformational transition of cytochrome c during its refolding pathway. The measured tr-FRET Trp fluorescence decay curves were first analyzed using SVD. SVD analysis results indicate two folding states, a transient state and an intermediate state, of cytochrome c during its first 500 μs refolding time domain. Therefore, a two-exponential decay model was used in the global analysis. 4. Objective 4 was fully realized. We demonstrated the combination of the time-resolved fluorescence resonance energy transfer (tr-FRET) measurement and the ultrarapid hydrodynamic focusing microfluidic mixer to observe very early steps and transient states events in the horse cytochrome c refolding by monitoring the distance between the tryptophan (Trp-59) -heme donor-acceptor (D-A) pair. The global analysis results reveal a transient state with the shortest decay rate of 0.81 ± 0.02 ns−1, corresponding to a D−A distance of ∼31 Å, and an intermediate state with a decay rate of ∼4.1 ns−1, corresponding to a D−A distance of ∼22 Å, are populated at ∼10 μs and ∼350 μs respectively.

621113.label: Major findings and research outcome
621113.value: 1) We demonstrated the combination of the time-resolved fluorescence resonance energy transfer (tr-FRET) measurement and the ultrarapid hydrodynamic focusing microfluidic mixer for investigating the early folding states of cytochrome c by monitoring the distance between the tryptophan (Trp-59) -heme donor-acceptor (D-A) pair. The ~6 ± 1 μs mixing time of the microfluidic mixer allows us to rapidly initiate protein refolding upon the dilution of a denaturant solution, guanidine hydrochloride, and the evolution of protein conformational change in the mixer is monitored through tr-FRET using a fast time correlated single photon counting (TCSPC) system. The transformation of folding states of cyt c in the first 500 μs of refolding was revealed on a microsecond time scale. When unfolded cyt c is rapidly triggered to refold, the extend conformation transitions rapidly within 10 µs to a transient state with a characterized Trp-59-heme distance of ~31 Å. Later, the protein chain further compacts and a folding intermediate with a characterized Trp-59-heme distance of ~22 Å is generally populated and becomes dominant after ~350 µs. (Analytical Chemistry 2015) 2) We further developed a three-dimensional (3D) flow focusing microfluidic mixer that is applicable for studying the formation of a wide range of nanomaterials. Using the mixer, we investigated the formation of aggregation-induced emission (AIE) hexaphenylsilole nanoparticles. We also demonstrated that the mixer can resolve the microsecond kinetics of nanoparticle self-assembly in two distinct steps, suggesting that nanoparticle formation follows the classical nucleation and growth theory. (IEEE Transactions on Nanotechnology, 2016) 3) We also conducted a collaborative project on quantifying molecular hydrophobic interactions by monitoring fluorescence induced by hydrophobic aggregation in a microfluidic mixer. We probed fluorescence induced by aggregation upon rapid mixing of water and hydrophobic solute and real-time monitored hydrophobic aggregation in bulk solution on a microsecond time scale. We then fitted the measured fluorescence to the classical nucleation-growth theory. We show that hydrophobic association of a Hexaphenylsilole monomer to its aggregate in water occurs at sub-microseconds, and the associated free energy change is ‒5.9 to ‒13.6 kcal/mol. (Nature Communication, in revision) 4) As a side project, we further developed an on-demand nanofluidic device for biomolecule concentration. By wisely implementing an on-demand droplet generation module, our system can adaptively encapsulate the highly concentrated sample and effectively enhance long-term stability. This study offers a mechanism to concentrate the sample in low-abundant biomolecules for detection and analysis. (Lab on a chip, 2015)

621113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
621113.value: Suggested work for further development: 1) The micromixer developed in this project is used for initiating protein folding/unfolding through a rapid change in denaturant concentration. Similarly, a pH or temperature jump can also trigger the protein conformational change. In future work, modified micromixers may be developed to enable the change in the pH or temperature of the buffer in the require range and microscale so that the rapid mixing scheme can be used for studying protein folding/unfolding in a broader aspect. 2) In principle, this combined tool can also be used to investigate any macromolecule conformational changes such as RNA folding, molecular interactions in enzyme catalysis, and protein-protein interactions on the micro- to millisecond time scale. In order to reveal locally specific or overall structural or conformational change during the process, we need to design the florescence probes such as FRET to capture intensity or lifetimes associated with these changes 3) This work can be extended for the investigation of nanomaterial self-assembling processes, which have been briefly explored by looking at AIE nanoparticle formation. Further research can be developed for other fundamental studies such as molecular hydrophobic interactions, aromatic stacking forces, etc.

621113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
621113.value: Protein folding is the process by which a protein structure assumes its functional shape or conformation. Proper folding is required for a protein to carry out its functions, while improper folding can be a source of diseases such as mad cow, Alzheimer’s, Parkinson's, and many cancers. Most fundamental events in structural formation of proteins take place in the range of microsecond to millisecond timescales. In this project, by leveraging the advantages of ultrafast mixing using microfluidics technology and advanced fluorescence microscopy using a two-photon excitation microscope, we have developed an approach for studying protein folding dynamics by real-time monitoring the fluorescence from the amino acid tryptophan. We developed a microfluidic mixing device that allows for rapid initiation of protein refolding upon the dilution of a biochemical solution that causes proteins to unfold, and assessment of intermediate states in the evolution of protein conformational change. We expect this platform will become a powerful tool for monitoring the dynamic processes of biomolecules in solutions on a microsecond timescale and enable us to diagnose the important events otherwise inaccessible, which may provide fundamentals of structural and conformational information in macromolecules or self-assembly of nanomaterials.

621213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
621213.value: To be able to control light and waves has been a century-long dream and fascination of human beings. The invention of metamaterials with exotic properties that are unavailable in nature and the state-of-the-art fabrication tools have enabled the realization of that dream. In the past decade, significant progress has been made towards wave manipulation. New materials and concepts have been proposed and implemented, resulting in unprecedented applications such as broadband sound insulation in the low-frequency range and superlenses with nanometer resolution. One of the most fascinating applications is the invisibility cloak. A seminar approach for realizing such a cloak is to utilize transformation-based solutions to the conductivity and Maxwell’s equations in curvilinear coordinate systems. This approach together with the concept of metamaterials provides an effective design tool for controlling acoustic and electromagnetic waves around arbitrarily sized and shaped solids, leading to a surge of interest and an emerging area known as transformation optics. Unfortunately, transformation based approaches are in general not applicable to the design of cloaking structures for elastic waves. As a consequence, very little work has been done on the controlling of elastic waves, largely due to the lack of an effective and systematic design tool. The goal of the proposed studies is to develop a systematic design methodology for elastic wave manipulation built upon optimization techniques. Accurate and efficient numerical methods based on the pre-corrected Fast-Fourier-Transformation accelerated boundary element method will be developed to predict wave fields in an inhomogeneous medium. The design tool will be applied to the design of two cloaking structures to control a shear wave propagating in a 2D medium and an elastic wave inside a 3D block. The ability of steering or redirecting elastic waves in a desired manner opens the door for a wide range of important applications such as vibration isolation and seismic cloaks, which would have a significant impact in aeronautic, automotive, ship industries and other aspects of human life. The successful completion of this project would produce, for the first time, a general design tool build upon high-fidelity numerical techniques that allows the control of elastic waves in a systematic way. The two proposed applications not only serve as test cases for evaluating the effectiveness of the design tool, but also pave the way towards the design of passive anti-earthquake systems for the protection of buildings. 一个世纪以来人类一直梦想能够控制光和波的传播。具有自然界本不存在的超常特性的超材料的发明及目前先进的制造手段可以实现这个梦想。在过去十年中，对波的控制已经取得了长足进步。新材料和新概念的提出和实施实现了前所未有的应用，例如低频范围内宽频带隔声和具有纳米级分辨率的超级透镜。 最引人入胜的应用之一是隐形斗篷。实现这种斗篷的启蒙思路是利用对曲线坐标系下的传导率和麦克斯韦方程进行坐标变换所得的解。这种方法与超材料的概念一起提供了一种有效控制声波和电磁波在任意大小和形状的固体周围传播的设计工具，从而开辟一个引人关注的新领域：变换光学。不幸的是，基于转换的方法一般并不适用于对弹性波的隐形结构的设计。因此，现有的工作很少有对弹性波进行控制的，其主要原因是缺乏一个有效而系统的设计工具。 本研究的目的是发展一个基于优化方法的控制弹性波的系统设计方法。我们将发展基于预校正的快速傅立叶变换加速边界元法的精确而高效的数值方法来预测在非均匀介质中的传播的波场。此方法将被应用于设计两个隐形结构分别控制弹性横波在二维介质和三维体积内的传播。 有效控制弹性波传播预示着广泛而重要的应用，如隔振和地震斗篷。这些应用将对航空，汽车和船舶等行业和人类生活的其他方面产生深远的影响。本项目的成功完成将首创一种基于高精度数值方法的能够对弹性波进行系统控制的普适设计工具。本研究所包含的的两个应用不仅作为有效评估设计工具的测试算例，同时也为保护建筑物的被动抗震系统的设计铺平了道路。

621213.label: Realisation of objectives
621213.value: The three objectives proposed in the proposal have all been achieved. We have successfully developed 3D boundary element codes, which are capable of simulating any elastic wave propagating inside a composite material with arbitrarily distributed inclusions/voids of any shape and size (objective 1). Two versions of the boundary element code were created, one was accelerated with the pre-corrected Fast Fourier Transfer (p-FFT) technique as mentioned in the proposal, and the other was accelerated with the fast directional multipole method, a relatively newly developed method, which was not mentioned in the proposal. Both versions can handle large-scale problems while the fast directional multipole method having a slightly lower complexity for general problems. The codes were verified with several benchmark problems of elastodynamics. In addition, by setting Poisson ratio equal to 0.5, the elastodynamic equation becomes Stokes equation, and the code can be used to simulate Stokes flow problems. As an additional application of the developed algorithms, numerical study of the effects of morphology and distribution of endothelial cells on flow transport in blood vessels was conducted. For the method development, we compared two competing approaches for simulation wave propagation: convolution quadrature method and frequency-domain approach. We pointed out, for the first time, the theoretical connection between the two methods and provided the guideline on the selection of the two methods. For the second objective, we have completed sensitivity analysis and developed the code, which has been integrated with the BEM code for elastic wave propagation and the sequential quadratic programming (SQP) technique to form a design tool. The tool was used to design a 2D cloak consisting of two-phase multilayered circular rings (objective 3). This material is able to shield any objects located inside the ring from the external shear wave. We also compared the performance of the SQP with that of the genetic algorithm and found that at least for this particular example, the performances of the two optimization techniques were comparable. In addition to the tasks proposed in the project, we have also developed design approaches based on topological optimization techniques and constructed codes, which allow us to design a much broad class of metamaterials for elastic wave manipulation. Using the developed codes, we have successfully designed hyperbolic metamaterials. Compared with the existing designs, our design has a higher imaging resolution and a lower energy loss. We have also designed metasurfaces with a prescribed phase profile. Metasurfaces are newly emerged artificial materials. Compared to the bulk metamaterials, metasurfaces are much thinner and thus have a wider range of applications. The current designs of metasurfaces either work for a single frequency or have low transmissions, which are not suitable for practical applications. With the developed design techniques, we were able to incorporate the requirement of high transmission and broadband operation. As a result, our designs all have a transmission coefficient larger than 0.9, and work within a frequency band of 10%. This work was conducted during the no-cost extension period.

621213.label: Major findings and research outcome
621213.value: Major findings and research outcomes corresponding to the three objectives and additional work are listed as follows. The original proposed work: A design tool consisting of (1) an efficient 3D elastic wave solver for any composite materials based on the Boundary Element Method accelerated with the pFFT or the fast directional multipole method, (2) a sensitivity solver for the displacement with respect to the design variables and (3) an optimization box based on either the SQP or the genetic algorithm has bee developed. The tool allows the design of metamaterials with fixed topology and shape. A 2D cloak material has been designed for shear wave. In addition, as the applications of the developed wave solver, study of the effects of the morphology and distribution of endothelial cells on flow transport in blood vessels has been conducted, which indicates the importance of these factors on the blood transport and consequently the atherosclerosis development. We also used the code to study coherent shear wave in porous materials. Based on the simulation results, a formula for the attenuation coefficient of the SH wave has been derived. During the course of the project, we initiated a collaboration with Prof. Martin Schanz from Graz University of Technology and worked on the theoretical and numerical study of the two popular methods in simulating wave propagation. A total of two conference papers and two journal papers have been resulted from this part of work. The extra work conducted during the no-cost extension period: We have developed a two-step topological optimization scheme and applied it to successfully design broadband non-resonant hyperbolic metamaterials. These artificial materials can be used as filters which allow only longitudinal wave to propagate within a desired frequency band. They can also be used as super lens with resolutions far beyond the diffraction limit. In addition, negative refraction and wave partial focusing can also be achieved and have been demonstrated. The work was presented in the World Congress of Computational Mechanics 2018, New York and a journal paper was just accepted by Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering (CMAME), the number one journal in computational mechanics. We have also just developed genetic algorithm based topological optimization method and applied it to design metasurfaces with a prescribed phase profile and high transmission. A series microstructures have been designed which are able to alter the phase of an incident elastic wave by a desired amount. This allows us to steel and control the wave propagation direction anyway we wish and would have important applications in areas such as structure health monitoring and bio-imaging. We are currently preparing two journal papers on this work. This would be the first reported work on broadband non-resonant metasurfaces with high transmission for longitudinal and shear waves.

621213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
621213.value: The design of artificial materials particularly the metasurfaces is still in its early research stage. There are many possible directions that one can follow to continue this research effort. We plan in the immediately near future to set up an experimental platform for elastic wave detection. We will use this platform to measure wave propagation in the designed metamaterials/metasurces and to demonstrate their performance in wave manipulation. In the meantime, we plan to continue the development of advanced design methods and apply them to design artificial materials suitable for practical applications, that is, those that are easy to fabrication, with low energy loss and robust, etc.

621213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
621213.value: To be able to control light and waves has been a century-long dream and fascination of human beings. The use of elaborately designed microstructures to alter the dispersion of materials consisting of these periodic microstructures has enabled the realization of this dream. In the past decade, significant progress has been made towards light and acoustic wave manipulation. However little has been done in the manipulation of elastic wave largely due to the difficulties in the design of microstructures. In this project, we have developed several design tools based on efficient Boundary Elememt Method and optimization techniques such as genetic algorithms and topological optimization. These systematic design tools allow us to successfully design a set of metamaterials/metasurfaces for elastic wave manipulation such as shear wave cloaking , arbitrary wave steering and focusing. These results pave the way for practical applications in structure health monitoring, earthquake protection and biological imaging.

621413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
621413.value: A database system's primary function is to answer users' queries. These queries can be broadly classified into two categories: reporting queries and aggregation queries. The former retrieves a collection of records from the database that match the query's conditions, while the latter only produces an aggregate, such as count, sum, average or max (min), of a particular attribute of these records. With reporting queries, the database is simply used as a data storage-retrieval tool. Many modern business intelligence applications, however, require complex analytical queries with a rapid execution time. Users issuing these analytical queries are interested not in the actual records, but some statistics of these records. This has therefore led to extensive research on how to perform aggregation queries efficiently. The techniques typically rely on pre-computation and various data structures (a.k.a. indexing structures) so that the aggregates can be computed efficiently at query time without going through the actual query results. Unfortunately, reporting and aggregation queries provide only two extremes for analyzing the data, by returning either all the records matching the query condition or one (or a few) single-valued aggregates. These simple aggregates are not expressive enough, and data analysts often need more insight into the data distribution. Currently, what they can do is to first issue a reporting query to retrieve all the records, and then use another tool to perform further analysis on the retrieved data. This is time-consuming and wasteful, as the analysts are not actually interested in all the raw results, which can be voluminous. In this project, we plan to design data structures that can be implemented inside the database so that it can efficiently return summaries that are more expressive and complex than the simple aggregates currently supported, instead of giving out the raw query results. The types of summaries we plan to support include heavy hitters, quantiles, histograms, and wavelets, which provide different views on the underlying data distribution to meet the analysts' different needs. An important feature of these summaries is that they allow a tunable size-accuracy trade-off, thus providing a smooth transition between the two extremes of reporting everything and a simple aggregate. 當前數據庫的查詢可以分為彙報查詢（reporting queries）和結果查詢（aggregate queries）兩種。可是在大規模數據分析任務中，兩種查詢方式均不能滿足用戶需求：彙報查詢返回全部結果，數據量太大，用戶還要進行冗長的後續分析，而結果查詢只返回單一結果，表達性不夠。因此，本研究目的在於引入概括查詢（summary queries），即返回全部結果的一個概括，使得用戶可以在總體上對查詢結果有一個概括性的瞭解。

621413.label: Realisation of objectives
621413.value: We have successfully achieved all 3 objectives of this project. Objective 1 To achieve objective 1, we first answer the theoretical question of whether optimal indexing is possible for summary queries. We first observe that the optimal query time can be easily achieved if the summary is subtractive. All sketches that are linear projections of the data, such as the Count-Min sketch and the AMS sketch, have this property. However, for nonsubtractive summaries, such as heavy hitters and quantile, the problem becomes nontrivial. To achieve optimality for these summaries, we define an exponentially decomposable property enjoyed by these summaries. We first show how this property leads to an optimal internal memory index, and then convert it to an external memory index with nontrivial data structuring techniques. Next, we turn to the practical aspect of the problem. Our theoretically optimal index is unlikely to yield a practical implementation, and the hidden constants in the big-O’s are quite large. The one for subtractive summaries is simple, but it is inherently static. Nevertheless, some ideas in the development of the theory are still useful in designing a simpler and practical index structure for summary queries. We then design a simplified, practical version of our index. In doing so, we have to settle for a slightly worse asymptotic running time in favor of smaller constants and easier implementation. In addition, the practical version of the index is fully dynamic, that is, it supports insertion and deletion of records efficiently. Objective 2 To extend our one-dimensional results to multi-dimensions, we take a sampling-based approach. We first consider how one may adapt existing methods to solve this problem, and show that these approaches suffer from various types of limitations. Then we design a new indexing structure, LS-tree, which is based on the idea of “level sampling”. It is a collection of R-trees where each R-tree indexes a set of samples from the original data set. The sampling rates for these sets of samples form a geometric series. The LS-tree needs to maintain and query multiple trees, which in practice may not be ideal. Thus, we design another new indexing structure, RS-tree, which needs to build, maintain, and query a single R-tree, by embedding samples into the R-tree. Finally, we tailor this structure for memory-based, disk-resident, and hybrid scenarios. Objective 3 Based on the indexing structures we have designed, we built a system prototype that supports various summary queries over multi-dimensional data. The system uses online sampling, which continuously returns randomly sampled points from a user specified spatio-temporal query region, until the user terminates the process or enough samples have been obtained to meet an accuracy requirement. An unbiased estimator, tailored towards a given analytical query, is built using the spatial online samples, and its approximation quality improves in an online fashion while more samples are being returned. To make it easy for users and different applications to enjoy the benefit of spatio-temporal online analytics and aggregation, our system also implements a data connector, so that it can easily import data in different formats and schemas, and enable spatio- temporal online analytics over such data without much efforts. Lastly, it features a number of built-in analytical modules so that a set of common analytical tasks can be executed without further engineering efforts once data have been imported. More complex and other analytical tasks can be built in a customized fashion.

621413.label: Major findings and research outcome
621413.value: 1. We have designed a fully dynamic index structure for one-dimensional summary queries that also support accuracy-size trade-offs. The result has been published in the first journal paper listed in Part C. 2. We have designed an indexing structure for multi-dimensional summary queries using sampling-based techniques. The result has been published in the third conference paper in Part C. 3. We have built a system prototype. The system has been demonstrated at SIGMOD'15 and received the Best Demonstration Award. 4. We have also studied various problems related to the main objectives of this project: (1) We have studied the flexible aggregate similarity search problem, which is a variant of the summary query problem where the result is presented as an aggregate. The result has been published in the second conference paper in Part C. (2) We have studied the robust set reconciliation problem, which is an application of summaries for the purpose of identifying differences between two sets under noise. The result has been published in the first conference paper in Part C. (3) We have also studied the priority queue, which is a fundamental data structure underlying all indexing structures, including those for summary queries. The result has been published in the second conference paper in Part C.

621413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
621413.value: Our system currently uses a sampling technique to support summary queries. For some specific summaries, such as heavy hitters, our theoretical investigation shows that there could be more efficient solutions. As further development of this project, we plan to investigate how to support these specific summaries more efficiently.

621413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
621413.value: Database queries can be broadly classified into two categories: reporting queries and aggregation queries. The former retrieves a collection of records from the database that match the query’s conditions, while the latter returns an aggregate, such as count, sum, average, or max (min), of a particular attribute of these records. Aggregation queries are especially useful in business intelligence and data analysis applications where users are interested not in the actual records, but their statistics. They can also be executed much more efficiently than reporting queries, by embedding properly precomputed aggregates into an index. However, reporting and aggregation queries provide only two extremes for exploring the data. Data analysts often need more insight into the data distribution than what those simple aggregates provide, and yet certainly do not want the sheer volume of data returned by reporting queries. In this project, we design indexing techniques that allow for extracting a statistical summary of all the records in the query. The summaries we support include frequent items, quantiles, and various sketches, all of which are of central importance in massive data analysis. Our indexes require small space and extract a summary very efficiently.

621513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
621513.value: 在現代的分析化學中，質譜分析是一個非常有效的分析手段。其主要通過測量離子的質荷比（分子質量與電荷比值）來測定分子的基本構成或者推斷基本的分子結構。為了有效的對樣品成分進行離子化，實驗人員需要對其先行進行汽化處理。當前一個通用的，對大分子進行無破損離子化的“軟”技術是電噴嘴離子化（ESI）。在電噴嘴離子化（ESI）中，液態樣品的微液滴通過一個帶有高電壓的尖端噴嘴進行分散。當進入質譜儀中進行分析時，這些微液滴已經變成了氣態的離子。為了達到更高的離子化效率和分析精度，這個離子化系統需要一個更為尖銳的電噴嘴（ESI）尖端，更低的樣品流速以及更低的電噴散射的電壓。更低流速（納升/分鐘）也能够与納米級液相色譜（nano-LC）分析相兼容。納米液相色譜（nano-LC）分離在低品質的溶質、小容量複雜混合溶液的分離中有著很高的分離效率。這一系列的相容性為納米級液相色譜（nano-LC）分離和質譜分析集成為一個強效的納米色譜-電噴嘴-質譜分析晶片（nano-LC-ESI-MS）提供了可能性。 在過去的二十年的發展和研究中，高效的基於晶片的電噴（chip-based ESI）設計和納米級液相色譜分離（nano-LC）的優異表現遠遠超出了傳統的相對標準。特別地，基於微加工技術的柱形陣列所構成的高度有序的分離柱，使得納米液相色譜(nano-LC)達到了更高的分離效率。然而，僅僅在近些年才有研究不斷嘗試去將這兩個系統集成在一個晶片上，進而去實現一個更加完整的方法去進行分析並且將損失的分析樣品降低到最小。但是，器件集成化的複雜加工工藝成為實現這一目標的主要障礙。 我們課題組發明的創新的加工工藝允許我們在矽片上設計加工出柱形的玻璃毛細管。在這裡，基於這一創新的工藝，我們提出設計一個高效集成化的納米級別色譜-電噴嘴-質譜儀分析(nano-LC-ESI-MS)微系統的方案。在這一微系統中，一個懸空的毛細管作為電噴嘴尖端，而這些柱形玻璃毛細管形成的高度有序陣列作為納米液相色譜分離柱。這種同一結構兩種功能的設計是新穎的，並且可以對兩個重要的結構實現無縫的單片集成化。由於集成的毛線管是透明封閉的結構，這一微系統避免了光學檢測中蓋板的使用。通過標準的光刻技術，我們能夠使得毛細管由較為粗糙的尺寸自行收縮成為一個亞微米尺寸，從而將納米液相色譜延伸到納米級別的分離空間。然而，在現階段的研究中，人們往往需要運用昂貴的先進光刻技術或者傳統的氧化矽納米毛細管來實現這一功能。

621513.label: Realisation of objectives
621513.value: This was a fabrication intensive project; the devices proposed featured three-dimensional structures (cylindrical capillaries) that are non-trivial to fabricate via lithography-based semiconductor processing techniques. Thus, a significant portion of our effort has been vested in addressing the issues arising from the fabrication of such structures. A further major effort dealt with demonstrating them for the intended applications for the first time. Despite many hurdles, both of the objectives have been met to a reasonable degree. Objective 1 is concerned with integrated silicon-based in-plane emitters as originally proposed for nano-ESI-MS analytics. These emitters leverage our unique process and feature suspended glass nozzles integrated on silicon, which are defined by the partially released segments of the self-enclosed glass capillaries. The nozzles present a cylindrical lumen in diameter that is tunable from several micrometers down to sub-micrometers through a glass thermal reflow process. The emitters featuring nozzles at various lengths and counts were prepared by filling them with a test liquid containing deionised (DI) water and organic solvents in which a trace amount of acetic acid was added so as to increase the conductivity. The emitters were then characterized for total ion currents (TIC) measured against applied steady voltage under various flow rates, and the results obtained were comparable to those from previous emitters. The emitters were also tested for mass spectrometry analysis using a peptide mass standard, Glu-Fibrinopeptide B (microTAS, Gyeongju, 2015). However, this last stage revealed an issue that needs to be further addressed because the mass spectra obtained from the emitters were found unstable and did not quite agree with those from commercial emitters (PicoTip™ New Objective). Investigations revealed that the emitters despite the successful formation of Taylor cones were unable to generate a plume, the collection of tiny droplets sprayed from a Taylor cone tip. Subsequent experiments, however, revealed that electrospraying from such fine tips with a large hydraulic resistance does occur despite the absence of a noticeable plume but under fairly high electric field strengths. Experiments also indicated that this electric field strength nearly ionizes the air and must be applied very close to the tip through a thin-film metal. Thus, the practical use of these emitters for Mass Spectrometry analyses appears to be currently limited and would require a considerable reduction in the hydraulic resistance. Indeed, our emitters with a lumen diameter of 1-2 μm and a length of 1 mm (inclusive of the suspended nozzle segment) impose a large hydraulic resistance that might limit the effective delivery of ions into mass spectrometry, which explains the observed unstable spectra. Attempts have been made to increase the lumen diameter and/or shorten the nozzle length for a low hydraulic resistance, albeit facing only minor improvement due to the nature of the fabrication process and the device structure. While working toward electrospraying, we moved forward by leveraging the integrated glass nozzles (emitters) in other application fronts for which they can be readily used without an issue. We demonstrated microfluidic emulsification, i.e. oil-in-water as well as water-in-oil emulsions generated through the integrated nozzles being independent of the surface wettability. This is a significant advance in microfluidic emulsification since existing microfluidic devices demand appropriate choice of surface treatment before switching the emulsion type. We described our findings along with a simple physical model based on the critical Capillary number (Applied Physics Letters, 2015). We subsequently characterized the integrated glass nozzles also for ultrafast microsecond mixing based on hydrodynamic flow focusing (Applied Physics Letters, 2016). Such small nozzles help address the pre-mixing issue in this type of mixers. Objective 2 is concerned with the integrated cylindrical glass capillaries and their characteristics for pressure-driven nanoliquid chromatography (nano-LC). These capillaries are identical to those described in Objective 1. As proposed, we investigated two distinct nano-LC designs including the one with a set of long open tubular capillaries featuring a cylindrical lumen 1-2 μm in diameter and the other with short capillaries (<1 mm) in web formation (proposed for emulating a column of pillars often used in existing nano-LC chips for enhanced interfacial area). The latter design, however, has faced the issue of enclosing capillary junctions upon glass thermal reflow whereas the former design has been successfully fabricated and thoroughly characterized for various nano-LC modes: normal- and reversed-phase, ion valance, and hydrodynamic chromatography (Analytical Chemistry, 2016). On-chip hydrodynamic chromatography of DNA has also been demonstrated for the first time through centimeters-long integrated capillaries (Analyst, 2017). While tackling the issue concerning the capillary web formation, we discovered a unique design, namely the capillary-well motif, which we conceived based on the capillary web (Patent pending). The capillary-well motif featured short capillary segments (1-10 μm) as well but at a much smaller diameter (70 nm). Through this unique design, we avoided the issue of enclosing capillary junctions and rather replaced the junctions with deep wells. We applied this unique design for the size-based separation of macromolecules including distinct mixtures of short DNA strands, long DNA chains, and SDS-denatured proteins in “gel-free” solution. Unlike nano-LC chips, which function under a high-pressure gradient, this chip is driven by a high-voltage supply for an effective electrophoretic separation of macromolecules. We also developed physical models reasonably explaining the distinct sieving mechanisms (Ogston sieving and entropic-trapping regimes). We field a US full patent on the design and reported our results in a reputable journal, (ACS Nano, 2015). Subsequently, we extended the design into a two-dimensional array and demonstrated continuous-flow electrophoresis of macromolecules (Analytical Chemistry, 2017). Lastly, we performed open tubular LC in rectangular microchannels in a design featuring a junction with integrated cylindrical glass capillaries. The required hydraulic pressure to drive LC is induced at the junction owing to a mismatch in electroosmotic flow rates of the glass capillaries and the side microchannels (Electrophoresis, 2014).

621513.label: Major findings and research outcome
621513.value: A major outcome of this project concerns the development of novel silicon-glass nanofluidic devices for the intended applications (nano-ESI and nano-LC) as well as for various other uses (e.g. ultrarapid micromixer for protein folding, and micro-emulsification). The underlying theme in all these devices is that they are fabricated using standard semiconductor processing techniques without the requirement of advanced lithography tools. Thus, the devices can be manufactured in batch mode for consumers leveraging the economies of scale; they would not be limited to research settings. Two nanofluidic devices have been demonstrated including an in-plane emitter array and a glass capillary array with a sample injection cross-junction. Both devices feature novel self-enclosed integrated glass capillaries and share key fabrication steps. Experiments on in-plane emitters revealed that electrospraying from such fine tips with a large hydraulic resistance occur under fairly large electric field strengths. Experiments also indicated that such large field intensities nearly lead the air to ionize and also must be applied very close to the tip through a thin-film metal. Thus, the practical use of these emitters for Mass Spectrometry analyses is limited for now and would require advances in design and fabrication to lower the hydraulic resistance. However, the utility of such emitters has been demonstrated here for microfluidic emulsification, generating oil-in-water and water-in-oil droplets inside microfluidic junctions without the requirement of switching surface wettability (see Publication 1; Section 8; Part C). The utility of the emitters has been further demonstrated in a hydrodynamic flow-focusing geometry for ultrafast microsecond mixing, which could facilitate the study of protein folding/unfolding kinetics (see Publication 4; Section 8; Part C). The nanocapillary array has been demonstrated for open-tubular LC in various modes: normal- and reversed-phase, ion valance, and hydrodynamic chromatography (see Publications 3 & 5; Section 8; Part C). Moreover, an array of centimeters-long nanocapillaries has been applied for on-chip hydrodynamic chromatography of DNA coils for the first time (see Publication 6; Section 8; Part C). Furthermore, a repeating unit of a short nanocapillary array (capillary-well motif) has been introduced as a highly effective artificial sieve for gel-free electrophoresis of nucleic acids and proteins in batch as well as continuous-flow modes (see Publications 2 & 7; Section 8; Part C). A US patent on the novel structure is pending (see Item 2; Section 11; Part C). These outcomes led to the training of three PhD students (see Section 10, Part C).

621513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
621513.value: In either objective, there are opportunities for further development. In objective 1, regarding the integrated emitters for electrospray ionization, a major amendment to the proposed process can be considered to lower the hydraulic resistance that leads to the requirement of fairly large electric field strengths. This might necessitate abandoning the thermal reflow process and the corresponding nozzles derived from the self-enclosed glass capillaries. Although various process candidates exist, their adoption for the required structure and electrospray ionization appears to be non-trivial and might face fabrication challenges. In objective 2, regarding the integrated cylindrical glass capillaries for pressure-driven nano-LC, both the device design/fabrication and high-pressure system can be further developed. The issue of the capillary web formation to emulate the pillar array present in other nano-LC chips can be further addressed through various new structural designs that can promote the enclosure of capillary junctions. Moreover, maximum supply pressure (currently 7 bar) can be increased for a separation at increased speed. The switching delay in pressure levels (currently ~100 ms) can be further minimized to obtain a reduced sample plug size. Accordingly, a detector with an increased sensitivity can be employed to observe the migration of short plugs through fine capillaries.

621513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
621513.value: New technologies that can facilitate the analysis of biological macromolecules including proteins and nucleic acids in a sample mixture are of utmost value to accelerate scientific discoveries, and further advance our understanding of the diseases to find more effective cures. Nanotechnology that has delivered modern computer microchips is among top candidates for fulfilling this task because it can provide microscopic components comparable in size to macromolecules. Using nanotechnology, this research project demonstrated microchips mainly for the separation of nucleic acids and proteins according to molecular size or electric charge through techniques, mainly involving electrophoresis and pressure-driven liquid chromatography. Not only, do these microchips offer significant performance advantage in analysis time and accuracy over traditional laboratory techniques but also shrink the equipment size into portable scales for potential deployment to hospitals, clinics, and check points (e.g. airports for a rapid screening of passengers against infectious diseases). With the microchips the analysis can be performed with a minimal amount of sample requirement, a feature considered of high value in some applications such as infant care and forensics. The project also demonstrated microchips offering advantages in fundamental studies such as the analysis of protein kinetics and electrospray ionization.

622013.value: 帶填料聚合物複合材料的導電性，是有賴於複合材料在固化過程中形成的導電性填料網絡。這是滲流主導的情況而滲流閾值具有導電性迅速增加的特徵。雖然填料的滲流取決於填料的分佈，填料形狀，填料/基體的相互作用和加工條件，固化聚合物複合材料的導電性是由填料網絡中填料的相互接觸電阻。相互接觸電阻由兩部分組成，當中隧穿電阻遠超收縮電阻。隧穿電阻是由滲流過程中填料之間的超薄相的聚合物層產生，隧穿電阻值是由相間層的厚度控制。以往的研究已顯示當發生相分離時，炭黑或碳納米管聚合物的滲流閾值可以降低[ 39,40 ]。同樣明顯是當石墨烯聚合物共混物產生相分離時，聚合物導電性得到優化[41] 。因此聚合物共混物相分離是一個很好控制滲流動力學和滲流閾值的機制。作者最近的工作顯示添加離子液體催化劑對銀聚合物複合材料的固化動力學和滲流閾值具有影響[43]。這觀察可以由相間層形成過程中受催化劑影響的凝膠化過程導致在速固化動力學環境解釋 。離子液體的選擇和用量也是另類用於控制滲流過程和最終的聚合物複合材料的導電性機制。最近的報告[ 48.49 ]表明，填料聚合物嫁接可以影響導電環氧樹脂複合材料創建相分離在複合金屬填料滲濾填料的潤濕性能。在這方案中將會進行銀聚合物複合材料的固化動力學研究。引入適當化學結構和適量離子液體催化劑的效果將被詳細研究。對填料進行硫醇聚合物嫁接並審查其對固化反應動力學和滲流閾。目標是優化使用離子液體催化劑和聚合物嫁接造成提高填料高分子複合材料的導電性。

622013.label: Realisation of objectives
622013.value: The effect of ionic liquid on curing kinetics and percolation of silver epoxy composite has been studied in the project. The result shows that the effect of the ionic liquid is critical in the formation of capillary bridges across silver flakes to form connected three dimensional particle network cater for electron and phonon conduction. The three dimensional network will enhance conductivity compared with the case of random connectivity in the regular silver epoxy composite systems. The capillary network formation only requires a small volume ratio of ionic liquid to silver flakes. This is governed by the three phase contact angle of the ionic liquid on silver surface enclosed by epoxy. A less than 90 three phase contact angle is necessary for the network formation. This forms the criterion for selection of ionic liquid for the silver epoxy system. The capillary bridge network formation is governed by the jamming theory of ternary material system. The specific surface energy of the constituents within the ionic liquid fused silver epoxy system controls the three phase contact angle and subsequently the network formation. The amount of ionic liquid dictates the network formation. Inadequate amount of the ionic liquid will only wet the silver flakes and may form small clusters. Increase amount of ionic liquid will lead to the formation of pendular network which allows electron conducting between particles. As electrons can hop across disconnected particles with a gap less than the quantum tunneling threshold distance of a few nanometers. A full blown pendular network will give maximum electrical conductivity. With further increase in ionic liquid volume fraction, the silver flake network transits into a more compact funicular network and thus facilitates phonon transfer. The compact direct particle to particle contact pertains to maximum thermal conductivity. The electrical conductivity at this ionic liquid volume fraction drops from its maximum value due to a more compact network with less branches, thus less conductive pathways. With further increase in the ionic liquid volume fraction, the binding force field starts to push the agglomeration of the silver flakes into clusters rather than forming a three-dimensional network. Thus the electrical and thermal conductivity drops to a lower level resembling that of a random network of silver clusters within the epoxy system. The networking formation function of the ionic liquid has lost due to shift in balance of the force field. The detail transition of the silver flake network has been explained in the published paper and the PhD thesis of Hongye SUN. The percolation and capillary bridge network formation are inter-related. Without the presence of the ionic liquid, the silver flakes will form network on a random basis and the percolation threshold is reached when sufficient volume fraction of silver flakes are mixed into the composite system. However, with the infusion of ionic liquid, the capillary bridges formed are able to facilitate the creation of a structured three dimensional network. Given the amount of silver flakes, this will enhance the conductive performance. However when the amount of ionic liquid exceeds the optimum amount, the clustering of the silver flakes will render the system back to a random connected structure as in the case of regular percolation. The effect of polymer grafted fillers on percolation of the silver epoxy has been studied in the earlier stage of the project and they are found to be less effective as compared with ionic liquid which acts as a capillary bridge formation facilitator. With a more thorough study of the ionic liquid capillary bridge formation reveals that the underlying particle jamming mechanism is key to the formation of capillary bridge network of silver particles. This is a physical phenomenon rather than a chemical phenomenon which dictates the polymer grafting of fillers. Comparing the two approaches, they are similarly anchored on the specific surface energy of the constituents of silver epoxy system. The polymer grafting of silver surface is a means to modify the specific surface energy of the particle and as the chemical bonding of the grafting polymer has to be sufficient strong, it will stay as an insulating layer between the silver particles resulting in reduced conductivity. In the case of ionic liquid, being liquid phase, it allows for direct connect between silver particles as reflected in the experimental results. It is therefore reasonable to focus the research on the use of ionic liquid to enhance the conductivity of the silver epoxy system. To substantiate the network transition of the ionic liquid infused silver epoxy system, characterization experiments were conducted to measure the three phase contact angle, the fluid-fluid interfacial tension, the silver epoxy electrical conductivity and thermal conductivity, the rheological properties, and the microstructure of samples. The contact angle of BMIM on silver surface enclosed with bisphenol is 45 degree. The other experimental data are all supportive of the network transition theory proposed. The macroscopic morphology of silver epoxy shows the transition from the liquid phase to gel state. Scanning electrical microscopy results also indicates the transition of the network with change in ionic liquid amount. The storage modulus and the yield strength of the silver epoxy shows a consistent trend as the conductivity measurements. The capillary bridge formation theory developed for ternary material systems with spherical particles was extended to the case of flakes using a platelet model. The static capillary force and bridge volume were evaluated using a simple capillary force model. It was concluded that the flakes will have a much stronger capillary force than the spherical system. This is due to a face-face binding configuration as compared to the point-based binding in the case of spherical particles. A dynamic capillary bridge model was developed based on collision model during mixing. The equilibrium bridge height is found to be 2.4 nm which is within the range of quantum tunneling threshold distance. This model is a preliminary step in understanding the mechanism for formation of capillary bridges in flake network, despite the encouraging result, it still needs to be further improved.

622013.label: Major findings and research outcome
622013.value: The research is leveraging on the understanding of gelation in a secondary fluid doped capillary suspension in the formation of a three dimensional network of filler particles in an epoxy system. The 3D network will form a conductive pathway allowing the flow of the electrons and phonons between the two end substrates joined by the silver epoxy system. The key finding is that the percolation threshold of an epoxy system with drops significantly from 20% to 10% silver flake volume fraction with the addition of the secondary fluid BMIM in a bisphenol-F epoxy with anhydride hardener system. The electrical conductivity of the silver epoxy remains on par despite of the reduction of the reduction in the silver content while the thermal conductivity actually increases. This observation is explained by the formation ionic liquid induced capillary bridging enabling the creation of 3D silver flake network to facilitate the improvement in conductivity. In the case of 10% silver content, the electrical conductivity peaks at an ionic liquid/silver flake volume ratio, , equals to 0.03 while the peak thermal conductivity equals to 0.048. This electrical conductivity peaks at a lower ionic liquid content is likely due to the formation of a less compact pendular network with electron conduction via quantum tunneling. The higher ionic liquid content facilitates phonon transfer via the formation a more compact funicular network. The transition of silver flakes from pendular network to funicular network is supported by morphology evolution observation from SEM images, storage modulus measurement data, and epoxy yield stress measurement. A mechanistic theory for bridge gelation was proposed for the effect of ionic liquid on silver epoxy systems. The formation of BMIM capillary bridges on silver flakes within the bisphenol system is governed by the three-phase contact angle of ionic liquid which should be less than 90˚ allowing BMIM to preferentially wet on silver flakes. Small amount of BMIM will wet on the silver flakes but not sufficient to form a network. Increasing BMIM volume will enable 3D silver flake network formation from less compact pendular network to more compact funicular network. Further increase in BMIM content will create capillary aggregate clusters which breaks up the 3D network and causing reduction in conductivity. The mechanistic theory aims to extend the current theory of capillary bridging of spherical particles to flakes or platelets. The theory demonstrates that flakes form a stronger network due to larger contact area.

622013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
622013.value: There are three potential areas for further development of the research: 1. Theoretical development of capillary bridging of spherical particles has been widely studied and this research has extended to cover flakes which are non-symmetric particles. While the proposed theory has explained the mechanism in the formation of the pendular network and the funicular network, it would be necessary to demonstrate this experimental using confocal microscopy. This will help further refinement of the theory. 2. The capillary bridge formation of 3D filler network is a very useful means to control properties of composite. This approach should be tested on other composite material system such as fibre systems to assist the fibre alignment process. 3. Nano capillary bridging and nano sintering would be other areas to be explored using the capillary bridging approach. Preliminary work on nanoparticle-core/bridge-shell structure has been demonstrated by other research group. Nano sintering has also been studied by other research groups. Nano sintering of networked nanoparticles will definitely be improvement over the existing method. Collaboration with Karlshrue Institute of Technology and Katholieke Universiteit Leuven has been developed to further pursue the proposed ideas.

622013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
622013.value: This research on capillary bridging has demonstrated that the ionic liquid has facilitated the formation of particle network in composite, in this case silver flakes in epoxy, resulting in substantially increased in the electrical and thermal conductivity of the composite. While maintaining the electrical and thermal conductivity of the epoxy composite; the content reduction of silver flakes, which constitutes the man cost component of the epoxy composite, will substantial improve the cost-performance of the silver epoxy. As silver epoxy is used extensively in the electronic packaging industry, this finding will have direct impact on the electronic industry. Furthermore, the research has also provide theoretical understanding in the formation of non-spherical particle network in a composite system with the addition of a secondary liquid of appropriate surface contact property. This study has wider impact in the helping to provide understanding and solutions for alignment of particles or solid fillers in composite. Criterion for formation of particle network has been defined and this will help to develop new networked composite material system with improved performance.

622613.label: Project Objectives
622613.value: To design a database for improving the performance of the multi-cell, infrastructure-based, dynamic spectrum access to TV white spaces. To extend traditional geo-location databases by adding related information to achieve better coordination among multiple APs. To design a new spectrum allocation algorithm for multiple APs to decide spectrum usage in a distributed manner. The spectrum allocation algorithm should be unique in the way that it considers both the non-uniform interference relationships among APs and the spectrum fragmentation. A new AP discovery scheme will be designed to enable the users to reliably identify the spectral bands used by different APs and select the one with the highest potential throughput to associate with. A prototype multi-AP system will be developed to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed system design. To propose a new hybrid pricing scheme for a TV database operator considering the heterogeneity of the SUs. To model the competition among the SUs and design a distributed algorithm for the SUs to achieve a Nash equilibrium (NE) with bounded iterations. Moreover, to optimize the pricing parameters the algorithms will apply contract theory under complete and incomplete information scenario, respectively.
