622613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
622613.value: As smartphones command an increasing share of the mobile market, demand for wireless data and therefore the needed spectrum is about to explode. After the transition from analog to digital television broadcasts, a substantial amount of TV channels are freed up, which are called “TV whitespace(TVWS)”. In 2010, America's Federal Communications Commission (FCC) released a rule to make TVWS available for unlicensed broadband services. To make sure the new networks and devices do not interfere with the existing TV receivers, the FCC requires that the TVWS can be accessed by secondary users (SUs) only after they have obtained a list of vacant TV channels via a geo-location database. Under such an architecture, geo-location databases will be managed by database operators (DOs) approved by the FCC to provide TV spectrum availability. However, the concrete functionality of the database and its interface to the network have not yet been finalized. Moreover, the FCC allows the DOs to determine their own pricing schemes for SUs, which have also not been fixed yet. This proposed project will address two important issues related to this database-assisted dynamic spectrum access (DSA) architecture. First, we will focus on how to leverage TVWS for designing a system consists of multiple access point (AP) with the help of database. We will design a local database extends the traditional geo-location database by adding information about APs such as their locations and interference relationships. By jointly considering both the non-uniform interference relationships among APs and spectrum fragmentation, we will propose a distributed spectrum allocation algorithm for multiple APs to allow non-continuous spectrum usage. We then propose to design a proper business model for the DOs. Normally database access can be priced with a registration scheme or a service plan scheme. In this project, we will for the first time investigate a business model for the TVWS database with hybrid pricing scheme. We will consider the scenario where a DO employs both pricing models to serve different types of SUs. We will investigate schemes for a DO to optimally determine the pricing parameters for both registration scheme and service plan schemes to maximize his profit. DSA has been discussed, debated and researched for the last two decades. The grounds for moving the vision of DSA from academia to implementation are very powerful. Efficient solutions resulting from this research will help to speed up this reform, which has tremendous technological and social significance. 隨著智能手機在移動市場的份額越來越大，用戶對無線數據的需求和因此所需要的頻譜需求是快要爆炸了。在電視廣播從模擬到數字過渡後，大量的電視頻道被釋放出來，這就是大家提到的“電視空白頻道（ TVWS ） ” 。在2010年，美國聯邦通信委員會（FCC）發布了一個規則，允許使用TVWS提供無需牌照的寬帶服務。為了確保新的網絡和設備不幹擾現有的電視接收機， FCC要求二級用戶（SUs）在訪問TVWS之前，要先通過地理位置數據庫獲得空置的電視頻道列表。在這樣的架構下，地理位置數據庫的管理必須由已獲得FCC的數據庫運營商（ DOs）進行，由這些DOs提供電視頻譜的可用性相關信息。但是迄今為止，數據庫的具體功能以及它對網絡的接口尚未敲定。此外， FCC允許Dos自主決定對SUs查詢的定價方案，這部分目前也尚未確定。 本項目將解決數據庫輔助的動態頻譜接入（ DSA ）架構下的兩個重要問題。首先，我們將重點放在如何利用T VWS來設計在數據庫的幫助下，有多個接入點（AP ）的系統。我們將設計一個本地數據庫，該數據庫擴展了傳統的地理位置數據庫，增加了AP的信息，如他們的位置和幹擾關系等。整個設計中我們將同時考慮AP之間的非均勻幹擾的關系以及頻譜碎片的存在，我們將提出一個在多個AP間進行的分布式的頻譜分配算法，以有效地允許非連續的頻譜使用。 然後，我們將為DOs設計一個適當的商業模式 。通常情況下，數據庫的訪問可以通過登記制度或服務計劃等兩種方式進行定價。在這個項目中，我們將在首次討論針對TVWS數據庫的基於混合定價機制的商業模式。我們將會考慮一個DO采用上述兩種不同的定價模式來為不同類型的SU進行服務 。我們將研究如何為DO最優化地決定定價中的相關參數以最大限度地提高他的利潤。 在過去的二十年， 人們對DSA進行了大量的討論，辯論和研究。目前工作的重心正由 學術界的DSA研究向實際的實施發展。這項研究產生的高效的解決方案將有助於加快這一改革，具有巨大的技術意義和社會意義。

622613.label: Realisation of objectives
622613.value: Through this project, we have successfully achieved all the objectives proposed and obtained the results from the following aspects. 1. Built up a hybrid pricing framework for TV white space database. Since TV white spaces (TVWS) can be accessed by secondary users (SUs) after a list of vacant TV channels is obtained via a geo-location database, proper business models are needed for database operators to manage geo-location databases. Database access can be simultaneously priced under two different schemes: the registration scheme and the service plan scheme. In the registration scheme, the database reserves part of the TV bandwidth for registered White Space Devices (WSDs). In the service plan scheme, the WSDs are charged according to their queries. In this work, we investigated the business model for the TVWS database under a hybrid pricing scheme. We considered the scenario where a database operator employs both the registration scheme and the service plan scheme to serve the SUs. With our developed framework, the database operator can optimally determine pricing parameters for both pricing schemes in terms of bandwidth reservation, registration fee and query plans. 2. Developed strategies to facilitate secondary spectrum trading markets 2.1 In secondary spectrum trading markets, auctions are widely used by spectrum holders (SHs) to redistribute their unused channels to secondary wireless service providers (WSPs). As sellers, the SHs design proper auction schemes to stimulate more participants and maximize the revenue from the auction. As buyers, the WSPs determine the bidding strategies in the auction to better serve their end users. In this work, we considered a three-layered spectrum trading market consisting of the SH, the WSPs and the end users. We jointly studied the strategies of the three parties. The SH determines the auction scheme and spectrum supplies to optimize its revenue. The WSPs have flexible bidding strategies in terms of both demands and valuations considering the strategies of the end users. We designed FlexAuc, a novel auction mechanism for this market to enable dynamic supplies and demands in the auction. 2.2 In the spectrum auction, if a buyer locates in a “critical” place, interfering with a lot of other buyers, his occupancy of the spectrum may deprive many other transmission opportunities. In this work, we proposed a Location-aware Online Truthful doUble auction Scheme (LOTUS), which incorporates the buyers’ location information into auction mechanism design. The simulation results show that LOTUS outperforms the existing online auction mechanism, significantly improving buyers’ and sellers’ utility. 2.3 Auctions are among the best-known market-based tools to solve the problem of dynamic spectrum redistribution. However, the issue of privacy preservation in spectrum auctions remains open. In this project, we developed PISA, which is a PrIvacy preserving and Strategy-proof Auction mechanism for spectrum allocation. PISA provides protection for both bid privacy and coverage/interference area privacy leveraging a privacy-preserving integer comparison protocol, which is well applicable in other contexts. 2.4 To match wireless users' soaring traffic demand, spectrum regulators are considering allocating additional spectrum to the wireless market. The spectrum regulator now simply allocates the spectrum to maximize its income, but such an income-centric allocation does not ensure the best spectrum utilization by the users. This motivates us to design a new spectrum allocation scheme which jointly considers the spectrum regulator's income and the users' aggregate utility by investigating three market tiers: the spectrum regulator, 4G and Super Wi-Fi operator coalitions, and all the wireless users. Compared with the traditional income-centric allocation, we prove that the proposed scheme significantly improves users' aggregate utility with a limited spectrum regulator's income loss. 3. Designed core components to enhance spectrum management efficiency 3.1 Fine-grained spectrum management designs have been advocated by the research community to embrace the heterogeneity in devices and services. However, manufacturers hesitate to make hardware investments without comprehensive understanding of these designs. To break this stalemate, software-defined wireless networking (SDWN) has been pushed to market as a cost-effective paradigm. Motivated by recent innovations in SDWN, in this project, we systematically investigated the spectrum management architecture design that reaps the benefits of SDWN while maintaining the features of fine-grained channelization. We shed light on design principles and key challenges in realizing the SDWN-enabled spectrum management architecture. With these principles and challenges in mind, we develop a general architecture with a new baseband virtualization design. 3.2 In cognitive radio networks (CRNs), collaborative sensing has been considered as an attractive means to improve spectrum sensing performance. However, privacy issues arise when multiple service providers (SPs) collaborate on learning the spectrum availabilities. To incentivize SUs to contribute their sensing data, the privacy of each SU should be guaranteed. In this work, we proposed a privacy preservation framework called PrimCos for multi-SP collaborative sensing, which addresses several competing challenges not yet considered in the literature, that is, being compatible with general collaborative sensing schemes, providing privacy guarantee for each SU and ensuring worst case privacy protection under collusion. 4. Developed core technologies to improve system performance 4.1 In this work, we presented OpenTDMF, an architecture to enable TDMA on commodity WLAN devices. OpenTDMF is inspired by and architecturally similar to Software Defined Networking (SDN). Specifically, we leveraged the backhaul of WLAN to coordinate all the stations for channel access. This fine-grained coordination is performed in a decoupled control plane which includes a central controller and programmable APs. To realize OpenTDMF on commodity WLAN devices, we developed several novel techniques to achieve microsecond-level time synchronization among all the APs. We also enabled AP-triggered uplink transmission so that all the transmissions in the WLAN can be determined. 4.2 Fixed channelization configuration in today’s wireless devices falls short in the presence of growing data traffic and heterogeneous devices. We propose SEER, a frame-level wideband spectrum adaptation solution which consists of two major components: i) a specially-constructed preamble that can be detected by receivers with arbitrary RF bands, and ii) a spectrum detection algorithm that identifies the desired transmission band in the context of multiple asynchronous senders by exploiting the preamble’s temporal and spectral properties. SEER can be realized on commodity radios, and can be easily integrated into devices running different PHY/MAC protocols. 4.3 Rate adaptation is an essential component in today’s wireless standards, which help approach the channel capacity and maximize the throughput. However, how to estimate the optimal data rate in a fluctuated channel remains of great concern. In this project, we observe that by digging into both PHY layer decoder and upper layer protocol headers, more reliable data bits with high confidence level can be exploited. These data bits, termed smart pilot, can be used to calibrate the channel estimation measurements cost-efficiently. Based on the calibrated estimation, we further propose a novel greedy rate selection algorithm to track the optimal data rate, which successfully avoids the impact of deep fading subcarriers in both legacy 802.11a/g and 802.11n MIMO systems.

622613.label: Major findings and research outcome
622613.value: 1. Built up a hybrid pricing framework for TV white space database. We proposed a hybrid pricing scheme for the database operator (DO) considering the heterogeneity of SU types. As far as we know, it is the first work considering hybrid pricing schemes for TVWS database. We modeled the competition among the strategic SUs as a non-cooperative game and proved the existence of the Nash Equilibrium (NE) under both complete and incomplete information. We also proposed algorithms for the DO to optimally decide pricing parameters. 2. Developed strategies to facilitate secondary spectrum trading markets 2.1 We considered a three-layered spectrum trading market consisting of the SH, the WSPs and the end users. We jointly studied the strategies of the three parties. We designed FlexAuc, a novel auction mechanism for this market to enable dynamic supplies and demands in the auction. 2.2 We proposed a Location-aware Online Truthful doUble auction Scheme (LOTUS), which incorporates the buyers’ location information into auction mechanism design. The simulation results show that LOTUS significantly improved buyers’ and sellers’ utility. 2.3 We developed PISA, which is a PrIvacy preserving and Strategy-proof Auction mechanism for spectrum allocation. PISA provides protection for both bid privacy and coverage/interference area privacy leveraging a privacy-preserving integer comparison protocol. 2.4 We designed a new spectrum allocation scheme which jointly considers the spectrum regulator's income and the users' aggregate utility by investigating three market tiers: the spectrum regulator, 4G and Super Wi-Fi operator coalitions, and all the wireless users. 3. Developed core technologies to improve system performance (only two typical ones are described below). 3.1 We proposed SEER, a frame-level wideband spectrum adaptation solution which consists of two major components: i) a specially-constructed preamble that can be detected by receivers with arbitrary RF bands, and ii) a spectrum detection algorithm that identifies the desired transmission band in the context of multiple asynchronous senders by exploiting the preamble’s temporal and spectral properties. 3.2 We observed that by digging into both PHY layer decoder and upper layer protocol headers, more reliable data bits with high confidence level can be exploited. These data bits, termed smart pilot, can be used to calibrate the channel estimation measurements cost-efficiently. Based on the calibrated estimation, we further proposed a novel greedy rate selection algorithm to track the optimal data rate, which successfully avoids the impact of deep fading subcarriers in both legacy 802.11a/g and 802.11n MIMO systems.

622613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
622613.value: The directions explored in this project are interesting and not fully investigated ones. Specifically, how to build up pricing model for operators who maintain the TV white space databse, how to design efficient strategies to promote secondary spectrum trading markets, how to design effective spectrum management architecture, how to develop technologies to enhance the network performance, etc. are the areas that still need more effort and still have open questions to be investigated.

622613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
622613.value: After the transition from analog to digital television broadcasts, a substantial number of TV channels are freed up, which are called ‘TV whitespace (TVWS)’. In 2010, Federal Communications Commission (FCC) released a rule to make TVWS available for unlicensed broadband services. To make sure the new networks and devices do not interfere with the existing TV receivers, the FCC requires that the TVWS be accessible by secondary users (SUs) only after they have obtained a list of vacant TV channels via a geo-location database. Under such architecture, geo-location databases will be managed by database operators (DOs) to provide TV spectrum availability. However, the concrete functionality of the database and its interface to the network has not yet been finalized. Moreover, the FCC allows the DOs to determine their own pricing schemes for SUs, which have also not been fixed yet. In this project, we built up a hybrid pricing framework for TVWS database and developed several effective strategies to facilitate secondary spectrum trading markets. Moreover, we designed software-defined wireless networking-based architecture to enhance spectrum management efficiency. Several core technologies have also been developed to improve system performance. Efficient solutions resulting from this research have tremendous technological and social significance.

622713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
622713.value: 有效的倉儲管理及其後應銷售情況而動態調整的定價策略是使供應與需求吻合的關鍵。此策略对企業銷售市場需求波動較大的季節性產品顯得尤為重要。在銷售季節臨近結束時，企業試圖通過降價來清空庫存及收回成本；否則，此部分產品將失去價值。在香港流行產品零售業中，一年主要有兩個清倉時期，夏天七八月份及冬天十二月至一月。在清倉銷售期間，購物者拥入全香港的商戶，尋找可能降價高達90%的商品。零售商也趁此機會為新產品清空庫存。 部分消費者總希望比其他人先購買到新產品，他們的這種習慣會促使一些本該以原價購買產品的機智消費者因期待大折扣而推遲他們的購買行為。我們把前者稱為短視型消費者，而把後者稱為策略型消費者。此外，還有一類消費者從來不在原價時購買，我們稱之為廉價追求者。他們的存在會進一步促使企業降價。當企業通過降價來快速回籠收益時，這些折扣率會被消費者記住。我們稱此記憶過程為消費者學習。而這種學習現象會引發相應的消費者策略性行為。因此，零售商的降價策略有可能導致越來越少消費者以原價購買產品，從而損害零售商的長期利潤。 本研究的目的在於探討當企業面臨多個銷售季節時，策略型消費者的行為會如何影響其定價及倉儲決策。我們所考慮的策略型消費者並不會對企業的降價決策形成均衡狀態下的理性期望，而是會從企業的定價歷史中逐漸學習。在過去的數十年中，有大量關於動態定價及倉儲決策的研究，考慮或不考慮策略型消費者的皆有。我們總結了最相關的研究及參考了此問題的各方面的調查論文。在動態定價及倉儲決策的文獻中，目前还有一項研究同時考慮到我們將要探討的以下四個關鍵點：（1）多個銷售季節，且每個季節均包含原價及降價階段；（2）每個季節的定價（原價和折扣價）及倉儲決策；（3）以往的折扣價會被消費者記住並影響他們的購買行為（消費者學習）；及（4）策略型消費者會根據他們所學習到的企業降價記錄來調整他們的購買時機。第（2）和（3）點分別闡述了企業和策略型消費者的決策。第（1）點是在動態決策中納入消費者學習的關鍵，並使得我們所提出的研究項目比現有研究更豐富及更具挑戰性。 我們的項目把策略型消費者根據歷史經驗調整購買時機的行為融入到動態定價及倉儲決策中。此項目的成果將會大大地拓寬相關研究範圍。在香港及世界範圍，極大的清倉折扣已經成為一些零售商的慣例。此慣例對消費者策略性行為及對企業長期利潤的影響通常被忽略。因此，我們的研究有可能會提醒企業檢視現有的定價及倉儲決策，並鼓勵他們關注更長遠的發展而不是專注於短期的收益。

622713.label: Realisation of objectives
622713.value: We have successfully carried out the proposed research with three main objectives. Dynamic pricing is an effective strategy for retailers in repeated purchase markets to increase revenue in response to uncertain market conditions. Despite the extra revenue gained from such effective demand management, dynamic pricing creates an incentive for consumers to time their purchases to exploit the variation in prices. After years of predictable late-season deep discounts, a retailer is likely to find that more and more consumers are reluctant to purchase at the full price and become trained to wait for heavy discounts. That is, in a repeat-purchase market where consumers interact with a retailer season after season, savvy consumers learn from the retailer’s past actions, form their expectations about a retailer’s future decisions, and behave strategically. We model consumers price expectations or reference prices based on the retailer’s actions in the past. Specifically, at the beginning of each season, consumers adopt a simple heuristic rule using the retailer’s past markdown prices to form their reference on the retailer’s pricing strategy in the current season. This reference price will then influence the timing of the purchases of the consumers and, along with the actual pricing strategy, the total demand during the season. To understand how the retailer should optimally influence consumers’ reference prices by appropriately choosing its markdown prices and stocking quantities over time so as to maximize the long-run profit, we assume that the full price in each season is known and remains the same throughout the planning horizon. This corresponds to the situation where a product or an upgraded version of the product is sold in each season at a relatively stable price. At the beginning of each season (stage 1), the retailer decides the stocking quantity based on consumers’ reference on the markdown price later in the season (stage 2) and sells the product at the full price. Since highly uncertain demand accompanied by price adjustment contingent on how supply matches with demand is a key feature of those aforementioned industries, we assume that the market size in each season is a random variable and realized during stage 1. Depending on the reference price, some consumers may delay their purchases and choose not to buy in stage 1. If there is inventory left at the end of stage 1, the retailer has the option to mark down the price or maintain the full price for the rest of the season (stage 2) and consumers who waited will purchase if the stage 2 price is at or below their willingness to pay. There are some interesting findings and insights. To mention a few, Under the optimal control, both the reference and markdown price have steady state distributions under very general conditions, confirming that markdowns and consumer learning do not necessarily destroy the stability of a business. Furthermore, the reference price should exhibit a mean-reverting pattern under some general conditions, i.e., the reference fluctuates around a mean value, reflecting the practice of most stable businesses. In the long run, whenever the reference deviates from the mean, it is expected to revert back to the mean soon. However, under some demand curves, there can be multiple reverting means for the reference. For instance, the reference can oscillate from around a high mean to around a low mean after the retailer discounts heavily over a series of seasons of low but not extremely low demand and from around a low mean to around a high mean after the retailer offers light or no discounts over a series of seasons of high or extremely low demand. Hence, the optimal reference can oscillate among reverting mean values. Such a phenomenon suggests that the current longstanding practices of predictable heavy end-of-season markdowns in some retail business may not be the best strategy.

622713.label: Major findings and research outcome
622713.value: 1. Under some general conditions, markdowns and consumer learning do not necessarily destroy the stability of a business and the reference price should exhibit a mean-reverting pattern under some general conditions. However, under some demand curves, there can be multiple reverting means for the reference. In this case, the optimal reference can oscillate among reverting mean values. Such a phenomenon suggests that the current longstanding practices of predictable heavy end-of-season markdowns in some retail business may not be the best strategy. 2. When demand is deterministic, the reference converges monotonically to a steady state for any given initial reference under a general condition. Although the reference may oscillate among different means with stochastic demand, it will not fluctuate with deterministic demand. Hence, demand uncertainty is the key driver for any oscillating behavior of the reference. 3. The retailer will order less inventory and discount less than a myopic retailer who ignores the impact of a markdown on future profits. Furthermore, the retailer’s markdown price is not monotone, whereas the myopic retailer will always discount more as demand decreases. At extremely low demand, the retailer would rather offer no discount because a markdown will only lower future references with little gain. 4. When consumers learn about the markdown price faster, they place a higher weight on the most recent discount price and adjust their reference price more quickly. Intuitively, the retailer should discount less to maintain the reference at a desirable level. However, the impact on the retailer’s profitability is mixed and depends on the ratio of the profit margin to the full price. On one hand, a deep markdown can cause the reference price in the next season to fall sharply as consumers learn faster, hurting the retailer. On the other hand, faster learning when the reference is low helps the retailer recover more quickly by simply raising the markdown price. Our study shows that a faster learning speed most likely hurts the retailer’s profit when his product has a low ratio of the profit margin to the full price but may benefit the retailer when this ratio is high. In the latter case, the retailer should be cautious in his ordering decision and rely less on discounts. Fast consumer learning enables the retailer to recover consumer references quickly in case they fall to low levels. See the first paper in Part C.

622713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
622713.value: There are several directions for further research. First, we have assumed that all consumers have the same learning speed in the current model. However, in reality, consumers may learn about the reference at different rates and hence the state (the reference prices) is of high dimensions. In this case, we need to redefine the mean-reverting behavior, perhaps in the spirit of defining a stable equilibrium of ordinary differential equations, e.g., via a Lyapunouv function. Second, because our focus so far has been to provide qualitative insights into the effects of the references of strategic consumers on the retailer’s dynamic pricing and inventory strategies, our work assumes that the retailer already knows the parameters of the aggregate demand functions. How to estimate these parameters from retailers’ sales data, or other information sources such as industry reports, consumer surveys, and forums, is another important research question. Third, in our current model, the full price is assumed to be exogenously given. An immediate future direction is to relax this assumption and allow the retailer to optimally determine both the full and markdown prices in each season.

622713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
622713.value: It is well accepted now that dynamic pricing is a two-edged sword. It serves as an effective means to manage uncertain demand and increase revenue as well as createing an incentive for strategic consumers to delay purchases until markdown price. In a repeated purchasing environment, consumers can learn about the history of a retailer’s markdown price, form the reference price, and adjust their purchasing decisions accordingly. This naturally raises a question of how a retailer should make its inventory and pricing decisions in response to such learning behavior. To answer this question, we build a joint pricing and inventory decision model incorporating reference updates over time. We found that the reference price follows a mean-reverting behavior under certain conditions. In the long run, whenever the reference deviates from the mean, it is expected to revert back to the mean in the near future. When the market size is deterministic, the reference always converges monotonically to a steady state for any give initial reference. That is, the reference will not fluctuate, let alone oscillate. Thus, demand uncertainty is the key driver for a cyclic pricing policy.

622813.label: Project Objectives
622813.value: We shall theoretically study the role of surface/interface stress in the size-dependent narrowing of the phase miscibility gap in three steps. A) We shall carry out thermodynamic analysis with consideration of the surface/grain boundary (GB) stress of original particle surfaces and GBs. B) We shall thermodynamically analyze the nucleation process of a compound phase from its parent phase. C) We shall develop a one-dimensional (1D) kinetic model, in which an extremely thin Pd film is exposed to a hydrogen gas environment. 622813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
622813.value: 固体的表面/界面应力在与材料表面/界面相关的物理、化学和力学性能中起着十分重要的作用，例如在吸附、催化、腐蚀、储氢和锂子电池等中。这些作用在具有大的比表面纳米颗粒和纳米晶材料中更为明显。由于表面/界面应力的作用，纳米颗粒和纳米晶材料表现出与尺度相关的性质。例如，当晶粒或颗粒的大小为纳米尺度时，介于固溶体相和对应的化合物相之间的互不相溶区（两相区）会显著地变窄，意味着固溶体相的溶质溶解度会增大，而化合物相中的溶解度会减小。这种与尺度相关的两相区变窄特行对于锂离子电池和储氢材料来说是极其重要的。尽管与尺度相关两相区变窄的研究，特别是实验方面，取得了不错的进展，但是表面/界面应力在其中扮演的角色还没有得到系统地研究。这已成为在推动固体表面/界面相关热力学理论进一步发展中必须要解决的瓶颈问题。基于我们在表面弹性力学、原子模拟、相场模拟和透射电子显微镜等方面的丰富研究经验，我们提出研究表面/界面应力在与尺度相关两相区变窄中所起到的作用。研究的目的是为了发展一套新颖的，可解释和预测与尺度相关两相区行为的热力学与动力学理论。为此，我们将要进行相应的理论研究、原子模拟和相场模拟、以及透射电子显微镜原位环境实验。立项的理论研究将进一步拓展我们先前关于纳米晶材料中溶质浓度与应变耦合行为的研究。我们将考虑表面/界面应力、母相和新相间的错配应变以及溶质的吸附和脱附速率，以发展纳米尺度下的热力学与动力学理论。我们将实施分子动力学模拟、第一原理分子动力学模拟以及相场模拟。这些模拟结果将给出与尺度相关的相变行为中原子尺度方面的信息，验证所拟理论研究中得到的公式并确定与表面和晶界相关的热力学参数。原位环境透射电子显微镜研究将提供，与尺度相关两相区变窄行为的直接实验证据。实验结果将验证理论公式以及原子模拟和相场模拟结果。圆满地完成所拟的研究项目将会推动与固体表面相关的热力学和动力学理论及技术的发展，这将对学术研究和工程实践带来重大的影响。此外，预期的研究成果将为发展与表面/界面相关的创新技术提供指导方针，并在高新科技产业中，特别是绿色能源工业中得到广泛的应用。

622813.label: Major findings and research outcome
622813.value: We have carried out thermodynamic analysis on the nucleation process of a compound phase from its parent phase with the consideration of the surface/grain boundary (GB) stress of original particle surfaces and GBs. We have developed a one-dimensional (1D) thermodynamic model to surface segregation of H in H-Pd films with different original H concentrations. We have also conducted molecular dynamics simulations on single crystalline Pd thin films with different thicknesses and various initial hydrogen concentrations at different temperatures. Since the size-dependent narrowing of the phase miscibility gap occurs during (de)lithiation of electrode materials in lithium-ion batteries, we have also investigated the size effects on the phase transformation behavior during (de)lithiation of electrode materials of CeO2 nanocrystals and Au nanoparticles. The preliminary Galvanostatic intermittent titration tests and electron diffraction results revealed that the Li solubility in CeO2 increased with decreasing CeO2 crystal size. In addition, we have demonstrated a new type of first-order transition below the Curie temperature, where the wide-distributed ultrahigh electrocaloric effects (ECE) are observed. (RSC Adv 2015) We have conducted the thermodynamics analysis and phase field simulations to demonstrate the mechanical compression-induced two types of pseudo-first-order phase transition, which could occur at a temperature below the Curie temperature. (Nano Energy 2015) We have conducted phase field modelling and thermodynamic analysis to investigate depolarization and compression induced large negative and positive electrocaloric effects (ECEs) in ferroelectric tetragonal crystalline nanoparticles. The results show that double-hysteresis loops of polarization versus electric field dominate at temperatures below the Curie temperature of the ferroelectric material, when the mechanical compression exceeds a critical value. (PCCP 2015) We have also conducted phase field simulations to investigate the frequency-dependent behavior of a ferroelectric single crystal with and without dislocation arrays. For the dislocation-free ferroelectric, both coercive field and remnant polarization increase with the increase in the applied electric field frequency. (Acta Mech 2017)

622813.value: The developed size-dependent thermodynamic and kinetic theories will be further developed to study the thermodynamic stability of nano-grained bulk materials.

622813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
622813.value: Nanomaterials have large surface-to-volume ratios and surfaces play significant roles in surface-related behaviors such as surface-chemistry-driven actuation, absorption, catalysis, corrosion and dealloying, stress-charge interactions, etc. Due to the large surface-to-volume ratios, nanomaterials behave different from their bulk counterparts. When the conventional continuum thermodynamic theory and kinetics are applied in the understanding and characterization of nanomaterials, the material properties exhibit the size-dependent behavior. In this project, we have developed novel thermodynamic and kinetic theories, in which the size of nanomaterials is an intensity variable, like temperature, pressure, and chemical composition. The successful completion of the project will facilitate the development of nanomaterials. In addition, the discovery of the pseudo-first-order phase transition (PFOPT) and the coexistence of ultrahigh positive and negative electrocaloric effects will have a significant impact on both academic research and engineering practice.

622913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
622913.value: Chlorination, chloramination, ozonation-chlorination, and ozonation-chloramination are widely used in drinking water disinfection. These disinfection processes afford great success in eliminating harmful microorganisms and acute waterborne diseases, but they may produce unintended halogenated DBPs due to the reactions of disinfectant(s) with natural organic matter, bromide, and iodide in source waters. About 600 halogenated DBPs have been identified in drinking waters. There are countless unidentified/ unknown halogenated DBPs. Epidemiological studies suggest that human consumption of chlorinated drinking water is somewhat associated with increased spontaneous abortions, stillbirth, birth defects, bladder cancer, and colorectal cancer. Toxicologic studies show that certain halogenated DBPs are cytotoxic, mutagenic, and genotoxic. A few halogenated DBPs have been regulated in the Disinfectants/DBPs Rule by the U.S. EPA, e.g., the maximum level for the sum of five haloacetic acids is set at 60 microgram/liter. Haloacetic acids are the most or second-most dominant group of halogenated DBPs in disinfected waters. Besides haloacetic acids, numerous other haloacids have been found in drinking waters. The ammonolysis of haloacids to prepare amino acids was mainly investigated in the early last century. About 500 amino acids are known. Alpha-amino acids are the building blocks of a vast array of proteins in human beings, and other amino acids can play critical biological roles as neurotransmitters and in transport and synthesis. In this project, the PI proposes to remove chlorine residual (as well as some neutral/volatile halogenated DBPs such as trihalomethanes) in tap water by a household point-of-use carbon device; then, for the tap water to be used for cooking (e.g., soup making), the PI proposes to add several drops of an aminating agent solution to it (just like the addition of vinegar or soybean sauce in cooking). By doing so, the PI expects to convert prevalent yet harmful haloacid DBPs in tap water to beneficial amino acids or less harmful dehalogenated products by ammonolysis. Effectiveness of the ammonolysis of haloacid DBPs will be examined in both chemical and toxicological aspects. The bottom line of such treatment is to reduce the overall adverse effects of halogenated DBPs in tap water. To ensure the reduction of the overall toxicity of tap water halogenated DBPs via ammonolysis, the comparative toxicity of each tap water before and after ammonolysis will be evaluated with the PI’s newly developed method, which enables the accurate/precise evaluation of the comparative toxicity of DBP mixtures with the sensitive embryo-larvae of a marine polychaete. 氯、氯胺、臭氧-氯和臭氧-氯胺被廣泛用於飲用水消毒。這些消毒劑在去除有害微生物和控制急性水生疾病方面取得了重大成效，但他們在消毒的同時能與水源中的天然有機物、溴離子和碘離子發生反應從而生成鹵代消毒副產物。迄今為止飲用水中已被鑑定的滷代消毒副產物大約有600種。仍有無數的滷代消毒副產物未被鑑定或未知。流行病學研究表明人類飲用氯消毒的飲用水與增加的自然流產、死胎、新生兒先天缺陷、膀胱癌和腸癌等有某種程度的相關性。毒理學研究顯示一些特定的滷代消毒副產物具有細胞毒性、致突變性和遺傳毒性。在美國國家環境保護局製定的消毒/消毒副產物法規中，一些鹵代消毒副產物已被列入規範，例如五種鹵代乙酸的總量不得超過60微克/升。鹵代乙酸是消毒後飲用水中存在的最主要或第二主要的一類鹵代消毒副產物。除了鹵代乙酸，大量的其它鹵代酸也已在飲用水中被發現。 利用鹵代酸的氨解反應來製備氨基酸的研究主要集中在上世紀初。迄今已知的氨基酸大約有500種。 Alpha-氨基酸是人體內大量蛋白質的基本組成單位，其它氨基酸也作為神經介質在人體傳輸和合成中起著關鍵的作用。在本項目中，首先擬用一個家用的活性炭裝置將自來水中的餘氯及一些中性的易揮發的滷代消毒副產物(如三鹵甲烷)去除；然後對用於烹飪的自來水(例如煮湯)，加入幾滴氨化劑(就像烹飪時加入醋和醬油一樣)，以期借助氨解反應將自來水中普遍存在的有害的滷代酸類消毒副產物轉化成有益的氨基酸或危害較小的脫鹵產物。對於鹵代酸類消毒副產物氨解反應的有效性將分別進行化學和毒理學方面的檢驗。該項處理工藝的最終目的是降低自來水中鹵代消毒副產物對人體健康的負面影響。為確保氨解反應後自來水中鹵代消毒副產物的整體毒性有所降低，將對氨解反應前後自來水的整體毒性進行評估。擬採用一種最新建立的比較毒性檢測方法，即一種對毒性敏感的海洋多毛目環節動物的胚胎幼蟲用作毒性受體來對消毒副產物的相對毒性進行精確的評估。

622913.label: Realisation of objectives
622913.value: (1) A new and sensitive method for detecting glycine (the amino acid corresponding to monohaloacetic acids) has been developed using ultra performance liquid chromatography/electrospray ionization-mass spectrometry (UPLC/ESI-MS) by setting selective ion recording (SIR) of m/z 74 in the ESI negative mode or by setting SIR of m/z 76 in the ESI positive mode. In combination with UPLC/ESI-MS SIR of m/z 75 in the ESI negative mode for the detection of glycolic acid (the hydrolyzed product of haloacetic acids), the ammonolysis/hydrolysis of a specific haloacid has been evaluated. The key parameters that affect the ESI ionization efficiency include cone voltage and capillary potential has been optimized by a glycine standard solution. Under the optimized conditions, glycine can be detected and the concentration of glycine in a water sample can be quantified even at the μg/L level. Accordingly, the new method significantly improves the sensitivity and precision in detecting the glycine concentration in a water sample. (2) By using the new and sensitive method, we studied the key parameters (i.e., haloacid species, reaction time, temperature, and aminating agent) that affect the ammonolysis of haloacetic acids (HAAs) in simulated cooking, which provided more important information about the ammonolytic reactions. Additionally, we studied the hydrolysis of individual haloacid DBPs in simulated cooking. (3) With a novel approach to evaluating the comparative toxicity of water samples by combining a freeze-drying pretreatment method with an in vivo assay using the embryos of a high-salinity-tolerance marine polychaete, P. dumerilii, we evaluated the developmental toxicity of water samples, including the individual DBP (i.e., iodoacetic acid) in a simulated raw water sample and the DBP mixtures in a simulated tap water sample, without and with ammonolysis. Accordingly, the reduction in the overall adverse effects of tap water halogenated DBPs via ammonolysis has been verified.

622913.label: Major findings and research outcome
622913.value: (1) We developed and optimized a new and sensitive method for detecting glycine using UPLC/ESI-MS by setting an SIR of m/z 74 in the ESI negative mode or an SIR of m/z 76 in the ESI positive mode. With the newly developed method, the sensitivity and precision in measuring the glycine concentration in a water sample have been significantly improved. (2) The effects of haloacid species, reaction time, temperature, and the aminating agent composition on the ammonolysis of HAAs in simulated cooking were investigated. Iodoacetic acid showed much higher conversion ratio during ammonolysis than the chlorinated and brominated analogues, which was attributed to the descending order of the carbon-halogen bond strength, i.e., C‒Cl > C‒Br > C‒I. The conversion of iodoacetic acid to glycine increased with increasing temperature or decreasing molar ratio of (NH4)2CO3 to NH3·H2O of the aminating agent. Moreover, the hydrolysis of iodoacetic acid to glycolic acid was also observed during ammonolysis. We found that the transformation to amino acids and the hydrolysis were the two major pathways of HAA conversion during ammonolysis. (3) With a novel approach, the developmental toxicity of the iodoacetic acid sample and the simulated tap water sample without and with ammonolysis were evaluated. After ammonolysis, the developmental toxicity of the iodoacetic acid sample and the simulated tap water sample were found to decrease by 8.2% and 16.4%, respectively, compared to the corresponding water samples without ammonolysis. We found that the ammonolysis was a “detoxification” process for individual HAAs and DBP mixtures in the chlorinated tap water. The results have been published or are under review for publication in top environmental journals including Environmental Science & Technology, Water Research, and Chemosphere. The results have also been presented in prestigious international conferences.

622913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
622913.value: (1) A sensitive method to detect glycine was newly developed using UPLC/ESI-MS by setting an SIR of m/z 74 in the ESI negative mode or an SIR of m/z 76 in the ESI positive mode. This new method may be extended for further application to the detection of other amino acids. (2) We found a reduction in the overall adverse effects of tap water halogenated DBPs via ammonolysis. The decrease in toxicity could be attributed to the conversion of halogenated DBPs to either amino acids or dehalogenated products. The PI would propose to further investigate the TOX decomposition and variation in DBP speciation via ammonolysis. (3) We found that hydrolysis might be an important “detoxification” pathway, via which the harmful DBPs were converted to the corresponding less harmful hydrolyzed products. The PI would propose to further investigate the hydrolysis of halogenated DBPs during cooking. For the tap water to be used for cooking, we propose to add an appropriate amount of carbonate to it (via the addition of baking soda in cooking). By doing so, we expect to accelerate the hydrolysis of halogenated DBPs during cooking by increasing the pH of the tap water.

622913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
622913.value: Disinfection achieves great success in eliminating harmful microorganisms and acute waterborne diseases, but it leads to the unintended formation of DBPs, which are associated with increased spontaneous abortions, and bladder and rectal cancers. Numerous haloacid DBPs are prevalent in disinfected waters and five HAAs have been regulated by the U.S. EPA. Most of previous studies focused on controlling the formation of DBPs, with little effort devoted to the treatment of formed DBPs. It has long been thought to be difficult and expensive to treat DBPs, once they are formed. Through this project, a new approach to controlling haloacid DBPs in tap water was developed via the ammonolysis of haloacid DBPs. The effects of haloacid species, reaction time, temperature and aminating agent on the ammonolysis of HAAs in household cooking were investigated. We found that the transformation to amino acids and hydrolysis were the two major pathways of HAA conversion during ammonolysis. Additionally, the overall toxicity of individual HAA and DBP mixtures in simulated tap water samples before and after ammonolysis was revealed for the first time. We found that the ammonolysis was a “detoxification” process for both individual HAA and DBP mixtures in the chlorinated tap water.

623013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
623013.value: Forecasting customer arrivals is essential for the effective management of many service facilities, such as popular tourist attractions and emergency departments, which require a projection of future demands in order to provide sufficient service capacity. In this project, we will study a representative profession, namely telephone call centers. Call centers, as the primary interface between customers and their service providers, have become an integral part of today’s economy. Because the bulk of a call center’s operating expense is the labor cost, staffing rules must be strategically developed to minimize cost while retaining service quality. Hence, an accurate arrival model is crucial for call center management. The Poisson process is the most widely used model for call arrival processes. However, many non-Poisson features have been observed in recent years. For instance, (i) daily call volume may have overdispersion relative to the Poisson distribution, and (ii) a call arrival process may have strong intraday/interday autocorrelations. Our goal is to develop a flexible, tractable, and parsimonious model for arrival processes that capture all the important statistical characteristics. Note that the arrival count exhibits overdispersion only when the time period is long, whereas for a short time period, it behaves Poisson-like. No prior work has raised the issue of time scale and our model can incorporate both Poisson and non-Poisson characteristics under a unified framework. In particular, we model the arrival process as a doubly stochastic Poisson process and its arrival rate process as a Cox-Ingersoll-Ross (CIR) process. Our preliminary results show that assuming no “time-of-day” effect, our model successfully captures the overdispersion and the correlation structure. We will extend the model to incorporate “seasonality” by using a time-dependent CIR process and investigate the associated estimation/prediction procedure. There are two levels of forecasting call centers may need. One is offline forecasting, i.e. forecasting several days ahead. In this case, we will use the Bayesian inference via the Markov chain Monte Carlo method. The other is online forecasting, since managers may hope to update their previous projections about afternoon call volume based on morning observations. We will use the particle filters method for that purpose. The results of this project are certainly not limited to call center management but are applicable to many other service industries such as health care, inventory management, etc. Therefore, this project will have significant impact on local society since service industries are the most important part of Hong Kong’s economy. 预测顾客到达对于诸如旅游景点、急救中心等许多服务设施的有效管理是很关键的，因为它们都需要对于未来的资源需求进行规划以保证足够的服务能力。在该项目中，我们将研究一个具有代表性的服务行业--电话呼叫中心。 电话呼叫中心是顾客和服务提供者之间主要的沟通渠道，它已经成为今天经济生活中不可或缺的一部分。由于呼叫中心的运营成本主要组成部分是人力成本，对人力资源必须进行有策略的规划以在提供优质服务的同时降低成本。因此，一个准确的顾客到达模型对于呼叫中心管理是很重要的。 泊松（Poisson）过程被广泛用作描述电话到达的模型，但是人们近年来观测到很多非泊松的特征。比如，一、日呼叫总量相比泊松分布有过度分散（overdispersion）现象；二、电话到达有很强的日内、日间的相关性。 我们的目标是构造一个灵活的、能计算的并且少参数的模型来描述重要的电话到达过程的统计性质。考虑一个时间区间内的电话总量，我们注意到这个电话总量在当时间区间大的时候会表现出过度分散，而在时间区间小的时候更像泊松分布。到现在为止还没有文献提出这个时间维度的问题，而我们的模型能够把泊松和非泊松的特征包括到一个统一的框架下。具体的说，我们用一个双层泊松过程来描述电话到达过程，而把到达速率过程描述成一个Cox-Ingersoll-Ross（CIR）过程。我们初步分析结果表明在假设没有"季节性"的条件下，我们的模型能很好的描述过度分散现象和相关性结构。未来我们将把这个模型推广成有时间变化参数的CIR过程以包含季节性，并且研究相对应的参数估计和预测问题。 呼叫中心需要两个层次的预测。一种是线下（offline）的 -- 预测若干天以后的情况。在这种情况下，我们将用通过Markov chain Monte Carlo方法进行贝叶斯（Bayesian）推断。另一种是线上（online）的 -- 管理者可能希望在观测到上午呼叫中心运营情况的条件下对于一天内剩余时间的电话到达进行相对应的预测修正。我们将用particle filters方法来解决相对应的问题。 该研究项目的结果实际上并不局限于呼叫中心管理，相反能够用到很多其他服务行业比如医疗保健、库存管理等。因此，基于服务行业在香港的重要地位，该项目将对本地社会经济产生重要影响。

623013.label: Realisation of objectives
623013.value: For objective (i): Poisson process plays a fundamental role in the field of operations research and management science. A great variety of research results on the performance of service systems and related decision-making problems depend critically on the assumption that the arrivals follow a Poisson process. However, data analysis in prior empirical studies gives different conclusions regarding whether the Poisson assumption is reasonable. One might attribute the difference in conclusions to the use of different datasets. We provide instead a novel perspective and demonstrate that the seemingly contradictory statistical evidence regarding the validity of the Poisson assumption is in fact manifestation of the stochastic behavior of the arrival data at different timescales. We have developed three distinct statistical tests for the same null hypothesis, that is, the arrival data follows a Poisson process. The tests are performed on different arrival data from two telephone call centers and the findings are consistent. First, we test whether the interarrival times have the exponential distribution, which is an implication of the null hypothesis. Neither the chi-square test nor the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test rejects the hypothesis. This suggests that the stochastic behavior of the arrival data at the micro timescale (of magnitude less than 1 second) is indeed Poisson. Second, we test whether the arrival counts have the Poisson distribution, which is another implication of the null hypothesis. The so-called Fisher dispersion test, which essentially examines the ratio between the variance of the arrival counts to the mean, rejects the hypothesis if the time interval is long (e.g., longer than 5 minutes), whereas does not reject the hypothesis otherwise (e.g., the time interval is less than 1 minute). This test suggests that the arrival data exhibits non-Poisson behavior at the macro timescale. Third, we test whether the arrival counts are correlated by fitting them to a simple autoregressive model and testing whether the autoregressive coefficient is nonzero. The test result to some extent explains how both Poisson and non-Poisson behavior can co-exist in the same arrival data. Specifically, the arrival counts in very short time intervals are “weakly” correlated, and the correlation is so insignificant that statistical tests cannot detect it. However, these insignificant correlations accumulate and eventually become significant at the macro timescale, attributing to the non-Poisson behavior, such as overdispersion. For objective (ii): Given the multiplicity of the stochastic behavior of the arrival data at different timescales, i.e., Poisson structure at the micro timescale, overdispersion and autocorrelation at the macro timescale, and even seasonality such as the time-of-day effect at an even longer timescale, we have developed a new model that uniﬁes the three distinct timescales to reconcile the seemingly contradictory but inherent features in the arrivals. Specifically, we model the arrival process as a doubly stochastic Poisson process (DSPP), that is, the arrival rate process itself is a stochastic process, but conditionally on the arrival rates the arrivals follow a Poisson process. In order that the DSPP model be parsimonious and has sufficient analytical tractability, we model the arrival rate process as a multiplication of two factors, one of which is a deterministic function that captures the seasonality whereas the other follows a so-called Cox-Ingersoll-Ross (CIR) process. The CIR process is a positive stochastic process that has been used broadly in finance and economics thanks to its analytical tractability. We then prove theoretically that the proposed DSPP model exhibits distinct kinds of behavior at different timescales. First, we show that the distribution of the arrival count under the DSPP model converges to the Poisson distribution as the length of the time interval goes to zero. This suggests that the DSPP model exhibits the Poisson behavior at the micro timescale. Second, we calculate explicitly the ratio between the variance to the mean of the arrival counts of a given time interval. This ratio turns out to be increasing roughly linearly in the length of the time interval. This theoretical result explains the finding of the statistical test on the Poisson distribution of the arrival count, that is, the Poisson assumption is rejected at the macro timescale but not at the micro timescale. Third, we calculate explicitly the correlation between the arrival counts at disjoint time intervals. In particular, such a correlation decays exponentially fast as the distance between the two intervals increases. Moreover, we compare the DSPP model with several popular arrival models in the literature and show that the proposed model fits the arrival data substantially better than the others. For objective (iii): Despite of its analytical tractability, the proposed DSPP model does impose a computational challenge for statistical inference. Specifically, it is nontrivial to estimate the parameters for defining the arrival rate process, because the arrival rates are unobservable. Typical methods for parameter estimation such as maximum-likelihood estimation would involve numerical integration that effectively “integrates out” the unobservable arrival rates to compute the likelihood of the observable arrival counts. The dimensionality of such integration equals the number of arrival counts, which is large in general, thereby making the integration computationally prohibitive. We have developed a Bayesian approach to address the parameter estimation and inference of the arrival rates. Following a Bayesian perspective, we view both the unknown parameters and the arrival rates as random variables, and characterize them with posterior distributions given the arrival counts. The joint posterior distribution itself lacks a tractable form, but it can be determined by its full conditionals, which are a set of conditional probability distributions of each random variable given the others. By choosing the prior distribution carefully and leveraging the Markovian structure in the arrival rate process, the full conditions can be reduced to tractable distributions, and thus we can develop a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method that integrates the Gibbs sampler and the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm to simulate them efficiently. For objective (iv): An important problem in call center management is the intraday forecasting of the call arrivals, which would facilitate real-time staffing decisions. For example, if the actual arrivals in the morning are significantly more than expected, then it is conceivable that the afternoon may witness significantly extra demand as well. If one can dynamically adjust the forecasts as more data become available in a timely fashion, then the manager can request additional temporal agents possibly from a third-party provider to prepare the call center for future surge in demand during the later time of the day. The MCMC method developed for parameter estimation could be used for this purpose in principle, but it is computationally inefficient in an “online” environment because for each new arrival count, all the historical data needs to be included in the computation as well. Therefore, we have developed a sequential forecasting method based on particle filters. This method provides both the point forecasts and the distributional forecasts of future arrivals. The computation is fast -- given each new arrival count, the computation needed for adjusting the forecasts does not involve historical data. Using real data, we show that the proposed method delivers substantially more accurate forecasts than several popular methods in the literature.

623013.label: Major findings and research outcome
623013.value: Poisson process has been widely used for modeling arrivals to a service system such as telephone call centers to develop managerial insight. Nevertheless, prior statistical studies regarding the validity of the Poisson assumption seem to be contradictory. Given the fundamental role of the Poisson model in operations research, it is critical to address this issue and to understand the stochastic behavior of the arrival data. Our first finding is that timescale is critical for describing the stochastic behavior. The arrivals exhibit Poisson behavior at the micro timescale, whereas strongly non-Poisson behavior at a longer timescale. The seeming contradiction in prior studies regarding the Poisson assumption does not stem from the use of different datasets, but from the fact that their statistical analysis focused on the behavior at different timescales. Second, we have developed a doubly stochastic Poisson process (DSPP) model for the arrivals than can incorporate their behavior at different timescales under one unified framework. Third, we have developed a Bayesian approach for estimating the unknown parameters of the proposed DSPP model. Because the parameters lie in the arrival rate process, which is unobservable, to estimate them following a frequentist approach such as maximum-likelihood typically involves a high-dimensional integration which can become computationally prohibitive. The proposed method circumvents such computational challenge. Fourth, we have developed an online forecasting method that can adjust arrival prediction dynamically as more data becomes available. Our method outperforms the existing methods in the literature significantly. The first two findings are summarized in the paper “Timescales in Modeling Call Center Arrivals” that is currently under review. The last two are summarized in the paper “Forecasting Overdispersed Arrivals via Bayesian Simulation” that is currently under review. Some preliminary results are reported in the conference papers “A Bayesian Approach for Modeling and Analysis of Call Center Arrivals” and “On-line Forecasting of Call Center Arrivals via Sequential Monte Carlo”. We have also done research beyond the project objectives. First, we study the overdispersion in large service systems and find that the variance and the mean of the arrival count follow a power law relationship. See the conference paper “Scaling and Modeling of Call Center Arrivals”. Second, the Bayesian methods for the DSPP model may not be easy to implement for practitioners. We therefore propose a simpler arrival model based on Poisson autoregression that is more computationally tractable. See “Poisson Autoregressive Models for Arrival Data” that is currently under review.

623013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
623013.value: This project has focused on modeling customer arrivals to service systems. However, to realize the full potential of the proposed arrival model, we need to further analyze the performance of the service system under the model and optimize the operational decisions. For instance, we may investigate the queueing performance such as mean waiting time of a multi-server queue under the new arrival model, and then derive the optimal staffing level (e.g., number of servers) to achieve certain quality of service. It is conceivable that given the additional random fluctuation captured by the new arrival model relative to the Poisson process, a higher staffing level is required to achieve the same quality of service than what the Poisson model would result in. Another possible extension is to incorporate geographic information in the proposed arrival model. Recent years have witnessed the rise of sharing economy around the world. Particularly, ridesharing platforms such as Uber open new research opportunities, and it is critical to understand the stochastic behavior of the arrival process of the ride requests. Clearly, spatial information is as important as temporal information in this context for developing a useful arrival model. This calls for an integrated spatial-temporal data analysis.

623013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
623013.value: Operational decision making in service systems usually depends largely on the characterization of the random fluctuations involved. In general, the higher the random fluctuations are, the more resources are required to achieve the same level of quality of service. Exogenous customer arrivals represent a primary source of uncertainty, and thus their stochastic behavior needs to be characterized carefully in order to deliver effective operations management. Due to its simplicity, Poisson process has been a highly popular model for describing the stochastic behavior of the arrivals. However, it may underestimate the magnitude of the random fluctuations, leading to insufficient service supply to accommodate the unexpected surge in demand. In this project, we have developed a set of sophisticated statistical tools for analyzing, modeling, and predicting customer arrivals in an accurate, timely fashion. In particular, the new class of arrival models proposed in this project can capture the kind of stochastic behavior that matters to system performance and enjoys a degree of tractability similar to the Poisson process. The new models be used to develop more effective operational decisions to optimize the performance of the service systems in the future.

623113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
623113.value: Full/partial closures of roads for utility trench works can incur huge social costs, which can be measured in many aspects such as delays, detours and other disruptions to road users. Few countries have developed a solid method for permit period assessment (PPA) of utility trench works. Permit periods are usually assessed based on engineers’ experience. One potential problem of an inaccurate PPA method is that the permit period granted by a relevant authority using this method can be unreasonably longer and consequently the closure of roads can be much longer than the actual working period needed by the utility company to complete the corresponding trench works. This would significantly increase the social costs and may even cause strong public complaints. This research proposes to develop an appropriate PPA methodology for drainage trench works, which will provide a robust incentive for utility companies to effectively plan their works, allocate adequate resources and formulate workable schedules to complete trench works within a reasonably short time such that the period of road closure is minimized for efficient road utilization and reduced social costs. A wide range of factors affect the permit period, including trench dimensions, work class, site location, road type, time constraint, weather conditions, geological conditions, and congested underground utility installations. A data-mining approach will be used in view of the many influencing factors and large amount of historical trench works permit data available from the excavation permit management system (XPMS) in Hong Kong. The first part of this research will prepare data and build a centralized multidimensional data warehouse. Raw data from the XPMS will be preprocessed to ensure the quality of data and prepared in the form of datasets containing appropriate “attributes” and “cases”. This will significantly facilitate exploratory data mining analysis from different perspectives/scenarios and at different levels of granularity. The second part of this research will first extract rules/patterns in drainage trench works through multidimensional analysis and quantitative association rule mining and then validate these rules/patterns through site surveys and expert interviews. The third part of this research will first formulate typical artificial neural network models to predict the working periods of drainage trench works in different scenarios and then develop a PPA module incorporating these typical models as a PPA decision support tool for drainage trench works. This PPA methodology can be extended to trench works in other utility trades or non-trench road works in the future. 因管線設施掘路工程所造成的道路全封閉或部分封閉會産生巨大的社會成本，這體現在道路延誤、繞行等許多方面的影響。很少國家已經開發出一種針對管線掘路工程的准許期限評估方法，准許期限評估主要依據工程師的經驗。一個潛在的問題是相關政府機構基于不准確的方法所確定的准許期限有可能過長，進而使得道路封閉時間超出實際所需完成掘路工程的時間。這將大大增加社會成本，甚至可能引起公衆的投訴。本研究旨在開發一個合適的給排水工程准許期限評估方法，以激勵公共事業公司制定行之有效的計劃，合理分配資源，並制定切實可行的工程進度表來盡量縮短掘路工程所占用的時間，使道路資源得到有效的利用，減少社會成本。影響准許期限評估的因素很多，包括溝槽尺寸、工程類型、開挖地點、道路類型、時間限制、天氣、地質條件以及地下管線擁堵狀況等。基于從香港掘路管理系統中所提取的大量曆史數據，擬采用數據挖掘的辦法來評判這些影響因素。 本研究的第一部分將集中在數據准備以及建立一個集中的多維數據倉庫。對香港掘路管理系統中提取的原始數據預處理，以確保數據質量並爲後期數據集提供相應的“屬性”和“關系”。這將大大有利于從不同的角度/場景和不同層次的粒度進行數據挖掘分析。第二部分將首先提出給排水工程的規則和模式，通過多維分析，定量化這些關聯規則，然後通過現場調查和專家訪談進一步驗證規則和模式。第三部分將首先建立典型人工神經網絡來預測在不同情況下的給排水管溝工程的工作周期，然後開發一個准許期限評估模塊，將這些典型模式作爲給排水工程的准許期限評估決策支持工具。此准許期限評估方法可以擴展到其他公用事業，或在未來應用于非開挖道路工程。

623113.label: Realisation of objectives
623113.value: (1) Realization of objective 1: To identify key factors that impact the working periods of drainage trench works The study team has analyzed a large number of permit records of drainage trench works through data mining, which is a process of extracting previously unknown, valid and actionable patterns or knowledge from large databases for crucial decision support. Compared to traditional methods, data mining techniques have demonstrated superior performance in analyzing large quantities of data: (a) Data mining is based on historical data rather than assumptions, (b) data visualization can present rules for better interpretation, (c) it is much faster in processing large amounts of data, and (d) data mining models can be reused and updated in real time by connecting to data sources. Data quality plays a fundamental role in the research methods taken in this study. Raw permit data of drainage trench works has been preprocessed to ensure the quality of data and prepared in the form of datasets containing appropriate “attributes” and “cases”. The study team has done the following preparative work: (a) identifying data requirements, (b) selecting data with attributes of interest and filtering out attributes not related to this study, (c) addressing data reliability and removing “noisy” data such as typing errors and invalid attribute values, (d) transforming some data attributes, and (e) building a new data warehouse where data are organized in multidimensional and multi-leveled structures. Through data mining, key factors that impact the working periods of drainage trench works have been identified. The key factors are trench dimensions (length, width and depth), work class (including conversion, laying pumping mains, laying sewers, replacing sewers, sewer connection, emergency works, landscaping, and propping installation), site location, road type (including expressways, urban trunk roads, primary distributors, rural trunk roads, district distributors, local distributors, major local distributors, minor local distributors, local roads, feeder roads, rural roads A, rural roads B, new streets/roads, non-motorable roads and footpaths, private roads, lanes, and open spaces), and multiplication factors (including time constraints, rainy seasons, hard rock, congested underground installations, and steep roads). (2) Realization of objective 2: To model the interactions of various impact factors and identify useful rules/patterns in drainage trench works The study team has taken a data mining approach to analyze the correlations between the working periods of drainage trench works and their impact factors and to identify useful rules/patterns. Both descriptive and predictive data mining models have been explored. The former aims to uncover previously unknown rules existing in data, e.g., detecting a small number of observations that are obviously different from the patterns of the majority. The latter aims to predict explicit values of unknown and future cases based on rules identified from known results. In descriptive data mining, the quantitative association rule mining (QARM) technique has been applied. The following algorithm is followed in applying QARM: (a) determine the number of partitions for each quantitative attribute, (b) map categorical and quantitative attributes to consecutive integers, (c) count the supports of quantitative and categorical attributes, (d) use the revised Apriori algorithm to find all frequent itemsets and generate association rules, and (e) determine and validate the association rules with domain experts. In predictive data mining, artificial neural networks (ANN) have been applied. ANN is of particular interest in this study because very often it can offer superior forecasting accuracy as a means to efficiently model large and complex problems that may have hundreds of interactive predictor variables. However, no single algorithm performs the best in accuracy and speed on all predictive modeling problems. To select a suitable algorithm, experiments and comparisons against multiple criteria (such as root mean square error, number of input variables required, and computing time) have been conducted. Regarding the network topology, relevant parameters are set by intuition initially and then optimized through multiple cycles of experiments. The study team has tried supervised learning and unsupervised learning to train the network. The error correction method and nearest neighbor method are used to adjust weights to appropriate values. (3) Realization of objective 3: To formulate artificial neural network models for the prediction of the working periods of drainage trench works in different scenarios The various permit attributes (e.g., work class, road type, trench dimensions, time constraints, rainy season, site location, hard rock, congested underground installations, and steep roads) are used as inputs (predictor variables) of the proposed ANN model, while the working period of a drainage trench work as the output. Some input attributes have categorical values, which are transferred to numerical ones. Then, the following procedures are undertaken to explore appropriate ANN models: (a) selecting a suitable algorithm, (b) optimizing the ANN topology, (c) selecting suitable training datasets, and (d) testing the ANN model. Models derived from this study have been validated to prove their creditability. In general, descriptive models can be validated through cause-effect analysis (e.g., based on site surveys to confirm the identified association rules) and further judgment by industrial experts; predictive models can be validated by testing on independent datasets and comparing “values predicted by models” with “actual values”. Surveys of drainage experts and work sites have been conducted to address the problem of data reliability and to validate the models established based on historical data. For example, the working period of an excavation is dependent on the interactions of all work activities involved and the various attributes of this excavation. These interactions have been measured through site surveys and interviews with drainage experts. Survey results have been analyzed to formulate an interaction matrix to validate the rules identified and to direct the training of ANN models for improved efficiency and accuracy. To select the representative work sites, the following conditions are considered: (a) the work sites involve work classes that most frequently occur in drainage services based on the historical permit data; (b) the work sites cover a broad geographical area, and (c) the work sites involve multiplication factors and are carried out by typical drainage service companies. A site survey record form is designed in consultation with drainage experts and excavation workers. In the site survey, real time information related to drainage trench works has been collected, including the overall arrangement of the work site, multiplication factors applied, resources (e.g., equipment and labor) deployed on site by the contractor, idling time, planned schedules, and actual progress of various work activities.

623113.value: Through data-mining, site surveys and expert interviews, this research has developed an improved permit period assessment (PPA) method for drainage trench works. This PPA method can significantly increase the accuracy in estimating the construction time of drainage trench works, and provide government authorities a useful tool for assessing the construction periods of drainage trench works and making informed decisions in issuing permits for drainage trench works. It will also create a strong incentive for drainage service companies to properly plan their works, allocate adequate resources and formulate workable schedules in order to complete their works within a reasonable time. This, in turn, will minimize the periods of road closures for efficient utilization of the road network and reduce the social costs to the general public.

623113.value: The PPA method developed for drainage trench works can be extended to other utility trades (e.g., electricity, telecommunication, gas and water supply) and non-trench road works in the future. 623113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
623113.value: Trench works are frequently required by utility companies for various reasons. Such works usually block roads and affect the normal utilization of the road network. Full or partial road closures incur social costs, e.g., delays, detours and other disruptions to road users. Through a systematic study approach of data-mining, site surveys and expert interviews, this research has developed an improved method that can more accurately assess the time needed to complete drainage trench works. This method would provide government authorities a useful tool for assessing the construction period of drainage trench works and making informed decisions in issuing permits for such works. It will also create a strong incentive for drainage service companies to plan and manage their works effectively such that they can be completed within a reasonable time. This, in turn, will minimize the social costs associated with road works.

623313.label: Project Objectives
623313.value: Develop a trans-scale model that can couple the mass transport through the porous electrode at the REV scale with the mass and charge transport at the pore scale. The model will not only allow creation of synergy among the transport of ions, electrons, and mass transport in the multi-scale electrode, but also enable rapid testing of hypotheses aimed at improving cell performance. Formulate a lattice Boltzmann model to understand the coupled mass and charge transport in the electrode pores. We are particularly interested in the study of the effect of complex solid-electrolyte interfaces. Devise a unique experimental setup with which the pore-level mass-transfer coefficient and REV-level effective diffusivity of vanadium species through the porous electrode can be experimentally determined and characterized. Special attention will be paid to the effect of dispersion induced by electrolyte flows through complex pore structures. Create high-activity electrodes with large specific surface area and high permeability. Radically different from conventional electrodes made of graphite felt, a new type of electrode will be made of carbon fibers with penetrated micro/nano pores to provide secondary paths for the transport of electrolytes. This idea will enable the specific surface area of the electrode to be increased without sacrificing the permeability. Moreover, a highly-active thin-film nitrogen-doped graphene catalyst layer will be deposited onto the surface of the electrodes to boost the reaction kinetics. Characterize the performance of the electrodes and optimize the design of the VRFB to maximize the performance. In summary, the most original and innovative aspects of this interdisciplinary research include: i) the trans-scale model to be developed will enable the mass transport through the porous electrode at the REV scale to be coupled with the transport and redox reactions at the pore scale; and ii) the proposed lattice Boltzmann model will provide insight into the effect of complex solid-electrolyte interfaces on mass transport; and iii) the creation of the high-activity electrode with large specific surface area and high permeability will bring about a drastic boost in the cell performance.

623313.label: Realisation of objectives
623313.value: During the undertaking of this project, we have achieved much more than what was listed in the original objectives. We have investigated the coupled mass and charge transfer in liquid electrolyte flows through porous electrodes with redox reactions at solid-electrolyte interfaces. In particularly, we have developed the comprehensive model to better understand the synergetic effect among the transport of ions, electrons, and mass transport in the multi-scale electrode. With the numerical studies, we have done several experimental optimizations in the practical systems, including the vanadium redox flow batteries, fuel cells and water electrolysis. Through those experimental investigations, we have achieved a relatively high performance output. Especially, the high-performance vanadium flow batteries have been achieved by designing the high-activity electrode with large surface area and high permeability and the high-efficiency membrane with good selectivity. With the above-mentioned experimental and theoretical investigations, we have not only got the in-depth understandings of the coupled mass and charge transfer in liquid electrolyte flows through porous electrodes with redox reactions at solid-electrolyte interfaces, but also achieved the high performance in the practical applications.
