623313.label: Major findings and research outcome
623313.value: With the support of the present RGC grant, we have made significant contributions to the study of the coupled mass and charge transfer in liquid electrolyte flows through porous electrodes with redox reactions at solid-electrolyte interfaces. The results obtained in this project have been presented in 7 top-rated journal papers, as listed in Sections 8. The major findings are summarized as follows: We have developed the systematic mathematical models to investigate the synergetic effect among the transport of the ions, electrons and mass transport during the multi-scale electrode in the redox flow batteries. With this model, we incorporated the effects of SOC-dependent electrolyte viscosity into the vanadium redox flow batteries modeling, and got a more comprehensive understanding about the ion transport in the electrolyte. We have investigated the effect of flow fields on the vanadium redox flow batteries performance experimentally. The relationship between flow rates and flow fields has been comprehensive studied, and it demonstrated that the adoption of flow fields in VRFBs could be an effective approach for improving system efficiency. We have devised a unique experimental setup to achieve the high-performance ethanol-hydrogen peroxide fuel cell by introducing a redox couple (V(IV)/V(V)) to the cathode while using hydrogen peroxide to chemically charge the redox ions. With this creative design, we have achieved much higher peak power density comparing with the conventional setup. With the motivation to get more comprehensive fundamental understandings about the flow batteries, we have summarized the recent numerical simulations development for such system. To increase the driven distance of electric vehicles, we have done the significant enhancements on the zinc-hydrogen peroxide fuel cell by introducing a redox couple (V(II)/V(III)) to the anode while using zinc to chemically charge the redox ions. With this creative design, we have achieved much higher peak power density and lower cost comparing with the conventional setup. We have applied polybenzimidazole membranes into vanadium redox flow batteries to improve the columbic efficiency and cycling performance by decreasing the crossover of vanadium ions. We have also fabricated a novel anion exchange membrane for water electrolysis to produce hydrogen. With this kind of membrane, we achieved much better water electrolysis for hydrogen mass production.

623313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
623313.value: The present project has primarily focused on the understandings of the coupled mass and charge transfer in liquid electrolyte flows through porous electrodes with redox reactions at solid-electrolyte interfaces, with which the ion transport and charge transfer were experimentally and numerically investigated. The outcome of this project has deepened our fundamental understanding of the synergetic effect among the transport of ions, electrons, and mass transport in the multi-scale electrode and the separator and provided the needed information for the design of the high-activity electrode and the high-efficiency membrane with applications in vanadium redox flow batteries, fuel cells and water electrolysis.

623313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
623313.value: It has been extensively demonstrated that energy storage technologies have the greater applications in the grid-scale electricity storage and the electric vehicles. However, the mechanisms behind those technologies, including VRFBs, fuel cells and water electrolysis, are complicated, especially the coupled mass and charge transfer in liquid electrolyte flows through porous electrodes with redox reactions. To better understand the synergetic effect among the transport of ions, electrons, and mass transport in the multi-scale electrode, the trans-scale model has been proposed to describe the multi-scale transport of ions and the coupled redox reactions. With this model, the effects of SOC-dependent electrolyte viscosity on the performance of VRFBs have been studied. In addition to the numerical investigations, the relationship between flow rates and flow fields in the VRFBs has been investigated experimentally. To achieve high performance for VRFBs, PBI membrane has been adopted and improved the columbic efficiency largely. As an effective energy storage technology for the electric vehicles, fuel cells have been enhanced by introducing redox couples (V(IV)/V(V)) and (V(II)/V(III)) into cathode and anode respectively while using previous cathode and anode active materials to chemically charge the redox ions. Moreover, a novel anion exchange membrane has been fabricated for hydrogen mass production by water electrolysis. Those theoretical descriptions on the mechanisms and experimental improvements on the practical applications have opened a breakthrough in the energy storage technology.

639613.label: Realisation of objectives
639613.value: All three research objectives of the project were successfully achieved. In several ways in fact, this project exceeded our original goals and expectations. Starting with the first goal, a key point in most design methodologies is the representation of a realistic structure with a simple (usually equivalent single degree of freedom) system. In the context of rocking structures, we proposed a methodology to derive dynamic equivalency between a variety of rocking configurations, including but not limited to, the (symmetric and asymmetric) rocking frame with the archetypal rocking block (see “Dynamically equivalent rocking structures” by DeJong and Dimitrakopoulos, 2014, Part C). The proposed methodology hinges on local linearization of the nonlinear equations of motion. The error associated with the proposed linearization was quantified and was deemed acceptable in comparison to the relatively large uncertainties associated with the ground motion prediction. Further, we paid special attention to the dynamics of the asymmetric rocking (segmental) frame. The investigation of an asymmetric configuration was utilized to account for potential differences in height of piers due to e.g., an inclined topography in the transverse or longitudinal direction of the bridge. From a kinematics perspective, the asymmetric rocking frame/bent was challenging and substantially more complicated compared to its symmetric counterpart. Specifically, the two piers do not exhibit the same rocking rotation and the connecting cap-beam, apart from a rigid body translation, sustains also rigid body rotation (see “Seismic response analysis of the planar rocking frame” by Dimitrakopoulos and Giouvanidis, Part C). One of the main contributions of that work was that despite the very different kinematics between the two configurations the potential asymmetry does not jeopardize the stability of the bridge bent. In the same context, we investigated the seismic response of the (symmetric and asymmetric) rocking bridge bent configuration enhanced with central tendons and/or viscous dampers transforming it into a “hybrid” rocking system. As a first approach, we focused on the comparison of its seismic response with the pertinent response of the freestanding (asymmetric) rocking frame. We also considered that after a certain elongation (or equivalently rocking rotation) the system of tendons/dampers fracture and the structure behaves as freestanding. We concluded that the higher the fracture elongation the more drastic the stability enhancement of the frame. In a subsequent research publication (see “Seismic performance of rocking frames with flag-shaped hysteretic behavior” by Giouvanidis and Dimitrakopoulos, Part C), we examined the influence of the prestressed central tendons and/or the buckling-restrained braces on the seismic rocking response. That study revealed the counter-intuitive effect of the presstressing force. Specifically, prestressing the tendons could be beneficial mostly for small rocking rotations. For large rocking rotations, however, the prestressing force becomes progressively detrimental as the size of the columns increases. The analysis also compared hybrid rocking frames with negative, zero, or positive post-uplift lateral stiffness. It revealed that increasing the stiffness of the frames does not necessarily lead to superior performance due to their sensitivity to the characteristics of a ground motion. Subsequently, a frame with negative stiffness could outperform a positive stiffness frame and vice versa. Intrigued by the sensitivity of the rocking response to the different characteristics of a ground motion, we revisited the rocking problem from a probabilistic point of view (see “Dimensionless fragility curves for rocking response to near-fault excitations” by Dimitrakopoulos and Paraskeva, Part C). Considering ground motions with near-fault characteristics, either solely coherent pulses or synthetic ground motions that include, in addition, a stochastic high-frequency component, we proposed (dimensionless) fragility curves that can estimate the overturning tendency, as well as the peak response rotation of different (in size) rocking structures. Importantly, that study unveiled the existence of a critical peak ground acceleration threshold, below and above which, the peak response scales differently. When the structure does not overturn, the peak rotation follows approximately a biplanar pattern with respect to the intensity and the predominant frequency of the excitation. Finally, the analysis also verified that rocking overturning depends primarily on the velocity characteristics of the ground motion. To investigate further the dynamic response and the rocking overturning mode of a structure, we examined analytically the stability of the rocking block when excited by a family of multi-lobe pulse ground motions (see “Closed-form rocking overturning conditions for a family of pulse ground motions” by Dimitrakopoulos and Fung, Part C). The analysis unveiled the plurality of overturning modes and the complex overturning spectra. It also showed that the crucial overturning mode is overturning after specifically one impact before the end of the excitation. That study also offered original closed-form solutions and self-similar spectra that capture completely the overturning conditions of the block. Finally, motivated by the complex rocking response, we formulated a more sophisticated methodology to capture the impact behavior; a phenomenon critical to rocking motion. The proposed framework stems from nonsmooth multibody dynamics with unilateral contacts. Specifically, we proposed a nonsmooth dynamics framework which treats discontinuous unilateral contact events and the transitions between different contact types as linear complementarity problems (LCPs) (see “Nonsmooth dynamic analysis of sticking impacts in rocking structures” by Giouvanidis and Dimitrakopoulos, Part C). Key feature of the proposed methodology is that rocking response can be decomposed into continuous (smooth) motion and discontinuous (nonsmooth) events (e.g., impacts). The proposed nonsmooth dynamic analysis approach resulted in a concise mathematical formulation of the impact phenomenon. The proposed LCPs encapsulated all physically feasible post-impact states. The analysis demonstrated, analytically and numerically, the ability of the LCPs to capture the complex post-impact behavior of both rigid and flexible rocking structures. The results of the nonsmooth dynamics approach verified pertinent analytical results from other methodologies. In addition, to validate the developed computational scheme, our numerical results were also validated with numerical and experimental results from literature.

Verification of the proposed numerical scheme: The results of the proposed non-smooth modelling scheme will be assessed primarily with experimental results available in literature

639613.label: Major findings and research outcome
639613.value: (i) We proposed a methodology to derive an equivalency between a variety of rocking configurations including but not limited to, the (symmetric and asymmetric) rocking frame with the archetypal rocking block (“Dynamically equivalent rocking structures” by DeJong and Dimitrakopoulos, Part C). (ii) Focusing on the dynamics of the asymmetric rocking frame, the potential asymmetry does not jeopardize the stability of the bridge bent. In addition, we investigated the seismic response of a hybrid rocking frame (supplemented with central tendons and/or viscous dampers) revealing the importance of the fracture elongation. The higher the fracture elongation the more drastic the stability enhancement of the frame (“Seismic response analysis of the planar rocking frame” by Dimitrakopoulos and Giouvanidis, Part C). (iii) In the same context, a hybrid rocking bridge bent is a rocking frame enhanced with prestressed central tendons and buckling-restrained braces exhibiting flag-shaped hysteretic behavior (“Seismic performance of rocking frames with flag-shaped hysteretic behavior” by Giouvanidis and Dimitrakopoulos, Part C). That study revealed the counter-intuitive role of the prestressing force in the stability. Prestressing the tendons could be beneficial mostly for small rocking rotations. For large rocking rotations, the prestressing force becomes progressively detrimental as the size of the columns increases (iv) Investigating the rocking problem from a probabilistic perspective, we revealed a hidden order in the rocking response. There is a critical peak ground acceleration, below and above which, the peak rocking response scales differently and follows approximately a biplanar pattern with respect to the intensity and the predominant frequency of the excitation (“Dimensionless fragility curves for rocking response to near-fault excitations” by Dimitrakopoulos and Paraskeva, Part C). (v) Emphasizing on the overturning mode of freestanding rocking structures, we showed that from a design perspective the crucial overturning mode is overturning after one impact before the end of the excitation. Further, we proposed original closed-form solutions that capture completely the overturning conditions (“Closed-form rocking overturning conditions for a family of pulse ground motions” by Dimitrakopoulos and Fung, Part C). (vi) Finally, we proposed a concise mathematical formulation that captures the impact phenomenon during rocking. The proposed nonsmooth dynamics framework treats discontinuous unilateral contact events and the transitions between different contact types as linear complementarity problems. We unveiled the ability of the proposed LCPs to capture the complex post-impact behavior of both rigid and flexible rocking structures verifying pertinent analytical, numerical and experimental results from literature (“Nonsmooth dynamic analysis of sticking impacts in rocking structures” by Giouvanidis and Dimitrakopoulos, Part C).

639613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
639613.value: As a further development of this project, research should focus on the identification of strong ground motion parameters tailored to the peculiarities of rocking motion. Original intensity measures are needed to reduce the dispersion in the rocking response and provide an estimation of the structural demand that is independent from seismological parameters in the case of realistic earthquake records. Also, an in-depth probabilistic analysis should be conducted on the seismic response of hybrid rocking bridge bents with different overall lateral stiffness (positive, or zero or negative). Such a comparison would reveal potential optimal design characteristics of the examined hybrid rocking frames. The present research should also be extended to account for the behavior of the abutments, and the deck-abutment interaction during rocking motion.

639613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
639613.value: The conventional design paradigm of bridge substructures is to resist earthquake excitation through strength and ductility. In contrast, the rocking design paradigm aims to diminish structural deformation, and therefore damage, during earthquakes, by allowing rigid body movements of structural segments around predefined interfaces. Rocking also allows the combined utilization of the benefits of seismic isolation with the merits of the precast construction method. To contribute to the maturing of this methodology and eventually its implementation in engineering practice, this research addressed major challenges focusing on the seismic response of rocking bridge frames. From a design perspective, it proposed a methodology to derive equivalent single degree of freedom structures from realistic (and more complicated) rocking configurations. Further, it examined the dynamics of both freestanding and hybrid (i.e., supplemented with re-centering and energy dissipation devices) rocking frames. This project also proposed closed-form expressions that describe completely the associated overturning (failure) modes. Finally, it proposed an original methodology to treat the contact phenomenon during rocking motion.

639713.label: Realisation of objectives
639713.value: Following the proposal, we have carefully carried out this project. Thanks to the hard work of the team, all of the proposed goals were realized. Details are given below in an item-by-item format. Objective 1: Ba0.95La0.05FeO3−δ (BLF) was studied combining molecular simulations and experiments on single crystal thin films. Lattice dynamics simulations were applied to study the stabilization of BaFeO3−δ upon doping with La3+. Simulation results reveal the defect energy for substituting one Ba2+ with La3+ in the cubic phase to be lower than that in the monoclinic phase, contributing to its stabilization. Also, our results suggested that the charge compensation mechanism upon doping is filling oxygen vacancies and La3+ tends to trap the mobile oxygen anions. Besides these, BLF, and SrNb0.1Co0.9O3−δ (SNC) were evaluated as cathodes for SOFCs and were grown on yttria-stabilized zirconia substrates using pulsed laser deposition. Their intrinsic properties were also evaluated, in particular, the oxygen reduction reaction mechanism of the thin films were analyzed. Both materials exhibit in the film configuration a low polarization resistance and therefore a high activity. Objective 2: In line with objective 2, we also aimed at establishing a rigorous link between experiments and computation by using traditional electrochemical techniques. For example, the electrical conductivity relaxation (ECR) technique is a common experimental method for determining the surface reaction rate k and the bulk diffusion coefficient D of mixed ionic and electronic conductors such as BLF and SNC. Yet, the reliability of estimating k and D using ECR is often questioned. We used asymptotic statistical methods to assess the quality of the two estimated parameters for different sample geometries. Furthermore, we developed analytical expressions that allow us to assess the combined identifiability of k and D estimates as a function of two sets of generalized parameters. We also highlighted the importance of considering higher order nonlinearities when determining the confidence on the estimated. We made extensive use of this analysis and found that SrCo1-xScxO3-δ with x=0.05 is the material with the highest activity. Furthermore, we linked the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy data to the distribution of relaxation time method, which allowed us to determine the timescales of the physical and chemical processes taking place within the various electrodes. Objective 3: Dopant element and doping site can play a significant role in determining SOFC cathode activities. In order to investigate the effect of dopants, we prepared a series of A-site and B-site doped BFO materials, including Ba0.95La0.05FeO3−δ (BLF), Ba0.95Sm0.05FeO3−δ (BSF), Ba0.95Gd0.05FeO3−δ (BGF), BaFe0.95Zr0.05O3−δ(BFZ) and BaFe0.95Ce0.05O3−δ (BFC). We found that A-site doping usually leads to higher electrical conductivity, while B-site doping results in a faster oxygen diffusion kinetics and higher ORR activity than A-site doping. We have also confirmed these findings by theoretical calculations. With these findings, we rationally designed a highly active SOFC cathode material, i.e., BaFe0.95In0.05O3-δ (BFI) by resorting to a combined isovalent and lower-valance co-doping strategy. Objective 4: We continued the development of integrated multiscale models featuring both continuum (finite element-based) and atomistic (molecular dynamics-based) methods. In that regard, we implemented and developed strategies to efficiently simulate the electrochemical response of symmetric thin-film fuel cell electrodes of mixed conductors such as BLF and SNC. Firstly, we developed a novel numerical impedance model for mixed-conducting thin films working as electrodes for solid oxide fuel cells. The team also developed atomistic strategies to understand and upscale the nature of diffusion in perovskites. In the classical molecular dynamics data analysis, one typically calculates the mean squared displacements to obtain the self-diffusion coefficients. Moreover, the clustering analysis allows the tracking of individual oxygen jump along with its corresponding location. This information can, in turn, be used to study the factors influencing oxygen diffusion. Additionally, we can detect the total number of oxygen jumps from various locations and the corresponding activation enthalpies in the model material. This method is particularly suited for studying the impact of the local atomic arrangements on the ionic transport and for the design of materials with enhanced conductivity. Additionally, it will allow reducing the dimensionality of molecular simulations and to design high fidelity reduced-order models, such as kinetic Monte Carlo models, and therefore extend the simulation time and reduce the computational complexity. More details are given in a companion attachment (section 12).

639713.label: Major findings and research outcome
639713.value: Firstly, we have verified critical factors, including oxygen vacancies, crystal structures, electronic and ionic conductivities, etc., affecting the electrochemical performances of electrode materials for solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs). Through our theoretical calculations, we obtained mechanistic insight into the oxygen ion transport. Such transport is one decisive factor that determines the activity of SOFC electrodes. Also, we have developed models to simulate and fit the parameters that determine the oxygen transport kinetics, including the surface reaction rate k and the bulk diffusion coefficient D. All of such characteristics can be used to screen highly-efficient SOFC electrode material. Moreover, thanks to experiments and theoretical simulations, we found that the physicochemical properties and electrochemical performance of mixed ionic and electronic conductors can be facilely tuned by lightly doping either A-site or B-site of a perovskite oxide. For example in BaFeO3-δ, A-site doping usually leads to higher electrical conductivity while B-site doping results in faster oxygen diffusion kinetics. These findings provide a significant reference for the rational design of mixed ionic-electronic conductors used as cathode materials for SOFCs. Finally, based on our theoretical prediction and experimental verification, we found that SrNb0.1CoO3-δ (SNC) and Ba0.95La0.05FeO3-δ (BLF) are highly active cathode materials for solid oxide fuel cells.

639713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
639713.value: BaFeO3−δ (BFO) stands out as one of the most electrochemically active iron-based cathodes for SOFCs. However, pristine BFO has a mixture of phase structures. Doping is found to be an effective strategy to stabilize the highly-active oxygen vacancy-disordered lattice phase. Even though various dopants at either A-site or B-site have been reported to stabilize the cubic phase of BFO, advanced techniques are needed to characterize and clarify this information. In future work, we plan to apply synchrotron-based near-edge X-ray absorption fine structure (NEXAFS) or extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectrum, as well as neutron diffraction, to carefully analyze the chemical environment of ions present in perovskites oxides. This will be critical i) to understand the nature of the bonds that occur with these materials and ii) to further improve their catalytic activity.

639713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
639713.value: Through this project, we carefully investigated a series of promising mixed ionic and electronic conductive perovskites oxides for SOFCs, a highly efficient sustainable energy technology. By combining atomistic computations and experiments, we clarified the relationship among chemical composition, material structure, and performance. As a result, we developed new exciting materials starting from SrNb0.1CoO3-δ (SNC) and Ba0.95La0.05FeO3-δ (BLF). Our new compositions hold great promise as electrodes for SOFCs. In summary, our work will likely serve as a reference for the rational design of novel SOFC energy materials.

639913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
639913.value: According to the plan of the Ministry of Railways of the People's Republic of China, over 23,000 km of high-speed railway lines will be constructed and put into service by 2015. In late 2010, the maximum speed of 486 km/h was attained on the line between Beijing and Shanghai. Besides, Hong Kong is also in the process to construct new high-speed railway lines to cope with the future logistic demand within the pearl-river delta region. However, the ever increasing numbers of fatal high-speed railway accidents in mainland China and worldwide under serviceable wind conditions, has rung the alarm bells for engineers to consider the safety issue at an operation level. The new generation of structural designs also involves the efficient and comfortable use of the structure by the end user. When this ‘design for the user’ concept is applied to bridges and viaduct systems, investigation of high-speed trains (HST) travelling on bridges subjected to self-excitation and strong wind attacks not only allow designers to have more understanding about the actual performance of a bridge at the operation level, but the safety and comfort of the passengers can also be studied. However, reliability analysis on a vehicle-bridge-wind system is such a complex problem that it is usually considered infeasible in actual practice. The dynamic behaviour of the train-track-bridge system and the safety of vehicles are not only influenced by the structural properties of the bridge but it is also strongly affected by the dynamic characteristics of the track, namely the ballast and the rail, as well as the dynamic properties of the vehicle. This study intends to construct a general, yet efficient, vehicle stability analysis framework and make it capable of estimating the maximum allowable train velocity on bridge and viaduct systems subjected to different wind intensities. Non-linear properties such as the vehicle self-excitations, high speed step-in and step-out effects, geometrical non-linearity and wind induced buffeting and fluttering effects are studied and implemented into the analysis framework. In addition, the numerical simulation procedure will also be optimized using the partial iterative process (PIP) and the continuous simulation technique (CST), which can significantly reduce the time taken for performing the reliability analyses. With the help of the coupled simulation method, a parametric study will be performed to identify key design parameters, in term of the design of both the train and the bridge, to increase the efficiency and safety performance of viaduct systems. 根據中華人民共和國鐵道部門的計劃，超過二萬三千公里的高速鐵路線將於2015建成並且投入服務。在2010年底， 行走於北京和上海之間的路線錄得每小時 486公里的最高時速。同一時間，香港也正在落實構建新的高速鐵路線，以應付未來珠江三角洲一帶地區的物流需求。然而近年來，在一般風速及環境下所發生的高速鐵路致命事故不斷在中國大陸和世界各地發生，並且在數目上有增加的趨勢。這是對工程師在設計及操作層面上考慮安全問題的警號。新一代的結構設計理應從使用者的角度出發，以提供高效和舒適的使用體驗為目標。當這個“用者”的概念被應用到橋樑和高架橋系統的設計上，高速列車（ HST ）於不同風力下在橋樑上的表現的研究不僅讓設計工程師對整個高鐵系統在操作層面上有更進一步的了解，且而能夠逹到改善乘客的安全和舒適性的深層目標。然而，列車-橋-風系統的可靠性分析是一個複雜的問題，它在實際應用中一直被認為是不可行的。 列車，軌道和橋面的關聯動力反應以及列車的安全性不僅只受到橋的結構特性影響，軌道(包括鎮流器和導軌)的特性以及列車的動態屬性，對整個系統也有著舉足輕重的影響力。本研究旨在構造一個高自由度和高效率的列車穩定性分析框架，並使其能夠評估橋樑和高架橋系統在不同風速強度下的列車最高時速。主要的非線性的屬性，例如自我激勵，列車的進出影響，幾何非線性效果以及由風引致的空气动力颤动將一一被納入分析框架。此外，數模擬的程序會通過迭代過程（Partial Iterative Process）和連續模擬技術（ Continuous Simulation Technique）進行優化，令可靠性分析所需的時間得到顯著的改善。上述的耦合模擬法將會用作參數研究，以確立列車和橋樑設計對列車穩定性影響的關鍵參數，並提出設參建議以增加高架高速鐵路系統的效率和安全性。

640313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
640313.value: 本計劃旨在研究文人畫家所描繪的具有佛教意涵的實景山水圖，探討這些地點的佛教聯繫如何影響了山水圖像的表現﹑繪製與流傳。計劃研究的範圍主要為元末明初，研究的重點包括李子曉（14世紀前期）的《雁蕩山圖》﹑吳鎮（1280-1354）的《嘉禾八景》和王蒙（1308-1385）的《太白山圖》。這三件作品的作者與佛教僧侶皆有頻繁的交往，這三件手卷也都透過圖文的方式凸顯了佛寺在畫作中的重要性，暗示了它們在主題與圖像塑造上與流通於宗教領域的名山佛剎圖像傳統的密切關係。換言之，這一類的作品不僅見證﹑記錄了文人僧侶的親密互動，更反映了不同圖像傳統的融合，而佛寺不但是這些互動的重要場所，更是不同圖像傳統融合的焦點。 本計劃將透過重建這三件作品創作與流傳的背景，探討實景山水的表現--尤其畫中關於佛寺的描繪--可能具有的功能與意義。另一個探討的重點是這些作品與流通於宗教領域的名山佛寺圖像的關係，以及不同圖像傳統的跨域與融合。本計劃的研究成果不僅可以豐富我們對文人的精神生活與宗教僧侶的社會﹑文化活動的瞭解，也可以運用于我們對其他突出宗教建築的實景山水的評估與解讀，拓寬我們對於文人實景山水與宗教聖域圖像的表現意涵與形式的理解。

640313.label: Realisation of objectives
640313.value: For Objective 1, a detailed comparison of the three artists’ involvement with Buddhism was achieved through collection of data in primary sources as well as secondary researches. Among the three artists, Wu Zhen and Wang Meng clearly enjoyed an intimate relationship with people of Buddhist associations. Due to the relative obscurity of the Li Zixiao, however, his interaction with Buddhist clergy can only be conjectured through the colophons attached to the handscroll he created. For Objective 2, the intended function and implied meanings of the three handscrolls could be established through close reading of their iconographic details and pictorial structures, as well as the textual materials attached to or surrounding the creation of the scrolls. Picture of Mount Yandang and Picture of Mount Taibai are each a visual record of a journey through landscape that culminated at a prestigious Buddhist temple structures. Picture of Mount Yandang follows a sequential character highlighting monasteries and sites of Buddhist associations along the way, while Picture of Mount Taibai emphasises the site portrait of Tiantong Monastery as well as inserts meaningful details in the landscape to commemorate the achievements of the recipient as the former abbot of the Monastery. Wu Zhen’s Eight Views of Jiahe reinterpreted its model Eight Views of Xiaoxiang by depicting local sceneries and architectures of Jiahe. By opening and closing the eight views with temple compounds and giving prominence to monasteries in the landscape, Wu Zhen also frames the eight views as a Buddhist landscape as a fund-raising appeal for a local temple. For Objective 3, it has become clear that each scroll conflates the representation and function of different genres. Picture of Mount Yandang is a travel record as well as a journey of pilgrimage and Buddhist meditation. Picture of Mount Taibai is a site portrait and honorific painting presented in a form of travel painting. Eight Views of Jiahe depicts the eight views as eight sections of travels through local landscape with the purpose of inspiring local pride and Buddhist associations for fund raising. For Objective 4, although the three handscrolls share the same preference for a handscroll format and a thematic focus on topographic representation, it is also clear that each scroll is unique in the way it conflates pictorial representations of different genres for variations of intended functions. For Objective 5, in the process of researching on this project, it has come to the PI’s attention detailed studies on Li Zixiao’s Picture of Mount Yandang and Wang Meng's Picture of Mount Taibai. The PI has as a result adjusted the focus of her research to focus more on Wu Zhen's Eight Views of Jiahe and enlarge the scope of the investigation to include the Buddhist-literati interaction in Suzhou in the following Ming period. One essay entitled “Buddhist-Literati Interactions and Ming Suzhou Painting” was published in 2016. The study on Wu Zhen’s Eight Views of Jiahe is still ongoing as the reconstruction of the implied journey through consulting topographical mapping is complicated by the change of geographic names and disappearance of landmark structures over time.

640313.label: Major findings and research outcome
640313.value: 1. Unlike Li Zixiao or Wang Meng, who traveled to Mount Yandang or Mount Taibai as visitors, Wu Zhen started a pattern of literati interaction with local Buddhist monasteries that would be continued by Ming literati in such cities as Suzhou or Songjiang. The localization of literati patronage of Buddhist monasteries, as witnessed by poetry and paintings created by Suzhou literati and discussed by the PI’s published essay, also tied in with observations on late Ming literati/Buddhist interaction made by studies such as Timothy Brook's Praying for Power. 2. Wu Zhen’s Eight Views of Jiahe was the first known example of a painting created as part of a fund-raising project of a Buddhist monastery. Together with another late Ming landscape album studied by Elizabeth Kindall as well as other surviving records, the visual and textual evidences point to the existence of such artistic endeavours now lost. 3. Scholars such as Shi Shou-chien has pointed Wu Zhen's conflation of pictorial conventions of the pre-Yuan paintings of Eight Vews of Xiao and Xiang as well as those of the topographical maps in Eight views of Jiahe. The PI seeks to further uncover its underlying pictorial structure as an implied journey through reconstruction of topographical mappings.

640313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
640313.value: The findings from the three proposed case studies as well as the Ming Suzhou literati not only broaden our appreciation of the expressive parameters of literati landscape painting but also reveal the literati-Buddhist interaction as an important context for the creation and reception of paintings from the late Yuan to the middle Ming periods. The PI plans to continue investigation on this theme into the late Ming period and integrate the findings into a book-length project.

640313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
640313.value: This project examines three late Yuan and early Ming depictions of specific places where Buddhist associations not only played significant roles in the iconographies of place-making but also in the creation and reception of such images. Other than the three literati artists Li Zixiao, Wu Zhen and Wang Meng originally proposed as the focus of investigation, the scope of study has been expanded to include literati-Buddhist interactions in Suzhou during the early and middle Ming periods and representation of Buddhist monasteries resulted from such interactions. The findings suggest association of laymen and monks had not only been an important aspect of literati culture but also occasioned the creation of landscape paintings that appropriated and redefined literati conventions for conveying Buddhist associations. The examples from late Yuan to early Ming also witness a temporal development toward greater localization in the literati patronage of Buddhist monasteries.

640413.label: Project Title(Chinese)
640413.value: 中国四川西部的经济发展

640413.label: Project Objectives
640413.value: Document and evaluate processes and levels of economic development in West Sichuan Document government economic development policies in West Sichuan and evaluate their effectiveness Document and evaluate the economic and social consequences of economic development in West Sichuan

640413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
640413.value: Development economists in the 1940s and 1950s debated different approaches to economic development in a backward country, from big push to balanced and unbalanced growth. In the early reform years, China’s economic development has been more an issue of economic transition (from “socialism” to “capitalism”) than of typical economic development. Only in recent years, with the systemic transition having largely run its course, has the focus of economic policy shifted to standard economic development issues. This is nowhere more relevant than in China’s Western region. China’s Western region faces the typical economic development problem of how to raise the living standards of a predominantly traditional, agricultural society. In 2000, China started the Western development program to enable the Western region to catch up. This project inquires into the process of economic development in a highly underdeveloped region of China: What forms of development are there, and how does development come about? What is the role of government economic development policies, and how effective are they? What are the consequences of economic development, and how are they being received? I focus on the (municipal-level) Ganzi Tibetan Autonomous Region which covers most of West Sichuan, with details on three counties (Daocheng, Xiangcheng, Ganzi County). A number of theoretical concepts inform the inquiry. These include top-down vs. bottom-up development (are they congruent or are they contradictory, which central policies can be successfully implemented and which ones cannot, what local initiatives are there and how do they fit in with the central policies); coordination of state and private sector initiatives (is the state or the private sector driving development and with what kinds of projects or initiatives, to what extent does development of the private sector hinge on public sector economic initiatives); effects of economic development on economic and social outcomes, ranging from income (living standards) to education and labor market outcomes (is the agricultural surplus labor, if any, being absorbed in the non-agricultural sector); and people’s reception of development and its consequences. 发展经济学家在20世纪40和50年代辩论了包括“大推进，”“平衡”和“不平横”的经济增长战略。在中国经济改革中，经济转型的问题（从 “社会主义”到 “资本主义” ）比典型的经济发展的问题一直更重要。只是在经济转型的过程基本完成的最近几年，中国经济政策的重点逐步转移到典型的经济发展问题。 这种转移特别在中国西部地区能看到。目前中国西部地区经济发展面临的问题就是如何提高传统的农业社会人民的生活水平。 2000年中国西部大开政策正是为了使西部地区能赶上。 此研究项目探讨在中国欠发达地区的经济发展过程： 经济发展有什么形式，以及经济发展是如何起来？ 政府的经济发展政策的作用是什么，效果如何？ 经济发展的后果是什么，是如何被接收？ 此研究项目专门注意于覆盖大部分四川西部的（市级）甘孜藏族自治州地区， 而选择三个县：乡城，稻城，甘孜县。 项目的背后有几种经济发展理论，包括： 自上而下与自下而上的发展协调理论（是一致或有矛盾，哪些中央政策可以成功执行，有什么地方举办的措施而他们怎么配合中央政策）; 国家和私营部门的协调（是国家或私营部门推动发展，有怎么样的项目或措施，在何种程度上私营部门的发展依靠公共部门的支持） ; 经济发展对经济和社会结果，包括收入（生活水平） ，教育和劳动力市场的结果（农业剩余劳动力，如果有的话，在非农业部门中被吸收？）； 和人民对经济发展及其后果的接收。

640613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
640613.value: 民国大学生社会来源的研究是全面理解民国社会的核心问题，对中国近、现代史研究具有重要意义。在中西方交流增加及全球化浪潮地推动下，20世纪的中国 社会经历了从“传统”逐渐走向“近代”（或“现代”），从“帝国君臣”到“共和民主”的重大转变。学界过往对这种巨大转变的研究，更多集中于关注新的政治制度、思想潮流和科技设施等的出现以及由此所带来的重要影响，而对其中最为关键的“新式”人群的出现却关注不够。比如获得新式教育，尤其是高等教育的人群在中国近代社会的规模性产生，与当时的社会职业组成、城市社会阶层构建乃至 整个中国近代化建设进程都密切相关。但目前学术界对这一人群的关注明显不足，尤其是缺乏可靠的数据资料来支撑各类观点。正是考虑到这一研究领域的不足，并结合李中清研究组二十多年来从事数据库建设和研究的经验，我们决定对国内各地档案馆所藏民国大学生学籍等相关资料进行数码化工作并进行研究分析，以期尽快弥补这一研究空白。

640613.label: Realisation of objectives
640613.value: 1. We have constructed a database called the China University Student Dataset – Republic of China (CUSD-ROC) with 113119 individual student records from 21 Republican Era universities and independent colleges based on archival records preserved at 8 provincial and 3 university archives. We are still expanding the database covering 27 Republican universities and colleges which represents over two-thirds of the surviving student records we have located in Chinese university and administrative archives. 2. Based on the above data, we have examined the trends and patterns of social and geographical origins of these students based on their parental occupation, feeder schools, family addresses, and place of origin. 3. We have made more than 20 academic presentations based on the above analyses. 4. We have also published 4 papers in major Chinese-language academic journals (历史研究, 社会学研究, 清华大学学报) three of which are already out (2014, 2015, 2017) and one will be out later this year (2017), and have just completed 1 paper in English which we will submit to a major international journal. We have also completed an initial draft of an on-line user guide to the CUSD-ROC, and have begun preparations to write a book manuscript on Republican tertiary education tentatively titled《民国大学生社会来源》, which we hope to submit to a Chinese language press by year end or in 2018 year beginning. I attach a table of content: Chapter 1 导论：民国大学的分布与招生方式变迁等 Chapter 2 民国大学生的家庭背景（兼及保证人分析） Chapter 3 民国大学生的性别结构 （学校、地区及专业的比较分析） Chapter 4 民国大学生的地理分布（籍贯、永久居住地等） Chapter 5 民国大学生入学前教育状况（中学类型比例、转学比例及规律分析） Chapter 6 民国大学生的专业选择（院系信息统计、志愿书信息收集分析、课程设计、毕业去向等） Chapter 7 总结：民国大学生群体的结构特征与阶层交流

640613.label: Major findings and research outcome
640613.value: For a summary of our research output from the project as well as the China University Student Dataset-Republic of China, please see Part One of our on-line course “Understanding China, 1700-2000: A Data Analytic Approach – Who Gets Education” ( https://www.coursera.org/learn/understanding-china-history-part-1​ ). We are reshooting and reorganizing the course content in summer 2017. This part will be moved to part 2 with more findings and new discoveries. 1. Based on the analysis from China University Student Dataset-Republic of China (CUSD-ROC), around 40 percent of undergraduate students in Republican China were the children of businessmen, 24 percent were the children of professionals, and 11 percent were children of civil servants. 2. Based on the analysis from China University Student Dataset-Republic of China (CUSD-ROC), according to students’ reported home address, the geographic distribution of educated elite in Republican China was quite regional and local. Except for Tsinghua University, most universities, even other national universities, mainly attracted students regionally.

640613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
640613.value: To gain a better understanding of the educated elites in the Republican Era, and of the social changes in modern China from Imperial to Republican times, we will expand our study of university student social origins to include the world of employment and work after student graduation. To better understand the second Great Transformation (from industrial to knowledge economy) as well as China over the long term, we will also extend this study to contemporary China.

640613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
640613.value: This project, by creating the CUSD-ROC, provides reliable, important and new quantitative evidence on social inequality in access to higher education in early 20th century China. This study fills a significant gap in our knowledge of China’s higher education in modern times. Understanding the social origins of the educated elites in Republican China is one way to understand changes in Chinese history, not just in terms of the academe, but also the overall socio-economic development of twentieth-century China. The China University Student Dataset-Republic of China (CUSD-ROC) is of great value to show various university student characteristics and also has potential to link other data on post-graduate careers and families.

640613.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
640613.value: Part of the project research output will be used or developed for the book in English version on Higher Education in Republic of China and online course “Understanding China, 1700-2000: A Data Analytic Approach – Who Gets Education.” The China University Student Dataset (CUSD) is being set up and will be further developed for other research projects. It analyzes the social and geographic familial background of university students in Republican China (ROC) and elite university students in the People’s Republic of China (PRC) including Hong Kong and Taiwan based on a collection of over 300,000 individual university student registration cards from over 30 universities. The dataset will be released to the public gradually, and will be useful for other research projects on the Republic of China.

641013.label: Project Title(Chinese)
641013.value: 英殖年代的電影審查與冷戰中的香港電影文化政治

641013.label: Project Objectives
641013.value: Delineating the impact of British colonial film policy on Hong Kong cinema Reconstructing the historical transnational relationship of Hong Kong cinema to Britain, China, Taiwan, and Southeast Asia Examining how the global politics of Cold War affected the aesthetics and identity of Hong Kong cinema
rows: Delineating the impact of British colonial film policy on Hong Kong cinema
Reconstructing the historical transnational relationship of Hong Kong cinema to Britain, China, Taiwan, and Southeast Asia
Examining how the global politics of Cold War affected the aesthetics and identity of Hong Kong cinema

641013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
641013.value: 本研究項目針對在冷戰時期（1950s-1970s）港英政府秘而不宣的電影審查制度和殖民地文化政策對香港電影的影響，從香港及東南亞地區的地緣政治角度，探討冷戰期間的殖民地的電影審查措施如何影響香港電影的文化傳播，以致在東南亞網絡中的生產，流通，和接收。研究希望從檔案館的資料入手，探討香港電影審查制度的性質和文化政治。其次，冷戰中的文化政治如何塑造香港電影的本質，及其與在中國大陸、台灣及東南亞的電影的跨境交流？政治和市場的潛在因素如何影響電影製作的美學和電影文化人的身份認同？ 研究者希望基於港英時代的檔案資料和記錄，配合大眾媒體報導，電影公司材料，影人回憶錄，及流行期刊和報紙資料等，重新揭示政府的潛在政策，和整理殖民地香港電影的發展脈落。此外，研究從歷史和美學幾方面探討中國和香港電影的文化政治，包括意識形態和商業化發展，片廠和明星制度，電影類型和美學，方言和觀眾的電影政治。研究的目標是將香港電影的發展作為全球性華語電影中的重要一環，尤其重視它在東南亞的華語電影網絡中發揮的歷史作用，結合文化歷史研究與文本閱讀互為參透，重新瞭解香港電影如何在殖民主義，後殖民主義，中國的民族主義的冷戰氛圍中表現出華語電影中獨特的可能性，可觀性，和歷史性。

641013.label: Realisation of objectives
641013.value: (1) Delineating the impact of British colonial film policy on Hong Kong cinema The project investigators employed part-time research assistants to conduct archival work in various university libraries and Hong Kong Public Records Office. The tasks entailed looking into the film columns of several Chinese newspapers in the 1950s and 1960s, and colonial government records of certain film censorship cases. We have successfully traced historical incidents of film censorship as battles of opinions on cinematic representations and ideological combats in Cold War Hong Kong. (2) Reconstructing the historical transnational relationship of Hong Kong cinema to Britain, China, Taiwan, and Southeast Asia The project investigators made several research trips to the National Archive in London to uncover files of British colonial cultural policies on Hong Kong and Southeast Asia (Singapore) as well as British diplomatic considerations of its relationships to Taiwan and China. They also went to Singapore to visit the National Archives to reveal further details in Southeast Asia, which were helpful for comparatively understanding the Hong Kong situation. We also regularly made visits to the Hong Kong Film Archive to study individual film materials. (3) Examining how the global politics of Cold War affected the aesthetics and identity of Hong Kong cinema.... The project investigators delivered a number of conference papers and achieved published works as a result of the research findings in this project. These papers cover key issues in Cold War cultural politics and Hong Kong cinema, including the institution and cinematic representation of Hong Kong leftwing cinema, radical adaptations of Chinese literature and folksy ghost narratives, reconstruction of the missing role of Hong Kong in Chinese animated films, and transnational Hollywood spy pictures in relation to Hong Kong as the combat grounds of production and exhibition.

641013.label: Major findings and research outcome
641013.value: The project investigators have mined important archival data and historical materials in popular print media. Combining the historical research with reading of film texts and cultural histories, we achieved several published works and conducted research on some others, thus fulfilling our objective of exploring how the global politics of cultural Cold War contributed to the identity and performance of Hong Kong cinema and Chinese-language cinemas at large. The PI has published one article in an English-refereed journal. The title of the article is “Suspended Animation: The Wan Brothers and the (In)animate Mainland-Hong Kong Encounter, 1947-1956,” published in Journal of Chinese Cinemas in 2017. It is about the role of Hong Kong in history of Chinese animation and the role of China in history of Hong Kong animation in the late 1940s and early 1950s. Situated in the Cold War context, it unravels the role of different political actors that shaped the complicated cinematic scene in Hong Kong at the time: the British government, the émigré leftists, and the influence of the socialist government from the mainland. An earlier version of this article was presented at the annual conference of the Society for Cinema and Media Studies in Montreal in March 2015. This conference paper was mainly based on the PI’s preliminary research conducted at the Hong Kong Film Archive in August 2014. The Co-I has published two English book chapters, thanks to the archival research to reveal the history of Cantonese leftwing cinema and larger colonial governmental surveillance of local cinemas. They are “The Resurrection of Female Ghosts from Classical Chinese Opera and the Hollywood Tradition in Cantonese Cinema,” and “Censorship at Work: Cold War Paranoia and Purgation of Chinese Ghost Stories,” and a Chinese journal article, “The Left-Wing Utopia of Hong Kong Cantonese Opera Films after WWII: Case Studies of Adapted Films by Union Motion Picture Enterprise.” (See Part C). The Co-I has also delivered conference papers, which were outcomes of the research in foreign archives. The revelation of US intervention in Asian Cold War politics with Hong Kong as a vital production and distribution center has been one of the major achievements in the project. It has led the Co-I to present in papers on US and Hollywood ventures (“When Gregory Peck Met Chairman Mao: Colonial Censorship and Cultural Politics in Cold War Hong Kong”), on American cultural discourse of “brainwashing” to refer to PRC political indoctrination (“‘Brainwashing’: Cultural Smuggling of a Cold War Lexicon in Asia (via Hong Kong)”), and American-sponsored Asia Pictures and Asia Press (“Cold War Cosmopolitanism: Chang Kuo-sin and His Fiction Enterprises”). The PI and Co-I have published and presented individual works separately because single-authored works are prized more highly than co-authored works in the humanities. Their works were the outcome of the collaborative project.

641013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
641013.value: The research in foreign and local archives combined with newspaper resources will encourage the Co-I to propose a monograph on film censorship and transnational Chinese cinema. The purpose of the book is to examine how global Cold War politics and cultural policies have affected the aesthetics and identity of Hong Kong and Chinese cinema (Objective 3). The Co-I is presently planning to write and submit a book proposal to potential international publishers. As mentioned, the revelation of US intervention in Asian Cold War politics with Hong Kong as a vital production and distribution center has been one of the major findings in the project. The Co-I has furthered develop this thesis to submit to a new GRF grant application for 2018–2019.

641013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
641013.value: Examining the cinematic politics of Hong Kong and Chinese-language cinemas in 1950–1970, the project reveals a turbulent Cold War era in which the governments and various political parties and forces attempted to make use of the immense power of cinema to shape the values and minds of the people. Focusing on Hong Kong and its networks with Southeast Asia, and studying how the Asian regions were invariably affected by US and UK foreign policies and yet maintained their cultural identity and integrity, our work has shed light on the historical role and function of colonial Hong Kong as the center of Chinese-language cinemas and literature. The project will not only renew our understanding of Chinese-language film histories by supplementing the missing chapter of Cold War Hong Kong, but it will also throw light on the inevitable and yet troubled relationships between Hong Kong and China. A lasting acknowledgment is the intrinsic worth of cinema and creative, performing art. The investigators have affirmatively explored the aesthetics and cultural innovations of the films produced under contending ideologies and political surveillance, and the constant pressures of market restrictions and individual traumas in a time of political turmoil.

641113.label: Project Title(Chinese)
641113.value: 本地化与全球化: 从比较的视野看中国企业在非洲

641113.label: Project Objectives
641113.value: Develop the first large-scale and theoretically-grounded approach to understanding why and how the problem of localization of Chinese enterprises abroad has been posed and plumb key issues raised in connection with the problem. Create systematic comparisons between the localization of Chinese firms abroad, especially in Africa, and the localization of comparable non-Chinese foreign enterprises in the same industries and localities, while also explaining variations in the localization of Chinese firms abroad themselves. Ascertain the expectations and consequences of localization of Chinese-owned firms abroad for both Chinese interests and the countries that host Chinese investors. Produce a monograph and three articles, on localization of employment, on cultural adaption by Chinese working abroad, and on localization policies for Chinese and host country government and peoples. They will place localization of Chinese firms in Africa alongside that of other foreign-owned firms and compare localization of Chinese enterprises in Africa with localization of such companies elsewhere.

641113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
641113.value: Localization of investment is a range of actions foreign investors take to more closely connect with host country institutions and people. Chinese firms abroad are said to be deficient in localization, because of the recentness of their surge into the world, but also due to political and cultural factors particular to China. The problem is prominent in global discussions of China’s rise, such as the China-in-Africa discourse. Yet, it does resonate with many people in developing countries and nowhere more so than in Africa, where economic opportunity is constricted and a post-colonial indigenist outlook present among elites, despite their imbrication with globalization and neo-liberalism. The proposed study will analyze the politics and culture of localization of Chinese firms abroad, hypothesizing that it a response to indigenist imperatives of host country elites and other factors. In most places, the sine qua non of localization concerns employment. Chinese firms are said to prefer to “bring their own people,” out of convenience, ethnic nepotism, or to advance a purported state policy of reducing unemployment in China through emigration. The proposed study will take up why and by whom the problem of localization is raised. It will compare why, how and to what degree Chinese firms and other foreign investors -- in select countries and in oil, mining, manufacturing, construction, agriculture, commerce and telecommunications -- have localized, including in terms of cultural adaption. Localization of Chinese firms in Africa will also be compared to what Chinese firms do elsewhere. The study will assess the requisites and consequences of localization for Chinese firms abroad, for the Chinese government, and for host states and peoples. Scattered news reports about localization exist and we have collected many. We have also briefly touched on localization in field interviews that have been devoted to a wide range of China/Africa topics and conducted in ten African countries and China. The most useful data on localization can only be secured however through surveys and interviews directly focused on the topic. We propose to do so in four African states and, for comparative purposes, in one developing Asian country and one developed country elsewhere. The result will be a monograph-length study and several articles that not only analyze the problem of localization, but also propose solutions, derived from the experience of Chinese and other firms, to the problem of deficient localization. 外来投资需采取一系列的措施才能与被投资国家的机构和民众发生比较紧密的联系。据一些媒体和研究报道，中国公司的海外投资在本地化方面比较欠缺，这些报道给出的原因既包括中国公司走出去的时间不长，也包括中国特有的政治、文化因素。中国公司的本地化已经成为国际上讨论中国崛起时一个显要的话题。这一问题在发展中国家的确得到不少人的呼应，尤其在全球化和新自由主义覆盖的非洲，正式就业机会相对短缺，当地精英中存在着本土意识。 本课题打算客观地分析中国公司在海外的本地化过程。在很多地方，外资公司的本地化几乎等同于雇佣本地员工。然而，本地化还包括一些其他丰富的内容，包括中国公司的海外雇员对海外社会文化的适应、技术技能的本地化等。据称，中国公司为了方便，也因为想照顾自己人，或因为国家政策导向，偏向于“带自己的人。”针对这样的看法，本课题将具体分析“本地化”是不是一个问题，何时成为一个问题，对谁是个问题，在不同的地方都有什么具体的内涵。我们将选择一些具体的国家和行业，比较中国公司与其他外国投资者为什么本地化，如何本地化，本地化的程度如何。我们也会把中国公司在非洲的本地化与其它地区的中国公司本地化相比较。在具体研究的基础上，本研究将分析中国公司的本地化需要哪些条件，可能产生哪些影响。

641113.label: Realisation of objectives
641113.value: 1. The first objective has been realized principally by engaging theoretical literature on workforce localization but, to a lesser extent literature, on other forms of localization, such as investor involvement in joint ventures and sub-contracting. Theories related to workforce localization are overwhelmingly found in the literature of management disciplines. They have emerged mainly from case studies of Western firms invested in labor-short, skills-deficit Gulf and Arabian Peninsula countries, and secondarily on case studies of Western firms in labor-abundant, skills-abundant China. Using our findings derived from documentary research and extensive interviews in African countries, we determined that localization patterns among Chinese enterprises in Africa diverge from those found in other case studies and have adumbrated reasons for this divergence. First, most Chinese companies in Africa have had a presence for less than a decade and at most two decades, while Western firms in the Middle East and China have generally been there for not less than two decades and many for generations. Second, conditions for Chinese firm workforce localization, joint venture formation and sub-contracting in Africa are significantly different than for Western firms in the Middle East or China, in that Africa is a mainly labor-abundant, but skills-deficit continent. That requires Chinese companies to compete with more established firms offering higher remuneration and significant cultural overlaps with Africans and competing with other Chinese companies as well. Third, relevant Chinese cultural and political norms are distinct from Western norms. For example, Chinese firms place a higher value on speedy and inexpensive production in construction, manufacturing, services, etc., than Western investors. They are unlikely to have their national standards already in place or insist on their standards being adopted in the host country. Chinese companies are less reliant on influence exerted by their home country governments in instances of conflict with host country governments and less insulated from criticisms involving host country domestic politics and third party antagonisms to a Chinese presence. Our contribution to theories of localization have thus been based on this previously unexplored distinctive set of characteristics. 2. The second objective has been only partially realized, as we have found an abundance of data on Chinese workforce and other localizations in Africa, but a paucity of data on such localizations among firms from other countries. Chinese firms are under political attack in Western media and seek to have close relations with host country governments. They thus regularly publicize their localization successes, especially with regard to workforce localization and training of local employees. We have generally confirmed these claimed achievements, by resort to data provided by African governments. Despite scarcity of data provided by non-Chinese companies, we have nevertheless been able to determine, largely through interviews with local officials and business people, that in certain industries, such as mining and construction, Chinese enterprises’ high degree of localization closely corresponds to that of other foreign enterprises, including not only Western, but also developing country investors (India, Turkey, Brazil, etc.). In some other industries, such as ICT (information and computer technology), Chinese enterprises are somewhat less localized in terms of employment, mainly because locals with the necessary skills have a greater awareness of and cultural affinity for Western firms. 3. The third objective has been overwhelmingly fulfilled. Our interviews, as well views expressed in the quite accessible Chinese and African media, have allowed us to fully gauge the expectations and consequences of localization for Chinese interests and those of host African countries. Interview subjects are very willing to speak about all aspects of localization and there is large body of commentary about such subjects in African and Chinese media, scholarly studies, reports of government, companies, NGOs, etc. There is in fact a wide range of opinion and considerable debate about the degree to which Chinese firms have localized and have the potential to do so. Our writings on Chinese localization in Africa are in large measure based on such commentaries and debates. We have determined that generally there has been increasing satisfaction among Chinese companies and host country societies with localization by Chinese firms, but also continuing criticism and self-criticism about remaining deficiencies. In general, there has been a strong upward curve in awareness of the need for strengthened localization and a response to it by Chinese companies at home and in the field. 4. The fourth objective has in large measure been fulfilled, in that we have produced several articles that in whole or in part are about the localization of Chinese enterprises and Chinese populations in Africa, especially in our main fieldsite country, Zambia. Besides the published articles we have a very rough manuscript draft of a more than 300,000 words that deals with all aspects of Chinese workforce and other localizations, not only in Africa, but also in comparative perspective, looking particularly at Chinese firms outside Africa, in Central, South and Southeast Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean, the United States and Europe, etc. In that way we can draw comparisons not only between Chinese and non-Chinese degrees and kinds of localization, but also comparisons among Chinese firms that have gone out to different regions abroad. What remains is to transform that very long, still rough manuscript into a shorter and more refined work that will be submitted for publication as a book.

641113.label: Major findings and research outcome
641113.value: One major finding is that, contrary to discourses of Western politicians and media and some counterparts in Africa, localization of Chinese enterprises in the continent has developed significantly, compared to earlier in the 21st Century. Localization is now advanced in most sectors of investment and infrastructure building, although ICT remains a challenge, due to local skill and experience deficits. The change has largely resulted from Chinese firms’ compliance with African state policies, laws and regulations requiring greater degrees of localization, especially of workforces. Part of the change however is due to growing reputations of Chinese firms in a continent long- dominated by ex-colonial and North American investors. Still another factor is the proliferation of Chinese firm training programs for local employees and a greater embeddedness of such firms in local society, thus increasing the likelihood of finding local business partners, sub-contractors and suppliers. A second major finding is the erosion of differences in localization between Chinese and other foreign firms in Africa, despite the linguistic and cultural overlap advantages of the latter. Although Chinese firm data is more abundant than data for non-Chinese investors in the continent, where data is comparable, Chinese and other foreign firms are roughly similar in terms of localization, especially in labor-intensive industries. The degree of Chinese enterprises’ localization in Africa is moreover intermediate between regions of lower levels of Chinese firm localization (Central Asia, Pacific and Caribbean island states) and very high levels of such localization (North America, Western Europe, Australasia). The differences are overwhelmingly related to variations in the abundance of local skills and experience. A third major finding is directly about the global discourse of Chinese firms in Africa not localizing. It focuses particularly on “Chinese companies bringing their own workforces” and has proved to be empirically erroneous. Our database of over 900 Chinese companies and projects in Africa shows that the mean percentage of workforce localization, derived from data involving over 40 African countries, is in the mid-to-high 80s. Our study’s result, derived independently from thousands of documentary and interview sources, was confirmed in 2017 by another study, of 1,000 Chinese firms in eight African states. The US consultancy McKinsey and Co. found workforce localization averaged 89%. Such results negate the common misapprehension of workforce non-localization among Chinese firms in Africa. The research outcome is reflected in existing and forthcoming publications, as well as the presentations made of our findings.

641113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
641113.value: The potential for further research development is not mainly about gathering more data. Existing data will be updated and additions made from what emerges in our new RGC-funded project, on Chinese agribusiness in Africa, but we need to use our existing super-abundance of localization data to produce several publications. First and foremost, we should produce papers that can be turned into journal articles. One article will summarize the findings from our construction of a database on workforce localization of Chinese enterprises in Africa. Another will compare Chinese localization apart from workforce composition; it should deal with training of locals workers, the forging of joint ventures, sub-contracting, use of locally-derived inputs to production, adaption of Chinese enterprise outputs to local conditions, and Chinese residents integration into local society and culture. Both the workforce localization and non-workforce localization papers should compare Chinese endeavors in Africa with those of other foreign investors. A third paper will compare Chinese localization-related activities in Africa with those of Chinese firms elsewhere. In all papers, the localizing role of the Chinese government and host governments will be underscored. The papers will be the key to reducing and refining our huge rough draft manuscript and producing a book.

641113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
641113.value: Our study of Chinese enterprise localization in Africa directly impacts a global discourse that asserts that these endeavors do not benefit Africa because Chinese companies choose to not localize in the continent. We have found the opposite: Chinese firms, though overwhelmingly present in the continent only in the 21st Century, have consistently sought to localize their workforces, joint ventures, sub-contracting, and production inputs and outputs, while still maintaining corporate cultures that emphasize low-cost production and rapid completion of tasks. Chinese enterprises have rapidly caught up in localization with those of other foreign investors, particularly in terms of workforce composition. They have done so despite the latter having a much longer presence and languages and cultures more similar to those of Africans. It has not proved as easy for Chinese enterprises to localize in Africa as in developed regions, but Chinese enterprises’ localization is more advanced in the continent than it is in several other regions where even more acute skills and experience deficits abound. Chinese enterprises in Africa are still far from being “Africanized” in terms of adaption to the disparate political systems and cultures of the continent, but they are much better adapted than commonly thought and increasingly so.

To detail the irregular development of qīngrù syllables in standard Mandarin (as spoken in Beijing) and in other Mandarin dialects. To make contributions to the study of language/dialect contact, shedding light on issues such as the actual processes of tonal influence between dialects, and types of words with different susceptibility to tonal change. To provide evidence for determining if Zhōngyuán Yīnyùn was based on the dialect of the then capital Dadu.

641413.label: Realisation of objectives
641413.value: The PI has achieved all the objectives (except for one) as listed in the project proposal. Detailing the findings, the PI’s comprehensive paper of 20-odd pages, to appear in _Zhongguo Yuwen_ in 2018, has dealt with all the five objectives except for No. (2), which is to build a database of fieldwork data. Even though all the fieldwork has been performed according to the research plan, it has been difficult to find a suitable computer programmer to work on the database. That is also part of the reason why the PI had not spent all the research funding. As the Director of the Center for Chinese Linguistics in the Division of Humanities, HKUST, the PI and his colleagues have already made plans to add to the two databases available at the Center’s website, namely “Early Cantonese Colloquial Texts: A Database” and “Early Cantonese Tagged Database”, which are outputs from two RGC-funded projects and have been rendered accessible to the public. 641413.label: Major findings and research outcome
641413.value: The chaotic derivation of the ancient qīngrù syllables/characters (i.e. rùshēng syllables/characters with voiceless obstruent initials) in the Beijing dialect was due to their second distribution. Based on the evidence found in _Zhongyuan Yinyun_ and modern dialects, it can be inferred that the qīngrù tone was slower in diachronic change and became an independent category for some time, and there was a tendency for it to merge with the rising tone (shǎngshēng). In subsequent development, owing to the radical change in the political situation and deepening of dialectal contact, the tone category of qīngrù disintegrated, with its syllables eventually adopting the yīnpíng, yángpíng, shǎng or qù tones. There are three major findings in the present study. (1) The principle of tonal polarity commonly runs through Chinese dialects. That is to say, in a disyllabic domain of tone sandhi, the two syllables involved tend to become tonally opposite in terms of pitch (high/low), contour (rising/falling) or duration (short/long). This tendency of tonal polarity would tentatively change the pitch contour (or tonal value) of a certain syllable, and subsequently the new tonal value got finalized as the prevailing form of the syllable in question. (2) It happened that a qīngrù syllable plus a neutral tone syllable, such as le (verbal suffix; sentence-final particle), guo (verbal suffix), zi (nominal suffix) and ma (interrogative particle), constituted a trochee, i.e. a long (or full) tone followed by a short (or neutral) tone. In light of duration in such a domain of tonal polarity, the preceding qīngrù syllable tends to pick up a long and level pitch (actually yīnpíng) under the retrogressive pressure of the following short neutral tone. This is the reason why some qīngrù syllables were fated to become the ones with the yīnpíng tone. (3) In the pattern of tonal polarity by pitch contrast, found in the quasi-iambic prosodic foot, the preceding qīngrù syllable tends to adopt a rising contour (actually yángpíng) under the retrogressive pressure of the following falling tone. This is the reason why some qīngrù syllables/characters were fated to become the ones with the yángpíng tone. (Other yángpíng syllables originated from qīngrù syllables are due to a process called “merged into yángpíng tone on the basis of identical initial and final”.)

641413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
641413.value: The PI has propounded the principle of tonal polarity in tone sandhi, a generalization applying to and even providing a motivation for many actual cases in different Chinese dialects. Specifically, the principle has been demonstrated in the present research project to include: (a) a trochee with a contrast in duration, i.e. a long (or full) tone followed by a short (or neutral) tone, and (b) a quasi-iambus with a contrast in pitch, such as a pattern of rising contour followed by falling. Further research has been planned by the PI to serve two aims: first to prove or disprove the application of the principle in various regions of Chinese dialects, and second to specify the conditions for a sandhi form to displace the original tone (and tone category) of a syllable/character.

641413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
641413.value: In the history of tones in Chinese dialects, a puzzle centers on syllables (or characters) of the rùshēng (entering tone) category, which originally ended in -p, -t or -k. In Early Mandarin (of the 14th century), having lost their endings, the entering-tone syllables started to adopt other tone categories in northern Chinese dialects (including Pekingese). However, no systematic conditioning can be found for the adopted categories of the rùshēng syllables beginning with a voiceless obstruent (like p-), called qīngrù (voiceless entering) in Chinese. An analysis of fieldwork data has yielded three major findings. (1) “The principle of tonal polarity” has been suggested: in a disyllabic domain of tone sandhi, the two syllables involved tend to become tonally opposite in terms of pitch (high/low), contour (rising/falling) or duration (long/short), accounting for the tone change of syllables including those of qīngrù. (2) Followed by a neutral tone, such as le or guo (verbal suffixes), a qīngrù syllable would take up a long and level pitch (the yīnpíng category), thereby producing a trochee pattern of long plus short. (3) Followed by a falling tone, the qīngrù syllable would adopt a rising contour (the yángpíng category), thereby producing a quasi-iambic pattern of high plus low.
