662713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
662713.value: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) involves the use of natural therapeutic agents under the guidance of Chinese medicinal science. TCM should be prepared as decoctions using a unique methodology according to formulae (named as Fu Fang 複方) specifying various combinations of different herbs. Within the complex chemical composition, the exact efficacy of each compound and its action mechanisms; however, has not been determined. In the last 15 years, we have been developing a strategy to reveal the molecular mechanism of Danggui Buxue Tang (DBT; 當歸補血湯) in treating women’s diseases. In DBT, Astragali Radix (Huangqi; 黃芪) is considered as Jun, while Angelicae Sinensis Radix (Danggui; 當歸) is Chen. Our studies at HKUST indicate Astragali Radix-derived calycosin, formononetin and astragaloside IV are the major chemicals playing important roles in DBT functions. In order to reveal the role of these components in DBT, we propose to knock-out few chemicals specifically from DBT decoction. Here, we aim to use chemical-specific antibodies in generating calycosin-depleted, formononetin-depleted, or astragaloside IV-depleted DBT. The functional differences of DBT, as compared to calycosin-, formononetin- and astragaloside IV-depleted DBT, in various cell culture models will be revealed by systems biology techniques, e.g. genomics, proteomics and metabolomics. The identification of the chemical-specific regulated protein(s), or gene(s), could give a better understanding of the material basis of TCM preparation as well as reveal the mechanistic actions of DBT decoctions. 中藥復方是按照中醫理論指導之下，按照君臣佐使，以不同的中藥組合而成。不同的中藥有不同的化學成分，有不同的生物活性。當歸補血湯由當歸：黃芪按照1:5比例組成，黃芪為君藥，當歸為臣藥，常用于治療婦科疾病。本研究小組已研究該復方歷時15年，研究結果表明：當歸補血湯中黃芪主要化學成分黃芪甲苷、毛蕊異黃酮和芒丙花素對其生物活性起主要作用。為了揭示這些化學成分在當歸補血湯的作用機理，本研究計劃逐一敲出這些成分之后，用不同的細胞模型，采用基因組學、蛋白組學和代謝組學研究當歸補血湯的生物活性是否改變，如何改變？通過這些研究其專屬的調節蛋白和基因，我們可以更好的理解當歸補血湯的作用機理。

662713.label: Realisation of objectives
662713.value: Objective #1 The commercial available antibodies, i.e. ferulic acid, were purchased from PLANTPROBES. We have utilized anti-ferulic acid antibody to specific knock-out ferulic acid from authentic DBT. Protein G was employed to pull down the targeted chemical from DBT decoction by centrifugation. Repeating the above procedure several times, the processed DBT decoction was injected into HPLC to calculate the depletion rate of ferulic acid. From the results, we found this antibody not only interacted within targeted chemical, but also pull-down un-targeted chemicals, which were verified by LC-MS/MS. The chemical profiles suggested that there was more than one chemical found within the pull-down fraction. Anti-calycosin antibody was obtained from Chemical and Scientific cooperation (Burlingame, CA); however, similar problems were revealed as that of anti-ferulic acid antibody. All these data suggested that the antibody pull-down method was not specific to the targeted chemicals. Objective #2. Chemical standardization is the critical step in ensuring the biological repeatability and reproductivity. It is crucial to collect the qualified raw material for preparing qualified DBT decoction. Indeed, the chemical compositions of Astragali Radix (AR, Huangqi) and Angelica Sinesis Radix (ASR, Danggui) are majorly influenced by the cultivated conditions. By comparing the bioactive constituents, i.e. total flavonoids, astragalosides, polysaccharides, amino acids and trace elements of different sources of AR, the 3-year-old AR from Shanxi province contained relative higher amounts of bioactive constituents as well as better biological functions as compared to the others. On the other hand, the chemical profiles of 2-year-old ASR gathered from Gansu possessed higher level of positive regulator, ferulic acid and lower content of negative regulator, Z-ligustilide. The extraction method was also optimized. Moderate heating is an essential factor to generate the best herbal decoction. Taking DBT decoction every 5 min during the boiling procedure from room temperature to boiling under gentle heating of ~2 hours, the composition of decoction was revealed by LC-MS/MS and HPLC, chemically. The major bioactive chemicals, i.e. astragaloside IV, calycosin, formononetin, calycosin-7-O-β-D-glucoside and ononin, were increased both in time- and temperature-dependent manners: the amounts of these chemicals were saturated after 2 hours. We have successfully prepared DBT decoction, the chemical profiles of DBT were detected both on HPLC and LC-MS/MS. The generations of DBTΔcal (calycosin knock-out DBT) and DBTΔfa (ferulic acid knock-out DBT) were performed on semi-preparative HPLC. Firstly, the HLPC condition was optimized to ensure no other chemicals overlap with calycosin or ferulic acid, and then semi-preparative column was applied here to create DBT∆cal or DBT∆fa. The fingerprint chromatograms of specific chemical knock-out DBT decoction were developed. The mobile phase consisted of acetonitrile (as Solvent A) and 0.1 % formic acid (as Solvent B). A series of gradient elution was utilized for creating DBT∆cal and DBT∆fa: 0 - 10 min, 15 % of solvent A; 10 - 45 min, 15 - 50 % solvent A; 45 - 50 min, 50 % of solvent A; 50 – 70 min, 50 % to 80 % solvent A. Revealing by HPLC-DAD and HPLC-ELSD detectors, the marker chemicals were further quantified. The combinations of fingerprint chromatograms and quantifications of marker chemicals ensured the quality of DBT∆cal and DBT∆fa extracts. The LC-MS/MS and 1H-NMR results of the collected fraction showed the existence of calycosin or feulic acid only. In summary, the extract of DBTΔcal or DBT∆fa contained same chemicals as in parental DBT, except the targeted knock-out chemicals. Objective #3 The estrogenic effect of DBTΔcal and DBT∆fa: The pERE-Luc stably transfected MCF-7 was employed to investigate the estrogenic activity of DBTΔcal and DBT∆fa as compared to parental DBT. From the results, the authentic DBT and DBT∆fa showed a dose-dependent in activating pERE-Luc activity, the activations of these two DBT decoctions were much stronger than that of DBTΔcal. Furthermore, different amounts of calycosin were added back to DBTΔcal decoction, and the activity in pERE-Luc was recovered. The effective dose of calycosin however required a much higher concentration as to achieve the same activation as that of DBT. Besides, we also revealed the estrogen receptor (ER) and MAPK phosphorylations. The results indicated that higher amount of calycosin within the decoction possessed much stronger inductions of MAPK and ER activations. The erythropoietic effect of DBTΔcal and DBT∆fa: Previous studies showed that DBT and calycosin, rather than ferulic acid, were able to stimulate the transcriptional activity of HRE, a critical regulator for erythropoietin (EPO) transcription, in cultured HEK293T cells. To reveal the transcriptional activity of HRE, a luciferase-reporter construct, containing six HREs derived from the promoter of EPO gene and tagged upstream of a luciferase gene (pHRE-Luc) was transfected into cultured fibroblasts. After treating DBT in cultured HEK293T for 48 hours, the pHRE-Luc activity was induced in a dose-dependent manner. The maximal inductions were revealed at ~1 mg/mL of DBT and DBT∆fa. However, DBTΔcal showed a much-reduced activation of pHRE-Luc, as compared to the others. The mRNA and protein expression levels of hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF-1α) showed similar patterns. The stimulations of calycosin-depleted DBT decoction possessed much weaker activations in regulating HIF-1α transcriptional and translational levels. The anti-oxidative functions of DBTΔcal and DBT∆fa: Ferulic acid was shown to benefit body health by decreasing the formation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) by increasing anti-oxidative functions. Thus, ferulic acid could be the one to account for anti-oxidative properties of DBT. The prevention of ROS formation and the induction of anti-oxidative proteins were compared between authentic DBT, DBTΔcal and DBT∆fa in cultured cardiomyocyte H9C2 cell. tBHP is frequently used to induce oxidative stress. The formation of ROS in H9C2 cell was in a dose-dependent manner in application of tBHP. The application of tBHQ, a positive control, could dramatically decrease the tBHP-induced ROS formation. Authentic and DBTΔfa were able to decrease the generation of tBHP-induced ROS by ~50%. In contrast, the reduction of ROS, induced by DBT∆fa, was much lower, as compared with that of authentic DBT and DBTΔcal. Ferulic acid by itself at ~800 ng/mL (a concentration being found in 1 mg/mL DBT) did not show effect on tBHP-induced ROS formation, except at a high dose. The omics studies of DBTΔcal and DBT∆fa: From RNA-seq results, it showed that the inductions of osteogenic differentiation markers, i.e. ALP, osterix and osteonectin, triggered by calycosin-enriched herbal decoction were much stronger than DBT∆cal in primary cultured osteoblasts. By signaling cascade analysis, the authentic DBT and DBTΔfa were capable of inducing osteogenesis by multiple mechanisms, i.e. MAPK/Erk and Wnt/β-catenin pathways; DBTΔcal was not capable of stimulating Wnt/β-catenin to induce bone formation. We also employed molecular biology method to verify the results, and it showed that authentic DBT and DBT∆fa triggered Wnt/β-catenin signaling cascades in regulating osteogenesis, including: (i) phosphorylation of GSK-3β; (ii) β-catenin nuclear translocation activity; and (iii) the blockage by application of DKK-1. Therefore, it indicated that calycosin played an essential role in monitoring osteoblastic differentiations, instead of ferulic acid from the decoction. By metabolomics analysis, we found the metabolites of treated cells of authentic DBT differed from DBTΔcal. Quantitative differences in the levels of metabolites, triggered by different DBT, might contribute to differences in pharmacological functions.

662713.label: Major findings and research outcome
662713.value: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) has been utilized for thousands of years, however, there are two challenges for the development of TCM (i) action mechanisms of each chemical found within herbal formula are unknown; and (ii) the identities of components within the herbal mixture are still behind the veil. Using DBT as a model, we would like to probe a systemically strategy for exploring the complexity omics studies of a traditional TCM formula. Here, we investigated the role of AR-derived bioactive chemical, calycosin, and ASR-generated biomarker, ferulic acid, in DBT decoction by the specific chemical knock-out methodologies. We have successfully prepared calycosin- or ferulic acid-depleted DBT, namely, DBT∆cal and DBT∆fa, respectively, and which have been confirmed by HPLC and LC-MS/MS. Furthermore, we also employed the cell biology, transcriptomics and metabolomics analyses to explore the synergistic functions of individual chemicals within a complex herbal mixture. The estrogenic and erythropoietic functions of DBT∆cal were markedly reduced as compared to the authentic DBT. On the other hand, the anti-oxidative functions of DBT∆fa in removing ROS were dramatically declined as compared to the authentic or DBT∆cal. Besides, the omics studies have shown that the expression levels of osteogenic differentiation markers were significantly increased under the treatments of DBT and DBT∆fa rather than DBTΔcal. The activations of DBT and DBT∆fa were induced by multiple mechanisms, Wnt/β-catenin and MAPK/Erk. By metabolomics analysis in DBT-treated osteoblasts, the profile of metabolites triggered by DBTΔcal showed distinction to that of DBT and DBT∆fa. All of these evidences indicated that each component possessed their unique and indispensable roles in order to achieve the maximal biological efficacies. Through the system analysis, i.e. chemical, biological, genomics and proteomics studies, a possible direction in comprehensive understanding the beauty and roles of each constituent in a herbal mixture, and it will help us to accelerate the acceptance of TCM in western world.

662713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
662713.value: We have investigated the role of major bioactive ingredients predominantly found within DBT decoction, preciously. Furthermore, the working mechanisms of each chemical in regulating specific pharmacological properties were also explored. We believed that this system verification could benefit us for the personalized treatment based on patient’s symptom. We attempted to employ the modified herbal formula to treat common ailments, relieve pain as well as improve the life qualities. On the other hand, the verified and isolated bioactive chemicals could re-combinate together as a novel medicine for mitigating specific diseases. The development of bioactive chemical, generated from TCM coupled with molecular biology, merges as the advanced and standardized method, which can promote the general acceptance of TCM.

662713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
662713.value: Multiple ingredients, targets and pathways are the major characteristics of TCM, and indeed, it is difficult to resolve the pharmacological activities and active mechanisms of TCM. Taking DBT as example, there are numerous bioactive chemicals found and identified within herbal decoction. The precise role of each chemical is still unknown. Hence, we utilized the targeted chemical fishing method to probe the major functions of each chemical by employing specific chemical depletion. From the results, we found each chemical possessed their singular functions within a herbal mixture but more importantly, they needed to work with other ingredients within herbal decoction in order to achieve the maximal pharmaceutical values. Therefore, we believed this finding could help us to comprehensively interpret the charming and mysterious aspect of TCM from molecular biology level.

662813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
662813.value: Estuaries are the interfaces of land, freshwater and sea, and are often the sinks of terrigenous pollutants entering the aquatic environments. With increasing industrialization in China, the estuary system is now suffering from unprecedented levels of metal pollution. Estuaries are also home to numerous shellfish farmings due to their abundant food supply and close proximity to human activity. Oysters are considered the hyper-accumulators of many toxic metals (e.g., copper, zinc and cadmium) and are the main shellfish species cultured in the estuarine region, including the Pearl River Estuary (PRE). Just recently, we discovered ‘colored’ (green and blue) oysters contaminated with extraordinarily high concentrations of copper and zinc (the highest amounting to 2-6% of tissue body weights) in many sites in the PRE. We also observed that the consumption of these toxic shellfish has affected human health and caused diseases. The discovery of these heavily contaminated oysters presents several major scientific questions: How are such phenomenal concentrations of metals accumulated in the oysters? How can the oysters tolerate and acclimate to such high levels of metals in the estuarine environment? Are there any scientific methods to remediate the metal contamination in the oysters? To address these fundamental scientific questions, this project will select different sites in the PRE and other Southern China estuaries known to be contaminated with different metals (cadmium, copper and zinc). Specifically, we will 1) determine the key biokinetic processes leading to high metal accumulation in oysters in a fluctuating estuarine environment, 2) elucidate the cellular handling, sequestration, and speciation of metals in oysters, as well as the animals’ development of tolerance towards metal contamination, and 3) seek possible ways of remediation based on our fundamental understanding of metal bioaccumulation in oysters. The significance of this project will be twofold. First, it will help us understand the fundamental processes through which oysters, a metal hyper-accumulator, accumulate and handle toxic metals. There is a lack of knowledge in the animals’ acclimation and tolerance to metals in extremely contaminated environments. Second, it can provide practical approaches for remediating the metal contamination in oysters. Given the extreme importance of the oyster industry in the Pearl River Estuary and in South China, this project will make a major impact both academically and economically. This project is also of major public interest due to the recent concerns over seafood safety in Hong Kong and worldwide. 河口是淡水和海水的交換地帶，也是污染物的沉降場所。隨著中國工業化的進展，河口也受到前所未有的污染。由於河口生產力很高，它同時也是許多貝類養殖的場所。牡蠣是珠江河口區的主要貝類養殖種類，但又是金屬超累積生物。最近我們在珠江口發現到有顏色的牡蠣，其金屬的含量非常高。這些受污染的牡蠣給我們提出了一些科學問題。比如牡蠣是如何累積金屬到如此之高的濃度？它們在河口區又是如何適應高污染的金屬？有沒有什麼科學方法可以治理這些受污染的牡蠣？要解決這些基本的科學問題，本項目1）測定金屬的基本生物動力學過程，瞭解它們如何在牡蠣體內達到很高的浓度，2）解析金屬在牡蠣體內的結合，解毒和存在形式，以及牡蠣耐受能力的發展，3）尋找可能治理金屬污染的途徑。 本項目的重要性在於它可以幫助我們瞭解牡蠣如何累積和處理重金屬污染，同時可以提供治理牡蠣重金屬污染的科學依據。由於珠江口的污染，相信本項目可以在科學研究和經濟方面都做出貢獻。

662813.label: Realisation of objectives
662813.value: The 3 objectives stated in the proposal were all achieved. 1. Determine the key biokinetic processes leading to high metal accumulation in oysters in a fluctuating estuarine environment: We have determined the kinetics of metals in oysters leading to high metal accumulation in oysters. The oysters were collected from different locations in contaminated environments and their kinetics were determined. We also compared the bioaccumulation of metals in oysters from different contaminated environments between two species. Some of the specific biochemical and physiological mechanisms leading to metal bioaccumulation were specifically probed, including the role of metallothioneins and cellular bindings. Other environmental conditions such as the nutrient levels and the salinity were also specifically examined for their potential influences on metal bioaccumulation. 2. Elucidate the cellular handling, sequestration, and speciation of metals in oysters, as well as the development of tolerance towards metal contamination: Extensive work was conducted in this task. We determined the subcellular storage as well as the localization of metals in the oysters, and the basal metal requirements and the controls of metal accumulation on metal toxicity. We used rather modern techniques such as X‑ray Absorption Spectroscopy to examine the chemical speciation of metals in the contaminated oysters. We also specifically examined the metal tolerance of oyster larvae from contaminated environments. 3. Seek possible ways of remediation based on our fundamental understanding of metal bioaccumulation in oysters: we conducted experiments to depurate the oysters which were metal contaminated and examine the rate of metal elimination from the oysters. We also attempted to test the possibility of growing triploid oysters in reducing the metal contamination. This remains to be a very interesting solution in possibly reducing the metal accumulation. Furthermore, we argue for further scientific research in this area.

662813.label: Major findings and research outcome
662813.value: Numerous findings were made in this project. A total of 13 papers were published in top international journals in Environmental Science, including 3 papers in Environmental Science and Technology. Some of the major findings are summarized below. 1.We demonstrated that seasonal metal accumulation in the oysters was strongly controlled by the biological process, while the variation as well as the concentration were dependent on the contamination levels and bioaccumulation ability (Weng and Wang 2014). The biokinetics of metals in the oysters were controlled by the metallothionein-like protein (MTLP) turnover, and there was a strong correlation between MTLP synthesis rate and metal dissolved uptake rate (Jin and Wang 2015). For the first time, we also found that metal accumulation may be related to the sodium and nutrient levels in the bivalves (Liu and Wang 2016). Furthermore, different affinities of metals can lead to very different bioaccumulation patterns and effects in the oysters (Liu and Wang 2014). 2. Metals in oysters were sequestered very differently in different subcellular pools, and such partitioning can greatly control their bioaccessibility to humans (Gao and Wang 2014). Different contamination levels in the oysters may lead to different binding and thus sensitivities to metals (Rainbow et al. 2015). Using X-ray-absorption near-edge structure (XANES) and the extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) techniques, we for the first time found that Cu and Zn occurred mainly in species resembling cysteine complexes in the gill of oysters, but their major metal species resembled histidine complexes or phosphates in the gills of contaminated ones (Tan et al., 2015). 3. The depuration of metals in contaminated oysters could be described by a first-order kinetic process. Depuration rates of contaminated oysters were significantly higher for Cd, Cu, Cr, and Ni than those from a less contaminated site, whereas the depuration rates of Ag, Co, Pb and Zn were comparable between the two populations. Significant changes in metal subcellular distribution were observed during the 4-month depuration and MTLPs became more important in sequestering the metals during the depuration period (Wang and Wang 2014). 4. One of the most important findings was that long-term metal exposure could greatly disrupt the reproduction cycle of the oysters and may finally affect the recruitment and population of this species (Weng and Wang 2015). A series of studies demonstrated that the field contamination of metals can affect the biochemical, physiological, and cellular responses of oysters (Liu et al. 2016a,b,c, Cao and Wang 2016).

662813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
662813.value: Oysters are very important in southern China, and given their hyper-accumulation potential of toxic metals, concerns about their safety are enormous in this region. However, we still lack a fundamental understanding of metal-oyster interaction in the following aspects: 1) what are the molecular mechanisms leading to metal transport, sequestration and elimination in the oysters. Different modern technologies such as genomics, proteomics, and others are required to further understand the mechanisms of metal uptake and handling strategies. 2) The impacts of metals in the real environments need to be further tested. In the field conditions, there are mixtures of metals coupled with many other environmental variables (such as pH, dissolved oxygen), which can create multiple ecosystem stressors. The interaction among these stressors remains to be very poorly known. The mixture effects should be specifically examined in further studies. It would be important to identify the specific metals causing any impacts in oysters in the complicated environments. 3) remediation remains to be a critical research direction. Although there are now some promising techniques that could perhaps reduce the metal levels in oysters, further exploration is needed.

662813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
662813.value: Estuaries are the interfaces of land, freshwater and sea, and are often the sinks of terrigenous pollutants entering the aquatic environments. With increasing industrialization in China, the estuary system is now suffering from unprecedented levels of metal pollution. Oysters are considered the hyper-accumulators of many toxic metals (e.g., copper, zinc and cadmium) and are the main shellfish species cultured in the estuarine region, including the Pearl River Estuary (PRE). In this project, we addressed three questions: 1) How are such phenomenal concentrations of metals accumulated in the oysters? 2) How can the oysters tolerate and acclimate to such high levels of metals in the estuarine environment? 3) Are there any scientific methods to remediate the metal contamination in the oysters? We show that the accumulation of metals in oysters is controlled by various environmental and biological processes. Metals are handled in the oysters in a very complicated manner, and one of the main strategies is to detoxify any incoming metals. With considerable pollution in the estuary, this study convincingly demonstrates that pollution is causing different biochemical, physiological, cellular, and reproductive effects in the oysters in a real environmental setting.

663613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
663613.value: PICK1 is a peripheral membrane protein that is important for protein trafficking. It controls the trafficking of neurotransmitter receptors in the brain and proacrosomal granules in the testis. PICK1 deficiency leads to male infertility and abnormalities in synaptic plasticity, a cellular model of learning and memory. PICK1 consists of a PDZ domain at its N-terminus, a BAR domain in the middle and an acidic region at the C-terminus. The PDZ domain of PICK1 interacts with a number of membrane proteins. In most cases, the interactions of PICK1 with these proteins regulate their trafficking by controlling either their subcellular localizations, their cell surface expressions, or both. For example, the interaction of PICK1 with GluA2, a subunit of the AMPA type glutamate receptors, regulates the synaptic targeting of GluA2 and its surface expression. This regulation was found to be important for synaptic plasticity. The BAR domain of PICK1 can form a dimer with itself or with ICA69, another BAR domain-containing protein. BAR domain dimers can sense the curved membrane of vesicles and bind to lipid membranes, especially membranes enriched with phosphoinositides. The combination of PDZ domain and BAR domain enables PICK1 to couple its PDZ-binding partners to trafficking vesicles. In addition to the two domains, PICK1 also has an acidic region at its C-terminus with a stretch of 10 positive-charged acidic residues. Our previous work has demonstrated that the C-terminal acidic region of PICK1 can inhibit the lipid binding capability of PICK1’s BAR domain. Whether this inhibition has any physiological significance is not clear. Our preliminary data indicate that the deletion of PICK1’s C-terminal acidic region changes its subcellular localization. We also found that the C-terminal region of PICK1 could be cleaved endogenously in neurons. This raises the possibility that the C-terminal acidic region of PICK1 could act as a switch to regulate protein trafficking. We propose to extend this line of study to fully reveal the functions of PICK1’s C-terminal acidic region in AMPA receptor trafficking, synaptic plasticity and infertility. 663613.label: Realisation of objectives
663613.value: In this study, we found that the C-terminus of PICK1 could be cleaved. To study the function of this cleavage, we first determined the subcellular localization of PICK1 mutant without its C-terminal acidic domain (PICK1-deltaC). Deletion of PICK1’s C-terminal acidic domain changed its cellular localization pattern from diffusing in the cytosol to forming numerous puncta inside the cells. We also found that deletion of PICK1’s C-terminal domain enhanced its lipid binding capability. Interestingly, we found that while wild-type PICK1 could cluster AMPA receptor subunit GluA2, PICK1-deltaC did not cluster GluA2, despite the fact that PICK1-deltaC formed cluster itself and PICK1-deltaC still interacted with GluA2. This supports the hypothesis that PICK1-deltaC could form clusters in subcellular structures that are inaccessible to GluA2. We also investigated the possibility of endogenous cleavage of PICK1’s C-terminal acidic domain. Our data indicate the PICK1’s C-terminal domain could be cleaved endogenously and this cleavage is enhanced when neurons were under stress. Further studies found that this cleavage is mediated by caspases. We then performed a systematic screening by mutating potential caspase cleavage sites one-by-one and identified Asp363 and Asp390 as the sites of cleavage. Together, our data suggests that activation of caspases by stimulation could induce cleavage of PICK1 at the C-terminus and this cleavage will regulate AMPA receptors trafficking in neurons.

663613.value: In this study we found that the C-terminus of PICK1 protein could be cleaved. This cleavage is mediated by caspases. We also determined the sites of cleavage. Cleaved PICK1 could still interact AMPA receptors, but could no longer cluster it. 663613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
663613.value: The molecular and cellular mechanisms responsible for learning and memory are central to understanding how the brain works. PICK1 has emerged as a key regulator of AMPA receptor trafficking in synaptic plasticity, the cellular model of learning and memory. In this study, we found that the C-terminus of PICK1 protein could be cleaved. Cleaved PICK1 affects its subcellular localization, and also PICK1-mediated AMPA receptor trafficking. We also found that PICK1’s cleavage is mediated by caspases, whose activation was found to be important for synaptic plasticity. Finally, we determined the site the cleavage. This study provides a good understanding of the structure-function relationship of PICK1, reveals the link between caspase activation and AMPA receptor trafficking in synaptic plasticity, and furthers our understanding of the molecular mechanism underlying learning and memory.

664013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
664013.value: Eukaryotic genomes are equipped with a large number of replication origins that are licensed for initiation by the loading of Mcm2-7 complex during G1 phase. The loaded Mcm2-7 hexamers are tightly bound to replication origins as double ring structures that encircle the duplex DNA to form the pre-replication complex (pre-RC) (Figure 1, I). During S phase, only a fraction of the licensed replication origins are activated. Which origins are selected for initiation depends on the affinity of the pre-RC bound replication origins for the limiting Dbf4-Cdc7 kinase (DDK) and the limiting initiation factors, Cdc45, Sld3, Sld2, Dpb11 and Sld7. Winners in this competition win the monopoly to recruit GINS, Mcm10 and the DNA polymerases. Subsequent melting of origin DNA, in which the Mcm2-7 double hexamer must reconfigure to allow each ring to encircle opposite single strands for bidirectional unwinding, is most critical yet least understood in the initiation process. Recent studies placed Mcm10 at the juncture of this melting step (Figure 1, II). Our previous study showed that Mcm10 is required for the removal of Mcm2-7 at licensed but unfired replication origins. Our latest study further supports a model in which Mcm10 does so by enabling the double hexamer to disassemble into single hexamers (Figure 1, III). Thus, we envision that origin-bound Mcm2-7 double hexamers are removed from replication origins in two ways, both requiring the action of Mcm10. At activated origins, Mcm10 takes part in the transitional step where the Mcm2-7 double hexamer reconfigures to form single rings that later become part of the replisome progression complex (RPC). At unfired origins, the Mcm2-7 double hexamers are directly released from chromatin by disassembling into single hexamers, also requiring the action of Mcm10. In this proposal, we will use genetic and biochemical approaches to investigate the role of Mcm10 in reconfiguring the Mcm2-7 ring structure through analyzing the conformational changes of the Mcm2-7 complex induced by the Mcm2 suppressors of mcm10. We will investigate the mechanism that controls the recruitment of Mcm10 to replication origins. We will also determine the interacting domains of Mcm10 with the Mcm2 and Mcm6 subunits of Mcm2-7, and examine their physiological function in regulating the conformational changes of the double ring structure. Understanding the basic mechanism for DNA replication will help identify targets for cancer drug therapy, devise diagnostics for early detection of cancer as well as elucidate the etiology of different cancer types. 真核生物的基因組中有許多的位點可以用于DNA複製的起始，但是，在複製的過程中，只有小部分的位點真正用于複製起始。這依賴于一批複製起始因子和起始位點的結合，從而激活DNA解旋酶Mcm2-7復合物，以促進DNA雙鏈的打開及隨後複製機器的組裝。在此過程中，Mcm2-7的構象改變發揮關鍵作用，但我們對其中確切的分子機理還缺乏足够的瞭解。我們初步的實驗結果顯示，複製起始蛋白Mcm10調控Mcm2-7的激活和解聚。在此研究計劃中，我們將使用遺傳和生化方法進一步探究Mcm10對于促進Mcm2-7構象變化的具體分子機制，以闡釋其在DNA複製起始中的生理作用。我們相信，由此研究得出的結果，將會深化我們對于DNA複製機理的理解，並有助于發現癌症藥物治療和檢測的新靶標。

664013.label: Realisation of objectives
664013.value: To address the role of Mcm10 in remodeling the Mcm2-7 ring structure, we have put much effort in carrying out extensive studies to realize the objectives listed in the proposal. The details of these research activities, the results achieved, and the problems encountered are presented here. Objective 1: Numerous studies have indicated that Mcm10 played an essential role in replication initiation. However, its detailed molecular function in this process remains poorly understood. In this study, we found that Mcm10 is required to remodel the Mcm2-7 complex such that the Mcm2-7 double hexamer could be uncoupled. As a result of the MCM DH uncoupling, the CMG helicases are activated at replication origins. Our analyses of replication fork progression through replication origin regions, using two dimensional gel electrophoresis and ChIP assays, suggest that the in vivo assembled CMG complexes are tightly linked to the origin DNA. If not properly activated by Mcm10, the pre-IC could become a barrier to the RFs migrating from nearby origins. Furthermore, using Pol1 ChIP-seq, we found that Mcm10 is required for the smooth passage of replication forks at replication origins across genome, at especially those where Mcm2 is most abundant suggesting that the obstacle encountered by the replication fork is associated with the Mcm2-7 complex. Interestingly, we further found that a mcm10 suppressor mutant, mcm2G400D, is able to rescue the defects of the mcm10 mutants in the CMG activation, the fork stalling at replication origins, and replication initiation as well. These results imply that the G400D mutation in Mcm2 may mimic the action of Mcm10 in remodeling the MCM2-7 complex for activating the assembled CMG helicases. To examine the influence of the mcm2G400D mutation in reconfiguring the MCM2-7 structure, we isolated the chromatin-bound MCM2-7 complexes using yeast G1 cells from both the WT and mcm2G400D mutant strains. Our results from both glycerol gradient ultracentrifugation and negative staining electron microscopy analyses indicate that the mcm2G400D mutation induces significant conformational change in the MCM ring, which lead to the separation of the MCM DH. It also reinforces the notion that Mcm10 plays an important role in uncoupling Mcm2-7 DHs for helicase activation by remodeling the conformation of Mcm2-7 complexes. Objective 2: To verify where Mcm10 is at different stages, we carried out genome-wide ChIP-seq of Mcm10 in G1 and early S phase cells. Our ChIP-seq analysis showed that Mcm10 does not associate with any replication origin at G1 phase. Furthermore, using ChIP followed by real-time qPCR, we found that the association of Mcm10 with early origins peaked at the earliest time point in S phase, and at a later time point with late and dormant origins that fire infrequently or rarely. These results suggest that Mcm10 is not preloaded at replication origins but recruited to these origins just prior to their activation at active origins or to CMG disassembly at unfired origins. In order to determine the domain of Mcm10 responsible for its origin association, several mcm10 deletion mutants have been constructed. We have shown that the Mcm10 C-terminal domain (aa464-502) is required for the smooth passage of replication forks through unfired origins and that the MCM2G400D mutation bypasses this requirement. An interpretation of this result is that this Mcm10 domain is required to reconfigure the Mcm2-7 complex and that the Mcm2 suppressor is able to assume that configuration without Mcm10. Our interaction analysis showed that, Mcm10∆C108 almost lost its interaction with Mcm2 while Mcm10∆C69 interacted well with Mcm2, suggesting that the 464-502 domain is specifically required for Mcm10’s interaction with Mcm2. Furthermore, the Mcm2G400D suppressor interacted strongly with Mcm10 independent of the C108 domain suggesting that Mcm2G400D has an altered conformation that allows it to interact with Mcm10 either via other subunits of the Mcm2-7 complex or with another domain of Mcm10. These results suggest that the interaction between Mcm subunits and Mcm10 might contribute to the loading of Mcm10 onto replication origins. Objective 3 To understand the intra- and inter-subunit salt bridges of Mcm2-7 DH complex that are important for regulating the remodeling of Mcm2-7 complex during helicase activation, we solved the structure of the Mcm2-7 DH at 3.8 Å using cryo-EM. The information derived from this structure provides a rich source for us to uncover the fine details of this large protein assembly. With this structure, now we understand how the two SHs are joined together to form a tilted and twisted dimer. The interdigitated interactions between their N-terminal zinc finger domains (ZFs) help to couple the two SHs. In addition, the N-terminal subunit-specific sequence extensions (NTEs) and insertions (NTIs) from Mcm3, 5 and 7 further strengthen this coupling. Together, these interactions contribute to a stable DH. The inter-subunit interactions between adjacent subunits are very similar, and can be categorized into three tiers based on their axial locations. The first one, also the most common one, is the tight stacking between two helices from the two contacting ATPase domains of the CTD ring. In a few cases (Mcm6:4, 7:3, and 2:6), EXT-HP (exterior hairpin) also significantly contributes to this helical stacking. The second tier, on the neck region of the hexamer, involves four conserved hairpins or loops from two adjacent subunits. PS1-HP (presensor 1 β-hairpin) of the first subunit is sandwiched between ACL (allosteric communication loop) and H2I-N (N-terminal helix of helix-2-insert) of the flanking second subunit. At the same time, ACL of the second also interacts with H2I-C (C-terminal helix of H2I), and in a few cases (Mcm6:4, 3:5, and 2:6) with the N-C linker of the first. The third tier, contributed by the ZF of a given subunit and two loops from the OB of a flanking subunit, are largely composed of hydrophobic interactions between respective β-strands or loops. Interestingly, the residue G400 of Mcm2 resides at the tip of the ACL, which has been shown to act as a hinge for coordinating the conformational changes between the N- and C-terminal domains of archaeal MCM. The ACL is highly conserved among MCM genes, indicating that this loop may perform a similar function in the MCM2-7 complex. Actually, considerable conformational changes between the NTD and CTD of each MCM subunit can be observed when the MCM SHs are assembled into the DH. Among these subunits, Mcm2 undergoes the most dramatic remodeling. In addition, the location of the Mcm2 ACL in the MCM ring is changed significantly during this process. In the DH, the Mcm2 ACL is inserted into Mcm6 at its neck region and in a position close to the M6 N-C linker. However, this same loop is shifted away from Mcm6 in the SH structure; the M6 N-C linker also flips toward another direction. Given the fact that the mcm2G400D suppressor destabilizes the DH, we hypothesize that Mcm10 activates the CMG helicase through regulating the M2 ACL to uncouple the MCM DH. We have also purified the mutant Mcm2-7 (M2G400D) SH complexes for structural determination by cryo-EM, which is still under investigation. This structure and the information from structural comparisons among the available high-resolution structures are expected to inform us the structural basis of the MCM DH uncoupling and unravel the molecular role of Mcm10 in this process.

664113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
664113.value: DISC1是一個與多種主要的精神性疾病（包括精神分裂症、躁鬱症、憂鬱症）高度關聯的遺傳致病因子。人類的DISC1基因編碼一個含854個氨基酸殘基的蛋白，但其大部份氨基酸序列會形成內在無序結構或卷曲-卷曲結構。DISC1蛋白能與上百種不同的蛋白結合，並在許多種大腦功能和活動（包括神經幹細胞的產生、神經元的遷移、神經通路的形成和突觸生成）中發揮著至關重要的作用。大量的遺傳學和分子細胞生物學硏究證實了DISC1在大腦正常發育中的重要作用，也確認了DISC1的突變與神經系統疾病之間的緊密聯繫。然而，與之形成鮮明對比的是，無論是對單獨的DISC1蛋白，還是對DISC1參與形成的蛋白複合物的生化和結構的硏究都十分稀缺。其瓶頸在於，純化一個適用於高分辨率結構硏究的DISC1或者其複合物的蛋白非常困難。而生化和結構硏究的短缺也嚴重地阻礙了我們對於DISC1功能和致病突變的病理機制的硏究。 在此次的提案中，我們計劃通過核磁共振（NMR）的方法解析出DISC1羧基端與三個結合蛋白分別形成的三個蛋白複合物的結構。這三個結合蛋白分別是Ndel1、ATF4和liprin-α。它們的功能都被很好地硏究過。在我們前期的硏究中，我們成功地表達並純化了性質很好、適用於結構解析的蛋白複合物。如果我們能解析出高分辨率的蛋白複合物的原子結構，我們將在此基礎上詳細地硏究DISC1與各個結合蛋白的相互作用及其功能。此外，我們的前期硏究還發現，DISC1羧基端有一段約150個氨基酸殘基的片段會形成閉合的結構。負責形成閉合結構的區域中包含有一個會導致疾病的氨基酸殘基突變（S704C）。我們計劃解析出這段約150個氨基酸殘基的DISC1片段的高分辨率結構，並硏究這種閉合構像的功能。我們也將探索S704C突變對閉合構像造成的結構和功能上的變化。如果我們能成功地完成這一系列的硏究，我們將給DISC1的硏究界帶來期待已久的生化和結構的數據。這不僅有助於我們對DISC1蛋白的科學認識，還將對由DISC1突變造成的人類精神性疾病的治療大有裨益。

664113.label: Realisation of objectives
664113.value: We have been very successful in carrying out this challenging project. The following is a brief summary: 1. We have determined the structures of the DISC1 C-terminal tail in complex with Nudel1 and ATF4 to high resolutions by NMR spectroscopy. These structures are, to our knowledge, the first detailed structural characterizations of DISC1. Our findings can form a foundation for understanding the structural basis of specific interactions of DISC1 with each of these three targets; and to provide a wonderful opportunity for further functional characterization of each of these interactions. 2. Based on our structural findings, we are investigating the roles of the DISC1/Ndel1interaction and DISC1/ATF4 interaction in cell cycle control, neurogenesis, and neuronal stem cell development. We have found that DISC1/Ndel1 interaction is important for mitosis, and thus mutation of DISC1 leading to interruption of the DISC1/Ndel1 interaction can affect neurogenesis and brain development. We have collaborated with Dr. Hongjun Song's lab in the Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine to directly assess the role of the DISC1/Ndel1 interaction in neurogenesis. We found that the DISC1/Ndel1 interaction directly regulate cell cycle of neuronal stem cells using human brain oganoid as a model. The revised manuscripthas just been accepted by Neuron and the paper is scheduled to appear online on Nov. 2. 3. The interaction between DISC1/ATF4 is very strong and specific. We are also collaborating with Dr. Hongjun Song's lab in investigating the role of the DISC1/AFT4 interaction in transcriptional control in neurons. This part of the story is underpreparation for publication, and we expected to have a manuscript ready by the end of October. 4. We have also determined the auto-inhibited structure of the C-terminal region of DISC1, and we are designing possible experiments to address potential functions of this autoinhibition.

664113.label: Major findings and research outcome
664113.value: Mutations of DISC1 (disrupted in schizophrenia 1) have been associated with major psychiatric disorders. Despite the hundreds of DISC1 binding proteins reported, almost nothing is known about how DISC1 interacts with other proteins structurally to impact human brain development. Here we solved the high-resolution structure of DISC1 C-terminal tail in complex with its binding domain of Ndel1. Mechanistically, DISC1 regulates Ndel1’s kinetochore attachment but not its centrosome localization during mitosis. Functionally, disrupting DISC1/Ndel1 complex formation prolongs mitotic length and interferes with cell cycle progression in human cells, and amplification of neural stem cells in human forebrain organoids. We further demonstrated deficits in cell cycle progression of neural stem cells in human forebrain organoids derived from a schizophrenia patient with a DISC1 mutation that disturbs its interaction with Ndel1. Our study uncovers a new mechanism of action for DISC1 based on its structure and has implications for how genetic insults may contribute to psychiatric disorders. The manuscript describing this work has just been accepted for publication by Neuron.

664113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
664113.value: With the detailed structural and biochemical characterization of DISC1 and its interaction with several of its binding partners, we have established a solid foundation to understand the mechanistic basis of DISC1 function in brain development and signaling under both physiological and diseases conditions. In the future, we will be studying: 1. Complete the study of the DISC1/ATF4 interaction in neuronal development and potential link to schizophrenia. 2. Further explore the potential function of the auto-inhibited conformation of the DISC1 C-terminal domain. 3. Further characterized the interaction between DISC1 and other targets including GSK3beta, PDE4, etc.

664113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
664113.value: A major challenge in understanding why mutations of DISC1 can cause psychiatric disorders is lack of clean and definitive mechanistic studies of interactions between DISC1 and its numerous reported interacting proteins. In addition, human brain-based mechanistic study in DISC1 is lacking. In this research, we determined the first atomic structure of DISC1 with one of its binding partner Ndel1/Nde1. Based on this structure, we devised a method which can specifically investigate functions of the DISC1/Ndel1 complex in vivo without interfering bindings of DISC1 to other proteins or Ndel1/Nde1-mediated dynein complex functions. Such method is applicable for studying functions of multi-domain scaffold proteins in general. Using this method, we discover that the DISC1/Ndel1 interaction can specifically regulate Ndel1’s kinetochore attachment and thus modulate cell cycle progression. Using human forebrain organoids, we show that the DISC1/Ndel1 complex is important for proper neuronal stem cell maintenance during brain development. As such, our study is a major advancement in understanding DISC1’s function in brain development and neuro-disorders.

689813.label: Project Title(Chinese)
689813.value: 噬菌體利用藍細菌的信號轉導系統以適應海洋環境

689813.label: Project Objectives
689813.value: The selective advantage for cyanophages to encode P-acquisition genes Phosphorus is essential for phage DNA replication. We hypothesize that phage-encoded P-acquisition genes pstS and phoA confer cyanophage selective advantages under P-limited conditions. In order to test this hypothesis we will first study the enzymatic properties of phage PstS and PhoA proteins. We will then knockout these two genes from cyanophage genomes to test whether they are beneficial for cyanophage replication in P-starved host cells. This will be the first study to test the selective advantage of host-like metabolic genes in marine viruses and will help understand the evolution of viruses in the oceans. The DNA binding specificity of PhoB between various host-phage pairs The expression of P-acquisition genes in bacteria is controlled by the PhoR/PhoB two-component signal transduction system. PhoB is the transcriptional activator and it can bind to the promoter region (pho box sequence) of P-acquisition genes to activate their transcription. Previously, we showed that host PhoB can bind specifically to the pho box sequence of pstS in the phage (47). We argue that the PhoB-binding affinity of phage pho box sequence should not be stronger than the host ones, otherwise it may interfere with the transcription of host P-acquisition genes. We will perform gel mobility shift assay to test this hypothesis. We will also ask whether the pho box sequence of a phage can be recognized by PhoB protein of a cyanobacterium that it can not infect. This will be the first study to link a phage’s host range to the specificity of the host’s signal transduction system and may open up another layer of adaptation strategy used by bacteriophages. Exploitation of host’s signal transduction system by cyanophages in response to nitrogen limitation Although phage infection shut off the transcription of most host genes, our preliminary transcriptome sequencing (RNA-Seq) data shows that the transcription of host P-acquisition genes was not affected during infection. We hypothesize that phage may exploit the host signal transduction systems for other environmental stresses. Like phosphorus, nitrogen (N) concentrations in the oligotrophic oceans are also extremely low and sometimes limit phytoplankton growth (12). Therefore we propose to use RNA-Seq to examine whether the N-starvation response of Prochlorococcus is affected by phage infection. This approach will also help us identify differentially expressed phage genes in response to N starvation. This will be the first transcriptome study on the effect of nutrient limitation on host and phage gene expression.

689813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
689813.value: Microorganisms constitute more than 90% of the living biomass in the sea and microbial communities are important for the nutrient and energy cycles in the world’s oceans. Far from being mere parasites, bacterial viruses (bacteriophages) play crucial roles in shaping their bacterial host’s genomes and population dynamics. As such, they are major players in the global geochemical and ecological processes. As phages coevolve with their hosts, there is a reciprocal exchange of selected genes. Phosphate acquisition genes of host origin have been found in the genomes of T4-like lytic phages (cyanophages) infecting the unicellular cyanobacteria Prochlorococcus and Synechococcus, which are the most abundant photosynthetic cells on Earth. Phosphate limits phytoplankton production in some regions of the oceans, with phosphate concentrations drawn down to the nanomolar range in some areas. The environmental availability of phosphorus exerts strong selective pressure on the evolution of cyanobacterial genomes. Since nucleotide biosynthesis requires significant amounts of phosphorus, these genes in the phages likely play a role in facilitating host P-acquisition for phage DNA replication during infection. We found that the transcription of phage-encoded P-acquisition genes was elevated in P-starved host cells relative to P-replete conditions. We further confirmed that these phage genes were regulated by the host PhoR/PhoB two-component signal transduction system, which is used by bacteria to sense environmental phosphate availability. This is the first example in which a virus exploits this system to be responsive to environmental conditions. The objective of this proposed project is to study how lytic phages have evolved to take advantage of signal transduction systems in their hosts to increase their fitness under resource-limited conditions. The research proposed herein is designed to explore the selective advantage for cyanophages to encode P-acquisition genes, examine the DNA binding specificity of PhoB between various host-phage pairs and study the response of cyanophages to other environmental stresses (e.g., nitrogen limitation). The research proposed here will deepen our understanding of the coevolution of bacteria and their viruses in the marine ecosystem. 原綠球藻和聚球藻屬於單細胞可以進行光合作用的藍細菌。它們是世界上數量最多的的光合作用生物。它們的噬菌體基因組包含磷代謝基因。磷在海洋中的濃度很低，制約著浮遊微生物的生長。我們之前的研究發現噬菌體的磷代謝基因可以在感染缺磷的宿主時被提高表達量，並且這個過程是由宿主的PhoR/PhoB二元信號轉導系統調控的。這是第一個病毒利用二元信號轉導系統的例子。我們將進一步研究病毒是如何利用二元信號轉導系統以更好適應海洋環境。

689913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
689913.value: In the adult central nervous system (CNS), mature neurons lose the intrinsic capacity toregenerate injured axons. A model to study such mechanisms is the axon regeneration of dorsal root ganglia (DRG) neurons, which are able to regenerate peripheral, but notcentral branches in the adult spinal cord. However, a pre-conditioning lesion to theperipheral axons allows the subsequently injured central branches to grow into and beyond the lesion site. A possibility is that the peripheral lesion results in the delivery of putative positive signals to cell bodies to reactivate axon re-growth. Recent studies implicated deletion of PTEN and Socs3 can promote robust growth in retinal ganglion neurons and other types of CNS neurons. We hypothesize that these pathways may also contribute to decreased regenerative ability in mature neurons in adults. A prediction of this hypothesis will be that relieving the inhibitory influences of PTEN or Socs3 or both signaling in these mature neurons may reprogram the neuronal growth states and allow efficient regeneration of adult neurons. In this proposed research, we will examine the role of the PTEN/mTOR and Socs3/Stat3 pathway in restricting axon regrowth ability in DRG neurons during development and after injury in adults. 在成年的中樞神經系統中，神經元損傷后喪失軸突再生能力。背根神經節神經元是可以用來研究這樣機制的模型。最近的研究表明敲除PTEN和SOCS3可以促進視網膜神經節神經元的軸突再生。我們推測，這些信號通路也可能普遍對神經再生能力下降起作用。在此提出的研究中，我們將研究限制軸突再生能力的PTEN / mTOR和Socs3/Stat3在背根神經元的作用。

689913.label: Realisation of objectives
689913.value: We crossed Raptor f/f, mTOR f/f, and Pten f/f with Advillin-Cre, and have successfully obtained Adv;Pten, Adv;Raptor mutant mice. We found that none of the mutant lead to significant axon elongation defect during dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neuron development. The gross anatomy of adult DRG axon projections does not get significantly affected. However, peripheral terminals showed abnormality in Pten, mTOR, and Raptor mutant mice. We are currently following up the unexpected findings. Then, we focused on the adult mice. We used genetic approaches to determine the role of mTOR signaling in sensory axon regeneration in mice. We showed that deleting mTOR in DRG neurons suppressed the axon regeneration induced by conditioning lesions. To establish whether the impact of mTOR on axon regeneration results from functions of mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1) or 2 (mTORC2), two distinct kinase complexes, we ablated either Raptor or Rictor in DRG neurons. We found that suppressing mTORC1 signaling dramatically decreased the conditioning lesion effect. In addition, an injury to the peripheral branch boosts mTOR activity in DRG neurons that cannot be completely inhibited by rapamycin, a widely used mTOR-specific inhibitor. Unexpectedly, examining several conditioning lesion–induced pro-regenerative pathways revealed that Raptor deletion but not rapamycin suppressed Stat3 activity in neurons. Therefore, our results demonstrate that crosstalk between mTOR and Stat3 signaling mediates the conditioning lesion effect and provide genetic evidence that rapamycin-resistant mTOR activity contributes to the intrinsic axon growth capacity in adult sensory neurons after injury. We further examined whether mTOR activation can enhance sensory axon growth after spinal cord injury. We intrathecally injected AAV-Cre at the lumbar level to infect L4–6 DRG neurons of WT, Ptenf/f, or TSC1f/f mice, and performed a bilateral dorsal column crush at T8 in 8-wk-old mice after 3 wk. WT mice with conditioning lesions were used as the positive control. We kept the mice for an additional 4 wk after injury. Two days before sacrificing the animals, we traced the dorsal column axons by injecting cholera toxin subunit B conjugated with Alexa488 (CTB488) into the sciatic nerve. In the control animals, there were no axons within or across the lesion site, and the injured axons had retracted certain distance from the lesion edge. By sharp contrast, in the animals with a conditioning lesion, fibers were observed coursing into the lesion site, some of which were distal to the lesion. In the Pten f/f mice, many axons were observed at the boundary of the lesion and a few axons grew into the lesion center. In the TSC1 f/f mice, axons grew closer to the lesion edge compared with controls, but we did not observe any axons across the lesion site. Our data indicated that Pten or TSC1 deletion increases axon growth capacity of DRG neurons after spinal cord injury. Thus, we have achieved our main aim to test the role of Pten/mTOR signaling in the axon regeneration of DRG neurons.

690013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
690013.value: 在美國股票市場中，機構投資者的持股比例有上升趨勢。據估計，在2010年，機構投資者的持股比例已高達67% 。同時，來自機構投資者的交易量比例也變得更高，這表明許多機構成為短線投資者。然而，儘管隨著時間的推移機構投資者越來越趨向于頻繁交易，並不是所有的機構投資者都如此。由於客戶偏好和信息獲取能力的差異，機構投資者的投資期限是不同的。在均衡狀態下，買賣同一支股票的機構投資者會擁有不同的投資期限。 我們推測，短線和長線投資者的持股比例可以解釋流動性波動。這是因為，長線投資者的交易由隨機投資組合需求推動，會導致股權週轉率的波動。相比之下，短線投資者的交易由消息推動，會向市場提供穩定的流動性。因此，更多短線投資者將傾向於抑制流動性波動，而更多長線投資者將會放大流動性波動。然而，流動性波動和短線投資者的持股比例之間的關係並不一定是單調的（反向）。這是因為如果只有短線投資者買賣股票，他們的羊群行為和動量交易將會導致流動性波動。 在實證分析中，我們按照投資組合週轉率（投資期限倒數）將機構投資者分為短線，中線和長線投資者。我們研究在一組橫截面股票中，哪一類投資者會貢獻更多的流動性波動。我們也建議未來可以研究流動性波動是如何與短線和長線投資者的加權平均週轉率的差異相關的，以及這種相關性是否是單調的。

690013.label: Realisation of objectives
690013.value: There are two objectives in the initial proposal: - Determine which category of investors (short-, medium-, or long-term) contributes more to the volatility of liquidity over time, and in a cross-section of stocks. - Investigate how the volatility of liquidity is related to the difference between the weighted-average churn ratios of short-term and long-term investors, and determine whether or not the relationship is monotonic Following these objectives and based on the U.S. market, we construct an empirical measure to capture how institutional investors holding the same stock may differ in their investment horizons, building on the intuition developed in the recent literature. We first compute the churn rate of each institution in each quarter, following Gaspar, Massa, and Matos (2005). The larger the churn rate, the higher the institutional investors’ portfolio turnover, and the shorter the investors’ investment period. Next, the stock-level heterogeneity in investment horizon (STDCR) is computed in each quarter as the standard deviation of the churn rate of all institutions holding a stock, scaled by the average churn rate of the same set of institutions. Our measures of illiquidity covers two dimensions: the price impact measure of illiquidity in Amihud (2002) (LOGILLIQ) and the trading activity measure based on the inverse of stock turnover used in Chordia, Subrahmanyam and Anshuman (2001). We find that investor heterogeneity is negatively related to both stock illiquidity and volatility of liquidity, as conjectured. For instance, a one standard deviation increase in STDCR is related to 0.74% lower stock illiquidity measured by LOGILLIQ for the NYSE/AMEX/Nasdaq sample during the period 1982─2016. Additionally, a one standard deviation increase in STDCR is associated with a decrease in liquidity volatility of 3.02%. We obtain similar findings when we use the trading activity measure of liquidity. The relation between investor heterogeneity and liquidity is robust to control for stock characteristics, including the level and concentration in institutional ownership. The relation between investor heterogeneity and liquidity is also robust when liquidity is based on the volatility of stock returns. The economic magnitude of our findings is stronger in the recent sample period from 2000 to 2016, with the growth in institutional investing. Using the addition of stocks to the S&P500 index as a quasi experimental setting, we find that these stocks experience an increase in investor heterogeneity as well as a decrease in stock illiquidity and volatility of liquidity. We also find evidence that a heterogeneous investor base better accommodates liquidity demand shocks, by examining the impact of flow-induced mutual fund transactions. We find strong supportive evidence that Coval and Stafford (2007) measures of flow-induced price pressure predicts return reversals in subsequent quarters for stocks with low investor heterogeneity. The price pressure induced by extreme capital flows in the mutual fund investors is significantly weaker for stocks with high investor heterogeneity. For example, the strategy of going long the stocks with extreme mutual fund flow-induced sales and short the stocks with extreme flow-induced purchases in a given year predicts a significant, risk-adjusted return of 6.95% over the subsequent year for stocks in the lowest investor heterogeneity quintile. On the other hand, for stocks that belong to the highest investor heterogeneity quintile, the same strategy yields an insignificant 0.97% risk-adjusted annual return. Our findings that capital flow motivated trading generates smaller price pressure when the investors in the stock have heterogeneous investment horizons support the idea that some investors absorb the liquidity shocks from other investor types. These findings complement the evidence on the negative effects of investor heterogeneity on illiquidity and liquidity volatility. Our findings on the role of heterogeneous investor base in affecting stock liquidity, the volatility of liquidity and cross-section of stock returns are robust to alternative ways of measuring differences in types of institutional investors. In particular, we obtain similar findings when we measure investor heterogeneity as the dispersion in the (fund) size of all institutional owners of a stock or the variation in the styles of the institutions holding the stock. As a placebo test, we show that the heterogeneity in investment horizon among closed-end funds owning a stock does not affect the stock liquidity and liquidity volatility. This is not surprising as closed-end funds are not subject to liquidity shocks from investor withdrawal and redemption. These findings support our explanation that the liquidity effects of the heterogeneous investor base are related to differences in the exposure of stocks to institution specific liquidity shocks, such as those emanating from investor fund flows due to withdrawals and redemptions. We also examine whether the illiquidity is priced, with a price premium for stocks of illiquidity. However, we only find weak evidence for that, with the premium for illiquidity concentrated among stocks with low investor heterogeneity. Overall, we do find the heterogeneity of investment horizon among Institutional investors in a stock is associated with higher stock liquidity and lower volatility of liquidity. In addition, extreme flow-induced trading by mutual funds has a bigger price impact among stocks with less heterogeneous investor base. Hence, a heterogeneous investor base facilitates the absorption of liquidity shocks and improves overall stock liquidity, particularly in the recent decades with increased participation by institutional investors. We also find that the premium associated with stock illiquidity is concentrated in stocks with low investor heterogeneity.

690013.label: Major findings and research outcome
690013.value: The main results in the paper are summarized as follows. We start with the conjecture that a heterogeneous investor base facilitates the accommodation of investor specific liquidity shocks. Consistent with our conjecture, the heterogeneity of investment horizon among investors holding a stock is negatively related to stock illiquidity. We find that the standard deviation of the portfolio churn rate across institutional investors holding a stock is negatively related to the stock illiquidity and volatility of liquidity, whereby the illiquidity measures are constructed based on the price impact measure of Amihud and the trading activity measure based on the inverse of stock turnover. This relationship is especially strong in the recent post-2000 period. In support of the hypothesis that a more diverse investor base better accommodates liquidity demand shocks from some investor types, we find that stocks with less heterogeneous investors suffer bigger price pressure associated with extreme fund outflows or fire sales by mutual funds. Hence, a heterogeneous investor base improves liquidity and reduces volatility of liquidity by absorbing liquidity shocks emanating from some investor types. Moreover, we find that the premium for illiquidity as a stock characteristic is concentrated among stocks with low investor heterogeneity. All these findings are economically significant and are obtained after accounting for effects due to other firm characteristics such as institutional ownership levels and concentration of ownership. The above results are robust to alternative ways of measuring differences in types of institutional investors, when we measure investor heterogeneity as the dispersion in the (fund) size of all institutional owners of a stock or the within firm variation in the styles of the institutions holding the stock. Moreover, we find that heterogeneity in investment horizon among closed-end funds owning a stock does not affect the stock liquidity and liquidity volatility. Thus, the heterogeneous investor base helps absorb idiosyncratic liquidity shocks from the institutions and therefore improves stock liquidity and smooths the liquidity volatility, but has no effect on closed-end funds as they do not face sudden portfolio inflows/outflows. Our results contribute to our understanding of the effects of heterogeneous investment horizons. With institutional investors representing a growing fraction of equity ownership and even larger proportion of trading activities, it is important to understand their influences on financial markets. We show that a balanced composition of short-term and long-term institutions, as reflected in a higher degree of investor heterogeneity of investment horizons, will help reduce stock illiquidity and liquidity volatility. Therefore, it is desirable for companies to attract both short-term and long-term institutions in holding the shares.

690013.value: The paper will be resubmitted to another journal.

690013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
690013.value: Institutional investors have been exerting dominating influence in financial markets, representing a larger fraction of equity ownership and even larger proportion of trading volume. However, Institutional investors can be quite different in terms of their investment objectives, mandates, and clienteles. One key source of heterogeneity among institutional investors is their investment horizon. In this paper, we examine how the heterogeneity of investment horizon, as reflected in the dispersion of investment horizon among institutional investors in a stock, will affect the stock liquidity. We show that the dispersion of investment horizon, as a reflection of the heterogeneous investor base, can explain both the stock liquidity and volatility of liquidity. The underlying reason is that if a stock has a heterogeneous investor base, investor specific liquidity demand shocks are less likely to be correlated and hence, easier to be absorbed by other investors. Therefore, it is desirable for companies to attract both short-term and long-term institutions in holding the shares.

690213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
690213.value: We intend to examine how the level of public corruption affects audit quality and shareholder wealth in a cross-country study. Corruption involves abuse of power by public officials for personal gains and is pervasive and economically significant, especially in developing countries. A large literature demonstrates that corruption negatively affects investment and economic growth. Even though corruption imposes costs on private firms and investors, there has been little research to date on whether and how corruption impacts corporate governance. To fill this void, we study the effect of corruption on audit quality and shareholder wealth. We believe that studying this effect is particularly relevant to auditing because the illegality of corruption and the need for secrecy should negatively impact audit quality. Furthermore, while corruption itself imposes a cost on shareholders’ wealth through wealth transfer, there is an addition agency cost owing to low-quality audits. We test these predictions in a cross-country dataset that uses publicly available measures of corruption. 本研究的目的是分析不同国家腐败和审计质量的关係, 并对理论分析提供实证支持。经济学家发现腐败严重会影响经济成长, 但很少研究腐败严重对企业行为的影响,我们研究腐败与企业审计质量,和投资回报的关係弥补这一空白。

690213.label: Realisation of objectives
690213.value: 1.We present a simple model of insiders who have the power to expropriate outsider shareholders, with a corrupted official who demand a portion of the proceeds from investment and an independent auditor who can detect diversion with some probability. Our theoretical model predicts that insiders’ incentives to divert resources increase with the level of corporation and that the value of audit increases with the level of corruption. 2.Our empirical results from audit fee data of 30 countries during period from 1992-2012 are consistent with the theoretical predictions. The results show that corruption has a negative relation with financial development but audit fees have a positive relation with financial development. We also find that the level of corruption has a positive relation the value of audit measured using an accounting-based valuation model

690213.value: Our empirical research based on corporate audit fees from 30 countries finds that corruption has a negative effect on equity value, and independent audit has a positive effect on equity value by deterring insiders’ diversion. Overall, the results suggest that government corruption and independent audit have opposite effects on equity value and that auditing plays a more important disciplining role in countries with higher levels of corruption.

690513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
690513.value: The ongoing crisis has made the use of standard macroeconomic tools in developed economies such as fiscal and monetary policy more challenging. A consensus formed during the "Great Moderation" period (1984-2007) that predictable adjustments in money market interest rates could reliably smooth business cycle shocks. In open economies, stabilizing interest rate adjustments also lead to stabilizing exchange rate movements. When an economy weakens, it might cut interest rates to stimulate domestic demand; falling interest leads to currency depreciation which also stimulates external demand. The severe nature of the events of the last half decade highlighted some shortcomings in this approach. First, the persistent economic decline has pushed optimal interest rates below the possible zero limit in many economies and near zero in most. Second, the crisis exposed asymmetries within the European Monetary Union with peripheral countries in Southern Europe having worse conditions than the core. In this environment, exchange rate flexibility might be destabilizing. When nominal interest rates are at the zero bound, real interest rates will be determined by deflationary expectations. Greater disinflation in an economy more severely impacted by a business cycle shock raises real interest rates, which leads to a currency appreciation, making the economy less competitive. In such an environment, a common currency union can offer greater macroeconomic stability We propose constructing a model incorporating the latest developments in macroeconomic theory to study the impact of these issues on macroeconomic policy in currency areas (potential and otherwise) such as the Eurozone. We will develop alternative macroeconomic policies which can aid stabilization in the time of crises. First, we consider how economies outside of a currency union (like Britain or Sweden) might construct monetary policies designed to avoid destabilizing appreciations when interest rates reach zero. The key involves committing to low interest rates in post-crisis periods. Expectations of low future interest rates can weaken exchange rates even absent current exchange rate adjustment. Second, we consider how economies inside a currency union might construct fiscal policies to stabilize the economy. We show that for a currency area there is a separation between the optimal aggregate level of government spending and the regional dispersion of spending. Total spending plans are identical regardless of the importance of trade within a currency area or the degree of asymmetry in business cycle severity shocks. However, the allocation of spending within the region can be adjusted to smooth business cycles within a currency union. 宏观经济持续危机等发达经济体的财政政策和货币政策更具挑战性的标准的宏观经济调控工具的使用。大缓和“时期（ 1984-2007年） ，货币市场利率在可预见的调整，可以可靠地平滑商业周期的冲击过程中形成的一个共识。在开放的经济体系，稳定利率的调整也导致稳定汇率的变动。当经济疲软时，它可能下调利率，以刺激国内需求，利率下降导致货币贬值，这也刺激外部需求。 在过去十年半的事件的严重性质，强调在这种方法中的一些不足之处。首先，经济持续下滑已推最优利率低于零可能限制在许多经济体和最非常接近零。其次，这场危机已经暴露出一些不对称，欧洲货币联盟内有更糟糕的条件比核心与周边国家在欧洲南部。在这样的环境下，汇率的灵活性可能会导致不稳定。当名义利率于零界，实际利率将由通缩预期。更大的通货紧缩的经济商业周期冲击更严重的影响，提高实际利率，从而导致一国货币升值，这使得经济竞争力较弱。在这样的环境中，一个货币联盟，可以提供更好的宏观经济稳定 我们建议使用一个模型，它采用了最新的宏观经济理论的发展潜力和其他）货币区（如欧元区的宏观经济政策研究这些问题的影响。我们将开发一些替代性的宏观经济政策，这可以帮助稳定在严重危机的时候。 首先，我们认为经济货币联盟以外的（如英国和瑞典）可能兴建的货币政策，避免不稳定增值，当利率达到零。低利率承诺的关键是在危机结束后的时期。未来低利率的预期减弱甚至缺席当前汇率调整汇率。 其次，我们考虑如何可能构建一个货币联盟内的经济财政政策，以稳定经济。我们可以证明，货币区之间的最佳总政府支出水平和区域分散的消费是一种分离。总开支的计划是一样的，不管货币区域内的国际贸易的重要性，或在商业周期的严重冲击不对称的程度。然而，区域内消费的分配进行调整，以平滑业务周期，在一个货币联盟内。

690513.label: Realisation of objectives
690513.value: To understand the achievements of the project, we begin with the initial context. This project continued a research agenda developed by the principal investigators over the last half decade responding to contemporary events in monetary policy and the business cycle environment. Beginning in 2010, the PI’s developed a two country sticky price model in order to study the open economy implications of the constraint on the monetary policy of the zero lower bound on policy interest rates. Prior to the global financial crisis, it was thought that interest targeting monetary policy could achieve first best outcomes for business cycle stabilization. However, in the context of a lower bound on nominal interest rates, it may be necessary to explore the use of alternate policy instruments in order to achieve second best outcomes. This project set out to explore the use of some of these instruments with a focus on the current situation of the Eurozone. From 2012, the European Central Bank followed the U.S. Federal Reserve and the Bank of Japan toward the zero lower bound. The European economies face a particularly interesting issue. The core countries of the Eurozone (e.g. Germany, France, etc.) have tended to have had milder disinflationary experiences than periphery countries (e.g. Italy, Spain). The particular issue facing the Eurozone, regional demand asymmetries, was one our model was well set up to study. This model emphasized that when countries had some home bias in trade, demand shocks concentrated in a single region could lead to disparate regional business cycle conditions. Preliminary work allowed us to solve the model in the case of a currency union. This allowed us to target two objectives. 1. Construct a model which allows the analysis of commitment to interest rate differentials to manage the terms of trade in a potential currency area. A key finding of our previous work was that exchange rates move in a perverse destabilizing direction at the zero lower bound. A key assumption of this finding was that monetary policy authorities lacked any commitment to future policy interest rates. In our proposal, we conjectured about what would happen if central banks were able to keep policy interest rates relatively low in the worst affected countries after the globe emerges from the liquidity trap, they could manage exchange rates not to move perversely during the crisis. Thus, we set out to explore the impact of commitment on relative interest rate differentials across countries. In our preliminary work developing the second part, we discovered that a currency union does actually act as a commitment device which commits to keeping real interest rates relatively low in the worst affected countries after the globe emerges from the liquidity trap. It made sense to combine projects. We built a model to compare a currency union with a flexible exchange rate economy in which central banks could use interest differentials as a commitment device. A model with a currency union or more plausible commitment policies required numerical solution methods. Efforts involved comparing welfare under three scenarios: flexible exchange rates under discretion; a currency union; and flexible exchange rates under commitment to interest differentials. Our results find that a currency union is welfare superior to flexible exchange rates under discretion, but inferior to flexible exchange rates under forward guidance about interest differentials. A paper to report this result: “Exchange Rate Flexibility at the Zero Lower Bound, “constructed for the project. This was accepted for publication at the Journal of International Economics, the leading publication in international economics. 2. Construct a model which allows the analysis of dynamic fiscal multipliers in a currency union and evaluate welfare effects of fiscal policies Previous work we had done constructed fiscal multipliers at the zero lower bound under flexible exchange rates. In this part of the project, we set out to construct multipliers in our model of a currency union. Shortly, following our CERG application some prominent authors published work similar to our objective, so we decided to focus are results on identifying how the impact of government spending on output (the multiplier) was impacted by the degree of home bias, a key element of our modelling strategy. As noted previously, the model of a currency union is dynamic, because the real exchange rate will act as a slowly adjusting state variable. This creates a challenge; much of the initial work in implementing the project went to deriving analytical results in a discrete time framework. We have been able to show that the fiscal spillovers in a currency union depend both on the macroeconomic state but also the openness to trade. We find that, at least in the short-run, the cross-country spillovers in a currency union are positive at the zero lower bound, but they will get smaller as home bias becomes more severe. This allows us to understand the policy problem of currency union members in setting policy. We then turn to evaluating optimal cooperative fiscal policy in a currency union at the zero lower bound. We are able to derive the conditions analytically. However, the dynamic nature of the currency union requires a numerical solution. Fiscal policy in this situation is interesting because we show that policy makers face potentially contradictory incentives. Policymakers should use fiscal policy to address a negative aggregate output gap for the union. However, fiscal policy should also try to narrow gaps between regions of the currency union. In an asymmetric contraction, the most badly affected region should always have a fiscal expansion. A less badly affected region (like the core countries of the Eurozone) may have a fiscal expansion or contraction depending on circumstances. However, if core country fiscal policy is the only instrument, it should be expansionary. This paper is accepted for presentation at the East Asian Econometric Society meetings of June 2017.

Main research findings Cross-country multipliers are smaller when home bias is larger. Optimal fiscal policy in a liquidity trap may be expansionary in both regions, or a combination of expansionary and contractionary, particularly when home bias is high. Optimal fiscal policy for a single country is always likely to be expansionary when one region is constrained.
