690513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
690513.value: Since 2012, the European Union has faced a constraint on using monetary policy to implement business cycle stabilization. This project has constructed a macroeconomic model to study the role that the Euro has played in this situation. We find that, as bad as things might be, the single currency area has prevented deflation in the periphery from Europe supporting a vicious cycle that reduced spending in those areas. If Euro countries had flexible exchange rates with each other, joint monetary policy institutions would need to be constructed to avoid a deflationary trap. We also ask whether an expansion in government spending in the healthier regions of the Eurozone (such as Germany) might be suitable. We find this would be questionable unless budget constraints restrict the worse of countries from implementing their own expansion. In such a case, fiscal expansion should be considered.

690713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
690713.value: Consumers’ welfare largely depends on the soundness of their financial decisions (Duclos et al. 2012). Accordingly, this research program proposes to investigate investment behavior and financial risk-taking. More specifically, we plan to examine the process by which investors encode and process financial information (e.g., performance graphs) to predict future stock prices and invest accordingly. The method used most commonly by financial-services providers (e.g., banks, brokers) to display stock performance over time is graphs (Raghubir 2010). We ask whether and, if so, how visual biases in data interpretation impact investment behavior? Relatedly, which forms of information display produce the most/fewest biases among investors? Our research plans to uncover when, how, and why graphical representation of financial information biases risk estimates, price predictions, and ultimately investment decisions. To this effect, we found in a series of preliminary experiments that the last trading days of a stock bear a disproportionally (and unduly) high importance. To document this anchoring bias, we presented participants the stock prices (in a graph spanning the previous 30 days) of various companies before asking them to (i) predict the next day’s stock price and (ii) invest money in (i.e., buy stock from) these companies. Unbeknownst to participants, the stock prices presented to them were in fact constructed strategically so as to follow precise characteristics (e.g., constant variance, skewness, kurtosis). Most importantly, these stock prices were randomly distributed over time so that no upward or downward trend could be identified overall. Despite the randomness of the stock-price distribution, we found a systematic bias in participants’ predictions and investment decisions. Specifically, if the last trading day followed an upward (vs. downward) trajectory, participants anticipated an even higher (vs. lower) price the next day and decided to invest more (vs. less) accordingly. The average investment asymmetry between groups was of 150%. Using peak-and-end theory and eye-tracking technology, we plan to explain this bias and offer corrective solutions. This research proposal draws on the respective strengths of both investigators. The PI specializes in human decision-making (e.g., prosocial behavior, financial risk-taking) and cross-cultural psychology. The Co-I is a pioneer in the development of eye-tracking methodology and is considered a worldwide authority on the matter. 消費者的福利很大程度上取決於有效的財務決策（Duclos et al. 2012 ） 。因此，這項研究計劃旨在研究投資行為和承擔財務風險的行為。更具體地說，我們計劃檢驗投資者如何通過編輯和處理財務信息（如股票圖表）來預測未來的股票價格和進行相應的投資。 金融服務提供商（如銀行，券商）最常使用圖表來展示隨著時間推移的股票表現（ Raghubir 2010） 。我們想了解在閱讀由圖形表達的財務信息的時候，由視覺效果導致的偏見會不會，以及如何影響投資行為。比如，哪種圖形會導致最多/最少的投資者非理性行為。我們的研究計劃試圖揭示何時，如何，以及為什麼由圖形表達的財務信息會導致投資者的偏見，包括風險估計，價格預測，以及最終的投資決策。 關於這個問題，我們進行了一系列初步的實驗。我們發現，最後一個交易日的股票表現得到投資者不成比例的過分重視。為了觀測這個“錨定偏見(anchoring bias)”，我們用圖表向實驗的參與者展示了很多公司跨越過去30天的股票價格 。之後，我們請實驗參與者（一） 預測這些公司下一日的股價，和（二）決定投入多少資金從這些公司購買股票。 不知情的參與者以為看到的是公司真實的股票價格圖。 實際上這些圖是研究人員特別繪製的，以滿足某些精確的特點（例如，恆定的方差、偏度、峰度） 。最重要的是，我們讓股票價格隨著時間的推移隨機分佈，因此每只股票整體上並不存在向上或向下的趨勢。 儘管股票價格實際上是隨機分佈的，我們發現實驗參與者的預測和投資決策存在著系統性的偏見。具體來說，如果最後一個交易日呈現向上（向下）的圖形軌跡，參與者預期下一日的股價會更高（更低）。相應的，參與者決定投入更多（更少）的資金來購買該股票。前者平均比後者多投入150%的資金購買股票 。使用“峰值－終點（peak-and-end）”理論和眼球追踪（eye-tracking）技術，我們計劃解釋這種非理性的投資者偏見，並提供一些方案來幫助投資者糾正這種偏見。 這項研究計劃借鑒了兩位研究人各自的學術優勢。主要研究者專攻人類的決策行為（例如，親社會行為，財務風險承擔行為）和跨文化心理學。合作者是眼球追踪方法領域的先驅，被認為是全球範圍內對此技術的權威。

690713.label: Major findings and research outcome
690713.value: Consumers’ welfare largely depends on the soundness of their financial decisions. To this effect, the present research examines how people process graphical displays of financial information (e.g., stock-prices) to forecast future trends and invest accordingly. In essence, we ask whether and how visual biases in data interpretation impact financial decision-making and risk-taking. Five experiments find that the last trading day(s) of a stock bear a disproportionately (and unduly) high importance on investment behavior, a phenomenon we coin end-anchoring. Specifically, a stock-price closing upward (downward) fosters upward (downward) forecasts for tomorrow and, accordingly, more (less) investing in the present. Substantial investment asymmetries (up to 75%) emerge even as stock-price distributions were generated randomly to simulate times when the market conjuncture is hesitant and no real upward or downward trend can be identified. Allying experimental manipulations to eye-tracking technology, the present research begins to explore the underpinnings of end-anchoring.

690713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
690713.value: Our application requested funds in the amount of HK$ 1.4M but we were granted only 1/3 of this sum (i.e., about HK$ 0.5M). Since nearly all of our funding was consumed by January 2015, we weren’t able to complete our second goal. Future research might thus examine whether and how (i) financial expertise and (ii) cultural orientation moderate investors’ anchoring bias. To do so, running the studies described at length in our original proposal might be useful.

690713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
690713.value: This research examined how investors process visual information to forecast asset-value and invest accordingly. We theorized that certain datapoints on a graph are more likely to draw attention and, in turn, impair financial decision-making. To this effect, five studies allying experimental manipulations to eye-tracking technology showed that a stock-price closing upward (downward) fosters upward (downward) forecasts for tomorrow and, accordingly, more (less) investing in the present. As noted earlier, our stock-price distributions were generated randomly to simulate times when the conjuncture in real-world markets is hesitant (i.e., trendless). In such times, recent price-movements are no more diagnostic than earlier ones. Yet, we find they do bias decision-making and, ultimately, can be quite harmful for investors. Given our ever-increasing reliance on graphs to convey financial information, understanding how visual biases in data interpretation (like end-anchoring) impact investment behavior seems important. It will help (i) financial-services providers refine their presentation of performance data; (ii) lay and professional investors free themselves from detrimental heuristics; and (iii) policymakers organize the dissemination of financial information so as to avoid panics in the market. Mirroring the rules governing product packaging, the present findings may help inform (and perhaps regulate) communications around financial products.

690913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
690913.value: The compromise effect refers to one type of context-dependent choice behavior whereby an option can become relatively more attractive in a choice set when it is an intermediate option than in a choice set when it is an extreme option. It has been pervasively observed in many domains and product categories, and can provide important practical implications for marketing strategies (e.g., new product introduction, positioning, product line design, promotion, sales tactics, and competitive strategies). The planned research tackles a few basic issues regarding how to explain the mechanism underlying the compromise effect. Our research objective is to present a rational explanation for this behavioral phenomenon, and to test it against other explanations by running a series of experiments. Our proposed explanation rests on a two-stage sequential decision process under which decision makers can endogenously construct their preferences through costly deliberation. That is, the decision makers can decide whether to incur a deliberation cost in order to reflect on and thus to know more about the relative utilities of the options in a choice set, and then subsequently decide which option to choose conditional on the outcome of the first-stage deliberation. It follows that the deliberation decision can be context dependent, and, as a result, so is the choice behavior. We show that the compromise effect can then arise, even with a context-free utility structure and the rationality assumption. The proposed two-stage sequential decision process can yield unique hypotheses that can be empirically tested. In particular, we predict that deliberation can mediate, as well as moderate, the compromise effect. This leads us to test our proposed explanation using lab experiments in which deliberation can be readily observed/measured. Moreover, we also plan to experimentally test another explanation for the compromise effect that is based on consumers making rational inference from the choice sets. Besides its theoretical contribution, the planned research can also be beneficial for practitioners. In particular, the planned research can improve our understanding about how and when the compromise effect may arise, and thus can shed light not only on how the effect can be exploited by firms, but also on how it can be fostered (e.g., through information provision) or impeded (e.g., under time pressure). 折中效应是受情景影响的选择行为（context-dependent behavior）中的一种，指某个中间选项被选择的可能性要大于当它是极端选项时候的可能性。这个现象广泛存在于很多产品种类中，能给很多营销战略问题带来很重要的实际指导意义(比如，新产品推出，产品定位，产品线设计，促销，销售技巧，竞争性战略等)。 我们计划研究关于折中效应的几个基本问题，着重于解释其内在机制。我们的研究目的在于对此现象提出一个理性的解释，并且用实验的方法来对我们的解释以及其它的解释进行检验。我们提出的解释的关键所在，是一个两阶段的决策过程，描述决策者的偏好如何受到在决策过程中的思考而影响。具体的说，决策者首先会决定是否要投入足够的时间来思考，以此决定对不同的选项的相对效用的了解程度，然后再在此基础上做出应该选择哪个选项的决策。因为这个关于思考多少的问题本身是一个决策，会受到情景的影响，所以最终的选择行为也会受到情景影响。我们据此能证明，折中效应可能会因此而出现，尽管在效用本身并不随情景而变化并且决策是完全理性的情况下。 基于这个两阶段的决策过程，我们得出了几个可供实证检验的理论结果。具体而言，思考这个决策变量可能会对折中效应有中介和调节作用。我们可以在实验环境中轻易的观察或测量到思考的时间，这使得我们可以对我们提出的解释进行实证检验。折中效应也有另外一个基于决策者从选项组中直接获得信息的解释，我们也计划对此进行实验检验。 除了理论方面的贡献，我们的研究也对实践有指导意义。具体而言，我们的研究可以帮助理解折中效应为何以及在什么情况下会发生，这可以指导如何利用此效应为公司利益服务，并且指导如何促使（比如通过信息提供）或者阻止（比如减少决策的时间）此效应的发生。

690913.label: Realisation of objectives
690913.value: First, to provide a rational explanation for the compromise effect, I developed a two-stage decision making theory of contextual deliberation that endogenizes the dependence of preferences on choice context. I show and explicate theoretically why the compromise effect may endogenously emerge in two types of experiment designs: one in which the middle option does not change, and another one in which it varies, across choice sets. I have finished all the analysis and reported the results in a paper titled “Contextual Deliberation and Preference Construction.” Second, to investigate the empirical validity of the proposed explanation, we conducted a series of laboratory experiments with more than one thousand subjects. We have completed all the data analysis, and obtained strong support for the main predictions of the theoretical model. We reported the results in a paper titled “Testing the Role of Contextual Deliberation in the Compromise Effect” and have gone through several rounds of polishing.

690913.label: Major findings and research outcome
690913.value: In the paper titled “Contextual Deliberation and Preference Construction,” I develop the theory of contextual deliberation as a potential explanation for behavioral phenomena of preference construction. I show that, when preference ordering in a choice set is ex ante unknown and state dependent, decision makers can engage in information acquisition activities (i.e., deliberation) before choice to improve knowledge about the state-dependent preference ordering. I find that choice context can influence ex post preference ordering through affecting the incentive to deliberate. Consequently, contextual deliberation may lead to preference construction and give rise to seemingly irrational behavioral phenomena such as the compromise effect. I also demonstrate that the theory of contextual deliberation can generate predictions that can be empirically tested to identify from other alternative explanations. This paper has been published at the journal Management Science. In the paper titled “Testing the Role of Contextual Deliberation in the Compromise Effect,” we report the results in a series of laboratory experiments to rigorously test the empirical validity of the theory of the contextual deliberation in explaining the compromise effect. We develop novel predictions that would necessarily arise under the premise that the compromise effect is caused by contextual deliberation. We then perform falsification tests to examine whether these predictions can be consistent with empirical data. We obtain robust results that do not allow us to refute the hypothesis that contextual deliberation can be a plausible explanation for the compromise effect. Specifically, we show that the compromise effect can be positively mediated by response time, cannot be mitigated by context information, but can be moderated by manipulating the level of deliberation (i.e., time pressure, preference articulation, task order). These findings are consistent with the predictions of the theory of contextual deliberation. The paper is currently submitted to a top journal for review.

690913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
690913.value: The theory of contextual deliberation can be extended to accommodate other types of preference construction. For example, different preference elicitation methods may endogenously influence decision makers’ incentive to deliberate, and thus may play an important role in the preference construction process. This can then provide a rational explanation for various seemingly disparate preference reversals. Similarly, other factors such as mood or decision framing may indirectly influence choice behavior through affecting the cost/effectiveness of deliberation. In addition, the theory of contextual deliberation can be expanded to account for paradoxes of risk preferences. Future research can investigate how the theory of contextual deliberation can predict the emergence of the compromise effect, i.e., the conditions under which it can be turned on and off. It would also be challenging but valuable to construct additional tests to experimentally identify the theory of contextual deliberation from other potential explanations of the compromise effect. More sophisticated techniques (e.g., eye tracking and neuroimaging tools) can be employed to measure deliberation and present complemental or supplemental tests for the theoretical predictions. Another fruitful area for future research is to construct structural empirical models to recover the cost of deliberation and improve our understanding and prediction for choice behavior.

690913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
690913.value: Classical economic theories assume that choices are rational. This implies that people’s choice behavior must obey some properties. If these properties are violated, the rationality assumption will be refuted and many economic theories will be invalidated. Unfortunately, numerous empirical studies accumulate to demonstrate violations of the properties of rational choice. One of the most cited examples is the compromise effect, referring to the finding that an option can be more likely to be chosen when it is in the middle of some physical attribute space (e.g., quality, price) relative to other options in the choice set In this research we provide a new perspective to reconcile the empirically observed compromise effect with the rationality assumption. We show both theoretically and experimentally that the compromise effect may emerge even when people are making optimal choices. Therefore, this research demonstrates that behavioral anomalies should not necessarily be viewed as arising from irrational decision making. It also suggests that the rationality assumption in classical economic theories should not be abandoned completely, but should be refined to account for the process of how preferences are constructed. In addition, this new theory can provide a parsimonious framework to account for many other puzzling behavioral anomalies.

691113.value: To theoretically and empirically analyze firms’ incentives to adopt strategic contracts in the multi-task agency framework: strategic contracts not only help the contracting parties to extract more rent from entrants, but also alleviate multi-task problems by reducing agents’ outside option. These results can also provide policy implications on whether strategic contracts should be allowed. These results can also provide policy implications on whether strategic contracts should be allowed.

691113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
691113.value: Contract can be used as a strategic tool against third parties such as entrants. Strategic contracts are widely adopted in various activities such as sales, acquisitions, and research and development (R&D) cooperation. There have been substantial interests in strategic contracts in economics. However, most of the existing studies are theoretical. This proposed research intends to examine firms’ incentives to adopt strategic contracts, using both theoretical and empirical analysis. The results will lead to empirical evidence and implications for contract design, as well as policy implications. This project will include two parts. The first part will focus on the adoption of strategic contract clauses such as most-favored-customer, rights of first refusal, rights of first offer, etc., in R&D agreements between clients and research agents. These clauses would give priority to contracting clients when other firms compete for purchasing R&D discoveries. I will first formulate an agency model where an agent can allocate time/effort between one R&D activity specified by the contract with a client, and another non-contracted R&D activity. There may be another firm as a potential entrant competing for the non-contracted R&D discoveries. I expect to show that strategic contracts not only help the contracting parties to extract more benefit from the entrant, but also motivate the agent to take effort in the contracted R&D activity by reducing the agent’s outside option from the non-contracted R&D activity. These effects will imply that strategic contracts are more likely adopted when there is larger entry threat. Based on these predictions, I will analyze data from a rich set of bio-tech R&D agreements between pharmaceutical firms and bio-tech agents in the US. The project will provide empirical evidence about the impact of entry threat and agents’ characteristics on the adoption of strategic contracts. The results will also shed light on policy discussions on whether strategic contracts should be allowed and implemented by courts. The second part will extend the above theoretical and empirical analysis to address the relationship between strategic contract clauses and unconditional termination rights which allow clients to terminate R&D projects. If the R&D agreement between a client and an agent includes unconditional termination rights, it will motivate the agent to take effort in the contracted R&D activity. Correspondingly, the potential benefit of including strategic clauses is reduced. Therefore, I expect to find empirical evidence on the substitution between strategic clauses and termination rights in contract design.

691113.label: Realisation of objectives
691113.value: All the project objectives have been realized and the results have been included in a research paper, currently under the third round review at the International Journal of Industrial Organization (IJIO). The first two objectives are closely related, and therefore we will explain the two together. (1) The first and second objectives: Strategic rights are contract clauses used as strategic tools against entrants. Research and development (R&D) agreements between clients and agents often contain strategic rights, such as most-favored-licensee, right of first refusal, right of first offer, etc. These rights provide some advantage to clients against entrants in their competition for the licensing of non-contracted discoveries made by agents. Although there is a large theoretical literature on strategic contracts, formal analysis has seldom been performed on how strategic contracts affect agents’ R&D incentives, and related empirical studies have been very limited. We first reviewed in detail the relevant literature and read many R&D agreements. Based on the deeper understanding gained from the literature and the data, in the paper, we construct a theoretical agency model with entry threat and multi-task problems: after a client devotes investments and hires an agent to conduct an R&D project, the agent can allocate effort to either the contracted project or other non-contracted R&D activities; and a potential entrant may compete for the license of non-contracted discoveries. Different from most studies in the literature, our model considers the agent’s R&D effort and uses the mechanism design approach. The model and the theoretical analysis have been revised several times after we received comments from conference attendants, the Editor of IJIO, and the referees. Within this framework, we illustrate the effects of strategic rights by analyzing the right of first refusal, and then, more generally, characterize the optimal strategic contract for the client. The final analysis has successfully captured firms’ incentives to adopt strategic rights in R&D agreements. In particular, it is shown that, compared to standard auctions, strategic rights not only help the contracting parties extract more rent from the entrant, but also enhance the agent’s incentives to put effort into the contracted project. Both effects become stronger when there is a higher likelihood of entry. Our theoretical analysis suggests that firms have greater incentives to adopt strategic rights when potential entry threat is larger. To empirically identify firms’ incentives in adopting strategic rights and the impact of entry threat, we use the Thomas Reuters Recap Dataset (Recap), which contains a full list of all R&D alliance deals between pharmaceutical firms and bio-tech agents during 1974-2009. Within the above list, Recap provides contract details for 1703 R&D agreements, which we use for the empirical analysis. As Recap only provides the original agreements but does not summarize most of the contract terms, we read through entire agreements to identify the various strategic rights and other contract terms. After this data collection and refinement process, we construct a dummy variable for the strategic rights as the dependent variable. The construction of entry threat measures requires more innovative thinking. The typical approaches in the literature cannot be used, because the information on historical entry is not available. Additionally, we need to address potential entry threats at the disease level, given that R&D agreements normally target certain disease types. Thus, we construct indirect entry threat measures based on historical clinical trials of the same disease type, as well as historical R&D/marketing projects of the same disease type, by other pharmaceutical firms before a particular R&D agreement was signed. Besides this main independent variable on entry threat, we also control for timing effects, project characteristics (including stage as a measure of uncertainty level of the R&D project, project size, and equity link between clients and agents), and agent characteristics (such as the agent’s R&D experience, previous relationship with the client, and whether the agent is publicly listed at the time when the R&D agreement was signed). Using the above specifications, we have obtained empirical results that firms are more likely to include strategic rights in R&D agreements when potential entry threat is larger. This result is robust under various specifications and consistent with our theoretical predictions. In the final version of our paper, we also discuss potential endogeneity problems and conduct robustness analysis. In sum, our paper provides empirical evidence on the impact of entry threats and other characteristics on firms’ incentives in using strategic rights. The above theoretical and empirical analysis not only contributes to the academic literature on incomplete and strategic contracts, but also provides rich implications for firm strategies and government/court policies. In particular, the final version of the paper shows whether and how a firm should design strategic rights into R&D agreements, given potential entry threats and agency problems. As policy implications, the results suggest that strategic rights may enhance social welfare by mitigating agency problems and encouraging clients to make R&D investments. (2) The third objective: This project also attempted to answer an important but understudied question: how do different contract clauses interact? To date, only a few studies in the literature have shown complementarity among certain contract terms. Our analysis provides both theoretical analysis and empirical evidence of a possible substitution relationship between strategic rights and termination rights, the latter of which allow clients to terminate projects without cause. We first extend our theoretical model by allowing the client and the agent to include a termination right in their R&D agreement. After the agent allocates his effort between the contracted project and non-contracted activities, the client may observe a signal about the progress of the contracted project and then decide whether to exercise the termination right, if it has been included in the agreement. We show that this termination right can mitigate the agency problems and motivate the agent to devote effort to the contracted projects. As we have shown earlier, strategic rights can also address the agency problems. Therefore, intuitively, strategic rights and termination rights can be substitutes in contract design. Our theoretical result confirms this intuition. We also characterize conditions under which firms use only strategic rights and conditions under which firms only use termination rights. We have also conducted empirical analysis for the above substitution relationship between strategic rights and termination rights. In the Recap dataset, all agreements grant clients termination rights, some with verifiable conditions and others without cause. Termination rights without cause provide stronger incentives for agents to devote effort than other termination rights. Thus, we construct a dummy variable, “Termination,” to reflect whether a R&D agreement includes termination rights without cause. To capture the possibility that the uncertainty level of R&D projects may affect the relationship between strategic rights and terminations rights, we also control for one interaction term, “Termination*stage.” Under various specifications, we have obtained empirical evidence that strategic rights and termination rights are substitutes, consistent with our theoretical predictions. Additionally, it is shown that, for R&D projects associated with the earlier stages of drug development, the substitution between termination rights and strategic rights becomes stronger.

691113.label: Major findings and research outcome
691113.value: This project has generated both theoretical and empirical findings on the adoption of strategic rights in R&D agreements, as well as the relationship between strategic rights and termination rights. In the theoretical part, we have constructed a model with entry threat and agency problems: after a client devotes investments and hires an agent to conduct an R&D project, the agent can allocate effort to either the contracted project or other non-contracted R&D activities; and a potential entrant may compete for the license of non-contracted discoveries. We illustrate the effects of strategic rights by analyzing the right of first refusal, and then, using the mechanism design approach, characterize the optimal strategic contract for the client. It is shown that, compared to standard auctions, strategic rights not only help the contracting parties extract more rent from the entrant, but also enhance the agent’s incentives to exert effort in the contracted project. Both effects become stronger when there is a higher likelihood of entry. More importantly, it is shown that the contracting parties often use either strategic rights or termination rights, but not both. That is, strategic rights and termination rights tend to be substitutes. In the empirical part, using the Recap dataset about R&D agreements between pharmaceutical clients and bio-tech agents, we have identified various strategic rights and constructed measures of entry threats at disease level. We have found empirical evidence consistent with the theoretical analysis. In particular, strategic rights are more likely to be adopted when potential entry threats are larger. We also find evidence of substitution between strategic rights and termination rights. This substitution relationship is stronger in projects at earlier R&D stages. Additionally, we have created a nice summary of various contract terms besides strategic rights from all the R&D agreements that we have read, which can be useful for future research projects. The above findings have been included in a research paper “Agency and Strategic Contracts: Theory and Evidence from R&D Agreements in the Pharmaceutical Industry.” The paper was submitted to the International Journal of Industry Organization in Dec 2015. Then we received the first “revise and resubmit” invitation from the journal in Apr 2016, and the second “revise and resubmit” invitation in late Dec 2016. The paper has been revised and resubmitted to the journal. Now it is under the third round of review at the journal (please see part C).

691113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
691113.value: As mentioned above, all of the findings have been included in the attached paper, which is under the third round of review at the International Journal of Industry Organization (please see part C). There are a few potential directions for future research. First, when reading the R&D agreements, we identified many other contract terms besides strategic rights. This dataset allows us to investigate other aspects of contract design. For example, most of the R&D agreements in our dataset grant clients exclusive licenses of potential contracted discoveries, while some agreements are non-exclusive. Some exclusive agreements also contain conversion rights, which have not been studied in the literature before. We plan to examine the design of exclusive contracts in another project. Second, the effect of contracting arrangements on innovation outcomes is also an important but under-investigated area. We have obtained another dataset on the progress of some R&D projects in the pharmaceutical industry, which can be useful for investigating the impact of contract design on R&D progress.

691113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
691113.value: When clients hire agents to conduct R&D projects, agents may privately shift investments and effort to activities not specified in contracts, which can result in non-contracted discoveries. Entrants may compete for the licenses of non-contracted discoveries. R&D agreements often include strategic clauses, which bring some competitive advantage to clients against entrants. By examining the motivations for clients to use strategic clauses, this project provides valuable implications for business strategies and policy discussions. First, strategic contract clauses force entrants to make larger payments, and also motivate agents to put effort into contracted R&D projects. Greater entry threats strengthen both effects. Consistent with these theoretical predictions, we find empirical evidence from the pharmaceutical industry that firms are more likely to use strategic clauses when the chance of having entrants is larger. These findings imply that strategic clauses can increase welfare by solving agency problems. Second, this project investigates the relationship between strategic clauses and termination rights without cause, the latter of which allow clients to termination R&D projects. We show, both theoretically and empirically, that firms often use either strategic clauses or termination rights without cause, but not both. This finding provides useful implications for practical contract design.

691213.label: Major findings and research outcome
691213.value: We exploit a randomized experiment to shed light on an important effect of short selling on firms’ financial reporting practices. The SEC’s Regulation SHO included a pilot program in which every third stock in the Russell 3000 index ranked by trading volume within each exchange was designated as a pilot stock. From May 2, 2005 to August 6, 2007, pilot stocks were exempted from short-sale price tests, thus decreasing the cost of short selling and increasing the prospect of short selling among these stocks. The costs of short selling in nonpilot stocks remained unchanged until July 6, 2007. We find that pilot and nonpilot firms have similar levels of discretionary accruals before the announcement of the pilot program. Once the program begins, pilot firms’ discretionary accruals decrease substantially, only to revert to preprogram levels after the pilot program ends. These patterns are not explained by changes in these firms’ investment around the program, firms’ incentives to issue equity, or a general increase in the attention investors paid to the pilot firms. The effect of the pilot program on firms’ tendency to manage earnings is also robust to the use of two alternative measures of earnings management, namely, the likelihood of meeting or marginally beating earnings targets and the likelihood of being classified as a misstating firm based on the F-score of Dechow et al. (2011). A unique advantage of the pilot program is that it enables us to use pilot and nonpilot firms’ unconditional probabilities of fraud detection to infer differences in their conditional probabilities of detection. We find that, for financial misconduct that occurred before the announcement of the pilot program, pilot firms are more likely to be caught after the pilot program starts than nonpilot firms. Furthermore, as we sequentially include cases of fraud initiated after the pilot program begins, the unconditional likelihood that pilot firms are caught for financial misconduct converges monotonically toward that for nonpilot firms. Previous research shows that short selling both anticipates and accelerates the public discovery of financial misconduct. Our result is, however, the first to reveal that an increase in the prospect of short selling increases the detection of financial misconduct. Overall, our results indicate that the pilot program lowered the cost of short selling sufficiently to increase potential short sellers’ incentives to scrutinize pilot firms’ earnings reports and uncover misconduct, and that managers responded to the prospect of increased scrutiny by decreasing earnings management.

691213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
691213.value: Since the financial crisis in 2007-2008, numerous countries in the world have increased their regulation of short selling activities. It is thus interesting to examine whether these changes in the regulations have the unintended consequence in managers' earnings management choices through their effects on short sellers.

691213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
691213.value: Although short selling remains a controversial activity, our results uncover important external benefits from short selling activity. In particular, a decrease in the cost of short selling curbs managers’ willingness to manipulate earnings, increases the likelihood of fraud detection, and increases the informativeness of stock prices with respect to earnings. We thus demonstrate one channel through which trading in secondary markets has an impact on firms’ business decisions. Finally, by demonstrating important benefits from short selling activity, our paper has significant implication for the stock market regulators such as SEC and SFC.

691413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
691413.value: Corporate suppliers and customers are perhaps the most important contracting parties to a firm, and it is widely cited in accounting textbooks that suppliers and customers are important users of accounting information. However, there is only an extremely small body of research that has touched upon how suppliers and customers may use the information in a firm’s financial statements (Bowen et al. 1995; Raman and Shahrur 2012; Hui et al. 2012), Additionally, there is no evidence on how suppliers and customers may use the information in a firm’s voluntary disclosures. In this project, we study the empirical associations between the importance of corporate suppliers and customers and observable characteristics of firm’s financial reporting and voluntary disclosure practices. We infer from these empirical associations about the preferences of corporate suppliers and customers on the characteristics of financial reporting and voluntary disclosures as well as managers’ incentives to respond to these preferences. Specifically, we propose to examine the following two questions. First, we propose to investigate the association between the importance of corporate suppliers and customers and firms’ earnings manipulation to beat/meet earnings benchmarks. Prior studies suggest that some stakeholders use heuristic earnings benchmarks such as zero earnings, zero changes in earnings, or zero earnings surprises to judge firm performance (e.g. Burgstahler and Dichev 1997; Degeorge et al. 1999). Missing earnings benchmarks may be perceived by suppliers and customers as important signals of increased likelihood of a firm’s potential failure to meet its future trading obligations. Consequently, suppliers and customers may impose more stringent trading terms to protect themselves, or switch to transacting with the competitors. Prior studies suggest managers manipulating earnings to beat/meet earnings benchmarks to avoid disappointing shareholders and bondholders. We propose to examine whether firms manipulate earnings meet earnings benchmarks with the presence of important suppliers and customers. Second, we propose to examine the associations between the importance of suppliers and customer and voluntary disclosure decisions. Prior research argues that managers tend to voluntarily issue optimistically biased forecasts to maintain favorable share valuation when there is greater difficulty for investors to detect this bias (Rogers and Stocken 2005, Hui et al. 2010). If suppliers and customers concern about firms’ future performance, managers may thus have an incentive to issue optimistic forecasts to inflate the earnings expectations. We therefore propose to empirically examine whether the importance of suppliers and customers is associated with the optimism in management annual forecasts. 公司供應商和客戶也許是最重要合同夥伴。在會計教科書, 供應商和客戶是重要的會計信息使用者。然而，只有一個非常少數的研究觸及供應商和客戶如何使用公司的財務報表的信息 (Bowen et al. 1995; Raman and Shahrur 2012; Hui et al. 2012)。此外，還沒有證據顯示供應商和客戶如何使用一家公司的自願性信息披露。在這個項目中，我們研究關聯企業供應商和客戶對 公司的財務報告和披露行為特徵的重要性。我們推斷關聯企業供應商和客戶的喜好會影響有關企業財務報告和披露的特點，以及經理的激勵機制。具體來說，我們建議檢查以下兩個問題。 首先，我們建議調查供應商和客戶對關聯企業及企業的盈餘操縱的重要性。此前的研究表明，一些利益相關者使用盈利的指標，如零收益，收益的變化，盈利驚喜來判斷企業績效（Burgstahler and Dichev 1997; Degeorge et al. 1999)。供應商和客戶的可能視不滿足盈利基準為企業未來的義務的潛在故障的重要信號。因此，供應商和客戶實施更嚴格的貿易條款來保護自己，或切換到與競爭對手進行交易。此前的研究表明，經理操縱盈利滿足盈利基準，以避免令股東和債券持有人失望。我們建議檢查企業是否操縱盈餘達到盈利基準與重要的供應商和客戶的關係。 其次，我們建議檢查供應商和客戶的重要性和自願披露決策之間的關聯。此前的研究認為，管理者往往自願發出樂觀偏見的預測，以保持良好的股估值，特別是當投資者有困難檢測到這種偏差（Rogers and Stocken 2005, Hui et al. 2010） 。如果供應商和客戶的關注公司未來的表現，管理者可能發出樂觀的預測，誇大盈利預期。因此，我們建議檢驗供應商和客戶與年度樂觀預測的重要性。

691413.label: Realisation of objectives
691413.value: We are able to achieve the project objectives. For the objectives regarding accounting choices, we hand collected customer and supplier data and processed it for data analysis, conducted empirical tests and find evidence that supplier firms are more likely to beat and meet earnings targets if customers have significant claims in the firm. We also conducted tests using customer firm characteristics as measures of their bargaining power, and find evidence that supplier firm accruals are related to the customer firm characteristics. For objectives regarding voluntary disclosures, we conducted empirical tests and find evidence that supplier firm management forecast properties are related to customer firm importance. For objective regarding interactions of firm with its supply-chain counterparts, we conducted extensive tests on customer power and firm accounting performances, our findings strongly support the rent extraction hypothesis of customer power on supplier firms.

691413.label: Major findings and research outcome
691413.value: Our project finds that customer power has significant impact on firm operations. In the context of accounting choices, customer power affects firms' accounting policies, its tendency to beat targets and voluntary disclosure decisions. In the context of accounting performances, customer power results rent extraction that lowers firm reported profitability. Market also prices these effects accordingly. In particular, our project reconciles prior evidence on the effect of customer power by improving the empirical measures and estimation methods. To better understand the effects of major customers and narrow the gap between theoretical prediction and empirical evidence, our project takes a closer examination of the measures of customer power. Note that major customer concentration emphasized in prior studies captures only the degree to which supplier firms depends on their major customers (i.e., the proportion of a supplier’s sales made to its major customers). Another important, but overlooked aspect is the degree to which major customers depend on a supplier firm (i.e., the proportion of major customers’ total purchases from the supplier). Customer power (relative to that of the supplier firm) should increase with customer dependence but decrease with supplier dependence. Thus, a more powerful measure of customer power should combine both customer dependence and supplier dependence. Empirically, we first follow prior studies and use major customer concentration (CC) to capture customer dependence, which is defined as the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI) of a supplier’s sales to its major customers. Following this approach, we construct supplier concentration to capture supplier dependence, which is defined as the HHI of major customers’ aggregate purchases from the supplier firm. The inverse of supplier dependence, which we refer to as supplier dispersion (SD), should increase with customer power. Customer concentration (CC) and supplier dispersion (SD) allows us to create a comprehensive measure of customer power that accounts for both customer and supplier concentrations, which is the multiplicative term of CC and SD. This composite measure is appealing because transaction volume is considered as the important determinant of power. In summary, our project contributes to the literature by documenting that the first-order effect of customer power on supplier firms’ accounting in a cross-section setting. We demonstrate the importance of customer claims in a firm's accounting and disclosure decisions. We are also able to reconcile the rent extraction from customer power that the economic theory predicts and the existence of supply-chain collaboration. Methodologically, our study develops a comprehensive measure of customer power and shows that truncating the dependent variables in a financial statement analysis may lead to biased inferences.

691413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
691413.value: Motivated by recent studies, our project focuses on the empirical association between customer power and supplier firm accounting in cross-section. Similar to prior work, we do not question, for instance, why some firms have more powerful customers; that said, our results do provide some indirect evidence that speaks to this issue. Future studies may seek exogenous events and/or more powerful empirical settings to study the related question. Our project is also silent on whether and how supplier firms benefit (e.g. by experiencing significant growth) when having major and powerful customers. For instance, our study doesn't address the consequence of customer power on the supplier firm operation in a multiple period setting, in which case the firm's own power may eventually countervails their customers’ power. We leave the time-series analysis of industry dynamics on supplier-customer relationships to future research.

691413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
691413.value: Theory and anecdotal evidence suggest that customer power should affect firms' accounting choices and its reported performances. Our project falls into two parts. In the first part, we show a firm's tendency to manipulate its earnings to beat/meet earnings targets is associated with the presence of powerful suppliers or customers. We also find evidence consistent with the presence of powerful suppliers and customers and the biases in voluntary management earnings forecasts. In the second part, we test the economic theories that powerful customers lower firms' profitability because customer power allows rent extraction. Recent studies find that major customer concentration is positively associated with supplier firms’ profitability, suggesting that customer power primarily facilitates supply-chain collaboration. We show that measures of major customer power are negatively associated with a supplier firm’s profitability, stock returns, and operating cash flows, but positively associated with a supplier firm’s accruals (i.e., less efficient working capital management). These results strongly support the rent extraction hypothesis of customer power on supplier firms.

691613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
691613.value: Consumer information search is an important topic to practitioners and academics since the search limits the products or services consumers can choose from and hence has an implication on consumer demand. Although the theoretical and behavioral research on consumer search abounds, the empirical research on this topic using a secondary data set has been relatively muted mainly due to the data limitation: it is very challenging, if not impossible, to observe the search behaviors of consumers. However, the internet clickstream data offer new research opportunities since they allow researchers to actually observe consumer search behaviors in a great detail. For this project, we have secured a very detailed, individual-level clickstream data from a major market research company in the US. With such a data set at our disposal, the overall goal in this project is to enhance our general understanding of consumer online search behaviors in a durable goods category. To that end, we first plan to study the nature of associations between consumer choice and search as well as to investigate the efficacy of consumer search as a predictor for consumer choice. In addition, we plan to investigate any systematic differences, if any, between searches that result in choice and that do not. The second objective of the project is to develop a more realistic and less abstract econometric model of consumer search and choice. The limited data set in the past often forced empirical researchers to adopt rather strong assumptions in the econometric models. Its serious implication may be that many important economic primitives such as consumer utility and search costs may have been identified in part by the functional model form. The detailed nature of our data may allow us to relax such assumptions and to achieve an empirical model that is more true to consumer behaviors. Lastly, once we have an empirical model of search and choice, we can discuss with a great confidence the implications of search and demand for marketing strategy. Overall, the outcome of this project will enhance our general understanding on consumer information search and help answer questions that marketers and policy makers face in many online shopping environments. In addition, from the substantive perspective, a greater understanding of consumer search process will help manufacturers devise better communication and distribution strategies as a part of their marketing efforts. 无论对理论研究者还是实际操作者而言, 消费者信息搜寻都是一个重要的课题. 因为搜寻限制了消费者可选择的产品或服务范围,从而会影响消费者需求. 虽然文献中已有大量关于消费者信息搜寻的理论研究和消费者行为学的研究,但是由于实际数据中很难观察到消费者的搜寻行为, 基于二手数据的实证研究却少之又少．然而，互联网点击流数据使得研究者可以观察到大量详细的消费者搜寻数据，从而提供了新的研究机会． 为了这个项目，我们从美国一家主流市场调研公司取得了非常详尽的个体层面的点击流数据．我们的目标是分析这些数据，而后通过这个项目来提高人们有关消费者对耐用品网络信息搜寻行为的整体了解．为了达到这个目标，首先，我们计划研究消费者选择和搜寻的本质联系，以及探讨通过消费者搜寻行为来预测消费者选择行为的有效性．其次，我们将研究那些最终导致了实际选择的搜寻行为和没有导致实际选择的搜寻行为之间是否存在系统性差异． 这个项目的另一个目标是建立一个研究消费者搜寻和选择行为的，更接近现实的，不那么抽象的计量经济模型．以往由于数据的局限性，实证研究者往往不得不在计量经济模型里采用很强的假设．这就意味着很多重要的经济原语，如消费者效用和搜寻成本，在函数形式的模型里可能只能被部分识别．然而，我们所拥有数据的详尽程度使我们能够放宽这些假设，从而使实证研究的模型更真实地反映消费者行为．最后，一旦建立好消费者搜寻和选择的模型，我们方可据此探讨消费者搜寻和需求对市场战略的意义．总的来说，这个项目的成果可以提高我们对消费者信息搜寻行为的认知，并帮助营销者和决策者解决在网络营销环境中所面对的问题．再者，从实际角度来讲，更好地了解消费者搜寻过程可以帮助制造商更有效地发挥市场效能，如设计出更好的市场沟通策略和分销策略．

691613.label: Realisation of objectives
691613.value: I assess that about 85% of the initial objectives were realized in this project. The objectives of 1, 3, and 4 were successfully achieved, which led to a publication in a top business journal. For the second objective, its achievement has been limited due to the following reasons: under-estimation of required efforts and the main technical challenges in developing an econometric model. For the investigation of the second objective, I had to recognize two groups of online consumers that we were initially interested in. a) online consumers who browse products and buy online b) online consumers who browse products online but do not buy online The research goal in #2 was to contrast the consumer groups between (a) and (b) above using a theory-based empirical models. I encountered the following issues for #2 above. First, the key component enabling this project was a very large scale, new data set of about 2T bytes in size that records very detailed browsing behaviors of online consumers. Its large size required a huge amount of efforts to clean up, process, transform and prepare the (big) data into a usable form. The resources required to secure data set related to (b) was judged to be very high compared to (a). We started the project with a initial focus on securing, preparing, and studying consumer group (a) above. Second, our efforts to develop a new econometric model was not very successful during the project period. Although we tried developing a econometric model and tested it with artificial data set during the second half of the project period(after the project adjustment period is closed), the model had some serious issues with identification. Combining these two issues, I focused on a paper that focuses on 1, 3 and 4 in full force. However, this fall (fall of 2017), my collaborators and I had very significant progress in model development for #2 and subsequently we have resumed the data preparation. Therefore, although our initial efforts during the project period was not fruitful, I believe that our continued efforts after the project closure will eventually lead to a successful publication in the next couple of years. In terms of objective assessment of the project achievement, the project focusing on 1, 3 and 4 led to a successful publication in Marketing Science, a top business journal. In addition, this paper was awarded 2016 Little Award by INFORMS that recognizes the best marketing paper in any INFORMS sponsored journals. The findings of this paper were also broadly communicated to both academic and business groups.

691613.label: Major findings and research outcome
691613.value: Our findings mainly offer insights to online consumers from the business perspective. First, our findings raise the possibility that marketers can intervene in the consumer search process prior to purchase and change its path and outcome. This can be done within and across consumers. Across consumers, early search is still informative about preferences. Hence, similar options can be advertised to those who search for them. Within consumers, one could imagine that incomplete search strings are highly effective targeting or direct marketing variables. For example, during the early stages of the search, advertising might focus on the brand, whereas during the later stages of the search process, it might focus on product lines or models. Later in the search, a retailer can change the order of items presented to more closely align with the preferences exhibited by those who search.

691613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
691613.value: Our analysis can be extended along multiple dimensions. First, we considered only one durable-goods category. Although we expect our results to be informative of search in durable consumer goods categories, consumer may search for less number of options in nondurable categories in which prices are low and consumer preferences are well fixed, such as consumer grocery goods. Second, still more detailed data could reveal further insights on consumer search. One would expect reviews, in particular, to affect the nature of search because the recommendations of experts and consumers are influential on consumers' final choice (West and Broniarczyk 1998, Chevalier and Mayzlin 2006). In our data, both review and product detail information exist on a single page, making it impossible to disentangle these effects. Likewise, because multiple product attributes are concurrently presented on a single product page, it is challenging to assess which particular attributes are searched. Hence, we characterize search for multiattribute goods, but cannot observe multiattribute search. Third, it is compelling to explore which search patterns are associated with purchase. This analysis might prove useful in characterizing how search relates to purchase incidence and interventions that might impact it.

691613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
691613.value: The findings in this research mainly helps businesses - online retailers and manufacturers - to better understand online consumers' browsing and choice behaviors. First, although consumers visit only one or two online retailers, they search a lot within a store. This implies that consumers do not search for better price but for better matching product. If consumers are looking for better price, we should observe a lot of consumer visits across stores. This is not the case. Second, when consumers come online for purchase, they already have a good idea of what to buy. This implies that online consumers, before coming to online stores, obtain a lot of products from other offline sources and browse products that best fit their needs. Third, we find that the products that consumers browse over and over again are more likely to be bought. Therefore, if an online store observes its visitirs browsing some products repeatedly, it is a very strong signal that the consumer may buy the products.

691713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
691713.value: The sizable literature on earnings quality and informativeness has thus far largely emphasized on the usefulness of earnings information to external users. Yet when firms are “learning by doing” (Arrow 1962), earnings provide valuable information not only to external users but to internal ones as well. In such environments managers use earnings information to make and evaluate investment and operating decisions. In the proposed study we will investigate the effect of the internal decision-usefulness of earnings on firm value. We will also study how managers’ propensity to under-invest, and how different institutional and firm-specific characteristics affect this relation. We propose a simple valuation model and show that the decision-usefulness of earnings increases firm value, provided that agency problems are not too severe. We will then empirically test the model’s predictions. The study contributes to the earnings quality literature and provides new insights into the interplay between the roles that accounting information plays in decisions by internal and external users. 目前在研究盈利质量及信息度的文献中，主要强调盈利信息对外部使用者的有用性。然而，公司在“边做边学”（Arrow 1962） 的过程中，盈利不仅对外部使用者而且对内部使用者都提供可贵的信息。在这样的环境下，经理人员需用盈利信息来评估投资项目及做出营运决策。本提案中，我们将研究盈利信息对公司内部决策的有用性及其对公司价值的影响。我们还会考虑由经理人员引起的投资不足的问题，以及制度与公司特性对此问题的影响。我们提出一个简单的定价模型，来说明盈利信息对决策的有用性会增加公司价值，其前提是代理问题不是过度严重。我们将用实证方法检验模型的论断。本研究将对盈利质量方面的文献作出贡献，并让我们对盈利信息在内部与外部决策中的两个作用的相互关系有更好的了解

691813.label: Project Objectives
691813.value: Derive equations to calculate the overall global welfare gains (i.e. the size of the gains) from trade costs reduction, population changes and innovation. Derive equations to estimate the welfare effects of above changes on individual countries of the world (i.e. the distribution of the gains). Derive equations to estimate the welfare impacts on individual countries resulting from 1. China’s trade liberalization resulting from accession to WTO; 2. Uruguay round of GATT negotiations. Document, for the Chinese manufacturing sectors, the pattern of firm-size (revenue, employment) distribution, productivity distribution, export behavior (export revenue) within each sector. Compare these variables across sectors, and how they vary over time. Then use the findings to confront the results of a multi-sectoral model with heterogeneous firms which we have already built. For each Chinese manufacturing sector, measure the firm-level effects (expand, contract, enter, exit, whether to export) in response to trade liberalization and confront the results with a multi-sectoral model with heterogeneous firms which we have already built. Use data from other countries, if available, to carry out similar analyses. Introduce variable markup in the above-mentioned theoretical models of global gains from reduction of trade barriers and firm-level responses to trade liberalization and differences in firm-level responses across sectors and see how variable markup affect the results theoretically. Having adjusted the models for variable markup, we apply these adjusted models to re-estimate the various effects stated above and see what differences it makes empirically. Introduce FDI into the above-mentioned theoretical models and carry out similar analyses as stated in the last objective.

691813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
691813.value: 在这个研究项目中，我们从两个角度来探索国际贸易对全球福利的重要性：1。减少贸易壁垒对全球福利有甚么影响？我们将特别探讨两个问题：（a）我们将研究全球整体以及个别国家的福利。我们会为这两种影响进行理论和实证研究。 （b）我们将处理关税壁垒和非关税壁垒。2。个别国家的内在变化如何通过国际贸易影响全球的福利？我们将专注于两种类型的变化：人口增长,和研究创新。 这些问题很重要，因为政策制定者需要评估他们的政策对福利的影响，企业需要预测其投资的成效。但评估国际贸易的效益往往取决于模型所采用的方法。在我们的研究中，我们将使用各种不同的模型以作比较。 我们预期的成果包括： 1。计算出中国加入世界贸易组织对全球整体以及个别国家的福利的影响。 2。基于我们已经建立的模型，我们可以预测中国不同行业的企业如何应对中国的贸易自由化。 3。推导出一个简单的方程组来计算技术创新和人口增长对福利的影响如何从一个国家通过贸易扩散到世界其他地区。 4 。把(a)贸易自由化造成更大的国内竞争,和(b)直接投资,这两个因素纳入我们的模型中,让模型更详细,更准确。

691813.label: Major findings and research outcome
691813.value: The greatest achievement of this project is that my co-authors and I have derived a simple formula for computing the global welfare effect of reduction of bilateral trade costs, such as shipping costs or the costs of administrative barriers to trade. The formula is applicable to a broad class of perfect-competition and monopolistic competition models and settings, including perfect competition with single-stage and multi-stage production and Melitz's (2003) heterogeneous firm model with general firm productivity distribution. We prove that the underlying mechanism is the envelope theorem. We then extend our analysis to models with non-constant markup. Finally, we carry out some empirical applications to show the user-friendliness of the formula. For example, we calculate that a reduction of border-procedure related trade transaction costs by one percent of the value of world trade in 2003 would increase global income by USD 44.3 billion, roughly the same estimate by OECD. In the second empirical application, we calculate that the reduction of shipping time during 1960-2010 has cumulatively increased global income by somewhere between 2.7 to 9.8 percent, a magnitude consistent with the literature. The above formula can be easily modified to carry out analysis of population changes and innovation. Then, we extend our formula above and derive a formula for calculating the welfare gains of individual countries from reduction of bilateral trade costs. It is then applied to calculate welfare gains of individual countries from China’s accession to the WTO. The second most important achievement of the project is that we extend the one-sector heterogeneous-firm model of Melitz (2003) to multiple sectors, and use the model to explain firms’ entries and exits, expansion and contraction, and exporting behavior in different manufacturing sectors of China in response to China’s accession to the WTO, which dramatically increased the imports of intermediate goods. We then test the theory with data. We find the results to be supporting the theory. For example, we found that, consistent with the model’s prediction, in sectors in which China has comparative advantage, firms would tend to have higher probability of entry into the export market, there was larger increase in fraction of firms that export, and larger increase in the revenue share from exporting. The third most important achievement of the project is that we develop a North-South international product-cycle model with fragmentation and foreign direct investment to investigate the determinants of fragmentation in product cycle trade. We also analyze how exogenous changes in the degree of fragmentation affect the North-South wage gap. The model is just a first step in addressing the causes and consequences of fragmentation in the product cycle. It paves the way for building a more sophisticated model that can incorporate endogenous rate of innovation, as well as global sourcing by both the North and the South. Thus, the model has a lot of potential for extension to yield much rich results.

691913.label: Project Title(Chinese)
691913.value: 在零售业里易腐商品的供货和清仓销售的协调

691913.label: Project Objectives
691913.value: First, the focus will be on the optimal timing of clearance sales. We have shown that clearance sales should start with the older items; that is, there is a threshold in terms of age. Any items older than the threshold should be cleared and any items newer than the threshold should be carried over to the next period. We have made good progress in this stage. What happens to the items whose age equals the threshold? Should its inventory level be cleared to a clear-down-to level? (The answer is positive under FIFO issuance.) These will be the remaining research questions in this stage. Second, many retailers regularly rotate older items to the front of a shelf. The purpose of the practice is to increase the searching cost for the newer items and hence induce FIFO behavior from shoppers. Retailers have achieved various successes. How would the optimal time for clearance sales depend on shopper behavior (i.e., the inventory issuing rules)? Third, we will move on to the characterization of the optimal policy on replenishment. We suspect that there will be a “segregation” phenomenon here. That is, no order of new items will be placed if the inventory level of the oldest items is either very low or very high. Finally, we will look for simple and yet effective heuristics. We are particularly interested in heuristics that have the following two features. First, the heuristics should leverage the insights that we have learned from the optimal policies. Second, the optimal policy relies on the full information about age. We have observed that many retailers, if not most, do not keep track of age information for their perishable items. We are particularly interested in heuristics that do not require the full information about age and hence, can be readily implemented without heavy investment in information technology.

691913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
691913.value: Many retail products, such as food items, pharmaceuticals, etc., have a short lifetime. Not only do these products generate a substantial amount of revenue themselves, they also boost store traffic. Indeed, empirical studies have consistently shown that customers’ choice of stores is influenced heavily by what perishable goods are on their shelves. Therefore, the management of perishable items is of main concern to retailers. The management of perishable goods, however, is challenging. The biggest challenge stems from matching perishable supply with uncertain demand. Retailers sometimes run out of stock, which leads to revenue loss, sometimes they have to throw away unsold items approaching their expiration dates, which is a waste and causes environmental concerns. To reduce waste, many retailers have used clearance sales as a strategy to sell those items that are approaching their expiration dates at a reduced price. To effectively use clearance sales for reducing the mismatch, it is important for retailers to determine the right timing and depth of sales and to coordinate clearance sale with replenishment decisions. These, unfortunately, are nontrivial, and to our best knowledge, there are simply no rigorous guidance or decision support tools available. Most retailers rely on crude and untested rules of thumb and there is typically no coordination between clearance sales and replenishment. In this study, we will fill this gap. We consider a retailer who replenishes its perishable inventory periodically and needs to decide when and to what extent it should clear its inventory through clearance sales. Our objective is to find the optimal strategy for both replenishment and clearance sales. This is a practically relevant and yet technically complex problem. It is technically complex because a) it has a multi-dimensional state space, and b) fresher items are typically sold first in retailing on a last-in-first-out (LIFO) basis and inventory systems under LIFO are known to lack common technical properties needed for analysis. Although perishable inventory management is a well studied area, in the vast literature, none has tried to find the optimal strategies under LIFO and a general lifetime. There is also a literature on clearance sales or dynamic pricing in general, but none has put the focus on retail perishable goods that have a finite lifetime and can be replenished. In summary, through our study, we will be able to contribute to both the literature on perishable inventory management and that on dynamic pricing and to retail practices.

691913.label: Realisation of objectives
691913.value: 1. First-in-first-out is optimal for clearance sales; that is, there is a threshold in terms of age. Any items older than the threshold should be cleared and any items newer than the threshold should be carried over to the next period. We can also describe the optimal policies by two thresholds for each age group of inventory: a lower one and a higher one. For an age group of inventory with a remaining lifetime of two periods or longer, if its inventory level is below its lower threshold, then there is no clearance sales; if it is above its higher threshold, then it will be cleared down to the higher threshold. The optimal policy for the age group of inventory with a one-period remaining lifetime is different. Clearance sales may occur if its inventory level is above its higher threshold or below its lower threshold. The phenomenon that a clearance sale happens when the inventory is low is driven by the need to segregate the newest inventory from the oldest inventory and is unique to the LIFO issuing rule. 2. If more customers adopt FIFO, would the retailer clears its inventories later? Not necessarily, although our numerical studies show that in most instances it would. 3. In terms of replenishment, we show that if the firm put any inventories with a remaining lifetime of two periods or longer on clearance sales, then it is optimal not to order new items. In addition, the optimal order quantity is decreasing in the number of the oldest inventories, but not necessarily in those of others. 4. We consider two myopic heuristics that require only partial information. The first requires only the information about the total inventory and the second requires the information about the total inventory as well as the information about the inventory with a one-period remaining lifetime. Our numerical studies show that the second outperforms the first significantly and its performance is consistently very close to that of the optimal policy. In summary, we have provided an unambiguous answer to each of the four research questions we raised in this project. The objectives have been fully realized.

691913.label: Major findings and research outcome
691913.value: We study joint replenishment and clearance sales of perishable goods under a general finite lifetime and a last-in-first-out (LIFO) issuing rule, a problem common in retailing. We show that the optimal policies can be characterized by two thresholds for each age group of inventory: a lower one and a higher one. For an age group of inventory with a remaining lifetime of two periods or longer, if its inventory level is below its lower threshold, then there is no clearance sales; if it is above its higher threshold, then it will be cleared down to the higher threshold. The optimal policy for the age group of inventory with a one-period remaining lifetime is different. Clearance sales may occur if its inventory level is above its higher threshold or below its lower threshold. The phenomenon that a clearance sale happens when the inventory is low is driven by the need to segregate the newest inventory from the oldest inventory and is unique to the LIFO issuing rule. The optimal policy requires a full inventory record of every age group and its computation is challenging. We consider two myopic heuristics that require only partial information. The first requires only the information about the total inventory and the second requires the information about the total inventory as well as the information about the inventory with a one-period remaining lifetime. Our numerical studies show that the second outperforms the first significantly and its performance is consistently very close to that of the optimal policy. The findings have been published in the journal Operations Research.

691913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
691913.value: Perishable inventory management under LIFO issuing rule is an important problem. However, there is not enough research on it due to its technical difficulty. The progress we have made is encouraging. We believe that there are three directions for future research. First, in practice, consumer behavior can be more complex. For example, what if only some customers search the newest items while the rest take whatever is on the front of the shelf? Second, the retailer may have a multi-criteria objective. In addition to maximizing profit, it may also be concerned about the environmental harm that waste causes. Third, since the problem is computationally challenging, it will be worthy to continue to look for good approximations and computation methods.

691913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
691913.value: We study the perishable inventory problem where customers always choose the newest inventories on shelves, a problem common in retailing. We find that the oldest inventories play a qualitatively different role than other inventories. This is reflected in the following ways: a) The optimal order quantity is monotone in it, but not necessarily in others; b) It may be optimal to clear all of the oldest inventories when there are only a few of them, a phenomenon we call segregation. However, clearance sales won't happen when other inventory levels are low enough; c) It is critically important to keep record of the oldest inventories, and the performance of myopic heuristics that take advantage of that record can be consistently close to that of optimal policy. However, the value of keeping record of other inventories is insignificant. These results mean that retailers should segregate the oldest inventories from the newest ones. Clearance sale is one approach to achieve that goal, but there are others such as rotation of inventories across different retail branches. In addition, it is important to keep record of the oldest inventories. These findings significantly enhance our understanding of this difficult problem that has been left open for decades.

692013.label: Major findings and research outcome
692013.value: We find that institutional funds - delegated institutional portfolios catering to pensions and non-profit organizations - have unique features and distinctive ow-performance relations. Fund investors face high search costs as institutional funds have low disclosure requirements and limited ability to advertise. Further, there is no liquidity sharing among investors of separately managed accounts. We find that while overall institutional fund flows are sensitive to past performance, funds with high investor search costs have extra flow sensitivity to good past performance, and funds offering a low degree of liquidity sharing exhibit muted flow sensitivity to poor past performance. Finally, institutional fund flows are negatively correlated with subsequent fund performance at short, intermediate, and long horizons. These findings suggest that in the institutional fund market, search costs and liquidity are important factors for investment delegation decisions, and that frictions in this market may have undermined the effectiveness of the delegation decisions. We are revising the paper after presenting the paper at various seminars and conferences and plan to submit the Journal of Finance afterwards.

692013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
692013.value: Extending this project, we are working on a further project related to another RGC grant that analyzes whether there is an economy of scale effect between fund family assets under management and return performance.

692013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
692013.value: Institutional investors seem to be different from retail investors in less behavior bias. They reduce investments in underperforming funds as much as they increase investments in outperforming funds. This is probably the result of a more systematic investment approach. However, using this approach does not show that they can pick winning funds and dropping losing funds successfully on a forward basis. The adjustment of investments to past performance is positively related to the liquidity sharing effects.

692113.value: 消费者学习机制下的企业动态定价和服务竞争

692113.label: Project Objectives
692113.value: Build a dynamic game model to incorporate the customer learning process into firms’ price and service decisions; and develop an approximate methodology to solve this dynamic game. Investigate the key tradeoff to driving firms' optimal strategy of price and service level, and better understand how firms’ price and service level decisions are affected by customer learning behavior, price and service sensitivites of consumers, and firms' capacity cost structure. Generate insights into how firms trade off between prices and service levels to profitably influence consumer learning in a competitive market in order to complement the existing body of research on price and service competition.
