692113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
692113.value: In the market for competing service facilities, firms compete on both price and service. Many service industries including banking, e-tailing and telecommunications, firms strive for a competitive advantage by improving cost efficiency or differentiating customer services. For example, there are many express delivery companies in Hong Kong such as S. F. Express, City Courier Service, City Ling Express and DHL Express. Faced with fierce competition, some companies may respond by lowering prices and compete head-to-head, while others may differentiate in the services they offer to customers. However, it is not clear how a company optimally balances the tradeoff between price and service in a competitive market in order to sustain market share and maintain long-term profitability. In this project, we consider a general problem of competing service firms offering service products at various prices and with different services; particularly, service is measured by the waiting time that consumers experience. Faced with a large number of service firms which provide differentiated service products at different prices and waiting times, consumers trade off prices and services and decide which firm to purchase from. Unlike prices, waiting times are experienced by consumers only after their purchase. Hence, previous shopping experiences greatly influence consumers’ estimates of waiting times. We assume that consumers use observed past information on waiting times to form their estimates according to an exponential smoothing model. We embed this consumer learning process in a dynamic game model of price and service competition over an infinite time horizon. As each firm has to track the price and service information of all the other competing firms, it is essentially infeasible to analyze this complex dynamic game when the number of firms grows. To circumvent the computational difficulty, we apply the recently proposed idea of mean field equilibrium to study an approximate game in which each firm maximizes its profit only with respect to the long-run average price and average waiting time. We will then explore how firms tradeoff between prices and service levels in an evolving dynamic game. We will also examine how the long-run equilibrium price and service level are affected by customer learning behavior, and their sensitivity to price and service level, and firms’ capacity cost structures. The successful completion of the project will provide managers with insights into joint decisions on price and service levels in a competing service industry, particularly when firms have imperfect information on the other competitors. 服务行业的企业包括银行，电子零售和通信等，主要在价格和服务水平两方面展开激列的竞争。企业要么通过降低成本争取价格优势，要么提供有特色的服务区别于业内企业的服务产品。例如，香港市场有众多的快递公司包括顺丰快递，城市快递，城市链接等。面对激烈的市场竞争，一些公司凭借低廉的价格争取市场份额，另一些公司侧重于提高服务的水平。那么，企业面临的一个问题就是如何平衡好价格和服务水平的关系争取长期的稳定获利。 这恰是我们这个项目的主要研究问题。我们的问题抽象为：多个服务企业提供相同功能的服务产品，但是在产品的价格和服务水平上不同；服务水平主要表现在消费者的等待时间上。面对众多的企业，消费者权衡价格和服务水平后决定从哪一家购买产品。不同于价格，具体的等待时间统通常在消费者购买产品后才能体验到。所以消费者要根据自己对各个企业的服务水平估计做出决策，这个估计可参考消费者以往的购物经验或者第三方的信息等。我们假定消费者可以通过以往的购物信息，运用指数平滑模型学习企业的服务水平。然后把消费者学习模型嵌入无限周期的价格和服务竞争的动态博弈。显然，在这个动态博弈模型下，每个企业要知道其他各企业在每个销售周期的价格和服务信息，因此求解模型非常困难，特别是在企业数目比较大的情形下。为克服这个困难，我们借鉴最近提出的均值平衡理念，去求解一个近似模型。值得一提的是，企业只需知道均值价格和均值服务就可做出决策。我们计划分析和求解企业的价格和服务均衡解，还计划进一步研究各个企业的价格和服务均衡解如何随着消费者的学习行为和对价格和服务的敏感程度，及企业的服务成本结构。我们预计若项目成功完成，可对服务领域的价格和服务竞争管理，特别是市场信息不完备的情形，提供重要的指导作用。

692113.label: Realisation of objectives
692113.value: The project studies how service firms compete on prices and service levels when customers do not know the true service levels, and instead learn about them through past service levels. To address this problem, we use an exponential smoothing method to model how customers form their beliefs on service levels, and then embed this learning model in a dynamic game model of firms’ price and service competition over an infinite time horizon. Such a dynamic game is essentially complicated to solve because each firm needs to track the information of prices and service levels for all the other firms. We thus apply the recently proposed idea of mean field equilibrium to the problem and develop an approximate game. In this approximate game, each firm maximizes its profit only with respect to the average price and the average service level in the long run. We prove that the mean field equilibrium of the approximate game is an epsilon-Nash equilibrium to the original dynamic game under certain conditions. The approximate game can be further reduced to a dynamic program, which facilitates analyzing each firm’s optimal decision on price and service level. We show that there exists a stationary equilibrium outcome. Specifically, each firm’s optimal policy eventually converges to either a high-price-and-high-service policy or a low-price-and-low-service policy. We then conduct comparative statics on the steady state of the firms’ joint price and service decision. In particular, we examine how the stationary equilibrium outcome is affected by consumer learning speed, consumer sensitivity to service, firm’s discount factor, etc. These results offer managerial insights into how firms should optimally choose the price and service level in the long term under different market conditions, and how they should balance the short-term service cost and the long-run benefit of service enhancement and hence improve future profit. To gain further insights into the role of learning, we explore the case when consumers can perfectly anticipate service levels provided by each firm. Such a problem can be modelled by replacing estimated service levels in the dynamic programming model with rational-expectation service levels, and the problem is then reduced to a single-period profit maximization problem. We compare the firm’s optimal decision on price and service level, and the firm’s average profit for these two cases. The results help us understand when the firm benefits from consumer learning.

692113.label: Major findings and research outcome
692113.value: One of our main findings is that the firm may downgrade its service when consumers are highly sensitive to service. This is more likely to happen when a firm has a smaller market base or a larger service cost. The result suggests that a firm with a small potential market size or a high operational cost should not compete fiercely on service in a competitive market. The other main finding concerns the role of learning. We find that the firm may not always benefit from faster learning consumers. While faster learning induces the firm to improve service level and increase future profits, it becomes increasingly costly to improve the service level. Consequently, the firm’s average profit may decrease in the learning speed of consumers once it exceeds a certain value. This implies that the firm is sometimes worse off when the consumer learning speed is higher. In comparison to the case when consumers have full information about firms’ service levels, we find that a firm provides a lower level of service, but earns a higher average profit when the firm values the future profit strongly and the consumers update their beliefs quickly. This work is under preparation for resubmission to the journal Production and Operations Management. In another paper, we study a repeated-purchase retailing business in which consumers do not know the markdown price in the future period, and thus they form a reference price via an exponential smoothing function. We explore the reference effects on a firm’s dynamic pricing and inventory strategies with strategic consumers. Specifically, we characterize the properties of the optimal ordering and markdown decisions and show that markdowns, if adopted appropriately, do not necessarily destroy the stability of a business even in the presence of strategic consumers. Furthermore, the consumers’ reference exhibits a mean-reverting pattern under certain conditions; that is, the reference fluctuates around a mean value, reflecting the practice of most stable businesses.

692113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
692113.value: First, the current model assumes that the demand rate of each firm is a linear function of prices and service level estimates of all the competing firms. Further research could consider other forms of demand functions such as attraction models to verify the robustness of the results. Second, the current work assumes that each individual firm is small so that it has a negligible effect on the other firms’ decisions. Therefore, an average level of price and service suffices to analyze each firm’s decision. Further work could study a concentrated market with a few dominant firms. In this case, the decisions of the dominant firms must be tracked. We expect that the game among firms would be analytically difficult to solve, and one possible direction is to develop computational methods to solve the problem.

692113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
692113.value: In this project, we consider a market with a large number of service firms, each of which provides differentiated a service product at a different price and service level. Unlike prices, service level is unknown prior to purchases, and consumers are thus assumed to learn about it through past service levels. We embed the consumer learning process in a dynamic game model of price and service competition over an infinite time horizon. Such a dynamic game is essentially complicated to analyze, and hence we study a relatively simple approximate game and prove the relationship between the approximate game and the original problem. We show that the firm’s optimal decision of price and service eventually converges to either a high-price-and-high-service policy or a low-price-and-low-service policy. We particularly highlight the role of learning and waiting in determining the firm’s equilibrium policy. In particular, the firm may downgrade its service when consumers are highly sensitive to service, especially when a firm has a smaller market base or a large service cost. We also find that the firm is sometimes worse off when the consumer learning speed is higher, even though faster learning enables the firm to improve its service level at a lower cost.

692313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
692313.value: 经纪公司执行金融市场的两个关键功能。首先，投资者买卖股票，通过这些经纪人。其次，许多这些券商雇用分析员生成报告和建议，为他们的客户。这些券商所扮演的双重功能创建一个独特的信息外溢的机会。知情人士经历的券商交易部门的交易中包含的信息是用来产生更好的预测或者建议（股票研究台）时产生的溢出。反过来，更准确的建议，导致更多的企业从满意的客户交易台。在这里，我们提出来看待这样一个券商和拥有一家公司的价值相关信息：该公司的“内部”交易当事人之间的联系。 具体来说，我们试图研究是否聘用的分析师经纪，处理一个公司CEO的个人交易账户漏洞信息行业，其中，以改善其预测/建议。 为了回答这个问题，我们首先要确定是否一个特定的经纪公司的CEO处理行业。我们打算这样做手工匹配144表格向SEC报告经纪人名称由该公司的CEO 。然后，我们将研究是否一个CEO所使用的经纪更容易覆盖公司。接下来，我们致力研究分析师受雇于谁处理首席执行官交易的经纪人（ “相连分析师” ）是否有更好的表现相比，这家公司预测/建议）其他分析师或b ）其他公司预测/建议。 请注意，在别人面前知道CEO的贸易是不连接的分析师的唯一源的优势 - 互动的CEO给经纪人，以搜集“软信息的机会。 ”谁交互与CEO的经纪人是可能超过什么市场看到 - 交易后，它被报道。即使每个人都可以观察到的事实，该公司CEO卖了一些股票，人们会不知道是什么原因。这可能是一个流动性驱动的贸易（例如， CEO需要支付大学学费，为他的儿子）或信息为基础的贸易。一个机会，谈的首席执行官和代理收到来自CEO的明确指示，可能就给了经纪人什么样的贸易，这很可能是一个信号。此信号不会被公开甚至在交易后观察报道。 设置我们心目中的独特优势是，我们可以聘请事务所，分析师，券商， CEO和时间固定效应。的变化，创造或破坏某一公司和分析师之间的联系，是什么将确定我们感兴趣的变量。例如，如果一个公司改变其CEO和新CEO采用了不同的经纪，我们应该期望从较早的券商分析师建议将变得不那么有利可图。同样地，如果分析师变化工作，他的准确性股票连接到老（新）经纪应的下跌（增加） 。

692313.label: Realisation of objectives
692313.value: We have produced a high quality working paper which addresses the objectives specified above. This paper has been accepted into 3 of the top-most refereed conferences in finance, namely the American Finance Association annual conference (AFA) 2018, the Financial Intermediation Research Society annual conference (FIRS) 2017, and the European Finance Association annual conference (EFA) 2016, and we intend to submit the paper to the Journal of Finance or the Journal of Financial Economics or the Review of Financial Studies approximately in July 2017, after polishing the paper further according to comments from our discussants/other conference participants at FIRS and CICF. We show in the paper that one important way through which information privy to insiders percolates into financial markets is through their trading behavior. Insider trading laws in many countries require that insiders reveal their trades – in particular the number of shares traded and the trade date – publicly and within a short time window, to limit information asymmetry. The question we ask in this paper is whether this disclosure of the trade is sufficient in eliminating all obvious sources of information asymmetry arising from the insider trading process? This is a very important question because the current regulatory regime operates under that assumption, so any answer in the negative makes a case for modifying it. Here we find evidence that the answer is indeed in the negative. We show that during the trading process, some relatively long-lived information advantage – beyond that contained in the public disclosure of the trade itself – passes to the broker used by the insider. The equity analyst who covers the insider’s firm at the same brokerage is able to benefit from this and make more accurate earnings forecasts. Since these forecasts are mostly issued after the occurrence of the trade itself becomes public knowledge through SEC filings, our evidence suggests that not all of the inside broker’s information advantage is eliminated by the trade disclosure.

692313.label: Major findings and research outcome
692313.value: We identify the stock broking house that firm insiders trade through, and show that analysts employed at such “inside brokers” have a distinct information advantage over other analysts, even after the trade is publicly disclosed. Our results challenge the common perception that information asymmetry arising from insider trading is acute only before trade disclosure. Unlike many other sources of analyst comparative advantage, the effect we document is stronger after Regulation Fair Disclosure, and hence, still very topical. We show that one source of the broker’s superior information is his knowledge of the nature of a trading instruction, which facilitates inference about the trade’s information content.

692313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
692313.value: Overall, our evidence has important implications for regulations needed to address information asymmetry arising from the process of trading, which brokers in particular are in a unique position to exploit. We have presented the paper at highly competitive conferences like the ABFER in May 2016, and the EFA in August 2016, and are scheduled to present it at the CICF in July 2017 and the FIRS (June 2017) Conferences. This paper has also been accepted to the American Finance Asociation (AFA) annual conference in 2018. After gathering feedback from these conferences, we intend to submit the paper for publication in a top academic journal such as the Journal of Finance.

692413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
692413.value: 眼大肚小 “(Don’t let) Your eyes become larger than your stomach” – Chinese Proverb People make over 200 decisions about food every day, including choices about what to eat, how much to take, and when to stop (Wansink and Sobal 2007). Some of these decisions are habitual (Khare and Inman 2006), but the vast majority are automatized reactions to cues in the environment (Wansink 2006). Indeed, merely reorganizing the available assortment can have profound influences on information processing and choice (Broniarczyk 2008). Yet, assortment presentations themselves are contextualized with marketing cues such as labels, price promotions, and nutrition information. How do consumers make decisions in such contexts? In this research, we propose to address this question in two ways. First, we will analyze in depth the data we have obtained from a year-long field experiment conducted at a local ice cream store in Hong Kong. During the course of this experiment, we have manipulated assortment display organizations (of relatively calorie-dense versus low-calorie flavors as well as different colors), label colors, and price promotions to incentivize choice and/or quantity upgrades. This has generated a large and rich data set, to be analyzed using a multinomial choice model which we will develop. Preliminary descriptive statistics from the first two months of data provide strong evidence of the attentional and motivational mechanisms that drive choice in the field – simple changes in assortment organization can influence choice differently for relatively healthy versus indulgent flavors. The observed effect sizes are up to 30% over baseline (with consequences for sales, profits and calorie consumption). The results of this experiment, albeit potentially important, will be limited to the specific context. Hence, in the second part of this research, we will explore the generalizability of these effects by investigating the attentional and motivational mechanisms in more detail using a set of laboratory experiments and further field experiments. These will combine standard choice experiments with eye-tracking data, to probe deeper into the interactions of assortment presentation (in vivo versus on a menu or product package), in the presence or absence of price and nutrition information. These insights will shed new light into assortment organization and menu design. Together, these inquiries have important implications for marketers and policy-makers. From a conceptual perspective, this research brings together the disparate consumer-psychological fields of self-control, product assortments, and visual information processing with the methodological areas of eye tracking and Bayesian modeling. 中文諺語當中有句眼大肚小 人們每天都要就食物作出超過200個決定，包括選擇食物、進食份量及何時停止進食(Wansink and Sobal 2007)。這些決定當中有的是根本習慣(Khare and Inman 2006)，但大部分的都是按環境提示作出的自然反應(Wansink 2006)。事實上，只需僅僅重新整理現有的商品就能對資料處理和選擇有深層的影響(Broniarczyk 2008)。不過，品種展示是把營銷暗示，如標籤、價格推廣及營養資料中情景化。究竟消費者如何在這些景況下作出決策？ 在本研究中，我們提議用兩個方法去論述這個問題。首先，我們會就在一間香港本地雪糕店實地實驗一年所得的數據作深入分析。在是次實驗中，我們以操縱商品陳列方式(按熱量高低和顏色來陳列口味)、標籤顏色、及價格推廣來刺激選擇並/或提升購買量。我們將會開發一個多項選擇模型來分析這個實驗帶來的巨大和豐富的數據庫。根據頭兩個月數據所得出的初步描述性統計充分証明了注意力和推動力的機制會促進實地選擇-簡單地改變商品陳列方式便可以影響相對地健康與放縱的口味選擇，而觀察得到的效果比基線高達30％(以銷售額、利潤和熱量吸收作出的結論)。 這個實驗的結果儘管具有潛在的重要性，但亦受制於某些特定環境。因此，在本研究的第二部分中， 我們會再透過一系列實驗室和實地實驗去仔細探討注意力和推動力的機制，從而探究這些影響的普遍性。這些實驗會在格價及營養資料存在或缺乏的情況下，結合標準選擇性實驗和眼動跟踪數據來對商品排列(在現實環境中與在菜單或產品包裝上)作出更深入探測。這為商品陳列方式和菜單設計提供了新的見解。

692413.label: Major findings and research outcome
692413.value: This project has added to knowledge about consumers' responses to food assortments and nutrition information in several different ways. The most prominent of these, which builds on research that was started under the PI's previous grant (GRF 642810) pertains to people's beliefs regarding the efficacy of diet versus exercise in terms of outcomes related to health and weight. Across a series of papers spanning multiple academic disciplines (psychology, consumer behavior, corporate strategy, and nutrition; please see Part 5.3 and Part C) we have established that people who implicate exercise, as opposed to poor diet, are more likely to be overweight or obese. These incorrect beliefs are largely attributable to promotional campaigns of food companies, and this represents, in one way among several, an instantiation of the obesity crisis as market failure. Our research therefore suggests several ways in which companies, policymakers, and nutritionists can come together to help resolve this problem. In a separate stream of research, we have investigated the effects of choice architecture and nutrition labeling on consumers' choices, quantity decisions, and consequently the overall efficacy of nutrition labeling guidelines. We have found that in situations where consumers have an existing goal to indulge, such as at an ice cream store, choice architecture can influence quantity decisions by inducing them to downsize, rather than choice decisions. Related to this, we have also found that while almost all extant research on the effect of nutrition labeling has found negligible or null effects, this is because people respond to nutrition information by compensating for consumption at subsequent meals, and hence nutrition labeling laws do have an effect, but only if viewed at a daily level. Finally, we have also investigated the effects of other types of information about food. In the paper titled "Do Costly Options Lead to Better Outcomes?" (see Part C) we looked at a different type of "cost" associated with food, namely taste, and found that people who believe that hard work leads to good outcomes (i.e., who believe in the Protestant Work Ethic) are more likely to prefer bitter foods, health foods, and cough syrups.

692413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
692413.value: As may be evident from 5.3 above, this research is moving ahead very promisingly on several fronts. At least three manuscripts should be completed and submitted to major journals in Spring 2017. Progressing these through the review process will take time and effort. In addition, the multi-country data are yielding rich insights, and have opened up investigation into GMOs and organic foods, which are highly topical and relevant domains, but scarcely investigated. In addition, new data collection efforts based on insights from the current data are also being planned. In this context, we will most likely apply for another GRF grant in the next cycle.

692413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
692413.value: Over 300 million people worldwide are obese, and obesity is responsible for around 5% of all deaths. Moreover, the number of overweight and obese individuals worldwide increased from 857 million in 1980 to 2.1 billion in 2013 . Indeed, a recent McKinsey report estimated the global economic impact from obesity at US$2.0 trillion; roughly equivalent to the global impact from smoking, or armed violence, war, and terrorism. As these numbers grow ever faster, the problem of understanding how people make food-related decisions grows in importance and urgency. In our research, we have shown that one of the likely causes of the obesity crisis is 'leanwashing' by the major food and beverage companies, who try to make consumers believe that obesity is not caused by poor diet. We have also shown that the obesity crisis represents a failure of the free market, and discussed different ways of regulation, such as taxes and bans. One common regulation being implemented in many countries is nutrition labeling. However, most extant research has found that labeling does not seem to influence choice. Our research finds that labels, and other "nudges" such as choice architecture, can influence consumption quantity, especially across meal occasions.

692513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
692513.value: We intend to study the farm space allocation problem of a farmer between multiple crops (e.g., corn and soybeans) over multiple years. Each year, the crops are exposed to yield uncertainty due to weather, disease and pest attacks. As a result, the farmer can harvest only a random proportion of the farm space allocated to each crop in each period. A key issue in the yield management is the benefit of crop rotation in consecutive years. The yields of rotated crops are better because of soil enrichment and reduction in the pest attacks. Besides the yield uncertainty, the crops are exposed to price uncertainty. In particular, as commodities, the crops are sold in the spot market after harvesting. The selling price is unknown to the farmer at the time of the allocation decision. In each period, the farmer decides the allocation of the farm space between the crops in the presence of yield and price uncertainties. We plan to investigate the optimal dynamic allocation policy and analyze the impact of yield and spot price uncertainties on the optimal policy as well as the farmer's profit. Using a calibration based on data on prices (to be collected in the project), our computational experiments will analyze the value of optimal dynamic allocation decision in comparison to widely-applied heuristic allocation policies (e.g., monoculture where the entire space is allocated to only one crop).

692513.label: Major findings and research outcome
692513.value: The project examines crop planning decision in sustainable agriculture--- that is, how to allocate farmland among multiple crops in each growing season when the crops have rotation benefits across growing seasons. We consider a farmer who periodically allocates the farmland between two crops in the presence of revenue uncertainty where revenue is stochastically larger and farming cost is lower when a crop is grown on rotated farmland (where the other crop was grown in the previous season). We characterize the optimal dynamic farmland allocation policy. Using a calibration based on a typical farmer growing corn and soybean in Iowa we provide rules of thumb for the effect of revenue uncertainty. In particular, we show that the farmer always benefits from a higher corn revenue volatility but benefits from a higher soybean revenue volatility only when this volatility is high; otherwise a lower soybean volatility is beneficial. We also show that growing only one crop over the entire planning horizon, as employed in industrial agriculture, leads to a considerable profit loss---that is, making crop planning based on principles of sustainable agriculture has substantial value. We propose a simple sustainable heuristic allocation policy and characterize the periodic allocation decision of this policy in closed form. Using our model calibration we show that the proposed policy not only outperforms the commonly suggested heuristic policies in the literature, but also provides a near-optimal performance.

692513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
692513.value: Farmers have to decide each year which crops and how much of each crop to plant on their land. This is a consequential decision for the profits of the farmer. In general, farmers follow heuristics (simple rules of thumb) that may not be in their best interest or environmentally sustainable. Our project is an effort to develop a decision support system which considers the key farming parameters (such as costs and crop prices) and also crop rotation benefits to recommend what proportion of land should be allocated to which crop to benefit the farmers.

692613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
692613.value: The disciplining role of executive turnovers is highlighted in theoretical and empirical studies of the executive labor market. The threat of dismissal is helpful in curbing agency costs and aligning the interests of managers and shareholders. A key insight is that the effectiveness of such threats depends on the expected costs to executives. The expected costs are given by the probability of dismissal multiplied by the personal cost of dismissal. Thus, from a governance perspective the personal cost of turnovers is as important as the probability of dismissal. Despite a large literature on executive turnovers there is surprisingly little systematic evidence on how costly forced turnovers are for executives. The main problem is that income and wealth typically are unobservable after forced turnovers, unless the fired executives resume positions at other public firms. Resuming an executive position at another public firm is just one of many job opportunities for ousted executives. Instead they might pursue alternative career paths by resuming positions at private firms (that do not disclose compensation), start their only businesses, work as management consultants, become professional investors, or retire. It turns out that the general lack of data availability on these alternative career paths makes it difficult to estimate the personal cost of executive turnovers. The main idea of this project is to provide evidence on the personal cost of forced turnover using detailed income and wealth data from the official records at the Danish Tax Authorities. This data allow me to observe income and wealth for all executives - before, during, and after their tenure. The quality of the income and wealth data is unique as the Danish Tax Authorities receives this information directly from the relevant sources as specified by the Tax Collection Act. Employers supply statements on wages paid to their employees and taxation of income is withheld at the source. Financial institutions report financial income on their customers' stock holdings, deposits, dividends, and on interest paid or received. The regulation also requires that financial institutions withhold taxes on financial income. As all sources of income are reported to the Tax Authorities it is possible to observe income from alternative career paths. With a rich income and wealth dataset at hand one can estimate the personal cost of forced executive turnovers, and examine whether the personal costs are related to the performance of the firm. 692613.label: Realisation of objectives
692613.value: The objectives of the project have been fully realized, and resulted in the working paper "Personal costs of executive turnovers". The results in the paper follow the outline of the reseach objectives, and are summarized below: I have obtaining novel data on executives' income and wealth from the offical records at the Danish Tax Authorities (Objective 1). The main advantage of these data is that income is reported to the tax authorities by third parties because taxation in Denmark mainly occurs at the source level. Thus, given the institutional setting, it is possible to systematically track the income of executives following turnovers irrespective of their career paths and, thereby, to overcome the main obstacle in estimating the personal cost of CEO turnovers. Following forced turnovers, I estimate that ousted CEOs’ personal income is 35-45% lower in the five years following forced turnovers (Objective 2). The decline in income is driven by a shift to lower income levels as more than 80% of all ousted CEOs earn less after they are ousted. The decline in income is affected by the stock price performance during the CEOs’ tenure. CEOs whose stocks underperformed the market during their tenure experience larger declines in income (Objective 3). Consistent with the executive labor market being the main channel for the lower income, I also find larger declines in income for executives with poor idiosyncratic firm performance during their tenures. Performance factors beyond the control of the executive, on the other hand, have no significant effect on future income. Consisitent with these findings, I find that turnovers motivated by poor performance carries a higher personal cost, than turnovers motivted by differences in strategy. Finally, I find that most ousted executives remain actively in the labor market (Objective 4), although few decide to undertake early retirement. In summary, the research objectives have been fully realized.

692613.label: Major findings and research outcome
692613.value: In this research project, I estimate the personal costs of executive turnover using highly reliable income data from the Danish Tax Authorities. The main advantage of these data is that income is reported to the tax authorities by third parties because taxation in Denmark mainly occurs at the source level. Thus, given the institutional setting, it is possible to systematically track the income of executives following turnovers irrespective of their career paths and, thereby, to overcome the main obstacle in estimating the personal cost of CEO turnovers. The main caveat with this approach is that the income data only covers individuals who live in Denmark. As a consequence of the limited international mobility of CEOs, the vast majority of CEOs of Danish firms between 1995 and 2007 satisfy this requirement. Between 1995 and 2007, only 14 out of 421 (3.3%) active CEOs were foreigners, and following turnovers, only 11 of the 137 ousted executives in the sample moved abroad. As a result, it is possible to track the income of 92% of CEOs who are ousted in this study. In comparison, income is observed for 27%, and 41% of the executive turnovers in Fee and Hadlock (2004), and Chang, Dasgupta, and Hilary (2010). Compiling a sample of 313 executive turnovers between 1995 and 2007, I estimate the effect of forced turnovers on total income, which is the sum of labor income, entrepreneurial income, and financial income. I find that forced turnovers result for executives in total income of 35%-45% lower than their income as CEOs. The decrease is driven by lower labor and entrepreneurial income, which declines by more than 45%, while financial income increases. As few as 20% of all ousted CEOs manage to recover the pre-turnover level of income after 5 years. That is, the decline in income is driven by a shift to lower income levels as more than 80% of all ousted CEOs earn less after they are ousted. The decline in income is affected by the stock price performance during the CEOs’ tenure. CEOs whose stocks underperformed the market during their tenure experience larger declines in income. Consistent with the executive labor market being the main channel for the lower income, I also find larger declines in income for executives with poor idiosyncratic firm performance during their tenures. Performance factors beyond the control of the executive, on the other hand, have no effect on future income.

692613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
692613.value: As described above all of the objectives of the research proposal have been realized. The proposed course of action therefore focuses on publishing the outcome of the project (i.e. the completed working paper "Personal costs of executive turnovers") in a top finance journal. After circulating the working paper for comments among peers, I have been invited to give seminars on the paper at Arizona State University, University of Oregon, and University of Washington in October 2016. As these seminars are likely to be a good testing ground for the publication potential of the research project, I have not yet submitted the paper for publication. After completing these seminars, I will in November 2016 submit the working paper for publication to one of the three top finance journals (i.e. Journal of Finance, Journal of Financial Economics, or Review of Financial Studies).

692613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
692613.value: This project examines the personal cost for executives when they are fired. The study finds that executives have 35% to 45% lower personal income in the five years following their dismissal. The personal cost is related to the stock price performance during the executives’ tenure: personal costs are higher for executives of firms who underperformed the market during their tenure, and smaller for executives who outperformed the market. The findings have relevance beyond the context of this study. I believe that the results highlight the importance of executive turnovers as an important internal governance mechanism. If personal costs are significant, dismissals become a credible threat, providing incentives to reduce agency problems ex-ante. High personal costs also have implications for the level of executive compensation. Higher incidence of executive turnovers would only result in higher compensation ex-ante if the personal costs of forced turnovers are significant. To this end, this study provides compelling evidence in support of this channel.

692713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
692713.value: The proposed research project will collect and analyze data from Gansu Province, China, to investigate relationships between child health, education and labor market outcomes in a poor region of a developing country. The project will explore in depth and for the first time important dimensions of youth-to-work transitions in developing countries by taking advantage of a unique longitudinal study with detailed measurements dating from early childhood into adulthood. We are particularly interested in understanding how early human capital formation affects future life opportunities through its impact on educational attainment and future career trajectories. Specifically, what are the impacts of cognitive skills, noncognitive skills, and health during childhood on educational attainment? And secondly, how do specific cognitive and noncognitive skills, as well as health, affect the labor force productivity of young adults? In investigating these questions, we examine how early experiences in the family and school environments influence different aspects of child development at different periods of a child’s life, and how these factors shape skills that predict future education and labor market outcomes. To address these questions, we propose to extend the Gansu Survey of Children and Families (hereafter GSCF), a longitudinal survey of 2000 children who were 9 to 12 years old when they were first interviewed in the year 2000 (GSCF-1), and who were re-interviewed at ages 13 to 16 in 2004 (GSCF-2) and at ages 18 to 21 in 2009 (GSCF-3). We seek support for collecting and analyzing a fourth wave of data in 2015, when the original sample will be 24 to 26 years old (GSCF-4). A fourth round will provide data that can be used to link childhood education, health, and family experiences with adult outcomes in the labor market. 本研究项目将收集和分析来自中国甘肃省的数据，来调查发展中国家贫困地区的儿童健康，教育和劳动力市场之间的关系。该项目将利用独特的从幼年追溯到成年的纵向研究首次深入探讨发展中国家青年工作转换重要要素。 我们特别感兴趣的是了解早期人力资本的形成是如何通过对教育程度和未来职业生涯轨迹的影响来影响未来生活的机会。具体来说，童年期间的认知能力，非认知能力，和健康对教育成就的影响是什么？其次，具体的认知和非认知能力，以及健康是如何影响青壮年劳动力的生产力的？为了研究这些问题，我们研究孩子早期在家庭和学校环境下的经历，如何在孩子生命的不同时期影响儿童发展的不同方面，以及这些因素如何塑造影响未来教育和劳动力市场的技能。 为了解决这些问题，我们建议延长对甘肃儿童和家庭的调查（以下简称GSCF）。纵向调查包括2000名青年。他们是在2000年第一次的采访时分别为9至12岁的儿童（GSCF-1）；第二次2004年采访时这些儿童13岁至16岁（GSCF-2）；第三次2009年采访时他们18至21岁（GSCF-3）。我们寻求支持用于2015年的第四轮数据收集和分析。届时这些原始样本将是24至26岁（GSCF-4）。第四轮数据的收集将儿童教育，健康，和家庭经历与他们在成人劳动力市场的结果相链接。

692713.label: Realisation of objectives
692713.value: The three objectives of the proposal have all been realized. First, a fourth wave of the longitudinal study Gansu Survey of Children and Families was successfully completed during the spring festival of 2015. About 70% of the original sample of 2000 children aged 9-12 during the first wave in the year 2000 were successfully re-interviewed either in person or by phone (after contacting them through their parents who still lived in the 100 surveyed villages). The work was conducted in collaboration with professors and graduate students of Northwest Normal University in Lanzhou (the capital of Gansu). The students served as enumerators. They were trained and supervised by the PI and one of the co-Is (Hannum), who were both on-site during the data collection. Most of the funds for the project went toward the data collection (originally budgeted as general expense but charged as staff expense since payment was made to consultant). All data were carefully checked and corrected/improved via follow-up phone interviews as necessary. All data have been double-entered to ensure no mistakes from the data entry process. In addition, much time was spent linking the newly collected data to earlier waves of the data, making sure that the respondents were the same across waves based on the demographic characteristics of their family members as reported in each wave. Entry, cleaning, and linking took nearly a year, so that the data were ready for analysis by the beginning of 2016. Interviews were conducted with the sample children as well as one of their parents. The questionnaire includes detailed information on final educational attainment, jobs, income, migration, marriage, children, personality, self-esteem, risk preferences, and depressive symptoms. Thus it will serve as a valuable resource for studies that link early childhood outcomes to early adult outcomes in rural China. Since nearly all of the sampled respondents have migrated, the longitudinal dataset also will be valuable for studying the process of migration. This data will eventually be made publicly available. The second objective was realized in two papers. The first is a paper that analyses data from the first 3 waves of the Gansu Survey to directly address the questions posed in the second objective. During the project period, substantial revisions of a preliminary draft of this paper were completed, and the paper was submitted for publication, revised in response to referee reports, and published in 2017 in the Journal of Economic Behavior and Organizations. The article, titled “Cognitive Skills, Noncognitive Skills, and School-to-work Transitions in Rural China” was co-authored with one of the PIs (Glewwe) and one of Glewwe’s former students (Huang). Analysis of how childhood human capital influences education and early work outcomes (the Objective 2 question addressed by the JEBO article) were extended using the newly collected wave 4 data as part of the paper “Intergenerational Mobility Pathways: Evidence from a Long Panel from Rural China”, co-authored with Xianqiang Zou, a PhD student I supervise at HKUST. This paper also addresses the third objective of the proposal, which is to study intergenerational mobility. Parent’s education and income influence child education income through human capital investments. Thus, to study the pathways through which parents influence children, we can break the relationship down into two parts—the impact of parents’ education and income on child human capital, and the influence of child human capital on adult outcomes. This second part is exactly Objective 2. The “intergenerational Mobility Pathways” paper extends the JEBO paper by examining completed educational attainment (the first paper must deal with censoring as some children were still in school during the 3rd wave), adding measures of physical health (not studied in the JEBO paper) and personality (based on the Big 5 personality traits). Objective 3 is realized in two papers. Most directly, it is studied in the “Intergenerational Mobility Pathways” paper described above, which quantifies intergenerational mobility for the sample surveyed in rural Gansu, revealing a high degree of income mobility. The paper examines both intergenerational mobility in education and in income, and examines how the correlations between parent and child outcomes is intermediated by different aspects of the child’s human capital (cognitive skills, noncognitive skills, and health). This paper has a full set of results, and will be submitted to a journal very soon (in January 2018). Objective 3 is also realized from another angle in another paper currently titled “Short- and Long-term Impacts of Family and Community Poverty in Rural China” that was completed as a major input into a book manuscript I prepared with support from a Humanities and Social Science Prestigious Fellowship that overlapped with the project period. The paper examines the impact of different dimensions of childhood poverty on child development as well as a range of early adult outcomes (educational attainment, employment, migration, wages, marriage, and fertility). This paper is motivated by recent influential work by Chetty that shows the importance of communities in influencing life opportunities of the poor in the US. We conduct a similar exercise for rural villages in China and also find an important role for community deprivations. This paper also has complete results and is expected to be submitted to a journal soon. Finally, the project supported completion of revisions to another paper that examined cognitive skill formation among youth in Gansu. Using the teacher data from the third wave of the Gansu data, we analysed how promotion incentives affected teacher effort in rural primary and middle schools. The paper “Promotion Incentives in the Public Sector: Evidence from Chinese Schools,” co-authored with a former PhD student Naureen Karachiwalla, was published in the Journal of Public Economics in 2017. In the interests of full disclosure, as noted above the project period overlapped with a one-year Humanities and Social Science Prestigious Fellowship (September 2015 to November 2016, with an interruption during Jan-Mar, 2016), which proposed to draft a book manuscript with project Co-I Emily Hannum tentatively titled Growing Up Poor in Rural China. Because the themes of the book project overlap with the objectives of the research project, I also included the content from the published JEBO paper, the paper on “Intergenerational Mobility Pathways”, and the paper on “Short- and Long-term Impacts of Family and Community Poverty in Rural China” as parts of the draft book manuscript. In terms of the genesis of the papers, the first two (JEBO paper and paper on “Intergenerational Mobility Pathways”) were written to address the objectives of the research project, while the paper on “Short- and Long-term Impacts of Family and Community Poverty” was motivated by a desire to answer the key motivating questions of the book project. However, since the latter also fits the 3rd research objective and the time of the work is part of the project period, I have included it as a product of the research project. The book manuscript also includes an introductory chapter and a lengthy descriptive analysis of the multidimensional nature of child poverty, consistent with its focus on Growing Up Poor in Rural China. Work on the Journal of Public Economics paper was supported by the research project (PI and RA time) and is not part of the book manuscript. Both published papers cite this research grant and not the Prestigious Fellowship.

692713.label: Major findings and research outcome
692713.value: The study “Cognitive Skills, Noncognitive Skills, and School-to-work Transitions in Rural China” is among the first to examine how both cognitive and noncognitive skills measured in childhood predict educational attainment and early labor market outcomes in a developing country setting. Analyzing longitudinal data on rural children from one of China’s poorest provinces, we find that both cognitive and noncognitive skills measured in childhood are important predictors of whether they remain in school or enter the work force. The predictive power of specific skill variables differ between boys and girls. Conditioning on years of schooling, there is no strong evidence that skills measured in childhood predict wages in the early years of labor market participation. In the study “Intergenerational Mobiiity Pathways” we find that a high degree of intergenerational income mobility in rural areas of a poor Chinese province, where children’s incomes are much greater than that of their parents and nearly all children migrate. The estimated intergenerational income elasticity is 0.099 while the intergenerational education transmission coefficient is 0.391. Decomposing the channels through which parents influence children’s outcomes, we find that the role of cognitive skills is important for accounting for intergenerational persistence of both education and income, while the roles of noncognitive skills and health are less important. In the study “Short- and Long-term Impacts of Family and Neighborhood Poverty in Rural China”, we define multi-dimensional poverty to include social and economic deprivations in the domain of the household, but also extend the concept to consider social and economic deprivations in communities (villages and schools). We investigate the impacts of different childhood deprivations on childhood cognitive and non-cognitive skills, and early adult outcomes such as years of schooling attained, college attendance, marriage, childbearing, migration, employment, wages, self-esteem, and depression. We find significant impacts of both family and neighbourhood deprivations on many of these outcomes, and are the first study to document the independent importance of communities in developing country settings.

692713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
692713.value: After publishing the completed papers, additional related papers can be completed. For example, we have generated preliminary results on gender differences in the impacts of childhood deprivations. We find, interestingly, that unlike in the US where boys are more sensitive to growing up poor, in rural China girls are more sensitive to poverty than boys. This is likely due to son preference which makes investments in girls more sensitive to income than investments in boys. We also find differences in parenting styles toward girls and boys in rich versus poor areas. As noted earlier, the study region is an area of high migration, so the data can be used to examine the long-term impacts of parent absence due to migration, and to the determinants of different migration outcomes.

692713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
692713.value: This research project supported the collection of a new round of longitudinal data for a cohort of rural children in China who were aged 9-12 when first surveyed in the year 2000 and were aged 24-27 during the new survey in 2015. The long span of the survey and the unique multidisciplinary measurements of cognitive and noncognitive skills throughout the multiple survey waves makes it the first dataset in developing countries of which we are aware that enable researchers to link different dimensions of childhood development to a wide range of adult outcomes. The project has found that early cognitive and noncognitive skills influence educational attainment; that intergenerational income mobility is high, perhaps due to widespread wage-earning opportunities through migration; that most of the intergenerational income correlation is due to cognitive skills; and that both family and neighbourhood poverty using multidimensional measures have large impacts on child development and a range of adult outcomes. The neighbourhood finding for rural villages is a new finding in the literature.

692813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
692813.value: 兩個接近的實體,通過更容易的互動，更便利的資訊，以及更大程度的監控, 會促進它們之間的聯系。例如，風險資本家更可能會進入當地企業的董事會（(Lerner 1995)。類似地，更靠近借款人的銀行更容易借錢給比較難搜集到信息的借款人，比如沒有任何財務記錄的借款人(Petersen and Rajan 2002; Mian 2006; Sufi 2007) 。最後，共同基金經理更可能持有當地公司的股份，他們從這些投資中獲得了顯著的異常報酬（Coval and Moskowitz 1999, 2001）。關於接近程度是否會促進產品市場範疇上的聯系，了解要少得多。我們計劃研究以下幾個問題：供應商公司是否可能因為更接近主要客戶而和其產生較強的聯系？如果是，那麽在增長創新和盈利方面，和主要客戶較強的聯系會對供應商產生哪些影響？ 在回答這樣的問題時，主要的困難是公司位置的選擇具有內生性。例如，供應商可能會選擇把公司開設在與他們有較強聯系或者期望與之產生較強聯系的客戶附近。這使得接近程度和關系強弱之間的因果聯系很難建立。我們研究的一個重要方面是解決這個問題。 大多數實證研究用地理上的接近程度來代表互動和信息搜集的容易程度。不過，我們認為接近程度更直接的代表是交通時間。例如，有些供應商和客戶，雖然地理上的距離甚遠，但是兩個城市之前有直航航班，他們相對於那些位於相同省份卻需要漫長的公路交通才能到達的供應商和客戶，將享受更輕松的互動。雖然地理上的接近程度和交通時間是相互關聯的，但是把註重點放在交通時間上，可以允許合理的外生性變動，使我們能夠解決內生性問題。具體來說，我們計劃利用引進新航線，以減少供應商和主要客戶之間的旅行時間。 我們的結果很可能是一些作為北美和歐洲的其他公司供應商的亞洲企業特別感興趣的。

693013.label: Project Title(Chinese)
693013.value: 區域集群的產業結構和促進企業合作的區域集群研究: 香港和東京的分析

693013.label: Co - Investigator(s)
693013.value: Prof Kajikawa, Yuya Lau, Ka Wing

693013.label: Project Objectives
693013.value: To assess the current status of regional clusters in Tokyo and HK through an innovation policy framework and organizational theories promoted by the OECD. Based on our review of the extant relevant literature (already completed), we will interview representatives from firms and institutions in both regions. The impacts of relevant government policies and public institutions on cluster performance will be examined. The focus of the investigation is to identify and assess innovation policy (IP) instruments in Japan and HK, especially those designed to promote collaboration and partnership among firms, universities, and research institutes. The study will focus on business collaborations that relate to innovation and knowledge creation, such as R&D contracting and the acquisition of disembodied technology. IP instruments are innovation policy instruments such as science and technology parks, support for innovative start-ups, innovation vouchers, and talent-attraction/retention schemes. We will also assess the firm-level capacity to utilize external knowledge acquired through business relationships in the sequential learning processes of acquisition, assimilation, transformation, and exploitation. To investigate the collaborative behaviors of suppliers, customers, universities, and institutions in the regional clusters. We will investigate innovation behaviors and interactions among main actors in the clusters in order to identify and characterize relationships between innovation inputs and outputs. We will also verify the explanatory power of the research model, focusing on both intra- and inter-cluster-level business activities and firm absorptive capacity. The researchers will collect data by means of e-mail, fax, telephone, survey mailings, and face-to-face discussions. Information from patent offices and selected websites will also be collected. Based on the research model, systematic investigation and research into business behaviors and inter-relationships among enterprises, universities, and other main actors will be carried out. Structural equation modeling adopted by the newly employed Research Fellow and social network analysis developed by a Co-I in Tokyo will be used to systematically examine linkages between the major actors that participate in business and research collaboration. The results will demonstrate how regional cluster activities and actors’ internal capabilities influence business collaboration. To develop a methodology for identifying and assessing opportunities for business collaboration among firms and institutions. Based on the results of the research model, a methodology for identifying and assessing opportunities for horizontal and vertical business collaboration among firms embedded in separate regional clusters will be developed to strengthen network ties and promote business partnerships. We will use product and technology profiles extracted from the surveys, patent claims, and web-based information to assess the business collaboration opportunities by a SVM machine-learning technique. Prior studies have examined the existence of a relationship between collaboration and product similarity, but to the best of our knowledge no one has attempted to generate predictions regarding new business collaboration. The relevance of the predicted results will be tested against the company cases in Tokyo and HK. The comparative analysis of the case study data across the clusters will validate and improve our methodology.

693013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
693013.value: China and Japan, the second- and the third-largest global economic powers, have recently been promoting business collaboration between Japanese and Chinese firms and institutions. In light of disruptions caused by the earthquake and tsunami in Japan and slower economic growth in China, such collaborations may serve as stabilizing factors for the global economy. To assist such collaborations, the OECD proposes a cluster-based approach to encourage interactions among companies, institutions, human capital, and knowledge. In spite of the importance of such collaborations, however, the relevant literature lacks sophisticated theoretical and empirical knowledge concerning the processes involved in collaborative business activities and the role of linkages between regional clusters in Japan and China. Moreover, some scholars have called into question how the regional cluster approach has been implemented, due in part to firm-level differences in the capacity to absorb new knowledge within the region. Owing to their close business trade relationships, we will investigate Hong Kong (HK) and Tokyo as regional clusters, drawing on absorptive capacity and system of innovation theories to analyze the current status of regional inter-/intra-cluster structures, investigate collaborative behaviors among relevant actors, and develop a new methodology for assessing opportunities for business collaboration. We suggest that product similarity and firm linkages affect business collaboration through an inverted U-shaped relationship. We also suggest that the extent of inter-/intra-regional business activities as well as firm absorptive capacity positively moderate such effects. The study should yield new insights to help bridge gaps between absorptive capacity and systems of innovation theories as applied to business collaboration. We will begin by evaluating the effectiveness of individual clusters, and the interactions across the clusters through a qualitative assessment of both regional clusters based on a literature review, secondary data, and interviews. We will then analyze the proposed research model with empirical data from two company surveys, patent offices, and selected websites. We will employ structural equation modeling and social network analysis to analyze the data. The study will develop a methodology for identifying and assessing opportunities for business collaboration, especially between small and medium enterprises in Japan and China, using a SVM machine-learning technique. Ultimately, the study should benefit companies in Japan and Hong Kong significantly. 作為全球第二及第三大經濟強國，中國和日本政府最近在促進雙方機構及企業之間的合作。鑑於日本的地震和海嘯所造成的破壞和中國經濟增長放緩，這樣的合作能夠成為對全球經濟的穩定因素。為了促進這些合作，經濟合作與發展組織（ OECD ）提出了一種基於集群的方式來鼓勵企業，機構，人力資本和知識之間的相互作用。儘管這種合作的重要性，但相關文獻缺乏成熟的理論和實證知識去了解協作業務活動中所涉及的過程和區域集群在日本和中國之間的聯繫的作用。此外，由於企業在區域內的吸收新知識的能力的差異，一些學者質疑區域集群的方法如何實施。 由於其密切的商貿關係，我們將調查香港及東京作為兩個區域集群，借鑒吸收能力和制度創新的理論來分析目前區域內部及跨區域集群之間的的狀態，調查有關行為者的協作行為，並發展一種新方法來評估業務合作的機會。我們認為，產品的相似性和企業之間的聯繫以通過一個倒U形關係來影響業務協作。我們還建議區域內部及跨區域集群之間的業務活動和企業吸收能力能加強這U形關係。這研究應該產生新的見解，以幫助吸收能力和系統的創新理論應用到業務合作的橋樑之間的差距。 我們將通過文獻回顧，輔助數據收集和訪談的基礎上開始進行對單個區域集群，及對這兩個區域集群之間的相互作用的有效性評估。然後，我們將通過兩次公司調查，一次專利局數據分析和一些網站的數據進行研究模型分析。我們將採用結構方程建模和社會網絡分析方法進行數據分析。這研究將使用SVM的機器學習技術技術開發一種方法來識別和評估日本和中國的中小型企業之間的業務合作的機會。最終，這項研究應該在日本和香港的公司受益明顯。

693213.label: Project Title(Chinese)
693213.value: 網上個人化內容及消費者選擇的關係

693213.label: Project Objectives
693213.value: To provide a theoretical linkage between consumer decision making process and web personalization by mapping the different stages of personalized engagement to those of consumer decision making. Based on the linkage so derived, theorize the impacts of personalization manipulations including name calling, referencing of past interaction, framing effect, and collaborative filtering on choice set consideration and decision outcomes. 693213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
693213.value: Web personalization technologies enable firms to customize product and service offerings to serve the needs of individual customers over the Internet. Using data mining and click-stream analysis, online merchants can now target potential customers with high precision and adapt web content in real-time to capture and even shape the customers’ spontaneous preferences. Web personalization is no longer low-level implementation details or transient technology opportunities that may fade away quickly. Instead, it becomes an integrated strategy of any business with a web presence. As such, findings of web personalization research will be judged on how they can be used to inform system design and whether high-level design principles can be derived. Research studies in the past decade have identified a number of factors that affect the effectiveness and outcomes of personalization. While findings of these studies have advanced our understanding on the potential and limitations of personalization technologies, they focused on isolated facets of the phenomena and drew from a wide array of reference disciplines. Furthermore, empirical findings were derived mainly from survey studies and laboratory experiments with few using real transaction data. Without an integrated framework and validation using field data, sustainable and systematic investigation of personalization effectiveness remains a challenge. The current proposal is built on the previous work of the PI and Co-I in web personalization. It has two objectives. First, it aims at identifying an integrated framework based on multistage consumer decision making to enable systematic categorization and investigation of factors affecting the effectiveness of web personalization. Second, under the framework, we will identify personalization manipulations in each stage and empirically assess their impacts on willingness to process the personalized messages, formation of choice set and its membership, and decision outcomes of customers. These manipulations include name calling, referencing of past interaction, framing effect, collaborative filtering and other industry-specific factors. Together these variables capture the core elements of common web personalization strategies. Hypotheses linking personalization manipulations to behaviors at different stages are proposed and empirically tested using data collected from real transactions in collaboration with a eMarketing solution provider and its clients. Findings will help to inform formulation of design principles for web personalization strategies. 網上個人化有助公司將產品及服務客制化，以滿足網上個人客戶的各種需求。目前，利用大數據分析，網上商戶可以準確鎖定潛在客戶，並即時調整網絡內容，以捕捉甚至塑造客戶的喜好。網上個人化已成為任何具備網絡的公司所實施的一個綜合性策略。因此，網上個人化如何能使用於系統設計將成為評判該項研究成果的準則。 過去數十年的研究已確定了一些影響個人化有效性及其成果的因素。雖然這些研究讓我們能預知網上個人化的潛力及局限性，但是這些研究都只注重於片面結論。而且，實證結果大多來自問卷調查及實驗室試驗，只有少數是來自真實的商業數據。如果沒有一個綜合理論依據並進行數據驗證，網上個人化效益的可持續發展及系統性研究仍然是一大挑戰。 本方案是建基於早前網上個人化的PI及Co-I研究。這個方案有兩個目標：第一，建立一個基於多階段客戶決策的綜合理論架構，從而對影響網上個人化效益的因素進行系統性的分類及調查；第二，在這個理論架構下，找出每個階段的個人化操控方法。我們提出了個人化操控及不同階段客戶行為關係的假設，並會與一間軟件公司及其客戶合作，驗證了從實際交易中收集到的數據。在制定網上個人化策略時，這些研究發現將有助形成策略設計準則。

693313.label: Project Objectives

To identify and validate the team performance outcomes resulting from software project teams’ use of agile methods.

693313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
693313.value: Systems development is a complex process consisting of many phases and activities. Given the complexity of systems nowadays, systems development methodologies (SDMs) are often used to manage and facilitate the development process. To keep up with changing technologies and user demands, a new batch of SDMs named agile methods have been introduced. Unlike traditional plan-driven methods (e.g., Waterfall), agile methods (e.g., Extreme Programming and Scrum) encourage lean thinking and agility. The leanness and agility concepts of agile methods are touted to improve the systems development process in terms of productivity and quality, as well as being better at dealing with the dynamic business environment nowadays. Industry reports indicate that many organizations have started to consider the adoption of agile methods for their software development projects in the coming years. The existing academic literature has discussed the pros and cons of agile methods, and how to fine-tune the steps in different agile methods. There are also studies on how to encourage adoption of these agile methods, and case studies on the successful use of agile-developed systems. While we now know quite a bit about the factors that influence the initial adoption of agile methods, we do not know as much about the impact of post-adoption use of agile methods on the software developers. In view of this gap in the literature, we propose to extend our knowledge beyond the adoption stage and investigate the conditions that contribute to the effective use of agile methods in the post-adoption stage among project team members. This proposed project will examine the impact of agile method use on software project teams’ performance. Drawing upon various theoretical perspectives from the literature on teams, we will develop models to explain how the use of agile methods results in different team performance outcomes. We will test our proposed research models with a longitudinal data collection in a field setting. The outcome of this project will contribute to both research and practice. From a scientific point of view, our work will introduce new theoretical perspectives (from research on teams) to explain the post-adoption outcomes associated with agile method use. For senior management in IT departments, the findings can translate into managerial action to facilitate the effective use of agile methods and the building of successful software project teams.

693413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
693413.value: This project concerns hypothesis testing and estimation of structural breaks in panel data models, in which we observe a large number of individuals over multiple time periods. During recent decades, panel data models have seen wide applications in various disciplines of economics and finance, largely due to their ability to control for unobserved heterogeneities among individuals. In the meantime, the increasing availability of high-quality panel data sets allows the analysis of new economic issues with appropriate tools. One such interesting issue is the possibility of economy-wide structural breaks that are common to all individuals. For example, the recent financial crisis and recession may lead to economic reforms among all economic sectors, long-term changes in the stock returns of every industry, etc. Technological advances or government policy shifts might affect every aspect of an economy. Ignoring such possible common structural breaks will lead to misleading statistical results from conventional panel data analysis. This project will first examine the problems associated with ignoring structural breaks in panel data models. We will consider breaks in both the individual fixed effects and regression coefficients. We will then provide a test procedure to detect the existence of common structural breaks, as well as to test K breaks against K+1 breaks. Finally, an efficient estimation algorithm will be provided to estimate the location of one or more common breaks. The developed tools can be readily applied in empirical research of labor economics, finance, international economics, where panel regressions have become increasingly popular. 本研究課題著眼於高緯面板模型中結構變化的估計和假設檢驗。面板模型被大量應用於經濟金融學的各個領域，這得益於其處理不可觀測的個體異質性之能力。在當今的實證應用中，高質量的高維面板數據使得許多新的經濟問題能夠被更好地研究，廣泛存在於經濟數據中的結構變化也可以被更系統科學地來處理。一個典型的例子是最近發生的金融危機引導了各行各業開始重新規範制度，使得行業股價的長期結構變化成為可能。另一個例子是技術革命或政府政策的變化通常會使得經濟的各個層面同時發生結構變化。在實證分析中如果忽略這種結構變化，將會導致錯誤的推論。本課題首先研究在面板模型中如果忽略結構變化可能引來的問題，個體的固定效應和回歸係數的變化將會被同時考慮。我們然後提供一個有效的檢驗過程來分析共同結構變化的存在性以及可能的數量。最後我們會給出系統的估計方法來精確地找出結構變化的時間。本課題所提供的工具能夠被廣泛地應用於勞動經濟學，金融學，國際經濟學等學科之實證分析。

693413.label: Major findings and research outcome
693413.value: This project provides a unified econometric framework to analyze multiple random structural breaks in panel data models. Unconditionally, such breaks are assumed to be independent draws from an unknown distribution, which can be either nonparametric in case of a single break or parametric when multiple breaks are allowed. The nonreversible hidden Markov chain proves to be a good candidate for the parametric distribution. Monte Carlo simulations show that the method greatly improves the precision of change-point estimation compared with alternative methods. In an empirical example, the method is applied to study the volatility change of quarterly income for 50 U.S. states.

693413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
693413.value: The proposed methodology can be extended to the more general panel regression analysis where the likelihood method is applicable. Another extension could be the explicit modelling of the dependence among breaks through observables instead of assuming independent breaks across individuals. For example, in the non-reversible Markov chain model, one can assume that different series have different transition matrices, which may be parametrized by individual covariates. I plan to address these extensions in a new paper.

693413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
693413.value: This project concerns the estimation and inference of structural breaks in panel data models, in which we observe a large number of individuals over multiple time periods. During recent decades, panel data models have seen wide applications in various sub-disciplines of economics and finance, largely due to their ability to control for unobserved heterogeneities among individuals. In the meantime, the increasing availability of high-quality panel data sets allows the analysis of new economic issues. One interesting issue is the presence of structural breaks. For example, the recent financial crisis and recession may lead to economic reforms among all economic sectors, long-term changes in the stock returns of every industry, etc. Technological advances or government policy shifts might affect every aspect of an economy. Ignoring such possible common structural breaks would lead to misleading statistical results from conventional panel data analysis. This project examines the problems associated with ignoring structural breaks in panel data models. We provide an econometric framework to analyze common as well as heterogeneous structural breaks. An efficient algorithm is provided to estimate the location of one or more common breaks. The developed tools can be readily applied in empirical research where panel regression has become increasingly popular.

693513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
693513.value: This project aims to formalize the Keynesian insight that sentiments about aggregate demand can generate output and employment fluctuations in a rational expectations framework. We will first develop a benchmark model, where each firm must make a production decision before demand is realized, based on noisy signals about what its demand will be. The signals, based on initial inquiries, advance sales, early orders, market research, and public forecasts about the state of the economy, provide imperfect information about firm-level demand and aggregate demand. After production decisions are made, demand is realized and prices adjust to clear the market. In this set-up firms have signal extraction problems that can lead to multiple equilibria and endogenous fluctuations in aggregate output. Self-fulfilling stochastic equilibria in our model will be not based on randomizations over fundamental certainty equilibria as it is in most of the existing literature. Since at such equilibria firms make their production decisions based on the correctly anticipated distribution of aggregate demand and their own idiosyncratic demand shocks, these self-fulfilling stochastic equilibria are consistent with rational expectations. Furthermore, we obtain such equilibria even though we have strategic substitutability in firms' actions: the optimal production of each firm is a declining function of other firms' total output. This implies that business cycle is a natural market outcome, which can be only avoided by carefully designed policies. We plan to characterize the desirable policies in our model and evaluate their welfare consequences too. We will also apply our framework, developed in the benchmark model, to financial markets. The objective is to capture the Keynesian beauty contest concept that asset price can be driven by sentiments, which can explain the excessive price fluctuations in equity markets. 凱恩斯曾猜想人們主觀情緒變化會導致總生產和就業波動。凱恩斯猜想通常被認為違背經濟學理性人這一基本假設而未引起足夠重視。本研究項目試圖證明凱恩斯猜想與理性預期模型並不矛盾。我們希望該研究能重新激發研究者對這凱恩斯經濟學思想的興趣。我們首先構造一個多企業模型。在模型中每個企業制定生產前面臨需求的不確定性。需求的不確定性來自兩個方面。首先總需求的變化可以導每個企業的需求變化。此外在總需求不變的情況下，消費者偏好的變化可以導致個別企業需求變化。通過市場研究， 企業能獲得一個帶有誤差的需求信號。企業根據該信號和對總統市場運行機制的了解決定生產。生產完成後，企業的實際需求決定個企業的產品價格。我們將證明， 在這一環境下企業由於分不清楚其需求變化的原因，將導致多重均衡和內生經濟波動。 有現有文獻， 經濟波動在我們模型並不是簡單的隨機化本來就存在的多均衡。因為在信息充分的情況下，均衡是唯一的。我們的模型要求企業預想總需求分佈跟時候實現的分佈一致，所以總需求的波動並不需要非理性經濟人假設。此外， 我們證明即是各企業產品替代品情況下依然會產生多重均衡。這意味經濟波動是人類經濟活動是不可避免的自然現象。只有通過慎密制定的經濟政策才可能消除經濟波動。 我們也將我們的基本模型擴展去研究金融市場。我們希望能證明凱恩斯的另外一個著名猜想： 股票市場就像選美比賽； 為了討好公眾評委會選擇公眾覺得漂亮的而非自己覺得漂亮的候選人。公眾的情緒從而會影響股票的價格。

693513.label: Realisation of objectives
693513.value: The project initially has four objectives. The main objective (objective 1) is to formalize the Keynesian insight that sentiments about aggregate demand can generate output and employment fluctuations. This objective is achieved in the paper entitled “Sentiments and Aggregate Demand Fluctuations”, published by Econometrica in 2015. The main idea is that firms’ production decisions must be made under imperfect information about expected consumer demand. Because of imperfect information in forecasting demand, consumer sentiments can matter in determining equilibrium aggregate supply. We find that despite the lack of any externalities or non-convexities in technology or preferences there can be multiple rational expectations equilibria. Fluctuations can be driven by waves of optimism or pessimism, or as in Keynes' terminology, by "animal spirits" that are distinct from fundamentals. A distinctive feature of our results is that in the sentiment driven equilibrium the underlying distribution of household sentiments is pinned down endogenously by deep structural parameters, and corresponds to the self-fulfilling distribution of actual aggregate output. We then extend the model to allow aggregate fundamental shocks (objective 2). We find that the model has a continuum of equilibria, which can be indexed by the variance of sentiment shocks. In other words, not only the level of aggregate output but also the volatility of aggregate output can both be endogenous and be driven by sentiment shocks. The aggregate level of output decreases with the variance of sentiment shocks. We can hence explain the intriguing phenomena that recessions often come with increased economic uncertainty, a well-documented empirical regularity business cycle studies. To achieve the fourth objective (objective 4), we incorporate this timing varying sentiment volatility into a DSGE model. We show the model can qualitatively explain the sharp rise of economic uncertainty in recessions. The third objective is realized in the paper “Private Information and Sunspots in Sequential Asset Markets”, published in Journal of Economic Theory in 2015. It is accomplished by studying a model where some agents have private information about risky asset returns and trade to obtain capital gains, while others acquire the risky asset and hold it to maturity, forming expectations of returns based on market prices. We show that under such a structure, in addition to fully revealing rational expectations equilibria, there exists a continuum of equilibrium prices consistent with rational expectations, where the asset prices are subject to sunspot shocks. Such sunspot shocks can generate persistent fluctuations in asset prices that look like a random walk in an efficient market. These sunspot-driven fluctuations capture Keynes' beauty contest notation, that people trade assets mainly based on their speculation on other people’s opinion instead on assets’ fundamentals.

693513.label: Major findings and research outcome
693513.value: This research project formalizes the Keynesian insight that consumer sentiments can generate large fluctuations in employment and production. In contrast to the conventional view that waves of optimistic or pessimistic sentiments are irrational behavior of economic agents, sentiment in our model are equilibrium phenomena when firms' production decisions must based on imperfect information in forecasting demand. The rational expectation equilibrium approach enable us to characterize the volatility of sentiments and hence make testable predictions on when and where such sentiment-driven fluctuations may arise. The project also formalizes another renowned Keynesian notation of "beauty contests", which asserts that financial markets are mainly driven by exuberant investors' sentiments. We show under imperfect information, exuberant financial market sentiments increase the price of capital, which signals strong fundamentals of the economy to uninformed investors and hence induce them to pay high price of capital, making sentiments self-fulfilling. The project produce two high quality publications at top-leading economics journals. The paper "Sentiments and Aggregate Demand Fluctuations " is published by Econometrica, arguably the most prestigious journal in economics. The paper "Private information and sunspots in sequential asset markets" are published by Journal of Economic Theory, another prestigious journal in economics.

693513.value: This project can be developed to understand many other puzzling phenomena such as excessive co-movement of asset prices, the excessive volatility of business cycles, and the counter-cyclic economic uncertainty. I will continue to pursue this line of research and apply financial support from RGC.

A large empirical finance literature has documented that sentiments are important driver of asset prices and business cycles. Our theory offers a novel explanation of this puzzling effects.
