700813.value: We have achieved the stated objectives; 12 papers have been published: Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. (4), Chem. Sci. (1), Chem. Commun. (2), Org. Lett. (1), Chem. Eur. J. (2) and Adv. Catal. Synth. (1). 10 presentations were delivered. Objective 1. Iron(III) complex supported on macrocyclic ligand (L = N,N'-dimethyl-2-11-diaza[3,3](2,6)pyridinophane) is an active catalyst for oxidation of water to oxygen using CAN, NaIO4 or Oxone as oxidant. Mechanistic study by spectroscopic methods and 18O-labelling experiments revealed that FeIV=O and/or FeV=O species are likely to be involved. Using CAN as oxidant at pH 1, the formation of FeIV=O intermediate was suggested. Using NaIO4 or Oxone as oxidant at pH 1, reactive FeV=O species with formula [FeV(L3)(O)2]+ was suggested by ESI-MS analysis. DFT calculations revealed that [FeV(L3)(O)2]+ is capable to oxidize water to oxygen with a reaction barrier of 15.7 kcal mol-1. [Chem. Sci. 2015, 6, 5891] A panel of chiral tetradentate N4 ligands and their iron and ruthenium complexes has been synthesized. Using these iron complexes as catalyst, cis-diols in up to 99.8% ee with 85% isolated yield were achieved in asymmetric cis-dihydroxylation (AD) of internal and terminal alkenes (both styrene and non-styrene alkenes) with H2O2 as green terminal oxidant and strikingly alkenes in limiting amount. This “[FeII-L1](OTf)2] + H2O2” protocol is applicable to both electron-deficient and -rich alkenes (14 examples, up to 1g scale). A related Fe(II) catalyst [(FeII-L2)(OTf)2] bearing chiral binaphthyl diamine unit was prepared, which exhibited promising enantioselectivity towards the AD of styrenes (up to 60% ee). Mechanistic studies revealed that a high-spin iron(III) η2-peroxide cationic species is responsible for the high enantioselective AD reaction. [Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2016, 55, 10253] We prepared the chiral [Fe(L-N5)]2+ complex with L-N5 ligand bearing terpyridine and camphor units. We found that this complex was catalytically active for intramolecular aziridination of allylic benzene to give aziridine in 76% product yield and 30% ee. ESI-MS analysis of the mixture of [Fe(L-N5)]2+ and PhI=NTs revealed the presence of high valent iron(V) bis-imido {[Fe(L-N5)](NTs)2}+ species. Addition of excess styrene into this mixture immediately quenched the {[Fe(L-N5)](NTs)2}+ signal intensity from 44% to 4% within 5 min with simultaneous regeneration of the [Fe(L-N5)]+ parent ion, renaissance of a very fast nitrene transfer reaction of {[Fe(L-N5)](NTs)2}+ of catalytic nature. Compared to previously reported [Fe(qpy)(NTs)2]2+ species detected by high resolution ESI-MS analysis responsible for C–H amination, the signal intensity of this {[Fe(L-N5)](NTs)2}+ ion was much higher under similar conditions. This suggests that highly reactive bis(imido/nitrene)iron species can be trapped and studied by using spatially congested ligands. (PhD dissertation of Dr. Kar-Yee Lam) Objectives 1 and 2. We prepared a series of ruthenium(VI) porphyrin complexes bearing axial bis-imido ligands [Ru(por)(NR)2]. X-ray crystal structure of [Ru(TMP)(N{Ar-Ar-p-OMe})2] (H2TMP = meso-tetramesitylporphyrin) revealed the presence of Ru=N bond by the shortened bond lengths of 1.829 and 1.824 Å (vs Ru–N bond of >1.95Å). The electrochemistry of these complexes was studied and their electronic structures were investigated by DFT calculation. Stoichiometric reaction of these ruthenium bis-imido complexes with cycloalkenes and benzylic hydrocarbons led to the transfer of the imido ligand to give the desired aziridines and amines, showing that the ruthenium bis-imido complexes are the reactive intermediates for the nitrene/imido transfer reactions. [Chem. Eur. J. 2014, 20, 11035] We have studied the reaction barrier for the generation of Ru-bis(imido) complexes [Ru(bpy)2(tmen-4H)]+ and [Ru(bpy)2(tmen-3H)]2+ from [RuII(bpy)2(tmen)]2+ (bpy = 2,2'-bipyridine; tmen = 2,3-dimethyl-2,3-butanediamine) and subsequent C–C bond cleavage and N–O bond formation reactions via DFT calculation. The proposed Ru-imido intermediate was consistent with the experimental findings from ESI-MS analysis. [Chem. Eur. J. 2014, 20, 15122] Objective 3. We found that ruthenium(II) porphyrin complex [Ru(TTP)CO] is catalytically active towards diimination of indoles with aryl azides as the nitrene source, giving the desired products in up to 94% isolated yields. This reaction features a high selectivity to diimination products and no monoimination products was detected in all entries. DFT calculation on the reaction mechanism revealed that a [RuVI(TPP)(NTs)2] species could be the reactive intermediate. [Chem. Commun. 2014, 50, 3373] We developed a “metal catalyst + PhI(OAc)2 + primary arylamines” amination protocol using [Fe(F20tpp)Cl] as catalyst. This catalytic method is applicable for both intra- and intermolecular amination of sp2 and sp3 C–H bonds (>27 examples), affording the amination products, including natural products such as rutaecarpine, in moderate-to-good yields. ESI-MS analysis and DFT calculations lend support for the involvement of {[Fe(F20tpp)(NC6H4-p-NO2)](PhI=NC6H4-p-NO2)} intermediate in the catalysis. [Chem Asian J. 2015, 10, 100] Ru(II) and Ru(IV) porphyrins [Ru(por)CO] and [Ru(por)Cl2] bearing bulky substituents can catalyze various C–N bond formation reactions with benzoyl azides. Ru(IV) porphyrins are the most reactive catalysts. Bulky aryl substituents on the porphyrin ligand can prevent Curtius rearrangement of reactive benzoyl nitrene species, which gives isocyanates as side products. ESI-MS analysis and DFT calculations suggests the involvement of a [RuV(Por)(NCOPhCl)(Cl)] intermediate. (Unpublished work by Mr. Ka-Pan Shing) Objective 4. We achieved oxidation of light alkanes with Oxone catalyzed by iron complexes containing neutral tridentate ligand and mono-anionic bidentate ligand. [FeIII(Me3tacn)(Cl-acac)Cl]ClO4 catalyzed the oxidation of ethane and propane with buffered Oxone at room temperature for 30 min to give the oxidized products with total TON of 3.0 and 16.3 respectively. Oxidation of cyclohexane by “[FeIII(Me3tacn)(Cl-acac)Cl]ClO4 + Oxone” has been achieved with over 40 product turnovers in just 5 min. A reactive oxoiron(IV) ligand-cation-radical intermediate has been characterized by high-resolution ESI-MS, UV-Vis absorption spectroscopy, DFT calculations, and 4K X-band EPR spectroscopy. [Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2014, 53, 798] We designed, synthesized and characterized a series of bis(NHC)ruthenium(II) porphyrin complexes. As a result of the stabilization of trans-M=CRR' / M=NR moiety by axial NHC ligand, these bis(NHC)ruthenium(II) porphyrin complexes show unprecedentedly high catalytic activity towards alkene cyclopropanation, carbene C–H, N–H, S–H and O–H insertions, alkene aziridination and nitrene C–H insertion with product turnover frequency up to 1950 min-1. The use of chiral [Ru(D4-Por)(BIMe)2] as catalyst led to highly enantioselective carbene/nitrene transfer and insertion reactions with up to 98% ee. Carbene modification of N-terminus of peptides at 37 oC has been achieved. DFT calculations revealed that the trans axial NHC ligand facilitates the decomposition of diazo compounds by stabilizing the metal-carbene reaction intermediate. [Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2014, 53, 2982] We have prepared several ruthenium complexes of tetradentate N4 ligands and their electrochemistry was studied. cis-Dioxoruthenium(VI) complex, cis-[(pyxn)RuVI(O)2](ClO4)2 (pyxn = N,N'-dimethyl-N,N'-bis(pyridin-2-ylmethyl)cyclohexane-1,2-diamine), was obtained from CAN oxidation of cis-[(pyxn)RuIII(O2CCF3)2]ClO4 in aqueous solution. This complex is a powerful oxidant with E[Ru(VI)/(V)] = 0.78 V (vs. Ag/AgNO3) in acetonitrile; E = 1.11 V vs. SCE (at pH 1) and a strong H-atom abstractor with calculated DO–H = 90.1 kcal/mol. In acetonitrile, this complex oxidized hydrocarbons with BDE up to 99.5 kcal/mol. cis-[(PDP)RuII(OH2)2]2+ (PDP = 1,1'-bis(pyridin-2-ylmethyl)-2,2'-bipyrrolidine), in combination with CAN as terminal oxidant, is an active catalyst for selective oxidation of tertiary and benzylic C–H bonds in alkane substrates, via a cis-dioxoruthenium(VI) intermediate. (Unpublished work by Dr. Chun-Wai Tse) Objective 5. Iron(III) porphyrin complex [FeIII(TF4DMAP)Cl] is catalytically active towards nitrene transfer reactions with arylazides under blue LED irradiation in dichloroethane at room temperature. Aziridination of alkenes and benzylic or unactivated C–H bond amination could be achieved in 40–99% yields. Control experiments showed that both the iron porphyrin catalyst and light are essential for the reaction. (Unpublished work by Dr. Yidan Du)

700813.label: Major findings and research outcome
700813.value: Some of the findings and research outcome from this project could be found in previous progress reports. In essence, we have accomplished the followings. [1] 12 publications in top international chemistry journals including Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. and Chem. Sci. [2] 10 presentations on this research topic were delivered in international conferences. [3] An important piece of work on the oxidation of light alkanes with Oxone as the terminal oxidant in the presence of iron catalyst was published in Angewandte Chemie International Edition 2014, 53, 798 as VIP paper. [4] With the use of iron(III) complexes supported on N4 chiral ligand, asymmetric cis-dihydroxylation of disubstituted alkenes were achieved with excellent enantioselectivity of up to 99.8% using H2O2 as terminal oxidant with alkene as the limiting reagent. The reaction could be performed in gram scale. [Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2016, 55, 10253] Further extension of the iron(III)-catalyzed reaction to tri-substituted alkenes led to the desired diols in up to 99.9% ee. (unpublished result) [5] By ESI-MS analysis and DFT calculation, we obtained a better understanding on the identity and electronic properties of the reactive high valent metal-oxo and metal-imido intermedates, and on the reaction mechanisms of the oxo- and nitrene/imido-transfer reactions. [Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2014, 53, 798 and 2016, 55, 10253; Chem. Eur. J. 2014, 20, 11035 and 15122; Chem. Asian J. 2015, 10, 100; Chem. Sci. 2015, 6, 5891] [6] Reactive ruthenium bis-imido complexes were synthesized and fully characterized. X-ray crystal structure of one of these complexes revealed a much shorter Ru–N bond of 1.82Å. Stoichiometric reaction of these complexes with cycloalkenes and benzylic hydrocarbons led to the corresponding aziridine and amine products, showing that the ruthenium bis-imido complexes are the reactive intermediates for the nitrene/imido transfer reactions. [Chem. Eur. J. 2014, 20, 11035] [7] New amination reactions, such as diimination of indoles with aryl azides [Chem. Commun. 2014, 50, 3373] and “metal catalyst + PhI(OAc)2 + primary arylamines” amination protocol using [Fe(F20tpp)Cl] as catalyst [Chem. Asian J. 2015, 10, 100] were developed, with the latter showing its application potential on the synthesis of natural product rutaecarpine. With the support of this GRF grant, novel cobalt porphyrin-catalyzed alkylcarbene transfer reactions were discovered. [Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2016, 55, 1810; Adv. Synth. Catal. 2017, 359, 2253] [8] Light-induced nitrene transfer reaction was achieved with arylazides as the nitrene source and iron(III) porphyrin complex as the catalyst. (Unpublished results)

700813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
700813.value: There is a great potential for further development of metal-oxygen or -nitrogen multiple bonded complexes in catalysis. We conceive that better understandings on the structures and reactivity of high valent reactive metal-oxo or -imido intermediates and mechanisms of action of oxo and/or nitrene/imido transfer reactions are essential for the further design of robust transition metal catalysts showing unprecedented reactivity and selectivity. Of particular interest would be to realize practical applications of selective activation of primary carbon-hydrogen bonds by the atom and group insertion reactions. Though we have obtained seminal achievements through this GRF project, further improvement of most of the reported reactions is needed prior to industrial applications. Realization of practical and robust transition metal catalysts for atom transfer reactions, especially the iron-based catalysts, may open an entry to new methodologies for chemical synthesis of invaluable complex organic compounds from saturated alkanes which are naturally abundant. This is also an emerging area of great interest in frontier chemical science in the forthcoming decades.

700813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
700813.value: This project has resulted in ground breaking works on catalytic oxidative reactions with the use of Earth abundant metal catalysts and on new methodologies for organic synthesis. Oxidation of light alkanes with Oxone, highly enantioselective cis-hydroxylation of alkenes with H2O2, and amination of primary C-H bonds with arylazides have been realized via iron catalysis. The mechanistic studies performed in these works could feedback to the further modification of the iron catalysts and other transition metal complexes, which is highly beneficial to the research fields of catalytic organic chemistry, inorganic and coordination chemistry. The results have already led to publications in top journals including four pieces of works in Angewandt Chemie International Edition and one in Chemical Science. New research areas on light-induced nitrene/imido transfer reactions and fine-tuning the reactivity of metalloporphyrin catalysts by axial carbon-based ligands have been resulted from this project. The accomplishments made in this project put Hong Kong as a world Center of Excellence in Synthetic Chemistry.

700913.label: Project Objectives
700913.value: Based on the wide-band-limit (WBL) approximation, a first-princples ac quantum transport theory had been developed by us, and confirmed with comparison against the time-domain simulation of corresponding transient current. In the first stage of this project, we will extend our theory beyond the WBL approximation. As such, the specific electronic structures of the electrodes will be taken into account, and their effects are included. A unresolved issue is the displacement current, for instance, how to distinguish its component to each electrode and evaluate its contribution to the total dynamic admittance. An accurate time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT) for quantum transport has been established and applied to simulate the transient currents through a series of molecular and nanoscopic deivces. It is based on the non-equilibrium Green’s function (NEGF) formalism, and is termed as the TDDFT-NEGF method. To confirm our new ac quantum transport theory, we will compare it with the results of the TDDFT-NEGF method. The steady state quantum transport through CNTs has been studied extensively, in particular, there are many theoretical studies on the subject. However, much less is understood about the ac current through CNTs. We will apply the new ac quantum transport theory to study the frequency dependent electric response of CNTs, in particular, CNTFETs. The sizes of the existing CNTFETs range from 9 nanometers to 100s nanometers. For CNTs with their lengths longer than the coherent length, the interaction between electrons and phonons is important. To account for this, we need to calculate the electronic self energy due to the coupling to phonon and include it as the part of the total self-energy. In addition, to simulate the CNTFETs of 100s nm in size, we need more efficient numnerical methods and algorithms. These would include the parallel computing on large computer clusters and to implement our theory with an approximate DFT method, density-functional tight-binding (DFTB) method.

700913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
700913.value: 電子器件的微型化極大地改變了我們的生活。與此同時，器件的頻率也越來越高。因此，我們需要發展交流量子輸運理論。 從1990年代起，這方面的工作就已經展開。1999年，一個唯像交流量子輸運理論出現，它滿足規範不變性和電流守恆，被廣泛接受，一直到近期。這兩年有幾個研究發現唯像交流量子輸運理論與含時量子輸運理論的結果相矛盾。突然，整個領域出現了混亂。我們由此出發，發展準確的微觀交流量子輸運理論。我們的理論滿足規範不變性和電流連續，但不要求電流守恆。我們會比較新的微觀交流量子輸運理論和含時量子輸運理論的結果。一旦新理論被驗證了，我們計劃利用新理論去研究納米碳管交流電學特性。硅半導體工業發展迅速，已經接近物理極限。基於納米碳管的晶體管很可能是下一代半導體場發射晶體管。在這個研究中，我們主要探討基於碳管的場發射晶體管的各種特性及其應用前景。

700913.label: Realisation of objectives
700913.value: We have derived a non-WBL ac quantum transport model based on DFTB, and have verified its accuracy by comparison against the well-established time-domain method (i.e., TDDFT-NEGF). In order to accommodate the increased computational cost, we have developed several fast numerical algorithms, e.g. the partial block inverse, which resulted in a speedup of over one order of magnitude for single-node solution. We have also developed techniques for massive parallelization and achieved nearly linear time reduction on over 100 CPUs using the computing resources in Shenzhen and Guangzhou supercomputing centers. We have derived a dissipative quantum transport model taking into account the quantum interference and electron-phonon interactions, which are important for accurate modeling of long devices, in a modified self-energy formulation. We have then improved the convergence speed of SCBA by developing a Gauss-Seidel type of nonlinear iteration scheme. With the theoretical and computational advancements, we have successfully simulated the dynamic response of CNTFETs of length up to 100nm, and analyzed the effects of different device lengths.

An accurate time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT) for quantum transport has been established and applied to simulate the transient currents through a series of molecular and nanoscopic deivces. It is based on the non-equilibrium Green’s function (NEGF) formalism, and is termed as the TDDFT-NEGF method. To confirm our new ac quantum transport theory, we will compare it with the results of the TDDFT-NEGF method.

The steady state quantum transport through CNTs has been studied extensively, in particular, there are many theoretical studies on the subject. However, much less is understood about the ac current through CNTs. We will apply the new ac quantum transport theory to study the frequency dependent electric response of CNTs, in particular, CNTFETs.

The sizes of the existing CNTFETs range from 9 nanometers to 100s nanometers. For CNTs with their lengths longer than the coherent length, the interaction between electrons and phonons is important. To account for this, we need to calculate the electronic self energy due to the coupling to phonon and include it as the part of the total self-energy. In addition, to simulate the CNTFETs of 100s nm in size, we need more efficient numnerical methods and algorithms. These would include the parallel computing on large computer clusters and to implement our theory with an approximate DFT method, density-functional tight-binding (DFTB) method.

700913.label: Major findings and research outcome
700913.value: 1. A non-WBL DFTB-based ac quantum transport theory has been derived, which demonstrated good match with the time-domain results. 2. A dissipative quantum transport models with explicit accounts for quantum interference and electron-phonon interactions for accurate modeling of long CNT devices. 3. An efficient software implementation integrating fast numerical algorithms and massive parallelization that enabled ac simulation of CNTFETs of 100nm length.

700913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
700913.value: For ac quantum transport theory, there are many directions for further pursuits and developments. First, the computational efficiency can be further enhanced by more advanced numerical algorithms and more effective parallelization. We have been currently investigating the selected inversion and a self-developed X-formulation method which showed promising results for further performance boost. Second, CNTFET is just one type of emerging nano-electronic devices. We may apply the developed ac quantum transport model to study other emerging devices such as tunneling FETs and junctionless transistors. Thirdly, we will investigate the inclusion of electron-photon interactions into the quantum transport model, which also requires modification of the self-energies. This will open up new opportunities for first-principle modeling of nano-optoelectronic devices that have numerous applications in different fields.

700913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
700913.value: Emerging electronic devices have been shrunk to nanometer size and their behaviours can only be accurately characterized by quantum mechanical models. While the steady-state quantum transport theories have been well-established and extensively applied, the frequency-domain counterpart, which is very useful in engineering practices, has not been fully available. The difficulties are due to physical complicatedness of ac quantum transport theories and the computational bottlenecks. In this work we proposed a capable yet high-efficiency model, which on one hand extends existing model to non-WBL and include electron-phonon interaction for better accuracy, and on the other hand addresses the performance issue by several new algorithms and massive parallelization. The new quantum transport model has been validated against the time-domain results, and applied to simulate CNTFETs of practical sizes. The success of the current project is expected allow scientists and engineers to evaluate and optimize new devices in computers before they are physically manufactured, leading to much faster development cycle and reduced cost.

701013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
701013.value: One of exciting discoveries by the Fermi gamma-ray satellite is detecting two giant gamma-ray-emitting bubbles in that extend nearly 10 kpc in diameter north and south of the Galactic center. The existence of the bubbles was first evidenced in X-rays detected by ROSAT satellite and later WMAP detected an excess of radio signals at the location of the gamma-ray bubbles. Quite a number of possible mechanisms that may contribute to the energy release and particle production necessary to explain the radiation emissions from the Bubble are proposed. All existing models can only provide partial explanation of all observed features. These features include (1) gamma-ray emission is quite uniform inside the Bubble but with a sharp edge, (2)a limb-brightening occurs in X-rays only, (3)radio intensity is fading rapidly perpendicular to the galactic plane etc. It has been proposed that the Fermi Bubble structure was created by some large episode of energy injection in the Galactic Center, such as a past accretion event onto the central supermassive black hole (SMBH) in the last 10 Myrs. Although our SMBH is not active currently, it can be activated to behave similar to active galactic nuclei after capture and tidally disrupt a star. These stellar capture phenomena have been observed in nearby galaxies. One important example of such events detected by the Swift X-ray satellite in 2011 is called Swift J1644+57. In the first two weeks the peak isotropic luminosity of Swift J1644+57 is about 3x10^48 erg/s, which is about 10^4 times larger than the Eddington luminosity of a million solar masses black hole. Due to this super-Eddington luminosity and the position of Swift 1644+57 relative to the center of its host galaxy, it is believed that Swift 1644+57 is powered by a relativistic jet created by accretion onto a several million solar masses black hole. There are strong observational evidences that similar processes have been occurred in our SMBH too. In this project we shall study the time dependent transient non-thermal emissions from the relativistic electrons accelerated by the forward and reverse shocks in the relativistic jets produced in the early stage of stellar capture process, which may explain some observed features similar to Swift 1644+57. We will also study possible consequences of the accumulated injected energies of the capture events in the past 10Myrs to see if they cause the observed properties of the Fermi Bubble. 能夠於銀河系中心的南北兩個方向觀測到兩個直徑近10 kpc 的伽瑪射線巨大光泡，是Fermi伽馬射線衛星最令人興奮的發現之一。這些巨大光泡的更早的存在證據包括被ROSAT衛星觀測到的X-射線以及後來被WMAP觀測過剩的無線電輻射存在於伽瑪射線光泡的位置。有很多不同的機制被提出來以解釋這些被釋放的能量的一部分，而粒子生產是其中一個必定機制。可是，所有現的的模型都只能解釋部分的觀測結果。這些現象包括 (1) 伽瑪射線的輻射量在光泡內非常平均，但有一個鋒利的邊緣。(2) 周邊發光的情況只在X-射線輻射出現。(3) 垂直於銀河平面方向，無線電輻射的強度迅速衰落等。有人認為這兩個光泡是由銀河中心射出的大量能量而造成的，如在一千萬年內恒星被吸積到中央黑洞的事件。雖然銀河系的中心黑洞已非在活躍，但類似的吸積事件或潮汐力撕裂恒星事件可令它如活躍星系的核心。這些恒星吸積現象有在附近星系中能觀察到，其中一個重要的例子就是在2011年Swift 衛星觀測到的Swift J1644 + 57。首兩星期Swift J1644 + 57的各向同性光度為3 × 10 ^48 erg/s，是大約100萬個太陽質量的黑洞的愛丁頓光度的10 ^4倍。由這個超愛丁頓光度以及Swift J1644 + 57在其宿主星系的位置看來，我們一般相信Swift J1644 + 57的能量來源為幾百萬個太陽質量的黑洞吸積事件所造成的相對論性噴流。有很強觀測證據說明類似的情形在我們的 SMBH也在發生。在這一個專題項目，我們會研究在早段恒星吸積事件所發出的相對論性噴流正向和反向衝擊加速的相對論性的電子所發出的時間依賴性瞬態非熱輻射，這可能能解釋Swift J1644 + 57的觀測現象。我們也會研究過去一千萬年內吸積事件的累計能量所可能帶來的情形以嘗試解釋Fermi觀測到的巨大光泡。

701013.label: Realisation of objectives
701013.value: For the first objective : “Study the direct emissions resulting from the stellar capture by the supermassive black holes including various shock acceleration mechanisms and emission processes of the charged particles at different evolution stages of the jet.” Swift J1644+57 is one of the most famous stellar capture event by the supermassive black hole observed by the X-ray satellite Swift in 2011. The observed luminosity from this source is 3-4 order of magnitude higher than the Eddington luminosity which leads to the conclusion that the observed X-ray emission is coming from the jet which is directly pointing to us. The Lorentz boosting effect can enhance the observed X-ray luminosity by 3-4 order of magnitude larger than the Eddington limit. Although its long term light curve is decreasing as expected, it shows multiple pulses behavior which cannot be explained by simple accretion model. In the standard model the light curve should decrease as t^-5/3, which is related to the time evolution of the accretion rate near the supermassive black hole. In pub. 3, we model the pulses as reverse shocks from collisions between the late ejected shells and the externally shocked material, which is decelerated while sweeping the ambient medium. The peak of each pulse is taken as the maximum emission of each reverse shock. With a proper set of parameters, the envelope of peaks in the light curve as well as the spectrum can be explained very well by our model. Since Swift J1644+57 is such important source for studying stellar capture processes. Many X-ray satellites including Chandra, XMM-Newtron and Swift have continued to observe this source from 2011 to 2016. After roughly 500 days after the capture the X-ray light curve drops even faster than exponentially. It is speculated that the accretion material in the disk may be exhausted. However after the light curve by 2 order of magnitude in only a few tens days, the X-ray light curve becomes flat for almost 3 years, which is totally unexpected. In pub. 6, we model this phenomenon by the Compton echo effect. In fact in our galactic center a very similar phenomenon has been observed. Some molecular clouds near the galactic center have been detected to emit intense X-ray flux one by one. It appears that they are lighted one by one by some external agency. Later it is proposed that actually a few hundred years ago, the galactic supermassive black hole became active and emit intense X-rays. But the X-rays cannot travel faster than speed of light, so the X-ray front emitted by the galactic supermassive black hole arrives these different molecular clouds one by one. The X-ray emission from these clouds can be very well explained by the Compton scattering of X-rays. We believe that the late time X-ray emission from Swift J1644+57 is exactly the same phenomenon. We can model the observed X-ray properties by choosing appropriate parameters of the cloud including the distance to the cloud, the density, size and configuration of the cloud near the supermassive black hole of Swift J1644+57. For the second objective : “Studying various high energy emission observed phenomena in the Galactic Center, which could result from the past stellar capture processes by the galactic supermassive black hole.” One of the possible consequence of stellar capture processes is the production of large amount of Cosmic Rays in the vicinity of the supermassive black hole. In pub. 2 we analyse the 6.4 keV iron line component produced in the Galactic Center (GC) region excited by cosmic rays in dense molecular clouds (MCs) and in the diffuse molecular gas. We choose Sgr B2 molecular complex to test our model calculation. We predicted that 6.4 KeV line from this cloud can be seen in several years. We strongly believe that the gigantic gamma-ray emission region located in the galactic center extended symmetrically north and south perpendicular to the galactic plane detected by the Fermi satellite, known as Fermi Bubble, is the consequence of the continuous past stellar capture events. We have estimated that the amount of power which is necessary to maintain the structure of the Fermi Bubble can be provided by the stellar capture events. The multi-wavelength emission from the Fermi Bubble result from shock acceleration processes. In pub. 1,3 and 5 we studied various acceleration mechanisms and emission processes in the Fermi Bubble. In pub. 1 We analyze processes of electron acceleration in the Fermi bubbles in order to define parameters and restrictions of the models, which are suggested for the origin of these giant radio and gamma-ray structures. In our analysis we found that the electrons must be produced in situ because their short life time is short due to energy loss processes including synchrotron and inverse Compton processes. Taking this assumption we studied how these electrons can be accelerated to relativistic energies via the stochastic acceleration by either a hydromagnetic or supersonic turbulence. We showed that the acceleration from the background plasma is able to explain the observed fluxes of radio and gamma-ray emission from the bubbles, but the range of permitted parameters of the model is strongly restricted. In pub. 4 we analyse the origin of the gamma-ray flux from the Fermi Bubbles in the framework of the hadronic model in which gamma-rays are produced by collisions of relativistic protons with the protons of background plasma in the Galactic halo. It is assumed in this model that the observed radio emission from the FBs is due to synchrotron radiation of secondary electrons produced by p-p collisions. However, if these electrons loose their energy by the synchrotron and inverse-Compton, the spectrum of secondary electrons is too soft, and an additional arbitrary component of primary electrons is necessary in order to reproduce the radio data. Thus, a mixture of the hadronic and leptonic models is required for the observed radio flux. However this model suffered some major set-backs, which required the magnetic field strength in the Fermi Bubbles and the power of Cosmic Ray sources are much higher than those followed from observations. In pub. 5 we analyse the model of stochastic re-acceleration of electrons, which are emitted by supernova remnants in the Galactic Disk and propagate into the Galactic halo, in order to explain the origin on nonthermal (radio and gamma-ray) emission from the Fermi Bubbles. We assume that the energy for re-acceleration in the halo is supplied by shocks generated by processes of stellar capture processes by the galactic supermassive black hole. We have done the numerical simulations which indicate that regions with strong turbulence (places for electron re-acceleration) are located high up in the Galactic Halo about several kpc above the disk. The energy of supernova remnant electrons that reach these regions do not exceed several GeV because of synchrotron and inverse Compton energy losses. At appropriate parameters of re-acceleration these electrons can be re-accelerated up to the energy 10^12 eV which explains in this model the origin of the observed radio and gamma-ray emission from the Fermi Bubbles.

701013.label: Major findings and research outcome
701013.value: Swift J1644+57 provides us a very important opportunity to study the direct emissions from the stellar capture events. The multi-wavelength observations can constrain the theoretical model predictions. The detail X-ray light curves of this source allow us to model the acceleration processes in the jet. Although the general trend of the light curve agrees with the standard model predictions, the details show that the light curve actually consists multiple peaks, which cannot be addressed by the standard model. In Pub. 3 we model these multiple peaks result from the reverse shocks produced by clumpy ejecta interacting with the ISM. In pub. 6 the long term light curve definitely beyond the standard model predictions we can explain the long term light curve in terms of well-known phenomenon observed in our own galaxy, which indicates that high density molecules also exist in supermassive black hole vicinity of other galaxies. In pub.1,2, 4 and 5 we study the multi-wavelength emissions from the direction of the galactic center. In particular the 6.4 KeV line from the molecular clouds near the galactic supermassive black hole (pub. 2) and the gamma-ray emission from the Fermi Bubble, both of them can be related to past stellar capture events which can be regarded as the energy sources for these two phenomena. We have carefully examined various acceleration mechanisms and radiation processes in the Fermi Bubble in pub. 1,4 and 5, we conclude that (1)stellar capture processes can be the possible energy sources for the Fermi Bubble and (2)the re-acceleration of supernova remnant electrons are more possible mechanisms for the radio and gamma-ray emission from the Bubble.

701013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
701013.value: We can extend our study to other active phenomena observed in the central region of the galaxies. There are some phenomena which are quite unique in this region. For examples some very high energy sources have been detected in GeV and TeV energy ranges but their origins are unknown so they are called "dark accelerators". Another example is that the cosmic ray intensities in the galactic center appear higher than those measured in the vicinity of the solar system. Do these phenomena relate to the activities of the galactic supermassive black holes, the active star formation region in the center or the extremely high supernova in this region ?

701013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
701013.value: In this project we try to understand some high energy phenomena observed in the galactic center. We find that one key reason makes the galactic center more special than other region in the galaxy, namely, the galactic center houses a supermassive black hole. Currently this black hole is inactive. However it does not mean it is inactive in the past too. According to the numerical simulations the supermassive black hole in the galactic center can capture a star when it enters the tidal disruption radius which is typically about 10^5 Schwarzchild radii. The captured star will be tidally disrupted and its mass will be accreted into the black hole. Part of accretion energy can be released to the vicinity of black hole via a jet. This amount of energy can result in many high energy phenomena, which are related to what we have observed. By modeling these phenomena we can infer the past activities of our galactic black hole.

701213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
701213.value: 同單調是一個成熟和在精算學和金融上很有用的概念。它描述了在相關結構中，變量總是在相同的方向上移動。這個概念有許多應用，如在風險計量的投資組合的風險，期權價格逼近，和一些資產配置問題。 Deelstra 等（2010）（An overview of comonotonicity and its applications in finance and insurance, Advanced Mathematical Methods for Finance (editors: Oksendal, Nunno) Springer, Germany）和 Dhaene等（2002）（The concept of comonotonicity in actuarial science and finance: applications, Insurance: Mathematics & Economics 31, 133-161）提供了這一概念的一個很好的概覽，最前沿的發展和應用。 Cheung（2009）（Upper comonotonicity, Insurance: Mathematics and Economics 45, 35-40）引入了同單調的泛化，稱為上同單調。這種新概念不僅放鬆了同單調這經典概念所施加的嚴格的條件，同時也保留了同單調各種好的解析性質。這個新概念的基本屬性之後被 Dong 等（2010）（Upper comonotonicity and convex upper bounds for sums of random variables, Insurance: Mathematics and Economics 47, 159-166），Cheung and Vanduffel（2011）（Bounds for sums of random variables when the marginal distributions and the variance of the sum are given, to appear in Scandinavian Actuarial Journal），和Nam 等（2011）（Characterization of upper comonotonicity via tail convex order, Insurance: Mathematics and Economics 48, 368-373）繼續研究。 相關結構，隨機排序，風險測量，最優化保險是現代金融經濟學和精算科學的主要議題，被廣泛研究。上部和尾部同單調正是在所有這些領域的交集。因此，進一步探討這個相對較新的概念和其上述領域的應用有重大的理論意義和實用價值。這個研究項目的主要目標是為這個概念建立一個鞏固的理論基礎，以便可以得到更充分的理解。各種同單調的現有理論結果和應用將推廣到上和尾部同單調。更具體地，這一研究項目的目標包括：1 ）研究尾同單調性質和特徵，及其與各種隨機排序和風險測量的關係， 2 ）利用尾上共單調和在尾上共單調（分）相加原則的基礎上其提出風險測量及保費計算的新公理，並研究相應的數學表達方式 ， 3 ）研究尾部行為和關係尾相依的相關結構， 4 ）應用理論到最優再保險和對沖問題。

701213.label: Realisation of objectives
701213.value: Overall speaking, the project has been completed very successfully. (Objective 1) Significant contributions have been made to develop the theory of upper and tail comonotonicity. The structure of upper and tail comonotonicity, tail mutual exclusivity, their relationships with the classical comonotonicity, mutual exclusivity and complete mixability, their probabilistic and asymptotic characterizations, and their properties in relation to various stochastic order are now much clear and well developed. The relationship between upper comonotonicity and comonotonic additive risk measures has been thoroughly studied. In particular, the additivity of TVaR and related distortion risk measures has been established. This lays firm foundation for various applications of this notion. (Objective 2) New notions of tail mutual exclusivity and multivariate countermonotonicity (called d-countermonotonicity) have been developed. Their various properties in relation to the underlying copulas and the concordance orders have been explored and characterized. The strength of the tail dependence can be reflected by some kind of threshold by construction, but general ways to compare the strength of multivariate countermonotonicity remains difficult unless extra structures are imposed. In general, the objective of establishment some new notions of stochastic ordering based on the degree of tail comonotonicity encounters some difficulty. In high dimensions, marginals interact in complicated ways, and it is difficult to describe the exact tail behavior except under trivial cases or very specific parametric families. Even under the structure of tail comonotonicity, the degree of tail dependence among different groups of marginals is hard to compare directly. After putting considerable effort, it seems that the difficulty of this problem is well beyond the original anticipation. (Objective 3) New risk measures and premium principles based on the idea of disappointment aversion, which is one of the key notions in behavioral economics, have been developed. Its properties and characterizations have been established. This new disappointment aversion premium principle has been shown to be closely related to comonotonicity, tail comonotoncity, and convex orders; it is also very useful providing realistic explanation to the behavior and choices of policyholders in insurance contracts. (Objective 4) Tail comonotonicity and upper comonotonicity have found wide applicability. These notions have been successfully applied to the study of optimal (re)insurance problems, effective hedging problems, and Pareto-optimal risk sharing problems. The tail comonotonic structure between the indemnity and the retained risk, which is one of the key assumptions made in most study in this area, allows us not only to decompose the objective functions (based on quantile-risk measures) into a decomposable integral form, but also unify the solution approach. Explicit solutions and insightful interpretations have been obtained. The notion of multivariate countermonotonicity has also been applied to solve a general class of optimization problem that is closely related to the notion of complete mixability. It has been shown that multivariate countermonotonicity is more general than classical complete mixability and this dependence structure can attain the minimum value of the variance minimization problem with fixed marginals. On the other hand, the notion of tail mutual exclusivity, under mild conditions on the marginals, was found to be the correct notion in characterizing the minimum of the expected value of a convex functional of the aggregate risk with fixed marginals. Asymptotic (varepsilon-optimal) results were also derived without any assumptions placed on the marginals.

701213.label: Major findings and research outcome
701213.value: (Outputs 1, 2, 4, 5) I revisited this notion and present versatile characterizations of mutually exclusive random vectors via their pairwise countermonotonic behaviour, minimal convex sum property, distributional representation and the characteristic function of the sum of their components. These characterizations highlight the role of mutual exclusivity in generalizing counter-monotonicity as the strongest negative dependence structure in a multidimensional setting. I studied the problem of finding lower bounds on three kinds of convex functionals, namely, convex expectations, Tail Value-at-Risk and the Haezendonck–Goovaerts risk measure, of a sum of random variables with arbitrary distributions. The sharpness of the lower bounds on the first two types of convex functionals was characterized via the extreme negative dependence structure of mutual exclusivity. Compared to existing results in the literature, our new lower bounds enjoy the advantages of generality and analytic tractability. I then generalized the joint mixability to d-countermonotonicity defined in Lee and Ahn (2014) through variance minimization problems and show that d-countermonotonic copulas are minimal copulas. I also extended the concept of mutual exclusivity to its tail counterpart and baptize this new dependency structure as tail mutual exclusivity. Several properties of this new negative dependence concept were derived. I showed that this dependence structure gives rise to the smallest value of TVaR of a sum of risks within a given Fréchet space, provided that the probability level of the TVaR is close enough to one. (Outputs 3, 6-10) A wide range of applications of the theory were studied. These include the study and generalizations of the classical Borch's theorem on Pareto optimal risk sharing, optimal insurance problems under general convex structures on both the objective functionals and the premium principles, the establishment of disappointment aversion premium principles and its use in the theory of optimal insurance, optimal risk-reducing hedging problems, and general minimization problems involving the expected value of a convex functional of the aggregate risk, such as the variance minimization problem, with fixed marginals. All results have been published in top international journals in actuarial science, and many of the findings have been presented in international conferences.

701213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
701213.value: Multivariate countermonotonicity remains one of the most challenging problems. There is no unifying way to define countermonotonicity in high dimensions. While this research project proposes tail mutual exlusivity and d-countermonotonicity as possible ways to model multivariate countermonotonicity, they are still special cases of even more general negative dependence structures. For instance, d-countermonotonicity specifies that risks after monotone transformation lie on a flat hyper-plane whose normal is positively oriented. This can obviously be generalized to other curved manifolds that are suitably oriented. The difficulty is that it is then very hard to describe and characterize mathematically. Nevertheless, this kind of structures could be useful when we study non-linear aggregation of risks.

701213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
701213.value: Dependence structures, stochastic orderings, risk measures, optimal insurance are the main topics under extensive study in modern financial economics and actuarial science. Tail comonotonicity lies at the intersection of all these areas. It is an abstract mathematical structure that models and describes possible interactions among various randomness in certain extreme situations. Therefore, it is of great theoretical and practical value to further explore this relatively new concept in the context of the above areas. This project builds a firm theoretical foundation of this notion so that better understanding can be gained, and paves the path for future applications. Various theoretical results and existing applications of comonotonicity have been extended to the case of tail comonotonicity and multivariate countermonotonicity. These abstract mathematical structures have found wide applicability in real world. In particular, many applications to financial economics and insurance have been studied, which deepen our understanding on how financial and insurance risks interact with each other and their impact of such interaction, and how such interacting risks can be managed and mitigated effectively. In particular, it is now understood how risks can be effectively hedged, how financial and insurance risks can be effectively and fairly shared among different companies, and how ordinary people should choose insurance coverage under the aversion of disappointment.

701513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
701513.value: Natural products have an excellent track record as leads for the development of successful pharmaceuticals. Although the ability of one organism to use another’s metabolites appears to be unpredictable, the enormous number of natural products and their structural diversity underwrite the chance of this kind of success. Among bioactive polycyclic natural products, a large number of them contain the carbobicyclo[m.n.1] framework. One example is the multi-drug resistance reversing natural product N-methylwelwitindolinone C isothiocyanate, which has the potential to be developed for cancer therapy. It contains the [4.3.1] carbobicyclic decanone as a core structure. The effective construction of these bicyclic frameworks is therefore essential for the synthesis of this and other related bioactive natural products. Our preliminary results show that the rhodium-catalyzed decomposition of fused bicyclic beta-hydroxy-alpha-diazoketones results in a skeletal rearrangement to form a range of bicyclo[m.n.1] systems. Therefore this reaction has the potential to be a single strategy or reaction type that could furnish a variety of functionalized bicyclo[m.n.1] systems and could be applicable to the synthesis of not just one, but a number of bioactive natural products. This proposal seeks to further explore this reaction, to determine its scope and its optimization. Based on these results, the synthesis of the important natural product, N-methylwelwitindolinone C isothiocyanate, will be studied based on the use of this reaction as a key strategy.

701513.label: Realisation of objectives
701513.value: The stated objectives have been largely achieved, but the final objective to study the total synthesis of the complex natural product within the timeframe was very challenging. 1. The scope of the reaction of the alpha-diazo-beta-hydroxyketones has been studied. A total of 18 substrates were synthesized, each of them via multistep syntheses. Their reactions have been investigated, and all of the products were elucidated. The majority of the diazoketones underwent rearrangement to generate bridged compounds as desired. The products synthesized included: bicyclo[3.2.1]octanediones, bicyclo[4.2.1]nonanones, bicyclo[3.3.1]nonanone , and bicyclo[4.3.1]decanones. After extending the scope of the substrates, we have also discovered some alpha-diazo-beta-hydroxyketones which rearrange to the fused bicyclic ketones by a competitive rearrangement. 2. Reaction parameters were investigated, including temperature and rhodium catalysts. Generally the best yields were obtained with Rh2(tfa)4 as the catalyst. A very low catalyst loading was effective. It was also found that the electron-rich bonds tend to migrate, giving us some ability to predict the products that would be formed in this reaction. 3. Many transformations of the bicyclo[m.n.1]products were investigated in the exploration of the synthesis of the core of the welwitindolinone family. 4. Two approaches were investigated to apply to the synthesis of the bicyclo[4.3.1]decane skeleton of the welwitindolinone family: (i) the rearrangement of a bicyclic[4.4.0]decane, or (ii) the rearrangement of a bicyclic [4.3.0]nonane followed by a one-carbon expansion. After exploring both routes, our studies found only the latter strategy to be viable. 5. N-methylwelwitindolinone C isothiocyanate is an extremely complex target. As a reference, Prof. John Wood, then at Yale University, first published efforts on the synthesis of this molecule in 1999 and finished the synthesis in a publication in 2006 with a dozen co-authors. Our studies also indeed required a lot of effort and time. Our methodology results were applied to a model study of N-methylwelwitindolinone C isothiocyanate. The model simplified the indole moiety to an aryl ring, and also avoided the steric hindrance of the gem-dimethyl group. In this context, the bicyclo [4.3.1]decane framework was successfully installed by a 14-step sequence. To further apply these results to a more closely related model, started from an indole substrate, also bearing the gem-dimethyl motif. The rhodium-catalyzed rearrangement was indeed successful, but it is still some steps away from the final target and some synthetic challenges still remain. The PhD student who is involved in this project is continuing the studies and he still has some time before he is due to graduate. Nevertheless, the results we have obtained so far should be applicable toward a total synthesis of this molecule or a closely related core.

701513.label: Major findings and research outcome
701513.value: 1. A series of alpha-diazo-beta-hydroxyketones were synthesized and their reactions studied. This was the first extensive study of this class of compounds. These studies have allowed us to prepare a range of bicyclo[m.n.1]alkanones using the same reaction type. This method would facilitate the synthesis of many types of bridged bicyclic frameworks of various bioactive natural products. 2. Previous work in this area were sparse and not many substrates were examined. Our extensive studies of 18 such compounds allowed us to better appreciate the factors affecting the desired rearrangement to yield bridged bicyclic compounds versus the competitive rearrangement that generates fused bicyclic products. We have found that the electron-density of the migrating bonds, the ring sizes and the activity of the rhodium-catalysts all impact the outcome of the reaction. We also have proof that the reaction proceeds via the intermediacy of a rhodium carbine. 3. Based on these results, we have applied them to the synthesis of the bicyclo[4.3.1] core of welwistatin, a natural product which shows anti-multiple drug resistance activity. Our model studies began with commercially-available dibromotoluene, then a 14-step sequence has yielded a phenyl-bearing product having the required bicyclic core, as well as having the vinyl chloride moiety on the 3-carbon bridge. 4. To address the indole moiety in welwistatin, we have also initiated another synthetic sequence, starting from a bromo-indole. We have been able to carry this forward through 8 steps to obtain the alpha-diazo-beta-hydroxyketone, and have also found that the rhodium-catalyzed rearrangement proceeds well to give a bicyclo[4.2.1]nonane framework. This sequence also addressed the gem-dimethyl substituents on the 4-carbon bridge successfully. We still need to complete the one carbon ring expansion to yield the bicyclo[4.3.1]decane, but we are confident that the previous results will enable us to complete the required transformation. Initially, our publication strategy was to combine all of the methodology and natural product synthesis results into one high-impact publication. However, as the final stages of the synthesis still require time to be realized, we have revised our publication plans. The methodology results (1, 2) has been submitted as a communication to the journal Organic Letters. The first model synthesis studies (3) is being prepared as another paper to Organic Letters. In due course we will complete the indole model and submit another publication based on that work.

701513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
701513.value: As we are still some steps away from the desired target, further work will be focused on transforming our most advanced intermediate to the bicyclo[4.3.1]decane framework as found in N-methylwelwitindolinone C isothiocyanate. After obtaining a series of complex bridged bicyclic intermediates, the compounds will be mined for their bioactive potential by screening as analogues of welwistatin for anti-drug resistance activity.

701513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
701513.value: Many biologically active natural products have complex, polycyclic structures. To synthesize them, methodologies to construct the polcyclic frameworks must be developed. We have studied and found that the rhodium-catalyzed rearrangement of fused bicyclic alpha-diazo-beta-hydroxyketones produced a range of bicyclo[m.n.1] alkanones effectively. These frameworks are in the core of many bioactive natural products. We have found the conditions and have built up an understanding of the reaction in order to be able to utilize it to synthesize desired targets. To demonstrate this, we are using this method that we have developed to further apply to the synthesis of a very important natural product, N-methylwelwitindolinone C isothiocyanate, which has many important biological effects including antifungal to microtubule depolymerization and reversal of P-glycoprotein multidrug resistance in cancer cells. Using our methodology, the bicyclo[4.3.1]decane framework of this natural product was successfully constructed.

701613.value: 氣相陽離子自由基導致沿肽骨幹和側鏈裂解工藝多元化的解離，從而揭示的結構信息。從這個提案中描述的研究，我們的目標是闡明的機制，熱力學和動力學，分子自由基肽離子的解離，我們專注於三個主要領域。 （一）首先，我們會評估骨幹中型和小型肽裂解產生異常[ Xn + H] +型片段，在這裡，我們將使用傳統的串聯質譜儀和低能量碰撞誘導解離 。 （二）接下來，我們將檢查氣相結構，熱力學，動力學和機制形成，使用原型肽系統和密度泛函理論計算，結合低能源CID實驗。 （三）最後，我們將決定實驗的熱力學和動力學中型肽Cα -C劈，導致個別的產生型片段，在這裡，我們將結合使用表面誘導解離實驗和的建模。我們預期此建議項目的結果將引發光異構化和形成之間的關係, 也將提供這種集成方式的根本基礎理解熱力學和動力學的激進網站重排.

701613.label: Realisation of objectives
701613.value: I have enjoyed productive collaborative experience funded recently by the research grant council ((Project Number: HKU 701613P). Our collective efforts have led to successful execution of the proposed project and result in significant contribution toward understanding of the gas-phase chemistry of peptide radical cations under low-energy CID. The initial phase of the project was devoted to elucidate the mechanism, energetics and kinetics of molecular radical peptide cations dissociation (objectives 1-3). Progress of this research was presented in ASMS (Mass Spectrometry) Conference as well as the upcoming Gordon conference-2017. An invited review article describing this work will be submitted for publication in chemical record. The details of the key results can be found in the attached manuscripts.This project has crystallized over 1 6 refereed articles, book chapters, and one review article, in the areas of gas phase chemistry of biological radical ions; new methodologies for biomedical analysis of molecular targets of downstream neurodegenerative processes; and the discovery of novel lead neuroprotective compounds. Two Ph.D. have been trained. A postgraduate student, Xiaoyan, Mu, who recently completed her Ph.D. defense, has been trained to perform research in biological mass spectrometry and structure and energetics calculations; she is co-supervised by the Co-PIs of the project for our interdisciplinary mass spectrometry-based ion-chemistry research. Xiaoyan attended intensive DFT computational calculation training in Christmas of 2015 and summer 2016 at the York University, Canada. . In the last phase of the project, we have extended the work to investigate the radical-mediated protein oxidation, stemming from our fundamental and bioanalytical chemistry research to the application of mass spectrometry on the molecular mechanisms of pathological processes under oxidative stress. Complementary to our fundamental research studies, we have developed efficient technologies with proven applications related to radical-mediated proteome-wide studies, as well as more-targeted studies of posttranslational modifications, including phosphorylation, glycosylation, and tyrosine nitration.

701613.label: Major findings and research outcome
701613.value: Our collective efforts have led to successful execution of the proposed project and result in significant contribution toward understanding of the gas-phase chemistry of peptide radical cations under low-energy CID. The initial phase of the project was devoted to elucidate the mechanism, energetics and kinetics of molecular radical peptide cations dissociation with focus (a) to initially evaluate the fundamental parameters facilitating Cα–C backbone cleavage of medium- and small- sized peptides to generate unusual [xn + H]•+ type fragments—using conventional tandem mass spectrometers under low-energy collision-induced dissociation (CID). A manuscript describing the fundamental parameters facilitating Cα–C backbone cleavage of medium- and small- sized peptides to generate unusual [xn + H]•+ type fragments." has been published in the Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 2014 (objectives 1-2 in Part B 5.1/5.2. Another four manuscripts describes the first study of the alpha-Radical-induced CO2 loss from the aspartic acid side chain of the collisionally induced tripeptide aspartylglycylarginine radical cation; and of the Ground and Excited-Electronic-State Dissociations of Hydrogen-Rich and Hydrogen-Deficient Tyrosine Peptide Cation Radicals. The details of the key results can be found in the manuscripts (objectives 2-3 in Part B 5.1/5.2). The structural an mechanistic features that facilitate radical peptide fragmentation and and its chemically modified analogs incorporating methylation have been elucidated using a combination of Rice–Ramsperger–Kassel–Marcus modeling and density functional theory. (objectives 3-4 in Part B 5.1/5.2). The mechanistic role of various radical–centered intermediates in prior to the Cα–C bond cleavage have been examined using DFT calculations and RRKM modeling on prototypical system. Novel nucleophilic substitution by amide nitrogen in the aromatic rings of [zn - H]+ ions; another manuscript describing the work of radical cations nucleophilic substitution by amide nitrogen in the aromatic rings of [zn - H]+ ions; the structures of the [b2 - H - 17]+ and {C1 - 17]+ ion." has been published in the Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys., 2016, 18, 11168--11175 (DOI: 10.1039/c6cp00405a). These studies have provided insight into the intrinsic factors—the role of the radical and charge site(s) as well as their mobility— that governs Cα–C backbone cleavage through a variety of rearrangements and isomerization leading to the subsequent dissociation toward the observation of the [xn + H]•+ product ion.

701613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
701613.value: Our fundamental research stems from our ongoing interest in obtaining an in-depth understanding several hallmarks of radical-induced peptide chemistry to shed light on the mechanisms of biological processes under oxidative stress. In the last phase of the project, we have extended the work to investigate the radical-mediated protein oxidation, stemming from our fundamental and bioanalytical chemistry research to the application of mass spectrometry on the molecular mechanisms of pathological processes under oxidative stress. Complementary to our fundamental research studies, we have developed efficient technologies with proven applications related to radical-mediated proteome-wide studies, as well as more-targeted studies of posttranslational modifications, including phosphorylation, glycosylation, and tyrosine nitration. Recent implementations of our MDLC technologies into commercial off-the-shelf instruments have been exemplified in our invited book chapters] and some of our recent articles [Anal. Chem. 2014 & 2015]. Progress of this research was presented in ASMS (Mass Spectrometry) Conference as well as the upcoming Gordon conference-2017. An invited review article describing this work will be submitted for publication in chemical record. The details of the key results can be found in the attached manuscripts.

701613.value: The research project on in Dissociation of Molecular Radical Cationic Peptides: Structures, Energetics, Kinetics, and Mechanisms of Cα–C Backbone Cleavage Toward [xn + H]•+. Formation been funded for 2013 Competitive Earmarked Research Grants application. We have examined the mechanisms, energetics, and kinetics of individual competitive dissociation reactions of peptide radical cations using a combination of biological tandem mass spectrometry (MS) experiments. Gas-phase fragmentation of a variety of odd-electron peptide radical ions has been provide a scientific basis underlying the establishment of reliable strategies for sequencing peptides in the gas phase; in which generate new peptide sequence information and, ultimately, protein identification via database searching in mass spectrometry-based proteomics; confident protein identification relies heavily on the ability to unambiguously sequence assignment of the resulting collision-induced dissociation (CID) spectra under low-energy conditions. 701813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
701813.value: In contrast with the intense study on the hole-doped manganites which showed variety of specific characteristics such as colossal magnetoresistance (CMR) and electroresistance (ER) effects, the research on the electron-doped manganites were very rare. To develop n-type manganites, substitution of tetravalent ions (Sn4+; Ce4+; Sb4+; Te4+) for trivalent La ions in LaMnO3 were reported. However, arguments were raised on whether it is intrinsically n-type conductive mechanism in these systems due to the existence of multi-valence of these doping elements. This research was triggered by our recent success in developing a novel Hf4+ doped LaMnO3 manganite (LHMO). Our preliminary results proved that such a LHMO is clearly electron doped as Hf shows sole tetravalence only. The realization of electron-doping provides a true and reliable n-type manganite for construction of all manganite p-n junctions and further detailed investigation. The heterojunctions composed with LHMO showed excellent rectifying behavior in a wide temperature range, which is comparable with those pn-junctions made of classic semiconductor. It makes LHMO to be a very promising candidate for fabricating all-manganite p-n junctions, which should be magnetically tunable. In this project, we will develop all manganite p-n junctions or heterojunctions using this n-type LHMO. Such heterostructures combining with n- and p-type CMR mangnites may emerge some fascinating features, like the switching of rich functionality and extreme sensitivity. Our efforts will be focused at the field effect, magnetic tunability and optoelectronic sensitivity. This research is of potential to develop novel functional field-effect transistors based on manganite perovskites. 本项目拟利用4价铪离子掺杂来获得电子导电型钙钛矿锰氧化物并展开氧化物p-n结器件的研究。我们近期的研究表明，四价的铪离子能有效替代钙钛矿锰氧化物中部分镧离子，形成电子导电型的锰氧化物。相比于其它掺杂离子（如Sn4+; Ce4+; Sb4+; Te4+等），铪的原子半径合适且具有单一价态，从而保证真正电子导电型的锰氧化物的合成。我们初期工作还显示，由镧铪锰氧化物构成的p-n结在宽温区都具有优良的整流特性，是发展全氧化物p-n结和场效应器件的理想材料。 我们将通过外加各类物理场，从微观和宏观尺度上系统研究外场下的电磁耦合及量子调控效应，探测其丰富的量子现象，并通过电光磁的多场调控，研究锰氧化物p-n结或异质低维体系中亚稳特性的变化规律，揭示其亚稳态中出现的物理过程。从微观角度理解非欧姆特性（如场致电阻、磁电阻）与电荷有序畴之间的关系，阐述相分离体系中场致电阻和磁电阻效应的关联及其内在机理。本项研究不仅对深入理解钙钛矿型锰氧化合物中亚稳特性和量子调控的物理机制具有重要意义，而且对探索电流/电场敏感的新型电子功能器件具有实际意义。

701813.label: Realisation of objectives
701813.value: The goal of this research is to develop all oxide heterojunctions based on electron-doped manganite. All three proposed objectives have been fully addressed. Successful fabrication of all-oxides heterostructures composed with electron doped La1-xHfxMnO3 (LHMO) is essential for this study. ABO3 manganites were integrated with different oxides by means of PLD. X-ray diﬀraction demonstrated that our samples were of good a good epitaxy and crystallinity. The temperature-dependent resistance has been investigated. It was observed that the as-grown film of LHMO exhibited a typical paramagnetic-ferromagnetic transition. Compared to those hole-doped manganites-based junctions, much stronger rectifying characteristics were observed in the formed junctions. Especially heterojunctions of LHMO/Nb-doped SrTiO3 exhibited much asymmetric I-V characteristics and remarkable temperature-dependent rectifying behavior in a wide temperature range, showing advantages of these junctions. The second objective is the investigation of structural characteristics, transport properties, and optoelectronic response in the formed heterojunctions and thin films of LHMO. To address this objective, various techniques were used to study effects of electric currents/fields on the transport of LHMO films and heterojunctions. We observed significant decrease of the peak resistance (Rp) with increase of the applied currents, showing a giant ER effect. Abnormal ER effect was examined as well. The matestable states induced by applied currents/fields and excitation time is clearly manifested. These heterojunctions showed much stronger rectifying characteristics and superior photoelectric response in comparing with other junctions. The rectifying ration reached ~103 at room temperature. In addition, these heterojunctions exhibited a remarkable photoelectric effect in a broad temperature range from 40 to 300 K, which is comparable to the best results reported on p-type manganite. It is notable that, under illumination of a light of 532 nm wavelength, the Voc dropped from 700 mV to 120 mV as the temperature increasing. These results revealed the feasible manipulation of electrical transport of LHMO/Nb-STO junctions by light irradiation, and suggested that these junctions can be good optoelectronic devices based on manganite perovskites. Strain effect on transport and meta-stability were systematically investigated in the formed hetero-structures through the whole project. Tunable colossal MR and ER effects were gained in heterostructures composed with manganite and ferroelectrics. We applied a constant current to a micro-bridge to excite manganite into metastable states. The feasibility to modulate electric and magnetic properties by tunable strain was achieved by using PMN-PT crystal. Our studies show that many metastable properties of manganite and ferroelectrics, like magnetoresistance (MR), electroresistance (ER), M-I phase transition, and photoconductivity, are strongly related to the lattice deformation, e.g. modulated throughthe converse piezoelectric effects of PMN-PT. For comparison, heterostructures made of hole-doped manganites were studied as well. It was found that the leakage current versus voltage curves show strong dependence on temperature. The I–V curves presented diode-like asymmetric characteristics. The switching coefficient increases with the elevated temperature. Such switching conduction might be of interest for nonvolatile memory applications. To achieve the third objective, i.e. to explore the field tunable character of these manganite-based junctions, we have systemically studied influence of magnetic field and lattice strain on rectifying behavior, diffusion/breakdown voltage and junction resistance etc. Strong dependence of magnetic and electric properties on lattice deformation as well as magnetic fields was observed. The resistance of LHMO exhibits different responses to the external fields. The field modification of charge/orbital ordering phase implies sensitivity to external fields like lattice strain. Such manipulative features by E/M fileds or light irradiation exhibit great potential for all-oxides functional sensors and detectors.

701813.label: Major findings and research outcome
701813.value: In this project, rich variety of physical properties and superior junction behavior were observed in heterojunctions composed with mixed-valence manganite and ferroelectrics. The major findings obtained in this project include: 1. Heterojunctions composed with electron doped manganite LHMO were epitaxially formed.[1-3, 5, 9] They showed excellent rectifying characteristics and pronounced tunability by applied fields, providing great feasibility for potential applications.[5, 9, 12, 22] 2. Such LHMO films and junctions revealed significant metastable properties, like magnetoresistance (MR),1electroresistance (ER),M-I phase transition,and photoconductivity.[1,3,5] 3. Optical response of these electron-doped perovskites under tunable strain fields were explored.[5, 9, 22] LHMO presented persistent and stable photovoltages upon light illumination. Rapid shift between small and large voltages corresponding to “light OFF” and “light ON” states, respectively, was observed, demonstrating reliable photo detection behavior. The injection of photoexcited charge carriers (electrons) could be responsible for the observed opto-response. 4. The LHMO compound demonstrated that their M-I phase transition, MR and ER effect strongly depend on the lattice strain.The competition between coexisted multi-phases could be also mediated by the applied strain induced by piezoelectric effect.[4, 7, 11] 5. Field effects on such heterojunctions were systemically studied.[12] Their transport properties are tunable electrically and magnetically. Photoinduced resistance was also observed as illuminated by visible light. The induced PR could be greatly enhanced by the compressive strain. 6. Different heterostructures by using such tunable metastability, like the field effect devices, heterojunctions, as well as switching memory devices,were designed and explored.[14, 18, 21] 7. Our efforts were also focused at heterojunctions composed with manganite and ferroelectric. Field control of magnetism, as well as ferroelectrically and magnetically co-coupling was observed.[20, 21] It is of great the potential to develop novel functional field-effect transistors based on manganite perovskites. 701813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
701813.value: In carrying out this research, we have developed all manganite heterojunctions by using electron-doped manganite oxides. These junctions can have excellent rectifying characteristics and superior photoelectric response. It was revealed that the junction properties could be modulated by external fields and lattice deformation. Sucha metastability is an intrinsic feature of electron doped manganite and it may even lie at the core of the phase separated perovskites. Further investigation and development may focus at the heterostructures of manganite and ferroelectrics. The integrated system combining manganite andferroelectrics is expected to emerge some fascinating features, like the switching of rich functionality and optoelectronic sensitivity.

701813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
701813.value: Heterojunctions composed with electron-doped manganite were developed successfully. Such junctions demonstrated excellent rectifying characteristics and superior photoelectric response in comparing with those junctionsmade of hole-doped manganite. Also, these heterojunctions showed remarkable MR and ER effects. Their properties can be modified by external fields and lattice strain. Such fascinating features, including controlled switching of rich functionality, the strong field effect, sensitive photoconductivity (PC),tunable metastability, give rise to the boostresearch interest and potential to develop novel functional sensors and devices.

702413.label: Project Objectives
702413.value: We propose to investigate the probability of capture into the 2:1 and 3:1 resonances by convergent differential migration. Differences in how they depend on migration rate, planetary masses, and orbital eccentricities may explain the observed differences in the number of planet pairs near the 2:1 and 3:1 resonances. We will investigate whether the near-resonance pairs discovered by the Kepler space telescope, which are mostly super-Earths and Neptunes, could be explained by improved migration theory for planets in this size range that allows outward migration in some regions of the protoplanetary disk. We will investigate whether a similar model could explain the lack of nearby planetary companion for the hot Jupiters (Jupiter-sized planets orbiting very close to their host stars). We will use our grid-based parameter exploration code to perform dynamical fits of the radial velocity data of systems with planets or substellar companions in orbital resonance.
