702413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
702413.value: Recent advances in the search for planets around other stars have led to a significant increase in the number of known extrasolar planetary systems with multiple planets, including many with pairs of planet in or near mean-motion resonances. The statistics of these planet pairs, as well as the orbital properties of individual systems, provide important constraints on the formation and dynamical evolution of planetary systems. (1) We propose to investigate the probability of capture into the 2:1 and 3:1 resonances by convergent differential migration. Differences in how they depend on migration rate, planetary masses, and orbital eccentricities may explain the observed differences in the number of planet pairs near the 2:1 and 3:1 resonances. (2) We will investigate whether the near-resonance pairs discovered by the Kepler space telescope, which are mostly super-Earths and Neptunes, could be explained by improved migration theory for planets in this size range that allows outward migration in some regions of the protoplanetary disk. (3) We will investigate whether a similar model could explain the lack of nearby planetary companion for the hot Jupiters (Jupiter-sized planets orbiting very close to their host stars). (4) We will use our grid-based parameter exploration code to self-consistently model the radial velocity data of systems with planets or substellar companions in orbital resonance. 天文學家已發現許多擁有多過一個行星的太陽系外行星系統，其中包括一些在共 振軌道（或非常接近共振軌道）的行星對。我們可以用這些行星對的統計，以及個別系外行星系統的軌道特性，來約束行星系統形成和演化的理論。（1）我們將研究觀察到的 2:1 和 3:1 共振行星對的數目差異是否基於不同行星的遷移率，質量，及其他因素。（2）我們將研究改進的行星遷移理論能否解釋開普勒太空望遠鏡發現的近共振行星對。（3）我們將研究類似的行星遷移理論能否解釋為何非常接近其主星的類木行星 的附近缺乏其他行星。（4）我們將會使用我們已經研製的計算機程序去模型共振軌道行星系統的視向速度觀察數據。

702413.label: Realisation of objectives
702413.value: We have used our grid-based parameter exploration code to model the radial velocity data of the star HD 73526. The HD 73526 system was known to have a pair of Jupiter-mass planets in 2:1 mean-motion resonance, but the previous fit to the data showed that one of the two resonance angles associated with the 2:1 resonance is circulating. Sudden perturbative effects from planet-planet scattering or rapid disk dispersal have been invoked to explain the circulation of one of the resonance angles. We have collaborated with Wittenmyer et al., who have obtained six years of new radial velocity data from the Anglo-Australian and Magellan Telescopes on this system. We have investigated both Keplerian and dynamical fits to all available data, using a parameter grid search to ensure a global search for the best fit. We have also investigated how the goodness-of-fit and long-term dynamical stability depend on the inclination of the coplanar orbits. There is no clearly preferred system inclination from dynamical stability tests, but the nearly edge-on dynamical fit provides the best combination of goodness-of-fit and long-term dynamical stability. We have analyzed the radial velocity data of the K giant star eta Ceti taken at the Lick Observatory by CoI Quirrenbach et al. The data clearly show two periodicities that are most likely caused by two planets with minimum masses of 2.6 and 3.3 Jupiter masses and orbital periods of about 407 and 740 days, respectively. The dynamical fit to the radial velocity data is a significant improvement over the double-Keplerian fit, but the best fit is highly unstable. We have performed dynamical fits and stability tests in parameter grids for different orbital inclinations. Edge-on fits give two regions of stable fits to the radial velocity data: a narrow region about 1 sigma from the best fit, with the two planets in 2:1 mean-motion resonance; and a wider region more than 3 sigmas from the best fit, with the planets on non-resonant, nearly circular orbits. Stability analysis of coplanar inclined fits shows that the planets cannot be more than ~ 1.4 times heavier than their minimum masses. We have performed dynamical analysis of the nu Ophiuchi system, which was reported to have two brown dwarf companions with minimum masses of 22 and 25 Jupiter masses orbiting the K giant star with periods close to 6:1 in ratio. Our analysis combined published radial velocity data with measurements taken at the Lick Observatory by CoI Quirrenbach et al. We studied large set of orbital configurations based on bootstrap analysis and systematic chi-square grid search coupled with our dynamical fitting model, and we examined their long-term stability. We also tested a large set of coplanar inclined configurations and found that, unless the inclination is very small, neither the goodness-of-fit nor dynamical stability is sensitive to inclination. After the grant period started, we found that other groups have already examined some aspects of the implications of the improvement in the theory of type I migration on the near-resonance pair discovered by the Kepler space telescope and the lack of nearby planetary companions for the hot Jupiters. So we decided to turn our attention to two important problems that utilize the expertise of the postdoctoral fellow Trifon Trifonov, who was working with the PI during the grant period. For the 6:1 resonance in the nu Ophiuchi system described above, as well as the 5:1 resonance in the HD 202206 system (which has an inner brown dwarf and an outer planet with minimum masses of 17 and 2.2 Jupiter masses, respectively), we have performed 3-body simulations with forced migration of the outer companion to constrain the conditions for assembling these high order resonances. The effects of different initial orbital eccentricities and migration rate, as well as the conditions needed to pass through other resonances, were examined. The radial velocity due to two planets in 2:1 resonance can mimic and be misinterpreted as that due to a single planets on an eccentric orbit, especially if the radial velocity curve is sparsely sampled or the measurement errors are large. We have started a new observational programme aimed at finding hidden multiple-planet systems. We have been awarded observing time with the high-precision HARPS spectrograph on the ESO 3.6m telescope and other instruments, and we have been monitoring the radial velocity of a total of ~ 45 stars previously known to host a single planet. For HD 27894, which was previously known to have a Jupiter-mass planet, we have analyzed the new data with archival HARPS data to discover 2 additional planets, with the inner two planets having a period ratio close to 2:1. The best fit does not show libration of the 2:1 resonance angles for the inner pair, but systematic variations of the orbital parameters within their uncertainties showed that the inner pair could be in 2:1 resonance. We have investigated the probability of capture into the 2:1 resonance by the convergent differential migration of planets. We have performed large sets of numerical 3-body integrations with forced migration using the symplectic integrator SyMBA to examine how the probability depends on migration rate, planetary masses, and initial orbital eccentricities. We examined (1) the circular restricted 3-body problem (in which one of the planets is massless and the other is on a circular orbit), where analytic results exist in the adiabatic limit, (2) the elliptical restricted 3-body problem in the adiabatic limit, and (3) the general non-restricted problem (in which both planets are massive), which is more applicable to extrasolar planets. In the circular restricted 3-body problem, unlike the 3:1 resonance, where the numerical results agree with the existing analytic results in the adiabatic limit, we found a discrepancy in the capture probability as a function of the test-particle eccentricity for the exterior resonance. In the adiabatic limit of the elliptical restricted 3-body problem, unlike the 3:1 resonance, the critical eccentricity of the test particle for certain capture does not decrease with increasing planet eccentricity for the interior resonance.

702413.label: Major findings and research outcome
702413.value: Our analysis of the two-planet system around the star HD 73526, with the addition of new radial velocity data, has shown that both of the 2:1 mean-motion resonance angles are librating about 0 degree, which means that it is no longer necessary to invoke sudden perturbative effects to explain the circulation of one of the resonance angles. A journal paper has been published. We have discovered a new two-planet system around the star eta Ceti. The planets are most likely in an anti-aligned 2:1 resonance configuration. Stability constraint on the orbital inclination excludes the possibility of two brown dwarfs and strongly favors a planetary system. A journal paper has been published. We have found that the two brown dwarfs orbiting nu Ophiuchi are locked in 6:1 mean-motion resonance, with all six resonance angles librating around 0 degree. The 6:1 resonance shows that very likely the two brown dwarfs formed like planets in a circumstellar disk and were captured into resonance through disk-induced convergent migration. A journal paper has been submitted. For the 6:1 and 5:1 resonances in the nu Ophiuchi and HD 202206 systems, which are the highest order mean-motion resonances discovered to date, we have determined the conditions for capture into the observed resonance configurations by disk-induced convergent migration of the companions. For nu Ophiuchi, migration significantly slower than type I migration rate and nonzero initial eccentricities are required. A journal paper will be submitted. We have discovered that the star HD 27894 hosts a Saturn-mass planet likely in 2:1 resonance with the previously known Jupiter-mass planet, and a more distant massive planet. It is the first extrasolar planet system to show signs of an asymmetric 2:1 resonance. This work has been published as a Letter to the Editor in Astronomy & Astrophysics, which is for "important new results that require rapid publication." We have studied how the probability of capture into the 2:1 resonance by convergent differential migration of the planets depends on migration rate, planetary masses and orbital eccentricities and how it differs from the 3:1 resonance. The critical migration rate for certain capture decreases with increasing inner-to-outer planet mass ratio, and there is no strong oscillatory behavior in the capture probability as a function of eccentricities in the equal mass case. A journal paper will be submitted.

702413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
702413.value: Our dynamical radial-velocity fitting code and bootstrap parameter distribution code can be used to perform detailed analysis of other extrasolar planetary systems to characterize their current dynamical states and to infer constraints on their formation and dynamical history. We have already analyzed some planetary systems in binary star systems, and are working on planetary systems that are being discovered by the on-going CARMENES survey of low-mass M dwarf stars. We have also been developing and testing new tools, such as the inclusion of stellar jitter as a fitting parameter and a Markov Chain Monte Carlo code for parameter distribution. We are continuing with the observational programme aimed at finding hidden multiple-planet systems. We have already been awarded additional observing time with HARPS and other instruments. From the observations obtained so far, at least 9 of our targets are likely to have a second planet. We are continuing to observe HD 27894 in this programme, and a better measurement of the orbital parameters of the inner pair of planets will allow us to determine whether they are really in an asymmetric 2:1 resonance configuration.

702413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
702413.value: We have investigated the dynamics and origins of extrasolar planetary systems. In particular, the systems with planets in resonances provide important constraints on the formation and dynamical evolution of planetary systems. A pair of planets can be captured into resonances by converging differential migration due to interactions with the protoplanetary disk during formation. (1) We have improved the orbital parameters of the pair of planets in 2:1 resonance around the star HD 73526 to show that they are consistent with assembly by smooth migration. (2) We have discovered a pair of planets orbiting eta Ceti that are likely in 2:1 resonance. (3) We have found that the two brown dwarfs orbiting nu Ophiuchi are locked in 6:1 resonance, the highest period ratio resonance known to date. (4) We have discovered two additional planets in the HD 27894 system, with two of the three planets likely in an asymmetric 2:1 resonance configuration that was only known as a theoretical possibility. (5) We have investigated how the capture into the 2:1, 5:1 and 6:1 resonances is affected by migration rate, planetary masses, and initial orbital eccentricities.

702613.label: Project Title(Chinese)
702613.value: 分位數時間序列模型的統計推斷

702613.label: Project Objectives
702613.value: Develop a tool to identify the order of a QAR model. This will be achieved by introducing the definitions of the new correlation, the quantile correlation, the quantile autocorrelation function (QACF) and the partial QACF. We will establish the cut-off property of the partial QACF for the QAR process, and derive the asymptotic distribution of the sample partial QACF. Develop tools to check for the adequacy of a fitted QAR model. This will be achieved by the introduction of the residual QACF, followed by the derivation of their asymptotic distribution, and the construction of a goodness-of-fit test. Develop bootstrapping approximations for the corresponding asymptotic distributions in Tasks 1 and 2. This includes an approximation for the asymptotic variance of the partial QACF of an observated time series and the QACF of the residuals. Develop tools to check for the adequacy of a fitted GARCH model by the quantile estimation method. Computer programs will be developed to study the large-sample property and the finite-sample performance in Objectives 1-4 and applications to real data such as value-at-risk estimation will be considered. Clearly, the objectives only reflect part of the possible developments in this area. Many other developments, such as the moving average-type quantile model and even model selection methods in high dimension, are also possible if time permits.

702613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
702613.value: Due to its easy interpretation, the autoregressive (AR) model is often used to explain the mean structure of a time series, however, there are more and more requirements in real applications to model the structures of certain quantiles of the sequence. It leads to the recent popularity of the quantile AR model and the quantile nonlinear AR model in many areas. In the meanwhile, the tools for their statistical inference are not as well developed as in the classical AR models. When compared with linear time series modeling as expounded in Box and Jenkins (1976), quantile AR modeling is still in its infancy, and there are many problems open. This motivates us to develop some new tools and methods in this area. It is noteworthy that correlations or autocorrelations play a key role in AR or even ARMA modeling. This project first proposes a new type of correlations, called quantile correlations, which play a role similar to the classical correlations. Using this new type of correlations, we can define the quantile autocorrelation function and the partial quantile autocorrelation function for a time series, based on which we can develop new tools for the identification and diagnostic checking of quantile AR models. A conditional density is involved in the corresponding asymptotic distributions, and a feasible bootstrapping approximation is also developed that facilitates statistical inferences. 由於其易於解釋，自回歸模型經常被用來擬合一個時間序列。但是在實際應用中，有越來越多的研究者對一個時間序列的分位數更感興趣。這使得分位數自回歸模型和分位數非線性自回歸模型最近非常流行。然而，他們的統計推論的工具卻非常缺乏。注意到，Box-Jenkins 方法廣泛的應用在線性時間序列自回歸建模中。這促使我們發明一些類似的工具來進行分位數自回歸建模。 注意到，相關係數或自相關係數在線性時間序列自回歸建模中扮演了一個重要的腳色。這個項目主要發明了一個新的相關係數，它的名字叫分位數相關係數。我們類似地又定義了分位數自相關係數，並把它們應用到分位數自回歸建模中。注意到，大樣本的方差包含了一個難以估計的條件密度函數。因此，我們同時又提出了一個便於實施的bootstrapping近似工具。

702613.label: Major findings and research outcome
702613.value: 1) A new measure for the relationship between two random variables and its application in time series. This finding was published at the Journal of the American Statistical Association (one of top four statistical journals). Refer to Li, Li and Tsai (2015) at Part C. 2) Discovering the role of climate on epidemics in Ming and Qing China. This finding was published at the Social Science and Medicine. Refer to Pei, Zhang, Li, Winterhalder and Lee (2015) at Part C. 3) Discovering the relationship between climate and macroeconomic structure in pre-industrial Europe. This finding was published at PLoS ONE. Refer to Pei, Zhang, Li and Lee (2015) at Part C. 4) A diagnostic tool for the adequacy of fitted autoregressive conditional duration models. This finding was published at the Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference. Refer to Zheng, Li and Li (2016) at Part C. 5) A new type of vector autoregressive models. This finding was published at the Annuals of Statistics (one of top four statistical journals). Refer to Zhu, Pan, Li, Liu and Wang (2016) at Part C.

702613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
702613.value: The proposed quantile correlation coefficient and its applications in time series can be applied to the modeling of all kinds of time series models with quantile inference. In addition, with slightly adjustment, it may have wider applications in other areas such as integer-valued time series. Finally the proposed network vector autoregressive model can be applied to interpret many high dimensional time series with network structure.

702613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
702613.value: This project introduced a new measure for the relationship between two random variables. It can be considered as the counterpart of the commonly used correlation coefficient in quantile inference, and enjoys many good properties of it. Especially the partial quantile correlation coefficient has been similarly defined. In the scenario of time series, this project has designed the quantile autocorrelation function (QACF) and the quantile partial autocorrelation function (QPACF). These two functions have been shown to be similar to their counterpart, ACF and PACF, repectively. As a result, a bridge between the classical Box-Jenkins' three stage modeling method and the quantile inference for time series has been established. This makes the quantile time series modeling easily implemented, and we may expect many following researches.

702813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
702813.value: Protein glycosylation is one of the most abundant protein post-translational modifications (PTM) to account for the complexity in higher or complicated organisms. Cell surface carbohydrates are involved in many cellular events, including viral and bacterial infections and cell-cell interactions. Protein posttranslational glycosylation is characterized by its heterogeneity, wherein several glycoforms are usually generated with potentially different biological properties (“glyco-codes”). To systematically explore the evolutionary and functional significance of such heterogeneity, homogeneous glycoproteins with the defined glycan structure are required. In contrast to biologically controlled methods, chemical synthesis can provide the glycosylated peptides or proteins with high purity and homogeneity, enabling the structure-activity relationship to be established. Although past decades have witnessed the development of increasingly sophisticated methods for glycopeptide synthesis, synthesizing a glycoprotein is still seen as a daunting task. This project seeks to extend a chemical peptide ligation strategy that we recently discovered to the convergent synthesis of glycoproteins. We aim to synthesize the glycosylated adiponectin collagenous domain and the relevant analogues. Adiponectin is a circulating glycoprotein selectively produced from adipocytes. Decreased adiponectin production is involved in the pathogenesis of insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, steatohepatitis and cardiovascular diseases. Adiponectin treatment for diseases related to adiponectin deficiency could be of major therapeutic benefit. Adiponectin contains four domains: signal peptide, variable region, collagenous domain and globular domain, with the collagenous domain being glycosylated. It will be beneficial if a minimal structure capable of eliciting the required pharmacological agonist activities could be identified. However, the difficulty in accessing the glycosylated adiponectin collagenous domain via the recombinant synthesis process has impeded detailed study of the function of this domain. This motivates us to study the structure-activity-relationship of adiponectin via a chemical approach. We expect that the chemical synthesis of the glycosylated adiponectin collagenous domain will be achieved, providing enough material to evaluate its structural and functional contributions to the adiponectin activity. In addition, a range of analogues with glycan mutations will be synthesized and evaluated to examine the relative impact of individual glycan on stability, activity and secondary structures. 蛋白質糖基化修飾作為廣泛存在的蛋白質翻譯後修飾形式之一，是高等微生物複雜性的重要構成因素。細胞表面多醣參與多種細胞過程，包括病毒、細菌感染與細胞-細胞相互作用。蛋白質翻譯後糖基化修飾具有非均一性的特徵，即可形成多種糖型，而不同糖型蛋白潛在的生物活性亦不相同。因此，對糖蛋白的進化與功能進行系統研究，有賴於獲取具有確定多醣結構的均一糖蛋白樣品。較之於生物學手段，化學合成途徑能夠製備具有高純度與均一性的糖肽和糖蛋白樣品，從而使相應的結構-活性關係研究成為可能。在過去的數十年中，為數眾多的精細合成方法被發展並應用於糖蛋白合成。然而，時至今日，糖蛋白的合成往往仍被視為一項艱鉅的任務。本課題項目旨在擴展本課題組今年來發展的基於絲氨酸/蘇氨酸殘基的多肽化學連接方法，研究其在糖蛋白匯聚合成中的應用。我們將合成糖基化的脂聯素蛋白膠原結構域，並合成具有不同糖基化程度的結構類似物。 脂聯素是一種由脂肪細胞產生的循環蛋白。脂聯素產生水平的降低與胰島素抵抗，II型糖尿病，脂肪肝，心血管疾病等病理過程密切相關。對脂聯素缺乏性疾病進行脂聯素治療具有良好的效果。脂聯素分子由四個結構域構成，分別為信號肽，可變區，膠原結構域，以及球狀結構域。其中膠原結構域具有糖基化修飾，且具有多個糖基化位點。目前，脂聯素生物活性所需的最小結構尚待確定。由於通過重組技術合成糖基化的膠原結構域尚面臨重重困難，故對該結構域活性的深入研究尚難以開展。這一現狀促使我們採用化學合成途徑對該結構域進行結構-活性關係研究。我們計劃對糖基化的膠原結構域進行合成，為生物活性研究提供充足的樣品。在此基礎上，通過合成具有不同糖基化模式的膠原結構域類似物，研究單個多醣結構對該結構域的穩定性、活性和二級結構的影響。

702813.label: Major findings and research outcome
702813.value: Protein glycosylation is an important class of protein posttranslational modifications and plays a key role in cell-cell interaction and signaling. Protein posttranslational glycosylation is a heterogeneous process that usually generates several glycoforms with potentially different biological properties (“glyco-codes”). Homogeneous glycoproteins with the defined glycan structure are needed to be able to systematically explore the evolutionary and functional significance of such heterogeneity and to develop glycoprotein-based therapeutics. In this context, protein chemical synthesis offers invaluable tools to generate homogenous glycoproteins correlating their structure with their function. Nevertheless, development of new and effective methods and strategies towards the chemical synthesis of glycoproteins is an important task. We have recently developed a chemoselective peptide ligation via serine/threonine residues. As serine and threonine residues are well present in glycoproteins, it is conceivable that the serine/threonine ligation could be an invaluable tool in the preparation of homogeneous glycopeptides and glycoproteins. In this project, we have successfully demonstrated the effectiveness of serine/threonine ligation in the preparation of the glycosylated adiponectin collagenous domain (42-107) and glycosylated interleukin-25. A decrease in the production of adiponectin, a circulating glycoprotein selectively produced from adipocytes, is involved in the pathogenesis of insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, steatohepatitis and cardiovascular diseases. Therefore, using adiponectin treatment for such diseases could be a highly beneficial approach. Of the four domains in adiponectin—signal peptide, variable region, collagenous domain and globular domain—the collagenous domain is glycosylated. The structure-activity-relationships of the individual domain within adiponectin have not been well defined; the minimal active motif is thus not yet clear. Many studies have focused on the globular domain, which can be readily obtained. The globular domain is found to be less active than the full-length protein. The glycosylated adiponectin collagenous domain cannot easily be accessed using the recombinant synthesis process, thus hampering detailed study of this domain’s function. Upon completion of this project, we have generated 8 analogues of the glycosylated adiponectin collagenous domains with different glycoforms for study on their structure-activity relationships via chemical synthesis. Our preliminary anti-cell proliferation studies have shown that the glycopeptide with two glycosylations at 68 and 77 had the best anti-cancer activities.

702813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
702813.value: From 8 obtained analogues of the glycosylated adiponectin collagenous domains with different glycoforms, we have identified that the glycopeptide with two glycosylations at 68 and 77 exhibited very potent anti-cancer activities, comparable to the glycosylated full-length adiponectin. This result is indeed very promising. There are four glycosylation sites adiponectin collagenous domain. To establish a comprehensive structure-activity relationship, we will need synthesize all possible glyco-variants from mono-glycosylatiion to tetra-glycosylation with different combination at different sites. However, with the constrained budget of the current grant due to significant cut from the applied amount, we have synthesized 8 analogues. We plan to apply for a "continuous grant" to complete the synthesis of all glyco-variants and study their anti-cancer activities, from which we will select the most potent one for its in vivo anti-cancer activities in mouse models.

702813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
702813.value: Adiponectin is a circulating glycoprotein selectively produced from adipocytes. Decreased adiponectin production is involved in the pathogenesis of insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, steatohepatitis and cardiovascular diseases. Adiponectin treatment for diseases related to adiponectin deficiency could be of major therapeutic benefit. However, the difficulties in producing adiponectin limit its therapeutic application. We plan to apply chemical synthesis to access the glycosylated adiponectin collagenous domains with which to search for the minimal structure of adiponectin capable of eliciting the required pharmacological agonist activities. In the regard, we have successfully synthesized the glycosylated adiponectin collagenous domain and its glyco-variants that are otherwise difficult to obtain, and we have discovered one analogue to exhibit the comparable anti-cancer activity as the full-length adiponectin. This finding will open up new opportunities to develop adiponectin-based novel therapeutics.

702913.label: Project Objectives
702913.value: The culturing of scytonemin-producing cyanobacteria, the extraction and characterization of scytonemin for further experiments. Candidates of scytonemin-producing cyanobacteria: Lyngbya sp., Calothrix sp., Scytonema javanicum and Synechococcus sp. Physical and chemical properties of scytonemin-containing biomass, pigments extractions and relatively pure materials under simulated thermal metamorphic conditions. Materials will be mixed with pure clay minerals, pure hematite, mixture of clay minerals plus hematite, and those materials mixing with Fe(II) and methane for high P-T experiments. The temperatures will be 100, 200 and 300ºC and pressures will be 1, 2 and 5 kbar. The measured Raman spectra with known physical and chemical processes will be verified by theoretical calculations and mass spectroscopic measurements. The theoretical calculations of Raman and infrared spectra of scytonemin, its reduced structure and various putative derivatives produced by Gaussian 09 software by high performance computing service at the University of Hong Kong. Combing the experimental and theoretical Raman spectroscopic results to construct a diagnostic model for rapid detection of scytonemin in banded iron formation, black shale and stromatolitic carbonates. Confidence levels will be given to evaluate the quality of data. The measurements of scytonemin, its reduction form, derivatives and various fragments produced under simulated geothermal metamorphic conditions by liquid chromatographic mass spectroscopy (LC-MS). Scytonemin treated under simulated geothermal conditions after reacting with various inorganic and organic reductants will be extracted and analyzed by LC-MS. The detected fragments of scytonemin will be combined with the observed putative Raman spectra and the theoretical calculated results to establish diagnostic criteria for understanding the geothermal changes of this molecule in sedimentary rocks. Scytonemin as a major component of kerogen. This is a more challenging approach that will not be counted as a promising objective. The Raman bands of scytonemin at ~1320 and ~1600 per cm sometimes show broadened peaks overlapping the D-peak and G-peak of kerogen, respectively. We speculate that scytonemin and its mixture with some other organics after thermal metamorphisms may have or produce chemical bonds between C and (C, N, O) that show kerogen-like structure/composition. We will test if these reaction pathways could provide new clue on the structure and thermal evolution of organic matters toward kerogen.

702913.label: Realisation of objectives
702913.value: The realisation of objectives is a combination of field trip, laboratory works on cell culturing, wet-chemistry, theoretical calculations, electron microscopic measurements of the high resolution structures of materials and vibrational spectroscopic identification of trace signals of organic matters in the collected earth materials. Object 1 is the base for many further studies. We chose Scytonema sp. strain FACHB-633 from collaboration for produce more scytonemin. Scytonemin extracted from biomass were not purified because it may give signals between those in the natural earth materials and the pure chemical. This part of work was carried out in my Geobiology laboratory where we do our routine bacterial culturing and wet-chemical analysis. The extracted scytonemin containing materials would be mixed with clay minerals, synthesised iron oxides for reactions that were used to simulate the natural processes in sedimentary environments (Object 2). Our theoretical calculations were mostly carried on a PC with upgraded computing performances (Object 3). The Object 4 is directly linked to the writing of research paper to interpret the combined measured results and calculated data. The approach of Object 5 was similar, but we did not actually measure peaks of scytonemin by LC-MS because in the meantime the other international groups reported the LCMS results of scytonemin and some calculated results. We are the first group that calculated the changes of Raman signals along with the decomposition of scytonemin and the combinations of scytonemin molecules and their trend to show Raman profiles similar to that of kerogen with numerous reports. Though we have list objectives that can convince the reviewer that we have clear plan and roadmap for our research, we still got surprise in the middle of our exploration. Biosignature of ancient rocks generally includes organic and inorganic. We realised in the middle of study that magnetite in banded iron formation, which has long been considered a biogenic mineral and invested by numerous researches trying to extract biological information, is partially abiotic. This thought led to some extra experiments that ended up to a paper on Earth and Planetary Science Letters. This journal is the best in fields of Earth and planetary sciences at large. Our results will have significant impact on the understanding of interactions between ocean, atmosphere and biosphere in the long Archean re-interpretation of REE and Fe-isotopic data on magnetite from banded iron formation. The result is better than what we expected in the plan. We investigated the fate of organic matter in the sedimentary materials/rocks with long evolution in the geological time. It is common that the the organic materials at the end of the evolution contain more hydrogen on the structure, while oxygen on the precursors would eventually be removed. This thought led to a hypothesis that what it should be if a biochemistry has no participation of active oxygen. We then calculated the stability and energy change for a few hypothesised molecules on which oxygen is replaced by -NH groups. Results is very interesting because it can provide an energy process on Titan, and this study gives a starting point of a living world different from us in biochemistry. The result was very welcome by the journal Astrobiology (November issue of 2017). This publication turns to a very interesting part of this study that is not previously expected. As banded iron formation is a typical marine sedimentary rock of early Precambrian, we wonder where did the clay mineral go because clays are common in the ocean sediments. So we went field trip to North Tibetan plateau to find a sedimentary basin with serial sedimentary strata from relative ancient time to the relatively recent environment, to collect clay materials for comparative study. Besides the measurements as we planned, we find those clay materials coexisting with salts representing strong evaporative environments and they make large structures that are stranger to Earth but share high similarities with those find on Mars. We devoted some of our time on this direction and it led to two research papers on the astrobiological aspects of these materials and the large-scale structures they made. These results do not fall in any of the objectives we listed but is, however, within the scopes of our astrobiological approaches as written in our proposal.

702913.label: Major findings and research outcome
702913.value: Here I list 3 major findings: 1. In our paper on Earth & Planetary Science Letters (2017) we proposed a new genesis of magnetite in banded iron formation. Our proposal will have significant influence on the study of banded iron formation in understanding the evolution of early Precambrian ocean, atmosphere and life by elemental and stable isotopic geochemical methods. Our just published paper has been discussed in depth by the other recent research papers. 2. In our paper on Astrobiology (2017) we proposed a completely new theory of biochemistry for LIFE AS WE DON'T KNOW IT. In this theory, we evaluate a set of potential biochemical molecules on which oxygen is absent. We also calculated the energy change of reactions that changes related to energy metabolism. This result will shed some new lights on the possible life in a world similar to Europa on which the billion years of atmospheric process produced a huge amount of organic matter. NASA is very interested if its chemistry can be anyhow related to biological processes. I think this is a very interesting paper because the first day of its publication, we get 4 emails requesting reprints of this work. 3. Our paper on Journal of Geophysical Research: Planet is one of the two earliest research papers that describe a corner of North Tibetan Plateau as a Martian analogue. This is an important discovery because China needs a Martian analogue to test its scientific and technological contents for her Mars Exploration. Based on this study, my group and a research group from Chinese Academic of Science collaborated to expand our study on this topic. This will make our group one of the most group in China whose focus are Martian analogue and Martian geology, which are important for Chinese Martian 2020 missions.

702913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
702913.value: Our paper on Earth & Planetary Science Letters in 2017 proposed a new mechanism for the genesis of magnetite and hematite microbands in Precambrian banded iron formation, which will shed some new lights on the future Fe-isotopic studies, new interpretation of REE geochemical data and the Archean oceanic chemistry. We have recently started to investigate the REE modals of banded iron formation with separated hematite and magnetite; Our paper on Astrobiology in 2017 proposes a completely new biochemistry for a world of life where oxygen is depleted, the next step will be the further calculations on the large potential biochemical molecules similar to peptide or RNA; Our paper on Journal of Geophysical Research: Planet has already led to a new field of study in my research group. There are two faculty members from Department of Earth Science of the University of Hong Kong are also very interested in the field we developed and are interested to collaborate for expanded researches.

702913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
702913.value: Earth has a history of 4.56 billion years; while life on Earth likely has a history of about 4 billion years. We are curious on how did life start and what the early biosphere was like. We know that the early microbes used photo or chemical energies to support their life and their activities could change the chemical conditions of their environments that resulted in the formation of some biogenic minerals. The geologically long time of such process might produce gigantic amount of those so-called "biosignature", which could be preserved for a few billion years until now. A careful scrutinisation of those rocks allows us to find out evidence of life existed in the deep time. The identification of mineral records of life on Earth can also be applied to the search for the similar markers of putative life on Mars, which is believed to also have habitable conditions as the early Earth. In this study we used various methods, including theoretical calculation, electron microscopic observation and vibrational spectroscopic methods, to stay the different feature of biogenic materials of different ages so as to establish criteria for tracing the ecophysiology of early life on Earth, and maybe elsewhere.

703313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
703313.value: Many physics and engineering problems involve locating the zeros of polynomials and their derivatives. The zeros of the first order derivative of a polynomial of one variable are called critical points and the precise locations of them will provide important information of the polynomial itself. It is also important to know the location of these critical points relative to the location of the zeros. For example, Gauss (1836) noted that the critical points can be considered as the equilibrium points of the electrical field whose charges were placed at the zeros. The famous Gauss-Lucas Theorem (1879) then says that the critical points must lie in the closed convex hull of the zeros. The Gauss-Lucas Theorem is about the general location of all the critical points relative to all the zeros. A more refined result was conjectured in 1958 by B. Sendov: if all the zeros lie in the closed standard unit disk, then for each zero, the closed unit disk centered at the zero must contain at least one critical point. Sendov conjecture remains unsolved although attempts to verify this conjecture have led to over 100 papers. In 2011, it was pointed out that the late Borcea has suggested a new approach to Sendov conjecture through the introduction of his p-variance conjecture where p≥1. Borcea noted that Sendov conjecture will follow if his conjecture is true for any particular p. So far, very little is known for Borcea's conjecture. In the first part of this project, the PI will apply techniques in matrix theory to show that Borcea’s p-variance conjecture is true for some large classes of polynomials. In the second part of this project, the PI will take a probabilistic approach to study the location of the critical points relative to the zero set. This approach was initiated by Rivin and the late Schramm in 2001. But the precise formulation of it was given by Pemantle and Rivin in 2011. Roughly, they conjectured that for a degree n polynomial whose zeros are chosen i.i.d. from a probability measure m supported on a subset of the complex plane, the critical points will converge in distribution to m as n trends to infinity. In the second part of this project, the PI will study a stronger conjecture when the mode of convergence is almost sure (a.s.) and the critical points are replaced by the zeros of various kinds of derivatives . 許多物理和工程問題都涉及多項式及其導數的零點定位。單變量多項式的一階導數之零點稱為臨界點，臨界點的精確位置提供關於多項式本身的許多重要信息。而臨界點與零點的相對位置亦同樣重要。例如，高斯（ 1836年）指出，臨界點可以被視為電荷位於零點的電場的均衡點。著名的高斯 - 盧卡斯定理（1879年）說，所有臨界點必須位於零點的凸包內。高斯 - 盧卡斯定理是關於所有臨界點對於所有零點的相對位置的一般結果。更精確的推測是由B. Sendov 在1958年提出：假設所有的零點都位於閉標準單位圓內，則以每個零點為圓心的閉單位圓內，必包含至少一個臨界點。 Sendov猜想至今仍未解決，但是嘗試驗證這個猜想的論文已有百餘篇。在2011年，有人指出，已故的Borcea曾提出透過他的p -方差猜想(p ≥ 1)來引進一個解決Sendov猜想的新方法。 Borcea指出如果可以證明他的猜想對任一特定的p是正確，則Sendov猜想是對的。到目前為止，對於Borcea猜想的認識還很少。在此項目的第一部分，首席研究員將應用矩陣理論來證明對一大類多項式，p -方差Borcea猜想是正確的。在此項目的第二部分， 首席研究員將採用概率論的方法來研究臨界點相對零點的位置。此進路是由Rivin和已故的Schramm在2001年提出。但它的精確陳述是Pemantle 和Rivin在2011年給出的。簡略地說，他們猜測，假設一個n次多項式的零點遵從相同而互相獨立的概率測度m，此概率測度m的支集為複平面上的一個子集，則當n趨向無窮大時，臨界點將分佈收斂到m。在這個項目的第二部分，首席研究員 將研究當收斂模式為幾乎處處收斂時和以其他不同導數的零點取代臨界點時，Pemantle 和Rivin的猜想是否成立。

703313.label: Major findings and research outcome
703313.value: The PI and his co-workers have applied the more general version of the D-companion matrix introduced by Cheung and the PI in 2010 to prove the strong Pemantle and Rivin’s conjecture for polar derivatives and eventually for the first order and any higher order derivative when the support of the probability distribution of the zeros is the unit circle. This work settles the strong Pemantle and Rivin’s conjecture when the support of the probability distribution of the zeros is the unit circle. The results have been published in Computational Method and Function Theory in 2015 and the PI has presented the results in a number of occasions. Following Z. Kabluchko's solution of the Pemantle and Rivin's conjecture for polynomials (in which the convergence of the measure is assumed to be almost everywhere), the PI and this co-workers showed that the Pemantle and Rivin's conjecture holds for random finite Blaschke products. This is the first probabilistic item in the polynomials versus finite Blaschke products dictionary. The PI and his former PhD student PL Cheung have presented the results in several occasions. The result was published in the conference proceedings of the 9th International Society for Analysis, its Applications and Computation (ISAAC) Congress, Krakow, Poland (August 2013) published in 2014. The PI also brings in the method of D-companion matrix to study Borcea’s p-variance conjecture and show that the 1-variance and 2-variance conjectures are true for some large class of polynomials in a talk at the CMFT2013 meeting. The PI has trained one PhD student P.L. Cheung who has completed his degree in 2014. As a side product of P.L. Cheung's studies on zeros of polynomials, we also studies zeros of systems of polynomials and it application to prove the finiteness of fixed equilibrium configurations of point vortices in the plane with a background flow. The results are published in Nonlinearity. The PI also supervised an undergraduate Mr. Yongquan Zhang for a project on dual Smale's mean value conjecture and we obtained the strongest result of this conjecture so far. The results are published in The Journal of Analysis in 2017.

703313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
703313.value: Results similar to our results on strong Pemantle and Rivin’s conjecture are studied by for critical points of characteristic polynomials of random matrix ensembles (Haar distributed on O(n), SO(n), U(n), Sp(n)) by O’Rourke recently.

703313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
703313.value: Many physics and engineering problems involve locating the zeros of polynomials and their derivatives. This project studies what happens to the location of critical points if one randomizes the location of zeros. A regular behavior of the critical points was conjectured and partially proved in 2011 and 2012 in two papers. The PI and his collaborators have completely solved this conjecture. This leads to other mathematicians to consider similar results in other directions, like random matrices.

703513.label: Project Objectives
703513.value: Study the reactions of selected arylnitrenium ions with protonated guanine monomer derivatives in acidic aqueous solutions using time-resolved resonance Raman spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations. These results will be compared to those previously obtained for corresponding reactions in near neutral aqueous solutions for the neutral form of the guanine monomer derivatives so as to ascertain the influence of the protonation on the arylnitrenium ions with guanine derivatives. Investigate the reactions of selected arylnitrenium ions with selected DNA oligomers of the four different kinds of nucleobases of DNA in aqueous solutions using time-resolved transient absorption spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations. This part of our project will focus on reactions of 2-fluorenylnitrenium ion with d-GGGGG, d-AAAAA, d-TTTTT and d-CCCCC. Analogous experiments will also be done for the corresponding monomers and compared to the results of the preceding oligomer systems in order to learn more about how the oligomer environment affects the arylnitrenium ion reactions with the G, A, T and C bases. Density functional theory calculations will also be done to model the reactions of the arylnitrenium ions with the monomer and oligomer systems of interest in order to help interpret the experimental results and gain more insight into the reactions of interest. Time-resolved resonance Raman experiments will be attempted for the reactions of the 2-fluorenylnitrenium ion and the 4-biphenylnitrenium ion with the d-GGGGG and d-AAAAA oligomer systems. These results will be compared to the analogous monomer reactions and intermediates so as to gain a deeper characterization of the structure and properties of the key reactive intermediates for the oligomer reactions and how the oligomer environments influences these relative to the corresponding monomer reactions. In addition, a comparison of the 2-fluorenylnitrenium and 4-biphenylnitrenium ion reactions will examine how the degree of iminocyclohexadienyl character of the arylnnitrenium ion affects the reactions and their reactive intermediates. Study the reactions of arylnitrenium ions with DNA oligomers with varying base sequences using time-resolved absorption spectroscopy so as to explore how the base sequence environment affects or influences the reactions and reactive intermediates. This part of the project will mainly use the 2-fluorenylnitrenium ion reacting with DNA oligomers like d-AAGAA, d-AGAGAG, d-GAAAG and others. Selected density functional theory calculations will be done for reactions systems similar to those examined in Objectives 3 and 4. These calculations related to Objective 3 experiments will help interpret the experimental results and also gain more insight into how the iminocyclohexadienyl character of the arylnnitrenium ion affects their reactions with DNA oligomers. The computations related to Objective 4 will help better understand how base sequence environment may influence the arylnitrenium ion reactions with DNA oligomers. If time and resources permit, we will attempt time-resolved resonance Raman spectroscopy experiments for reactions of the 2-fluorenylnitrenium ion with DNA oligomers of varying base sequences. These experiments can potentially provide a deeper characterization of the structure, properties and chemical reactivity for these reactions and may allow more insight into how the base sequence environment affects the reactions of interest.

703513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
703513.value: Aromatic amine compounds can be found in trace products of some industrial processes and in the products of combustion processes such as automobile exhaust and tobacco smoke. A number of aromatic amines are carcinogenic and may transfer an arylamine to DNA that then can undergo metabolism to change mainly the guanine moieties in DNA. This DNA damage at the guanine sites can lead to tumors or cancer production in animals and humans. Past research work has found that arylnitrenium ions are able to selectively react with guanine bases in DNA. Thus, arylnitrenium ions are likely the critical intermediates involved in the metabolism of carcinogenic aromatic amines that result in guanine damage in DNA and it is very important to characterize and understand the structure, properties and chemical reactivity of arylnitrenium ions with a range of substrates and their chemical reactions that lead to DNA damage. Since the guanine base molecular environment influences the type and distribution of DNA adducts observed in different DNA environments or sequences of bases in DNA, it is very important to directly investigate the reactions of arylnitrenium ions with DNA oligomers of varying base sequences and DNA strand environments. We propose to use a combination of time-resolved spectroscopic methods such as time-resolved transient absorption spectroscopy and time-resolved resonance Raman spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations to directly study the reactions of selected arynitrenium ions with DNA oligomers of varying base sequences and strand environments. The results of the proposed research will be compared with previous results obtained for monomer bases of DNA to help better understand how the DNA oligomer and sequence of bases influences the chemical reactivity of arylnitrenium ions with various bases in DNA. The research proposed in this project will lead to a range of new information and an improved characterization and understanding of the structure, properties and chemical reactivity of arylnitrenium ions with guanine and other bases in DNA oligomer environments of varying base sequences. These time-resolved spectroscopy and density functional theory computational results will be linked with literature results of product analysis of DNA adducts so as to develop an improved understanding of structure-reactivity relationships of arylnitrenium ion reactions that cause different types of DNA damage. These results may also be useful in trying to find ways to minimize or mitigate DNA damage from the metabolism of aromatic amines found in the environment. 摘要： 在一些工業過程的跟蹤產物和燃燒過程的產物中可以探測到芳香胺化合物，如汽車尾氣、香煙烟霧等。許多芳香胺都是致癌物質，在反應過程中可能轉移芳基胺到DNA中，并通過新陳代謝，主要改變DNA中鳥嘌呤部份。鳥嘌呤位點的DNA損傷可誘發動物和人體中腫瘤或癌症的形成。過去的研究發現，芳香胺離子能夠選擇性地與DNA的鳥嘌呤堿基發生反應，因而芳香胺離子可能是參與致癌芳香胺代謝的關鍵中間體。這種代謝會引起DNA中鳥嘌呤損傷。因此，探明和表徵芳香胺離子與不同的底物的結構、反應特性和化學反應活性以及它們之間的化學反應導致的DNA損傷機理是至關重要的。因為不同DNA環境或DNA堿基序列中的鳥嘌呤堿基分子會影響DNA加合物的類型和分佈，所以需要直接研究芳香胺離子與不同堿基序列的DNA低聚物和DNA鏈的反應。結合時間分辨光譜方法如時間分辨瞬態吸收光譜和時間分辨共振拉曼光譜以及密度泛函理論計算，我們可以直接研究選定的芳香胺離子與不同堿基序列和不同鏈環境的DNA低聚物之間的反應。該研究結果結合先前得到的與DNA單體堿基反應的結果能幫助我們更好地理解DNA低聚物和堿基序列如何影響芳香胺離子與DNA中不同堿基的化學反應。本項目的目標是獲得芳香胺離子與不同堿基序列的DNA低聚物中的鳥嘌呤和其它的堿基反應的一系列新的信息，包括反應中間體的結果特徵，反應特性和化學反應活性的理解等。這些時間分辨光譜和密度泛函理論計算結果將與文獻中報導的DNA加合物的產物分析結果結合在一起，能更好地理解芳香胺離子反應誘導下的不同類型DNA損傷反應中的結構與反應活性的關係，這些結果也有助於探索和尋找減少或減輕環境中芳香胺的代謝引起的DNA損傷的方法。

703513.label: Realisation of objectives
703513.value: We have synthesized and characterized several precursors for the 2-fluorenylnitrenium ion and related derivatives (like 4-biphenylnitrenium ion and the 4-phenoxyphenylnitrenium ion) to use to generate the arylnitrenium ions of interest and investigated their reactions with commercially available guanine containing DNA oligomers of varying length and base compositions (including different sequences) using time-resolved transient absorption and time-resolved resonance Raman spectroscopy methods. These time-resolved spectroscopy experiments directly observed the reaction of the 2-fluorenylnitrenium ion with selected DNA oligomers and saw an intermediate possessing a similar C8-structure with intermediates produced from the reaction of monomeric guanosine derivatives with arylnitrenium ions. However, the oligomeric guanine exhibits noticeably more reactivity towards 2-fluorenylnitrenium ion compared to monomeric guanine derivatives. We found the -biphenylnitrenium ion and the 4-phenoxyphenylnitrenium ion to be less reactive and substantially less signal was observed. This work addressed 100% of objectives 2,3, 4 and 6 and most of objective 1 and were reported in publications 1 and 6 in part C of this completion report. In order to learn more about substituent effects and the properties of arylnitrenium ions we started collaborating with another research group to investigate new precursors that can be used to study oxenium ions and arylnitrenium ions which are related types of reactive intermediates that are both thought to be involved in DNA damage. It should be noted that oxenium ions and nitrenium ions are isoelectronic closely related reactive intermediates that differ only by there being an oxygen atom in the relevant oxenium ion compared to a nitrogen atom in the analogous nitrenium ion. We have successfully employed these new precursor compounds to generate the p-biphenylyloxenium ion and a ground state triplet m-dimethylamino-phenyloxenium ion for the first time and characterized these novel reactive intermediates with time-resolved spectroscopy methods and DFT calculations. We found that the singlet aryloxenium ions were much more reactive toward water than the singlet arylnitrenium ions and hence the singlet aryloxenium ions were less likely to react with nucleobases and DNA that were much less prevalent than water in biological systems. However, the triplet ayloxenium ions were much less reactive and more comparable to the reactivity of singlet arylnitrenium ions towards water. These results indicate that the imine character of arylnitrenium ions plays a key role in the selectivity towards water and guanosine, These results help indirectly address how the iminocyclohexadienyl character of arylnitrenium ions affects their chemical reactivity in objectives 3 and 5 and were reported in publications 2 and 5 in part C of this completion report. We also further examined related reactive intermediates also known to damage DNA like ketoprofen (KP) toward purine nucleobases in KP-purine dyad systems, beta-lapachone and bifunctional quinone methides and these reactive intermediates behaved differently than arylnitrenium ions due to their differing chemical structures and properties and hence provide some insight into how the degree of iminocycloheadienyl character of the arylnitrenium ions influences its selectivity towards guanosine in DNA and the position of attack in guanosine. The KP-dyads formed the most different reactive intermediates and hence preferred to damage the sugar backbone of guanosine rather than the guanosine ring like the 2-fluornenylnitrenium ion. In addition, the bifunctional quinone methides we examined are known to selectively attack guanosine in DNA like arylnitrenium ions such as the 2-fluorenylnitrenium ion but the bifunctional quinone methide reactive intermediates prefer to form N7 adducts while the arylnitrenium ions like the 2-fluorenylnitrenium ion prefer to make C8 adducts indicating that the imino character has an important role in the position of guanosine attack. The work on these related systems helped to address objectives 1, 2 and 5 and were reported in publications 3, 4 and 7 of this in part C of this completion report.

rows: Study the reactions of selected arylnitrenium ions with protonated guanine monomer derivatives in acidic aqueous solutions using time-resolved resonance Raman spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations. These results will be compared to those previously obtained for corresponding reactions in near neutral aqueous solutions for the neutral form of the guanine monomer derivatives so as to ascertain the influence of the protonation on the arylnitrenium ions with guanine derivatives.

Investigate the reactions of selected arylnitrenium ions with selected DNA oligomers of the four different kinds of nucleobases of DNA in aqueous solutions using time-resolved transient absorption spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations. This part of our project will focus on reactions of 2-fluorenylnitrenium ion with d-GGGGG, d-AAAAA, d-TTTTT and d-CCCCC. Analogous experiments will also be done for the corresponding monomers and compared to the results of the preceding oligomer systems in order to learn more about how the oligomer environment affects the arylnitrenium ion reactions with the G, A, T and C bases. Density functional theory calculations will also be done to model the reactions of the arylnitrenium ions with the monomer and oligomer systems of interest in order to help interpret the experimental results and gain more insight into the reactions of interest.

Time-resolved resonance Raman experiments will be attempted for the reactions of the 2-fluorenylnitrenium ion and the 4-biphenylnitrenium ion with the d-GGGGG and d-AAAAA oligomer systems. These results will be compared to the analogous monomer reactions and intermediates so as to gain a deeper characterization of the structure and properties of the key reactive intermediates for the oligomer reactions and how the oligomer environments influences these relative to the corresponding monomer reactions. In addition, a comparison of the 2-fluorenylnitrenium and 4-biphenylnitrenium ion reactions will examine how the degree of iminocyclohexadienyl character of the arylnnitrenium ion affects the reactions and their reactive intermediates.

Study the reactions of arylnitrenium ions with DNA oligomers with varying base sequences using time-resolved absorption spectroscopy so as to explore how the base sequence environment affects or influences the reactions and reactive intermediates. This part of the project will mainly use the 2-fluorenylnitrenium ion reacting with DNA oligomers like d-AAGAA, d-AGAGAG, d-GAAAG and others.

Selected density functional theory calculations will be done for reactions systems similar to those examined in Objectives 3 and 4. These calculations related to Objective 3 experiments will help interpret the experimental results and also gain more insight into how the iminocyclohexadienyl character of the arylnnitrenium ion affects their reactions with DNA oligomers. The computations related to Objective 4 will help better understand how base sequence environment may influence the arylnitrenium ion reactions with DNA oligomers.

If time and resources permit, we will attempt time-resolved resonance Raman spectroscopy experiments for reactions of the 2-fluorenylnitrenium ion with DNA oligomers of varying base sequences. These experiments can potentially provide a deeper characterization of the structure, properties and chemical reactivity for these reactions and may allow more insight into how the base sequence environment affects the reactions of interest.

703513.label: Major findings and research outcome
703513.value: Like the reactions with monomeric guanine derivatives observed in our previous project in this area, in the presence of oligomeric guanine the decay of the 2-fluorenylnitrenium ion (and some other related arylnitrenium ions) can be fit well with a single exponential function and the decay rate constants are dependent on the oligomer concentrations examined. The second order rate constants for the 2-fluorenylnitrenium ion with some DNA oligomers are given in publication 1 of part C. Inspection of the data given in publication 1 of part C suggests that each guanine in the oligomers is a reactive unit except those with more than three consecutive guanines present (like d-AGGGA and d-GGGGG), and the guanine unit has a reaction rate constant towards 2-fluorenylnitrenium ion of 2~3×109 M-1s-1, which is noticeably faster than those of monomeric guanosine derivatives (7~9×108 M-1s-1). It is interesting to note that the self-complementary oligomer d-ATGCAT has a rate constant of 3.1×109 M-1s-1, much faster than a related previously published result that the kSS≈ 0.27kd-G, where kSS and kd-G are rate constants of d-ATGCAT and 2’-deoxyguanosine towards N-acetyl-N-(2- fluorenyl)nitrenium ion, respectively. This work addressed objectives 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 and was mainly reported in publication 1 of section C. Substituent effects were examined by studying other related reactive intermediates that also damage DNA like arylnitrenium ions such as oxenium ions in which the N atom is substituted by an O atom (see publications 2 and 5 of section C) and bifunctional quionone methides (BQMs) which has a similar cyclohexadienyl character as arylnitrenium ions (see publication 7 in part C). Comparison of the reactivity of several aryloxenium ions and arylnitrenium ions with water found that singlet aryloxenium ions were much more reactive with water than singlet arylnitrenium ions while a triplet aryloxenium ion had reactivity with water similar to singlet arylnitrenium ion. Both arylnitrenium ions and some BQMs selectively attack guanine bases in DNA but alkylate guanine at different positions. The first time-resolved vibrational spectroscopic observation and characterization of a BQM species enabled a detailed comparison of the structure and properties to arylnitrenium ions. Comparison of the results obtained for the aryloxenium ions and BQMs with those for arylnitrenium ions indicates that both the degree of the cyclohexadienyl and inimo properties of arylnitrenium ions have key roles in determining their selectivity toward guanine bases in DNA and also influence the position of attack on the guanine base.

703513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
703513.value: The research work in this project lays the foundation for investigating DNA damage reactions of arylnitrenium ions and related intermediates like some bifunctional quinone methides (BQMs) that can also undergo alkylation reactions with guanine bases in DNA. Future research to gain information about the similarities and differences in the reactions of primary arylnitrenium ions (like the 2-fluorenylnitenium ion) versus secondary arylnitrenium ions (like the diphenylnitrenium ion and its derivatives) will be very useful as this will give a better understanding into how the imine and cyclohexadienyl character of arylnitrenium ions affects their chemical reactivity at a new level of detail. Ns-TR3 spectroscopy was done to observe and characterize the structure and properties of a BQM intermediate for the first time in this project. Therefore it will be very useful to explore the generation of different kinds of BQMs in various aqueous conditions so as to gain insight and guidance on how to generate them more efficiently. Future work on directly observing and characterizing the reactions of the BQM intermediates with guanosine and DNA oligomers will be very important to do in order to better understand their alkylation and cross-linking processes that lead to some BQMs being very effective anti-cancer agents.

703513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
703513.value: Aromatic amines can be found in cigarette smoke (and in some other pollutants) and can be metabolized in the body to produce very short-lived reactive intermediates called arylnitrenium ions. These arylnitrenium ions may selectively react with guanine bases in DNA to produce modified DNA that can result in mutations in the DNA that may lead cancer in some cases. This project used several types of time-resolved spectroscopy experiments with suitable precursor compounds to generate and directly observe selected short-lived arylnitrenium ion intermediates and their reactions with guanosine and DNA oligomers. This research gained new data and insight into the structure, properties and chemical reactivity of arylnitrenium ions and their reactions with guanosine and DNA oligomer. This project also examined several other reactive intermediates that can damage DNA. In particular, bifunctional quinone methide (BQM) intermediates that also selectively attack guanine bases in DNA like arylnitrenium ions were also investigated with time-resolved spectroscopy methods and new information was obtained to better understand how selected BQM intermediates are formed in water solutions and also regarding their structure and properties.

703713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
703713.value: Majorana particles are their own anti-particles, which has been pursued for a long time as elementary particles since 1930s. About one decade ago, theorists realized that electron and hole’s characteristics in superconductors may provide a platform to simulate the particle-antiparticle correspondence in particle physics, and the Majorana fermions may be realized in unconventional superconductors or fractional quantum Hall systems. Recent years several theoretical proposals stimulated a hot search of Majorana fermions in semiconductor-superconductor devices. Majorana fermions appear as topological excitations or mid-gap bound states in topological superconductors. Majorana particles have some extremely unusual and interesting properties which have potential applications in quantum computation. For example, the quantum statistics of Majorana fermions is non-abelian, i.e., exchange of majorana fermions results not only in a change of the phase of quantum mechanical wave-function, but also in the change of the internal states. This will provide a powerful method for quantum information processing. Modern nanotechnology makes it possible to realize and to detect this novel particle in a controllable laboratory environment. Several groups have reported possible signatures of Majorana fermions in hybrid superconductor-semiconductor nanowire devices. Although each observation is incapable of excluding all other possible explanations, independent measurements systematically and strongly indicate or support the hypothesis of Majorana fermions. Now the Majorana fermions become a hot topic which attracts both theorists and experimentalists, and a lot of theoretical issues are waiting to be solved. The primary objective of this proposal is to investigate the formation and robustness of Majorana fermions in condensed matters, the interplay between the Majorana fermions and quantum dots, and the effect of decoherence, impurities, and interaction. The tunneling of Majorana fermions in various setups of quantum dots will be studied, and an efficient and controllable way to detect or measure and manipulate Majorana fermions in semiconductor systems will be explored. This project will enable significant advance in theoretcial understanding the Majorana fermions in condensed matters, and in exploring possible applications in semiconductor technology. It will enrich our knowledge of elementary particles in Nature, and have impact for education in curriculum development. 馬約喇納費米子是一類特殊的費米子,它們的反粒子就是其本身。從1937年至今，物理學家一直在基本粒子領域尋找馬約喇納費米子。近年來，理論物理學家意識到超導體中的粒子空穴對可以用來類比粒子物理中的粒子和反粒子特性，並指出馬約喇納費米子可以存在於非傳統超導體或者分數量子霍爾體系中。最近很多理論方案的提出掀起了一輪在半導體-超導複合器件中追尋馬約喇納費米子的熱潮。相關的理論預言，馬約喇納費米子可以出現在拓撲超導體中的拓撲激發態或者帶隙內的束縛態。馬約喇納費米子反常和有趣的特性在量子計算領域有潛在的應用前景。例如，其滿足非阿貝爾的統計特性。當馬約喇納費米子之間交換時不僅會改變波函數的相位，並且會改變體系內部性質。這為量子資訊處理過程提供了一種有力的方法。現代先進的納米技術讓在實驗可控的環境下實現和探測這種奇異粒子成為了可能。最近幾個實驗小組相繼報導了在納米線與超導體組成的複合量子器件中馬約喇納費米子可能存在的信號。儘管不能排除其它所有可能的物理機制，但這些實驗還是很有力地支援或者展示了馬約喇納費米子的存在。現在對馬約喇納費米子的研究形成了新的研究熱點，並吸引了大量的理論和實驗物理學家投入其中，很多相關的理論問題亟待解決。本課題將針對凝聚態物理中馬約喇納費米子的形成和穩定性，其與量子點耦合以及相關的退相干和雜質態效應展開研究。我們將研究各類量子點與馬約喇納費米子耦合器件中的輸運性質，提出在半導體體系中探測、測量和調控馬約喇納費米子的有效方案。通過本課題的研究，希望能夠在理論上更進一步地理解馬約喇納費米子的物理特性，並探索其在半導體技術中的可能應用。這不僅可以豐富我們對自然界基本粒子的理解，而且可以完善相關的課程教育。

703713.label: Realisation of objectives
703713.value: The primary objective of this project is to investigate the formation and robustness of Majorana fermions in condensed matter, the interplay between the Majorana fermions and quantum dots, and the effect of decoherence, impurities, and interaction. The tunneling of Majorana fermions in various setups of quantum dots are studied, and an efficient and controllable way to detect or measure and manipulate Majorana fermions in semiconductor system was explored. We have focused these issues and completed a series of works. 7 papers related to this project were published, including 5 in Physical Review B, 1 in Scientific Reports and 1 in National Science Review. We have addressed all the objectives in the original application. The interplay and correlation between Majorana fermions were investigated in a quantum dot-Majorana hybrid system. Two relevant papers were published. 1. Current noise cross correlation mediated by Majorana bound states (Phys. Rev. B 90, 195404 (2014) We study the transport properties of a quantum dot-Majorana hybrid system, in which each of the paired Majorana bound states is connected to one quantum dot. With the help of the nonequilibrium Green's function method, we obtain an exact solution of the Green's functions and calculate the currents through the quantum dots and nonlocal noise cross correlation between the currents. As a function of dot energy levels ε1 and ε2, we find that for the symmetric level configuration ε1=ε2, the noise cross correlation is negative in the low lead voltage regime, while it becomes positive with the increase of the lead voltages. Due to the particle-hole symmetry, the cross correlation is always positive in the antisymmetric case ε1=−ε2. In contrast, the cross correlation of non-Majorana setups is always positive. For comparison, we also perform the diagonalized master equation calculation to check its applicability. It is found that the diagonalized master equations work well in most regimes of system parameters. Nevertheless, it shows an obvious deviation from the exact solution by the nonequilibrium Green's function method when all eigenenergies of the dot-Majorana hybrid system and simultaneously the energy intervals are comparable to the dot-lead coupling strength. 2. Enhanced current noise correlations in a Coulomb-Majorana device (Phys. Rev. B 93, 245418(2015) Majorana bound states (MBSs) nested in a topological nanowire are predicted to manifest nonlocal correlations in the presence of a finite energy splitting between the MBSs. However, the signal of the nonlocal correlations has not yet been detected in experiments. A possible reason is that the energy splitting is too weak and seriously affected by many system parameters. Here we investigate the charging energy induced nonlocal correlations in a hybrid device of MBSs and quantum dots. The nanowire that hosts the MBSs is assumed in proximity to a mesoscopic superconducting island with a finite charging energy. Each end of the nanowire is coupled to one lead via a quantum dot with resonant levels. With a floating superconducting island, the devices show a negative differential conductance and giant super-Poissonian shot noise, due to the interplay between the nonlocality of the MBSs and dynamical Coulomb blockade effect. When the island is strongly coupled to a bulk superconductor, the current cross correlations at small lead chemical potentials are negative by tuning the dot energy levels. In contrast, the cross correlation is always positive in a non-Majorana setup. This difference may provide a signature for the existence of the MBSs. We explore the topological superconducting states, which host Majorana fermions around the boundary or the vortex in the materials. 3. Topological superconducting states in monolayer FeSe/SrTiO3 (Phys. Rev. B 92, 165104 (2015) The monolayer FeSe with a thickness of one unit cell grown on a single-crystal SrTiO3 substrate (FeSe/STO) exhibits striking high-temperature superconductivity with transition temperature Tc over 65 K reported by recent experimental measurements. In this work, through analyzing the distinctive electronic structure, and providing systematic classification of the pairing symmetry, we find that both s- and p-wave pairing with odd parity give rise to topological superconducting states in monolayer FeSe, and the exotic properties of s-wave topological superconducting states have close relations with the unique nonsymmorphic lattice structure which induces the orbital-momentum locking. Our results indicate that the monolayer FeSe could be in the topological nontrivial s-wave superconducting states if the relevant effective pairing interactions are dominant in comparison with other candidates. We studied the disordered effect of topological superconductuing phases. 4. Disorder-induced topological phase transitions in two-dimensional spin-orbit coupled superconductors (Scientific Reports 6, 39188 (2016)) Normal superconductors with Rashba spin-orbit coupling have been explored as candidate systems of topological superconductors. Here we present a comparative theoretical study of the effects of different types of disorder on the topological phases of two-dimensional Rashba spin-orbit coupled superconductors. First, we show that a topologically trivial superconductor can be driven into a chiral topological superconductor upon diluted doping of isolated magnetic disorder, which close and reopen the quasiparticle gap of the paired electrons in a nontrivial manner. Secondly, the superconducting nature of a topological superconductor is found to be robust against Anderson disorder, but the topological nature is not, converting the system into a topologically trivial state even in the weak scattering limit. These topological phase transitions are distinctly characterized by variations in the topological invariant. We discuss the central findings in connection with existing experiments, and provide new schemes towards eventual realization of topological superconductors. We also studied the interacting effect of one-dimensional superlattice from the topological aspect. 5. Complete phase diagram and topological properties of interacting bosons in one-dimensional superlattices (Phys. Rev. B 91, 134101(2015)) The interacting bosons in one-dimensional inversion-symmetric superlattices are investigated from the topological aspect. The complete phase diagram is obtained by an atomic-limit analysis and quantum Monte Carlo simulations and comprises three kinds of phases: superfluid, persisted charge-density-wave and Mott insulators, and emergent insulators in the presence of nearest-neighbor hoppings. We find that all emergent insulators are topological, which are characterized by the Berry phase π and a pair of degenerate in-gap boundary states. The mechanism of the topological bosonic insulators is qualitatively discussed and the ones with higher fillings can be understood as a 1/3-filling topological phase on a background of trivial charge-density-wave or Mott insulators.

703713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
703713.value: Physics of Majorana fermions and their possible applications to quantum computation have become one of the active topics in condensed matter physics and material science. More systems have been reported to host Majorana fermions such as the semiconductor nanowires, ferromagnetic atomic chain on a superconductor, and interface between topological insulator and supoerconductors. Majorana fermions can exist in various forms, the end states in quasi-one dimensional systems, point-like state confined in a vortex or chiral edge states around a 2D system. These provide new platforms to explore novel properties of Majorana fermions. In the future we shall continue to investigate the formation of Majorana fermions and their correlation and interplay in various devices.

703713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
703713.value: Majorana particles are their own-antiparticles, which has been pursued for a long time as elementary since 1930s. Recently theorists realized that superconductors may provide a platform to simulate Majorana fermions in solid. The primary objective of this project is to investigate the formation and robustness of Majorana fermions in condensed matter, the interplay between the Majorana fermions and quantum dots, and the effect of decoherence, impurities, and interaction. The tunneling of Majorana fermions in various setups of quantum dots are studied, and an efficient and controllable way to detect or measure and manipulate Majorana fermions in semiconductor system was explored. This project enables significant advances in theoretical understanding the Majorana fermions in condensed matter, and in exploring possible applications in semiconductor technology. It enriches our knowledge of elementary particles in Nature, and has impact for education in curriculum development.
