703913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
703913.value: 細胞是生物多樣性的基本單元。單細胞水平的隨機基因和蛋白表達已經得到清楚的證實，因此相同細胞對抑製劑或藥物等的外界刺激反應不同。單細胞分析對闡述細胞的多樣性和異質性非常重要。熒光流式細胞術是現今最備受廣泛應用的單細胞水平蛋白分析方法，然而，熒光標記的光譜重疊往往限制其於單細胞水平分析上的應用。基體輔助激光光解析電離質譜（MALDI）和激光燒蝕電噴霧電離質譜（LAESI）都已用於進行蛋白和代謝物的輪廓分析。利用鑭係金屬離子取代熒光基團連接抗體的技術，質譜流式細胞術可同時監測單細胞中的34個參數。這種方法連用高靈敏度等離子體發射光譜(ICP-MS)可用來檢測單細胞中的過渡金屬元素。 不同金屬離子於細胞中累積，然而其效果卻是把雙刃劍。一方面，他們可充當酶輔助因子（如鐵和銅）；另一方面，他們也展示毒性，從而導致不同的疾病。對超過一千種已知三維結構的不同酶的生物學調查中顯示40%的蛋白酶均需要金屬。有些元素儘管並不是生物體內最基礎的元素，也已經廣泛使用於治療（鉑抗癌藥物）或診斷的人體保健中。然而於單細胞水平上，金屬和金屬藥物以及金屬藥物處理細胞的機理信息仍不為人所知悉。鉑和砷的化合物在臨床上被廣泛應用於治療各種癌症，而已知它們可與蛋白質相互作用。 該項目的目的是以鉑和砷作例子，透過「單細胞金屬組學」而利用最先進的ICP-MS對金屬抗癌藥物進行詳細的研究。具體而言： （1）利用時間分辨ICP - MS進行基本金屬與金屬藥物的單細胞金屬組學研究，並分析它們在細胞週期中不同階段的吸收。 （2）研究單細胞在金屬抗癌藥物（順鉑及三氧化二砷）的刺激後對金屬（銅、鐵、鋅、錳）的反應 （3）比較正常單細胞和癌單細胞在不同細胞週期中的金屬和金屬藥物水平。 （4）利用蛋白質組學及流式細胞術初探不同細胞週期中的順鉑-蛋白質相互作用。 此研究將解釋細胞在不同細胞週期中對金屬及金屬藥物的吸收，與金屬的相互作用和所生成的代謝產物，從而提高我們對單細胞中金屬藥物的認知。這項研究的長期目標是建立一個單細胞水平的藥物無機化學和化學生物學研究平台。

703913.label: Realisation of objectives
703913.value: 1. A single cell-based metallomics for metals and metallodrug ( arsenic trioxide) by time-resolved ICP-MS, was established. Uptake of arsenic trioxide at different cell cycle was examined carefully and found to be G2/M>G1>S. The uptake was also compared with ZIO-101, a new organoarsenial compound in clinical trial. 2. We successfully coupled the fluorescence with ICP-MS which allows metal update at specific cell phase to be detected simultaneously. Arsenic update at single cell level (using NB4 and HL60 cells) was monitored for the first time which provides the basis of the strategy as well as the mechanism of arsenic. For example, we showed higher uptake levels of arsenic trioxide in single NB4 than HL60 cell, which may account for the observed high sensitivity of the NB4 cells to arsenic trioxide. Pronounced apoptosis but less obvious differentiation induced by arsenic trioxide was observed in both the cell lines, suggesting that arsenic trioxide kills leukemia cells mainly through the induction of apoptosis. A correlation between apoptosis and arsenic concentration was established (Zhou, Li, Sun, Chem Commun 2017, 53(20), 2970-2973. 3. To quality both the metallodrugs and key proteins at single levels, a metal-antibody conjugation, i.e. anti-CD116-DOTA-Dy and annexin-V-DOTA-Nd, was also synthesized and examined at single cell level using arsenic trioxide as an example. 4. An integrated metallomic approach for metallodrugs at single cell level was studied and provide a new method for metallomics. The objectives have been successfully as proposed.

703913.label: Major findings and research outcome
703913.value: As proposed, we have optimized time-resolved ICP-MS for measurement of metals and metallodrugs at single cell levels. We carefully investigated the uptake of arsenic trioxide and cispolatin at different cell cycle and found the order of arsenic trioxide to be G2/M>G1>S. We also studied the uptake of ZIO-101, a new organoarsenial compound in clinical trial for comparison. Overall, the uptake of ZIO-101 is much higher than arsenic trioxide, providing a partial basis for the potential applicaton of the com[pound in clinical. We showed higher uptake levels of arsenic trioxide in single NB4 than HL60 cell, which may account for the observed high sensitivity of the NB4 cells to arsenic trioxide. Pronounced apoptosis but less obvious differentiation induced by arsenic trioxide was observed in both the cell lines, suggesting that arsenic trioxide kills leukemia cells mainly through the induction of apoptosis. A correlation between apoptosis and arsenic concentration was established and the work was published (Zhou, Li, Sun, Chem Commun 2017, 53(20), 2970-2973. To quality both the metallodrugs and key proteins at single levels, we synthesized a metal-antibody conjugation (a metal-tag antibody), i.e. anti-CD116-DOTA-Dy and annexin-V-DOTA-Nd, and examine relationship of metallodrug uptake and cell death at single cell level. A correlation between apoptosis and arsenic concentration was established. We further studied the possibility of establishment of an integrated metallomic approach for metallodrugs at single cell level and explore the relationship of metallodrug uptake and biological clock (circadian). This approach may open a new horizon for precision medicine.

703913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
703913.value: The proposed approach may readily be extended to precision medicine if mass cytometry can be used. Metallodrug uptake at single cell level may offer new information for drug discovery.

703913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
703913.value: Individual cells are different and cell growth has four phases and importantly, certain protein levels are regulated by biological clock. Measurement of (metallo)drug at single cell level will provide more accurate information for our understanding of life process as well as mode of action of (metallo)drug. In this propose, we have build up a time-resolved ICP-MS for measurement of metals and metallodrugs at single cell levels. We carefully investigated the uptake of anticancer drug arsenic trioxide and cispolatin at different cell cycles. Pronounced apoptosis but less obvious differentiation induced by arsenic trioxide was observed in both NB4 and HL60 cells, suggesting that arsenic trioxide kills leukemia cells mainly through the induction of apoptosis. We also found the uptake of ZIO-101, a new organoarsenial compound in clinical trial is much higher than arsenic trioxide. To quality both the metallodrugs and key proteins at single levels, we prepared a metal-antibody conjugation (a metal-tag antibody) and examine relationship of metallodrug uptake and cell death at single cell level by time-resolved ICP-MS. A correlation between apoptosis and arsenic concentration was established. Our approach may open a new horizon for precision medicine.

704013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
704013.value: Sm-Nd和Lu-Hf同位素體係被廣泛應用於岩石成因研究，因其可以提供關鍵的信息有助於破譯有關岩漿源區，岩漿成因，構造環境，地殼增長和地球演化的地球化學特徵。在許多情況下，Lu-Hf同位素體系密切反映Sm-Nd同位素系統，導致Hf和Nd同位素比值之間的高度相關性（耦合的行為）。然而隨著近年鋯石Hf同位素組成測試發展成常規的分析方法，越來越多的研究實例顯示了兩個同位素體系的不一致行為（解耦）。這就不可避免地導至矛盾的岩石成因解釋，因而在解耦狀況下數據如何解釋成了一個關鍵的學術問題。因此開展全面系統的研究，以便更好地理解相關的地球化學過程是十分迫切的。 廣泛出露的中國阿爾泰早－中古生代花崗岩具有明顯的Nd-Hf同位素解耦現象(eg. Chen and Jahn, 2002; Wang et al., 2009; Sun et al., 2008) 。這種現象的原因不清，導致了相反的解釋，即全岩Sm-Nd數據意味著古老的地殼物質顯著地參與了岩漿的形成，而鋯石的Lu-Hf數據則表明岩漿源為年輕物質。在中國阿爾泰地區花崗岩侵入體佔40％以上，出露良好容易採樣，大多數岩體已有全岩Nd和鋯石Hf同位素的研究，我們的研究團隊已在該區工作多年，並發表了大量的論文，因而該區是研究Nd -Hf同位素解耦的理想區域。此申請的研究項目擬選取中國阿爾泰早－中古生代花崗岩的代表樣品，計劃利用LA-MC - ICP - MS和SIMS等先進的分析技術，進行全面的Nd ，HF ，Sr，和O-同位素以及單礦物（如鋯石，磷灰石和斜長石）稀土元素分析。 我們相信，我們的研究結果將大大有助於我們了解Nd- Hf的解耦過程。我們預期在我们研究數據基础上給出有關這些花崗岩的岩漿成因的地質模型。其研究價值是澄清該區一些激烈爭辯論的地質問題，並揭示中亞造山帶的大地構造過程。

704013.label: Realisation of objectives
704013.value: Zircon Hf and whole-rock Nd isotopic data for granites from the Chinese Altai give contrasting implications for the nature of the lower crust (ancient or juvenile). This dilema (so called Nd-Hf isotopic decoupling) resulted in controversial interpretation of the Altai mountain belt. One group of researchers envisage it as a continental block, mainly based on Nd isotopic data, whereas the other group of researchers regards it as part of a juvenile arc system. This problem greatly hindered our correctly understanding of the geological history of the Central Asian Orogenic Belt, and because mineralization is directly related to the geological nature, the problem bothered activity of mineral exploration in the region. In this study, our whole-rock Nd–Hf isotopic analyses for representative middle Paleozoic I-type granite and strongly peraluminous granites and rhyo- lites from the Chinese Altai confirmed that the decoupling is not due to "zircon effect" in sedimentation processes (the magma source may contain some sedimentary component), and was not originated from an ancient basement with elevated Lu/Hf ratios. Our results, combined with other available data, revealed that Nd was selectively enriched over Hf due to metasomatism in the mantle wedge, and the prolonged subduction and crust–mantle interaction caused the Nd–Hf isotopic decoupling in the lithospheric mantle beneath the Chinese Altai. This conclusion is supported by the findings in modern island arcs, such as the Lesser Antilles and Sunda. The Chinese Altai crust was extracted from the lithospheric mantle and thus inherited the Nd–Hf isotopic decoupling feature. Therefore, the Hf, rather than Nd, isotopic data more faithfully reflect the nature of the lower crust. Our study thus clarified that the crust in the region was quite juvenile in the Paleozoic, and old continental basement does not exist in the region and the Chinese Altai represents an early Paleozoic magmatic arc possibly built near western Mongolia. In order to further decipher the above mentioned mantle processes, we analysed Sr–Nd–Hf–Pb isotopic compositions for the Devonian mafic intrusions in the Chinese Altai. Our data reveal that the precursor magmas were generated from the depleted lithospheric mantle but variably metasomatised by hydrous melt from subducted sediments, melt from subducted oceanic crust, or fluids derived from subducted sediments. The melting and dehydration of subducted oceanic crust and sediments indicate the Devonian subduction of a hot slab beneath the Chinese Altai, which could be related to a ridge subduction model previously proposed by us. The involvement of hydrous melts and fluids promoted the melting of the lithospheric mantle which was responsible for intensive felsic magmatism with abrupt increase of juvenile component and high temperature metamorphism in the region.

704013.label: Major findings and research outcome
704013.value: - Our whole rock Hf and Nd isotopic results confirmed the Nd-Hf sitopic decoupling that was previously suspected, based on zircon Hf isotopic data and whole rock Nd isotopic data (Yu et al., 2017a). - Our study found that Nd was selectively enriched in the mantle over Hf due to metasomatism in the mantle source (Yu et al., 2017a and 2017b). - Our study found that the metasomatism in the mantle underneath the Chinese Altai was very complicated, it involved hydrous melt from subducted sediments, melt from subducted oceanic crust, and fluids derived from subducted sediments (Yu et al., 2017b). - Our study found that the Chinese Altai crust was extracted from the mantle and inherited the Nd-Hf. decoupling from the mantle.

704013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
704013.value: The Chinese Altai is part of a subduction system in the Paleozoic. Its Hf isotopic data decrease significantly at ~ 400 Ma. This must have a significant tectonic meaning. We speculate a tectonic switch in the evolution of the history of the Central Orogenic Belt. We consider to develop a new project to make an important contribution.

704013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
704013.value: The Central Asian Orogenic Belt is the largest accretionary orogen (mountain belt) in the world. It had a long evolutionary history, and some ancient continental blocks and large amount of juvenile oceanic materials were accreted and preserved as the huge mountain belt. Identification of old versus juvenile geological units is critical to understand its history and crucial for mineral exploration, since mineralization is very different in different geological units (i.e. old continental blocks vs. juvenile oceanic materials). Nd and Hf isotopic data provide powerful tools to identify the nature of a geological unit. However, in the Chinese Altai, Nd and Hf isotopic data give contradictory implications for its geological nature. This dilema is called Nd-Hf isotopic decoupling and occurs in some other areas as well. This study clarified that Nd was selectively enriched over Hf due to metasomatism in the mantle wedge under special conditions. The Chinese Altai crust was extracted from the lithospheric mantle and thus inherited the Nd–Hf isotopic decoupling feature. Therefore, the Hf, rather than Nd, isotopic data more faithfully reflect the nature of the lower crust. Our study thus clarified that the crust in the region was juvenile in the Paleozoic, rather than an old continental basement as some previous researchers proposed. Thus the Chinese Altai represents an early Paleozoic magmatic arc. This conclusion has significant contribution to understand the evolutionary history of the Central Asian Orogenic Belt, and provides guidance for mineral exploration.

704513.label: Project Title(Chinese)
704513.value: 探索一些新奇量子系統的Majorana費米子和邊緣態

704513.label: Project Objectives
704513.value: We plan to explore Majorana fermion states in an s-wave superfluid of cold atoms in the presence of spin-orbital coupling and an additional harmonic potential. Since the superfluid boundary is induced by a harmonic trap, it is expected that some exotic Majorana Fermion states may emerge. We intend to propose a new but more feasible experimental scheme with cold atoms in one-dimensional optical lattices to simulate the Kitaev's unpaired Majorana fermions model, where Majorana fermions can be used to encode a topologically-protected qubit.
rows: We plan to explore Majorana fermion states in an s-wave superfluid of cold atoms in the presence of spin-orbital coupling and an additional harmonic potential. Since the superfluid boundary is induced by a harmonic trap, it is expected that some exotic Majorana Fermion states may emerge.

We intend to propose a new but more feasible experimental scheme with cold atoms in one-dimensional optical lattices to simulate the Kitaev's unpaired Majorana fermions model, where Majorana fermions can be used to encode a topologically-protected qubit.

704513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
704513.value: With the recent experimental advancement of cold atoms and solid-state devices, it has been real to simulate and control a variety of novel quantum systems including the so-called spin-orbit (SO) coupled ones, whom are thought to have the so-called topological states and edge modes, such as the long-sought Majorana fermions whose anti-particles are themselves. Besides, it is also very arresting and challenging to explore whether topological edge modes can also emerge in some interacting boson systems. On the other hand, superconductors with unconventional f-wave pairings have long intrigued physicists, but have never been found in natural materials. Meanwhile, from an intuitive understanding, their edge modes may be Majorana fermions. In this project, we propose (i) to investigate some spin-1/2 SO coupled fermionic pairing systems subject to a harmonic potential in two-dimensional optical lattices and possible unconventional Majorana edge modes; (ii) to design feasible experimental schemes to simulate and manipulate the Majorana edge modes with cold atoms; (iii) to explore topological properties of bosons with repulsive interactions in low-dimensional optical super-lattices; and (iv) to study spin-3/2 SO coupled paring fermions and to elaborate rigorously that the chiral f-wave superconducting states can emerge. It is expected that the proposed research will make a timely and valuable contribution to the interdisciplinary field related to condensed matter and cold atoms. 由於冷原子系統和固態器件的實驗進展，科學家們能夠模擬和控制所謂的自旋-軌道耦合系統，而他們可具有拓撲相和Majorana費米子的邊緣態。此外，探索拓撲邊緣模是否可在某些玻色子系統中出現也是極具挑戰和誘人的課題。在此項目中，我們計劃研究某些低維自旋-軌道耦合系統的性質和可能的Majorana費米子狀態，并嘗試用冷原子系統來模擬和控制它們。 預計我們的研究成果將會對凝聚態和冷原子的交叉領域做出及時和有價值的貢獻。

704513.label: Realisation of objectives
704513.value: 1. We investigated Majorana fermion states in an s-wave superfluid of cold atoms in the presence of spin-orbital coupling and an additional harmonic potential. An exotic Majorana Fermion state was numerically observed. In addition, we also explored possible Majorana fermion states induced by a charged-impurity in topological superconductors 2. We revealed an intrinsic connection between the topological superconductors and their gapless Majorana boundary-modes. Various topological types of Majorana modes have been exploited and their applications in realizing topologically-protected qubit have been addressed. Feasible experimental schemes to quantum-simulate some exotic Majorana-fermion models were worked out. Moreover, theoretical studies and quantum simulations of new topological types of gapless and gapped modes, such as DIII-types, were made, with several exotic results being revealed.

704513.label: Major findings and research outcome
704513.value: From our investigation of Majorana fermion states in an s-wave superfluid of cold atoms in the presence of spin-orbital coupling and an additional harmonic potential, we observed an exotic Majorana Fermion state numerically. In addition, we also disclosed Majorana fermion states induced by a charged-impurity in topological superconductors We revealed an intrinsic connection between the topological superconductors and their gapless Majorana boundary-modes. Various topological types of Majorana modes were found, whose potential applications in realizing topologically-protected qubit were noted. Feasible experimental schemes to quantum-simulate some exotic Majorana-fermion models were worked out. Moreover, new topological types of gapless and gapped modes, such as DIII-types, were found to have exotic properties.

704513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
704513.value: Our results may have potential application in topological quantum computing in future.

704513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
704513.value: Majorana fermions, whose anti-particles are themselves, can exhibit various novel properties and have potential application in robust quantum computing. In this project, we numerically observed an exotic Majorana Fermion state in a superfluid of cold atoms. In addition, we revealed an intrinsic connection between the topological superconductors and their gapless Majorana boundary-modes, and proposed experimentally feasible schemes to quantum-simulate them. In particular, we worked out a realistic scheme for realizing universal topological quantum computing.

705113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
705113.value: There has been an ever increasing demand for the development of selective and specific assay methods and protocols for analytes of environmental and biomedical interests as a result of the higher health consciousness and expectation of the general public for an improved health care system and quality of life. From the synthetic viewpoint, the development of new materials with tunable properties represents an important and viable option. In addition, the parallel development of simple, inexpensive and sensitive assay methods is equally important. Methods based on luminescence readout are especially attractive given their high sensitivity, selectivity via wavelength discrimination and temporal resolution, spatial resolution and availability of rather inexpensive setup and instrumentation. In this project, we will focus on the construction of metal-ligand chromophoric ensembles, conjugates and inorganic-organic hybrids based on the attachment of metal-ligand chromophores to two main classes of materials, namely the conjugated polyelectrolytes and the nanostructured materials such as quantum dots, metal nanoparticles, and other carbon-based nanostructures, via covalent linkage, electrostatic assembly, ligand exchange or non-covalent interactions. While most works in the area involve the coupling or assembly of molecular components, mainly organic dyes, luminophores and biomolecules, to conjugated polyelectrolytes and nanostructured materials, corresponding studies on the use of chromophoric and luminescent metal complexes for conjugate, ensemble or hybrid formation are less explored. Given the wide diversity of metal-ligand chromophores/luminophores with readily tunable excited-state properties, we believe that the coupling of fluorescent conjugated polyelectrolytes or nanostructured materials with metal-ligand chromophores either via covalent attachment or via electrostatic or non-covalent interactions would provide interesting new research dimensions for the study of photoinduced electron transfer and energy transfer processes, and for the discovery of new classes of multi-chromophoric systems and conjugates/ensembles/hybrids with recognition or signalling properties. Thus in this project, novel classes of luminescent metal-ligand conjugates, ensembles and hybrids will be designed and synthesized, which will form the basis for their utilization as probes for “proof-of-principle” molecular recognition and signalling. An understanding of the factors and the fine interplay of electrostatic, solvophobic and non-covalent interactions that govern their stability will be made. Their unique ratiometric luminescence behaviour will be exploited. It is envisaged that the proposed work will provide a fundamental understanding of the factors that govern the formation of the metal-ligand conjugates, ensembles and hybrids and their associated spectroscopic properties, which will provide insights and guiding principles for the rational design of novel probes for molecular recognition and signalling. 由於健康意識的提升和大眾對改善醫療體系及生活素質的期望，人們對發展具選擇性和特定化驗方法來應用於環境及生物醫學方面的需求日益增加。從合成的角度而言，發展具有可調性質的嶄新材料乃一個既重要又可行的選擇。此外，並行開發簡單、低成本和靈敏的化驗方法亦同等重要。基於發光讀出的方法是通過識別波長和時間分辨率，它的靈敏度和選擇性甚高。此外，這種方法的空間解析度，以及相對低成本的設施和器材也令這種方法更具吸引力。本項目會集中研究金屬—配體發色組裝體和共軛物的合成，以及透過共價連結、靜電組裝、配體交換或非共價相互作用來把金屬—配體發色團附加在共軛聚合電解質及納米結構材料如量子點、金屬納米分子和其他碳基納米結構上，以製備無機—有機雜化物。這範疇的研究大多涉及分子元件的偶合或組裝，如有機染料、發光團和生物分子、共軛聚合電解質和納米結構材料，利用發色和發光金屬配合物來生成共軛物、組裝體或雜化材料的研究則相對較少。有鑒於金屬—配體發色團／發光團的多樣性及其激態之可調性，我們相信透過共價接合、使用靜電或非共價相互作用來把螢光共軛聚合電解質或納米材料跟金屬—配體發色團偶合，可以為研究光誘導電子傳輸和能量傳輸過程，及開發具識別和信號傳導特性的新型多發色體系和共軛物／組裝體／雜化物的研究帶來新的研究方向。因此本研究項目會設計與合成嶄新類型的發光金屬—配體共軛物、組裝體和雜化物，並將之應用於「概念驗證」分子識別和信號傳導的探針。我們亦會理解控制其穩定性的因素，以及靜電、疏溶劑及非共價作用之間的相互影響。同時也會研究它們獨特的比率發光特性。此項目預期可為控制金屬—配體共軛物、組裝體和雜化物的合成，以及其關聯光譜特性的因素提供根本的了解，進而為新型分子識別和信號傳導探針的理性設計提供更深入的了解和指引方針。

705213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
705213.value: 天然产物一直以来是新药研发过程中先导化合物筛选的重要源泉。鉴别天然产物的靶标和其作用机理能有效提高天然产物的活性并减少毒副作用。雷公藤内酯醇是从中药雷公藤(Tripterygium wilfordii Hook F.)根中提取的一种二萜内酯天然产物，是雷公藤最主要的活性成份。近年来雷公藤内酯醇被发现有多重生物学作用而引起了广泛兴趣，其活性包括强效的抗肿瘤﹑抗炎﹑抗慢性肾病和自体免疫调节。为了基于雷公藤内酯醇开发出活性更好，毒性更小的新药，亟待确定其直接作用的靶标蛋白。已知的雷公藤内酯醇的靶标蛋白包括XPB（转录因子TFIIH的亚基）等。然而，这些靶标蛋白并不能完全解释雷公藤内酯醇的生物学活性。同时，已知的研究方法有明显缺点，比如不能有效浓缩低丰度的靶标蛋白，或者由于传统生物素探针的穿膜能力受限而不能用于细胞水平的研究。 本课题组先前的研究优化了雷公藤内酯醇及其衍生物的合成路径，并通过对其衍生物库的生物学活性研究确定了构效关系。在此基础上，可以设计有良好活性的化学探针并用于寻找雷公藤内酯醇的新靶标。 本课题的主要目标是用可穿膜的化学探针在活细胞水平上鉴定雷公藤内酯醇的靶标蛋白。我们计划合成两类化学探针。一类是携带叠氮基或炔基的雷公藤内酯醇衍生物，利用“点击”化学(click chemistry)实现对靶标蛋白的生物体系共轭标记。另一类化学探针是在此基础上增加一个光亲和标记基团。这样即使探针分子与靶标蛋白非共价结合，也可以通过光解作用在探针分子与靶蛋白之间引入共价键，从而同时捕捉共价结合与非共价结合的靶标蛋白。 本课题的另一目标是结合化学﹑生物化学﹑分子生物学和细胞生物学方法，具体研究雷公藤内酯醇与其靶标蛋白之间的相互作用及相关机理。该研究结果将有效指导进一步理性设计高效低毒的雷公藤内酯醇衍生物，从而开发出更好的药物。另一方面，通过直接调节影响靶标蛋白, 雷公藤内酯醇﹑其衍生物及化学探针可作为新的研究工具而用于研究相关的机理及信号传导途径。

705313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
705313.value: Nowadays, many insurance companies and financial institutions are involved in trading variable annuity and equity-indexed insurance contracts. The contractual structures of these products are more sophisticated than traditional insurance products. In particular, these products contain various exotic derivatives features. So, advanced quantitative tools and methods are required for the valuation of these products. This represents a practically relevant and challenging research problem. In this project, we first consider valuation of Guaranteed Minimum Death Benefits (GMDB) in variable annuity and equity-indexed annuity contracts. Based on the valuation results, we will investigate the risk measures and risk management of these products. Some ruin theory related problems can be solved as a by-product. Since the exercise time of the embedded options in these products is a random variable, the embedded option is of neither the European style nor the American style. It is a life-contingent option. In Gerber et al. (2012a), considerable interesting results for valuing contingent options have been obtained. Many simple closed-formulas have been obtained. With these formulas and results, we can calculate many risk measures very quickly, and we can extend our model in a various directions. We shall investigate the problem in the cases of jump diffusion and general Levy processes. Under the framework of Gerber et al. (2012a), we can easily obtain closed form formulas if we add some features of the product, such as lapse, bonus rates and resets, as pointed out in Gerber et al. (2012a). However, if we consider dynamic lapse, the problem becomes challenging. We shall investigate this problem in this project. We shall extend the results to other models, such as Markovian regime switching models, etc. We would like to emphasize that results in this project are not restricted to valuing death benefits. Instead of a time-until-death random variable, we can consider a time-until-catastrophe random variable, and so on. We believe that our work paves a way to stimulate the development of some new and appropriate theories and methodologies to study equity-indexed insurance contracts, help us understanding and managing risks of these products, and generate opportunities for further research. Our research will shed light on the inter play between actuarial science and finance, advance our knowledge and make significant impact on both actuarial science and finance. 近年來很多保險公司和金融機構都推出變額年金和與股票相關的保險產品。這類產品的結構要比傳統產品複雜，比如這類產品包含不同的奇異期權特性。因此需要更高深的工具和方法來討論它們的定價。這是一個具有挑戰的研究課題。 在這一項目中，我們首先考慮附有最低保證的身故給付的定價。然後進一步研究這些產品的風險度量及風險管理。作為附帶研究問題我們考慮一些精算學中相關的問題，比如破產概率。由於在這些產品中嵌入式期權的執行時間是隨機的，這些嵌入式期權既不是歐式期權也不是美式期權。這些期權與人壽風險相關。Gerber et al. (2012a) 給出了非常有意義的關於這類期權的定價的結果。得到了很多顯式公式。應用這些公式我們可以很容易地計算與股票相關的保障產品的風險度量。我們也可以從不同方向推廣我們的模型。在Gerber et al. (2012a)，股票指數是用幾何布郎運動描述的，我們可以得到類似的結果如果我們用帶跳的擴散過程來描述股票指數且假定上下跳都是複合Poisson 過程。在一般Levy過程模型下我們將研究類似的問題。 在Gerber et al. (2012a) 中死亡風險率可以是任何隨機變量，我們用指數分佈的線性組合來逼近這個隨機變量，在實際中如何用指數分布的線組合逼近一個隨機變量是值得研究的問題。我們將建議一些可行的方法。如果這些產品包含一些別的特性，這類問題一般也能解決，但如果產品含有動態失約率，問題會變得很困難。我們將在這一項目中研究這一問題。我們將把我們的結果推廣到別的模型，比如馬氏狀態轉換模型等。我們的結果不僅僅局限在人壽保險，我們的模型中的死亡時間隨機變量也可以解釋為巨灾時間等。 我們相信我們的工作會促進與股票有關保險產品的定價理論和方法的發展，幫助我們認識和管理這些產品的風險，從而提出很多進一步研究的問題。我們的研究屬於金融和精算的交叉領域，這一研究將增進我們對金融和精算的理解。

705313.label: Realisation of objectives
705313.value: We have addressed all the topics of this project and obtained very satisfactory results. 18 papers have been published on the theme of this project. Four papers on valuation of the equity linked insurance products have been published in top journals in actuarial science. Our research proposed a new approach for valuing Guaranteed Minimum Death Benefit and related insurance products. This kind products are complex, the common used way is by simulation. The running time of simulation is a problem in practice. Our approach provides simple closed formulas which can be used to reduce the running time significantly. One paper on optimal investment and reinsurance has been published in a top system science journal: Automatica. One paper on optimal portfolio strategy in a model with uncertainty has been published in a top operation research journal: European Journal of Operational Research. 14 papers on the themes of this project including insurance risk models, optimal dividends, optimal reinsurance have been published in top actuarial science and related journals. The PI and his students have attended a number of international conferences and presented our research results in the conferences. PI has invited a number of visitors and RAs. 2 Ph.D. students supported by this project have been working on the themes of this project, and one of them has successfully completed the study and other one is in satisfactory progress. For the numerical and real data part of this project, in my co-authored paper appeared in ASTIN Bulletin, we have some numerical examples. In one of my Ph.D. students' thesis, a lot of numerical results are included. For the real data and computer software, we have studied the problem, it need more time and effort, also, as we learned that Manulife Financial, Canada has used our approach in valuing and managing risk of the equity linked products. This in some way has proved that our approach is applicable, therefore, our purpose of considering the real data has been fulfilled. So we need to consider the problem in a different direction. In any case, we have obtained a lot considerably interesting results, some of them are unexpected. The objectives of the project have been achieved.

705313.label: Major findings and research outcome
705313.value: 18 papers on the theme of this project have been published. Most of the papers have been published in top actuarial science and related journals. 1 paper on valuing equity-linked insurance product in a discrete model has been appeared in Insurance: Mathematics and Economics which is a top actuarial science journal and 1 paper on valuing equity-linked death benefits in a Regime-Switching Framework has been published in a top actuarial science journal ASTIN Bulletin. A substantial series of closed-form formulas is obtained, for the contingent call and put options, for lookback options, for barrier options, for Margrabe options or exchange options, for dynamic fund protection, and for dynamic withdrawal benefits. For the case where the contracts have a finite expiry date, closed-form formulas are found for the contingent call and put options. From these, results for De Moivre's law are obtained as limits. We have also discussed equity-linked death benefit reserves and investment strategies for maintaining such reserves. Whereas in the most important applications the stopping time is the time of death, it could be different in other applications, for example, the time of the next catastrophe. We also obtained closed-form formulas if some features of the product such as lapse, bonus rates and resets, are added in the models mentioned previously. However, if we consider dynamic lapse, the problem becomes quite challenging. In practice, one common used assumption for dynamic lapse is that it is a step function of the price of the underlying index. This can be modeled using a series of barrier type options. Therefore, the closed form formulas for barrier options can be used to deal with the dynamic lapse.

705313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
705313.value: We have obtained a series considerably interesting results on the theme of this project. There are many possible future research topics on this line. First, we can consider the general mathematical framework for this kind of problems. The PI is working on problems of stopped stochastic processes. The PI has submitted another GRF grant application on this topic. The PI also consider to write a book on this area based on the results obtained in this project.

705313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
705313.value: Nowadays, many insurance companies and financial institutions are involved in trading variable annuity and equity-indexed insurance contracts. The contractual structures of these products are more sophisticated than traditional insurance products. In particular, these products contain various exotic derivatives features. Therefore, advanced quantitative tools and methods are required for the valuation of these products. The most popular way to value this kind of products is by using Monte Carlo simulation. However, the computation time by simulation is a problem in practice, in particular for hedging and risk management. In this project, the PI and his co-authors have found a new valuation approach for these products. Our approach provides simple closed formulas which can be used to reduce the running time significantly. Manulife Financial, Canada has used our approach in valuing and managing risk of the equity linked products. Since our approach is a general method for dealing with variable annuity related products, all insurance companies could use our approach to reduce the running time of valuation and risk management of this kind products. Our approach can also be applied to other insurance products, for example, the approach can be used when the claim occurs at the time of the next catastrophe event.

705413.value: 高維因子模型的統計分析

705413.label: Project Objectives
705413.value: Develop consistent estimators for the number of factors in a large-dimensional factor model with independent observations and a general error covariance structure; Develop consistent estimators for the number of factors in a large-dimensional time series factor model; For the likelihood inference in a large-dimensional factor models (with independent observations), find estimable functionals and develop the corresponding consistent estimators; Develop applications of these new tools to real data analysis (finance / biology /telecommunication).

705413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
705413.value: Multivariate methods such as principal components, canonical correlations or factor analysis are well-established tools for data exploration and analysis. However when the number of the variables say p is large compared with the sample size say n, we are faced with a new statistical context, namely the high-dimensional data context. An example of this context is the daily returns of S&P stocks over two years where the number of variables (returns) is p=500 and the sample size is about n=500. Another example is the micro-arrays of gene expression data where the number of tissues (sample size n) is in the hundreds while the number of expressed genes (value of p) can be several thousands. In these types of situations, the aforementioned multivariate methods lose their efficiency dramatically; in some situations it is simply impossible for them to be implemented. Statisticians are faced with the modern challenge of developing new tools to handle high-dimensional data. Following several studies that we have previously undertaken in this general area, we propose in this project to investigate several statistical problems for factor analysis with large-dimensional data. In a factor model, the eigenvalues of its sample covariance matrix are well known to form two parts: a main part (bulk) and some extreme eigenvalues that are well separated from the bulk. These separated eigenvalues, called spikes, represent the strength of the unobserved factors. The first problem we address in this project is the determination of their number. Existing results cover the strict factor model only (i.e. idiosyncratic errors are cross-sectionally homogeneous and uncorrelated). We will extend these results to cover more general structures. Next, we consider a closely related context where factor models are used for dimension reduction of high-dimensional time series. In this context, inference for the number of factors is very different and few results have been proposed . Using tools from the random matrix theory, we will establish a consistent estimator of this number for high-dimensional time series. Furthermore, as the number of parameters in a factor model explodes as O(p²) when the data dimension p is large, the likelihood inference is non trivial since all the parameters cannot be estimated simultaneously. We will define new estimable functionals in the model and provide associated consistent estimators. Finally, data analysis using new methods from this research will be conducted on the stock prices data or micro-array data mentioned above.

705413.label: Realisation of objectives
705413.value: In order to address the Objectives 1 and 2, we have developed a series of work (see Papers 1, 2, 4 and 5 in Part C) which laid the theoretic foundations of the methodology. The final method is proposed in Paper 5 which achieved completely the two objectives. The Objective 3 is considered in Papers 3 and 6. Paper 3 prepares the theory for deriving an asymptotic distribution for spectral statistics of large covariance matrices. In paper 6, a method is proposed to estimate the base spectrum in a high-dimensional factor model. This objective has been achieved completely. Finally, the Objective 4 is considered in Papers 6 and 7 in some statistical models which encompass the factor models of the project. Methods for real data analysis are proposed in these two papers and several real data sets from financial industry and genetic studies. The Objective 4 has been achieved completely.

705513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
705513.value: Single spins localized by quantum dots in semiconductors are promising building blocks for spintronics devices and spin based quantum computer. The primary objective of this proposal is to explore the quantum physics and potential quantum applications of quantum dot spins in a new class of 2D semiconductors, i.e. monolayers of group-VI transition metal dichalcogenides MX2 (M = Mo or W; X = S or Se). These monolayer semiconductors are attracting extensive interest for their remarkable properties including: (1) a multiple valley band structure with a direct bandgap in the visible range; (2) a spin and valley dependent optical selection rule for interband transitions which enables optical control of spin and valley; (3) pronounced spin-valley coupling that suppresses both spin relaxation and valley relaxation. The proposed study on quantum dots in monolayer MX2 is motivated by these remarkable properties of the 2D host materials. In particular, a novel ingredient here is the valley index with the direct optical accessibility, which may be both exploited to facilitate the control of spins and used as an extra information carrier. We will investigate various types of quantum dot confinement in monolayer MX2, and develop novel schemes for optical and electrostatic controls of spin and valley dynamics in various quantum dot configurations. We will also explore the possibility of realizing controllable interplay between the spin and valley degrees of freedom of an individual carrier as well as the interplay between adjacent carriers. We will formulate the coupling of the quantum dot electron and hole with the lattice nuclear spins, and investigate the electron/hole spin decoherence induced by the nuclei. We will also explore the possibility to control the spin and valley of the electron and hole by utilizing the nuclear field which may be established through dynamic nuclear polarization by the electron and hole. The research proposed here would be a timely study on novel quantum dot systems realizable in monolayer MX2, where the quantum physics can be both of fundamental interest and of practical importance for quantum technologies. 局域於半導體量子點中的單個電子自旋是構成未來自旋電子器件乃至自旋量子計算機的理想組件。這個研究計劃的主要目標是探索一類新興的二維半導體材料中形成的量子點中的自旋所具有的新的物理現象以及可能的新的應用。此類二維半導體包括單層的二硫化鉬，二硫化鎢，二硒化鉬，二硒化鎢等，均屬六族過渡金屬二硫化物。這些二維半導體的一些特殊屬性目前引起了廣泛的興趣，包括：（1）能帶結構具有可見光波段的位於兩個簡並能谷的直接帶隙；（2）跟能谷和自旋自由度相關的帶間躍遷的光學選擇定則；（3）自旋和能谷自由度之間的強耦合，以及由此引起的對自旋弛豫和能谷弛豫的抑制。這些特殊的物理性質啟發我們對單層過渡金屬二硫化物中形成的量子點進行相應的研究。其中，能夠通過光學屬性來分辨的能谷自由度將扮演一個重要的角色，它既可以扮演一個單獨的信息載體的角色，同時也可以作為媒介來實現對自旋的相應操作。我們將會研究單層過渡金屬二硫化物中的各種類型的量子點束縛，並且探索如何對其中的自旋和能谷自由度通過光和電控制的辦法進行動力學調控。我們還將探索如何在單個電子的能谷和自旋自由度之間實現可控的互動，以及如何實現相鄰電子的相應自由度之間的互動。我們計劃研究量子點中電子或空穴跟原子核自旋的相互作用的形式，以及由核自旋引起的電子或空穴自旋的退相幹現象。我們還將探索這樣一種可能性，即利用動力學核極化過程中產生的核自旋極化場來進行對電子及空穴自旋的調控。此類新型的量子點系統中的量子現象對未來的量子科技可能帶來根本的並具有重要應用價值的影響，本課題將對此進行適時的研究。

705513.label: Realisation of objectives
705513.value: Objective 1 This objective has been achieved. We have investigated quantum dot confinement of electrons and holes in monolayer MX2. Based on the experimental progresses on these monolayer semiconductors, we can outline two possibilities for realizing quantum dot confinement: (1) by patterned electrodes, similar to the QDs in III-V heterostructures; (2) by lateral heterojunctions of different MX2 (i.e. a crystalline monolayer with lateral variation of chemical composition by controlled growth). In both cases, the QDs have a unique type-II band alignment with its surroundings, with a smooth variation of the confining potential at the boundary for the first realisation (defined by electrodes), and a sharp change of confining potential for the second realisation (lateral heterostructure). We have investigated the degree of valley hybridization, due to the QD confinement, an outstanding issue which may significantly change the valley physics in QDs from its form in the 2D bulk. We performed a systematic study of the intervalley coupling by QD confinement potentials on extended MX2 monolayers using two approaches: (1) the evenlope function approach in conjecture with first principle wave functions at band edges; (2) the real space tight-binding approach based on a three-band tight binding model we previously developed for monolayer MX2. We find that the intervalley coupling in such geometry is generically weak due to the vanishing amplitude of the electron wavefunction at the QD boundary, and hence valley hybridization can be well quenched by the strong spin–valley coupling in monolayer MX2 and the QDs can well inherit the valley physics of the 2D bulk. We also discover sensitive dependence of intervalley coupling strength on the central position and the lateral length scales of the confinement potentials, which may possibly allow tuning of intervalley coupling by external controls. Objective 2 This objective has been achieved. We have investigated the optical quantum manipulation of the internal degrees of single electron or hole localized by monolayer MX2 nanostructures including charged impurities and small quantum dots (with length scale of 10 nm or smaller). The localized single carrier has a spin degree of freedom as well as a valley degree of freedom inherited from the bulk band structures, both of which can be exploited to encode quantum bit (qubit). We have explored the optical quantum control possibilities of spin-valley qubit carried by single electron under two different scenarios: (i) in the presence of finite valley hybridization due to the confinement and (ii) in the absence of valley hybridization. The latter scenario is considered for the confinements that has C3 or higher rotational symmetry about a chalcogen atom site or the hollow center of the hexagon formed by metal and chalcogen atoms or when this symmetry is only weakly broken so the residue intervalley coupling can be well quenched by the spin-valley coupling. We show that the bulk valley and spin optical selection rules can be inherited in different forms in the two scenarios, both of which allow the coherent rotation between spin-valley states of the electron controlled by optical pulses. A single electron in the ground state of the QD confinement has four spin-valley configurations that can be exploited to encode two qubits, and we have proposed scheme to realize logic control between the two qubits. Moreover, we have investigated exciton (a bound pair of an electron and a hole, convertible with a photon) at the type-II heterojunction that defines the quantum dot confinement. A unique feature of exciton in this quantum dot system is that, because of the type-II band alignment, while the electron component of the exciton is confined in the dot, the hole component energetically favor the region outside the dot but is attracted to the vicinity of the dot by the electron-hole Coulomb interaction. This feature can facilitate the mediation of interplay between electrons in neighboring dots by the presence of an interface exciton (with its hole component located between the dots), which can be virtually excited by optical pulses for realizing a tunable coupling. Objective 3 This objective has been achieved. We have formulated the hyperfine interaction between lattice nuclear spins and the electron or hole spin in monolayer MX2 quantum dot within the envelop function approximation. We find that the hyperfine interaction has important intervalley terms besides the usual intravalley terms because of its short-range nature (which can supply the momentum needed for an intervalley transition). We have investigated the decoherence and population relaxation between the spin-valley states of the single electron due to the statistical fluctuations of the unpolarised nuclear spin bath through the intravalley and intervalley hyperfine coupling. Moreover, based on the hyperfine interaction, we have developed the level schemes for optically controlled interplay between the electron and nuclear spin via the intermediate charged exciton state, which allow the generation of electron-nuclear spin entanglement as well as transfer of the electron spin polarization to nuclear spin.

705513.label: Major findings and research outcome
705513.value: (1) We have investigated quantum dot confinement of electrons and holes in monolayer MX2 QDs with type-II band alignment with its surroundings. We performed a systematic study of the intervalley coupling by QD confinement potentials and find that the intervalley coupling in such geometry is generically weak due to the vanishing amplitude of the electron wavefunction at the QD boundary, and hence valley hybridization can be quenched by the strong spin–valley coupling in monolayer MX2 and the QDs can well inherit the valley physics of the 2D bulk. We also discover sensitive dependence of intervalley coupling strength on the central position and the lateral length scales of the confinement potentials, which may possibly allow tuning of intervalley coupling by external controls. (paper 1 in research output). (2) We have investigated the optical control possibilities of spin-valley qubit carried by single electrons localized in MX2 QDs. We show that the bulk valley and spin optical selection rules can be inherited in different forms in the presence or absence of valley hybridization, both of which allow the definition of spin-valley qubit with desired optical controllability, including the optically controlled two-qubit operations in a single quantum dot. We also investigated nuclear spin-induced decoherence and quantum control of the interplay between electron and nuclear spin via intervalley terms of the hyperfine interaction. (paper 5 in research output) (3) We have investigated interface exciton at the type-II heterojunction on monolayer MX2 with type-II band alignment (in both quantum dot and quantum wire geometry), which can be exploited for mediating the interplay between adjacent dots through its virtual excitation by optical pulses. (paper draft 9 in research output) (4) We have investigated optical selection rules for the transition to and between various exciton states, and also discovered unique valley-orbital coupled Dirac spectra of excitons in monolayer MX2, which point to versatile optical control possibilities of exciton valley pseudospin that can be relevant for indirect quantum control of localised electron through exciting delocalized excitons in its neighbourhood. (paper 4,8 in research output) (5) We have worked together with experimental groups on the investigation of lateral heterojunctions and impurities that can be exploited for localizing single carrier in monolayer MX2, as well as experimental demonstration of spin-valley optical control in bulk monolayer MX2 (paper 2,3,6,7 in research output).

705513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
705513.value: Our theoretical studies have established understanding of basic properties of internal quantum degree of freedom of single electron localized in monolayer MX2 quantum dot including the level scheme, optical selection rule and controllability, hyperfine interaction and control possibility on the interplay with lattice nuclear spin. We have put forward several control schemes for quantum manipulation of the electron spin-valley qubit and nuclear spin in the MX2 quantum dot. High-quality realizations of quantum dot (as well as quantum wire) by type-II lateral heterostructures on monolayer MX2 has become practical very recently by advances in growth of these monolayer semiconductors. It is good timing for us to move forward to work closely with experimental group for further experimental characterization of the quantum dot system and for experimental implementation on the spin manipulation in such quantum dots heterostructures. We plan to team up with sample growers and nano-optoelectronic experimental group to tackle these tasks.

705513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
705513.value: Spin of single electron or hole localized by quantum dots in semiconductors can be exploited as building blocks for spintronics devices and spin based quantum computer. The newly emerged monolayer transition metal dichalcogenide MX2 realize direct bandgap semiconductors in truly two-dimensional limit, featuring excotic properties associated with carriers' spin and valley pseudospin, the latter referring to the degenerate band edges in momentum space. This project has theoretically investigated the quantum dot confinement of single carrier by the unique type-II lateral heterojunction in these 2D semiconductors, and the spin quantum control possibilities therein. We have discovered novel energy level schemes for the optical quantum manipulations of the spin and valley pseudospin states of the confined single carrier, and the interplay with lattice nuclear spins, exploiting the valley properties inherited from the monolayer bulk. Experimental realizations of this novel quantum dot system has become practical very recently by advances in growth of these monolayer semiconductors, and our theoretical findings form the basis for further experimental studies on the quantum control of spins.

705613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
705613.value: Clinical trials are essential to new drug development. Nowadays, more and more drugs and biomarkers are available for testing. Clinical trials are becoming increasingly expensive and difficult, as they generally require more examination procedures and also more patients in order to identify treatment effects particularly when the treatment can only benefit a subset of the patient population. To make undertaking trials more efficient and flexible, we propose three new statistical methods for designing phase I and phase II clinical trials. In the era of personalized medicine, most of the targeted therapies are cytostatic; that is, they are generally safe and tolerable compared with cytotoxic agents. For cytostatic agents, the maximum therapeutic effect of the drug is of more interest, in contrast to the maximum tolerated dose for cytotoxic agents. First, we will develop a two-stage dose-finding method for cytostatic agents, which is suitable for finding the so-called optimum biological dose with stage 1 focusing on toxicity and stage 2 on efficacy. Second, we will propose a seamless two-stage transition design for trials moving from single-arm to double-arm. This design inherits advantages of both single-arm and multi-arm trials—such as being more objective and saving sample size as well as attracting more trial participants—and can also maintain the frequentist type I and type II error rates. Third, we will develop a new phase II randomized trial design based on the posterior and predictive probabilities for trial monitoring with time-to-event data. In the proposed three clinical trial designs, decision making is based on the prior information and the strength of the observed data which are naturally integrated in the Bayesian framework. Because the inference is not constrained on a fixed study design, it is more flexible in terms of the frequency and time for the interim analysis. Valid inference still can be drawn even when the study condition deviates from what was originally planned. The proposed statistical designs will improve cancer clinical trial conduct in phase I and phase II studies. During the trial, more frequent interim analysis can be implemented, more adaptive decisions can be made and, as a result, treatment comparisons become more efficient, objective, and accurate, which in turn will expedite new drug development. To facilitate the routine use and broad application of our proposed trial designs, we will develop user-friendly software for each method. 临床试验在新药研发进程中起着重要的角色。目前，有越来越多的药物和生物标记物可供我们测试研究。临床试验的成本和难度正在日益加大，因为试验往往需要更多的检验步骤以及更大的病人总数，才能探测出不同疗法之间的疗效差异。在癌症药物的研发中，大多数的靶向疗法是针对细胞抑制功能，与细胞毒性药物相比，这些靶向药物更加安全。对于细胞毒性药物而言，我们研究药物的最大耐受剂量，而对于细胞抑制药物，我们则更想了解其所能达到的最大疗效。为了提升临床试验的效率和灵活性，我们提出三种新的统计学方法，可以广泛地用于设计一期和二期临床试验。第一，我们提出一种针对细胞抑制药物的两阶段的剂量寻找方法，用于寻找所谓的“最适生物剂量”，该方法的第一和第二阶段分别探寻药物的毒性和疗效。第二，我们提出一种无缝衔接的两阶段试验设计，可将一阶段的单臂试验和二阶段的双臂试验自然连接起来。该设计结合了单臂试验和多臂试验各自的优点，既具有客观性，又能节约样本容量，而且还可以吸引更多的病人参与试验，并同时控制统计第一类和第二类错误率。第三，我们提出一种在二期试验中，针对事件发生时间类型的数据的随机化试验设计，该设计可利用后验预测概率来监测临床试验的进程。在以上三种临床试验设计中，我们采用贝叶斯方法的框架可将先验的信息和试验中观测的数据自然地整合，从而做出最终的决策。我们可以更加灵活地安排中期分析的次数和时间，并可做出正确有效的统计推断。我们提出的这些试验设计将能够提升一期和二期的癌症临床试验的效率与性能。在试验进行的过程中，利用更频繁的中期分析我们可以密切监测试验的进程，利用适应性的设计我们可以作出灵活的决策，故而在比较疗法差异时我们可以做到更加高效、客观和精准，从而加快新药的研发进程。

705613.label: Realisation of objectives
705613.value: All three aims have been fully addressed. The research results have produced a total of 8 publications. Aim 1 is to develop a Bayesian two-stage dose-finding method for cytostatic agents, in which stage 1 uses a mixture of parametric and nonparametric models to search for the maximum tolerated dose and stage 2 takes a Bayesian model averaging continual reassessment method to identify the optimum biological dose. The result for this aim is published as "Bayesian two-stage dose finding for cytostatic agents via model adaptation" in Appl. Statist. (2016) 65, Part 3, pp. 465–482. Aim 2 is to propose a single-to-double arm two-stage transition design for phase II clinical trials, and Aim 3 is to develop a two-arm randomized design for phase II clinical trials based on the Bayesian posterior and predictive probability monitoring with time-to-event data. Both aims are also fully addressed with several publications listed in the midreport. In addition, some neighboring ideas have also been explored. Beyond the midreport, three more publications have been produced.

705613.label: Major findings and research outcome
705613.value: Bayesian two-stage adaptive design provides a flexible framework for clinical trials. Stage 1 searches for the maximum tolerated dose by using a beta–binomial model in conjunction with a probit model, for which decision making is based on the model that fits the toxicity data better. Stage 2 identifies the optimal biological dose while still controlling the level of toxicity. The single-to-double arm two-stage transition design for phase II clinical trials can expedite the development of new drugs by eliminating the gap between two studies. Bayesian posterior and predictive probability monitoring with time-to-event data have become more and more important in phase II trials due to the emergence of a large number of cytostatic (targeted) agents. The proposed methods have successfully demonstrated their advantages in designing more adaptive and flexible trials, and making trial conduct more conherent and efficient. The related softwares (R packages) have been requested a number of times by different clinical trialists.

705613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
705613.value: Tremendous advances in our understanding of cancer genetics have led to an exciting and new type of early phase clinical trials, namely `basket' trials. In such trials, the drug is tested simultaneous in different baskets. Compared with the conventional clinical trial, the basket trial implements a hypothesis-driven strategy incorporating precision medicine or target therapy into clinical trial even for generic aberrations that are rare or difficult to study solely with a disease-specific context. Our methods can potentially be extended to such basket trials or platform trials, or even basket/platform trials where a number of new drugs and a number of biomarkers are being matched for treatment effectiveness prediction.

705713.value: 關於精算中相依風險模型的一些問題

705713.label: Project Objectives
705713.value: The first objective proposes a time-series risk model with claim number following a Poisson ARCH process. We carry out ruin analysis for the model through deriving the associated adjustment coefficient, and numerical studies to examine the effect of the Poisson ARCH dependence structure on several risk measures including ruin probability, value at risk, and conditional tail expectation. Based on the Poisson ARCH process, risk models with the common shock or thinning dependence can also be constructed. In the second objective, we consider the Poisson common shock and thinning risk models. Instead of the commonly-used expected value premium principle, the reinsurance premium principle is assumed to be the variance principle. Under the criterion of maximizing the expected exponential utility, we aim at deriving explicit expressions for the optimal strategy and value function, and studying numerically the impact of the model parameters on the optimal strategy. The third project objective involves several ruin problems for the bivariate compound binomial model defined in a Markovian environment. We first discuss how to compute the infinite-time survival probability numerically for the sum of two individual surplus processes. In the bivariate case, we define the ruin time as the minimum of the two individual ruin times. We focus on constructing upper bounds for the bivariate infinite-time ruin probability and investigating how the bivariate model of study relates to the bivariate Cox risk model.

705713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
705713.value: Due to the complexity of modern insurance and financial products, the study of dependence between various risks plays a major role in various pricing and hedging problems. Improper management of dependent risks may result in huge insurance claims after occurrences of natural disasters or terrible adversity after major financial market crashes. In the actuarial literature, modeling of dependent risks has been around for a few decades. Although much research has been done in this direction, many significant but unsolved problems remain to be investigated. In this project, we consider three actuarial problems in each of which the risk model of study possesses certain dependence structure. Time series modeling has a wide range of applications, in particular, to the study of economic and financial data. The first objective proposes a discrete-time risk model with claim number following a Poisson ARCH process. Our goal is to perform ruin analysis for the model through deriving the associated adjustment coefficient. We also plan to carry out numerical studies to examine the effect of the Poisson ARCH dependence structure on several risk measures including ruin probability, value at risk, and conditional tail expectation. The second project objective studies the optimal proportional reinsurance problem for risk models with two dependent classes of insurance business. Specifically, two types of dependence among the two claim-number processes, namely the common shock dependence and the thinning dependence, are considered. Under the criterion of maximizing the expected exponential utility with a variance principle, we try to obtain explicit expressions for the optimal reinsurance strategy and value function, and investigate the existence and uniqueness of the optimal strategy. We then numerically examine the impact of the model parameters on the optimal strategy. The third project objective introduces a bivariate compound binomial risk model in which the claim occurrences of the two different classes in each time period are governed by a Markovian process. Here, the occurrence random variables in the two classes depend on the change of state, perhaps indicating the change of economic or environmental condition from one period to the next period. For the sum of the two individual surplus processes, we discuss how to compute the infinite-time survival probability numerically. We then extend our study to the bivariate case. Specifically, we derive upper bounds for the bivariate infinite-time ruin probability, and show how the bivariate compound binomial risk model relates to the bivariate Cox risk model.

705713.label: Realisation of objectives
705713.value: For the first project objective (Objective 1 below), we propose a discrete-time risk model with the claim number following an integer-valued autoregressive conditional heteroscedasticity (ARCH) process with Poisson deviates. In this model, the mean of the current claim number depends on the previous observations. We first obtain some statistical properties for the aggregate claims process with Poisson ARCH(1) claim numbers. Within this framework, the equation for finding the adjustment coefficient is derived through the use of the moment generating function of the aggregate claims. We also show how our result can be extended to the Poisson ARCH(q). Finally, numerical studies are carried out to examine the effect of the Poisson ARCH dependence structure on the ruin probability. These results are presented in a paper entitled "A discrete-time risk model with Poisson ARCH claim-number process". It is expected that these results can be easily applied to Poisson ARCH risk model with common shock or thinning dependence. In practice, different classes of insurance business are usually dependent in some way. A typical example is that an earthquake, hurricane or tsunami, often leads to various kinds of insurance claims such as medical claims, death claims, and household claims. This example demonstrates a practical scenario that a single event generates claims from different lines of insurance. To depict such a dependence structure among several classes of business, the so-called common shock risk model and the thinning risk model are of some practical relevance. On the other hand, the problem of optimal reinsurance has been studied by many authors in the past two decades. Although research on optimal reinsurance is increasing rapidly, only a few papers deal with the problem in relation to dependent risks. In view of this, the second original project objective focuses on investigating 3 problems of optimal proportional reinsurance for the common shock and thinning risk models. They are stated in Objectives 2, 3, and 4 below. In Objective 2, we consider the optimal proportional reinsurance strategy in a risk model with two dependent classes of insurance business, where the two claim number processes are correlated through a common shock component. Under the criterion of maximizing the expected exponential utility and the variance premium principle, we adopt a nonstandard approach to examining the existence and uniqueness of the optimal reinsurance strategy. Using the technique of stochastic control theory, closed-form expressions for the optimal strategy and the value function are derived for the compound Poisson risk model as well as for the Brownian motion risk model. From the numerical examples, we see that the optimal results for the compound Poisson risk model are very different from those for the diffusion model. The former depends not only on the safety loading, time, and the interest rate, but also on the claim size distributions and the claim number processes, while the latter only depends on the safety loading, time, and the interest rate. In Objective 3, we consider the optimal proportional reinsurance strategy in a risk model with multiple dependent classes of insurance business, which extends the work in Objective 2 to the case with the reinsurance premium calculated under the expected value principle and to the model with two or more classes of dependent risks. Under the criterion of maximizing the expected exponential utility, closed-form expressions for the optimal strategies and value function are derived not only for the compound Poisson risk model but also for the diffusion approximation risk model. In particular, we find that the optimal reinsurance strategies under the expected value premium principle are very different from those under the variance premium principle in the diffusion risk model. Specifically, under the expected value premium principle, the optimal strategies depend not only on the safety loading, time and interest rate, but also on the claim size distributions and the counting processes, while the optimal strategies depend only on the safety loading, time and interest rate. Finally, numerical examples are presented to show the impact of model parameters on the optimal strategies. In Objective 4, we consider the problem of optimal reinsurance in a compound Poisson risk model with dependent classes of insurance business. It is assumed that the risk process in each class follows a compound Poisson process, and that all classes are correlated due to the so-called thinning-dependence structure. Under the criterion of maximizing the adjustment coefficient, methods for finding the optimal reinsurance strategies are discussed under the expected value premium principle as well as the variance premium principle. Numerical examples are also provided to illustrate the impact of the model parameters on the optimal reinsurance strategies. In the actuarial literature, there are risk models with dependence different from those in Objectives 2, 3 and 4. For example, it is sensible to assume that the risk process of an insurance company not only depends on the correlation among different risks but also on some economic factors. For the third original project objective, we consider another two risk models, namely a two-dimensional delayed renewal risk model with Sarmanov dependent claims and a discrete semi-Markov risk model which appear in Objectives 5 and 6, respectively. In Objective 5, we consider a two-dimensional delayed renewal risk model with a constant interest rate and dependent claims, where an insurance company operates two lines of business. Each line is assumed to be exposed to catastrophic risks like earthquakes, floods or terrorist attacks. Such risks may affect the two lines of the company at the same time, so the two lines of business share a common claim-number process and some dependence structure may exist between them. It is assumed that the claim sizes of the two lines form a sequence of independent and identically distributed random vectors following a common bivariate Sarmanov distribution. In the presence of heavy-tailed claim sizes, some asymptotic formulas are derived for the finite-time and infinite-time ruin probabilities. The asymptotic formulas successfully capture the impact of the underlying dependence structure of the claims of the two lines. In a Markov-modulated risk model, the premiums, claim amounts and claim number process are usually assumed to be (conditionally) independent given the environmental Markov chain, that is, they only depend on the current state of the Markov chain. However, this (conditional) independence assumption may be somewhat too strong in some applications. In Objective 6, we consider the survival probability for a discrete semi-Markov risk model, which assumes individual claims are influenced by a Markov chain with finite state space and there is autocorrelation among consecutive claim sizes. Our semi-Markov risk model is similar to the one studied by Reinhard and Snoussi (2001,2002) without the restriction imposed on the distributions of the claims. In particular, the model of study includes several existing risk models such as the compound binomial model (with time-correlated claims) and the compound Markov binomial model (with time-correlated claims) as special cases. The main purpose of this objective is to develop a recursive method for computing the survival probability in the two-state model, and present some numerical examples to illustrate the application of our results. References Reinhard, J.M. and Snoussi, M. (2001). On the distribution of the surplus prior to ruin in a discrete semi-Markov risk model, ASTIN Bulletin 31, 255-276. Reinhard, J.M. and Snoussi, M. (2002). The severity of ruin in a discrete semi-Markov risk model, Stochastic Models 18, 85-107.

705713.label: Major findings and research outcome
705713.value: For Objective 1, we derive the equation for finding the adjustment coefficient for a discrete-time risk model with the claim number following an ARCH process with Poisson deviates. The results are summarized in the paper entitled "A discrete-time risk model with Poisson ARCH claim-number process" which has been submitted to Applied Mathematics and Computation and is currently under review. For details, see Part C Item 15. For Objective 2, we investigate the optimal dynamic reinsurance for dependent insurance risks under the variance premium principle. The results are presented in the paper entitled "Optimal dynamic reinsurance with dependent risks: variance premium principle", which has been published in Scandinavian Actuarial Journal. For details, see Part C Item 11. For Objective 3, we study the optimal proportional reinsurance strategy in a risk model with multiple classes which are under the common shock dependence. The results are presented in the paper entitled "Optimal proportional reinsurance with common shock dependence", which has been published in Insurance: Mathematics and Economics. For details, see Part C Item 6. For Objective 4, we consider a risk model with thinning dependence and derive explicit expressions for the optimal reinsurance strategies under the expected value premium principle as well as the variance premium principle. The results are presented in the paper entitled "Optimal reinsurance in a compound Poisson risk model with dependence", which has been accepted by Journal of Applied Mathematics and Computing. For details, see Part C Item 16. For Objective 5, we consider a two-dimensional delayed renewal risk model with a constant interest rate, where the claim sizes of the two classes form a sequence of independent and identically distributed random vectors following a common bivariate Sarmanov distribution, and derive asymptotic formulas for the finite-time and infinite-time ruin probabilities. The results are presented in the paper entitled " Finite-time and infinite-time ruin probabilities in a two-dimensional delayed renewal risk model with Sarmanov dependent claims", which has been published in Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Application. For details, see Part C Item 13. For Objective 6, we consider the survival probability for a discrete semi-Markov risk model, which assumes individual claims are influenced by a Markov chain with finite state space and there is autocorrelation among consecutive claim sizes. The results are presented in the paper entitled "Survival probabilities in a discrete semi-Markov risk model", which has been published in Applied Mathematics and Computation. For details, see Part C Item 1.

705713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
705713.value: In relation to the project theme, namely actuarial problems for risk models with dependence, there are still many other interesting problems that one may consider. During the three-year project duration, we have published quite a number of additional research papers related to the project. These papers appear in various journals including IMA Journal of Management Mathematics, Insurance: Mathematics and Economics, Journal of Applied Probability, Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics, Journal of Industrial and Management Optimization, Lithuanian Mathematical Journal, Mathematical Methods of Operations Research, Methodology and Computing in Applied Probability, Scandinavian Actuarial Journal, Statistics and Probability Letters, Stochastic Analysis and Applications, and Stochastics and Dynamics. For details of these publications, see Part C Items 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14, 17, 18, and 19. For further research, one may consider incorporating other realistic features such as investment, dividends and capital injection into the optimization problems with dependent risks. Of course, these optimization problems become more complicated and challenging. In fact, the principal investigator has proposed some of these problems in the GRF 2016 grant application, and the grant application was successful.

705713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
705713.value: As the rapid growth of insurance products makes the financial analysis more and more complicated, research on the relationships between various lines of insurance risks is crucial to the development of more sophisticated tools for dynamic financial analysis. In reality, it is very likely that a natural disaster causes different kinds of claims such as disability, life, medical, motor, and property insurance claims, and that the amounts of claims among different lines of business are positively correlated. In daily life, medical and motor insurance claims occur due to a severe car accident. These examples certainly justify the importance of studying the financial impact of dependent risks on insurance business. As a result, careful and thorough analysis of various dependence structures is needed to obtain accurate risk assessment. Furthermore, companies often purchase reinsurance at the expenses of making less potential profit as the financial impact of huge claims on the insurance industry could be considerable. Therefore, in the presence of dependent risks, it is important for an insurer to determine the reinsurance strategies that optimize some pre-specified objectives. This project tackles some of the central problems in these directions, and hence the findings and research outcome are of practical and theoretical significance.

706013.label: Project Title(Chinese)
706013.value: 基於結構的網絡流研究

706013.label: Project Objectives
706013.value: To prove Karzanov's conjecture on total dual 1/4-integrality in the maximum multiflow problem; To characterize all pairs (G, H), where G is a planar supply graph having H as a demand graph, such that the cut condition is always sufficient for the existence of a feasible multiflow; and To establish that every 2-edge-connected multigraph with no so-called fully odd K4-partition admits a nowhere-zero 3-flow, which is the dual version of an important 3-color theorem obtained independently by Thomassen and the PI.
rows: To prove Karzanov's conjecture on total dual 1/4-integrality in the maximum multiflow problem;
To characterize all pairs (G, H), where G is a planar supply graph having H as a demand graph, such that the cut condition is always sufficient for the existence of a feasible multiflow; and

To establish that every 2-edge-connected multigraph with no so-called fully odd K4-partition admits a nowhere-zero 3-flow, which is the dual version of an important 3-color theorem obtained independently by Thomassen and the PI.

706013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
706013.value: 網絡流理論，由於其深刻的理論內容和廣闊的應用背景，在過去六十年得到了廣泛的研究，使之演變成既有優美理論又有高效方法的一個領域。最大流問題是該領域的一個最基本問題，旨在給定的網絡中尋找從源到匯運輸單樣物資的滿足弧的容量限制的最大可行流。眾所周知，最大流問題在強多項式時間內可解，並且在弧的容量都是整數時，該問題存在整最優解。在眾多求解最大流問題的算法中，增廣路算法最具數學美感，它在給出了最大流的同時，作為其副產品，不僅能找出最小割，還導出了著名的最大流最小割定理。最大流最小割定理是網絡流理論中的核心定理，它可用來解決許多優化問題（例如可行流問題和環流問題等），從而具有深遠的影響力。 運輸多種物資的情形卻截然不同：最大多種物資流問題的整最優解未必存在。因此，整值的最大多種物資流最小割定理不成立。此外，割條件（它要求每個割的容量不小於經過這個割的總需求量）不再是可行多種物資流存在的充分條件。更有甚者，最大整多種物資流問題和可行整多種物資流問題都是NP-困難的。因此，除非P=NP，否則人們不可能找到有效的算法來確切地解決這兩個問題中的任何一個。對離散數學中的難問題，常用的方法是利用結構上的限制來揭示其本質。本項目的研究內容主要包括最大多種物資流問題，可行多種物資流問題，以及經典環流問題的一個變形問題。基於結構分析的方法，本項目旨在給出這些問題所具有的重要的整性和可行性，擬針對以下幾個問題展開研究： (1) 對於最大多種物資流問題，證明Karzanov 提出的1/4 全對偶整性猜想； (2) 對G是平面圖的情形，刻畫所有的 (G，H) 對，使得前面提到的割條件是可行多種物資流存在的充分條件，其中G是供應圖，而H是需求圖； (3) 證明：若一個2-邊連通圖G不存在全奇（fully odd）K4-劃分，則G存在處處非零的3-流。該問題是由本項目負責人所證明的一個重要的三色定理的對偶形式。

706013.label: Realisation of objectives
706013.value: I have completely resolved the problem specified in Objective 3. I have also made significant progress towards the resolution of problems specified in Objectives 1 and 2; I firmly believe that complete solutions to these two problems are within reach. Moreover, with the support of the current grant, I have successfully resolved several other long-standing open problems.

706013.label: Major findings and research outcome
706013.value: With the support of this grant, I have successfully proved that every 2-edge-connected multigraph with no so-called fully odd K4-partition admits a nowhere-zero 3-flow, thereby establishing the dual version of Toft's conjecture I confirmed before. I have also made significant progress on Karzanov's conjecture on total dual 1/4-integrality in the maximum multiflow problem, and have established several steps towards the characterization of all pairs (G, H), where G is a planar supply graph having H as a demand graph, such that the cut condition is always sufficient for the existence of a feasible multiflow. I strongly believe that the solutions to the latter two problems are within reach. Moreover, jointly with my collaborators, I have managed to resolve several ong-standing open problems, such as the Cameron-Edmonds conjecture on box-perfect graphs and open problem on kernel polytope posed by Egervary Research Group on Combinatorial Optimization (EGRES), Eotvos Lorand University, Hungary.

706013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
706013.value: A complete proof of Karzanov's conjecture on total dual 1/4-integrality in the maximum multiflow problem, and a complete characterization of all pairs (G, H), where G is a planar supply graph having H as a demand graph, such that the cut condition is always sufficient for the existence of a feasible multiflow.

706013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
706013.value: The present project has both theoretical interest and practical value. First, the proposed problems are all fundamental and attractive; solution to any of them will represent a solid contribution to discrete mathematics. In fact, the dual integrality property and cut sufficiency in multiflows have been subjects of extensive research; successful completion of the first two objectives will yield a substantial strengthening and generalization of many existing results. Moreover, nowhere-zero integer flow and graph coloring are dual concepts, and the study of them has led to rich developments in several fields. The 3-flow theorem addressed in the third objective, if obtained, will nicely complement Tutte's 3-, 4-, and 5-flow conjectures, which are "arguably the most significant problems in the whole of graph theory", as remarked by Bondy and Murty in their book entitled Graph Theory (see page 567). Second, since our research topics cover a wide spectrum of combinatorics and optimization, in our investigation we have to develop various new solution techniques and exhibit a wealth of new structural properties enjoyed by flow networks, which, we believe, can surely be carried over to the study of some other prominent open problems in network flow theory. Finally, as both the maximum multiflow problem and the feasible multiflow problem arise in a rich variety of applications, the results obtained in this project can be applied to solve many important real-world problems.
