706213.label: Project Title(Chinese)
706213.value: WISE全天区巡天中行星状星云的探测

706213.label: Project Objectives
706213.value: Search for new Galactic planetary nebulae (PNe) with the WISE All-Sky Survey. Search for faint extended infrared structures of PNe, and study the history of asymptotic giant branch stellar winds and the PN-interstllar medium interaction. Investigate the dust distribution and intrinsic structures of PNe. Promote the astrophysics education in Hong Kong.
rows: Search for new Galactic planetary nebulae (PNe) with the WISE All-Sky Survey.
Search for faint extended infrared structures of PNe, and study the history of asymptotic giant branch stellar winds and the PN-interstllar medium interaction.
Investigate the dust distribution and intrinsic structures of PNe.
Promote the astrophysics education in Hong Kong.

706213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
706213.value: When low- or intermediate-mass stars evolve off the asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stage, they eject the matter from stellar surfaces into the interstellar medium (ISM) to form planetary nebulae (PNe). PNe, therefore, play a vital role in understanding the interaction between stellar material and the ISM. Traditionally, the census of PNe is through observations at visible wavelengths. However, due to the extinction of interstellar dust, the number of Galactic PNe discovered through various optical surveys is far less than the theoretical prediction. Interstellar dust can also obscure the extended structures of some PNe, and thus that the ``observed'' nebular masses were less than the real values. This hampers the study of PN-ISM interaction, and leads to misclassification of the morphology of PNe. Recently, the highly improved infrared observation technique opens a new window to investigate PNe. It is well established that PNe contain a substantial quantity of dust that can strongly emit in the infrared range. Unlike optical emission, infrared observations are hardly affected by interstellar extinction, and thus have considerable advantages in searching for new PNe and extended structures. The observations by the Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE)-- a recent all-sky survey mission at four infrared bands with high spatial resolution and sensitivity-- provide an invaluable resource for that purpose. Here we propose to use the publicly available WISE archive data to study PNe. Our aims are threefold: (1) to search for new PNe and PN candidates; (2) to search for extended structures of previously known PNe and study their interaction with the ISM; and (3) to study the spatial distributions of dust and ionized gas within PNe by comparing optical and infrared images. Finally, we would like to emphasize that promoting astrophysics education in Hong Kong is an important purpose of our project. The grant would be used to partially support one student getting involved in this research.

706213.label: Realisation of objectives
706213.value: 1. We systematically compared the colours of different sources whose natures have well known, and studies their locations in the color-color diagrams. A sample of new planetary nebula (PN) candidates has been selected based on the colours indicated from the WISE catalogue. We found that these infrared colours can only provide very loose constrains on PN natures. Specifically, we cannot distinguished HII regions and PNe form the WISE colour diagrams. Therefore, we performed new optical spectroscopies to identify these sources, and found a few of them are likely to be real PNe. Although a long manuscript (by Yu, Zhang et al.) on WISE PNe has been unfortunately rejected, some of these results have been published in ApJ. 2. Based on our investigation of the WISE images of some bright PNe, we have found weak signals of new extended PN structures. We performed new observations of H2 emission using the CFHT, and identified many interesting features that are far away from but still associated from PNe. The newly discovered structures provide important clues on the mass-loss history of PNe. Based on the studies of young and old PNe, we presented a hypothesis how the PN morphologies evolved from multi-polar to symmetric. 3. Based on the WISE and new CFHT, we found that the dust and molecular hydrogen have a similar spatial distributions, supporting the formation of H2 on dust surfaces. The H2 emission appears to be clumpy and filamentary, suggesting the molecule can largely shield the strong UV radiation from the central star and survive during the PN evolution. The infrared images of some PNe differ from their optical images, suggesting that one may misclassify the PNe if only basing on their optical observations. To reproduce these image observations, we also constructed 3D models of PNe using the SHAPE code. The main challenge is that there are too many free parameters. To overcome that, we have to make some reasonable assumptions. 4. We have trained a summer student from the Beijing Normal University (Miss Niu Ze Xi). A local PhD student (Mr Chau Wayne) has been working this project. Mr. Chau has found that O-rich and C-rich evolved stars show different tracks in the WISE color-color diagram, and we have discussed the insights of this finding. The main problem is that not many students in Hong Kong are willing to take astrophysics as their lifelong profession. We must devote long-term efforts to promote the astrophysics eduction in Hong Kong.

706213.label: Major findings and research outcome
706213.value: This research project results in a total 11 papers, all of which are published in top astrophysics journals, as well as 5 conference papers. New planetary nebulae (PNe) and PN structures were discovered for the first time. Deep spectra of a few of them were obtained (e.g. Hsia et al. 2014, A&A). An interesting example is that two pairs of knots are found around Hb 12. They are very far away but symmetric with respect to this PN, indicating to a bipolar, rotating, episodic jet (Hsia et al. 2016 conference proceeding, Fang et al. in preparation). We found that some PNe show very interesting infrared emission, which can be identified as hydrogenated C60 (including about 100 atoms). This is the largest molecules detected in space so far. This result has been published in ApJ recently (Zhang et al. 2017, ApJ), and I was invited to give a review talk in a IAU symposium (Zhang 2017). Some infrared features in PNe are due to complex organics. We discussed their possible carriers and origins (Zhang et al. 2015, ApJ). This research may shed some insights on the formation of life seed. We examined the tradition opinion that the energy distribution of free electrons in PNs follow a Maxwell-Boltzmann law by developing a novel plasma diagnostics (Zhang et al. 2014, 2016, ApJ). Furthermore, we investigate the infrared images of a likely pre-PN IRAS 19312+1950, which might be a new type of class I methanol maser (Nakashima et al. 2015, PASJ, 2016, ApJ). We also investigate several PNe in extra-galaxy, which provides information about the formation of M31 (Fang et al. 2018, ApJ).

706213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
706213.value: The size of WISE data is extremely huge. So far we studied part of the data in its early release. We intend to continue to search for new PNe and PN structures using recently re-reduced data. Our sample selected from WISE database merit further optical spectroscopy to confirm their nature. It is worth to re-observe these extend infrared structures in a ten-year scale to investigate their proper motions, which will inform us the velocity of the early stellar winds. The informations of these infrared PN structures can be further revealed by recently released Herschel infrared data. Combining the WISE, CFHT, and Herschel images can inform us about the spatial distributions of dust grains with different size, and the dust temperatures.

706213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
706213.value: When a low or medium star die, it will eject material into the space to forming planetary nebulae (PNe) with many intriguing structures (e.g. butterfly-shaped, ant-shaped, starfish-shaped, Eskimo-like). It is unclear how a round star is able to create such asymmetrical structures. This problem is related to the fate of the Sun. In this project, we has studied the spatial distributions of dust and molecule components of PNe using the WISE database. WISE is a wide-filed infrared survey explorer launched by NASA, and is particularly suitable to study the large-scale nebular structures. The survey data have been released to the public for various research projects. Our project can provide insights on the mass-loss history of PNe and how the different structures are developed.

706313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
706313.value: The Paleo-Asian ocean was a Neoproterozoic to Paleozoic ocean located between Tarim-North China and Siberia, whose opening was related to the breakup of Rodinia and whose expansion and closure led to the formation of the Central Asian Orogenic Belt (CAOB) and collision of Tarim-North China and East Europe-Siberia. As the largest accretionary orogen in Earth’s history, the CAOB has attracted much attention of the international geological community in the past decade and extensive geological investigations have been carried out on this belt, producing large amounts of new data and competing interpretations. However, most of these investigations were focused on the accretionary processes of the belt, and especially on the formation and evolution of active continental margins on both sides of the ocean and island arcs within the ocean. Comparatively, few studies were concentrated on the final closure of the Paleo-Asian ocean and consequently, it still remains controversial when Tarim-North China was fused with East Europe-Siberia. This is particularly the case with the Chinese Tianshan orogen, which is considered to have resulted from the closure of the western sector of the Paleo-Asian ocean, called the Tianshan ocean, between the Tarim craton in the south and the Illi-Central Tianshan arc in the north. Controversy has long surrounded the timing of the closure of the Tianshan ocean, with different models proposed, ranging from those invoking the late Devonian or late Carboniferous closure to those arguing for the late Permian or Triassic collision. These models were mainly established on the basis of a few unconformities and mineral Ar-Ar ages obtained for blueschists and eclogites from the west Tianshan orogeny. The unconformities and mineral Ar-Ar ages are open to different interpretations and thus cannot provide convincing constraints on the timing of the final closure of the Tianshan ocean. This forms the justification for this proposed project in which we will utilize a new and alternative approach to resolve the above issue by tracing the provenance of clastic sediments and especially U-Pb ages and Hf isotopes of detrital zircons from Paleozoic strata on the northern margin of the Tarim craton in order to determine when the basins on this margin started to receive sediments from the Illi-Central Tianshan arc, which can be used to mark the timing of the final closure of the Tianshan ocean and collision between the Tarim craton and the Illi-Central Tianshan arc. 古亚洲洋是塔里木-华北和西伯利亚大陆之间的晚元古代-古生代古大洋。它的开启与Rodinia超大陆裂解有关，而它的扩张和闭合导致中亚造山带和形成和木-华北和西伯利亚的拼合。作为地球历史上最大的增生性造山带，中亚造山带在过去十年里吸引国际地学界的大量目光并开张了广泛的地质研究，产生了大量新数据和竞争性的解释。然而，这些研究中绝大部分集中在该造山带的增生过程，尤其是集中在大洋两侧活动性大陆边缘和洋内岛弧的形成和演化方面。相对而言，有关古亚洲洋的闭合研究却很少。因此，有关塔里木-华北和东欧-西伯利亚大陆合适拼合在一起的问题一直存在争论。作为古亚洲洋西段（称为天山洋）闭合产物的中国天山造山带更是如此。该造山带被认为是位于南部的塔里木克拉通和和北部的伊犁-中天山弧拼合而成。有关天山洋何时闭合一直存在争论，并提出了不同模式，包括那些认为晚泥盆或晚石炭纪拼合和那些认为是晚二叠或早三叠碰撞模式。这些模式主要基于西天山几个不整合和蓝片岩、榴辉岩矿物氩-氩年龄。然而，这些不整合和矿物氩-氩年龄有不同的解释，因此它们对天山洋最终闭合不能提供令人信服的制约。这就是我们提出这个研究项目的主要目的。在这个项目中，我们将通过一种新的研究途径解决上述争论，即通过追踪塔里木克拉通北缘古生代碎屑锆石物源，尤其是U-Pb年龄和Hf同位素组成来确定这些盆地何时开始接收来至北面犁-中天山弧的碎屑物，由此来限定天山洋最终闭合时间和塔里木克拉通和和北部的伊犁-中天山弧拼合拼合时间。

706313.label: Realisation of objectives
706313.value: We have successfully completed all six objectives designed for this project as follows: Objective 1 is to determine the spatial distribution and sequences of the Paleozoic strata at the northern margin of the Tarim craton. This objective was completed by four times of fieldwork: June 4- July 16, 2014; August 10-19, 2014; June 28-July 20, 2015; and July 25-August 24, 2015. During these field trips, the Principal Investigator (Guochun Zhao), two CIs (Yanhong He and Chaohui Liu) and PI’s Phd and MPhil students (Yigui Han, Xiaoran Zhang, Paul Reinhold Eizenhofer, Wenzhu Hou, Yanlin Zhu, Qian Liu and Hui-Chun Chen) went to the northern margin of the Tarim craton and the West and East Tianshan areas, where Cambrian to Permian strata with clastic sediments are widely exposed. In the field, we carried out large-scale mapping work on the spatial distribution of major Paleozoic strata in these areas, and we also collected ~900 samples for petrographic, structural, whole-rock geochemical and zircon U-Pb age dating and Hf isotopic studies. Objective 2 is to determine the nature of the major structural episodes at the northern margin of the Tarim craton. This objective was completed by detailed structural investigations along the N-S-trending Kalpin-Akeqi and South Wushi cross sections and the E-W-trending Aksu-Wushi-Akeqi cross section in the Artux-Aksu area. In the field, we took statistics and measurements of various foliations, lineation and various senses of thrusting and shearing by which we identified three episodes of deformation (D1 to D3) of which D1 is represented by small isoclinal and recumbent folds, D2 produced large-scale asymmetric folds and an associated penetrative axial planar foliation, a mineral stretching lineation and regional-scale ductile shear zones, and D3 is indicated by open to tight folds of varying scales, axial crenulation cleavages and EW-striking thrust faults, involving broadly N-S compression. Objective 3 is to restore the paleocurrent direction and it was completed by studying asymmetry wave ripples, oblique beddings and cross beddings on the basis of eliminating structural effects in the field. Our results show that the paleocurrents along the northern margin of the Tarim craton were mostly northward before Early Devovian but changed to southward direction after the Early Devonian. The tectonic implication of such a paleocurrent direction shift has been discussed in a paper entitled “Paleozoic accretionary orogenesis in the Paleo-Asian Ocean: Insights from detrital zircons from Silurian to Carboniferous strata at the northwestern margin of the Tarim Craton (Tectonics v. 34(2), p. 334-351; see Publication No. 2 in Part C). Objective 4 is to discriminate the sedimentary environments of Paleozoic strata on the northern margin of the Tarim craton. This objective was completed by studying detrital components of sandstones combined with whole-rock geochemical analysis. During the fieldwork carried out on June 4-July 16, 2014; August 10-19, 2014; June 28-July 20, 2015; and July 25-August 24, 2015, we have collected 300 geochemical samples, of which 186 samples were finally selected for whole-rock analysis. The results of our study suggest that the northern margin of the Tarim craton represented an active continental margin arc during Early Paleozoic time but changed to a passive continental margin from the Late Devonian to Late Carboniferous. The research outcomes of this objective have been reflected in Publication Nos. 1-5 listed in Part C. Objective 5 is to determine the provenances of clastic sediments. We completed this objective by utilizing the SHRIMP and LA-ICP-MS U–Pb zircon dating and Lu-Hf analyzing techniques to determine U-Pb ages and εHf values of detrital zircons from the bottom to top sequences of Paleozoic strata on the northern margin of the Tarim craton. During the fieldwork carried out on June 4-July 16, 2014; August 10-19, 2014; June 28-July 20, 2015; and July 25-August 24, 2015, we have collected 500 samples SHRIMP and LA-ICP-MS U–Pb zircon dating and Lu-Hf analysis. Our results indicate that the zircon age patterns of Early Paleozoic strata from the Central Tianshan terrane remarkably match those of Early Paleozoic strata at the northern margin of the Tarim Craton, whereas their zircon age patterns became to be different since the Middle Devonian, which suggests that the Central Tianshan terrane may have been part of the northern margin of the Tarim craton during Early Paleozoic time but was broken off from the Tarim Craton since the Middle Devonian. The results are reflected in Publication Nos. 2-8. Objective 6 is to determine the time of the final closure of the Tianshan ocean. We completed this objective by tracing when the basins at the northern margin of the Tarim craton started to receive sediments from the Ili-Central Tianshan arc. Our results also suggest that the final closure of the Tianshan Ocean (a branch of the Paleo-Asian Ocean) was closed along the West and East Tianshan Orogen at about 300 Ma. The results are reflected in Publication Nos. 1 and 2.

706313.label: Major findings and research outcome
706313.value: In the last three years, the PI and his research group have carried out extensive and comprehensive investigations on Paleozoic strata on the northern margin of the Tarim craton and produced large amounts of new data and interpretations which are reflected in 26 refereed papers that we published in leading international journals including Geology, Tectonics, GSA Bulletin, etc (see Publications listed in Part C). We summarize our major findings and research outcomes as follows: 1. We demonstrated that the initiation of southward subduciton of the Paleo-Asian Ocean beneath the northern margin of the Tarim and North China blocks was caused by collision of the two blocks with the northern margin of Gondwana at 500-470 Ma, whereas the tectonic transition from advancing to retreating subduction on the northern margins of the two blocks resulted from the breakup of the two blocks from Gondwana. The results of this study was published in Geology, one of the highest level journals in earth sciences (See Publication No. 1 listed in Part C). 2. Our study has revealed that the evolution of the western segment of the Paleo-Asian Ocean was involved in the closure of an ancient Tianshan Ocean and opening of the South Tianshan Ocean during late Devonian time and the closure of the South Tianshan Ocean during late Carboniferous to early Permian time (310-280 Ma). The related results have been published in a number of leading international journals including Tectonics, GSA Bulletin, Lithos, etc (see Publication Nos. 2-5 and 7-12). 3. Our results confirm the scissor-like closing of the Paleo-Asian Ocean from the west (310-280 Ma), through the middle (280-265 Ma), to east (270-240 Ma) segments. The related results are reflected in Publication Nos. 6 and 14-18 (see Part C). 4. Our results also confirm that the Central Tianshan Terrane represented an active continental margin arc bordering the northern margin of the Tarim Craton during Early Paleozoic time and later was broken off from the Tarim Craton with the opening of a new Tianshan Ocean that was closed at about 310-280 Ma, leading to the amalgamation of the Tarim Craton in the south and the Illi-Central Tianshan arc in the north. Papers related to this research outcome have been published in a number of leading international journals (see Publication Nos. 2-5 and 7-12 listed in Part C).

706313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
706313.value: Our results from this project confirm that the Central Tianshan Terrane represented an active continental margin arc bordering the northern margin of the Tarim Craton during Early Paleozoic time and later was broken off from the Tarim Craton with the opening of a new Tianshan Ocean that was closed at about 310-280 Ma, leading to the amalgamation of the Tarim Craton in the south and the Illi-Central Tianshan arc in the north. Whether or not our model established in this project can be tested with paleomagnetic data for Neoproterozoic and Paleozoic rocks at the northern margin of the Tarim Craton and the Central Tianshan Terrane. In future, we plan to apply for a Hong Kong RGC project entitled “Paleomagnetic study on the Neoproterozoic and Paleozoic rocks at the northern margin of the Tarim Craton and the Central Tianshan Terrane”.

706313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
706313.value: The timing of collision in many classical continent-continent collisional belts can determined by dating metamorphic zircons from medium- to high-grade rocks. However, some collisional belts have only low-grade rocks and thus the timing of collisional events cannot be well determined. This is the case with the Tianshan Orogen that resulted from the closure of the western sector of the Paleo-Asian Ocean. In this Hong Kong RGC GRF project (HKU7063/13P), we applied a new approach to resolve the above issue by tracing the provenance of clastic sediments from Paleozoic strata on the northern margin of the Tarim craton in order to determine when the basins on this margin started to receive sediments from the Illi-Central Tianshan arc, which can be used to mark the timing of the final closure of the Tianshan ocean and collision between the Tarim craton and the Illi-Central Tianshan arc. Our results also confirm that the Central Tianshan Terrane represented an active continental margin arc bordering the northern margin of the Tarim Craton during Early Paleozoic time and later was broken off from the Tarim Craton with the opening of a new Tianshan Ocean that was closed at about 310-280 Ma.

706413.label: Project Objectives
706413.value: Cenozoic basalts from NE and SE China have different PGE (Yang et al., 2011b). Why there are such differences is not well understood because of the lack of systematic dataset. This project will provide systematic PGE data on representative Cenozoic basalts from both NE and SE China. With the new dataset, we will explore whether or not the chemical differences between the basalts from NE and SE China were caused by different mantle sources or magmatic evolutions. Published major and trace elemental and Sr-Nd isotopic compostions on Cenozoic basalts from Eastern China suggest these basalts especially alkaline basalts may have not undergone significant crustal contamination (e.g., Zeng et al., 2010; Xu et al., 2012). This project will utilize isotopic data to re-evaluate the effects of possible crustal contamination on the compositions of the basalts. The basalts will be compared with those in Tengchung, SW China, and MORBs in Indian ocean.

706413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
706413.value: Basalts provide important information on the evolution of the Earth because they are the most abundant crustal rock type derived directly from the mantle. Cenozoic basalts are abundant in Eastern China. They have been extensively described in the literature but their tectonic environment of formation is still widely debated. Some workers proposed models related to the subduction of the Pacific Plate, whereas others preferred a hotspot origin. Dispute continues as to whether they were derived from metasomatised lithospheric mantle or from an asthenospheric source. Systematic studies of platinum group elements (PGEs) and Re-Os isotopic compositions of the lavas are not currently available for these rocks, largely because of the analytic difficulties involved. These elements and isotopes, in conjunction with data on lithophile elements and isotopes, should provide significant information about the mantle source(s) and compositional evolution of the basalts. Because PGEs partition into sulfides much more readily than into silicates, they can provide very robust constraints on sulfide saturation and silicate fractionation of mafic magmas. Re-Os isotopic compositions can be used to examine mantle sources (lithospheric vs. asthenospheric mantle) and the effects of crustal contamination. Previous studies have shown that Cenozoic basalts in NE and SE China have significantly different PGE and Re-Os compositions but these differences need to be confirmed with more comprehensive dataset. If these variations can be confirmed, the causes of such variations can be better understood with systematic geochemical and isotopic datasets for these rocks. This project will provide new, high-quality, and systematic PGE and Re-Os isotopic data on representative Cenozoic basalts from both NE and SE China. Although Cenozoic basalts in SE China are believed to originate from a mixed source involving a depleted MORB mantle (DMM) and an enriched mantle component (EM1 and EM2 for basalts from NE and SE China, respectively), there is no consensus on the nature or origin of the EM1 and EM2 components in the mantle and their contributions. In this project, we will use PGE and Re-Os isotopic compositions of the Cenozoic basalts to identify possible end-member mantle sources, and we will explore whether the chemical differences between the basalts in NE and SE China reflect different sources or different magmatic evolutions. The project will have general implications for the genesis of basalts. 玄武岩能为地球演化提供重要的信息，因为它是直接来源于地幔的体积最大的地壳岩石类型。中国东部发育大量的新生代玄武岩，然而由于分析难度较大，对这些玄武质熔浆缺少系统的铂族元素（PGE）和铼锇（Re-Os）同位素研究。前人研究表明，中国东北和东南的新生代玄武岩有明显不同的PGE和Re-Os组成，但是缺乏系统的数据来证实。本项目将为中国东北和东南典型的中生代玄武岩提供新的高质量的和系统的PGE成分和Re-Os同位素数据。尽管中国东南的中生代玄武岩被认为起源于亏损MORB地幔（DMM）和富集地幔端员（EM1-中国东北玄武岩，EM2-中国东南玄武岩）的混合源区，EM1和EM2端员的特点和起源以及它们的贡献还没有达成一致的结论。本项目将通过中生代玄武岩的PGE和Re-Os同位素组成来判断可能的地幔端员源区，同时也将探索中国东北和东南玄武岩化学成分的不同是否反应不同的源区或不同的岩浆演化过程。本项目将对玄武岩的起源有重要的指示意义。

706413.label: Realisation of objectives
706413.value: This project involved the work of a post-doctor fellow, Su Benxun, and PhD students, Yang Yang and Liu Pingping. Since the start of this project, we have carried out field work and extensive laboratory work both in Mainland and HK. In the past, we have been in the field two times and have also attended some conferences. Extensive collaboration with geologists in Mainland was part of the project. This includes work with Dr. Huang Xiaowen from Institute of Geochemistry, Chinese Academy of Science in Guiyang and Dr. Zeng Gang from Nanjing University, China. PGE and Re-Os isotpe analyses were also carried out. Although the study was partially based on the previous findings of the research group of Zhou at HKU, we have also generated many new ideas during the work in this project. We have focused the studies in the surrounding areas of HK but also include Penghu Island of Taiwan and Cenozoic basalts in Jiangsu province. Specifically Dr. Huang worked on samples from Taiwan and Fujiang and published a most recent paper on PGE and Re-Os data for these basalts in Lithos. Dr. Zeng， together with other group members, have conducted PGE and Re-Os analyses on rocks from Jiangsu and published the results in 2016, also in Lithos. With new observation and lab work, we reached the objectives with 8 papers published. Some results were presented in international conferences and were well received.

706413.label: Major findings and research outcome
706413.value: Our previous objectives set in our original proposal are all reached. Our activities related to the project have been productive. As expected, there were no major problems during the project period. The project was in fact a continuation of several previous studies of our research group at HKU but tackled new problems with significant implications. To study Cenozoic basalts in East China, we have also investigated Indian ocean ridge basalts (MORB) and analyzed their PGE and Re-Os isotopic compositions as well as magmatism in subduction zone environments under which podiform chromite deposits formed （Yang et al. 2013, 2014, Gao et al. 2015; Zhou et al. 2014）. We have examined PGE contents in the Cenozoic Tengchong volcanic rocks (Huang et al. 2013) and in porphyry Cu deposits (Gao et al. 2015) Basalts from the western, central, and eastern belts in SE China are PGE-depleted due to sulfur-saturation fractionation. Fractional crystallization and partial melting are not sufficient to explain the observed PGE variations in these basalts. These basalts have been derived from compositionally variable mantle sources with variable sulfide retention in the mantle and variable sulfide removal during magma ascent. The temporal PGE variations in these basalts may reflect the heterogeneity of the mantle source beneath SE China, which could be attributed to variable fluid/melt metasomatism in the SCLM, related to the subduction of the Paleo-Pacific Plate. This finding is published in Lithos (Huang et al. 2017). In our studies of basalts from Jiangsu Province, both low-Ca and high-Ca alkaline basalts from Nanjing basaltic field are highly depleted in PGEs relative to Ni and Cu and were derived from sulfide-saturated, partial melts of the mantle source. High-Ca alkaline basalts have highly variable Cu/Pd and Pd/Ir ratios and have undergone sulfide-saturated assimilation-fractionation crystallization (SAFC). Some high-Ca alkaline basalts deviate from the trend of crustal contamination, which can be explained by the fractionation of laurite or Ru–Os–Ir alloys with olivine. PGE compositions of low-Ca alkaline basalts are primarily controlled by xenolith-magma interaction (Zeng et al. 2016). Overall, this project was successful with important findings published in highly ranked journals in the field of the study. There are totally 8 full articles published in international refereed journals including 3 papers in Lithos (IF-impact fact =>3) and 1 in Chemical Geology (IF>3), 1 in Journal of Asian Earth Sciences (IF=2.7), 1 paper in Ore Geology Reviews (IF>3) and 2 paper in Gondwana Research (IF>7). .

706413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
706413.value: The project was completed with all objectives realized. The remaining problems are identified for further studies and include better constraints on the origin of the primary compositions of magmas. To do this, more experimental investigation is needed. A particularly useful aspect is to examine melt inclusions in silicate minerals including olivine and clinopyroxene. We anticipate to eventually establish a new model that involves the subduction of the Pacific oceanic plate that contributed to the generation of basalts in various ways.

706413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
706413.value: Objectives set in our original proposal were basically obtained and all the activities related to the project were smooth. As expected, there were no major problems during the project period. Post-doc fellow, Su Benxu, was an essential member, for extensive field investigation and laboratory analyses. The project was in fact a continuation of several previous studies of our research group at HKU but tackled new problems with significant implications. In this project, we have been working on Platinum-group elements and Re-Os isotopic geochemistry of basalts. The main focus is to understand the process of sulfide saturation during the magma evolution. To realize the objectives, we examined Indian middle ocean ridge basalts, ophilitic complexes and Tengchung volcanic rocks in addition to the studies of Cenozoic basalts in East China. We have made some major achievements in the understanding of their origin and evolution. Overall, this project was successful with important findings published in highly ranked journals. There is a major breakthrough, particularly sulfide saturation history in Cenozoic basalts. Isotopic and textural evidence is provided in this study. A model for the origin of these basalts is now well established.

709313.label: Project Objectives
709313.value: We will study the phase diagram of the Bose-Hubbard model subjected to spin-orbit coupling using a new slave boson theory. We shall investigate the role of magnetic ordering and its fluctuations in the vicinity of the superfluid-Mott insulator transition and the characteristics of the phase transition. Excitations on top of the ordered states will be investigated and their evolution across the phase transition determined. Experimental aspects will be addressed. We will also study the possibility of exotic topological phases in which both charge and spin are disordered at zero temperature. We will study the two-body problem of fermions with spin-orbit couplings in an optical lattice and investigate the effects of Fermi surface on its energy and stability. Based on this, we will study possible pairing schemes in fermion systems. Possible topological phases will be studied and the possibility of their experimental observation will be investigated.

709313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
709313.value: Ultra-cold atomic gases have emerged as excellent laboratories for investigating strongly interacting quantum many-body systems due to their high degree of controllability. They provide an ideal platform to gain insight into correlated quantum phases and phase transitions, areas that are of intense interest to the condensed matter physics community and yet which are still poorly understood in many regards. With the recent realization of synthetic gauge fields and spin-orbit coupling for neutral atoms, it has become possible to study a wider array of quantum phases that not only have direct relevance to condensed matter systems such as topological insulators and superfluids, but also are unique in their own right. In this proposal, we plan to study two cases of immediate interest: (1) The Bose-Hubbard model with spin-orbit coupling and (2) the Bose-Einstein condensate to Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BEC-BCS) crossover of lattice fermions with spin-orbit coupling. Both systems are now being actively implemented in experiments. In the first part, we plan to investigate the phase diagram of the Bose-Hubbard model with spin-orbit coupling using a new slave boson formulation and to study in detail the interplay between magnetism and superfluidity. In particular, we would like to understand how this interplay modifies the character of the superfluid-Mott insulator transition. To corroborate the slave boson formulation, we plan to carry out Quantum Monte Carlo simulations of projected variational wave functions. A key advantage of our new slave boson formulation is that we can investigate the possibility of new topological quantum phases in the Mott insulating regime. In the second part of the proposal, we will investigate the possible pairing schemes for spin-orbit coupled fermions in “optical lattices”, periodic potentials constructed from counter-propagating laser beams that mimic the role of ion lattice in solid state systems. We will approach this problem by first studying in detail the structure of two-body bound states in vacuum as well as in medium to understand the role of many-body physics. Our goal is to find new topological quantum phases and identify robust experimental signatures of these phases. 近年来，超冷原子体系成为研究量子多体问题的一个重要平台。由于其高度可操控性，超冷原子提供了一个可以模拟凝聚态物理的量子体系，从而让我们可以更加深入的了解一些现在仍然棘手的强相互作用的体系。最近几年，合成规范势以及自旋轨道耦合在冷原子中得实现，不但扩大了冷原子本身的研究范围，同时也与凝聚态物理中的拓扑性质息息相关。在这里，我们提出研究两个很有意义的问题。第一是关于自旋轨道耦合波色子在光晶格中的行为；第二是自旋轨道耦合费米子在光晶格中的超流性质。在第一个方面，我们的主要目的在于研究体系的相图，尤其是磁性和超流的关系。我们这里主要使用的方法是平均场以及我们提出的一个新的理论 (slave boson)。后者可能有助于我们了解体系是否存在新的拓扑相。在第二部分，我们主要的目的在于通过研究两体问题来了解多体情况下自旋轨道耦合费米子的量子行为。我们希望通过研究，可以找到更好的拓扑相的实验探测方法。

709313.label: Major findings and research outcome
709313.value: [Paper number refers to the list of papers in Part C.] 1. An exact numerical investigation of the Bose-Hubbard model with spin-orbit interaction using density matrix renormalization theory is carried out [paper 1]. What we found here is that the usual superfluid and Mott insulating transition is modified due to the concomitant magnetic ordering and the non-uniformity of the superfluid state. Strong coupling magnetic phases and phase transitions are investigated, using both numerical and exact analytic ways. We show here a hidden topological transition, analogous to the Kitaev model. 2. The quantum phases and phase transitions in the recently realized flux lattice were investigated [paper 2]. Here the synthetic gauge flux renders the single particle spectrum of the similar form as that for a spin-orbit coupled system. We investigated the existence of tricritical point in the phase diagram and calculate the collective excitations of the system. 3. Motivated by the success of the realization of two-dimensional Haldane model (a Chern insulator), we proposed a new scheme to realize three-dimensional Weyl metal [see paper 3]. 4. The application of slave particle approach to the Bose-Hubbard model is considered in a review article that I wrote for Annual Review of Cold Atom and Molecule [paper 4]. It offers only slightly advantage over the inhomogeneous mean field theory in that it gives a way of understand the emergence of various magnetic phases in the superfluid states. 5. In the case of Fermi systems, we have investigated the problem of topological states with the magnetic flux (using shaking) appropriate to the Haldane model [paper 8]. This paper appears in publication much later due to various other activities happening in 2015 and did not manage to use the ECS grant. 6. During the year 2015, due to a lot of interest in the transport properties, I spent much time on the two problems presented in paper 5 and paper 6, which received part support from the ECS grant. 7. A study on Bose system with spin-orbit coupling in 2D homogeneous space is carried out with exact diagonalization [paper 7] using ECS grant where we show that at large values of interaction, there are indications that the system ceases to be a ususal condensate.

709313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
709313.value: There are still some interest in characterising the topological superfluid state of fermions in the optical lattices that we discussed in the last paper of Section C. We are looking into the vortex structure of the topological superfluid state with C=2.

709313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
709313.value: The research focuses on the exotic superfluid state of matter, which has the curious properties of being able to flow without any resistance. It is exotic because of the fact that topologically it is different from the usual superfluid and manifests itself in the zero energy bound state that can be used for quantum computations. Our work in the fermionic case is based on a realistic model that has been realised experimentally in cold atom physics and could lead to further interest. Our calculation in the bosonic case (1D) is the first systematic study of interplay between interaction and spin-orbit coupling in bosons and its resulting new phases.

709413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
709413.value: Why is biodiversity in the tropical western Pacific (TWP) so high, and will it persist? More specifically, why is biodiversity higher in the TWP than in higher latitudes? These are some of the most important but still poorly explored questions in marine (paleo)ecology and (paleo)biogeography. The TWP Ocean is known as a biodiversity hotspot, showing the richest species diversity in the world in many taxonomic groups (e.g., corals, coastal fishes, gastropods), but surprisingly few studies have focused on the temporal dynamics of large-scale biodiversity patterns over geological time-scales in the western Pacific Ocean. Although tropical-high and polar-low latitudinal species diversity gradients (LSDGs) is one of the most pervasive and persistent ecological patterns on the earth and the present day LSDG is very well documented, we know little about how it has been assembled over geological time, with the exception of a few studies (molluscs and shallow-marine and deep-sea foraminifera), none of which include the TWP. Furthermore, the driving force(s) of spatial and temporal variation in species diversity including LSDGs are still hotly debated, and there are several leading hypotheses for the causes to be tested, including speciation/extinction and differences of physiological temperature tolerance among species. This proposal will examine the spatial and temporal patterns of biodiversity in the TWP throughout the Neogene (the last ~24 million years, which includes the Miocene, Pliocene, and Pleistocene) and compare these with patterns of biodiversity in extratropical areas. This study will provide a latitudinal transect of variation in biodiversity which can be used to investigate LSDGs in the northwestern Pacific Ocean at multiple Neogene epochs and, thus provide a better understanding of the causes, origin, and temporal dynamics of LSDGs. The study will focus on the most recent geological period of the Neogene, as this period includes both evolutionary and ecological time-scales and continues into the present day. Fossil ostracods will be used as a model system of organisms as they are ecologically, morphologically, and taxonomically diverse and have an excellent fossil record. Finally PI Yasuhara will test the above-mentioned hypotheses. Analyzing the diversity of fossil records of ostracod will enable a better understanding of the mechanisms driving the LSDG and the formation of the TWP biodiversity hotspot. This information is urgently needed to enable better management of biodiversity in the tropics which is currently threatened by anthropogenic activities. 為何熱帶西太平洋會有如此之高的生物多樣性呢？而這個現象又會持續嗎？更具體而言，為甚麼熱帶西太平洋的生物多樣性會高於較高緯度地區的生物多樣性呢？這些都是一些最重要的海洋（古）生態和（古）生物地理學問題，但一直未被深入探討。在熱帶西太平洋，很多生物分類群（例如：珊瑚、近岸魚類和腹足動物）都擁有全世界最高的生物多樣性，因此被譽為生物多樣性熱點。然而，有關熱帶西太平洋的大規模生物多樣性模式及其長期的時間動態之研究則出奇的少。｢熱帶的生物多樣性較高、極地的生物多樣性較低｣¬――這種緯度物種多樣性梯度（LSDGs）是地球上最廣泛和最持續的生態模式之一，而且時至今日，很多文獻已經記載了這種生態模式。儘管如此，對於緯度物種多樣性梯度和地質時間的關係，我們已知的其實很少。除了小部分的研究（如：軟體動物、淺海及深海有孔蟲）外，其他研究都沒包括熱帶西太平洋。此外，物種多樣性在時間和空間上的變化（包括：緯度物種多樣性梯度）的原因仍然被受爭議，而且現在還有幾個重要的假設未被驗證，包括物種形成∕滅絕和物種之間的生理耐溫性差異。本計劃將研究熱帶西太平洋的生物多樣性在整個新近紀（距今大約二千四百萬年，當中包括中新世、上新世和更新世）的時間和空間變化，並將這些模式跟熱帶以外的地區作對比。在是次研究中，研究員將以一條緯度樣帶來探求生物多樣性的變化，從而研究西北太平洋的緯度物種多樣性梯度在新近紀不同時期的變化，由此便可以對緯度物種多樣性梯度的緣由和在時間上的變化作更深入的了解。這項研究將集中在新近紀中最近代的時期，因為這個延續到今天的時期包括了進化和生態上的時標。由於介形類化石在生態、形態和分類學上都有很多樣化，並且有良好的化石紀錄，所以被用作今次的模型生物系統。最後，是次研究項目的首席研究員安原博士會驗證以上提及的假設。介形類化石的多樣性分析可以讓人更深入理解緯度物種多樣性梯度背後的原理和熱帶西太平洋的生物多樣性熱點的形成過程。人類活動正威脅著熱帶地區的生物多樣性，是次研究的結果將會是改善熱帶生物多樣性管理上迫切需要的資料。

709413.value: 1. to reconstruct spatial and temporal Cenozoic TWP diversity patterns at the species and genus levels for an important metazoan group (ostracod) We successfully reconstructed Cenozoic TWP diversity patterns of fossil ostracods and published the result as Yasuhara et al 2017 Journal of Biogeography and Shin et al 2018 in press Journal of Crustacean Biology. 2. to compare this pattren with existing Cenozoic extratropical data to evaluate spatiotemporal northwestern Pacific fossil diversity patterns ranging from the equator to polar areas We compared our results with existing data from the outside of the tropics in Yasuhara et al 2017 Journal of Biogeography and Shin et al 2018 in press Journal of Crustacean Biology. 3. to test hypotheses on driving force(s) of large-scale diversity patterns including LSDGs by (paleo)ecological modeling using data from (1) and (2) above and through comparison with existing molluscan data We tested representative hypotheses on driving forces of large-scale diversity patterns and found that the plate tectonics is a major driver of the Cenozoic TWP diversity patterns. 709413.label: Major findings and research outcome
709413.value: We found that the Western Pacific Cenozoic biodiversity was dynamic in time and space. In the Western Pacific, all of low, mid, and high latitude regions show increasing diversity over time with initial Miocene diversification and then remarkable Pliocene diversification. This is in contrast with the results from the tropical Western Atlantic Ocean. Contrasting patterns between oceans suggest an important role for regional factors (e.g. plate tectonics and temporal geomorphological dynamics) in shaping the biodiversity of the Western Pacific (Yasuhara et al 2017 J Biogeography). It is important to note that present-day level high biodiversity was established through Pliocene diversity jump probably not only in the West Pacific region, but also others such as the tropical western Atlantic (Shin et al 2018 in press, Journal of Crustacean Biology). We published many other papers to fill the data gap, to develop the theory and hypotheses, and to improve our basic knowledge (eg taxonomy) needed to better understand the biodiversity history in the region, and also had multiple presentations on this topic in international conferences (as seen in Part C).

709413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
709413.value: We prefer to have more spatial coverage (especially in the tropical region) for more comprehensive understanding of the northwestern Pacific biodiversity during the Cenozoic, although our specific objectives are well achieved by this project as mentioned above.

709413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
709413.value: Cenozoic changes of species diversity patterns are not well understood, especially for the Western Pacific including Hong Kong, in part, because of the paucity of good fossil data from the tropical areas. This project aimed to understand the changes of species diversity in time and space in the broad Western Pacific region through the Cenozoic (past 65 million years), focusing on the Coral Triangle biodiversity hotspot (known for the highest marine biodiversity in the world). We reconstructed Low-, mid- and high-latitude regions all show a similar diversity trend: diversity was low in the Eocene (56–34 million years ago, Ma hereafter) and Oligocene (34–23 Ma), increases from the Miocene (23–5 Ma) to the Plio-Pleistocene (sometime during 5–0.01 Ma) but then declines to the present day. Present-day high biodiversity was established during the Pliocene with a remarkable diversity increase at that time. Diversity patterns with latitude are relatively flat and never show a simple decline from the tropical region to higher latitudes, the commonly known pattern. Our results in comparison with the known results from other regions suggested an important role for regional factors (e.g. plate tectonics and temporal geomorphological changes) to shape the biodiversity patterns of the Western Pacific region.

709713.label: Realisation of objectives
709713.value: The primary goal of this project is to understand the diversity of magnetic field geometry in pulsar wind nebulae (PWNe). We presented detailed studies of three representative PWN systems at different evolutionary stages. The new results revealed a remarkably diverse magnetic field geometry among these objects. For the young source MSH 15-52, we found toroidal B-field about the jet direction, as expected from theories. On the other hand, we found that there is a lack of radio emission at the X-ray jet, which could indicate a different particle acceleration mechanism. For G327.1-1.1, we obtained the first detailed polarization measurement of a crushed PWN. and discovered a highly ordered magnetic field structure, which is a big surprise given the turbulent environment. Based on this measurement, we employed simulations to constrain the characteristic scale of the turbulence. For bow-shock PWNe, , we identified similar helical B-field geometry in two different systems, J1015 and J11014, which are moving at very different space velocities. The results clearly reject the idea that a helical field can only be produced in slowly moving pulsars. We demonstrated that velocity is not a critical factor determining the field geometry and proposed that other parameters, such as the alignment angle between pulsar spin and velocity, could play a more important role. In addition to magnetic field from radio polarization measurements, our studies also revealed many small-scale structure in PWNe, such as magnetic loops, filaments, and bubbles. The radio spectra we obtained also provide indispensable part of the multi-wavelength spectra.

We found toroidal field in the young system, a highly ordered magnetic field structure crushed PWN, and helical B-field in two bow shock systems. We proposed that the field geometry depends more on the pulsar spin alignment rather than the space velocity.

Our radio maps show that magnetic loops and filaments and common in radio PWNe. These could be magnetic loops torn by the termination shock. We also identified a synchrotron bubble in a bow shock, which could be caused by flow instability.

We mapped the detailed radio morphology of the above-mentioned systems and performed a detailed comparison with the X-ray structure. We obtained multi-wavelength spectrum of G327.1-1.1 from radio to X-rays to gamma-rays. The new radio spectrum of MSH 15-52 also helps to refine the multi-wavelength picture.

I have proposed (as PI) a couple of new radio observations of bow-shock PWNe using world-class telescopes. The proposals were accepted after competitive review processes and the observations have been carried out. These include observations of J1549-4848 using the Australia Telescope Compact Array (ATCA) and B0355, J1740, and J0357 using the Very Large Array (VLA). Unfortunately the new observations showed no radio detection of these systems.

709713.label: Major findings and research outcome
709713.value: 1. We discovered a bubble-like structure in the PWN J1015, and the result has been published in The Astrophysical Journal (Ng et al. 2017). 2. My student and I discovered a highly ordered magnetic field structure in the crushed PWN system G327.1-1.1. The result has been published in The Astrophysical Journal (Ma et al. 2015) and the student's thesis. 3. My student and I performed high resolution radio observations of the young PWN MSH 15-52. We found a toroidal magnetic field and rich small-scale features. The results have been presented in various conferences and published in the student's thesis. He has recently passed the oral defense and we are now turning the thesis into a journal paper for submission. 4. My student and I found a helical magnetic field structure in the fast-moving bow shock PWN J11014-6103. This is the first time such a geometry is found in fast moving systems. The results have been published in the student's thesis. She has recently passed the oral defense and we are now turning the thesis into a journal paper for submission.

709713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
709713.value: Our study shows a diverse magnetic field structure and rich small-scale radio features in PWNe. A comprehensive follow-up study to map the details of all bright PWN systems will be very useful. Our results also set a stage for further theoretical modeling to investigate the magnetic field geometry and evolution in PWNe.

709713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
709713.value: Magnetic field is an important ingredient in particle acceleration process in pulsar wind nebulae. This study identifies the magnetic field geometry in these systems through radio polarization observations. We found a diverse geometry and proposed the connection with the underlying physical parameters.

709813.label: Project Objectives
709813.value: Aim 1: To develop chemical reporters for detecting and identifying malonylated and succinylated proteins and their modification sites. The identification of posttranslationally modified proteins and their PTM sites is key to unravel PTM-mediated cellular processes. In preliminary studies, we have developed a chemical reporter (MalAM-yne) for robust in-gel fluorescent visualization of protein malonylation dynamics and rapid profiling of malonylated proteins in human cells. Using this chemical reporter, while 14 out of all the 17 currently known malonylated proteins were found, we also identified another 361 proteins as new candidates of malonylation substrates. We will use a similar strategy to develop chemical reporters to examine protein succinylation. In addition to identifying malonylated and succinylated proteins, we will also develop a chemical reporter-based strategy to analyze specific malonylated and succinylated lysine sites. Aim 2: To examine how malonylation and succinylation affect biological functions of proteins. Functional studies of malonylation and succinylation have been lacking. To fill this knowledge gap, we will combine chemical and biochemical approaches to study biological effects of malonylation and succinylation on their protein substrates. Of the malonylated and succinylated proteins identified by us and others, we prioritize the in-depth analysis of malate dehydrogenase (MDH2) a metabolic enzyme involved in regulating the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle. We will analyze how malonylation or succinylation may influence the enzymatic activity of MDH2. Aim 3: To identify proteins that recognize lysine malonylation and succinylation ‘marks’. PTMs can often serve as a signaling platform that could be recognized by specific binding proteins, which would then, in turn, execute downstream cellular programs. Therefore, comprehensive understanding of the functional consequences of malonylation and succinylation requires identification of proteins that recognize malonyl- and succinyl-lysine ‘marks’. To this end, we will use a photo-cross-linking based chemical proteomics approach to identify interaction partners of lysine malonylation and succinylation. We will first focus on a recently discovered succinylation site on histone H3 lysine 14 (H3K14-Succ). The biochemical and structural approaches will be used to validate and characterize the identified proteins, as it is also of interest to elucidate the structural features of these binding proteins that enable the recognition of these distinct chemical modifications.

709813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
709813.value: 蛋白质翻译后修饰（PTM），例如乙酰化、甲基化及磷酸化，参与众多细胞过程的调控，包括DNA复制及基因表达、细胞周期控制、信号传导及新陈代谢等。考虑到PTM在正常细胞生理过程中发挥的重要作用，其调节异常将导致疾病的发生。因此，理解不同的PTM并解析它们的生物学意义就显得十分重要。尽管目前已有300多种PTM被报道，但对于它们所参与调控的复杂的细胞机制及功能的深入研究却非常有限。尤其对那些新发现的PTM更是知之甚少。所以我们有必要进行系统深入的研究以阐明这些PTM的生物学意义。 此项研究将重点关注两个新发现的PTM，即赖氨酸丙二酰化和琥珀酰化。此两种PTM分别将丙二酰基和琥珀酰基以共价键的方式连于赖氨酸侧链的氨基上。鉴于丙二酰基和琥珀酰基含有羧酸片段的化学本质，丙二酰化和琥珀酰化能将正常情况下带正电荷的赖氨酸转化为带负电荷。由此预测，丙二酰化和琥珀酰化将在很大程度上改变蛋白质的结构及其功能。但是，针对这两个PTM的研究还很匮乏，对其在不同细胞过程中起到的作用亦不明确。为了解析这两个PTM的生物学重要性，我们将致力于开发能够检测赖氨酸丙二酰化和琥珀酰化的化学方法。研究目的有三：首先，我们将设计并合成化学探针，用以检测和确认蛋白质丙二酰化和琥珀酰化的蛋白质底物及修饰位点；其次，我们将结合化学和生物化学方法来研究丙二酰化和琥珀酰化对其蛋白质底物产生的生物学影响；最后，我们将利用一个基于光交联技术的化学蛋白组学方法来寻找能特异性识别丙二酰化和琥珀酰化的蛋白质。之后，我们将进一步运用生物化学和结构生物学方法来表征所发现的由PTM介导的蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用。这一研究的结果将对解析赖氨酸丙二酰化和琥珀酰化复杂的调控网络提供有效信息。从长远来看，此研究的发现，也可能为寻找因这两个PTM调控异常所引发疾病的治疗靶点打下基础。

709813.label: Realisation of objectives
709813.value: Objective 1: To develop chemical reporters for detecting and identifying malonylated and succinylated proteins and their modification sites. In our study, we developed a chemical reporter, MalAM-yne, for protein malonylation. Using similar strategy, we have designed and synthesized the chemical reporters for protein succinylation (SuccAM-yne). In addition, we also developed chemical reporters for protein glutarylation (GluAM-yne) and HMGylation (HMGAM-yne), two newly identified protein modifications with similar negatively charged carboxylates as malonylation and succinylation. Using the three reporters (i.e., Succ/Glu/HMGAM-yne), we examined the dynamics of protein succinylation, glutarylation and HMGylation. The following proteomics studies led to the identification of histones and other proteins as novel substrates of glutarylation and HMGylation. The glutarylation and HMGylation sites on histones have been mapped. The above results facilitated further investigation for the regulatory mechanisms and biological functions of succinylation, glutarylation and HMGylation (see Objective 2 below). Objective 2: To examine how malonylation and succinylation affect biological functions of proteins. The lysine acyl modifications with negatively charged carboxylates change the net charge of the modification site from +1 to -1, and are therefore likely to directly affect the structure of the substrates or the interactions between the substrates and other macromolecules to exert their biological functions. To investigate if and how these modifications impact the structure and interactions of the substrates, we used different protein chemistry strategies, including chemical ligation and surrogate mimicking, to generate specifically and stoichiometrically modified proteins, which are MDH2 protein with succnylation marks on K301, K307, K314, and K324 residues, and histone H2BK34succ, H4K77succ, H4K31succ, H4K91glu, H2BK120glu, and H3K122glu. Objective 3: To identify proteins that recognize lysine malonylation and succinylation ‘marks’. We have designed and synthesized photo-affinity probes for the identification of proteins that potentially recognize succinylation marks on histone H4K12, H2BK120, H3K9, and H3K27. In combination with SILAC, a quantitative proteomics technology, we carried out the comprehensive profiling of the binding partners of these four histone succinylation marks in whole cell proteomes. Proteins enriched from the experiments were analyzed by high-resolution mass spectrometry.

709813.label: Major findings and research outcome
709813.value: The negatively charged lysine acyl modifications are newly identified posttranslational modifications (PTMs), including malonylation (verified) and succinylation (Ksucc), which are focused at the beginning of our study in this project, as well as glugtarylation (Kglu) and HMGylation (Khmg), which were identified by others during our study. The regulatory mechanisms and biological significances of these negatively charged PTMs remain less understood. In this project, to fill such knowledge gaps, we developed chemical reporters for the detection and identification of the substrates of the four negatively charged PTMs. Pulldown experiments after metabolic labeling of MalAM-yne during cell culture resulted in the enrichment of 14 out of 17 then known substrates of malonylation. Moreover, more than 300 substrate candidates were identified. Five of the newly identified protein substrates were verified, including PSMD2, EF2, HSPA1, PRDX1 and CDC37 (Bao et al. Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2013, 52, 4883–4886). Using similar methods, we identified histones as novel substrates of glutarylation and HMGylation. LC-MS/MS analysis of the extracted histones resulted in the identification of 27 Kglu sites (Bao et al. manuscript under review) and 6 Khmg sites (Bao et al. Chem. Sci., 2018, DOI: 10.1039/c8sc02483a). As the negatively charged modifications change the net charge of lysine from +1 to -1, it is highly likely that the substrates structurer or the interactions with other molecules are affected by the modifications. To test this hypothesis, one challenge is to prepare the homogeneously modified proteins with the PTM of interest installed at stoichiometric level. In our study, we used different protein chemistry strategies, including chemical ligation and surrogate mimicking, to generate modified proteins, which are MDH2 protein with succnylation marks on K301, K307, K314, and K324 residues, and histone H2BK34succ, H4K77succ, H4K31succ, H4K91glu, H2BK120glu, and H3K122glu. The modified histones were further reconstituted into nucleosomes and estimated their effect on nucleosome dynamics by multiple biochemical and biophysical methods. Specifically, we discovered that H2BK34succ (Jing et al. Cell Chem. Biol., 2018, 25, 1-9) and H4K77succ (Jing et al. manuscript in preparation) may weaken the histone H2B-DNA interaction, H4K91glu may disrupt the H4-H2B contacts (Bao et al. manuscript under review). We also carried out chemical proteomics studies to profile proteins that recognize histone H4K12succ, H2BK120succ, H3K9succ, and H3K27succ marks. Sirt5, a know desuccinylase was enriched from the whole cell proteomes, demonstrating the experiments were successful. However, the results revealed no other candidates that bind to these Ksucc marks.

709813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
709813.value: In our studies, we identified and verified PSMD2, EF2, HSPA1, PRDX1 and CDC37 as novel substrates of protein malonylation, AF9, and KAT2A as novel substrates of HMGylation. However, their modification sites have not been mapped. The regulatory mechanisms and biological functions of the modifications on these proteins are not clear. In our current study, we have obtained the H4K31succ, H2BK120glu, and H3K122glu proteins that have not been investigated for their effects on nucleosome and chromatin dynamics. In our current study, we comprehensively profiled the proteins that recognize histone H4K12succ, H2BK120succ, H3K9succ, and H3K27succ marks, but no candidate was identified. Changes of photoaffinity probes, change of modification sites can be the further directions to pursue. The above questions will be explored in our further studies. In fact, we have already applied for fundings (as PI and Co-I) to support our continuous studies, including Regulation and Function of Novel Histone Modifications (CRF C7029-15G), Chemical Biology Approach to Molecular Medicine (AoE/P-705/16), The Regulation of Chromatin Structure and Dynamics by Histone Glutarylation (GRF 17125917), and Examining the Influences of Histone Succinylation on Nucleosome/Chromatin Structure and Dynamics and Identification of Readers of Histon Succinylation (NSFC 91753130).

709813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
709813.value: Protein posttranslational modifications (PTMs) are small chemical tags added to the protein substrates which may influence the subtrates' structure and function. In this project, we have been focusing on newly identified negatively charged PTMs, malonylation, succinylation, glutarylation, and HMGylation, whose regulatory mechanisms and biological functions remain poorly understood. We use multidisciplinary approaches to identify the substrates of the PTMs, map the modification sites, characterize the impacts of the PTMs on the interactions between the substrates and other macromolecules, and profile the proteins that recognize the PTMs to carry out downstream biological events. Our results provide useful information about these less-explored PTMs and advance our knowledge on them. Moreover, the information may help the development of potential therapeutic strategies for the treatment of human diseases associated with malfunctions of these PTMs.

710313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
710313.value: 有機電子器件的迅速發展提出了新的應用，例如可穿戴式電子設備或人工電子皮膚。在這些器件中，有機存儲晶體管中起著非常重要的作用。今天，多數有機存儲晶體管的研究，如電荷保留時間或載流子遷移主要是基於單個設備。雖然這些研究可以提供有用的信息，但無法捕捉到他們在實際應用中的存儲互連之表現。更重要的是，以陣列形式的存儲設備中，由於較高的存儲密度，因此導致較高的工作溫度，該存儲器丟失效。如今，大多數的柔性裝置的開發基於聚合物基板，如PEN和PET 。雖然這些聚合物基板具有高機械彈性和表面光滑，他們有一個非常長的降解時間，在大批量生產下，會造成嚴重的環境問題。為這基材的問題提供一種可行的解決方案，我們將製作大面積的存儲器陣列的可生物降解的纖維素纖維紙。 在當前項目中，我們嘗試結合一些最新的特性和製造技術，研究大面積有機非揮發性記憶體陣列紙基板的熱效應。該存儲器陣列將通過絲網印刷方法來製造。我們專注於大面積陣列有三個主要的原因，（i）在較高的密度在，我們要調查的產生和機制有機存儲器晶體管陣列，了解荷電保持降解過程中，（ii）我們要改善，荷電保持性能的兩個新的結構設計及（iii）驗證的規模增長能力的印刷方法。當前項目的成功，將是擴大有機存儲器晶體管的實際應用邁出了重要一步。廢熱研究可以提供存儲晶體管退化的新理解，並提高高磁錄密度存儲器陣列的可靠性。該存儲器陣列可以增強的各種的便攜式傳感器或RFID的功能，提供的信息存儲能力。此外，可生物降解的紙基板能帶來靈活的電子與聚合物基板相比，更加符合環保要求。

710313.label: Realisation of objectives
710313.value: Objective 1 Objective achieved. We have performed real-time thermal image of the organic memory array by multi-probe micro-thermocouples with diameters with 30um. The temperature distribution during on states of the memory devices agree with the current distribution. Depending on the IDS value in the devices which is governed by the size of the source-drain electrodes, temperature increase from 0.1K to 1.3K is observed in the organic memory. The charge retention time of the DNTT organic memory transistor on the paper substrate is up to 10000s. As the charge retention time is measured based on maintaining the organic memory transistor at the on-state continuously, the charge retention time of 10000s is actually combining the thermal effects with the bias stress degradation under a constant electric field. It is important to note that similar to the thermal assisted charge de-trapping from the trap states, a continuous bias under an electric field will also cause the detrapping of the trapped charges from the charge trapping states. Objective 2 Objective achieved. In characterizing the thermal stability of the devices, we isolated the bias stress effect by storing programmed memory transistor under elevated temperature without electrical bias. These measurements allow us to investigate the thermal assisted de-trapping process in the organic memory transistors without the detrapping effects induced by the electric fields. In the floating nanoparticle devices, we noticed that by storing the device under 50oC environment for 1 hour, the on state charge retention time decreases to 6400 s. By further increasing the storage temperature to 80 oC, the retention time further decrease down to 1800 s. In the floating gate structure device, the thermal stability is in general stronger than the floating nanoparticle one where the trap states induced metal nanoparticles are inserted into the active layer rather than the gate dielectric. The charge retention time only decreases from around 17000 s to around 12000 s and 9300 s when the storage temperature increases from 50 oC to 80 oC. We attributed this improvement due to thermal annealing effect of the BST dielectric during the fabrication process of this high-k dielectric. It can significantly stabilize the defects or release the shallow traps in the floating gate dielectric. Objective 3 Objective achieved. We have successfully fabricated the organic memory device on both paper and plastic substrates. For the paper substrate, we use standard FUJI XEROX printer paper (15BC040080). For the flexible substrate, we used 12 m polyethylene naphthalate (PEN). For the organic semiconductor, we used both solution processed barium-strontium titanate (BST), anodizied aluminum oxide (AlOx) and vapor phase deposited parylene. In both BST and AlOx organic transistor devices, we can achieve an operating voltage at gate bias below 2.5 V. In the carrier mobility study, we have applied various kind of organic semiconductors as the active channel of the organic memory transistor including pentacene, DNTT, C10-DNTT, BBTNDT and DPH-BBTNDT. For the pentacene, we generally obtain a mobility around 0.5 cm2/V-s. For the DNTT, the mobility we obtained in all three kinds of dielectric are ranging between 0.8 cm2/V-s to 1.3 cm2/V-s. For the C10-DNTT, all the mobilites are higher than 1 cm2/V-s while the highest one can be up to 5.6 cm2/V-s. For the BBTNDT, the averaged mobility is 7.7 cm2/V-s while the highest is 8.9 cm2/V-s. For the DPH-BBTNDT, the averaged mobility is 4.16 cm2/V-s. Objective 4 In this part, after we tested the memory window effect by adjusting the metal nanoparticles in the organic semiconductor active layer and BST thickness. We noticed that there is certain minimum thickness requirement of the BST around 40 nm to avoid the unwated leakage current in the devices. To address this issue and further optimize the memory window, we switched to use adjusted the memory window of the organic semiconductors by using a polymer electret polystyrene (PS). The optimized memory window of the DNTT memory transistor is larger than 100 V. The device shows multiple level of data storage with a n expected charge retention time around 50000 s. In the memory window optimization process, the electrical bias memory device is further modified into combined optical and electrical biased to enlarge the storage capacity of the memory transistor.

710313.label: Major findings and research outcome
710313.value: The major research findings of the project are: 1. We confirmed the thermal induced memory loss in the organic memory transistor and deviate it from the bias stressed effect. Based on the thermal characteriziation tests, we have better understanding on the thermal induced degradation in different layers of the organic transistor memory, including electrodes, active semiconductor layer, dielectric and etc. 2. We develop a memory transistor with a large memory window up to 120V for multilevel storage. 3. We fabricate a series of organic transistor and memory transistor based on different semiconductors and structures. We tried to explain the structure and fabrication method to transparent devices and solution processing organic semiconductors. 4. In the array structure, we have successfully demonstrated two different organic transistor array. One is the transistor memory array on cellulose paper substrate to drive the LED circuit. Another one is on flexible PEN substrate and use the memory trap states to sense the temperature of the object in the transistor array. 5. Based on this project, we also start to investigate the thermal properties of different organic semiconductors both experimentally and numerically. 710313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
710313.value: This project allows us to have more in-depth understanding on not only the thermal effect of memory transistors, but also provide an opportunity to my research team to overcome all these challenges and hurdles. We have enriched our device fabrication skills on both paper substrates and polymer flexible substrates. The fabrication recipe will be an important cornerstone for us and the research community to further develop or scale up the transistor array for practical applications. The new organic transistor structures and fabrication methods developed in this project can also further expand into new research directions later on. Among these, the solution processing and thermal properties characterizations work done by our team provide great contributions to the research community.

710313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
710313.value: In the rapid development of organic electronics, it is expected that complicated circuit chips based on all organic semiconductors would be demonstrated in the near future. Comparing with other components such as organic solar cells or light emitting diodes, the memory transistor development is left behind although it is an essential and critical element in the practical application. Comparing with the inorganic memory, the organic memory transistor usually has a shorter retention time. However, retention time in the orders of days is sufficient for the memory buffer applications which is exactly what we need for the portable device on flexible or paper substrate. In this project, we try to provide a more in-depth understanding of the thermally induced degradation of organic memory and how can we address them by better device structure or fabrication method. This project provided valuable and timely findings to the research community as well as the further development of organic memory transistors.

710913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
710913.value: Modern integrated circuits (ICs) are without doubt complex physical systems involving a wide spectrum of interrelated physical effects, and accurate physics-based modeling is of fundamental importance in driving the advancement of semiconductor technology. Modeling and simulation (M&S) of these physical effects for IC components such as transistors and interconnects, however, have long been carried out in a stand-alone fashion. On one hand, specific physical phenomenon is more often analyzed within an isolated context from other co-existent and relevant phenomena due to the theoretical and practical difficulties of combining distinct physical models. On the other hand, the limited capabilities in coupling physical models, though has been provided, are still attached to a conventional division of front-end-of-line (FEOL, e.g., transistors) and back-end-of-line (BEOL, e.g., metallic interconnection). Characterization of physical interactions among FEOL and BEOL remains a less-explored yet increasingly important topic due to the ever-rising integration density and heterogeneity. Recognizing the lack of capabilities in modeling multiple physics at the same time, this project aims at three objectives: 1) to set up a multi-physics framework, which combines the four major types of physical models pertinent to modern IC design: electromagnetics (EM), semiconductor physics, thermodynamics and structural mechanics, for accurate multi-domain modeling and simulation. Different from the traditional ``black box'' scheme (different physical equation systems are solved individually and coupled via boundary data exchange), the framework features a tightly-coupled paradigm wherein all physical models are handled in a unified manner, with regard to discretization, solver scheme and data storage, and solved simultaneously; 2) to develop efficient numerical solution techniques to cope with the dramatically increased computational cost required by multi-physics modeling, in particular the quadratic growth of problem size with the number of models included in the tightly-coupled strategy; 3) to verify the efficacy of the framework via industrial examples and apply it to investigate complicated problems in microelectronics. The outcomes of this project will enable unprecedented physical modeling opportunities in electronic design automation (EDA) for modern chips to address the challenges stemming from the continuous growth in integration density and functional diversification. More accurate compact models with comprehensive account of relevant physical effects can subsequently be generated for system-level simulation and costly experiments can be minimized, leading to faster design closure and improved manufacturing yield. The knowledge and insights of the proposed framework will also interest researchers and practitioners in other scientific areas given the extensive use of physical M&S tools. 大規模集成電路無疑是當今最複雜的物理系統之一，其中包括大量相互關聯的物理效應，因此準確的物理建模對於推動半導體技術發展具有至關重要的作用。然而，長久以來，對於IC部件中物理效應的模擬与仿真(M&S)都是以一種分立的方式來進行的。一方面，由於各種理論上和實踐中的困難，對特定物理效應的分析通常在一個孤立的環境中進行，而不考慮同時存在并与之相互關聯的其他物理效應。另一方面，儘管有限程度的多物理耦合建模已經存在，他們仍舊依賴於傳統的前端工序（FEOL，例如三極管）和後端工序（BEOL，例如金屬互聯線）的劃分。對前，后段工序之間的物理相互作用的刻畫和分析，儘管對於現今不斷提高的集成密度和分化度來說越來越重要，還處於一個相對落後的階段。 針對當前數值分析中難以同時模擬多種物理作用的不足，本項目主要提出以下三個目標：1）建立一個多物理建模框架，能同時描述當今IC設計中涉及的主要四種物理效應，包括電磁效應，半導體效應，熱力學效應和結構應力效應。与傳統的“黑盒”算法（即分別對不同物理效應單獨求解，然後通過邊界條件實現耦合）不同，新框架採用了緊密耦合的方式，即對所有物理模型都採取統一的方式處理，包括相同的離散化方式，求解方法和數據儲存結構，并同時求解所有模型；2）設計高效率的數值求解算法，用於解決紧密耦合多物理建模所帶來的急速提高的運算量，尤其是跟随模型数量平方增加的数值系统大小；3）通过工业实例来验证新仿真框架的准确性，并用之来分析微電子領域中的複雜問題。 本項目的成果可以爲電子設計自動化(EDA)帶來前所未有的仿真準確性，解決不斷提升的集成密度和功能分化給IC設計帶來的困難和挑戰。多物理模擬可以用於爲係統級仿真建立具有物理準確度的集約模型，從而減少對昂貴的實驗的需求，帶來更快的設計閉合和更好的工業產出。同時，由於模擬仿真工具在其他科研領域的廣泛應用，新仿真框架也會給其他研究者和使用者帶來啓發。

710913.label: Realisation of objectives
710913.value: Objective 1: To setup a tightly-coupled multi-physics M&S framework, combining EM, advanced semiconductor (HD or EB), thermal and mechanical models, to enable true multi-physics analysis for complex IC components, in particular for FE-BE mixed structures This objective has been MOSTLY ACHIEVED. We have developed a tightly-coupled multi-physics modeling and simulation (M&S) framework combining EM, hydrodynamic (HD) semiconductor and thermal models. This framework simulates simultaneously front-end (FE) devices and back-end (BE) interconnects with full consideration of the physical interactions among the above-mentioned physical mechanisms. Specifically, the physical coupling is realized via carefully-designed temperature-dependent material parameter models (such as conductivity, semiconductor parameters, and thermal parameters), and clever treatment of FE-BE interface. The convergence of the tightly-coupled model has been demonstrated to be significantly better than that of the loosely-coupled counterpart when the physical interaction is strong. The mechanical model has not been fully incorporated into the tightly-coupled framework, because our research reveals that the feedback from mechanical deformation to the other three physical models is relatively weak in the microelectronics context, thus it is more cost-effective to integrate the mechanical effects in a loosely-coupled manner. An external tool for mechanical modeling is now linked to the proposed framework to enable mechnical analysis based on the calculated current and temperature profile. Objective 2: To develop efficient numerical solution techniques for the PDE systems arising from the above multi-physics framework to enable practical time- and frequency-domain M&S capabilities This objective has been FULLY ACHIEVED. The numerical solution of the resulting PDE has been substantially accelerated by two innovative techniques. First, the block matrix structure in the Jacobian of the tightly-coupled system is exploited to eliminate part of the unknowns, which reduces the number of fill-ins in the preconditioner needed in iterative solution. Second, a new nonlinear exponential-integrator-Newton-Krylov (EI-NK) approach is proposed to overcome the limitation of traditional methods in terms of time step size and capability of handling strong nonlinearity. All these achievements enable sufficient computational efficiency for using the tightly-coupled multi-physics framework to investigate practical problems required for Objective 3. The numerical algorithms stemmed from this project have also been employed in the quantum mechnical simulation of semiconductor device leading to considerable speedup. Objective 3: To verify the proposed framework via industrial examples and apply it in cutting-edge problems in microelectronics. This objective has been FULLY ACHIEVED. Specifically, the framework has been applied to investigate the self-induced magnetic field effects including Lorentz force in industrial ESD protection structure. It is also employed to study the electro-thermal coupling problem in power electronics. Long-term impact: In short, through combining systematically important physical models and corresponding numerical support, the proposed multi-physics framework provides a physically holistic and practically competent solution to model the interactions between FE and BE structures. To the PI and Co-Is' best knowledge, no such framework exists before. The long-term impact of this project is guaranteed by the growing importance, alongside with difficulties, in integrating different EDA research efforts of physical modeling. This has also been highlighted in the latest International Technology Roadmap of Semiconductors (ITRS): ``If one examines the cycle time for development of a new technology, much of that time and cost is not in the individual module development, but at the integration level'' [6]. To this end, the rich experience of the PI in multi-physics modeling and numerical methods can be fully leveraged and promising results are already coming out in the EM-TCAD endeavor. The project can also equip students and research assistants with the necessary knowledge to contribute to the EDA/semiconductor industry or academia. Educational content of this project can be readily integrated into university graduate courses and trainings.
