710913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
710913.value: When carrying out this project, the PI and Co-Is have found the huge benefits of multi-physics modeling and simulation in solving real-world problems that are difficult to be addressed in single-physics paradigm. 710913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
710913.value: Modern microelectronic components are naturally complicated systems involving multiple physical mechanisms interacting with each other. Traditional way of simulating such systems is to model one physical mechanism at a time, couple several of them via boundary data exchange at the software level, and iterate until convergence is achieved, i.e., the loosely-coupled (LC) scheme. When interactions of these component physics are strong, the LC scheme tends to require many iterations to converge and thus becomes inefficient. This project has successfully developed a tightly-coupled (TC) modeling scheme solving multiple physical models in one shot. By combining all physical models in one system, the information exchange among different solvers can be avoided and thus the convergence speed can be largely improved. A series of advanced numerical techniques have also been proposed to enable fast numerical solution of the TC system. Huge benefits have been demonstrated in the applications of the TC framework to study cutting-edge microelectronic problems. The PI and Co-Is also see great potential to employ the tightly-coupled multi-physics idea in other research areas involving strong physical interactions.

711213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
711213.value: It is well-known that networked control systems are of fundamental importance in engineering. A key index in networked control systems is represented by the topological entropy, which is directly related to stabilizability and performance limitations. Indeed, the topological entropy provides the minimum data rate of the channel required for designing a stabilizing controller, and defines the lowest quantization density for infinite logarithmic quantizers. For networked control systems with linear dynamics, the topological entropy is a known function of the unstable eigenvalues of the state transition matrix, in particular depending on their product in discrete-time systems or on their sum in continuous-time systems. For networked control systems with nonlinear dynamics, the topological entropy can be similarly defined based on the linearization of the dynamics in a region of interest of the state space. Unfortunately, networked control systems are unavoidably affected by uncertainties. This means that the coefficients of the model are not exactly known, in particular depend on unknown parameters that consequently affect the topological entropy of the networked control system. Two fundamental problems arise in such a context. The first problem is the determination of the critical value of the topological entropy, i.e. the maximum value of the topological entropy over the set of admissible uncertainties, which is required for establishing stabilizability and performance against the presence of uncertainties. The second problem is the design of feedback controllers for minimizing such a critical value, since this minimization can allow one to achieve stabilizability and increase performance. It turns out that these are difficult problems. Indeed, the critical value cannot be found through standard tools by attempting to maximize the topological entropy due to the presence of local maxima, and cannot be found with gridding techniques due to the prohibitive growth of the number of required samples with the number of unknown parameters. Moreover, the situation is even worse in the synthesis framework since the topological entropy also depends on the unknown feedback controller. The aim of this project is to introduce a new methodology that allows one to systematically solve these problems. Specifically, the target is to provide the sought critical value or an upper bound of it for the first problem, and a controller that minimizes the critical value or an upper bound of it for the second problem. It is expected that this will greatly help the analysis and synthesis of networked control systems. 很多人已經知道網絡控制系統在工程學上具有根本的重要性。網絡控制系統中的鍵索引以拓撲熵來表示。這跟可穩定性和性能限制有直接關係。其實拓撲熵在設計穩定控制器時提供了管道所需的最低資料速率，並在無限大的對數量化器中設定了最低的量化密度。 就在線性動力學的網絡控制系統而言，拓撲熵是一個在狀態轉移矩陣中擁有不穩定特徵值的已知函數，特別取決於特徵值在離散時間系統的乘積或在連續時間系統的總和。而在非線性動力學的網絡控制系統上，拓撲熵可以類似地定義為在線性化動力學裡利益區域的狀態空間。 可惜的是，網絡控制系統無可避免會受到一些不確定因素影響。即是系統模型裡的係數未必是已知數，這些係數尤其依賴未知參數，所以最終會影響到網絡控制系統的拓撲熵。 這情況會衍生兩個根本問題。第一個問題在於拓撲熵臨界值的決定，即在一系到容許的不確定性之內，拓撲熵的最大值。這需要面對不確定情況出現時所產生的可穩定性及表現。由於將臨界值最小化可以讓人去達到可穩定性和增加表現，所以將臨界值最小化時所用的反饋控制器的設計會構成第二個問題。 結果發現這些都是難題。事實上，臨界值不能在因出現局部最大值而嘗試將拓撲熵最大化的標準工具中找到，也因為所需樣本的數及未知參數禁止增長，所以在化網格技術之中都不能找到拓撲熵。再者，由於拓撲熵同樣依賴未知的回饋控制器，所以在合成框架上情況更差。 這個研究項目主要是介紹一套新方法，讓人可以有系統地解決以上種種問題。具體目標旨在找到一個臨界值或一個上限去解決第一個問題，以及在第二個問題上，運用控制器將臨界值或上限最小化。預計這個研究會大大幫助網路控制系統的分析和合成。

711213.label: Realisation of objectives
711213.value: The objectives have been realized, in particular, we have developed techniques for 1) determining the critical value of the topological entropy, 2) designing controllers that minimize this value, 3) investigating the topological entropy in nonlinear systems.

Develop a new methodology for designing a controller that minimizes the critical value of the topological entropy in uncertain networked control systems with linear dynamics.
Develop a new methodology for addressing the previous analysis and synthesis problems in uncertain networked control systems with nonlinear dynamics.

711213.label: Major findings and research outcome
711213.value: We have shown how one can formulate the determination of the critical value of the topological entropy through a convex optimization problem by exploiting eigenvalue techniques or parameter-dependent Lyapunov functions. Moreover, we have shown how one can search for a controller that minimizes this value through a convex optimization problem by introducing a novel methodology for exploiting classic stability criteria. Lastly, we have shown how this machinery can be extended to deal with nonlinear systems where the equilibrium points are unknown.

711213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
711213.value: It is expected that the found results may open the door to research in several direction. Indeed, when dealing with complex systems, not only the equilibrium point should be considered for determining the critical value of the topological entropy but also the space covered by the trajectories of the system. Also, complex systems may present time-varying dynamics or multiple-dimension dynamics. The determination of the critical value of the topological entropy is an open problem in these cases, and the results found in this project may help to proceed in this research.

711213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
711213.value: The project has developed novel methods to determine and to control the critical value of the topological entropy in uncertain systems, which is important for achieving stability. The proposed methods require the solution of convex optimization problems that can be easily solved with existing software.

711413.label: Project Objectives
711413.value: To study the problem of maximizing seller’s revenue for situations where the seller cannot control the price but can decide the amount sold in a sequence of transactions (motivated by, for example, stock market trading and the sale of electricity in a grid). To study the problem of maximizing seller’s revenue for other situations where the seller can set the price, and the amount sold to batches of buyers with different valuations, but can only make a limited number of sales (motivated by, for example, the Hong Kong first-hand property market, the Chinese New Year flower market and the sale of airline tickets).

711413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
711413.value: This project involves the study of problems for which the objective is to maximize the revenue of a seller. More specifically, the problems we propose to study are motivated by various interesting real-life situations, namely: (1) situations where the seller cannot control the price but can decide the amount sold at each sale – e.g. in the stock market trading and the sale of electricity to a grid settings, where the seller is concerned about how many units he should be selling at the prevailing market-determined price at various times to maximize sale proceeds, and (2) situations where the seller can set the price but can only make a limited number of sales – e.g. in the Hong Kong first-hand property market, the Chinese New Year flower market and the sale of airline tickets settings, where all units have to be sold by a preset deadline. The aim is to devise computationally efficient strategies for the seller to maximize revenue under different assumptions about the buyers’ behaviour and, at the same time, to gain a better understanding about the market mechanism and different trading strategies. 本課題的研究是針對價格在線波動的市場環境中，設計在線分配算法來最大化賣方的收益。該課題來源於一些重要的實際應用模型：（1）賣方不能設定出售物品的價格，但可以決定出售物品的數量。比如在股票市場或在電力網絡中，股票價格或電力價格由當前市場決定而不是由賣方決定，但賣方可以通過設定所售股票或者電力的數量來最大化其收益。（2）賣方可以設定所售物品價格，但交易的時間或者次數有一定的限制。比如在香港一手物業市場，新年花市，以及機票銷售中，所有物品（物業，鮮花，機票）必須在一個事先設定的截止日期前出售，超過這個截止日期，所售物品將不再有價值。本課題的目標是在不同的用戶行為模型假設下，設計高效的算法來最大化賣方的收益。同時，深化我們對不同市場價格機制以及不同交易策略的理解。

711413.label: Realisation of objectives
711413.value: We consider a computational economics model having two kinds of participants: the seller and the buyer. The seller has some items, which will be sold to buyers and; the buyer will buy the items at a price. The objective is to maximize the total revenue of the seller by assigning items to the buyers. We studied two problems in this project and achieved objective 1 for these two problems. To illustrate the first problem, suppose the seller wants to sell all shares in the stock market to achieve the highest revenue. The price of the shares fluctuates with time, and at each time, the seller must decide the number of shares, if any, to be sold at the prevailing price, without any knowledge of future prices. To illustrate the second problem, suppose a travel agent has some products such as flights and hotels to sell to buyers (or users) with the target of maximizing revenues. Each buyer is interested in a package of flights and hotels, which she may value differently from other buyers. The travel agent must decide the price and package (bundles of multiple items) sold to each buyer on her arrival. These two problems are different in nature and are formulated differently. (a) In [J2, C1], we studied the one-way trading problem. In the one-way trading problem, a seller has no control of the prices, and when a buyer arrives, he can only determine the amount of the product to be sold at the then-prevailing market price. This kind of situation occurs in the stock market or money-exchange context. Suppose we are dealing with the money-exchange context with prices being exchange rates. The one-way trading problem studied is the bounded version where the range of exchange rates (or rates, for short) is in [m, M], where m and M are fixed values. Based on the relationship between m and M, El-Yaniv et al. presented an optimal online algorithm by using a threat-based policy, having a competitive ratio of Θ(log(M/m)). If the highest possible rate is unbounded, even for a fixed number of transactions, the threat-based policy cannot be implemented since the ratio between any two rates can be arbitrarily large. In the bounded one-way trading problem, the remaining amount of the initial currency after the last transaction will be changed to the target currency with the minimum rate m. However, if the highest possible rate is unbounded, in the worst case, the total revenue is dominated by the revenue from high rates and the revenue from the remaining asset using the minimum rate is very tiny and ignoring this part will hardly affect the performance. In summary, the key features of this problem are: (1) the player has no control of the exchange rate which fluctuates over time; (2) the player has no knowledge, or incomplete knowledge, of the future; and (3) the player can decide the amount to be changed only upon the arrival of each rate. In [J2 and C1], we consider the unbounded one-way trading algorithm that does not need to impose any constraint on the market prices, and we derive a bound on its competitive ratio that depends directly on the input, or more precisely, depends on r* = p* / p1, the ratio of the highest price p* and the first price p1 (in fact, our algorithm will treat p1 as the lowest price and ignore any prices lower than p1). Furthermore, the algorithm does not make any assumption on the number of prices in the input sequence and an adversary can terminate the sequence at any time by giving buyers extremely low prices. Our generic algorithm gives us a class of one-way trading algorithms with a bounded competitive ratio in terms of r*. We also show that the bounds are almost tight by employing the divergence of a class of functions and designing an adversary such that, given any online algorithm A for the problem, the adversary gives a sequence of buyers σ such that the revenue obtained by an optimal offline algorithm on σ and that obtained by A is bounded below by similar functions with similar competitive ratio. (b) In [J1], we study the online pricing for bundles of multiple items. Formally speaking, given a seller with k types of items, i1, i2, …, ik, the amount of each type is m. A sequence of users {u1, u2, …} come one by one. Each user is single-minded, i.e., each user is interested only in a particular bundle of items. For example, user u’s bundle of interest is Iu = {i1, i2} (or Iu = {1, 2}). The seller must set the unit price and sell a certain number of bundles to each user on his/her arrival. In [J1], we first show that a lower bound of the competitive ratio for this problem is (log m + log k), where m is the highest unit price to be paid among all users. We then give a deterministic online algorithm, Pricing, whose competitive ratio is O(√k log m log k). When k = 1, the lower and upper bounds asymptotically match the optimal result O(log m) for a single item. As for the objective 2, when the seller has the option of setting any price, the problem is only realistic when the seller also knows the buyers’ behaviors, i.e., the demand curve (the amounts the buyers are willing to purchase at each price). If there is no information about the future prices, no algorithm achieved a competitive ratio better than a logarithm factor. When some partial information about the price is given, the performance could be improved greatly. In [C2], we assume that the distribution on the highest price among all buyers is known. We then consider a general variant where the sequence of prices of buyers is independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.). To measure the performance of the online algorithm, the competitive ratio is often used, which denotes the ratio between the result form the online algorithm and the optimal offline algorithm. For the online algorithm with distributions, we use the expected competitive ratio for evaluation. There are mainly two kinds of expectations of competitive ratio, i.e., E[OPT]/E[ALG] and E[OPT/ALG]. Both of them are considered with respect to different situations and their values may vary a lot. For the former measure, since the expected value of the optimal solution is independent of the algorithm solution, the target is to maximize the expected output of the algorithm. In the paper [C2], we give constant competitive algorithms if the distribution is on the highest price among all buyers. We also prove that the variant with i.i.d. distribution on each buyer can be reduced to the variant of the previous case, and thus constant-competitive algorithms can be obtained too.

711413.label: Major findings and research outcome
711413.value: This project involves the study of problems where the objective is to maximize the revenue of a seller. Past research has focused on how the seller should price the products he sells. The problems we propose to study are computationally interesting and non-trivial and are motivated by real-life situations. The motivation is from, for example, the stock market trading situation where the seller wishes to sell shares ‘at market’ as the market share price fluctuates with time: the focus in this situation is determining the number of shares to sell when given the price at a certain time. In other words, the key features of the selling problem are: (1) the seller has no control of the market price which fluctuates with time; (2) the seller can only decide the amount to be sold to the buyer (who is willing to buy an almost unlimited amount) at the market price; and (3) the seller has no knowledge, or incomplete knowledge, of future market prices. In general, there are two ways for a seller to maximize revenue, controlling the selling price and/or controlling the amount sold. Past research work has exclusively focused on price setting. Our problem is focused on determining the selling amount. We studied the basic problem which can be formulated as follows: devise a maximum revenue selling strategy for a single seller trying to sell m units (of a single item), which can be sold fractionally to multiple buyers σ = {u1, u2, ...}, served one at a time, in order to maximize revenues. For each buyer ui, the seller decides on the amount to be sold to this buyer based on his valuation vi, i.e., is the unit market price which the buyer ui is willing to pay (market price). In [J1], we extend the problem to bundles of multiple items, instead of individual items. In [J2, C1], we eliminate the assumption that the range of the selling price is known. This problem is difficult when the maximum selling price is unbounded, for which we have devised a performance bound. However, both assumptions of knowing and not-knowing the maximum selling price are unrealistic; in [C2] we assume that the maximum price follows some distribution with monotone hazard rate, which is well-adopted in Economics. Again, we have derived competitive bounds for this problem. Besides these results, the grant also supported the research as indicated in [J3] and [J4].

711413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
711413.value: Item selling is a realistic and important problem in computational economics, and the aim is to devise fast algorithms to give the optimal, or a reasonably good approximate, selling scheme. On the seller’s side, both multiple types of items and single type of items have been considered. For each type of item, the amount may be unlimited or bounded. As for the buyer behaviors, there are mainly three models that have been considered: single-minded (each user is interested only in a particular set of items), unit-demand (each user will buy at most one item in total) and envy-free (after the assignment, no user would prefer to be assigned a different set of items with the designated prices; loosely speaking, each user is happy with his/her purchase). Previous works have considered different combinations of the behavior of the seller and that of the buyer (e.g., envy-free pricing for single-minded users when there is unlimited supply). We are interested to explore this one-way trading problem with these different buyer behaviors.

711413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
711413.value: This project involves the study of problems for which the objective is to maximize the revenue of a seller. More specifically, the problems we propose to study are motivated by various interesting real-life situations, namely: (1) situations where the seller cannot control the price but can decide the amount sold at each sale – e.g. in the stock market trading and the sale of electricity to a grid settings, where the seller is concerned about how many units he should be selling at the prevailing market-determined price at various times to maximize sale proceeds, and (2) situations where the seller is selling a package of items, for example, a travel agent has products, e.g., flight tickets and hotel rooms, to sell with the target of maximizing his revenue. Each buyer is interested in a package (i.e., combination of flights and hotels), for which his valuations may be different from that of other buyers. At any specific time, a seller needs to decide whether he should, in the above respective two scenarios, (1) sell some shares, and if so, the number of shares to sell, and (2) decide the package to sell and at what price.

711713.label: Project Objectives
711713.value: To understand how higher order nonlinear Schrodinger models might arise. Using the propagation of wave packets near a critical depth as an example, asymptotic re-scaling will produce a derivative nonlinear Schrodinger equation with quintic (fifth order) nonlinearity. To calculate the permanent propagating modes of nonlinear evolution systems using this derivative nonlinear Schrodinger equation as an illustrative example. Two invariants (or integrals of motion) are identified, one of which is usually the energy or Hamiltonian of the system. The modes to be investigated include localized pulses, fronts and dark solitary waves. To obtain 'explode-decay' or rogue waves of higher order nonlinear Schrodinger models by the Hirota bilinear transformations, and to study / compare this approach with the Darboux transformations used widely in the past ten years. To identify regions of stability computationally. A numerical scheme will be developed to trace the evolution of wave profiles perturbed by random noise. To study the occurrence of 'rogue waves' in other oceanic settings, e.g. in the deep water regime or for layered fluids. Other evolution models then need to be called upon, e.g. (a) For deep water, the Benjamin-Ono model should be employed; (b) For layered or continuously stratified fluids, long wave - short wave resonance occur whenever the group velocity of the short wave matches the phase velocity of the long wave. To provide a platform for highly talented undergraduates to acquire research experience. Some analytical treatments involve only a modest mathematics backgroud, e.g. ordinary differential equations and hyperbolic functions, and are within the capabilities of undergraduates (Item 3, Part II).

711713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
711713.value: 背景: 非線性波動的研究近年來在科學界十分普遍，如流體力學、光學和離子體物理學等。很多類的演化模型, 不單在物理學上可應用，同時亦具備有優美的分析結構。這些分析令我們對流體力學和光學有進一步的瞭解，提供從實際上和實驗角度上的真知灼見。立方非線性薛定諤模型是一個很好的例子，它的特點是在色散和立方非線性平衡中得出孤立波。 目標和關鍵問題: 目標是 ● 要找尋出那一類的情況下，立方非線性薛定諤模型對流體力學和光學不再是一種適當的描述 ； ● 分析和澄清參與的非線性動力學的新模式。 我們用兩個來自流體力學的例子去研究這些新的方程式，但從這研究所獲取的知識將會適用于其他領域。一個統一的主題是用高層次非線性薛定諤方程。首先，在海水表面的波浪，立方非線性在某一個關鍵的深度下會削弱，較精密的計算會衍生一個五次方的非線性薛定諤系統。第二個示例是使用高層次非線性薛定諤方程來研究突發的巨浪, 這些名叫殺手波 ˴ 異常波或極端波的巨浪，它們能從平靜的海面上突然冒升，會對海上船隻構成極大的威脅。我們從理論上計算一個高層次非線性薛定諤方程的孤立波，對海上較大的異常波或極端波的研究有幫助。 研究方法: 我們建議用一種概念上很簡單但新穎的演算法。首先是隔離一個或多個和能量有關的不變數。第二項是要搜索隨時間波動的孤立波，然後使用功能強大的廣田雙線性變換法去計算這些異常波。 初步結果: 孤立波的模式初步已經確定，但全面的研究，包括連續波浪背景上的孤立波將須更深入的探討。此外，該等波浪的穩定性將要靠大型電腦來計算。在應用科學方面，這研究對海洋裡的長短波共振有幫助，令我們從科學上有進一步的瞭解。 意義: 非線性科學的理論研究將會進一步擴大。科學家將會實現用另一個角度來理解水波動力學。這寶貴的見解和知識可以很容易擴展到其他領域，例如光學， 先進的光纖技術必會使實驗示範更容易達到。

711713.label: Realisation of objectives
711713.value: (1) and (2): Higher order nonlinear Schrödinger equations beyond the effects of quadratic dispersion and cubic nonlinearity are considered, and these theoretical models are relevant in various branches in engineering and applied science, e.g. water waves and optical fibers. Traveling waves of such higher order Schrödinger equations are sought by reducing the evolution system to an ordinary differential equation (ODE). Two invariants are identified where one is the Hamiltonian (or the energy) of the dynamical system. By solving the ODE with elementary (e.g. hyperbolic) or elliptic functions, localized and periodic pulses are derived. This exercise is conducted for two cases as illustrative examples: (a) quintic (fifth order) nonlinearity, expressed as the amplitude of the wave packet to the algebraic power of five, and (b) self-steepening nonlinearity, described as a product of the intensity of the wave packet and the slope of the wave profile. (3) A few classes of 'explode-decay' modes of nonlinear dynamical systems were explored in the literature in the 1970s to 1990s. Here we examine 'rogue waves' as another scenario of 'explode-decay' modes. Using words frequently used in the literature these days, rogue waves 'come from nowhere and disappear without a trace'. These waves have been known in the oceanic setting for more than a century and are currently actively studied in the optical setting too. We make contribution in this intensely studied field by utilizing the Hirota bilinear method to find the lowest order rogue waves of dynamical systems analytically. (4) The existence of rogue waves is intimately connected with the onset of modulation instability of dynamical systems. Modulation instability refers to the spontaneous growth of disturbances on plane waves due to the interplay of dispersive and nonlinear effects, and has been known to scientists since the 1960s from studies of waves in water channels as well as theoretical investigations. Such instability favors the localization of energy and hence the likely formation of 'explode-decay' modes like rogue waves. However, growth of background noise will also occur as an inevitable consequence. The competition between a 'noisy background' and the main rogue wave is usually studied by numerical simulations these days. We developed our own codes using fourth order Runge-Kutta method in time and pseudo-spectral schemes in space. Very promising and encouraging results have been obtained. One example is the extension of coupled nonlinear Schrödinger system from two components to three components. Ranges of instability thresholds were demonstrated to be wider if the number of components increased. Numerical simulations had also been conducted (our paper in Applied Sciences 2017, attached). Our work on modulation instability is recognized internationally. We had been invited to contribute to a book chapter (our paper in Lecture Notes in Physics 2016, attached). The scope of that work covers the comparisons between modulation instability in long wave (Korteweg-de Vries type) models versus hierarchy of nonlinear Schrödinger equations. (5) The nonlinear Schrödinger equation had been derived in the literature for packets of water waves under a weakly nonlinear (in amplitude), narrow band (in frequency) assumption. Similar expansion schemes have been worked out for optical waveguides too. Over the years, scientists have investigated other regimes of wave evolution, e.g. (a) long wave-short wave resonance in layered and stratified fluids, where the group velocity of the short wave coincides with the phase velocity of a long wave; (b) long waves in a layer of shallow fluid under the influence of dispersion of an adjacent fluid of great depth, leading to the Benjamin-Ono equation with a Hilbert transform operator representing a 'non-analytic' dispersion relationship. We have successes in treating (a), with papers published in Nonlinear Dynamics (2016) and Physical Review Fluids (2018), to be reported later in conjunction with other grants from the Research Grants Council. Point (b) poses more difficulty due to the peculiar form of the bilinear operator involving auxiliary functions with poles in the upper/lower half planes of complex variables. We shall keep working on this aspect. In pursuing other connections with fluid dynamics, we have obtained results concerning a model on the compressible Euler equations with damping. A generalized setting of differential operators in the matrix settings is employed, and exact solutions are derived. One such solution exhibits 'explode-decay' type character (our paper in Studies in Applied Mathematics 2017, attached). (6) We had identified one talented undergraduate in the duration of the grant, and shall continue to search for motivated students.

711713.label: Major findings and research outcome
711713.value: (a) Propagating pulses of a nonlinear Schrödinger equation with self-steepening and quintic (fifth order) nonlinearities were calculated analytically by identifying two invariants of motion (Communications in Theoretical Physics 2014). (b) 'Explode-decay' type modes (rogue waves) were calculated for the derivative nonlinear Schödinger equation using the Hirota bilinear method (Physical Review E 2014). (c) Localized modes for discrete evolution equations with gain/loss were computed (European Physical Journal Special Topics 2014, Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society 2014). Information and insight from these works eventually led to our studies of rogue waves in discrete systems in 2018. (d) Properties of optical pulses governed by coupled nonlinear Schrödinger equations were studied for the case of fibers with birefringence and polarization effects (Optics Communications 2014). (e) To demonstrate the applicability of the bilinear method, rogue wave and localized mode were calculated for a specially designed evolution system (Applied Mathematics Letters 2015). (f) The emergence of rogue waves / 'explode-decay' modes from an arbitrary initial condition is a critical issue in current research. One approach is to conduct numerical simulations. Using the Hirota equation (nonlinear Schrödinger equation with third order dispersion) as an illustrative example, the appearance of rogue waves from a 'noisy background' was elucidated. With modulation instability, background noise might grow too, and the robustness of rogue waves against these competing effects was highlighted (Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulations 2016). (g) The comparisons and contrasts between wave packets of a group of waves with finite wavelengths versus long waves, i.e. nonlinear Schrödinger equations versus the Korteweg-de Vries equations, were described from the perspective of modulation instability. We had been invited to contribute a book chapter on this topic (Lecture Notes in Physics 2016). (h) As further efforts in the nonlinear dynamics of fluid mechanics and optics, our group wrote two papers in 2017: (i) The effects of damping for the compressible Euler equations - A fluid with density variation in the presence of energy loss was treated in a generalized formulation using differential equations in a matrix setting (Studies in Applied Mathematics 2017). (ii) Periodic patterns for optical waveguides where the nonlinearity displayed modulations expressed explicitly in terms of Jacobi elliptic functions - Stability was treated in two perspectives. The first one was through the spectrum of a linearized differential operator. The second one was through a direct numerical simulation with perturbed initial conditions (Europhysics Letters 2017).

711713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
711713.value: Knowledge of rogue waves generated can be used to study 'extreme and rare events' in several fields in engineering and applied science, in particular, dynamics, fluid mechanics and optics. (a) In discrete dynamical systems, the Ablowitz-Ladik equations serve as useful analytical framework for randomness versus dispersion, as well as oscillators with a fourth order nonlinearity. Knowledge from this project has led to our published papers in 'AIP Advances' and 'Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation' in 2018. (b) Applications to realistic oceanic settings, e.g. long wave-short wave resonance in layered and stratified fluids, have led to a publication in 'Physical Review Fluids' in 2018. We plan to extend the consideration to wave interaction scenarios with even faster time scales. (c) Detection of unexpectedly large signals in optical rogue waves has attracted a lot of attention recently. We have employed a research assistant, Mr. WEI Yuan, in conjunction with the experimental group of Professor K. K. Y. Wong of the Electrical and Electronic Engineering Department of the University of Hong Kong, to initiate an effort in this direction.

711713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
711713.value: Nonlinear evolution systems provide insightful dynamical models in fluid mechanics and optics, by providing analytical formulation of generation, propagation and instability of 'explode-decay' modes. In hydrodynamics, rogue waves constitute one particular class of motions which may attain unexpectedly large amplitudes from otherwise tranquil configurations. Such waves obviously pose immense risk to marine shipping and offshore structures. Recently similar modes are demonstrated experimentally in optical waveguides, and have been used as a convenient platform to study 'extreme and rare events in physics'. In this project, we first identify traveling waves through identification of two invariants of many dynamical systems. The Hirota bilinear method is then shown to be applicable in the analytical calculations of the rogue waves. Numerical simulations are conducted to elucidate the occurrence of rogue waves from a 'noisy background'. Graduate students (and hence future scientists) were trained through the awarding of doctoral degrees. A highly talented undergraduate was encouraged to participate in our research projects. His work eventually was published and was classified as a 'highly cited paper' (November 2018). Collaborations with distinguished experts overseas: (a) Australia - University of New South Waves, (b) Israel - Tel Aviv University, were sustained through constructive dialogues and joint publications.

711813.label: Project Objectives
711813.value: Exploring physical mechanisms and effects of plasmon-induced carriers in metal/metal oxide systems for OSC applications By establishing multiphysics models, the metal absorption, and the carrier transport and tunneling properties of metal/metal oxide systems will be investigated. Together with our experimental studies, we will understand how the parameters (e.g. material, geometry, and concentration) of metal nanostructures, metal oxide materials, and external bias affect the electrical properties of metal/metal oxide systems. Designing wideband and angle-insensitive metal/metal oxide buffer layers The wideband and angle-insensitive optical properties are not only the important issues for the light absorption of active layers (which are better recognized and addressed) but also buffer layers for enhancing carrier extraction (affected by the wavelength-dependent properties) and stabilizing device performances at different irradiation directions (affected by the angle-dependent properties). We will design the metal nanoantenna compatible to metal oxides for wideband and angle-insensitive carrier generation in metal/metal oxide buffer layers. The physical mechanisms for designing the metal nanoantenna embedded in the buffer layers will be explored. The substrate effect, electron collection and tunneling probability will be considered for achieving good carrier generation. Enhancing OSC performances by using metal/metal oxide CTLs (a) Understanding the effects of metal/metal oxide CTLs in OSCs. We will develop models to investigate multilayered OSCs taking into account the extraction and injection barriers due to the insertion of metal/metal oxide CTLs. The roles of the plasmonic-electrical effects on the carrier transport in the CTLs can then be investigated. The J-V characteristics and carrier transport properties of OSCs with the CTLs will be studied experimentally. With the newly developed models, the theoretical carrier and current distributions will help us to understand the features and physics of the measured J-V characteristics. The transition from Schottky to ohmic contact through the incorporation of plasmonic metal nanostructures and selection of CTL materials will also be studied theoretically and experimentally. (b) Improving OSCs performances by optimizing metal/metal oxide CTLs. With the theoretical and experimental investigations, we will design the CTLs with the material and thickness of metal oxides and CTL locations, as well as metal nanostructure parameters (i.e. material, geometry and concentration), and understand their roles in carrier transport, collection, and recombination of OSCs. We will optimize the carrier transport properties, energy band alignment, and optical transmission of metal/metal oxide CTLs for highly effective carrier extraction covering a wide range of wavelengths and incident angles for enhancing OSC performances. *** Note: to show our capability to manage the project, we have started to study metal/metal oxide CTLs. The preliminary results show that hot carriers will generate at plasmonic wavelengths and modify the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of OSCs. Details will be discussed in “Research Plan and Methodology”.
rows: Exploring physical mechanisms and effects of plasmon-induced carriers in metal/metal oxide systems for OSC applications By establishing multiphysics models, the metal absorption, and the carrier transport and tunneling properties of metal/metal oxide systems will be investigated. Together with our experimental studies, we will understand how the parameters (e.g. material, geometry, and concentration) of metal nanostructures, metal oxide materials, and external bias affect the electrical properties of metal/metal oxide systems.

Designing wideband and angle-insensitive metal/metal oxide buffer layers The wideband and angle-insensitive optical properties are not only the important issues for the light absorption of active layers (which are better recognized and addressed) but also buffer layers for enhancing carrier extraction (affected by the wavelength-dependent properties) and stabilizing device performances at different irradiation directions (affected by the angle-dependent properties). We will design the metal nanoantenna compatible to metal oxides for wideband and angle-insensitive carrier generation in metal/metal oxide buffer layers. The physical mechanisms for designing the metal nanoantenna embedded in the buffer layers will be explored. The substrate effect, electron collection and tunneling probability will be considered for achieving good carrier generation.

Enhancing OSC performances by using metal/metal oxide CTLs (a) Understanding the effects of metal/metal oxide CTLs in OSCs. We will develop models to investigate multilayered OSCs taking into account the extraction and injection barriers due to the insertion of metal/metal oxide CTLs. The roles of the plasmonic-electrical effects on the carrier transport in the CTLs can then be investigated. The J-V characteristics and carrier transport properties of OSCs with the CTLs will be studied experimentally. With the newly developed models, the theoretical carrier and current distributions will help us to understand the features and physics of the measured J-V characteristics. The transition from Schottky to ohmic contact through the incorporation of plasmonic metal nanostructures and selection of CTL materials will also be studied theoretically and experimentally. (b) Improving OSCs performances by optimizing metal/metal oxide CTLs. With the theoretical and experimental investigations, we will design the CTLs with the material and thickness of metal oxides and CTL locations, as well as metal nanostructure parameters (i.e. material, geometry and concentration), and understand their roles in carrier transport, collection, and recombination of OSCs. We will optimize the carrier transport properties, energy band alignment, and optical transmission of metal/metal oxide CTLs for highly effective carrier extraction covering a wide range of wavelengths and incident angles for enhancing OSC performances.

*** Note: to show our capability to manage the project, we have started to study metal/metal oxide CTLs. The preliminary results show that hot carriers will generate at plasmonic wavelengths and modify the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of OSCs. Details will be discussed in “Research Plan and Methodology”.

711813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
711813.value: While the optical effects of plasmonic metal nanostructures (e.g. nanoparticles (NPs), nanoprisms, etc) and the material effects of the metal nanostructures have recently been individually studied for enhancing the performances of organic solar cells (OSCs) (see “Background of research”), the effects of plasmon-induced changes in electrical properties, hereafter named as the plasmonic-electrical effects, on OSCs have not been well studied. Here, we propose to investigate the plasmonic-electrical effects such as plasmon-induced carrier generation and change of carrier extraction properties in OSCs. To be more specific, the multiphysical (optical, electrical, and quantum mechanical) understanding of the plasmonic-electrical effects of metal oxides incorporated with metal nanostructures (hereafter named as metal/metal oxide) on OSCs and the utilization of metal/metal oxide systems as efficient carrier transport (buffer) layers (CTLs) of OSCs will be investigated. The challenges to study the plasmonic-electrical effects of metal/metal oxide systems on OSCs lie at: (1) fully considering the plasmon-induced carrier generation (governing by classical electromagnetics), and carrier tunneling and transport (governing by semiconductor physics and quantum mechanics) in metal/metal-oxide systems at the same time, (2) evolving the fundamental physics of metal/metal oxide systems to the device physics and mechanisms (e.g. current density (J)-voltage (V) characteristics, space charge accumulation, etc) of organic optoelectronic devices, (3) designing conclusive device configurations (through selections of material and thickness of organic active layer, as well as thickness and combination of metal/metal oxide CTLs) for understanding device physics and optimizing device performances. In this project, we will (1) theoretically and experimentally explore the tunneling and transport properties of plasmon-induced carriers on metal/metal oxide systems (i.e. fundamental physics of electrical properties), (2) design the metal nanostructures compatible to metal oxides for achieving broadband and minimizing angle-dependence in carrier generation and collection (i.e. fundamental physics of optical properties), (3) design versatile device architectures to understand the roles of metal/metal oxide systems in carrier transport, collection, and recombination (i.e. device physics), and optimize OSC performances. Consequently, apart from contributing to OSC performance enhancements by using metal/metal oxide systems as CTLs, this research will allow better understanding of the fundamental multiphysics of metal/metal oxide systems and their effects on OSC optical and electrical properties. Moreover, the plasmonic-electrical effects are strongly related to semiconductor physics, which is the foundation of semiconductor devices. The research can bridge the knowledge from conventional semiconductor devices to organic devices. Furthermore, we will publish our results in international journals and train research students and professionals. 關於電離子電納米結構的光學特性和金屬納米結構的材料特性在提高有機太陽能電池方面最近被廣泛得獨立研究。然而電離子產生的在有機太陽能電池上的電特性還沒有得到很好的探索。 這裡，我們提出了研究電離子電特性所產生的載流子生成和載流子抽取性能的改善在有機太陽能電池中的應用。深入研究和理解金屬納米結構電離子產生的多重物理特性在嵌於作為有機太陽能電池高效載流子傳輸界面層的金屬氧化物中的作用以及應用。 研究有機太陽能電池中金屬/金屬氧化物系統的電離子性能主要有以下幾個挑戰： （1）如何全面和同時考慮電離子產生的載流子生成和載流子隧穿及傳輸在金屬/金屬氧化物中的作用。 （2）如何從基礎物理推導出金屬/金屬氧化物的在有機光電器件的器件物理和機制。 （3）如何設計最終器件屬性來優化器件效率。 在這個項目中，我們將（1）從理論和實驗研究電離子產生的載流子在金屬/金屬氧化物種的隧穿和傳輸特性；（2）設計兼容於金屬氧化物的金屬納米結構來達到寬頻帶和減少角度依賴的載流子生成和收集；（3）設計多元化的器件結構來理解在金屬/金屬氧化物中載流子傳輸，收集和復合的機制以及來優化有機太陽能電池的性能。 因此，除了通過作為載流子傳輸層的金屬/金屬氧化物系統來提高有機太陽能電池的表現，這個研究同時將更加深入的理解金屬/金屬氧化物系統中的基礎多重物理和在有機太陽能電池中的光電特性。此外，電離子電特性與半導體物理緊密相關，是半導體器件的基礎。這個研究將會加深傳統半導體器件到有機半導體器件的知識的連接。同時，我們將會把我們的研究結果發表在國際學術期刊上，訓練研究生和專業人員。

711813.label: Realisation of objectives
711813.value: For objective 1, we have studied the effects of plasmonic bandstructure and find that we can significantly extend the group velocity of the electromagnetic waves at the plasmonic band edge [Opt. Lett., 39, 158, 2014]. We also propose the use of integration of grating and discrete metallic nanostructure to achieve various coupled plasmonic resonances and particularly explaining the original physics through the a hybridized excitation of propagating Bloch-Plasmon and localized surface-plasmon modes [Nanoscale, 7, 16798, 2015]. With the different structure, in order to evaluate the influences in device performances, we developed exciton Delocalization Incorporated Drift-Diffusion Model for Bulk-Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells [J. Appl. Phys., 120, 213101, 2016.]. Regarding different metal oxide for uses in the metal/metal oxide system, we have further investigated the metal oxide of TiOx nanoparticles for electron transport layer formed from our proposed self-assembly method favoring the application of for high speed and low dark current photodetectors [Adv. Opt. Mat., 2, 1082, 2014]. For improving workfunction alignment with organic active layer and electrode, the incorporation of metal nanomaterials into the metal oxides, we propose the new room-temperature based solution processed of NiOx nanoparticles [Adv. Mat., DOI: 10.1002/ adma.201405391; ACS Nano, 10, 6808, 2016] and carbon nanotubes [Adv. Mat. Interface, 2, 1500324, 2015.] without sophisticated treatments in forming the carrier transport layers. The incorporation of metal nanomaterials into the NiOx carrier transport layer is under investigation. In addition, for improving the electrical mobility, Cs is intercalated into the metal oxides [Adv. Function. Mat., 24, 7348, 2014] to tune conduction of electron and hole for functioning as either electron or hole transport layer [Light: Science & Applications, doi: 10.1038/ lsa.2015.46.] Recently, by using MoOx hole transport layer together with metal grating in anode, we introduce the concept of plasmonic-electrical effects of plasmonically induced photocarriers redistribution into organic solar cells [Scientific Reports, 4, 6236, 2014; highlighted in SPIE Newsroom. DOI: 10.1117/2.1201505.005930]. While space charge limit (SCL) of photocurrent is an intrinsic feature of typical organic semiconductors, we can use the plasmonic-electrical effects to shorten the transport path of low-mobility holes and break SCL in organic semiconductors [Progress in Electromagnetics Research, 146, 25, 2014]. Finally, we proposed a general design rule to manipulate the photocarrier transport path in solar cells and its realization by the plasmonic-electrical effect [Scientific Reports, 5, 8525, 2015]. For Objective 2, in order to adjust the wavelength region and achieve angle-insensitive optical properties of the metal nanostructure, we propose and experimentally and theoretically demonstrate a new class of microscopically random (micro-random) and macroscopically periodic (macro-periodic) metal nanostructures for achieving wideband optical enhancement and reduce the angular sensitivity [Scientific Reports, DOI: 10.1038/srep07876]. Besides, we can turn the space between metal nanoparticles and metal plate to adjust the coupling of plasmonic resonances of the discrete nanoparticles and metal plate for wideband absorption enhancement [Adv. Opt. Mat., 3, 1220, 2015, Nanoscale, 7, 11291, 2015]. In addition, the optical transmission properties of metal plate can be tuned by introducing high index nanoparticles (e.g. Si nanoparticles) and dielectric layer functioning as transparent electrode [Nano Energy, 17, 187, 2015.]. With the knowledge of plasmon-electrical effects gained in last objective, we simultaneously achieve plasmon-electrical and plasmon-optical induced enhancement in solar cell performances [Small, 12, 5200, 2016.]. Meanwhile, by introducing plasmonic light-induced chemical reaction, silver nanoparticles are selectively grown and chemically integrated in-situ at the junction where silver nanowires meet to form silver nano-network [ACS Nano, 8, 10980, 2014, Adv Function. Mat. 25, 4211, 2015.]. The nano-network structure can offer strong plasmonic enhanced scattering effects. In addition, by placing metal nanoparticles into different regions of organic light emitting devices, we can use the near-field enhancement and far-field scattering enhancement of plasmonic resonances to explain and enhance the light emitting properties [ACS Appl. Mat. & Interfaces, 6, 11001, 2014.] Finally, we summarize different approaches using multiple metal nanostructure for enhancing the light trapping in thin film organic solar cells [Chem. Comm., 50, 11984, 2014, IEEE J. Selected Topics Quant. Elect., 10.1109/JSTQE.2015.2442679.]. For Objective 3, we propose a novel NFG system by introducing ultrathin monolayer graphene as well-defined sub-nanospacer between Ag NPs and Ag film (named G(graphene)-NFG system). The new G-NFG system offers tremendous near-field enhancement with one of the highest enhancement ratio of 1700 reported to date in the graphene-metal plasmonic combination system [Adv. Funct. Mat., 24, 3114, 2014]. This work has been featured as the frontispiece cover; highlighted as research new in MaterialsViewsChina.com published by Wiley. We also use our solution-processed metal oxide carrier transport layer in organic solar cells made from other new polymer materials [Adv. Funct. Mat., 24, 6540, 2014]. Since the multilayered structure of organic solar cells here are made from solution process, we can incorporate metal nanomaterials to further enhance device performances [Adv. Mat., 2014, 26, 5368, 2014., J. Mat. Chem. A, 3, 23955, 2015]. Recently, we used our p-type and n-type metal oxides developed in objective 1 to form efficient interconnecting layer and build tandem solar cells [Adv. Energy Mat., DOI: 10.1002/aenm.201500631, Nanoscale, 8, 3638, 2016, Nano Energy, 21, 123, 2016.]. We also study the operation mechanism and optimize the performance of tandem cells by studying the quantum tunneling and thermionic emission properties of the interconnecting layers. It should be noted that the outputs stated in this progress report are achieved through the financial supported from this GRF fund together with some other internal small seed funding, collaborative research funds from RGC and Croucher-CAS Funding Scheme for Joint Laboratories.

711813.label: Major findings and research outcome
711813.value: The findings of our projects are that (1) theoretically and experimentally understand the tunneling and transport properties of plasmon-induced carriers on metal/metal oxide systems (i.e. fundamental physics of electrical properties such as band bending concepts), which is the foundational important for electronic and optoelectronic semiconductor devices. Therefore, our results can bridge the knowledge from conventional semiconductor devices to organic devices. (2) different combination of metal nanostructures (e.g. gratings and nanoparticles with different geometries) to achieve wideband and angle-insensitive metal absorber for enhancing carrier generation and collection which is of board interests (and thus can have contribution) in many fields, e.g. inorganic photodetectors and photovoltaic devices. (3) different designs of device architectures to understand the roles of metal/metal oxide systems to improve carrier transport, collection, and recombination (i.e. device physics), and optimize device performances e.g. carrier transport and tunneling properties from metal nanostructures to metal oxides, which is particularly helpful to evolve the emerging organic optoelectronics.

711813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
711813.value: With the understanding the physics of metal nanostructure and the demonstration of various metal/metal oxide systems as electron and hole transport layers. Our work have conceptually demonstrated high efficiency organic solar cells. The work can extended to large scale organic solar cells and the potential applications in flexible electronics. Meanwhile, the device stability shall be studied taking into account the oxygen and moisture effects for their practical applications.

711813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
711813.value: In this work, we have proposed and demonstrated the plasmon-electrical effects such as plasmon-induced carrier generation and change of carrier extraction properties in organic solar cells. We have established the multiphysical (optical, electrical, and quantum mechanical) understanding of the plasmonic-electrical effects of metal oxides incorporated with metal nanostructures on organic solar cells and utilized of metal/metal oxide systems as efficient carrier transport layers of organic solar cells. With the understanding, we have designed the metal nanostructures compatible to metal oxides for achieving broadband and minimizing angle-dependence in carrier generation and collection and understand the roles of metal/metal oxide systems in carrier transport, collection, and recombination (i.e. device physics). We then achieve high performance organic solar cells by using the optimized metal/metal oxide system. Consequently, apart from contributing to device performance enhancements by using metal/metal oxide systems as carrier transport layers, this research allow better understanding of the fundamental multiphysics of metal/metal oxide systems and their effects on device optical and electrical properties. Moreover, the plasmonic-electrical effects are strongly related to semiconductor physics, which is the foundation of semiconductor devices. The research also bridge the knowledge from conventional semiconductor devices to organic devices for evolving new class of organic electronic devices.

712213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
712213.value: 奈米流體為含有懸浮奈米顆粒的液體，已引起了廣泛關注於提升熱傳的方法及其潛在應用能源技術。部分實驗觀測比馬克斯威爾等效介質理論預測有更高的導熱係數，潛在的機制，如布朗運動、團聚、液體分層、熱泳和近場輻射，但不清楚提升奈米流體的熱傳導原因，仍具強烈爭議性。由我們先前的實驗研究結果，以穩定懸浮石墨維持奈米粒子的團聚和熱滲流效應是熱傳導性提升的主要貢獻，除了熱傳導改變，我們亦發現了以硝酸處理過的石墨片可提升導電性的另一個有趣現象。這種化學改質的石墨懸浮液，通過施加幾十秒鐘的一個外部電勢，可以大大地提升導電率，顯示在懸浮液中形成石墨網絡，它是已知化學修飾的奈米粒子分散到溶液中，奈米粒子藉由表面官能基的離子吸附獲得表面電荷。然而，傳統的有效電導率模型於奈米流體中，並不考慮表面電荷效應，因為沒有施加外部的電勢，早期的大多數實驗顯示表面電荷效應可能是微不足道的。在外部電勢的存在下，我們相信表面電荷在修飾石墨片懸浮液中的分散性和連接性扮演重要的角色，由於電勢相依表面反應介於石墨表面官能基和基礎液體中離子的反應，此外，通過操作外部的電勢，修飾後的石墨懸浮液之熱導率可以提高，並伴隨固相的網絡。目前奈米流體的研究工作主要集中於熱傳導機制、懸浮液的穩定性和其優越的熱性能，關於奈米流體的有效電導率研究是相對有限的。 因此，本計畫致力於（1）研究表面電荷對石墨懸浮液導電性影響的基本原理和（2）通過使用外部的電勢提高奈米流體的熱傳導。研究結果預期將刺激奈米流體的基礎研究興趣和促進我們的理解用於設計下一代奈米流體系統。

712213.label: Realisation of objectives
712213.value: As mentioned in the proposal, we have demonstrated that the application of an external electrical potential to a functionalized graphene (SG)/water suspension distinctly enhances the electrical conductivity via the structural transition from isolated clusters to a 3D SG network. Microstructural and alternating current impedance spectroscopy studies indicate that the surface charge plays an important role in the state of dispersion and connectivity of the SG in the suspension due to the potential-dependent interactions with functional groups on the SG surface in the presence of an external electrical potential. In addition, the conductive SG/ice can be produced via liquid–solid phase transition of the SG/water suspension in the presence of an external electrical potential, which shows a one-order magnitude improvement in electrical conductivity compared with pure ice. The electric-field tunable property advances the understanding of nanofluid systems and has many potential applications.

712213.label: Major findings and research outcome
712213.value: 1. We report the effective use of an electrical field to enhance and regulate the electrical conductivity in SG/water suspensions, where the formation of percolation networks is dependent on the volume fraction and the intensity of the electrical field. 2. Isolated SG clusters percolate to 3D networks under an external electrical potential. AC impedance explains the corresponding change in the potential-dependent interaction between SG–SG and cluster–cluster by manipulating the electrical field. 3. When the SG/water suspension is frozen under the electrical field, the liquid–solid phase transition produces conductive SG/ice with a one-order magnitude improvement in electrical conductivity compared with pure ice.

712213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
712213.value: Our experiments lead to new insights into the state of dispersion and connectivity of SG in liquid suspension and liquid–solid phase transition when an electrical field is applied. We believe that both the electrical conductivity and thermal conductivity of SG/water suspensions can be enhanced via the solid phase network. These electric-field tunable nanofluids may find applications in energy systems, such as thermal convection and thermal energy storage.

712213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
712213.value: Nanofluids, liquids containing solid nanoparticles, attract wide attention due to their enhanced heat and electrical transfer properties and their potential applications in energy technologies. Carbon-based materials with a high aspect ratio, such as carbon nanotubes (CNT), graphite, and graphene, are excellent additives to achieve high thermal and electrical conductivity. It is known that chemically modified nanoparticles gain a surface charge when dispersed into the solution because surface functional groups tend to adsorb ions in the base solution or dissociate themselves spontaneously. The surface charge effect may be negligible in the majority of previous experiments because of the lack of external electrical potential. A distinct enhancement in electrical conductivity under an external electrical potential indicates that the presence of an electrical field contributes to the formation of percolation networks among the graphene nanosheets, resulting from the potential-dependent surface charge effect of the functional groups on the graphene surface. To understand the solid-liquid phase transition of the graphene/water suspension, they further demonstrate a conductive graphene/ice with a one-order magnitude of improvement in electrical conductivity compared with pure ice when freezing graphene/water suspension under an external potential. These electric-field-tunable nanofluids may find applications in energy systems, such as thermal convection and thermal energy storage.

712513.label: Project Title(Chinese)
712513.value: 基于周期密封式双边拍卖的动态运输服务采购

712513.label: Project Objectives
712513.value: To propose a new modeling approach based on auction theory for TSP in a dynamic bilateral exchange transportation market. This approach will take into account the stochastic arrivals of demand and supply. To develop a method to determine the optimal operational strategy (e.g., auction timing, dynamic pricing and allocation) for the third-party auctioneer. To devise truthful, asymptotically efficient auction mechanisms for TSP under four situations, namely, symmetric demand and supply, simple less-than-truckload constraint, supply-demand imbalance, and mixed one-sided and bilateral exchange. To demonstrate how the power of dynamic double auctions can enable this static TSP problem to be extended to include additional important real-world operational considerations. To test and evaluate the proposed models using collaborator’s industrial data.

712513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
712513.value: In recent years, Internet commerce has played a powerful role in the freight transportation market due to the explosive growth of the information and communication technologies and an ever-increasing pressure on companies to operate more efficiently. Unfortunately, few game theoretical models known so far are able to make a realistic representation of this new transportation trading market. An increasing emphasis has recently been placed on using auctions for transportation service procurement (TSP), signifying the enormous potential for online auctions to improve the transportation market efficiency. TSP refers to a general problem of determining transportation and exchange relationships across a transportation market with shippers, carriers and a third-party exchange service provider. However, most research on auction-based TSP is concerned with the auctions hosted by individual shippers. These shipper-biased auction mechanisms impose a daunting computational burden on agents (shippers and carriers), especially when trucking companies are small in a market with numerous agents. This computational burden impedes the trades, especially in combinatorial auctions. This project is among the first attempt to study PERIODIC SEALED DOUBLE AUCTIONS (PSDA) for TSP in a dynamic setting. Under PSDA, buy and sell orders are accumulated during a specific time interval and wait for being cleared. All orders remain sealed until clearing time, and then the aggregated demand and supply are realized. We will first address the TSP problem in a transportation market with stochastic but balanced or “symmetric” demand and supply. We will propose a basic PSDA model for TSP using insights from the well-known McAfee double auction. Under this PSDA, truthful bidding is a dominant strategy for each player (INCENTIVE COMPATIBILITY). We will then consider more complex transportation marketplaces with simple less-than-truckload constraint, supply-demand imbalance, and mixed one-sided and double auction. Each of these extensions will require a rigorous and precise treatment to determine the strategic-timing, dynamic pricing and allocation problems that the third-party auctioneer faces in a periodic double auction. To further simplify bidding strategy for each agent, we will devise a novel PSDA to realize incentive compatibility. Meanwhile, each new PSDA will lead to ASYMPTOTIC EFFICIENCY. Therefore, the inefficiency loss under each auction mechanism compared with maximal social welfare is negligible when the market is sufficiently large. Moreover, the auctioneer’s revenue management policies will be compared from both short-term and long-term points of view. Finally, the proposed models will be tested and evaluated by using collaborator’s industrial data. 近年来，由于信息通信技术的快速发展以及日益增长的企业经营压力，互联网商务在货物运输市场将扮演越来越关键的角色。然而，针对这一新兴运输交易市场参与者之间的利弊关系，很少有研究能从博弈论的角度给出有力的论点和说明。日前一些研究提倡用拍卖的方法分析运输服务采购（transportation service procurement），预计网上拍卖在改进运输市场有效性上有着巨大潜力。运输服务采购是指在发货方、运货方、以及第三方交易服务提供商之间确立服务与利益关系。但目前大部分基于拍卖的运输服务采购都是以发货方为主要服务对象。这类偏向发货方利益的拍卖机制将给市场参与者（尤其对规模较小的运输公司）带来巨大的计算负担，从而在一定程度上限制了拍卖交易的灵活性和持续性。 本项目将开创性地研究基于周期密封式双边拍卖（periodic sealed double auctions）的动态运输服务采购问题。在周期密封式双边拍卖的环境下，运输服务的需求和供应每隔一段时间将以特定的双边拍卖机制撮合；且在撮合之前，运输服务的需求和供应信息都是密封的。首先，本项目将研究在随机且“对称”的运输服务供需环境下的运输服务采购问题。针对这一问题，本项目将基于McAfee一次性双边拍卖方法，提出一个基本的周期密封式双边拍卖机制。在此拍卖机制下，真实投标（truthful bidding）策略将是一个贝叶斯纳什均衡，也称之为激励兼容。 其次，本项目将研究以下三类问题：（i）在随机且“不对称”的运输服务供需环境下的运输服务采购问题；（ii）卡车零担环境下的运输服务采购问题；（iii）混合的单双边拍卖机制下的运输服务采购问题。针对以上每类问题，本项目都将涉及第三方拍卖商的最优拍卖时机问题、动态定价问题、以及运输服务分配问题。为了简化发货方和运货方的投标策略，本项目进而提出一种新颖的周期密封式双边拍卖，来实现激励兼容和运输市场的渐进有效性（asymptotic efficiency）。因此，在此拍卖机制下，一个密集型运输市场的无效性则可以忽略不计。此外，本项目还将从短期和长期的视角来分析第三方拍卖商的利润管理策略。最后，本项目所提出的模型将由实业数据验证并作相应的改进。

712513.label: Major findings and research outcome
712513.value: Most of our research findings have been reported in publications in top journals in the field. The paper "Efﬁcient auctions for distributed transportation procurement" proposed allocatively efﬁcient auction mechanisms for the distributed transportation procurement problem (DTPP), which is generally the problem of matching demands and supplies over a transportation network. The paper "Transportation service procurement in periodic sealed double auctions with stochastic demand and supply" presented a double auction model to study transportation service procurement (TSP) in a dynamic single-lane transportation environment. We ﬁrst address TSP in a transportation spot market with stochastic but balanced or ‘‘symmetric’’ demand and supply. A periodic sealed double auction (PSDA) is proposed for TSP. Using a packing approach that considers possible bids and/or asks in an integral manner, we then devise a modiﬁed PSDA (M-PSDA) to address TSP with ‘‘asymmetric’’ demand and supply. The paper "Efﬁcient intermodal transportation auctions for B2B e-commerce logistics with transaction costs" is among the ﬁrst to consider transaction costs into auctions, proposing efﬁcient intermodal transportation auctions for the B2B e-commerce logistics problem (ELP). The paper "Auction-based transportation procurement in make-to-order systems" is one of the first integrating auction-based TSP and inventory, presenting an auction-based model for transportation service procurement (TSP) in make-to-order systems. The paper "Private parking slot sharing, Transportation" extends the auction mechanisms developed in this project to address the private parking slot sharing problem during regular working hours in a big city.

712513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
712513.value: Auction mechanisms are limited in providing operational decisions especially when more variables and factors are considered. It is desirable to explore the practicality of the proposed models for daily operational decision making. This is particular meaningful to recent commercial initiatives that are based on rudimentary theoretical models. During the process of this project, several business ventures have taken place across the world and many more companies are interested. Chuanghua Logistics in Zhejiang Province of Mainland China has merged its transportation service procurement businesses into its parental company listed on the stock market. GogoVan is a new business venture in Hong Kong by a group of young graduates. Our research provides theoretical foundation and proof for these new business models but not yet for daily operational decisions. At present, the consideration of time windows is inadequate. This also needs further investigation.

712513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
712513.value: This project is among the first attempt to study PERIODIC SEALED DOUBLE AUCTIONS (PSDA) for TSP (transportation service procurement ) in a dynamic setting. Under PSDA, buy and sell orders are accumulated during a specific time interval and wait for being cleared. All orders remain sealed until clearing time, and then the aggregated demand and supply are realized. We first addressed the TSP problem in a transportation market with stochastic but balanced or “symmetric” demand and supply. We proposed a basic PSDA model for TSP using insights from the well-known McAfee double auction. Under this PSDA, truthful bidding is a dominant strategy for each player (INCENTIVE COMPATIBILITY). We then considered more complex transportation marketplaces with simple less-than-truckload constraint, supply-demand imbalance, and mixed one-sided and double auction. Each of these extensions required a rigorous and precise treatment to determine the strategic-timing, dynamic pricing and allocation problems that the third-party auctioneer faces in a periodic double auction. To further simplify bidding strategy for each agent, we devised a novel PSDA to realize incentive compatibility. Meanwhile, each new PSDA led to ASYMPTOTIC EFFICIENCY. Therefore, the inefficiency loss under each auction mechanism compared with maximal social welfare is negligible when the market is sufficiently large. Moreover, the auctioneer’s revenue management policies were compared from both short-term and long-term points of view. Finally, the proposed models were tested and evaluated within collaborators' industrial context.

712713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
712713.value: The fact that grain boundaries act as a barrier for dislocation glide has been used as a traditional strengthening mechanism for metals according to the Hall-Petch relation. Recently, another strengthening mechanism employing coherent twin boundaries as obstacles for dislocation glide has attracted tremendous attention due to the discovery of nanotwinned Cu. The extraordinary feature of nanotwinned Cu is that it possesses simultaneously high strength and high ductility. This is due to the fact that coherent twin boundaries are different to grain boundaries as they act not only as barriers but also as slip planes for dislocation glide. Besides nanotwinned Cu, recent exploratory experiments have shown that some austenitic alloys containing intensive nanotwins also possess extremely high strength and high ductility. Unlike nanotwinned Cu which is fabricated by electrodeposition, nanotwinned austenitic alloys are produced by a simpler processing route (i.e. cold rolling followed by a recovery heat treatment), which is commonly used in the current metal industry. No additional facilities are required for the metal industry to produce such nanotwinned alloys, which make them potential engineering alloys for realistic industrial applications. The present project proposes to study in detail these nanotwinned alloys, with particular focus on the fundamental understanding of their processing-microstructure and microstructure-properties relationships. These relationships are currently not well understood. To achieve understanding of the processing-microstructure relationship, the following four experimental and modelling tasks will be performed: (1) investigation of thermal stability of nanotwins, (2) study of the effect of cold rolling reduction on the average nanotwin spacing, (3) study of dislocation annihilation kinetics during recovery heat treatment, and (4) construction of a Time-Temperature-Transformation (TTT) diagram of carbide formation as carbides can reduce the ductility and may be formed during recovery heat treatment. For the fundamental understanding of the microstructure-properties relationship, the following three important topics will be studied: (1) quantification of the relationship between yield stress and nanotwin spacing, (2) simulation of the macroscopic stress-strain behaviour, and (3) investigation of the strain rate sensitivity. It is hoped that the fundamental understanding of processing-microstructure and microstructure-properties relationships gained from the proposed project will help industry to design nanotwinned alloys with optimum mechanical properties for structural applications in the near future. 晶界可以阻礙位錯的運動，所以傳統上金屬材料的強度可以通過晶粒細化來實現，正如Hall-Petch關系所描述的那樣。但是，除了晶界以外，共格的孿晶界也可以阻礙位錯的運動。最近由於納米孿晶銅的發現，納米孿晶作為強化機制得到材料學界很大的重視。納米孿晶銅之所以能同時具有很高的強度以及很好的韌性，主要是因為納米孿晶界既可以阻礙位錯的滑移也可以為位錯提供另外的滑移體系。 除了納米孿晶銅以外，最近的實驗也發現了含有大量納米孿晶的奧氏體合金也同時具有很高的強度和很好的韌性。納米孿晶銅采用化學電鍍方法來制備。與納米孿晶銅不同的是，納米孿晶奧氏體合金可以通過常見的工業方法來制備，即冷軋和回火熱處理工藝。這種簡單的工藝可以確保金屬工業界在不增加設備的前提下，利用現有設備就可以制備出納米孿晶合金。這樣可以使這種納米孿晶合金容易得到廣泛的應用。 本項目擬研究納米孿晶合金的工藝與微觀結構之間的關系以及微觀結構與力學性能之間的關系。目前對這兩個關系的理解還不是很深入，需要更多的基礎研究。為了深入理解工藝與微觀結構之間的關系，本項目擬進行以下四個實驗及模型工作： （1）研究納米孿晶的熱穩定性；（2）研究冷軋量對納米孿晶平均間距的影響；（3）研究在回火處理過程中位錯湮滅的動力學；（4）創建碳化物形成的TTT圖，因為碳化物的形成會降低納米孿晶合金的韌性。對於微觀結構與力學性能之間關系的研究，本項目將側重以下三個方面：（1）定量分析屈服應力與納米孿晶間距的關系；（2）模擬拉伸應力－應變曲線；（3）研究應變率的敏感性。 本項目希望通過深入研究工藝與微觀結構之間的關系以及微觀結構與力學性能之間的關系，在不久的將來可以指導工業界設計出最佳的工藝，以便制備出具有最佳的機械性能的納米孿晶合金。

712713.label: Realisation of objectives
712713.value: For objective 1, different heat treatments at various temperatures and duration have been carried out for nanotwinned steels, leading to various microstructure. Recovery, partial recrystallization and full recrystallization conditions are fully investigated. In addition, the evolution of twins and dislocations during recovery heat treatment is thorough investigated. Both modelling and experimental works are carried out to understand the processing-microstructure relationship. Therefore, this objective has been achieved. For objective 2, evolution of dislocations and twins of nanotiwnnned steels has been investigated for quasi-static and high strain rate deformation. A physical model is proposed to predict the evolution of the dislocations and twins as well as the stress-strain relation. Therefore, this objective has been achieved.

712713.label: Major findings and research outcome
712713.value: 1. Strain rate sensitivity and evolution of dislocations and twins in a twinning-induced plasticity steel are investigated. Details are described in Output No. 1 and No. 5. 2. Evolution of dislocations and twins of the nanotwinned steel during quasi-static deformation are investigated. Details are described in Output No. 10. 3. Microstructural Evolution of a Nanotwinned Steel under Extremely High-strain-rate Deformation are investigated. Details are described in Output N0. 19. 4. The recovery and recrystallization kinetics of the nanotwinned steel are investigated. Details are described in the PhD thesis entitled “ Process – microstructure – property relations of nanotwinned steels” In summary, 25 Journal papers partially supported by this project have been published in Science, Acta Materialia, JMPS, Scripta Materialia etc. This project also leads to a PhD thesis entitled "Process – microstructure – property relations of nanotwinned steels".

712713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
712713.value: Nanotwinned steels are a new class of ultrahigh strength steels with excellent ductility. The present project investigated in detail these nanotwinned steels, with particular focus on the fundamental understanding of their processing-microstructure and microstructure-properties relationships. To achieve understanding of the processing-microstructure relationship, experimental and modelling works have been carried out to investigate (1) thermal stability of nanotwins and (2) the recovery and recrystallization kinetics. For the fundamental understanding of the microstructure-properties relationship, experimental and modelling works have been carried out to investigate: (1) the evolution of dislocation and twins at quasi-static and high strain rate loading conditions, and (2) simulation of the macroscopic stress-strain behaviour. The fundamental understanding of processing-microstructure and microstructure-properties relationships gained from the proposed project will help industry to design nanotwinned steels with optimum mechanical properties for structural applications in the near future.

712913.label: Realisation of objectives
712913.value: The objectives of this project have been met with some conceptual breakthroughs in wireless power transfer (WPT) research. The research outcomes are published in 5 journal papers in top IEEE Transactions. We have successfully developed a fast parameter identification method (Objective-1) and used such method for input power control in a WPT system without wireless load power feedback (Objective-2) as reported in Paper #2. For objective-3, we have developed new multi-frequency WPT with multiple loads as reported in Paper #4 and Paper #5. In the process of this research project, we have gladly pioneered the new concept of Maximum Energy Efficiency Tracking method. Paper #3 on this new breakthrough has been awarded the 1st Place IEEE Transactions Prize Paper Award. Also, we laid down the principle on how to make a 3-coil WPT system more efficient than a 2-coil system for WPT applications with extended transmission distance. We also laid down the methodology to ensure a 3-coil WPT system can be more efficient than a 2-coil one (Paper #1).

712913.label: Major findings and research outcome
712913.value: The major outcomes of this project are recorded in 5 IEEE Transactions papers. Paper 1 reports, for the first time, the design criteria under which a 3-coil WPT system can be more than a 2-coil one. The idea is to reduce the conducting power losses in the transmitter circuit and coil by using a relay coil resonator to enlarge the current (and thus magnetic flux). In this way, a large current occurs in the relay coil-resonator while the current (and its associated conducting losses) in the transmitter circuit and coil can be reduced. This idea paves the way for the Qi standard to extend the transmission distance. Paper 2 summaries the parameter identification method and a power flow control method for WPT systems without using wireless feedback from the receiver side. By using mathematical manipulation, we proved that the load conditions can be obtained from the current and voltage information on the transmitter side. Consequently, all control variables can be obtained from the transmitter side of the WPT system. Paper 3 is a major breakthrough because this is the first paper reporting a novel concept of Maximum Energy Efficiency Tracking for WPT. This paper won the 1st Place IEEE Transactions Prize Paper Award from the IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics (which is the top journal in WPT with an impact factor of 7.0). Paper 4 reports several new resonator-topologies that allow power flow in WPT systems at multiple frequency. This invention provides selective power flow to be directed to different loads through the same WPT structure by using frequency control. Paper 5 extends previous WPT work by enabling transmitter-side control (i.e. without using wireless feedbacks from the load side) for WPT systems with multiple loads.

712913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
712913.value: The maximum energy efficiency tracking principle reported in Paper 3 has become a hot topic, which has triggered a new series of WPT research. In principle, this idea is analogous to the Maximum Power Point Tracking in a Photovoltaic system or a wind power generator. It is envisaged that this new principle will be adopted in all future WPT products.

712913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
712913.value: In this project, the we have achieved both major conceptual and technological advancements in wireless power transfer. They have pioneered the new concept of Maximum Energy Efficiency Tracking principle, which is expected to become a "must-have" technology in future WPT systems. We have also laid down new principle that allows a 3-coil WPT system to be more energy-efficient than a 2-coil one. This concept has been adopted by industry to meet the new Qi standard with extended transmission distance. We also developed new transmitter-side control methods which do not need any wireless feedback from the receiver side, consequently reducing circuit complexity and costs for the WPT industry.
