713713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
713713.value: Dynamic systems in engineering are constantly subject to the influence of external disturbances that may drive the state trajectory of a control system into undesired regions, and even result in destructive effects. One of the prime objectives of control engineers is to assess the level of these influences and provide measures to reduce or eliminate them. Over the past decades, several performance-based approaches such as H-infinity control and dissipative control have been developed to attenuate the adverse effects of energy-bounded external disturbances. However, these approaches have paid little attention to the regions that the system states remain in under the effects of the bounded external disturbances. This has inspired researchers to develop approaches for estimating the reachable set of systems with bounded external disturbances. However, their theories are far from complete, especially in the field of time-lag systems. The proposed project will study the reachable set estimation problem for a variety of time-lag systems with bounded disturbances, including retarded and neutral types of linear systems, stochastic systems, and T-S fuzzy systems. The time lags may take the form of discrete and distributed delays, which are either constant or time-varying. An ellipsoidal technique will be developed to estimate the reachable set; that is, an ellipsoid will be determined such that it contains all the system states in the presence of bounded disturbances. Delay-dependent and delay-rate-dependent conditions for the existence of desired ellipsoids will be derived. To reduce the conservatism of the derived conditions, novel techniques to optimize the obtained ellipsoids will be proposed. Fundamental techniques and theories will be developed on estimation using polyhedrons. Apart from the estimation problem, this project will also investigate synthesis issues for various time-lag systems with reachable set specifications. Research efforts will be devoted to designing controllers such that the reachable set of the resulting closed-loop system is contained in some prescribed connected region and/or outside of certain regions. These synthesis problems, which have not been solved to date, have strong potential applications in engineering. This project aims to provide a systematic theory for studying reachable set synthesis. Such theories will be useful for the robustness study of control systems against bounded external disturbances. They would also be applicable for constrained controller design, parameter estimation and multi-agent task planning. The obtained results will considerably narrow the gaps between theories and applications, and offer more powerful control systems with higher robustness and reliability.

713713.label: Realisation of objectives
713713.value: All the objectives have been achieved. The details are listed below. In the development of techniques, we have focused on various classes of dynamic systems. For bounded disturbance inputs (unit-energy bounded or unit-peak bounded), the Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional approach is used for establishing delay-dependent reachable set estimating conditions for systems with distributed delays. These conditions guarantee the existence of an ellipsoid that contains the system state under zero initial conditions. Based on these results, the problem of how to design a controller such that the state of the resulting closed-loop system is contained in a prescribed ellipsoid has been studied. For systems with discrete delay and time-varying polytopic uncertainties, delay-dependent and delay-rate-depended conditions have been obtained. The uncertain parameters are differentiable and their derivatives are bounded by known scalars, parameter-rate-dependent conditions for the existence of a desired ellipsoid are derived by using a parameter-dependent Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional. The reachable set estimation is taken into account in the controller design. The purpose is to determine an ellipsoid and find a state-feedback controller such that the determined ellipsoid contains the reachable set of the resulting closed-loop system. Sufficient conditions for the solvability of the control synthesis problem are obtained in terms of linear matrix inequalities. Based on these results, the problem of how to design a controller such that the state of the resulting closed-loop system is contained in a prescribed ellipsoid is studied. By introducing the non-uniform delay-partitioning method and the triple integral technique, an improved reachable set estimation condition is proposed. The reachable set estimation problem for discrete-time linear systems with multiple constant delays and bounded peak inputs has been studied. Delay-dependent conditions for the solvability of the addressed problem are derived by employing a novel Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional. The obtained conditions are expressed in terms of matrix inequalities, which are linear when only one scalar variable is fixed. On the basis of these conditions, an ellipsoid containing the reachable set of the considered system is obtained. On the other research front, the reachable set estimation problem of singular systems has been investigated. Based on the Lyapunov method, a sufficient condition has been established in terms of a linear matrix inequality to guarantee that the reachable set of singular system is bounded by the intersection of ellipsoids. Then the result is extended to the problem for singular systems with time-varying delay by utilizing the reciprocally convex approach. A very general relaxation technique has been developed for obtaining passivity conditions related to neural networks with time-varying delays. The main improvement is the non-requirement of all the symmetric matrices involved in the employed quadratic Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional to be positive definite. Such a technique is valuable for all reachable set estimation approaches involving systems with delays, it can reduce the conservatism of the results for a variety of estimating and synthesis problems for delay systems. The technique has been applied to the stability analysis of distributed delay neural networks. Using this technique and two kinds of integral inequalities, global asymptotic stability conditions have been established, and further improvement is obtained by applying the delay partitioning technique. Another technique for singular systems has also been developed. The characterization problems of robust admissibility and admissibilization for uncertain discrete-time singular system with interval time-varying delay have been tackled. A new comparison model is introduced to transform the original singular system into two connected subsystems. After this transformation, a singular system without uncertainty and delay can be handled by the Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional method. By virtue of the scaled small gain theorem, an admissibility condition of the original singular system is proposed in terms of linear matrix inequalities. Moreover, the problem of robust admissibilization of uncertain discrete singular time-varying system has been achieved by iterative linear matrix inequality algorithm with initial condition optimization. These techniques are useful for other problems studied in this project. The problems of reachable set estimation and state-feedback controller design for discrete-time switched linear systems under bounded peak disturbances have been fully investigated. For the reachable set estimation problem, a Lyapunov-based inequality is developed based on the multiple Lyapunov strategy. Appropriate Lyapunov functions are used to obtain the ellipsoidal reachable set estimation conditions of discrete-time switched linear systems. In order to make the estimated ellipsoids as small as possible, three optimization approaches are proposed. Specifically, the Genetic Algorithm is used to search for the optimal parameters satisfying the obtained reachable set estimation conditions. In addition, the state-feedback controller design problem for discrete-time switched linear systems is considered. The function of the controller is to manipulate the reachable set of the closed-loop system to lie within a given ellipsoid or make the reachable set small. The project has further investigated the reachable set estimation problem for positive linear time-invariant systems with constant coefficients and specific exogenous disturbance. In particular, the problem of finding a hyper-pyramid to bound the set of the states that are reachable from the origin in the Euclidean space has been addressed, subject to inputs whose (1, 1)-norm, (∞, 1)-norm or (∞, ∞)-norm is bounded by a prescribed constant. The Lyapunov approach is applied and a bounding hyper-pyramid is obtained by solving a set of inequalities. Iterative procedures (with an adjustable parameter) for reducing the hyper-volume of the bounding hyper-pyramid for the reachable set have been proposed. Moreover, the case when systems exhibit periodic behavior has been studied under bounded peak disturbances. This is achieved by employing the lifting approach and the pseudo-periodic Lyapunov function approach. The periodic system is transformed into several time-invariant systems, the bounding ellipsoids are determined through the transformed time-invariant systems. By applying the pseudo-periodic Lyapunov function approach, the bounding ellipsoids are determined through the original periodic system directly. Genetic Algorithm is adopted in the pseudo-periodic Lyapunov function approach to search for the optimal value of the decision variables. Moreover, based on the reachable set estimation results, state-feedback controllers are designed for manipulating the reachable set. Finally, numerical examples are presented to verify the effectiveness of the theoretical findings.

713713.label: Major findings and research outcome
713713.value: For reachable set estimation problem under unit-energy or unit-peak disturbances, the project has developed theoretical and computational solutions for distributed delay systems using Lyapunov-Krasovskii approach and delay-partitioning techniques. Delay-dependent reachable set estimation results in the form of bounding ellipsoid are obtained in [1] with the corresponding state-feedback controller synthesized for the resulting reachable set prescribed with a given ellipsoid. For discrete-time systems with multiple delays, the corresponding reachable set estimation conditions in the form of matrix inequalities which are linear when fixing only one scalar are obtained [4]. Generalization to systems with polytopic parameter uncertainties is provided. An important aspect of the technical development relies on some relaxation techniques aiming at reducing the conservatism in the Lyapunov-Krasovskii approach. The main advancement comes from the removal of the positive definiteness requirement in some of the matrices appearing in the quadratic functional which is developed and used in [2] for passivity analysis and [6] for stability analysis. Further improvement is provided for systems with delay under bounded peak inputs and time-varying polytopic uncertainties, and delay-rate-dependent results have been established [8]. A different technique based on non-uniform delay-partitioning and triple integral technique has provided improved reachable set estimation condition and state-feedback synthesis condition using linear matrix inequalities [3]. For the first time, reachable set estimation problems have been studied for singular systems. A linear matrix inequality condition is developed for bounding the reachable set by the intersection of multiple ellipsoids [5]. The results are generalized to singular systems with time-varying delay. During the study of singular systems, results on robust admissibility and admissibilization for uncertain discrete-time singular systems have been characterized using the scaled small gain theorem [10]. Further developments include a number of important classes of dynamic systems. For switched systems, a Lyapunov-based inequality has been developed based on a multiple Lyapunov strategy, and three optimization approaches have been proposed to make the reachable set estimating ellipsoids as small as possible [7]. The reachable set estimation problem for discrete-time periodic system using the lifting approach and a pseudo-periodic Lyapunov function has been proposed, so that the bounding ellipsoids can be determined through the transformed time-invariant systems [9]. Finally, for the first time, the problem of finding hyper-pyramid to bound the reachable set involving positive linear systems has been successfully tackled for inputs whose (1, 1)-norm, (∞, 1)-norm or (∞, ∞)-norm is bounded by a prescribed constant [11].

713713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
713713.value: Amongst the many potential applications and extensions of the results developed in the project, there are two areas where the results can be further developed (a) The problem of reachable set estimation for discrete-time switched positive systems under different classes of exogeneous disturbance can be considered. The multiple linear copositive Lyapunov function approach may be applied to determine the bounding hyper-pyramids for the reachable set. Based on some Lyapunov-based inequalities and the linear version of the S-procedure technique, the bounding hyper-pyramids for the reachable set can be determined by solving a set of inequalities. (b) The problems of reachable set estimation for dynamic systems with time-varying delay and random delay. The switched systems approach, which is different from the traditional Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional method, may be adopted to study the reachable set estimation problem for time-varying delay systems. Through augmentation, time-varying delay systems can be transformed into switched delay-free systems. The reachable set of a time-varying delay system may be estimated based on its corresponding augmented switched system.

713713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
713713.value: Dynamic systems in engineering are constantly subject to the influence of external disturbances that may drive the state trajectory of a control system into undesired regions, and even result in destructive effects. One of the prime objectives of control engineers is to assess the level of these influences and provide measures to reduce or eliminate them. Over the past decades, performance-based approaches such as H-infinity control and dissipative control have been developed to attenuate the adverse effects of energy-bounded external disturbances without paying attention to the regions that the system states remain in under the effects of the bounded external disturbances. In this project, we have developed techniques for estimating the reachable sets, in ellipsoidal or hyper-pyramidal form, of various classes of linear systems. These include time-lag systems in continuous and discrete time having retarded and distributed delays, singular systems, switched systems, and periodic systems. Improved Lyapunov-Krasovskii techniques have been developed which can significantly reduce the conservatism of the derived results. These techniques have much broader applications beyond the problems within this project. Moreover, the corresponding reachable set synthesis problems using state-feedback and observer-state-feedback techniques to design or enhance the reachable set in the closed loop have been provided.

713813.label: Project Objectives
713813.value: To identify cases of strong dynamic interference phenomena between two neighbouring tall buildings leading to large magnifications of across-wind and along-wind excitation forces on the buildings. 713813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
713813.value: A tall building is usually mildly flexible and wind-induced dynamic wind loads and building responses are crucial factors in its design. Wind engineers are aware of these dynamic wind excitations in the across-wind, along-wind and torsional directions but there has not been a comprehensive flow field investigation aiming at a physical understanding of the excitation mechanisms of these fluctuating wind forces from the wind flow field. Furthermore in an urban setting, a tall building rarely exists in an isolated single building situation. It is very common to find a tall building surrounded by other buildings in its vicinity. Dynamic wind effects on the building are known to be affected and modified by presence of neighbouring buildings. This “dynamic interference effect” can lead to large increase in the along-wind or across-wind excitations on a tall building. There have been numerous wind tunnel investigations on building interference and in most of them, wind loads were measured on a tall building model being placed in different arrangements of surrounding buildings. A lot of useful data and design information have been obtained from these studies for many building geometries and arrangement patterns. However, the set of possible variables of these and other parameters in a real-life urban environment is too large to be covered exhaustively. Thus, a more physically-based approach to the dynamic interference problem would be an investigation on the underlying excitation mechanisms of wind load modification due to interference. This understanding will help building designers avoid or mitigate undesirable wind-induced dynamic interference phenomena on the fluctuating wind excitations of a tall building. Wind effects on a tall building are consequences of the wind flow pattern around the building and the resulting wind-induced pressure and forces on different building faces. Thus, this project proposes to make simultaneous measurements of the fluctuating wind forces on a tall building model under building interference from another tall building in the vicinity, concurrent with measurements of wind flow patterns around the two buildings. The aim is to understand how the interfering building changes the turbulent characteristics of wind flow reaching the subject tall building and subsequently modify the generation of fluctuating wind pressures and dynamic wind loads on the building. Investigations will be made on a number of dynamic interference phenomena leading to strong magnifications of the across-wind and along-wind forces on the building. 高層建築通常表現出一定的彈性，導致風荷載以及其風致效應成為高層建築設計中的關鍵要素之一。風工程師們對於橫風向、順風向以及扭轉方向的動態風荷載的應激響應已經有了一定的認識，但是對於脈動風與風場之間的應激響應關係仍然缺乏一個全面的理解。 此外，在城市中，高層建築很少以單個的形式存在于周圍環境。通常一座高層建築周圍總是存在一些其他建築。高層建築的動態風效應會被其周圍存在的建築影響和改變。因此這種建築之間的“動態相干關係”會導致順風向和橫風向的風荷載的增加。 在結構的相干效應方面，已經有了許多風洞實驗研究。其中的大部分，目標高層建築都是在周圍建築不同的佈局下，進行風荷載測量。對於不同的幾何尺度和佈局模式下的高層建築，這些研究已經獲得了相當多有效的數據和設計信息。然而在現實生活中上，所有這些可能的參數的設定變化太多以至於很難全面概括。因此在這種相干現象中潛藏的風荷載應激效應研究將會帶來對於該問題的更加基於物理本質的理解。這將幫助結構設計者避免或者緩和那些不良的風致效應。 高層建築的風致效應是建築周圍流場導致的建築不同表面的風壓、風力相互作用的結果。因此，本項目將同時測量在一棟高層建築干擾下的目標建築的脈動風和這兩棟建築周圍的流場。其目的在於瞭解當風經過干擾建築到達目標建築之後，風場的湍流特性是如何變化的以及最終是如何影響結構脈動風壓和風荷載的變化。本研究將基於多個導致橫風向和順風向風力產生顯著變化的動態相干現象而展開。

713813.label: Realisation of objectives
713813.value: The three project objectives regarding generation mechanisms of dynamic wind loads on a tall building and excitation mechanism of interference between two tall buildings have been accomplished through extensive experiments in the boundary layer wind tunnel of Department of Civil Engineering, HKU. In Year 1, wind tunnel tests were performed at a geometric scale of 1:1000 due to limitations of the PIV setup. Interference studies using this scale were rarely reported in the literature and therefore interference effects were measured for two tall buildings arranged on a dense grid of 222 relative locations using both high-frequency force-balance and pressure scanning. The interference results are found similar to past studies using a larger geometric scale of 1:300 or 1:400, thus supporting future investigations using the smaller-scale building models. Towards project objective (1), the staggered and near-tandem building locations are identified for strong magnification of the dynamic across- and along-wind loads, respectively. During Year 0.5-1.5, efforts were made to overcome the difficulties encountered in synchronizing the PIV and pressure measurements from two different equipment systems. After extensive trials, concurrent measurement was achieved by synchronizing PIV acquisition and pressure scanning using the first firing instant of the double laser pulses. Thereafter, towards objective (2), numerous wind tunnel experiments with PIV and pressure scanning were carried out on the tall building model of dimensions, in metre, (B:D:H) = (0.03:0.03:0.18) and several other building models of different shapes. Large-scale flow structures were identified in the building wake and their roles on the velocity-pressure-force relations for along- and across-wind dynamic building force generation are investigated using spatio-temporal identification techniques including conditional sampling, phase averaging, and proper orthogonal decomposition (POD). In Years 2-3, synchronized pressure and wind field measurements were conducted for two tall buildings under interference. Measurements were made at 41 relative building locations covering the tandem, side-by-side and staggered arrangements. Detailed analysis of wind flow fields and their roles on force generation on the principal tall downstream building were made for the critical locations of strong interference of across-wind and along-wind forces. Coherent flow signatures responsible for these strong magnifications of dynamic wind forces were identified by the conditional sampling and phase-averaging techniques. For across-wind interference, a synchronization process among several quasi-periodic aerodynamic phenomena is found as the underlying mechanism and several interference regimes of staggered arrangement were proposed. For this objective (3), excitation mechanisms have been revealed for the interference of both across-wind and along-wind forces.

713813.label: Major findings and research outcome
713813.value: The project successfully unveil the excitation mechanisms for dynamic along-wind and across-wind forces on an isolated tall building and two interfering tall buildings in proximity. This is achieved through extensive wind tunnel experiments in which simultaneous data of building pressures and turbulent wind fields by PIV are obtained and analyzed in details. For an isolated building, instantaneous wind flow patterns and synchronized wind pressure distributions support the role of quasi-periodic vortex shedding in producing across-wind fluctuations on the building. On the vertical plane, fluctuating along-wind forces are related to the features of recirculating flow near the leeward wall. Conditional sampling results show a clear relationship between peak along-wind forces and speeds of flow approaching the building and size and location of the large recirculating vortex in the upper part of building wake (see conference paper [C2]). For the quasi-periodic across-wind excitation, the phase averaging technique reveals distinct vortex shedding from the building for most of the time, which exhibits evident phase relationship with the across-wind forces (journal paper [J4]). Dominant patterns of wind pressures and building wakes are extracted by POD analysis [J5 J6]). For two tall buildings under interference, the use of building models at geometry scale 1:1000 is validated by comparison with other studies using larger geometry scales, thus supporting future investigations using the smaller-scale building models [J1]. In the interference mechanism of two tall buildings in near-tandem arrangement, the magnitudes of mean and fluctuating along-wind force on the downstream building is found highly correlated to the characteristics of the approaching flow affected by the upstream building [J1]. In the staggered building arrangement, strong magnification of the fluctuating across-wind force occurs on the downstream building. Instantaneous PIV and building pressure results identify a synchronization process among a number of quasi-periodic aerodynamic phenomena as the excitation mechanism which is further confirmed by phase averaging analysis. In particular, the longitudinal building separation determines an in-phase relationship between the sideway oscillation of the upstream building wake and vortex development on the downstream building. Several staggered arrangement regions are proposed for different across-wind interference mechanisms [J2, J3]. The related problem of shielding effect from a group of upstream medium-rise buildings to a tall building is also investigated. The degree of shielding is found to be governed by the combinations of several arrangement parameters of the sheltering buildings and multiple regression empirical equations are proposed to predict the shielding effect [J7].

713813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
713813.value: The project unveils the excitation mechanisms of dynamic wind forces on an isolated tall building and two tall buildings under interference. For the across-wind force, quasi-periodic vortex shedding from the building is found as the main excitation cause and presence of an upstream building can enhance the vortex shedding through synchronization swaying of the approaching streamlines. Future confirmation studies are worth making in which the synchronization process is disturbed, say, by placing a third building or a splitter structure in between. The effect of slenderness, i.e., height-to-breadth, of the tall building is also worth investigating as it has strong influence on the periodicity and strength of vortex shedding. For the along-wind force, a complete understanding of the roles of other dominant flow structures has not been fully obtained. The along-wind force results from forces on the windward and leeward building walls and it is worth studying the possibly distinct excitation mechanisms for the forces on the two walls. In addition to wind tunnel experiments, computational wind engineering approach using large eddy simulation can be used to study the same flow. It has the advantage of obtaining complete three-dimensional flow information.

713813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
713813.value: Wind effects are important for the structural safety and serviceability of tall buildings. However, there is not yet a comprehensive understanding of the excitation mechanisms of dynamic wind forces from the turbulent wind flow field past the building. Moreover, it is common to find a tall building surrounded by other buildings in its vicinity. In this situation, building interference occurs and wind forces on the building are modified by presence of surrounding buildings. This project explores how the instantaneous wind flow around a tall building causes dynamic wind forces on the building in the along-wind and across-wind directions. The excitation mechanisms for strong magnifications of wind forces on two tall buildings under interference are also investigated. The project is based on extensive measurements of fluctuating pressures on building models in a wind tunnel together with concurrent measurement of instantaneous wind flow fields using the technique of particle-image velocimetry. For the across-wind forces, quasi-steady vortex shedding from the tall building is found as the main excitation mechanism. For two buildings in staggered arrangement, vortex shedding from the downstream building is found to be enhanced by a synchronization of swaying of upstream building wake, thus causing strong magnification of across-wind forces.

714313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
714313.value: 通過開發清潔能源以解決當今緊迫的能源與環境問題近年來在全球範圍內被廣泛地關注和研究。本項目作為這些研究工作的一部分，將利用微流體技術的優勢，開發出新一代具有高能量密度的鋁- 空氣電池。 鋁化學有望取代傳統電池技術以滿足便攜式電子系統不斷增長的電源容量需求。鋁除了具備資源豐富，可回收及成本低的優勢外，相比其他常見能源載體，它擁有最高的體積能量密度，這使得鋁成為便攜式能源載體的不二選擇。鋁-空氣電池以空氣中的氧為氧化劑，將鋁陽極中的化學能轉換為可以直接使用電能，是一種清潔、高效的鋁能量轉換方式。而微流動體係與傳統流動體系相比能提供更高效的傳熱傳質過程，更大的表體比和簡單的結構，因此更具優勢。微流動作為一種極具潛質的新興技術，有望被用於控制和強化化學/電化學反應。本項目將結合微流動和鋁化學的優勢，開發新型微流動鋁-空氣電池平台，突破現有的電池容量限制。 本項目提出基於對沖混沌流微流動平台和酸鹼混合電解質的鋁-空氣電池這一新概念。這個新體系的可逆電位將比常規鋁-空氣電池高34%， 同時滿足低成本和產物可回收的條件。本項目側重於基礎研究(即新體系中的電化學，流動和傳輸過程)，將從微觀和系統不同層面上對電池進行表徵。在微觀層面上，我們將結合光學觀測，電化學測試和有限體積法模擬對電池的傳輸/反應方式進行表徵，並氂清電池性能的決定因素。電池的整體性能將通過製造的系統模型測出。為便於未來的產品化或商品化，基於數學模型的參數研究也將進行，用於優化電池的工作條件和幾何參數以實現最佳的輸出功率。 這項研究不僅有助於解決微電子應用中的能源挑戰，同時也可通過將數個電池單元疊加到一起來滿足大型應用的需求。此外，研究所得的知識也將給微流動電化學帶來啟發。微流動電化學是一個前沿的、多學科交叉領域，在能量轉換，微機電系統，化學合成和生物研究中有十分廣泛的應用。

714313.label: Realisation of objectives
714313.value: Realisation of objective 1: A new concept of mixed pH-media aluminum-air cells with increased open circuit potential and power density based on microfluidic technology has been verified. The cell employs a co-laminar flow configuration so as to eliminate the necessity of a membrane as in a PEM fuel cell. The result shows that, compared with a single-alkaline-electrolyte cell, a dual-electrolyte cell has a significant advantage of higher open-circuit potentials (37.5% higher) and has superior performance with a peak power density twice that of the values obtained from its single alkaline electrolyte counterpart. More details of the above finding can be found in the publication Chen et al. 2017 (see Part C). Realisation of objective 2: New phenomena under microfluidic conditions were explored, this include the membraneless operation using an inorganic/organic hybrid electrolyte and their electrochemical impedance (EIS) characteristics. EIS technique was incorporated to investigate the full fuel cell performance. More details of the above findings can be found in Chen et al. 2016a and b in Part C. Realisation of objective 3: A numerical model was developed that successfully coupled the microfluidic hydrodynamics, species transport in the flowing electrolyte, and electrochemical reaction kinetics on the electrodes’ surface for predicting the counter-flow microfluidic cell (MFC) performance, which also considered the effect of fuel crossover under low flow rate operation mode. The model was validated with experimental result conducted. Primary conclusions are summarized as follow: A. The counter-flow MFC is found to suffer an inherent disadvantage on its power output ability, whose peak power density is only half of that of the co-flow MFC. This is mainly attributed to the uneven ionic resistance across its electrode surface. Therefore, shorter and wider electrodes (that is, smaller aspect ratio) are more suitable for the counter-flow cell rather than longer and narrower electrodes. B. The counter-flow MFC achieves a much higher tolerance to extremely low flow rates than the co-flow MFC. C. When the concentration of cross-over fuel at cathode surface is stipulated to be less than 10 mM, the counter-flow cell can utilize a 15 times lower electrolyte flow rate and obtain a 6 times higher fuel utilization. This superiority in fuel utilization and energy density makes the counter-flow cell more competitive for practical applications, which is attributed to its special flow configuration in which the diffusive fuel crossover is impeded by the convective electrolyte flow. Detailed description of the model and the findings can be found in Wang et al. 2015 and Wang et al. 2017 in Part C; Realisation of objective 4: New devices were developed and evaluated their performance: - A system that utilizes low-cost materials (secondary Al and carbon paper) for energy production and collects the H2 generated from the parasitic corrosion of Al. this system eliminates the use of super pure Al alloys or corrosion inhibitors to overcome the low utilization efficiency problem. The fluidic electrolyte helps to refresh reaction materials, and flush away the produced aluminum hydroxide, avoiding precipitation or gelling of electrolyte. The mechanically rechargeable cell structure allows replacement of new Al anode once consumed. The product in the waste electrolyte can be recycled to produce industrial grade Al. - A novel Al-feed MFC stack for small-power applications with individual cell designed to share the same electrolyte flow in sequence, while the exit flow from the last cell was further utilized for H2 generation via the Al-H2O reaction. The complex electrolyte distribution and effluent management subsystems were both eliminated, resulting in a much simpler, more practical, and very cost-efficient MFC stack system. Peak power of 531mW and short-circuit current of 248mA were achievable with 2M NaOH as electrolyte and at a relatively small flow rate of 100μlmin-1. The energy density was calculated to be 1kWhkg-1(Al) based on the continuous discharge tests. This stack can be fed directly with daily low-cost Al sources, such as kitchen foil or soft drink can, and can be passively operated without a pump. More details of the above two new systems can be found in Wang & Leung 2016 and Chen & Leung 2016 in Part C.

714313.label: Major findings and research outcome
714313.value: • a novel dual-electrolyte membraneless Al–air cell (built on a Y-shape microfluidic platform) was developed that can achieve higher cell voltage and power output than its single alkaline counterpart. The cell employs a co-laminar flow configuration so as to eliminate the necessity of a membrane as in a PEM fuel cell. The result shows that, compared with a single-alkaline-electrolyte cell, a dual-electrolyte cell has a significant advantage of higher open-circuit potentials (37.5% higher) and has superior performance with a peak power density twice that of the values obtained from its single alkaline electrolyte counterpart. The cell can achieve a power density as high as 216mWcm-2 with a channel thickness of 0.3 mm. • The influences of electrolyte concentration and water content on cell performances were established and the reaction mechanisms of Al in KOH methanol-based solution were proposed. The capacity tests showed that the self-corrosion of Al can be effectively inhibited by using KOH methanol-based solution as anolyte. Under this operation, the Al-air cell achieved a high specific capacity with low cost commercial Al foil. The highest specific capacity of 2507 mAh g-1 was achieved (84.1% of the theoretical value), which is among the highest values achieved to date. • EIS analysis on full Al-air cell was conducted for the first time. The equivalent circuit model was validated against experimental results. Through the impedance fitting results, different resistances were identified, which revealed the electrochemical losses on the cell performance. Multiplexing scaling up strategy to obtain higher cell power output can be done by combining this direct dimensional scale up method with porous electrode and cell stacks. • A new numerical model was developed that describes the governing processes in the microfluidic aluminum-air cell, which can explain the phenomena in the cell. The developed model successfully coupled the microfluidic hydrodynamics, species transport in the flowing electrolyte, and electrochemical reaction kinetics on the electrodes’ surface for predicting the MFC performance, and fuel crossover effect. This facilitates our fundamental understandings on the cell performance and allow us to optimize operational parameters of the aluminum cells. Based on the above findings new microfluidic aluminum-air cell devices were designed and their prototypes were fabricated and tested with the optimized design with suitable scaling and stacking. Excellent cell performances can be achieved with the novel scaling and stacking designs. The study generated 6 journal papers, 1 book chapter, 1 conference paper and 1 patent as detailed in Part C.

714313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
714313.value: In this study, we have proved different concepts of microfluidic Al-air cells and proposed new microfluidic platforms, which can also be beneficial to other microfluidic-related fields, such as patterning and T-sensors. We have conducted electrochemical testing to study their device-level performance and micro-scale processes within Al-air cells. Impedance analysis gives an in-depth understanding of the critical processes that govern the performance of cells. As we have already developed a numerical model, modeling analysis is recommended as the direction for future works. The modeling is going to give the theoretical explanation of the device-level performance and the influence of the factors such as electrolyte concentration. More underlying fundamentals, such as electrode kinetics, mass and charge transport and fluid-structure kinetics interaction are also needed to be analyzed. The model will serve as a time-efficient and low-cost toll to perform parametric analysis so as to optimize the design and operation of cells modified for different applications.

714313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
714313.value: This study proposed and proved a novel concept of a mixed pH media aluminum-air cell built on a microfluidic platform with streams of alkaline anolyte and acidic catholyte flowing separately without convective mixing. Due to the laminar flow characteristic, expensive membrane is not required. The proposed cell yields a reversible potential 34% higher than conventional aluminum-air cell designs, while the cell is of low cost and end-life recyclable. Major cell fundamentals, including electrochemistry, fluid flow and mass transport, have been studied and got understood. System-level performance tests have been conducted with cell prototypes. Enhanced performance of the cell has been demonstrated by scaling and stacking of multiple cells. A numerical model has been developed so that model-based parametric study can be carried out to facilitate future product development and commercialization, The study will not only contribute to tackle the power challenges in microelectronic applications, but also be beneficial to macro appliances whose energy requirements can be met by grouping a number of microfluidic cell units together. Moreover, the knowledge gained from the study will shed light on microfluidic electrochemistry, a cutting-edge interdisciplinary area with wide applications in energy conversion, micro-electromechanical systems, chemical production and biological researches.

714713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
714713.value: Mounting evidence suggests that neuron-extracellular matrix (ECM) and neuron-neuron adhesion are essential for processes like neurite outgrowth and the formation of synapses where information is exchanged between neural cells. Furthermore, recent studies have also indicated that impaired adhesion ability of neurons is related to many neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD). As such, a precise knowledge of how neural cells interact with each other or with the surrounding environment will not only be the key for our understanding of how nervous system and learning develop but may also shed light on finding ways to control or cure various diseases. Several important issues remain unsettled in the study of neural cells. First, almost all the previous experimental investigations on neuron adhesion are qualitative in nature, however, a method enabling quantitative characterization of neuron-ECM interactions is still lacking. Next, although it has been reported that AD can lead to disruption of cytoskeletal structure in neural cells and weaken their ability to adhere to the ECM, a connection between the mechanical and adhesion response of neurons and the progression of AD has not been established. In this project, we plan to conduct a combined experimental and modeling study to address these issues. Specifically, protocols will be developed to quantitatively characterize neuron-substrate adhesion by peeling neurite from the substrate with an atomic force microscope (AFM) probe while, simultaneously, monitoring the roles of various adhesion molecules with a total internal reflection fluorescence microscope (TIRFM). The method will then be used to systematically examine the response of AD-affected neurons. Data to be generated here in conjunction with subsequent theoretical modeling, taking into account realistic features that were neglected in previous studies, will allow us to establish a mapping between the progression of AD and the adhesion ability and mechanical properties of neural cells. If successful, this study could provide a solution to the long-standing problem of how to quantitatively measure neuron-ECM interactions while, simultaneously, monitor the roles of different adhesion molecules. Experimental and simulation results from this project will unambiguously confirm or refute our primary hypothesis that changes in the adhesion and mechanical response of neurons will be induced by the progression of Alzheimer’s disease and hence greatly enhance our understanding of this disorder. In addition, predictions and data obtained here can also be extremely valuable for the development of new methods to diagnose AD as well as evaluate the effectiveness of various treatments/drugs. 越来越多的证据表明，神经元细胞之间以及同胞外基质（ECM）的黏附是神经轴突的生长和神经元突触的形成所必不可少的。此外，最近的研究还表明，神经元粘附能力的丧失同许多神经疾病，例如阿尔茨海默氏病（AD），紧密相关。因此，准确的了解神经细胞之间以及同周围的环境的互动不仅是我们理解神经系统发展的关键，还有可能为找到治愈各种疾病的方法提供有用信息。 然而，几个在神经细胞研究中的重要问题仍未得到解决。首先，几乎所有已有的对于神经细胞黏附的研究都是定性的，我们仍然缺乏一个能对神经元同胞外基质之间相互作用进行定量表征的方法。此外，虽然已有研究表明阿尔茨海默氏病可以破坏神经细胞中的骨架结构以及削弱其同外界黏附的能力，此疾病的发展同这些现象具体的关联仍未建立。在本项目中，我们计划进行实验和模拟相结合的研究来解决这些问题。具体而言，我们将利用原子力显微镜（AFM）将粘附在基板上的神经突起剥离，从而定量地表征神经细胞同胞外基质的相互作用。在剥离同时，我们将运用全内反射萤光显微镜来监测各种粘附分子在此过程中的动态响应。然后，该方法将被用来系统地研究阿尔茨海默氏病是如何影响神经细胞的力学行为的。生成的实验数据将同随后提出的理论模型相结合，从而允许我们建立一个阿尔茨海默氏病的进展和神经细胞的黏附能力和机械性能之间的映射。 如果成功，这项研究可解决一个长期悬而未决的问题，即如何定量地测量神经细胞同外界的相互作用以及监控不同粘附分子在此过程的角色。本项目的实验和仿真结果将明确的证实或驳斥我们的主要假设，既阿尔茨海默氏病的进展会影响附神经元的黏附能力和力学响应，从而大大提高我们对这种疾病的认识。另外，从本项目获取的实验数据和理论预测对于阿尔茨海默氏病的诊断以及对各种疗法或药物有效性的评估也将是非常有价值的。

714713.label: Realisation of objectives
714713.value: 1. We have developed a method to probe the fundamental characteristics of neuron adhesion through repeated peeling of well-developed neurite branches on a substrate with an AFM cantilever. At the same time, a total internal reflection fluorescence microscope (TIRFM) is also used to monitor the activities of neural cell adhesion molecules (NCAMs) during detaching. 2. The adhesion and mechanical response of neural cells, subjected to various Aβ treatments to mimic the progression of Alzheimer’s disease, were systematically measured using the method developed in (1) as well as atomic force microrheology. 3. A statistical model was developed to describe the peeling of an axon, represented by an elastic strip, in adhesion with a flat substrate via an array of non-covalent molecular bonds. Here realistic features like the stochastic breaking and re-formation of bonds, as well as the bending and shearing of the strip, have all been taken into account.

714713.label: Major findings and research outcome
714713.value: 1. A novel method to measure the fundamental characteristics of neuron adhesion through repeated peeling of neurite branches from a substrate with an AFM cantilever has been developed. In this setup, a total internal reflection fluorescence microscope (TIRFM) is also used to monitor the activities of neural cell adhesion molecules (NCAMs) during detaching (refer to item 9-1, 9-2, and 10-1 in Part C). 2. We showed that the insertion of amyloid-beta peptide into the cytoskeleton of neural cells (a hallmark in Alzheimer's disease) will significantly alter their mechanical and adhesion response. Specifically, it was found that both the storage and loss moduli of neural cells increase gradually within the first 6 hours of Aβ treatment before steady-state values are reached, with a higher dosage of Aβ leading to larger changes in cell properties (see item 8-2 in Part C). In addition, using the method developed in (1), we demonstrated that NCAMs will aggregate into clusters at the neurite-substrate interface, resulting in strong local attachment. Furthermore, it was also observed that the characteristic time for the re-establishment of stable neurite-substrate attachment, with an apparent adhesion energy of 0.5 mJ/m^2, is between 2-5 minutes (item 10-2 in Part C). 3. From our statistical peeling model, it was shown that, under an imposed tensile peeling force, the interfacial bonds undergo diffusion-type transition in their bonding state, a process governed by a set of probabilistic equations coupled to the stretching, bending and shearing of the elastic strip (representing the neurite). Because of the low characteristic energy scale associated with molecular bonding, thermal excitations are found to play an important role in such escaping process, leading to propagation of the peeling front well below the threshold peel-off force predicted by the classical theories (item 8-3 and 8-5 in Part C) .

714713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
714713.value: 1. The method for characterizing the mechanical and adhesion response of neural cells could potentially be used for the detection and classification of neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease. 2. Our model could be extended to examined other interesting problems like the rate-dependent rupture or damage of axon during the peeling/stretching process. Studies along these lines are underway.

714713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
714713.value: We have developed a novel method to quantitatively characterize neuron-substrate adhesion by peeling neurite from the substrate with an atomic force microscope (AFM) probe while, simultaneously, monitoring the roles of various adhesion molecules with a total internal reflection fluorescence microscope (TIRFM). Using this setup, it was found that the progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD) greatly affects the mechanical and adhesion response of neural cells. Findings from this project will help us understand how the capability of neurons in executing biological duties is impaired by AD, as well as provide insights for the possible development of new ways to diagnose this disease.

714913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
714913.value: Atmospheric pollutant dispersion is usually calculated by the Gaussian plume models in which the dispersion coefficients are parameterized empirically as functions of stabilities. Their applications over rural areas have been well received by the industry for decades. Urbanization changes ground features and surface roughness that subsequently influences the turbulence structures and pollutant transport in the urban boundary layer (UBL). Thermal stratification, either solar heating or radiative cooling, modifies the UBL energy budget that further complicates the heat and mass transfer in neighborhood scales. Apart from the enhanced turbulent transport for flows over rough urban areas, thermal stratification induces updraft (unstable) or downdraft (stable), leading to plume meandering and ground-level extreme pollutant concentrations. They affect the pollutant distribution and chemistry in the UBL plume. Although Gaussian models are cost-effective, assuming Gaussian-shape dispersion often overlooks the aforementioned important nonlinear dynamics and chemistry coupling, resulting in uncertain air quality estimates in the UBL where most urban inhabitants reside. To bridge the knowledge gap, this project, LESPlume, is conceived to elucidate the UBL transport phenomena of chemically reactive pollutants over different configurations of building roughness and thermal stratification. As a pilot attempt, idealized street canyons, hypothetical heating/cooling and irreversible/reversible chemistry mechanism will be employed to address the core scientific question: “How urban morphology and atmospheric stability collectively affect the dynamics and chemical kinetics in UBL plume dispersion”. In particular, we attempt to derive an innovative formulation of dispersion coefficients that is able to handle the coupled pollution physics and chemistry over urban areas. A complementary approach consisting of experiments and computer modeling will be sought for a fundamental knowledge base. Measurements in wind tunnel and water-towing tank will be conducted to investigate the turbulence structures and UBL plume behaviors in neutral and thermal stratification. Gas-phase NOx-O3 chemical reactions will be simulated in the wind tunnel with bottom heating to examine the UBL reactive plume dispersion and meandering. Sensitivity tests will be conducted using the large-eddy simulation (LES) code, LESPlume, to constitute an in-depth understanding of the interaction between UBL dynamics and chemistry. LESPlume will serve the scientific community by improving dispersion coefficients that account for building roughness, atmospheric stability and pollution chemistry. It will also help refine urban planning guidelines and effectuate emission control strategies. This project will demystify our technical concern on the UBL reactive plume dispersion: Whether our current practice of Gaussian models over dense urban areas is reliable in the engineering perspective. 大氣污染物擴散通常是運用高斯羽流數學模型去計算，其中的擴散系數是大氣穩定性的經驗參數，它們在郊區中的應用已深受業界肯定多年。城市化改變地表特點和表面粗糙度隨後影響城市邊界層湍流結構及污染物輸移。熱分層，包括太陽加熱和輻射冷卻，改變城市邊界層的能量分配並進一步複雜化鄰里尺度內的熱能和質量輸移。除了流過粗糙城市範圍時增強了的湍流輸送，熱分層引起的上升氣流(不穩定)或下降氣流(穩定) 會導致曲折羽流和地面的極端污染物濃度。它們影響城市邊界層羽流內污染物的分佈和化學作用。雖然高斯模型是符合成本效益的，但假設高斯形狀擴散，往往忽視上述重要的非線性動力學和化學耦合，引致在有大部分市民居住的城市邊界層內對空氣質量的不確定評估。 為了彌補上述的知識溝，這個項目，LESPlume，就構想出來以闡明城市邊界層內各種污染物在不同建築物粗糙度和熱分層的配置下的輸移現象。作為新的試點，將會運用到理想化的街道峽谷、假設性的加熱/冷卻和可逆/不可逆的化學機理以解決下列的核心科學問題：” 城市形態及大氣穩定性如何共同影響城市邊界層中羽流擴散的動力學和化學動力學” 。最特別的是，我們試圖得出能夠同時處理在市區上空污染物物理跟化學耦合的創新擴散系數配方。利用一個包括實驗和計算機模擬的互補方法去尋求最基本的知識基礎。進行風洞測試和拖曳水池實驗以調查城市邊界層在同溫和熱分層的程況下的湍流結構和羽流行為。在底部加熱的風洞裏模擬氣相氮氧化物-臭氧的化學反應以細研污染物的曲折擴散。將採用大渦模擬(LES) 的電腦編碼LESPlume去進行有系统的敏感性測試以深入瞭解城市邊界層中動力學和化學的相互作用。 LESPlume會服務科學界，由提供一個包括建築物粗糙度、大氣穩定性和污染物化學的優化擴散系數開始。它也會有助完善城市規劃指引並有效推行排放控制策略。這個項目將解答我們對於城市邊界層化學化應污染物擴散的主要技術關注：在工程的角度來看我們目前慣於運用高斯羽流數學模型於人口密集的城市地區的做法是否可靠。

714913.label: Realisation of objectives
714913.value: 1. Investigate the effects of aerodynamic resistance on plume dispersion over urban areas: A complementary solution approach, using both mathematical modeling and laboratory experiments, was used to study the effects of aerodynamic resistance on plume dispersion over urban areas. A sophisticated large-eddy simulation (LES) computational fluid dynamics (CFD) code (LESPlume) was used in which a passive/insert tracer-transport equation was integrated into to calculate the turbulent plume dispersion over hypothetical urban areas in the form of idealized/identical roughness elements. Arrays of ribs of square cross-section in cross flows were used to control the aerodynamic resistance. A series of sensitivity tests were conducted based on those arrays to formulate the basic understanding of plume dispersion/coverage. In addition to LESPlume, wind tunnel experiments were sough to complement the LESPlume findings. Analogous to the LES mathematical modeling, aluminum square ribs were placed in the wind tunnel in cross flows to study the dynamics over rough surfaces. The separation of ribs was adjusted to modify the drag in order to perform the sensitivity tests. Recently, we extended our two-dimensional (2D) roughness elements to three-dimensional (3D) ones by using arrays of LEGO to fabricate the rough surfaces in the wind tunnel that provided much flexibility of roughness configuration. Apart from tracer gas dispersion, we successfully developed a laboratory protocol of using water vapor for passive/inert plume dispersion study in wind tunnel experiments. Apart from the (much cheaper) cost, the major benefit of using water as the tracer is its health concern that is easier to fulfill most of the occupational and safety regulation. Based on the results obtained from the aforementioned mathematical modeling and laboratory experiments, we developed a quite comprehensive theory of plume dispersion over urban areas in isothermal conditions. A functional form of the vertical dispersion coefficient was formulated in terms of surface roughness and the distance after the pollutant source that would be useful to air quality study as well as environmental impact assessment. Besides, the results obtained paved a simple relation between street-level ventilation and urban morphology in terms of aerodynamic resistance that would be helpful to green urban planning. 2. Examine the plume meandering in thermal stratification and the associated dispersion enhancement/suppression: The mathematical model and laboratory experiments mentioned above paved a solid knowledge foundation to study the influence of thermal stratification on the dynamics and plume dispersion. Boussinesq approximation was integrated into LESPlume to study the classic Monin-Obukhov Similarity Theory (MOST) in slightly unstable thermal stratification and test if it could be applied to the dynamics over urban areas. Apart from electrical coil heaters, a compact heating-cooling system using Peltier heaters/coolers was developed to build the thermal stratification in the wind tunnel. The benefit of Peltier heaters/coolers over electrical heaters was the development of heating/cooling across the vertical extent of the wind tunnel (compared with only bottom heating) that increased the degree of thermal stratification in the laboratory setups. A theory of mean wind profiles over rough surfaces in thermal stratification was developed that could be used with the velocity gradient to estimate the turbulence intensity over urban areas. Generally, we found that unstable stratification enhanced turbulence intensity and cross-wind plume dispersion compared with its isothermal counterpart. Moreover, the direction of buoyancy could be easily reversed by switching the power supply, facilitating the development of stable stratification in the wind tunnel and the related tracer dispersion. 3. Elucidate the nonlinear coupling among urban morphology, thermal stratification and reactive pollutants, and improve the plume dispersion parameterizations: Mechanism of NOx-O3 and NOx-O3-VOCs was integrated into LESPlume to examine the pollution physics and chemistry coupling over urban areas. An analytical solution to the vertical dispersion coefficient over hypothetical urban areas, making use of the time scales of pollution physics and chemistry, was developed. The output from LESPlume was then used to verify the analytical solution. Generally, it was found that pollution chemistry reduced the value of dispersion coefficient giving out secondary pollutants. Moreover, rough urban surfaces enhanced mixing so did chemical reactions. LESPlume results showed that chemical reactions were dominated near the urban canopy level so urban surfaces enhanced secondary pollutant production. As the result, the conventional Gaussian plume model must be applied with caution. Finally, it was apparently that, based on the LESPlume results, Gamma distribution was a reasonable candidate for reactive plume dispersion parameterization over urban areas.

714913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
714913.value: In this project, mathematical models and laboratory experiments were used concurrently to examine the reactive plume dispersion over urban areas. Flows and transport processes over rough surfaces were served as the theoretical solutions to elucidate the coupling of pollution physics and chemistry over urban areas. Based on the results obtained, we improved the understanding of how urban areas (aerodynamic resistance) and atmospheric stability (thermal stratification) collectively influenced reactive plume dispersion. Generally speaking, urban roughness and unstable atmospheric boundary layer enhanced mixing and the chemical kinetics, enhancing the production of secondary pollutant over urban areas. The results obtained could be helpful to urban planning, taking into account of how urban morphology influenced street-level ventilation and air quality. The modeling and laboratory results obtained collectively suggested that the pollutant distribution over urban areas could be more accurately represented by the Gamma distribution instead of the conventional Gaussian one. Chemical reactions were peaked at the urban canopy level that were attributed to the enhanced pollutant mixing induced by urban areas. Hence, urban morphology would be another factor affecting secondary pollutant production in addition to pollution chemistry and atmospheric condition. More studies are needed to verify the newly proposed functional forms of dispersion coefficients.

715213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
715213.value: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent, debilitating joint disease causing disability and poor quality of life in the elderly that leads to a heavy socioeconomic burden. Degeneration of the articular cartilage is a major hallmark of OA. Once the degenerative process of articular cartilage is initiated, there are no effective treatments to attenuate or cure OA except surgically replacing the totally damaged joint with an artificial one. Thus, it is much needed to identify the triggering events at the onset of OA for discovery of the structure modifying agents to prevent or attenuate the disease. Collagen fibrils, being the basic structural components of the articular cartilage, ensure the proper mechanical performance of the articular cartilage. Disruption of collagen fibrils has been witnessed prior to significant loss of proteoglycans in Hartley strain guinea pigs - a naturally occurring OA model. Recently, stiffening of the collagen fibril meshwork at the onset of OA has been reported in various animal models of OA. Therefore, it is imperative to investigate the nanomechanical changes happening at individual collagen fibrils’ level possibly as a triggering event for the initiation of OA. With the sustained funding support from Research Grant Council, we have established a nano-biotechnology research platform equipped with state-of-the-art equipments such as the atomic force microscopy (AFM) and optical tweezers. These techniques allow us to tackle individual collagen fibrils via nanoindentation and nano-scale tensile tests. Technically, we have modified the algorithm built in AFM nanoindentation to accommodate the viscoelasticity of biological materials. Also, we compared the nanostiffness of individual collagen fibrils of healthy and OA cartilage specimens of huamn beings, and observed stiffening of individual collagen fibrils at the osteochondral junction and the articular surface in OA specimens. This finding has been published in one of the leading journals in the filed of orthopaedics - Osteoarthritis and Cartilage. Following this, we propose to delineate the nanomechanical changes of individual collagen fibrils with the onset of OA in a spatiotemporal manner using a well-accepted OA model - Hartley strain guinea pigs. Specifically, this project is designed to • Evaluate the nanostiffness of collagen fibrils using our modified algorithm under AFM nanoindentation, • Test the tensile strength of individual collagen fibrils extracted from articular cartilage via optical tweezers. This project will provide the biomarker for early OA, and ultimately facilitate the discovery of new structure modifying agents for early intervention of OA. 骨性关节炎是一种退行性关节疾病，高发于中老年人群中。骨性关节炎可导致患者行动不便，影响其生活质量，对社会造成严重的经济负担。骨性关节炎以关节软骨退化为主要特征，目前尚无有效治愈手段，患者最终只能通过膝关节置换术以人工关节代替。因此，当务之急是通过对其发病机制的研究来寻求有效的干预手段。 胶原纤维是关节软骨基质的主要组成成分，其作用是维持正常的力學机械性能。因此，在骨性关节炎发病初期，单个胶原纤维的纳米机械性能是否发生改变，这种改变是否是该病的触发因素之一，值得进行深入研究。 在本研究中，我们将选用一种具有自发骨性关节炎的动物模型——Hartley豚鼠，对单个胶原纤维纳米机械性能的改变与骨性关节炎发病的时空相关性进行探索。具体包括： 1. 通过原子力显微镜纳米刻痕技术，并使用改良算法，评估胶原纤维的刚性。 2. 利用光镊从关节软骨中分离单个胶原纤维并测定其张力。 本研究结果可作为早期骨性关节炎诊断的生物力学标记，并促进寻求新的结构改性剂以期干预骨性关节炎的进程。

715213.label: Realisation of objectives
715213.value: In current project, we have conducted following experiments and tests to realise our objectives. Human Specimens Collection and Preparations A total of 100 human cartilages were collected, both cartilages harvested from OA patients, cartilages were harvested from three OP patients, We have also collected 10 cartilages were harvested from normal patients. The specimens collected from diseased patients have undergone total joint replacement. The specimens were harvested and stored at -80°C. The healthy specimens were collected from victims of accidents in People’s Republic of China. The process of collecting all specimens has been approved by the university’s ethics committee. Collagen Extractions All specimens were thawed at 4°C for approximately 24 hours prior harvesting cartilage, which were all harvested from non-load bearing zones with surgical scalpel. Afterwards, they were all cut in sliced into piece of 1mm2 to 4mm2, and then they were placed into a buffer containing, 7.5mM of sodium chloride, 0.1mM of sodium phosphate, 0.1mM of EDTA, 3mM of 6-Amiohexanoic acid, 5mM of benzamidine, 0.1mM of PMSF, and 5mM of NEM. The mixture was then be dispersed with a homogenizer (T10 Basic Ultra-Turrax, Cat. No. 3420000, IKA, Germany) equipped with a dispersing element (S10N-8G Dispersing Element, Cat. No. 3305500, IKA, Germany). The mixture was centrifuged at 27000g (Himac CR-GIII, Cat. No. CR22GII, Hitachi Koki, Japan) with a rotor (Cat. No. R20A2, Hitachi Koki, Japan) for 30mins at 4°C. The supernatant was collected, and the pellet was homogenized and centrifuged for another 2 times. All supernatant was ultra-centrifuged at 115000g (Himac CP-WX, Cat. No. CP100WX, Hitachi Koki, Japan) with a rotor (Cat. No. P70AT2, Hitachi Koki, Japan) for 2hrs at 4°C. The final pellets were dispersed and stored in 2%SDS + H2O. These extraction procedures were modified based on previous studies (Aladin, et al., 2010; Kassner, et al., 2003). The solution containing collagen fibrils were placed the collagen fibrils on polylysine-coated glasses. The samples were dried, washed in DD H2O for 2 mins, and then they were dried again. Afterwards, these samples were ready to proceed for imaging and biomechanical tests. Scanning Electron Microscope Imaging Prior to imaging the collagen fibrils with scanning electron microscope (SEM), the samples were sputter-coated with 10nm layer of gold-palladium. The samples were imaged at 80K. At least 100 images were collected, and each image was 2μm apart from each other to minimize the chance of duplicate measurements. All fibrils on each image were measured, and the diameters of at least 350 fibrils were measured. Nano-Indentation with Atomic Force Microscope (Ambient) Although AFM is one of the most popular imaging apparatus, it is also an equipment to perform nano-indentations. In order to provide a hard surfaceunderneath the fibrils, the samples were placed on relatively hard glass slides along with the sample glass slid. After the samples were mounted on the stage, intermittent mode was selected to imaging the fibrils and the tip applied had spring constant of 42N/m, while the radius of the tip was not larger than 8nm. Sensistivity calibration was performed, and nominal spring constant of tip cantilever was applied. During nanoindentation, tip was retracted to 0.5μm, and then 1nN was applied to the fibrils. Fifty fibrils were randomly selected from each specimen for nanoindentation under ambient condition. Nano-Indentation with Atomic Force Microscope (Hydrated) Unlike performing nanoindentation under ambient condition, samples were placed and indented on a lid of petich dish. The fibrils were immersed in DD H2O for 30mins prior to nanoindentations. The tip selected for this part of the experiment also owned a tip radius of no larger than 8nm. Sensitivity calibrate was performed, as well as the spring constant was measured by thermal noise. The fibrils were imaging with contact mode and nanoindentation was performed with the similar schedule as tested under ambient condition, but only 20 fibrils were randomly selected from each specimen. Animal tissue observations: Similarly, we have also collected tissues from Hartley strain guinea pigs with spontaneous OA in comparison with control guinea pigs without OA. Major part of the results have been published in our papers.

715213.label: Major findings and research outcome
715213.value: Osteoarthritis (OA) is one of the most concerned diseases in the field of orthopaedics. During the process of this disease, articular cartilages are degenerated and worn out at the end stage, which create pain and disabilities to the patients. Our results showed that the collagen fibrils extracted from OA cartilages were thinner than the ones extracted from OP and healthy cartilages. It was believe that the fibrillation and derangement of collagen network spread from superficial zone towards deeper zones. However, the number of thinner collagen fibrils increased in OA specimens could be the reason of the loss of larger fibrils and/or fragmentation occurred in the superficial zone, where contains thinner fibrils. The biomechanical tests showed that fibrils extracted from OA cartilages owned the highest elastic modulus, while the ones from OP had the lowest; significant differences were found between all groups when tested under ambient condition. Alternatively, the same pattern of results could also be found when hydrated fibrils were tested; however, due to the limited amount of samples, only the difference between OA and OP were considered significant. In addition, no individual difference was found; no significant difference between samples within each group could be observed. Since nano-indentations were performed at the center of each fibril, the elastic moduli measured represented the stiffness of the crosslinks and molecules within fibrils. Assuming the triple helix structure of collagen is relatively tough, the decrease of tensile modulus of superficial zone in OA cartilages could due to the changes of the crosslinks between fibrils in collagen network.

715213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
715213.value: Current study explained the importance of biomechanical properties of collagen network towards the progression of OA. In future, it was reasonable to examine the differences of the tensile properties of collagen fibrils from various cartilages; that could directly evaluate the effect of the changes of individual fibrils towards the network. Due to several technical problems encountered when testing fibrils with optical tweezers, the quantitative results could not be produced until the processes of biotinylation and the problems of massive fluid flow are improved and resolved. Nevertheless, performing nano-indentation on individual fibrils could examine the stiffness of collagen molecules and crosslinks within the fibrils. In order to further confirm if the changes of the crosslinks are significant, testing the fibrils again with modified crosslink may better imply the role of these changes towards the diseases. Secondly, increasing the number of measurements of elastic moduli tested under hydrated condition may suggest whether the differences between various groups are significant. Furthermore, even though there are multiple biochemical factors leads to the changes of collagen fibrils, performing some biochemical analysis, such as SDS PAGE or mass spectrometry, may help establishing a relationship between the changes of biomechanical properties and the alternations of compositions.

715413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
715413.value: In the past decade, there is an increasing interest by researchers and companies in analyzing social network data. Typical targeted applications include recommendation systems, viral marketing, social behavior analysis and link prediction. Modern social networking applications record data beyond simple links between users; for each user, the system maintains a profile and keeps track of a behavioral history: connections that the user has established with other users, places that the user has visited (check-ins), user opinion via tagging or commenting in conversations. As a result considering a social network as a simple graph where edges connect users with an established relationship (e.g., friendship in Facebook) is no longer adequate for sophisticated analysis. More recently, researchers considered the overlap between user profiles or visits as a factor of similarity between them. These attempts result in a refined social network model, which reflects more accurately the relationships between users and their trends. Although there is ample recent work on modeling and predicting relationships between users and places, there is little work on developing geosocial data management solutions for large-scale data routinely collected by location-based social network services, such as Foursquare and Facebook places. In this project, we will study the efficient evaluation of search operations in geosocial data, which are common modules of analysis and prediction tasks. More specifically, we will investigate appropriate indexing techniques which facilitate the fast retrieval of similar users to a given user based on multi-variate information (e.g., user profiles and locations, social proximity, places which the users visit). In addition, we plan to support search for the most appropriate places for a given user to visit, based on the user's location and the visits or recommendations of her social links and users similar to her. We also intend to support similarity search for similar places to a given place, which finds application in clustering and other data analysis tasks. Finally, we intend to extend our system to support additional operations, like message and news ranking, on-line analytical processing of historical geosocial data, (spatio-)temporal queries, etc. The project goals include the (i) identification of common search modules in queries and analysis tasks over geosocial data, (ii) design of storage, indexing, and search methods that facilitate similarity retrieval for users, places, and news/messages, (iii) development and testing of advanced querying and data mining approaches, such as clustering, on-line analytical processing, and (spatio-)temporal search based on the developed system. 在過去十年中，社交網絡數據分析引起了科研工作者和公司越來越多的關注。典型的目標應用包括推薦系統、營銷、社會行為分析，以及關係預測等。現代的社交網絡應用記錄的數據已經超越了用戶間的簡單關係；對於每個用戶，系統保存其個人信息與行為歷史（該用戶與其他用戶建立的關係、該用戶到訪過的地方、該用戶在標記或評論時體現的觀點等）。因此，簡單地吧社交網絡看做一個以邊連接用戶關係（如Facebook中的好友關係），已經不再適用於複雜的分析。最近，研究人員在嘗試將用戶信息和訪問地點二者結合起來，作為用戶間相似度的一個衡量因素。這些嘗試帶來了一個修訂后的社交網絡模型，它更準確地反應用戶之間的關係及其變化趨勢。 近來雖然有很多關於用戶和地點間的建模與關係預測研究，但对于由基於位置的社交網絡服務（如Foursquare和Facebook）收集的大規模地理﹣社交數據，卻很少有工作研究它们的管理和解决方案。在本項目中，我們將研究如何高效地搜索地理﹣社交數據，这是分析、預測等工作中的常用模塊。更具體地說，我們將探討適當的索引技術，從而對於給定用戶，可以更快速地獲取基於多變量計算而出的相似用戶（這些變量包括用戶信息和位置，社交相似度，訪問過的地點等）。此外，我們計劃根據給定用戶的位置及其好友或相似用戶的訪問或推薦，來幫助用戶搜索推薦最適於其訪問的地點。我們還打算支持對於給定地點的相似地點搜索，這在聚類和其他數據分析工作中有著重要應用。最後，我們希望拓展我們的系統來支持更多操作，如消息與新聞排序、歷史地理﹣社交數據的線上分析處理、時間（時空）數據查詢等。該項目的目標包括：(1)研究地理﹣社交數據搜索與分析中常用的搜索模塊；(2)設計高效的存儲、索引和搜索方法，從而加速用戶、地點、新聞/信息等的近似查詢；(3)基於開發的系統，開發測試先進的查詢和數據挖掘方法，如聚類、線上分析處理，以及時間（時空）數據查詢。

715413.label: Realisation of objectives
715413.value: The objectives have been achieved 100%. In journal paper titled "Joint Search by Social and Spatial Proximity", we studied the operation of finding the nearest person in a social network to a given user both in terms of location and in terms of social distance. This result addresses to a high degree objectives 1 & 2. In journal paper titled "An Effective Encoding Scheme for Spatial RDF Data" we studied the evaluation of pattern queries with a spatial component in linked data. These data are similar to geo-social data, so our techniques can be applied there too; this work partially addresses objectives 1 and 2. Journal paper "Reverse Top-k Search using Random Walk with Restart" studies a novel search operation in social networks and it is related to all objectives of the project. Conference publication "Weighted Coverage based Reviewer Assignment" is a side-product of this project. It studies a complex bipartite graph matching problem. It is related to objective 3. Conference publication "Diverse and Proportional Size-l Object Summaries for Keyword Search" again studies a novel search operation in large tuple networks and it is related to objective 3. Conference publication "Activity-Partner Recommendation" studies the recommendation of activities to a user which have high chances to also be done by their friends in a social network. Again, a novel analysis problem in social network data analysis, related to objective 3. Publication "A Revisit to Social Network-Based Recommender Systems" improves the performance of classic recommenders, taking under consideration the social network. This work is highly related to objectives 1 and 3. Publication "Density-based Place Clustering in Geo- Social Networks" studies the clustering of geo-social network places according to their spatial distance and the social relationships between users that visit these places. This work is addresses to a high extent all project objectives. Publication "Location Recommendation in Location-based Social Networks using User Check-in Data" is directly related to the project proposal, addressing the problem of place recommendation to geo-social network users based on location and social relationships of users. This work addresses objectives 1 and 2. Publication "Efficient Point-based Trajectory Search" is directly related to objective 3. It proposes an efficient algorithm for conducting search on spatio-temporal data. Publication "Overlapping Community Regularization for Rating Prediction in Social Recommender Systems" advances the state-of-the-art of recommender systems, considering the social relationships between users. It is related to objectives 1 and 2. Publication "Meta Structure: Computing Relevance in Large Heterogeneous Information Networks" proposes a novel measure for modeling the relevance between nodes in a heterogeneous network. The findings can be applied to social networks and it is directly related to objective 1.

715413.label: Major findings and research outcome
715413.value: The project was very fruitful in terms of research results. We have published three journal papers and nine conference papers. Two MPhil and one PhD student were trained and graduated. One best paper award (in SSTD 2015) was received. The major findings of this project are as follows: 1) Joint spatial and social search is a very effective means for obtaining relevant information (e.g. user search or place search) using both spatial and social dimensions, as reported in Journal publication 1. In addition, we have developed efficient algorithms for this type of search. This addresses objectives 1 and 2 to a high degree. 2) Joint graph and spatial search and analysis was studied in different contexts, e.g., spatial search on RDF data (Journal publication 2), place clustering in geo-social networks (Conference publication 5), location recommendation (Conference publication 6). These publications address all three objectives to a high degree. 3) The project initiated research on improved search and analysis of large graphs and networks. Journal publication 3 proposes a new technique for analyzing large social graphs from the point of view of a pivot user. Conference publication 1 analyzed the relationships between reviewers and papers in a large bipartite relevance graph for the purpose of paper assignment. Conference publication 2 analyzes large relational graphs for the purpose of extracting meaningful summaries. Conference publications 3 and 8 extends recommender systems to recommend partners together with items related to activities (e.g. movie tickets). Conference publication 4 improves classic recommenders using information from social networks. Conference publication 9 proposes a novel similarity measure for nodes in a heterogeneous network. All these works are directly related to objective 3. 4) We also produced original research on trajectory search (spatio-temporal data). This is also related to objective 3.

715413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
715413.value: Our work motivates additional research directions in analyzing and searching geo-social graphs. The challenge is the complex nature of the data, which calls not only for efficient indexing approaches but also for meaningful and practical search models that should be evaluated with real users. Our plan is to analyze in-depth the relationships between the different data elements (nodes and edges, spatial information, temporal information, etc) to find combinations thereof and problem setups that find practical applications. After this, we plan to design appropriate algorithms and indexing approach for supporting the search models identified as useful and practical.

715413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
715413.value: In this project, we have studied the management of large volumes of data that are generated in location-based social network services, such as Foursquare and Facebook places. Our ultimate goal was to efficiently support search and analysis operations on such data that would bring useful information to data analysts and common users (e.g., social network users looking for friend recommendations). To this end, we developed an effective model for conducing spatial and social search simultaneously by combining spatial and social proximity measures. For example, in a friend recommendation application, both graph proximity (e.g., friends of friends) and location proximity (e.g., people who live in the same neighborhood) were considered. In addition, we developed an influential algorithm that identifies automatically clusters of places which are close to each other geographically and they are also visited by users who are close to each other in a social network. During the course of the project we also studied fundamental operations on graphs and networks (proximity search, similarity measurement, matching) as well as other operations that use graphs to improve their effectiveness (recommendation). The results of the project were published in top journals and conferences of data management, information retrieval, and data mining research.
