718513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
718513.value: This project studies economic issues involved in practical operation of a federated cloud, and designs efficient online algorithms for pricing and scheduling of resources to maximize economic benefits of the clouds. Federated clouds are newly emerged paradigms of cloud computing, where cloud services in disparate data centers of different cloud providers are interconnected based on common standards and policies. A federated cloud exploits availability of resources and diversity of operational costs among different data centers at different times, to provide a seemingly infinite pool of resources and to serve jobs at low costs: when one cloud experiences a spike of demand, it can borrow idle resources from other clouds; when the electricity price is high at one data center, the cloud can schedule jobs onto other clouds with lower power charges at the moment. To achieve a federated cloud, significant efforts have been devoted to developing standards to enable interoperability among data centers running different cloud technologies. On the other hand, fundamental problems on cloud economics remain under-explored: How should a cloud charge other clouds leasing its idle resources? Should a cloud serve a job using its own resources or others’? Would it be more beneficial for a cloud to keep its servers running to serve jobs, or to turn some of them down to save electricity cost? Answers to these questions are critical to decide profits and hence incentives for a cloud to operate in a federation. In this project, we address economic issues in a federated cloud with dynamic mechanisms and algorithms, designed to optimize profits obtained by individual clouds and the federation aggregately over its long-term operation. We seek to design a double auction-based mechanism for resource trading among the clouds, with trading volumes and prices dynamically set to balance demand and supply. Closely combined with the auction, a fully distributed online algorithm carefully guides each cloud in its resource trade in the auction, optimally schedules dynamically-arriving jobs with different resource requirements and SLAs (Service Level Agreements) onto different data centers, and judiciously turns on and off servers in the cloud over time. Our mechanisms and algorithms are intended to maximize the long-term average profit for each individual cloud, and approach the long-term average social welfare achieved by an ideal federation without inter-cloud resource usage charges. We will implement our mechanisms and algorithms in a cloud management toolkit, and deploy it onto distributed cloud platforms in an emulated federation.

718513.label: Realisation of objectives
718513.value: We have fully achieved Objectives 1-3 in this project to 100%, and achieved Objective 4 to 80%. Objective 1: For Goals 1) and 2), we designed a double auction mechanism for inter-cloud VM trading, which achieves (i) truthfulness, (ii) individual rationality, (iii) ex-post budget balance, as well as (iv) computational efficiency (polynomial time complexity). What's more, the auction mechanism is closely combined with an online Lyapunov optimization framework, to carefully decide the true valuations of VMs for setting the sell/buy bids in the auction, optimally schedule randomly-arriving jobs with different resource requirements (e.g., number of VMs) and SLAs (e.g., maximum job scheduling delay) onto different data centers, and judiciously turn on and off servers in the clouds based on the current electricity prices. The combined framework is proven to achieve close-to-offline-optimal individual profit for each cloud and social welfare in the entire federated cloud system, over the long run of the system. The result was reported in our publication 8.1 in Part C. In addition, we have applied a similar auction+Lyapunov optimization framework for online spectrum auction, in which each secondary link strategically decides its channel evaluation/bids, transmission rates and packet dropping in each time slot, and the primary user selects a set of collision-free bids as the winners of the auction of its channel. The auction is truthful-in- expectation, and achieves close-to-offline-optimal time-averaged social welfare and individual utilities with polynomial time complexity. The result was reported in Publication 9.1 in Part C. For Goal 3): When modeling one cloud as one seller in the auction, who owns multiple geo-distributed data centers that provision VMs at different costs, we have designed online/offline auction mechanisms to allocate dynamically composed resource bundles to users upon demand. The mechanisms, as in publications 9.2-9.5 in Part C, are shown to be truthful, computationally efficient, and achieves close-to-optimal social welfare. For the case of modeling each cloud data center as one player to participate in the auction, such that data centers owned by the same cloud provider may collude, we have investigated a similar case that multiple cloud users may conduct shill bidding (a form of collusion), and designed a new type of core-selecting VM auctions, to guarantee economic efficiency and truthful bidding. The result was reported in publication 9.6 in Part C. Objective 2: Goals 1) and 2) have been achieved as in publications 8.1, 9.1 and 9.7. We investigated the SLA that each job in a cloud is either scheduled or dropped (subject to a penalty) before its maximum tolerable response delay, and seamlessly combined the Lyapunov optimization framework with the auction mechanism to decide true valuation, job scheduling and server provisioning. Each job demands specified VM(s) for one or multiple time slots, where the requested instance-timeslots are scheduled on one VM at a time before the job's completion by the maximum tolerable response time. For scheduling concurrent execution of a job on multiple VMs and possibly different geo-distributed data centres, we have designed online auction mechanisms for resource allocation and job scheduling among different bidders in various settings, as well as incentivising voluntary energy reduction for emergency demand response. The results are presented in publications 8.2 - 8.3. The results related to Goal 3) are given in publication 9.7. We consider multiple cloud data centers that charge users at different prices. Cloud users are free to choose the data centers to run their jobs, based on a joint consideration of monetary charges and quality of service. We designed an efficient online algorithm for dynamic pricing of VM resources at different data centers together with job scheduling and server provisioning, to maximize the profit of the cloud provider over a long run. In another relevant study, we investigate a cloud broker's market, where the broker sets the offered prices to buy spare resources from different clouds and schedules dynamically-arriving user jobs on the available resources. We model the interaction between the broker and the clouds as a two-stage Stackelberg game, and design the online algorithms for the broker to set the prices and schedule jobs and for the private cloud to decide the numbers of VMs to lease, based on the Lyapunov optimization theory. We prove that the economic benefits of both the broker and the clouds are maximized. The results were published in publication 9.8. For Goal 4), we designed online VM scaling algorithms that take VM migration cost into consideration in cost minimization, and designed auction models which schedule not only VM allocation but also server provisioning, considering the overhead. The results were reported in publications 8.4, 8.5, and 9.9. We also modelled long-term service plans and studied the pricing issues in publication 9.10. Objective 3: Goals 1), 2) and 3) have all been achieved with results reported in publications 8.1, 9.1, 9.7 and 9.8. We design online algorithms based on the Lyapunov optimization framework to schedule jobs across cloud data centers, with each VM occupied for one or multiple time slots. We rigorously prove that optimizing the 1-shot objective can maximize long-term time-averaged profit for each cloud, in addition to other desired properties including truthfulness, individual rationality, ex-post budget balance of the auction mechanism, and SLA guarantee of the jobs. In particular, in publication 8.1, we also prove that asymptotic optimality in long-term average social welfare in the federation can be achieved by the distributed online algorithm carried out by each cloud under homogeneous cloud settings, by comparing it with a centralized dynamic algorithm that maximizes long-term average social welfare. The achieved social welfare under heterogeneous cloud settings also approaches the optimum, as shown by our extensive simulations driven by the real-world Google cluster usage traces. Objective 4: We developed the cloud management toolkit, which implements our mechanisms and algorithms designed. We evaluated our algorithms in most publications reported in simulated/emulated systems on our own testbed with workloads produced following the Google cluster-usage data, and reported evaluation results with various job completion deadlines, occupancy instance-hours of the corresponding VMs, electricity prices, etc. We have made efforts on constructing a cross-institutional cloud testbed, but have found it very difficult due to different policy/security regulations of different institutes and lack of management and technical support in different institutes. On the other hand, we realized that the main contributions in the project, scheduling and pricing mechanisms/algorithms designed, can be reasonably well evaluated using emulated systems following real-world traces. So we have largely resorted to evaluations on our own testbed.

718513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
718513.value: A cross-institutional cloud testbed would still be ideal for evaluating cloud-based systems and algorithms, with a set of unified equipment for researchers to experiment on. It will be very nice if such a platform can be built across different institutes in Hong Kong. We have experienced difficulty to build such a platform during the course of this project, due mainly to lack of management and technical support from different institutes, as well as the lack of funding. We look forward to an initiative from the RGC on building such a cross-institutional cloud testbed in Hong Kong.

718913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
718913.value: 水泥增强是一种很有前途的用于恢复骨质疏松性椎体骨折的方法。聚甲基丙烯酸甲酯（PMMA）是一种常见的用于椎体增强的骨水泥，在骨固定和缓解疼痛方面疗效显著。然而，人们在长期应用中发现PMMA生物活性差，这在一定程度上增加了在聚合过程中由于与骨的力学性能不匹配而导致的相邻椎体骨折的风险。此外，PMMA在聚合过程中发生的强放热反应可能导致周围软组织坏死和肺栓塞。甲基丙烯酸甲酯单体溶出到血管系统中可能引起血压突然下降而导致死亡。随后一些研究组通过将磷酸钙和生物玻璃与PMMA结合和使用其它钙基骨水泥解决了这些并发症。遗憾的是这些改性水泥的力学性能不足以恢复骨质疏松性椎体骨折，降低了术后脊柱的稳定性。因此有必要开发一种新型的骨替代物。 在这项研究中，我们将开发一种由聚己酸内酯（PCL）和镁颗粒组成的生物可降解和可注射的骨替代材料。这种材料具有可调控性，可作为骨填充物适用于具有不同骨密度的患者。初步研究表明，该材料具有射线不可透过性，体内可降解性以及在植入过程中没有发生明显放热反应等特点。在先前的RGC-GRF（＃718507）支持下 ，我们已经证实了从聚合物涂覆镁植入体中溶出的少量镁离子具有促进体内新骨形成的功效。并且溶出离子可有效中和聚合物降解所产生的局部微酸环境。这有效增强了成骨细胞活性，提高了骨替代材料的生物活性。本项目将研制一种由镁和PCL组成的新的可降解骨替代物。其力学性能可通过调节镁颗粒量，镁颗粒形状以及偶联剂类型而实现可控性。我们将全面地研究这些新型生物材料的力学性能和体内外生物学反应（包括骨传导和骨诱导），以解决目前使用的骨水泥存在的问题，从而避免各种与生物材料相关的术后并发症，帮助那些需要椎体增强的患者早日康复。

718913.label: Realisation of objectives
718913.value: In this GRF project, we aimed to establish a detailed profile of the mechanical properties and release pattern of magnesium ions of the new bone substitutes by manipulating the amount, geometry of magnesium granules and the type of silane coupling agent used. All objectives of this project have been successfully achieved. Our team has established a new bone substitutes made from magnesium and FDA approved biodegradable polymer (polycaprolactone, PCL). We have successfully demonstrated the alterations of the mechanical properties, ion leaching property, in vitro and in vivo biological responses of the silane coupling agent-treated bone substitutes by incorporating different amount and size of the magnesium granules into PCL. In the results of the in vitro experiments, the silane coupling agent treatment on the magnesium granules was able to enhance the cell proliferation and osteogenic differentiation property. In animal testing, we have created an ovariectomized (OVX) rat model and conducted the in vivo animal study to investigate the inflammatory response, bioactivity and biocompatibility of the selected bone substitutes, bone forming ability and the mechanical properties of the newly formed bone. All these pre-clinical findings have been published in few journal papers already. Hence we believe that these evidences are very convincing to put forward these bone substitutes in clinical trial in near future.

718913.label: Major findings and research outcome
718913.value: In the mid-term report, we have already fabricated different types of silane coupling agent-treated bone substitutes and screened out the bone substitutes with the best performance regarding to the cell proliferation and osteogenic differentiation property. After checking the osteoblastic differentiation properties by using ALP assay, the properties were further assessed by real-time RT-PCR. ALP, Col1a1, Runx2 and Opn mRNA levels were checked by culturing MC3T3-E1 mouse pre-osteoblasts on pure PCL and TMSPM-treated bone substitutes. The ALP and Runx2 mRNA levels of all the samples increased gradually with culture time. Significant higher (p < 0.05) ALP and Opn expressions were found on the TMSPM-treated bone substitutes on days 3, 7 and 14 when compared to pure PCL. Moreover, 45μm TMSPM-treated bone substitutes showed a significantly higher Runx2 expression on days 3, 7 and 14 when compared to pure PCL. Furthermore, 150μm TMSPM-treated bone substitutes showed a significantly higher Col1a1 expression on day 14 whereas 45μm TMSPM-treated bone substitutes showed a significant higher Col1a1 expression on both days 7 and 14 when compared to pure PCL. This suggested that the TMSPM-treated bone substitutes were more favorable for osteogenic differentiation. After the in vitro studies, the next stage would be the in vivo studies. Pure PCL and PMMA were served as the control and used to compare with the TMSPM-treated bone substitutes (i.e. 0.1g 45μm and 150μm TMSPM-treated PCL-Mg bone substitutes). Ovariectomized (OVX) rat model was developed by identifying the change in bone mineral density and mechanical properties after 3 weeks of operation. After that, new bone formation of post-operation was studied at particular time points with the use of Micro-CT. Increased bone volume was found on all the tested samples throughout the implantation period. More than 15% new bone formation was found on the TMSPM-treated bone substitutes after week 1 post-operation and approximately 40% more new bone was found after 3 weeks when compared to pure PCL. In addition, no significant difference of the serum magnesium levels of all the rats implanted with different samples was found. Furthermore, consistent result also found in the histology data in which more new bone formation was observed around the TMSPM-treated bone substitutes as compared to PMMA and pure PCL. From the higher magnification of the histological photographs, no inflammation was observed. No giant cells or macrophages were found around all of the implants which indicated that they possessed good biocompatibility. All the results obtained in this study suggested that the TMSPM-treated bone substitutes were able to enhance the osteogenic differentiation and hence bone formation. Further details of these experimental data can be found in the publication list in Part C.

718913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
718913.value: With the current promising results that obtained in mechanical, in vitro and in vivo animal studies, the next stage of work will be studying the long-term in vivo study by using both small and large animal models for the application of osteoporotic spinal fractures. Once we finish all the in vivo studies and confirm the use of these bone substitutes, we plan to submit another proposal for industrial funding to carry out human clinical trial. Ultimately, patients undergoing osteoporotic spinal fracture management will be benefited by avoiding post-operative complications associated with present biomaterials, and possible quickening patient recovery.

718913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
718913.value: Cement augmentation is a promising approach for restoring osteoporotic spinal fractures. Polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) is a commonly used bone cement for vertebral augmentation, and believed to be highly effective in bone stabilization and pain relief. However, its application over the years has found drawbacks such as unsatisfactory bioactivity which does not help convince new bone formation, it has a much higher compressive modulus in comparison to human cancellous bone. In addition, a strongly exothermic reaction during curing is another concern. These problems can be resolved by either incorporating other materials such as calcium-phosphate and bioglass to PMMA and other resins, or fabricating other calcium-based bone cements. However, calcium-based bone cements are brittle in nature which will affect spinal stability. Therefore, development of other bone substitute is necessary. We therefore created an adjustable, biodegradable and injectable bone substitute comprising of polycaprolactone and magnesium granules to generate various mechanical strengths. We have successfully altered the mechanical properties of the bone substitutes by adjusting the amount of magnesium granules added. Moreover, we have also demonstrated superior osteogenic differentiation property of the silane treated bone substitutes. The results were found to be consistent in the animal studies as well. More new bone formation was found on the new bone substitutes as compared to PMMA and pure PCL. Therefore, our newly developed bone substitutes are one of the possible alternatives for cement augmentation.

719313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
719313.value: Image and video segmentation is a fundamental and necessary operation in many tasks in image-based graphics, computer vision, and medical imaging. For example, image segments can be further grouped into layers that are important for image-based rendering and scene understanding. Segmentation is also essential for editing the appearance and shape of an image or video object. Extracting objects from an image sequence, i.e. ``rotoscoping", is perhaps the most frequent operation in the visual effects industry. Levelset-based image segmentation represents a popular class of segmentation algorithms. A significant limitation that has prevented it from being widely used for high-quality image/video segmentation is that they are extremely vulnerable to local minima and bad initializations. In this proposal, we advocate to overcome this limitation by incorporating supervised machine learning with the level set method. To achieve this goal, we define a novel class of level set functions and propose a new levelset-based segmentation framework that adopts supervised probabilistic classification as well as a novel classification-based force term. We plan to further extend our approach in multiple directions, including interactive video segmentation, 3D biomedical image segmentation, multiphase segmentation as well as a novel parts-based deformable shape prior. The outcomes of the proposed research will significantly advance the state of the art in interactive image and video segmentation. Incorporating supervised machine learning eliminates a fundamental limitation and makes the level set method insensitive to local minima of the energy function it minimizes. Our parts-based shape prior for articulated objects will represent a significant technical advancement in Bayesian image/video segmentation. Our new multiphase segmentation algorithm would also be able to elevate the state of the art in image/video layer extraction. In summary, our suite of new techniques has the power to break the ``ceiling" and make it possible for the level set method to realize its full potential in segmentation. The proposed research also has important practical values. Our new algorithm has the potential to become a top choice for challenging image/video segmentation tasks, such as ``rotoscoping". Our active learning approach to interactive video segmentation would relieve the user's workload, and make video segmentation a more pleasant task. And high-quality biomedical image segmentation opens the door for further high-level analysis, 3D reconstruction and visualization. 圖像分割對於基於圖像的圖形學，計算機視覺，醫療成像中的很多任務來說是一個基本的和必要的操作。例如，圖像片段可以進一步合併為層，這些層對於基於圖像的繪製和場景的理解是非常重要的。分割在編輯圖像或視頻對象的外觀和形狀方面至關重要的。從一個圖像序列中抽取對象也許是在視覺效果行業中最頻繁的操作。 基於水平集（Levelset）的圖像分割代表了一類流行的分割法。對於局部極小和初始解的極度脆弱是它的一個重大局限，這阻止了它被廣泛用於高品質的圖像/視頻分割。在這個申請書中，我們主張把有監督機器學習與水平集方法相結合來克服這個局限。為實現這一目標，我們定義了一類新的水平集函數并提出了一種新的基於水平集的分割框架，採用有監督的概率分類以及一種新型的基於分類的力場。我們計劃從多個方向進一步擴展我們的方法，包括三維生物醫學圖像分割，多相位分割以及一種新型的可變形的形狀先驗模型。 這項研究的成果將大大推進交互式圖像分割的研究水平。結合有監督機器學習，消除了一個根本性的限制，使水平集方法對能量函數的局部極小不敏感。總之，我們提出的一套新技術有可能使水平集方法充分發揮其在圖像分割方面的潛力。這項研究也有重要的實用價值。我們的新算法有潛力成為一個具有挑戰性的圖像分割任務的首選解決方案。我們基於主動學習的交互式視頻分割方法，減輕了用戶的工作量，並使視頻分割成為一種比較愉快的任務。高質量的生物醫學圖像分割為進一步高層次的分析，三維重建和可視化打開了通道。

719313.label: Realisation of objectives
719313.value: 1. Extended classifier driven level-set algorithm for 3D medical image segmentation. We have developed a robust and accurate method for 3D biomedical image segmentation using level sets of probabilities. Our method integrates a probabilistic classifier with the level set method, making the level set method less vulnerable to local minima. Given the local attributes within a neighborhood of a voxel, this classifier outputs an estimated likelihood of the voxel being part of an object of interest. Our method obtains a posterior probabilistic mask of the object of interest according to such estimated likelihoods, an edge field and a smoothness prior. We further alternate classifier training and the level set method to improve the performance of both. The input to the classifier consists of 3 color channels and Gabor filter responses. Oriented filter banks have proven to be an effective method to characterize textures. We extend Gabor filtering to volume images by performing 2D Gabor filtering respectively in the X-Y, Y-Z and Z-X cross sections of the volumetric neighborhood of a voxel. We apply 24 Gabor filters at 6 orientations and 4 scales at every voxel in the grayscale version of the image, and such filtering is performed on three orthogonal cross sections, respectively. Thus, every voxel has a 72-component filter response vector. We perform 3D edge detection before the construction of the 3D edge field. We generalize the principles of traditional 2D Canny edge detection to 3D spaces. An edge in a 2D image is a curve while it becomes a surface in a 3D volume image. In our technique, we use 3D Sobel kernel to compute the gradient of every voxel and rely on nonmaximum suppression to detect 3D Canny edges in a volume image. For color volume images, we need to convert them to grayscale images before edge detection is performed. We have successfully applied our method to the segmentation of various organs and tissues in the Visible Human dataset. Experiments and comparisons demonstrate our method can accurately extract volumetric objects of interest, and outperforms traditional levelset-based segmentation algorithms. 2. Shape prior and its integration with shape alignment within the level-set method An image segmentation method usually starts with some initial information regarding foreground objects and background pixels, which are commonly given through user interaction. With the recent advancement in salient object detection, automatic segmentation of generic objects is made possible. Given an image, a saliency detection model produces a saliency map within which the intensity of a pixel indicates how likely it belongs to a foreground object. Recent salient object detection methods based on deep learning give very good estimation of foreground objects without user interaction, making them ideal choices for automatic initialization of segmentation methods. Our integrated method starts with a deep neural network-based object proposal method for object proposal generation. A nonmaximal suppression over those bounding boxes is then performed to narrow down the locations of potential objects. Given a bounding box of a potential object, its saliency map gives a strong clue on where the object is located as well as the shape of the object. In this project, we use the shape of the detected salient object as a shape prior. In practice, we exploit the DeepContrast saliency detection model proposed by the PI’s own research group for shape prior generation. We use this saliency map based shape prior to initialize the level-set function. Within the saliency map, the foreground is initialized as pixels with saliency values greater than a predefined threshold, and the remaining pixels are treated as the background. The combination of object proposal generation and saliency based shape prior completely eliminates the need for user interaction in locating objects. For the evolution of zero level-set fronts in our integrated level-set method, we design a speed force that exploits both low-level information and high-level information, such as convolutional features and object boundaries extracted from pre-trained deep neural networks. These features are categorized into two kinds, the boundary and region features. The boundary feature controls object boundary localization, and is obtained as follows: (i) we extract object boundary through integrating two edge maps generated by a neural network-based contour detector CEDN and Canny edge detector; (ii) boundary feature is obtained by enhancing the extracted boundary with gradient vector flow (GVF) oriented for propagating the influence of boundaries to nearby regions. Provided with boundary and region features, our method is organized in an iterative two-pass manner. Level-set evolution is exploited to produce a foreground segmentation result with the help of boundary feature and trained foreground classifier. After the level-set method gets converged, the segmentation result is in turn used in re-training a better foreground classifier. The two steps are alternated iteratively until there is no significant change in segmentation result. 3. Generalized level-set method for multiphase image segmentation. For multiphase image segmentation, we propose a new nonlinear embedding, called piecewise flat embedding (PFE), which is solved using a generalized level-set method, called Bregman iterations. PFE attempts to identify segment boundaries while suppressing variations within segments. It is based on the theory of sparse signal recovery since segment boundaries consist of a sparse subset of the original pixels. We adopt an L1-regularized energy term in the formulation to promote sparse solutions. A sparse solution in our context implies that there only exists a sparse subset of point pairs whose distances in the new feature space are sufficiently large, and the distances between the rest of the point pairs are almost zero. Such an embedding essentially form well-separated clusters, each of which is a point cloud tightly distributed around a single center. We further develop an effective numerical solution based on Bregman iterations to our L1-regularized objective function. Bregman iterations are a type of generalized level-set methods that are specifically tailored for sparsity-regularized optimization problems. We devise a two-stage numerical algorithm based on Bregman iterations as well as effective initialization schemes to solve the proposed embedding. Our numerical solution effectively nests two existing algorithms that handle L1 regularization and orthogonality constraints respectively. The first algorithm is the Splitting Orthogonality Constraint (SOC) algorithm capable of enforcing orthogonality constraints. The second one is the Split Bregman algorithm, which solves an L1 regularized optimization problem iteratively by transforming the original optimization into a series of differentiable unconstrained convex optimization problems. We further attempt to promote sparse solutions with multiple dimensions by adopting an Lp-regularized (0 < p <=1) energy term in the objective function. This Lp-regularized embedding is a generalization of the above L1-regularized formulation, with extra space for sparsity pursuit and increased degree of nonconvexity as p becomes smaller. Inspired by iteratively reweighted L1 algorithms (IRL1), we further design an iteratively reweighted algorithm based on the numerical solution to the L1-regularized optimization to solve the more generic Lp-regularized problem. The proposed piecewise flat embedding can be easily integrated into multiphase image segmentation frameworks, including segmentation based on spectral clustering and hierarchical segmentation based on contour detection. Experiments on a popular benchmark (BSDS500) indicate that segmentation algorithms incorporating this embedding can achieve significantly improved results in both frameworks. Such segmentation algorithms integrating our embedding also produce state-of-the-art performance on three other benchmark datasets (SBD, MSRC and PASCAL Context).

Develop a deformable shape prior and its integration with shape alignment. The shape alignment process is iterative and resembles that for active contours and levelsets. It can tolerate shape distortion incurred by changing viewing directions.

719313.label: Major findings and research outcome
719313.value: Incorporating a supervised probabilistic classifier within the level set framework is well suited for 3D medical image segmentation and high-quality results can be achieved. This finding is reported in the fourth research output in Part C. Research outcome associated with this finding includes effective volume texture descriptors and volume edge detectors as well as an EM-style method for iteratively improving the performance of both supervised classification and level-set evolution. Integrating a deep learning based shape prior with shape alignment is well suited for automating the initialization of the level-set method. Integrating deep learning based contour detection with the level-set method can further improve the segmentation performance. These findings are reported in the first research output in Part C. Research outcome associated with these findings includes an effective multi-pass level-set based pipeline for automatic object extraction that incorporates deep learning based object proposal generation, salient object detection and object contour detection. Nonlinear piecewise constant embedding can significantly benefit multiphase image segmentation. Piecewise constant embedding is closely related to sparse signal recovery and can be obtained by solving an optimization problem with an L1- or Lp-regularized (0 < p <=1) objective function. Such an optimization problem can be effectively solved using a generalized level-set method, called Bregman iterations. These findings are reported in the third and fifth research outputs in Part C. Research outcome associated with these findings includes a piecewise flat embedding based on an L1-or Lp-regularized (0 < p <=1) objective function, a two-stage numerical algorithm based on Bregman iterations as well as effective initialization schemes to solve the proposed embedding, and multiphase image segmentation algorithms incorporating the proposed embedding.

719313.value: This research topic has been well explored during the course of this project, and we do not plan to propose further action.

719313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
719313.value: Image segmentation is a fundamental and necessary operation in many tasks in image-based graphics, computer vision, and medical imaging. Image segments can be grouped into layers that are important for image-based rendering, occlusion analysis and scene understanding. In computer graphics, there is a long history of using images and photos as the raw data for further manipulation and synthesis. For example, image matting can be considered as a type of “soft” segmentation that generates a continuous alpha channel as the segmentation mask. Segmentation is essential in many image-based graphics problems, such as extracting, removing or replacing objects in images. In medical imaging, 3D image segmentation often serves as an indispensable preprocessing step for many other operations. The level-set method and its generalizations represent an important approach for (medical) image segmentation. A significant limitation of level-set based methods is that they are vulnerable to local minima. Consequently, level-set based segmentation results are very sensitive to initialization. In this project, we propose new level-set based segmentation algorithms that overcome this limitation by incorporating machine learning and classification. Our suite of new techniques make it possible for the level set method to realize its full potential in segmentation.

719813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
719813.value: Emulsions, droplets of one liquid dispersed in another immiscible liquid, are widely used in food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical formulations. In addition to direct applications, they are also used as templates for fabricating useful particles, for example, drug delivery vehicles. The use of emulsions is critically dependent on their size: in medical in vivo applications, large particles can be easily detected by the immune system, whereas small particles can be rapidly excreted. Thus, the size distribution of particles affects their performance. Traditionally, emulsions are generated by stirring two immiscible liquids, similar to preparing a vinaigrette. Despite its robustness and relative ease of application, the method provides little control over emulsion attributes. One recent approach to address this problem is to prepare emulsions in tiny channels with diameters in the tens of micrometers. This droplet microfluidic technology allows the routine production of emulsions with superior encapsulation efficiency, better defined properties and more complex structures, thereby creating new opportunities for applications such as drug delivery that require high encapsulation efficiency and the tunable release of active ingredients. However, current droplet microfluidic technologies are best suited to generating emulsions and particles with sizes greater than ten micrometers. Further size reduction is challenged by the need for submicron-sized channels, which require high pressure to operate and are easily clogged by debris. This challenge significantly limits the use of microfluidics in such areas as intracellular drug delivery. One way to achieve a significant droplet size reduction without reducing the channel size is to electrically charge the fluids, leading to tiny liquid jets. Although this approach has been demonstrated as a viable way to generate sub-micron droplets, its use to generate particles and capsules with a complicated architecture remains poorly explored. The aim of the proposed project is to address this important subject by developing a physical understanding of electrostatics in micro-scale multi-phase flows, developing an electro-microfluidic platform for forming particles with a tunable size and customizable architecture, demonstrating the scale-up production of these particles through parallelization, and applying these technologies to generate designer sub-micron structures. In the short term, the study will lead to a fundamental scientific understanding of the formation of small droplets from a charged jet and technological development of an electro-microfluidic platform. In the long run, it will contribute to the next generation of emulsion formulation technologies and offer better options for applications that require small emulsions and particles. 乳液是由一種溶劑分散在另一種不相溶的溶劑中形成的，它們在食品、個人用品和藥品等方面有著廣泛的應用。除了這些應用外，乳液也可用做模版來製造微顆粒，例如藥物傳輸微粒。乳液的尺寸在一定程度上決定了它們的應用：在人體體內的應用，尺寸過大的顆粒很容易被免疫系統檢測到，而較小的顆粒就很快被代謝。因此，顆粒的尺寸分佈影響它們的實際應用效果。傳統製備乳液的工藝是通過機械攪拌兩種不相溶的溶劑，就像生活中製作油醋汁一樣。傳統工作簡單易操作，但幾乎不能控制所製備出的乳液的性質。 最近，用微米級的通道來製備乳液的工藝解決了對乳液性質的控制問題。液滴微流體技術提供性質精確可控的乳液液滴，這些液滴有著出眾的包載率，結構複雜卻可控，為需要高包載率和釋放可調的應用，如傳輸藥物等提供了新的契機。但是，現有的液滴微流體技術一般用來製備尺寸在幾十微米及以上的材料。在此基礎上縮小尺寸可以用過進一步縮小通道的尺寸到次微米級， 但是次微米級的通道十分容易被碎片堵住，通道內的壓強也十分大，這些都帶來技術難題。所以液滴微流體技術在細胞內藥物傳輸等方面應用就被大大限制了。另外一種大幅度縮小尺寸的方法是使帶電的溶劑在電場中形成極小的射流而斷裂。雖然這種方法曾被用來製備次微米級的液滴，但如何用此種方法製備出結構複雜的次微米級的顆粒或膠囊還未被充分研究過。 本項目的立項目的是通過對微米級多相流的靜電受力的物理研究，開發出電液微流體平台來製備結構精確可調的液滴及顆粒，並在此基礎上通過平行操作來大規模生產特需設計的微米級結構。 短期來看，這項研究會對帶電射流斷裂形成小液滴這個物理現象帶來更深更全面的理解，並帶來電液微流體平台的技術開發。長期來看，本項研究會為下一代乳液製備技術做出貢獻，並且為所有涉及次微米級、納米級乳液和顆粒的應用提供更好的選擇。

719813.label: Realisation of objectives
719813.value: The objectives have been achieved: 1. We have investigated the effects of variables, such as viscosity and interfacial tensions, on the behaviors of emulsion droplets in electrical fields in micro-scaled channels and understood how their dynamics depend on dimensionless numbers, such as capillary number, while keeping other conditions constant. In particular, during the studies, we discovered a new dynamical regime between two charged droplets in n enclosed device. 2. We have applied electro-microfluidic approach to generate particles of different size, shape and structure. For instance non-spherical alginate were generated in a controlled manner. The approach has also been demonstrated to fabricate aqueous-aqueous-droplet-templated particles with controlled morphology and shape. Droplets prepared have been solidified using different strategies, including common ones, such as UV-polymerized, heating induced and ion-gelated, as well as a new osmo-solidification approach. 3. We have demonstrated scalable approaches to form electro-microfluidic devices with more channels. For example, 3D printed nozzles can generate particles with sophisticated geometry. The works also inspired us to explore another scalable technique for forming droplets by taking advantage of the breakup of the liquid layers for forming droplets. Moreover, we also explore approach to minimize the droplet size by reducing further manipulating the folding of the interface.

719813.label: Major findings and research outcome
719813.value: - Introducing electrodes in designing microfluidic nozzles enable better control over the properties of droplets generated, such as size and shape. - New fluid dynamical regime and transition in electrified systems have been discovered, with potential applications in material fabrication and beyond. - Electro-microfluidic systems are more amenable to integration for manufacturing of droplets with a smaller size. - Advantages offered by electro-microfluidic platforms can be extended beyond conventional emulsion drops to drops with ultra-low interfacial tension, organic-solvent-free drops as well as particle-stabilized drops. Most of the results have been presented in various international conferences (e.g. MRS meeting, APS march meeting, etc.) and published in respected international journals (e.g. Physics of Fluids, Biomicrofluidics, Lab on a Chip, Soft Matter, Langmuir, etc.), as shown in Part C. Note that at least one related manuscript is approaching the final stage of editorial process in a top journal appealing a general audience (e.g. PNAS). Other results are being integrated with other applications and wrapped up for publication due to their potential for a greater impact.

719813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
719813.value: The research has demonstrated excellent potential to benefit a wide range of applications that use droplets as templates, such as design of drug carriers, encapsulation for food and beverage applications, as well as cosmetic applications. The proposed course of action include discussing with potential industrial and/or clinical collaborators who are closer to the market and thus will be in a better position to advise on the most suitable applications. In addition, we also propose to approach machine automation experts to discuss possible development of machines that utilize the electro-microfluidic platforms for better translation of the outcomes of the proposal. These efforts will be facilitated by research grants, such as those from the Innovation and Technology Fund (ITF) of Hong Kong, and some other funding sources that connect the industries and academia in Hong Kong, Shenzhen and Guangdong province, where manufacturing is very mature. Some of the discussions and developmental plans have already started, with great interest from various collaborators. We expect to get to the stage where we are ready to submit research proposals soon.

719813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
719813.value: Droplets are ubiquitous, and encountered in food, cosmetics, paints, personal care products and many others. New formulations with a different function require new techniques to form the droplets. In this project, we investigate the benefits that we can derive from electrically charging droplets in devices that consist of microchannel(s), known as microfluidic devices. We developed a physical understanding of the effects of electrical charging on the properties of the droplets. The understanding has led to discovery of new phenomena exhibited by the charged droplets, creating opportunities to form droplets with different size and shape. We also explored different ways electrodes can be incorporated into the devices, and different manners electric fields can be implemented. The approach has also been demonstrated in different types of droplet systems, which are also used as templates for conversion to particles. In doing so, users of the final applications can choose from a wider range of techniques, and droplets for meeting the needs of their target applications. We also explored droplet formation devices that are more easily scalable. Our works are expected to facilitate the development of new formulations that can find uses in food and beverage, cosmetics, drug delivery and other applications that involve encapsulations.

739113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
739113.value: 许多公司在其日常运作中消耗巨量的交易所交易的大宗商品。其采购计划通常用库存控制模型来确定。由于大宗商品价格的频繁波动，一些公司也采用大宗商品衍生工具来规避采购价格的不确定性。保证避险决定与采购计划相符对取得最佳避险效果至关重要。为了解决这个问题，我们通过多期随机库存控制模型，对采购价格随市场波动的商品，在规避风险的情况下同时优化库存和避险决策。 本项目将致力于刻画最优的库存及避险策略。我们会分别就离散时间及连续时间模型，在有限及无限的计划时段下进行研究，并将侧重于以下方面： - 市场上交易着许多大宗商品衍生工具。我们能否仅采用其中一部分的衍生工具来达到最优避险效果？这些衍生工具又应该如何选择？在运用金融工具规避运营风险的相关文献中，本研究是对稀疏最优解的首次探讨。 - 最优库存策略是否是独立于现货价格演变主观概率的基本库存策略？虽然类似的结果在其它假设条件下已经被证明，但这些文献中也肯定了在我们的模型设定下证明这一结果的挑战性。 - 最佳策略是否对各种变量和参数存在单调性？例如，我们会研究（1）最优基本库存水平是否对现货价格递减，（2）决策者对风险的态度如何影响最优库存及避险策略，（3）某种用于避险的衍生工具的持仓量是否对最优订货点量存在单调性，以及（4）引入金融避险是否会增加或减少最优订货点量。虽然不考虑金融避险的风险中性模型已经研究了其中的一些性质，但现有文献已证实将这些单调性拓展到风险规避模型中并不容易。 我们已经在离散时间的有限时段模型的研究方面取得了初步的成果。对以上这些问题的解答可以在业界确定库存补货及避险策略时提供指导性的管理启示，同时可以在数值研究中通过减少最优解的搜索区域，从而显著地降低计算量。 此外，我们将研究上述问题在两方面的扩展。虽然文献中广泛采用交易成本为零的假设，我们会在模型中引入交易成本，以更好地对实际情况建模。另一方面的扩展则会考虑决策者通过动态定价将现货价格的不确定性（部分）转移给客户的情况。我们会对这些扩展的最优政策进行分析，同时也会探讨它们独有的研究问题，例如，交易成本或定价决策会怎样影响最优避险策略。

739113.label: Realisation of objectives
739113.value: This project has led to 1 paper published in Production and Operations Management (Lu et al. 2016), 1 paper published in European Journal of Operational Research (Liu et at. 2015), 1 PhD thesis (Zhai 2015), and 6 presentations in international conferences. Furthermore, we are also preparing the following working paper, which will be soon submitted for peer review at Production and Operations Management: Song, M. and Y. Zhai. 2018. Optimal inventory control with financial hedging under stochastic purchasing prices. Working paper. The Hong Kong Polytechnic University. The project objectives have been fully achieved. The details are provided as follows: 1. Finite-horizon discrete-time inventory control problem with financial hedging: This problem considers a company that consumes a certain commodity in its operations over a planning horizon consisting of a finite number of periods. This commodity can be procured from the spot market at a price varying over time stochastically. A set of derivatives based on this commodity are also liquidly traded in the financial market. Therefore, besides keeping inventories on hand, the company may choose to hold a portfolio of the derivatives to hedge the risk associated with the uncertain spot price. This objective is to jointly optimize the on-hand inventory and the hedging portfolio in a risk-averse setting. We have constructed the dynamic programming model, characterized the optimal inventory control and financial hedging policies, and studied the monotonic properties of the optimal decisions. Furthermore, for the purpose of comparison, this project has also studied the risk-neutral and risk-averse inventory control problems without financial hedging, respectively. We have constructed the corresponding dynamic programming models, characterized the optimal inventory control policies, and studied how the parameters of the optimal policies change with respect to the model inputs. Based on these results, we have investigated the impact of risk aversion and financial hedging on the optimal inventory decisions. 2. Finite-horizon continuous-time inventory control problem with financial hedging: This problem considers the case that the demand of the commodity follows a combined Poisson process and the log-price of the commodity is assumed to be an Ito diffusion. We have constructed the dynamic programming model, characterized the optimal inventory control and financial hedging policies, and studied the monotonic properties of the optimal policies. 3. Infinite-horizon inventory control problem with financial hedging: This problem targets to optimize the inventory and hedging decisions over an infinite planning horizon. We have constructed both the discrete-time and continuous-time dynamic programming models, characterized the optimal inventory control and financial hedging policies, and studied the monotonic properties of the optimal policies. 4. Inventory control problem with financial hedging and transaction costs for derivatives: The aforementioned problems assume that the transaction cost in the financial market is negligible. This assumption, although common in the finance literature, is relaxed in this problem. We have constructed both the discrete-time and continuous-time dynamic programming models, characterized the optimal inventory control and financial hedging policies, and studied how the parameters of the optimal policies change with respect to the transaction cost rate. 5. Joint inventory and pricing problem with financial hedging: This problem considers the joint decision of inventory, pricing, and hedging, which captures the practice of sharing the uncertainty in the commodity price with customers through pricing. We have constructed both the discrete-time and continuous-time dynamic programming models, characterized the optimal inventory, pricing, and hedging policies, and studied the monotonic properties of the optimal policies. Besides, we also analyzed a generalized model where the revenue function is not known completely. For this model with incomplete information, an approximation algorithm has been proposed, its worst-case performance bound has been analyzed, and extensive numerical experiments have been conducted to evaluate its performance.

739113.label: Major findings and research outcome
739113.value: This project has generated 2 journal papers, 1 PhD thesis, and 6 conference presentations. One working paper will also be soon submitted for publication. The major findings of the project are summarized as follows: 1. Finite-horizon discrete-time model with financial hedging (see Song and Zhai 2018 and Zhai 2015). The structural properties of the optimal inventory and hedging policy are summarized as follows: (i) The optimal inventory policy is a base-stock policy depending on the spot price. (ii) Under the arbitrage-free assumption, a hedging portfolio is optimal if and only if it satisfies a set of linear equations specified by a risk-neutral measure. (iii) Under the arbitrage-free assumption and a sufficiently diversified financial market, the optimal inventory decision can be obtained independent of the optimal hedging decision. (iv) Conditions are identified under which the optimal inventory or hedging decision is monotone with respect to the spot price, the inventory position, or the risk-aversion parameter. The risk-neutral and risk-averse models without financial hedging are also studied. The state-dependent base-stock inventory policy remain optimal. The optimal decision for the risk-neutral model is monotone with respect to the spot price, but this property does not hold for the risk-averse model. We have also identified conditions under which the optimal base-stock levels of these two models are higher (lower, resp.) than those for the model with hedging. 2 & 3. Finite-horizon continuous-time / infinite-horizon models. We have the same results as those for the finite-horizon discrete-time model. 4. Models with transaction costs. The optimal inventory policy is a base-stock policy depending on both the spot price and the hedging position. For the optimal hedging policy, the hedging portfolio will not be rebalanced as long as it falls in a certain region that depends on the spot price. Numerical results illustrate how the optimal decisions change with respect to the transaction cost. 5. Inventory-pricing models (see Song and Zhai 2018 and Lu et al. 2016). The optimal inventory-pricing policy is shown to be a base-stock list-price policy depending on the spot price. Properties analogous to (ii), (iii) and (iv) for the inventory model is established as well. We also consider the case where the revenue is only known at some discrete selling prices. An approximation approach is developed based on approximating the incomplete revenue function. The worst-case performance bound is established for the risk-neutral model. Numerical results validate that the approximation algorithm performs strongly.

739113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
739113.value: In this project, we focus on the uncertainty in the purchase price of one commodity. A natural generalization is to consider the uncertainty in the purchase prices of multiple commodities. For instance, for a retailer that imports multiple products from overseas, exchange rate fluctuations will result in the changes in the purchase prices of all these products. South China Morning Post reported in March 2018 that 759 Store, a leading Hong Kong chain store specializing in Japanese goods, suffered significantly in early 2016 due to a strong Japanese yen. In response to the depreciation of the Hong Kong dollar in early 2018, it had marked up some of the recently imported products by 3 to 5 per cent. In this setting, although the uncertainty in the purchase prices can be modeled through one factor, i.e., the exchange rate, the problem cannot be decomposed into multiple single-commodity models proposed in this project because the hedging decision affects the inventory decisions of all commodities. It is of practical importance to study such a multi-commodity inventory (and pricing) model with financial hedging and we leave this for future research.

739113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
739113.value: The market traded commodities are crucial to many companies. For instance, crude oil is the most important raw material used by the refining and chemical industry. Physical inventories of the commodity are kept to satisfy the consumption needs, which are exposed to a major risk due to the fluctuations in the commodity price. To hedge the risk, companies often hold a portfolio of financial derivative based on the commodity. Since the best hedging effect can only be achieved when the hedging and procurement decisions are jointly optimized, this project studies a risk-averse multi-period stochastic inventory model with financial hedging for a commodity whose price is subject to market uncertainty. Variations of the model are also proposed in a continuous-time setting, over an infinite planning horizon, with transaction cost considerations, and/or to incorporate pricing decisions. For each model, we have characterized the optimal inventory and hedging policies and analyzed the structural properties of the optimal policies. These results could serve as managerial insights providing valuable guidelines to industrial practitioners when making the inventory and/or hedging decisions. They can also be used to effectively accelerate the computation of finding numerical optimal solutions.

739413.label: Project Title(Chinese)
739413.value: 多維度超音波形變影像技術用於評估心臟組織之非等向性

739413.label: Project Objectives
739413.value: (i) Develop and assess the multidimensional ultrasound deformation imaging (MDUDI) method with finite-element models of anisotropic media. A finite-element (FE) model will first be used to determine the mechanical response of anisotropic (transversely isotropic and orthotropic) soft tissue under dynamic deformation. An ultrasound image formation program will then be utilized to simulate sequential ultrasonic images of deformed tissue possessing acoustic anisotropy as a result of the FE fiber structure. The new MDUDI technique will be developed based on the PI’s prior work [8-10, 18] to assess all the mechanical parameters (displacement, strain, rotation, twist) in various (ultrasound Cartesian, cardiac, local fiber, principal) coordinates from the simulated ultrasonic images. The relationship between anisotropic tissue structure and all the estimated mechanical parameters will be fully investigated. (ii) Develop anisotropic tissue-mimicking phantoms for MDUDI to examine the relation between structural and kinematic anisotropy. Deformable anisotropic tissue-mimicking phantoms will be developed in a controlled experimental setup. Layer specific kinematics will be assessed by MDUDI to verify the effect of local fiber orientation on the mechanical behavior of anisotropic tissue. The performance of MDUDI will subsequently be tested using an ellipsoidal anisotropic phantom, which will be constructed and deformed to simulate realistic dynamics of anisotropic myocardium. (iii) Test the feasibility of MDUDI in depicting the anisotropic mechanical behavior ex vivo and in vivo; determine the potential of shear deformation in detecting pathological myocardium. Excised large animal hearts deformed in a controlled manner will be assessed with MDUDI for their realistic geometry, fiber architecture, acoustic anisotropy, and the deformation behavior. The evaluation of the structural and kinematic changes by ultrasound strain imaging methods in congenital heart disease, not yet achieved extensively to date, will be the major exploratory clinical application of MDUDI. Shear deformation, which is often neglected throughout the literature, will be estimated to characterize the pathological myocardial region.

739413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
739413.value: 心血管疾病為世界十大死因之首，因此，可靠性非侵入式影像技術不僅急需被開發以用於預測與診斷心功能不全，並且亦有助於了解心血管疾病演進之基本機制。 相較於其他醫學影像系統，超音波影像仍是臨床上診斷心功能之首要選擇，因為它能實時提供跳動中的心臟的結構、運動狀態和血流狀況。有別於心臟腔室體積量測，例如：射出分率，此類總體性數值，心臟超音波應變影像可以量化區域性之心肌運動狀態。此種影像技術已於近年內快速發展為具潛力之診斷工具，以利偵測心臟疾病引起之心肌缺損。 至今，為數可觀之研究將主力放在採用現有之應變影像技術來診斷多種心臟疾病，例如：心肌缺氧、心肌梗塞與擴張型心肌病。然而，在其被廣泛應用於臨床診斷前，我們必須先解決幾項關鍵技術問題：一、在超音波系統固有之不佳橫向解析度下，準確量測橫向運動；二、評估所有運動量參數，包括位移、應變、旋轉和扭轉等之靈敏度和專一性，便於心肌之特性描述；三、針對正常收縮以及有缺損的心臟建立出心肌結構，亦即肌纖維走向，和運動力學間的關係。 此研究計畫涵蓋兩項主要目標。一為研發出一個新穎多維度超音波形變影像技術，並試圖克服前述之所有技術限制，以完整並精確地計算出所有心肌運動參數。另一為使用此影像技術以檢測並且證實非等向性之心肌結構對區域心肌運動之影響。此新技術包含原始信號班點追蹤和應變計算，並且透過座標轉換考慮幾個主要空間座標系下之運動狀態。此外，本研究亦將藉由電腦模擬、體外心臟實驗和臨床案例去探討具最佳敏感度之運動量參數與空間座標系。 本計畫預期建立出一非侵入式、穩健和可量化之多維度超音波形變影像技術，以達評估心臟固有之力學非等向性。其架構和產出將有助於基本心臟電力學、三維心臟電腦模擬、早期心肌疾病診斷和監測心肌功能變異過程。

739413.label: Realisation of objectives
739413.value: Three objectives have all been realized with further details provided below. Objective 1: This objective was built upon computer simulations for the development of the proposed multidimensional ultrasound deformation imaging method. Unlike existing literature which only evaluated ultrasound methods for isotropic homogeneous soft tissues, our study targets at the heart muscle, which is anisotropic and inhomogeneous. We first developed a simulation framework that incorporates finite-element models of anisotropic soft media and an ultrasound image simulation tool (Part C: Research Output- 8, No. 3-4, 10). An indispensable fully programmable open architecture ultrasound imaging system and motion stages were procured under this funding support to realize all the objectives. In the first place, we validated our developed multidimensional ultrasound deformation imaging method (Part C: Research Output- 8, No. 3) from simulated models with ground truth. Using the simulation models, we were able to develop and optimize the method to its highest performance. Objective 2: The simulations in the first phase of the study were the prerequisite of in vitro experiments. We then developed a protocol of making transversely isotropic tissue-mimicking phantoms using polymers whose stiffness and degree of anisotropy could be controlled. We evaluated the performance of our developed multidirectional ultrasound deformation imaging method in both phantoms and in vitro muscle samples (Part C: Research Output- 8, No. 5, 9, 12). Transverse isotropic phantoms required careful selection of the chemical compounds whose acoustic and mechanical properties could mimic real tissues. Now, bulk and hollow cylindrical transverse isotropic phases were able to be made reproducibly, but we are testing a new way of making such type of phantom that could take care of the structure in a less labor intensive way. Objective 3: We lastly evaluated the performance of our developed multidimensional ultrasound deformation imaging method in the in vivo diseased nerve and heart, both of which are deemed anisotropic tissues (Part C: Research Output- 8, No. 1, 8, 11; Research Output- 9, No. 16). The requirement of the imaging frame rate for the anisotropic nerve was less loose than that for the heart muscle. The successful application of our developed deformation imaging method on the early detection of the nerve pathology led to the performance evaluation for the heart muscle. Our discussion with cardiologist collaborators made us focus on the critical evaluation of post-infarction heart which may potentially remodel to be better or worse, progressing to heart failure. Although our preliminary results show the good performance of our multidimensional deformation imaging method, especially the introduction of unconventional deformation components, we discovered that front-end image formation played an equally crucial role. This highlighted our research outputs and future directions as stated in Section 6.

739413.label: Major findings and research outcome
739413.value: Objective 1: We have substantiated our hypothesis and revealed that muscle anisotropy due to its intrinsic fiber structure greatly influenced the ultrasound quantification of muscle kinematics in this simulation framework (Part C: Research Output- 8, No. 4). In addition, we uncovered that ultrasound quantitative analysis of the tissues was directly and greatly affected by ultrasound image formation methods, especially in muscles, which are anisotropic (Part C: Research Output- 8, No. 2, 4; Research Output- 9, No. 5). Our collective findings suggest that uniform spatial resolution throughout the imaging field of view achieved by coherent summation of received signals in ultrasound is essential for quantifying tissue properties and kinematics. Objective 2: Our results show that structural and thus mechanical anisotropy caused differential deformations in multi-dimensions and inherent differential accuracy of deformation estimation by ultrasound (Part C: Research Output- 8, No. 5, 9, 12). Beyond this, we further observed that nonlinear behavior differed in multi-dimensions of a transverse isotropic soft medium and discovered that our multidimensional ultrasound deformation imaging could be combined with another in-house technique of ours to evaluate the nonlinear behavior of the muscle (Part C: Research Output- 8, No. 9, 12). We are looking into the theoretical and experimental corroborations and deriving a potential index for clinical diagnosis of muscle abnormality (Part C: Research Output- 8, No. 9, 12). Objective 3: We found that our developed method could differentiate abnormal from normal tissue regions. In particular, our method could yield shear deformations accurately to improve the differentiation sensitivity of abnormal from normal tissues (Part C: Research Output- 8, No. 1, 8, 11; Research Output- 9, No. 16).

739413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
739413.value: Beyond what is stated in the proposed project, the findings from Objectives 1 and 2 led us to look into front-end ultrasound image formation, whose quality highly impacts the deformation estimation. We have therefore developed new ultrasound image formation methodologies, two of which have been published office (Part C: Research Output- 8, No. 6-7) and one of which has been filed to US patent office (Part C: Research Output- 12, No. 1). We will continue this work and explore its feasibility of mapping blood flow. We have been developing a new way of making anisotropic fibrous tissue-mimicking phantoms by 3D printing hydrogel. A commercial 3D printer has been modified to successfully print out directly soft fibers on the order of sub-milliliter in diameter. We continue optimizing the printing materials and parameters. More in vivo data are need to evaluate the diagnostic performance of our developed method. In view of the enormous healthcare burden of heart failure (HF), new treatments for HF prevention have been proposed and advanced. Our developed method can be a potential non-invasive tool of monitoring the post-treatment efficacy using animal models in collaboration with HKU cardiologists who develop new treatment for infarct heart prior to heart failure.

739413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
739413.value: Cardiovascular disease is the leading killer worldwide, and its healthcare burden is foreseen to escalate in this aging society. In this research project, we developed a new ultrasound deformation imaging method that can non-invasively measure regional contraction and relaxation of the heart muscle within a heartbeat as a reliable, safe, fast diagnostic tool of cardiac function. We uncovered that the intrinsic muscle fiber structure affected quantification accuracy and suggested that a quantitative methodology adaptive to the fiber-direction-dependent kinematic behavior and providing multi-parametric indices be devised. Moreover, we developed a new ultrasound image formation technique that outperformed existing ones in terms of imaging speed, penetration, and noise level. This new image formation technique is shown to further improve the performance of our deformation imaging method and beyond. Ultrasound imaging is the predominant imaging tool of the heart in the clinic, and hand-held ultrasound devices become commercially available. Our research project findings and developed methods can be incorporated into these commercial systems and are aspired to pave the way for comprehensive functional assessment of the cardiovascular system by point-of-care ultrasound at low cost.

739713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
739713.value: A reliable supply of electricity is essential to sound economic development and societal vitality. Recent catastrophic blackouts in North America, Europe, and India serve as powerful reminders of the need for a reliable, resilient, and responsive power grid. This requirement can be achieved by either redundant investment in costly facilities or sophisticated operating strategies of existing facilities, or both. In the context of the smart grid, this proposal addresses the issues associated with the second approach. The architecture of a strategic defence system (SDS) in the new energy paradigm, as well as some selected essential applications for vulnerability mitigation and outage restoration, will be extensively researched in this proposed project. By integrating state-of-the-art technologies on renewables, responsive loads, information, and communication, a smart grid promises a clean, efficient, reliable, resilient, and responsive electric energy infrastructure. However, due to the increasing complexity of power grids, and the growing integration of variable and uncertain components, such as renewables and responsive loads, the impact of power grids on reliability has yet to be seen. An established SDS should have the capability to implement accurate vulnerability assessment, prompt violation mitigation and rapid outage reconfiguration. This proposed research project systematically addresses the architecture of SDS that is compatible with emerging technologies for wide-area system control and coordination in power systems, focusing on some selected critical functionalities. This research covers three inter-related aspects: real-time information processing and vulnerability identification, vulnerability mitigation, and outages restoration. First, two distributed state estimation methods will be built using advanced statistical re-sampling methods. Based on the estimated state, coherent condition-driven risk indicators will be established using the security region technology. Second, a game-theoretic framework will be established to determine load responses for mitigating the identified real power violations; meanwhile, electric springs will be introduced to mitigate voltage-related violations. The third task will address the identified outage restoration. The impact of renewables during restoration, as well as the branch and bound scheme associated with the interior point methods for load pickup, will be studied. Hybrid CPU-GPU architectures will be developed to implement the tremendous computational burden of time-domain simulation in the aforementioned research tasks. This research project is built upon our past efforts and will contribute to state-of-the-art research. In the long run, the accomplishments will represent a systematic methodology towards implanting a strategic defense system in smart grids context. The research project will also provide ample opportunities for student training. 可靠的電力供應對於健康的經濟發展和社會進步至關重要。近期分別在北美、歐洲以及印度發生的災難性的大停電提醒我們建設一個可靠的、有彈性的、以及響應迅捷的電力網絡的重要性。這一目標可通過投資建設更多昂貴的設備以及在電網現有設備基礎上構建更成熟的運行策略來實現。在智能電網的背景下，本項目旨在研究與運行策略相關的問題，包括在新的能源結構下電力系統戰略防禦系統的架構設計，潛在脆弱性消除方法以及發生停電事故后的系統恢復策略等方面。 智能電網將整合可再生能源、負荷響應、信息技術以及通信科技等方面的最新成果，試圖建立一個清潔、高效、可靠、具有彈性和響應迅捷的電能供應體系。隨著可再生能源和可響應負載等具備不可控特性元件的不斷接入，電網的複雜程度日益增加，這些新的特性對電網可靠性的影響亟待深入研究。針對新電網結構構建的戰略防禦系統，應該具備精確的系統運行脆弱性評估、及時的故障消除以及快速的停電恢復的能力。 本項目將系統地研究智能電網條件下戰略防禦系統的構建問題，使其具有廣域系統控制和協調的能力。本項目主要針對以下三個關鍵問題開展研究：實時的資訊處理和脆弱性識別，脆弱性消除策略構建和停電的快速恢復方法。首先，識別系統的狀態：針對系統中元件的隨機特性，利用統計采樣方法，建立兩種分布式的狀態估計方法。基於狀態估計的結果，利用安全域技術，建立條件驅動的風險指標。第二，研究負荷響應策略以消除系統的擾動：利用博弈論構建有功負荷響應的決策方案，兼顧系統安全和用戶效益，同時引入電力彈簧消除電壓相關的擾動。第三，迅捷的停電恢復策略構建。基於以往的研究成果，本項目主要研究可再生能源對恢復過程的影響，以及基於分支定界和內點法的含網絡約束的負荷恢復策略。爲了應對研究任務中涉及的巨大運算量以及時域仿真的需求，本項目還將開發CPU-GPU的混合計算體系。 本研究項目將基於本研究團隊過去的成果，試圖應對最前沿的科學需求。長遠來看，本研究的成果將對智能電網的戰略防禦系統提出一個系統化的方法。此外，本研究項目也將為學生提供充分的學習和研究的機會。

739713.label: Realisation of objectives
739713.value: This project addresses the architecture of a strategic defense system. This architecture mitigates vulnerability and restores outage under the new energy paradigm. All proposed objectives have been accomplished and summarized as papers, technical reports, software, and a book chapter. The findings of this project provide essential theoretical support for establishing the defense system. The research accomplishments of this project include vulnerability measurement, vulnerability mitigation technology based on the vulnerability measurement, load restoration method, and highly efficient algorithms to implement the proposed technology. (1)Research accomplishments were summarized in 14 top-tier journal papers (one paper is under review) and 16 conference papers. 3 papers in IEEE Trans. on Smart Grids, 4 papers in IEEE Trans. on Power Systems, 1 papers in IEEE Trans. on Industrial Informatics, 1 paper in IEEE Trans. on Sustainable Energy, 1 paper in IEEE Trans. on Power Delivery, 2 paper in IET Generation Transmission & Distribution, and 1 paper in IEEE Power and Energy Magazine. (2) The restoration method proposed in this project has been used in Guangdong Power Grid. The accomplished entitled “Power System Restoration with Fast-cut-back Units in Guangdong Power Grid”, awarded the First Class Award for Progress in Science and Technology, Guangdong Power Grid Corporation in 2015 [Part C. Conference 4]. (3) Some highly efficient algorithms for large-scale power system restoration [Part C. Journal 1, 4, 12, Conference 5, 7, 9] were integrated into the software development commissioned by Electric Power Research Institute, USA. SRN 4.0 was successfully released in 2015. (4) The condition-based maintenance strategies and lifecycle management have been used in Zhejiang Power Grid [Part C. Journal 3, Conference 2, 6]. (5) Partly supported by this project, the PI has graduated 3 Ph.D students and 2 more Ph.D students are in training. (6) Supported by this project, 3 undergraduate students research helpers have been trained. (7) Some accomplishments for uncertainty analysis were summarized in a book chapter: Y. Hou, C.-C. Liu, and H. Salazar, "Electricity Price as a Stochastic Process," in Advances in Electric Power and Energy, IEEE Press/Wiley books. (8) Some databases and related results have been released on the PI’s website and benefit other researchers. The accomplished objectives are: 1. Vulnerability measurement methods - Situation awareness with distributed state estimation: This research proposed a distributed dynamic state estimation method for multi-area systems with PMUs’ measurements. Due to the computational tractability and information privacy, a multi-area distributed model has been used. An extended Kalman filter with equality constraints based on PMU measurements was proposed. This strategy ensures the consistency of the boundary buses connecting the multi-area systems. The obtained information was used to construct vulnerability measures [Part C. Journal 5]. - Measuring condition-driven vulnerability: This research quantified the risk of a given operating point for a power system with renewables, including controllability of the conventional generators, transmission systems, and variability /uncertainty of the renewable energy sources. The steady-state security region was constructed. A stochastic differential equation modeled renewables. The Fourier-Motzkin elimination and Chebychev center was used. The risk was defined as the expected exit-time for renewable outputs leaving the uncontrollable region [Part C Conference 1]. -Assessing event-driven vulnerability due to loss of components and condition-driven vulnerability due lack of flexibility: We quantify the frequency, magnitude, and intensity of potential loss-of-load due to loss of components and injections of variable/uncertain renewables. Unexpected transmission/generation outages and N-k contingency were modeled as trigger events; variability and uncertainty of renewable, spinning reserve and corrective control limit constraints were a model as system essential condition. The potential loss-of-load was quantified by a two-stage robust optimization model [Part C, Journal 7]. 2. Vulnerability mitigation technology -Mitigating vulnerability by enhancing equipment’s health: We proposed a dynamic coordinated condition-based maintenance strategy to mitigate the vulnerability. Component deterioration was modeled as a Markov process with interactions between different maintenance strategies on various components, as well as influences on the operation of the entire system. It was solved by a backward induction algorithm associated with a searching space reduction approach. The results have been used in Zhejiang Power Grid[Part C, Journal 4, Conference 2, 6]. -Mitigating the voltage and frequency vulnerability with Electric Springs: To mitigate the vulnerability due to voltage and frequency fluctuations, a control method of electric springs for the phase angle and amplitude of the voltage were proposed. The dynamic load response for the active power and reactive power were implemented. A distributed control strategy were proposed for multi-ESs with limited communication. [Part C Journal 9, 14, Conference 12]. -Sequential risk-limiting dispatch to mitigate vulnerability: We proposed an operating strategy to mitigate the vulnerability with updated prediction information for uncertainties of renewables generations. The multi-period risk-limiting dispatch method covers network constraints, multiple delivery periods, and alternative risk index. The risk-limiting unit commitment and sequential dispatch methods are constructed with accepted risk. [Part C Journal 8, 11, 13, Conference 8, 16]. The methods to operate the system with uncertainties were summarized in [Part C Journal 2]. -Dynamic game based cyber vulnerability mitigation: We propose a game theoretic approach to capture the plausible attack-defense dynamics. The defenders minimized expected the loss of load and generator tripping. The attackers maximized their payoff. The boundary between these two, referred as subgame perfect Nash equilibrium, was identified in a dynamic game model. [Part C Journal 12, Conference 13] 3. Self-healing strategies after outages - Load restoration strategy with discrete load and reserve constraints for renewables: The load restoration process was divided into a series of co-related steps with inter-temporal operational constraints. Each step maximized load pickup with AC power flow, discrete loads, the ZIP load model, the cold load effect, frequency security. An efficient B&C solver was constructed. The required reserve for renewables integration during load restoration was also discussed. [Part C Journal 4, Conference 9] -Risk-based on-line system restoration strategy: The mapping from the branch-bus model to the breaker-based model was established so that the restoration plan can be executed in realistic power systems. [Part C Conference 7]. The availabilities of components were integrated into the system restoration models and the risk of a restoration strategy was identified [Part C Conference 5].
