739713.label: Major findings and research outcome
739713.value: The major outcome of this project is a strategic defense system, which assesses risk, mitigates vulnerability and restores systems from an outage. All proposed objectives have been successfully accomplished. The major findings are: (1) Vulnerability assessment: the system information can be acquired by a distributed multi-area dynamic state estimation [Part C. Journal 5]. The security-region based methods quantify the condition-driven vulnerability with controllability of generators, transmission systems, and variability /uncertainty of the renewables [Part C Conference 1]. A comprehensive vulnerability assessment should include event-driven vulnerability due to loss of components and condition-driven vulnerability due to lack of flexibility. The frequency, magnitude, and intensity of potential loss-of-load serve as index [Part C, Journal 7]. (2) Vulnerability mitigation: enhancing equipment’s health is an efficient method to mitigate system vulnerability. Dynamic coordinated condition-based maintenance strategy can be designed [Part C, Journal 4, Conference 2]. Uncertainties are critical for designing operation strategy with renewables[Part C Journal 2]. Renewables with updated prediction can be dispatched by a sequential risk-limiting dispatch [Part C Journal 11, 13]. Proactive load response mitigates the vulnerability. Electric springs with voltages’ phase angle and amplitude control implement dynamic load response efficiently. Multiple electric springs with distributed control have been validated [Part C Journal 9, 14, Conference 12]. The vulnerability may also come from cyber systems [Part C Journal 6]. A game theoretic approach can be used to capture the plausible attack-defense dynamics [Part C Journal 10]. (3) Self-healing strategies after outages: load restoration can be modeled as a series of co-related steps with inter-temporal operational constraints. The required reserve for renewables integration needs to be carefully identified. [Part C Journal 4, Conference 9].Risk-based on-line system restoration strategy should be established based on the breaker-based model [Part C Conference 7]. The availabilities of components should be used to identify the risk of a restoration strategy [Part C Conference 5]. Steady-state and dynamic constraints should be considered [Part C Conference 3]. (4) Highly efficient methods: Vulnerability mitigation and restoration consist of a sequence of optimal power flow. Enhanced dual-bound primal-dual interior point framework is a promising method for realistic large-scale systems [Part C Journal 1]. The dynamic time-domain simulation can be implemented in a GPU platform [Part C Journal 15]. (5) Implementing the proposed methods in the realistic power systems: the efficiency of the proposed restoration methods have been integrated into industrial level software and used in realistic power systems in US and China [Part C Journal 12].

739713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
739713.value: This project established an architecture for a strategic defense system, which mitigates vulnerability and restores outage under the new energy paradigm. Based on the preliminary results from this project, further research should address the methods to fully utilize this architecture. A comprehensive strategic defense system should include physical and associated cyber systems. The interdependent cyber-physical systems need to be studied. The vulnerability of cyber systems, as well as the vulnerability of physical systems due to the cyber systems should be carefully identified. Since these two systems are with different time-scales and characteristics, the mechanism of interactions between these two systems also needs to be carefully identified and modeled. The coordinated strategies for vulnerability mitigation and outage restoration should be studied. Currently, the strategies for mitigating vulnerability and restoring outages are decoupled as two problems. However, under some extreme events, components restoration have to be implemented. The vulnerability mitigation strategy provides the initial condition for system restoration. Sophisticated vulnerability mitigation strategy should be designed to implement an effective restoration. A GPU-based platform has been validated as an effective tool. For different problems, how to allocate computation loads to GPUs and CPUs needs to be studied.

739713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
739713.value: A sound economic development and societal vitality is highly dependent on a reliable, resilient, and responsive power grid. In order to defence the catastrophic blackouts as well as the disturbances from renewables, sophisticated operating strategies for power systems are highly indispensable. This project has developed an architecture of strategic defence system (SDS) in the new energy paradigm, as well as some applications for vulnerability mitigation and outage restoration. The proposed SDS has the capability to implement vulnerability assessment, violation mitigation and outage reconfiguration in an environment of large-scale integration of renewable generations. The architecture of SDS has covered three inter-related aspects, including vulnerability identification, vulnerability mitigation, and outages restoration. The proposed strategies can mitigate vulnerability due to loss of system components and uncertainty of renewable energy sources. Risk and associated mitigating strategies of power systems due to cyber attacks are also studied. This project also studied how to restore a power system after an outage. Especially, the load restoration strategy has been proposed with the characteristics of the system and loads. Some proposed methods have been applied in realistic power systems. The finding of this project provides essential technologies for the emerging smart power grids with large-scale renewable energy sources.

740113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
740113.value: We propose to investigate the physical and physiological factors that affect the development of speech articulation of children from 2.5 years to 7.5 years of age, children who are learning Cantonese, English, or Putonghua as their first language. As a child grows, proportions change -- within the mouth cavity, of the tongue, and of the two with respect to each other. How does the language learning child change articulatory strategies as the physical apparatus matures? Are all children equally successful? Specifically, we are concerned with the oral tract articulatory results of immature motor control. Some children continue particular immature speech behaviors even as their vocal tracts become more adult-like, and are often diagnosed as possessing a Speech Sound Disorder (SSD). We hope to establish that at least some of these behaviors are conservative, normal behaviors from a younger age that were the result of articulatory factors. One phenomenon of particular interest is “neutralization”, when an adult perceives a child using a single sound, such as “k”, for two distinct adult sounds, such as “t” and “k”. We hypothesize that in at least some cases, the child makes an articulatory distinction which cannot be perceived by the adult listener: the “neutralization” is apparent, not real. We will explore physical and perceptual causes and results of these phenomena. Our hypotheses are: 1) the independence of the control of different sagittal regions of the tongue is not as great for young children as for adults; 2) control of different regions progresses at different rates as the human matures; 3) the phenomenon of “neutralization” is due to adults’ categorical perception, and 4) that conservative articulatory gestures result in SSDs. The proposed data source is simultaneous ultrasound and acoustic recordings to be obtained at the University of Hong Kong and in the field. These data will be obtained for three groups of children for each of three language situations (Cantonese, Hong Kong English, and Putonghua): a) 2.5 to 3.5 year-olds, b) 6.5 to 7.5 year-olds without SSD, c) 6.5 to 7.5 year-olds with SSD(s). A fourth adult group will serve as a comparison point, and all groups will be prompted to pronounce specific single syllable words. The results of this project will provide new insight into how language learners navigate changes in their articulation that are forced by the changing relationships of tongue to oral cavity. 此研究旨在探究影響兩歲半至七歲半兒童言語發聲發展過程中的身體及生理因素，研究兒童母語分別為廣東話，普通話及英文。兒童成長過程中，口腔內，舌頭及二者的比例會相應發展變化。隨著身體器官愈加成熟，兒童語言學習者的發音方式會有何變化？ 特別是發展並未成熟時口腔發聲情況。一些兒童雖然聲帶已發展至近成人水平，但仍有某些特定的不成熟言語行為，，這些通常被診斷為有言語發音障礙。此研究旨在說明在兒童較小年齡時，部份以上行為表現由於發音因素的影響只是保守的，正常的行為。 其中一個特別有趣的現象是“中和化”，即成人感知到兒童用一個單音，例如/k/，來代替兩個不同的成人音，例如/t/和/k/。此研究假設至少某些情況下，兒童可以區別發出不同的音而成人卻無法感知，因而，“中和化”顯然不是真實的。 研究將探索身體及認知因素和這些現象產生的結果。我們的假設為：1）兒童不同舌體各矢状部位的運用獨立性不如成人；2）成長過程中不同部位發展速度不；同3）“中和化”現象是由於成人的分類認知；4）有限的發音姿勢導致言語發音障礙。 同步超聲波及聽力錄音的數據將在香港大學及相關地方進行。每種語言環境下有三組兒童，語言環境分別是廣東話，香港英文，及普通話，三組兒童包括：a）兩歲半至三歲半兒童；b）六歲半至七歲半無言語發音障礙兒童；c）六歲半至七歲半有言語發音障礙兒童。成人對照組是第四組。研究過程將會引導所有組別參與者發出一些特定的單音節字的音。 此研究結果將對語言學習者駕馭舌頭口腔關係來產生發音變化提供新的見解。

740213.label: Realisation of objectives
740213.value: All the objectives have been 100% achieved. OBJECTIVE 1: The Classroom Observation Scale (COS) we developed and validated with 1,164 preschool children in Hong Kong. The 13-item tool was used with reliable and valid results by observers without clinical training (research assistants and preschool teachers): COS scores around age 3 (from 2 years 10 months to 4 years 5 months) significantly predicted clinical diagnosis of ASD (including mild cases) around one year to 1½ years down the road. OBJECTIVE 2: The local preschools were generally highly structured and offered relatively less free-play time, whereas the international preschools were less structured and offered more free-play time. The COS proved to be a reliable and valid screening tool for ASD in both kinds of environment. OBJECTIVE 3: We found that the existing validated Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS-2) was useful for screening children under age 4½ in Hong Kong (Study 2) in predicting ASD diagnosis on average 1½ years down the road. This is the first published relatively large scale cross-cultural validation of SRS-2 (Preschool Form) outside the U.S. Importantly, the newly developed COS outperformed the SRS-2 (Preschool Form).

740213.label: Major findings and research outcome
740213.value: While moderate to severe cases of ASD may be noticed by parents and preschool teachers and readily diagnosed by clinicians by age 2 or 3, milder cases often go undiagnosed until 1st or 2nd grade. In this series of three studies, we developed a new tool for identifying children under age 4½ years at risk for even mild ASD—based on a very simple idea. We used peer interaction without adults hovering around as a naturalistic stress to see which children may have difficulty in navigating their social world with peers, and that may foretell long-term social impairments. We created a user-friendly screening tool—Classroom Observation Scale, COS—that can be used by non-clinicians (e.g., preschool teachers, research assistant with less clinical training than the typical assistant therapists) to screen children under age 4½ and to predict ASD diagnosis one to 1½ years down the road. There are very few existing screening tools for identifying children under age 4½ at risk for mild ASD. The new tool COS outperforms the Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS-2; Study 2) developed in the U.S. and the locally developed ASD Preschool Social-Communication Scale (APSCS; Study 3). This user-friendly 13-item Classroom Observation Scale (COS) enables observers without clinical training to identify, with reliable and valid results, preschoolers at risk for even mild ASD, thereby helping assistant therapists or preschool teachers collect valid information to supplement, or even serve in lieu of, an experienced clinical psychologist’s preschool visit. It can also enhance preschool teachers’ ability to identify children at risk for even mild ASD, thereby enhancing the chances for early diagnosis and early effective treatment.

740213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
740213.value: Preschool teachers in international preschools, as well as our research assistants, could use the Classroom Observation Scale (COS) with reliable and valid results. On the other hand, preschool teachers in the Chinese-speaking local kindergarten seemed unable to use COS effectively, even though our research assistants with just several hours of training could. Further research is needed to understand why. Note that Chinese-language local preschools generally allow children much less free-play time and their teachers much less time to observe the children in free play (not only because of the less free-play time in the time-table but also because the teachers often would be supervising children to do as-yet-unfinished in-class seat-work during the scheduled free-play time). It will be informative to examine the effects of experimentally freeing teachers in local preschools during free-play time and to see if having more opportunities to observe spontaneous peer interaction among the children would make COS a more useful tool for the teachers.

740213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
740213.value: About 1 in 68 children is now estimated to have Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). While more severe cases can be readily diagnosed by age 2 or 3, milder cases often go undiagnosed until age 6 or 7. Earlier diagnosis and treatment of ASD can give these children a crucial head start and launch them on a better lifelong path in understanding the social world and developing health social bonds. With the family size trending downward, especially in single-child families, parents might notice something is off without realizing their children might be at risk for ASD. By contrast, preschool teachers are in a better position to compare children. We developed a new tool to identify children under age 4½ at risk for even milder ASD. We used peer interaction as a naturalistic “stress test”—to observe young children interacting with peers without supportive or familiar adults hovering nearby. The new tool Classroom Observation Scale (COS) is user-friendly and can be used by observers without clinical training with reliable and valid results. It predicts ASD diagnosis one to 1½ years down the road, doing even better than widely-used existing screening tools developed in the U.S. and in Hong Kong.

740313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
740313.value: Hong Kong’s border with Shenzhen is incrementally dissolving. By 2047, 50 years after the 1997 handover of Hong Kong the border will no longer exist. This also will mean the dissolution of the economic and political zones of the “One Country Two Systems” policy; significantly the Special Administration Region of Hong Kong and the Special Economic Zone of Shenzhen. As part of the re-integration process serious considerations need to be made concerning the potential impact this will have on the urban development of both sides of the border as well as the larger impact this may have on the entire Pearl River Delta region. As part of this re-integration in 2011 the Hong Kong Government will redraw the boundary of the Frontier Closed Area allowing almost 2000 hectares of land to be openly accessible to the public as well as being available for potential development. The Frontier Closed Area was created in 1951 as a buffer zone to control migration and crime from the mainland. Since then the land has remained untouched by urban development – very little has changed in over fifty years. This is in stark contrast to the rapid urbanization that has taken place directly adjacent to this area in Shenzhen which has seen the city develop from a fishing village with a population of 200,000 in 1982 to over 11 million today. The Frontier Closed Area, as well as being a testament to what Shenzhen used to be like, contains a rich landscape of eco-systems, (including the RAMSAR site), fish farms, fresh water streams, primary forests as well as historic villages and abandoned military posts. The research project has 3 main aims: 1. To understand the border region as part of a larger urban ecology existing between the cities of Hong Kong and Shenzhen. To examine specific processes of urbanization that have occurred within the zone and to understand the forces that will play a role in determining the future of the border zone. 2. To propose an urban strategy for the Frontier Closed Area that engages with the specific relationships that exist across the border to make a proposal that is mutually beneficial to both Hong Kong and Shenzhen. 3. To position Hong Kong’s unique border condition within a larger frame of academic discourse on border studies. 香港與深圳的邊境，逐步溶解。到2047年，繼1997年香港回歸的50年後，這邊界即將消失。這也意味著在“一國兩制” 的經濟和政治區域上也將會解除。特別在香港特別行政區和深圳經濟特區。在重新整合的程序中，需要認真地考慮到有關於即將受到城市發展而影響的兩方邊界，以及較大影響的整個珠三角地區。 在2011年的重新整合當中，香港政府將重新繪畫邊境禁區的邊界。使近2000公頃的土地，公開向公眾開放以及給予有發展潛力的項目。在昔日1951年所創建的邊境禁區，目的是為了控制及監管來自大陸的移民與犯罪的一個緩衝地帶。從那時以來，該土地一直未被城市方面發展 – 五十多年來都沒有改變。對比在相鄰的深圳地區，從1982年的一個只得二十萬人口的漁村相比現今的有過於一千一百萬人口。可見到深圳是那麼快速地城市化。邊境禁區是一個可以看到昔日深圳的地方，同時包含了豐富的景觀生態系統，（包括RAMSAR site），養魚場，淡水溪流，原始森林，以及歷史悠久的村莊和被遺棄的軍事哨所。

740413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
740413.value: The primary aim of this project is to investigate how the Japanese state used new forms of architecture and urban space in an attempt to better manage society and daily life in interwar Tokyo. The starting point is the Great Kantō Earthquake and fires which destroyed 45% of the capital in early September 1923. The destruction created what many bureaucratic elites believed would be an unprecedented opportunity to reconstruct a grandiose, awe-inspiring, modern capital designed to combat social ills and better manage daily life in post-World War I Japan. How did these visions materialise? Recent studies have suggested that the reconstruction of Tokyo was not as grand as many individuals envisioned because of political opposition, budget restrictions and citizen protest over the controversial land readjustment project (Schencking, 2006, 2008, 2013). Nevertheless, when the Imperial Capital Reconstruction Project was completed in 1930, Tokyo had much reason to celebrate. Surprisingly, despite renewed interest in the Great Kantō Earthquake, no one has documented what planners did with the limited funds they were given. How and why was the city constructed the way it was? Drawing on contemporary journal articles, memoirs, speeches, newspapers and magazines, as well as local ward histories, municipal government records, and official reconstruction documents, my interdisciplinary study will examine the buildings, infrastructure and spaces of New Tokyo. I suggest that the schools, parks, hospitals, childcare and social welfare facilities, roads and bridges, and train and transport networks were designed and built to showcase Tokyo as more than just an imperial capital and “fountain-head of national civilization” but as “one of the great metropolises of the world” (Tokyo Municipal Office, 1930). By documenting how and why Japan began to use new forms of architecture and space, this study will add an important new dimension to studies on post-disaster reconstruction, social management, urban reform, as well as interwar Japanese state and society. My findings, when published as a research monograph, will shed light on how post-disaster reconstruction projects can shape the urban environment and help inform rebuilding in other disaster stricken places in the world. 此計劃的首要目的是探討日本政府如何嘗試利用新式建築和城市空間，改善對兩次世界大戰之間的東京社會及其市民的日常生活的管理。此嘗試源於一九二三年九月初，關東大地震及其引致的火災摧毀了百份之四十五的東京。很多官僚精英相信此規模的破壞造就了前所未有的機會去重建一個宏偉、凜然、現代的首都，以對抗日本在第一次世界大戰後的社會弊病，和改善政府對市民日常生活的管理。 這些願景如何實現？ 近期的研究提出因政治反對、財政限制和市民對具爭議性的土地重新規劃計劃的抗議，東京的重建並沒有如很多人所預期的宏偉 (Schencking, 2006, 2008, 2013)。儘管如此 ，帝都復興計劃在一九三零年完成的時候，東京市民仍有很多值得去慶祝的原因。出奇地，雖然學術界對關東大地震重新提起興趣，未有人記錄城市規劃者如何運用他們手上有限的資金。這個城市的重建結果是怎樣？是甚麼原因構成這結果？ 根據當代期刊文章、回憶錄、演講辭、報章和雜誌，以及當地區份歷史， 市政府檔案，和官方重建文件, 我的誇學科研究將探討新東京的建築、基礎設施和空間。我提出學校、公園、醫院、育兒和社會福利設施、道路和橋樑、以及鐵路和交通網絡，都是為展示東京為不僅是一個帝都和 “全國文明的泉源” ，更是 “世上其中一個大都會”而設計和建造（東京市役所，1930）。 此研究記錄日本如何及為何採用新式建築和空間，並將為災後重建、社會管理、城市改革，以及兩次世界大戰之間日本的國家和社會的研究加入重要的新層面。我的研究結果在出版成研究專著後，將揭示災後重建計劃如何塑造城市環境，並為全球的受災地區提供有關重建的資料。

740413.label: Realisation of objectives
740413.value: The primary aim of this project was to investigate how the Japanese state used new forms of architecture and urban space in an attempt to better manage society and daily life in interwar Tokyo. My original use of the term “Japanese state” should be refined at this point. The individuals, intellectuals and officials responsible for describing their visions for reconstructed Tokyo were far more wide-ranging than I first expected. Of course they included politicians and local government officials, but individuals such as school teachers, playground supervisors, architects, engineers, health and hygiene experts, and even police inspectors, contributed to debates and discussions on how Tokyo should be reconstructed. In order to understand how and why they wanted to reconstruct Tokyo, and subsequently how the city was rebuilt, I conducted research in a range of primary source material including: contemporary journals and newspapers, ward/city/government publications (pamphlets, statistics, posters, official histories), commemorative volumes (published photo and map collections). This rich visual data will also be used as the basis of my companion website (www.earthquakechildren.com), to be launched after the publication of my book manuscript. I achieved 100 per cent of my research objectives and significant research outputs while simultaneously undertaking onerous administrative duties as an early career tenure-track Assistant Professor. I served as Director of the Department of Japanese Studies (2014-2017), a large and successful program with the fourth highest number of majors in the Faculty of Arts (162 majors) and the highest number of minors (229 minors), as well as an extensive network of exchange and internship partnerships. To summarise, my most significant findings are as follows: 1. The Great Kantō Earthquake revealed the extent to which government officials had failed to prepare society for a catastrophic disaster both in terms of infrastructure and also disaster training. The earthquake galvanized ongoing efforts to build resilience in daily life (by promoting health, hygiene and moral qualities of individuals), and also build resilience in society for times of a disaster (construct earthquake and fire-resistant buildings, increase green space, improve water supply, train people). 2. The Reconstruction Institute and Municipal Government used new forms of architecture, both in terms of building material (reinforced concrete multi-storey buildings to maximize space and minimize footprint) and design (functional, plain, austere). Analysis of contemporary journal articles reveal that they were motivated both by a desire to protect residents in case of future disasters, and a desire to reflect the kind of moral values government officials sought to promote in 1920s Japan such as austerity and simplicity. 3. A significantly reduced reconstruction budget hindered many visionary’s hopes to build a grandiose city complete with modern infrastructure. My case study of small parks illustrates how innovative urban planners overcame budget restrictions to greatly improve access to parks in eastern Tokyo. The careful placement of small parks next to primary schools was a clever urban planning solution that benefited both children and local residents. The 52 new small parks covered a total area of 14.59 hectares and in 1932 accounted for only 6.6 per cent of Tokyo’s total public park space of 222 hectares. By contrast, the three new large parks (Sumida, Kinshi and Hamachō) added 28.79 hectares of green space to Tokyo. As my article illustrates if we measure the small parks by size, they appear to be less impressive than the big parks. In fact, I argue, urban planners, educators and child experts held big designs for these small parks that were intended for use as sites of play, exercise, rest, guided recreation, and emergency refuge. 4. Writing in journals and newspapers, or speaking on the floor of parliament or post-disaster meetings, key individuals involved in the reconstruction of Tokyo described ambitious hopes for the capital. While some were practical (such as architect/engineer Sano Toshikata who was a strong advocate for reinforced concrete even before the earthquake and fires), many were idealistic if not unrealistic in their quest to combat social ills. The one thing they shared in common was that they believed the earthquake would provide an opportunity to use new forms of architecture and space in the reconstruction of the capital, and in doing so achieve long-held goals aimed at promoting the moral and physical health of Tokyo’s residents. For the first six months, discussions were characterized by optimism and opportunity. 5. Despite the scaled back reconstruction budget, architects, urban planners, landscape architects and educators still endeavoured to shape the urban environment in subtle ways that reflected their larger goals of social management. For example, small parks attached to primary schools were typically elevated half a metre above road level. In some places this was necessary to install drainage, especially in low-lying wards prone to flooding such as Honjo and Fukagawa. But even in places not prone to flooding, the Parks Director Inoshita Kiyoshi explained that they elevated the ground to distance park users from the congested city and the busy traffic on the road. 6. The findings of my study challenge the idea that little innovation comes out of post-disaster planning and design. Tokyo’s reconstructed small parks and their innovative placement next to primary schools are a case in point. In the aftermath of the 1923 earthquake, small parks became an ideal solution to perceived problems of urban modernity, Tokyo’s vulnerabilities, and the young demographic nature of the capital. Japan’s urban planners, landscape architects, educators and child experts projected their hopes for healthy children and residents on to small parks, much like their counterparts elsewhere in the world. It is important to note, in a field heavily influenced by teleological approaches that view history back from the trauma of the Second World War, that small parks were not designed or conceptualized as spaces for mobilization or the militarization of Japan’s youth in mind or body. Moreover, as Thomas Havens points out, ‘Nowhere in this official rhetoric was any mention of physical strength for potential military purposes’. By the mid-1930s, however, the parks increasingly became sites in which the state could project aims of more intrusive and assertive social management and suasion. In addition to two journal articles, the most significant outcome of my research is my book manuscript “Earthquake Children: Building Resilience from the Ruins of Tokyo”. Now in the final stages of preparation, the University of Hawaii Press (Ms Stephanie Chun) has already expressed interest in publishing this manuscript and I will meet her, and other publishers, in March 2018 at the annual AAS Conference in Washington DC.

740413.label: Major findings and research outcome
740413.value: 1. Earthquake Children: Building Resilience From the Ruins of Tokyo Being prepared and responding to catastrophes with stoic resolve are not innate qualities of Japanese people. Rather, they are a learned and practiced behaviour that began in earnest after Japan’s most deadly and destructive natural disaster of the modern era: the 1923 Great Kantō Earthquake. Earthquake Children explores this epic disaster from the viewpoint of children and those teachers and education officials responsible for their recovery, development and emergence as strong, healthy, and prepared citizens of Japan. Earthquake Children documents how children, schools, and education became a focus of preparedness and resilience in Tokyo during Japan’s early interwar-era transition from a disaster vulnerable nation to a prepared and resilient society. 2. “Voices of Vulnerability and Resilience: Children and their Recollections in Post-Earthquake Tokyo,” Japanese Studies 36, no. 3 (2016): 299-317. Tokyo’s school children began writing essays about the Great Kantō Earthquake within weeks of the disaster as a pedagogical exercise. These remarkable accounts provide a panoramic view into children’s firsthand experiences of Japan’s worst natural disaster and life in the aftermath. Their usefulness, however, does not end there. In the period following the earthquake, children possessed a new and different utility to the state as the future generation to be listened to, learned from and inspired by. Children’s essays struck a fine balance between reflecting on the past and dreaming of a better future. Moreover, they were ideal role models of resilience in an era of spiritual and physical reconstruction. Their promises to study hard, save money and reconstruct Tokyo ‘even better than before’ were exactly the kind of values government officials wanted to cultivate in 1920s Japan. 3. “Small Parks, Big Designs: Reconstructed Tokyo’s New Green Spaces, 1923-1931,” under review Urban History This article explores the genesis of small parks in Tokyo following the 1923 earthquake. It sheds new light on an example of innovative urban design and post-disaster reconstruction, and highlights the growing place children occupied in Japanese society. Originally conceived as a means to increase space for children to play and exercise, all 52 parks were strategically located beside primary schools. As the state’s goals of social management expanded, officials recognized the potential to use small parks as sites of rest, recreation and refuge. A history of Tokyo’s small parks offers a window in to the relationship between the built environment, health, and society in interwar Japan.

740413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
740413.value: One possible trajectory for this project would be to explore efforts to manage society beyond 1930, and how showcases of reconstructed Tokyo were actually used by children and local residents. A glance through the Tokyo Asahi Shinbun reveals that the original architects of small parks continued to promote the health and lifestyle benefits of parks in daily life for children and adults. Ultimately, however, big designs for these small parks were malleable. By the mid-1930s, small parks were increasingly used as sites to mobilize citizens for war. In late 1936, parks featured in two very different articles published by the Tokyo Asahi Shinbun. Beginning from November, the newspaper announced, a series of events aimed at helping children ‘play well together’ would be held in the small parks. Two weeks later, another headline read ‘Model bombs in 35 locations, a spectacle in small parks.’ By 1941 the newspaper informed people how they could use small parks in the imperial capital to cultivate vegetables. How did larger developments in Japanese state and society influence the needs and eventually the harsh realities of people living in an ever-changing urban environment? Alternatively, I could explore efforts to build resilience in contemporary Japan following 3/11.

740413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
740413.value: In 1923, a magnitude 7.9 earthquake revealed the extent to which Japanese educators and government officials had failed to protect – or even prepare – Tokyo’s youngest and most vulnerable residents. The Great Kantō Earthquake killed more than 5,000 children, destroyed two-thirds of Tokyo’s primary schools, and left thousands more hungry, homeless, and helpless. In the aftermath, Tokyo’s earthquake children became a focus of recovery and reconstruction efforts following the 1923 earthquake. Government and education officials recognized the important role children could play in a society recovering from disaster and they used their candid voices for a variety of commemorative, pedagogical, and political purposes. Most significantly, my research findings have shown that government and education officials sought to safeguard future generations through a new and modern built environment that showcased spaces for children to learn and to play. Facilities such as reinforced concrete primary schools and adjacent small parks embraced new technologies aimed at promoting the health and hygiene of the next generation, and also building their resilience for daily life and disaster. My work not only provides new insights into the origins of Japan’s disaster preparedness, but also historicizes current efforts by government officials to build resilience in children and strengthen disaster preparedness today.

740613.value: 摘要 據世界衛生組織統計，不育是一個漸趨普遍的生殖健康問題，至少影響全球約15%正值繁育年齡的夫婦，當中，發展中國家的不育率為8 至12%。本港最常採用的生殖科技程序為體外受精 (in vitro fertilization，IVF)。據香港＜人類生殖科技管理局＞記錄，於2010年間，3,340對夫婦曾於本港進行合共4,016次體外受精療程。 相比其他生殖科技，體外受精 (IVF) 過程冗長、繁複及具侵入性，但成功率只有20-25%。在IVF治療期間，女性往往會有抑鬱和焦慮症狀，除了面對在胚胎移植後等待結果時以及治療失敗時(Verhaak et al, 2005)，對有些人來說，決定是否繼續或停止治療是很困難的。對於選擇繼續治療的女性，她們必須作出另一個決定:選擇實際風險較低但主觀成功率較低的單胚胎移植 (Single embryo transfer, SET) 或實際風險較高但主觀成功率較高多胚胎移植(Multiple embryo transfer, MET) 是很困難的。就本港以言，大部份選擇繼續治療之女性，只有27%會選擇單胚胎移植 (SET)。由於生殖科技成功率因人而異，因此接受體外受精(IVF)的女性往往很難於治療風險及治療成效之間取得平衡，選擇最適合的治療。 文獻指出，病人的治療決定往往影響病人滿意度、配合程度及整體健康(Joosten et al, 2008)。然而，針對不育治療的病人治療決定研究欠奉。本研究主要是了解1) 香港婦女在決定參與輔助生育技術的角色、2) 文化信仰和個人的價值觀如何影響治療決定，以及3) 探討在作出治療決定後的短期心理調整。 本研究為量化前瞻性研究，目標對象為138位剛被告知體外受精 (IVF)治療失敗之女性。參加者需要在三個不同的時間完成一份問卷：被告知體外受精 (IVF)治療失敗當天、事後與醫生會談當天，以及一個月後。獲取之數據將以線性迴歸(Linear Regression) 進行分析以判斷香港婦女在決定參與輔助生育技術的角色會否影響其心理質素及對治療成效的滿意度。 過往十年，首席研究員 (Principle Investigator, PI) 投入發展香港的不育輔導服務以及進行實證為本的研究。過去兩年，她為生殖科技界內專業人士提供專業訓練課程和組織專業研究小組，期望提昇服務質素及推廣道德實踐。本研究將為不育病人的治療決定注入嶄新理論及數據。

740613.label: Realisation of objectives
740613.value: Our research objectives were achieved by asking 151 women who had experience in vitro fertilization (IVF) treatment failure to complete a battery of questionnaires at 3 time-points. Throughout the study period, 338 potential participants were approached at the university-affiliated infertility clinic. 246 consented to participate in our study. 95 participants eventually opted to withdraw during participation, due to reasons such as started new fertility treatment, time constraints and personal reasons. In all, 151 women completed all 3 time-points of data collection: immediately upon receiving news about treatment failure (T0), next doctor’s appointment (T1) and 3 months after T1 (T2). In general, all our research objectives had been realized to satisfaction, with details below. Objective 1 was realized by a cross-sectional analysis collected from the 246 consented participants on the Problem-Solving Decision-Making (PSDM) Scale, which distinguished treatment decisions into two dimensions: “problem-solving” (PS) and “decision-making” (DM) and will yield seven categorizations of preferred role in decision-making. Given the complex nature of IVF treatment, we differentiated between decision making vignettes on general health issue and fertility treatment to allow within-subject comparison across different health contexts. Objective 2 was realized by means of regression analysis on 151 participants to study the relation between their Chinese Childbearing Belief Scale (CCBS), Childbearing Importance Index (CII) at T0 and Perceived Decision Making Involvement and Difficulties (PDMID), and Decisional Conflict Scale (DCS) at T1. Objective 3 was realized by means of bivariate correlations to indicate the associations among decisional conflict, decisional regret, psychological well-being and fertility related quality of life. Mediation analyses were conducted using the PROCESS macro to explore the psychological adjustments after making decisions regarding whether to continue or terminate further IVF treatments.

740613.label: Major findings and research outcome
740613.value: In understanding the preferred roles in infertility treatment decision-making among Hong Kong Chinese women, Chinese infertile women appeared to be more compliant in making treatment decisions as compared to their Western counterparts. Most women indicate preference shared by leaning passive role (41.9%) or total passive role (40.4%) in the Problem-Solving Decision Making Scale. 89.4% of them thought doctors should best decide diagnosis and evaluate treatment options, and only 10.1% preferred sharing responsibility. No one assumed an autonomous role. Similarly, most women preferred minimal role and relied heavily on physicians in deciding whether to continue or terminate further treatments (84.3%), only a small proportion preferred sharing responsibility (7.1%) or asserting autonomy (8.6%). Regarding how cultural beliefs and personal values affect treatment decision-making, analysis revealed both Total and Core Fertility Related Quality of Life of our sample were higher than that from a Western sample reported by Boivin et al (2011) (t=8.10 and 8.36, p < .01) while no difference was found in Treatment score (t=1.41, n.s.). In specific, Total and Core FertiQoL were negatively associated with identification to Chinese beliefs “It’s Wife responsibility to childbearing’ (B= -3.384, p <.001), “No children is the biggest issue” (B= -2.97, p <.05). For Treatment FertiQoL, high identification with “It’s daughter in-law’s responsibility to continue lineage” significantly predicts poorer outcomes (Beta= -3.356, p <.01). For the short-term psychological adjustment after treatment decision-making correlational analysis revealed decisional conflict was positively related to decisional regret. Further, decisional conflict was related to higher levels of anxiety and depression, as well as lower levels of FRQOL at T2. Decisional regret was concurrently associated with depression and treatment-specific FRQOL. Our research underscore how decisional conflict on psychological adjustment may vary among patients with different clinical characteristics, despite their common experience of an unsuccessful IVF cycle.

740613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
740613.value: Given a woman’s decision to continue or terminate treatment will place her at a crossroads of medical treatment and other alternatives in family formation, our research capture the short-term psychological adjustments up to 3-months post-decision. Long-term follow up will be necessary in understanding how the women’s decision had impacts on her reproductive live, marital relationship, and subsequent family planning. Also, as infertility not only the woman but also the man in the marriage, the impact of unsuccessful treatment on the male perspective is worth exploring. Last but not least, the current study advocate for continuous psychosocial care for women undergoing IVF treatment, not just the beginning or the end, but throughout the whole treatment process. Future research should adopt a policy perspective to review the need to include compulsory psychosocial care in the existing guidelines for regulating Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) clinics, in Hong Kong, and also other Asian counterparts.

740613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
740613.value: Our study aim to understand the psychosocial impact of treatment failure in women who are undergoing in vitro fertilisation treatment, and the relationship between her decision making style and subsequent decision in continuing or terminating further fertility treatment. Results revealed our Chinese sample prefer minimal role in decision making and relied heavily on physicians in deciding whether to continue or terminate further treatments. In terms of adjustment to treatment failure, a group of women were identified as having adjustment difficulty, which might potentially turn into long-term psychological distress. The current study adds to our understanding of Hong Kong Chinese women’s role preference and level of involvement in infertility treatment decision making by providing quantitative evidence from patients subject experience. It also inform physicians and nurses of the best practices in facilitating decision making and maximize treatment outcomes. This study also enhance scope and depth of existing fertility counseling services.

740713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
740713.value: Background: Although it is widely believed that victimization greatly impairs the mental and physical health of children with disabilities, little is known about the mechanisms underlying the victimization of disabled children. Objectives: Building on reliable estimates of the prevalence of different types victimization across disabilities among children in Hong Kong, the proposed study will provide evidence for the associated factors of such victimization. In addition, the proposed study will be among the first to provide information about the disability-specific mechanisms of the relationship between disability and child victimization. Study design: A representative sample of 3,761 children attending primary, secondary or special school in Hong Kong will be sampled using a multi-stage stratified procedure. Children who are in Primary 4 to Secondary 6 will be invited to complete a survey about their disability diagnosis and experience of victimization. For children who are in Primary 1 to Primary 3 and those who are not capable of completing the survey, their parents or guardians will be recruited as proxies to report their experiences. Both child version and parent version of survey will include questions about child-related factors, including health, interpersonal skills and problematic behaviours. Also included in the parent version will be questions about parent-child relationship and parenting stress). Contributions of the study: The proposed study will extend existing knowledge on victimization of children with disabilities by providing empirical evidence of the possible mechanisms underlying the increased risk of victimization. By including different types of disabilities and different forms of victimization in the analysis, information about disability-specific victimization and associated factors can be obtained. As to the clinical implications, findings of the proposed study will inform the development of disability-specific screening and intervention programmes. 背景： 雖然研究者普遍認為受侵害會極大地損害殘疾兒童的身心健康，但是研究者對于受侵害對殘疾兒童影響的機制知之甚少。 研究目的： 這項研究旨在探討香港殘疾兒童遭遇的不同類型受侵害的普遍性的可靠估計，會為這些受侵害的相關因素提供証據。此外，本研究是第一個探討殘疾和兒童受侵害的具體機制的研究。 研究設計： 採用多階段分層取樣的方法，本研究將調查香港3,761名小學、初中和特殊學校的學生。小學4年級到初中6年級的學生完成了一份關于他們的殘疾狀況診斷和受侵害經歷的問卷。小學1到3年級或自己不能完成問卷的學生，他們的父母或者監護人代表他們報告相關的經歷。兒童版本和父母版本的調查問卷將包括一些與兒童有關的因素的問題，包括健康、人際技能和問題行為。父母版本的問卷調查還包括親子關系和教養壓力的一些問題。 本研究的貢獻： 通過提供增加受侵害風險的可能機制的証據，本研究將會擴展現有的關于殘疾兒童受侵害的知識。在分析中，通過包括不同類型的殘疾狀況和不同形式的受侵害狀況，我們將會獲得與殘疾有關的受侵害及其相關因素的信息。關于臨床意義，本研究的結果將會指導發展針對殘疾兒童的篩查和幹預的計劃。

740713.label: Realisation of objectives
740713.value: The project objectives have been fully achieved by successfully recruited targets that have been committed by the proposal. Although it is widely believed that victimization greatly impairs the mental and physical health of children with disabilities, little is known about the mechanisms underlying the victimization of disabled children. Building on reliable estimates of the prevalence of different types victimization across disabilities among children in Hong Kong, Using a large and representative sample of school-aged children in Hong Kong, this study aims to fill the research gap by providing reliable estimates of the prevalence of disability and the direct and indirect experiences of violence among children with disability. The study also compares the prevalence of child maltreatment, parental intimate partner violence (IPV), and in-law conflict to explore the factors related to the association between disability and violence victimization. The prevalence of disability among children was about 6%. Children with disability were more likely to report victimization than those without disability: 32% to 60% of the former had experienced child maltreatment, and 12% to 46% of them had witnessed IPV between parents or in-law conflict. The results of a logistic regression showed that disability increased the risk of lifetime physical maltreatment by 1.6 times. Furthermore, low levels of parental education and paternal unemployment were risk factors for lifetime child maltreatment. The risk of child maltreatment could have an almost sixfold increase when the child had also witnessed other types of family violence. Possible explanations and implications of the findings are discussed.

740713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
740713.value: Apart from analysing prevalence and risk factors of children with disability and victimisation, further analysis on the prevalence of various types of child victimization across different types of disabilities among children will be conducted. Even though this study has focused, alongside other research, on the effect of disabilities on victimization, one should be cautious before drawing any conclusions about a causal relationship. There is evidence that some types of disabilities may be a consequence of early victimization, and it is not necessary for disability to precede the experience of violence.To fully establish the causal direction in the relationship between disabilities and victimization, future research, especially those with a longitudinal design, is needed.

740713.value: The proposed study will extend existing knowledge on victimization of children with disabilities by providing empirical evidence of the possible mechanisms underlying the increased risk of victimization. By including different types of disabilities and different forms of victimization in the analysis, information about disability-specific victimization and associated factors can be obtained. As to the clinical implications, findings of the proposed study will inform the development of disability-specific screening and intervention programmes.For example, if peer victimization is associated with poor social skills among children with externalizing or internalizing disorders, intervention for children with such problems may include measures to help them improve relationships with others. Similarly, if maltreatment of children with disabilities is related to increased parenting stress and burden of parents or guardians, intervention may include a focus on the development of social support and relevant coping skills among parents and guardians.

741113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
741113.value: This project aims to examine (a) the rationale and choice of policy designs and instruments adopted by the provincial and municipal governments in industrial planning under the integration plans (yitihua guihua) of the Pearl River Delta (PRD) since 2009, (b) the politics of the policy process in making and implementing these policy measures, and (c) whether these designs and instruments have contributed to better policy coordination and intergovernmental collaboration, and the difficulties and challenges encountered in the process. “The Outline of the Plan for the Reform and Development of the Pearl River Delta: 2008–2020 (The Outline Plan)” was promulgated in early 2009 by the State Council to jumpstart Guangdong’s reform and development. The integration of the PRD and its closer cooperation with Hong Kong and Macao are the key goals of the Outline Plan. Soon afterwards, the provincial government decided on measures to implement this initiative through formulating integration plans for the PRD. Five major policy plans—(a) industrial planning (chanye buju), (b) infrastructure, (c) urban-rural integration (chengxiang yitihua), (d) environmental protection, and (e) public services—were promulgated in 2010 to foster policy coordination and intergovernmental collaboration and lay the foundation for the sustained and coordinated socio-economic development of the PRD. The timeframe of this study is the 2009-2012 period because these four years are regarded by the province as critical for launching these plans. While industrial planning is my focus, its connections with infrastructural integration will be examined because the two are closely related. Comparison with implementation efforts of the other three plans will also be made in order to capture the distinctive features of the policy process. This project will examine the following issues: 1. Why did the provincial government choose the policy goals and instruments in the integration plan on industrial planning? What kind of policy measures have the nine municipal governments in the PRD formulated to carry out these provincial guidelines? Why did they adopt these specific policy designs and instruments? 2. How did the provincial and municipal governments and enterprises interact and advance their respective interests in the policy making and implementation process? 3. To what extent have the particular policy designs and policy instruments adopted by these two levels of governments contributed to better policy coordination and intergovernmental collaboration in the PRD? What were the major challenges and difficulties encountered in this process?

741113.label: Realisation of objectives
741113.value: “The Outline of the Plan for the Reform and Development of the Pearl River Delta: 2008–2020 (the Outline Plan)” was promulgated in early 2009 by the State Council to jump-start Guangdong’s reform and development. To implement this initiative, the Guangdong provincial government under the leadership of the former provincial party secretary Wang Yang (2008-2012) formulated five integration plans for the Pearl River Delta (PRD), covering (a) industrial layout, (b) infrastructure, (c) urban-rural integration, (d) environmental protection, and (e) public services in 2010. These plans aimed to foster policy coordination and intergovernmental collaboration and lay the foundation for the sustained and coordinated socio-economic development of this region. (There is no clear definition of what yituhua exactly refers to in the policy documents and it will therefore be translated into “integration” in this study). The Integration Plan for Industrial Layout (chanye buju yitihua 产业布局一体化规划) (the Industrial Layout Plan) constitutes the core of the proposed division of labor between these nine cities in the PRD. In order to implement these plans, the nine cities were designated into three economic circles: Guangzhou-Foshan-Zhaoqing, Shenzhen-Dongguan-Huizhou, and Zhuhai-Zhongshan-Jiangmen, on the basis of geographical proximity as well as economic complementarity. This project aims to analyse the policy design and implementation of the Industrial Layout Plan undertaken by Guangdong during 2009-2012. This project has three main objectives: (a) Examine the rationale and choices of policy designs and policy instruments employed by the provincial and municipal governments in industrial planning in the PRD (b) Analyze the politics of the policy process involving the provincial and municipal governments and enterprises in the making and implementation of the integration plan (c) Assess whether these policy designs and instruments have contributed to better policy coordination and intergovernmental collaboration, and the difficulties and challenges encountered in the process My research objectives have been largely achieved. Data Collection: During 2014 – 16, I have carried out systematic data collection with the help of both a full-time RA and part-time RAs. My documentary data collected include the economic and industrial statistics and relevant yearbooks of the Pearl River Delta (PRD) cities as well as all the key industrial policy plans, five-year plans, as well as documents concerning the implementation of the Outline Plan and the Industrial Layout Plans of the nine cities and the three economic circles. Some documents were not publicly available so my RA and I had to summarize them during research trips to Guangzhou. I have access to most, but not all, of the key documents related to this policy. I have further interviewed officials in relevant bureaus in four of the PRD cities (including one from each of the three circles) as well as other experts in Guangzhou who were knowledgeable about this industrial planning. Nonetheless, despite repeated attempts through different liaison, I was unable to arrange interviews with officials from the other cities or the Provincial Outline Plan office. After analyzing (and tabulating) this huge amount of policy documents and interview information, I have already come up with my answers to the objectives of this study (please see below and the section on research findings and outcomes). (a) Rationale and Choice of Policy Design and Policy Instruments: Policy Objectives: The main objectives of the Industrial Layout Plan are: the clustering of key competitive industries, a rational division of labour among industrial sectors (to avoid too much convergence), coordination of locations of industries, more efficient allocation of resources, enhanced competitiveness, and improvement in environment. There is also an overall guideline for the spatial distribution of these sectors: (a) the development of knowledge-intensive industries and services in the eastern bank (mainly eastern and central parts of Guangzhou, Dongguan and Shenzhen), (b) the development of technological-intensive industrial belt in the western bank (mainly northern and southern parts of Guangzhou, Foshan and Zhongshan-Zhuhai), and (c) the heavy industrial belt along the coast (coastal parts of Huizhou, Shenzhen, Zhuhai and Jiangmen), and (d) a rational division of labor and coordination between the three economic circles identified earlier. The policy goals of the Industrial Layout Plan as well as the subsequent implementation plans of the three economic zones and the nine cities were tabulated, compared and analyzed in this project. Policy Design and Policy Instruments: The policy design for the five integration plans is based on an elaborate mix of policy instruments, including (a) formal deliberation mechanisms at the provincial and municipal level that would meet regularly, such as Leadership Small Groups at both levels, and joint mayoral or leadership meetings at the economic circle level; (b) a performance appraisal mechanism which includes very detailed indicators to be achieved, (c) a set of fixed time frame for policy completion and assessment, namely the “four years of major achievement” (2009-2012), and “nine years of great strides” (2012-2020), and (d) the establishment of dedicated offices for coordinating the information collection and implementation of the Outline Plan and integration plans. My analysis of the policy design and instruments was done mainly through a systematic analysis of the evolution of these measures adopted in the implementation. (b) Politics of the Policy Process: My analysis of the politics of the policy process was achieved through a careful comparison and analysis of the objectives promulgated in the Industrial Layout Plan and changes in the policy decisions and measures adopted by the three economic circles and the nine cities. The nine cities were found to be keenly aware of their own interests and responded strategically to provincial initiatives through formalistic and selective implementation. Under the pressure for firm implementation through regular administrative evaluation, these municipal governments were compelled to cooperate on more feasible projects, namely infrastructure or other areas rather than the coordination of industrial development. (c) Analysis of the Policy Design and Instruments in Policy Implementation The policy instruments adopted by the provincial government have major limitations which could not bring about the intended effects, according to my analysis of the performance indicators based on the documents and interviews with relevant officials and experts involved in the assessment. For instance, the performance indicators were related to socio-economic development, rather than effectiveness in coordination or division of labor among the nine cities. The assessment system of the Outline Plan targets the overall achievement of this grand plan, rather than a detailed assessment of each of the five integration plans, which was only conducted once in 2011. One major defect of the policy design is that the provincial government had not designed a clear set of integration indicators because most indicators measure general economic and industrial development. Further, there are considerable elements for hasty and subjective evaluation by experts invited by the provincial authorities given the constraint of time and brief on-site assessment. The lack of consensus over policy goals and the competition among the cities also aggravate the difficulties for implementation. While the elaborate assessment mechanisms have created enormous pressure for these cities to follow provincial directives, they could only bring about formalistic and selective implementation, rather than substantive and effective implementation of the Industrial Layout Plan. Cities were reluctant to coordinate among themselves even though they were in the same economic circle because this would affect their own ranking in assessment.

741113.label: Major findings and research outcome
741113.value: An intricate set of policy instruments were employed to implement the industrial layout plan in the PRD in 2009-2012: (a) authority: using administrative rules, (e.g. provincial rules and regulations), decision making mechanisms (the leadership small groups and joint conferences in the economic circles), inspection and assessment, (b) organization: establishing the meeting system and the creation of the Outline Plan offices and other organs for liaison and coordination, and (c) information: compilation and reporting of information, and publication of assessment results. Nonetheless, (d) financial instruments were not employed. The characteristics of the strategies of policy implementation include: (a) the “campaign-style” policy implementation initiated by the provincial authorities, (b) prioritization of more feasible projects by cities at the level of economic circles, (c) formalistic implementation by the economic circles and the cities, and (d) strategic/selective implementation of policy priorities by the cities. Further, the elaborate formal process of evaluation and the political attention of the provincial authorities may create an impression that there was effective implementation, but this was really not the case. This study has shown that policy design matters. The policy design—many ambitious policy goals and less feasible policy instruments, and the ineffectiveness of the policy instruments adopted, explain why this policy implementation was not as effective as expected. Despite the adoption of many authority, organization and information tools by the provincial government and the top-down, “campaign-style” implementation with a tight schedule, this policy implementation could not achieve all its intended goals. These observations are the most important contributions to the growing literature on policy implementation, state rescaling and development planning in China. Three outputs have so far been delivered, namely a refereed book chapter, one conference paper for an international conference in 2017, and another short presentation for another international conference in 2016. Owing to personal reasons stated in previous progress report and also unexpected extra teaching commitment in 2017, I have not yet fully published the findings of this project. My key findings were summarized in the 2017 conference paper (attached to this report) and it is now being revised into two separate journal manuscripts, one focusing on the politics of policy implementation for an area studies journal and another one focusing on policy design and instruments for a policy studies journal. Then, I plan to write one more article on the politics of state rescaling for an urban or regional studies journal.

741113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
741113.value: This study has shown that it is useful to apply concepts and theoretical frameworks from public policy studies to the analysis of policy implementation in contemporary China. If there is further funding and the possibility for collaboration and access to data in Guangdong, it would be useful to carry out a similar study of the implementation of the other integration plans, especially the infrastructural plan, under the Outline Plan, and systematically analyze whether the implementation of the other plans has achieved its intended objective. Further research into the other policy domains of the five integration plans would provide more data for a more systematic comparison of the political and policy dynamics involved.

741113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
741113.value: The Outline Plan for the Reform and Development of the Pearl River Delta (PRD) aims to expedite the coordinated development of the region which was characterized by decentralization and competition among its nine cities. The formulation of five integration plans, covering (a) industrial layout, (b) infrastructure, (c) urban-rural integration, (d) environmental protection, and (e) public services was the means to accomplish such a vision. An intricate set of policy instruments were employed to implement the industrial layout plan: (a) authority: setting rules and regulations, decision making (the leadership small groups and joint conferences in the economic circles), inspection and assessment, (b) organization: establishing the meeting system and the creation of the Outline Plan offices and other organs for coordination, and (c) information: requesting the compilation and reporting of information, and publication of assessment results. However, despite the reliance on such tools and intense attention from the provincial leadership in implementation, the actual process has turned out to be less successful than expected because of the faulty policy design and complicated instruments adopted. Therefore, it is important for scholars to conduct systematic analysis of policy implementation in order to find out more about what really happens in the Chinese policy process.

741213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
741213.value: About 20% of the world population live in China. Of these, 99% of young adults (aged 15 to 24 years) can read and write. Despite the enormous number of Chinese readers, not much is know about the visual requirements of Chinese reading. Our main goal is to use the principles of visual science to understand Chinese reading. Chinese characters are a special class of visual symbols because they occupy a square area despite the wide range of visual complexity levels. How does visual complexity influence the visual requirements of Chinese reading? The visual complexity is a dimension that cannot be addressed though the study of English reading. The current research plan consists of three series of experiments. In Series 1, we will focus on the character size and contrast requirements of Chinese reading. Human vision varies in sensitivity depending on the level of fine-detailed information present in the visual pattern. We will explain the visual limitations in Chinese reading due to character size, contrast and visual complexity by the fundamental limitations in human vision. In Series 2, we will focus on explaining reading performance by a concept called visual span. Visual span is the number of recognizable characters without shifting one’s eye gaze. We will explain Chinese reading as a bottom-up process with Chinese character recognition being an intermediate step. In Series 3, we will focus on visual crowding, a key factor affecting the visual span. The roles of parts and whole in recognizing a flanked, complex object are still not well understood. Chinese characters is a perfect stimulus class for studying how parts and whole influence visual crowding of a complex object. Results from this proposed project will provide a new perspective on how the role of visual complexity on reading. 中國人口佔全世界人口大約百分之二十；其中，百分之九十九的青壯年（年齡介乎十五至二十四歲）能夠閱讀並書寫 。儘管能夠閱讀中文的人如此多，科學界對中文閱讀的視覺要求所知的非常有限。我們這個研究項目的主要目的是要運用視覺科學的原則去了解中文閱讀。中文字符是一類非常特殊的視覺符號，因為無論是視覺複雜程度如何不同的中文字，它們也是佔據着面積大概相同的一個正方格 。中文字的視覺複雜程度如何影響中文閱讀的視覺要求呢？相比之下，視覺複雜程度所帶來的影響就不能在英文閱讀的框架下研究。 我們目前的研究計劃包括三個系列的實驗。在系列（一），我們將著重於中文閱讀的字符大小和亮度對比的要求。人類視覺的靈敏度取決於在視覺圖案中信息的精細程度。我們將透過人類視覺的基本局限，去解釋中文閱讀因字符大小、亮度對比和視覺複雜程度而有的視覺限制。 在系列（二），我們將著重於用一個叫做視覺廣度的概念來解釋中文閱讀能力。視覺廣度是指當一個人凝視於一點時所能識別的字符數目 。我們將解釋中文閱讀為一個自下而上的過程，而中文字符識別是這個過程中的一個步驟。 在系列（三），我們將著重於一個影響視覺廣度的關鍵因素—視覺擁擠 。當一個複雜的物件的週圍有其他物件時，這物件的部件和整體在識別這物件中的角色仍然未得到很好的理解。中文字符是非常合適研究物件的部件和整體如何影響一個複雜物件的視覺擁擠的一類視覺符號。 這個研究項目的結果將提供一個嶄新的角度去理解視覺複雜程度在閱讀中的角色。

741213.label: Realisation of objectives
741213.value: A detailed report is attached in Part C. Objective 1. To investigate the effect of visual complexity on the visual requirements (character size and contrast) of Chinese reading. We finished six psychophysical experiments investigating the reading-speed-versus-character-size and reading-speed-versus-contrast curves. We studied the effects of presentation method (flashcard vs. rapid-serial-visual-presentation) and sentence structure (real sentences vs. random character strings) on reading-speed curves in the first two experiments. The two experiments laid the foundation for subsequent experiments. The other four experiments addressed the effect of visual complexity on the reading-speed-versus-character-size and reading-speed-versus-contrast curves using real sentences or random character strings. An important summary measure of the reading-speed-versus-character-size curve was the critical print size, the smallest print size achieving 80% of the maximum reading speed. Interestingly, critical print size changed with complexity only when random character strings were used. On the other hand, critical contrast changed with complexity regardless of whether random character strings were used. Objective 2. To explain Chinese reading using the contrast-sensitivity-function (CSF) model. In the original proposal, we planned to study the spatial frequency properties of reading. However, as we started implementing the plan, we realized that we would need to address the spatial frequency properties of the precursor of Chinese reading⎯Chinese character recognition. We studied the spatial frequency properties of Chinese character recognition in one psychophysical experiment. We measured the Chinese-character based contrast sensitivity functions (CSF) under three complexity conditions. Peak tuning frequency in each CSF function was used as a summary measure. We found that the relationship between peak tuning frequency and character size was modulated by complexity. Objective 3. To investigate the effect of visual complexity on visual span in Chinese reading. We finished two psychophysical experiments addressing the impact of visual complexity on visual span in Chinese reading. In the first experiment, we formed character groups with different levels of average complexity. We measured character recognition accuracy in a trigram recognition task. We found that visual span shrank in size as average complexity increased. In the second experiment, we formed character groups with different levels of complexity variability. Higher variability in complexity in a group led to lower similarity in complexity within a trigram. Interestingly, variability in complexity did not influence visual span size. Objective 4. To investigate the roles of parts and whole in visual crowding of complex Chinese characters. We finished one psychophysical experiment addressing the effects of internal part scrambling on crowding of complex Chinese characters. We had published findings on this experiment in the Journal of Vision.

741213.label: Major findings and research outcome
741213.value: A detailed report is attached in Part C. We found the following: 1. Different from English reading, rapid-serial-visual-presentation (RSVP) method did not lead to higher reading speed than flashcard method in Chinese reading. 2. Critical print size changed with complexity only when random character strings were used. 3. Critical contrast changed with complexity regardless of whether random character strings were used. 4. The relationship between peak tuning frequency and character size was modulated by complexity. 5. Visual span shrank in size as average complexity increased. 6. Variability in complexity within a trigram did not influence visual span size. 7. Compared with the real-character flanked condition, scrambled-character flanked condition had significantly lower threshold elevation, but pseudo-character flanked condition and non-character flanked condition did not.

741213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
741213.value: Findings from the experiments supported by this grant laid an important foundation for further understanding of the visual process in Chinese reading. The concept of visual span had been used to explain difficulties in English reading encountered by people with visual impairment. It will be an important direction to understand whether the same can be applied in Chinese reading. With the current findings, we can now turn to study the visual requirements of Chinese reading among people with different forms of visual impairments.

741213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
741213.value: This project aimed to understand the visual requirements in Chinese reading. We first studied how reading speed changed with character size and with contrast. We then explored the role of a unique feature of Chinese characters—wide range of visual complexity—in reading. Our findings laid important and necessary foundation for further investigation of the determining or limiting factors in reading. Such investigation has important clinical implications when we seek to help people with visual impairments read better.

741613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
741613.value: Widowhood is a common life experience in older population. Majority can come to terms with the loss without formal intervention. Yet available studies consistently show that about one fifth of the bereaved persons experience persistent difficulties and in need of bereavement intervention. In Hong Kong, about one third of the older population is widowed. Widowhood is considered as the most upsetting psychosocial challenge faced by older people. Extreme emotions as well as adverse effects in health and daily functioning are routinely evidenced among widows and widowers. While aging in later life produces significant challenges, widowed older adults face even more. Coupled with growing numbers of nuclear families and diminishing number of children per couple, the natural familial support for widowed older adults is weakening. There is a need to develop formal support in the community. The level of effectiveness of psychosocial interventions for bereaved persons varies across different studies, reflecting the diversities of types of bereavement interventions. There is a call for more sensitive and systematic way in defining the psychosocial bereavement interventions and more vigorous empirical evaluation of these interventions. Over the last four years, the co-investigators in the United States developed a structured bereavement group for widowed older adults. It adopts a group work approach consisting of fourteen sessions. Switching from the convention bereavement intervention, which is loss-oriented and focus solely on handling the separation distress, extra attention is paid to the handling of adjustment to the life without the deceased or focus in the restoration. Adopting from the Dual Process Model, the leading theory in the field of bereavement, the intervention accentuates the unique feature of oscillations between loss-orientation and restoration-orientation into the intervention. This intervention has been shown to help widowed older persons cope with loss. The intervention model is replicated in Hong Kong and has undergone robust procedures in translation and refinement to fit into the cultural context. Pilot tests were carried out and the result concurred with the findings in the United States. This proposed study is the next step to perfecting the intervention model. Adopting a higher standard through randomized controlled trials in testing and restricting to those who have complicated grief, this proposed study will be the first of its kind in Asia. The proposed study will relieve distresses induced by widowhood faced by the growing numbers of Chinese older adults in Hong Kong, China and other parts of the world. 喪偶是很多長者所面對的挑戰。儘管大部分長者在沒有外來幫助下，仍能繼續生活，但研究顯示，約有五份一的喪偶人士，需要專業的幫助。在香港，每三名長者，就有一名為鰥寡者。老年喪偶可算是最影響長者心靈的經歷，令他們有各種身體、情緒、社交及思想上的困擾。 隨著社會家庭結構的改變。很多長者並不是與子女同住，甚至分隔萬里。加上生育率下降，長者的家庭支援網絡漸漸萎縮。導致社會要發展正式的支援。然而國際上的喪親介入法成效研究結果不一，而喪親介入法又各式各樣。故迫切地需要更嚴謹的研究，去評估最有效的喪親介入法。美國的研究伙伴，在過去四年，設計及改善了一套共有十四節的心理小組喪親介入法。其特色為：以理論為本，應用盛行的「喪親雙軌理論」為鑑，對失缺及適應均同樣重視。突破以失缺為本的舊介入模式。香港的研究員，亦為這西方模式注入華人元素，再為這模式作先導研究。結果亦同樣正面。本研究基於先導研究的結果，再以更嚴謹的方法去檢視這模式的成效。這亦是亞洲的首項相關研究，期盼能為未來面對喪偶的長者，減輕面對喪偶的傷痛。

742513.label: Project Objectives
742513.value: To analyze the newly enthroned ruler of Ming Dynasty following the well- established tradition in Chinese history to patronize the development of traditional astronomy as part of his legitimate duties. To understand the dual managerial and competitive mechanism between the Chinese and Islamic astronomical systems within the Astronomical Bureau of Ming government. To evaluate the impact of translation endeavour of Islamic astronomical- astrological literatures in early Ming. To unfold the hidden links of Islamic astronomical instruments in the imperial court and private studies of such instruments amongst the Chinese Muslim-Confucian groups in early and mid Ming period. Based on the detailed records and images of astronomical instruments found in both the rare books of the Ming edition and Ottoman manuscripts, electronic three dimensional models of astronomical instruments will be devised and delivered online via apps to mobile devices. Assembling detailed documentation and archival information of these instruments and their producers so as to create a timeline-based website to facilitate in-depth appreciation and understanding of Islamic-China technology transfer before the arrival of the Jesuits in East Asia.

742513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
742513.value: The aim of this project is to study the relationship between the “imperial patronage” and the advancement of exact science (astronomy in particular) in Ming Dynasty before the coming of the Jesuits in the late 16th century. Special cases demonstrating knowledge transfer, for instances, translation endeavour of Islamic astronomical- astrological literature in early Ming, making of Islamic astronomical-astrological- horological instruments in early-and-mid Ming, and knowledge dissemination of Islamic astronomy amongst Chinese Muslim-Confucian groups in mid Ming will be investigated comprehensively. Besides, scientific lineage of Chinese and non-Chinese astronomical officials (Islamic inclusive) in Ming period will also be added. With the aid of the latest computer technologies, searchable full-text Chinese databases and instrument display gallery for fundamental research of the history of Chinese science and technology will be created. 本研究旨在究明明初以迄明季耶穌會士來華前“帝王翼贊”與精密科學(特別是天文學)推進之相互關係。舉凡史事涉知識傳播如明初伊斯蘭天文占星文獻之翻譯、明初迄中葉伊斯蘭天文—占星—計時儀器之製作、明中葉回儒社群間伊斯蘭天文學知識之傳衍等歷史個案皆在詳細考察之列。再者，明欽天監漢族與少數民族天文官員(含伊斯蘭天文官)之科技系譜亦將論述。復在近時最新電腦技術輔助下，具備全文檢索功能之中文數據庫與供中國科學技術史基礎研究之儀器演示廊亦將建立。
