742813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
742813.value: In the West where arbitration is widely used and favored by the international business community, arbitration laws culminate from the jurisprudence of the 1985 Model Law on International Commercial Arbitration (ML) published by the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL). In order to catch up with the Western trend and to transform into favorable fora of international business dispute resolution, Asian jurisdictions start to reform their arbitration legislations on basis of the ML since mid-1990s. Since 1994, the Chinese experiment of transplanting the ML has met varied problems: the administrative governance system of arbitration originally practiced in China clashes with the autonomous principle of international arbitration norms, and her regulatory system for international arbitration is still young. This project studies the emergence of Asian jurisdictions in receiving the ML in developing themselves into regional or international centers of dispute resolution. The jurisdictions under consideration represent a selected sample in Asia which have similar legal backgrounds to China (i.e. South Korea, Japan) and close economic ties with China (i.e. Hong Kong) which have substantially reformed their arbitration legislations on basis of the ML over the past decade. A first aim of the study is to provide a comprehensive review of the way in which how arbitration systems are reformed in these jurisdictions. A second and ultimate aim is to study the issues that need to be explored for the reform of the arbitration system of the mainland China, by comparing the Chinese arbitration laws and operational experience to those in the ML-based Asian jurisdictions. It seeks to distill successful elements from these jurisdictions, identify best experiences, analyse local circumstances, and formulate ways to frame these elements for the reform in the legal as well as socio-political, socio-economic contexts of China. The aims of the proposed project are both theoretical and practical, and when completed it will be both a valuable contributor to Chinese arbitration reform by offering important insights and a first-time cross-jurisdiction comparative study of the developing world of arbitration in Asia.

742813.label: Realisation of objectives
742813.value: In the GRF research proposal, the PI has suggested that a conference is desirable for the sharing of experience of individual Asian jurisdictions under investigation. The conference is also intended to conduct a comparative study of arbitration reforms among Asian jurisdictions, and to shed light on China’s future reform. To prepare for the conference, since the beginning of the project, the PI has been in active contact with potential country experts in Asia. After sufficient preparation, a GRF-projected one-day conference was organized by the PI. The conference was entitled, “The Developing World of Arbitration: A Comparative Study of Arbitration Reforms in China and Asia Pacific”, held on 27 October 2015, at University of Hong Kong Faculty of Law. The conference has attracted wide interests, in particular, interests from United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL) Headquarter (in Vienna, Austria), its Asia Pacific Regional Office (in Incheon, Korea), Hague Conference Asia Pacific Regional Office (in Hong Kong), Australia Center for International Commercial Arbitration (in Sydney), and National Judges’ College of China (in Beijing). Due to the high interests from international, regional and national organizations, the Faculty of Law of the University of Hong Kong decided to sponsor the conference, which explains why the budget item for “General Expenses” allocated in the GRF project has not been much used. The PI has had the pleasure where some of the international organizations became collaborators in the organization of the conference. We were indeed honored that the UNCITRAL Secretary General, Mr. Renaud Sorieul, gave the closing remark for the conference. The conference information was available on the UNCITRAL website, http://www.uncitral.org/pdf/english/TAC/RCAP/Conference_on_Arbitration_Reform_in_the_Asia_Pacific_--_27_October_2015.pdf. To achieve research objectives and research outcomes, while planning the conference, the PI has been working tirelessly on book proposals (with a unanimous template to be applied to all Asian arbitration jurisdictions to answer relevant research questions envisaged by the GRF project), working on sample chapters (written by PI herself), and approaching potential publishers. The PI has been in strong wish to turn the outputs in the conference into a volume with internationally reputable publishers in law. Hart Publishing quickly showed interest and the peer review process by three international reviewers all went smooth. The entire book manuscript has now been submitted to Hart. The book will be published in February 2018 at Oxford. The PI has also conducted a few research trips to China and visited some of the investigated Asian jurisdictions to contextualize the research findings. Most of the research trips were conducted while the PI was invited to attend conferences there. As such, the budget item, “Field Trip”, allocated in the project has not been much used. Lastly but very importantly, the budget on “Teaching Relief” has enabled the PI to relieve teaching duties and to buy out her time for concentrated research. The PI has benefitted tremendously from the valuable “teaching relief” and have published quite prolifically in this project. The research outputs include 1 book, 2 book chapters, and 4 journal articles. The PI is happy to report that all research outputs have been published by, or will be forthcoming with, leading international law publishers and leading international law journals. Moreover, all the book chapters and journal articles have been solely authored by myself, which echoes the importance and effective use of “teaching relief” to relieve me from teaching so that excellent research outcomes can be achieved. The budget for hiring research assistants (RAs) is also important. The RAs helped a lot in collecting literature in the initial period of research. The RAs are again critical in the footnote checking and bibliography compilation stage when the manuscripts are completed. To conclude, the PI is happy to report that the research objectives have all been satisfactorily achieved, and the research funds are well and properly used. Major findings and research outcomes arising out of the GRF project will be summarized below, under Section 6.

742813.label: Major findings and research outcome
742813.value: Major findings: The book provides a comprehensive analysis of the ways in which arbitration law and practice have recently been reformed in selected Asian jurisdictions (China, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan, Korea, and Singapore) under investigation. The book analyses these jurisdictions representing varying patterns and degrees of arbitration development, whether top-down (Japan, Korea, Singapore, Taiwan), bottom-up (China), or from a hybrid impetus (Hong Kong). The book findings present a first-time cross-jurisdiction comparative study of the arbitration reform in Asia and contributes to international arbitration literature from an Eastern perspective. The journal articles and book chapters contribute to the reform of the arbitration system in China, by comparing the Chinese arbitration law and operational experience to those investigated Asian jurisdictions. The comparative research shows that the Chinese path to arbitration reform is led from the top (such as the institutional arbitration monopoly), reflecting its prevailing political ideology on arbitration, while at the same time being reliant on and even accommodating of competition at the local level. The Chinese trajectory of arbitration reform is thus an attempt to synthesize a unique socio-economic dynamic, with both controlling element and free market features, and the free market features have become a more important force driving arbitration reform in China over the past decade. 742813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
742813.value: Perhaps for further development, future research could aim to identify an Asia Pacific model of arbitration modernisation, one that may be distinct from a Western model, and predicts future trajectories of development and challenge in light of the ever-increasing competition between Eastern and Western-based arbitration centres. This has been mentioned in the conclusion chapter, in Anselmo Reyes and Weixia Gu (eds), The Developing World of Arbitration: A Comparative Study of Arbitration Reform in the Asia Pacific (Oxford, Hart Publishing), forthcoming, February 2018. The ever-increasing competition between Eastern and Western-based arbitration centres is worthy of further studies, from both law, market, and economic perspectives.

742813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
742813.value: The project studies the recent emergence of Asian jurisdictions as regional or international arbitration centres. The project provides an up-to-date and comprehensive analysis of the ways in which arbitration laws and practices have recently been reformed in selected Asian jurisdictions (such as China, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan, Korea, and Singapore). The project analyses these jurisdictions representing varying patterns and degrees of arbitration development. Setting the arbitration systems and reforms of each investigated jurisdiction in the context of its economic, political, and judicial dynamics, this project presents a first-time cross-jurisdiction comparative and contextual study of the arbitration reform in Asia and contributes to comparative international arbitration literature from an Eastern perspective. A second and ultimate value is to contribute to the reform of the arbitration system of China, by comparing the Chinese arbitration law and operational experience to those investigated Asian jurisdictions which either share similar dispute resolution traditions, or have close economic ties, with China. The Chinese arbitration system has been governed by a rather backward law (China Arbitration Law 1994), although the arbitration market, as identified by the project, has been formed in China in the past decade.

742913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
742913.value: When we look at other people, we notice that in many ways there are great differences among us, but yet in other ways we are all the same. The discipline of Psychology reflects this view, focusing on some aspects of people that show salient differences (e.g., personality, culture, gender, etc.) and on other aspects in which people are highly similar to one another (e.g., memory, perception, neurophysiology). One issue that is rapidly growing in importance is the way in which fairly basic psychological processes, often assumed to be similar in all groups of people, show differences associated with culture or gender. In this project, we investigate a key example of cultural differences on Cognition. Previous research, primarily from our labs, has shown that East Asians and Caucasians scan faces in different ways. Whereas Caucasians make a triangular pattern of eye-movements, fixating on the two eyes and the mouth with successive saccades, Asians spend more time fixating towards the centre of the face, in particular the nose. While this pattern of difference is very clear, its underlying causes have so far not been established. In this project, we investigate three causes. First, we evaluate whether it is associated with a tendency by Asian participants to encode global aspects of a stimulus (for example, the background of a picture) and Caucasian participants to focus of figural objects. Second, we examine whether it is caused by socialization among Asian participants to avoid direct gaze (that is, looking into someone’s eyes). Third, we determine whether differences between Asian and Caucasian eye fixation patterns are reduced for 3D depictions of faces (using stereoscopic disparity). Taken together, these studies will enable us to draw firm conclusions about the cause of this cultural difference in the way that people acquire information about faces. N/A

743413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
743413.value: Background: As seen in many other places in the world, Hong Kong is experiencing rising inequalities among social groups and city neighborhoods. Our earlier UGC GRF funded study generated evidence, for the first time in Hong Kong, that a gap in school readiness between the rich and the poor exists before entering primary school. However, little is known about how this gap changes dynamically across time and contexts as students transition from kindergarten to formal education, and the extent to which family processsuch as parenting styles and the home learning environmentcan be useful in closing the gap. Objectives: Using our previous study on school readiness at Kindergarten Level Three (K3) as the baseline, this study will revisit the same cohort of children in 2014 when they are in Primary Grade Three (P3). With the data collected at the two time points, we will explore the predictive power of school readiness at K3 on school success (in terms of both academic achievement and psycho-behavioral outcomes) at P3 in Hong Kong Chinese society. In particular, this study will focus on those starting with developmental vulnerabilities at K3, to examine whether the chance for them to catch up depends on family socio-economic status (SES). If so, how much of the impact from SES is due to family process. Study design: The cohort comprises 567 children who were originally assembled from 21 kindergartens randomly selected from high-income (Hong Kong Island) and low-income (Yuen Long) districts. During the baseline study (completed in 2011/12), children’s school readiness and family SES were measured. In this proposed study, when the children will be in P3 (first semester), their academic achievement (in Chinese and mathematics) will be assessed with a set of standard academic tests. Their parents/caregivers will be invited to complete a survey on the children’s psycho-behavioral outcomes, home learning environment, parenting style and socioeconomic characteristics. Contributions of the study: Together with the baseline study, the proposed work will be the first in Hong Kong to investigate the dynamics and impact of social inequality on child development from kindergarten to formal schooling age. Without imposing any additional interventions in schools, the evidence gathered from this study will allow us to explore the extent to which the current formal education in Hong Kong is effective in mitigating the impact of poverty on children with disadvantaged background. 背景： 正如在世界其他許多地方，香港也經歷社會和社區群體之間的不平等現象。我們早期的 UGC GRF研究結果發現，香港的貧富懸殊影射到兒童發展上的差距，在準備就讀小學之前已經存在。然而，我們還不知道這個差距如何能因應時間和環境動態的變化，從幼兒園過渡到正規教育中，父母教養方式和家庭學習環境是否有助於縮小差距的程度。 研究目的： 我們用早前的研究『在學準備』上幼兒園高班（K3）的資料為基線，這項研究將在2014年在他們就讀小學三年級（P3）會再次作學術研究。我們將就兩個不同時間收集的數據，我們將探討兒童在K3的學前準備到學校全面發展（在學習成績和心理行為的結果） 的關係和進度。特別是，本研究重點將放在那些在K3開始發展的漏洞，評估他們是否能夠趕上的機會是否取決於對家庭社會經濟地位（SES） 。如果是這樣，有多少是由於家庭背景引發影響到家庭社會經濟地位（SES）。 研究設計： 本研究將包括567最初的高收入（香港島）和低收入（元朗）區隨機抽取21所幼兒園的兒童作學術研究。在基線研究（已在2011/12完成 ）孩子在學準備和家庭社經地位進行評估。在這個建議的研究中，當孩子就讀P3時（第一學期），他們的學術成就（中文和數學）將作學術測試評估。我們會邀請他們的父母/監護人完成一項調查，當中包括孩子的心理行為的結果，家庭學習環境，父母教養方式和社會經濟特點。 研究貢獻： 加上基線的研究，本研究將是第一個在香港由兒童發展研究動態和社會不平等的現象對幼兒園到適齡的兒童的影響。在不施加任何額外的干預學校的情況之下，從本研究收集的結果將允許我們去探索香港目前的正規教育是否有效減輕貧困兒童的衝擊與其弱勢背景。

743413.label: Realisation of objectives
743413.value: A total of 519 parent-child dyads have been successfully followed up and reassessed. Children's academic achievement and psychosocial well-being were assessed using the proposed standardised measurements (LAMK and SDQ); family environment and parenting style were self-reported by parents using validated instruments. The data collected sufficiently and satisfactorily achieved all the four proposed objectives. Objective 1 Using the standardised scores of academic achievement and psychosocial well-being, this study has verified the existence of socioeconomic gap in school success in 9-year-old children. The effect size of SES index (a comprehensive indicator of socioeconomic status) on children’s cognitive performance was medium sized (eta-squared 0.09; p<0.0001) while that on their psychosocial wellbeing was small-to-medium (eta-squared 0.05; p<0.0001). Objective 2 Using the same data-set, this study was able to test whether school readiness at K3 could predict the school success in P3. In general, school readiness and its sub-domains were able to predict both academic achievement (beta 0.17, 95% CI 0.08-0.26, p<0.001) and psychosocial well-being (beta 0.22, 95% CI 0.13-0.31, p<0.001). Among the five sub-domains of school readiness, language and cognitive ability has the strongest predictive association with academic achievement (beta 0.21, 95% CI 0.12-0.29, p<0.001) whereas social competence has the strongest with psychosocial well-being (beta 0.20, 95% CI 0.13-0.31, p<0.001). This suggests the importance of school readiness in early childhood in Chinese population. Objective 3 To study whether the socioeconomic gap was attenuated or intensified during the three years, the effect sizes of SES index on cognitive and psychosocial development were compared across two time points. In K3, the Cohen's d of SES index on both cognitive and psychosocial development were about 0.02 (p=0.01), which are equivalent to small sized effects. After three years of formal schooling, however, the effect size of SES index on academic achievement (cognitive development) was increased to 0.09 (p<0.001) and that on psychosocial wellbeing was increased to 0.05 (p<0.001). The increment in both effect sizes were statistically significant (p=0.0009 & p=0.016). The findings signify that the socioeconomic gap was intensified after three years of formal schooling, particularly on academic achievement. Objective 4 The dynamic of changes in gaps at the two time points in relation to family process related factors were studied using path analysis on a series of potential mediators, including parent-child interaction, family learning environment, parental involvement in school, parenting style, child's sleep duration, electronic device use, and physical activity level. In the first stage, these factors were tested individually in univariate mediation analyses, in which significant factors were then used in multivariable path analysis models. The path analyses showed that time spent in video gaming at K3 and family learning environment at P3 were both significant mediator between SES index and academic achievement. These two factors mediated more than 40% of the socioeconomic gap.

743413.label: Major findings and research outcome
743413.value: This project is one of the first studies in Chinese community to longitudinally examine the influence of family socioeconomic status on academic achievement and psychosocial wellbeing. In this study, we identified a significant socioeconomic gap among P3 primary school students. Children from families of higher socioeconomic status scored better in both academic achievement and psychosocial well-being. This gap was actually intensified compared with that in the third year of preschool (K3). This signifies that the current formal schooling in Hong Kong is not sufficient to bridge the cognitive and psychosocial gap between the rich and the poor. The study also found that the socioeconomic gap at P3 was partially mediated by time spent on video gaming at K3 and family learning environment at P3. These two factors added together were responsible for more than 40% of the relationship between SES and school success. Controlled for family socioeconomic status, school readiness in early childhood also significantly predicts academic achievement and psychosocial wellbeing in P3. The first part of the findings has already been published in Early Child Research Quarterly. The predictive power of school readiness and the dynamic changes in socioeconomic gap are going to be reported in two separate papers. In addition, this project also identified that sleep deprivation in early childhood, a very common problem in low income families, longitudinally associated with attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder after controlling for family background. This suggests that sleep hygiene and habit in early childhood may serve as a potential entry point to tackle the developmental disparity related to family socioeconomic gradient. These findings had already been reported in a paper submitted to The Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry. Meanwhile, findings of this study has also been presented in various local and international conferences, such as the Seminar on Public Issues of Excessive use of Internet, Computers, Smartphones and Similar Electronic Devices co-organised by World Health Organisation and Hong Kong Department of Health (9 September 2016) and Roadmap for Scaling Up Early Child Development — Investment in Human Capital for Economic Growth and Poverty Alleviation organised by China Development Research Foundation (27-28 October 2016).

743413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
743413.value: This study identified the widened socioeconomic gap in both academic achievement and psychosocial wellbeing which may lead to intergenerational poverty. The study also identified the important mechanisms of the socioeconomic gradient, which opens a potential entry point to tackle intergenerational poverty through early intervention. We are going to seek for funding to develop a comprehensive intervention programme based on the findings of this study. The intervention will have components to build up the parenting capacity of underprivileged families as well as supporting kindergartens in poorer areas. In addition, this Chinese cohort with comprehensive data on family background, parenting, and development can be further followed in the future to study whether the widened socioeconomic gap will change. Over 80% of the cohort are followed up so far. More than 70% of the parent-child dyads also approved us to retrieve their hospital utilisation records in Clinical Diagnosis and Analysis Report System (CDARS) in the Hong Kong Hospital Authority. This will allow us to conduct pioneering social epidemiological studies on the health disparity in a Chinese community. Last but not least, this study provides valuable preliminary data on children's use of electronic devices, which lead to the successful acquisition of the UGC Theme-based Research Project on Digital Citizenship.

743413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
743413.value: Our study in kindergartens already showed children from wealthier families had better school readiness than their peers from underprivileged families. However, it was still uncertain whether the education system in Hong Kong could act as an equaliser to bridge the gap between the rich and the poor. In other words, we did not know whether the socioeconomic gap in early childhood will intensity or attenuate. This study addressed this question by following up the children and parents in the original kindergarten study. After three years in formal schooling, the developmental gap of children has widened, particularly on academic achievement. The socioeconomic status of families may affect children’s development through multiple mechanisms and this study suggested that early exposure to video gaming and family learning environment during primary school were two important pathways. It was also noted that sleep deprivation in early childhood, a common issue among underprivileged children, is associated with attention deficit/hyperactive disorder.

743513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
743513.value: In “Times of Turbulence”-- when resource constraints pair with intractable social problems, the public expects heroic acts on the part of its civil servants (Waldo 1971). Conduct of public business according to the ordinary virtues associated with the administrative role—procedural justice, neutrality, and fidelity to the law-- cannot fulfill the expectations of a public that expects heroic-- courageous, innovative, and risk-acceptant-- efforts to fulfill public policies. Heroic public service requires internal motivation to apply uncommon virtues on the part of civil servants. Building upon theses posited in my previous book project, I argue here that effective public and non-profit administration requires employees of public organizations to manage themselves ethically under the prevailing conditions of complex interdependence, cross-cultural collaboration, innovation, entrepreneurship, and turbulence. Coping with these conditions requires rethinking the importance of internal motivation to serve the public. I argue here that the ideal source of internal motivation is a set of profession-specific virtues that employees of public organizations, specifically, should adopt. These six “uncommon” virtues—meekness, propriety, temperance, magnanimity, ingenuity, and beneficence are essential to the mission of public organizations to fulfill justice in both its procedural and substantive forms. The virtues of procedural justice—meekness, magnanimity, and beneficence—guide collaboration between administrative agencies, administrators and contractors, and between administrators and their clients. The virtues of substantive justice or of innovation under conditions of resource scarcity and conflict are: propriety, temperance, and ingenuity. To make the case for this book, I advance the thesis that public service ethics that focus on merely obeying the law or abiding by the tenets of professional codes of conduct do not provide administrators with sufficient material to cope with value pluralism and international collaboration. Instead, an internally motivated, virtue-based perspective is needed. However, consistently carping upon public servants to adopt the virtues commonly advocated for employees of public organizations stymies administrators’ efforts to exercise heroism—or innovative practical wisdom and entrepreneurial creativity-- in the conduct of their work. Developing this virtue perspective, I adopt a virtues in the profession model that hearkens to the work of both Edmund Pellegrino and Carl Friedrich and extends the assumptions of their work to support a heroic public management ethics. 743713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
743713.value: 喬治•奧威爾與亞洲 本專案提案是首次圍繞喬治•奧威爾作品中亞洲的位置、再現與意義的具體研究。喬治•奧威爾是二十世紀英國最重要的作家之一。 在他只有二十餘載的寫作生涯，他出版了大量的文學作品，其中包括小說、新聞、政論以及個人自傳。這些作品使他在冷戰時期聞名於世，而他正是第一個將該時期稱作“冷戰時期”的人。在現今後殖民和全球化時期，他更是聲名遠播。奧威爾是以政論作品而闻名，所以儘管在1998年, 他的全部著作已收錄全20卷的《喬治•奧威爾全集》，但對他的文學批評研究並不多，尤其是從新興的後殖民批評角度對他所有作品的文學研究還是一片空白。這也是本項目試圖填補的空白。 身為英國人，奧威爾寫了不少有闗「英國風格亅的作品，也曾被譽為特別「英式亅的作家。這是準確的描述。但他也歸屬於家庭和民族的人，大英帝國時期和其逐漸走向衰落的過程，都深深地影響著他。他也見證了英帝國最早的、也是最重要的兩次分別對愛爾蘭和印度的非殖民化。他的家境遭遇同寫作生涯與亞洲息息相關。奧威爾於1903年出生於印度。他父親是印度行政官員，在主事鴉片專賣部門工作。，離開學校後，在反大英帝國統治情緒逐漸高漲的時期，奧威爾在緬甸殖民地成為了印度帝國警務處的官員，任職五年。 他出版的第一本小說《緬甸歲月》以及兩篇最著名的文章《絞刑》和《射象》都是基於他在緬甸的經歷所寫。在二十世紀三十年代，奧威爾是反帝國主義的強硬派。之後，他成為了一名社會主義者。在他的政論作品中，他總是會回到反帝國主義這一主題上，甚至在《通往威根碼頭之路》一文中用了相當長的篇幅來描述在緬甸警署任職的經歷。在第二次世界大戰時期，他在英國廣播公司東方部門負責節目製作，同時廣泛寫作，用於在印度廣播。 本項目試圖尋求殖民時期的亞洲對奧威爾的意義。本專案從不公正制度的帝國模型出發，緊緊圍繞奧威爾這主人公同時又是「帝國骯髒工作亅的共謀者展開討論。其關鍵不僅是分析奧威爾作品中的東方，更能投射他的全部作品，從《巴黎倫敦落魄記》的東方化世界到《一九八四》中的恐懼帝國。本項目也能為在全球化的二十一世紀中理解奧威爾的意義奠定基礎。

743713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
743713.value: George Orwell, possibly the greatest English writer of the 20th Century, is usually thought of as particularly English, or at least European. But he was born in India, and worked as a young man in the Indian Imperial Police in colonial Burma, where his political identity was formed. His first novel is set in Burma. This project reorients Orwell as an Asian writer, whose anti-imperialism was and remained the emotional and intellectual basis for his socialism, and inflects all his later writing, both novels and non-fiction, up to "Nineteen Eighty-Four" and beyond. (Two of the above publications find a genealogy for Orwell's representations of law and order in colonial history, for example.) The project aspires to effect a significant change in the way Orwell is read.

743913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
743913.value: 德國文學對維多利亞文學的影響：理念、形式、體裁 摘要 這個研究項目追溯德國文學對英國維多利亞時代文學的影響。具體來說，它旨在展示德國的美學思想和實踐在英國作家小說作品的重要性，包括由Carlyle、Bulwer-Lytton、勃朗特姊妹以至蓋斯凱爾夫人、狄更斯、薩克萊、前拉斐爾派、Lewes、喬治•艾略特、哈代、Meredith、Moore、吉辛，還有佩特與王爾德。 德國傳統對英國浪漫主義（約公元1789年至1830年）的影響已被妥善記載，然而，當我們走至數十年以後的維多利亞女王統治時期（ 1837-1901 ），並進入19世紀的中期和後期，情況便有所不同。在這時期，英德關係，以及原先或同時在德國研究的英國美學理念、形式和體裁，幾乎全無記錄。 1830年以後，對德國文學和美學的顯著興趣，實是一目了然：除了大量有關德國寫作的文章刊登於英國文學雜誌外（如Monthly及Quarterly Review、Foreign Review和Blackwood’s Magazine），英國倫敦大學學院和國王學院（ 1828年和1831年）的德學教授亦同樣大大印證了這興趣。在他們的傳記中，我們也意識到數位英國作家深受德國文學和思想的影響：Carlyle、Lewes、喬治•艾略特、Meredith及Moore緊貼歐洲文學的發展，閱讀新的作品，甚至翻譯了其中的一些，並就英國和德國審美之差異和類近之處發表理論。 不過，我的研究提出德國的文學、理念、形式和體裁對維多利亞散文寫作的影響，遠遠超越個別作者的作品。它旨在探討德國的體裁和敘事方式，如何有意識或無意識地被大多維多利亞時期的作家融會、吸收、模仿和改造。 具體而言，此研究著眼於七種起源於德國，或在維多利亞時期於德國和英國同時出現的體裁和形式。 按（美學）的理念、形式、體裁、探究的範疇和集中的焦點分類如下： （1）哥德式故事， （2）成長小說， （3）童話故事和 （4）中篇小說； 以及，敘事方式之中的， （5）現實主義， （6）自然主義和 （7）唯美主義。 （重）回比較語言學的做法，這個研究項目是學術上一重要的提醒，維多利亞文學並非存在於一個獨立的文化空間，反之，它和歐洲的美學有不斷的互動交流。這研究以獨特的方式，把這種交流的理論學說與重要作品、理念和體裁的詳細分析結合。

743913.label: Realisation of objectives
743913.value: I am immensely pleased with the results of this GRF grant: the project had a bit of a slow start as I took the grant reviewers’ suggestions for a further limitation of research questions, genre(s) and primary corpus seriously and took some time to review and reformulate what would eventually become the Chapters of my research monograph. A strong focus on the realist novel emerged from this focalisation, and the project has become significantly stronger for it. I have discussed the book at various points with publishers (CUP and Routledge) at international conferences, and I am in the process of writing a formal book proposal for, first, Cambridge’s consideration. The monograph stands currently at 83,000 words and is to 90% completed, missing the revised Introduction and a short Conclusion. All data has been collected and there is only some writing to do. I am pleased that I published two internationally peer-reviewed articles from Chapters 1 and 2 (totalling 18,000 words), introducing my comparative research to the wider scholary community but still staying within the 20% requirement for a subsequent publication of my research in a monograph. (Academic publishers usually have the rule that no more than 20-25% of a monograph can have been already published in earlier drafts.) Objectives 1-5 have therefore been realised at 100%. Objective 6 (articles plus monograph draft), which I have currently estimated at 90%, will be realised to 100% within the first half of 2019. (See attachment of partial manuscript draft.) In 4 book chapters (Objective 1 and 6), I have traced the shape realism took in theoretical treatises and, consequently, the nineteenth-century German novel and I have compared the German deliberations and manifestations with select Victorian fiction (Objective 5). Chapter 1 traces the correlation between George Eliot’s becoming of George Eliot and her thoughts on realism (which she developed while living in Germany) and Fanny Lewald’s various aesthetic essays on the realist project: the chapter reads Eliot’s 'Felix Holt, the Radical' and Lewald’s novel 'Wandlungen' through the lens of a democratisation of the novels’ personnel and agenda. Chapter 2 reads Julius Schmidt’s theorisation of realism in the journal 'Die Grenzboten' before it embarks on how this critic and two other German authors, Gustav Freytag and Wilhelm Raabe, embraced Charles Dickens’s Bildungsroman model – which Dickens had himself adjusted from Johann Wolfgang Goethe’s model in 'Wilhelm Meister'. 'David Copperfield', 'Soll und Haben' and 'Der Hungerpastor' are here analysed through a focus on personal development and becoming (Objective 2 and 4). Chapter 3 focuses on William Makepeace Thackeray’s 'Vanity Fair' and Theodor Fontane’s 'Frau Jenny Treibel' and 'Effi Briest', read through a focus on class and money. Karl Marx’s 'Economic and Philosophical Manuscripts' as well as 'Das Kapital' are here used to explore a burgeoning capitalism (in the realist novel) but also what this means for human 'heroism’. Chapter 4 is a comparative analysis of Anthony Trollope’s 'Barchester Chronicles' (esp. 'Barchester Towers'), Gottfried Keller’s novella 'Romeo und Julia auf dem Dorfe' and Theodor Storm’s novellas 'Der Schimmelreiter' and 'Immensee' (Objective 4) through the concept of knowable communities, the concept of ‘the local’ versus ‘the world’ and an encroaching secularisation; concepts I develop through a critical reading of Raymond Williams. My Introduction and Conclusion argue that it is limiting to only conceptualise Victorian realism, as is commonly done, through the French and Russian models (from Flaubert, Stendhal and Zola to Tolstoy, Pushkin and Dostoevski): the German connection yields both surprising (and eventually unsurprising) affinities which, of course, result from Britain’s Germanophilia for most of the nineteenth century, and Germany’s leadership in industry, education, social reform and literature. Germany was as close to the British as was France, and even closer than Russia (Objective 3). [Please note that subcategories in various of the above Objectives – e.g. Gothic, fairy tale, naturalism, aestheticism – have become context and subtext in individual chapters as my focus cemented itself in the realist novel.]

743913.label: Major findings and research outcome
743913.value: Finding the focus on realism as genre, or modality, and also the appropriate author pairings for each chapter (and subsequent comparative readings of select prose texts) required a lot of reading and screening. My bilingualism (English and German) and academic background in Comparative and German Literature (as well as English Literature) has helped me read German nineteenth-century texts that are not available in translation but which I can now make available to a wider scholarly community. I am glad to have done so much reading and researching as the completed monograph ('the research outome') – which I expect to be primarily read by Victorian fiction/ realism scholars in the Anglo-American world – will provide a lot of ‘thick description’ and background information of a multitude of especially German realist text that the Victorian scholar may not necessarily have read. Victorian fiction scholars have all read Flaubert’s 'Madame Bovary' and Tolstoy’s 'War and Peace' (in English translations) but they will, through my research, now also ‘know’ canonical German realist texts. I am therefore confident that the research outcome and 'the major findings' -- namely, that the Anglo-German connection and the German realist models cannot be ignored by the future scholar who tries to understand the ‘theories’ and manifestations of British realism, as evidenced by the four author pairings that I foreground in my monograph -- will have both immediate and a lasting impact on Victorian studies.

743913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
743913.value: I will put this project to rest for now – I think I have said enough in my monograph and as much as I want to say, although one could, of course, extend the enquiry into other German and British authors. The next step is to bring my monograph to publication (ideally, with CUP) and dissemination in a larger scholarly community, in the shape of talks and having my monograph reviewed. In terms of research, I will continue with my interest in the form of the nineteenth-century novel in the GRF project submitted for consideration in the 2018-19 round: here, I will look at how, e.g. George Eliot’s and William Thackeray’s travelogues (about Germany, no less) manifested various narrative features and characteristics that would eventually flow into the development of the modern, realist novel. The new project, overall, analyses (starting with Daniel Defoe’s 'Robinson Crusoe', via Fanny Trollope, Eliza Lynn Linton, George Eliot, Charles Dickens, William Thackeray, Robert Louis Stevenson and ending with George Gissing’s 'By The Ionian Sea') how the older form of travel writing influenced and shaped the modern, realist novel: here, I focus on characteristics including plotting, ideology, mimesis and diegesis, protagonists and chronotopes. So this completed GRF's focus on the realist modality has built the foundation of the next monograph and GRF project.

743913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
743913.value: Over the last 120 years, critics of the British realist novel have looked to the French and Russian models developed simultaneously, to understand British realism’s aesthetic and political agenda. The German realist model, however, also happened at the same time and was, moreover, much closer in intellectual comparability as well as emotional affinity but has been unjustly overlooked by scholars – although this was not the case before 1920 where there existed a lot of Anglo-German comparative research. My completed GRF project and resultant monograph make the case for Britain’s indebtedness to the German aesthetic and a hitherto neglected cross-fertilisation of aesthetic ideas and literary outputs. In four chapters (plus Introduction and Conclusion) I exemplify this indebtedness and cross-fertilisation by recourse to Germany’s and Britain’s most important canonical authors, such as Eliot, Thackeray, Dickens and Trollope and, on the other side, Lewald, Fontane, Freytag, Raabe, Keller and Storm. Scholars of Victorian fiction will find this original contribution useful for their understanding of the realist novel; scholars of German studies and German literature between the 1830s and 1890s will here find critical paradigms and a focus on form and modality (rather than content) they do not usually find in the German academic tradition.

744013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
744013.value: The quantity and quality of its engineers is vital in the continuing development of Hong Kong (HK). Little systematic, rigorous or representative information exists to explain why/why not secondary students choose engineering as a career while, in HK, there has been a noticeable decline in engineering as a career choice. This decline also characterizes engineering career choice/engagement in post-industrial countries (e.g. UK) and contrasts with industrializing countries such as China. Given the need for engineers in industrializing and post-industrial countries, it is important to study when and why secondary school students may choose to pursue engineering studies. This proposal locates HK at the crux of industrializing and post-industrial countries, with a history of innovative engineering. HK students are offered many technology/engineering courses in upper secondary and vocational schools, and extra-curricular opportunities sponsored by engineering/manufacturing organizations. Understanding why engineering opportunities have not led to engineering career choice and what is likely to engage students in engineering education in HK (and elsewhere) is the basis of this proposal. Our findings will draw evidence-based conclusions concerning theory (underlying career choice), practice (pedagogies that support engineering engagement/career choice) and policy (contrasting diverse approaches in industrializing and post-industrial cultures). Our research is based on: 1) current literature which notes that no systematic or rigorous study exists regarding engineering education, 2) students are active participants in their course/career choices - but choice is constrained by organizational, pedagogic and personal/familial opportunities; and 3) a pilot investigation into engineering education opportunities among secondary school students in HK and China. In HK the pilot study found many students interested in engineering topics, especially younger students; traditional teaching methods unlikely to engage student interest; migrant and minority students more positively inclined towards engineering than home students; and, girls’ interest enhanced via single-sex opportunities. Compared to HK, Chinese students were more actively engaged in engineering education activities while being offered fewer engineering opportunities; and, more positive in attitudes to and contributions by engineers. Pilot findings were based on small-scale, opportunistic samples, and offer limited insight into organizational, pedagogic and personal opportunities associated with a career in engineering. Thus, we propose an integrated three-part study, comprised of: a representative engineering education survey of (2000+) secondary school students in HK; representative, explanatory case/interview studies of (18) secondary school students making career choices in HK; and comparative/cultural surveys of secondary school students in industrializing and post-industrial engineering cultures in China and the UK. 工程師的數量和質素對香港的持續發展有一定的影響。正當在香港投身工程行業的學生明顯地下降，現存僅有少數有系統、詳盡或具代表性的研究可以解釋中學生選擇工程師作為職業的原因。跟工業化國家如中國作比較，這下滑的傾向在后工業國家(如英國)也備受關注。基於這些國家對工程師的需求，探討中學生何時決定投身工程行業及其原因是十分重要。 這項研究把香港定位為介乎於工業化國家與後工業化國家之間，且擁有悠久歷史的創新工程。香港高中學校和職業培訓機構均提供了很多與科技或工程學有關的課程給學生報讀，而工程或製造業相關的組織亦贊助不少課外活動予學生參與。此研究旨在了解為何學生在很多機會接觸工程學的情況下，仍不選擇投身工程界的原因；以及有何因素吸引香港(及其他地方)的學生報讀工程系。根據研究所得之數據而作出的結論將會集中關於三方面：理論(職業路向的選擇)、實踐(鼓勵學生投身工程界的教學方式)和政策(工業化國家與後工業化國家所採取截然不同的策略)。 此研究建基於以下三點：1.) 現存文獻顯示至今還沒有與工程教育有關的具系統性或詳盡研究，2.) 學生可自由選擇課程或未來職業，但他們往往受到組織、教學方式、個人或家庭因素的局限；以及3.) 一項試驗調查，了解香港及中國的中學生能接觸工程教育的機會。調查結果發現：香港大部份學生對工程學感興趣，當中尤以年輕學生為主；傳統教學模式並不能引起學生興趣；對比本地學童，新移民或少數族裔學童更有意於工程行業；透過單性別教育，女學童提高了對工程學的興趣。結果亦發現對比起香港學生，中國學生雖然有較少機會接觸工程系，但他們普遍更積極參與有關工程教育的相關活動；而他們對工程師及其貢獻有較正面態度。由於試驗調查只屬小規模，作出小數抽樣調查，只能提供有限見解說明組織、教學方式和個人際遇對影響學生選擇工程師作為職業的關係。因此，我們計劃進行一項綜合研究，共分為三部份：針對香港中學生對於工程教育的具代表性問卷調查；對學生的職業路向作出具代表性和詳細的訪問研究；和就中國工業化與英國後工業化的工程文化作對比調查。

744013.label: Major findings and research outcome
744013.value: The project acknowledged the importance of engineering for society, while fewer students were starting the study of engineering. Findings (see Part C) advanced: theory (in conceptualizing results and geo-engineering comparisons): methodology (design/validation of a large-scale, international survey instrument and the use of HLM and SEM statistical models) and hold practical impacts (particularly for Hong Kong and the UK). Phase 1: Piloting and initial international comparisons: Unique to this project were the development of a questionnaire, the focus on engineering education at the secondary school level, development of a representative sample of schools/students in HK and comparison between post-industrial and industrializing regions (in HK, China and the UK). The questionnaire combined information on student demography, school-type attended, attitudes, perceptions and motivation towards engineering, curricular/extra-curricular courses attended and developed an engineering efficacy scale. After validation in pilot regions, initial analyses identified low uptake in engineering-oriented courses in HK and the UK, and significantly higher engineering aspirations among China Mainland students. Analyses identified a relationship between geo-engineering region and engineering aspirations that separated specific experiential/attitudinal differences between post-industrial/industrializing regions. Phase 2: Intensive exploration of the background to engineering aspirations among HK Students: Full HK sample analyses were undertaken at descriptive and analytic levels. Key finding included: a) HK students displayed similar demographic, attitudinal and perceptual qualities as had been found in Western-based/post-industrial studies – with boys having more positive engineering aspirations than girls and leading to a suggestion of components that may engender Engineering Capital among students; b) Students received very limited curricular/extra-curricular engineering experience, even though they were offered high levels of STM (science, mathematics, technology) education; c) Hierarchical linear modelling identified that schools/experience offered by schools was not significantly related to engineering aspirations; and d) Structural equation modelling clearly identified that the major proportions of explainable aspiration variance was associated with students’ engineering efficacy – a topic area that did not characterize secondary schooling. Phase 3: Evaluating engineering interventions programmes within schools in the UK: The project questionnaire and Prof Kutnick undertook a control/intervention evaluation of programmes designed to enhance engineering aspirations among secondary school students in two UK regions over time. Main findings included: a) The intervention programmes were responsible for positive increases in attitudes and perceptions of engineers among students; b) the longer that schools were involved in the intervention, the more positive the increases in attitudes and perceptions of students; but c) while attitudes and perceptions increased, engineering efficacy remained the same – and this was tied to a limited increase in aspiration. Phase 4: Comparisons of geo-engineering regions in China and Hong Kong: Samples were drawn from 3 geo-engineering regions in China (Beijing, ShanXi, Guangzhou) and compared with Hong Kong. Results identified: a) Significantly more positive attitudes, experience, motivation, perceptions and efficacy across China than Hong Kong; b) Within China regional differences emphasizes positive effects of schooling and efficacy in Guangzhou, positive attitudes in Beijing and comparative inexperience of engineering in ShanXi. Key advances in this project: 1) Development of questionnaire that integrates a range of theoretical perspectives and representative HK sample for this age group; 2) Verification of engineering efficacy (from Bandura) in engineering aspiration; 3) Identification of the theory of planned behaviour (Ajzen) versus identity and social cognitive theories of career aspiration; 4) Introduction of Engineering Capital in explanation of high/low engineering aspiration; 5) Identification of geo-engineering regional variations add complexity to post-industrial/industrializing arguments.

744013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
744013.value: a) Evaluation of ‘Connecting STEM Teachers’ in the UK: The Royal Academy of Engineering (UK) has hired Prof Kutnick to lead an evaluation on its ongoing programme to train and support secondary school teachers to enhance the role of STEM subjects in their schools. b) Development of school-based engineering programmes likely to enhance students’ engineering aspirations: We are currently completing discussion with the Royal Academy of Engineering to develop a programme for schools that will encourage engineering efficacy among teachers and students. c) Towards the end of the current project, the Education Bureau (Hong Kong) recognized the vital role of STEM subjects for the development of economic life within the region. Our representative study currently challenges the approach recommended by the Hong Kong Curriculum Development Council in its reliance on traditional subjects of science, mathematics and technology to encourage STEM. Our results identify two areas that can add to current practice: 1) that actual courses in engineering be introduced into secondary schools at the youngest age groups (current engineering courses are only offered to the oldest age groups); and 2) any engineering topics/courses develop/draw upon aspects of engineering efficacy rather than traditional teach-led pedagogies

744013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
744013.value: There is an increasing demand in post-industrial societies (as HK) for engineers to enhance economic opportunities, but few secondary school students are selecting engineering as a career. As no current/previous HK research concerning students’engineering aspirations existed at the start of the project, we asked whether these aspirations existed, whether they were affected by secondary school experiences and whether HK outcomes were similar to Western/post-industrial societies or the industrializing Mainland. We found that current HK schooling experience offered little (to students) to enhance their engineering aspirations and stereotypical, often male dominated, orientations to engineering characterized our outcomes. Analyses also showed that a pedagogic approach that focused on competence and confidence in engineering activities (efficacy) was most likely to enhance aspirations – and we are developing this approach for schools (and note that this is a current priority in HK schools). Our international and comparative findings extend knowledge about current school-based engineering education: While showing that HK is strongly post-industrial in orientation, Mainland regions are more likely to encourage engineering aspirations - although there is much variation in Engineering Capital between its geo-engineering regions. And UK/HK findings show the importance of incorporating engineering efficacy into the school curriculum (for teachers and students).

744113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
744113.value: The research will use both existing and new methodologies to assess the quality of urban life (QOUL) in Hong Kong, about which there is a paucity of detailed analysis and systematic understanding. QOUL is seen as a significant issue impacting the liveability, performance and competitiveness of major metropolitan regions. Such measures are increasingly being used in the global economy to guide governments and multinational companies place employees on international assignments. Coming to consensus on the specific dimensions of QOUL is difficult because of dissimilar local concerns and cultural influences. QOUL has been examined using different approaches: human development, world city, economic growth, city planning, life satisfaction, health status, and sustainability. Additionally, QOUL issues are viewed differently between local residents and foreign workers or immigrants. Before the creation of a uniform index that is sensitive to inequality between approaches and places, it is important to acquire an understanding of inequality within cities. This research aims at examining the city planning approaches to quality of life, well being, and liveability focussing specifically on the quality of the urban environment and neighbourhood design. While the qualities sought by urban planners may be universally relevant, recent development directions of many Asian cities have been significantly different in terms of the dynamics of urban sprawl and the accelerating rate of high-rise and high density urban living. The patches of built-up areas interspersed with rural areas in Hong Kong should provide some reflections on the possibility of a QOUL index tailored specifically to Asian cities. QOUL indicators may be either objective or subjective. Objective indicators are quantitative in nature and verifiable. Subjective indicators concern people’s perceptions. Many subjective assessment tools rely on observational and questionnaire surveys; the former by trained observers and latter through survey respondents or focus groups. Ultimately, the research hopes to derive objective and broader measures that can be used for international comparison. This study proposes a three-staged research process: (1) apply the geographic information systems (GIS) technique to abstract objective measures of the physical layout and structure of neighbourhoods; (2) employ a social survey to collect subjective perception of neighbourhoods; and (3) establish agreements and disagreements of a range of objective variables and subjective well-being to arrive at a small number of well-chosen QOUL indicators for Asian cities that are more focussed and easily understood. 探索香港城市生活質量的測量——亞洲視角 城市生活質量﹝Quality of Urban Life = QOUL﹞對大都市圈的宜居性，性能以及其競爭力的影響佔有重要地位。城市生活質量的測量已於全球經濟中，逐漸用來引導政府以及跨國公司進行外派人員的管理。香港的QOUL研究目前還缺乏具體的分析和有系統的理解，此研究將會使用現存的以及探索新的檢驗方法來評價香港的城市生活質量。 由於關注點和文化影響的差異，使得各界人士對QOUL的具體範圍達成共識變得非常困難。過去我們引用了不同的關注點，包括透過人類發展、世界城市、經濟增長、城市規劃、生活滿意度、健康狀態以及可持續性來檢驗QOUL。另外要考慮的因素是當地居民和外國僱員或者移民者對於QOUL的敏感度也不是一致的。想要建立一個統一並且可以有效平衡地區之間不對等性的QOUL指數，最重要的還是要對不同城市之間的不對等性有深刻了解。 此研究的目標是利用城市規劃的方法來檢驗生活質量，幸福度以及宜居性，特別著重於城市環境的質量和社區設計。隨著城市規劃者對質量的追求，不難察覺到許多現代亞洲城市，已經與以前追求城市擴張和高層高密度的城市生活有了顯著不同的發展方向。香港具有繁華建築區卻不乏農村地區的城市特徵，可以比較全面的針對亞洲城市的QOUL指數做出檢驗改進。 QOUL指標包括客觀指標和主觀指標。客觀指標是可以被量化以及證實的。而主觀指標則側重於人們的感知。許多主觀評估工具是透過訓練有素的觀察員的觀察以及對受訪者和焦點人群做問卷調查。本研究希望通過客觀的立場導出可被廣泛採用的指標，用於分析比較國際間的競爭優勢。 本研究提出了三個研究階段：（1）運用地理信息系統（GIS）用客觀的方法提取社區的設計佈局和結構；（2） 採用社會調查的方法收集社區內居民的主觀感受；（3） 通過考量客觀變量和主觀變量之間的一致性和不協調性，仔細篩選出一小部份具有聚焦點并容易被人們理解的指標，可以一致性而又系統化的用于評價亞洲城市的生活質量。 關鍵詞： 1）城市生活質量 2）GIS建模 3）城市化 4）幸福指數 5）亞洲

744113.label: Realisation of objectives
744113.value: Objective 1: Our study establishes that quality of urban life (QOUL) for Hong Kong is viewed differently from those of Brisbane (Australia) and of the greater Detroit (USA) region. Hong Kong still lags behind the two regions in most aspects of the QOL life domains and the QOUL living domains. The comparisons have implied that the differences between these urban regions are beyond east-west influence in the perception of QOL and more attributable to disparities in urban environments. In this regards, we have tailor made an objective measure of the QOUL in Hong Kong by assessing the land use/environmental characteristics to explain the varying living characteristics in urban areas of Hong Kong. Objective 2: This study employed a GIS (geographic information system) approach that made use of digital spatial data and satellite/aerial images from official sources to extract the physical layouts and structures of 89 neighbourhoods in Hong Kong. Various land use characteristics (such as street pattern, road density, plot area, built and non-built coverage, etc.) were included in the analysis. The GIS-based method was effective in deriving the so-called environmental QOL sub-index. The method can be easily applied in other urbanised settings to offer a direct and objective way to compare environmental QOUL which is multifactorial in nature. Objective 3: A social survey was conducted between July and August 2015 to collect subjective perception of QOUL in neighbourhoods in Hong Kong. The study population included 1163 subjects recruited by stratified random sampling conducted by The University of Hong Kong Public Opinion Programme to ensure a representative sample. The QOUL survey instrument assembled three categories of data based on subjective assessments: Part A – life and living domains; Part B – social capital measures; and Part C – personal and family aspects. In general, the majority of respondents (43.5%) perceived their QOL to be satisfied and very satisfied whereas 15.5% of respondents reported dissatisfied and very dissatisfied ratings. 41% of respondents were neutral in their assessment of QOL. Objective 4: Both objective and subjective variables must be considered in assessing QOL. Our study selected PM2.5 air quality to explore the differences between objective and subjective measurements. Preliminary results showed that geographic variation of air pollutant concentration does affect people’s perception and tolerance level of air quality. Given effects of acclimatisation, the relationship between objective and subjective measures of air quality is ambivalent. The results also suggested that variation in perception is place specific and largely influenced by the interplay between environmental surroundings and socioeconomic standing of individuals. We shall continue to explore other variables being collected (such as road density versus convenience; land use mix versus convenience; greenery versus QOL ratings, etc.) to establish more concrete findings stratified by socioeconomic characteristics.

744113.label: Major findings and research outcome
744113.value: 1) Apart from health status, residents of Hong Kong perceived QOL to be highly associated with housing and economic characteristics as reflected through their standards of living or personal wealth status. 2) Hong Kong is still lagging behind the western counterparts in most aspects of the QOL life domains and the QOUL living domains, as detailed in our paper to be published in Social Indicators Research. 3) An objective environmental sub-index has been devised to compare varying QOUL in Hong Kong. Our GIS-based method offers a simple, direct and objective way of examining environmental QOL and the method can be replicated in other cities and defined neighbourhoods. 4) This research has prompted the organisation of an international conference about the geographies of health and living in cities. The conference was attended by over 180 participants from 17 countries and has helped to foster international research collaboration. 5) This research has produced a number of publications: (a) a peer reviewed paper, (b) a doctoral dissertation, and (c) a few conference papers (Procedia Environmental Sciences). Two scholarly manuscripts are being written for submission to academic journals.

744113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
744113.value: This research has explored influences of environmental and socioeconomic factors on the perception of QOUL based on 89 neighbourhoods of Hong Kong. As QOUL is multifactorial in nature, the GIS-based approach demonstrated in this study suggests the need for more in-depth analysis be carried out to focus on specific domains of QOUL at different levels – housing, neighbourhood, or community – in predicting the overall life satisfaction of residents in a compact and rapidly growing Chinese metropolis. It is also important to study how these urban attributes vary between different socio-demographic groups. Furthermore, the GIS-based methodology can be replicated in other urbanised settings with varying spatial scales to offer a direct and objective means of comparing environmental QOUL. This research has assembled and constructed an extendible spatial database that unifies multi-source data for 89 neighbourhoods in Hong Kong that can offer baseline measures to enable longitudinal studies about QOUL. There is also potential research collaboration to apply the methodology in Northern China to examine QOUL of migrant populations moving to new developments and extant populations living in nearby urban areas.

744113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
744113.value: This research, with a central focus on place, investigated the influence of socioeconomic, demographic, and environmental factors on the quality of urban life (QOUL) using urban areas in Hong Kong as a case study. The research offers a systematic framework to derive both objective indicators and subjective assessments of QOUL domains for Hong Kong. The methodology provides a standardised approach and comparable QOUL measures suitable for Asian cities that are undergoing rapid urbanisation and social transformation. The research also suggests the need to employ both objective/quantitative and subjective/qualitative measures in QOUL assessments at varying spatial scales. Although the multifactorial nature of QOUL can be summarised into a combined index for easy comparison, the summary statistic must be interpreted with care and in conjunction with various contributing component factors and spatial knowledge of the place. While urban development is still primarily assessed using economic and financial indicators, this research advocates the use of QOUL indicators to capture the well-being aspect of development that relates to environmental and socio-demographic settings. In particular, the research proposes the use of geographic information technologies to devise objective QOUL measures for wider application in the future, especially for developing countries/cities where many well-being statistics may not exist or are not well-established.

744213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
744213.value: 該研究項目旨在發現外語學習者的文化價值觀是如何影響學生在課外自主使用技術輔助外語學習。 提高學生在課外自主使用技術來輔助語言學習對於充分實現技術的教育優勢極為重要。而理解影響學生是否使用技術的因素則是首要任務。現有文獻提出了多種可能影響學生技術使用的個體和社會因素。然而，文化價值觀與學生對技術的看法和使用緊密相關，而這一因素卻未能充分探討。該項目旨在填補這一研究空白，揭示文化價值觀對外語學生自主使用技術輔助語言學習的影響。我們認為文化價值觀影響著外語學生對技術輔助語言學習的看法以及如何選擇和使用技術來輔助語言學習，並且文化價值觀與其它的個體和社會因素共同作用影響學生是否在課外自主使用技術輔助語言學習。 該研究將採用問卷調查和訪談相結合的研究方法。通過問卷調查，建構文化價值與其它個體、社會因素相互作用共同影響自主使用技術輔助學習的路徑模型。其後的訪談將深入探索文化價值觀如何影響學生選擇和使用不同技術來輔助語言學習。 輔助學生在課外積極使用技術進行語言學習對提高語言教學極為重要。在全球化的影響下，學生多樣性越來越明顯，他們帶著不同的文化價值觀，因而在輔助學生學習時，必須考慮到這些文化價值觀的影響。通過探討文化價值觀對技術使用的影響，該研究項目能給我們提供有用信息，建構更為有效的、多樣的輔助學生使用技術輔助語言學習的途徑。 關鍵詞： 技術：學生在日常生活中經常使用的各種電子技術包括維基合作平臺、社交網站、博客、網絡視頻和音頻、多媒體軟件及各種移動電子設備如手機、MP3播放器等。 社會價值觀：學生個體的文化價值觀。例如，文化價值觀的一個層面是個體和集體觀，指的是學生認為個人的意願和成就與集體歸屬哪個更重要。

744213.label: Realisation of objectives
744213.value: The project objectives have been achieved. A conceptual model of the direct and moderating effects of individual espoused cultural values on learners' self-directed use of technology for language learning beyond the classroom was constructed. A questionnaire that measures learners' frequency of self-directed out-of-class technology use, learners' individual espoused cultural values and other influencing factors was constructed and pilot tested. 713 survey responses on the final questionnaire have been collected from university foreign language learners in three regions -- mainland China, Hong Kong and USA. 28 follow-up interview responses on how individual espoused cultural values have influenced their self-directed selection and use of technology for language learning beyond the classroom have also been collected. Statistical modeling has been conducted to unravel the direct and moderating effects of learners' espoused cultural values on their self-directed use of technology for language learning outside the classroom.

744213.label: Major findings and research outcome
744213.value: The project found that the influence of individual espoused cultural values on learners' self-directed technology use for learning beyond the classroom manifested more in direct effects than in moderation effects. It further found that long-term orientation and uncertainty avoidance were two individual-level cultural value orientations that played important roles in the voluntary adoption of technology for self-directed learning beyond the classroom. Long-term orientation, collectivist orientation and power distance were found to positively influence technology use, whereas uncertainty avoidance was found to negatively influence technology use. In addition, long-term orientation was found to positively influence learners' performance expectancy, and uncertainty avoidance was found to positively moderate the impact of social influence on intention to use technology. Two research papers have been generated out of this research project: 1. Lai, C., Wang, Q., Li, X., & Hu, X. (2016). The influence of individual espoused cultural values on self-directed use of technology for language learning beyond the classroom. Computers in Human Behavior, 62, 676-688. 2. Lai, C., Li, X. & Wang, Q. (Revise and Resubmit). Students' perceptions of teacher impact on their self-directed language learning with technology beyond the classroom: Cases of Hong Kong and U.S. Submitted to Educational Technology Research and Development.

744213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
744213.value: The research examined the factors that influence the frequency of learners' self-directed use of technology for language learning. What needs further exploration is the nature of learners' self-directed technology use for learning and, more importantly, the quality of learners' self-directed technology use. Further development of the research may want to focus on these two aspects, understanding the nature of learners' self-directed technology use and the factors that influence different types of self-directed technology. Further development may also focus on the quality of learners' out-of-class language learning in general. My future work will focus on these two aspects to gain in-depth understanding into language learners' out-of-class language learning.

744213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
744213.value: The research project examined the influence of learners' cultural value orientations influence their self-directed use of technology for language learning beyond the classroom. The research data consists of survey and interview responses of university foreign language learners from three regions: mainland China, Hong Kong and USA. The research identified the direct and moderating influence of learners' cultural value orientations on the frequency of their out-of-class technology use for language learning. The research project is significant in that it examined how the fundamental values that learners hold shaped the variations in learners' technology-enhanced learning behaviors. The research identified that long-term orientation and uncertainty avoidance were two critical variables that may influence learners' technology use in the informal learning contexts. The findings provide suggestions on critical issues that eductors need to pay attention when trying to promote learners' technology use for learning beyond the classroom: 1) broaden learners' value-judgement beyond immediate cognitive benefits and help them see the value of learning activities that may generate delayed benefits; and 2) strengthen social influence in regions with high uncertainty avoidance on average.

745113.label: Project Title(Chinese)
745113.value: 中國歷史上農耕時期的氣候變化、人口增長及人口週期：空間尺度及區域地理因素的影響

745113.label: Project Objectives
745113.value: To determine the climate-population relationship in historical China at multiple spatial scales and geographic levels ranging from the whole of China down to physiographic regions, provinces, and counties. To explore whether and how far the synergistic effect of population growth and climate change at different geographic levels is mediated by spatial scale and regional geographic context.
rows: To determine the climate-population relationship in historical China at multiple spatial scales and geographic levels ranging from the whole of China down to physiographic regions, provinces, and counties.
To explore whether and how far the synergistic effect of population growth and climate change at different geographic levels is mediated by spatial scale and regional geographic context.

745113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
745113.value: This project seeks to verify whether and to what extent the synergistic effect of population growth and climate change upon historical Chinese population growth dynamics is mediated by spatial scale and regional geographic context, showing whether the synergistic effect is deterministic or contextual in nature. The presence of secular population cycles in historical China has long been known. Five demographic collapses occurred in China during the last millennium, each with population losses ranging from 30–80 million. In the traditional view, scholars presume rapid population growth to be the driving force of those cycles. In a more recent view, scholars suggest climate change to be the root cause. In either case, the demographic impacts of ‘population growth’ and ‘climate change’ have been considered individually, while their synergistic impact in driving population cycles is overlooked. The PI has demonstrated in his studies that the recurrence of population crises in historical China is primarily determined by the synthesis of population growth and climate change. Nevertheless, he has only taken the whole of China as a single analytical unit to obtain his results. Three issues remain unresolved: First, the key explanatory variable of population growth dynamics may change substantially along different geographic levels. It is necessary to check whether the synergistic effect of population growth and climate change can be spatially downscaled to explain the fluctuation of population size in historical China at lower geographic levels (for example, provinces/counties). Second, the societal impact of climate change is often characterized by strong regional variation (i.e., more significant in regions with lower land carrying capacity). However, it has yet to be determined whether the synergistic effect of population growth and climate change varies across different regions (physiographic regions with different land carrying capacity, for instance) in China. Third, the linkages and feedback loops for the climate-population relationship may be non-stationary in nature. More sophisticated methods should be used to test the possible non-stationarity of the relationship. This project plans to investigate the above issues because they are imperative for comprehending the historical Chinese population growth dynamics. In addition, it represents pioneering research which systematically examines the climate-population relationship in historical China at multiple spatial scales and geographic levels. The associated findings may completely challenge the widely accepted classic Malthusian/post-Malthusian interpretations of historical Chinese population cycles and help to explain the demographic risks faced by tropical countries that are in some ways similar to historical agrarian China. 中國歷史人口的增減是由人口增長及氣候變化兩者一同驅動的，這個研究項目主要是驗證有關的機制會否在不同的空間尺度及區域地理環境下有所改變，從而找出人口增長及氣候變化兩者對人口增減影響的絕對程度。中國歷史上的人口週期早已廣為人知，在過去一千年，中國先後發生了五次人口銳減，而每次的人口銳減造成30–80萬人死亡。傳統的觀點認為這些週期是由人口快速增長所驅動的。近年，有學者認為氣候變化才是造成人口週期的根本原因。可是，在這兩種的觀點下，“人口增長”和“氣候變化”只會被單獨考慮，而它們的協同效應往往被忽略。項目負責人在他早前的研究已經證明，中國歷史上重複不斷的人口危機主要是由人口增長和氣候變化兩者一同造成的。儘管如此，他是以全中國作為一個分析單元而得出有關結論，而且有三個問題尚未解答： 首先，在不同的空間尺度下，造成人口增減的因素有可能是不一樣的，所以我們有必要去驗證人口增長和氣候變化兩者是否能解釋較小的地理尺度（例如，省／縣）的歷史人口波動。 其次，氣候變化對社會的影響往往是帶有地域性（在土地承載能力較低的地區，影響會更為明顯）。然而，人口增長和氣候變化兩者在中國不同地區（例如在不同土地承載能力的自然地理區域）對人口的影響，尚未仔細考查。 再者，氣候變化與人口之間的聯係及反饋迴路，可能存在非線性的關係，所以有需要用更複雜的方法去驗證這種有可能存在的非線性關係。 這個研究項目主要是探討上述的問題，而這些問題對了解中國歷史人口增減是非常重要的。另外，這是一個開創性的研究，在多個空間尺度和地理層面上有系統地去考察中國歷史上氣候與人口之間的關係。有關的研究結果有可能會全面挑戰馬爾薩斯／後馬爾薩斯理論對中國歷史人口週期的詮釋，並有助於了解那些在某程度上與歷史農耕時期中國情況類似的熱帶國家所面對的人口風險。

745113.label: Realisation of objectives
745113.value: To kick-started this research project, the PI summarized his previous works to illustrate the connection and also the causal mechanisms between climate change and various human crises in pre-industrial human societies in a macro-historic perspective. Comparison was also made between historical China and pre-industrial Europe such that a more holistic overview about the climate-population relationship in historical China could be offered [Research Output #2]. This laid the foundation for this research project. Then, the PI proceeded to systematically examine the climate-population relationship in historical China at multiple spatial scales and geographic levels. He collected huge amount of Chinese historical data such as paleo-climate data, population data, and socio-economic & human-ecological data (including agricultural production index, cultivated land area, cultivated land area per capita, harvest indexes, nomad migrations, nomad invasions, famine, wars and rebellions, epidemics, flood & drought disasters, natural calamities, loss of life caused by famines, epidemics, and various natural disasters, and so on). With the help of his collaborator in Nanjing University, the PI could get access to some archaeological records such as the geographic distribution of archaeological sites, plant remains, animal remains, and so on. The PI based on the above datasets to verify the climate-population relationship. The main theme of this research project is to downscale and contextualize the climate-population relationship in historical China. The PI did so by employing three different analytical approaches. The first one is multi-scalar comparison, in which data were disaggregated (from time series to panel data) and analyzed statistically at various geographic levels (from country, to physiographic region, province, and county), with the statistical results at different geographic levels compared [Research Output #1 and #11]. The second one is inter-regional comparison, in which the climate-population relationship among different physiographic regions (agro-ecological zones) was compared [Research Output #4 and #11]. The third one is regional study, in which the climate-population relationship in small regions (say, province, county, and river basin) was investigated in-depth [Research Output #5, #6, #8, #9, #10, and #12]. The first approach is designated to explore the influence of spatial scale on the climate-population relationship, while the second and third approaches are designated to explore the influence of regional geographic context on the climate-population relationship. In this research project, the PI also drilled into the synergistic effect of population growth and climate change on epidemics outbreak [Research Output #3 and #11] and mass migration [Research Output #4] in Chinese history. Epidemics outbreak and mass migration are two important phenomena affecting population growth dynamics. Regarding epidemics, it is one of the Malthusian checks in materializing the climate-population relationship. But, the synergistic effect of population growth and climate change on epidemics in Chinese history has not been systematically addressed in academia. Therefore, the PI tried to fill this research gap. Regarding mass migration, it is an important factor in mediating the climate-population relationship, especially at lower geographic levels. Although climate-induced food strain could result in population collapses at the country level, the food strain might trigger mass migration instead of population collapses at lower geographic levels. This is an important dynamics which mediates the climate-population nexus, which should be addressed in this research project. When exploring the synergistic effect of population growth and climate change on epidemics and mass migration, the PI incorporated several contextual factors into his analysis, such as economic well-being, cultural factors, government policies, and regional geography. By doing so, a more nuanced interpretation about the climate-population relationship was offered. Out of those abovementioned contextual factors, the economic well-being is deemed to be the most important factor in mediating the climate-population nexus. Therefore, the PI worked with his colleagues to further drill into the triangulation among the climate change, economic fluctuation, and population growth dynamics in historical China at the country level [Research Output #3 and #7]. PI’s previous studies highlight the disastrous demographic impact brought by climate change in a broad sense, which is a bit environmentally deterministic in a sense. However, the PI also realized that the picture could be very diversified at lower geographic levels. In some regions, climate change is the driving force of population growth; in other regions, the climate plays an essential and yet, supporting role. In unison, there are also regions where the effect of climate change is secondary. This is one of the hypotheses to be tested in this research project. Therefore, the PI conducted several in-depth regional studies to scale down the examination of the climate-population relationship. In this regard, northwestern China and northeastern China were focused. This is because they are both environmentally-fragile regions. It will be interesting to see whether the climate-population relationship there is more apparent or not. Besides, owing to scarce historical records in those regions, northwestern China and northeastern China are not fully researched in PI’s previous studies as well as existing literature. With the help of his collaborator in Nanjing University, the PI employed archaeological records (e.g., archaeological sites, plant remains, animal remains, etc.), which are supplemented with historical records, to examine the climate-population relationship in northwestern China (Sha’anxi, Gansu, Ningxia, Qinghai, and Hualong County) and northeastern China (West Liao River Basin and Xar Moron River Basin). The PI found that, to certain extent, environmental factors played a very important role in shaping human population growth dynamics. For instance, the northern limit for the dispersal of human settlements in northeastern China in pre-historic period was primarily determined by temperature [Research Output #9]. Besides, the ethnic diversity in Northern Tibetan Plateau was driven by habitat variability [Research Output #12]. On the other hand, the PI also found that human societies adapted to climate deterioration by using various means, say, through the implementation of environmentally suitable subsistence strategies, relocation of human settlements, government policies, or even introduction of foreign crops [Research Output #5, #6, #8, and #10]. Briefly, the climate-population relationship deems to be very diversified at lower geographic levels, even in environmentally-fragile regions. It is almost impossible to simply attribute the fluctuation of population growth dynamics to climate change. With the implementation of abovementioned tasks, the project objectives have been fully achieved (cf. Section 6.1 Major findings and research outcome).
