745113.label: Major findings and research outcome
745113.value: In this research project, the PI proved that: First, the strength of climate-population nexus changed across spatial scales. Although population checks were negatively correlated with the temperature in historical China at various geographic levels, a stark reduction in the correlational strength was observed at lower geographic levels (Project Objective #1). Second, the climate-population nexus was significantly mediated by regional context. Some regional factors amplified the vulnerability of population checks/social crises to climate change (e.g., increasing population pressure, unsustainable farming practices, etc.), while some regional factors helped human societies buffer against the impact brought by a deteriorating climate (e.g., change of subsistence strategies, relocation of settlements, government policies, introduction of foreign crops, etc.) (Project Objective #2). Briefly, the synergistic effect of population growth and climate change upon historical Chinese population growth dynamics was not entirely deterministic in nature, even in environmentally-fragile regions. The climate-population nexus was mediated by spatial scale and regional geographic context. This project substantiated the above notion with empirical evidence. Instead of seeking environmentally-deterministic conclusion about the climate-population relationship in historical China, the concept of spatial scale and regional context should be given thorough consideration. The theoretical implication of the above findings is that they demonstrate the importance and necessity of downscaling and contextualizing the climate-population relationship in academic research. Researchers need to consider the scale effect in the course of statistical analyses, which are currently predominantly conducted on a national/single scale; and also the importance of how the study area is delineated, an issue which is rarely discussed in the climate-population literature. Future research may leverage the results of this project and provide a cross-analysis with those derived from spatial analysis. The findings of this research project have been published in a peer-reviewed book chapter [Research Output #1]and 11 research papers [Research Output #2–12] in internationally peer-reviewed journals (including Climate Research [Impact Factor in 2015: 1.690], Environmental Research Letters [Impact Factor in 2015: 4.134], Frontiers of Earth Science [Impact Factor in 2015: 0.760], Quaternary International [Impact Factor in 2015: 2.067], Scientific Reports [Impact Factor in 2015: 5.228], Social Science & Medicine [Impact Factor in 2015: 2.814], The Holocene [Impact Factor in 2015: 2.135], and Journal of Archaeological Science: Reports) [Scopus Indexed]. The PI would like to take this opportunity to thank the financial support provided by RGC. Or else, it is impossible to have such a fruitful outcome. Thanks a lot!

745113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
745113.value: In the past, the PI relied on historical documents as primary data source to examine the climate-population relationship in historical China. However, in this project, he realized the huge potential of archaeological records in revealing population growth dynamics in ancient China. The value of archaeological records is that they help extend study time span from historical period to pre-historical period, and help extend study area to those regions where historical records are scarce (such as northeastern China and northwestern China, which are also environmentally-fragile regions). Through the integration of archaeological records and historical records, it can give a more holistic picture about how historical population growth dynamics across the whole of China is driven by climate change. Recently, the PI and his collaborator are using the archaeological records for stone bridges together with historical documents to trace the spatial distribution of population in relationship to climate change in the lower Yangtze River Basin in late imperial China. The results are quite encouraging, while a manuscript is being prepared. Given the fruitful outcome of this project, the PI will try his best to pool up the expertise of historians and archaeologists in drilling into the historical climate-population relationship in the future.

745613.label: Project Title(Chinese)
745613.value: 近代中國營養知識的建構 (1850-1950)

745613.label: Project Objectives
745613.value: To trace the development of biochemical nutritional science in modern China and the coining of the word “nutrition” (yingyang營養) to express a new scientific idea. To capture the critical transition from traditional dietetic regime to modern nutritional precepts on food, body, health, and diseases; from “life-nurturing” (yangsheng 養生) practices to a scientific and hygienic regime (weisheng衛生). To relate this development to China’s state building and social engineering by studying the role of institutions involved (national and regional governments, schools, universities and research institutes, military research units, and international health organizations), and the role of key actors (scientists, educators, bureaucrats, doctors). To analyze how scientism became an integral part of the Chinese state in the 20th century. To investigate the negotiation between the new nutritional science and traditional dietetics in popular literature on food, health, and disease, with special attention on such literature in south China for the purpose of understanding regional differences. To analyze the changing production and consumption of certain foods (e.g. rice, wheat, tea, porridge, sugar, soya etc.) and long-standing indigenous nutritional habits, such as vegetarianism that best articulate changing nutritional precepts for the improvement of personal and national health. To do a preliminary survey on the impact of new nutritional knowledge developed in this period on food policies in the greater China region of the immediate post-war period.

745613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
745613.value: Nutritional science demonstrates how “Western” science merged with the process of modern Chinese state building. Evolving from biochemical research conducted in Europe and colonial Asia from the late 19th to the early 20th centuries, this cutting-edge research field developed new ideas such as “malnutrition” which were applied to the ignorant poor and indigenous populations in European colonies. In China, the new science coined the term “nutrition”(yingyang 營養) as a scientific concept at the turn of the century. This new science had great appeal to both political and intellectual elites and became firmly institutionalized in Republican China in the 1920s and 1930s with “Western” trained experts taking up bureaucratic and academic positions in government and major universities, hospitals, and research institutes including those in the military. The grand project of improving the Chinese race was now articulated on policies to improve national health by reforming popular dietary habits. The project examines three related historical processes of the construction of nutritional knowledge and its implementation in modern China: first, the development and characteristics (as compared to the research focus in Europe) of biochemical nutritional science in China; second, the roles of relevant institutions and of key intellectuals and bureaucrats involved in the research and application of the science; third, reception of the new science by society at large as revealed in modern “life-nurturing” (yangsheng 養生) and “dietetic medical”( shiliao 食療 ) texts based on old Chinese dietetic traditions, popular literature on nutrition (yingyang), and the work of popular writers who promoted hybrid dietetic practices based on traditional and new ideas. Special attention will be paid to regional differences, with emphasis on South China, including Hong Kong. The project will also examine the changing production and consumption of a few key foods controversial in nutritional debates, such as white rice, sugar, tea, milk etc., and the public discussions on indigenous habits such as vegetarianism that would best articulate changing nutritional precepts in terms of bodily practice and national health promotion. The study of the multi-layered process of nutritional knowledge construction and its implementation in this period, within and outside of public networks, and by different historical actors, will capture with precision the complexity of China’s quest for modernity in new light. It will also provide a useful and productive perspective for assessing the broad social engineering project of the modern Chinese state captivated by the idea of “science”.

745613.label: Realisation of objectives
745613.value: I have realized most the objectives in four book chapters (2015, 2017, 2019, under review) and one journal article (2019), and two edited book volumes (2017, 2019). I have in particular studied the modern phenomenon of jioaqi 腳氣, an old Chinese ailment that was used to translate what Western biomedical doctors of the late 19th century “discovered” as a “new” East Asian disease, beriberi, considered to be caused by malnutrition. The East Asian traditional explanation of Jiaoqi as an ailment of bad “life nurturing” (yangsheng養生) lifestyle with excessive food and drink accompanied by the lack of physical activity, was progressively replaced by the modern biomedical discourse on Asian malnutrition based on rice eating in the region. The history of this “translation” or mis-translation fully illustrates the transition from traditional dietetic regime from yangsheng to a hygienic modernity focused on the notion of nutritional weisheng. I discussed the modern history of the jiaoqi ailment in two book chapters published in 2015 and 2017, and in a book chapter under review on the most important 19th-century Chinese monograph on jiaoqi as a new medical genre in the period. These three articles fully address objectives 1, 2, 4. I have also dealt with the question of nutrition in relation to the emergence of new institutions (hospitals, government bureaus, associations etc.) in one forthcoming journal article, in which I pay special attention to the development in southern China, and one forthcoming book chapter (probably 2019) on the controversy on vegetarianism in modern China. The latter article will be published in a book volume that I co-edit in which contributors discuss nutritional and technological issues of other modern Asian foods (tea, soy milk, sugar etc.) These two articles and the book volume address fully objectives 3, 4 and 5. The only objective that I have not fully dealt with is no. 6 as time has not allowed me to treat the post-war period fully. However, I have obtained another GRF grant in 2018 on modern entrepreneurship in the making of soy sauce. I will thus continue to look at post-war technologies and institutions on food manufacture, and the changing discourse of nutrition.

745613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
745613.value: This project has been one of the first to study the emergence of modern Asian nutritional regimes. I have covered mostly the transitional period from the 19th to the early 20th centuries when Western biomedical nutritional science research emerged in Asian colonies. I opened up the field by focusing on the encounter of traditional Asian “life-nourishing” practices and this emerging new nutritional knowledge. The history of the development of nutritional knowledge and practice in China and East Asia in the post-war period, however, has yet to be explored in depth. The project also opens up the field of food study not only related to nutritional issues, but also to changing technologies that affect the quality and identity of Asian foods. This is an interest that came out from this project that I am undertaking with a new GRF grant obtained in 2018. This new research on the modern history of soy sauce making, from traditional handicraft to early industrialization reveals a different set of food-related socio-cultural and health issues. As the concern of food safety and food authenticity is a growing concern in today’s world, this field of study has great potential for further development.

745613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
745613.value: The project examines three related historical processes of the construction of nutritional knowledge in modern China: first, the development of biochemical nutritional science in China; second, the roles of relevant institutions and of key intellectuals and bureaucrats involved in the research and application of the science; third, reception of the new science by society, popular literature on nutrition (yingyang 營養), and hybrid dietetic practices based on traditional and new ideas. I have looked more closely at such changes in Southern China, including Hong Kong, where the traditional jiaoqi (腳氣) ailment was now used to frame a new disease beriberi, considered by biomedical doctors as one of mal-nutrition, caused by white rice eating. From here I further examine changing discourses on dietetic practices such as vegetarianism versus the necessity of animal protein as different approaches to modern nation building for a new China. The study provides a useful perspective for assessing the broad social engineering project of a modern China captivated by the idea of “science”.

746013.label: Project Title(Chinese)
746013.value: 在自身运动中对物体运动的感知

746013.label: Project Objectives
746013.value: Test the accuracy and measure the angular function and speed tuning of flow parsing. Test whether flow parsing is a purely motion-based process. Test how extra-retinal signals about eye movements interact with optic flow for the recovery of scene-relative object motion.
rows: Test the accuracy and measure the angular function and speed tuning of flow parsing.
Test whether flow parsing is a purely motion-based process.
Test how extra-retinal signals about eye movements interact with optic flow for the recovery of scene-relative object motion.

746013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
746013.value: How do we perceive object motion during self-motion? It has been proposed that we can use retinal or extra-retinal motion cues to estimate self-motion and then remove the retinal motion component due to self-motion to recover scene-relative object motion. Much research has shown that observers can indeed use retinal motion cues such as optic flow to parse self-motion out of retinal motion for object motion perception, but it is still unclear how accurate this “flow parsing” process is and whether it operates on motion information only. Furthermore, it still remains in question how extra-retinal motion cues (such as vestibular, proprioceptive information, and efference copy of motor commands) are used for object motion perception during self-motion. We plan to address these questions in this proposed research. First, using a novel method that we have developed to quantitatively measure the flow parsing gain, we will measure the angular function and speed tuning of flow parsing and examine whether flow parsing is a purely motion-based mechanism. Second, we will examine how extra-retinal signals about pursuit eye movements interact with optic flow for the recovery of scene-relative object motion. Third, we will examine the contribution of extra-retinal cues about self-motion to object motion perception during walking. We will computationally model the performance data to develop a comprehensive understanding of how the brain combines multimodal sensory cues for the perception of object motion during self-motion. The findings from the current project can inform the architecture of a model of the underlying neural mechanism responsible for this perceptual process. The findings will be applicable to the design of biomimetic robots, unmanned vehicles, and advanced motion sensors. 我们在自身运动中是如何感知物体的运动呢？有理论提出我们可以用视觉信息先判断自身运动，然后再将物体在视网膜上的由自身运动引起的运动成分去除来判断物体在世界中的运动。许多研究发现我们确实可以用视觉信息例如光流来去除在视网膜上的由自身运动引起的物体运动成分，但是这个过程的准确性和这个过程是否用到运动信息尚未定论。另外，我们如何运用非视觉信息(如前庭和本体知觉信息, 以及肢体运动命令的发出复制信号等)在自身运动中感知物体运动仍是一个未解答的问题。在本研究课题中，我们将对上述问题逐一作出答复。首先，我们将研发一个新的方法准确测量用光流在多大程度上可以去除在视网膜上的由自身运动引起的物体运动成分。我们将用此方法检验角度和速度是如何影响去除量的大小并且去除过程是否只是用到运动信息。然后，我们会检验定义眼动的非视觉信息如何与光流信息相互作用来影响在自身运动中对物体运动的感知。我们将会对实验结果进行数学建模来全面了解在自身运动中人脑如何运用不同感知信息来判断物体运动。本课题的研究成果将帮助了解我们在自身运动中是如何感知物体运动的神经机制，并可以运用在生物机器人，无人驾驶车辆， 和高级运动感知器的设计上。

746013.label: Realisation of objectives
746013.value: Regarding Objective 1 – Test the accuracy and measure the angular function and speed tuning of flow parsing, we developed a retinal motion nulling method to directly measure and quantify the magnitude of flow parsing (i.e., flow parsing gain) in various scenarios to examine the accuracy and tuning of flow parsing for the visual perception of object motion during self-motion. We found that flow parsing gains were below unity for all displays in all experiments; and that increasing self-motion and object motion speed did not alter flow parsing gain. We conclude that visual information alone is not sufficient for the accurate perception of scene-relative motion during self-motion. Although flow parsing performs global subtraction, its accuracy also depends on local motion information in the retinal vicinity of the moving object. Furthermore, the flow parsing gain was constant across common self-motion or object motion speeds (Niehorster & Li, 2017). Regarding Objective 2 – test whether flow parsing is a purely motion-based process, we conducted two experiments. In Experiment 1, we used a minimal display to examine the contribution of optic flow and form cues. Human participants indicated the direction of movement of a probe object presented against a background of radially moving pairs of dots. By independently controlling the orientation of each dot pair, we were able to put flow cues to self-movement direction (the point from which all the motion radiated) and form cues to self-movement direction (the point all the dot pairs were oriented toward) in conflict. We found that only flow cues influenced perceived probe movement. In Experiment 2, we switched to a rich stereo display composed of 3D objects to examine the contribution of flow and position cues. We moved the scene objects to simulate a lateral translation and counter-rotation of gaze. By changing the polarity of the scene objects (from light to dark and vice versa) between frames, we placed flow cues to self-movement direction in opposition to change of position cues. We found that again flow cues dominated the perceived probe movement relative to the scene. Together, these two experiments indicate the neural network that processes optic flow (i.e., motion information) has a primary role in the identification of scene-relative object movement (Rushton et al., in press). We further examined the relationship between the perception of heading, and the identification of object movement during self-movement. We designed stimuli that allowed direct comparison of the precision of heading and object movement judgments. Across a series of experiments, we found the precision was typically higher when judging scene-relative object movement than when judging heading. We also found that manipulations of the content of the visual scene can change the relative precision of the two judgments. These results demonstrate that the ability to judge scene-relative object movement during self-movement is not limited by, or yoked to, the ability to judge the direction of self-movement (Rushton, Chen, & Li, under review). Furthermore, regarding heading perception, we have found that target drift is a surprisingly powerful cue for the perception of naturalistic object-relative heading, and that that occlusion of the focus of expansion in the background flow is not a prerequisite for moving objects to induce a heading bias, and that the bias can be due to either object motion or position (Li et al., accepted). Regarding Objective 3 – Test how extra-retinal signals about eye movements interact with optic flow for the recovery of scene-relative object motion, we used a control-theoretic approach to examine whether concurrent manual tracking enhances smooth pursuit of an unpredictable moving target. We have found that concurrent manual tracking enhances smooth pursuit, and that this effect is not specific to predictable target movement but is a fundamental property of eye-hand coordination (Niehorster, Siu, & Li, 2015). Regarding the underlying neural mechanism responsible for eye-hand coordination, we have found the first behavioral evidence showing that common neural sensory signals drive both eye and hand motor systems and limit eye-hand coordination. This is consistent with the neurophysiological findings of common neural substrates that serve both eye and hand tracking. We further examined the effect of action gaming on motion processing and visuomotor control. We have found the first empirical evidence for a causal link between action gaming (for as short as five hours playing) and enhancement in visual motor control. The findings have practical implications for developing training tools to improve performance on daily visual motor control tasks such as driving (Li, Chen, & Chen, 2016). Furthermore, we have found that action video game play increases the coupling between visual motion processing and the sensory-motor system that uses motion information for visuomotor control.

746013.label: Major findings and research outcome
746013.value: 1. Visual information alone is not sufficient for the accurate perception of scene-relative motion during self-motion. Although flow parsing performs global subtraction, its accuracy also depends on local motion information in the retinal vicinity of the moving object. Furthermore, the flow parsing gain was constant across common self-motion or object motion speeds (Niehorster & Li, 2017). 2. Neural network that processes optic flow (i.e., motion information) has a primary role in the identification of scene-relative object movement (Rushton et al., in press). 3. The ability to judge scene-relative object movement during self-movement is not limited by, or yoked to, the ability to judge the direction of self-movement (Rushton, Chen, & Li, under review). 4. The visual system does not treat independent object motion separately for the perception of heading during self-motion. This is surprising because we all can segment a moving object from the global flow field and perceive its scene-relative motion independent of self-motion. Our findings suggest that the perception of self-motion with independent object motion and the perception of object motion during self-motion are performed by different neural mechanisms (Li et al., accepted). 5. Concurrent manual tracking enhances smooth pursuit, and that this effect is not specific to predictable target movement but is a fundamental property of eye-hand coordination (Niehorster, Siu, & Li, 2015). 6. We have found the first empirical evidence for a causal link between action gaming (for as short as five hours playing) and enhancement in visual motor control. The findings have practical implications for developing training tools to improve performance on daily visual motor control tasks such as driving (Li, Chen, & Chen, 2016). 7. People use heading and target egocentric direction but not path for goal-oriented locomotion control, and their reliance on heading increases at higher travel speeds. The increased reliance on heading for goal-oriented locomotion control could be due to an increased reliability in perceiving heading from optic flow as the magnitude of flow increases with travel speed (Chen, Niehorster, & Li, 2017).

746013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
746013.value: Given the findings of the current research project, we plan to examine the neural bases underlying the perception of object motion during self-motion. The findings of the current project suggest that the perception of self-motion with independent object motion and the perception of object motion during self-motion are performed by different neural mechanisms. We thus plan to use both task-activation and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to address this question. First, using an MVPA fMRI analysis approach, we will identify the brain networks subserving the heading and object motion perception regions. We will then vary visual information in the display to confirm the identified brain networks subserving the two perception processes. In addition, we will examine whether the resting-state functional connectivity of the identified brain networks correlates with the behavioral data observed in the psychophysical experiments.

746013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
746013.value: How do we perceive object motion during self-motion? It has been proposed that we can use retinal or extra-retinal motion cues to estimate self-motion and then remove the retinal motion component due to self-motion to recover scene-relative object motion. Much research has shown that observers can indeed use retinal motion cues such as optic flow to parse self-motion out of retinal motion for object motion perception, but it is still unclear how accurate this “flow parsing” process is and whether it operates on motion information only. Furthermore, it still remains in question how extra-retinal motion cues (such as vestibular, proprioceptive information, and efference copy of motor commands) are used for object motion perception during self-motion. The current project addressed these existing important questions. The findings of the current project inform the architecture of the underlying neural mechanisms responsible for the perception of self-motion and the identification of object motion during self-motion. The findings are applicable to the design of biomimetic robots, unmanned vehicles, and advanced motion sensors.

746413.label: Project Title(Chinese)
746413.value: 中国的城市化：竞办大事件，超前融资，与城市发展-北京，上海，和广州的特例研究

746413.label: Co - Investigator(s)
746413.value: Prof DU, Debin Prof He, Canfei

746413.label: Project Objectives
746413.value: Identify the formation and implementation of hosting mega events as a strategy to mobilize capital and transform the urban built environment; Investigate the social and political origins of practicing the new mega-event-driven urban development strategy; Critically evaluate the impacts of the mega-event-driven developmental strategy on economic growth, urban transformation, and regional inequality.
rows: Identify the formation and implementation of hosting mega events as a strategy to mobilize capital and transform the urban built environment;
Investigate the social and political origins of practicing the new mega-event-driven urban development strategy;
Critically evaluate the impacts of the mega-event-driven developmental strategy on economic growth, urban transformation, and regional inequality.

746413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
746413.value: 本研究结合当前有关中国城市化过程的理论进展，探讨中国城市以 举办大事件为城市发展策略的根源和结果。 研究目标为：揭示以 举办大事件为城市发展策略的制定和实施，调查其形成的社会和政治根源，并评估其对城市经济发展，空间重构，和区域差异的影响。本研究以中国的三大都市区—北京，上海，广州—为特例，对全国，地区，和市级的统计数据作定量分析，并对社会调查获得的信息作定性分析。充分利用我们团队多年来积累的丰富野外调研经验和当地关系网络，本研究将为中国城市化理论进展和城市可持续发展政策的制定贡献新的知识。

746413.label: Realisation of objectives
746413.value: Objective 1 has been successfully accomplished through the collection and analysis of three sets of data: 1) data for China’s 287 cities at and above the prefectural level; 2) data for China’s 36 provincial capitals and special municipalities; and 3) data for the three chosen cases of Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou at the district level. Our data collection and analysis focused on five important respects, namely 1) urban economic growth (GDP per capita inclusive of the migrant population); 2) fixed asset capital investment and growth and composition of local debts; 3) changes in the urban built-environment and urban infrastructure; 4) spatial inequality (redistribution of GDP per capita at the city level and at the district level and redistribution of the migrant population at the district level); and 5) career advancement of mayors and party secretary (comparison of the posts held by leading government officials before and after the hosting of mega-events). We have decided to define “mega-events” as those state-mobilized public events of national and international significance and we focused on the time period that covers the duration from the date when the hosting status was announced to the date when the event was held. Our analysis started with cross-sectional modeling of the data for the 287 cities at and above the prefectural level and the 36 provincial capital cities and special municipalities. This was then followed by a longitudinal analysis for the three chosen cases of Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou. This has allowed us to identify the pattern and process of using the hosting of mega-events as a strategy to mobilize capital and transform the existing urban built-environment. Objective 2 has been accomplished satisfactorily by a combined approach that dealt with panel data at the national level and the insightful information obtained through social survey at the local level. At the national level, we have collected and analyzed panel data concerning changes in the positions held by the mayors and party secretaries for China’s 287 cities at and above the prefectural level for the period of 2000-2010 using the hosting of mega-events as a dummy variable. At the local level, we have conducted documentary research, interviews, and field investigations involving key stakeholders (i.e. government officials, key decision-makers, planners, and affected urban residents inclusive of migrants) in the process of hosting mega-events in the three focused study sites of Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou. This approach has enabled us to identify the general pattern concerning the political motive for hosting mega-events for Chinese cities at the national level and understand the strategic interests, individual perspective, value, and considerations of the decision-makers and participants involved in the practice of mega-event-driven urban development strategy. Objective 3 has been successfully achieved in accordance with the original plan. For consistency and comparability, we have used GDP per capita (inclusive of the migrant population) at the urban district level as a measurement of urban economic growth. Evaluation of the impacts upon the urban built environment has been made focusing on a) expansion of the city-boundary and urban built-up area, b) changes in the urban infrastructure (ring-roads, subway rails, green space, social and cultural services), c) relocation of state-owned industries, d) redistribution of the migrant population, e) changes in air quality, and f) incidents of mass grievance and social discontents. Changes in regional inequality are measured by Coefficient of Variance using per capita GDP at the city/county level for the time period of 2000-2012. A consistent scheme of analysis is adopted to classify spatial units at the urban district level into the categories of increase, decline, and unchanged as well as upward converging/diverging and downward converging/diverging. Our research has generated novel research findings, some already published and others submitted for publication in leading internationally refereed journals (see Research Outcome and Research Output below for details). Overall, we are highly satisfied with the results of our research as what we have originally planned.

746413.label: Major findings and research outcome
746413.value: This project has generated a considerable number of important findings, some of which have already been published in leading internationally refereed journals and presented in international conferences while others are in the pipeline of submission and publication. Our research findings include: 1. Contrary to popular perceptions, the impacts of hosting mega-events upon urban economic growth are found to be insignificant and inconclusive. No convincing evidence is found to suggest that hosting mega-events leads directly to the expansion of the urban economy. 2. Hosting mega-events has significantly and directly contributed to both the improvements of the urban infrastructure and the growth of local debts. Hosting mega-events has been used by the city involved as a means to deploy (overdraft) resources from the future and elsewhere for a momentary improvement of the urban built-environment. 3. The bulk (over 60%) of the funds needed for mega-events have been mobilized by municipal governments by the means of “self-raised funds” (inclusive of land sales) and domestic loans and securities. 4. Only a small proportion (less than 15%) of the funds mobilized has been invested into the building of the facilities used directly by the mega-events and the balance (over 80% of the funds mobilized) is found to be invested in the development of the urban built environment. 5. A common pattern is observed from large Chinese cities where the announcement of hosting a mega-event is immediately followed by a rally of land sales from the city government. Hosting mega-events has been used by Chinese municipal governments as a justification for accelerated land expropriation, urban sprawl, land sales, and removal of old state-owned industrial enterprises out of the city center. 6. Hosting mega-events is found to have a significant but short-lasting effect upon the instant improvement of the environmental quality of the city. 7. Hosting mega-events has been used by the governments as a means to create temporarily at least a unified social space in which social discontents are effectively sidetracked and covered up in the name of hospitality and collective interests. Deeply rooted problems and built-in crises are simply delayed and postponed without any fundamental solution. 8. Hosting mega-events has had significant impacts upon the career advancement of the party secretary of the municipal government, but insignificant impacts upon the career advancement of the mayor. 9. Hosting mega-events has brought significant benefits to selected social groups in the city but displaced and marginalized the laid-off workers from state-owned enterprises and the migrant population exacerbating the problems of segregation, exclusion, and social discontents. Geographically, hosting mega-events has further enhanced the leading position held by the central city and hence led to increased regional inequality. 10. The current approach to urban development using mega-events as a catalyst can be improved in two important ways: In the strategic interests of long-term economic sustainability, the popular local practice to create momentarily a spectacular urban space financed by state credits, liability and looming debts needs to be closely monitored and regulated in line with international standard. For social stability and justice, municipal governments must take special steps to ensure that the benefits from momentary urbanization are not monopolized by only a few elites but instead shared across space and among all segments of the society inclusive of the unfortunate laid-off SOEs workers, landless farmers, and displaced migrant population.

746413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
746413.value: This project has helped push forward the research frontier in urban China studies. Three important issues arisen from this project are believed to have significant potentials for further research and development. First, this research has focused on the practice of an event-driven urban developmental strategy in the three leading Chinese cities. Further research is needed to investigate cases in other Chinese cities and compare the Chinese experiences with others found elsewhere in the world (e.g. Japan, South Korea, USA, Canada, Australia, etc.). Second, this research has identified a general pattern in which hosting mega-events has been used as a justification for urban renewals involving the removal, relocation and redevelopment of old factories, neighborhoods, and villages-in-the city—what have been referred to as san jiu gai zao 三旧改造 (literally “renewals of the three olds”). Is this phenomenon simply accidental and isolated, or is it indicative of a new trend whereby China’s urbanization shifts its emphasis from the mode of urban sprawl into urban renewal? Further research is needed. Finally, this research has brought to the forge a new local practice to finance the development and upgrading of the existing urban built-environment by state credits, liability and debts. Is urban China following the footsteps of the American marching along a dangerous path of transition from “growth-machine” into “debt-machine”? Are Chinese cities dragged into the new global theatre of financialization? Are these simply isolated incidents or are we opening up a can of worms? Further research is needed.

746413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
746413.value: This research investigates how and why hosting mega-events has recently been practiced as a new strategy of development in China and what social and economic effects this strategy has had focusing on the cases of Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou. Three underpinning forces are identified: hosting mega-events has been pursued as a strategy to 1) (over)draft capital from the future for momentary improvements of the urban infrastructure, 2) create tangible and visible records of political accomplishments, and 3) temporarily dispel grievance and social discontents. Contrary to popular perception, no convincing evidence is found to suggest that hosting mega-events leads significantly to accelerate economic growth. A common pattern is identified in which hosting mega-event has functioned as an instrument (ab)used by the city government to expedite land expropriation and land sales, relocate state-owned industries, and drive the migrant population out of the city center. Improved environmental quality is found to be short-lived. The leading edge of the central city over its periphery has been further enhanced leading to increased regional inequality. The research calls for special attention to the looming local debts resulting from mega-events and the unfortunate victims of the new urban developmental strategy—displaced factory workers, landless farmers, and excluded migrant population.

746913.value: 香港高中課程中「批判性思維」的話語建構: 語言差異及跨課程支援

746913.label: Co - Investigator(s)
746913.value: Dr Fung, Dennis, C. L. Dr Yip, Valerie W.Y.

746913.label: Project Objectives
746913.value: To investigate how Hong Kong senior secondary students conduct critical thinking in different language codes (English and Chinese) To investigate how the same group of students conduct critical thinking in different media of communication (speech and writing) To investigate how critical thinking is supported in the Liberal Studies, Chinese, and English language curricula in the Hong Kong senior secondary curriculum
rows: To investigate how Hong Kong senior secondary students conduct critical thinking in different language codes (English and Chinese)
To investigate how the same group of students conduct critical thinking in different media of communication (speech and writing)
To investigate how critical thinking is supported in the Liberal Studies, Chinese, and English language curricula in the Hong Kong senior secondary curriculum

746913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
746913.value: Since 2001, critical thinking (CT) has been identified in the Hong Kong secondary school curriculum as a generic skill to be promoted across different core curricula including Chinese Language, English Language, and Liberal Studies in response to potential risks arising from information explosion. Very little research, however, has been conducted to investigate the impacts of this curriculum initiative on students’ critical thinking ability. The proposed project seeks to examine Hong Kong senior secondary students’ critical thinking ability through analyzing the discourse in their language productions (including Chinese and English), and exploring whether and how CT can be supported across the core curricula of Chinese, English, and Liberal Studies. The mutually mediating relationship between language and higher-order thinking is a central tenet of the Vygotskian sociocultural perspectives of learning. As far as CT is concerned, a series of debates took place in the United States in the 1990s about the practicality of teaching CT, a mode of thinking that was believed to be US-centric and culture-specific, to immigrant students whose first language was not English. The language barrier was considered to have disadvantaged non-native English immigrant students in courses where CT abilities were required. With trilingualism and biliteracy being the language education goals in Hong Kong, senior secondary students are expected to display CT abilities in both Chinese and English. The proposed project aims to investigate the impacts of language codes and medium of communication on students’ critical thinking. Samples of speech and writing showing how senior secondary students from a variety of schools in Hong Kong conduct critical thinking in different language codes (English and Chinese) will be collected through tasks that involve critical reading of texts involving popular sociocultural issues. In-depth interviews will be conducted with students and teachers of Chinese, English and Liberal Studies to explore their notion of critical thinking, their perceptions of the connection between language and thinking, and their experiences of whether and how CT can be supported as a cross-curricular concern. The findings from quantitative and qualitative discourse analyses of the data are expected to reveal generic features of CT in different language codes and media, and enable local and international educators, researchers, curriculum planners, students and parents to better understand whether and how critical thinking can be facilitated through cross-curricular input covering both language and content. 自2001年起，批判性思維便成為香港學校核心課程包括中、英及通識科中其中一項學習目標，以協助學生應對訊息爆炸下帶來的危機。然而，關於這個課程措施對批判性思維的影响的研究卻甚為缺乏。本項目皆在探究香港高中學生如何運用中、英兩種語文及說話和寫作兩種媒介表達批判性思維，並研究批判性思維如何能夠在中、英及通識科三個核心科目中獲得發展。 語言運用和高階思維的關係是維谷斯基「社會文化理論」的中心論點。關於批判性思維，自1990年起便有一連串關於教授批判性思維的可行徃的研究，一些學者認為批判性思維是以美國特定文化為中心的思巧模式，因些並不適合非英語為母語的移民學生，語言的障礙或會不利移民學生在要求批判性思維能力的課程中的表現。 然而，「兩文三語」是香港語文教育的目的，社會期望高中生有能力用中、英文表達批判性思維。本研究項目於是探究香港高中學生如何運用中、英兩種語文和通過說話和寫作兩種溝通媒介來表達批判性思維。我們會蒐集學生運用中、英兩種語文對一些富社會文化意義的文章的討論和寫作的數据，輔以跟學生及中、英、和通識科老師的深度訪談，從而探討他們對批判性思維的理解、對語言和思考關係的看法、及對批判性思維如何在跨課程中得到發展的意見。通過有關話語的量性和質性的分析，本研究的結果將揭示批判性思維表現於不同語言和不同溝通媒介的文体特徵，有助本地和海外教育人員、學者、課程設計者、學生和家長更好了解批判性思維如何通過不同科目得到提昇。

746913.label: Realisation of objectives
746913.value: As already reported in the Annual Report 2013-14, all data collection activities pertaining to the three project objectives were completed in the first year of the project (Nov 2013-Oct 2014). It was also reported in the above-mentioned Annual Report the reasons why we were unable to meet the proposed number of target participants and why we were unable to collect some types of data from some students and teachers. Due to practical constraints (e.g. some data collection tasks have to be conducted in groups, change of school personnel, the occupy central movement resulting in attendance chaos, and no responses from two schools despite repeated contacts), we were unable to make up for the uncollected data. However, as data has been collected from the majority of the participants (93% of student participants; 80.5% of teacher interviews, and 72% of teacher questionnaires), we tend to believe that the lower number of participants than proposed has not created any negative impacts on the representativeness of our findings. Research activities in the second year of the project focused on data analysis to address the three project objectives: 1. To find out how Hong Kong senior secondary students conducted critical thinking in different language codes (English and Chinese) (project objective 1) and how the same group of students conducted critical thinking in different media of communication (speech and writing) (project objective 2), all the written scripts and discussion recordings generated from the text-reading tasks were turned into electronic data and coded by the researchers based on the themes identified (e.g. identification of authorial intent, identification of permeating assumptions, values & ideologies, etc.) with NVivo8. Simple frequency counts of the number of students having displayed certain evidence of critical thinking were conducted to identify a general pattern of performance. Students' performance was categorized into four scenarios: (1) Chinese text Chinese writing/speaking; (2) Chinese text English writing/speaking; (3) English text Chinese writing/speaking; (4) English text English writing/speaking. Due to the small number of students in each category (only 82 and 73 out of 135 students displayed CT evidence in writing and speaking respectively), no statistical analyses were conducted to test the significance of the differences. Instead, qualitative content analyses of the students' utterances were conducted to find out whether and how they differed in their performance in different language codes and media of communication. 2. Data from the student questionnaires were inputted into an excel file. Our focus of analysis was to identify how students understood the notion of critical thinking. The free responses from students were gone through carefully and similar responses were categorized into key perspectives, for example, 'to distinguish the right from the wrong', 'to think from multiple perspectives', 'to think independently.' Such data would enrich the researchers' interpretation of students' performance in the text analysis tasks. 3. As indicated in the annual report 2013-14, interviews with teachers of English language, Chinese language, and liberal studies were conducted to collect their perceptions on their students’ ability to conduct critical thinking, and whether and how they developed critical thinking in their subject-specific curriculum (project objective 3). Their responses were transcribed and a qualitative content analysis without any pre-determined themes or codes was conducted particularly to identify their existing and desired practices to develop students' critical thinking in their specific subject. Similar patterns of practices and views were then further identified.

746913.label: Major findings and research outcome
746913.value: The results of the study generally lent support to our hypothesis that more students would be able to display critical thinking (CT) evidence when reading and expressing ideas in their first language (L1), Chinese/Cantonese, as compared to the same performance in English, their L2 (second language). The same outcomes applied to both speaking and writing even though there was a slightly larger number of students having displayed CT evidence in writing (62.1%) than speaking (55.3%). Such a difference is likely to be due to the availability of more time to plan and check references (e.g. making use of on-line translation tools) during the writing process. The findings also show that 42.68% and 36.98% of students having displayed CT evidence in writing and speaking respectively also displayed partial or distorted representation of the text content; and among these students, 68.18% (writing) and 70.37% (speaking) read the Chinese text. This means many students were not necessarily able to comprehend and/or express ideas precisely even when working in their L1. Such distorted representation of text content also revealed some students' inadequate understanding of the rhetorical strategies and semiotic conventions of the genres in focus. The CT skill that most students displayed (57.31% writing and 54.79% speaking) is 'Identification of deficiencies/inadequacies in arguments'. This finding seemed to align with the questionnaire results where about one-third (27.1%) of the students defined CT as the ability to distinguish the right from the wrong (分辨對錯), which was the most frequently expressed view, followed by ‘thinking from multiple perspectives’ (多角度思考) (12.5%), another popular view of CT among educators in Hong Kong. These results show that a considerable number of students tended to understand CT as a fault-finding skill and they seemed to think that right and wrong can be neatly dichotomized. All teachers supported the idea of cross-curricular development of CT skills, but most of the language teachers seldom consciously attempted to develop this skill systematically. The English teachers in particular had reservations about students' ability to express CT in English. Overall speaking, most teachers agreed that the type of text-analysis tasks implemented in the research would be effective in developing students' CT skills, but they indicated that only high academic achievers would be able to do well, and most students need heavy guidance and scaffolding from teachers.

746913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
746913.value: The findings revealed some students' inability to interpret the text content or data in light of the genre of the texts and their related rhetorical strategies and generic conventions even when reading in their first language. Language familiarity does not guarantee effective display of critical thinking. Students need to develop the skills to situate CT in specific genres and disciplinary discourse. These point to the need to strengthen students' critical genre awareness, or the awareness of how semiotic resources (including both linguistic and visual) can be deployed to construct values, beliefs and ideologies. Subsequent research can investigate whether and how critical genre awareness could enhance students' cognitive processing of text data in terms of critical thinking such as sensitivity to hidden values and beliefs, authorial intent, logical flaws and biases, etc.. Possible design of the study could involve two groups of students with one group (experimental) experiencing an intervention focusing on genre-based language teaching with pre- and post-data collection of students' critical text reading similar to what had been conducted in the present study.

746913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
746913.value: This project was designed to investigate how a group of senior secondary students learning English as a second language in Hong Kong displayed critical thinking (CT) through different language codes (Chinese and English) and media of communication (speaking and writing). 135 students and 58 teachers teaching English, Chinese, and Liberal Studies were involved. The results of the study support our hypothesis that more students were able to display CT evidence when reading and expressing ideas in their first language, Chinese/Cantonese, compared to the same performance in English. The data, however, also revealed many students' superficial and/or distorted reading of even the Chinese text. Overall speaking, the findings showed that critical thinking is closely related to genre-specific textual strategies. Language familiarity does not guarantee effective display of critical thinking. There seems to be a need for language teachers in Hong Kong to go beyond general text comprehension and sentence-based grammar and engage students in analyzing discourse strategies of specific text types with a view to deconstructing the logics and meanings, authorial intent, and underlying ideologies.

747113.label: Project Title(Chinese)
747113.value: 構建教育政策和參與柬埔寨私人輔導之間關係的理論模型

747113.label: Project Objectives
747113.value: Build and refine a theoretical model of the influence of education policies on participation in mainstream schooling and in private tutoring. Use this model to empirically identify which policies, at which thresholds, influence participation in tutoring in Cambodia.
rows: Build and refine a theoretical model of the influence of education policies on participation in mainstream schooling and in private tutoring.
Use this model to empirically identify which policies, at which thresholds, influence participation in tutoring in Cambodia.

747113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
747113.value: 此研究計畫旨在建立一個政策環境和參與柬埔寨私人輔導之間關係的理論模型。 在柬埔寨的許多地方，學校一天分為兩個部分，一部分是免費的且向所有人開放，而另一部分被認為是需要付費的“私人輔導”。至於“私人輔導”，學生們普遍認為是有必要的，他們可以接受全面的教育，教師則普遍認為可以借此賺取一定的生活费。 以前的一些关于亞洲的教育政策對私人輔導影響的模型很大程度上建立在對東亞社會的研究，如日本，韓國，新加坡和香港。許多研究理論把私人輔導作為一個是對主流教學的“影子”或“補充”。 最近的研究表明，東亞把私人輔導作為主流教學系統“影子”或“補充”的理論在一個發展中的環境下是不恰當的。比如柬埔寨，那裏的主流教育系統和其他一切之間的界限是模糊不清的。事實上，私人輔導可能會取代而不是補充主流系統，因為教師可能為了在學校課程結束後賺取更多的費用，會在教學中有所保留。這種系統的劃分導致貧困學生不能接受全面的課程，也對實現普及免費、優質基礎教育的目標構成了挑戰。此外，這種私人輔導取代而非補充的本末倒置的現象，可能確實發生在許多其他的教育系統，包括在那些更發達的國家。 但儘管舊的理論已經出現了裂縫，可是新的理論又尚未完全浮現，這就導致難以去構建模型——教育政策可能會影響參與私人輔導是如何發生變化的。而此研究項目通過對柬埔寨暹粒省的六所初中進行調查，研究教育政策是如何影響私人輔導和主流教學之間的關係，將有助於找到一個替代的理論。在這些學校中，我們將對九和十二年級的1800名學生和76名教師進行調查，隨後是個別訪談。而調查和訪談，將會探討八個可能會對私人輔導產生影響的政策。 這個研究項目將對私人輔導和私人市場及公共教育的作用兩方面的文獻作出重大貢獻。此外，它還將幫助決策者更好地瞭解各種教育政策和參與私人輔導之間的相互關聯。

747113.label: Realisation of objectives
747113.value: The research successfully identified components for the theoretical model, and demonstrated relationships between them. It did this through both quantitative and qualitative analysis, as intended. It then identified levers through which policy-makers could intervene. The research and therefore the policy implication are of course context-specific, but Cambodia has sufficient similarity to other countries in a comparable income group to have generalisable lessons. Indeed this has been recognized by the publishers of the outputs and particularly the International Journal of Educational Development. Major components in the theoretical model are salary levels of teachers, density of the curriculum, selection mechanisms for students to advance to subsequent steps in the education system, and social perspectives on the extent to which it is reasonable for households to pay for extra lessons. A significant contribution of the project is the observation that while many stakeholders (including the government) criticize the existence of private supplementary tutoring – and especially that provided by teachers to their own students – the system is to some extent perpetuated because the stakeholders benefit. The families benefit because their children can keep up (or keep ahead) in the competitive environment; the teachers benefit because their can secure extra incomes; the schools benefit because they can keep some of the revenue and they can claim achievements from students’ academic performance; and the government benefits because it can continue to under-pay teachers yet retain them in the profession due to their supplementary incomes. In addition, the research has made a major methodological contribution. A chapter was devoted to the project in a book entitled Researching Private Supplementary Tutoring: Methodological Lessons from Diverse Cultures. This is the first book to focus specifically on methodology in this field, and is making a cross-national impact. The instruments have been shared with researchers elsewhere. They were themselves derived from an instrument first used in Hong Kong and later used with adaptations in China, Dubai, India, Iran, Jamaica and Malaysia, and are now being used with further adaptations in Myanmar and Pakistan.

747113.label: Major findings and research outcome
747113.value: Among the sampled students, 74.7% in Grade 9 and 89.8% in Grade 12 were receiving private supplementary tutoring, mostly from their own teachers or from other teachers in their schools. Most of this tutoring was received either before or after official lessons on the school premises. Greater proportions of urban students received tutoring compared with counterparts in suburban and rural locations. This was in line with patterns elsewhere, but the gap was modest. Slightly more females (82.8%) received tutoring compared with males (80.9%). Most students who received tutoring did so in several subjects. Nearly half received tutoring in three to five subjects, and 1.7% of students received it in over six subjects. Not only did Grade 12 students receive more tutoring, they also did so in more subjects. The most popular subjects were Mathematics, Chemistry, Khmer, Physics, and Biology. Among the students who responded, 64.9% felt and 19.3% strongly felt that the expenditure on private tutoring was a financial burden. Only 15.8% of respondents felt that the tutoring was not a financial burden. Two thirds of respondent indicated that standardised fees were charged, while one third indicated that teachers charged differential fees according to students’ ability to pay. The latter finding does indicate some amelioration of the negative effects of the system on social inequalities, but overall the system clearly disadvantaged low-income families. Teachers were also asked about the significance of tutoring to their incomes. Most responding teachers indicated that they earned as much from tutoring as from their official salaries. However, some teachers chose not to provide tutoring because other ways to supplement their incomes were more remunerative. Concerning the students’ reasons for seeking tutoring, findings stressed the importance of the national examination, especially in Grade 12. Such motivation is common in many countries. More distinctive to Cambodia, despite the fact that the private classes were given by regular teachers, was the demand for private classes to secure exposure to different pedagogical methods. More light was shed on the matter by the interviews. Students commonly indicated that tutoring provided better opportunities to practice exercises. During regular lessons, they felt, teachers mainly explained content and put less emphasis on exercises. In the private classes, teachers treated the students more like customers and were more responsive to the students.

747113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
747113.value: The research has only focused on students in two grades of secondary schooling in one province of the country. It would be very useful to extend to the primary level and to other regions. Particularly instructive would be a parallel survey in Phnom Penh, the capital city, where incomes are higher and commercial activities are more developed. Further, while it has data from students and teachers, this project did not collect data from parents or other family members. Such data through further research would provide valuable triangulation and complementarity. Already some follow-up is being undertaken in the same province by one of the PI’s (Master of Education (MEd) students. The PI is also in discussion with counterparts in the Cambodian research community. Further, the methods and insights are being disseminated beyond Cambodia through the work of HKU’s UNESCO Chair in Comparative Education. A new project has been launched in Myanmar, with funding from UNESCO and partnership with the Yangon University of Education (YUOE).

747113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
747113.value: This project focused on a phenomenon widely known as shadow education. The metaphor describes forms of private supplementary tutoring provided in parallel to official instruction in regular schooling and mimicking the content of that schooling. In the Cambodian context, much of the tutoring is also shadowy in the sense of being of doubtful legality and of questionable social impact. High proportions of students paid for supplementary lessons, most of which were provided by their own teachers. Shadow education has become a major phenomenon around the world. Patterns in Hong Kong are rather different from those in Cambodia, since Hong Kong teachers are less in need of supplementary income. As such, the research in Cambodia showed a model of shadow education that contrasted with models in Hong Kong and other prosperous societies. This contrast helps in conceptual understanding at an international level. At the same time, Cambodia has similarities not only with its immediate neighbours but also with other low-income countries around the world. Again, therefore, the project has provided valuable data not only for Cambodia itself but also cross-nationally.

747113.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
747113.value: The work has demonstrated value not only in the conceptual and academic literature but also in policy-making and capacity development both in Cambodia and elsewhere. The capacity development includes the NGO with which the GRF-funded team worked. Further, the PI has excellent professional links with the Ministry of Education in Cambodia, and made presentations both there and to the Education Sector Working Group that brings together international agencies and NGOs. The written text of the presentation is attached. Indeed the work has contributed to a broader Impact Case Study which in a Mock Research Assessment Exercise (RAE) has been rated as 4*. More widely, the research is contributing to global considerations of the nature of ‘hidden’ privatisation and the implications for the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It is doing this through the PI’s links as UNESCO Chair in Comparative Education. On the positive side, private supplementary tutoring provides extra resources for education and can enhance learning. However, it has far-reaching implications for social inequalities. The PI’s work has been cited in the United Nations’ Report of the Special Rapporteur on the Right to Education and in UNESCO’s Education for All Global Monitoring Report. The empirical data collected through this project add force to generalised statements and therefore specificity and impact

748013.label: Project Objectives
748013.value: The overall aim of the proposed study is to conduct a randomized controlled trial for rigorously evaluating the efficacy of the group therapy for stagnation. Multidimensional outcome measures are adopted and the specific objectives are: (i) To evaluate the efficacy of intervention in terms of clinical assessment by a Chinese medicine practitioner according to diagnostic criteria; (ii) To evaluate the efficacy of intervention in terms of self-report scales, which include stagnation, depression, anxiety and body-mind-spirit well-being; and (iii) To evaluate the efficacy of intervention in terms of a biological marker, which is salivary cortisol for assessing hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis neuroendocrine dysfunction.

748013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
748013.value: 背景 「鬱」是不流淌、纏繞和堵塞的意思。中醫學「鬱證」以身心梗阻為主要癥狀，例如患者感覺頭、咽喉、胸、胃、或腹等部位阻塞不舒。我們在過去的研究中，將鬱證操作化為一個心理徤康建構，發展岀一個三因子、十六題的「鬱證量表」。在優配研究金（GRF）的資助下，我們進一步採集了隨機社區樣本，調研香港成年人「鬱」的情況。結果顯示鬱證的點患病率為6.2%，由於鬱證在中醫被歸納為身體而非精神疾病，因此患者普遍對鬱證持有較低的負面社會標纖感，約近30％的患者積極尋求治療。對精神衛生工作者而言，鬱證是一個切合華人文化，調動當亊人求助積極性的介入點。根據過去的研究結果，我們並且發展了一套六節的鬱證團體治療。鑒於在先導試驗中所取得的鼓舞成果，我們計劃為這套鬱證團體治療進行更嚴格深入的臨床試驗。 目的和設計 本研究計劃採用隨機對照臨床試驗，對鬱證團體治療的療效進行嚴格評估。參與者將會從香港大學中醫診所招募。樣本由7對干預和對照組所組成，每組有9名參與者[總樣本為126名參與者；功率分析(power analysis)表明，雙臂設計最少樣本量要求為每臂55名參與者]。為了抵消群體社交效應，對照組將會接受6次中醫常識講座，和干預組的時間安排一致。我們將為每一組於三個關鍵時間點進行以下的測量： （1）臨床評估：由中醫根據診斷標準做出評估，（2）自評量表：鬱證、抑鬱(depression) 、焦慮和身心靈徤康; （3）生理指標：唾液皮質醇，用以測量下丘腦 - 垂體 - 腎上腺軸的神經內分泌功能。 預期結果 強調身心連接是中醫學的傳統理念，鬱證正好是這一理念的典型例子。然而，尤其在现代繁忙的醫療單位中，傳統一對一的醫療諮詢模式難以實現這一傳統理念。本研究中所檢驗的團體治療方案，將不僅會成為一種有效和實用的治療方法，而且對於中醫實務的革新更會帶來正面的推動作用。這種革新性將體現於引入團體治療諮詢模式和精神衛生專業人員，恊助實現中醫學強調身心連接的傳統理念。

748013.label: Realisation of objectives
748013.value: The proposed research has been executed carefully according to the original plan. Difficulties have been encountered in the recruitment of participants at the first Chinese medicine clinic – the Chinese Medicine Clinic of the School of Chinese Medicine, The University of Hong Kong at Sassoon Road, Hong Kong. Most patients there showed no interest in joining research. After a few months of hard work without satisfactory progress, we included one more Chinese medicine clinic – the Tung Wah Hospital at Sheung Wan. The move sped up participants recruitment significantly. Totally 135 patients gave consent and were screened. Eventually 56 and 55 patients participated in the intervention and control groups respectively, and received the pretest assessment. Because there is a capacity limit that each group may take, totally 4 pairs of intervention-control subgroups were implemented, with an average of about 14 participants per group. The completion rates were satisfactory, with 49 (87.5%) and 51 (92.7%) patients completed the intervention and control groups respectively, and received the posttest assessment. Completion rates at 2-month follow-up assessment remained satisfactory, with 47 (83.9%) and 47 (85.5%) in intervention and groups respectively completed all assessments. The laboratory providing salivary cortisol analysis service to the project experienced some manpower problems. As a result, supply of the cortisol data was delayed by a few months. Nevertheless, subsequent statistical analyses on the dataset revealed positive findings and provided evidence supporting the efficacy of the intervention in both self-report scales and salivary cortisol levels. More details are depicted in the next section ‘Research Outcome’. Grounded on the findings, presentations were made in 5 international conferences, including some very top ones such as the Society of Behavioral Medicine 38th Annual Meeting and Scientific Sessions, and the 24th World Congress on Psychosomatic Medicine. Regarding publications, 4 peer-reviewed journal papers/abstract were published in the Journal of Psychosomatic Medicine (Impact factor 3.638, 2015), World Journal of TCM Psychology (Chinese journal), the Annals of Behavioral Medicine (Impact factor 2.976, 2016) and Evidence-based Complementary and Alternative Medicine (Impact factor 1.740, 2016). Furthermore, 1 paper is currently under review by the BMC Complementary and Alternative Medicine (Impact factor 2.288, 2016). In knowledge exchange, we organized a public symposium jointly with the Depression Clinical and Research Program, Department of Psychiatry, Harvard Medical School in March 2017. More details are depicted in Part C. In late October/early November 2017, I visited and delivered invited lectures at the Depression Clinical and Research Program, Department of Psychiatry, Harvard Medical School, and developed a close working relationship with them. Sharing common interest on mild depression, functional somatic syndrome and TCM stagnation syndrome, we are keen to collaborate in these research areas in future.

748013.label: Major findings and research outcome
748013.value: BACKGROUND Stagnation syndrome, a diagnostic entity in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), is characterized by mind-body obstruction-like symptoms. Although TCM has long-established symptom-relief treatments, a comprehensive mind-body intervention was called for. PURPOSE The study evaluated the efficacy of a six-session body-mind-spirit (BMS) group therapy for persons with stagnation syndrome. METHOD A 2-arm randomized controlled trial design was adopted. The control group received a parallel general TCM instruction course. Both groups completed a pretest (T0), posttest (T1), and 2-month follow-up assessment (T2). The measures included self-report scales on stagnation, depression, anxiety, physical distress, daily functioning, and positive and negative affect; the other measure was of salivary cortisol, a biological marker of stress. RESULTS Data on 111 adults with stagnation syndrome were included in the analysis. Completion rates were high (over 87%) for both the intervention and control groups. Repeated measures multivariate MANOVA revealed a significant combined effect with large effect size (eta-squared = 0.37). Repeated measures ANOVA further revealed that the intervention group showed significant improvements in stagnation, the primary outcome, with medium effect size (eta-squared = 0.11). The intervention group also showed significant improvements in depression, physical distress, everyday functioning and negative affect (eta-squared = 0.06 to 0.13). Post hoc analysis revealed that the intervention group showed significant improvements over the control group in cortisol level at 2-month follow-up assessment (T0 vs T2) with small effect size (eta-squared = 0.05), but not at posttest (T0 vs T1). CONCLUSIONS Overall, the findings indicate that our brief BMS group therapy intervention for stagnation syndrome is efficacious. Moreover, the intervention resulted in a number of substantial improvements in the physical and mental health domains.

748013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
748013.value: TCM stagnation syndrome has significant overlap with mild depression and functional somatic syndrome. Mild depression and functional somatic syndrome may sound ‘less severe’ (in terms of clinical symptoms) than major clinical depression. However, these ‘mild’ conditions affect the daily function and quality of life of many people. Treatments for major clinical depression (e.g. antidepressant medications and electro-convulsive therapy) are often irrelevant to these people. Findings of our current study has aroused the interest of researchers in related fields. In particular, I have established a close working relationship with the Depression Clinical and Research Program, Department of Psychiatry, Harvard Medical School. We are keen to collaborate in these research areas in future.

748013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
748013.value: BACKGROUND Stagnation syndrome, a diagnostic entity in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), is characterized by mind-body obstruction-like symptoms. To avoid a psychiatric connotation, stagnation syndrome is strategically put under internal medicine in TCM. By addressing the presenting somatic symptoms first, stagnation syndrome is a good entry point to engage people in distress, PURPOSE The study evaluated the efficacy of a six-session body-mind-spirit (BMS) group therapy for persons with stagnation syndrome. METHOD A 2-arm randomized controlled trial design was adopted. The control group received a parallel general TCM instruction course. Both groups completed a pretest (T0), posttest (T1), and 2-month follow-up assessment (T2). The measures included self-report scales on stagnation and related mental health variables; the other measure was of salivary cortisol, a biological marker of stress. RESULTS Data on 111 adults with stagnation syndrome were included in the analysis. Completion rates were high (over 87%) for both the intervention and control groups. Statistical analyses revealed that the intervention group showed significant improvements in stagnation, the primary outcome, as well as in depression, physical distress, everyday functioning, negative affect and cortisol level. CONCLUSIONS Overall, the findings indicate that our brief BMS group therapy intervention for stagnation syndrome is efficacious.

748113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
748113.value: Background: Having a first child is a key marker of the transition into parenthood that requires substantial adjustment of couples’ life. A recent meta-analysis published in the Journal of American Medical Association reports that both women (23.8%) and men (10.4%) suffer from perinatal depression [1]. The father’s involvement during pregnancy can positively influence health outcomes not only for the man, but his partner, and their children [1,2]. However, the effectiveness of father’s involvement in prenatal care in preventing paternal and maternal depression, is still unknown. Aims: This study seeks to: (1) evaluate the effect of a father inclusive psychoeducation program for first-time Chinese mothers and fathers on depressive symptoms (primary outcome), marital relationships and quality of life at 6 weeks, 6 months and one year postpartum; and (2) explore fathers’ involvement, their perceived benefits of participating in the program and factors influencing the effectiveness of the program. Methods: This study employs a longitudinal, randomized, pre and post-test design. A convenience sample of 576 couples will be recruited at antenatal clinics and randomly assigned to one of three groups: (1) the experimental group with both couples receives the intervention on top of usual perinatal care; (2) the comparison group with only the women receives the intervention on top of usual perinatal care; and (3) the control group receives usual perinatal care only. The intervention consists of a single 3-hour session during pregnancy and two telephone follow-up at postpartum week one and week two. Primary outcome on postnatal depression will be assessed by Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale. Secondary outcomes on marital relationship and quality of life will be assessed by Dyadic Adjustment Scale and Medical Outcomes Study Short Form 12-item Health Survey, respectively, at baseline, 6 weeks, 6 months and one year postpartum. Process evaluation will be conducted at 6 weeks postpartum using individual telephone interview on 20 couples randomly selected from the experimental group. Data analysis: A repeated-measures multivariate analysis of variance will be used to test for significant differences among three groups on outcome variables. Interview data will be analyzed by content analysis. Significance: The knowledge gained from this study can provide the direction for developing flexible, accessible and culturally sensitive care to enhance both maternal and paternal well-being in Chinese society. The results may be utilized to improve perinatal services and reduce healthcare costs on the treatment of postnatal depression in light of fiscal limitations in contemporary healthcare system. 摘要 背景：為人父母是人生中重要的理程碑，夫婦二人在生活上都需要作出重大的適應。最近美國醫學協會雜誌發表了一篇薈萃分析文章，內容指出有23.8％的婦女及其丈夫(10.4％)在產後都証實患有抑鬱症。在太太懷孕期間，丈夫的參與不但對他自已的健康，甚至懷孕中的太太及未來孩子的健康都可以產生正面的影響。然而，產前丈夫的參與是否能有效防止父母的抑鬱症仍是未知數。 目的：這項研究的目的：（一）探討準父母參與的產前教育課程對產後抑鬱症、婚姻關係及生活質量在產後六個星期，六個月和一年的成效；（二）探討影響丈夫參與產前教育課程的因素，及其參與對夫婦的影響。 方法：這項研究採用了隨機對照組前後比較設計，在產前門診部以方便取樣方式招募576對懷孕夫婦，並隨機分配到以下三組其中一組：（一）實驗組—懷孕夫婦同時參與研究的干預；（二）對照組—只有懷孕婦女參與研究的干預；及（三）對照組—懷孕夫婦二人都沒有參與研究的干預。研究的干預包括一堂三小時的產前教育課程和兩次產後電話咨詢，三組夫婦均在干預前填寫「愛丁堡產後抑鬱量表」、「婚姻關係量表」及「生活質量量表」，並在產後六周、六個月及一年再次填寫。另外在產後六周，實驗組隨機抽取二十位夫婦進行單獨的電話訪問。 數據分析：採用「重複測量多元方差分析」測試三組的問卷數據，及「內容分析」分析電話採訪數據。 意義：從這項研究中獲得的知識可以提昇夫婦懷孕時期及產後的護理，促進為人父母的健康，及降低產後抑鬱症對醫療體系造成的財政負擔。

748113.label: Realisation of objectives
748113.value: Objective 1 has been completed. A total of 388 childbearing couples were recruited at three regional public hospitals and were randomly allocated to the couple-based cognitive behavioural intervention (n = 134), the women-alone intervention (n = 124) or the control groups (n = 130). All participants in the couple-based and women-alone interventions attended the single antenatal session and around 80% completed at least one telephone follow-up at postpartum. A total of 381 couples (98·2%) completed post-test measures at 6 weeks postpartum, 370 couples (95.4%) at 6 months postpartum, and 325 couples (83.8%) at 12 months postpartum. Objective 2 has been completed. A purposive sample of 30 first-time Chinese parents who had participated in the couple-based cognitive-behavioral intervention was interviewed at 6 weeks postpartum. Data were transcribed and analyzed using content analysis.

748113.label: Major findings and research outcome
748113.value: The results showed that the depression score of mothers was significantly lower in the couple-based intervention group than in the women-alone comparison group (p < 0.05) and control group (p < 0.01) at 6 weeks postpartum, but the differences were not statistically significant at 6 and 12 months. For fathers, there was no significant between-group difference in depression score at all time points. There was no significant difference in the secondary outcomes of marital relationship and health-related quality of life between the three groups at all time points. The qualitative data revealed that Chinese fathers perceived the couple-based cognitive-behavioral intervention to be helpful in increasing their confidence in the paternal role, increasing sense of support, and enhancing emotional control in themselves and their partners during the perinatal period. Suggestions for improvement included extending the intervention with sharing sessions to facilitate paternal role taking and involving other family members in the intervention, such as their parents and parents-in-law.

748113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
748113.value: The effect for the couple-based intervention on depressive symptoms was modest (Cohen’s d = 0.30). Given the brief treatment of the intervention, a more intensive intervention targeting at high risk couples may be needed in future study. Furthermore, the positive effects of the couple-based intervention were evident only among the mothers. Further study is needed to establish what type of strategies and interventions work best for the fathers to prevent postnatal depression.

748113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
748113.value: The present findings add to the growing evidence that couple-based cognitive behavioural interventions are associated with a significant reduction in postnatal depression among mothers. Couple-based therapy is providing a growing conceptual and empirical foundation for prevention efforts in postnatal depression, given the growing evidence of its prevalence among both parents and the close relationship between maternal and paternal depression. The successful delivery of this trial shows the possibility of engaging both partners and promoting their collaborative coping to prevent postnatal depression in the Chinese society.
