748213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
748213.value: While the questions of how languages acquire new grammatical constructions and how these become more productive have received considerable attention in linguistics, the reverse phenomenon of “constructional attrition”, a decrease in the productivity of constructions, is one that has been much less investigated. It has recently been spotlighted as an area of investigation in the novel discipline of “diachronic construction grammar”, which takes a holistic, cognitively adequate, view at shifts in the constructional resources of languages. This project will contribute to the development of this field of study through a corpus-linguistic investigation of the evolution of a grammatical construction which is hypothesized to have become significantly less frequent and productive over the past couple of centuries, viz. the construction which pairs a pattern that consists of a passive verb phrase complemented by a to-infinitive with an obligative meaning. Present-day examples of this construction are: (1) You ARE SUPPOSED TO sit up with a straight back. (2) It will not be long before they ARE OBLIGED TO come looking for me. Examples of older realizations of the construction which have grown out of use are: (3) Philip found that he WAS WANTED TO hold the jug full of milk. (4) Before the end of the year, I WAS NECESSITATED TO preach a discourse on almsgiving. [both 18th century] In orthodox grammaticalization theory, the pattern exemplified in (1) has been considered in isolation, as an individual grammaticalization of BE SUPPOSED + TO. In a diachronic construction grammatical approach, on the other hand, the development of this construction is placed in the context of the evolution of both formally and functionally similar patterns. If, as expected, it turns out that the pattern is a remnant of a more general pattern that used to be more inclusive, this adds a whole new dimension to the study of the grammaticalization of specific constructions which, like BE SUPPOSED TO, are sufficiently entrenched to be listed in grammar books. This project will document the evolution of the frequency and the inclusiveness of the general pattern and will look for cognitively plausible explanations for the predicted downward trend. The evolution of the English construction will be contrasted with the development of the cognate Dutch construction for the explanatory insights a contrastive perspective is expected to generate. Corpus-linguistic techniques pioneered in previous research will be fine-tuned to broaden the empirical basis for statements on constructional semantics.

748213.label: Realisation of objectives
748213.value: Objective 1: The research has focused on three descriptive areas which converge on constructional attrition: 1. The attrition of the Modal Auxiliary construction in the very recent history of, on the one hand, the two main metropolitan varieties, or “supervarieties”, of English, i.e. British English and American English, and, on the other, two Asian varieties, viz. Hong Kong English and Singaporean English. This component of the research was sparked off by an invitation to contribute to an edited volume on grammatical change in different national varieties of English and while not part of the original research plan it contributed significantly to achieving the project’s objectives in that it ties in with the part of the burgeoning research on recent/current changes in (World) English(es) which is concerned with the general decline, in British and American English, of the frequency of the modal auxiliaries. This research strand was pushed forward, both in terms of the time span covered as well as methodologically, by making use of Factiva®, a business information and research tool which had not been exploited in published linguistic research before. 2. The type and token frequency decline in British English, during the course of the Late Modern English period (18th to early 20th century), of the instantiations of a schematic deontic BE-Ven-to-inf construction (like “be bound to”, “be obliged to” and “be required to”), through documentation of the evolution of the frequency of all the microconstructions instantiating the schema in the three 70-year period components of the Corpus of Late Modern English Texts (CLMET). 3. The (halted) attrition of the Dutch schematic nominative-and-infinitive construction, which only survives as two microconstructions in Present-day Dutch, viz. “geacht worden te” (‘be considered/supposed to’) and “verondersteld worden te” (‘be supposed to’). The description of the attritional post-constructionalization evolution of these three distinct schematic constructions forcefully consolidated constructional attrition as an important research area within diachronic construction grammar. Objective 2: The bulk of research in the grammaticalization theoretical strand of diachronic construction grammar has focused on how new constructions come into being, while post-constructionalization constructional changes remained an underresearched area. The research activities on constructional attrition that went towards Objective 1 contributed to filling this gap. The research in each of the descriptive areas made important theoretical contributions. The World Englishes research on the Modal Auxiliary construction showed constructional attrition to be genre and variety specific. The investigation of the deontic BE-Ven-to-inf construction determined that in the case of two homonymous constructions there is no inherent causal relation between the rise of one of the homonyms and the attrition of the other. The study on the attrition of the Dutch nominative-and-infinitive identified “constructional renovation” as a phenomenon relevant to attritional developments. The descriptive research also led to theoretical reflections on what a “radically usage-based” constructionist approach to language change should look like and what the methodological implications are of such an approach. As a radical deviation from the dominant grammaticalization theoretical strand in diachronic construction grammar they constitute a critical contribution to grammaticalization theory. Objective 3: To prepare for the study on the evolution of the Dutch schematic nominative-and-infinitive construction a new Dutch historical corpus was extracted from the newspaper component of the Delpher text archive of the Dutch Royal Library. The results of the data analysis suggested that influence from French, specifically legal French, in the first half of the 19th century, was likely to have been a major factor in the survival of the Dutch “geacht worden te” microconstruction, which led us to look at the use of similar constructions in the Napoleonic Code and how they are matched in its early-19th-century Dutch translation, as well as in the original texts and the Dutch translations of the early-19th-century French Criminal Code, the Code of Criminal Procedure and the Code of Civil Procedure. Complementing the PI’s and Co-I’s previous pioneering research in contrastive diachronic construction grammar this investigation added convincing demonstration of the explanatory potential of this novel approach in diachronic construction grammar. Objectives 4 and 5: All potential instantiations of a schematic deontic BE-Ven-to-inf construction were automatically extracted from the three components of the Corpus of Late Modern English Texts (CLMET) using MonoConc Pro 2.2 and subsequently manually sifted. The latter is a time-consuming task and due to the volume of the data generated, as well as the fact that the project coincided with the second and third year of the PI’s headship of the School of English, which meant a huge infringement on available research time, the documentation of the evolution of relevant microconstructions during the Late Modern English period did not progress as far as originally planned, but enough progress was made to be able to confirm the existence of a schematic deontic BE-Ven-to-inf construction, contributing significantly to the attainment of Objective 4 and supplying complementary corroboration of similar results of independent research which surfaced after the start of the project (Disney 2016). In order to reach partial achievement of Objective 5, a case study was carried out which zoomed in on the Late-Modern-English development of the microconstruction “be bound to” and revealed it to be conformant with the hypothesis of an attritional evolution of the deontic construction. As part of the investigation of its cause, this case study unavoidably led to a thorough treatment of the development of the “epistemic” “be bound to” construction as well, the results of which substantially fed into the critical reflections that contributed to the achievement of Objective 2. Objective 6: To the extent that the Dutch nominative-and-infinitive construction overlaps with the more schematic deontic geV-zijn-te construction, the historical evolution of the latter was also addressed by the research that went towards Objective 3. Time constraints and research priority issues of the Co-I, who as the Dutch linguist on the team was in charge of the Dutch data, prevented a more encompassing treatment of the geV-zijn-te construction. Objective 7: As a result of the state of the progress towards Objectives 5 and 6, insufficient data were available for collostructional analysis, so that Objective 7 could not be addressed. Reference: Disney, Steve. 2016. Another visit to BE SUPPOSED TO from a diachronic constructionist perspective. English Studies 97(8). 892–916.

748213.label: Major findings and research outcome
748213.value: The project has to date delivered two journal articles and two book chapters which make significant contributions to the study of the disappearance of grammatical constructions, and to usage-based diachronic construction grammar more generally. 1. A chapter in a volume on “Grammatical change in English world-wide” established that it is important to take variety and genre context into account when studying constructional attrition. It showed that while the schematic Modal Auxiliary construction is on the decline in data which are meant to be representative of American English generally, the construction recently became more frequent in American printed news publications. Hong Kong English data reveal exactly opposite trends. In the Hong Kong newspaper South China Morning Post the construction is declining, which stands in contrast to variety-as-a-whole evidence presented in earlier research, but is similar to what can be observed in British newspaper data. The chapter makes a methodological contribution in that it shows the usefulness of the online business information tool Factiva® for the investigation of recent developments in the frequency of use of constructions in certain genres. 2. A short article published in the Belgian Journal of Linguistics presents the state-of-the-art in the new field of diachronic construction grammar and makes a plea for a “radically usage-based” approach to constructional change through a contrast of two purportedly usage-based models of constructionalization. Such an approach should separate individual linguistic knowledge from languages as external systems, and disentangle innovation and conventionalization. It requires an onomasiological methodology as an alternative and/or complement to a semasiological one. 3. A more substantial article published in Lingua expands the argument for a radically usage-based approach and validates it through a detailed onomasiological, analogy-based account of how the pattern “be bound to” became a ‘participant-external/epistemic necessity’ microconstruction, as an alternative to seeing it as having evolved through reanalysis of the deontic “be bound to” construction, which would be the account dictated by the orthodox perspective on constructionalization in the grammaticalization-theoretical strand in diachronic construction grammar. 4. A book chapter included in a volume on “Cognitive Contact Linguistics” introduces the notion of “constructional renovation” as an important addition to constructional change phenomena that have been identified to date. It covers cases of halted or reversed constructional attrition through the influence of cognate constructions in another language in a contact situation, exemplified here with the survival of a Dutch nominative-and-infinitive microconstruction as a result of contact with French.

748213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
748213.value: The project has generated a huge amount of data which have so far remained unprocessed, specifically on the development of individual microconstructions instantiating the BE-Ven-to-inf schema. The plan is to continue with their processing so as to reach full achievement of Objective 5. The methodological repercussions of the “radically usage-based” approach developed in the course of the project could not be fully implemented in the data collection. A new project on constructional attrition phenomena that would consistently implement a radically usage-based perspective in its data collection methodology would be meaningful.

748213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
748213.value: While language change is often associated with the creation of new words and constructions, and their dissemination in a language community, words and constructions can also fall out of use again. This may appear less obvious in the case of grammatical constructions than in the case of words and until this project the phenomenon of “constructional attrition” had not been systematically investigated. This project looked at three groups of disappearing, or seemingly disappearing, constructions and situated the phenomenon of constructional attrition in an account of language change that puts the language user centre-stage, rather than “the language”. We found that while the core modal auxiliary construction may appear to be disappearing in data that make abstraction from contexts of use, it is surviving quite well in certain genres in some varieties of English. In a second study, the gradual disappearance of the construction “be bound to” as an expression of ‘obligation’ in the last 300 years was shown to be quite unrelated to speakers’ adoption of the same pattern for the expression of ‘certainty’. A third study showed that certain groups of speakers’ experience of similar constructions in another language will cause them to hold on to disappearing constructions.

Devising viable choice of law rules for the PRC and Hong Kong suited to their special conditions and needs that will attain the level of certainty and predictability, and preferably also uniformity of results, that will better protect reasonable and legitimate expectations of the parties concerned, and reduce current uncertainties that are inimical to the stability of their markets so as to enhance confidence in them. 748313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
748313.value: Where corporations and securities transactions cross borders, as they commonly do these days, domestic substantive laws no longer deal with the issues that arise adequately, putting these corporations and the wider business communities at risk. The issues are complicated by the fact that the laws of the jurisdictions of the world do not treat these corporations and transactions in the same way, giving rise to conflict of laws. This creates uncertainty that is of course inimical to the stability of the corporate, financial and securities markets. This study focuses on the cross border issues that arise out of corporations, and financial and securities transactions crossing the divide between the legal systems of the People's Republic of China (“PRC”) and Hong Kong. Following from the “one country, two systems” policy pursuant to which Hong Kong became part of the PRC on 1 July 1997, Hong Kong retains a separate legal system from the PRC, and its own conflict rules. In respect of the same dispute (as cases have demonstrated), a judge sitting in the PRC may come to a different conclusion from his brethren in Hong Kong. This is because the PRC conflict rules may direct the PRC judge to apply PRC law to the dispute and the Hong Kong judge to Hong Kong or some other law, and these laws do not treat the dispute the same way. The issues do not arise only in the PRC and Hong Kong of course. They do however arise (possibly) more frequently and in a different way because of the sheer volume of foreign investment they attract and the uniqueness of the PRC’s laws and systems. The uncertainties will seriously undermine investor confidence in the PRC and Hong Kong if not properly addressed. As Hong Kong and Shanghai are major financial centres with their links to other financial and securities systems, the uncertainties will also be inimical to the stability of corporate, financial and securities markets elsewhere. The recent joint venture between the Hong Kong, Shanghai and Shenzhen Exchanges for the development of financial products will lead to even more cross border activities and issues. The study’s premise is that the resolution of these issues lie in the development and harmonisation of the relevant choice of law rules, not the harmonisation of substantive laws and systems. It is this choice of law solution which this study seeks to achieve.

748313.label: Realisation of objectives
748313.value: All of the objectives have been achieved, possibly more. This notwithstanding that the project turned out to be more challenging than anticipated. This was in large part because of the difficulty of distilling the PRC position. The research found very limited consideration of the issues by courts, academics and others. Rules that exist are unclear, of uncertain scope and application and often inconsistent in related legislation. They also appear in legislation that are not immediately relevant. The absence of direct rules meant that there was a need to research wide and beyond the obvious. This was exacerbated by the difficulty in procuring judgements as the PRC does not have a system of reported judgements. This was both time-consuming and painstaking, but it has produced an outcome that exceeds that of the objective of identifying what is conflicting between the PRC and Hong Kong. Identification of the precise difficulties with distilling the PRC rules themselves is an important outcome that has to be taken into account before solutions can be devised for the PRC and Hong Kong. The Hong Kong rules, whilst less difficult to identify, also lack certainty and are underdeveloped in many areas. This is surprising and worrying given Hong Kong’s status as an international financial centre, and its considerably longer history of cross border transactions than the PRC. The research concludes that the Hong Kong rules do not provide a viable template for inter-regional harmonisation. As neither Hong Kong nor the PRC’s rules provide suitable or viable solutions consideration of solutions proposed or implemented elsewhere became of increased importance to the research. Here too the research concluded that none of these are themselves fully viable, but they have been more extensively considered than in Hong Kong and the PRC, providing fodder for analyses. The PI’s research into and analyses of the theoretical and practical underpinnings of these solutions has yielded an outcome that challenges the bases upon which choice-of-law has developed in these areas in the past century. It has sign-posted the way forward for solutions that are practically viable and theoretically coherent, not just for Hong Kong and the PRC but globally, an outcome that exceeds the objectives of this project. The PI is grateful for the extension of time given to complete the project because of the medical treatment that she was undergoing in the course of it.

748313.label: Major findings and research outcome
748313.value: 1. The PRC and Hong Kong’s choice-of-law rules are out of step with each other and those elsewhere in the areas of research 2. The PRC rules are uncertain and in many areas non-existent. Its private international law code is of uncertain scope and application in these areas, and complicated by inconsistent rules in other legislation that continue to apply. 3. Its rules on cross border corporate insolvency are particularly difficult to distil. The widely held view that PRC courts do not have the jurisdiction to wind up foreign companies (itself debatable) should not preclude development of choice-of-law rules on the myriad of other insolvency related issues. The PI has been approached by a PRC judge to assist in this. 4. Hong Kong’s choice-of-law rules whilst better established are nonetheless underdeveloped in relation to the areas of consideration, particularly those relating to corporations and securities. There is more judicial consideration in the area of cross border insolvency but even that is not without uncertainty, particularly in relation to the PRC. They would not be suited as a template for harmonisation. 5. There is probably the greatest argument for specific bilateral arrangement for insolvency as the treatment of insolvency, more so than corporations and securities, reflects national policies. The extent to which the treatment should be different where other jurisdictions are involved will need to be considered against the direction of such treatment in other major jurisdictions. 6. For corporations and securities there is greater argument for choice-of-law rules that do not distinguish amongst jurisdictions. The measures put in place for the Stock Connects between the PRC and Hong Kong fail to take into account that transactions through these systems involve more than PRC and Hong Kong securities and investors/financiers giving rise to uncertainties where they do. 7. No ready and viable solutions exist. Views remain divided on how these issues should be treated internationally. Neither the Hague nor the Geneva Securities Conventions provide viable global solutions or solutions that meet the requirements of the PRC and Hong Kong in relation to intermediated securities. There are good reasons not to ratify them. 8. The fragmented treatment of the issues is the reason why existing proposals will never be fully viable. Conversely convergence of the issues and rules will simplify and make for more coherent choice-of-law for corporations, securities and insolvency. This challenges the very basis upon which choice-of-law has developed in these areas but the PI has demonstrated that they are theoretically coherent and practically viable.

748313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
748313.value: The research has built a framework to pave the way for the development of more coherent and viable choice-of-law rules in these and related areas, not just for the PRC and Hong Kong, but globally. The PI intends to build upon the findings of this research to do just that, and to develop global solutions for a wider range of corporate, financial and securities dealings and the myriad of issues that remain unresolved in relation to corporate collapses and rescues. This will be undertaken over several years focussing in turn on specific areas and issues. The very recently launched (June 2019) Shanghai-London Stock Connect will be an important initial consideration as it brings the earlier Stock Connects to an international platform. Research into this new Stock Connect will build upon research commenced here in relation to the Stock Connects between the PRC and Hong Kong. It will consider, inter alia, the extent to which use of depository receipts in the Shanghai-London Stock Connect should distinguish it as a matter of choice-of-law. The impact of the further research will be extensive, and its findings critical to the continued viability of these new trading systems and instruments.

748313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
748313.value: The research has sign-posted the way forward for the resolution of issues arising out of cross border corporate, securities and financial transactions and insolvencies. The resolution of these issues will be important directly to the stability of the securities and financial markets of the PRC and Hong Kong, and indirectly to markets elsewhere. As the PRC and Hong Kong are the focus of transactions emanating from many jurisdictions the treatment of these issues is of critical importance beyond the PRC and Hong Kong. The research findings have also paved the way forward for the development of rules that treat these issues globally. The PI intends to build upon the findings of this research to develop global solutions for a wider range of corporate, financial and securities dealings and the myriad of issues that remain unresolved in relation to corporate collapses and rescues. The research is of importance both as a matter of development of the law and practical application. Its findings challenge the basis upon which choice-of-law has developed in these areas over the past century. The impact of the research will be extensive, and the findings critical to the continued viability of trading systems and instruments.

748413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
748413.value: In 1900 the Reverend E.J. Hardy complained, “a person who is only middle-aged feels quite antique at Hong Kong, not so much by reason of the enervating climate as because there are scarcely any old people in the colony. All leave … when still young.” An essential, though little studied, dimension of the history of empire in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries is the sociological fact of youth on the move. While ideas about youth influenced empire, youth and generation were more than mere idioms of empire. The making of empire within ‘epistemic’ European colonial communities was often a youthful pursuit. Late nineteenth century census records reveal 62% of British residents in Hong Kong were under age thirty in 1891, a pattern far from unusual in colonial Asia. From colonialists’ attempts to manage ‘youthful’ indigenous populations, to medical experts’ selections of ideal colonial bodies as biologically young, to commercial, military and administrative recruitment structures, age mattered profoundly in European entanglements with Asia in modern times. Remarkably, given the social and cultural significance of youth to empire, and the profound influence of empire upon age relations, historians have only addressed these histories tangentially. Scholars have tended to discuss ‘empire’ in terms of the Indian subcontinent and white dominions (or Algeria in Francophone research), assuming that “the empire that mattered was the countries of settlement” (Darwin, 2012, 292). An important consequence has been the failure to address the significance of youth to empire, and the influence of empire upon age relations. By turning our attention to non-settlement colonies, where youth was more prominent, this project highlights the cultural symbolism that developed around age, the social production of ‘seniority’ and ‘juniority,’ and the negotiation of youthful identities across empires. Adopting an innovative comparative, pan-imperial approach focusing upon British and French colonial centres in Asia, this project confronts the history of youth and age in Asia for the light it can shed upon the history of empire more generally. It examines how age formed a key ‘tension of empire’ and brings to light a series of social and cultural conflicts developing along generational fault-lines within highly mobile, transient and distinctively youthful communities in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. It aims to show how these tensions developed following the ‘great acceleration’ in a period marked by intellectual challenges to European colonial rule and the increasingly ominous military-strategic situation arising from the military expansion of Japan. 一九九零年 E.J. Hardy 牧師埋怨說：「一個中年人在香港感覺自己頗年老， 並不完全是因為令人衰弱的氣候，而是因為這殖民地幾乎沒有老人。所有人離開時…仍年青。」一個重要，但很少被研究的十九和二十世紀帝國歷史的層面，是青年人口不斷流動這個社會學上的事實。雖然有關青年的想法影響了帝國，青年和世代並不只是帝國的常用字。歐洲殖民社區中的帝國建成活動通常都是由年青人參與。 十九世紀後期的人口普查記錄顯示香港百份之六十二的英國居民都是三十歲以下，在殖民地的亞洲這是一個遠遠不尋常的現象。從殖民者嘗試管理「年青」原居民，到醫學專家挑選生理上年輕的人為理想的殖民者，到商業，軍事，和行政招聘架構，年齡在現代歐洲與亞洲的糾纏上是非常重要的。 值得注意的是，儘管青年在社會和文化方面對帝國很重要，而且帝國影響著不同年齡的人之間的關係，歷史學家對這些歷史的研究只是輕輕帶過。學者傾向以印度次大陸和白種人的領地（或阿爾及尼亞法語研究）這些用語去討論「帝國」，並假設「[歐洲人去]定居的國家是帝國重要的部份」(Darwin, 2012, 292)。這想法的一個重要後果是未能確立青年人對帝國的重要性，和帝國對不同年齡的人之間關係的影響。此計劃集中注意較多年輕人的非定居殖民地，以突出圍繞年齡，「資深」和「初級」的社會結果，和帝國間界定年青身份所發展出來的文化象徵。 通過採用一個創新比較和泛帝國的角度去集中研究英國和法國在亞洲的殖民地， 此計劃針對青年和年齡在亞洲的歷史，以更全面地揭示帝國歷史。這個計劃研究年齡如何造成關鍵的「帝國緊張關係」，並揭示一系列十九世紀後期和二十世紀初，在高流動，短暫多變，和特別地年青的社群間所發展出來的，在世代斷層間的社會和文化衝突。計劃的目的是展示這些緊張關係如何在「大加速」後，在一個歐洲殖民管治面對思想上的挑戰，和因日本軍事擴充而惡化的軍事戰略形勢的時期間發展出來。

748413.label: Realisation of objectives
748413.value: The project output was to constitute *two articles and a book *(of which the articles will constitute two chapters). I surpassed this output. I completed: 1. all research and 9 draft chapters of the book (output 1) 2. two chapters published in a very well reviewed book (output 2), 3. two chapters in a second book of which I am also sole editor (with Bloomsbury, forthcoming) (output 3), 4. a journal article submitted for review to a special issue with a major journal (output 4) 5. and another journal article submitted for review with the leading journal in my field (output 5). Output 1. Scholarly Monograph 'Young Colonials: How Mobile Youth Made Modern Empires'. Cambridge University Press have expressed a strong interest in publishing this work. Output 2. Introduction and Chapter 5 of Transnational Histories of Youth in the Twentieth Century (Introduction as "The Transnationality of Youth," (with Richard I. Jobs) chapter 5 as “Colonial Circulations: Vietnamese Youth, Travel and Empire, 1919-1940,” in Transnational Histories of Youth in the Twentieth Century ed. Richard Ivan Jobs and David M. Pomfret (Palgrave Macmillan, 2015), 115-43 ISBN: 9781137469892 (output 3) Output 3. *Two* chapters in a second book, of which I am sole editor, entitled Youth in the Age of Empire. I secured a contract to publish the volume with Bloomsbury. It contains an introductory chapter written solely by myself, and a chapter entitled 'Spaces and Places' written solely by myself, and 9 other essays contributed by leading scholars in the field. (A Cultural History of Youth in the Age of Empire, as sole editor, under contract with Bloomsbury) Output 4. I completed “Imperial Rejuvenations: Youth, Age and Degeneration in Tropical Asia, 1830-1914 ” and this article is under review with The Journal of Social History, as part of a special issue on ‘Rejuvenation’ Output 5. I completed “Empires of Emotion: Youth, Leprosy and Imperial Danger,” which is under review with Journal of History of Childhood and Youth. Other outputs: In 2017, 'I won the 'Grace Abbott Book Prize'; in 2016 I won the Faculty Research Output Prize. In various ways, these books, chapters and articles all accomplish the objectives set out above in that it re-examines the history of European empire through the lens of age and generation, across colonial centres and networks of empire, examines the significance of youth and empire to the (re)fashioning of identities, and the mobility of youth, and nuances histories of youth and histories of empire focusing upon settlement colonies. Attempts to Overcome Problems - Output 1. the scholarly monograph would have been with the publisher already if I had been able to take sabbatical leave to finish writing up the manuscript as planned. However, instead, I was made chair of the Department of History at a critical time in 2015. This was something I could not turn down. And, at the conclusion of my appointment as chair I was then appointed Head of School. I could not turn down either of these important leadership roles, but they prevented my steering the book into print. Not only did I take on an extraordinarily heavy administrative load - often taking responsibility for serving as chair, Research Postgraduate coordinator and Undergraduate coordinator *together* at the same time, but in addition to this, I won the UGC Teaching Excellence Award in 2012. Thus I faced the challenge of completing this $500,000 UGC Teaching Excellence project from 2013-2016 - at the exact same time as completing my GRF project *and* taking on the Chairmanship of my department, *and* teaching among the heaviest teaching loads in terms of student enrolments of any teacher in my department. Nevertheless, in the end as I hope you may see I not only achieved the specified GRF project outputs (1 draft monograph, 2 articles), I *vastly* exceeded these outputs - 1 draft monograph, 2 articles under review, 2 edited books (1 published, 1 under review), 4 chapters (2 in each edited volume). In addition to this I won two major book prizes, gave 3 keynote lectures and a string of other conference presentations related to the project, and the outputs published to date have garnered highly favourable reviews.

748413.label: Major findings and research outcome
748413.value: The project has the archival depth and conceptual breadth that enables it to break the bounds of the kind of Indo-centric empire history that – despite lots of calls for new transnational imperial narratives – still predominates for the modern period. The youth theme allows movement in and out of all kinds of questions, from governmentality to hygiene to sex to demographic change. The comparative colonialism method is a major strength and contribution of the project. Ranging freely and authoritatively across multiple cities and spheres of influence requires an impressive command of the various literatures upon which both the regions and the youth theme touch. The project uses youth as a lens through which to understand cultures and processes of European imperialism from the 19th century up to the second world war. Reviewers of 'Transnational Histories of Youth' noted that it "answered Akira Iriye’s call for a study of youth and transnationality" by setting forth arguments "that the history of modern youth is inherently transnational, characterised by mobility, rapidity and connectedness." (Briony Nelson, review in Modern and Contemporary France), "these essays offer substantial insight into how young people variously functioned as emblems and agents of modernity, reconstruction, national identity, mobility and hybridity." Another reviewer advised, following a "logically structured and theoretically insightful introduction ... Jobs and Pomfret’s collection adds important new pieces to the historiographical puzzle and greatly enhances our understanding of the reciprocities of the histories of modern youth and modern globalization."(Mischa Honeck, Journal of the History of Childhood and Youth)

748413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
748413.value: Imperial history is unavoidably comparative in nature, but most scholarly discussions of empire, like so much else, take place within the confines of a single (nations) empire. The occasional comparative exception typically foregrounds one among the case studies engaged, drawing on the others to illuminate the central subject’s claims to our attention. This project is unusual if not unique in its systematic engagement with British and French cultures of youth under colonial conditions. Along these same lines, this project advanced scholarly efforts to illuminate the channels through which ideas and people travelled back and forth between Europe the colonized world. These connections were not limited to the ties binding metropolitan Europe to a colony. The publications arising from the project also illuminated overlapping connections: between French and British colonies in Asia, between British and French ideas about youth more generally and youth practices in British and French colonies more specifically. Relying on a wide range of published and archival sources, they have illuminated how metropolitan and colonial discourses and practices relating to youth intersected and interacted, and how their articulation changed over time.

748513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
748513.value: Like expertise in any education domain, surgical expertise is highly valued. The multifaceted nature of the surgical profession and reductions to doctors working hours poses a time management challenge for educators. Current time allocated to technical skills training is insufficient to adequately prepare trainees for the demands of the operating theatre; however, it is unlikely that more time will be earmarked for training in an already bulging curriculum. Instead surgical educators must ensure best use of the limited time available. Developing empirically-based training interventions is more achievable once markers of surgical expertise are identified and understood within established theoretical frameworks of motor learning. Electroencephalography (EEG) provides an objective means of identifying neuropsychological markers of psychomotor efficiency that are exhibited by surgical specialists. In precise motor skills outside the surgical domain the psychomotor efficiency of expertise is reasonably well defined. Nonessential activity of the brain region associated with verbal-analytical activity is reduced and/or the region’s communication with motor planning areas is attenuated; consistent with stage models of motor learning. It remains unclear if surgical expertise is defined by the same refinement of brain activity or how common intra-operative stressors might impinge on psychomotor efficiency. The extent to which established training curricula develop psychomotor efficiency is also unknown. Once neuropsychological markers of expertise are identified, the design of training interventions can be tailored toward the attainment of these markers. Ordinarily, individuals cannot reliably change their brainwave patterns because they lack awareness of them; however, EEG software allows the online presentation of neurofeedback. Theoretically, this technology can be used to promote self-regulation of brain activity during actual practice of a technical skill. Potentially, neurofeedback training provides an elegant means of expediting surgical skills training. We propose a series of studies that will a) identify neuropsychological markers of psychomotor efficiency exhibited by surgical specialists, b) investigate changes in psychomotor efficiency caused by the introduction of common intra-operative stressors, c) evaluate the psychomotor efficiency of trainees who have attained current expert-derived markers of technical skill proficiency, and d) examine online EEG neurofeedback as a means to train psychomotor efficiency of technical skills. The findings will have significant implications for the science of surgical skills education and for the subsequent performance of surgical procedures in a clinical setting. 與任何教育領域的專業技術 一樣，外科專業技 術亦受到高度重視。基於外科專 業的多層面性質及醫生工作時數縮減，這對教育工作者 構成一個時間管理的挑戰。現時 分配於專業技術能培訓的 時間不足，讓學員難以應付手術室的需求；可是，在已經膨脹的課程中不太可能增加時間。反而外科教育工作者 必須確保 充分 利用有限的培訓時間。在已建立運動學習理論框架內，一旦識別和認識外科專業技術的標記，將更容易實現以經驗為本的培訓措施。腦電波儀 (EEG) 提供了一個客觀的方法用於識別外科專家精神運動效率之神經心理 標記。對於外科領域以的精確運動技能，人們已將其專業知識的精神運動效能，合理而清楚地解釋了。大腦 非必要的，但與言語分析相關活動減少，及／或該大腦區域的運動規劃通訊減弱，都符合運動學習階段 的模型。外科手術的專業水平是否能顯示大腦活動的能力，或者大腦公共內部操作的壓力怎樣影響著人的精神運動效能，目前仍未弄清楚。一旦識別專業技術的標記，培訓措施的設計 便能夠 向獲得這些標記為前題來定制。通常，個人缺乏腦電波模式的意識，因此不能確實地改變他們的腦電波模式 ；但是，EEG軟件 容許神經反饋的在線呈現。理論上，這項技術能應用於提高實際運用專業技能上的腦部活動之自我調節。神經反饋培訓有潛在提供促進外科技能培訓的講究方式 。我們建議一系列的研究可以： a）識別外科專家的精神運動效率之經心理標記， b） 研究由共同內部操作刺激源而產生的精神運動效率改變， c）評估已獲得目前來源於專家技術能效率的標記的學員之精神活動效率， d）考察 在線 EEG神經反饋的方法用於訓練技術能神經運動效率。研究結果將對外科技能教育科學及在臨床情境下的一系列外科程序績效有 著重大的意義。

748913.label: Project Title(Chinese)
748913.value: 美國海嘯式的援助: 日本1923大地震災難後的同情，機會主義和錯覺

748913.label: Project Objectives
748913.value: Promote our understanding of how a major post-disaster humanitarian relief effort can be used to illuminate politics, diplomacy, and international relations and help us better comprehend the political aims and objectives of contemporary post-disaster relief initiatives. Document how and why the newspapers in America and within the Japanese-American communities dramatized the disaster and amplified the notion that an unparalleled opportunity existed to further political, social, economic, and even religious goals. Explore how and why the newly sworn-in president, Calvin Coolidge, State Department officials, and Navy leaders saw opportunity following disaster and believed that a successful public relief effort could be parlayed into improved diplomatic relations during a turbulent, racially-charged moment revolving around emigration and trans-Pacific affairs. Document and explain why anti-Japanese groups such as the Ku Klux Klan, the American Legion, and various jingoistic, anti-Japanese newspapers on the American west coast advocated generous donations to Japan as a way to lessen the likelihood that greater numbers of Japanese would attempt to emigrate to American as much of eastern Japan lay in ruins. Examine the opportunities that businesses and religious organizations saw in post earthquake Japan and document how this influenced patterns of collection and giving across America. Explore how the Japanese language press in America packaged an independent disaster relief effort as a chance to demonstrate patriotism and love of the mother country and document how this influenced patterns of giving. Illuminate how and why the independent dōhō relief effort caused great fissures between local Japan Associations and Japanese consulates throughout the West Coast of America.

748913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
748913.value: This research project aims to transform our understanding of one of the largest American-led humanitarian relief effort that followed a natural disaster in the pre-WWII era: assistance to Japan after the disastrous 1923 Great Kantō Earthquake. While recent publications analyze Japan’s unprecedented disaster from the perspective of Japanese history (Borland 2006, 2009; Kitahara, 2011, Schencking 2006, 2008, 2009, 2013), art history (Wiesenfeld 2012), and literature (Bates 2010), no study exists in any language that explores the tsunami of aid that followed in the calamity’s wake. This scholarly lacuna is surprising given the fact that the relief effort—like the disaster itself—was unprecedented. In less than two months, Americans gave roughly $US 21.5 million in cash and commodities to stricken Japan; more than all other nations combined. As a percentage of GDP, Americans gave more in 1923 than they did in total to all nations affected by the 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami. Remarkably, more money was given to Japan in inflation-adjusted dollars than the American Red Cross collected and the US Congress appropriated for relief following the 1906 San Francisco Earthquake (Fradkin, 2005). The generosity directed toward Japan raises important questions that my project will answer: Why Did Americans give so much and what did they hope to accomplish through giving? Why did president Calvin Coolidge, the State Department, and navy officials take such an active part in public relief campaigns? Why did American Legion branches, and rabidly anti-Japanese newspapers, and even Ku Klux Klan chapters run—and be seen to lead—“Save Japan” campaigns? Why did Japanese-American communities reject Japanese consular requests to give aid directly to the American Red Cross and instead establish independent dōhō [brethren] collection funds that garnered US$ 2 million? Politics, I hypothesize, played a fundamental role behind the establishment of well-organized and highly visible “Save Japan” campaigns. Perceived political opportunities likewise influenced patterns of giving. Each major aid organizer and often those who gave, hoped to accomplish objectives that resonated with and reflected larger political, ideological and economic pursuits that shaped American politics and Japanese-American relations. When published, my findings will not only alter the way we understand diplomacy, humanitarianism, and early twentieth century Japanese-American relations, but it will also historicize a point made by The Economist in 2005 and scholars who investigate post-disaster humanitarianism today: namely, that despite the lofty rhetoric of compassion, politics influence virtually every aspect of disaster relief (Ching 2005; Nishikawa 2005; Williams 2006). 此研究計劃的目標是改變我們對第二次世界大戰前其中一個最大型，由美國領導，針對自然災害的人道援助計劃的認知: 在1923年關東大地震後對日本的援助。近期出版的文章和書籍從日本史(Borland 2006, 2009; Kitahara, 2011; Schencking 2006, 2008, 2009, 2013), 藝術史 (Wiesenfeld 2012), 和文學 (Bates 2010) 的角度分析這日本前所未見的災難，但未有任何語言的研究探討災後如海嘯般的援助。 這片學術上的空白是出乎意料的，因為此規模的救災援助—正如這災難一樣— 都是前所未見的。 美國人在少於兩個月內捐出約二千一百五十萬美元的現金和物資給正受災的日本；超過所有其他國家捐獻的總和。以全國生產總值計算，美國人在1923年捐出的，比他們在2004年南亞海嘯後捐給所有受災國家的更多。值得注意的是，在考慮通漲因素後，捐給日本的金額，比1906年三藩市地震後美國紅十字會籌得的金額和美國國會撥出的援助更多 (Fradkin, 2005)。 我的計劃會解答美國對日本的慷慨引申出來的疑問：為甚麼美國人會捐出此高額，他們希望捐獻會達成甚麼結果？為甚麼美國總統柯立芝 (Calvin Coolidge)，國務院，和海軍官員踴躍地參與公眾救災運動？為甚麼美國退伍軍人會支部，狂熱地反日的報章，甚至連三K黨(Ku Klux Klan) 都進行—和公開地領導—「拯救日本」運動？ 為甚麼美籍日裔社區拒絕日本領事要他們直接捐助給美國紅十字會的要求，反而設立獨立的弟兄(dōhō)集資，並籌得二百萬美元? 我推測政治在這場有組織和高曝光率的「拯救日本」運動中擔當根本的角色。同樣地，捐助者認為捐助會帶來的政治機會也影響了他們捐助的方式。每一個主要的援助發起人，以及往往捐獻者，都希望用捐獻達到各種目標。這些目標緊扣著塑造美國政治和美日關係的政治，意識形態和經濟活動。我的研究結果在出版後不但會改變我們對外交，人道主義，和二十世紀初美日關係的認知；更能把《經濟學人》在二零零五年，以及現時研究災後人道主義的學者所提出的觀點歷史化：儘管同情的聲音很響亮，政治影響著救災工作的幾乎所有方面 (Ching 2005; Nishikawa 2005; Williams 2006) 。

749313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
749313.value: 本項目考察瑪利亞信仰在十七世紀中國的發展和演變。研究重點集中在超德、異蹟與欽崇這三個核心概念，以及三者如何緊密關聯、相互作用，促成瑪利亞形象在帝制晚期中國語境中的重構。通過對大量宗教敘事、聖像乃至崇拜行為的分析，本研究將深入探討以下議題：天主教傳教士如何附會儒家的道德理想，將瑪利亞塑造成一個新的德行表率；瑪利亞如何與本土女神在信仰的正統性和靈異能力上展開競爭；瑪利亞如何成為家庭崇拜的中心；信眾如何借助形式化的禮儀和祈禱構建一種新的集體身份認同。瑪利亞信仰在教義、文學藝術、崇拜行為等方面的流行，對明清之際基督教在中國的本土化有積極促進作用，使其從一個外來宗教轉變成為一個邊緣型的中國宗教。 本項目既包括前人研究中常用的文獻，同時也將很多此前鮮有關注的文本、視像資料納入考察範圍。對這些文獻資料的多角度分析，有助於進一步審視某些重要的議題。在十七世紀中國興起的瑪利亞信仰，不論是私人場合還是公開場合，都顯示出一種行為先於教義的模式，恰與歐洲瑪利亞信仰發展過程中教義先於行為的主導模式相對。傳教士用大量中文著述塑造了一個多面性的瑪利亞形象，然而他們對於中國人的俗世化崇拜傾向一直持有戒心。更複雜的是，精英信徒和普通信徒對瑪利亞採取了不同的解讀模式：前者強調新的瑪利亞表率形象在教義及道德層面的正統角色，而後者則更強調瑪利亞的靈異能力，以期建立一種新的女神信仰傳統。這些因素錯綜交織，最終促成了明清以降直至現代歷久不衰的中華聖母崇拜文化。 上述議題將被置於一個互動–交流的歷史語境下進行考察。經過傳教士的引介，歐洲的瑪利亞信仰成為中國信徒組建聖母會的原型。同時，中國的聖母會也利用並吸納了儒教、佛教善會機構的某些固有模式，從而影響到瑪利亞信仰在十七世紀晚期的儀式化進程。此外，瑪利亞與本土女神（尤其是觀音菩薩）的相互借用效仿，導致信仰模式的混合傾向，其後更成為日本教徒在受迫害期間所秘密崇拜的瑪利亞觀音的一個源頭。瑪利亞信仰的跨文化流動，為進一步考察近世基督教穿越宗教邊際的傳播開啟了諸多可能。

749313.label: Realisation of objectives
749313.value: Since I carried out this research project, I have engaged in intense work in data collection, critical analysis, and scholarly writings. Up to now, almost all the objectives have been realized through my committed efforts and continuous achievements. In the early stage of my research, I collected a large number of primary and secondary sources. I found many key Marian texts and images available in facsimile editions and online databases, such as João da Rocha’s Song nianzhu guicheng 誦念珠規程 (Rules for Reciting the Rosary, c. 1619), Alfonso Vagnone’s Shengmu xingshi 聖母行實 (Biography of the Holy Mother, 1631) Giacomo Rho’s Shengmu jingjie 聖母經解 (Exegetical Explanations of the Hail Mary, 1632), and Ludovico Buglio’s Shengmu xiao rike 聖母小日課 (Officium parvum beatae Mariae Virginis, 1676). Meanwhile, I made several research trips to Europe, Russia, and Mainland China to study and reproduce some rare manuscripts that have long been neglected in previous research. They include Niccolò Longobardo’s Shengmu dexu daowen 聖母德敘禱文 (Prayer on the Virtues of the Holy Mother, c. 1625), Giulio Aleni’s Shengmu Meiguijing shiwu duan 聖母玫瑰經十五端圖像 (Fifteen Illustrations of the Mysterious Rosary, 1637), Juan Bautista’s Shengmu rike 聖母日課 (Psalterium majus beatae Mariae Virginis, 1698), etc. I also identified some lesser known Marian prayers and exegeses in the compilations of Chinese Christian texts, e.g., Thomas Mayor’s Shengmu xingji daowen 聖母行蹟禱文 (Prayers on the Acts of the Holy Mother) from Nianjing zongdu 念經總牘 (Corpus of Prayers, 1628) and Francesco Brancati’s Shengmu jingjie 聖母經解 from Tianshen huike 天神會課 (Duties of the Congregation of the Guardian Angels, c. 1673), etc. In addition, I collected and studied numerous Marian texts by Chinese converts as well as the non-believers. The former group includes Xu Guangqi 徐光啟, Yang Tingyun 楊廷筠, Zhu Yupu朱毓僕 in the late Ming period and Zhang Xingyao 張星曜, Wu Li 吳歷, He Shizhen 何世貞in the early Qing period. They mostly contributed eulogistic and apologetic writings on Mary. The latter group includes uninterested literati and anti-Christian figures, who produced a variety of cultural representations containing misidentified or distorted images of Mary. In the early months of 2015, I visited some Catholic churches, seminaries, and institutions in several cities in Mainland China, including Chengdu and Leshan in Sichuan, Taiyuan and Xinjiang in Shanxi, and Baoji, Fengxiang, and Xi’an in Shaanxi. Most Catholic communities in these cities have been established as early as in the 17th century. I conducted a series of interviews with local priests, nuns and sworn virgins, and senior church members, from whom I recorded abundant personal and collective memories on the history of a local church and the recent development of a Catholic community. The abundant textual and visual sources that I collected through different channels enabled me to explore how Chinese Marian devotions emerged and evolved into a religious movement in the 17th century. I have carefully studied the key sources collected, whether a popular Marian prayer, a reproduced Marian image, a Mariological treatise, or a folktale of Mary, so as to capture the vital mechanisms and crucial factors in the phenomenal rise of a Chinese Marian culture in late imperial China. While conducting more in-depth critical analysis, I devoted myself to scholarly writings on this subject. The major research outputs include two journal articles (one forthcoming in 2018 and the other under preparation) and four conference papers. They reflect a group of separate but interrelated case studies, in which I develop a number of new and sophisticated arguments on the following key issues: how Nestorian and Franciscan missionaries in the Tang and the Yuan times made the earliest known attempts to introduce Mary to China, how Catholic missionaries (especially the Jesuits) in the 17th century made strategic efforts to present a composite image of Mary and promote her as the new model of womanhood tied with Confucian moral norms, how the Chinese people made multilayered responses to and reinterpretations of this prominent Christian icon, how the elite and ordinary converts developed class-based discourses in their devotions to Mary, and how Mary was turned into a deified figure comparable to popular native goddesses in private and communal worships. By carefully examining varied types of examples, I can reconstruct a dynamic interplay of three key factors—virtue, miracle, and faith—that have constituted the remodeling of Mary in the late imperial Chinese context. The last objective of the project is to publish a monograph and present a comprehensive study on the rise of a Chinese Marian culture, as compared to the research on the other major Marian devotions in global history. Using all the key sources and summing up the important arguments in the previous research outputs, I am now about to complete most parts in the major chapters of the draft book manuscript. In fact, two publishers have contacted me recently asking my intention for publication. I have decided to publish my monograph with the Ricci Institute for Chinese-Western Cultural History at the University of Southern California, a leading research institute in this field, as part of its newly launched project “Historical Legacies of Christianity in East Asia” in collaboration with Brill Academic Publishers in the Netherlands. I will prepare a complete book manuscript for the peer reviews soon, and then secure a book contract with the Ricci Institute. I am confident that this cutting-edge monograph study will make noticeable contributions to future research on this important yet largely underexplored subject.

749313.label: Major findings and research outcome
749313.value: This research project presents several important findings that have not been fully digested in previous scholarship. They are listed and briefly explained as follows: 1. The Catholic missionaries and Chinese converts made continuous efforts to advocate Marian devotions in 17th-century China. In their visual representations, prayers, theological works, and devotional activities, they endeavored to create a composite image of Mary that could meet both Catholic standards for the Mother of God and Confucian expectations of ideal womanhood. (see “The Many Faces of Our Lady” and “From Perpetual Virgin to Queen Mother” in Part C) 2. There appeared multilayered Chinese representations and reinterpretations of Mary, often embedded with a self-other paradox or a Sinocentric mindset. They were created not just for propagation of Christian-Confucian syncretism, or for a total rejection of Christianity as an evil religion. Some descriptions on Mary rather carried a distinct in-between feature, showing how the Chinese writers tried their own ways to make sense of this prominent Christian icon introduced by the missionaries from the West. It is not surprising to see that Mary went through a process of displacement and distortion in their representations and became a deified figure comparable to a Bodhisattva or an immortal in native religious beliefs. (see “The Many Faces of Our Lady” in Part C) 3. The leading Confucian converts composed many refined literary pieces to advocate the model image of Mary. They marked a distinct character of the elite discourse that repeatedly underlined Mary’s exemplary virtues of purity, virginity, and benevolence in connection with the Confucian concept of moralistic orthodoxy. In contrast, the lower-class Chinese converts developed a different tendency. They more frequently used a register of terms to affirm the great power and other divine attributes of Mary in miraculous healing and protection. These different discourses suggest a class-based division among elite and commoners in the early development of Chinese Marian devotions. 4. Due to the lack of a doctrinal foundation and the direct control under church authorities, the missionaries in China mainly focused on the introduction of key Marian dogmas by way of simply prayers and catechetical texts. They meanwhile promoted or supported various kinds of devotional activities among the converts. As a result, early Chinese devotions to Mary, whether in private or public, revealed a practice-oriented pattern in contrast with the prevailing doctrine-based tradition in medieval Europe.

749313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
749313.value: There are two potential areas for further development of the current research. The first may be an expansion of the time span, namely, to examine the later development of Chinese Marian devotions from 1700 to 1840. I am particularly interested in research on how the new Chinese cult of Mary could survive such a difficult period known for suppression of Christianity by the Qing government. The study may be compared with the Maria Kannon worship of the kakure kirishitan (hidden Christians), under the suppression of the Tokugawa shogunate over a period of two centuries. The second potential area may be the compilation of a multivolume collection of Chinese Marian texts through China’s late imperial period. It will present a broad coverage, including not only Catholic texts from the 17th to the 19th centuries but also Russian Orthodox texts during the 19th century. Since these primary sources are mostly scattered, and some are not accessible to scholars and general readers, this collection will provide them an opportunity to gain solid knowledge of the original texts and conduct further research. It may also serve as a companion reader for my book and other studies on this subject.

749313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
749313.value: This research project explores the early development of Chinese Marian devotions in the 17th century. By examining a variety of texts, images, and devotional activities, I will uncover how Catholic missionaries made strategic efforts to create a composite image of Mary and promote Mary as a new model of virtues tied with Confucian moral ideals, how Mary competed with native Chinese deities for religious orthodoxy and miraculous power, how Mary was venerated in private and communal worship, and how Marian piety in face of anti-Christian criticisms became a bond to consolidate the collective identity of the Chinese coverts. I will also highlight the dynamic interplay of three key factors—virtue, miracle, and faith—that constituted the remodeling of Mary in the late imperial Chinese context. Along with the manifold and changing representations, Mary was turned into an ever-virgin, a filial daughter, a caring and merciful mother, a noble lady, and above all these, a powerful mediatrix between God and man. Her image embodied an all-inclusive list of attributes tied with Christian spirituality and Confucian morality, thereby giving shape to a persistent Chinese Marian culture during and after the 17th century.

749413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
749413.value: Building on my past work, I will provide a detailed and comprehensive philosophical and ethical analysis of terrorism, arguing that terrorism can be justified under certain narrowly circumscribed circumstances. I will proceed by first developing a definition of terrorism that is intuitive, fits the empirical facts, and avoids double standards. A central feature of that definition is that it makes the intentional severe violation of rights part of the meaning of “terrorism.” A paradigmatic example of such rights violations is the killing of the innocent. However, I will also examine what I call “pseudo-terrorism”: acts that under my definition are not terrorism at all but that many other authors (and politicians) would nonetheless label “terrorism.” I then will distinguish four different broad potential justifications of terrorism, and reject two of them while accepting two others, namely lesser evil and necessity. My focus will be on the latter (which is also used in law as a defense for rights violations or infringements). I will then systematically deal with a host of objections that have been leveled against the justifiability of terrorism. I demonstrate that all these objections fail to show that terrorism is absolutely impermissible under realistic circumstances. Finally, I will demonstrate that even conventional war is much closer to terrorism than many would like to believe, and that this insight should inform our attitudes towards war and armed conflict. The findings of this study are relevant not only for our discourse about terrorism, terrorists, war, and just war theory, but also for broader issues like political legitimacy, utilitarianism, fairness, reciprocity, and the vexed question, which has recently drawn renewed attention in the legal literature, of whether it can ever be justified to kill innocent people if this is necessary to save others. 藉助于我之前的研究工作，我將會對恐怖主義展開周詳的哲學、倫理學分析，并論證在某些嚴格限定的情景中，恐怖主義在道德上是可辯護的。我將首先給出對恐怖主義的定義，這個定義不僅直觀，符合經驗事實，而且避免雙重標準。按照此定義，蓄意嚴重侵害他人權利是恐怖主義的重要構成部份。這種權利侵害的典型例子是殺害無辜。然而，我同樣會檢驗我稱之為“偽恐怖主義”的行為，這種行為按我的定義不算是恐怖主義，但很多作者（以及政客）卻仍給其貼上“恐怖主義”的標籤。接著，我將區分四種對恐怖主義的不同辯護策略，駁斥其中兩種，并接受另外兩種，即訴諸于“兩權相害取其輕”原則以及“必要性”原則。但我會集中關注訴諸“必要性”原則的策略（在法律中，該原則也被用於為侵權辯護）。隨後，我會系統地檢視列針對恐怖主義之可辯護性的一系列反對意見，并論證所有這些反對意見都無法表明恐怖主義在現實情景中下是絕對不可接受的。最後，我將論證即便是常規戰爭都比人們想像的更靠近恐怖主義；這一點應該觀照我們對于戰爭與武裝衝突的正確態度。這項研究的發現不僅關乎我們關於恐怖主義、恐怖分子、戰爭以及正義戰爭理論的論說，也關乎其他一些大的議題，例如政治正當性、效用主義、公平原則、交互原則，以及一個長期以來爭議不斷的問題。這個問題最近在法律文獻中又引起了新的關注，它便是：如果為了救其他人的生命而必須殺害一個無辜的人，這種行為在道德上是否是可辯護的？

749413.label: Realisation of objectives
749413.value: The project’s objectives have been to 100 % achieved; in fact, I have produced and achieved significantly more than I had originally announced. I have written 20 papers during the time of the current GRF project, which amounts altogether to more than 220,000 words, while I had originally announced merely a 75,000 words book. Thus, I made excellent use of the funding and of the time provided by it. Many of the research results are expressed in the published, forthcoming, or submitted papers (15 of the 20 papers mentioned above); others will be published in my new book project. To wit, while I had originally planned to publish a separate book on the current GRF project, I have realized that it is strategically wiser and more fruitful to integrate this research into a much larger and ambitious project I am currently working on during my sabbatical, namely into my opus magnum provisionally entitled Just War Theory and the Ethics of Violence: Foundations and Applications. (There will be a symposium on this manuscript at the Centre for Applied Philosophy and Public Ethics of the Charles Sturt University, Canberra, Australia, in April 2016.) This project partly draws on, but goes far beyond, my past GRF project “Self-Defense, Real Wars, and the Moral Equality of Combatants,” my past Seed funded project “Unconventional Warriors: Guerrillas, Warlords, Mercenaries, and Robots,” and the project “Ethics and Terrorism: The Philosophical Debate,” on which I am reporting here. My aim is to write a comprehensive book on just war theory and the ethics of violence that is impossible to ignore and will be a standard reference for years to come. Therefore, I have used the time to also write on a number of basic questions of just war theory beyond the terrorism debate, including the definition of self-defense, different justifications of self-defense, the imminence condition of self-defense, and the liability of justified combatants. Obviously, I have also written on all the issues squarely concerning the ethics of terrorism – for instance on the necessity and the lesser evil justification, rights forfeiture and reciprocity, just cause and right intention, punishment, prospects of success, the doctrine of double effect, proportionality, and legitimate authority.

749413.label: Major findings and research outcome
749413.value: 1. I have undertaken analyses of the necessity and the lesser evil justification. These analyses show that terrorism can in principle be justified. They also show that such justifications need not rely on any “fundamentalist” conceptions but are instead readily available in Western liberal law and philosophy. I also demonstrate that all absolutist counter-arguments against the justifiability of torture fail. 2. Simultaneously, I have demonstrated the erroneousness of so-called “combined lesser evil/liability justifications”. 3. My analysis of the self-defense justification shows that it is not applicable to the case of terrorism. In other words, there is no self-defense justification for terrorism. 4. However, my analysis of self-defense, with its emphasis on the imminence condition, shows that, conversely, counter-terrorist measures can also rarely (almost never) be justified under an appeal to self-defense. They can be more easily justified under an appeal to necessity; but such a justification is more restrictive than self-defense. 5. My analyses of the just war criteria of just cause, right intention, legitimate authority, prospects of success, last resort, and proportionality show that terrorism can satisfy all these criteria. 6. My analyses of terrorism, torture, and war show that conventional war is much closer to torture and terrorism than many Western politicians and just war theorists would like to believe.

749413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
749413.value: As already stated, this project will form part of my project entitled Just War Theory and the Ethics of Violence: Foundations and Applications. Thus, my research on terrorism will both inform this larger project and profit from the research undertaken in its context. Being part of this larger project will also increase the visibility of my project on terrorism.

A central feature of that definition is that it makes the intentional severe violation of rights part of the meaning of “terrorism.” I systematically deal with a host of objections that have been leveled against the justifiability of terrorism. I demonstrate that all these objections fail to show that terrorism is absolutely impermissible under realistic circumstances. Finally, I demonstrate that even conventional war is much closer to terrorism than many would like to believe, and that this insight should inform our attitudes towards war and armed conflict. Thus, far from endorsing violence (but also without outright condemning it), I urge a less self-deceptive attitude towards it. It comprises of four levels of institutional requirements of ROL arranged in a coherent and interconnected manner. To develop an analytical framework on the cultural requirements of ROL by mapping out the specific values, attitudes, beliefs, orientations of the legal culture rule needed for the smooth operation of ROL institutions of each level of ROL. 749513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
749513.value: Rule of Law (“ROL”) is considered to be the cornerstone of Hong Kong’s success. There have been comments that ROL in Hong Kong is not performing as well as before in recent years. Explanations need to be sought so that remedies can be made. A more comprehensive understanding about ROL reveals that it has both institutional and cultural dimensions. It is difficult for legal institutions to achieve its designed purposes and to maintain ROL without a supporting legal culture. Our research question is to assess the performance of the legal institutions in Hong Kong in satisfying the requirements of ROL and how far the general public of Hong Kong possesses the cultural values required for the maintenance and development of ROL in Hong Kong. To ascertain the actual state of ROL in Hong Kong, inquiring into the legal institutions in Hong Kong is necessary but not sufficient. An understanding of the legal culture in Hong Kong is also essential. Our understanding of the legal culture of Hong Kong remains inadequate. An assessment in the form of expert comments to ascertain the performance of ROL institutions in Hong Kong and a survey in the form of questionnaires to investigate the legal culture of Hong Kong will be conducted. The aim is not to conduct an opinion poll of how the people of Hong Kong rate our legal system but to uncover the knowledge, beliefs, values, attitudes and expectations of the people of Hong Kong towards the different aspects of our legal system which are central to the maintenance of ROL in Hong Kong. The results of both the assessment and the surveys will be analyzed to determine the nature of the relationship, if any, between the performance of institutions and culture of ROL can then be articulated. The key strength of the research team is that we have members with legal training who have an established record in research on ROL and legal culture and members who have rich experience in conducting empirical research using social survey methods and data. Legal knowledge will be critical to designing a comprehensive and meaningful questionnaire on legal culture together with the experts in social survey. The knowledge gained from the study of the popular legal culture of Hong Kong as a Chinese society may also provide insights by identifying cultural categories for conducting similar research in other Chinese societies. 法治被視為香港成功的基石。但有意見認為香港法治近年的情況未及以前面。我們必須尋出原因並尋求補救方法。更全面對法治的認知指出法治包含了體制及文化兩個方面。法治體制若缺乏相配應的法治文化，它們將難以發運作用。我們的研究計劃是要評估香港法治體制是否符合法治的要求，並香港的普羅市民是否擁有相配應的法治文化以維持香港的高手平法治及讓它能進一步發展。 要了解香港法治的情況，單單是研究法治體制是需要但卻是不足的。要了解香港的法治文化是必須的。但我們對香港法治文化的認識卻是有限。我們會以專家評估的方法去評定香港法治體制的表現，並會以問卷調查的方式去調研香港的法治文化。這調研的目的不是要香港市民對香港的法治作一次民意表達，而是要探討港人對法制的各方面的認識、信念、價值、態度、及期望。我們會分析相關的結果以掌握它們之間的關係。 我們研究團隊的強項是我們既有法律專業人士，並有法治、法律文化研究的良好出版記錄，也有從事實証社會調研擁豐富經驗的人員。法律知識及實証社會調研的專門知識對設計一份全面及有意義的法治文化問卷都是重要的。 從這研究計劃所得到的知識，亦可為未來在其他中國人社會進行相類似研究提供啟發。

749613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
749613.value: The increasing number and severe impacts of hazards has seen disaster risk reduction become a central theme in international governance. There has been an increasing discussion on institutionalization of disaster risk reduction measures in international policy and decision-making structures. They emphasize the urgency of promoting community participation in disaster risk reduction as well as building the resilience of nations and communities to disasters. However, literature of post-disaster reconstruction has demonstrated that current dominant approaches, have often been top-down and exclusionary, and failing to reach the marginalized. Several scholars found that resilience measures during recovery and disaster preparedness, rarely address the underlying causes of vulnerability and trajectories of social inequality in disaster prone societies. The controversies highlighted above illustrate that the current disaster risk reduction governance addresses problems that are characterized by multiple legitimate perspectives on what constitutes the actual causes of a given risk. Because ‘outsiders’ and ‘insiders’ measure and describe risk in different ways, the distinction between risk perception and actual risk loses its justification. Perceptions on hazards also vary among different cultural systems. Indigenous Peoples interpret and react to climate change impacts in creative ways, drawing on traditional knowledge as well as new technologies to find solutions. Disaster risk reduction governance, therefore, involves a complex set of processes that brings together multiple stakeholders representing agencies and organizations with different mandates and agendas and operating at different levels. For a long term development of the local region and harmonious cooperation among different stakeholders, sustainable reconstruction (SR) should be an integrated approach to reconstruction. As a long term strategy, SR not only emphasizes on copying with challenges in the present, but also “promotes a culture of prevention for the future” so as to achieve “building back better”. To achieve the goals, SR depends on “strengthening cooperation between international and national institutions, NGOs and local communities.” Therefore, all stakeholders’ knowledge as traditional ecological knowledge and scientific ecological knowledge should all be included in a reconstruction plan. 750513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
750513.value: The project aims at understanding the school and family effects on the rural-urban literacy gaps in primary education in China. In China, an enormous disparity in literacy achievement exists between rural and urban children. For instance, approximately 50% of rural children perform below the minimum literacy requirements, whereas less than 10% of urban students do so (Wang & Li, 2008). Such an extensive literacy gap could lead to further widened achievement gaps in later school years. This study is also dedicated to understanding the emergence and development of this literacy gap and the ways of closing the gap. The study is grounded in the theoretical debate over “school vs. family” effects on student achievement. Evidence from developed countries supports stronger school effects while findings from developing countries support stronger family effects. We hypothesize that school and family effects may function differently in societies at different developmental stages. In this sense, the rising China with huge disparities within the country offers an ideal setting to test our theory of contextual effects of schools and families in advanced and under-developed regions. A two-year longitudinal mixed-method study will be conducted. The quantitative part consists of (1) three waves of literacy achievement tests of 2400 primary students in grades one, three and five, and (2) two waves of school and parental surveys, over the period of two years. Cluster sampling will be used to recruit 10 schools (five rural and five urban) in Guizhou and Shandong provinces, respectively. The data will be used to measure the rural-urban literacy gap and model the mechanisms of the emergence and development of this gap. The qualitative part is a multiple case study of four typical schools (two in each province, one urban and one rural). Class observations, in-depth interviews with teachers and school principals, and focus group interviews with parents will be conducted to collect detailed information about schooling and parenting practices. Findings will reveal the similarities and differences in specific dynamics between rural and urban schools and across regions, and help to identify the effective ways of closing the rural-urban learning gap. This study will make significant contributions to theoretical and practical development in closing the rural-urban literacy gap. It will shed light on the effective ways/strategies to reduce the disparity in basic education quality. Implications for China and other developing countries can be made accordingly to better achieve the target of Education for All. 本项目旨在了解学校和家庭因素对城乡小学生读写能力差距的影响。 在中国，农村儿童与城市儿童的语文读写能力存在着巨大的差距。例如，约50％的农村儿童识字能力低于最低课程要求，而类似的城市学生却只有10％（Wang & Li，2008）。这样一个巨大的文化鸿沟，可能导致儿童在高年级的学习差距进一步扩大。因此，本研究也着重了解语文读写能力差距的产生和发展，并将致力于寻求缩小该差距的方法。 这项研究的理论出发点基于“学校或家庭”对学生成绩的影响的争论。来自发达国家的证据支持更强的家庭影响力，而来自发展中国家的研究结果支持更强的学校效应。我们推测，学校和家庭的影响在不同的社会、在不同的社会发展阶段，可能有不同的表现。在这个意义上，中国的崛起与在该国巨大的内部差距提供了一个理想的环境，来测试我们的先进和欠发达地区的学校和家庭环境效应的理论。 我们将使用混合研究方法进行为期两年的跟踪调查。定量研究部分包括：在两学年内（1）对一，三，五年级的2400名小学生进行三次识字水平测验，（2）对学校和家长进行两次问卷调查。我们将使用整群采样的办法， 分别在贵州和山东两省选择10所学校（五所乡镇学校，五所城区学校）。这些数据将被用来衡量城乡儿童的文化差距和并对产生和发展该差距的机制建立模型。 定性研究部分是一个多案例研究，将对四种典型的学校（在每个省，城市和农村各一所学校）进行调查。我们将进行课堂观察，对教师和校长进行深入访谈，对家长采用焦点小组访谈，针对学校和家庭教育方式收集详细信息 。调查结果将揭示在城乡之间以及区域之间的异同及其动态关系，并将帮助我们确定缩小城乡学习差距的有效途径。 这项研究将对缩小城乡文化差距的理论和实践发展作出重大贡献。它将揭示提高基础教育质量、缩小贫富差距的有效途径与战略。本研究对中国和其他发展中国家更好地实现全民教育的目标具有重要意义。

750513.label: Realisation of objectives
750513.value: The project objectives have been achieved. First, the emergence and development of the rural-urban literacy gap were measured and documented through descriptive data analyses on student literacy scores. The standardized and observed rural-urban literacy gap across grade were demonstrated by standardized score comparisons and data visualizations. Additional descriptive analyses were also applied to document the rural-urban gap in family- and school-based factors. Second, the contextual effects of schools and families on student literacy achievement were explored and examined through qualitative and quantitative investigations. The specific indicators and patterns found in the qualitative phase were then closely examined by Structural Equation models and Hierarchical Linear models demonstrating and measuring the magnitude of family and school effects. Third, effective strategies/practices for narrowing the rural-urban literacy gap in China were identified through a series of investigations. (1) the existing strategies/practices for addressing the gap were collected by thorough literature reviews. (2) In-depth qualitative observations and interviews were conducted to further explore the possible strategies/practices. (3) These strategies/practices were then examined and compared through advanced quantitative investigations with three waves of data collected over two academic years. And the most effective strategies/practices were identified by model comparisons. Findings identify two most important strategies to narrow the literary gap: (1) home-based literacy practices and (2) school-based teacher professional learning communities. Our analyses have revealed further details of the two strategies, which will make meaningful contribution to school practices and policy making.
