750513.label: Major findings and research outcome
750513.value: 1. Rural-Urban gap in student literacy achievement and contexts of family and school. Longitudinal data over two years cross six primary grades show that literacy disparity between rural and urban students was minor in lower grades (on average 1.1 to 8.36 points, 0.67 to 1 SD), and developed to be more pronounced in middle grades (on average 10 to 14 points, 0.92 to 1.1 SD) and persisted to higher grades (on average 7 to 10 points, 0.75 to 1.3 SD) (Wang, J., Wang, Li & Li, 2016, Wang, J., Li, & Wang, 2018; Wang, J. Wang, & Li, under review). Moreover, significant rural-urban gap was also found in both family and school contextual features. Rural parents were significantly less educated than urban parents and possessed significantly less family literacy resources than urban families. In school, apart from poorer training of teachers and inferior working conditions in rural schools, striking discrepancies were also found in the intensity and effectiveness of site-based Teacher Professional Learning Communities (PLCs) for teacher collaborative learning (Wang, D., et al., 2017; Wang, J. et al., under review). Disparities in PLC explain the different instruction quality and student outcomes between rural and urban schools (Wang, D., et al., 2017; Wang, J. et al., under review). Moreover, urban schools also tended to have higher social capital than rural ones (Wang, D., Apr. 2018). 2. Contextual effects of families and schools and effective strategies/practices for closing the rural-urban literacy gap. Family socioeconomic status was significantly predictive of student literacy outcome. However, the SES effect can be mediated by effective home literacy practices (Wang, J. Li & Wang, 2018). Home-based literacy resources and practice at home explained the rural-urban literacy gaps (Wang, J., Wang, Li & Li, 2016; Wang, J. Li & Wang, 2018). In school, the discrepancy in the quality of teacher PLCs better explained the rural-urban literacy gap than teacher qualifications and working conditions did. Specifically, school management and organizational context conducive for teacher collaboration were predictive of better instruction and literacy outcome (Wang, D., et al., 2017; Wang, J., Wang, & Li, under review; Wang, D., Apr. 2018). Therefore, policies aiming at reducing rural-urban literacy gap should focus on strengthening school capacity for developing teachers in PLCs rather than exclusively training individual teachers through formal education and workshops.

750513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
750513.value: Based on findings of the current project, future studies should further explore the contextual effects of families and schools on the quality of teaching and learning in rural and urban schools. Specifically, practices of management and leadership of the professional learning communities require more in-depth investigations to identify strategies that may improve teachers’ teaching and thereby student learning in rural schools. Future investigations should also apply longitudinal research on a larger school sample (ideally over 40) to establishing the casual relationship between professional learning communities and rural-urban gap in student learning outcome with better measures and aim at examining the rural-urban gaps in PLCs, from the perspective of school management, leadership and organizational context of PLCs.

750513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
750513.value: This project thoroughly documents the rural-urban educational gap in student literacy achievement in primary schools. It is found that rural students significantly underperform urban students throughout the course of primary education. Such gap is largely caused by (1) the differences in home literacy practices and resources and (2) the disparities in the school organizational contexts that encourage or frustrate effective teachers’ collaborative professional learning. Two effective strategies are identified to narrow the rural-urban literacy gap. (1) Improving the quality of home literacy activities and resources. Rural schools should partner with families to reinforce and extend students’ literacy learning after school. Local governments should invest in improving the community literacy environment by establishing village libraries or cultural centers to compensate home disadvantages. (2) Strengthening school capacity for advancing teachers and teaching. Effort and investment should be put in improving the school organizational context to enable regular and continuous teacher collaborative learning. Through professional collaboration, rural schools can accumulate, sustain, and update its pool of professional knowledge and practices. This would be a fundamental way to transform teaching and teachers in rural schools. Theoretically, the research calls for re-conceptualizing rural-urban achievement gaps from a collective, instead of individualistic, approach.

750813.label: Project Title(Chinese)
750813.value: 二十世紀台灣文化政策與現代台灣意識形成之關係

750813.label: Project Objectives
750813.value: To conduct a theoretically informed empirical study of the interrelationship amongst Japanese colonial legacies, KMT’s Sinicization policies, Lee’s bentuhua policies and Taiwanese consciousness and produce a book for publication. To examine how and why the Japanese colonial regime was able to occupy the native consciousness in a wide range of daily practices. To examine how and why the KMT regime occupied the consciousness of the native Taiwanese through the imposition of a series of Sinicization policies. To investigate the bentuhua policies of Lee and how they were shaped and informed by the two previous cultural policies. To explore how Japanese elements lingering from colonial era could become an integral part of the local Taiwanese culture and later even the cultural source against which Lee Teng-hui based his own version of bentuhua. To explore how Lee’s bentuhua movement contributed to Taiwanese consciousness. That is, how the cultural separatist movement can be turned into a political separatist movement.

750813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
750813.value: 本研究旨在釐清過去一個世紀日本殖民地政權、國民黨威權式政權和李登輝政權在臺灣實施的主要文化政策，並進一步分析這些文化政策與現代臺灣意識形成之關係。本研究認為，我們應把上述的文化政策理解為一個Comaroff夫婦（Comaroff and Comaroff 1991: 4）所說把本土居民的意識殖民地化（“colonization of consciousness”的過程。在這個過程中，本土居民的意識將會被一套特殊的世界觀所取代（Comaroff and Comaroff 1991: 4）。然而，這樣並不等於說本土居民會完全被殖民地化，無差別地接納或擁抱這套外來的世界觀。相反地，這個殖民地化的過程反而是引起甚或鼓勵另外一套世界觀之形成的主要原因。本研究認為，過去一世紀於臺灣發生錯綜複雜的殖民地化過程正為現代臺灣意識埋下重要的文化歷史背景。 本研究更認為，李登輝政權的文化政策，尤其是當中的「本土化」深受前政權各種文化政策的影響。國民黨威權式政權銳意把戰後臺灣社會「中國化」使得李登輝的本土化措施變相成為一個「去中國化」的過程，目的在於把臺灣從大陸那邊分割出來。有趣的是，在這個過程中去中國化措施的內容被擴大，進一步包含了所有「非」中國的文化內容。殘留在現代臺灣社會中各式各樣的日本生活模式正正被李登輝所利用，使得再日本化具有相同於「本土化」的文化意思。也就是通過鼓吹或喚起殘留在臺灣的日本文化，來證明臺灣文化有別于中國文化。從這樣的角度來看，本土化其實是前政權各種措施下的獨有產物。 這架構對本研究如何思考日本殖民政策、國民黨文化政策、李登輝本土化政策以及臺灣人意識形成之相互關係有著重要的影響。具體來說，本研究首先分析日本殖民政權以及國民黨政權如何間接或直接塑造本土意識之形成，展現於日常生活中各式各樣的習慣中。第二，本研究將分析國民黨的文化措施如何左右李登輝文化措施的方向。第三，本研究會分析日據時代殘留下來的日本文化如何成為本土臺灣文化不可或缺的一部份，最後甚至能成為李登輝本土化運動的原材料？最後，我們將會探究李登輝的本土化如何成就所謂的臺灣意識。也就是說，一個文化分離措施如何能變成為政治分離措施呢？

750813.label: Realisation of objectives
750813.value: 1) Through carrying out in-depth research on the cultural policies of the Japanese colonial rule, the KMT regime and Lee Teng-hui regime and their impacts on the daily life of the people of Taiwan, the interrelationship among the cultural policies of the three regimes and the role of the cultural policies of the three regimes in shaping the formation process of modern Taiwanese consciousness, we were able to identify, clarify and compare the nation-making processes taken place throughout the Japanese, KMT and Lee Teng-hui regimes. Our focus on the ‘nationalizing’ and ‘renationalizing’ efforts of the regimes addresses the limitations of Benedict Anderson’s ‘imagined community’ approach, which fails to explain in detail the emergence of Taiwanese consciousness in contemporary Taiwan as it tends to ignore the actions of the crucial actors during the process and the power struggle among them. We also included a comparative perspective to compare the case of Taiwan and colonial Hong Kong after the Second World War so that we were able to better identify and explain the nature and features of the emergence of modern Taiwanese consciousness. We conducted extensive literature review, archival research, interview and ethnographic research to examine the cultural policies of the Japanese colonial government, the KMT regime and Lee Teng-hui’s regime respectively, the ways how Lee’s bentuhua policies were informed by the previous two regimes and Lee’s strategy in leading a political-separatist movement through the cultural-separatist movement. 2) Through our intensive reading of secondary material about colonial Taiwan and interview with old kōmin (imperialized citizens, referring to those who subjected themselves to the Japanese rule by giving up their Han Chinese names), we identified several important policies such as ‘the co-education between Taiwanese and Japanese’ of 1921, the ‘Law concerning the Japanese ordinances to be enforced in Taiwan’ (called Law No. 3), the use of Japanese style weddings and funerals, dressing, the worship of Shinto shrines, and the adoption of Japanese customs, language and even names through which the Japanese colonial regime occupied the native consciousness in everyday life of the people of Taiwan. 3) Through our intensive archival research on the KMT regime, we investigated how the KMT regime imposed on local people ‘a particular way of seeing and being’ and inhabited their consciousness with signs and practices of the ‘alien Chinese culture’ in order to secure full control of the native Taiwanese people. We also discovered that KMT adopted a series of policies to discipline body, manner and gender comportment to lodge into their bodies new principles that entailed a new whole set of values speaking not only to the ‘Chineseness’ but also the superiority of ‘Chineseness’. 4) By conducting interviews with former officials in charge of formulating the cultural policies during Lee’s regime, we confirmed that Lee’s cultural policy aimed to reverse the KMT’s intention to impose a Han Chinese culture on the people of Taiwan by establishing a Taiwanese culture that distanced from the Han Chinese culture. 5) Through intensive ethnographic fieldwork in Taiwan, we discovered that Japanese elements such as language, food culture and architectural structure were fully incorporated into the lifestyle of the people of contemporary Taiwan because they were rehearsed in everyday life of the people of Taiwan. We also conducted an analysis of the change of the landscape of Hsimenting over the past century to investigate how the recent renewal of Hsimenting as a heaven for Japanese pop culture in contemporary Taiwan was related to Lee’s strategy of distancing Taiwanese culture from Chinese culture. 6) Through intensive interviews with the former officials who led the Council for Cultural Affairs especially Professor Chen Chi-nan, we found out that Lee aimed to nurture a strong attachment to local communities among the people of Taiwan in order to develop among them a distinctive cultural consciousness which is different from that of the Han Chinese culture. We also visited some local communities and interviewed local people to see how they built the awareness of community among themselves on their own. According to the fact that the cultural logic of the Chinese concept of ‘guojia’ (nation-state), nation-state in Chinese culture is based on the same culture, history, and language, we concluded that the logical conclusion of Lee’s cultural separation has to be political separation.

750813.label: Major findings and research outcome
750813.value: Our research reveals how the formation of modern Taiwanese consciousness has to be understood as a complex process informed by complex articulations and mediations among the Japanese colonial policies, KMT’s Sinicization policies and Lee Teng-hui’s bentuhua policies. Specifically, the research enables us to better understand how the Japanese and ‘Chinese’ elements had been discarded, inserted and reshaped by the three different regimes to construct the local Taiwanese subjectivity. We are working on seven monographs—among them six have been contracted—to present the findings of the research and to reveal the dynamics of the transformation of modern Taiwanese consciousness under the three regimes. The contracted manuscripts in preparation include four Chinese books examining respectively the relationship between the cultural policies of the Japanese colonial rule, the KMT regime and the Lee Teng-hui regime, the emergence and development of modern Taiwanese consciousness (Part C, Item 3-5) and the identity formation processes in post-war Taiwan and Hong Kong (Part C Item 2); one Japanese book comparing the nation-making processes in Taiwan and Hong Kong after the Second World War (Part C, Item 1) and one English book comparing the cultural policies of the three regimes in Taiwan and the British colonial rule and the Chinese rule in Hong Kong (Part C, Item 6). We are also working on another English manuscript–which we will send out to seek a book contract very soon–examining the nationalizing and renationalizing processes of the KMT and Lee Teng-hui regimes and their impacts on the development of Taiwanese identity today. For the Japanese book (Part C, Item 1), we have already completed the whole manuscript and sent it out for translation. The book will be published by the end of 2017. We will also complete all the remaining manuscripts by the end of 2017. We will try our very best to make sure that all the monographs derived from the current research project will be published by the end of 2018.

750813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
750813.value: We are convinced that further research should be carried out to investigate the interaction between the state and the people in the three regimes in modern Taiwan (Japanese colonial rule, KMT rule and Lee Teng-hui’s regime). Further development of the research should focus on two interrelated aspects. First, we believe that further research should focus on examining the resistance and collaboration of the Taiwanese people with the respective regimes to investigate how and why the Taiwanese acted, responded and interacted with the regimes in those specific ways and how their identity and subjectivity were formed and reformed through the process. Second, further research should also be carried out to examine how the three regimes systematically exercised authority over the Taiwanese through their power of the control and distribution of the material, social and political resources. For instance, to better understand the impact of the KMT rule on the people, we should examine how the regime established a comprehensive welfare system for civil servants, military personnel and educators in order to foster the dependence of the latter on the former. We shall prepare and submit another GRF proposal in the near future to investigate these issues.

750813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
750813.value: Our research revealed that the emergence and formation of modern Taiwanese consciousness is a complex process informed by the cultural policies of the three regimes namely, the Japanese colonial rule, the KMT rule and Lee Teng-hui’s regime. Our research showed that in order to understand the nature and transformation of modern Taiwanese consciousness, we should not study the three regimes independently but interdependently. We demonstrated that Lee’s bentuhua policies, which aimed to inhabit a Taiwan-centric instead of China-centric ‘way of seeing and being’ among the people, were informed by the Japanization efforts of the Japanese colonial government and the de-Japanization and re-Sinicization policies of the KMT regime. We further explained how Lee, through emphasizing the Japanese elements during the bentuhua movement, attempted to construct a new Taiwanese consciousness which is culturally distant from China and one which therefore provided a cultural argument for a politically independent Taiwan. The research also results in a series of monographs to be published in English, Japanese and Chinese to reach and engage the widest audience possible.

750913.label: Project Objectives
750913.value: To identify and compare the values that are characteristic of law students in Hong Kong, Mainland China and Taiwan; To assess the significance of values in the decision-making process of law students in the Greater China Region; To investigate the effect of class and gender on the value orientations of law students in the Greater China Region; To evaluate the impact of law school education on the value orientation of law students in the Greater China Region; To investigate the contextual factors, both external and internal to law schools in Hong Kong, Mainland China and Taiwan, that impact the values of their students; To identify and develop strategies that can help both the governments and law schools in the Greater Chin Region to reform their curricula on value development of their law students.

750913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
750913.value: 本研究針對中國大陸、香港和台灣的法學專業學生的價值觀比較研究。律師在法律實務中扮演重要角色，因此，探究法學專業學生的價值觀有助於我們對預測他們未來在法律工作中的職業道德。目前，有關於律師或法學專業學生價值觀的研究仍然罕有。 本研究主要從以下四個方面來探討中國大陸、香港和台灣法學專業學生的價值觀。第一，哪些價值觀會對他們在未來法律實務中面臨選擇困惑時產生決定性的影響；第二，在該三個地區之間是否存有共同的核心價值；第三，該三個地區的法學專業學生是否持有迥異的價值取向；第四，該三個地區的法學專業學生中是否存在性別上對價值層次認識的不同。 針對上述問題，本研究將分別對中國大陸、香港和台灣的法學專業學生開展問卷調查和訪談。本研究是建立在澳洲一項同領域的研究之上，通過借鑒其問卷調查的內容以擴展適用至對中國大陸、香港和台灣法學專業學生價值觀的研究。 本研究具有重大意義，因為它是首份對中國大陸、香港和台灣法學專業學生價值觀進行探析的實證比較研究，同時，它將促進該三個地區法學院校開展法律職業道德的教育和相關課程的改革。

750913.label: Realisation of objectives
750913.value: Objective One (identification and comparison of the values that are characteristic of law students in Hong Kong, Mainland China and Taiwan): this objective was fully achieved by firstly, pilot studies and interviews undertaken with 20 law students in each of Hong Kong (University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong), Mainland China (Shanghai Jiaotong University, Shanghai) and Taiwan (Soochow University, Taipei) between June and July 2014; secondly, questionnaire surveys undertaken with 330 law students in Hong Kong (three law schools including University of Hong Kong, Chinese University of Hong Kong and City University of Hong Kong); 670 law students in Mainland China (eight law schools including Tsinghua University, Peking University, China University of Political Science and Law, Shanghai Jiaotong University, Shenzhen University, Peking University School Transactional Law, Shandong University, and Jilin University) and 348 law students in Taiwan (three law schools including National Taiwan University, National Chengchi University and Soochow University) between July and December 2014. Objective Two (assessment of the significance of values in the decision-making process of law students in the Greater China Region): this objective was fully achieved by firstly, pilot studies and interviews undertaken with 20 law students in each of Hong Kong (University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong), Mainland China (Shanghai Jiaotong University, Shanghai) and Taiwan (Soochow University, Taipei) between June and July 2014; secondly, questionnaire surveys undertaken with 330 law students in Hong Kong (three law schools including University of Hong Kong, Chinese University of Hong Kong and City University of Hong Kong); 670 law students in Mainland China (eight law schools including Tsinghua University, Peking University, China University of Political Science and Law, Shanghai Jiaotong University, Shenzhen University, Peking University School Transactional Law, Shandong University, and Jilin University) and 348 law students in Taiwan (three law schools including National Taiwan University, National Chengchi University and Soochow University) between July and December 2014. Objective Three (investigation of the effect of class and gender on the value orientations of law students in the Greater China Region): this objective was fully achieved by firstly, pilot studies and interviews undertaken with 20 law students in each of Hong Kong (University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong), Mainland China (Shanghai Jiaotong University, Shanghai) and Taiwan (Soochow University, Taipei) between June and July 2014; secondly, questionnaire surveys undertaken with 330 law students in Hong Kong (three law schools including University of Hong Kong, Chinese University of Hong Kong and City University of Hong Kong); 670 law students in Mainland China (eight law schools including Tsinghua University, Peking University, China University of Political Science and Law, Shanghai Jiaotong University, Shenzhen University, Peking University School Transactional Law, Shandong University, and Jilin University) and 348 law students in Taiwan (three law schools including National Taiwan University, National Chengchi University and Soochow University) between July and December 2014; and thirdly, literature review undertaken on the impact of class and gender on value hierarchies of law students. Objective Four (evaluation of the impact of law school education on the value orientation of law students in the Greater China Region): this objective was fully achieved by firstly, pilot studies and interviews undertaken with 20 law students in each of Hong Kong (University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong), Mainland China (Shanghai Jiaotong University, Shanghai) and Taiwan (Soochow University, Taipei) between June and July 2014; secondly, questionnaire surveys undertaken with 330 law students in Hong Kong (three law schools including University of Hong Kong, Chinese University of Hong Kong and City University of Hong Kong); 670 law students in Mainland China (eight law schools including Tsinghua University, Peking University, China University of Political Science and Law, Shanghai Jiaotong University, Shenzhen University, Peking University School Transactional Law, Shandong University, and Jilin University) and 348 law students in Taiwan (three law schools including National Taiwan University, National Chengchi University and Soochow University) between July and December 2014 and thirdly, literature review undertaken on the legal education development of Hong Kong, Mainland China and Taiwan. Objective Five (investigation of the contextual factors, both external and internal to law schools in Hong Kong, Mainland China and Taiwan, that impact the values of their students): this objective was fully achieved by firstly, pilot studies and interviews undertaken with 20 law students in each of Hong Kong (University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong), Mainland China (Shanghai Jiaotong University, Shanghai) and Taiwan (Soochow University, Taipei) between June and July 2014; secondly, questionnaire surveys undertaken with 330 law students in Hong Kong (three law schools including University of Hong Kong, Chinese University of Hong Kong and City University of Hong Kong); 670 law students in Mainland China (eight law schools including Tsinghua University, Peking University, China University of Political Science and Law, Shanghai Jiaotong University, Shenzhen University, Peking University School Transactional Law, Shandong University, and Jilin University) and 348 law students in Taiwan (three law schools including National Taiwan University, National Chengchi University and Soochow University) between July and December 2014; and thirdly by literature review undertaken on the impact of Chinese culture, particularly family influence, on the value development of law students in Hong Kong, Mainland China and Taiwan. Objective Six (identification and development of strategies that can help both the governments and law schools in the Greater China Region to reform their curricula on value development of their law students): this objective was fully achieved by firstly, plot studies undertaken with 20 law students in each of Hong Kong (University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong), Mainland China (Shanghai Jiaotong University, Shanghai) and Taiwan (Soochow University, Taipei) between June and July 2014 and secondly, questionnaire surveys undertaken with 330 law students in Hong Kong (three law schools including University of Hong Kong, Chinese University of Hong Kong and City University of Hong Kong); 670 law students in Mainland China (eight law schools including Tsinghua University, Peking University, China University of Political Science and Law, Shanghai Jiaotong University, Shenzhen University, Peking University School Transactional Law, Shandong University, and Jilin University) and 348 law students in Taiwan (three law schools including National Taiwan University, National Chengchi University and Soochow University) between July and December 2014 and thirdly, by literature review on the ethics education of law school focusing on clinical legal education and legal ethics teaching.

750913.label: Major findings and research outcome
750913.value: Major Findings and Research outcome (please refer to the research output in Part C, particularly the three journal articles at the end of the session) 1. Law students in the Greater China Region are similar in their ranking of ‘professional integrity’ and ‘business efficacy’. However, Hong Kong students rank the value of ‘clients’ interest’ higher than their counterparts in Mainland China and Taiwan, while law students in Mainland China rank ‘family members’ well-being’ as well as ‘friendship loyalty’ higher than, and ‘personal integrity’ lower than, their counterparts in Taiwan and Hong Kong. 2.Hong Kong law students have developed ethical values more similar to common law students than their counterparts in Mainland China and Taiwan. 3. Education background of parents has no significant effect on the value orientations of law students in the Greater China Region. 4. Some correlations exist between gender and ethical values of law students in Hong Kong. Female law students are more motivated by the value of ‘business efficacy’ than their male counterparts. They are also more motivated by the values of ‘access to legal justice’ and ‘civic duty’ than their male counterparts. 5. Mainland China and Taiwan have a higher percentage of students taking the legal ethics course, but their students have not exhibited more ethical behavior. For example, a higher percentage of their law students is inclined to make a profit by insider trading, and prefers not to report the wrongdoing of their relatives in abusing client account. 6. In future, law schools in the Greater China Region should expand their legal clinics programmes to inculcate upon their students the value of ‘access to legal justice’. 7. Law schools in the Greater China Region should strengthen the ethical values of law students by developing their “personal conscience“, “ethics of duty”, and “ethics of aspiration”. They should also cultivate such virtues like honesty, perspective, and fairness among their students to help them encounter ethical dilemmas. 8. A new generation of law students has emerged in the Greater China Region who cherish work-life balance. They rate personal values of “family loyalty” and “family members’ well-being” higher than professional values like “obedience to the law firm partner/supervisor”, “professional ambition” and “loyalty to the firm”. 750913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
750913.value: As we have studied the ethical values of law students in the Greater China Region, we should research the ethical values of law student in other Asian countries. These include both common law countries like Singapore and Malaysia, and civil law countries like Japan, South Korea and Vietnam. On basis of the findings of this project, Dr Wu (PI) applied for a GRF grant to study the ethical values of law students in three Asian common law jurisdictions (Hong Kong, Singapore and Malaysia) in 2013 and was awarded a sum of HK$680,580 (Project No.1740914) in 2014. Subsequently, Dr Wu (PI) applied for another GRF grant to study the ethical values of law students in four Asian civil law countries (China, Japan, Vietnam and South Korea) in 2014 and was awarded a sum of HK$798,480 (Project No.17601815) in 2015. In 2016, Dr Wu (PI) also applied for another GRF grant to study the ethical values of law students in four fastest growing Asian countries (N.B. extract of the research grant proposal is attached in item 6, Section 8). The study aims to compare the ethical values of law students in China, India, Philippines and Thailand from an empirical perspective.

750913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
750913.value: This project investigates empirically the ethical values of law students in the Greater China Region. It found that law students in this region are similar in ranking of values like ‘professional integrity’ and ‘business efficacy’, but Hong Kong law students have developed ethical values more similar to those in other common law countries. This study also recommends law schools in the Greater China Region to cultivate virtues like honesty, perspective, and fairness among their students in future. This project is significant as it has enhanced our understanding of the ethical values of law students in Hong Kong, China and Taiwan. It is also invaluable in developing a new field of academic inquiry by leading to two more research projects on the ethical values of law students in other Asian common law countries like Singapore and Malaysia; and Asian civil law countries like Japan, South Korea and Vietnam. It also leads to another possible project on other Asian fastest growing countries like India, Philippines and Thailand. Overall, this project is a pioneering study of the ethical values of Asian law students. It has made an important contribution to the academic discourse on the ethical values of law students and Asian legal education.

751013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
751013.value: Although the First World War began almost a century ago, comprehension of the important role Asia played in the conflict and the war’s profound impact on Asian societies remains at best incomplete. The world has still not fully understood the deep connections between Asia and the Great War. Nor have Asians yet fully recognized the war’s legacy and impact on their history and development as nations. To date, no single volume has sought to assess Asia’s overall role in the war. This proposal will help remedy this inexplicable gap by producing a book highlighting the multi-layered engagement of several key Asian nations with the twentieth century’s “great seminal catastrophe.” This project will constitute classic international history in terms of its use of multi-archival sources. Bringing together several layers of analysis, it seeks to synthesize conventional “high” diplomatic and political relations among states with transnational wartime encounters at the non-state level, while incorporating social and cultural history perspectives from the bottom-up by focusing on the experiences of individual Asians who participated in or were affected by the war. This project will focus on the shared experiences, aspirations, and frustrations of Asian peoples, especially such questions as how the varied involvement of several Asian countries made the Great War both a true “world” war and also a “great” war, a conflict that generated forces that would transform Asia both internally and externally. Besides recapturing the authentic voices of Asian men and women who participated in the Great War and whose lives and contributions to that conflict have until now been largely ignored and neglected, it will also address such crucial issues as how Asian war experiences influenced different countries’ post-war search for national identities and new places in a re-configured world order; how the Great War became a turning point for both individual Asian nations and Asia overall; how the war and its aftermath affected Asian and Western thinking on race and racial equality, colonialism, gender relations, and the differences between Western and Eastern civilizations; the economic effects of the war and its aftermath on Asia; and the war’s role in the rise of nationalism and national ambitions. The key issues this project will seek to address are the dreams, ambitions, frustrations and disappointments that Asians had in common during the First World War, and the extent to which both Asians and Westerners alike shared similar experiences of war. 虽然第一次世界大战发生在100年前，但我们至今对亚洲与一战的关系仍知之甚少。我们不清楚亚洲对一战的贡献如何，也不熟悉一战对亚洲的深刻影响及遗产。迄今为止，尚无一本英文专著从比较和国际史角度来研究亚洲与一战的关联。本书旨在填补这一空白。本书将利用国际史的研究方法，通过多国档案资料及比较视野来论证亚洲诸国（中国，日本，印度，越南，朝鲜）与一战的密切关系。本书将特别强调它们与一战之间的共享的经历，价值体系以及一战对其发展进程的共同影响。本书认为，亚洲和一战之间有非常密切关联，亚洲的加入在真正意义上将“欧战”变为“世界”大战及“大”战。亚洲对一战贡献颇多，一战对亚洲各国发展及国家认同和国际化影响甚巨。 一战因此也成为上述诸国的重要历史发展里程碑。深入研究亚洲与一战的关系不仅对研究一战的国际历史有重要意义，更重要的是，对研究亚洲各国的发展及国际地位也有重要价值。

751013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
751013.value: There is no single volume that shines a light on Asia’s collective involvement and the war’s impact on its societies. Moreover, no volume in any language explores the experiences Asian countries shared as they became embroiled, with divergent results, in the war and its repercussions. The book focuses on one rising power (Japan), one country desperately trying to use the war to change its national fate (China), one British colony (India), one French colony (Indochina or Vietnam), and one Japanese colony (Korea). this book is intended more as a rumination on the shared journey and the war’s impact on these Asian nations than a comprehensive narrative. In other words, the subtitle of this book - “a shared history”- will actually serve as a true focus of this book. It moves beyond the national or even international level by trying to present history from non-national and transnational perspectives. I hope it will provoke response and stimulate debate. I also attempt to highlight the history that Asians and Westerners shared through their experiences of the Great War. I focus on the themes of expectation, observations, sufferings and frustrations among Asians—these were to some extent shared by the Europeans.

751113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
751113.value: 不少研究嘗試探討照顧者對患腦退化長者作出虐待行為的普遍性、相關因素和後果，相對上卻較少關注或會帶來傷害卻不構成虐待的行為。然而，以往的研究表示受壓的照顧者有很大的可能會對患者作出潛在的傷害行為，如尖叫、粗暴地對待被照顧者或威脅要送他們到護養院等等。 依據壓力過程模式，是次研究將探討照顧者對患腦退化長者作出潛在傷害行為的各種相關因素。研究理解到影響日常照顧狀況的複雜因素及多原關係，因此亦會考慮照顧者、被照顧者及環境因素以更了解香港腦退化症老人患者的照顧情況。 根據過往的研究，是次研究將假設照顧者的壓力與其潛在傷害行為有著確切的相聯，而被照顧者的行為障礙同時與照顧者壓力及潛在傷害行為有著同樣的相聯。另外，研究亦假設行為障礙透過其對照顧者的壓力的影響，影響潛在傷害行為。最後，是次研究亦假設照顧者的"受困感"調節著其壓力與潛在傷害行為兩者的關係。 這項是首個有系統地探討香港腦退化症老人患者當中有關潛在傷害行為的研究，因此，它有著相當重要的理論、學術和實踐價值。在理論層面上，識別出照顧腦退化症老人患者以致的潛在傷害行為的各種因素，將能加強現存的理論知識。在學術層面上，對於將來不同地方或文化的比較研究中，是次研究結果對於評估個別因素在不同環境上的輕重有莫大的作用。在實踐方面，有關潛在傷害行為的具體因素將提供一個合理的基礎以制定有效的預防及介入方案，了解到有關的不同因素將有效促進早期介入及防止事件演變成虐待案件。最後，了解到做成照顧者壓力的相關因素有助增強他們的長處，同時亦為他們照顧腦退化症患者這項挑戰作好準備。

751113.label: Realisation of objectives
751113.value: Guided by the Stress Process Model, the proposed study investigates the various factors associated with potentially harmful behaviors directed towards older persons with dementia by their caregivers. The study recognizes the multifactorial causality in the caregiving situation and therefore aims to take account caregiver, care recipient and situational characteristics in order to understand better the caregiving situation of older Chinese with dementia in Hong Kong. We proposed that we would interview a total of 300 family caregivers providing informal care to older persons with dementia. Preliminary analysis of data found that participants we recruited from the two hospitals tended to have better socioeconomic status and thus received better support for caregiving. We thus approached various non-governmental organizations to refer their case to our study. We ended up with a convenient sample of 592 Chinese family caregivers providing informal care to persons with dementia in Hong Kong. Participants were individually interviewed by trained research assistants upon providing written consent to participate.

751113.label: Major findings and research outcome
751113.value: Our study findings established that abuse is common, 46% of the caregivers reported varying degree of potentially harmful behaviors. The proposed hypotheses are supported, in that: 1. caregiver stress and care recipient's behavioural disturbances were directly associated with caregiver's harmful behaviours. 2. caregiver sense of entrapment mediated the associations between care participant's behavioural disturbances and caregivers harmful behaviors. 3. Situational factors such as co-residing days, assistance from a domestic helper are associated with caregiver stress.

751113.value: Study findings have been disseminated in various local and international conferences as well as in international journal papers and book chapters. We will continue to disseminate study findings and develop a proposal to further explore the effective intervention strategies for elder abuse.

751113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
751113.value: Family caregivers providing care to older persons with dementia experience tremendous stress. At the same time, older persons with dementia may display various behavioural problems, which adds to the stress of caregiving. Some caregiver may feel they are entrapped in the caregiving situation with little opportunity to escape. At times, caregivers may engage in behaviours that have high potential of hurting the care recipients. These are called "potentially harmful behaviours". We conducted interviews with 592 caregivers in the community asking them their experience in providing care to an older person with dementia. Our results show that while older care recipient's behavioural problems and caregiver stress predicts greater opportunities for harmful behaviours, sense of entrapment further adds to the likelihood of family caregivers hurting the care recipients.

751313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
751313.value: This study investigates empirically how modern universities, which are uniquely European in origin and characteristics, have developed in four selected Chinese societies. It examines how research universities in these systems reconcile the tension between attaining world-class status and retaining cultural heritage and local relevance. It is set in a context when national governments are introducing policy initiatives to create world-class universities, especially in East and Southeast Asian Chinese societies. Meanwhile, there have been intense debates about exactly how to establish world-class universities, and whether or not flagship universities can maintain and even enhance local relevance while racing ahead to raise their global profiles. Some even argue that building world-class universities can have a negative impact on the rest of a country’s higher education system if equity and other issues are not taken into account. With such questions in mind, this project proposes a comparative policy study about building world-class universities in Mainland China, Hong Kong, Taiwan and Singapore. The results will lead to a better understanding of how higher education in these societies attempts to meet conflicting demands. It is expected to benefit institutional and societal policy-makers. Taking advantage of an unusually strong comparative case study design-four societies, almost a continuum, and two types of universities in each society-this comparative analysis can strengthen understanding and lead to more general propositions than simple descriptive studies. A case study approach is used to gain an in-depth understanding of the complexities of policy on world-class universities from within individual universities in their own unique settings. Cross-case analysis will be undertaken to identify common themes evident across universities within and between societies. Themes emerging from cross-case analysis will build an understanding of rapidly evolving policies on world-class universities in a context of globalization. Two universities will be chosen from each society based on their institutional nature: ‘comprehensive’ or ‘technological.’ They are Peking and Tsinghua Universities in Mainland China; The University of Hong Kong and The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology; National Taiwan and Tsing Hua Universities in Taiwan; and the National University of Singapore and Nanyang Technological University in Singapore. Within each case, five administrators (the president, other senior executives, and administrators working in international programs) and five academics respectively from faculties of the humanities and social sciences, sciences, and engineering will be invited to participate. Principal methods of data collection will be document analysis and semi-structured interviews. 本研究对于现代大学这一源于欧洲具备西方特性的文化机构在华人社会的发展进行实证研究，分析华人社会中研究型大学如何在追赶世界一流的同时坚持文化传统和本土联系。研究的背景是东亚及东南亚诸国均出台建设世界一流大学的政策，而尚未就何谓一流及其旗舰大学是否可以在保持本土联系的同时实现国际一流水平达成共识，相反，有人甚至主张世界一流大学建设对于一国的高等教育公平具有负面效用。该研究致力于分析此类问题，试图进一步了解中国大陆、香港、台湾和新加坡的高等教育是如何在此类诸多矛盾中加以协调统一的，旨在有利于院校及制度层面上的决策。

751313.label: Major findings and research outcome
751313.value: Findings of the project have been quite encouraging. Indeed they challenge the existing literature on East Asian higher education development in a number of ways. Firstly, in contrast to most existing studies on higher education, which have overwhelmingly portrayed the powerful influence of economic and political realities, I have adopted a cultural perspective that gives weight to the impact of traditional ways of cultural thinking on contemporary development. Secondly, I have moved beyond conventional paradigms in assessing higher education development in East Asia featured by dichotomies between extreme views. Thirdly, I have employed different frames of reference to enable me to find both the actual achievements and the serious problems in the systems that are not always obvious when observed in previous lens. Fourthly, based on rich empirical data, I have argued that emerging signs show longstanding efforts by East Asian societies to learn from the West have begun to pay off. Their best universities have demonstrated a possibility of striking a balance between East Asian and Western ideas of a university that have been conventionally perceived as mutually exclusive. Fifthly, I have criticized using soft power in analyzing East Asia’s international engagement in higher education. Set in an implicit yet powerful context of conflicting national self-interests, the notion is a Western construction, with deep roots in modern history featured by conflicts. It leads to a view of Asia’s rising soft power as a zero-sum game, and judge whether East Asian universities are followers or leaders. Indeed, East Asia’s global engagement in higher education functions more than a soft power. The cultural mission of their modern higher education aims to combine East and Western elements to bring together the aspects of both philosophical heritages. My findings have attracted international attention. I have been invited by a number of major universities around the world (such as Peking, Tsinghua and Shanghai Jiao Tong in China, Universities of Queensland and Melbourne in Australia, Aarhus University in Europe and Universities of Pennsylvania and Southern California in the USA, to name but a few) to talk about my findings from the project. I have also been invited by international journals, media, and associations/foundations to write about my findings. I have produced a number of outputs from this projects in a variety forms.So far, over 19 publications and 26 keynote and/or plenary speeches have been published already based on the project findings, with more on the pipeline.

751313.value: Based on the findings of the project, I developed further understanding of the issues. I have particularly found the significant role played by educational traditions. I then submitted another GRF application, and have now just been awarded another GRF project: Project Number 17602017, Project Title: (Re)Conceptualizing Chinese Education: China's Educational Traditions and their Modern Transformation, Approved Duration: 36 Months.

751313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
751313.value: Since the late 19th century, East Asia, as a latecomer to modernization, has prioritized Western learning. Modern university were created in East Asia in the late 19th century to serve such a strong purpose with little linkage to their rich indigenous cultural traditions. Modeled on European and North American experiences and operating in a Confucian social and cultural contexts, East Asian universities have long been struggling with their cultural identity. In line with recent development, East Asia’s higher education has made impressive progress, and cultural experiment has been placed increasingly highly on the agenda. With an understanding of East Asian and Western knowledges by the elites, East Asia’s very best universities have the promise to integrate both traditions in their day-to-day operation. Such a bi-culturality, or even multi-culturality, is in stark contrast to the still largely mono-cultural university operation environment in the West. The integration would open spaces for East Asian universities to explore an alternative to Western models that have dominated world’s higher education since Western industrialization. Based on fieldwork at premier universities in Beijing, Hong Kong, Singapore, and Taipei, findings from this project suggest a different angle to observe East Asia's experience in higher education. They argue that cultural experiment would enable top East Asian universities to bring back their cultural traditions to integrate with Western values, and thus contribute to inter-civilizational dialogue.

752113.label: Project Title(Chinese)
752113.value: 中、韓、日流傳《風雨賦》的研究

752113.label: Project Objectives
752113.value: ● Completing a monograph with the title of Fengyu Fu jizhu風雨賦集注. This monograph will be a collated collection of the annotations in each and every extant edition of Fengyu Fu in China, Korea and Japan. Following the complied annotations of each sentence, there will be a commentary from the editor as well. This monograph is expected to reach 200,000 words and published by international press. ● Publishing two relative articles in international-standard journals. Each article will respectively address these topics: The philological issues and textual studies of Fengyu Fu; The overseas spread of Fengyu Fu and cultural exchange issues among ancient China, Korea and Japan; The interdisciplinary studies between literature and other fields such as traditional divination, agriculture and strategics suggested by Fengyu Fu.

Each article will respectively address these topics: The philological issues and textual studies of Fengyu Fu; The overseas spread of Fengyu Fu and cultural exchange issues among ancient China, Korea and Japan; The interdisciplinary studies between literature and other fields such as traditional divination, agriculture and strategics suggested by Fengyu Fu.

752113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
752113.value: This project takes Fengyu Fu風雨賦 (rhymed-prose on wind and rain) as its object. Fengyu Fu is originally a book by Liu Qiming 劉啟明, a scholar of divination presumably lived between the Tang (618-907) and the Song (960-1279) Dynasties. It takes the form of “rhymed-prose” (“LvFu”律賦) which is commonly used during the Tang and Song period. In the Ming (1368-1644) Dynasty, this book was added with detailed annotations by other scholars and was spread to the then Korea and Japan. It was highly valued both by the government and the common people in the three countries. Being applicable to multiple fields, Fengyu Fu could serve as the basis for the court to monitor the sign of Heaven and promulgate decrees accordingly, as the guidance for the military to judge the situation and deploy forces, as the key for the farmers to forecast the weather and seek rich harvest, as well as the secret for the prophets to predict destiny and omens. All in all, it has exerted a significant influence in history. Therefore a thorough study of this book will not only help enhancing our understanding of the relationship between the folk religion and the literary mode, but also provide valuable insight to the research concerning traditional meteorology and cultural exchange among ancient China, Korea and Japan. 《風雨賦》本是唐宋之際術數家劉啟明原創的占候書，採用唐末宋初通用的律賦體裁。此書在明代被其他學者增加註釋，並得到廣泛傳播，流傳到韓國和日本。或作為朝廷司天測候，頒佈政令的依據；或作為兵家審時度勢，調兵遣將的指南；或作為農家觀風望雨，勤勞致富的訣竅；或作為術數家占天測地，預測吉凶的秘笈，在歷史上產生過相當大的影響。研究此書，不僅有助於理清民間宗教與文學樣式的關係，而且對於研究古代傳統的氣象學，以及觀察中、韓、日三國的文化交流，也有一定的參考價值。

752113.label: Major findings and research outcome
752113.value: This project has benefited from a wealth of literature from China, Japan and South Korea. After studying all the different versions of Feng Yu Fu available from my personal collection, I find that the versions from China, Japan, and South Korea can complement each other and that a comparative approach is necessary for an in-depth and comprehensive understanding of the text.

752113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
752113.value: This project can serve as a solid foundation for future research on the cultural and literary interactions between China, Japan, and Korea during pre-modern times.

752113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
752113.value: The significance of this project lies in the following three aspects. First,it shies away from a single national literary study by taking into the literary interactions between China, Japan, and Korea into consideration. Second, it resonates with the current trend of Sinophone studies, but traces its origin back to the dynamic premodern China-Japan-Korea Sinograph encounters. Third,it enables an interdisciplinary research that combines literary studies with other areas such as agricultural and military histories as well as folk religions of the aforementioned countries.

752513.label: Project Title(Chinese)
752513.value: 大躍進期間的北京“十大建築”

752513.label: Project Objectives
752513.value: Carry out an in-depth architectural case study of Beijing's ‘Ten Great Buildings’ project. Examine the ‘Ten Great Buildings’ as the culmination of the 'Maoist Architecture Movements' during the 1950's. Investigate the ‘Ten Great Buildings’ as a focal point within the framework of the 20th century architectural history of China. Move beyond a simple formal description towards a more comprehensive account of China’s architectural development in the late 1950’s. Fill in the enormous gap between two sets of historical knowledge – namely, the social history and architectural history of China’s ‘Great Leap Forward.’

752513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
752513.value: China has long been obsessed with constructing enormous monumental buildings, often at a huge human and social cost. Beijing’s ‘Ten Great Buildings’ project, built between 1958 and 1959, marked a new milestone in the nation’s recent history, and its legacy still exerts a powerful influence over China’s architectural, urban and social development. My research examines how Beijing’s ‘Ten Great Buildings’ project was envisioned as part of an architectural and urban initiative of Mao’s ‘Great Leap Forward’, and investigates how the architects working on the project became embroiled in an ongoing struggle to devise a style that would be suitable for the new socialist regime. It also explores how the project, which consumed enormous resources and labor, was built in 10 months to meet the government’s deadline to commemorate the 10-year anniversary of the ‘New China,’ at the very moment that China was experiencing one of its most dire socioeconomic crises. Based on a study of the project in relation to the vehement sociopolitical campaigns, intellectuals’ ‘Thought Reforms’ and urban transformations that were conducted by the Chinese Communist Party in the 1950’s, my research further explores how the red legacy of ‘Building Big’ still persists on many levels of governance in China today, and how this legacy is often transformed into a new hybrid when China’s revolutionary sediments are mixed with the currents of globalization. 中國歷來有不惜消耗巨量人力和社會成本，建造宏大紀念碑式建築的傳統。建於1958到1959年的北京“十大建築”，在中國當代史上樹立了一個新里程碑。它對中國的建築、城市和社會發展產生了深遠影響。 本研究考察“十大建築”是如何被策劃為毛澤東的“大躍進”中的城市建築啟動項目，參與的建築師們又是如何奮力試圖發展出一種適合新社會主義政權的建築風格。本研究也探討該項目，如何耗費了超常的資源和人力，僅在10個月左右建成，為的是趕上“新中國”國慶十週年的慶典——而在同時，中國正在滑入最深重的社會經濟災難之一。 通過研究“十大建築”與1950年代共產黨發起的一系列社會政治運動、知識分子“思想改造”和北京城市改造之間的關係，本研究還嘗試進一步探討“修建大項目”的紅色遺產如何仍在當代中國個階層政權管理上仍在持續施加影響，以及這些中國革命的“沉澱物”如何又於全球化浪潮攪拌在一起，形成新型的混合建築文化。

752513.label: Realisation of objectives
752513.value: Objective 1 & 5 I made my first breakthrough with a paper “Building Big, with No Regret: From Beijing’s ‘Ten Great Buildings’ in the 1950s to China’s Mega-projects Today,” which was published in the book Red Legacies in China: Cultural Afterlives of the Communist Revolution (Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Asia Center, 2016). My paper investigated the design and construction process of Beijing’s ‘Ten Great Buildings’ and examined the project’s powerful influence over China’s architectural, urban and social development. Objectives 2-5 To further illustrate the sociopolitical context of China in the late 1950s, I expanded my research with a series of five papers entitled “Reading Liang Sicheng: The Maoist Architectural Movements and Liang’s Thought Reform,” which examined the work of the prominent Chinese architectural historian Liang Sicheng and his connection to Mao’s political campaigns between1949-1959. I published my papers first in Domus: China and Times + Architecture in 2013, and compiled into a book Liang Sicheng and His Times published by Guangxi Normal University Press (Beijing) and Oxford University Press (Hong Kong) in 2014. My book has made a big impact on China’s architectural academia and generated a new wave of interest in the writing of China’s modern architectural history, as the 2012 Pritzker Architecture Prize Laureate Wang Shu commented: “The significance of Zhu Tao’s book is that it manages to use meticulous detail accounts to successfully rewrite a history that has become almost impossible to rewrite.” My research on Chinese architecture in the 1950s and 1960s also helped me develop a better understanding of China’s architectural development in the Reform Era. Between 2013 and 2014, I wrote a chapter for the book A Critical History of Contemporary Architecture 1960-2010 (London: Ashgate, 2014), the first comprehensive survey of the world’s architectural developments during the past five decades. As one of 22 international scholars/contributors invited by the editor, I contributed the chapter on China’s architectural development from 1978 to 2010, which was the first critical survey of this subject in English.

752513.value: My paper “Building Big, with No Regret: From Beijing’s ‘Ten Great Buildings’ in the 1950s to China’s Mega-projects Today,” published in the book Red Legacies in China: Cultural Afterlives of the Communist Revolution (Cambridge, MA: Harvard University Asia Center, 2016), investigates the design and construction process of Beijing’s ‘Ten Great Buildings’ and examines the project’s powerful influence over China’s architectural, urban and social development. My book Liang Sicheng and His Times (Guilin: Guangxi Normal University Press; Hong Kong: Oxford, 2014) examines the work of the prominent Chinese architectural historian Liang Sicheng and his connection to Mao’s political campaigns between1949-1959. My book chapter for A Critical History of Contemporary Architecture 1960-2010 (London: Ashgate, 2014) makes a critical survey of China’s architectural development from 1978 to 2010.

752513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
752513.value: China has long been obsessed with constructing enormous, monumental buildings, often at a huge human and social cost. Beijing’s ‘Ten Great Buildings’ project, built between 1958 and 1959, marked a new milestone in the nation’s recent history, and its legacy still exerts a powerful influence over China’s architectural, urban and social development. This research examines how Beijing’s ‘Ten Great Buildings’ project was envisioned during Mao Zedong’s Great Leap Forward, and investigates how the architects working on the project became embroiled in an ongoing struggle to devise a style that would be suitable for the new socialist regime. It also discusses how the project, which consumed enormous resources and labor, was built in ten months to meet the government’s deadline to commemorate the ten-year anniversary of the ‘New China,’ at the same moment that China was experiencing one of its most dire socioeconomic crises. By exploring the project’s relation to the Maoist sociopolitical campaigns in the 1950s, the research further explores how the red legacy of ‘Building Big’ still persists on many levels of governance in today’s China, and how this legacy is often transformed into a new hybrid when China’s revolutionary sediments become mixed with the currents of globalization.

757013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
757013.value: Most previous studies on writing development have focused on alphabetic languages. This proposed project aims to address the lack of research on writing development among beginning writers learning to write in Chinese, a nonalphabetic language. Findings from the project can help develop a framework of understanding writing development across different languages. The first objective of the project is to investigate the cognitive factors that are important to Chinese writing development among typically developing primary school children in Hong Kong. The writing development of three hundred typically developing participants from grade 1, grade 3 and grade 5 from three primary schools will be followed for two years. They will be administered a number of measures of cognitive skills that are potentially important to writing development among primary school children (including memory, handwriting skills, linguistic skills and oral language skills) and written composition tasks. Statistical analyses will be conducted to find out the cognitive skills that bear close relationships with written composition in each grade. The project will also study Chinese children with reading and writing difficulties. While a wealth of literature on the identification and remediation of Chinese reading difficulties has accumulated over the past decade, no comparable amount of work has been done on Chinese writing difficulties. The findings from the project will provide the theoretical bases for understanding the challenges encountered by Chinese children with writing difficulties and for future development of identification tools. 66 children diagnosed with reading and writing difficulties, 33 from grade 2-3 and 33 from grade 4-5, will be recruited. They will be administered the same measures for the typically developing primary school children. Statistical analyses will be conducted to find out the cognitive skills that are important to writing development among children with reading and writing difficulties. The patterns of the findings from the two groups of participants (typically developing children and children with reading and writing difficulties) will shed light on the similarities and differences in writing development between the two groups. The performance of the two groups of participants on the cognitive skills and written composition measures will also be compared to examine the strengths and weaknesses of children with reading and writing difficulties in learning to write. The findings from the project will therefore provide valuable information for the development of effective writing instructions and intervention for Chinese children with and without reading and writing difficulties. 鑒於以往有關寫作發展的研究大多以拼音語系為主，缺乏如中國語文之非拼音語系研究，故本研究將着重於學童在中文方面的寫作發展，以期建立中文寫作發展的框架，並能與其他語系進行比較。 本研究旨於探討影響本港小學學童在中文寫作發展方面的主要認知因素。研究將以三百名學童為對象，分別來自三所小學的小一、小三及小五，參加為期兩年的研究，以跟進其中文寫作之發展情況。期間，學童會接受一系列與寫作發展相關之認知能力測試（包括記憶力、書寫技能、語言能力及口語能力）與寫作練習，研究人員將以統計分析數據結果，找出各種認知能力因素與各級寫作能力之相關性。 本研究亦以讀寫障礙之學童為對象。近年，本港已有大量有關中文閱讀困難之文獻，但在中文寫作困難方面的研究卻較為缺乏，而本研究結果則有助建立中文寫作之理論基礎，除能加強對寫作困難學童之支援外，更可作為日後發展識別工具之基礎。本研究擬招募六十六名讀寫障礙學童，當中三十三名為小二至小三學童，另三十三名為小四至小五學童。他們將接受與其他參加者相同的測試項目，並以統計分析其數據結果，以發現認知能力對讀寫障礙學童寫作發展之重要性。 另外，本研究將比較兩組參加者（一般學童與讀寫障礙學童）在中文寫作發展之異同，其認知能力及寫作練習之結果亦有助教育界了解讀寫障礙學童在學習寫作時的優勢及難處。 總觀而言，本研究將為教育界提供寶貴的資料，有助日後發展一套有效的寫作教學及支援，以提昇學生的寫作能力，惠及全體學童。

757213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
757213.value: 親密伴侶暴力已被確認為是一個全球性的公共健康議題，也有隱藏的醫療負擔。研究顯示，受虐婦女中，發現九成以上的有頭部創傷，並或會導致創傷性腦損傷。而且，研究發現身體受傷的受虐婦女中，約六成是有輕度創傷性腦部損傷。雖然這種較輕度的創傷性腦損傷通常不一定能以實驗室測試，X射線和斷層掃描儀器檢查出來，但是婦女可能在生活上已受到一些干擾，例如，頭痛，頭暈，乏力，煩躁不安，失眠，難以集中和記憶出現困難。 親密伴侶暴力相關的輕度創傷性腦損傷的後遺症可能與交通意外相關的輕度創傷性腦損傷不同，因為我們前期工作顯示親密伴侶暴力相關的輕度創傷性腦損傷可能會反復多次出現。親密伴侶暴力相關的輕度創傷性腦損傷的後遺症也可能與運動損傷的不同，因為受虐婦女也與此同時受慢性心理創傷的影響。現時，只有一個橫斷面研究，評估受虐婦女在輕度的創傷性腦損傷後的認知功能（記憶力，注意力，執行功能和學習），但是研究並沒有區分受虐婦女的認知功能障礙是否心理壓力導致的結果。此外，一直沒有縱向研究評估受虐婦女在輕度的創傷性腦損傷後的認知功能。這些表明迫切性的需要評估受虐婦女在輕度的創傷性腦損傷後的認知功能。 本研究是一項前瞻性的追蹤研究，旨在評估受虐婦女在輕度的創傷性腦損傷後的認知功能及與對照組（受虐婦女但沒有輕度的創傷性腦損傷）的比較，時點在進入研究， 三個月及六個月後。研究對象來自於兩間香港公共醫院急診科，兩百名受虐婦女會由例行親密伴侶暴力篩查系統而被挑選及招募。根據我們以前的經驗，大約七至八成受虐婦女的身體傷害是頭部受傷。婦女的心理和生活質量也將進行評估。 本研究是由多學科研究小組進行，具有經驗豐富及專業訓練的醫生，護士，社工和統計學家。這將確保這項研究能成功地了解親密伴侶暴力對婦女的認知功能的損害，從而將有利於適時的介入及提供照護，以及如何調理受虐婦女的身理，心理和認知的影響。

757613.label: Project Title(Chinese)
757613.value: 學生違規行為的成因：三年追蹤研究

757613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
757613.value: Student misbehaviour can disrupt teaching and the classroom environment, cause teacher stress and strain, lower the students’ academic achievement, and increase future delinquent behaviour. As in Western contexts, it is a growing area of concern in Chinese school contexts. However, student misbehaviour and its precursors is a relatively under-researched area in Hong Kong. This research will therefore examine the psychological predictors and perceived causes of school misbehaviour among Chinese junior secondary school students, particularly exploring the roles of positive youth development, life satisfaction and school satisfaction in influencing school misbehaviour. The positive youth development approach emphasizes the strengths students have for healthy growth that can thwart problem behaviour and enable them to strive in adversity. But little research has looked specifically at the role of positive youth development on school misbehaviour. Satisfaction with life and with school may also have mediating effects on this behaviour. Furthermore, few studies investigate the causal explanations for misbehaviour from both teachers’ and students’ perspectives. The proposed project therefore aims to address these gaps through a three-year longitudinal study adopting mixed-method research strategies, including (i) a quantitative study examining the predictive influences of positive youth development, life satisfaction and school satisfaction on school misbehaviour over time, and (ii) a qualitative study investigating causal explanations for school misbehaviour amongst students and teachers and their discrepancies, and related changes across time. Stratified cluster sampling will be used to randomly recruit twelve secondary schools in Hong Kong, and about 2,160 Grade 7 students will participate in the three-year longitudinal survey. The direct and mediating effects of positive youth development, life satisfaction and school satisfaction on school misbehaviour will be tested, and statistical models will be developed. Furthermore, 24 Grade 7 students and 24 teachers in these schools will be recruited to join individual interviews. The interview findings will give a fuller picture of the antecedents of school misbehaviour with richer information from multiple perspectives. Integrative data analysis will be used to compare the results of quantitative and qualitative data analyses to provide an integrative account of the roles of positive youth development, life satisfaction and school satisfaction in influencing school misbehaviour. With triangulation by different research methods and data types, this research will provide a complete portrait of the research phenomena, and will have significant contributions to theoretical and methodological advancement in related research areas, practices of school guidance and discipline, and teachers’ professional development. 學生違規行為在華人學校漸受關注。不少文獻指出違規行為會阻礙課堂教學，增加老師壓力，影響學生的學業成績。可是，尤其在香港，很少研究集中了解違規行為的前因。因此，是項研究將探討香港初中學生的違規行為，與青少年正面成長、生命滿足感和學校滿足感的因果關係。 這是一項三年的追蹤計劃，包括量性及質性研究。在量性研究中，透過分層群集抽樣，大概2,160位來自12所中學的中一學生，分別會在中一、中二及中三學年填寫問卷。收集數據經統計及分析後，用以了解正面成長、生命滿足感及學校滿足感與違規行為的機率關係。在質性研究中，24位曾參與量性研究的學生將會在中一、中二及中三學年接受個人訪問，以了解他們對違規行為的因果解釋。此外，24位老師亦會接受個人訪問，以了解老師與學生的見解之相同或差異。最後，量性和質性數據將會被綜合分析，以進一步了解青少年正面成長、生命滿足感、學校滿足感與違規行為的因果關係。此研究不但能對研究課題作出深入的了解，豐富現有理論及研究方法，亦能對學校的訓輔工作及教師培訓作出貢獻。

757713.label: Project Objectives
757713.value: To determine whether logographemes (subcomponent units) are represented during character recognition. To identify the neural correlates of logographeme representation in reading.
rows: To determine whether logographemes (subcomponent units) are represented during character recognition.
To identify the neural correlates of logographeme representation in reading.

757713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
757713.value: This project aims to address two fundamental questions regarding the orthographic representation of Chinese characters; do logographemes features affect word recognition during reading, and if so, when during the character recognition process are such features are accessed and used? The latter question will be answered using event-related potential (ERP) methods. Within the past two decades, psycholinguistic studies of character recognition have amassed a body of evidence demonstrating that complex characters are automatically decomposed into sub-lexical components referred to as radicals during reading and writing in Chinese. However, some studies have argued that the decomposition of characters goes beyond the level of radicals and to the logographeme level of representation. Logographemes are reoccurring patterns composed of a series of stroke patterns but appear to be smaller sub-lexical units than the radical. Yet, the only source of evidence that has demonstrated that such a level of representation exists in the orthographic processing system has come from less than a handful of patient case-studies examining writing errors. Thus, the generalizability of such claims remains inconclusive given the small sample size and observations being limited to spelling tasks per se. The proposed project aims to fill this research gap by extending beyond writing and into reading processes that assume similar representational levels exist in reading and writing. Such evidence for logographeme representation in reading will have widespread implications for character recognition models such as the Lexical Constituency model (Perfetti & Liu, 2006; Perfetti, Liu & Tan, 2005) and the Multilevel Interactive-Activation framework (Taft, 2006; Taft & Zhu, 1997; Taft, Zhu, & Peng, 1999), which do not assume a logographeme representational level.

758413.label: Project Title(Chinese)
758413.value: 「鄰避症候群」？ 詮釋反對公屋的合理性

758413.label: Project Objectives
758413.value: To understand why opposition to the siting of public housing has increased in Hong Kong To investigate how actors construct the legitimacy of different oppositional frames To explore possible strategies which may help alleviate conflicts over siting of public housing in Hong Kong
rows: To understand why opposition to the siting of public housing has increased in Hong Kong
To investigate how actors construct the legitimacy of different oppositional frames
To explore possible strategies which may help alleviate conflicts over siting of public housing in Hong Kong

758413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
758413.value: This project examines the tensions which emerge in the siting of affordable housing. While the public accepts the need for affordable housing in general, there is often strong opposition when concrete projects are proposed. Although siting conflicts are nothing new, the issue takes on a different hue in Hong Kong, a city where the government enjoys ownership over all land and dominant powers over development rights. Thus in the past, the government of Hong Kong has faced relatively limited constraints in developing public rental housing. In recent years, however, there has been increasing resistance to the siting of public housing across different districts, which is a matter of key concern given the worsening problem of housing affordability in the territory. The primary aim of this research is to develop an interpretive understanding of opposition to siting of affordable housing in Hong Kong. The first part of the project involves tracing the siting strategies of affordable housing providers in Hong Kong, to establish the characteristics of neighbourhoods where opposition to siting proposals has increased over the years. In particular, it adopts the three concepts of beliefs, traditions, and dilemmas from interpretive institutionalism to account for such changes. In doing so, it addresses a key gap in the literature on siting conflicts, which tends to focus on compiling typologies of rationalities to account for oppositional behavior, but which pays less attention to understanding why public reaction to siting proposals changes over time. The second part focuses on the notion of legitimacy, to investigate how the legitimacy of different oppositional frames are actively constructed and reconstructed within the policy debate over affordable housing. Through analysis of documentary data and in-depth interviews with actors involved in controversial sites, it seeks to explore how some opposition motives are regarded as legitimate concerns, while other motives are labeled as illegitimate ‘NIMBY’ behavior. The final part explores how actors respond to the frames constructed by other actors, which offers us insights into possible strategies of reframing that could help alleviate siting conflicts. Overall, this project adds to our understanding of siting conflicts, by moving away from static explanations towards a more dynamic interpretation of how actors construct legitimacy and how their beliefs and actions may change over time. In doing so, it provides valuable insights into possible reframing of apparently intractable debates, and how future tensions over the siting of affordable housing could possibly be reconciled. 社會大眾普遍支持興建公屋，但當計劃推出時，往往遇上很大阻力。反對公屋的聲音在香港愈來愈大，而且遍及各區，要解決龐大的公屋需求，實在困難。 本研究透過詮釋理論，解究反對公屋的理由。研究先了解反對地區的特質，再透過分析文獻和深入訪問，了解為何部份反對理由被視為合理訴求，其他理由卻被標籤為「鄰避症候群」。 研究旨在跳出「鄰避症候群」的狹窄框架，嘗試了解文化、價值在爭議中扮演的角色，有助日後解決公屋選址問題。

758413.label: Realisation of objectives
758413.value: The primary aim of this research was to explore the emerging phenomena of opposition to public housing in Hong Kong. The first objective was to understand why opposition has increased in recent years, through examining documentary evidence on controversial cases. This objective has been successfully achieved through reviewing minutes of meetings held by all 18 district councils of Hong Kong over a ten-year period, as well as news reports on high-profile cases of community opposition, in order to identify all sites that involve opposition to public housing, and to zoom into those districts with particularly significant cases of controversy. After this review, three key districts were identified for more in-depth case study research. Key actors from these three districts were interviewed to gauge their perceptions of the reasons behind opposition, and to compare their perceptions with common explanations found in the international literature. These key actors mainly included elected district councilors, resident representatives as well as concern group representatives, who were especially familiar with the history of controversial projects in their neighbourhoods. The second objective was to investigate how different actors involved in these planning conflicts constructed the legitimacy of oppositional frames, through reviewing documentary data as well as in-depth interviews with key actors. This objective was also successfully achieved in each of the selected case study areas. Broadly speaking, two different types of neighbourhoods could be identified – one type being dominated by existing private homeowners, the other type being dominated by public housing residents. Prior to conducting in-depth interviews, the researcher identified key oppositional frames from documentary records, including news reports, minutes of district council meetings and Town Planning Board meetings. In particular, the researcher analysed how these frames changed over time, and how these changing framing strategies may help explaining the changing dynamics of selected case study projects. For example, it was observed that there was a tendency for private homeowners to justify their opposition through references to negative environmental impacts, which appeared to be more legitimate than concerns for property values. However, over time, emerging discourses on the severity of low-income housing problems appeared to have dampened the credibility of opponents’ oppositional frames, which helps explaining eventual approval of contested housing projects. In addition, since these planning cases tended to extend over a period of time, the researcher also explored the negotiations underpinning conflict resolution processes, throughout different phases of selected projects. As expected, it was relatively difficult to gauge these processes from documentary evidence alone, since meeting records only reflected discussions in formal council meetings, without fully reflecting the interactions between key stakeholders outside of formal meetings. Nevertheless, the researcher was able to investigate these processes through conducting in-depth interviews with key stakeholders, especially those who were heavily involved in all phases of planning processes. These interviews successfully revealed the negotiations which were conducted between local politicians and the government, especially those which took place through informal consultation meetings. Thus, the triangulation of multiple sources of data helped achieving the second research objective, by uncovering the formal and informal arenas in which framing contests have unfolded. The third and final objective of the study was to explore possible strategies which may help alleviate conflicts over siting of public housing in Hong Kong. This was achieved by asking interviewees to respond to the claims of other actors, such as responding to allegations of NIMBYism from the media and the government. In addition, the researcher paid attention to areas of overlap or contradiction, which may indicate potential scope for reconciling opposing views. Indeed, further analysis indicated that some opponents have actually agreed to trade-offs between open space and public housing developments in their neighbourhoods, after mitigation measures have been introduced. Nevertheless, they have often been blamed for causing housing undersupply problems, although they have expressed legitimate concerns about infrastructure deficits in high-density neighbourhoods, and their requests have not led to insurmountable delays in the planning process. Thus, in the latter stages of the study, it was necessary to return to the international literature, to identify theoretical frameworks that may help explain why this type of opposition has been negatively labelled in recent years. Theories from the political literature were identified to support interpretation of these findings, which highlights how the label of NIMBYism can be strategically deployed to attribute the cause of housing undersupply to neighbourhood resistance. This could be interpreted as a political tactic to divert attention away from alternative interventions that may increase land supply for public housing, but which may materially interrupt the status quo. Indeed, these analyses suggest that apart from examining the strategies which may help alleviate conflicts over public housing projects, it may be helpful to examine who gains and who loses in deploying the language of NIMBYism, and to critically consider the power relations which underpin this discursive struggle, which may represent fundamental obstacles to new housing delivery. In other words, reframing the debate away from site-specific mitigation strategies may facilitate problem resolution, by directing attention towards alternative siting strategies that may help address ongoing challenges of increasing public housing supply in the city.

758413.label: Summary of objectives addressed
