760413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
760413.value: Background: Glass ionomer cements (GICs) are common filling materials used to restore dental decay, especially decay involving tooth roots. However, although they release fluoride ions that help teeth become more resistant to decay, the available clinical evidence has not conclusively shown that GICs prevent decay. A new ion-releasing agent based on proteins found in cow’s milk, namely, casein phosphopeptide amorphous calcium phosphate (CPP-ACP), has been shown to prevent tooth decay and heal early decay in human teeth. Laboratory tests demonstrated that CPP-ACP, when incorporated into a GIC filling material, can prevent acid dissolution of teeth better than GICs that do not contain CPP-ACP. If this filling material is able to stop the acid attack associated with decay, it may serve as an effective treatment option for root surface caries and prevent decay in enamel. Objectives: This study will investigate 1) the ability of a GIC containing CPP-ACP to inhibit decay on tooth roots and enamel surfaces using an artificial mouth model and 2) biofilm (bacterial growth) formation on modified GIC surfaces in comparison to natural tooth surfaces and other filling materials. Methods: Blocks of extracted human teeth with enamel and root surface cavities will be prepared and filled with either the CPP-ACP GIC or comparison materials. Subsequently, they will be exposed to dental decay using an artificial mouth model. Twenty blocks of each material will be prepared, inoculated with decay-forming bacteria in an anaerobic artificial mouth and periodically supplied with sucrose nutrients during a 3-week period. Blocks will be evaluated for hardness, elemental composition, biofilm pH variation and development. Potential Results and Benefits: The CPP-ACP GIC filling material may be effective at preventing and stopping decay in tooth roots, which could benefit elderly patients and those with special needs who frequently have this decay. Furthermore, this material is simple to use, even in locations where dental facilities are limited (e.g., nursing homes). The CPP-ACP GIC can also be used to prevent/heal early decay on the biting surfaces of paediatric teeth. CPP-ACP is known to change biofilms on tooth surfaces, and an altered biofilm on the modified GIC can help to prevent new decay from occurring after a filling is placed. The CPP-ACP GIC is a more simplified and less costly treatment option for all age groups and serves as an effective preventive coating material for teeth, especially for individuals with limited access to treatment (e.g., infirm and special needs patients).

760413.label: Realisation of objectives
760413.value: The 4 objectives of the study were achieved by this study. Firstly, we found the new CPP-ACP containing GIC inhibited the development of on root surfaces of extracted human teeth in vitro. Secondly, we found the new CPP-ACP containing GIC inhibited the development of caries/demineralization on enamel surfaces of extracted human teeth in vitro. Thirdly, we found the new CPP-ACP containing GIC could remineralise early caries lesions on enamel and root dentine surfaces in vitro. Finally, we found the new CPP-ACP containing GIC could not alter biofilm formation (quantity and quality) in comparison with GICs without the CPP-ACP. A total of 4 publications indexed in major databases for Dentistry such as ISI Web of Science, PubMed and Scopus. One student project based on this grant has won one of the prestigious award (2017 IADR Heraeus Travel Awards) of The International Association of Dental Research.

761013.label: Project Title(Chinese)
761013.value: CD44在狼瘡性腎炎發病機制中的作用

761013.label: Project Objectives
761013.value: NZBWF1/J mice will be treated with a pan anti-CD44 antibody that blocks CD44-HA interactions. Mice will be sacrificed to assess the effect of CD44 on serologic, clinical and histologic changes pertaining to lupus nephritis, with particular focus on the inflammatory and fibrotic processes. Age- and sex-matched BALB/c mice will be used as controls. Mesangial cells and proximal tubular epithelial cells will be isolated from glomeruli and proximal tubules respectively that have been obtained from BALB/c and NZBWF1/J mice. 761013.label: Realisation of objectives
761013.value: CD44 is a family of glycoproteins that has wide tissue distribution and can exist in multiple isoforms generated by alternative splicing. Under physiological conditions, immune and non-immune cells synthesize the standard form of CD44 (CD44s), whereas the expression of CD44 variants is associated with inflammatory conditions and cancer. CD44 is a major cell surface receptor for hyaluronan and plays important roles in cell proliferation, migration, cell-matrix interaction and tissue remodeling. This study aimed to (i) investigate the role of CD44 in inflammatory and fibrotic processes in the pathogenesis of lupus nephritis, (ii) determine the expression of CD44s and its variants (CD44v3 and CD44v6) in renal specimens from patients with lupus nephritis and their association with clinical, serological and histological parameters of disease, and (iii) measure the level of soluble CD44s and CD44v6 in sera from patients with lupus nephritis and ascertain whether CD44s and/or CD44v6 may serve as biomarkers of disease. We have fully completed Objectives 3 and 4, and Objectives 1 and 2 are ~80% completed. In Objective 1, female NZBWF1/J mice with active lupus nephritis were randomized to 3 groups and treated with PBS, Control IgG and pan anti-CD44 antibody (150 micrograms/mouse) once weekly by tail-vein injection, for up to 12 weeks. Age- and sex-matched BALB/c mice were used as controls. The dose of anti-CD44 antibody was chosen based on our preliminary studies that showed that this concentration could reduce proteinuria by ~30% after administration for 2 weeks, and also on the feasibility of its generation and costs. Administration of anti-CD44 antibody to BALB/c mice for 12 weeks had no effect on kidney histology throughout the study period. Kidney histology in PBS- and Control IgG-treated NZBWF1/J mice with active disease showed glomerular hypertrophy and mononuclear cell infiltration into the perivascular, periglomerular and interstitial space. As disease progressed, glomerulosclerosis, crescent formation, tubular atrophy and protein casts were observed, and this was accompanied by increased ERK, p38 MAPK, PKC-alpha and AKT/PI3K activation, and increased expression of IL-6, MCP-1, fibronectin and collagen in the kidney parenchyma. CD44 gene and protein expression increased with progressive disease and was detected in parietal epithelial cells, mesangial cells, podocytes and tubular epithelial cells. Intense CD44 expression was also noted in crescents and in areas of interstitial fibrosis. A subpopulation of inflammatory cells infiltrating glomeruli and tubulo-interstitium were also stained positive for CD44. Administration of CD44 antibody to NZBWF1/J mice showed moderate improvement in histology with decreased influx of infiltrating cells into the tubulo-interstitium, less tubular atrophy and decreased amount of protein casts but had no apparent effect on glomerular and interstitial inflammatory and fibrotic processes. Furthermore, there was no statistical difference in serum creatinine, albumin or anti-dsDNA antibody levels or proteinuria in PBS-, Control IgG- and anti-CD44 antibody-treated mice. In Objective 2, glomeruli were isolated from BALB/c and NZBWF1/J mice by differential sieving and mesangial cells obtained by collagenase treatment. Mesangial cells constitutively expressed low CD44 level. CD44 expression was significantly increased in cells stimulated with exogenous IL-1beta, but not IL-6, TNF-alpha, MCP-1 or TGF-beta1. This was accompanied by increased fibronectin, collagen III and hyaluronan expression and activation of ERK, JNK, p38 MAPK and PI3K signaling pathways. Using specific inhibitors to MAPK and PI3K, IL-1beta was shown to induce CD44 through p38 MAPK, JNK and PI3K activation. Pharmacological inhibition of hyaluronan was accompanied by decreased CD44 expression, suggesting that IL-1beta and hyaluronan regulated CD44 expression. Recombinant mouse CD44 had no effect on cell viability or proliferation, and increased fibronectin and laminin expression in a dose- and time-dependent manner through activation of p38 MAPK and PI3K signaling pathways. Our data suggest that CD44 may contribute to increased fibrogenesis through increased cytokine secretion by resident renal cells and activation of MAPK and PI3K signaling pathways. In Objective 3, we investigated the expression of CD44s and its variants in renal biopsies from patients with lupus nephritis and compared their expression to that detected in patients with non-lupus renal diseases such as IgA nephropathy and diabetic nephropathy, and normal kidneys. Intense staining for CD44s, CD44v3 and CD44v6 was observed in the glomerulus and tubulo-interstitium in patients with active proliferative lupus nephritis and non-lupus renal diseases, whereas CD44s was weakly expressed in normal kidney specimens. The expression of CD44v3 and CD44v6 were negligible in normal kidney specimens. In patients with lupus nephritis and non-lupus renal disease, subpopulations of infiltrating immune cells were also stained positive for CD44v3 and CD44v6 in the glomerular and tubulo-interstitial compartments. As observed in lupus-prone mice with active disease, CD44s was also detected in crescents and areas of fibrosis. Tubulo-interstitial CD44s expression was associated with inflammatory cell infiltration, tubular atrophy and tubulo-interstitial fibrosis. In Objective 4, we determined serum levels of CD44s and CD44v6 in patients with lupus nephritis and compared the level with that detected in patients with non-lupus renal disease and healthy subjects. Serum CD44s level was significantly higher in patients with lupus nephritis, especially during active disease, when compared to control groups. Similar findings were also observed for CD44v6 level. Serum CD44s level in patients with lupus nephritis correlated with serum anti-dsDNA antibody, creatinine, IL-8 and MCP levels, and inversely correlated with C3 level. CD44v6 level in patients with lupus nephritis correlated with serum creatinine, IL-8 and MCP-1 levels, and inversely correlated with serum IgG level. Receiving operating characteristic curve analysis showed that serum CD44s, but not CD44v6 level distinguished patients with active lupus nephritis from healthy subjects with sensitivity and specificity rates of 83.33 and 90.38% respectively (P<0.001). Taken together, our data highlights an association of CD44 and its variants with serological and clinical parameters of disease and a possible role in systemic and kidney inflammation, and kidney fibrosis. Our observation that the CD44 antibody showed no apparent effect on inflammatory and fibrotic processes in the kidney may be due to the fact that the concentration used was too low to neutralize the increased level of CD44 synthesized during chronic inflammation and severe disease. We have modified our methodology to generate more anti-CD44 antibody and in the coming 4-6 months, we plan to administer higher doses to lupus-prone mice to determine whether it can improve clinical, serological and histological parameters of disease.

761013.label: Major findings and research outcome
761013.value: In this study, we demonstrated that CD44s and its variants contribute to renal inflammation and fibrosis in lupus nephritis. Serum CD44s and CD44v6 levels were significantly higher in patients with active lupus nephritis when compared to lupus nephritis patients in remission, patients with other renal diseases and healthy subjects, the level of which showed a temporal relationship with disease activity and correlated with clinical and serological parameters of disease and inflammation. Serum CD44s level could distinguish patients with active lupus nephritis from healthy subjects. Assessment of renal specimens from patients and mice with active lupus nephritis showed that CD44s was weakly expressed in normal kidney whereas CD44v3 and CD44v6 expression was absent. In renal specimens from patients and mice with active lupus nephritis, intense staining for CD44s, CD44v3 and CD44v6 was observed in the glomerulus and tubulo-interstitium and was detected in areas of fibrosis, in crescents and in areas of increased influx of inflammatory cells. Tubulo-interstitial CD44s expression was associated with inflammatory cell infiltration, tubular atrophy and tubulo-interstitial fibrosis. Increased CD44s and its variants was not specific to lupus nephritis patients since similar findings were also noted in renal specimens from patients with non-lupus renal diseases such as IgA nephropathy and diabetic nephropathy, suggesting that CD44 may contribute to both acute kidney injury and chronic kidney disease. Our in vitro studies showed that hyaluronan and IL-1beta regulated CD44 expression through activation of ERK, p38 MAPK, JNK and PI3K signaling pathways in murine mesangial cells isolated from NZBWF1/J mice. CD44 in turn increased matrix protein expression through of MAPK and PI3K activation. Taken together, our data suggests a role of CD44 in inflammatory and fibrotic processes in lupus nephritis and may represent a novel target for therapeutic intervention. Part of the data have been presented at four international meetings including the American Society of Nephrology Kidney Week, which is the top-ranked international nephrology meeting. Part of the data generated from this study have also been included in an invited review published in Clinical Immunology, and a manuscript on the clinical data is currently under preparation.

761013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
761013.value: Published data have shown that different variants of CD44 have distinct functions to CD44s and may exert favorable or detrimental effect on tissues. Further development of this project will include studies to delineate the functional role of CD44v3 and CD44v6 in the pathogenesis of lupus nephritis. Since alternative splicing can generate up to 10 different CD44 variants, the identification of other variants in progression of lupus nephritis and their function in renal injury will be assessed, and findings validated in knockout mice. Since CD44 is also expressed in parietal epithelial cells, podocytes and endothelial cells, we will apply for funding support from the Food and Health Bureau and RGC General Research Fund to further elucidate the distinct role of CD44 variants in renal inflammation and fibrosis and whether the effect is mediated through their interaction with hyaluronan or is independent of hyaluronan.

761013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
761013.value: Lupus nephritis is an important cause of acute injury and chronic kidney failure in this locality. The pathogenesis of disease remains to be fully defined. Although treatment of lupus nephritis has improved considerable over the past 2 decades, the use of immunosuppressive agents is associated with many adverse side effects. Knowledge of the underlying mechanisms that contribute to pathogenesis is important in order to devise novel and specific therapeutic intervention. In this study we demonstrated that serum CD44 level was significantly increased in patients with lupus nephritis especially during active disease when compared to control groups, and was associated with markers of kidney injury and disease activity. Kidney CD44 expression was markedly increased in lupus nephritis patients when compared to normal kidney specimens and was associated with kidney inflammation and fibrosis, especially in the tubulo-interstitium. Given that the tubulo-interstitium accounts for almost 90% of the kidney volume, changes in this compartment of the kidney will have a profound effect on kidney function. In murine mesangial cells, we further demonstrated that CD44 increased matrix protein expression and contributed to kidney fibrosis. Our data provide insight into the pathogenic role of CD44 in lupus nephritis.

761113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
761113.value: In adult life, loss or damage to articular cartilage that lines the bone surfaces of joints is the hallmark of arthritic diseases, which are common reasons for people of all ages to seek medical care. Synovial joints are encased in a capsule, stabilized by ligaments and tendons on the outside and lined by a synovial membrane inside. Within the synovial joints, articular cartilage provides a smooth, wear-resistant structure that reduces friction and absorbs impact forces. A clear understanding of how a synovial joint develops and the identification of progenitor cells that contribute to its formation and maintenance is essential for the development of therapeutic strategies for degenerative joint diseases. Recently, we identified a stem cell marker, Lgr5, to be expressed specifically in interzone cells at the earliest stage of joint formation. We showed that Lgr5-expressing (Lgr5+) interzone cells are progenitors that contribute to the formation of the supporting tissues such as the ligaments and synovial membrane, and more importantly the articular cartilage surfaces. We further identified cells co-expressing Lgr5+ and an extracellular matrix gene, Col22a1. With the progression of joint development these cells become mainly Col22a1+ cells lining the surface of the articular cartilage. We propose this expression pattern represents the progression of cell fate in joint development, with the double-positive cells comprising cells committed to becoming articular cartilage. Using mouse reagents that already exist for marking Lgr5 and Col22a1 expression, we will test this hypothesis. We will also use these markers to isolate the different pools of cells in the interzone so as to obtain their molecular signature, with the aim of gaining insights into the molecular regulation required to establish in vitro differentiation of interzone cells. We further hypothesize that some Lgr5+ cells become resident progenitor cells in the synovium membrane or articular cartilage, and that these participate in the repair process when a joint is damaged. Mouse strains (MRL and LG/J) heal with complete closure and tissue regeneration of ear-hole puncture wounds and re-growth of damaged articular cartilage. The cellular contribution to the healing process is not known. We propose to study the role of Lgr5+ cells in the repair process in vivo and the potential of exogenous Lgr5+ interzone cells in the repair of cartilage defects, comparing these strains with normal controls, addressing the role and fate of Lgr5-expressing cells and their potential function as progenitors in the formation and repair of the articular cartilage. 各年齡階段的成年人都會受到關節炎的困擾而尋醫問藥。關節軟骨位於骨關節的表面，它的磨損或破壞是關節炎的共同表征。滑膜關節被一層關節囊包裹，由外部的韌帶和肌腱固定，囊內襯有滑膜。在滑膜關節內部，關節軟骨提供了一個光滑的結構來減少相鄰兩骨間的摩擦以及運動帶來的壓力。深入理解滑膜關節的形成並鑒定祖細胞在關節形成及維護中的作用，對於研發退化性關節疾病的臨床治療策略是至關重要的。最近，我們證明了一個祖細胞標記分子 Lgr5, 在關節形成最早期的關節中間區具有特異性表達。我們的數據顯示，表達 Lgr5 (Lgr5+）的關節中間區細胞具有祖細胞特性，它們參與關節及其附屬組織如韌帶，滑膜，甚至關節軟骨表層的形成。我們更進一步證明了隨著關節的發育，共同表達Lgr5和細胞外基質蛋白 Col22a1的細胞會逐漸轉變為主要表達Col22a1的細胞而存在於關節軟骨的表層。我們認為這種表達模式可以反應出細胞在關節發育過程中的命運變化，即同時表達 Lgr5 和 Col22a1的細胞將最終分化形成關節軟骨。我們利用現有的轉基因小鼠模型來標記 Lgr5 和 Col22a1 的表達以驗證這一假設。同時，我們還將利用這些標記手段來分離位於關節中間區的不同細胞群以獲得其分子特性的相關信息。這將有助於我們深入了解關節中間區細胞的分子調控機制，從而建立關節中間區細胞的體外分化方法。我們進一步提出假設，一些表達 Lgr5 的細胞可以長期存在於關節滑膜和關節軟骨中，並且在關節受到損傷時參與關節的損傷修復過程。MRL 和 LG/J 小鼠品系具有很強的再生的能力，比如其刺穿的耳孔可以完全愈合，其損傷的關節軟骨可以在一定程度上再生。參與這些愈合過程的細胞機制尚未清楚。我們將對Lgr5表達細胞在損傷修復過程中的作用進行在體研究，並考查外源性Lgr5表達細胞修復損傷軟骨的能力。將這些具有較強再生能力的小鼠與正常品系的小鼠相比較，我們可以了解Lgr5表達細胞作為祖細胞在關節軟骨的行成和損傷修復過程中發揮的作用及其細胞命運。

761213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
761213.value: We firstly reported that Transforming growth factor (TGF)-β-activating kinase 1 (TAK1) is a serine/threonine kinase which is frequently associated with human cancer progression through the activation of NF-κB signaling. Furthermore, we showed that GRO-α and IL-8 are major chemokines in the tumor microenvironment of cancerous omenta and are associated with increased ovarian cancer aggressiveness. Both chemokines can activate TAK1/NFκB signaling via the CXCR2 receptor and particularly higher in metastatic ovarian cancer cells. Blocking CXCR2 by genetic or pharmaceutical approaches significantly attenuated TAK1/NFκB signaling and decreased in vitro and in vivo oncogenic and metastatic potential, suggesting CXCR2 plays a key role in the GRO-α and IL-8-governed metastatic spreading of ovarian cancer cells in the intraperitoneal cavity. Intraperitoneal metastasis is a common occurrence and is usually involved in the poor prognosis of ovarian cancer. Its specific metastatic pattern implies that certain indispensable microenvironmental factors can direct metastatic ovarian cancer cells to permissive niches for secondary lesion formation. Our findings highlights the significance of GRO-α and IL-8 and suggests the utility of targeting their receptor CXCR2 or in combination of TAK1 signaling could be a potential target-based therapy for peritoneal metastases of ovarian cancer.

761213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
761213.value: Clinical observations have shown that ovarian cancer accompanied with peritoneal metastases usually indicates a very poor prognosis. Emerging evidence suggests that malignant ascites act as a reservoir, providing plenty of fatty acids, soluble growth factors and chemokines for use in remodeling shed ovarian cancer cells to more aggressive metastatic cancer cells. However, how of the chemokines as oncogenic drivers to promote ovarian cancer progression are ill defined. In this study, we decipher n underlying molecular mechanism of two major chemokines; IL-8 and GROa, could enhance ovarian cancer oncogenic properties through activation of TAK1/NFkB signaling through a cell membrane receptor, CXCR2. If we use genetic approaches such as gene knockdown or knockout to remove CXCR2, or pharmaceutical approaches such as CXCR2 inhibitor (SB225002) or TAK1 inhibitor ((5Z) -7-Oxozeaenol) could remarkably impair the oncogenic properties of ovarian cancers. Our findings underscore the relevance of the tumor microenvironment in facilitating ovarian cancer metastatic progression and aid in the exploration of CXCR2 as a potential therapeutic target for ovarian cancer metastasis.

761413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
761413.value: 無論是在西方國家還是香港，卵巢癌都是導致女性死於癌症的重要原因之一。卵巢癌主要的治療包括手術以及之後的化療。然而，即使經過最佳的治療，癌症復發的情況依然很常見，總體預後不容樂觀。卵巢癌細胞同時表達兩種雌激素受體——經典的雌激素受體（ERα）和新的雌激素受體（ERβ）。在乳腺癌細胞中，這兩種受體有著完全相反的作用， 但它們在卵巢癌中扮演的角色仍然不甚清晰。在之前的研究中，我們發現卵巢癌細胞中ERβ的表達降低，預示其對腫瘤有抑制作用。激素療法的副作用很小，因而一度很受歡迎。然而，它莫西芬——一種選擇性雌激素受體調節劑（SERM），對卵巢癌的治療效果不甚理想。由於它莫西芬可以同時和上述兩種在致癌過程中可能有著相反作用的雌激素受體結合，所以使用新研製具有選擇性亞型的SERM能增強其對腫瘤細胞的治療效果。 ERβ異構體的發現進一步豐富了其生物學作用。我們初步的研究顯示ERα和ERβ異構體（ERβ1, ERβ2 and ERβ5）在卵巢癌中有蛋白質的表達。和ERβ1的低表達形成對比的是，我們檢測出ERβ2和ERβ5在卵巢癌中有較高表達。但是它們在卵巢癌中的臨床地位、作用以及對SERM治療的影響還不得而知。此外，不管是體外實驗還是體內實驗，我們發現ERα拮抗劑（MPP）對ERα的阻滯作用或者ERβ激動劑（DPN）對ERβ的刺激作用都很大程度地抑制了卵巢癌細胞的繁殖，並降低了蛋白激酶B（AKT）的活性。 我們提出這樣的假設，ERα, ERβ1, ERβ2 和 ERβ5在卵巢腫瘤的發生過程中扮演不同的角色。根據ER的亞型和ERβ的異構體的表達，計而採取特定的SERM治療法來靶向個體化的ER亞型，通過基因途徑和信號通路，從而對腫瘤起到抑制的作用。 我們建議：（1）評估ERα, ERβ1, ERβ2 和 ERβ5在卵巢癌中的亞細胞定位以及臨床地位；（2）顯示單獨使用或聯合使用針對特定ER亞型的SERM治療對卵巢癌細胞增殖、凋亡和細胞轉移以及體內腫瘤生成的效果；（3）檢查在有和無SERMs療法的情況下，ERβ2和ERβ5對癌細胞功能的影響作用；（4）探究引導上述功能的基因途徑和信號通路。這些臨床前期的研究成果可以為卵巢癌確立新的治療目標，同時有可能為體內表達不同ER亞型和ERβ異構體的病人制定出選擇化、個體化的激素治療法，使副作用減至最少，從而達到最佳的臨床效果。

761413.label: Realisation of objectives
761413.value: Objective 1: To evaluate the subcellular localization and clinical significance of ERα and ERβ variants (β1, β2 and β5) in ovarian cancer Work has been done: We have evaluated the subcellular localization and clinical significance of ERα and ERβ variants (β1, β2 and β5) in 139 formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue blocks of ovarian cancer, including 13 benign cystadenomas, 20 borderline tumors, 90 carcinomas with different histological subtypes and 16 corresponding metastatic foci. Results showed differential expression of ERα, ERβ1, ERβ2, ERβ5 in the nucleus/cytoplasm of benign/borderline and malignant ovarian tumors. Significantly higher nuclear (n)ERα and nERβ5 and lower cytoplasmic (c)ERα expression were found in advanced cancers. We also observed significant lower ERβ1 expression in high grade cancers. Significant loss of nERα and cERβ2 expression were detected in clear cell histological subtypes. Higher nERβ5 and lower cERβ5 expression were associated with serous/clear cell histological subtypes, poor overall and disease-free survival. Positive cERα, and higher cERβ1 expression were associated with better overall and disease-free survival. Further analysis showed nERβ5 as an independent prognostic factor for overall survival. Furthermore, subcellular expression of ERα, ERβ1, ERβ2 and ERβ5 in nuclear and cytoplasmic fractions of SKOV3, an ovarian cancer cell line, was also confirmed by western blot analysis. Objective 2: To characterize the effects of individual or combined treatment of SERMs (through specific ER subtypes) on ovarian cancer cell proliferation, apoptosis and cell invasion as well as in vivo tumorigenicity. Work has been done: We have investigated the effect of selectively targeting each ER subtype on ovarian cancer growth. Ovarian cancer cell lines SKOV3 and OV2008, expressing both ER subtypes, were treated with highly selective ER modulators. XTT assay revealed that treatment with 1,3-bis(4-hydroxyphenyl)-4-methyl-5-[4-(2-piperidinylethoxy)phenol]-1H-pyrazole dihydrochloride (MPP) (ERα antagonist) or 2,3-bis(4-hydroxy-phenyl)-propionitrile (DPN) (ERβ agonist) significantly suppressed cell growth in both cell lines. In contrast, 4,4',4″-(4-propyl-[1H]-pyrazole-1,3,5-triyl) trisphenol (PPT) (ERα agonist) or 4-[2-phenyl-5,7-bis(trifluoromethyl)pyrazolo[1,5-a]-pyrimidin-3-yl]phenol (PHTPP) (ERβ antagonist) significantly enhanced cell growth. These in vitro results were further evaluated with a xenograft model where SKOV3 cells were injected s.c. into ovariectomized mice. The average size of xenografts in both the DPN-treated group and the MPP-treated group was significantly smaller than that of the vehicle-treated group. Furthermore, we also observed that combined treatment with MPP and DPN in SKOV-3 cells showed a synergistic effect in suppressing ovarian cancer cell growth. Our findings indicate that targeting ER subtypes may enhance the response to hormonal treatment in women with ovarian cancer. We also examined the effect of 2-(3-Fluoro-4-hydroxyphenyl)-7-vinyl-1,3-benzoxazol-5-ol (ERB-041) (ERβ agonist in clinical trial on rheumatoid arthritis) on ovarian cancer cell migration and invasion. Transwell migration and invasion assays revealed that treatment with ERB-041 significantly inhibited cell migration and invasion in cell lines with ERβ expression including SKOV3 (8 hours after plating cells), A2780CP (40 hours) and ES-2 (16 hours) cells. However, XTT and TUNEL assays revealed no significant effect on cell proliferation and apoptosis after ERB-041 treatment. Objective 3: To examine the effects of ERβ2 and ERβ5 on cell functions with or without SERMs treatment. Work has been done: ERβ2 and ERβ5 full length plasmids were constructed. Stable overexpression of ERβ2 and ERβ5 in ES-2, OVCA420 and OVCAR-3 was performed. The effects of ERβ2 and ERβ5 on cell migration, invasion and proliferation were examined. A wound healing assay revealed a faster migration rate in ES-2 stably transfected with ERβ2 and ERβ5. In addition, transwell migration and invasion assays also revealed significantly increased migration and invasion in ERβ2 and ERβ5 overexpressing ES-2, OVCA420 and OVCAR-3 cells. By cell count method, ERβ5 significantly induced cell proliferation in ES-2, OVCA420 and OVCAR-3 cells at days 8/9. By focus formation assay, the number of colonies from OVCA420 cells overexpressing ERβ5, but not ERβ2, increased by about 75% compared with control cells. Transient overexpression of ERβ2 and ERβ5 in TOV-21G (a clear cell histotype) was also performed. Transwell migration and invasion assays revealed significantly increased migration and invasion in ERβ2 and ERβ5 overexpressing TOV-21G cells. We also determined the effects of ERβ2 and ERβ5 on cell migration, invasion with ERB-041 treatment in ES-2 and TOV-21G. Transwell migration and invasion assays revealed ERβ2 and ERβ5 mediated increase in cell migration and invasion was blocked by ERB-041 treatment. Objective 4: To delineate genomic and non-genomic signaling pathways in mediating the above effects. Work has been done: We examined the effects of SERM treatment on the expression of estrogen-responsive genes. We found that EGFR and FBLN-1 showed altered protein expression in SERMs-treated cells in the presence of E2. In vehicle-treated SKOV3 cells, the addition of E2 induced the expression of EGFR and FBLN-1. The addition of MPP, DPN, or combined SERM treatment (MPP+DPN) suppressed the expressions of EGFR and FBLN-1 induced by E2. We then determined the nongenomic pathway and found that phospho-AKT expression in SKOV3 cells were reduced by 80% after treatment with MPP and DPN, suggesting the AKT pathway was involved. As the phosphorylation of serine 473 in AKT is an activating phosphorylation of the AKT protein, these results indicated that the AKT activity in SKOV3 cells was suppressed by MPP and DPN. We also detected decrease of phospho-focal adhesion kinase (FAK) in SKOV3 cells after treatment with ERB-041. We further investigated the possible downstream signaling of ERβ5. FAK, a cytoplasmic tyrosine kinase, is a key component of cell-matrix adhesion complexes, thus play a critical role on cancer cell migration, invasion and metastasis. We found that ERβ5, but not ERβ2, induced FAK activity as detected by phosphorylation on Tyr 397. To examine the involvement of ERβ5-induced FAK activity on cell migration and invasion, overexpressing ERβ5 ES-2 and OVCA420 cells were treated with a FAK inhibitor (FAK inh 14). FAK inh 14 inhibited FAK activation and abolished both basal and ERβ5-mediated cell migration and invasion. Besides metastasis, FAK also promote cell proliferation. Intriguingly, FAK inh 14 blocked the ERβ5-mediated increase in ES-2 and OVCA420 cell proliferation.

761413.label: Major findings and research outcome
761413.value: Major findings: We found that aberrant ERα, ERβ1, ERβ2 and ERβ5 expressions contribute to ovarian tumorigenesis. Since tamoxifen binds to both ERα and ERβ1 which appear bear opposing oncogenic roles, the histotypes-specific expression pattern of ERs found in the present study indicates that personalized ovarian cancer treatment for women based on their ERs expression status using selective estrogen receptor modulators may improve response rate. This study also suggests nuclear ERβ5 to be a potential prognostic marker and therapeutic molecular target in ovarian cancer. Functionally, we found that ERβ5 overexpression promoted ovarian cancer cell migration, invasion and proliferation via activation of FAK whereas ERβ2 induced cell migration and invasion. Our findings of in vitro and in vivo SERM treatment suggest that targeting specific ER subtypes after determining the relative ER subtypes may enhance the response to hormonal treatment in women with ovarian cancer. We found that blockage of ERα by ERα antagonist (MPP) or stimulation of ERβ1 by ERβ agonist (DPN) in ERα+ or ERβ1+ ovarian cancer cells inhibited cell proliferation, implicating the opposing roles of ERα and ERβ. Synergistic effect was achieved when using ERα antagonist and ERβ agonist together in ERα+ERβ1+ cells. We also observed ERβ agonist (ERB-041) reduced cell migration and invasion in ovarian cancer cells. Akt and FAK pathways were involved in SERM treatment in ovarian cancer Hormonal treatment offers a very good option for women because of its low toxicity profile. Selective ERβ agonist has already been developed for clinical use and has been tested in phase 2 clinical trial for treatment of menopausal symptoms and rheumatoid arthritis. Our preclinical results on ER subtypes selective modulations and their mechanisms of action in ovarian cancer can potentially translate to selective, personalized ovarian cancer treatment for patients with different ERs status to obtain better clinical response with minimal side effects. Research outcome: 1. A conference abstract was published in International Workshop on Women’s Reproductive Health Research in 2014. 2. A paper ‘Targeting estrogen receptor subtypes (ERα and ERβ) with selective ER modulators in ovarian cancer’ was published in Journal of Endocrinology in 2014. 3. A paper ‘Differential expression of estrogen receptor subtypes and variants in ovarian cancer: effects on prognosis, cell invasion and proliferation’ has been submitted to BMC Cancer and is in revision. 4. Another paper related to the effect of ERB-041 in ovarian cancer is in preparation for submission.

761413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
761413.value: Our present findings suggest selective ER modulators targeting ER subtypes may be better hormonal agents compared to the current standard hormonal treatment with tamoxifen in ovarian cancer patients. ERB-041, a ERβ selective agonist, is already in clinical trials for rheumatoid arthritis. With our preclinical data, this drug can be further explored for possibility of clinical trials in ovarian cancer patients. Apart from these synthesized compounds, naturally occurring compounds were also found to act selectively at ERβ . Epidemiological studies found that soy isoflavone intake is associated with reduced risk of ovarian, breast and prostate cancers in china and Japan. Soy isoflavones are considered as phytoestrogens which can mimic the binding of estrogens to ERs, exerting estrogenic effects on target organs. As the prime source of isoflavones, soybeans contain 12 isoflavones in total, with genistein and daidzein constituting 60%, 30% of total isoflavones respectively. Genistein and daidzein were found to act via the effects on ERβ. In our preliminary study, we observed that genistein and daidzein inhibited ovarian cancer cell migration, invasion and proliferation. Future in vitro and in vivo studies will be performed to investigate the potential use of isoflavones on anti-tumoriogenesis in ovarian cancer.

761413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
761413.value: Ovarian cancer cells are hormone responsive, making hormonal therapy an attractive treatment option because of its good side effects profile. In this study, we explored the possibility of targeting estrogen receptor β (ERβ) for treatment of ovarian cancer. The ERβ receptor has many variants (ERβ1, ERβ2 and ERβ5). We found that in different ovarian cancer cell types, the subcellular location of these receptors were different eg there was high nuclear ERβ5 expression in serous/clear cell ovarian cancer and this was associated with a poorer prognosis. We found that ERβ5 overexpression promoted ovarian cancer cell migration, invasion and proliferation via FAK activation. This suggested that nuclear ERβ5 would be a potential prognostic marker and therapeutic target in ovarian cancer. Furthermore, we demonstrated that ERβ1 stimulation by ERβ agonist significantly inhibited cell proliferation, migration and invasion. The combined treatment with ERα antagonist and ERβ agonist displayed a synergistic effect in suppressing ovarian cancer cell growth in vitro and in vivo and these effects were associated with reduced AKT activation. Our results on ER subtypes selective modulations and their mechanisms of action can potentially translate to personalized treatment for ovarian cancer patients, with better clinical response and less side effects.

761713.value: 食管鱗狀細胞癌特別流行於亞洲，於香港癌症死亡率排名第八。由於高復發率和高轉移率，食管鱗狀細胞癌的總體預後較差。因此，對這個高度侵襲性疾病進行更有效的治療需要有效的目標識別以開發新療法。最近，我們進行一個綜合性的轉錄組測序（RNA-SEQ）三對病人源性食管鱗狀細胞癌和相關食管鱗狀細胞癌的淋巴結轉移灶的分析，成功地確定了一些經常差異表達的基因。我們最近報告了標記CD90在淋巴結轉移中顯著上調，它標誌著一個特定的食管癌腫瘤幹細胞（CSC）的子集（鄧等，癌症研究，在修訂中）。同時，神經纖毛-2（NRP2）被我們發現是在淋巴結轉移對比原位食管鱗狀細胞癌時最顯著上調的基因。隨後在較大量的臨床樣本驗證中進一步表明NRP2基因組和蛋白質水平上調在淋巴結轉移比較在原位食管鱗狀細胞癌常見。大部分食管鱗癌細胞株相比匯集正常對照組（5個正常食管樣本）或永生化正常食管細胞系NE3，也有發現NRP2上調。 NRP2被擊倒後食管鱗狀細胞癌轉移被壓抑，但促進了上皮-間質轉化（EMT）標記和基質金屬蛋白酶（MX / WS）的表達。此外，我們發現NRP2優先表達於CD90+轉移性食管鱗狀細胞癌CSC亞群，並賦予它們的自我更新能力和轉移能力。我們推測NRP2在特定的CD90+食管癌CSC子集，通過調節EMT和基質金屬蛋白酶，在食管鱗狀細胞癌轉移中起著至關重要的作用。鑑於這些令人振奮的新數據，我們建議：1）使用在體外實驗和在體內轉移模型來顯示NRP2在食管鱗狀細胞癌轉移中起的功能性效果，2）檢查NRP2 在CD90+食管CSC子集的表達，和NRP2於促進食管CD90+幹細胞驅動腫瘤的復發和轉移上的劃定作用，3）利用臨床食管鱗狀細胞癌組織樣本，評估NRP2獨自或結合CD90表達的臨床及預後意義。據我們所知，本研究將代表第一次調查NRP2在食管癌轉移的作用。此研究將提供一個NRP2在食管鱗狀細胞癌轉移功能效果的在體內有力示範。由NRP2驅動食管鱗狀細胞癌轉移的CD90+癌幹細胞樣細胞特定子集和NRP2驅動癌症幹細胞類似的行為的作用也將被探討。此外，這項臨床相關性研究將有助於確定NRP2作為一種潛在的食管癌預後和治療的新型標記。我們預計這些新的分子途徑，能確定有助於食管鱗狀細胞癌的進展和發展新的食管鱗狀細胞癌的靶向治療策略。

761713.label: Major findings and research outcome
761713.value: Oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is the most common histological subtype of oesophageal cancer. The disease is particularly prevalent in southern China. The incidence of the disease is on the rise and its overall survival rate remains dismal. Identification and characterization of better molecular markers for early detection and therapeutic targeting are urgently needed. Here, we report levels of transmembrane and soluble neuropilin-2 (NRP2) to be significantly up-regulated in ESCC, and to correlate positively with advanced tumor stage, lymph node metastasis, less favorable R category and worse overall patient survival. NRP2 up-regulation in ESCC was in part a result of gene amplification at chromosome 2q. NRP2 overexpression promoted clonogenicity, angiogenesis and metastasis in ESCC in vitro, while NRP2 silencing by lentiviral knockdown or neutralizing antibody produced the opposite effect. This observation was extended in vivo in animal models of subcutaneous tumorigenicity and tail vein metastasis. Mechanistically, overexpression of NRP2 induced expression of ERK MAP kinase and the transcription factor ETV4, leading to enhanced MMP-2 and MMP-9 activity and, as a consequence, suppression of E-cadherin. In summary, NRP2 promotes tumorigenesis and metastasis in ESCC through deregulation of ERK-MAPK-ETV4-MMP-E-cadherin signaling. NRP2 represents a potential diagnostic and prognostic biomarker, and therapeutic target of ESCC.

761713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
761713.value: We propose to further the study by applying NRP2 neutralizing antibody, alone or in combination with standard chemotherapy treatment, in an in vivo animal model of ESCC.

761713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
761713.value: The study aimed to characterize the role of NRP2 gene in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), and to explore the potential use of NRP2 for diagnosis, prognostication and treatment of ESCC. Results of the present study has uncovered a novel oncogenic and metastatic role of NRP2 in ESCC, and assert its potential use as a diagnostic and prognostic biomarker. A novel underlying mechanism by which NRP2 drives this malignant progression, via ERK-MAPK-ETV4-MMP-E-cadherin signaling was deciphered. Based on the scientific information we have gathered so far, further works are needed to test the hypothesis that targeting NRP2 and its signaling pathway, can provide us with a novel and effective treatment modality of ESCC.

761813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
761813.value: The lung repair and regeneration following acute lung injury plays a crucial role in the outcome from severe pneumonia and recent publications strongly suggest the adult distal airway stem cells play critical role during this process. The discovery of p63-expressing airway stem cells in lung repair using a murine-adapted H1N1 influenza virus mouse model, and the cloning of the same cell types in human deep airways suggest new therapeutic avenues. However, the role of lung stem cells on lung regeneration upon highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 virus infection has not been investigated. Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), the most severe form of acute lung injury, has been the cause of severe illness and death in most patients with H5N1 disease. The high lethality of human H5N1 disease, especially in the context of its continued pandemic potential, makes it important to explore the underlying disease mechanisms, as well as the role of lung stem cells, in regenerating the damaged lung post-H5N1-infection. Our recent unpublished data (the first study in the world) led us to hypothesize that the p63-expressing distal lung stem cells may contribute to the lung repair process following H5N1 infection in the mouse. In this research proposal, we propose to investigate the mechanism underlying the proliferation, migration and differentiation of p63-expressing stem cells during lung repair following influenza H5N1 virus infection using in vitro human cell and in vivo mouse models and use low pathogenic influenza H1N1pdm virus for comparison. We hypothesize that HPAI H5N1 virus differs from low pathogenic influenza virus in its ability to achieve lung regeneration that these differences are the critical factor governing the significant clinical outcome from such infections. Finally, we will investigate the role of selected soluble factors, e.g. Krt6a, Serpinf1, Klk7, that are likely to be essential for determining the kinetic and regulation of lung regeneration after influenza H5N1 virus infection. I believe that the investigation of these mechanisms will offer new insights and potentially lead to the development of new treatment options for patients suffering from ARDS caused by influenza H5N1 virus infection and also other pathogens that cause severe lung injury. 在最近發表的研究顯示，成年遠端氣管幹細胞對重症肺炎造成肺急性肺損傷後的修復和肺部再生擔當著重要的角色。研究發現，會表達p63的氣道幹細胞能在肺修復模型中，修護被已適應的小鼠甲型H1N1流感病毒感染的肺部,所以在人類深呼吸道複製出相同類型的細胞能開拓新的治療途徑。但是，幹細胞對高致病性禽流感 (HPAI) H5N1病毒感染後的肺再生過程中的角色還需要進一部研究。感染 H5N1病毒令大多數病患者出現急性呼吸窘迫綜合症候群 (ARDS),這是一種最嚴重的急性肺損傷，會引致嚴重的疾病和死亡。在對人類有高殺傷力的高致病性禽流感Ｈ５Ｎ１病毒持續流行的潛在性背景下，探索其疾病機制和肺幹細胞在肺部受H5N1病毒感染後復元過程中所擔當的角色變得尤其重要。根據我們近期未發表的數據（世界上的首批研究），我們推測帶有p63表達的遠端肺幹細胞可能有助於實驗老鼠修復受H5N1病毒感染的肺部。在這項研究建議中，我們會以人體細胞體外和活體小鼠模型調查p63表達幹細胞在流感 H5N1後的增殖、遷移和分化機制，並使用低致病性的 H1N1pdm流感病毒進行比較。我們推測H5N1型高致病性禽流感病毒，跟低致病性流感病毒會有不同的肺部再生作用，而這些差異是決定臨床結果的關鍵因素。最後，我們將調查某些被選的可溶性因子，例如 Krt6A, Serpinf1, Klk7, 這些很可能是H5N1流感病毒感染後感染動力學和調節肺部再生的重要因素。我相信研究這些機制將對H5N1流感病毒及和其他病原體感染引起的ARDS提供新的見解，並發展新的治療方案。

762213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
762213.value: Influenza virus disease causes significant public health concerns. Although seasonal influenza virus usually not leading to fatality, its high transmissibility in humans makes the disease burden substantial. Influenza virus is not yet eradicable because of its vast reservoir in animals and high mutation rates. Scientists employ various strategies, including cell cultures and animal models to study the tissue tropism and pathogenesis of these viruses. Amongst all the available studying models, primary human respiratory organ cultures take a very important role in providing clinically relevant data to reflect host responses of human upon influenza infection. This setup of human airway culture has been established and utilized in our laboratory for more than six years. Briefly, human lung tissue alone (without circulation system) is cultured with optimized conditions outside human body with a viability and physiological relevance up to a week. With this model, we have addressed important questions regarding the tissue tropism of highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 viruses, the 2009 pandemic H1N1 virus and also employed as a risk assessment model to evaluate the likelihood for the swine and avian viruses that isolated from Hong Kong surveillance program to start a new pandemic in humans. With a further analysis of the virus replication efficiency in human respiratory tract culture, it may serve as a useful predictor to virus transmissibility and if we read the data in a yearly manner, a correlation with the epidemiology of the population is observed. The experimental result generated from this setup is the largest and most comprehensive infection series to date. Here, we generated a hypothesis based on the yearly pattern of virus replication data that, without the peripheral immunity from the circulation, human lung can exert local immunity to control influenza virus infection in a strain specific manner, possibility through the antibody present at the alveolar epithelial lining fluid and the resident memory T cells. To prove this hypothesis, we are going to determine if lung fluids possess neutralization effect towards specific influenza virus strain and examine the effect of lung resident memory T cells in affecting the pattern of replication by eliminating them from the lung culture in situ. I believe that the investigation of these mechanisms will offer new insights and potentially lead to the development of new treatment options for patients suffering from novel strain of influenza virus infection. 流感病毒造成重大公共衛生問題。雖然季節性流感病毒通常不會導致患者死亡，但它在人類之間的高度傳染性，仍造成持續性的社會負荷。由於流感病毒的高突變率和大部分流感病毒都於動物界積存，使到流感病毒尚未可以根除。 科學家採用不同的策略來研究這些病毒的組織向性及發病機制，當中包括細胞培養和動物模型。原代人類呼吸道器官培養是個非常重要的模型，這個研究模型能提供臨床相關的數據，以反映人類流感病毒感染後的宿主反應。 我們實驗室已經建立並使用此人類呼吸道培養設置超過六年。簡單地說，我們能把人肺組織獨立地（無循環系統下）培養在一個已優化的體外環境長達一個星期，該組織並同時具有存活性及生理相關性。利用這個模型，我們了解有關高致病性禽流感H5N1病毒，及2009年的流行性H1N1流感病毒的組織向性等重要問題。此外，我們也為香港監察計劃中分離出來不同的豬流感和禽流感病毒進行了風險評估，推測它們會爆發成為新的流感大流行的可能性。透過分析病毒在人類呼吸道的複製效率，我們能預測病毒傳播能力，並按每年所讀取數據，觀察到流行病學的相關性。通過此實驗模型所產生的結論是目前最大和最全面的。 我們根據每年病毒的複製模式數據生成一個假設。在不需要循環系統的外週免疫下，人類肺部有可能通過在肺泡上皮表面液體的抗體和駐肺記憶T細胞，產生對特定流感病毒菌株的局部免疫性。為了證明這項假設，我們要確定肺流體是否對特定的流感病毒株具有中和作用，並以原位的方式消除肺組織培養中的駐肺記憶T細胞，以檢查它們對病毒複製模式的影響。 我們相信，這些機制的研究將對流感病毒提供新的了解，並為感染未知流感毒株的患者開發新的治療方案。

762213.label: Realisation of objectives
762213.value: The original budget request for the project was HK$1,205,560 and the funded budget was HK$692,826, which is 57% of the requested budget. Therefore, the number of subjected recruited into this study had to be readjusted and the number of experiments had to be reduced due to the budget cut. Nevertheless, this project served as a proof-of-concept project to check if the lung local immunity would play a role in influenza virus defense. Objective 1: 100% In the first objective, we measured the concentration of Ig, IgA, and IgG of the epithelial lining fluid (ELF) using ELISA assay and detected the presence of influenza virus-specific antibody using indirect immunofluorescence assay (IIFA) and neutralization test from individual lung and tested for their association towards its susceptibility to influenza virus inoculation. Lung wash and lung homogenate were prepared from 19 lung samples. Lung wash from each individual was generally having higher total Ig than lung homogenate (Figure S1A and B), while both of these samples have detectable Ig. In contrast, IgA concentration in lung homogenate from the same donor was higher than those detected in lung wash samples (Figure S1C and D). IgG concentrations in both the lung wash and lung homogenate samples were mostly below 20 ng/ml, and some of which were below detection limit with an exception of donor 19 (Figure S1E). In the representative donor, individual variation across the donor population in terms of the presence of specific IgA towards H1N1pdm was observed. The intensity of the fluorescence signal was not well correlated with the IgA concentration detected in the ELISA assay. However, this may due to the difference in the influenza-specific IgA to the total IgA ratio. Objective 2: 100% Hemagglutination inhibition (HI) assay was used to quantify the concentration of influenza A virus-specific antibody against A/HK/54/98 (H1N1) and A/HK/415742/09 (H1N1pdm) as described previously. However, from the 21 lung wash samples tested, only two of them have a HI titer of 1:20 to seasonal H1N1 (A/HK/54/98) and one of them has an HI titer of 1:10 to H1N1pdm (A/HK/415742/09), others were all negative in the HI test of these three strains of influenza viruses. A similar result was found in the HI test using lung homogenate samples, three out of 20 samples were having 1:10 or 1:20 HI titer against seasonal H1N1, while there were no positive samples found in the HI test using H1N1pdm. Therefore, it suggested that the local immunity of ex vivo lung culture may not contribute to the Ig in the alveolar ELF Objective 3: 100% The serum titer showed no difference between H1N1pdm and H1, with a mean HI titer of 1:190 and 1:164, respectively (Figure 1A, n = 37) and a mean MN titer of 1:65 and 1:76, respectively (Figure 1B, n = 35). If we used the protective titer of 1:40 as the cutoff value for a 50% reduction in the prevalence of infection1, all of the samples collected after 2015 exceeded this threshold (Figure 1C). However, it is worth to note that, this 1:40 cutoff value is controversial and varies across age group. Moreover, an age-adjusted value cutoff value for H1N1 would be much higher than 1:40. At the same time, the same serum sample which had an HA titer might not necessarily neutralize the H1N1pdm or H1 virus in the microneutralization (MN) assay, e.g. L279 and L309 for H1N1pdm and L264, L287, L292 and L302 for H1N1(Figure 1C and D). The virus replication competence of these two viruses in the lung slice ex vivo culture infection study was plotted from 24 hours post infection (hpi) to 48 hpi. The total viral yield was expressed in the area under curve (AUC) as described3. The overall and time-stratified replication efficiency of the seasonal H1N1 virus was higher than H1N1pdm (Figure 2A, p < 0.0001, pair-t-test, two-tailed). With the comparable HI and NN titers between H1 and H1N1pdm but a higher viral load of H1 than H1N1pdm in the ex vivo lung infection experiment, it was tested by regression that there were no associations identified between the HI titer (Figure 2B) and MN titers (Figure 2C) in the serum to the viral yield in the ex vivo infection of the lung. This piece of data infers the specific antibody titer in the circulation does not pose a specific effect to the decreased virus replication kinetics of A/HK/415742/09 (H1N1pdm). Objective 4: 100% We proposed to perform in situ depletion of CD4 and CD8 T cell population. We had performed three more trials with modified incubation length and the inclusion of a shaker at 30 rpm to enhance a more efficient antibody penetration. However, no significant decrease in either the CD4 or the CD8 T cell population were achieved in these attempts. Therefore, with the failure of the in-situ depletion, the specific objective 4b) the addition of lung CD4 and CD8 memory T cell into the depleted lung slice culture was not performed. This was mentioned in the second progress report. Objective 5: 100% The original protocol to be used to isolate the lung resident memory T cells was adopted from PLoS ONE. 2011;6(1): e16245. However, after three attempts and personal communication with Dr Purwar (email conversation and protocol exchange), the published method was still not working. We switched to the protocol used in mouse lung memory T cell isolation and determined the number of lung resident memory T cell by flow cytometry. Eleven human lung samples were acquired from Feb to July 2017 for single cell isolation using a combination of collagenase II and DNase I. Using this method, an average of 6.6+/-3.0x10^6 cells/ gram of lung tissue could be obtained with an average viability of 86.6+/-5.7% as indicated in the trypan-blue exclusion assay. Flow cytometry was used to further examine the population of this lung cell suspension (Figure 3). 5.2+/-0.6% of the overall cell population were lymphocyte and the viability of them was 77.2+/-2.1% in freshly prepared cell suspension. Within these lymphocytes, 56.5+/-1.4% (fresh) to 29.0+/-1.5% (frozen) of them were CD3+ cells. Among the CD3+CD4+ cells, 12.2+/-0.3% (fresh) to 18.4%+/-1.3% (frozen) of them were CD69+CD103+ (T resident memory cells, TRM), and among these cells 4.9+/-1.3 % (fresh) to 2.5+/-3.6% (frozen) of them were CD11A+CXCR5+. In contrast, the frozen step enhanced the proportion of CD3+CD8+ cells (p = 0.01) from 21.0%+/-0.8% (fresh) to 44.5+/-0.4% (frozen). Interestingly, there was no significant difference percentage of the CD3+CD8+CD69+CD103+ cell and the CD3+CD8+CD69+CD103+CD11A+ CXCR5+ cell. We performed 1) the CD8+ T cell tetramer staining using multi-parameter flow cytometry to identify the percentage of influenza-specific CD8+ T resident memory cells and 2) the intracellular cytokine staining (ICS) of the CD4+ and CD8+ T resident memory cells using viral stimulation to examine their functional response. In the tetramer staining assay, we identified that the higher percentage of CD8+ Tet+ (Figure 4B, p = 0.09) and the TRM CD8+ Tet+ (Figure 4F, p = 0.08) were having a trend to reduce the replication competence of H1N1pdm in the ex vivo lung culture. In the ICS assay, we stimulated the lung cell suspension at an MOI of 4 and detected the IFNg+CD4+TRM and the IFNg+CD8TRM cells at 12 hpi. However, no correlation was identified with the virus replication competence in the ex vivo culture.

762213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
762213.value: The direct translation of the circulating influenza antibody titer to the protectiveness of influenza virus infection might warrant further investigation. The presence of CD8+TRM which is specific to influenza would help to reduce the virus replication competence in the local epithelium. The mechanism of such required further investigation. 762213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
762213.value: The project was originated from the observation of the seasonal H1N1 and the pandemic H1N1/2009 influenza virus replication patterns in the human lung ex vivo cultures from 2006 to 2012. We observed an interesting pattern of a steep increase in H1N1pdm virus replication in the human lung ex vivo culture collected during April to July 2009 to the almost flattened replication curve in the period of August 2011 to July 2012 onwards. As in our human lung ex vivo infection model, the system is isolated from the circulatory immunity, we aimed to determine the effect of the lung local immunity towards influenza virus. We found that though the epithelial lining fluid contains immunoglobulin, its concentration was not able to inhibit the binding of influenza virus to its receptors. The serum neutralizing competence was not associated with the virus replication competence in the ex vivo lung culture. In contrast, the local lung immunity towards H1N1pdm replication might contribute to the abundance of influenza-specific CD8+ and CD8+ lung resident memory cell (TRM). The mechanism to boost the influenza-specific CD8+ and CD8+TRM could be complementary to the vaccine which stimulates the virus-specific antibody in the circulation.

762313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
762313.value: 許多研究證明G蛋白偶聯受體能夠調控興奮性神經回路的突觸可塑性。在大腦皮層和海馬上，研究人員發現，不同腎上腺素受體分別偶聯的兩種G蛋白亞型（Gs和Gq蛋白）對長時程壓抑（LTD）和長時程增強（LTP）這兩種狀態有推拉的調控作用。但是目前還不清楚啟動同樣偶聯有Gs和Gq蛋白的不同五羥色胺受體能否調控這兩種蛋白信號通路的平衡，並且通過調節上述兩種G蛋白亞型通路對能否進一步掌控前庭活動依賴的突觸可塑性狀態也有待驗證。 由此我們提出一個假說，五羥色胺通過調整Gs/Gq蛋白的平衡實現對突觸可塑性不同狀態的推拉調控作用，而突觸可塑性狀態又限定了某種特定的前庭行為活動。進一步我們推測五羥色胺通過調節中樞前庭神經核團的突觸可塑性狀態來調控前庭行為活動。首先，用全細胞膜片鉗的方法，施加針對Gs或Gq偶聯受體的特異激動劑/拮抗劑來闡明在中樞前庭核團的興奮性突觸上，五羥色胺是如何誘導其對前庭活動依賴的長時程壓抑和長時程增強狀態的雙向調控（推拉調控）作用。當然，對於形成這種興奮性突觸可塑性細胞內機制也會說明，包括對細胞膜上AMPA受體插入和內吞的具體細節。 從這個研究中獲得的資訊可以為是否在活體中調製這類突觸可塑性具有可操作性這個問題提供參考框架。在整體上，用線性加速模式強烈啟動前庭細胞間突觸後，我們再施加Gs或Gq偶聯受體的特異激動劑/拮抗劑。此後，再離體取材，評估在啟動的前庭神經突觸中，五羥色胺對長時程可塑性的雙向調控作用。而且我們還會觀察這種五羥色胺的作用方式對整體前庭行為活動的影響。因此，該研究結果會揭示五羥色胺通過對Gs/Gq蛋白的作用實現調控突觸可塑性平衡的重要意義，因為不同的突觸可塑性平衡會驅動不同的前庭功能。 我們之前的實驗發現在前庭核團的離子型受體相關的突觸可塑性對於出生後建立空間圖譜和獲得重力感知能力是極為關鍵的。因此，這個結果自然讓我們提出假說：五羥色胺通過調控前庭神經元的突觸可塑性來完善發育過程中前庭神經網路的形成，以此來提高空間識別能力。此外，在出生後不同的發育時間點，我們用藥物干擾五羥色胺受體偶聯的Gs/Gq蛋白，以此能揭示動物獲得前庭感知的關鍵期，而這關鍵期又與五羥色胺調控突觸可塑性密切相關。

762313.label: Realisation of objectives
762313.value: The anxiolytic effects of serotonergic neuromodulation are well studied, but how the neuromodulatory function of serotonin (5-HT) affects sensorimotor coordination and postural control is unclear. The medial vestibular nucleus (MV) in the brainstem is a major output station for neurons that project to the vestibulo-spinal pathway. We hypothesized that different 5-HT receptor subtypes, with their distinct G-protein signalling pathways, would differentially modulate synaptic plasticity and/or neuronal excitability in vestibular circuits to suit the needs of the animal. We aim to find the relevant 5-HT receptor subtypes and reveal the behavioural relevance of the neuromodulatory effect of 5-HT on vestibular-mediated behaviour. OBJECTIVE 1: Using whole-cell patch-clamp techniques in brainstem slices of young rats, we showed that 5-HT could significantly enhance both inhibitory (GABAergic and glycinergic) and excitatory (glutamatergic) transmission within the MV. In particular, we revealed a novel subgroup of MV neurons with greatly enhanced glycinergic transmission after exposure to 5-HT. These effects were action potential-dependent, indicating that 5-HT acted on presynaptic neurons. This is corroborated by immunohistochemical evidence showing 5-HT receptor expression on glycinergic MV neurons. Taken together, these findings demonstrate that 5-HT regulates the excitability of MV neurons via adjusting GABAergic, glycinergic and glutamatergic inputs. G-protein-coupled 5-HT receptors expressed in the MV include 5-HT1A (Gi/o-coupled), 5-HT2 (Gq-coupled) and 5-HT7 receptors (Gs-coupled). We then pursued the role of each of these receptors in the MV. We showed that treatment of MV neurons with 5-HT7 receptor agonist reduced the amplitude of evoked-EPSC while treatment with 5-HT1A receptor agonist reduced the amplitudes of both evoked-IPSC and -EPSC. Conversely, treatment with the 5-HT2 receptor agonist enhanced both spontaneous-IPSC and -EPSC in MV neurons. These suggest that 5-HT1A/ 5-HT7 and 5-HT2 receptors exert differential effect to fine tune the response of MV neurons towards 5-HT. MV neurons in juvenile rodents show high degree of synaptic plasticity in the form of stimulation-dependent long-term depression (LTD) of neurotransmission. For plasticity of excitatory transmission, we found that high frequency stimulation (HFS) robustly induced LTD in 90% of type B neurons in the MV, while only 10% of type A neurons were responsive, indicating that type B neurons are the major contributors to excitatory LTD in the MV. To determine which 5-HT receptor was responsible for modulating LTD, combinations of single and dual agonist/ antagonist to target each specific 5-HT receptor were tested. This allowed us to pinpoint 5-HT7 receptors, but not 5-HT1A or 5-HT2 receptors, as the mediator for suppression of long-term depression (LTD) of excitatory transmission in MV neurons. For plasticity of inhibitory transmission, we found 5-HT1A receptors enhanced LTD induction of GABAergic transmission. This highlights functional segregation between 5-HT receptor subtypes, with Gs-coupled 5-HT7 receptor modulating plasticity of excitatory transmission and Gi/o-coupled 5-HT1A receptor modulating plasticity of inhibitory transmission. OBJECTIVE 2: Acute administration of 5-HT to the MV of postnatal day (P)14 rats impaired their performance in negative geotaxis (a behavioral readout of gravity detection) as well as balance beam test and rota-rod task (indicators of motor coordination), as compared with the saline control. The time required for the rats to accomplish the negative geotaxis reflex was significantly prolonged (from 4 s to 7 s) following 5-HT treatment. The time taken for the rats to traverse the horizontal balance beam was also significantly increased (from 10 s to 30 s). For rota-rod task, the time during which the treated rats stayed on the rod was significantly reduced (from 20 s to 10 s on the first training day, from 90 s to 20 s on the second training day, and from 120 s to 20 s on the third training day). To find the relevant 5-HT receptor, 5-HT1 and 5-HT7 receptor co-agonist 8-OH-DPAT or 5-HT2 receptor specific agonist alpha-M-5-HT was in vivo administered to the MV of P14 rats. Only 8-OH-DPAT resulted in poor performance in vestibular-related tasks similar to direct in vivo administration of 5-HT. To differentiate the contribution of 5-HT1 and 5-HT7 receptors, 5-HT1A receptor antagonist WAY 100135 was co-administered with 8-OH-DPAT. WAY 100135 co-administration abolished all 5-HT induced behavioural deficits. Altogether, this indicates 5-HT1A as the specific receptor for mediating the behavioural effects of 5-HT in the rat MV. To recruit serotonin-induced synaptic plasticity in vivo in P28 rats, we used two approaches. First, as a proof of concept test, the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor fluoxetine (Prozac) was given to rats in drinking water to increase 5-HT concentrations throughout the brain. Second, we used a chemogenetic approach to achieve spatially restricted 5-HT release in the MV. Retrograde labelling virus was used to specifically express chemogenetic activator proteins in serotonergic neurons in the raphe nucleus that projected to the MV. Addition of the chemogenetic activator CNO resulted in specific activation of serotonergic MV projecting neurons, and thus localized increase in 5-HT concentration. In both approaches, the percentage of cells exhibiting LTD of GABAergic transmission increased from less than 30% to more than 60%, a value similar to P5 rats. This effect was abolished by the use of specific agonists for 5-HT1A receptors, indicating that 5-HT1A receptors were responsible in mediating LTD in GABAergic transmission. This indicates successful in vivo recruitment of plasticity with serotonin by activation of 5-HT1A receptors. OBJECTIVE 3: Postnatal emergence of negative geotaxis reflex tested with rats placed on the slope at either mediolateral (ML) or anteroposterior orientation (AP) was accelerated following treatment of the VN at P1 with 5-HT2 receptor agonist (alpha-M-5-HT), as compared with the saline control. For the test at ML orientation, the emergence of adult-like response was shifted from P7 to P5. For the test at AP orientation, the time of emergence was shifted from P9 to P7. No long-lasting effect on negative geotaxis performance was observed when alpha-M-5-HT was applied at P14, after the emergence of the reflex. This indicates that neonatal perturbation of serotonergic synapses in the VN influences maturation of vestibular-related behaviour.

762313.label: Major findings and research outcome
762313.value: OBJECTIVE 1: Whole-cell patch-clamp recordings demonstrated that 5-HT1A and 5-HT2 receptors bidirectionally affected EPSC and IPSC frequency and amplitude, suggesting that they may form a “push and pull system” for excitability of MV circuits. The efficacy of LTD induction was taken as readout for plasticity of MV circuits. We revealed a novel function for 5-HT7 receptors in attenuating LTD of excitatory transmission in rats. Using combinations of specific agonists and antagonists for 5-HT receptor subtypes, we were able to rule out the participation of other 5-HT receptor subtypes reported to be expressed in the MV. (published in Li YH, et al. (2017) Neuropharmacology 123:242-8.). Conversely, 5-HT1A receptors were found to enhance LTD of inhibitory transmission in the MV. This suggests that 5-HT1A and 5-HT7 receptors could function as a “push and pull system” to fine tune MV neuron plasticity. OBJECTIVE 2: We further showed that the effects of 5-HT on vestibular-related behaviours were mediated by 5-HT1A receptor activation in the MV. The effect of 5-HT on behaviour was revealed using 3 vestibular-related tasks, namely negative geotaxis test, balance beam test, and rota-rod test. Acute 5-HT infusion to the MVN impaired the performance of rats in all tasks. The effect of 5-HT could be recapitulated using specific agonist for 5-HT1A receptor, and abolished with co-administration of 5-HT1A receptor antagonist. (manuscript submitted to Neuropharmacology) OBJECTIVE 3: Given that neonatal perturbation of serotonergic synapses in the MV delayed postnatal emergence of graviceptive negative geotaxis reflex, we showed that postnatal perturbation of serotonergic synapses in the MV affects the developmental formation of the spatial map of serotonin receptor-expressing MV neurons that are functionally activated by natural vestibular stimulation (i.e. horizontal sinusoidal linear acceleration) in postnatal and young adult rats. Perturbation in young adult rats after emergence of graviceptive righting reflexes at P14 had no effect on the spatial map. We thus revealed a critical period for serotonin to modulate the maturation of vestibular function for acquisition of vestibular-related behaviours. (manuscript submitted to Journal of Physiology)

762313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
762313.value: This project delineates the differential contribution of Gs-, Gq- and Gi/o-coupled 5-HT receptors on excitability and plasticity of MV neurons. This highlights their specific roles in regulating activities of neural circuitry responsible for the expression of vestibular behavior. We found serotonergic neuromodulation to affect signal processing in the MV and impair sensorimotor functions. This suggests that use of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor antidepressants may impact synaptic transmission in neural circuits in the MV and affect higher functions such as vestibular-related spatial cognition. We demonstrated the efficacy of recruiting plasticity in vivo. These findings provide the basis for development of strategies to harness this plasticity in achieving functional rewiring of the brain for the treatment of neurological and emotional disorders.

762313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
762313.value: Different subtypes of serotonin (5-HT) receptors are coupled to distinct G-proteins and mediate specific signalling functions. 5-HT receptors were found to be organized into push/ pull systems for bidirectional modulation of signal processing in the central vestibular circuits. For example, 5-HT2 and 5-HT1A receptors function to increase or attenuate the excitability of the vestibular system respectively. Similarly, 5-HT7 and 5-HT1A receptors fine tune the plasticity of excitatory and inhibitory neurotransmission respectively in vestibular circuits. This forms the basis for development of strategies that harness such neural features to promote functional rewiring of neuronal circuits to treat neurological and emotional disorders. Using tests for graviceptive righting reflexes and for motor coordination, we found acute increase of 5-HT concentration in the brainstem vestibular nucleus resulted in impairment of motor function mediated by 5-HT1A receptors. This suggests the application of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors or activation of intrinsic serotonergic system to modulate central vestibular circuitry for rehabilitation of spatial cognition performance.

762713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
762713.value: Psychotic disorders are severe mental illnesses causing enormous burden to patients and society. Early intervention for psychosis has been the major focus in mental health care development worldwide in the last decade with particular emphasis on using operationalized clinical criteria in identifying individuals at high-risk for psychosis. It is suggested that intervention in this pre-psychotic period may prevent progression to full-blown psychosis. However, the major challenge is to accurately differentiate those who will become psychotic from those who will not before illness onset. Thus far, no robust predictors of psychosis transition have been identified and sensitivity of these clinical criteria remained low. Reward learning paradigm has been increasingly applied in psychosis research in recent years. First, reward system is related to dopamine, which is the key neurotransmitter dysregulated in psychosis, and the primary target of current drug treatment. Second, brain systems involved in reward processing are abnormal in psychosis. Third, reward system provides a useful theoretical framework linking symptom manifestations to neurobiological dysfunction underlying psychosis. Further, reward learning may be a useful candidate in psychosis prediction as studies demonstrating an association between dopamine dysfunction and psychosis transition in high-risk individuals. Literature indicated reward learning abnormalities in schizophrenia. Nonetheless, most studies are cross-sectional and examined chronic patients with longstanding dopamine-blocking treatment that may interfere with the results. Studies examining early psychosis patients before treatment initiation are sparse. Despite its close relationship with dopamine transmission and potential clinical implications in psychosis prediction, no studies evaluating reward learning in clinical high-risk sample have been reported. Additionally, the issue of whether reward learning may represent a trait marker (endophenotype) for psychosis remains unexplored. In this project, we will conduct (1) prospective 2-year follow-up study on clinical high-risk subjects to examine whether reward-learning independently predicts psychosis transition; (2) prospective 1-year follow-up of first-episode psychosis patients and healthy controls to investigate the course of reward learning deficits after illness onset; (3) comparisons between patients, their unaffected siblings and controls in reward learning to clarify its potential endophenotype status; (4) neuroimaging study to examine abnormal neural responses to reward learning in patients and at-risk subjects. We hypothesized that applying reward learning assessment in at-risk sample will enhance psychosis prediction which may facilitate pre-emptive intervention for psychosis in the future. Additionally, results on evolution and neural correlates of learning impairment will provide insights in neurobiological mechanisms underlying psychosis, thus enhance prospects of timely interventions to improve illness outcome. 思覺失調疾病是嚴重的精神病，對患者和社會造成巨大負擔。在過去十年中，思覺失調早期介入治療一直是全球精神健康服務發展的重點。新近發展的早期介入治療特別強調使用各種臨床標準來辨識可能出現思覺失調及精神分裂等相關病患病發的高風險人士。有研究指出在這段高風險時期作出介入治療可阻止病情發展至全面的思覺失調疾病。然而，要在徹底發病前準確辨識哪些人士將會患上思覺失調是一個重大的挑戰。到目前為止，醫學界仍沒有準確的預測標準去辨識哪些高風險人士將會演變成全面病發，而現有的臨床標準的準確度仍然不足。 近年來，獎勵學習認知範式越來越被廣泛應用於思覺失調研究。首先，腦部獎勵學習認知系統和一種神經遞質多巴胺有密切關係。思覺失調患者有多巴胺失調的情況，而目前的藥物治療主要用於抑制多巴胺失調。其二，思覺失調病人在進行獎勵學習認知時所涉及的大腦神經系統方面有異常。其三，獎勵學習認知系統提供了一個比較完整的理論框架去連繫臨床徵狀和思覺失調疾病的神經生物學功能障礙。此外，獎勵學習認知可能提供一個有用的標準去預測思覺失調的病發。研究指出高風險人士的多巴胺失調和思覺失調病發有著顯著關聯。 文獻指出精神分裂患者有獎勵學習認知功能障礙。儘管如此，大多數研究採用橫截面方法去研究長期患者，而他們長期接受有關多巴胺調控的治療亦可能會干擾研究結果。至今只有少量研究關注早期思覺失調患者在開始治療前的獎勵學習認知表現。儘管獎勵學習認知功能與腦部多巴胺活動關係密切，在預測思覺失調病發方面亦有潛在而且重要的臨床價值，但到現時為止仍沒有研究報導關於這類臨床高風險人士的獎勵學習認知表現。除此之外，關於獎勵學習認知功能是否可能成為代表思覺失調疾病的一個（內表型）特徵標記仍是未知數。 在這個項目中，我們將（一）進行為期兩年針對臨床高風險人士的跟進研究，以驗證獎勵學習認知功能是否能獨立預測思覺失調病發; （二）進行針對首發思覺失調患者及健康對照組的一年跟進研究，探討病發後獎勵學習認知功能的變化; （三）探討及比較病人、其未發病的兄弟姊妹以及健康對照組的獎勵學習認知功能，以澄清其潛在的內表型狀態; （四）進行腦掃描研究，探討病人及高風險人士在獎勵學習認知過程中可能出現的異常腦神經反應。我們推論有關獎勵學習認知功能的評估有助改善思覺失調病發預測和針對臨床高風險人士的早期介入治療。另一方面，關於獎勵學習認知功能的演變及腦神經關聯方面的研究結果亦可釐清思覺失調疾病背後的神經生物學成因機制，從而改善治療方法和效果。

762713.label: Realisation of objectives
762713.value: 1. Objective 1 -This was successfully achieved. We have recruited 110 clinical-high-risk (CHR) subjects and 41 demographically-matched healthy controls. Prospective 2-year follow-up for CHR sample was completed. Clinical, functional, cognitive and reward learning assessments were successfully conducted. To avoid confounding effort of genetic high-risk status on psychosis transition in CHR sample during follow-up, we restricted our subsequent analysis on reward learning to 97 CHR subjects who did not have family history of psychosis. At baseline, comparison of reward learning performance between CHR and control groups showed that CHR subjects exhibited significantly poorer rapid and gradual positive reinforcement learning (RL) than controls. In an attempt to examine the role of negative symptoms on learning performance and to minimize potential confounding effect of comorbid depression (as common secondary negative symptoms), we further classified CHR subjects into those with versus without primary negative symptoms (PNS) which was operationalized as having at least moderate level of negative symptom severity and no clinically significant depression. Comparison analyses were repeated among three groups: PNS CHR subjects (n=23), non-PNS CHR subjects (n=74) and controls (n=41). Results revealed that PNS group had the worst performance in both rapid and gradual positive RL, while non-PNS and control groups showed largely comparable task performance. Although, no significant correlations were found between RL parameters and negative symptom severity, our categorical analyses suggested that PNS may be critically associated with RL impairment in CHR sample. There were no deficits in value-guided decision-making ability observed either in the whole CHR sample or in PNS group. At 2-year follow-up, 14 out 97 CHR subjects were diagnosed to have full-blown psychotic disorder, with conversion rate of 14.1%. Prediction analysis indicated that baseline functioning, positive symptom severity and overall Go-bias (tendency to respond irrespective of reward feedback) independently predicted psychosis transition in CHR sample. Gradual positive RL was also found to be significantly difference between converters versus non-converters but was not retained in the final regression model for psychosis prediction. Taken together, our results provide evidence suggesting that reward learning performance measured at service entry may be a potentially useful measure to further enhance prediction model for psychosis development in individuals at CHR for psychosis. 2. Objective 2 -This was successfully achieved. We have studied 34 antipsychotic-naïve first-episode psychosis (FEP) and 41 demographically-matched healthy controls in reward learning. At 1-year follow-up, 27 FEP patients and 27 controls repeated reward learning experiment. Clinical, cognitive and functional assessments were also conducted for patient sample. At baseline, comparison analyses revealed that FEP patients showed significantly poorer performance in rapid positive RL as well as gradual positive and negative RL than controls in acquisition learning phase. No significant group difference was observed in transfer learning phase, indicating that value-guided decision-making ability was largely preserved in FEP patients. Association between rapid positive RL measure and negative symptom severity approached significance (p=0.056). At 1-year follow-up, FEP patients still continued to exhibit rapid positive RL impairment as compared to controls. Patients also showed poorer performance than controls in both gradual positive and negative RL, but only the latter approached significance. Transfer learning phase revealed no significant main effect of groups and no significant correlations between symptom and RL measures were noted. There was also no significant longitudinal relationship between baseline RL measures and 1-year symptom outcome. In sum, our findings indicated that FEP patients exhibited RL impairment. Such impairment was not attributable to dopamine D2 blockade effect of antipsychotic medication, but was likely due to inherent illness effect. Deficits in RL performance, in particular rapid learning persisted even after commencement of antipsychotic medication treatment, thereby suggesting RL abnormality as a trait rather than state impairment in psychotic illness. 3. Objective 3 -This was successfully achieved. We have evaluated 43 FEP patients (including both medicated and mediation-naïve FEP patients), 43 unaffected siblings and 33 healthy controls for comparison of reward learning performance. Our results showed that FEP patients and siblings had significantly poorer rapid positive RL performance than controls. FEP patients also exhibited significantly worse gradual positive RL than both siblings and controls (with the latter groups showed comparable performance). Hence, our findings indicated that, overall, siblings exhibited the degree of RL impairment largely intermediate between FEP patients and controls, and suggested that RL impairment may be a potentially useful endophenotype parameter for further research in psychotic disorders. 4. Objective 4 -This was successfully achieved. We have assessed 31 FEP patients, 23 non-psychotic siblings, 20 CHR subjects and 32 controls for fMRI investigation of reward learning. Behavioral results suggested reduction in learning in FEP patients and CHR subjects, with controls and siblings showing largely comparable performance. Compared with controls, FEP patients, CHR subjects and siblings showed attenuated ventral and dorsal striatal activation during learning experiment, with FEP patients showing the greatest degree of signal attenuation. Negative symptom severity was marginally correlated with signal attenuation in FEP sample, but not in CHR subjects. Our results thus suggested abnormal neural response to reward learning in patient with psychotic disorder as well as clinical and genetic high-risk samples.
