762713.label: Major findings and research outcome
762713.value: Major findings of the project are summarized as follows: Behaviorally, antipsychotic-naïve first-episode psychosis (FEP) patients exhibited rapid positive reinforcement learning (RL) impairment as well as gradual positive and negative RL at baseline relative to healthy controls. Negative symptom severity was found to be marginally associated with rapid positive RL measure. Value-guided decision-making ability was relatively preserved in FEP patients. At 1-year follow-up, FEP patients still continued to display rapid positive RL impairment. Patients also showed poorer performance than controls in both gradual positive and negative RL, but only the latter approached significance. No abnormality in value-guided decision-making was observed at follow-up. Baseline RL parameters did not significantly predict 1-year symptom or functional outcomes. Hence, RL impairment observed in FEP was not attributable to antipsychotic dopamine blockade but likely reflected inherent illness effect, and persisted after treatment commencement, Regarding patient-sibling comparison, our results revealed that siblings had impaired rapid positive RL relative to controls. On the other hand, FEP patients had significantly worse gradual positive RL than both siblings and controls, while the latter two groups showed no significant between-group differences in gradual learning parameters. Thus, overall, siblings had the degree of RL impairment intermediate between FEP and controls. For clinical high-risk (CHR) sample, we found that CHR subjects exhibited rapid and gradual positive RL impairment as compared to controls. Specifically, CHR subjects with primary negative symptoms (PNS) displayed the worst RL performance relative to both non-PNS CHR subjects and controls. Our categorical analyses thus suggested that PNS may be critically associated with RL impairment in CHR sample. There were no deficits in value-guided decision-making ability observed either in the whole CHR sample or in PNS group. At 2-year follow-up, 14.1% of CHR subjects converted to full-blown psychotic disorder. Prediction analysis indicated that baseline functioning, positive symptom severity and overall Go-bias (tendency to respond irrespective of reward feedback) independently predicted psychosis transition in CHR sample. This suggested that reward learning measures may be potentially useful to enhance psychosis in CHR sample. Our findings on functional MRI were largely consistent with the behavioral results, showing attenuated striatal activations to reward learning in FEP patients, CHR subjects and siblings, relative to controls, with negative symptom severity marginally related to abnormal neural responses in FEP sample.

762713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
762713.value: To facilitate translation of research findings of reward learning into real-world clinical application in clinical high-risk (CHR) populations, further prospective follow-up research with a large sample size is warranted so as to replicate our study findings and to confirm the potential utility of reward learning in enhancing prediction of full-blown psychotic disorder in individuals presenting with CHR. Additionally, adoption of combined neuroimaging approach of functional MRI and molecular imaging (i.e., PET imaging for in-vivo dopamine neurotransmission) will help to unravel the inter-relationships between abnormal neural responses, dysregulated dopamine striatal synthesis capacity and impaired reward learning in CHR sample, and hence the aberrant neurobiological mechanisms underlying psychosis transition. Given that value-guided decision-making is impaired in more chronic illness but relatively spared in FEP, longer-term follow-up of FEP sample is required to clarify the evolution and trajectory of value-guided decision-making abnormality, as well as its longitudinal relationship with symptom and functional outcomes.

762713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
762713.value: Reward learning is a promising translational research paradigm in psychotic disorders. Substantial evidence indicates reward learning abnormalities in schizophrenia, but most previous studies were cross-sectional in design and focused on chronic illness. This is the first longitudinal study to systematically simultaneously examine key reward learning sub-components, i.e., rapid versus gradual and positive versus negative reinforcement learning across first-episode psychosis (FEP) patients, their unaffected siblings (at genetic high-risk for psychosis) and individuals at clinical high-risk (CHR) for psychosis. Our findings demonstrated reward learning impairment in FEP, sibling and CHR groups. Impairment was most evident in rapid learning via positive feedback which was found to be related to negative symptoms. Importantly, we showed that learning impairment in FEP was not due to medication-induced effect and persisted after treatment. Further, reward learning was found to predict psychosis development in CHR individuals. Neuroimaging investigation also revealed abnormal neural responses to reward learning in patients and high-risk samples. Taken together, our findings provide evidence supporting the potential utility of reward learning in improving psychosis prediction in clinical-risk populations, and indicate that reward learning impairment likely reflects neurobiological abnormality inherent in illness that may also be useful to facilitate genetic investigation for psychotic disorder.

762813.value: 在现有的教科书中，软骨细胞和成骨细胞，虽归属不同的细胞系，但已被阐明来源于共同的成骨-软骨祖细胞，而转录因子Sox9的活性是决定祖细胞分化成为软骨还是成骨细胞的关键因素。在骨发育过程中，软骨细胞通过一系列的分化步骤而形成软骨，随后终极分化的肥大软骨细胞会死亡消失。随着血管的入侵，成骨细胞逐渐成熟形成内源性骨，并最后取代软骨。然而，关于肥大软骨细胞是否能转变成为成骨细胞并成为成骨细胞系的一部分已经被争论了近一个世纪，而如今我们的研究已经解决了这个议题。借助于一个它莫西芬诱导（tamoxifen-inducible）调控的遗传重组的方式，我们得以追踪小鼠骨内肥大细胞的命运。我们的数据显示肥大软骨细胞不仅可以于软骨-骨的转化中存活，并且得以转化成为胚胎期及成年期内源性骨的骨系细胞。更令人惊奇的是，其中一些胚胎期的肥大软骨细胞的子代细胞是很长寿的，可以一直存活到成年阶段。然而，许多问题也就应运而生，比如由这些肥大软骨细胞分化而成的成骨细胞具有什么样的生理功能；什么样的分子和细胞层面的变化对这个转化机制起了调控作用。我们推测在这两种细胞的转化过程当中，细胞须重新进入细胞周期，并且软骨细胞要转化至软骨-骨祖细胞或者骨祖细胞的状态。我们进一步推断这些由肥大软骨细胞转化而来的成骨细胞（HC-Obs）很大程度上有助于的内源性骨的形成，并且在我们骨折后，作为祖细胞参与骨折后的愈合过程。针对这个推测，我们设计了以下实验方案：a）比较肥大软骨细胞转化而来的成骨细胞（HC-Obs）和骨膜生成的成骨细胞之间分子特性的区别；b）在细胞的转化阶段，针对细胞周期和分子变化进行遗传分析； c）对HC-Obs是如何参与并维持成年骨的稳态以及是如何参与骨折愈合过程进行遗传学分析。我们发现软骨细胞可以转化成为成骨细胞，这一研究结果已经改写了成骨细胞发生学的一贯理念。而以上所提出的研究方案不仅将加深我们对不同来源的成骨细胞在骨生长发育过程中作用的理解，揭开这些细胞是如何参与骨折愈合这一过程的机制，此外，这些研究还为我们提供了一个关于骨稳态调控以及骨发育异常病理机制研究的理论基础。

762813.label: Realisation of objectives
762813.value: Objective 1. Analyse the cell cycle and molecular changes that accompany the HC to osteoblast transition. We have shown that during endochondral bone formation, hypertrophic chondrocytes (HCs) can become osteoblasts and osteocytes contributing to bone formation and maintenance (Yang et al. 2014). To understand the molecular mechanism governing this lineage transition we determined transcriptomic changes that occur at single cell resolution by analysing single cell transcriptomes of 349 lineage-activated fluorescent protein-expressing HCs and HC-descendants, generated by the Smart-seq2 protocol. Hierarchical clustering and pseudotime trajectory analyses reveal that HCs can also become mesenchymal-like cells (expressing Cxcl12, Msx1, Pdgfrb). Live imaging of scapula explant culture showed that red fluorescent HC-descendants gradually expressed Col1-GFP near the chondro-osseous junction, indicating the commitment to osteoblast fate takes time and many cells may remain in “transition” or mesenchymal status near the junction. The RNA Velocity algorithm which employs unspliced/intronic reads to estimate cellular state, suggest the mesenchymal-like cells are distinct cell type from the osteoblast lineage. These data suggest there is an as yet undefined HC-descendant transition cell population, which may be rare. To define this cell population requires determining the transcriptomes of additional cells. We are now using tamoxifen inducible Co10a1Cre-ERT2;R26-tdTomato mice to collect HC-descendants 24 hours after tamoxifen induction for single cell RNA-seq. The addition of the new datasets will help identify the transition cell population and their signature. From our data we sought to identify novel regulators of the process. The PAGODA algorithm was used for unbiased identification of enriched gene sets. To identify the gene regulatory network controlling the transition, we employed the SCENIC algorithm. PAGODA detected cell cycle gene sets (e.g. Cdc20, Ccnb1) enriched in mesenchymal-like and pre-osteoblast populations. SCENIC identified E2f1 and E2f2 regulons, drivers of cell cycle progression, are enriched in the mesenchymal-like and pre-osteoblast populations. HC re-entry into the cell cycle was confirmed by short term (2 hour) and chase (8 days) BrdU labeling of HC-descendants in trabecular bone. Interestingly, SCENIC also revealed, a subpopulation of cells in the mesenchymal-like population express Pparg and Cebpa regulons, suggestive of adipogenic potential and/or a change in metabolic phenotype. This is supported by the Dynamical Network Biomarker algorithm which identified genes related to fatty acid metabolism and mitochondrial activity (e.g. Acadm and Plin2, Slc25a51 and Steap4). We found that 2.5% cells expressed adipogenic marker (Pparg+Osx-) in contrast to 68.3% osteogenic (Pparg-Osx+) suggesting that some HC-descendants can become adipocytes but these are only a very small minority, and the major fate of HCs is osteogenic. The SCENIC anlysis also revealed that Myc and Tcf7 (both are Wnt/beta-catenin signaling targets) regulons are enriched in the pre-osteoblast/osteoblast populations supporting the idea that Wnt signaling is important for osteoblast fate commitment (see below). Objective 2. Assess the relative contribution of HC-Obs in maintaining postnatal bone We employed the conditional ablation approach, to ablate beta-catenin gene (Ctnnb1) compromising canonical Wnt signalling to test whether it is critical in promoting the HC to osteoblast transition. We employed HC-specific Col10a1-Cre (HC-Cre) (together with the lineage reporter R26-tdTomato) mice to inactivate Ctnnb1 in the HC lineage (Loss-of-function; LOF) or to constitutively stabilize Ctnnb1 by deleting exon3 (Gain-of-function; GOF). LOF mutants displayed dramatic reduction of trabecular bones in contrast to GOF mutants which showed increased bone mass. These phenotypes are consistent with those reported recently for conditional LOF and GOF Ctnnb1 mutations in the HC lineage (Houben et al., 2016 Development). However in that study there was no description of the impact of these mutations on cell fate. To understand the impact of Ctnnb1 LOF and GOF on the HC to osteoblast lineage, we compared the transcriptomes of the HC lineage in these 2 types of mutants with that of wild-type. Bulk RNA-seq data from HC-cre;R26-td-Tomato HC-descendants from 5-day-old control and mutant proximal tibiae (70 manually isolated cells from each pup; 2 controls, 4 LOF, 2 GOF pups) showed osteoblast markers were upregulated in GOF. Interestingly, while osteoblast markers were downregulated in LOF mutants consistent with impaired osteoblast differentiation, we found a concomitant and striking up-regulation of genes associated with adipogenesis (e.g. Pparg, Cebpa and Adipoq), indicating preferential commitment towards adipocyte differentiation, a process regulated by the master transcription factor PPARgamma. Canonical Wnt signalling in known to repress adipogenic differentiation of mesenchymal/osteoblast progenitors, therefore Wnt/beta-catenin LOF in HCs alters the balance toward adipogenesis. Antibody staining against perilipin, a mature adipocyte marker, suggested that bone marrow adipose tissue (BMAT) expansion is detectable in 5-day-old LOF mice. At 4-week-old, huge expansion of BMAT was evident as shown by osmium tetroxide staining. In addition, bulk RNA-seq data revealed an upregulation of adiponectin gene (Adipoq) expression in LOF suggesting alteration in metabolic control since BMAT is suggested to be an important source of circulating adiponectin which regulate glucose and fatty acid metabolism and can promote metabolic and cardiovascular health. Hence, HC-descendants play an important role in maintaining a normal BMAT to bone ratio. We observed a marked changed levels of Irx3 and Irx5 in LOF and GOF mutants and investigated their roles in endochondral bone formation with emphasis on the HC-lineage, by generating Irx3 and Irx5 null and Irx3 conditional mutants in collaboration with Dr. C.C. Hui (University of Toronto, Canada). Importantly, it has recently been shown that human IRX3 is associated with adipogenesis and obesity. We found that HCs, osteoblasts and osteocytes in P10 pups express both Irx3 and Irx5. Trabecular bone volume in P10 pups negatively correlated with the gene dosage of Irx3/5, with the lowest value detected in Irx3/5-CKO mutant which is homozygous for Irx3-floxed and Irx5-null allele, heterozygous for HC-Cre (HCcre::Irx3f/f-Irx5-/-) so that only the HC-descendants are double-null for Irx3 and Irx5. Lineage tracing in Irx3 KO mutant and Irx3/5-CKO mutants revealed fewer HC-descendants, implying impaired HC lineage progression. The number of Col1a1-expressing HC-descendants was also decreased in Irx3/5-CKO mutants, consequently resulting in inadequate bone ossification and formation. Using adipocyte marker perilipin 1 and osmium tetroxide staining, we found that BMAT was increased in Irx3 and Irx5 single null mutants. Thus both Irx3 and Irx5, like beta-catenin, negatively regulate adipogenesis in the HC-lineage and help to maintain a normal BMAT to bone ratio. We also investigated the role of membrane-bound matrix metalloproteinase 14 (Mmp14) in the HC lineage since its expression is detected at the chondro-osseous junction of the growth plate suggesting a potential role in HC lineage transition. Conditionally ablating Mmp14 in HC-lineage using HC-Cre (Mmp14-CKO) resulted in increased trabecular bone, in particular in region closer to the chondro-osseous junction, suggesting cell type specific activity of Mmp14 in HC-lineage. The increased osteoblastic activity suggested Mmp14 is a negative regulator of osteoblast differentiation by suppressing bone-promoting signal in a cell autonomous manner. Parathyroid hormone related peptide (PTHrP) signalling was a candidate for its known action to stimulate bone anabolism through targeting PTHrP receptor (encoded by Pth1r gene) on osteoblasts. We showed that PTHrP injection to juvenile mice can significantly induce trabecular bone mass and expansion of Col1-GFP-positive HC-descendants but the response is dramatically enhanced in Mmp14-CKO mutants. In contrast, the increased bone mass phenotype of Mmp14-CKO is reduced in mutants carrying a PTh1r-null allele. Biochemical analysis showed that Mmp14 transfection promoted the degradation of PTHrP receptor, indicating that Mmp14 negatively regulates osteoblast differentiation by targeting PTHrP signalling.

762813.label: Major findings and research outcome
762813.value: 1. To identify transitioning cells and the descendants we analysed the HC lineage by single cell transcriptome methods and analytical tools (smart-seq2, pseudotime trajectory, PAGODA, SCENIC and RNA Velocity) to identify factors and signals that regulate HC-lineage progression and cell cycle regulation. From the data we discovered that HC-descendants can become mesenchymal-like cells as well as osteoblasts. We also show by live imaging of scapula explant cultures that the HC to osteoblastic progression occurs over a period of 10 hours. 2. A combination of knowledge of skeletal development and the transcriptome data identified potential regulators of the HC to osteoblast transition. We used genetic approaches in mice and revealed the roles of Wnt-signaling, MMP14 and Irx3/5 in controlling this process. a) By conditional HC-specific manipulation of the beta-catenin gene we showed that HC-specific beta-catenin loss of function (LOF) results in reduced bone formation and in gain-of-function (GOF) mutants an increase in bone formation. Interestingly LOF mutants show that the HCs become adipocytes rather than osteoblasts, revealing the key role for Wnt signaling in the fate determination of HCs. The consequential increase in bone marrow fat (BMAT) development leads to an unbalanced BMAT to bone ratio and is associated with altered metabolic phenotype at 12-14 months old. These LOF mutants showed decreased percentage of body fat mass and increased percentage of muscle (lean) mass. These preliminary findings may have important implications for the contribution of the HC to osteoblast lineage in influencing metabolic state and have ranslational value. b) By studying LOF mutants of Irx3 and Irx5 in the HC-lineage we found that deficiency in Irx3 and Irx 5 singly and in combination resulted in reduced bone formation and accelerated BMAT development (10-day-old mice). We hypothesise that Irx3 and Irx5 may cooperate with beta-catenin to predispose HC-lineage commitment towards osteogenic fate. c) We found the membrane bound metalloproteinase, Mmp14, is expressed at the chondro-osseous junction in the growth plate. HC-specific Mmp14 LOF mutants displayed increased trabecular bone formation. Introducing a Pth1r null allele in Mmp14-CKO mutants partially restored normal bone mass implicating PTH signaling. Biochemical analyses revealed a direct role for MMP14 in processing Pth1r, the PTH receptor. We hypothesise that the LOF of MMP14 results in elevated PTH signaling causing increased bone synthesis. We are currently preparing 3 manuscripts to describe these important findings.

762813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
762813.value: Our genetic and single cell transcriptomic analyses of the transition of the HC to osteoblast transition suggest that there may be yet another source of stem/progenitor cells in cartilage-bone interphase, associated with the “transdifferentiation” process. While controversial, it may be that HCs are quiescent stem cells/progenitors that can transdifferentiate into at least three cell types- osteoblasts, mesenchymal cells and adipocytes, depending on signals. We have shown that manipulating Wnt and PTH signaling (via Mmp14), and Irx3/Irx5 can control HCs fate and bone mass with implications for bone healing and disorders such as osteoporosis. Enhancement of PTHrP signaling via Mmp14 to promote bone growth may provide a strategy for PTHrP treatment for osteoporosis. Interestingly we found HC lineage control also includes adipogenic cell fate. Our data shows that tight regulation of the HC fate by different factors (beta-catenin, Irx3, Irx5) is critical for keeping balanced BMAT to bone ratio, with consequential implications for whole body metabolic homeostasis. The beta-catenin LOF and GOF mutants and Irx3/5-CKO may serve as important tools to understand how BMAT develops, its regulation and its role in modulating local (bone marrow) and systemic metabolic homeostasis including glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity.

762813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
762813.value: We have shown that growth plate cartilage hypertrophic chondrocytes become osteoblasts and thereby contribute to the formation and maintenance of bone. We used genetic approaches using mice and state-of-the-art single cell transcriptome approach to dissect the transition process and found that the non-dividing hypertrophic chondrocytes acquire the ability to undergo cell division. Furthermore we discovered that the transition process is more complex because the chondrocytes can also become mesenchymal-like cells and have the potential to become fat cells (adipocytes). We discovered that at least three signaling pathways/factors control the transition. Dysregulation of these pathways/factors change the fate of the chondrocytes and therefore bone density, bone marrow homeostasis and body metabolism. A thorough understanding of the process of changing from chondrocyte to bone is of clinical significance because this lineage may represent a potential source of skeletal stem cells that can contribute to bone healing after fracture. Our discovery of signals that control this transition also opens up the development of new strategies to improve bone mass in disorders such as osteoporosis. Our mutant mice may serve as models for understanding the relationship between bone and its marrow fat in regulating whole body metabolism such as glucose levels and insulin sensitivity.

762913.label: Realisation of objectives
762913.value: Host cells utilize multiple mechanisms to restrict virus replication in infected cells. Our previous study revealed that cellular processing bodies (P-bodies) and stress granules (SG) are involved in influenza virus replication and non-structural protein (NS1) of influenza virus interacts with Rap55 to block this restriction (1). Since Rap55 presents in both P-bodies and SG, we found that Rap55 plays as a key mediator in regulating viral protein translation efficiency of influenza A viruses through interactions with cellular stress granules and P-bodies in infected cells. Our study on this subject led to the identification of nuclear factor 90, NF90, as a new component of stress granules and a novel host antiviral mechanism in which NF90 upregulation of PKR phosphorylation restricts virus infection (2). In this part of study (also supported by a RGC grant), we found that NF90 migrates to the cytoplasm to facilitate PKR phosphorylation in response to virus infection or the presence of dsRNA during virus replication. Activation of PKR leads to the phosphorylation of eIF2a and subsequently triggers formation of stress granules that involve NF90, PKR, and other stress granule components. However, viruses adapt different mechanisms to antagonize NF90–PKR antiviral activity. Influenza A viruses express NS1 to inhibit phosphorylation of PKR, which also interacts with NF90, to enhance virus replication. It appears that PKR antiviral activity can be activated by NF90-dependent mechanism as identified in this study, or by NF90-independent manner by IFN to exert antiviral activity as described in previous studies. To further characterize molecular mechanism underling host restriction of influenza virus replication through modulation of viral protein synthesis, this study used Rap55 as bait to further identify a core factor of P-bodies, 5'-3' exoribonuclease 1 (Xrn1), as participating in this process. Xrn1 is best known for its role as a decay factor, degrading cytoplasmic mRNA in P-bodies in Drosophila, yeast and mammals. Xrn1 has been shown to degrade/host mRNAs following virus-induced exonucleolytic cleavage processes, thereby suppressing cellular gene expression and aiding in evasion of host antiviral innate immune defenses. The mechanistic details of how Xrn1 also facilitates virus replication remain unclear, however. This study utilizes viral RNA FISH, protein-protein interaction experiments and various mutant viruses to characterize the interaction between influenza virus and cellular P-bodies and investigate the role of Xrn1 in virus replication. In this study, we identified a novel interaction between influenza virus nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) and Xrn1 in infections using various influenza strains, including H1N1 (A/WSN/1933), H5N1 (A/Vietnam/1194/2004) and H7N9 (A/Zhejiang/2013). Knockdown of Xrn1 expression significantly decreased virus replication, suggesting that Xrn1 positively influences the influenza virus life cycle. We further characterized Xrn1 as being one of the host factors present in P-bodies that is targeted by NS1 for virus replication. In virus infected cells, we showed that wild-type NS1 co-localizes with endogenous Xrn1 in the cytoplasm, and that Xrn1 co-localizes with viral mRNA, but not vRNA. Screening of a series of NS1 mutants revealed that the E96 and E97 residues in the NS1 protein directly associate with the C-terminal region (1174-1706 aa) of Xrn1 in an RNA binding independent manner. Association of the NS1 protein with cellular P-bodies in virus-infected cells was found to contribute to suppression of host Xrn1 ubiquitination via a direct interaction and regulate Xrn1 exonuclease activity. Our results suggest that influenza virus utilizes the NS1 protein to hijack the function of Xrn1, promoting degradation of cellular mRNA, which results in suppression of the host innate immune response, and facilitation of viral replication through stabilization of viral mRNA (Part of the results have been presented in the IX Options for the control of influenza conference and a manuscript focus on this part of study is in preparation). The NS1 protein of influenza A virus is a well-defined virulence element, with multiple functions in virus infection. Besides its essential function antagonizing the host antiviral response, it is suggested that NS1 is also involved in regulation of virus replication. However, it is not clear how NS1 is involved in virus genome transcription and replication. Our studies found that the NS1 protein plays essential role in counteracting host restriction of virus replication through formation of antiviral P-bodies and stress granules in infected cells. It would be necessary to monitor the process of P-bodies and stress granules with knockout of NS1 in influenza virus. This study has developed a panel of influenza A virus with deletion of the NS1 gene. To obtain influenza virus with knockout of the NS1 gene, we first found that M gene expression in DelNS1 virus infection was significantly reduced compared to that for WT virus, with the M2 mRNA splicing ratio being significantly lower than that of the WT virus. It is hypothesized that the process of M gene expression may be subject to regulation by viral protein(s) including NS1 as well. We identified an A14U substitution in the M segment non-coding region that supports replication of NS1-deleted (DelNS1) virus derived from the A/WSN/33 strain. We found that M-A14U mutation supports virus replication through modulation of alternative splicing of mRNAs transcribed from the M segment. Our findings give insight into the role of NS1 in influenza virus replication and provide an approach for constructing replication-competent strains with NS1 deletions for use in functional and vaccine studies (3). Notably, construction of DelNS1 versions of other influenza strains revealed that different strains require different adaptive mutations to restore virus replication when NS1 is deleted. We have extended on our study and successfully developed a panel of DelNS1 viruses including WSN (H1N1), PR8 (H1N1), CA04 (2009 H1N1), 1194 (H5N1) and ZJ1 (H7N9). Importantly, adaptive mutations allowing replication of these DelNS1 viruses were identified, with adapted viruses able to replicate to a comparable level to the wild type virus in embryonated chicken eggs and MDCK and Vero cells. While replication is almost totally restored by the adaptive mutations, these viruses are attenuated with regard to their inhibition of interferon expression and avirulent in infected mice. These DelNS1 viruses derived from different subtypes of influenza virus provide valuable tools for studying the host restriction through induction of cellular P-bodies and stress granules and for further exploring the role of the NS1 protein in supporting virus replication. Application of using these DelNS1 as live attenuated vaccine is being evaluated in our ongoing study (two patents have been filed and one manuscript is in preparation). References 1. 762913.label: Major findings and research outcome
762913.value: Our study revealed that cellular processing bodies (P-bodies) are involved in influenza virus replication and Rap55 was identified as a component in the P-bodies to interact with the non-structural protein (NS1) of influenza virus. Using Rap55 as a marker, we further identified NF90 as a novel component of stress granules and NF90 dependent PKR antiviral signaling. We found a core factor of P-bodies, 5'-3' exoribonuclease 1 (Xrn1), as participating in this process. Xrn1 is best known for its role as a decay factor, degrading cytoplasmic mRNA in P-bodies, following virus-induced exonucleolytic cleavage processes, thereby suppressing cellular gene expression and aiding in evasion of host antiviral innate immune defenses. The mechanistic details of how Xrn1 also facilitates virus replication remain unclear, however. We identified a novel interaction between influenza virus NS1 and Xrn1 in infections using various influenza strains, including H1N1, H5N1 and H7N9. Our finding suggested that Xrn1 positively influences the influenza virus life cycle. We further characterized Xrn1 as being one of the host factors present in P-bodies that is targeted by NS1 for virus replication. To map the detail of interaction between Xrn1 and the NS1 protein, we used DelNS1 virus (below) and a series of NS1 mutants and revealed that the E96/E97 residues in the NS1 protein directly associate with the C-terminal region of Xrn1 in an RNA binding independent manner. Association of the NS1 protein with cellular P-bodies in virus-infected cells was found to contribute to the suppression of host Xrn1 ubiquitination via a direct interaction and regulate Xrn1 exonuclease activity. The NS1 protein of influenza virus has multiple functions. Besides its role in antagonizing host antiviral activity, NS1 is also believed to be involved in regulating virus replication, but mechanistic details are not clear. To understand how NS1 regulates virus replication through interaction with Rap55 and Xrn1, this study characterized a replication-competent DelNS1 virus which carries an A14U substitution in the 3’ noncoding region of the vRNA M segment. We found that M-A14U mutation supports virus replication through modulation of alternative splicing of mRNAs transcribed from the M segment. In conclusion, our results suggest that influenza virus utilizes the NS1 protein to hijack the cellular function of Xrn1, promoting degradation of cellular mRNA, which results in suppression of the host innate immune response, and facilitation of viral replication through stabilization of viral mRNA during influenza virus infection. Our findings give insight into the role of NS1 in influenza virus replication and provide an approach for constructing replication-competent strains with NS1 deletions (Part C published reference 3 and manuscript in preparation- see conference paper 1).

762913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
762913.value: This project is based on our original findings which revealed the NS1 protein of influenza A virus interacts with cellular processing bodies (P-bodies) and stress granules through RNA-aassociated protein 55 (RAP55) during virus infection. It is an area of continuous study and we have further characterized other host factors, including NF90, Xrn1 and Ago2, are involved in this process. The host restriction in cellular p-bodies during virus replication have led to the identification of a novel mechanism of virus host interplay in which viral mRNAs are targeted to P-bodies/stress granules while NS1 counteracts this host restriction mechanism. It is notable that Xrn1 is identified as an important positive regulator for influenza virus replication and could be a new antiviral target. It appears that the NS1 protein plays the essential role in evading host restriction in this process. To delineate the underling mechanism, studies in this area have led to the discovery of unique mutations allow virus replication without the expression of the NS1 protein. A panel of DelNS1 viruses derived from various subtypes are being further developed with cold adapted properties and evaluated for the potentiality of application in live attenuated flu and other respiratory viral vaccines.

762913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
762913.value: Viruses rely on host machinery to replicate the viral genome in infected cells and host utilizes multiple mechanisms to restrict virus replication. The interplay of virus and host determines the outcome of infection. While influenza virus utilizes viral polymerase for genome replication, viral protein synthesis completely relies on host machinery. This project aims to identify host factors associated with cellular processing bodies (called P-bodies) which regulate the stability of viral and cellular mRNAs for protein synthesis in restricting virus replication. Significantly, we identified host Xrn1, a 5'-3' exoribonuclease, as regulator of virus replication through screening interaction with Rap55 and its interacting partner of the NS1 protein of influenza virus. Our study found Xrn1 to be one of the few host factors so far identified to be able to positively regulate virus replication. Strategies targeting these factors may serve to screen for novel antiviral drugs. More importantly, through this project we have been able to establish a panel of influenza viruses with the deletion of key virulent factor, NS1. These DelNS1 viruses are valuable for functional studies on influenza virus replication and are being evaluated for application in the development of new live attenuated flu and other respiratory viral vaccines.

764113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
764113.value: Mobilization of intracellular calcium (Ca2+) through the ryanodine receptor (RyR) channels in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) generates cellular signals that control virtually all aspects of life. The characterization of single RyR channel properties is therefore the fundamental to understand the generation and modulation of intracellular Ca2+ signaling events. Although the intracellular localization of RyR restricted its accessibility by conventional patch-clamp electrophysiology, single channel properties of RyR have been extensively studied by incorporating the channel proteins into artificial planar lipid bilayer. Up until now, the physiological properties of RyR channels in the native ER membrane have never been investigated. All the gating properties and ligand regulations of RyR single channel were obtained exclusively from the bilayer method. The single RyR channel characteristics and its regulations observed in the artificial membrane might not fully reflect the physiological behavior of the channel in the native membrane. To overcome this obstacle, we applied the nuclear membrane electrophysiology on a stable cell line expressing recombinant RyR channels which allows us to investigate single channel properties of RyR in the native membrane environment. We successfully recorded single channel activities on the nuclear membrane of the RyR expressing cells. The detected channel had all the characteristics of RyR, including the sensitivity to caffeine and cADPR and inhibition by ruthenium red. Our preliminary results demonstrated for the first time that single RyR channel activities can be studied in the native membrane. Furthermore, we identified a short sequence in the N-terminus of RyR protein which is conserved with the NAD binding pocket of the ADP-ribosyl cyclase. This homology sequence suggests that cADPR may activate RyR channel by direct binding to the receptor. In this research project, we will define the properties of single RyR channel, including the permeation properties and ligand regulations, in the native nuclear membrane and elucidate the activation of the RyR by cADPR using the nuclear membrane electrophysiology. This proposal focuses on: Aim 1. To characterize the permeation properties of single RyR channel in nuclear envelope. Aim 2. To characterize the ligand regulations of RyR channel in nuclear envelope. Aim 3. 764113.label: Realisation of objectives
764113.value: i. To characterize the permeation properties of single RyR channel in nuclear envelope The permeation properties of single RyR channel determined the amount of particular ion flows through the open channel and it reflects the relative ease of an ion to enter the permeation pathway of the channel pore. Using nuclear membrane electrophysiology under the activation of 2 mM caffeine, we recorded RyR single channel activity from HEK293 nuclei expressing mouse RyR type 2 (HEK293-mRyR2). In symmetrical recording solution containing 140 mM K+ as the major permeant ion, these HEK293-mRyR2 single channels has slope conductance of about 650 pS, smaller than those recorded in the presence of 250 mM K+ (~750 pS). The detected RyR2 channel conductance by nuclear membrane electrophysiology is similar to those recorded using the lipid bilayer method. Besides the alternation in conductance, we do not observe any significant changes in the channel detection rate and channel open probability (Po). We also investigated the permeation of Cs+ through the single RyR2 on the nuclear membrane by replacing the symmetrical 140 mM K+ with Cs+. The result indicates Cs+ permeation through the RyR2 also has a linear I/V relationship with slope conductance of about 400 pS, similar to the result obtained from RyR1 channel using the nuclear membrane electrophysiology (Wagner II et al, 2014). Since the RyR2 is bathing with a complex ionic environment in cell and thus we have also investigated the relative ion permeation properties of single RyR2 channel expressed on the nuclear membrane. The relative ionic permeabilities of the RyR2 channel was determined by the reversal potential (Vrev) of the I/V relation of the channel under particular ionic conditions and calculated by the Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz equation. Our results indicate PBa/PK is about 4.8 whereas PCa/PK is about 5.2 which suggest RyR2 channel does not has a strong selective to divalent cation while has a strong preference to divalent cation over monovalent cations. Although we have made significant progress on the investigation of RyR2 channel permeation properties, PI faced hurdle that prevent us to finish this specific objective (will explain later). We still need to further investigate the permeation properties of the RyR2 channel using this nuclear membrane electrophysiology before we can submit a manuscript for publication. ii. To characterize the ligand regulations of RyR channel in nuclear envelope The RyR2 Ca2+ release channel is a crucial element in generating and modulating of intracellular Ca2+ signal events in cardiac muscles. It is under complex regulations by different ligands, including Ca2+and cADPR. In this research aim, we have investigated the steady-state Ca2+ regulation of RyR2 single channel activity by including a wide range of Ca2+ and 1 µM cADPR into the pipette solution. RyR2 single channel Po increases dose-dependently from 0.23 ± 0.04 at 1 M Ca2+ to 0.61 ± 0.05 at 30 M Ca2+. Channel Po further increased as Ca2+ concentration increases and reached a maximum of 0.74 ± 0.03 when 2 mM Ca2+ was included in the pipet. Further increases Ca2+ concentration in the pipet solution had led to the fall in Po when 3 mM Ca2+ was included in the pipette solution. When Ca2+ concentration increased beyond 3 mM RyR channel Po drops sharply suggesting RyR2 single channel activity is biphasically regulated by cytoplasmic Ca2+ concentrations. To gain mechanistic insights into the influence of Ca2+ on mRyR2 channel activity, we performed dwell time analyses on recorded mRyR2 currents activated with different Ca2+ concentrations in the pipette solution. The results indicate that raising the pipette [Ca2+] from 1 M to 50 µM does not significantly affect the channel mean open time (o), yet the channel mean closed time (c) is decreased dose-dependently from 6.50 ± 0.38 ms at 1 M Ca2+ to 2.45 ± 0.30 ms at 30 M Ca2+. The channel mean closed time continue to decrease when Ca2+ concentration was further increased. The channel mean closed time reached a minimum when 2 mM Ca2+ was added in the pipet, however, it started to increase when the Ca2+ concentration was increased further to 50 µM. Our results indicate that Ca2+ affects RyR2 channel Po by modulating the stability of channel’s closed state. iii. To characterize the activation of RyR single channel by cADPR It has been well-documented that the cADP-ribose (cADPR) mobilizes ER Ca2+ by acting on the RyR channels. However, whether it binds directly to the RyR is controversial. We addressed this question by investigating the activation of RyR2 by cADPR using the nuclear membrane electrophysiology. We added cADPR directly into the pipet solution and demonstrated that cADPR (1µM in the pipet solution) with 2 µM Ca2+ is capable to activate RyR2 single channel similar to which is activated by caffeine suggesting cADPR is a physiological ligand for the RyR2. To gain insight into the regulation of RyR2 channel activity by cADPR, we tested the influence of different cADPR concentrations on the RyR2 channel activity. Our results showed mRyR2 single channel Po increases dose-dependently from 0.19 ± 0.03 at 1 nM cADPR to 0.39 ± 0.06 at 10 nM cADPR . RyR2 single channel Po continue to rise when cADPR concentration was increased further. Its Po reached plateau at about 0.57 when cADPR concentration was at 1 µM. We also performed dwell time analysis on the gating kinetics of the cADPR-activated RyR2 single channel. The time constants for channel closing (c) were not significantly affected by raising [cADPR] from 1 nM to 10 M, while the time constant for channel opening (o) was increased dose-dependently from 1.46 ± 0.34 ms at 1 nM cADPR to 2.57 ± 0.53 at 10 nM cADPR. mRyR2 channel mean open time continue to increase when cADPR concentration was increased further. The mean open time was 3.36 ± 0.50 ms and 3.89 ± 0.48 ms when 100 nM cADPR and 1 M cADPR was included in the pipet solution, respectively. The mean open time reached a maximum of 4.89 ± 0.42 ms when 10 M cADPR was presence in the pipet. Our results showed that increase in [cADPR] enhanced mRyR2 Po by increasing the channel mean open time; whereas the channel mean closed time remain unaltered suggesting cADPR modulates RyR2 Po by modulating the stability of the channel’s open state. In summary, with support of this GRF funding, we characterized the mouse cardiac isoform of RyR (RyR2) using the nuclear membrane electrophysiology which should resemble a more physiological environment of the native RyR2 when compared to the current widely used artificial planar lipid bilayer approach. We completed most of the objectives proposed in our initial proposal, however, we need further investigation to achieve a more complete ion permeability characteristic of the RyR2. The major hurdle of the project is that PI switched Institutions from HKU to HKBU. One of the major equipment piece, an inverted microscope, was withheld by HKU although the microscope was funded by PI’s RGF grants. With the support from HKBU, PI built a new patch-clamp setup and PI’s group will continue to complete this project and publish a manuscript very soon.

764113.label: Major findings and research outcome
764113.value: One of the major findings of this research project is that we validated the nuclear membrane electrophysiology can be applied to study ER Ca2+ release channels, such as InsP3R and RyR. The nuclear membrane electrophysiology was originally designed to study the InsP3R expressed on the nuclear envelope, we are the first research group demonstrated that the nuclear membrane patch can also be applied to study the channel function of RyR2 (Mak et al, 2013, Cold Spring Harb. Protoc). Using the nuclear membrane approach, the “most” physiological characteristics of RyR channel in native membrane can be investigated. Our data indicates mouse RyR2 expressed on the nuclear envelope of the HEK293 cell conferred a large-conductance cation channel. The recorded RyR2 single channel has about ~650 pS conductance in symmetrical 140 mM K+ as a charge carrier. The channel exhibits linear I/V relationship in symmetrical ionic conditions. It shows strong selectivity to divalent ion over monovalent ion but barely selective between monovalent ions. Since the RyR is regulated through a Ca2+-induced Ca2+ release mechanism, we demonstrated that cytoplasmic Ca2+ biphasically regulate RyR2 channel activities with low Ca2+ concentrations activate the channel while high concentrations of Ca2+ supress the channel openings. With the dwell time analysis, we revealed Ca2+ regulates RyR2 activity by modulating the channel closed duration. In addition to Ca2+, ER Ca2+ through the RyR has been showed to be mediated by second messenger, cADPR. Intriguingly, using the nuclear membrane patch, Wagner II et al failed to demonstrate the regulation of RyR1 by cADPR. However, in this project we showed evidence that cADPR dose-dependently regulate RyR2 channel activity suggesting the regulation of RyRs by cADPR is isoform specific. We have been selected to present a “Flash symposium” in the XIV International meeting of the European Ca2+ Society in 2016 in Spain. We will finish some of the remaining ion permeability measurement and submit a manuscript for publication (manuscript is in preparation). In addition, we have established collaboration with a group in Shanghai, China. Using the nuclear membrane electrophysiology technique to found the InsP3R interacts with SEC5 protein and modulates innate immunity against the C. albicans infection (manuscript is accepted by BMC Biology; Impactor factor: 6.779). Another review article on Ca2+ signaling in Alzheimer’s disease and therapies was submitted to BBA Molecular Cell Research (IF: 4.521).

764113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
764113.value: The RyR-mediated Ca2+ release plays significant roles in maintaining the Ca2+ homeostasis and generating Ca2+ signals that not only contribute to normal physiological processes but also implicate on pathophysiological conditions. Because of the intracellular localization of the RyR in the cell, it is always difficult to elucidate the physiological and pathophysiological roles of RyR. Using the nuclear membrane electrophysiology, we can now robustly investigate the ligand regulation and ion permeability of the RyR channel in its native membrane environment. In this research project, we characterized the type 2 RyR, cardiac isoform, Ca2+ channel properties. We found the cADPR is a physiological ligand for activating the RyR2. In the future, we may use the nuclear membrane patch of the RyR channel to study the implication of functional defects of the channel in disease conditions. Furthermore, we can use this approach as a tool to screen for small molecules that can modulate the RyR single channel activities and help new drug development for treating diseases due to malfunction of the RyR channel.

764113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
764113.value: Release of intracellular calcium (Ca2+) through the ryanodine receptor (RyR)channels in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) generates cellular signals that control numerous cellular processes. Although the RyR-mediated Ca2+ signalling is important, its intracellular localization limited our investigations on the regulation of RyR channel activities by ligands and pharmacological reagents. In this research project, we explored the application of nuclear membrane electrophysiology to study the regulation of RyR2 single channel activities by calcium ion and second messenger, cyclic-ADP-ribose. We successfully recorded single channel activities on the nuclear membrane of the RyR expressing cells. The detected channel had all the characteristics of RyR, including the sensitivity to caffeine, cADPR and cytoplasmic Ca2+ dependency. Our preliminary results demonstrated for the first time that single RyR channel activities can be studied in the native membrane. Since the RyR2 signal channel activities are robustly detected by this nuclear membrane electrophysiology technique, we can use this novel approach to investigate the pathophysiology of RyR channels in different diseases such as cardiac failure or neurodegeneration. We believe the nuclear membrane patch of RyR can also be used to screen for small molecules that can correct abnormal RyR function for disease treatment.

764213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
764213.value: With the loss of teeth, the jaws gradually degenerate. The atrophy is compounded by the expanding maxillary sinus in the posterior maxilla resulting in lack of bone volume for dental implant insertion and stability. We have developed a technique of concentrating bone marrow aspirated cells from rabbits’ tibia and confirmed that some were viable stem cells able to form cell colonies and differentiate into bone cells that could form bone tissue in laboratory environment. We have further established a rabbit maxillary sinus grafting model at our animal laboratory. This bone marrow stem cell (BMSC) concentrate were mixed with bovine bone particles (xenograft) and compared with different bone graft materials grafted to the rabbits’ maxillary sinuses. The results showed that bone regeneration of the BMSC bovine bone group was confirmed and was quicker than bovine bone alone and autogenous bone. We have successfully translate the animal study to a human pilot study confirmed the feasibility of setting up a single-step intra-operative BMAC approach for maxillary sinus grafting in humans. We propose a clinical trial project to be divided into 2 parts. For patients indicated for sinus grafting of both sides, it will be designed as a split mouth comparison of BMSC with xenograft versus xenograft alone (study 1). For patients indicated for sinus grafting of one side, it will be a randomized controlled trial between BMSC with xenograft versus autogenous bone (study 2). The results of this clinical research project will have important clinical implications on redefining the gold standard if this less morbid method, which has potential of forming more bone than autogenous bone or xenograft alone. Other important aspects including success of implant rehabilitation and patients’ reported outcome measures. Suitable patients with missing teeth in the posterior maxilla being seen at our Joint Implant Assessment clinic will be recruited. They will be allocated either to study 1 or 2 depending on whether both or one sides require maxillary sinus grafting, respectively. With their informed consent, they will be assigned to the specific treatment methods with the grafts being placed into the maxillary sinus using a standard surgical technique. Dental implants will be inserted with bone biopsy performed on the grafted bone at time of implant placement for histological and micro-CT investigation. The psychological changes and quality of life will be assessed by questionnaires and any surgical morbidities and implant success will be regularly monitored.

765113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
765113.value: 小腦功能失調，常表現為運動協調及運動學習缺陷，目前尚缺乏有效治療手段。大量研究表明小腦Purkinje神經細胞可接收來自不同神經細胞的興奮或抑制性輸入電流，並對其整合分析，因此在運動協調及運動學習過程中發揮關鍵作用。我們研究團隊已證實胰泌素可有效促進Purkinje細胞抑制性電流輸入，並可能進一步調節Purkinje神經細胞功能。基於這項研究和其它實驗，我們提出如下假設：胰泌素可通過調節Purkinje神經細胞興奮性，進而調控運動協調及運動學習過程。為證實上述假設並明確胰泌素的細胞作用機制，我們成功培育Purkinje細胞特異性胰泌素基因敲除小鼠。我們對該小鼠模型以及胰泌素基因敲除和胰泌素受體基因敲除小鼠進行了行為學研究，包括開放場（open field），懸掛（wire hanging），垂直攀爬（vertical climbing）以及跑步機平衡（Rotarod）實驗。初步實驗表明，Purkinje細胞特異性胰泌素基因敲除小鼠表現較弱的神經肌肉強度，運動協調以及運動學習能力。這一結果提示我們Purkinje細胞中表達的胰泌素對於小鼠運動功能的重要作用。為進一步證實我們的假設，這份研究計畫將著重利用上述轉基因小鼠研究：（1）詳盡的行為學實驗以明確Purkinje細胞中胰泌素和神經肌肉強度，運動協調及運動學習過程的關係；（2）神經電生理手段記錄Purkinje細胞及其下游小腦深部核團的細胞電流，以瞭解胰泌素在細胞水準上調節運動行為的機制；（3）Purkinje細胞在缺少或人為添加胰泌素表達條件下的發育形態學改變。該項研究的結果將有助於更好瞭解胰泌素對於Purkinje細胞生理功能以及小鼠運動行為的調控機制，並為針對小腦功能失調的藥物研究提供理論基礎。

765113.label: Realisation of objectives
765113.value: Objective 1: A) Developing Purkinje cell-specific secretin knockout (Pur-Sct-/-) mice To develop such conditional knockout mice, the Cre-loxP recombination system was adopted. Two strains of mice were used: 1) Pcp2-Cre mice (from Department of Biochemistry, HKU), in which the Cre-recombinase transgene is specifically expressed in Purkinje cells and retinal bipolar cells under the promoter of Purkinje cell protein 2 (Pcp2); 2) secretin (SCT)-loxP mice, in which the SCT-coding region is flanked by two loxP sites. Pcp2-Cre mice were mated with SCT-loxP mice, producing offspring in which the SCT-coding region is deleted in Purkinje cells only. B) Genotyping of Pur-Sct-/- mice To genotype Pur-Sct-/- mice, genomic DNA was extracted from juvenile tail cuts and dual PCR amplification using specific primers for the SCT-loxP sequence or the Pcp2-Cre sequence was employed. The mice with both SCT-loxP and Pcp2-Cre genes were expected to be Pur-Sct-/- ones. C) Confirmation of SCT deficiency in Purkinje cells Paraffin-embedded parasagittal brain slices were prepared from wild-type (WT) and Pur-Sct-/- mice Immunohistochemical staining and in situ hybridization were performed to examine SCT transcript and protein expression in different brain regions, including cerebellum, hippocampus and hypothalamus. Minimal levels of SCT transcript and peptide were found in cerebellar Purkinje cells of Pur-Sct-/- mice whereas SCT was strongly expressed in the soma and dendrites of Purkinje cells from WT mice. There was prominent SCT expression in the deep cerebellar nuclei, the hippocampus and hypothalamus from both WT and Pur-Sct-/- mice, indicating the specificity of the SCT knockout in Purkinje cells. D) General behaviour observations in a novel open field. To evaluate general motor functions and anxiety levels of sample mice, an open field test was employed. One mouse was put into a transparent plastic box and was allowed to freely explore the field for 60 min. Parameters were recorded and analysed, including the velocity, time in movement, time in the central/marginal zone, and average distance toward the zone border or field center. No significant difference among these parameters was found between WT and Pur-Sct-/- mice, suggesting that the general motor ability and stress status were intact in Pur-Sct-/- mice. E) Neuromuscular strength To measure the neuromuscular strength of transgenic mice, the wire hanging test was performed. One mouse was made to grab a metal wire mesh while upside-down. The latency that each animal spent holding the wire mesh was recorded. Twn sessions were performed on the same individual with a 30-min interval and the longer latency was used for analysis. Pur-Sct-/- mice had significantly shorter holding latencies than WT animals, suggesting impaired neuromuscular strength. F) Motor coordination The vertical climbing test was performed to assess motor and sensorimotor abilities. Each mouse started from the bottom of the mesh with its head facing downwards. After the mouse was released, the time required for it to climb all the way to the top was recorded. Two sessions were performed for each mouse with a 30-min interval, and the shorter time was used for analysis. Pur-Sct-/- mice spent longer time to complete the task as they climbed relatively slowly, stayed still, or even fell off the wire, providing evidence for impairments in fine motor coordination. G) Motor learning functions To investigate the motor learning functions of Pur-Sct-/- mice, the rotarod test was performed using a constant speed task and an accelerating speed task. The test began with a short training session, in which the mouse was trained to stay on a still wooden rod for at least 30s. Each animal was then enrolled into either of the following two paradigms: 1) the constant speed test, in which the rod speed was fixed at 20 rpm; 2) the accelerating speed test, during which the rod was accelerated from 10 to 40 rpm over 5 min. The end point was defined as the time when any paw of the mouse left the rod. Three daily sessions in the constant speed paradigm and six daily sessions in the accelerating speed paradigm were performed for each mouse. With repeated trials, only minor improvements of rotarod performance were found in Pur-Sct-/- mice at the last trial whereas the control animals showed a significant increase of latency on the rod, illustrating motor learning deficits. H) Screening of neurodevelopmental milestones To evaluate the postnatal development, a set of developmental milestones and neural reflexes was checked on juvenile mice. Selected developmental markers were evaluated on each day beginning from postnatal day 4 (P4) to P20. Among all these markers, Pur-Sct-/- juveniles had a later onset of surface righting and negative geotaxis reflexes, suggesting that SCT knockout in Purkinje cells can lead to neural developmental delays in the cerebellum. I) Neural degeneration To determine whether SCT knockout in Purkinje cells leads to neural degeneration, an age-dependent study was performed in wire hanging and accelerating rotarod tests. Age-dependent motor deficits existed within each genotype but not between two genotypes. However, wire hanging test showed decreased latencies starting from month 2 in Pur-Sct-/- but only after month 6 in WT animals, indicating that SCT knockout in Purkinje neurons could lead to early onset motor neuron degeneration. Objective 2: A) Recording the inhibitory postsynaptic currents (IPSC) to Purkinje neurons To evaluate SCT’ effects on the inhibitory input from basket cells to Purkinje neurons, whole-cell patch clamp was performed on Purkinje neurons and spontaneous IPSC was recorded. 50 nM SCT significantly increased both amplitude and frequency of spontaneous IPSC in WT Purkinje neurons, while Sctr-/- mice showed no response. The comparison between WT and Sctr-/- Purkinje neurons revealed a lower basal level of spontaneous IPSC in Sctr-/- mice. To further identify the involvement of pre- or post-synaptic mechanisms, miniature IPSC was recorded in the presence of TTX. The frequency of miniature IPSC was significantly enhanced after SCT perfusion while the amplitude somehow remained unchanged. Both spontaneous and miniature IPSCs were further recorded in Pur-Sct-/- Purkinje neurons, strengthening the important role of SCT in facilitating GABAergic transmission in basket-Purkinje cell synapse via a pre-synaptic mechanism. Objective 3: A) Purkinje cell density and dendritic arborization Purkinje cell-specific marker, Calbinidn-D28K, was used for immunofluorescence staining on mouse cerebellum paraffin sections. The linear Purkinje cell density was calculated by dividing the total number of Purkinje cells by the length of Purkinje cell layer along the lobule IV/V. The density of Purkinje cells was significantly decreased in Sct-/- mice since P10 until the adult age P28. To further investigate the dendritic morphology of individual Purkinje cells, Golgi staining was performed. Purkinje cells close to the apical regions of cerebellar folia was captured under a bright-field microscope. The soma and dendrites of Purkinje cells was plotted and then sholl analysis was performed, in which the soma was localized as the center of concentric circles with 10-μm intervals. The number of intersections of dendritic branches and the total length of dendrites within each circle was calculated. To evaluate dendritic spine density, the numbers of spines from both proximal and distal dendrites was counted and the spine density was calculated by dividing the number of spines by the dendritic length. Sct-/- juvenile mice displayed significantly fewer Purkinje cell dendritic branches and shorter dendritic lengths in the distal (70–110 mm from soma) section and this impaired dendritic arborization persisted in adult P28 mice. A remarkable decrease in spine density of Purkinje cell dendrites was further observed in Sct-/- mice.

765113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
765113.value: In this project, we have successfully developed the Purkinje cell‐specific SCT gene knockout (Pur‐Sct‐/‐) mouse model, which helped us to establish a solid role of SCT in the cerebellum in regulating motor coronation and motor learning. Our lab has further demonstrated that multiple potential mechanisms exist underlying the role of SCT in the cerebellar behavioral control, including neural transmission and neural development. Taken from the whole-cell patch-clamp recordings in Purkinje cells, a working model for SCT-facilitated inhibitor transmission at the basket cell-Purkinje cell synapse has been proposed. In brief, SCT released from Purkinje cells directly binds to the pre-synaptic SCTR in basket cells and facilitates the release of inhibitory transmitter GABA from basket cell terminals. In addition, SCT has been identified as a previously unrecognized participant in regulating postnatal development of the cerebellum, particularly Purkinje and granular cells. A role of the cAMP/PKA and MAPK/ERK1/2 signaling pathways in SCT-mediated anti-apoptosis has also been established for the first time. Taken together, the critical effects of SCT on neural transmission and cerebellar development have helped to explain the motor coordination and learning deficits without intact SCT-SCTR axis.

765213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
765213.value: 介紹 蛀牙（齲齒）是一種常見的兒童疾病，影響51％的香港5歲兒童。齲齒顯著的影響兒童的營養、生長、發育和健康。氟化氨銀是一個安全，具成本效益的齲阻斷劑，符合世界衛生組織的千年發展目標。不同的氟化氨銀方案已被使用，但他們缺乏證據基礎。 目的 為了找到制止兒童齲齒最合適的氟化氨銀的濃度和應用週期。 目標 兩個市售、濃度為38％和12％的氟化氨銀溶液，應用週期为每年或每半年，比較其應用36個月以上阻斷兒童齲齒的療效。 研究背景 原始研究建議是由健康與衛生服務研究基金支助，該研究基金只支持24個月的研究項目。這項研究於2012年開始，隨訪18個月。因為臨床試驗報導稱，氟化氨銀的有效性隨著時間的推移而降低，氟化氨銀治療的長期效果是很重要的。因此，我們希望申請優配研究金繼續這項研究的後續隨訪。 方法 此雙盲研究共統計了600名3-4歲患有齲齒的幼稚園兒童。樣本的大小足夠進行合適的統計學分析。根據患齲率的高低以及不同的齲病治療方法將幼稚園兒童分成四組： A組：每半年應用12%的氟化氨銀 B組：每一年應用12%的氟化氨銀 C組：每半年應用38%的氟化氨銀 D組：每一年應用38%的氟化氨銀 幼稚園兒童會在幼稚園被隨訪到36個月直到他們升入小學。6個月一次的臨床檢查評價齲齒是否被阻斷。口腔衛生習慣、氟化物的使用等干擾因素在研究開始和每次隨訪時通過父母的問卷調查收集。 可能的結果和意義 此研究有助於決定制止兒童齲齒最適合的氟化氨銀的濃度和應用週期。因為氟化氨銀用於制止齲齒是無痛、簡單和低成本的治療，可以被廣泛的推薦和提供給需要控制齲齒的兒童以及有困難負擔常規牙齒保健的兒童。此項研究結果的適用性以及對公共衛生的影響將是巨大的。

765513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
765513.value: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease that damages multiple systems and has significant morbidity and mortality. It affects over 7,000 people in Hong Kong alone and many more in other Asian countries. Early-onset SLE (onset <16 y) accounts for up to 20% of all SLE cases. This form has higher disease severity and persists into adulthood with significant long-term burden. The pathogenetic mechanism of early-onset SLE is largely unknown. DNA methylation is a well-studied epigenetic mark of SLE and loss of DNA methylation in immune cells has been shown to be fundamental in the pathogenesis of SLE. To the best of our knowledge, no studies on profiling of the DNA methylation have been done in patients with SLE of early onset. We previously studied the whole genome DNA methylation profile of SLE patients with adult onset, using peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). PBMCs consist of many functionally and developmentally distinct cell populations in varying proportions and each has a unique role in the immune system. We hypothesize that important differences exist in the DNA methylation of PBMCs, selected purified T cells, B cells and neutrophil lineages, and these particular variations would each contribute to the pathogenesis of early-onset SLE. In this proposal, we have three main objectives: 1) To identify SLE relevant epigenetic targets in SLE patients with early onset using a genome-wide DNA methylation array; 2) To compare cell lineage-specific differentially methylated genomic targets in SLE patients with early onset among important blood cell populations; and 3) To correlate these changes with cell lineage-specific changes in the transcriptome using a genome-wide expression array, and with the clinical manifestation in the same cohort of patients. We propose to use the Illumina HumanMethylation450 BeadChip, which is a genome-wide DNA methylation array that can interrogate DNA methylation levels at 450,000 CpG sites in over 99% of known genes in the human genome. We will use the Illumina Human HT-12 v4 BeadChip expression array to study cell lineage-specific transcriptome in the same patients. Together with our ongoing work on SLE in patients with adult onset, our study could provide an integrated analysis on the role of epigenetic modulation in the pathogenesis of SLE. This study will enhance our understanding of the pathogenesis of SLE. Importantly, epigenetic changes are potentially reversible and our results could lead to the identification of epigenetic targets for pharmacologic interventions. 紅斑狼瘡(Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, SLE) 是一種會損壞身體多個系統的免疫疾病，有顯著患病率及死亡率。紅斑狼瘡最主要影響亞洲人，在香港就已經有超過七千名患者。有兩成的紅斑狼瘡病人是在成年前發病。這類早期發病的紅斑狼瘡有更高的疾病嚴重性及持續至成年，引致顯著的長期負擔。早期發病的斑狼瘡的致病原因仍然未明。 基因甲基化在紅斑狼瘡是一種經過充分研究的表觀遺傳指標，免疫系統細胞的基因甲基化下跌是引致紅斑狼瘡發病的其中一種成因。據我們所知，基因甲基化剖析從未在早期發病的紅斑狼瘡病人中研究過。我們曾使用血液單核細胞來研究成人發病紅斑狼瘡病人的全基因組基因甲基化的變化。血液單核細胞包括很多不同種類的細胞群，它們在免疫系統都各有不同的功能。我們推測在血液單核細胞的T細胞、B細胞和嗜中性球之間出現不同的基因甲基化差別，而這些差別是早期發病的紅斑狼瘡之致病原因。在這研究中，我們有三個目標：一) 使用全基因甲基化微陣列技術於早期發病的紅斑狼瘡病人識別有關紅斑狼瘡的表觀遺傳基因；二) 於早期發病的紅斑狼瘡病人的重要細胞群中比較細胞的基因甲基化的分別；及三) 研究基因甲基化的改變對基因表達的影響，並和病人臨床症狀作出關聯對比。 我們將使用Illumina Methylation 450 BeadChip，一種可以在99%已知的人類基因中，偵測超過450,000個CpG位置的基因甲基化改變。我們將同時研究基因表達的改變。這個研究將結合我們現時正進行中的成人發病紅斑狼瘡研究，為將紅斑狼瘡作完整的表觀遺傳分析。由於表觀遺傳是有可能被逆轉的，因此這個研究將可能找出表觀遺傳基因作為藥物治療的標靶。

765513.label: Realisation of objectives
765513.value: All objectives have been achieved. In this project, genome-wide DNA methylation analysis has been carried out in 16 SLE patients and 13 controls using the Illumina MethylationEPIC microarray (EPIC microarray), which is a new microarray launched in late 2016. This new microarray detects the DNA methylation level of more than 850,000 CpG sites, and 90% of the content in 450k microarray has also been retained in the new microarray. In addition, this new microarray consists of more than 350,000 CpG sites targeting the enhancer regions, including the FANTOM5 enhancers, ENCODE open chromatin and enhancers, DNase hypersensitivity sites and miRNA promoters. As a result, it has been chosen to use for DNA methylation analysis instead of using the old 450k microarray as proposed in grant application. Using this new microarray, we have studied the DNA methylation changes in multiple immune cell lineages of patients with paediatric-onset SLE, including CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cells, B cells, neutrophils, and also in whole blood which represents a mixture of immune cell lineages. For objective 1, analysis of DNA methylation data of different cell lineages revealed that there were 21 probes showing loss of DNA methylation in all immune cell types. These 21 probes represented 15 genes, and gene ontology analysis showed that these genes were enriched in type I interferon signaling pathway. The result suggested that a robust SLE-specific DNA methylation signature existed in different immune cells of patients with SLE, and this SLE-specific DNA methylation signature can also be revealed by whole blood. For objective 2, we found there were some genes that were differentially methylated in specific cell lineages. Some of these genes have been reported to be associated with SLE, whereas some genes have never been reported in SLE. The findings of cell lineage-specific differentially methylated genes facilitated the understanding of the molecular pathophysiology of SLE in each immune cell population. For objective 3, we tried to correlate the DNA methylation signature with clinical manifestation (i.e SLE disease activity scores). The robust SLE-specific DNA methylation signature separated SLE patients into two groups, where one group had greater loss of DNA methylation. In T cells, the DNA methylation level was correlated with SLEDAI, yet such correlation was not statistical significant in other cell types. Further study involving a larger number of patients is required to confirm the correlation.

765513.label: Major findings and research outcome
765513.value: There were four important findings in this study. First, principal component analysis of the initial DNA methylation data set showed that the 145 samples clustered according to cell types rather than disease manifestation. This supported that importance of studying DNA methylation changes in specific immune cell populations instead of whole blood as it consists of mixture of immune cell types. Second, a robust SLE-specific DNA methylation signature can be identified in all cell lineages, which constituted of 21 hypomethylated CpG sites representing 15 genes. Gene ontology analysis showed that these genes were enriched in type I interferon signaling pathway. Principal component analysis using this robust SLE-specific DNA methylation signature showed that the 145 samples could be separated according to both the disease manifestation and cell types. The result suggested that (i) loss of DNA methylation in type I interferon-related genes is a common phenomenon in the major blood cell lineages in SLE patients; (ii) pinpointed the importance of type I interferon signaling pathway in SLE from the epigenetic point of view; (iii) suggested that DNA methylation changes in SLE can be partially revealed by whole blood and also in any immune cell populations; and (iv) the robust SLE-specific DNA methylation signature can be used as a biomarker for diagnosis of SLE, which is particularly useful in patients with paediatric-onset SLE because diagnosis of SLE in children is challenging. Third, the robust SLE-specific DNA methylation signature identified in paediatric-onset SLE had significant overlap with that of the adult-onset patients, suggesting that hypomethylation of genes in the type I interferon signaling pathway is a common phenomenon in SLE regardless of the age of disease onset. Finally, there were some differentially methylated genes which can only be identified in specific immune cell population. These cell lineage-specific differentially methylated genes indicated specific epigenetic dysregulation in each cell type. The cell type-specific DNA methylation changes facilitated the elucidation of cell-type specific molecular pathophysiology of SLE. The study has trained a PhD student who has submitted his thesis in December 2017. We are now preparing the manuscript.

765513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
765513.value: It is clear that patients with paediatric-onset SLE usually present with more severe clinical courses than the adult counterpart, with different patterns of organ involvement (Kamphuis and Silverman, 2010). As a result, the diagnosis of SLE in children is more difficult in a general paediatric setting. The identification of the robust SLE-specific DNA methylation signature indicated that it can be used as a biomarker for diagnosis of SLE. However, further research involving a large cohort of SLE patients and controls are required. We are planning to develop a biomarker with high sensitivity and specificity in SLE. Furthermore, we are planning a whole-genome transcriptome analysis in patients with SLE. Specifically we are interested to study the isoform expression changes.

765513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
765513.value: We found that there was a SLE-specific DNA methylation signature in the major blood cell types of patients with SLE. This SLE-specific DNA methylation signature provides more insight in SLE pathogenesis. In addition, it can potentially be used as a biomarker for SLE. Cell type-specific DNA methylation analysis showed some genes were differentially methylated in specific blood cell types, suggesting that some dysregulations are unique in each cell type. All the above findings allow the discovery of epigenetic changes that are important in SLE, and provide a list of genes which allows in-depth studies in the future.

766613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
766613.value: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is one of the most common fatal malignances of the digestive tract. Despite advances in diagnosis and multimodality therapies, ESCC continues to carry a grim prognosis. The major reason for this poor survival is the fact that ESCC frequently metastasizes to regional and distant lymph nodes, even at initial diagnosis. Earlier studies from our group found that the tumor stroma secreted WNT2 plays a critical role in the malignant progression of esophageal cancer cells via Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway, supporting the importance of the cancer microenvironment in the development and progression of esophageal cancer. Our preliminary data have demonstrated that conditioned medium (CM) from WNT2 transfected CHO (Chinese Hamster Ovary) cells induces epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-transcription factors (TWIST1, SLUG and ZEB1) as well as stemness markers (NANOG, SOX2, OCT4 and ALDH1A1) in ESCC cells, indicating that stromal signal WNT2 may promote cancer cell metastasis by inducing stem-like cells through EMT. Next, we treated the ESCC cells cultured in CHO-WNT2 CM with or without anti-WNT2 mouse monoclonal antibody (mAb). The results showed that the anti-WNT2 mouse mAb inhibits the Wnt/β-catenin pathway in ESCC cells. Importantly, the therapeutic potential of the anti-WNT2 mouse mAb has been demonstrated in a subcutaneous mouse xenograft model showing the paracrine WNT2 bioactivity. In the present research proposal, we extend our studies to investigate the prognostic significance and therapeutic efficacy of the microenvironment factor WNT2 in ESCC. Hence, the objectives in the present proposal will be achieved through the following interrelated specific aims: 1) to characterize the role of microenvironment factor WNT2 in metastasis and progression of ESCC; 2) to investigate the therapeutical role of anti-WNT2 mouse mAb in ESCC; and 3) to develop and characterize humanized WNT2 antibody for ESCC therapy. These research objectives will be tackled with a multidisciplinary approach combining biochemistry, molecular and cell biology, and animal model. This proposed study is significant in several respects. First, this study will provide considerable insight into how the microenvironment surrounding the cancer cells is an active participant during the metastatic process. Second, the proposed work will contribute to understanding the clinical significance of the microenvironment factor WNT2 in ESCC. Third, this study will provide rational and advantageous new approach for the therapy of ESCC. Therefore, the outcomes of this proposal will help elucidate the clinical implications of the microenvironment factor WNT2 in esophageal cancer. 食管鱗癌是一種常見的消化系統惡性腫瘤。儘管目前在食管癌的診斷和綜合治療方面都取得了相當進展，但其預後仍然不盡人意，成為嚴重影響人類生命健康的疾病。前期研究發現，腫瘤相關成纖維細胞(TF)分泌的WNT2蛋白通過激活食管鱗癌細胞Wnt/ β-catenin信號通路以及促進EMT過程的發生，進而參與食管鱗癌的惡性發展進程。預實驗結果顯示，含有WNT2的條件培養基可誘導食管鱗癌細胞中乾細胞標誌物(NANOG、 SOX2、 OCT4 及ALDH1A1)表達增強，提示腫瘤微環境因子WNT2與食管腫瘤幹細胞的相關性。此外，當鼠源WNT2特異性單克隆抗體中和條件培養基內的WNT2之後，與對照組相比，腫瘤細胞β-catenin的核轉移被顯著抑制。更重要的是，初步實驗結果顯示WNT2單抗可有效抑制裸鼠皮下移植瘤的生長，因而成功建立WNT2單抗治療的體內動物模型。為了進一步了解腫瘤微環境因子WNT2是否可以作為單抗治療食管癌新的分子靶向，本課題擬通過實現以下幾個目標1）探討腫瘤微環境因子WNT2在食管鱗癌惡性轉移中的作用及機制；2）研究WNT2單抗對食管鱗癌的潛在治療作用；以及3）研究和開發人源性WNT2單克隆抗體，最終為發展新型食管癌的治療方法提供堅實的理論基礎。

766613.label: Realisation of objectives
766613.value: 1. We identified that WNT2 ligand could directly bind to the Frizzled-7 (FZD7) receptor in ESCC. WNT2 promoted ESCC cell metastatic ability and self-renewal potential via the FZD7 receptor. 2. We developed a novel anti-WNT2 monoclonal antibody (designate as F003 mAb) against the secreted human WNT2 ligand, and examined its effect on ESCC cells with or without recombinant human WNT2 protein (rWNT2) stimulation in vitro. The results showed that F003 mAb significantly abolished the metastasis-promoting effect of WNT2 in ESCC cells by interfering the WNT/β-catenin and EMT pathways. The stemness-promoting effect of WNT2 on ESCC cells was also reversed by F003 mAb via inhibiting the phospho-STAT3 activity. Synergistic inhibitory effects of F003 mAb and STAT3 inhibitor were also observed on ESCC cells. The therapeutic potential of F003 mAb by targeting CAFs secreted WNT2 in ESCC was further studied in LN metastasis mouse model in vivo. We found that the F003 mAb could significantly suppress the popliteal LN metastasis in NOD/SCID mice without toxic effects on normal mouse tissues. 3. Mouse anti-WNT2 Fab (fragment-antigen binding) antibody was identified and humanized by CDR-grafting followed by framework optimization for improved affinity and solubility by site-directed and random mutageneses in combination with antibody phage display and yeast display selections. Humanized antibody gene was converted to IgG1 by subcloning the antibody gene to a mammalian expression vector containing human genomic Fc gene. The therapeutical effect of humanlized WNT2 Ab was similar to the mouse WNT2 Ab.

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
766613.value: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is one of the most common fatal malignances of the digestive tract and often metastasizes to lymph nodes (LNs). Despite advances in diagnosis and multimodality therapies, ESCC continues to carry a grim prognosis. New therapeutical strategies for effective clinical treatment of ESCC patients are urgently needed. Our previous studies found that the cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) secreted WNT2 plays a critical role in the malignant progression of ESCC. In this study, we further found that WNT2 could promote metastasis and induce stemness in ESCC. Notably, cancer stem cells (CSCs) are responsible for chemotherapy resistance and local recurrence or distant organ metastasis, which are the major causes of cancer mortality. Conventional cancer treatments do not consistently prevent cancer recurrence. Thus, we developed a novel anti-WNT2 antibody to test its therapeutic potential in ESCC. We found that anti-WNT2 antibody can significantly block the microenvironment released WNT2 factor and their induced CSCs, as well as effectively minimize the lymph node metastatic ability in ESCC, suggesting that anti-WNT2 antibody could be a potential anti-cancer drug for ESCC patients. Ultimately, we look forward the research outcomes of this proposal could facilitate the collaboration between university and industry for technology transfer.

766913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
766913.value: 先天性膽管擴張（先天性膽總管擴張/膽總管囊腫/ CCD）導致膽汁淤積，引起膽管炎、胰腺炎和惡性腫瘤等相關的倂發症。 CCD非常罕見，僅有個案報導。CCD的發病率跟種族有關，亞洲人最高（1/1，000而白種人1/150，000）。 CCD的主要發病機制表明膽管擴張是继发于肝膽胰系統發育中出現的結構畸形。因此，調控肝膽胰腺系統發育的基因發生改變可以導致CCD。用於CCD的遺傳指標為：一）男性/女性的偏差；二）跨人種的發病率顯著差異；三）稀有性和病症的早期表現，四）先天性結構異常。 A)罕見的染色體異常（拷貝數變異/ CNV）或微小的DNA改變（“突變”）干擾基因的功能都會導致稀有的遺傳性疾病，B）非遺傳性和/或隱性遺傳的特徵解釋了CCD的罕見和散發的性質，因此我們推測，非遺傳性或隱性遺傳的危害性突變/ CNVs可以導致CCD。非遺傳性突變來源於：i）父母配子（生殖細胞或其他細胞）或ii）受精卵發育異常（細胞分化異常）。肝膽胰系統祖細胞（內胚層）的非遺傳性突變可能既不會傳代，也沒有在血液DNA中檢測出來（不同胚胎來源）。這些現象可以共存並說明了：1）CCD罕見和散發的性質;2）不同類型的CCD；3）CCD患者癌癥發病率高。 大多數突變/ CNVs影響了基因的編碼序列（CDS-外顯子），所以我們利用全外顯子測序和高分辨率染色體核型分析對75名 CCD患者進行研究，分別找出CDS突變和/或CNVs。研究這種罕見的散髮性疾病，最好的方法就是“家庭研究（父母與子代）”，患病的兒童和健康的父母經過實驗分析、對比和篩查後找出非遺傳性突變/ CNVs。嬰兒的DNA將從切除的CCD組織中提取，因CCD組織是遺傳性和非遺傳性(體细胞或生殖細胞)突變共存的區域。因此，我們的研究方案不僅能發現罕見的家庭遺傳性突變，也可以發現新非遺傳性突變(體细胞或生殖細胞)的起源，為研究該疾病的發病機制提供重要線索。 發生率較高的基因突變和染色體區域/基因突變，將在散發病例（N=200）中驗證，以確定這些基因突變和染色體區域/基因和CCD的關係。這是首次對CCD開展的基因研究。

As for the screening of additional patients, given that: * Sample size limited: investigate more samples for mutations in the genes identified by this study * As the genes identified are known to be involved in cancers arising from the bile-ducts walls, we believe that in the long term, if our results are replicated in a larger sample size, cancer preventive measures could be designed or envisaged.
