766913.label: Major findings and research outcome
766913.value: Congenital dilatation of the bile-duct (CDD) is a rare, mostly sporadic, disorder that results in bile retention with severe associated complications. CDD affects mainly Asians. To our knowledge, no genetic study had ever been conducted. We aimed to identify genetic risk factors by a "trio-based" exome-sequencing approach, whereby 31 CDD probands and their unaffected parents were exome-sequenced. Seven-hundred controls from the local population were used to detect gene-sets significantly enriched with rare variants in CDD patients. We identified 21 predicted damaging de novo variants (DNVs; 4 protein truncating and 17 missense) were identified in several evolutionarily constrained genes (p < 0.01). Six genes carrying DNVs were associated with human developmental disorders involving epithelial, connective or bone morphologies (PXDN, RTEL1, ANKRD11, MAP2K1, CYLD, ACAN) and four linked with cholangio- and hepatocellular carcinomas (PIK3CA, TLN1 CYLD, MAP2K1). Importantly, CDD patients have an excess of DNVs in cancer-related genes (p < 0.025). Thirteen genes were recurrently mutated at different sites, forming compound heterozygotes or functionally related complexes within patients. We have also identified two de novo recurrent copy number variants at chromosome 21 encompassing four genes related to autoimmunity. Links are being investigated Our data supports a strong genetic basis for CDD and show that CDD is not only genetically heterogeneous but also non-monogenic, requiring mutations in more than one genes for the disease to develop. The data is consistent with the rarity and sporadic presentation of CDD.

766913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
766913.value: Congenital dilatation of the bile-duct (CDD) is a birth defect (present at birth) that causes obstruction of the bile ducts and retention of bile. This leads to jaundice and an enlarged liver and may trigger serious liver damage. The causes are not known but we thought that it may be due damage in the DNA of the affected child (the damage can be inherited from both unaffected parents or occur anew in the child). We screened the DNA of 31 patients and their parents and found that there exists DNA lesions that vary from person to person even though the outcome is the same: CCD

767313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
767313.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most common cancers worldwide. According to the cancer stem cell (CSC) model, cancer originates from a subset of stem like cells characterized with elevated stemness (e.g. self-renewal and chemo-resistance) and maintained in a dedifferentiated status. The molecular mechanisms governing stemness and differentiation status of HCC still remains poorly understood. Therefore, targeting on critical proteins that regulate cancer stemness and differentiation emerges as a novel therapeutic strategy in cancer treatment. Recent reports suggest that chromodomain helicase DNA-binding (Chd) family plays important roles in embryonic stem cell differentiation. CHD1L, which belongs to the Chd family, is a well-studied oncogene isolated by my laboratory from a frequently amplified chromosome region at 1q21 of HCC. Our previous studies indicate that CHD1L could transcriptionally activate several oncogenic pathways and promote HCC cell proliferation, apoptosis and metastasis. Overexpression of CHD1L can elevate stemness of HCC such as chemo-resistance and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). To systematically understand the transcriptome regulated by CHD1L, high-throughput Chip-sequencing was performed to identify CHD1L binding targets in HCC cell line PLC8024. Network analysis finds that 5 out of the 10 top-ranked networks are associated with system development including embryonic development. In addition, our preliminary data strongly suggest that CHD1L might be involved in regulating liver cancer stemness and differentiation, including 1) CHD1L confers resistance to chemotherapeutic agents; 2) CHD1L can promote EMT; 3) CHD1L is associated with fetal liver development and poor differentiation of HCC; 4) CHD1L may regulates critical genes associated with stemness and differentiation, including NFκB, Wnt/β-catenin and c-myc. Therefore, I plan to investigate the effects of CHD1L on the regulation of HCC stemness and differentiation. The molecular mechanisms and critical networks of CHD1L in regulating HCC stemness and differentiation will be also addressed. A better understanding of the physiological and pathological roles of CHD1L will significantly improve our knowledge of HCC pathogenesis. Such knowledge has long-term implication for the development of new therapeutic method targeting on CHD1L-mediated networks for the regulation of stemness and differentiation of HCC. 肝細胞肝癌（HCC）是世界上最常見的惡性腫瘤之一。根據腫瘤幹細胞（CSC）模型，腫瘤起源於一類幹細胞類細胞，它們具備幹細胞的特徵（如自我更新和耐藥性）並維持去分化狀態。目前對肝癌如何維持幹細胞幹性和細胞分化的分子機制瞭解甚少，因此尋找維持幹細胞幹性和細胞分化的關鍵蛋白可以作為肝癌治療的新策略。最近相關報導指出CHD家族成員在胚胎幹細胞去分化的調控中起重要作用，CHD家族成員之一的CHD1L是我們實驗室從肝癌常見染色體擴增區1q21中分離的癌基因，我們以前的研究發現CHD1L可以在肝癌中調高一些與細胞分裂、凋亡和轉移相關的信號傳導通路表達，也可以提高肝癌幹細胞幹性（如耐藥性和上皮-間質細胞轉換）。為了進一步瞭解CHD1L在轉錄調控中的作用，高通量ChIP測序技術被用來發現CHD1L在肝癌細胞株PLC8024中結合的可能靶基因，基因網路調控分析發現在前10名調控網路中，與胚胎發育和系統發育相關的網路占了5名。此外，我們初步的實驗結果也表明CHD1L可能密切參與調控肝癌細胞的幹性和分化。證據包括：1）CHD1L增強了肝癌細胞對化療藥物的耐受性；2）CHD1L促進肝癌細胞的上皮間質轉化；3）CHD1L與胎肝發育及肝癌分化水準密切相關；4）CHD1L可能參與調控包括NFκB, Wnt/β-catenin 和c-myc在內的與細胞幹性及分化相關的關鍵信號通路。基於以上初步結果，我們計畫進一步研究CHD1L對肝癌幹性及分化水準調控以及相應的的分子機制。我們相信深入瞭解CHD1L在肝癌發生發展中的角色將有助於我們進一步闡明肝癌的發病機制。長遠來看這也有助於我們進一步針對CHD1L調節肝癌幹性及分化的細胞信號通路設計新的治療藥物。

767313.label: Realisation of objectives
767313.value: In this proposal, I have addressed all three objectives. High-grade tumors with poor differentiation usually show phenotypic resemblance to their developmental ancestral cells. Cancer cells that gain lineage precursor cell properties usually hijack developmental signaling pathways to promote tumor malignant progression. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying this process remain unclear. In this study, the chromatin remodeler chromodomain-helicase-DNA-binding-protein 1-like (CHD1L) was found closely associated with liver development and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tumor differentiation. Expression of CHD1L decreased during hepatocyte maturation and increased progressively from well-differentiated HCCs to poorly differentiated HCCs. Chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by high-throughput deep sequencing found that CHD1L could bind to the genomic sequences of genes related to development. Bioinformatics-aided network analysis indicated that CHD1L-binding targets might form networks associated with developmental transcription factor activation and histone modiﬁcation. Overexpression of CHD1L conferred ancestral precursor-like properties of HCC cells both in vitro and in vivo. Inhibition of CHD1L reversed tumor differentiation and sensitized HCC cells to sorafenib treatment. Mechanism studies revealed that overexpression of CHD1L could maintain an active “open chromatin” conﬁguration at promoter regions of estrogenrelated receptor-beta and transcription factor 4, both of which are important regulators of HCC self-renewal and differentiation. In addition, we found a signiﬁcant correlation of CHD1L with developmental transcriptional factors and lineage differentiation markers in clinical HCC patients. Conclusion: Genomic ampliﬁcation of chromatin remodeler CHD1L might drive dedifferentiation of HCC toward an ancestral lineage through opening chromatin for key developmental transcriptional factors; further inhibition of CHD1L might “downgrade” poorly differentiated HCCs and provide novel therapeutic strategies.

767913.label: Realisation of objectives
767913.value: We have completed the three objectives in the study according to the experiments proposed in the original RGC proposal. However, we face a problem on the isolation of the neonatal cardiomyocytes, therefore, we did not determine the effects of A-FABP in endothelial cells contributing to the diabetic cardiomyopathy in vitro. However, our in vivo data have clearly demonstrated that 1. A-FABP is significantly induced in endothelial cells but not in cardiomyocytes after diabetes and myocardial ischemic/reperfusion injury; 2. A-FABP KO mice exhibited an attenuated diabetes- or MI/R- induced cardiac reactive oxygen species production associating with increased eNOS phosphorylation and NO production. 3. Treatment of NOS inhibitor (L-NAME) abolished the cardioprotective effect of A-FABP KO mice on MI/R. All these indicated the increased expression of A-FABP in the endothelial cells under diabetes or MI/R condition impaired eNOS-NO pathway contributing to endothelial dysfunction by increasing oxidative stress and nitrative stress which eventually lead to cardiomyocyte apoptosis and inflammation (cardiac dysfunction) (please refer to our publication; Zhou M et al., 2015, Clinical Science).

767913.label: Major findings and research outcome
767913.value: 1. The circulating levels and the cardiac expression of A-FABP were significantly increased after STZ induction as well as under high fat diet induction. 2. Immunohistochemistry result suggested that the major cardiac cell source of A-FABP is endothelial cells but not cardiomyocytes. 3. A-FABP deficiency greatly alleviated the STZ or HFD-induced cardiac hypertrophy and fibrosis as confirmed by reduced cardiomyocyte diameters and reduced collagen accumulation stained by Sirius red staining as compared to their wildtype (WT)-littermates. Under HFD induction, A-FABP KO mice also exhibited reduced lipid accumulation in the cardiac muscle as compared to the WT littermates. 4. A-FABP deficient mice exhibit preserved cardiac systolic and diastolic function when under diabetic condition comparing to WT mice. Furthermore, high fat diet-induced cardiac dysfunction was alleviated in A-FABP deficient mice. The improved cardiac function in A-FABP deficient mice is associated with reduced expression of hypertrophic markers and disease markers of cardiomyopathy. These data indicated that A-FABP deficiency protects against diabetes and high fat diet-induced cardiomyopathy and cardiac dysfunction. 5. Diabetes-induced superoxide anion production in heart tissues was greatly attenuated in A-FABP KO mice. However, diabetes does not cause the increased accumulation of nitrotyrosine and elevation of proinflammatory cytokines in cardiac muscle of WT and A-FABP KO mice. In contrast, A-FABP KO mice showed a reduced superoxide anion production, ER stress and inflammation after high fat diet induction as compared to their WT littermates. 6. In WT mice, diabetes did not cause impairment of eNOS-NO signaling pathway. Notably, diabetes induced a markedly increase of eNOS phosphorylation in A-FABP deficient hearts, this consistently associated with a slightly elevated nitric oxide production in the KO mice as compared to their WT littermates. These findings suggest that activation of the eNOS-NO pathway upon diabetes was suppressed in the presence of A-FABP. 7. Furthermore, treatment of A-FABP selective inhibitor BMS309403 which competes for the free fatty acid binding site of A-FABP can significantly alleviated cardiac hypertrophy and fibrosis in db/db diabetic mice. The left ventricular cardiac function was improved and accompanied by reduced ER stress, inflammation and superoxide production as determined by Q-PCR, Western blot analysis and DHE staining. These data indicated that A-FABP inhibitor is a potential therapeutic treatment for diabetic cardiomyopathy and cardiac injury. 8. In this study, we concluded that A-FABP is a key mediator of diabetes and obesity-related cardiac dysfunction and heart failure. Pharmacological inhibitor of A-FABP may a potential strategy for the treatment of diabetic cardiomyopathy and cardiac injury.

767913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
767913.value: In addition to the proposed experiments in the original proposal, we have found that A-FABP deficiency attenuates myocardial ischemic-reperfusion (MI/R) injury under normal and diabetes conditions as indicated by reduced myocardial infract size, diminished cardiomyocyte apoptosis which are associated with improved systolic and diastolic functions comparing to their WT littermates. A-FABP deficiency also decreased MI/R-induced oxidative stress and nitrative as indicated by reduced staining of cardiac nitrotyrosine and cardiac superoxide production. A-FABP deficiency protects against cardiac injury by activating the endothelial eNOS-NO signaling pathway associating with reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine production. Therefore, we concluded that A-FABP deficiency protects mice against diabetic cardiomyopathy and MI/R-induced cardiac injury at least partially acting through activating eNOS-nitric oxide pathway. We have further verified the pharmacological effect of BMS309403 (the selective A-FABP inhibitor) on obesity/ diabetes related cardiac dysfunction using a high fat diet-induced obese model (a more physiological relevant model). The result demonstrated that diet-induced cardiac dysfunction such as fat accumulation, collagen deposition and the increased cardiomyocyte size were markedly alleviated by the treatment of BMS309403. The expression of hypertrophic markers, inflammatory markers and ER markers are also greatly reduced. This further supports the drug that targeting A-FABP can be the potential therapeutic for treatment of obesity and diabetes associated cardiac complications. This part was assigned as the project for our student of master of medical science (Miss Zhong Dan) and she was trained with several laboratory techniques including H&E staining for histological analysis, Oil Red O staining, sirius red staining, Western blot analysis and quantitative PCR. The results were used for her dissertation writing (Please refer to part 10).

767913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
767913.value: There is increasing incidence of diabetes mellitus worldwide. It is a major cause of morbidity and death in Hong Kong and is the key risk factor for vascular disease contributing to the development of cardiac dysfunction. In this study, we showed that a fat derived hormone, the fatty acid binding protein (A-FABP) is the key mediator of obesity related cardiac dysfunction and diabetes cardiomyopathy through suppressing eNOS activation and NO production leading to the increased oxidative stress, inflammation and ER stress. We also found that the use of BMS309403 which is a selective inhibitor of A-FABP could significantly alleviate genetically obesity associated- and high fat diet-induced cardiac dysfunction in mice. Our findings highlight the importance of A-FABP in the cardiac disorders and suggest that A-FABP is a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of obesity and diabetes associated heart complications.

768113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
768113.value: 在微管上進行逆向運輸所需的保守的馬達蛋白Kinesin-1是由兩條重鍊和兩條輕鏈組成；Kif5b是廣泛表達的馬達蛋白重鏈。目前已經知道：在到達細胞邊緣的微管正極時，Kif5b釋放所運輸的貨物並離開微管；但是，仍然不清楚Kif5b離開微管後的命運和可能參與的功能。 籠形蛋白介導的內吞通路對於調節細胞表面許多蛋白的水平非常重要，這些蛋白包括對胞外信號作出響應和介道的質膜上的G-蛋白耦連受體。一旦被其特異性的配基激活，大多數的G-蛋白耦連受體於是進行籠形蛋白介導的內吞，然後進入早期內吞體和溶酶體進行降解或者重新循環回到質膜。籠形蛋白介導的通路包括一系列高度協調的步驟，例如，包被形成和內陷、籠形蛋白包被小泡的解聚。干擾其中任何步驟可能影響了整個內吞過程，從而改變質膜上或全細胞的受體水平，最終導致信號轉道的異常。 我們的初步數據顯示Kif5b通過籠形蛋白重鏈結合到內吞途徑上的籠形蛋白包被小泡上。內吞途徑上的籠形蛋白包被小泡一旦在內吞過程中就迅速地在細胞邊緣解聚，另一方面，Kif5b負責的是由里向外的運輸，基於這些已知知識：這些籠形蛋白包被小泡應該不是被Kif5b運輸的貨物。在已建立的的籠形蛋白包被小泡解聚的體外實驗中我們發現：下調Kif5b水平減少內吞途徑上的籠形蛋白包被小泡解聚，加入Kif5b C端促進解聚過程。接著我們研究G-蛋白耦連受體的一種亞型------乙酰膽鹼受體，該受體參與到阿爾茲海默症認知障礙。我們觀察到下調Kif5b表達水平增加全細胞及細胞質膜上的1-和3-型乙酰膽鹼受體水平。同時， 我們發現過表達一段能夠結合籠形蛋白重鏈的Kif5b片段增加了Neura2a細胞中的3-型乙酰膽鹼受體水平； 我們猜想過表達的該片段同內源性的Kif5b競爭結合籠形蛋白包被小泡，從而對籠形蛋白介導的內吞產生了類似Kif5b下調的效果。

768313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
768313.value: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is well-established therapy for patients with malignant hematological diseases. Varicella zoster virus (VZV) reactivation, clinically manifested as herpes zoster (HZ), is a major complication that affects up to 50% of patients. Most patients will require hospitalization. Despite treatment with high-dose acyclovir, patients may develop severe complications including the disabling post-herpetic neuralgia, corneal ulceration, viral dissemination and secondary bacterial infection. The median onset of infection is the fifth month following transplantation, with 91% of cases occurring within the first year. Direct vaccination of transplants recipients with subcutaneous live-attenuated VZVv before transplantation and up to one year after transplantation is contraindicated. A small prospective non-randomized study has demonstrated that subcutaneous vaccination for donors before HSCT may offer some protection against VZV reactivation in the recipients. Recently, dose-sparing influenza vaccine delivered via a novel intradermal microneedle has been shown to elicit a good immunogenic response in both healthy and elderly subjects. We sought to assess the efficacy and safety of the novel intradermal live-attenuated VZVv in sibling donors undergoing HSCT. We plan to enroll 120 pairs of adult donors and patients who undergo allogeneic HLA- matched sibling HSCT in this prospective randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial over a period of 3 years. Enrolled donors and patients will be randomized into 4 groups: Group 1: intradermal reduced dose live-attenuated VZVv; Group 2: subcutaneous full dose live-attenuated VZVv; Group 3: intradermal 0.9% normal saline as control and Group 4: subcutaneous 0.9% normal saline as the second control. All vaccines will be given to the donors at 28 days. All intradermal vaccines will be given via a microneedle syringe. Both the investigators and participants will be blinded to the randomization process. The primary end points are the safety and immunological response in the donors. The secondary end point is the occurrence of HZ in the patients within 12 months of transplantation. Adverse reactions of the vaccine will be assessed immediately and for 21 days after vaccination. Donors and recipients in the three groups will be tested for immunity against VZV at 30 days prior to transplantation (before vaccination) and 0, 30, 90, 180 and 360 days following transplantation. Immunity to VZV will be measured. Clinical evaluation of zoster will be performed by patient self-reporting via hotlines, and by monthly interview with investigators in the first year after transplant. Diagnosis of zoster will be confirmed by indirect immunofluorescence of vesicular fluid to detect VZV-specific antigens. 用血幹細胞移植治療惡性血液病患者是非常成功。然而水痘 - 帶狀皰疹病毒（VZV ）在移植病者的激活併發症，則多達50％。發病期的中位數則在移植後的第五個月， 91％的病例在第一年內發生。儘管用高劑量的阿昔洛韋在治療，患者遭受帶狀皰疹併發症的機會仍很高，其中包括帶狀皰疹後神經痛，角膜潰瘍，病毒傳播和繼發性細菌感染。 細胞介導的免疫力被認為發揮著重要作用，接受阿昔洛韋預防規定的第一個月移植後，帶狀皰疹的風險可能會降低，但它通常發生在預防停止後。 在移植前和移植後的一年用皮下皰疹疫苗直接接種移植者是絕對不適合, 而接種熱滅活的實驗疫苗是有潛在風險. 因此, 我們提出了一個前瞻性雙盲，隨機，安慰劑對照研究, 嘗試用皮內注射為血幹細胞移植提供者接種皰疹病毒疫苗, 繼而評估在移植者的安全性，免疫原性和臨床療效。

768613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
768613.value: 全世界超過兩千萬人受到人T細胞白血病病毒1型(HTLV-1)的感染，其中約3%的人會發展為凶險而且致死率極高的血癌，稱為成人T細胞白血病(ATL)，而另外1%則罹患另一種名為熱帶痙攣性癱瘓(TSP)的慢性神經性炎症。盡管發病周期很長而發病原因及階段很多，但ATL與TSP發病總是與高企的HTLV-1原病毒載量呈現正相關。ATL與TSP無特效療法，其治療效果差強人意。 HTLV-1編碼反式激活蛋白Tax，透過CREB、CBP和CRTC(又稱為TORC)等細胞轉錄調節蛋白強力刺激病毒長末端重複(LTR)的轉錄。此外，Tax還透過CREB和NF-kB刺激多種細胞基因的表達。Tax在ATL和TSP的發生發展過程中具有關鍵的作用。對抗Tax的活性或清除表達有Tax的細胞均有一定療效，而醫治HTLV-1感染的其中一個發展方向就是研製小分子化合物來控制Tax及Tax調節蛋白的功能。本項研究旨在確定SIRT1脫乙酰酶對Tax的調控作用並探討諸如Resveratrol一類的SIRT1刺激物在抗HTLV-1治療中的應用前景。 SIRT1可透過其依賴於NAD 的脫乙酰酶活性修飾組蛋白、轉錄因子及輔助調節蛋白從而在轉錄調控中發揮關鍵作用。SIRT1 在衰老、代謝、應激反應、癌症及人類免疫缺損病毒感染中的意義已有充分研究。SIRT1 可作用於CREB和CRTC1並抑制其活性。我們在已進行的預實驗中發現，SIRT1可與Tax結合並通過本身的脫乙酰功能強力抑制Tax的活性。SIRT1的表達可抑制HTLV-1感染細胞中病毒的轉錄，而採用RNAi或藥物抑制SIRT1則可增強HTLV-1的轉錄。此外，用Resveratrol激活SIRT1後，HTLV-1轉化的T淋巴細胞中病毒基因的表達也受到抑制。 在本項研究中，我們將全面深入研究SIRT1脫乙酰酶在HTLV-1轉錄及致腫瘤發病過程中的作用。首先，我們將在HTLV-1感染細胞中採用過表達和敲減等方法研究SIRT1對HTLV-1轉錄的負調控作用。其次，我們將闡明SIRT1抑制HTLV-1轉錄的分子機理，逐一探討SIRT1與Tax的相互作用、SIRT1及其他調節蛋白在LTR的募集以及SIRT1對CREB和CRTC的作用。再次，我們將揭示SIRT1在HTLV-1病理中的意義，確定SIRT1在HTLV-1感染細胞中表達和活性並釐清SIRT1對HTLV-1轉化細胞增殖和轉化的影響。最後，我們將研究一組SIRT1的小分子刺激劑，確定其在感染細胞中的抗HTLV-1活性。 HTLV-1轉錄對ATL和TSP的發生至關重要。本項研究可揭示SIRT1脫乙酰酶與Tax的相互作用並闡明HTLV-1轉錄調控的新機理。我們的發現還將為研製新的小分子SIRT1刺激劑作為防治HTLV-1相關疾病的新的標靶藥物奠定基礎。其中Resveratrol一類的藥物可能具有一定的應用前景，可在HTLV-1帶毒人群中試作預防及治療用途。

768613.label: Realisation of objectives
768613.value: All four specific aims stated in our original proposal have been accomplished successfully. All experiments proposed and many more additional experiments have been done. One high-quality research article on this topic of SIRT1 suppression of HTLV-1 gene expression has been published in Journal of Virology in 2015. 1) Characterization of SIRT1-mediated restriction of HTLV-1 transcription: We have documented SIRT1 suppression of HTLV-1 transcription in infected T cells by multiple gain-of-function and loss-of-function assays. Whereas overexpression of SIRT1 in HTLV-1-infected T cells or treatment of these cells with Resveratrol suppresses HTLV-1 transcription, knockdown of SIRT1 by siRNA or inhibition by Sirtinol or Ex527 boosts LTR activation by Tax. Mutants of Tax and SIRT1 have been used extensively in the characterization of this suppression. 2) Mechanism of SIRT1-mediated restriction of HTLV-1 transcription: We have carried out mechanistic study to characterize the interaction between Tax and SIRT1, the recruitment of Tax, SIRT1, CREB and CRTCs to LTR, as well as the requirement of acetylase activity and Tax-SIRT1 interaction for the suppression of HTLV-1 transcription. Our current model is that SIRT1 activity presents the interaction between Tax and CREB and the recruitment of CREB and CRTC1 to LTR. We have also characterized the impact of SIRT1 on Tax activation of NF-kB. 3) On one hand, we characterized the expression and activity profiles of SIRT1 in HTLV-1-transformed ATL cells C8166, MT2 and MT4. On the other hand, we found that overexpression of SIRT1 or activation of SIRT1 by Resveratrol inhibits growth and proliferation of C8166, MT2 and MT4 cells. Similar results were also obtained from Jurkat T cells freshly infected with HTLV-1. Collectively, SIRT1 is a critical antiviral protein involved in cellular response to HTLV-1 infection and particularly cellular regulation of HTLV-1 transcription activated by Tax. 4) We performed one round of activity screening for anti-HTLV-1 and antiproliferative effect of small-molecule activators of SIRT1. We found that treatment of HTLV-1-transformed C8166, MT2 and MT4 cells with Resveratrol led to SIRT1 activation, reduction in Tax expression, and inhibition of cell growth and proliferation. Our findings laid a solid foundation for further analysis of the anti-HTLV-1 and anti-ATL activity of Resveratrol and other SIRT1 activators.

768613.label: Major findings and research outcome
768613.value: 1) We demonstrated the suppression of Tax activation of HTLV-1 LTR by SIRT1 deacetylase. The transcriptional activity of Tax on the LTR was largely ablated when SIRT1 was overexpressed, but Tax activation of NF-κB was unaffected. On the contrary, the activation of the LTR by Tax was boosted when SIRT1 was depleted. Treatment of cells with Resveratrol shunted Tax activity in a SIRT1-dependent manner. The activation of SIRT1 in HTLV-1-transformed T cells by Resveratrol potently inhibited HTLV-1 proviral transcription and Tax expression, whereas compromising SIRT1 by specific inhibitors augmented HTLV-1 mRNA expression. The administration of Resveratrol also decreased the production of cell-free HTLV-1 virion from MT2 cells and the transmission of HTLV-1 from MT2 cells to uninfected Jurkat cells in co-culture. SIRT1 associated with Tax in HTLV-1-transformed T cells. Treatment with Resveratrol prevented the interaction of Tax with CREB and the recruitment of CREB, CRTC1 and p300 to Tax-responsive elements in the LTR. Our work demonstrates the negative regulatory function of SIRT1 in Tax activation of HTLV-1 transcription. Small molecule activators of SIRT1 such as Resveratrol might be considered as new prophylactic and therapeutic agents in HTLV-1-associated diseases (Tang et al., J. Virol., 2015). We also extended our analysis of the regulatory roles of CREB and CRTCs to other oncogenic viruses, particularly hepatitis B virus (HBV). We found that CRTC1 is induced in HBV-infected cells (Tang et al., Nucl. Acids Res., 2014). However, we found that the role of SIRT1 in HBV transcription is opposite to its suppression of HTLV-1 LTR activity. 2) We performed a study to investigate how HTLV-1 Tax might regulates cellular activation of innate antiviral response. We found that Tax potently suppresses type I IFN production by interacting with and inhibiting IRF3 kinases TBK1 and IKKi. IFN-β induction was compromised in HTLV-1-transformed C8166, MT4 and MT2 cells as well as T lymphocytes acutely infected with HTLV-1. Tax is responsible for the suppression of IRF3 phosphorylation. Interestingly, Tax alone was capable of repressing both the PACT-RIG-I and the cGAS-STING pathways. Its action point is thought to be upstream of IRF3 activation since it has no activity on phosphomimetic mutant IRF3-5D. Tax mutants deficient for CREB or NF-κB activation were fully active in the suppression of IFN production. Tax interacts with TBK1, IKKi, STING and IRF3. In vitro phosphorylation assay indicated that Tax inhibits TBK1 phosphorylation (Yuen et al., 2016).

768613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
768613.value: We published one research article in Journal of Virology in 2015 to report on SIRT1-dependent regulation of HTLV-1 gene expression. Another related research article on Tax function in HTLV-1 infection and HTLV-1 induction of interferon β production was also published in Journal of Virology in 2016. The funding from RGC GRF enable us to demonstrate again to the world our unique strength and vigor in HTLV-1 research. We aim to further develop our study on HTLV-1 towards two important directions concerning anti-HTLV-1 drug discovery and HTLV-1 evasion of innate immunity. We have a strong track record and we are confident that we can do well in these two areas. Unfortunately at this point we have zero public funding to support our continuing work in this field and have to rely upon private donation which is very unstable and unsustainable in Hong Kong. I will work harder to secure new funding from RGC and other sources to support our long-standing research on HTLV-1 so that it will not be interrupted in the next few years.

768613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
768613.value: Human T-cell leukemia virus type 1 (HTLV-1) chronically infects 5-20 million people worldwide with particularly high infection rate in Japan and some other areas. In a small subset of infected people HTLV-1 is the cause of an aggressive and fatal blood cancer named adult T-cell leukemia (ATL). Treatments for ATL are unsatisfactory and treatment options are limited. A better understanding of how HTLV-1 gene expression is controlled will provide new ideas and methods for treatment of HTLV-1 infection and ATL. Small-molecule compounds targeting protein deacetylases such as SIRT1 are potentially useful for precision treatment of cancer. One of these compounds named Resveratrol has already been widely used in nutritional supplements. Thus, elucidation of how protein deacetylases control HTLV-1 gene expression might help to identify new compounds for precision treatment of ATL. In this study we showed SIRT1 to be an inhibitor of HTLV-1 gene expression. Small-molecule activators of SIRT1 such as Resveratrol are therefore potentially useful in the treatment of HTLV-1 infection and ATL. Our findings not only generate new knowledge in HTLV-1 biology but also have important implications in the rational design and development of new anti-HTLV-1 and anti-ATL agents for prevention and control of HTLV-1-associated human diseases.

768713.label: Realisation of objectives
768713.value: Periodontal (gum) disease consisting of gingivitis and periodontitis is a major global oral health burden with huge healthcare costs and socio-economic impacts. Severe periodontitis is the predominant cause of tooth loss and edentulism in adults, and yet it closely links with systemic diseases like diabetes mellitus and cardiovascular diseases through the underlying pathways of infection, inflammation, dysbiosis and shared risk factors (e.g. tobacco usage). Scientific evidence shows that periodontal disease is initiated by the shift of microbial symbiosis to dysbiosis and dysregulated immuno-inflammatory response, resulting in substantial destruction of tooth-supporting tissues and eventually leading to tooth loss. Currently, P. gingivalis is recognized as a keystone periodontopathogen. It enables to drive the shift of symbiotic bacteria to dysbiotic ones, and critically accounts for the onset of disease and tissue destruction. P. gingivalis LPS is one of its crucial virulence factors strongly involved in periodontal pathogenesis [Papers I & II]. It is well documented that P. gingivalis acts differently in response to hemin- and temperature-related microenvironmental conditions, through producing various isoforms of LPS with heterogeneous lipid A structures. Notably, oral/gingival epithelia are the frontline host cells interacting with the complex microbial challenges including P. gingivalis, and account critically for the integrity of host defense system and periodontal health. Our previous RGC-funded studies (Jin et al 2011; GRF 766909) show that human gingival epithelia act as crucial biological barriers against microbial invasion. The present project has explored how these hemin- and growth temperature-dependent phenotypes of P. gingivalis may affect the bacteria-host corsstalk and resultant immuno-inflammatory response, through a defined bacteria-host interactive model. Furthermore, the differential effects of oral commensals with reference to oral pathogens including P. gingivalis on modulation of immuno-inflammatory response in human oral keratinocytes (HOKs) and monocytes (THP-1) were investigated using the established bacteria-HOKs/THP-1 interactive models. Considering P. gingivalis as a keystone periodontopathogen, this project has extended to identify new approaches/drugs against this noxious pathogen and related oral biofilms. Based upon our preliminary work, appropriate adjustment of the scope and methodology has been made within the framework of the project. This enables us to timely address the research questions and maximize the outputs with the limited budget. As such, a series of experiments were undertaken, and the following findings were made: 1) Establishment of defined bacteria-HOKs/THP-1 interactive models in vitro, through assessment of essential factors including oxygen levels, antibiotic effects, time duration and the appropriate multiplicity of infection (MOI) [Manuscript I, submitted to J Periodont Res]. Alternatively, the effects of bacterial lysates (e.g. P. gingivalis lysates) on immuno-inflammatory responses in HOKs and THP-1 were tested as well. 2) Hemin- and growth temperature-dependent phenotypes of P. gingivalis enabled to affect their interactions with both HOKs and THP-1 monocytes and the resultant immuno-inflammatory responses. Herein, we provided the first evidence that the P. gingivalis phenotypes grown under increased hemin levels (1 µg/ml vs 10 µg/ml) or growth temperature (37°C vs 41°C) may downregulate the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (e.g. IL-1β, IL-8 and TNF-α) and TLR-4. Both PCR array and cytokine array further indicated that P. gingivalis lysates cultured under high hemin (10 µg/ml hemin) and/or high temperature (41°C) conditions exhibited decreased expression or secretion of the cytokines and MMPs (e.g. IL-1β, IL-8, MMP-9, Osteopontin and PDGF). These findings well indicate that the noxious phenotype of P. gingivalis at the subgingival niches under an inflamed condition enables to suppress innate host response and facilitate its survival for disease progression [Manuscript in preparation]. Therefore, targeting this pathogen may be one of the new therapeutic approaches worthy for further investigation. 3) Periodontal commensals and pathogens differentially modulated immuno-inflammatory response in HOKs, implying that the complex innate response of HOKs to commensal and pathogenic bacteria may not be necessarily determined by the commonly classified categories of “commensal” and “pathogenic” species [Manuscript I, submitted to J Periodont Res]. In addition, periodontal commensals (e.g. S. mitis and S. sanguinis) induced notable expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines in THP-1 monocytes, through TLR2 and TLR4 pathways. Whereas, THP-1 cells fail to mount significant innate host response to major periodontal pathogens like P. gingivalis. Moreover, the interaction of HOKs with P. gingivalis exhibits significantly less chemotactic effects on THP-1 monocytes as compared with those challenged by periodontal commensals (e.g. S. sanguinis). These findings suggest that P. gingivalis may develop underlying mechanisms to evade innate immune surveillance and thereby contribute to periodontal pathogenesis. 4) P. gingivalis grown under different temperatures interacts differentially with THP-1 monocytes. These monocytes were able to mount a strong immuno-inflammatory response to P. gingivalis prior grown at 37°C, while P. gingivalis prior grown at a higher temperature weakened the host response in these cells. The observation suggests that P. gingivalis could modulate immuno-inflammatory response in different periodontal conditions under which temperature could be niche- or site-specific in connection to various bacteria-host crosstalk [Manuscript in preparation]. As such, P. gingivalis may evade host defense under an inflammatory condition with elevated temperature, and thereby contribute to the initiation and development of periodontal disease. Taken together, our findings well reflect the emerging scientific notion that host environmental factors like existing inflammation crucially account for the shift of microbial symbiosis to dysbiosis, such as the altered phenotypes of P. gingivalis in periodontitis. It is therefore essential to proactively promote effective control of periodontal inflammation and risk factors like tobacco smoking for optimal oral/periodontal and general health [Papers III-V]. Several publications have been made for highlighting this important issue. 5) We have recently identified the profiles of P. gingivalis persisters and explored their survival mechanisms, indicating that P. gingivalis persisters as specific phenotypes may represent an undefined mechanism underlying persistent periodontal infection and inflammation [Manuscript II, submitted to Frontiers in Microbiology]. 6) Bismuth drugs (e.g. Ranitidine) enable to disrupt the cellular structures of P. gingivalis and its iron acquisition, affect its virulent attributes and perturb extensive gene transcription and protein expression. Such suppressive effects of the drugs were also validated on the internalized P. gingivalis within host cells. This novel finding suggests that the commonly used anti-H. pylori bismuth drugs could effectively suppress P. gingivalis and may potentially serve as new antimicrobial agents for effective treatment of chronic periodontitis [Manuscript III to be submitted shortly to Nature Microbiology]. In addition, the nickel ‘microcosmos’ in microorganisms has recently been intensively reviewed [Paper VI]. Further investigations on the nickel homeostasis systems of bacteria including P. gingivalis and potential crosstalks of mental homeostasis among microbes/biofilms and during bacteria-host interactions are highly warranted. Novel antimicrobial agents targeting nickel enzymes may be possibly developed for tackling persistent infection and inflammation like human periodontitis. #The reasons for under-achievements and outline attempts to overcome problems: Based upon the preliminary experiments of the study and current research focus on microbe-host symbiosis/dysbiosis, the present research scope and approaches have been adjusted as appropriate within the overall framework of the project and limited budget. The series research work undertaken were summarized as above, and this final report addresses the main findings and research outputs. As concerned above, the experimental work on the effects of hemin- and growth temperature-dependent phenotypes of P. gingivalis on the epigenetic status of HOKs/THP-1 cells and relevant signaling pathways were to some extent delayed, and will be under investigation shortly, and the results would be presented internationally and submitted for publication.

The factors for establishing the working models, e.g. oxygen levels, antibiotic effects, time duration and the appropriate multiplicity of infection (MOI), were assessed appropriately. It showed that an MOI of 1 was appropriate for subsequent experiments of bacteria-host cell interactions with substantial amounts of viable bacterial cells and HOKs in an antibiotic-free medium under aerobic conditions. [PhD Thesis by HJ Li] 2) Hemin- and temperature-dependent phenotypes of P. gingivalis affected their interactions with HOKs/THP-1 monocytes and resultant immuno-inflammatory response as well as TLR-signaling. These findings suggest that P. gingivalis phenotypes grown under rich hemin levels or increased growth temperature, likely reflecting the inflamed conditions of chronic periodontitis clinically, may downregulate the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines and TLR-4 signaling. The study highlights that the ‘disease-associated’ phenotype of P. gingivalis enables to suppress innate host response and thereby facilitate its survival for disease onset and development. 768713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
768713.value: It is evident that the keystone periodontopathogen P. gingivalis contributes to the shift of microbe-host symbiosis to dysbiosis and tissue destruction (Hajishengallis et al 2011, Cell Host Microbe 10:497-506; Hajishengallis et al 2012, Nat Rev Microbiol 10:717-725; Maekawa et al 2014, Cell Host Microbe 15:768-778). Based upon our work, there are two potential areas worthy for further investigations: 1) Our findings on the microenvironment-dependent phenotypes of P. gingivalis affecting innate host response strongly encourage further study on identifying the relevant biomarkers of monitoring host/environment conditions and microbial profiles for biologically defining healthy status and effective oral/periodontal healthcare. 2) Our findings on bismuth drugs (e.g. Ranitidine) as potential new antimicrobials directly targeting the ‘disease-associated’ phenotype of P. gingivalis essentially require further basic and clinical studies on fully understanding the underlying mechanisms, and setting up appropriate protocols/regimes for randomized clinical trials. We will further investigate the P. gingivalis phenotypic persisters under different micro-environmental conditions, their effects on innate immunity and how they could be tackled using our newly developed nanoparticle-encapsulated antimicrobial agents [Paper VII]. New proposal(s) will be submitted for seeking research funds to undertake in vitro and in vivo studies, through our multidisciplinary teamwork.

768713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
768713.value: Severe gum disease (periodontitis) as the main cause of tooth loss in adults worldwide badly affects oral health, yet closely links with systemic diseases like diabetes and heart diseases. Gum disease is initiated by pathogenic microbes (P. gingivalis as a key bacterial pathogen) and dysregulated immuno-inflammatory response. Oral/gingival epithelial cells interact with the complex microbes and play a critical role in gum health. This project investigated how host environmental condition-dependent phenotypes of P. gingivalis affect immuno-inflammatory response in human oral keratinocytes and monocytes, through our established bacteria-host interactive models. This project has also extended to identify new drugs against P. gingivalis. This study shows that P. gingivalis phenotypes grown under inflammation-like conditions with high hemin levels and growth temperature can weaken host defense system and contribute to disease onset and progression. Therefore, it is of great importance to effectively control gum inflammation and common risk factors like tobacco smoking for oral/gum health and general health. The study also indicates that the bismuth drugs like Ranitidine (commonly used against H. pylori bacterium involved in stomach diseases) could effectively suppress P. gingivalis, suggesting that these drugs may potentially serve as new antimicrobial agents for treatment of periodontitis patients in the near future.

768913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
768913.value: Patterns of dispersal and degree of genetic divergence can vary between populations of a species, and this variation is thought to be driven by habitat differences such as availability of resources, predation pressure, and sometimes level of habitat isolation or anthropogenic pressures and human-induced barriers. In cetaceans, intra-specific variation in dispersal and genetic structure may also reflect their complex social structures and varying patterns of group formation. Identifying and understanding the mechanisms driving genetic differentiation of free-ranging populations is critical to the understanding and maintaining biodiversity and it remains a central challenge in population ecology and conservation biology. In this project, equipped with powerful techniques in molecular genetics and mark-recapture models, we investigate population structure, connectivity, patterns of dispersal and barriers to gene flow in a shallow-water dolphin species, the Indo-Pacific humpback dolphin in the coastal systems of the China-Taiwan region. Throughout its range, humpback dolphins associate with shallow-water coastal habitats, which in many parts of the world are increasingly degraded by over-harvesting and habitat destruction. This renders humpback dolphins particularly susceptible to adverse environmental pressures; in China, the remaining populations range in numbers from few tens to few hundreds, with apparently the only notable exception of the Pearl River population. Our recent findings, however, might share a new perspective into this frequently cited notion. The project proposed here builds-up on several years of previous research by researchers in mainland China and Taiwan and the PI's own work in the Pearl River delta; all currently known locations in China, Hong Kong and Taiwan with confirmed presence of humpback dolphins will be surveyed with a suite of modern research techniques and sophisticated analytical treatment to quantify the pattern of population connectivity, determine patterns of dispersal and estimate the rate of gene flow across this large geographic area. Consequently, we will construct a model of stock structure of humpback dolphins in China-Taiwan, and by doing so we will identify management units for conservation. Our work will be instrumental in identifying local population structures, assessing the severity of impacts and proposing management measures; as such it will contribute to a high-profile conservation issue of major international significance. In the region where humpback dolphins are increasingly seen as an icon of marine biodiversity conservation with a symbolic value approaching that of giant panda, the type of work as described in this proposal is much needed, long overdue, and can provide a significant lasting contribution. 單一品種的不同族群之分佈格局和遺傳分歧程度可能不盡相同，而該差異被認為是由棲息地的差別所引致，例如資源可得性、捕食壓力、棲息地分隔、人為的壓力和分隔因素。在鯨豚動物中，同一品種內的基因分佈結構差異亦能反映其複雜的社會結構及群組構成的模式。因此認知在自由放養族群中的遺傳分化推動機制，對於了解和維持生物多樣性非常關鍵；不過該範疇在群體生態學及保育生態學始終是一大難題。 本研究計劃運用分子遺傳學和標誌重捕模型的技術，從而研究在中國台灣兩地沿岸生態系統的印度太平洋駝背海豚的族群結構、連通性、分佈格局及基因流動之阻隔因素。印度太平洋駝背海豚棲息於沿岸淺水區域；在其分佈範圍內，很多沿岸棲息地正有增無減地被資源過度採收和生境破壞所影響。這導致駝背海豚對於不利環境壓力的影響特別敏感。在中國範圍僅存的族群中，族群數量由幾十至幾百不等，只有在珠江的族群除外。不過本實驗室近期發現這一常被引用的說法可能有需要改變觀點。 本研究計劃建基於中國大陸、台灣兩地研究員以往多年的研究項目，以及本計劃項目負責人在珠江三角洲的研究。一系列嶄新的研究技術和精密的分析將用於考察在中國、香港、台灣所有已知有駝背海豚出沒的地方，以量化該廣闊地區中之族群連通性的模式、了解其分佈格局、及估算其基因流動率；最終將建立一駝背海豚的系群結構模型，從而鑒別應有的保育管理單位。本研究計劃將對了解本地族群結構、評估環境影響的嚴重程度、及建議有關保育管理措施起關鍵的作用，並藉此對該國際重視的保育議題作出貢獻。特別對於駝背海豚作為保育海洋生物多樣性標誌的地區，其象徵性已可比大熊貓；本計畫所描述的工作內容正是該地區長期欠缺而且急需的，並將為該地區提供有效而長遠的貢獻和影響。

769313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
769313.value: 二羥基丙酮（DHA）激酶是一個序列保守的蛋白質家族，它能夠催化Dha到磷酸Dha的轉化反應。該反應有兩種磷酸供體：在高等真核細胞和某一些特定的細菌中，該反應的磷酸供體是三磷酸腺苷（ATP），在其他細菌中則是磷酸烯醇丙酮酸（PEP​​）。 PEP依賴的Dha激酶是一個由三個不同亞基組成的蛋白質複合物，而ATP依賴的Dha激酶是一個含兩個結構域的多肽鏈。 在細菌代謝中，Dha激酶涉及甘油代謝和甲醇同化的通路，但是在高等真核細胞中，Dha激酶的功能尚不清楚。由於Dha激酶的缺乏會導致寄生蟲布氏錐蟲（Trypanosoma brucei）的死亡，因此可以推測，Dha激酶的功能之一可能是清除Dha以消除其細胞毒性。研究已經證實，除了激酶活性以外，ATP依賴的Dha激酶還有另外一種催化活性：催化環狀黃素單核苷酸（FMN）形成黃素腺嘌呤二核苷酸（FAD）。並且，人源的Dha激酶已被確認是天然免疫反應蛋白MDA－５的唯一負調控子。為了更好地理解人源Dha激酶的功能，本提案旨在揭開人源Dha激酶所催化的這兩個反應的分子細​​節。此外，我們還希望探索人源Dha激酶與天然免疫反應蛋白MDA－５的相互作用模式。

770213.label: Realisation of objectives
770213.value: Objective 1 was studied at two aspects. First, the expression of specific miRNAs in pDCs from lupus and control mice was examined. Initial evaluation of let-7a, miR-17 and miR-20a expressions in 3 to 6 independent sets of experiments revealed no significant difference in TLR-7 stimulated expression between control and SLE pDCs. We then refined our TLR7 stimulation condition and repeated the miRNA low density array experiments, which showed that miR-155 had the highest differential expression between the control and SLE pDCs. Validation by 5 independent sets of experiments further indicated significant up-regulation of miR-155 in the SLE pDCs. Thus the effects of miR-155 were studied instead. Objective 1 was studied at two aspects. First, the expression of specific miRNAs in pDCs from lupus and control mice was examined. Initial evaluation of let-7a, miR-17 and miR-20a expressions in 3 to 6 independent sets of experiments revealed no significant difference in TLR-7 stimulated expression between control and SLE pDCs. We then refined our TLR7 stimulation condition and repeated the miRNA low density array experiments, which showed that miR-155 had the highest differential expression between the control and SLE pDCs. Validation by 5 independent sets of experiments further indicated significant up-regulation of miR-155 in the SLE pDCs. Thus the effects of miR-155 were studied instead. Second, the association of miR-155 overexpression in lupus pDCs with phenotypic and functional abnormalities was evaluated. A panel of ten activation markers including costimulatory molecules and TLR-related targets were studied. Among the tested markers, the expression of costimulatory molecules CD40, CD86 and the antigen presentation molecules MHC-II in lupus/symptomatic pDCs were found significantly elevated upon TLR7 activation (R837 stimulation) when compared with control/pre-symptomatic pDCs. Next, TLR7-mediated functional abnormalities in lupus pDCs were also examined. A panel of functional molecular targets including four cytokines and three interferon sensitive genes (ISGs) expression were also examined at basal levels as well as upon TLR7 stimulation at different stimulation settings. Except Ifitm3, there were no significant induction of these cytokines and ISGs between these two groups of pDCs with differential miR-155 expression. Pertaining to objective 1, we successfully identified miR-155 as the dysregulated microRNA that could mediate the abnormal TLR7-mediated pDC responses, as measured as elevated CD40, CD88, MHC-II and Ifitm3 expression, in lupus mice. Since miR-155 was identified in lieu of let-7a, miR-17 and miR-20a as stated in the original proposal, we therefore studied the regulatory mechanisms mediated by miR-155 in the second objective. For objective 2, we first modulated miR-155 expression and evaluated its impact on the changes in a number of potential targets in response to TLR7 stimulation. A panel of 7 targets were screened, including 6 cytokines and 2 ISGs, but no significant changes were observed upon miR155 overexpression. Next, we focused on the identified targets with dysregulated functional changes in lupus pDCs as found in objective 1. Encouraging results indicated that the overexpression of miR-55 can mediate upregulated expression of CD40 and Ifitm3 when compared with controls. Finally, we studied several known direct molecular targets (including Tab2, SOCS1 and SHIP1) by which miR-155 may act upon to mediate functional changes in CD40 expression. Tab2 and SOCS1 have been previously reported as miR-155 direct target in human leukocytes. However, in mouse pDCs, their expression were not affected by miR-155 over-expression in our study. On the other hand, miR-155 modulated the expression of Ship1 in a negative correlation manner with Cd40 expression. In conclusion, we successfully delineated a possible mechanism by which miR-155 could contribute to the functional abnormalities in SLE pDCs.

770213.label: Major findings and research outcome
770213.value: In summary, this study sought for potential microRNAs that might be involved in bone marrow (BM)-derived plasmacytoid dendritic cell (pDC) functional abnormalities in systemic lupus erythematosus and major findings include the following: 1) pDCs derived from BM precursors of lupus mice, despite being phenotypically unremarkable, were hypersensitive to TLR7 stimulation with enhanced upregulation of MHC class II and other costimulatory molecules including CD40 and CD86; 2) by microRNA profiling of purified pDCs, we revealed an elevated induction of miR-155 in lupus pDCs upon TLR7 activation; 3) overexpression of miR-155 in pDCs led to consistently increased expression of Cd40, indicating possible miR-155-mediated augmented CD40 expression in lupus pDCs; 4) overexpression of miR-155 also led to a downregulation of Ship1, whose expression was found negatively correlated with Cd40 expression. These findings suggest that miR-155 may target the negative immune-regulator Ship1 directly and mediate the enhanced CD40 expression in lupus pDCs. These findings were published in a research article titled “MicroRNA-155 mediates augmented CD40 expression in bone marrow derived plasmacytoid dendritic cells in systemic lupus erythematosus” in International Journal of Molecular Sciences 2016 (see research output)

770213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
770213.value: This study has revealed miR-155 as an epigenetic regulator that contributes to the functional abnormalities in plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs). Dendritic cells (DCs) constitute an important cell type that orchestrates adaptive immune responses and plays critical roles in SLE pathogenesis. To further substantiate its regulatory role in DC function, its impact on another important subset, namely myeloid DCs (mDCs) should also be explored first. Along with pDCs, abnormalities in mDCs of SLE patients were reported by our group previously. In the NZBW F1 lupus mouse model, we also observed functional abnormalities in mDCs which were shown to contribute to the development of follicular T helper cells for the induction of autoimmune responses (part of this work was carried out by a PhD student trained under this project). Thus, we plan to examine the role of miR-155 in mediating lupic mDC abnormalities using the established microRNA analysis platform. Together, these studies could set the scientific basis for exploiting miR-155 as a target for therapeutic immunomodulation in SLE.

770213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
770213.value: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a multi-organ autoimmune disorder that affects young women. We and others have previously shown that dendritic cells (DCs), particularly plasmacytoid DCs (pDCs), play a pivotal role in SLE development. SLE peripheral blood and bone marrow derived pDCs exhibit activated phenotypes and display a higher cell stimulating capacity than heathy controls. The underlying regulatory factor that mediates such aberration in lupus remains unclear. In this study, we used a lupus mouse model and identified an augmented expression of miR-155, a microRNA, in pDCs. MicroRNA is a gene expression regulatory mechanism that affects almost all biological processes. Particularly, many immune functions can be modulated by microRNAs. Here, we further found that the elevated miR-155 expression could contribute to the heightened phenotypic and functional aberrations in pDCs. By manipulating miR-155 levels in our experimental platform, the expression of various immune activities markers (e.g. CD40 and Ifitm3) were modulated accordingly in pDCs. As such, these results suggest that miR-155 may potentially serve as a target for immunomodulation. Overall, our findings provide additional information to the current understanding of lupus immunopathogenesis and should ignite further interests, ideas and efforts in exploration of therapeutic targets for SLE.

770313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
770313.value: X-linked agammaglobulinemia (XLA) is characterized by impaired antibody response resulting from Bruton’s tyrosine kinase (BTK) mutation. Recurrent encapsulated bacterial infections are the hallmark of XLA. Unlike other humoral immune deficiency with no predisposition to extraordinary risk of viral infection, XLA renders a unique susceptibility to infection of enteroviruses including poliovirus, whereas other viruses such as influenza virus are seldom reported. Oral polio vaccine (OPV) can induce paralytic poliomyelitis in XLA patients. Of great public concern is that the attenuated OPV can persist and revert to a virulent form in these patients, which renders a high risk of reintroducing virulent poliovirus into general population. It has been demonstrated that toll-like receptor 3 (TLR3)-mediated type I IFN responses play critical roles in host protection against poliovirus infection. BTK is involved in TLR3 signaling pathway by directly phosphorylating TLR3. But TLR3 is not necessary for anti-influenza virus response. Therefore, we hypothesize that BTK mutations in XLA impair TLR3-mediated type I IFN response, leading to the unique susceptibility of poliovirus infection in XLA patients. Preliminarily we have shown that XLA immune cells have impaired TLR3 response to poly (I:C) stimulation. We also have demonstrated normal cytokine response of XLA immune cells upon influenza virus stimulation, indicating TLR3 is not critical for anti-influenza response. These data provide preliminary evidence to support our hypothesis. In this project, we propose to directly use the primary immune cells of XLA patients to test our hypothesis. Importantly, we will confirm our hypothesis from different angles. First, we will investigate the TLR3-mediated IFN response against poliovirus and virus clearance in XLA patient cells. Then the underlying BTK-TLR3-IFN signaling pathway will be examined. Finally we will adoptively transfer wild-type BTK gene into XLA immune cells to demonstrate the restoration of TLR3-mediated IFN response and anti-poliovirus activity. Our Asian Primary Immunodeficiency Network facilitates and guarantees the smooth implementation of this study. The completion of this project will substantially enhance our understanding of the immunopathogenesis of poliovirus infection in XLA. The resulting knowledge will also provide potential targets for developing appropriate measures to treat OPV associated polio and prevent its spread. It will undoubtedly facilitate the end-game of global polio eradication. X連鎖無丙種球蛋白血症（X-linked agammaglobulinemia, XLA）由Bruton酪氨酸激酶（Bruton's tyrosine kinase, BTK）突變所致，導致抗體反應低下，其顯著特徵是反复莢膜類細菌感染。體液免疫缺陷對病毒感染無特別的易感性，但XLA對包括脊髓灰質炎病毒在內的腸道類病毒特別易感，其他病毒如流感病毒感染卻鮮有報導。口服脊髓灰質炎疫苗（Oral polio vaccine, OPV）可導致XLA病人發生麻痺性脊髓灰質炎，備受公眾關注的是，減活OPV可在此類病人中持續存在，幷轉變為毒力株，使其普通人群中引入毒性脊髓灰質炎病毒的危險性大大增加。 Toll樣受體3（Toll-like receptor 3, TLR3）介導的I型乾擾素在機體抵抗脊髓灰質炎病毒感染中發揮著關鍵作用。 BTK通過直接磷酸化TLR3參與其信號傳導。但TLR3在抗流感反應中非必需。因此，我們假設XLA中BTK突變抑制TLR3介導的I型乾擾素反應，從而導致此類病人對脊髓灰質炎病毒感染的特殊易感性。我們初步證實，XLA患者的免疫細胞對PolyIC刺激的TLR3應答降低，但當流感病毒刺激時，此類免疫細胞產生了正常的炎症反應。這些結果表明TLR3對抗流感應答並不重要，同時也提供了初步證據以支持我們的假設。 在此項目中，我們將直接使用XLA患者的原代免疫細胞來驗證我們的假設。重要的是，我們將從不同的角度去證實此假設。首先，我們將研究XLA病人免疫細胞抵抗脊髓灰質炎病毒的TLR3介導的I型乾擾素反應和病毒清除能力；然後檢測BTK-TLR3-IFN信號通路的潛在缺陷。最後，我們將在XLA患者免疫細胞中導入正常BTK基因，幷檢測TLR3介導的干擾素應答及抗脊髓灰質炎病毒活性是否得以恢復。我們的亞洲原發性免疫缺陷網絡將保證此項研究得以順利實施。 該項目的完成將顯著提高我們對XLA患者感染脊髓灰質炎病毒免疫致病機理的認識，所取得的研究結果也將為治療OPV相關脊髓灰質炎及防止其傳播提供潛在的靶標，這無疑將有助於全球最終根除脊髓灰質炎。

770313.label: Realisation of objectives
770313.value: 1. Using primary immune cells of XLA patients to study impaired BTK-TLR3-IFN response to poliovirus infections. We collected primary immune cells from 9 XLA patients and 23 Hong Kong Red Cross blood donors to investigate impaired BTK-TLR3-IFN response to poliovirus infections. We successfully differentiated monocyte-derived dendritic cells (DCs) from the monocytes isolated from peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) of XLA patients and blood donors. We successfully cultured DCs with oral poliovirus vaccine (OPV) and H1N1 influenza to study their type I IFN responses. 2. To investigate the type I IFN response against poliovirus and virus clearance in XLA patient We have successfully demonstrated type I IFN response against OPV in DCs of XLA patients was reduced compared to that in healthy donors. In addition, we also demonstrated type III IFN response against OPV in DCs of XLA patients was reduced compared to that in healthy donors. 3. To clarify the BTK-TLR3-IFN signaling pathway in response to poliovirus stimulation in XLA patient We were able to demonstrate functional BTK is critical in mounting type I and III IFN response towards OPV stimulation by reproducing type I and III IFN production impairment in DCs of healthy donors by inhibiting the BTK via LFM-A13. We were unable to demonstrate the impaired TLR3 phosphorylation in response to OPV stimulation due to lack of specific antibodies towards phosphorylated TLR3 during Western blot (please refer to previous mid-term progress report for detail). Based on our findings and literatures, loss of BTK function in XLA patients results in impaired TLR signaling, which is the dominant pathway over MDA5 (a type of RIG-I like receptor) to coordinate IFN production in response to OPV stimulation. On the other hand, either TLR or RIG-I is sufficient to mount IFN production against H1N1. 4. Rescue of BTK-TLR3-IFN signaling and anti-poliovirus response by adoptively transferring wild-type BTK gene We were unable to rescue the signaling pathway in DCs of XLA patients due to limited DCs we collected from XLA patients. Instead we selectively inhibited the BTK in DCs of healthy donors by LFM-A13 to reproduce the impairments seen in DCs of XLA patients.

770313.label: Major findings and research outcome
770313.value: 6.1 Major findings and research outcome (maximum 1 page; please make reference to Part C where necessary) The findings were submitted in manuscript titled ‘Type I and III Interferon Production is Impaired in X-linked Agammaglobulinemia Patients Towards Poliovirus but not Influenza Virus.’ to Frontier Immunology Journal, currently submission in progress. 1. DCs of XLA patients had selective type I IFN, type III IFN and IP-10 production impairment towards OPV but not H1N1 stimulation. Type I IFN, type III IFN and IP-10 production was lower in DCs of XLA patients compared to that in healthy donors upon culturing with OPV. However upon culturing with H1N1, these cytokines production was similar between DCs of XLA patients and healthy donors. 2. Selective type I and III IFN production deficiency towards OPV but not H1N1 stimulation in DCs of XLA patients was due to lack of BTK function. Type I and III IFN production was lower in BTK inhibited DCs of healthy donors compared to that in healthy donors upon culturing with OPV. However similar to DCs of XLA patients, there was no difference in the type I and III IFN production between BTK inhibited DCs and DCs of healthy donors upon culturing with H1N1. 3. Phenotypic maturation of DCs of XLA patients was impaired upon culturing with OPV but not H1N1. Upon culturing with OPV, the mean fluorescent intensities (MFI) of CD83, CD86 and MHC-II in DCs from XLA patients was similar to that upon mock stimulation, while upon culturing with H1N1, the MFI of CD83, CD86 and MHC-II were significantly higher than that upon mock stimulation. This indicated selective impaired phenotypic maturation of DCs of XLA patients upon culturing with OPV but not H1N1. The MFI of CD83, CD86 and MHC-II in DCs of healthy controls were significantly higher in response to both OPV and H1N1 stimulation compared to that in response to mock stimulation.

770313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
770313.value: With the use of oral poliovirus vaccine (OPV), global eradication of poliovirus is almost achieved. However for patients with X-linked agammaglobulinemia (XLA), they are prone to suffer complications such as paralysis after taking OPV. The OPV are prone to mutate back to the deadly form in these patients who become chronic excretors and transmit these mutant OPV in the population. To this date we still do not know why these patients are vulnerable to develop complications from OPV but not to other viruses. In our study, we discovered XLA patients produced less type I and III interferon (IFN) in response to OPV, but produced adequate IFNs in response to influenza virus. We established this IFNs production problem was due to the loss of Bruton’s tyrosine kinase (BTK) function, which is the underlying cause for the disease XLA. In addition, we found the immune cells matured poorly in response to OPV but not to influenza virus. These findings suggest that reduced type I and III IFN production in XLA patients may explain why they are selectively vulnerable to have complications from OPV. Based on our findings, we may investigate the use of IFNs to help these patients to facilitate global eradication of polio.

770813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
770813.value: 胚胎與女性生殖道之間的相互作用對受精、胚胎發育及著床有重要影響。女性生殖道（如輸卵管、子宮）為胚胎運輸及發育提供了適宜的微環境，而植入前胚胎也可分泌多種因子（如人絨毛膜促性腺激素，白血病抑制因子，蛋白酶等）調節輸卵管及子宮腔上皮的分泌活動，以此促進胚胎發育與著床。齧齒類動物的輸卵管可選擇處於適宜發育階段的胚胎并將之運送至子宮腔。然而，胚胎著床只能發生於一個被稱為“植入窗”的特定時間段，人類胚胎的“植入窗”通常為女性月經週期內黃體生成素高峰日后的5至9天。“植入窗”以外著床的胚胎往往表現出較低的繼續妊娠率及活產率，說明胚胎和子宮內膜的同步發育對胚胎著床和維持妊娠至關重要。 微小核糖核酸是一類短小的（長度僅為19-22個核苷酸）非蛋白編碼核糖核酸，它們可直接與靶信使核糖核酸的3’端非編碼區配對，導致其降解或抑制其蛋白翻譯，從而調節靶基因的表達。我們及其他學者的研究均表明，人絨毛膜促性腺激素可促進子宮內膜細胞、卵泡顆粒細胞及垂體促性腺細胞中微小核糖核酸-132/-212的生成。硅片微小核糖核酸靶標預測結果顯示嗅球蛋白-1可能受微小核糖核酸-132/-212的調節。嗅球蛋白-1在容受性高的子宮內膜組織中表達下降；在胚胎著床的體外模型中，人重組嗅球蛋白-1可抑制滋養細胞球體（人囊胚類似物）與子宮內膜上皮細胞間的粘附作用；而螢光素酶報告基因分析也表明微小核糖核酸-132/-212可調節嗅球蛋白基因轉錄物的3’端非編碼區。綜上所述，我們推定人絨毛膜促性腺激素可調節子宮內膜上皮中微小核糖核酸-132/-212的生成，從而抑制嗅球蛋白-1的表達，以便胚胎粘附及著床。本研究有以下四個目的：（1）探討人絨毛膜促性腺激素通過調節微小核糖核酸-132/-212對子宮內膜上皮嗅球蛋白-1的影響；（2）探索人絨毛膜促性腺激素通過激活其子宮內膜上皮細胞受體對微小核糖核酸-132/-212的調節作用；（3）探索微小核糖核酸-132/-212通過調節嗅球蛋白-1對胚胎粘附的影響；（4）進一步探索胚胎與女性生殖道相互作用過程中人絨毛膜促性腺激素及各種胚胎源性因子對子宮內膜微小核糖核酸的影響。本研究的結論將揭示胚胎與女性生殖道相互作用的重要性，為胚胎源性因子通過調節子宮內膜微小核糖核酸以利胚胎著床提供有力證據。

770813.label: Realisation of objectives
770813.value: (1) To study the action of hCG on endometrial Olfm1 expression through miR-132/-212 regulation (100% completed) - We confirmed the regulatory role of miR-132/-212 on Olfm1 expression in the endometrium by carrying out the following experiments. First, the expression of Olfm1 in the HeLa and Ishikawa cells were confirmed by Western blotting. Transfection of miR-212 precursor miRNA down-regulated Olfm1 and CtBP1 expression; while transfection of miR-212 inhibitor up-regulated Olfm1 and CtBP1 expression in vitro (Kottawattage et al., 2015). The 3’UTR of Olfm1 and CtBP1 were isolated and cloned into psiCHECK vector. Mutated 3’UTR of Olm1 and CtBP1 were also generated. The expression of luciferase reporter was measured with or without miR-212 precursor or inhibitor treatment. It was found that miR-212 precursor down-regulated luciferase expression; while miR-212 inhibitor up-regulated luciferase expression in the transfected HeLa cells. No changes in luciferase expression when the mutated constructs were used (Kottawattage et al., 2015). (2) To investigate the regulation of miR-132/-212 expression by hCG through hCG receptor activation in endometrial cells (100% completed) – We have studied the effect of hCG on the activation of cAMP in endometrial cells and the combined effect of steroid hormones and hCG on the changes in gene expression. However, no detectable change of cAMP was found (unpublished observation). We also studied the role of hormone receptors with or without inhibitors on miR-132/-212 expression in human endometrial cells. The effect of steroid hormones (E2 and P4) on the expression of miR-212 in endometrial Ishikawa and oviductal OE-E6/E7 cells was studied. Estrogen (1-100nM) and Progesterone (0.6-60nM) did not significantly increase miR-212/-132 expression in Ishikawa cells; while hCG stimulates miR-212 but suppresses the expression of Olfm1 transcript in both Ishikawa and OE-E6/E7 cells (Kottawatta et al., 2015; So et al., 2015). However, hCG has no effect on CtBP1 transcript expression in both Ishikawa and OE-E6/E7 cells. In terms of protein expression levels, hCG down-regulated both Olfm1 and CtBP1 expression in Ishikawa and OE-E6/E7 cells (Kottawatta et al., 2015; So et al., 2015). (3) To determine the role of miR-132/-212 in regulating Olfm1 expression on embryo attachment (100% completed) – The effect of hCG on spheroid attachment was investigated. HCG (0.25-25IU/mL) increased JAR spheroid attachment onto oviductal OE-E6/E7 cells (So et al., 2015). Similarly, the attachment rate of Jeg-3 spheroids onto endometrial Ishikawa cells increased significantly at 25IU/mL hCG (Kottawatta et al., 2015). Also, the role of miR-132/-212 on spheroid attachment was studied. HCG (25IU/mL) treated Ishikawa or OE-E6/E7 cells have increased attachment rate when compared to the treated Jeg-3 cells alone (Kottawatta et al., 2015; So et al., 2015). The attachment rate of miR-212 precursor treated Ishikawa cells was significantly higher than the miRNA control which was significantly higher than miR-212 inhibitor treated group (Kottawatta et al., 2015). In the OE-E6/E7 cells, hCG treatment up-regulated the expression of Wnt-signaling molecules (active-b-catenin) and stimulated ERK pathway (So et al., 2015). On the other hand, treatment with Wnt inhibitor (XAV939) up-regulated Olfm1 expression and suppressed JAr spheroid attachment (So et al., 2015). Similarly, treatment with ERK inhibitor (U0126) up-regulated Olfm1 expression but suppressed JAr spheroid attachment (So et al., 2015).

770813.label: Major findings and research outcome
770813.value: In this project, we investigated the role of hCG and steroid hormones (estrogen and progesterone) on the regulation of Olfactomedin-1 and Ctbp1 expression through miR-132/-212 regulation. We firstly used endometrial (Ishikawa) and fallopian tube (OE-E6/E7) epithelial cell lines to serve as model to study the regulation of genes in the eutopic and ectopic site of implantation. The following objectives were studied and completed. (1) To study the action of hCG on endometrial Olfm1 expression through miR-132/-212 regulation, (2) To investigate the regulation of miR-132/-212 expression by hCG through hCG receptor activation in endometrial cells, and (3) To determine the role of miR-132/-212 in regulating Olfm1 expression on embryo attachment. We confirmed the regulatory role of miR-132/-212 on Olfm1 and CtBP1 expressions in vitro (Kottawattage et al., 2015). We also studied the role of hormone receptors with or without inhibitors on miR-132/-212 expression in human endometrial cells and oviductal OE-E6/E7 cells. Estrogen (1-100nM) and Progesterone (0.6-60nM) did not significantly increase miR-212/-132 expression in Ishikawa cells; while hCG stimulates miR-212 but suppresses the expression of Olfm1 transcript in both Ishikawa and OE-E6/E7 cells (Kottawatta et al., 2015; So et al., 2015). Finally, the effect of hCG on spheroid attachment was investigated. HCG (25IU/mL) treated Ishikawa or OE-E6/E7 cells have increased attachment rate when compared to the treated Jeg-3 cells alone (Kottawatta et al., 2015; So et al., 2015). The attachment rate of miR-212 precursor treated Ishikawa cells was significantly higher than the miRNA control which was significantly higher than miR-212 inhibitor treated group (Kottawatta et al., 2015). In the OE-E6/E7 cells, hCG treatment up-regulated the expression of Wnt-signaling molecules (active--catenin) and stimulated ERK pathway (So et al., 2015). On the other hand, treatment with Wnt inhibitor (XAV939) up-regulated Olfm1 expression and suppressed JAr spheroid attachment (So et al., 2015). Similarly, treatment with ERK inhibitor (U0126) up-regulated Olfm1 expression but suppressed JAr spheroid attachment (So et al., 2015). In summary, we established the regulation of Olfm1 and Ctbp1 expression through hCG and steroid hormones via miR-212 expression. hCG secreted from pre-implantation embryo, seems to be a key molecule in regulating various signaling pathways (e.g. Wnt-signaling) through Olfm1 expression on implantation. In terms of research output, two papers were published in the field of Reproductive Biology: Fertility & Sterility and Biology of Reproduction, in which one figure was used as cover photo in Nov issue of Biol Reprod. Six conference abstracts were accepted for poster presentation in local and international conference. Two PhD students were trained and they were graduated in time.

770813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
770813.value: In this research study, we have established co-culture model to study eutopic and ectopic pregnancy using OE-E6/E7 and Ishikawa cells for spheroid attachment, respectively. We also established transfection assay to study miRNA regulation on the 3’-UTR of Olfm-1 and Ctbp-1 transcripts. However, it is likely other miRNA could be involved in this regulatory process and warrant further investigation. Similarly, hCG and steroid hormones also play important role on the expression of endometrial receptivity proteins/markers (e.g. E-cadherin, integrins and Hoxa10). Whether miRNA play a role in fine tune the expression of these proteins is not clear. Our data suggested that changes in Wnt-signaling pathway and protein kinase pathway could affect implantation process in vivo. Tissue-specific knock-out of these genes in the uterus could help to delineate the molecular mechanism of implantation failure using the mouse model.

770813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
770813.value: In this project, we investigated the role of hCG (a molecule secreted from the embryo before implantation) and steroid hormones (estrogen and progesterone) on regulation of the expression of proteins (Olfm-1 and Ctbp-1) on the lining of the womb through microRNA-132/-212. We used cell lines of the lining of the womb and Fallopian tube as models to study the regulation of genes in the different tissues. We confirmed the regulatory role of miRNA-132/-212 on Olfm-1 and Ctbp-1 expressions in the cells. Although, estrogen (1-100nM) and progesterone (0.6-60nM) did not increase miR-212/-132 expression in the lining of the womb, hCG stimulated miR-212 but suppressed Olfm1 transcript expression in both lining of the womb and the tube. Interestingly, hCG (25IU/mL) treated cells from lining of the womb and the tube have increased attachment rate when compared to the treated Jeg-3 cells alone, and this process is mediated through miR-212 regulation. In the cells from the tube, hCG treatment up-regulated the expression of Wnt-signaling molecules (active-b-catenin) and stimulated ERK pathway. In summary, we established the regulation of Olfm1 and Ctbp1 expression through hCG and steroid hormones via miR-212 expression.

771213.label: Realisation of objectives
771213.value: In this proposal, we have investigated the clinopathological relevance and prognostic significance of CD47 expression in human HCC, and elucidate the molecular mechanism by which CD47 functionally contributes to the tumor initiation, self-renewal, invasiveness and chemoresistance. Lastly, we have examined the effect of CD47 knockdown and anti-CD47 antibody alone or in combination with sorafenib for treatment of HCC both in vitro and in vivo. Specifically, we report the following data: 1) The percentage of CD47+ cells in the xenografts/HCC specimens ranged from 3.93% to 98.5%. Patients with high CD47 expression had significant shorter overall and disease survival rates than those with low CD47 expression (p=0.009 and P=0.007, respectively, log rank test). 2) CD47 was found to be upregulated in enriched liver CSC populations (CD24+/CD133+) when compared with their negative counterparts. 3) Knockdown of CD47 reduced the stem/progenitor characteristics of HCC cells including tumorigenicity, self-renewal, metastasis and chemoresistance. 4) CD47 drove tumor initiation, self-renewal, chemoresistance and invasiveness through up-regulation of cathepsin S (CTSS). Clinically, CD47 expression was correlated with CTSS expression in a cohort of 26 HCC patient samples (p<0.001, R2=3.93, Pearson’s correlation. 5) CD47regulated CTSS expression through NF-KB activation. 6) CD47 regulated liver CSCs through autocrine secretion of CTSS mediated PAR2 activation 7) Serum CTSS was detected in clinical HCC samples, and found a stepwise increase in the serum level of CTSS in HCC progression from healthy subjects, via early HCC to advanced HCC. 8) In vivo mouse xenograft model, suppression of CD47 by morpholino suppressed the growth of HCC and sensitized the effect to doxorubicin treatment. 9) In vivo mouse PDTX xenograft model, anti-CD47 antibody suppressed the growth of HCC and sensitized the effect to doxorubicin treatment. 10) Suppression of CD47 by lentiviral based knockdown approach and anti-CD47 antibody induced macrophage-induced phagocytosis. 11) CD47 expression was found to be increased in sorafenib-resistant HCC cells which was endowed with enhanced CSC populations. 12) In vivo mouse PDTX xenograft model, anti-CD47 antibody suppressed the growth of HCC and sensitized the effect to sorafenib treatment. 771213.label: Major findings and research outcome
771213.value: Identification of therapeutic targets against cancer stem cells (CSCs) is a priority in the development of new therapeutic paradigms against cancer. Using an in vitro liver CSC enrichment protocol, CD47 was found to be up-regulated, which contributed to tumor initiation, self-renewal, and metastasis. Clinically, Patients with high CD47 expression had significant shorter overall and disease survival rates than those with low CD47 expression (p=0.009 and P=0.007, respectively, log rank test). Repression of CD47 suppressed stem/progenitor cell characteristics through the CTSS/protease-activated receptor 2 (PAR2) loop. Clinically, serum level of CTSS provides diagnostic and prognostic value to HCC patients. Suppression of CD47 by morpholino approach suppressed growth of HCC in vivo and exerted a chemosensitization effect through blockade of CTSS/PAR2 signaling. Blockade of CD47 with an anti-CD47 monoclonal antibody in vitro as well as in human HCC xenograft models resulted in a significant reduction in tumor growth and synergized the effect of doxorubicin and sorafenib treatments. Furthermore, we found that CD47 knockdown and anti-Cd47 antibody induced macrophage induced phagocytosis. Patent application Combination use of CD47 antibodies/inhibitors with sorafenib for treatment of liver cancer” (US patent US20170071918) (2017) Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO), NCBI Database Deposit / Contribution -GSE47563 and GSE53005) (2014) – pertaining to profiling data described in the paper referenced in this completion report.

771213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
771213.value: Cancer immunotherapy is currently a hot research area in cancer therapy. CD47 is regarded as “don’t eat me” molecule to macrophage, and its blockade by anti-CD47 antibody resulted in macrophage-mediated phagocytosis. Upon phagocytosis, macrophage acts as antigen presenting cells and prime the function of T cells. Based on this hypothesis, we are currently exploring on the role of anti-CD47 antibody in combination of anti-PD1 treatment to observe the possibility of synergistic effect to tumor suppression using syngeneic mouse model. This is a project that continues on the interesting leads identified from the current funded project.

771213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
771213.value: Liver cancer (HCC) is the fifth most common cancer worldwide. The prognosis of this disease is poor due to frequent relapse and drug resistant nature of this disease. Recently, cancer stem cells (CSCs) is regarded as the root of tumor relapse and therapeutic resistance. Thus, targeting these cells may be a novel therapeutic strategy against HCC. In the current proposal, findings presented in this study not only provide evidence to show the clinical relevance of CD47 expression in HCC but also demonstrated its pivotal role in regulation of liver CSCs. Most importantly, we have demonstrated the therapeutic implications of targeting CD47 for HCC treatment. We believe that targeting CD47 may be potentially developed as a novel treatment regime for this disease.
