771513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
771513.value: Spermatogenesis in mammals is a timely process during which developing germ cells in the seminiferous tubules are migrating from the base to the apex of the seminiferous epithelium where fully developed germ cells are released into the lumen for eventual transport to the epididymis. Two important events which govern the success of this developmental passage of germ cells in the seminiferous epithelium are (i) the translocation of germ cells across the blood-testis barrier (BTB) and (ii) the release of germ cells from the seminiferous epithelium into the lumen at spermiation. These two events occur concurrently at the opposite ends of the seminiferous epithelium at stage VIII of the spermatogenic cycle in adult rats. In human, seminiferous epithelium is divided into six stages and the two events occur concurrently at stage II. The PI has recently identified a novel regulatory loop which coordinates these two events and thus regulates the timely process of spermatogenesis. It is hypothesized that at spermiation, release of germ cells from adhesion at the apical epithelium generates specific peptide fragments which travel via an extracellular route to induce BTB restructuring at the junction of the apical and basal epithelium. The present proposal seeks to characterize further this functional axis to understand how the cellular events of (i) BTB restructuring that facilitates the transit of preleptotene/leptotene spermatocytes across the barrier, and (ii) spermiation that allows the depletion of fully developed spermatozoa into the tubule lumen, are coordinated and regulated at the biochemical and molecular level. Coordination of these two events are required to programme spermatogenesis precisely in space and time, such that a good numbers of competent spermatozoa are continuously produced from the testis. Failing such the organisms are infertile as a species and thus incapable of passing on their genes. The resulting information would be most helpful to investigators in the field on their current and future studies to examine spermatogenesis, infertility, male contraception and germ cell implantation. The broad, long-term and health-related objective of this application is to offer insights in identifying new targets for male contraception, and on the etiology of unexplained infertility in men. 哺乳類動物的精子生成 (spermatogenesis) 過程，有兩個環節十分重要。其一是精子如何穿過血睪屏障；其二是精子如何脫離精小管上皮，輸送至管腔。這兩個環節分別發生在精小管上皮的相對兩邊。但無論是大鼠或是人類，兩個環節都是在同一刻發生；那就是說在大鼠精子生成週期的第八階段與及人類精子生成週期的第二階段。 我們先前的研究提出一個發生在睪丸的自體作用，證實附着連結 (adherens junctions) 解體令精子分離(spermiation) ，是可導致緊密連結 (tight junctions) 解散令血睪屏障開啟。兩個機制環節絲絲緊扣，讓精子生成綿綿遞增。 在這最新一環的研究中，我們將提出縫隙連結 (gap junctions)，以及焦連結激酶 (focal adhesion kinase) 的磷酸化作用在這自體作用上的重要及影響。 血睪屏障分解讓細線期精母細胞通過，與精子分離讓精細胞掉進精小管管腔，這兩個環節的相互牽引制衡，絕對是促使精子生成連綿不絕的重要一環。破解這個機制背後所存在的奧秘，有利我們更深認識精子生成的空時對配。這結果對研究精子生成、不育、避孕及生殖細胞移植有確實的影響。

772013.label: Realisation of objectives
772013.value: Kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1) serves as a useful marker for monitoring tubular injury. Sustained KIM-1 expression may implicate in healing of the injured kidney tubules. We examine the kinetic and mechanism of KIM-1 release in human kidney proximal tubular epithelial cells (PTEC) under the activation by major pathologic players in various kidney diseases including human serum albumin (HSA), glycated albumin (AGE-BSA) and high glucose. The kinetic of KIM-1 release by PTEC under activation with HSA, AGE-BSA and high glucose, were determined by RT-PCR and ELISA. The activation profiles of major signaling pathways in PTEC were identified by PCR array. Based on the array data, blockade experiments were designed to assess their regulatory roles on KIM-1 release. Our data reveal that prompt shedding of KIM-1 was observed in PTEC cultured 4 h with HSA and AGE-BSA, but not with high glucose. Culturing PTEC for 3 days with AGE-BSA exhibited sustained up-regulation of KIM-1 release, but not with HSA. In all culture experiments, high glucose did not induce KIM-1 release in PTEC. HSA and AGE-BSA activated multiple signaling pathways in PTEC including NFκB, ERK1/2 and the oxidative stress pathways. Long-term culturing PTEC with AGE-BSA but not HSA activated the Jak-Stat pathway. While incubation of PTEC with reactive oxygen species (ROS) inhibitor, diphenyleneiodonium (DPI), blocked the short-term release of KIM-1 mediated by HSA or AGE-BSA, Jak-Stat inhibitors diminished the long-term KIM-1 release by PTEC induced by AGE-BSA. Our data demonstrated that KIM-1 release in PTEC was differentially upregulated by HSA and AGE-BSA. The short-term KIM-1 shedding was mediated by the ROS whereas Jak-Stat pathway regulates the long-term KIM-1 release. We then studied the effect of KIM-1 overexpression or knockdown on healing of the injured PTEC. Stable murine PTEC line with KIM-1 overexpression was generated by transfecting PTEC with KIM-1 full-length cDNA. Two PTEC injury models were used: (i) Oxidative injury model by 1 H2O2 treatment, and (ii) in vitro scratch model. Our data obtained from both model indicate that injured PTEC have increased apoptosis, up-regulated dedifferentiated phenotype and enhanced expression of TNF-α, IL-6, CCL-2, CCL-5, CX3CL1, IL-8, TGF-β1, CSF-1 and FGF2. While the expression of CX3CL1, TGF-β and CSF-1 were further increased by KIM-1 overexpression, the apoptotic events and the dedifferentiated phenotype was not affected. Knockdown of KIM-1 did not increase the apoptotic events or the dedifferentiated phenotype but up-regulated the expression of TNF-α, IL-6 and CCL-2. We have further studied the effects and mechanism of KIM-1 overexpression on healing of injured PTEC and macrophage polarization. Oxidative injury model by H2O2 was established in murine PTEC with KIM-1 overexpression (KIM-1 hi PTEC). Cell viability, proliferation and apoptosis were determined after injury. The expression of vimentin, N-cadherin, TNF-α, MCP-1, TGF-β1 and CSF-1 were determined. To delineate the role of humoral factors released by injured KIM-1 hi PTEC on macrophages (Mø) polarization, bone marrow–derived Mø were cultured with injured PTEC in transwell setup. The temporal expression of markers for classical M1 or alternative activated M2 including iNOS, TNF-α, IL-23, CD206, IL-10 and arginase-1 were evaluated. Our data reveal that KIM-1 overexpression ameliorates PTEC apoptosis and accelerates the phagocytosis-dependent healing. Worth noticing, our data implicate that enhanced KIM-1 expression is beneficial in acute but undesirable in chronic tubular cell injury. We have also examined the role of KIM-1:TIM-4 pathway in regeneration of injured PTEC. To our surprise, the presence of artificial polarized bone marrow derived Mø or M2 subpopulation cannot improve the heaing of injured PTEC. In addition, the expression of TIM-4 by Mø or M2 is not altered with the presence of injured PTEC. Our data suggest that macrophage TIM-4 do not have critical role in the PTEC healing process. Two models of Mø depletion: (i) clodronate liposomes (CL) ablation of Mø subsets and (ii) diphtheria toxin (DT) administration to the mice transgenic for the human DT receptor were established to investigate the impacts of Mø subsets on healing of the kidney tubules after ischemia and reperfusion injury (IRI). In both models of Mø depletion, there are no significant changes in the kidney healing process. In summary, we show for the first time the short- and long- term KIM-1 release is regulated differentially by the oxidative stress and Jak-Stat pathway. We proposed that early induction of KIM-1 after acute kidney injury serves an adaptive function to clear apoptotic and necrotic cells and debris from injured tubular lumen and thereby decrease the early undesirable immune and inflammatory responses at site of tubular damage. However, persistent KIM-1 expression leads to sustained release of inflammatory cytokines and M1 polarization and infiltration. Our data suggest that enhanced KIM-1 expression is beneficial in acute but undesirable in chronic tubular cell injury. Unexpectedly, our data did not support the relevancy of KIM-1:TIM-4 pathway between PTEC and Mø to the regeneration process after injury.

772013.label: Major findings and research outcome
772013.value: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a common complication of diabetes with variable rate of kidney function decline after the development of disease. DN is traditionally considered as a glomerular disease but increasing evidences show the associated tubulointerstitial injury is also an important factor in pathophysiology and progression of DN. Albumin, AGE and high glucose are the major mediators for the pathogenesis of DN. We have explored the differential effects of high glucose, AGE-BSA and albumin on KIM-1 release by PTEC and the associated signaling pathways. We demonstrated that KIM-1 release in PTEC was differentially upregulated by HSA and AGE-BSA. The short-term KIM-1 shedding was mediated by the ROS whereas Jak-Stat pathway regulates the long-term KIM-1 release. This part of data have been published in Inflamm. Res. (2014) 63:831–839. (Part C; No 1) Other than DN, IgA Nephropathy (IgAN) is another chronic disease that lead to PTEC injury and eventually progress to end stage renal failure. In a review article, we have pointed out that In IgAN patients, expression of NLRP3 (Nod-like receptor pyrin domain-containing-3) is located primarily to the tubular epithelium but not glomerular. Furthermore, NLRP3 expression is colocalized with the KIM-1 expression, suggestion the amplification of tubulointerstitial inflammation by the NLRP3 activation. Interestingly, KIM-1 expression in IgA nephropathy has been correlated with hypoxia and tubulointerstitial inflammation. We have published these comments in Seminars in Nephrology, 2018 PII S0270-9295(18)30080-9. (Part C; No 2) We have also examined the effects and mechanism of KIM-1 overexpression on healing of injured PTEC and macrophage polarization. Oxidative injury model by H2O2 was established in murine PTEC with KIM-1 overexpression (KIM-1 hi PTEC). Our data show that apoptosis induced by H2O2 was ameliorated in KIM-1 hi PTEC. KIM-1 overexpression accelerates the phagocytosis-dependent healing. The enhanced M2 polarization by TGF-β1 and CSF-1 released from the injured KIM-1 hi PTEC, further contributes to the recovery process. Persistent KIM-1 overexpression leads to sustained release of inflammatory cytokines including TNF-α and MCP-1, plus M1 polarization and infiltration. Our results implicate that enhanced KIM-1 expression is beneficial in acute but undesirable in chronic tubular cell injury. The data are now being incorporated into a manuscript for submission to peered reviewed Journal. (Part C; No 3)

772013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
772013.value: Our data propose that early induction of KIM-1 after acute kidney injury serves an adaptive function to clear apoptotic and necrotic cells and debris from injured PTEC and thereby decrease the early undesirable immune and inflammatory responses of injured tubules. However, epithelial cells that express KIM-1 accumulate cellular toxic components continuously from the tubular lumen during chronic tubular damage and eventually cause chronic interstitial inflammation, which may act in a paracrine fashion to recruit mononuclear cells into the renal interstitium, ultimately promote and amplify further tubular damage and lead to renal fibrosis and loss of renal function. Our present data demonstrated the temporal expression pattern of KIM-1 is essential to define if KIM-1 is a "friend or foe" in PTEC regeneration. Further investigation on the mechanism and manipulation of the temporal KIM-1 expression is a key for developing rational therapeutic approaches to diminish the kidney epithelial tissues injury. While KIM-1 overexpression ameliorates PTEC apoptosis and enhanced M2 polarization-dependent healing, our data did not support KIM-1:TIM-4 pathway is important for the regeneration and healing of injured PTEC. Further studies should focus on searching whether there are unidentified KIM-1 ligand other that TIM-4, which may play a essential role in controlling the KIM-1 fucntions.

772013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
772013.value: Regardless of the original causes, the progression of kidney function declines toward end-stage renal disease follows a final common pathway associated with the injury of kidney proximal tubular epithelial cells (PTEC). Of particular interest, PTEC possess a remarkable capacity to repair and regenerate following injury. Kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1) acts as a double-edged sword in kidney injury and healing. While KIM-1 expression in PTEC is associated with kidney inflammation and fibrosis, KIM-1 also helps in clearance of debris from damaged renal tubules, and implicate in the process of regeneration of injured tubules. The regulatory role of KIM-1 and its released soluble form on the restoration of tubular integrity after injury is still not understood. In this project, we have shown that the short- and long- term KIM-1 releases were mediated by different mechanisms. Our data reveal that KIM-1 ameliorates PTEC apoptosis and accelerates the phagocytosis-dependent healing. Interestingly, we have also demonstrated that enhanced and sustained KIM-1 expression in PTEC is beneficial in acute, but undesirable in chronic tubular cell injury. In summary, data in this project uncover a KIM-1–dependent machinery that aids in tubular regeneration and counters tubular destruction following kidney injury.

772113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
772113.value: 大段骨缺损是骨科手术中常见的问题。自体骨移植是重建骨缺损的金标准。然而，自体骨的不足及取骨相关的并发症是其存在的主要问题。取自尸体或捐献的异体骨是自体骨良好的替代品。异体骨提供了良好的骨结构，但其有疾病传播的风险，限制了其临床应用。因此，迫切需要发展一种生物活性材料的骨替代品。各种材料，如羟基磷酸钙、磷酸钙陶瓷等被发展出来。但是，这些材料往往力学强度不足仍是其临床应用的障碍。 治疗骨缺损的理想的材料应具备骨传导性、骨诱导性，力学强度大的特点，并且骨折愈合后，其逐步被吸收。因为镁的力学特性与骨相近，并且可降解，其为一种潜在的骨替代物。但是由于其降解速度太快，并且释放出氢气，限制了镁在临床的应用。 为了解决这个问题，我们应用先进的材料表面处理技术成功的控制了镁的降解速度。出乎意料的是，我们发现释放出的镁离子在浓度为50~150ppm时可刺激骨形成。随后，我们进一步的发展了一系列的镁的复合材料（Mg-PCL）。在前期研究中，这些镁材料已被证明可刺激新骨形成，并且力学上和松质骨相匹配。然而，这种新材料能否用于临床治疗大段骨缺损尚不清楚。因此，这个课题的目的既是将这种新的骨替代物材料用于临界骨缺损的固定。 我们将系统的研究：1）不同含量Mg-PCL镁离子的释放及降解过程中Mg-PCL的力学性质；2）细胞对Mg-PCL材料的生物活性及毒性反应；3）在大鼠临界骨缺损模型中研究其成骨性及骨-材料的融合性，以及材料术后的生物力学性质。这项研究是将这种材料用于临床之前非常重要的一步。这种新型的生物活性材料将是大段骨缺损患者的潜在的良好的骨替代物。

772413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
772413.value: Gastric cancer is the second leading cause of cancer death in the world. Although Helicobacter pylori is the most important etiological agent for gastric cancer, the exact mechanisms underlying how chronic bacterial infection induce gastric cancer remain largely unknown. Atrophic gastritis and intestinal metaplasia are the intermediate steps of the H. pylori induced gastric carcinogenesis cascade. Atrophic gastritis is associated with low acid production, which would facilitate the colonization of the stomach by other bacteria. It has been suggested that the overgrowth of bacteria in the stomach with low acid output contributes to gastric cancer development by direct formation of carcinogen or by alteration of gastric mucosal inflammatory response and activation of potential carcinogenic cascade. This was further supported by a recent animal study which showed that the presence of other bacteria in the stomach hastened the development of H. pylori induced gastric cancer in genetically susceptible mice. However, conventional bacterial culture technique fails to isolate these non-Helicobacter species in the stomach. With the amplification of the 16S ribosomal RNA gene of bacteria and conventional low resolution cloning techniques, previous studies have demonstrated the presence of other bacterial microbiome in the stomach of patients with gastric cancer as well as in patients infected with H. pylori. In recent few years, the availability of new technology like the next generation sequencing enables a more detailed and in-depth characterization of microbiome but data in the human stomach are sparse. This study attempts to characterize the bacterial microbiome in the stomach of H. pylori infected individuals with different stages of histological changes including chronic gastritis, intestinal metaplasia and gastric cancer. We will also compare the gastric microbiome in patients with and without H. pylori infection and the role of H. pylori eradication therapy on changes of gastric microbiome. All these will be performed by the latest next generation sequencing technique. The results of this study will help to unravel potential role of other non-Helicobacter bacterial species in the pathogenesis of gastric cancer, which may help in the understanding of the complex interaction between H. pylori and other bacterial organisms. 胃癌在世界上癌症死亡病例中排第二。雖然幽門螺桿菌是胃癌最重要的病原體，從慢性細菌感染誘發胃癌的確切機制仍是未知。萎縮性胃炎和腸上皮化生是幽門螺桿菌導致胃癌發生的中間步驟。萎縮性胃炎可引起低胃酸輸出, 從而促進幽門螺桿菌及其他細菌在胃中過度生長。有研究指出低胃酸輸出及細菌過度滋生可能形成致癌物質，或通過改變胃黏膜的炎症反應並啟動癌變過程。最近在有遺傳易感性小鼠上進行的研究進一步支持了在其他細菌的存在下，由幽門螺桿菌引起胃癌的進程會被加快。 然而傳統的細菌培養技術不能隔離這些非幽門螺桿菌物種。在之前的研究中，利用傳統的細菌16s核糖體核糖核酸擴增及低分辨率克隆技術，已經闡明在胃癌及檢測到幽門螺桿菌陽性的病人胃中有其他細菌。近幾年來，新一代測序等新技術的出現可使微生物得到更詳細和深入分析。但是有關胃微生物的數據仍然稀缺。 本研究試圖刻畫在幽門螺旋桿菌感染不同階段的個體(包括慢性胃炎，腸上皮化生與胃癌) 的胃細菌微生物的特徵。我們也將比較病人在有無幽門螺旋桿菌感染的胃細菌微生物的差異，及在幽門螺桿菌根除治療後胃微生物的變化。新一代測序技術將被用於此研究中。這項研究結果將有助於解開非幽門細菌物種在胃癌的發病機制中的角色及其潛在相互作用。

772413.label: Realisation of objectives
772413.value: Objective 1:To characterize the gastric microbiota in individuals with and without HP infections Endoscopic gastric biopsies were obtained from patients with and without H. pylori infection. Bacterial 16S rRNA was extracted from gastric biopsy and sequenced on next generation sequencing platform (454 pyrosequencing and Illumina MiSeq). Operational taxonomic unit (OTU) clustering, diversity indexes calculation, taxonomic classification, PCoA and statistical analyses were performed after quality control and raw sequence processing. Hierarchical clustering of samples obtained from HP-positive patients and HP-negative individuals demonstrated two divergent cluster groups. The first cluster (cluster A) contained mostly HP-negative samples while the other cluster (cluster B) comprised exclusively of HP-positive samples. The HP-negative group also had higher bacterial diversity than the HP-positive group. There was a strong negative association between HP relative abundance and Shannon diversity index. Objective 2: To demonstrate the difference in gastric microbiota in individuals with different histological stages of gastric carcinogenesis. We compared the gastric microbiota of patients with HP gastritis, gastric intestinal metaplasia (IM), gastric carcinoma and normal controls who were negative for HP. Hierarchical clustering of these samples showed that they were mainly segregated by the presence of HP rather than by histological stages. Gastritis samples tended to have similar bacterial composition as IM samples. In contrast, cancer samples had distinctive bacterial composition as well as reduction in bacterial diversity as compared to other histological groups including the IM group. Objective 3: To determine the changes in gastric microbiota after HP eradication Serial gastric biopsies were obtained from patients with H. pylori infection to determine the changes in gastric microbiota composition after receiving H. pylori eradication therapy. When compared with pre-eradication samples, the average relative abundance of Helicobacter decreased from 83.70% in the pre-treatment to 6.88% in the post treatment samples. Accordingly, the relative abundance of non-HP Proteobacteria has increased from 4.55% to 51.70%. The relative abundance of other major phyla including Bacteroidetes, Fusobacteria and Actinobacteria were also found to be increased in post-eradication samples. Both the Shannon index and phylogenetic diversity index significantly increased after HP eradication. Based on these findings, we conclude that H. pylori colonization results in alteration in gastric microbiota and reduction in bacterial diversity, which could possibly be restored by antibiotic treatment. There are significant changes in the relative abundance of different bacterial species in the stomach during progression from IM to cancer.

772413.label: Major findings and research outcome
772413.value: While gastric cancer is still a leading cancer in Asia, there is a pressing need to identify the mechanism underlying gastric cancer development. Although Helicobacter pylori (HP) is strongly associated with gastric cancer, the role of other bacteria in the stomach remains elusive. We aimed to characterize the gastric microbiota in individuals with different histological stages of gastric carcinogenesis and after receiving HP eradication therapy. Endoscopic gastric biopsies were obtained from subjects with HP gastritis, gastric intestinal metaplasia (IM), gastric cancer (GC) and HP negative controls. Gastric microbiota was characterized by next generation sequencing targeting the 16S rDNA. Apart from the dominant H. pylori, we observed other Proteobacteria including Haemophilus, Serratia, Neisseria and Stenotrophomonas as the major components of the human gastric microbe. Although samples were largely converged according to the relative abundance of HP, a clear separation of GC and other samples was recovered. Whilst there was a strong inverse association between HP relative abundance and bacterial diversity, this association was weak in GC samples which tended to have lower bacterial diversity compared with other samples with similar HP levels. Eradication of HP resulted in an increase in bacterial diversity and restoration of the relative abundance of other bacteria to levels similar to individuals without HP. H. pylori colonization results in alterations of gastric microbiota and reduction in bacterial diversity, which could be restored by antibiotic treatment.

772413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
772413.value: Our findings suggest a novel benefit of eradicating H. pylori in restoring the gastric microbiota composition and loss of bacterial diversity in individuals with HP infection. Further studies may be necessary to characterize the gastric microbiota in different regions with diverse background incidence of gastric cancer, and identify potential association with specific gastric microbiota profiles or diversity that may be linked to cancer development. Future study may also be directed to study the potential correlation of gastric microbiota with various environmental factors such as smoking and dietary habits. Our study findings open up new research direction on the potential role and dynamic changes of gastric microbiota in H. pylori infected individuals and during gastric cancer development, which has not been fully characterized.

772413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
772413.value: Gastric cancer is still one of the leading cancers in Asia. Although H. pylori has been classified as a type I carcinogen for gastric cancer by the World Health Organization, the mechanism underlying H. pylori induced gastric cancer development remains elusive. Apart from H. pylori, the potential role of other bacteria present in the stomach remains elusive. This study characterized the gastric microbiota in individuals in different stages of gastric carcinogenesis cascade by using next generation sequencing. Our results showed that H. pylori dominated the gastric microenvironment in infected individuals leading to lower bacterial diversity. Eradication of H. pylori resulted in restoration of gastric microenvironment and increase in bacterial diversity. During gastric carcinogenesis, the most remarkable changes in gastric microenvironment occurred in cancer stage while gastric microbiota were similar in gastritis and premalignant gastric lesions. Gastric cancer stage is characterized by further reduction in bacterial diversity when compared to non-cancerous samples with similar H. pylori abundance. In conclusion, we have demonstrated a marked different gastric bacterial composition in patients infected with H. pylori infection, which are potentially reversible by antibiotics treatment and may be linked to gastric cancer development. Further studies are needed to characterize the gastric micrbiota in different geographic regions as well as its relationship with diet and smoking, both of them are considered risk factors for gastric cancer development.

772913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
772913.value: Heart diseases have been a major cause of death worldwide. Indeed, loss of nonregenerative, terminally differentiated CMs due to aging or diseases is irreversible. Current therapeutic regimes are palliative in nature, and in the case of end-stage heart failure, transplantation remains the last and only resort. Unfortunately, myocardial repair is significantly hampered by a severe shortage of donor cells and organs, leading to substantial mortality and morbidity as well as socio-economical costs. Recent advances in the identification and isolation of pluripotent or multipotent stem cells have enabled clinicians and scientists to pursue the revolutionary paradigm of Regenerative Medicine. Human embryonic stem cells (hESCs), isolated from the inner cell mass of blastocysts, can self-renew while maintaining their pluripotency to differentiate into all cell types, including cardiomyocytes (CMs). Therefore, hESCs may provide an unlimited ex vivo source of CMs for cell-based heart therapies. Recently, direct reprogramming of adult somatic cells to become pluripotent hES-like cells (a.k.a. induced pluripotent stem cells or iPSCs) has been achieved, eliminating potential ethical concerns. Using the same cardiac differentiation protocol originally developed for hESCs, iPSCs can be similarly differentiated into spontaneously beating CMs. Although promising, however, the functional properties of hESC/iPSC-CMs remain very poorly defined; electrophysiological and contractile functions are two FUNDAMENTAL properties of working cardiac muscle cells. Do hESC/iPSC-CMs display the proper Ca2+-handling properties that are central to their primary function as contractile muscle cells? If not,how do these Ca2+-handling properties affect the efficacy of hESC-CMs in transplantation, and as models for studying heart diseases and for cardiotoxicity screening? This proposal aims to build on our expertise, previous work and existing knowledge in the field to address a major gap: to better understand the poorly defined Ca-handling properties of hESC-CMs and the underlying basis, and thereby develop an effective method for driving maturation and enhancing efficacy as donor cells, disease models and cardiotoxicity screening. Not only does the proposal promise to deliver pragmatic tools that will be useful for the field of cardiac regeneration but the knowledge gained is also anticipated to improve our understanding of the processes of human cardiac differentiation and maturation that cannot be readily experimentally studied (e.g., due to various ethical and practical concerns involved in obtaining healthy human hearts for experiments). 772913.label: Realisation of objectives
772913.value: In Objective 1, we tested the hypothesis that nuclear Ca2+ signaling plays a pivotal role in the developmental biology of hESC-VCMs, and is mechanistically and functionally distinct from cytosolic Ca2+ signaling. We found that active Ca2+ release in the nucleus of hESC-VCMs is mediated by ryanodine receptors (RyR) but not inositol 1,4,5-triphosphate receptors (IP3R), distinctly different from mouse. We also discovered the structure nuclear reticulum (NR). As proposed, we also investigated the functional consequences in hESC-VCMs, as single-cells and 3D engineered cardiac tissues (ECT), after ventricular-specific genetic inhibition of nuclear and/or cytoplasmic Ca2+, during cardiac maturation. Differential effects were observed. We analyzed these data using bioinformatic approaches. As for Objective 2, we tested the hypothesis that the combinatorial approach of simultaneously engineering CSQ, PLB, SERCA and NCX. These data were collected and compared to individual and simultaneous overexpression. Changes in Ca2+ sparks and transients, action potential (AP), other cellular properties as well as contractility and inotropic response were examined in single cells, and in select cases, tissue constructs as well. With the functional experiments done, we analyzed these data using bioinformatics approaches as proposed.

772913.label: Major findings and research outcome
772913.value: We showed that nuclear Ca2+ signaling, which stems from unitary sparks due to the diffusion of cytosolic Ca2+ that are mediated by RyRs on the so-called nuclear reticulum, is functional. We also investigated the effect of Ca2+ on gene transcription in hESC-VCMs, and the involvement of nuclear factor of activated T-cells (NFAT) pathway was identified. Finally, the role of Ca2+-sensitive, nuclear localized Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II δB (CaMKIIδB) overexpression was studied. We have dissected the roles of CSQ and NCX in Ca2+–handing of hPSC-VCMs by systematically engineering their expression levels. SERCA overexpression shortened the decay phase of low frequency (0.5 Hz) electrical stimulation-elicited Ca2+ transient without affecting the transient amplitude, SR Ca2+ content and Ca2+ baseline. Interestingly, shRNA-based suppression of NCX in hESC-VCMs did not prolong the decay phase of Ca2+ transient, indicating a compensatory response for Ca2+ removal. Although hESC-VCMs exhibited a negative frequency-transient response, SERCA overexpression led to increased transient amplitudes at high frequencies (>2 Hz) by accelerating Ca2+ sequestration to SR. Based on these results, we concluded that 1) SERCA and NCX genetic manipulations had limited modulating effects on low frequency stimulation-elicited Ca2+ transient, 2) SERCA, rather than NCX, was the main Ca2+ remover during diastole in hESC-VCMs, and 3) hESC-VCM harbored a negative-frequency response and SERCA overexpression partially rescued this phenotype. In our study, we confirmed that PLB protein was differentially expressed in hESC (HES2, H9)- and iPSCderived and adult vCMs. Importantly, AdPLB–transduced hES2-vCMs uniquely responded to isoproterenol. Ad-S16E-PLB–transduced hES2-vCMs displayed an intermediate phenotype. The same trends were observed with H9- and iPSC-vCMs. Directionally, similar results were also seen with Ad-PLB–transduced and Ad-S16E–transduced hvCMTs. However, Ad-PLB altered neither the global transcriptome nor ICa,L, implicating a PLB-specific effect.

772913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
772913.value: To correlate the biological roles in hESC and hESC-VCMs to the affected pathways identified, we placed emphasis on Ca2+-related proteins. Therefore, for instance, if nuclear enlargement and increased cell size turns out to associate with calcineurin activation/upregulation, cells will be treated with the calcineurin inhibitor Cyclosporin A (CsA). We will see if NFAT localizes in the nucleus, and if so, whether CsA treatment would prevent NFAT translocation and hypertrophy. Other unlimited possibilities include calmodulin binding‐peptide CaMBP4 that is essential for histone deacetylases translocation in adult VCMs, etc, will be studied as needed. Various other conditions or proteins have been reported to alter SERCA or NCX expression or activity, thereby affecting intracellular Ca2+ cycling. For instances, SERCA and NCX can be reciprocally regulated by redox. SERCA and NCX activity may also be affected by other Ca2+-sensitive proteins like S100A1. SERCA can be modulated by SUMO1, Sorcin and Calumenin. In adult and neonatal cardiomyocytes, NCX promoter is differentially regulated by Nkx2.5 and Serum response factor. All these potential players may be investigated in hESC-VCMs, which is beyond the scope of current study.

772913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
772913.value: In Summary, we sought to develop a cause-and-effect relationship between any changes in nuclear or cytosolic Ca2+ signals and the corresponding biological responses. We conclude that 1) nuclear Ca2+ signal has a delayed kinetics compared to cytosolic Ca2+ signal during global Ca2+ changes like waves or transients, indicating nuclear Ca2+ is initiated by Ca2+ diffusion from cytosol, 2) local nuclear Ca2+ sparks in hESC-VCMs are mediated by RyRs, and NR serve as structural basis. In addition, PV-mediated Ca2+ buffering can successfully manipulated Ca2+ transient and stimuli-induced apoptosis in hESC-VCMs. Moreover, hESC-VCMs harbored functional endogenous cytosolic Ca2+/CN/NFAT pathway, and overexpression of nucleus-localized CaMKIIδB led to cardiac hypertrophy through nuclear Ca2+/CaMKIIδB/HDAC4/MEF2 pathway. Collectively, these findings firstly provide the insights of nuclear Ca2+ signal in hESC-VCMs, which may lead to novel strategies for maturation as well as improved systems for disease modeling, drug discovery and cell-based therapies. In the present study, we investigated the effects of lentivirus-based manipulation of Ca2+ removers SERCA2a and NCX1 in hESC-VCMs. Our results indicated that SERCA was the major remover of elevated Ca2+ during electrical stimulation induced Ca2+ transients, and the compensative effect of NCX on Ca2+ removal could be observed after SERCA inhibition. Moreover, hESC-VCMs harbored negative frequency response and SERCA2a overexpression partially rescue this phenotype at both single cell and tissue level. Engineered upregulation of PLB expression in hESC/iPSC-vCMs restores a positive inotropic response to β-adrenergic stimulation. These results not only provide a better mechanistic understanding of the immaturity of hESC/ iPSC-vCMs but will also lead to improved disease models and transplantable prototypes with adult-like physiological responses.

773313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
773313.value: A de novo G608G mutation in LMNA gene activates an alternate splicing site, leading to a truncated prelamin A called progerin, which is the predominant cause of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome (HGPS). Mice lacking Zmpste24, a metalloproteinase responsible for processing prelamin A to its mature form, recapitulate many progeroid features observed in HGPS. One of the hallmarks of progeroid cells is misshapen nucleus, which leads to disorganized heterochromatin and mislocalized nuclear proteins. Previously, we and others have shown that accumulation of prelamin A and progerin compromised DNA damage repair in HGPS dermal fibroblasts and Zmpste24 deficient mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs), evident by accumulation of unrepaired/irreparable DNA damage. However, the precise molecular mechanism underlying defective DNA repair is still largely unknown. We recently found that the accumulation of prelamin A and progerin compromised DNA damage-induced chromatin remodeling, and levels of H3K9me3 and H4K20me3 were significantly increased in cells deficient for Zmpste24. Given that compact confirmation of heterochromatin builds up a barrier for DNA repair, and heterochromatic factors, including Suv39h1/2, HDAC1/2 and HP1α/β/γ, regulate global chromatin remodeling and DNA repair, we ask whether epigenetic changes lead to defective DNA repair and accelerate senescence in HGPS and progeroid mouse model. In this project, we would like to investigate (1) whether A-type lamins, referring to lamin A, prelamin A and progerin, stabilize Suv39h1 and Suv4-20h2 methyltransferases thus increasing levels of H3K9me3 and H4K20me3; (2) whether down-regulation of H3K9me3 and/or H4K20me3 levels via RNA interference, genetic depletion or pharmaceutical inhibition of Suv39h1 and/or Suv4-20h2 could rescue defective DNA repair and alleviate progeroid features in HGPS cells and mice deficient for Zmpste24. These studies will provide not only mechanistic insights into how epigenetic changes contribute to premature aging and normal aging process, but also additional therapeutic strategies for HGPS. 一般機體老化是緩慢、漸進的,但特異的基因突變可引起老化加速和一些生理功能障礙,從而出現早衰。兒童早老症(Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome)是一種非常典型的,由LMNA基因突變引起的早老性遺傳病。LMNA G608G突變啟動了一個潛在的mRNA剪接位點,造成異位剪接,引起異常Lamin A 蛋白的堆積,稱為衰老素(Progerin)。人類正常細胞中也存在少量Progerin並隨年齡增加而累積,提示正常衰老與兒童早老症有共同的細胞分子生物學基礎。LMNA基因首先合成Prelamin A,後經法尼基化、甲基化及金屬蛋白酶ZMPSTE24 切割而成為成熟的Lamin A。在小鼠中敲除Zmpste24 引起Prelamin A 的累積,導致類似兒童早老症的表型。人類與正常小鼠的生命週期較長,衰老過程不易研究,因此Zmpste24 敲除小鼠提供了一個很好的研究兒童早老症和正常衰老機理的動物模型。我們前期研究發現早老細胞中DNA損傷修復相關蛋白不能有效地募集到DNA損傷位點,以致DNA損傷不能有效、及時地修復,從而誘發兒童早老症的基因組不穩定性與細胞早老。然而導致DNA損傷修復缺陷的分子機理尚不清楚。 通常情況下,DNA在細胞核內以致密染色質的形式存在。當遇到損傷的時候,染色質就會鬆弛開來,説明募集與損傷修復相關的蛋白到達損傷位點,因此染色質重塑對DNA損傷修復至關重要。我們之前的研究發現,早老細胞存在明顯的染色質結構異常,並且參與調控異染色質結構的H3K9me3與H4K20me3等組蛋白修飾水準顯著升高。據此,我們提出假說:異染色質重塑缺陷可能導致DNA損傷修復缺陷,並最終引起細胞及機體衰老。為驗證這一假說,我們將研究(1)Prelamin A與Progerin是否與H3K9三甲基化酶Suv39h1及H4K20三甲基化酶Suv4-20h2直接相互作用並調控其蛋白質穩定性,從而促進H3K9me3與H4K20me3水準上調;(2)通過RNA干擾、基因敲除或者小分子藥物等手段降低H3K9me3與H4K20me3水準,是否可以挽救DNA損傷修復缺陷,延緩細胞和機體衰老,最終延長小鼠壽命。預期成果不僅有助於加深理解染色質重塑調控DNA損傷修復的分子生物學,推進人類對衰老的細胞及分子機理的認識,還有助於研發新的治療兒童早老症及促進人類健康並延長壽命。

773313.label: Realisation of objectives
773313.value: Objective 1: To understand the mechanism by which A-type lamins regulates Suv39h1 level thus modulating heterochromatin confirmation. (100% realization) To understand the regulatory role for lamin A in Suv39h1 and H3K9me3, we examined whether loss of lamin A affects Suv39h1 stability and level of H3K9me3. We found that H3K9me3 was consistently and significantly decreased in Lmna null MEFs compared with that from wild-type littermate controls, while no significant changes in levels of H3K27me3, H4K20me3, H3K9me, H3K9me2, H3K4me3, acetylated H4 or acetylated H3 was observed. To distinguish effects of lamin A in the transcriptional and post-translational regulation of Suv39h1, we knocked down LMNA by siRNA in HEK293 cells where ectopic GFP-SUV39H1 driven by a CMV promoter was expressed. The level of GFP-SUV39H1 was examined by Western blotting. Levels of GFP-SUV39H1 and H3K9me3 were both significantly reduced when lamin A/C level was downregulated, indicating that lamin A/C stabilizes GFP-SUV39H1 protein. Further investigation demonstrated that lamin A could stabilize Suv39h1 and thus prevent it from proteasomal degradation as incubation with proteasome inhibitor MG-132 increased the level of Suv39h1 in Lmna–/– cells. To test whether prelamin A and progerin have increased binding capacity to SUV39H1, we compared the interactions between GFP-SUV39H1 and different A-type lamins, i.e. lamin A, prelamin A and progerin by co-immunoprecipitation. Significantly more prelamin A and progerin were detected in the anti GFP immunoprecipitates though comparable level of lamin A, prelamin A and progerin was found in the input and comparable GFP-SUV39H1 was pulled down, indicating increased binding capacity of SUV39H1 to prelamin A and progerin compared with lamin A. To further confirm the increased binding capacity between prelamin A/progerin and SUV39H1, we examined the mobility of SUV39H1 as increased association of SUV39H1 with prelamin A and progerin would decrease its mobility. Fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) was employed to compare the mobility of GFP-SUV39H1 between Zmpste24−/− cells and wild-type controls. The recovery rate of GFP-SUV39H1 was significantly delayed in Zmpste24−/− cells and HG003 cells compared with that in wild-types or PH cells, suggesting that prelamin A and progerin have an enhanced association with SUV39H1 than lamin A therefore the increased immobilization of SUV39H1. We tested nd found that the association of SUV39H1 with prelamin A/progerin protects it from degradation. Objective 2: To investigate whether up-regulation of Suv39h1 and H3K9me3 contributes to delayed chromatin remodeling, defective DNA repair and premature aging. (100% Realization) We examined whether depleting Suv39h1 in Zmpste24−/− mice could rescue accelerated cellular senescence, ameliorate progeroid features and extend lifespan. We crossed Zmpste24−/− mice with Suv39h1−/− mice to obtain Zmpste24−/−/Suv39h1−/− compound mutant mice. Loss of Suv39h1 significantly rescued the shortened replicative lifespan in Zmpste24−/− cells determined by a continuous passaging assay, and early senescence determined by senescence-associated β-galactosidase assay. Similarly, knocking down Suv39h1/2 also rescued early senescence in Zmpste24−/− MEFs. To examine whether loss of Suv39h1 ameliorates progeroid phenotypes, the body size, bone mineral density and lifespan were monitored accordingly. Body size, bone volume, bone mineral density and body weight were significantly increased in Zmpste24−/−/Suv39h1−/ mice compared with those in Zmpste24−/−mice. Remarkably, the median survival was extended more than 60 %. The maximal lifespan (average lifespan of the most long-lived 10% of examined mice) was prolonged almost 40 %. Collectively, reducing H3K9me3 by depleting Suv39h1 significantly delayed the onset of premature aging in Zmpste24−/− mice. These data suggest a regulatory role for heterochromatin regulation in senescence and premature aging. Objective 3: To examine whether A-type lamins regulate Suv4-20h2 and H4K20me3 and whether H4K20me3 also contributes to defective chromatin remodeling, DNA repair and premature aging. (100% realization) To address this objectives, we have examined how mutation in lamin A will affect SUV4-20h2 and H4K20me3. Our data showed that lamin A interacts with Suv4-20h2 and the level of Suv4-20h2 protein is upregulated in Zmpste24 deficient MEFs. To test if A-type lamins might regulate Suv4-20h2 stability, and upregulation of H4K20me3 might also contribute to defective DNA repair and premature aging, we examined the protein and mRNA level of Suv4-20h2 in progeroid cells and HEK293 cells stably expressing lamin A, prelamin A or progerin. Suv4-20h2 mRNA level is not affected by the presence of prelamin A or progerin, however, Suv4-20h2 stability is protected by the presence of progerin or prelamin A. Further more, loss of LMNA in HEK293 cells accelerates the degradation of Suv4-20h2. Similar to Suv39h1, co-immunoprecipitation was performed in the presence of prelamin A or progerin to examine whether the abnormally processed carboxyl tail could interfere their interaction with Suv4-20h2. We found that lamin A directly interacts with and stabilizes Suv4-20h2, Although the presence of progerin and prelamin A exhibited higher level of H4K20me3 compared to their wild-type counterpart, the level of H4K29me3 in both mutant and wild-type MEFs goes down gradually with the passage, suggesting that decreased H4K20me3 is a consequence of senescence and aging. As decreased H4K20me3 is involved in normal aging/senescence, we therefore focused more on the potential cause of the down regulation of H4K20me3 in aging/senescence. In collaborate with Prof Wei TAO from Peking University, we have systemically examined H4K20me3 in senescence. We found that activated TGF-β signaling gives rise to acute accumulation of miR-29a and miR-29c, both directly suppressing their novel targets, Suv4-20h, and thereafter leading to the reduction of H4K20me3 in a Smads-dependent manners. Reduced H4K20me3 in turn compromises DNA damage repair and genome stability. Furthermore, disruption of TGF-β signaling restores H4K20me3 and improves recovery of cardiac functions in aged mouse heart.

773313.value: We found that lamin A regulates chromatin dynamics through interacting with chromatin modifying enzymes such as SUV39H1 and Suv4-20h1 to modulate histone H3K9me3 and H4K20me3. Progerin/prelamin A increases such interaction, leading to elevated H3K9me3/H4K20me3 and increased heterochromation in Zmpste24-deficient mice, compared with the wild-type counterpart cells. However, both histone modifications are decline during senescence and aging though their levels are higher in the presence of prelamin A. Modulating these important histone modifying enzyme can significantly improved epigenetics, chromatine remodeling, DNA repair, senescence and aging. The TGF-β signaling is up-regulated during senescence which gives rise to acute accumulation of miR-29a and miR-29c, both directly suppressing a novel targets, Suv4-20h, and thereafter leading to the H4K20me3 reduction in a Smads-dependent manners. Interfering TGF-β signaling restores H4K20me3 and improves function of aging mouse hearts.

773313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
773313.value: Our genome is organized into a structure called chromatin which consists of duoble strand DNA and a core histone complex. Chromatin conformation is controlled by DNA methylation and histone modifications. When our genome is damaged by various endogenous and exogenous agents such as reactive oxygen species and irradiation, the double strand DNA are broken. To repair this, chromatin will change the conformation so that repair proteins will be able to access to the damage sites. This process is regulated through histone modifications. However, if the histones are not properly modified upon DNA damage or altered after cell replications, the response to DNA damage declines therefore DNA damages accumulate. Eventurely cells will not be able to handle and become senescence, e.g. they will not divide and become functional defecient. This will lead to tissue repair defect and organism aging. There are many different histone modifications. Some are more important than others and are critical in determining the cellular senescence. In this study we have determined what are those histone modifications that are more likely the driving force for senescence and aging using animal model of human accelerated aging syndrome called Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome (HGPS). We have identified several modifications including H3K9me3 and H4K20me3 that are important for chromatin conformation changes and remodeling. We also revealed why these modifications changes during aging. The modifying enzymes responsible for these modifications are associated with nuclear lamins and mutations in nuclear lamins altered their affinities, therefore affecting their activities. By modulating the changes in these modifications, we can improve the chromatin remodelling and enhance the DNA repair and extended lifespan in mice.Similar changes were also found in normal aging, suggesting that it is possible by targeting these modifications, we can improve the aging-associated physiological changes and diseases.

773613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
773613.value: Neuroprotection has become a major strategy for treating eye diseases with retinal degeneration including hereditary retinal dystrophies, ischemic retinopathies and retinal detachment. Although recent advances enabled discovery of new therapeutic factors, few effective treatments are available due to lack of efficient delivery system. As these are retinal disorders in inner eye, traditional delivery methods (e.g. eye drops) are ineffective while blood-retinal barrier precludes use of other conventional (e.g. oral, intravenous) means of administration. Administration by direct intravitreal injection is commonly performed but can cause safety issues due to repeated injections necessitated by factors’ short half-lives. Our goal is to develop cell-based intraocular delivery system for sustained release of neurotrophic factor as therapy for retinal degeneration. We previously demonstrated use of collagen microspheres to encapsulate cells and inclusion of alginate to prevent cell leakage. We further confirmed possibility of collagen-alginate composite gel with encapsulated genetically-engineered cells that constantly delivers glial cell-derived neurotrophic factor (GDNF) as ideal drug delivery system in vitro. Our preliminary results established intravitreal gel for efficacy assessment in vivo and most importantly, demonstrated that collagen-alginate composite gel secreted GDNF and partially rescued photoreceptors when injected into the eyes of Royal College of Surgeons (RCS) rat, a classic animal model of inherited retinal degeneration. This rescue effect is clinically relevant as photoreceptor death is a common pathology in many retinal diseases. In this proposal, we hypothesize that long-term GDNF delivery from cells encapsulated in collagen-alginate composite gel will preserve photoreceptors in the RCS rat model of retinal degeneration. We aim to (1) establish injectable collagen-alginate composite gel which encapsulates cells that not only constitutively express GDNF but also caspase 8 (upon doxycycline exposure) using Tet-on strategy, allowing inducible suicidal cell death and therefore cessation of GDNF release without device retrieval by surgery; and (2) assess safety and efficacy of GDNF delivered by collagen-alginate composite gel in the RCS rat model of retinal degeneration. With this sustained cell-based GDNF-delivery device, we hope to achieve neuroprotection on photoreceptors in retinal degeneration. Since various cells including autologous cells (e.g. mesenchymal stem cells or fibroblasts) can be genetically engineered to secrete various therapeutic agents, this drug delivery system may also be useful in other chronic neurodegenerative diseases. 神經保護已經成為治療視網膜退行性病變（包括遺傳性視網膜變性, 缺血性視網膜病變和視網膜脫離）的主要方法之一。儘管不斷有新的治療方法出現，但是由於缺少了有效的給藥系統而使得這些方法不能達到很好的療效。因為視網膜退行性病變是發生在內眼的疾病，所以傳統的給藥方法（例如滴眼劑）是沒有效用的，同時血-視網膜屏障又阻止了其他常用的給藥方式（例如口服，靜脈注射）的使用。臨床上通常使用直接玻璃體內注射以達到更好的療效，但是卻需要多次注射藥物以保持有效的藥物治療濃度。我們的目標是希望開發一種以細胞為基礎的能夠持續釋放神經營養因子的給藥系統用來治療視網膜退行性病變。我們之前已經證明了使用膠原蛋白微顆粒和海藻酸鈣包裹細胞可以防止細胞滲漏，並且進一步在體外實驗中確定了包裹在膠原蛋白-海藻酸鈣複合膠裡的經過基因改造的細胞能夠持續釋放膠質細胞源性神經營養因子(GDNF)，故而有可能成為理想的給藥系統。我們的前期結果不僅建立了在體檢測已注射入玻璃體內膠的效力的方法，更重要的是膠原蛋白-海藻酸鈣複合膠可以釋放出GDNF並且能夠部份挽救RCS鼠（Royal College of Surgeons rat），一種遺傳性視網膜退化的動物模型，的感光細胞。這個治療作用是與臨床密切相關的因為感光細胞死亡是很多視網膜疾病中常見的病理表現。因此我們假設膠原蛋白-海藻酸鈣複合膠內細胞長期釋放出的GDNF能夠保護RCS鼠的視網膜感光細胞。我們計劃(1)設計一種適合注射的包裹細胞的膠原蛋白-海藻酸鈣複合膠，同時複合膠裡的細胞不僅能夠持續表達GDNF而且可以通過Tet-on調控細胞凋亡蛋白酶8的表達（在強力黴素的參與下），從而誘導細胞自殺以達到不需要通過手術而停止GDNF釋放的目的；(2)在RCS鼠上評估膠原蛋白-海藻酸鈣複合膠釋放出的GDNF的安全性和有效性。我們希望借由這個以細胞為基礎的持續表達GDNF的裝置達到在視網膜退行性病變中對感光細胞的神經保護作用。各種細胞，包括自體細胞（例如間充質幹細胞或成纖維細胞）都可以通過基因改造分泌不同的治療性因子，因此這個給藥系統也有可能用於其他的慢性神經退行性病變的治療。

773613.label: Realisation of objectives
773613.value: In this proposal, we first aimed to establish a collagen-alginate composite (CAC) gel, which encapsulates cells that not only constitutively express glial-derived neurotrophic factor (GDNF) but also caspase 8 (upon doxycycline exposure). We successfully demonstrated, 1) generation of stable clones showing high TetR protein levels 2) successful encapsulation of stable clones in CAC gels with sustained GDNF secretion with the optimal cell numbers 3) complete cell death in CAC gels in vitro within 72 hours of doxycycline treatment with active caspase 8 expression and positive TUNEL signals 4) complete cell death in intravitreal CAC gel in vivo upon 48 hours of oral doxycycline treatment with active caspase 8 expression and positive TUNEL signals in rat eyes 5) good mechanical stability, unimpaired cell proliferation and sustained GDNF delivery of CAC gels after 28 days and even 6 months of implantation These results suggested that we have achieved highly stable TetR repression under normal conditions and effective doxycycline-induced genetic control for intravitreally implanted devices. Our strategy of using the Tet-On system to control cell death and therefore device termination was successful. Our CAC gels showed good biocompatibility and were well tolerated in rat eyes for up to 6 months. We have completely achieved Objective 1. In objective 2, we aimed to assess the safety and efficacy of GDNF delivered by collagen-alginate composite gel in RCS rat, a model of retinal degeneration. We successfully demonstrated, 1) intravitreal injection of CAC gels (single or double) encapsulated with cells expressing TetR and GDNF into RCS rat eyes with retinal degeneration 2) improvement in outer nuclear layer (ONL) thickness, photoreceptor nuclei density and organisation after 4 weeks of CAC gel implantation 2) functional rescue in rat eyes receiving CAC gels by electroretinography 3) both morphological and functional rescue were more pronounced when 2 CAC gels were injected Our results suggested that GDNF secreted by these cells encapsulated in our CAC gel was safe and bioactive in rescuing photoreceptors in RCS rat eyes with retinal degeneration. More importantly, there is a dose-response as better outcome was observed when 2 CAC gels were injected, suggesting that our design can yield a multiplexing effect. We have completely achieved Objective 2.

773613.label: Major findings and research outcome
773613.value: 1) We have successfully engineered and demonstrated the efficacy of our injectable collagen-alginate composite (CAC) gels in rats with retinal degeneration. Good mechanical stability, unimpaired cell proliferation and sustained GDNF delivery of CAC gels were observed after 28 days and even 6 months of implantation in rat eyes. Complete termination of the CAC gels was achievable by oral doxycycline administration. These CAC gels with sustained GDNF release can provide morphological and functional rescue in RCS rats with retinal degeneration; the beneficial outcome was more pronounced when an additional CAC gel was injected, suggesting the possibility of dosage adjustment by multiplexing. 2) The earlier data has been published as a research paper (Part C Section 8 #2) and presented (oral and poster) in international conferences (Part C Section 9 #1 - 3). The oral presentation for #3 won an award (Best Presentation, Runner-up in Visual Sciences, Part C Section 11). 3) The results on the newer injectable CAC design with the externally-controllable biosafety switch have been presented (oral and poster) in international conferences (Part C Section 9 #4 - 14) where several awards were received (#9 - Travel Award for ARVO-Asia, #10 Young Investigator Award, #12 - Best Paper Award, 3rd Prize, Part C Section 11). 4) Our contribution in the area of drug delivery is recognized and we have been invited to publish review articles (Part C Section 8 #1, 3) and a book chapter (accepted, Part C Section 8 #4). 5) Two students (a PhD and a MRes) in the Faculty of Medicine, The University of Hong Kong Have been trained in this research project (Part C Section 10), both of whom won several awards for their work (Part C Section 11). 6) We have compiled our data and a manuscript has been submitted to the journal PNAS (MS#2018-10746).

773613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
773613.value: Retinal degeneration and photoreceptor cell death are common in a number of eye diseases, including retinal detachment and retinitis pigmentosa. Therefore, therapeutic strategies that target photoreceptor cell death are considered attractive in having broad clinical applications. We have established and confirmed the morphological and functional rescue of photoreceptors in RCS rats with retinal degeneration when they received the collagen-alginate composite (CAC) gels. Our CAC drug delivery design provides a platform to show that it can be applied to deliver protein-based drugs using xenogenic cells in rodents. It is now timely to validate the potential applications of CAC gels using large eye animals (rabbits) for translational purposes. The work will support the beneficial role of CAC gel implantation using natural materials such as collagen and alginate, which could lead to an achievable and inexpensive therapy for eye disease with neuronal loss such as retinal detachment, retinitis pigmentosa, age-related macular degeneration, glaucoma, and ischemic retinopathies. The results will provide us with preliminary data for future grant applications.

773613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
773613.value: Encapsulated-cell therapy (ECT) is an attractive approach to treat blinding diseases by providing long-term local drug delivery and overcoming the need of repeated invasive drug injections. To address the performance and biosafety issues faced by these systems in clinical trials, we engineered an injectable gel platform with an externally-controllable biosafety switch. Our collagen-alginate composite gel design uses natural collagen I, which is a well conserved structural protein with excellent biocompatibility and negligible immunogenicity. The inclusion of alginate, a FDA-approved natural polymer widely used in drug delivery, prevents possible migration of the entrapped cells that can in turn elicit immunological reactions. Moreover, the biosafety switch allows the injected gel to be effectively terminated by an oral trigger (doxycycline) when required, but remain functional and viable for drug delivery applications. Most importantly, we showed that prolonged gel treatment achieved structural and functional rescue in rats with retinal degeneration and drug dosage could be adjusted by multiplexing. Furthermore, gels retrieved after six months of implantation exhibited robust biocompatibility, platform integrity and cell viability without immunosuppressants. This platform can potentially be engineered to deliver other protein drugs for treating an array of eye disorders in a safe and controllable manner.

774213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
774213.value: 在精子的發生過程中，發育中的生殖細胞需穿過由緊密連接（TJ）和黏着連接（AJ）形成的血睾屏障（BTB）而進入近腔室完成其成熟過程。血睾屏障將生精上皮分隔成基底室和近腔室，從而形成一種特殊的微環境將發育中的生殖細胞與體循環分隔開而避免自身免疫的發生，因此血睾屏障是生精上皮的一個重要結構。在生精上皮週期的特定階段，血睾屏障經歷動態重建過程以協助生殖細胞延生精上皮遷移。 血睾屏障的完整性由包括occludin、 claudin-11、連接黏附分子（JAM）以及柯薩奇病毒和腺病毒受體（CAR）在內的一系列跨膜蛋白所維持。一些研究表明，敲除claudin-11, occludin或者JAM其中任意一個蛋白就足以導致男性不育， 這似乎意味中任何一個細胞連接蛋白對於維持BTB的完整性和功能都是不可缺少的。體外研究發現，CAR在胚胎睾丸索和出生後的睾丸中表達，並且CAR也是構成BTB的細胞連接蛋白。在出生後睾丸中，CAR在位於BTB的支持細胞和遷移中的生殖細胞中均表達並且可能對協助生殖細胞穿過BTB有重要作用。然後，由於傳統方法敲除CAR導致胚胎死亡，所以直至目前CAR在睾丸中的生理學重要性仍未被探明。 與其他構成BTB的連接蛋白相似，我們發現促炎症細胞因子使CAR表達下調。我們於是假設CAR在BTB的表達和其他位於BTB的細胞連接蛋白由某共同的機制所調控，此機制使促炎症細胞因子在BTB發揮有效的破壞作用並在炎症發生過程中導致不育。 在本研究計劃中，項目負責人將鑑定CAR在睾丸胚胎發育和精子發生過程中的功能，以及其在炎症發生時的調控。本課題的研究目的，一是建立CAR敲除動物模型並在此模型基礎上研究CAR在睾丸中的功能；二是通過體內和體外研究闡明促炎症細胞因子IFN-和TNF對CAR表達的影響及其調控機制。本研究的成果將對理解BTB的結構功能以及生殖細胞的發育有著重大意義及貢獻。

774213.label: Realisation of objectives
774213.value: The objectives stated in the proposal have been extensively studied during the grant period. For objective 1, we successfully generated the SC-specific CAR knockout male mice (SC-Cxadr-/-) using the Cre/loxP system. Functional investigations, RNA sequencing, proteomics on SC-Cxadr-/- testes and in vitro Cxadr-depleted cell culture model were employed to identify and unravel the regulatory mechanisms involving in male reproductive impairment. For objective 2, an array of techniques including cell culture, transfection, siRNA knockdown, immunoprecipitation, immunofluorescence, ChIP assay and promoter assay has been employed to unravel the effects and regulatory mechanisms of pro-inflammatory cytokines, IFN-gamma and TNF alpha, on the expression of CAR in vitro

774213.label: Major findings and research outcome
774213.value: The Cre excision of Cxadr in SC-Cxadr-/- male mice was achieved under the control of SC-specific Amh gene. The deletion of CXADR was confirmed by PCR and immunohistochemistry. Adult SC-Cxadr-/- mice exhibited a 44% reduction in fertility efficacy, as well as the reduced ratio of testes/body weight observed from 120 days old onwards due to GC apoptosis and loss. Compromised BTB function also has been observed in SC-Cxadr-/- testes. An array of BTB components including occludin/ZO-1 complex and β-catenin were down-regulated or mislocalized in SC-Cxadr-/- seminiferous epithelia. Up-regulation of non-phosphorylated β-catenin and inhibition of Cdc42 were further found in SC-Cxadr-/- seminiferous epithelia with disorganized F-actin at the apical ES. Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses of SC-Cxadr-/- testes revealed that the enriched gene ontology (GO) terms of biological process indeed related to reproduction. Up-regulation of several Wnt targets were confirmed in Cxadr-depleted mouse testes or Sertoli cell line, including Wnt6 and Wnt9a. Combined the genome-wide data and functional analyses of SC-Cxadr-/- testes, the Rap1/Wnt/Hippo signaling network was identified and predicted to cause fertility impairment in the knockout mice. Apart from being a structural protein at the BTB, CXADR also served as the signaling mediator to trigger the downstream effects on junction disruption and actin reorganization via non-phosphorylation of β-catenin and Cdc42 inhibition. Interestingly, overexpression of constitutively active Cdc42 in Cxadr-depleted Sertoli cell line (MSC-1) model could partially recover the CXADR-mediated disorganization of F-actin filaments in vitro. We have studied the effect of IFNG and TNF (IFNG+TNF) on CAR in testicular cells. Combined treatment with IFNG+TNF exerted a synergistic effect by downregulating CAR mRNA and protein levels. Immunofluorescence staining revealed that IFNG+TNF treatment effectively removed CAR from cell–cell contact. IFNG+TNF treatment down-regulated CAR protein level via promoting CAR protein degradation by cycloheximide treatment. Using various inhibitors and co-immunoprecipitation analyses, we confirmed that IFNG+TNF-induced CAR degradation was mediated via ubiquitin-proteasome pathway. IFNG+TNF down-regulated CAR mRNA level, but it was not mediated by altering the stability of the transcript. To check whether IFNG+TNF reduces CAR mRNA level via gene transcription, 5’-deletion luciferase constructs were generated for promoter assays. The promoter region between nt -160 and -110 is crucial and responsive for IFNG+TNF-induced CAR gene repression. Mutational studies have shown that IFNG+TNF-induced CAR repression was achieved by suppression of basal transcription. EMSA and chromatin immunoprecipitation assays further confirmed that IFNG+TNF treatment inhibited binding of the basal transcription factors and promoted binding of NFKB subunits and Sp1 (negative regulators).

774213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
774213.value: Our current studies have clearly shown that Cxadr play important roles in serving as a structural transmembrane protein at the cell junctions and functioning as a signalling platform to other signalling molecules for other testicular cellular events. A thorough understanding on how Cxadr maintains spermatogenesis and how Cxadr serves as a signal platform are of great important during spermatogenesis Data obtained from knockout model model and integrated comics analyses enable us to design the in vitro models to further elucidate the potential involvement of Cxadr in regulating various events other than junction restructuring during spermatogenesis in the testis. Further detailed investigation in the area is warranted and it definitely will shed new light in understanding unexplained male infertility.

774213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
774213.value: In this study, the function of Cxadr and its regulation have been examined. We have identified the cytokines such as IFNG+TNF and respective signalling pathways involved in regulating the expression of Cxadr so as to regulate the junction restructuring in the seminiferous epithelium required for germ cell development. The in vivo Cxadr knockout model clearly demonstrated that Cxadr is a key structural protein and a signalling dock to transduce signalling. The results obtained from this study make crucial contribution to the understanding of Cxadr during spermatogenesis. In fact, the findings are not be limited to testicular physiology since Cxadr are junction proteins that can be found in other tissues. Our studies serve as blueprints for other tissue models. This study provides two novel pieces of information that Cxadr is in fact important transmembrane protein that facilitates cell adhesion and it serves as a signaling platform in germ cell development.

774413.label: Realisation of objectives
774413.value: 1. To elucidate the functional role of ECM1a and ECM1b in ESCC, we first examined their expression in ESCC. Our RNA-seq analysis showed that both ECM1a and ECM1b are down-regulated in ESCC tissue samples compared to normal tissue controls. ECM1b is down-regulated more significantly than ECM1a. ECM1b is also highly down-regulated in our previous ESCC oligonucleotide microarray analysis and a publicly available ESCC cDNA microarray analysis. We used lentiviral transduction to efficiently express ECM1a and ECM1b in a panel of ESCC cell lines and injected the cells subcutaneously in a nude mouse tumorigenesis model; only ECM1b-expressing cells show the tumor suppression effect. Therefore, we focused on ECM1b for further testing. To test the effect on metastasis in vivo, we applied an experimental metastasis nude mouse tail-vein injection model using a well-established metastatic ESCC cell line KYSE150. However, ECM1b-expressing KYSE150 cells did not induce significant lung metastasis suppression effects. To further elucidate the tumor suppressive effect observed in vivo, we performed various in vitro assays to test the proliferation, cell growth, apoptosis, and migration/invasion of ECM1b-expressing cells compared to a GFP-expressing control. We also profiled the gene expression signature related to angiogenesis and EMT. The most consistent and significant finding was that ECM1b suppresses cancer cell growth. 2. To study the mechanistic insight of how ECM1b suppresses cell growth, we first performed geneset analyses using publicly available ESCC cDNA microarray and RNA-seq data. We found that ECM1 expression is significantly reversely correlated with c-myc targets and MTORC1 signaling in ESCC. These two signaling pathways are well-known cell growth regulators. Therefore, we examined c-myc expression and MTORC1 signaling in ECM1b-expressing ESCC cancer cell lines. We found that ECM1b expression suppresses c-myc protein expression and Akt/MTORC1 signaling. We confirmed by RNA profiling and protein degradation inhibitor assays that ECM1b did not regulate c-myc transcription or protein degradation. We showed that EGF treatment rescues ECM1b-induced c-myc protein expression suppression. We confirmed by expression of a constitutively active AKT construct that regulation of MTORC1 signaling by ECM1b is AKT-dependent; the constitutively active AKT pathway compensates partially for the tumor suppression by ECM1b. We also found that knockout of ECM1 enhances c-myc expression and MTORC1 signaling in a normal immortalized esophageal epithelial cell line. We examined the subcellular localization of ECM1b by immunofluorescent staining and subcellular fractionation. ECM1b shows colocalization with the endoplasmic reticulum. These data suggest ECM1b suppresses c-myc expression and Akt/MTORC1 signaling, likely through regulation of MTORC2 pathway in the endoplasmic reticulum to regulate cell growth. Inspired by a previous study showing p63 silencing increases ECM1 RNA expression, we examined the role of p63 in regulating ECM1b expression in ESCC. We showed that p63 knockout increases ECM1b RNA expression in ESCC cell lines; the p63 knockout suppresses c-myc protein expression and Akt/MTORC1 signaling, phenocopying ECM1b expression in ESCC cell lines. Expression of p63 also shows positive correlation with the c-myc target and MTORC1 signaling in geneset analyses using public RNA-seq ESCC data. These data suggest ECM1b plays a role in p63-related c-myc and MTORC1 signaling regulation. The C-myc pathway and MTORC1 signaling both have been associated with chemoresistance in cancer. We then showed by cell viability assays that ECM1b expression increases sensitivity to cisplatin treatment in ESCC cell lines.

774413.label: Major findings and research outcome
774413.value: The current study verified the tumor suppressive role of ECM1b in ESCC using both well-controlled in vivo and in vitro functional and molecular assays. Only the ECM1b variant, but not the other ECM1 variant ECM1a was able to suppress tumor growth and induce anti-cancer effects. In an in vitro cell culture model, ECM1b expression leads to reduced cell growth. The molecular mechanism of tumor suppression associated with ECM1b was also analyzed. ECM1b suppresses c-myc expression and MTORC1 signaling, both well-known for regulating cell growth. Geneset analyses using publicly available data also showed that ECM1 expression negatively correlates with c-myc target and MTORC1 signaling in ESCC. ECM1b regulates c-myc through translation, but not transcription or protein degradation. ECM1b regulates MTORC1 signaling through AKT, as expression of constitutively active AKT counteracts the MTORC1 molecular alterations and tumor suppression by ECM1b. ECM1b was also found to colocalize with the endoplasmic reticulum. The regulation of ECM1b expression was also examined. TP63 was found to negatively regulate ECM1b expression and to positively regulate c-myc expression and MTORC1 signaling in ESCC cell lines. TP63 expression was also found to positively correlate with c-myc targets and MTORC1 signaling in geneset analyses using public data in ESCC. We also showed that ECM1b expression increases sensitivity to cisplatin treatment in ESCC cell lines. A manuscript based on this research project was published in 2015 in BioMed Research International for the orthotopic animal model. A second manuscript is now in preparation and aims at high impact cancer research journals. The results of this project have been presented in the form of poster presentation in a renowned international cancer research conference, the American Association for Cancer Research Annual Meeting 2016, held in the United States.

774413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
774413.value: The current results suggest a regulatory role of ECM1b on two critical oncogenic pathways: c-myc pathway and MTORC1 signaling, both well-known for regulating cell growth and also for drug-resistance. Therapeutic potential for targeting the c-myc pathway and MTORC1 signaling has long been proposed as important anti-cancer approaches. ECM1b may then serve as a biomarker for c-myc and/or MTORC1-related signaling. Large-scale ESCC patient tissue sample analyses using methods such as immunohistochemical staining are needed to further verify this possible utility of the findings from this project. The current study also suggested a role of ECM1b in TP63-mediated oncogenic functions. TP63 has been proposed to play a critical role in ESCC tumorigenesis. The current study provides insight into TP63-mediated pro-cancer roles in ESCC development. Further detailed functional and molecular analysis is needed to elucidate the molecular events in ESCC tumor initiation and progression.

774413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
774413.value: We studied the tumor suppressive effect of the gene ECM1 in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, a form of esophageal cancer highly prevalent in the Chinese population. We found that one specific variant of the gene, ECM1b, possesses anti-cancer function. We performed various assays to analyze how ECM1b suppresses tumor development to exert its anti-cancer effects. We found that ECM1b regulates the activities of critical cell growth-promoting molecular players inside cancer cells. These findings increase our understanding of esophageal cancer progression and allow future development of biomarker and therapeutic applications to aid in the diagnosis and targeted treatment of esophageal cancer to improve clinical outcomes.

774513.label: Realisation of objectives
774513.value: We investigated the clinical significance, functional role, and therapeutic implications of annexin A3 (ANXA3) in CD133+ liver cancer stem cell (CSC)-driven hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). We identified caveolin-1-dependent endocytosis to mediate internalization of secretory ANXA3 into HCC cells, thereby activating a dysregulated JNK pathway to promote CSC-like properties. We also developed a monoclonal antibody specific against ANXA3 (anti-ANXA3 mAb) and showed in vivo that the use of this antibody alone or in combination with cisplatin could efficiently lead to a reduced ability of HCC cells to initiate tumor growth and self-renewal, concomitant with a decrease in liver CSC proportions. Specifically, we report: 1) Transcriptome sequencing profiling identifies ANXA3 to be preferentially expressed in the CD133+ liver CSC subset. 2) Endogenous and secretory ANXA3 overexpression to be tightly associated with HCC pathogenesis. 3) Endogenous ANXA3 regulates both cancer and stem cell-like properties in HCC. 4) ANXA3 contributes to augmented tumorigenic and metastatic phenotype and is critical for growth and maintenance of the CD133+ liver CSC subset. 5) Secretory ANXA3 confers tumorigenic, metastatic and self-renewal abilities in HCC. 6) Exogenous ANXA3 is internalized through caveolin-1 dependent endocytosis. 7) ANXA3 induces a feed-forward loop that is mediated by the MKK4/JNK signaling cascade. 8) ANXA3 neutralization suppresses growth and self-renewal of HCC in vivo, sensitives HCC to chemotherapy, and eradicates the CD133 liver CSC subset. Please kindly refer to our publication for further details: Tong M, Fung TM, Luk ST, Ng KY, Lee TK, Lin CH, Yam JY, Chan KW, Ng F, Zheng BJ, Yuan YF, Xie D, Lo CM, Man K, Guan XY, Ma S. ANXA3/JNK signaling promotes self-renewal and tumor growth, and its blockade provides a therapeutic target for hepatocellular carcinoma. Stem Cell Reports 2015; 5: 45-59. All proposed objectives have been achieved. Work for the project was primarily carried out by a then PhD candidate Ms. Man TONG under the supervision of Dr. Stephanie Ma (PI).

774513.label: Major findings and research outcome
774513.value: Frequent tumor relapse in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has been commonly attributed to the presence of residual cancer stem cells (CSCs) after conventional treatments. We have previously identified and characterized CD133 to mark a specific CSC subset in HCC. In the present study, we found endogenous and secretory annexin A3 (ANXA3) to play pivotal roles in promoting cancer and stem cell-like features in CD133+ liver CSCs through a dysregulated JNK pathway. Blockade of ANXA3 with an anti-ANXA3 monoclonal antibody in vitro as well as in human HCC xenograft models resulted in a significant reduction in tumor growth and self-renewal. Clinically, ANXA3 expression in HCC patient sera closely associated with aggressive clinical features. Our results suggest that ANXA3 can serve as a novel diagnostic biomarker and that the inhibition of ANXA3 may be a viable therapeutic option for the treatment of CD133+ liver-CSC-driven HCC. 774513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
774513.value: We are currently exploring on the role of ANXA3 in conferring sorafenib resistance in HCC. This is a project that continues on the interesting leads identified from the current funded project.

774513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
774513.value: Collectively, findings presented in this study provide evidence to show the clinical relevance, functional significance, and therapeutic implication of both endogenous and secretory ANXA3 in CD133+ liver CSCs and HCC. We believe that ANXA3 can be used as a novel biomarker for the better detection of HCC and that targeting ANXA3 can be potentially developed as a novel treatment regime for this disease.
