775113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
775113.value: As osseointegrated dental implants have become the mainstream treatment for complete edentulism, there is a growing number of patients with implant-supported Fixed Dental Prostheses (FDP). Such treatments have significantly improved patients' quality of life and are often regarded as a "gold standard". However, implant-supported FDPs are still plagued by a high number of complications, which affect as many as 40% of the reconstructions within the first 5 years. The management of such complications demands time and expensive interventions, while in some cases it can threaten the survival of the reconstruction. Research has shown that the most frequently encountered complications in implant supported FDPs involve a) fracture of the ceramic or acrylic veneer and b) loosening or fracture of abutment screws. There is at present very little evidence as to the factors that predispose or lead to such frequent technical failures. Recent pilot data indicated that “passive fitness” of the metal framework to the implant anchorage is hardly ever achieved in clinical conditions and a certain degree of misfit is to be expected. Even a minor misfit will place the reconstruction under strain, which will lead to certain degree of deformation. Such a deformation could impact the implant-abutment interface and the interface between the metal framework and the different layers of the veneer material. However, the threshold of tolerance of the FDP, as well as the implications of the strain caused by misfit for the long-term success of the reconstruction remain unknown. Research has indicated that FDP design, implant number and locations, abutment-joint design and abutment screw material can influence the results of strain on the reconstruction and are also related to the extend, frequency and type of complications. Finite Element Analysis (FEA) is a process, which can reliably reconstruct complex technical structures and predict the impact of different forces on the mechanical components. The proposed project aims to reproduce the actual micromorphology of popular commercially available abutments through slicing and Scaning Electromicroscopy and then simulate clinical conditions encountered in a full arch FDP with different degrees of misfit through Finite Element Analysis, including critical variables related to the FDP and the abutment design. The outcomes of this project will produce some novel understanding of the mechanisms that lead to technical failures, will identify restoration designs that are more resistant to problems from misfit and will help clinicians predict, prevent and effectively treat a large number of commonly encountered problems. 隨著骨整合種植體已經成爲全口無牙患者的主要治療方式，越來越多的患者接受種植體支持的固定義齒（FDP）修複。這種修複治療顯著改善病人生活質量，並經常被看作“金標准”。然而，FDP仍存在很多並發症影響其應用，這些並發症會影響治療後首年0％的重建。治療這些並發症耗時耗錢，而且有些病例出現的並發症會威脅到重建的成活率。 本科研項目研究目的爲利用磨片和掃描電鏡複制市場上流行的種植體基台的實際超微形態結構，並利用有限元分析技術模擬臨床上遇到的全牙列FDP各種角度的不適合，包括與FDP和基台相關的關鍵變量。該研究結果將對FDP技術失敗産生一些新的認識，確定能夠防止出現不適合問題的修複體設計，以及幫助臨床醫生預測，防止並有效治療大量的常見問題。

775113.label: Realisation of objectives
775113.value: The objectives of the study have been achieved to a very high extent, with some final analysis still underway and the last of the critical results being expected soon. The slicing of the different implant-abutment junctions has been completed and included a total of 12 different implant abutment units (3 anaysed in paper 1, -Mattheos et al 2016) 3 in paper 2 (Mattheos et al 2017) and further 6 in paper 4 (Fokas et al 2017 in press). The results of the slices analysis in Scanning electron microscopy were used to develop the Finite Element Analysis models which were analysed individually (paper 1) and then combined into a 3-unit implant supported bridge for final analysis of clinically relevant scenaria. In detail: Objective 1: This objective has been approached in 2 different ways: a) through the development of a real model tested in-vitro (paper 3, Lofgren et al 2017), which investigated the impact of misfit of 150 μm under cyclical load with significant results (100% complete). b) through the development of a FEA model with the same microstructure and further testing for the impact of misfit of 200, 150, 100 and 50 μm (paper 5 Mattheos et al, currently in preparation). As the results were revealing the possibility for even minor misfits to influence clinical outcomes, we are currently analysing further for misfit of 10, 20 and 30 μm while also replicating the analysis for different materials (80% completion). Objective 2: This objective is completed, as both the results of in-vitro testing (papers 2 and 3) as well as the FEA have so far revealed consistent types and location of complications under load in the presence of misfit (100 % complete). Objective 3: This objective is partially completed from the in vitro and FEA studies, but the final FEA analysis is anticipated to offer a better insight with regards to the different parametres and their impact (80% Completion) .

775113.label: Major findings and research outcome
775113.value: The slicing and SEM measurements on 12 different implant-abutment units revealed significant differences in the design and micromorphology between the different units that were analysed (studies 1,4) and offered realistic understanding of the actual (and not the ideal) configuration of the components. Further construction of Finite Element Analysis 3D models and subsequent analysis of the behavior of the units under different clinically loading scenaria, confirmed that the differences in the micromorphology and tight contact can lead to different preformance under clinical scenaria and predispose to technical complications (studies 1, 5) . Selected single unit implant abutment configurations with different fit and micromorphology were tested in-vitro under cyclical load of 2 million cycles, without however observing significant differences in the prevalence of complications (study 2). Among the limitations of this study however were the relatively small number of samples tested, small number of cycles and axial loading conditions, unlike some other in-vitro testing standards where the loading comes at 30 degrees. However, when misfit was tested in-vitro with a 5-unit implant supported bridge (3 implants), the results indicated a significant increase in technical complications, even with a small number of chewing cycles (study 3). This fact combined with the results of study 2, is indicative of how the increase of complexity of the reconstruction can significantly "amplify" the clinical implications of differences in micromorphology and misfit. As the in-vitro testing was however unable to test a large array of misfit configuration, due to budget and time feasibility (study 3). Consequently, the final stage is the FEA reproduction of the identical settings and repeating the analysis for an array of misfit settings from 200 μm (as used in-vitro), to 150, 100, 50, 30, 20, and 10 μm. The analysis of the 200-50 μm is completed and points out to a non-linear relation between the extent of misfit and the prevalence of complications, while a misfit of only 150 μm (something previously considered widely as clinically acceptable)m was found to be detrimental. Therefore the last few analyses were decided (30,20,10 μm) in order to completely understand the extent of misfit that can be tolerated and where the margins of destructive influence occur.

775113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
775113.value: The collaboration with Malmo University has enriched the project with the expretise related to in-vitro testing and with the authentic FEA analysis models already developed, there is a great potential for creating and testing different clinically relevant scenaria and configurations of implant prosthesis. The coupling of testing the same model both through FEA and in-vitro has helped us to relate the outcomes and document the potential of FEA to actually predict the clinical performance of mechanical components, sotheing that was not done before. In the future, we aim to further develop this collaboration aiming to test more complex clinical scenaria and components, hopefully increasing our understanding of both the function of micromorphological elements as well as damaging misfit. This could help to design and deliver more predictable reconstructions and prevent or minimise technical problems and implant / prosthesis failures.

775113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
775113.value: Implant therapy is today well established, while expectations for long term success of the prosthesis have increased. At the same time, technical complications of implant prosthesis are reportedly affecting as many as 60% of the patients. The abutment is the critical interface between the prosthesis and the implant anchorage. There is currently a large number of manufactirers of implant abutments, but little knowledge how the micromorphology of the abutment and potential misfit can impact the long term stability of the prosthesis. This project through a series of slicing and microscopical observation has provided a authentic picture of the implant abutment configuration, which was then used in order to reconstruct authentic 3D models. The models where analysed in computer simulating actual clinical conditions, while selected implant configurations were further analysed in real conditions. Matching the computer analysis with the in-vitro tests has helped us identify the detrimental impact that even minor misfit of 150 μm can have on the implant prosthesis, even if that level of misfit was deemed in the past as acceptable. Further analyses with the developed models can help us identify more compromised scenaria and lead to making implant prostheses that are more stable and longer lasting.

775313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
775313.value: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease that affects predominantly young women and is more frequent among Chinese compared to whites. This disease is characterized by immune-complex deposition causing inflammation and damage to internal organs. Current therapy involving corticosteroid and immunosuppressants are associated with significant side effects. There is a compelling need to identify biological target for immunotherapy in SLE. The pathogenesis of lupus is believed to involve defective regulation of both innate and adaptive immune responses. We have previously shown that macrophages in SLE patients are less efficient in clearance of dead cells, thus providing a source of autoantigens for development of autoimmunity. In lupus nephritis, macrophages infiltrate kidneys early and produce pro-inflammatory cytokines causing local inflammation and attract migration of T and B cells that are responsible for adaptive immunity. In this study, we hypothesize that interleukin (IL)-33, a novel innate cytokine, has potential therapeutic effect on lupus disease via its immunomodulatory function on macrophages and T cells. IL-33 has been shown to polarize macrophages to M2 phenotype and to mediate T-helper (Th)-2 response, both are associated with anti-inflammatory effects. Furthermore, our preliminary data revealed that M2 macrophages from normal mouse strain can induce differentiation of regulatory T cells (Treg) which play an important role in immune tolerance. In a pilot study, we found that lupus prone mice given intraperitoneal IL-33 developed less proteinuria compared to control mice. Indeed, we have recently found higher level of soluble IL-33 receptor in lupus serum that correlated with disease activity, suggesting a role of this cytokine in the pathogenesis of human SLE. In this project, we seek to (1) establish a role of IL-33 in disease attenuation in lupus mouse model via its immunomodulatory effect on macrophages and T cells, (2) to delineate M2 macrophages and M2 induced Treg as the underlying mechanisms and (3) to evaluate the clinical relevance of IL-33, M2 macrophages and Treg in relation to renal inflammation and damage in human lupus nephritis. We will examine disease activity, phenotypes of systemic and tissue macrophages and T cells in IL-33 treated lupus mice and delineate the underlying mechanisms by adoptive transfer of IL-33 generated M2 macrophages and M2 induced Treg. We will examine the clinical relevance of IL-33 in relation to abundance of M2 macrophages and Treg and the histological severity of inflammation and damage on renal tissue from patients with active lupus nephritis. 白介素-33對巨噬細胞的演化和免疫調節功能在系統性紅斑狼瘡症病理機制的作用 系統性紅斑狼瘡症是一種自體免疫病，由免疫複合物沉積於身體內臟器官，引起炎症及損害。系統性紅斑狼瘡症主要影響年輕婦女，與白人相比，中國人更為常見。目前用於系統性紅斑狼瘡症的主要治療藥物包括皮質類固醇和免疫抑製劑，兩者均有相當顯著的副作用。因此，有需要對系統性紅斑狼瘡病的發病機制作多方面的研究，以發現相關的細胞或細胞因子可用作新的免疫生物標靶治療。我們先前的研究顯示，系統性紅斑狼瘡患者巨噬細胞於清除凋亡細胞的效率較正常人低，過剩的凋亡細胞成為自身抗原的來源。而且，巨噬細胞在狼瘡性腎炎中最早出現並且浸潤腎臟，產生炎性細胞因子，引起腎臟發炎和吸引後天免疫T細胞和B細胞遷移腎臟，增加炎症。白介素-33是一種近期發現的先天細胞因子，可誘導巨噬細胞演化成具抗炎功能的M2型巨噬細胞，以及對T細胞誘導成抗炎的Th-2反應，因而對免疫調節功能有影響。而且，我們初步發現M2型巨噬細胞可誘導調節性T細胞。因此，我們推測白介素-33通過對巨噬細胞和T細胞的免疫調節影響，對狼瘡疾病具有潛在的治療效果。我們這項研究目的，（1）從白介素-33對巨噬細胞和T細胞的免疫調節作用，調查其在狼瘡小鼠發病機制的影響，（2）探測M2巨噬細胞和其2誘導的調節性T細胞於狼瘡小鼠發病的相關機制，以及（3）評估人類狼瘡性腎炎中白介素-33、M2巨噬細胞和調節性T細胞與腎臟炎症和損壞的臨床相關性。

775313.label: Realisation of objectives
775313.value: As one of the recently identified members of the IL-1 cytokine family and an alarmin, IL-33 has been reported to possess dual pro- and anti-inflammatory effects in different disease conditions. We sought to examine the effect of IL-33 on systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), a prototypic multi-systemic autoimmune disease, and the underlying cellular mechanisms. Our study aimed to examine (1) the role of IL-33 in disease attenuation in murine lupus erythematosus, (2) the role of anti-inflammatory M2 macrophage and regulatory T cells (Treg) as the underlying mechanisms for the immunomodulatory effect of IL-33, and (3) the relationship between IL-33, M2 macrophages and Treg in lupus nephritis in human SLE patients. To address the role of IL-33 in disease attenuation in murine lupus, we started by examining the effect of IL-33 on the phenotype of MRL/lpr, murine lupus-prone mice week 12 of age, when they are expected to develop early disease. We tested out different injection protocols of recombinant mouse IL-33 and eventually selected an administration protocol that involved injection frequency 3 times per week for 6 weeks which was comparable to previous studies that demonstrated biological effects of IL-33 in other chronic disease models. We used both 1% Bovine serum albumin and PBS as diluent for IL-33 and control groups. 1% BSA as diluent for IL-33 and control groups brought about more obvious changes in clinical features including skin rash and proteinuria and was adopted for examination of IL-33 effect on disease phenotype. Parallel experiments were performed using PBS as diluent for IL-33 and control for immunophenotyping of immune cells. As expected, control mice developed progressive hair loss, skin rash and proteinuria. IL-33 treated mice had ameliorated disease including milder hair loss examined semi-quantitatively as skin score, less proteinuria by albustix and quantitative protein assay. There were significantly fewer glomerular proliferative changes, hyaline deposits and crescents in renal histology by H&E staining. This phenotype of milder disease paralleled the findings of reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine expression (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6) in the kidneys as detected by quantitative PCR. Multiplex bead immunoassay also showed lower serum pro-inflammatory cytokines including TNF-α, IL-6 and IL-17. These data suggested that IL-33 possessed systemic and local anti-inflammatory effects in lupus disease. However, humoral immune response was not affected by IL-33. Serum antibody levels including anti-double stranded DNA antibodies, anti-BSA antibodies and total IgG measured by ELISA were not different between IL-33 treated and control groups. C3 deposits in glomeruli as evaluated by immunofluorescence was similar. To address the first objective of the study, this data showed that IL-33 possessed disease attenuation effect on murine lupus. IL-33 was first characterized by its Th2 promoting effects but has subsequently been found to possess more diverse effects on various immune cells. To delineate M2 macrophages and Treg as the underlying cellular mechanisms mediating the immunomodulatory effects of IL-33, we examined phenotype of splenic and renal macrophages and T cells in IL-33 treated mice. In the kidneys, there was significant skewing in mRNA expression profile towards anti-inflammatory M2 macrophages with upregulated ArgI, Ym-1, FIZZI and IL-10 and downregulated iNOS. There was also upregulated Foxp3, transcription factor of regulatory T cells (Treg) and reduced tbx21 and rorc, transcription factors for Th1 and Th17 respectively. Same features were observed in splenocytes and isolated CD11b+ splenocytes in IL-33 treated mice compared to controls. There was significant expansion of splenic Treg as reflected by higher CD4+CD25+, Foxp3+/CD4+CD25+ and Foxp3+CD25+/CD4+ populations by flow cytometry. These Treg expressed significantly higher level of ST2, the IL-33 receptor, suggesting autoregulation by IL-33. We originally sought to validate the role of Treg and M2 macrophages mediating the effect of IL-33 on murine lupus by adoptive transfer experiments. We adoptive transferred splenic CD4+CD25+ Treg from IL-33 treated lupus mice in two injections (week 12 and week 15 of recipient) to recipient mice of age week 12 and serially examined phenotype of recipient lupus mice. However, there was significant variation in the observed effect of the transferred Treg on proteinuria, which was partly related to transfer of the studied mice and breeders to a different animal facility when the PI changed to the new institution. To overcome the suboptimal observation of ex vivo Treg transfer on the phenotype of the recipient mice, we examined for immunomodulatory phenotype and functions of Treg and macrophages under the effect of IL-33 in in vitro experiments. We found that IL-33 promoted IL-4 primed M2 macrophage polarization with increased expression of M2 mRNA transcript CD206 and ArgI, produced significantly higher anti-inflammatory IL-10 and suppressed allogeneic T cell proliferation. Treating IFN-γ- and LPS- induced classical macrophages with IL-4 and IL-33 led to enhanced production of TGF-β. Treating IL-4 and IL-33- induced macrophages with TGF-β led to reduction in IL-6 production upon IFN-γ and LPS challenge, and suppressed T cell proliferation in a dose-dependent manner. In co-culture experiments, IL-4 stimulated macrophages promoted CD4+ T cell differentiation into Foxp3- and CD25- expressing Treg, which were further enhanced by adding IL-33. IL-33 and IL-4 treated macrophages also demonstrated suppressive effect on T cell proliferation, and the co-cultured T cells produced negligible IFN-γ and IL-17 as measured by ELISA. On the other hand, IL-33 promoted CD4+ T cells differentiation into Treg with higher CD25 MFI in TGF-β and IL-2- inducing condition but not upon treatment with IL-33 alone. These induced Treg had stable Foxp3 expression upon challenge by T cell receptor stimulation for 48 hours. TGF-β production by Treg was negligible but was detectable by ELISA upon addition of IL-33. To address the second objective of the study, these data demonstrated that IL-33 possessed direct potentiation effect on Treg differentiation in the presence of TGF-β and IL-2, and Treg may also be induced indirectly by alternatively activated macrophages induced by synergistic effects of IL-33 and IL-4. Lastly, we studied the relationship of Treg, macrophages and IL-33 in lupus nephritis. As we had restricted access to human renal tissue archive after the PI changed to new institution, we resolved to examine expression of Treg and macrophages in the kidneys of IL-33 treated and control mice by immunohistochemical analysis. We found Foxp3- expressing Treg among perivascular infiltrate in kidney sections of IL-33 treated mice, which is in close proximity with Iba+ expressing macrophages. Iba marker was used for macrophages as we failed to stain F4/80 and CD206 despite various antigen retrieval methods. To address to the third objective of the study, this data demonstrated interaction between IL-33 induced Treg and macrophages in murine lupus nephritis. In conclusion, our data showed that IL-33 ameliorated renal inflammation and proteinuria in murine lupus, with in vivo evidence of expansion of Treg and M2 macrophage polarization. IL-33 demonstrated direct induction effect of Treg in vitro and expansion of Treg in vivo under autoregulation as these Treg had upregulated level of ST2. In addition, IL-33 potentiated IL-4 induced polarization of M2 macrophages, which were capable of inducing more Foxp3- expressing Treg, providing a positive amplification loop reinforcing the immunomodulatory effects of IL-33. Thus, our study demonstrated that IL-33 treatment attenuated murine lupus disease by induction of M2 macrophages and Treg, suggesting that IL-33 may be a potential novel therapeutic option in the treatment of SLE.

775313.label: Major findings and research outcome
775313.value: As a recent identified member of the IL-1 cytokine family, IL-33 has been revealed to possess dual pro- and anti-inflammatory effects on various immune cells and different disease conditions. Our study aimed to examine the role of IL-33 on systemic lupus erythematosus, a prototypic autoimmune disease and to delineate the underlying cellular mechanisms. Our study showed that recombinant IL-33 had ameliorating effect on pre-diseased lupus-prone MRL/lpr mice resulting in milder hair loss, significantly less proteinuria, milder glomerular and tubular inflammatory score, and lower mRNA level of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6) in the kidneys compared to controls. Immunohistochemical examination revealed Foxp3-expressing cells among Iba+ expressing macrophages in the perivascular infiltrates in the kidneys of IL-33 treated mice. Systemically, IL-33 treated mice had significantly lower serum levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6 and IL-17). However, antibody responses including serum anti-dsDNA antibodies and IgG levels were not affected by IL-33. Next, we demonstrated that IL-33 induced regulatory T cells (Treg) and polarization towards anti-inflammatory M2 macrophages were cellular mechanisms mediating its ameliorating effects on murine lupus. Extracts of kidney, spleen and isolated splenic CD11b+ monocytes showed skewed mRNA expression of M2 macrophage including upregulation of ArgI, Ym-1, FIZZI and IL-10 and downregulation of iNOS. IL-33 treated mice had increased splenic Treg which expressed significantly higher level of ST2, the IL-33 receptor, with reduced IFN-γ expressing CD4+ cells. We demonstrated potentiating effects of IL-33 on induction of M2 macrophages and Treg and their interaction in vitro. IL-33 promoted IL-4 primed bone marrow derived macrophages to M2 macrophages which expressed significantly higher CD206 and ArgI. These macrophages induced significantly higher CD25 and Foxp3 expression in co-cultured T cells and suppressed proliferation of allogeneic T cells with negligible IFN-γ and IL-17 production. In the presence of anti-inflammatory TGF-β, these macrophages suppressed allogenic T cell proliferation and IL-6 production. Combination of IL-4 and IL-33 treatment of classically activated macrophages induced by IFN-γ and LPS produced more TGF-β. While these results suggested that IL-33 promoted Treg induction via alternatively activated macrophages, IL-33 also showed direct induction effect on Treg from conventional T cells under IL-2 and TGF-β inducing condition with upregulated expression of CD25 and Foxp3. In conclusion, our study demonstrated that IL-33 ameliorated murine lupus disease mediated by M2 macrophage polarization and induction of Treg under autoregulation. IL-33 possessed direct effect on Treg induction, and indirectly via its potentiating effect on M2 macrophage polarization, which contribute to immunomodulatory effects of IL-33.

775313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
775313.value: Our data demonstrated that IL-33 ameliorated lupus disease via induction of Treg under autoregulation. Recent literature unravels a distinct tissue-resident population of Treg which express ST2. They reside predominantly in non-lymphoid tissues and possessed different gene expression profile. Thus, it is intriguing to know (1) whether there is any difference in the phenotype and function between IL-33 induced ST2+ Treg in lymphoid tissue, constitutively expressed tissue resident ST2+Treg in lymphoid and non-lymphoid tissue and ST2- Treg in lymphoid tissue; and as IL-33 upregulated ST2 expression on Treg, (2) how is the epigenetic control of activation and stabilisation of Foxp3, Treg transcription factor, under the effect of IL-33 in relation to other transcription factors found in ST2+ Treg such as Gata3, St2 and Batf. We plan to characterize the phenotype, function and gene expression profile of splenic and non-lymphoid ST2+ Treg in comparison to splenic ST2- Treg in IL-33 treated and control lupus mice, and the phenotype, function and gene expression profile of inducible Treg (iTreg) under TGF-β and IL-2 polarising condition in vitro in the presence or absence of IL-33; and to examine the epigenetic regulation of Foxp3 in relation to other reported ST2+ Treg transcription factors by chromatin immunoprecipitation in the presence or absence of IL-33.

775313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
775313.value: IL-33 is a novel cytokine that has recently been shown to possess diverse effects on various immune cells and is linked to various disease conditions. We have previously found elevated serum level of IL-33 receptor in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), an autoimmune disease affecting predominantly young women. Elevated IL-33 receptor level correlated with SLE disease activity suggesting involvement of IL-33 in the lupus pathogenesis. In this study, we examined the effect of exogenous administration of recombinant IL-33 to murine lupus mice and the underlying cellular mechanisms. Our study showed that IL-33 treated mice had milder lupus disease including hair loss, proteinuria and kidney inflammation. Serum, spleen and kidney examination revealed a less pro-inflammatory state compared to control mice. The underlying beneficial effect of IL-33 was mediated by induction of regulatory T cells (Treg) and anti-inflammatory macrophages. Indeed, in vitro experiments showed that IL-33 induced Treg from conventional T cells, and IL-33-modulated macrophages acquired anti-inflammatory functions, which also indirectly induce Treg, enhancing its immunomodulatory effect. As SLE is characterized by defective regulation of immune system with inflammation in multiple internal organs, IL-33 may be a potential immunotherapy in the treatment of this disease.

775513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
775513.value: Liver cancer (hepatocellular carcinoma, HCC) is a major malignancy worldwide and the second commonest fatal cancer in China including Hong Kong. Despite definite improvements in the outcome of patients with HCC, the overall prognosis of this cancer is still unsatisfactory because of late presentation and frequent tumor recurrence after surgical resection. New adjuvant treatment modalities for HCC are much awaited. Oncogenic activation of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway is common in HCC. We have a long-standing interest in this important pathway. From our and others’ previous data, β-catenin overexpression in human HCC is frequent (50-68%) but somatic mutations of β-catenin much less frequent (12-40%). This indicates that factors other than β-catenin mutation contribute to β-catenin activation and the upstream players in this pathway play important roles in hepatocarcinogenesis. Leucine-rich repeat-containing G-protein-coupled receptor (LGR5) is a novel co-receptor of the Wnt signaling pathway. The Lgr5 gene encodes an orphan 7-transmembrane protein, and R-spondins function as ligands of LGR5 to regulate Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Importantly, LGR5 has been identified as a marker of cycling stem cells in several epithelial tissues, including the small intestine, colon, and stomach. Very recently, Lgr5 has been identified as a selective marker for human colorectal cancer stem cells. Our preliminary data in HCC have shown that Lgr5 is variably expressed in a panel of HCC cell lines and is overexpressed in 30% of HCC samples from HCC patients. Using the reporter assay, we have observed that R-spondin1 greatly enhances the Wnt3a-mediated Wnt/β-catenin signaling in HCC cells, whereas knockdown of Lgr5 abolishes this activation. Importantly, knockdown of LGR5 reduces the hepatosphere formation ability in HCC cells, which is an assay of self-renewal ability as for cancer stem cells. In this proposal, we hypothesize that the Wnt target Lgr5 is a marker for liver cancer stem cells and hyperactivates oncogenic Wnt signaling pathway predisposing to HCC formation. We will evaluate the clinical significance of Lgr5 in HCC and its role as liver cancer stem cells. We propose to 1) evaluate the expression and clinical significance of Lgr5 in HCC; 2) delineate the role of Lgr5 as a marker of liver cancer stem cell; and 3) examine its effects on hepatocarcinogenesis using liver-specific knockout and chemical carcinogenesis anaimal models. 775513.label: Realisation of objectives
775513.value: All the objectives were realized. We showed that the LGR5 promoter activity was enhanced by a post-translational modification of Dishevelled-3 (Dvl3). This in turn resulted in the upregulation of LGR5 expression in human hepatocellular carcinomas (HCCs). The upregulated LGR5 expression was associated with increased cancer stemness in HCC, which we demonstrated with the in vitro sphere formation assays and in vivo tumorigenicity assays in immunodeficient NOD-SCID mice. Dvl3 is regarded as a binding hub with many different interacting partners. In this study, we showed that Dvl3 was significantly overexpressed in human HCCs and promoted cancer stemness both in vitro and in vivo. Our findings also established that HIPK2/PP1Cα/ITCH axis sustains the de-phosphorylation of Dvl3. We found that the non-phosphorylated (NP)-Dvl3 was more stable than the phosphorylated form, more active in activating β-catenin transcriptional activity, and more potent in enhancing self-renewal ability in HCC cells. Mechanistically, we confirmed that the homeodomain-interacting protein kinase-2 (HIPK2) and E3 ubiquitin ligase ITCH were able to physically bind to Dvl3 protein. Knockdown of HIPK2 and the protein phosphatase regulatory unit C-alpha (PP1Cα) resulted in sustained Dvl3 phosphorylation and hence decrease in the NP form of Dvl3. On the other hand, knockdown of E3 ubiquitin ligase ITCH reduced the phosphorylation-induced degradation and stabilized the phosphorylated Dvl3 protein. This post-translational modification of Dvl3 in turn maintains LGR5 expression and enhances the cancer stemness properties in HCC.

775613.value: To test the hypothesis that cardiomyocytes generated from patients with primary LAMP2 deficiency can serve as a reliable cellular model for studying the pathophysiological aspects of DD-induced cardiomyopathy. The resultant CMs will be treated with various topoisomerase inhibitors to unsilence the inactive wildtype LAMP2 allele. 775613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
775613.value: Danon Disease (DD) 是一種由LAMP2 基因突變而引起的X-連鎖顯性遺傳性病。LAMP2 基因位於X染色體上，負責編製II型溶酶體相關膜蛋白(LAMP2)。II型溶酶體相關膜蛋白在調控跨溶酶體膜的物質傳遞功能上擔當了很重要的角色，從而能夠幫助清除自噬物質。LAMP2基因缺陷會令受影響的細胞聚集大量的肝糖和自噬物質 。臨床表現上，受影響的男性病人在青少年時期就出現病發初期的症狀，如近端肌肉病變，肥厚型心肌病，視網膜病，和不同程度的心智遲緩。大部份的病人最終都會患有心肌病及致命性室性心律失常，如果沒有移植心臟，他們不大可能活過三十歲。患DD的女性病人通常較遲才出現病發症狀，因為其體細胞上的X染色體有隨機的失活，所以只有一部份的體細胞，如心肌細胞，會顯出DD的顯型。無論怎樣，大部份患有DD的女性病人都會發展到心肌病，出現嚴重的心律不齊，甚至死亡。不幸地，因對DD 的病理基礎缺乏詳細理解，目前尚沒有有效治療DD的方法。雖然LAMP2基因剔除的小鼠模型曾被用作為探討DD病理基礎的工具，但在心肌生理學上，始終人類和小鼠是有很大的差別。由於能夠取得人類心肌組織的機會很有限，所以一直缺乏以人類心肌細胞為基礎的模型，這樣，在全面分析DD的病理機制和藥物作用的驗證時，有很大的障礙。 誘導多功能幹細胞技術的出現，讓我們能製造出有病人特定的多功能幹細胞，以便用作研究遺傳性心肌病變的病理機制和決定治療的方法。在這計劃書上，我們提出採用誘導人類多功能幹細胞的技術和心肌細胞功能的詳盡評估來建立一個以人類心肌細胞為基礎的模型作為探討DD病理基礎的工具。這手法能為DD體外模型實驗及藥物測試提供源源不絕有病人特定的心肌細胞。這個項目明確的目的是在取自一位LAMP2雜合的女病人身上的誘導多功能幹細胞上，試驗性的修改X染色體和採用拓樸異構酶抑制劑作治療，使滅活了的X染色體當中的原株LAMP2等位基因不再沉默，從而減輕這些心肌細胞的功能障礙。這項研究的結果定能說明DD的病理機制，以及開拓治療DD和其他X-連鎖顯性遺傳性病的新方法。

775613.value: Objective 1: Addressing Objective 1, we first collected the skin fibroblasts or the urine samples from members of a local family suffered from X-linked cardiomyopathy. Then, we performed sequencing analysis and confirmed that these subjects carry a Danon disease associated LAMP2 mutation (Fig.1A to 1C). Functionally, this mutation completely abolished the LAMP2 protein production from the affected allele (Fig.1D). For the male patients (Patient II-1 and II-2), since they only contain the mutant LAMP2 allele, the iPSCs lines from these patients were generated with standard reprogramming procedures. For Patient I-1, who carries both wildtype and mutant LAMP2 allele, we have performed additional experiments to generate genetically identical (isogenic) iPSC lines with distinctive LAMP2 productivity (Fig.1E). The details will be discussed in the Objective 2 section of this report. As showed in Fig.1F and 1G, both the LAMP2-producing and LAMP2-deficient iPSCs lines were able to differentiate into cardiomyocytes (CMs), and the X-chromosome inactivation status (as indicated by LAMP2 productivity) remain unchanged during cardiac differentiation. After obtaining the iPSCs-derived CMs (iPSC-CMs), we have extensively characterized the structural and functional differences between the LAMP2-producing and LAMP2-deficient iPSC-CMs. We first looked at the organizations of the myofibrils using immunostaining analysis. As showed in Fig.2A, over 50% of the LAMP2-deficient iPSCs-CMs showed distinct patterns of myofibril disorganization, while less than 20% of the LAMP2-producing iPSC-CMs showing such phenotype. In addition, the LAMP2-deficient iPSCs-CMs were also significantly larger than the LAMP2-producing iPSCs-CMs. We have also evaluated autophagosomes and glycogen accumulations (the two phenotypic hallmarks of Danon disease) in the iPSC-CMs. As shown in Fig.2B, accumulation of LC3 punctate was observed in over 50% of the LAMP2-deficient iPSC-CMs, but in less than 5% of the LAMP2-producing iPSC-CMs (Fig.2B). And similar results were obtained in the glycogen deposition analysis (Fig.2B). These observations have been further verified using transmission electron microscopy (Fig.3). These results demonstrated that the LAMP2-deficient iPSCs recapitulated the Danon disease phenotypes and represented desirable models for disease modeling. Next, we further evaluated the changes in the LC3-I and LC3-II level in the presence of autophagy activator (rapamycin) and inhibitor (bafilomycin A1) in the iPSC-CMs (LAMP2-producing: Pt-I-1-LAMP2-WT; LAMP2-deficient Pt-I-1-LAMP2-c.520C>T). As shown in Fig.4A and B, under all conditions, the LC3-II/LC3-I ratio in the LAMP2-deficient iPSC-CMs was significantly higher than that in LAMP2-producing iPSC-CMs. This indicated that autophagosome is excessively accumulated in the LAMP2-deficient iPSC-CMs. Based on the functional properties of LAMP2, we speculated that the increased accumulation of autophagic material was due to failure in clearing the autophagosomes. To confirm this, we further evaluated the degradation of endogenous substrates by measuring the p62 levels. As shown in Fig.4C, rapamycin significantly reduced the p62 levels in the LAMP2-producing iPSC-CMs, suggesting that the activation of autophagy increased the clearance of p62 in the normal CMs. On the contrary, rapamycin treatment further increased the level of p62 in LAMP2-deficient iPSC-CMs (Fig.4C). These findings indicated that LAMP2-deficient iPSC-CMs cannot clear the autophagic cargoes efficiently. These data suggest that the accumulation of autophagic material in the LAMP2-deficient iPSC-CMs was due to failure in autophagosome clearing rather than over-activation of the autophagy pathway. For cardiac functions, we have evaluated the LAMP2 deficiency associated changes in contraction and calcium handling. Using IonOptix contractility analysis, we showed that the contractility was significantly reduced in LAMP2-dificient iPSC-CMs (Fig.5A). For the calcium handling analysis, we have performed confocal microscopy-based calcium imaging to evaluate the intracellular calcium transient during resting and stimulated condition. As shown in Fig.5B, under resting conditions, LAMP2-deficient iPSC-CMs exhibited a significant reduction in amplitude, Vmaxrise and Vmaxdecay values of intracellular calcium transients compared with LAMP2-producing iPSC-CMs. This reduction in calcium handling ability of the LAMP2-deficient CMs is likely due to a reduced cellular protein level of calcium handling proteins as demonstrated by Western blot analysis (Fig.5C). For the effects of isoproterenol on the calcium transient events of the iPSC-CMs, in all groups, brief isoproterenol exposure increased the contraction rates. Nonetheless the acceleration was short-lived in the LAMP2-deficient iPSC-CMs, and they arrested within 50 seconds of the application of isoproterenol (Fig.5D). This difference was likely due to the reduced calcium handling ability observed in the LAMP2-deficient iPSC-CMs. As a whole, Objective 1 have been fully achieved as we have demonstrated cardiac and autophagic dysfunctions in the LAMP2-deficient IPSC-CMs. Objective 2. Addressing Objective 2, we first collected the skin fibroblasts from the heterozygous patient (Patient I-1), and evaluated their LAMP2 productivities. Using immunostaining analysis, we confirmed that the heterozygous fibroblasts exhibited mosaic pattern of LAMP2 productivity (Fig.1D), which is likely due to randomized X-chromosome inhibition, in which, the cells carrying the LAMP2 mutant allele on the silenced X-chromosome are LAMP2-producing, and vice versa. As such, we first separated the LAMP2-producing and LAMP2-deficint fibroblasts by repeated serial low density passages (Fig.1E). After that, we reprogrammed these clonally selected fibroblasts individually using standard method. This allowed us to create isogenic iPSCs with distinct LAMP2 productivity. As showed in Fig.1F and G, the X-chromosome inactivation statuses in these lines remain unchanged during reprograming and cardiac differentiation. The isogenic iPSCs lines were then characterized as described in Objective 1. In brief, the iPSC-CMs that express the wildtype LAMP2 allele (Pt-I-1-LAMP2-WT) produced similar levels of LAMP2 proteins as compare to the normal control (Fig.1F) and were structurally and functionally normal (Fig.1-4). On the other hand, the LAMP2-deficient counterparts (Pt-I-1-LAMP2-c.520C>T) exhibited Danon disease phenotypes similar to the LAMP2-deficient iPSC-CMs derived from the male patients (Pt-II-1 and Pt-II-2). Overall, Objective 2 has been fully achieved as we have successfully created isogenic iPSCs-CMs with distinctive X-chromosome inactivation status and disease phenotypes. These isogenic iPSCs lines allowed us to study the effects of LAMP2 deficiency without the interference from the difference in genetic background. More importantly, our result has reinforced the current notion that the presences of LAMP2-producing cells in the heterozygous female patient may be accounted for their better survivals compare to the male patients. Objective 3. Addressing Objective 3, we first tested the effects of topoisomerase inhibitors on reactivating the silenced LAMP2 allele. Although we have observed that DNA topoisomerase inhibitor treatments increased the population of LAMP2-producing cells in the primary fibroblasts isolated from the Patient I-1 (Fig.7A and 7B), after clonal selection and reprogramming, the Pt-I-1-LAMP2-c.520C>T iPSCs became non-responsive to these drugs. As such, we changed to test the effects of DNA methylation inhibitor that has also been show to reactive silenced genes. As showed in Fig.6C to 6F, 5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine treatment restored the production of LAMP2 proteins in both Pt-I-1-LAMP2-c.520C>T iPSCs and iPSC-CMs. Interestingly, despite only a certain portion of the cells showed LAMP2 protein production after drug treatment, the treated iPSC-CMs showed significant improvements in contractility and calcium handling ability against the increased work load increased by isoproterenol treatment (Fig. 6G and 6H). Overall, we have fully achieved Objective 3 by showing the beneficial effects of the reactivation of the silenced wildtype alleles in the LAMP2-deficient iPSCs.

775613.label: Major findings and research outcome
775613.value: In this study, we have successfully created several iPSCs from local patients carrying the Danon disease associated LAMP2 mutation. Using these iPSCs lines we have provided the first evidence that autophagic dysfunction caused by LAMP2-deficiency is due the failure in the clearance of the autophagosome rather than via the uncontrolled activation of autophagy in a human cardiomyocyte-based model (1). More importantly, we have also been successfully created an isogenic iPSCs pairs from the fibroblasts collected from a heterozygous female patient whole carries one wildtype and one mutant LAMP2 allele. The isogenic iPSCs lines are genetically identical but exhibited distinctive X-chromosome inactivation pattern. Using these isogenic iPSCs lines, we have revealed the therapeutic potential of the reactivation of the wildtype LAMP2 allele on the inactivated X-chromosome in ameliorating the autophagic dysfunction associated with complete LAMP2 deficiency. In brief, in our study, we have showed that the application of DNA demethylating agent, 5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine were able to reactivate the wildtype LAMP2 allele and improved the cardiac function of the patient-specific iPSCs derived cardiomyocytes (1). This has provided important insights into the therapeutic potential of X-chromosome reactivation on X-linked dominant disorders. In addition, although our major aims were focused on the cardiac dysfunctions, our study have also provided some experimental evidences on the effects of LAMP2 deficiency on oxidative stress induced neuronal injury, which may help explain the development of mental retardation in certain patients with Danon disease (2). In terms of research achievements, we have published our research works in 3 international peer-review articles (1-3), and one of these articles (1) are published in Circulation (Impact factor 17.2), which is one of the best ranked journals in cardiology. 775613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
775613.value: One of our major finding in our study is the proof-of-concept demonstration of the therapeutic effects on reactivating the wildtype alleles in ammoniating the disease phenotypes associated with the X-linked dominant Danon disease. Our study showed that this can be achieved by the application of , 5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine (Decitabine), which caused the demethylation of the inactivated X-chromosomes. Although Decitabine is an FDA approved drug, since the effects of global DNA demethylation could are non-specific, it may also lead to undesirable activation of non-target genes. As such, as a follow up study, we like to further investigate the possible side effects of X-chromosome reactivation and to evaluate other agents that that may cause X-chromosome reactivation. In addition, we would also like to extent our study to other X-linked disease models, such as the Rett syndromes and the Fabry disease.

775613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
775613.value: The mutations in the LAMP2 genes that leads to LAMP2 protein deficiency have been implicated in the development of the X-linked dominant Danon disease. However, due to the lack of appropriate human cardiomyocytes-based model, the pathophysiological mechanism underlying LAMP2 mutation remains unclear. Addressing this issue, our study was aimed to evaluate the pathological mechanism underlying the Danon disease associated cardiomyopathy using a patient specific iPSCs based model. Since iPSCs are pluripotent and can be differentiated into different cell types, such as cardiomyocytes and neurons, thus the patient-specific iPSCs-derived cardiomyocytes represent a desirable model for investigating human cardiac disorders. Our results provided evidences that LAMP2 protein deficiency impaired the clearance of autophagic materials, which in turn impaired the contraction and calcium handing ability of the affected cardiomyocytes. In addition, our results also demonstrated that inhibition of DNA methylation can reactivate wildtype LAMP2 allele on the silenced X-chromosome and restored the production of LAMP2 proteins in the iPSCs derived cardiomyocytes of heterozygous patients. This revealed the therapeutic potential of DNA demethylating agents, such as Decitabine, in ameliorating the cardiac dysfunctions in the heterozygous patients with Danon disease.

775713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
775713.value: Leukemia is a cancer with dysregulation of normal hematopoiesis by primitive population of blast cells in bone marrow. Mixed Lineage Leukemia (MLL) gene forms more than 60 different fusion proteins in human acute leukemias, and yet the mechanisms underlying the establishment of MLL leukemia stem cells (LSCs) remain largely unknown. It has been demonstrated that a subset of genes in LSC is highly expressed in normal hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs), thus highlighted the importance of activation of stem cell program in LSC. An emerging area in cancer research in recent years has focused on epigenetic modifications, which regulate gene expression without alteration in DNA sequence. MLL fusion proteins mediate an altered histone modification pattern at the target gene loci; in particular, the MLL-EEN/PRMT1 oncogenic complex induces transformation of primary myeloid progenitors via introduction of aberrant histone H4 arginine methylation. Nevertheless, the leukemogenic role of PRMT1 in the establishment of LSC remains unclear. Previously we have generated an Mll-Een invertor mouse model to demonstrate the leukemogenity of the Mll-Een fusion protein. We further established an Mll-Een expressing leukemic cell line to investigate the leukemogenic mechanism mediated by protein arginine methyltransferase Prmt1. We discovered that a subpopulation of Mll-Een expressing cells is CD41-positive, which demonstrated enhanced self-renewal ability and stronger expression of genes associated with HSC activities, suggesting that part of the HSC transcriptional program is re-activated. We hypothesize that epigenetic dysregulation mediated by Prmt1 protein can activate a leukemia stem cell program through the induction of the master regulator Runx1, which contribute to the initiation of CD41-positive LSC population in MLL-rearranged leukemia. We aim to understand the mechanisms in the establishment of LSC by using the next generation sequencing technology to study the correlation between aberrant epigenetic modification pattern and global transcriptional dysregulation by Prmt1 in MLL leukemic cells. The CD41+ leukemic cells will be further characterized by their LSC functions and CD41 can potentially serve as a novel LSC marker in MLL-rearranged leukemia. The involvement of downstream target gene RUNX1 provides us additional clues that the function of PRMT1 may not only be restricted in MLL-rearranged leukemia, but it may also be involved in other leukemia with RUNX1 gene mutation or with AML1-ETO fusion protein. Taken together, studies on the role of PRMT1 can provide novel insights in the establishment of LSC and facilitate the development of therapeutic treatment for the eradication of LSC in human leukemias. 白血病是一種由於原始骨髓癌細胞的造血功能失調而導致的癌症。在人類急性白血病中，混合系白血病（ MLL ）基因形成60多個不同的融合蛋白，但MLL白血病幹細胞（LSCs）的建立機制仍是未知。在LSC中有一組的基因已被證明會跟正常造血幹細胞（HSC) 一樣的高度表達，從而強調了在LSC中活化幹細胞程序的重要性。以不改變DNA序列而調節基因表達的表觀遺傳修飾是近年癌症研究中的一個新興領域。MLL融合蛋白能改變在目標基因的組蛋白修飾，尤其是MLL-EEN/PRMT1能通過引入異常的組蛋白H4精氨酸甲基化而誘導主髓系祖細胞癌變。然而， PRMT1的白血病作用在 LSC的建立上仍不清楚。我們先前已經利用MLL- EEN的小鼠模型證明MLL - EEN融合蛋白的致癌性。我們更進一步建立了MLL-EEN的白血病細胞系來調查PRMT1的白血病機制。我們發現一部分的MLL - EEN細胞是CD41陽性，它們表現更強的自我更新能力和更多與HSC活動相關的基因表達，意味著HSC的轉錄程序被重新激活。我們推測，PRMT1蛋白能通過誘導Runx1來啟動白血病幹細胞程式，這有助於在MLL基因重排的白血病中萌生CD41陽性的LSC。我們的目標是要瞭解LSC的建立機制，利用新一代測序技術來研究PRMT1在MLL白血病細胞中引致異常的表觀遺傳修飾模式和全轉錄失調的相關性。CD41陽性的白血病細胞將會進一步記錄它的LSC功能，CD41 將有可能在MLL基因重排的白血病中成為一種新的LSC標記。下游的靶基因RUNX1的參與將為我們提供更多的線索，PRMT1的功能可能不僅被限制在MLL基因重排的白血病，更可能與RUNX1基因突變或AML1-ETO融合蛋白的白血病有關。總括而言，PRMT1的研究可以在建立LSC方面提供新的見解，促進發展以消滅LSC來治療人類的白血病。

775713.label: Realisation of objectives
775713.value: For Objective 1, we have performed Prmt1 knockdown in Mll-Een expressing cells. Knockdown of Prmt1 would significantly reduce the proliferation and colony forming potential of the Mll-Een expressing cells. RNA samples of the knockdown cells were collected and examined the quality. On the other hand, Prmt1 can mediate H4R3me2 epigenetic modification in Mll-Een expressing cells. We have demonstrated that knockdown of Prmt1 would lead to reduction of H4R3me2 at Hox loci. The H4R3me2 ChIP samples were collected after Prmt1 knockdown and subjected to ChIP-Seq experiment. Analysis of the ChIP-seq data demonstrated enrichment of H4R3me2 was significantly reduced once Prmt1 has been knockdown. The loss of H4R3me2 was associated with decreased expression of many genes involved in heamtopoesis and cell proliferation. These results suggest that H4R3me2 mediated by Prmt1 is crucial in the transcriptional regulation in MLL-transformed leukemia cells. For Objective 2, we have optimized the in vitro culture condition which allows us to maintain hematopoietic stem cell population. We have found that knockdown of Prmt1 would lead to decrease in CD41+ population. RNA-Seq analysis of the CD41+ and CD41- leukemia cells demonstrated a panel of Hox genes was upregulated in CD41+ population, which might confer to higher leukemogenic potential. Gene ontology analysis also showed that the deregulated genes are associated with hematopoiesis, cell differentiation, cytokine-mediated signaling pathway and other transmembrane signaling pathways. The CD41+ cells also demonstrated higher colony forming ability and were able to maintain leukemia colony formation in serial replating assay, demonstrating it leukemia-initiating potential. For Objective 3, we have designed the CRISPR/Cas9 system to knockout Runx1 gene in the Mll-Een expressing cells. Knockout of Runx1 gene leads to significant reduction of cell proliferation, colony forming ability, and CD41+ population of the Mll-Een leukemia cells. We have also performed the protein co-immunoprecipitation experiment to show that PRMT1 interacts with RUNX1 in human leukemia cell line Kasumi-1. It thus supports that PRMT1 interacts with Runx1 in the maintenance of leukemic cell properties.

775713.label: Major findings and research outcome
775713.value: The major findings of this project included: 1) we discovered the epigenetic mechanism of Prmt1 in the regulation of leukemia transcriptional program via H4R3me2; 2) we demonstrated the leukemia-initiating potential of CD41+ cell population in MLL-rearranged leukemia cells; 3) we found the protein interaction between Prmt1 and Runx1 in the maintenance of leukemia cell properties and the association of the stemness of CD41+ cells in MLL-rearranged leukemia cells. We believe our findings can provide valuable information on the understanding the molecular events in MLL-rearranged leukemia. The outcomes of this project are: 1) a research article based on the findings from this study was published in Cytokines in 2014, which is attached with this report; 2) this work was presented as a poster presentation in 56th American Society of Hematology (ASH) Annual Meeting & Exposition at San Francisco USA in 2014; 3) a PhD student has been recruited and continue the work on this project.

This study provides novel insights in the establishment of LSC and facilitate the development of therapeutic treatment for the eradication of LSC in human leukemias.

775913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
775913.value: Accumulating evidences indicate that sub-population of cells resided in tumor are responsible for the resistance to cancer therapy and recurrence. Identification and characterization of these sub-population cells is important to enhance the response for cancer treatment. However, the identity of such cells resided in cervical cancer has not yet been clearly defined due to limited clinical materials. In our pilot study, we isolated sphere forming cells from primary cervical tumor tissues which exhibited self renewal ability. Higher expression of “stemness” genes including Bmi-1, Nanog and Oct-4 have been detected in sphere cells as compared with their attached cells counterpart. Gene expression profiling identified a cell surface marker CD55 was up-regulated in primary cervical cancer sphere cells. CD55 is a membrane-bound complement regulatory protein (mCRPs) which is overexpressed in tumor cells. Enhanced expression of CD55 protects tumor cells to escape from complement attack. By flow cytometry, CD55(+) cells isolated from cervical cancer cell line C33A exhibited significant sphere-forming ability than CD55(-) cells. Functional characterization on these cells revealed that CD55(+) cells showed enhanced in vitro tumorigenicity, cell migration and resistance against irradiation than CD55(-) cells. Notably, abundant CD55(+) population was detected in Human Papilloma Virus (HPV) positive cervical cancer cells and elevated population size of CD55(+) cells was found in HPV-negative cells overexpressing HPV-E6 protein. Our preliminary data suggested that HPV-E6 protein expression enrich CD55(+) population in cervical cancer and CD55(+) population play an important role in the contribution of radio-resistance and tumor progression in cervical cancer cells. We hypothesize that HPV-E6 protein enriches CD55(+) population which promotes radio-resistance in cervical cancer. In this proposed study, we aim to (1) evaluate and functional characterize CD55(+) population isolated from cervical cancer cell lines, primary cervical cancer cell lines and cervical tumor tissues; (2) study the effects on CD55(+) population by manipulation of HPV-E6 protein expression in cervical cancer cell lines and normal cervical cells; (3) investigate the significance of CD55(+) population in contributing radio-resistance and DNA repair pathway; (4) examine the effectiveness of CD55 blockade in targeting CD55(+) population in cervical cancer. We believe that a better understanding of CD55(+) population in cervical cancer will significantly advance our understanding of radio-resistant cells resided in cervical cancer and provide insight for the establishment of novel strategies and effective therapies.

775913.label: Realisation of objectives
775913.value: 1. To isolate and functional characterize CD55(+) population in cervical cancer cell lines, primary cervical cancer cell lines and cervical tumor tissues To characterize CD55(+) population, we isolated CD55(+) and CD55(-) populations in cervical cancer cell lines C33A and primary cervical cancer cells CP-1 and CP-2 by flow cytometry using FITC-conjugated CD55 antibody. The purity of the CD55(+) and CD55(-) populations was examined and confirmed by flow cytometry. We found that the cell proliferation rate, clonogenic survival after irradiation, in vitro and in vivo tumorigenicity and self-renewal ability were enhanced in CD55(+) population as compared with CD55(-) population. To study the clinical significance of CD55 in cervical cancer tissues, the expression of CD55 protein was examined in cervical cancer tissue microarray (TMA) with 70 cervical cancer tissues and 5 normal-benign cervical tissues. We confirmed that CD55 was over-expressed in cervical cancer tissues and no CD55 expression was detected in normal-benign cervical tissue. 2. To study the effects of HPV-E6 protein expression on CD55(+) population in cervical cancer cells To study the effects of HPV-E6 protein of the high-risk type HPV in cervical cancer cells, we established stable clones expressing E6 protein of two high risk types HPV (HPV16 and HPV18) in HPV negative cell line C33A cells. We successfully established stable clones of C33A cells overexpressing HPV16E6 and HPV18E6. We found that HPV-E6 protein (both HPV16 and HPV18) enriched CD55(+) population in all established stable clones. In addition, to determine whether the tumorigenicity of C33A cervical cancer cells could be enhanced by HPV-E6 protein, an anchorage-independent soft agar assay was performed. Both HPV16E6 and HPV18E6 stable clones formed larger colonies in soft agar than control clones within the same period of time. To further investigate whether HPV-E6 protein also augments the tumorigenicity of C33A cells in vivo, HPV16E6 and HPV18E6 stable clones and control clones were subcutaneously injected into immunodeficient mice. The tumors formed by HPV16E6 and HPV18E6 stable clones were significantly larger than those formed by control clones and C33A parental cells. These data indicated that HPV-E6 protein enhances both in vitro and in vivo tumorigenicity. 3. To investigate the significance of CD55 and HPV-E6 protein in contributing radio-resistance and DNA repair pathway We examined the effects of irradiation on CD55 populations in cervical cancer cell line and primary cervical cancer cells, enriched CD55(+) cells were detected after irradiation treatment. Furthermore, clonogenic assay was performed to evaluate the survival rate of CD55(+) population in primary cervical cancer cells. We also found that the survival rate of CD55(+) cells was higher than CD55(-) cells after irradiation treatment. Furthermore, suppression of CD55 in Caski cells and knockdown of CD55 in HPV-E6 stably expressing clones sensitized cells in response to irradiation. These data suggested that CD55 plays an important role in contributing radio-resistance of cervical cancer cells. However, no significant difference in the expressions of DNA damage related genes was found by Quantitative Real-time PCR with Human DNA damage-induced array and western blot between CD55(-) and CD55(+) cells. 4. To examine the effectiveness in targeting CD55(+) cells in cervical cancer by the blockade of CD55 We employed shRNA to knockdown the endogenous CD55 expression in cervical cancer cell line Caski, which show high percentage of CD55(+) population and the ability to form xenograft in nude mice, for further investigation. Besides, to test whether the tumorigenic properties of HPV-E6-mediated enrichment of the CD55(+) population in C33A cells can be reversed by eliminating CD55 gene expression, knockout of the CD55 gene was induced in HPV-E6 stably expressing clones. CRISPR/cas9 was employed to knock out the CD55 gene in the 18E6-5 clone, which harbored the highest percentage of the CD55(+) population (79.3%) among all HPV-E6-overexpressing stable clones. Our data demonstrated that silencing of CD55 by shRNA in Caski cells or knockout of CD55 by CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing system in HPV-E6-overexpressing C33A cells contributed to inhibition of in vitro and in vivo tumorigenecity, cell proliferation, clonogenic survival and self-renewal ability.

775913.label: Major findings and research outcome
775913.value: Clinical significance of CD55 in cervial cancer Microarray was performed to compare the expression profile between attached and spheroid cells. We identified CD55 as one of the potential cell surface marker for the isolation of sub-population cells. Furthermore, overexpression of CD55 was found in human cervical cancer tissues and HPV-positive cervical cancer cell lines. This observation suggested that CD55 is enriched by HPV and may play an oncogenic role in cervical cancer. Oncogenic roles of CD55 in cervical cancer We isolated CD55(-) and CD55(+) populations using flow cytometer in cervical cancer cells. Functional assays were performed to study the roles of CD55 in cervical cancer. CD55 was found to promote cell proliferation, cell migration, cell renewal, clonogenic survival, in vitro and in vivo tumorigenicity of cervical cancer cells. Furthermore, knockdown of endogenous CD55 expression in HPV-positive cervical cancer cell line sensitized the response to radiation treatment and inhibited cell proliferation, self-renewal ability, in vitro and in vivo tumorigenicity. These data suggested the oncogenic role of CD55 in the cervical carcinogenesis and radio-resistance of cervical cancer. Role of HPV-E6 and CD55 in promoting tumorigenesis in cervial cancer Flow cytometric analysis was performed to examine the percentages of CD55(+) sub-populations in cervical cancer cells. We observed that the expression of the CD55 cell surface marker was correlated with the HPV viral status. In addition, we established C33A cells overexpressing HPV16 or HPV18 E6 proteins. Flow cytometric analysis demonstrated that the CD55(+) population size was increased in all the HPV-E6-overexpressing clones. By nude mice injection assay, we observed that the HPV-E6-overexpressing clones enhanced the in vivo tumorigenicity. Taken together, these results indicated that HPV-E6 protein expression enriched the CD55(+) population in C33A cells, which might contribute to tumorigenesis. Blockade of CD55 suppressed the oncogenic roles of HPV-E6 and CD55 To test whether the tumorigenic properties of HPV-E6-mediated enrichment of the CD55(+) population in C33A cells can be reversed by eliminating CD55 gene expression, knockout of the CD55 gene was induced in HPV-E6 stably expressing clones. CRISPR/cas9 was employed to knock out the CD55 gene in the HPV-E6 stably expressing clones. To study the effects of the elimination of CD55 expression, we performed functional assays with the established CD55 KO clones. We successfully demonstrated that knockout of CD55 reversed the oncogenic properties in HPV-E6 stably expressing clones. Research outcome The findings in this study were published in The Journal of Pathology in 2017.

775913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
775913.value: The novel findings presented in this study describe an association of HPV-E6 protein and CD55 for the promotion of oncogenesis in cervical cancer. Since CD55(+) population is enriched by HPV-E6 protein in cervical cancer cells, it may potentially serve as a therapeutic target in cervical cancer and is necessary to be further investigated. We found that CD55(+) population is more radio-resistant while knockdown or knockout of CD55 expression in cervical cancer cells sensitized cells in response to irradiation. Therefore, downregulation of CD55 may play an important role in sensitizing tumor cells to cancer treatments including irradiation and may serve as a therapeutic strategy to eradicate cancer cells by the host immune system. Future studies on the effects of the blockade of CD55 together with other potential cancer-related cell surface markers will be necessary to improve the efficiency in targeting sub-population cells in cervical cancer.

775913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
775913.value: In this study, we demonstrate a novel association between HPV-E6 protein expression and the upregulation of the CD55 surface marker in cervical cancer cells. We found that the HPV-E6 oncoprotein enriched the CD55(+) population in cervical cancer cells, which enhanced cell proliferation, cell self-renewal ability, cell migration, radio-resistance and tumorigenicity. Suppression or knockout of CD55 expression in HPV-E6-expressing cells could reverse the tumorigenic phenotypes of cervical cancer cells. The findings in this study underline the impact of HPV-E6 protein on the induction of CD55 expression in cervical carcinogenesis, and reveals a potential target for the establishment of novel strategies and effective therapies.

776213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
776213.value: Influenza A virus attaches on the host cell surface by binding to sialic acid (SA). In general, avian and human viruses prefer to bind to α2,3-linked SA and α2,6-linked SA, respectively. The binding specificity of influenza virus is one of the well-known viral determinants for controlling tissue tropism and host adaptation. After attaching to the cell surface, the virus can adopt different modes of entry to achieve infection. Even influenza virus is considered to be one of the best studied viruses, little is known about the cellular requirements for virus entry events beyond the initial attachment step. Interestingly, we have recently reported that host fibronectin is important for the entry of influenza viruses that have a specificity for α2,6-linked SA (J Virol. 86:10704-13). Blocking the biological function of fibronectin in our models can specifically inhibit the post-attachment entry event of influenza viruses that have an α2,6-linked SA binding preference. Strikingly, this inhibitory effect cannot be observed in cells infected by viruses with an α2,3-linked SA specificity. The underlying mechanism accounts for these observations, however, are yet to be elucidated. Besides, it is not known whether this fibronectin-mediated viral infection is a universal feature for influenza viruses that have an α2,6-linked SA binding preference. Fibronectin is encoded by a single gene. It is a major extracellular matrix protein. Its internalization from cell surface to cytoplasm is critical for protein trafficking and cell signaling. Here, we propose to characterize the fibronectin-mediated viral event. Several human in vitro and ex vivo models will be incubated with human and animal influenza viruses with known SA binding specificity, followed by anti-fibronectin treatments. This is to determine whether cellular fibronectin is an essential factor for most human viruses to achieve infection. Moreover, we shall mutate the critical domains on this host protein. Human cells that have an exclusive expression of mutated fibronectin will be used to study the mechanism of action of fibronectin required for the infection. Lastly, we shall test inhibitors that are known to have direct or indirect effects on fibronectin for their antiviral activities. Overall, these studies will answer whether fibronectin-mediated viral infection is a general event for human influenza viruses. Results from our investigations are expected to provide novel insights on basic biology, virus-host interaction and host/tissue specificity of influenza virus. This work will also help to reveal a new strategy for the control of influenza virus infection. 甲型流感病毒藉著與細胞表面的唾液酸[sialic acid (SA)]結合從而依附於宿主細胞表面。一般來說，禽流感病毒和人類流感病毒分別偏好與α2,3鍵唾液酸（α2,3-linked SA）和α2,6鍵唾液酸（α2,6-linked SA）結合，而這亦是病毒之組織嗜性及宿主適應性的決定因素。當依附於宿主細胞表面之後，病毒便可以採用不同的模式進入細胞內，使細胞受到感染。 即使流感病毒被認為是其中一種受到廣泛研究的病毒，但關於這病毒依附在細胞表面後如何進入宿主細胞的認識仍然極小。我們最近發現宿主細胞內的纖維結合蛋白（fibronectin）對於偏好與α2,6鍵唾液酸結合的流感病毒進入細胞有著重要的作用（J Virol. 86:10704-13）。在我們的實驗模型中，阻斷纖維結合蛋白的功能能夠在偏好與α2,6鍵唾液酸結合的流感病毒依附在細胞表面後的融合有抑制的作用。這抑制作用並未出現於受到偏好與α2,3鍵唾液酸結合的病毒感染的細胞中。但是，有關機制到目前為止仍未能夠完全被理解。此外，現在還未清楚這發現是否普遍存在於所有偏好與α2,6鍵唾液酸結合的流感病毒中。 纖維結合蛋白是一個主要的細胞外基質蛋白，這個蛋白自細胞表面進入細胞質的過程對於蛋白運輸及細胞信號傳導有著重要的作用。在此研究計劃中，我們希望鑑定與纖維結合蛋白有關的病毒感染機制。我們會將已知唾液酸結合特性的人類流感病毒與動物流感病毒用於幾個體內及體外感染模型，然後再模型中添加纖維結合蛋白抗體，以斷定細胞中的纖維結合蛋白是否大部分人類流感病毒感染的一個必要元素。此外，我們會使纖維結合蛋白中的重要位置產生基因突變，把這變異的纖維結合蛋白表達在人類細胞中，以便用來研究纖維結合蛋白於流感病毒的感染機制。最後，我們會測試纖維結合蛋白對於抑制流感病毒的作用。總括來說，這些研究能說明與纖維結合蛋白有關的病毒感染機制是否適用於所有人類流感病毒。我們期望研究結果能為基礎生物學、病毒與宿主細胞互動以及流感病毒的宿主偏好或組織嗜性提供新的觀點，並能提供流感病毒感染控制的新策略。

776213.label: Realisation of objectives
776213.value: Objectives 1-2: In order to determine whether different viruses would have different dependences on the fibronectin-mediate viral entry pathway, a total of 18 influenza viruses were tested for their sensitivity to anti-fibronectin antibody treatments. This panel of viruses included human, swine and avian influenza viruses (H1, H3, H5 and H9) and their mutants. The receptor binding specificities of these viruses have been characterized by glycan arrays in previous studies by us or others. This panel of virus was known to have alpha 2,6 sialic acid (human-like receptor), alpha 2,3 sialic acid (avian-like receptor) or dual binding specificity (i.e. both 2,3 and 2,6 sialic acids). Mutants of the studied mutants contained mutations at positions that are known to alter viral receptor binding preferences. These viruses were tested in an in vitro models (MDCK). The numbers of infected cells were stained by immunofluorescence assays specific for viral NP antigen. The amounts of progeny viruses produced by the infected cultures were assayed by standard hemagglutination (HA) assays, plaque assays and/or RT-PCR reactions. To determine whether the anti-viral effect of anti-fibronectin antibody would have different effects at different cell types, we also conducted similar work using other in vitro cell cultures (e.g. A549). In addition, we also used human ex vivo cultures to test the above viruses. The infected tissues and cultures supernatants were studied as described above, except the infected tissues were processed for immunohistochemistry staining for viral NP antigens. Objective 3: To define how fibronectin might mediate viral entry, we obtained a mouse fibronectin null cell line (J Sottile, University of Rochester). This cell line, however, was found to be difficult to be cultured and it was considered not to be a suitable cell line for the proposed study. To overcome this hurdle, we subsequently used zinc finger nuclease technologies to generate a fibronectin knockout A549 cell line. Clones of A549 fibronectin knockout cells were successfully generated. The expressions of fibronectin of these clones were confirmed to be negative by immunofluorescence assays. In addition, we also acquired fibronectin expression plasmids (Ohashi, Duke University) for expression. Fibronectin KO cells were infected by influenza viruses. Besides, fibronectin expression plasmids and it mutants with deletions at various functional domains were transfected into the normal and fibronectin KO cells to test for their effects on virus replications. Infected cells and progeny viruses were studied as described above. We also tested a number of antibodies which are specific to different domains of fibronectin (Types 1 and 2) for their inhibitory effects on virus replication. In addition, we also used siRNA to knock down the expression of fibronectin and test for its effect on virus replication. Objective 4 In order to determine which viral entry pathway is mediated by fibronectin, a panel of chemicals (Chlorproamize, Filipin, Dynasore, 5-(N-Ethyl-N-isopropyl)amiloride, fetal calf serum) which are known to inhibit various major influenza viral entry pathways (e.g. caveolin-mediated endocytosis, clathrin-mediated endocytosis and macropinocytosis) were used in the study. MDCK cells were treated with these inhibitors in different combinations (N=11), followed by influenza virus infections. Cells infected with a human H1N1 or H5N1 virus were then incubated in culture medium with or without anti-fibronectin antibodies. In addition, the corresponding receptor binding mutants were also tested in this model as controls. Infected cells were harvested at 48 hour postinfection and characterized as described above. Fibronectin is also known to interact with integrins (e.g. α5β1 and αVβ3) to stimulate various cellular signaling pathways. To determine whether the inhibitory effect of anti-fibronectin antibody is due to the inhibition of major structure changes of extracellular matrix or the disruption of signaling pathways triggered by fibronectin-integrin interaction, we used a RGDS Peptide which is known to inhibit the interaction between fibronectin and integrin in our studied model. Briefly, we treated MDCK cells before, during and after virus infection. The amounts of progeny viruses generated from infected cultures were quantified by standard HA assays.

776213.label: Major findings and research outcome
776213.value: Objectives 1 & 2 Influenza viruses, which were known to have strong binding affinities to alpha 2,3-linked glycans, was not found to be sensitive to the anti-fibronectin antibody treatments in vitro. For viruses that are known to binding to alpha 2,6-linked glycans, they were found to have different susceptibilities to the antibody treatment in vitro. Interestingly, for the tested mammalian field strains which are sensitive to the antibody treatment, they were all found to have a very strong bias to extended N-acetyllactosamine structures (Neu5Aca2-6Galb1-4GlcNAcb1-3Galb1-4GlcNAcb-Sp0 and Neu5Aca2-6Galb1-4GlcNAcb1-3Galb1-4GlcNAcb1-3Galb1-4GlcNAcb-Sp0). These results suggested that influenza viruses might have different dependence on fibronectin for viral entry in vitro. The spectrum of this inhibitory effect of anti-fibronectin antibody in human lung ex vivo culture was found to be different from the one observed in in vitro conditions. Strikingly, viruses, which were not susceptible to the fibronectin treatment in in vitro conditions (e.g. avian H9N2), were found to be highly sensitive to the anti-fibronectin antibody treatment ex vivo. This suggested that the fibronectin matrix expressed by mono-cell culture is intrinsically different from the one expressed by human lung tissues. Our results demonstrated that fibronectin might play a much prominent roles on influenza viral entry in ex vivo and possibly in in vivo conditions. Objectives 3 and 4 Using different combinations of chemicals to inhibit influenza virus entry in in vitro conditions, we observed that many of the studied viral entry pathways were susceptible to the antibody treatment. The additional of anti-fibronectin antibody generally can greatly reduce the number of influenza virus positive cells, suggesting the fibronectin fiber is involved in all major viral entry pathways. These results further suggested that the anti-fibronectin antibody prevents major structure changes of fibronectin matrix for endocytosis, instead of inhibiting cellular signaling pathways triggered by fibronectin (also see the evidences below). Fibronectin knockout cells and cells expressed with mutated fibronectin proteins did not allow robust virus replication, demonstrating that the functional fibronectin is essential for virus replication. Additional data generated from experiments using various antibodies and fibronectin inhibitors further suggested that influenza viral entry does not require the activation of signaling pathways regulated by integrins. Overall, these results suggested that the viral entry of influenza virus might relate to structural changes of fibronectin. Others Several studies using the techniques developed from this work were published in peer-reviewed journals. Research outcome A total of 5 publications (4 published and 1 under review) were supported by this research projects.

776213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
776213.value: 1. Our ex vivo studies suggest that the fibronectin extracellular matrix might have different properties than the one observed from cell cultures. Further systematical comparison of extracellular matrix from in vitro and ex vivo conditions will be needed. 2. Our in vitro studies suggested that extended N-acetyllactosamine structures are important for viral entry in in vitro conditions. It is of interest to determine whether fibronectin in cell cultures might also be modified by these types of glycan. In addition, the antiviral effects of these glycans in in vitro conditions can be explored. 3. Fibronectins can be expressed into a wide range of isoforms in tissue specific manner, a systematic study of their expression in various in vitro and ex vivo conditions will be needed.

776213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
776213.value: Influenza A virus attaches on a host cell by binding to sialic acid (SA). In general, avian and human viruses prefer to bind to α2,3-linked SA and α2,6-linked SA, respectively. This binding specificity is a well-known viral determinant for controlling tissue tropism and host adaptation. In this investigation, we studied the role host’s fibronectin, a major cellular extracellular matrix protein, on influenza virus entry. It was observed that the SA binding specificity of influenza virus has a great effect on the virus entry mediated by fibronectin in vitro. Viruses with a strong α2,6-linked SA binding preference, in particular to those which like to bind to extended glycans, are more dependent on fibronectin in vitro. Interestingly, viruses, that are not sensitive to anti-fibronectin antibody in vitro, were found to be sensitive to the same antibody treatment in ex vivo conditions. These results suggested that fibronectin plays a key role of virus entry. Furthermore, the effect of fibronectin ex vivo was not restricted by the SA binding specificity. Our work also indicated that the viral entry does not require the activation of signaling pathways regulated by the fibronectin-integrin interaction, suggesting the fibronectin-mediated viral entry might only involve structural changes of fibronectin fibers.

776313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
776313.value: 真核細胞總是不斷面臨的來自環境和內源的挑戰,在正常細胞中DNA損傷是經常發生的。不及時應對DNA損傷可能導致發育和神經系統的缺陷，早衰和癌症。為了應對DNA損傷，細胞 擁有多個DNA修復途徑和檢查站來準確有效地修復受損的DNA。 S期檢查點檢測複製叉停滯或損傷，並發送信號，暫停S期進展，同時保持停滯的複製叉的穩定性，待DNA損傷修復後，DNA複製就可以恢復正常。 進化上保守的蛋白複合物TIM/TIPIN不僅在正常的DNA複製過程中穩定複製叉,在激活DNA複製檢查點也起到了核心作用. TIM/TIPIN 複合物與其他複製叉蛋白如RPA, Claspin And-1结合,共同應對DNA損傷激活複製檢查點. TIM/TIPIN複合物促進ATR调节的Chk1的磷酸化,以獲得最佳的S期檢查點激活. TIM還促進ATM调节的Chk2调节的DNA雙鏈斷裂的信號傳導. TIM缺少的細胞表現出的S期和G2/M期檢查點缺陷，以及γ-H2AX的磷酸化的高水平. 我們的初步數據顯示, TIM與PARP1形成複合物,可能參與了DNA斷裂的修復與複製. 有趣的是, TIM基因敲除導致胚胎死亡. 在以前的人類乳腺癌和大腸癌的基因組掃描中發現Tim有突變. 另一方面, 在膀胱癌細胞裡Tim被發現過量表達. 總體而言，越來越多的證據表明TIM/TIPIN形成必不可少的複製叉保護複合物. 然而, TIM/TIPIN如何維護複製叉穩定的精確的分子機制, 以及如何激活複製檢查點, 還完全沒有理解. 此外, TIM和PARP1互動的體內功能意義仍有待探討. TIM或TIPIN的三維結構信息未知, 這嚴重地限制了我們理解TIM如何參與蛋白質複合體來維持基因組的穩定性. 在這個項目中，我們將完成以下目標: （i） 表徵TIM與PARP1 结合, TIM/PARP1晶體結構將被確定, TIM和PARP1互動的體內功能會被研究.（ii）表徵TIM識別DNA的分子基礎.
