776513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
776513.value: Recent GWAS have contributed important insights into the genetic architecture of common human diseases. The findings indicate that these diseases are typically under the influence of a very large number (at least hundreds) of sequence variants. The number of known susceptibility loci has reached 277 for autoimmune diseases, and 107 for metabolic traits. The majority of these loci have very small effect size, with allelic odds ratio of less than 1.5. The effects of multiple loci, that are significant at a certain p-value threshold, can be summated to give a “polygenic score” that significantly discriminate cases from controls. If the polygenic model is indeed a good approximation to reality, then the translation of GWAS findings to clinical practice (e.g. early diagnosis, risk assessment, prognostic evaluation) will probably involve the calculation of polygenic scores in order to summarize the information from numerous loci into a few interpretable indices. The central aim of this proposal is to develop new statistical methods of detecting and characterizing QTLs from GWAS data. These methods are based on the central tenet that the polygenic liability-threshold model is a good approximation for the underlying genetic architecture for many common diseases. The proposed methods are primarily statistical in nature, being concerned only with GWAS phenotype and genotype data. As such they should complement methods that leverage on functional information, such as gene-based and pathway-based analyses. The first proposed method is regression analysis using the estimated liability distributions of individuals as dependent variable, rather than affection status. This approach may offer advantages for the analysis of family data and the inclusion of known covariates. The second method is based on comparing the observed pattern of correlations between loci in affected individuals, to that expected for additive effects under polygenic liability-threshold model. The ultimate test of the two proposed methods is to apply them to real GWAS datasets. Since the above methods are predicated on the classic polygenic liability threshold model for complex disease, they may not work unless the assumptions of this model holds, at least approximately, in reality. Therefore, if the proposed methods work well in real data and lead to the detection of additional SNPs that reach the genome-wide level of significance, then this would provide strong support for the classic polygenic liability-threshold model. In practice, the additional SNPs detected will also enable the calculation of more informative polygenic scores, and provide novel targets for intervention. 最近全基因組關聯研究（GWAS）使科學家對人類常見疾病的遺傳方式有更深入的了解。這些研究發現人類常見的疾病通常受到大量（至少上百種）序列變異的影響。現在已知的自身免疫性疾病和代謝特性的易感基因位點已分別達到277與107個。儘管這些位點大部分的影響都非常小（等位基因的比值比小於1.5），但多個有一定顯著水平的位點的影響可累加得出「多基因分」用以從人口中區分出病患者。如果多基因模型真的接近常見疾病的遺傳方式的話，那麼通過多基因分的計算，科學家便可將無數位點的信息簡化為幾個可解釋的指數用於臨床實踐上（例如，早期診斷，風險評估，預後評估）。 這個提案的核心目標是要開發新的統計方法用以檢測GWAS數據中的數量性狀遺傳位點（QTL）和描繪其特性。這些方法的核心原則是用多基因傾向性阈值（liability-threshold）模型來解釋許多常見疾病的遺傳方式。由於建議的方法主要涉及GWAS的表型和基因型統計數據，它們與利用功能信息的方法（例如，以基因和通路為基礎的分析方法）正互補不足。 建議的第一種方法是回歸分析，但使用個人的疾病傾向性分佈作為因變量，而不是個人的病況。這可為家系數據與加入已知協變量的分析提供一定優勢。第二種方法是比較在病人觀察到的位點相關性模式與（在多基因傾向性阈值模型的加性效應下）預期的分別。 上述兩個方法將用到實際的GWAS數據作最終測試。由於這些方法的前提是多基因傾向性阈值模型，如果這假設在現實中不成立，這些方法可能就無法達到預期的效果。因此，如果這些方法在真實數據中產生預期的效果及檢測出更多（達到全基因組顯著水平）的單核苷酸多態性（SNP），這將為多基因傾向性阈值模型提供強而有力的支持。另一方面，額外檢測到的SNP可用作計算更信息性的多基因分，並為幹預提供新的目標。

776513.label: Realisation of objectives
776513.value: We have developed methods for the detecting of quantitative trait loci, including a new method of prioritization of pathogenic variants using inheritance-mode specific annotation data (Hsu et al, 2016), and a method for directly imputing the p-values of untyped polymorphisms from the p-values of neighboring polymorphisms, without needing to perform individual-level genotype imputation (Kwan et al, 2016). A regression-based methods for 2-stage QTL analysis has been developed, to take full account of the family history of the study subjects (Campbell et al, under review).This paper includes illustrative applications of the method on twin data on neuroticism. In collaboration with Dutch scientists, we have developed a new method of association analysis of multiple phenotypes, and demonstrated its power in a real data set on metabolic traits (Van der Sluis et al, 2015). We have also developed a simulation tool for power calculation (Li et al, 2015), and reviewed study design issues of genome-wide association studies of complex and quantitative traits (Sham and Purcell, 2014). Finally, we have applied our statistical methods to detect novel Asian-specific loci for blood lipid levels (Tang et al, 2015), and collaborated with UK scientists to demonstrate the presence of polygenic effects on the hypoglycemic response to oral diabetic medication (Zhou et al, 2014). Thus we have developed new statistical methods for the detection of quantitative trait loci and the characterization of polygenic components of complex traits, and applied these methods to real datasets to uncover novel loci and gain new insights.

776513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
776513.value: We have developed new methods for analyzing data from genome-wide association studies to identify DNA sequence variants that affect common diseases and health-related traits. The methods include one enables DNA sequence variants to be prioritized based on public data on their likelihood of involvement in dominant or recessive diseases, the convenient and fast calculation of the evidence of disease association, tools for determining optimal study design and sample size, a method for analysis several diseases or traits simultaneously, and a method can makes good use of family history information to boost the power to detect disease associations. Using our methods, we uncovered novel loci for metabolic traits from am existing datasets, and detected 3 novel Asian-specific low-frequency variants for blood lipid levels in the Chinese population.

776613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
776613.value: Low back pain (LBP) is a worldwide socioeconomic and health-care burden. Intervertebral disc degeneration is a risk factor associated with LBP. Studies have noted that altered metabolism may affect the normal integrity of the disc, which may contribute to degenerative changes and LBP. The Hong Kong Degenerative Disc Disease (DDD) Cohort Study is the world’s largest population-based study to systematically assess the clinical, environmental/lifestyle, and genetic aspects related to disc degeneration on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Based on this cohort, 1,800 subjects over the age of 40 years old were also assessed for cardiovascular risk factors in relation to disc degeneration and pain (i.e. DDD-Cardiovascular Cohort Study), within which 810 subjects underwent the world’s first metabonomic assessment via serum nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy. Initial analysis has identified for the first time various biomarkers, such as valine to histidine ratio, that were highly associated with the presence and severity of lumbar disc degeneration in this cohort. The current proposal will further address the role of serum metabonomics in relation to lumbar disc degeneration on MRI. The aim of the proposal is three-fold. For one (Aim #1), the proposal will address metabonomic profiling of the entire DDD-Cardiovascular Cohort Study participants (n=1,800) to further verify the initial metabonomic analysis in the 810 individuals. Secondly (Aim #2), replication studies will be performed to address metabonomic risk factors associated with disc degeneration between Asian and Caucasian populations (i.e. Finnish Birth Cohort 1966). Thirdly (Aim #3), a prospective study will be addressed to assess the prognostic utility of identified metabonomic biomarkers, specifically valine:histidine, to the future development of disc degeneration progression or protection in subjects who presented with no disc degeneration at baseline. Of these subjects with no disc degeneration at baseline, 50 subjects who had high-risk levels of the biomarker valine:histidine with no disc degeneration will be matched to 50 individuals with non-high-risk levels of the biomarker and will be assessed at the 5 and 8 year follow-up intervals to baseline. Imaging, clinical, and metabonomic profiling of these 100 subjects will be performed at each time interval since baseline. The stability or change of metabonomic levels between all three time points and their role in disc degeneration in time will also be assessed. These studies will broaden the understanding of the role of serum metabonomic biomarkers in relation to disc degeneration. Information gained will facilitate the world's first-ever assessment of Genome-Metabonomic-Environmental/Lifestyle studies of disc degeneration.

776613.label: Major findings and research outcome
776613.value: Lower back pain (LBP) is one of the most prevalent global health issues and a main cause of disability. Lumbar disc degeneration (LDD) is one of the major reasons for LBP, which could be evaluated by radiographic observations through magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Nevertheless, these MRI observations, as diagnostics for LBP/LDD, are prone to human error and may be insufficient in detecting real-time variations of complex biological systems. In our study, we aim to identify novel LDD biomarkers related to altered metabolism, which could aid personalized diagnosis and treatment of LBP. This study is based on a population cohort of 3, 584 southern Chinese. Over 1,000 individuals are followed with MRI scans, which are read by experienced physicians specialized in LDD. Statistical analyses show that (1) the severity of LDD is signicantly associated with lower disc level and (2) the five disc levels form two clusters. Accordingly, a systematic way to quantify the degree of LDD from raw MRI reads is adopted. Apart from phenotyping, 2,482 samples in the cohort are genotyped, and the serum samples of 757 individuals are acquired for proton NMR spectroscopy, resulting in 130 metabolomic measurements over three molecular windows. In order to discover genetic variants associated with different metabolomic measurements, genome-wide association studies (GWAS) are conducted on 571 individuals for each of the 130 metabolomic measurements. In total, 123 unique SNPs are found to be signicantly associated with one or more metabolomic measurements; among them, intergenic variants are underrepresented, whereas exonic, intronic and UTR3 variants are enriched. Our results suggest signicant associations between 42 different metabolomic traits and a number of genetic loci. For instance, polyunsaturated fatty acids are found to be signicantly associated with the FADS1/FADS2 loci, and CTTNBP2 is identied as a potential risk locus for a cluster of lipid / fatty acid related metabolites. The human metabolome is next estimated based on the summary statistics from previous GWAS and our GWAS via meta-analysis and polygenic scoring. The associations between (estimated) metabolomic data and various phenotypes (anthropometric, behavioral, clinical, and LDD-related) are tested using different regression methods, ranging from simple linear models to Lasso. Potential metabolomic biomarkers for LDD are identied, including blood lipid levels, the mean diameter for VLDL particles, sphingomyelins and tyrosine. In addition, our metabolomic dataset was also used to assess the implications of metabolic markers in different ethnic populations. This large-scale study was recently published in Frontiers Genetics (2018) and serves as a landmark paper in the field.

776613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
776613.value: We have established a collaboration platform with the Finnish cohort, and collected the GWAS and metabolomics data of our cohort subjects. This data can serve as the baseline for comparison with future follow up of these patients to study the prospective impact of metabolomic measurements on LDD and pain as well as their interaction with genetic markers.

776613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
776613.value: Lower back pain (LBP) is one of the most prevalent global health issues and a main cause of disability. Lumbar disc degeneration (LDD) is one of the major reasons for LBP, which could be evaluated by radiographic observations through magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Nevertheless, these MRI observations, as diagnostics for LBP/LDD, are prone to human error and may be insufficient in detecting real-time variations of complex biological systems. In this study we aim to identify novel LDD biomarkers related to altered metabolism, which could aid personalized diagnosis and treatment of LBP. From a cohort consisted of 3,584 community based Southern Chinese, over 757 individuals were assessed for proton NMR spectroscopy to assess their metabolomic measurements. Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) analysis were also performed on 571 individuals to assess the genomic influrence on metabolomic measurements and LDD. Our study is the "world's first" to have found significant genetic association with 42 metabolomic traits and identified the genetic locus that are associated with it. The associations between these metabolomic data and various phenotypes (anthropometric, behavioral, clinical, and LDD-related) are being tested.

776713.label: Project Objectives
776713.value: To evaluate the phylogenetic utility of a range of molecular markers which have not previously been used for the family in order to identify optimal markers for resolving comparatively recent evolutionary relationships within Goniothalamus. To generate a robust, well-supported and well-resolved phylogeny of Goniothalamus and related taxa, based on extensive taxon sampling and a broad range of molecular markers, and estimate divergence dates for critical nodes in the phylogeny by applying Bayesian relaxed molecular clock methods. To assess diversification rates within Goniothalamus and tribe Annoneae as a whole by generating semi-logarithmic lineages-through-time (LTT) plots, and to test for shifts in diversification rates over time using both temporal and topological approaches. To infer the sequence of past geographical migrations by optimizing the most probable ancestral areas for internal nodes in the phylogeny, and hence identify possible geographical explanations (e.g., founder effect) for changes in diversification rate. To infer evolutionary changes in morphology by reconstructing the most probable character states for internal nodes in the phylogeny, and hence identify possible key innovations that may provide adaptive explanations for changes in diversification rate. To further investigate possible adaptive causes for the putatively rapid evolutionary radiation by studying the pollination ecology, breeding system and seed dispersal mechanism of exemplar species of Goniothalamus. To investigate whether sister species have similar climate niches and to deduce the relative impact of climate niche divergence on speciation.

776713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
776713.value: Evolutionary biology research often focuses on either the process of evolution or the pattern resulting from this process. Molecular phylogenetic research, which is widely used to reconstruct evolutionary patterns, can also be used as the basis for understanding evolutionary processes, including functional interpretations of morphological evolution and the processes underlying past biogeographical migrations and dispersal events. The proposed research further consolidates the application of molecular phylogenetic data in understanding the process of evolution by testing hypotheses of evolutionary diversification. ‘Evolutionary radiation’ is commonly defined as the rapid diversification of a lineage, and is regarded as ‘adaptive’ if it can be shown to be correlated with morphological characters of functional significance and/or evidence of ecological diversification. There are many cases where sister group lineages (which are by definition of the same age) show markedly contrasting degrees of diversification. The study of such differences is of considerable interest in evolutionary biology as is key to understanding how factors such as the timing of diversifications, species attributes, environmental conditions, and the size and complexity of geographical regions have shaped current patterns of biodiversity. The Annonaceae, a species-rich pantropical family of flowering trees and woody lianas, is an ideal taxonomic group for studying evolutionary radiation. The genus Goniothalamus (with over 130 species) is of particular interest, as it appears to have undergone exceptionally rapid, recent diversification in Asia. The crown age of the genus has previously been estimated at c. 10–3.6 Ma, very young for such a species-rich genus. The proposed research has the following main objectives: (1) to generate a robust, well supported and resolved phylogeny of Goniothalamus and related taxa, based on extensive taxon sampling and a broad range of molecular markers; (2) to estimate divergence dates for critical nodes in the phylogeny by applying Bayesian relaxed molecular clock methods; (3) to assess diversification rates by generating semi-logarithmic lineages-through-time (LTT) plots, and to test for shifts in diversification rates over time using both temporal and topological approaches; (4) to correlate the results with the historical biogeography of the genus (by optimizing the most probable ancestral areas for internal nodes in the phylogeny and hence determine likely geographical migrations), and possible key evolutionary innovations (by reconstructing the most probable ancestral morphologies for internal nodes); and (5) to study the reproductive biology (pollination ecology, breeding system, and seed dispersal mechanism) of exemplar species to identify possible adaptive causes of the rapid evolutionary radiation. 进化生物学研究通常专注于进化的过程或者由此过程导致的模式。分子系统发生学研究广泛应用于进化模式的重建，也用于作为理解进化过程的基础，包括形态进化的功能解释和对过去生物地理上的迁徙和散布事件的过程理解。本研究进一步巩固了分子系统发生学数据通过验证进化多样化的假设以理解进化过程的应用。 “进化辐射”一般被定义为一个谱系的快速多样化，并且被认为是“适应性的”，如果这种多样化被证明与有功能意义的形态特征及/或者生态多样化证据有联系。很多姐妹群谱系（根据定义有相同的年龄）在多样化程度上呈现出显著的对比。研究这种差异在进化生物学中具有重要意义，因为这是理解一些因素是如何塑造现今的生物多样性模式的关键，如多样化的时机，物种的特性，环境的条件，以及地理区域的大小和复杂程度。 番荔枝科是一个物种丰富的包括开花的树及木质藤本的泛热带科。它是一个研究进化辐射的理想类群。其中特别有趣的一个属是哥纳香属（有超过130个种）。这个属似乎经历了最近在亚洲异常迅速的多样化。在之前的研究中，这个属的冠年龄估计为大约10–3.6百万年前，对于这样一个物种丰富的属来说异常年轻。 本研究有以下的主要研究目的：（1）利用大量的物种取样及多种分子标记生成一棵支持率高的解决的哥纳香及相关分类群的系统树；（2）应用贝叶斯松弛分子钟估算系统树中的关键节点的分歧时间；（3）通过生成半对数线的谱系时间图来评估多样化速率，并且通过时间及拓扑结构的途径检测多样化速率随时间的变化；（4）将结果与这个属的历史地理（通过优化进化树的内部节点的最可能祖先地区，并以此推断可能的地理迁徙）及可能的关键进化变革（通过重建内部节点的最可能祖先形态特征）相关联；（5）研究取样物种的生殖生物学（传粉生态学，繁殖体系，以及种子传播机制）以鉴别迅速进化辐射的可能适应性原因

776713.label: Realisation of objectives
776713.value: This was a highly integrative study, involving: (a) phylogenetic reconstruction of the genus Goniothalamus (in the early-divergent angiosperm family Annonaceae) based on a broad range of molecular markers (equivalent to objectives 1 and 2 as listed in section 5.1, above); (b) an assessment of diversification rates within the genus and the broader tribe Annoneae in which Goniothalamus is classified (objective 3); (c) an investigation of spatio-temporal changes in taxon distributions (objective 4); (d) an evaluation of changes in morphological characters perceived to be of functional significance (objective 5); (e) empirical studies of the pollination ecology, breeding system and seed dispersal mechanisms (objective 6); and (f) the use of ecological niche modelling to deduce the relative impact of climate divergence on speciation (objective 7). The project was largely successful, with objectives 1–6 all fully addressed, as detailed below. We successfully addressed objectives 1 and 2, generating a taxonomically well-sampled phylogeny (65 Goniothalamus species, representing 48.5% of the genus) based on the analysis of nine chloroplast DNA markers (atpB-rbcL, matK, ndhF, psbA-trnH, psbM-trnD, rbcL, trnL-F, trnS-G, and ycf1; representing in total 11,214 aligned positions). This was a significant advance on previous studies, which included only 20 Goniothalamus species and based on only three chloroplast regions. Our robust and expanded phylogeny was first published in Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution (impact factor = 4.419) in 2015, with an associated ‘data paper’ appearing simultaneously in Data in Brief. In addition to the robust taxonomic framework necessary for reconstruction of the phylogeny (with unpublished taxonomic data provided by the principal investigator), our studies furthermore identified a new species, Goniothalamus palawanensis, which was published in PhytoKeys (impact factor = 1.116) in 2013. The assessment of diversification rate changes (objective 3) confounded our expectations, however, by failing to identify evidence for a statistically significant acceleration in speciation rate in Goniothalamus (contradicting preliminary data previously generated in other research labs). We responded to this by broadening the scope of the diversification rate analysis to include the entire family: this was a major undertaking, which necessitated a much broader sampling strategy, extending this part of the work beyond the initial scope of the funded project. We are still analysing the data arising from this, and anticipate future publications from this. We decided against pursuing our investigation of the impact of ecological niche divergence of sister species on speciation (objective 7), however, because of this failure to successfully identify diversification rates shifts in the genus. Despite this setback, we proceeded to use the robust phylogeny generated for Goniothalamus as the basis for various down-stream analyses, including a biogeographical study of the genus and the broader tribe Annoneae. This paper is currently available as ‘early view’ in Journal of Biogeography (impact factor = 4.248) and will appear in print later this year. The work included the estimation of divergence dates for critical nodes by applying Bayesian relaxed molecular clock methods (included as part of objective 2) as well as the reconstruction of likely past geographical migrations (objective 4). We demonstrated that the significance of the ‘boreotropics’ hypothesis (in which intercontinental biotic migrations were possible via tropical forests that extended into northern latitudes during the Late Palaeocene-Early Eocene thermal maximum, 52–50 Mya) over alternative long-distance dispersal hypotheses. Our data revealed evidence for multiple vicariance events in the tribe Annoneae, including the crown node of the tribe (57–49 Ma, between Africa and N/S America), and the Disepalum-Asimina split (27–24 Ma, between Asia and N America). The Goniothalamus crown node was dated to 24–21 Ma, with several dispersal events from continental SE Asia to W Malesia identified in the Miocene, bridging the marine gap between the Sunda and Sahul Shelves by long-distance dispersal or rafting on tectonic plate microfragments. We also inferred evolutionary changes in functionally important morphological characters (objective 5) by identifying synapomorphies and estimating the phylogenetic signal of characters. The resultant study (published in 2015 in Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution; impact factor = 4.419) focused on fruit and seed characters in relation to patterns of frugivory and seed dispersal, concluding that fruits borne on older branches and/or on the main trunk have larger monocarps than fruits borne on young branches, and monocarps that contain seeds with a hairy testa are larger than those with glabrous seeds. We discussed fruit morphologies and potential explanations for the inferred correlations, suggesting that they are the result of adaptation to different frugivores (birds, larger non-volant mammals, and primate seed dispersers, respectively). The most exciting discoveries during the present research, however, are arguably those focused on empirical ecological studies of the reproductive biology of selected Goniothalamus species. We studied the floral phenology, pollination ecology and breeding systems of two sympatric Goniothalamus species in Brunei, with our results published in Scientific Reports (impact factor = 4.259) in 2016. Both species were protogynous with abbreviated anthesis over 23–25 h, and both are predominantly xenogamous and pollinated by small beetles. We demonstrated that coevolution and reproductive resource partitioning, reducing interspecific pollen transfer, is achieved by temporal isolation, due to contrasting floral phenologies; and ethological isolation, due to contrasting floral scents that contain attractants specific to the two beetle families. An effective pollinator trapping mechanism was furthermore demonstrated for both species, representing the first such report for the family. We regard this discovery of pollinator trapping as particularly significant, and potentially a key evolutionary innovation for Goniothalamus, increasing pollination efficiency by increasing pollen loading on beetles during the staminate phase, promoting effective interfloral pollinator movements, and increasing seed-set by enabling rapid turn-over of flowers. We extended our study to address the possible correlation with the daily activity patterns of the beetle pollinators, discovering a close temporal alignment between patterns of pollinator activity and the floral phenology driving the trapping mechanism. In addition to broadening the range of potential pollinators based on their circadian rhythms, this ‘circadian trapping’ of pollinators endows other selective advantages, including the possibility of an extended staminate phase to promote pollen deposition, and enhanced interfloral movement of pollinators. This work was published earlier this year in Frontiers in Plant Science (impact factor = 4.298). We also studied the function of the copious exudate that forms over the surface of the stigmas of many Annonaceae species, including Goniothalamus, with our results published in Journal of Integrative Plant Biology (impact factor = 3.962). We demonstrated that the stigmatic exudate functions in three ways: as a nutritive reward for pollinators; as a pollen germination medium; and as an extragynoecial compitum that enables pollen tube growth between carpels.

776713.label: Major findings and research outcome
776713.value: We developed a robust, well-supported and taxonomically extensively sampled phylogeny of the species-rich genus Goniothalamus, significantly extending previous studies (with 20 species, based on three chloroplast DNA regions) to include 65 species, based on nine regions. Our new phylogeny was published in Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution (92: 124-139) in 2015, with an accompanying ‘data paper’ (Data in Brief 4: 410-421). This phylogeny was initially used for several down-stream applications, including an evaluation of morphological evolution in the genus (Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution 92: 124-139). We were able to correlate changes in fruit and seed morphology with adaptations to different frugivores and seed dispersers (birds, larger non-volant mammals, and primates). We subsequently used the phylogeny as a basis for understanding spatio-temporal changes in distribution ranges (Journal of Biogeography, early view), demonstrating the importance of the ‘boreotropics’ hypothesis, in which intercontinental biotic migrations were possible via tropical forests that extended into northern latitudes during the Late Palaeocene-Early Eocene thermal maximum (52-50 Mya). We also identified several dispersal events from continental SE Asia to W Malesia during the Miocene, bridging the marine gap between the Sunda and Sahul Shelves by long-distance dispersal or rafting on tectonic plate microfragments. Our research therefore represents a solid contribution to a growing body of work on the historical biogeography of SE Asia. We also undertook a series of empirical ecological studies on the reproductive biology of selected species. We demonstrated coevolution of sympatric Goniothalamus species with associated reproductive resource partitioning with reduced interspecific pollen transfer, achieved by a combination of temporal isolation due to contrasting floral phenologies, and ethological isolation due to contrasting floral scents that contain pollinator-specific attractants (Scientific Reports 6: art. 35674. 2016). We also demonstrated the existence of pollinator trapping in Goniothalamus (Frontier in Plant Science 8: art. 1119. 2017), in which there is close temporal alignment between the patterns of pollinator activity and the timing of the floral phenological changes. This ‘circadian trapping’ mechanism has never been described in flowering plants before, and is of potential relevance to other plant lineages. We also undertook an evaluation of the function of the copious stigmatic exudate that forms in many Annonaceae species (Journal of Integrative Plant Biology, early view), confirming that the exudate functions in three ways: as a nutritive reward for pollinators; as a pollen germination medium; and as an extragynoecial compitum, allowing intercarpellary growth of pollen tubes.

776713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
776713.value: There are several avenues for potentially extending this research. We have plans to extend our work on circadian trapping of pollinators to assess its significance in other lineages, both within the Annonaceae and in other families. In addition to identifying circadian trapping in Goniothalamus, we also demonstrated its presence in the Dasymaschalon-Friesodielsia and Artabotrys lineages of the same family; although we were unable to confirm a statistically significant shift in diversification rate in Goniothalamus, we plan to conduct a parallel study of Dasymaschalon-Friesodielsia and Artabotrys. We also plan to assess whether circadian trapping occurs beyond the Annonaceae, and have identified Aristolochia species (Aristolochiaceae) as potentially having trap flowers that may function by the alignment of floral phenological changes with pollinator circadian rhythms. Our phylogenetic research on Goniothalamus integrates well with parallel studies of other genera with the same tribe Annoneae, including Disepalum. This has the potential for undertaking integrated studies of floral evolution and pollination ecology across the tribe.

776713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
776713.value: Evolutionary biology often focuses on either the process of evolution or the pattern resulting from this process. We applied molecular techniques, which are widely used to reconstruct evolutionary patterns, to understand evolutionary processes, including functional interpretations of morphological evolution and the processes underlying past biogeographical changes. We generated a robust evolutionary tree for Goniothalamus based on extensive species sampling and nine molecular markers, and estimated evolutionary divergence dates in the tree. We furthermore assessed diversification rates, although with limited success. We were nevertheless able to correlate the phylogeny with the historical biogeography of the genus (optimizing the most probable ancestral areas and hence determining likely geographical migrations), and possible key evolutionary innovations (by reconstructing the most probable ancestral morphologies). Our study also focused on the pollination ecology and breeding system of exemplar species. One of our most important discoveries was evidence for reproductive resource partitioning, in which co-occurring Goniothalamus species had adapted the timing of floral events and their floral scents so that they utilised different primary pollinators. More exciting, however, was our discovery of pollinator trapping and the alignment of the timing of the trap mechanism with the peak activity times of the pollinators.

777313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
777313.value: Stroke and neurodegenerative diseases are the most common diseases in aging population. Current therapies are seldom successful for improving clinical outcomes of those diseases. Recent progress indicates that neural stem/progenitor cells (NSCs) could be important therapeutic targets for brain repair. During neurogenesis, NSCs proliferation and cell fate decision are two key therapeutic targets for regeneration therapy, which are modulated by complex cellular signaling networks. Understanding the cellular signaling mechanisms in NSCs proliferation and cell fate decision are critical for regeneration therapy. Cellular signaling molecules for energy metabolisms appear to play a critical role in regulation of cell proliferation and development. APPLs could be one of the representatives. As endosomal adaptor proteins, APPLs can interact with many cellular signaling molecules for insulin secretion and energy metabolism, and its functions are initially linked to obesity and diabetics. Recent studies suggest that APPLs could regulate cellular growth and differentiations. APPLs comprise of APPL1 and APPL2 isoforms. APPL2 is reported to regulate cell proliferation and embryonic development, but its function in neurogenesis is unknown. During neurogenesis, Notch signaling pathway is well known to be a critical regulator for NSCs proliferation and cell fate decision. Thus, we conducted pilot studies to explore the roles of APPL2 in regulating Notch signaling pathway and neurogenesis. Overexprssion of APPL2 in mouse brain revealed to enhance Notch1 signaling, promote astrocytic differentiation but inhibit neuronal differentiation. Knockdown of APPL2 inhibited Notch1 signaling pathway, enhanced neurogenesis and decreased astrocytic differentiation in cultured NSCs. Those results indicate that APPL2 could be an unexplored signaling molecule in the modulation of NSCs proliferation and differentiation. Therefore, we hypothesize that APPL2 can modulate NSCs proliferation and cell fate decision through activating Notch signaling pathway. This proposal will include three special objectives: (1) To investigate whether APPL2 can regulate NSCs self-renewal and proliferation and promote astrocytic differentiation but decreased neuronal differentiation; (2) To study the potential roles of APPL2 in modulating olfactory performance in adult mice; (3) To verify whether Notch signaling pathway is involved in the regulations of APPL2 for cell fate decision. If the hypothesis can be verified, we will advance current knowledge about the molecular mechanisms of neurogenesis. Moreover, the success of the study will let us develop a novel molecular target for guiding proliferation and cell fate decision of NSCs for regeneration therapy, which will impact on developing novel therapeutic approaches for treatments of stroke and neurodegenerative diseases in future. 中風和神經退行性疾病是老年人最主要的兩大疾病，目前並沒有完全有效的治療方法。近期的研究顯示神經幹細胞可以成為大腦修復的重要靶點。在神經再生的過程中，神經幹細胞的增殖和分化由複雜的細胞間信號分子網路調控，是再生治療中兩大重要的研究方向。因此瞭解神經幹細胞增殖和分化的機制在再生治療的發展中起著非常重要的作用。 調節能量代謝的細胞信號分子在細胞增殖和生長過程中起著非常關鍵的作用。APPLs蛋白是其中一類代表蛋白。作為核內體的接頭蛋白，APPLs可以與很多信號分子相互作用從而調節胰島素的分泌及能量代謝，在肥胖及糖尿病的發生發展中起重要的作用。近期研究顯示APPLs也可以調節細胞生長和分化。APPLs包括APPL1 和APPL2兩個亞型。已有報導顯示APPL2可以調節細胞增殖和胚胎發育，但是還未見有報導闡述其在神經再生中的作用。在神經再生的過程中，Notch信號通路是已知經典的神經再生調節通路，其調節了神經幹細胞的增殖和定向分化。因此，我們進行了一系列的前期實驗揭示APPL2在神經再生及Notch信號通路的調節作用。我們的結果顯示過表達APPL2的轉基因小鼠Notch1信號通路增強並伴隨著增加的膠質細胞分化以及被抑制的神經細胞分化。降低APPL2可以抑制Notch1信號通路並抑制神經幹細胞向星形膠質細胞方向分化。這些結果提示了APPL2在神經幹細胞的增殖和分化過程中有著重要的作用。因此，我們假設APPL2可以通過啟動Notch信號通路調節神經幹細胞的增殖和分化。本研究計畫包括以下三個研究目標：（1）研究是否APPL2可以調節神經幹細胞的自我更新和增殖，並抑制幹細胞向神經元方向分化而促進其膠質分化。（2）研究APPL2在神經再生中的作用是否影響了成年小鼠嗅覺表現。（3）驗證是否APPL2定向分化的調節作用是由Notch通路介導的。如果我們的假說被驗證，將對神經再生的分子機制的研究有了進一步的認識。此外，此研究也將為再生治療的靶點研究提供一定的線索，為開發新型中風和神經退行性疾病的治療藥物提供基礎。

777313.label: Realisation of objectives
777313.value: Based on the main objectives of the project, we investigated the roles of adaptor protein, phosphotyrosine interaction, PH domain and leucine zipper containing 2 (APPL2) in modulating adult neurogenic regulations in mice. We have reached all of the goals in the original proposal. The research work mainly fulfills three objectives previously claimed in this project including (1) the roles of APPL2 in modulating adult neurogenesis; (2) the functions of APPL2 to regulating relative neural behaviors; and (3) the correlated signaling mechanisms of APPL2 to regulate adult neurogenesis. Details are showing the following content: 1. The roles of APPL2 to regulation of adult neurogenesis 1) APPL2 expression was increased in the process of induced NSCs differentiation in cultured neural stem cells (NSCs) in vitro. APPL2, rather than APPL1, was increased gradually after NSCs were induced to differentiate into both neuronal and astrocytic direction. Those discoveries suggest APPL2 are getting involved with the process of neurogenesis. 2) Overexpression of APPL2 oriented the NSCs developing into more astrocytes while knockdown of APPL2 enhanced neuronal differentiation in the cultured NSCs in vitro. The results of the in vivo animal experiments are consistent with the in vitro study. Compared with wild type mice, APPL2 transgenic (APPL2 Tg) mice had more glial cell formation in the Corpus callosum (CC) while fewer newborn neurons in olfactory bulb (OB). Thus, APPL2 could regulate cell fate choice of the NSCs during development. 3) APPL2 Tg mice had the suppressed neurogenesis at hippocampus, showing the limited NSCs proliferation, reduced neurogenic fate choice and up-regulated gliogenic fate choice, as well as the delayed maturation of young neural progenitor cells (NPCs). Those phenotypes eventually resulted in the decreased neuronal production in hippocampus of APPL2 Tg mice. In summary, we conclude that APPL2 could affect the cell fate choice in NSCs and regulate the neurogenesis at OB and hippocampus in adult brain. Those results suggest that APPL2 performs as the negative regulator to adult neurogenesis. 2. To study the roles of APPL2 in regulating animal behaviors relative with adult neurogenesis 1) Given the suppressed adult neurogenesis in OB, adult APPL2 Tg mice perform less sensitive in the olfactory discrimination tests (ODT) compared with WT mice. Moreover, the olfactory sensitivity test also indicates that APPL2 Tg mice presented the decreased sensitivity to odorant when comparing with WT mice. Additionally, with a mild stress induced by short-term corticosterone administration, the APPL2 Tg mice had the compromised olfactory sensitivity maintenance when compared with WT mice. Those results further indicate that APPL2 could regulate olfactory behaviors, affecting the adaptability of mice to psychiatric stress. 2) We further explored the emotional behaviors of mice in related to hippocampal neurogenesis. The behavioral tests showed APPL2 Tg mice exhibited a decreased mobility in forced swim test (FST) and tail suspension test (TST), reduced activity time in open field test (OFT) and the prolonged feeding latency in novelty suppressed feeding (NSF). The results suggest that APPL2 over-expression contributes to the inadaptability to stress in the mice and the mechanisms could be related to the decreased hippocampal neurogenesis. Olfactory system and hippocampus were two major neurogenic niches in adult brains. The strength of neurogenesis in those two sub-regions has important functions in mediating different neural behaviors. The behavioral studies on APPL2 Tg mice further confirmed the roles of APPL2 in regulating olfactory and emotional behaviors related with both neurogenic niches. Those results suggest the application potentials of APPL2 as a new target to regulate neural functions in neurological or psychiatric disorders. 3. To investigate the molecular mechanisms of APPL2 to adult neurogenesis 1) Our further investigation indicates that APPL2 can partially modulate Notch1 signaling pathway. Overexpression of APPL2 increased Notch intracellular domain (NICD) and hairy and enhancer of split-1 (Hes1) which could be considered as the downstream of Notch signaling pathway. Furthermore, in vitro study showed that knockdown of APPL2 suppressed NICD expression followed reduced astrocytic differentiation detected by GFAP expression. Moreover, DAPT, common Notch pathway inhibitors, conversely attenuated Notch1 signaling pathway with increased Tuj-1 expression and reduced GFAP expression in APPL2 overexpression group. Those results suggest that Notch1 is one of the main modulators of APPL2 to affect adult neurogenesis. 2) To test whether APPL2 could regulate adult neurogenesis related with the adaptability of animal to stress, we investigated the activity of glucocorticoid receptor (GR) in hippocampus. Compared with WT littermates, APPL2 Tg mice had enhanced GR phosphorylation under basic condition but had no different plasma CORT level and GR phosphorylation under stress stimulation. APPL2 Tg mice had the decreased hippocampal neurogenesis that was reversed by RU486, a GR antagonist. Combined with these discoveries, we conclude that APPL2 could affect the sensitivity of GR to peripheral stress hormone and consequently affect adult neurogenesis in hippocampus. Notch pathway is widely recognized as its central roles in controlling the transition of self-renew and lineage commitment of NSCs. Our findings offer the evidence that APPL2 regulates cell fate choice by mediating Notch pathways. Moreover, GR is the key to link with the neurogenic impairments with development of depression. APPL2 could affect neurogenesis by regulating activity of GR at baseline and its response when undergoing stress. Those findings help to deepen the understanding on the mechanisms of APPL2 in regulating adult neurogenesis. In summary, our studies identified the roles of APPL2 as the regulator to adult neurogenesis. The behavioral tests further offer new insight into the roles of APPL2 in modulating neurological functions. Given the relationship between metabolism factors with neural functions and their roles in neurological or psychiatric disorders, APPL2 could be a new therapeutic target in the treatments of neurological/psychiatric diseases via regulating adult neurogenesis. This is the first time to explore the function of APPL2 in nerve system. The discoveries in this project expand the horizon to recognize the new identified metabolic factor APPL2 from the angle of neurogenesis and neural functions. More importantly, our work provides the novel target to release the depression induced emotional and olfactory deficits, which could be a new area in drug development.

777313.label: Major findings and research outcome
777313.value: We have made following progress and had the major discoveries in the project: (1) APPL2 is involved with the differentiation process of NSCs by promoting glial formation but inhibiting neuronal differentiation in neurogenic regulations. APPL2 overexpression limits neurogenesis but stimulates gliogenesis in SVZ/OB system and hippocampus, two major neurogenic niches in adult brain. (2) APPL2 overexpression induces the impairment olfactory behaviors including odorant discrimination and olfactory sensitivity as well as the in-adaptability to psychiatric stress. (3) Notch signaling pathway and glucocorticoid receptor are two major signaling systems involved in the regulatory roles of APPL2 to adult neurogenesis. The study bring novel insight into understanding the mechanisms of APPL2 in modulating adult neurogenesis. More importantly, the study discovers that the metabolic factor like APPL2 could modulate adult neurogenesis and neural functions. Particularly, the neurogenic regulation from APPL2 impacts on the depression induced emotional and olfactory deficits and stress adaptability, which could be a new area for drug discovery.

777313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
777313.value: Given that APPL2 regulates adult neurogenesis and neurological behaviors, we propose that APPL2 could be a target for drug discovery in depression-related neurological disorders. Depression is the most common psychiatric disease associated with neurogenic impairment in the hippocampus. Recent progress suggests that the striking olfactory deficits are associated with the patients with major depression disorder (MDD). Animal study also showed that the decreased neurogenesis in SVZ/OB region and hippocampus are main contributors to olfactory deficits and emotional disorders in depressive disorders. With the discovery of APPL2 regulating adult neurogenesis and neural behaviors, we raise the hypothesis that APPL2 could be a potential target to attenuate depression induced emotional symptoms and olfactory deficits. Our further studies showed that baicalin, an active compound from a medicinal plant, improved the olfactory and emotional impairment in APPL2 Tg mice via promoting neurogenesis in the SVZ/OB and hippocampus. Moreover, baicalin performed as the antidepressant and alleviated the depression induced olfactory dysfunctions. Therefore, we believe that this is an important research direction for further study. We could further explore the therapeutic application potentials of APPL2 and use APPL2 as a therapeutic target in the treatment of depression and olfactory dysfunctions.

777313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
777313.value: Adult neurogenesis is a process of neural stem cells raises into mature neurons/glial cells in adult brain. Abnormal changing of neurogenesis usually results in different neural behavioral dysfunctions. With the support of RGC GRF grant, we conducted the studies to explore the roles of APPL2, a metabolic molecule, in affacting adult neurogenesis and depression and olfactory dysfunctions. We have identified APPL2 as a new neurogenic regulator affecting adult neurogenesis. APPL2 plays critical roles in regulating olfactory and emotional behaviors. Based on our discovery, a manipulation of neurogenesis in adult brain could achieve by targeting APPL2. Therefore, the most important progress of the study is that we step forward to understand the mechanisms of adult neurogenesis in related to depression and olfactory dysfunctions.The discovery make us search new drugs targeting on APPL2 for effectively treating psychiatric disorders like depression. Given that depression is one of the major psychiatric disorders in Hong Kong, our study would benefit Hong Kong public community.

777713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
777713.value: 心肌細胞主要提供心臟收縮功能。心肌梗死心肌細胞的損失是不可逆的由於其有限的再生能力，和通常會導致心臟衰竭。心臟移植術的終末期心衰療效治療受到捐助器官短缺。因此，基於細胞療法作為一種新型治療戰略心臟再生中已經出現。基於細胞療法的初始前提源自一系列開創性、 概念證明實驗展示卓越的再生力量的胚胎幹細胞來修復受損的心肌。然而，從它的發現後，超過十年的深入研究，胚胎幹細胞基礎治療中的兩個主要障礙仍未決定： (1) 免疫排斥反應和 (2) 道德關切。最近，人類誘導多能幹細胞由皮膚成纖維細胞的重程式設計返回到早期胚胎狀態而生成，已成為未來的細胞治療該最有吸引力的選擇。然而，幾個重要障礙必須要加以解決，然後才考慮任何有意義的臨床試驗。具體地說，像胚胎幹細胞，人類誘導多能幹細胞的自發心肌分化是效率非常低，呈現不足心肌細胞治療用途。更重要的是，人類誘導多能幹細胞分化出來的心肌細胞跟胚胎幹細胞源性心肌細胞極為相似表現出不成熟電生理和鈣處理屬性。這種不成熟的生理屬性不只導致的移植細胞跟本身心肌細胞不能融合，但也可能引起致命性心律失常。未能大型規模生產成熟人類誘導多能幹細胞分化出來的心肌細胞會嚴重妨礙幹細胞作為新型治療心功能衰竭的前景。從不同細胞類型生成的人類誘導多能幹細胞有不同的表觀遺傳記憶體,其前的分化狀態的機體功能。雖然此記憶體次要的殘餘的表觀遺傳印記呈現不完整重新程式設計，這種表觀遺傳記憶另一方面作為提高產量的最終所需細胞類型的一般性戰略被利用。在這裡我們建議，探討從心臟成纖維細胞重新分化入人類誘導多能幹細胞分化出成熟心肌細胞用於心肌再生上。從這項工作中獲得的功能和安全結果將大大改善我們對人類誘導多能幹細胞根據心臟的再生，隨後可能會導致這新的有效治療的治療終末期心衰平移應用的知識。

777713.label: Realisation of objectives
777713.value: Human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) have been successfully generated from a variety of somatic cell types. Although genuine cardiomyocytes can be readily differentiated from human iPSCs, there have been emerging evidences for an iPSC “memory” of its former differentiated phenotypes. This epigenetic memory could on the other hand be exploited as a general strategy to improve the yield of the ultimately desired cell types from human iPSCs. In the context of cardiac regeneration, this strategy may somehow be marked by restrain. This is because although adult cardiomyocytes possess the ideal set of epigenetic imprints to re-differentiate into cardiomyocytes after acquiring the pluripotent state, they do not normally proliferate and can only be maintained ex vivo for a very limited period thus making them an impossible cellular candidate for reprogramming. Alternatively, cardiac fibroblasts, the most populous cell type within the adult mammalian heart, which readily proliferate ex vivo and are easily transduced with reprogramming vectors, may be served as a better starting cell candidate for reprogramming. In fact, in addition to synthesis extra-cellular matrix in the adult heart, cardiac fibroblasts play an important role in cardiomyocyte growth during heart development. More importantly, during the embryonic cardiac development, cardiac fibroblast is envisaged to be derived from the proepicardium via epithelial-to-mesenchymal transformation, sharing the common origin of a common cardiogenic precursor population. Despite human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes representing a potential unlimited cell source for cell transplantation, their immature electrophysiological and calcium handling properties implying poor host-graft electromechanical integration and arrhythmogenicity is an ever so disturbing fact. Thus, it is needed to generate human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes with more mature phenotypes for safer transplantation. Exploiting cardiac fibroblasts, which possess the genetic imprints closer to cardiomyocytes, human iPSCs with higher cardiogenic potentials can be generated, and the resultant human iPSC-derived might have more mature electrophysiological and calcium handling property. Totally four human iPSC lines from different donor cell sources were successfully generated. In our preliminary experiment, skin fibroblasts (SFs) and cardiac fibroblasts (CFs) from two adult human donors were isolated and expanded. Then the SFs and CMFs were reprogrammed through retroviral transduction with SOX2, KLF4, OCT4 and c-MYC. After approximately 1 month, colonies positive for alkaline phosphatase with ESC-like morphology were isolated and expanded. By observation, both CF-iPSCs and SF-iPSCs exhibited similar morphologies, grow properties and expression of pluripotency surface markers (Figure 1). The pluripotency of the iPSC lines were confirmed using teratoma-formation assays with demonstration of derivatives of all 3 germ layers. Following characterization, the iPSC lines were differentiated into iPSC-CMs using EB formation method. At day 12 of cardiac differentiation, spontaneously beating EBs could be observed under brightfield microscope. Beating EBs were dissociated into single cells and characterized by fluorescent microscopy for immunostaining against cardiac-specific marker (e.g. cardiac troponin T). At day 21, a significant higher percentage of contracting EBs could be observed in CF-CMs (>80%) group than in SF-CMs (5%) group. The results were further confirmed and verified by flow cytometry (Figure 2A&B). The mRNA expression of cardiac specific markers (TNT/NKX2.5) increased significantly in CF-CMs group than in SF-CMs group using real-time PCR for detection (Figure 2C). The expression profiles of specific markers that involved in cardiac differentiation were investigated over the cardiac differentiation process. CF-CMs expressed a significantly higher level of cardiac gene, MESP1 (early cardiac mesodermal transcription factor) and GATA4 (late-stage cardiogenic transcription factor) during the process of differentiation (Figure 3). To examine DNA methylation status in four differentiated cell lines (SF18, SF19, CMF18, CMF19), four iPSCs (SF18-iPSCs, SF19-iPSCs, CMF-18iPSCs, CMF19-iPSCs), four iPSC-CMs (SF18-iPSCs-CMs, SF19-iPSCs-CMs, CMF18-iPSCs-CMs, CMF19-iPSCs-CMs) and two ES (HES3, H7) as control, the genome-wide DNA methylation were performed using Illumina’s 450K Infinium methylation assay according to the manufacturer’s protocol. The 450K data was subtracted from the background and normalized to the control in GenomeStudio. Quantitative socres of DNA methylation levels were obtained as β-values determined from the Illumina analysis ranging from “0”, for completely unmethylated, to “1”, for completely methylated. As assessed by unsupervised hierarchical clustering analysis and scatter plot of DNA methylation, human iPSCs could be clearly discriminated from their parent cells and were similar to ESCs. Comparison of differentially methylated site (DMSs) between SF- and CMF-iPSCs, and between iPS and ES cells show slight but significant difference (Figure 4A&B). The Venn Diagram showed around 166 DMSs between iPS and ES cells are IPS-specific DMSs, of which 148 sites overlapped between SF- and CMF-iPSCS, 11 sites are SF-iPSC specific and 7 are CMF-iPSC specific (Figure 5). Intracellular Ca2+ handling properties of both SF- and CF-CMs were also examined. Immature cardiomyocytes are less efficient in handling the intracellular calcium released during EC-coupling. In order to evaluate the calcium handling abilities of the iPSC-CMs, we have recorded the electricity stimulated calcium transients in the CF-iPSCs and SF-iPSCs derived cardiomyocytes using confocal microscopy. As shown in Figure 6. under low pacing frequencies (0.05 and 0.1 pace/second), the calcium transient profile in both CF-CMs and SF-CMs were similar. At higher frequencies (0.2 and 0.5 pace/second), the amplitudes of calcium transients were reduced in both group, but irregular transient profiles were only observed in the SF-CMs. Interestingly, when the stimulation rate were lowered 0.05 Pace/second, the calcium transient profiles of the CF-CMs returned to that observed at the beginning, however, in the SF-CMs, about 30-40% of the cells showed fibrillation. These results suggested that the CF-CMs were more resistant to stimulation induced calcium handling impairment and cardiac fibrillation. The real-time PCR revealed that the expression of calcium handling protein RyR2 increased in CF-CMs group (Figure 7). Abstract of the findings was submitted to a Medical Research Conference (MRC) in 2015 and presented as poster. The manuscript of the above findings is in preparation and will be submitted in peer-reviewed scientific journal. The 1st hypothesis (human iPSCs derived from cardiac fibroblasts exhibits a preference for redifferentiation into cardiomyocytes) is accomplished by generating human iPSCs from cardiac fibroblasts and dermal fibroblasts, and in vitro cardiac differentiation, followed by detailed assessment of the efficacy of cardiac differentiation. The results revealed that the number of cardiomyocyte yield was increased in CF-CMs as determined by flow cytomety analysis, enhance of cardiac gene expression as determined by RT-PCR, and identify genes of importance in cardiac differentiation using DNA methylation study. The 2nd hypothesis (human iPSC derived from cardiac fibroblasts exhibits more mature electrophysiological and calcium handling properties than that from dermal fibroblasts) is accomplished by performing cellular electrophysiological assessments and confocal microscopy for calcium transients. The data suggested that the CF-CMs were more resistant to stimulation induced calcium handling impairment and cardiac fibrillation which could be possibly due to the higher expression of RyR2 in CF-CMs (see attachment in Part C)

777713.label: Major findings and research outcome
777713.value: Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) have been derived from various somatic cells population through ectopic expression of defined factors and are a potentially unlimited source for the generation of cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs). However, it remains unclear whether iPSC-CMs generated from various cell sources of iPSCs are molecularly and functionally similar. This study aimed to assess the effect of epigentic memory on differentiation and function of iPSC-CMs generated from skin fibroblasts iPSCs (SF-iPSCs) and cardiac fibroblasts (CMF-iPSCs). Skin fibroblasts (SFs) and cardiac fibroblast (CMFs) from same adult human donors were reprogrammed into iPSCs through retroviral infection and then differentiated into iPSC-CMs by small molecules that inhibit WNT signalling pathway. The DNA methylation profiling of different iPSCs were then studied by BeadChip array. Following iPSC characterization, SF-iPSCs and CMF-iPSCs were differentiated into iPSC-CMs. At day 12 of cardiac differentiation, spontaneously beating CMs could be observed under brightfield microscope. Beating CMs were dissociated into single cells and characterized by fluorescentmicroscopy for immunostaining against cardiac-specific marker (e.g. cardiac troponin T). At day 21, a significant high percentage of contracting CMs could be observed in CMF-iPSC-CMs than in SF-iPSC-CMs group. The results were confirmed and verified by using flow cytometry. The expression levels of specific markers that involved in cardiac differentiation were investigated over the cardiac differentiation process. CMF-iPSC-CMs expressed a significantly higher level of MESP1 (early cardiac mesodermal transcription factor) and GATA4 (late-stage cardiogenic transcription factor) during the process of differentiation. To examine DNA methylation status in different lines, the genome-wide DNA methylation were performed using Illumina’s 450K Infinium methylation assay according to the manufacturer’s protocol. The 450K data was subtracted from the background and normalized to the control in GenomeStudio. Quantitative socres of DNA methylation levels were obtained as β-values. As assessed by unsupervised hierarchical clustering analysis and scatter plot of DNA methylation, human iPSCs could be clearly discriminated from their parent cells. Comparison of differentially methylated site (DMSs) between SF- and CMF-iPSCs showed slight but significant differences. Intracellular Ca2+ handling properties of both SF- and CMF-iPSC-CMs were also examined. The data showed functional variations between the iPSC-CM from different cell sources. Our results suggested that iPSCs retain an epigentic memory of their somatic cells of origin. These observations may influence ongoing attempts to use iPSCs for disease modelling and could also be exploited in potential therapeutic applications to enhance differentiation into desired cell lineages.

777713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
777713.value: These findings demonstrate that iPSC-CMs phenotype may be influenced by their cells of origin, and suggest that CF-CMs’ skewed differentiation potential may be advantageous for cell replacement therapy. Next, we are interesting in testing the cardiac functions of the engraftment of CF-and SF-CMs in our rodent myocardial infarction (MI) model to see if the cardiac function can be improved after the iPSC-CMs engraftment.

777713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
777713.value: Human-induced pluripotent stem cells derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs) are a promising cell source for disease modeling, drug screening, and vascular tissue engineering. However, current protocols for iPSC-CM derivation facing number of challenges, including variability in somatic cell sources and inconsistencies in cardiac differentiation efficiency. Although iPSCs are supposed to be genetically identical, the recent studies showed that their therapeutic discrepancy may be caused by the tissue-of origin epigenetic memory. In this research project, we aimed to investigate the potential effect of epigenetic memory on differentiation and function of iPSC-CMs generated form somatic cell sources of cardiac (cardiac fibroblasts, CFs) versus non-cardiac (skin fibroblast, SFs) origins. Our data highlight that donor cell source may affect lineage differentiation propensity and functional behaviors of their human iPSC derivatives. The CF-CMs perform better than the SF-CMS in terms of cardiac differentiation efficiency and electrophysiological properties. In conclusion, by generating genetically matched iPSC cardiomyocytes from different cell origins, we demonstrate that cellular origin of human iPSCs do affects the function of cardiomyocytes and using cardiac fibroblasts for iPSC generation could be a promising way to improve the efficiency in heart regenerative therapy in the future.

778213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
778213.value: 持久性泄殖腔（ PC ）是最極端的先天性肛門直腸問題，其特徵是直腸，陰道和尿道合流到一個共同管道並形成一個單一的會陰口。持久性泄殖腔的整形外科治療，對小兒外科醫生是一個挑戰，主要困難是恢復排尿和排便的控制和生殖功能。患者需要接受多次手術並終身監控。 PC的病例都是無家族史，而患者全都是女性。 PC是一個成因不明的發育障礙。然而，它可能與遺傳病因有關, 因為：(一）PC偶爾與遺傳性的多系統綜合症並全; (二）PC是一種最嚴重的肛門直腸畸形, ，其遺傳易感性通過我們以前的全基因組關聯研究得到確定; ，(三）有脊柱尾部發育相關基因變異的動物具有類似泄殖腔的表徵。可以肯定，那些發育基因的DNA變異可以導致PC。但是，目前還沒有在已檢測候選基因的患者發現特定的基因異常。事實上，罕見，散發和先天性疾病的遺傳病變是違反傳統的遺傳學（病例少，而不是家族性）。遺傳學上，這些情況只能在有非遺傳性或隱性遺傳DNA變異的患者身上發現。非遺傳性變異解釋了為什麼危及病人生殖健康的罕見及毀滅性疾病（如PC）仍時有發生。 我們建議透過全基因組測序（ WGS ）再加上10個受影響的女孩和不受影響父母的高分辨率染色體核型分析, 找出導致PC的遺傳病變 。 選擇WGS的原因是控制基因表達的DNA調控元件位於基因以外, 其他測序方法是不能函蓋的。之所以將重點放在調控元件是因其在妊娠過程中可調控基因表達的時空控制。調控元件變異可能導致先天性疾病。 家庭（父母與子代）為基礎的方法允許通過家長/孩子篩查, 找出PC家庭遺傳性的, 及生殖細胞非遺傳性的變異。發生率較高的基因突變或染色體區域/基因突變，將在不同的患者組（N=50）中驗證，以確定這些硏究發現和PC的關係。 這是首個PC的全基因組研究。由於WGS越來越實惠，並最終將被用作臨床設置，我們希望為香港開創一個先例。將WGS常規使用於罕見疾病的診斷。

778213.label: Major findings and research outcome
778213.value: The most important finding is the discovery of damaging de novo CDX2 variants in two patients. These variants altered the expression of CYP26A1, a direct CDX2 target encoding the major retinoic acid (RA)-degrading enzyme. Other RA genes, including the RA-receptor alpha, were also mutated. Moreover, genes governing the development of cloaca-derived structures were recurrently mutated and over-represented in the basement membrane components set (q-value<1.65x10-6). This is the first evidence that PC is genetic, with genes involved in the RA metabolism at the lead. For the first time, a gene recapitulating PC in mouse models is found mutated in humans.

778213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
778213.value: Given the frequency of CDX2 de novo variants and the role of RA, our observations could potentiate preventive measures.

778213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
778213.value: We have found that Cloaca is due to alterations in the DNA of genes that control the regulation of the caudal/anal region during gestation. Importantly, the alteration affects a protein that metabolizes vitamin A. This means that perhaps the disease could be prevented by giving vitamin A to pregnant mothers at risk. Nevertheless, there may be other genes also causing the same disorder and caution is needed.

778813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
778813.value: 傳染病仍然給發展中地區帶來災難性的影響，高死亡率和高發病率往往與其無效的診斷方法息息相關。21世紀科學技術的一大挑戰是開發低成本、簡單易用、功能強大、現場即時（POC）的診斷方法，以便在資源貧乏的環境下有效的診斷和管理傳染病。世界衛生組織針對POC診斷發布的ASSURED准則即：經濟、靈敏、特異、易使用、快速穩定、無需設備和可送遞。本課題的負責人近期開發了用於瘧疾診斷的核酸適體，並應用其識別瘧原虫蛋白。本課題的協同負責人在POC診斷發展方面處於世界領先地位，其開發的很多診斷測試目前已經在臨床使用。本課題中，我們將結合專長開發一種能夠實現ASSURED准則的POC診斷：“三維印刷適體啟用的瘧疾診斷多米諾”。 三維印刷是一種低成本的定制設計和制造方法，完全改變了個體親自設計的方式，改善並發展了三維對象和設備。最近在三維印刷反應容器和微流體設備方面的發展已經証明此項技術可應用於生物技術領域。在此，我們意在使用三維打印制造“診斷多米諾”，其中一個模塊就是一個微流體裝置，可在針刺血液中檢測到瘧疾蛋白的存在，不需昂貴（或任何）的設備即可通過肉眼確認顏色的明顯變化。 本課題中，我們將設計、開發、三維打印和測試四個診斷多米諾，並將其串聯作用於最后的裝置中 ─ 檢測瘧原虫乳酸脫氫酶（泛種瘧原虫檢測，診斷一般性瘧疾），檢測瘧原虫富含組氨酸蛋白II（惡性瘧原虫特異性檢測，診斷其引發的高危性瘧疾），作為陽性對照，作為陰性對照。我們還將進一步在三維打印的支架中對抗體和核酸適體進行橫向比較。這種方法在理論上可以擴展到從單一的針刺血液中實行模塊化的多種疾病的診斷。整個設備的成本將不超過30美分，且不需要專門的儀器，這種新技術有可能對發展中世界除瘧疾之外其他疾病的診斷具有重大影響。

778813.label: Realisation of objectives
778813.value: All objectives have been fully realized for this research project. We have developed 3D-printed devices for diagnostics (though after peer review we did not use the term 'dominoes' although the idea is similar in our papers). We have compared to antibody-based devices (eg. see our Chem Comm paper). We have built various types of prototypes (eg. see ACS Sensors and Biosensors & Bioelectronics papers) and we are perfectly positioned now for the follow-up work. If there is any shortfall in objectives it is in the modularity in objective 4, but actually we have determined this is not necessary at this time. In our early work on this project we demonstrated the development of an assay terms aptamer-tethered enzyme capture (APTEC) which was shown to reliably diagnose malaria in clinical blood samples. This was published in Chem Comm in 2015. We next integrated with 3D printing to develop two designs of diagnostic test in a comparative approach. This was published in ACS Sensors in 2016. Next we found we needed to improve the Aptamers to get higher sensitivity by a new method we termed ‘Aptamer Affinity Maturation’ which was published in Analytical Chemistry in 2016. Finally we developed an entirely reagentless magnet-guided 3D printed diagnostic assay which was tested in various clinical scenarios which was recently published in Biosensors & Bioelectronics in 2018. In all these papers the PI was communicating author and various of his PhD students were first authors. In addition, we filed two patents on this work. These are now being licensed by an Australian diagnostics company who will partner to move onto clinical trials in developing world. Taken together, this has been a remarkably successful project which is even being considered as an Impact Case for RAE.

778813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
778813.value: Diagnosis of malaria at the point of care remains a significant challenge. Better technologies which are more sensitive, more robust and less expensive will significantly reduce global deaths from malaria. We had previously identified new binding molecules made of DNA called Aptamers to help identify the molecules in our blood which indicate malaria infection. In this grant, we had successfully integrated these molecules into innovative, cheap, sensitive assays using 3D printing for diagnosing malaria. We tested these approaches in clinical blood samples and demonstrated they could be better than other presently used methods. The next stage of this research is to partner with other stakeholders to investigate device mass production, clinical testing and clinical trials in larger populations. If this is successful this could lead to better, cheaper and faster ways to diagnose malaria with the potential to significantly reduce malaria deaths. Furthermore, the technologies developed can have impact more widely in biomedical diagnosis.

779313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
779313.value: Tendon injury is common. It can result from sports injury, accident or overuse. Despite improvement in the management of tendon injury over the past few decades, we still face the problems of tendon re-rupture, weakness, pain and stiffness after tendon injury. Tendon healing is a complicated process. It is initiated by inflammation at which inflammatory cells migrate to the injured areas to remove debris. The is followed by the proliferation of tenocytes to repair the injured tendon by depositing new tissue onto it. However, the repaired tendon is usually mechanically weaker because they are being replaced by structurally inferior fibrotic tissue. Furthermore, the tendon is surrounded by adhesions, which further affects the normal tendon movement. Tissue fibrosis is not unique to tendon injury and it can take place in different organs of the body. There is clear evidence supporting that inflammation is closely related to tissue fibrosis. It is logical to think that suppressing inflammation is the key to control fibrosis. Silver nanoparticles have very unique physicochemical properties. It has great anti-inflammatory action, cell regulatory function, and antibacterial effect. Our research group has previously shown that silver nanoparticles can help to speed up wound healing and restore the mechanical property of the skin by enhancing collagen maturation. We believe that such potent wound healing power is likely contributed by their anti-inflammatory and cell regulatory action. Since the skin and tendon share many similarities in their healing, we further explore the use of silver nanoparticles in tendon healing using an animal model. From our preliminary results, we find that silver nanoparticles significantly improve the tendon healing by enhancing the collagen production and deposition even at an early phase of healing. We hypothesize that silver nanoparticles can modulate the inflammation caused by tissue injury and prevent excessive production of extracellular matrix. This therefore helps to regulate tissue regeneration and to minimize tissue fibrosis. We also postulate that silver nanoparticles can stimulate cell activities in the process of tendon healing and therefore speed up the healing process. The aim of this study is to know how silver nanoparticles alter cell activities in terms of the extracellular matrix production and thereby enhances tendon healing. To the best of our knowledge, the role of silver nanoparticles in tendon healing has never been reported in the literature. 肌腱損傷是一種常見的損傷。運動損傷，意外事故或過度使用都可能造成肌腱損傷。儘管在過去幾十年中，肌腱損傷的治療取得了一定進展，治療後的肌腱仍然存在再次斷裂，強度差，疼痛和僵硬等問題。肌腱的癒合是一個複雜的過程。癒合的初始階段是炎症反應，表現為炎症細胞遷移到損傷區域並清除損傷的組織碎片。之後，肌腱細胞開始增殖並在其上沉積新的組織以修復受損的肌腱。然而，修復的肌腱的機械強度通常比完好的肌腱差。這是因為部分肌腱組織被纖維組織取代，導致肌腱的結構完整性變差。另外，癒合的肌腱被黏性組織包裹，進一步影響了肌腱的活動。 組織纖維化不僅會發生在肌腱損傷中，也會發生在身體裡的其它器官。有充分的證據支持，炎症反應與組織纖維化有密切的關係。因此，抑制炎症反應很可能是防止組織纖維化的關鍵。銀納米顆粒具有非常獨特的理化性能。它表現出很強的抗炎症作用，細胞調控功能以及抗菌能力。我們前期的研究表明，銀納米顆粒可以加速皮膚傷口癒合，並能促進膠原成熟從而使癒合的皮膚恢復機械性能。我們相信銀納米顆粒這種促進傷口癒合的能力很可能歸因於它的抗炎症作用和細胞調控功能。由於皮膚和肌腱的癒合過程非常相似，我們利用動物模型，進一步研究了銀納米顆粒在肌腱癒合中的作用。該研究發現，銀納米顆粒非常明顯地加速了肌腱損傷的癒合。即使在癒合的早期階段，銀納米顆粒也能極大地促進膠原的產生和沈積。我們推測銀納米顆粒調節了組織損傷引起的炎症反應，防止過量細胞外基質的產生，因此能幫助組織再生並極大降低組織纖維化的發生。我們還假設銀納米顆粒在肌腱癒合的過程中可以激發細胞活性，從而加速癒合的過程。本課題的目的是研究銀納米顆粒如何調節細胞活性以改變細胞外基質的產生，從而促進肌腱的癒合。據我們所知，銀納米顆粒在肌腱癒合中的作用尚未有文獻報導。

779313.label: Realisation of objectives
779313.value: All objectives have been achieved and one peer reviewed paper has been published in the Journal of Nanomedicine: Nanotechnology, Biology, and Medicine in 2014. The results of the studies were presented in a number of scientific meetings internationally, regionally and locally. (1) Establishment of tendon injury animal model: An injury model was successfully created in both mice and rats. The study was based on the rat injury model because of the size seemed more appropriate. (2) Evaluation of the effects of AgNPs on tendon function recovery: The gait analysis of the rats and tensile strength of the regenerated tendon were evaluated. The information of the tensile strength of the tendon was published in the paper mentioned above. (3) Assessment of repair and fibrosis progression by immunohistochemistry to establish a temporal relationship in tendon healing: The evaluation was done and results were published accordingly. In addition, another evaluation process "Second Harmonic Generation Imaging" was used to supplement the effects. (4) Identification of the modulatory action of AgNPs by studying the anti-inflammatory action, cell activity and extracellular matrix: The above were all completed. The proteoglycans were evaluated in the studies and the relationship between AgNPs and the cellular activities were established.

779313.label: Major findings and research outcome
779313.value: This study demonstrates a novel method of using silver nanoparticles for Achilles tendon injury healing. In vitro results indicated a stimulatory effect on cell proliferation and collagen synthesis with silver nanoparticles. Biomechanical test on the 42-day post operation Achilles tendon sample exhibited a significant improvement in tensile modulus when compared to the untreated group. Histology suggested that silver nanoparticles promoted cell alignment and proteoglycan synthesis. The collagen deposition was also improved. An alleviation of tumor necrosis factor α, and an increase in fibromodulin and proliferating cell nuclear antigen expression were seen in silver nanoparticles group by immunohistochemistry. This study further corroborates the finding of our previous study that silver nanoparticles help to restore the functionality of injured connective tissues. We believe that the anti-inflammatory nature of silver nanoparticles has an important role in accelerating the healing process and reducing scarring, leading to better functional outcome.

779313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
779313.value: There is great potential to apply the nanomedicine to clinical practice. The benefit is huge as it will help to speed up the tendon healing in patients suffering from tendon injury.

779313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
779313.value: Tendon injury is common. The healing process is long and potentially problematic e.g. weakness and stiffness of the joint. This study is the first study demonstrating that silver nanoparticle can improve and speed up tendon healing in rat's Achilles tendon. Silver nanoparticles are shown in this study to control adverse inflammation and improve the structural architecture of the repaired tendon to achieve better structural property within a short period of time. This is well demonstrated in the tensile strength tests, histology and imaging studies. Silver nanoparticles are also safe as there is no adverse effects identified in the animals. Further studies will be required in larger animals including humans to demonstrate its effectiveness. It is potentially very useful clinically as it can help patients to recover faster especially the athletes who need to return to competitive sports activity earlier.

779513.label: Realisation of objectives
779513.value: The study was able to characterize the effect of esophagectomy on pharyngeal phase of swallowing with the following significant findings 1.Twenty-nine post-esophagectomy patients who were more than six months postoperative were assessed using validated swallowing-related, general and esophageal cancer-specific quality of life (QOL) questionnaires. Reductions in swallowing-related QOL were apparent, yet general QOL was similar to the general population. This suggests continued swallowing issues late after esophagectomy and suggests that more focus should be placed on swallowing at this stage. 2.Twenty-nine long-term post-esophagectomy patients underwent video-fluoroscopic swallowing study (VFSS). Dysphagia predominantly affected the pharyngeal phase and was of mild to moderate severity. 3. Risk factors for developing pharyngeal dysphagia included males, and those of advanced age at esophagectomy and advanced age at swallowing assessment. Higher pN stage and less time from esophagectomy were associated with worse penetration and aspiration. 4. High resolution manometry (HRM)was performed on 29 long-term post-esophagectomy patients and showed that all measured pressures differed from norms except for velopharyngeal maximum pressure. Average maximum pressures in the residual cervical esophagus were higher than norms. We were not able to assess the efficacy of early swallowing therapy on improving swallowing dysfunction after esophagectomy, primarily on the improvement of the upper esophageal sphincter function through a randomised controlled trial. We were only able to recruit 2 subjects with oropharyngeal dysphagia early post-esophagectomy underwent six weeks of swallowing therapy are presented. Definitive improvements were seen on VFSS. Changes on HRM measures were seen after swallowing therapy. We cannot concluded that the changes were due to improvement with time or effect of swallowing therapy as we were not able to conduct a randomised trial. The failure in achieving the the randomisation is due to the reluctance of the patients to undergo further rehabilitation exercise after a long period of treatment for their oesophageal cancer. Also most patient subjectively do not feel the presence of pharyngeal dysphagia after esophagectomy

779513.label: Major findings and research outcome
779513.value: Mild to moderate pharyngeal dysphagia is present in patients who had undergone esophagectomy for oesophageal cancer.The major deficits included delayed onset of the pharyngeal swallow; all patients had some degree of valleculae residue and all patients had impaired laryngeal elevation. The majority of the patients had pyriform sinus residue and pharyngeal coating, while the pharyngeal transit time was within normal limits. The majority of this cohort had supraglottic penetration. The mean Penetration-Aspiration Score was 4.1 (SD = 2.5, range 1 to 8) and 1.5 (SD = 0.9, range 1 to 4) for thin and semisolids respectively. This study found that dysphagia was more severe in males, and in those of advanced age at esophagectomy and swallowing assessment. A higher pN stage was associated with more difficulties on thin fluid and time since esophagectomy was an important factor that was associated with penetration and aspiration. These findings may have implications on which patient groups should be prioritized for early swallowing assessment and therapy.

779513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
779513.value: Pharyngeal dysphagia is definitely present in patients after esophagectomy. Future research concentrate on the use of pre-emptive swallowing therapy to improve the pharyngeal muscle function and swallowing effort during the stage of neo-adjuvant chemo-radiation in addition to early post-operative swallowing assessment to identify patients with swallowing dysfunction and application of early swallowing therapy to improve the long term swallowing function.

779513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
779513.value: Esophagectomy is a surgery to remove part of the disease oesophagus for cure of esophageal cancer. Esophargeal cancer patients usually have swallowing problems due to the mechanical obstruction of the esophagus by the tumor. Surgical removal of the diseased esophagus should improve the swallowing problem. The current study finds that even though the mechanical obstruction of the oesophagus is removed after esophagectomy, the swallowing function in the pharynx did not return to normal. Actually patients after esophagectomy had persistent mild to moderate swallowing problems that include delay in triggering swallowing and penetration of food particles into the larynx. These abnormalities can lead to loss of quality of life and risk of developing chest infection from aspiration. Risk factors for developing more severe swallowing function included male gender, advanced age and presence of larger metastatic lymph nodes in the original cancer. Pilot study showed that swallowing therapy may improve the swallowing impairment in this group of patients but larger scale studies would be needed to determine the extent and timing of the swallowing therapy.
