779713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
779713.value: EBV游离基因体在宿主鼻咽上皮细胞中的动态变化 摘要： EBV感染一直被认为是与鼻咽癌的发病密切相关的一个重要因素。低分化型鼻咽癌是华南及香港地区人群中最常见的鼻咽癌类型。研究发现，100%的低分化鼻咽癌组织中都存在着EBV感染。然而，目前除了一株细胞株之外，其他所有被EBV感染的鼻咽癌细胞株在体外培养一段时间后都极易丢失EBV基因体。这表明在体外培养环境中，被EBV感染的鼻咽癌细胞缺失选择性的生长优势。关于EBV在宿主细胞中的动态变化以及保持EBV长存于宿主鼻咽癌组织中的调控机理如今仍不明确。 本实验室长期利用永生化的鼻咽上皮细胞进行关于EBV感染的研究。EBV在即时感染鼻咽上皮细胞后，游离基因体通常会在感染后两周内丢失。但是，通过从被感染的鼻咽细胞中筛选单克隆株，本实验室成功建立被EBV稳态感染并且能在体外分裂增殖的鼻咽上皮细胞株。这些稳态感染细胞株是很重要的细胞模型,可以用以研究EBV游离基因体在宿主细胞中的动态变化以及维持此稳态感染的机制。这些研究将有助于我们了解EBV在癌前病变的鼻咽上皮细胞中建立稳态感染的生物学机制。 本课题将运用荧光原位杂交技术（FISH）来检测在宿主鼻咽上皮细胞中EBV游离基因体的拷贝数，同时利用活细胞成像技术（live cell imaging）研究可视化EBV在感染鼻咽上皮细胞后几轮细胞分裂的动态过程。我们还将明确及记录EBV在鼻咽上皮细胞中复制以及分离的活动。 本课题将进一步探究其他相关基因的调节机制（例如p16及cyclin D1）对EBV游离基因体动态变化的影响，并研究EBV入侵鼻咽上皮细胞后是否会进行基因组扩增。本课题还将深入探讨EBV编码的两种主要病毒蛋白EBNA1 和BZLF1对于维持EBV游离基因体在宿主鼻咽上皮细胞中的稳定水平的作用。 此外，我们观察到，长期体外培养筛选出的EBV宿主鼻咽上皮细胞对白介素-6的反应更敏感, 更容易激活的STAT3通路。 STAT3通常被认为是能够激活ENBA1基因表达的特异性启动子，而EBNA1的表达则对于EBV游离基因体在宿主细胞中的长期维持极其重要。 因此, 本课题将继续研究激活或者抑制STAT3的活性是否影响EBV游离基因体在宿主鼻咽上皮细胞中的存在和维持,并探索这种影响是否有利于EBV在体内癌前病变鼻咽上皮组织中的持续感染。这些研究结果将阐明STAT3通路或/和其他可能的炎症因子主导的信号通路的激活对于维持EBV在体内鼻咽癌组织内稳态感染的作用。

779713.label: Realisation of objectives
779713.value: Objective 1. To examine the dynamics of loss of EBV episomes in EBV-infeced nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. There are two approaches for this part of investigation: (i) The dynamics of loss of EBV episomes was examined in 3 immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells infected with a GFP-tagged EBV. On average, we were able to achieve a 30 to 60% of EBV infection rate in immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. The quantization of EBV in the infected cells was by EBV-FISH and quantitative PCR. The major findings are: (a) Loss of EBV was rapid in the first two weeks post infection and was likely to be induced by multiple factors including arrest of cell cycle in EBV-infected cells, induction of lytic reactivation, induction of innate defense of host cell to EBV infection and degradation of liberalized EBV; (b) stable EBV infection could be achieved in these EBV-infected nasopharyngeal epithelial cells after repeating cell sorting by FACS guided by the GFP-tagged EBV. The nature of EBV infection switched from lytic to latent infection. During this process, there may be epigenetic modification of EBV in infected nasopharyngeal cells achieving latent infection and (c) Activation of cyclin D1 and notch signaling were observed in infected epithelial cells which may be involved to support latent EBV infection in epithelial cells. (ii) The dynamics of loss of EBV episomes in stable EBV infected epithelial cells was monitored by real-time live cell imaging using the AGS cells using a visible EBV tagged with tomato red fluorescence protein. (This part of work was carried out in close collaboration with Prof. Bill Sugden at University of Wisconsin, Madison, USA. This involved exchange of research materials involved in this project and training of a postgraduate student, Ms. Zhou Yuan, for six month in Prof. Sudden's lab in Madison, Wisconsin, USA and the successful transfer of the special imaging platform to University of Hong Kong. This part of the investigation was carried out in different stages: (a) Establishment of stable infection of a visible virus in human epithelial cell line (AGS-CR2). Professor Bill Sugden's laboratory has generated the visible EBV which enables live cell imaging of the dynamics of EBV episome at a single cell level . This visible EBV is genetically modified to encode hygromycin resistance gene, the lactose repressor protein (Lacl)-tdTomato fluorescent fusion protein and 250 copies of lactose operator (lacO) sequence. In a host cell’s nucleus, the Lacl-tdTomato fluorescent fusion protein specifically binds to lacO sites on EBV genome and “lights up” the EBV genome for live cell imaging. The increase in intensity of fluorescence signals reveals the replication and partition process of EBV episomes. The infection of viEBV was attempted in two epithelial cell lines, NP460hTert (immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells) and AGS-CR2 cells (gastric cancer cells). The infection efficiency of NP460hTert with viEBV was low and could not be used for dynamic study of EBV episomes during cell division. viEBV infection of AGS-CR2 cells was successful and was used for live cell imaging of EBV replication and partition in this study. (b) Visualization of EBV dynamics during cell division of infected AGS-CR2 cells. Live cell imaging was used to observe the dynamics EBV replication and partitioning through the cell cycle. A LED light source provided low intensity light to minimize phytotoxicity and highly sensitive EMCCD camera was used to detect the weak fluorescence signal. The dynamics of EBV replication and partition in mitotic cells was monitored for 60 hours. The EBV episomes were identified as punctuate fluorescent signals distributed in the nuclei. CAPS was used to select and measure fluorescent signals in microscopy images in multiple z planes with subtraction of background. Segregation of EBV-infected epithelial cells was observed to be highly uneven which may contribute to rapid loss of EBV particles in infected epithelial cells. On average, one daughter cell received 17% more viEBV genomes than the other daughter. In the absence of selective force, these EBV episomes will be lost in infected epithelial cells upon propagation which may explain the common loss of EBV episomes in most EBV-infected epithelial cells notably nasopharyngeal carcinoma cells. The current live cell imaging system for EBV dynamics will enable further investigations into cellular factors on persistence of EBV in epithelial cancer cells which are largely unknown at present. Elucidation of these conditions will contribute to the understandingof the role of EBV infection in human epithelial cells and its potential contribution to epithelial malignancy. The summary of this part of the study is submitted to Scientific Report and was invited for resubmission with minor revision. Objective 2. To examine the involvement of specific EBV genes in the dynamics of EBV episomes. We have monitored the effects of EBV genes involved in the dynamics of EBV episomes. Expression of the latent EBV genes, notably the EBNA1, are most important in the maintenance of EBV episomes. Using a specific drug against EBNA1, we observed specific killing of EBV-infected NPC cell lines. The expression of EBNA1 was stabilized in stably infected epithelial cells. Stabilization of EBV episomes in infected epithelial cells involved stable expression of latent EBV genes. Elevation of other latent EBV genes including EBER, LMP1 and 2 were also observed in stably infected nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. The profile of EBV gene expression during establishment of stable EBV infection was followed carefully in immortalized nasopharyngeal epithelial cells at early and late stages of infection. Lytic EBV genes were more prominent observed at early stage of EBV infection which was replaced by expression of latent EBV genes. The switching of EBV gene expression is likely to involve epigenetic modification which will be examined in the next stage of investigation. This part of the study has been submitted to J. of General Virology for publication and is recommended for major revision before resubmission. Objective 3.To examine the role of STAT activation in the dynamics of EBV episomes in infected nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Using the various EBV-infected epithelial cells, we have examined the various growth conditions and cell signaling pathways supportive of stable maintenance of EBV episomes in infected epithelial cells. We have tried multiple cytokines. Among them, the IL6, which activate STAT3 signaling, could enhance the maintenance of EBV episomes in infected epithelial cells. Careful dissection of the underlying factors showed that regulating growth rate of culturing cells has an even more important impact in maintenance of EBV episomes in infected cells. Hence, we have modify our hypothesis to examine the role of EBV to support survival of infected cells under stress situation. Elimination of growth factors in the culture medium slowed down the growth of EBV-infected epithelial cells but interestingly increase the % of EBV infected cells in the population as well as the number of EBV copy in infected cells. This observation was also confirmed in our newly established NPC cell lines harboring EBV infection. We found that inclusion of IL6 and lowering the concentration of EGF as well as serum concentration in culture medium support EBV infection in nasopharyngeal carcinoma cells. Growing EBV infected cells as 3D-tumour spheroids also increases the number of EBV in infected cells. This support our new hypothesis that EBV infection in epithelial cells may provide survival advantage (rather than proliferative advantage) to infected cells in vivo.

779713.label: Major findings and research outcome
779713.value: The examination of dynamics of EBV infection in epithelial cells will provide insights into the role of EBV infection in epithelial carcinoma cells. In contrast to B cell infection, EBV episomes in infected epithelial cells is commonly lost upon propagation, suggesting induction of cell proliferation is unlikely to be the role of EBV in infected epithelial cells (at least in culture condition). In this study, we have carefully investigate the dynamics of EBV infection in premalignant nasopharyngeal epithelial cell model and observed a rapid loss of EBV episomes in the early phase of EBV infection. Upon repeated cell sorting guided by GFP-tagged EBV, stable EBV infected epithelial cells could be selected. There was a switch of EBV genes from lytic to latent in nature. In particular, the EBNA 1 appears to be crucial for survival of EBV-infected nasopharyngeal carcinoma. The possibility of targeting EBNA1 for therapeutic application was published in a collaborative study with investigators from Baptist University (See part C). Monitoring of the replication and partition dynamics using a visible EBV under live imaging reveal imperfect replication and unequal partition of EBV particles. EBV infection does not directly confer growth advantage to epithelial cells. Hence the infected EBV episomes will be eventually lost in the absence of selection force. Stress resistance may provide the selection advantage of EBV-infected nasopharyngeal epithelial cells in patient. Two publications directly related to this study have been submitted for publication to Scientific Report (minor revision required) and J. of General Virology (major revision required). The PDF of the two manuscript and a conference abstract are included in Part C.

779713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
779713.value: We have established the investigation platforms to study the dynamics of EBV infection in epithelial cells which would contribute to the elucidation of role of EBV infection in human cancers. More carcinoma cell lines should be examined to elucidate events supporting latent EBV infection in human cancer using the platform established in this study and may contribute to the development of specific EBV-targeting theaperutic target for EBV-associated epithelial malignancies.

779713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
779713.value: EBV infection could be detected in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) cells. Intriguingly, EBV episomes are rapidly lost in NPC cells upon passage in culture. The selective advantage of EBV in infected NPC cells in patient is poorly defined. This project aims to elucidate the dynamics of EBV loss in infected human epithelial cells in an attempt to elucidate the selective force to retain EBV in infected epithelial cells by directly examining replication and partition of EBV in infected epithelial cells by live cell microscopy. Furthermore, the dynamics of loss of EBV in early infection and stable infection in nasopharyngeal epithelial cells were monitored together. Stable EBV infection requires a change from lytic to latent infection. Establishment of stable latent EBV infection in epithelial cells require adaptation of both host cell factors and epigenetic modification of EBV genome. In contrast to B cell infection, EBV does not confer growth advantages to infected epithelial cells. In contrast, EBV infection slows down growth of infected epithelial cells. Our study suggests that EBV infection confers a stress-resistant phenotype to epithelial cancer cells which may provide growth advantage of their growth and metastatic spread in patients.

779813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
779813.value: 三氧化二砷(As2O3)在治療急性早幼粒細胞白血病(APL)中展現的療效頗為顯著。患者的癌細胞對三氧化二砷具有獨特的敏感性，主要是因為三氧化二砷能夠介導APL特有的腫瘤嵌合蛋白PML-RARα的降解。除此之外，三氧化二砷還可以通過其他的分子機制來誘發腫瘤細胞的死亡，這意味著三氧化二砷或許對其他急性骨髓性細胞白血病(AML)類型也可以發揮療效。然而，不難理解的是，三氧化二砷首先要被運送入細胞從而發揮細胞殺傷作用。我們在先前的研究中已證明，跨膜蛋白AQP9是細胞轉運三氧化二砷至胞漿的過程中的關鍵蛋白，並且在癌細胞對三氧化二砷的敏感度中是一項重要的決定因素。癌細胞中AQP9表達水平與胞漿內三氧化二砷濃度正相關，即AQP9表達較高的癌細胞胞漿內三氧化二砷的濃度越高，因此對三氧化二砷的敏感度就更高。我們的初步數據也進一步顯示，通過使用去甲基化藥物，如氮胞苷(Azacytidine)可以提升AML細胞的AQP9水平。在這項研究計劃中，我們將致力於觀察氮胞苷是否能夠通過提升AQP9的表達水平進而增強三氧化二砷的抗癌作用以達到協同效應。同時，我們將探索氮胞苷上調AQP9蛋白水平的機理。最後，我們將運用基因表達譜分析(Gene Expression Profiling)的方法發掘AML細胞中潛在的三氧化二砷與信號傳到分子的相互作用。這項研究的目的在於將三氧化二砷的抗癌作用推廣至AML及其他癌症。

779813.label: Realisation of objectives
779813.value: The objectives of the project have been achieved. We have shown using cell lines and primary human AML cells, that azacytidine enhances the cytotoxic action of arsenic trioxide. We also showed that azacytidine demethylates the gene promoter of HNF1A, resulting in increased expression of HNF1A that in turn activates the expression of the arsenic transporter AQP9. As a result, azacytidine facilitates the transport of arsenic into the cell to effect cytotoxicity.

779813.label: Major findings and research outcome
779813.value: We have shown using cell lines and primary human AML cells, that azacytidine enhances the cytotoxic action of arsenic trioxide. We also showed that azacytidine demethylates the gene promoter of HNF1A, resulting in increased expression of HNF1A that in turn activates the expression of the arsenic transporter AQP9. As a result, azacytidine facilitates the transport of arsenic into the cell, thereby enhancing the cytotoxic action of arsenic trioxide. One of the mechanisms of action of arsenic is the induction of reactive oxygen species. (ROS). During the course of investigation of the mechanism of action of arsenic, we have identified nucleophosmin (NPM) mutant in AML and NPM-ALK fusion protein in anaplastic large cell lymphoma as targets of arsenic trioxide.

779813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
779813.value: Our project has provided the proof-of-concept that therapeutic application of arsenic trioxide (ATO) may be extended to the treatment of acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) through up-regulation of the arsenic transporter AQP9. It has also provided the rationale for the clinical trial on the use of combination demethylating agent and arsenic trioxide in AML. The findings are of great importance to facilitate the development of novel therapeutic approach for AML.

780013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
780013.value: 高血壓佔成年病人人口的20-30%，是心血管疾病最主要的死亡危害原因。雖然近年來在治療高血壓藥物方面已取得了很大的進展，例如阻斷腎素－血管緊張素－醛固酮系統和交感神經系統等藥物。然而，仍然有很大比例的高血壓病人未能控制血壓到最佳標準，甚至超過20-40%臨床控制高血壓的病人也未能達到理想的血壓值。 更為重要的是，未控制達到理想血壓值的高血壓病人會伴隨較高的心血管並發癥，包括中風，冠脈疾病和心臟衰竭。 我們都知道交感神經系統在高血壓的發生發展中扮演著重要角色，交感神經類藥物，如ß受體阻斷劑，可有效地降低血壓，但是其作用具有非選擇性，會產生許多不良反應。近些年來，越來越多人關註“交感腎上腺軸”在難治性高血壓中的角色。增加腎臟感覺傳入信號可以直接影響中樞交感神經，引起全身交感興奮引發高血壓。腎臟去甲腎上腺素（NE）釋放也是交感神經活性激活的主要原因。試驗的臨床研究表明，導管介入腎交感神經去神經支配是壹種有效的針對交感腎上腺軸的非藥物治療高血壓方法。然而，腎交感神經去神經支配不是對所有的高血壓病例都有降低血壓的作用。有趣的是，去神經支配對由血管緊張素-II或者醋酸脫氧皮質酮（DOCA）所引發的高血壓動物模型沒有降低血壓的作用。這些研究表明，在動物模型的高血壓的發展中，內臟神經活性比交感神經起著更加重要的作用，而不同種類的交感神經激活引發不同機制的高血壓。事實上，早有臨床研究表明，在外科腹腔神經節切除手術中進行內臟神經去神經支配可以有效的降低高血壓病人的血壓水平。內臟神經去神經化所引發的降低血壓機制可能包括減弱交感神經介導的內臟循環血管阻力的變化以及內臟器官和腎上腺釋放去甲腎上腺素水平。然而，腹腔神經節切除術因為要進行創傷性外科手術，所以它的開展受到了很大的限制，解剖學上來說，腹腔神經叢起源於腹腔神經節所環繞的腹腔動脈和腸系膜上動脈，因此，如腎交感神經去神經支配壹樣，由導管介導的射頻消融在腹腔動脈和腸系膜上動脈部位進行內臟神經去神經支配是可行的。這項技術可能因此而被證明是壹種有效的高血壓患者的治療選擇。然而，導管介導的內臟神經去神經支配的安全性和有效性還不清楚。我們希望去研究導管介導的內臟神經去神經在臨床相關的由血管緊張素-II和 DOCA誘發的大動物高血壓性心肌病模型中對降低血壓和心室重構的作用的長期效果。以及在內臟神經去神經化後再進行腎交感神經去神經化治療，是否有潛在的增加治療效果的作用。這項研究的結果將會對導管介導的交感神經去神經化新型非藥物治療方法治療高血壓的發展提供重要依據。

780013.label: Realisation of objectives
780013.value: To address Objective 1, we first established a large animal model of hypertensive heart disease induced by angiotensin-II infusion and DOCA treatment. We successfully induced sustained and hypertension using continuous angiotensin II infusion using an implantable pump together with implantation of subcutaneous DOCA pellets in 9 pigs. Telemetry blood pressure recording in those ambulatory animals showed significant elevation of both systolic and diastolic blood pressure (Figure 1). Serial echocardiogram examination showed progressive left ventricular (LV) hypertrophy with thickening of intraventricular septum (IVS) and LV posterior wall (LVPW) (p<0.01), and significantly increased LV mass index (p<0.05) without any changes in LV diastolic dimensions (LVDD) and LV systolic dimension (LVSD) after 18 weeks (p>0.05). The LV ejection fraction (LVEF) was significantly increased at 10 weeks as compared to baseline, but then decreased at 18 weeks, suggestive of deterioration of LV function over time with persistent hypertension (Figure 2). Invasive hemodynamic studies demonstrated elevated pulmonary arterial wedge pressure (PAWP) and LV end-diastolic pressure at 10 and 18 weeks follow-up as compared with baseline (p<0.05, Figure 1). Pressure-volume loop assessment showed that the LV +dP/dt was significantly lower at 18 weeks follow-up as compared to 10 weeks follow-up (p<0.05) without any changes in LV-dP/dt, cardiac output or end systolic pressure-volume relationship (ESPVR) (p>0.05). However, the end diastolic pressure-volume relationship (EDPVR) was significantly increased at 10 and 18 weeks follow-up as compared with baseline (p<0.05). Taken together, these findings demonstrated that those animals develop impairment of LV diastolic function but preserved LV systolic function with persistent elevated arterial blood pressure (Figure 3). To address Objective 2, we have successful performed catheter-based renal denervation (n=6) and splanchnic denervation (n=6) at 10 weeks in animals with hypertensive cardiomyopathy following Ang-II infusion and DOCA implantation. Our data on telemetry blood pressure monitoring demonstrated that splanchnic denervation significantly decreased systolic blood pressure at 18 weeks follow-up (p<0.05, Figure 1). Echocardiographic assessment showed significant regression of LV wall thickness LV mass after splanchnic denervation (p<0.05) but not in control or after renal denervation (p>0.05, Figure 2). Moreover, invasive hemodynamic study showed that PAWP and EDPVR were also significant improved after splanchnic denervation but not in renal denervation (p<0.05, Figure 1 and 3). To address Objective 3, we measured serum norepinephrine (NE) levels at different sites as baseline, 10 and 18 weeks follow-up, and tissue NE levels at different tissues. Our results showed that only splanchnic denervation attenuated the systemic elevation of the serum BNP levels at 18 weeks as compared with baseline (Figure 4). Most importantly, the splanchnic venoarterial gradients of NE (p<0.05, Figure 5) were decreased after splanchnic denervation which is likley attributed to the reduction in the splenic NE content(p<0.05, Figure 6). Nevertheless, there are no significant changes in the tissue NE content in the heart and kidney after renal or splanchnic denervation. As shown in the above, we have successfully completed all the study objectives.

780013.label: Major findings and research outcome
780013.value: In conclusion, in porcine model of hypertensive cardiomyopathy due to severe hypertension, splanchnic denervation was more effective than bilateral RD using catheter-based RF to decrease blood pressure and improves left ventricular diastolic function via reduction in splanchnic NE gradients and splenic content of NE. Our findings suggest that splanchnic denervation using catheter-based RF is a potential novel non-pharmacological approach for treatment of hypertensive cardiomyopahty. Based on these findings, we have presented two abstracts in major international cardiology congress and the full publication is now under preparation.

780013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
780013.value: Based on the findings of this pre-clinical study in large animal model of hypertensive cardiomyopathy, future clinical studies should be performed to investigate the safety and efficacy of this approach for treatment of patients with hypertensive cardiomyopathy due to severe hypertension. Indeed, we have started to discuss with the industries for potential collaboration for the development of novel catheter for splanchnic denervation as therapeutic approach for hypertensive cardiomyopathy.

780013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
780013.value: In a clinical relevant large animal model of hypertensive cardiomyopathy due to severe hypertension, our findings suggest that splanchnic denervation using catheter-based RF to destroy splanchnic nerves and reduce splenic NE spillover is a potential novel non-pharmacological for treatment of hypertensive cardiomyopathy. These results should provide important proof of principle data to perform clinical trial to investigate the safety and efficacy of this approach for treatment of patients with hypertensive cardiomyopathy due to severe hypertension.

780113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
780113.value: Influenza virus continues to threaten global human health with significant morbidity and mortality. Although strategies including vaccine and antiviral drugs have achieved a great advance to control influenza virus infection, the efficacy of these strategies is still limited by the highly frequent mutations in the viruses and the emergence of drug-resistance strains. Human gammadelta-T cells, as a small population of human immune system, play an indispensible role in the host innate and adaptive immune defense systems against virus infection. Our previous studies have demonstrated human gammadelta-T cells have potent antiviral activities against human and avian influenza viruses by directly killing virus-infected cells and producing antiviral cytokines. However, it is still unknown whether human gammadelta-T cells can help B cells produce influenza virus-specific antibodies. Our preliminary data indicate that phosphoantigen-activated gammadelta-T cells can help B cells produce influenza virus-specific antibodies to a level comparable to that produced with the help from conventional CD4 T cells in vitro. Here, we will test our hypothesis that human gammadelta-T cells can help B cells produce influenza virus-specific antibodies, and phosphoantigen can improve the efficacy of influenza vaccine through boosting human gammadelta-T cell immunity in vitro and in vivo using humanized mouse model. The mechanisms underlying the B-helper function of gammadelta-T cells will be further investigated in this proposal. This study will help establish a novel approach by targeting gammadelta-T cells to improve the efficacy of influenza vaccines. 流感病毒可導致嚴重的發病率和死亡率，至今仍威脅著全人類健康。儘管包括疫苗和抗病毒藥物在內的一些措施在控制流感病毒感染中取得了巨大進展，但由於流感病毒的高突變率和耐藥株的出現，這些措施的效果仍然非常有限。gammadelta-T細胞在人類免疫系統中僅占小部分，但其在機體對抗病毒感染的天然免疫和獲得性免疫中均發揮著不可缺少的作用。我們的前期工作表明，人類gammadelta-T細胞通過直接殺傷被病毒感染的細胞和產生抗病毒的細胞因子，對人類流感和禽流感病毒具有潛在的抗病毒作用。然而，目前還不能確定人類gammadelta-T細胞是否能夠輔助B細胞產生抗流感病毒特異性抗體。 我們通過的體外預實驗表明，磷酸化抗原活化的gammadelta-T細胞和傳統的CD4 T細胞一樣，可以輔助B細胞產生相同水準的抗流感病毒特異性抗體。在本研究中，我們將驗證人類gammadelta-T細胞是否可以輔助B細胞產生抗流感病毒特異性抗體；我們還將在體外實驗和人源化小鼠模型的體內實驗中，驗證磷酸化抗原是否可以通過提高人類gammadelta-T細胞的免疫性來增強流感疫苗的有效性。在此基礎上，我們將會進一步研究gammadelta-T細胞對B細胞輔助功能的機制。本研究可望為提高流感疫苗的有效性提供了一條新途徑。

780613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
780613.value: 老化是心血管疾病的主要危險因素。與年齡相關的血管結構性變化包括管腔擴張，管壁增厚，血管硬化，以及血管內皮細胞衰老[其特點是內皮細胞的再生能力下降和功能異常]。內皮細胞衰老在動脈粥樣硬化性心血管疾病的發展過程中發揮核心作用。 SIRT1是一種催化去除蛋白質底物上賴氨酸殘基的乙酰基的酶。由於其潛在的抗衰老活性, 在過去十年中， SIRT1已經引起極大的關注。SIRT1的遺傳變異加速老化。越來越多的證據表明， SIRT1具有心血管系統抗衰老活性，並防止與年齡相關的動脈結構重塑和血管內皮功能惡化。 在衰老的內皮細胞中， SIRT1表達水平下降，而其目標蛋白絲氨酸/蘇氨酸激酶LKB1水平是增多的。LKB1基因表達誘導細胞衰老，阻止內皮細胞的再生。 SIRT1減少LKB1的表達，促進其蛋白質降解。SIRT1介導的LKB1下調的分子機制有待研究。 HERC2是SIRT1和LKB1的結合蛋白質。我們的研究結果表明， HERC2的表達水平在衰老的內皮細胞中逐步下降，併且導致LKB1蛋白表達增高。更重要的是，在內皮細胞和小鼠動脈中， HERC2和SIRT1的表達顯示出同樣的晝夜變化規律。這些證據表明， HERC2在內皮細胞衰老以及SIRT1/LKB1信號傳導中起重要的調節功能。 在這個項目中，我們將使用體內和體外的方法重點闡明HERC2在抗內皮細胞衰老和抗血管老化中的功能。結果將對設計與衰老相關的動脈粥樣硬化性心血管疾病的治療提供重要的線索。

780613.label: Realisation of objectives
780613.value: All objectives have been satisfactorily achieved and the results confirmed our initial hypothesis of "HERC2 acts to prevent the development of endothelial senescence and vascular aging, at least in part by forming complexes with SIRT1 and LKB1, and regulating their functions". For the first Objective, we have obtained the detailed domain-domain interactions between HERC2 and SIRT1, HERC2 and LKB1, as well as the three molecules. For the second Objective, we have confirmed that HERC2 is indeed the E3 ubiquitin ligase for LKB1; the modification needs SIRT1's involvement to facilitate the interactions of the three molecules in nucleus. As a result, LKB1, especially the acetylated version of this kinase, is degraded via a proteasome-dependent pathway in nucleus. For the third Objective, using two different animal models (hypertension and atherosclerosis), we have discovered that knocking down of HERC2 promotes adverse arterial remodeling and vascular abnormalities associated with age. The results have also revealed an interesting role of a feed-back regulation in controlling the circadian rhythmic changes of blood pressure. In summary, the project not only extended our previous findings but also opened a new field of research and development.

780613.label: Major findings and research outcome
780613.value: 1. SIRT1, via its amino-terminus, binds to the DOC domain of HERC2 [HECT and RLD domain containing E3 ubiquitin protein ligase 2], which then ubiquitinates LKB1 in the nuclear compartment of endothelial cells. 2. Acetylation at lysine (K) 64 of LKB1 is important in the formation of the SIRT1/HERC2/LKB1 protein complex and subsequent proteasomal degradation. 3. Accumulation of acetylated LKB1 in the nucleus leads to endothelial activation, in turn stimulating the proliferation of vascular smooth muscle cells and the production of extracellular matrix proteins. Knocking down either SIRT1 or HERC2 results in an increased association of LKB1 with the positive regulatory elements of TGFβ1 promoter. 4. In mice without endothelial nitric oxide synthase, selective overexpression of human SIRT1 in endothelium prevents hypertension and age-related adverse arterial remodeling. 5. Lentiviral-mediated knockdown of HERC2 abolishes the beneficial effects of endothelial SIRT1 on both arterial remodeling and arterial blood pressure control. 6. Conclusion-By downregulating acetylated LKB1 protein via HERC2, SIRT1 finetunes the crosstalk between endothelial and vascular smooth muscle cells to prevent adverse arterial remodeling and maintain vascular homeostasis

780613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
780613.value: The results provided two potential areas for further development: First, it is very important to determine the LKB1-mediated feedback regulation of SIRT1 in cells as well as organs; Second, it is even more important to reveal the pathophysiological relevance and the clinical application values of the cross-regulation between SIRT1, LKB1 and HERC2.

780613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
780613.value: With age, arteries change in both structure and function. To slow or reverse the ageing process of arteries represent a promising strategy for diseases including heart failure, stroke and dementia. By focusing on a longevity regulator, SIRT1, the study reveals an important pathway to prevent or reverse arterial ageing by targeting LKB1 via HERC2.

780713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
780713.value: Periodontal diseases, such as periodontitis, are caused by chronic bacterial infections of the gingival (gum) tissues surrounding the root of the tooth. They promote an abnormal host inflammatory response, which results in the progressive destruction of the gums and underlying connective tissues and bone that anchor the teeth in place. More than one billion people are estimated to suffer from severe forms of periodontitis, which is the main cause of tooth loss in adults. More effective, personalized treatment strategies for periodontitis are severely hindered by our poor-understanding of the detailed compositions of the bacterial communities that inhabit diseased versus healthy periodontal sites. Furthermore, existing knowledge is based almost exclusively on data obtained from the analysis of pooled samples taken from multiple diseased or healthy sites within the same oral cavity. There is very little data on the composition of bacterial communities within specific ‘healthy’ or diseased periodontal sites around single teeth. This is the key to understanding this complex disease. Previous studies have strongly implicated two groups of bacteria with severe periodontitis: Synergistetes and oral treponemes. Here, we will use a combination of molecular approaches to analyze and compare the Synergistetes and treponeme populations present within individual diseased versus ‘healthy’ sites in subjects with chronic periodontitis. We will also compare Synergistetes and treponeme populations in equivalent ‘healthy’ periodontal sites, in periodontitis subjects versus healthy-control subjects. Using our recently-developed genetic system for identifying individual treponeme strains, we will characterize specific ‘genetic lineages’ of oral treponeme species present within diseased versus healthy periodontal sites. On the basis of our preliminary results, our working hypothesis is that multiple lineages (strains) of many different treponeme species may co-inhabit individual diseased sites. This suggests that the bacterial communities underlying periodontitis may be even more complex than previously suspected. We will also establish whether certain Synergistetes phylotypes (cultivated/uncultivated ‘species’) can be used as accurate biomarkers for periodontitis. Our recent data suggests that there may be notable differences within distinct ethnic/geographical populations. The results of this grant will greatly improve our understanding of the bacterial basis of periodontal disease, as well as the human oral microbiome in general. As treponemes and Synergistetes are commonly encountered in other non-oral human and animal niches, our findings will also have direct implications for various tissue infections and chronic infectious-inflammatory conditions in humans, e.g. inflammatory bowel diseases; as well as for economically-important infections within livestock animals. 牙周疾病尤其是牙周炎是細菌感染的牙周支持組織慢性疾病。牙周細菌感染導致宿主異常炎癥反應，繼而引發牙齦及齦下牙周支持組織的破壞。據估計，全球超過十億人患有不同程度的牙周炎，罹患牙齒缺失。目前，牙周細菌種群研究多採用收集患者全口健康或病患位点匯集牙菌斑的模式，而針對同一牙周炎患者的患病位點及健康位點中互養菌及密螺旋體的種群分佈對比研究較少，因此牙周病患的個性化治療方案研發受到了一定的阻礙。通過對比研究同一牙周炎患者病患及其健康位點的牙周細菌種群，可成為進一步瞭解牙周病及完善發展牙周病個性化治療的一個關鍵途徑。 研究證實互養菌及密螺旋體與重度牙周炎關係密切。本課題組將通過一系列分子生物學方法比較慢性牙周炎患者的病患及健康位點中互養菌及密螺旋體的種群分佈。此外，本課題組還同樣對比健康人與牙周炎患者健康牙位點中這兩細菌的種群分佈；通過本課題組最近建立的密螺旋體基因鑒別方法，在病患位點及健康位點表徵出特定的口腔密螺旋體遺傳譜系；同時驗證特定的互養菌表型能否成為牙周炎確診的生物標記物之一。基於本課題組的初步研究結果，推斷不同種類的密螺旋體或共生於同一病患位點，提示導致牙周炎的細菌種群構成遠比此前認知的複雜。此外，本課題組最新研究發現導致牙周炎的細菌種群分佈存在種族及地域差異。本研究計畫的結果有助於提高我們對牙周微生物乃至人類口腔微生物菌落構成的認識。由於密螺旋體及互養菌廣泛存在於人類及動物體內的其他部位，本課題組的研究或可對人類慢性感染或炎症疾病, 如腸胃炎等的治療具有一定意義，亦可減少因家畜感染導致的農業損失。

780713.label: Realisation of objectives
780713.value: The study of oral treponeme and Synergistetes bacteria, and their respective roles in oral diseases, represent long term areas of investigation for the PI and Co-I (WKL). The PI is very grateful to the RGC, and to the grant reviewers, for enabling him to continue his research in this field. Problems overcome Only extremely small amounts of subgingival plaque can generally be collected from individual healthy tooth sulci. In addition, Treponema and Synergistetes taxa typically comprise very minor components of the ‘healthy’ subgingival microbiota (e.g. ca. 0-2%). In practice, it was by-and-large impossible to obtain PCR products from DNA purified from plaque sampled from individual subgingival sites from healthy subjects (using the Synergistetes/Spirochaetes-specific 16SrRNA primers). Furthermore, it was near-impossible to purify sufficient DNA to enable quantitative-PCR analysis to be performed (which requires multiple replicates). This meant that it was not possible to directly compare the Treponema/Synergistetes compositions of individual healthy sites in healthy individuals, versus diseased sites, in diseased individuals; using either a clone-based approach (objective 1) or via a quantitative-PCR-based approach (objective 4). Similarly, for objective 5, due to the quantities of subgingival plaque isolated from healthy sites being extremely low, we were unable to reliably label significant numbers of Synergistetes/Treponema cells in healthy subgingival plaque samples using a FISH-based approach. Thus, we were unable to directly compare levels of Treponema/Synergistetes cells between individual healthy and diseased sites using a FISH approach. In light of this, we used alternative approaches to generate results that would still give us novel, informative data regarding subgingival Treponema and Synergistetes populations, as is briefly outlined in studies A-F (each of which span one or more of the original objectives): (A) Use a clone-based approach using novel Synergistetes-specific PCR primers to study Synergistetes taxa present within individual ‘healthy’ and diseased periodontal sites a cohort of individuals (n=18) who had both implantitis and periodontitis. In this cohort, we sampled individual periodontitis sites (DT), implantitis sites (DI), asymptomatic (‘healthy’) periodontal sites (HT), and asymptomatic (‘healthy’) peri-implant sites (HI). (Spanning objectives 1, 3, 4, 5) (B) Use Next-generation DNA sequencing of 16S rRNA clone amplicon libraries (Illumina PE300 MiSeq sequencing of V3-V4 regions) to analyze the bacteria present within the same cohort, which would enable the Treponema and Synergistetes taxa to be compared. (Spanning objectives 1, 3, 4, 5) (C) Use Illumina MiSeq PE300 sequencing to analyze and compare bacterial taxa present in individual gingivitis and peri-implant mucositis sites, with focus on Treponema and Synergistetes taxa. (Spanning objectives 1, 3, 4, 5) (D) Employ a clone-based approach using primers that specifically targeted the msp gene (encoding the Major Surface Protein) to analyze distributions of phylogroup 1 and 2 treponemes in pooled, multi-site samples of subgingival plaque collected from periodontitis (n=10) and periodontitis-free (n=10) subjects. (Objective 2) (E) Employ a clone-based approach using 2 primer sets that respectively targeted the highly conserved pyrH gene of phylogroup 1 and 2 treponemes, respectively, to analyze treponeme populations within pooled, multi-site samples of subgingival plaque collected from chronic periodontitis (n=5), aggressive periodontitis (n=5), gingivitis (n=5), age-matched periodontitis-free (n=10) subjects. (Objective 2) (F) Employ a combination of 454 pyrosequencing and clone-based approaches to analyze the bacterial taxa present within subgingival plaque samples from horse; with focus on Treponema and Synergistetes taxa. (Objectives 1 and 3) In study (A) we designed two sets of Synergistetes-specific primers, that respectively targeted oral cluster A (e.g. Fretibacterium fastidiosum) and oral cluster B (e.g. Pyramidobacter piscolens) taxa. Detection limits for the cluster A, and cluster B Synergistetes-specific PCR primer sets were shown to be ca. 3,500 cells and 500 cells, respectively. Only 21/72 sites (in 18 subjects) yielded PCR products using the oral cluster A and cluster B Synergistetes-specific PCR primer sets. All products corresponded to Synergistetes taxa (100% specificity). This gave a good indication of the quantities of oral cluster A and B Synergistetes taxa typically present in individual sites. A total of 1,338 Synergistetes reads were classified into 26 operational taxonomic units (OTUs, 98.5%). Results revealed a highly complex picture of Synergistetes communities in each site. This work was published in Microbial Pathogenesis in 2016. In study (B) Treponema was most abundant in peri-implantitis (DI) sites, comprising 4.14% of total bacteria (based on total reads), and was least abundant in healthy subgingival plaque (1.03%). Somewhat-surprisingly, Synergistetes had the highest relative abundance in healthy subgingival (HT) sites (3.37%), whilst levels were relatively similar within peri-implantitis (DI), periodontitis (DT) and healthy implant (HI) sites (2.1-2.47%). Upon close inspection, these results were fairly-consistent to those obtained in study (A). Broadly speaking, the PCR-based approach had greater sensitivity, but poorer depth of coverage, compared to the Illumina-based approach. We also performed a comprehensive comparative analysis of the bacterial taxa present in each site (with 26 phyla detected in total). A number of very interesting findings were noted, especially regarding the respective distributions of SR1 and TM7 phyla, as well as Alloscardovia, Bergeyella and Halomonas genera. A manuscript describing this study will be submitted shortly. In study (C) we analyzed the bacterial microbiota resident within peri-implant mucositis and gingivitis sites within a cohort of 22 Chinese individuals who possessed both such niches. Intra-oral, as well as inter-site differences were studied. In general, differences in bacterial taxonomic composition and community structure were complex. However, several highly-interesting differences were noted, including the relative distributions of Prevotella sp., Veillonella sp., Actinomyces sp. and Neisseria sp.). Of note, Pyramidobacter piscolens and Fretibacterium sp. oral taxon 362 levels were significantly higher in peri-implant mucositis sites, compared to gingivitis sites. A manuscript describing this study will be submitted shortly. Regarding objective 2, we obtained some very exciting results from the analysis of the treponeme msp and pyrH genes; which we believe represent the most novel, and ‘highest impact’ findings generated from this grant. In study (D), we obtained 626 clinical msp gene sequences for analysis, which were compared to a reference set of msp genes from oral phylogroup 1 and 2 treponeme strains. There were clear differences in the distributions of clinical ‘msp genotypes’ (95% identity cut-off) between periodontitis versus periodontitis-free controls (e.g. Libshuff, Unifrac, parsimony P-test analyses). Notably, we found that healthy subjects harboured extremely diverse treponeme populations: enriched in T. vincentii and phylogroup 1 treponemes. The T. denticola OTK lineage was over-represented in diseased niches. The msp gene lineage corresponding to the ATCC 35405 strain was prevalent in both health and disease. This work was recently published in Molecular Oral Microbiology. In study (E), we found that clinical pyrH sequences within aggressive periodontitis subjects were highly-distinct from those in chronic periodontitis, gingivitis, or healthy controls. Six distinct clinical pyrH lineages predominated within the cohort, with the lineage corresponding to T. denticola MS25/GM1 being highly-prevalent in all clinical groups. Diversity of treponemes was greatest in the chronic periodontitis subjects, and lowest in the gingivitis subjects. A manuscript describing these exciting results is currently being prepared. In study (F) we analyzed the bacterial composition of equine subgingival plaque, with focus on Synergistetes and Treponeme populations. We showed that humans, horses, cats and dogs share many similarities. Whilst certain species (HOTs, COTs, FOTs, or species-level phylotypes) are common to the four hosts, our small-scale study reveals that many Treponema and Synergistetes taxa appear to show distinct host-specificities. This work was published in Microbial Pathogenesis in 2016.

780713.label: Major findings and research outcome
780713.value: Major Findings Whilst Synergistetes taxa are generally more diverse and abundant within diseased periodontal niches, they are still prevalent, and taxonomically-diverse within healthy (asymptomatic) periodontal niches. Synergistetes levels may be high within asymptomatic peri-implant niches. However, Synergistetes are present in low levels in many oral niches. There are considerable site-to-site variations in their community composition, and clear-cut correlations between ‘species-level’ phylotypes and periodontal/peri-implant disease-status are not generally apparent. Thus, Synergistetes play a more nuanced role in disease etiology and/or progression. Through this GRF grant, we identify many novel ‘species-level’ taxa within oral cluster A, including putative members of the genus Fretibacterium. By analyzing 16S rRNA, msp and pyrH gene sequences, we show that oral treponeme populations show several correlations with periodontal/peri-implant disease status. Phylogroup 1&2 treponeme species richness is highest in chronic periodontitis; compared to health, aggressive periodontitis and gingivitis subjects. The ‘pyrH genotype’ corresponding to T. denticola MS25/GM-1 is highly prevalent in periodontal disease and health. Healthy and chronic periodontitis subjects could be clearly distinguished by their respective populations of msp genotypes. Notably, T. vincentii ‘msp geneotypes’ were positively associated with periodontal health. Based on these results, my general hypothesis is that many different treponeme species/phylotypes can stably-occupy subgingival niches in healthy as well as diseased subjects. However, in disease, certain treponeme phylotypes/lineages become enriched, and these play a disproportionately greater role in pathogenic processes. The cell-surface Msp protein plays one such role, as it has previously been shown to directly mediate/possess virulence-related processes. The phylogeny of msp is highly distinct from that of pyrH or other ‘housekeeping’ genes, and shows much higher levels of sequence variability, and speculatively, greater host specificity. Research Outcomes We have made several notable accomplishments during the course of this GRF research grant, which has resulted in three journal publications so far. This grant has directly supported the studies of one PhD student (Dr. YU Xiaolin; abstract attached) and also supported the PhD studies of another (Dr. GAO Wenling). Both Dr. Yu and Dr. Gao have submitted their PhD theses (for examination in July/August 2017). Three more publications are in preparation, and will be submitted during September-November 2017. These three studies are respectively described in individual chapters in the theses of Dr. Yu and Dr. Gao, and are described in Section 5.3 above. In conclusion, the data and results generated through this research grant greatly improve our detailed understanding within two key areas of periodontal disease etiology.

780713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
780713.value: This project may be extended in many ways. My priorities would be to extend the investigations into the distributions of clinical msp and pyrH gene sequences within a larger number of subjects, and increase the scope to include different clinical groups (e.g. dental implant infections), and socio-geographical groups, and animals. A focused investigation into treponeme (pyrH) lineages within aggressive periodontitis subjects would be particularly-informative. Our (published) msp data revealed several clinical-correlations that were fractionally-below the threshold of significance (especially regarding possibly pathogenic T. denticola lineages). It is important to validate/refute these potentially-significant correlations. Through genome sequencing of diverse treponeme species, it may be possible to correlate msp gene sequences with those of other virulence-related factors, such as the Chymotrypsin-like protease (CTLP) complex, the trypsin-like (BANA) protease. We have recently initiated some such projects. The involvement of Synergistetes in the etiology of periodontal disease appears highly-complex. I would extend molecular investigations to include enlarged subject groups, different clinical categories (as above), and different socio-geographical cohorts. Ultimately, we envisage that results from such investigations may be applied for the development of future diagnostic approaches that can be used to monitor periodontal/peri-implant disease susceptibilities and the effectiveness of different preventive/therapeutic modalities.

780713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
780713.value: Periodontitis is a severe gum disease that affects many hundreds of millions of people. It is caused by persistent bacterial infections of the gum tissues that surround the tooth. No single bacterial species is responsible: there are many hundreds of different species involved, and this varies considerably from person to person. Here, we used a DNA-sequencing based approach to investigate two different ‘families’ of bacteria that are generally-considered to play important roles in the development of periodontitis, and related oral infectious diseases. These two bacterial families are called Treponema and Synergistetes. We identified new members of the Treponema and Synergistetes families, within the dental plaque of both healthy and periodontitis-affected people. Our data reveals that the correlations between periodontitis and members of the Treponema and Synergistetes families are highly complex and variable. However, we did identify certain ‘types’ of Treponema and Synergistetes bacteria that were good indicators of disease. Our results significantly improve our detailed understanding of two important 'families' of bacteria that cause severe gum infections. We envisage that the results described here will be important for the future development of more targeted or ‘personalized’ anti-infection treatment strategies, and more accurate approaches for disease monitoring.

780913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
780913.value: 海洋雙殼貝類，如貽貝和牡蠣，在人類社會中扮演着很重要的角色。有些物種是有益的，它們是很重要的食物資源，并擔當構建生態群落的角色，而有些物種是外來入侵或污損物種，帶來負面的影響。因此，我們越來越有興趣研究有益的海洋雙殼貝類物種如何應對不斷變化的環境，如全球變暖，以及有害的外來入侵物種是否可能勝過甚至取代有益的本地物種。這種影響可能會體現在物種分佈範圍的變化上，較強忍耐性或生長在溫暖水域的物種會取代較弱忍耐性的物種，而後者會向兩極遷迻。鑑於預期的氣候變化速度之快，物種將不會有足夠的時間來適應氣候變化。生物個體不得不在生命週期內馴化并改變其生活史特徵來忍耐氣候變化。要確定物種將會如何應對氣候變化，我們需要在不斷變化的，尤其是海洋溫度變暖的環境條件下，，估計不同物種成功應對的可能性。使用動態能量平衡（DEB）的方法，在既定的環境條件下（主要是溫度和食物供應），可預測一個物種的功能反應（生長，成熟年齡和繁殖輸出）。基本上DEB可以預測物種在一定數量的資源下如何使用和分配這些資源來生長和繁殖。 DEB已被廣泛應用於商業雙殼類養殖。為達到DEB模型在東南亞地區的應用，四種重要的雙殼貝類，包括有益和有害的外來入侵或污損物種，將用於預測現今物種如何應對環境的變化。評估這些物種的功能反應，將能預測哪些物種在未來氣候變化下表現好或不好，進而預測它們相對的物種分佈變化。為了測試物種的適應潛力，對于每一測試物种，一組在正常水溫下飼養的動物會和另一組在較暖水溫（預測的將來的海水溫度）下飼養多於6個月的動物作出比較，測試它們不同的反應，并應用DEB模型對兩組動物的功能性狀作出預測。 應用此方法可以評估哪一物種的生理反應的改變能力很有限，可能無法適應不斷變化的氣候，而哪一物種可以修正它們的生理反應，並能在較熱的溫度下表現良好，以此來預測未來的20年內，這些重要物種的分佈和存活幾率的改變。

780913.label: Realisation of objectives
780913.value: Objective 1: to construct Dynamic Energy Budget models (DEB) for four important target bivalve species The DEB model was built from literature sourced variables and empirically derived variables (laboratory based experiments) which were then entered into a standard, mechanistic, Matlab routine, together with locally relevant environmental data (Hong Kong Observatory, Environmental Protection Department or satellite data) to derive predictions of the life history parameters for the four bivalve species in question. This was the major component of the project and the data involves the work of a number of students: Ms Michelle Luk; Alicia Tan and Mr Martin Cheng (all HKU), in collaboration with Dr Alessandro Rinaldi and Mr Antonio Giacoletti (Palermo University, students of the co-Investigator, Prof Gianluca Sara). The incorporation of literature data is an important component for the DEB parameterisation, however, available datasets for the studied species (with the possible exception of Crassostrea) are either limited or highly variable. Parameterisation of the DEB model is also, preferably, based on datasets from local populations due to possible variation in reponses over a species geographic distribution where the organisms experience different environmental conditions. In order to overcome the lack of data for some aspects, and to improve the accuracy of our models, most of the DEB parameters were estimated from our experimental studies and field observations (model validation) based on the local distributions of the studied species. Whilst sourcing sufficient Septifer and Perna locally was possible, samples of Mytilopsis could not be found in sufficient numbers in Hong Kong and Crassostrea needed to be sourced from China. This proved challenging at first but finally became part of very successful collaborations as Ms Tan travelled and worked for extended periods at Xiamen University (for Mytilopsis) and the Marine Biotechnology R&D Center, Institute of Oceanology, Chinese Academy of Sciences (IOCAS), Qingdao (for Crassostrea). Other issues with bivalve collection involved die-offs of animals associated with red tides (in Hong Kong) and due to reclamation (in Xiamen). These problems were overcome by sourcing other local populations (in Hong Kong) and by repeating the experiments fieldwork (in Xiamen) DEB parameters for Septifer virgatus, Perna viridis and Mytilopsis sallei are now publicly available at http://www.bio.vu.nl/thb/deb/deblab/add_my_pet/species_list.html (this database hosts parameters for all DEB models which have been validated and approved by an editorial process). The available online DEB model for Crassostrea gigas has a more comprehensive dataset compared to our model which has better model performance. Our model for C. gigas is, therefore, awaiting validation by the website curators. Objective 2: to use DEB models to predict functional responses of these bivalves to environmental conditions Present-day environmental data (sea water temperature and chlorophyll a) were collected from the Hong Kong Observatory (HKO) or Environmental Protection Department (EPD) or extracted from satellite data. Spatial and/or temporal resolution of environmental data are important in driving the robustness of the model predictions, whilst hourly data are important to ensure the accuracy of model predictions. The collected environmental data, however, are mainly measured on daily and/or monthly basis. The monthly or annual mean of environmental data cancel out the daily or weekly fluctuations, seasonal changes and might also exclude extreme scenarios, which will have significant influences on the predicted life history traits. Unfortunately, there is a lack of long term record of environmental data at the study sites where the animals were collected (and from this region in general). To accommodate this, environmental data were, therefore, collected from areas nearest to the study sites, which are part of long term monitoring by HKO or EPD; or had to be extracted from satellite data (with larger scale coverage and more coarse time scales). These data were integrated with DEB models of four targeted species. The models predicted life history traits of targeted species (an example of some of the data are summarised in Table 1). These data were able to correctly predict the majority of functional responses (life-history traits such as maximum length, number of eggs and reproductive events relative to the energy reserve) in response to present day environmental conditions. Application of the DEB predictions to observed datasets showed that the models for the four targeted species are capable of successfully reproducing (as based on field based validation) the observed pattern of growth (e.g. in situ growth rate) and fitness (number of eggs produced) at the study sites, which in turn, indicates the robustness of the model. Where there were discrepancies; adjustments were made to the methodology or errors were corrected to improve the model validity. Functional response (LH) Septifer Perna Crassostrea Mytilopsis Maximal length (cm) 5.35 8.66 10.32 3.49 No. of total reproductive event 12 8 6 8 Lifetime egg production (millions) 5 3.35 105 0.29 Objective 3: to integrate this information to predict the future distribution of these species under projected climate change scenarios In order to be able to predict species performance under changing environmental conditions across both time and space in our model predictions, historical and predicted sea surface temperature (SST) and chlorophyll a (Chl-a) under conservative RCP2.6 and severe RCP8.5 climate change scenarios derived by IPCC CMIP5 (model: MPI-ESM-MR) were downloaded. To understand the future distribution of the four targeted species under projected climate change, the spatial spread of the data covered the region from 19°N to 57°N, 103.93°E to150.95°E, with a spatial resolution of 4 x 4 km to obtain 9102 pixels. This work was conducted in collaboration with Dr Juneng Liew and Mr Jing Xiang Chung (National University of Malaysia). Although hourly data are more appropriate to produce a better prediction of species’ life history traits, the higher resolution of predicted data are only available at a monthly scale. A major problem with this approach was that the model, however, was not able to predict accurate Chl-a data at the small spatial and temporal scale as the CIMP5 model predictions and significantly underestimated the small scale Chl-a concentration. The observed (i.e. on site observations) concentrations (satellite or buoy data) are generally in the range of 10-6 kgm-3 - 10-5 kgm-3 along the coastal areas of China whereas the predicted concentration (for the same period) are much smaller in the range of 10-9 kgm-3 - 10-7 kgm-3. Due to the predicted Chl-a data having a relatively higher bias and being much lower than the realistic values, therefore, we needed to adopt an alternative approach to obtain realistic Chl-a concentrations. The approach taken was to use three levels of chlorophyll-a data to detect potential response at low, average and high level scenarios in the future. DEB models were, therefore, run with uniformly increased SST and air temperature by + 1 °C and + 1.5 °C (RCP 2.6) and + 3 °C and + 6 °C (RCP 8.5) or predicted SSTs downloaded from CIMP5 model with decreasing the current chlorophyll-a concentration from 5-20% for RCP2.6 and 10%-30% for RCP8.5 scenario to predict the future (LH) traits of targeted species at different spatial scales. Finally, the results of the models were used to inform relevant future changes in ecological function (Septifer); invasion potential (Mytilopsis); and aquaculture production and management (Perna and Crassostrea).

780913.label: Major findings and research outcome
780913.value: DEB models were successfully constructed for the four ecologically and economically important bivalves, Septifer, Perna, Crassostrea and Mytilopsis and, under current environmental conditions, the predicted life history traits of these bivalves were successfully validated. DEB models were run under future climate scenarios, using average and extreme IPCC predictions. Under the average climate change scenario, the ecosystem engineer mussel; Septifer was predicted to reproduce annually and local populations could be self-sustaining. Under the more severe scenario, however, reproductive failure occurred after the first year and individuals only gained enough energy to reproduce in their 4th year. Given the mortality rates, Septifer will not be locally sustained under this scenario unless populations are replenished by larval dispersal from adjunct populations. This loss of the northern mussel could have large biodiversity impacts in the future given its role as an ecosystem engineer. Under both climate change scenarios, the aquaculture mussel Perna achieved larger body size and had more spawning events, with increased egg production suggesting that Perna will be locally sustained. The acclimation of this species was also simulated and compared with the DEB model, which further illustrated its future success (Cheng et al. in submission). Such increased egg production may also help Perna to settle in new areas and expand its biogeographic distribution. Simulations to estimate the aquaculture potential of this species were used to generate management options to enhance future gain (Cheng et al. 2018). Mytilopsis is an invasive mussel which impacts aquaculture and is moving northwards along the China coast. Both climate change scenarios showed an increased northwards shift (within 30 years) along the China coast in the Mytilopsis reproduction niche, suggesting the poleward expansion of this invasive species is related to increasing temperature regardless of decreasing food concentration. As such, this species will become a future threat to aquaculture operations in northern China. In general, fecundity of the edible and commercially harvested oyster Crassostrea from the East China sea to Japan Sea will decrease under both climate change scenarios. As a result, Crassostrea did not show any northwards expansion to North Korea within the next 30 years. Model predictions show that these oysters could survive along the North Korea coast, however, due to low fecundity and/or reproductive failure, they will not be locally sustaining in the long term. Hence, in there does not appear to be the potential to expand the future aquaculture of the oyster to the north.

780913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
780913.value: The current models for three species have been validated and incorporated into published DEB routines available at http://www.bio.vu.nl/thb/deb/deblab/add_my_pet/species_list.html. These models are available for other researchers and for continued development and can be used to inform aquaculture practices; determine local viability and invasive impacts by the application of species-specific environmental parameters. As such these models can be used as predictive mechanistic tools for many potential management and ecological questions. The DEB models for Crassostrea and Mytilopsis were combined with large scale spatio-temporal environmental data under different climate change scenarios to predict future distribution of these species. These models can be further developed to assess the invasive potential and aquaculture performance of the two species (Tan et al in prep). The predictions for Septifer and Perna were made at a more local scale and in the future can be integrated with larger spatial scale environmental data to predict how changing climate affects future performance and subsequently their biogeographic distribution, which have profound implication on adjacent communities along the China coast. The present models have been used to inform aquaculture management (Perna) and in the case of Septifer forms the basis of a predictive model to assess biodiversity loss in a recent RGC GRF submission.

780913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
780913.value: Dynamic Energy Budget (DEB) models, which predict the performance of species under various environmental conditions, were built for four ecologically and economically important bivalves, Septifer, Perna, Crassostrea and Mytilopsis. The models successfully reproduced present-day performances (life history, LH, traits) of the species. Models were then used to predict species’ responses under two (medium/extreme change) climate change (CC) environments and the results used to infer impacts on biological invasion, aquaculture management and community structure. The ecologically important mussel, Septifer which enhances local biodiversity, was unable to maintain a viable local population under future CC which will impact local biodiversity. The commercially important mussel, Perna showed enhanced LH traits under CC, which should encourage aquaculture production in Hong Kong. The oyster, Crassostrea is an important aquaculture species in China, however, the model predicted a negative effect of CC; reducing aquaculture production. Performance may also be affected by the northward expansion of the invasive Mytilopsis, which DEB models showed will expand northwards and may impact aquaculture facilities. The application of DEB models to different environmental scenarios (present day vs future climate change; local to regional scales) is, therefore, an extremely important tool to predict changes in ecological communities and commercially important aquaculture species.

781013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
781013.value: 腫瘤血管生成是癌症侵襲轉移中的重要步驟，相關血管生成調控因子及其調控機制的研究受到廣泛關注。E-cadherin是一種細胞間黏連蛋白，它的缺失是癌症侵襲轉移的標志物。我們已於早前發現了卵巢癌中E-cadherin的失調機制及其與癌症發展的關係。E-cadherin合成后以跨膜蛋白的形式發揮作用，其胞外區被剪切后釋放出可溶性E-cadherin (sE-cad)，進而使細胞表面功能性E-cadherin迅速減少。sE-cad在卵巢癌病人的血清和癌性腹水中的含量增高，但是其相關的腫瘤侵襲調控機制仍不明確。許多研究只關注E-cadherin缺失在減弱細胞間黏附中的作用，但是sE-cad本身是否具有生物活性尚不清楚。而於最近，我們首次發現sE-cad能夠介導血管生成的相關信號，並一步証實腫瘤來源囊泡與sE-cad剪切及釋放的激活密切相關。根據以上結果我們推測sE-cad對血管形成至關重要，腫瘤來源囊泡是激活sE-cad級聯信號的關鍵機制之一。 我們希望通過體內外實驗繼續深入的研究：(1)揭示sE-cad在血管生成不同階段中的作用；(2)剖析sE-cad在內皮細胞中的功能及調控機制，及其可能涉及一種新的sE-cad-VE-cadherin信號軸；(3)闡明腫瘤血管形成過程中sE-cad剪切及釋放的機制。這個研究將揭示腫瘤血管生成與腫瘤侵襲的關係，為血管生成調控提供理論基礎，並為新型靶向治療藥物的開發提供思路。

781013.label: Realisation of objectives
781013.value: Objective 1: Angiogenesis is a multistep process which involves cell adhesion, migration, differentiation, and growth. As such, we assayed for these activities to define a mechanism of action. In this report, we have successfully shown for the first time that soluble E-cadherin (sE-cad) is a key regulator of tumor angiogenesis, which is involved in one or more rate-limiting steps of the angiogenic cascade in vitro and in vivo. Besides ectodomain shedding, we also present evidence for a novel paradigm of sE-cad production in the form of exosomes. Using a refined analysis, we showed that sE-cad was predominantly expressed in Golgi/Trans-Golgi network-enriched fractions. By employing various tests on morphology (electron microscope), density (sucrose gradient), protein composition (Western blotting), and size (nanoparticle tracking), we showed exosomes as a vehicle for sE-cad. Using immunoelectron microscopy and BODIPY-TR ceramide fluorescent dye, we further showed the surface localization and uptake of exogenous purified sE-cad-positives exosomes by endothelial cells. sE-cad-positive exosomes were a potent inducer of angiogenesis. Furthermore, sE-cad-positive exosomes could also be found in the ascites of ovarian cancer patients and promoted angiogenesis in vitro and in vivo, confirming that sE-cad involved in it is clinically relevant. Percentage achieved: 100% Objective 2: In search of mechanisms underlying sE-cad regulation of angiogenesis, we found that sE-cad mediated heterophilic transconnection with VE-cadherin. This provides a novel and attractive mechanism whereby endothelial cells, which lack E-cadherin, can lead to angiogenic signaling. This heterophilic interaction may serve as a new paradigm of cell-cell communication. We further showed that a Wnt/b-catenin signaling cascade was critically involved in this novel sE-cad/VE-cadherin heterotypic transconnection that contributed to angiogenesis. Although the mechanism of b-catenin activation could be mediated through MAP kinase, we ruled out this possibility and showed that these events were mediated via a PI3K/Akt-dependent signaling. We also showed that sE-cad-VE-cadherin transduced a novel sequential activation of b-catenin and NFkB signaling, which should provide further new insights into the mechanisms of sE-cad functions. Percentage achieved: 100% Objective 3: In search of how the sE-cad on exosomes is cleaved, we show that this is mediated through activation of the membrane-bound metalloproteinases ADAM10 and MMP25. Moreover, we show that Rab25, which is highly expressed in ovarian cancer cells but not normal ovarian surface epithelium, is required for exosome release. Interestingly, we found that HGF, EGF, and hypoxic stimulus augmented the generation and release of exosomes containing ADAM10, MMP-25, Rab25 and E-cadherin, suggesting that metastatic factors in the tumor microenvironment may be responsible for sE-cad release. These studies provide the first evidence for the regulation of a novel form of tumor-endothelial interaction in the molecular control of angiogenesis. 781013.label: Major findings and research outcome
781013.value: Objective 1: Here, we show for the first time that sE-cad (an 80-kDa soluble form), which is highly expressed in the malignant ascites of ovarian cancer patients, is a potent inducer of angiogenesis. We demonstrated that sE-cad stimulates (a) endothelial cell migration, (b) permeability, (c) endothelial cell tube formation, and (d) neovascularization in Matrigel implants. In addition to ectodomain shedding, we provide further evidence that sE-cad is abundantly released in the form of exosomes. In vivo and clinical data prove the relevance of sE-cad-positive exosomes for malignant ascites formation and widespread peritoneal dissemination. We confirm the localization of sE-cad on the surface and its uptake by the endothelial cells. Publications: Journal articles: #1, #2 Conference proceeding: #4 Objective 2: We show for the first time that sE-cad mediates heterophilic transconnection with VE-cadherin. This provides a novel and attractive mechanism whereby endothelial cells, which lack E-cadherin, can lead to angiogenic signaling. We also show that sE-cad-VE-cadherin transduces a novel sequential activation of b-catenin and NFkB signaling, which should provide further new insights into the mechanisms of sE-cad functions. Whereas crossregulation between b-catenin and NFkB has been generally reported, we found that they were two parallel pathways, which may allow continuous input from the signaling pathway for sustaining transcriptional and subsequent cellular response. The combined operation of different mechanisms suggests that the interaction of sE-cad/VE-cadherin is a crucial event and emphasizes the important role of sE-cad/VE-cadherin that has in contributing to the angiogenic process. Publications: Journal articles: #1, #2 Conference proceeding: #5 Objective 3: On exploring how the sE-cad on exosomes is cleaved, we show that this is through two critical members of the membrane-bound metalloproteinases, ADAM10 and MMP-25. Moreover, we show that Rab25, which is highly expressed in ovarian cancer cells but not normal ovarian surface epithelium, is required for exosome release. Interestingly, we found that this cleavage and release of sE-cad could be regulated by metastatic factors in the malignant ascites, in particular HGF, EGF and hypoxic stimulus, suggesting a role for the tumor microenvironment. To date, while exosomes may help create a tumor microenvironment is well defined, the underlying mechanisms of how the tumor microenvironment may regulate the cleavage and release of exosomes are largely unknown. These studies provide the first evidence for the regulation of a novel form of tumor-endothelial interaction in the molecular control of angiogenesis. Publication: Journal article: #3 Taken together, our data strongly support the important role for sE-cad in ovarian cancer metastasis and provide a mechanistic rationale for targeting sE-cad or its associated signaling in the treatment of metastatic ovarian cancer.

781013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
781013.value: We reveal the novel identification of sE-cad regulation on angiogenesis that has a pivotal role in the metastatic progression of ovarian cancer. This reveals a new direction for understanding the oncogenic role of sE-cad in ovarian cancer metastasis and implicate that sE-cad could be a promising therapeutic target. We found that sE-cad possessed similar VEGF efficiency in angiogenesis, but in a VEGF-independent manner. We are actively pursuing in this direction to document such effect using more extensive in vitro and in vivo studies with and without anti-VEGF agents. Given the development of resistance in targeting VEGF and that VEGF inhibitors also interfere with the normal VEGF pathway leading to numerous adverse side effects, it is of great interest to identify other angiogenic regulators with complimentary mechanisms. High serum sE-cad level has also been detected in patients with breast, gastric, and colon cancer and its expression positively correlates with the aggressive behavior. To expand our understanding of the angiogenic properties of sE-cad, we plan to examine if the sE-cad release is also seen in peritoneal cancers or other cancer types. We will also examine the level and effect of sE-cad in healthy donors or non-cancerous patients. These findings should highlight the functional importance of sE-cad in impacting malignant cell behavior and implies important clinical implications.

781013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
781013.value: One of the greatest unmet needs compromising the successful treatment of cancer is metastasis. A key to successful metastasis is the formation of new vasculature, known as angiogenesis. Therefore, unraveling molecular mechanisms of angiogenesis is of obvious importance. Several of our new findings of this project indicate that sE-cad, which is highly expressed in the serum and malignant ascites of ovarian carcinoma patients, is a pivotal regulator of angiogenesis and that it could be a promising target. (i) We show for the first time a new role for sE-cad on angiogenesis. (ii) We also present evidence that exosomes are a novel major platform for the cleavage and release of sE-cad. (iii) We uncover a new heterophiliic interaction between sE-cad and VE-cadherin that transduces a novel sequential activation of b-catenin and NFkB signaling that may explain its significant angiogenesis promoting effects. These results reveal a new direction for understanding the oncogenic roles of sE-cad and highlight its importance as a viable therapeutic target. Targeting sE-cad may thus be a useful approach to decrease ascites formation, the most distressing complication for ovarian cancer.

781113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
781113.value: 垂體腺細胞分泌的生長激素 (GH) 能通過調控肝臟中胰島素樣生長因子(IGF)-I 來影響身體生長和代謝, 這現象就是解釋 GH 作用的“生長調節素介導假說” 的理論基礎。肝臟也是胰激素的主要作用目標, GH 和胰島素在肝臟中的相互作用是能量平衡和生長信號交流的一個重要介面。在哺乳動物中, IGF-II 僅在胎兒發育過程中發揮作用, 而在成體的肝臟幾乎不表達, 所以通常被認為不是GH的調控目標。然而, 在魚類中 IGF-I 和 IGF-II 都能在成體肝臟中表達, 並共同促進魚類出生後的生長發育。我們最近對草魚肝細胞的研究發現: (i) 胰島素能夠通過 PI3K/Akt 信號通路提升 IGF-I 和 -II 基因表達, 而 GH 也可以通過 JAK2/STAT5, MEK/ ERK 和 PI3K/Akt 信號通路來增加 IGF-I 和 -II mRNA水平; (ii) 胰島素的協同處理能夠明顯地增強 GH 對 IGF-I 和 -II 基因表達, 與此同時細胞膜上GH 受體 (GHR) 和胰島素受體 (IR) 被激活及引起 GHR:IR 異源受體結合; (iii) 在 GH 誘導下, IR, Akt 與 ERK1/2 的磷酸化水平能夠被快速提升, 並且通過阻斷 JAK2, STAT5, MEK1/2, 和 PI3K 這些細胞內信號通路也可以抑制 GH 和胰島素對 IGF-I 和 -II 基因表達的協同效應; (iv) 胰島素可以增加 GHR 和STAT5 mRNA 表達水平, 也能同時降低一個 GHR 信號轉導的反饋抑制因子 SOCS2 的基因表達。基於以上的初步發現, 我們懷疑 GHR 和 IR 能夠在肝細胞膜中形成一個異源受體聚合物, 一方面, GH能夠通過 MAPK 和 PI3K/Akt 信號通路來提升 IR 的活化; 另一方面, IR 的活化又能夠刺激 GHR 及 STAT5 表達來加強 GH 的信號傳遞, 並且利用降低 GH 信號抑制因子SOCS2 的表達來下調 JAK2/STAT5 信號的終止機制, 而這些又能反過來提升對GH的的敏感性。整體而言, 細胞內信號通路的多層次提升能夠導致 GH 和胰島素對草魚肝臟中 IGF 表達的協同效應。通過這個項目, 我們期望能：(i) 證實 GHR 和 IR 之間確實能夠形成異源受體聚合物, 並找出證據來證明形成 GH 和胰島素協同效應的信號通路後續修飾；(ii) 闡明胰島素誘導 GHR 和 STAT5 表達的機理, 並且檢查它與 GH 協同處理所可能產生的加性或協同效應；(iii) 確立 SOCS2 作為一個信號抑制因子下調草魚 GHR 信號傳遞的功能角色, 並且找出胰島素抑制草魚肝臟細胞 SOCS2 表達的信號傳導通路。我們的研究不僅能夠為 GH 和胰島素在肝臟的協同效應研究方面提供一些新的信息，而且可以闡明關於 SOCS2 調控的新機制，這個新機制目前在非哺乳動物的 GHR 信號通路方面仍然是一個未知的領域。

781113.label: Realisation of objectives
781113.value: (I) Realization of Objective (1) : In primary culture of carp hepatocytes, growth hormone (GH) could induce rapid phosphorylation of JAK2, STAT5, MEK1/2, ERK1/2, P38 MAPK, PI3K & Akt and GH-induced IGF-I & -II mRNA expression could be inhibited by pharmacological blockade of JAK2/STAT5, MAPK and PI3K/Akt pathways. Similar treatment with insulin was also effective in triggering protein phosphorylation of MEK1/2, ERK1/2, P38 MAPK, PI3K & Akt but not JAK2 & STAT5 with parallel rises of IGF-I & -II mRNA expression. The stimulatory actions of insulin on IGF-I & -II gene expression were mediated by insulin receptor (InsR) but not IGF-I receptor (IGF1R) and could be reduced/negated by blocking PI3K/Akt but not MEK1/2//ERK1/2 & P38 MAPK pathways. These results indicate that both GH & insulin could serve as the stimulators for IGF regulation at the hepatic level via overlapping and yet distinct post-receptor signaling mechanisms. In our studies, co-treatment of GH & insulin was found to markedly enhance the stimulatory actions on IGF-I & -II mRNA expression in carp hepatocytes. As revealed by co-immunoprecipitation, these potentiating effects occurred with notable rise in protein:protein interaction between GH receptor (GHR) & phosphorylation form of InsR. Of note, GH co-treatment could also enhance insulin-induced InsR activation with concurrent potentiation of insulin-induced ERK1/2 & Akt phosphorylation but GH-induced JAK2 & STAT5 phosphorylation were not affected by insulin co-treatment. Furthermore, the synergistic effects of GH & insulin on IGF-I & -II mRNA expression were inhibited/totally negated by pharmacological blockade of the JAK2/STAT5, MAPK & PI3K/Akt pathways. These results suggest that GH & insulin can act synergistically in the carp liver to induce IGF expression via InsR interaction with GHR & signal enhancement of InsR via MAPK & PI3K/Akt cascades. Although the MAPK pathway was not involved in IGF responses caused by insulin alone, it could serve a key component for signal transduction mediating the potentiating effects triggered by insulin & GH co-treatment, presumably by coupling with GHR activation. [ Manuscript submitted & currently under review in Front Endocrinol. ] (II) Realization of Objective (2) : The potentiating effects of insulin on GH-induced IGF-I & -II mRNA expression in the carp liver may also involve parallel rises of GHR and STAT5 expression. In carp hepatocytes, insulin treatment was found to elevate GHR & STAT5 mRNA levels with parallel rise in GHR protein expression. The stimulatory effects on GHR & STAT5 mRNA and GHR protein expression were also sensitive to the pharmacological blockade of the MEK1/2/ERK1/2, P38 MAPK & PI3K/Akt but not JNK pathways. However, insulin did not alter the half-life of GHR mRNA but could up-regulate basal expression of GHR primary transcript, suggesting that the stimulatory action of insulin on GHR expression is mediated through GHR gene transcription rather than modification of GHR transcript stability. This idea was also confirmed by the results of GHR promoter studies in alpha-T3 cells. In our study, a 1.7 kb 5’promoter of carp GHR was isolated and subcloned into pGL3.basic Luc reporter for GHR promoter studies. Given that (i) carp hepatocytes could not be transfected with Luc reporter by lipofection/electroporation, and (ii) the hepatic cell lines examined (e.g., HepG2 cells) did not confer inducible GHR promoter activity, the alpha-T3 cells with InsR expression were used as the host cells for our studies. In this case, insulin was found to be effective in stimulating GHR promoter activity after transfection with Luc reporter carrying the carp GHR promoter. Using 5’ deletion analysis, the insulin-responsive sequence of GHR promoter could be mapped to the proximal region down-stream of position -331. Consistent with the presence of cis-acting elements including IRE, SRE & ETS sites in this region, GHR promoter activity expressed in alpha-T3 cells induced by insulin could be negated by pharmacological blockade of the MEK1/2/ ERK1/2, P38 MAPK & PI3K/Akt cascades or over-expression of the dominant negative mutants for Ras, Raf, MEK1 & Akt. Our findings, taken together, indicate that insulin can modify GH signaling in the carp liver by transcriptional activation of GHR expression coupled with up-regulation of STAT5 expression via the MAPK & PI3K/Akt pathways. [ Manuscript in preparation. ] (III) Realization of Objective (3) : To unveil the functional role of SOCS in GHR signaling in carp species, four members of type II SOCS, including SOCS1, SOCS2, SOCS3 & CISH, had been cloned in grass carp and confirmed to be single-copy genes in the carp genome. Using RT-PCR and LC/MS/MS, expression of individual members of type II SOCS, both at the transcript & protein level, have been demonstrated in the carp liver. In carp hepatocytes, GH treatment not only could induce IGF-I/II mRNA expression but also trigger parallel rises of transcript expression of SOCS1-3 & CISH with different kinetics and the stimulatory effects on type II SOCS expression were found to be sensitive to the pharmacological blockade of JAK2/STAT5, MAPK & PI3K/Akt pathways. In CHO cells with carp GHR expression & transfection with a Luc reporter with carp IGF-I promoter or STAT5-responsive promoter of mammalian origin, IGF-I promoter activity & STAT5 responsiveness at promoter level could be induced by GH induction and these stimulatory effects was reduced/totally negated by over-expression of carp SOCS1, SOCS2, SOCS3 & CISH, respectively. These results imply that type II SOCS can serve as intracellular feedback inhibitors for STAT5 signaling coupled to GHR activation in carp species. In parallel studies with carp hepatocytes, insulin treatment was found to inhibit both basal & GH-induced SOCS2 mRNA expression without affecting transcript levels of other members of type II SOCS. These inhibitory responses could be noted during the same period with insulin-induced GHR & STAT5 expression at the hepatic level and the drop in SOCS2 mRNA expression induced by insulin could be reverted by blocking the PI3K/Akt but not MEK1/2/ERK1/2 & P38 MAPK cascades. These results, as a whole, raise the possibility that insulin treatment can enhance GH signaling via JAK2/STAT5 pathway by down-regulation of the intracellular feedback mediated by SOCS2 in the carp liver. [ Paper for type II SOCS published in J Endocrinol 229:171-186, 2016. ]
