781113.label: Major findings and research outcome
781113.value: Using carp hepatocytes as a model, both GH & insulin were shown to act directly in the carp liver to induce IGF-I & -II mRNA expression via overlapping and yet distinct post-receptor signaling mechanisms, with JAK2/STAT5, MAPK & PI3K/Akt cascades coupled to GHR activation but only the PI3K/Akt component for insulin induction. Of note, co-treatment of GH & insulin could also markedly enhance IGF-I & -II gene expression at the hepatic level. During the process, increase in protein:protein interaction between GHR & InsR, GH enhancement of insulin-induced InsR activation, and notable potentiation of subsequent ERK1/2 & Akt phosphorylation were observed. Parallel studies by pharmacological approach also revealed that the synergistic action of GH & insulin was dependent on STAT5, MAPK & PI3K/Akt pathways. Apparently, insulin alone could induce IGF-I/-II expression via PI3K/Akt cascades and yet its co-treatment with GH could potentiate MEK1/2/ERK1/2 & PI3K/Akt pathways coupled to GHR activation. In carp hepatocytes, insulin was effective in triggering GHR & STAT5 expression and these stimulatory actions were mediated by MEK1/2/ERK1/2, P38 MAPK & PI3K/Akt but not JNK pathways. The GHR responses not only could be noted at transcript level but also at protein level and insulin-induced GHR mRNA expression was not mediated by alteration of GHR transcript stability but via activation of GHR gene transcription. Functional expression of GHR promoter in alpha-T3 cells also confirmed that promoter activation of carp GHR gene could be induced by insulin via MAPK & PI3K/Akt pathways, presumably via cis-acting elements located downstream of position -331 in the proximal promoter region. In the carp liver, type II SOCS, including SOCS1, SOCS2, SOCS3 & CISH, could be up-regulated by GH with parallel rises of IGF-I & -II mRNA expression and these stimulatory effects were mediated by JAK2/STAT5, MAPK & PI3K/Akt pathways. Over-expression of individual members of type II SOCS, in contrast, could inhibit STAT5 signaling and block GH-induced IGF-I promoter activity expressed in CHO cells, implying that type II SOCS can serve as feedback inhibitors for GH signaling via JAK2/STAT5 pathway. Interestingly, insulin treatment in carp hepatocytes was found to inhibit both basal & GH-induced SOCS2 expression via activation of PI3K/Akt cascades. These findings, as a whole, suggest that GH & insulin can act in a synergistic manner to enhance IGF-I/-II gene expression in the carp liver via modulation of receptor interaction, signal transduction and intracellular feedback for signal termination.

781113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
781113.value: In our laboratory, goldfish is used as a parallel model for grass carp as its small size is highly suitable for in-house in vivo experiments prior to large scale studies in grass carp. Based on our studies in goldfish, spexin, a novel peptide with pleiotropic functions in mammals, has been confirmed to be a satiety factor in fish model and insulin was shown to be a functional link between food intake & spexin expression in the liver (Endocrinology 158:560-577, 2017). Recently, we had cloned grass carp spexin and its receptor GalR2b and confirmed their expression in the carp liver. Similar to goldfish, insulin could induce spexin expression in the carp liver. In carp hepatocytes, spexin by acting in an autocrine/paracrine manner could up-regulate GHR expression via cAMP- & Ca2+-dependent pathways and spexin co-treatment, similar to insulin, was effective in potentiating GH-induced IGF-I mRNA expression. These results, taken together, suggest that spexin via GHR regulation may be a new component for GH & insulin interaction in the carp liver and contribute to their synergistic action on IGF-I/-II expression. As a follow-up, GRF grant has been submitted in 2017 based on these findings to apply for funding to examine this new direction.

781113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
781113.value: In this project, the functional interaction of GH & insulin on IGF regulation was examined at the hepatic level in grass carp. Using carp hepatocytes as a model, GH & insulin were shown to stimulate IGF-I & -II mRNA expression via overlapping and yet distinct post-receptor signaling mechanisms. Interestingly, GH & insulin could act synergistically to potentiate IGF-I & -II expression by increasing protein:protein interaction between GHR & InsR, enhancing insulin-induced InsR activation by GH, and potentiating of ERK1/2 & Akt signaling by GH & insulin co-treatment. As revealed by pharmacological approach, the potentiation on IGF-I/-II expression by GH & insulin interaction was mediated by JAK2/STAT5, MAPK & PI3K/Akt cascades. In carp hepatocytes, type II SOCS induced by GH were shown to function as the intracellular feedback inhibitors for GH signaling via JAK2/STAT5 pathway. Meanwhile, insulin could induce GHR & STAT5 expression at hepatic level with concurrent drop in SOCS2, a key member of type II SOCS, and these effects were mediated by differential coupling with MEK1/2/ERK1/2, P38 MAPK & PI3K/Akt pathways. Our findings, as a whole, shed light on the mechanisms for the synergistic action of GH & insulin on IGF regulation in the carp liver.

781213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
781213.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most common and lethal malignancies worldwide. The mortality rate of HCC patients is extremely high due to late presentation and frequent cancer metastasis. Metastasis is the major cause of tumor recurrence and organ failure, particularly in the context of liver cirrhosis in HCC; therefore, understanding its underlying mechanisms is important to the development of new therapeutic approach for HCC. Recently, metastasis is shown to be greatly dependent on two steps, tumor microenvironment and metastatic niche formation. Emerging evidence has shown that lysyl oxidase (LOX) family members may play an important role in these processes. LOX family comprises 5 members: LOX and LOX-like (LOXL) 1-4. Studies have shown that LOX-mediated cross-linking of components in the extracellular matrix (collagen) in primary breast cancers creates a microenvironment that promotes focal adhesion formation and thereby enhances tumor progression. Furthermore, LOX secreted from primary breast cancers mediates cross-linking of collagen at the metastatic tissues (lung) and enhances the adhesion of bone marrow-derived cells (BMDCs). Collagen cross-linking and BMDCs infiltration in the lungs create favorable metastatic niche for breast cancer cell colonization. However, knowledge about primary HCC tumor microenvironment and metastatic niche formation is still scarce and warranted. Interestingly, our preliminary data showed that LOXL2 is significantly overexpressed in tissues and sera of a small cohort of HCC patients. Also, we showed that LOXL2 expression is regulated not just by HIF-1α but TGFβ, suggesting a new regulatory pathway to LOXL2 deregulation. Our in vitro and in vivo data further showed that LOXL2 modified collagen, enhanced BMDC recruitment, promoted HCC local invasion and lung metastasis. Therefore, we hypothesize that LOXL2 is an important player in HCC progression and might serve as an attractive tumor biomarker and a therapeutic target in HCC. In this proposal, we will first study the clinical and prognostic relevance of LOXL2 up-regulation in human HCC in an expanded cohort of HCC patients. Second, we will investigate the functional implications of LOXL2 in HCC metastasis by knockdown and overexpression systems in multiple HCC cell lines. Third, we will examine serum LOXL2 expression in a larger cohort of HCC patients with our established detection platform. Fourth, we will examine the suppressive effect of LOXL2 inhibitor in HCC metastasis. Taken together, our study will bring valuable insight into the biological and molecular mechanisms of HCC metastasis and facilitate the development of better diagnostic and therapeutic regimen for HCC patients. 肝癌（HCC）是世界上最常見的致命癌癥之一。由於病人確診時常屬晚期且常出現癌癥轉移，肝癌病人的死亡率非常高。癌癥轉移是腫瘤復發及器官衰竭的主因之一，而這種情況在患有肝硬化的肝癌患者中尤為嚴重。因此，了解癌癥轉移的機制對於研發新的肝癌治療手段非常重要。最近研究發現，癌癥轉移主要依賴於兩個步驟，腫瘤微環境以及轉移微環境的形成。越來越多的證據表明，賴氨酰氧化酶（LOX）的家族成員可能在癌癥轉移過程中發揮了重要作用。LOX家族由5名成員組成: 賴氨酰氧化酶和賴氨酰氧化酶樣蛋白（LOXL）1-4。 研究表明，在原發性乳腺癌中，LOX介導的細胞外基質（膠原）交聯促進粘著斑的形成，從而增進癌癥發展。此外，從原發性乳腺腫瘤分泌出來的LOX介導了轉移靶器官組織（肺組織）中的膠原交聯，從而增強了骨髓衍生細胞（BMDCs）的粘附性。肺組織中的膠原交聯以及骨髓衍生細胞浸潤為乳腺腫瘤細胞定植創造了有利的轉移微環境。然而，目前人們對於原發性肝癌中的腫瘤微環境及轉移微環境的了解仍然缺乏。有趣的是，我們的初步數據顯示， LOXL2在一部分肝癌病人的腫瘤組織和血清中顯著過表達。此外，我們還發現LOXL2的表達不僅僅只受HIF-1α 和TGFβ調控。這暗示了一條調控LOXL2的新的信號通路。我們的體外及體內數據進一步證實LOXL2可以修飾膠原質，促進骨髓衍生細胞聚集，增強肝癌細胞的局部浸潤和肺轉移。因此，我們推測LOXL2在肝癌進展中發揮了重要作用，並有可能成為一個極具前景的肝癌腫瘤標誌物和治療靶點。在這個研究計劃中，我們將首先探討LOXL2上調在肝癌病人中的臨床及診斷意義。第二，我們將在不同的肝癌細胞株中敲低或過表達LOXL2，以此研究LOXL2在肝癌轉移中的作用。第三，我們將運用我們現有的實驗平臺檢測肝癌病人血清中LOXL2的表達水平。第四，我們將會評估LOXL2抑制劑對於肝癌轉移的抑制作用。綜上所述，我們的研究將會為肝癌轉移的生物和分子機制提供新的啟示，從而促進研發更好的肝癌診斷及治療方案。

781213.label: Realisation of objectives
781213.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a common malignancy worldwide. HCC ranks the second most lethal cancer only after lung cancer. High death rate in HCC is mainly due to metastasis; unfortunately, there is to date no promising therapy targeting HCC metastasis. Knowledge on this biological process of HCC is particularly warranted. Our current study unequivocally revealed the precise molecular mechanisms by which primary HCC promoted metastasis through modification of extracellular matrix (ECM) in the tumor microenvironment and metastatic niche. This process relies on a secretory protein, lysyl oxidase-like 2 (LOXL2), which is one of the five members of the LOX family. The LOX family members have been shown to cross-link ECM components such as collagen and elastin. Clinically, we found that LOXL2 is the only LOX family member over-expressed in tissues and sera of HCC patients. Up-regulation of LOXL2 in human HCC was significantly associated with aggressive clinicopathological HCC feature. Mechanistically, we demonstrated that frequent up-regulation of LOXL2 in human HCC was attributed to the combinatorial effects of HIF-1α-mediated hypoxia response, hyperactivation of TGFβ/SMAD4 signaling pathway, and loss of LOXL2-regulatory microRNAs, miR-26 and miR-29 families. Functionally, we demonstrated that suppression of the LOXL2 pathway inhibited collagen cross-linking, bone marrow cell recruitment, and HCC cell invasion in vitro. We also found that LOXL2-mediated tissue stiffening within the tumor microenvironment activated a key cell motility regulator, rho-kinase (ROCK), which then orchestrates HCC cytoskeleton. Furthermore, we found that LOXL2 secreted by primary HCC tumor facilitated metastasis by directing bone marrow-derived cells (BMDCs) to colonize the distal metastatic sites. We found that LOXL2 inhibitor is not very effective in vivo but HIF inhibitor is able to suppress LOXL2-mediated effects in HCC. Taken together, our comprehensive study has greatly deepened our understanding of HCC biology, particularly on the aspect of the reciprocal interactions between tumor microenvironment and tumor progression. Since LOXL2 is the central player of this pivotal biological process, our study has provided the basis for the development of diagnostic platforms and therapeutic strategies for HCC using LOXL2 as marker and target, respectively. Taken together, we have achieved all the proposed aims. Majority of the work was published in a high impact journal. 781213.label: Major findings and research outcome
781213.value: Poor prognosis of cancers including hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is mainly associated with metastasis. We found that HCC metastasis relied on an extracellular matrix (ECM)-modifying enzyme, lysyl oxidase-like 2 (LOXL2), which drove the formation of tumor microenvironment and metastatic niche in HCC. METHODS: LOXL2 expression in tissues and sera of HCC patients were analyzed by real-time quantitative PCR, IHC, and ELISA. Promoter and 3’ untranslated regions (3’UTR) of LOXL2 were analyzed for the identification of LOXL2 regulators. Stable knockdown of LOXL2 and its regulators were established in HCC cell lines to evaluate the in vitro and in vivo effects in HCC metastasis. RESULTS: First, we showed that LOXL2 was significantly over-expressed in the tumorous tissues and sera of HCC patients, indicating that LOXL2 may be a good diagnostic marker for HCC patients. Second, we found not only that LOXL2 was regulated by hypoxia/ HIF-1α, but also that TGFβ activated LOXL2 transcription via SMAD4, whereas two frequently under-expressed microRNA (miRNA) families, miR-26 and miR-29, cooperatively suppressed LOXL2 transcription through interacting with the 3’UTR of LOXL2. Third, we demonstrated the imperative roles of LOXL2 in modifying the ECM components in the tumor microenvironment and metastatic niche of HCC. LOXL2 promoted intra-hepatic metastasis by increasing tissue stiffness, thereby enhancing the cytoskeletal reorganization of HCC cells. Furthermore, LOXL2 facilitated extra-hepatic metastasis by enhancing recruitment of bone marrow derived cells (BMDC) to the metastatic site. CONCLUSION: Overall, our findings have comprehensively revealed the clinical relevance, molecular regulations, and functional implications of LOXL2 in HCC metastasis. These results have highlighted the importance of ECM remodeling in cancer metastasis and revealed the complex interlinked pathways that converge to regulate LOXL2 expression in HCC. Our results also have underscored the diagnostic value of LOXL2 and suggested the therapeutic potential of inhibitors that target LOXL2 or its regulators in HCC.

781213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
781213.value: The most striking finding from this study was that we found that LOXL2 could be detected in the sera of HCC patients and may be used as a diagnostic marker for HCC. We also revealed the regulations and molecular roles of LOXL2 in microenvironment formation and HCC progression. As LOXL2 is regulated by HIF-1, we examined the effects of HIF-1 and LOXL2 inhibitors and found that HIF-1 inhibitor could suppress LOXL2-mediated events and HCC progression. HIF-1 inhibitor could be potentially used as a therapeutic agent for HCC patients as single or combination therapy.

781213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
781213.value: HCC cells are embedded in a modified extracellular matrix (ECM). LOXL2 secreted by HCC cells cross-links collagen creating a stiffer microenvironment that would activate the cytoskeletal network and local invasion of HCC cells. LOXL2 also remodeled distant microenvironment in the metastastic sites to facilitate recruitment of bone marrow-derived cells (BMDCs) and promoted metastasis. We identified the multiple regulators of LOXL2, namely TGFbeta/SMAD4, HIFs, as well as microRNAs (miR-26 and miR-29). Overexpression of LOXL2 could be detected in sera of HCC patients and is an attractive diagnostic marker for HCC. Targeting HIF by digoxin could also suppress LOXL2-mediated events and be employed as a new therapeutic strategy for HCC patients.

781713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
781713.value: Despite successful surgery to treat rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD), the visual outcome is often disappointing. The reason is that apoptosis occurs early and rapidly after the onset of the RRD. Neuroprotection has been considered a promising strategy to improve the visual outcome. Lutein as an anti-oxidant is currently being investigated by the US Federally sponsored National Eye Institute for the treatment of age-related macular degeneration. Over the last 5 years, in a series of experiments and publications, others and we have shown that lutein has potent anti-apoptotic as well as anti-oxidative properties. We have demonstrated the neuroprotective effect of Lutein specifically in rhegmatogenous retinal detachment in a rat model. This led us on to carry out a pilot, prospective, randomised, double-masked and controlled trial and the results indicate a statistical and clinically significant difference in the outcome. We now wish to mount the definitive trial. 儘管手術能夠成功醫治孔源性視網膜脫落，但患者在手術後的視力往往未如理想。這是由於在孔源性視網膜脫落後，細胞在早期便開始凋亡，而且速度十分快。現時，以神經保護為基本的治療已被視為一種有希望改善視力的方法。美國國立眼科研究所正在研究利用葉黃素(一種抗氧化劑)來治療老年黃斑病變。在過去5年，經過一連串的實驗，我們和其他學者可以證明葉黃素除了抗氧化外，還有防止細胞凋亡的特性。我們亦曾在孔源性視網膜脫落的老鼠身上試驗，證明葉黃素是有保護神經的能力。所以，我們進行了一個前膽性、隨機雙盲對照的試驗性研究。研究結果顯示服用葉黃素能夠有效改善孔源性視網膜脫落患者在手術後的視力。現在我們希望進行一個確認性研究。

781913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
781913.value: Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a common childhood disorder characterized by symptoms of hyperactivity, inattention and impulsivity. Research from Hong Kong (HK) and Taiwan has shown that 3% to 9% of Chinese children are suffering from ADHD. Many children with ADHD find it difficult to understand instructions, keep up with schoolwork and control their emotions/temper and need behavioral treatment and/or medications. Methylphenidate and atomoxetine are licensed for the treatment of ADHD in HK when medication is considered appropriate. In the past two decades, the use of ADHD medications has increased rapidly in the USA and Europe. Our research group studied the Hospital Authority(HA) prescription data and found that 1% of HK boys in the general population were on ADHD medications in 2011. There is a clear need to know more about the current practice of ADHD medication prescribing in HK and the benefits and risks of this treatment. It is well-known that patients with ADHD are prone to accidents. ADHD medications reduce ADHD symptoms and theoretically should reduce accidents; hence Accident and Emergency Department (A&E) attendance. Reduction of A&E attendance not only represents a significant reduction of healthcare costs but also is a good indicator of reduction of harm due to accidents in children. There is limited research in this important area. Together with a European ADHD research consortium, we developed this ATHAN (ADHD Treatments and Hospital Accident and emergency Attendance aNalysis) proposal to address the research question: Does the use of ADHD medication reduce A&E attendance due to injury? Our pilot study showed that the HA electronic patient record system contains sufficient data (>12,000 ADHD children) to conduct a study to answer our research question. We will extract the data from these electronic records using a programme (CDARS) provided by HA. The data will then be transferred to our secure data server. Self-controlled case series (SCCS) analysis will be used to compare how often children are admitted to A&E when they were on- and when they were off-ADHD medications. Using SCCS the effects of various factors e.g. age, month of the year and major school-holidays can be adjusted for/tested. The probability (Incidence-Rate-Ratios) of A&E attendance while the patients were on- compared to when they were off-ADHD medications will be calculated. Factors which increase the risk of A&E attendance due to injury will be identified. All patient details will be anonymised and the study will fully comply with HK laws. 專注力失調／過度活躍症﹝ADHD﹞是一種常見的兒童精神失調狀況，其主要徵狀包括過度活躍、專注力弱和行為較衝動。根據香港與台灣的研究顯示，每100名華裔兒童之中，約有3至9人患有ADHD。與同齡的兒童相比，患有ADHD的兒童較難按照指示做事、容易在學業上出現困難及無法自我控制情緒。患者普遍需要同時使用藥物及行為心理治療以改善病情。 需要接受藥物治療的患者可服用刺激神經中樞傳導物的藥物改善精神集中能力，已在香港註冊的該類藥物有哌醋甲酯﹝methylphenidate﹞和托莫西汀﹝atomoxetine﹞。在過去二十年間，針對ADHD患者使用藥物治療於歐美國家日催普及。於2011年，我們的研究團隊對醫院管理局的ADHD藥物處方進行研究，發現每100名香港男童之中，約有1人服用哌醋甲酯或托莫西汀。可見有關ADHD藥物治療在香港的使用情況及藥物本身的效益與風險仍有待深入研究。 眾所周知，ADHD病人較易因發生意外而受傷。藥物治療有助改控制病情從而減少發生意外的機會，因而進一步減低患者的急症室使用量。減低急症室使用量不單是代表減少醫療支出，更是ADHD患者減少受傷的重要指標，但現今的醫學文獻對這範疇的研究非常缺乏。有鑑於此，我們連同歐洲的研究團隊提出了這項名為「專注力失調／過度活躍症的藥物治療與急症室使用量之分析」﹝ATHAN﹞的研究計劃，研究ADHD的藥物治療是否能夠減少患者的急症室使用量。 我們的初步研究發現醫管局的電子病歷系統記載了足夠的研究資料﹝多於12,000名ADHD病人的記錄﹞可進行流行病學研究。通過醫管局的電子病歷資料庫﹝CDARS﹞，我們把研究所需的資料存進我們專屬的數據庫，分析方法主要為病例個案自我對照法﹝self-controlled case series﹞，檢定在同一個案身上，在藥物治療及非藥物治療期間因受傷而使用急症室的發生率﹝incidence﹞。病例個案自我對照法使用同一病例個案本身即為自己作對照組，可修正固定之干擾因子，如性別或本身慢性疾病等對相關性評估的影響，亦能夠修正歲數、季節與學校假期對研究結果的影響。透過在藥物治療及非藥物治療期間因受傷而使用急症室的發生率，我們可得出發生率的率比值﹝incidence-rate-ratio﹞，用於審視藥物治療是否能夠減少患者的急症室使用量。此外，我們還會探討其他導致ADHD病人受傷的原因。所有病人資料將絕對保密。

781913.label: Major findings and research outcome
781913.value: 1) The prevalence of children being prescribed medication for Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in Hong Kong increased 14 times from 0.072% in 2001 (95% confidence interval [CI] = [0.068%, 0.077%]) to 1.027% (95% CI = 1.008%, 1.047%) in 2013. Prevalence in females increased at a faster rate than in males. The prescribing trend in kindergarten children (3 to 5 year-olds) was relatively steady from 2001 to 2008 [(0.025%, 95% CI 0.019%, 0.033%) in 2001]. However, a marked increase was observed from 2009 to 2013 [0.121% (95% CI = 0.105%, 0.139%) in 2013. We concluded that the prevalence of ADHD medication prescribing in Hong Kong was increasing but remained lower than most Western countries. However, the prevalence of ADHD medication prescribing for kindergarten children should be monitored to ensure appropriate use. 2) Using a self-controlled case series study design, the relative incidence of trauma-related Emergency Department (ED) admissions was compared with periods of patient exposure and non-exposure to methylphenidate (MPH) in children and adolescents. Among 17 381 patients prescribed MPH, 4934 had at least 1 trauma-related ED admission. The rate of trauma-related ED admission was lower during exposed periods compared with non-exposed periods (incidence rate ratio [IRR]: 0.91 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.86-0.97]). The findings were similar when only incident trauma episode was assessed (IRR: 0.89 [95% CI: 0.82-0.96]). A similar protective association was found in both genders. In validation analysis using non-trauma ED admissions as a negative control outcome, no statistically significant association was found (IRR: 0.99 [95% CI: 0.95-1.02]). All sensitivity analyses demonstrated consistent results. We concluded that MPH was associated with a reduced risk of trauma-related ED admission in children and adolescents and this association was found in both male and female patients. This protective association should be considered in clinical practice.

781913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
781913.value: Our research has shown that the percentage of children being prescribed medication for Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in Hong Kong increased 14 times from 2001 to 2013. The percentage of kindergarten children being prescribed ADHD medication increased 6 times from 2009 to 2013. We concluded that ADHD medication prescribing in Hong Kong was increasing but remained lower than most Western countries. However, ADHD medication prescribing for kindergarten children should be monitored to ensure appropriate use. We identified 17,381 children and adolescent patients who had been prescribed methylphenidate (MPH) which has been shown to be an effective treatment for ADHD. Of these patients, 4934 had at least 1 trauma-related Emergency Department (ED) admission. The rate of trauma-related ED admission was lower during MPH treatment periods compared with non-treatment periods. We concluded that MPH treatment was associated with a reduced chance (risk) of trauma-related ED admission in children and adolescents. This protective association should be considered in clinical practice.

782213.label: Project Objectives
782213.value: To evaluate the effectiveness of the family-centered oral health promotion in increasing the proportion of parents brushing their infants’ teeth at 1 year, establishing proper feeding and dietary habits, reducing the transfer of MS from the parents to their infants and reducing the risk of ECC of the children at 3 years. 782213.label: Realisation of objectives
782213.value: In the original application, a 4 year randomized controlled trial of family-centered oral health promotion for new parents was proposed so that early childhood caries (ECC) of children can be assessed at 3 years old. Initially the GRF grant was funded for 3 years and we did apply funding for continuation (RGC Ref No. 17105117), however, the application was not successful. Thus this grant provided funding to collect data until the children reached 2 years old instead of 3 years old. We are using our own resources to continue the 3 years old follow up. During June 2014 to June 2016, a total of 1,989 first time pregnant women (and their husbands) were approached and 589 families met eligibility criteria and agreed to participate in this trial at 5 recruitment sites. After random allocation, 297 and 292 families were assigned in the test and the control groups, respectively. In the test group, oral hygiene instruction (OHI) for the expectant mothers and their husbands together with oral health education materials on infant’s tooth development and eruption, establishment of proper feeding, dietary and toothbrushing habits were given before the delivery of the new born babies. Reinforcement of OHI and demonstrations on how to clean the infant’s oral cavities and perform toothbrushing were delivered after the babies were born at different follow up visits. In the control group, pamphlets on the same topics were distributed to the parents as standard care. The recruited families were followed up at 32nd week of gestation and when the infants (children) reached 1, 2 and 3 years old. The data collection includes questionnaire survey and dental examination. We have successfully achieved at least 70% follow up rate at each time point and completed the 2 years old data collection in Nov 2018. The follow up at 3 years old is ongoing and expected to finish in Dec 2019. Analysis of the collected data enable us to evaluate the effectiveness of the family-centered oral health promotion set in the two objectives.

782213.label: Major findings and research outcome
782213.value: Among the recruited first time pregnant women at baseline, dental visit during pregnancy was not common (<10%) even though they perceived a need for dental visit (~50%, refers to conference abstract #1). About three-quarters of them experienced oral health problems: bleeding gums (37%), bad breath (35%) and sensitivity to hot/cold (30%). Those who were regular dental attenders and having positive oral health attitude were less likely to experience oral health problems. (refers to conference abstracts #3 & #4). Thus it is important to encourage the pregnant women to go for dental visit during pregnancy. Upon the delivery of oral health education (OHE) for the pregnant women, the level of visible plaque (VP) and bleeding on probing (BOP) at the 32nd gestation-week follow up decreased significantly in both groups (p<0.001, refers to conference abstract #2). At the 12-months post-delivery follow up, VP among pregnant women in the test group was maintained while in the control group the effect could not be sustained (p<0.001). Regarding BOP, both groups showed significant decrease but significantly lower in the test group (refers to conference abstracts #2, 6 and publication #1). Providing individualized OHE to pregnant women at early stage of pregnancy can better improve their oral hygiene and periodontal health compared to distribution of OHE brochure, and the effect can be sustained over a longer period. When the infants reached 1 year old, most parents reported satisfactory infant feeding habits. Most parents wiped their infant’s oral cavity regularly before tooth eruption (test: 71%, control: 71%; p>0.05) and cleaned their infant’s teeth regularly after tooth eruption (test: 77%, control: 73%; p>0.05). The proportion of infants with visible plaque was significantly lower in the test group than in the control group (19% vs 55%, p<0.001) indicating those infants in the test group had better oral hygiene (refers to conference abstract #5 and publication #2). In addition, significantly lower proportion of infants in the test group had early sign of caries (white spot lesion, test: 7%, control: 14%, p=0.011, refers to publication #2). Bigger difference in the proportion of infants who had early sign of caries are observed at 2 years old (test: 12%, control: 25%, p<0.05). With these results, it is anticipated that there will be significantly lower proportion of children with ECC in the test group than in the control group at 3 years old. This will support that the family-centered oral health promotion is effective in preventing ECC.

782213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
782213.value: We have conducted a cross-sectional survey and a qualitative study among pregnant women enrolled in the antenatal program in public hospitals in Hong Kong to better understand their dental utilization and oral health problems. Using the collected plaque and saliva samples for the infants, our research team has successfully obtained a funding from Science, Technology and Innovation Commission of Shenzhen Municipality to further explore the temporal and spatial variation of oral microorganisms and to construct a risk assessment model of early childhood caries (ECC) (Project No. 201708183000, RMB500,000). Based on this trial, our team has proposed another randomized controlled trial which aims to investigate the effectiveness of xylitol toothpaste in preventing dental caries among young children with moderate-to-high caries risk and successfully funded by GRF (Project No. 17106117, HK$996,045). As some parents are experiencing challenges when brushing their children's teeth due to their children's noncooperation, our research team is planning to submit an external grant application for investigating the effectiveness of a cognitive behavior approach in helping the parents to perform toothbrushing for their children. We also plan to follow up the participated families when the children reached 5-6 years old to observe the long term effectiveness of the family-centered oral health promotion in reducing ECC.

782213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
782213.value: Early childhood caries (ECC) is a global health problem that causes pain and infection to the children affected. Additionally, it has negative effects on the nutrition, growth and development and general health of the children. It is a common disease among preschool children in Hong Kong. In order to prevent the development of ECC, it is important for parents to establish proper feeding habits for their children and be able to help brushing their children's teeth effectively. This study is a randomized controlled trial of family-centered oral health promotion for new parents (recruited during early-to-mid pregnancy stage) which aims to reduce the risk of ECC of the children at 3 years. We also aim to improve the oral health status of the new parents. Altogether 589 families participated in this study at baseline. Results from this study show that the oral health of the pregnant mothers are improved after receiving the oral health education. Majority of the parents are successful in establishing proper feeding and oral health habits for their 1-year-old infants and the caries risk of children is lower for those who received individualized oral health education compared to distributing pamphlets alone.

782613.label: Project Objectives
782613.value: To investigate the mechanism of how individual resilience factors operate to promote better psychological outcomes in FSWs; and, To develop and evaluate a culturally-adapted and target-specific personal effectiveness intervention as a prevention of psychological stress and potentially the spread of HIV infection in FSWs in Hong Kong.
rows: To investigate the mechanism of how individual resilience factors operate to promote better psychological outcomes in FSWs; and,

To develop and evaluate a culturally-adapted and target-specific personal effectiveness intervention as a prevention of psychological stress and potentially the spread of HIV infection in FSWs in Hong Kong.

782613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
782613.value: Female sex workers (FSWs) are long considered as a reservoir, if not a vector, of HIV and other sexually transmitted infections (STIs) (1). Building upon the existing evidence on the role of psychological health in HIV/STI infections, including our work on FSWs over the last decade, HIV prevention targeted at mental health for FSWs could be an innovative strategy in controlling the spread of the infection. Recent research on resilience provides a positive direction to reinforce individual strengths i.e. self-esteem, self-efficacy and coping, to facilitate positive adaptation. Thus, this study will aim to provide an evidence-based resilience-promoting, personal effectiveness intervention targeted at the mental health, and ultimately, positive sexual health attitudes and safe sexual practices of the targeted population. We propose to conduct a randomised controlled trial (RCT) on 118 FSWs recruited through two local non-governmental organisations (NGOs) randomly assigned to either the intervention or control groups. Between December 2011- March 2012, 23 FSWs were recruited through NGOs to participate in an in-depth semi-structured interview focused on how they had managed their work in the unique environment and its impacts on their psychological health. Their responses were audio-taped and transcribed for analysis to inform and fine-tune the intervention provided in the RCT. The personal effectiveness programme will consist of 6 sessions at one-to-three weeks’ intervals in order to accommodate the nature of their erratic working hours and mobility. The content includes awareness, expression and management of their emotions/ roles, effective problem-solving skills, identifying personal strengths through techniques such as positive reframing, externalising negative events, and reshaping their life experiences. An independent rater will assess all participants’ HIV risk behaviour as well as psychological outcomes such as their perceived stress, self-esteem, self-efficacy, coping and resilience at baseline, post-treatment (after completion of all sessions or 18 weeks whichever comes earlier) and 3-month post-intervention. It is anticipated that this study will: (i) increase our understanding of the relationships between individual resilience attributes, positive adaptation, psychological health and sexual health practices; (ii) apply the identified personal resilience factors and responses held by FSWs in Hong Kong to develop a more effective intervention to promote both psychological well-being and positive sexual health behaviours for this high risk population, so as to provide a new direction for HIV prevention.

782613.label: Realisation of objectives
782613.value: The Randomised Controlled Trial In order to achieve the first objective, a randomised controlled trial was first conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of Personal Resilience and Enrichment Program (PREP) in reducing psychological distress and preventing HIV infections amongst female sex workers (FSWs) in Hong Kong. To address the second objective, the mechanism of how individual resilience factors operate to promote better psychological outcomes in FSWs, i.e. process evaluation, intervention feedback was collected from regular meetings with NGO staff. In addition, the study also explored the operation of resilience factors among FSWs through a mediation model in which intervention received by FSWs would influence psychological outcomes through effects of individual resilience factors (e.g. higher self-esteem, self-efficacy, coping and overall resilience). Furthermore, a focus group discussion with 12 FSWs was conducted to explore the barriers and perceived benefits of the intervention. These provided supplementary information to understand how individual resilience influenced their psychological health and HIV risk behaviours. We contacted several local NGOs and three NGOs, namely Action for Reach Out, JJJ Association, and the Society of Rehabilitation and Crime Prevention Hong Kong, agreed to assist in recruitment and helped organise the intervention for the investigative team. FSWs who worked in different sex work establishments such as nightclubs, single-household brothels and street sex workers, and districts from Yaumatei to Yuen Long in Hong Kong were recruited through these NGOs. FSWs who were: 1) 18 years or older; 2) claimed to have working as a FSW in Hong Kong with in the previous six months; and, 3) were able to speak Cantonese or Putonghua were invited to participate in the study. At recruitment, the group facilitator (Clinical Psychologist by training who was doing this project for her PhD) and a research assistant approached potential FSW participants during outreach services or at the service centres of the NGOs. They explained to the potential participants the purpose and procedure of the study. FSWs were screened and excluded from the study if they had known diagnosis of mental disorders (such as psychosis, bipolar disorder, severe affective disorders) or had been screened positive for suicidal ideation. Before randomisation, all recruited participants would complete a comprehensive baseline survey described below and again at post-intervention (after completion of all sessions or within 15 weeks of enrolment whichever came earlier) and at 3-month follow-ups. Additional arrangements were adopted to minimise attrition: 1) FSWs were contacted and followed up by NGO outreach staff; 2) Stand-alone sessions and flexible time intervals between sessions to accommodate FSWs’ mobile job nature; and, 3) small group size of three-to-six persons so they could feel more comfortable to share their experience. The Intervention The intervention, PREP was designed as six one-hour sessions, based on resilience model and the Transactional Model of Stress and Coping. The content and mode of delivery was based on the previously published qualitative study (Yuen at el. 2014) and observations of FSWs in the local context as specific examples and concerns raised in the qualitative study were incorporated into the intervention. The therapeutic approaches of the intervention utilised psychoeducation, cognitive-behavioural strategies and social learning principles. Psychoeducation addressed personal knowledge on stress, the association among cognitive, emotional, behavioural and physiological components, as well as individual resilience. Cognitive-behavioural strategies targeted thinking processes, emotional experiences and behaviours, and they were used to modify maladaptive thoughts, emotions and behaviours through learning, guided discovery and reflection. Social Learning Principles allowed individuals to learn to express emotions, deal with situations more effectively, and apply their strengths through interactions with the facilitator and other group members. Usual Care Control Participants who were assigned to the control group would receive standard services provided by the NGOs, including outreach visits, attending HIV/STI screening, and social activities according to their personal preferences. Participants were advised not to join any psychological programmes during the study period or they would need to leave the trial. Evaluation of the Randomised Controlled Trial This RCT was evaluated using the Complex Intervention Evaluation Framework based on the Medical Research Council’s guideline on developing and evaluating complex interventions, and included both effectiveness and process evaluation. As the ultimate goal of this intervention was to promote HIV prevention, the primary outcome was the rate of consistent condom use during the last vaginal sexual intercourse with clients. The secondary outcomes were the scores on the Connor-Davison Resilience Scale, Rosenberg’s self-esteem scale, the generalised self-efficacy scale, Brief COPE, psychological distress as measured by General Health Questionnaire, as well as sexual health behaviours such as condom use during oral sex and with partners, and HIV/ STIs screening. Data Analysis The baseline demographics of the intervention and control groups were compared using independent sample t-tests for continuous variables and chi-square for categorical variables. Intention-to-treat approach was adopted with missing values replaced by the last observed values. Repeated measures ANOVA was used to detect any change on sexual health risk behaviour (condom use) and psychological outcome measures (scores on self-esteem, self-efficacy, coping, resilience and General Health Questionnaires) over time between the two groups. For comparison of the dichotomous outcomes between the groups, including condom use with clients and partners and screening for HIV and STIs, chi-square tests or Fisher’s exact tests (when the number was small) were used. New variables (0=no, 1=yes) were created to indicate improvements in condom use from pre- to post-intervention between the two groups. The data collected from focus group discussion was transcribed, coded with open coding and categorised into sub-themes and themes. A multiple mediator model was conducted using the techniques proposed by Preacher and Hayes (2004). This multiple mediation bootstrapping technique resamples the data and estimate the confidence intervals of the mediating effecting. Bootstrapping is a non-parametric sampling procedure without assuming multivariate normality in the sampling distribution to test the significance of the indirect effects. In the mediation analysis, we resampled the data 5,000 times using bootstrapping as recommended by Preacher and Hayes (Preacher & Hayes, 2008) and the results for indirect effect were interpreted for significance by determining whether zero was contained within the 95% confidence interval. The treatment outcome tested was the change in the scores of General Health Questionnaire and improvement in condom use follow up. Independent variables were intervention allocation and changes in psychological measures between pre-intervention and post-intervention. All statistical analyses were conducted using SPSS 23.0 and a macro designed for multiple mediation models was used to test the hypothesis (2008). Statistical tests with p-values of 0.05 or less were considered statistically significant.

782613.label: Major findings and research outcome
782613.value: A total of 165 FSWs were assessed for eligibility and 38 were excluded because they did not fulfil the inclusion criteria (n=15) or declined to participate (n=23). Sixty-four (50.39%) participants were randomly allocated to the control group and 63 (49.61%) joined the intervention group. In total, 70.10% (89/127) of the participants completed both pre- and post-intervention questionnaires, and 52.76% (67/127) of them completed the 3-month follow-up survey. At baseline, the overall psychological distress measured by GHQ-12 was 14.72 (SD=5.56). The scale had a cut-off threshold of 11/12 so 62.5% of FSWs scored >12 at baseline indicated they were highly stressed. Independent sample t-tests showed no significant baseline differences between intervention and control groups in psychological distress, perceived stress, self-esteem, self-efficacy and psychological resilience, except for the maladaptive coping style. It was noted that over 90% of the participants in both groups reported using a condom during vaginal sex in their last transaction, and no significant differences found between groups. As for the changes at post-intervention and 3-month follow-up, participants in the intervention showed greater improvements in resilience scores (F(1.75, 218.55)=6.13, partial eta square =.05, p<.01) and self-esteem scores (F(1.98, 247.21)=6.04, partial eta square=0.05, p<.01), and lowered in psychological distress (F(1.81, 214.25)=6.01, partial eta square=0.05, p< .01) than those of the control groups. The improvements were sustained at 3-month follow-ups. Participants reported more adaptive coping at post-intervention (p<0.001) and at 3-month follow-ups (p<0.001) with those in the intervention showed a more adaptive coping than those in the control. There were no significant time X group interactions in self-esteem scores, maladaptive coping and perceived stress. Since participants reported a very high condom use rate at baseline, only three participants reported a change in their condom use in the last sexual intercourse with clients at post-intervention. Although the results showed no significant differences in condom use, the rate of “always” use condoms during transactions in the past one week among the intervention group increased from 81.03% to 86.67%. At the 3-month follow-up, the rate of “always” use condoms during the past one week were different between intervention and control groups (chi-square = 4.35, p < .01). In the multiple mediation analysis, the total indirect effect of the mediation model was significant. The changes in self-esteem and resilience after intervention significantly mediated the effect of intervention on reduction in psychological distress at follow-up (Figure 1).

782613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
782613.value: The results of the trial were presented in several regional and international conferences (Part C) and, have been and will continue to be published in peer-review journals to stimulate discussions with local and international researchers and frontline professionals in the field. Future research work would include further exploration of the resilience-based framework to understand the experiences of FSWs or other marginalised groups, and its roles in mental health. In view of significantly increased psychological distress experienced by FSWs, it is strongly recommended that the policymakers should re-consider a comprehensive mental health service and access for this population. It becomes apparent that the current HIV prevention programmes based on Health Belief Model, seldom take the emotion of FSWs into account, PREP should be disseminated to other NGOs working with FSWs to improve the psychological well-being and any other interventions that address both psychological health and sexual health could be explored and tested.

782613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
782613.value: This research was aimed to develop an HIV prevention programme that, through improving psychological health, would promote safe sex behaviour in female sex workers (FSWs) in Hong Kong. The effectiveness of this intervention, Personal Resilience and Enrichment Program (PREP) was evaluated through a randomised controlled trial of 127 FSWs. FSWs in our study had high levels of psychological distress and, low resilience and self-esteem at baseline. After 6-hour group modules, the intervention group showed greater improvements in self-esteem, adaptive coping, overall resilience as well as reduction in psychological distress compared to those of the control. Only insignificant changes in condom use were observed as the baseline condom use was high. Self-esteem and resilience was found to have mediated the relationship between intervention and reduction in psychological distress. This study has several significances as it was the first to assess the psychological health and outcomes of FSWs in Hong Kong, and adopted a resilience framework to reframe the HIV prevention to achieve holistic approach to the well-being of FSWs. It takes on new direction in sex work research as well as the understanding of resilience in marginalised groups, and concludes that PREP should be disseminated to other NGOs working with FSWs.

783113.label: Project Objectives
783113.value: To conduct a population-based survey in Hong Kong on local age-specific patterns of social contacts based on the methodology used by the contact survey in Europe. To investigate whether differences in social contact patterns between Hong Kong and European countries is sufficiently large to result in significant difference in age-specific infection attack rate and optimal vaccination strategies for influenza.

To investigate whether differences in social contact patterns between Hong Kong and European countries is sufficiently large to result in significant difference in age-specific infection attack rate and optimal vaccination strategies for influenza.

783113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
783113.value: Many infectious diseases in Hong Kong such as influenza, tuberculosis, and varicella/zoster rely on close contacts between humans for their transmission. Social contact patterns determine both the speed at which these infections spread and the effectiveness of interventions against them (e.g. vaccination, screening and social distancing) [1]. Therefore, understanding the local pattern of social contacts between different groups in a population (with age groups being the most important) is a key step for advancing our knowledge of local epidemiology and control of infectious diseases. Large population-based surveys of age-specific social contacts have been funded by the European Commission for many European countries [2] and by the World Health Organization for low and middle income Asian countries [3]. In contrast, no such surveys have been conducted in high-income urban settings in Asia such as Hong Kong, Singapore and Taiwan. Consequently, mathematical modeling studies of influenza in Hong Kong (as well as the United States) have largely used the contact data from developed countries in Europe for their model parameterization [4,5,6], thus relying on the premise that age-specific social contact patterns are similar to that in Europe which is a questionable assumption. To acquire this missing building block for modeling studies of infectious diseases in Hong Kong, we propose to conduct a population-based survey on local patterns of social contacts. We will adopt the methodology used by the contact survey in Europe both to allow comparability with that study as well as to take advantage of the well-tested methodology [2]. Using the collected data to parameterize our mathematical models for influenza, we will investigate whether differences in age-specific social contact patterns between Hong Kong and European countries result in significant differences in age-specific infection attack rates and optimal vaccination strategies [6]. 在香港，很多傳染病都是通過人與人之間的緊密接觸傳播，例如流感、肺結核和水痘等等。人與人之間的日常接觸模式不但影響傳染病的傳播速度，而且影響各項傳染病防控措施的效果(例如疫苗接種、病例篩查和隔離等等)。因此，對香港不同人群之間的日常接觸模式，尤其是不同年齡組之間的日常接觸模式的了解非常重要。這將有助於增進對傳染病傳播的了解，以及改善傳染病的防控措施。很多歐洲國家已經資助了針對了解當地不同年齡組之間日常接觸模式的大型調查。世界衛生組織也資助了一些中等或低收入亞洲國家進行此類調查。但是這樣的調查卻從來沒有在香港、新加坡和台灣這些高收入亞洲城市地區進行，因而香港和美國的流感數學模型研究人員不得不假設自己當地的接觸模式和歐洲發達國家的相類似，並且利用這些歐洲國家的日常接觸數據作為參數。可是這樣的假設經常會受到質疑。爲了填補傳染病模型研究中缺少的這一項，我們提議採用與歐洲國家相同的調查方法，在香港進行類似的針對人群日常接觸模式的調查。因為他們的方法已經測試可行，而且這樣我們的研究可以和他們的相比較。當得到本地的日常接觸數據之後，我們將會比較香港和歐洲的日常接觸模式是否不同，並且探討不同的接觸數據參數是否對流感數學模型的結果有明顯影響，例如是否影響不同年齡組流感感染率的估計，或者是否需要對疫苗接種策略作出調整等。

783113.label: Realisation of objectives
783113.value: Objective 1 Using similar methodology to a large European contact survey, we examined social contacts and quantified the contact mixing pattern in Hong Kong. Overall, we recorded a mean of 8.1 contacts per participant per day, which was substantially lower than the 13.4 contacts in the European data and 18.0 contacts reported in the previous Hong Kong contact survey. Participants using paper questionnaires reported a significantly greater number of contacts and longer contact duration than those using online questionnaires, and the choice of questionnaire was strongly associated with age, education and income level. Similar to the European data, we found significant overdispersion in contact number and total contact duration, and pronounced assortativity in the age-specific contact matrix. We found participants with more years of education and higher income levels were more likely to choose online questionnaires, and to report more contacts, after adjusting for questionnaire mode in the propensity score analysis. The finding was consistent with time use data from census statistics, showing a tendency for individuals with more years of education and higher income levels to spend more time on social and leisure activities, while the individuals with less education and lower income levels spent more time on household commitments. The comparison of data obtained from paper and online questionnaires was not part of our original study design. This post-hoc analysis was done because of the apparent difference observed in the number of reported contacts between the two modes. Nonetheless, our study is one of the few contact surveys to investigate both the determinants and outcomes of using paper vs online questionnaires in all age groups. More investigation of questionnaire design and administration should be considered in the future contact survey studies, given with the rapidly growing use of online tools for data collection. We analyzed the effect of prospective and retrospective completion by assessing the actual time that participants filling in each contact entry. We found that more than 95% of participants were likely to have completed the questionnaires retrospectively, even though we encouraged them to do it prospectively. Despite the limited number of prospective participants, we found that more contacts were reported in prospective participants, and the effect was statistically significant among online questionnaires. The overall low average number of reported contacts in our survey might reflect the recall bias introduced by the retrospective behavior of our participants. While the analyses we were able to do was limited by the small number of prospectively filled questionnaires, more comparisons between prospective and retrospective surveys could be conducted if future contact surveys incorporate information about recording time. With the increasing use of smart phones and wearables, future social contact surveys might also consider using these devices to send out several reminders during the assigned days, or upon changes in the location of participants such as home to school or work to leisure, hence minimizing reliance on participants’ memory to record contact events retrospectively. Heterogeneities among the various methods used in social contact surveys make it difficult to directly compare contact data obtained from different populations. More comparison between different social contact surveys could be done if more detailed documentation of contact data were available online. Objective 2 We explored the potential effects of different social contact data in the estimation of influenza infection attack rates in an age-stratified influenza transmission model we used for the influenza pandemic in 2009, and found that the difference did not generate substantial differences in the model estimates. Estimates of infection attack rates and severity (i.e. age-specific infection hospitalization probability in the context of the 2009 influenza pandemic) were similar to the estimates we obtained before with the European POLYMOD contact matrices. Vaccine allocation strategies will not be significantly affected if the allocation is optimized in the influenza transmission model with the similar age-specific infection attack rates and severity estimates. We evaluated the characteristics of social contacts and mixing patterns relevant to the spread of respiratory infectious diseases in Hong Kong. Our data provide important information to improve the parameterization of mathematical models for infectious disease transmissions in Hong Kong, especially respiratory infections through close contacts such as varicella, RSV and influenza. Our findings could help to improve the design of future social contact surveys, and inform intervention strategies based on the outputs of modelling studies.

783113.label: Major findings and research outcome
783113.value: We conducted a population-based social contact survey in Hong Kong using participant-completed diaries similar to those used in the European POLYMOD study by Mossong et al, using both paper and online questionnaires. Participants using paper questionnaires reported more contacts and longer contact duration than those using online questionnaires. Participants reported 13 person-hours of contact and 8 contacts per day on average, which decreased over age but increased with household size, years of education and income level. Prolonged and frequent contacts, and contacts at home, school and work were more likely to involve physical contacts. Strong age-assortativity was observed in all age groups. The choice of the mode of questionnaire was strongly associated with participant age, education and income level in our sample, and therefore its effect on the number of reported contacts and contact duration may be confounded. In the mediation analysis, the number of contacts reported in paper questionnaires was found to be significantly higher than online questionnaires after other participant characteristics were considered. Despite the small number of prospective participants identified, there was a statistically significant difference in the number of reported contacts between prospectively and retrospectively filled-in online questionnaires. We explored the potential effects of different social contact data in the estimation of influenza infection attack rates in an age-stratified influenza transmission model we used for the influenza pandemic in 2009, and found that the difference did not generate substantial differences in the model estimates. Estimates of infection attack rates and severity (i.e. age-specific infection hospitalization probability in the context of the 2009 influenza pandemic) were similar to the estimates we obtained before with the European POLYMOD contact matrices. Vaccine allocation strategies will not be significantly affected if the allocation is optimized in the influenza transmission model with the similar age-specific infection attack rates and severity estimates.

Nonetheless, our study is one of the few contact surveys to investigate both the determinants and outcomes of using paper vs online questionnaires in all age groups. 783113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
783113.value: The spread of many respiratory infections is determined by contact patterns between infectious and susceptible individuals in the population. There are no published data for quantifying social contact patterns relevant to the spread of respiratory infectious diseases in Hong Kong which is a hotspot for emerging infectious diseases due to its high population density and connectivity in the air transportation network. We adopted a commonly used diary-based design to conduct a social contact survey in Hong Kong in 2015/16 using both paper and online questionnaires and evaluated the characteristics of social contact patterns relevant to the spread of respiratory infectious diseases in Hong Kong. We explored the potential effects of different social contact data in the estimation of influenza infection attack rates in an age-stratified influenza transmission model we used for the influenza pandemic in 2009, and found that the difference did not generate substantial differences in the model estimates. Vaccine allocation strategies will not be affected if the allocation is optimized in the influenza transmission model. Our findings could help to improve the design of future social contact surveys, parameterize transmission models of respiratory infectious diseases, and inform intervention strategies based on model outputs.

783413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
783413.value: Blood glucose levels are tightly regulated within a very narrow range in our bodies to maintain metabolic homeostasis. While hyperglycemia is a hallmark of diabetes and its cardiovascular complications, hypoglycemia causes seizures, unconsciousness, brain damage and even death. In healthy people, hormonal network plays a central role in controlling glucose homeostasis in response to nutritional and circadian changes. In the fed state, insulin is released from β cells to promote glucose clearance from bloodstream. During fasting/starvation, catabolic hormones, such as glucagon and glucocorticoids, maintain blood glucose supply by enhancing glucose production. Aberrant production and/or malfunction of these hormones are implicated in the pathogenesis of glucose dysregulation in diabetes and many other metabolic diseases. Fibroblast growth factor (FGF) 21 is a metabolic hormone mainly secreted from hepatocytes. As therapeutic administration of recombinant FGF21 has been shown to exert multiple metabolic benefits on obesity-related disorders, it has recently attracted a great interest in pharmaceutical industry. Physiologically, hepatic FGF21 expression and circulating FGF21 concentration are markedly induced by fasting/starvation, and elevated FGF21 in turn mediates metabolic adaptations to fasting/starvation, including ketogenesis and growth inhibition. However, the physiological role of FGF21 in regulating glucose metabolism remains unclear. Our recent study on FGF21 knockout mice found that FGF21 deficiency has no obvious effect on postprandial blood glucose levels, but causes a severe hypoglycemia during prolonged fasting/starvation. Such a hypoglycemic phenotype in fasted FGF21 knockout mice is associated with a marked impairment in secretion of glucocorticoids from adrenal gland and its upstream hypothalamus regulator corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH). Notably, central administration of FGF21 into the hypothalamus region reverses fasting hypoglycemia and impairment in CRH/glucocorticoid production in FGF21 knockout mice. These findings promote us to propose that FGF21 is a key metabolic hormone for maintaining glucose homeostasis during fasting/starvation, by activating the hypothalamus-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis to produce glucocorticoids, which in turn enhances hepatic glucose production. In this study, we will use an integrated in vivo and in vitro approach to test this hypothesis, and will investigate the receptor and postreceptor signaling mechanisms whereby FGF21 controls glucose homeostasis via its actions in the HPA axis. The results will not only enrich our knowledge on hormonal control of glucose metabolism, but also help to validate the feasibility of using FGF21 and its receptors as a therapeutic target for combating the global epidemic of diabetes and other metabolic diseases. 爲了維持代謝穩態，健康人體的血糖水平被嚴格控制在非常小的範圍內。高血糖是糖尿病及其心腦血管併發癥的特徵標誌，而低血糖則可以引發癲癇發作、昏迷、腦損傷、甚至死亡。在應對營養和晝夜節律性變化的過程中，健康人體內的激素調控對血糖穩態發揮了主導性的作用。在飽餐狀態下，分泌自胰腺的胰島素能夠將血液循環中的葡萄糖清除。而在空腹狀態下，一些參與分解代謝的激素，例如胰高血糖素和糖皮質激素，則能夠通過促進肝臟中葡萄糖的產生而維持穩定的空腹血糖水平。如果這些激素的生成或者功能發生異常，則會造成糖尿病和其他代謝性疾病中常見的血糖失調的病理性病變。 成纖維生長因子(FGF) 21 是一種主要自肝臟細胞分泌的代謝激素。最近研究發現使用重組FGF21治療能夠顯著改善眾多肥胖相關的代謝性疾病，因而引起醫藥行業的廣泛興趣。在生理狀態下，禁食或者飢餓能夠促發肝臟合成和分泌FGF21，并提高血液循環中FGF21的水平。在這種情況下，FGF21能夠介導機體去適應飢餓的狀態，包括促進生酮作用和抑制生長的作用。然而，FGF21對生理狀態下糖代謝的調控作用依然未知。 我們最近在FGF21基因敲除小鼠上的研究發現，FGF21的缺失沒有對餐後血糖產生影響，但是在長時間飢餓的狀態下，能夠導致基因敲除小鼠產生嚴重的低血糖。這種低血糖癥狀伴隨著從腎上腺分泌的糖皮質激素及其上游調控因子-下丘腦促皮质素释放激素（CRH）的合成和分泌功能顯著受損。值得注意的是，將FGF21補充進FGF21敲除小鼠的下丘腦中可以逆轉飢餓導致的低血糖和受損的CRH和糖皮質激素的分泌。這些發現促使我們提出這樣的設想：在禁食或者飢餓狀態下，FGF21作為一種重要的代謝激素，能夠通過激活下丘腦-腦下垂體-腎上腺（HPA）軸而增加糖皮質激素的分泌，并進一步增加肝臟的生糖功能，從而維持血糖穩態。 在這個研究中，我們將使用體內和體外的實驗方法來驗證這個設想。同時我們亦將從受體和受體后信號機制的水平深入研究FGF21通過激活HPA軸來調控血糖穩態的分子機制。這些研究結果不僅有助於增加我們對糖代謝的激素調控機制的認識，同時亦有助於驗證將FGF21和它的受體作為治療糖尿病或者其他的代謝性疾病的治療靶標的這種可行性。

783413.label: Realisation of objectives
783413.value: This study aims to investigate how the liver-derived metabolic hormone FGF21 controls blood glucose homeostasis during fasting/starvation, and to uncover the molecular pathways involved. Realization of objective-1: To further explore the physiological roles of FGF21 in maintaining glucose homeostasis during prolonged fasting and to interrogate whether such an effect is mediated by induction of glucocorticoids, we performed a series of glucose clamping studies in FGF21 knockout (KO) mice, PPARα KO mice and their wildtype littermates using 14C-labelled glucose tracer. Our results consistently showed that FGF21 KO mice exhibited hypoglycemia during prolonged fasting (12 hours or above), which was accompanied by reduced hepatic glucose production (HGP) and impaired fasting-induced production of adrenal glands-derived glucocorticoids, whereas peripheral glucose proposal in skeletal muscle and fat tissue was not affected. Furthermore, we found that intracerebroventricular (i.c.v) injection of recombinant FGF21 (rFGF21), at a dosage not detectable in the peripheral blood, reversed the hypoglycemia and impaired HGP and glucocorticoids in both FGF21 KO and PPARα KO mice, suggesting that FGF21maintain fasting glucose homeostasis via its central actions, but not the direct effects on hepatocytes. Indeed, by performing in vitro experiments in both primary hepatocytes and liver explants of mice, we did not observe any direct effect of FGF21 on expression of hepatic gluconeogenic gene expression and glucose production, further confirming that the effect of FGF21 on induction of hepatic gluconeogenesis is indirect. We further conducted both gain- and loss-of-functional experiments to define whether glucocorticoids act as a downstream effector of FGF21 in induction of HGP. Replenishment with glucocorticoids was found to be sufficient to counteract the defective HGP and hypoglycemia in FGF21 and PPARα KO mice, whereas the central effects of FGF21 on induction of hepatic gluconeogenic program and HGP were abrogated by either pretreatment of mice with the glucocorticoid receptor (GR) antagonist RU486 or by surgical removal of adrenal glands (adrenalectomy) to deplete endogenous corticosterone. This series of animal data demonstrated that FGF21 maintains fasting glucose homeostasis via mediating the crosstalk between liver and brain. Realization of objective-2: To investigate whether the central effects of FGF21 in regulating glucose homeostasis is mediated by its receptors in specific brain regions, we firstly performed immunocytochemistry and Western analysis for the localization and abundance of FGFR1 and ß-klotho (co-receptor), and our results showed that both of them were highly expressed in the hypothalamus region of the brain, and co-localized with corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH)-expressing neurons of the paraventricular nucleus (PVN) region. Furthermore, we found that the central effects of FGF21 on induction of CRH expression, induction of glucocorticoids, and stimulation of hepatic gluconeogenesis were abrogated by either central blockage of FGFR1 using its neutralization monoclonal antibodies, or by hypothalamus-specific ablation of ß-klotho. Furthermore, we characterized the metabolic changes of the hypothalamus-selective β-klotho KO mice in C57BL/6J background, and found that the mice normal glucose in fed status, but display hypoglycemia, impaired hepatic glucose production, and blunted adrenal gland release of glucocorticoids (corticosterone) in fasted condition, resembling to those observed in FGF21 KO mice. Realization of objective-3: To elucidate the molecular mechanism underlying FGF21-induced production of CRH in the hypothalamic neurons, we firstly interrogated the direct effects of rFGF21 on induction of CRH using ex vivo explants of hypothalamic slices isolated from β-klotho KO mice and WT controls treated with different concentrations of rFGF21, followed by followed by real-time PCR analysis for quantification of CRH mRNA levels and ELISA for measurement of CRH in the conditioned medium. This analysis demonstrated rFGF21 stimulated CRH expression and release in a ß-klotho-dependent manner, which was accompanied by activation of the MAP kinase ERK1/2. By using pharmacological inhibitors, siRNA knockdown and chromatin immunoprecipitation, we found that ERK1/2 mediated the stimulatory effects of rFGF21 on CRH expression by phosphorylation-dependent activation of the transcription factor CREBP (cAMP response elements-binding protein), which in turn transactivated the CRH gene. We further confirmed the physiological relevance of the abovementioned findings by demonstrating that central administration of rFGF21 in the hypothalamic region induced phosphorylation of ERK1/2 and CREBP in the PVN using both Western blot and immunostaining analysis. Furthermore, pretreatment of mice with PD98059 (a selective ERK1/2 inhibitor) by ICV administration blocked the effects of FGF21 on phosphorylation of CREBP and expression of CRH in hypothalamic neurons, release of ACTH from pituitary glands, elevation of circulating glucocorticoids, expression of gluconeogenic genes in the liver and HGP. Therefore, this series of in vitro and animal studies consistently suggest that FGF21 induces the expression of the CRH gene by binding to its receptor complexes (FGFR1/ß-klotho) in hypothalamic neurons, which in turn activates the ERK1/2-CREBP signaling axis.

783413.label: Major findings and research outcome
783413.value: In this project, we uncovered a novel physiological role of FGF21 as a fasting-responsive hormone mediating fasting/starvation-induced hepatic glucose production, thereby avoiding excess fluctuation and hypoglycemia, as summarized below: 1. Upon fasting/starvation, FGF21 is induced in the liver by the nuclear receptor PPARα, enters into the bloodstream, and transverses the blood-brain barrier into the hypothalamic region. 2. Both FGF21 KO mice and PPARα KO mice obvious hypoglycemia due to impaired hepatic gluconeogenesis during prolonged fasting, accompanied with impaired activation of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis (HPA) and blunted release of corticosterone from adrenal glands into bloodstream. 3. FGF21 has no direct effects on induction of hepatic gluconeogenic program and glucose production in either primary hepatocytes and liver explants of mice. 4. Central administration of recombinant FGF21 via intracerebroventricular, but not peripheral injection, reverses fasting hypoglycemia and impairments of hepatic glucose production by restoration of corticosterone in both FGF21 KO and PPARα KO mice 5. The hypoglycemic phenotype of both FGF21 KO and PPARα KO mice are reversed by administration of cortisol, whereas the central effects of FGF21 on induction of hepatic gluconeogenesis and reversal of hypoglycemia are blocked by the pharmacological or surgical removal of corticosterone, monoclonal antibody-based inhibition of hypothalamic FGFR1, genetic depletion of hypothalamic β-klotho, or pharmacological inhibition of ERK1/2. 6. FGF21 acts directly on the hypothalamic neurons to activate FGFR1/β-klotho-ERK1/2-CREBP signaling axis, leading to the transcriptional activation of corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH) and subsequent activation of the HPA axis. Collectively, our study suggests that FGF21 maintains glucose homeostasis during prolonged fasting by fine tuning the interorgan cross talk between liver and brain. This project resulted in two publications in Diabetes (Liang Q, 2014 Dec;63(12):4064-75), Diabetes Metab J (Jin L, 2016 Feb;40(1):22-31), and the paper in Diabetes was selected as a commentary article (entitled “Head over hepatocytes for FGF21, by Potthoff MJ). Our Diabetes paper has already been cited by 76 times so far. The PhD student trained under this project (Qing Ning Liang) received Li Ka Shing Prizes for outstanding PhD thesis.

783413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
783413.value: This study uncovered a novel physiological action of FGF21 in the brain, and identified hypothalamic neurons as a target cell of FGF21. The findings open a new field to study how FGF21 handles various stresses by integrating the crosstalk among the major organs and by regulating hormonal network. The results from this project led us to propose that FGF21 may be a key mediator of physical exercise-induced improvement of depression via its neuronal actions and/or through multiorgan crosstalk. A HMRF grant has been awarded to further test this hypothesis. Furthermore, we are using β-klotho-floxed mice established in this project to further dissect the actions of FGF21 in other stress conditions such as environmental cold and nutritional excess, which has been funded by another GRF grant. Additionally, we have established collaborative network with several clinical teams in mainland China (Prof. Jia Weiping, Shanghai 6th hospital) and Australia Clinical Trial Centre at University of Sydney (Prof. Anthony Keech) to further explore the clinical relevance of FGF21 in regulation of glucose homeostasis in different ethnic groups.

783413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
783413.value: Maintenance of glucose homeostasis is a key aspect of our metabolic heath. Both hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia are harmful to our body. During fasting/starvation, our brains send the hormonal signals to the liver for stimulation of glucose production, thereby avoiding hypoglycemia. However, how the brain can sense fasting/starvation signals to activate hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis for hepatic glucose production remains elusive. In this connection, this study uncovered the liver-secreted hormone as the missing link by sending the starvation signal to the hypothalamic neurons, where it triggers the release of a neuronal peptide hormone for activation of the HPA axis, which in turn maintains fasting glucose homeostasis. These findings not only shed new light on how our glucose levels are maintained through a complex hormonal network and multi-organ crosstalk, and but also reinforce FGF21 as a key stress-responsive hormone and master regulator of metabolic homeostasis. Our results can also explain why several recent clinical trials failed to observe any glucose-lowering effects of recombinant FGF21 in obese individuals with diabetes, despite the promising outcomes in insulin sensitivity and dyslipidemia. The data obtained from this study will help the rationale design of FGF21 analogs for treatment of various metabolic disorders.
