783513.label: Realisation of objectives
783513.value: I. Results and findings following the funding proposal Objective 1. Substantiate the anaerobic induction of selective efflux genes at mRNA and protein levels. 1.1. Reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) to analyze the transcripts of acrEF, acrD, and mdfA during anaerobiosis in glucose M9 medium. RT-qPCR was conducted in triplicates following the standard protocol using two genes, gmk and gyrB, as references. The results indicated only ~15% increase of the expression of the three genes under anaerobic condition than aerobic condition. We next examined the expression of the whole collection of promoter-lacZ fusions of efflux genes under a broad range of carbon sources and electron acceptors under anaerobic conditions. 1.2. Transcription assay of promoter-lacZ fusions in the presence of various carbon sources and electron acceptors. Recently, it was reported that an oxidized sulfur compound tetrathionate is produced during gut inflammation through the metabolic interaction between the host microbiota and immune responses. S. typhimurium can utilize this compound and respire tetrathionate to promote its growth and rapid transmission in this circumstances. We then examined the transcription of all efflux genes during the anaerobic respiration of tetrathionate by β-gal assay and found that transcription of acrD was significantly induced under this condition. 1.3 Substantiate the induction of acrD during tetrathionate respiration at mRNA and protein levels. We then performed RT-qPCR and found a 3-fold increase of mRNA level of acrD during anaerobic tetrathionate respiration comparing with that under aerobic conditions. We also constructed a strain in which the acrD locus is tagged with triple-FLAG and examined the production of AcrD-3FLAG protein by Western-blot. We found a significant production of AcrD-3FLAG when S. typhimurium respires tetrathionate under anaerobic condition. In addition, we also examined the effect of tetrathionate respiration on the induction of acrD in the presence of a wide range of carbon sources and found that AcrD was also upregulated when glucose, glycerol, pyruvate, and citrate serves as the carbon source, suggesting a genera role of AcrD in the tetrathionate respiration of S. typhimurium. The objective 1 is completed. Next, we focus on the regulation and physiological roles of AcrD. Objective 2. Study the regulatory mechanisms of the induced efflux (AcrD) expression. 2.1. The role of the global regulators FNR and ArcAB. It is known that in both E. coli and S. typhimurium, two global regulatory systems control the transition from the aerobic to anaerobic lifestyle: the global transcription factor FNR (fumarate and nitrate reduction) and the two component system (TCS) ArcAB (anaerobic respiration control). We constructed fnr and arcA deletion strains and found that deletion of fnr led to significant reduction of the production of AcrD-FLAG under anaerobic tetrathionate respiration, whereas deletion of arcA had no detectable effect, suggesting that the induction of acrD under anaerobic tetrathionate respiration was dependent on FNR. However, when we examined the transcription of acrD using the PacrD-lacZ fusion, we did not observe decreased transcription of acrD in the Δfnr strain, suggesting FNR indirectly regulate the expression of acrD. 2.2. acrD is activated by the two component systems BaeSR and CpxAR under anaerobic tetrathionate respiration. The Co-I Nishino et al has reported that in E. coli, expression of AcrD is regulated by two two-component-systems (TCS) BaeSR and CpxAR which senses envelope stresses. Moreover, our proteomics (see below) study revealed that expression of BaeSR and CpxAR is induced under anaerobic tetrathionate respiration. We then constructed ΔbaeSR and ΔcpxAR and found that deletion of baeSR or cpxAR abolished the induction of acrD under anaerobic tetrathionate respiration condition at both transcriptional and protein level, suggesting that induction of acrD under anaerobic tetrathionate respiration was regulated by BaeSR and CpxAR. 2.3. Induction of AcrD under anaerobic tetrathionate respiration is mediated by the production of sulfide. It is known that several metabolic intermediates are produced during tetrathionate respiration, including thiosulfate, sulfite, and sulfide. To examine how the BaeSR and CpxAR systems are induced under tetrathionate respiration, we first examined the effect of these metabolic intermediates and products. β-galactosidase assay revealed that supplement of NaHS, a donor of sulfide, but not sulfite, induced the acrD transcription, and deletion of baeSR abolished this induction, suggesting that sulfide is the signal that induces the BaeSR system which in turn activates the expression of acrD. RT-qPCR analysis confirmed this finding. Sulfide has been reported to chelate biological transition metals, such as Cu and Zn, to form metal-sulfide precipitations in the cell. This reaction dysregulates metal homeostasis and causes envelope stress in bacterial cells which is the physiological perturbation that activates the BaeSR and CpxAR regulatory systems. To examine this, we performed transmission electron microscopy (TEM) of S. typhimurium cells grown under aerobic and anaerobic tetrathionate respiration, and found that dark electron dense granules representing metal sulfide complexes are present in cells cultured under anaerobic tetrathionate respiration. Deletion of acrD led to further accumulation of these granules, suggesting that sulfide production leads to envelope stress which leads to the activation of AcrD and induction of AcrD is necessary to detoxify the effect of sulfide under tetrathionate respiration condition. Objective 2 is completed. In addition to the initially proposed studies, TEM was conducted to confirm the occurrence of envelope stress during anaerobic tetrathionate respiration and the role of AcrD to detoxify sulfide cytotoxicity. Objective 3. Physiological roles of the anaerobically induced efflux pump. 3.1. Drug susceptibility profile of anaerobically grown S. typhimurium. Owing to the upregulation of AcrD, S. typhimurium cells grown under anaerobic tetrathionate respiration displayed decreased susceptibility to aminoglycoside antibiotics (gentamycin, kanamycin, streptomycin) and increased tolerance to the detergent SDS. 3.2. Roles of these efflux proteins to the anaerobic metabolism of S. typhimurium. Since sulfide displays high affinity to transition metals and cause metal dysregulation, S. typhimurium cells lacking acrD displayed increased sensitivity to Cu and Zn, and displayed competitive disadvantages when it is co-cultured with the WT under anaerobic tetrathionate respiration condition. 3.3. Roles of these efflux proteins to the fitness and intracelluar survival of S. typhimurium. Cells lacking acrD displayed decreased replication and survival in the macrophage cells J774A.1 and RAW 264.7. Objective 3 is completed. Taken together, these results suggest that multidrug efflux pump (AcrD in this case) has physiological roles in bacteria and its expression is subject regulation by stress responses transcription factors. Given their well-established roles in causing antibiotic resistance, antimicrobial therapies inhibiting these proteins or their regulators have the potential to target both pathogenicity and antibiotic resistance. II. Additional experiments conducted and the findings achieved 4. Comparative proteomics of S. Typhimurium 14028s during during tetrathionate respiration and aerobic respiration. 4.1. Our proteomic analysis identified 126 proteins which showed different expression levels under tetrathionate respiration conditions compared to those under aerobic respiration conditions. Among them, 103 proteins were up-regulated and 23 proteins were down-regulated. 4.2. COG analysis revealed that down-regulated proteins are those mainly involved in amino acid transport and metabolism and up-regulated proteins mainly include those in energy production, coenzyme transport and cell motility. 4.3. Network analysis using the STRING database revealed protein networks among the down-regulated and up-regulated proteins, respectively. 5. U-pregulation of a novel disulfide bond formation system ScsBC under anaerobic tetrathionate respiration. (details are shown in section 6.2) 6. Identification of a novel cysteine thiol post translational modification (S-sulfhydration) during anaerobic tetrathionate respiration. (details are shown in section 6.3)

783513.label: Major findings and research outcome
783513.value: Major findings: Recent studies show that the metabolic interaction of microbiota and host immune response led to the production of tetrathionate in the inflamed gut. However, how S. Typhimurium adapts to this metabolic status remains largely unknown. In this proposal, we explored the role of multidrug efflux pumps and conducted a high-throughput study to investigate the functional proteomics of S. Typhimurium ATCC 14028s in response to tetrathionate respiration. Expression of 126 proteins is found to be altered during tetrathionate respiration compared to that during aerobic respiration. Among them, 23 proteins are down-regulated and 103 proteins are up-regulated. Particularly, tetrathionate respiration leads to 3-fold up-regulation of the multidrug efflux pump AcrD. We found that this up-regulation is mediated by the envelope stress response regulators BaeSR and CpxAR, which are activated by the metabolic product sulfide. S. Typhimurium cells lacking acrD displays increased sensitivity to aminoglycoside antibiotics and SDS, and decreased replication and survival in macrophages. In addition, proteomics analysis identified the up-regulation of two proteins, ScsBC, which function does not show directly relevance to metabolism shift under anaerobic tetrathionate respiration. We found expression of ScsBC, a disulfide bond formation system, is up-regulated 35-fold during tetrathionate respiration. This led us to hypothesize that protein disulfide bond formation is defected during anaerobic tetrathionate respiration, presumably due to the production of sulfide during this metabolic process. Indeed, LC-MS/MS identified novel Cys thiol PTM, S-sulfhydration, in four proteins, HisJ, STM3650, GlpQ, and OppA in S. Typhimurium cells undergo tetrathionate respiration. scsBC leads to decreased viability of the bacterium, increased sensitivity to copper (Cu), reduced swarming motility, and reduced secretion of SPI-1 effector SipB. scsBC is found to be necessary for the survival of S. Typhimurium in the intestine of C. elegans host. Taken together, these studies revealed two novel adaptation strategies S. Typhimurium utilizes to adapt to the physiologically relevant tetrathionate respiration condition. These studies advanced our understandings on the virulence and drug resistance development during bacterial stress adaptation. Outcomes: Publications: 1. 783513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
783513.value: The most interesting finding in our investigation is the up-regulation of the disulfide bond formation protein ScsBC during the anaerobic tetrathionate respiration. Several virulence related phenotypes such as the swarming motility and production and secretion of the effector protein SipB were defected in scsBC deletion strain, suggesting its role in the stress adaptation and virulence of S.Typhimurium. In addition, four proteins with a novel thiol post translational modification were identified in scsBC deletion S. Typhimurium, implying a novel function of ScsBC in protecting cysteine thiols from S-sulfhydration PTM. Further investigation of these molecular details could lead to the identification of novel Cys thiol PTMs and the novel functions of the Dsb (Disulfide bond formation) family enzymes. A proposal based on these interesting findings and preliminary data has been submitted for GRF funding in 2018.

783513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
783513.value: Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium is a foodborne pathogen that infects both animals and humans and causes acute intestinal inflammation. During its infection of the hosts, S. Typhimurium is challenged with various physiological stresses including low oxygen tension, host derived antimicrobial peptides, reactive oxygen species etc.. Investigating how the pathogen adapt to these environments, especially through altering the expression profiles of various stress response and virulence proteins, is essential to develop novel antimicrobial therapies. It is known that during gut inflammation, the metabolic interaction of microbiota and host immune response lead to the production of tetrathionate which promotes S. Typhimurium growth and transmission through tetrathionate respiration. In this proposal, we conducted a high-throughput study to investigate the functional proteomics of S. Typhimurium ATCC 14028s in response to tetrathionate respiration. 23 proteins are found to be down-regulated and 103 proteins are up-regulated. We specifically investigated the up-regulation of two systems: the multidrug efflux pump AcrD and the disulfide bond formation enzymes ScsBC. Our studies led to the identification of novel post translational modifications essential for the virulence of S. Typhimurium and clearly showed that these two proteins, ScsC and AcrD, can serve as targets for the development of novel antimicrobials.

783613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
783613.value: 肝细胞癌（HCC）在东南亚地区发病率非常高，成为香港因病死亡的第二杀手。高复发率和转移率导致HCC患者的总体预后很差。Met是肝细胞生长因子（HGF）的受体酪氨酸激酶，HGF可以激活Met，从而继发大范围的生理信号级联反应。人类肿瘤通常伴有HGF-Met信号通路紊乱，因而，Met成为一个潜在的肿瘤治疗靶点，并且正在开展应用Met拮抗剂治疗肿瘤的临床试验。然而，越来越多的研究表明核Met在某些肿瘤组织和细胞系中存在表达，这说明在细胞核内，核Met还有些未知功能。这一发现无疑对当前针对于细胞表面Met受体的治疗方法提出了质疑和挑战。研究发现，细胞核Met来源于Met受体的蛋白裂解，但Met的加工过程及其从细胞表面转移至核内的机制尚不清楚，且核Met的绝大部分功能也是未知的。仅有零星研究发现，核Met具有生物活性。 Met已经被证实在HCC中呈过表达状态，但核Met表达情况未见报道。我们研究发现，在HCC中确实存在核Met过表达，而且与HCC进展和静脉侵袭有关。只有在使用针对Met羧基末端的抗体时，才能检测到核Met，表明核Met仅仅参与构成Met蛋白胞浆部分的羧基端。不论HGF存在与否，均可以在细胞核裂解物或胞核显像中检测到较Met具有更低分子量的核Met。在功能方面，核Met的表达能够促进HCC细胞侵袭，因此，我们推测，核Met通过在细胞核中发挥作用而促进了HCC的发生和转移。本项目旨在阐明核Met在HCC中的功能角色和分子途径。为此，我们将（1）评估核Met与HCC的临床相关性；（2）明确核Met在HCC转移中的作用；（3）描绘核Met参与HCC发生发展的分子途径。据我们所知，这是首次报道核Met在HCC中的功能研究，本研究将揭示肝癌崭新的发生发展机制，为HCC的治疗干预措施提供新的视角。

783613.label: Realisation of objectives
783613.value: 1. To evaluate the clinicopathological relevance and prognostic significance of nMet in HCC To evaluate the clinicopathological relevance and prognostic significance of nMet in HCC Immunohistochemistry of nMet was performed using tissue microarray comprising 103 cases of paired HCC tissues and corresponding non-tumorous liver tisses. Statistical analysis of nMet overexpression with clinicopathological parameters was performed. The study on this objective was successfully accomplished. 2. To characterize the functional role of nMet in HCC invasiveness and metastasis To characterize the functions of nMet in HCC, we first encountered the problem in stably expressing nMet in HCC cell lines after several attempts using different expression vectors of nMet and in different HCC cell lines. Due to the possible toxic effect of nMet in cells, we finally established stable clones of nMet in different HCC cell lines using an inducible expression system. The expression of nMet was induced by the addition of doxycycline in culture or in drinking water for the animal. These stable clones with inducible nMet expression were subjected to various in vitro and in vivo functional assays. This objective was successfully addressed. 3. To delineate the molecular pathways of nMet in HCC To delineate the molecular pathways of nMet in HCC, we tested the effect of nMet on various reporter systems. We identified NF-kB as the downstream pathway provoked by nMet. Furthermore, we also identified TAK1 as the intermediate molecular player between nMet and NF-kB. To test whether the functional effect of nMet is driven by TAK1/NF-kB pathway, expression of NF-kB and TAK1 was suppressed in nMet overexpressing cells. The knockdown cells were then subjected to various functional assays. This objective was successfully addressed.

783613.label: Major findings and research outcome
783613.value: 1. To evaluate the clinicopathological relevance and prognostic significance of nMet in HCC Using immunohistochemistry, our findings revealed intense nMet staining in 89.3% (92/103) of HCC tissues but weak staining in all corresponding non-tumorous livers. Overall nMet expression was significantly higher in tumorous tissues than in corresponding non-tumorous tissues (P < 0.0001). We also observed a progressive increase in nMet expression during the development of HCC from non-tumorous livers with chronic hepatitis (17.0%) and cirrhosis (17.4%) as well as early HCC (30.1%) and advanced HCC (40.6%). Elevated nMet level was significantly correlated with the presence of venous invasion (P = 0.029). Herein, we have provided the first evidence about the presence of nMet in HCC (ECC 2013; AACR 2014). 2. To characterize the functional role of nMet in HCC invasiveness and metastasis The functional assays showed that the induced nMet expression significantly promoted HCC cell growth and anchorage independent growth. It also significantly augmented HCC cell migration and invasiveness. In animal model of subcutaneous injection and orthotopic liver implantation, induced expression of nMet enhanced tumor formation in liver and distant metastasis to lungs. This finding suggests a pivotal role of nMet in HCC tumorigenesis (HKICC 2014). 3. To delineate the molecular pathways of nMet in HCC Out study revealed that nMet activated NF-κB pathway. In the stable clones of nMet, expressions of phospho-p65 and phospho-IKKbeta were enhanced when compared with the vector control cells. In addition, we found that nMet upregulated TAK1 mRNA and protein level leading to the activation of NF-kB pathway. Taken together, our study identify TAK1/NF-kB pathway as the molecular basis underlying the functional activity of nMet (AACR 2015, APASL 2016).

783613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
783613.value: In the continual study of nMet, we are interested to investigate involvement of NF-kB downstream targets in the functional role of nMet. We will examine the expressions and activities of the putative downstream targets of NF-kB in the stable clones of nMet. Besides, we are also interested to study how nMet promotes distant metastasis to lungs. Our preliminary data showed that exosomes derived from nMet stable clones enhanced the migratory and invasive potentials of HCC cells as well as metastasis to lungs from liver primary tumor in mice injected with exosomes prior to orthotopic liver implantation. The role of exosomes in the modulation of tumor microenvironment in lung tissues will be explored.

783613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
783613.value: Our study focuses on the study of nuclear Met in liver cancer. Met receptor is found on the cell surface which functions as sensors to receive external signals on the cell surface and transmit the signal into the cells. Our study however has provided data to show that Met exists in the nucleus of liver cancer cells. Our results showed that nuclear Met has a higher expression level in liver cancer cells than the corresponding non-tumorous liver tissues. Higher nuclear Met expression is associated with a poorer survival rate than patients with lower nuclear Met expression. Our findings suggest that the expression of nMet may have prognostic value in liver cancer. In addition, our functional characterization studies showed that nuclear Met promotes liver cancer cell growth and motility in cell culture whereas enhances tumor formation and metastasis in animal model. We also addressed the mechanistic pathway underlying the promoting activity of nuclear Met. This information gained contributes to the understanding of the development of liver cancer.

783813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
783813.value: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease affecting more than 6,000 people in Hong Kong and more than 1 million people in Mainland China. Human leukocyte antigens (HLA) are among the first susceptibility genes found to be associated with SLE. Studies on both European populations and Han Chinese indicated that many HLA alleles and non-HLA genes in this region may be independently associated with the disease. However, due to the enormous diversity of HLA alleles, the long range linkage disequilibrium (LD) in this region, and difficulties of HLA typing, the exact HLA and non-HLA genes associated with SLE remain unclear. A huge population gap also exists: studies were conducted overwhelmingly on European populations, and ethnic differences have been suggested but never fully addressed. We have conducted GWAS on SLE on Han Chinese in Hong Kong and Anhui, China. We have access to a total of 8,511 patient DNA samples and 8,865 controls matched in geography and ethnicity. We will first genotype selected HLA genes on a number of samples already with genome-wide SNP genotype data. Making use of these samples, and other available genomic data, we will build a reference panel with HLA types and SNP markers in this region. We will then perform imputation on the 5 million SNPs and HLA genes and meta-analysis of the two Chinese GWAS, and identify potential independent association signals. We will then replicate these selected signals (both SNPs and HLA genes) in additional cohorts to seek high power. This study promises to identify HLA alleles as well as non-HLA genes in this region independently associated with the disease in Chinese populations, a long standing question perplexing researchers in the field of SLE genetics. For the first time for non-European populations, available GWAS data and large collection of patient samples have become available, and have made it possible for a detailed study of the HLA region. Comparison of results on Chinese and reported data on European populations (and with potential collaborations) will highlight ethnic differences. Stratification on disease subphenotypes will reveal association of HLA and non-HLA genes with specific disease manifestations, which could lead to better prediction of disease risks and prognosis, and personalized treatment. Furthermore, the rich data generated from this study are also valuable for preliminary prediction of common HLA types using SNP genotypes, which may set up the stage for public health applications in the future. 系統性紅斑狼瘡 (SLE) 是一種自身免疫性疾病，在中國大陸 影響超过100 萬人， 香港的患者超过 6000 人。人類 當中找到的與系統性紅斑狼瘡相關聯的第一個易感基因就是白細胞抗原 (HLA)基因。歐洲人和漢族的研究表明，很多 HLA 等位基因和在此區域中的非 HLA 基因可能與這種疾病有獨立關聯。然而，由於這一區域有長範圍的多樣化的連鎖不平衡 性（LD）和 確切的 HLA 检测的困難，與系統性紅斑狼瘡相關的HLA 等位基因和非 HLA 基因的细节至今仍不清楚。对这一区域的研究也存在龐大的人口差异： 已進行的研究多數以歐洲人口为对象，種族间的差異决定了欧洲人的研究不能完全解決亚洲人的遗传因素。 我們用GWAS 的方法上對居住在香港和安徽省的中國漢族人系統性紅斑狼瘡進行了研究。我們總共有 8,511 患者的 DNA 樣本和 8,865匹配的對照樣本。我們將對HLA區域進行詳盡分析，比對和運算，以推測與系統性紅斑狼瘡相關聯的HLA基因和非白細胞抗原基因， 然後在大樣本上進行驗證，以找到在中國人群中與系統性紅斑狼瘡相關聯的易感基因。 本研究是非歐洲人群中类似研究的第一例，已有的 GWAS 資料和收集的患者的大樣本为本研究提供了便利。将中國人群的結果和歐洲人口的結果进行比较， 將让我们更了解民族间差異。我们也将研究本基因组区域基因與特定疾病表現的关系，可能會找到更好的預測疾病風險和預後，以及個人化的治療的方法。此外，本研究产生的豐富的資料为将来使用單核苷酸多態性基因型来初步預測常見的 HLA 類型也是有價值的，因此，它对未来系統性紅斑狼瘡的治疗和HLA的群体检测都有重要价值。

783813.label: Realisation of objectives
783813.value: HLA imputation relies on the use of a reference panel where the association between the SNP genotypes or haplotypes composed of multiple SNPs and HLA alleles is known, and a model is built on capturing the relationship between the two, allowing imputation of HLA alleles when only SNP genotype data on this region is known. Recent work has shown the importance of having population specific reference panels for HLA allele imputation. Working together with our long term collaborator, Dr. Zhang Xunjun from Anhui Medical University in the mainland, we have gained access to around 20,000 Han Chinese samples with comprehensive HLA typing from capture of the MHC region and next generation sequencing (NGS), as well as dense SNP genotypes in the MHC region (Zhou et al, Nature Genetics, 2016 48(7):740). We have built a Han Chinese-specific HLA imputation panel using a different algorithm, HIBAG (Pharmacogenomics J. 2014 Apr;14(2):192-200). The imputation panel we have built has shown to be performing extremely well, much better than any of the available tools and the framework from the original publication (Zhou et al, Nature Genetics, 2016 48(7):740). HIBAG is a machine learning imputation framework that uses Ensembl classifier to impute HLA alleles from genotypes, which was used to build classifiers to impute HLA alleles to 4 digits accuracy for 8 HLA loci, including 3 loci in HLA class I and 5 loci in HLA class II (HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DQB1, HLA-DPB1, HLA-DQA1, HLA-DPA1). The machine learning approach of HIBAG makes it robust towards genotyping errors. We have shown that using the largest population-specific HLA dataset to date as a reference panel has led to increased accuracy in predicting HLA alleles for imputation and increased number of HLA alleles imputed. We also provide a web interface where the user can input their genotype data and impute HLA alleles using Han Chinese, Pan Asian or multiethnic reference panels. This work allows us to easily impute at high accuracy the HLA alleles of GWAS samples, and allows for subsequent precise HLA allele association analysis. The web interface is currently hosted at https://js91.shinyapps.io/refpanelwebsite/ and we are still improving the performance of the server and also preparing a manuscript on this piece of work. On a different note, we have tried to make better HLA allele calls from whole exome sequencing (WES) data, which becomes increasingly available and will potentially aid the study on HLA alleles associated with complex diseases including SLE. The work is published in Genome Medicine (Huang et al, Genome Med. 2015 Mar 16;7(1):25.). Calling SNPs in the MHC region itself is a challenge due to the extreme polymorphic nature of the HLA alleles in this region, including not only single nucleotide variants (SNVs) but indels and other structural variants, which increase the difficulties of accurate mapping and SNV calling. In this regard, we have developed and have experience in calling SNP genotypes and indels from NGS data on the MHC region. In fact, using our enhanced SNP-calling pipeline, we were able to increase the number of SNPs called by four fold. In summary, we have built this reference panel for imputing HLA alleles from SNP genotype data based on by far the largest sample on Han Chinese population and a superb algorithm. The webserver will further help the community to do studies on the MHC region. After imputation of HLA alleles using the afore mentioned reference panel and HIBAG, we have imputed the HLA alleles for the SLE samples and the controls from our genome-wide association study data, including 612 cases and 2193 controls. Association analysis on HLA alleles were carried out. In summary, there is little or no association in HLA-A,B,C, DPB1; there are multiple associations shown in HLA-DQA1, DQB1, DRB1. HLA-DRB1*03:01-HLA-DQB1*02:01 and HLA-DRB1*15:01 –HLA-DQB1*06:02 haplotypes have been reported as the most common HLA haplotypes in SLE in which patients with compound heterozygous for HLA-DRB1*03:01 and HLA-DRB15:01 are under the highest risk. In this dataset, we could replicate the risk allele of HLA-DRB1*15:01 but could not find association with HLA-DRB1*03:01 and HLA-DQB1*02:01, which is consistent with previous report of population differences in HLA association with SLE. Novel HLA allele association were found especially in HLA-DQA class with the single most significant HLA-allele at HLA-DQA1*01:02. Other novel HLA alleles associated with SLE include HLA-DRB1*05:02 and HLA-DQB1*06:01. We have used the remaining samples from our Hong Kong cohort, and a PCR and NGS technology for HLA typing to replicate the findings from the above imputation. We used a multiplexing barcoding system to try to pool up to 96 samples together for a sequencing run to save cost on the HLA typing. Some technical difficulties in this effort slowed down our progress somewhat. We have finished the HLA typing and the results are very promising. We are currently writing up the findings and preparing a manuscript summarizing the results. In summary, imputation of HLA alleles associated with SLE showed very interesting novel findings on the HLA alleles associated with SLE and most of them can be replicated in additional samples from the Hong Kong SLE cohort. This study improves our understanding of the HLA genes associated with SLE. There are significant population specificities on the HLA alleles associated with SLE susceptibility. This is highlighted by the lack of association of DRB1:0301 with the disease in Chinese populations, although it is a prominent susceptibility allele in populations of European ancestry. There are speculations that non-HLA genes in the MHC region that are also associated with the disease. For example, genes in the Class I region are thought to be associated with SLE in European ancestry. Comparing GWAS Manhattan plots between Chinese populations and the European populations clearly shows a twin peak in Europeans (Class I and Class II) comparing to a lone peak in Chinese (Class II). The idea is to capture and sequence this region in large number of samples and to elucidate the non-HLA genes associated with the disease independent of HLA alleles and their correlation with clinical subphenotypes. However, to do this on 2000 Hong Kong samples (1000 cases and 1000 controls) alone, a minimum sample needed to have reasonable power, will cost 1.2 million HKD, far surpassing the budget allowed for this project (400,000 HKD roughly for consumables). We will have to keep working on securing enough funding to complete this process, a project that holds much promise for the understanding of the genetic architecture of SLE and to correlate genetics with clinical manifestations.

783813.label: Major findings and research outcome
783813.value: We have built a comprehensive reference panel for imputing HLA alleles from SNP genotype data based on by far the largest sample on Han Chinese population and a superb algorithm. The webserver will further help the community to do studies on the MHC region in a wide range of areas. In addition, we have compiled the most updated HLA allele frequencies for Han Chinese populations based on large samples, which is going to be very useful for studies involving the MHC region, such as organ transplantation, genetic studies on complex diseases, cancer and adverse drug responses. Imputation of HLA alleles associated with SLE showed very interesting novel findings on the HLA alleles associated with SLE and most of them can be replicated in additional samples from the Hong Kong SLE cohort. This study improves our understanding of the HLA genes associated with SLE, shed new light on the genetic architecture of the disease.

783813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
783813.value: There are both HLA alleles and non-HLA genes in the MHC region associated with SLE and there are prominent population differences in disease susceptibility in this region. However, due to the complicated nature of linkage disequilibrium of this region, it is hard to distinguish signals from HLA and non-HLA genes. Eventually, sequencing of this region on large number of samples is necessary to solve the puzzle. This is an area that is very promising, although requiring a larger budget and technically challenging.

783813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
783813.value: In many scenarios HLA alleles are not directly examined but the SNPs nearby are genotyped. There are certain correlations between the SNP genotypes and HLA alleles. Elucidating the relationships will help us impute the HLA alleles from SNP genotypes. In this study, based on large dataset on Han Chinese samples with both HLA allele information and SNP genotype, we have built a reference panel and a webserver to allow people to accurately impute HLA alleles from SNP genotypes for their studies. Making use this panel ourselves, we have performed imputation of HLA alleles in our cohort on SLE studies including SNP genotype data on SLE cases and controls. This allows us to detect the HLA alleles associated with SLE and to further understand the genetic architecture of this prototype autoimmune disorder.

783913.value: 背景 如今，許多成年人為了把牙齒排齊而求治于矯齒醫生，因為他們想擁有整齊的牙齒和迷人的笑容以提高他們的生活品質。但很多成年患者受牙周病的困擾。因此，矯齒醫生需要接診越來越多受牙周炎症影響的成年患者。包括炎症在內的牙齒問題（例如牙周炎）會引起嚴重的牙齦疾病，甚至破壞牙支援組織和骨組織。 核心問題和假說 矯齒治療依賴於矯治器的機械力作用，通過骨組織的改建以重新排列牙齒。機械力作用於牙周組織（圍繞及支援牙齒的組織）中的細胞，啟動細胞的信號傳導，進而細胞分化、聚集，並生成導致骨吸收和骨形成的破骨細胞和成骨細胞。矯治器施加的機械力能啟動促使細胞間資訊傳導的口腔生物信號。然而，牙周炎症會引起病理性骨吸收----這是影響牙齒移動的潛在性問題。在炎症得到控制後，那些曾經受過炎症影響的細胞其信號傳導是否與未受過炎症影響的細胞一致？當炎症未受控制時會發生哪種類型的細胞信號傳導？這些問題的答案仍然未知。如果我們能夠進一步了解這些細胞信號傳導的核心原理，將能對其加以干預（加強或阻斷），從而對合併牙周炎的成人患者提供更好的矯齒治療。最近的研究發現Eph-ephrin通路（與細胞信號傳導耦合）是牙周細胞和骨細胞之間新的雙向傳導通路。因此我們推測以往受過的炎症刺激和/或正經受的炎症刺激通過Eph-ephrin通路對牙周細胞造成影響，介導炎症環境中機械力作用下的骨改建。 研究目的和計劃 我們將運用體外實驗檢測上述假說，在三種情況下（無炎症刺激，曾受過炎症刺激，正經受炎症刺激），分別對不同類型的牙周細胞（牙周膜幹細胞、牙周膜細胞和成骨細胞）施加張力和壓力。我們將研究兩種主要Eph-ephrin通路（ephrinB2- EphB4和ephrinA2- EphA2）在不同類型及不同狀態下的牙周細胞中如果介導細胞分化以及骨形成和骨吸收。 研究意義 本研究的結果將會對曾受過及正經受炎症刺激下的特定力作用機制有更好的理解。基於ephrin- Eph功能的干預將為發展全新治療方案提供可能，從而預防病理性骨吸收及加強骨形成，為牙周炎病人提供更好的矯齒治療。

783913.value: Objective 1. To investigate the effects of inflammation (previous and on-going) on cell communication between periodontal cells through ephrin-Eph signalling in the following respects: (1) effects on the differentiation of PDL stem cells/PDL cells mediated by cell communication through ephrin-Eph signalling. The objective has been 100% achieved with an in vitro study. The human periodontal cells were cultured and challenged by P. gingivalis lipopolysaccharides (LPS) at different concentrations (from 0.001 to 10 µg/ml) for 6-48 h. The western blot was used to assess the protein expression of ephrinA2-EphA2 and ephrinB2-EphB4 signaling, while the Quantitative real time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) was performed to evaluate the mRNA expression of the differentiation markers such as alkaline phosphatase (ALP), osteocalcin (OCN) and Runt-related transcription factor 2 (Runx2). Output: Effects of Lipopolysaccharide on Ephrin/Eph Signaling in Periodontal Ligament Fibroblasts. The 28th Annual Scientific Meeting of IADR SEA, 9/2014/Malaysia. (Conference abstract) Objective 2: To investigate the effects of inflammation (previous and on-going) on cell communication between periodontal cells through ephrin-Eph signalling in the following respects: (2) effects on osteogenesis mediated by cell communication through ephrin-Eph signalling. The objective has been 100% achieved with an in vitro study. Human periodontal cells were divided into 4 groups: a. mechanical force application alone; b. LPS stimulation for the first 24 h which followed by concurrent LPS and mechanical force for 4 h (ongoing inflammation); c. LPS stimulation for the first 24 h which followed by mechanical force with no LPS for 4 h (previous inflammation); d. control group received no intervention. The western blot was used to assess the protein expression of ephrinA2-EphA2 and ephrinB2-EphB4 signaling, while the qRT-PCR was performed to evaluate the mRNA expression of osteogenesis related markers such as receptor activator of nuclear factor kappa-Β ligand (RANKL), Osteoprotegerin (OPG), ALP, and Runx2. Alizarin Red S staining was performed to analysed the mineralization of periodontal ligament cells. Outputs: 1) Influence of Lipopolysaccharide on Ephrin/Eph Expression in Human Periodontal Ligament Fibroblasts. The 91st Congress of the European Orthodontic Society, 6/2015/Italy. (Conference abstract) 2) Porphyromonas gingivalis lipopolysaccharide regulates ephrin/Eph signalling in human periodontal ligament fibroblasts. J Periodontal Res. 2017;52:913-921. (Peer-reviewed journal publication) Objective 3: To investigate the effects of inflammation (previous and on-going) on cell communication between periodontal cells through ephrin-Eph signalling in the following respects: (3) effects on osteoclastogenesis mediated by cell communication through ephrin-Eph signalling under mechanical loading. The objective has been 100% achieved with an in vitro study. Recombinant ephrinB2-Fc chimeras were used to activate forward signaling via EphB4, while siRNA-mediated transfection was used to knock down the expression of ephrinA2 in periodontal cells. Subsequently, ongoing LPS and mechanical force application was exerted to the cells. The qRT-PCR was carried out to assess the mRNA expression of bone remodelling markers. The siRNA-ephrinA2-treated periodontal cells with the above concurrent stimulation were co-cultured with RAW264.7 cell line, and the osteoclastic differentiation was measured by tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase (TRAP) staining. 783913.label: Major findings and research outcome
783913.value: 1. Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation to periodontal cells was able to increase the expression of RANKL/OPG ratio and decrease the expression of Runx2 and OCN, which suggests the enhanced osteoclastic activities and suppressed osteogenic activities in LPS-stimulated cells. Meanwhile, the EphB4 signaling was downregulated, while the ephrinA2 signaling was upregulated. (Objectives 1 & 2) 2. Mechanical force-loaded periodontal cells treated with ongoing inflammation showed decreased EphB4-ephrinB2 signaling and increased ephrinA2 signaling. However, previous inflammation treatment could partially reverse these modulations. Furthermore, ongoing inflammation led to more profound osteoclastic differentiation than previous inflammation did. These findings imply that the periodontal cells previously exposed to LPS can partly regain an ordinary condition when the inflammatory challenge has been controlled. (Objective 3) 3. Both positive regulation of EphB4 signaling and negative regulation of ephrinA2 signaling were able to recover the ongoing inflammation-induced enhancement of osteoclastogenesis, which demonstrates that inflammation controlling regulate periodontal cell communication through Eph-ephrin signaling. (Objective 3) 4. Osteoblastic differentiation of periodontal cells was affected by LPS stimulation and mechanical force through the expression of ALP and Runx2, and was regulated by Eph-ephrin signaling. (Objectives 1 & 2)

783913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
783913.value: 1. Illuminating the underlying mechanism in the present study shed light on the understanding of inflammation controlling and the clinically therapeutic strategies or pharmacological interventions to facilitate orthodontic tooth movement in patients with periodontitis. 2. In vivo animal model could be adopted to evaluate the temporal-spatial distribution of Eph-ephrin signaling in periodontium tissue during inflammation controlling, especially their relationship between alveolar bone and periodontal ligament. 3. In-depth studies may be needed to elucidate the upstream pathways and potential mechanisms that affect the LPS-mediated Eph-ephrin signaling.

783913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
783913.value: An increasing number of adults visit orthodontists to straighten misaligned teeth as they want a well-aligned bite and attractive smile. Orthodontists thus need to treat teeth affected by periodontal inflammation in many adults. Periodontitis, a dental problem involving gum inflammation, can cause tooth-supporting tissues' breakdown and pathological bone resorption. Therefore, orthodontic treatment should only be performed after periodontal therapy to bring the active inflammation in the controlled status. The present study was performed to apply mechanical force to the periodontal cells and to investigate the cellular activities before and after inflammation controlling through Eph-ephrin signaling. Findings from the results show that when being subjected to mechanical loading, the periodontal cells exposed to ongoing inflammatory stimuli display higher level of bone-resorbing activities compared to normal cells with no inflammation. However, cells previously exposed to inflammation show partial recovery of these modulations, which suggest that inflammation controlling can affect cellular communication via Eph-ephrin signaling. Understanding the cellular mechanism involved in inflammation controlling contributes to the development of novel therapeutic strategies for tooth repositioning in patients with periodontitis. Relative interventions may be applied to prevent pathological bone resorption and to enhance bone formation.

784213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
784213.value: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) rupture is one of the commonest injuries in sports medicine. Despite the prevalence of ACL reconstruction surgery, method in achieving prompt and reproducible healing of soft tissue tendon graft is still a significant issue to address. The healing of the graft within the bone tunnel (graft osteointegration) and the remodeling of the intra-articular portion of the graft to an ACL-like structure (graft ligamentization) are the two main areas of concern. The healing of soft tissue graft within the bone tunnel occurs by Sharpey fiber formation at around 12 weeks after the operation. This is followed by “ligamentization” of the intra-articular portion of the graft, which lasts for six to twelve months in animal researches and up to two to three years in human studies. The graft is significantly weaker than the native ACL during this healing process. Graft fails in mechanical testing by pulling out from the bone tunnel in early post-operative period and mid-substance rupture during the “ligamentization” phase. This leads to the need of prolonged protection and avoidance of pivoting sport for six to nine months after surgery. We have developed a novel strontium enriched calcium phosphate cement (Sr-CPC) by incorporating 5% strontium into the CPC system. Our in vitro data suggested that this 5% Sr-CPC was superior to traditional CPC in terms of cell adhesion study, cell proliferation study and alkaline phosphatase expression of the treated osteoblasts. The hypothesis that the local release of strontium could lead to an accelerated osteointegration of soft tissue tendon graft within the bone tunnel was confirmed in our previous rabbit ACL reconstruction study. The histiomorphometric data suggested that the healing in the Sr-CPC treated graft was accelerated by three to six weeks when compared with the untreated control group. Complete remodeling of the allograft-bone junction into native ACL ligament-bone insertion with tendon-fibrocartilage-bone transition was found at 24 weeks post-operation in the Sr-CPC group. As the initial healing of soft tissue tendon graft within the bone tunnel is accelerated by the local application of Strontium, we further postulate that this will lead to an equal acceleration of the subsequent “ligamentization” of the graft. This hypothesis will be tested in a rabbit bilateral ACL reconstruction model comparing Sr-CPC treated graft in one limb with the untreated graft in another limb. Histological and biomechanical experiments of the intra-articular portion of the graft during this “ligamentization” process will be conducted. 前交叉韌帶斷裂是運動醫學中最常見的病患。儘管前交叉韌帶重建是一種非常普遍的手術，但是肌腱的癒合仍然是一個重要的課題。移植物何時在骨隧道內癒合和移植物怎樣重新韌帶化是前交叉韌帶研究的兩個主要領域。 軟組織移植物在骨隧道內的癒合大約在手術後12週發生，主要是因為Sharpey纖維形成。移植物的韌帶化則在術後的六到十二個月發生。 在癒合過程中，移植物明顯較為脆弱，因此患者需要在手術後6至9個月避免進行劇烈運動。 我們開發了一種新型的含鍶磷酸鈣生化骨水泥（ SR - CPC ）。我們將5 ％的鍶加入系統中。我們的體外研究數據顯示，這5％的Sr- CPC在細胞粘附的研究，細胞增殖研究和成骨細胞鹼性磷酸酶表達方面的研究都明顯比傳統的磷酸鈣生化骨水泥優勝。我們在白兔進行前交叉韌帶重建的研究，證實局部釋放鍶是可以加速肌腱在骨隧道內的癒合。前交叉韌帶移植物經含鍶磷酸鈣生化骨水泥處理後，骨隧道內癒合的速度比未經處理的前交叉韌帶移植物，快三到六週。 因為以上的觀察，我們假設移植物的韌帶化也將相應加快。為了驗證這個假設，我們會在白兔進行前交叉韌帶重建的研究。

784313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
784313.value: Influenza virus may transmit by contact, droplet, or aerosols via infectious particles of different sizes. Ferrets have been adopted as a surrogate model for humans to assess the pandemic potential of zoonotic influenza viruses emerged from animal reservoirs. Specifically, human influenza viruses transmit efficiently from an infected ferret to a naïve recipient housed separately in adjacent cages, allowing transfer of droplet and aerosols (respiratory droplet route); in contrast, viruses that cause sporadic zoonotic infection in humans can only transmit to co-housed ferrets (direct contact route). Termed “respiratory droplet transmission”, the exact transmission route among ferrets is not fully elucidated as transmission can be conferred through droplets or aerosols that differ by particle size and the ability to remain suspended in the air. There is also limited information on the specific cut-off particle size that allows movement from the infected ferret to the naïve ferret and confers to the respirator droplet transmission. Applying a vertical transmission tunnel with adjustable flow velocity, we propose a novel experimental design that would allow us to control the movement of infectious particles by size from an infected donor to a naïve recipient ferret. This experimental setting will be applied to study the transmissibility of A(H1N1)pdm09 and its genetically related swine influenza viruses that we have demonstrated previously to possess different respiratory droplet transmissibility in ferrets. We and others have previously identified that the molecular determinants of the A(H1N1)pdm09 virus that confer to efficient respiratory droplet transmissibility in ferrets reside in the segments 4, 5, and 7, via a mechanism associated with increased infectious particle release. We hypothesized that a unique gene constellation may affect viral droplet and aerosol transmissibility in ferrets by (i) affect the quantity and the size of infectious particles released into the aerosol from the ferret respiratory tract, (ii) affect the stability of the virus in the aerosol, or both. The proposed study will help to understand if viral and environmental factors would facilitate influenza transmission via large and small infectious particles in the ferret model. The information would provide a better understanding regarding the application of the ferret model to study influenza transmission. 流感病毒的傳播途徑主要有接觸傳播，飛沫傳播，和空氣傳播。雪貂是評估動物源性流感病毒是否具有在人群間爆發大流行潛力的最佳動物模型。人類季節性流感病毒可以在雪貂之間輕易的通過直接接觸將病毒傳染給共同飼養在同一籠具中的易感雪貂，還可以通過空氣傳播感染飼養在臨近籠具的易感雪貂。然而，動物源性流感病毒在雪貂間往往只能通過直接接觸傳播而缺乏通過空氣傳播的能力。飛沫傳播和空氣傳播的區別是根據飛沫粒徑的大小，粒徑大的飛沫和粒徑小的飛沫核在空氣中停留時間有很大的差異，而兩種途徑在流感病毒於人群間傳播的重要性中還未完全闡明。目前對於如何定義雪貂模型中觀察到的空氣傳播(感染飼養在臨近籠具的易感雪貂) 的粒徑閾值也還不明確。本研究將控制不同粒徑的飛沫從感染雪貂到達易感雪貂，從而分別研究不同粒徑的飛沫及飛沫核在流感傳播中的重要性。在2009年引起大流行的A(H1N1)pdm09流感病毒源自於豬流感病毒的基因重組。我們之前的實驗中發現A(H1N1)pdm09流感病毒以及基因上有關聯的豬流感病毒在雪貂模型中表現出不同的空氣傳播能力。我們和其他研究人員都發現，導致A(H1N1)pdm09能夠高效率傳播的主要由於基因片段4，5和7上的決定因素使得感染個體釋放出更多的感染性病毒。我們認為特異的流感病毒基因組合可能影響被感染的雪貂呼吸道中釋放出的飛沫數量和粒徑大小，或者影響病毒在飛沫及飛沫核中的穩定性，甚至兩個方式同時作用，來決定流感的空氣傳播方式。本研究將有助我們瞭解病毒和環境因素如何影響流感病毒的傳播。而且，這些資訊將會使得我們知道如何更好的利用雪貂模型來研究流感傳播途徑。

784313.label: Realisation of objectives
784313.value: Influenza can potentially be transmitted from person to person by three modes: contact transmission, in which infectious secretions are transferred directly or indirectly via fomites; droplet transmission, in which respiratory fluid-containing particles larger than 5 µm travel ballistically through the air and deposit onto mucous membranes within 3 meters due to gravity; and airborne transmission, in which vaporized particles (droplet nuclei) smaller than 5 µm that remain suspended in air over longer distances and time spans are inhaled and deposited in the respiratory tract. While influenza is transmitted via these non-mutually exclusive modes, the relative importance of each is unclear. This project aimed to study viral and environmental factors that affect transmission of A(H1N1)pdm09 influenza via large and small infectious particles in ferrets. Ferrets are naturally susceptible to influenza infection and support influenza transmission via “direct contact” (co-housed donors and recipients) or by “respiratory droplets” (donors and recipients housed in cages separated by varying distances. However, these conventional experimental settings cannot clarify the relative transmission efficiency of airborne particles of different size that mediate droplet and airborne transmission. To address this knowledge gap, we developed a novel exposure chamber capable of separating influenza virus-laden particles into specific size ranges by the application of impactors. Our system captures particles larger than the desired cut-off size via inertial impaction while allowing smaller particles to remain in the air stream. We first evaluated the transmission efficiency of A(H1N1)pdm09 (A/California/04/09; CA04) that has been shown to transmit efficiently among ferrets via “direct contact” and “respiratory droplets” under conventional experimental settings. Ferret-to-ferret transmission of the CA04 virus was efficiently mediated by particles that passed through the 9.3 μm, 5.3 μm, and 2.5 μm impactors with viral shedding detected in 4/6 (5/6 seroconverted), 4/6, and 3/6 recipient ferrets, respectively. Interestingly, no ferret-to-ferret transmission of the CA04 virus (0/6) was observed with the 1.0 μm impactor, which permitted particles < 1.5 μm (d95) to pass from the donor chamber to the recipient chamber during exposure. For comparison, an H1N2 Triple Reassortant swine influenza virus (A/Sw/Kansas/00246/04; KS246) capable to transmit to co-housed ferrets by “direct contact” (2/2) but with delayed transmission via “respiratory droplets” to naïve ferrets housed in adjacent cages (1/2) was studied; no ferret-to-ferret transmission was observed by particles that passed through the 9.9 μm or 5.3 μm impactors. The replication kinetics of CA04 and KS246 viruses in ferret nasal washes was evaluated; the swine influenza virus KS246 showed a slight delay in the replication kinetics with lower titers detected in nasal washes on 2 and 4 days post-inoculation (dpi). We further determined the size and quantity of influenza virus-laden particles in air released by donors during exposure using the NIOSH bioaerosol sampler that collects particles into three size ranges (> 4 µm, 1-4 µm, and < 1 µm) followed by quantitative real-time RT-PCR to detect influenza viral RNA segment 7. Higher quantities of virus-laden particles at particle sizes > 4 µm were detected in air sampled from the donor chambers from ferrets inoculated with CA04 or Rg-WH359 than those inoculated with KS246 virus, suggesting that efficient ferret-to-ferret transmissions via the airborne route is directly associated with the quantity of virus-laden particles in air released by the donor ferrets during the exposure period. Environmental condition may affect the viability of influenza viruses within aerosols. The viability of aerosolized CA04 and KS246 viruses was evaluated at 30%, 50%, and 80% relative humidity (RH) levels using of the aerosol management platform (AeroMP; Biaera Technologies). The temperature was maintained at 25-26°C during the experiments. Aerosols were generated by nebulizing viruses in culture media (diluted to 106 plaque forming units/ mL) using a one-jet Collison nebulizer (BGI, Inc) running at 2.5 LPM and delivered into a 40L chamber. NIOSH bioaerosol sampler was applied to sample viruses at 30%, 50%, and 80% RH followed by plaque assay to determine viability. In all three size fractions (> 4 µm, 1-4 µm, and < 1 µm), the highest viability for both CA04 and KS246 influenza viruses was detected at the 80% RH, followed by the 30% RH, and the lowest at 50% RH. The HA, NA and M gene segments have been reported to confer increased transmission potential for the A(H1N1)pdm09 virus. We further investigated viral factors that differentiated the airborne transmission potential between the Triple Reassortant-swine influenza virus (KS246) and the A(H1N1)pdm09 virus (CA04). Four recombinant viruses, Rg-CA04, Rg-KS246, and reassortant viruses Rg-CA04PB2,PB1,PA,NP,NS x KS246HA,NA,M and Rg-KS246 PB2,PB1,PA,NP,NS x CA04HA,NA,M, generated by plasmid-based reverse genetics replicated to comparable titers in differentiated human airway epithelium cells after 48 hours. Scanning or transmission electron microscopes, the recombinant viruses formed predominantly short and few long filamentous (> 1µm) virions without significant differences in the virion length (P = 0.076, One-way ANOVA). Airborne transmissibility was assessed by exposing naïve ferrets to donors on 1 dpi using the 5.3 μm impactor. The Rg-CA04 and Rg-KS246 viruses showed comparable transmission potential as the parental CA04 and KS246 viruses and were transmitted to 4/4 and 0/4 recipient ferrets, respectively. Introducing the HA, NA and M gene segments of the CA04 virus into swine influenza KS246 increased the airborne transmission potential, the Rg-KS246 PB2,PB1,PA,NP,NS x CA04HA,NA,M virus being transmitted to 4/4 recipients. Replacing the HA, NA and M gene segments of CA04 with that of the KS246 virus reduced the transmissibility of the Rg-CA04PB2,PB1,PA,NP,NS x KS246HA,NA,M virus to 3/4 (4/4 seroconverted) but did not completely abolish airborne transmission, suggesting that the five remaining gene segments of CA04 contain determinants that facilitate airborne transmission. Although all four recombinant viruses replicated to comparable titers in the donor nasal washes, more virus-laden particles, predominantly at particle size > 4 μm, were detected in air sampled from the donor chambers during the exposure of Rg-CA04, Rg-KS246 PB2,PB1,PA,NP,NS x CA04HA,NA,M, and Rg-CA04PB2,PB1,PA,NP,NS x KS246HA,NA,M viruses (P = 0.148, Kruskal-Wallis test). These data suggest that the A(H1N1)pdm09 virus possesses multiple viral factors that contribute to its increased airborne transmissibility in ferrets by increasing the release of virus-laden particles in air. Collectively, our results demonstrated that airborne transmission of CA04 among ferrets was mediated via virus-laden particles ≥ 1.5 μm in air released from donor ferrets during the exposure period. Viral viability was better maintained at 80% or 30% RH but was the lowest under 50% RH. Multiple viral determinants facilitated airborne transmission potential by affecting the quantity and size of virus-laden particles released from infected ferrets. The results provided direct experimental evidence to support droplet transmission and airborne transmission among ferrets, albeit at different efficiencies. Overall, we have fully addressed aim 1 “Generate recombinant A(H1N1)pdm09 virus with different HA/NA/M constellation and evaluate the effect of large and small infectious particles on viral transmission in ferrets”. As for aim 2 “Assess the stability (infectivity) of the recombinant viruses under different relative humidity and temperature after being aerosolized into small and large particles sizes”, we have studied the effect of RH on viral viability. However, the effect of temperature was not fully addressed due to the limitation of the aerosol management platform, which only allowed monitoring and recording temperature changes during the experiments. Future experiments can be performed inside a temperature-controlled room to test the effect of temperature on viral viability.

784313.label: Major findings and research outcome
784313.value: The novel development of the transmission chamber that allows separation of virus-laden particles by size to delineate the sizes of particles mediating airborne transmission of influenza viruses is one of the major achievements of this project. Applying the transmission chamber, we demonstrated that airborne transmission of the A(H1N1)pdm09 virus among ferrets was mediated via virus-laden particles ≥ 1.5 μm in air released from donor ferrets during the exposure period. Multiple viral gene segments were found to contribute to the increased airborne transmission potential of the A(H1N1)pdm09 virus. This is the first study delineating the sizes of particles that mediate airborne transmission for influenza virus. The results provide direct experimental evidence to support the role of droplet and droplet nuclei in mediating influenza transmission among ferrets. While the results obtained from ferrets cannot be extrapolated to infer modes of transmission among humans, our design can be further modified for human challenge studies. High and low RH were observed to support better viral viability in aerosols than at 50% RH; this can be further investigated to improve the environmental infection control measures in health care settings or in public locations. A PhD student was trained under this project from March 2013 to February 2017. A manuscript describing the results of this study has been summarized and will be submitted for peer review pending on the pre-submission inquiry result. Most valuably, this project provided a chance for investigators from different disciplines to build collaboration that has extended into additional projects and funding opportunities.

784313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
784313.value: A novel exposure chamber was designed and validated in the current study to delineate the sizes of particles mediating airborne transmission of influenza viruses. This experimental setting can be applied to other pathogens, or with modification, for studies with human volunteers. Applying the experimental approach to evaluate the relative significance between different modes of transmission of influenza will enable the development of evidence-based infection control measures. Through the experiments, we observed that airborne transmissibility depends on the quantity and size of virus-laden particles released by the influenza-infected ferrets, while multiple viral factors were found to increase the release of virus-laden particles in air after infection. It is possible that the release of virus-laden particles in air is regulated by specific virus-host interactions. Identifying the specific host factors or signaling pathways involved in the regulation of virus-laden particles release from an infected host may provide targets for pharmaceutical intervention to prevent the spread of influenza during epidemics or pandemics.

784313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
784313.value: Influenza is transmitted by multiple non-mutually exclusive modes. The relative transmission efficiency of droplets or droplet nuclei of different particle sizes has not been defined experimentally. We developed a novel exposure chamber that separates virus-laden particles by size and determined the particle sizes mediating the airborne transmission of influenza viruses among ferrets. Ferret-to-ferret transmission via the airborne route was mediated by particles larger than 1.5 μm, consistent with the quantity and size of virus-laden particles released by the donors. Multiple virus gene-segments enhanced the airborne transmissibility of a swine-origin H1N2 influenza virus among ferrets by increasing the release of virus-laden particles into the air. High (80%) and low (30%) relative humidity levels were observed to support increased viral viability in aerosols than that at 50% relative humidity. This is the first study delineating the sizes of particles that mediate airborne transmission for influenza virus. The results provide direct experimental evidence to support the role of droplet and droplet nuclei in mediating influenza transmission among ferrets. Adopting a similar experimental setting in humans to directly assess the transmissibility of virus-laden particles by size would provide evidence-based guidance for developing interventions to reduce transmission of influenza viruses during epidemics and pandemics.

784413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
784413.value: Cervical cancer is the second commonest cause of cancer death in women worldwide. Human papillomarvirus (HPV) is the most important etiologic agent in the development of the disease as it occurs in 99% of the cervical cancer tissue. However, HPV alone is insufficient for development of the disease. This is shown by the large difference in the life-time risk of HPV infection (~75%) and the risk of cervical cancer (0.7%). The identity of the additional factor(s) required for the development of the disease is not known. Cervical cancer is associated with aberrant expression of some small ribonucleic acid molecules known as microRNAs, which do not produce proteins but inhibit the production of proteins from messenger ribonucleic acids. One of the aberrantly expressed microRNAs in cervical cancer is miR-135a. We found that increase in miR-135a activated an important intracellular signaling pathway known as Wnt/β-catenin, and transformed normal cervical cells into tumor, in line with a previous report showing transformation of HPV-infected epithelial cells into cancer cells by activation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway. E2F1 is a transcription factor produced by a region of chromosome that is frequently gain in cervical cancer. Our data also showed that E2F1 enhanced the expression of miR-135a in cervical cancer. Consistently, we detected high expression E2F1, miR-135a and β-catenin in cervical cancer tissues. Recently, a minor cell population in cancer known as cancer stem cells has been hypothesized to initiate tumorigenesis. While there are debates on the origin of these cells, Wnt/β-catenin signaling has been implicated in their formation. Solid evidence on presence of cancer stem cells in cervical cancer is lacking. Interestingly, we found that miR-135a could induce transformation of HPV-infected normal cervical cells into cells with cancer stem cell-like properties. This project aims to extend the above preliminary observations and study the relationship between miR-135a and transformation of cervical cancer. The hypothesis of the project is miR-135a contributes to the transformation of HPV-infected cervical epithelial cells to cancer and cells with cancer stem cell-like properties. Eradication of cancer stem cells during treatment is believed to be important in avoiding recurrence of tumor. The project will provide valuable information on the formation of cervical cancer. The results would be useful in the development of new therapeutic strategy for cervical cancer targeting on cancer stem cells, and in the development of sensitive assays for their detection for prognosis and diagnosis of the disease. 子宮頸癌是全球女性第二位最常見的癌症死亡原因。人乳頭狀瘤病毒病毒（HPV）是最重要的病原體，因為它的DNA能在99％宮頸癌組織偵察到。然而， HPV感染風險（〜75％）和患子宮頸癌風險（0.7％）的巨大差異顯示單獨HPV感染是不足以發展為癌症。我們不知什麼額外的因素才能發展成為宮頸癌。 宮頸癌與一些細小的RNA名為微RNA的不正常表達相關，這些RNA不製造蛋白質，但抑制蛋白質的生產。miR-135A是在宮頸癌中異常表達的微RNA之一。我們發現，增加miR-135a 的表達能啟動細胞內的一個被稱為Wnt /β-catenin的重要信號轉導通路，並把正常宮頸細胞轉化成癌細胞。這觀察與以前的報告顯示，激活的Wnt/β-catenin能轉化HPV感染上皮細胞為癌細胞一致。E2F1基因是一種轉錄因子，它存在的染色體區域，經常在宮頸癌組織中發生增加。我們的數據還表明，E2F1增強miR-135A在宮頸癌細胞的表達。我們還發現E2F1，miR-135a 和β-catenin在宮頸癌組織中都有高的表達。 近年來，在腫瘤組織發現一個稀有的細胞群體，稱為癌症幹細胞。研究人員推測癌症幹細胞引發腫瘤。雖然這些細胞的起源仍有爭論，數據顯視WNT /β-catenin的信號與它們的形成有關。癌幹細胞是否存在宮頸癌仍缺乏確鑿的證據。有趣的是，我們發現，有少部分miR-135a轉化的癌細胞擁有癌幹細胞的特性。 這項目旨在繼續上述的初步觀察和研究miR-135a和轉化宮頸癌之間的關係。這項目的假想是miR-135A轉化HPV感染的宮頸上皮細胞為癌症與癌幹細胞。 消除腫瘤幹細胞被認為是避免腫瘤復發的重要治療。這項目將提供宮頸癌形成的有價值的信息。其結果將可用在針對宮頸癌癌幹細胞的新治療策略的發展，並有助發展對宮頸癌的敏感檢測，預後和診斷。

784413.label: Realisation of objectives
784413.value: The project aims to study the actions of microRNA-135a (miR-135a) on transformation of a normal cervical epithelial cell line (NC104 E6/E7) without any tumorigenic activities into cancer cells and cells with cancer stem cell-like (CSC-like) properties. We have fully addressed and achieved all the objectives as stated in the proposal. a. To define the molecular events involved in miR-135a-induced transformation of NC104 E6/E7 cells to cancer: MiR-135a was transfected into NC104 E6/E7 cells. The tumorigenecity of the cells was examined by in vitro assays (migration, invasion and anchorage-independent growth in soft agar) and in vivo tumorigenicity models using immune-deficient mice. The molecular targets of miR-135a were identified by in silico approach and validated by in vitro experimentations. In addition, Laser capture microdissection was used to determine the expression levels of molecules potentially involved in the transformation such as miR-135a, β-catenin, and seven in absentia homolog 1 (SIAH1) in cervical biopsies from normal women and those with cervical cancer at different stages of the disease. b. To monitor the process of miR-135a-induced transformation into cancer cells: MiR-135a was transfected serially into NC104 E6/E7 cells and the tumorigenecity of the cells were examined every time after miR-135a induction. The gene expression profiles of the miR-135a-indced cells were examined by microarray analysis. The differentially expressed genes and differentially activated biological pathways were identified. Some of the differentially expressed genes were further confirmed by quantitative polymerase chain reactions (qPCR). c. To determine the role of human Papillomavirus (HPV) on the effects of miR-135a-induced transformation, the tumorigenic activities of miR-135a in E6/E7 positive/negative cell lines and in NC104-E6/E7 with or without E6/E7 knockdown were determined. d. To characterize the role of Wnt/β-catenin signaling in tumor transformation of cervical epithelial cells with force-expression of miR-135a: CD133+ cells from cervical cancer cell lines and miR-135a-transformed cancer cells were found to exhibit CSC-like properties by anchorage-independent growth in soft agar, tumorsphere formation in non-adherent culture at low seeding density, and in vivo tumorigenic assay at low seeding density. Difficulty was encountered in the in vivo tumorigenic assay at low seeding density; no tumor was formed when only the CD133+ cells were inoculated. The difficulty was solved by inclusion of mouse fibroblasts (3T3) in the inoculation; primary tumor could be formed with 300 CD133+ cells, while the secondary tumor with 100 cells. To confirm that the CD133+ cells but not the supporting 3T3 mouse fibroblast cells were responsible for the growth of tumor, a GFP expressing NC104 E6/E7-135a cell-line for the in vivo tumor formation assay. e. The association of Wnt/β-catenin signaling and CSC-like properties was examined in cervical cancer cells, normal cervical cells and oviductal cells. The effect of activation and inhibition of Wnt/β-catenin signaling on the CSC-like properties of CD133+ and CD133- cells isolated from the miR-135a transformed cells were assessed as above. In addition, we examined whether prolonged activation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling is essential for maintenance of the CSC-like properties of the transformed cells. f. To study the CSC-like subpopulations in miR-135a transformed cancer cells and cervical cancer tissues: The CD133+ and the CD133- cell subpopulations were isolated in the miR-135a-transformed cells. The tumorigenecity of the two cell subpopulations were compared by in vivo and in vitro assays as above. The expression of active β-catenin, Oct4 and some chemoresistance genes were compared between the two subpopulations. The differentiation ability of the CD133+ and the CD133- cells were examined by serum challenges. We also examined the CD133+ subpopulation in biopsies from patients with cervical cancer, their tumorigenecity, miR-135a and β-catenin expression levels and compared the results with their CD133- negative counterpart. g. To study the mechanism regulating the expression of miR-135a: The association of Wnt/β-catenin signaling and expression of miR-135a in cervical cancer cells were established. The CpG methylation pattern at the promoter region of CD133 in CD133+ and CD133- expressing cells were examined.

784413.label: Major findings and research outcome
784413.value: a. MiR-135a induced formation of cervical cancer cells through suppression of SIAH1, leading to up-regulation of β-catenin/T cell factor signaling. Force-expression of SIAH1 partially nullified the effect of miR-135a in cervical cancer carcinogenesis. In cervical specimens, miR-135a was significantly overexpressed in malignant cells when compared with precancerous lesions. b. The tumorigenecity of the cells increased with increasing number of miR-135a induction. Cells receiving 1 time of induction behaved similar to the mock induced cells, while cells receiving 3 to 5 times of induction exhibited cancer properties in both in vitro and in vivo assays. The tumors formed in vivo after 5 times of induction were larger than those formed after 3 times of induction. c. The HPV E6/E7 proteins are prerequisite for miR-135a as an oncomiR. d. Microarray analyses showed that miR-135a induced activation of pathways related to carcinogenesis such as the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway, Toll-like receptor signaling pathway and ECM-receptor interaction pathways. The expression of some of the differentially expressed genes related to tumor formation such as, CXCL14, ITGB6, FGF2 and IL-8 were validated by qPCR. e. MiR-135a induced formation of CD133+ cells with CSC-like properties: Compared with the CD133- cells, the CD133+ cells possessed significantly higher self-renewal ability. They formed tumorspheres in low attachment plate, and their secondary tumorspheres grew larger and faster. The cells had higher expression of Oct4, β-catenin and chemoresistance-associated genes, ABCB1 and ABCG2. Inoculation of 500 CD133+ cells was sufficient to induce tumor formation in the presence of mouse fibroblasts in immunodeficient mice. The CD133+ cells also possessed limited differentiation ability into keratinocytes upon serum challenge. f. The CD133+ cells were identified in archived cervical cancer biopsies but not in precancerous tissues by immunostaining. The CD133+ cells isolated from fresh cancer biopsies exhibited higher tumorigenicity than the corresponding CD133- subpopulation. g. Treatment with Wnt/β-catenin inhibitor (XAV939) significantly suppressed expression of CD133 and also reduced the CSC-like properties of the treated cells in terms of self-renewal ability and expression of drug resistance genes. h. The extent of DNA methylation of the CpGs of CD133 promoter was compared between the CD133+ and the CD133- cells. The overall methylation pattern of the two populations were similar. However, there was a significant difference in the methylation pattern of the β-catenin response element (TCF/LEF) binding site; more than 60% of the CpGs were methylated in the CD133- cells while only 20% were methylated in the CD133+ cells.

784413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
784413.value: The main finding of the project is the association of miR-135a and cervical cancer carcinogenesis. Importantly, miR-135a induced the transformation of normal cells to cancer cells with CSC-like properties, which may initiate and sustain tumor growth. Thus, miR-135a can be a potential therapeutic target for cervical cancer. Another potential therapeutic target derived from the project is the Wnt/β-catenin signaling, which is required for maintenance of CSC-like properties of the miR-135a transformed cells. A few compounds have been developed to modulate the Wnt pathway, some of them have FDA approval while others are being or will be tested for treatment purposes. Future experiments should test the possible impact of these compounds on the miR-135a-transformed cells and cervical cancers. Microvesicles containing miRNAs are released into body fluids. It is known that early detection of cancer improves patient survival and prognosis. Whether miR-135a in microvesicles can be detected in the female reproductive tract and use as a cervical cancer marker is unknown. We are comparing the levels of miR-135a in the conditioned media from normal and cancer cervical cell lines. The investigation will provide preliminary data for the detection of miR-135a in body fluid as for non-invasive monitoring of cervical cancer carcinogenesis.

784413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
784413.value: Cervical cancerous tissues were found to have a higher expression of a small RNA called microRNA-135a (miR-135a) when compared with pre-cancerous tissues. Treatment of normal cervical cells with miR-135a transformed normal cervical cells into cancer cells. The transformation was more efficient in human papillomavirus (HPV) infected cervical cells. Treatment of the cells with miR-135a triggered activation of a number of other intracellular signaling pathways known to be involved in carcinogenesis, including one known as Wnt/β-catenin pathway. A minor cell population in cancer known as cancer stem cells (CSCs) is known to initiate tumor formation, relapse and chemoresistance. We found that miR-135a not only transformed cervical cells to cancer cells but also to cells with CSC-like properties. These latter cells expressed a cell surface protein CD133, chemoresistance genes, high level of Wnt/β-catenin and formed tumor in mice when only 500 of them were injected into the animals. Activities of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway was essential for maintaining the CSC-like properties of the miR-135a transformed cells. The CD133 expressing cells in cervical cancer tissues also expressed high level of miR-135a. The information obtained provide insights to cervical carcinogenesis and may be used to develop new therapeutic strategies for cervical cancer.

785013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
785013.value: 風濕性關節炎是香港最常見的風濕性疾病之一，其發病率約為總人群的1%-5%。重要的是，風濕性關節炎病人因為心血管疾病的原因，所以有高發病率和死亡率。其中一個原因就是過早發生的動脈粥樣硬化。實際上，一些研究已經表明，與正常人相比，多層螺旋CT檢發現這些病人存在高度的血管鈣化。儘管如此，對於這方面的潛在機制是未知的。而且，目前并沒有能夠有效預防風濕性關節炎病人動脈粥樣硬化的治療方法。 動脈僵硬度，一種測量動脈順應性的方法，可以通過肱動脈和脛後動脈之間的動脈速度來估算。動脈僵硬度已被證實與普通人群的血管鈣化和心血管疾病死亡率有關。風濕性關節炎病人的動脈僵硬度和血管鈣化在以前的研究中并沒有被估算出來。我們假設主動脈鈣化將有助於風濕性關節炎病人的動脈僵硬度變化。 基质γ-羧基谷氨酸蛋白(MGP)是血管鈣化的一個強抑製劑。在普通人群中進行的前期研究表明低MGP水平與血管鈣化密切相關。另外，與MGP緊密相關的成骨內皮祖細胞(EPCs)也已被證實有助於血管鈣化的發展。然而, MGP和成骨EPCs在風濕性關節炎病人血管鈣化中的作用機制還不清楚。因此，我們提出來去調查MGP和成骨EPCs和風濕性關節炎病人血管和瓣膜鈣化的關係。 MGP的激活需要羧化作用，是一種依賴於維生素K的過程。先前的研究已經顯示服用維生素K拮抗劑的病人將增加血管和瓣膜鈣化的發生。重要的是，最近的隨機法研究顯示維生素K的補充可以減少人群中血管鈣化的進程。動脈粥樣硬化的重要性導致了風濕性關節炎病人死亡率的增加，測量表明它可以阻止發展進程是臨床上相關的。迄今為止，沒有一種治療方法已被證實可以有效的預防這些病人的血管鈣化。我們計劃維生素K的補充給藥法可能會使風濕性關節炎病人的血管和瓣膜鈣化進程變慢。

785113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
785113.value: 頸動脈壁面剪切率及血流渦度之檢測一直被視為有臨床價值，能促進頸動脈粥樣硬化的早期診斷。醫護人員尤其希望在臨床無創情況下測量這些參數。 有見及此，本項目將致力研發一個新型醫學影像模式來檢測頸動脈壁面剪切率及血流渦度，特別是其在心動週期不同階段之動態轉變。此模式將會基於超聲平面波發收的高幀率成像技術，能以亞毫秒時間分辨率進行採樣及流矢量估計。這些功能將能有效實現動脈壁面剪切率及血流渦度的運算及時空分析。 本項目將進行三方面的研究工作。首先，我們會設計基於高幀率超聲成像技術的脈壁面剪切率及血流渦度的算法，並利用電腦模擬方式驗證其準確性。接著，我們會進行頸動脈仿體實驗來進一步確認此影像模式對脈壁面剪切率及血流渦度之時空分析的效用。之後，我們將進行前期體內試驗來研究此影像模式對動脈粥樣硬化早期診斷之可行性。

785113.label: Realisation of objectives
785113.value: Our team has successfully developed various engineering solutions that are critical to realize the development of high-frame-rate ultrasound as a new tool for wall shear rate and vorticity dynamics monitoring. In particular: (a) Objective #1 has been met by completing Objectives #2, #3, and #4, as described in the next three points. (b) Objective #2 has been achieved with the design of a robust vector flow estimation algorithm. Such an estimator exhibits high accuracy and low estimation variance that are critical to derive wall shear rate and vorticity values without error. This robust flow vector estimation algorithm is based on the measurement of Doppler shifts from more than two angles. Least-squares fitting is then applied to derive vector estimates (Journal publication #1, attached in the subsequent sections). The key merit of this algorithm is that it can produce flow vector estimates with minimum mean-squared error at every pixel of the imaging view, thereby enhancing the overall flow vector estimation consistency over the entire image frame. Our team has demonstrated that this vector computation method, when used in conjunction with data regularization schemes which remove spurious Doppler estimates from the vector estimation process, can play a key role in achieving lucid visualization in complex flow scenarios (Journal publication #1). Furthermore, real-time adaptive clutter filter solutions have also been developed using GPU-based parallel processing to ensure that the Doppler signal used for flow estimation is free from tissue clutter biases (Journal publication #6). (c) Objective #3 has been achieved with the development of two novel flow phantom design frameworks and related experiments. First, we have developed a new phantom design protocol to develop anatomically realistic carotid bifurcation phantoms (Journal publication #2). This new protocol has enabled us to develop a library of carotid phantom models with different carotid vessel geometries including stenotic narrowing features that resemble atherosclerosis. The second phantom design protocol which our team has developed is a wall-less intracranial aneurysm model (Journal publication #5). The reason for working on this additional flow model design framework is to develop patient-specific models to truly reconstruct in-vivo flow conditions for experimentation of new algorithms. (d) Objective #4 has been achieved by completing human scans and developing patient-specific models based on the acquired human data sets to perform correlative analysis with computational fluid dynamics. In particular we have studied the hemodynamics in intracranial aneurysms (Journal publication #4) where flow dynamics is known to be complex. We have also attempted to pursue a preliminary study on urodynamics and related impact on the vorticity dynamics of urinary flow (Journal publication #7). These results vividly demonstrate the technical feasibility of using high-frame-rate ultrasound to investigate hemodynamic parameters such as wall shear rate and vorticity. Related research outcomes are described later in this report. IMPORTANT NOTE: The grant is originally awarded to Dr. Alfred C. H. Yu in 2013. As he had left the University of Hong Kong in 2016 to take up an academic post at the University of Waterloo, Canada, Professor K. W. Chow acted as a 'care-taker' of this grant in the last few months of the project.
