785113.label: Major findings and research outcome
785113.value: Our team has published seven journal articles and has made several conference presentations based on research achievements supported by this grant. Here is a summary of our research output: (1) Journal publication #1: Presented our vector flow visualization technique for high frame rate flow imaging (Objective #2). A preliminary study on carotid bifurcation phantoms was also conducted (Objective #3). We received a Young Scientist Award for this work at the 2013 Symposium on Ultrasonic Electronics. (2) Journal publication #2: Presented our new framework for designing anatomically realistic flow phantoms based on multi-part lost-core casting principles (Objective #3). (3) Journal publication #3: Reported a new robust vector flow estimator for high-frame-rate ultrasound imaging using least-squares fitting principles (Objective #2). This method is crucial to wall shear rate and vorticity estimation. (4) Journal publication #4: Described a joint experimental and computational study on intracranial aneurysms derived from in-vivo data (Objective #4). (5) Journal publication #5: Proposed a new wall-less intracranial aneurysm phantom design model for ultrasound flow imaging experimentation (Objective #3). (6) Journal publication #6: Proposed a new eigen-processing clutter filter method to derive high-quality ultrasound images which were not affected by tissue clutter bias (Objective #2). The technique was realized in real-time using the GPU. (7) Journal publication #7: Reported the first study on using high-frame-rate ultrasound to study vorticity dynamics in the urinary tract (Objective #4). This new domain serves to attest the broad applicability of methods developed by our team to various application arenas.

785113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
785113.value: With the technical achievements realized in this project, the logical next step would be to push forward our solutions toward clinical practice. For this effort, there will be a need to develop a live wall shear rate and vorticity imaging platform that can allow bedside use of our solutions, and conducting in-vivo pilot studies in vascular patients with various disease conditions. We anticipate that the scope of such work would be a suitable topic for Health and Medical Research Fund grant applications. There is also an opportunity to translate our technical achievements to the ultrasound industry. Such industrial translation effort would fall within the scope of the Innovative and Technology Support Program funding schemes.

785113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
785113.value: Since stroke remains a leading cause of death in the industrialized world, it is undoubtedly necessary to devise effective strategies to foster stroke prevention. This project has addressed the critical engineering issues in applying high-frame-rate ultrasound to the monitoring of wall shear rate and vorticity dynamics in carotid arteries, aneurysms, and urinary tract. We have demonstrated the possibility of using ultrasound to track these complex hemodynamic quantities at very high frame rates of >1,000 fps. This achievement is made possible by a number of novel engineering contributions which we achieved in this project, including robust signal processing frameworks for flow vector estimation and anatomically realistic flow phantom design. These technical innovations will ultimately enable clinicians to make more informed diagnostic decisions on stroke prevention. Risk mitigation mechanisms can be developed. Consequently, both patients and front line clinical personnel will be the principal beneficiaries.

785213.label: Project Objectives

rows: To further determine the function of TPC2 signaling in autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion.
To dissect the molecular mechanisms underlying TPC2-induced autophagy arrest.

785213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
785213.value: Autophagy, an evolutionarily conserved lysosomal degradation pathway, has been implicated in a wide variety of cellular processes, yet the underlying mechanisms remains poorly understood. The two pore channel 2 (TPC2) is a new member of the superfamily of voltage-gated Na+/Ca2+ channels located on lysosomes. Accumulating evidence indicates that nicotinic acid adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NAADP), one of the most potent Ca2+ mobilizing nucleotides, elicits Ca2+ release from lysosomes via TPC2 in many cell types. Herein, we explore the role and mechanism of TPC2 signaling in regulation of autophagy in mammalian cells. We found that overexpression of the wildtype TPC2, but not the inactive mutant, in Hela cells that lack the expression of endogenous TPC2 induced a marked accumulation of autophagosomes. Treatment of TPC2 overexpressing cells with NAADP-AM, a cell-permeant NAADP agonist, further induced the accumulation, whereas Ned-19, a NAADP antagonist, reversed it. Interestingly, autophagy is gradually induced during in vitro neural differentiation of mouse embryonic stem (ES) cells initiated by a monolayer culture and is accompanied by a dramatic downregulation of endogenous TPC2. Consistently, TPC2 overexpression in mouse ES cells induced the accumulation of autophagosomes during early neural differentiation, whereas TPC2 knockdown not only decreased the accumulation of autophagosomes but also promoted the formation of autolysosomes. Taken together, our data indicate that the activation of the TPC2 signaling antagonizes the progression of autophagy by inducing the accumulation of autophagosomes. We speculate that TPC2 signaling actually inhibits the fusion of autophagosomes with lysosomes, thereby arresting autophagy. In the current proposal, we propose to (1) further determine the function of TPC2 signaling in autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion, and (2) dissect the molecular mechanisms underlying TPC2-induced autophagy arrest. Given that autophagy plays important roles in a wide variety of cellular processes and dysfunctional autophagy has been associated with many human diseases, the elucidation of the mechanism and role of TPC2 signaling in autophagy regulation will be fundamentally important for identification of novel targets for pharmaceutical intervention in treatment of autophagy-related human disorders. 自噬溶酶体降解途径在进化上保守，且在多种细胞过程有作用，但其基本的机制仍然知之甚少。两个孔道2 （ TPC2 ）是一个位于溶酶体的电压Na + / Ca2 +通道超家族的一个新成员。越来越多的证据表明，烟酸酰胺腺嘌呤二核苷酸磷酸（ NAADP ） ，一个最有力的Ca2 +动员核苷酸，通过TPC2诱导Ca2 + 从许多类型的细胞的溶酶体中释放。在这里，我们探索TPC2信号在哺乳动物细胞中调控自噬的作用和机制。我们发现，高表达野生型TPC2 在Hela细胞中诱导自噬体显着积累。可穿透细胞的NAADP激动剂NAADP-AM能进一步诱发自噬体的积累，而NED- 19 ， 一种NAADP拮抗剂，逆转自噬体的积累。有趣的是，自噬作用在小鼠胚胎干细胞（ES细胞）体外神经分化过程中被诱导，并伴随着一个内源性TPC2的下调。TPC2在小鼠胚胎干细胞中过度表达也诱导自噬体在早期神经分化过程中积累，而TPC2敲除不仅减少了积累的自噬体，但也促进形成autolysosomes 。总而言之，我们的数据表明， TPC2信号阻止了自噬进展从而诱导自噬体的积累。我们推测 TPC2信号抑制自噬体与溶酶体的融合，从而阻止细胞自噬。在此项目中，我们建议：（1）进一步确定TPC2信号在自噬体和溶酶体融合中的功能，及（2）解析TPC2阻止自噬诱导的分子机制。由于自噬在多种细胞过程中起着重要作用，自噬功能障碍与许多人类疾病有关，因此阐明 TPC2信号在自噬调控中的机制和作用将对找到治疗与自噬相关的人类疾病新的目标是非常重要的。

785213.label: Realisation of objectives
785213.value: Objective 1. To determine the function of TPC2 signaling in autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion. Autophagy is an evolutionarily conserved lysosomal degradation process, and is involved in various cellular processes. Although the research on the molecular machinery in controlling autophagy progression has made great progress in recent years, the detailed mechanisms underlying autophagy, especially the fusion between autophagosome and lysosome, still remain elusive. TPC2 is a non-selective Na+/Ca2+ channel and is mainly located in lysosomes, and in this project we first assessed whether TPC2 is involved in autophagy progression in two cancer cell lines, 4T1 mouse breast cancer cell and HeLa human cervical cancer cells. We established several TPC2 knockdown or overexpressing 4T1 or HeLa cells. We found that TPC2 overexpression in 4T1 cells or HeLa cells blocked the fusion between autophagosome and lysosomes, manifested by the accumulation of autophagosomes and increased levels of both LC3-II and p62. On the other hand, TPC2 knockdown in 4T1 cells facilitated the autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion, manifested by the increased numbers of autolysosomes and the decreased LC3-II levels. Therefore, these data demonstrate that TPC2 inhibits the autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion. We speculated that the accumulated autophagosomes in TPC2 overexpressing cells might turn to be secreted out of cells. However, we found that TPC2 overexpression in 4T1 or HeLa cells markedly inhibited the secretion of exosomes of different size ranges, whereas exosome secretion was significantly increased in TPC2 knockdown 4T1 cells. Interestingly, we also found that exosome uptake in TPC2 overexpressing HeLa cells was significantly decreased as compared to that in control HeLa cells. Since both exosome secretion and autophagy have been implicated in tumor cell migration, we assessed the role of TPC2 in the migration of cancer cells. We found that the migration of TPC2 knockdown 4T1 cells was significantly inhibited as compared to that of control 4T1 cells, whereas the migration of TPC2 overexpressing cells only exhibited marginal differences as compared to that of control 4T1 cells or HeLa cells. We also found that TPC2 knockdown cells proliferated slower than control or TPC2 overexpressing cells, suggesting that the slow growth rate in TPC2 knockdown cells might lead to fewer cells in the migration assay. Taken together, these data indicate that TPC2 not only mediates autophagy but also is involved in exosome secretion and uptake (Sun and Yue, manuscript submitted). Besides TPC2, we also studied the role of TRPM2, a non-selective Ca2+ permeable cation channel previously reported to be located in both plasma membrane and lysosome, in autophagy regulation. We found that TRPM2 is mainly located in plasma membrane, not lysosome. We then demonstrated that oxidative stress triggered TRPM2-dependent Ca2+ influx to inhibit the induction of early autophagy, which rendered cells more susceptible to death. On the other hand, oxidative stress induced autophagy in the absence of the TRPM2-mediated Ca2+ influx. Moreover, in response to oxidative stress, TRPM2-mediated Ca2+ influx activated CaMKII at levels of both phosphorylation and oxidation, and the activated CaMKII subsequently phosphorylated Beclin1 on Ser295. Ser295 phosphorylation of Beclin1 in turn decreased the association between Beclin1 and Vps34, but induced binding between Beclin1 and Bcl2. Clinically, acetaminophen (APAP) overdose is the most common cause of acute liver failure worldwide. We demonstrated that APAP overdose also activated the ROS-TRPM2-CaMKII-Beclin1 signaling to suppress autophagy, thereby causing primary hepatocytes more vulnerable to death. Inhibiting the TRPM2-Ca2+-CaMKII cascade significantly mitigated APAP induced liver injury. In summary, our data clearly demonstrate that oxidative stress activates the TRPM2-Ca2+- CaMKII cascade to phosphorylate Beclin1 resulting in autophagy inhibition (Wang et al. Autophagy 2016). In addition, we found that oxidative stress activated the TRPM2-CaMKII cascade to further induce intracellular ROS production, which led to mitochondria fragmentation and loss of mitochondria membrane potential, indicating that oxidative stress activates the TRPM2-Ca2+-CaMKII-ROS signal loop to inhibit autophagy and induce cell death (Wang et al., Biochim Biophys Acta-Mol. Cell Res, 2017). Thus, we have successfully completed the objective 1. Objective 2. To dissect the mechanisms underlying TPC2-induced autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion. To date, many factors and proteins, e.g. lysosomal pH, Rab7, SNAREs, the HOPS complex, and LAMP1/2, have been implicated in regulating autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion. Yet, the underlying molecular mechanism remains poorly understood. We found that TPC2 overexpression in HeLa cells prevented both the localization of RAB7 to autophagosomes and the localization of STX17, a SNARE member, to autolysosomes. Moreover, we found that TPC2 overexpression in both HeLa cells and 4T1 cells increased lysosomal pH, accompanied with the nuclear trans-localization of TFEB. Lysosomal re-acidification abolished TPC2-induced autophagosome accumulation. These data demonstrate that TPC2 alkalizes lysosomal pH to suppress the late stage of autophagy progression. We propose that the release of Ca2+ and H+ from lysosomes via TPC2, or after Ca2+ release from lysosomes via TPC2, Ca2+ refilling via a putative Ca2+/H+ counter-exchanger, or a P-type Ca2+ pump, or the sequential coupling of several cation counter-exchangers, e.g., Ca2+/Na+ and Na+/H+, could lead to lysosomal alkalization. The lysosomal alkalization, in turn, prevents the relocation of RAB7 or STX17 to autophagosomes or autolysosomes, respectively, to block the fusion between autophagosome and lysosome (Sun and Yue, manuscript submitted). During the course of studying TPC2-mediated autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion, prompted by the fact that many available autophagy inhibitors targeting this fusion process lack either potency or specificity, we set up a fluorescence image-based assay to screen small molecules affecting this late stage of autophagy. We first selected a panel of small chemicals that are commercially available and have been previously shown to affect vesicle trafficking or organelle morphology, and screened their effects on autophagy regulation in tfLC3 expressing HeLa cells. We found that the small chemical vacuolin-1 potently and reversibly inhibited the fusion between autophagosomes and lysosomes in mammalian cells, thereby inducing the accumulation of autophagosomes. Interestingly, vacuolin-1 was less toxic but at least 10 folds more potent in inhibiting autophagy compared to chloroquine. Vacuolin-1 treatment also blocked the fusion between endosomes and lysosomes, resulting in a defect in general endosomal-lysosomal degradation. Treatment of cells with vacuolin-1 alkalinized lysosomal pH and decreased lysosomal Ca2+ content. Besides non-specifically and marginally inhibiting vacuolar ATPase activity, vacuolin-1 treatment markedly activated Rab5 GTPase activity. Expression of a dominant negative mutant of Rab5A or Rab5A knockdown significantly inhibited vacuolin-1 induced autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion blockage, whereas expression of a constitutive active form of Rab5A suppressed the lysosomal-autophagosomal fusion. These data suggest that vacuolin-1 activates Rab5 to block autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion. Vacuolin-1 and its analogues present a novel class of drug that can potently and reversibly modulate autophagy (Lu et al., Autophagy, 2014). In addition, we performed the virtual drug screening and identified 14 vacuolin-1 analogues as autophagy inhibitors. Based on these virtual screening results, we further designed and synthesized 17 vacuolin-1 analogues, and found that 13 of them are autophagy inhibitors and a couple of them are as potent as vacuolin-1. In summary, these studies expanded the pool of useful autophagy inhibitors and reveal the structural-activity relationship of vacuolin-1 analogues, which is useful for future development of vacuolin-1 analogues with high potency and for identification of the molecular targets of vacuolin-1 (Chen et al., Molecules 2017). In summary, we have successfully completed the objective 2 as well.

TPC2 overexpression in 4T1 cells or HeLa cells blocked the fusion between autophagosome and lysosome, manifested by the accumulation of autophagosomes and increased levels of LC3-II and p62. 3. Migration of TPC2 knockdown 4T1 cells was significantly inhibited. 10. Proliferation of TPC2 knockdown 4T1 cells was significantly inhibited. The above findings were presented in a manuscript entitled “TPC2 mediates autophagy progression and exosome secretion in cancer cells”, which has been submitted for publication. 11. 785213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
785213.value: We speculate that NAADP elicits Ca2+ release from lysosome via TPC2 to trigger proton exit from lysosomes, thereby increasing lysosomal pH and inhibiting autophagy. Therefore, we purified the TPC2 complex from HeLa cells that stably express TPC2-Flag-His6 by tandem affinity purification, and identified 10 potential TPC2 binding proteins by MS analyses. However, by individually knocking down these 10 genes, we found that none of them were involved in TPC2-mediated autophagy arrest and NAADP-induced Ca2+ release. Alternatively, we have recently constructed two mammalian expression vectors encoding TPC2 fused to N- or C-terminal of an engineered ascorbate peroxidase (APEX), and established two APEX-tagged TPC2 expressing HeLa cell lines. APEX will biotinylate proteins which are the near-neighbors of the fusion protein in a proximity-dependent manner in living cells, and the biotinylated proteins can then be purified by streptavidin-coated magnetic beads and be identified by MS with high fidelity. In the near future, we will apply this approach to spatiotemporally identify TPC2 interacting proteins in living cells treated with or without NAADP or its antagonists. We aim to establish a complete TPC2 interaction network and determine the roles of its binding protein(s) in NAADP-mediated Ca2+ release, lysosomal pH changes, and autophagy regulation. Interestingly, we found that TFEB is translocated to the nucleus in TPC2 overexpressing cells although mTOR in these cells is still active. We speculate that TFEB might not only act as the transcriptional factor but also be involved in the fusion between autophagosome and lysosome. Therefore, TFEB nuclear localization in TPC2 overexpressing cells might contribute to the fusion blockage between autophagosome and lysosome. We are currently studying the role of TFEB nuclear translocation in autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion, and how TPC2 signaling induces TFEB nuclear translocation.

785213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
785213.value: Autophagy, a conserved lysosomal degradation pathway, is involved in variety of cellular processes. TPC2 is a Na+/Ca2+ channels located on lysosomes. NAADP, a potent Ca2+ mobilizing nucleotide, elicits Ca2+ release from lysosomes via TPC2. In this project, we explored the role and mechanism of TPC2 in autophagy regulation. We found that TPC2 overexpression in 4T1 mouse breast cancer cell line or in HeLa human cervical cancer cell line inhibited the fusion between autophagosome and lysosome, resulting in the accumulation of autophagosomes accompanied with increased lysosomal pH and TFEB nuclear localization. On the other hand, TPC2 knockdown in 4T1 cells resulted in the increases of autolysosomes. Interestingly, we found that exosome secretion was markedly induced in TPC2 knockdown cells but inhibited in TPC2 overexpressing cells. However, migration of TPC2 knockdown, not TPC2 overexpressing, cells was inhibited. Taken together, these results support a role of TPC2 in autophagy progression and vesicle trafficking in cancer cells. Since dysfunctional autophagy has been associated with many human diseases, the elucidation of the mechanism and role of TPC2 signaling in autophagy regulation is fundamentally important for identification of novel targets for pharmaceutical intervention in treatment of autophagy-related human disorders.

785313.label: Realisation of objectives
785313.value: Objective 1: Determine the role of RbAp46/48LIN-53 in CENP-A/HCP-3 centromere assembly hierarchy in holocentric C. elegans 1. Determine the functional relationship between RbAp46/48/LIN-53 and M18BP1/KNL-2 in CENP-A/HCP-3 localization As mentioned in the midterm report, based on RNA interference and localization dependency experiments by live imaging and immunofluorescence, we found that CENP-A/HCP-3 centromeric localization is dependent on RbAp46/48LIN-53. In turn, the nuclear and centromeric localization of RbAp46/48/LIN-53 is dependent on CENP-A/HCP-3 and M18BP1/KNL-2, whereas M18BP1/KNL-2 localization is unaffected by RbAp46/48/LIN-53. Thus, we concluded that M18BP1/KNL-2 is upstream of RbAp46/48/LIN-53, and that RbAp46/48/LIN-53 and CENP-A/HCP-3 are interdependent of each other in the centromeric chromatin assembly process. 2. Determine if RbAp46/48/LIN-53 affects the mRNA and protein expression level and stability of CENP-A/HCP-3 and other canonical histones As mentioned in the midterm report, after RbAp46/48LIN-53 depletion, CENP-A/HCP-3 and H4 protein level dropped, but CENP-A/HCP-3 and H4 mRNA level remained unchanged. Our results suggest that RbAp46/48/LIN-53 recruits and stabilizes CENP-A/HCP-3-H4 nucleosomes to holocentromeres. On the other hand, H3 and H2B protein levels were reduced to a lesser degree, suggesting the effect of RbAp46/48/LIN-53 on CENP-A/HCP-3/ and H4 nucleosomes is specific, even though RbAp46/48/LIN-53 is also a H3-H4 chaperone. 3. Determine the chromosome missegregation frequency in RbAp46/48/LIN-53 depletion When RbAp46/48LIN-53was depleted, the metaphase plate could still be observed, yet 72% of one-cell embryos contain anaphase bridges and 41% undergo chromosome missegregation. Considering other cell stages in embryos, 24% of cells are aneuploid in at least one of the chromosomes. Objective 2: Elucidate the role of RbAp46/48LIN-53 in centromeric chromatin remodeling and mitotic chromosome structure 1. Determine if RbAp46/48LIN-53 affects histone acetylation and H3K27 methylation patterns by immunofluorescence To determine whether RbAp46/48/LIN-53 RNAi affects centromeric or global histone acetylation, we performed immunofluorescence on metaphase chromosomes. In wild-type, the poleward-facing holocentromeric region was not hypoacetylated, consistent with the lack of negative correlation between CENP-A/HCP-3 and H3/H4 acetylation from chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by DNA microarray (ChIP-chip) analysis in C. elegans (Liu et al., 2011, Gassmann et al., 2012). Global H3K9 and H4 acetylation (H3K9ac and H4K5/8/12/16ac) levels after RbAp46/48/LIN-53 RNAi were comparable to wild-type by immunofluorescence and western blot. These results suggest that RbAp46/48/LIN-53 does not regulate CENP-A/HCP-3 centromeric localization via histone acetylation in C. elegans. One of the RbAp46/48/LIN-53-containing complexes, polycomb repressor complex 2 (PRC2), has a role in generating the transcriptional repression mark, trimethylated H3 at K27 (H3K27me3), for gene silencing (Bender et al., 2004). This mark positively correlated (correlation index = 0.64) with CENP-A/HCP-3 based on ChIP-chip analysis in C. elegans (Gassmann et al., 2012), but whether a causal relationship exists between H3K27me3 and CENP-AHCP-3 localization is unknown. However, when we analyzed the H3K27me3 pattern on wild-type metaphase chromosomes by immunofluorescence, we did not observe an enrichment of this modification at centromeres at this resolution. Depletion of CENP-A/HCP-3did not affect the level of chromosomal H3K27me3, but RbAp46/48/LIN-53 depletion reduced H3K27me3 level on metaphase chromosomes to 11% compared to wild-type. To test whether RbAp46/48LIN-53 depletion affects CENP-A/HCP-3 localization through modulating H3K27me3 level, we depleted histone methyltransferase EZH2/MES-2 in PRC2 complex, which reduced chromosomal H3K27me3 level to 17% of wild-type. However, EZH2/MES-2 depletion did not significantly reduce centromeric GFP::CENP-A/HCP-3 level. This suggests that RbAp46/48/LIN-53 does not recruit CENP-A/HCP-3 to the centromere through PRC2 complex. We also systematically depleted the core enzymatic component or the largest subunit of the other six RbAp46/48/LIN-53-containing complexes. None of these perturbations led to a decrease in centromeric GFP::CENP-AHCP-3 level. These results suggest that RbAp46/48LIN-53’s role in centromeric CENP-AHCP-3 deposition may be independent of its roles as part of these known chromatin-modifying complexes. 2. Determine if RbAp46/48LIN-53 affects chromosome condensation in mitosis As mentioned in the midterm report, chromosomes afterRbAp46/48/LIN-53 depletion displayed a condensation kinetics pattern that is comparable to that after mock treatment. Also, the metaphase plate width in RbAp46/48LIN-53 depletion was similar to that in mock treatment. These results suggested chromosome condensation was not impaired in RbAp46/48LIN-53 depletion. Objective 3: Determine the dynamics of CENP-A/HCP-3 assembly over the cell cycles and the requirements for new CENP-A/HCP-3 loading 1. Validate that CENP-A/HCP-3 on chromatin is newly assembled during every cell cycle in C. elegans embryos: Following up on the mid-term report, both N- or C-terminal Dendra::CENP-A/HCP-3 transgenic strains do not give green fluorescence signal before photoconversion. After photoconversion trial, there is also no red fluorescence signal. However, we confirmed that most (93.7%) of CENP-A/HCP-3 on chromatin is turned over in the next cell cycle based on GFP::CENP-A/HCP-3, consistent with our previous finding in Gassmann et al., 2012. 2. Elucidate the requirements for new CENP-AHCP-3 loading during the cell cycle in C. elegans: To test if spindle checkpoint activation affects CENP-A/HCP-3 turnover, we depleted ZYG-1, which is required for centriole duplication and results in monopolar spindle in the second mitosis. In ZYG-1 depleted embryos, as in WT, the CENP-A/HCP-3 turned over completely (98.2%) within the anaphase of the first division and the metaphase of the second mitosis (during which the spindle checkpoint is activated). However, the variable cell shapes in the third mitosis prevent us from analyzing the turnover in the next cell division. This result suggests that spindle checkpoint is not required for HCP-3 turnover, or alternatively, HCP-3 was exchanged between the time when we photobleached (anaphase) and checkpoint activation (next metaphase). We permeabilized the embryos by PERM-1 RNAi, and treated GFP::CENP-A/HCP-3 embryos with latrunculin A, nocodazole and clasto-lactacystin-beta-lactone separately. Latrunculin A inhibits actin polymerization, hence it prevents furrow ingression when added before the event. Nocodazole inhibits microtubules polymerization, hence it blocks cytokinesis when added after anaphase onset. As Latrunculin A-treated and nocodazole-treated embryos simply arrested before the next metaphase or occasionally have their two daughter nuclei fused back, it is not feasible to measure the ratio between the bleached sister versus the unbleached sister in the next cell cycle. Clasto-lactacystin-beta-lactone is a specific 26S proteasome inhibitor that can prevent metaphase to anaphase progression when added before nuclear envelope breakdown (NEBD). Clasto-lactacystin-beta-lactone treated embryos are expected to arrest in metaphases of the second mitosis. Most (71.2%) CENP-A/HCP-3 on the chromatin is turned over in the next cell cycle, which is not significantly different from the (perm-1 RNAi) control embryos (75.5%). In summary, we have found that perturbed centrosome duplication or reduced proteasome activity in mitosis do not affect HCP-3 turnover from our photobleaching experiment.

DOI:http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2016.01.065 (as in Part C 8) • 2016 Impact factor: 8.282; 5-Year Impact Factor: 8.728; • SJR 8.588; SJR ranking 101/29715= top 0.33%; 32/1848 = top 1.73% (Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology); • Number of citations: 2; • Precise role of contribution: Corresponding author; the other 2 authors are my PhD students • The paper has been awarded 2016 Second Research Output Prize, Strategic Research Theme of Development and Reproduction, University of Hong Kong, HK$20,000 (as in Part C 11) Summary: Centromeres, the specialized chromosomal regions for recruiting kinetochores and directing chromosome segregation, are epigenetically marked by a centromeric histone H3 variant, CENP-A. To maintain centromere identity through cell cycles, CENP-A diluted during DNA replication is replenished. The licensing factor M18BP1/KNL-2 is known to recruit CENP-A to holocentromeres. Here, we show that RbAp46/48/LIN-53, a conserved histone chaperone, is required for CENP-A/HCP-3 localization in holocentric Caenorhabditis elegans. Indeed, RbAp46/48/LIN-53 and CENP-A/HCP-3 localizations are interdependent. RbAp46/48/LIN-53 localizes to the centromere during metaphase in a CENP-A/HCP-3- and M18BP1/KNL-2-dependent manner, suggesting CENP-A/HCP-3 loading may occur before anaphase. RbAp46/48/LIN-53 does not function at the centromere through histone acetylation, H3K27 trimethylation, or its known chromatin-modifying complexes. RbAp46/48/LIN-53 may function independently to escort CENP-A/HCP-3 for holocentromere assembly but is dispensable for other kinetochore protein recruitment. Nonetheless, depletion of RbAp46/48/LIN-53 leads to anaphase bridges and chromosome missegregation. This study unravels the holocentromere assembly hierarchy and its conservation with monocentromeres.

785313.value: In Brief: Histone H3 variant CENP-A epigenetically marks all functional centromeres, but how it is assembled on holocentromeres is unknown. We show that the histone chaperone RbAp46/48/LIN-53 is required for CENP-A/HCP-3 localization and accurate chromosome segregation in holocentric C. elegans. RbAp46/48/LIN-53 may function to escort CENP-A/HCP-3 for holocentromere assembly. Highlights: • RbAp46/48/LIN-53 is crucial for chromosome segregation in holocentric C. elegans • RbAp46/48/LIN-53 localizes to centromeres in metaphase and disappears in anaphase • RbAp46/48LIN-53 localizes and stabilizes CENP-AHCP-3 for holocentromere assembly • RbAp46/48LIN-53’s centromeric role is not due to histone acetylation or methylation

785813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
785813.value: 精神分裂症或思覺失調是嚴重精神疾患﹐影響著世界上近1%的人口。香港和內地分別約有7萬和130萬人患有思覺失調症。雖然抗精神病藥物為治療精神分裂症的主要手段﹐但仍有相當患者復發和病情加重。這很大程度上是由於各種副作用所引起的藥物依從性低下和中斷治療所致。高催乳素症是抗精神病藥治療中常見的副作用。高達70%的精神分裂症病人出現高催乳素症﹐其主要症狀為閉經﹐泌乳﹐性功能損傷和不孕。目前尚缺乏安全有效治療高催乳素症的方法。因此﹐對尋找新型治療製劑有著很高期盼。 我們已證實﹐一種稱為芍藥甘草湯的中藥方劑可有效降低精神分裂症患者的高催乳素症﹐而且其抗高催乳素的作用與調節多巴胺D2受體和其它調制物有關。這些發現引導我們去進一步探討該中藥方劑中可能在抗高催乳素症中起主要作用的成分及其機製。我們已鑒定出甘草次酸是芍藥甘草湯中的一種主要成分。我們初步研究發現﹐甘草次酸具有良好的安全性﹐能顯著抑制離體細胞和動物模型的高催乳素水平。其抗高催乳素作用與調節多種多巴胺調制物有關。早前研究已顯示﹐甘草次酸亦調節5-羥色胺和P物質所誘發的行為。 除下丘腦多巴胺神經元系統外﹐其它多種神經調制物也參與垂體泌乳素的調節。最重要的調節物是5-羥色胺和P物質。它們或直接作用於垂體泌乳素細胞或間接作用於下丘腦水平。在下丘腦水平﹐5-羥色胺解除對多巴胺釋放的抑制而P物質則加強多巴胺的釋放。 除D2受體外﹐其它多種神經調制物也參與抗精神病藥所誘發之高催乳素症的病理機製。我們推測﹐甘草次酸的抗高催乳素作用可能與多方面的精神藥理效應有關﹐尤其是中樞多巴胺﹑5-羥色胺和P物質神經元系統。為驗證該推測﹐我們制定下列研究目標: (1) 應用各種離體培養細胞﹐鑒定多巴胺﹑5-羥色胺和P物質相關受體在調節甘草次酸抗高催乳素症作用中的角色; (2) 在由多巴胺抑制劑所製成的高催乳素動物模型中﹐確定全身阻斷5-羥色胺和P物質相關受體是否可改變甘草次酸的抗高催乳素症作用; (3) 探測甘草次酸全身給藥對大鼠動物模式腦區和垂體中相關受體表達的影響。 該研究將為支持甘草次酸發展為治療高催乳素症製劑提供精神藥理學證據。該研究也從新角度更好理解泌乳素分泌的中樞調節和抗精神病藥所誘發之高催乳素症的病理生理過程。簽于我們已證實了芍藥甘草湯治療高催乳素的臨床療效﹐該研究將把這一傳統方劑帶回實驗室做進一步的機製探討﹐這種從病床到實驗室﹐而不是從實驗室到病床的研究路線將為傳統中醫中藥開闢一種新的研究模式。

785813.label: Major findings and research outcome
785813.value: [1] We have conducted a series of in vitro and in vivo experiments to identify the role of related receptors of dopamine (DA), serotonin (5-HT), and substance P (SP) in the regulation of the anti-hyperprolactinemia (hyperPRL) effects of 18beta-glycyrrhetinic acid (GA). DA and 5-HT neuronal systems, but not SP neuronal system, are involved in anti-hyperPRL effects of GA. GA treatment for 24 h inhibited PRL synthesis and secretion in MMQ cells and cultured pituitary cells in a dose-dependent fashion; but this effect was not reproduced in GH3 cells that lack the expression of functional dopamine D2 receptors. GA suppressed elevated PRL level and growth hormone, and normalized several sex hormones in a rat model of hyperPRL, produced by repeated injection of the dopamine blocker metoclopramide. GA also modulated the expression 5-HT1A and 5-HT2A receptors in both in vivo and in vitro models. These results indicate that GA is effective in suppressing PRL hyperactivity caused by the blockade of dopamine D2 receptors. This suppressive effect of GA may be related to its modulation of the serotonergic system. [2] GA induced cellular damage in rat pituitary adenoma-derived MMQ and GH3 cells, GA also caused G0/G1 phase arrest, increased apoptosis rate and increased mitochondrial membrane permeabilization by suppressing the mitochondrial membrane potential and down-regulating a ratio of B cell lymphoma 2 (Bcl-2) and Bax. GA activated calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII), c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) and P38; but these activating effects were attenuated by pretreatment with N-acetyl-L-cysteine, a ROS inhibitor. Pretreatment with KN93, a CaMKII inhibitor, also abolished the GA activation of JNK and P38. GA remarkably inhibited growth of pituitary adenoma grafted on nude mice. This study provides experimental evidence in the support of further developing GA as a chemotherapeutic agent for pituitary adenoma. [3] We additionally examined another similar compound called liquiritigenin (LQ), also derived from liquorice. LQ inhibited cell viability, dissipated MMP, and reduced the expression of Ras, B-cell lymphoma 2 and B-cell lymphoma-extra large. LQ also inhibited the activation of extracellular signalling-regulated kinases (ERKs) and the translocation of from cytoplasm to nucleus. LQ markedly reduced tumour size without affecting bodyweight in mice with GH3 cells xenograft. These results indicate that LQ effectively inhibits pituitary adenoma tumour growth and induces cell apoptotic death mainly via Ras/ERKs and ROS-dependent mitochondrial pathways. [4] Four papers directly derived from this project have been published.

785813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
785813.value: [1] Our studies have well demonstrated that GA and its alike compound LQ are promising agents to be further developed as an adjunct for the treatment of hyperPRL and a chemotherapeutic agent for pituitary adenomia. [2] Next, we will develop a translational research protocol to translate and commercialize these two novel agents into market.

785813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
785813.value: HyperPRL is a common side effect induced by antipsychotic drugs. There are no effective interventions available. Herbal medicine and naturally occurring compounds may have the potential to alleviate hyperPRL. Our previous studies have shown the effects of herbal medicine in treating hyperPRL. The present study further investigated anti-hyperPRL and anti-tumor effects of a natural compound called 18beta-glycyrrhetinic acid (GA) and alike compound called liquiritigenin (LQ) as well as the underlying mechanisms. We found that GA is effective in reducing hyperPRL. Both GA and LQ have the potential in reducing pituitary tumor. These results provide preliminary evidence to support the further development of these compounds into the clinical use.

785913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
785913.value: Exploration of effective connectivity (i.e., causal interactions) between spatially distributed brain regions is crucial for understanding the neural mechanisms of highly organized human brain. Effective connectivity analysis based on the concept of Granger causality and the multivariate autoregressive (MVAR) model has demonstrated powerful capacity for evaluating the direction and strength of causality between brain regions. Sensory stimuli and/or cognitive events elicit transient and complicated changes of effective connectivity in the brain, which are usually inferred from time-varying Granger causality (tvGC) analysis of electrophysiological signals (such as electroencephalography, EEG) with millisecond precision. Due to the extremely noisy and complex nature of electrophysiological data, tvGC is conventionally estimated from multiple trials of electrophysiological responses elicited by repeatedly presented stimuli or events. However, the conventional tvGC analysis can only estimate common tvGC patterns across multiple trials, while tvGC patterns exhibit substantial trial-to-trial variability most probably due to fluctuations of single-trial stimulus parameters and cognitive factors. Therefore, it is highly desirable to analyze tvGC at single-trial level for exploring physiologically relevant single-trial tvGC patterns that convey novel and important information about effective connectivity of the brain. The aim of this proposal is to develop and apply a single-trial tvGC analysis scheme for the inference of effective connectivity from electrophysiological signals. This scheme consists of (1) a single-trial event-related potential (ERP) detection method to isolate stochastic EEG activities for fitting an MVAR model; (2) a regularized recursive least squares method to identify the time-varying MVAR model for obtaining tvGC measures of effective connectivity; (3) a multivariate pattern analysis method based on partial least squares regression for identifying physiologically relevant tvGC patterns at single-trial level. Simulated EEG data will be used to evaluate and validate the single-trial tvGC analysis scheme and the methods involved. Further, we will apply the scheme to identify tvGC patterns correlated with the intensity of pain perceived by human subjects from laser-evoked EEG responses, which are considered the best tool for investigating the pain processing and pathways in physiological and clinical studies. The long-term goal is to provide a dynamic and detailed characterization of physiologically relevant effective connectivity patterns related to various sensory stimuli and cognitive events, which will be a fundamental theoretical and practical contribution for improving our understanding of brain mechanisms. In addition, the physiologically relevant time-varying effective connectivity patterns can serve as indicators of behavior and/or cognitive processes, which will be of great scientific and clinical significance. 探索不同腦區間的有效連接（即因果性）對於理解高效組織在一起的人類大腦的神經機制起著非常關鍵的作用。基於格蘭傑因果性和多元自回歸模型的有效連接分析已經表現出了強大的評估腦區間因果性強度和方向的能力。對電生理信號（如腦電信號）進行時變的格蘭傑因果性分析可以識別出由感官刺激或認知活動引起的大腦內瞬時（毫秒級別）及複雜的有效連接的變動。由於電生理信號嚴峻的噪聲環境和複雜的自然特性，時變格蘭傑因果性分析通常是基於多次反復的刺激或多次事件形成的多次電生理響應平均估計而來。然而，傳統的時變格蘭傑因果性分析只能估計出多次響應共有的時變格蘭傑因果性特徵，而由於單次試驗參數和認知因素的波動，多次試驗之間的時變格蘭傑因果性特徵常常表現出極大的不同。因此，分析基於單次試驗的時變格蘭傑因果性有重大意義，它有助於揭示在單次試驗尺度內的時變格蘭傑因果性與生理學相關的成份，從而帶來新的關於大腦有效連接的重要信息。 本研究的目標是開發一套在單次試驗（single-trial）尺度上動態估計格蘭傑因果性的方案，並應用該方案推斷真實腦電信號中的有效連接隨時間變化的規律，及其與生理學因素相關的成分。該方案包括以下要素：（1）一種在單次試驗尺度上從腦電提取事件相關電位（Event-related potential）的方法。提取出來的事件相關電位將被用于擬合時變多元自回歸模型。（2）一種用于估計多元自回歸模型參數的規範化遞推最小二乘法。估計出的時變多元自回歸模型將被用于計算時變格蘭傑因果性的測度。（3）一種基于偏最小二乘回歸的多元模式分析方法。該方法將適用于在單次試驗的基礎上識別出時變格蘭傑因果性中與生理因素相關的成分。我們將會通過腦電仿真信號評估並驗證該方案及其所使用方法的可靠性。之後，我們會將該方案應用在從人類受試者身上采集到的由激光刺激誘發的痛覺所産生的腦電數據（激光刺激在疼痛研究領域被認爲是現階段最優的工具）。我們希望通過該方案找出格蘭傑因果性的時變規律中與人類主觀痛覺強度相關的成分。 本企劃的長遠目標是爲多種感官刺激或認知活動從有效連接性的角度提供一種動態、精細的表述，這將有助于從基礎理論與技術層面增進我們對大腦工作機制的理解。另外，這種與生理學相關的有效連接性在時域上的變化規律能用來指示行爲與認知上的狀態，因此其在科學與臨床研究中有重要的意義。

785913.label: Realisation of objectives
785913.value: [Objective 1] We have developed a new single-trial time-varying EEG connectivity analysis scheme, which basically consists of two parts: an adaptive window time-varying connectivity estimation method based on local polynomial regression (LPR), and (2) a multivariate pattern analysis method to identify connectivity correlates of behavioral data at the single-trial level. First, we have developed a new method, named local polynomial regression (LPR), to estimate the time-varying connectivity between two non-stationary time-course data. The new LPR method can smooth (with adaptively-selected window size) the inner product of two signals to estimate the time-varying correlation, which is a common metric to infer time-varying brain connectivity. The major novelty of the LPR method is that the window size can be adaptively and locally selected to cater for connectivity dynamics so that important dynamic information of the connectivity will not be overlooked while spurious patterns will not be wrongly identified. Second, we combine dimension reduction and multivariate linear regression, to identify connectivity correlates of behavioral data at the single-trial level. Unlike conventional single-trial methods based on multiple linear regression models to detect physiologically relevant EEG patterns, the new method can describe the relationship between behavioral data and connectivity metrics (which are high-dimensional in the temporal-spatial domain, or in the temporal-spectral-spatial domain) using a machine learning model (partial least-squares regression, PLSR). Our results show that the PLSR-based single-trial connectivity analysis scheme can identify meaningful connectivity patterns and have higher robustness against noise. Hence, the first objective of this study (to develop new methods for single-trial time-varying brain connectivity estimation) is successfully achieved. [Objective 2] The proposed single-trial EEG connectivity analysis scheme has been rigorously tested using simulated data and has been successfully applied on several real-world EEG data sets and fMRI data sets. Firstly, the performance of the LPR-based time-varying correlation estimation method and the PLSR-based dimension reduction method has been validated in a wide variety of simulation scenarios to make sure their performance is robust to various experimental parameters, such as signal-to-noise ratio, sampling rate, the extent of variations, etc. Next, the performance of the proposed scheme has also been tested on several datasets, including laser-evoked EEG data, auditory-evoked EEG data, visual-evoked fMRI data, and even electrooculography (EOG). We identified a set of meaningful connectivity features using the proposed new methods and these features are crucial for improving our understanding of several neuroscientific questions, such as pain-related connectivity patterns, inter-individual difference in auditory responses, transient network reconfiguration in visual tasks, etc. Thus, the second objective (to validate and apply methods on simulated and real-world data) is achieved. [Objective 3] We have carried out a laser-evoked EEG experiment on around 100 subjects with the specific aim to identify pain-related EEG connectivity patterns. The proposed scheme performed well on the laser-evoked EEG and fMRI data and we have identified some important EEG and fMRI correlates of pain perception. First, we observed that pre-stimulus EEG oscillations and synchronization in the alpha (at bilateral central regions) and gamma (at parietal regions) bands negatively modulated the perception of subsequent stimuli and combining information about alpha and gamma synchronization predicted subsequent perception significantly more accurately than either measure alone. Furthermore, to better localize the pain-related EEG synchronization on the cortex, in a parallel fMRI experiment, we found that pre-stimulus fMRI connectivity also modulated the perception of subsequent stimuli: perceptual ratings were higher when the BOLD signal was higher in the sensorimotor network and lower in the default mode network. Overall, results show that proposed methods can effectively identify pain-related connectivity patterns of EEG and fMRI data, whereby Objective 3 (to identify laser-pain-related brain connectivity patterns) is accomplished.

785913.label: Major findings and research outcome
785913.value: The novel single-trial brain connectivity scheme and the methods involved (PLSR and LPR) have been validated on simulated data and applied to real-world neuroimaging data, and the results are reported in a number of journals and conferences (listed in Part C of this report). For example, the PLSR method has been used to identify single-trial EEG features in [J1], and to estimate single-trial EOG features for human-computer interface [C3], [J3]. The LPR-based time-varying connectivity estimation method has been successfully applied to estimate transient fMRI connectivity in a visual task [J2], [J4]. The whole scheme has been used to estimate pain-related EEG and fMRI connectivity features and to predict pain perception using pain-related brain connectivity features in [C1], [C2], [C4], [J5], [J6] and [J7]. In these publications, we reported a series of findings, mainly focusing on brain activity patterns that are predictive of subjective pain perception. For example, in [J5], we found that (1) two distinct EEG features (alpha oscillations at bilateral central regions and gamma oscillations at parietal regions) can predict both the intensity of perception and the brain responses elicited by a subsequent somatosensory stimulation, and (2) two distinct sets of brain networks whose level of baseline functional activity predicted the perception of subsequent stimuli in different directions (high baseline connectivity in S1, SMA, ACC, MCC, and DLPFC predicted higher perceived intensity, whereas low baseline connectivity between mPFC, precuneus, angular gyrus, amygdala, and parahippocampal cortices predicted lower perceived intensity). These findings provide a more comprehensive physiological basis to pain mechanisms, and could contribute to new pain treatment protocols.

785913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
785913.value: In this project, new methods for extracting single-trial brain connectivity are proposed, which are of a general nature and will pave the way for further studies in brain connectivity under various experimental paradigms. In future, the methods developed in this project has the potential to provide a dynamic and detailed characterization of physiologically relevant brain connectivity patterns related to various sensory stimuli and cognitive events, which will improve our understanding of brain mechanisms in tasks. Furthermore, the physiologically relevant time-varying brain connectivity patterns can serve as indicators of behavior and/or cognitive processes, which will be of great scientific and clinical significance. For example, we plan to harness the pain-related single-trial brain activity patterns with the aim to develop new pain assessment tools for patients who cannot reliably report their pain feelings, which will be of great importance in clinical practice.

785913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
785913.value: The human brain has billions of neural cells that interact over time and space to support our mental activities, such as perception and cognition. Brain connectivity describes the interconnections of brain regions, and it is fast becoming one of the most important research fields for its promise to yield scientific, clinical, and economic benefits, such as diagnosis and therapy of mental diseases. But, it is still difficult to fast and reliably detect brain connectivity from the brain’s electrical signals (normally sampled by electroencephalography EEG), mainly because the brain’s signals are typically buried in heavy background noises. This project developed a new scheme to identify subtle and meaningful EEG brain connectivity in a fast, accurate, and automated manner. Such a brain connectivity detection scheme enables the construction of a new dynamic and high-resolution picture showing how different brain regions work in symphony in response to stimulation or tasks. The models developed in the project will contribute towards a better understanding of how brain connectivity supports normal brain functions and how brain connectivity might be altered by neurological disorders, which could be useful in developing new diagnosis tools for neurological diseases.

786013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
786013.value: Angiogenesis is a tightly regulated process in which newly formed capillaries outgrow from existing blood vessels. Abnormal angiogenesis often associates with pathological conditions. FGF2 and VEGF are the most potent angiogenic inducers among the variety of growth factors. We have previously demonstrated MT1-MMP is required for FGF2-induced angiogenesis as loss of MT1-MMP results in defective corneal neovascularization in response to FGF2. Our recent study demonstrated that MT1-MMP regulates activities of ADAM9 and ADAM15 by shedding them from the cell surface. Loss of MT1-MMP results in up-regulation of both ADAM9 and ADAM15 in mice. Loss of ADAM9 rescues calvarial osteogenesis in MT1-MMP deficient mice through restoring FGFR2 signaling. However, defective FGF2-induced corneal angiogenesis is not rescued, suggesting a distinct regulatory mechanism of FGF signaling by MT1-MMP in corneal angiogenesis. When crossed with ADAM15-/- mice, inflammation-induced angiogenesis in MT1-MMP-/- mice is restored in MT1-MMP/ADAM15 double knockout mice, suggesting that ADAM15 up-regulation is responsible for the defective corneal angiogenesis in the absence of MT1-MMP in mice. As FGF2-induced corneal angiogenesis depends on FGFR1 and cross-talks with VEGF, ADAM15 may be involved in the shedding of FGFR1 and/or VEGFR1. We therefore hypothesized that MT1-MMP exists as a master proteinase to maintain proper balance of proteinases. MT1-MMP inactivates ADAM15 to protect FGFR1 and VEGFR1 to protect proper angiogenic response in cornea. We propose to investigate the role for ADAM15 in regulating FGFR1 and VEGFR1 in cornea. This study will for the first time reveal the interplay between MT1-MMP and ADAM15, especially in the corneal angiogenesis. This study will also uncover the mechanism underlying defective angiogenesis in Mmp14-/- mice and provide insight into not only the regulation of corneal angiogenesis by ADAM15 but also strategy to control abnormal angiogenesis in human disorders including eye inflammation, tumor growth and metastasis. 血管生成是嚴格監管的過程中，新形成的毛細血管從現有的血管長大。血管異常生長往往與各種病理改变密切相关。 FGF2和VEGF是最重要的血管生成誘導因子。之前我們已經證實FGF2誘導血管生成需要MT1 – MMP。我們最近的研究表明， MT1-MMP可以将ADAM9和ADAM15從細胞表面脫落，从而調節它們的蛋白酶活性。MT1 – MMP 基因敲除小鼠中，FGF2誘導角膜新生血管的缺陷并伴有ADAM9和ADAM15上調。但是在MT1 – MMP 基因敲除小鼠中敲除ADAM9并不能拯救FGF2誘導角膜新生血管的缺陷。 提示MT1- MMP在角膜有不同的監管機制调控FGF信號及血管生成。當MT1 – MMP 基因敲除小鼠中敲除ADAM15时，炎症誘導的血管生成消失了，這表明MT1 – MMP 基因敲除小鼠中ADAM15上調可能是导致FGF2誘導角膜新生血管的缺陷的原因。FGF2誘導角膜新生血管生成有可能與膜上FGFR1受体以及其它血管內皮生長因子有关。ADAM15可能參與FGFR1和/或VEGFR1的脫落 。因此，我們推理， MT1-MMP作為重要的蛋白酶，平衡细胞膜上其它蛋白酶及生长因子受体。MT1-MMP滅活ADAM15保護FGFR1和VEGFR1，从而保護角膜適當的血管生成響應。我們建議研究ADAM15在調節角膜FGFR1和VEGFR1的作用。本研究首次揭示角膜的血管生成过程中MT1-MMP和ADAM15之間的相互作用。這项研究目的是揭示MT1-MMP 缺失小鼠角膜血管生成缺陷的機制。将有助于了解ADAM15調節角膜新生血管机理，以及蛋白酶在人類角膜血管異常生長疾病，炎症，腫瘤的生長和轉移的作用。

786013.label: Realisation of objectives
786013.value: Membrane Type I-Matrix Metalloproteinase (MT1-MMP/MMP14), a membrane anchored enzyme, is essential for diverse physiological and pathological processes through extracellular matrix remodeling and pericellular proteolysis. Deficiency in MT1-MMP leads to severe growth retardation, craniofacial deformities, angiogenic defects and premature death in mouse (Zhou et al., 2000). Our previous findings revealed that defective calvarial osteogenesis in Mmp14-/- mice is a consequence of compromised Fibroblast Growth Factor (FGF) signaling. In calvarial osteoblasts, MT1-MMP cleaves and inactivates ADAM9 to protect FGFR2 from ectodomain shedding by ADAM9 to maintain optimal FGF signaling for calvarial development (Chan et al., 2012). However, this ADAM9/MT1-MMP dependent regulatory loop for FGF signaling is tissue-specific as depletion of ADAM9 fails to rescue defective FGF-2 induced corneal angiogenesis in Mmp14-/- mice, suggesting that other proteinases, apart from ADAM9, may be involved in MT1-MMP-dependent vascular development (Wong et al., 2012). As MT1-MMP also cleaves and inactivates ADAM15 (Wong et al., 2012). Therefore, it is possible that in cornea, instead of ADAM9, ADAM15 may be responsible for the defective FGF signaling. Objective 1: To investigate if ADAM15 is responsible for the defective FGF2-induced angiogenesis in Mmp14-/-cornea Our previous data found that loss of MT1-MMP leads to increased expression of ADAM15 in the cornea (Wong et al., 2012). To further confirm ADAM15 is involved in defective angiogenesis in Mmp14-/- mice, we examined the expression of MT1-MMP and ADAM15 in mouse corneas by immunofluorescent staining using specific antibodies against MT1-MMP and ADAM15. Unfortunately, we used different commercially available specific antibodies against ADAM15 to perform the staining, but none of them gave positive staining in the cornea. The failure in immunostaining is likely attributed to the poor quality of antibodies. To solve this problem, we will examine their colocalization by different approaches, such as in situ hybridization. We have previously shown the physical interaction between ectopic MT1-MMP and ADAM15. To further substantiate this finding, we examined the endogenous interaction between MT1-MMP and ADAM15. Indeed, endogenous MT1-MMP physically interacts with ADAM15 in primary mouse calvarial osteoblasts. Furthermore, we found that recombinant catalytic domain of MT1-MMP promotes the degradation of recombinant ADAM15 in vitro. To examine the function of ADAM15 in MT1-MMP-dependent FGF2-induced angiogenesis, we planned to perform corneal micropocket angiogenenic assay using pellets containing FGF2 in wild-type, Mmp14-/-, Adam15-/- and Adam15-/-Mmp14-/- mice. However, we observed more severe growth retardation and higher mortality rate in premature Adam15-/-Mmp14-/- mice when compared to age-matched Mmp14-/- mice, and so we could not perform corneal pocket assay in Adam15-/-Mmp14-/- mice. To solve this problem, we generated Mmp14flox/floxTie1-cre mouse and Mmp14flox/floxlyzM-cre mouse that specifically lose the expression of MT1-MMP in the endothelial linage and the myeloid linage respectively. We found that mice lacking MT1-MMP in either lymphatic endothelial cells or macrophages are viable and recapitulate corneal lymphangiogenic phenotypes observed in Mmp14-/- mice (Wong et al., 2016), suggesting that they are suitable animal models for studying the impact of ADAM15 deficiency on corneal angiogenesis. We will cross Adam15-/- mouse with these two conditional knockout mice to generate Adam15-/- Mmp14flox/floxTie1-cre mouse and Adam15-/- Mmp14flox/floxlyzM-cre mouse in the future. Objective 2: To investigate if ADAM15 sheds FGFR1 The restore of inflammation-induced angiogenesis in Adam15-/-/Mmp14-/- suggests either FGFR or VEGFR mediated signaling, or even both signaling, is rescued. To understand the underlying mechanism of the restored angiogenesis by loss of Adam15 in Mmp14-/- mice, we examined whether ADAM15 sheds FGFRs both in vitro and in vivo. Firstly, we examined the expression of FGFR1 in corneas by Western blotting using specific antibody against FGFR1. No significant change in both full length and truncated FGFR1 could be observed among wild-type and Mmp14-/- corneas. Secondly, we also examined if MT1-MMP sheds FGFR1 in vitro. We failed to detect any changes in full length and truncated FGFR1 in the cell lysate of Mmp14-/- calvarial osteoblasts. As we previously showed ADAM9 sheds FGFR2, we examined FGFR2 shedding in HEK 293T cells expressing flag-tagged FGFR2 with ADAM15. Unlike ADAM9, ADAM15 does not cleave FGFR2 to generate a truncated fragment of FGFR2. These data suggest that MT1-MMP does not regulate the FGFR1 ectodomain shedding. Objective 3: To investigate if ADAM15 sheds VEGFR1 To understand how ADAM15 causes defective angiogenesis, we first investigated which growth factor receptor signaling is responsible for the defective corneal angiogenesis in MT1-MMP deficient mice. We first examined VEGFR1. Indeed a truncated fragment of VEGFR1 was found to be accumulated in Mmp14-/- corneas and injection of neutralizing antibodies against VEGFR1 in Mmp14-/- mice induces spontaneous corneal angiogenesis similar to that of Mmp14-/- Adam15-/- corneas. Based on these preliminary findings, we hypothesized that the upregulation of ADAM15 resulted from the loss of MT1-MMP may be responsible for the formation of truncated VEGFR1 fragments. To test this hypothesis, ADAM15 and VEGFR1 were ectopically expressed in 293T cells. Unexpectedly, we did not detect any truncated fragment of VEGFR1 in ADAM15/VEGFR1 co-expressing cells. This suggest that ADAM15 is not responsible for the accumulation of truncated VEGFR1 in Mmp14-/- corneas. To find out what is responsible the defective FGF-induced angiogenesis in MT1-MMP cornea, we decided to examine if altered inflammatory factors is responsible for the abnormal angiogenesis. Interestingly, this deviation from the original objective resulted in a big discovery. We found that loss of MT1-MMP leads to spontaneous activation of macrophages and increased inflammatory responses in corneas during eyelid opening and corneal maturation, resulting in aberrant vascularization of lymphatic vessels (lymphangiogensis) in the corneas. Mechanistically, MT1-MMP directly cleaves LYVE-1 on lymphatic endothelial cells to inhibit LYVE-1-mediated lymphangiogenic responses (Wong et al., 2016). In addition, MT1-MMP-mediated PI3Kδ signaling restrains the production of VEGF-C from prolymphangiogenic macrophages through repressing the activation of NF-κB signaling (Wong et al., 2016). As ADAM15 was recently shown to restrain the toll-like receptor (TLR) signaling to suppress the inflammatory responses in immune cells (Ahmed et al., 2013), it is therefore possible that loss of ADAM15 may further dampen the inflammatory responses to induce both spontaneous angiogenesis and lymphangiogenesis in Mmp14-/- corneas. To address this hypothesis, we examined the inflammatory response in the corneas deficient in both MT1-MMP and ADAM15. Indeed, several inflammatory cytokines and angiogenic factors, such as TNF-α, IL-1, VEGF-A and VEGF-C, were significantly upregulated in MT1-MMP deficient corneas when compared to those of wild-type controls. Depletion of ADAM15 further increased the expression of these cytokines in MT1-MMP deficient corneas, suggesting that ADAM15 may suppress the inflammatory responses in MT1-MMP deficient corneas. We looked for any potential targets of TLR signaling cascade that may be regulated by MT1-MMP-dependent cleavage of ADAM15. TIR-domain-containing adapter-inducing interferon-β (TRIF) is a key adapter in responding to the activation of TLRs. Surprisingly, we found that TRIF was significantly down-regulated in MT1-MMP deficient macrophages. Loss of ADAM15 restored the reduced expression of TRIF in MT1-MMP deficient macrophages to the wild-type level, suggesting that MT1-MMP may maintain the expression of TRIF through inactivating ADAM15.

786013.label: Major findings and research outcome
786013.value: In this project, we studied how MT1-MMP regulates corneal vascularization. We identified MT1-MMP as a key regulator for both physiological angiogenesis and lymphangiogenesis. Mice lacking MT1-MMP in either endothelial cells or macrophages recapitulate corneal vascularization phenotypes observed in Mmp14−/− mice, suggesting that the spontaneous vascularization is both endothelial cells autonomous and macrophage associated. Mechanistically, MT1-MMP directly cleaves LYVE-1 on lymphatic endothelial cells to inhibit LYVE-1-mediated lymphangiogenic responses. In addition, MT1-MMP-mediated PI3Kδ signaling restrains the production of VEGF-C from macrophages through repressing the activation of NF-κB signaling. Furthermore, loss of ADAM15 dampens the pro-inflammatory responses in Mmp14-/- corneas, restoring the defective angiogenesis in Mmp14-/- corneas. MT1-MMP may inactivate ADAM15 to regulate TRIF-mediated TLR signaling in inflammatory macrophages. Thus, ADAM15 may serve as a mediator for MT1-MMP-dependent suppression of inflammatory responses. The findings regarding the role of MT1-MMP in lymphangiogenesis have been published in Nature Communications and we are now preparing a manuscript for reporting the functional crosstalk between MT1-MMP and ADAM15.

786013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
786013.value: We found that MT1-MMP may inactivate ADAM15 to regulate TRIF-mediated TLR signaling in inflammatory macrophages, which may contribute to the regulation for corneal angiogenesis. However, the mechanism by which ADAM15 regulates TRIF remains unexplored and deserves further investigation in the future. This project identified MT1-MMP as an important regulator for physiological vascularization. However, the role of MT1-MMP in pathological vascularization, such as lymphatic metastasis, is unexplored. Increased activities of MT1-MMP have long been regarded as a driving factor for cancer progression and metastasis in various cancers and targeting MT1-MMP in cancer has been a therapeutic approach for cancer treatment. However, numerous clinical trials using inhibitors of MMPs were unsuccessful in a variety of cancer types. The inhibitory effects of MT1-MMP on lymphangiogenesis also suggest that inhibiting MT1-MMP in cancer therapy may not necessarily be beneficial, as it may promote lymphatic metastasis. Moreover, most of the previous studies regarding MT1-MMP primarily focus on its cell-autonomous oncogenic activities in cancer cells, but the role of MT1-MMP in tumor-associated cells, like immune cells and endothelial cells, is largely unknown. Thus, to evaluate the therapeutic potential for targeting MT1-MMP in cancer treatment, it is important to investigate how MT1-MMP may influence the prolymphangiogenic properties of tumor-associated macrophages and the angiogenic potential of tumor lymphatic vessels, and hence lymphatic metastasis.

786013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
786013.value: The lymphatic vasculature is required for fluid homeostasis, absorption of dietary lipids from the small intestine and trafficking of immune cells. Congenital defects in lymphatic vessel development usually result in embryonic lethality and individuals with dysfunctional lymphatic vessels often suffer from systematic oedema and impaired immune responses. Lymphangiogenesis has been recently identified as a primary cause of metastasis for many cancers. Despite its importance in physiology and pathological conditions, the inhibitory factors for lymphatic vessel growth remain largely unknown. We show that MT1-MMP represents an endogenous negative regulator of lymphangiogenesis. This study will lay the foundation for the advances in therapeutic approaches for lymphatic diseases.

788913.label: Major findings and research outcome
788913.value: Forty-eight subjects (19 males, 29 females) with bilateral lower third molars in close proximity to the IAN were recruited in this study. The mean age was 26.6 years (S.D. 5.8 years), with the range of 19 to 45 years. A total of ninety-six coronectomies were performed, with 48 coronectomies in each group. Objective 1: Root exposure and root migration rate: No roots were exposed in both groups within the 24 months follow-up period. The mean root migration (S.D.) of the Study Group were 0.043mm (0.20mm), 0.55mm (0.92mm), 0.82mm (1.1mm), 0.94mm (1.1mm) and 1.0mm (1.3mm) at post-operative 2 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, 12 months and 24 months, respectively. The mean root migration (S.D.) of the Control Group were 1.6mm (1.3mm) at post-operative 3 months and reached 3.5mm (1.9mm) at post-operative 24 months. The root migration measurements in the Study Group were less than that in the Control Group at all time-points, and were significantly different from post-operative 3 months onward (post-operative 2 weeks p = 0.069; 3 months p = 0.000; 6 months p = 0.000; 12 months p = 0.000; 24 months p = 0.000). Objective 2: Periodontal attachment measurements There were trends of reduction in the PD at all three sites in both the Study Group and the Control Group, but were no statistical difference between the two groups. It was noted there were increased PD at the mid-distal and distobuccal at post-operative two weeks when compared to the pre-operative measurements. The PD at the two sites were back to the pre-operative state by post-operative 3 months, and appeared to be further improved in terms of periodontal attachment (i.e. reduction in PD) from post-operative 6 months onwards. Objective : Surgical morbidities and patient reported outcome There were no post-operative IAN deficit in all cases. There were 32.6% and 17.4% of the subjects complaining pain at post-operative 2 weeks in the Study Group and in the Control Group, respectively, but was no statistical significant difference (p=0.15). There was no statistical difference between the two groups in terms of the pain severity for those who experienced pain (p=0.53).

788913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
788913.value: A longer follow-up study will be indicated to show the long term benefit of adjunctive GBR after coronectomy. Patients with advanced age requiring coronectomy may benefit from adjunctive GBR for periodontal regeneration. The patients in this study were relatively younger and may not be able to show the benefit in periodontal regeneration after GBR. Older patients with longer period of periodontal bone loss from the lower third molar may be the subject of study in future research.

788913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
788913.value: Lower third molar impaction is common and cause infection and localized periodontal disease. Lower third molar surgery carries a risk of nerve injury because the root is close to the nerve. Coronectomy is a lower third molar surgery technique that remove only the crown of the tooth and leave the root in the bone., thus minimizing the risk of nerve injury. However, most retained roots will migrate and some may become exposed and need a second surgery to remove. This research compared coronectomy with or without guided bone regeneration (GBR), a technique that will grow bone and hopefully will stop the roots from migration and exposure. The results showed 1) coronectomy with GBR will have minimal migration when compared to coronectomy alone; 2) Both techniques carry similar morbidities and periodontal regeneration after surgery. The technique should reduce the risk of root exposure and the need of a second re-operation in long term.

789213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
789213.value: Long term care institutions face a formidable challenge with the projected increase in the population of dependent elders in the coming decades. Poorer oral health has been consistently observed amongst institutionalized elders compared to community-dwelling elders, and this has been attributed to a number of factors including compromised physical and mental capabilities, resulting in a general loss of functional independence. This is further compounded by a general lack of awareness and neglect of oral hygiene by nursing home staff, whom residents depend on for the majority of their daily self-care. Absence of daily oral hygiene results in the build-up of dental plaque and allows the uninhibited growth of opportunistic bacteria, which have been shown to cause lower respiratory tract infections such as aspiration pneumonia, one of the most common infectious causes of death among institutionalized elders. While there is a general consensus that an antimicrobial agent should be used as part of an optimal daily oral hygiene regimen in institutionalized elders, agreement has yet be reached regarding the optimal agent and its method of application. Delivery of an antimicrobial agent as a mouthwash may be problematic for frail elders who may be mentally impaired and unable to follow instructions, or have swallowing impairments and at a risk for aspiration. The use of an oral spray has been shown to be effective in other patient groups, and may be more appropriate and applicable for institutionalized elders. While chlorhexidine serves as the gold standard for anti-plaque effectiveness, prolonged usage is contraindicated due to side effects which include tooth staining and calculus formation. Chlorine dioxide is an effective antimicrobial agent, and short term studies have suggested a comparable anti-plaque activity compared to chlorhexidine, as well as the absence of these side effects. We have prior experience in the development of oral hygiene protocols for patients following stroke, and now propose to test the effectiveness of a chlorine dioxide spray against a chlorhexidine spray in the reduction of dental plaque, oral respiratory pathogens, and incidence of aspiration pneumonia amongst institutionalized elders. All participants will be expected to benefit from the administered interventions, and we hope to develop an optimal oral hygiene protocol which can easily be adopted at a low cost by nursing homes regionally in Hong Kong, and potentially worldwide. Furthermore, the project has implications for the integration of oral health within the broader domains of holistic healthcare provision in such facilities. 在未來數十年，長期護理機構將會面對依賴性長者人數預期不斷增長的艱巨挑戰。從持續觀察中發現住院長者的口腔衛生問題較社區長者為差。這情況歸因於若干因素包括: 喪失體能及精神上的能力，而導致整體獨立功能性損退。由於住院長者大部份日常自顧事項需要得到照顧，倘若院舍護理員對長者口腔衛生欠缺警覺性及疏於照料，情況會更為惡化。缺乏每天口腔衛生護理會形成牙菌膜，以及讓機會致病菌任意生長，情況顯示會造成下呼吸道感染，例如吸入性肺炎，就是其中一種最普遍導致住院長者的致命傳染病。正當整體同意使用抗菌劑是維護住院長者口腔衛生的最佳方法，有關最適當的藥劑及其使用方法已經達成共識。不過身體虛弱的長者使用抗菌劑如漱口水會遇上一定的困難，他們可能會由於精神上的損退而未能跟從指引；或有吞嚥障礙而造成抽吸上的風險。鑒於口腔噴霧劑有效幫助其他病人群組，因此口腔噴霧劑對住院長者來說，可能是更為適合和可應用的選擇。當洗必泰成為有效抗牙菌斑形成的金標準，但延長使用會導致副作用，包括形成牙漬及牙結石。二氧化氯是一種有效抗菌劑，而在短期研究中有建議與洗必泰作抗牙石比較項目，並未有這些副作用。由於我們先前已有關於中風患者口腔衛生發展草案的經驗，因此現在我們建議為洗必泰噴霧及二氧化氯噴霧作效果比較，測試住院長者的牙菌斑及口腔呼吸道致病菌之減低程度，與吸引性肺炎之比率。所有參加者將預期從實施介入中獲益，我們希望發展一個最佳的口腔衛生方案，能夠以較低成本令香港的護理院舍方便採用，並有潛力推廣至全球各地。此外，此項目有可能影響口腔健康融合到更廣泛領域的全面醫療保健提供。

789413.label: Realisation of objectives
789413.value: Note that during this study, psr1p (pole separation regulator 1) was named as csi1p (chromosome segregation impaired protein 1) in another publication. Both proteins correspond to the same systematic name: SPBC2G2.14. To be consistent, we refer to SPBC2G2.14 as psr1p/csi1p in this final report. During the funding period, we have followed the proposed research plan to address the two revised objectives as shown in 5.2, and the attempts were successful. (1) Objective 1.a: Using yeast-two -hybrid and biochemical assays, we have successfully determined the precise interacting domains of mal3p and sad1p in psr1p/csi1p. Specifically, the amino acid regions 445-460 and 191-220 in psr1p/csi1p are responsible for interacting with mal3p and sad1p, respectively. Further, by yeast-two-hybrid screening, we have identified the conserved microtubule associated protein alp7p/TACC as a new interacting protein of psr1p/csi1p whose interacting domain for alp7p/TACC was also mapped to the region 460-465. (2) Objective 1.b: We employed a combination of mutagenesis, biochemistry, and live-cell imaging approaches to successfully determine the functions of the interactions of psr1p/csi1p with mal3p, sad1p, and alp7p. Functional characterization showed that the interaction between sad1p and psr1p/csi1p is to recruit psr1p/csi1p to the spindle pole body, while the interaction between mal3p and psr1p/csi1p appears to have a minor role in bipolar spindle formation but the interaction between alp7p and psrp1/csi1p plays a critical role in bipolar spindle formation (See our publication Zheng et al MBC 2014). *Therefore, our studies demonstrate that psr1p/csi1p recruits multiple microtubule associated proteins (mal3p and alp7p) to the spindle pole body to promote bipolar spindle formation. Thus, objective 1 has been achieved. (3) Objective 2.a: Using yeast-two -hybrid and biochemical assays, we have successfully determined the precise interacting domains of nuf2p in psr1p/csi1p. Interestingly, the amino acid regions 77-220 and 460-480 in psr1p/csi1p are important for interacting with nuf2p. (4) Objective 2.b: Finally, we employed a combination of mutagenesis, yeast genetics, and live-cell imaging to address the function of the interaction between psr1p/csi1p and nuf2p. Malfunction of either nuf2p or psr1p/csi1p gives rise to a similar phenotype of interphase kinetochore declustering. Similarly, the psr1p/csi1p truncation mutants that cannot interact with nuf2p result in interphase kinetochore declustering. *Therefore, we conclude that psr1p/csi1p is involved in kinetochore clustering through linking the kinetochore protein nuf2p to the spindle pole body. Thus, objective 2 has been satisfactorily addressed.

789413.label: Major findings and research outcome
789413.value: Note that psr1p (pole separation regulator 1) is the same protein as csi1p (chromosome segregation impaired protein 1) that was shown in another publication. To be consistent, we refer to this protein as psr1p/csi1p in this final report. This proposed project was based on our preliminary finding that the absence of psr1p/csi1p could cause remarkable spindle and chromosome segregation problems, aiming to reveal the molecular mechanisms underlying spindle formation and chromosome dynamics. Following the designed research plan, we have successfully established that psr1p/csi1p coordinates with multiple microtubule associated proteins (MAPs) including mal3p, alp7p, and nuf2p to regulate bipolar spindle formation and interphase kinetochore clustering. Major findings and research outcomes are as follows. (1) New molecular mechanism underlying bipolar spindle formation. Psr1p/csi1p recruits multiple microtubule associated proteins, in particular alp7p, to the spindle pole body to promote efficient bipolar spindle formation during early mitosis. This work establishes that psr1p/csi1p is a key player in recruiting MAPs to the spindle pole body where MAPs function to properly organize spindle microtubules. This finding has been published in Mol Biol Cell (See Part C, Zheng et al MBC 2014). (2) New molecular mechanism underlying kinetochore clustering in interphase. Psr1p/csi1p serves as a linking protein to cluster kinetochores at the spindle pole body by interacting with nuf2p, a conserved protein residing at the outer layer of kinetochores. The manuscript for this work is under preparation. (3) New molecular mechanism regulating microtubule depolymerization. While carrying out microscopy visualization screening for new MAPs involved in spindle functions, we identified the new MAP mcp1p and functional characterization establishes that mcp1p plays a critical role in promoting microtubule depolymerization. This work has been published in FEBS Lett (See Part C, Zheng et al FEBS Lett 2014). In addition, we have confirmed the critical role of MAPs in establishing the connections between microtubules and mitochondria (See Part C, Li et al Sci Rep 2015).

789413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
789413.value: While we have successfully revealed new molecular mechanisms underlying bipolar spindle formation and kinetochore clustering and have achieved the proposed objectives, our current work also lays a solid foundation for future studies. The possible research directions are as follows. (1) To further understand how the interactions of psr1p/csi1p with mal3p, alp7p, and nuf2p are spatiotemporally regulated. As the interactions among these proteins are transient and appear to be cell cycle dependent, it is likely that the cell cycle dependent kinase CDK1 and the polo family kinase plo1 are involved. One research direction could be to test if psr1p, mal3p, alp7p, and nuf2p are substrates of the two kinases and to characterize the function of the phospho-regulation. (2) To solve the structure of psr1p/csi1p. This will facilitate further understanding the action mechanisms of psr1p/csi1p as psr1p/csi1p consists of distinct regions responsible for interacting with different MAPs.

789413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
789413.value: In general, chromosome segregation failures are associated with cancer development. Therefore, to develop new strategies for cancer prevention and intervention, it is important to comprehend how chromosomes within the cell are properly segregated during mitosis. Proper chromosome segregation depends on the microtubule apparatus, the spindle, and requires kinetochore (a large proteinaceous structure responsible for attaching chromosomes to microtubules) clustering at the spindle poles at the onset of mitosis. Further mechanistic studies are required to fully understanding how the bipolar spindle is assembled and how the kinetochores are clustered near the spindle poles. This project has identified a key protein responsible for bipolar spindle formation and kinetochore clustering, i.e. psr1p/csi1p, and has established new molecular mechanisms regulating the two processes essential for proper chromosome segregation. Therefore, our current work has provided important insights into understanding genome instability and cancer.
