799813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
799813.value: In the proposed project, we will examine how an individual’s sense of self can influence his or her own emotions and estimations of the emotions of others, thereby changing consumer communications. Its particular focus will be how affirmation of the self through reflection on one’s core values can change consumer word-of-mouth (WOM) communications about consumption experiences or marketing appeals. Emotions play an important role in interpersonal contexts, which are both ubiquitous and consequential. They include such social situations as gift-giving and price negotiations, in which emotions can serve communicative and social functions because they convey information about one’s own and others’ thoughts and intentions. We posit that self-affirmation broadens an individual’s perspective on the feelings of other. Accordingly, self-affirmed consumers are more attentive to others’ feelings. We suggest such changes in understanding of others’ emotions will influence their WOM communications as well as their understanding of those of others. We will explore two types of consumer WOM communications: communications about consumption experiences (one’s own or those of others) and communications about marketing appeals. In our investigation of the former, we will examine how self-affirmation influences the way consumers spread or listen to WOM. We propose that self-affirmed consumers are more likely to speak up for others’ product and service failures. In the case of negative consumption experiences, affirmed consumers are expected to feel less angry, which reduces their willingness to generate negative WOM. However, affirmed consumers are expected to predict stronger emotional reactions from others, rendering them more likely to complain on others’ behalf. We will also examine how consumers interpret others’ WOM communications (online reviews), and expect to show that self-affirmation can lead consumers to estimate the emotions of review writers as more intense regardless of whether the review is positive or negative. In our investigation of consumer WOM communications about marketing appeals, we will examine what type of appeal is more likely to “go viral” in social networks. In daily online activities (e.g., Web surfing, social networking), consumers are exposed to various types of marketing appeals. We hypothesize that self-affirmed customers are less responsive to commercials that appeal to their own emotions, but more responsive to appeals that ask them to adopt the emotional perspective of others (e.g., children suffering from hunger). 此研究項目將探討消費者的自我概念如何影響個人情感和對他人情感的判斷，從而改變消費者之間的溝通。此研究著眼於如何通過對個人核心價值的反思而達到自我肯定來改變消費者對消費體驗或營銷訴求的口碑傳播。人際關系是無處不在和極其重要的，而情感在人際關系中發揮著重要的作用。在送禮和價格談判等社交場合中，情感能發揮其溝通和社交功能，有效地傳達有關自身和他人的想法和意圖。我們假設自我肯定能拓寬一個人對他人感受的看法。因此，自我肯定的消費者更能關注他人的感受，我們並推斷這種變化會影響口碑傳播以及對他人的理解。 我們將探討兩種消費者口碑傳播：有關消費體驗（自身或他人的）和有關營銷訴求的口碑傳播。對於消費體驗的口碑傳播，我們將研究自我肯定如何影響消費者散播或接收訊息的方式。我們認為自我肯定的消費者更有可能為他人的產品和服務失當提出意見。對於不愉快的消費體驗，自我肯定的消費者將顯露較少憤怒，從而減少產生負面口碑的可能性。然而，自我肯定的消費者對他人情感的預測則會更為強烈，從而較容易替其他人抱怨。我們還將研究消費者如何闡釋他人的口碑傳播(網絡評論), 並預料不管評論是正面或負面的，自我肯定的消費者將對評論家情感的預測更為強烈。 對於有關營銷訴求的口碑傳播，我們將探討什麼類型的訴求更可能在社交網絡中進行“病毒式的傳播”。在日常的網絡活動中（如上互聯網、社交網)，消費者都能接觸到多類型的營銷訴求。我們推斷自我肯定的消費者對一些吸引自己情緒的廣告會有較少反應，但對一些要求投入他人情感角度（如兒童遭受飢餓）的廣告將反應較大。

799813.label: Realisation of objectives
799813.value: Objective 1. Examine real consumption experiences and related WOM communications Through several experiments, we examined the effect of self-affirmation on individuals’ willingness to share information about others’ hardships in their social networks (e.g., Facebook). In one study, we used materials from a real charity, Kids-In-Danger, addressing defective products for children. Participants with (without) children were considered high-identification (low-identification) participants. We found that self-affirmation increased individuals’ willingness to spread information about others’ hardships and that this effect was particularly pronounced when individuals did not closely identify with the victims (i.e., when they had no children). The findings were disseminated at the invited talk at the National University of Singapore in 2014; they were also included in a paper that is currently under a second round of review at Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin. In six studies, we examined the opposite state of affirmed self. Particularly, we examined consumers’ enjoyment of a computer game under self-threats. We found that consumers enjoyed a computer game less when their sense of self, particularly felt autonomy, was threatened by a computerized helper imbued with humanlike features. This negative effect on enjoyment was attenuated when consumers’ sense of self was restored via self-affirmation. The findings were published in Journal of Consumer Research (2016). In another study, we measured the effect of self-affirmation on sensory experiences. Specifically, we measured reactions to emotion-laden stimuli, finding that self-affirmation increased the estimated intensity of others’ sensory experiences. For example, after listening to a loud sound for two minutes, non-affirmed participants estimated that they felt more pain than others, but this difference was attenuated when they were affirmed, in which case they estimated others would feel as much pain as they did. The findings were disseminated at the invited talk at National University of Singapore in 2014. Objective 2. Strengthen the self-affirmation mechanism We provided evidence for ego-defensive processing by measuring attention to information about others’ misfortunes. Specifically, in one study we used a real charity, “Are You Dense,” which educates the public about delayed diagnoses of breast cancer. We found that self-affirmation increased how much time participants spent reading the charity materials as well as how much they actually donated to the cause, particularly in the case of male participants (i.e., low-identifiers). In another study, we directly measured participants’ construal of others’ misfortunes. We provided student participants with materials about a program to help business school students in need. We found that self-affirmation made non-business major students (i.e., low-identifiers) less likely to downplay the hardships of the business school students in need. In two further studies, we found that affirmed individuals perceive other consumers’ distress from product and service failures as more intense than did non-affirmed individuals. The findings were disseminated at the invited talk at the National University of Singapore in 2014; they were also included in a paper that is under the second round of review at Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin. Objective 3. Examine the effectiveness of advertisements in social networks In two studies, we presented participants with advertisements, including real consumer reviews from Amazon.com. We found that affirmed consumers, compared to non-affirmed participants, perceived the reviewers’ distress from their negative purchasing experience to be more intense. In three other studies, we used charitable messages from real charity foundations (e.g., Kids-In-Danger and Change.org), and we found that participants were more likely to comply with the charitable messages when they were affirmed, because affirmed participants estimated that the victims felt greater pain. These findings indicate that advertisements appealing to consumers’ empathy toward others’ misfortunes will be more effective when consumers are self-affirmed. The above findings were disseminated at the invited talk at the National University of Singapore in 2014. Compared to the other four objectives, this objective is relatively under-achieved, because we did not find direct empirical evidence showing what kinds of advertisements are likely to “go viral” in consumers’ social networks. In some studies, we only measured participants’ “intention” to share charitable messages in their social networks, rather than their real behaviors. We will attempt to examine consumers’ real Facebook behaviors in order to test whether self-affirmation can enhance consumers’ sharing of charitable messages on their Facebook website. Objective 4. Explore possible moderators of the self-affirmation effect In several studies, we found that the self-affirmation effect was stronger among people who are more motivated to ignore other’s misfortunes (i.e., low-identifiers), because they will feel a greater need to ego-defensively justify their ignorance in order to avoid negative implications for the self. For example, self-affirmation was more effective in increasing WOM intentions to support a charity that addressed defective products for children among participants without children (low-identifiers) than among those with children (i.e., high-identifiers). Similarly, self-affirmation was more effective in enhancing intentions to support business students in need among non-business majors than among business majors, and it was more effective in increasing real donations to support a breast-cancer-related charity among male participants than among female participants. These findings are included in a paper that is under the second round of review at Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin. Objective 5. Developing new methods to change consumers’ sense of self We developed a more practically meaningful way to manipulate self-affirmation. As part of our attempt to adopt a more ecologically valid task, we tested this newly developed manipulation in several laboratory experiments. Unlike the classic essay-based self-affirmation task, the new manipulation task, which consists of multiple-choice questions, can be more easily embedded in consumer surveys. The findings were disseminated at the invited talk at the National University of Singapore in 2014. Although prior work on self-affirmation has focused on reminding of long-held values such as religion and creativity to participants, affirmed sense of self can be experienced via other methods. For example, one important aspect of sense of self is stability of the self. Some people might believe that their sense of self regarding personality or intelligence is stable through life (entity theory), whereas others believe it is malleable (incremental theory). We found that people who believe that their sense of self is malleable (vs. fixed) are more self-affirmed and thus are less vulnerable to setbacks in their lives and less likely to display various ego-defensive behaviors (e.g., giving up on a task). This finding is included in a paper published in Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin in 2015. We also found that individuals’ sense of self can be threatened even in the absence of a real person. Specifically, when a computerized helper in a computer game had humanlike features, consumers avoided seeking useful help so as to protect their sense of self (e.g., autonomy), even when receiving help could improve their performance. In such situations, a self-affirmation task was effective in reducing individuals’ ego-defensive behaviors. The findings were published in Journal of Consumer Research in 2016.

799813.label: Major findings and research outcome
799813.value: We found that self-affirmation can increase consumers’ willingness to share information about others’ hardships (e.g., negative consumption experiences) in their social networks (e.g., Facebook). The findings were included in a paper that is currently under the second round of review at Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin. We examined consumers’ enjoyment of a computer game under self-threats (i.e., the opposite of a self-affirmed state) and found that consumers enjoyed a computer game less when their sense of self, particularly felt autonomy, was threatened by a computerized helper imbued with humanlike features. The findings were published in Journal of Consumer Research (2016). We found that self-affirmation leads consumers to be more likely to pay attention to others’ hardships and less likely to ego-defensively construe those hardships as commonplace. These findings were included in a paper that is currently under the second round of review at Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin. We found that the positive effect of self-affirmation (e.g., reducing ego-defensive processing of others’ misfortunes) is stronger among people who are more motivated to ignore other’s misfortunes (i.e., low-identifiers), who will feel a greater need to ego-defensively justify their ignorance to avoid negative implications for the self. These findings were included in a paper that is currently under the second round of review at Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin. We found that individuals’ sense of self can be threatened even in the absence of a real person. Specifically, when a computerized helper in a computer game was imbued with humanlike features, consumers did not seek useful help to protect their sense of self (e.g., autonomy) even when receiving such help could improve their performance. The findings were published in Journal of Consumer Research (2016). We found that people who believe their sense of self is malleable are more self-affirmed and less likely to display various ego-defensive behaviors (e.g., giving up on a task or avoiding useful help). The finding is included in a paper published in Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin in 2015.

799813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
799813.value: The current research focuses on consumers’ estimates of others’ distress from negative experiences. However, does self-affirmation also influence estimates of others’ happiness from positive experiences? The answer may depend on whether others’ happiness can evoke self-threats; future research can explore under what circumstances this can occur. In addition, future research can examine others’ misfortunes with different levels of severity. Whereas we focused on relatively intense suffering of others, including harm to children and cancer, future research can examine whether the self-affirmation effect occurs with relatively mild misfortunes of others. Future research can also explore whether self-affirmation can increase the accuracy of the estimates of others’ emotions. Our findings that self-affirmation reduces ego-defensive downplaying of others’ misfortunes do not necessarily suggest that self-affirmed individuals’ estimation is more accurate. Examining this question will further increase our understanding of the role of self-affirmation in emotional perspective taking. Future research can also find other ways to affirm the sense of self. In this research, we investigated how individuals’ implicit theories (incremental vs. entity theories) are associated with their sense of self. Discovering other ways to either manipulate or measure self-affirmation will be helpful in providing more practical and theoretical implications.

799813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
799813.value: In this project, we examined how one’s sense of self can influence estimations of others’ emotions and change consumer experiences. In different papers, we examined affirmed and threatened states of the self and their different consequences. Specifically, in a paper under the second round of review at Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin, we examined how self-affirmation can enhance people’s willingness to spread the word about others’ misfortunes. This paper contributes to the literature on self-affirmation by identifying charitable giving as a new downstream consequence of self-affirmation. In a paper published in Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin (2015), we examined how beliefs about one’s own intelligence as a fixed versus malleable trait can influence individuals’ sense of self and how they react to setbacks. This research contributes to the literature on self-affirmation by identifying a new antecedent to an affirmed sense of self (i.e., malleable beliefs about intelligence). In a paper published in Journal of Consumer Research (2016), we examined how self-threats (e.g., threatened autonomy) can occur in the absence of other people when a product has humanlike features. This paper contributes to the literature on self-affirmation by identifying a new antecedent of self-threats (i.e., a humanized product).

809813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
809813.value: The purpose of this study is to synthesize the functionalized-graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) by a newly developed in-situ ultrasonic spray induced gas phase functionalization approach under pyrolysis, in order to enhance their photocatalytic ability for air purification. Photocatalytic degradation of pollutants to nontoxic CO2 and H2O under visible light irradiation (43% of the incoming solar energy) has been regarded as one of the best green strategies to solve the pollution problem. Recently, non-oxide-type photocatalysts, particularly graphitic carbon nitrides (g-C3N) are proven to be active under visible light irradiation. This finding opens up important new possibilities for solar-driven photocatalysts for environmental purification. Although significant efforts have been devoted to develop stable and efficient g-C3N4, their efficiencies are not high enough for practical applications. The low efficiencies may be attributed to their low surface areas or poor crystallinity. In addition, the catalytic, electronic and optical properties of the g-C3N4 are by principle adjustable, using the rich chemistry of carbon and nitrogen. Several studies have been conducted to bind or intercalate different compounds or metals into the matrix, which provides a convenient means of fine-tuning the structure and reactivity of g-C3N4. However, the homogeneity in the distribution of dopants/binded compounds into/on the g-C3N4 matrix have never been reported, which is ultimately important for the interfacial transfer and scavenge of the photo-generated charges, hence increasing the photocatalytic efficiency. We propose a three-year study to (i)synthesize the g-C3N with high crystallinity and large surface area by pyrolysis under controlled conditions, (ii)modify the g-C3N with functional species, which are homogeneous distributed by a newly developed in-situ ultrasonic spray induced gas-phase functionalization method, (iii)investigate the effects of spray aerosol with functional species on the formation of g-C3N under pyrolysis (iv)evaluate the photocatalytic performance of functionalized g-C3N in the degradation of air pollutants such as nitrogen oxygen and formaldehyde under visible light and (v)interpret their degradation mechanism of such air pollutants. A particular scientific focus of this study is the simultaneous formation and modification of g-C3N4 in a single step. Our previous works suggested g-C3N can be prepared with good surface area, crystallinity and enhanced activity by pyrolysis. The newly developed in-situ ultrasonic spray induced gas-phase functionalization is expected to further improve the homogeneity distribution of functional atoms or groups in the matrix or surface of g-C3N4 during the formation. The effect of spray aerosol on the formation of g-C3N4 during pyrolysis method will firstly be studied. 人們平均有七成以上時間是在室內環境中度過的。室內空氣的質量對人類的身體健康有著直接影響，光催化已顯示為一種有前途及有效的空氣除污 、淨化和脫臭的技術。現時不少空氣清新機均採用光催化技術，透過利用紫外線及二氧化鈦光催化物料，產生極活躍的 氫氧基，降解空氣中的污染物，例如: 裝修材料及傢俬所釋放的甲醛及揮發性有機化合物，減少對眼睛及呼吸氣管等過敏情況。傳統的光催化劑如二氧化鈦，只能被紫外光激發，而且，光催化物料的表面面積相對較低，降解空氣污染物的效能亦較低，為了提升光催化技術的效能及應用，何博士將利用三年時間，研究可利用「可見光」（即日光、室內燈光）取代傳統的「紫外光」作為光催化過程的能量來源的光催化劑---氮化碳(Carbon Nitride)，並透過不同化學改良方法，提高其在光催化過程中的效能，從而縮短降解空氣污染物的時間，大幅提高空氣淨化系統的潔淨效能，而且更有利於相關技術在日常生活的應用。

809813.label: Realisation of objectives
809813.value: As shown below, research activities related to the objectives have been done, including (i) the synthesis of functionalized visible-light-driven photocatalysts, i.e. graphitic carbon nitride by using nitrogen-rich precursors using different approaches mentioned in the proposal; (ii) improving the physical and chemical properties such as surface area and crystallinity of the g- C3N4 by the optimization of the preparation conditions as well as modification of g-C3N4 with functional species by different approaches; (iii) evaluation the photocatalytic performance of functionalized g-C3N4 in the degradation of air pollutants such as NOx under visible light and their degradation mechanism of such air pollutants. (I)Enhanced visible-light-driven photocatalytic removal of NO: Effect on layer distortion on g-C3N4 by H2 heating We reported a simple strategy for realizing the tunable structure distortion of graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) layers by H2 post calcination to improve the intrinsic electronic structure and the photocatalytic performances of g-C3N4 samples. In comparison with the O2 or N2 post treatment, the H2-modified g-C3N4 developed new optical absorption above 460 nm and enhanced photocatalytic activity for NO removal. The combined characterization results reveal that H2heating induced the structure distortion of g-C3N4 layers is originated from the creation of amino groups within the structure and generation of the strong hydrogen bonding interactions between layers. The distorted structure allows electron transitions in g-C3N4 to increase visible-light absorption. The structure distortion also enables more electrons to be available for initiating the photocatalytic reaction and the separation of photogenerated charge carriers in g-C3N4. This work provides a simple strategy for realizing the tunable structure distortion of g-C3N4 layers to adjust its electronic structure and photocatalysis. (II) Copolymerization with 2,4,6-Triaminopyrimidine for the Rolling-up the Layer Structure, Tunable Electronic Properties, and Photocatalysis of g‑C3N4 Copolymerization with 2,4,6-triaminopyrimi- dine (TAP) is developed for precise substitution of one nitrogen with carbon atom in the triazine ring of polymeric g- C3N4. Direct incorporation of C4N2 ring from TAP into the network retains the structural features of g- C3N4, but induces the rolling-up of g-C3N4 sheets into tubular configuration. The band gap energy is narrowed from 2.7 to 2.4 eV by a negative shift of valence band of the g-C3N4 photocatalyst, which enhances charge-carrier migration and separation, leading to higher photocatalytic activity for NO gas pollutant removal. It is attributed to the decrease of the π- deficiency and the generation of imbalanced electron density in π-electron conjugated units of g-C3N4 by TAP incorporation. This work provides a significant technique for precise control of heteroatom in the framework of g-C3N4 to finely adjust its intrinsic electronic properties and its photocatalytic properties. (III) Facile synthesis of porous graphene-like carbon nitride (C6N9H3) with excellent photocatalytic activity for NO removal We reported the possible synthesis of a new porous graphene-like carbon nitride (C6N9H3) by simply adding hydrochloric acid in the precursor of block g-C3N4. The formation of the porous graphene-like C6N9H3 can be attributed to the change in the thermal condensation modal of the precursor and the acidic condition induced by Cl− and H+. The photocatalytic activity of the samples was evaluated by the removal of NO under visible light illumination. We found that the porous graphene-like C6N9H3 exhibited enhanced photocatalytic activity compared to the block g-C3N4.We also researched the removal mechanism and found that the removal ofNOin our systems was due to the synergic effect of h+ and •O2 .This study could shed light on the design of efficient photocatalysts and facilitate a deep understanding of the NO removal mechanism through photocatalytic technology. (IV) Sulfur-doped g-C3N4 with enhanced photocatalytic CO2-reduction Performance In this study, sulfur-doped g-C3N4 was fabricated by simply calcinating thiourea at 520 ◦C. Sulfur-doped g-C3N4 (TCN) was found to absorb light up to 475 nm corresponding to a band gap of 2.63 eV, which was narrower than that of un-doped g-C3N4 (MCN) with a band gap of 2.7 eV. First principle calculations based on spin-polarized density functional theory were utilized to investigate the theoretical partial density of states of the TCN and MCN, indicating that the band gaps of TCN and MCN were the same, but impurities existed in the TCN sample. Consequently, photogenerated electrons could easily jump from the impurity state to the conduction band or from the valence band to the impurity state. PL spectrum analysis and transient photocurrent responses were also carried out to verify the suggested photocatalysis mechanism. (V) Enhancing the photocatalytic activity of bulk g-C3N4 by introducing mesoporous structure and hybridizing with graphene Bulk graphitic carbon nitride (CN) suffers from small surface area and high recombination of charge carriers, which results in low photocatalytic activity. To enhance the activity of g-C3N4, the surface area should be enlarged and charge carrier separation should be promoted. In this work, a combined strategy was employed to dramatically enhance the activity of bulk g-C3N4 by simultaneously introducing mesoporous structure and hybridizing with graphene/graphene oxide. The mesoporous g-C3N4/graphene (MCN-G) and mesoporous g-C3N4/graphene oxide (MCN-GO) nanocomposites with enhanced photocatalytic activity were fabricated via a facile sonochemicalmethod. The visible light-harvesting ability of MCN-G and MCN-GO hybrids was enhanced and the conduction band was negatively shifted when 1.0 wt% graphene/graphene oxide was incorporated into the matrix of MCN. As electronic conductive channels, the G/GO sheets could efficiently facilitate the separation of chare carriers. MCN-G and MCN-GO exhibited drastically enhanced visible light photocatalytic activity toward NO removal. This enhanced photocatalytic activity could be attributed to the increased surface area and pore volume, improved visible light utilization, enhanced reduction power of electrons, and promoted separation of charge carriers. (VI) Metal-free disinfection effects induced by graphitic carbon nitride polymers under visible light illumination Covalent carbon nitride polymers were applied as metal-free robust catalysts for the inactivation of Escherichia coli K-12 (E. coli), a common Gram-negative bacterium, under visible light illumination. The results demonstrated that the creation of antibacterial function on the surface of conjugated polymers has now become possible. In summary, a graphitic carbon nitride polymer was found to be an effective, recyclable catalyst for bacterial inactivation in water under visible light irradiation, without any bacterial regrowth. The study of the mechanism indicates that the performance of bacterial inactivation could be related to light-induced holes on the surface of carbon nitride. Further electronic and textural modifications such as co-polymerization, doping and morphology engineering of thin films/ coatings are expected to produce a series of soft functional materials for environmental disinfection. (VII) Mechanism of NO Photocatalytic Oxidationon g-C3N4 Was Changed by Pd-QDs Modification Quantum dot (QD) sensitization can increase the light absorption and electronic transmission of photocatalysts. However, limited studies have been conducted on the photocatalytic activity of photocatalysts after modification by noble metal QDs. In this study, we developed a simple method for fabricating Pd-QD-modified g-C3N4. Results showed that the modification of Pd-QDs can improve the NO photocatalytic oxidation activity of g-C3N4. The Pd-QD modification changed the NO oxidation mechanism from the synergistic action of h+ and O2_ to the single action of _ OH. We found that the main reason for the mechanism change was that Pd-QD modification changed the molecular oxygen activation pathway from single-electron reduction to two-electron reduction. It favored the visible light absorption of g-C3N4, but also improved the separation efficiency of photogenerated carriers and, thus, enhanced the NO photocatalytic oxidation activity.

809813.label: Major findings and research outcome
809813.value: The major finding of our study is the simultaneous formation and modification of graphitic carbon nitrides in a single step. In order to chemically modify the g-C3N4, different kind of elements were doped into the photocatalysts during the formation of g-C3N4, which is an effective strategy for tuning physicochemical properties of the parent materials and extends their applications. We tailored the texture and surface chemical properties, as well as the electronic properties of traditional photocatalysis. This heteroatom doping strategy was applied to tune the carbon nitride materials. Different dopant sources of noble metals, metals, non-metals and transition metals were added during the formation of carbon nitride by pyrolysis of thiourea or urea. In this strategy, additive was added before the lattice was formed, and heteroatoms such as different types of non-metals or other grafts will be incorporated into the matrix in-situ. This in-situ doping approach can also be extended to incorporate other heteroatoms by changing the anion or cation of precursors into C,N-based materials, which opens up the possibility of designer material synthesis for specific applications. We believe that the use of this facile one-step functionalization approach to fabricate the doped metal-free, organic, semiconducting polymer as a catalyst with high surface area and crystallinity for air purification makes the solar-driven reactions for environmental purification interesting from both an economic and environmental point of view. We also successfully (i) enhanced visible-light-driven photocatalytic efficiency of g-C3N4 on NO removal through layer distortion by H2 heating; studied the rolling-up layer Structure, tunable electronic properties and photocatalysis of g‑C3N4 via copolymerization with 2,4,6-triaminopyrimidine; (iii) Facile syntheszed the porous graphene-like carbon nitride (C6N9H3) with excellent photocatalytic activity for NO removal; (iv) doped sulphur with g-C3N4 with enhanced photocatalytic CO2-reduction performance; (v) Enhanced the photocatalytic activity of bulk g-C3N4 by introducing mesoporous structure and hybridizing with graphene; (vi) investigated metal-free disinfection effects induced by graphitic carbon nitride polymers under visible light illumination; and (vii) studied the changed mechanism of NO photocatalytic oxidation on g-C3N4 by Pd-QDs modification. All of the above research results have been published in different international journals mentioned in Part C.

809813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
809813.value: The unique structure of C3N4 materials makes the polymer possess highly stable with respect to thermal and chemical attack, and an appealing electronic structure, being a medium-bandgap, indirect semiconductor. This allows its direct use as a multifunctional heterogeneous metal-free catalyst. In addition, the catalytic, electronic and optical properties of the structure are by principle adjustable, using the rich chemistry of carbon and nitrogen. Many organic, inorganic compounds or metals could bind or intercalate into the matrix and provide a convenient means of fine-tuning the structure and reactivity of g-C3N4. In this study, doping of functional atoms or groups in the matrix or surface of the carbon nitride during the formation of g-C3N4 not only has good crystallinity and high surface area, it also undoubtedly greatly improved its performance and expanded applications. In the future, further modification of this functionalized metal-free, organic, semiconducting polymer as a catalyst for the degradation of other air pollutants such as VOCs will also open new possibilities to form different hybrid C3N4 materials with new and probably exciting applications in solar-driven photocatalytic environmental purification. Other potential applications of this new material can be energy conversion, hydrogen and carbon dioxide storage, solar cells, humidity and gas sensors.

809813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
809813.value: Photocatalytic degradation of pollutants using solar energy has been regarded as one of the best green strategies to solve the pollution problem. Recently, graphitic carbon nitride has attracted much attention owing to its visible-light-driven photocatalytic activity for environmental purification, chemical stability, and photostability. In this project, we (i) synthesized the graphitic carbon nitrides with high crystallinity and large surface area under controlled conditions; (ii) modified the graphitic carbon nitrides with different functional species in order to enhance their efficiency, (iii) evaluated the photocatalytic performance of functionalized graphitic carbon nitrides in the degradation of air pollutants under visible light and (iv) interpreted their degradation mechanism of such air pollutants. The most attractive feature of this our study is that in-situ chemical modification through different precursors such as metal salts or dopants can be occurred during the fabrication of graphitic carbon nitride. Different approaches were also used for increasing their crystallinity and surface area or enhancing their photocatalytic properties through functionalization on the g-C3N4. The newly developed visible light-driven g-C3N4 showed significantly improved visible light photocatalytic activity. The superior physical and chemical properties of these new materials allow expectation of significant visible-light-driven photocatalytic degradation of air pollutant such as nitric oxides.

809913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
809913.value: This project focuses on the theories, applications, and implications of stochastic covariance among risky assets no dynamic mean-variance portfolio selection (MVPS) and asset-liability management (ALM). There is strong evidence that correlations among risky assets are randomly changing over time. Hence, researchers have used the Wishart process to model the stochastic dynamics of covariance matrix. This approach has gained financial and statistical interests in recent years. When the stochastic covariance model is applied to precommitment dynamic MVPS problems, this project shows that the solution is related to a backward stochastic differential equation (BSDE) in which the solution can be linked to an exponential affine form. The uniqueness of the solution to the BSDE is also addressed through the theory of decoupled forward-BSDE. This framework is then extended to ALM by incorporating uncontrollable insurance liabilities and diffusion liabilities. In addition, this project solves the time-consistent MVPS problem with stochastic covariance matrix and extends it to ALM problems. Asymptotic analysis is carried out to deduce the economic interpretation of the model under stressed situations. Empirical studies are performed to validate the use of the developed theories and verify the deduced economic properties. 此專案集中研究動態均值方差之投資組合及資產負債管理的理論、應用和其隨機共變數的影響。由於有很多學術文獻指出高風險資產之間的相關系數會隨著時間隨機改變。因而，有學者利用威夏爾特過程作為隨機動態共變數矩陣的模型。此專案主要利用倒向隨機微分方程找出此隨機共變數矩陣模型於預先承諾動態之問題的解。從而擴展於動態均值方差之投資組合及資產負債管理在“時間一致”上的情況。最後，利用漸近分析和實證研究此模型的經濟性質及經濟理論。

809913.label: Major findings and research outcome
809913.value: When the variance-covariance matrix follows a stochastic process maintaining the positivity of the matrix, the optimal trading strategy is very different from the classic result of assuming a deterministic variance-covariance matrix. However, closed-form solutions are still obtained for many practical situations, including the consideration of asset-liability management ([2], [11]), the situations of pre-commitment ([1], [4]) and time-consistent strategies ([3], [6]). The application covers many asset classes such as interest rates ([1], [9], [10]), longevity securities ([3]), insurance risk ([2], [7]), and commodities ([5]). However, the stochastic variance-covariance matrix also requires additional conditions to make the trading strategy stable (non-blow-up). The stability is important for the verification theorem if the optimisation is based on the HJB framework. In [2], [4] and [7], we discuss the verification theorems under different situations in detail. The conclusion is that one has to choose a shorter investment horizon to ensure a stable optimal control. The analysis is based on some asymptotic approach. The asymptotic analysis uncovers the risk associated with the estimation error for the variance-covariance matrix in continuous-time finance. Using the asymptotic result associated with the Wishart distribution of the variance-covariance matrix, we propose and prove the use of a big data technique to process real-time financial data for portfolio optimisation purpose [8]. Not only mathematical proof is given but also a series of empirical evidence. When the information is insufficient to estimate parameters accurately, we incorporate model ambiguity to the project as in [12]. It is clearly a future research direction of mine.

809913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
809913.value: There are several future developments from this project. 1. Although empirical analysis on the stochastic model and the economic implication of the strategy are provided in this project, it remains to test for the empirical performance in the sense of statistical arbitrage, which concept is detailed in [6]. 2. Our big data technique is constructed and proven for the pre-commitment mean-variance strategy. We are planning to work on its time-consistent extension. 3. This project does not consider additional market constraints such as position limit, no-shorting, and consumption. These are promising theoretical extensions. 4. Model uncertainly and ambiguity are recent hot topics. Robust pre-commitment and time-consistent strategies subject to stochastic variance-covariance matrix seem to be very interesting too.

809913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
809913.value: Optimal investment strategy is a longstanding problem in finance. An important issue is the randomness and uncertainty of information from the financial data. Traditional approach quantifies the randomness through the variances and covariances of returns of financial securities. This project addresses the issue that the variances and covariances themselves are full of randomness too. It develops several practical solutions to improve investment outcome by taking into account of the randomness of the variances and covariances. The framework is justified mathematically, tested empirically and implemented efficiently. The project also addresses the potential use of the mathematical formulas in the big data environment of the modern financial market. In addition to the aforementioned advantages of the mathematical and statistical approach, this project also offers reasonable conditions under which the investment strategy can be implemented stably. The conditions provide insight into the favourable market regime and the investment horizon.

840013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
840013.value: As a key measure to strengthen the implementation of inclusive education in Hong Kong, government-supported schools were given an additional vice principal’s position to include the roles of a special educational needs coordinator (SENCO) beginning in the 2008-2009 school year. The SENCOs are a new tier of middle leaders in a vital position to change and restructure the schools for effective implementation of inclusive education. To this date, however, only one small-scale qualitative study has examined the establishment of the SENCOs and the results suggested that four years into the policy, SENCOs fell short in delivering expected effects and outcomes. Thus, this study attempts to confirm these issues territory-wide and examine ways by which they may be overcome. Attempting to offer theoretical and practical insights into SENCO leadership in building inclusive schools, the proposed project will involves two phases adopting both qualitative and quantitative research methods. The first phase consists of qualitative case studies that examine and triangulate from principals, SENCOs, and members of student support teams from 12 primary and secondary schools on (a) the ways in which SENCOs exert leadership and relevant contributing factors; (b) the ways in which SENCOs are limited in leadership and contributing factors, and (c) the considerations and suggestions respondents have for effective leadership of SENCOs. Data from the case studies, together with the existing literature and findings from the pilot study, will be used to finalize the territory-wide quantitative questionnaire survey in the second phase of the study. Anticipated findings will map the similarities and differences across primary and secondary schools in Hong Kong with regard to the implementation of the SENCO policy and its effects. Through capturing a fuller picture of SENCO leadership in inclusive education, the project will ultimately facilitate the development of new conceptions and possible reinterpretation of the models of SENCO leadership in Hong Kong, and serve as a Hong Kong data set for comparing the implementation of SENCO policy with that in the UK. This study is significant in its implications for informing policy and practice on how best to integrate inclusive schooling into mainstream schools, leadership training needs, and future research in this area. 自2008-09學年起, 政府資助的學校獲增配多一個副校長職位以擔任「特殊教育统筹主任」的角色, 作為加強實施香港融合教育的一個重要措施。特殊教育统筹主任作為學校新的中層領導，負責改變和重組學校, 以使融合教育實施得更為有效。但到目前為止, 只有一個小規模的質性研究去檢視該措施的實施情況。而且研究結果表明， 自措施實行的四年內，該措施還未能達到預期的效果和成果。因此，是次研究希望能全港性地確認上述問題, 並驗證此問題的不同解決方法。本研究分成兩個階段，分別從質性和量性的研究法，試圖為以此措施建設融合教育學校提供理論性及實用性的洞見。研究第一階段採用質性個案研究法，檢驗十二所中小學的校長、特殊教育统筹主任、以及學生支援團隊的成員，探究（一）特殊教育统筹主任以何種方式發揮領導能力及與其相關的因素；（二）限制特殊教育统筹主任發揮其領導能力及與其相關的因素；（三）受訪者對於特殊教育统筹主任發揮有效領導力的考慮及建議。根據個案研究收集到的資料、前期研究發現及現有文獻，會被用作修訂最終的全港性問卷調查，用於第二階段的研究。預計研究結果將刻劃出, 全港的中小學實施特殊教育统筹主任政策在果效方面的異同。此研究項目透過較為全面的檢驗獲取特殊教育统筹主任領導能力在融合教育方面的情況，終將促進有關特殊教育统筹主任領導能力的新慨念發展, 及可能重新詮釋香港特殊教育统筹主任領導力能的理論模型。同時，所得數據亦可作為香港實施特殊教育统筹主任政策的參考, 及與英國的相同政策作對比研究。是次研究將對如何有效地制定及實施於主流學校內的融合教育、領導能力的培訓需要、及將來的相關研究, 皆有正面積極的作用。

840013.label: Realisation of objectives
840013.value: Though a smaller sample of participants was approved by the RGC due to limited funds, eight instead of six principals and SENCOs were interviewed during the project period. Together with the ones interviewed during the pilot stage just before the project period, all resource school principals and their SENCOs as well as four additional principals of general schools were interviewed for the qualitative component. Group interviews of teachers of student support teams involved 42 teachers as planned and proposed. As for the quantitative component, questionnaires were sent to 100 primary and 100 secondary schools in addition to resource schools as planned. The response rate was just below 50% after follow-up calls with 50 primary schools and 49 secondary schools returning the questionnaires. The number of teacher respondents was 504 and the number of SENCOs was 48 from primary schools. As for secondary schools, the number of teacher respondents was 356 with 49 SENCOs. Together, a total of 860 teachers and 99 SENCOs responded to the questionnaire, 163 less than targeted. The lower number appeared to be related to the high workload of school staff who found it difficult to spare time to respond to the questionnaire. Some of the school personnel also informed us during our follow-up phone calls that they received a high volume of questionnaires from various projects and thus took up their spare time. The smaller sample, however, did not seem to affect the results as the results of the 959 respondents across regions and school sectors were rather consistent. Thus, all of the objectives of this study are judged to have been achieved by in-depth interviews of principals and special educational needs coordinators, focus-group interviews with student support team members, meeting observations, and the territory-wide survey designed based on the qualitative data and the existing literature. The first three objectives (how the purposes and outcomes of the SENCO policy toward inclusive education were perceived, how SENCOs practiced their leadership in implementing inclusive education, and how to support SENCO leadership) were targeted in both interviews, observations, and surveys. The qualitative and quantitative data were compared as well. The final objective (examining the way forward for effective SENCO role) was partly achieved by inserting appropriate questions in interviews and items in the surveys, and partly by drawing insight from data. Though it was approved to cut in half the sample size of the qualitative component, participants of the original sample size was Results of this study came from a smaller sample than originally planned because of the substantially smaller amount of funds appropriated for the study. Even though the data sources may have come from a smaller sample, data appeared to be consistent across regions and types of schools (primary and secondary). Results have offered adequate insight into participants’ perceptions of the SENCO policy for inclusive education, SENCOs’ leadership practices, conditions necessary to support and challenge SENCO leadership, and the way forward for the successful roles of SENCOs.

840013.label: Major findings and research outcome
840013.value: Major findings of this study are threefold: (1) an emerging relationship schema of effective leadership attributes; (2) dilemmas arisen from principals’ unilateral decision making to participate in inclusive education versus the need to form partnership with teacher leaders during implementation; and (3) teacher leaders’ needs and measures that can sustain their leadership in inclusive education. Three main sets of effective leadership attributes were revealed: (a) demonstrating a clear vision; (b) forming a close partnership with teacher leaders; and (c) creating conditions to sustain teacher leadership. These attributes must be substantiated by what was termed as the foundational attributes to be effective, suggesting an emerging relationship schema of among them. Teacher leaders perceived their principals as having a vision only when the vision was effectuated by: (a) principals’ ability to communicate their vision clearly including implications for school staff and confronting problems during implementation; (b) principals’ adequate knowledge of inclusive schooling to prove that they really understood their vision; and (c) principals’ perseverance to reach the goals of their vision. In addition, teacher leaders considered principals’ ability to build a close partnership with them as a foundation for them to take leadership roles. They entailed the basis for partnership formation: (a) role modeling, (b) sharing decision making, and (c) sensitivity to their needs. The last set of attributes focused on principals’ ability to create two conditions to sustain teacher leaders’ roles: empowerment by a formal leadership position and stable staffing to allow time for professional development. With regard to leadership dilemmas, findings from principals revealed two context-specific dilemmas: (a) struggling between benefits and issues of participating in inclusive education and (b) unilateral decisions versus need for partnership. The first dilemma caused struggles in the decision making process while the second created obstacles for implementation and required measures to bring changes and move toward effective practices. Principals’ decisions to participate in inclusive education were affected by three dimensions. The first two dimensions led to their decisions to participate: (a) the need to have more students to avoid potential closure of their schools due to low birth rate in Hong Kong and (b) the need to enhance relationships with the Education Bureau. The last dimension of increased parental rejection to enroll their children without disabilities in those schools drew a dilemma when placed in the contexts of the first two dimensions.

840013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
840013.value: As an exploratory study to examine the understanding, practices, and challenges, of SENCO leadership, this study can be further developed and the course of action is proposed as follows: (a) examining how schools recognized as effective inclusive schools practice the 3-tier intervention model under the current policy for inclusive education as the next step to further develop the current study; (b) identifying elements or factors that lead to high student outcomes; (c) setting common criteria for measuring student outcomes and beginning a database to compare the student outcomes through a longitudinal study; and (d) using data collected to inform policies for inclusive education, school and SENCO leadership training, teacher education programs, and school practices. The PI has already submitted another GRF proposal to examine various aspects of the 3-tier intervention model as a follow up.

840013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
840013.value: Most research on middle leadership in schools has been carried out in UK. To this date, the Education Bureau has not published data regarding SENCOs’ work in Hong Kong schools. Therefore, this study represents a significant effort to understand how school leaders, SENCOs, and other teachers conceptualize the role of SENCOs, their involvement in shaping changes for inclusive practices, the school contexts that affect the way in which they play their roles, and challenges they have encountered in Hong Kong schools. Through capturing a fuller picture of SENCO leadership in inclusive education, the project has the following significance and values: (a) offering empirical evidence to facilitate the development of a theory of middle leadership for inclusion in the Chinese context, (b) providing some indicators of effective SENCO leadership to be used for school and SENCO self-evaluation, (c) facilitating international comparison of leadership discourse and practices for inclusive education in the era of globalization, (d) informing policymakers, teacher educators, and school personnel about the current and potential roles of SENCOs, and (e) generating knowledge to contribute to leadership preparation and professional development programs.

840313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
840313.value: The globalization of higher education increases opportunities for students from different cultures to study in new cultural contexts. To be successful, international students must adapt psychologically and socioculturally to their host context. An understanding of students’ psychological and sociocultural adaptation is critical to reduce student stress and help them cope (Misra & Castillo, 2004). It can also assist institutions attract and better support a culturally diverse range of students. While study of international student acculturation is complex, it needs exploring, particularly in Asian contexts (Spencer-Oatey & Xiong, 2006) This study is grounded in cross-cultural psychology (Shiraev & Levy, 2010). The purposes are to find out those factors that affect the psychological and sociocultural adaptation of international students to study in Hong Kong. In so doing certain comparisons i.e., academic self-efficacy and psychological adaptation will be made with local students. In addition it will explore the level and effect of contact between local and international students, and international student views of social and institutional support with regard to their adaptation, and their academic self-efficacy. A mixed method sequential approach involving focus group discussions, interviews and questionnaire surveys will be used. Student focus groups from four of the eight HKSAR government-funded higher education institutions will pilot the questionnaires. Using student feedback, changes will be made to the surveys and questions stemming from pilot discussions will be appended to a questionnaire that includes Ward and Kennedy’s (1999) Sociocultural Adaptation Scale. To measure psychological adaptation, students will also complete Zung’s (1965) Self-Rating Depression Scale. These instruments can be easily adapted to provide psychometrically sound measures (Spencer-Oatey & Xiong, 2006). To allow comparison between local and international students, a sample of 2000 international and 1000 local students from the four institutions will be recruited to participate. Focus group discussions will follow completion of the questionnaires to obtain further descriptive data. Data from focus group discussions and questionnaires will be collected at predetermined intervals of 3, 6 and 12 months over a two-year period. The study focus and Asian context make this study distinctive within the field. The findings will not only strengthen empirical understandings but will provide critical data for use by Hong Kong and other Asian higher education institutions in their support of international students.

840313.label: Realisation of objectives
840313.value: The study adopted quantitative and qualitative research methods, based on a questionnaire survey and focus-group discussions conducted among local, Mainland and international students studying in six-UGC funded universities in Hong Kong. Ethical approval was obtained from the human research ethics committee at the University. We first contacted stakeholders in the eight public universities in Hong Kong to seek their help on publicizing our research. Six out of eight UGC-funded universities agreed to participate and directed us to get in touch with relevant offices that could help us send out the “Call for Participants” email. In the email, a link to an on-line survey was included so that if the students were willing to participate, they could click on the link and be directed to the website of the survey on Survey Monkey. Meanwhile, hardcopies of the questionnaires were sent to classrooms where course teachers were willing to assist in the distribution of the questionnaires. A lucky draw was conducted in order to reward the participants who completed the questionnaire. Data collection lasted from September 2015 to February 2016. After collecting survey data from each university, we compiled a list of participants who had indicated their willingness to participate in the focus groups. Due to the limited number of survey participants from two universities, we decided to only conduct focus groups with participants from the remaining four universities. With the generous administrative support from four universities, we conducted focus groups in meeting rooms or classrooms separately at each university. Each focus group lasted around sixty minutes. Given the participants’ linguistic backgrounds, we chose either Canoness, Putonghua or English as the communication language in all the focus groups. After conducting each focus group, we transcribed and translated the discussions immediately. In total, we got 6223 responses to our survey questionnaires which included 3,357 local students, 2,140 Mainland students and 726 international students. We interviewed 124 students across 31 focus groups which included 32 local students, 61 Mainland students, and 31 international students. With these rich data, all the research objectives have been fully addressed. Driven by the data, two papers have been published, one paper is under review, and three papers are under preparation. Besides, the results have been reported in two international conferences and two local conferences, one internal seminar with the attendance of senior management at one university. More importantly, we have completed and submitted four university reports to universities where we got data of both survey and focus group discussions. In the reports, we presented the major findings based on data in each university and made recommendations to policy makers, teaching and administrative staff on how to better support non-local and local students in Hong Kong. We received enthusiastic and positive feedback from the senior management of all the four universities.

840313.label: Major findings and research outcome
840313.value: Comparisons between local, Mainland and international students 1. Significant differences were found when local, Mainland and international students in Hong Kong universities were compared. Generally speaking, Mainland students reported significantly higher levels of psychological adaptation, academic adaptation and academic efficacy, while local students reported the significantly lower levels of academic efficacy and academic adaptation (Yu, July-August 2016). 2. Based on the self-reported friendship networks, we found three social circles were generally formed: among local students, among Mainland students, and among international students (Yu, July-August 2016). 3. Adaptation to an English-medium-of-instruction was a concern for local and Mainland Chinese students, while international students noted that limited English proficiency among other students undermined classroom discussions and led to tensions in group projects (Yu & Wright, 2017). 4. Local students faced challenges in adapting to a wider range of assessment modes and academic writing, while mainland Chinese and international students reported how teacher-student relations and teaching approaches differed from prior educational experiences (Yu & Wright, 2017). 5. For both local and non-local students, English proficiency, social support, academic efficacy and psychological adaptation were significant predictors of academic adaptation (Yu, April 2016). Comparisons between Mainland, Taiwan, South-Asian and Western students 6. South Asian students displayed disadvantages while Mainland students displayed advantages in all the three aspects of adaptation (academic, psychological and socio-cultural) when compared to Taiwan and Western students in Hong Kong (Yu, April 2016). Comparison between Asian and Western international students 7. Asian students displayed more disadvantages in academic self-efficacy, social support, English proficiency and being discriminated than Western students, except for perceived Cantonese proficiency. There was no significant difference in socio-cultural adaptation and contacts with local students (Yu, November 2016). 8. Both Asian and Western international students reported Cantonese proficiency as the major factor and English-language proficiency as the significant factor in their socio-cultural adaptation in Hong Kong.They attributed different weights to the role of academic self-efficacy, social support and contact with local students in predicting the socio-cultural adaptation (Yu, November 2016). 9. Both groups expressed difficulties in integrating into the Hong Kong academic society, and society in general. Both groups reported limited interactions and friendship with local students; their interactions and friendships were primarily with other international students. Both agreed that good language proficiency in English and Cantonese, especially the latter, was important in ensuring a successful socio-cultural adaptation (Yu, November 2016). In-depth study on Mainland students 10. Linguistic adaptation, social network, political identification, and discrimination were the most significant acculturative stressors reported by Mainland students (Yu & Zhang, 2016).

840313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
840313.value: This research serves as groundwork for a three-year (January 2019-December 2021) GRF project proposal submitted to RGC in 2017-18 with the aim to develop a holistic framework to capture the dynamic features and significant predictors of cross-cultural adaptation of non-local students in Hong Kong. This study will inform the literature on international student adaptation in the East Asian context, and offer practical and managerial insights for educational policymakers, university senior management and administrations, academicians and research communities on how to manage the changes and accommodate the needs of non-local students so that we can attract a culturally diverse body of students. In October 2017, I was invited to present my findings at the meeting of International and Greater China Affairs Committee (IGCAC) at the Education University of Hong Kong, which received a lots of interests from senior management in suggesting me on proposing a courses to study-abroad students, and academic and administrative staff whose work involves international students. I also think it is important to develop a course called “Intercultural Communication and Cross-cultural Adaptations” which will incorporate the research findings from this GRF and from my previous studies. Hopefully, this course will be implemented in 2018-19.

840313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
840313.value: The globalization of higher education (HE) is increasing opportunities for students from different cultures to study in new cultural contexts. To be successful, international students must adapt psychologically and socio-culturally to their host countries. To ensure institutions attract, retain and support a culturally diverse range of students, an understanding of their psychological and socio-cultural adaptation is required. However insufficient attention has been paid to the complexities of international student acculturation (Spencer-Oatey & Xiong, 2006) and little is known about how international students adapt to life and study in an Asian context. Grounded in the field of cross-cultural psychology (Shiraev & Levy, 2010) the purpose of this study is, through the use of a mixed method approach involving focus group discussions and questionnaires, to determine factors that affect the psychological and socio-cultural adaptation of international students to life and study in Hong Kong. The study will provide new perspective of how international students from different cultural backgrounds (Mainland vs International; Asian vs Western etc.) adapt to study in Asian higher education institutions. In so doing it will make available information that will impact on higher education policies and practices worldwide and specifically in Asia and Hong Kong.

840513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
840513.value: 二十世紀十年代，本土文學在香港萌芽，香港本地文學又與中國大陸的「新文學」互為影響。本研究嘗試以跨文化角度，深入探討二十至四十年代香港文學評論的流轉，理出早期香港文學的發展脈絡及文化涵意。研究內容圍繞以下項目：文學評論這種文學類型，在香港最初如何成形？早期的文學評論家中，以哪幾位最具代表性？他們的文化背景、文學理念等有何異同？香港的文學評論家在推動本地文學及引入外國文學方面有何貢獻，對內地的文學發展又有沒有影響？另外，早年香港文壇曾發生幾場重要論爭，如三十年代末至四十年代初期，李育中、林煥平等「抗戰文學」的支持者，與主張「和平文學」的文人展開筆戰；1939年，著名詩人徐遲在報章發表了〈抒情的放逐〉一文，掀起關於抒情主義的論爭；1940年，報人楊剛撰文批評香港年輕作者的浪漫主義，引起極大迴響，作家、評論家等紛紛發表談論「新浪漫主義」的文章。深入分析這些評論，不但可勾勒出當時香港文壇的面貌，對瞭解早期香港社會的演變、文化發展等亦大有裨益。

840513.label: Realisation of objectives
840513.value: On the whole the objectives have been well met. The following gives an explanation of how each of the three goals have been approached and realized: 1. Delineate the shape, complexity and characteristic features of the development of literary criticism in Hong Kong before 1949. The PI has attempted to accomplish this task by first building a data bank of early literacy criticisms and related writings, and then carrying out a rigorous process of screening such that the best and most representative critical writings can be selected. Because many of these articles are dated and not of superior quality in terms of printing, much time had been spent in verifying and editing the content. This time-consuming task has been rewarding in two respects. First, by categorizing the articles, sorting out the relationship between them and arranging them in proper order, this field which received little academic attention in the past has to some extent been structuralized. A clearer shape of the development of early literary criticism has emerged, important critics became identifiable and their thinking and ideas more easily understandable. Second, the process has enabled the writer to develop his own viewpoint on the subject. It has helped him grasp the intricacies involved in the topic--from the near impossibility of defining a Hong Kong writer to the tenseful relationship between literary creation and criticism. The PI understood early Hong Kong literature as a dynamic system full of fulfilled and unfulfilled possibilities. He has elaborated his ideas in a range of his articles. 2. Identify the important literary theorists, as well as evaluate the literary and cultural value of their representative critical works. The project has imcorporatd works of many literary theorists. It aims to increase understanding on early critics and writers whose works have not recieved the commendation they deserve. Two examples can be cited here. First, Yuan Chun Ying (袁振英) , a graduate of Hong Kong Queen’s College, published a Chinese translation of Ibsen’s Love’s Comedy in a Hong Kong literary journal in the 1910s. In the 1920s and early 1930s, he wrote a string of articles on Ibsen, Tolstoy and Western philosophical and literary theories. He later participated in the May Fourth New Culture Movement and was much appreciated by Hu Shih (胡適). This member of Hong Kong’s new literature movement shows that Hong Kong played a role in the larger arena of modern Chinese literature and contributed to Chinese understanding of the West in the early years. Second, writer and critic Leung Chi Poon (梁之盤) demonstrated multifaceted talent in his translation, creative writing and literary discussions. He has demonstrated a broad vision, by introducing Western literary trends in his articles. For example, in one of his journal essays he explains the epic tradition in Russia, Britain, India and other foreign countries, and lements the fact that Chinese culture lacks comparable epic works. More important, he founded and was chief editor of Hong Dou (Red Beans 紅豆), one of the most important Hong Kong literary journals in the 1930s. This beautifully conceived journal distinguished itsself by having a strong concern for literary development in foreign countries; it also provided a venue for publication for many young writers who would take up prominent roles in the Hong Kong literary scene, such as Li Yuzhong (李育中), Lu Lun (侶倫), Lu Yishi (路易士), Liu Xiamu (柳下木), and Chen Jiangfan (陳江帆). 3. Investigate the historical and political meaning of the critical texts under review and explain their significance to the socio-intellectual history of pre-1949 Hong Kong. Sorting out and making sense of the abundant materials that have been collected was a challenging process, but we made some illuminating discoveries. First, we noticed that early Hong Kong critics were highly concerned about literary development in Western and other countries. They made effort to keep abreast of new literary ideas in different places even during the war period. This might be related to the city’s socio-political history. Being a colony and located in the margin of its cultural motherland, it was constantly plagued by a sense of instability and insecurity. This gave rise to a negative feeling of rootlessness, yet it also created a strong desire to learn, to absorb knowledge from different sources so as to fill the cultural void. On the other hand, early Hong Kong critics showed interest in old and new literatures, works of local writers and new developments in modern Chinese literature. Although many of them had not been fully realized, there had been lots of “possibilities” in the literary history of Hong Kong. One can observe that Hong Kong is not without the capability of cultivating writers who are new and progressive in their thinking. It has the “potential” to becoming a platform on which different trends and ideas converge or collide, a place with a “cultural” and “literary” significance, in a deeper sense of the words. In Hong Kong, government policies and public discourses both tend to focus on economy and politics. Literature is seldom taken enthusiastically, yet it has made progress in an environment which is less than favorable. It can also be added that the search for and discovery of “literary Hong Kong” is an attempt to counter “deliberate forgetfulness,” with literature being one of the most effective tools that can be used for reflecting on the strengths and weaknesses of a place's culture. There are many related issues that can be explored: What conclusions can be drawn if we compare and contrast early Hong Kong literature with the present day one; Has the role of literature in the local society changed over time; Has the power of literature increased or waned, and why? -- But these topics are beyond the pararmeters of the present research and have to be examined in other studies. Finally, the PI will further develop the present study by working on literary criticisms written after 1949. Some serious thoughts will be given to how the historical data collected during the course of the research can be made useful for the public. The feasinility of buliding a publicly accessible data base will be actively looked into.

840513.label: Major findings and research outcome
840513.value: This project has recovered a host of early literary criticisms which would otherwise be neglected and forgotton. Representative critics and writers have been identified, their literary career and achievements introduced, and thier relevance and importance to Hong Kong cultural history carefuly analysed. The study foregrounds these areas: the socio-political situation of Hong Kong in the first few decades of the past millennium and how it impacted the growth of the local literary world, the interactions between local and Mainland writers, remarkable literary trends and their meaning and implications, and how Hong Kong literature could be positioned in the literary historiography of Chinese literature. The massive data that has been accumulated shows that early Hong Kong literature has a lot more fecundity and vitality than people would expect, and there was an interesting two-way influence between Hong Kong and Mainland Chinese literary worlds, in the sense that Hong Kong writers and critics had made important contributions in making the city a cultural and literary "entrepot" for China. The research has sketched out a picture of early Hong Kong literary criticism and, in so doing, built a groundwork for further studies on this area, which offers huge potentials in deepening our understanding of the tradition of Hong Kong culture. The research outputs include an edited book, a number of articles and conference proceedings. The following is a brief introduction of these outputs: 1) Edited book "Compendium of Hong Kong Literature 1919-1949" is a twelve-volume anthology covering all major literary genres. The PI served as the chief editor and also edited one of the volumes, "Literary Criticism I." The PI selected and edited a host of articles which are representative works of literary criticism published from the 1920s to 1940s, and wrote a detailed introduction that explains the development history of the genre in early Hong Kong. The introduction has been translated into Japanese and Korean and published in the two countries. *Part C includes a copy of the aforementioned Introduction, in the original Chinese version. 2) Refereed/Other journal article Articles related to the research topic have been published in these journals: Journal of East China Normal University Philosophy and Social Sciences (華東師範大學學報 哲學社會科學版), Wen Xun (文訊), Newsletter of the Institute of Chinese Literature and Philosophy (中國文哲研究通訊), Hong Kong Literature (香港文學). *Please see Part C for pubilcation details. 3) Conference presentation The PI made presentations at several conferences in Hong Kong and Taiwan during the project period. *Please see Part C for abstracts of the conferences and other details.

840513.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
840513.value: This completed project should be understood as the beginning of a study on the background, tradition, and characteristics of Hong Kong literature. The area has huge development potential because while Hong Kong literature has attracted wider attention in recent years, there is still a lack of academic works which examine the field in sufficient depth. Many topics remain underexplored, and many earlier writers and their works have yet to receive the critical attention they deserve. The research outputs that have been published so far should be useful references for researchers interested in early Hong Kong literature. They should also enrich investigations of post-war Hong Kong literature by providing a historical perspective and framework. Building on what has been done, I have carried out a new research on early Hong Kong poetry. A more ambitious project is a 16-volume anthology of Hong Kong literature of the 1950s. It is scheduled to be launched in 2017 and I will serve as the chief editor. I aim to create a body of work on Hong Kong literature that is diverse in its content and coherent in its viewpoint, and the completed research is an essential part of it.

840513.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
840513.value: Hong Kong gives an impression of being a predominantly commercial place. Even local people are alive to the idea that thier city has little to offer in a cultural sense. This study challenges the idea by introducing literary criticisms written in the early years and explaining their meaning and significance. By foregrounding the achievements made by early literary workers, the study shows that Hong Kong has a literary tradition. It might have been eclipsed by the city's other achievements, those made in the socio-economic front in particular, but early literary workers made many valuable contributions. They created for the place a vibrant and diverse literary past, a past which deserves more thorough examination being an ineluctable part of our socio-cultural history. The project outcomes should have the effect of deepening understanding of early Hong Kong literature. They should also be relevant for other topics, such as pre-war Hong Kong history and the formation of cultural identity. It is hoped that understanding our literary past--the hopes and dillusionment, potentials and limits, climaxes and anticlimaxes--involved in the grand project of the creation of a literary tradition would cast light on what can be done to further enliven and enrich our present day literary scene.

840813.label: Project Objectives
840813.value: To demonstrate the practice of synchronizing two approaches, philological and philosophical, to study the key words/terms in traditional and excavated texts in early Chinese intellectual history. To re-examine the development of early Chinese intellectual history based on the new understandings derived from “two-approach” studies of key words/terms. To re-examine certain methodological issues discussed by scholars in the studies of silk manuscripts and bamboo slips in the past decades. This re-examination will be carried out in the form of workshops/symposiums to encourage public and open discussions with scholars from the East and the West.
