840813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
840813.value: This project aims to examine the method and methodology of philology and philosophy, and to search for the possibility of merging these two approaches in order to apply them to the study of newly excavated Chinese silk manuscripts and bamboo slips in light of early Chinese intellectual history. Our goal is to benefit from these two approaches by applying them to the study of excavated texts and early Chinese thought. Our research will re-examine important ideas (key words/terms) in ancient classics/cannons including “天,” "仁," "義," “性,” “情,”"道," "德" which were also broadly used in the silk manuscripts and bamboo slips excavated in recent decades, so as to help scholars to rethink the connections of these ideas to the grand picture of early Chinese intellectual history. Besides, as these ideas are set forth within the context of the Chinese language, the particularities of the language structure involved should be seriously considered. One single word in the Chinese Classics often contains multiple meanings connected to an unbelievably complicated intellectual background. This is why the PI emphasizes the synchronization of both the philological and philosophical approaches to avoid bias or blind spots in our research. Professor Cheng Kat Hung Dennis, the PI of this project proposes to write one detailed article for each idea, elaborating on its etymological meanings and philosophies. He will also work with the co-investigators and international scholars of different disciplines in editing a research volume in which these seven ideas and related problems are discussed.

840813.label: Realisation of objectives
840813.value: Objective 1: To demonstrate the practice of synchronizing two approaches, philological and philosophical, to study the key words/terms in traditional and excavated texts in early Chinese intellectual history. Realization of objective 1: One of the five refereed journal article “On Tian [Heaven]”(釋「天」) originally presented at an international conference on “經典、經學與儒家思想的現代詮釋” (Contemporary interpretation on Chinese Classics and Confucianism, held at the Shenzhen University [深圳大學] on 24th January, 2015) should be a model representing how the project objectives were achieved. In gist, the ancient character “Tian” (天) is an image of a human body highlighting the head to represent the sky, the Heaven as well as the celestial space. The philosophical meaning of the character was actually developed from the philological structure. The nature of “Tian” reflected by the celestial phenomena is a never ending cycle, the name of the ten “tian-gan” (heavenly stems) and celestial phenomena are used by the Yin people to name their Emperors, while the Emperors burn the sacrifices to show their respect to the “Tian”. The Zhou people inherits part of the philosophy of “Tian” by the Yin people but switch the focus to the solar/masculine/positive power as well as the political morality of “Tian” which reflects the main spirit of the mandate of heaven. This paper attempts to rebuild the meaning system of “Tian” especially its development in the Yin Zhou transition by incorporating the ancient people’s knowledge of astronomy and calendar to reinterpret the historical records in early Chinese classics and canons and excavated texts. By revisiting the philological research on the character “Tian” by leading scholars including Wang Guo-wei (王國維) and Herrlee G. Creel (顧立雅) of the early 20th century, I further reexamines the theory of “five meanings of Tian” declared by Feng Youlan (馮友蘭). I consequently explains how and why the multi layers of meaning of the character “Tian” were developed. This paper justifies that it would be crucial for scholars to apply philological approach as well as philosophical approach simultaneously to study key words/notions in ancient classics. In the conference on key words held by this project and co-organized by the Jao-Tsung-I Academy of Sinology of the HK Baptist University in 2014, I published a paper "釋天(續)" which is an extending study of the "釋天". Objective 2: To re-examine the development of early Chinese intellectual history based on the new understandings derived from “two-approach” studies of key words/terms. Realization of objective 2: One conference article “Early Chinese Intellectual History in Language Discourses” (語言陳述中的先秦思想史芻議) which is also directly related to the project was presented in an international conference held in 11-12 June 2016 at the Academia Sinica, and in the process of revision. This paper reexamines how linguistic elements play a crucial role in early Chinese intellectual history. “Language” should not be a factor which affects the development of intellectual history but more accurately it should be a method of representation of the thoughts of the ancient philosophers. Objective 3: To re-examine certain methodological issues discussed by scholars in the studies of silk manuscripts and bamboo slips in the past decades. This re-examination will be carried out in the form of workshops/symposiums to encourage public and open discussions with scholars from the East and the West. Realization of objective 3: In my book chapter “易學與校勘學” contributing to the editing volume 《經典與校勘論叢》authored by Liu Yucai (劉玉才) and Mizukami Masaharu (水上雅晴) (北京: 北京大學出版社, 2014) I give a series of examples to elaborate the “multiplicity of meanings” (多義性) of Chinese characters in ancient Chinese classics. This paper echoes to other publications by me in rebuilding the inner logic embedded in ancient texts, which helps clarifying the development of ancient Chinese intellectual history. Objective 4: To write detailed articles on the key words/terms mentioned above. The final goal is to author a book containing 8-10 chapters , and to edit a volume on the discussion of ideas in early Chinese intellectual history. Realization of objective 4: Except for my discussion of 天, 人, 仁, in my published papers, a paper “論「群」、「獨」與清代儒學思潮” presented at an international symposium “Revisiting Intellectual History of the Ming-Qing Transition” held by the Institute of Modern History of the Academia Sinica on 23-25 June 2016. Other several key words/terms have also been discussed in my paper “Early Chinese Intellectual History in Language Discourses” (語言陳述中的先秦思想史芻議). Readers may also note that objective 4 should be a long term goal which I have been pursuing for quite some years.

840813.label: Major findings and research outcome
840813.value: The focus of the project was to reexamine the integration of philological approach and philosophical approach in studying key words/notions in early Chinese intellectual history. Upon the completion of the project, five articles (試論子思遺說, 先秦經典「中」字字義分析──兼論《保訓》「中」字 were published in the same year the RGC granted me this GRF project. 易象新議, 釋天, 歸藏平議 were completed afterwards) in refereed journals and one book chapter (易學與校勘學) which are directly related to the project and attached to the completion report have been published. Besides, six conference papers (one for a distinguished guest lecture) are also produced. Sponsored by the GRF project budget, I had held two international conferences: 1. The 2nd International Conference on the Art of Interpretations of Chinese Canonical Texts (第二屆中國經典文獻的詮釋藝術國際學術研討會) was held on 17-18 October, 2014 in the then HKIEd. 2. The International Conference on the Interpretation of Key Words in the Pre-Qin Classics (先秦經典字義源流) collaborated by the HKSAR government GRF -2013/16 Project “Inspirations and Challenges from Silk and Bamboo-slip Texts: Philosophical Investigation Based on Interdisciplinary Researches (Phase II)” and the Jao Tsung-I Academy of Sinology (饒宗頤國學院) on 3-4 October 2015. In the meanwhile I am working with the Jao Tsung-I Academy of Sinology in editing the conference proceeding which will address objective 3.

840813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
840813.value: I will kick start another plan on rewriting the History of Chinese Intellectual History volume one focusing on the early period covering 10 century BCE to AD 2 century. The aforementioned article “Early Chinese Intellectual History in Language Discourses” (語言陳述中的先秦思想史芻議) will be the major part of the first draft.

840813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
840813.value: This project reexamines the key notions which bridge up the study of excavated texts and the study of early Chinese philosophy. Scholars working on excavated texts use to focus on the linguistic elements of the texts and pay little attention to philosophy, while experts of Chinese philosophy may ignore the linguistic elements. By highlighting on key words/characters, the PI attempts to revisit the philosophical meanings of these key words/characters by studying their philological background and structure. The integration of philology and philosophy, the bridging up of the study of ancient Chinese texts and ancient Chinese philosophy are the two major intellectual merits. Take one of the research outcomes, a top journal article “On ‘Tian’ (Heaven)” as an example, it analyses previous research views on the key notion “Tian” (Heaven) by leading scholars in the past century and breaks new ground by incorporating background knowledge of ancient calendar to broaden the scope and depth of meanings of “Tian”. The two international conferences organized by the PI imposed impacts to the field. Leading scholars in studying ancient Chinese texts and philosophies contribute to this research and support the PI to establish a research network facilitating the pursuance of further studies.

840913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
840913.value: There is a wealth of research evidence that the ability to critically reflect upon one’s own experiences is a desirable learner attribute which often leads to deep learning and acquisition of professional knowledge. To foster students’ reflective ability, electronic portfolio (ePortfolio) has been increasingly used in both learning and assessments across different disciplines because of two main reasons. First, ePortfolio can enable students to collect and select multimedia artifacts showcasing their learning experiences as a basis for reflection. Second, it can engage students in the reflective process of connecting the artifacts to appropriate outcomes, goals or standards. Despite the beneficial role of ePortfolio in reflective learning, its full advantages cannot be realized if students are not provided with timely and adaptive feedback on the quality of their reflection. On the one hand, individually tailored feedback can potentially help students to enhance their reflective skills. On the other hand, it creates issues of workload and consistency in evaluating a sizeable amount of reflective entries generated by students, hindering the effective implementation of ePortfolio in education. Recent advances in Natural Language Processing (NLP) technology have brought in new computer-based methods in grading students’ written summary and free text answers with results comparable to those of human ratings. The technology offers a promising approach to address the said problem in ePortfolio. Nevertheless, to the best of our knowledge, there has not been any research into applying the automatic classification techniques in NLP to identify the level of student reflection and generate instant tailored feedback within ePortfolio contexts. Nor has there been any research into the role of automatic evaluation in students’ reflective learning. In this regard, the proposed project seeks to support students to reflect on their English language (L2) experience in an ePortfolio system by making the best use of the affordances of the automatic classification technology. To guide students towards critical reflection, the project will develop an automatic software tool to evaluate levels of student reflection and subsequently generate immediate, adaptive and individualized feedback based on the evaluation results. The project will also investigate the impact of the automatic tool on students’ reflective ability. It is expected that by integrating the automatic classification techniques into ePortfolio environments, the project will create more innovative and interactive learning experiences for students in reflective practice, in addition to developing teachers’ expertise and institutional capacity in applying the NLP technology for teaching and learning. 有大量的研究證據顯示，針對個人經歷的批判性反思能力能促進學生進行深度學習並獲取專業知識。為了培養學生的反思能力，電子學習歷程檔案(ePortfolio)已逐漸地被應用於不同學科的學習及評估之中，其主要原因有兩個：首先，電子學習歷程檔案讓學生能收集及選取多媒體作品，以展示他們的學習經歷，並藉此作為反思的基礎。第二，它能令學生投入反思的過程中，讓他們把選取的作品連繫到相關的成果、目標或標準。儘管電子學習歷程檔案有利於反思性學習，但如果未能就學生的反思提供即時及適性化的回饋，其優勢將無法充分地發揮。為學生提供適切的回饋能改善他們的反思能力，但是，回饋大量學生的反思亦同時產生了老師工作量提高和評估不一致的問題，阻礙了電子學習歷程檔案在教育上的有效推行。 自然語言處理(NLP)技術的進展為學生的寫作撮要和文字答案引進了以電腦為基礎的方法，其所得的結果與透過老師進行評級的結果相近，這種技術為上述有關電子學習歷程檔案的問題提供了可行的解決方法。然而，據我們所知，到目前為止還沒有任何研究是透過運用自然語言處理中的自動分類技術對學生的反思進行評級並提供即時的回饋，也沒有任何研究分析自動化評級對學生的反思性學習所帶來的影響。因此，本研究的目的是旨在透過應用自動分類技術以支援學生在電子學習歷程檔案系統中對英語學習經驗的反思。為了引導學生進行批判性反思，本研究將開發一套自動化評級軟件來評估學生的反思水平，並按照評估的結果產生即時化、適性化和個人化的回饋。另外，本研究亦會探討自動化評級軟件對學生的反思能力所帶來的影響。據我們估計，透過把自動分類技術整合到電子學習歷程檔案的環境中，本研究成果將會為學生在反思性實踐中製造更多創新和互動的學習經驗，同時亦在教學中應用自然語言處理技術的領域上，發展教師的專業知識和學院的能力。

840913.label: Realisation of objectives
840913.value: The project has fulfilled satisfactorily the five stated objectives, as explained below: OBJECTIVE 1. To develop an effective computer-based model for automatic classification of student reflection in an ePortfolio environment. This objective was successfully achieved by drawing on the literature on reflective learning to propose a classification framework for students’ reflective skills, highlighting key characteristics central to the identification of different levels of reflective skills. The classification framework, namely A-S-E-R, was designed to evaluate and classify students’ reflective L2 (second language) proficiency by analysing their written reflective entries. The A-S-E-R framework is characterised by four elements: (1) Analysis, reformulation and future application, (2) Strategy application, (3) External influences, and (4) Report of events or experiences. For each element, the framework further identifies four hierarchical levels, ranging from Level 1 (i.e. developing) to Level 4 (i.e. competent). A corpus of 748 reflective entries were collected from 398 undergraduate students during the project period. The average length of each entry is 239 words (or 13 sentences). In accordance with the A-S-E-R framework, every reflective entry was manually and independently annotated by two researchers. Differences in annotation results between the researchers were identified and discussed to reach a consensus on the annotation standards. The basic unit of annotation was either a single sentence or an aggregate of consecutive sentences signifying the emergence of a category (i.e. an A-S-E-R element and its level). Each unit might be labelled with multiple categories depending its properties. An effective computer-based model was subsequently generated by applying Latent Semantic Analysis (LSA) to transform the annotated entries into a vector space model representing the A-S-E-R framework. OBJECTIVE 2. To implement an automatic software tool for identifying level of reflection and generating immediate feedback based on the classification model specified in the first objective. This objective was successfully achieved by developing a web-based system (http://gp.ied.edu.hk) to classify students’ reflective L2 learning skills and provide automated feedback. Furthermore, the system serves as a platform to showcase the project and its outcomes. For example, the system offers a detailed description of the A-S-E-R framework and an illustration of using the framework to discriminate between levels of reflective skills with respect to L2 learning. The system is mainly driven by the computer-based model stated in objective 1. It was implemented using Python and its Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK) (http://www.nltk.org). Authorised users can log into the system at any time to input their reflective entry and generate an automated feedback report based on the content of the reflective entry. Essentially, the system starts by reading through each sentence of a reflective entry and counting the frequency of pre-determined keywords (i.e. features). The reflective entry will then be transformed into a vector of features in the vector space model, and be classified into different categories (e.g. A1, S2) based on its similarity with each category. An online automated feedback report will finally be created to display four different sections: annotated entry, scoring and descriptors, remarks on total score, and suggestions for improvement. Users can save the feedback report in PDF format for future reference. OBJECTIVE 3. To evaluate the agreement of ratings between the automatic tool and human annotators. This objective was successfully achieved by measuring the accuracy of the automatic classification system. Accuracy refers to the percentage of the automatic classifications that agree with the manually annotated results in the testing data set. Besides this measurement, Cohen’s kappa (K) was used to evaluate the agreement between human and machine annotation, while taking the possibility of chance agreement into account. To determine the effectiveness of the proposed method, the accuracy of the automatic classification system was compared with that of two commonly used baseline methods, namely naïve Bayes (NB) and binary relevance (BR). NB is a simple probabilistic classifier based on Bayes’ theorem, which assumes that the features in a category are independent of each other. BR is a fundamental approach to address the multi-label classification problem, which constructs a set of binary classifiers to distinguish one single category from all other categories. Five-fold cross-validation was applied to assess the overall performance of the automatic classification system. During the cross-validation, all annotated entries in the corpus were randomly split into five equal-sized groups. Four groups were used as training data while the remaining group was used as testing data. This process was repeated five times until all groups were used for both training and testing purposes. The overall result was calculated by averaging the individual results derived from the five iterations. OBJECTIVE 4. To examine the impact of the automatic tool on the level of student reflection. This objective was successfully achieved by examining if the use of automated feedback can improve the quality of students’ reflective skills. Specifically, this question was addressed by assessing and comparing the A-S-E-R scores for the reflective entries prepared by the students who were given access to the automatic classification system (i.e. experimental group) and those who were not (i.e. control group). A research procedure was undertaken in a 13-week, credit-bearing English course entitled Advanced English for University Studies (AEUS) between September 2014 and May 2015. Four class groups (with 82 students in total) were assigned to the experimental group and two class groups (with 56 students in total) were assigned to the control group. There was no significant difference between the experimental group and the control group in the results of the English language public examination. Participants in both groups were taught by the same class teacher, and they received the same instruction on academic and reflective writing in class. They were all required to submit three individual reflective journals (of no less than 170 words each) documenting their English learning experience and achievement by the end of weeks 3, 7 and 10, respectively. The reflective journals were manually assessed according to the A-S-E-R framework. The assessment results were used to examine whether or not the use of the automatic tool can impact on the level of student reflection. OBJECTIVE 5. To collect and analyze students’ and teachers’ views on the value of the automatic tool in reflective learning. This objective was successfully achieved by gathering and analysing questionnaire and interview data. An online questionnaire was designed to solicit students’ attitudes towards using the automatic classification system to support reflection. The questionnaire consists of seven self-report items. The first two items concern the number of entries submitted and the number of automated feedback received. The next three measure the level of agreement on the effectiveness of the automated feedback and the level of willingness to receive the automated feedback in future. The last two items are open-ended questions which allow students to provide their written comments. To cross-validate the questionnaire results and to elicit further views on the effectiveness of the automatic classification system, participants were invited to attend a focus group interview. During the academic year 2014-15, the online questionnaire was administered to 339 participants who had trialled the automatic classification system. A total of 203 completed questionnaires were returned, yielding a response rate of 60%. Furthermore, six focus group interview sessions were arranged. Twenty-seven participants were randomly selected to share their views and experiences towards the automatic classification system during the interview.

840913.label: Major findings and research outcome
840913.value: The research has successfully yielded the following findings and outcome: (I) A framework and an online system for classifying reflective skills in L2 learning A framework namely A-S-E-R was designed to classify students’ reflective L2 learning skills by analysing their reflective entries. Four key elements of reflective skills are considered in the framework: (1) Analysis, reformulation and future application, (2) Strategy application, (3) External influences, and (4) Report of events or experiences. Each element is further divided into four hierarchical levels, progressing from level 1 to level 4. Based on the A-S-E-R framework and Latent Semantic Analysis (LSA), an online automatic classification system was successfully implemented at http://gp.ied.edu.hk to offer automated feedback to students. (II) Impact of the automatic classification system on on the level of student reflection The results of this research project indicate that the use of automated feedback could improve the overall quality of students’ reflective entries, especially in the areas of analysis, reformulation and future application (A) and external influences (E). It is also found that the score on A for the reflective entry was significantly and positively correlated with the overall score of the final essay and all the sub-scores (i.e. content, organisation, language and referencing). This finding adds evidence to the literature that students with a higher level of ability to analyse their L2 learning experiences tend to achieve a higher grade in their academic essay. (III) Strengths and limitations of the automatic classification system Themes emerged from questionnaire and interview data reveal that automated feedback could bring benefits to students including increasing awareness of key elements of reflective L2 learning, offering quick feedback on strengths and weaknesses of one’s reflective writing, and giving examples to illustrate critical reflection. Other themes point to limitations of automated feedback in three main categories: technical effectiveness (the classification accuracy for words that are unknown to the system); affective issue (the importance of care and encouragement from the teacher); and psychological effect (the motivation to further improve reflective writing given that a low score was given to reflection). (IV) Publications & scholarly activities The results of this research project were presented in five international conferences (ICITCS2013, SEME2014, ICSSAM2015, ICALT2015, TALE2016). A paper discussing the project findings has been accepted by Australasian Journal of Educational Technology. Another paper about this project is currently under review by The Internet and Higher Education, a renowned journal devoted to reviewing innovations in post-secondary education.

840913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
840913.value: The results of the qualitative data analysis suggest that both teacher and automated feedback have their attractions and drawbacks, and that no single feedback type can fit all students’ needs. Given this, further research should be undertaken to explore how the automatic classification technology can be integrated into the traditional feedback process within different learning contexts. In this research project, data was collected from only one English course in a university. Data from similar courses offered by other universities can be collected and analysed to gain a fuller understanding of the impact of automated feedback on students’ reflective writing. Additionally, this project was primarily designed to focus on the use of automated feedback but teacher feedback is known to perform a unique role that cannot be replicated by automated feedback. Hence, a blended approach involving the use of both teacher and automated feedback can be designed to support and enhance students’ development of reflective L2 learning skills. The benefits and challenges of implementing the approach can be evaluated in the context of higher education.

840913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
840913.value: The research project has three implications for researchers and practitioners of technology-assisted learning. First, the project contributes to the development of an automatic classification system for generating immediate and individualised feedback on students’ reflective skills in L2 learning. It lends further support to the view that technology can play a beneficial role in the process of evaluating the quality of student submissions and then providing automated feedback on them. The findings of this project suggest that the accuracy of the automatic classification system can be comparable to that of human assessors. Second, it is also found that most participants value the immediate and comprehensive feedback from the system and they appreciate the opportunity to revise their reflective entries based on the feedback at an early stage before teacher feedback is received. Third, the automated feedback generated by the system can enhance students’ reflective L2 learning skills by fostering their autonomy in producing, evaluating and revising their own writing.

841013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
841013.value: Previous model of dementia caregiving stress has focused on negative stress appraisals (i.e., burden) resulting from care-recipient (CR) conditions such as behavioral and psychological symptoms (BPSD), with the end point being various caregiver health and mental health outcomes (e.g., depression). Another dimension of psychological reactions to caring for a dementia patient, that one is losing a close family member to the disease (e.g., Alzheimer’s disease [AD]), has been little researched. This study attempts to articulate an integrative model by which CR conditions leads to caregiver depression via separate pathways involving grief and burden as mediators. This model further postulates that the relationships between CR conditions on the one hand, and caregiver grief and burden on the other, are moderated by premorbid relationship quality (i.e., closeness between caregiver and care-recipient prior to dementia onset). To investigate these questions, we propose a 2-wave longitudinal study with the waves being 12 months apart. We aim at recruiting 150 primary caregivers caring for family members with AD. Because loss and grief are deeper in the later phase of the disease, we will aim at one-third of the care-recipients being at the late stage of dementia at baseline, which will be determined by Clinical Dementia Rating. Measures of grief and premorbid relationship quality have been piloted. At each wave, caregivers will be interviewed on grief, burden, and depression, as well as care-recipient’s BPSD and cognitive and functional impairments. We will examine how behavioral problems, grief, burden, and depression relate to each other cross-sectionally as well as how their changes over time affect their relationships. 過往的腦退化症照料壓力模型主要關注被照料對象（CR）本身的狀況，如其身體與心理症狀（BPSD）引起的消極壓力評估（如負擔），以照料者各身體及心理健康指標（如抑鬱）作為最終的關注點。而腦退化症照料者的另一個心理反應維度，即由於疾病（如阿爾茲海默症[AD]）而失去了一位親密家人，卻鮮有研究考察。本研究試圖闡明一個整合模型，該模型中CR的狀況將分別通過悲傷和負擔兩種不同的途經導致照料者的抑鬱。該模型進一步假設，將CR的狀況與照料者的悲傷及負擔分別作為關係的雙方，它們之間的關係是受關係質量（即CR病前與照料者的親密程度）這一變量調節的。爲了探討這些問題，我們提出了一個雙波段縱向研究，兩個波段之間相隔12個月。我們計劃招募150名AD患者的主要家庭照料者。因為喪失感和悲傷感在疾病晚期會更深，我們目標的基線會定於有1/3研究參與者為照料晚期患者的家人。悲傷和病前關係質量問卷已做了初探性研究。對於每一個波段，照料者將被問及悲傷感、負擔、抑鬱狀況及被照料者的腦退化症的行爲和心理症狀 (BPSD)、認知及功能損傷狀況。我們將橫向地探討CR的行為問題、照料者的悲傷、負擔及抑鬱各因素之間的關係，並研究隨著時間的變化，這些因素的改變將如何影響其關係的變化。

841013.label: Realisation of objectives
841013.value: The original proposal pledged to recruit 150 caregivers, equally divided by the stages of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) of their relatives (i.e., mild, moderate, and severe), and to interview them twice separated by 12 months apart. We eventually recruited 173 caregivers, of which 62, 61 and 50 caregivers of relatives with mild, moderate, and severe; those with milder grades were over-sampled because of the difficulty with recruiting caregivers of relatives with severe AD. At the 12-month follow-up, 40, 47 and 36 (total = 123, or 71% of the baseline sample) of these caregivers were successfully interviewed. Rarely do research studies feature such a high proportion of care-recipients (CRs) with severe AD and the retention rate over a 12-month interval was exceptional in this literature. We worked very hard to maintain contact and to solicit goodwill by giving the caregivers a phone call every few months to update their situation and to remind them of the next interview. We performed both cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses on the data. As will be evident from Part 6.1, the study hypotheses were not supported. Even though that is the case, we think that all the study objectives have been met for the following reasons: 1) We have successfully recruited a special sample that was sufficiently powered to test the hypotheses; 2) We have exceeded the expected retention rate (the original proposal assumed a retention of 65% over 12 months and a follow-up sample size of 98 only); 3) We have exhausted the data in terms of exploring the relationships among the variables and have tried to make good use of the data to make contributions to this under-studied topic in the literature; and 4) Despite the odds, we have provided the field with a new instrument to measure caregiver grief (Cheng, Ma, & Lam, 2019) and at least one more paper is to be written up.

841013.label: Major findings and research outcome
841013.value: The following are the major findings from the study: 1) Although grief was moderately correlated with depressive symptoms (r=.31, p<.001; Cheng, Ma, & Lam, 2019), it did not predict depressive symptoms either cross-sectionally or longitudinally, on top of burden. 2) The CR’s behavioral and cognitive symptoms did not predict grief, whether the total score or scores of the two subscales (see #4). 3) In the proposal, we hypothesized that premorbid relationship quality would moderate the relationship between the CR’s behavioral and cognitive symptoms on the one hand, and grief and burden on the other. This hypothesis was also not supported, both cross-sectionally and longitudinally. 4) Under the circumstances, we needed to come up with new angles to analyze the dataset and to make use of it to advance the literature. Because we used a new measure of caregiver predeath grief in this study, we wanted to report it as a new psychometric instrument for the benefit of the field. However, because our study was not set up as a psychometric study, we naturally could not provide a thorough psychometric evaluation of the instrument. Nevertheless, we were able to publish a psychometric paper in a very respectable journal (Cheng, Ma, & Lam, 2019; see Part C). We found, as predicted that our instrument consisted of two correlated dimensions, namely relational deprivation (RD) and emotional pain (EP). We carefully demonstrated the convergent-discriminant validities of these two dimensions. This is the first time a brief, yet multidimensional measure of caregiver predeath grief was demonstrated with such evidence of validity. We believe that the brief instrument will be very useful to the field as caregivers do not prefer to be burdened by a lengthy questionnaire if they have to enrol in a study. The establishment of these two dimensions are also useful for further analysis of the data (see below). 5) We are now focusing in the longitudinal findings for our next paper. Specifically, we found: a - The CR’s Clinical Dementia Rating sum-of-box scores (a measure of global cognitive impairment) predicted RD, but not EP, at follow-up, controlling for baseline measures of RD and EP and other confounding factors (e.g., behavioral and cognitive symptoms of CR). However, because only a relatively small proportion of CRs progressing to more severe stages of AD, the data were not suited to test whether clinical deterioration of the CR was associated with caregiver grief. b - Premorbid relationship quality interacted with behavioral problems such that caregivers were more depressed at follow-up if caregivers who felt closer to the CR before the onset of dementia also had to deal with more challenging behaviors. This finding was obtained after controlling for baseline depressive symptoms and other confounding factors. We are now working to bring these findings together in a coherent framework and we will prepare another paper for publication in due course. 6) In addition to the above, the PI has used the literature review part of this project to contribute to a review paper on dementia caregiver interventions and have acknowledged RGC support (Cheng, Au et al., 2019).

841013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
841013.value: As the hypothesized model was not supported by data, it is difficult to contemplate the next step in research, especially when grief did not have incremental value predicting depressive symptoms when the effect of burden is taken into account. However, the availability of a brief instrument to measure caregiver grief would facilitate more research into this area, e.g., as a convenient and valid outcome measure for evaluating interventions that target caregiver grief. Furthermore, our findings may prove to be useful for matching caregivers to interventions/services. As caregivers who were close to their CRs prior to dementia onset and whose CRs display more challenging behaviors were at higher risk for depression, these caregivers would probably benefit more from psychosocial interventions and support services. While the extent of problem behaviors by CRs is usually known to service providers, our findings suggest the need to assess premorbid relationship quality between the caregiver and the CR as well.

841013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
841013.value: Caring for a relative with dementia is a very long process which is sometimes described as “witnessing a slow death.” Family members often feel a sense of loss and grief when seeing the relative changes and deteriorates. This is an important but under-studied aspect of the caregiving experience. To contribute to our knowledge of this phenomenon, this study recruited 173 caregivers with care-recipients roughly equally divided between mild, moderate and severe stage in terms of the severity of Alzheimer’s disease at the start of the study. We interviewed the caregivers individually face-to-face and then again after 12 months. We found that grief was experienced by caregivers early in the process, with those caring for someone with more severe dementia reporting more grief. We also found that more intense grief was reported by caregivers who were emotionally close to the care-recipient prior to dementia onset, while caregivers experiencing grief were more depressed. As we examined this experience more deeply, we found that caregiver grief consisted of two interrelated components—emotional pain and relational deprivation, referring to the emotional suffering and the increasing lack of mutuality and intimacy in the relationship with the CR.

841213.label: Project Title(Chinese)
841213.value: 社群目標的複雜性及互動性：揭示香港學生的學習動機

841213.label: Co - Investigator(s)
841213.value: Prof Lam, Shui Fong Prof McInerney, Dennis Michael

841213.label: Project Objectives
841213.value: To design and validate, through both the classical and item response theory, an instrument that measures the emic level of social goals held by Hong Kong students. To use the purposely designed social goals instrument to investigate student endorsement of social goals in comparison to mastery and performance goals. To examine the relationship of social goals to desired educational outcomes when controlling for mastery and performance goals. To analyze the developmental changes of students’ social goals and their relations to educational outcomes over time when controlling for gender.
rows: To design and validate, through both the classical and item response theory, an instrument that measures the emic level of social goals held by Hong Kong students.
To use the purposely designed social goals instrument to investigate student endorsement of social goals in comparison to mastery and performance goals.
To examine the relationship of social goals to desired educational outcomes when controlling for mastery and performance goals.
To analyze the developmental changes of students’ social goals and their relations to educational outcomes over time when controlling for gender.

841213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
841213.value: 在過往的學習動機研究中，通達目標(mastery goals)及表現目標(performance goals)受廣泛探討。以通達為目標的學生求學是為了獲取知識，而以表現為目標的學生則是為了表現自己的能力。近年的研究顯示，要更全面理解學生的學習動機，研究的內容需包含社群目標(social goals)(Dowson & McInerney, 2001, 2003, 2004)。由於中華文化強調人與人之間的相互關係，這個觀點對華人社會尤其重要。與非華人學生相比，華人學生有較強的社群原因努力求學，例如要對父母和家人履行社會責任、得到朋輩和老師的認同等(Hau & Ho, 2010; Li, 2002, 2005; Tao & Hong, 2000)。即使社群目標在華人社會很重要，過往很少研究以此為題。我們特意探究這個重要但被忽略的課題，期望能為學習動機的研究作出貢獻。 這個量化研究為期兩年。在首六個月，我們將設計一個量度香港學生社群目標的調查工具，並作出驗證。參加者為3,000名中一至中六的香港學生，他們分別來自6間高、中、低學業成績的中學。接著的六個月，我們會把新設計的社群目標調查工具，連同一些西方固有的調查工具向1,200名中一及1,200名中三香港學生施行，以量度他們不同的學習目標。我們亦會施行其他工具以量度學生三個方面的學習成果：行為(成績分數)、認知(學習策略)及情感(價值效用)。這些參加者分別來自6間高、中、低學業成績的中學。在第二年，我們將向他們再施行兩次所有的調查工具。這個為期18個月的縱貫研究採用交叉延宕及橫斷設計，能確定新設計的社群目標調查工具的重測信度，探討學生不同學習目標的發展和改變，更重要的是能以時序模型顯示學習目標與學習成果的跨年份關聯。 本研究的重點是在通達目標及表現目標以外，全面探討社群目標扮演的角色，並探究這個目標是建基於表現能力、獲取知識、還是一些受中華文化影響下的互動因素。本研究有助建立一個超越通達目標及表現目標的學生學習動機理論架構。通過了解社群目標，本研究亦能帶出一些實用的教學策略以提升學生的學習動機。

841213.label: Realisation of objectives
841213.value: All the project objectives have been achieved. A social goals instrument was developed and validated in a sample of 3,025 Hong Kong seventh- to eleventh-graders from six secondary schools in Hong Kong (Objective 1). Based on the reliability analysis, exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, and Rasch analysis, the instrument was found to be reliable, internally valid and externally valid. The psychometric properties of the instrument are satisfactory. After the development and validation of the social goals instrument, a 18-month longitudinal study with cross-lagged and cross-sectional designs was conducted. The participants were 2,816 Hong Kong seventh- to ninth-graders from seven secondary schools. There were three time points, at an interval of 6 months, in the longitudinal study. The participants completed a questionnaire in each time point, which included the newly developed social goals scales, the Western validated mastery and performance goals scales and the educational outcome measures. The outcomes were measured by psychometrically sound instruments, including behavioral (e.g., behavioral engagement and behavioral disaffection), cognitive (e.g., academic planning), and affective (emotional engagement, enjoyment, pride and hopelessness) outcomes. To investigate students’ endorsement of social goals in comparison to mastery and performance goals (Objective 2), individual standardized means of all the goals were computed. Repeated measures ANOVAs were conducted for the whole sample as well as separately for each grade level. To examine the relationship of social goals to educational outcomes when controlling for mastery and performance goals, (Objective 3), hierarchical regression analyses were conducted. The results were further verified across the three time points. To analyze the developmental changes of students’ social goals and their relations to educational outcomes over time when controlling for gender (Objective 4), structural equation modeling was conducted to investigate how different variables were related across time. The key research findings are presented in Section 6.1.

841213.label: Major findings and research outcome
841213.value: A social goals instrument, namely the Social Goal Orientation Scale (SGOS) that assessed students’ social reasons to achieve academic success, was developed and validated. The instrument consists of 28 items that measures eight types of social goals. Among the eight types of social goals, two of them were related to parents (externally oriented and internally oriented), two of them were related to teachers (externally oriented and internally oriented), two of them were related to peers (social involvement and intellectual exchange) and two of them were related to the society (contribution to society and social status). Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses confirmed the construct validity of the instrument. All subscales were found to be reliable, with satisfactory Cronbach’s alphas. Rasch analysis further indicated good fit of the items with good item and person quality. There were no significant differences on students’ endorsement of social goals, mastery goals and performance goals. The results were consistent across grade level and across time, indicating students’ endorsement of multiple goals. Another key findings of the project is the bifurcation of externally and internally oriented goals with respect to both parents and teachers. In general, internally oriented goals (i.e., study hard because of the internalized influences) were more adaptive to educational outcomes than externally oriented goals (i.e., study hard because of the external pressure). For example, students who endorsed internally oriented goals were mastery oriented, which in turn predicted high enjoyment in learning. On the other hand, students who endorsed externally oriented goals were performance oriented, which in turn predicted high level of pride than enjoyment. In the longitudinal study, when compared to externally oriented goals, internally oriented goals (Time 1) predicted high behavioral engagement (Time 2) which subsequently predicted academic planning (Time 3), a kind of positive coping in view of failure. The findings indicate that studying hard for the sake of parents and teachers might carry different meanings and functions on educational outcomes, depending on whether the goals were internally or externally oriented. Regarding the two goals related to peers, when compared to social involvement goals (i.e., study hard to get along with peers), intellectual exchange goals (i.e., study hard to achieve academic exchange with peers) (Time 1) predicted more positive outcomes, including higher behavioral and emotional engagement, and lower behavioral disaffection (Time 2). The major findings are progressively reported in conference papers, book chapters and journal articles in preparation.

841213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
841213.value: The current research is an initial attempt to develop an instrument that measures Hong Kong students’ social goals and examine how these social goals are related to educational outcomes. More studies are needed to investigate the internally versus externally oriented social goals with respect to parents and teachers, including their meanings, functions and the underlying mechanisms that affect the educational outcomes. Emotion is an important outcome that deserves further investigation given the pressing concern on Hong Kong students’ emotional problems, in which many of the problems are related to the influence of parents and teachers. Future research could adopt experimental design to establish the cause-and-effect relationship between social goals and educational outcomes. It is also practically important to investigate the antecedents of the different types of social goals as well. In response to these research directions, a GRF proposal, as an extension of the current project, was submitted. It examines how and why internally oriented social goals are helpful or harmful to students’ emotional functioning, learning motivation and academic performance.

841213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
841213.value: Educators strive hard to enhance students’ learning motivation. To achieve this, we must investigate students’ underlying reasons of studying hard/not studying hard and how they are related to students’ learning behavior, cognition and emotion. This project develops and validates an instrument to measure the social goals held by Hong Kong students. It provides a solid theoretical framework of student motivation that goes beyond mastery and performance goals. Under the influence of the Confucian Heritage Culture, Hong Kong students study hard for their parents and teachers. Our findings indicate that studying hard for parents and teachers could carry different meanings and functions and thus predict different motivational outcomes, depending on whether the goals are externally or internally oriented. Further research is needed to verify the findings, expand the motivational outcomes involved, and uncover the underlying mechanisms of externally versus internally oriented goals. The research on social goals provides significant practical implications on the strategies to enhance Hong Kong students’ learning motivation.

841413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
841413.value: 中國古籍汗牛充棟，歷史久遠。傳世文獻中的《尚書》、《詩經》、《易經》等古籍，年代可追溯到西周。但這些典籍都是透過輾轉傳抄才得以保留下来，成為今天的模樣。更早用古文字所寫的版本，例如：漢代魯恭王壞孔子宅，發現的古籍或西晉初年出土汲郡冢書，都曾經在歷史上出現過。但我們今天只能看見當時學者整理後的資料，見不到原本的竹簡。 二十世紀末及二十一世紀初，我們相繼發現了《郭店楚墓竹簡》、《上海博物館藏戰國楚竹書》和《清華大學藏戰國竹簡》等古籍抄本，這些都是用戰國時代的古文字臨寫的抄本，是同一類性質的先秦古籍。隨著出土材料的日益豐富，我們今天能有幸從中得窺在漢代以前古書的真實面貌。 本研究計劃的對象《逸周書》是一本爭議非常大的古籍。它原名《周書》，《漢書藝文志》著錄「《周書》七十一篇，周史記」。敘事上起西周初年文王、武王，下至春秋時的靈王、景王，文體類《尚書》。《隋書經籍志》著錄時，誤以為《逸周書》同《竹書紀年》、《穆天子傳》等書一樣，出土於西晉初年汲郡的戰國魏王墓，於是在《周書》十卷下注有「汲書」。歷代對這部書都議論不斷，有的懷疑其為偽書，有的認為當中有真、有假；連具體成書的年代，觀點都莫衷一是。然而正由於《逸周書》爭議大，才吸引近年來許多學者的興趣，也催生本研究計劃的出現。我們首先要研究該書的真偽？又或是半真半偽？及各篇章具體寫成的年代？是西周、春秋、戰國，還是漢代？隨著過往研究者所付出的努力，各時代的版本、註釋或其他參考材料，都收集的相當齊全。（黃懷信等，1995）這正是本計劃可以繼續深入的基礎。由於過往研究偏重於與傳世文獻的對比、校正，本計劃則更多利用出土材料與傳世材料的互相比照，綜合研究各篇章。筆者相信這個角度，仍大有空間。 本計劃以出土文獻，例如：清華簡和兩周青銅器銘文材料，輔以《尚書》等傳世文獻，重新研究《逸周書》這部著作。透過出土文獻，例如清華簡《皇門》和《逸周書.皇門解》的校讀，嘗試還原古本的某些原貌；并由其各篇所反映的具體內容、思想和語言現象，重新研究《逸周書》各篇的著作時代。希望找到一些帶有時代標記的語言、思想、文化等標準特徵。進而重塑上古漢語前段的資料。這樣我們才有機會將上古漢語早段的資料，嘗試分出更細緻的年代段落。并從中填補先秦史的某些具體內容。

841413.label: Realisation of objectives
841413.value: 傳世本《逸周書》無疑是先秦典籍。稱《逸周書》是清代四庫全書之後的定說。最早見到這個名字，是在東漢許慎的《說文解字》。《說文》稱逸《周書》，應該非專名。《說文》另有《逸論語》，如《逸論語》曰：“如玉之瑩。”及《逸論語》曰：“玉粲之璱兮。其XXX猛也。”透過我們的研究，認為《逸周書》71篇本，成書應該到了漢代。然而當中這些篇章在戰國時已出現，但仍未編撰成書。先秦當時似仍未有書的概念，以篇為主，聚篇為類。此外，透過《皇門》等出土簡與傳世文獻對比，發現兩者差別不大。可證戰國版與現代的傳世本基本上只是用字差異。大抵是古文字隸寫為今文字時的變化。這也可以反映出漢代或晉代學者整理文獻的細心。以此推之，其他典籍亦相似。（參考拙文《皇門篇校讀》及先秦古籍的年代標記--以《逸周書皇門篇》為例）。 本計劃研究的目標主要為以下三項，回答這些研究問題，筆者編撰了《逸周書研究資料彙編》共八章。 1.研究《逸周書》的來源與傳承：例如先秦時的形態、古籍徵引的情況、西晉而後的發展、成書年代的上、下限，以及國別等問題； （參考《彙編》第一、二章及個人呈交論文。） 2.研究《逸周書》版本及各篇章的具體內容，包括史事、人物、思想、典章制度及語言特徵等，尤其關注文本中所具的標尺作用的特徵，包括：語體、詞彙、語法等； （參考《彙編》第三至第七章。） 3.確定文本的斷代標記：內容、思想、典章制度、語詞、語法特徵；并對過往的成說加以糾正、辨謬。（參考個人論文。） 《逸周書》的編撰者可能是劉向、劉歆父子。從選文角度言，全書關於國家大事：政治、經濟、軍事和禮法。 編書者有心把這類文章歸在一起，很有意思。它主要是歷史檔案、記錄，但由之所發展的政書、禮書、軍事及經濟類內容，均為富國強兵的內容。若以道、術的角度來分別，《逸周書》偏向應用，應屬術的範疇。《逸周書》內容橫跨的年代很長，從周初到戰國。然而，被認定為先秦典籍應該完全沒有問題。但具體篇章成於何時，甚至經何人之手，則較難確定。原因是：從新出土的楚簡，我們越來越清楚中國古代書籍的概念，起源相當晚。早期的書，都是不同篇章匯集而成。即便《六經》的概念，恐怕也正如李零先生所說的是“類別”而非“專名”。這也是《論語》成書時，連篇名都只取首兩字的原因。故此，《周書》、《周志》等當為類屬文章，而非專書。但《逸周書》的內容主要論及政治、經濟、軍事及禮制，其核心主題主要圍繞治國的考慮。無論故事、文章、說理、議事均如此。有人謂這是儒家的思想。我們反而覺得這與儒家關心的課題雖一致，但著眼點不同。偏向“術”。反而是西周經典從王官到民間，各自發展的路向不同。由於當時沒有印刷術，這些篇章在抄錄時，是否參入抄錄者新的內容，導致不斷更新版本，增入內容，這些變更有多少？ 比對出土和傳世文章，我們得到以上的訊息。西周早1045BC-戰國後期295BC（目前簡的年代），中間相差700多年。沒見到更早的竹簡（《曾侯乙墓》簡約433BC）。 考訂資料時，史實與人物是否可信？制度或軍事的內容等是否有託古之嫌？此外，內容有相近的 《管子》和《孫臏兵法》，年代是否一定較《逸周書》為晚？又或是均出現在差不多的背景下，春秋戰國霸王之世。

841413.label: Major findings and research outcome
841413.value: 傳世《逸周書》71篇本，是漢代編輯的。或出於劉向、劉歆父子的古籍整理團隊。《逸周書》篇章時代跨度大（謂自周初至戰國），各篇內容完整或殘佚不全，有的頗簡短，似不成篇。但來自戰國時代的抄本應該沒有問題。由於中國古代書籍的觀念起源較晚，逐步形成的。這些篇章，不一定出自一時一地一人之手，著作權的觀念在春秋戰國時代，仍不強烈。所以《逸周書》篇章中，托古記事，對歷史事件有加工的痕跡，應該是存在的。當然，從歷史事件、人物、篇章語言的使用，仍能一定程度上反映材料的來源有先後。復經過有心人編輯、收集，才能保留下來。而編撰者，更有心將內容向歷史、經濟、軍事和制度等國家大事側重，篇章多與國家大事、政治民生有關聯。 透過出土材料與傳世本對比，我們可以得到以下印象。先秦典籍確實起來有自。漢、晉學者過去在整理這些新發現的古文字材料時，態度非常認真、嚴謹。這才是我國古籍為什麼能流傳、可信、可讀的原因。 《逸周書》篇章內容的取向，重實際而不尚玄理。我們覺得跟先秦九流十家著重思想的取徑不同。較側重“術”的角度。重具體可操作。這也反映先秦時，我國對政治、經濟、軍事和禮制的看法。這些很值得跟戰國時代其他學派的學說對比研究。可以反映出中國先秦古代哲學思想的真實面貌。

841413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
841413.value: 《逸周書》撰集成書為71篇，恐怕是漢代的事。可能是經劉向、劉歆父子之手。從選文角度言，全書篇章均關於國家大事：政治、經濟、軍事、禮法。關於本書可持續研究的空間： 一． 編一詞典，研究文本中“概念”內涵的流變；二． 與當時代其他思想交流？補充？三．從政治、經濟、軍事和禮制的角度探討，其與當時社會氛圍、不同學派學說的關係。但細緻則看材料

841413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
841413.value: 關於《逸周書》的研究，過去較少人問津。自清代後，才逐漸有學者，做專門的探究。近年來，隨著新出土簡帛材料的發現，讓我們對於先秦傳世文獻的理解，更為全面。本研究對《逸周書》做了全面而整體的研究及梳理，在這個基礎上提出我們的看法。例如：傳世七十一篇本《逸周書》，我們認為是漢代恐怕才成書。此外，當中的篇章，具體的撰述年代和作者，也不容易確定。主要是在先秦，著書立說的理解，跟後世不同。很多篇章恐怕是在傳抄的過程中，已經由不同的學者加工潤色。這種情況，並不是單獨在《逸周書》中得到反映。

841613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
841613.value: Recently, because the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR) plans to introduce a means-tested “Old Age Living Allowance”, a hot debate has arisen on whether the new scheme should be universal or means-tested. Although most people would agree that means-tested benefits are more cost-effective in reducing poverty and income inequality than universal ones, some assert that universal transfer by virtue of their universality reach everyone and may thus, depending on the benefit amounts, be more effective in terms of poverty eradication. Nevertheless, in Hong Kong, our knowledge about the impact of universal and means-tested benefits remains inadequate. How effective are these programs in alleviating poverty rates as well as reducing income inequality? To what extent can these programs fill the gap between the current income levels and the poverty line of poor families? Are they financially sustainable in the long term? Compared with older adults, although the poverty of households with children and single mothers have also drawn a lot of attention, they have been largely neglected in our controversy on cash transfer welfare benefits even though a few studies have been conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of universal and means-tested programs for these two targeted groups in Western countries. Therefore, to address this research gap in a local context, we will focus on households with children (aged 17 and younger) as well as single mothers in this study. The purpose of the project is to assess the existing means-tested cash transfer programs and the proposed universal as well as other means-tested programs on their reduction of poverty, income inequality, their financial sustainability in the coming three decades, and their public acceptance. The proposed project will be led by a multidisciplinary and inter-institutional research team consisting an actuary, an economist, a policy analyst, a political scientist, and an expert in social survey – a team with substantial research experience in studying poverty issues from different perspectives using different methodologies, including face-to-face household and phone surveys, micro-simulation modeling, and qualitative analysis based on in-depth interviews or focus groups. Based on the research findings, the proposed project will offer concrete policy recommendations for reforming the current income protection arrangements for households with children and single mothers. The findings of the proposed study are expected to make a substantial contribution to policy debates in Hong Kong and, eventually, improve the living conditions of children and single mothers in the territory. 最近，就香港特別行政區政府應否對《長者生活津貼》設立資產審查引起了社會各界熱烈討論。雖然普遍市民認同設立資產審查更能集中資源幫助真正有需要的長者，在降低貧窮率和收入不平等方面更具成本效益。另一方面，主張全民退休保障的人士認爲，假如津貼金額足夠的話，全民性的津貼在扶貧窮方面更有效。然而，在香港，我們對全民性和有入息及資產審查的福利的認識並不足够。例如這些計劃能如何有效地減輕貧窮率，以及減低收入不平等呢？這些計劃又能否幫助收窄貧窮家庭的的收入和貧窮線之間的差距呢？財政方面是否可持續呢？ 與長者比較，雖然貧窮家庭兒童和單親媽媽這兩個羣體亦受到很多關注。但我們對於針對這兩個目標群體的全民性和資產審查的福利，卻未作出深入研究。爲了這個原因，我們將集中研究有17 歲及以下子女的家庭以及單親媽媽家庭這兩個羣體。本研究目的是探討現有和建議中的資產審查和全民性的福利在扶貧、減低貧富懸殊的成效；以及在未來的三十年它們在財政方面的可持續性和公眾接受程度。 本研究將會由多個學科和大學間的研究團隊率領：精算師、 經濟學家、 政策分析師、政治科學家和在社會調查專家，組成一個具有豐富研究經驗的團隊。從不同角度及不同的方法研究貧窮問題，包括面對面的家訪和電話調查，微觀模擬、和基於深入訪談或焦點小組的定性分析。 根據研究結果，是次研究將對有兒童和單親媽媽的家庭提供具體的政策建議，包括改革目前的收入保障安排。預期研究項目的結果將會在香港的政策辯論作出重大貢獻。最終，令本港兒童和單親媽媽的生活條件得到改善。

841613.label: Realisation of objectives
841613.value: All objectives of this project have been achieved successfully. The study conducted encompasses four parts: 1) assessing sensitivity of child poverty rate measure; 2) assess efficacy of six major welfare program operating in Hong Kong, 3) testing the efficacy of existing and hypothetical welfare program models with statistical stimulation, and 4) sensitivity study for single-parent household. Part 1: Assessing Sensitivity of Child Poverty Measurement Poverty threshold, usually set at half of the median population household income, is the most used measure of poverty and its accuracy is largely dependent on how one control for household size. We tested ten different household adjustment methods on 5% of the 2011 Hong Kong Population Census data, focusing on persons aged 17 or younger, in order to identify a more robust poverty measure. Household adjustment methods tested include: 1) Hong Kong government official definition with six categories of household sizes (1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6+ members); 2) Six Cutler-Katz type equivalence scales of different formulas, including AE = A+K, AE = A + 0.5K, AE = A + 0.60K, AE = (A+0.75K), AE = (A+0.75K)0.85 and AE = (A + 0.5) 0.90 (Cutler and Katz, 1992); 3) the original and modified OECD scales; and 4) a square root scale. Sensitivity of these control methods to poverty rate was gauged with three measures of poverty: poverty rate, poverty depth indexes and poverty severity indexes. Furthermore, we explored the impact of these different methods on poor household identification among demographic groups categorize by age, gender, parental education levels, parental age, household composition and housing tenure. Part 2: Assessing Efficacy of Six Major Welfare Program Operating in Hong Kong Six operating welfare programs in Hong Kong were evaluated on their effectiveness and efficacy in child poverty reduction, including Comprehensive Social Security Assistance (CSSA) scheme, Public Rental Housing (PRH), Old Age Living Allowance (OALA), Student Allowance (SA) and Community Care Fund (CCF). Demographic data used in this analysis include household income (from different sources), household composition and housing tenure, collected via survey with 1,188 children aged 17 or younger in 2015. Scheme effectiveness was measured by program coverage and the percentage of the poor families and children brought back to above poverty line (Avram, 2016). Program efficiency was evaluated by inclusion error (e.g. giving benefits to non-poor families) and the ratio between program expenditure and effectiveness. Tradeoff between effectiveness and efficiency was also investigated. Part 3: Testing Efficacy of Existing and Hypothetical Welfare Program Models with Statistical Stimulation Design of Hypothetical Welfare Programs To identify programs which are efficient and effective in child poverty alleviation, we’ve designed and stimulated welfare programs which varies on 1) three different benefit levels, 2) two delivery methods, 3) three sets of asset and income limit, and 4) two levels of application procedures strictness (3 and 4 for mean-test programs only). In other words, we tested 6 universal (3 benefit levels x 2 delivery methods) and 36 mean-tested welfare programs (3 benefit levels x 2 delivery methods x 3 sets of asset and income limits x 2 levels of strictness of procedures). One of the mean-test programs represents the existing CSSA (current benefit level, slide scales, current asset and income limit, and current standard in strictness of application procedure). Current benefit level of means-test programs was estimated based on administrative data, household size and household composition, while benefit level of the universal schemes was set at HKD2,410, according to the current standard rate of CSSA scheme for children. Stimulations were conducted on data collected via above mentioned survey. Program Efficiency Evaluation Measures Targeting efficiency of models was evaluated by 1) coverage indicator: the ratio of household receiving benefits vs poor household; 2) adequacy indicator: the proportion of household expenditure covered by benefits, as well as portion of benefits that is shared with other poor; 3) inclusion error: the percentage of welfare recipients who are non-poor; and 4) exclusion error: ratio of poor families who are excluded from benefits. Program associated costs were subsequently evaluated in relation to targeting efficiency. Program’s Poverty Reduction Effectiveness Evaluation Measures Model’s impact on poverty and income inequality reduction are assessed by their efficiency in lowering three poverty measures: poverty rate (percentage of poor children in the whole children population), poverty gap (distance between household income and poverty line, equal to money needed to raise family out of poverty by number of household members) and poverty gap index (average poverty gap in all families as a percentage of the poverty line). Squared poverty gap index, the mean of squared poverty gap, was also incorporated. Poor families were identified using the official poverty threshold of Hong Kong in 2015, with square root formula household adjustment method (OECD, 2015). We further categorized households with Low, Middle and High income (after receiving benefits) according to the 10th, 50th and 90th percentile of the equalized household income distribution. Level of economic inequality was assessed by the ratios of income difference between Low and Middle, High and Middle, High and Low, as well as S80 and S20 (top and bottom 20%). The Stimulation Referencing the Congressional Budget Office’s long-term micro-simulation model and Simulating Social Policy for an Ageing Society (Evandrou et al. 2001), the research team developed a dynamic microsimulation model, and conducted the stimulation using the flexible and powerful C++ programming language. Based on data of the cross-sectional 2015 household survey, we projected the schemes’ impact on income and financial asset holding of each individual household annually from year 2017 to 2047. Economic status changes were computed based on a chronological sequence (discrete time model) with following phrases: (1) mortality, (2) fertility, (3) new immigrant added to the household, (4) marital status, (5) living arrangements, (6) economic activity (including economically activeness, employment status, changes in job, industry and occupation), (7) changes in liabilities, income and assets, and (8) changes in welfare participation in terms of receiving cash transfer benefits. Programs’ financial expenditure as GDP percentage were also estimated. Part 4: Sensitivity Study of Single-Parent Household Demographic data of 775 single-parent households with children aged 17 or younger in 2014, such as sex, age, educational attainment, marital status, current economic activity, employment status and amount of income from different sources, were collect through surveys and home interviews. We then repeat the above analysis and stimulation (of part 2 and 3) with this sample.

841613.label: Major findings and research outcome
841613.value: Sensitivity of Poverty Measurements Different household adjustment methods of poverty threshold yielded similar child poverty rate, poverty depth index, poverty severity indexes and categorization of poor and non-poor among different demographic subgroups (age, gender, parental educational levels, parental age, and household composition, and housing tenure). This result is reported in another publication of the authors in Social Indicators Research (Cheung and Chou, in press) Efficacy of Six Major Welfare Program Operating in Hong Kong Six major welfare programs in Hong Kong assessed in this study (CSSA, PRH, OALA, SA and CCF) were found to have little impact on child poverty alleviation, among normal and single-parent household, due to deep poverty gap and high exclusion error. Four out of six programs were found to be low in efficiency. However, increasing efficiency by lowering inclusion error would lead to strong stigmatization of welfare recipients and high administration cost. No tradeoff between efficiency and effectiveness was observed, paralleling to studies conducted in Central and Eastern Europe. Based on these results, policy implications were drawn for future social assistance programs (Chou, 2017). Welfare Models Stimulation Results of welfare models stimulation showed that universal schemes have lower exclusion error and could substantially improve all child poverty and income inequality indicators, over and above means-tested programs of similar poverty reduction effect and annual cost (for details see Lee and Chou, 2017). Taken together with the fact that flat-rate benefits have higher adequacy (amount of benefits for poor households) then slide scales (amount of welfare depend specific criteria), authors conclude that universal benefits with flat rates is the preferred welfare model to combat child poverty. Nonetheless, for poverty reduction in single-parent household, our result indicates that means-test schemes are more efficient and less costly.

841613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
841613.value: Results of this study will be disseminated through press conference and op-eds, and the analytical methods used could be applied to examine other welfare programs. For instance, the Low-income Working Family Allowance Scheme, initiated by the Hong Kong government in 2016 as an effort to reduce intergenerational poverty, has a very low take up rate. Only 25,345 families were benefited in the same year by receiving a HKD 800 allowance for each child, despite the administration’s effort to encourage enrollment by lowering income limit and parents’ working hour requirement. Investigation of the effect of different asset and income limits, as well as working hours’ requirement, on the take up rate is need to improve the program’s effectiveness and efficiency.

841613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
841613.value: Child poverty is a pressing issue yet largely overlooked in the existing welfare system of Hong Kong. As the introduction of means-test screening process to the “Old Age Living Allowance” spiked heated debate on universal versus targeted welfare schemes, it is the goal of this study to identify the most effective and cost efficient social security models to eliminate child poverty. Examination of the six major welfare program currently operating in Hong Kong (CSSA, PRH, OALA, SA and CCF) reveals that these welfare models have little impact on child poverty alleviation, due to the severity of existing income inequality. Four out of six programs were found to be low in cost efficiency, and at the same time, their stringent program enrolling requirements excluded many poor families from the much needed financial assistance. Hypothetical universal and means-test welfare schemes were compared with statistical stimulation, and we’ve found that universal benefits with flat rates is the most effective child poverty and income inequality reduction method. On other hand, means-test schemes are more efficient and less costly is alleviating child poverty in single-parent households. Policy implications and recommendations were drawn from these results.

To understand the origin and the influence of the rise of Madrasah in the East-Asians and Chinese societies on the implication of education policy in Hong Kong; ii. 842513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
842513.value: This research focuses on the recent rise of Madrasah (Islamic learning institutions) in Hong Kong. Using qualitative research methods (participant observations, focus group interviews, and in-depth interviews), this study aim to address the following questions: 1) How do ethnic Muslim students and their parents perceive the importance of Madrasah education in terms of religious piety, moral education, and family honour? 2) What are the emerging challenges faced by Muslim students and Hong Kong educators in conventional schooling? and 3) What could be implemented to improve the urban planning, multicultural policy, and teaching resources driven by current research on the Madrasah education in Hong Kong? While many studies focus on the issues and difficulties of ethnic Muslim students facing modern education in daytime Chinese conventional schools, this ethnographic study explores the rise of Madrasah schools and how ethnic Muslim youths remain faithful to the Islamic tradition by studying and memorising the Qur’an in the Madrasah after daytime schooling. The Madrasah as an Islamic institution has been increasingly subjected to global policing because of its suspected links to terrorist attacks in the post-9/11 era. Consequently, the increasing number of Madrasah schools in Hong Kong is understudied. Unlike the security concerns and stereotypical concepts on the Madrasah in the West, the current ethnographic study traces the demographic expansion of ethnic minorities and socio-political transformations to explain the rise of the Madrasah in Hong Kong in the past decade. 這項研究旨在剖析本港伊斯蘭宗教學校的源起、發展及影響。通過定性研究方法(參與者觀察，焦點團體訪談，深度訪談等)，本研究嘗試理解幾個問題：一、穆斯林家長就伊斯蘭宗教教育的觀感，伊斯蘭宗教教育與宗教虔敬、德育培養和家庭聲望有何關係？二、伊斯蘭宗教教育的興起對穆斯林少年和日間學校的教育工作者帶來了什麼影響？三、伊斯蘭宗教教育的興起對現存的城市規劃、多元文化政策和教育資源帶來了什麼啟示？過去關於穆斯林少數族裔的研究集中於日間教育的相關議題，這研究則以不同角度，探討在港的穆斯林少年在日間上課後，部分會在傍晚前往伊斯蘭宗教學校內研習和背誦古蘭經的情況。有別於西方研究文獻對伊斯蘭宗教學校的研究方向，本研究探討穆斯林少數族裔的人口增長及香港社會政治的轉型，用以探討過去伊斯蘭宗教學校在港興起的原因。

842613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
842613.value: Hong Kong is a multicultural society without any multicultural policy support. Schools have a predominantly Chinese student population but some 1.94% of our students are ethnic minorities. (School Education Statistic Section, EDB, 2012). These students remained invisible in the school system until the 2008 Racial Discrimination Ordinance and the implementation of inclusive education policy in 2002 (EDB, 2010, 2011). Without a broad multicultural environment supporting our schools, how do teachers better support the learning of ethnic minority students, make them feel included and address the issues of diversity involved? It can be argued that teachers’ lack of knowledge of ethnic minority students’ backgrounds and cultures impedes effective teaching and learning and the promotion of inclusion. Hence the broad aim of this proposed study is to address the issue of Hong Kong’s teachers’ multicultural competence in supporting the learning of ethnic minority students at the various levels of classroom, school and teacher professional development, as identified in our prior research projects (Hue, 2008; Hue & Kennedy, 2012; Kennedy & Hue, 2011; Kennedy, 2008). Specifically the study will explore teachers’ views of culturally responsive teaching and how such teaching can support the learning of these students in public schools. These students are among our lowest academic achievers, come from low socio-economic backgrounds, face problems of social adjustment and experience learning difficulties in the foreign languages of Chinese and English. The study will examine: 1) teachers’ and students’ constructs of cultural responsiveness and multiculturalism; 2) teachers’ perceptions of multicultural teaching competence; 3) schools’ influence on the creation of culturally responsive classrooms; 4) teachers’ difficulties in promoting cultural responsiveness and multicultural competence and 5) teachers’ professional development needs for the promotion of culturally responsive teaching. Both quantitative and qualitative methods will be employed. Quantitatively, a survey will be conducted to measure teachers’ perceptions of multicultural teaching competence, using the Multicultural Teaching Competency Scale validated by Spanierman et al. (2011). Teachers from the 30 designated schools for ethnic minority students will participate in this survey. Qualitatively, case studies will be conducted to explore the classroom experience of teachers and students and school differences. Theoretically, the study will advance our understanding of multiculturalism by exploring its meanings in Chinese contexts. The results will help policy makers, school administrators and teachers to formulate policy and practices for promoting the academic success of all students and achieving the wider ethos of equity and social justice. 摘要 香港是一個沒有多元文化政策支持的多元文化社會。華人學生佔整體學生人數的主要部份，但為數百分之1.94的學生為少數族裔 (School Education Statistic Section, EDB, 2012)。這一小撮的學生一直以隱形的狀態存在於教育系統裏，直至2008年的《種族歧視條例》及2002年的共融教育政策生效後，問題才浮現出來。要解決這問題，有人認為學校不能缺乏一個廣泛的多元文化環境，否則，教師便無法好好向少數族裔學生施教，令學生未能感覺到被接納，更遑論解決因文化差異而衍生的問題。但亦有人辯稱，問題在於教師本身欠缺有關少數族裔學生的背景及多元文化知識，妨礙有效施教﹑學習及達至共融的產生。這研究的方針，如我們之前的研究所指 (Hue, 2008; Hue & Kennedy, 2012; Kennedy & Hue, 2011; Kennedy, 2008)，是旨在查察香港教師在不同程度的教室﹑學校及教師專業進修下，為這些學生提供多元文化教學的能力。這研究會專門探討教師對文化回應教學的看法，以及這教學方式如何能協助公立學校的少數族裔學生學習。這些學生通常來自經濟社會的低層，是學校裡成績欠理想的一群，這些背景因素往往令他們難於融入社會，加上使用中英文等外語來學習，感到困難重重。 本研究將查證︰1) 教師及學生對文化回應及多元文化論的構想﹔2) 教師對多元文化教學能力的看法﹔3) 學校對建構文化回應教室的影響﹔4) 教師在推動文化回應及多元文化能力的困難﹔以及 5) 教師促進文化回應教學所需的專業培訓。我們會進行定量及定性分析。定量方面，我們會採用 Spanierman et al. (2011) 的多元文化教學量表 (Multicultural Teaching Competency Scale)，量度教師對多元文化教學的感知能力。來自30間被揀選的少數族裔學校的教師將會參予是次調查。定性方面，我們會施用個案研究分析來探索教師﹑學生以及學校在課室內的不同經歷。理論上，這研究能深化我們對多元文化理論在華人社會中的理解。研究結果定能協助政策制定者﹑學校行政人員及教師制定相關方針及實踐政策，以提升學生全民的學術水平及實現一個彰顯公平和公義的社會精神。

842613.label: Realisation of objectives
842613.value: 1. To examine teachers’ and students’ constructs of cultural responsiveness and multiculturalism Teachers conceptualized “multiculturalism” as the division between the local and the non-local, in terms of people, cultures, religions and ways of living. They classified four categories of students: Hong Kong Chinese students, ethnic minority students (EMS) born in Hong Kong, new immigrant EMS, and new immigrant students from Mainland China. The first category was considered “the local”, whereas the others were “the non-local”. Multiculturalism was also referred as language diversity where teachers felt that language was the most prominent type of diversity among these different group of students that needed to be fully addressed because of the wide range of students’ abilities in English and Chinese. In the context of teaching and learning, “cultural responsiveness” was mainly constructed as how different learning styles of these groups of students could be managed to address cultural diversity in classroom. In managing cultural diversity, teachers did not think it was enough to merely promote multiculturalism within the school. They felt that ethnic minority students should be enabled to integrate into wider Hong Kong society. The teachers also stressed that fulfilling the diverse learning needs of students could become a challenge for them when using the current ethos of “cultural harmony” to promote multiculturalism, as the Confucian doctrine of fairness, justice and equity is still deeply rooted in the dominant Hong Kong culture. They thus asserted the need for formulating “a new rationale of multiculturalism” and for developing a fresh model of “cultural harmony”. 2. To investigate teachers’ perceptions of multicultural teaching competence Teachers’ conceptualization of multicultural teaching competency for cultural responsiveness has three components: Redressing the ethos of difference and equality At present, the strategies for diversity management could be described more as promoting “harmony” for the minority and the majority, but less as promoting equality between individuals. It is proposed that the rationale of cultural responsiveness should be further extended, from the existing ethos of “cultural harmony” to the promotion of individual difference and equality. Learning and re-learning of cultural knowledge A cross-cultural process of learning and re-learning one’s own culture and that of others is identified as a crucial element of teachers’ multicultural competency. Teachers should be equipped with a competency to examine their ideologies and confront their misconceptions and ignorance, in relation to their cultural knowledge of the majority and the minority. They should develop strategies for helping EM students to engage in the same process of learning and re-learning as well. Promoting cultural congruities between school, home and community Teachers should develop a competency to promote the cultural congruities between school, home and community by understanding how ethnic minority students’ familial and religious ideologies affect their learning at school and home and engagement in the community. 3. To explore school differences by identifying factors affecting the creation of culturally responsive classrooms Creating culturally responsive classroom requires teachers to enhance their multicultural competency and various school stakeholders, school managers, professional parties, and policy makers who work with teachers to create a supporting policy framework, school culture and environment. All parties’ concerted efforts should explore effective strategies for supporting students’ learning and managing their cultural diversity, not only within the classroom, but also at other levels of schooling. Implementing culturally responsive classroom also requires a need to broaden the discussion of ethnic minority education, and to examine in depth the concept of educational purpose and culture related to the schooling of these students and school practitioners’ understanding of ‘school success’. Such a conversation would help create a broad, culturally responsive classroom environment by enhancing teachers’ multicultural competency and promoting effective teaching and learning. Through the creation of a culturally responsive classroom, learning can become transformative, but not a resocializing process, wherein students are not necessarily referred in terms of deficiency or congruency. Classrooms of this kind would not only benefit classroom practitioners working with ethnic minority groups; rather, all teachers must unlearn and relearn the historical and cultural significance of the ethnic minorities in mainstream society, and use such cultural knowledge to link learning to social justice, equity, and human rights. It is hoped that this will lead to a transformation in the ‘contents’ and ‘images’ of the mainstream culture in the various contexts of the classroom, school, home, community, and society. To achieve this, teachers should enhance their leadership role and multicultural competency. They should also be better equipped with the skills and knowledge in order to help transform mainstream schools, and even society, into more just and culturally diverse institutions. 4. To find out the difficulties of promoting cultural responsiveness and multicultural competence Four challenges were identified: Domination of monoculture The unexamined ethos of ‘integration’ and ‘harmony,’ which is currently being promoted by all schools involved in the study, is a reflection of the dominant monoculture of the local society, under which the vast majority of teachers and students in Hong Kong have grown up and hence have had little exposure to other cultures and backgrounds. Although they have a sense of belongingness to Hong Kong society, the ways in which they act and think are largely within the culture of the mainstream society, without necessarily taking ethnic minority cultures as their frame of reference. Managing cultural diversity Cultural influence should be taken into account when promoting ethnic minority students’ learning. Teachers believed that cultural diversity among students brought unique characteristics to the classroom in relation to their learning, such as their language ability in Chinese and English, the way they thought about and conducted mathematical operations, their learning styles and classroom behavior, and their concept of themselves as learners. Dealing with discrimination beyond the classroom Promoting the value of multicultural education and cultural responsiveness merely within a school or among an ethnic minority group of students is inadequate; it is equally important to make urgent changes in the majority group’s negative stereotypes and the labeling of ethnic minorities in mainstream society. Cultural incongruities In promoting cultural responsiveness, the teachers also faced the challenge of dealing with the cultural incongruities between students’ homes and the school. Although parents were aware that they had a responsibility for their children’s learning, they were unable to meet the teachers’ expectations and supervise their children’s homework because of their background. 5. To identify teachers’ professional development needs for the promotion of the culturally responsive teaching Four categories of students (i.e. Hong Kong Chinese students, ethnic minority students (EMS) born in Hong Kong, new immigrant EMS, and new immigrant students from mainland China) brought unique characteristics and diversities to the schools and the classrooms in Hong Kong. Against each of them, teachers are needed to equip themselves with some specific multicultural competencies. Overall, when devising professional development programmes for promoting teachers’ multicultural competency, it is important to consider areas such as teaching strategies, classroom management, managing language diversity, effective communication and emotional management, and understanding knowledge of how cultural factors affecting the features of student diversities and their learning in the classroom and beyond.
