842613.label: Major findings and research outcome
842613.value: Mixed research method was adopted in the research and survey (Multicultural Teaching Competency Scale). Semi-structured interview and focus group were conducted. 381 quantitative data are collected for teachers’ perspective on cultural responsiveness and multiculturalism and 38 interviews with teachers and students were conducted. Major findings on teachers’ perception of multicultural teaching competence and obstacles hindering the promotion of cultural responsiveness are discussed below. To construct a cultural responsiveness classroom, it is found out that language difference of students is one of the significant factors as communication among students with different cultural background plays a significant role in building cultural harmony in classroom. To further expand cultural harmony in classrooms, re-learning individual, cultural differences, family values and religious ideology will be critical for teachers and students to practice. Promoting cultural harmony can not only enhance the learning efficacy of ethnic minority students, but it can break down the social stigma of ethnic minority students in the society. However, factors have been discovered standing in the way of building a cultural responsiveness classroom in mainstream schools in Hong Kong as school policy and practice, teaching ideology and classroom management techniques did not cater for diverse learning and personal development needs. Teachers should value and respond to different learning and cultural needs and integrate them on teaching materials and course structure design. Transformation and integration of cultural context should be valued and expected in classrooms. In a society where monoculture dominates all, it is important to promote equality and understanding of ethnic minority population. In the research project, parent support is found to be one of the major reasons hindering both the academic and personal development of ethnic minority students. Teachers should think of different strategies and contact methods to communicate, understand and cooperate with families with different values. It is suggested that teachers should equip themselves with skills, knowledge and understanding of cultural references to better support ethnic minority students towards building a culturally responsiveness classroom.

842613.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
842613.value: This research is a first step towards exploring what teachers’ multicultural competency may look like in the context of Hong Kong. Furthering the research along this line will certainly yield a research-informed and systematically developed teachers’ multicultural competency framework (TMCF) in Hong Kong. In turn, this can help review the national teachers’ competency framework and highlight the need for incorporating TMCF in it. Moving into this direction will also be helpful for the greater East Asia region given the common influence of Confucian cultural philosophies in these societies. In the longer term the research also should move into such a direction that the competency work will take into account not only students’ ethnic and racial diversity but also other forms of diversity such as gender, class, religion, sexual orientation, disability, refugee status etc. Different forms of diversities may co-exist in students’ lives and their interactions greatly affect their learning. Therefore, teachers need to have the competencies to deal with those students having more than one diversity and teachers need to function such a way that they can address those students’ needs stemming at the intersection of multiple disadvantages.

842613.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
842613.value: The demographic realities coupled with the racial, ethnic, religious, cultural, and linguistic diversity shape teachers’ concept of multiculturalism in Hong Kong. Teachers strive for a new rationale in developing culturally responsive schools beyond the Confucian philosophies of justice, fairness, and equality that are deeply rooted in mainstream Hong Kong culture. Instead, having a deeper understanding of social justice based on equity, anti-discrimination, pluralism, intercultural learning, and mutual respect is fundamental to teachers’ conceptualisation of multicultural teaching competence. They desire to create culturally responsive classrooms and make schools successful role models through their intercultural skills and knowledge in collaboration with all stakeholders. However, this would require them to examine and change the current monocultural teaching and learning practices that are hardly sensitive to the ethnic minority cultures. Culturally responsive teaching is possible if teachers are prepared to address students’ diverse learning and emotional needs, manage classroom diversity and students’ behaviour, help students improve their language abilities, and facilitate students’ intercultural interaction and learning. Thus, addressing the challenges of ethnocentrism, discrimination, and cultural incompatibility through appropriate policies and practices is critical to managing cultural diversity in both schools and society in Hong Kong.

843513.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
843513.value: The importance of pragmatic development in children has been widely recognised. Recent years have seen the growth of research on discourse abilities of children in different languages and ethnic groups. In Hong Kong, the study on Cantonese children's linguistic ability mainly focuses on phonological and grammatical development, with little emphasis on pragmatic competence. The aim of this project is to investigate one of the most common forms of oral discourse, i.e., making refusals, in the development of pragmatic competence in Cantonese-speaking preschool children. Compared with making requests, making refusals is more complex because it is not a preferred response to an act initiated by the other party. Building on previous research on pragmatic development of children in other languages, this study focuses on how Cantonese children of different age groups make refusals. Findings from this study have both theoretical and practical values. Theoretically, the findings will add to our knowledge of the pragmatic development of children in acquiring Cantonese. It will enable us to conduct comparative studies on children’s pragmatic abilities and contribute to our understanding of oral discourse development in children. Practically, findings from this study will provide useful information on the typical development of oral language in Hong Kong children. Such information will be useful for teachers and other educators involved in teaching, designing and planning the language curriculum for typically developing children and children learning Cantonese as a second language. The developmental data will also be a useful reference for Hong Kong speech and language therapists in assessing children with pragmatic problems and difficulties. Furthermore, the database generated from this study will provide useful data for further research on Hong Kong children's oral discourse development. N/A

844313.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
844313.value: The inclusion of students with special educational needs (SEN) is still considered very challenging in Hong Kong (CSNSIE, 2003; Forlin & Sin, 2010), when it comes to the issue of achieving equal learning opportunity. In inclusive practice, SEN students, who study in the same classroom with their same age peers, always have adjustment difficulties in learning the same curriculum at the same pace (Sin, 2012). They need effective inclusive teaching and support strategies for overcoming learning barriers (EOC, 2012). Teaching assistants (TAs) have been introduced to support SEN students and teachers for quality learning (EDB, 2007). However, most TAs are not adequately trained to work towards this goal and there is a lack of empirical evidence about how TAs support SEN students and teachers, and their effectiveness (Au et al., 2012; Blatchford et al., 2012). Among a wide range of effective support strategies for inclusion, the Mediated Learning Experience (MLE) from Feuerstein’s theory is widely recognized in school practices in European countries (Lebeer, 1995). The MLE has been introduced and advocated in special needs courses at HKIEd since the visit of Dr. Lebeer in 2009. In this study, this facilitation technique – one that builds a child’s capacity to learn more independently, will be used as an approach for TAs supporting SEN students. It is chosen because it addresses academic learning and provides well-researched evidence that it facilitates SEN students to learn better in inclusive settings (Lebeer, 2006). Our project, lasting for 24 months, aims at identifying the difficulties of TAs and modes of support to teachers and SEN students, and examining the effectiveness of MLE in strengthening professional collaboration and student learning. A territory-wide survey on TAs’ support and difficulties will be conducted (N=1000). Forty pairs of teachers and TAs (N=80) will take part in focus group interviews, classroom observations and in-depth study in collaboration. The facilitation technique will then be introduced to an experimental group. The learning behavior and changes in academic performance of student participants will be assessed for a year. Both quantitative and qualitative outcomes will be collected at the pre-, midway, and post-intervention stages, by questionnaires, videotaping analysis, teachers’ reports on student’ academic performance, written feedback and strategic reflections. Our local findings will be of practical use and have impacts on future teacher and TAs training, with regard to the skill validation driven by the MLE and research practices on TA’s effectiveness in Chinese communities. 香港的融合教育實踐，如何為有特殊教育需要學生 (融合生) 實現平等學習機會，仍然面臨許多挑戰 (CSNSIE, 2003; Forlin & Sin, 2010; EOC, 2012)。在共融過程中，融合生和同齡夥伴在課堂內以相同進度學習相同課程，經常面對許多適應困難 (Sin, 2012)。有效的融合教學和支持策略，將有助學生克服學習障礙 (EOC, 2012)。近年來，許多學校都聘請教學助理（助教），以支援融合生學習及課堂教學。然而，大部分助教都沒有足夠培訓，而助教支援融合生及教師的效能，仍缺乏實證 (Au et al., 2012; Blatchford et al., 2012)。 在眾多融合教育的有效策略中，從Feuerstein 理論發展出來的「介導學習經歷」 （Mediated Learning Experience, 簡稱MLE），廣泛應用於歐洲國家的學校內 (Lebeer, 1995)。自2009年Lebeer博士訪港後，香港教育學院的特殊教育需要課程，逐漸引入及推廣MLE理論。在本研究中，助教將會運用MLE來支援有特殊教育需要的學生，以促進學童建立獨立學習能力。選用MLE的原因， MLE能處理學生學習的問題，研究證據顯示，MLE能促進有特殊教育需要的學生在融合環境中更好地學習（Lebeer, 2006）。 本研究為期24個月，研究目的是辨識助教在支援教師和融合生的模式和困難，並探討不同支援模式如何增強專業合作和學生學習的效能。本研究也會檢視「介導學習經歷」對加強專業合作和學生學習的成效。20組在融合教育環境中工作的教師和助教，將參與焦點小組訪談、課堂觀察和問卷調查，以了解本地融合教育課堂內的困難，而實驗組的教師和助教也會實踐MLE的教學策略，其學生於一年內定期接受學習行為和學習成績的評估。研究員將在實踐方案之前期、中期及後期階段內，收集質性及量性的研究結果，資料來源包括問卷調查、錄影分析、教師書面報告、學生學業成績、參與者意見及反思報告。最後，研究員期望透過運用「介導學習經歷理論」以驗證有關技巧，與及在華人社會中，進行助教效能研究。研究結果具實用價值，將對教師及助理的培訓，有深遠的影響。

844313.label: Realisation of objectives
844313.value: Objectives in the research proposal Teaching assistants (TAs) have undergone an exceptional development internationally in the past decade. In the development of inclusive practice in Hong Kong schools, the deployment of TAs in classroom support has been identified as vital in supporting the learning process and maintaining students with special educational needs (SEN) in mainstream classrooms. However, most TAs in Hong Kong are not adequately trained to work for this goal. The Mediate Learning Experience (MLE) from Feuerstein’s theory, among a wide range of effective support strategies for inclusion, is widely recognized in school practices in European countries. As stated in the proposal, our study aimed at exploring the following objectives: a) To identify the practical difficulties experienced by TAs in their existing mode of teaching and support for SEN students in classroom settings b) To compare the differences between primary and secondary school TAs in terms of the difficulties encountered c) To design and implement a training course for TAs of SEN students that will integrate the teaching and support strategies into a strategic model d) To evaluate the effectiveness of the adapted model with reference to the attitudes, self-efficacy, outcome of TAs in teaching students with SEN Realization of the objectives In regard to the revised objectives and plan, the research team conducted the study with a mixed methodology for the data collection, including literature review, survey, interviews, observation, training, tryouts and comparative study. The subject recruitment included teaching assistants and teachers teaching SEN students in Hong Kong regular schools. (1) The training and the use of Mediated Learning Experience (MLE)-based mode as a teaching and supporting strategies for TA of SEN Students: For verifying the effectiveness of the MLE as a teaching and supporting strategy for TA of students with SEN, including regular school-based consultation and support, the team conducted training workshops, evaluation and comparative study among pairs of TAs and their teacher participants. After the completion of the training, the follow-up visits, classroom observation, video taped try-outs and focus group interviews were conducted in the months. Teachers, teaching assistants, parents and students about their views towards the supporting mode of MLE were carried out. The team built up a data bank for the qualitative and quantitative analysis, for verifying the effectiveness of the supporting mode specified in the study. The outcome did help to achieve the objective (d) of the study. (2) The survey on the role and support of TAs in schools: With the support of 250 school teachers from the subsidized primary and secondary schools in Hong Kong, a total of 500 copies of the questionnaire were distributed and 113 valid responses obtained from the sample of TAs. These would be helpful to identify the scenario, role differentiation, strategies of support and difficulties of TAs in primary and secondary school settings. The outcome did help achieve the objectives (a) and (b) of the study. (3) The in-depth examination and case study of TAs in schools: Six schools (3 primary and 3 secondary) were selected for the interview. These six schools were chosen based on common similarities: (1) all schools participated in the whole-school approach to integrated education, (2) all schools included students with SEN and had TAs supported these students in the school, (3) all schools agreed the research team to interview their TAs, classroom teachers partnering with TAs, school personnel responsible for TAs or students with SEN such as a position similar to a SENCO or a student support group head, and school principals, in separate groups. A total of 20 interview groups took place. Interviewees included 6 principals, 2 vice-principals, 3 SENCOs, 1 student support group head, 10 teachers, 1 social worker and 12 TAs. The techniques of timelog and classroom observations were used for the data collection. The outcome did further help achieve the objective (a), (b) and (d) of the study. (4) Development of the self-efficacy scale: For evaluating the self-efficacy of TAs in teaching students with SEN, our research team developed and validated a scale (Teaching Assistant Efficacy Scale, TAES) for measuring TA’s efficacy on identified capabilities. A total of 531 teaching assistants from the training course participated in the survey. The multidimensional Rasch model was used to analyse the data. The results revealed that a 5-dimension structure of TA’s efficacy was supported. The final 30-item version of TAES assesses TA’s efficacy on learning support, teaching support, behaviour management, cooperation, and administrative support. The Rasch reliabilities for all five dimensions were around 0.90. The 6-category response structure worked well for the scale (Yan, Z., Lum, C. W., Lui, T. L.R., Chu, S. W. S., & Lui, M., 2015). Utilizing this validated 30-item Teaching Assistant Efficacy Scale (TAES), a quantitative survey was conducted to assess the self-efficacy of teaching assistants in Hong Kong with the participation of a further 547 teaching assistants from the training course. The outcome did help achieve the objective (d) of the study. (5) Review and making recommendations of the training workshop for TA: Based on the findings and evidence-based practice, the team reviewed the current training for TA and made recommendations on the course design, contents and delivery. With the support from the Education Bureau, some of the recommendations were integrated into the training course titled “Workshops on Catering for Diverse Learning Needs for Teaching Assistants (TAs) Working in Ordinary Schools”. Furthermore, the findings also shed insights to the course development in BEd(SN), BA(SE) and MEd(SNGC) at EdUHK for the strategic support for TAs in the classroom settings. The outcome did help achieve the objective (c) of the study. In short, all the objectives have been achieved accordingly.

844313.label: Major findings and research outcome
844313.value: Difficulties and role of TAs in inclusive schools The difficulties and role of TA in the inclusive practice were identified. It was known that the TA post was dominated by female, their level of formal educational attainment was high and they were in the age bracket of 21-30 years old representing a young workforce. It was undesirable that the TA post had a high turnover. The main cause was that the TA position was not structured in the current school system. There was no promotional opportunity and salary increment. 94% of TAs were employed on a yearly contract and required to work above 40 hours a week. Furthermore, the role of TAs in schools were too diversified. It was found that TAs were engaged in 24 different types of tasks. Among them, 12 tasks were related to supporting students, 6 supporting teachers and 6 supporting the school. In the classroom observation, it was observed that there was limited interaction between the teacher and the TA especially in primary schools. Training for TAs supporting SEN students In regard to the professional needs of TAs in supporting the SEN students, the results indicated that the current training workshop offered by EDB should be replaced by a structured and comprehensive mode of training. The job specifications and requirements should be redefined. TAs should be with professional training with the study of a wide range of effective supporting strategies. Evaluation of the attitudes and self-efficacy of TAs in teaching students with SEN The results showed that TAs got the highest marks on cooperation, followed by administrative support and teaching support while the score of behavioral management and learning support are the second lowest and the lowest respectively. The inter correlations between these five perspectives are high. The highest correlation locates between teaching support and learning support, which may indicate a changing teaching ecology among Hong Kong TAs as the role of TAs has been gradually transformed into that of Assistant teachers (ATs). The introduction of A Mediated Learning Experience (MLE)-based strategic mode The MLE method was found to be a very promising tool for supporting TA in the six schools tested. All TAs participated found it both a useful and stimulating platform to both teaching and supporting their SEN students. The approach should be widely promoted in the training.

844313.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
844313.value: In regard to the outcome, the partnership of the teachers and TAs in the inclusive practices is always the concern. Under the concept of whole school approach, schools will have a wide range of strategies in deploying the TAs in the supporting SEN students. It will be worth examining the successful case of manpower deployment of TAs at the management level. With good example and evidence-based practice of professional collaboration, the strategic use of TAs will be more effective. Also, the Mediated Learning Experience (MLE)-based strategic mode in inclusive practice will be another area of examination in Chinese community.

844313.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
844313.value: The study is of significance by reporting the difficulties, role and professional training of TAs in supporting SEN students in Hong Kong schools. The findings showed that TAs played a diversified role in supporting SEN students in schools. Their job security and career development were undesirable. The workforce of TAs was mostly young and educated. The reasons of high turnover rate are due to no career path, low starting salary and short employment contract. In regard to the inclusive practices, training for TAs is a concern. A very promising strategy that could be deployed to support TAs in Hong Kong is the Feuerstein approach but its implementation in local schools might be hampered by its high training and running costs. Furthermore, by investigating the current situations of Hong Kong TA’s self-efficacy, this study finds a change of existing ecology among TAs. Such a change is alarming. It indicates that the role and function of TAs are not clear and in turn lead to their inappropriate deployment. The relationship between self-efficacy and turnover rate of TAs warrants further investigation.

844813.label: Realisation of objectives
844813.value: In order to meet the four stated research objectives, the Principal investigator (PI) underwent the following venture for the project: In the Preparation Phase in the first six months from October 2013 to March 2014, 32 scripts of social video vignettes based on Hong Kong contexts were developed and produced by a professional video production house. In the pilot study phase in the second three months from April to June 2014, the social video experiment set up was trialed using the eyetracker. The principal investigator contacted the potential participating schools and agencies via phones, emails and direct on-site visits. Poster flyers to promote the project were developed in addition to the invitation information letter and consent form. The package was sent to two NGOs (namely Project Aspire and Heep Hong Society Parents Resource Centres) for the recruitment of children with ASD and two primary schools for the recruitment of children without ASD. Parents were invited to accompany their participating child to the two-hour assessment eyetracker appointment session in the Institute during the briefing sessions arranged by the NGOs. In the main study phase in the third six months from July to December 2014, a total of 113 children with their parents participated exceeding the stated number of subjects (n=90) originally proposed. Specifically, 17 children were tested in the pilot study from April to May 2014. 96 children with their parents participated in the main study from June to December 2014. Among them, 41 children belonged to the control group with typically developing (TD) subjects while 55 children belonged to the experimental group with high functioning Autism Spectrum Disorders (HFASD) subjects. However, 20 subjects out of the 55 experimental groups were later excluded from the main study since they were found to have other comorbid diagnoses such as mild grade intellectual disabilities, etc. Both the control and experimental groups were comparable in terms of age, gender and visual reasoning abilities as screened by the Raven Standard Progressive Matrices (RSPM) test of visual-perceptual and reasoning abilities. Since the official launch of Data Collection Phase in April 2014, the team had been doing eye-tracking assessments on most saturdays and sundays and during school holidays such as Easter break as the participants needed to attend schools on regular weekdays. Each of the participants was assessed using the eyetracker with the social video stimuli experimentally manipulated in order to achieve the three modes, namely, visual / auditory / visual-auditory attention, visual organization and memory, stated in the three objectives. In January 2015, the project entered the Data Set-up Phase. As the data involves several complicated eye-tracking data sets of four components, namely, the Raven data, the parents response data, the human photo and voice discrimination data, and the social information processing data, it had taken three full months to set up and edit each of the four data files consuming the entire year of 2015. On 28-30 September 2015, the PI presented the validation of the newly developed measure, “the Social Information Processing Interview Schedule”(SIPIS) at the international conference on Adolescent Medicine & Child Psychology at Houston, USA. As a result, the PI has received invitations for publication submission and conference speakers both internationally and locally, for instances, the journals, EC Psychology and Psychiatry in August 2016 and Clinical Psychiatry (CP) in January 2017. However, the PI decided to submit the first manuscript entitled as, “Using the Video-Based Social Information Processing Interview Schedule (SIPIS) to Identify Differences in Empathic Functioning between Children with ASD and/or ADHD” to a more well-established journal instead but have been unsuccessful to rank A journals. Revisions were made upon rejections. It is currently under review by a rank B journal, Measurement and Evaluation in Counseling and Development Manuscript ID - MECD-16-08-082 since its submission on 4th September 2016. While pending on the editors’ decision, The PI will wait til a decision is made by the MECD before the manuscript can be cleared and submitted to a journal such as CP that has indicated acceptance of the manuscript. The second manuscript, entitled as, “Eye-tracking study on facial emotion recognition tasks in individuals with high-functioning Autism Spectrum Disorders” was successfully accepted by a rank A journal, Autism, Sage publisher in August, 2016. The journal is ranked Q1 (15/69) in Developmental and Psychology with an impact factor of 3.170 in 2015. The PI organized dissemination activities to report the results to the parents and colleagues. Part of the project results were presented in departmental research meetings on 28 April 2015 entitled as “Progress report on the GRF project – What thou see and hear? Eye-tracking assessment of social information processing in children with high-functioning autism spectrum disorder” and entitled as “Eye-tracking study on facial emotion recognition tasks in individuals with high-functioning Autism Spectrum Disorders” on 19 July 2016 respectively. In sum, Objectives 1-4 were completed in August 2016 and achieved the following deliverables: (i) 2 articles for peer-reviewed journal publication (ii) 2 abstracts for local and international conferences (iii) 2 public seminar on social information processing for students with ASD

844813.label: Major findings and research outcome
844813.value: The eye-tracking experiment was carried out to assess fixation duration and scan paths that individuals with and without high-functioning autism spectrum disorders (ASD) employed when identifying simple and complex emotions. Participants viewed human photos of facial expressions and decided on the identification of emotion, the negative-positive emotion orientation and the degree of emotion intensity. Results showed that there was an atypical emotional processing in the high-functioning ASD group to identify facial emotions when eye-tracking data were compared between groups. That is, the high-functioning ASD group more readily distinguishes overt emotions such as Happiness and Sadness. However, they perform more inconsistently in covert emotions such as Disgust and Angry, which demand more cognitive strategy employment during emotional perception. Their fixation time in eye-tracking data demonstrated a significant difference from that of their controls when judging complex emotions, showing reduced ‘in’ gazes and increased ‘out’ gazes. The data was in compliance with the findings in their emotion intensity ratings which showed individuals with ASD misjudge the intensity of complex emotions especially the emotion of Fear. In sum, the results of this study demonstrated atypical emotional processing in the high-functioning ASD children when identifying facial emotions and in rating their intensity. We suggest that high-functioning ASD children prefer to use a rule-bound categorical approach as well as a featural processing strategy in the FER tasks.

844813.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
844813.value: A better understanding of the processing style or strategies adopted by individuals with high-functioning ASD will give us hints on how to make full use of their learning preferences to help them acquire social interaction skills, such as perception of others’ emotions. Future ASD interventions that include emotion perceptual skill training can narrow the focus on those social situations that trigger understanding of complex emotions. Using a systematic rule-bound analysis of complex everyday social situations, the high-functioning individuals with ASD can be guided through the simulated social episodes and practice emotion perceptual compensatory strategies and social interaction. The employment of cognitive and language-based compensatory strategies can also be incorporated to guide them successfully to meet daily social interaction challenges. In sum, future intervention design should match these evidence-based strategies with the learning styles of individuals of ASD to maximize intervention efficacy. The findings will be shared with students who are in-service or pre-service teachers in their special needs courses. Their assignments are to develop effective intervention programs for individuals with ASD. The knowledge gained from this study will be transferred to them so that they will be more competent in designing effective ASD intervention and training to suit the learning styles of individuals with ASD.

844813.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
844813.value: Eye-tracking technology is used to measure where an individual is looking whilst they are completing a particular task. Past eye-tracking research on high-functioning individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD) has yielded controversial findings. A generally accepted explanation is that individuals with ASD have more difficulties in recognizing complex emotions (such as fear) because they do not look at human eyes as much as their TD peers. Our findings suggest that the high-functioning ASD group prefers to use rules to identify others’ emotions (e.g., the more curled-up the mouth is, the happier the person is). Therefore, the high-functioning ASD group more readily distinguishes overt emotions (such as Happiness and Sadness), but perform more inconsistently on covert emotions (such as Disgust and Anger). This is because the rules defining covert emotions are more abstract and demand greater interpretation of the whole face context instead of isolated face features. The findings will be shared with my students who are in-service or pre-service teachers in their special needs courses. Their assignments are to develop effective training programs for individuals with ASD. They will learn more how to develop effective teaching and learning support for students with ASD in their classrooms to suit the learning styles of individuals with ASD.

844913.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
844913.value: Since the handover in 1997, the Hong Kong government has adopted a “biliterate and trilingual” policy with the aim of enabling Hong Kong residents to become biliterate in written Chinese and English, and trilingual in Cantonese, Putonghua and spoken English. Currently, Hong Kong primary schools do not have an agreed approach or method for the implementation of trilingual education, and there is an urgent need to explore current successful or unsuccessful models. Following a successful preliminary case study into the implementation of trilingual education in a single HK primary school (Wang & Kirkpatrick, 2012), this project aims to carry out a more complete inquiry into trilingual education in Hong Kong primary schools. The research questions are: 1) What are the models of trilingual education in HK primary schools? To answer this question, we need to find out which language is used as the Medium of Instruction (MOI) in what subjects in different schools, the number of class hours devoted to each of the three languages, the variations across different grades, and reasons for the variations. We will also investigate the schools’ language policies in different subjects (e.g., one-language-at-a-time, or code-switching and co-languaging allowed (if so, to what extent)), and the rationales behind. 2) Which models are more effective in fostering trilingualism? To answer this question, we will examine the reasons for choosing different languages as the MOI for different subjects, and if it leads to effective trilingual education. We will also investigate how much English/Cantonese/Putonghua is actually used in EMI/CMI/PMI lessons, whether teachers are keen to use the assigned language to teach such subjects, and what their priorities are. To evaluate how successful the schools are in producing trilingual children, we need to look at students’ language benchmark results before graduation, and also invite them to self-evaluate their language proficiency level. Teachers’ reflections on their own teaching can also inform us about the effectiveness of the trilingual education models adopted in the schools. Research methods will include document analysis, ethnographic case studies, questionnaire surveys, interviews, and classroom discourse analysis adopting a corpus linguistics approach. The outcomes of this project would be a better understanding of how to implement trilingual education in Hong Kong primary schools. Upon successful completion of the project, it is expected that a trilingual education model that is likely to be effective across schools in general would be proposed and recommended to Hong Kong primary schools. 自1997年香港回歸中國後，香港政府開始實行“兩文三語”政策，希望香港居民能同時掌握中文、英文書寫，以及粵語、英語和普通話口語。目前，香港並沒有一個大家都已認同的三語教育模式供香港小學參考，因此對現今不同學校推行的成功或不太成功的三語教育模式進行研究至關重要。我們最近已在香港一所小學就該校的三語教育模式進行了個案調查，在此基礎上，本課題旨在對香港小學正推行的三語教育模式進行更全面系統的研究。研究問題包括： 一． 香港小學現今正推行怎樣的三語教育模式？ 要回答這個問題，我們需要瞭解在不同的學校內哪一種語言在哪一門課程裡被用做了教學語言，三種語言在課堂教學中各占的總時長，這些總時長在不同年級間存在的差異，以及產生這些差異的原因。我們還會調查學校在不同科目中實施的語言政策（例如，一門課只准用某一種語言，或者允許語言混用/並用（如果允許，到什麼程度）），以及制定這些語言政策的依據。 二． 哪些模式能更有效地幫助學生掌握三語？ 為了回答這個問題，我們會調查選用不同語言作為不同科目教學語言的原因，以及這些安排是否成功達到了三語教育的目的。我們還會瞭解在以英文/廣東話/普通話為教學語言的課程中，該語言在課堂上實際應用的情況，教師是否支持用該語言作為教學語言，以及他們所看重的因素。為了衡量各學校是否成功教育出了具備兩文三語能力的學生，我們將查看學生們畢業前語言課程基準試的成績，並邀請他們對自己的三種語言的能力進行自我評估。教師對自己教學的反思也能讓我們進一步瞭解學校推行的三語教育模式是否高效。 我們將採用的研究方法包括文獻分析，人誌學個案研究，問卷調查，訪談，以及基於語料庫語言學的課堂話語分析。 本課題的研究成果將使我們更好地瞭解如何在香港小學中實施三語教育。課題成功完成後，我們期望能提出一個在大部分小學都能有效推行的三語教育模式，並將該模式推薦給各小學參考。

844913.label: Realisation of objectives
844913.value: To find out what the models of trilingual education are in Hong Kong primary schools and to investigate the schools’ language policies in different subjects, and rationale behind these policies, we first conducted a questionnaire survey with the principals in Hong Kong primary schools, including government schools, aided schools and direct subsidy scheme (DSS) schools. The questionnaire was designed to find out how the ‘biliterate’ and ‘trilingual’ language policy was implemented in Hong Kong primary schools. We received responses from 155 primary schools. The findings of this survey have provided an overall picture of the current situation of trilingual education implementation in Hong Kong primary schools. First, the findings suggest that the implementation of trilingual education varied significantly from school to school, and the effectiveness of the trilingual education models varied as well. The reason why schools do not have an agreed approach or method for implementing trilingual education is that the Hong Kong government has never made a clear policy on Medium of Instruction in primary schools. Second, Cantonese is the predominant language used as the MoI in subjects such as mathematics, General Studies, Visual Arts, Music, Physical Education and Information Technology/Computer in most surveyed schools, especially in government schools and aided schools, as Cantonese is the mother tongue of Hongkongers and in the 155 surveyed schools, the majority of students are local Hongkongers (83.57%), while 12.58% of the students come from Mainland China, 3.18% come from a South Asian area and only 0.67% of the students come from other areas such as Britain. Third, when implementing trilingual education in schools, the greatest problem, reported by principals, was to find qualified and suitable teaching staff. Fourth, code-switching/code-mixing between Cantonese and Putonghua in the teaching of the Chinese subject or between Cantonese and English in the teaching of the English is allowed in some schools. Lastly, there is no distinct relationship between the origins of students and the MoIs chosen by the surveyed schools. To examine which models are more effective in fostering trilingualism and to recommend a trilingual education model that is likely to be generally effective in Hong Kong primary schools, case studies have been carried out in three sample schools, one on Hong Kong Island, one in Kowloon and one in the New Territories. Follow-up case studies in selected primary schools are needed to answer some of the unanswered questions due to the limitations of the questionnaire survey. For example: How is the trilingual education model structured in the school? What is the role of Cantonese in classes in which English or Putonghua is used as the MoI, and vice versa? What languages are used to teach which subjects, when and why? How successful is the school in creating trilingual and biliterate children? A multi-modal approach for the case study was adopted so as to obtain as complete a picture of the setting as possible. Our sources included interviews with teaching staff and parents, focus group interviews with students, classroom discourse data analysis, student questionnaire survey, teachers’ reflection, and ethnographic field research data analysis. First, interviews were carried out with teaching staff including the school principal, the subject panel chair and subject teachers in the researched schools. The interviews with school principals focused on the rationale behind the present trilingual education model implemented in the school and the extent of the success of the model. Altogether we also interviewed thirty-one teachers in the three schools to collect their views on the respective trilingual education models. About ten parents from each of the three schools were interviewed individually so that their views on trilingual education could be collected. All the interviews were transcribed into English. Second, we recorded and transcribed a total of 30 lessons in the research schools so as to analyse what actually happened in different lessons taught in different MoIs. Each lesson lasted for 35 minutes. Third, those teachers whose lessons were observed and video-taped reflected on the lessons afterwards. This engages them in reviewing, analyzing and evaluating the situation which would enhance professional growth. Fourth, a 5-point Likert scale (Strongly Agree, Agree, Neutral, Disagree, Strongly Disagree) questionnaire survey in Chinese and English was designed to collect students’ perceptions of the trilingual education model in the school. 405 P4 to P6 students in the three schools completed the questionnaire. Fifth, one student Focus Group Interview was conducted in each of the three schools to collect the students’ views on the trilingual education model implemented in the schools. In each Focus Group, there were 8-10 P4-P6 student interviewees. In total, 27 students were interviewed and each Focus Group Interview lasted for about an hour. Lastly, we conducted ethnographic research in School A, in which the ethnographer observed how the three languages were used in two events on campus: the school Morning Assembly, and the Prize-giving Ceremony and the 2nd Annual General Meeting of the 8th Parents-teacher Association. In addition, the ethnographer attended the school’s 14th Parent-child Sports Day held in the Aberdeen Sports Ground. The ethnographer also took photos of signs and bulletin board displays written in a variety of languages. Through the case studies, we find that students and parents were positive towards the trilingual education model adopted in individual schools. Both students’ and parents’ views varied towards the use of different MoIs, especially regarding the use of Putonghua as the MoI in the study of the Chinese subject. Students’ and parents’ ethnic and linguistic backgrounds are likely to be the major reason for these differences. Despite their ethnic and linguistic backgrounds, most of the parents argued for an increased use of English as the MoI in teaching different subjects, especially Computing, Mathematics and the science topics in General Studies. It would seem wise for policy makers and schools to take these factors into consideration when making MoI policies and seek the views of parents and students. Based on the research findings, the following trilingual education model has been proposed for Hong Kong primary schools: 1. The three languages should be used as media of instruction, but the ratio of each should alter as students progress through primary, with the emphasis on Cantonese in the early years. 2. Either Putonghua or Cantonese could be used as the MoI for the Chinese subject from P1. Students should be allowed to choose the MoI they prefer. In later years, Putonghua could be further promoted in the Chinese subject. 3. Special classes in Cantonese should be provided for P1 students whose mother tongue is not Cantonese. 4. English could be used as the MoI for English and for PE from P1. Maths, General Studies, Music, IT and Visual Arts should be taught in Cantonese, but the other languages can be introduced whenever appropriate. 5. All teachers sharing the same MoI should work together more closely and develop cross-curriculum activities which require the use of that particular language. 6. A multilingual pedagogy can be adopted, with the aim of enhancing students’ trilingual development. 7. Tests should be given at the end of P3 and P6 to assess students’ proficiency in the three languages.

844913.label: Major findings and research outcome
844913.value: The survey with the principals in Hong Kong primary schools shows that without government guidelines, individual primary schools have adopted their own policies regarding the use of medium of instruction in teaching different subjects, even across the same type of schools, i.e., government schools, aided schools and Direct Subsidy Scheme (DSS) schools. Some patterns of the current situation of trilingual education implementation in Hong Kong primary schools have been identified: the majority of the schools use Cantonese as the major MoI in most subjects except the English subject and Putonghua subject, but the DSS schools are predominately EMI schools. Many schools do not encourage code switching in the classroom, but some allow a certain amount of code switching, but mainly in junior grades. The language subjects dominate school curricula. The DSS schools seem to be more confident than the aided schools and government schools regarding their graduates’ proficiency level in the three languages, and the aided schools and government schools have rather low confidence in their graduates’ English language proficiency (both spoken and written). When asked about difficulties encountered in the implementation of trilingual education, the surveyed schools found that finding qualified and suitable teaching staff was the biggest challenge. Around half of the schools also found that students’ low level of English standards has hindered the implementation of trilingual education (Please refer to Part C 8.1). In the case studies conducted in three primary schools, we find that students and parents from the three schools were happy with the different trilingual education models implemented in the schools. Having said this, both students’ and parents’ views vary towards the use of different MoIs, especially regarding the use of PTH as the MoI in the study of the Chinese subject. Students’ and parents’ ethnic backgrounds and their mother tongue as well are likely to be the major reason for these differences. Despite their ethnic and linguistic backgrounds, most of the parents argued for an increased use of English as the MoI in teaching different subjects, especially Computing, Mathematics and the science topics in General Studies. It would seem wise for policy makers and schools to take these factors into consideration when making MoI policies and seek the views of parents and students. Based on the research findings, a trilingual education model has been proposed for Hong Kong primary schools (Please refer to 5.3 for details).

844913.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
844913.value: After investigating the implementation of trilingual education in Hong Hong primary schools, it is our interest to further investigate the trlingual education models being adopted in Hong Kong secondary schools. The EB announced the ‘fine-tuning’ of Medium of Instruction for secondary schools in 2010. Schools are no longer bifurcated into “Chinese-medium schools” and “English-medium schools”. Under the fine-tuned MOI framework, all schools have the discretion with varying degrees to make professional judgment in each of the school years within a six-year fine-tuned MOI cycle, having regard to their school circumstances, to devise school-based MOI arrangements. This explains why we have applied for a new GRF project focusing on trilingual education in Hong Kong secondary schools.

844913.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
844913.value: 155 primary schools responded to our survey about trilingual education in Hong Kong primary schools, and a clear overview was obtained. For better understanding of how trilingual education is implemented in Hong Kong primary schools, follow-up case studies in 3 selected primary schools were conducted to answer some of the unanswered questions and to allow us to propose a trilingual education model that would suit most schools. The significance of the case studies is to bridge a gap in both the international and local literature and provide a better understanding of students’ and parents’ perceptions of the trilingual education in Hong Kong primary schools. In general, students and parents were positive towards the trilingual education models adopted in schools. However, most parents, regardless of their ethnic background and mother tongue, argued for an increased use of English as the MoI in teaching different subjects, especially Computing, Mathematics and the science topics in General Studies. The major reason is to bridge the gap between primary education and secondary education in which the latter often uses English as the MoI in those subjects. Based on the findings, a trilingual education model has been proposed for Hong Kong primary schools.

845013.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
845013.value: Tests (including examinations, inventories, questionnaires, and observations) have been widely used in the human sciences. In general, tests can be classified as two categories: normative and ipsative (from the Latin ipse: he, himself) (Cattell, 1944). In normative tests, different persons are compared on the same latent trait (e.g., who is more proficient in problem solving). Most tests are normative because many decisions are made based on inter-individual comparison. Ipsative tests with forced-choice items have been commonly used in education, psychology and industry for career guidance and personnel selection. A typical item in ipsative tests is to request respondents to select one statement from a pair of statements (e.g., “attending parties” vs. “visiting museums”) that they prefer (i.e., pairwise comparison). Ipsative tests, as the name reveals, produces person-centered measures that can be compared only within individuals. Popular ipsative tests, to name only a few, include: Chinese Personality at Work, Jackson Vocational Interest Survey, Kostick Perception and Preference Inventory, Occupational Personality Questionnaire, PAL Personality Profile System, Performax Personal Profile System, Personal Profile Analysis, and Personality and Preference Inventory. Item response theory (IRT) models have been developed for normative tests, mainly because of their advantages over classical test theory, including their specific objectivity, independent estimation of item and person parameters, diagnosis of fit, individualized measurement error, applications of test linking, differential item functioning, and computerized adaptive testing, and model generalization (e.g., multilevel and mixture modeling). Little has been done to develop IRT models for ipsative tests because of theoretical difficulty. To date, only two IRT models are available (Stark, Chernyshenko, & Drasgow; 2005; Brown & Maydeu-Olivares, 2011). Unfortunately, the Stark et al.’s approach has serious limitations, and the Brown and Maydeu-Olivares’s model is erroneous (details shown below). Consequently, the development of IRT models for ipsative tests is missing, and IRT advantages cannot be actualized. This project aims to fill the missing half by developing a new class of IRT models for ipsative tests and investigating relevant technical and practical issues. The new model processes specific objectivity and can be generalized to cope with complicated ipsative data, including multiple statements and multiple blocks, model invariance, multilevel data structure, and mixture distributions. Upon completion, this project will generate a long-standing impact on theoretical and technical advancements of IRT models for ipsative tests, the initiation of new research lines, and operational procedures in the design, analysis, and revision of existing and new ipsative tests. 測驗（包含考試、量表、問卷、和觀察等）經常被使用於人類學科。一般而言，測驗可以分為兩大類：他比和自比(Cattell, 1944)。在他比測驗裡，我們用同一個潛在特質來比較人們（例如誰比較會問題解決）。大部分的測驗屬於他比測驗，因為很多的決定取決於人們之間的比較。 強迫選題的自比測驗也在教育、心理、和企業上使用，作為職業諮商、人事甄選等之用。典型的自比測驗是要求受試者從兩個陳述裡選擇一個較喜歡的（例如參加聚會 vs. 參訪博物館）。顧名思義，自比測驗會產生以個人為中心的測量，僅供個人之內的比較。著名的自比測驗有華人工作相關性格量表、傑克遜職業興趣量表、Kostick感知與偏好量表、職業性格問卷、PAL性格型態系統、Performax性格型態系統、個人型態分析、性格與偏好量表。 試題反應理論常被使用在他比測驗，只要是因為其相對於古典測驗理論的優越性，包括特定的客關性、題目與能力估計的獨立性，模式吻合度的檢測，個人化的測量誤差，在測驗連結、試題差異功能、和電腦化適性測驗上的應用，以及模式的延展性（如多層次和混和模式等）。相反地，很少有試題反應模式可以用來分析自比測驗，主要是受到理論上的障礙。截至目前為止，只有兩個試題反應模式可用。可惜的是。第一個模式有很大的侷限，而第二個模式則有錯誤。因此阻礙了這類模式的開展，使得試題反應模式的優點無法展現於自比測驗中。 這個計畫旨在彌補此一遺憾，打算開發一系列的針對自比測驗的試題反應模式，並研究其相關的技術性和實用性議題。這些新的模式擁有上述的優點，如特定的客觀性，也可以進一步擴展以分析複雜的自比測驗，包括多個陳述、多個區組、模式不變性、多層模式、和混和分布等。計畫完成後，將對自比性測驗的試題反應模式的理論和前端技術，新的研究主題，以及測驗設計、分析和修訂上的操作程序上，產生長期的影響。

845013.label: Realisation of objectives
845013.value: Upon the completion of the project, the four objectives have been successfully achieved. The objectives and the activities we carried out during the period are given below: Objective 1: To develop a new class of IRT models for ipsative tests (January 2014 to March 2015) To achieve Objective 1, we have clarified the major fundamental problems in previous studies. It was analytically shown that the ipsative tests are not applicable for between-person comparisons. Moreover, we have developed a new and general class of IRT models for ipsative tests, including (1) a new model for multidimensional pairwise-comparison (MPC) items where two statements are paired in an item; (2) new models for polytomous MPC items where each item has more than two categories of preferences; (3) new models for multidimensional ranking items where respondents are required to rank several statements according to their preferences; (4) new models for partial ranking items where respondents are required to indicate which statement they prefer most and which statement they prefer least; (5) new models for ipsative tests where more than two facets are involved. For example, in working place a manager is required to judge the employees’ performance using MPC items. In this case, three facets are involved: statement, person (employee), and rater (manager); (6) new models for ipsative tests with multilevel data structures where respondents are randomly sampled from different organizations and the organizations are randomly sampled from a population of organizations. The new models are also applicable for longitudinal surveys using ipsative tests. All these new models belong to the family of Rasch models, therefore, the models inherits the good measurement properties of specific objectivity and sufficient statistics for item and person parameters. They are useful in describing psychological differentiation (e.g., interests differentiation and emotional differentiation) among latent traits within a person. Objective 2: To develop parameter estimation procedures and evaluate their performance through simulation, so as to provide practitioners with clear guidelines for ipsative test design (January 2014 to March 2015) To achieve Objective 2, we have conducted comprehensive simulation studies to explore the parameter recovery and model-data fit of the new models. Two kinds of estimation methods have been implemented and investigated in this project: the marginal maximum likelihood estimation (MMLE) method and the Bayesian estimation with Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method. The efficiency and applicability of two computer programs--ConQuest, which implements the MMLE method, and JAGS, which is a freeware that implements the MCMC method, were used across a variety of conditions (e.g., test length, number of latent traits, and linking design). Guidelines for practitioners in designing ipsative test are provided. Objective 3: To develop methods for assessment of differential statement function and model-data fit, and evaluate their performance through simulation (June 2014 to March 2016) Measurement invariance has been investigated. Both non-IRT-based (e.g., logistic regression) and IRT-based methods have been adapted to assess differential statement functioning (DSF) in ipsative tests. Simulations were conducted to evaluate the performance of the new methods for DSF assessment. The manipulated variables included number of categories, sample size, number of latent traits, percentage and magnitude of DSF statements, and so on. The dependent variables included the power and Type-I error rate of the DSF detection. Moreover, the DSF assessment method has been applied to an empirical example. Objective 4: To demonstrate the implication and applications of the new class of IRT models through empirical data analyses (June 2014 to June 2016) In achieving this objective, we have applied the new models to three empirical data sets which consisted of triad ranking items, polytomous MPC items, and quad partial ranking items. They were: (1) A workplace personality test with triad ranking items (2014) The test included 66 triads with 132 statements measuring 12 latent traits: Energy, Assertiveness, Sociability, Concern for Others, Dependability, Organized, Achievement Orientation, Initiative, Multitasking, Innovative, Self-Confidence, and Self-Control. The data were collected from more than 2600 job applicants, who were instructed to rank three statements based on their preference. (2) A career interests survey with polytomous MPC items (2015) We conducted a career interests survey using polytomous MPC items. The questionnaire was constructed from the popular Holland Code which assesses six types of career interests including realistic, investigative, artistic, social, enterprising and conventional. Statements were retrieved from open-accessed sample items. The questionnaire consists of 36 items and takes about 20 minutes to complete. A total of 301 participants who were mainly college students were invited to complete the questionnaire anonymously. They were required to compare their preference on the two activities related to different careers and choose one of the four categories (I prefer A much more to B; I prefer A a little more to B; I prefer B a little to A; I prefer B much more to A) according to their preference. (3) A career interests survey with quad partial ranking items (2016) The design of survey is similar to that of the second survey. More than 600 college students were invited to complete the questionnaire anonymously. The participants were required to select one statement they preferred most and one they preferred least. The new models were fit to the datasets using ConQuest or JAGS. Model-comparison and model-data fit were checked with Bayesian methods. The between- and within-individual comparisons in terms of psychological differentiation were provided. To promote the new models, we have developed computerized adaptive testing (CAT) algorithms based on the new models. Special features in CAT for ipsative tests have been identified. The proposed algorithms include: (a) quick statement selection methods, (b) within-person exposure control methods, and (c) variable-length CAT algorithms. These algorithms have been explored for both MPC items and ranking items. Simulation studies have been conducted to evaluate their performance. Additionally, several CAT algorithms have been applied to real ipsative tests.

845013.label: Major findings and research outcome
845013.value: Major findings include: 1. The fundamental errors in previous IRT models for ipsative tests have been identified and a new class of IRT models that do not suffer such errors have been developed, which are applicable for different ipsative item formats, including MPC, (partial) ranking, and polytomous MPC items and able to cope with practical issues in ipsative data such as measurement invariance for test fairness, multilevel data structures or longitudinal survey with ipsative tests, ipsative tests that involve raters, and CAT for ipsative tests. 2. The parameters of the new models can be well recovered by using the MMLE estimation method implemented in ConQuest or the MCMC method implemented in WinBUGS/JAGS. 3. Empirical examples are given to demonstrate the applications of the new models in education, psychology and industry. The results showed a good model-data fit, an accurate estimation of statement utilities, and between- and within-individual comparisons on psychological differentiation of the latent traits. 4. The new methods for DSF assessment perform very well. The proposed CAT procedures are effective. The outcomes from this project have substantial impacts both theoretically and practically. Specifically, the erroneousness of previous studies are corrected and new IRT models are developed, which fills the missing part of IRT models for ipsative tests and opens a new research line for future studies. Findings have been widely disseminated in various forms as an article published in world-leading journal, book chapter, and conference papers (including papers presented in a symposium in which project team was the organizer). The detailed information can be found in Part C of this report. The project team will continue to prepare manuscripts for publication and generate more outcomes. The PI was invited to deliver four keynote speeches / invited talks and give seminar for researchers, practitioners, educators, and graduate students in Mainland China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. Finally, a website (http://ipsativeproject.weebly.com) has been constructed where an adaptive testing platform for career interests survey can be freely downloaded. Researchers and practitioners can use the platform to help stakeholders (e.g., students, employers, and job applicants) with career guidance and personnel selection. Instructions, computer code, and examples are also available in the website.

845013.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
845013.value: Although we have conducted pioneering work for ipsative data, more research is needed. Two issues are listed as an example: (1) ties are often found in ranking items, (2) covariates (e.g., gender, education background) are useful to explain variations in person measures or item parameters. Future studies could be conducted to investigate these issues. In this project, I focused on ipsative categorical data. In many other areas, such as organizational culture assessment and values assessment in industrial organization, marketing, education, and psychology, multidimensional compositional items (MCI) are also widely used, where respondents are requested to allocate a fixed total number of points (e.g., 100) to a set of statements in an item. MCIs produces ipsative “continuous” data. None of the IRT models are applicable for such data. A new class of IRT models for MCI are needed.

845013.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
845013.value: Ipsative tests, such as Jackson Vocational Interest Survey and Occupational Personality Questionnaire, are popular in personality and career interests assessment. A typical item in ipsative tests is to request respondents to select one statement from a pair of statements (e.g., “attending parties” and “visiting museums”), or to rank several statements (e.g., “attending parties”, “visiting museums”, and “doing scientific experiments”) according to their preference. This project develops a new class of IRT models for ipsative tests and investigates relevant technical and practical issues. The new models possesses specific objectivity and can be generalized to different item formats, including pairwise-comparison, (partial) ranking, and polytomous forced-choice items and can cope with complicated issues in ipsative data, such as measurement invariance, longitudinal survey, multilevel data structures, ipsative tests with raters, and computerized adaptive testing. These news models and new methods have been well established, evaluated via extensive simulation studies, and applied to several empirical datasets. This project has generated a long-standing impact on theoretical and technical advancements of IRT models for ipsative tests, and operational procedures in design, analysis, and revision of existing and new ipsative tests.

845013.label: Other impact (e.g. award of patents or prizes, collaboration with other research institutions, technology transfer, etc.)
845013.value: Thanks to the continued support from the RGC, EdUHK, and my collaborators, I received the President’s Awards for Outstanding Performance in Research (EdUHK) in March 2016 in recognition of my research excellence. In this project, I have established strong collaboration with Dr. Sage Ro, who works as the director of psychometrics and research department in the IBM software group in USA. Dr Ro's team has developed a workplace personality test with ipsative form and our team has completed the data analysis using the new models. Dr Ro is one of the coauthors of our two key publications. We have created a CAT platform which can be freely downloaded from our website (http://ipsativeproject.weebly.com). Practitioners (e.g., teachers, consultants and human resource officers) can use the platform to help stakeholders (e.g., students, employers, and job applicants) with career guidance and personnel selection. Instructions, computer code, and examples are available on the website as well.

845113.label: Project Title(Chinese)
845113.value: 提升香港4歲幼兒英文口語詞彙量和音韻覺識能力的介入研究

845113.label: Co - Investigator(s)
845113.value: Dr Perry, Conrad Prof Siegel, Linda

845113.label: Project Objectives
845113.value: To investigate the performance differences in oral vocabulary and PA between children from disadvantaged families and those of higher SES To examine the within-group and across-group changes in oral vocabulary and PA over the intervention period To examine the extent to which the children retain their vocabulary and PA knowledge six months after the cessation of the intervention
rows: To investigate the performance differences in oral vocabulary and PA between children from disadvantaged families and those of higher SES
To examine the within-group and across-group changes in oral vocabulary and PA over the intervention period
To examine the extent to which the children retain their vocabulary and PA knowledge six months after the cessation of the intervention

845113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
845113.value: Language and literacy research has shown that children’s oral vocabulary status and their level of phonological awareness (PA; i.e., ability to attend to and manipulate phonemes in words) are predictive of their future success in reading English. In the Hong Kong context, importance is attached to early English exposure, but the quantity and quality of English language input varies widely across kindergartens in the territory. Children from families of low socio-economic status (SES) may be disadvantaged as they may receive little English language support at home and may also have only limited exposure to English in their school environment. Such limited exposure may influence these children’s early vocabulary and development of PA, and their response to intervention. The proposed project, therefore, seeks to examine the effectiveness of a 2-year intervention program that enhances the oral vocabulary and PA of Hong Kong kindergarten children. Vocabulary will be enhanced through the use of detailed discussions centered on specific topics and PA will be enhanced through stories and games that directly focus on the sound structure of English. Three types of programs will be compared: the target intervention developed in this proposal, a language experience program (i.e., non-target intervention) developed by Wong (2009), and a non-intervention control group. Both high and low SES groups will be recruited, and the children’s (N= 240) vocabulary and PA will be tested at four time points: pre-test, during intervention, post-test, and 6 months after the program. In other words, a 3 (Training Group) × 2 (SES) × 4 (Time) design will be used, resulting in six groups of 40 children that will be tested at four different times. To control for possible teacher bias, the transcripts of teacher-child interactions will be analyzed in terms of lexical diversity, mean length of utterance, the use of various communication strategies in classroom interactions, and other potentially confounding variables. 研究顯示，「英文口語詞彙理解能力」(指個人所理解的英文口語詞彙) 與「音韻覺識能力」(指個人能否專注於和運用構成英文生字的個別語音) 能有效預測幼兒將來的閱讀能力。在香港，一般家庭都相當重視幼兒的早期英語學習，然而本地幼兒學校在課堂上使用英語的質和量都存在很大的差異。來自基層家庭的幼兒在英語學習上面對較大的挑戰：他們在家中未必有機會接觸英語，而在校的英語上課時間可能亦很有限。這些環境因素很可能影響他們的英文口語詞彙量和音韻覺識能力，以及他們對教學介入的反應。本研究計劃將會推行一項爲期兩年的教學介入，透過討論形式的活動和針對語音的故事及遊戲，以提升幼兒的英文口語詞彙理解和音韻覺識能力。在研究方法上，我們會招募來自基層和非基層的幼兒各120名。他們會被編入三組：（一）標靶教學介入組（幼兒透過大量談話活動和語音遊戲學習英文）；（二）非標靶教學介入組（幼兒透過全語文學習法學習英文）和（三）對照組。幼兒在K1至K3期間，會接受五次語言評估。爲了進一步了解和控制教學差異對幼兒的影響，部分課堂内容將被錄音，用作分析老師們在互動策略、詞彙和句長等方面上之差異。

845113.label: Realisation of objectives
845113.value: Objective 1: This objective was achieved. With respect to English receptive vocabulary, we found a 13.32 point difference at the beginning of the intervention between the high and low SES groups (120 children in each group). Also, this achievement gap between the two groups had widened by the end of the intervention (a 20.65 point difference). With respect to PA, the achievement gap between the two groups was not pronounced. The two SES groups had the same score at the beginning of the study (1.93), and the high SES group only scored 1.02 point higher than the lower SES group by the end of the intervention. Objective 2: This objective was achieved. The participating children from the two SES groups were assigned to one of three conditions: (1) target intervention (extended discussions after shared reading sessions + PA training); (2) non-target intervention (no extended discussions after shared reading sessions + PA training); and (3) no intervention. In the area of vocabulary, a comparison of pre- and post-test scores (scores obtained at the end of intervention – scores obtained at the beginning of intervention) revealed that within the low SES group, the children receiving the target intervention had made the highest gain in vocabulary (with a 13.05 point difference), and the children receiving no intervention had made the least gain (with a 7.23 point difference), whereas the gain made by the non-target intervention group fell in the middle. The patterns of results were basically the same for the high SES group. However, of note is that by the end of the intervention, the vocabulary status of the low SES children receiving the target intervention (score: 23.89) was still lower than the average initial vocabulary score (score: 24.54) and the average end vocabulary score (score 41.7) of the high SES children. In the area of PA, within the low SES group, the children in the three conditions performed poorly in a 10-item sound-matching task (target: 2; non-target: 1.84; control: 1.96). All groups gained less than 1 point by the end of the intervention. The patterns of results were similar for the higher SES group, except that the high SES group had made a 1.87 point gain over the intervention period. Objective 3: This objective was achieved. Irrespective of treatment conditions, at six months after the cessation of the intervention, the children’s English vocabulary scores and PA scores were higher than the corresponding scores at the end of the intervention. However, when examining the different conditions, we found that the children in the control condition had made the most gain in their oral vocabulary during the six-month period following the end of the intervention, although their “retention” score (test results at six months after the end of the intervention) was still lower than the corresponding score of the target condition group. With respect to PA, mixed results were observed for the two SES groups. For the low SES group, the target and non-target groups had made the most gain in the six-month period following the end of the intervention. On the other hand, for the high SES group, the control group had made the most gain in their PA skills.

845113.label: Major findings and research outcome
845113.value: 1. The vocabulary skills but not phonological awareness (PA) skills of children from families with a lower socioeconomic status (SES) have improved after having received the target intervention program 120 four-year-old low SES children were assigned to one of three conditions: target intervention, non-target intervention and no intervention. The duration of treatment across all conditions was 44 weeks. A comparison of pre- and post-test scores revealed that the children receiving the target intervention had made the highest gain in English receptive vocabulary (with a 13.05 point difference), and the children receiving no intervention had made the least gain (with a 7.23 point difference), whereas the gain made by the non-target intervention group fell in the middle. With respect to PA, by the end of the intervention, all of the low SES children still performed poorly in the sound matching task (see 5.3 above). The data suggested that extended discussions centering upon the content of storybooks (e.g., what did you like about the story? Do you like the ending? Why or why not?) can improve the English vocabulary skills of low SES children, compared to other conditions. However, PA training appears to be ineffective for 4-year-old low SES children. 2. There was an SES-related achievement gap in vocabulary at the beginning of the intervention, and the gap had widened after the intervention. When comparing the performance differences between the two SES groups in this study in terms of their initial vocabulary status and their vocabulary growth, we found a 13.32 point difference at the beginning of the study, and the gap between the two groups had widened by the end of the intervention (a 20.65 point difference). In the area of PA, although the two SES groups had the same score at the beginning of the study (1.93), the higher SES group scored 1.02 point higher than the lower SES group by the end of intervention. Since all of the participants had the same amount of English instruction time at school, the initial differences in vocabulary might have been caused by factors other than school, such as exposure to English at home. If the Government wants to narrow the SES-related achievement gap in early English vocabulary, besides providing support to schools (e.g., by providing onsite support related to effective English teaching strategies), targeting the home environment might be important because of the achievement gap evident at the beginning stage of preschool education.

845113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
845113.value: (1) The participating children are now in their second year of primary education. It will be useful to conduct a follow-up study to investigate whether the achievement gap between the two SES groups has changed overtime. (2) Because an achievement gap between the SES groups was already evident at the beginning of the intervention, a possible line of future research would be to investigate the relationship between SES and home support available for enhancing young children’s English in different Hong Kong families. (3) Whilst there are policies targeting the Chinese language development of non-Chinese-speaking children in Hong Kong preschools, there are no policies which focus on the English language development of children from disadvantaged families. Another possible line of future research would be to conduct a policy study that aims to examine the types of support that can be offered to preschools serving disadvantaged families, with the goal of maximizing the English learning experience of children from disadvantaged families.

845113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
845113.value: This study examined the influence of a one-year English intervention program on the English oral vocabulary and phonological awareness (PA) skills of 240 Hong Kong preschoolers, with half of the children from families with a lower socioeconomic status (SES). Children from the high and low SES groups were assigned to one of three conditions: target intervention, non-target intervention and no intervention. Results showed that within the low SES group, the children receiving the target intervention had made the highest gain in vocabulary, and the children receiving no intervention made the least gain, whereas the gain made by the non-target intervention group fell in the middle. However, of greater importance is the fact that if we simply compare the two SES groups in terms of their initial vocabulary status and their vocabulary growth, we found a 13.32 point difference at the beginning of the study, and the achievement gap had widened over the intervention. With respect to PA, by the end of the intervention, all of the low SES children still performed poorly in the sound matching task. In terms of significance, the data showed that whilst quality English instructions can help enhance the English vocabulary skills of low SES children, intervention at the level of school may not be adequate in removing initial SES-related achievement gaps. Also, PA intervention for children below age 5 might not be beneficial.
