859113.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
859113.value: This project aims to investigate age differences in cognitive control and control strategies and emotional experiences in daily life, and how these processes impact physical and emotional health over time. In-depth understanding of our everyday experiences is essential for the study of human stress resilience. Positive affect in positive daily events is inversely associated with physiological stress responses (i.e., cortisol levels) whereas negative affect in negative daily events is positively associated with these responses. Daily positive affect and negative affect also predict affective symptoms among people with depression in respective directions, but no previous studies have contextualized the link between daily emotional experiences and long-term physical and emotional health within normal adult development. Older adults relative to younger adults demonstrate higher cortisol levels, report lower negative affect, and are more motivated to enhance positive affect. Older adults also differ from younger adults in coping with stress, for they are more likely to change themselves to fit with environmental demands because of their declining physical and mental resources for attaining desired goals. Chinese younger (n=120) and late middle-age (n=120) adults will be recruited and interviewed at baseline (T1) and at 12-month (T2) follow-up. In the seven days following the T1 assessment, participants will complete self-reported measures five times a day to include: momentary events, i.e., valence of the events at the sampling moment, control strategies, i.e., making changes to the environment to fit with personal wishes or making changes to themselves to fit with environmental demands, and emotional experiences, i.e., positive and negative affect. Physiological stress responses, i.e., salivary cortisol levels, affective symptoms, i.e., anxiety and depression, and cognitive control, i.e., abilities to vary thoughts and actions in relation to one’s goals, will be assessed at T1 and T2. We shall provide robust evidence on (i) age differences in cognitive control and the use of control strategies in daily life, (ii) age differences in the impact of control strategies on the associations between cognitive control and emotional experiences in daily life, and (iii) age differences in the association between emotional experiences in daily life and physiological stress responses and affective symptoms over time. This project will significantly contribute to aging and health psychology research by delineating the cognition-emotion interactions that characterize human resilience. The potential findings will inform development of age-appropriate, ecologically valid training protocols for enhancing physical and emotional health of people across the adult lifespan. 是項研究計劃目的是探究日常生活中的認知控制能力、控制策略和情緒體驗上的年齡差異，以及其對身心健康的長遠影響。在人類壓力抗逆力的研究中，必需深入了解日常生活的經歷。年長的相對年輕的成人有較高皮質醇水平，較少消極情緒及更有動力增加積極情緒。在處理壓力方面，年長和年輕的成人亦有不同表現。研究人員將邀請中國藉的年輕及長者各120 位，分別於基線（T1）和12個月後（T2）進行訪問。在 T1 評估後的七日內，參加者需完成每天量度五次的自填量表。在 T1 和 T2 的評估中，亦會量度參與者面對壓力的生理反應、情緒症狀以及認知控制能力。透過勾畫出塑造人類壓力特徵的認知及情緒間之互動，是項研究將對老齡研究和健康心理學研究作出貢獻。研究所得的結果，有助提升成人階段的身心健康，並提供適齡而具環境效度的訓練建議。

859113.label: Realisation of objectives
859113.value: All the three objectives have been fully achieved. Details about how each objective was realized are given below. Objective 1 and 2. Control strategies is one of the essential elements in this project. To begin with, we sought to identify self-report questionnaire that was suitable for assessing control strategies across adult lifespan. No validated scale or item was available for assessing control strategies in Chinese at the time of study. Our research team adopted a combined etic-emic approach to translate 11 items that were extracted from the Optimization of Primary and Secondary Control Scale (Schulz & Heckhausen, 1998). The Scale has been widely used for assessing preferences for the three control strategies (Chipperfield & Perry, 2006; Hall, Chipperfield, Heckhausen, & Perry, 2010; Haynes et al., 2009). We also checked and ensured that the items were consistent with the most updated version of the theory (Heckhausen et al., 2010). The items were translated into Chinese by a trained bilingual translator and then back translated by a naïve second translator. The original English meanings were preserved while Cantonese expressions that were equivalent to or approximate the English meanings were used. The research team examined and achieved semantic and conceptual equivalence of the original and back-translated versions. Discrepancies in the two versions were resolved by joint meetings between the translators and the research team and when necessary by reiteration of the translation process. We then pilot-tested the items among 46 younger adults (age range =20-25 years; M=21.86, SD=1.53, 36 females) and 16 older adults (age range =65-82 years; M=72.65, SD=5.93, 12 females) using the same experience sampling protocol. Debriefing sessions invited participants’ comments on item wordings and interpretability. The Chinese items were then modified based on their comments. To assess cognitive control, we developed and adopted Simon task (Simon & Small, 1969). In the Simon task, participants were presented with a colored stimulus that appears on the left or the right of fixation, and are required to respond, as quickly and accurately as possible, by pressing the appropriate response key according to the color of stimulus delivered either to the left or to the right of the fixation (Proctor & Lu, 1994). Participants had to respond according to the color of the stimulus while ignoring its spatial location. With valid and reliable self-report measure of control strategies and computerized task of cognitive control, we examined the momentary associations of goal-engagement control strategies with positive and negative emotions in everyday life among younger and older adults. A total of 200 adults (100 younger and 100 older) reported valence (positive/negative) and valence ratings of momentary events, positive and negative emotions, and selective primary control, selective secondary control, and compensatory primary control five times a day over seven days. Controlling for demographic covariates and valence ratings, multilevel modeling revealed that selective primary and secondary control were positively associated with positive emotions in positive events. Compensatory primary control was positively associated with negative emotions in positive events. No age differences were found in the associations between the three control strategies and positive and negative emotions across positive and negative events in everyday life. In another set of analyses, participants with lower cognitive control who increased their use of compensatory primary control strategies that getting help from others would experience more decline in positive emotions under negative events. Selective secondary control was more strongly associated with positive emotions across positive events among adults with lower levels of cognitive control relative to their higher counterparts. Our prospective study is the first of its kind to assess age differences in control strategies and its associations with emotions in everyday life. Our findings provide an important evidence base for subsequent research on the interplay among age-related coping, cognitive ability, and emotional experience in everyday life across the adult lifespan. Objective 3. We have utilized a subsample of our data and analyzed the impact of social movement on everyday emotional reactivity, variability, instability, and persistence, and whether and how these predicted subsequent psychological distress and well-being. Psychological distress and well-being were assessed at baseline (T1) and 3-month follow-up (T2). Hierarchical linear modeling revealed lower valence ratings of positive events during the Umbrella Movement. Lower positive emotional reactivity and higher negative emotional reactivity in positive events were reported during the Movement. Controlling for demographics and T1 scores, the positive association between negative emotional reactivity in positive events and T2 depressive symptoms and the inverse association between positive emotional instability and T2 positive emotions were significant only among the comparison group. The positive association between positive emotional reactivity in positive events and T2 life satisfaction was significant only among the Umbrella Movement group. This project provides novel evidence for developing timely counseling services for enhancing well-being of affected populations during and after social movements.

859113.label: Major findings and research outcome
859113.value: First, this project provides one of the first empirical findings on the associations between goal-engagement control strategies and emotions in everyday life (Part C-8). Control strategies have been assessed as individual differences or traits in previous studies. The current findings add to previous literature by showing that preferences for control strategies could be manifested in individuals’ behavior and associated with emotions in everyday life. In particular, we found that daily practice of selective primary and secondary control was consistently associated with higher emotional well-being across the adult lifespan. This study also provides an initial evidence base for investigating the association of control strategies with positive and negative emotions not only in daily negative and stressful events but also uplifting events across the adult lifespan. Second, we investigated the associations between control strategies and emotional experiences in positive and negative events in everyday life and how this association is moderated by cognitive control and age group (Part C-8). This is a novel direction for investigating age-related differences in the interaction effect of cognitive control and control strategies on navigating positive and negative events in everyday life. Individuals with lower cognitive control who increased their use of strategies such as help seeking would experience higher decline in positive emotions under negative events. Our findings provide an initial evidence base for investigating the association of compensatory primary control with not only in positive emotions in uplifting events but also in daily stressful events across the adulthood lifespan. The moderating effect of cognitive control on selective primary and selective secondary control were more strongly associated with negative emotions in general among younger adults relative to their older counterparts. These implied that younger adults with higher cognitive control who adopted more selective primary control or younger adults with lower cognitive control who adopted more selective secondary control would experience lower levels of negative emotions. Third, this project analyzed emotional reactivity and variations in reactivity in everyday life during social movement and the extent to which these emotional variables predict psychiatric symptoms and subjective well-being post-movement (Part C-8). This evidence has both conceptual and practical implications, as emotion theorists have highlighted the crucial role played by a broad range of contextual factors that influence the nature of emotional experience and expression and the ways in which emotions influence other people and long-term adjustment (Aldao, 2013; Bonanno & Burton, 2013; Cole et al., 1994).

859113.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
859113.value: Future studies can consider the potential role of selective control in capitalizing positive emotions in positive events and cultural differences in the emotional benefit of compensatory primary control across everyday positive and negative events. The causality between control strategies and emotions should also be investigated. For instance, the associations between positive/negative events and control strategies might change as a function of the positive/negative emotions as well. More studies are needed to investigate these interesting and intricate issues relating to control strategies in everyday life. Another promising future direction is that apart from dealing with stressors and regulating practices and routine in everyday life during social movement, our findings in people undergoing social movements suggest that savoring intervention (Smith, Harrison, Kurtz, & Bryant, 2014) could be implemented to facilitate more recalls of past positive events, positive moment-to-moment attentional focus, and anticipation of desirable experiences. This comprehensive approach could be useful for enhancing positive emotions during a period with devalued positive events, contributing in turn to higher subsequent mental health.

859113.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
859113.value: This project aimed to investigate age differences in cognitive ability, preferences in problem solving (e.g., work harder or seek help), and emotional experiences in daily life, and how these processes impact physical and emotional health over time. We recruited a total of 200 Chinese adults (100 younger and 100 older) in Hong Kong. They completed a test of cognitive ability. Then, they reported events and emotions they experienced and problem solving preferences five times a day over seven days. The findings importantly contribute to aging and health psychology research by delineating the cognition-emotion interactions that characterize psychological well-being. The findings will inform development of age-appropriate, ecologically valid training protocols for enhancing physical and emotional health of people across the adult lifespan.

859213.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
859213.value: This proposed study aims to investigate China’s ongoing national health care reforms from a provincial and comparative perspective by examining the cases of Fujian and Shanxi. It intends to contribute to the study of health policy and economics with deeper understanding on the difficulty of implementing health care reforms in a highly decentralised system with huge regional variation, and the actual role played by the provinces in implementing reforms. It will also shed fresh light on the literature of China studies and public administration by substantiating how the provinces as intermediary sub-national governments translate central reform directives and manage local initiatives, depending on their varying fiscal and administrative capacities. The research findings and implications generated will facilitate evidence-based policy learning in China’s ongoing national health care reform. China’s failure in health care reforms has attracted enormous scholarly attention. The literature, however, either focuses heavily on particular interventions with health economics methods, or approaches the reforms from a macro policy perspective. There have been calls for a study of China’s health care reforms from the political economy perspective. Few past studies focused on the provincial governments that have the primary responsibility for implementing health care reforms. From a public administration perspective, little is known about how provincial governments in varying capacities deal with health care reform imperatives and other competing policy agendas. This project adopts a comparative and provincial perspective in examining China's ongoing national health care reform. This is not only due to the crucial role of the provinces in implementing reform programmes, but also because the provinces possess high levels of autonomy and discretion in undertaking local reform initiatives, compounded by fiscal federalism and peculiar political considerations. These largely explain the various approaches taken and different outcomes shown across Chinese localities. Hence, a thorough study from a provincial perspective would greatly supplement the existing literature by enhancing critical knowledge about the political economy of health care reforms in China. For investigation purposes, this study will choose Fujian Province in the east and Shanxi Province in the central west, which present contrasting fiscal and administrative capacities. Among many aspects of health care reforms, this study will specifically focus on how provincial authorities address rapid cost inflation, the primary symptom of China’s ailing system. Employing a multi-level triangulation design, this study will provide an up-to-date review of China’s ongoing health policy reform and draw implications for reforms in transitional and developing countries. 本研究旨在透過對福建省和山西省“醫改”的比較研究，來分析中國大陸正在進行中的醫療衛生政策改革。它對於衛生政策和衛生經濟學的貢獻在於，幫助人們更加深入地理解艱難的醫療改革如何在一個高度商業化和政治分權化並且地區發展不均衡的大國展開，尤其是著重于理解省級政府在大國“醫改”中扮演的角色。本研究同時意在通過對不同財政和行政條件下的省級政府在執行中央政策和推行本地改革中作用的分析，為中國研究做出貢獻。 中國大陸醫療衛生體系的眾多問題以及後續改革已經廣為學界關注。但是目前的研究或者聚焦于對特定政策干預的經濟學分析，或從宏觀面向做出一般分析和描述。近年來已經有學者指出，對中國大陸“醫改”的分析應該更多從政治經濟學角度著重分析地方一級的"醫改"如何實質改變大陸的"看病貴"和"看病難"問題。 目前學界的研究很少關注到省級政府在執行“醫改”政策中扮演的重要角色。從政治學和公共行政的角度來看，對於具有不同財政能力和行政能力的省級政府如何在推進“醫改”的同時，有效進行其他改革，知之甚少。 本研究採用比較研究的方法來檢視中國大陸正在進行中的醫療衛生政策改革中省級政府的作用。選取這個視角的原因首先在於，中國大陸的省級政府具有承上啟下的重要作用，不但需要承接中央政府的政策指令，同時在制定和執行本地改革方案中也擁有較大權力。在中國財政聯邦主義的體制下，由於地區發展不均等原因，在醫療衛生政策改革中，不同省份也呈現出非常不同的特點。對不同省份的比較研究將可以深化人們對於中國大陸省一級公共政策規律的認識。 本研究選擇在東部的福建省和中西部的山西省展開，這兩省代表著經濟和財政實力較強的富裕省份和相對落後省份。中國大陸醫療衛生領域的眾多問題中，最為突出的莫過於超常規增長的醫療費用。因此本研究著重分析省級政府在執行中央政策過程中如何控制醫療費用的過快增長。 本研究使用多層三角檢驗的研究設計，通過量化和質化相結合的方式進行研究。研究結果不但將提供關於中國大陸“醫改”的最新發現，亦將為發展中國家和轉軌國家的醫療衛生政策改革提供借鑒。

859213.label: Realisation of objectives
859213.value: Objective #1 has been largely realized. Extensive in-depth interviews and analysis of secondary qualitative data have helped us deepen our understanding on the implementational structure of health policy in China, especially the role played by provincial governments. The PI’s manuscript (submitted to the China Quarterly; currently under revision) and one of the Co-I’s articles at Journal of Asian Public Policy provide analysis on this regard. When proposing Objectives #2 and #3, significant variation was hypothesized. Interestingly, the actual fieldwork revealed much less variation than anticipated. One of the Co-I’s articles at Journal of Asian Public Policy offers an institutionalist explanation. We argue that the inertia is structural in nature, compounded by bureaucratic interests. It needs to be reported that the fieldwork in Shanxi encountered challenges as a key informant in the provincial health bureau left the organization and thus wasn't able to provide more assistance in data collection and referring additional interviewees. The research team attempted to overcome this by collecting more open-source materials and mapping the structure from the bottom (health care providers and middle-level bureaucrats). Objective #4 has been adequately realized. The pilot program of clinical pathway in Shanxi Province, as a flagship reform initiative was evaluated with a mixed-methods approach. The evaluation was published in the International Journal of Health Care Quality Assurance. In Fujian, the experiment of alternative payment methods has been a key reform initiative. The PI’s coauthored article at International Journal of Healthcare provided more accurate estimation of payment costs, with a specific disease as tracer. While the project was rolling out, the health care reform in Sanming City of Fujian Province became a national star of local health reforms. The research team has paid heavy attention to the progress and achievements of this reform. A qualitative study based on Sanming’s reform has been submitted to the China Quarterly and is currently under revision. Objective #5 has been adequately achieved. General policy implications and specific (technical) recommendations have been drawn based on our analytical results and can be found in our research outputs. Some research outputs emerged from this project have been cited by a very high-profile research report released by the World Bank, World Health Organization and the Chinese Government, entitled Healthy China: Deepening Health Reform in China, Building High-Quality and Value-Based Service Delivery.

859213.label: Major findings and research outcome
859213.value: As the intermediary level of the entire administrative machinery, provincial governments are supposed to play a very important role in health policy implementation. However, we found an inertia and sometimes resistance in their response to centrally imposed reform mandates and local policy innovations. In the case of Shanxi, the implementation of central policy program appeared fairly passive, without considering the incentive environment that powerfully shaped provider behaviors. Therefore, as revealed in the PI’s article published in the International Journal of Health Care Quality Assurance, providers are often trapped in conflicting incentives which in turn resulted in limited reform outcomes. In the case of Fujian, the PI’s under-revision manuscript (submitted to the China Quarterly) provides more detailed account for the dynamics of local health care reforms, especially the tension between local policy entrepreneurs and conservative provincial authorities that tend to obstruct “bold” reforms in order to defend their own bureaucratic interests. The same manuscript also finds several important strategies adopted by entrepreneurial reformers in their maneuver within the fragmented bureaucracy in order to push the reform. One of the Co-I’s articles in Journal of Asian Public Policy elucidates the fundamental institutional reasons for the observed bureaucratic behaviors, and argues that a reallocation of authority within the administrative system is necessary to pave the way for effective health care reforms. Overall, this project suggests mixed outcomes of China’s ambitious health care reform and argues for the critical importance of reversing not only the perverse incentives that drive provider behaviors but also bureaucratic incentives that determine the behaviors of policy implementation agents. This project has led to a collection of journal articles and a special issue, some of which attracted attention from a very high-profile research report of the World Bank, the World Health Organization and China’s central ministries, serving as strong testament of the impact of this project. As reported in the mid-term report, when the project was rolling out, the escalation of doctor-patient tension in China started to attract enormous attention in both the society and the academia. The damaged relationship between doctors and patients is reflective of the deficiencies of the ongoing health care reform. The research team decided to pay additional efforts to investigate this issue. Three articles were published in referred international journals including Social Science and Medicine, Health Economics Policy and Law, and Public Organization Review. ***One of the research outputs titled "Reallocating authority in the Chinese health system: an institutional perspective" should have acknowledged the funding of this project. The PI sincerely apologizes for this error.*** perspective

859213.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
859213.value: As one of the biggest health policy interventions in the world, China’s ongoing national health care reform offers an invaluable window for examining not only health care issues but also policy and governance logics in this authoritarian system. While undertaking this project, we have become interested in the variety of reform models observed throughout the country. What structural factors explain the variation? Does some form of policy diffusion exist? These questions are of theoretical as well as policy significance in terms of understanding the logic of policy experimentation, a key feature of policy process in China. We are interested in pursuing another research project to answer them. We have planned to apply the General Research Fund (GRF) scheme in 2017.

859213.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
859213.value: This project employs both quantitative and qualitative methods in analyzing health policy reforms in a highly commercialized and decentralized system and the role played by provinces as crucial intermediary agents in policy implementation and reform management. It has also evaluated two important reform initiatives in two representative provinces, generating evidence-based recommendations. This research project has led to the publication of several journal articles, some of which have been cited by a leading report of the World Bank, World Health Organization and the Chinese government.

859413.label: Project Title(Chinese)
859413.value: 微塑膠在香港的河流、沿海地區及海洋環境中的質量與來源

859413.label: Project Objectives
859413.value: Establish a baseline for the spatial distribution for the different types of marine microplastic debris in Hong Kong and their abundance; Identify the sources of microplastics in Hong Kong waters through a program of fieldwork; Determine the concentration of DDT adsorbed by microplastic fragments in different environments; and Determine the relative abundance of macro- and microplastics.

Determine the relative abundance of macro- and microplastics.

859413.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
859413.value: The ocean is one of the final sinks for anthropogenic solid waste. Accumulation of marine debris is ubiquitous on a global scale. It is a relatively well established fact that there is abundance of macrodebris in the oceans, easily identified by the naked eye, which is adversely impacting the marine environment. There has been general agreement that plastic is the dominant form of marine debris. However, a portion of the plastic debris that has been overlooked by the scientific community consists of debris of smaller particle sizes, known as microplastics. The plastic pellet spillage which occurred in Hong Kong waters in July 2012 represents one of the many sources of microplastic pollution. These smaller plastic particles have a potential toxic effect on the biota. The toxicity may originate from the plastic itself or from the adsorbed hydrophobic pollutants such as DDT. It is suggested that accidental ingestion of microplastics by marine fauna is a potential pathway through which organic pollutants are transferred to the food chain. Hong Kong is known to produce significant amounts of plastic waste annually. Moreover, Guangdong Province nearby accounts for up to a quarter of the total production of plastics in China. There is a lack of information on the abundance, temporal and spatial distribution of the various major types of microplastics in the fluvial, littoral and marine environments of Hong Kong. Furthermore, only very limited data on DDTs adsorbed by microplastics in Hong Kong have been reported. This knowledge gap needs to be filled in order for Hong Kong to understand the extent and severity of this emerging environmental issue. This is important because the marine waters of Hong Kong represent precious resource in terms of recreation, ecology and biodiversity and mariculture. Through sample collection from different environments in Hong Kong with the employment of different sampling methods (marine, beach and fluvial surveys) and the application of laboratory analyses by visual identification and instrumental aids, the proposed project aims to produce a “master map” showing the temporal, spatial and abundance distribution of different types of marine microplastic debris in Hong Kong as well as to identify their sources. This “master map” would be an important source of intelligence from an environmental management perspective as monitoring with good quality data can provide a platform for comprehensive assessment of the nature and origin of microplastics, and through which, appropriate management intervention can be brought in, where necessary. 由人類的產生的固體廢物最終會落入海洋。現時，海洋垃圾的堆積已成為全球的一個普遍情況。對於能夠被肉眼觀測的大型海洋垃圾對環境的影響，人類都有比較豐富和完善的認識。塑膠一直被認為是海洋垃圾的主要組成物。然而，科學界一直忽略塑膠廢物的一個部分──塑膠小顆粒，亦稱為微塑膠。在2012年7月，曾有大量塑膠粒散落在香港水域，這事件是微塑膠污染的一個實例。這些細小的塑膠粒的潛在毒性會為生物群帶來影響。其毒性源自塑膠粒本身或者透過吸附疏水性污染物，例如DDT。海洋生物誤食微塑膠是一個有機污染物轉移到食物鏈的潛在途徑。 香港每年產生大量的塑膠廢物。此外，鄰近的廣東地區的塑膠原材料生產佔全中國總產量的四分之一。對位於珠江口的香港而言，這無疑是個微塑膠污染的潛在來源。然而，我們對於微塑膠在香港各主要河流、沿海地區和海域的時空分佈的資料是缺乏的。另外，關於DDT吸附在本土的微塑膠的資料也是鮮有被報告。為了評估這個新出現的環境問題對香港的影響程度及其嚴重性，我們確有需要填補在這方面的知識差距。這對於香港是十分重要的，因為香港的近岸海域是供康樂活動、海水養殖以及生態／生物多樣性保育方面的重要資源。 是次的項目會在香港的不同地區，利用抽樣方法對海洋、海灘及河流作出調查。另外，透過目測和儀器分析樣本，我們希望能夠產生一個顯示在香港海洋微塑膠時空分佈的「主圖譜」，以識別它們的來源。從環境管理方面而言，這個「主圖譜」為全面評估微塑膠的特性和來源作提供一個平台，並藉著它開發出相應的干預措施。

859413.label: Realisation of objectives
859413.value: An extensive fieldwork programme on microplastic (MP) and macro debris had been carried out in Hong Kong in winter and summer of 2015. To achieve the objectives of the project, 200 samples from 25 sandy (non-gazetted) beaches (littoral environment); 60 neuston net samples from 15 sites around the local coastal waters (marine environment); and x samples from the Taipo river (fluvial environment) were collected. During the process of sample analysis, it had been realized that visual identification of microplastics from a sediment matrix (littoral samples) and volume-reduced sample from neuston net (marine and river samples) took considerably more time than expected. For example, the four samples in Fun Lau East beach took nearly one month to identify and count in total, due to the sheer number of plastic pieces extracted from the sand. Because of quality control concerns, we resisted the idea of hiring more student helpers to carry out identification and enumeration procedures. We have then resorted to sub-sampling. For sediment samples, we adopted a shuffle sample splitter and for wet samples, a Folsom plankton sample splitter had been used. In addition, the manta net, which is designed for taking marine samples, were too large for the small river channels in Hong Kong. A custom made neuston net sampler had been constructed to overcome the issue. Objective 1: This study involved systematic methods to survey and analysis the abundance of MP in Hong Kong. Because this is the first of its kind, the data represent a baseline for the area. It is discovered that on sandy beaches, the abundance for MP was 3242 ± 1991 (SE) items per m2. Compared to similar studies done elsewhere, the local abundance is relatively high. For the marine environment, MP densities was found at 3.97 ± 1.18 items per m3. The density of marine MP in Hong Kong is comparable to other marine studies. In river, the density was higher than what was observed in the marine environment, at 7.49 ± 3.68 pieces/m3. It was also observed that EPS fragments were the most abundant type of MP, both in our littoral and marine samples, whilst fibre and films were the dominant type of MP in the fluvial samples. Objective 2: A significant difference in seasonal abundance had also been observed for beach samples (wet season 5595 ± 3950; dry season 889 ± 350) and marine samples (wet season 6.12 ± 2.12; dry season 0.26 ± 0.09). The spatiotemporal distribution of MP in both littoral and marine environments in Hong Kong pointed to the fact that the Pearl River is a major potential source of the local MP pollution. This is also in agreement with a recent study carried out at the very mouth of Changjiang, where the observed MP density was 400 times higher than what was found in this study, in which samples were obtained from at least 40 km from the mouth of the Pearl River. Objective 3: Due to the low environmental concentration of DDT, a large sample size is required for the determination of this organic pollutant. The DDT and its metabolites were detected on all MP samples collected from two sandy beaches. And the concentrations were 6.09 ± 1.10 ppb, 5.06 ± 0.68 ppb and 8.64 ± 1.08 ppb for DDE, DDD and DDT respectively. The values are comparable to that observed in the same area by the International Pellet Watch, which analysis were only based on pellet samples (representing only a small fraction of the MP assemblage). In addition, the DDT/(DDD+DDE) ratio pointed out that the DDT in the eastern side of Hong Kong may have a “fresher” source. Objective 4: From the beach samples, 87%, and 86% of all plastic debris collected were MP, for the littoral and marine samples respectively. Due to the small size of the custom net, no large plastics were collected in our river samples.

859413.label: Major findings and research outcome
859413.value: The study had established a baseline on microplastic and large debris abundances in different environments in Hong Kong. Results illustrated that Hong Kong, and coastal South China Sea in general, is a hotspot of MP pollution. The spatiotemporal distribution of MP in both littoral and marine environments in Hong Kong pointed to the fact that the Pearl River is a major potential source of the local MP pollution. While the relative abundance of MP represented more than 85% of all plastic debris. These findings serve as a reference point for further evaluation of the severity of local microplastic and large plastic debris pollution.

859413.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
859413.value: Our results demonstrate that the nearby Pearl River is a major potential source of both microplastics and large debris found in Hong Kong. Evidence have showed that the river input can modulate the spatio-temporal distribution of plastic debris in both the local littoral and marine environments. Further investigation naturally points to a survey of microplastic densities in the Pearl River.

859413.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
859413.value: Micropalstic (MP) pollution is recognized by the UNEP as an emerging global environmental issue in 2014. MP are small plastic debris which is potentially harmful, physically and chemically, to a wide range of biota. This pollutant has also been identified in various habitats. Home to nearly 60 million population, the Pearl River Delta is one of the most densely populated river deltas in the world. The amount of plastics produced and discarded in this region is enormous. As it rains, the mismanaged plastic waste will be washed into the drainage systems and eventually into the ocean. Nonetheless, there have been no systematic study with regard to MP abundance at the Pearl River Estuary. This study had established a baseline on MP and large debris abundances in different environments in Hong Kong. Results illustrated that Hong Kong is a hotspot of MP pollution. The spatial distribution of MP in both littoral and marine environments of Hong Kong pointed to the fact that the Pearl River is a major potential source of the local pollution. These findings serve as a reference point for further evaluation of the severity of local MP and large plastic debris pollution.

859613.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
859613.value: Pavarotti said in a broadcast from Lincoln Centre, “before I sing a tone I must have thought it”. According to voice teachers, who describe imagery as a condition for learning, “the musician lives in a world of imageries”. Voice teachers and vocal pedagogical literature often cite verbal imagery (e.g., “sing as if you are biting an apple”) as a teaching tool for communicating desirable physical sensations, vocal characteristics, musical interpretations, concepts of vocal production, and appropriate vocal quality. Indeed, voice teachers use verbal imagery to unlock and communicate physical sensations, and to describe vocal characteristics and musical attributes that are often difficult, if not impossible, to literally describe. While both practitioners and researchers consider verbal imageries to be a fundamental means of communication in contemporary teaching and learning of singing, there is a dearth of objective and systematic research concerning verbal imagery not only in vocal pedagogy but in music education as well. Hence, a pilot study using the newly designed observation and interview form (OIF) as a reporting instrument for investigating the nature and effectiveness of verbal imagery in vocal studios in Beijing and Houston was conducted by the principal investigator to serve as PhD thesis. The conduct of this project shall consequently be followed by the publication of a book relating to verbal imagery in vocal pedagogy. The purpose of this project is to identify the role and efficacy of verbal imagery in the teaching and learning of voice using the previously tested OIF in the case study of reputable voice teachers and their students in Greater China, particularly at Beijing Conservatory of Music, Shanghai Conservatory of Music, Hong Kong Academy of Performing Arts, and Taipei Municipal University of Education. The principal investigator intends to develop an insight on verbal imagery as means of communication specifically for identifying the nature and effectiveness of verbal imagery in the teaching and learning of voice used in the Chinese language and culture. Data analysis will focus not only on how verbal imageries are used as a teaching tool, but on how students perceive those verbal imageries in enhancing vocal quality and music performance as well. In-depth case studies involving observation of singing lessons as well as interview sessions with voice teachers and their students will offer first-hand data and insights based on the pedagogical wisdom of the voice teachers and the practical experience of their students in using verbal imagery in singing. 名男高音帕伐絡第曾在林肯中心的廣播中說過，『我演唱每一個音前，必定仔細想過。』由此可知聲樂家在發聲，演繹作品及角色上多與想像力和心理科學緊密連接。 許多聲樂老師和音樂學者都認同，藉由形象、比喻和隱喻法是音樂學習中必備的狀態，因為『音樂家在豐富的想像世界裡進行溝通』。 聲樂老師和聲樂教學的文獻時常形容，使用形象、比喻和隱喻法利於有效及有系統的傳授唱歌時身體的感受，正確及舒適的發聲法，演繹聲樂作品所需的音色、情感及角色 (例如，『想像開嘴唱歌的口型有如咬頻果一樣』)。 由於聲樂老師無法在示範時完全的展現身體內部肌肉的用法和協調性，使用形象、比喻和隱喻法的聲樂教學法早已行之多時，成為現代聲樂教學法不可或缺的利器。 但是多年以來在此方面的研究幾乎微之其微，因此作者於其博士論文，專門研討使用形象、比喻和隱喻法的相關試驗性研究，研究對象包括在中國北京和美國休士頓著名的聲樂老師；此研究並已出版成書。 現時研究計畫的目的在於使用前試驗性研究所得的研究結果和經驗，深入大中華地區的四個指標性音樂學院：例如北京中央音樂學院、上海音樂學院、香港演藝學院及台北市立教育大學，利用觀測教學過程和訪談著名聲樂老師以剖析如何使用形象、比喻和隱喻法的聲樂教學法，如何使用中文來溝通形象、比喻和隱喻法的特徵及其細節，同時也訪談被觀測教學過程的聲樂學生，在學習過程中是否利用形象、比喻和隱喻法和老師溝通及幫助學習。

859713.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
859713.value: 傳統粵語方言學研究主要以田野調查為手段，通過對年長的發音人來了解有關方言的面貌。過去二十多年，不少十九世紀至二十世紀初用粵語編寫的方言材料陸續被發現，粵語歷時研究成為了另一個研究重點。這些早期方言材料反映二十世紀中葉前後，粵語出現不少重要轉變，當時的粵語很有可能同時存在變化前後的語言特徵。另一方面，現今距離二十世紀中葉已有六十多年，粵語應當有不少的變化，然而很少研究探討二十世紀中葉時期的粵語，而且當時的粵語材料，相比十九世紀時代，也十分少。 我們認為單憑和年長的發音人做訪問調查並不能夠全面地和準確地了解早期語言的面貌。本研究項目擬運用「實時方法」(real time approach)，搜集當時實實在在使用過的語言材料。 本項目的語料會以香港五六十年代粵語長片的對白為基礎。本項目會把五十套電影（包括不同體裁，內容，粵劇除外）的對白記錄下來，進行初步處理後，如分詞和注音，並建構成語料庫。語料庫將會配以檢索功能，並在網上分享，好讓其他有興趣的學者使用。 通過這些語料，我們可以分析半世紀前香港粵語在詞匯，語義和句法等各範疇的面貌，同時也可以跟十九世紀粵語和現代粵語進行比較，對粵語過去約二百年的發展，有進一步的了解。除了語言學研究，這些語料也可以用來探討語言和香港社會文化的關係。

859713.label: Major findings and research outcome
859713.value: This project adopted a corpus-based approach to study the diachronic development of Hong Kong Cantonese. The corpus data was drawn from the dialogues of 60 Cantonese movies (also known as 粵語長片) produced between 1940 and 1970. A total of 61 hours of speech data was transcribed. The corpus has 764k character tokens and 5200+ word types and 376k word tokens [objective 1]. With this amount of corpus data, we are able to carry out a number of studies on the Cantonese language. There are two types of research that can be carried out with this set of corpus data. 1. Examining the linguistic features of Cantonese in the mid-20th century (objectives 2 and 3). One of the output of the project is a paper on the verbal aspect 着 as in the sentences like 好揀唔揀,揀着個爛燈盞. This aspect marker is rarely used in contemporary and is often left out in the study of Cantonese aspectual system. The movie dialogues allowed us to extract not just the sentences containing this aspect marker, but also the context in which it is used. These allow us to have a better picture about the usage of the marker concerned (refer to the joint paper by Lai Yik Po and the PI). 2. The interactive nature of corpus data can allow us to conduct studies from the discourse and sociolinguistic perspectives. One of the studies is on classifiers. Previous studies on Cantonese classifiers focus on their usage in terms of describing the dimensions of the objects, and the properties of definiteness. There is one usage of Cantonese classifiers which was not studied before - the co-referential usage of classifiers. One example is 你個衰女 in which 你 is co-referential with 衰女 meaning that "you, the bad daughter" instead of "your bad daughter". The joint paper by the PI and his RA (Crono Tse) examined the similarities and differences of this classifier usage and those of the possessive usage. There are a number of discourse factors involved in this usage which are not found in the possessive usage. The recent paper by the PI and his RA (Ou Lili) examines the kinship terms found in the corpus and how the development of these terms can reflect the societal development and family structure of mid-20th century Hong Kong. Another paper by the PI is on the rhetorical function of xiehouyun 歇後語, which is like riddles. Through the examination of xiehouyu used in the movie, we explored some deeper issues related to human communication such as why people only express the riddle (謎面) but not the answer (謎底) which in fact is the intended meaning of the speaker. That paper attempted to explore the explore this issue in terms of rhetorical function (修辭功能). The project has also attracted media's attention. As listed in the Section C, the PI was invited to introduce the corpus as well as the research outcomes and Cantonese studies. Overall speaking, the project has achieved the three objectives satisfactorily and successfully.

859713.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
859713.value: The data of this project does not only provide linguistic data for Cantonese linguistics studies. It also serves as a basis for developing other resources for the area of Digtial Humanities. Besides traditional keyword search, the new corpus also incorporates theasurus information from 《實用廣州話分類詞典》compiled by Mai Yun and Tan Bukang. The theasurus data provides more information to examine words with semantic relatedness. For example, searching the word 爸爸 will also yield the results of 爹哋, 老竇, etc. Other relevant kinship terms such as 媽媽, 仔女, etc. will also be retrieved and presented for users' reference. This kind of ontological and lexical semantic information is important for studying words that can bears cultural elements. For example, the transportation tools of mid-20th century differ significantly from contemporary. This search algorithm can capture this kind of information. At present, no such ontological tools have been developed for the Cantonese language. The corpus data can thus serve as a basis for this new direction of research in Cantonese linguistics which has been focusing on the language internal system.

859713.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
859713.value: This project took on a real-time and corpus-based approach to study the linguistic change and situation of Hong Kong Cantonese in the mid-20th century. The data of the project came from one of the most valuable cultural assests - early Cantonese movies. Dialogues of 60 Cantonese movies produced between 1940 and 1970 were transcribed to produce a textual database which can help us to reconstruct the Cantonese language of six decades ago. The data can also help us to trace the changes of the language since then. In addition, we can also look at some socio-cultural issues through the language used in the period concerned. Kinship terms are one of the examples. At the same time, the interactive dialogic nature of the corpus data also allows us to look at the use of Cantonese at the pragmatic and discourse levels. This project can be seen as a timely response to the First Inventory of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Hong Kong released by the Hong Kong SAR Government in June 2014. Mid-20th century was a critical period in Hong Kong's history during which a large number of immigrants with diverse cultural and language backgrounds came to Hong Kong. Nonetheless, Cantonese remains an important language in Hong Kong today, which is still spoken as the first language by the majority of Hong Kong's population. Placing the project under this historical and sociolinguistic context, the project would not only advance our understanding of the development of Cantonese, but also the inter-relationship between language, society and culture.

859813.label: Project Objectives
859813.value: Describe how Chinese laypersons reason about their immorality judgments, with participants from the Mainland and Hong Kong helping define the diversity of Chinese moral principles. Use a combined emic-etic approach (Cheung, van de Vijver, & Leong, 2011) to test and extend Moral Foundations Theory (Haidt & Joseph, 2004), by comparing Chinese-generated principles to those generated by Moral Foundations Theory. Document how Chinese laypersons think about uncouth behavior, showing that Mainland students in particular perceive uncivilized behavior to be “immoral,” and use this data to challenge current thinking on the psychological division between morals and conventions (Turiel, 1998). Illustrate the practical consequences of the moralization of uncouth behavior for interpersonal interactions by examining the degree to which Chinese judgments of uncivilized behavior match consequences usually dependent on having a sense of moral conviction (Skitka, Bauman, & Sargis, 2005), such as social distancing.

859813.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
859813.value: Moral judgments are among the most important and motivating of psychological phenomena, making cultural differences in what is considered to be immoral a significant source of negative impact on cross-cultural interactions. But our recent research on Chinese concepts of immoral behavior suggests that not only are there cultural differences in what is considered to be immoral, but that Chinese categories of immoral behavior challenge basic assumptions in Western theories of moral cognition. For example, philosophers have argued that Confucian morality concepts are intrinsically connected with appropriate social behavior, an assertion supported by our recent finding that more Beijing university students apply the word “immoral” to “talking and laughing loudly in a public place” than “killing someone.” Such findings question the psychological distinction between morals and conventions as well as the assumption that the most seriously wrong acts are would universally be considered immoral. Most important, it suggests that more research into Chinese concepts of morality is vitally needed to inform theories of moral cognition. Using a multi-method approach, this investigation builds on our recent and ongoing research to examine the following research questions: 1. Do recently influential, Western-developed theories of universal moral principles (i.e. Moral Foundation Theory; Haidt & Joseph, 2004) fit indigenous Chinese ideas of why behaviors are immoral? Or do Chinese morality concepts require explanation by new “moral foundations” that are not yet included in the list? 2. Do Chinese truly treat social norms for civilized behavior as an intrinsic aspect of morality, and does that mean that a) theories of a universal mental division between moral rules vs. social conventions are implausible (Turiel, 1998), and b) that severe interpersonal consequences will arise from violations of Chinese social conventions (for ingroup members, but not members of other cultures)? The study of Chinese concepts of morality is of particular interest, due to both China’s unique moral traditions and its ever-growing international prominence. Moreover, China is a culturally diverse nation, with competing claims on citizens’ moral systems. This project addresses basic philosophical and practical questions about the nature of morality. Two sets of studies are proposed with the goal of both testing and extending current influential theories of morality. We hope that findings from this research program will shed light on the practical and theoretical consequences of cultural differences in moral concepts, thus telling us more about the possibilities of human moral cognition. 道德判断是最重要的和最能影響行為的心理现象之一，所以不同文化對何謂不道德的不同理解可成為负面跨文化交流的重要原因。我们近期所做的关于中国人對不道德行为的概念的研究却顯示，除了对何謂不道德有文化差异外，中国人視為不道德行为的种类與西方道德认知理論的基本假设亦大相逕庭。例如，哲学家们认为儒家的道德概念与合宜的社会行为有必然關係，这見解在我们最近的研究发现中得到了支持，更多的北京大学生應用“不道德” 這詞 於“在公众场所高声說話及谈笑”，而不是“杀害某人”上。这些发现质疑了心理学上对于道德与成規的区别，也质疑了一个的假设，即那些被认为是最严重错误的行为在不同文化都會被认为是不道德的。尤其重要的是，它說明我們極需要更多有关中国道德概念的研究，從而丰富道德认知的理论。 通过使用多种研究方法，这研究在我們近期和正在进行的研究基础上探討以下研究问题： 1. 现今具有影响力的由西方发展的文化共通道德原则理论（即道德基础理论;Haidt& Joseph，2004年）是否符合中国本土對不道德行为的理解？抑或是中国的道德概念需要尚未包括在西方道德理论中的新“道德基础”来解释？ 2. 中国人是否真的把文明行为的社会规范視为道德的一个必然層面，那是否意味着：a）把道德规则和社会成規劃分為放諸四海皆準的不同心理現象的理论是不可信的？（Turiel，1998年）以及 b）違反中国的社会成規(針對內團體成員，而非指其他文化的成员而言)會導致严重的人际交往后果）？ 这项关于中国道德概念的研究是十分有意义的，不仅因为中国道德传统的独特性，也因为它日益增长的国际地位。而且，中国是一个文化多元国家，对公民的道德有不盡相同的要求。这项研究探討关于道德本质的基本哲学与实際问题。透過两组研究，希望能檢驗与拓展现今具影響力的道德理论。 我们希望，这个研究项目的成果幫助我們了解因为道德概念的文化差异而产生的实際与理论上的结果，从而豐富我们對人类道德认知各種可能性的認知。
